docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The weather is an estimate of past weather (ERA5 temperature, CAMS irradiance), which flatters the solar term, and CAMS's anomaly attenuation lowers K-iii.
  • The filter's residuals use past weather up to the information cut.
  • The vintage is itself uncertain by ±20%, and MVA substations have no capacity truth.
  • The real generator case is a hindsight fit and enters no forecast score.
  • The trial MVA substations barely bounce, so reverse flow rests on one substation (D12) and the known-answer test.
  • The paired bootstrap months were fixed before the 24-month window was chosen, test 4's alignment tolerance is a judgement, and the interval gate is weak evidence (20 substations, months drawn independently). K-iii's paired-ratio coverage was not tested.
  • Every forecast is day-ahead (D+1), so these results say nothing about longer leads.
  • Node blocks are 7 days long, a deliberate choice for a quick look. A 3-day follow-up is the next step if the node is wanted.
  • One year's screening interval is about ±0.4 points, so C3 and the small contrasts are descriptive.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether any change to the capacity arms can make capacity identified. The data show a capacity within ±20% of the vintage at 4 of 5 substations, but a 90% range wider than the floor at 3 of 5, and arms that close the demand routes (K-iii) fail the known-answer gate. The hypothesis recorded before any scored fit is that day-of-year harmonics, drift, and the per-band profile absorb the seasonal cycle of temperature and clear-sky PV, leaving only day-to-day weather anomalies to identify slope and capacity. A test is a gate in which harmonics, drift, and profile are removed in turn.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
• Substations appear by D-label only. No figure, table, or bullet names a Primary.
  • G-c is generator data. Published text describes G-c as "a Primary with an embedded generator, summed with its neighbour", shows no dates, and links it to no D-label. G-c appears in no figure.
  • Injected farms appear as ratios only.

docs.title: What Part 5 asked, and the bar it started from
docs.text:
Part 5 asks four questions, each answerable on its own:

  1. Capacity identification. Does the fitted PV capacity stay put when the routes by which demand terms can imitate solar are closed, and does it land near the capacity estimates that were available in real time (the "vintages" of experiment 45)?
  2. The MVA observation layer. Does reading the 8 MVA Primaries through P = D − PV, Q = tanφ·D + q0, |S| = √(P² + Q² + ε) forecast |S| at least as well as reading |S| as P, and does a learned Q beat NGED's convention Q = 0?
  3. The unmetered generator node. Does a flat, non-negative, piecewise-constant generator recover an injected generator, and stay off on real demand substations?
  4. The export clip. Does the smooth clip recover an injected clip, stay open where Part 1 found none, and help at D5, the one decision site Part 1 flags (clipping in 4 of 7 summers)?

The bar is the convex model, not the pooled neural model. In Part 3's scored year the pooled neural model lost to the per-site neural model (+0.385 points; verdict capped at inconclusive by a failed known-answer gate), while the convex model with every year of history scored 2.726 and, with Part 4's filter and pinned capacity, 2.29 (2.90 without the filter). Part 3 also found that the pooled model's fitted capacity follows its starting value, but that its profile has a minimum near the convex capacity: the data identify capacity to about 15%. The "near the vintage" band and the precision floor below are read with that figure in mind. Every decision contrast gets a replicate year, a season split, and a row without D16.

docs.title: Which model and which base arm Part 5 runs on
docs.text:
The default is the convex per-site model studies.dp_gam with pinned capacity and Part 4's filter.

  • The base arm B is Part 4's A2 (all years from each site's first usable date, lockdown out, no drift, pinned capacity, the Kalman filter), at Part 4's three cuts, reused as stored. If Part 4's contrast C4 fails (drift still needed), B is A3 (drift D1 plus filter). If Part 4 hands the exponentially weighted mean to Part 6, B uses it.
  • The node's base is B-D1, Part 4's A3 (D1 plus filter), whatever B is. A non-negative step path on a base without drift absorbs any fall in demand (D10's fell from 55 to 43 points), so the node needs a drift term beside it to be read as a generator.
  • Every arm is scored twice: after the base's filter (hyperparameters by marginal likelihood on that arm's own tuning-year residuals), which is the forecast that would be used, and without it, which is the structural reading. Planned contrasts are read filtered, with the unfiltered contrast beside each, because the filter absorbs part of what a node or clip explains. The known-answer gates run without the filter.
  • The pooled branch is switched off. Part 3's gate failed, so the pooled questions go to the partially pooled convex model (N0) and to a variable-projection fit of the pooled model, planned separately. The manager may switch the branch on before the scored fits; if so, it adds the layer in dp_pooled and capacity arms on three starts, on the GPU.

docs.title: Size triggers
docs.text:
• Stored data: private files only, and one new row set (dp_mva_sunlit_v1).
  • Serving path: not touched.
  • Degradation rules: not touched.
  • Several defensible designs: yes, and this page pre-registers one of each.
  • Callers: Parts 5 and 6 of the series, and N9. The module pull request goes to main first, with two Opus reviews (leakage and known-answer truths first), and merges before any real score.

docs.title: Module changes (studies.dp_gam, studies.dp_operator; each test under 5 minutes)
docs.text:
• (i) Orthogonal demand terms. A quadratic penalty λ·Σ cov(term, u)², taken separately for the harmonics block and the heating block, over daylight rows, within each calendar quarter × half-hour cell, where u is the derated unit PV shape. Covariance is linear in θ, so the fit stays convex. Lighting is left out: its ramps are a function of elevation and anti-correlated with u by construction, so the penalty would only delete lighting. Its midday movement is reported. λ is in units of the Gram matrix's mean diagonal over the penalty matrix's mean diagonal.
  • (ii) Demand terms blind to clear-sky output. The day-of-year harmonics get one coefficient shared by all hour bands (no day-of-year × time-of-day term), and the heating hinge uses only the 72 and 168 hour smoothed temperatures, whose day-to-day link to sunshine is weak.
  • (iii) Capacity from irradiance anomalies only. The solar term becomes C·(u − ū) + A[month, half-hour], with ū u's month-by-half-hour mean over the training window and A ≥ 0 a free solar climatology per site under a ridge (A is aliased with the profile). A cannot grow with capacity, so K-iii trains on the last two season-years only. Forecasts use both terms.
  • Fitted capacity in each K arm follows Part 2's behaviour. K-base is A2 with fitted capacity. The convex solver solve_bounded_quadratic takes no start, so the K arms need no start check.
  • The meter fit (fit_gam_through_meter). The loss (|S| − √(P² + Q² + ε))² is not convex: a mirror basin exists wherever P can change sign, and tanφ·D(θ) is bilinear. The fit is Gauss-Newton: linearise √ at the current P and Q and solve each step with the existing solve_bounded_quadratic, which keeps the bounds exact. With learned Q, θ steps alternate with (tanφ, q0) steps. The fit is multi-start from four states (capacity 0.5, 1, and 2 times N's, and G-dark's demand with no solar), keeps the lowest loss, and reports the spread across starts. qmode is zero (tanφ = q0 = 0, NGED's convention) or learned. tanφ ≥ 0 (lagging load), which removes the (tanφ, q0) → (−tanφ, −q0) mirror. The power-factor prior is centred on 0.97 with 95% of its mass on 0.95 to 0.99. q0 is free in sign (cable capacitance makes it negative) with scale 2 points. MVA capacity is fitted, because MVA sites have no vintage.
  • The unmetered generator node (flat type, behind a typed interface). Net power is D − PV − G(t) with G(t) ≥ 0 built from daily positive and negative step parts under an L1 penalty, so an outage is a pair of steps. The level is aliased with the profile: it is identified only as the deepest outage under G ≥ 0, so where no full outage occurs it is unrecoverable and only the steps are read. A fit with G(t) below zero fails loudly.
  • The smooth clip. PV = P_max − softplus(β(P_max − m·C·u))/β, with β = 2 per point, one P_max per site, and a capacity multiplier m. For given (m, P_max) the clipped PV is a fixed column, so both are profiled on a 2-D grid (m from 0.7 to 1.3 in steps of 0.05; P_max from 40 to 100% of m·C in 5% steps), with one convex fit each. Profiling m stops the clip absorbing error in the pinned capacity (D5's convex-to-vintage ratio is 0.85, close to a 70 to 90% "clip").
  • Tests.
    1. With λ = 0, route switches off, A = 0, no node, m = 1, and P_max infinite, every option reproduces B's fit exactly.
    2. The meter fit with qmode zero on P > 0 everywhere matches the plain convex fit to 1e-5.
    3. The apparent operator's gradient is finite at P = Q = 0.
    4. The leakage asserts of Parts 2 and 4 hold, including that ū, A, the clip grid, tanφ, and q0 use training rows only.
    5. The node on a synthetic series with no generator stays under 0.5 points. The module pull request also times one site's multi-start meter fit.

Part 4's three cuts, so that every choice is made on a year that is never scored:

Year Cut Role 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30 2023-07-01 tuning: λ, the node's penalties, the XGBoost bar, C4's arm 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30 2024-07-01 replicate, and the first capacity cut 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 2025-07-01 scored: the verdict, and the second capacity cut

Pinned capacity follows dp_pinned_capacity exactly, including D14's held value and the disclosed leak at the tuning cut.
  • Leads: 09:00 UTC daily, 7 days ahead; the headline is D+1.
  • Predictions written: time_series_id, valid_time, power_fcst_init_time, all 11 levels (q01, q05 to q95, q99), actual, lead_hours, arm, seed, and filtered. Meter arms add p_mw and q_mvar, and node arms add generator.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Every arm is screening tier: one frozen fit per cut, on the CPU.

Capacity identification (all three cuts; the label reads the 2024-07-01 and 2025-07-01 cuts):

Arm What closes the route Window K-base nothing (A2 with fitted capacity) all years K-i (i) per-term covariance penalty in quarter × half-hour cells all years K-ii (ii) no day-of-year × time-of-day term, slow temperature only all years K-iii (iii) anomalies only last two season-years K-ii+iii (ii) and (iii) together (exploratory) last two season-years

The capacity bootstrap costs one batched solve per arm. Each arm gets 20 month-block bootstrap weightings in the batched Gram matrix, at the cost of one fit.

The MVA layer (all three cuts):

Arm MVA rows Meter Role N dark and sunlit none: |S| read as P (experiment 79's naive fit) C2's comparator L0 dark and sunlit Q = 0 the decision arm: NGED's convention LQ dark and sunlit learned Q tests the Q = 0 assumption G-dark dark only demand alone, Parts 2 to 4's rule the no-solar reference

L0 minus N isolates the meter. L0 and N differ only in reading |P| against P, so L0 minus N isolates the meter. L0 minus G-dark measures training a solar term on sunlit MVA rows, not the meter.

The generator node and the clip:

  • B-node: B-D1 with the node at every MW site, where the node must stay off.
  • B-clip: B with the clip at D5 only. B-clip-all: the clip at every MW site, where the clip must stay open at each site Part 1 did not flag.
  • B-gen: B-D1 with the node at every MW site and the clip at D5, the full generation-side model.
  • The real generator case (hindsight only). G-c is a Primary with an embedded generator, summed with its neighbour. The node is fitted over the whole usable history of the sum, and the node's level is compared with the mean dark-row export of the series that carries the generator, which is mostly the generator (no temperature slope). The fit covers the scored months, so it is labelled hindsight and enters no forecast score. There is no forecast arm: the history before the 2025-07-01 cut is too short to identify heating or a season.

XGBoost bars (CPU, lagless, experiment 87's Primary hyperparameters without the three power lags, 11 quantiles, Part 2's ERA5 and CAMS inputs, on B's window). Part 4's X-best, X-bestz, X-bestamq, X-bestam, and its C6 bar (the tuning-year winner of X-best and X-bestamq) are reused as stored, with X-best+K (the filter on XGBoost's residuals) beside it. X-mva is X-best on |S| at each MVA site (no offset, because there is no vintage), filtered and unfiltered. Lagged XGBoost at 24.5 to 48 hours is descriptive. BG2 does not enter Part 5, because it is Part 6's bar. References are climatology and manual_heuristic.

Tuning (on 2023-24, fitted at the 2023-07-01 cut):

  • λ for K-i: the smallest value on {0.1, 1, 10, 100} at which every penalised term's |corr| with u falls under 0.05 in every daylight cell. If none does, λ = 100 and the residual correlations are reported; the arm is still judged.
  • The node's step and level penalties (3 × 3 grid) on an injection that gate test 4 never uses: flat generators of 6 and 15 points with one step and one 14-day outage, injected at D5 (D9 has no usable rows at the tuning cut) on other dates. The chosen values are the largest at which that injection is recovered.
  • C4's arm: among the K arms, the one with the best tuning-year score, recorded before any later fit.

docs.title: Known-answer gate (pre-registered)
docs.text:
A failed blocking test stops scoring of the component it tests until it is fixed. If it cannot be fixed inside the part, that component counts as failed, and the verdict follows "Decision rule".

  1. Injected PV from a mismatched plant. Subtract synthetic PV at extra capacities of 10, 30, and 60 points from each MW decision site's net power, built from real CAMS irradiance through a plant unlike dp_features.FLEET: an east-west mix (azimuth 90° and 270°, tilt 15°), DC:AC 1.3 with inverter clipping, no temperature derating; and a second plant facing south-west at tilt 25°, otherwise the same. PV with the model's own shape lies in the capacity column's span, and any linear fit would recover it exactly, so only a mismatched plant tests anything. A K arm passes if the fitted capacity rises by the injected AC capacity within 20% at every site, level, and plant.
  2. Injected farms (experiment 39's harness, at D10, D11, D14, and D16, keeping night rows at the injected site). A K arm passes if the median ratio of recovered to injected capacity lies in [0.75, 1.25]. For K-iii the ratio is also reported divided by its K-base ratio.
  3. The meter recovers sign, capacity, and power factor. At the MW decision sites, inject a farm at experiment 79's level 1.0 (the window's median absolute midday power) so that reverse flow is common. Build Q = tanφ·D with power factor 0.97 from the demand component of the pinned B fit (not from the reading, which carries rooftop PV), and replace each reading by √(P² + Q²). Fit L0 and LQ from the multi-start. The test passes if LQ's balanced accuracy of flow direction is at least 0.78 (experiment 79's 0.779), each site's capacity is within 15% of LQ fitted to the signed series, and the median recovered power factor is within 0.01 of 0.97. A variant at experiment 79's level 0.5 (little reverse flow, the real sites' regime) is reported, not blocking.
  4. The node recovers a generator. Into D10, D11, D14, and D16 (one fit each, on B-D1), inject a flat generator of 10 points, with one +5-point step on a known date, a 14-day outage, and a 1-day outage. The test passes if the step is placed within 7 days and sized within 30%, the 14-day outage is found, and the level, read at that outage, is within 20%. The 1-day outage is reported only.
  5. The clip recovers an injected clip. At D10, D11, D14, and D16, inject a farm and clip the total PV (pinned rooftop C·u plus the farm) at 60% of that total's summer peak, so that the truth has the model's form. Fit the 2-D profile. The test passes if P_max is within 10% of the injected clip at 3 or more of 4 sites.
  6. Module tests 1 to 5 pass.

No output shows an injected farm's power. Injected farms are metered generators, so only ratios appear in any output.

docs.title: The capacity rule (pre-registered; labels, not contrasts)
docs.text:
A K arm (other than K-iii) is identified at a cut if, at 4 or more of the 5 decision sites, both of these hold for the last trained season-year:

  • Precise: the 90% bootstrap range (the 2nd to the 19th of the 20 ordered values) is at most max(3 points, 10% of the capacity).
  • Near the vintage: the capacity lies within ±20% of the vintage's season-year mean (experiment 40's capacity uncertainty). D14 is judged against dp_pinned_capacity's held value and flagged. Part 3's profile found capacity identified to about 15%, so a ±20% band is already loose.

The label needs both capacity cuts and gate tests 1 and 2. Otherwise the arm is not identified, with the failing clause named per site. The bootstrap measures sampling noise, not route bias, so precision alone proves nothing, and the closed-route arms carry the bias test. robust holds if at least two non-base K arms are identified and both agree with K-base within the precision floor at 4 or more of 5 sites. K-iii is judged by its ratio to K-base: it is consistent if, at 4 or more of 5 sites, the bootstrap range of K-iii / K-base overlaps [0.65, 0.87], the slope with which CAMS tracks a real farm's anomaly (experiment 63). A ratio in range supports K-base, and a ratio near 1 or below 0.65 does not.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
Five contrasts were pre-registered. Five planned contrasts, Bonferroni-corrected (99% intervals from studies.bootstrap, resampling whole calendar months of stored predictions, paired across arms), at day D+1. Each is reported with site counts, every arm's absolute score, the mean-forecast error, the replicate year's estimate and count, the unfiltered contrast, and the robustness rows. The margin is 0.10 points. One year's screening interval is about ±0.4 points, so non-inferiority is decided on the point estimate, as in Part 3's screening ruling. The interval is reported, and an interval wholly above zero means refuted.

  • C1, the generation side does not harm the MW forecast: B-gen minus B-D1 at the MW decision sites. It passes if the point estimate is at most +0.10 in both years. The arms are nested and the node and clip are sparse, so a pass is weak evidence on its own, and the components' real-data clauses ("Decision rule") carry the rest.
  • C2, the meter: L0 minus N on |S| at the 8 MVA sites, all rows, with sunlit and dark rows reported apart. It passes if the point estimate is at most +0.10 in both years. The expected result is near zero, because the trial MVA sites barely bounce.
  • C3, learned Q against Q = 0: LQ minus L0 on |S| at the MVA sites (two-sided).
  • C4, fitted against pinned capacity: C4's arm (chosen on the tuning year) minus B at the MW decision sites, at most +0.10 in both years. It runs only if that arm is identified.
  • C5, the DP against lagless XGBoost: B minus Part 4's C6 bar, unfiltered against unfiltered, with B minus X-best+K beside it. It is labelled and is not part of the verdict.

C3 and C4 cannot be decided at this noise level (predicted within ±0.05 against a ±0.4 interval). Each is reported descriptively, with no verdict word, wherever its interval spans both −0.10 and +0.10, and a choice handed on from either is labelled provisional.

Exploratory at 95%: L0 minus G-dark (a solar term trained on sunlit MVA rows), with its dark-row part as a control that should be zero; each K arm minus B; K-ii+iii; per-site power factor and q0 with bootstrap intervals; B-node minus B-D1 and B-clip minus B per site; and L0 minus X-mva. Descriptive only: D9; coastal D5 and D9; bank holidays, the Christmas run, and days below 0 °C; L0's MW against experiment 79's fit, which includes the scored months.

docs.title: Changes made before any scored fit
docs.text:
Five changes were made before any scored fit. These follow the module reviews and the script review, and the maintainer's wish for a quick look at the node. They change this plan's text above; the rest of the plan stands.

  • The node's blocks are 7 days long, a deliberate choice for a quick look. A node fit takes 2 to 10 seconds at 7-day blocks and 14 to 34 seconds at 3-day blocks. Outages of 14 days or more are resolved, so the tuning outages and the gate's long outage are 14 days, not 3 and 7. If the node arm looks promising, a follow-up at 3-day blocks is the next step.
  • The node's costs do not depend on the window length (the step cost per point, the level cost per point per day), and a node needs a drift term beside it. A generator is evidenced only by an outage, so the real-data clause "node under 1 point" reads the depth of the deepest outage (generator_evidence), not the range of the level path.
  • Known false positives of that readout, pre-registered: a short unmodelled rise in demand (7 days, 4 points reads as 2.3 to 2.6 points) and D10's jump in November 2024.
  • The learned reactive power is fitted only where the data hold reverse flow (at least 0.5% of training rows); otherwise it is held at a power factor of 0.97 and the fit says so.
  • The gate certifies the configuration the scored arms use: every gate fit uses the scored arm's window (all years), tests 1 and 3 include D5, a farm half-hour with no reading or a dropout leaves training instead of being injected as zero, and test 5's truth is the rooftop output times 1.25, clipped at 60% of its peak, so that the truth lies in the profile's grid.
  • Intervals. The capacity bootstrap keeps each calendar quarter's months and is widened by sqrt(m / (m - 1)) (experiment 113), and the ratio of K-iii to K-base uses the same month draws. A separate calibration gate (e00110_gate_intervals.py) tests the capacity intervals of the four capacity arms on 20 synthetic substations each, at independent noise of 5.0 points and at noise made of the real residuals of random months of the same quarter. It tests both the 80% interval (coverage 70 to 90%) and the 90% range that the cards and the identified rule print (coverage 80 to 100%), reports the counts with binomial ranges, and is weak evidence: 20 substations pass an interval that truly covers 80% about 84% of the time, and one that covers 60% or 95% about a quarter of the time. Months are drawn independently, so it cannot catch dependence between months. The point tolerances of the main gate stay as the pre-registered record. The substation cards show capacities with intervals, and the line "weakly identified at real noise levels (experiment 112); compare across substations with care".
  • C4's arm is chosen among K-base, K-i, and K-ii, because K-iii has no identified label, and C4 runs only if its arm is identified. robust does not require K-base, and handing fitted capacity to Part 6 also requires K-base identified. D14 is judged against its held capacity.
  • Hypothesis to test: day-of-year harmonics, drift, and the per-band profile absorb the seasonal cycle of temperature and clear-sky PV, leaving only day-to-day weather anomalies to identify slope and capacity.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
Each prediction was written before any fit, and each can fail. Written before any fit. Each line can fail, and none overrides the decision rule.

  • K-base: precise at 5 of 5 sites; within ±20% of the vintage at 3 or 4 (Part 2's convex capacity runs 4 to 21% below the vintage); identified at one cut or both.
  • K-i and K-ii: within the floor of K-base at 4 of 5 sites; at least one identified, so robust is reachable but not certain. K-ii's unfiltered score is 0.05 to 0.20 worse than B's.
  • K-iii: ratio to K-base 0.65 to 0.87 at 4 of 5 sites (consistent); bootstrap range wider than K-base's at every site.
  • Gate test 1: K-base recovers 0.85 to 1.05 of the injected AC capacity; the east-west shape is the harder case for K-iii.
  • Gate test 3: LQ's balanced accuracy 0.78 to 0.85; power factor 0.96 to 0.98; at level 0.5 the power factor's interval spans most of 0.95 to 0.99.
  • Real power factors: recovered (bootstrap interval narrower than 0.95 to 0.99) at 2 or fewer of 8 MVA sites, since on dark rows secφ folds into the demand scale.
  • Node: with D1 beside it, under 1 point at 4 or more of 5 decision sites; D10 is the likeliest false positive (its demand fell from 55 to 43 points, and it has a jump in November 2024). On the hindsight sum, the node's level lies within 25% of the dark-row reference.
  • Clip: the profiled m at D5 is 0.80 to 0.95; P_max sits at the grid top at every site Part 1 does not flag; B-clip minus B at D5 on summer midday rows is −0.05 to −0.3 unfiltered.
  • C1: within ±0.05 filtered and ±0.10 unfiltered, in both years. C2: within ±0.03. C3: within ±0.05. C5: −0.2 to −0.6 unfiltered; B minus X-best+K −0.1 to −0.4.
  • Tails: B-gen's q05 and q95 coverage within 3 points of nominal, and q01 and q99 within 1.5.
  • Run time: the default plan in under 2 hours of wall clock on 8 CPU cores.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
The verdict answers whether the convex model can represent the generation side without making the demand forecast worse. Capacity gets its own labels (identified, robust, consistent), stated in the take-home message and the bullets, never in the verdict field.

A component passes when its gate and its real-data clause both hold:

  • Layer: gate test 3 passes and C2 passes.
  • Node: gate test 4 passes; on real data the node stays under 1 point at 4 or more of 5 decision sites in both years, and the hindsight sum's level is within 25% of the dark-row reference.
  • Clip: gate test 5 passes, and on real data B-clip-all's P_max stays at the grid top at every MW site that Part 1 does not flag.

The verdict:

  • supported: all three components pass and C1 passes.
  • partly supported: C1 passes and one or two components pass.
  • refuted: C1's interval lies wholly above zero in the scored year, so the generation side makes the MW forecast worse.
  • inconclusive: anything else, including any gate that cannot be fixed inside the part.

What is handed on, each needing the same sign in both years:

  • Capacity to Part 6 and N9: if K-base is identified and robust, Part 6 may run fitted convex capacity as a variant beside pinned capacity. Otherwise capacity stays pinned, and the failing clause names what to try next.
  • The layer: L0 goes to N9 if the layer passes. LQ replaces L0 only if C3 lies below −0.10 in both years.
  • The node: it stays behind its switch, with drift beside it, and is used only where Part 1's screen flags a generator, if the node passes.
  • The clip: it is used at D5 only if the clip passes and B-clip minus B at D5 is below zero in both years, filtered.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, part 6: the DP as a forecast engine on ENS, against BG2
docs.text:
The Kalman filter on recent errors lowers the convex differentiable-physics (DP) demand model's score when the model is driven by ECMWF ensemble weather forecasts, and that is the part of the hypothesis this year of data supports. The model's standing against lagless XGBoost and against the production recipe (BG2, the best guess of experiment 87) is undecided.

The five planned contrasts are C1 (GAM-0 minus X-nl), C2 (GAM-K minus X-nl+K), C3 (GAM-margin minus Xlag-d), C4 (GAM-K minus GAM-0), and C5 (the production recipe with and without the DP's margin). GAM-0 is the convex DP model with drift and no correction. GAM-K is the same model with no drift and with the Kalman filter. GAM stands for generalised additive model. X-nl is lagless XGBoost, with its default start. Xlag-d is lagged XGBoost, and GAM-margin is Xlag-d given the DP's forecast as its base margin (the starting prediction the trees then correct). A negative contrast favours the first arm. "Replicate months" are the even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, and SIMP1 is the earlier experiment that fitted lagless XGBoost on ensemble weather.

Scores are quantile scores in points of the substation's effective capacity (lower is better), at the five decision Primary substations D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, over leads of 0.5 to 168 hours, on every half-hour outside the hand-filtered switching events (switching events marked by hand in the telemetry). The scored year is 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. The filter lowered the convex model's score by 0.151 points (98.75% interval -0.295 to -0.008), by 0.392 points at leads under 24 hours and by 0.017 beyond 144 hours. GAM-K was 0.134 points better than lagless XGBoost with the same filter (-0.305 to +0.014, which includes zero). GAM-K differed from BG2 by +0.020 points (-0.109 to +0.157, not like for like, with BG2 better at 3 of 5 substations). GAM-K is the DP's candidate for the roughly 1,300 substations of Flexpectation v2. The DP's own forecast, given to lagged XGBoost as a starting point, changed nothing measurable.

We asked whether the physical model, driven by real weather forecasts as production would be, forecasts demand better than XGBoost when both see the same weather forecast and the same recent observations, and whether giving the production recipe the physical model's forecast as a starting point improves it. Parts 1 to 5 of the series drove the physical model with estimates of past weather (ERA5 temperature and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) irradiance), which a live service would not have. Here the model runs once per member of the 51-member ensemble, with the ensemble's temperature and irradiance calibrated onto ERA5 and CAMS, and the filter reads the model's recent errors made with the ensemble's own 9.5-to-33-hour forecasts. XGBoost trains on ensemble control-member rows. We took the branches of the plan from Parts 3 and 4 (see "Arms, rows, and settings"). BG2 is compared with GAM-K only as an exploratory contrast, because BG2 differs in three lags, a five-member blend, and weekly refits. C5, the confirmation run that would compare the production recipe with and without the DP's margin like for like, was not run: the plan's literal trigger (C3 below zero) was met by the estimate of -0.023, but the series owner ruled that C5 would run only if C3 showed a gain, and an interval from -0.217 to +0.183 shows none.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and settings
docs.text:
• Branches taken (Parts 3 and 4). GAM-K has no drift (Part 4's C4 passed non-inferiority in both years) and a 24-month training window (Part 4's C1 was not supported); GAM-0 keeps drift. The capacity is pinned to experiment 45's real-time vintage in every arm. The pooled arms of Part 3 were not run, because Part 3's onboarding and short-history contrasts were not supported. Part 4's drift step of 30 sat at the edge of its grid, so GAM-0's step was tuned afresh on the tuning months over 30 to 100,000 and the step of 30,000 won, inside the grid (mean tuning scores 3.180 at 30, 3.021 at 10,000, 3.018 at 30,000, 3.040 at 100,000).
  • Periods. Tuning is the odd months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, replicate is the even months, and the scored year is the 292 runs of fold_a_daily_gap_v1. The solar shrink chosen on the tuning months was 1 in every lead band (no shrink); the spread factors were 0.9 to 1.15, with 0.9 at the lower edge of the plan's grid for GAM-K in three bands, where the score differs by 0.003 to 0.013 points from a factor of 1.
  • Calibration. Fitted on the tuning months per site, season, lead band, and hour band: the temperature shift ranged from -1.15 to +2.05 K (mean +0.20) and the daylight irradiance ratio from 0.80 to 1.11 (mean 0.95) over the decision substations (Figure 6).
  • DP arms. GAM-0 (drift, no correction), GAM-K (the main arm), GAM-E (14-day weighted mean in place of the filter), GAM-K-era5 (the filter on ERA5 and CAMS residuals, which a live service would not have), and GAM-ens (trained on ensemble control rows, fitted once at 2025-07-01).
  • XGBoost arms. X-nl is SIMP1's no-lag monthly recipe (500 rounds, eta 0.05, half-life 0.5 years), reused for the scored year from SIMP1's stored refits after one refit at D10 reproduced within -0.003 points of quantile score, and refitted here for the 12 tuning and replicate months. X-nl is SIMP1's raw refit, with no spread factor: SIMP1's stored p_nl_monthly widens its quantiles by 1.15 and scores 3.110 against 3.088 here. X-nl+K adds the same Kalman filter, fitted on X-nl's 24-hour block residuals. Xlag-d is the lagged member with three origin lags, GAM-margin is Xlag-d with the DP's forward-chained forecast as the base margin, both refitted monthly at 150 rounds and eta 0.15 on leads up to 168 hours. X-nl-z and X-nl-o (zero start; median plus experiment 64's solar offset) ran for the scored year only.
  • Predictions are stored in the experiment store, one set per arm and period (<arm>_scored and <arm>_replicate), in points of effective capacity with the 11 quantiles, the observed power, the lead, and a switching-event flag; the filter arms add the filter's level and transient, and GAM-margin adds the DP's margin.
  • Rows. 464,358 half-hours shared by the arms of C1 at the five decision substations in the scored year; D9 is scored beside them in the 6-substation rows; D18 is descriptive and enters no contrast.

docs.title: Decision rule and verdict
docs.text:
• The verdict is partly supported. The label rests on the series' Phase A rule (a negative estimate with at least 4 of 5 decision substations better, and no interval requirement), applied to C2 and C4. Under that rule C2 is supported: -0.134 (-0.305 to +0.014), 4 of 5 substations better, and the same sign in the replicate months (-0.098 in February, April, and June 2025 with 4 of 5; -0.316 with 5 of 5 over all even months). Its 98.75% interval includes zero, so the page calls C2 undecided in its headline. C4 (the filter's gain on the convex model) is wholly below zero (-0.151, -0.295 to -0.008) and inside the predicted range at both ends of the lead range. C3 is neither supported nor small gain (its interval spans zero). C5, the only contrast that can say "beats BG2", was not run (see "Departures from the plan"). No contrast is wholly above zero, so the verdict is not refuted.
  • Production status is candidate. GAM-K with the filter is the DP's candidate for the roughly 1,300 substations of version 2, because its filter gain survives ensemble weather and its score is within 0.02 points of BG2's, although the interval (-0.109 to +0.157) allows BG2 to be better, and BG2 is better at 3 of 5 substations (not like for like: BG2 has three lags, a five-member blend, and weekly refits). The candidate carries four caveats: C2 is undecided, XGBoost's history is short, five substations over one year is a small sample, and the margin gave no gain.

docs.title: Headline numbers
docs.text:
Scored year, five decision substations, quantile score in points (negative favours the first arm); the interval of C1 to C4 is 98.75% (Bonferroni across four) and every other interval is 95%, from resampling whole calendar months of run initialisations, paired across arms. The numbers come from e00111_report.py, saved as report.md.

  • C1, GAM-0 minus X-nl (X-bar): -0.137 (-0.513 to +0.185), 3 of 5 substations better. Absolute scores 2.951 and 3.088. The median-forecast error contrast is -0.218. C1 is -0.670 from November to March and +0.215 from April to October. Without D14, C1 is -0.031.
  • C2, GAM-K minus X-nl+K: -0.134 (-0.305 to +0.014), 4 of 5 better. Absolute scores 2.800 and 2.934; median-forecast error -0.159. At leads under 24 hours C2 is -0.162 (-0.315 to -0.029). Without D5, C2 is -0.210 (-0.337 to -0.098).
  • C3, GAM-margin minus Xlag-d: -0.023 (-0.217 to +0.183), 3 of 5 better. Absolute scores 2.853 and 2.877; median-forecast error +0.001. Without D5, C3 is +0.014.
  • C4, GAM-K minus GAM-0: -0.151 (-0.295 to -0.008), 3 of 5 better. By lead: -0.392 (-0.498 to -0.288) under 24 hours, -0.244 from 24 to 48 hours, -0.100 from 48 to 144 hours, and -0.017 (-0.165 to +0.159) from 144 to 168 hours. C4 is -0.026 from November to March and -0.234 from April to October.
  • Replicate months. All even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, where XGBoost trained on 3 to 14 months of ensemble rows: C1 -0.679 (-2.193 to +0.257), 4 of 5 better; C2 -0.316 (-0.721 to +0.035), 5 of 5; C3 -0.103 (-0.691 to +0.386); C4 -0.215 (-0.396 to -0.057), 5 of 5. In February, April, and June 2025 only (10 or more months of XGBoost rows; three months, so the figures below are the pooled estimate and the range of the three single-month estimates, not intervals): C1 +0.221 (months -0.092, +0.287, +0.446), 1 of 5 better; C2 -0.098 (-0.363, -0.191, +0.241), 4 of 5; C3 +0.334 (+0.402, +0.092, +0.510), 1 of 5; C4 -0.377 (-0.494 to -0.312 across months), 5 of 5. So the sign of C1 and C3 is not stable, C2's is positive in June, and C4's is negative in all three months.
  • Substations in the scored year. C4 by substation: D10 -0.489, D11 -0.250, D14 -0.225, D5 +0.128, D16 +0.130, so the filter worsens GAM-K at D5 and D16. X-nl+K minus X-nl by substation: D14 -0.648, D16 -0.058, D10 -0.050, D5 -0.016, D11 +0.015.
  • D9 and D18. D9 is scored beside the decision substations: with it, C1 is -0.109 (-0.454 to +0.190), C2 -0.121 (-0.298 to +0.051), C3 +0.014 (-0.175 to +0.206), and C4 -0.152 (-0.297 to -0.007). D18 is one substation whose DP fits start in July 2025 and whose X-nl comes from SIMP1's refit with D18's commissioning months cut, so its rows are descriptive: GAM-K minus GAM-0 -0.756 (-1.924 to +0.413), GAM-K minus BG2 +0.215 (-0.411 to +0.982), X-nl minus BG2 +0.314 (+0.022 to +0.572), GAM-0 minus X-nl +0.675 (-0.399 to +2.156).
  • Exploratory, scored year. GAM-K minus BG2 +0.020 (-0.109 to +0.157, not like for like), better at 0 to 24 hours (-0.060) and worse beyond 144 hours (+0.063). X-nl minus BG2 +0.308 (+0.196 to +0.450). GAM-K minus Xlag-d -0.077 (-0.218 to +0.067). X-nl+K minus X-nl -0.154 (-0.308 to -0.023). GAM-K-era5 minus GAM-K -0.008 (-0.024 to +0.008). GAM-E minus GAM-K +0.034 (-0.011 to +0.082), worse at 0 to 24 hours (+0.174). GAM-ens minus GAM-0 +0.248 (+0.007 to +0.513). GAM-margin minus Xlag-o -0.020 (-0.192 to +0.150), which agrees with C3. X-nl-o minus X-nl-z -0.023 (-0.077 to +0.023) and X-nl-o minus X-nl -0.006 (-0.039 to +0.037).

docs.title: Absolute scores
docs.text:
Arm (scored year, 5 decision substations) Quantile score BG2 2.780 GAM-K-era5 2.792 GAM-K 2.800 GAM-E 2.834 GAM-margin 2.853 Xlag-d 2.877 X-nl+K 2.934 GAM-0 2.951 X-nl 3.088 GAM-ens 3.200

Each row is on the rows it shares with its contrast partner, so scores quoted from two contrasts differ in the third decimal. Climatology and the manual heuristic are in Figure 3 and 7.

docs.title: What the filter does
docs.text:
• The filter's gain sits in the first two days for the convex model, and the two model families gain in different places. GAM-K minus GAM-0 is -0.392 under 24 hours and -0.017 beyond 144 hours, and the first two lead days carry about 60% of the pooled gain. X-nl+K minus X-nl is -0.382 and -0.028 by lead, but its pooled gain of -0.154 is almost all at D14 (-0.648; -0.027 without D14), while the filter worsens GAM-K at D5 (+0.128) and D16 (+0.130). The families also gain in opposite seasons: GAM-K from April to October (-0.234) and X-nl+K from November to March (-0.379). In the replicate months the two disagree in size (-0.377 against -0.058 in February, April, and June 2025; -0.215 against -0.578 over all even months), so "the filter helps both families equally" is not supported. Part 4 found -0.61 on past weather at the day-ahead lead; the ensemble gain at 0 to 24 hours is about two thirds of that.
  • The persistent level carries the correction (Figure 5). The transient part is about 0 at every lead.
  • ERA5 residuals add nothing. GAM-K-era5 minus GAM-K is -0.008 (-0.024 to +0.008), so a live service gains nothing from waiting for ERA5.
  • The 14-day weighted mean is worse at short range. GAM-E minus GAM-K is +0.174 at 0 to 24 hours and -0.043 beyond 144 hours.

docs.title: What did not help
docs.text:
• The DP's forecast as a base margin. C3 -0.023 in the scored year and +0.334 in February, April, and June 2025. D5 contributes the gain: without D5 C3 is +0.014.
  • Training the convex model on ensemble rows. GAM-ens minus GAM-0 +0.248 (+0.007 to +0.513), +0.591 from November to March, which is the opposite of what the train-each-weather-on-its-own- history rule would predict for this model, which the plan flagged as a departure from that rule, and the result is worse, not better.
  • Experiment 64's solar offset on lagless XGBoost. X-nl-o minus X-nl-z -0.023 and minus X-nl -0.006 over all rows. On the April-to-September daytime rows the plan names (08:00 to 16:00 UTC), X-nl-o minus X-nl is -0.116 (-0.145 to -0.084) and X-nl-o minus X-nl-z -0.034 (-0.093 to +0.028), so the first is inside the plan's -0.05 to -0.20 and the second is not.

docs.title: Predictions against results
docs.text:
Prediction Result Within? C1 -0.05 to -0.40, gain concentrated in 0-48 h -0.137; the gain is spread across leads (-0.152 at 0-24 h, -0.093 at 144-168 h) estimate yes, shape no C2 -0.05 to -0.25, same sign in replicate months -0.134 scored; -0.098 in February, April, and June yes C3 -0.02 to -0.15 -0.023 scored; +0.334 in the replicate months barely, and the replicate disagrees C4 -0.3 to -0.6 at 0-24 h, under -0.1 beyond 144 h -0.392 and -0.017 yes C5 -0.01 to -0.08 not run (see "Departures from the plan") no result GAM-K 0.0 to 0.4 worse than BG2 +0.020 yes X-nl 0.5 to 1.4 worse than BG2 +0.308 below the range GAM-K-era5 beats GAM-K by 0.05 to 0.20 at 0-24 h -0.044 no (just outside) X-nl-o minus X-nl-z -0.05 to -0.20 on April-to-September daylight rows -0.034 on those rows (-0.023 over all rows); X-nl-o minus X-nl is -0.116 on them edge Tails: q05 and q95 within 3 points of nominal, q01 and q99 within 1.5 GAM-K's coverage is within 1.84 points of nominal at every level and band (largest: q05 at 24-48 h, +1.84; q01 at 24-48 h, +1.40); GAM-margin and Xlag-o are 3 to 5 points off (see "Tail calibration") yes for GAM-K, no for the margin arms Each arm under 10 minutes seconds for the DP, about 1 minute per XGBoost refit when the GPU is free, 7.88 job-hours for the XGBoost arms in total no

The SIMP1 audit partly explains the X-nl gap. SIMP1's lag penalty is 0.361 points as an average over the 16 Primaries, including D15, and 0.125 without D15, not the 0.9 points assumed in the plan. The five decision substations each had a lag cost of at most 0.22 there, so our 0.308 is larger than SIMP1 alone predicts. X-nl minus BG2 also carries BG2's five-member blend and its weekly refits, which X-nl does not have.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The median forecast minus the mean forecast is under 0.17 points at every site and DP arm (for GAM-K -0.117 at D5, -0.043 at D11, -0.037 at D10, +0.015 at D14, +0.002 at D16), because the ensemble mixture is not symmetric. XGBoost arms hold only the median.
  • The median-forecast error agrees in sign with the quantile score for C1, C2, and C4, and disagrees for C3 (-0.023 against +0.001, both about 0) and for X-nl-o minus X-nl-z (-0.023 against +0.032).
  • Six of the seven audit triggers fired.
    • Trigger 1, a control fails: the first run of the gate failed two readings, both from a sign error in the gate's own fake irradiance (the fake scaled CAMS up by 1.25 where the plan scaled it down by 0.8, and the test expected the wrong ratio); the second run passed 22 of
    • X-nl's reproduction of SIMP1 held at the one refit checked, at one substation.
    • Trigger 2, a result contradicts a prediction: fired for X-nl minus BG2 (+0.308 against +0.5 to +1.4), partly explained by the SIMP1 audit (see "Predictions against results"), for C1's shape, and for the offset rows.
    • Trigger 3, the quantile score and the median-forecast error disagree: fired for C3 and for X-nl-o minus X-nl-z, both within noise.
    • Trigger 4, leaving a site out flips a contrast: fired for C3, where D16 carries more than D5 (without D16 +0.048, without D5 +0.014), and changes C2's label (without D5 -0.210, -0.337 to -0.098, wholly below zero).
    • Trigger 5, a nested arm beats its container, or a null control moves: fired on the plan's pairs. GAM-0 beats GAM-K at D5 (+0.128) and D16 (+0.130), and X-nl beats X-nl+K at D11 (+0.015). The null control GAM-K-era5 minus GAM-K (-0.008) stayed within its interval.
    • Trigger 6, an interval far wider or narrower than a sister's: fired for C3, whose half-width of 0.20 is about four times experiment 87's 0.05 for nested steps, and for C1 and C2, whose widths (0.70 and 0.32) are under half and under a fifth of Part 4's C6 (1.69).
    • Trigger 7, a later design depends on an unreplicated result: did not fire. The candidate status rests on C4, which replicated in the even months (-0.215, -0.396 to -0.057, 5 of 5 substations better).
  • An audit was called for. Triggers 1 to 6 fired, so a fresh Opus audit of the numbers ran before the prose review; the page states its findings.

docs.title: Known-answer gate
docs.text:
The gate passed 22 of 22 readings on its second run. The first run failed two readings, from a sign error in the gate's own fake irradiance; both runs are kept (gate_run1_sign_error.json). The gate ran on the tuning months before any replicate month or scored run. The calibration recovered a temperature bias of +1.5 to +3 K and an irradiance factor of 0.8 within 15%, and the calibrated fake scored within 0.05 points of ERA5 and CAMS. The calibrated ensemble's irradiance peaked within one half-hour of CAMS's at every site (a pass at the limit: the offset was exactly one half-hour at 6 of 7 sites), with a midday ratio of 0.88 to 0.90. The filter carried a median 1.07 of an injected transfer by the end of day 2, 0.93 from day 2 to the end, and 0.000 three days after the end (16 transfers at D10, D11, D14, and D16). The margin's error on earlier runs was 0.98 of its error on the tuning months' runs, and the module's tests passed (Figure 8).

The recovery readings are exact (0.000) by construction. The fake's member noise has zero mean across the 51 members, so the readings check the indexing and the arithmetic and not the calibration's response to noise.

The calibrated-fake reading passes narrowly and compares unlike scores. The calibrated fake's error differed from ERA5's by 0.049 against a limit of 0.05. That reading compares mean absolute errors where the plan says quantile score, with the real ensemble's analysis proxy (the control member of the latest run, standing in for the weather analysis) kept in the noise-free fake.

Test 4 (the margin's stability across periods) is a stability check, not a leakage check. It compares margin errors by period, cannot catch a leak in the training join, omits the replicate months, and compares April to June 2024 with the odd months, so the season differs.

docs.title: Departures from the plan
docs.text:
• Compute. The plan estimated 1.5 to 2 GPU-hours for the XGBoost arms; one 500-round refit on the whole history took 247 s while the GPU was shared, matching SIMP1's log, so the estimate was about 20 times too low. The margin family therefore refitted monthly, not weekly, on leads to 168 hours at 150 rounds and eta 0.15; X-nl for the scored year reused SIMP1's refits; X-nl-z and X-nl-o ran for the scored year only; the placebo margin, the zero-start lagged arm (Xlag-z; Xlag-o is the median plus experiment 64's solar offset), GAM-K-w and GAM-K-fc (two planned filter variants), and the tuning-month choice among start rules were not run, so X-bar is X-nl with its default start; and C5, the like-for-like comparison with BG2, was not run. The plan's literal trigger (C3 below zero) was met by the estimate of -0.023, but the series owner ruled that C5 runs only if C3 shows a gain, judged -0.023 (-0.217 to +0.183) not to be one, and the budget was short. The production-setting pair was coded and then removed from the scripts. The XGBoost jobs logged 7.88 job-hours (including about 0.02 job-hours of smoke jobs), plus the early refits, which were not logged.
  • Implementation. No WeatherInputLayer was filled (the pooled arms did not run). The PV shape is not derated by the member's temperature in the weather layer, because the convex model derates it itself. A member with a missing shortwave value is dropped from its run at that site (member 36 of the 2025-06-04 run at D9 and D11). The last scored run (2026-06-30) is left out of the DP and margin arms because the grid ends before the held-out period. The offset arms' training rows omit the last two weeks of June 2025, which experiment 87's anomaly table lacks. The filter's hyperparameters were fitted in one round, with Part 4's fitted prior, not by the plan's empirical-Bayes rounds. The plan's "all rows" robustness row (the contrasts on every row, switching events included) was not run.
  • The XGBoost arms' spread was not tuned, where the plan tunes a factor per arm on the tuning months. The code review found that even the best factor chosen on the scored year would gain at most 0.004 points, so C1 and C2 are unaffected.
  • Xlag-bar is Xlag-d, fixed in advance of the margin results, where the plan chose it among Xlag-d, Xlag-o, and Xlag-z on the tuning months. Xlag-o minus Xlag-d is -0.003, and C3 against Xlag-o would be -0.020.
  • X-nl+K at D10 in July 2025 uses this experiment's own reproduction refit and not SIMP1's (an effect of about 0.003 points).
  • The offset arms use held capacity. X-nl-o, and the offset start in general, take experiment 64's held capacity for training and prediction rows alike, and not experiment 87's real-time capacity vintages.
  • The tails table is on each arm's own rows and not on shared rows, and holds no threshold-weighted CRPS; curtailment cost was not computed.
  • GAM-0's drift step was retuned on this experiment's tuning months (30,000, inside a grid of 30 to 100,000), where Part 4 chose 30 at the edge of its grid.
  • X-nl was reproduced at one refit at one substation (D10) before SIMP1's stored refits were reused for the scored year. X-nl+K got no spread factors.
  • The substation cards omit panels the series asks for (no heating slope and no fitted capacity, and no per-site intervals beyond the note under the cards).
  • The pinned capacity uses hindsight weeks, as Part 4 discloses for its vintages.
  • C1's shared rows are 464,358 half-hours, and C4's are 464,363, because the arms' row sets differ by 5 half-hours.
  • D18. SIMP1's refit with D18's commissioning months cut is the source of D18's X-nl rows; D18 enters no contrast.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• XGBoost had 3 to 27 months of ensemble history, and the convex model years of past weather. The replicate year flatters the DP for that reason (C1 -0.679 in all replicate months, +0.221 in the three months with 10 or more months of rows). The range is 3 to 14 months in the replicate months and reaches 27 in the scored year.
  • The tuning months are in-sample for the spread, and the replicate months are interleaved with them.
  • The 73 stride runs of the scored year (every fifth day, never scored) chose BG2's blend and offset, and BG2's spread factor of 1.15 is experiment 18's.
  • Two mild shared leaks: the 2024-25 margins use a calibration fitted on the same odd months, and the convex model's last training rows use ERA5 that a live refit would not yet have.
  • The analysis proxy is the control member of the latest run, not an analysis.
  • Hindsight switching masks apply to every scored row.
  • Five substations, one year. The intervals resample 12 months.
  • The reversal of C1's sign in February, April, and June 2025 may be seasonal: the scored year's C1 is +0.215 from April to October, and +0.221 in those three months.
  • BG2 is not like for like with GAM-K, and BG2 is better at 3 of 5 substations; a difference of +0.020 is not evidence that the two forecast equally well.

docs.title: Tail calibration
docs.text: GAM-K's q01, q05, q95, and q99 coverage sits within 1.84 points of nominal in every lead band, and lagless XGBoost's q95 coverage is 4.4 to 5.5 points below nominal at every lead band (Figure 7). The margin arms are worse: GAM-margin's coverage is 3 to 4.5 points off nominal at every tail level (for example q05 at 9.0 to 9.5% and q95 at 90.8 to 91.5%), and Xlag-o's is 1 to 4.6 points off (q95 at 90.4 to 91.3%). Xlag-d's q95 is 1.8 to 2.7 points low. GAM-margin's quantile spread from q01 to q99 is 23.8 points, against 51.6 for Xlag-d and 38.2 for BG2, so its intervals are too narrow. Curtailment cost against manual_heuristic was not computed: at the MW Primaries experiment 87 found no event at the scaled limit that the metric could rank forecasts on.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text: Provisional: fitted to past weather, forecast on ensemble weather, screening run. The cards show the weekday daily profile of GAM-K's fit at the 2025-07-01 cut, the pinned solar capacity (an input from experiment 45's real-time estimates, not a fitted value), and the filter's weekly mean level over the scored year. No heating slope or fitted capacity is shown. Heating slopes and capacities are weakly identified at real noise levels (experiment 112); compare across substations with care, and interpret no threshold per site. Identification improves with more weather anomalies, which is a reason a longer history could help interpretability.

docs.title: Open questions after this experiment
docs.text:
• Does a longer ensemble history (the 2021 to 2024 backfill on Source Cooperative) settle C1 and C2? The maintainer decides whether to fetch it.
  • Does the filter lower the production XGBoost blend's score as it lowers X-nl's? The result is a candidate for the next release review.
  • Does the filter, which lowers GAM-K's score at only 3 of 5 substations, gain more at substations whose level changes (D15, D18 predicted)? D18's descriptive row (-0.756) points that way, from one substation.
  • Does the margin help at weekly cadence? The plan's cadence needs about 60 GPU-hours at the speed measured here.
