docs.title: Differentiable physics, NRA: edge flows between Primaries, and the normal-running forecast
docs.text:
The registered flow fit failed its known-answer gate on all seven readings, so the verdict is inconclusive. Fitted with the settings chosen before any fit, the flows find 0.22 of the megawatts that we injected as transfers over 1 day (the gate needs 0.77) and change no forecast. Settings that find more also put flow on pairs of substations with no interconnection. In the tuning grid, every configuration with recall above 0.5 put 17 to 30 MW-days a year on the two tuning placebo pairs, against a limit of 0.05. The post hoc variants, which are exploratory and play no part in the verdict, recover up to 0.86 of the injected megawatts over 1 day and put 18 and 29 MW-days on the two pairs. The placebo pairs probably soak up the opposite-signed slow drifts that a demand model with no drift term leaves in its residuals. Flows fitted this way therefore cannot be read as switching without a drift term or a topology check; this page proposes both as next steps and does not commit the project to either.

The failure is a limit of the registered objective, and the zero placebo is an ordering artefact. The Huber loss caps each row's pull on the flow, so a step in the flow appears only if the block of rows is long enough to outweigh the step penalty. At the chosen step constant of 300 that is 174 hours on the D10–D11 edge and 207 hours on the D5–D16 edge, against a longest gate transfer of 113 hours. In 5 re-fitted gate transfers the fitted step at onset was exactly 0 each time, so the recall of 0.22 comes from a flat offset across the whole window, not from detecting the transfer. A level constant of 0 also makes the minimiser non-unique, because a constant flow costs nothing: the constant lands on whichever path the fit visits first. The tuning placebo path was visited last, so its flow read about 0 for every configuration with level constant 0. With the placebo path visited first, the chosen configuration puts about 23 and 46 MW-days a year on the two tuning placebo pairs (measured on 4 tuning tiles of 72 days in total, then scaled to a year), against a limit of 0.05. This does not change the verdict.

We asked whether load that the network operator moves between two neighbouring Primary substations can be found from the half-hourly power readings alone. The method fits a flow for each interconnection between two substations to the residuals of a convex demand model (the model's forecast error), with a penalty that keeps flows constant for hours. We checked the method by adding known transfers of load between two substations to the real residuals (400 per set, on two interconnected pairs, D5–D16 and D10–D11). We asked how much of the moved power the fit found again, whether it found flow between pairs with no interconnection, and whether removing the flows from the training data or adding them back to the forecast changed the day-ahead error. The method did not pass: the registered settings find almost nothing, and the looser settings also find flow where none can exist.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The gate. The registered configuration (half-hourly flows, step constant 300, level constant 0, Huber threshold 1.5 noise scales) was chosen on 400 tuning transfers by the largest recall with under 0.05 MW-days of flow on each tuning pair. The gate then read 400 other transfers in the tuning year. All readings failed:

  • moved-MW ratio, the median over transfers of the fitted mean flow over the true mean flow: 0.05 (needs 0.8 to 1.25);

  • release, the share of found transfers whose causal flow is under 20% of the moved MW at the deadline: 0 (needs 0.5), on one transfer, because only 1 of the 201 large gate transfers reached a recall of 0.5 and so entered the test;

  • recall: 0.22 over 1 day (needs 0.77), 0.10 for 6 to 24 hours (needs 0.5), and 0.46 over 1 day on the realistic set (needs 0.5);

  • placebo in the replicate year: 0.0 MW-days on replicate placebo pair 1 and 2.9 on pair 2 (needs under 0.05 each; the 0.0 on pair 1 is probably the same path-order artefact);

  • normal-running gap: the forecast with the causal flows removed has a mean absolute error of 7.07 points against 5.82 for the plain filter and 3.76 for the oracle (the share of the gap closed is -0.60, needs 0.5). The first run of this reading, 7.28 points and -0.71, removed each substation's outside path as well as its edge flows by mistake; it was corrected in the experiment's script e00116_causal.py (not in the module), and only arm A5 was re-run, on module commit 6a57d0944; both runs are on file. The negative gap closure probably comes from the same free constant: a constant offset in each 30-day window, carried forward by the warm start, may sit on the edge and then be removed from the filter's level (plausible, not measured).

C1, the hindsight reconstruction. The edge flows rebuild 0.25 (98.33% interval 0.179 to 0.264) of the injected megawatts on 400 realistic transfers, against a requirement of at least 0.5 with the lower end above 0.25. Models trained on the injected history forecast the clean scored year with mean absolute errors of 5.82 (as trained), 5.79 (flows removed), and 5.78 points (oracle mask): transfers of up to a fortnight barely move a model with no drift.

C2, no harm outside events. Training with the edge flows removed (A4) scores 2.258 points against 2.262 for training on every row (A0) in the scored year: the difference is -0.003 (-0.015 to +0.010), and in the replicate year it is +0.007 (-0.002 to +0.018). Both upper ends are under the 0.05 margin, so C2's interval sits inside its margin. The failed gate blocks C2, though, and the flows are nearly empty, so this shows only that removing almost nothing changes almost nothing. Dropping the hand-filtered events (A1) changes the score by -0.000 (-0.006 to +0.005) in the scored year.

C3, causal flows in the forecast. On a sample of 100 injected transfers per year, A5 (A4's fit with causal flows) minus A4 is -0.002 (-0.026 to +0.017) in the scored year and -0.007 (-0.033 to +0.020) in the replicate year; it needs -0.5 or lower. The oracle, which knows the true flow, scores 4.02 points better than A4 in the scored year (-4.02, -4.69 to -3.12) and 4.46 points in the replicate year, so a correct flow would matter a great deal: scaled by the 4.5% of rows that lie inside hand-filtered events, the oracle gain is 0.18 points on all rows. A5 closes 0.0004 of the gap. The absolute scores are row means (A4 6.522, A5 6.512 points, a difference of -0.010), while the contrast is the mean over the 13 seeds of each seed's difference (-0.002), so the two do not reconcile by subtraction. A5 minus A4 on real rows outside events is -0.0003 (scored) and +0.017 (replicate); the limit is +0.03.

Post hoc variants (exploratory, chosen after the gate failed; the verdict does not use them). On 100 gate transfers of 25% and 40% of the receiving load: registered penalties with a Huber threshold of 10 noise scales give recall 0.35 over 1 day; step constant 10 and level constant 0.3 give 0.69 over 1 day with 28.6 MW-days on tuning placebo pair 2; adding the larger Huber threshold gives 0.70 and 43.7; step constant 3, level constant 0, and the larger threshold give recall 0.86 over 1 day, 0.74 for 6 to 24 hours, a moved-MW ratio of 0.79, and 18.4 and 29.5 MW-days on the two pairs.

Real transfers (descriptive, no verdict role). Three of the eight hand-filtered events on the two gate edges fall in a year with hindsight flows. The registered fit puts a mean flow of 1.19 MW on the edge over a 371-hour event that the labeller put at 1.5 MW, 0.10 MW over a 5.5-hour event labelled 2.8 MW, and nothing over a 101-hour event labelled 0.8 MW.

docs.title: Winter
docs.text: Winter changes no conclusion: no winter contrast has an interval that excludes zero, apart from one. Winter is November to March, a cold-snap day has a UTC-day mean ERA5 temperature under 2 °C, and an evening peak ends between 16:30 and 20:00 UTC; the rules were fixed before any score was read. C2 on winter rows: A4 minus A0 is -0.001 (-0.026 to +0.020) in the scored year and +0.010 (-0.005 to +0.024) in the replicate year. On cold-snap days (10 days scored, 20 replicate) it is +0.026 (-0.028 to +0.155) and +0.015 (-0.007 to +0.064), and on evening peaks -0.005 (-0.035 to +0.025) and +0.009 (-0.010 to +0.032). The one exception is A1 minus A0 in the scored winter (+0.007, +0.002 to +0.012; 0 of 5 sites better), where dropping the hand-filtered events is slightly worse. The cold-snap intervals are wide. No arm is proposed for production, so none is held back. A figure of the cold nights themselves is below: at the three substations with 10 cold-snap nights (D10, D11, D14) both forecasts run about 0.2 to 0.5 MW under the median observed power overnight, A0 and A4 alike; D5 and D16 have 2 cold-snap nights, too few to read. A5 is not on that figure, because its day-ahead run covers one origin in three days, which leaves too few cold nights; A5 equals A4 wherever the fit finds no flow, which is nearly everywhere. C3 on winter rows: A5 minus A4 is -0.010 (-0.027 to +0.044) in the scored year (28 transfers, too few) and +0.006 (-0.006 to +0.039) in the replicate year (37 transfers). On cold-snap days it is -0.065 (-0.237 to -0.009) on 6 transfers in the scored year and -0.052 (-0.052 to +0.002) on 11 in the replicate year, both too few to read. On evening peaks it is -0.022 (-0.044 to +0.060) on 28 transfers (too few) and -0.003 (-0.019 to +0.020) on 37. The evidence holds two independent winters (2024-25 and 2025-26); the 2023-24 winter was used for tuning and the gate. The two series labelled G-c have no winter in the data, and the injected transfers give no winter result at G-c.

docs.title: Checks and bullets
docs.text:
• Arms. A0: convex model (24-month window, no drift, pinned capacity) trained on every row. A1: the same with the hand-filtered events dropped. A4: A0 refitted on power minus the edge flows of the tuning and replicate years. A5: A4 with flows refitted causally at each origin on the trailing 30 days and added back with a Kaplan–Meier decay. Oracle: the true flow removed and added back.

  • Example forecasts. The four transfers in the forecast figure are, for each gate site, the first injected transfer by identifier in the 100-transfer scored-year sample that lasts at least 24 hours and moves load onto the site; the rule was fixed before any score was read.

  • Rows and scoring. 13 to 14 Primaries with data at each cut; scoring sites D5, D10, D11, D14, D16, with D9 beside them; quantile score in points of effective capacity, rows outside hand-filtered events; filter hyperparameters fitted on the tuning year; spreads from each arm's own run over the year before. C3 rows are origins every 6 hours from 6 hours before a transfer to 48 hours after its end, leads 0.5 to 48 hours, both ends of the transfer.

  • Tails. Scored year, rows outside events, day ahead: coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99 is 0.015, 0.053, 0.941, 0.983 for A0 and 0.015, 0.053, 0.941, 0.983 for A4; pinball loss at q01 and q99 is 0.173 and 0.183 (A0) and 0.173 and 0.183 (A4). On injected-transfer rows the plain filter's q01 coverage is 0.124 and q99 coverage 0.872 (nominal 0.01 and 0.99), and the oracle's are 0.014 and 0.983.

  • Checks. The median forecast equals the mean forecast at every site by construction, because the spread is centred on its median (difference 0.000). The mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast agrees in sign for every C2 contrast outside events (-0.007 and +0.009 against -0.003 and +0.007 in the scored and replicate years). The plumbing controls pass: the module's 42 tests, causality of the causal fit (exact), A5 with zero flows equal to the plain filter (difference 0), the same fits with the label file emptied or the power after the cut changed (difference 0), noise scales from pre-cut rows (difference 0), and 66 hand-filtered events (35 conserved, 31 one-sided).

  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 fired (the gate failed). Trigger 2 fired (a contradiction): the real 371-hour event is recovered at 1.19 of 1.5 MW although the injected recall is 0.22, and C1 and the gate recall are far below the predicted 0.55 to 0.85 and 0.8 to 0.95. Trigger 3 fired weakly for C3 in the replicate year (quantile score -0.007, mean error +0.000, both inside their intervals). Trigger 6 fired and is explained: the 98.33% intervals of C2 are 0.025 (scored) and 0.020 (replicate) points wide, under half the 0.29 to 0.40 of experiment 111's 98.75% intervals, as expected when two arms differ only by nearly empty flows. Triggers 4 (leave one out) and 5 (nested arms, including A5 with S = 1) were not run: the exploratory arms were skipped after the gate failed. Trigger 7 did not apply, because there is no positive verdict. An Opus audit of this page and the module has been done, and its fixes are applied.

  • Deviations from the plan. The block-coordinate sweeps stop at a tolerance of 1e-3 or 12 sweeps, not the 1e-6 the plan states; all whole-year fits and all re-run local fits stopped at 12 sweeps unconverged, and a re-run with 400 sweeps at 1e-9 left recall and the moved-MW ratio unchanged on 5 transfers. C2 and C3 were run although the plan says a failed gate stops them, to report them descriptively; C3 ran on a 100-transfer sample per year (seeds 0 to 12) instead of 400, because the registered flows are nearly empty and the gate had failed. Injected transfers are fitted as neighbourhoods (the paths at the two ends, on a window of 3 days either side) instead of as whole-year fits. Realistic transfers last at most 14 days. Replica spreads use the 09:00 UTC origin of every third day. The step-size rule for outside paths takes the node's first edge by name. A5 takes out edge flows only. C1 and the gate readings use the replicate and tuning years' frozen fits. The exploratory arms (demand-shaped shares, S = 1, a larger outside factor, the MVA rescale, and the sensitivity with G-c) were not run, because the registered gate failed.

  • Module. Tuning, the gate's first run, and the 400 tuning-year transfer runs used studies.dp_edge_flow at commit 6a57d0944; C1, C2, the replicate- and scored-year flows, the replicas, and C3 used commit abaac6097 (the Sonnet review's fixes). The Opus reviews of the module (causal window, then solver and audit) found no solver bug and no leak, and the tests that killed three surviving mutants were added before the merge.

  • What to try next (proposal only). Add a slow drift term per substation to the convex model before fitting flows, and compare flows on connected and unconnected pairs again; or accept a candidate flow only where the topology says the two substations are connected and the residuals move oppositely over days. The oracle's 4-point gain on injected rows says the payoff of a correct flow is large; the problem is finding it.

  • Privacy and links. Substations are shown by D-label; the two generator-carrying series are not shown. Plan and scripts are in pull request 1399. The module is in pull request 1400. The numbers on this page are printed by e00116_report.py.

docs.title: Substation cards (provisional)
docs.text: Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run. Each card shows two weeks fixed before any score was read, the first full weeks of December 2025 and June 2026: the day-ahead forecast of A4 with its 80% and 90% bands against the observed power, hand-filtered events shaded, the hindsight flows on the substation's edges and its outside path, and how A4 and A0 score on cold-snap days (with the day count, and "too few days" where there are under 10). The cards name each substation's interconnected partners as pairs and show no other topology. The flows are small because the registered penalties are stiff.

docs.title: The plan, as registered
docs.text:
The sections below are the plan committed before any fit, with the tuning result and the predicted gate failure recorded before the gate ran. They are kept as registered.

This plan's PR creates the Network theme (stub pages, a navigation entry under "Differentiable physics", a pointer in the two switching themes' plan.md). One id, one PR for plan and result; the module has its own PR off main.

docs.title: What experiment A asks, and what the data allow
docs.text:
Experiment A is a switching-and-NRA experiment, not a mean-forecast experiment. A perfect detector was worth 0.42% of the best guess's score (experiment 44), and label masks move the out-of-event score by under 0.03 points (experiment 75). Events touch 1 to 3% of rows, so a 10-point in-event gain moves the all-row score by about 0.2 points at most; contrasts are read on transfer rows, with that ceiling beside them.

Only two MW–MW edges have data in the tuning and replicate years: D5–D16 and D10–D11. The two series labelled G-c have only a few months of usable history at the scored cut (experiment 103), so every edge that touches them is exploratory. Of the 66 hand-filtered events, 6 have MW meters on both sides before the scored year, all on D5–D16. The verdict rests on injected transfers alone.

The gate, and every claim it licenses, covers those two edges. MW–MVA edges are reported, not gated; C3 injects only on D5–D16 and D10–D11 (sites D5, D10, D11, D16). D14 enters C2 only.

The Kalman filter already carries long transfers (experiment 106: 0.94 of the moved MW by day 2, all but 0.004 released within 3 days), so a causal flow can add skill only in a transfer's first day, the two days after it ends, and transfers under a day. C3 is built around those rows.

docs.title: The base model and the graph
docs.text:
GAM-K is experiment 111's decision form, run on past weather. The convex GAM has no drift, a 24-month window, and pinned capacity; Part 4's Kalman filter runs under the 3.5-hour telemetry delay, hyperparameters fitted by marginal likelihood on the tuning year per base arm. Weather is ERA5 and CAMS under the "lab conditions first" rule (experiment 111: ENS-driven residuals were as good for the filter, −0.008 points); ERA5-driven causal flows are not available at forecast time, and the page says so. Residuals enter the edges in MW (points × effective_capacity_mw / 100); an MVA site's dark-row residual enters in MVA, rescaled by 0.97 in a sensitivity.

Decision graph: the 21 metered edges that do not touch G-c, plus an outside path g_i per node. The interconnection file holds 37 undirected edges (17 pairs listed twice), 25 of them metered at both ends; the rest touch G-c. g_i carries transfers to unmetered partners, with step and level penalties ρ times the edge penalties, ρ ≥ 1, so a conserved transfer costs λ_f on its edge and 2ρλ_f on two g paths. MVA ends carry weight only on dark rows. The edges that touch G-c and the g paths of the two G-c series are zero in every decision arm. Exploratory sensitivity "with G-c": each such edge is split between the two G-c series and a link between them (30 edges, recounted by the script), with one G-c series given a convex fit (drift D1, fitted capacity) on its short history; its triangles are checked for circulations in P2. The script commits the edge counts before any residual is read.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Arm GAM Flows Filter A0 GAM-K, no switching masks none plain A1 GAM-K, hand-filtered masks (experiment 111's form) none plain A2 A0's frozen fit flat, half-hourly, hindsight plain A2-b A0's frozen fit flat, on 3-hour block means, hindsight plain A3 A0's frozen fit demand-shaped shares, hindsight plain A4 A0's GAM refitted once on y minus the chosen edge flows as chosen plain A5 A4's GAM the chosen model, refitted causally per origin flows as known input, held by S OR A4's GAM the true injected flows as A5, true flow and true end (ceiling)

A2, flat flows. For edge e = (i, j) with sign +1 at i and −1 at j, the path f_e minimises Σ_t H_i(r_i,t − f_t) + H_j(r_j,t + f_t) + λ_f Σ|f_t − f_t−1| + λ_l Σ_obs |f_t|, with r each end's partial residual (other paths removed) and H a Huber loss weighted by 1 / σ_i² and thresholded at 1.5 σ_i (σ_i the site's robust half-hourly residual scale in MW, from pre-cut rows only). The level penalty acts only on observed rows, and a path is held flat across rows with no reading at either end, so a gap neither pays λ_l nor ends a flow. A common shift leaks into f unless the end weights are equal, and fully on an MVA edge in daylight, which is why MW–MVA edges stay outside the gate. Block-coordinate descent stops when the objective's relative change and the largest path change (in MW) both fall under 1e-6.

Each path is solved exactly by a dynamic programme in the style of Johnson (2013) (stated there for squared error; the Huber, weight, and level extension is this module's, guarded by P1). ADMM (Boyd et al., 2011) on a banded Cholesky factor solves a non-negative flow and cross-checks the programme in the tests. Measured on the module branch: the exact programme takes 1.8 seconds for a 17,520-point solve whatever the penalties and 0.14 seconds for a 1,440-point window, and ADMM took 4.5 to 22 seconds at tolerances of 1e-3 to 1e-8, so the programme is the solver. Condat (2013) with soft-thresholding (Friedman et al. (2007)) is the unweighted reference.

A2-b answers the series brief's advice (experiment 67's hourly fit found 0.108 of the moved MW against 0.646 for a 24-hour step; experiment 113's half-hourly autocorrelation is 0.83): the same solver on 3-hour block means. A2 or A2-b is chosen on seeds T by the placebo rule, before seeds G are drawn; "the chosen flows" below means that choice.

A3 (exploratory), demand-shaped shares: f_e(t) = a_ij(t)·D_i(t) − a_ji(t)·D_j(t), D each end's fitted demand (fitted net power plus the pinned solar term), two non-negative piecewise-constant shares, λ_l > 0 (alike shapes leave the shares unidentified), on the MW–MW edges only.

A4 refits A0's GAM once on y minus the chosen edge flows, never minus g, whose level also absorbs growth and new connections.

A5, the causal metered forecast. At each origin τ:

  1. Build the trailing 30 days of residuals ending at τ − 3.5 hours with dp_assimilation.stitch_out_of_sample_residuals, so no origin reads in-sample residuals.
  2. Refit every path touching a scored node causally on that window, warm-started; no path is taken from the hindsight fit.
  3. Rerun the filter over the window on the residual minus that flow path, from the state the previous origin's run held at the window's start.
  4. Forecast GAM + ℓ + φ^h·z + f_now · S(a + h) / S(a), with f_now the newest causal flow and a the age of its current run.

S is a Kaplan–Meier estimate of the chosen hindsight flows' run lengths (|f| over 0.1 MW; runs cut by the window's end censored) in each cut's 24-month window, never fitted from labels.

Injections copy experiment 43's harness, with two shapes (its donor-shaped share, and a flat block drifting between 0.5 and 2 times its start), conserved on D5–D16 or D10–D11, never within 48 hours of a hand-filtered event or of D10's two unlabelled windows (2024-11-08 to 2024-12-01, 2025-11-17 to 2025-12-14). Counts are not limited by the real event rate: each seed holds up to 4 non-overlapping transfers per edge-year, at least 7 days apart, and each disjoint set (T, G, C1, C3) has 50 seeds drawn independently of the residuals, about 400 transfers. T and G span 4 sizes (0.5 MW, and 10%, 25%, and 40% of the receiving load) by 3 durations (3 to 6 hours, 6 to 24 hours, over 1 day, log-uniform within), at least 30 per cell; gate readings 1 to 3 use the 25% and 40% cells. The realistic set (C1, C3) draws size and duration jointly from the 66 events (median 1.0 MW for 31 hours, with durations capped at 14 days because one of the 66 lasts 31 days), the distribution S also sees. Expected 98.3% half-widths, measured on T before G is drawn: about ±0.06 on a recall or ratio per duration band and ±0.2 points on C3; if C3's exceeds 0.4 on T, every set doubles to 100 seeds.

Hundreds of injected transfers are fitted as neighbourhoods, not as whole-year fits. A whole-year fit of the 33 to 35 paths takes about 8 minutes, so each injected transfer instead gets a fit of the paths that touch its two ends, on a window that starts 3 days before the transfer and ends 3 days after the transfer's 48 post-event hours, with every other path at zero. The tuning and gate placebo flows are read the same way, on non-overlapping windows of 18 days that tile the year. The whole-year fits (tuning, replicate, and scored years, from experiment 111's base form) supply the real-data flows that A4 removes and the run lengths for S. An injected transfer is added to the frozen fit's residuals, which is exact for a fit that did not train on the injected rows; C1 is the exception, and refits A0 on the injected history.

docs.title: Years, rows, and the tuning split
docs.text:
Period Cut Role 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30 2023-07-01 tuning (seeds T; placebo pairs 1 and 2 of the tuning year); gate (G) 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30 2024-07-01 gate placebo (replicate placebo pairs 1 and 2); replicate; C1 rows 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 2025-07-01 scored: the verdict

Tuned on seeds T only: λ_f = c / σ_e, c in {3, 10, 30, 100, 300}; λ_l = c_l / σ_e, c_l in {0, 0.3, 1} (A3: {0.3, 1}); σ_e is the robust MW scale of the edge target (r_i − r_j)/2 on pre-cut rows; ρ = 1. The choice is the largest MW-weighted recall on T with under 0.05 MW-days per pair-year on the tuning placebo pairs; ρ = 2 is kept only if it adds 0.05 recall. Placebo edges are fitted in separate runs with the real graph present and never enter A2 to A5.

Scoring rows. Decision sites D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 (MW ends); D9 beside them. C2 uses day D+1 from 09:00 UTC origins, with and without D10's two unlabelled windows. C3 uses origins every 6 hours and leads 0.5 to 48 hours, because experiment 88 found no 09:00 origin inside a real transfer with both sides at most half missing. Predictions carry the keys, q01 to q99, actual, lead_hours, level, anomaly, flow, and an in-event flag. Spread: LeadSpread at day D+1; for C3 a lead-hours spread fitted on the replica through each arm's own pipeline.

docs.title: Plumbing controls and the known-answer gate
docs.text:
Plumbing controls run first; an unfixable failure makes the verdict inconclusive:

  • P1: the path solver matches a brute-force quadratic program on 200 random small problems (Huber, weights, zero weights, a gap inside a step, level penalty, non-negativity) to 1e-6; P1b: block-coordinate descent matches a joint program on a three-node graph, path by path;
  • P2: with zero residuals, every injected flat transfer is recovered on its edge with a moved-MW ratio of 1 to 1e-6 as λ → 0, nothing appears on other paths, and the "with G-c" triangles carry no circulation;
  • P3: changing any reading, residual, or flow input after τ − 3.5 hours leaves A5's forecast at τ unchanged; no fit trains on a row after its cut; σ_i, σ_e, and the Huber scale use pre-cut rows only; A0, A4, and A5 forecasts are unchanged when the label file is emptied; no origin's window holds in-sample residuals; A5 with flows forced to zero equals A4 exactly;
  • P4: the 66 events filter as experiment 101's real_events does (35 conserved, 31 one-sided).

The gate is blocking: a failed reading stops C2 and C3 and caps the verdict at inconclusive. It runs on seeds G in the tuning year, both shapes pooled; the release clock runs from the end in valid time, so the 6-hour allowance includes the 3.5-hour delay.

  1. Moved-MW ratio: median fitted over true mean flow, true edge and window, in 0.8 to 1.25.
  2. Release: the causal flow under 20% of the moved MW within the larger of 6 hours and 10% of the duration after the end, in at least half the transfers (experiment 101's end rule).
  3. Recall: MW-weighted recall (Σ min(fitted, true) MW-hours, right edge and sign, over Σ true) at least 0.77 over 1 day (RO-NC's injected figure) and 0.5 for 6 to 24 hours; at least 0.5 over 1 day on the realistic set.
  4. Placebo, out of sample: the two held-out replicate placebo pairs carry under 0.05 MW-days of |flow| per pair-year in the replicate year.
  5. NRA gap: on in-event and 48-hour post-event rows, the NRA forecast (A5 without the flow added back) scored against the uninjected truth closes at least 50% of the gap from A0 to the oracle (experiment 88: lag correction 51%, oracle-trained model 83%).

Reported, not blocking: reading 1 on in-sample residuals (injections in the 2023-07-01 cut's window, GAM refitted); MW–MVA power curves; one-sided injections at D11 and D16.

docs.title: Winter breakdown
docs.text:
Winter matters most, so every contrast is also read on winter rows. The best model reaches production in about a month, and the network operator first sees it in winter. Three winter scopes are defined here, before any scored contrast is read: winter is a valid time in November to March; a cold-snap day is a UTC day whose mean ERA5 temperature at the substation is under 2 °C, read within winter; an evening peak is a half-hour ending between 16:30 and 20:00 UTC, read within winter. C2 and C3 report each contrast on winter rows, on cold-snap days, and on evening peaks, with the same paired intervals where the rows are numerous enough, and say "too few days" where a scope holds fewer than 10 days or fewer than 30 transfers. A winter loss is a reason to hold an arm back even when the annual mean improves, and the verdict text says so; the thresholds of the decision rule below do not change.

The evidence holds few independent winters. The scored year holds the 2025-26 winter and the replicate year the 2024-25 winter, so C2 and C3 have two. The tuning year (the 2023-24 winter) carries the gate only, since A4 equals A0 there. Injected transfers are placed anywhere in the year, so the winter subset of C3 holds about 5 of the 12 months of each year's transfers, from the same two winters. The two series labelled G-c have no winter in the evidence, and the page says so.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
Three contrasts, Bonferroni-corrected (98.3% intervals from studies.bootstrap, resampling whole calendar months within each seed with seeds pooled, paired across arms), each with site counts, every arm's absolute score, the mean-forecast error, and the replicate year's estimate. Screening tier: one frozen GAM fit per cut and arm; the seed spread is printed.

  • C1, hindsight NRA reconstruction on injected training transfers (seeds C1, realistic set, in the 2024-07 to 2025-06 rows of the scored cut's window): 1 − Σ|y − f̂ − y_clean| / Σ|y − y_clean| over in-event rows at both ends, with the chosen flows f̂. Passes at an estimate of at least 0.5 with the interval's lower end above 0.25. Beside it, descriptive: the clean scored year's forecast by A4, A0, and an oracle GAM masked on the injected windows, all trained on the injected history; with no drift in GAM-K this gap is expected within noise.
  • C2, the label-free NRA model does no harm outside events: A4 minus A0 on real data, all rows outside the hand-filtered events, day D+1. Non-inferiority, margin 0.05 points (about 2% of GAM-K's day-ahead score): passes if the interval's upper end is at most +0.05 in the scored year and the replicate year. The power at a true zero, from the replicate's width, is printed. A4 minus A1 (can flows replace the labels?) and A1 minus A0 are reported beside it.
  • C3, the causal flow during and after transfers: A5 minus A4 (plain filter) on seeds C3 (about 400 realistic transfers) in the scored year, on in-event rows and the 48 hours after each end. Supported if the interval lies wholly below zero, the estimate is at most −0.5 points, 3 of the 4 sites improve, A5 closes 25% of the A4-to-oracle gap, and A5 minus A4 on real rows outside events is at most +0.03. Ceiling beside it: the oracle's gain, and that gain scaled by the in-event share of all rows (about 0.2 points at most). A5 minus A0 is reported beside it.

Exploratory at 95%: A2-b against A2; A3 minus A2; A5 with S = 1; C3 by event day; ρ = 2; the MVA rescale; "with G-c". Real events, a separate descriptive section with no verdict role: the 6 usable MW–MW events, the 66 by duration bin, and D10's two unlabelled windows.

Tails, every arm: coverage and pinball at q01, q05, q95, and q99 on all and in-event rows, per role, and the receiver's q99 exceedance inside against outside transfers; no curtailment cost (no generator forecast; experiment 87 found 0 events at f = 0.9 here). Comparators: every arm, climatology, manual_heuristic, and experiment 111's GAM-K (2.800) and BG2 (2.780) on ENS.

docs.title: Tuning result, recorded before the gate runs
docs.text:
The registered choice rule picked a configuration that finds little of the injected megawatts. Tuning ran on the 400 transfers of seeds T and the two tuning placebo pairs (module commit 6a57d0944). The chosen configuration is the half-hourly form with step constant 300 and level constant 0; its MW-weighted recall is 0.216 and its placebo flow is about zero, because almost no flow survives. Looser settings recover more (step constant 3, level constant 0: recall 0.776) but put 9.6 and 21.9 MW-days a year on the two placebo pairs, against the 0.05 limit. A pair with no interconnection absorbs the opposite-signed slow drifts of two substations, and a level penalty of 0.3 or more per megawatt leaves 25 to 31 MW-days on tuning placebo pair 2. The 3-hour block form (A2-b) is no better: its chosen configuration has recall 0.212.

Prediction added after tuning and before the gate: the gate's recall readings (0.77 over 1 day and 0.5 for 6 to 24 hours) will very likely fail with the registered configuration, which caps the verdict at inconclusive. The gate runs exactly as registered and its first run stays on the page. Any variant run afterwards, such as a larger Huber threshold or a looser step constant that ignores the placebo limit, is labelled post hoc and exploratory, and cannot change the verdict.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
Written before any fit; each line can fail, and none overrides the decision rule.

  • Gate: moved-MW ratio 0.85 to 1.1; recall 0.8 to 0.95 over 1 day and 0.4 to 0.7 for 6 to 24 hours (the reading most likely to fail, and better for A2-b than A2); realistic recall 0.5 to 0.8; release passes; placebo 0.01 to 0.04; NRA gap closed 0.5 to 0.8.
  • C1: 0.55 to 0.85; the clean-year forecast gap between A0 and the oracle GAM within ±0.02.
  • C2: A4 minus A0 within ±0.02; A1 minus A0 within ±0.03 (experiment 75).
  • C3: −0.5 to −2.0 points, closing 25 to 60% of the oracle gap, over two-thirds of it in each event's first day and the first 24 hours after its end; the all-row effect under 0.05 points.
  • Other: A3 beats A2 on donor-shaped injections only; S = 1 loses most of C3's post-event gain; A4's receiver q99 exceedance inside transfers is 3 to 10 times nominal, and A5 halves it.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
The gate first, then C1, C2, and C3; C2 and C3 must hold in the replicate year too.

  • supported: the gate passes; C1, C2, and C3 pass in both years.
  • partly supported: the gate and C2 pass, and only one of C1 and C3 passes, or C3 passes in the scored year but reverses sign in the replicate year.
  • small gain: the gate, C1, and C2 pass, and C3's interval lies wholly below zero but misses its size, site, or gap condition.
  • refuted: the gate passes and C2's interval lies wholly above +0.05 (the flows harm the NRA model), or C1's estimate is under 0.25 and C3's interval lies wholly above zero.
  • inconclusive: a failed plumbing control or gate reading (the take-home names the reading and what it rules out), or anything else.

The verdict rests on injected transfers only; real events never enter it.

docs.title: Substation cards and privacy
docs.text:
Each decision site's card gets a "network" panel: hindsight and causal flows with labelled events shaded, the g path, S, and A4's NRA forecast for a winter and a summer week. Edges are labelled by D-label pair (for example "D5–D16"); no edge to G-c appears; one fleet figure shows moved MW-days per D-label pair beside the placebo pairs. Labelled "Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run".

The published page uses "G-c" alone for the two generator-carrying series and their sum: never beside a D-label, name, or identifier; no dates; day counts on axes; own-capacity units; aria=False; "with G-c" only as G-c ratios and counts. No generator's public name with its series. The page may name interconnected D-label pairs, but no substation names and no other topology (no supply-point membership, no unmetered partners, no edge counts per named site).

docs.title: Audit before merge: the seven triggers
docs.text:
1. A control fails: any plumbing control or gate reading.
  2. A contradiction: C3 beyond the oracle; real-event recall above injected recall at the same size; A5 worse than A4 outside events while the placebo passes.
  3. Quantile score against mean error: C2 or C3 with opposite signs in the two.
  4. Leave one out: dropping D5–D16, D10–D11, or any decision site flips C2 or C3.
  5. Nested arms: A5 with S = 1 beating A5; A3 losing to A2 on donor-shaped injections.
  6. Interval width: C2's over twice or under half experiment 106's or 111's day-D+1 widths.
  7. Dependence: v2's NRA design rests on C1 and C2, so any positive verdict triggers an audit.

"Checks" bullets: median minus mean forecast per site and arm, mean error beside each contrast.

docs.title: Module, run order, compute, and open questions
docs.text:
Module studies.dp_edge_flow (own PR, two reviews, green tests): graph builder, path solver and ADMM fallback, block means, block-coordinate descent, stitched causal fit, Kalman known-input wrapper over run_kalman, Kaplan–Meier survival, lead-hours spread; tests P1 to P3, each under 5 minutes. Unmasked and oracle fits need no dp_gam change: scripts replace y, switching_mask, and default_rows (in_pool & ~lockdown & ~mask) on SiteFeatures.

Compute, CPU only, at most 6 cores: about 3 to 5 hours of wall clock. GAM fits about 12 minutes; hindsight flows (30 tuning fits of about 37 paths × 3 to 5 sweeps × 1.8 seconds per year-long solve, so about 4 minutes a fit, then each seed warm-started from the uninjected fit) about 2 hours on 6 cores; causal flows (730 daily origins, plus about 400 transfers × 10 six-hourly origins per year, each refitting the paths at the scored nodes on a 30-day window at 0.14 seconds a solve) about 1 hour.

Thinning decision, made before any fit: one 17,520-point solve takes 1.8 seconds, over the 1 second mark, and ADMM is slower, so the pre-registered thinning applies. C3's origins are every 6 hours, not every 3.

Settled before the run: C2's margin of 0.05 points stands, and the page reports A4 minus A0 (the decision contrast) beside A4 minus A1. C3 is A5 minus A4, with A5 minus A0 beside it. A failed gate caps the verdict at inconclusive, not refuted. The module adds no dependency.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, H2: a graph prior on the pooled convex model's parameters
docs.text:
At the weight we tested, tying the parameters of interconnected substations together did not improve the forecast, and it made two kinds of parameter interval too confident. In the scored year (2025-26) it worsened the average quantile score by 0.020 points (the interval spans zero) and the score in winter evening peaks by 0.173 points (the replicate year, 2024-25, gave −0.021). On synthetic substations with a known truth, the tie narrowed only heating-slope intervals, and the 80% intervals of PV (photovoltaic) capacity held the truth 17% of the time with the tie against 78% without it. A tie on heating slopes alone worsened the real-data score by 0.006 and 0.001 points in the two years (both intervals span zero), which is an exploratory lead and not a result. The pre-registered verdict is refuted.

We asked whether a penalty on neighbouring substations' parameters narrows their intervals without breaking coverage. The pooled convex demand model of experiment 109 predicts a Primary substation's demand from the calendar, the weather, and a PV term, and it fits each substation's own parameters: a heating slope (how much demand rises per 10 °C of cold, in each part of the day), a PV capacity, the scale of the daily profile, and a level for holidays. An 80% interval says how well two years of half-hourly readings fix a parameter, and its coverage is the share of such intervals that hold the true value. Experiment 113 found heating slopes known only to within about 38% of their size. Here a penalty pulls the parameters of interconnected substations (a pair such as D5 and D16 that are electrically connected) towards each other, with a weight set in rows of evidence per interconnection, and we required that the forecast get no worse than 0.03 points.

We tested the penalty on synthetic fleets with a known truth, and then on real data. A synthetic fleet is 15 substations built from the real calendar, weather, and PV shape of five Primary substations, with noise copied from real residuals. In the smooth cell the true parameters of interconnected substations are alike (correlation 0.8), and in the unlike cell they are drawn independently. We ran 120 fleets per cell (40 in each of three sets). The real data are the five decision substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16) fitted jointly with D9 and eight substations that train on night-time readings only, on a graph of 14 substations and 21 interconnections. Each fit is frozen at 1 July and scored over the next 12 months: 2023-24 tunes the weight (10,000 rows of evidence per interconnection), 2024-25 is the replicate year, and 2025-26 is the scored year.

The penalty narrowed only the heating-slope intervals, and a randomly rewired graph narrowed them just as much. On the synthetic fleets, heating-slope intervals shrink to 0.59 of the width of fitting each substation alone but cover the truth 70% of the time (76% without the penalty), and the profile-scale and PV-capacity intervals cover it 56% and 17% of the time (75% and 78% without). On real data neighbours' heating slopes differ by a mean squared amount about half that of random pairs, yet three randomly rewired graphs (each substation keeping its number of interconnections) narrow the real intervals as much, so the narrowing is not evidence that neighbours are alike.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Points are percentage points of a substation's effective capacity (a high percentile of its absolute power), so 1 point is about 1% of capacity. A heating slope is in points per 10 °C of cold. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles of the forecast, in points; smaller is better.
  • Arms. G fits each substation alone. N pulls every substation towards a fleet mean with a penalty of 3,000 rows of evidence (experiment 109's choice). H pulls interconnected substations' heating slopes, profile, holiday coefficients, and PV capacity together with a penalty of 10,000 rows of evidence per interconnection; a row of evidence is one training row's worth of weight. NH has both penalties. P-hol pools only the holiday coefficients of the five decision substations to a fleet mean (10,000 rows). H-perm is H on a rewired graph.
  • Contrasts are the first arm minus the second, so a negative number favours the first. R1 is H minus G, R2 is NH minus N, R3 is P-hol minus G on event days, and R3b is P-hol minus G on other days. R1w, R2w, and R3w are R1, R2, and R3 on winter rows. The plan required R1 and R2 non-inferior at +0.03 points in both years.
  • Event days are the days of the holiday periods the demand model carries (each bank holiday, Easter, the bridge days, and the Christmas to New Year run), without the clock-change days. Winter is November to March. The evening peak is the half-hours that start from 16:00 to 19:30 UTC. A cold-snap day is a winter day whose mean temperature is at or below the substation's 10th percentile of winter days in the two years before the cut.
  • Gate is the synthetic-fleet test. Readings (a), (b), and (c) are its pre-registered pass lines: (a) smooth-cell coverage within 5 points of G's, (b) interval widths of at most 0.85 of the reference arm's in two of three parameter families, and (c) unlike-cell coverage within 10 points of G's. The hold-back rule caps the verdict when a winter contrast's upper end is above +0.03 points in the scored year.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows the graph prior worsening the score a little on average and more in winter evenings. In the scored year H minus G is +0.020 points over all days, +0.055 over November to March, and +0.173 over the winter evening peak. P-hol scores 0.099 points better on event days in the scored year and level on other days.

Figure 2 shows the graph prior leaving scale and capacity intervals overconfident. Over 120 smooth-cell fleets, H covers the true heating slope 70% of the time (G: 76%), the profile scale 56% (G: 75%), and the PV capacity 17% (G: 78%). The fleet mean alone (N) also under-covers heating slopes, at 59%.

Figure 3 shows the narrowing being confined to heating slopes. H's median slope interval is 0.59 of G's width, and NH's is 0.81 of N's. Scale and capacity intervals narrow by 5 to 7% at most, and the holiday interval widens to 1.14 times G's.

Figure 4 shows a rewired graph narrowing real slope intervals as much as the real graph does. In the scored year H is 0.89 of G's width for heating slopes and the three rewired graphs give 0.80 to 0.90; H is 1.03 times the rewired graphs' width (1.04 in the replicate year).

Figures 5 and 6 give every arm's absolute score. In the scored year G is ahead of N, H, and NH on all days (by 0.02 to 0.07 points), in winter, and in the winter evening peak, and P-hol is level with G. In the scored year N, H, and NH are ahead of G on cold-snap days (4.04 to 4.06 against 4.20) and on event days (2.87 to 2.93 against 3.05). In the replicate year all arms are within 0.02 points of each other on all days. Every arm scores better than climatology and the manual heuristic in every column shown, by 0.13 to 1.2 points.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Verdict refuted, by the pre-registered coverage rule. The controls pass and the planted failure is detected. At a weight that passed the harm bound, H's smooth-cell coverage is under 60% and more than 10 points below G's for profile scale (56.3%, G 75.3%) and PV capacity (17.1%, G 78.0%), and so is NH's (54.5% and 16.0%). These are synthetic-fleet results, so the capacity and scale findings are worded as synthetic-only. Readings (a) and (c) fail, and reading (b) fails because only heating slopes narrow to 0.85 or less (H 0.59, NH 0.81; scale 0.94 and 0.98, capacity 0.95 and 0.97). Reading (d), a bias under a quarter of the interval width, fails for capacity (1.39 for H, G 0.20) and scale (0.28, G 0.24). The hold-back rule applies too: R1w's upper end is +0.102 and R2w's is +0.065 in the scored year, both above +0.03.

  • Real-data contrasts (98.75% intervals for R1 to R3b, R1w, R2w, and R3w; 95% otherwise; scored year, then replicate year). The R3 intervals resample whole days, not days within each holiday period as the plan said, because a period has one day per year.

    Contrast Scored year Replicate year R1, H minus G, all days +0.020 (−0.014 to +0.059) +0.014 (−0.009 to +0.039) R2, NH minus N, all days +0.013 (−0.012 to +0.041) +0.019 (+0.008 to +0.032) R3, P-hol minus G, event days −0.099 (−0.282 to +0.002) −0.018 (−0.071 to +0.024) R3b, P-hol minus G, other days +0.000 (−0.002 to +0.002) −0.001 (−0.005 to +0.002) R1w, H minus G, winter +0.055 (−0.006 to +0.102) +0.020 (−0.014 to +0.053) R2w, NH minus N, winter +0.031 (+0.003 to +0.065) +0.031 (+0.009 to +0.055) R3w, P-hol minus G, winter event days −0.106 (−0.438 to +0.020) +0.000 (−0.038 to +0.029) H minus G, winter evening peak +0.173 (+0.090 to +0.253) −0.021 (−0.085 to +0.045) NH minus N, winter evening peak +0.147 (+0.100 to +0.205) +0.033 (−0.008 to +0.070) H minus G, cold-snap days −0.165 (−0.414 to +0.043) −0.005 (−0.137 to +0.129) NH minus N, cold-snap days +0.016 (−0.087 to +0.121) +0.153 (+0.105 to +0.214) N minus G, all days +0.058 (+0.022 to +0.102) −0.004 (−0.047 to +0.041) H minus N, all days −0.037 (−0.079 to −0.003) +0.018 (−0.013 to +0.046)

    Non-inferiority of R1 at +0.03 is not shown in either year, and the scored half-width of R1 (0.036) is over the 0.025 limit, so the non-inferiority question is undecidable. H is better than G at 2 of 5 substations in both years. The P-hol event-day intervals rest on 22 event days in the scored year and 21 in the replicate year, with 1 or 2 days per holiday period, so the evidence is thin, and P-hol does not meet the plan's gain rule (interval wholly below zero) in either year. The cold-snap evidence is 11 to 13 days a substation-year. N pools 14 substations here and 7 in experiment 109, whose scored-year N minus G was +0.031.

  • Absolute scores (quantile score in points; five decision substations, outside switching events and clock-change days).

    Arm Scored, all days Scored, winter Scored, winter evening peak Replicate, all days G 2.883 3.36 3.45 3.166 N 2.941 3.49 3.63 3.163 H 2.903 3.41 3.62 3.180 NH 2.954 3.52 3.78 3.181 P-hol 2.879 3.35 3.45 3.165 Manual heuristic 3.484 4.10 3.91 3.843 Climatology 4.065 4.65 4.49 3.904

  • The synthetic gate (smooth cell; 120 fleets; coverage of 80% intervals).

    Family G N H NH H width / G NH width / N Heating slopes 76.1% 58.7% 70.1% 60.9% 0.59 0.81 Profile scale 75.3% 69.5% 56.3% 54.5% 0.94 0.98 PV capacity 78.0% 72.9% 17.1% 16.0% 0.95 0.97 Holiday level (not gated) 49.2% 49.3% 53.6% 47.3% 1.14 0.72

    In the unlike cell H covers 56.1% (slopes), 32.8% (scale), and 14.0% (capacity) against G's 74.9%, 72.2%, and 77.3%. In the wrong-graph cell (truth smooth on a different graph) H covers 69.0%, 49.8%, and 19.2% against G's 76.3%, 76.1%, and 77.7%. The planted failure (a weight of 100,000) covers 44.7% of slopes, 23.0% of scale, and 13.4% of capacity in the unlike cell, which is 30.1, 49.2, and 63.9 points below G (20.8, 15.6, and 32.1 standard errors), so the planted failure is detected. Correlated noise (not part of the verdict): 40 fleets per cell with a smooth truth and neighbour noise correlation 0.3 and 0.6. H covers heating slopes 75.3% and 70.3% against G's 76.2% and 75.4%, profile scale 53.6% and 48.0% against 81.4% and 73.0%, and capacity 18.2% and 19.5% against 77.7% and 77.5%, with slope width 0.58 of G's in both. Correlated noise does not rescue the scale or capacity intervals.

  • Why capacity fails (diagnosis on four smooth fleets, not part of the gate). The capacity term acts on the sum of a substation's capacity increments, a single number that the data fix with about 1,230 rows of information. At 10,000 rows per interconnection the weight on that sum is about 510, and a substation has 2.8 interconnections on average, so the penalty is as strong as the data and neighbouring capacities are tied almost completely. A graph penalty on capacity alone gave a mean absolute capacity error of 4.3 points against 0.85 without it and coverage of 25%; a penalty on heating slopes, the profile, or holiday coefficients alone left capacity at 80% coverage.

  • Tuning (before the gate). Every weight from 0 to 30,000 scored within one standard error of the best on the synthetic interval score, so the largest weight whose real tuning-year harm stayed within +0.02 points was chosen: 10,000. The holiday weight, 10,000, is at the top of its grid, so the event-day score might fall further at a larger weight.
  • The next weight up (30,000, exploratory; the plan's next grid value). In the smooth cell H covers slopes 66.0%, scale 46.5%, and capacity 16.6% (slope width 0.53 of G's). On real data H minus G is +0.048 (+0.013 to +0.086) in the scored year and +0.031 (+0.007 to +0.056) in the replicate year (95% intervals); NH minus N is +0.038 and +0.041. A larger weight narrows slopes more, lowers every coverage, and worsens the score more.
  • Real parameter intervals. Neighbours' heating slopes are alike: the mean squared difference across interconnections is 0.46 to 0.57 times that of random pairs for the four times of day in the scored year (two just under the predicted 0.5) and 0.32 to 0.79 in the replicate year; for the profile scale it is 0.88 and 1.17, and for the holiday level 0.35 and 0.33. H's heating-slope width is 0.89 (scored) and 0.70 (replicate) of G's, the three rewired graphs' is 0.80 to 0.90 and 0.60 to 0.71, and H over the rewired graphs is 1.03 and 1.04, so the real graph adds nothing over the three rewired graphs tried. G's residuals correlate 0.24 and 0.29 along interconnections.
  • Tails (all rows; coverage of the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles). Scored year: G 0.7%, 2.7%, 84.1%, and 93.9%; H 0.7%, 2.7%, 83.9%, and 93.7%; N 0.7%, 2.8%, 83.1%, and 93.1%; NH 0.7%, 2.8%, 83.5%, and 93.1%. Replicate year: G 1.9%, 5.5%, 79.9%, and 90.5%, and the other arms are within 0.3 points. The upper tail is under-covered by 11 points at the 0.95 quantile in the scored year and 15 in the replicate year, as in experiment 109, whose shortfall the plan attributed to a spread taken from one replica year. The pinball loss at the 0.95 quantile is 0.852 for G and 0.864 for H in the scored year.
  • Exploratory lead (not a result; the plan listed these arms as exploratory). A graph penalty on heating slopes alone (gamma 10,000) worsens the score by 0.006 (−0.011 to +0.026) in the scored year and 0.001 (−0.017 to +0.018) in the replicate year, and by 0.021 (−0.011 to +0.048) and 0.012 in winter (95% intervals). On the synthetic fleets it leaves scale (75.5%) and capacity (81.6%) coverage at G's level and narrows slope intervals to 0.59 of G's, but covers slopes only 68.0% of the time in the smooth cell (G 75.7%) and 55.0% in the unlike cell (G 72.9%), on the 40 fleets of set 1. A graph penalty on the holiday coefficients alone is level with G (−0.001 and +0.000).

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text:
• R1 and R2 inside ±0.02 with a half-width of 0.02 to 0.03: the estimates held (R1 +0.020 and +0.014, just at the edge in the scored year; R2 +0.013 and +0.019), and two half-widths failed: R1 in the scored year (0.036) and R2 in the replicate year (0.012).
  • R3 −0.1 to −0.5 and R3b inside ±0.01: R3 was −0.099 (just short of −0.1) and −0.018; R3b held (+0.000 and −0.001).
  • Smooth-cell coverage of H and NH 72 to 88% and within 5 points of G: failed (H 70%, 56%, 17%; NH 61%, 55%, 16%). Width ratio 0.6 to 0.9 for slopes and scale, 0.8 to 1.0 for capacity: slopes were just under the range (0.59, 0.81 for NH), scale was above it (0.94, 0.98), and capacity held (0.95, 0.97). Unlike-cell coverage 65 to 80%: failed (56%, 33%, 14% for H). The planted failure covers 40 to 60%: slopes 44.7% (held), scale 23.0% and capacity 13.4% (lower).
  • Real data, edge-similarity ratio 0.5 to 0.9 for slopes: 0.46 to 0.57 in the scored year (two bands just under 0.5) and 0.32 to 0.79 in the replicate year. H's width ratio against G 0.8 to 0.95 and against the rewired graphs 0.85 to 1.0: 0.89 held and 0.70 did not; 1.03 and 1.04 against the rewired graphs did not. Capacity changing by under 5% (two interconnections): not testable in the scored year, where capacity is pinned; in the replicate year H's capacity width is 1.02 and N's 1.15 of G's.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, per substation and arm: 0.000 at every decision substation for G, N, H, NH, and P-hol, because the spread is centred on the median. This check cannot show a shifted spread here; the mean-forecast error beside each contrast is the informative check.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each contrast (scored year): R1 +0.036, R2 +0.030, R3 −0.166, R3b −0.002, R1w +0.090, R2w +0.073, and the evening peak +0.312 (H minus G). The signs agree with the quantile-score contrast except for R3b (+0.000 against −0.002) and two replicate-year contrasts: the winter evening peak (−0.021 against +0.087) and N minus G (−0.004 against +0.003).
  • Audit triggers (the seven in the ml-experiment skill). Fired: 2 (the H-perm placebo matches H on real slope widths, 1.03 and 1.04 times, while the smooth cell shows a narrowing, which the placebo itself explains; the coverage, unlike-cell, scale-width, and N-minus-G predictions also failed, and only the capacity failure has a diagnosis), 3 (the signs above), 4 (dropping D11 takes R1 from +0.020 to +0.0005 and R2 from +0.013 to −0.0006, so one substation carries most of R1; dropping D10 puts R1's interval (+0.009 to +0.078) and R2's (+0.002 to +0.041) wholly above zero; dropping the D10–D11 interconnection turns R2's reading from undecided to non-inferior; no other substation, interconnection, or night-time substation changes a reading), and 5 (NH is worse than both N and H in both years, 2.954 against 2.941 and 2.903 in the scored year, and the holiday weight is at its grid's top). Not fired: 1 (the five controls pass and the planted failure is detected; the 10-fleet power check had standard errors over 4 points, which the plan reads at the pooled size, see Disclosures), 6 (R1 and R2 half-widths are 0.5 to 1.6 times experiment 109's C1 half-width of 0.022), and 7 (a negative result: no later design builds on it). No Opus audit was run: the design session ruled, through the experiment manager, that a negative result merges on the Sonnet reviews alone.

docs.title: Disclosures
docs.text:
• Controls at the scored cut. The plumbing controls P1 to P4 (parameter comparisons between arms only) and P5 (re-scoring experiment 109's published scored-year N) ran fits at the 2025-07-01 cut before the module review, and the manager accepted them as plumbing controls. No H, NH, or P-hol score at the replicate or scored cut was computed or seen until the real-data stage, which ran after tuning and beside the gate with the manager's approval. P5 reproduces experiment 109's N score exactly (2.929030 against 2.929030 on 104,033 rows), using 109's pool of seven series.
  • Code under test. The module is studies.dp_gam_graph (pull request 1411, merge commit dbbfd2e84). The tuning set, the 10-fleet power check, and the real-data fits of G, N, H, NH, P-hol, the next-gamma arms, and the rewired graphs ran on its CPU path at commit 67deaa053. The main gate, the correlated-noise cells, the heating-only and holiday-only real fits, and the tail passes ran at commit c008d9f4b or the merge commit, which add a GPU path and tests; the CPU and GPU solves agree to 4e-10, and the Cholesky solver equals the LU solver to 1e-7 on a 15-node fleet (a module test). One arm of a 15-node fleet (41 fits) took 12 seconds on the GPU and about 118 seconds on 6 CPU threads at a machine load of 27.
  • Deviations from the plan. The winter evening-peak and cold-snap contrasts use 95% intervals, and the stored predictions hold one seed because a frozen fit has no random element (the plan said three seeds). Clarifications made before any fit, after seeing the module or the power check, are in the branch's planning commits: a relative identification rule for profile and holiday columns, centring over the coordinates both ends identify, the per-edge meaning of the weight, dark rows as CAMS irradiance below 1 W/m², the node set of N, NH, and P-hol, the winter breakdown, and the reading of the power-check sizing rule at the pooled size.
  • Compute. Each of the 41 fits of an arm on a 15-node fleet took about 3 seconds on 6 CPU threads, so the gate would have taken about 33 hours on the CPU; a warm-started Cholesky solver and a GPU path took it to about 9 hours.
  • Not done. No onboarding or short-history arm and no 0.97 power-factor sensitivity. The clock-change days are excluded from every score, and the fits train on them as before.

The panels show each decision substation's parameters with 80% month-block intervals for G, N, H, and NH, and example weeks of G and NH. The four example weeks start on 21 July 2025 (summer), 13 October 2025 (autumn), 19 January 2026 (winter), and 13 April 2026 (spring).
