docs.title: Appendix: the plan as committed before the fits, with its clarifications
The question, and what earlier experiments already say
docs.text:
B0's single hinge already makes the heating response non-negative and convex, so MH asks only whether more bends help. B0 has 16 heating columns: one relu(15.5 - T) hinge for each of 4 smoothings of ERA5 temperature in each of 4 hour bands, with non-negative slopes. Five hinges per column let the slope per degree grow in steps as it gets colder (zero above 18 C, and growing at each of 18, 16, 14, 12, and 10 C). This is a free, monotone, convex temperature curve of the kind the literature fits, in place of one fixed threshold.

Experiment 114 gives two reasons to expect a small gain and one to expect none.

  • Its loss profile over a single hinge preferred a threshold at or below 12 to 14 C at 4 of 5 substations, yet the per-site threshold lowered the filtered score by only −0.012 points (97.5% interval −0.030 to +0.007). One hinge cannot represent a flat region and a steep region together.
  • Splitting each hinge by half-band gained −0.039 (−0.070 to −0.014). MH tests a different missing piece, the shape across temperature, and is not expected to gain as much.
  • Against: experiment 113 found a band heating slope weak at real noise (80% interval about 38% of the slope wide). Five hinges split each slope five ways on the same mild-weather days.

Every contrast is a past-weather ceiling (ERA5 temperature of the target half-hour); only the ENS confirmation in "Handed on" tests transfer.

docs.title: Base model, years, sites, and rows
docs.text:
All as in briefs/dp_n3n4.md, so that experiment 114's stored predictions remain comparable.

  • B0 and B0-K: dp_gam with drift="none", capacity="pinned" (studies.dp_pinned_capacity), ridge 0.1, TrainingWindow(months=24), lockdown out. B0-K adds dp_assimilation.run_kalman under the 3.5-hour cut with four filter hyperparameters per site, fitted on each arm's tuning-year residuals by fit_filter_hyperparameters with Part 4's prior.
  • Years: tuning 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30 (cut 2023-07-01), replicate 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30, scored 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. Screening tier: one frozen fit per arm and cut, no refits, one seed. Each cut's spread comes from the replica fit 12 months earlier (dp_gam.replica_residuals), so fits run at 2022-07-01, 2023-07-01, 2024-07-01, and 2025-07-01. Nothing scores a valid time on or after 2026-07-01.
  • Sites: D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16 decide (4 of 5 needed to improve); D9 descriptive in the scored year only. MVA sites, D15, and D18 are not fitted.
  • Masks, leads, predictions: as experiment 114 (hand-filtered switching list padded 24 hours, 09:00 UTC origins, day D+1, the same prediction columns).

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Each arm is B0 with its 16 heating columns replaced, solved by dp_gam.solve_bounded_quadratic on per-month Gram matrices (the pattern of e00114_design.py, copied, not imported). Each arm runs unfiltered and filtered (suffix -K).

Arm Heating columns Role B0 one hinge at 15.5 C (16 columns) reference, refitted MH B0's 15.5 C hinge plus hinges at 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 C (96 columns), all slopes non-negative, B0's ridge 0.1 on every column decision arm; nests B0 (the five added blocks at zero) MH-5 the five hinges alone (80 columns) exploratory: the free curve with no fixed hinge MH-sh MH with the five added blocks' ridge multiplied by m in exploratory; m chosen on the filtered tuning-year score, and m to infinity is B0 114 refs T-all-K, T2-K, H-site-K re-read from experiment 114's stored predictions
  • The hinge is relu(theta - T_k) / HEATING_SCALE_C on the same four smoothed temperatures as e00114_design.hinge_block, called at five thresholds. The sign bounds make each slope a non-negative increment, so the curve cannot fall as it gets colder, and it stays convex.
  • Fair comparison: the decision arm MH is B0 plus extra non-negative columns at B0's own ridge, and nothing about MH is tuned, so B0 and MH are on the same footing (B0 has no tuned setting to match). dp_gam's ridge is not scaled by the row count, so on 35,000 rows it shrinks almost nothing (see briefs/dp_n3n4.md); the non-negative bounds are the main regulariser. MH-sh is the one place a penalty is tuned, with the grid starting at 10 because multiplier 1 is MH itself. It is exploratory because B0 cannot be tuned in the same way. The effective degrees of freedom of the added columns are printed for MH and for each m. A difference penalty on adjacent hinge slopes was considered and left out to keep the plan small.
  • Why these positions: 12 and 14 C straddle the loss minima of experiment 114; 16 and 18 C cover the mild side; 10 C is the only cold-tail hinge. Positions are fixed before any fit.

docs.title: Night-step arms (NS)
docs.text:
Why: a read-only check of experiment 111's stored GAM-K predictions (one winter, November 2025 to February 2026, and one summer pair, July to August 2025 and May to June 2026, weekdays only) found an unmodelled step at 01:00 (the 00:30 to 01:00 half-hour) in winter. Actual demand steps up by 7.1, 10.7, and 7.4 points at D5, D10, and D16 (1.9 to 3.4 points at D11, D14, and D9), and GAM-K's residual step is 4.4, 7.3, and 5.4 points at D5, D10, and D16. In summer the step shrinks to 1.7 points or less, and its position (UTC or local clock) cannot be told apart. The check used one winter and one summer pair, so the summer reading is weak. Winter local time equals UTC, so winter rows cannot separate the two indexings; only British Summer Time (BST) rows can.

Four arms (NS-HW was added before any replicate or scored fit; see the clarifications), each B0 plus extra columns at B0's ridge 0.1, so each nests B0; each runs filtered (-K) and unfiltered.

Arm Extra columns Sign NS-L one level per half-hour of the 20 half-hours from 22:00 to 08:00 local time free NS-U the same, indexed on the UTC clock (22:00 to 08:00 UTC) free NS-H B0's 15.5 C hinge (4 smoothings) times an indicator for 00:00 to 07:00 UTC non-negative NS-HW the same hinge (4 smoothings) times each of the 20 UTC night half-hours (80 columns) non-negative

NS-H lets the step grow in cold weather, as storage heating does. NS-L and NS-U agree on every winter row, so the NS-L against NS-U contrast uses BST nights only. The 20 levels are free, with B0's ridge. Half-hour labels are start times (the 01:00 step is the half-hour 00:30 to 01:00). NS-H's window (00:00 to 07:00 UTC) is narrower than the 22:00 to 08:00 window of the other arms, so NS-H cannot see a step before midnight. NS-L is a null control, not a candidate (see the clarifications).

docs.title: Known-answer test and gate
docs.text:
Order: test 1, then tuning (the MH-sh multiplier and the filter hyperparameters, hashed with the 114 SHA into decisions.json), then the gate, all before any MH row of the replicate or scored year is fitted or read. The B0-K reproduction in test 1 reads stored B0 output only. A failed test 1 stops the scored reading. A failed gate does not stop it (the data cost is zero), but the verdict is then fixed so that the MH label is not powered and C1 is printed with no label. The gate can fail by design.

  1. Reproduction (blocking). MH with only the 15.5 C hinge reproduces dp_gam.fit_gam for B0 to 1e-8 relative in the parameters; MH with the five added blocks forced to zero reproduces B0's fitted values to 1e-5 points; B0-K's filter on stored B0 residuals reproduces run_kalman called directly; B0-K reproduces experiment 114's stored B0-K scored-year score to 1e-4; no training row after its cut.
  2. MH power check (synthetic, run through the filter, can fail). The truth is B0's real fit at the 2024-07-01 cut with its heating block replaced by a five-hinge curve: B0's slopes spread across the hinges, the cold-end share scaled by a common amplitude per draw.
    • Noise: experiment 113's real-noise rule (e00114_noise.py, copied), whole donor months from the other decision sites' B0 residuals. Donor residuals are in-sample, so they are inflated by the ratio of B0's out-of-sample to in-sample RMSE on the tuning year, per site. Only covariates (temperature, calendar) of the 2024-25 year enter the held-out synthetic year, and no 2024-25 residual does. Power is still an upper bound.
    • Sizing, as a formula: oracle gain = score of B0-K (fitted to the draw) minus score of the true-parameter forecast with B0-K's filter, on the held-out synthetic year, minus the same difference under a single-hinge truth at 15.5 C. The amplitude is set on 5 pilot draws so that the oracle gain is 0.03 points after the filter, the decision margin. The unfiltered oracle gain is printed beside it.
    • Pass if (a) the paired mean of MH-K minus B0-K over the 100 draws (20 per site, B0-K's filter hyperparameters) is at most −0.015, half the oracle gain, with its 80% interval over draws wholly below zero; and (b) on a single-hinge truth at 15.5 C, the paired mean of MH-K minus B0-K over 100 draws is no worse than +0.01. Per-site counts and the share of the oracle gain recovered are descriptive.
    • Failure: not powered; see "Decision rule".

  3. Pooled-curve coverage (descriptive, in the same draws). The 80% month-block bootstrap interval (I1 of experiment 113: calendar quarters kept, widened by sqrt(m/(m-1))) for one pooled summary: the fitted heating response at 5 C divided by the response at 12 C, summed over the four bands and four smoothings. Coverage of the truth over the 100 draws is printed. If coverage lies outside 70 to 90%, no curve summary appears on the page. A pass says the interval is calibrated on synthetic data only, not on real data. The summary is also dropped if any decision site has fewer than 500 half-hours below 5 C in any fit window (the counts below 5 C and below 10 C are printed per site and cut). It carries no label.

  4. Night-step indexing gate (synthetic, unfiltered, can fail). Same generator and noise as step

  5. The truth is B0's real fit plus an injected 4-point step at 01:00 UTC, indexed in UTC in one set of 100 draws and in local time in another (the two differ only in BST rows). Pass if (a) on each truth, the matching arm beats the other indexing on BST nights in at least 80% of draws, (b) on winter nights both arms beat B0 on both truths in at least 90% of draws, and (c) on each truth the mismatched arm does not recover the injected level on BST nights (its fitted level at the injected half-hour is under half the injection). Failure: indexing not identified; the NS-U against NS-L contrast is printed unlabelled.

docs.title: Clarifications made after the tuning-year work and before any replicate or scored fit
docs.text:
These changes follow the first tuning-year run (cuts 2022-07-01 and 2023-07-01 only). No replicate-year or scored-year fit had been run, and no score of those years had been read. They are agreed with the experiment manager.

  • NS-L is redundant by construction. B0's free profile has one level per day type and local half-hour of day, so a free level per local half-hour adds nothing: its added effective degrees of freedom are 0.0 at every decision site, and its fitted values equal B0's. NS-L is kept as the labelled control that shows this. NS-U differs from the profile only in British Summer Time rows, so it tests UTC-fixed timers, not a winter step.
  • NS-HW is added as a full arm (N4), judged on winter nights like N1 to N3. It is B0 plus the 15.5 C heating hinge of each of the four smoothed temperatures times each of the 20 UTC night half-hours (80 columns, non-negative slopes, B0's ridge). It models a step that grows with cold, which is how storage heating (Economy 7) behaves. It was added after the tuning-year run showed NS-L and NS-U cannot represent a winter-only step. The night family is now four contrasts, so the Bonferroni level is 99.375%.
  • The MH-sh multiplier grid is extended to {10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000}. The first tuning run chose 1000, the edge of the grid {10, 100, 1000}. The extension is made on the tuning year alone.
  • Gate 4 is run as written, and its result is recorded as it stands. Winter local time equals UTC, and a winter step is already free in B0's profile, so criterion (b) (both NS-L and NS-U beat B0 on winter nights) fails by construction. A failure of gate 4 as written does not cap any other label.
  • Gate 4' replaces gate 4 as the gate for the indexing contrast and for N4. On the same generator and noise as gate 4: (a) with a flat 4-point step injected at 01:00 UTC, NS-U beats B0 on British Summer Time nights in at least 80% of draws; with the step injected at 01:00 local time, B0 beats NS-U on those nights in at least 80% of draws (B0's profile already holds a local step). (b) with a step that grows with cold injected on winter nights (4 points on average over the winter nights, proportional to the 15.5 C hinge of the first smoothed temperature), NS-HW beats B0 on winter nights in at least 90% of draws, and the mean of NS-HW minus B0 is wholly below zero. A failure of 4'(a) makes the indexing contrast unlabelled (indexing not identified); a failure of 4'(b) makes the N4 label not powered. NS-L is not part of 4'.
  • Winter breakdown and cold snaps (maintainer priority). Every contrast is also reported on November to March rows, on a cold-snap subset, and on evening peaks within them, with paired intervals against BG2 and lagless XGBoost where their stored predictions cover the same rows. A cold snap is the days of the scored winter whose daily mean ERA5 temperature at the site's cell is in the coldest 10% of days of that winter; the rule and the day count are stated, and "too few days" is reported where fewer than 5 days qualify. A winter loss alongside an annual gain is stated in the verdict as a reason to hold the arm back. The page states how many independent winters the evidence holds. The substation cards gain a cold-snap panel and the fitted night step (as a score change, not a level).
  • The night step was found on scored-year rows, so the replicate winter confirms it. The step was read from experiment 111's stored GAM-K residuals for November 2025 to February 2026 and for two summer pairs, all in the scored year. The choice of the 01:00 half-hour, of D5, D10, and D16 as the large cases, and of the "3 of 5 sites" rule came from scored rows, so the scored winter is not a clean test for the night arms. A night label of gain therefore also needs the replicate winter (2024-25) winter-night estimate to be below zero with a 95% interval wholly below zero, or at most half the scored estimate. Without it the label is not replicated. The evidence is two winters (replicate and scored), plus the tuning winter (2023-24) for descriptive checks.
  • Which gate covers which label. A label whose gate fails is not powered, and the verdict treats not powered as not gain. Gate 2 covers C1 (the MH label). Gate 4'(a) covers N2 (NS-U-K) and the indexing contrast. Gate 4'(b) covers N4 (NS-HW-K), and the same test run for NS-H on the cold truth (NS-H-K beats B0 on winter nights in at least 90% of draws) covers N3. N1 (NS-L-K) is a null control with no label: its fitted values must equal B0's, so any gain is a bug and audit trigger 5 fires. Gate 4 as written covers nothing. Gate 4' was written after gate 4 had failed by construction; the first-run results of both are kept in the write-up. The NS label is the best label among N2, N3, and N4.
  • Gate 4' as first written is kept, and gate 4'' replaces it (redefined after seeing gate 4' fail, before any replicate-year or scored-year fit; agreed with the experiment manager). Gate 4' as first written failed: NS-U beat B0 on British Summer Time (BST) nights in 74% of draws (80% needed), B0 beat NS-U on a local-time step in 60%, and NS-HW beat B0 on winter nights with a cold-dependent step in 72% (90% needed); the descriptive 01:00 version gave 77%, 45%, and 80%. Those thresholds were set without a statement of the effect size or of a power target. Gate 4'' derives its thresholds from both, and they are fixed here before the gate runs. If gate 4'' fails, the labels it covers stay not powered, the verdict stays inconclusive, and the gate is not redefined again.
    • Injected steps. A step of 4 points and a step of 7 points of effective capacity (the sizes seen at D5, D10, and D16; the units bullet below converts to MW) in the half-hour starting 00:30. The night-row noise has a standard deviation of 4.6 to 7.7 points at D5 and D10, so 4 points is about one noise standard deviation. Three kinds: a flat step on the UTC clock all year (utc), a flat step on the local clock all year (local), and a cold-dependent step on the UTC clock (cold, equal to a constant times the 15.5 C hinge of the first smoothed temperature, scaled so the mean over the winter rows of that half-hour equals the stated size). A placebo has no step.
    • Units. The quantile score and every step are in points, that is, percent of the substation's effective capacity, and not in MW. A step of p points is p times the effective capacity divided by 100 in MW. The effective capacity is a single table value per substation (5.72 MW at D5, 5.40 MW at D10, 10.78 MW at D11, 11.71 MW at D14, and 9.12 MW at D16), so the MW conversion of a step carries the interval of the step in points and no additional interval. A 4-point step is 0.23, 0.22, 0.43, 0.47, and 0.36 MW at D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, and a 7-point step is 0.40, 0.38, 0.75, 0.82, and 0.64 MW. The measured residual steps of 4.4, 7.3, and 5.4 points at D5, D10, and D16 are 0.25, 0.39, and 0.49 MW.
    • Statistic. For an arm, the mean quantile score minus B0's on the label's own rows (BST nights for NS-U, winter nights for NS-H and NS-HW), unfiltered, on the same noise.
    • Critical value. The 5th percentile of the statistic over 100 placebo draws (20 per substation, draws 0 to 19). An arm detects a step in a draw when its statistic is below the critical value, so the false-positive rate on the placebo is 5% by construction. It is checked on 100 further placebo draws (draws 100 to 119), where at most 8% may detect (the target is 5%; 100 draws carry a Monte Carlo error of about 2 points).
    • Pass. (a) NS-U detects the 4-point utc step in at least 80% of draws, and detects the 4-point local step in at most 10% of draws (so the clock is identified); (b) NS-HW detects the 4-point cold step in at least 80% of draws; (c) NS-H detects the 4-point cold step in at least 80% of draws. (a) covers N2 and the indexing contrast, (b) covers N4, and (c) covers N3.
    • Descriptive. The same statistics for 7 points, and on the rows of the injected half-hour only, per substation. These cannot rescue a label.
  • Scoring rows and wording of gate 4'. "Beats" means a lower mean quantile score (unfiltered, as in gate 4) over the stated rows, and a tie is not a beat. Gate 4'(a) scores all 22:00-to-08:00 British Summer Time (BST) night rows. Gate 4'(b) scores all winter-night rows. The cold step in gate 4' is a step in the half-hour starting 00:30 UTC whose mean over the winter rows of that half-hour is 4 points. Because a step in one of 20 night half-hours is diluted in these scores, the descriptive 01:00 gate repeats 4' on the rows of the injected half-hour only. It is labelled descriptive and cannot rescue a label.
  • Non-inferiority bound against noise. The +0.02 bound is smaller than the sister contrast's half-width (about 0.023 at 97.5%). Night terms change few rows, so the contrast on all other rows should be much tighter than that reference, and the report prints its width. A pass shows only that the upper bound is under +0.02. It does not show equivalence. The winter-night subset has fewer rows than the sister contrast, so its interval is wider, and the 0.05 margin is judged against the printed width.
  • One winter definition for labels. Labels use winter nights (November to February, 22:00 to 08:00 local). The breakdown tables also show November to March, and "summer" in the winter-against-summer contrast means June to August. A winter loss beside an annual gain is stated in the verdict as a reason to hold the arm back from production; it does not change the label. Intervals against BG2 and lagless XGBoost are 95% and exploratory, with no multiplicity correction. The "daily mean" in the cold-night rules is the local calendar day.
  • The indexing label ignores the cold-night count. The indexing contrast pools the BST nights of all five substations. The cold-BST-night count and "cannot tell" are reported per substation and do not change the pooled label.
  • If the MH-sh pick is again at the grid edge (100000, nearly B0), the page reports "at the edge" and MH-sh stays exploratory.
  • NS-UT, an evolving UTC night step, is added as an exploratory arm (maintainer steer, before any replicate or scored fit). The size of the Economy 7 effect may change from winter to winter at each substation (experiment 121's tuning year does not show this; the E7 step-by-winter table of PR 1416 suggests it). NS-UT is B0 plus one non-negative level per month of the 24-month training window (25 monthly knots, linear between them) times an indicator for the UTC half-hours starting 00:30 to 07:00, a second-difference penalty of weight 1000 between neighbouring knots (fixed here, not tuned) on top of B0's ridge, and the last knot's level held through the forecast year. It is judged against the fixed-step NS-U on winter nights (a 95% exploratory contrast, NS-UT-K minus NS-U-K), carries no label and no gate, and is outside the Bonferroni family. The cards show its fitted step by winter (mean of the monthly levels from November to February), in points and MW. The UTC-against-local split by year is read descriptively from the NS-U-K minus NS-L-K contrast on British Summer Time nights in the replicate and scored years, with "cannot tell" where a year has fewer than 10 cold British Summer Time nights.
  • Does the forecast show the 01:00 step on cold winter nights? (maintainer steer; an operator who sees the step in demand and none in the forecast will distrust the rest.) A cold winter night is a night from 22:00 to 08:00 local time in November to February whose local calendar day has a daily mean ERA5 temperature below 8 C at the substation's cell, a rule fixed here before any score is read; the report prints the number of such nights per substation and year. The descriptive readout, per decision substation, in the scored and replicate years, for B0-K and each night arm: the median over cold winter weekday nights of the forecast step (median forecast of the half-hour starting 00:30 minus the median forecast of the half-hour starting 00:00) against the actual step (the same difference in observed power), in points with the MW conversion once (the units bullet above), with a 95% interval from resampling whole days. The figure for the cards shows the median over cold winter nights of the forecast median and 80% band, and of the observed power, from 22:00 to 08:00, B0-K against the best night arm, at every decision substation. A one-line list names any other miss visible on those nights (for example the timing of the morning rise). This readout is descriptive and does not change a label, but a visible miss on cold winter nights counts against release even when the mean score is unchanged, and the verdict says so.
  • The night step on the substation cards (maintainer request; Economy 7 may be reported to NGED). For each decision substation (D-labels), the card shows the fitted night step from the best night arm: its size in points of effective capacity and in MW, its start time, whether it follows local time or UTC (from the NS-U against NS-L comparison, with an interval), and the winter-against-summer contrast with an interval. This replaces the plan's rule that night levels appear as score changes only. Sizes are in points and in MW because the substations are not generators. A generator-linked series, if any, appears only under a G-label with normalised units and no dates. The result states the hand-built arms' winter-night scores plainly, so that the learned daily-shape library of experiment 120 can be compared with them.
  • Cold nights in British Summer Time (maintainer request, before any replicate or scored fit). Most Economy 7 load is storage heating, so the night step should grow with cold and a small step is expected in summer. UTC and local time differ only between the clock changes, so a clean test of the clock needs nights that are both cold and in British Summer Time. The page reports, for each decision substation and for the replicate and scored years, the number of such nights. A night counts as cold when the daily mean ERA5 temperature at the substation's cell is below 8 C (the threshold of the cold-tail bin in the plan), fixed here before any score is read. Where a substation has fewer than 10 cold British Summer Time nights in a year, the UTC-against-local contrast for that substation is written "cannot tell". The fitted night step on the cards is shown as a slope per degree below the 15.5 C hinge and a size on a stated cold night (daily mean temperature 3 C), both in points and in MW with intervals from the month-block bootstrap, beside a separate small base level (the free night levels of NS-U), not a single fixed size.
  • A winner is carried as a standard GAM-K piece in the recommendation (subject to the ENS confirmation in "Handed on").

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text:
One planned contrast: 97.5% interval from studies.bootstrap, resampling whole calendar months of stored predictions, paired across arms, at day D+1, after the filter. Reported with the count of sites moving each way, every arm's absolute score, the mean-forecast error contrast, the replicate year's estimate and count, November to March against April to October, the four hour bands, and leaving one site out.

  • C1: MH-K minus B0-K (decision, if the gate passes). Beside it: MH minus B0 (unfiltered).
  • N1, N2, N3, N4 (night family): NS-L-K, NS-U-K, NS-H-K, and NS-HW-K each minus B0-K, on winter nights as the primary score (November to February, valid times 22:00 to 08:00 local), at 99.375% (Bonferroni over four). Non-inferiority on all other rows: the contrast on every row outside winter nights must have its 99.375% upper bound at most +0.02 points. The annual average is reported and is not decisive. Calendar-type terms act on a few hours of the year, so the annual mean dilutes them. Each arm has its own filter hyperparameters, with the control below.
  • Indexing contrast: NS-U-K minus NS-L-K on BST nights (April to October), 95%, labelled UTC if wholly below zero (consistent with GMT-set timers), local if wholly above, unresolved otherwise, only if gate 4'(a) passes. The summer step is 1.7 points or less, so unresolved is the likely outcome.
  • Filter-fit control: MH-K and each night arm run with B0-K's stored filter hyperparameters (MH-K-b0 and so on). If C1's label differs between MH-K and MH-K-b0, or the estimate moves by more than its half-width, C1 is inconclusive: the gain sits in the filter fit, not the curve.
  • Row alignment: contrasts against 114's arms use an inner join on (time_series_id, valid_time, lead_hours), row counts printed, 114's masks unchanged.
  • Exploratory (95%): MH-5-K minus B0-K, MH-sh-K minus B0-K, MH-K minus H-site-K, and MH-K minus T-all-K (descriptive: T-all-K is expected to beat MH-K).

Margin and noise reference. MH adds 80 columns to the same bounded solver, so porting a gain into GAM-K costs almost nothing. The 0.03 margin is therefore not a porting-cost threshold; it justifies an ENS confirmation run, which needs its own plan. The sister contrast is Part 4's C4 (A2 minus A3, scored year, D+1): −0.015 (−0.053 to +0.003) at 99.17%, about ±0.023 at 97.5%. Experiment 114's C1 and C2 half-widths were 0.028 and 0.018. A contrast that reaches 0.03 with an interval wholly below zero cannot be noise at the reference level, and a gain below 0.015 is inside what the reference noise alone could produce.

Tails, every arm: coverage and pinball at q01, q05, q95, and q99 beside the headline; a gain that moves q95 or q99 coverage more than 1 point from nominal is flagged (no label change). No curtailment cost: these are demand Primaries.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
Written before any fit; each line can fail, and none overrides the decision rule.

  • C1: MH-K minus B0-K between −0.03 and +0.01 in both years, and small gain or tie as a label. A weak gain is the optimistic case. More than 0.02 of any gain sits in November to March and the cold tail (daily mean temperature below 8 C), where the 10 C hinge carries weight.
  • MH-K versus H-site-K (−0.012): within ±0.02; versus T-all-K (−0.039): worse by at least 0.02. MH-5-K within 0.01 of MH-K.
  • Unfiltered MH minus B0: more than 1.5 times the filtered gain in magnitude, because the filter absorbs a level error from missed curvature.
  • Gate 2: (a) passes narrowly, recovering 50 to 70% of the oracle gain; (b) passes with a paired mean between 0 and +0.01 (per-site misses of 0.005 to 0.01 at up to 3 sites do not fail it). The chance of not powered is judged at about one in three.
  • N2 to N4: winter-night gain of −0.10 to −0.30 points at D5, D10, and D16 and under 0.03 at D11, D14, and D9 for the arm that fits the step; non-inferiority holds. N1 (NS-L-K) ties B0-K to 1e-5 points. NS-U-K and NS-L-K are within 0.01 on winter nights. The indexing label is indexing not identified if gate 4'(a) fails, and otherwise unresolved. The tuning year already shows NS-U-K 0.043 points better than B0-K after the filter, which is not predicted to carry over to winter nights.
  • Pooled-curve coverage under 70%, so no curve summary is drawn. B0-K within 0.01 of its experiment 114 value (2.255); the run under 1 hour.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
• Label for C1 (gate passed and MH-K-b0 agrees): gain if the estimate is at most −0.03 points, the 97.5% interval lies wholly below zero, the replicate year's estimate is below zero, and at least 4 of 5 sites improve in the scored year. small gain if the interval lies wholly below zero, the estimate is between −0.03 and zero, and the replicate year's estimate is below zero. not replicated if the scored interval lies wholly below zero but the replicate sign (or, for gain, the site count) fails. worse if the interval lies wholly above zero; tie otherwise. The replicate condition is required because the MH-sh multiplier and the filter's hyperparameters are chosen on the tuning year. The replicate estimate is printed beside every scored estimate in the headline chart and tables.
  • Label for N2 to N4 (each gated as the clarifications say; N1 is a null control): gain if the winter-night estimate is at most −0.05 points, the 99.375% interval lies wholly below zero, the replicate year's winter-night estimate is below zero with its 95% interval wholly below zero or at most half the scored estimate, at least 3 of 5 sites improve (the step is large at three substations), and non-inferiority holds. small gain if the interval lies wholly below zero, the estimate is between −0.05 and zero, and the replicate is below zero. not replicated and worse (interval wholly above zero) as for C1; tie otherwise. Failure of non-inferiority gives worse on other rows and no gain. The NS label is the best label among N2 to N4. The indexing contrast is the only statement about which clock the step follows.
  • Gate failure or control disagreement (MH): label not powered (gate) or inconclusive (filter control); the scored C1 is still computed and printed with no label, and the MH label is not gain. Take-home then says whether the printed estimate reached the margin, as information only.
  • Verdict: supported if both the MH label and the NS label are gain; partly supported if one is (a not powered label never counts as gain); small gain if neither and one is small gain; refuted if none of those and a decision contrast is worse (this refutes only these five hinge positions with this ridge, or these night terms; the weakly identified fits could have overfitted, and the take-home says so); inconclusive otherwise, including not powered, not replicated, tie, and a blocking test that cannot be fixed. A failed MH gate leaves the MH label not powered, which counts as not passing.
  • Handed on: a gain becomes a candidate for GAM-K's base only after an ENS confirmation with Part 6's monthly refits, which needs its own plan and approval. A tie or not powered keeps the single 15.5 C hinge. A night-step gain also needs an ENS confirmation, since the step is in the observed demand and may be shaped by weather. Combining MH with T2 or the night terms, per-site positions, and a knot-count search are not in this plan.

docs.title: Audit before merge: the seven triggers
docs.text:
Run the ml-experiment skill's seven triggers on the results, and add the "Checks" bullets (median minus mean per site after the filter; mean-forecast error per contrast; which triggers fired). Trigger 7 fires on any gain, so an Opus audit is planned for that case.

  1. A control fails: test 1, gate 2(b), or B0-K missing 114's stored B0-K by more than 1e-4.
  2. Contradiction: C1 gains more than 0.10 points; the pooled-curve coverage lies within 70 to 90% although experiment 113 found slopes weak; B0-K misses 114's B0-K.
  3. Score and mean-forecast error disagree in sign for C1.
  4. Leaving one site out flips the sign of C1 or changes its label.
  5. A nested arm wins, or a null control moves: NS-L's unfiltered fitted values differ from B0's by more than 1e-5 points, or NS-L-K scores differently from B0-K by more than its own paired half-width; B0 beats MH on the tuning year by more than MH's paired half-width; the single-hinge reproduction moves the score at all; MH-K-b0 moves C1.
  6. Interval width: C1's 97.5% interval more than twice or under half the width of Part 4's C4 at the same level (about ±0.023).
  7. A later design depends on it: a gain would change GAM-K's base, on one year plus a replicate at the screening tier.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: D-labels only, with dates. D15, D18, and their sum are generator data, labelled G-c with day counts, never dates and never beside a D-label; none is fitted here. The page may name interconnected D-label pairs such as D5-D16, and no substation names and no other topology. Never print a generator's public name beside its series. No per-site curve interpretation from weakly identified fits: no per-site hinge slope, curve, or curve summary is printed; the only curve figure is the pooled summary of gate step 3, drawn only if its coverage lies within 70 to 90%. The night step is the exception, by the maintainer's request: per D-label substation the cards show the step's size in points and MW, slope per degree, start time, and base level with intervals, because a step that grows with cold is the quantity NGED asked about, and the per-site NS-H or NS-HW slopes are identified by the sharp 01:00 timing rather than by the weakly identified band slopes of experiment 113. A generator-linked series appears only under a G-label, normalised, without dates. The step's start time is the first half-hour whose fitted step exceeds a tenth of the largest half-hour step, and its end time is the last such half-hour. A card shows the step of the night arm with the lowest winter-night score even if no arm earned a label, and says so.

docs.title: Substation cards
docs.text:
Section label: "Provisional: fitted to past weather on a screening run". One card per decision substation (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16; D9 marked short-history), from MH-K and B0-K at the 2025-07-01 cut.

  • Sample weeks: one week per season of the scored year (the week starting on the second Monday of the season's middle month), plus the coldest week (the Monday-to-Sunday week with the lowest mean 24-hour-smoothed ERA5 half-hourly temperature at the site's cell), all fixed before any score is read. Each panel shows B0-K and MH-K with the median, 80% and 90% bands, and observed power. Generator-linked series appear only under G-c labels in normalised units with no dates; none is expected.
  • Safe fitted properties: daily profile by day type, holiday and Christmas effects, lighting, and the filter's level state, as on experiment 114's cards. B0's band slopes appear labelled "weak" with no interval, or not at all; there is no MH heating panel.
  • Cross-substation figure: per-site MH-K minus B0-K with the replicate beside it, and the pooled-curve summary only if its coverage gate allows.

docs.title: Run order, reuse, compute, and time
docs.text:
Reuse from experiment 114 (merge SHA pinned). Copy and edit; scripts import only their own folder, studies.*, and reviewed packages.

  • Code to copy: e00114_common.py, e00114_design.py (Gram builder and hinge_block; MH adds a multi_hinge_block calling it at five thresholds), e00114_noise.py, e00114_tune.py, e00114_pipeline.py, e00114_report.py, e00114_gate2.py (generator and amplitude pilot), and the card and chart layouts, with the interaction, threshold, and profile code deleted.
  • Stored fits to read, not refit: data/ml-experiments/00114-*/predictions/ for B0, B0-K, T2-K, T-all-K, and H-site-K, plus work/decisions.json and work/coefficients.pkl.
  • Order: copy scripts and run test 1; Gram matrices for MH and MH-5 (5 sites by 4 cuts, about 100 columns each, one pass over the rows); tuning (ridge multiplier and filter hyperparameters, hashed into decisions.json); the gate; fits, spreads, filters; scoring and write-up.
  • Compute: a solve of about 100 columns takes roughly 0.05 seconds. Real fits are about 250 solves plus seconds per filter. The gate is about 30,000 solves. Gram building about 5 minutes. About 40 minutes of wall clock on 6 cores, budgeted at 1.5 hours; no GPU. If over budget, cut the bootstrap weightings from 50 to 30, then drop MH-sh.

docs.title: What the write-up must contain (beyond the series brief's standing rules)
docs.text:
The take-home says whether a free monotone convex temperature curve beats the single 15.5 C hinge after the filter, by how much, how it compares with experiment 114's T-all-K and H-site-K, that every number is a past-weather ceiling, and that no per-site curve is shown.

  • Figures: the headline chart (C1 and the exploratory contrasts with intervals, site counts, the replicate, and the unfiltered contrast) first; absolute scores per site with experiment 114's arms and Part 4's references (WK 2.267, A2 2.275, lagless XGBoost with the filter 2.496, manual heuristic 3.488, climatology 4.068); C1 by month and hour band; C1 by temperature bin (below 8 C against the rest); gate 2's power; the tails table; the sample weeks.
  • Caveats: the scored year has served experiments 106, 111, and 114 and this one, and MH was chosen after seeing 114's scored-year contrasts on the same rows; the replicate year protects the label; past weather; one scored year, frozen fits; hindsight masks; in-family truths cannot show a wrong PV shape; hinge positions were fixed from 114's profile. Leaks (none reaches a scored row): the 2022-07-01 replica reads the 2023-08-07 capacity vintage, 13 months late; the 2023-07-01 cut has the 5-week vintage leak; D9's 2024-07-01 fit reads the 2025-04-14 vintage; the replicate-year filter spread is in sample for the filter hyperparameters.

docs.title: Open questions for the manager
docs.text:
1. Is an ENS confirmation of MH (together with T2) pre-approved if C1 is a gain, or does that wait for the manager's next re-plan?
  2. Should hinge positions be shifted for ENS, whose temperature calibration shifted by −1.15 to +2.05 K, or is ERA5 training followed by ENS inference acceptable for a screening run?
  3. The plan puts the chance of not powered at about one in three, which gives a fixed inconclusive verdict. Proceed to the scored reading in that case (as written, at zero data cost), or stop after the gate? Should a 0.10-point gate amplitude run beside the 0.03 one?
  4. The night family has its own margin (0.05 on winter nights) and non-inferiority bound (0.02); are those the right values?
  5. Does the manager want the shrinkage grid MH-sh {10, 100, 1000} promoted from exploratory to decision arm if the plain MH gate fails but MH-sh passes it?

Compute: about 40 minutes on 6 cores (budget 1.5 hours), no GPU; slot D or G.

docs.title: Differentiable physics: GAM-K against the plain GAM and lagless XGBoost over three winters
docs.text:
In all three winters, GAM-K forecast tomorrow's demand at Primary substations 1.8 to 3.1 points of capacity better than both comparison models, but the gain is largely a level correction and partly in-sample. GAM-K is a physics-based demand model, fitted once and frozen for a year, with a Kalman filter that corrects it from recent errors; experiment 111 chose it as the differentiable-physics series' candidate. The comparison models are the same model without the filter (the plain model) and lagless XGBoost, an XGBoost model given no recent power. A Primary substation steps the voltage down for the local distribution network. A point of effective capacity is 1% of a substation's capacity. We rescored the stored day-ahead forecasts of experiment 114 (the plain model and GAM-K) and experiment 109 (lagless XGBoost) for November to March of 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26, at five Primary substations. Nothing was refitted. Each mean absolute error is a mean over the winter's days, in points of effective capacity, and each interval comes from resampling blocks of 7 consecutive days.

Past-weather scoring ranks model structure and does not give production skill. The inputs are ERA5 temperature estimates and CAMS irradiance estimates of past weather, so no weather-forecast error enters. The gap under live weather forecasts is unknown.

Most of the gain is consistent with the filter removing a level error, and this experiment did not separate level from structure. The plain model and lagless XGBoost are each frozen for a year after their fit and carry a level error: both under-forecast by 2 to 7 points at most substations in 2024-25 and 2025-26, and both over-forecast by 11 to 12 points at D10 in 2023-24 (figure 3). GAM-K's filter corrects that error from recent residuals. Lagless XGBoost has no recent power as an input. A post hoc check at the audit supports this. Subtracting each plain model's own winter-mean signed error at each substation, in hindsight, leaves GAM-K ahead of the debiased plain GAM by 0.63 (0.41 to 0.86), 0.71 (0.38 to 1.08), and 0.35 (0.09 to 0.69) points in the three winters, and ahead of the debiased lagless XGBoost by 0.95 (0.66 to 1.21), 1.05 (0.64 to 1.49), and 0.95 (0.40 to 1.58) points. Against level-corrected plain models, 5 of the 6 contrasts would miss the 1-point bar, so the gain over a model that sees recent power is smaller than the planned contrasts show.

The verdict is supported. All six planned contrasts meet the bar (estimate at most −1.0 points, 95% interval wholly below zero). There are three independent winters: separate weather samples, whose fits share part of their 24-month training window. No winter is clean on every count. 2023-24 is the year on which the filter settings were fitted. The ridge penalty was tuned on a year that contains 2024-25. 2025-26 was read in an earlier analysis before this plan, and only 2023-24 was a new test in that sense. The three winters are therefore less independent than the count suggests.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows all six planned contrasts well past the 1-point bar. The smallest estimate is −1.83 points (GAM-K against the plain model in 2024-25, interval −2.47 to −1.28).

Figure 2 shows GAM-K's error at 3.7 to 4.2 points in every winter, against 6.0 to 6.8 for the plain models. The plain model and lagless XGBoost are within 0.3 points of each other in each winter.

Figure 3 shows that the plain models are biased and that the filter removes the bias, which is consistent with level tracking being the source of the gain. The bias is the mean signed error over the winter, by substation.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Mean absolute error of the median forecast, all November to March days, points of capacity (report.txt has every table):

Winter GAM GAM-K Lagless XGBoost GAM-K minus GAM GAM-K minus lagless XGBoost 2023-24 6.79 3.73 6.83 −3.06 (−3.54 to −2.52) −3.10 (−3.57 to −2.63) 2024-25 5.97 4.14 6.14 −1.83 (−2.47 to −1.28) −2.00 (−2.60 to −1.46) 2025-26 6.09 4.19 6.36 −1.90 (−2.49 to −1.36) −2.17 (−2.99 to −1.45)

Exploratory: cold-snap days. The coldest 10% of each winter's days (15 days in each winter) by daily mean temperature. GAM-K minus the plain model is −3.33 (−3.99 to −2.65), −3.48 (−5.52 to −1.65), and −2.11 (−3.92 to −0.66) in the three winters. GAM-K minus lagless XGBoost is −3.47 (−4.16 to −2.30), −3.26 (−4.53 to −1.33), and −0.99 (−3.03 to +0.29): the 2025-26 interval crosses zero. Cold-snap days come in a few spells, so these intervals rest on a few blocks and are rough.

Exploratory: evening peaks (16:00 to 20:00). GAM-K minus the plain model is −3.33, −2.09, and −2.13 points, and GAM-K minus lagless XGBoost −3.47, −2.17, and −2.45 points. Every 95% interval lies wholly below zero (report.txt).

Post hoc: a sixth Primary. Adding D9 to 2025-26 gives −1.64 (−2.12 to −1.20) against the plain model and −1.82 (−2.48 to −1.23) against lagless XGBoost. D9 is in the 2025-26 winter only, because its history is too short at the earlier cuts.

Interval choice. Consecutive days share weather, so a day-level resample would be too narrow, and a month-level resample leaves 5 blocks in a winter. A 7-day block was chosen to span a typical weather spell. A 14-day block gives the same estimates with wider intervals (for example −1.83 (−2.75 to −1.16) in 2024-25), and the verdict is unchanged. The intervals cover within-winter weather only, not the differences between substations or between years.

docs.title: Predictions against outcome
docs.text: The plan predicted GAM-K minus the plain model at −1.0 to −1.8 points, and minus lagless XGBoost at −1.0 to −2.0, in 2023-24. The outcome was −3.06 and −3.10, outside the predicted range. The level-shift explanation below is a post hoc reading, not a test. In 2023-24 the plain model over-forecast by 12.0 points at D10 and 6.6 at D11, and lagless XGBoost by 11.4 and 6.9 (figure 3), a level shift that a frozen fit misses and the filter corrects. Leaving D10 out, a post hoc check of how much of the gap D10 carries, gives −1.62 (−1.94 to −1.28) against the plain model and −1.85 (−2.21 to −1.48) against lagless XGBoost, inside the predicted ranges. That check shows the gap is concentrated at D10. It does not show that a level error is the mechanism, which only the debiasing check above addresses. The plan's other predictions held: the cold-snap interval crosses zero in one winter, and GAM-K is ahead on evening peaks in every winter.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: each stored set has a mean column that equals the median (q50) exactly, so mean-forecast contrasts are the median contrasts. As a separate stand-in, the median minus the mean of the 11 quantiles is between −0.5 and +0.8 points for every arm and winter (report.txt).
  • Quantile score beside the error contrast: the quantile-score contrasts agree in sign with the mean-absolute-error contrasts in all six cases, for example −2.17 (−2.53 to −1.77) in 2023-24 against the plain model.
  • Leave-one-substation-out: every contrast in every winter still meets the bar (smallest −1.55, 2025-26 against the plain model without D10).
  • Triggers fired: triggers 2 and 7, with the Opus audit of this pull request. Trigger 2 fired because the result lay outside the prediction and its explanation is supported only by post hoc checks. Trigger 7 fired because a release candidate may lean on this headline. Triggers 1, 3, 4, and 5 did not fire. Trigger 6 (interval width against a sister experiment) cannot be checked, because no sister experiment scored these rows.
  • Code review: one Sonnet review of the scoring script found no code change needed. It confirmed that each stored fit stops at its cut, and that every join, mask, and interval is as planned.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Settings chosen on the scored winters. GAM-K's filter settings (the four numbers that set the filter's level and noise, per substation) were fitted on the 2023-24 residuals in experiment 114, and experiment 109 chose its XGBoost variant on 2023-24. The convex model's ridge penalty was tuned on 2024-07 to 2025-06 and its 24-month window was chosen on 2023-24 (experiments 104 and 106). The tuning of the filter settings favours GAM-K in 2023-24. The ridge and the window favour both convex models over XGBoost in 2023-24 and 2024-25, and cancel in GAM-K minus the plain model.
  • Past weather. Every input is an ERA5 temperature estimate or a CAMS irradiance estimate of past weather.
  • Filter spread in sample in 2024-25. Experiment 114 records that the replicate year's filter spread is in sample for the filter's hyperparameters. GAM-K in 2024-25 is therefore partly in sample for the filter, and this does not cancel in GAM-K minus the plain model.
  • Capacity vintage at the 2023-07-01 cut. Experiment 114 records a 5-week leak of capacity vintage at that cut, which touches every arm's 2023-24 normalisation. The stored lagless XGBoost sets were also written at different code versions: the 2023-24 set from an uncommitted working tree, and the 2024-25 and 2025-26 sets from a clean commit. The two versions differ by the capacity-vintage fix and by changes to the spread.
  • Five substations. D9 is left out of the planned contrasts, because its history is too short at the 2023-07-01 and 2024-07-01 cuts.
  • Lagless XGBoost has no recent power as an input, unlike the lagged XGBoost models of experiment 111.
  • Quantile score uses stored quantiles, so the median-minus-quantile-mean check is a proxy.

Substation cards are not needed: the experiment fits nothing and has no new fitted properties.

docs.title: Plan, written before any result existed
docs.text:
Hypothesis. On past weather, GAM-K forecasts Primary demand one day ahead better than both the plain convex model and lagless XGBoost in each of the three winters, by at least 1 point of mean absolute error.

Decision rule. A contrast meets the bar if its estimate is at most −1.0 points and its 95% interval lies wholly below zero. The 1-point bar was set by the maintainer, and it reflects what the filter adds: GAM-K adds a pipeline step over the plain model and a different model family over XGBoost. One point is about a sixth of the plain models' winter error. Supported: all six contrasts meet the bar. Partly supported: 3 to 5 meet it and none is wholly above zero. Small gain: at most 2 meet it and all six intervals lie below zero. Refuted: any interval lies wholly above zero. Inconclusive: anything else. The rule uses 95% intervals without a multiplicity correction, because "supported" needs all six to pass.

Size. Simple. What gets stored: one private scoring table. Serving path: not touched. Degradation rule: not touched. More than one defensible design: no, because the arms, cuts, row set, and scoring follow experiments 107, 109, and 114. Code whose callers could not be named without searching: none. The plan is the first commit of the branch.

Cold-snap rule (fixed in the plan commit). In each winter, the coldest 10% of covered days by daily mean ERA5 2 m temperature over the five substations, at least 3 days.

Planned contrasts. GAM-K minus the plain model, and GAM-K minus lagless XGBoost, each in the three winters, on all winter days. Everything else is exploratory.

Row set. dp_mw_v1 at D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, rows outside the hand-filtered switching events, an inner join of the three arms, no valid time on or after 2026-07-01.

docs.title: Differentiable physics, E7: how large is the winter night step at Primary substations, a pattern like that of storage heating, and how does it grow with cold?
docs.text:
Status: results for winters 2021-22 to 2024-25 (the headline winters), with winter 2025-26 (the selection winter) read afterwards and reported in its own section. The selection winter is the winter in which D5, D10, and D16 were picked. It was read only after PR 1397 (experiment 114) merged. The plan, committed before any code ran, follows the results.

We examined 14 Primary substations, labelled D2 to D22 to keep them anonymous. Six of them (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) were set before any fit as the substations the conclusion rests on; we call them the decision substations. D5, D10, and D16 are the three where earlier experiments first saw a step in winter 2025-26 demand. The other eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22) were added as a check; we call them E7-X.

We asked how much demand rises in the small hours of a winter night, the pattern that storage heaters (heaters that charge from cheap night-rate electricity, switched on by timers) would produce, and whether the rise grows with cold. On each winter night we took the mean demand over the five half-hours starting 00:30 to 02:30 and subtracted the mean over the four half-hours starting 22:00 to 23:30. We fitted that difference against how far the day's mean temperature (from the ERA5 reanalysis, a weather-agency estimate of past weather) fell below 15.5 C. We then subtracted the same difference measured on June to August nights, which we treat as the no-step baseline. We measure demand in points, where one point is 1% of that substation's 99th percentile of demand. On a night with a daily mean of 3 C, demand rises by 9.9 points averaged over the six decision substations (90% interval 6.2 to 13.5; the average weights each substation by how precisely its step is known, using Hartung-Knapp random-effects pooling). The eight E7-X substations, which were not chosen for showing a step, average 13.2 points (6.8 to 19.6), above the decision substations' 9.9.

Take-home message: demand at 13 of the 14 Primary substations steps up around 01:00 on winter nights, and the step is larger on colder nights. The step is not special to the three substations that prompted the study.

The eight E7-X substations have an average step as large as the six decision substations, so the analysis does not show that D5, D10, and D16 stand out (it does not rule that out, because the eight were not a random sample). The full step depends on the assumption that summer nights have no step. The part that grows with cold needs no such assumption, and that part is smaller: 1.1 to 4.7 points at the six decision substations (the slope times 12.5 degrees, the gap between 15.5 C and a 3 C night). The rise looks fixed to UTC on British Summer Time nights (a post hoc check). On cold winter nights the day-ahead forecast of experiment 114 runs below actual demand from about 01:00, at D5 and D16 on the two pre-registered winters and at D10 in winter 2024-25 alone. The verdict word is inconclusive. By the literal decision rule it would be supported, because every per-series gate row passes and both pooled intervals lie above 0. We keep inconclusive because the audit found the gate weaker than supported needs: its four gated shapes are one test, its pooled-interval row cannot fail, and its one misspecified cell under-covers (the gate paragraph below). The estimates above stand. The independent audit has run, and its findings are applied.

Summary, by question (winters 2021-22 to 2024-25 unless stated; every number is printed in report.txt):

  • How large is the night step at a daily mean of 3 C? Pooled over the six decision series, 9.9 points (Hartung-Knapp interval 6.2 to 13.5; resampling whole series 7.0 to 12.6). Per series, from 3.0 points at D14 to 15.4 at D10. D5, D10, and D16 (selected for showing the step) average 13.2 points; D9, D11, and D14 average 6.5.
  • Does the step grow with cold? Yes at all 14 series: every slope is positive and the 90% interval of every slope excludes 0. The slopes are 0.09 to 1.12 points per degree, and 0.25, 0.37, and 0.26 at D5, D10, and D16.
  • Is the step specific to the chosen substations? No. The eight further Primaries (E7-X) pool to 13.2 points, above the six decision series. One of the eight (D8) has no step (0.5 points, 90% interval -0.7 to 1.7).
  • Does the step have a fixed clock time? The step starts in the half-hour starting 00:30 (ending at 01:00) at all 14 series (at D4 the interval reaches one half-hour earlier). On cold British Summer Time nights the largest jump falls one hour later by the clock at 13 of 14 series, which fits timers set to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) (a post hoc check, chosen after seeing the data; D14 shows a shift of 4 half-hours).
  • How much of the step do experiment 114's day-ahead forecasts already remove? R, the step left in the errors of its baseline model divided by the full step, is 0.53 to 0.78 at D5, D10, and D16 (stored predictions for winters 2023-24 and 2024-25 only).
  • Where does the baseline forecast miss on cold nights? At D5 and D16 actual demand runs 5.6 and 9.4 points above the forecast in the half-hour starting 01:00 on the two pre-registered winters; at D10 it runs 12.2 points below the forecast in the half-hour starting 23:30, because in winter 2023-24 D10's cold nights sit about 11 points lower and the baseline is 9 to 17 points too high all night (figure 9).
  • What do the data and methods support? An estimate of the size and shape of the night step in four winters of one weather product. They do not support a cause: daylight, lighting, and switching schedules also change at night, and NGED has not confirmed storage heating.

Known-answer gate: the gate holds one real test of the interval, and that test under-covers. We added a known step to the real nights, resampled in 14-day blocks, and asked whether the 90% interval holds the true step. The four gated shapes (matched, ramp-plateau, flat, and placebo) are one test, not four: the estimator is linear, and all four injected shapes lie in its column space, so each moves the estimate by exactly its truth. Within every draw the point error is identical across the four cells, and their coverages differ only through the random numbers of the inner bootstrap. They show coverage of 87.0 to 87.5% pooled over series (target 85 to 95%) and 82 to 93% for each series (target 80 to 98%), and the mean estimate is within 0.20 points of the truth everywhere (target 0.5). That checks the bootstrap on resampled residual noise once. The Hartung-Knapp interval for the pooled mean covered the true mean in 100% of the 200 draws (target 85 to 95%), but that row cannot under-cover. The gate defines the true mean as the mean of a fixed set of steps (0, 0, 4, 4, 7, and 7), each series recovers its step within about 0.3 points, so the pooled estimate misses that mean by at most 0.52 points while the interval half-width is at least 2.13. The 100% therefore says nothing about whether the real pooled interval is conservative. The one misspecified cell is the night-temperature cell. If the true step follows the 18:00 to 08:00 mean temperature instead of the daily mean, coverage falls to 79% pooled at 7 points and to 43% at the worst series (descriptive, no target), so the daily-mean proxy matters. The gate also centres the summer nights on 0, so it cannot test the assumption that summer nights have no step. It tests only the shapes this plan chose, with noise that is independent between 14-day blocks.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The raw nights show the pattern before any fitting. On winter nights demand rises after midnight, where on summer nights it falls. At D10 the difference between the later and earlier half-hours averages -5.5 points in summer, and the raw mean on cold nights (daily mean at most 8 C) is 14.9 points above that summer value. That raw mean sits within 0.4 points of the fitted line at all 14 series (the plan allowed up to 2 points).

The step has the same sign in every winter at the six decision substations, and falls over the four winters at D10. At D10 it falls from 17.0 points in 2021-22 to 14.2 in 2024-25, and it also falls at two E7-X substations (D19 and D22). At D3 it falls and then levels (8.2, 6.8, 5.5, and 6.0 points), and at D2 it is level over the last two winters (13.7 in both). At D5, D11, and D16 the four winters stay within 3.4 points of each other, and at D14 the step is 1.3 to 4.2.

The eight substations chosen for nothing have the same average step as the three that prompted the study. The mean over D5, D10, and D16 is 13.2 points against 6.5 for D9, D11, and D14, but the eight E7-X substations also average 13.2. That does not rule out a selection effect, because the eight were not a random sample of Primary substations. The between-series standard deviation is 4.1 points for the six decision series (profile-likelihood interval 2.7 to 7.2) and 8.9 for E7-X (6.2 to 14.3). One series, D19, has a step of 33.5 points, which pulls the E7-X and all-series means up.

Experiment 114's day-ahead forecast errors still contain a large part of the step. R is the same regression run on the difference between actual demand and the median forecast of experiment 114's baseline model, divided by the full step over the same two winters. R is 0.78, 0.63, and 0.53 at D5, D10, and D16 (and 2.05 at D14, where the step in the errors exceeds the full step). With the model's recent-error filter R is 0.96, 0.74, and 0.59, and with the interaction model and the filter 0.52, 0.42, and 0.31.

On cold British Summer Time nights the jump arrives one hour later on the clock. The pre-registered rule (the sign of the difference between the local-clock and UTC-clock windows) printed UTC at all 14 series. For a pure step the rule does separate the two clocks: a step fixed to the local clock gives a positive difference (+0.25 of the step) and a step fixed to UTC a negative one (-0.4 of the step). The confound is the ordinary load shape, which makes the difference negative with no step at all, on summer nights (-0.2 to -6.0 points) and on mild British Summer Time nights. Against that summer placebo, cold British Summer Time nights are more negative at 13 of 14 series (D4 is level), which supports UTC. The post hoc check in the figure compares the half-hour of the largest mean rise on cold summer-time nights with the same half-hour on cold winter nights. The search runs from the transition into the half-hour starting 23:30 to the one starting 05:00, and finds a shift of 2 half-hours at 12 of 14 series (D14 shows 4; D9 shows 9, a jump at 05:00 on 18 nights). Inside 23:30 to 03:00, D9 also shifts by 2, which makes 13 of 14. The counts of cold summer-time nights in the cards and the figure are the same (18 at D9 and 68 to 90 at the others).

Demand rises within about one half-hour around 01:00. Demand then stays raised until the morning rise. The profile of cold-winter-night demand minus summer-night demand, relative to the 22:00 to 23:30 level, has the same shape at nearly all substations.

docs.title: Selection winter 2025-26 (first run)
docs.text:
Winter 2025-26 and experiment 114's scored-year residuals were read once, after PR 1397 had merged: decisions.json held the merge commit's SHA (503ce3a3de408d1f0c2bdbada5ba88032ff238bb) before the fit for this winter ran. This is a first run; figures 3 and 9 and the R and cold-night numbers that include winter 2025-26 are first-run numbers.

Winter 2025-26 gives a similar step to the headline winters at every substation except D12, and the three substations picked on that winter are about 2 points higher in it. The step fitted to winter 2025-26 alone has a 90% interval above 0 at all 14 substations (D8, which has no step in the headline winters, reaches 2.4 points, interval 0.5 to 4.0). Pooled over the six decision substations it is 10.8 points (Hartung-Knapp 6.3 to 15.4), against 9.9 (6.2 to 13.5) in the headline winters; over all five winters, 10.0 (6.2 to 13.9). The mean of D5, D10, and D16 is 15.2 points in winter 2025-26 against 13.2 in the headline winters, a rise of 1.1, 2.3, and 2.6 points at the three. D9, D11, and D14 average 6.5 in both. The E7-X substations average 13.8 (7.6 to 19.9) against 13.2, and D12 rose by 9.6 points. The three substations picked on winter 2025-26 are therefore higher in it by about 2 points, a modest selection effect on an estimate of 13 to 15 points.

  • Experiment 114's scored winter. With the scored-year residuals, the share of the full step left in the baseline model's errors over winters 2023-24 to 2025-26 is 0.76, 0.63, and 0.52 at D5, D10, and D16 (0.64 at D11 and 1.97 at D14).
  • Replicate-winter rule. The plan's rule that the step is positive in the replicate winter 2024-25 alone holds at all six decision substations (figure 3, which now includes 2025-26).
  • Cold nights. The cold-night figure above uses winters 2023-24 to 2025-26.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast: R and figure 9 use the median forecast of experiment 114's baseline model. On cold nights its median minus its mean is 0.0 at D5, D10, and D16. R and figure 9 include the hand-filtered switching half-hours; excluding them moves D5's miss at 01:00 from +6.1 to +6.8 points and moves the other substations by at most 0.1 points. The step fits themselves exclude those half-hours in the switching control only.
  • Hand-filtered switching list: refitting the six decision series without experiment 103's switching events changes no step by more than 0.3 points (11.0, 9.8, 15.4, 7.0, 3.0, and 13.5 for D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, against 10.8, 9.5, 15.4, 7.0, 3.0, and 13.4).
  • Block length: with blocks of 7, 14, and 28 days (100 draws), the coverage in the matched and placebo cells is 88%, 86%, and 84%, and the mean interval width 1.7, 1.9, and 2.1 points. The 28-day coverage is just below the 85% edge of the pooled band.
  • Audit triggers (conditions in the plan under which a result needs an independent audit). Trigger 1 (a control fails: test 1, the rank check, or the placebo coverage) fires: the gate's pooled-interval row, a known-answer test, gave 100% against 85 to 95%, and the tariff-edge placebo failed. Trigger 2 fires: the E7-X pooled step (13.2) is above the decision substations' (9.9), and 8 of the 10 predictions missed, some by 2 to 7 times. Two post hoc explanations are available. The predictions were anchored on experiment 121's residual steps, while the step here is the full step: dividing 121's 7.1 points at D10 by R = 0.63 gives about 11. And the flat part inherits the summer decline through the night (summer reference -0.7 to -13.4 points). Trigger 3 does not fire: no substation has a step and a raw contrast of opposite sign. Trigger 4 does not fire: leaving each decision substation out moves the pooled mean to between 8.8 and 11.2, inside 6.2 to 13.5. Trigger 5 does not fire: bounding the slope at 0 changes no slope. Trigger 6 does not fire: the widest decision-substation interval is 1.8 points (D9). Trigger 7 (a later design depends on the result) fires, because the cards and experiment 121's night arms use these numbers. The audit has run: every headline number reproduced, and its findings are applied on this page.

docs.title: Cold nights: actual demand against the baseline forecast
docs.text: On cold nights actual demand runs above the baseline forecast of experiment 114 from about 01:00 at D5 and D16 on the two pre-registered winters (by 5.6 and 9.4 points), and at D10 in winter 2024-25 alone (+7.6 at 01:00); at D10 the two-winter median is dominated by a level error in winter 2023-24. The figure shows the median and the 25th to 75th percentile, across the 104 cold winter nights per substation of winters 2023-24 to 2025-26 (the coldest 10% of days, the plan's cold-snap rule), of actual demand and of the day-ahead median forecast, in points. The largest median misses (actual minus forecast) are D5 +6.1 in the half-hour starting 01:00, D9 +2.9 starting 01:30, D10 +6.7 starting 01:00, D11 +3.6 starting 03:00, D14 +4.0 starting 02:00, and D16 +9.6 starting 01:00. The half-hour of the largest rise between 05:00 and 08:00 differs between actual and forecast at D5 (07:00 against 06:00), D9 (06:00 against 07:00), D11 (06:30 against 06:00), and D16 (07:00 against 06:30), and matches at D10 and D14. The two earlier winters alone (72 nights, before the selection winter was read) gave the same pattern at D5 and D16 (+5.6 and +9.4 at 01:00) but a different largest miss at D10 (-12.2 in the half-hour starting 23:30). The cause is winter 2023-24: D10's cold nights sit about 11 points lower than in the other winters (about 42 points against 52 to 54), and the baseline forecast is 9 to 17 points too high through the whole night. That level drop is not in the switching mask, and it also lowers D10's 2023-24 step. Winter 2024-25 alone shows +7.6 at 01:00 and +7.0 at 00:30, the same pattern as D5 and D16, and adding winter 2025-26 dilutes the 2023-24 error rather than creating the rise. report.txt prints both.

docs.title: Follow-up readouts (post hoc and exploratory)
docs.text:
These readouts come from an unverified summary of Economy 7 tariff practice, whose claims are hypotheses to test; nothing here cites it as a source. They were chosen after seeing the main results, so they are post hoc, and they read winters 2021-22 to 2024-25 only (cold British Summer Time nights up to October 2025), leaving the scored-year lock unchanged. The script is e00123_followups.py, and report.txt prints every number.

  • No substation shows a local-clock component on cold British Summer Time nights. For each cold night we found the half-hour entered by the largest rise between 23:30 and 03:00. On cold winter nights that half-hour is the one starting 00:30 on 66% to 100% of nights (11 of 14 substations are at 85% or more). On cold British Summer Time nights it falls at the local-clock step (starting 00:30) on at most 11% of nights (D22) and at the UTC step (starting 01:30, one hour later on the clock) on 24% to 100% of nights, with the remainder at other half-hours. D14 (24%) and D9 (50%) have the weakest UTC share, and their steps are the smallest or the least observed (3.0 points at D14, 18 cold British Summer Time nights at D9), so a mixture of clocks is not shown, and not ruled out.

  • The step ramps over about one half-hour and has no visible second window. Averaged over cold winter nights and minus the summer shape, demand reaches 7% to 56% of its plateau in the half-hour starting 00:00 and 81% to 119% in the half-hour starting 00:30. No substation has a second rise of at least 30% of the main one. The end of the window is not visible: the largest fall between 05:00 and 10:00 is small (0.5 points or less at seven substations) and falls at 07:30 at only four substations (D9, D10, D2, and D19), where the roughly 7-hour window would end if it began at 00:30. The morning demand rise overlaps the end of any window.

  • The step by winter falls at five substations, rises at one, and cannot be told at eight. The label compares the first and last winter's 90% intervals. It falls at D10, D2, D3, D19, and D22, rises at D11, and is cannot tell elsewhere, including D9, which has two winters. Only winter 2024-25 is the latest winter here, so the step by year cannot yet say anything about the 2025 and 2026 closures; that waits for winter 2025-26.

  • Descriptive only for now: fixed-window heat-pump and electric-vehicle tariffs that would add a night step on the local clock, and bespoke half-hourly contracts.

docs.title: UTC-fixed and local-clock shares by year (post hoc and exploratory)
docs.text:
The step could come from a tariff fixed to the local clock as well as from the legacy step fixed to UTC. The following start and end times are hypotheses from a search for equivalents, to be checked against Elexon's public tables, and are not sources: the legacy Economy 7 standard window 00:30 to 07:30 on Greenwich Mean Time, Intelligent Octopus Go 23:30 to 05:30, Octopus Go 00:30 to 05:30, and a Cosy heat-pump tariff. This page does not say which of them follow Greenwich Mean Time or local time.

For each cold British Summer Time night (daily mean below 8 C, March 2021 to October 2025) we found the half-hour entered by the largest rise between 23:30 and 03:00 on the local clock. The first percentage in each cell is the share of nights where it is the half-hour starting 01:30 local, where a step fixed to UTC at 00:30 would fall. The second is the share where it is the half-hour starting 23:30 or 00:30 local, where tariffs fixed to the local clock would fall. The number of nights is in brackets, and cannot tell marks a year with fewer than 10 nights. The 2025 column holds spring and summer nights only. The shares do not sum to 100% because the largest rise can fall elsewhere. e00123_clock_by_year.py prints the table, and the night profiles in figure 8 and figure 9 are indexed on the local clock, with UTC one hour earlier in British Summer Time.

The UTC share is 100% in every year with a reading at D2, D3, and D4, and 92% to 100% at D19, and a local-clock share above 10% appears only at D8 and D22 in 2023 (31% and 38%) and at D12 (15%) in 2024. docs.title: Tariff edges on the local clock (post hoc and exploratory)
docs.text:
Local-clock tariff edges are not visible at Primary level: the control failed, and no change since 2021 beyond the placebo limit appears at the Octopus Go edges outside D8. The tariff windows are unverified hypotheses from a search for equivalents, not sources: Intelligent Octopus Go 23:30 to 05:30, Octopus Go 00:30 to 05:30, and Cosy 04:00 to 07:00, 13:00 to 16:00, and 22:00 to 24:00 on winter weekdays. The script is e00123_tariffs.py; report.txt prints every number. Saving Sessions and demand-flexibility events are not modelled.

For each edge we took the rise in demand entering the half-hour starting at the edge, minus the median rise at the four half-hours either side, on British Summer Time nights (April to October, when the UTC-fixed Economy 7 step falls an hour later on the local clock) for the Octopus edges, and on winter weekdays for Cosy. Intervals resample 14-day blocks. Half-hours with no hypothesised edge (21:00, 03:30, 10:00, and 18:30) serve as placebos.

  • The level of the statistic is not a test. The ordinary daily load shape gives every half-hour a non-zero rise against its neighbours: the 90% interval excluded 0 in 76% to 79% of series-years at the placebo half-hours (5% expected), so a visible edge in one year means nothing. The median half-width of the intervals is 0.3 points.

  • Known-answer injection. Adding a step of S points (1, 2, and 4) to the edge statistic shifts the estimate and its interval by exactly S, so recovery is exact and the interval width is unchanged. The placebo is the control that failed; the injection says nothing about the load-shape confound.

  • The change between years cancels the load shape but the control still fails. Comparing the first and last year (2021 and 2025 for the Octopus edges; winters 2021-22 and 2024-25 for Cosy), the 90% interval of the change excluded 0 at 21% to 43% of placebo series (10% expected for either sign), because the load shape drifts between years by more than the sampling error. The empirical detection limit is therefore the 90th percentile of the placebo changes, 1.19 points (about 0.06 to 0.22 MW across the 14 substations).

  • Against that limit, the Octopus Go and Intelligent Octopus Go edges show a change at D8 only. At D8 the 23:30 edge changed by +2.5 points and the 05:30 edge by -2.3, in the expected signs. D8 has no Economy 7 step and large changes at the Cosy edges too (-12.4 points at 16:00), which points to a change in the substation's load, not to a tariff. The 00:30 Octopus Go opening, the edge the legacy step could be confused with in summer, shows no substation beyond the limit; the median change over the 14 substations is +0.6 points at 23:30, -0.06 at 00:30, and +0.03 at 05:30.

  • Cosy is not distinguished from other load changes. Beyond the limit, in the expected sign: the 07:00 closing at 4 substations (D11, D21, D22, and D8), the 16:00 closing at 5 (D10, D12, D16, D22, and D8), the 04:00 opening at 2 (D12 and D8), the 13:00 opening at 2 (D12 and D8), and the 22:00 opening at 3 (D19, D3, and D8). D8 and D12 appear at most edges, which fits a change in their loads. A heat-pump tariff would add its edges together; no substation other than D8 and D12 shows more than one opening and one closing together.

The detection limit is 1.19 points of a substation's demand, which is the smallest year-on-year change in an edge this design can tell apart from placebo drift. A tariff effect smaller than that at Primary level is not visible here. The sizes by year at each substation are in report.txt. The design could improve by using a matched control substation or by shortening the comparison to neighbouring years.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Summer is assumed step-free. On summer nights the later half-hours average 0.7 to 13.4 points below the earlier ones, which is the ordinary decline of demand through the night, and the winter-night shape differs from it for reasons besides storage heating. The full step carries that difference. The slope does not.
  • Four headline winters of one weather product, from one set of substations. The winters are separate years, and neighbouring cells share one ERA5 product.
  • The gate says nothing about the pooled intervals, which may be too narrow in practice. The gate's 100% pooled coverage is built in (the gate paragraph). The substations share one weather product, so their errors are not independent, which would make the intervals too narrow.
  • Cold-snap means rest on few winters. The raw cold-snap means per winter (November to March beside November to February) are in report.txt, with 32 to 38 nights per winter. They cover four winters at 13 substations and two at D9, and the winters are not independent experiments.
  • The daily mean temperature is a proxy for the temperature that sets heater charging. In the gate, a step that follows the 18:00 to 08:00 mean temperature was covered by the interval in 79% of draws pooled at 7 points, and in 43% at the worst substation.
  • Winter 2025-26 was read once, after the headline winters. The page's headline numbers use the headline winters, and the selection winter appears beside them.

docs.title: The plan, as committed before any fit
docs.text: E7 is an estimation experiment. The result is a table of estimates with intervals, not a win-or- lose verdict, and the experiment forecasts nothing. The word calibrated is used only for the known-answer gate (interval coverage within a stated band), and detectable only for the per-series reading. The plan follows briefs/dp_series.md, then briefs/common.md. The Sonnet plan review is triaged at the end of this page. No data on or after 2026-07-01 is read, nothing in packages/ changes, and no dependency is added.

docs.title: Pre-fit clarification: what the headline is (written before any fit)
docs.text:
The headline is the pooled step over all six decision series (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), with a random effect across series, at a daily mean of 3 C. The extension series, E7-X, are shown separately. D5, D10, and D16 are reported as the subset that prompted the study, labelled "selected for showing the step", and no verdict rests on them alone. Every fitted series, including each with no step, appears in the unpooled table. This replaces the earlier draft, in which the verdict rested on D5, D10, and D16.
