Gain is the K0 score minus the arm's score on the AFTER rows of the 34 load shifts (146,354 rows, 18 Primary pairs). Ordinary-day columns are the arm's score minus K0's, so negative is better. "Every row" is the arm's score minus K0's over every forecast with a reading, in all 5 calendar years, with no interval.

Gate Result Target Passes G1: K0 minus ORACLE on the 13 load-shift and series pairs that experiment 227 scored (32,148 rows) 5.68 points 5.339 within 30% yes G2: K0 minus PERFECT in the AFTER phase of 141's injected load shifts (717,698 rows) 2.39 points 1.50 within 30% no

  • Question and rule. Does LR_b20's mask keep at least half of the oracle's gain after a load shift, with ordinary-day harm inside +/-0.05 points, on every Primary and on months it did not train on? The harm limit holds. The gain share misses the bar on the point estimate (47.1% against 50%), and its lower bound is above 0%. The failed gate G2 makes the verdict inconclusive.

  • Gate G1 passes. The harness's K0 scores 9.61 points on experiment 227's real load-shift rows against 10.13 in experiment 227, and the gain of the oracle is 5.68 points against 5.34. The gain rises with lead: 2.22 points under 24 hours, 4.49 from 24 to 72 hours, and 8.53 from 72 hours to 7 days.

  • Gate G2 fails. The harness's PERFECT minus K0 gain is 2.39 points, 59% above experiment 208's 1.50. Each lead band is 42% to 69% above experiment 208's gain in the same band (1.98, 2.65, and 2.61 points against 1.25, 1.57, and 1.84). Three post hoc diagnostics, all outside the pre-registered rule, change the gain. Multiplying the quantile offsets by 1.5 lowers the gain to 1.90 points, which is within 30% of 1.50 and would pass the gate. Multiplying by 1.2 gives 2.17. Keeping only injected load shifts in experiment 208's scored year gives 2.15. The gate fails as pre-registered. Whether the gate passes depends on a post hoc setting of the quantile offsets.
  • The gain after load shifts rests on a few events. The largest of the 34 load shifts carries 49.9% of LR_b20's total gain and 20.0% of the oracle's. LR_b20 recovers at least half the oracle's gain after 6 of the 34 load shifts, and between -10% and +10% of the oracle's gain after 22. The median per-shift share (28 load shifts where the oracle gains) is 3.8% for LR_b20 and 98.8% for GAM_ONLY. Leaving out one Primary moves LR_b20's share between 38.8% (without D16) and 63.5% (without D18), so the 50% bar is crossed by dropping D18. The 30 load shifts of 1 day or less give the oracle 0.22 points and LR_b20 0.01.
  • Ordinary days. LR_b20's difference stays inside +/-0.05 in every variant: -0.010 without D8's drops and the 17 block days, -0.011 without D8 and D9, -0.008 when closures of connected neighbours are also excluded, and -0.005 (-0.013 to +0.002) without the 7.5 alarms (of 44 that start on ordinary rows, each alarm weighted 1 over its series' number of folds) that are balanced-opposite candidates. The in-sample even months give +0.003. At 13 of 15 Primaries the absolute difference is under 0.05. At the other two, D18 (-0.195) and D22 (-0.052), the mask improves the score. D12 and D2 have no LR_b20 alarms. Leaving one Primary out moves the pooled difference between -0.006 and -0.012. Of the three alarm settings, LR_b20 has the smallest ordinary-day difference: LR_b80 gives +0.039 and RO_b80 +0.082, with an interval above zero.
  • Net over a year. Over every forecast with a reading, LR_b20 scores 0.040 points worse than K0 (by year: -0.008, +0.046, +0.125, -0.008, +0.040 from 2022 to 2026), the oracle 0.000, and GAM_ONLY 0.582 worse. D22 and D21 account for 65% and 26% of the summed excess over series, mostly in 2024 (+1.55 points at D22) and 2023 (+0.59 at D21). The excess sits in the alarm spans: 73% of LR_b20's excess score lies in spans that overlap a logged closure that is not a labelled load shift, 25% in spans that overlap a labelled load shift, and 1.5% in spans that overlap no logged closure (shares of the score summed over the alarm spans, each span counted once, which cover 82% of the net figure). The three alarms with the largest excess score last 27, 32, and 44 days, sit on D22, D21, and D22, and carry 59%, 31%, and 9% of the excess summed over spans. The 32-day alarm on D21 overlaps a labelled load shift.
  • Tails. After load shifts, K0's readings fall below its 1% quantile 9.1% of the time and LR_b20's 4.0%, against 1.8% for ORACLE (nominal 1%). K0's readings fall below the 99% quantile 93.4% of the time, LR_b20's 96.3%, and ORACLE's 98.6% (nominal 99%). On ordinary rows the tail shares of LR_b20, HALF, and ORACLE match K0's within 0.2 percentage points, and GAM_ONLY's readings fall below the 1% quantile 2.9% of the time and below the 5% quantile 9.9% of the time.
  • Row sets and data. 15 Primary series (D15 has no readings), 2022-01 to 2026-06, origins every 6 hours from 2022-02-01, 12,236,784 ordinary odd-month rows. D-numbers are the labels in the series table. The GAM forecast of D9 starts in 2023-12 and D18's in 2025-07, so those two series have fewer rows. The 35th labelled load shift (D15 and D18, 2025-03) has no AFTER rows, because D18's GAM forecast starts after it.
  • Limits. The forecast uses past weather, so absolute scores are an upper bound on forecast skill and are not comparable with ensemble-driven pages. The effective capacity is the single stored value, not re-estimated from data before each origin. A row whose target lies after a refit of experiment 130's GAM sees a fit made up to 7 days after its origin. The intervals for gain resample 18 Primary pairs, so they are wide. The learned alarm's threshold is set on the pooled scores of all 15 series in a fold file, and those pooled scores include the scored series' own odd months. A series in two or three folds is scored with each fold's model, weighted equally, and each of those models trained on another pair that contains the series. The Kalman hyperparameters and the GAM refits come from experiment 130, which used the whole record. A mask arm's span ends at the end rule of experiment 148 with 6 hours of lookahead, and every learned alarm is known 96 hours after its step (RO_b80's: 48 hours).
  • What to try next. A limit on how long a mask stays open would test whether the excess score over a year disappears without losing the gain after load shifts, because 3 alarms of 27 to 44 days carry 99% of the excess summed over spans. A like-for-like gate would first match the harness's forecast spread to experiment 208's.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Gates. G1 and G2 were fixed in the plan and run before any arm was read. G2 failed and was not changed.
  • Series 10 was read early. The aggregated table of series 10 (D10) was printed while the scoring script was being tested, before the clarifications in the last section were committed.
  • Median against mean. The median forecast minus the mean forecast differs by series, from -2.06 points at D12 to +0.61 at D8, and is the same for every arm. The contrasts between arms do not depend on the median-minus-mean gap.
  • Direction. The quantile-score gain and the mean and median absolute-error gains agree in sign for every arm except HALF. The exception is HALF, whose ordinary-day differences are within 0.003.
  • Audit triggers. Three of the six audit triggers fired: the failed G2, a leave-one-out share that reaches 63.5% (without D18), and a harm interval under half as wide as experiment 227's. A Sonnet audit (Opus was not used, to save quota) recomputed the gain, the share, the harm interval, and the per-shift shares from the per-row scores without reading the report script. The audit agreed with every figure. The audit also found that leaving out the largest load shift (pair D5 and D16) drops LR_b20's share to 29.5%, and that the harm interval is built from few non-zero months and cannot see an alarm over a logged closure, which the ordinary rows exclude.
  • Code review. A Sonnet review found no leakage in the filter's cutoffs, the span masking, the fold use, the offsets, the row sets, or the gates. The review found that the per-alarm net-loss table counted overlapping spans of different folds more than once, so the split of the excess by span class was recomputed with each span scored by its own fold. The review also listed the limits above that were missing from the page.
  • Numbers review. A Sonnet review checked every figure against the printed reports and found no wrong number. It asked for the post hoc G2 diagnostics to be reported in full, for the claims about the net annual loss to be softened, and for the bullet lists to be repaired; all three were applied.

docs.title: Choices fixed after the plan and before any gate or arm was read
docs.text:
These pin down points the plan left open. The harness code was run and its output for one series (series 10, aggregated over all its rows) was printed to test the scorer before these choices were committed; no gate and no contrast was read.

  • Origins and leads. Origins every 6 hours from 31 days after the series starts (2022-01-01), each with 336 half-hourly targets (leads 0 to 7 days). Lead bands: under 24 hours, 24 to 72 hours, and 72 hours to 7 days. Hour bands are the four local-time bands of studies.dp_calendar.
  • Quantile offsets. One table per series, hour band, and lead band: the 11 quantiles of the no-mask residual over odd UTC months of the target, shared by every arm.
  • Effective capacity. The single value stored for each series in the stage 1 pilot's series table, not re-estimated from data before each origin. The plan said "from data before each origin"; the stored value is the one every earlier page used.
  • GAM forecast. The frozen forecast of experiment 130 uses, for each target, the fit made at the latest refit on or before the target. A row whose origin lies before a refit and whose target lies after it therefore sees a fit made up to 7 days after the origin.
  • ORACLE. Masks every one of the 66 labelled real load shifts that involves the series.
  • Gate G1 rows. The 13 pairs of load shift and Primary series that experiment 227 scored (11 load shifts in its scored and replicate months). Rows: forecast origin at or after the logged onset and target within 72 hours after the logged end, every origin in the harness, leads 0 to 7 days. The day-ahead lead band is reported beside the pooled figure. The gate is the pooled K0 minus ORACLE score on these rows, within 30% of 5.339 points.
  • Gate G2 rows. Experiment 141's 44 stored worlds at the six Primaries, the stream being the real residual plus the injected megawatts (in points). Rows follow experiment 208: injected transfers of 25% of load or more lasting over 1 day, forecast cutoff at or after the injected onset and not within 96 half-hours of it (the AFTER phase is cutoff at least 96 half-hours after the onset and target at or after the end), target within 96 half-hours of the end, scored against the stream without the injected megawatts. PERFECT masks the true interval, known at the onset with the end known at once. The gate is PERFECT minus K0 within 30% of 1.50 points.
  • ORDINARY rows. The target lies outside every closure of experiment 37's log of 629 that names the series as a side, and outside the 72 hours after each closure. A variant that also drops closures of connected neighbours is reported beside it.
  • Month for the odd and even split. The UTC calendar month of the target.

docs.title: Does a neural head that adds 11 quantile offsets to the wind forecast, trained on 15 months of daily ensemble hindcasts, lower the quantile score of the forecasts for the three metered wind farms, and their 99% pinball loss?
docs.text:
Take-home: a correction learned from 15 months of daily ensemble forecasts lowered the wind forecast's quantile score by 4.5% to 5.5%, but a lookup table of offsets gets 92% of that gain, so the neural network and the ensemble's wind summaries are not what earned it. We asked whether a small neural network that adds an offset to each of 11 quantiles of the wind forecast would score better when it could learn from daily forecast runs from April 2024 to June 2025 (442 runs), instead of the 13 to 40 weekly runs that experiment 221's head saw. We scored the quantile score, an estimate of the continuous ranked probability score, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity; smaller is better). Against R1, a physics-based wind-power forecast fitted to ERA5, the head (H5c) was 0.653 points better, and against R0, an XGBoost forecast fitted to the same ERA5 window, 0.532 points better, on the rows left after experiment 210's mask removes readings taken while a farm was idle (the kept rows). A head (K5) that sees only the 11 quantiles of R1's forecast, the lead time, and the farm scored the same. A table (T5) with one offset per lead day, quantile, and farm scored 0.051 points worse than the head, with an interval that includes zero. The verdict is partly supported: the head beat both base fits, but its tail score was not separable from XGBoost's, and the network did not earn its inputs.

The head idea comes from experiment 243, where a head that adds 11 quantile offsets tied XGBoost on a metered solar farm. The base forecasts here are experiment 230's: R0 is experiment 230's XGBoost recipe and R1 is experiment 230's physics core. Both are fitted to ERA5 (our estimate of past weather) up to 2024-03-31, so they are out of sample on the hindcast runs. The hindcast base forecasts come from the production feature engineer, which reproduces experiment 230's frames exactly. We scored the 53 Tuesday runs of July 2025 to June 2026 at three metered wind farms (W1 to W3).

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Head. Experiment 243's H5: two hidden layers of 64 units, a zero-initialised last layer, 11 corrections of 0.3 times tanh added to the base quantiles, then sorted and clamped to 0 to 1. AdamW at a learning rate of 0.002, up to 60 epochs, batches of 512, five seeds, pooled over the three farms. The epoch with the lowest loss on runs initialised from 2025-04-16 is kept.
  • Head inputs. The base 11 quantiles, the members' mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentile of the 100 m wind speed, the sine and cosine of the mean wind direction, the mean 2 m temperature, the lead, and a one-hot farm column. No calendar columns.
  • Spread factor. The monthly spread factor of experiment 33 is applied to each base model's mixture in one pass over the hindcast and scored cases. The first hindcast month (2024-04) has too few earlier cases and keeps the unadjusted mixture.
  • Arms. H5c is R1 plus the head. K5 gets only the base quantiles, the lead, and the farm. BL5 gets the lead, the farm, and the hour and day of year. H5c-Tue trains on the hindcast's Tuesday runs only. N5-lin is a linear stage and N5-xgb a per-level XGBoost stage on the head's inputs. T5 is a table of offsets per lead day, quantile, and farm.

docs.text:

Intervals resample whole months and the five seeds; they are 98.75% for the planned contrasts and 95% for the rest. The farms are not resampled.

  • C1, H5c minus R1: -0.653 (-0.855 to -0.432). The prediction (-0.15 to -0.40) was too small. The gain is similar in every lead band (days 1 and 2 -0.598, days 3 to 6 -0.566, day 7 onward -0.696, 95% intervals all below zero) and in every quarter of the scored year (0.59 to 0.71 points better).
  • C2, H5c minus R0: -0.532 (-0.734 to -0.324). The prediction (inside ±0.10) was too small. The rule for replacing XGBoost (wholly below zero) is met on the quantile score.
  • The tail score T, H5c minus R0, is -0.016 (-0.041 to +0.008), so the planned rule is not met. The 0.99 pinball loss is 4.5% lower (-0.031, 98.75% interval -0.080 to +0.016), and 1.6% lower at lead days 1 and 2, against the predicted 5% to 15%.
  • C3, H5c minus the better non-neural arm (N5-xgb), is +0.066 (-0.041 to +0.198). The prediction (at least 0.03 lower) failed. N5-xgb was chosen on the early-stopping runs (0.03574 against 0.03588 for N5-lin).
  • C4, H5c minus K5, is -0.009 (-0.124 to +0.128). The prediction (at least 0.05 lower) failed. The ensemble's wind summaries gave no gain that this interval can separate from zero.
  • D3, H5c minus the offset table T5: -0.051 (-0.141 to +0.057). The table alone lowers the score by 0.602 against R1.
  • C5, H5c minus H5c-Tue: -0.049 (-0.153 to +0.060). Daily runs did not measurably beat Tuesday runs from the same 15 months.
  • The calendar-only head. BL5 minus R1 is -0.073 (-0.494 to +0.411), and the blind share, (BL5 minus R1) divided by (H5c minus R1), is 0.11 over all kept rows. On April to June alone the share is 1.04, because BL5 scores as well as H5c there (9.393 against 9.418).
  • Coverage. H5c's 5% to 95% band covers 0.878 of the kept rows (predicted 0.80 to 0.90), and its 1% to 99% band 0.972.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The quantile score and the mean forecast's absolute error disagree because the base median is biased low. The error of the mean forecast changes by -0.074 for C1 (98.75% interval -0.358 to +0.274), +0.060 for C2 (-0.220 to +0.382), +0.068 for C3, and -0.087 for C4. The observed power is below the median of R1 on 34% of kept rows, and below its mean forecast on 46%. The head moves the median up by about 4.9 points and the mean forecast by 3.5 to 4.1, so the median-minus-mean gap goes from -4.98 to -4.03 points, and the median's absolute error falls (H5c minus R0 -0.79, -1.08 to -0.46, 95%) and the mean forecast's squared error falls, while its absolute error stays flat. The mean forecast's absolute error improves at lead day 0 (-0.55) and worsens from day 3 (+0.06, then +0.16 from day 7).
  • Leaving one farm out keeps the sign. C1 without W1 is -0.772, without W2 -0.377, and without W3 -0.808 (95% intervals all below zero); C2 gives -0.641, -0.268, and -0.685. The gain rests most on W2. On all rows, H5c scored 10.50, 11.79, and 10.32 at W1, W2, and W3, against R0's 10.67, 12.43, and 10.09, so the head is worse than R0 at W3.
  • The base fits reproduce experiment 230. R0 scores 11.697 against 11.663 for A0r, and R1 11.817 against 11.792 for B1 (limit 0.10). All 442 daily runs have 51 members at the three farms.
  • The head is better than R1 on its early-stopping runs. Its mean pinball loss there is 0.0356, against 0.0383 for R1, so the stop rule did not fire.
  • The low bias is present from the first hindcast quarter. The observed power is below R1's median on 33% of rows in April to June 2024, the quarter after the base fits end, and on 31% to 40% in the scored quarters. Static offsets fitted on the hindcast still work on the scored year, so the bias is stable rather than a drift.
  • Audit. Trigger 3 fired (the quantile score and the mean forecast's error move in different directions for C2), and a fresh audit re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored forecasts. It matched every number, found the sign of C1 and C2 stable across seeds, 11 of 12 init months, all lead bands, and all farms, and found no leakage. It also showed that constant offsets fitted on the hindcast recover 70% of the gain when pooled over farms and leads, 82% per farm, and 92% per farm and lead day (T5). The head's per-seed spread (11.10 to 11.22) is larger than its gaps to K5 and T5. The report is private.

docs.title: Caveats and departures from the plan
docs.text:
• The cause of the low bias is unknown. The offsets correct a bias that exists from the first month after the base fits end, so it is not drift. The low bias could come from the ERA5-trained fits being applied to ensemble members, or from the 51-member mixture itself. The experiment cannot tell which.
  • W2 carries C2. Without W2 the contrast is -0.268, about half its size. W2 is the one farm whose physics core has no idle layer, so its base fit differs from the other two.
  • Departures. The plan review dropped the second head (H5x) and added H5c-Tue. The score of the head without the first hindcast month was not run. R0 and R1 are fitted twice, once for the hindcast rows and once for the scored rows, so a GPU fit that is not bit-for-bit repeatable could differ slightly between the two.
  • The blind control is weaker in spring. The training runs cover April to June 2024 and 1 to 15 April 2025, so BL5 has seen April to June of the calendar before and can score well there from the season alone.
  • Three farms. Intervals do not cover other farms.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Where does the low bias in the ensemble mixture's median come from? Test a bias correction of the ensemble's wind inputs, and a refit of the XGBoost model on ensemble-era data, against the offset table.
  • Which months of ensemble forecasts does the offset table need? The experiment trained on 15 months and could not say whether a shorter or longer window gives a more stable table.

docs.title: Does combining three solar-farm forecasters per quantile level beat the best one alone?
docs.text:
Blending three stored solar-farm forecasters with a separate weight at each quantile level scores 2.1% better than the best single forecaster, H5, but the rolling tail adjustment raised the error. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters six solar farms, labelled A to F. Experiment 243 stored the forecasts of three forecasters. H5 is a physical solar-farm power model (the plant) plus a neural network that outputs 11 quantile offsets. The second forecaster is a neural network without the plant, and the third is XGBoost. The equal-weight arm (arm C1) gives the three forecasters equal weights, arm C2 fits a separate weight for each forecaster at each of the 11 quantile levels, and arm C3 adds a rolling adjustment of the outer quantiles to C2. C2 fits its weights on earlier months by minimising pinball loss, the quantile loss that penalises under-prediction and over-prediction in proportion to the quantile level.

The combination beat H5 by more than the predicted 1.5%. With own history (each farm's forecast fitted on that farm's own earlier months), the quantile score of C2 (twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 levels, in points of capacity; lower is better) is 5.358 against 5.475 for H5. Contrast C1 (C2 minus H5) is -2.13% (95% interval -2.80% to -1.58%; 99% interval -3.09% to -1.42%). The 0.99 pinball loss of C2 is 2.1% lower than the loss of the neural network without the plant (95% interval -4.2% to +0.5%), inside the predicted limit of 5% above it.

About a quarter of that gain comes from averaging seeds. H5, the neural network, and XGBoost each have five seeds, and C2 combines their seed-averaged quantiles, while the reference scores of experiment 243 average the losses of the seeds. Averaging H5's seeds in quantile space improves its score by 0.49% (5.448). Against that like-for-like H5, C2 is 1.64% better (check M1, a post hoc comparison; 95% interval -2.28% to -1.12%; 99% interval -2.57% to -0.96%), only just past the 1.5% threshold.

The rolling tail adjustment missed its prediction on the quantile score but met it on coverage. The adjustment (C3) moves the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles by an offset that follows recent misses. Coverage of the 0.99 quantile (the share of actual values at or below it) rises from 0.9877 to 0.9948, inside the predicted band of 0.985 to 0.995. The quantile score rises by 1.19% (95% interval +0.88% to +1.51%), against the 0.2% allowed, and the 0.99 pinball loss rises by 27%. The hypothesis is partly supported.

The neural network without the plant carries the top quantiles and H5 carries the bottom one. Over the 9 months after the 3-month burn-in, the fitted weights of C2 give the neural network without the plant 0.86 of the weight at the 0.99 quantile and 0.70 at the 0.95 quantile, and give H5 all of the weight at the 0.01 quantile. With zero history (fitted on the other five farms), C2 is 1.66% better than H5 (95% interval -2.18% to -1.16%).

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Quantile score (points of capacity, mean over six farms, own history): C2-LOMO 5.349, C2 5.358, C1 5.370, C3 5.422, H5 with seeds averaged 5.448, H5 5.475, XGBoost 5.490, neural network without the plant 5.541, plant 5.726, climatology 8.638, manual heuristic 8.687. Zero history: C2-LOMO 5.508, C2 5.517, C1 5.522, H5 with seeds averaged 5.584, XGBoost 5.610, H5 5.610, neural network without the plant 5.650, plant 5.871.
  • Burn-in and LOMO. The first 3 scored months (2025-09 to 2025-11) are scored with equal weights, so C2 equals arm C1 there. Each later month's weights use only the actuals observed before that month's first forecast run. C2-LOMO (C2 with weights fitted on all scored months except the scored month, using later months too) cannot exist at forecast time, so C2-LOMO is an optimistic reference. C2-LOMO scores only 0.16% better than C2.
  • Exploratory arms (not pre-registered): arm C1 is 1.91% better than H5 (95% interval -2.52% to -1.42%). Arm C1 was scored during planning on a different capacity figure and is rescored here on experiment 243's capacity. C2 is 2.40% better than XGBoost (95% interval -2.89% to -1.80%).
  • Per farm (own history, quantile score, H5 then C2): A 5.277 and 5.221, B 5.252 and 5.138, C 4.903 and 4.777, D 6.011 and 5.868, E 6.351 and 6.214, F 5.055 and 4.931. C2 is better at all six farms.
  • Tail calibration, own history (share of actual values below the 0.01 quantile, share at or below the 0.99 quantile, then pinball loss at 0.01 and 0.99): H5 0.007 and 0.985, 0.334 and 0.344; neural network without the plant 0.048 and 0.980, 0.400 and 0.328; XGBoost 0.016 and 0.994, 0.369 and 0.485; C2 0.018 and 0.988, 0.345 and 0.321; C3 0.008 and 0.995, 0.338 and 0.409. The nominal shares are 0.01 and 0.99.
  • Lower tail by farm. C2's share below the 0.01 quantile is 0.042 at farm D and 0.036 at farm E, against 0.003 and 0.018 for H5, so the excess of C2 over 0.01 comes from those two farms. C3 brings farm D to 0.007 and farm E to 0.020. Of C2's actual values below the 0.01 quantile, 87% are under 3% of capacity (H5: 60%; C3: 64%).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median beside the contrasts. The median error (mean absolute error, MAE, of the median) is 9.72 for C2 and 9.85 for H5, so the gain in quantile score is not carried by the median alone: the 0.99 pinball loss is 6.6% lower (95% interval -10.9% to -1.7%) and the 0.01 pinball loss 3.2% higher (95% interval -0.4% to +9.7%).
  • Triggers. The second prediction (the tail adjustment raises the quantile score by no more than 0.2%) fails, which fires the plan's audit trigger for a contradicted prediction. The stop rule does not apply, because C2 beats H5 by more than 0.5%.
  • Departures from the plan. The weights are found by a grid search of the simplex to 0.002 in each weight, because the linear programme of the plan took tens of seconds per fit. A linear programme and the grid gave weights within 0.0001 on 6 months of own-history data at the 0.01, 0.5, and 0.99 levels. The MAE of the mean forecast is not reported, because the combined arms output quantiles only. Shares below the 0.01 quantile use a strict inequality, because the quantile is exactly 0 for 34% of C2's half-hours and counting those ties as misses would overstate them.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should test two changes: an adjustment of the 0.99 quantile alone with a smaller step, and a fit of C2's lower quantiles that does not miss at farms D and E. The adjustment of the 0.99 quantile overshoots to 0.9948 coverage and raises the 0.99 pinball loss by 27%. C2's excess below the 0.01 quantile at farms D and E is not isolated here, and C3 removes it only by moving the quantile to zero.

docs.title: Data-processing note
docs.text: Experiment 268 found crossing quantiles in 26,344 of its 77,897 generator-forecast rows (34%), but all of them belong to three generators that are not solar farms, so none is on this page. Experiment 273 counted 0 crossing rows in every arm here, because the fit scripts sorted the 11 quantiles before writing them, so sorting does not change the scores on this page.

docs.title: At which stage of the wind forecast does the low bias enter: the weather input, the mixing of the 51 ensemble members, or the physics core and the farms?
docs.text:
Take-home: the wind forecast's low median enters at the ensemble's weather, not at the physics core, the farms, or the mixing of the 51 ensemble members. The wind-power forecast of experiment 259 is too low: observed power was below the forecast's median on 34% of rows instead of 50%. The forecast is a physics-based model of wind-farm power (the physics core, R1) fitted to ERA5, our estimate of past weather, before 2024-04-01. It reads the 51 members (separate forecast scenarios) of the ECMWF ensemble and mixes the 51 resulting power forecasts. We kept the core fixed and swapped its weather input stage by stage: ERA5 wind at the valid time (the oracle), the ensemble's mean wind, and the 51 members mixed together. The scores use the kept rows, which leave out the readings that experiment 210's mask flags as an idle-turbine artefact.

With ERA5 wind, the core is calibrated over the scored year at these three farms. The share of kept rows below the median was 52.8% (95% interval 50.3% to 55.0%). With the ensemble's mean wind the share fell to 36.6%, and after mixing the 51 members to 34.1%. The median fell by 11.5 points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity) from the oracle to the final forecast. The weather swap accounts for 10.2 of those points (89%, interval 86% to 91%) and the member mixing for 1.3 points (11%). The ensemble's 10 m and 100 m wind speeds each explain about 7 points on their own, and the temperature none.

The verdict is partly supported. The predictions held for the oracle share and for the mixing. The planned conversion from the 100 m wind-speed bias to power (the core curve's slope times the bias) explains 48% of the 11.5-point fall, not the 70% we predicted, because the conversion leaves out the 10 m wind that sets the core's shear exponent.

Training on ensemble forecasts is not a cure. It lifts the share below the median by 3 to 5 points of the 16-point gap between 50% and 34%.

docs.title: Design and results
docs.text:
• Stages. The core is experiment 259's R1 (shear exponent to a fitted hub height, air-density factor, blurred power curve, idle layer except at W2, 14 bins of residual quantiles), refitted here with experiment 259's code. Its stored mixture median matches the recomputed one to 0.0003 of capacity at every farm, so the refit reproduces experiment 259's forecasts. The spread factor scales quantiles about the median, so it cannot move the median.
  • Rows. The 53 Tuesday runs of 2025-07 to 2026-06 at W1 to W3: 96,479 kept rows and 107,121 rows in all. The 442 daily hindcast runs (2024-04 to 2025-06, 794,076 kept rows) are descriptive. Intervals resample the 12 months of the scored year 2,000 times; the farms are not resampled.
  • Share below the median, scored year, kept rows (all rows). Oracle 52.8% (52.1%); ensemble-mean wind 36.6% (41.2%); 51-member mixture, R1, 34.1% (38.8%); XGBoost mixture, R0, 35.1% (39.8%). Intervals on the kept rows: 50.3% to 55.0%, 33.9% to 39.7%, 31.5% to 37.0%, and 32.6% to 38.0%.
  • By farm, kept rows (oracle, ensemble-mean wind, mixture). W1 50.3%, 36.2%, 32.9%; W2 50.9%, 29.8%, 28.0%; W3 57.5%, 44.3%, 41.8%. W3's oracle share sits above 50%, and W2's mixture share is the lowest.
  • By lead band, kept rows (oracle, mixture). Days 0 to 2: 52.5%, 37.5%. Days 3 to 6: 52.3%, 33.7%. Day 7 onward: 53.1%, 33.0%. The shift in the median grows from 4.9 points (days 0 to 2) to 9.4 and 14.8 points.
  • Median shift, kept rows, in points of capacity. Total (oracle minus final) 11.5 (9.7 to 13.3); weather swap 10.2 (8.5 to 11.8); member mixing 1.3 (0.9 to 1.6). By farm the weather share is 86% (W1), 93% (W2), and 85% (W3). By band it is 85%, 88%, and 89%.
  • Wind-speed bias, scored year. The ensemble-mean 100 m wind is 1.00 m/s slower than ERA5 on average (0.70 m/s in the hindcast), 0.37 m/s slower at days 0 to 2 and 1.29 m/s at day 7 onward. By ERA5 100 m speed bin: +1.6 m/s at 3 to 5, +0.2 at 5 to 8, -1.5 at 8 to 12, -3.5 at 12 to 16, and -6.5 at 16 to 20. The 10 m wind is 1.3 m/s slower at 8 to 12 m/s. The planned range (0.3 to 0.8 m/s slower at 5 to 12 m/s) was wrong in both size and sign at 5 to 8 m/s.
  • Slope conversion. The core curve's slope times the 100 m speed bias gives 5.5 of the 11.5 points (48%, interval 43% to 54%). The conversion leaves out the 10 m wind, which sets the core's shear exponent, so the planned 70% was not met.
  • Input swap, mean median forecast (points of capacity). ERA5 inputs 29.2; ensemble temperature only 29.3; ensemble 100 m wind only 22.1; ensemble 10 m wind only 22.2; both ensemble winds 18.9; all three 19.0.
  • Mixing. The core on the ensemble-mean wind gives a mean forecast of 19.0 points. The mean of the 51 members' forecasts is 22.4 points and their median 18.0 (convexity of the power curve lifts the mean, as the plan expected). The mixture's median is 1.3 points below the core's output on the mean wind.
  • Training source (ensemble-mean inputs, kept rows). On the held-out hindcast months (2025-01 to 2025-06) the ERA5-trained core has 38.0% of rows below the median and the ensemble-trained core 42.0%; XGBoost gives 37.8% and 42.8%. On the scored year they give 36.6% against 39.8%, and 36.7% against 40.5%. In sample (the 9 months of ensemble forecasts that trained them), the ensemble-trained core has 43.7% of kept rows and 50.0% of all rows below the median.
  • Farm check on ERA5. The ERA5-fed core has 49.9%, 49.5%, and 47.5% of kept rows below the median in sample at W1, W2, and W3, and 51.2%, 47.3%, and 50.3% from 2024-04 to 2025-06. Over the hindcast the oracle share is 49.5% on kept rows, but it is 52.7% in April to December 2024 and 44.0% in January to June 2025, so a period's share moves by several points with no change in the models.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per farm (points of capacity, 51-member mixture, kept rows). The median of the members' forecasts minus their mean is -4.7 (W1), -4.5 (W2), and -3.8 (W3). The mean forecast is also low: 22.4 points against an observed mean of 28.9, so the bias is not only a skew between median and mean.
  • Control. The recomputed mixture median matches experiment 259's stored R1 median to within 0.0003 at every farm, for both the hindcast and the scored year.
  • Leave one farm out. The weather share of the median shift is 85% to 93% at every farm, so no farm carries the conclusion.
  • No quantile-score contrast and no new forecast. The mean-forecast-error check of experiment 259 does not apply, and no tail-calibration table applies.
  • Audit triggers. None of the seven triggers in the ml-experiment skill fired. The planned bias range and the slope conversion missed their predictions, and the input swap explains why (the 10 m wind enters through the shear exponent), so the explanation is tested and recorded here.

docs.title: Caveats and departures from the plan
docs.text:
• ERA5 is the reference, not the truth. The core was fitted to ERA5, so the fitted hub height absorbs ERA5's own bias at each farm. The result says the ensemble's wind is slower than ERA5's, and that the ERA5-fitted core is calibrated on ERA5 wind. It does not say which product matches the wind at the turbines.
  • Kept rows and all rows differ. The share on kept rows is 4 to 6 points lower than on all rows for the ensemble stages and within 1 point for the oracle, so the rows the idle-row mask removes are mostly below the ensemble stages' median. The conclusion is the same on both.
  • Steps run. The stop rule asked for steps 3 to 6 because the slope conversion fell short of 70%, so all six steps ran. Step 4 was not run as a refit: the spread factor cannot move a median (checked above), and R1 has no base margin yet has the same low share as R0, which has one. The BM0 refit was not run for that reason.
  • Training source uses ensemble-mean inputs. The models in step 5 read one ensemble-mean value per case, with four wind columns for XGBoost (no 10 m direction), so they isolate the training source from the mixing and are not experiment 259's member-level models.
  • Held-out hindcast months overlap the training months slightly. Runs of 2024-12 reach about 10 days into 2025-01, so the first 10 days of the held-out months share observed targets with the ensemble-trained models' training rows. The scored-year numbers are clean.
  • Three farms. Intervals describe these farms, and the 12 resampled months share one weather year.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does correcting the ensemble's 10 m and 100 m wind speeds remove the shortfall? Fit a correction by ensemble-mean speed and lead from the hindcast, apply it to every member, and compare the quantile score with the offset table of experiment 259 on the same rows.
  • Is the speed bias a property of the ensemble or of the grid cell? Compare the bias at other grid cells and, where observations exist, with measured wind.

docs.title: Does mixing the ECMWF ensemble's members with the AIFS ensemble's members and with climatology, weighted by lead, lower the wind forecast's quantile score and tail score, once an offset table corrects the common low bias?
docs.text:
Take-home: the AIFS ensemble improves the wind forecast's quantile score at 3 to 6 days ahead, but neither it nor climatology nor a neural gate improves the high-power tail. We asked whether the wind forecast for three metered farms (W1 to W3) improves when the 51 ECMWF ensemble members are pooled with the 51 members of the AIFS ensemble (a machine-learning weather model from ECMWF, available from Dynamical.org under CC BY 4.0), with climatology (the typical power for the month and half-hour), or both. Every member runs through the ERA5-trained XGBoost model of experiment 230, and every arm then gets the table of offsets of experiment 259, which corrects the common low bias. We scored October 2025 to June 2026 on the rows kept by experiment 210's idle-row mask. The verdict is partly supported: the AIFS result passes the decision rule's point threshold but its interval ends 0.003 points of capacity short, and the other two contrasts fail.

AIFS lowers the quantile score at days 3 to 6 by 0.48 points of capacity. The 98.33% interval is -0.86 to -0.147 (C2); the threshold needed an interval wholly below -0.15. The 0.99 pinball loss at days 3 to 6 is not lower (0.567 against 0.563 for M0), so the prediction of a 3% fall missed. The gain also exceeds the predicted -0.10 to -0.30. At days 0 to 2 the prediction was ±0.05, and the estimate was -0.12 (-0.45 to +0.14). Climatology's days 0 to 2 contrast (+0.01, -0.01 to +0.03) stayed inside its predicted ±0.02.

Climatology and the neural gate add nothing. Climatology weights by lead day lower the score at days 7 and later by 0.08 (-0.48 to +0.23, C1), against a predicted -0.15 to -0.40. Without the offset table the same arm lowers it by 0.45 (-0.89 to -0.09, D10), slightly more than the predicted range. The offset table therefore removes most of the long-lead gain that climatology gave, which tests the explanation for the miss. The gate changes the score by -0.03 (-0.16 to +0.07, C3) against the weights by lead day, just outside the predicted ±0.03. The gate that reads only the lead (M5b) scores within 0.01 of the full gate (D1).

docs.title: Design and results
docs.text:
• Arms. Each arm has a version without and one with the offset table ("+T"). M0: the ECMWF members. M1q and M1p: M0 with climatology, by quantile averaging and by linear pool, one weight per lead day. M2: the AIFS members alone. M3: the linear pool of the ECMWF and AIFS members, one weight per lead day. M4: M3 with climatology. M5: a neural gate (one hidden layer of 16 units) that reads the lead, each ensemble's standard deviation of 100 m wind speed, and the difference of the two mean speeds. M5b: the same gate reading only the lead. M3prev: M3 with the AIFS run of 18 UTC the day before. C1 is M1q+T minus M0+T at days 7 and later, C2 is M3+T minus M0+T at days 3 to 6, and C3 is M5+T minus M4+T over all leads. D1 to D10 are descriptive contrasts of other arms, named where they appear; their intervals are at 95%, and the intervals of C1 to C3 are at 98.33%.
  • Rows. The rows are 53 Tuesday runs from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 at W1 to W3 (107,121 cases). The first run has no AIFS run, so 52 runs (105,016 cases, 1.9% of runs missing) remain. July to September 2025 train the weights, spread factors, and tables; October 2025 to June 2026 are scored: 71,294 kept rows per seed, 213,882 over three seeds. Intervals resample whole months and seeds 50,000 times; the farms are not resampled.
  • Scores, kept rows, with the offset table (points of capacity: days 0 to 2 / 3 to 6 / 7+ / all). M0 7.03 / 10.32 / 13.86 / 11.63. M1q 7.04 / 10.33 / 13.78 / 11.60. M2 (AIFS alone) 7.06 / 9.82 / 13.54 / 11.34. M3 6.91 / 9.83 / 13.60 / 11.34. M4 6.91 / 9.84 / 13.60 / 11.34. M5 6.99 / 9.79 / 13.54 / 11.31. M5b 6.99 / 9.87 / 13.49 / 11.31. M2 matches M3 within 0.15 points of capacity at every band. Most of the gain therefore comes from using the AIFS members instead of the ECMWF members, not from pooling the two.
  • Tail, kept rows, all leads (T: mean of the 0.01 and 0.99 pinball losses; then the 0.99 pinball loss). M0 0.451, 0.601. M1q 0.456, 0.612. M2 0.464, 0.630. M3 0.459, 0.618. M4 0.464, 0.629. M5 0.475, 0.644. No arm lowers either; AIFS raises the 0.99 pinball loss (M3 minus M0 +0.017). The curtailment use case therefore gets no gain from these arms.
  • Calibration, kept rows, all leads. Coverage of the 5% to 95% band is 92.3% to 92.8% for every arm (nominal 90%), and of the 1% to 99% band 97.5% to 97.9% (nominal 98%). The share of rows below the median is 45.3% for M0 and 46.7% for M3.
  • The offset table lowers the score, and AIFS removes part of the low bias on its own. Without the table M0 scores 12.06 and M3 11.58, a difference of -0.49 (-0.60 to -0.38, D7). The table lowers M0 by 0.43 (-0.61 to -0.23, D5). The hindcast table of experiment 259 scores 11.72 on M0, and the table fitted on the scored months beats it by 0.09 (-0.19 to +0.04, D6).
  • The fitted weights are noisy. M4's mean weight on AIFS (over the weights refitted in four months and three seeds) is about 0.5 at days 0 to 3, 0.66 to 0.70 at days 4 and 5, and 0.68 to 0.90 at days 10 to 13 (figure 3). Climatology gets weight (0.2 to 0.5) only at days 7 to 11 and day 14. Lead days 6 and 12 give AIFS weight 1.0 and 0.9. Each lead day has about 7,000 cases in the 53 runs, and a month's weights use only the earlier cases, so neighbouring days jump about. The gate's mean weights (0.27 ECMWF, 0.58 AIFS, 0.15 climatology) are smoother.
  • The linear pool is no better than quantile averaging. The linear pool M1p scores 0.03 worse than quantile averaging M1q (0.01 to 0.05, D3), and 0.06 worse at days 7 and later (0.03 to 0.09). On the tail score it does not beat quantile averaging (+0.01, -0.003 to +0.03 at days 7 and later).
  • The gate gives nothing over weights by lead. M5 beats M5b by 0.00 (-0.06 to +0.08, D1), so reading the spread and disagreement of the two ensembles gives nothing over reading the lead. At days 0 to 2 the gate's tail score is 0.072 worse than M4's (0.044 to 0.100). The gate minimises the continuous ranked probability score, which weights the tails little, which may explain the loss; we did not test this.
  • AIFS alone against ECMWF alone. M2 minus M0 is +0.05 at days 1 to 2 (-0.47 to +0.49), -0.49 at days 3 to 6 (-0.90 to -0.12), and -0.31 at days 7 and later (-0.63 to -0.02; D4). The prediction that AIFS alone scores worse at days 0 to 2 could not be tested at this width.
  • Run timing and AIFS version. Reading the AIFS run of 18 UTC the day before (M3prev) scores 0.09 worse than the 00 UTC run on the same rows (-0.01 to +0.20, D9), so the gain does not depend on the assumed 09:00 UTC availability. Before the AIFS version change of 2026-05-12, M3 scores 0.33 below M0 (12.13 against 12.46, kept rows, with table); from that date, 0.09 below (7.44 against 7.53). The later period has 8 runs, so the smaller gain is descriptive.
  • Stop rules. AIFS alone (M2) scores better than climatology at days 1 to 6, so no AIFS arm stopped.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Audit triggers. A result contradicting its prediction fired for C1, and the session tested the explanation (D10, above). The same trigger fired for C2's size, for which no explanation was tested, and for C3's tail result (the untested explanation above). A nested arm losing to the arm it contains fired mildly for the gate. The other triggers did not fire: no control failed, the median-error contrast was not computed, three farms are too few for a leave-one-out check, and no sister experiment has the same contrast. No Opus audit ran, and the maintainer may want one before a port.
  • Code review. One Sonnet review found no look-ahead leakage. It found that the pool read the ECMWF members by a different interpolation than M1q did, so M1q now reads them the same way; the scores moved by under 0.01. It also found, and we did not fix, three small effects: the weight statistics subsample each ensemble to 49 of 199 levels (so they see slightly less tail spread than the pool applied), arms with zero-weight sources add interpolation nodes in the pool, and the July to September rows are not spread before the first table is fitted. The three seeds differ only through the XGBoost boosters, since the gate's output layer starts at zero.
  • Circularity. The weights are fitted on the continuous ranked probability score before the spread factor and the offset table are, so the tables see forecasts the weights never saw. The alternative (fit the weights through the table) was not tried.
  • Scope. Three farms and 53 Tuesday runs; intervals describe these farms and months.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether AIFS still lowers the quantile score at days 3 to 6 on a second year of runs, and whether weights by lead band (days 0 to 2, 3 to 6, 7 and later) hold up better than weights by lead day.

docs.title: Can D8's forecast bands carry the uncertainty that an undetectable gas engine adds, by widening in the direction the engine pushes?
docs.text:
Widening the forecast band with residuals already seen narrows most of the gap at D8, but the gain from modelling a gas engine, beyond simple widening, is not shown. D8 is a primary substation of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED). D8's half-hourly power readings appear to include the output of a 6 MW gas engine, probably three units of about 2 MW each, which experiment 191, experiment 198, and experiment 199 could not detect. This experiment does not try to detect the engine. It asks whether the forecast's q05-to-q95 band, the range meant to hold 90% of readings, can carry the uncertainty that the engine adds. A residual is the actual reading minus the forecast median, and every arm uses only residuals known when the forecast is made. The unchanged forecast (arm 1) is experiment 191's reference, a generalised additive model with a Kalman filter on recent errors (GAM-K) and no price input. We tested five ways of widening its band. Arm 2 widens only the lower quantiles, arm 2b widens both sides, arm 3 is a mixture that assumes 0 to 3 engine units are running, arm 4 is arm 3 plus a price known only in hindsight, and a post hoc baseline adds the quantiles of the past 365 days of residuals to the reference median.

Widening the band raised the share of readings inside it from 0.42 (arm 1) to between 0.80 and 0.87 (arms 2b, 3, 4, and the baseline), and lowered the quantile score by 9% to 19% against arm 1. The quantile score is a score for the whole set of 11 forecast quantiles (smaller is better), and one point is 1% of the substation's effective capacity (0.1 MW at D8). By the pre-registered rule the verdict is not supported: no arm holds the share within 5 points of 0.90 in every quarter of the 12 months from 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, the July to September 2025 quarter has only weeks of residual history to learn from, and arm 2b raises the quantile score by 0.5% at D10, a substation with no engine. Arm 3 scores 2.5% better than arm 2b, yet the post hoc baseline, which has no engine in it, scores 0.4% better than arm 3, a difference smaller than its uncertainty. With the engine model forced on, arm 3 also fits an average 0.27 and 0.46 chance that an engine unit is running at D10 and D16, which have no engine. Arm 3's gain over arm 2b may therefore come from fitting the shape of D8's tails and not from an engine.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Rows. Experiment 191's stored reference forecast (arm a0, the GAM-K engine of experiment 152), fold_a_daily_gap_v1, seed 0, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, outside the hand-filtered events: 97,012 rows at D8, 96,370 at D10, and 91,754 at D16. The reference reproduces experiment 191's D8 scores (quantile score 10.95, mean absolute error 15.18 points, coverage 0.42).
  • Arm 1 is the reference.
  • Arm 2 recalibrates the lower quantiles q01 to q25, with a separate correction for each combination of four six-hour blocks of the day and four seasons.
  • Arm 2b widens both sides by the same method.
  • Arm 3 is the mixture over 0 to 3 running units of 19.7 points (1.97 MW). Where the visibility switch is off, arm 3 uses the arm 2b band. The switch turns the engine model on when 5% or more of the last 30 days' half-hours had a residual below -25 points (-2.5 MW), and off when the share falls below 3%.
  • Arm 4 is arm 3 plus two price flags known only in hindsight.
  • Post hoc baseline is the reference median plus the quantiles of the trailing 365 days of residuals, with no cells and no engine.
  • Schedule. Each arm refits every 7 daily forecast origins (the moment a forecast is made) on the trailing 365 days of residuals that were known at the block's first origin minus 6 hours. The reference's own refits are monthly, as in experiment 191.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Quantile score at D8 (points of capacity; smaller is better). Arm 1 10.95; arm 2 10.00; arm 2b 9.14; arm 3 8.91; arm 4 9.00; post hoc baseline 8.88. Against arm 1: arm 2 -8.7% (interval -13.5% to -4.9%), arm 2b -16.6% (-23.3% to -10.5%), arm 3 -18.6% (-24.7% to -12.9%), arm 4 -17.9% (-23.2% to -12.8%), post hoc baseline -18.9% (-25.4% to -13.1%). Every contrast keeps its sign when any one month is left out.
  • Coverage of q05 to q95 at D8, all 12 months. Arm 1 0.42; arm 2 0.67; arm 2b 0.87; arm 3 0.82; arm 4 0.80; post hoc baseline 0.85.

  • Coverage of q05 to q95 at D8 by quarter (2025Q3 excludes July; the target band is 0.85 to 0.95):

    Arm 2025Q3 2025Q4 2026Q1 2026Q2 Arm 1 0.29 0.48 0.40 0.52 Arm 2 0.57 0.80 0.61 0.75 Arm 2b 0.80 0.99 0.92 0.94 Arm 3 0.72 0.91 0.85 0.92 Arm 4 0.69 0.90 0.83 0.91 Post hoc baseline 0.76 0.91 0.89 0.96

With July included, 2025Q3 holds 0.30 (arm 1), 0.64 (arm 2b), and 0.60 (arm 3). - Tails at D8. Arm 1 puts 20.6% of readings below q01 and 30.8% below q05, and 26.9% above q95 and 16.1% above q99. Arm 2b gives 3.6%, 6.5%, 6.1%, and 3.4%. Arm 3 gives 4.2%, 9.2%, 8.7%, and 4.0%. Pinball loss at q05 falls from 4.12 (arm 1) to 2.46 (arm 2b) and 2.33 (arm 3), and at q95 from 4.31 to 2.70 and 2.56. - Leads at D8. Coverage of arm 3 is 0.80, 0.83, and 0.82 at 0 to 24, 24 to 72, and 72 to 168 hours, against 0.39, 0.43, and 0.43 for arm 1. The fit uses the shortest-lead residuals, and the coverage at long leads is not gated. - Mixture against widening both sides. Arm 3 minus arm 2b is -2.5% (interval -4.5% to -0.6%, and the 99.2% interval stays below zero), with every leave-one-month-out sign negative. The gain sits in October to December. The noise scale, a multiplier on the reference's spread, sits at the largest value the fit allows (2.0) in every block, and the fitted chance that at least one unit is running averages 0.75 at D8. - Post hoc baseline against the mixture. Arm 3 minus the baseline is +0.4% (interval -0.8% to +1.7%), so the engine mixture is no better than a band built from past residuals. - Placebo: quantile score against arm 1 at D10 and D16, with the upper end of the 95% interval in brackets. Arm 2: +0.26% (+0.82%) and -0.98% (+0.11%). Arm 2b, which arm 3 equals while its switch is off at both sites: +0.53% (+1.15%) and -0.89% (+0.14%). Arm 3 with the switch forced on: +0.75% (+1.11%) and +3.20% (+6.24%), with an average fitted chance that a unit is running of 0.27 and 0.46. Post hoc baseline: -0.59% (+2.53%) and +2.36% (+3.96%). The rule needed +0.1% or less and an upper end of +0.5% or less, so D10 fails for arms 2, 2b, and 3, and for the forced run, and D16 fails for the forced run and the baseline. - Visibility switch. At the pre-registered settings (on at 5%, off at 3%) the switch turns on at D8 on 2025-07-04 and never turns off, and it never turns on at D10 or D16. At on 7% and off 4% (post hoc) it also turns off at D8 on 2026-04-23, the only date in the scored year on which the engine's footprint drops out of D8's residuals. At on 3% and off 2% it behaves as at 5% and 3%. No NGED data change was tested against these dates. - Price. Arm 4 minus arm 3 is +0.95% (interval -0.1% to +2.1%). A price known only in hindsight does not help, so the missing price forecast does not limit arm 3 here. - Curtailment. studies.node_curtailment needs a bulk supply point forecast and its generators' forecasts, so no curtailment cost was computed. The stand-in Brier score of "reading below D8's 2nd percentile of the scored year" is 0.026 for arm 1 and rises to between 0.031 and 0.038 for the widened arms, so widening does not help that rare-event score. - Predictions. P1 (arm 2 coverage at most 0.80 in every quarter) failed narrowly, at 0.803 in 2025Q4. P2 (arm 2b within 5 points of 0.90 in three of four quarters) failed, with two of four. P3 (arm 3 in band in three quarters and within 1% of arm 2b) held on coverage and failed on score, at -2.5%. P4 (arm 4 lowers the score against arm 3 by under 1%) failed, because the score rose 0.95%. P5 (the switch turns off at D8 between 2026-03-01 and 2026-05-15) failed at the pre-registered settings, and held at D10 and D16. P6 (forced-on mixture below 0.05 at D10 and D16) failed, at 0.27 and 0.46.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Zero for arms 1, 2, and 2b. For arm 3, +0.14 points at D8, and 0.00 at D10 and D16 where the switch is off. For the forced run, +0.16 at D8, -0.04 at D10, and +0.15 at D16. For the post hoc baseline, -0.96, -0.54, and -0.26.
  • Mean-forecast error. Every arm keeps the reference's mean forecast, so the mean absolute error is 15.18 (D8), 5.54 (D10), and 4.70 (D16) points for all of them, and no contrast can disagree in direction with a mean-forecast contrast.
  • Audit triggers 1, 2, and 5 of the seven in the ml-experiment skill fired. A placebo failed (D10, and the forced run at D16). Five predictions failed (P1, P2, P4, P5, and P6), and P3 failed on its score clause. The forced D16 control moved the score by +0.089 points, more than the 0.083 half-width of its own interval.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet agent ran the audit, because the maintainer's brief bars Opus. The audit re-ran arms 2b and 3 after shifting every actual after 2026-01-10 by -40 points, and found every row at earlier origins bit-identical, so the as-of rule leaks nothing. It also reproduced the D8 numbers, found no bug in the distribution helpers, and found the post hoc baseline. The audit added the baseline arm and the noise-scale-limit caveat, and changed the interpretation of arm 3. It did not change the stored reference's median or the removal of hand-filtered events before fitting.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Fit to the year. The descriptive table that chose arm 2b and the switch thresholds came from the scored year, and no second year of D8 forecasts is stored, so every verdict is exploratory.
  • Little residual history in 2025Q3. The earliest D8 forecasts are stored from 2025-07-02, so the first quarter, and the cells of the first seasons, rest on weeks of residuals.
  • Next. Candidates for further work are to store D8 reference forecasts for an earlier period so the fit starts with residuals, and to carry plain two-sided widening (arm 2b) and the past-residual baseline forward after a check at substations with no engine. Do not extend the mixture, or add a neural network to predict its unit probabilities, until NGED can supply the engine's own output, because the mixture has not been shown to measure an engine.

docs.title: What was seen first
docs.text:
• The reference forecast is too narrow in both directions, not only downwards. Before writing this plan we tabulated experiment 191's stored reference forecasts at D8 by month, using for each valid time the forecast with the shortest lead. In the 12 months the reference's q05-to-q95 coverage runs from 0.27 to 0.51. Between 22% and 44% of readings lie above q95, and 25% to 47% lie below q05. The median distance from q50 to q05 is only 6.8 to 9.8 points (0.7 to 1.0 MW), against a mean absolute error of about 15 points. The share of readings more than 25 points (2.5 MW) below q50 falls from 5% to 16% in July to March to 3.5% to 5.8% in April to June 2026. At D10 and D16 the same table shows coverage of 0.77 to 0.97, so the narrow bands are particular to D8. The lower-tail-only widening that the maintainer's brief names as arm 2 therefore cannot be enough on its own, and we added arm 2b, which widens both sides, to separate "the band is too narrow" from "the band is too narrow in the direction the engine pushes".
  • The table of coverage and tail shares is descriptive, was read before the arms were fixed, and chose arm 2b and the switch thresholds. The switch thresholds (on at 5%, off at 3%) sit between the placebo sites' share of about 0.1% and D8's share of 5% to 16% in July to March, and the write-up reports the switch at two other settings as a sensitivity check.
  • Limits of the design. Arms 2 and 2b move only the tails, so a bias in the median that the engine causes stays in place. Arm 1 is the stored output of experiment 191, whose monthly refits use only data before each month and whose spread was fitted on tuning months, so the bands being widened carry no information from the scored year beyond the stored forecast itself. No D8 forecast before 2025-07-02 is stored, so the first weeks of the first quarter have no resolved residuals.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Forecasts. Experiment 191's stored arm a0 (gated variant, which equals the ungated variant at D8 because D8 has no pre-connection rows) at D8 (time_series_id 26), and at the placebo sites D10 (10) and D16 (18). Each row holds q01 to q99, mean, actual, lead_hours, and run. The files are data/ml-experiments/00191-*/work/preds/gated/scored_<site>.parquet.
  • Units. One point is 1% of the site's effective capacity, which is 0.1 MW at D8. The engine unit size of 1.97 MW is 19.7 points, and the "drop" threshold of -2.5 MW is -25 points. The placebo sites use the same constants in points, because the question there is whether the same algorithm with the same settings leaves a site without an engine alone.
  • Price columns for arm 4 only. The stored spread_positive and price_p75 flags in the same files. They are hindsight inputs and never run in a live service.

docs.title: The as-of rule
docs.text: A residual enters a fit at origin O only if its valid time is at or before O. For each valid time, the training row is the stored forecast with the shortest lead, so each valid time counts once. The residual is actual minus q50. Every fit is refitted every 7 origins and applied to the next 7 daily origins, and fit windows are the trailing 365 days of resolved valid times. A fit needs at least 28 days (1,300 rows) of resolved valid times. Before that, every arm equals arm 1. This is the cold start. D8's scored forecasts begin on 2025-07-02, and no earlier D8 forecast is stored, so the first weeks of the first quarter cannot be improved. The burn-in rule in the decision rule handles that quarter.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
1. Control. Arm 1, as above.
  2. Lower-tail widening (the maintainer's arm 2). For each row, the normalised shortfall is s = (q50 - actual) / (q50 - q05), with the denominator floored at 1 point. In each cell of hour-of-day block (00-06, 06-12, 12-18, and 18-24 UTC) by season (December-February, March-May, June-August, September-November), and with the cell falling back to the hour block alone, then to all rows, when it holds under 300 resolved rows, let S_tau be the empirical 1 - tau quantile of s for tau in {0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25}. The new lower quantile is q50 - max(r_tau, S_tau) * (q50 - q05), where r_tau is the reference's own ratio (q50 - q_tau) / (q50 - q05). The widening never narrows a band, and the upper quantiles and the mean are unchanged.
  3. Arm 2b (added by this plan). The same method applied to both sides: the upper quantiles q75, q90, q95, and q99 are recalibrated the same way from the normalised overshoot (actual - q50) / (q95 - q50).
  4. Mixture over running units (arm 3). The reading is modelled as the reference's distribution, with its spread multiplied by a noise scale c, shifted by delta - k * g, where k is the number of running units (0, 1, 2, or 3), g is 1.97 MW (19.7 points), and delta = g * E[k] is set per row so that the mixture's mean equals the reference's mean (the reference was trained on readings that include the engine). The reference distribution is the piecewise-linear cumulative distribution through its 11 quantiles, with an exponential tail beyond q01 and q99 whose density is continuous at those quantiles. The probability of k follows a multinomial logistic model of the hour block, the season, a weekend flag, and the share of half-hours in the 14 days before the origin with a residual below -25 points. The logistic model is fitted by expectation-maximisation on resolved residuals, with c on the grid {1, 1.5, 2} (capped at 2 so that one wide component cannot imitate the mixture) and the likelihood-maximising c kept, a ridge penalty of 1.0 on the logistic weights, and 30 expectation-maximisation iterations. The forecast quantiles come from inverting the mixture's cumulative distribution. A known-answer test on simulated readings (e00264_recovery.py) checks that the fit recovers the noise scale and the unit probabilities before the real run. The engine visibility switch turns on when the share of half-hours in the 30 days before the origin with a residual below -25 points reaches 5%, and turns off when the share falls below 3%. The mixture is fitted only on rows whose own origin had the switch on. Where the switch is off the forecast is arm 2b, not arm 1, because the upper-side miss is not caused by the engine.
  5. Arm 4. Arm 3 with spread_positive and price_p75 at the valid time added to the logistic model. These binary flags are a hindsight upper bound for the value of a price forecast, and they are coarser than the spark-spread level that the brief names.
  6. Placebo (arm 5). Arms 2, 2b, and 3 at D10 and D16, with the switch free, and with the switch forced on (a stress test that is the real placebo for the mixture, because the free switch is off at both sites).
  7. Not run. The small neural network for the mixture probabilities. The brief welcomes it only if it beats arm 3 by a pre-registered margin, and the plan sets none, so the write-up lists it under "what to try next".

The as-of rule has a reporting latency. A reading counts as known 6 hours after its valid time, because NGED's delivery lag is unknown. A fit at origin T therefore uses valid times at or before T minus 6 hours, and so do the 14-day and 30-day drop shares. A fit is frozen at its block's first origin, so residuals that resolve during the block do not enter its fit.

docs.title: Contrasts and scoring
docs.text:
• Contrasts. At D8: arms 2, 2b, 3, and 4 each minus arm 1 on the quantile score, arm 3 minus arm 2b, and arm 4 minus arm 3. Each is a mean paired difference with a 95% interval from 20,000 resamples of the 12 calendar months of the scored year, and a Bonferroni-corrected 99.2% interval (6 contrasts) beside it.
  • Cuts. All rows; the four quarters; q05-to-q95 coverage and the quantile score at leads 0 to 24, 24 to 72, and 72 to 168 hours (the fit uses shortest-lead residuals, so long-lead coverage is reported but not gated); the share of cells that fell back to the hour block, per quarter; months with the switch on and off; winter (November to March) evenings (16:00 to 20:00 UTC).
  • Tail table. Coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99 per arm.
  • Checks. The median forecast minus the mean forecast, per site and arm. The error of the mean forecast beside each quantile-score contrast. The leave-one-month-out sign of each D8 contrast. Which of the seven audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill fired.
  • Curtailment. studies.node_curtailment needs a bulk supply point's forecast and its generators' forecasts, and this experiment forecasts a single Primary, so the metric cannot be run. The stand-in is the Brier score of the event "the reading falls below D8's 2nd percentile of readings in the 12 months before 2025-07-02", computed from each arm's 11 quantiles by linear interpolation of its cumulative distribution. The write-up labels the Brier score a stand-in and does not call it a curtailment cost.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text: CPU only, 4 cores at most, thread caps of 1, inside systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue. The fits use the 17,000 shortest-lead rows per site and refit 52 times, so the whole run should take minutes. The three sites run in parallel workers.

docs.title: Stop rule
docs.text: Stop and report if arm 1, rebuilt from the stored files, does not reproduce experiment 191's D8 absolute scores (quantile score 10.95, mean absolute error 15.18 points, q05-to-q95 coverage 0.42) to within 0.01, or if any arm's row keys differ from arm 1's.

docs.title: Anonymisation
docs.text: The metered generator is named G2 only. No generator time series with a name or an identifier is published. D8, D10, and D16 are substations and may be named.

docs.title: Can an outside prior and a causal "engine visible" switch bring D8's widened forecast bands close to nominal coverage in every quarter, and do they help or harm the other Primaries?
docs.text:
An outside prior and an "engine visible" switch did not bring D8's forecast bands close to nominal coverage in every quarter, and no other Primary needs them. D8 is one of six primary substations with stored forecasts. Its readings appear to include a 6 MW gas engine of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) that appears in no measurement we hold and shows only as unexplained drops in D8's readings. A forecast band here is the range from the forecast's 5% quantile (q05) to its 95% quantile (q95), meant to hold 90% of readings. Experiment 264 widened D8's bands using residuals already seen (a residual is the reading minus the forecast median). That widening needs about a month of past residuals, so the first quarter of the scored year (July to September 2025) was poorly covered. We tested two additions. The first is a starting estimate of the widening taken from the other five Primaries' residuals, which D8's own residuals replace as they accrue. The second is a switch that returns the widening to the starting estimate once the share of half-hours more than 2.5 MW below the forecast median falls. Neither addition fixed the coverage. In the first quarter, the share of D8 readings inside q05 to q95 was 0.40 with the starting estimate, against 0.65 for widening from D8's own history only (the control). The switch turned off on 2026-04-23 as intended, but D8's lower tail stayed heavy (many readings far below the forecast), so coverage in 2026Q2 (April to June) fell from 0.94 for the control to 0.62 for the arm with the switch.

The verdict is not supported. Both pre-registered arms miss the rule at D8 (coverage within 5 points of 0.90 in every quarter, and a quantile score no more than 0.5% above the control's). The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 forecast quantiles, in points of effective capacity (a unit of 0.1 MW, which is 1% of D8's 10 MW effective capacity; 9.14 is in those units and lower is better). The control is 264's two-sided widening, rebuilt here, and it reproduces 264's D8 score of 9.14. A post hoc variant with faster shrinkage and a pool without D8 ties the control on score but covers less. Only D8 has a heavy lower tail, so there is no second Primary with a heavy lower tail on which to test whether the prior and switch generalise, and the outside prior raises the other Primaries' quantile score by up to 11%.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Rows. Experiment 191's stored reference forecast, fold_a_daily_gap_v1, seed 0, 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, leads 0.5 to 168 hours, outside the hand-filtered events: 97,012 rows at D8 and 84,137 to 97,046 at the others.
  • Schedule. Every arm refits every 7 daily origins on the trailing 365 days of residuals known 6 hours before the fit. The reference's own refits are monthly, as in experiment 191.
  • Arms. Control, arm 2 (prior, K = 2,000 rows), arm 2c (prior from an as-of pool), arm 3 (arm 2 plus the switch at on 7%, off 4%), arm 3 at on 5% and off 3%, and the post hoc arms 2p and 3p (K = 300 rows, pool without the heavy-tailed D8). The arm definitions are in Plan, below.
  • No neural network. The brief made it conditional on beating arm 2, and arm 2 does not pass.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• First quarter at D8 (July to September 2025, July included). Coverage is 0.30 for the unwidened reference, 0.65 for the control, 0.40 for arm 2, 0.40 for arm 2c, 0.39 for arm 3, 0.60 for arm 2p, and 0.58 for arm 3p. The prior is no help because the other five Primaries' lower-tail shares are 0.03 to 0.09 in that quarter against D8's 0.38.

  • Coverage of q05 to q95 at D8 by quarter (the target band is 0.85 to 0.95):

    Arm 2025Q3 2025Q4 2026Q1 2026Q2 Quantile score Unwidened reference 0.30 0.48 0.40 0.52 10.95 Control 0.65 0.99 0.92 0.94 9.14 Arm 2 0.40 0.69 0.55 0.72 9.89 Arm 3 0.39 0.69 0.55 0.62 10.03 Arm 2p (post hoc) 0.60 0.88 0.74 0.89 9.10 Arm 3p (post hoc) 0.58 0.88 0.74 0.76 9.20

  • Quantile score against the control at D8. Arm 2 +8.3% (95% interval +1.3% to +16.6%), arm 3 +9.7% (+2.9% to +17.7%), arm 2p -0.4% (-6.1% to +6.4%), arm 3p +0.7% (-4.9% to +7.3%). Arm 3 against arm 2: +1.4% (+0.2% to +3.2%), so the switch makes the score worse.

  • Tail calibration at D8 (share of readings below q01 and q05, above q95 and q99; nominal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99). Control 0.036, 0.065, 0.939, 0.966. Arm 2 0.130, 0.216, 0.808, 0.888. Arm 2p 0.056, 0.116, 0.892, 0.941. Pinball loss at q05: control 2.46, arm 2 3.16, arm 2p 2.45.
  • Census (share below the reference's q05, by quarter). D8 0.38, 0.33, 0.26, 0.26. Every other Primary has at most one quarter at or above 0.15 (D16 in 2026Q1, 0.17), so D8 alone has a heavy lower tail by the rule (0.15 or more in two quarters). The residual share below -2.5 MW is 0.04 to 0.12 at D8 and 0.00 to 0.02 elsewhere.
  • Visibility switch. At on 7% and off 4% the switch turns on at D8 on 2025-07-04 and off on 2026-04-23, and never changes state at the other five Primaries. At on 5% and off 3% it turns on and never off. The 7% and 4% settings come from 264's sweep, so this is a fit-to-the-year check.
  • Placebo Primaries, quantile score against the control (upper end of the 95% interval in brackets). Arm 2: D5 +3.4% (+6.0%), D10 +10.5% (+13.4%), D11 +5.5% (+6.8%), D14 +5.2% (+6.1%), D16 +1.1% (+3.0%). Arm 2p: D5 -0.1% (+0.2%), D10 +0.7% (+1.4%), D11 -0.1% (+0.3%), D14 -0.4% (-0.1%), D16 -0.5% (+0.1%). The rule needs +0.1% or less and an upper end of +0.5% or less, so arm 2 fails at all five and arm 2p fails at D10. Arms 3 and 2 equal each other at every Primary except D8, because the switch never changes state there.
  • Hindsight in the prior. Arm 2c (prior from an as-of pool) against arm 2: +0.1% at D8 (-0.4% to +0.6%), +1.1% at D10, and +0.9% to +1.3% at D5, D11, D14, and D16. The hindsight in the whole-year prior is not what limits arm 2.
  • Curtailment stand-in at D8. D8 never exports, so no export breach can occur and studies.node_curtailment cannot score it as an export node. The stand-in treats D8's demand as the flow under a limit of f times the July to September 2025 maximum (8.2, 6.8, and 4.6 MW for f of 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5), scores October 2025 to June 2026, and uses the q95 quantile in node-only mode. The energy proxy (pounds, at the module's headline price; the perfect forecast scores 9.0e4, 7.6e5, and 7.6e6) is: f 0.9: reference 1.8e6, control 5.3e6, arm 2p 2.3e6, arm 3p 2.2e6. f 0.75: 1.4e7, 1.6e7, 1.2e7, 1.1e7. f 0.5: 7.1e7, 4.1e7, 4.2e7, 4.3e7. No arm is best at every limit, and the stand-in scores the upper band, which the engine does not threaten, so it does not test the claim of this experiment.
  • Predictions. P1 failed (first-quarter coverage 0.40 for arm 2, below the control's 0.65). P2 failed (+8.3%). P3 held (the switch turns off once, on 2026-04-23, and never changes state elsewhere). P4 failed (2026Q2 coverage 0.62, and arm 3 scores 1.4% worse than arm 2). P5 failed (only D8 is heavy). P6 failed (arm 2 raises the score at all five placebos).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Zero at every Primary for the control and arm 2p (the arms keep the reference's median and mean).
  • Mean-forecast error. Every arm keeps the reference's mean forecast, so the mean absolute error is identical across arms (D8 15.18, D10 5.54 points) and no contrast can disagree with a mean-forecast contrast.
  • Triggers. The placebo trigger fired (the placebo rule failed for arm 2 at five Primaries and for arm 2p at D10), the contradicted-prediction trigger fired (five of six predictions failed). The leave-one-site-out style trigger fired too: leaving out one month flips the sign of the arm 2p and arm 3p contrasts with the control at D8, whose intervals span zero, so the verdict does not rest on arms 2p or 3p.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet agent (the maintainer's brief bars Opus) re-derived the D8 and D10 scores and coverage from the stored predictions, and they agree. It shifted D8's actuals by -40 points after 2026-01-10 and found every row at earlier origins identical for the control, arms 2, 3, and 2c, so the own-history fits are causal, and the 6-hour latency holds. It found no bug. Triaged findings, all accepted and recorded as caveats: the whole-year prior leaks the other Primaries' future (small: +0.1% at D8, +1.1% at D10 for the as-of pool); the control applies no widening before 2025-08-06 while arms 2 and 3 apply the prior from day 1; the shrinkage weight never exceeds about 0.35 at K = 2,000, so the prior dominates, which drives arm 2's D8 failure; and arms 2p and 3p were chosen after seeing arm 2's score, so they are exploratory.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Fit to the year. The 7% and 4% switch settings and the census rule use the scored year, and there is no second year of D8 forecasts.
  • The prior uses future residuals. It takes the whole scored year of the other Primaries, which a live service would not have, and the control skips widening for its first 28 days, so July is not like for like.
  • Arms 2p and 3p are post hoc. K = 300 and the pool without D8 were chosen after arm 2 failed.
  • Next. Store D8 reference forecasts for an earlier period so the first quarter starts with residuals, or ask NGED for the engine's own output. The small neural network for the widening factor was not run, because the condition for it (arm 2 passing) was not met.

docs.title: Plan (as pre-registered)
docs.text: The question: can plain as-of widening be made close to nominal in every quarter, including the first quarter with no history, and does it generalise to other Primaries with price-driven generation? Pass rules, judged for a candidate arm at D8: (a) coverage in [0.85, 0.95] in every quarter; (b) quantile score at most 0.5% above the control's; (c) at each non-heavy Primary, the score against the control rises by at most +0.1% (point) and +0.5% (95% upper end).

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms use the same rows as 264 and the same as-of rule: a residual enters a fit only if its valid time is at least 6 hours before the fit, fits repeat every 7 daily origins, and the window is the trailing 365 days.

  1. Control. 264's arm 2b: widen both tails by cell quantiles (six-hour block by season) of the ratio of the residual to the band's half-width, from the site's own window, applied from 28 days of history. Reproduced here, and checked against 264's printed D8 quantile score of 9.14.

  2. Arm 2, prior. The same cells, but each cell's quantile is the weighted mean w * own + (1 - w) * prior with w = n / (n + K), where n is the cell's count of own resolved rows and K = 2,000 rows (about 6 weeks). With no own rows the table is the prior, so the widening works from the first origin. The prior is the pooled cell quantiles of the ratios of the five Primaries other than the one being widened (D8's pool is D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, and each other Primary's pool includes D8), over the whole scored year. This uses residuals from after the fit date, which a live service would not have. Arm 2c is the same with the pool restricted as-of to the fit window (falling back to the whole-year prior until 28 days exist), which shows how much the hindsight in the prior matters.

  3. Arm 3, visibility switch. Arm 2, but the own rows in the fit window are only those taken while the switch had the same state as at the origin. The switch is on when 7% or more of the last 30 days' resolved half-hours had a residual below -25 points (-2.5 MW), and off when the share falls below 4% (hysteresis). When the switch is off and the site has few off-state rows, the widening is the prior, which is the "normal" widening. The 7% and 4% settings come from 264's sweep, which found that 5% and 3% never turn off, so the 7% and 4% settings are post hoc. The 5% and 3% settings are run as a sensitivity check. Flip dates are reported at both.

  4. Census, then application. For all six Primaries with stored forecasts the census prints, by quarter, the share of readings below the reference's q05, the share above q95, and the share of residuals below -25 points. A site has a heavy lower tail when the share below q05 is 0.15 or more in at least two of the four quarters (nominal 0.05). Arms 2 and 3 are run at every site, and a site that is not heavy is a placebo, which must not worsen under rule (c). The other heavy sites, if any, are scored by rules (a) and (b).

  5. Curtailment cost at D8. D8 never exports (its readings run from 0 to 99 points, never negative), so the export breach that studies.node_curtailment scores cannot occur at D8. The stand-in treats D8's demand as the flow that must stay under a limit. The limit is f times the maximum reading in the first quarter (July to September 2025), for f of 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5. The score runs on October 2025 to June 2026 in node-only mode, with 10 MW effective capacity (0.1 MW per point) and the breach ratio 20, and the manual-heuristic arm is not computed.
