docs.title: Gain by group
docs.text:
Gain of A at 168 to 240 hours, with the 95% interval. The groups use realised temperature and sunshine, so they overstate what a forecaster could know in advance.

  • Cold winter nights (2,384 rows, daily temperature below 2 C, local 18:00 to 07:00, November to March): 55.1% over the heuristic (50.4 to 68.1) and 56.4% over climatology (53.2 to 65.4).
  • Winter, November to March (96,315 rows): 15.7% (-0.3 to 29.1) and 21.4% (12.3 to 29.7).
  • Sunny daylight (37,612 rows): -5.2% (-15.3 to 2.7) and -2.4% (-17.4 to 10.2).
  • April to October (140,594 rows): -0.7% over the heuristic and 4.0% over climatology (no interval computed).

docs.title: Robustness checks and audit
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus the mean of the 11 quantiles, per site, in points: D10 -0.53, D9 -0.29, D11 -0.02, D14 +0.16, D16 +0.15, D5 +0.15.
  • Sites. The gain at 168 to 240 hours over the heuristic is +24% at D11, +21% at D14, +2.9% at D10, +1.6% at D9, -3.2% at D16, and -3.8% at D5. Leaving D11 out cuts the gain at 216 to 240 hours from 5.3% to 1.8%, and leaving D14 out cuts it to 2.8%.
  • Trigger 2 fired (a result contradicts its own prediction: the chain beats climatology at 216 to 240 hours instead of tying it). The explanation was tested. The ensemble temperature forecast's anomaly correlation with ERA5 is 0.97 at 0 to 24 hours, 0.82 at 144 to 168, 0.76 at 168 to 192, 0.71 at 192 to 216, and 0.67 at 216 to 240. The gain over climatology is 21% in November to March and 4% in April to October.
  • Trigger 4 fired (leaving one site out changes a verdict): leaving D11 or D14 out takes the gain over the heuristic below the 5% threshold.
  • Triggers 3, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire. Trigger 3 is a quantile-score contrast and a median-error contrast pointing in different directions, trigger 5 a nested arm beating the arm containing it, trigger 6 an interval more than twice or less than half the width of a sister experiment's, and trigger 7 a later design depending on an unreplicated result. For trigger 6, the reproduction of experiment 251's contrast gives -0.818 with interval -1.087 to -0.572, against its -0.818 with -1.080 to -0.574.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet auditor re-derived the per-band scores, gains, and intervals from the raw chain files and experiment 87's stored benchmarks. Scores matched to 3 decimals, gains to 0.1 percentage points, and interval ends to 0.3 percentage points (a different random seed). It found no leakage (lead equals valid time minus origin on all 245,463 chain rows beyond 168 hours, before the row filters, and the day-10 and day-1 errors at one valid time correlate at 0.64), a heuristic whose score and band width are flat in lead, and no site scoring over twice the median. It confirmed that D11 and D14 carry the gain over the heuristic. It did not re-derive the sunny- daylight result. Triage: all findings accepted; its two minor notes are recorded here (48 rows of experiment 87's actual are NaN, so scoring uses the chain's actual, and report.json's two actual_gap entries are NaN for that reason).

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Refit H and S to leads of 168 to 240 hours, or extend BG2, to remove the departure from the default's full recipe.
  • Fit the cold-day widening of fix O on leads beyond 168 hours; this run reuses its multipliers.
  • Look at why D5 and D16 lose to the heuristic beyond 168 hours.

docs.title: Does giving the mixture-density head of the metered solar-farm forecast more inputs, especially the forecast lead, lower its quantile score?
docs.text:
Giving the mixture-density head of the solar-farm forecast more inputs does not lower its quantile score at any lead from 1 to 10 days. It lowers only the 0.99 pinball loss (the loss on the upper tail), by about 5% at days 3 to 7. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters six solar farms, labelled A to F. Metered solar farms research default 1 (experiment 300, scored to 10 days by experiment 310) starts from a physical model of the farm's output (the "plant") and corrects the plant's 11 quantiles with a three-component mixture density network (the "head"). We refitted that head with more inputs: the lead in whole days, the hour of day and day of year as sine and cosine pairs, and the ensemble's spread of shortwave irradiance. We also trained one head for all six lead bands instead of one head per band, and added the two arms that experiment 313 motivates: the network with no plant, and the same network given the plant forecast as a column. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantiles, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of the farm's capacity), and lower is better. "Own history" means the head trains on the farm's earlier months, and "zero history" means it trains on the other five farms only.

The verdict is partly supported, and nothing is adopted. The extra inputs fail the research default's minimum gain of 0.02 points on the quantile score at every band, so the head of research default 1 stays as it is. The gain that appears is on the 0.99 pinball loss, which replicates in both halves of the scored year and in zero history. Scores are at leads of 12 to 252 hours (days 1 to 10), with quarterly refits.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. "default" is experiment 310's head (plant forecast, plant spread, availability ratio, lagged power and its missing flag, clear-sky index, lead hours). "lead" adds the lead in whole days. "full" adds the lead in whole days, the hour-of-day and day-of-year sine and cosine pairs, and the irradiance spread (cloud cover itself is not stored, and the clear-sky index was already an input). "full_pooled" and "default_pooled" train one head on all six bands. "full_shuffled" shuffles the added columns (control), and "full_nolag" drops lagged power and the availability ratio (the named control for the previous day's plant error, which experiment 310 found adds nothing). "pure_pooled" and "pure_lead_pooled" are the network with experiment 313's no-plant inputs, pooled, without and with the lead day. "pure_plant" is the no-plant inputs plus the plant forecast as a column, per band.
  • Absolute scores, own history (default; climatology; manual_heuristic). 5.36 (8.64; 8.69) at day 1, 6.08 (8.64; 8.68) at day 3, 7.35 (8.64; 8.73) at days 6 to 7, and 7.75 (8.64; 8.83) at days 8 to
  • Zero-history default scores 5.53 points at day 1 and 7.91 points at days 8 to 10. Experiment 313's pure network scores 5.34 and 8.03.
  • C1, lead minus default, quantile score (own history). +0.002 at day 1 to -0.006 at days 8 to 10; every interval lies within ±0.03 points. The 0.99 pinball loss changes by at most 0.002. Prediction P1 (a gain of 0.02 points beyond 36 hours) fails.
  • C2, full minus default, quantile score (own history). +0.005 (-0.094 to +0.073) at day 1, +0.023 at day 3, +0.037 at days 4 to 5, +0.125 (-0.091 to +0.422) at days 6 to 7, and +0.102 at days 8 to 10. No interval excludes zero, and the point estimates are above the no-harm tolerance of 0.02 points from day 3. The second half-year drives the rise (+0.20 at days 6 to 7); the first half- year is flat. In zero history the change is -0.024 to +0.082.
  • C2, 0.99 pinball loss (own history). -4.8% (-0.016 points, interval -0.030 to -0.006) at day 3, -5.6% at days 4 to 5, -5.3% at days 6 to 7, and -2.6% (interval includes zero) at days 8 to 10; -1.4% and -2.4% at days 1 and 2 (intervals include zero). The change replicates: in the first half-year it is -6.2% to -8.1% at days 3 to 7, and in the second half-year -2.9% to -4.2% at days 1 to 7. In zero history it is -2.9% to -4.7% at every band. Prediction P2 (3% or more, pooled over days 3 to 10) holds at -4.6%.
  • C3, one head for all leads (own history). full_pooled minus full: -0.024 to -0.001 points at days 1 to 3 and days 8 to 10, -0.035 (-0.083 to +0.014) at days 6 to 7; no interval excludes zero. default_pooled minus default is -0.015 at day 1 and -0.005 at days 8 to 10. full_pooled minus default lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by 5.0% to 6.3% at days 2 to 7 and 3.0% at days 8 to 10. Pooling alone does nothing for the plant-based head.
  • C4/C5, the network with no plant. pure_pooled minus experiment 313's per-band pure_mdn: -0.04% at day 1 and -3.0% (-0.24 points, interval -0.69 to -0.03) at days 8 to 10, so one head for all leads closes most of experiment 313's gap: pure_pooled scores 0.4% above the default at days 8 to 10 and 0.4% below it at day 1. Adding the lead day to pure_pooled (pure_lead_pooled minus pure_pooled) makes the score worse by 0.008 to 0.033 points (days 8 to 10 interval +0.003 to +0.063). Prediction P5 (a gap under 1.5% at days 8 to 10) holds, at 0.85% (pure_lead_pooled against the default), but pooling did the work and the lead day did not.
  • C6, the plant forecast as a column of the no-plant network (pure_plant). pure_plant differs from experiment 313's pure network by -0.4% to +0.2% at every band (intervals include zero), so the plant column adds nothing measurable to the network. Against the default it scores 0.244 points (3.1%) worse at days 8 to 10 (interval includes zero) and 0.012 better at day 1. Prediction P6 holds only for the first comparison; the comparison with the default mixes in a different parametrisation (the default models the residual from the plant, pure_plant models the output).
  • Controls. full_shuffled minus default is +0.009 at day 1 and -0.003 at days 8 to 10 (intervals within ±0.04), so P3 holds and the 0.99 gain comes from the added inputs. full_nolag minus full is +0.006 and +0.007 points at days 1 and 8 to 10 (intervals include zero), so the previous day's plant error adds nothing again.
  • Lower tail (P4). The share of actual values below the 0.01 quantile is 0.0355 for the default at day 1 and 0.0329 at days 8 to 10; 0.0371 and 0.0339 for full; 0.0358 and 0.0343 for full_pooled; 0.0343 and 0.0328 for pure_pooled. Against a nominal 0.01 every arm is 3.3 to 3.7 times too high, and no arm moves it by more than 0.2 points, so P4 fails. Coverage of the 0.99 quantile is 0.982 to 0.989 for every arm.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, own history, farms pooled (points of capacity). Default +0.40 at day 1 and +0.30 at days 8 to 10; full +0.36 and +0.51; full_pooled +0.40 and +0.31. Per farm at day 1 (default): A -0.10, B +0.22, C +0.12, D +0.61, E +1.15, F +0.41.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast. full minus default on the absolute error of the mean forecast is -0.015 at day 1 and +0.113 at days 6 to 7 (intervals include zero), the same direction as the quantile score; the 0.99 gain has no counterpart because it concerns a tail the mean does not see.
  • Audit triggers fired: 2 and 5. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction): P1 and P4 failed. We tested the explanation that the head already holds the lead in hours (C1, and pure_lead_pooled getting worse). Trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm containing it): default beats full by 0.10 to 0.13 points at days 6 to 10, inside the interval's half-width (about 0.25 points). A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the quantile score, the 0.99 pinball loss, and the 0.01 coverage from the raw predictions and found every contrast within 0.0013 points of the stored value (stored absolute scores run 0.002 to 0.003 points above the agent's, an unexplained gap that affects both arms of a contrast alike), no duplicate keys, no missing values, and identical row counts across arms. Bands d1, d2, and d4 to 5, the zero-history setting, and the interval limits were not re-derived. Trigger 4 did not fire: dropping any one farm leaves the 0.99 change of full negative at days 3 to 10 (-0.0035 to -0.023). Triggers 1 (a failed control), 3 (the mean-forecast error disagrees), 6 (an interval much wider or narrower than a sister experiment's), and 7 (a later design depends on this result) did not fire.

docs.title: Method and schedule
docs.text:
• Schedule. Quarterly refits on all earlier months (screening schedule), so absolute scores could shift slightly under weekly refits, and the contrasts were not tested for dependence on the schedule. The head is the mixture network of experiment 310 (copied from its fitter), with five seeds averaged in own history and three in zero history. The default reproduces experiment 310's head (-0.14%, from two extra seeds).
  • Rows. Experiment 310's scored-year rows (2025-09 to 2026-08, farms A to F, 12 to 252 hours), common to every arm and to the floors; intervals resample the 12 scored months at 99.17% (Bonferroni, six planned contrasts per band and setting). The half-year intervals resample six months and are coarse. The pooled arms and the arms lead, full_shuffled, full_nolag, and pure_plant ran in own history only.
  • Reuse. The scripts import experiment 310's folder; the no-plant columns are copied from experiment 313.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Leads. The scored range is 12 to 252 hours (days 1 to 10), which covers NGED's horizon.
  • The blend was not rescored. The head is one of three blend members, so a head gain of 0.05 points or more at the 0.99 quantile may shrink in the blend.
  • Experiment 313's caveats stand. Experiment 313's intervals (-2.4% to +1.0% at day 1, -1.3% to +10.4% at days 8 to 10) show no detectable difference, not equivalence. Its zero-history test uses six farms in one region with one fleet-shape plant, so it cannot show whether a physical plant transfers better to a farm with a different tilt or climate. The plant also keeps value that is not accuracy: explainable parameters, a farm card, and a ceiling check.
  • Lead day is redundant. lead_day is a step function of lead_hours, which every arm already holds, so C1 and pure_lead_pooled test only a coarser copy; the effect of an hour-of-lead feature cannot be separated here.
  • Pooled arms confound pooling with training budget. A pooled head sees about six times the rows at the same number of epochs, so full_pooled and pure_pooled also take more gradient steps.
  • Next. The lower tail needs a different remedy, such as a dedicated tail head or recalibration of the 0.01 quantile on the farm's own history; the 0.99 gain should be retested inside the blend.

docs.title: Does extending the two-number solar summary, or blending with the manual heuristic, improve Primary demand research default 1 at 7 to 10 days?
Take-home message
docs.text: Using the spread of the 51 weather-forecast members in the solar term of the demand forecast still helps at 7 to 10 days, and a blend with the manual heuristic helps more but worsens cold winter nights. Primary demand research default 1 is the demand forecast for the six Primary substations that we use for research. Extending its two-number solar summary (the mean and the standard deviation of the 51 weather-forecast members' solar responses, each response being the change in the forecast when that member's sunshine replaces the average member's) from 168 to 240 hours ahead lowers the quantile score by 2.0% and by 6.6% on sunny daylight half-hours. The default had scored 5.2% worse than the manual heuristic on those half-hours. Blending the median of the convex chain (the additive model with a Kalman filter on recent errors) with the manual heuristic's median lowers the quantile score by 4.5%, and the blend's score is 11% lower than the heuristic's. The blend scores 0.076 points of capacity worse on cold winter nights, past the family's tolerance of 0.05 points, so only the solar summary is adopted, as Primary demand research default 2. The verdict is partly supported: the solar summary held on every pre-registered part, and the blend held on all but its no-harm bound and the share of its gain in April to October. A blend that leaves cold winter nights alone is an option for a later experiment.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text: Experiment 317 showed two weak spots of Primary demand research default 1 at 168 to 240 hours: sunny daylight half-hours, and April to October, where the convex chain beats climatology (a table of typical demand by month and time of day) by only 4%. We tested one fix for each, as two pre-registered arms against the default. Arm x1 extends the two-number solar summary S of experiments 193 and 202 from 168 to 240 hours. Arm x2 blends the convex chain's median with the median of NGED's manual heuristic (an ensemble of demand at the same time of day on earlier weeks), with a weight fitted per 24-hour lead band and season. Below 168 hours both arms equal the default. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity (one point is 1% of a substation's capacity; smaller is better). Cold winter nights are November to March half-hours after dark on days the ensemble forecast to be cold, and sunny daylight half-hours are daylight half-hours with a high clear-sky index. The convex chain is the additive model with a Kalman filter on recent errors that experiment 317 extended to 240 hours. D5 to D16 are anonymised Primary substations. Every interval resamples the 12 months of forecast date.

docs.title: Results at 168 to 240 hours
docs.text:
Lead range: 0.5 to 240 hours, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, six Primaries, 798,116 rows (236,909 of them past 168 hours). Each row is one half-hour at one Primary for one forecast origin. Retraining: monthly refits of the arms' factors and weights on the trailing 12 months of completed runs (experiment 202's rule); the convex chain is experiment 317's stored forecasts. Whether either contrast depends on that schedule was not tested.

  • Absolute scores, 168 to 240 hours. Default 3.215, x1 3.152, x2 3.071, manual heuristic 3.456, climatology 3.663. At 0.5 to 240 hours: 2.768, 2.749, 2.725, 3.414, and 3.664.
  • x1 minus default. -0.064 points (2.0%) at 168 to 240 hours, 99.5% interval -0.095 to -0.037; -0.019 points at 0.5 to 240 hours, 99.5% interval -0.028 to -0.011. Each 24-hour band's 99.5% interval is wholly below zero (168 to 192 hours: -0.089 to -0.030).
  • x2 minus default. -0.145 points (4.5%) at 168 to 240 hours, 99.5% interval -0.251 to -0.056 (by band: -0.252 to -0.043, -0.249 to -0.043, and -0.261 to -0.073); -0.043 points at 0.5 to 240 hours. The gain over the manual heuristic is 12.4%, 11.2%, and 9.9% in the three bands, each 95% interval wholly below zero.
  • Gain by group. Sunny daylight: x1 6.6% (99.5% interval -0.678 to -0.169 points), x2 6.5% (-0.703 to +0.007). The chain's deficit against the heuristic turns into x1 +1.7% and x2 +1.6%, both with 95% intervals that include zero (x1 -8.4% to 10.4%). Cold winter nights: x1 0.0 points (it changes daylight rows only), x2 -2.6% (+0.076 points, one-sided 95% upper bound +0.189). November to March: x1 2.1%, x2 3.9%. April to October: x1 1.9%, x2 5.0%.
  • Where x2's gain sits. 63% of x2's gain at 168 to 240 hours is in April to October, under the pre-registered 70%.
  • No-harm bounds (one-sided 95% upper bound of the harm, tolerance in brackets). x1 passes every one at 0.5 to 240 and 168 to 240 hours: pooled -0.047 (0.02), sunny-daylight q99 pinball +0.039 (0.05), cold winter nights 0.0 (0.05), twCRPS gain 1.2% or better. x2 fails cold winter nights at 168 to 240 hours (+0.189 against 0.05); at 0.5 to 240 hours its bound is +0.037, inside the tolerance.
  • Leave one Primary out, 168 to 240 hours. The sign of every contrast holds when any one of the six Primaries is left out (x1 -0.057 to -0.071, x2 -0.132 to -0.157 points). Per Primary, x1 ranges from -0.026 (D11) to -0.098 (D5).
  • Replicate year (2024-25). Fitted on the odd months, applied to the even months of 2024-25 (155,202 rows past 168 hours): x1 -0.034 points (95% interval -0.050 to -0.017), x2 -0.079 points (-0.143 to -0.017), the same sign as the scored year.
  • Tails and coverage, 216 to 240 hours. Share of readings inside the 5% to 95% band: default 87.3%, x1 88.9%, x2 89.0% (nominal 90%). Share below q01: 2.9%, 2.1%, 2.2% (nominal 1%).
  • Benchmark rows and gates. Below 168 hours the default scores 2.579 (experiment 251's 2.579) and x1 and x2 equal it to 0.0. The default at 168 to 240 hours equals experiment 317 (3.177, 3.228, 3.242 by band). The rebuilt heuristic median differs from experiment 87's stored median by 0.002 points on average (maximum 2.45 over 245,343 rows). The member-response code reproduces experiment 184's stored responses to 0.0 on 1,344 rows of two Primaries below 168 hours. BG2 is not scored past 168 hours.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site (points, mean of the 11 quantiles). D5 +0.06, D9 -0.27, D10 -0.48, D11 -0.02, D14 +0.18, D16 +0.18 for the default and x2 (x2 shifts all quantiles together); x1 changes D10 to -0.43 and D9 to -0.24.
  • Mean absolute error of the median forecast at 168 to 240 hours. Default 5.474, x1 5.460, x2 5.225, manual heuristic 6.122, climatology 6.555. Both arms move in the same direction as the quantile score.
  • Placebo for x1. Setting every member response to zero and refitting the offsets (post hoc control) changes the score by -0.003 points (95% interval -0.007 to +0.001); x1 beats the placebo by 0.061 points (interval -0.080 to -0.044), so the gain comes from the member information.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 of the audit rule (a result contradicts its own prediction) fired for one sub-prediction, the share of x2's gain in April to October (63% against 70%). No other trigger fired. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the numbers from the stored forecasts: all five checks agreed (pooled scores, leakage in the fits, the rebuilt heuristic, the cold-night sign, and quantile ordering) (report in the private briefs/e319_audit_report.md). Pooled scores matched to 0.001 points; the fits never see rows whose run ends after the month they are applied to; the rebuilt heuristic uses only readings at least 3.5 hours before the origin; the quantiles are monotone. One nuance: the cold-winter-night harm of x2 (+0.076 points) rests on 3 month blocks. It holds for the stored flag that marks half-hours the ensemble forecast to be cold, and not for a proxy of winter nights with demand of winter nights with demand below the monthly median, where x2 helps (-0.151 points). Whether the harm is a property of cold nights or of that flag was not resolved, and the no-harm verdict for x2 uses the stored flag, as the family rule does.
  • Adoption conditions for x1. Gain (99.5% interval wholly below zero, point estimate above the minimum gain of 0); no harm (above); replication (above); controls (placebo above, audit below); serving: the change reuses the ensemble member responses that Primary demand research default 1 already computes to 168 hours, and needs no inputs beyond what exists at forecast time. x2 fails the no-harm condition and stays a candidate.
  • Pre-registered predictions. P1 holds on all four parts (6.6% on sunny daylight against 3%; within 2% of the heuristic; pooled 2.0% against 1%; equal below 168 hours). P2 holds on three of four parts (4.5% against 2%; 9.9% to 12.4% against 7% with intervals above zero; not the 70% share in April to October). P3 was not tested, because the combination runs only if both arms pass; the sum of the two gains is 6.5%.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• An option: a blend that excludes cold winter nights from its weight, or gives them a separate weight, tested against Primary demand research default 2.
  • Sunny daylight half-hours remain the weakest group at 168 to 240 hours (4.74 points against the heuristic's 4.82): the graft of a sunshine response, tried in experiment 316 on a few April to June weeks, replicated on more weeks.
  • An option: narrowing the forecast bands at night, which experiment 316 found gave 63% of the gain of its larger band change.
  • A small neural layer for the heuristic's weight as a function of the forecast temperature (it would have to beat the convex blend on cold winter nights).

docs.title: Code and data
docs.text: Scripts in ml-experiments/00319-primary-demand-default-1-solar-summary-and-heuristic-blend-at-7-to-10-days/: e00319_members.py calls experiment 184's member code with the 480-half-hour window of experiment 317; e00319_arms.py builds x1 and x2 with experiment 202's arm code; e00319_score.py scores them with experiment 317's scoring helpers and e00319_charts.py draws the figures. The stored forecasts of the two arms are the private files work/arms/scored_long_lead.parquet and replicate_long_lead.parquet.

docs.title: Pre-registered plan (written before any score was read)
docs.text:
Lead range of every figure: 0.5 to 240 hours (NGED's 1 to 10 days). Schedule: monthly refits as in experiment 202; the default's chain is experiment 317's stored forecasts.

  • x1. Member-level solar responses are built past 168 hours by running experiment 184's member code with the 480-half-hour forecast window of experiment 317. Offset factor f and spread factor s are fitted per 24-hour lead band (168 to 192, 192 to 216, 216 to 240 hours) on the trailing 12 months whose runs had completed before each scored month (experiment 202's rolling rule), and the daylight bands are rebuilt as in experiment 193.
  • x2. The heuristic is rebuilt for 2024-07 onward from the feature cache with the recipe of experiment 161 (weekly lags 1 to 6 and annual lags 49 to 55 weeks, 3.5-hour telemetry delay), and gated against experiment 87's stored heuristic on the scored year. The chain's weight is fitted per 24-hour lead band and season group by minimising pinball loss on the same trailing-12-month completed-history rule, and shifts all 11 quantiles by the change in the median.
  • Stop rules. The gate fails, or a member response cannot be built past 168 hours at one of the six Primaries.

docs.title: Can a blend with the manual heuristic that leaves cold winter nights alone, or a night band-width correction, improve Primary demand research default 2 at 0.5 to 240 hours?
Take-home message
docs.text:
The blend with the manual heuristic still gains about 4% at 7 to 10 days, but its harm on the coldest winter nights cannot be removed by switching it off where the weather forecast predicts a cold night, and a night band-width correction helps one substation only. Primary demand research default 2 is our research demand forecast for six Primary substations (anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), up to 10 days ahead. It is a convex additive model (the convex chain) with a Kalman filter on recent errors, and it gives 11 quantiles per half-hour. Experiment 319 found that blending the default's median with the manual heuristic's median lowers the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantiles, in points of the substation's effective capacity) by 4.5% at 168 to 240 hours but scores 0.076 points worse on cold winter nights. Here, switching the blend off on half-hours that the ECMWF ensemble weather forecast calls cold winter nights (B1) keeps the whole gain (-0.136 points, 4.3%, the same as the blend without the rule on the same base) and cuts the harm only to +0.048 points, because at 7 to 10 days the forecast temperature rule flags only 31% to 52% of the realised cold winter nights, depending on the lead band, and the unflagged ones carry the harm. A blend weight that varies smoothly with the forecast temperature (B2) gains slightly more (-0.146 points) and harms cold nights by +0.075 points. A width multiplier on the night bands (N) lowers D10's score by 0.117 points (0.246 on night half-hours) and moves the other five Primaries by +0.008 points on average.

Verdict: partly supported. B1 and B2 remain candidates, and no arm is adopted.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text: We tested three pre-registered changes against Primary demand research default 2 (experiment 319's solar summary to 240 hours). B1 and B2 act at 168 to 240 hours. B1 uses experiment 319's blend weights but sets the chain weight to 1 on forecast cold winter nights (November to March, after dark, local 18:00 to 07:00, ensemble-mean 24-hour temperature at the forecast time (09:00 UTC) below 2 °C). B2 replaces the weight table by a logistic function of the same temperature, fitted per lead band and per daylight or night. N multiplies every quantile's offset from the median by a factor between 0.6 and 1.2, fitted per Primary and per night or day block on the previous 90 days, at 0.5 to 240 hours. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity (smaller is better). Cold winter nights are experiment 317's realised group: 2,384 half-hours at 168 to 240 hours. The weights and factors are fitted on the convex chain's rows and applied to the default's quantiles. The six Primaries are anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Lead range: 0.5 to 240 hours (1 to 10 days). B1 and B2 equal the default below 168 hours. Rows: six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, origin 09:00 UTC, rows outside the hand-filtered events (798,116 rows, 236,909 at 168 to 240 hours). Retraining: the convex chain is not refitted here; blend weights and band factors are refitted monthly as-of.
  • Reproduction gate passed: the default scores 2.749 at 0.5 to 240 hours and 3.152 at 168 to 240 hours (experiment 319: 2.749 and 3.152). The 319 blend with no rule reproduces its harm on cold winter nights, +0.076 points.
  • Absolute scores, 168 to 240 hours (95% interval): default 3.152 (2.940 to 3.393), B1 3.016 (2.829 to 3.211), B2 3.006 (2.818 to 3.203), N 3.125 (2.900 to 3.382), manual heuristic 3.456 (3.127 to 3.805), climatology 3.663 (3.318 to 4.027). At 0.5 to 240 hours: default 2.749, B1 2.709, B2 2.705, N 2.735, heuristic 3.414, climatology 3.664. BG2 (to 168 hours only) scores 2.375 at 0 to 24 hours and 3.016 at 144 to 168 hours.
  • B1 (PB1): -0.136 points at 168 to 240 hours (99.5% interval -0.235 to -0.053), -0.040 at 0.5 to 240 hours. It keeps 100% of the blend's gain and beats the manual heuristic by 12.7%, so two parts of PB1 hold. Cold winter nights are +0.048 at 168 to 240 hours, against the predicted +0.03 or less, so PB1 fails; the one-sided 95% upper bound is +0.168 against the tolerance of 0.05.
  • B2 (PB2): -0.146 points at 168 to 240 hours, and B2 minus B1 is -0.010 (-0.024 to +0.004). The point estimate meets the 0.01 threshold and the interval includes zero. Cold winter nights are +0.075, past the tolerance.
  • N (PN): D10 -0.117 points at 0.5 to 240 hours (predicted at least 0.08, so this holds, and it is above the 0.04 that would have refuted the hour-of-day explanation), the other five Primaries +0.008 on average (predicted under 0.02 together, so this holds), pooled -0.014 (99.5% interval -0.054 to +0.016; predicted at least 0.013, so the point estimate holds and the interval includes zero). On cold winter nights the q01 and q99 pinball rise by 0.068 and 0.093 points (tolerance 0.05), so PN fails on its tail clause.
  • PX: neither arm of each pair passes the no-harm gate, so the combination is exploratory: N with B2 scores -0.057 points at 0.5 to 240 hours, with +0.088 on cold winter nights.
  • Replicate year (fits on the tuning months, 168 to 240 hours): B1 -0.071, B2 -0.054, N +0.011 against the default; the blend arms keep their sign and N does not.

docs.title: Why B1 keeps most of the harm
docs.text:
• The forecast rule flags 75%, 84%, 90%, 85%, 78%, 69%, and 68% of the realised cold-winter-night half-hours at 0 to 168 hours, and 52%, 41%, and 31% in the three bands past 168 hours.
  • At 168 to 240 hours, the 966 realised cold half-hours the rule flags have B1 minus default of 0.000 (the blend is off), and the 1,418 it misses have +0.081, the same as experiment 319's blend.
  • The exploratory best chain weight (fitted in-sample on the scored year) falls with lead from 0.80 at 0 to 24 hours to 0.55 at 216 to 240 hours in April to October, and from 0.95 to 0.70 in November to March.

docs.title: Gain by group, 168 to 240 hours (difference from the default, points)
docs.text: Group B1 B2 N All rows -0.136 -0.146 -0.026 Sunny daylight -0.236 -0.242 +0.029 April to October -0.145 -0.155 -0.034 November to March -0.123 -0.134 -0.016 Cold winter nights +0.048 +0.075 +0.128

docs.title: Band-width correction N
docs.text:
• D10 night half-hours gain 0.246 points and D10 day half-hours 0.008; the other five Primaries' night contrasts range from -0.019 (D14) to +0.027 (D16). At 168 to 240 hours D10 gains 0.189 and the other five Primaries move by 0.000 to +0.016, so leaving D10 out flips the sign of the pooled contrast to +0.007.
  • Tail coverage at 216 to 240 hours: share below q01 is 2.1% for the default, 2.9% for N, and 1.5% for B1; share below q99 is 98.2% for the default, 98.0% for N, and 98.3% for B1.

docs.title: Tail calibration (0.5 to 240 hours, cold winter nights, difference from the default)
Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site (points, 0.5 to 240 hours, default): D5 +0.04, D9 -0.24, D10 -0.43, D11 -0.02, D14 +0.18, D16 +0.19. B1 and B2 shift all quantiles together, so these are unchanged; N moves D10 by +0.04, D5 by +0.07, and D16 by +0.02.
  • Mean absolute error of the median beside each contrast, 168 to 240 hours: default 5.460, B1 5.224, B2 5.203, N 5.460, manual heuristic 6.122. N does not move the median, so its error is unchanged, and the blend arms' error and score both fall.
  • Triggers: the check that a result depends on one Primary fired for N: leaving D10 out changes the pooled 168 to 240 hour contrast from -0.026 to +0.007. The check that a result contradicts its own prediction was considered for PB1 and PN, and the explanations were tested (the flag-share figure, and the night-and-day split for N), so it did not fire.
  • Audit: a fresh Sonnet sub-agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored files and found no discrepancy over 0.005 points: default 3.151 at 168 to 240 hours, B1 -0.136, B2 -0.146, N -0.026, D10 -0.189, and 2,057 half-hours flagged by the rule at 168 to 240 hours, of which 966 fall in the 2,384-half-hour realised group. It found no leakage, no shifted quantiles, no crossing quantiles, and no integer overflow in the night-block calculation. Its notes: the fits ignore the 210-minute delay with which telemetry arrives (harmless, because the fitted rows end 240 hours before the month starts), it scored 120 of 237,029 rows more than this page (no effect on any score), and the replicate year is a held-out set of days, not an as-of replay.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Not adopted. B1 and B2 pass the gain condition but fail the cold-winter-night non-inferiority bound at 168 to 240 hours; the group has only 2,384 half-hours there, so the bound is wide enough that it cannot pass unless the harm is clearly negative. N fails the tail and cold-night bounds. The research-default log is unchanged.
  • Intervals use 99.5% (the level of experiment 319), a little narrower than the 99.67% that three pre-registered arms set; no conclusion depends on the difference.
  • Fits on the chain: the weights, logistic fits, and width factors are fitted on the convex chain's rows and applied to the default's quantiles, because the default's own rows exist for the scored year only.
  • No example-week figure of D10's night bands before and after N is drawn, because the scoring files keep only the median of each arm.
  • Options for later work: switching the blend off on the realised cold nights is unavailable at forecast time, because it uses the observed temperature. A cold-night rule that works at 7 to 10 days would need a better predictor than the ensemble-mean temperature. Alternatively the cold-night harm can be accepted for the pooled gain, which is the maintainer's decision. The sunshine-response term of experiment 316 (D5 and D9 only) could be replicated over more April to June weeks.

docs.title: Which single change brings the 0.01 quantile of the metered solar-farm forecast to its nominal coverage at leads of 1 to 10 days without costing the quantile score or the 0.99 gain?
docs.text:
The lowest quantile of the solar-farm forecast needs no fix for a farm with its own earlier data, because the earlier "3.3 times too many misses" counted half-hours that read exactly zero. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters six solar farms, labelled A to F. Metered solar farms research default 1 is the fixed reference forecast for these farms (experiment 300, scored to 10 days by experiment 310). It blends a generalised additive model, a mixture-density neural network (the "head"), and XGBoost fed with the physical model of the farm's output (the "plant"). A "0.01 quantile" is the output below which the forecast says 1% of actual values should fall. Experiment 310 found 3.3% to 3.5% of actual values at or below the 0.01 quantile of research default 1, and experiment 318 found 3.3% to 3.7% for its heads. We tested four changes: a recalibration table (arm 1), a head that also predicts an exact zero (arm 2), a head for the tail quantiles only (arm 3), and one head for all leads with no plant forecast (arm 4).

"Own history" means a farm's forecast trains on that farm's earlier months, and "zero history" means it trains on the other five farms only, as for a new farm. Scores cover leads of 12 to 252 hours in six bands (day 1, day 2, day 3, days 4 to 5, days 6 to 7, and days 8 to 10), with quarterly refits. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of the farm's capacity), and lower is better. Intervals come from resampling the 12 scored months in blocks, and each is a 99.83% interval, the level that corrects for six planned contrasts per band.

The verdict is partly supported, and nothing is adopted. Counting only values strictly below the 0.01 quantile, research default 1 already sits at 1.2% to 1.4% in own history and 1.4% to 2.1% in zero history (Figures 1, 2, and 6). The recalibration table brings the zero-history share to 1.0% to 1.2% and costs nothing there, but unshrunk it raises the own-history score by 0.03 to 0.05 points. No arm lowers the own-history score by the 0.03 points that the research-default rule asks of a new head. This family also has no pre-agreed subset of farms or leads on which a change that helps only that subset could be adopted. So the shrunk table for zero history, the tail-targeted head (arm 3), and the no-plant head (arm 4) stay candidates.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute scores, own history (day 1 to days 8 to 10). Research default 1 scores 5.30, 5.65, 6.05, 6.69, 7.35, and 7.77 by band. climatology scores 8.64 and manual_heuristic 8.69 to 8.83 at every band; research default 1 is 0.9 to 3.3 points below climatology (intervals below zero). Zero history: 5.45 to 7.89.
  • Each family alone, own history (days 1, 3, and 8 to 10). The mixture-density head scores 5.36, 6.08, 7.76; the GAM 5.46, 6.18, 7.85; plant-fed XGBoost 5.50, 6.33, 8.63. The blend beats the best single family (the head) by 0.07 points at day 1 and by 0.03 points or less at days 3 to 10.
  • Strict 0.01 share, research default 1 against nominal 1%. Own history: 1.42%, 1.32%, 1.29%, 1.21%, 1.15%, 1.22% by band. Zero history: 1.82%, 2.07%, 2.08%, 2.02%, 1.51%, 1.41%. The share at or below the quantile is 3.3% to 3.5% because 3.0% of half-hours read exactly zero.
  • C1, arm 1 (recalibration table), minus research default 1. Own history, score: +0.031 to +0.051 points (intervals include zero); strict 0.01 share 0.95% to 1.12%. Zero history, score -0.025 to +0.026 (intervals include zero), strict share 0.98% to 1.21%. The shrunk table (k/(k+3)) changes the own-history score by at most 0.007 points. P1 holds for the coverage in both settings and fails for "under 0.02 points" (full table in own history; both tables in zero history, where the score falls).
  • C2, shrunk table in zero history. The score falls by 0.052 (interval -0.076 to -0.021), 0.051, 0.052, 0.043, 0.049 (-0.087 to -0.015), and 0.024 (-0.077 to +0.022) points by band, and it falls in both halves of the year (first half -0.018 to -0.044, second half -0.011 to -0.067). The one-week-stale table matches the table (own history +0.05 to +0.08, zero history within ±0.06 of zero), and the table of another farm is worse by 0.08 to 0.26 points (intervals above zero), so the gain is farm-specific and not a calendar artefact.
  • C3, arm 2 (zero-inflated head in the blend). The score falls by 0.004 to 0.035 points (only day 3 has an interval below zero, -0.035 to -0.006); the 0.01 pinball loss falls 3.7% at day 1 (interval -9.1% to -0.2%) and changes by -1.5% to 0.0% from day 2. P2 (at least 5% against research default 1) fails. The head alone puts 0.5% to 0.9% strictly below its 0.01 quantile, below nominal. In zero history the change is -0.045 to +0.006 points. The 0.99 pinball loss falls 2.4% to 3.8% at days 4 to 10 (intervals below zero).
  • C4, arm 3 (tail head in the blend). The 0.99 pinball loss falls 3.7% (interval -8.1% to +0.7%), 5.4%, 6.2%, 6.2%, 6.3%, and 5.0% by band, with intervals below zero at days 2 to 7; the score falls by 0.008 to 0.015 points (intervals include zero). P3 holds for the numbers (at least 4.8% at days 3 to 7, and 3.7% to 5.4% at days 1 and 2) but the control undoes the attribution: the head with lead and clear-sky index shuffled lowers the 0.99 loss by 3.5% to 6.9%, and tail minus shuffled is -1.5% to +0.7% (intervals include zero). Coverage of the 0.99 quantile (strictly below) is 98.3% to 98.7% for the tail head against 99.05% to 99.2% for research default 1. In zero history the 0.99 pinball loss changes by -5.5% to -7.3%, and the 0.01 pinball loss rises 2.9% to 9.0% (intervals include zero).
  • C5, arm 4 (one head for all leads, no plant). The score is within 1% of research default 1 at every band in own history (+0.044 at day 1, -0.002 at day 3, +0.054 at days 8 to 10; intervals include zero), so P4 holds. The 0.99 pinball loss falls 6.1% to 8.5% at every band (intervals below zero), and its 0.99 coverage is 98.4% to 98.9%. Zero history: the score changes by -0.061 to +0.020 points, and the 0.99 loss falls 7.2% to 8.5%.
  • Arm 5 was not run. Its precondition (arms 1 and 3 each pass their own prediction) failed, because arm 1's table fails its "under 0.02 points" condition in own history.
  • Adoption test, one line per arm. Arm 1 (tier 0, minimum gain 0): no gain in own history (+0.03 to +0.05), so not adopted. Arm 2 (new head, 0.03 points): condition 1 needs an interval wholly below zero and a gain of 0.03 points, and the gains are 0.004 to 0.035 with intervals including zero at five of six bands, so not adopted. Arm 3 (new head, 0.03 points): gains of 0.008 to 0.015, so not adopted. Arm 4: no gain. No arm reaches condition 1, so conditions 2 to 5 are moot, and no row is added to the research-default log.
  • Wind cross-breed (descriptive only). We applied the same table, fitted on earlier months, to the stored forecasts of the three metered wind farms from experiment 259: R1 (the physics model of the farm), R0 (XGBoost), and H5c (R1 plus a neural quantile head), on its 53 Tuesday runs from 2025-07 to 2026-06. The table lowers the score of R1 by 0.28 points at day 1 and 0.36 at days 5 and later, and of R0 by 0.22 and 0.31. It lowers the score of H5c by 0.03 points at day 1 and raises it by 0.04 to 0.14 points beyond day 1. The table moves the share of values strictly below the 0.05 quantile of R1 and R0 from 1% to 2% up to 4% to 6%, close to the nominal 5%. The strict 0.01 share stays at 0.4% to 1.7% before and after. All three arms use the neural head's kept rows (6,885 at day 1 to 69,555 at day 5 and later). The full table is wind_recalibration.csv in the private data folder.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, own history (points of capacity, farms pooled, day 1 and days 8 to 10). Research default 1: +0.05 and +0.72; tail head: +0.17 and +0.81; zero-inflated blend: +0.05 and +0.79; no-plant head: +0.68 and +0.88. At day 3 the tail head raises the median relative to the mean by 0.1 to 0.2 points on every farm; its median ends above its mean on five of the six farms (farm A stays below, -0.28 against -0.48).
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast. Absolute error of the mean forecast against research default 1, own history: table +0.3% to +0.6% (shrunk table -0.1% to +0.1%), tail head -0.1% to +0.1%, zero-inflated blend -0.4% to +0.2%, no-plant head -0.1% to +1.9%. Every own-history interval includes zero. In zero history the shrunk table lowers the error of the mean forecast by 0.7% to 0.8% at days 1 to 3 (intervals below zero). In every row, the sign of the error matches the sign of the score contrast.
  • Farm E drives the lower-tail share. A fresh Sonnet agent found 4.6% of farm E's values strictly below the 0.01 quantile for research default 1 and 4.0% for the zero-inflated blend, against under 1% at the other farms, so more than half of the farm-equal 1.2% to 1.4% comes from farm E.
  • Audit. Triggers 1 (the shuffled-input control keeps the 0.99 gain), 2 (P1, P2 failed), and 5 (the shuffled control moves the score by 0.004 to 0.011 points, more than its interval's half-width at day 1) fired. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the scores, the 0.99 pinball loss, and the strict 0.01 share from the stored forecasts: scores agree within 0.002 points, the 0.99 loss within 0.0005, and the strict share within 0.0005 (0.0133 against 0.0129 at day 3, the difference comes from the row set, because the audit intersected the rows of 6 arms rather than 15). It found no crossed or negative quantiles and no sign flip when any one farm is left out for the tail head's 0.99 loss, the shrunk table's zero-history score, or the no-plant head's 0.99 loss; farm A is worse than research default 1 on the tail head's 0.99 loss and on the no-plant head's 0.99 loss. The audit agent did not check other bands, other metrics, or seeds beyond the first. Triggers 3, 4, 6, and 7 did not fire (trigger 6 was not compared against a sister experiment).
  • Reviews. One Sonnet code review found no leakage or bug; its two suggestions (row-count and seed-count assertions) were applied. The default is read from stored forecasts, so the plan's reproduction gate was not needed; the blend with experiment 318's five-seed head (rd1_5seed) scores within 0.003 points of research default 1.

docs.title: Method and schedule
docs.text:
• Arms. Arm 1: offsets per farm, lead day, and level, the empirical quantile of actual minus forecast over rows whose valid time precedes the month's first run (30 rows minimum per cell), clipped at zero and re-sorted; the shrunk version multiplies by k/(k+3). Arm 2: the head gains a logit for an exact-zero half-hour (output at or below 0.002 of the scale) with the default inputs plus hour as sine and cosine, and the blend uses it in place of the mixture head. Arm 3: a network on experiment 318's full inputs outputs offsets from the plant forecast at 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.95, 0.98, and 0.99, trained pooled with the pinball loss and a non-crossing penalty, and replaces the blend's 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles. Arm 4: experiment 318's pure_lead_pooled (own history from its stored forecasts; zero history fitted here).
  • Schedule and seeds. Quarterly refits on all earlier months (the screening schedule); five seeds in own history and three in zero history (three for the shuffled control). Absolute scores could shift under weekly refits and the contrasts were not tested for dependence on the schedule.
  • Rows. Experiment 310's scored-year rows (2025-09 to 2026-08), common to every arm and to the floors; weather at every lead is the 00 UTC ECMWF ensemble run, available at forecast time, and the farm's own power enters at a lag of ceil(lead / 24) days.
  • Reuse. The scripts import experiment 310's folder for rows, Setting, the head, and the rolling blend, and experiment 318's folder for the added columns, batches, and training loop.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Leads. The scored range is 12 to 252 hours (days 1 to 10), which covers NGED's horizon.
  • Coverage definition. The strict share is the headline because zero actuals sit on a point mass. The "at or below" shares of experiments 310 and 318 are in the private score tables.
  • Months without history. Months with no earlier rows, and cells under 30 rows, pass through unchanged, which dilutes the table's effect in the first months.
  • Upper-tail trade. The tail head and the no-plant head lower the 0.99 pinball loss while covering the 0.99 quantile less often (98.3% to 98.9% against 99.05% to 99.2%). For curtailment the missed events matter, so the cost of curtailment at a substation and its generators (the node metric) should be scored before porting the tail head or the no-plant head.
  • Not tested. Weekly refits, the blend rescored with the new tail head's gain per farm (farm A is worse), and a table fitted on more than the 12 scored months.
  • Next. Score arm 3's and arm 4's forecasts on the node curtailment metric, and test the shrunk table on a farm genuinely absent from the training set.

docs.title: Can a blend with the manual heuristic confined to daylight (or to nights an ensemble share rule calls mild) improve Primary demand research default 2 at 0.5 to 240 hours, and does the sunshine graft of experiment 316 replicate?
Take-home message
docs.text:
Using the manual-heuristic blend only by day causes no harm on cold winter nights but gives up nearly half of the blend's gain, and a hard switch on the share of cold ensemble members keeps the whole gain with almost no cold-night harm, though that switch was not pre-registered. Primary demand research default 2 is our research demand forecast for six Primary substations (anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), up to 10 days ahead. Experiment 319 found that blending the median of Primary demand research default 2 with the median of the manual heuristic (NGED's rule of thumb, built from the same half-hour in earlier weeks and years) lowers the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in percentage points of the substation's capacity) by 4.5% at 168 to 240 hours, and experiment 320 found that the blend harms cold winter nights (winter half-hours after dark, from 18:00 to 06:30 local time, that turn out to have a 24-hour mean temperature under 2 °C). We asked whether confining the blend to daylight half-hours (the daylight-only blend, D1) removes the harm, whether a night weight built from the share of the 51 ensemble members below 3 °C (D3) recovers the night gain without the harm, and whether the sunshine graft of experiment 316 replicates. D1 lowers the score by 0.075 points (99.5% interval 0.028 to 0.151) at 168 to 240 hours, against the default's 3.152, which is 55% of the all-hours blend's 0.136, and is 11.0% better than the manual heuristic. D3 keeps the whole gain (0.135 points) and raises the score on cold winter nights by 0.069 points, over the 0.05-point bound on harm there. The sunshine graft (the sunshine response of a depth-1 XGBoost refit, added to the convex fit's forecast) recovers 0.50 of the refit's advantage over the convex fit at D5 and D9 in April and June 2025.

Verdict: partly supported. D1 meets the five adoption conditions and becomes Primary demand research default 3. D3 fails the cold-night bound. Lead range: 0.5 to 240 hours for stages 1 and 2, 0.5 to 168 hours for stage 3, where arm D is stored to 168 hours only. The research default's absolute scores are in the first figure.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate passed. The default scores 2.749 at 0.5 to 240 hours and 3.152 at 168 to 240 hours, as in experiment 319. All arms equal the default below 168 hours.
  • Single forecast sources at 168 to 240 hours (stage 1 row set, 236,909 half-hours): default 3.152 (2.940 to 3.391), manual heuristic 3.456, climatology 3.663, all-hours blend 3.016, D1 3.077, D2 3.013, D3 3.017. D1's added value over the best single family (the default) is -0.075 (99.5% interval -0.151 to -0.028). At 0.5 to 240 hours D1 scores 2.727 against 2.749 (-0.022, -0.044 to -0.008).
  • D1 by group, difference from the default at 168 to 240 hours (all-hours blend in brackets): sunny daylight -0.236 (-0.236); all daylight -0.166 (-0.166); all night 0.000 (-0.111); Economy 7 nights (01:00 to 07:00 local, 56,980 half-hours) 0.000 (-0.105); April to October -0.105 (-0.145); November to March -0.032 (-0.123); cold winter nights 0.000 (+0.076, one-sided 95% bound +0.189). D1 therefore keeps all of the gain on sunny daylight, 55% of the pooled gain, and none of the night gain.
  • D2 (day and night weights refitted separately): -0.139 pooled and +0.112 on cold winter nights (bound +0.230). Freeing the night weight reproduces the harm, as predicted.
  • The member-share rule (flag: at least half of the members below 3 °C) at 168 to 240 hours: flags 71.6% of the 2,384 realised cold winter-night half-hours (83%, 74%, and 61% in the three 24-hour bands) against 40.5% for the ensemble-mean rule, at a false-flag rate of 8.4% against a base rate of 4.6% (1.7 to 1.9 times). The prediction (at least 65%, at most twice the base rate) holds pooled and fails in the 216 to 240 hour band (61%).
  • D3: -0.135 pooled, -0.059 against D1 (99.5% interval -0.130 to -0.015, so at least the 0.02 predicted), and +0.069 on cold winter nights (bound +0.164), over the 0.03 predicted and the 0.05 tolerance. D3 is not adopted.
  • D3b (D3 with a hard switch; post hoc, not pre-registered): the experiment 319 blend everywhere except on half-hours the member-share rule flags as cold winter nights, where the chain alone is kept. D3b scores -0.134 pooled (99.5% interval -0.228 to -0.054), 12.7% better than the heuristic, and +0.008 on cold winter nights (one-sided 95% bound +0.061, point estimate under the 0.05 tolerance but the bound just over it). Its replicate-year pooled gain is -0.071.
  • Replicate year (fits on the tuning period, 155,202 half-hours at 168 to 240 hours): all-hours blend -0.075, D1 -0.027 (99.5% interval -0.079 to +0.008, same sign), D3 -0.045 (-0.147 to +0.109), D3b -0.071. D1's replicate gain is smaller than the scored year's, and its November-to-March change is +0.013.
  • Tails at 216 to 240 hours (default, D1, D3b): coverage below q01 is 2.1%, 1.9%, and 1.5%; coverage below q99 is 98.2%, 98.4%, and 98.3%; q01 pinball 0.235, 0.227, and 0.212; q99 pinball 0.245, 0.239, and 0.234. The 90% band holds 88.9%, 89.7%, and 90.5% of actuals. No arm moves a tail by more than 0.023 points. Curtailment cost against the manual heuristic is not scored, because the node-plus-generators metric needs forecasts for substations and their generators, and this experiment forecasts six Primaries only.
  • Per Primary, D1 minus default at 168 to 240 hours: D5 -0.097, D9 -0.120, D10 -0.064, D11 -0.026, D14 -0.056, D16 -0.091. Leaving one Primary out gives -0.066 to -0.085.
  • Stage 3, sunshine graft (0.5 to 168 hours, worst quarter of daylight half-hours by arm D's own score). At D5 and D9 pooled (5,521 half-hours, 11 ISO weeks) in April and June 2025, the sunshine graft recovers 0.50 (95% interval 0.34 to 0.67) of the refit's advantage, the recent-power graft -0.15 (-0.23 to -0.08), the calendar graft 0.01 (-0.02 to 0.04), temperature 0.17, and all families together 0.50. The same selection in April to June 2026 gives 0.35 (0.29 to 0.42), -0.08, -0.02, 0.13, and 0.50. By Primary the sunshine graft recovers 0.44 at D5 (0.32 to 0.57) and 0.93 at D9 (interval -5.6 to 6.6, because the refit's advantage over arm D is only 0.47 points there), against 0.45 and 0.19 in 2026. The placebos recover 0.28 at D10 and 0.21 at D16 (0.01 to 0.47), so part of the sunshine response is better in the refit everywhere.
  • Stage 3 predictions: sunshine at least 0.25 pooled and 0.15 at each Primary (point estimates 0.50, 0.44, and 0.93); recent power and calendar each under 0.25 (-0.15 and 0.01). All four predictions hold, so the sunshine-graft lead of experiment 316 is not noise.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site (points, default and D1, which differ only past 168 hours): D5 +0.04, D9 -0.24, D10 -0.43, D11 -0.02, D14 +0.18, D16 +0.19. D1 and D3b shift all quantiles together, so the offsets do not change.
  • Mean absolute error of the median, 168 to 240 hours: default 5.460, D1 5.326, all-hours blend 5.224, D3b 5.227, manual heuristic 6.122. The error and the quantile score move in the same direction.
  • Triggers and audit. Two pre-registered predictions failed (D1 keeps 55%, not 70%, of the gain; D3 harms cold nights), so the "contradicts its own prediction" trigger is treated as fired. The explanations were tested in this page (gain by day and night, and the D3b arm). A fresh Sonnet sub-agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored files: default 3.151, all-hours blend -0.136, D1 -0.075, D1 equal to the blend on daylight and to the default elsewhere (exactly), cold winter nights +0.076 for the blend and exactly 0 for D1, and leave-one-out -0.066 to -0.085. Its differences: the interval's lower bound is -0.145 against -0.151 here (an equal-weight version gives -0.143, same conclusion), and the cold-night count is 2,196 under an 18:00 to 06:00 definition and 2,384 only when 06:30 is included, and the 2,384 figure uses that second definition. It found no leakage in the as-of fits or the member share, did not read the upstream kind flag (solar geometry from experiment 319), and noted that D3b is computed in the scoring script and is not a stored column.
  • Adoption. D1 meets the five conditions of the research-default page: its interval is wholly below zero with minimum gain 0, no protected group is harmed (cold winter nights exactly 0), the replicate year has the same sign, the controls passed, and the change uses the sun's elevation at the valid time and the heuristic median, both available at the forecast time. Porting needs the weekly-analogue heuristic in the serving path.
  • Not pre-registered. D3b and the day-and-night, season-by-night splits are post hoc. The worst-quarter selection in stage 3 deviates from experiment 316 (no BG2 forecast exists for the replicate year), and selecting on arm D's own score inflates both the refit's advantage and the graft's recovery, so only the replicate against the same-selection 2026 figures is comparable.
  • Fits on the chain: the weights and logistic fits use the convex chain's rows, as in experiments 319 and 320.
  • Candidate next steps: pre-register D3b with the cold winter nights of the replicate year pooled so the bound has more half-hours; test a flexible sunshine response in the convex fit against Primary demand research default 3.

docs.title: Does a flexible sunshine response in the convex fit improve Primary demand research default 3 at 0.5 to 240 hours?
Take-home message
docs.text:
A smooth sunshine curve added to the demand model's solar term does not close the gap to the XGBoost model on April-to-June daylight half-hours, and it makes the pooled score slightly worse. Primary demand research default 3 is our research demand forecast for six Primary substations (the substations that feed local areas from the transmission network, anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), up to 10 days ahead. Experiment 322 took the sunshine response of an XGBoost model with one-level trees, which scored better than the default on the worst April-to-June daylight half-hours at D5 and D9, added it to the default, and recovered half of that difference. We asked whether a smooth correction in clear-sky index (measured irradiance over clear-sky irradiance) and sun elevation does the same. The correction is fitted in the least-squares fit that gives each of the 51 weather-forecast ensemble members its solar term. F1 gives each Primary its own correction. F2 gives all six Primaries one shape and a scale per Primary. Neither reaches its pre-registered target. Lower scores are better. F1 improves the score at D5 and D9 in April to June by 0.044 points of effective capacity at 0.5 to 168 hours (99.5% interval -0.152 to +0.077, which includes zero), against a pre-registered improvement of 0.30. Over the whole year F1 worsens the pooled score by 0.011 points.

Verdict: not supported. The scored lead times are 0.5 to 240 hours, with BG2 (the best-guess forecast stack) as a reference to 168 hours. Before scoring, the rebuilt default had to match experiment 322's default, and it does: 2.7265 points at 0.5 to 240 hours against 2.727, with a largest difference of 1.5e-5 in any quantile.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Sign convention. Every contrast is the variant's score minus the default's score, so a negative number is an improvement.
  • Arms. Default: Primary demand research default 3 (experiment 322's D1). F1: 30 spline columns per Primary (6 clear-sky-index knots by 5 sun-elevation knots), added to the T-all fit of experiment 184, free in sign, with a second-difference penalty (100) and a ridge (10) fixed before any score was read. The T-all fit is experiment 184's least-squares model of net demand with separate heating and lighting terms by day type, and the D5 export clip is not part of it. F2: one shape (the same 30 columns) with a non-negative scale per Primary, fitted by 6 alternating rounds. F3 (the monotone network) was not run, because F1 fell far under its pre-registered 0.15 floor at D5 and D9.
  • How the response enters. Each member's response is the response-bearing fit's forecast with the member's weather minus its forecast at the ensemble-mean weather. The difference between the response-bearing and the stored T-all fit at the ensemble-mean weather is added to the chain's mean and quantiles. Experiment 202's rolling replay (0.5 to 168 hours, with experiment 220's median correction added afterwards) and experiments 319, 320, and 322 (168 to 240 hours, daylight blend) were then rerun with every factor refitted on completed history. The chain's own Kalman-filtered mean is not refitted, so the response is not fitted in exactly the same least-squares fit as the solar term.
  • Row set and schedule. Six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, 798,116 rows outside the hand-filtered events, origin 09:00 UTC, monthly refits of T-all as in experiment 184.
  • Absolute scores (points of capacity, 0.5 to 240 hours). Default 2.727; F1 2.737; F2 2.742; manual heuristic 3.414; climatology 3.664. At 0.5 to 168 hours: default 2.579, F1 2.595, F2 2.602. At 168 to 240 hours: default 3.077, F1 3.075, F2 3.073.
  • Contrasts against the default (99.5% intervals, 12 initialisation months). Pooled, 0.5 to 240 hours: F1 +0.011 (+0.001 to +0.024), F2 +0.016 (+0.004 to +0.029). 168 to 240 hours: F1 -0.002 (-0.010 to +0.006), F2 -0.003 (-0.013 to +0.006).
  • Stage 0 (passes). The fitted response rises with clear-sky index at all six Primaries, and more steeply at higher sun elevation (D5 rises by 3.9 points between index 0 and 1.2 at 30 degrees, 13.6 at 45 degrees, and 25.1 at 65 degrees; D9 by 7.9, 10.2, and 12.1), with the same sign at D5 and D9. The refit's own partial-dependence curve was not drawn, so the comparison is with the correction alone.
  • PF1 (fails on three clauses). April-to-June daylight at D5 and D9 together, 0.5 to 168 hours: F1 -0.044 (99.5% interval from ISO-week blocks -0.152 to +0.077); D5 -0.039, D9 -0.049. The pre-registered improvement is 0.30 with an interval below zero. The pooled clause also fails (F1 worsens the score by 0.011 against a required improvement of 0.02), and the sunny-daylight clause passes. The replicate year (April and June 2025, A+S without the median correction, daylight taken as 06:00 to 18:00 UTC): F1 -0.176 (95% interval -0.284 to -0.076), June -0.200, April -0.152 (-0.384 to +0.018). The sign agrees, and the size does not. D10 and D16 (placebos) move by +0.030 at 0.5 to 168 hours and +0.022 at 0.5 to 240 hours, over the 0.02 bound.
  • Where F1 helps. Sunny daylight at 0.5 to 240 hours: F1 -0.091 (99.5% interval -0.139 to -0.034), F2 -0.135 (-0.188 to -0.063). All daylight at 0.5 to 168 hours: F1 +0.031, F2 +0.046. Night half-hours and cold winter nights are unchanged (+0.003 and -0.002).
  • PF2 (fails). F2 is 0.035 points worse than F1 at D9 (April-to-June daylight, 0.5 to 168 hours: F2 -0.014, F1 -0.049), against the 0.05 points better that PF2 required.
  • PF3 (passes, but the gain is not adoptable). At 168 to 240 hours sunny daylight improves by 1.9% for F1 (-0.085 points) and 3.4% for F2 (-0.155 points), against the 1% bar, while the pooled score at those leads does not change.
  • No-harm bounds. Pooled, q01, q99, cold winter nights, and sunny daylight stay inside the tolerance table. The pooled score and the D10 and D16 placebos are worse, so the gain condition fails.
  • Leaving one Primary out does not flip the sign of the pooled F1 contrast at 0.5 to 240 hours (+0.008 to +0.016). At 168 to 240 hours, leaving D5 out flips the sign (+0.003 against -0.002 pooled), and D5 alone is -0.027.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site (default / F1, points): D5 0.04 / 0.04, D9 -0.24 / -0.25, D10 -0.43 / -0.44, D11 -0.02 / -0.02, D14 0.18 / 0.18, D16 0.19 / 0.19. The response does not change how far the median sits from the mean.
  • Error of the median forecast beside the quantile score (0.5 to 240 hours): mean absolute error 4.752 for the default, 4.774 for F1, 4.782 for F2, in the same direction as the quantile score. The mean signed error shrinks (-0.185, -0.099, -0.063), so the response reduces the median's bias while raising its scatter.
  • Tails (pooled, 0.5 to 240 hours): pinball loss at q01 changes by -0.001 and at q99 by +0.002 for F1. The coverage of the 1% and 99% quantiles at 168 to 192 hours is 1.8% and 98.3% for the default and 1.8% and 98.2% for F1. The threshold-weighted score changes by 0.6% (worse).
  • Audit triggers. The trigger "a result contradicts its own prediction or an earlier finding, and no explanation has been tested" fired: the result contradicts its own prediction and experiment 322's graft. Untested candidates are that the graft carries the refit's interactions with other inputs, and that the chain's Kalman-filtered mean is not refitted here. The triggers for a failed control, a mean-error contrast in the other direction, a leave-one-out sign flip of a planned contrast, a nested arm beating its container, and an interval width mismatch did not fire. The trigger for a later experiment depending on this result's sign may apply.
  • Audit (fresh Sonnet agent, no Opus). It re-derived the headline contrasts from the saved arms with its own code and found no method fault: pooled F1 +0.0109 and F2 +0.0156, D5 and D9 in April to June -0.0440, all daylight at 0.5 to 168 hours +0.0314, D10 and D16 +0.0224, no crossing quantiles, and the rebuilt default equal to the stored one to 1.5e-5. Its sunny-daylight figure was -0.0934 against the page's -0.091, from a slightly different sunny-flag join, and its row count was 798,236 against 798,116 because it did not join the reference forecasts. A partial test of the double-counting explanation removed each row's median shift from F1 (a proxy, because the stored files hold only the combined shift): the result scores -0.001 against the default at 0.5 to 240 hours and -0.013 at D5 and D9 in April to June daylight. Nearly all of F1's pooled harm therefore sits in the level shift. This fits the double-counting explanation and does not prove it, so the explanation stays untested.
  • Limit of the test (code review). The chain's mean is experiment 184's T-all forecast plus the Kalman filter's level and anomaly, and experiment 220's median correction is added afterwards. Both were estimated from the recent residuals of the stored fit without a response, so they may already contain part of the sunshine bias that the response now explains. The variants add the response on top of them unchanged, which could count that bias twice, most at short leads on sunny days. This was not tested: a rerun with the filter and the median correction refitted on each variant's own residuals would settle it. The verdict is therefore "not supported" for a response added in this way, and the hypothesis for a response inside a fully refitted convex fit is still open.
  • Curtailment cost was not scored: the six Primaries have no generator forecasts here.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• A boosted-tree sunshine term could use more inputs at once, since a curve in two inputs did not reproduce the graft.
  • Run the post hoc arm that changes only the members' responses (no level shift), to find which of the two parts of F1 raises the score on other daylight half-hours.

docs.title: Which findings from the metered solar farms carry over to the three metered wind farms, at leads of 1 to 10 days?
docs.text:
Take-home: one of four solar-farm findings carried over to the three wind farms, with limits. We built a small neural network (a mixture-density network, which outputs a probability distribution) that corrects the 11 quantiles of the physics-based wind forecast. On the half-hours when a farm is not idle, its quantile score was 0.27 points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity) better than XGBoost plus a lookup table of offsets, with a 95% interval from re-drawing whole months of -0.38 to -0.16. The gain appears at days 1 to 2 (weaker) and at days 3 to 10, sits in the median and the lower half of the distribution, and vanishes when the idle half-hours are included. The upper tail is no better, and the network needs the farm's own forecast history to learn from. We chose to report the non-idle half-hours after seeing that the all-half-hour gain was near zero, so that choice is post hoc. Verdict: partly supported (of the five predictions, P4 held, P1 held in direction but not size, P3 was inconclusive, and P2 and P5 failed).

We asked whether four findings from the six metered solar farms hold for the three metered wind farms (farms W1, W2, and W3), at lead times of 1 to 10 days. The findings are: a mixture-density network (as in experiment 310) fed by a physical power model beats that model alone; lead features help it; one pooled network across leads matches separate networks per lead band; and the experiment 321 recalibration table lowers the lower-tail loss. The physical power model is the physics core with the wind-speed adapter of experiment 285, run on the 51 ensemble members as in experiment 303. Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity (lower is better), on experiment 33's 53 Tuesday runs from July 2025 to June 2026, with three seeds. Intervals re-draw whole months and seeds, and farms are not resampled. "Kept rows" are the 96,479 of 107,121 rows outside experiment 210's idle-band mask, which removes half-hours of near-zero wind where the metered series holds a reactive-power floor. A "hindcast" is the 442 daily ensemble forecasts issued from April 2024 to June 2025. A "lead day" is the number of calendar days from the run's date to the valid time. The "offset table" is experiment 259's table of power offsets per farm, lead day, and quantile level. Arms are named W0 to W8; the text says "farm W1" when it means a farm.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and weather
docs.text:
• Arms. W0 is climatology (per farm, month, and hour of the hindcast year's observed power). W1 is experiment 303's P1, XGBoost on the members plus the experiment 259 offset table. W2 and W3 are experiment 313's pure XGBoost and pure MDN (weather only, ERA5-trained, own history, applied to the members). W4 to W7 and W5 for a farm with no history train a three-component Gaussian mixture head on the hindcast, with the adapter alone (experiment 303's P2) as base. W4 is one head per farm with no lead input. W5 adds the lead as sine and cosine of the hour of the lead day plus the raw lead. W6 is one head across the farms and leads with a learned farm embedding. W7 is one such head per lead band (days 0 to 2, days 3 to 6, and days 7 or later). W8 applies experiment 321's rolling-origin offset table to W1 and W4. The adapter alone and the adapter plus the offset table are experiment 303's P2 and P3.
  • Departures from the plan (written before any score was read): the adapter's effective wind speed is not stored per case, so the heads read the adapter's quantiles and the members' summaries of speed, direction, and temperature; W2 and W3 are experiment 313's stored predictions, not refits per lead band; W9 (pre-training on public farms) is skipped because experiment 288 has not merged; no manual heuristic exists for wind; the curtailment-cost metric is not run because it scores a node plus its generators.
  • Weather and training. The adapter and XGBoost are trained on ERA5 before 2024-04-01. The heads train on the 442 ensemble hindcast runs (2024-04-01 to 2025-06-16), init and valid time before 2025-04-16, with early stopping on later runs. ERA5 is not read at forecast time. The research default does not apply to wind farms yet, so no row is added to the log.
  • Compute. About 3 GPU minutes in total. Code reused from the folders of experiments 303, 310, 313, and 321.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
The planned contrasts are C1 (W4 minus W1), C2 (W5 minus W4), C3 (W6 minus W7), and C4 (W3 minus W2). A label such as x8 names an extra contrast in the score file.

  • P1, W4 beats W1 by 0.05 to 0.2: the direction held and the size did not. W4 minus W1 is -0.272 (95% -0.383 to -0.161; 99% -0.416 to -0.128), beyond the predicted 0.2.
  • P2, W5 beats W4 by at least 0.03: failed. W5 minus W4 is +0.001 (99% -0.104 to 0.089).
  • P3, W6 within 0.03 of W7: inconclusive. W6 minus W7 is -0.035 (99% -0.149 to 0.064); W6 is nominally better and the interval is wide.
  • P4, W3 no better than W2: held. W3 minus W2 is -0.009 (99% -0.112 to 0.068).
  • P5, the recalibration table lowers W1's strict 0.01 pinball loss by at least 5%: failed. The loss is 0.284 before and after. The table lowered W1's score by 0.066 (95% -0.258 to 0.162, not distinguishable from zero) and raised the 0.99 pinball loss from 0.640 to 0.707.

docs.title: Scores (points of capacity; pinball losses on the kept rows)
docs.text:
Single-family rows come first: XGBoost (W1, W2), physics core plus adapter (the adapter alone, and with the table), and mixture network (W3). W4 to W7 are the blends. Best single family: the adapter plus the offset table, 11.26. W4 minus that row is -0.182 (95% -0.285 to -0.082), the improvement of the head.
