  • Absolute skill. All arms beat climatology by 2.2 to 2.8 points on the kept rows (W1 minus W0 -2.49, 95% -3.27 to -1.71). The table is scored at 1 to 10 days, with days 1 to 2 and days 3 to 10 separately.
  • W4 against W1 at both lead splits (kept rows). Days 1 to 2: -0.226 (95% -0.393 to -0.047). Days 3 to 10: -0.248 (-0.414 to -0.095).
  • Per farm, W4 minus W1: farm W1 -0.174, farm W2 -0.392, farm W3 -0.250. Without farm W1, W2, or W3 the gain is -0.323, -0.211, and -0.282.
  • Leave one farm out. W5 trained on the other two farms scored 0.361 worse than W5 (95% 0.111 to 0.619) and 0.090 worse than W1 (-0.183 to 0.390), so the gain depends on the farm's own hindcast.
  • The recalibration table on W4 made it worse, by 0.102 (95% -0.045 to 0.290, not distinguishable from zero), and raised the share of observed power below the median to 50.2%.
  • The curtailment-cost metric was not run (see the departures above).

docs.title: Tail calibration (kept rows)
docs.text:
Arm Below q01 (nominal 1%) Below q05 (5%) Above q95 (5%) Above q99 (1%) q05 pinball q95 pinball W1 XGBoost plus table 0.5% 1.3% 6.7% 1.8% 1.356 2.610 W3 mixture network 0.5% 1.3% 7.6% 2.3% 1.357 2.691 W4 adapter plus head 0.9% 4.8% 7.0% 2.4% 1.312 2.581 W5 W4 plus lead terms 1.1% 5.2% 7.4% 2.7% 1.319 2.611 W8 W1 plus recalibration 0.7% 4.8% 5.3% 1.5% 1.334 2.698
  • The head fixes the lower half and not the upper tail. The share below q05 moves from 1.3% to 4.8%, and the share above q99 stays at 2.4% against 1% nominal (W1: 1.8%).
  • The 5% to 95% band is narrower than W1's (88.2% coverage against 92.1%), because the head brings the quantiles down towards the observations.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast is in the last column of the score table. It is -3.87 points for W4 and -4.81 for W1, so every arm's median sits below its mean forecast. W4's gap is the smaller.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile score. Trigger 3 fired for W4 against W1: the score fell by 0.27 and the mean-forecast absolute error moved by +0.04 (95% -0.09 to 0.18). The median's absolute error fell by 0.41. W4 reshapes the quantiles around a similar mean forecast. W8 on W1 lowered the score by 0.07 and raised the mean-forecast absolute error by 0.55 (95% 0.27 to 0.88).
  • All rows against kept rows. W4 minus W1 is -0.037 on all 107,121 rows (95% -0.121 to 0.047): -0.245 from the kept rows and +0.208 from the 10,642 idle half-hours, where W4 scored 2.1 points worse because it trains on kept rows only. This is cancellation, not a spurious gain.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the W4 minus W1 contrast from the stored predictions, with its own code. The agent reproduced -0.272 on the kept rows, found no leakage and no row misalignment (hindcast rows, experiment 313's arrays, and the W8 scatter all line up), and found the gain on each of the three seeds (-0.274, -0.285, -0.256). The agent also found the gain between -0.24 and -0.30 when dropping any one month, but uneven by month: the scored month of May 2026 shows none, and April 2026 and July 2025 show the most. Remaining caveat: the adapter's base quantiles on the hindcast rows may be in-sample for the adapter, as for experiment 303's own head; the scored result is out of sample either way.
  • Triggers (from the ml-experiment skill's audit list; trigger 3 is a quantile-score contrast that disagrees with the same contrast on the mean forecast, trigger 4 a sign flip when one farm is left out). Trigger 3 fired (above). Trigger 4 did not fire for W4 minus W1, whose sign holds without any one farm; W6 minus W7 changes from -0.035 to +0.001 without W3, inside its interval.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Three farms. The intervals hold for these three farms only, because farms are not resampled.
  • Post hoc choices. The heads' hyperparameters (40 epochs, batch of 2,048) were fixed before the scores were read. The prediction text names the kept rows, but we looked at both the kept-row and all-row scores before choosing the kept rows as the headline. The plan and the results were committed together, because the run took 3 minutes.
  • Next. Fit the head with the idle half-hours in its training rows; give the head the upper tail's own loss (experiment 321's tail head); test W5 for a farm with no history after fitting on more than one hindcast year.

docs.title: Does refitting the stack around a sunshine response, and restricting the response to sunny half-hours, improve Primary demand research default 3 at 0.5 to 240 hours?
docs.text:
The refitted sunshine response removes the all-daylight harm of experiment 323's F1, but the pooled gain is under 0.01 points, below the 0.02-point minimum for a fitted step, so nothing is adopted. All numbers are at 0.5 to 240 hours, six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, 798,116 rows, in points of effective capacity (smaller is better). F1s and F1sel were added after stage 0 failed its prediction, so they are post hoc.

  • Arms. Default is Primary demand research default 3, rebuilt and averaged over 6 network seed sets. F1 is experiment 323's unrestricted sunshine response with the rest of the chain left unrefitted. F1r is the unrestricted response with the Kalman level, night offset, recipe R, spread table, and median correction refitted on its own errors. F1s multiplies the response basis by clip((index - 0.6) / 0.1, 0, 1) * clip((elevation - 15) / 5, 0, 1); the 5-degree ramp was chosen before any score. F1sel uses F1s at a Primary only where it beat the default by at least 0.02 points on sunny daylight over the previous 12 months.
  • Absolute scores. Default 2.732 (stored default from experiment 322: 2.727), F1 as run 2.737, F1r 2.727, F1s 2.725, F1sel 2.723, manual heuristic 3.414, climatology 3.664.
  • Pooled contrasts against the default (99.5% interval). F1r -0.005 (-0.019 to +0.008), F1s -0.007 (-0.019 to +0.002), F1sel -0.009 (-0.020 to -0.001). The gain is similar at 0.5 to 168 hours (-0.010 for F1sel) and 168 to 240 hours (-0.007).
  • By group. Sunny daylight: F1r -0.029 (-0.082 to +0.027), F1s -0.051 (-0.105 to -0.006), F1sel -0.051 (-0.094 to -0.016). All daylight: -0.010, -0.022, -0.023. Night: -0.001, +0.004, +0.002. Cold winter nights: -0.001, +0.021, +0.006. D10 and D16 (placebo): +0.007, +0.005, +0.001. April to June daylight at D5 and D9: -0.100, -0.114, -0.114.

  • Prediction outcomes.
    • PR1 (F1r): partly failed. The all-daylight change at 0.5 to 168 hours is -0.011, not harm, and the pooled score is at most 0. F1r keeps 0.033 of F1's sunny-daylight gain (0.117 against this experiment's default, 0.091 in experiment 323), under the 0.064 required, so refitting alone removed most of the gain as well as the harm.
    • PR2 (F1s): failed. Pooled -0.007, not -0.020. Sunny daylight -0.051, not -0.080. Sunny 168 to 240 hours improves 0.9%, not 1.5%. All daylight is no worse than +0.005 (-0.024), and the April to June gain at D5 and D9 at 0.5 to 168 hours is 0.112, above 0.10. In the replicate year (April and June 2025) F1s is -0.248 (-0.330 to -0.183), the same sign.
    • PR3 (F1sel): mostly passed. D10 and D16 move by +0.002 and +0.001. D5 and D9 keep all of F1s's gain (-0.049 and -0.013). D11 had no F1s gain (+0.006), and D14's F1s gain was 0.003. No Primary's switch flipped more than twice (D10 twice, D11 and D16 once, D14, D5, and D9 never). The switch drops D14's F1s gain of 0.003, so the 80% retention test fails there.
    • Stage 0: failed. 52% of F1's all-daylight harm sits at index 0.3 to 0.9, under the 60% predicted. Another 23% sits under 0.3 and 25% above 0.9. Above 0.9, F1 also harms the placebo Primaries most.

  • The fitted responses. The response rises with clear-sky index at every Primary and more steeply at higher sun elevation, as in experiment 323.

  • Tails and curtailment. Over all rows the q01 and q99 pinball losses change by 0.003 or less for every arm. On cold winter nights the q01 pinball loss changes by up to 0.007 (F1s), and on sunny daylight by up to 0.016 (F1s), inside the 0.05 tolerance. The relative twCRPS (threshold-weighted continuous ranked probability score) changes by 0.3% or less over all rows, by 1.6% to 3.2% on sunny daylight, and by up to 1.1% on cold winter nights, inside the 2% tolerance except for F1r on sunny daylight, at 3.2%. Leaving one Primary out never changes the sign of the pooled contrast for F1sel.
  • Seed noise. Six seed sets of the median-correction network give a control score between 2.5787 and 2.6038 at 0.5 to 168 hours, so one seed set moves the pooled score by 0.01 to 0.02 points. Experiment 322's stored default sits 0.006 below the six-set mean (99.5% interval -0.011 to +0.000), so it was a lucky draw. Every contrast above averages the six sets. The month-resampled intervals do not include seed noise, so the all-rows gains of 0.005 to 0.010 points are within it, while the sunny-daylight and all-daylight gains stand clear of it (audit, 2 to 4.5 standard deviations).
  • Reuse. The scripts import experiments 136, 155, 184, 201, 202, 220, 251, 317, 319, 320, 322, and 323 from their folders.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction gates. The refitted F1 equals experiment 323's stored F1 to 8e-11. The rebuilt no-response chain equals the stored chain to 1.5e-5, its network deltas equal experiment 201's exactly, and its score is 2.7265 against 2.727.
  • Median minus mean, by Primary. Under F1sel the gaps are D10 -0.44, D11 -0.02, D14 +0.18, D16 +0.19, D5 -0.09, D9 -0.29, close to the default's except at D5 (+0.04 under the default).
  • Mean absolute error. Default 4.763, F1r 4.757, F1s 4.758, F1sel 4.755 (manual heuristic 6.060, climatology 6.557), so the ranking of arms matches the quantile score.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 4 fired: leaving D5 out of the pooled score removes F1sel's gain (-0.002, 99.5% interval -0.011 to +0.004, with D5 left out). The result is therefore a D5 result.

docs.title: Does adding temperature and air density, the clock, the neural adapter's effective wind speed, or one wind-speed scale factor improve Wind farms research default 1?
docs.text: Take-home: giving XGBoost the neural adapter's corrected wind speed lowers the wind forecast's quantile score by 0.099 points of capacity (about 0.9%), scored at 1 to 10 day leads. Of four changes, only this one has a 99.75% interval wholly below zero. We asked whether any of four changes, each added alone to Wind farms research default 1, lowers the quantile score of the three metered wind farms (W1 to W3). The default is an XGBoost model (gradient-boosted trees) fitted to ERA5 (our estimate of past weather). It runs on the 51 members of the ensemble forecast from ECMWF (the European weather centre), then adds one correction per lead day, quantile level, and farm, fitted on 442 daily ensemble forecasts. The four changes were: (a) 2 m temperature and air density as extra inputs, (b) hour of day and day of year, (c) the effective wind speed of a small neural adapter (a neural network fitted to ERA5 that rescales the wind speed that a physics-based wind-power model reads), and (d) one wind-speed factor of 1.13 applied to every member. The score is a quantile score over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better), on the kept rows: the rows left after the mask of experiment 210 removes half-hours when a farm is idle. The default scores 11.352 points on the kept rows. The adapter (c) passes all five adoption conditions of the research-default rule. Porting (c) puts a neural network in the production service, and the rule leaves that adoption to the maintainer, so this page names (c) a candidate and logs no version. The verdict is supported.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Family and default. Wind farms research default 1: experiment 33's ERA5-trained XGBoost on the members, with the spread factor and experiment 259's offset table, as experiment 303's P1 and experiment 285's xgb_B4. Rows fold_a_tuesdays_v1 (53 Tuesday runs, July 2025 to June 2026), 3 farms, 3 seeds. Scored at 1 to 10 days. The XGBoost models and the adapter are fitted once on ERA5 before 2024-04-01 and the table once on the hindcast, not refitted quarterly and monthly as the family settings say.
  • Arms and tier. Tier 2 (inside the fitted stage), code imported from experiments 259, 285, 303, and 307. (a) and (b) added columns, (d) a changed setting (minimum gain 0); (c) a new fitted step (minimum gain 0.02 points). Adoption order c, b, a, d; interval read at 99.75% (four arms). Arm (c) is experiment 303's P8, read from storage.
  • Controls. Column subsampling off. Month-shuffled placebos for (a) and (b) (the added columns taken from a randomly paired other calendar month, in the ERA5 rows and the member rows) and a permuted-column placebo for (c). Known-answer test for (d): the refit factor after scaling the members by 0.85 times 0.85 equals the unscaled factor (difference 3e-8). Reproduction gate: the refit default is bit-identical to P1 (11.352 points, difference 0).
  • Replicate. The offset table and (d)'s factor refitted on hindcast cases with valid times before 2025-01-01; the daily runs of 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-16 scored. Six months.
  • Intervals resample whole months and the 3 seeds (50,000 resamples); the farms are not resampled, so every interval is conditional on these three farms.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:

  • Benchmarks, kept rows. The default scores 11.352. The frozen XGBoost reference (the default without the table) scores 11.697, so the table gains 0.345 (95% interval 0.274 to 0.418). Climatology scores 13.547, so the default is 2.195 better (1.577 to 2.808). Persistence is scored on hours 0 to 6 only (1,696 kept rows): 15.566 against the default's 6.568 on the same rows.
  • (c) minus default: -0.099 (99.75% interval -0.185 to -0.011; 95% -0.157 to -0.041). Predicted -0.05 to -0.15, held. The prediction of a larger gain at days 1 to 2 than days 3 to 10 failed; the gains are -0.086 (-0.155 to -0.021) and -0.093 (-0.167 to -0.021). The gain of (c) is negative at W1, W2, and W3 (-0.091, -0.129, -0.078) and without any one farm (-0.104, -0.084, -0.109), and negative in 10 of 12 months. Placebo for (c): -0.001 (99.75% interval -0.002 to +0.001), so the share recovered is 0.6%.
  • (b) minus default: -0.092 (99.75% interval -0.190 to +0.014). The prediction (-0.05 to -0.15) held. The prediction that its placebo recovers over half the gain failed. The placebo is -0.001 (-0.069 to +0.071), a share of 0.8%, so the gain is not a date fingerprint. The ERA5 fits cover 2019 to 2024 and never see 2025 and 2026 dates, so a fingerprint was unlikely; the placebo tested it.
  • (a) minus default: -0.032 (-0.136 to +0.060). The prediction (a gain under 0.1) held. Placebo -0.001.
  • (d) minus default: +0.014 (-0.094 to +0.137). The prediction (a gain under 0.05) failed in sign: the factor lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by 0.010 and the below-median share rises to 42.4% from 40.4%, but days 1 to 2 are worse by 0.091 and W3 by 0.262.
  • Tails. No arm raises the 0.01 pinball loss (upper 95% bound at most +0.0001) or the 0.99 pinball loss (at most +0.031, arm (b)) by more than 0.05, as predicted. Coverage of the 5%-95% band falls from 92.1% to 91.1% for (b) and stays at 92.0% for (c).

docs.title: Adoption conditions for (c)
docs.text:
• 1, gain: met. The 99.75% interval is wholly below zero and the gain 0.099 exceeds 0.02.
  • 2, no harm: met. The one-sided 95% upper bounds of the harm are -0.0006 at 0.01 and +0.013 at 0.99, against 0.05. Reported without pass or fail: each farm is better; days 1 to 2 are better by 0.086; rows with wind above rated are better by 0.45, on a small subset whose interval the month resampling cannot give.
  • 3, replication: met. The replicate gain is -0.084 (99.75% interval -0.211 to +0.062), the same sign and above half of 0.02. The t test on the six monthly differences gives p = 0.13, so the sign is not contradicted but not established either.
  • 4, controls: met. The reproduction gate, the permuted-column placebo, and the known-answer test passed. No audit trigger fired for (c) (see Checks).
  • 5, serving: met on inputs, with a port that touches the serving path. The inputs are ensemble weather only. Porting needs the adapter, a neural network, in the production service, so the rule requires the maintainer's approval before adoption.

Only (c) passes condition 1: (b), (a), and (d) do not. (b) is next in the adoption order. Each of the four arms has a wide 99.75% interval because there are three farms and 12 months, as the research-default page predicted for a family of three farms.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Kept rows: default -4.805 points, (c) -4.720, (b) -4.548. The median sits below the mean in every arm, as in experiment 259.
  • Mean absolute error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. (c): quantile score -0.099, mean absolute error of the mean forecast -0.122, median absolute error -0.130, all three measures fall. (b): -0.092, -0.100, -0.109. (d): +0.014, +0.116, -0.019, so (d)'s mean forecast is worse.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction) fired for the lead pattern of (c) and the placebo of (b), and is explained above by tested placebos and a flat gain across lead. Trigger 2 bears on (b) and on the prediction about lead, not on (c)'s gain. Triggers 1, 3, 4 (leaving any one farm out keeps the sign of (c)), 5, 6 (the 95% interval of (c) matches experiment 303's P8 against P1, which is the same rows), and 7 did not fire.
  • Reproduction. The refit default equals experiment 303's P1 to the last digit. Refit default versus stored default gives no difference, so every contrast reads the same against either.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scored at 1 to 10 days, three farms, 12 months. Intervals do not cover other farms.
  • The fits are single ERA5 fits, not the quarterly refits the family settings name, so the contrasts could differ under refitting.
  • The replicate is 6 months and its interval is wide; its sign agrees with the scored year for (c) and (b), (a) is null in both periods, and (d) is worse in both.
  • The curtailment-cost metric of experiment 277 is not scored. It needs a substation node with its generators, and W1 to W3 have no node forecast in this experiment. Tail calibration is above.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does the adapter's gain survive quarterly refits of the XGBoost model and the adapter? Run (c) with the family's refit cadence.
  • Is hour of day and day of year real? Test (b) alone on a longer replicate, with the adapter already in the default.

docs.title: Does masking load shifts found by a label-free detector improve a forecast of the normal running arrangement?
docs.text: Masking the readings that a label-free detector flags as load shifts makes a forecast of the normal running arrangement (NRA) recover faster after a shift, and loses no accuracy on ordinary days. The masked forecasts were trained and corrected with no label from the network operator (NGED). On the injected worlds, the rows during and after a shift score 1.04 points of capacity on the 95% pinball loss with the label-free pipeline (arm A), against 1.79 with no mask and 0.81 with the true spans masked. On the real record's ordinary rows, arm A scores 0.016 points better than no mask, and its 98.75% interval runs to -0.060 on the better side. The verdict is partly supported, because the pre-registered bar for the ordinary rows asked for that interval to lie inside plus or minus 0.05.

docs.title: What the experiment did
docs.text:
The detector reads only how unusual the observed power is. A lagless demand model (the convex model of experiment 130, ridge 0.1, 24-month window, refitted monthly, ERA5 reanalysis and CAMS past weather) gives quantiles for each half-hour. The observed power is converted to a normal score in those quantiles, per Primary and hour band (the band position of experiment 309). The 12 hour mean of the score is read at each 6-hourly origin. An alarm opens when the absolute mean passes a per-Primary threshold, set so that odd months alarm 5 times per Primary-year with no label look. An alarm closes when the signed mean falls below half the threshold at two consecutive origins, or after 14 days. The neighbour filter of experiment 315 then drops alarms that two or more neighbours echo.

The alarmed half-hours are removed from both the demand model's training rows and the Kalman filter's inputs. The demand model is refitted without the alarmed half-hours at each monthly cut, and the two-state Kalman filter of studies.dp_assimilation treats the alarmed half-hours as missing and re-runs from the onset. Arms:

  • A: the pipeline above.
  • B: the 24 hour mean residual with the same neighbour filter, through the same mask and train stages.
  • C: no mask.
  • D: the logged and labelled spans masked (a reference that uses labels).
  • E: arm A with a second detection pass on the demand model refitted without the pass-1 alarms.
  • AF: arm C's demand model with arm A's mask in the filter only (post hoc, to see which stage carries the gain).

On the injected worlds (experiment 297's 44 worlds at six Primaries) every arm uses the frozen demand model, so the arms differ in the filter's mask only. The real record is experiment 258's harness: 15 Primaries, 6-hourly origins, 336 half-hour leads, scored on even months.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The headline contrasts (C1 and C2) decide the verdict. Points of capacity; negative is better than no mask.

Contrast Arm A minus no mask 95% interval 98.75% interval Bar C1: injected worlds, during and after a shift, 95% pinball loss -0.752 -1.340 to -0.322 -1.533 to -0.257 at least 0.05 better, interval below zero: met C2: real record, ordinary rows, 95% pinball loss -0.016 -0.048 to +0.006 -0.060 to +0.010 point within 0.02, interval inside 0.05: not met (lower end) Real record, ordinary rows, mean quantile score -0.036 -0.073 to -0.007 not a bar descriptive Real record, 48 hours after a shift, 95% pinball loss -0.953 -2.393 to -0.179 -2.953 to -0.118 descriptive

Arm A beats arm B on the injected worlds. During and after a shift, arm A minus arm B is -0.276 points (95% interval -0.486 to -0.104). On the real record's 48 hours after a shift the two arms are close (A -0.953, B -1.095, no-mask score 1.670).

With no mask, the 95% pinball loss is 1.79 during and after injected shifts and 0.71 on real ordinary rows.

Rows No mask (K0 or C) Arm A Arm B Logged or true spans masked Injected, during and after: 95% pinball loss 1.789 1.037 1.313 0.811 Injected, during and after: mean quantile score 4.462 3.179 3.644 2.557 Real, ordinary rows: 95% pinball loss 0.712 0.696 0.697 0.707 Real, ordinary rows: mean quantile score 2.761 2.725 2.738 2.744 Real, 48 hours after: 95% pinball loss 1.670 0.717 0.575 0.556

The tails stay calibrated on ordinary days, and the upper tail improves after a shift. On the real record's ordinary rows the share of readings below the 0.01 quantile is 0.0081 for arm A and 0.0084 for no mask. The share above the 0.99 quantile is 0.0068 for arm A and 0.0077 for no mask. On the injected worlds, during and after a shift, the share above the 0.99 quantile is 0.211 with no mask, 0.101 with arm A, 0.154 with arm B, and 0.026 with the true spans masked. Arm A still under-covers the upper tail there, by a factor of ten.

The gain comes from the filter mask. Arm AF (the filter mask alone) scores -0.046 on ordinary rows and -0.954 at the 48 hours after a shift, against -0.036 and -0.953 for arm A. Retraining the demand model on masked power adds nothing measurable. At the short-history Primary 7, whose first 24 months are the fitting window, the monthly error of arm A and the no-mask arm is about the same after month 30.

docs.title: The detector alone
docs.text:
Arm A finds about as many of the 35 real shifts as arm B, and a second pass finds none more. Of the 35 labelled shifts, arm A matches 25 (95% interval 20 to 30) with 221 alarms and 85 false alarms, which is 8.8 alarms per matched shift. Arm B matches 26 (21 to 31) with 231 alarms and 85 false alarms. Arm E (pass 2) matches 24 (18 to 29). The median lag from onset to alarm is 17 hours for arm A and 24 hours for arm B. Of the 19 long-and-deep shifts, A and B each match 15 and E matches 14. The neighbour filter cuts arm A's alarms from 313 to 221 and its false alarms from 148 to 85, at the loss of one matched shift.

P1 holds as written, P2 is met, and P3 is refuted.

  • P1 (the headline gain) holds as written. Arm A beats no mask by 0.75 on the injected rows, and the ordinary rows change by -0.016, under the 0.02 limit. The verdict's stricter interval bar on the ordinary rows (inside plus or minus 0.05) is not met.
  • P2 (arm A matches at least as many long-and-deep shifts as arm B) is met. Arms A and B each match 15 of the 19. Over all 35 shifts arm A matches 25 against arm B's 26 (A minus B -1, interval -5 to +3).
  • P3 (pass 2 finds 20% more shifts than pass 1) is refuted. Pass 2 finds 24 against 25 (E minus A -1, interval -3 to 0).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. During and after an injected shift the mean absolute error of the median is 5.43 for arm A and 5.42 for the mean forecast, and 7.29 against 7.25 with no mask. The mean forecast gives the same contrast as the median (A minus no mask -1.84 against -1.85).
  • Per site. The mean-forecast error falls under arm A at 5 of the 6 sites (D10 -6.2, D14 -4.4, D9 -2.1, D11 -2.1, D16 -0.7 points) and rises at D5 (+0.9).
  • Leave one site out. Without D11, arm A's gain on the injected rows falls from 0.75 to 0.30 points, and the true-spans reference shows no gain (+0.05). The gain on the real record's ordinary rows survives dropping any one of the 15 Primaries (-0.030 to -0.041 in the quantile score).
  • Audit triggers. Two audit triggers fired: a nested arm (AF) beat the full pipeline on ordinary rows (-0.046 against -0.036), and leaving out D11 shrank the injected gain. Both are reported above and neither changes the verdict. A Sonnet audit ran in place of the Opus audit, because the brief allows no Opus.
  • Fits. No masked fit was refused for lack of training rows (0 for arms A, B, and E).

docs.title: Inputs and what uses labels
docs.text:
Labels enter only the scoring groups, the match rule, and arm D. Four constants carry label knowledge from earlier work into every arm, including arm C:

  • the filter's step_penalty and the prior for its four hyperparameters (experiment 106's tuned.json);
  • the frozen demand model of experiment 297 in the injected worlds;
  • the neighbour list, a literal dictionary copied from experiment 227's module, whose source is not documented;
  • the neighbour filter's theta of 0.25 (set by experiment 315 against labels).

The quantile function, the alarm thresholds, the offset tables, and the filter hyperparameters are fitted on all odd-month half-hours, which include the shifts and lie partly after some even-month cuts. Fitting on all odd-month half-hours is non-causal, and every arm shares it. The detector's demand model also sees the shifts as targets, so a shift it has learned as normal will not alarm.

docs.title: Deviations and what was not run
docs.text:
• The 95% pinball loss replaces the threshold-weighted continuous ranked probability score, and the 11-quantile score replaces the continuous ranked probability score.
  • The mixture-density arm (a neural network that outputs a density in place of quantiles), the scoring with ECMWF ensemble (ENS) weather at six Primaries, and the curtailment cost were not run. The ENS stage could not change a verdict, and the harness carries no node and generators for the curtailment metric.
  • The end rule is adapted from experiment 147's rule R2: an alarm closes when the signed mean falls below half the threshold at two consecutive origins, or after 14 days.
  • The training stage is not rerun on the injected worlds.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: A test of the filter mask alone at more sites, on real shifts rather than injected ones, would settle the case. The injected gain rests mostly on D11. A test on the 35 real shifts at the six Primaries with ENS frames would show whether the 48-hour gain (-0.95) holds with the weather that production serves.

docs.title: Does modelling permanent regime changes beat retraining on a recent window?
docs.text:
Take-home: adding effects for a detected permanent change does not forecast better than refitting the model on the last 24 months. We injected a permanent step of 10% or 25% of load into the recorded demand of 14 Primary substations (the substations that feed local distribution feeders), and compared forecasts that add new effects after a detected change with forecasts refitted on the last 24 months (arm B). Arm B scored as well as or better than every pre-registered regime arm in the first 90 days after a step, because the two detectors raise their alarms late and miss small steps. At D8, the Primary with a real gas-engine connection, the difference in the first 90 days was smaller than its interval (B minus C2 -0.040, interval -0.262 to +0.154). The verdict is not supported, which means the hypothesis that regime effects beat a recent-window refit did not hold.

The forecast model is a lagless generalised additive model (GAM) fitted to past weather (ERA5 and CAMS), with a one-day-ahead level filter, so the result applies to a lab setting and not to Primary demand research default 3. A "lagless" model reads no recent power. D8's gas engine is the only real change we identified in the 15 Primaries' records, so the real-record evidence is D8 alone.

Arm key. A is one fit on all history, B one fit on the last 24 months, C1 a fit frozen at the detected change plus new effects, and C2 a joint fit of old and new effects. D1 and D2 are C1 and C2 with the level filter reset at the change. Suffixes mark post hoc variants: t uses trailing 365-day bands, o uses the true change date (an oracle), r is arm A with bands from only the residuals since the detected change, and n removes the level filter.

docs.title: Controls and audit
docs.text:
• Median forecast against mean forecast: not applicable. Every arm forecasts quantiles and the median directly; no mean forecast exists. The mean absolute error of the median is printed beside every score in printed_report.txt and points the same way as the quantile score.
  • Audit triggers that fired: (1) the pre-registered placebo (C arms against A at 14 Primaries with no change) failed at +0.055 (C2) and +1.364 (C1); the tested explanation is the regime-band rule (arm Ar minus A is +0.098) and stale frozen fits after false alarms. (5) nested arm A, which C1 and C2 contain, beats both on the real records.
  • A Sonnet audit (Opus was excluded for this session) re-derived the 25% step contrasts from the stored forecasts and matched. Triage: the one-day look-ahead in known_regime (an alarm raised on the origin day) was fixed and every score re-run; the filter subtracting a step twice once a regime is known was tested with the no-filter arms below; the bootstrap clusters of one Primary and one onset were too fine, so the headline intervals now cluster by onset (eight clusters), which widens them. The oracle placebo C2o equals A by construction when no true change exists, so it checks the plumbing only.
  • Leaving D8 out is not applicable to the injected contrasts, which exclude D8.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text:
• Thresholds were fixed on 7 tune Primaries (at most 1 false change per Primary-year) and read on 7 held-out Primaries with even-month onsets. The first threshold grid never reached 1 false change per Primary-year, so the grid was widened before any recall was read.
  • Rolling GAM (CUSUM 64): recall within 60 days of 10% steps 0.26 (0.12 to 0.42), of 25% steps 0.56 (0.36 to 0.70), of 30-day ramps to 10% 0.21; median delay 40 days (10%) and 19 days (25%).
  • Weekly histogram (penalty 128): recall 0.00 for 10% steps and ramps, 0.10 for 25% steps.
  • D8 (break 2023-08-15): rolling GAM dates the change 2023-08-20 but alarms on 2023-12-06 (113 days late); histogram dates it 2023-08-17 and alarms 2023-10-19 (65 days late).
  • The Embedded Capacity Register holds 3 generators of at least 1 MW connected since 2020-06-01 at these Primaries, none at D8 near 2023-08, so the Register gave no independent check of the D8 date.
  • False changes count real load shifts, so the rates are upper bounds.

docs.title: Forecast
docs.text:
• Quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 levels (0.01 to 0.99), in points of capacity. Intervals are 98.75% (four pre-registered contrasts) and resample the eight onset months of the injected worlds, or the calendar months of the real records.
  • Injected 10% steps, first 90 days: A 3.273, B 3.270, C2 3.389, D2 3.358. B minus C2 is -0.118 (-0.200 to -0.059); B minus D2 is -0.088 (-0.146 to -0.038); C1 and D1 are about 1.4 points worse.
  • Injected 25% steps, first 90 days: A 3.945, B 3.978, C2 4.231, D2 4.171; B minus C2 -0.252 (-0.320 to -0.181).
  • Post hoc, trailing bands (C2t, D2t): B minus C2t +0.004 (-0.034 to +0.046) at 10% and -0.081 (-0.183 to +0.029) at 25% in the first 90 days, and +0.051 (+0.011 to +0.092) at 25% after day 90.
  • Post hoc, no level filter on any arm: the level filter matters more than the regime effects. Without it, C2 against the no-filter recent window (Bn) is +0.015 (-0.353 to +0.379) at 10% and +0.782 (-0.033 to +1.508) at 25% in the first 90 days, and +0.198 (+0.066 to +0.334) and +0.859 (+0.419 to +1.277) after day 90. The true-date oracle gains +1.331 (+0.757 to +1.868) at 25%. Every filtered arm still scores far better than every unfiltered arm (arm B 3.978, arm Bn 8.047 at 25% steps, first 90 days).
  • D8, first 90 days after the break: B minus C2 -0.040 (-0.262 to +0.154); post hoc B minus C2t +0.065 (+0.037 to +0.129); all rows after the break B minus C2t +0.150 (-0.057 to +0.372). The D8 intervals rest on 3 to 4 monthly forecast origins. The q99 exceedance after the break is 0.031 for arm B and 0.031 for C2t against a nominal 0.010, so no arm is calibrated at D8.
  • Primaries with no injection (14, real records): B minus A -0.021 (-0.037 to -0.004), C2t minus A -0.030 (-0.046 to -0.013), D2t minus A -0.033 (-0.050 to -0.016), against the 0.01 margin. C2 minus A is +0.055 (+0.019 to +0.102) and fails it.
  • Tail calibration: q01 and q99 exceedance and pinball loss are in printed_report.txt. The tail-weighted continuous ranked probability score and the curtailment cost were not computed.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Lab shortcuts: past weather in place of ensemble members, a filter that sees yesterday's reading, a lagless GAM base with a simple fixed-gain level filter instead of the effects filter. The experiment 264 as-of band widening at D8 was not reproduced, so the success criterion for D8 against that comparator is untested.
  • The level filter absorbs a step within days, which leaves regime effects little to add. In this implementation the filter also subtracts a known step a second time once regime effects exist, which biases the regime arms against themselves; the no-filter rows above remove that bias but are far worse in absolute terms.
  • Untested: confirming each candidate regime date by whether arm C2 improves out of sample on blocked time folds, then scanning 60 days either side of each candidate, needs a new design. A regime arm that replaces the level filter, instead of stacking on it, is also untested, and would need testing on the full Primary demand research default 3.

docs.title: Does building the 7-to-10-day demand bands from the 51 ensemble members' own solar responses (and a climatology of the response) close the sunny-daylight weakness of Primary demand research default 3?
Plan
docs.text: The research default (Primary demand research default 3, still current in the research-default log after experiment 325 adopted nothing) is our research demand forecast for six Primary substations, up to 10 days ahead. Its 7-to-10-day bands come from experiment 319's two-number summary of the 51 ensemble members' solar responses (a mean and a standard deviation, after experiment 193).

docs.title: The five plan items
docs.text:
1. Question. At 168 to 240 hours, does a solar-response distribution built from the 51 members and the training years (not only their mean and standard deviation) close the sunny-daylight weakness of the research default, and where does the weakness come from?
  2. Prediction that can fail. The weakness is a fault of the predictive distribution (the lower tail on realised-sunny half-hours), not of the median. The thresholds are in the front matter.
  3. Rows and period. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, replicate year 2024-25, origin 09:00 UTC, rows outside hand-filtered events. The headline range is 168 to 240 hours, and 0.5 to 240 hours is the no-harm check.
  4. Metric. The quantile score over 11 levels in points of effective capacity, with the research-default page's protected groups and tolerances and 12-month block bootstrap intervals.
  5. Stop rule. The reproduction gate fails, or stage 0 finds no weakness left in the default on sunny daylight at 168 to 240 hours.

docs.title: Stage 0 (zero-fit diagnostic)
docs.text: Score the default against the manual heuristic and climatology on sunny daylight at 168 to 240 hours, by 24-hour lead band and by Primary. Report the probability-integral-transform histogram and the below-q05, below-q01, above-q95, and above-q99 rates for the default and the heuristic, the q50's mean error, and the same scores on forecast-sunny half-hours (ensemble-mean clear-sky index of 0.9 or more, from the stored ensemble's shortwave radiation over the Haurwitz clear-sky value, as in experiment 178).

docs.title: Arms (run only if stage 0 passes)
docs.text:
All arms change the bands after the median, and are re-centred on the default's stored q50.

  • Default: Primary demand research default 3.
  • X1, member solar distribution: at 168 to 240 hours, the 51 members' solar responses replace the Gaussian points of experiment 319's arm x1 (centres chain mean + response, each with the chain's offsets times a factor f fitted per lead band). Daylight half-hours only.
  • X2, X1 mixed with climatology: the member responses are mixed with the empirical distribution of the response at that Primary in completed earlier origins within plus or minus 15 days of the day of year at the same hour; the mixture weight per 24-hour lead band is fitted as-of by pinball loss before each scored month.
  • X3, lagged-ensemble pooling: X1 with the responses of the two previous daily runs for the same valid time added, each earlier run down-weighted by a fitted per-lag weight. It uses only earlier runs whose response is stored (lead up to 240 hours), so lag 2 covers the 168-to-192-hour band only and lag 1 the first two bands.
  • References: manual heuristic and climatology (static), BG2 below 168 hours.

Experiment 319's code and stored member responses are reused (the folders of experiments 317, 319, 320, and 322 are named in the scripts), and each month's fits use only completed runs before that month's first origin, as they do. Schedule: the arms refit nothing but the band widths and mixture weights each month, so a weekly-retrained median would give the same contrast.

docs.title: Take-home message
docs.text: The weakness this experiment set out to fix is already closed in Primary demand research default 3, so the experiment stopped after its first diagnostic (stage 0) and ran none of its three planned arms. Primary demand research default 3 is our research demand forecast for six Primary substations (anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), up to 10 days ahead. The weakness was a worse score than the manual heuristic (NGED's rule of thumb, built from the same half-hour in earlier weeks and years) on sunny daylight half-hours, at leads of 168 to 240 hours. A half-hour counts as sunny when it is among the sunniest third of a Primary's daylight half-hours by the sunshine that was realised, as in experiment 178. We planned to build the uncertainty bands from the 51 weather-forecast members' own solar responses and tested first whether any weakness was left. The quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in percentage points of effective capacity; smaller is better) of Primary demand research default 3 on those half-hours is 4.50, against the manual heuristic's 4.82. That is 6.6% better, with a 95% interval of 1.3% to 11.3% better and a 99.5% interval of 1.7% worse to 13.4% better. Experiment 317 had found the convex chain (the stack before any weather summary or blend) 5.2% worse, at 5.07. The two-number solar summary of experiment 319 and the daylight-only blend of experiment 322 closed the gap. One Primary, D5, is still behind the heuristic, at 6.09 against 5.47 percentage points of effective capacity.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate passed: Primary demand research default 3 scores 2.727 at 0.5 to 240 hours and 3.077 at 168 to 240 hours, the values of experiment 322 (2.727 and 3.077).
  • Sunny daylight, 37,612 half-hours at 168 to 240 hours: Primary demand research default 3 scores 4.50, the manual heuristic 4.82, and climatology 4.95. It beats the heuristic in each 24-hour band (4.48, 4.52, and 4.51 against 4.83, 4.83, and 4.81).
  • Per Primary (Primary demand research default 3, then the heuristic): D5 6.09 and 5.47, D9 3.99 and 4.05, D10 5.41 and 6.21, D11 3.55 and 4.06, D14 3.64 and 3.96, D16 4.48 and 5.23. Without D5, Primary demand research default 3 is 10.4% better than the heuristic (95% interval 5.4% to 14.8%).
  • Tails on realised-sunny half-hours: Primary demand research default 3 has 1.7% below q01, 7.7% below q05, 0.7% above q95, and 0.2% above q99. The heuristic has 12.9%, 18.0%, 1.3%, and 0.8%.
  • Two of the stage 0 predictions failed, and one stop condition is met only through selection: the below-q05 rate was 7.7% (predicted above 8%), and the q50 bias, defined as q50 minus realised demand, was +5.6 points (predicted under 0.1). Realised sunshine selects half-hours with low demand, so the bias is a selection effect: over all daylight half-hours it is +0.01.
  • Forecast-sunny half-hours (ensemble-mean clear-sky index of 0.9 or more) number only 601. There Primary demand research default 3 scores 5.02 against the heuristic's 4.27, with a q50 bias of -6.4 and 17.0% of realised demand above q95. This is the mirror image of selecting by realised sunshine: the ensemble forecasts sun on days that turn out cloudier. The rows are too few to rank forecasts, and the group is not the one the brief defines.
  • Stop rule: the default already beats the heuristic on sunny daylight, so the experiment stops. The three arms (X1, X2, X3) were not run, no model was refitted, and the run used about 10 core-minutes.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus chain mean, per Primary, at 168 to 240 hours (points): D5 -0.53, D9 -0.26, D10 +0.01, D11 -0.17, D14 -0.22, D16 -0.07.
  • Error of the median beside the score: mean absolute error of the median on realised-sunny half-hours is 8.20 for Primary demand research default 3 and 8.71 for the heuristic, which points the same way as the score.
  • Triggers: none fired. The stage 0 results differ from the brief's expectation, and the cause is tested above (the convex chain, Primary demand research default 2, and Primary demand research default 3 scored on the same rows). Leaving D5 out strengthens the contrast and does not flip it, so no audit ran.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lead range: 168 to 240 hours, the 7-to-10-day range, six Primaries, one scored year. The replicate year was not scored, because the experiment stopped at stage 0.
  • Interval: the 99.5% interval of the default against the heuristic on sunny daylight includes zero (-1.7% to 13.4%), so "6.6% better" is established at 95% only.
  • Next: look at the solar term at D5 and D9 (coastal Primaries) at 168 to 240 hours, where experiment 325 also found a sunshine response helps. The member-distribution arms stay available if a later weakness at long leads shows a skewed tail.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00329-primary-demand-default-3-member-solar-distribution-at-7-to-10-days/ imports the folders of experiments 184, 202, 317, 319, 320, and 322 and reads their stored files.

docs.title: Does the standard forecasting architecture (a physics core, a learned input adapter, and a mixture-density output head) match Primary demand research default 3?
docs.text:
Take-home: The standard architecture is a small neural network with a learned input adapter (two layers that map weather inputs into the network) and a mixture-density output (a spread of forecast quantiles from three overlapping bell curves), fitted on top of the frozen convex stack of the default. At forecast lead times of 0.5 to 168 hours (7 days) it forecasts demand at six Primary substations (33/11 kV substations) slightly better than Primary demand research default 3. At the all-rows score, demand therefore does not need a different architecture from wind and solar at those leads, and the mixture output is the part that gains. The 95% interval excludes zero but the 99.5% interval does not, and one Primary (D10) supplies most of the gain. The range 168 to 240 hours was not run, so the headline lead range is 0.5 to 168 hours, not the 0.5 to 240 hours that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) needs. Scores are quantile scores in points of effective capacity, and lower is better.

We asked whether replacing the default's median-correction network, spread table, and band steps with one network (the standard architecture, STD) costs accuracy. The mixture-density output follows Bishop (1994), and the setup reuses the rows, refit dates, and inputs of experiments 311 and 314. STD scored 2.525 points of capacity against the default's 2.579 (difference -0.053). The adapter with a median-only output (STD-A) scored 2.578, so the mixture output makes the difference.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms (scored year, 0.5 to 168 hours, six Primaries, 561,207 rows, six seeds averaged, monthly refits on a 24-month pool, the P-roll schedule): default 2.579, G 2.537, STD 2.525, STD-A 2.578, BG2 2.715, manual heuristic 3.397, climatology 3.665 points of capacity. The reproduction gate passed (default 2.579 against 2.579 stored).
  • STD against the default: -0.053 (95% interval -0.089 to -0.008; 99.5% interval -0.100 to +0.016; 11 of 12 months better). P1 holds (the gap is below +0.03). STD is 0.19 points better than BG2 and 0.87 better than the manual heuristic.
  • STD-A against the default: -0.000 (95% interval -0.048 to +0.056). P3 is not met in the form predicted: STD and STD-A differ by 0.053 (95% interval -0.079 to -0.025), and STD is the better of the two on the all-rows score, so the mixture output does not hurt that score. Whether it helps the tails is not shown (see the no-harm bounds).
  • STD against G: -0.012 (95% interval -0.055 to +0.040).
  • Replicate year (2024-25 even months, against experiment 169's arm A bands): STD -0.093 and STD-A -0.043 points (95% intervals -0.121 to -0.064 and -0.066 to -0.020), absolute scores STD 2.497, STD-A 2.547, and default 2.589 (the arm A bands play the default's part in that year).
  • No-harm bounds (one-sided 95% upper bounds, pooled six Primaries; tolerances 0.02 pooled, 0.05 for each of q01, q99, cold winter nights, sunny daylight, 2% for the tail-weighted score): pooled -0.017, q01 pinball -0.000, q99 pinball -0.001. P2 is not shown: sunny daylight +0.075 (estimate -0.034), cold winter nights +0.245 (estimate -0.079), and the tail-weighted CRPS at the 95th percentile is 2.9% worse with an upper bound of +6.5%.
  • Tail calibration (all rows): coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99 is 0.012, 0.056, 0.939, 0.983 for STD against 0.013, 0.049, 0.951, 0.984 for the default.
  • Absolute scores by lead band (STD against default, points): 0-24 h 2.112 and 2.150; 48-72 h 2.434 and 2.487; 96-120 h 2.620 and 2.681; 144-168 h 2.861 and 2.931. STD has the lowest score of default, G, STD, and STD-A in every 24-hour band. Its margin over G is 0.008 points at 0 to 24 hours and 0.002 at 144 to 168 hours.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary (points): STD -1.07 (D10), -0.51 (D11), -0.23 (D14), -0.53 (D16), -1.02 (D5), -0.48 (D9); the default's are +0.72, -0.50, -0.20, -0.84, +0.01, -0.75. STD's median sits below its mean at every Primary, and the gap is markedly larger than the default's at D10 and D5.
  • Error of the median and of the mean forecast (mean absolute error, points): median 4.463 for STD against 4.510 for the default; mean 4.483 against 4.601. Both point the same way as the quantile score.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. The sign survives leaving out D10 (-0.009), but the verdict was already "interval includes zero at 99.5%", so trigger 4 (leaving one Primary out flips the sign or the verdict of a contrast) does not fire.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lead range: 0.5 to 168 hours only. The stored feature rows end at 168 hours, and the 168-to-240 stage needs rows that experiment 322 stored only for the replicate and scored years.
  • Not done: the as-of calibration of experiment 164 was not applied to STD, and the adapter reads the stored columns (temperature hinges, solar term, band width) rather than the 51 members' two-number summaries, which the stored rows do not hold.
  • Seeds: STD and STD-A average 6 seeds, and the stored default averages 3, so part of the gain could be a larger ensemble of seeds; STD-A, with the same 6 seeds, scores -0.000.
  • No calibration or night steps: the default carries its as-of calibration and night offsets and STD carries none, so the contrast is conservative on that count.
  • Replicate year: the comparator is experiment 169's arm A bands, an older forecast than the default, so -0.093 is not like-for-like with -0.053.
  • Schedule: monthly refits on a 24-month pool (P-roll), six seeds; absolute scores could move slightly under weekly refits.
  • Next: run STD at 168 to 240 hours with experiment 322's rows, with more seeds on cold winter nights, and test the mixture output alone (without the adapter) on the wind and solar families.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: Primary demand research default 3 is our research demand forecast for six Primary substations. This experiment asks whether a standard architecture shared across demand, wind, and solar forecasts costs demand any accuracy. The architecture is a physics core (here the frozen convex stack), a learned input adapter, and a mixture-density output head. The mixture head follows Bishop (1994).

docs.title: The five plan items
docs.text:
1. Question. Does the standard architecture (STD) score within 0.03 points of Primary demand research default 3 at 0.5 to 240 hours, and what is its gap at each lead band?
  2. Prediction that can fail. P1 to P4 in the front matter.
  3. Rows and period. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, replicate year 2024-25, origin 09:00 UTC, rows outside hand-filtered events.
  4. Metric. The quantile score over 11 levels in points of effective capacity, with the research-default page's protected groups and tolerances and 12-month block bootstrap intervals, and tail calibration at q01, q05, q95, and q99.
  5. Stop rule. The reproduction gate fails (the default equals experiment 322's default 3 to within 0.01 points), or STD is more than 0.10 points worse than the default at the first full run.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• STD: one network trained jointly on a median correction and a three-component mixture on the residual of the frozen core's mean, replacing the median-correction head, the spread table, the night offset's width part, and the solar standard-deviation band step. A two-layer adapter maps the ensemble summaries (temperature and solar response, mean and standard deviation) into the trunk; the other inputs are those of experiments 311 and 220. The as-of calibration of experiment 164 was planned and not applied (see the caveats).
  • STD-A: STD's median correction and adapter, with the default's band construction.
  • References: the default, arm G of experiment 314, BG2 to 168 hours, the manual heuristic, and climatology.

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
• Stage 1 (0.5 to 168 hours). Experiment 311's rows, 24-month pool, and monthly refits (the schedule is P-roll, a contrast of 0.03 points is read on at least six seeds averaged). The core is arm D, which is the default's core below 168 hours.
  • Stage 2 (168 to 240 hours). The stored feature rows end at 168 hours, so the core above 168 hours is the default's stored median and width (experiment 322), and the pool is the stored 168-to-240-hour rows that end before each refit (an expanding pool that starts with the six replicate months). The pooled 0.5-to-240-hour figure is reported only if stage 2 runs; otherwise every headline says "0.5 to 168 hours" and names the missing range as the result's main caveat.

docs.title: Checks to run
docs.text: Median minus mean forecast per site, the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast, leaving one Primary out (D10 carried experiment 311's gain), and the seven audit triggers.

docs.title: Does giving recent rows more weight improve next-month Primary demand forecasts?
docs.text:
Take-home: refitting the additive demand model every month with older rows weighted less improves next month's forecast by about 0.025 points of quantile score (equal weights score 1.499), but training on only the last 24 months gains the same. Smooth recency weights therefore add nothing to a plain 24-month window. Half of the pooled gain comes from one Primary substation, D8, whose demand shifted in 2023. The verdict is not supported: we predicted the best weighting would beat equal weights by at least 0.02 points and would fail if the 24-month window matched it, and the window matched it.

We asked whether, when the additive model (a generalised additive model, GAM) with a Kalman filter on its daily residual is refitted every month, giving older training rows less weight forecasts the next month better. A quantile score of 1.499 means the average loss over 11 forecast quantiles, in percent of a substation's effective capacity. The setup follows experiment 328, whose code and 15 Primary substations we reuse, and the idea follows experiment 17, which found a gain for XGBoost. We refitted each month from 2020-09 to 2026-06 and scored the following month from 2021-09 on past weather (ERA5 reanalysis and CAMS). Half-lives, ridge penalty and Kalman gain were chosen on odd months and scored on even months, then swapped.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms: R0 equal weights on the full history; W24 the last 24 months; H3, H6, H12, and H24 exponential weights with half-lives of 3, 6, 12, and 24 months; SH3, SH6, SH12, and SH24 the same weights with a seasonal bonus (rows within 30 days of the forecast month's mid-date and at least 335 days old count double). "Best half-life" is the H arm chosen on the other half of the months, and "seasonal arm" is the SH arm with that half-life. Weights are normalised to mean 1.
  • Row set: 15 Primaries and 58 monthly origins, with hand-filtered load-shift rows removed. Each month is scored with the settings chosen on the other parity of months.
  • Absolute scores (quantile score, points of capacity): R0 1.499, W24 1.474, H3 1.504, H6 1.476, H12 1.474, H24 1.481, best half-life 1.474, seasonal arm 1.462. Excluding D8: R0 1.359, best half-life 1.347, seasonal arm 1.334. Winter (December to February): R0 1.475, best half-life 1.473.
  • C1, best half-life minus R0: -0.0248 (95% -0.0322 to -0.0171). Each half-life minus R0: H3 +0.0055, H6 -0.0227, H12 -0.0248, H24 -0.0175. The point passes the 0.02 minimum. The 24-month window minus R0 is -0.0243 (95% -0.0321 to -0.0167).
  • C2, best half-life minus W24: -0.0005 (95% -0.0051 to +0.0039). The window matches the best half-life, which is the pre-registered failure condition.
  • C3, seasonal arm minus best half-life: -0.0118 (95% -0.0141 to -0.0095). The seasonal arm scores 1.462, 0.012 points better than W24 (1.474). The seasonal bonus is a candidate and not adopted, because no second period has replicated it.
  • Without D8: C1 is -0.0119 (95% -0.0183 to -0.0054), below the 0.02 minimum. D8's own change is -0.199 points, which contributes 0.0133 of the pooled -0.0248.
  • Winter (December to February): the best half-life minus R0 is -0.0020 (95% -0.0110 to +0.0074), so the weights give no measured winter gain.
  • By year of the forecast origin (post hoc): C1 is +0.027 in 2021 (4 origins), then -0.009, -0.030, -0.031, -0.041 and -0.039 in 2022 to 2026. Weights hurt while history is short and help once several years exist.
  • Tail calibration (best half-life, R0): q01 coverage 0.0117 and 0.0117 (nominal 0.01); q99 coverage 0.0118 and 0.0120 (nominal 0.01); q95 pinball 0.7927 and 0.8052; q99 pinball 0.2487 and 0.2510. Differences: q95 -0.0125, q99 -0.0023, both intervals wholly below zero.
  • Non-inferiority (margin 0.01, one-sided 95%): the pooled upper bound without D8 is -0.0065, a pass. Per Primary, 13 of 14 pass; D5 is worse by +0.0088 (upper +0.0205), a look and not a failure.
  • D8 after its 2023-08-15 break (3 origins): the q99 exceedance rate is 0.1707 for R0 and 0.1752 for the best half-life against a nominal 0.01, so the secondary prediction fails; only H3 is lower (0.1637). Quantile score after the break: R0 6.768, H3 6.323. All arms are far off, so a better forecast of the level did not produce calibrated tails.
  • Effective winters at the last origin (median over Primaries): R0 5.65, H24 4.29, H12 2.82, W24 2.00, H6 1.63, H3 1.09. H3's winter score is 1.534 against 1.475 for R0, which is the noise that about one winter of data produces.
  • Post hoc without the Kalman filter (Kalman gain set to 0): C1 is -0.0327 (95% -0.0561 to -0.0088), and the best half-life minus W24 is -0.0157 (95% -0.0377 to +0.0074). Without the filter the weights may beat the window, but the interval includes zero.
  • Not run: the ENS-scored variant, the curtailment cost, and the manual_heuristic and climatology reference rows, because the lab base is not Primary demand research default 3. This experiment compares weights and not model families, so the standard-architecture arm does not apply.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate: passed. R0 and W24 at ridge 0.1 and gain 0.10 reproduce experiment 328's arms A and B per Primary to 0.0000 points.
  • Placebo: marginal miss. A half-life of 1000 years differs from R0 by up to 0.0012 points (gate 0.001), and by 0.0013 in the no-filter run. We believe the solver tolerance causes the difference and did not test that. The difference is about 17 times smaller than the minimum gain.
  • Known answer: failed. On injected steps of 10% and 25% of load (200 worlds, 8 onsets), H3 is worse than R0 over the first 90 days by +0.212 (95% +0.108 to +0.328) and H12 by +0.025. We tested the explanation that the Kalman filter absorbs a constant step: without the filter H3 is better than R0 by -0.319 (95% -0.563 to -0.043) and H12 by -0.146. The explanation holds, and a constant step cannot test recency weights in a model with a level filter.
  • Leakage: none found. Weights use only the row end time and the cut, fit_gam rejects rows after the cut, the filter level uses earlier days only, and the offsets use the previous 365 days.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed. The offsets are residual quantiles of each arm's own forecast, and the error of the median forecast points the same way as the quantile score (best half-life minus R0 on the mean absolute error of the median: -0.1034, 95% -0.1316 to -0.0737).
  • Audit triggers fired: a failed control (the known-answer test), a result that contradicted its prediction (the injected steps, with the explanation tested), and a gain that halves when one Primary is left out (D8). The other four triggers did not fire. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the experiment.
  • Audit findings, triaged: an independent re-derivation from the raw forecasts agreed with C1, C2, and C3 (accepted). Autocorrelation of the monthly differences is 0.74 at lag 1, and a 6-month-block bootstrap widens C1 to -0.0371 to -0.0133 and C2 to -0.0092 to +0.0043 (accepted, added post hoc; the conclusion is unchanged). Every arm chose the largest ridge (0.3) and gain (0.20), so the selection tested nothing at the edge (accepted as a caveat; a wider grid is advice). The filter uses actuals of earlier days in the forecast month (accepted as a caveat). The gain grows with history (accepted, shown by year).

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Lab conditions: past weather, a one-day-ahead Kalman level inside the scored month, and the month after each origin and not a 1 to 10 day lead. Absolute scores are optimistic, and the contrasts are conditional on the filter.
  • Selection: the cross-fit is a two-way check, not leakage-free, and the bootstrap does not resample the selection of the best half-life from four.
  • Grid edges: ridge 0.3 and gain 0.20 were the largest values offered, in every arm and both halves.
  • Options for later: a change experiment on Primary demand research default 3 could test the 24-month window and the seasonal bonus, with a wider ridge and gain grid.

docs.title: Does masking load shifts found by a label-free detector lower curtailment cost?
docs.text:
Masking the load shifts that a label-free detector finds lowers curtailment cost by about a third when the forecast is judged against the normal running arrangement, but not when it is judged against the power the electricity network carried. A load shift is demand moved from one substation to another for a period. The detector finds load shifts from the power readings alone, with no switching log. Masking means treating the flagged readings as missing when the forecast is corrected. The normal running arrangement is the network layout without any shift. Against observed power, the mask changes cost during and after shifts by -3.0% (95% interval -24% to +30%, from resampling whole worlds) and raises it by 1.3% on ordinary half-hours, the half-hours far from any shift. Adding the true moved megawatts to the true spans lowered during-shift cost, but adding them to the label-free mask did not, so this page cannot say what a live service would need. Verdict: not supported.

We asked whether the quantile-score gain that experiment 327 found for its label-free detect-and-mask pipeline also shows up as lower curtailment cost. Curtailment cost is the cost of cutting generation because a forecast let a substation's flow pass a limit, as defined by experiment 268. We scored experiment 327's forecasts on 44 worlds in which transfers of load between six Primary substations had been injected, and on the real record at one bulk supply point (D13) with its metered solar farms. A Primary has no published limit, so the injected-world costs rank forecasts and state no money saved.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and data
docs.text:
• Arms. C is no mask. A masks the readings a label-free detector flags. B masks with a plain 24-hour residual detector. D masks the true (logged and labelled) spans, as a reference. E is A with a second detection pass. All five are experiment 327's, with its filter hyperparameters and quantile offsets unchanged. The filter was re-run to rebuild the quantiles, which 327 does not store.
  • Injected worlds (Part 1). Experiment 327's inj folder: 44 worlds at six Primaries, even calendar months, 12 to 36 hour leads, arms C, A, B, and D only. The limit is f times the Primary's largest real observed power before 2024-08-04 (before any scored row), the same for every arm and for both targets.
  • Real record (Part 2). The bulk supply point D13 has 7 child Primaries, all with stored forecasts. Its node forecast is the sum of the 7 child forecasts plus quantile offsets fitted on odd months. Its generators are the metered farms A, C, and E and two other generators. Experiment 243's quantile forecast for the farms and experiment 48's for the others are paired by valid time, which is a lab shortcut. D17 lacks one child forecast, so it is not scored.
  • Headline price is GBP 2,000 per MWh, breach ratio 20, Curtailment Limit 0 hours.
  • Not run. The long-and-deep stratum of experiment 327 has too few rows at cost-bearing limits to score. Arm E has no injected-world rows, so it is scored on the real record only.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Deciding contrast (A minus C, during and after pooled, observed power, limit 0.5). GBP 39 lower per half-hour (3.0% of C's GBP 1,291), 95% interval -310 to +392, from 10,149 half-hours. The smallest difference this design resolves is GBP 514. The interval includes zero, so the prediction fails.
  • Ordinary half-hours. A minus C is +GBP 18.7 per half-hour (+1.3%, interval +16.6 to +21.2), above the 1% bound.
  • By group, observed power. During: +295 (+36%, interval +75 to +641). After (48 hours): -213 (-13.8%, interval -604 to +311). Before the alarm: +218 (+17.4%, interval +16 to +547).
  • Against the true series. During and after pooled: -697 (-32.8%, interval -1,126 to -359). During: -1,118 (-35.5%). After: -477 (-29.9%). B minus C is -334 (-15.7%), D minus C is -986 (-46.4%), and A minus B is -363 (interval -654 to -118).
  • Moved megawatts added back (observed power, as experiment 312's perfect-megawatts arm). D with them: during -139 (-17.1%, interval -242 to -30). A with them: during +134 (interval -196 to +458), pooled -94 (interval -399 to +289). The true megawatts are used, so these are upper bounds.
  • Leave one Primary out (deciding contrast). Without D11: -117 (interval -223 to +2). Without D16: +46 (interval -301 to +599). Per Primary, D14 (-362, interval -654 to -66) and D16 (-282, interval -476 to -101) gain, and none of the other four has an interval below zero.
  • Winter (November to March), observed power. During: +339 (interval +75 to +613, 176 half-hours). After: -134 (interval -389 to +113, 596 half-hours).
  • Limit sensitivity (observed power, A minus C, during and after). At 0.75 the base cost is GBP 16 per half-hour and the difference is +17.5 (interval -4.9 to +64). At 0.9 no cost arises. Neither the 0.75 nor the 0.9 result is evidence.
  • Real record at D13, ordinary half-hours, limit 0.5 (12,544 distinct half-hours; 9,344 rows, each an origin and lead pair, were excluded because a span or label masks a child's target). Cost: C GBP 6.41 million, A 6.47 million, B 6.41 million, D 6.38 million, perfect forecast 0.45 million. A minus C is +GBP 56,300 (+0.9%, interval 0 to +160,494) against a smallest resolvable difference of GBP 138,727. B minus C is +3,349 (interval -8,258 to +18,306). Cost arises in April and June only. The after-shift groups hold no rows in the farm window.
  • Tails. Quantile q01 and q99 coverage were not recomputed here. Experiment 327 reports them.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, and the mean-forecast error beside each contrast. Not applicable. No forecast was trained, and the stored mean-forecast errors are experiment 327's.
  • Triggers fired. Three of the seven audit triggers fired. First, a control failed: the true-span arm D loses to arm C during a shift on observed power. Second, the result contradicts its own prediction. The add-back arm supports the moved-megawatts explanation for the true spans (D) and not for the label-free mask (A). Third, leaving one Primary out flips the sign of the point estimate (without D16 it is +46), but the interval includes zero with and without D16, so the verdict does not change.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the deciding contrast from the raw files with its own code, in place of an Opus audit, because this run was set to use no Opus. It found GBP 38.9 lower per half-hour (interval -309 to +388), ordinary +18.68 (+1.27%), and both leave-one-out values, with no error. A single world holds 22% to 41% of the pooled difference at D11 and D16, which is why the intervals resample whole worlds. The files hold both the earlier and the scored periods, and both are used, as in experiment 327.
  • Weak node forecast. At D13 the NGED baseline (generators assumed at capacity, an assumption NGED has not confirmed) costs GBP 5.89 million, below every demand arm. The node forecast, which ignores the farms, is the weak link, so the real-record levels are not money saved. Arm contrasts share that weakness.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the mask together with an estimate of the moved megawatts. The true spans with the true megawatts added back lowered during-shift cost, and the label-free mask with them added back did not. Experiment 312 scored the megawatts with oracle values.
  • Score the real record on a node that carries more shifts. D13 has no after-shift rows in the farm window, so a longer farm forecast history is needed before the money question can be asked of real data.

docs.title: Does a pre-trained time-series foundation model, used without training, forecast Primary demand as well as Primary demand research default 3?
docs.text:
Take-home: A pre-trained foundation model, Chronos-2, forecasts the demand of six Primary substations clearly worse than Primary demand research default 3 (called "the default" below), at every lead time from 0.5 to 240 hours (10 days). A lead time is how far ahead of the forecast time a half-hour lies. Scores are quantile scores in percentage points of each substation's effective capacity, and lower is better. Chronos-2 given only each substation's own history (Z0) scores 0.65 points worse than the default (95% interval +0.42 to +0.91). With extra inputs known in advance, called covariates (Z1), it scores 0.55 points worse (+0.35 to +0.79), so the covariates close about one sixth of the gap (0.65 down to 0.55 points). They help on cold winter nights and make sunny daylight worse. The 0.5 to 240 hour range is the 1 to 10 day horizon that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) needs.

We tested whether a foundation model that never saw our data can match the default. The foundation model is a neural network pre-trained on a large collection of unrelated time series. Chronos-2 (Ansari et al., 2025) is published under the Apache-2.0 licence with 120 million parameters, and we ran it without fine-tuning. We ran two arms: Z0 uses the substation's own history only, and Z1 adds five covariates (the ensemble-mean temperature forecast, the sun's elevation, the local half-hour of the day, the day of the week, and a bank-holiday flag). At each 09:00 UTC forecast time, Chronos-2 saw the 8 weeks of readings that had arrived by then (the newest ended 3.5 hours earlier) and forecast the next 10 days at 11 quantile levels. The six Primaries are called D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 below. The default is the convex stack of experiments 251 and 322, which supply the rows, the metric, and the stored forecasts of the default. The manual heuristic is a rule that mimics NGED's manual forecast, and climatology is the typical demand for the same month, half-hour, and day type.

Arm Quantile score, 0.5 to 240 hours Default 2.733 Z0 (history only) 3.387 Z1 (with covariates) 3.286 Manual heuristic 3.421 Climatology 3.668

Figures 1 to 3 show the score by lead band, the gap to the default by lead band, and the gap by group of half-hours.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Every arm trails the default, and the reproduction gate passed. The scored year has 788,004 rows at six Primaries (2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, 09:00 UTC forecast times, rows outside the hand-filtered events). Rebuilt from stored files, the default scores 2.733 at 0.5 to 240 hours and 3.078 at 168 to 240 hours, against 2.727 and 3.077 in experiment 322, within the 0.01 tolerance.
  • Z0 trails the default by 0.653 points (95% interval +0.423 to +0.909; without D10 +0.657, +0.445 to +0.903). The first half of prediction P1 holds, because the gap exceeds 0.50.
  • Z0 beats the manual heuristic at short leads only. The differences are -0.78 at 0 to 24 hours, -0.49 at 24 to 48 hours, and -0.25 at 48 to 72 hours, all with intervals below zero. At 72 to 96 hours the difference is -0.12 (interval -0.29 to +0.03). Z0 is level with the heuristic from 96 to 144 hours (-0.01 and +0.06 points) and trails it clearly from 144 hours (+0.11 at 144 to 168 hours, +0.50 at 216 to 240 hours). The second half of P1 fails, because it predicted that Z0 trails the heuristic beyond 48 hours.
  • A likely reason is that Z0 sees the recent demand level and the manual heuristic does not, so Z0's advantage fades as the lead grows. The lead trend fits this explanation, and we did not test it further.
  • Z1 trails the default by 0.552 points (95% interval +0.354 to +0.791; without D10 +0.573, +0.374 to +0.812). Prediction P2 fails: Z1 closes 16% of the Z0 gap at 24 to 120 hours (+0.636 for Z0, +0.534 for Z1), against the predicted half. Prediction P3 holds, because the smallest gap in any 24-hour band is +0.44 (Z1, 0 to 24 hours), far above 0.03.
  • We cannot say Z1 is better than Z0 overall. Z1 minus Z0 is -0.101 (-0.294 to +0.040). The sign differs by group (figure 3): cold winter nights -2.57 (-3.30 to -1.31), all other half-hours -0.17 (-0.36 to -0.02), sunny daylight +0.43 (+0.21 to +0.76).
  • Groups scored separately because they matter to NGED, Z0 and Z1 against the default (0.5 to 240 hours): cold winter nights +4.39 and +1.83, sunny daylight +0.61 and +1.04, all other half-hours +0.62 and +0.45. On cold winter nights the scores are 2.77 for the default, 7.16 for Z0, 4.59 for Z1, and 6.63 for the manual heuristic.
  • Z0 and Z1 are worse than the default in both tails. Pinball loss at the 1st-percentile quantile is 0.188 for the default and 0.226 for both arms. At the 99th percentile it is 0.220 for the default, 0.270 for Z0, and 0.240 for Z1. Coverage at the 1st percentile is 1.5% for the default, 0.9% for Z0, and 1.6% for Z1, and at the 99th percentile 98.4%, 98.6%, and 98.8%. Threshold-weighted CRPS (at each Primary's own 90th-percentile demand) is 0.306, 0.420, and 0.395.
  • Quantile score by 24-hour lead band (default, Z0, Z1): 0 to 24 hours 2.175, 2.647, 2.616; 96 to 120 hours 2.688, 3.330, 3.238; 216 to 240 hours 3.091, 3.920, 3.838.
  • Z2 (a fine-tune of a few training steps) did not run. Its rule needed Z1 within 0.30 points of the default in some 24-hour band, and the smallest gap is 0.44. The second stop rule did not fire either, because both arms beat the manual heuristic by a wide margin at 0 to 24 hours.
  • How a reader could explain one forecast: a Z0 forecast is a function of the previous 8 weeks of readings through a transformer neural network with 120 million parameters, so no input can be named. Z1 adds five named covariates, but their effect is not separable. A forecast from the generalised additive model (GAM) in the default has one named term per input, such as temperature, the sun's elevation, and the calendar, and each term can be read as a curve.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: no information. Chronos-2 returns its median as its mean, so the difference is exactly 0.00 at every Primary. The mean absolute error of the median forecast is 6.02 percentage points of capacity for Z0, 5.86 for Z1, and 4.77 for the default, the same ranking as the quantile score.
  • Quantile score per Primary (default, Z0, Z1): D5 3.52, 4.10, 4.06; D9 2.50, 3.10, 2.80; D10 3.41, 4.04, 3.86; D11 2.41, 3.33, 3.38; D14 2.09, 2.69, 2.62; D16 2.57, 3.13, 3.08. Z0 and Z1 both trail the default at all six Primaries.
  • Audit triggers: none fired on a headline contrast. The audit rule tests seven conditions, such as a failed control, a result that contradicts its own prediction, a gap that changes sign when one Primary is left out, and a nested arm that beats the arm containing it. The one near miss is the second half of P1, where Z0 beats the manual heuristic out to 72 hours; the lead trend is consistent with the explanation above, and the gap to the default does not depend on it. Leaving out any one Primary keeps both gaps above +0.4. Z1's overall gain over Z0 is not established, and Z1 is worse than Z0 on sunny daylight; the page reports that split as a result.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Z1 holds the last temperature of a truncated weather run. Where a numerical weather prediction run ends before 240 hours, Z1 repeats that run's last temperature, because a later run is not known at forecast time.
  • The covariates are weaker than the default's weather inputs. The temperature covariate is the ensemble-mean 24-hour mean temperature, and for past half-hours it comes from the weather run with the shortest lead. Both are available at forecast time. The sun's elevation is computed from the date and location. Neither the temperature nor the elevation carries cloud, so Z1's solar input is weaker than the default's.
  • One foundation model and one context length: Chronos-2 with 8 weeks of context and its default quantile outputs. TimesFM, Moirai, and Toto were not run, because Chronos-2 alone accepts the covariates that Z1 needs.
  • Next: score a foundation-model forecast alone against the default, on cold winter nights and on sunny daylight as well as overall, before using it as a blend member, and test a solar input that includes cloud cover.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: The plan below was fixed before any score was read.

docs.title: Foundation-model choice
docs.text:
• Chronos-2 (amazon/chronos-2): Apache-2.0 licence, 478 MB of weights, accepts covariates.
  • Not run: TimesFM, Moirai, and Toto, which would have repeated Z0 without giving Z1.

docs.title: The five plan items
docs.text:
1. Question. How far behind research default 3 is a zero-shot foundation model, by lead band?
  2. Prediction that can fail. P1 to P3 in the front matter.
  3. Rows and period. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, 09:00 UTC forecast times, all rows except those in hand-filtered events.
  4. Metric. The quantile score over 11 levels in percentage points of effective capacity.
  5. Stop rule. In the front matter.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• Z0: history only; the context is 2688 half-hours ending 3.5 hours before the forecast time.
  • Z1: Z0 plus the ensemble-mean 24-hour temperature, the sun's elevation, the local half-hour of day, the day of week, and a bank-holiday flag, all known at forecast time.
  • Z2: only if the rule in the front matter holds; it did not.
  • References: the default, the manual heuristic, and climatology.

docs.title: Does a neural network that replaces the whole convex stack (a mixture-density network, a recurrent network, or a temporal fusion transformer) forecast Primary demand better than Primary demand research default 3?
docs.text:
Take-home: None of four neural networks that replace the whole forecasting stack beats Primary demand research default 3, so the stack stays.
