Research default 3 is the current best research forecast of the demand at 33/11 kV substations ("Primaries"): a generalised additive model (GAM, a sum of smooth, named terms for heating, lighting, and solar) with a Kalman filter that tracks its recent errors. The best neural network (R) trails the default by 0.041 points at 0.5 to 240 hours, and the other three trail it by more. Scores are quantile scores: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of effective capacity (percent of the substation's rated capacity), and lower is better. Gaps are the neural network's score minus the default's, so a positive gap means the neural network is worse.

We asked whether a neural network with no GAM and no Kalman filter could forecast demand at six Primaries at least as well as the default over leads of 0.5 to 240 hours. The four neural networks were M1 (a mixture-density network, Bishop (1994)), M2 (M1 given an explicit unmetered-solar signal instead of the weather inputs), R (a gated recurrent unit that encodes the past 7 days of power and decodes the 480 half-hours of the forecast), and T (a compact temporal fusion transformer, Lim et al. (2021)). All four were refitted monthly on the rows and refit dates of experiments 311 and 330, and calibrated with the as-of temperature-class widening of experiment 164. No neural network came out ahead of the default. The maintainer decides what counts as a decisive improvement, and no arm is called a candidate for production.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Terms: STD is experiment 330's standard architecture (a small neural network added on top of the default's stack, scored to 168 hours only); BG2 is the earlier best-guess stack, scored to 168 hours; a cold winter night is a November-to-March half-hour between 18:00 and 07:00 local time, after dark, on a day flagged cold (day-mean temperature below 2 °C); sunny daylight is a daylight half-hour that experiment 178's rows flag as sunny; D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 are the anonymised labels of the six Primaries.
  • Lead range: 0.5 to 240 hours on every headline. Scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, six Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16), 797,756 half-hours with a reading outside the hand-filtered events, origin 09:00 UTC. Intervals resample the 12 forecast-origin months. Monthly refits on a 24-month pool (the P-roll cadence), so these are not weekly-refit scores.
  • Reproduction gate: the default rebuilt from experiments 251 and 322 scores 2.722 on the common rows against 2.727 stored (limit 0.01), so the gate passes. 360 reference rows at D5 and D16 (origins 2026-01-06 and 2026-01-08, leads 171.5 to 240 hours) have no network forecast and are left out of every arm.
  • Absolute scores, 0.5 to 240 hours: default 2.722, M1 2.890, M2 2.929, R 2.763, T 2.790, manual heuristic 3.413, climatology 3.663. At 0.5 to 168 hours only: default 2.579, STD (experiment 330) 2.525, BG2 2.715, M1 2.798, M2 2.831, R 2.666, T 2.674.
  • Gap to the default (positive is worse), 0.5 to 240 hours, 95% interval, with D10 left out in brackets: M1 +0.168 (+0.036 to +0.308) [+0.187]; M2 +0.207 (+0.044 to +0.373) [+0.232]; R +0.041 (-0.053 to +0.146) [+0.069]; T +0.068 (-0.023 to +0.161) [+0.098].
  • By lead range: R +0.087 at 0.5 to 168 hours (-0.007 to +0.194) and -0.068 at 168 to 240 hours (-0.218 to +0.086). T +0.095 (+0.003 to +0.187) and +0.004 (-0.146 to +0.158). M1 +0.219 and +0.047. M2 +0.252 and +0.101.
  • Gap of the best network to experiment 330's STD (the standard architecture), 0.5 to 168 hours: R trails STD by 0.140 points (95% interval +0.044 to +0.253), 5.6% relative. STD is 0.053 better than the default at those leads, so the standard architecture on top of the stack is the one neural arm scored on these rows that beat the default (at 0.5 to 168 hours).
  • Pairwise: R minus M1 -0.127 (-0.175 to -0.077); T minus M1 -0.100 (-0.167 to -0.047); M2 minus M1 +0.039 (-0.012 to +0.099); T minus R +0.027 (-0.025 to +0.076).
  • Protected groups, gap to the default (95% interval): cold winter nights M1 +0.734 (+0.180 to +1.558), M2 +0.777 (+0.213 to +1.635), R +0.315 (-0.502 to +1.447), T +0.774 (-0.283 to +1.981); sunny daylight M1 +0.063 (-0.208 to +0.303), M2 -0.222 (-0.521 to +0.007), R -0.032 (-0.368 to +0.265), T +0.021 (-0.292 to +0.310). Threshold-weighted score at the 95th percentile relative to the default: M1 +4.3%, M2 +5.5%, R -0.6%, T -0.3%. The research-default page's no-harm tolerances are not shown to be met by any arm on cold winter nights (tolerances: 0.02 pooled, 0.05 for q01 pinball, q99 pinball, cold winter nights, and sunny daylight, and 2% relative for the threshold-weighted score). T also has a q01 pinball loss 0.027 above the default's (95% interval +0.010 to +0.047). R beats the default in 7 of the 12 forecast-origin months.
  • Tail calibration (all rows; q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage; pinball at q01 and q99): default 0.014, 0.051, 0.952, 0.984; 0.186, 0.218. M1 0.009, 0.039, 0.915, 0.982; 0.185, 0.219. M2 0.007, 0.032, 0.910, 0.981; 0.185, 0.224. R 0.010, 0.040, 0.918, 0.983; 0.176, 0.215. T 0.011, 0.042, 0.932, 0.986; 0.214, 0.220. All four networks under-cover the upper tail at q95.
  • Replicate year (even months of 2024-25, 0.5 to 168 hours, against experiment 169's arm A bands as the reference, 3 seeds): M1 +0.206 (+0.157 to +0.256), M2 +0.175 (+0.119 to +0.230), R +0.033 (-0.022 to +0.085), T +0.048 (+0.004 to +0.091); absolute reference 2.589, R 2.622, T 2.637. The gaps have the same sign as in the scored year, and R beats T in both years. M1 and M2 swap order: M2 beats M1 by 0.031 points in the replicate year, which carries M2's disclosed D9 capacity leak.
  • Predictions: P1 holds (M1 trails by 0.168, above the predicted 0.10). P2 fails: M2 trails M1 by 0.039 instead of beating it by 0.03. P3 fails: R and T beat M1 by 0.127 and 0.100, not by under 0.03. P4: a single seed varies by 0.021 to 0.043 points (standard deviation of the pooled score across six seeds), above the 0.01 to 0.02 that experiment 325 found for the stack, so every contrast is read on the six-seed average. The stop rule did not fire: the gate passed, and no arm trails the default by more than 0.30 at every lead band.
  • Explaining one forecast: M1, M2, R, and T are opaque. For M1 and M2 a reader can ablate inputs or read permutation importance (about 34 inputs in 2 hidden layers of 64 units); for R and T the past 7 days of power also feed in, and T's variable-selection weights and attention weights give a partial account. None gives the named heating, lighting, and solar terms of the GAM.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean of the 11 quantiles, per site (points): the networks sit 0.07 to 1.5 below their quantile means (D10 -1.3 to -1.5 for M1, M2, and R, against -0.43 for the default), The offsets show that the forecast distributions of the neural networks are skewed upward at D10. The default's offsets are -0.43 to +0.19.
  • Error of the forecast beside the quantile score: mean absolute error of the median forecast: default 4.75, M1 5.15, M2 5.21, R 4.92, T 4.87; the order agrees with the quantile score except that T's median is as good as the default's within 0.13.
  • Triggers fired: the trigger for a result that contradicts its own prediction (M2 against P2) and the trigger for a leave-one-out sign flip (leaving out D11 turns R's gap to -0.004, though both intervals span zero). An independent audit re-derived every headline number from the stored fits and reproduced them to four decimals; it found no defect that changes a sign or verdict.
  • M2 against M1, tested: the post hoc arm M2D (M2 plus darkness and sun elevation, 6 seeds) scores 2.919 pooled, recovering only 0.010 of the 0.039 gap to M1, so the missing sun-geometry inputs are not the main cause. The audit locates the loss on daylight without strong sun (M2 +0.271 against M1) and in spring and early summer; M2 is 0.285 better on sunny daylight. A possible explanation, not tested here, is that M2 lacks the shortwave and solar-term inputs that carry cloud information.
  • Calibration: the as-of calibration of experiment 164 helps M1, M2, and R by 0.013 to 0.021 points and hurts T by 0.010, almost all in 2026-01. It leaves calibrated q95 coverage on cold winter nights at 0.87 to 0.90.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Inputs differ from the default's: the stack's recent-error features (experiment 220) do not exist without the stack, so recent power stands in for them. The store holds ensemble means of temperature and shortwave only, so member spread and wind are not inputs. M2's explicit solar signal omits the D5 export clip, and its pinned capacity uses a later vintage for D9 before 2025-04 (a disclosed leak in the replicate year only).
  • Seed averaging favours the networks slightly: each network averages 6 seeds in quantile space, the default's forecasts below 168 hours average 3 fits, and above 168 hours they are one fit. A single R seed scores 2.82 to 2.87, so the six-seed average is 0.06 to 0.11 better than a single fit; the default still wins.
  • Code: all arms share the input table e00334_prep.py, the refit logic e00334_fit.py, and e00334_score.py (scripts of experiments 164, 278, 311, 317, 320, and 322 are imported). The temporal fusion transformer is compact: one shared gated residual network after variable selection, hidden size 16, one head, chosen from three configurations on validation loss (pre-registered).
  • Not scored: the curtailment-cost saving against the manual heuristic, because this experiment forecasts demand only and has no generator forecasts.
  • Next: if a neural part is wanted, build it on top of the stack (experiment 330's STD), and test R's past-week encoder as the input adapter there. The result does not support a replacement; building a neural part on top of the stack is the option the evidence favours.

docs.title: Can a per-lead-band calibration of the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles bring the tails of Primary demand research default 3 to nominal at every lead from 0.5 to 240 hours?
Take-home message
docs.text:
Primary demand research default 3 is already close to calibrated at 1 to 10 days, and tail calibrations fitted on earlier months do not improve it. Primary demand research default 3 is our demand forecast that our experiments currently treat as the one to beat, for six Primary substations (anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16), up to 10 days ahead, for National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED). We asked whether correcting its 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles, with a different correction for each 24-hour lead band and each kind of half-hour (season, day or night, forecast cold night), brings the share of observations beyond each quantile to nominal. Three corrections were tested, each fitted only on origins completed before each month: C1 widens or narrows each tail by a table of factors (the recipe of experiments 160 and 164 in every band), C2 replaces the tails with a Student-t fitted to the errors, and C3 is adaptive conformal prediction (Gibbs and Candès (2021)) with a 60-day window. No correction reaches nominal: the share below q01 stays at 0.6% to 1.6% (the default: 1.1% to 1.95%). The quantile score, twice the mean pinball loss in points of effective capacity, does not improve (C1 +0.0014, 95% interval -0.0019 to +0.0054 points), and the q01 and q99 pinball loss rises by 0.003 to 0.011 points. Fitting the C1 table in-sample on the scored year gives 1.00% in every band and lowers the score by 0.0038 points. That shows the table can describe the year, and does not show that the miss repeats across years, which this experiment did not test.

Horizon: leads 0.5 to 240 hours (NGED's 1 to 10 days). Retraining schedule: the stored forecasts of experiment 322 are used unchanged, so no model was refitted here. The check that this experiment reproduces experiment 322's scores passed: the default scores 2.7265 at 0.5 to 240 hours and 3.0767 at 168 to 240 hours (expected 2.727 and 3.077).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms: default (Primary demand research default 3); C1 (factor on the distance of q01, q05, q95, and q99 from the median, per band and group, bounded 0.8 to 1.6, shrunk to 1 under 500 half-hours per cell, interior quantiles unchanged apart from a sort); C2 (Student-t tail beyond q10 and q90); C3 (adaptive conformal, step 0.005, 60 days, per band, no groups). Groups: Apr-Oct day, Apr-Oct night, Nov-Mar day, Nov-Mar night, Nov-Mar forecast cold night (at least half of the 51 members below 3 °C; the member share is missing below 168 hours, so those half-hours fall in "Nov-Mar night").
  • Rows: fold_a_daily_gap_v1, six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, origin 09:00 UTC, 798,116 half-hours outside hand-filtered events. History for the fits is the replicate year (even months of 2024-25, 168 to 240 hours only) plus earlier scored months, so the first cuts have no history below 168 hours and use a factor of 1 there.
  • Quantile score at 0.5 to 240 hours: default 2.7265; C1 2.7280; C2 2.7321; C3 2.7319; manual heuristic 3.4143; climatology 3.6644. BG2 is not scored past 168 hours. At 168 to 240 hours the default scores 3.0767 and C1, C2, and C3 score 3.0786, 3.0839, and 3.0858.
  • Contrasts against the default (0.5 to 240 hours, 95% interval, 12 origin-month blocks): C1 +0.0014 (-0.0019 to +0.0054); C2 +0.0056 (+0.0012 to +0.0098); C3 +0.0054 (+0.0002 to +0.0116). Threshold-weighted continuous ranked probability score (twCRPS): C1 +0.0004, C2 +0.0012, C3 +0.0016 (each interval includes zero except C3 against C1).
  • Tail calibration (pinball difference against the default, 0.5 to 240 hours; positive is worse):
Arm q01 q05 q95 q99 C1 +0.0032 +0.0059 -0.0004 +0.0026 C2 +0.0082 +0.0044 +0.0072 +0.0107 C3 +0.0028 +0.0093 +0.0073 +0.0112
  • Share below q01 by lead band, per cent (nominal 1): default 1.1 to 1.95; C1 1.0 to 1.6; C2 0.6 to 1.4; C3 1.0 to 1.3.
  • Share above q99 by lead band, per cent (nominal 1): default 1.4 to 1.9; C1 1.5 to 1.7; C2 0.7 to 1.3; C3 1.1 to 1.4.
  • Coverage of the 5% to 95% band (nominal 90%): default 89.3% to 90.9%; C3 89.4% to 89.9%.
  • Worst month: the largest tail miss in one month is 3.4 points for the default, 2.9 for C1, 2.5 for C2, and 1.6 for C3.
  • Cold winter nights: C1 lowers the score by 0.014 points (95% interval -0.028 to 0.000) at 0.5 to 240 hours. The share above q95 at 216 to 240 hours stays at 9.6% to 10% under every arm (nominal 5%), and at 168 to 216 hours C1 brings it from 7.2% to 5.2% and from 7.1% to 5.8%.
  • Sunny daylight: no arm changes the score by more than 0.009 points (all intervals include zero).
  • In-sample fit (post hoc): the C1 table fitted on the scored year itself gives 1.00% below q01 and above q99 in every band, apart from 1.02% to 1.06% below q01 past 192 hours, and lowers the score by 0.0038 points.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary: D5 +0.04, D9 -0.24, D10 -0.43, D11 -0.02, D14 +0.18, D16 +0.19 points for the default. The values differ by arm because the mean of the 11 quantiles moves with the tails (D10: C1 -0.26, C2 -0.64, C3 -0.47; D9: C1 -0.17, C2 -0.33, C3 -0.29).
  • Error of the median forecast beside each contrast: mean absolute error 4.7523 points for every arm, so the contrasts above come from the tails only.
  • Triggers: trigger 2 fired for the prediction that C1 brings the tail shares within 0.3 points of 1%. The in-sample fit above reaches 1.00% with the same method, which shows the method is not the limit, so no audit was run. Leaving one Primary out does not change the sign of any contrast. No other trigger fired.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Predictions: stage 0 predicted a miss of at least 0.8 points at every band past 96 hours, and the miss was 0.45 to 0.95 points, so that prediction failed in part. The prediction for C1 (PC1) failed, because the tail shares stay beyond 0.3 points of 1% and the q01 and q99 pinball loss does not improve by 0.03 points. The prediction for C2 (PC2) failed, because at 168 to 240 hours C2 improves q01 pinball over C1 by only 0.0059 points and worsens q99 pinball by 0.0203. The prediction for C3 (PC3) failed, because the 5% to 95% band of C3 misses 90% by 5.5 percentage points in its worst month (the prediction was within 3 points), although its worst-month tail miss is 1.3 points smaller than C1's.
  • The curtailment-cost metric was not scored: the metric needs an electricity-network node with generators attached, and the Primary demand series have none.
  • The replicate-year rows carry no day or night flag, so they enter the day cell of their season and the night cells and the forecast-cold-night cell get no replicate history. C2 factors are not bounded to 0.8 to 1.6 (3.6% of cells fall outside) and C2 does not shrink thin cells.
  • The history below 168 hours is short for the first cuts of the scored year (see Rows), which makes C1 and C2 weaker there.
  • Next: a forecast-model input feature for the cold-winter-night upper tail at 216 to 240 hours, and a calibration that adapts within the year (a faster conformal update) only if NGED need the tail shares at 1.0%.

docs.title: Does setting the wind forecast to zero where the wind speed is below the turbines' cut-in speed improve Wind farms research default 1?
docs.text: Take-home: setting the wind forecast, or the training target, to zero below the turbines' cut-in speed does not improve the forecast, and the one change that gains, dropping the low-wind rows from training, mostly lifts the quantiles upward. We tested the maintainer's proposal that rows below the turbines' cut-in speed (the speed at which a turbine starts to turn) are noise and should be zeroed. The default is Wind farms research default 1, the current best wind forecast: an XGBoost quantile model (gradient-boosted trees) fitted to ERA5 (our estimate of past weather), run on the 51 members of the ensemble forecast from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), plus an offset table that shifts each forecast quantile by an amount fitted on 442 daily hindcast runs. We scored three readings on the three metered wind farms (W1 to W3), at 1 to 10 day leads. The score is a quantile score over 11 quantile levels in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better), on the kept rows, which are the half-hours that the mask of experiment 210 does not flag as idle-band readings. The default scores 11.352. Zeroing the forecast where the ensemble-mean wind speed is below cut-in (x1) scored 0.004 points worse, and zeroing the training target there (x3) scored 0.001 points worse. Dropping the low-wind rows from training (x2) scored 0.117 better (99.67% interval -0.160 to -0.059; the interval re-draws whole months and seeds, at the level for three arms), but an audit by the Sonnet language model traced most of that to an upward shift of the quantiles, so the verdict is partly supported and x2 stays a candidate.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Plan. Committed before any score, in the first commit of this branch. The prediction text for x2 on the ensemble was written with the wrong sign (it said "raises (worse)"); the brief and experiment 276 say dropping rows lowered the score by 0.03 to 0.1 with the ensemble as weather. Read against that, x2's gain of 0.117 is a little above the predicted range.
  • Family and default. Experiment 326's default (XGBoost fitted once on ERA5 before 2024-04-01, offset table fitted once on the hindcast), rows fold_a_tuesdays_v1, 3 farms, 3 seeds, 107,121 scored half-hours. The XGBoost models are not refitted quarterly. Tier 2 for x2 and x3 (inside the fitted stage), tier 1 for x1; minimum gain 0 for all three.
  • Cut-in speeds from experiment 230's fitted power curve: W1 2.69, W2 2.85, W3 3.38 m/s (all inside 2 to 5 m/s). Sensitivity: plus and minus 1 m/s, and 3.0 m/s.
  • Arms. x1: all 11 quantiles set to zero when the ensemble-mean 100 m speed is below cut-in (variants: every member below cut-in; each member zeroed on its own speed before pooling, x1m). x2: ERA5 rows below cut-in dropped from XGBoost training and from the offset table's cases (x2e also drops the experiment 210 rows). x3: training target set to zero on those rows. Interval level 99.67% (three arms), months and seeds resampled, farms not resampled.
  • Controls. Reproduction gate: the refit default equals experiment 303's P1 exactly (11.352, difference 0). Shuffled-mask placebos (same share of rows at random within farm and month). Leakage check: the forecast masks read only ensemble members, and their mean speed equals experiment 307's (largest difference 3e-6 m/s). The known-answer test confirms the mask flags every synthetic row below cut-in and none above it, but it calls the same one-line comparison that it tests, so it cannot fail and is weak evidence.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
| Arm | Kept rows | All half-hours | Days 1 to 2 | Days 3 to 10 | 0.01 pinball | 0.99 pinball | 5%-95% coverage | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Default | 11.352 | 10.825 | 6.612 | 11.759 | 0.284 | 0.640 | 92.1% | | x1 zero forecast | 11.356 | 10.837 | 6.643 | 11.766 | 0.284 | 0.649 | 92.0% | | x2 drop training rows | 11.235 | 10.777 | 6.597 | 11.705 | 0.284 | 0.638 | 91.4% | | x3 zero training target | 11.353 | 10.831 | 6.635 | 11.761 | 0.284 | 0.641 | 92.2% |

  • x1 minus default: +0.004 on the kept rows (99.67% interval 0.000 to 0.012), +0.012 on all half-hours (0.002 to 0.037). The forecast rule is slightly worse. On the 0.77% of half-hours it zeroes, the score rises from 2.39 to 3.92, so the farms produce small real output there. A cut-in 1 m/s higher is worse (+0.048, 0.012 to 0.116); 1 m/s lower and "every member below cut-in" do nothing (+0.000). Zeroing each member on its own speed (x1m) gives +0.002 (-0.010 to +0.014). Predicted: kept rows lower by under 0.05. The kept-rows prediction had the wrong sign.
  • x2 minus default: -0.117 on the kept rows (-0.160 to -0.059), -0.048 on all half-hours (-0.099 to +0.003). The gain is -0.015 at days 1 to 2 and -0.055 at days 3 to 10. The gain is negative at each farm (-0.129, -0.115, -0.107) and without any one farm (-0.111, -0.119, -0.122), and in 11 of 12 months. The score on the rows below the ERA5 cut-in rises from 5.37 to 6.00. A higher cut-in gains more (x2hi -0.202, x2e -0.205) and a lower one less (x2lo -0.046), and the random-row placebo gains 0.007, 6% of x2's gain.
  • x3 minus default: +0.001 (-0.010 to +0.012). No better than x2, as predicted. The x3 placebo (random rows zeroed) is 0.058 worse.
  • Replicate period (January to June 2025, 6 months). x2 gains 0.079 on the kept rows. The 99.67% interval (-0.150 to +0.006) includes zero, while a t test on the 6 monthly differences gives p = 0.04, so the sign is supported and the size is uncertain. x1 is worse by 0.002, x3 better by 0.009 (-0.026 to +0.010).
  • How much each mask covers. The ERA5 rule flags 5.4% of scored half-hours (4.7%, 4.8%, and 6.8% at W1, W2, and W3). Of those, 99.9% lie inside experiment 210's mask, and they are 54% of the mask's rows, so the speed rule misses 46% of the idle half-hours (predicted: covers under half; it covers slightly more). The ensemble-mean rule flags 0.77% of half-hours and 7% of the mask's rows. The rule "every member below cut-in" flags 0.03%.
  • Evaluation-only variants (descriptive, never adopted). c1: the default scores 11.136 on the rows outside the ERA5 mask and 10.891 outside the ensemble-mean mask, against 10.825 on all half-hours, so "scoring only the rows above cut-in" is just a different row set. c2: scoring the default against a target set to zero on the ERA5-masked rows gives 10.875 on all half-hours against 10.825 against observed power, and no change on the kept rows.
  • Tails. No main arm raises the 0.01 pinball loss (upper 95% bound at most +0.0001) or the 0.99 pinball loss (at most +0.017) by more than 0.05. The x1 variant with a 1 m/s higher cut-in raises the 0.99 pinball loss by 0.093, and the random-row placebo of x1 by 0.165.
  • Benchmarks, kept rows. The default scores 11.352. The default without the offset table scores 11.697, so the table gains 0.345 (95% interval 0.274 to 0.418). Climatology scores 13.547, so the default is 2.195 better (1.577 to 2.808). Persistence is scored on hours 0 to 6 only (1,696 kept rows): 15.566 against the default's 6.568 on the same rows.

docs.title: Adoption conditions for x2 (the only arm that gains)
docs.text:
• 1, gain: met on the kept rows (interval wholly below zero, gain 0.117 above minimum 0).
  • 2, no harm: met. Upper 95% bounds of the harm are +0.00004 at 0.01 and +0.00007 at 0.99, against 0.05. Reported without pass or fail: the score on the rows it masks worsens by 0.63, and the 5%-95% coverage falls from 92.1% to 91.4% (90.1% against 91.5% on all half-hours).
  • 3, replication: met (same sign; the t test supports it).
  • 4, controls and audit: the audit leaves x2 a candidate. Trigger 3 fired (below). A Sonnet audit re-derived the gain from the stored predictions and confirmed it, then found its cause.
  • 5, serving: met. x2 changes training only, so no serving-path change is needed.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
An audit trigger is one of the seven conditions in the ml-experiment skill that sends a result to a fresh reviewer before it merges. Trigger 2 is a result that contradicts its own prediction, trigger 3 is a quantile-score contrast that disagrees with the mean-forecast error, trigger 4 is a sign flip when one farm is left out, and trigger 5 is a control that moves the score. "Tier 1" and "tier 2" are the research-default rule's names for changes that act on stored forecasts and inside a fitted stage. "P1" is experiment 303's name for the default.

  • Median minus mean forecast, kept rows. Default -4.805 points, x2 -4.737, x1 -4.804.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. x2: quantile score -0.117, absolute error of the median -0.176, but absolute error of the mean forecast +0.032 (replicate +0.117). x1 and x3 move all three measures by under 0.01. Trigger 3 fired for x2.
  • Other triggers. Trigger 2 fired (x2's gain was above the predicted range, and the plan carried a sign error; both explained in Design). Trigger 4: leaving out any one farm keeps the sign. Trigger 5: the controls behave (the x2 placebo moves the score by 0.007, within about a seventh of the x2 interval's half-width). Trigger 6 does not apply (no sister experiment on a matching contrast). Trigger 7: not yet; nothing is built on x2.
  • Audit findings (Sonnet; report in the private briefs folder). The gain is real and identical in all three seeds. It sits at the middle quantile levels (q25 to q75), is spread over 11 of 12 months and all 24 hours, and the top 5% of rows carry 55% of it. x2 raises the median by about 0.9 points of capacity on 97% of rows: the default's median sits 9.0 points below the observed value on average. Adding a constant +0.9 to the default's quantiles reproduces about 85% of x2's gain and the same loss in the mean forecast. The gain scales with how far each variant lifts the quantiles. Triage: accepted. The finding changes what x2 means (a bias correction, not noise removal) and is why x2 is not adopted. We did not run the constant-shift arm as a new experiment.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scored at 1 to 10 days, 3 farms, 12 months. Intervals do not cover other farms.
  • The XGBoost models are single ERA5 fits, not the quarterly refits the family settings name.
  • The ERA5 mask is an oracle at training time only. The forecast-time masks use the ensemble members. The "wind above rated" group holds under 0.1% of rows at the 95%-of-peak definition used here, so it is not reported.
  • The physics core with the adapter is not scored as an alternative family, and the curtailment-cost metric of experiment 277 is not scored (the farms have no node forecast here).
  • x2 holds the base margin flat below cut-in. With the low-wind rows dropped from the binned curve, member speeds below cut-in take the lowest retained bin's value.
  • The replicate is 6 months and its interval is wide.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does a constant upward shift of the quantiles, fitted on the hindcast, match x2's gain? The audit says the shift should match it (85% of the gain); a pre-registered arm would settle whether x2 adds anything beyond a bias correction, and why the offset table leaves a median bias of -9 points of capacity.
  • Is the physics core with the adapter helped by dropping low-wind rows? Not tested here.

docs.title: Does the standard forecasting architecture (a physics core, a learned input adapter, and a mixture-density output head) match Primary demand research default 3 at 168 to 240 hours?
docs.text:
Take-home: The standard architecture is a small neural network with a learned input adapter and a mixture-density output (a spread of forecast quantiles from three overlapping bell curves). It sits on top of the frozen convex stack of Primary demand research default 3. At forecast lead times of 168 to 240 hours (7 to 10 days) it forecasts demand at six Primary substations (33/11 kV substations) slightly better than the default, as it did at 0.5 to 168 hours in experiment 330. With experiment 330, the result now covers the 0.5-to-240-hour range that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) needs. The 95% interval includes zero, so a small harm cannot be excluded, and two Primaries (D10 and D16) supply most of the gain. Scores are quantile scores in points of effective capacity, and lower is better.

We asked whether replacing the default's median correction, spread table, and band steps with one neural network makes the forecast less accurate at 7 to 10 days. The mixture-density output follows Bishop (1994). The arms, network, and settings are those of experiment 330. STD scored 2.954 points against the default's 3.077 (difference -0.123). The same neural network with a median-only output (STD-A) scored 3.051 (difference -0.026).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms (scored year, 168 to 240 hours, six Primaries, 236,909 half-hours, six seeds averaged, monthly refits on a pool of up to 24 months, the P-roll schedule): default 3.077, STD 2.954, STD-A 3.051, manual heuristic 3.456, climatology 3.663 points of capacity. The reproduction gate passed (default 3.077 against 3.077 stored). BG2 has no forecasts past 168 hours.
  • STD against the default: -0.123 (95% interval -0.276 to +0.017; 99.5% interval -0.346 to +0.072; 9 of 12 months better), a relative change of -4.0%. P3 holds (STD is better with D10 included, as predicted). STD is 0.50 points better than the manual heuristic and 0.71 better than climatology.
  • Without D10: -0.055 (95% interval -0.223 to +0.074; relative -1.9%). P1 holds on the estimate (the gap is below +0.03), but the interval cannot exclude +0.074. Experiment 330's figure without D10 was -0.009 at 0.5 to 168 hours.
  • STD-A against the default: -0.026 (95% interval -0.153 to +0.081), -0.022 without D10. P2 fails by a small margin (predicted under 0.02, observed 0.026). STD against STD-A is -0.097 (95% interval -0.151 to -0.048), so the mixture output carries most of the gain.
  • By lead band (STD minus default, points): 168 to 192 h -0.103, 192 to 216 h -0.122, 216 to 240 h -0.144; the gain grows with lead.
  • By Primary (STD minus default, points): D10 -0.447, D16 -0.331, D14 -0.026, D11 +0.004, D9 +0.029, D5 +0.046. Leaving out D10 gives -0.055; leaving out D16 gives -0.082 (99% interval -0.254 to +0.080).
  • No-harm bounds (one-sided 95% upper bounds; tolerances 0.02 pooled, 0.05 for each of q01, q99, cold winter nights, sunny daylight, 2% for the tail-weighted score): pooled -0.004, q01 pinball -0.006, q99 pinball +0.037, tail-weighted CRPS at the 95th percentile -0.7% (relative). Not shown: cold winter nights +0.263 (estimate -0.023, 2,384 half-hours), sunny daylight +0.217 (estimate -0.086), and the pooled bound without D10, +0.056.
  • Tail calibration (all rows; coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99): STD 0.010, 0.052, 0.950, 0.985; STD-A 0.015, 0.052, 0.946, 0.982; default 0.019, 0.057, 0.952, 0.984. Pinball loss at q01 is 0.177 for STD against 0.224 for the default; at q99 it is 0.238 against 0.239.
  • Cold winter nights (STD-A): -0.143 against the default (95% interval -0.276 to -0.098).
  • Economy 7 night (00:30 to 07:30): STD -0.206 (95% interval -0.337 to -0.096), -0.123 without D10.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary (points): STD -1.35 (D10), -0.65 (D11), -0.34 (D14), -0.96 (D16), -1.49 (D5), -0.41 (D9); the default's are +0.01, -0.17, -0.22, -0.07, -0.53, -0.26. STD's median sits further below its mean than the default's at every Primary, as at 0.5 to 168 hours.
  • Error of the median and of the mean forecast (mean absolute error, points): median 5.259 for STD against 5.326 for the default; mean 5.342 against 5.459 (without D10: 5.071 against 5.149). Both point the same way as the quantile score.
  • Audit triggers: none of the strict triggers fired. The sign survives leaving out D10. The 95% interval for STD is 3.6 times as wide as experiment 330's at the same contrast, the size that audit trigger 6 names; the rows differ (168 to 240 hours against 0.5 to 168), so the trigger does not strictly apply. The width has an explanation in the per-Primary gains (D10 and D16 gain 0.45 and 0.33 points, D5 and D9 do not) and in the 12 months of resampling blocks. No independent audit has been run on this result.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lead range: 168 to 240 hours only. With experiment 330 the full 0.5-to-240-hour range is covered, with different training rows for each part.
  • Training rows: only the ensemble era (July 2024 onward) has 168-to-240-hour rows, so the pool grows from 233,628 rows at the first refit (12 months) to 408,691 at the last (about 23 months), against 24 months of rows for experiment 330. The networks were trained on 168-to-240-hour rows only.
  • Inputs: the filter's level is the level of the same run and hour band at 168 hours or less, and the anomaly is zero (its mean absolute value is 0.009 points at 144 to 168 hours).
  • Comparator and not done: the default is experiment 335's stored default 3 forecast (the daylight heuristic blend past 168 hours), and the as-of calibration of experiment 164 was not applied to STD. No replicate-year check was run, because the replicate months are in the training pool.
  • Seeds: STD and STD-A average six seeds, and the stored default averages 3.
  • Schedule: monthly refits on a rolling pool (P-roll); absolute scores could move under weekly refits.
  • Next: score STD at 0.5 to 240 hours in one run once more months of 168-to-240-hour rows exist, and test the median-only adapter on cold winter nights at long leads.

docs.title: The question, prediction, rows, metric, and stop rule
docs.text:
1. Question. Does the standard architecture (STD) score within 0.03 points of Primary demand research default 3 at 168 to 240 hours, with and without D10?
  2. Prediction that can fail. P1 to P4 in the front matter.
  3. Rows and period. Six Primaries, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, origin 09:00 UTC, rows outside hand-filtered events, valid times 168 to 240 hours after the origin. Rows come from experiment 317's stored chain (the ensemble era only), so the training pool grows from 12 months at the first refit to about 23 months at the last.
  4. Metric. As in experiment 330: the quantile score, the research-default page's protected groups and tolerances, tail calibration at q01, q05, q95, and q99, and month-block intervals.
  5. Stop rule. The reproduction gate fails, or STD is more than 0.10 points worse than the default at the first full run.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Arms. STD and STD-A as in experiment 330, with experiment 330's network code imported. Monthly refits on the P-roll schedule, six seeds averaged.
  • Core and inputs. The core is arm D's mean from the chain (identical to the stored arm D below 168 hours). The inputs are experiment 278's arm 2 columns. The level comes from the same run and hour band at 168 hours or less, the anomaly is zero past 168 hours (mean absolute value 0.009 points at 144 to 168 hours), and the weather is the 51-member mean of experiment 111's store.
  • Training rows. Only rows at 168 to 240 hours, from the chain's ensemble-era periods, ending before each refit.
  • Differences from experiment 330. The replicate-year check is dropped, because the replicate months are in the training pool.

docs.title: Can the adapter's effective wind speed be had as an XGBoost column without a neural network in the serving path?
docs.text: Take-home: a lookup table keeps 5% of the neural network's gain in forecast score and boosted trees keep 51%, so no non-neural column passes the adoption rule. Experiment 326 found that giving XGBoost one extra input, the wind speed corrected by a small neural network (the neural adapter), lowers the wind forecast's score by 0.099 points. We asked whether a simpler method can produce that input, so that the production service needs no neural network. The input is the 100 m wind speed from the ensemble forecast of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), multiplied by a speed scale that depends on wind direction, temperature, and the ratio of the 10 m to the 100 m wind speed. We replaced the neural network by three simpler methods for choosing the speed scale: a lookup table by direction, speed ratio, and temperature (x1), boosted decision trees on the neural network's inputs (x2), and a table filled in from the neural network's own speed scales (x3). Each method was fitted as the neural network was: it minimises the error of a physics-based wind-power model against the power observed at three metered wind farms (W1 to W3, anonymised), driven by ERA5 (our estimate of past weather) before April 2024. The score is the quantile score over 11 quantile levels, in percentage points of each farm's capacity, scored at forecast leads of 1 to 10 days on the rows that experiment 210's mask keeps (lower is better). The default forecast, Wind farms research default 1, scores 11.352. The neural adapter (x4, experiment 326's arm (c)) lowers the default's score by 0.099. The lookup table lowers it by 0.005, the table copying the neural network by 0.016, and the boosted trees by 0.051. The boosted trees and the copied table have a 95% interval for that difference below zero, but the 99.75% interval that the adoption rule uses includes zero for all three non-neural columns. The hypothesis, that a non-neural column keeps most of the gain, is not supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Arm Kept rows All rows Days 1 to 2 Days 3 to 10 0.01 pinball 0.99 pinball 5%-95% coverage Default 11.352 10.825 6.612 11.191 0.284 0.640 92.1% x4, neural adapter 11.253 10.746 6.525 11.097 0.283 0.639 92.0% x2, boosted trees 11.301 10.785 6.568 11.134 0.283 0.641 91.9% x3, table copying the network 11.336 10.810 6.585 11.174 0.284 0.638 92.1% x1, lookup table 11.347 10.821 6.624 11.177 0.284 0.640 92.1%
  • Scored at 1 to 10 days, on 3 farms and 12 months. Intervals resample whole months and the 3 seeds (50,000 resamples) and do not cover other farms.
  • Benchmarks, kept rows. The default's 11.352 compares with 13.547 for climatology (the default is 2.195 better, 95% interval 1.577 to 2.808), 11.697 for the frozen XGBoost reference without the offset table (0.345 better, 0.274 to 0.418), and on hours 0 to 6 only 15.566 for persistence against the default's 6.568 on the same 1,696 rows.
  • Gain over the default, kept rows (95% interval; 99.75% interval). x4: -0.099 (-0.157 to -0.041; -0.185 to -0.011). x2: -0.051 (-0.089 to -0.012; -0.109 to +0.007). x3: -0.016 (-0.034 to -0.001; -0.046 to +0.007). x1: -0.005 (-0.040 to +0.028; -0.060 to +0.043).
  • Share of the neural adapter's gain kept (95% interval). x2: 51% (20% to 82%). x3: 16% (1% to 35%). x1: 5% (-54% to 34%). The prediction that x1 keeps at least half failed, and the prediction that x2 keeps at least 80% failed (its point estimate is 51%, and 80% sits at the top of its interval).
  • By lead. x2 keeps 50% at days 1 to 2 and 60% at days 3 to 10; x3 keeps 31% and 18%; x1 keeps -14% and 15%. The prediction that the kept share is smaller at days 1 to 2 held for x2 and x1 and failed for x3, and every pair of intervals overlaps, so the prediction is not established.
  • Drop-one tables. Without the direction sector the table gains 0.007, and without the speed ratio 0.010, against x1's 0.005, so each version gains nothing within its interval. The prediction that the sector and the ratio carry the gain cannot be tested when the full table has no gain.
  • Per farm (x2 minus default). W1 -0.061, W2 -0.070, W3 -0.018, and negative without any one farm (-0.045, -0.041, -0.066), in 9 of 12 months. x1 is -0.017, -0.015, and +0.020, and so has no consistent sign.
  • Replicate period (daily runs of January to June 2025, six months). x2: -0.067 (99.75% interval -0.171 to +0.084; t test on six monthly differences, p = 0.32). x4: -0.084. x3: -0.015. x1: -0.009. Every arm agrees in sign with the scored year, and no interval excludes zero.
  • Tails. No arm raises the 0.01 or 0.99 pinball loss by more than 0.05; the one-sided 95% upper bounds are at most +0.0124 (x2 at 0.99).
  • Serving each arm needs. x1 and x3: a table file of 192 numbers per farm. x2: a boosted-tree model file per farm. x4: a neural network per farm. All four also need the fitted physics core (power curve, hub height, idle layer, and air-density terms) to turn the 10 m and 100 m speeds and the temperature into the effective speed, and x2 also needs the hour of day.

docs.title: Why the table fails
docs.text:
An adapter's gain on the forecast follows how much it lowers the physics core's error on ERA5. On the ERA5 training rows the core's mean absolute error of expected power, as a fraction of capacity, is lowest with the neural adapter, then boosted trees, then the lookup table, and no better than no adapter with the table copying the network. The table below gives these errors for seed 0.

Farm No adapter x4, neural x2, trees x1, lookup table x3, copied table W1 0.0702 0.0633 0.0657 0.0672 0.0705 W2 0.0822 0.0725 0.0760 0.0784 0.0870 W3 0.0906 0.0802 0.0831 0.0860 0.0966
  • The lookup table closes 39% to 44% of the network's ERA5 error reduction (W1 43%, W2 39%, W3 44%), yet keeps 5% of its forecast gain. Whatever the table learns on ERA5 mostly does not carry to the ensemble members' wind speeds.
  • The copied table is worse than none. The median of the network's factor in a cell loses the network's variation inside the cell, and the physics core was fitted jointly with the network, so the table does not reproduce the network's wind-power curve.
  • The columns differ by about 0.4 to 0.7 m/s from the network's on the scored year's member rows, against 0.7 to 1.1 m/s for no adapter (mean absolute difference). All correlate at 0.97 or higher with the network's column.

docs.title: Design as run
docs.text:
• Column. Every arm hands XGBoost the physics core's effective hub-height speed (the 100 m speed after the core's shear, air-density, and adapter terms), the same definition as x4. The plan's phrase "100 m speed times the table value" is this column.
  • x1. The table and the core are fitted together by the optimiser that fitted the neural adapter (1,200 steps of full-batch AdamW on the mean absolute error of expected power), with each cell's scale held between 0.8 and 1.25.
  • x2. Boosted trees (depth 3, learning rate 0.1) give the log scale through a custom objective (pseudo-Huber loss on the core's power, delta 0.1). Pass 1 runs 60 rounds with the core fixed at the fit without an adapter, the core's curve is then refitted with the scale held fixed, and pass 2 adds 30 rounds. The monotone constraints took the sign of the Spearman correlation between x1's fitted scale and each input, before any forecast was scored: +1 on the speed ratio at all three farms, and +1 on temperature at W1 and -1 at W2 and W3 (the same for every seed).
  • x3. The first fit gave medians outside the table's range of 0.8 to 1.25 at low speeds, which produced undefined values. The medians are now clipped to the range, and the arm was refitted before any forecast score was read.
  • Replicate. Every arm's mixtures come from the same ERA5 fits, with only the offset table refitted on hindcast cases before 2025-01-01, as in experiment 326.

docs.title: Controls and adoption conditions
docs.text:
• Reproduction gate: passed. The default through the offset table scores 11.352 points on the kept rows, identical to experiment 303's P1 (difference 0).
  • Placebos: passed. A column permuted across rows gives -0.001 (99.75% interval -0.003 to +0.001) for x1 and -0.001 (-0.004 to +0.001) for x2.
  • Known-answer test for x1: passed. Power generated with known speed scales by sector (0.90 to 1.12) was fitted by x1 on W1's ERA5 inputs, and the effective speed was recovered to within 0.7% in every sector (the limit is 3%).
  • Leakage check: passed. Every table and tree input is ensemble weather at forecast time: the 10 m and 100 m wind speeds, the 100 m direction, the 2 m temperature, and the hour of day (x2 only). The fits use ERA5 before 2024-04-01.
  • Conditions for x1, x2, and x3, in that order. Condition 1 (gain): failed for all three, since no 99.75% interval lies wholly below zero. Condition 2 (no harm to the 0.01 and 0.99 tails): met. Condition 3 (replication): met on sign, with no interval excluding zero. Condition 4 (controls): met. Condition 5 (inputs available at forecast time): met. No arm is adopted, and no arm is kept as a candidate, because each fails condition 1.

  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. Mean absolute error, kept rows: x4 -0.122, x2 -0.066, x3 -0.009, x1 +0.009. Median absolute error: x4 -0.130, x2 -0.074, x3 -0.021, x1 -0.008.

Trigger 4 fired for x1 alone (+0.020 at W3, -0.017 at W1), and x1's verdict does not depend on it. docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scored at 1 to 10 days, 3 farms, 12 months. Three farms rarely reach the research-default bar.
  • Single ERA5 fits, not the quarterly refits the family settings name, as in experiment 326.
  • The boosted trees (x2) were fitted with one set of settings (depth 3, 60 rounds then 30 rounds after a refit of the core, learning rate 0.1), chosen before any score. Other settings might keep more of the gain.
  • Table bins are quantiles of the ERA5 rows (8 sectors, 6 speed-ratio bins, 4 temperature bins). A finer table was not tried.
  • The curtailment-cost metric is not scored, as in experiment 326, because W1 to W3 have no node forecast.
  • Replicate period is six months, so its intervals cannot confirm or refute any arm.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Can a non-neural adapter fit the core's ERA5 error as well as the network does? The ERA5 error ranks the adapters in the forecast's order, so a cheap search on ERA5 alone (more trees, more inputs such as the lead-independent spread, or a larger table) could find an adapter worth a forecast run, without a forecast run per candidate.
  • Does the neural adapter's gain survive the family's quarterly refits? This was already the open question after experiment 326.

docs.title: Does a mixture-density head on the wind adapter's quantiles improve Wind farms research default 1 once the idle half-hours are handled?
docs.text:
Take-home: a small neural network that corrects the wind forecast's quantiles lowers the quantile score by 0.27 points of capacity on the farms' normal half-hours, but the gain is a recalibration, and no arm passes the adoption conditions. The quantile score measures how well a forecast's 11 quantiles match the observed power, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better).

We asked whether the mixture-density head of experiment 324 can improve Wind farms research default 1, called "the default" below. The head is a small neural network that fits three bell curves to each forecast. It takes the 11 quantiles of the physics core plus adapter (a physics-based wind-power forecast with a learned correction to the wind speed) and summaries of the 51 ensemble members (the 51 perturbed runs of the ECMWF weather forecast) for speed, direction, and temperature. The default is an XGBoost model trained on ERA5 (our estimate of past weather) and run on the 51 members, plus a table of per-quantile offsets.

The head scored 11.080 against the default's 11.352 on the kept rows, the half-hours that experiment 210's mask does not flag as idle-band readings (small noisy power readings while a farm is idle). On the idle-band rows the head scored 8.146 against 6.051. We tested two repairs: x2 adds a rule that forecasts the farm's idle floor (the median power of its idle-band readings) wherever the ensemble-mean wind speed is below the speed at which the turbines start generating (the cut-in speed), and x3 trains the head on every half-hour. The rule recovered none of the 2.1-point loss. Training on every half-hour (x3) removed the 0.27-point gain.

The pinball loss at the 0.99 quantile, the score of the upper tail that matters for curtailment, rose by 0.05 points. The adoption rule allows a rise of at most 0.05 with 95% confidence, and the bound is 0.092. A control run afterwards, in which the head saw only the 11 quantiles and no weather summaries, scored 11.050, so the weather summaries add nothing. The verdict is partly supported, and the head stays a candidate: no arm is adopted.

  • Serving. x1 needs a small neural network (about 2 minutes to train per farm on a graphics processing unit), its input quantiles from the physics core plus adapter, and the 11 member-summary columns. x2 adds a rule and a floor value per farm (1.4%, 0.4%, and 2.6% of capacity at W1 to W3). x3 needs the network only.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does a hindcast-fitted correction of the default's quantiles (a shift or a small head on the default's own quantiles) match the head's 0.27 points? The post hoc controls say a shift reaches about half and a base-only head reaches all of it.
  • Can the head's upper tail be repaired? Above q99 the head covers 2.4% against 1% nominal; a tail-specific term in the mixture is the obvious test.

docs.title: Does a constant upward shift of the wind quantiles reproduce the gain of dropping low-wind training rows in Wind farms research default 1?
docs.text:
Take-home: a single upward shift of the wind quantiles, fitted on past forecasts, does nothing, and the shifts that do reproduce the gain of dropping low-wind training rows also harm the forecast at low winds. Experiment 336 found that dropping the training rows with wind below the turbines' cut-in speed (the speed at which a turbine starts to turn) improves the forecast (its arm x2, called X2 here), and its audit suggested the gain is only a constant upward shift of the forecast quantiles. We tested that. The forecast is Wind farms research default 1, the wind forecast with the best score in the experiments run so far, on the three metered wind farms (W1 to W3, anonymised) at 1 to 10 day leads. The score is the quantile score in points of capacity (a point of capacity is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better) on the kept rows: the half-hours at a farm that the mask of experiment 210 does not flag as idle. The default scores 11.352. Arm S adds one constant to every forecast quantile, fitted on the 442 hindcast runs (the forecasts made retrospectively on 442 earlier days) that also fit the forecast's offset table, the correction per farm and lead day built into the default. The fit returns 0.000 points, because the offset table already minimises the score on those runs. Arm S therefore equals the default (gain 0.000). A shift reproduces the gain only when fitted on data from after the table's fitting window, and the two such shifts we tried raise the score on the rows with ERA5 wind (our estimate of past weather, used here as the observed wind speed) below cut-in by 0.5 to 0.8 points. The verdict is not supported, and nothing is adopted.

Differences are the arm's score minus the default's, so a negative difference is an improvement.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Plan. Committed before any score, in the first commit of this branch. Its caution (a hindcast-only probe showed an optimum near +0.2 points) was optimistic: the fitted constant is 0.000. The plan did not say that the S+X2 constant is fitted on all usable hindcast rows, not on the kept rows; it is.
  • Family and default. Wind farms research default 1, experiment 336's refit, 3 farms, 3 seeds, 107,121 scored half-hours. Code reused from the folder of experiment 336 (and through it 326, 303, 285, 259, and 230); X2 is read from 336's stored mixtures. Tier 1 for S and S-q, tier 2 for X2. Minimum gain 0.02 points for S, S-q, and S+X2 (each adds a fitted step) and 0 for X2.
  • Arms. S: one constant added to the final quantiles. S-q: one constant per quantile level. X2: dropped low-wind rows. S+X2: x2's quantiles plus a constant fitted on x2's hindcast. Post hoc and never adopted: Sdrift and SX2drift (constant fitted on the January to June 2025 hindcast runs scored with the table fitted before 2025, then applied to the scored year), Soracle (fitted on the scored year), and the sign-reversed placebos.
  • Reproduction gate. The refit default and X2 equal experiment 336's stored forecasts exactly (largest difference 0), and the default scores 11.352, the same as experiment 303's stored forecast (named P1 there).
  • Controls. Known-answer test: the fit recovers an injected 1.2-point shift to within 0.001. Leakage check: the hindcast ends on 2025-06-16 and the scored year starts on 2025-07-01. Placebo: with the sign of the shift reversed, S and S-q change nothing, and S+X2 gains 0.17 points, because reversing x2's negative constant raises the forecast, the useful direction for X2.

docs.text:
• Code review and audit (Sonnet, one agent). No leakage: every shift fit reads hindcast rows only, which end on 2025-06-16, before the scored year starts on 2025-07-01. It re-derived the contrasts of X2, the drift shift, the oracle shift, and S+X2 from the stored quantiles and matched every number in this page, and refitted S independently to 0 on both the headline score and a plain 11-level pinball loss. Findings, all low severity: condition 5 is set to true in code and the audit-trigger part of condition 4 is not computed (accepted, both are read by hand on this page); the per-level fit ignores the later clip and sort (accepted, S-q is a null arm); the S+X2 constant is fitted on all hindcast rows (accepted, now stated in Design).
  • Prose review (Sonnet, one agent). Accepted: define x2, hindcast, offset table, cut-in, and ERA5 in the opening, link experiment 336 at first mention, split the two-claim sentences, scope the law-like sentences and advice, fix the q95 range, the trigger-5 and caveat wording, and the 0.007 to 0.006 figure, and add the sign convention. Rejected: deleting the pre-registration sentence in Design (the skill requires the commit order to be shown); rewording 0.017 and 0.579 (rounding of unrounded scores); bolded leads on table paragraphs (convention on these pages).

docs.text:
• A correction that depends on wind speed is untested. One offset per bin of ensemble-mean 100 m wind speed (for example 0 to 5, 5 to 8, 8 to 12, and above 12 m/s), fitted on the hindcast, could lift the forecast at 8 to 15 m/s and leave it alone below 5 m/s, as the power-curve figures suggest. Its gain on the kept rows and its score below cut-in are the numbers to read.
  • The cause of the 0.8 to 1.2 point drift is untested. The hindcast years and the scored year differ in median bias; refitting the offset table every few months might remove the difference.

docs.title: How small a change in a wind farm's usable capacity can its output in strong wind show, and how fast?
docs.text: A loss of about half a wind farm's capacity is found within 60 days at 91% to 93% of start dates at all three farms, a loss of a quarter at 26% to 77%, and anything smaller is not found reliably. The proposal to look only at the strongest winds does not help, because strong wind fills 0.18% to 1.1% of half-hours and most 28-day blocks hold too few of them for a stable high quantile. The best statistic is the ratio of observed to expected power over every half-hour at 20% of the farm's maximum output or more. The verdict is not supported: two of eight pre-registered predictions held, and one of the two held only because the strong-wind statistic is missing in almost every block. W1, W2, and W3 are three metered wind farms, anonymised.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text:
We asked how small a loss of a wind farm's usable capacity its output can show, and how fast. Capacity falls when turbines fail and returns when they are repaired. Experiment 233 divided observed power by the power that a fitted wind-turbine model expects, over the half-hours when the model expects at least 95% of the farm's maximum output, and was too slow (a 25% loss was found within 120 days at about half the start dates at W1 and W2 and at none at W3). This experiment changes the statistic and the detector. The statistic is a high quantile of observed power in half-hours when the ERA5 100 m wind speed is at least 2 m/s above the speed at which the fitted power curve saturates (the "strong set"). The detectors are a change-point search (optimal partitioning, after Killick et al. (2012)) and a two-sided CUSUM test (cumulative sum, after Page (1954)).

We tested the detectors by cutting the observed power in known ways and counting the start dates at which each detector found the cut. We cut power by whole turbines, by 10%, 25%, and 50%, and by half a turbine, for 3 to 365 days from each of 30 random start dates (2024-07 to 2025-12). We also clipped output at 90%, 75%, and 50% of the 99.9th percentile (a lost export cable), added seasonal swings and a slow drift, and added a 5% error in wind speed. Five arms were compared: A (the 99.9th percentile in the strong set), B (the average log ratio of observed to expected power over half-hours at 25% to 100% of scale, weighted by the inverse of each half-hour's variance, which is lower at saturation where wind-speed errors do not matter), C (B with a fitted speed-scale term per block), D (experiment 233's ratio), and E (W2 against W3, which share one ERA5 cell). Arms F and G (public neighbour farms) could not be run: none of the 65 public farms with a known position among the 287 candidates of experiment 288 lies within 150 km of W1, W2, or W3, and the other 222 candidates have no position.

The result narrows the search to larger losses and to statistics that use every busy half-hour. It rules out the strong-wind quantile. It also finds that the real records show repaired episodes and no permanent steps. The penalty rule fired a stop (below), so the change-point penalty was chosen separately for each arm after the injection test and before the real series was read.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Pre-registered predictions: two held, four failed, two untestable. P1 failed (arm A at the planned 2 m/s margin found a 25% step at 0% of start dates at W1 and 10% at W2, although at W1 and W3 that arm has fewer than 8 observed blocks, so the 0% is structural). P2 held vacuously: arm A at the 2 m/s margin raised 0, 0, and 0 new change points under a 9% swing (W1, W2, W3) against 1, 2, and 1 for D, only because it has almost no blocks (at the saturation speed, arm A raised 2, 4, and 0). P3 failed: D finds a 10% step at 31% of W3 start dates, and arm A at the saturation speed flags every size from half a turbine (3.8%) to 50% at the same 50% of start dates at W1 (its statistic is so flat that any dip in a block that exists is flagged). P4 failed (State-space fit). P5 held (episodes shorter than 7 days: D finds 3-day 25% episodes at 0%, 0%, and 14% of start dates and 7-day ones at 0%, 3%, and 27%). P6 is untestable: it names the gap to the registered capacity, which was not available, and the effective capacity comes from the same readings. P7 failed (Weighted evidence). P8 is untestable (no public farm with a known position within 150 km).
  • Strong wind is rare. At the 2 m/s margin the strong set holds 0.31% (W1), 1.12% (W2), and 0.18% (W3) of half-hours, on 3.2%, 5.1%, and 1.3% of days. At the margin of 0 m/s (experiment 233's above-rated set) the shares are 1.6%, 3.3%, and 0.65%, on 7.3%, 11.1%, and 3.1% of days. The saturation speeds of the fitted curve are 15.3, 15.8, and 18.6 m/s at 100 m. Of strong-set half-hours at the 2 m/s margin, 0%, 4.7%, and 12.8% have observed power under half of scale (an outage or an ERA5 error). The check for an export limit at strong wind is circular, so it shows nothing either way. The 99.9th percentile of observed power in the strong set is 4% (W1), 16% (W2), and 17% (W3) above the fitted scale. The fitted scale comes from the same readings, so this check is circular and the visibility margin is not identified without turbine ratings. Coverage is the clear limit on seeing a loss. For W1 and W3 the observed power is in MVA, so reactive power adds to the readings.
  • The stop rule fired and the penalty was chosen per arm. At c = 2, the worst primary combination of farm, arm, and block length raised 4.9 change points per farm-year in 2021-09 to 2024-06, against the limit of one. At the largest penalty the worst was 1.06, because several change points of the unmodified series are probably real. Only change points that vanish at the largest penalty were then counted as false alarms (Figure 6). The chosen multipliers are 2 (A), 8 (B), 16 (C), and 4 (D); the CUSUM limits are 5 (A), 10 (B), 8 (C), and 8 (D). The noise estimates (relative speed error and power noise per farm) are 0.125 and 0.056 (W1), 0.139 and 0.098 (W2), and 0.116 and 0.148 (W3).
  • Steps lasting 90 days, 28-day blocks, change-point search, share found within 60 days (95% interval from resampling calendar months of start dates).
Farm and step A, 2 m/s margin A, 0 m/s margin B C D W1, 25% 0% 50% (19 to 81) 54% (23 to 81) 46% (13 to 77) 63% (30 to 88) W1, 50% 0% 50% 75% 82% 93% W2, 25% 10% 74% (44 to 100) 8% (0 to 25) 0% 26% (3 to 57) W2, 50% 13% 74% 81% 29% 91% W3, 25% 0% 0% 29% (3 to 61) 0% 77% (50 to 95) W3, one turbine (50%) 0% 0% 90% (72 to 100) 23% (0 to 52) 93% (82 to 100) W1, one turbine (7.7%) 0% 50% 0% 0% 0% W2, one turbine (12.5%) 0% 45% 0% 0% 0%
  • Smallest step found at 80% of start dates or more within 60 days: 50% of capacity at every farm (arm D, 93%, 91%, and 93%), and no smaller size reaches 80%. Median delay of arm D at a 50% step is 28 days at W3; at a 25% step it is 42 days (W1) and 36.5 days (W3), and W2's median is 78 days, past the 60-day limit.
  • CUSUM on the saturated set flagged 25% steps at 83% of start dates at W1, 100% at W2 (median delay 34 days), and 14% at W3, on 18, 17, and 7 valid start dates. At W1 it flags a one-turbine step at the same 83%, so this reflects the flat statistic and not a faster detection. It also raised more new alarms under a 9% swing (6, 2, and 0 for the 99.9th percentile at 0 m/s margin).
  • Weighted evidence (arms B and C) did not speed detection up. Arm B found a 25% step at 54%, 8%, and 29% and arm C at 46%, 0%, and 0%, against arm D's 63%, 26%, and 77%. Under a 9% seasonal swing at 28-day blocks arm B raised 1, 0, and 0 new change points and arm C raised 0, 3, and 0. Under a 5% speed bias that lowers observed power for 30 days, arm D raised a false step at 45% of start dates at W3 and arm C at 0% (arm B 4%), so the weighting, not the speed-scale term, removed most false steps.
  • Episodes (7-day blocks, arm D): a 25% episode that then ends is found within its length plus 60 days at 0%, 0%, and 14% of start dates when it lasts 3 days, at 7%, 10%, and 40% when it lasts 14 days, and at 77%, 52%, and 73% when it lasts 60 days (W1, W2, W3). A one-turbine episode at W3 is found at 20%, 43%, 73%, and 90% of start dates at 3, 7, 14, and 60 days.
  • Two farms, one ERA5 cell (arm E, 14-day blocks, arm B): a 50% step is found in the W2 minus W3 series at 52% (W2) and 73% (W3) of start dates, a 25% step at 4% and 40%, and a one-turbine step at W2 at 0%. The result does not show that the shared speed error cancels: a 25% step at W2 is found at 4% of start dates, no better than arm B on W2 alone (8%), and no correlation between the two farms' ratios was measured.
  • State-space fit. The fit could not be validated, so no clip result is claimed. With 7-day blocks the fit labelled the unmodified series at W2 as not nameplate near every start date, so no W2 start date is valid. With 14-day blocks W2 has 30 valid start dates, and 5 of the 14-day 25% episodes were labelled as turbines out, none of the clips as a clip. At W1, 14-day episodes that cut output by 25% were labelled as turbines out for 7 of 30 start dates (7-day blocks) and 2 of 21 (14-day blocks), and 14-day clips at 75% of the 99.9th percentile as a clip for none. The 99.9th percentile of the strong set exists in under 3% of 7-day and 14-day blocks at W1 and W3, so the fit falls back on fixed reference values there. The lattice-constrained variant never returned a whole-turbine state at W1 or W3 for the same reason, so that result does not test the lattice. The interquartile range of the strong set is near zero on the flat top, so it carries no signal for a clip, and the fit used only the 99.9th percentile and the mid-wind ratio.
  • Real series (dates are change points of arm D in 14-day blocks, with arm A as a check). W1: one 2-week episode from 2024-03-10 to 2024-03-23 at 0.34 times expected power against 1.00 before and after, which overlaps three of experiment 210's idle runs (2024-03-16 to 2024-03-19), and no permanent step. W2: 2021-09-26 to 2021-12-18 at 0.82 against 0.99 (a loss of 17%), and 2025-11-02 to 2025-12-13 at 0.70 against 1.02 (a loss of 31%, 34% on the 99.9th percentile), which overlaps an idle run of 2025-11-14 to 2025-11-16; both end in a return to the earlier level. W3: 2024-10-20 to 2025-01-25 at 0.61 against 1.02 (a loss of 40%, and 53% on the 99.9th percentile, about one of the two turbines), a return on 2025-01-26, and a second, smaller drop from 2025-12-28 to the end of the record (0.82 against 1.03) with no return in the data. W3 also shows many short drops in 2020 and has 151 of the 183 idle runs of experiment 210. W1's annual 99th percentile of output over its effective capacity is 0.99 to 1.01 in every year from 2019 to 2025, so no gap to that capacity opens inside the record (the effective capacity is itself estimated from the same readings).
  • Whole-turbine lattice test. Steps of arm A at the saturated set in W1 are single 28-day blocks 7% to 9% below their neighbours, close to one turbine (7.7%); 5 of 9 lie within a tenth of a turbine at 13 turbines (binomial p = 0.02), but 5 of 9 also at 12 turbines (p = 0.02) and 3 of 9 at 14 (p = 0.26), so the test cannot tell the counts apart. A dip and its return count as two steps, so the 9 steps are about 4 to 5 independent events and p = 0.02 is overstated; no correction is made for the several counts and two arms. At W2, 0 of 6 steps of arm A (p = 1.0) and 1 of 4 of arm D (p = 0.59) lie near a multiple of one eighth. At W3, 3 of 5 steps of arm A lie near a multiple of one half (p = 0.06) and 0 of 7 of arm D. The 31% loss at W2 lies between 2 and 3 turbines. No upward step is permanent: every rise is the return from a downward episode. A private capacity-state table (full, reduced by an estimated share, or out) for every half-hour of the three farms is saved under work/capacity_state.parquet, built from the change points of arm D and experiment 210's idle runs. A later experiment could test it as a training mask and as an as-of feature.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• No forecast is produced, so forecast-error and tail-calibration checks do not apply.
  • Audit triggers (listed in the ml-experiment skill): trigger 1 fired (a 9% swing raises new change points for arm A at the saturated set and for arm D) and trigger 2 fired (arm A failed its prediction). The strong-set shares and Figure 1 explain the second. The worker brief allowed Sonnet only, so a fresh Sonnet reviewer stood in for the Opus audit: it re-derived the shares and median delays of the table, the strong-set shares, and the idle-run counts from the stored rows and matched all of them. It found no leakage in the injected effects or the prefix replay. Two steps use data from after the start date. The noise scale and the ln(n) in the change-point penalty use the whole 2019 to 2026 series, and the fitted core was fitted before 2025-06-17, so about 12 of the 18 months of start dates lie in the core's fitting data.
  • The seasonal swing is a one-off ramp. It begins at 2024-07 and falls by its range over half a year, so it is a half cycle and not a stationary seasonal pattern.
  • Lab conditions: the injected power cut multiplies the observed power from the start day, the fitted core is frozen, and 30 start dates share each cell, so the intervals resample 18 calendar months of start dates. Starts whose unmodified series already shows a consistent change point are excluded and counted in each cell's n (for example 18 to 30 of 30).

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Arm A at the saturated set, the CUSUM comparison, and the 0 m/s margin are post hoc. The 2 m/s margin and the change-point search are the pre-registered rows.
  • The state-space fit is an unfinished tool and is not evidence about clips.
  • Turbine counts (13, 8, and 2) come from the public planning register and are tied to the anonymous labels, as the worker brief required for step sizes.
  • Next: test the capacity-state table as a training mask; replicate on more farms, because three farms with 2 to 13 turbines cannot separate whole-turbine steps from a continuous distribution. A learned correction of the ratio by wind speed is a candidate neural component; its prediction that could fail is that arm C then finds a 25% step at W2 within 60 days at more than 50% of start dates.

docs.title: Can the upper quantiles of Wind farms research default 1 be made to cover the observed power, and does an ensemble-aware correction beat a plain recalibration?
docs.text:
Take-home: corrections fitted on past forecasts do not fix the wind forecast's upper tail, and the ensemble members add no information beyond the forecast's own quantiles. The wind forecast (Wind farms research default 1, the forecast scored in experiment 340) sets its 99% quantile (q99) too low: observed power exceeds it in 1.8% of the scored half-hours, where 1% is intended. The forecast is also capped: no quantile exceeds the 99.9th percentile of the farm's observed power in the hindcast, and the arms below leave that cap in place. We tried three corrections for the upper quantiles, all fitted on the daily hindcast runs (the 442 daily runs up to 2025-06-16: forecasts made retrospectively on earlier days). The default already contains an offset table, which adds a fitted offset to every quantile for each farm and lead day. An offset table keyed by wind speed (x1) changed the 0.99 pinball loss by +1.0%. A boosted-tree head (x2), in the manner of the tail head of experiment 284, lowered it by 0.9%. A probability mass at the cap, set by the share of ensemble members above the farm's rated speed (the speed above which its power stops rising; x3), changed it by 0.0%. The share of observed power above q99 stayed at 1.8% to 1.9% in the three arms. The head without any ensemble input gained as much as the head with it. The verdict is not supported, and nothing is adopted.

A pinball loss is the quantile-forecast loss at one level. Pinball losses and scores are in points of capacity (a point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better) on the kept rows, the half-hours that the idle-band mask of experiment 210 does not flag. The three metered wind farms are anonymised as W1 to W3, and the lead range is 1 to 10 days. Differences are the arm's score minus the default's, so a negative difference is an improvement. The arms add to the default, so "x2" below means the default plus the head, and "targeted" means the mean of the 0.95 and 0.99 pinball losses.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Plan. Committed before any score, in the first commit of this branch. Changes after the first run, all recorded here: (1) the plan's cap, taken from the rows with ERA5 wind at or above the rated speed, lowered W3's forecasts to 53% of capacity and raised every arm's score by 0.2 to 0.9 points. The cap in the arms is now the 99.9th percentile of each farm's observed hindcast power (for the replicate, of the hindcast before 2025). The plan's cap remains as the descriptive arm x1capstrong. (2) The plan's speed-bin edges (0, 5, 8, 11, and 14 m/s) became six bins with an edge added at 17 m/s, because W1's rated speed is 16.25 m/s. (3) The plan's x1lit was described as "the default plus the cap"; the code's x1lit is the farm-and-lead-day offset table plus the cap, and x1cap is the cap alone. (4) x3's constant is fitted on the pinball losses at q90, q95, and q99. (5) Condition 2 also checks the 0.99 pinball loss against 0.05, as the plan's metric line states. The code review in Review led to two further fixes before the numbers on this page were produced.
  • Family and default. Default plus x against Wind farms research default 1, 3 farms, 3 seeds (the default's; the head's five seeds are a separate check), 107,121 scored half-hours. Code reused from the folder of experiment 340, and through it 336, 326, 303, 285, 259, and 230. All arms are tier 2. The default is reproduced exactly (difference 0.000 from experiment 303's P1, 11.352 on the kept rows).
  • Arms. x1: offsets for q90, q95, and q99 per farm, lead day, and ensemble-mean speed bin, fitted on the default's hindcast quantiles, plus the cap. x2: one tree model (depth 3, 150 rounds) per level at q90, q95, and q99, fed the default's 11 quantiles, the members' speed mean, standard deviation, and share above the rated speed, the lead, and the farm. x3: a mass at the cap with weight lambda times the share of members above the rated speed (the speed at which the farm's ERA5 power curve reaches 95% of its maximum: 16.25 m/s at W1, 22.25 m/s at W2, 21.75 m/s at W3); lambda per farm is 0.25 at W1 and 0.00 at W2 and W3. Descriptive: x1lit, x1cap, x1capstrong, x2base (no member summaries), x2plc (member summaries from another case of the same farm and lead day), x2lofo (trained on two farms), and the references of experiments 340 (drift shift) and 339 (mixture head, its arm x1).
  • Controls. Known-answer test: the speed-keyed fit recovers an injected +3.0 point offset at speeds from 8 m/s as +2.99 and at lower speeds as +0.03. Leakage: the hindcast ends on 2025-06-16 and the scored year starts on 2025-07-01; the replicate's fits stop on 2024-12-31. The shuffled placebo (x2plc) is identical to x2base to the last digit, because the trees never split on shuffled summaries. The placebo therefore keeps 111% of x2's gain, which fails the plan's placebo condition; the reading is that x2's gain is recalibration, not information.

docs.text:
