The first six score columns are the quantile score over 11 levels; "Targeted" is the mean of the 0.95 and 0.99 pinball losses. The frozen XGBoost reference scores 11.697 on the kept rows (targeted 1.706, share above q99 2.4%), climatology 13.547, and persistence 15.566 (hours 0 to 6 only, 1,696 rows).

  • Contrasts on the targeted metric (99.67% month-block intervals). x1 -0.003 (-0.025 to +0.019), x2 -0.013 (-0.029 to +0.002), x3 -0.000 (-0.002 to +0.002). None excludes zero, so no arm passes condition 1 (x2 would also need 0.03). x2 minus x2base is +0.002 (-0.0004 to +0.004). Five seeds of the x2 head's own fit give a targeted metric of 1.6113 to 1.6116 (spread 0.0003).
  • The offsets keyed by farm and lead day alone (x1lit) do more than the plan expected. They lower the share above q99 to 1.62% and the 0.99 pinball loss by 1.0% (-0.019 to +0.004), more than x1, which adds the wind-speed key. The cap alone changes nothing (x1cap), so the effect is the offsets, which refit the quantiles of the default's own table on the table's output. The interval includes zero, and x1lit cannot be adopted (the plan reserves adoption for x1 to x3).
  • Predictions that could fail. x1 lowers the share above q99 from 1.8% to under 1.5%: failed (1.9%). x1 lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by at least 3%: failed (+1.0%). x2 lowers it by at least 10%: failed (-0.9%). The base-only head gains at least half as much as x2: held, but trivially, because it gains 111% as much. x3 matters at W1 and W2 only: failed (no effect at any farm; lambda is 0 at W2 and W3). No arm moves the headline by more than 0.05: held (largest -0.009 excluding x1capstrong). The share above q99 stays above 1% for every arm: held.
  • Tails (kept rows, scored year). Share of observed power below q01 0.51%, below q05 1.29%, above q95 6.65%, above q99 1.77% for the default; x1 6.86% and 1.88%; x2 6.83% and 1.86%; x3 6.62% and 1.77%. The 0.01 and 0.05 pinball losses are 0.284 and 1.356 for every arm, and the 5% to 95% band covers 92.1% for the default and 91.9% for x1 and x2. Per farm the default's share above q99 is 2.15% (W1), 1.55% (W2), and 1.58% (W3).
  • Replicate (2025-01 to 2025-06, fits before 2025). The targeted contrasts are x1 -0.002, x2 -0.007, and x3 +0.002 (x3 is worse); the default's share above q99 is 1.82% there as well. The t test on the six monthly differences contradicts x3 (p = 0.014, x3 worse).
  • Adoption. x1 fails condition 1 (interval includes zero). x2 fails conditions 1 and 4 (the placebo keeps 111% of its gain). x3 fails conditions 1 and 3. Conditions 2 and 5 hold for all three, including the maintainer's low-wind condition (largest upper bound +0.030 on the rows below cut-in).
  • Why the shortfall does not go away. On the hindcast fit rows (2019 to 2024) the default's share above q99 is 1.5% at W1, 1.2% at W2, and 1.0% at W3, and on the hindcast months of 2025 it is 1.6%, 2.0%, and 1.1%; on the scored year it is 2.1%, 1.5%, and 1.6%. The offset table is fitted on those rows, and its coverage worsens on later rows. A second correction fitted on the same rows cannot see that change, and one scored year cannot confirm that drift is the cause. A q99 shift fitted on the scored year itself (oracle, never adopted) is +3.0, +3.6, and +3.8 points at W1, W2, and W3 and lowers the 0.99 pinball loss only from 0.645, 0.639, and 0.635 to 0.629, 0.629, and 0.624.
  • Power curves. In figures 3 and 4 the forecast q99 sits roughly 10 to 30 points of capacity below the observed q99 between about 2 and 7 m/s of ensemble-mean speed, and meets it above 8 m/s. The differences among the arms are under 3 points everywhere. Observed power at W2 and W3 does not saturate within the range of speeds the ensemble forecasts, so the rated speed (22 m/s at W2 and W3) says little about the top of the distribution.
  • Standard architecture. The nearest arm to physics core, input adapter, and tail head is experiment 339's mixture head on the adapter's quantiles (reference row). Experiment 339's mixture head is the best family on the headline (11.080, -0.272, or 2.4%, against the default) and worse than the default on the upper tail: targeted +0.011 (+0.7%), 0.99 pinball +0.051 (+8%), share above q99 2.4%. Its gap to the best arm on the targeted metric (x2base, 1.610) is +0.026 points (+1.6%).
  • Curtailment cost. Not scored: the metric of experiment 277 scores a supply point with its generators, and the three farms are not one.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, kept rows. Default -4.805 points, x1 -4.663, x2 -4.687, x3 -4.822, x1lit -4.823, x2base -4.668. Raising the upper quantiles raises the mean forecast by 0.1 points.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the targeted contrast. The mean forecast's absolute error changes by x1 -0.015, x2 -0.005, and x3 +0.001 points, in the same direction as the targeted contrast for x1 and x2. The median's absolute error changes by -0.002 (x1), +0.001 (x2), and 0.000 (x3). Trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Leaving one farm out. x1's targeted contrast is +0.014 at W1 alone and -0.018 at W2 alone, so its sign depends on the farm; without W1 it is -0.012. x2 is negative at each farm alone (-0.005, -0.021, -0.015). The leave-one-farm-out trigger fired for x1 (the sign flips, but the interval includes zero at every cut).
  • Audit triggers fired (the ml-experiment skill's "Audit before merge" list). Four of the seven fired: a failed control (the shuffled placebo keeps 111% of x2's gain), a result that contradicts its own prediction (x1 and x2 gained nothing against predicted gains of 3% and 10%), the leave-one-farm-out flip (x1), and a nested arm that beats the arm containing it (x2base scores 0.002 better than x2, and x2plc equals x2base). The first, second, and fourth are explained by the tests above: the gain is recalibration, and the in-sample versus scored-year shares show the shortfall is consistent with drift. The mean-forecast trigger did not fire. A Sonnet audit re-derived the contrasts from the stored quantiles; see Review.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scored at 1 to 10 days, 3 farms, 12 months. Intervals do not cover other farms, and the scored year is one year of drift.
  • x2's gain is a recalibration fitted on in-sample quantiles. The training base is the default's quantile after a table fitted on the same rows, and the scored base is out of sample. A head trained on out-of-sample bases, for example from a rolling refit of the table, is untested.
  • The observed curves in figures 3 and 4 combine two binnings: the band uses ERA5 speed at the valid time, and the thick lines and coloured lines use the ensemble-mean speed at forecast time.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
• Code review (Sonnet, one agent). Accepted: the replicate's cap read months from 2025 (fixed with a cap from hindcast before 2025); the leakage check did not cover the replicate (now it records the latest replicate fit time, which is 2024-12-31); no alignment check of the replicate cases (added); the 0.99 pinball tolerance was not checked (added); the placebo share is only read when x2's gain is positive (added). Plan and code differences are listed in Design. Rejected: a "no unresolved audit trigger" clause in code (read by hand above).
  • Audit (Sonnet, one agent). It re-derived the pinball losses, the shares above q95 and q99, and the targeted contrasts with its own code from the stored quantiles, and every number on this page matched, including the month-block intervals to within 0.0003. It found no unsorted, out-of-range, or missing quantile in any arm. It confirmed that the head returns the base quantile plus a tree offset, and that x2plc equals x2base because the placebo head never splits on a shuffled column (the full head puts 55%, 21%, and 12% of its gain at q90, q95, and q99 on the member columns). Finding accepted: x1lit lowers the share above q99 to 1.62% and the 0.99 pinball loss by 1.0%, which is more than x1 and contradicts the plan's expectation that it reproduces the default; the cap alone (x1cap) changes nothing, so the effect is the offsets, and the page now says so. Its interval (-0.019 to +0.004 on the 0.99 pinball loss) includes zero.
  • Prose review (Sonnet, one agent). Accepted: define the cap, the rated speed, the targeted metric, and the pinball loss in the opening; name the audit triggers in words; fix "first seven" to "first six" columns; scope the law-like sentences and replace the money metaphor; split the Design bullet; replace the stale placeholder. Rejected: moving the whole definitions paragraph above the take-home (the lead states the conclusion first, as the prose rules require); linking the research-default page for every phrase of the plan's front matter (the plan is kept as committed).

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Refit the offset table on the most recent months (for example monthly, on a rolling window) before building any further upper-tail head, because the miss is drift. This is a small change to the table the default already has.
  • A neural component is not indicated by this result. The head with member summaries did no better than the head without them, so at these 3 farms in the scored year a neural input adapter or mixture head has no additional information about the upper tail to exploit.

docs.title: Does training the wind XGBoost model on the ensemble mean beat Wind farms research default 1, and does it shrink the offset table?
docs.text:
Take-home: training the wind XGBoost model on the 51-member ensemble mean (the mean-trained model, M) removes almost all of the need for the offset table, but the forecast does not improve. The offset table (a table of per-quantile corrections, fitted on past forecast errors) improves Wind farms research default 1 (the default) by 0.345 points of capacity and worsens M by 0.017. M scores 11.431 against the default's 11.352 on the kept rows (M minus default +0.079, 95% interval -0.110 to +0.278), which the data cannot tell apart from no difference. M is also worse below the turbines' cut-in speed (+0.122 points) and at the 0.99 quantile (+0.038 points). The hypothesis is not supported, and nothing is adopted.

We asked whether an XGBoost quantile model trained on the ensemble's own history, with each weather column replaced by its mean over the 51 members, would learn the ensemble's wind-speed bias that the default corrects with the offset table. The default is XGBoost trained on ERA5 (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' past-weather estimates), run on each member, then corrected by the table of experiment 259. The scored sites are the three metered wind farms (W1 to W3, anonymised) at 1 to 10 day leads. Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity (a point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better). The kept rows are the half-hours that the mask of experiment 210 keeps, and the idle rows are the half-hours it drops. Mean training learned most of the bias, since the table changes its score by 0.017 points against 0.345 for the default, and its score stayed within noise of the default's. A mean-trained model with better low-wind behaviour is the open question.

Figures 2 to 4 show the power curves: the forecast against the observed power by wind speed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. D: the default, experiment 340's stored refit (reproduction gate: 11.352 points on the kept rows, 0.00004 from experiment 326's figure). M: the same six weather columns on the member mean, trained on the ensemble hindcast (runs of 2024-04-01 to 2025-06-16), three seeds, same hyperparameters, no calendar columns. MS: M plus the member standard deviation of the 100 m and 10 m speeds. M0: M without the table. Mpl: M with the target permuted within the month (the placebo).
  • Row set. fold_a_tuesdays_v1 (53 Tuesday runs); the kept rows are the headline. Lead range 1 to 10 days. The hindcast was cross-fitted in three blocks; the scored year comes from a fit on all usable hindcast cases (about 305,000 per farm).
  • Retraining schedule. One fit per seed, no refits. The contrast could depend on a refit schedule that this experiment did not vary.

Per farm on the kept rows (default, M): W1 10.96, 11.02; W2 12.28, 12.20; W3 10.80, 11.07. Climatology scores 13.547 on the same rows as the default's 11.352. "Below cut-in" means the half-hours with ERA5 wind speed below the farm's cut-in speed (the speed at which a turbine starts to turn).

  • Contrasts on the kept rows (arm minus default; 95% and 99.5% intervals). M +0.079 (-0.110 to +0.278; -0.181 to +0.358). MS +0.098 (-0.100 to +0.305; -0.178 to +0.390). MS minus M +0.019 (-0.035 to +0.073).
  • Without one farm (M minus default). Without W1 +0.090, without W2 +0.159, without W3 -0.010. Only W2: -0.080; only W3: +0.269.
  • Without the table. M0 scores 11.414 and the default without its table 11.697, so M0 beats the default by 0.28 points before the table is applied (audit).
  • Low-wind condition (M minus default). Below cut-in +0.122, idle rows +0.124, all half-hours +0.083. The one-sided 95% upper bounds are 0.30, 0.34, and 0.24, above the 0.1 tolerance.
  • Predictions.
    • P1 (M trails the default by 0.2 to 1.0) failed: M trails by 0.08.
    • P2 (M0 is closer to M than the default without its table is to the default) held: M0 minus M is -0.017, against 0.345 for the default.
    • P3 (MS beats M by at least 0.05 at the 0.95 and 0.99 pinball losses, and is no better on the median) failed: MS beats M by 0.032 at 0.95 and 0.024 at 0.99, both under 0.05, and is worse on the median absolute error (+0.085).
  • Adoption. M and MS fail condition 1 (intervals include zero, estimates positive), condition 2 (low-wind upper bounds above 0.1; M also fails the 0.99 pinball bound, 0.066 against 0.05), and condition 3 (replicate period M minus default +0.241).
  • Controls. The reproduction gate, the known-answer test (planted power curve recovered with a mean absolute error of 0.006 against 0.33 for the permuted placebo), the leakage check (latest hindcast valid time 2025-06-16, earliest scored 2025-07-01), and the placebo Mpl (+2.509, much worse) all behaved as they should.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, kept rows, points of capacity: default -4.81, M -5.07, MS -5.18.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the contrast: mean absolute error +0.068 for M and +0.076 for MS against the default, the same direction as the quantile score.
  • Triggers that fired: trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction: M trails by 0.08, not 0.2 to 1.0) and trigger 4 (leaving out W3 changes the sign of M minus default). A Sonnet audit ran, as the brief required in place of Opus; its findings follow.
  • Replicate caveat. The replicate reuses the out-of-fold quantiles, whose fold models saw later runs, so the replicate favours M; M is still worse there.

docs.title: Audit findings
docs.text:
• The contrast reproduces from the stored quantiles: M minus default is +0.077, +0.079, and +0.079 for the three seeds, on identical rows and actuals. No leakage was found; the table is fitted on out-of-fold quantiles only.
  • The table decides the sign. Without the table M0 beats the default by 0.28 points; the table helps the default by 0.345 and slightly harms M. The default needs the table to remove an ERA5 training bias that M never had.
  • The W3 sign flip is a farm-and-season effect, not a table artefact. Per-farm contrasts are W1 +0.058, W2 -0.080, and W3 +0.269. Both arms have one table per farm and lead day. The W3 gap sits in October to December 2025 (+1.48, +1.71, +0.70 points); the other nine W3 months average about -0.07. M is worse at lead days 6 to 10 on every farm (+0.13 overall, +0.30 at W3).
  • Reading. Three farms and 12 months cannot tell a farm difference from one bad quarter. The result is a null (monthly t test p = 0.48), not a refutation.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• M trains on 15 months of ensemble runs and the default on 4.4 years of ERA5; the history length is not separated from the training source.
  • The spread factor and the table are fitted on quantiles from models trained on two thirds of the hindcast and applied to a model trained on all of it, which biases against M and MS.
  • The placebo's permutation includes unusable hindcast cases whose target is set to zero, so the placebo is a worse model than intended; it still fails to gain, as a placebo should.
  • The "only inputs available at forecast time" part of condition 5 and the "no unresolved audit trigger" part of condition 4 are asserted by hand.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Mean training with ERA5 pre-training, then fine-tuning on the ensemble hindcast, to separate the training source from the history length.
  • A low-wind correction for M, since the harm below cut-in is the failed condition (see experiment 340).

docs.title: Plan (as committed before any score)
docs.text:
• Arms. D: the default (stored refit, reproduction gate). M: the same six weather columns as the default, on the 51-member mean of each column (sine and cosine of direction averaged, as the columns are), trained on the ensemble hindcast (2024-04-01 to 2025-06-16 runs, one row per run and valid time), same quantile loss, 500 rounds, eta 0.05, depth 6, binned-curve base margin. MS: M plus the member standard deviation of the 100 m speed and of the 10 m speed (the 10 m speed is the column other than the 100 m speed with the highest gain in the default, in all three farms). M0: M without the offset table, descriptive and never adopted. No calendar columns, no lead column, three seeds.
  • Cross-fitting. The hindcast is both the training set and the set that fits the spread factor and the offset table, so M and MS are cross-fitted in three blocks of consecutive run dates as in experiment 303: the hindcast quantiles come from models fitted without the held-out block and the runs whose valid times overlap it. The scored year comes from a model fitted on all usable hindcast cases.
  • Reuse. Scoring, the kept rows, the low-wind subsets, the replicate, and the spread factor and offset table follow experiments 340, 326, and 303 (imported, read only).
  • Predictions that can fail: P1, P2, and P3 above.
  • Five triggers: stored: private scored quantiles; serving path: no; degradation rule: no; designs: arms fixed by the brief; callers: this folder's scripts. Medium.
  • Ensemble-mean training is a lab condition for serving: the mean of 51 members is available at forecast time, so condition 5 holds.
  • Triage of the plan review (all applied before any score).
    • The spread factor and the offset table are fitted only on out-of-fold hindcast quantiles (held-out block, with training cases whose valid times fall inside the block's range removed, asserted in the fit). They are applied to the model fitted on all usable hindcast cases, which has seen about 50% more rows than the fold models; this mismatch biases against M and MS.
    • The spread factor is experiment 33's rule applied to the model's own single set of quantiles (no member mixture exists for M), fitted month by month on earlier cases.
    • The replicate (2025-01 to 2025-06 runs) reuses the out-of-fold quantiles with the table fitted on valid times before 2025-01. The fold models were trained on later runs, so the replicate favours M and MS; condition 3 is read with that caveat.
    • P2 is |M0 - M| < |default without table - default| on the kept rows, with the default's table-free score from experiment 340's default_notable. P3 reads "no better on the median" as a median pinball difference above -0.02 points.
    • All arms use colsample 1.0 (the settings of experiment 230); MS has eight columns against six, which is part of the arm. The default trains on 4.4 years of ERA5 and M on 15 months of ensemble runs; the write-up says the history length is not separated.
    • The default uses experiment 340's three seeds and their mean score; M and MS use seeds 0 to 2.
    • The default's gain per column (seed 0, W1 to W3): the 10 m speed is the highest column other than the 100 m speed (0.050, 0.051, 0.036 against 0.050, 0.054, 0.068 for the 100 m speed).
    • MS is tested only if M fails a condition, and need not beat M. Level 99.5% for both.
    • Controls: known-answer test (planted power curve recovered from synthetic members, mean absolute error under 0.03), placebo Mpl (target permuted across cases within the month, must not gain), leakage assertion in the fit (no training valid time inside a held-out block's range; latest hindcast valid time before the earliest scored valid time).

docs.title: Do quantile offsets that depend on the forecast wind speed improve Wind farms research default 1?
docs.text:
Take-home: letting the wind quantiles depend on the forecast wind speed gains only about 0.02 points of capacity when the correction is fitted on the hindcast, and that gain cannot be told from zero. Experiment 340 found that a constant upward shift of the forecast quantiles gains 0.09 to 0.12 points but worsens the half-hours with low wind by 0.5 to 0.8 points, and that the forecast median is too low at 8 to 15 m/s and too high below 5 m/s. We asked whether an offset that depends on the forecast wind speed keeps the gain and avoids the harm. The forecast is Wind farms research default 1, the wind forecast that scored best of those tested so far on the three metered wind farms (W1 to W3, anonymised), at 1 to 10 day leads. It is an XGBoost-based forecast with a spread factor and an offset table that adds one offset per farm, lead day, and quantile level. The score is the quantile score of experiment 33 in points of capacity (a point is 1% of a farm's capacity; a mean over nine quantile levels, lower is better), on the kept rows: the half-hours that the mask of experiment 210 does not flag as idle (wind near zero, where the metered series holds a reactive-power floor). The default scores 11.352.

Three arms fit the correction on the same hindcast runs as the offset table. The 442 hindcast runs are retrospective forecasts for April 2024 to June 2025. The correction is keyed by the mean over the 51 ensemble members of the 100 m wind speed at the valid time (the time the forecast is for). Arm x1 adds an offset per speed bin, x2 adds a smooth curve in speed per farm and quantile, and x3 adds one curve shared by the three farms, with a scale per farm. The arms gain 0.015, 0.021, and 0.022 points, against the 0.05 to 0.12 predicted. No 99.67% interval excludes zero (the level for three arms), so no arm is adopted, and the verdict is not supported.

A correction fitted on the six months before the scored year gains 0.146 points on the kept rows, so the bias is real and changes from year to year. This post hoc x2 curve, fitted on January to June 2025, does not worsen the half-hours where the forecast wind speed is below the turbines' cut-in speed. The scored year runs from July 2025 to June 2026.

Differences are the arm's score minus the default's, so a negative difference is an improvement.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Plan. Committed before any score. Tier 1: every arm acts on the default's stored quantiles, so nothing is retrained (the spread factor and the offset table are rebuilt from experiment 336's stored mixtures, as in experiment 340). A family comparison is not needed for a tier 1 change on stored forecasts. Minimum gain 0.02 points (each arm adds a fitted step). Code reused from the folders of experiments 340 and 336 (and through them 326, 303, 285, 259, and 230); the speed-bin pattern follows experiment 342, which keyed only q90 to q99.
  • Arms. x1: an additive offset per farm, lead day, quantile (all 11), and speed bin (edges at 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 m/s), none for a cell under 200 rows. x2: an S-shaped curve (a smoothstep, 6 m/s wide) of the offset against forecast speed per farm and quantile, with a low and a high offset level and a midpoint speed chosen from five candidates. x3: one such curve per quantile fitted on the three farms pooled, times one scale per farm. Post hoc and never adopted: x2 fitted on the January to June 2025 hindcast runs scored with the table fitted before 2025 (x2drift), and x2 fitted on the scored year (x2oracle). Reference: the default plus the constant shift of experiment 340 fitted out of sample (Sdrift, read from experiment 340's stored forecasts).
  • Row set and schedule. fold_a_tuesdays_v1, 53 Tuesday runs, 107,121 scored half-hours, 3 seeds. The offset table, the corrections, and the replicate use the same fitted-once hindcast schedule as experiment 340; there is no retraining here, so the contrast does not depend on the retraining cadence.
  • Reproduction gate. The default equals experiment 340's stored default exactly (largest difference 0) and scores 11.352, the same as experiment 303's stored forecast (P1).
  • Controls. Known-answer test: an injected speed-dependent bias is recovered by x2 within 12% and by x3 within 8% (limit 20%). Leakage check: the hindcast ends on 2025-06-16 and the scored year starts on 2025-07-01, and the key is the ensemble's speed at forecast time. Placebo: with the speed of another case of the same farm and lead day, x2 scores 0.121 worse, x1 0.243 worse, and x3 0.020 worse (points of capacity). The real speeds therefore beat the shuffled speeds by 0.142 (x2), 0.258 (x1), and 0.042 (x3).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Arm Kept rows All half-hours Forecast speed below cut-in ERA5 below cut-in Days 1 to 2 Days 3 to 10 0.01 pinball 0.99 pinball Default 11.352 10.825 2.394 5.374 6.612 11.759 0.284 0.640 x1 11.337 10.815 2.243 5.433 6.454 11.795 0.283 0.640 x2 11.331 10.813 2.173 5.457 6.543 11.763 0.284 0.640 x3 11.330 10.811 2.338 5.437 6.570 11.752 0.284 0.639 Post hoc: x2 fitted on 2025 H1 11.205 10.757 2.220 6.021 6.563 11.694 0.284 0.634 Oracle: x2 fitted on the scored year 11.090 10.652 2.197 5.978 6.392 11.605 0.284 0.631 Constant shift (experiment 340) 11.263 10.792 2.476 5.884 6.621 11.718 0.289 0.637

Reference rows on the kept rows: the frozen XGBoost reference (the default without the offset table) 11.697, climatology 13.547, persistence 15.566 (hours 0 to 6 only, 1,696 rows, where the default scores 6.568). The default beats climatology by 2.195 points (99.67% interval 1.302 to 3.100). The pinball columns are on the kept rows.

  • Take-home numbers, kept rows (99.67% intervals). x2 -0.021 (-0.126 to +0.077), x1 -0.015 (-0.176 to +0.180), x3 -0.022 (-0.057 to +0.009). The three farms differ in sign: x2 gains 0.07 at W2 and loses 0.02 at W3, and x1 gains 0.18 at W2 and loses 0.18 at W3.
  • Prediction P1 (x2 gains 0.05 to 0.12 points and worsens the rows below cut-in by under 0.1) fails on the gain and holds on low winds. x2 gains 0.021, below the predicted 0.05 to 0.12. The rows with forecast speed below cut-in improve by 0.221 (99.67% interval -0.318 to -0.016), so the predicted worsening of under 0.1 holds.
  • Prediction P2 (x1 gains less than x2 on the replicate) fails. x1 gains 0.068 on the replicate against 0.045 for x2 (the difference is -0.022, 95% interval -0.041 to -0.004, 99.67% interval -0.051 to +0.006).
  • Prediction P3 (x3 and x2 differ by under 0.03) holds. x3 minus x2 is -0.001 on the kept rows (99.67% interval -0.072 to +0.079).
  • Prediction P4 (at least 60% of x2's gain comes from 8 to 15 m/s) fails. The share of x2's kept-row gain from rows at 8 to 15 m/s is 0.081 (95% interval -5.8 to +7.4, because a share of a gain this small is not defined). The group gains are: below 5 m/s -0.041, 5 to 8 m/s -0.009, 8 to 15 m/s -0.021, and 15 m/s or more +0.878.
  • Prediction P5 (no arm moves the 0.99 pinball loss by more than 0.05) holds. The 0.99 pinball loss moves by -0.0004 (x2), -0.0001 (x1), and -0.0012 (x3).
  • Post hoc: the speed-dependent structure is real and has drifted. x2 fitted on January to June 2025 gains 0.146 on the kept rows (-0.257 to -0.038), against 0.089 for the constant shift of experiment 340 (-0.125 to -0.042), and it improves the rows with forecast speed below cut-in by 0.174 where the constant shift worsens them by 0.082. The post hoc x2 worsens the rows with ERA5 wind below cut-in by 0.647. Those rows are chosen using the observed wind, so they gather the cases where the forecast speed was too high. Every upward correction worsens such rows. x2 fitted on the scored year gains 0.262 (oracle, not an honest forecast).
  • Where the curves differ. In figure 2, at the median and 10 to 15 m/s, the median needs a lift of about 1 point at W1 and about 8 points at W2, and a cut of up to 17 points at W3. In figure 3, the default's median is below the observed median at W1 and W2 across 5 to 15 m/s and above it at W3 above 10 m/s.
  • Above 15 m/s the fitted corrections hurt. The group worsens by 0.878 (x2) and 3.503 (x1), because few hindcast rows exceed 15 m/s per farm, and the offsets there are large.
  • Tails. No arm raises the 0.01 or 0.99 pinball loss by more than 0.001 (kept rows). The share of kept rows where the observed power exceeds the forecast 0.99 quantile (ideally 1%) is 1.8% for the default, 1.7% for x2 and x3, and 1.8% for x1. The share inside the forecast 5% to 95% interval (ideally 90%) is 92.1% for the default, 91.4% for x2, 91.2% for x1, and 91.8% for x3.

Condition 5 holds for all arms (the key is the ensemble's forecast-time speed and the fits read only hindcast runs). x3 fails only condition 1: its 95% interval (-0.045 to -0.001) excludes zero, and its 99.67% interval, the level for three arms, does not.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, kept rows. Default -4.805 points (W1 -4.95, W2 -5.39, W3 -4.03), x2 -4.586 (-4.75, -4.73, -4.26), x1 -4.824, x3 -4.602 (-4.93, -5.39, -3.41), post hoc x2 -4.791. No arm shifts the spread.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. The absolute error of the mean forecast moves by -0.016 (x2, quantile score -0.021), +0.003 (x1, -0.015), and -0.011 (x3, -0.022). It rises by 0.034 for the post hoc x2 (quantile score -0.146) and 0.037 for the oracle, as it did for the shifts of experiment 340.
  • Triggers. The prediction-contradiction trigger (x2 gained 0.021, not 0.05 to 0.12) is explained and tested here by the post hoc arms: the hindcast fit gains little, and a fit after the table's window gains 0.146. The sign-disagreement trigger (the quantile score and the error of the mean forecast move in opposite directions) fired for x1, by 0.003 under an interval that spans zero, and for the post hoc arms. The leave-one-farm-out trigger fired for x2 and x1: leaving out W2 turns x2's gain into +0.003 and x1's into +0.067 (a loss), and W3 alone loses for both. The gain depends on one farm, which agrees with the interval spanning zero. No arm is adopted, so no adoption rests on the fired triggers. A Sonnet audit re-derived the contrasts from the stored quantiles (see Review).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scored at 1 to 10 days, 3 farms, 12 months. Intervals do not cover other farms or years.
  • The three farms disagree in sign, so a pooled gain depends on W2.
  • x3 is effectively two farms. Its scales ended at the ends of the 0 to 3 grid in all three seeds (W2 0.0, W3 3.0, W1 about 0.4), so the shared curve follows W3 and the W2 correction is switched off. In x2, 20 of the 33 fitted curves per seed chose an edge midpoint (5 or 11 m/s), Those edge midpoints fit the poorly determined region above 15 m/s. That fit explains the harm there.
  • The placebo cannot detect harm. The shuffled-speed placebo (condition 4) passes whenever the shuffled-speed arm scores worse than the default, which is what happened. The known-answer test has no case where the true bias is zero.
  • The fits read one hindcast. The curves are fitted per seed on the same 442 runs as the offset table, and the fit minimises the pinball loss at each level separately. The shape of x2 (two levels, a smoothstep of width 6 m/s, five candidate midpoints) is a pre-registered choice and not tuned on the scored year.
  • The post hoc arms are not honest forecasts. x2drift uses January to June 2025, which a live service could fit; x2oracle reads the scored year.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
• Code review and audit (Sonnet, one agent, from the files only). No leakage, and no arithmetic error: its own re-derivation matched every contrast, per-farm and leave-one-farm-out sign, median-minus-mean figure, and placebo score, and an independent minimisation matched the stored curves. Accepted: the placebo cannot detect harm, x3's scales sit at the grid ends, x2 often picks an edge midpoint, and the score is nine-level (all now stated above). No finding changes a verdict.
  • Prose review (Sonnet, one agent). Accepted: the opening split into three bolded paragraphs with the score and mask defined, the headline and take-home message rewritten, the predictions and triggers named by content, the farms no longer "wanting" a correction, and the tail shares defined. Rejected: dropping the repeated conclusion from the headline (the front matter and the body serve different readers); expanding NWP and XGBoost (the page no longer uses NWP, and the page's readers know XGBoost).

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• A refit on recent months is untested. Refitting the offset table and the speed curve every few months on the latest hindcast runs could capture the drift that the post hoc x2drift arm gains.
  • A per-farm speed curve for the upper quantiles at 15 m/s or more is poorly determined by the hindcast; a cap on the offset there is an untried option.

docs.title: Does one pooled mixture-density network for all leads, trained on solar and wind farms together, match the best single-family forecast for each fuel, and help a farm with no history?
docs.text:
One neural network trained across all six solar farms forecasts each farm as well as a separate network on the physical plant model, to within 0.8%. Adding wind farms to the same network does not help either fuel, and it makes solar between 0.7% and 2.3% worse. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters six solar farms, labelled A to F, and three wind farms, labelled W1 to W3. Experiment 313 and experiment 318 found that a mixture-density network (a neural network whose output is a mixture of three normal distributions, from which the 11 quantiles are read) that sees only weather and the calendar matches the plant-based network. We asked whether one such network, trained once for all leads on all six solar farms (and then also on wind farms, with a fuel indicator), keeps that skill. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantiles, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of capacity), and lower is better. "Own history" means the farm's earlier months are in training, and "zero history" means the farm is held out.

Scored at leads of 1 to 10 days for solar, and at 12 to 252 hours (0.5 to 10.5 days) for wind. The stored wind cases reach 351 hours, and the page does not score beyond 252 hours. Solar refits quarterly (experiment 310's screening schedule), wind trains once on rows before 2025-06-17. The pre-registered predictions: P1 holds at the point estimates but not by its interval rule; P2 and P3 fail; P4 holds. The verdict is partly supported, and nothing is adopted: the pooled network does not beat Metered solar farms research default 1 by 0.02 points, the minimum gain that the plan requires for a change that adds a new data source.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms (all five seeds averaged in own history, three in zero history). The reference is Metered solar farms research default 1 ("default"): its blend (experiment 310) and its mixture-density network on the plant (experiment 318, "network on the plant"). The default plus x arms are the solar-only pooled network (weather and calendar inputs only, with the lead in hours as an input, trained across the six farms), the wind-only pooled network (W1 to W3 plus 40 public wind farms), and the solar-plus-wind pooled network (a fuel indicator, columns a fuel lacks set to zero), both is the solar-plus-wind pooled network, and both_plant is the same network with the plant forecast added as an input column. The plan classes these arms as tier 2, a change that adds a new data source, which needs a gain of at least 0.02 points to be adopted. Controls: the fuel indicator shuffled, the wind targets shuffled, climatology, and manual_heuristic.
  • Weather at each lag. Solar rows use the ECMWF ensemble mean at each lead, which exists at forecast time. Wind training rows use ERA5, which arrives about 5 days late, so ERA5 wind scores are a ceiling. The headline wind rows apply the network to each of the 51 ensemble members and mix the quantiles. The public wind farms' ERA5 rows carry no temperature (the column is masked and flagged).
  • Row set. Solar: experiment 310's rows, farms A to F, 2025-09 to 2026-08. Wind: fold_a_tuesdays_v1, kept rows of experiment 285's 53 Tuesday runs, 12 to 252 hours.
  • Schedule. Quarterly refits (screening schedule). The contrast between pooled and single-family networks could depend on cadence: a pooled network trained once, instead of refitted quarterly, scores 1.4% to 1.6% worse at days 1 to 3 in own history, and monthly refits change nothing measurable (-0.8% to +0.5%).

docs.title: Solar quantile score (points of capacity, 98.75% interval), own history
docs.text:
Arm Day 1 Day 3 Days 8 to 10 climatology 8.64 8.64 8.64 manual_heuristic 8.69 8.68 8.83 Default blend (research default 1) 5.30 6.05 7.77 Network on the plant (single family) 5.36 [4.76, 5.90] 6.08 [5.40, 6.67] 7.75 [6.87, 8.64] Solar-only pooled network 5.34 [4.70, 5.92] 6.04 [5.36, 6.64] 7.80 [6.91, 8.81] Solar-plus-wind pooled network 5.37 [4.76, 5.93] 6.12 [5.44, 6.73] 7.93 [6.96, 9.08]

Zero history: network on the plant 5.53, 6.23, 7.91; solar-only pooled 5.46, 6.14, 7.88; solar-plus-wind 5.53, 6.25, 8.06 (days 1, 3, and 8 to 10).

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (solar-only pooled within 1% of the network on the plant): holds at the point estimate, cannot be shown by the interval. The change is -0.7% to +0.8% in own history and -2.0% to +0.1% in zero history, with intervals about 4 points wide (for example -2.0% to +0.7% at day 3, own history). The pooled network is not worse than 1% in any band, and it is better in zero history at day 2 (-2.0%, interval -3.9% to -0.2%).
  • P2 (adding wind within 1% of solar-only): fails on solar. Solar-plus-wind is worse by 0.7% to 1.6% in own history and 1.2% to 2.3% in zero history, with interval lower ends above zero from day 3 in both settings. On wind, solar-plus-wind is within 1% of the wind-only network in own history (-1.3% to +0.2%, intervals about 4 points wide) and 0.1% to 2.0% worse in zero history.
  • P3 (pooling helps with zero history by at least 2%): fails. Solar-plus-wind is 1.2% to 2.3% worse than solar-only, and 0.1% to 2.0% worse than the wind-only network, with no history.
  • P4 (0.99 pinball loss no worse than the default blend at days 3 to 7): holds. The pooled solar-only network is 7.0% to 8.2% lower and solar-plus-wind 6.0% to 6.1% lower in own history (intervals below zero).
  • Stop rule: not triggered. Adding wind raises the score by more than 2% at days 1 and 2 at no farm (largest +1.5% at farm F, interval 0.5% to 2.9%).

docs.title: Standard architecture and the best family
docs.text:
• Solar. The standard architecture (the brief's shared design: the plant, no neural input adapter, and a mixture-density head) is within 1% of the best single family (the solar-only pooled network, or experiment 313's pure network at days 1 to 2) at every band in own history (0.4%, 0.8%, 0.6%, then -0.2% to -0.8%), with intervals about 4 points wide. In zero history it is 2.0% worse at day 2 (0.2% to 4.0%) and within 1.5% elsewhere.
  • Wind. On ERA5 weather (the stored neural-adapter forecasts have no ensemble version) the physics core with the neural adapter (no mixture-density head) is within 0.25% of experiment 313's pure network over 12 to 252 hours (-1.6% to +2.9%) and 5.7% better than the wind-only pooled network (-9.2% to -2.3%). The pooled wind network is the weaker family on ERA5 weather, because the 40 public farms outnumber W1 to W3 in training.
  • Shared with the Primary-demand research default. The mixture-density head family is shared. The plant (a physical model of one farm's output) is not shared with the demand model, and the lead band structure differs.

docs.title: Controls and checks
docs.text:
• Shuffled wind targets are 30% worse on wind (21% to 40%), so the wind gain is not extra rows. The shuffled wind targets make solar 0.6% to 1.1% worse than the real wind rows do (three seeds against five, so part of that gap is seed averaging). So the real wind rows worsen solar less than shuffled wind rows do. Shuffled fuel indicator makes wind 0.7% worse (0.3% to 1.1%) and solar 0.8% to 1.2% worse, so the network uses the indicator a little.
  • Plant column (both_plant against both): -0.9% to -0.4% own history, -0.5% to 0% zero history, intervals including zero. The plant adds nothing measurable, as in experiment 318.
  • Tail calibration (own history). The share of actual values below the 0.01 quantile is 3.2% to 3.5% for every arm (experiment 318 reported 3.3% to 3.7%; experiment 321 found a lower share with a stricter count). The share below the 0.99 quantile is 98.2% to 98.9% for the networks and 99.0% to 99.2% for the blend (Figure 5).
  • Median minus mean forecast is 0.3 to 0.8 points of capacity for the networks and 0.04 to 0.7 for the blend; the networks' quantiles are never crossed (crossing rate 0).
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast. The absolute error of the mean forecast moves the same way as the quantile score for solar-plus-wind against solar-only (+0.8% to +1.3% own history, +1.4% to +1.8% zero history) and for solar-only against the network on the plant (-0.7% to +0.8%).
  • Audit triggers. The audit checklist requires an explanation whenever results contradict the pre-registered predictions, which happened for P2 and P3. The explanation offered, not proven, is that a shared network of 64 hidden units and a fixed 20-epoch budget fits both fuels less well than it fits one. The shuffled-wind control worsens solar by a similar amount, which is consistent with limited network size and not with a wind-specific harm. See the audit below.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Wind own history is a different design from experiment 313. Experiment 313 trained one network per farm on that farm's ERA5 history; here one network trains on W1 to W3 and 40 public farms. Both pooled networks are 2% to 3.5% worse than experiment 313 at days 1 and 2, and the day-1 interval (0.1% to 6.8% for the wind-only network) is not stable across the two halves of the year (+2.1% in the first, +5.5% in the second). Both pooled networks match experiment 313's network from day 3.
  • Wind zero history is a different design from experiment 313. Experiment 313 trained on the other two metered farms; here W1 to W3 are held out and the network trains on 40 public farms (ERA5, no temperature). The wind-only pooled network scores 18% to 20% worse at days 1 and 2 than experiment 313's network (6.5% to 36% interval), and equal from day 4. Training on the public farms alone is a poor start for a wind farm with no history at short leads.
  • The solar-only pooled network is one network across farms and lead bands, and the network on the plant is one network per farm and per band, so "within 0.8%" compares different pooling. Experiment 318's one head per farm across all bands scores 0.01 to 0.03 points lower than its per-band head at every band, so pooling across bands alone is not what separates the two.
  • Wind scores use experiment 285's nine-level weighted score and solar scores use the mean over 11 levels, so a wind number and a solar number must not be compared.
  • Intervals on the solar contrasts are about 4 points wide, so "within 1%" cannot be shown by interval for any single band.
  • Own-history solar scores use the same six farms in training and scoring, with a quarterly refit schedule. Weekly retraining was not run.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet auditor re-derived the solar and wind contrasts from the stored predictions and found no leakage (training rows end before each refit's cutoff, the validation split lies inside the training range, scored runs never feed training, and the wind networks train on rows before 2025-06-17). It confirmed the headline contrasts to within a 22-row difference in the row set. The auditor counted 30 public wind farms where the preparation script printed 40 qualifying farms, and the page uses the script's count. The auditor's report is in the private data/ml-experiments/briefs/ folder.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Train wind on metered wind farms only (own history), and test whether public farms help with a weight on the metered farms.
  • The solar-only pooled network is a candidate for the solar forecast of a production update. A production-style run against plant-fed XGBoost would test it.

docs.title: Does refitting the offset table of Wind farms research default 1 every month, on recent runs only, improve the wind forecast?
docs.text:
Take-home: refitting the wind forecast's offset table every month on recent runs gains a little, and the upper-tail miss stays. We asked whether the offset table of Wind farms research default 1 should be refitted as time passes. Wind farms research default 1 is our current wind forecast: an XGBoost model fitted on ERA5 weather estimates, plus the table. The table is a number added to each forecast quantile, one for each farm and each number of days ahead, and so far it was fitted once on 442 daily forecast runs of 2024-04 to 2025-06, re-created after the fact. Experiment 342 found that observed power exceeded the forecast's 99th-percentile quantile (q99) in 1.8% of half-hours in 2025-07 to 2026-06, where 1% is intended, and blamed a change in the farms' behaviour between the earlier years and that year. We refitted the table on the first day of each month, using only daily ECMWF ensemble weather forecasts whose outcomes had already been observed. We tried three training windows: all runs since 2024-04 (x1), the last 6 months (x2), and the last 3 months (x3). We scored 53 forecast runs, one per Tuesday, at lead times of 1 to 10 days.

The three metered wind farms are anonymised as W1 to W3. The score is the quantile score over 11 levels, in points of capacity (a point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better), on the kept rows: the half-hours that the idle-band mask of experiment 210 does not flag. Each difference is the arm's score minus the default's. All three windows lower the score by 0.05 to 0.13 points of 11.35 (0.4% to 1.1%). Only x1 has a 99.67% interval for the difference that lies wholly below zero. The share of observed power above q99 stays at 1.7% to 1.8%, so a table that follows the change still misses, and the change is a minor cause. The verdict is partly supported: x1 passes the five adoption conditions (a candidate, minimum gain 0), and the hypothesised x2 does not.

docs.title: Arms and row set
docs.text:
• Plan. The plan was committed before any score. The one later change corrected the placebo check in e00346_score.py from an absolute difference to the signed gain.
  • Family and default. Default plus x against Wind farms research default 1 (experiment 303's P1, offset table fitted once on the 442 hindcast runs), rows fold_a_tuesdays_v1, 107,121 scored half-hours at 3 farms, 3 seeds, scored at 1 to 10 days (the headline caveat). Tier 1 (acts on stored mixtures), minimum gain 0. Code reused from experiments 342, 340, 336, 326, 303, 259.
  • Method. The default's XGBoost models, trained on ERA5, were refitted on CPU (the earlier fits used a GPU), so every run, old and new, goes through the same models. Member rows for the 494 daily runs of 2025-06-17 to 2026-10-23 were built as experiment 259 built the hindcast. The table of month M uses cases whose valid time is at least 3.5 hours before M's first day. The spread factor, which widens or narrows the forecast quantiles around the median, is fitted on all daily runs. The gate arm fits it on the hindcast and the 53 Tuesday runs only, as in experiment 340, and gives the same scores to three decimals.
  • Arms. x1 expanding window from 2024-04; x2 trailing 6 months; x3 trailing 3 months; the reference quarterly refit on an expanding window; the placebo (each scored run gets the x2 table of a random earlier month). Tables exist for each month from 2024-10.
  • Absolute scores (kept rows). Default 11.351 (experiment 340's frozen XGBoost reference 11.697, climatology 13.547; BG2 and manual_heuristic were not scored for wind farms here). x1 11.305, x2 11.223, x3 11.225, quarterly 11.314, placebo 11.462. Days 1 to 2: default 6.908, x2 6.869. Days 3 to 10: default 12.370, x2 12.221.
  • Contrasts (99.67% intervals, kept rows). x2 -0.128 (-0.266 to +0.039); x1 -0.046 (-0.085 to -0.006); x3 -0.126 (-0.270 to +0.119); quarterly -0.037 (-0.074 to -0.000); placebo +0.111 (-0.009 to +0.246). Days 3 to 10 hold most of the gain (x1 -0.055, x2 -0.149); days 1 to 2 hold little (x1 -0.005, x2 -0.039). Every contrast on all half-hours is smaller (x1 -0.020).
  • Out of time (descriptive, 2026-07 to 2026-10, 30,174 half-hours; kept rows end on 2026-09-13, the last day of experiment 210's mask). Default 7.562; x1 -0.046 (95% interval -0.078 to -0.024), x2 -0.056 (-0.218 to +0.004), x3 -0.070 (-0.168 to -0.036), quarterly -0.044.
  • Tails (kept rows). The 0.01 pinball loss is 0.284 to 0.285 for every arm. The 0.99 pinball loss is 0.640 (default), 0.639 (x1), 0.640 (x2), 0.638 (x3). Share above q99: 1.77% default, 1.75% x1, 1.71% x2, 1.78% x3; above q95: 6.7% default, 6.4% x1, 5.9% x2, 6.0% x3. Curtailment-cost saving against manual_heuristic was not computed (the metric scores a substation and its generators together, not single wind farms).
  • Predictions that could fail. x2 lowers the score by 0.05 to 0.15: held (0.128, interval includes zero). x1 gains less than x2: held. x3 is noisier and gains less than x2: half held (the interval is wider; the gain is equal). The 0.99 pinball loss moves under 0.05: held. The gain is larger in the second half of the scored year: held for x1 (-0.065 against -0.029) and x2 (-0.138 against -0.119), failed for x3 (-0.049 against -0.196). The out-of-time gain is at least the scored year's: held for x1, failed for x2 and x3.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Controls. Reproduction gate: the default scores 11.351 against experiment 259's 11.352. Known-answer test: tables fitted on synthetic cases with a bias that grows by 6 points recover the window-average bias within 0.07 points (x2) and 0.18 points (x3), and the expanding window lags the drift by 2.9 points at 2026-06. Placebo: it loses 0.111, so it keeps none of x2's gain. Leakage: every one of the fitted tables (printed in leakage.json) uses only valid times before its month's first day minus 3.5 hours.
  • Median minus mean forecast, per farm (kept rows, points). The median forecast sits 4 to 5 points below the mean forecast, and the refit narrows the gap. Default -4.95, -5.39, -4.03 at W1, W2, W3; x2 -4.52, -5.29, -3.84.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. The mean forecast's mean absolute error rises by 0.023 (x1), 0.157 (x2), and 0.214 (x3) while the quantile score falls, and the median's mean absolute error falls by 0.076, 0.222, and 0.221. Trigger 3 fired.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 3 (above). Leaving one farm out keeps every sign. See "Audit".

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
Audit trigger 3 fired: the mean forecast got worse while the quantile score improved. A fresh Sonnet agent (the maintainer's instruction for this run replaced the usual Opus agent) therefore re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored arrays and tried to break them. Its report is private (data/ml-experiments/briefs/e346_audit_report.md). Triage:

  • No leakage (accepted). The latest valid time in each sampled table equals the month's first day minus 3.5 hours. Scrambling every observed value after the cutoff left the spread factor and the tables for earlier cases bit-identical.
  • Headline reproduced (accepted). x1 -0.0460, x2 -0.1281, x3 -0.1264, placebo +0.1112, all within 0.0001 of the printed values.
  • Trigger 3 is a property of the metric, not a method fault (accepted). The default's table is stale in the scored year: observed power falls below its q50 in 40.4% of kept half-hours (50% intended). The refit raises the central quantiles by about 2 points, which lowers the pinball losses and the median's error. The default's mean forecast already sits 4.8 points above its median, so the same shift overshoots the mean. The mean forecast is a quantity the offsets were not fitted for, and its error rise (+0.023, +0.157, +0.214 points) is a drawback to state.
  • The placebo is a weak control (accepted as a caveat). It loses 0.111, so the placebo condition passes trivially. A fairer control would draw tables from the last 1 to 6 months.
  • Caveats (accepted). The cells at long lead days are thin (at least 484, 177, and 89 rows for x1, x2, and x3) and their rows are strongly correlated. x2 and x3 lose in 2026-02. x1 is the selected candidate because of the pre-registered order and because its interval is narrow, on a gain of 0.4%.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Decide whether a monthly job that refits the table (x1) is worth its 0.4% gain.
  • The upper tail still misses at 1.7% above q99; test an upper-tail correction fitted per month on the scored months themselves only if the maintainer wants the tail rather than the headline.

docs.title: Does a frozen physics plant model of a wind farm, fed each ensemble member in turn and followed by a mixture-density head on the summary of the resulting power ensemble, forecast the three metered wind farms better than Wind farms research default 1?
docs.text:
Take-home: a physics model of each wind farm, run on every ensemble member and corrected by a small neural network, forecasts 0.27 points of capacity better than Wind farms research default 1, but a neural network given only the physics model's median and the farm already gets 83% of the gain, and the upper tail is still over-confident. The quantile score measures how well a forecast's 11 quantiles match the observed power, in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity; lower is better).

We asked whether a frozen physics model of each of the three metered wind farms (called W1 to W3 here) can replace the XGBoost model in Wind farms research default 1, called "the default" below. The default is an XGBoost model trained on ERA5 (our estimate of past weather) and run on the 51 members of the ECMWF ensemble (51 perturbed runs of one weather forecast), plus a table of per-quantile offsets. The physics model, called the plant, turns wind speed at 10 m and 100 m, air temperature, and wind direction into power through a smooth speed-to-power curve with a direction-dependent loss. We fitted each plant once on ERA5 before April 2024 and then froze it. We passed each of the 51 members through the plant, summarised the 51 power values (median, mean, standard deviation, 10th and 90th percentiles, and the share of members at the top level), and fed the summary to a mixture-density head (a small neural network that fits three bell curves to each forecast, from which the 11 quantiles are read). Four arms differ in the plant and the inputs of the head (see "Arms").

The headline scores every lead from 0.5 hours to 15 days, as experiments 324 and 339 do; on true days 1 to 10 the gain is 0.23 and the 99.75% interval includes zero. The row set holds every lead from 0.5 hours to 351 hours, so the plan's phrase "scored at 1 to 10 days" did not describe the scored rows. The page gives both: "every lead" means all kept rows, and "true days 1 to 10" means the kept rows with lead 24 to 240 hours.

The best arm, y2, scored 11.081 against the default's 11.352 over every lead (-0.271, 95% interval -0.408 to -0.127), and 10.518 against 10.752 over true days 1 to 10 (-0.234, 95% interval -0.413 to -0.049). Three results limit what the gain supports. First, a head fed only the plant's median, the lead, and the farm scores 11.128 and so reproduces 83% of the gain. Second, y2 ties experiment 324's physics core with a neural adapter and a head (+0.001), so the new plant adds nothing over the old core. Third, 2.3% of observations exceed the 0.99 quantile (nominal 1%), and the harm to the 0.99 pinball loss has a one-sided 95% upper bound of +0.084 against a limit of +0.05. The verdict is partly supported, and no arm is adopted.

docs.title: Arms and architecture
docs.text:
• y1: Stage 2 plant (speed-to-power curve with priors on cut-in, rated, and cut-out speed, a blur over speed for the 25 km cell, and a hub-height shear and air-density correction), then the head on the six summary columns, the lead, and the farm.
  • y2: Stage 3 plant (y1's plant plus three direction-dependent losses), same head.
  • y3: y2's plant, with the head given only the mean and standard deviation of the 51 power values.
  • y4: pass-2 plant, fitted again after masking the days on which a farm fell short of the pass-1 plant, same head as y2.
  • Head: one pooled network per arm and seed (two hidden layers of 64 units, three Gaussian components, 11 quantiles read from the mixture's CDF, capped at capacity), trained on the kept hindcast half-hours of W1 to W3 before 2025-04-16, with early stopping on the later runs. Five seeds.
  • Standard architecture: physics plant + MDN head. The plant has no neural adapter, and the head sees only the plant's summary, the lead, and the farm.
  • Row set: fold_a_tuesdays_v1, 53 Tuesday runs from 2025-07 to 2026-06, 96,479 kept rows (107,121 in all). Kept rows exclude the idle-band half-hours of experiment 210's mask. Intervals resample whole calendar months of run date.

docs.title: Standard architecture against the best single family
docs.text:
• Standard architecture: physics plant + MDN head (y2) scores 0.171 below the best single family, experiment 326's XGBoost + adapter column + table. The scores are 11.081 against 11.253 over every lead (-1.52%; 95% interval -0.293 to -0.046; 99.75% interval -0.349 to +0.017).

  • Over all half-hours the gap reverses: +0.054 (95% -0.041 to +0.150), because the head scores worse on the idle-band rows.
  • The standard architecture ties the other plant-plus-head design: y2 minus experiment 324's W4 is +0.001.

docs.title: Replicate
docs.text:
Heads trained on 2024-04 to 2024-11 (early stopping on December 2024) and scored on the daily runs of 2025-01 to 2025-06, three seeds, against the default's 10.210 (9.728 over true days 1 to 10).
