All four arms beat the default in each of the six months (Figure 15), so the sign replicates.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Head fed the plant's median, the lead, and the farm (five seeds): 11.128 over every lead and 10.587 over true days 1 to 10. y2 minus this control is -0.047 (95% -0.104 to +0.011) and -0.069 (95% -0.154 to +0.010). The control minus the default is -0.224 (95% -0.351 to -0.093), which is 83% of y2's gain (70% over true days 1 to 10).
  • The first, unequal control gave the head no farm columns and scored 11.273, and y2 minus it was -0.192 (95% -0.353 to -0.034). The two controls differ by 0.145 (95% 0.008 to 0.283), so the missing farm columns, not the missing spread summaries, explain most of that gap. Only the control with the farm columns is the fair one.
  • Shuffled spread only (the placebo): the head scores 12.102 when the standard deviation, the 10th and 90th percentiles, and the saturation share come from another month of the same farm, and the true median and mean are kept. The spread-only placebo scores +1.020 above y2 (95% +0.856 to +1.204), and +1.264 over true days 1 to 10. The same shuffle costs +1.057 for y1, +0.718 for y3, and +0.970 for y4. The head therefore reads the spread columns, and mismatched spread is worse than none (+0.973 above the median-and-farm control).
  • Shuffled every summary including the median: 15.982, +4.901 above y2 (95% +4.247 to +5.519). The all-summaries placebo shows that the plant's median carries the signal, and does not test the spread.
  • Leave one farm out (no farm columns, trained on the other two): 11.469 for y2, +0.117 above the default (95% -0.075 to +0.317) and +0.387 above y2 (95% +0.186 to +0.588). A farm with no history gains nothing from the head.
  • Nested arms: y3 minus y2 is +0.034, and the median-and-farm control minus y2 is +0.047 (95% -0.011 to +0.104). Neither nested arm beats its container.

docs.title: Stage 3 and 3b outcomes
docs.text:
• Direction term on ERA5: the Stage 3 plant lowers the pooled ERA5 hold-out score from 5.968 to 5.892 (-0.076, 95% -0.132 to -0.018). The prediction of a gain of 0.02 to 0.1 holds. The prediction of a larger gain at W1 and W2 than at W3 fails (W1 0.047, W2 0.058, W3 0.128).
  • The injection test missed its criterion at W1 and W2. The criterion was detecting at least 80% of injected blocks with under 5% false flags. A 25% power loss over 3 to 14 days was found in 12% of blocks at W1 and 1% at W2 (3 robust standard deviations), and the loss of one turbine in 2% and 0%. The robust standard deviation of the daily log ratio is 0.13 to 0.18, so a 25% loss moves one day by only 1.6 to 2.1 standard deviations. At W3 the largest injected loss was found in 98% of blocks, with 10.6% false flags.
  • The flagged days are mostly isolated days of ERA5 speed error, not hardware outages. The unmodified series flags 7.2% (W1), 3.8% (W2), and 11.4% (W3) of days at 3 standard deviations, against 0.13% for a Gaussian, and the longest block is 3, 3, and 7 days. Arm y4 therefore tests a plant fitted on a thinned training set, and says nothing about hardware outages.
  • Third pass: a third fit after masking gives nearly the same flagged days (Jaccard 0.97 to 1.00 against pass 2) and a hold-out score within 0.001 of pass 2's.
  • Placebo mask: masking the same number of random day blocks moves the fitted parameters by amounts that the real mask exceeds by more than two placebo standard deviations for some quantities (the rated speed at W1 and W3, the scale at W2, and the hold-out score at W2 and W3). All the shifts are small: the hold-out score changes by at most 0.009 points. The prediction that y4 differs from y2 by under 0.05 holds (+0.003).

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• Holds: y2 beats y1 by under 0.05 (-0.016).
  • Fails: y2 within 0.15 of the default and not beating it by 0.03. y2 beats it by 0.271.
  • Fails: y3 within 0.03 of y2 (+0.034, interval -0.011 to +0.084).
  • Fails narrowly: a head fed only the plant's median does as well as the full head. With the farm columns the median-only head scores 0.047 worse than y2 (95% -0.104 to +0.011), which is past the 0.03 line and inside noise.
  • Holds: the share above q99 stays above 1% (2.25% to 2.34%).
  • Holds: y4 differs from y2 by under 0.05 (+0.003).

docs.title: Adoption conditions
docs.text:
• Condition 1 (gain) passes over every lead and fails over true days 1 to 10. The 99.75% intervals of arm minus default are below zero for all four arms over every lead (y4 -0.473 to -0.053, y3 -0.450 to -0.016, y2 -0.472 to -0.057, y1 -0.458 to -0.017), and include zero over true days 1 to 10 (upper ends +0.051 to +0.107).
  • Condition 2 (tails) fails for every arm over every lead. The 0.99 harm bound of +0.076 to +0.084 is above +0.05. Over true days 1 to 10 only y3 passes (+0.046), and y3 fails condition 1. The upper tail therefore blocks adoption, and no arm is adopted.
  • Condition 3 (replicate) passes for all four arms at both scopes.
  • Condition 4 (controls): the reproduction gate and the seed check pass, the spread-only placebo costs 0.72 to 1.06 points, and two audit triggers fired and are triaged below.
  • Condition 5 (serving): see the next section.
  • Candidate: y4, y3, y2, and y1 each win condition 1 over every lead and fail condition 2, so all four stay candidates, with y2 and y4 the best.

docs.title: Serving needs
docs.text:
• y1: frozen plant parameters per farm (about 15 numbers: the three speed thresholds and their widths, a scale, a blur, and a hub height), one pass of each of the 51 members' four weather columns through the plant, and one mixture-density head.
  • y2, y3, and y4: the same, plus three direction losses per farm in the plant. y3 feeds the head two summary columns instead of six.
  • Nothing else: no XGBoost model, no offset table, no neural adapter, and no ERA5 at forecast time.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per farm (every lead, points of capacity), W1, W2, W3: default -4.95, -5.39, -4.03; y1 -4.08, -4.29, -3.29; y2 -4.06, -4.40, -3.35; y3 -4.26, -4.48, -3.54; y4 -4.06, -4.34, -3.25; median-and-farm control -3.98, -4.37, -3.11. The heads bring the median 0.7 to 1.0 points of capacity closer to the mean than the default's median is.
  • Error of the mean and median forecast beside the y2 contrast with the default (every lead): quantile score -0.271 (95% -0.408 to -0.127), mean-forecast squared error -15.5 (95% -27.1 to -3.2), median-forecast squared error -50.6 (95% -66.4 to -34.8), median-forecast absolute error -0.382 (95% -0.592 to -0.166), and mean-forecast absolute error +0.116 (95% -0.076 to +0.308). The root mean squared error of the mean forecast is 21.56 for y2 against 21.92 for the default. Over true days 1 to 10 the same errors are -12.5 (95% -25.7 to +1.9), -41.4 (95% -61.2 to -23.2), -0.339 (95% -0.616 to -0.063), and +0.117 (95% -0.078 to +0.338). The mean forecast is the nine-level mean, and absolute error is minimised by the median, so squared error is the matching yardstick for a mean forecast. y1, y3, y4, and the median-and-farm control agree with y2.
  • Audit triggers fired: trigger 1 (a control fails) fired because of the injection test, and trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fired for the four predictions above. Trigger 3 fired on the first scoring run, on the mean-forecast absolute error, and does not fire once squared error is the check. Triggers 4 (leave-one-farm-out flips a contrast), 5 (a nested arm beats its container), and 6 (interval width, 1.27 to 1.37 times experiment 339's) do not fire. Trigger 7 holds: the replicate supports the sign.
  • Audit findings and triage. A fresh Sonnet auditor recomputed the headline from the stored predictions and found no leakage.
    • Finding 1, the lead scope: accepted, and fixed by scoring true days 1 to 10 and labelling both scopes.
    • Finding 2, the control without farm columns: accepted, and fixed by rerunning the control with the farm columns (five seeds; the auditor's three-seed run gave 11.140 against 11.128).
    • Finding 3, quantile score against mean-forecast error: accepted as a yardstick fault, and fixed by adding squared errors.
    • Finding 4, the capacity ceiling: accepted as a caveat. The fix (a ceiling above capacity) changes the head after the scores are read and breaks comparability with experiment 339, so it belongs in a new experiment.
    • Finding 5, the placebo that shuffles the median: accepted, and the spread-only placebo is now the placebo, with the docstring corrected.
    • Finding 6, the injection test: accepted as a limitation of the daily-ratio rule.
    • Finding 7, leakage: no change. prior_scales() reads the capacity-scale prior from ERA5 through 2025-06-16, and the effect on Stage 4 is negligible (prior sd 15%). The auditor did not trace how the effective-capacity file was built, and every arm and the default share it.
    • Findings 8 and 9, pairing and anonymisation: no change. Nothing was rejected outright.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scope: the headline scores every lead from 0.5 hours to 15 days (31% of rows have a lead of at least 240 hours). The pre-registered condition 1 names days 1 to 10, and on that scope no arm passes it.
  • Three farms, one scored year: 53 Tuesday runs and 12 month blocks. The interval on the gain is wide, and W3 alone shows no clear gain.
  • ERA5-trained plant on ensemble input: the plant is fitted to ERA5 and run on ensemble members, whose mean 100 m wind speed is 4% below ERA5's at W1 at leads under 24 hours. The head absorbs that offset, so the plant's physics is not tested on its own.
  • Idle-band rows: y2 scores 8.241 on them against 6.051 for the default.
  • Not computed: the curtailment-cost saving and the threshold-weighted CRPS. The predictions (11 quantiles, actual, lead hours, and time series) are stored privately for that node metric.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Raise the quantile ceiling above capacity or add a tail model to the head, and test whether the share above q99 falls to 1% and condition 2 passes.
  • Test a head fed the median of experiment 326's arm c and the farm, because the plant's median and the farm already give 83% of the gain, and the test shows whether the plant adds anything over the adapter column.
  • Fit the plant's parameters on the ensemble members' own hindcast instead of ERA5, so that the plant's speed bias is a fitted quantity.

docs.title: Does fixing the upper tail of the frozen physics plant plus mixture head let it beat Wind farms research default 1 on the three metered wind farms?
docs.text:
Take-home: the frozen physics plant with a mixture head stays about 0.23 points of capacity better than Wind farms research default 1 over days 1 to 10, but no tail fix inside the head calibrates the top quantile without raising the pinball loss at that quantile, and the plain recipe of blending the plant's residual band with the default's XGBoost quantiles is the only arm whose gain is clear. Verdict: partly supported. The next step is to build on that blend, and to fit a point mass with a likelihood.

We asked whether five changes to the upper tail would make experiment 347's best arm (a physics model of each farm run on the 51 weather-ensemble members, then a three-component Gaussian mixture head) adoptable. The head scored 0.23 points better than the default but put 2.2% of observed power above its 0.99 quantile (2.3% over every lead). The five changes were a loss that weights the top quantiles (z1), a point mass at the farm's maximum plus a cap (z2), monotone increments above the 0.9 quantile (z3), z1 plus z2 (z4), and a blend of the plant's residual band with the default's XGBoost quantiles, the recipe used for the metered solar farms (z5; experiments 270, 287, and 300). All scores are in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a farm's capacity). Terms: W1 to W3 are the three metered wind farms, whose names are withheld. The forecast 99th percentile, q99, should lie below 99% of observations. The pinball loss at a quantile is the standard score of that quantile. The "kept" half-hours are those that survive experiment 210's mask of idle or unreliable periods. The "scale" is each farm's fitted maximum output in the plant model. "True days 1 to 10" means lead hours 24 to 240, on the 53 Tuesday runs of fold_a_tuesdays_v1, kept half-hours, scored at true days 1 to 10 (lead 24 to 240 hours).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. Base is experiment 347's y2 (Stage 3 plant, summary of the 51 member powers, head with three Gaussian components). z1 to z4 as in the plan. The reference y2p is y2 trained with the pinball loss, weights 1. z5 works on stored quantiles: the plant's residual band in six equal-count bins of the plant's mean forecast and four lead bands, blended per quantile and lead band with weights chosen on earlier scored months. Wind farms research default 1 is XGBoost plus experiment 259's offset table (the research-default log has no wind version yet, so this page uses the name experiments 259, 339, and 347 gave it). Code reuse: experiments 230, 303, 310, 326, 336, and 347. - Headline, true days 1 to 10 (kept rows, default 10.752). y2 10.518 (-0.234; 99.8% interval -0.512 to +0.056); y2p 10.507 (-0.245); z1 10.527 (-0.225; -0.496 to +0.060); z2 10.508 (-0.244; -0.523 to +0.059); z3 10.514 (-0.238; -0.501 to +0.048); z4 10.507 (-0.245; -0.516 to +0.048); z5 10.605 (-0.147; -0.274 to -0.059). Days 1 to 2: head arms -0.05 to -0.07, z5 -0.172. Days 3 to 10: head arms -0.28 to -0.31, z5 -0.158. Every head arm is within 0.011 of y2, and every head arm is within 0.02 of y2p (z1 is the furthest, 0.020 worse). - Reference rows (true days 1 to 10). XGBoost alone 11.102; XGBoost with the adapter column 10.639; experiment 324's head 10.523; climatology 13.860. Seed sd of the head arms on kept rows is 0.011 to 0.044. - Standard architecture (physics plant + mixture head). The best head arm (z4, 10.507) sits 0.016 points (0.1%) below the best other family row (experiment 324's W4, 10.523) and 0.245 points (2.3%) below the default. - Replicate (heads trained on 2024-04 to 2024-11, scored on the daily runs of 2025-01 to 2025-06, default 9.728): y2 -0.376; y2p -0.354; z1 -0.343; z2 -0.356; z3 -0.329; z4 -0.331; z5 -0.209 (95% -0.371 to -0.070; t test on six monthly differences p = 0.028). All have the same sign.
Arm (true days 1 to 10) Below q01 (%) Above q95 (%) Above q99 (%) p01 p95 p99 5 to 95 coverage (%) default 0.55 6.62 1.66 0.285 2.415 0.603 92.0 y2 0.81 6.69 2.15 0.283 2.382 0.626 88.9 z1 0.52 6.43 1.95 0.283 2.384 0.613 90.8 z2 0.62 6.43 1.11 0.283 2.387 0.756 89.9 z3 0.53 6.68 2.21 0.283 2.393 0.620 90.5 z4 0.63 6.48 1.11 0.283 2.388 0.756 90.0 z5 0.68 6.62 1.79 0.287 2.407 0.602 90.8 z5a (plant + offsets) 0.63 6.32 1.59 0.285 2.419 0.610 89.9 z5b (plant + residual band) 1.02 7.18 2.32 0.295 2.543 0.650 89.0 y2p 0.58 6.38 1.93 0.283 2.377 0.612 90.3
  • Tails. z2 and z4 put q99 on the farm's scale for almost every row (figure 3), so their 1.1% above q99 is the share of observations above the scale. The pinball loss gives the point mass's weight no gradient at levels above 1 minus that weight. The head therefore cannot learn to lower the weight. By farm, the share above q99 is 0.69%, 2.57%, and 0.04% for W1, W2, and W3 (W2's scale is below capacity).
  • Controls. The reproduction gate holds (y2 refit 11.081 against 11.081 on all leads, kept rows). A base-only head (plant median, lead, farm) reproduces 71% (y2), 74% (y2p), 75% (z1), 66% (z2), 77% (z3), and 75% (z4) of each arm's gain. The shuffled-summary placebo scores 5.6 to 5.8 points worse than the default. The plant is frozen and the head sees ensemble weather only.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per farm (true days 1 to 10) is -3.3 to -4.5 points for the default and -3.0 to -4.1 for every arm, so every arm's median stays 3.0 to 4.1 points below its mean, close to the default's. The mean-forecast squared error and the median absolute error move in the same direction as the quantile score for every arm. No audit trigger fired: the head arms' failed predictions (below) are explained in the tails bullet, no control failed, and no sister experiment has an interval to compare with.
  • Pre-registered predictions.
    • z4 brings the share above q99 under 1.5% (holds, 1.11%) and the 0.99 pinball loss within 0.03 of the default's (fails, 0.153 above), so the joint prediction fails.
    • z2 does most at W1 and W2 and less at W3: fails (by share above q99, W2 is worst at 2.57% and W3 best at 0.04%).
    • z1 lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by under 0.03 (holds, 0.013 against y2) and raises the quantile score by under 0.03 (holds, 0.009).
    • The headline stays within 0.05 of y2's for every arm (holds), and the base-only head reproduces at least 70% of the gain (holds for y2, y2p, z1, z3, and z4; fails for z2).
    • z5 lowers the 0.99 pinball loss by 10% (fails, 0.2%), puts the share above q99 under 1.5% (fails, 1.79%), and is within 0.1 of z4 on the headline (holds, 0.098).
  • Adoption (order z4, z5, z3, z2, z1). No head arm passes condition 1 (every 99.8% interval includes zero), and z2 and z4 also fail condition 2 (0.99 pinball loss harm up to 0.212). z5 passes conditions 1 to 4 (gain 0.147, harm to p01 and p99 at most 0.013, replicate -0.209), The replicate of z5 was added after the main scores were read, because the plan said that the default's replicate forecasts did not exist, and they do. Therefore z5 stays a candidate, and nothing is adopted.
  • Serving. z1 to z4 need what y2 needs: the plant run on each member, then the head. z5 needs the plant, a stored table of offsets by bin, and the default's XGBoost quantiles.
  • Curtailment metric. Not scored: studies.node_curtailment needs a node's export and its generators' forecasts together, and this experiment forecasts the three farms alone.
  • Caveats. Scored at true days 1 to 10 only; three farms and 53 runs give wide intervals. z5's blend weights for the first runs of a month use actuals of the earlier month that were not yet observed at those runs' issue times, a small look-ahead. z5 fits on earlier scored months. Each head was fitted once on the hindcast and never refitted. Whether refitting changes the contrast was not tested.
  • What to try next. (1) Fit the point mass's weight with a likelihood or a classification loss on saturated half-hours, then retest z2. (2) Apply the solar recipe to the head's own quantiles (plant plus head, then band, then blend), a tier 1 step. (3) Repeat z5 with a pre-registered replicate before any adoption.

docs.title: Does replacing the pinned solar capacity with the experiment 269 estimate improve Primary demand research default 3 on sunny daylight half-hours?
Take-home message
docs.text:
Replacing the pinned solar capacity with the capacity estimate of experiment 269 did not lower the score on sunny half-hours, and no group improved by more than 0.011 points. The research forecast of demand at six Primary substations (anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) subtracts the output of unmetered rooftop solar from each substation's demand. The size of that solar (its capacity) is pinned to the values of experiment 45. Experiment 269 found that a table learned from six metered solar farms recovers 0.89 to 0.97 of the output of an injected farm, where the physical fleet shape recovers 0.78 to 0.83.

We asked whether a capacity read that way gives a better forecast. We refitted the first stage of the forecast (a convex demand model with a Kalman filter, from experiment 139) with the pinned capacity swapped for the new estimate, which was refitted each month on earlier rows only.

Scores are quantile scores in points of the substation's effective capacity, smaller is better. On the sunniest third of daylight half-hours (the third of each Primary's daylight half-hours with the highest solar output per unit of capacity), the score rose from 4.371 to 4.418, a change of +0.047 points (95% interval from resampling whole months, -0.029 to +0.135). A positive change means a worse score. The interval includes zero, so the data cannot tell. Verdict: inconclusive. The pre-registered rule asks for an interval wholly below zero, which the score did not reach.

The later stages of Primary demand research default 3 (the neural-network head, the solar summary, and the blend with the manual heuristic) and the 168 to 240 hour range were not rerun. The first stage showed no gain to carry into those stages. A gain after the first stage cannot be ruled out.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and what was refitted. The experiment changes the solar capacity inside the fitted stage and imports the default's code (a tier 2 change), and adds a plant-response table and a capacity fit per month. Arm A is the first stage with the pin (experiment 45's frozen vintage). Arm B replaces the capacity with the experiment 269 estimate, refitted at each of 27 monthly origins (2024-04 to 2026-06) on rows before the origin. Arm C holds arm B's value at the 2025-07-01 origin for the whole scored year. The stack's own unit solar shape is unchanged.
  • How the estimate is scaled. A fit to the real series reads too little of a solar farm's output. Each fit is therefore divided by the median recovery of five farms injected at that origin into the same Primary's demand, each read with the shape of the other five farms.
  • Row set and range. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, six Primaries, rows outside the hand-filtered events, forecast origin 09:00 UTC, lead 0.5 to 168 hours and 24 to 168 hours. The 168 to 240 hour range needs the experiment 317 chain, which was not rerun, so the result covers 7 of the 10 forecast days that NGED (the distribution network operator) cares about.
  • Headline, sunniest third of daylight half-hours (B minus A, scored year). At 0.5 to 168 hours: +0.047 (-0.029 to +0.135). At 24 to 168 hours: +0.044 (-0.037 to +0.133). Error of the mean forecast on the same rows, 0.5 to 168 hours: +0.120 (-0.002 to +0.277).
  • Absolute scores, sunniest third, 0.5 to 168 hours: A 4.371, B 4.418, C 4.448 (24 to 168 hours: 4.511, 4.555, 4.583). All half-hours: A 2.773, B 2.777, C 2.784. C minus A is +0.077 (-0.012 to +0.158) and C minus B is +0.030 (-0.004 to +0.076).
  • Replicate year (2024-07 to 2025-06), sunniest third, B minus A. At 0.5 to 168 hours +0.040 (-0.004 to +0.084). At 24 to 168 hours +0.044 (+0.004 to +0.085), an interval wholly above zero. Error of the mean forecast +0.106 (+0.006 to +0.187) at 0.5 to 168 hours. Both years point the same way, and the replicate year's 24 to 168 hour interval excludes zero. Arms B and C are identical in the replicate year, because both read the 2025-07-01 origin or an earlier one.
  • The other groups, B minus A at 0.5 to 168 hours: no group other than the sunniest third moved by more than 0.011 points, as the table shows.
Group Change in score 95% interval All half-hours +0.004 -0.006 to +0.012 All daylight +0.001 -0.020 to +0.020 Darkest third of daylight -0.011 -0.025 to +0.006 Night +0.006 -0.001 to +0.015 Winter nights (December to February, after dark) -0.007 -0.010 to 0.000
  • By Primary, sunniest third, B minus A (checks.log): D5 -0.023, D10 +0.155, D11 +0.037, D14 -0.046, D9 -0.063, D16 +0.218. Leaving one Primary out gives +0.013 (without D16) to +0.070 (without D9), so the sign holds. On all half-hours, leaving out D16 gives -0.006 (-0.014 to 0.000) against +0.004 with it, so D16 carries the all-half-hours result.
  • Capacities (figure 3; ratios of the estimate to the pin for the latest season-year). At the start of the scored year (2025-07-01) the estimate is 28% below the pin at D16 (30.9 against 43.2 points of effective capacity), 15% below at D9, and 17% above at D14. By 2026-06 the pin has risen above the estimate at D11 (0.79), D14 (0.83), and D16 (0.74), and the estimate is 8 to 10% below at D5 and D9. D10 matches the pin (1.00). D9's first monthly folds keep the pin, because D9 has too little history for an estimate there (1,513 path weeks took the pin in the fit log, about four folds).
  • Tails, six Primaries, 0.5 to 168 hours (A, B, C). Coverage below q01 is 2.20%, 2.17%, and 2.18%; below q05 6.68%, 6.67%, and 6.73%; below q95 94.74%, 94.68%, and 94.67%; below q99 98.35%, 98.30%, and 98.30%. Pinball loss at q01 is 0.215, 0.216, and 0.216; at q05 0.721, 0.725, and 0.727; at q95 0.720, 0.715, and 0.716; at q99 0.220, 0.220, and 0.220. No tail moves by more than 0.006 points.
  • Reference rows. The first stage alone is not Primary demand research default 3, so it is not placed against the manual heuristic or climatology. The research default's own scores (2.727 at 0.5 to 240 hours, against 3.414 for the manual heuristic and 3.664 for climatology) are in the research default log.
  • Model family. The experiment evaluates one model family and no blend.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Wiring gate. Arm A equals experiment 139's stored pin forecasts at all six Primaries (95,939 to 97,046 rows each, largest gap in q01, q50, and q99 0.0; logs/checks.log).
  • Median minus mean forecast, per Primary and arm: 0.0 points for all three arms.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast: it moves in the same direction as the quantile score on the sunniest third (+0.120) and on winter nights (-0.019).
  • Triggers. None fired. B's point estimate on the sunniest third (+0.047) is just outside the pre-registered band (within 0.03 points either way), but its interval covers the band and the predicted direction (no gain) held. Leaving one Primary out does not flip the sunniest-third sign.

docs.title: Caveats and lab shortcuts
docs.text:
• The plant-response table is not as-of. It is fitted once on the six farms' history to 2026-06-30, and the farms' scale (their 99th percentile of output) uses all daylight half-hours. Only the capacity fit, the pin, and the injection recoveries stop at each origin. The capacity is as-of; the shape it is read against is not.
  • The first stage only. The neural-network head, the solar summary, the blend, and the 168 to 240 hour range need the chain of experiments 155, 160, 164, 317, 319, and 322 refitted from the new forecasts.
  • Unit shape unchanged. The estimate is applied to the stack's physical unit shape, not to the empirical shape it was fitted with.
  • No scale factor. Experiment 139's post hoc factor of 1.15 was not repeated.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Apply the experiment 269 estimate with the empirical shape it was fitted with, in the first stage and in the ensemble's solar response.
  • Test a scale factor on the estimate.

docs.title: Can a learned curve of irradiance, with no PV capacity estimate, replace the pinned capacity times the unit solar shape in Primary demand research default 3?
docs.text:
Take-home: dropping the PV capacity estimate is not yet safe. A learned curve of irradiance does no better than the pinned capacity over five of the six Primaries (+0.025 points, interval -0.252 to +0.346). Only D5's interval excludes zero (-0.969), where either the pinned capacity or the unit solar shape is probably wrong. D11 is significantly worse with the curve (+0.223 [+0.100, +0.360]). The useful next step is to check the D5 pin and unit shape. A curve is also a low-effort fallback for a Primary with no trustworthy capacity. Verdict: not supported.

Definitions. PV capacity is the peak output of the solar panels behind a Primary, in points (1 point is 1% of the Primary's effective capacity). The pinned capacity is the capacity taken from the weekly vintages of experiment 45. Irradiance is the shortwave radiation reaching the ground, in W/m2. The Primaries are six NGED primary substations (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16, and D9). The gate is the reproduction check that must pass before any contrast is read. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. Recipe R is the fitted recipe that turns the Kalman filter's output into quantiles, and the spread table holds the fitted widths of those quantiles.

We asked whether the forecast of Primary demand can do without an estimate of how much solar generation each Primary has behind it. The current forecast subtracts a solar term from demand: the pinned capacity times a fixed unit solar shape. Experiments 110 and 139 had found that fitting the capacity from the Primary's own power did not help. We replaced the solar term with a curve of irradiance that the fit learns, once with one shape shared by all Primaries (arm B) and once with a shape per Primary (arm C), and compared both with the refitted pinned-capacity forecast (arm A). We scored sunny daylight half-hours, the half-hours where the sun is more than 5 degrees above the horizon and the ensemble-mean shortwave is in the top quarter of the Primary's daylight half-hours. Both curves scored better than arm A on average (arm A 4.321 at 24 to 240 hours, smaller is better; 1 point is 1% of a Primary's effective capacity), but not reliably, and only one Primary, D5, has an interval that excludes zero.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. A: experiment 136's convex fit refitted with the pinned capacity times the temperature-derated unit shape. B: the solar term replaced by one monotone curve of irradiance (eight saturating ramps) with a learned scale per Primary, fitted on each cut's training window. C: B with a curve per Primary. The Kalman filter, offset, recipe R, and spread table are refitted for each arm. The neural-network head, the solar summary, and the heuristic blend are not refitted, because they bake in the old solar term. The experiment therefore compares only the convex stage. Monthly refits on a 24-month window. Reference rows: Primary demand research default 3 as stored, the manual heuristic, and climatology.
  • Row set. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, six Primaries, 798,116 half-hours scored 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30 (origin 09:00 UTC), 90,562 of them sunny daylight. Intervals resample calendar months of the forecast's issue time. The decision rule's 1 - 0.05/2 level gives 97.5% bounds in the results below, and the headline row quotes 95% bounds. The conclusion is the same at 95%: the upper bound at 24 to 240 hours is +0.163 for B and +0.092 for C, both above +0.05.
  • Gate. Arm A reproduces the stored convex stage of the chain of experiment 317 to within 0.000 (three decimals; largest quantile difference 0.000), so the gate passes. Arm A scores 0.118 worse than the stored research default 3 on all rows (2.845 against 2.727; interval +0.063 to +0.180) because the head, summary, and blend are not refitted. The stored default is read from experiments 322, 220, and 251.
  • Absolute scores, sunny daylight, 24 to 240 hours. A 4.321 [3.959, 4.707]; B 4.191 [3.918, 4.509]; C 4.122 [3.871, 4.409]; manual heuristic 4.749; climatology 4.834. All rows, 0.5 to 240 hours: A 2.845, B 2.838, C 2.829, stored default 3 2.727, manual heuristic 3.414, climatology 3.664.
  • Stored default 3 beats every arm. On sunny daylight 0.5 to 240 hours the stored default 3 scores 4.021 against A 4.236, B 4.128, and C 4.058. The contrasts below are taken against arm A, the convex stage, because the stored default includes the head, summary, and blend that were not refitted.
  • Headline, sunny daylight, B minus A (then C minus A). At 0.5 to 240 hours -0.108 [-0.407, +0.183] (-0.178 [-0.472, +0.112]); at 24 to 240 hours -0.131 [-0.446, +0.163] (-0.199 [-0.509, +0.092]). The simplicity case (97.5% upper bound under +0.05) fails for both arms at both ranges (upper bounds +0.215, +0.141, +0.190, +0.121), and the gain case (interval wholly below zero) fails too.
  • Leave-one-Primary-out criterion: failed. The decision rule requires that dropping one Primary at a time does not flip the sign of the headline contrast. Dropping D5 flips B minus A from -0.131 to +0.025 at 24 to 240 hours.
  • Predictions. P1 fails: the point estimates are better than the band's lower edge of -0.10 (B -0.108 and -0.131; C -0.178 and -0.199, nearly twice the lower edge), and the upper bounds exceed +0.05. P2 fails: C minus B is -0.070 [-0.111, -0.037] at 0.5 to 240 hours, so a shared shape is slightly too stiff. P3 holds: cold winter nights, q01 and q99 pinball, and the pooled score move by less than 0.03 (pooled B minus A -0.007 and C minus A -0.016 at 0.5 to 240 hours; cold winter nights -0.003 and -0.005). P4 holds. The one no-harm bound that breaks apart from the sunny row is B on all rows at 0.5 to 240 hours (upper bound +0.022 against 0.02).
  • Where the gain is. Only D5's interval excludes zero: B minus A -0.969 [-1.708, -0.176], C minus A -1.106 [-1.958, -0.174], at 24 to 240 hours. Over the other five Primaries together the contrast is +0.025 [-0.252, +0.346] (B) and -0.031 [-0.280, +0.254] (C). D9 has a point-estimate gain (B -0.329 [-0.883, +0.180]). D11 is significantly worse with the curve (B +0.223 [+0.100, +0.360]).
  • Replicate (even months of 2024-07 to 2025-06, sunny daylight): B minus A -0.108 [-0.261, +0.098] and C minus A -0.147 [-0.349, +0.070] at 0.5 to 240 hours; the same sign.
  • Curtailment metric. Not scored: the experiment forecasts six Primaries' demand with no generators beside them.

Tails, sunny daylight and all rows, lead 24 to 240 hours (coverage is the share of observations at or below the quantile; the target is the quantile's level):

Rows Arm q01 coverage q01 pinball q05 coverage q05 pinball q95 coverage q95 pinball q99 coverage q99 pinball sunny daylight A 0.0188 0.2510 0.0625 0.9472 0.9286 1.1071 0.9730 0.3124 sunny daylight B 0.0303 0.2532 0.0827 0.8996 0.9354 1.1099 0.9762 0.3035 sunny daylight C 0.0278 0.2449 0.0812 0.8774 0.9378 1.1071 0.9773 0.3025 all rows A 0.0246 0.2259 0.0692 0.7381 0.9468 0.7802 0.9807 0.2386 all rows B 0.0250 0.2213 0.0688 0.7227 0.9447 0.7840 0.9803 0.2387 all rows C 0.0246 0.2204 0.0685 0.7207 0.9451 0.7833 0.9805 0.2387
  • Tails. The q99 pinball changes little (0.3124, 0.3035, 0.3025 on sunny rows). Every arm covers the upper quantiles too little on sunny rows: q95 coverage is 0.929 to 0.938 against 0.95, and q99 coverage is 0.973 to 0.977 against 0.99. On sunny rows B and C move the lower tail the wrong way: the share below q01 rises from 0.019 to 0.030 and 0.028, and the share below q05 from 0.063 to 0.083 and 0.081, although the q05 pinball loss falls.
  • Fitted curves (figure 4, last cut 2026-06-01). At 1000 W/m2 arm B subtracts 64.8 points at D5 against a pinned capacity of 70.2, and 29.6 to 43.9 points at the others against pins of 41.5 to 57.2.
  • Check: median against mean. The median forecast minus the mean forecast is 0.0000 at every Primary for every arm.
  • Check: error of the mean forecast. The error of the mean forecast points the same way as the quantile score (sunny daylight, 24 to 240 hours: B minus A -0.284 [-0.860, +0.294], C minus A -0.417 [-1.005, +0.179]), so the mean-forecast-error trigger (trigger 3) did not fire.
  • Check: audit triggers. The leave-one-Primary-out trigger (trigger 4) fired: leaving D5 out flips the sign of B minus A, from -0.131 to +0.025 at 24 to 240 hours. The failed-predictions trigger (trigger 2) fired because P1 and P2 failed; the audit tested the explanation, a gain confined to D5, with the leave-one-out row. The nesting trigger (trigger 5) did not fire, because B is nested in C and loses to it. Triggers 1, 6, and 7 were not assessed from the printed report.
  • Audit. A Sonnet agent ran the audit. The report is private (data/ml-experiments/briefs/e350_audit_report.md). The audit re-derived the numbers from the stored predictions and found no lookahead. Triage of its findings:
    1. The gain is D5's and comes from the median, not the spread. Recentring A's quantiles on B's median takes A's D5 score from 5.678 to 4.825 (B's is 4.710), and giving B A's median raises B's score to 5.771. This page reports the finding.
    2. The gain varies by month. B minus A runs from +0.49 (March; +0.88 in February on 47 rows) to -0.80 (May), and the pooled figure has nine months with sunny rows, so figure 3 shows it.
    3. The headline interval is the most conservative of the block choices: day blocks give [-0.23, -0.04] and ISO-week blocks [-0.33, +0.04]. This page uses the month blocks that the plan specified.
    4. Under other sunny definitions (top decile -0.246, top tercile -0.095, clear-sky index -0.019) the sign stays and the size varies.
    5. B turns A's small positive bias into -0.6 to -0.9 points at D10 and D16, a new bias.
  • Caveats. The head, summary, and heuristic blend were not refitted, so the stack-level effect is unknown. The D5 forecast error does not isolate a cause: A's D5 bias (actual minus median) is -2.5 at 300 to 430 W/m2 (forecast too high) and +5.9 above 550 W/m2 (forecast too low), so a level error alone would not explain it, and either the pinned capacity or the unit shape is wrong. The experiment covers one scored year, nine months with sunny rows (October has 25 rows and February 47), and six Primaries. The cut schedule is monthly refits, which may matter little for a contrast of this size but was not tested.
  • What to try next. (1) Fix or re-estimate the D5 pin and unit shape and rerun arm A against B and C; if D5's gain vanishes the curve has nothing left to offer there. (2) Use arm B's curve as a sanity check on each Primary's pin, and as a fallback where a Primary has no trustworthy capacity. (3) If a capacity-free solar term is wanted for a stack-level port, refit the head, summary, and blend with it first.

docs.title: Does reading the solar capacity out in the stack's own physical unit shape, monthly and as-of each origin, improve Primary demand research default 3 on sunny daylight half-hours?
Take-home message
docs.text:
Estimating the solar capacity with the clear-sky output curve that the forecast already uses made the forecast slightly worse on sunny half-hours, so mixing two curves is not why experiment 349 did not improve the forecast. The experimental forecast of demand at six Primary substations (anonymised as D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) subtracts the output of unmetered rooftop solar from each substation's demand. The solar capacity is fixed per substation at the values of experiment 45, which we call the pinned capacity. Experiment 349 estimated the capacity from the average daily output curve of six metered solar farms (experiment 269). It then multiplied that capacity by the forecast's own clear-sky output curve (the physical unit shape), which is a different curve. The write-up of experiment 349 lists this as a shortcut that could explain why it did not improve the forecast.

We asked whether estimating the capacity with the physical unit shape, the curve the forecast later multiplies it by, gives a better forecast. We refitted the first stage of the forecast (a demand model fitted by convex optimisation, with a Kalman filter; see experiment 139) at the start of every month (the forecast origin), using only rows before the origin. Each estimate was divided by a recovery ratio: the median fraction of the output of five metered solar farms that the same fit recovered when that output was added to the demand data on purpose (0.74 to 0.86 at the 2025-07-01 origin).

Arm A is the pinned capacity, arm B is experiment 349's estimate, and arm P is the physical-shape estimate. Scores are quantile scores in points of the substation's effective capacity. Smaller scores are better, so a positive change is worse. On the sunniest third of daylight half-hours (the third of each Primary's daylight half-hours with the highest solar output per unit of capacity), arm P scored 4.436 against 4.371 for arm A, a change of +0.065 (95% interval from resampling whole months, +0.017 to +0.126). The pre-registered rule (an interval wholly above zero) gives refuted. A Sonnet audit reproduced the numbers but found that the interval includes zero when D16 or D10 is left out, so the verdict is softened to not supported: no gain, and probably slightly worse, with D16 and D10 carrying the harm. The first stage only was refitted, so the later stages of the forecast and the 168 to 240 hour range are untested.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. This is a tier 2 change: the capacity is read inside the fitted stage, with the default's code imported from the experiment folders that hold it. A is the pinned capacity (experiment 45's frozen vintage). B is experiment 349's arm B, refitted here from its stored as-of table. P is the monthly as-of read-out in the physical unit shape, divided by its own injection recovery (a table of 27 monthly origins, 2024-04 to 2026-06, at five Primaries and 24 at D9). R is P without the divisor. Arm P2, a read-out on the stack's own residual solar signal, was skipped because that signal exists only after the later stages are refitted.
  • Code reused. ml-experiments/00351-primary-demand-capacity-physical-shape-readout/ copies the scripts of experiment 349 and drops the empirical shape from the table builder (e00351_asof_table.py); it reads experiment 349's private as-of table for arm B.
  • Row set and range. fold_a_daily_gap_v1, scored year 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30, six Primaries, rows outside the hand-filtered events, origin 09:00 UTC, lead 0.5 to 168 hours and 24 to 168 hours. The 168 to 240 hour range was not rerun, so the result covers 7 of the 10 forecast days that NGED (the distribution network operator) cares about.
  • Schedule. Monthly refits of the first stage on a 24-month window, as in experiment 349. The contrast could depend on the schedule only through the capacity path, which changes monthly.
  • Reproduction gate. Arm A equals experiment 139's stored pin forecasts at all six Primaries (largest gap in q01, q50, and q99 0.0). Arms A and B reproduce experiment 349's stored scores on the sunniest third (4.371 and 4.418) and on all half-hours (2.773 and 2.777).
  • Headline, sunniest third (scored year, 0.5 to 168 hours). C1, P minus A: +0.065 (+0.017 to +0.126). C2, P minus B: +0.018 (-0.020 to +0.054). C3, R minus A: +0.048 (-0.077 to +0.173). B minus A: +0.047 (-0.029 to +0.135). At 24 to 168 hours C1 is +0.068 (+0.018 to +0.131), C2 is +0.025 (-0.014 to +0.063), and C3 is +0.035 (-0.099 to +0.160). Error of the mean forecast, P minus A, 0.5 to 168 hours: +0.142 (+0.070 to +0.249).
  • Absolute scores, 0.5 to 168 hours (A, B, P, R). Sunniest third 4.371, 4.418, 4.436, 4.419. All half-hours 2.773, 2.777, 2.775, 2.790. At 24 to 168 hours the sunniest third scores 4.511, 4.555, 4.580, 4.546.
  • Replicate year (2024-07 to 2025-06), P minus A. Sunniest third +0.066 (+0.016 to +0.088) at 0.5 to 168 hours and +0.073 (+0.018 to +0.099) at 24 to 168 hours, so both years point the same way. P minus B is +0.026 (-0.039 to +0.071).
  • The other groups, P minus A at 0.5 to 168 hours. Improvements (negative changes) of more than 0.01 points: cold winter nights (December to February, after dark) -0.015 (-0.019 to -0.007) and the darkest third of daylight -0.041 (-0.064 to -0.019). No change beyond 0.01 points in all half-hours (+0.002), night (0.000), or all daylight (+0.006).
  • By Primary, sunniest third, P minus A. D5 +0.033, D10 +0.182, D11 +0.029, D14 -0.056, D16 +0.213, D9 -0.009. Leaving one Primary out gives +0.036 (-0.006 to +0.091) without D16, +0.041 (-0.016 to +0.111) without D10, +0.071 (+0.040 to +0.113) without D5, +0.073 without D11, +0.081 without D9, and +0.090 without D14.
  • Capacities (figure 3, the capacity each fit applies, in points of effective capacity). At the 2025-07-01 origin P exceeds the pin by 10% at D5, 10% at D10, 12% at D11, and 26% at D14, and is below it by 24% at D16 and 7% at D9; B differs from the pin by under 3% at D10, D11, and D5 and by -29% at D16. Over the origins (27, and 24 at D9), P differs from the pin by more than 10% in 18 (D10), 18 (D11), 20 (D14), 23 (D16), 8 (D5), and 1 (D9) origins. P differs from B by more than 10% in 20 (D10), 27 (D11), 2 (D14), 4 (D16), 1 (D5), and 8 (D9) origins; P is above B at every Primary. The divisor (0.74 to 0.86) scales a capacity that is already in the physical shape's units.
  • Tails, six Primaries, 0.5 to 168 hours (A, B, P, R). Coverage below q01 is 2.20%, 2.17%, 2.12%, and 2.19%; below q05 6.68%, 6.67%, 6.61%, and 6.70%; below q95 94.74%, 94.68%, 94.71%, and 94.65%; below q99 98.35%, 98.30%, 98.34%, and 98.26%. Pinball loss at q01 is 0.215, 0.216, 0.216, and 0.215; at q05 0.721, 0.725, 0.727, and 0.725; at q95 0.720, 0.715, 0.716, and 0.716; at q99 0.220, 0.220, 0.220, and 0.219. No tail moves by more than 0.006 points.
  • Reference rows. The first stage alone is not Primary demand research default 3, so the manual heuristic and climatology are not placed beside it. The research default's own scores (2.727 at 0.5 to 240 hours, against 3.414 for the manual heuristic and 3.664 for climatology) are in the research default log.
  • Model family. One model family and no blend.
  • Prediction scorecard. Predicted P minus A within -0.03 to +0.05: missed (+0.065). P minus B within plus or minus 0.03: held (+0.018). R minus A within 0.03: missed (+0.048). Cold winter nights and tails within 0.02: the winter-night change is -0.015 and the tails hold.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary and arm: 0.0 points for all four arms.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast: P minus A on the sunniest third is +0.142 (+0.070 to +0.249), the same direction as the quantile score. On cold winter nights the mean-forecast error moves the same way as the quantile score (-0.037, -0.050 to -0.015).
  • Triggers. Audit trigger 4 (leaving one Primary out changes a verdict) fired: leaving out D16 or D10 turns the verdict of C1 from refuted into inconclusive (+0.036, -0.006 to +0.091; +0.041, -0.016 to +0.111), although the sign holds. Audit trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction) is borderline: C1 misses its predicted bound by 0.015 points. One explanation was tested: P sits 5 to 13% above B, and arm R, which has no divisor, is nearer to the pin but has a wide interval. The explanation is not confirmed.
  • Audit (Sonnet, as the manager directed). An independent re-derivation from the stored forecasts, with its own scoring and bootstrap code, reproduced every figure above to three decimals (interval ends differ in the third decimal because of resampling). Leaving out both D16 and D10 gives -0.001 (-0.044 to +0.059). In the replicate year, leaving out D16 gives +0.036 (-0.032 to +0.067). D16 is worse in 10 of 12 months and D10 in 11 of 12, so the harm is not from a few months, although the 10 worst days carry 41% of D16's total and 32% of D10's. The audit found no row-alignment or quantile-score flaw. The verdict is therefore not supported: no gain, and probably slightly worse, with the harm carried by D16 and D10.

docs.title: Caveats and simplifications
docs.text:
• The plant-response table of arm B is not as-of. Arm B reads experiment 349's table, which was fitted once to the six farms' history to 2026-06-30. Arm P uses no plant-response table: only the capacity fit and its injection recoveries are used, both with rows before each origin.
  • The first stage only. The neural-network head, the solar summary, the blend, and the 168 to 240 hour range were not rerun.
  • Divisor choice. P divides by the injection recovery, which makes its capacity larger than the physical-shape units imply; R is the unit-consistent version, with a wide interval.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the capacity's effect on cold winter nights and the darkest daylight third, where P scored better than the pin, in the full stack.
  • Read the capacity out in the empirical shape and apply it in the empirical shape, in the first stage and in the ensemble's solar response, if the mismatch is still suspected.

docs.title: How much does the score of Primary demand research default 3 on sunny half-hours depend on the solar capacity it is given, with and without the Kalman filter?
Take-home message
docs.text:
The sunny-half-hour score of the demand forecast moved by only 0.010 points (interval -0.104 to +0.088) when the assumed solar capacity was 20% too low, but rose by 0.124 points when it was 20% too high, and the Kalman filter halves that rise. The forecast of demand at six Primary substations (anonymised D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) subtracts the output of unmetered rooftop solar from each substation's demand, and the size of that solar (its capacity) is fixed to the weekly capacity estimates of experiment 45, which this page calls the pin. Experiment 349 and experiment 350 found no reliable gain from a different capacity. We asked how much the score depends on the capacity at all.

We refitted the first stage of Primary demand research default 3 (a convex demand model, with a Kalman filter that corrects the forecast using the latest readings; the later stages add a neural-network head, a summary of the solar term, and a blend with a manual heuristic) five times, with the pinned capacity multiplied by 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, and 1.4, and forecast each with and without the filter. The arm at scale 1.0 with the filter (arm A of experiment 349) reproduces experiment 349's stored default exactly. On the sunniest third of each substation's daylight half-hours, with the filter, the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of the substation's effective capacity, smaller is better) is 4.361 at 0.8, 4.371 at 1.0, and 4.495 at 1.2. Verdict: partly supported (one of the two predictions held). We predicted that, with the filter, the sunny score would differ by under 0.1 points between any two scales from 0.8 to 1.2 (largest minus smallest). That failed: the difference was 0.134 (95% interval 0.054 to 0.321). We also predicted a difference of over 0.3 without the filter. That held: 0.367 (0.129 to 0.614). The curve is flat from 0.8 to 1.0 times the pin and rises above 1.0. The later stages of the stack (neural-network head, solar summary, blend) and the 168 to 240 hour range were not refitted.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 2: with the filter, the sunny score is flat from 0.8 to 1.0 and rises above 1.0.

Figure 3: D5 and D9 prefer a lower capacity and the other four Primaries prefer the pin.

Figure 4: on all half-hours the filter helps and the pin is the best of the five scales.

Figure 1a: experiment 349's loss came from D16 and D10 at every lead band.

Figure 1b: the loss concentrates in January to March at D5 and D16.
