The stack alone scores 2.86, 3.04, 2.59 at the signed-MW six and 3.49, 3.29, 3.07 at the MVA-only seven (without D8, which has no fold before 2025-08) in April, May, and June 2025, against 3.09, 3.26, 2.85 at the signed-MW six a year later. The MVA-only figures a year later include D8 (5.05, 4.00, 3.86) and are not comparable. The reference files hold only the 292 daily_gap runs, so no replicate reference exists.
  • Overlay C: default 3's stored forecasts, days 8 to 10 only. Experiment 322 stored default 3's quantiles at 168 to 240 hours at the signed-MW six, on its older folds (one fit, not monthly folds). On the 245,463 half-hours that both hold, pooled over the six: default 3 scores 3.276, the stack without S 3.335, and BG2 3.358. Beyond 240 hours and at the other ten Primaries default 3 is not fitted. The comparison crosses a change of training regime, so the 0.06 gap is descriptive.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control gate. Not a row-for-row reproduction, because experiments 374 and 376 stored one fixed fit with one tuning month and no monthly folds. On the headline contrasts, the signed-MW stack minus BG2 in experiment 376 was -0.02 (-0.17 to +0.13, 0.5 to 168 h) against -0.07 here, a difference of 0.05, which is at the limit; the MVA-only gap there was +0.57 (naive fit, 95%) against +0.34 here, which is not within 0.05. Most of the difference comes from D8: here the D8 row is the own-residual arm, and the D8 gap to BG2 is +1.61 against +3.77 in 376.
  • Median against mean forecast. The median minus the mean is 0.00 at every Primary: the stored mean is the corrected mean around which stage 2 centres the quantiles, so the median equals it by construction and no independent mean-forecast contrast exists.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired (P5 failed and the cause is untested). Trigger 7 applies, because the experiment 378 session builds on the stored stage-2 forecasts. Trigger 1 fired in part (the control gate above is not within 0.05 at the MVA-only eight, with the cause given). Triggers 3 (the mean equals the median), 4 (no leave-one-out sign flip), 5, and 6 (no sister experiment at demand-v1) did not fire. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the headline contrasts by its own code from the stored forecasts and reproduced them (signed-MW -0.068, MVA-only +0.344, +0.178 without D8, D8 +1.613). It found no unit error and no lookahead in the stage-2 spread. It found that 55 to 92 rows at D8 and D9 store a missing reading as zero in the stage-2 inputs (under 0.05% of rows, scoring unaffected); this was not fixed.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries. The naive fit of experiment 374 is used at all eight; the rule-chosen fit through the meter at D12 was not run.
  • The stack has no solar summary S below 168 hours, so the stack is not default 1 as the research default log defines it, and the sunny-half-hour gap may be an effect of that absence.
  • The tier-1 daylight blend of experiment 322 (D1) was not tried: its weights are fitted per fold from trailing rows in experiments 317, 319, and 322 and tied to their six-Primary chain.
  • The load-shift detector arm (default 1 with a detector, without, and with the hand labels as an oracle) was not run in this experiment; the load-shift detector arm is a separate follow-up.
  • Missing readings at D8 and D9 enter stage 2 as zeros in under 0.05% of rows (see Checks).
  • Days 11 to 14 are beyond NGED's 1 to 10 day horizon and are descriptive only.
  • The protocol page says D15 and D18 are scored from earlier months than the code allows: with the 12-month rule D18 is first scorable in 2026-01 and D15 in 2026-03.
  • D15 has no pool rows in experiment 103, so a local feature mask supplies its training rows, and its ensemble arrays were built from the production archive read-only (the same extraction as experiment 152, checked against D10's stored arrays with a maximum difference of 0).

docs.title: Primary demand research default 3, ported to all 16 Primaries, scored against BG2 under demand-v1
docs.text:
Default 3 scores level with BG2 at the six Primaries that report signed megawatts, and trails BG2 at the eight that report only apparent power, almost all of that at Marsh Lane (D8). Default 3 is our research demand forecast for a Primary, a 33 kV to 11 kV substation (labelled D2 to D22 here). BG2 is the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, which production does not run. The next paragraph defines the other terms.

Terms.

  • Default 1 and default 3. Default 1 is the generalised additive model (GAM) stack of experiment 377, with the two-number solar summary S added below 168 hours. S summarises the solar response of the 51 ensemble weather members as a mean and a standard deviation. Default 3 is default 1 with S also at 168 to 240 hours, and with a blend towards the manual heuristic's median on daylight half-hours (sun above 5 degrees) at 168 to 240 hours. The "stack without S" is experiment 377's forecast as stored, with S at no lead.
  • Score. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles. It equals the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) up to the error from using 11 quantiles. Scores are in points of effective capacity (percent of a Primary's capacity). A difference below zero favours the first-named forecast. twCRPS is the threshold-weighted CRPS of the protocol, which weights the high-demand tail. The 1%, 5%, 95%, and 99% quantiles are written q01, q05, q95, and q99, and their coverage is the share of readings at or below the quantile.
  • Signed-MW and MVA-only. Signed-MW Primaries report real power in megawatts (MW), with its sign. MVA-only Primaries report apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA), so every result there assumes reactive power is zero. They use the naive fit of experiment 377 (the fit that treats the meter reading as real power), not the rule-chosen fit of experiment 374 (a fit through the meter, chosen by a rule per Primary).
  • D8 spread. D8 has less than 12 months of history, so its forecast spread comes from the residuals of six other Primaries ("donor spread"); experiment 377 also fitted a spread from D8's own past errors ("own-residual spread").
  • Short history. D15 and D18 have under 12 months of history before the scored year, so they are report only and enter no tally.

Signed-MW six: supported. Default 3 minus BG2 at days 1 to 10, pooled over the six, is -0.12 (99% interval -0.31 to +0.06, 20,000 resamples of whole months). The registered margin was an upper end below +0.20, and +0.06 is below it. Days 8 to 10 (168 to 240 hours; BG2 is stored out to 351 hours) give -0.14 (-0.33 to +0.01). Default 3 minus default 1 is -0.03 (-0.06 to -0.02) at days 1 to 10 and -0.12 (-0.19 to -0.05) at days 8 to 10.

MVA-only eight: partly supported. Default 3 minus BG2 is +0.63 (+0.35 to +0.94) with D8 and +0.16 (-0.02 to +0.35) without. The registered prediction (+0.30 to +0.90 with D8; -0.05 to +0.25 without) holds on both ranges. D8 alone is +3.97 (95% interval +2.29 to +5.81). D8 uses the donor spread in every arm here; with its own-residual spread, experiment 377 found +1.61 for the stack without S. Default 3 minus default 1 is -0.02 (-0.05 to -0.004) with D8 and -0.02 (-0.04 to -0.01) without. At days 8 to 10 it is -0.08 with D8 (-0.16 to -0.01), inside the registered range of -0.20 to 0.

D15 and D18 (short history, report only). Default 3 minus BG2, pooled over half-hours, is -0.001 (-0.93 to +0.70) over 6 months at D18 and 4 months at D15. D15 scores worse than default 1 (+0.62, -0.20 to +1.32) because it takes the signed-MW fits of S and the blend, and its 4 months of scored history leave the interval wide.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Rows. Experiment 377's second-stage forecasts at all 16 Primaries on the demand-v1 folds, one fit per fold month on earlier months only. Experiment 378 adds S at 0.5 to 168 hours, and S and the blend at 168 to 240 hours (the band that days 8 to 10 cover).
  • Solar summary S. Each ensemble member's solar response is passed through the Primary's monthly fit of the solar term (experiment 184's code, run on experiment 377's setup; the gate on D5 matched experiment 184's stored values exactly). S is the mean and standard deviation of the 51 responses, with a scale and a spread factor fitted per lead band on the trailing 365 days of runs completed before the fold month.
  • Daylight blend. At 168 to 240 hours the median moves towards the manual heuristic's median with a weight fitted per lead band and season group on the same trailing rows. The blend applies only where the sun is above 5 degrees.
  • Fit groups. The fits are pooled within the signed-MW six and within the MVA-only seven without D8. D8 takes the MVA-only fits, and D15 and D18 take the signed-MW fits. The first fold month has no earlier rows, so S and the blend leave the forecast unchanged there.
  • Intervals. Pooled contrasts use 99% intervals (20,000 resamples), as registered. Per-Primary contrasts use 95% intervals (2,000 resamples) because a single Primary has few months to resample.

docs.title: Results (quantile score in points of effective capacity; lower is better)
docs.text:
• Absolute scores, days 1 to 10.
Primary Default 3 Default 1 BG2 Manual heuristic Climatology D5 3.99 4.04 3.94 4.35 4.48 D9 2.45 2.50 2.51 2.92 2.99 D10 3.21 3.25 3.45 4.16 4.31 D11 2.41 2.42 2.57 3.41 3.55 D14 2.18 2.20 2.39 3.01 3.47 D16 3.15 3.18 3.24 3.80 4.20 D2 2.46 2.47 2.30 2.86 2.93 D3 1.66 1.67 1.75 2.11 2.33 D4 2.43 2.45 2.51 2.80 2.83 D8 11.61 11.65 7.64 8.54 9.76 D12 7.47 7.52 6.75 7.92 8.83 D19 3.28 3.29 3.18 3.79 3.93 D21 2.34 2.35 2.38 2.77 2.91 D22 4.08 4.10 3.75 4.71 5.47 D15 13.67 13.05 13.35 22.59 46.20 D18 2.44 2.47 2.65 4.02 7.11
  • Per-Primary default 3 minus BG2 (95%, 2,000 resamples). The interval lies wholly below zero (default 3 is better) at D11 (-0.16), D14 (-0.21), and D18 (-0.21). It lies wholly above zero at D12 (+0.72), D22 (+0.33), and D8 (+3.97).
  • Primaries won, days 1 to 10 (the 14 Primaries with a full history). Against BG2, default 3 has the lower score at 8 and the higher at 6. Against the manual heuristic and against climatology, it has the lower score at 13 and the higher at 1 (D8). Against default 1 it has the lower score at all 14, and the interval lies wholly below zero at 10 of them.
  • Against the other references, pooled, days 1 to 10 (99%). Minus the manual heuristic: -0.71 (-1.06 to -0.39) signed-MW, -0.02 (-0.38 to +0.31) MVA-only with D8, -0.46 (-0.78 to -0.22) without D8. Minus climatology: -0.94 (-1.33 to -0.57), -0.46 (-0.91 to -0.09), -0.79 (-1.27 to -0.41).
  • Against the stack without S (99%). Default 3 minus the stack without S is -0.05 (-0.09 to -0.03) at the signed-MW six and -0.02 (-0.05 to -0.00) at the MVA-only eight at days 1 to 10, and -0.12 and -0.08 at days 8 to 10. These differ from the contrasts against default 1 (-0.03 and -0.02) because default 1 already carries S below 168 hours, which accounts for the extra 0.02 at the signed-MW six.
  • Leave one Primary out (95%). Default 3 minus BG2 at the signed-MW six stays between -0.10 and -0.15 whichever Primary is left out, with intervals that lie wholly below zero only when D5 or D9 is left out. The MVA-only gap stays between +0.62 and +0.74 whichever Primary but D8 is left out, and is +0.16 (+0.02 to +0.30) without D8. Default 3 minus default 1 is negative with an interval wholly below zero in every leave-one-out case in both groups.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrasts (99%). The mean absolute error of the median points the same way as CRPS in every row: default 3 minus BG2 -0.22 (-0.55 to +0.12) signed-MW, +0.41 (+0.01 to +0.80) MVA-only with D8; default 3 minus default 1 -0.04 (-0.09 to -0.01) and -0.04 (-0.07 to -0.01); minus the manual heuristic -1.28 and -0.72.
  • Tail calibration, days 1 to 10 (share of readings at or below each quantile, mean over the group; ideal 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, 0.99). Signed-MW default 3 0.018, 0.058, 0.947, 0.983; BG2 0.010, 0.045, 0.932, 0.975. MVA-only default 3 0.041, 0.097, 0.918, 0.965; BG2 0.005, 0.042, 0.955, 0.995. MVA-only without D8, default 3: 0.021, 0.070, 0.946, 0.985 (within 0.02 of nominal). D8 alone: 0.183, 0.291, 0.721, 0.826. D15 and D18: 0.034, 0.077, 0.867, 0.947. At the signed-MW six the 1% quantile is too high at D16 and D5: 0.036 and 0.032 of readings fall below it, against 0.01 ideal. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, q99 (default 3 against BG2, signed-MW): 0.245 against 0.222, 0.739 against 0.686, 0.793 against 0.882, 0.262 against 0.323. At the MVA-only eight the pinball loss at q05 is 1.27 against 0.86 for BG2, mostly D8 (4.36).
  • twCRPS, days 1 to 10, mean over the group (default 3, BG2). Signed-MW 0.324, 0.355; MVA-only 0.206, 0.195. Default 3 is better at the signed-MW six and worse at the MVA-only eight, the same split as the CRPS.
  • Replicate months. None: demand-v1 has no replicate period.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control gate. The port reproduces experiment 322's stored default 3 at 168 to 240 hours on experiment 319's own rows at the six Primaries: 3.07596 points against 3.07596 (difference 2e-10, largest single-quantile difference 1e-5), well inside the 0.05-point gate. The gate runs the same replay as the 16-Primary run, on experiment 322's rows and fold structure.
  • Median against mean forecast. The median minus the mean is 0.00 at every Primary: the stored mean is the corrected mean around which stage 2 centres the quantiles, so the median equals it by construction and no independent mean-forecast contrast exists. The error of the median is reported beside the CRPS contrasts above, and agrees in direction in every row.
  • Triggers (the seven audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill). The control gate passed (trigger 1). The registered predictions hold (trigger 2). The error of the median and the CRPS agree in direction (trigger 3). No leave-one-out case flips a sign (trigger 4). Trigger 5 (a nested arm beating the arm that contains it) did not fire. The pooled signed-MW interval is 0.37 wide against 0.42 in experiment 377 (trigger 6). Trigger 7 (a later experiment will use default 3 as its base) applies, and a fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored forecasts by its own code (-0.121, +0.634, +0.158, and -0.034 against default 1, all within 0.01), found no lookahead in the fits and no unit error, and confirmed that the median equals the mean in experiment 377's stage 2. It did not check the bootstrap intervals, the control gate, twCRPS, or the leave-one-out table; the control gate was checked by the gate script above.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries, and the naive fit of experiment 377 is used at all eight. The rule-chosen fit of experiment 374 at 240 hours was not run.
  • D8 uses the donor spread in every arm here, so its row differs from experiment 377's own-residual arm (+3.97 here against +1.61 for the stack without S against BG2). It is unproven whether a generator connected to D8 explains the steps and the gap at D8.
  • The fits of S and of the blend are pooled within a group, so a Primary whose behaviour differs from its group's, such as D15, gets a fit that suits it less.
  • The sunny-half-hour, Christmas, and load-shift slices of experiment 377 were not recomputed here.
  • Experiment 378 reads the second-stage forecasts of experiment 377 and its stored ensemble arrays, so an error there carries into every number above.

docs.title: What does each component of BG2 contribute at all 16 Primaries, out to 14 days, under demand-v1?
docs.text:
Take-home message: a plain weekly-refitted XGBoost model scores within 0.05 percentage points of capacity of BG2 at the six Primary substations whose meters record the direction of power flow, and within 0.02 points at the eight whose meters record apparent power only. BG2 is the five-model blend built in experiment 87, so the blend adds little over its weekly-refitted XGBoost member, and two of its five members add nothing measurable. BG2's upper tail is too narrow at the six signed-MW Primaries: 93.2% of outcomes fall below its 95% quantile, and 97.6% below its 99% quantile. The verdict is supported: no single blend member, the solar offset twins, or the spread factor changes the score by 0.10 points or more.

We asked how much each part of BG2 adds to its score. A Primary substation steps 33 kV or 66 kV down to 11 kV, and the 16 Primaries here carry anonymised labels (D2 to D22). BG2 blends five models: weekly-refitted XGBoost (W), monthly-refitted XGBoost (M), an analogue model (AN), an XGBoost model pooled across substations of the same type (PT), and a frozen XGBoost model with a 14-day error correction (ST). Each model's quantiles are widened about its median by a spread factor of 1.15. At 5 of the 16 Primaries, the models also have twins that include a forecast of embedded solar output (the solar offset twins). We rebuilt BG2 from experiment 87's stored forecasts with no refit, as experiment 360 did at four Primaries. We re-blended BG2 without each member, and scored each member alone. The scoring follows the demand-v1 protocol at all 16 Primaries, at every lead to 14 days. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), estimated from 11 quantiles, in percentage points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of a Primary's capacity; smaller is better). The protocol reports three groups separately. The six signed-MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) have meters that record the sign of the flow. The eight MVA-only Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22) have meters that record apparent power only, so their numbers assume reactive power is zero. D15 and D18 have short histories and are reported without counting in any verdict. The reference forecasts are manual_heuristic (NGED's rule of thumb) and climatology (the average for each month, half-hour, and weekend flag). Production does not run BG2.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are CRPS in percentage points of effective capacity for forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead, unless stated. They cover the 3,660,652 half-hours scored by every arm in July 2025 to June 2026. A negative difference in a drop-one contrast means the dropped part helps. Pooled intervals are 99% intervals from resampling whole calendar months of the forecast origin (20,000 resamples). Per-Primary and leave-one-out intervals are 95% intervals (2,000 resamples).

  • BG2 scores 3.016 at the signed-MW six and 3.788 at the MVA-only eight. Without D8, the MVA-only eight score 3.236, and D15 and D18 together score 7.285. At the signed-MW six, manual_heuristic scores 3.606 and climatology 3.831. At the MVA-only eight they score 4.438 and 4.872. BG2 beats manual_heuristic by 0.589 (0.398 to 0.819) at the signed-MW six and 0.650 (0.504 to 0.823) at the MVA-only eight, and beats climatology by 0.814 and 1.084.
  • The weekly XGBoost model alone trails BG2 by 0.044 (0.006 to 0.090) at the signed-MW six. It scores 3.061. At the MVA-only eight it trails by 0.018 (-0.013 to 0.056) and scores 3.807, and without D8 it trails by 0.025 (-0.006 to 0.063). The gap at the signed-MW six shrinks with lead: 0.080 on day 1, 0.034 on days 5 to 7, 0.019 on days 8 to 10, and 0.014 on days 11 to 14 (-0.024 to 0.066). The weekly XGBoost model alone is within 0.14 points of BG2 at 15 of 16 Primaries; D15 is the exception at +0.617 (0.219 to 1.049). It scores better than BG2 on the point estimate at D4, D5, D8, and D9, with intervals that include zero.
  • Dropping the frozen-stack member (ST) changes the signed-MW six's score most. Dropping ST changes the score by -0.061 (-0.094 to -0.030) at the signed-MW six and -0.010 (-0.039 to +0.025) at the MVA-only eight. Dropping W changes it by -0.037 (-0.067 to -0.012) and -0.031 (-0.065 to -0.003), and dropping AN by -0.031 (-0.052 to -0.011) and -0.023 (-0.035 to -0.013).
  • The monthly XGBoost and pooled-by-type members add nothing measurable. Dropping M changes the score by -0.001 (-0.004 to 0.000) at the signed-MW six and 0.000 at the MVA-only eight. Dropping PT changes it by +0.005 (0.000 to 0.019) and +0.002, so BG2 scores marginally better without PT. PT alone is the weakest member, 0.401 (0.306 to 0.475) behind BG2 at the signed-MW six.
  • The solar offset twins help at the signed-MW six only. BG2 minus the same blend without the offset twins is -0.045 (-0.081 to -0.004) at the signed-MW six, where D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 carry the twins. It is exactly 0 at the MVA-only eight, which have none. At days 11 to 14 the difference is -0.011 (-0.035 to +0.026).
  • The spread factor 1.15 is not shown to matter. BG2 minus BG2 with spread factor 1.0 is -0.023 (-0.053 to +0.004) at the signed-MW six and +0.008 (-0.014 to +0.028) at the MVA-only eight.
  • Experiment 87's build-up of BG2 gains little at each step. The stages are the frozen XGBoost model, the same with a 14-day correction (the stack), monthly refitting, weekly refitting, the blend without offset twins, and BG2. At the signed-MW six they score 3.160, 3.209, 3.122, 3.090, 3.061, and 3.016, so the five steps change the score by +0.049 (-0.012 to +0.116), -0.087 (-0.203 to +0.006), -0.032 (-0.068 to 0.000), -0.029 (-0.066 to -0.002), and -0.045. At the MVA-only eight the six stages score 3.950, 4.023, 3.848, 3.807, 3.788, and 3.788. At D15 the frozen XGBoost model scores 34.366 against 35.178 for climatology, because its median is 0.47 of capacity too low, close to climatology's 0.54. The 14-day correction removes most of this bias. The training window of the frozen model was not checked.
  • Experiment 377's GAM stack, on the half-hours it shares with BG2. The stack is Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 hours. It scores 2.954 against BG2's 3.016 at the signed-MW six (difference -0.062, 99% interval -0.268 to +0.145), and 4.083 against 3.743 at the MVA-only eight (+0.340, +0.108 to +0.577). D8 drives the MVA-only gap: +1.589 (95% interval +0.534 to +2.871). It is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap at D8.

docs.title: Tail calibration
docs.text:
Pinball loss (in points of effective capacity) and coverage at four tail quantiles, and the threshold-weighted CRPS (twCRPS, which weights outcomes above each Primary's 95th-percentile reading more heavily), for forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead. Coverage is the share of outcomes below the quantile, and its nominal value is 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99.

Group Forecast Pinball 1% 5% 95% 99% Coverage 1% 5% 95% 99% twCRPS Signed-MW six BG2 0.222 0.686 0.878 0.321 0.010 0.045 0.932 0.976 0.353 Signed-MW six Weekly XGBoost alone 0.212 0.679 0.905 0.344 0.010 0.041 0.923 0.973 0.372 Signed-MW six manual_heuristic 0.280 0.792 1.011 0.457 0.050 0.070 0.892 0.921 0.413 Signed-MW six climatology 0.222 0.840 1.057 0.396 0.018 0.040 0.904 0.952 0.428 MVA-only eight BG2 0.261 0.863 0.970 0.353 0.005 0.042 0.955 0.995 0.195 MVA-only eight Weekly XGBoost alone 0.258 0.865 0.983 0.357 0.005 0.043 0.954 0.995 0.200 MVA-only eight manual_heuristic 0.413 1.005 1.162 0.476 0.068 0.094 0.903 0.930 0.238 MVA-only eight climatology 0.379 1.160 1.189 0.348 0.045 0.085 0.928 0.968 0.243
  • BG2's upper tail is too narrow at the signed-MW six. The 95% and 99% quantiles cover 0.932 and 0.976, below the nominal 0.95 and 0.99. The weekly XGBoost model alone is slightly worse (0.923 and 0.973).
  • BG2's tails are slightly too wide at the MVA-only eight. The 1% quantile covers 0.005 and the 99% quantile 0.995, against nominal 0.01 and 0.99.
  • The references have worse tail calibration than BG2. manual_heuristic covers 0.050 at the 1% quantile at the signed-MW six, five times the nominal value.

docs.title: Load-shift events, weather slices, and curtailment cost
docs.text:
• During hand-labelled load-shift events, BG2 scores 7.953 at the signed-MW six. The weekly XGBoost model alone scores 8.521 and manual_heuristic 9.040, on 35,150 half-hours.
  • In the 7 days after each event ends, the references beat BG2. BG2 scores 5.022 and the weekly XGBoost model alone 4.566, against 3.933 for manual_heuristic and 4.412 for climatology, on 26,870 half-hours at the signed-MW six.
  • On sunny half-hours from April to June, BG2 and the weekly XGBoost model alone are close. At the signed-MW six they score 3.692 and 3.717.
  • On cold nights (3 °C or below), the weekly XGBoost model alone trails BG2 by 0.33. At the signed-MW six, BG2 scores 4.531, the weekly XGBoost model alone 4.864, and the frozen-stack member alone 4.563.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, scaled limit. The cost is the measure of studies.eval_protocol at a price of £2,000 per MWh. The limit is 0.9 of each Primary's maximum flow before the scored year; the published thermal limit is not used. Summed over the six Primaries for the scored year, the cost is £8.35 million for BG2, £10.59 million for the weekly stage of experiment 87's build-up (no offset twins), £6.11 million for the frozen-stack member alone, £12.66 million for manual_heuristic, and £13.72 million for climatology. D16 drives the frozen-stack member's lead (£3.95 million against £6.05 million for BG2).
  • D15 and D18 (report only). BG2 scores 7.285 across both, the weekly XGBoost model alone 7.610, and manual_heuristic 10.769.
  • We found no replicate period. The stored forecasts start in July 2025, so no earlier year can be scored, and no month is excluded by the 12-month training-history rule.

docs.title: CRPS per Primary, days 1 to 10 (percentage points of effective capacity)
Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary: not available. BG2 and its members store 11 quantiles and no mean, so the check cannot run. The mean absolute error of the median, beside each CRPS contrast, is the substitute below.
  • Error of the median beside each contrast (days 1 to 10, points): the drop-one, offset, and alone-versus-BG2 contrasts have the same sign in the mean absolute error of the median as in CRPS. For example, dropping W changes the CRPS by -0.037 and the error of the median by -0.040. The weekly XGBoost model alone minus BG2 is +0.044 in CRPS and +0.074 in error of the median at the signed-MW six. The one disagreement we found is the spread factor at the MVA-only eight: CRPS +0.008, error of the median -0.016. The CRPS interval for that contrast includes zero.
  • Gates: the re-blended BG2 equals experiment 87's stored BG2 on all 4,099,680 forecast rows of the 16 Primaries (no gap above 0.000005 points). The actuals stored with experiment 87's forecasts equal the readings in the feature cache to 0.0001 MW on the 4,004,653 forecast rows where both exist. The fast month bootstrap of e00379_contrasts.py agrees with the protocol module's headline_month_bootstrap_contrast for BG2 minus BG2 without W at the signed-MW six. Both give -0.03684, and the intervals are -0.0669 to -0.0119 and -0.0659 to -0.0121, which differ only through the random draws.
  • Audit triggers. The ml-experiment skill lists seven. Four fired: trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction: P2, P3, and P4 below), trigger 3 (the CRPS and the error of the median disagree in sign: the spread factor), trigger 4 (dropping one Primary flips a contrast's sign: the step from the frozen XGBoost model to the stack at the signed-MW six, +0.049 in total and -0.002 without D5), and trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm that contains it: BG2 without PT scores slightly below BG2).
  • A fresh Sonnet audit. The audit re-derived the BG2 and weekly-alone CRPS, the drop-W contrast, the exact match between the re-blended and the stored BG2, the absence of leakage in the drop-one blend weights (each month's weights use only earlier valid months), and the unit handling. All were confirmed. It explained P2, qualified P3, and found the zero readings below. It did not check triggers 3 to 5, the tail table, or the curtailment cost. We accepted every finding.
  • Six isolated zero readings are scored. At D9 (5 half-hours, 50 forecast rows) and D16 (1 half-hour, 10 forecast rows), the feature cache holds a reading of exactly 0.0 between readings of 43 to 59 points of capacity, which looks like telemetry dropping out. Experiment 87's stored actual is missing for these rows and this experiment keeps them, so the signed-MW six's absolute score is 3.016 here and 3.014 on experiment 87's rows. The paired contrasts move by well under 0.01.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held: each drop-one change is under 0.10 points (the largest is 0.061).
  • P2 failed (weekly refitting beats monthly by 0.05 to 0.20). Weekly beats monthly by 0.022 (-0.047 to +0.002) at the signed-MW six and 0.041 (0.015 to 0.069) at the MVA-only eight. The audit found that experiment 87's 0.123 is an all-16-Primary figure, carried by D15 and D18 (0.56 to 0.69 each). The same stored forecasts give 0.032 at the signed-MW six and 0.041 at the MVA-only eight under the protocol, and the change of metric explains about 0.02 of the difference.
  • P3 failed (the offset gain is under 0.03 at the signed-MW six). The gain is 0.045. The prediction diluted the offset's effect over 5 of 16 Primaries, but 5 of the signed-MW six carry the twins, and each gains about 0.053. The gain spreads over all hours, including nights, so the contrast is BG2 minus the same blend without the offset twins. It also reflects the blend weights that are re-chosen when the models carry the twins. The audit could not separate those two effects.
  • P4 failed in both halves (each member alone within 0.30 of BG2, except ST, which trails by over 0.50). PT alone trails BG2 by 0.401, above 0.30, and ST alone trails by 0.145, under 0.50.
  • P5 held (BG2's lead over its best single XGBoost model narrows with lead). The gap narrows from 0.080 on day 1 to 0.014 on days 11 to 14.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Add the stack's 14-day error correction to the weekly XGBoost model alone. Compare the result with the five-model blend on cold nights, where the weekly XGBoost model alone trails BG2 by 0.33 points and the frozen-stack member does not.
  • Widen the upper tail of the weekly XGBoost model. Its 95% quantile covers 0.923 at the signed-MW six.

docs.title: Code and data
docs.text:
• Scripts are in ml-experiments/00379-bg2-components-all-16-primaries-to-14-days/. e00379_build.py imports experiment 87's assembly code (e00087_assemble.py and e00087_common.py) from that experiment's folder, and e00379_adapter.py is a copy of experiment 377's adapter.
  • Stored forecasts and scores are in data/ml-experiments/00379-*/work/ (private, never committed). Experiment 377's GAM stack is read from its work/ folder and never written.
  • Refit schedule. BG2 and its members keep the weekly and monthly refits that experiment 87 fixed, and no model was refitted here. The refit schedule is under test: the contrast between weekly and monthly refitting is one of the results.

docs.title: The GAM stack taken apart at all 16 Primaries, and why it is jagged
docs.text:
Two stages of the GAM stack carry its score and two do not. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation. The labels D2 to D22 are the study's anonymised labels, and they are not consecutive because the study covers 16 of the 22 substations in the original numbering. We took apart the forecasting pipeline (the "stack") that experiment 377 scored. Stage 1 is a generalised additive model (GAM) per Primary with a Kalman filter that corrects it from recent errors. Stage 2 is a winter night offset (a fixed correction to winter night-time forecasts), recipe R (a 14-day error profile subtracted from the forecast), and quantile bands whose width is refitted each month on earlier months. We removed one stage at a time and scored what remained against BG2, the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, a blend of five forecasts that production does not run. We also built the stack up from the plain GAM, and asked whether the stack does worse at the Primaries whose demand is less regular.

A score is the quantile score: twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, which equals the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) up to the estimation from 11 quantiles. The unit is percentage points of a Primary's effective capacity (the capacity its meter can carry), and a lower score is better. "Signed-MW" Primaries are the 6 that report power in signed megawatts. "MVA-only" Primaries are the 8 that report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA); every number for those Primaries assumes reactive power is zero. D15 and D18 have under a year of history and are report only. A "step" is a half-hour change in power above 5% of capacity. In the lists below, "positive: the stage helps" means that removing the stage raises the score.

Verdict: partly supported. The Kalman filter and recipe R earn their place under the thresholds pre-registered in this page's front matter. The winter offset and the per-fold spread do not, apart from D8. The regularity hypothesis is not supported at n = 16, and 16 Primaries are too few to refute it.

docs.title: Results (quantile score, points of effective capacity)
docs.text:
• Arms. full is experiment 377's stack, rebuilt; it reproduces the stored quantiles exactly (largest difference 0.0 at all 16 Primaries). Stages: Kalman filter on stage 1's residuals (K), winter night offset (O), recipe R (R), per-fold spread (F). Not in the stack and not ablated: the solar summary S, the correction network H, and the daylight heuristic blend.
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10, mean over Primaries (full, plain GAM, BG2, manual heuristic, climatology). Signed-MW six: 2.95, 3.32, 3.02, 3.61, 3.83. MVA-only eight: 4.14, 4.87, 3.78, 4.41, 4.86. D15 and D18 (report only): 7.67, 19.98, 8.00, 13.30, 26.65. Pooled full minus BG2 (99%): -0.07 (-0.28 to +0.14) signed-MW; +0.34 (+0.09 to +0.60) MVA-only; +0.18 (-0.02 to +0.39) without D8. The plain GAM minus BG2: +0.30 (+0.07 to +0.54), +1.05 (+0.73 to +1.39), +0.61 (+0.38 to +0.90).
  • Removing one stage (positive: the stage helps), days 1 to 10, 99% interval (signed-MW six; MVA-only eight with D8; MVA-only seven without D8). K: +0.121 (+0.026 to +0.219); +0.465 (+0.179 to +0.821); +0.330 (+0.120 to +0.604). O: -0.002 (-0.011 to +0.008); -0.049 (-0.116 to -0.005); -0.003 (-0.020 to +0.012). R: +0.027 (+0.014 to +0.040); +0.095 (+0.047 to +0.149); +0.079 (+0.043 to +0.120). F (stage 1 tuning-month spread instead): -0.001 (-0.015 to +0.011); +0.270 (+0.138 to +0.420); +0.017 (-0.006 to +0.044). At D8 the per-fold arm is the own-residual spread and the replacement is the donor spread, so the +0.270 is D8's own effect of +2.21 (95% +1.37 to +3.12), averaged over eight Primaries, and not a general spread effect.
  • Thresholds from the plan. K (0.05): earns its place at both groups with D8; at the signed-MW six the point estimate is +0.12 and mostly comes from day 1. O (0.02): does not. R (0.02): earns its place at the MVA-only Primaries (+0.08 to +0.10) and at the signed-MW six (+0.027, just over the threshold, interval +0.014 to +0.040). F (0.02): does not outside D8.
  • Build-up (negative: the added stage helps), days 1 to 10 (signed-MW; MVA-only with D8; without D8). Adding F to the plain GAM: -0.001, -0.266, -0.039. Adding K: -0.328 (-0.466 to -0.193), -0.397, -0.293. Adding O: -0.011 (-0.031 to +0.008), +0.048 (-0.022 to +0.154), -0.022. Adding R: -0.027 (-0.040 to -0.014), -0.095, -0.079. The filter is the largest single step by far.
  • The Kalman filter by lead, filter removed minus full (signed-MW; MVA-only with D8). Day 1: +0.499 (+0.204 to +0.939); +0.646 (+0.340 to +0.963). Days 8 to 10: -0.074 (-0.293 to +0.115); +0.341 (+0.029 to +0.726). Days 11 to 14: -0.154 (-0.455 to +0.087); +0.303 (+0.003 to +0.666).
  • Leave one Primary out (95%). K stays positive and excludes zero whichever Primary is left out (signed-MW +0.075 to +0.150; MVA-only +0.330 to +0.524). R stays positive (+0.025 to +0.030; +0.079 to +0.107). O never excludes zero at the signed-MW six.
  • Slices, days 1 to 10, full against filter removed (signed-MW; MVA-only). Sunny daylight 4.49 against 4.27; 5.68 against 5.72. Sunny April to June 4.38 against 4.20; 5.58 against 5.53. Cold nights 4.18 against 4.94; 3.30 against 4.27. Christmas 4.38 against 4.20; 3.41 against 3.81. The filter makes the sunny-half-hour and Christmas scores worse at the signed-MW six, the slices where the stack trails BG2 (4.00 and 3.72 for BG2 on sunny daylight and Christmas).
  • D15 and D18. Without the filter the mean score of D15 and D18 is 17.2 (7.7 with it): D15 30.7 against 12.8, D18 3.6 against 2.5. Without the filter q95 coverage is 0.32 at D15. The unfiltered forecast there is badly biased and the cause was not investigated.
  • Jaggedness measures (registered in the plan; readings before 2025-07-01, hand-filtered events excluded). M1: share of variance in a half-hour-of-week profile, 0.12 (D15) to 0.65 (D9). M2: extra share explained by binned temperature, 0.01 (D4) to 0.50 (D3). M3: lag-1 autocorrelation of what remains, 0.84 to 0.98. M4: share of half-hour changes above 5% of capacity, 0.03 (D4) to 0.35 (D12). M5 (reverse-flow share, signed-MW six only) is 0.000 to 0.002.
  • Spearman correlation with the gap (stack minus BG2, days 1 to 10), registered sign in brackets. n = 16: M1 -0.02 (-) with permutation p = 0.94; M2 -0.02 (-) p = 0.94; M3 -0.19 (+) p = 0.46; M4 +0.19 (+) p = 0.48; M5 -0.21 (+) n = 6. The decision rule needs M1 at most -0.5 and M4 at least +0.5 with p under 0.025, so H2 is not supported. Leave-one-out ranges: M1 -0.24 to +0.09, M4 +0.04 to +0.39. Post hoc at n = 14 (D15 and D18 dropped): M1 -0.45 (p = 0.105), M4 +0.53 (p = 0.057), leave-one-out M4 +0.45 to +0.74. Both correlations point the registered way, and neither passes the decision rule. D15 (M1 0.12, M4 0.32) and D18 (M1 0.13, M4 0.21) have the stack ahead of BG2 (-0.51 and -0.15), against the registered direction. The gap is large at D8, D12, and D22, which have low weekly-profile shares (0.14, 0.18, 0.16), and at most +0.18 at D3 and D2, which have the highest shares after D9 (0.48 and 0.46); D9, with the highest share (0.65), has zero gap.
  • Placebo. Time-shuffled readings give M1 to M3 near zero (0.003, 0.0002, 0.00) and M4 near 0.82 (every Primary), so the measures read time structure. M1 is inflated on short histories (shuffled M1 is 0.57 at D15, 0.41 at D18, 0.03 at D9), so D15 and D18 are unreliable for M1 and the n = 14 rows are the cleaner test.

docs.title: Tail measures and curtailment cost
docs.text:
• Tail calibration, days 1 to 10, mean over Primaries (coverage q01, q05, q95, q99; pinball q05, q95). Signed-MW: full 0.022, 0.067, 0.946, 0.982; 0.773, 0.815. Filter removed 0.014, 0.046, 0.917, 0.968; 0.725, 0.914. Plain GAM 0.011, 0.036, 0.875, 0.952; 0.756, 1.007. BG2 0.010, 0.045, 0.932, 0.975; 0.686, 0.882. MVA-only: full 0.021, 0.070, 0.944, 0.982; 1.001, 1.124. Filter removed 0.024, 0.074, 0.928, 0.975. Spread removed 0.036, 0.088, 0.918, 0.963 (D8's donor spread and the stage 1 spread are narrow in both tails). BG2 0.005, 0.042, 0.955, 0.995. The stack's upper tail is better than BG2's at the signed-MW six (pinball q95 0.815 against 0.882) and its lower tail worse (q05 coverage 0.067 against 0.045). The full per-Primary table is below.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, limit 0.9 of the earlier maximum, in pounds (full, filter removed, plain GAM, BG2, manual heuristic). All rows: 4.24 million, 10.09 million, 10.59 million, 7.31 million, 10.41 million. Event rows (D5, D10, D14, D16 only; D9 and D11 have no scored half-hour above the limit): 2.81 million, 7.55 million, 7.80 million, 5.24 million, 6.88 million. The 7 days after events: 0.343 million, 0.226 million, 0.234 million, 0.285 million, 0.496 million.
  • At limit 0.5 (same order). All rows: 59.8 million, 85.2 million, 98.2 million, 72.9 million, 104.8 million. Event rows: 7.75 million, 22.99 million, 27.41 million, 11.96 million, 18.28 million. The 7 days after events: 3.25 million, 2.67 million, 3.09 million, 4.07 million, 3.57 million. The filter lowers the cost on all rows and during events. In the 7 days after events it raises the total at both limits, mostly at D16 at limit 0.9 (£45,000 without the filter against £155,000 with it) and with mixed signs by Primary at limit 0.5, which agrees with experiment 367's finding that the Kalman transient adds error after a step.
  • No input is nulled in this experiment, so there are no nulled rows to compare.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Control. The arm full equals experiment 377's stored stack: the largest absolute difference in q50 and q95 is 0.0 at all 16 Primaries on the scored year.
  • Median minus mean forecast, per site. 0.0 at every Primary and every arm: the stored mean is the centre of the centred spread tables, so no independent mean-forecast contrast exists.
  • Predictions. P1 failed on days 1 to 10 (+0.12 and +0.47, not under 0.05) and held on day 1. P2 held at the signed-MW six (+0.027) and failed at the MVA-only eight (+0.095). P3 held at the signed-MW six and failed at the MVA-only eight (-0.049, D8; held without D8, -0.003). P4 held without D8 (+0.017) and failed with it (+0.270, D8's donor spread); q05 coverage worsened at the MVA-only eight (0.070 to 0.088) and moved from 0.067 to 0.064 at the signed-MW six. P5 held at the signed-MW six (+0.37) and failed at the MVA-only eight (+0.73). P6 failed.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 2 (predictions P1 days 1 to 10, P2 and P3 at the MVA-only eight, P5 at the MVA-only eight, and P6 failed, and the MVA-only misses are explained by D8 alone only partly); trigger 5 (the arm without the winter offset beats the full stack at the MVA-only eight, and the arm without the filter beats it at days 8 to 14 at the signed-MW six, within noise). Triggers 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 did not fire.
  • Placebos. A permutation placebo (10,000 shuffles of each measure across Primaries) gives the p values above; a time-shuffled-readings placebo gives M1 to M3 near zero.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The stack is experiment 377's, without S, H, and the heuristic blend; stage contrasts may differ in default 3, which experiment 378 builds.
  • The per-fold spread contrast at D8 compares the own-residual arm with the donor spread, so it reports D8's spread choice and not whether refitting the spread monthly helps.
  • D15 and D18 without the filter are badly biased; their contrasts are report only.
  • The regularity hypothesis was tested at 16 Primaries with measures M1 to M4 that are not independent of each other. A larger test would use more Primaries or simulated series with set regularity.
  • Next: a filter that fades out beyond day 7 (signed-MW days 8 to 14 score better without it), and a stack without the winter offset is a simpler release candidate.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet agent audited the numbers (about 75 quoted numbers, all 384 entries of the per-Primary tail table (16 Primaries, 3 arms, 8 measures), and a re-derivation of four Primaries' scores from the stored arms, which agree within 0.01 and 0.1 at D15) and a second agent reviewed the code. Findings and triage:

  • Accepted and fixed: D8's spread effect was misquoted (+2.21, not +1.6); the D15 score of 17.2 is a mean of D15 and D18; BG2's sunny-daylight score is 4.00; the sign conventions were missing from two list headings; P4 was not scored; the claim that the stack trails BG2 where steps are large, "after day 7" and "day 1 only" overstated the evidence; the offset harm is D8's; the post-event curtailment rise is mostly D16. The permutation p value now adds one to numerator and denominator, and the placebo header names which measure is near zero.
  • Rejected: the claim that D8's fold months were built from D8's own first reading and cover about two months. The control prints 219,674 D8 rows for full and the stored stack alike. The claim that stage 1's spread may be uncentred: the median minus the mean is 0.0 for every arm, including the arms that keep stage 1's spread.

docs.title: A single weekly XGBoost model for Primary demand against the GAM stack
docs.text: A single XGBoost model per Primary, refitted weekly, is as good as the GAM stack at 9 of 14 Primaries and better on average at the eight whose meters hide reverse flow. At the six Primaries with signed readings it is level on average but worse at D11 and D14, and its upper tail is narrower. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation, labelled D2 to D22. The XGBoost model is the weekly member of BG2 (experiment 87), which uses the weather forecast of the 51-member ECMWF ensemble, the local hour and day of week, bank-holiday distances, and the three most recent power readings. We tested seven small changes to it, one at a time, on monthly refits. We then refitted the three changes that helped, together, every week. The GAM stack is "Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 hours" from experiment 377, without the solar summary below 168 hours. All scores are CRPS (the quantile score over 11 levels) in points of effective capacity at days 1 to 10 on fold_a_daily_gap_v1, under demand-v1. A negative difference means the XGBoost model is better. Every MVA-only number assumes reactive power is zero. The XGBoost model is refitted weekly and the stack monthly, so the contrast mixes the model family with the refit schedule.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Hypothesis. Not supported as stated: the XGBoost model is not within +0.05 points of the stack at all 14 countable Primaries. Verdict "partly supported" because it is at 9 of 14.
  • Matches the stack (point estimate within +0.05). D8, D12, D22, D5, D2, D19, D4, D9, D21. The 95% interval lies wholly below zero at D8 (-1.62), D12 (-0.80), D22 (-0.29), and D5 (-0.25), although the audit's alternative bootstrap puts D5 at -0.62 to +0.11. Worse than the stack with an interval above zero: D14 (+0.30; +0.04 to +0.63) and D11 (+0.15; +0.02 to +0.30). Inconclusive: D10 (+0.16), D16 (+0.09), D3 (+0.050, which misses the tolerance by 0.0002). The worst Primary is D14. D15 and D18 are report only: +2.34 (0.14 to 4.24) over 4 months and +0.07 over 6 months.
  • Pooled, 99% interval. Signed-MW six +0.075 (-0.120 to +0.266). MVA-only eight with D8 -0.361 (-0.602 to -0.101), without D8 -0.197 (-0.399 to -0.025). Leaving one Primary out never changes the sign (signed-MW +0.03 to +0.14; MVA-only -0.20 to -0.42).
  • Against the other references. Minus BG2: +0.007 (-0.048 to +0.062) signed-MW, -0.016 (-0.069 to +0.042) MVA-only. Minus the stored weekly baseline: -0.038 (-0.092 to +0.008) signed- MW, -0.034 (-0.063 to -0.004) MVA-only. Minus manual_heuristic: -0.58 and -0.65. Minus climatology: -0.81 and -1.09 (all 99%).
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10 (bundle, stack, BG2, manual heuristic, climatology). Signed-MW: D5 3.83, 4.08, 3.94, 4.35, 4.48; D9 2.51, 2.51, 2.51, 2.92, 2.99; D10 3.43, 3.27, 3.45, 4.16, 4.31; D11 2.58, 2.43, 2.57, 3.41, 3.55; D14 2.51, 2.21, 2.39, 3.01, 3.47; D16 3.29, 3.20, 3.24, 3.80, 4.20. MVA-only: D2 2.28, 2.47, 2.30, 2.86, 2.93; D3 1.72, 1.67, 1.75, 2.11, 2.33; D4 2.42, 2.45, 2.51, 2.80, 2.83; D8 7.61, 9.23, 7.61, 8.31, 9.64; D12 6.72, 7.52, 6.75, 7.92, 8.83; D19 3.17, 3.29, 3.18, 3.79, 3.93; D21 2.36, 2.35, 2.38, 2.77, 2.91; D22 3.81, 4.10, 3.75, 4.71, 5.47.
  • Screening, each change minus the monthly control (99.86% interval, Bonferroni for seven arms). Daily mean shortwave (A2): -0.051 (-0.086 to -0.019) signed-MW, -0.016 (-0.049 to +0.023) MVA- only. 1-year half-life (A5): -0.019 (-0.034 to -0.006) and +0.004. Sunny flag: -0.002 at both groups. Economy 7 input (A1): 0.000 (-0.002 to +0.002). Lead-dependent half-life (A3): +0.007 and +0.025 (worse at MVA-only). 12-month window: +0.043 and +0.024. 0.25-year half-life: +0.072 and +0.039. The refitted control matches the stored monthly member in the median (mean gap 0.02 MW) but not fully in CRPS (up to 0.066 points at D16; see "Audit"). The screening used all 365 daily runs.
  • Predictions. P1 holds (9 of 14 against 9 to 11 predicted). P2 fails: the Economy 7 input moved the Economy 7 step hours by -0.002 (signed-MW) against a predicted -0.03 to -0.10. The local hour is already an input, so a tree can split on the step. P3 partly holds: the solar summary lowers the score on sunny April-to-June half-hours by 0.074 at the signed-MW six and 0.056 at the MVA-only eight. P4 holds (lead-dependent half-life +0.007 and +0.025, both under 0.03). P5 fails: the sunny flag removes about 0.15% of the D12 bias (4.92 to 4.91 points).
  • MVA-only handling. The control under-forecasts demand on sunny half-hours at D12 by 4.92 points of capacity (median minus actual) and over-forecasts it by 6.19 points at D19, 4.75 at D21, and 9.88 at D8. The sunny flag leaves each bias unchanged to within 0.05 points at the 14 countable Primaries. The rule-chosen reverse-flow column of experiments 366 and 374 is off at D12, D2, and D8 (the three checked) when computed from forecast shortwave (correlation +0.21 to +0.28 at D12 against a threshold of 0.3), so that arm equals the control by construction and was not fitted. The signed-MW six serve as controls: the sunny flag moves their bias by under 0.05 points.

docs.text:
Measure, days 1 to 10 Signed-MW bundle Signed-MW stack MVA-only bundle MVA-only stack Pinball loss q05 / q95 0.68 / 0.89 0.77 / 0.81 0.86 / 0.95 1.00 / 1.12 Pinball loss q01 / q99 0.25 / 0.36 0.26 / 0.27 0.25 / 0.33 0.28 / 0.33 Coverage q05 / q95 (ideal 0.05 / 0.95) 0.053 / 0.916 0.067 / 0.946 0.068 / 0.938 0.070 / 0.944 Coverage q01 / q99 (ideal 0.01 / 0.99) 0.007 / 0.984 0.022 / 0.982 0.013 / 0.992 0.021 / 0.982 twCRPS 0.372 0.327 0.197 0.226
  • The upper tail is the XGBoost model's weakness at the signed-MW six. Its q95 coverage is 0.916 and its q99 pinball loss is 0.36 against 0.27 for the stack. At the MVA-only eight the XGBoost model has the lower pinball loss at q05, q95, and q01, and the lower twCRPS.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, scored year. At a limit of 0.9 times the maximum observed export, the stack costs less at 4 of 6 (D16 £2.95 million against £6.64 million; D14 £0.54 million against £1.69 million). At a limit of 0.5 the stack costs less at all six. The cost is not defined at the MVA-only eight (reactive power assumed zero).
  • Load-shift events (hand-labelled). Event rows: signed-MW bundle 8.23 against stack 7.35 and BG2 7.96; MVA-only 5.18 against 5.46 and 5.15. The 7 days after: signed-MW 4.55 against 5.11 and 5.07; MVA-only 2.90 against 2.98 and 2.88. No pass or fail is drawn.
  • Lag-missing rows. Only 0.2% of scored half-hours have a missing power lag (3,630 at the signed-MW six, 3,226 of them at D5; 2,238 at the MVA-only eight). Their 5%-to-95% interval is 23.6 points wide at the signed-MW six against 20.1 on rows with lags, and 23.3 against 26.0 at the MVA-only eight. Coverage of that interval is 0.826 and 0.842 on missing rows, against 0.863 and 0.870 on present rows (nominal 0.90). No widening rule was fitted: 3,630 rows, concentrated in one Primary, are too few to fit a factor.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean. Not computed: the stored frames hold quantiles only and no mean. The mean absolute error of the median points the same way as CRPS at the contrasts that matter: D14 4.34 against 3.90 for the stack, D11 4.61 against 4.34, D8 14.06 against 15.94, D12 12.08 against 13.20.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fires: the Economy 7 prediction (P2) was contradicted, and the explanation (the local hour is an input) is structural and was not tested by a removal arm. Triggers 1, 3 to 6 do not fire. The leave-one-out contrasts keep their sign. Trigger 7 does not fire. The Sonnet audit and its triage are listed under "Audit" below.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lead range. The headline is days 1 to 10. Days 11 to 14 are not read here.
  • Schedule confound. The XGBoost model is refitted weekly and the stack monthly. The stack has no solar summary below 168 hours, so it is not the protocol's current research default.
  • Selection. The three changes were chosen on the scored year. The weekly bundle's gain over the stored weekly baseline (-0.04 signed-MW, -0.03 MVA-only) is an upper bound.
  • Next. Give the signed-MW six a better upper tail (a calibration step on the XGBoost quantiles). Try a custom folded-latent loss for the MVA-only reverse-flow bias. GAM partial effects as XGBoost inputs (out-of-fold values per refit) need a separate experiment.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored predictions with its own join and pinball code (report: briefs/e381_audit_report.md in the private data folder). Triage:

  • Headline numbers reproduce. Bundle at D5, D12, and D8 is 3.827, 6.716, and 7.615 (log: 3.829, 6.716, 7.612), and bundle minus stack is -0.253, -0.800, and -1.618 (log: -0.253, -0.799, -1.615). Accepted: nothing changes.
  • The reference gate is only partly met. The refitted monthly control differs from the stored monthly member by up to 0.066 points of CRPS per Primary (D16 breaks the plan's 0.05 gate) and by +0.031 on average at the signed-MW six. The printed gate was a median gap (mean 0.02 MW), not a CRPS gate. A cause such as GPU non-determinism is likely and untested. Accepted: the screening contrasts compare two refits made the same way, so they are unaffected, but the bundle's gain over the stored weekly baseline (-0.04 signed-MW, -0.03 MVA-only) is the same size as this reproducibility gap and is not read as a gain.
  • D5 is borderline. The agent's row-weighted month bootstrap gives -0.62 to +0.11 for D5 against the stack. Accepted: the headline names three Primaries (D8, D12, D22) with clear gains and D5 as borderline.
  • Screening rows. The screening used all 365 daily runs (4,012,330 half-hours), not the registered 292 fold_a_daily_gap_v1 runs. Accepted as a caveat: the final comparison uses the shared rows (2,824,844 half-hours, which BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology limit to the 292 runs, and the stack limits further at D8, D15, and D18).
  • Selection. Almost all of the bundle's gain over the control comes from the solar summary, and the sunny flag is kept on a 0.002-point effect, both chosen on the scored year. Accepted: stated in the caveats.
  • No leakage found. The previous-day shortwave mean is missing on the first day of every run, and every scored run is served by the latest refit at or before its origin. The daily shortwave mean has a negligible train-and-serve difference (half-hours with missing power are dropped from training).
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fires and its explanation holds: the control already has hour_local. Triggers 3 and 4 do not fire. The audit did not compute trigger 6, and did not rerun the tail, curtailment, or load-shift sections.

docs.title: Arms (pre-registered in the plan above)
docs.text: A1 Economy 7 input, A2 daily mean shortwave, A3 lead-dependent half-life, A4 sunny flag (the MVA remedy), A5 recency (0.25-year and 1-year half-lives, 12-month window), A7 rule-chosen reverse-flow column (not fitted, see above), and the bundle of A2, A4, and the 1-year half-life. A6 (GAM shapes as inputs) was not run.

docs.title: Plan as registered
docs.text: Plan (written before any score was read). The question is whether a plain XGBoost model, retrained every week and with no stacked parts, can match the GAM stack at each of the 16 Primaries. The baseline is the weekly member of BG2 (experiment 87), scored under the demand-v1 protocol by experiment 379. The baseline already holds the three recent-power lags (experiment 371 found these carry the gap at D8), the local hour and day of week, the distance to the nearest bank holiday and to Christmas, and lead_hours, so those candidates are in the control and are not tested again.

docs.title: Plan: pre-registered arms
docs.text:
• Control. Experiment 87's n1h recipe, refitted monthly for screening (the stored only_M arm of experiment 379 is the reference; the refit must reproduce it within 0.05 points before any other arm is read) and weekly for the final comparison (the stored only_W arm). colsample_bytree and colsample_bynode stay at 1.0 in every arm, so no arm gains from column subsampling.
  • A1, Economy 7. Adds two inputs: a 0/1 flag for the local half-hours 1 to 6 (the protocol's Economy 7 step hours) and the number of half-hours since local 00:30, clipped to 0 to 12.
  • A2, solar summary stand-in. Adds the mean forecast shortwave over the local day of the valid time (the same ensemble member, the same run) and the mean over the previous local day. It is a cheap stand-in for the GAM's two-number solar summary S.
  • A3, lead-dependent recency. Row weights use a half-life of 0.25 years for rows at leads under 48 hours and 1 year for rows at longer leads, in place of the single 0.5-year half-life.
  • A4, MVA remedy (eight MVA-only Primaries only; the signed-MW six are controls). Adds a sunny flag (forecast shortwave over the Haurwitz clear-sky irradiance above 0.6) and its product with shortwave. A second variant reads the rule-chosen fit of experiments 366 and 374 as an input column if the stored fit exists for the run origins and uses data from before each origin only; the plan records at the start of the work whether it does, and drops the variant otherwise.
  • A5, recency (maintainer, 2026-10-28). Experiments 17 and 34 found that a half-life of 0.5 years beats 2 years by 0.03 to 0.15 points (experiment 34) and that a 12-month sliding window is about as good (experiment 17: -0.92 for the half-life, -0.84 for the window, against an expanding window), while a 6-month window is worse. The control already uses 0.5 years, so the arms test the neighbours: hl025 (0.25 years), hl1 (1 year), and win12 (a 365-day window with the 0.5-year half-life). The half-lives are fixed here and not chosen on tuning months, which lie before the scored year.
  • A6, GAM shapes as XGBoost inputs (optional, only if time allows). Not run in this experiment. It would fit the GAM per fold on that fold's training window only, take its fitted partial effects for time of day, day of week, and temperature and its stage-1 fitted value, and give the training rows out-of-fold values (the GAM refitted with each training month held out in turn) so that no row sees an in-sample fit; the scored rows use the fold's full-window fit. This needs the GAM stack fitted on 12 held-out-month folds per refit, so it is a separate experiment.
  • A7, rule-chosen reverse-flow column (MVA-only eight; added 2026-10-29 at the manager's request, after the A1 to A5 screening). One extra column, no second model: experiment 366's rule recomputed at each monthly refit from that refit's training rows only (sunny midday readings: the Pearson correlation with shortwave above 0.3, or a 1st percentile below 1.0 point of capacity, switches the column on), times the fitted slope of those readings on shortwave, times the forecast shortwave. Prediction: the rule switches the column on at D12 only; the column is a monotone function of shortwave at D12, which a tree can already split on, so the arm moves the D12 score by under 0.02 points and leaves the sunny-half-hour bias at about -4.9 points. A bigger change would mean the shortwave inputs interact badly with the folded meter. Tested monthly at the eight MVA-only Primaries with the signed-MW six as unchanged controls (the rule is off there). A signed-capacity-times-irradiance column from the same fit is the same function again, so it is not run separately.
  • Bundle. The arms kept by the decision rule, fitted weekly.

docs.title: Diagnostics before the arms
docs.text:
• MVA handling. Residuals of the control (median minus actual) on sunny half-hours at D12 (known reverse flow), at the other seven MVA-only Primaries, and at the signed-MW six, by group and lead band, before and after A4.
  • Reference rows. The stack from experiment 377, BG2, manual_heuristic, climatology, and the stored weekly baseline, each reported with its absolute score.

docs.title: Tails and nulled inputs (maintainer, 2026-10-28)
docs.text: Tail pinball loss and coverage at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles are reported per group and per Primary beside CRPS and twCRPS, and the take-home names the tail result. The control and every arm already carry the three recent-power lags, which are missing (NaN) when the telemetry has a gap near the origin. The write-up reports mean 5%-to-95% interval width and coverage on half-hours whose lags are missing against half-hours whose lags are present, and tries one simple widening rule (scaling the quantile distances from the median by a factor fitted on the earlier months of the same fold) if coverage on the missing rows falls short.

docs.title: Avoidable-curtailment cost (maintainer, 2026-10-28)
docs.text: Because the arms feed missing lags on event rows, the write-up reports the protocol's avoidable curtailment cost (studies.eval_protocol) during each hand-labelled load-shift event, in the 7 days after it ends, and across all rows, per group and per Primary, beside CRPS and the tail measures. The cost is defined only for the signed-MW six, so the MVA-only eight carry the label "not defined". The take-home names it.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text: Sonnet only. At most 3 threads and MemoryMax=16G per job. The GPU is shared. Tail calibration, slices, load-shift rows, per-Primary table, leave-one-out, and the D8 own-residual and donor-spread arms follow the protocol page. Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries.

docs.title: Do three recent-power lags, added to the GAM stack as smooth terms, close the gap to monthly XGBoost at substation D8?
Do three recent-power lags, added to the GAM stack as smooth terms, close the D8 gap?
docs.text:
Giving the forecast three recent readings of the substation's power did not help at D8, the substation where the competing XGBoost method leads, and made D8's forecast worse. We asked whether a forecast of electricity demand improves when it is told how much power a substation drew in the hours just before the forecast was made. The extra readings raised D8's forecast error by 0.445 points of the substation's effective capacity (error 9.672 against 9.227). At 12 of the other 13 counted substations the error moved by under 0.05 points; at D22 it rose by 0.096.

The three readings are the newest one available at forecast time, the reading one day earlier at the target half-hour, and the reading one week earlier. Experiment 371 found that monthly XGBoost leads the GAM stack at D8 mainly through these readings. We gave the GAM stack of experiment 377 (Primary demand research default 1, extended to 336 hours) the same readings. The stack fits in two stages: the first predicts from weather and calendar for each target time, so it cannot use readings taken before the forecast was made, and the second corrects the first stage's mean forecast. We added the readings to the second stage as smooth terms, each fitted every month on earlier months only. Each reading enters as the reading minus the stack's own forecast for that half-hour.

Scores are the quantile score (CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score estimated from 11 quantiles) in points of effective capacity; lower is better, and a contrast is the arm with the readings minus the stack without them. The "spline arm" is the pre-registered design, the "linear arm" is a sensitivity check, and the "penalised spline arm" was added after the audit. BG2 is the best-guess forecast of experiment 87. D8 and the other labels D2 to D22 are Primary substations. The signed-MW six are the six Primaries that report signed megawatts. The full design is in the plan below.

Results (days 1 to 10, spline minus default, 99% intervals, 20,000 resamples of whole months).

  • D8 (own-residual arm): +0.445 (+0.090 to +0.983); default 9.227, spline 9.672, BG2 7.615.
  • Days 1 to 2 at D8: +0.108 (-0.064 to +0.391). Days 3 to 10: +0.531 (+0.115 to +1.184). Days 8 to 10: +0.695 (+0.162 to +1.489). The harm grows with lead, the opposite of the prediction that the gain would be larger at days 1 to 2.
  • Signed-MW six: -0.019 (-0.052 to +0.008); days 1 to 2: -0.043 (-0.061 to -0.028).
  • MVA-only eight with D8: +0.055 (+0.012 to +0.125); without D8: +0.004 (-0.022 to +0.027).
  • Penalised spline arm (post hoc; smoothness penalty weight 100,000 in place of 10, added after the audit found the pre-registered weight almost zero; not adoptable): D8 +0.080 (-0.012 to +0.154); signed-MW six -0.027 (-0.056 to -0.004); MVA-only eight with D8 +0.004 (-0.018 to +0.023); D2 and D4 -0.026 (-0.054 to -0.003); short-history group +0.016 (-0.019 to +0.063).
  • Placebos D2 and D4 pooled: -0.023 (-0.066 to +0.007). The pooled change is slightly towards a gain, the opposite direction to D8, so neither placebo fails.
  • Per Primary (95%, pre-registered spline): D8 +0.445 (+0.127 to +0.838), D22 +0.096 (+0.037 to +0.159), D15 +0.283 (+0.020 to +0.654, report only), D14 -0.048 (-0.074 to -0.019), D4 -0.048 (-0.095 to -0.010). The spline wins at 10 of 14 counted Primaries. The worst Primary is D8.
  • Linear arm: D8 +0.089 (+0.004 to +0.162); signed-MW six -0.022 (-0.043 to -0.001).
  • D8 by month (days 1 to 10): +1.89 (2025-08), +1.46, +0.50, +0.20, +0.32, +0.03, +0.10, +0.07, +0.15, +0.03, +0.04 (2026-06). Leaving out August 2025 moves the pooled D8 difference from +0.445 to +0.293.
  • Donor-spread arm at D8: default 11.588, spline 12.112 (+0.524).

Tails. At D8 the coverage of the 0.05 quantile is 0.0589 (default) and 0.0583 (spline), of the 0.95 quantile 0.934 and 0.933, and of the 0.99 quantile 0.970 and 0.968, so the lags neither fix nor break the lower-tail undercoverage that experiment 377 found. The printed report holds the pinball loss at the four tail quantiles and the twCRPS per group and per Primary for all six arms. The twCRPS contrast at D8 is +0.050 (+0.011 to +0.118) (the spline is worse); at the signed-MW six it is -0.004 (-0.015 to +0.002).

Nulled rows. A row is nulled when any of the three lags is missing (a gap in the power record). Such rows are under 2% of every Primary: 19 to 3,226 rows per Primary against 55,178 to 172,783 un-nulled rows. Their coverage of the 5% to 95% interval is erratic because the samples are tiny (0.42 to 1.00), and interval width on nulled rows is not systematically wider, since the treatment adds no widening rule. A widening rule was not tried, because nulled rows are under 1% of every Primary except D15 (1.1%) and D5 (1.9%).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The zero-shift gate (no shift reproduces experiment 377's stored stack) was run at D2 only.
  • Median minus mean forecast per site is 0.0 points for default and spline at every Primary, so the spread does not shift the forecast. The mean-forecast absolute error at D8 rises from 15.93 to 16.47 points, in the same direction as the quantile score.
  • Triggers that fired: 2 (the result contradicts its prediction P1, and the only tested explanation is the monthly pattern above, which is post hoc) and 5 (the default arm, nested inside the spline arm, beats it at D8). Triggers 1, 3, 4, and 6 did not fire (the placebos did not fail; the quantile and median-error contrasts agree in sign; leaving one month out leaves D8 positive at +0.293 to +0.489). Trigger 7 does not apply. An independent audit by a Sonnet agent found no lookahead (it corrupted readings after the newest usable one and the anomalies did not change) and no code bug, and reproduced D8's stored forecast exactly. It found that the pre-registered penalty was almost zero and that D8's early fits rested on 21 to 29 independent daily origins per lead band; both are now stated here, and the post hoc penalised arm above was added in response. Not acted on: the missing intercept in the fit (a free constant made D8 worse in the audit's test), and the whole-table cleaning pass that 377 shares.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The terms are stage 2 additive terms, not stage 1 GAM terms and not interactions with the weather inputs. The refutation covers that form only.
  • D8 has under 12 months of history for the whole scored year. Its first scored month rests on one month of history, and its fits use 21 to 29 independent daily origins per lead band in August 2025 (rows per band overstate this, because the newest-lag term takes one value per origin). This departs from the 12-month rule in the plan, as experiment 377's D8 own-residual arm does. The linear and penalised versions stay slightly positive at D8 through spring 2026, so more history alone may not turn the result.
  • Rows before 2024-07 carry no shift in the spread pool of the early fold months, which slightly widens the treated spread there.
  • Next: the lags as origin-dependent inputs to stage 1, or an interaction of the day-lag anomaly with the stack's weather terms, tested at the Primaries with a year of history first.

Reuses experiment 377's folder (e00377s2_common, e00377s2_corrections, e00377s3_stack, e00377_adapter, e00377_score) unchanged, and studies.eval_protocol. Schedule: monthly stage 2 refits, weekly stage 1 fits as stored by 377; the contrast depends on the schedule only through the stage 2 fits. Lag source: the cleaned power the GAM trains on, available at forecast time up to 3.5 hours before the origin.

docs.title: Plan, registered before any score was read
docs.text:
Where the terms enter. The stack's stage 1 GAM predicts from the valid time's weather and calendar and does not depend on the forecast origin, so a lag measured from the origin cannot be a column of its design matrix without re-fitting stage 1 on one row per origin and valid time. The stage 2 correction already depends on the origin (it contains recipe R, a profile of recent residuals), so the terms enter there: one additive shift of the stage 2 mean, then the same fold-by-fold spread. This is a stage 2 smooth term, not a stage 1 GAM term, and the write-up says so in its opening.

The three lags and their anomaly form. For a run with origin o and a row with valid time v, the newest usable reading is the half-hour ending at o - 3.5 h (371's telemetry delay of 3 hours plus the half-hour a reading spans), the day lag is the latest earlier reading with v's half-hour of day, and the week lag is the latest earlier reading with v's weekday and half-hour, all no later than the newest usable reading (the definition of origin_lags in experiment 87). Each lag enters as an anomaly: the reading minus the stack's own corrected mean for that half-hour, taken from the run with the latest origin not after that half-hour (always before o, so it is known at o). The anomaly removes the daily and weekly shape that a raw lag would carry, which a lag-only additive term cannot remove.

No lookahead, and no leaky lags. Every lag time is at least 3.5 hours before o, so no lag is at or after the origin at any lead; the nullification of leaky lags that the feature pipeline does for lags shorter than the lead cannot trigger, and the code asserts that every lag index is at most the newest usable index. A missing reading gives no contribution (the term is zero), so absent data degrades to "default".

Term form. For each lag and each of the six protocol lead bands, a penalised cubic B-spline (8 basis functions, second-difference penalty, weight fixed at 10 before any score is read) of the anomaly, clipped to the 1st to 99th percentile of the fit rows; the shift is the sum of the three terms, fitted by penalised least squares on the residual of the stack's mean, on rows whose origin and valid time both precede the fold month's first instant (the 12-month rule), outside the hand-filtered events. The spread for each fold month is fitted on earlier months' residuals of the treated mean, each earlier month using its own out-of-fold shift. Fits start at cut 2024-07-01 (rows before it get no shift). A band with under 2,000 fit rows gets no shift and is listed. Sensitivity arm, pre-registered: the three terms linear (penalty weight infinite).

Arms. default (the 377 stack as stored, unchanged), default_plus_origin_lags, and default_plus_origin_lags_linear (sensitivity only; at most one pre-registered arm can be adopted, and it is the spline arm). BG2, climatology and the manual heuristic are the references.

Rows and unit. The 16 Primaries of experiment 377; D15 and D18 are report only, D8 follows 377's two-arm rule. Compute: 3 threads.

Tails and nulled inputs. The write-up reports pinball loss and coverage at the 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 quantiles per group and per Primary, beside CRPS and twCRPS, and names the tail result in the take-home. Rows whose lags are missing form the nulled rows; the write-up gives interval width and coverage on nulled and un-nulled rows, and tries a simple widening rule if coverage falls short.

docs.title: Nulled load-shift lags and wider bands in the weekly XGBoost model
docs.text:
Telling the weekly XGBoost model which of its power lags lie inside a load-shift event does not repair its upper-tail forecasts. The XGBoost model forecasts each Primary substation's half-hourly power 1 to 10 days ahead and is refitted every week. A load shift is a period when National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) moves a substation's load onto its neighbours. A power lag is the substation's own power at the forecast origin, at the same time on the latest day, or at the same time in the latest week. We took the hand-labelled load-shift events as known, which is a perfect detector, and tested three fixes on the forecasts whose power lags lie inside an event. The fixes were to set those lags to missing, to switch to a model with no power lags, and to widen the forecast band.

At the six Primaries whose meters report signed megawatts (signed-MW), the model with no power lags lowered the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lower is better), but the interval includes zero and the result rests on two events. At the eight Primaries whose meters report only apparent power (MVA-only), the same model raised the CRPS. The 5% to 95% band should contain 0.90 of the readings. Fixed widening left the signed-MW share at 0.77 to 0.82. Widening by a factor fitted on earlier months raised the share to 0.88 to 0.93, but the factor sat at its cap of 2 in most months, which doubles the band width. Gate O is the pre-registered test of whether perfect labels help enough to justify building a detector. Gate O failed, so the detector arm b2 was not run.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Verdict: not supported. Gate O fails four of its five conditions (listed under Gate O below); the detector arm b2 did not run, as the stop rule requires.
  • Rows: the contaminated-lag rows are rows outside events, days 1 to 10, with at least one of the three lags inside an event: 21,601 at the signed-MW six (6 months) and 22,232 at the MVA-only eight (8 months). They make up 2.2% and 1.6% of the main-score rows.
  • Arms: d, the weekly member of BG2 (experiment 87, stored). c1, event targets dropped, lags inside events set to missing in training and at test time, 30% pseudo-event lag dropout in training. c2, a lagless model (event targets dropped) served on the contaminated rows, d elsewhere. Fixed widening (k = 1.28, tuning-adjacent) and as-of widening (k from earlier months, cap 2) on the contaminated rows. Seed 0, colsample 1.0, weekly refits, ENS control-member training.
  • CRPS on contaminated rows (points of capacity), signed-MW six: d 5.477, c1 5.539, c2 4.153, d plus widening 5.296, c1 plus widening 5.326, c2 plus widening 4.070, BG2 6.095. MVA-only eight: d 3.197, c1 3.292, c2 3.846, d plus widening 3.326, c1 plus widening 3.442, c2 plus widening 3.967, BG2 3.150.
  • Contrasts against d (95% Bonferroni over 6, month bootstrap):
Group Contrast CRPS Tail pinball (mean of q95 and q99) signed-MW c1 + widening -0.15 (-0.86 to +1.06) -0.22 (-0.39 to +0.06) signed-MW c2 + widening -1.41 (-3.12 to +0.32) -0.70 (-2.23 to +0.06) signed-MW widening alone -0.18 (-0.46 to +0.16) -0.34 (-0.89 to +0.06) MVA-only c1 + widening +0.24 (+0.09 to +0.35) +0.11 (-0.05 to +0.25) MVA-only c2 + widening +0.77 (+0.17 to +1.54) +0.18 (-0.03 to +0.51)
  • Tail calibration on contaminated rows, signed-MW six (d, c1, c2, c2 plus widening): q95 pinball 2.29, 2.58, 1.58, 1.19; q99 pinball 0.58, 0.86, 0.43, 0.29; coverage of q95 0.774, 0.709, 0.743, 0.824; coverage of q99 0.917, 0.889, 0.926, 0.972; coverage of the 5% to 95% band 0.705, 0.696, 0.731, 0.820. At the MVA-only eight d already covers 0.882.
  • Nulled against un-nulled rows (signed-MW six, 5% to 95% band): d covers 0.705 on contaminated rows (width 21.7 points) and 0.876 on ordinary rows (20.2). Widening by 1.28 widens the contaminated rows to 27.8 points and lifts coverage to 0.774. c1 and c2 do not widen the band (22.7 and 21.7).
  • Main score, outside events, days 1 to 10, minus d (90% interval): signed-MW c1 -0.015 (-0.032 to 0.000), c2 -0.029 (-0.066 to 0.000); MVA-only c1 -0.004 (-0.018 to +0.009), c2 +0.011 (+0.003 to +0.019). Largest per-Primary difference among the countable Primaries: D12 +0.058 for c2. The report-only D18 is worse by +1.95 (c1) and +1.51 (c2), and D15 by +0.97 (c1).
  • Placebos D2, D9, D11, and D21: arms c2 and widening equal d, bit for bit.

docs.title: Gate O: whether perfect labels justify building a detector
docs.text:
1. The CRPS interval of c2 plus widening includes zero (-3.12 to +0.32), and the tail pinball interval includes zero (upper bound +0.06). Fails.
  2. The 5% to 95% coverage of c2 plus widening on contaminated rows is 0.820, 0.08 under 0.90. Fails.
  3. Main headline per group within 0.02: signed-MW passes; MVA-only c2 plus widening has an upper bound of +0.023. Fails for c2.
  4. No countable Primary worse than 0.05: D12 is +0.058 under c2. Fails for c2.
  5. Placebos identical to d. Passes.

docs.title: Where the c2 gain comes from
docs.text:
• Two events carry most of it. On the contaminated rows attributed to each event, c2 minus d is -3.69 for the D16 event of 17.5 days over Christmas and -4.77 for the D10 event in November. For the 42-day D5 event it is -0.83. Leaving out the D16 event over Christmas moves the signed-MW c2 plus widening contrast from -1.41 to -0.98 (the audit's attribution by lag gives -0.86, and -1.05 without the D10 event, and -0.44 without both). Leaving out the D5 events leaves it at -1.37 and -1.57.
  • The gain grows with time since onset. Signed-MW c2 minus d is -0.57 within 1 day of onset, -0.68 from 1 to 3 days, and -1.85 beyond 3 days. A detector can see events only after about a day (experiment 298), so the first-day rows are the ones it would miss.
  • No contaminated signed-MW rows lie in 20 December to 10 January, because the events that cover that period exclude the rows.
  • D18 is the exception that matters. One D18 event (December, 3 days) has a CRPS of 8.5 for d and 53.0 for c2, a rise of 44 points, and drives the report-only group's loss.

docs.title: Avoidable-curtailment cost
docs.text: The cost is in pounds at the scaled limit of 0.9 times the earlier maximum, over leads of 12 to 36 hours, for the signed-MW six (D9 and D11 have no event rows). No interval has been computed, because the metric returns one total per series. During events D16 costs 7.76 million pounds for d, 9.87 million for c1, 9.56 million for c2, and 7.31 million for d plus widening; D5 costs 241 thousand for d and 236 thousand to 246 thousand for the other arms; D10 and D14 cost about nothing.
