Experiment 383's interim figures for the signed-MW six (21,601 rows; q95 0.774, q99 0.917, band 21.7 points) agree in direction.

Most of the failure is on rows whose target also lies inside an event. Of the 56,285 rows with an event lag, 20,742 (37%) also have their target inside an event, and their bundle q95 coverage is 0.566 (CRPS 9.21). Rows with an event lag and a target outside an event have q95 coverage 0.855 (CRPS 4.42), against 0.933 and 3.56 for rows that are clean in both ways. The failure comes from D5 (0.640), D16 (0.591), D10 (0.528), D18 (0.744), and D22 (0.796). At D12, D14, D3, D4, and D19 the event rows score 0.93 to 0.98, and D8, D9, D11, and D15 have no event rows. The event-versus-clean contrast therefore mixes a contaminated lag with a target that is itself shifted.

The upper tail fails most in the middle of a long event. The bundle's q95 coverage, with the number of events in brackets and the GAM stack beside it:

Slice Bundle GAM stack First 24 hours of the event (15) 0.777 0.876 24 hours or more after the onset, before the end (11) 0.646 0.778 Up to 7 days after the end (19) 0.885 0.928 Events of 1 to 7 days (17) 0.899 0.946 Events of over 7 days (2, descriptive only) 0.578 0.730

The depth quartile cuts come from all 115 events, so the four scored groups are not quartiles of the scored events. Depth quartiles, from shallowest Q1 to deepest Q4, hold 4, 2, 5, and 7 events and give bundle q95 coverage 0.902, 0.574, 0.931, and 0.707, so no steady depth effect shows. Slices with fewer than 5 events (Q1, Q2, over 7 days) are descriptive only. No event is shorter than 24 hours, because the mask is padded.

When the forecast is issued before an event starts and the target lies inside it, neither forecast is calibrated. Across these 19 events (all three lags clean), readings inside an event fall inside the 5th-to-95th-percentile band 70% of the time for the bundle (interval 59% to 81%) and 73% for the GAM stack, against 90% for a calibrated forecast. The bundle puts 1.6% of readings below its q01 and 7.3% above its q99, and the stack 4.6% and 11.0%, against 1% each.

The median is not clearly pulled towards the lagged level. The signed median error (median minus actual, in points of capacity) for rows whose target lies in an event is -2.43 with an event lag against -2.23 with clean lags for events of 1 to 7 days (bundle, 17 events), and -3.19 against -12.76 for events of over 7 days (2 events). The GAM stack gives -0.44 against -0.63 and +1.29 against -11.51. The bundle's median on rows with an event lag is lower than the stack's (mean signed error -2.46 against +0.41 points over all event-lag rows), with about equal mean absolute error (9.5 and 9.2 points). Prediction P4 (the bias follows the event's depth) is not supported. The with-lag and clean-lag rows differ in when the forecast was issued, so these comparisons are not like for like. The mean absolute error of the median on rows with an event lag is 9.5 points for the bundle, against 6.4 on clean rows.

Not done. The panel of synthetic injected events is missing: experiment 88 (the synthetic-transfer recovery experiment) stores only logs, and an injection needs a refit, which this analysis excludes.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean. Not computed: the stored forecasts hold quantiles only. The mean absolute error of the median appears beside the Part B numbers above.
  • Which audit triggers fired. One: the result contradicted prediction P1, and the explanation (the Kalman filter, not a level offset, carries the gap) was tested with experiment 380's stack without its filter, as Part A records.
  • Verdict. Partly supported: P2 holds at D14 only, P1 fails, P3 holds, and P4 fails. The hypothesis that the bundle lacks the Kalman filter's level tracking is supported only through the no-Kalman-filter arm, not through the offset.
  • Cadence. The monthly-refit rule does not apply, because nothing is refitted.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Part B rests on 19 events with an event lag (33 end in the scored year, 29 of those with a depth label), 2 of them over 7 days. Those two events give the lowest coverage figures (0.578 and 0.574).
  • The demand quartiles are cut on the realised readings, so a forecast that shrinks towards the mean loses on the highest quarter by construction, and the 79% and 93% shares partly reflect that choice.
  • Part A covers two single series over one winter, and the signed-MW six gap (+0.075) has an interval that includes zero.
  • Event depth comes from a hand label table, matched by Primary and onset.
  • The Kalman filter acts on the stack's own residual terms, so this analysis does not show which part of its adaptation matters. Experiment 388 (lagged-power column sets) could add a recent-level input of that kind. Experiment 389 (tail calibration) could score event-lag rows separately and test a widening rule on them.
  • The avoidable curtailment cost was not re-scored here.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A Sonnet audit confirmed every quoted number against the printed reports, found no leakage in the offset or the lag flags, and checked that every arm is scored on the same rows. Its findings and their triage:

  • Accepted, high: the event-lag contrast mixes contaminated lags with shifted targets and five Primaries. The page now says so and gives the split.
  • Accepted, medium: the count of events in Part B (19, not 33); the offset is not matched to the forecast's lead and the D14 test is underpowered; the demand quartiles use the realised outcome; the stack's median is less biased than the bundle's. All are now in the text.
  • Accepted, low: the 12:00 block wording; the stack's lower tail; the phase label; the depth cuts; the Kalman result holds at D11 and D14 only; the B2 wording.
  • Rejected: none. The empty-window offset of 0.0 is left as it is, because no window was empty.

docs.title: Does a "surprise" input let XGBoost handle load-shift events?
docs.text:
A "surprise" input does not let the monthly XGBoost demand model handle load-shift events, and it makes the forecast slightly worse on the ordinary rows. A load shift moves demand between substations, so a lagged power reading inside one misleads the model. The surprise input is the normal score of each lagged reading's probability integral transform against a lagless forecast from a first-stage model, at the Primary and at its neighbours. On rows whose lag lies inside a labelled event, the surprise columns did not help (+0.110 points of CRPS, interval -0.249 to +0.432). On rows outside events they cost +0.072 (+0.006 to +0.145), against a +0.02 tolerance. A Primary is one of the 16 primary substations scored here. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, in points of effective capacity.

The oracle did not beat the control either. The oracle O gets hand-label flags for the target and each lag. On event-lag rows it scored +0.218 points worse than the control (all 16 Primaries). The interval against seed 1 is -0.052 to +0.542, so the result is "no gain" and not "harm". BG2 scores lower than B0 (3.016 against 3.123), so headroom exists elsewhere in the model.

The explicit detector failed its pre-registered check, so whether detector state adds to surprise is untested. Arms N2, N2 without the veto, and N3 were not fitted: the manager held them after the known-answer gate failed and the surprise arms came out worse than the control. This experiment therefore answers the question about surprise columns and leaves the detector-state half open.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
All numbers are CRPS differences in points of effective capacity (above 0 is worse), days 1 to 10, raw bands. Intervals are 99.29% (Bonferroni across the seven planned contrasts at a 95% family level), resampling whole events on event slices and calendar months elsewhere. "Event-lag rows" are rows whose target lies outside an event but has a lag inside one.

Contrast Primaries Event-lag rows Rows outside events and 7 days after Seed 1 minus seed 0 of the control (noise floor) 16 +0.024 (-0.017 to +0.097) +0.001 (-0.002 to +0.006) N1 minus B0, seed 0 16 +0.110 (-0.249 to +0.432) +0.072 (+0.006 to +0.145) N1 minus B0, seed 1 16 +0.086 (-0.251 to +0.404) +0.071 (+0.006 to +0.143) O minus B0, seed 1 16 +0.194 (-0.052 to +0.542) +0.012 (+0.000 to +0.032) N0 minus B0 (own surprise only) 7 -0.038 (-0.649 to +0.578) +0.055 (+0.015 to +0.103) N1 minus N0 (neighbours) 7 +0.314 (+0.062 to +0.749) +0.028 (+0.007 to +0.054) N1-ERA5 minus N1 (hindsight weather) 7 -0.004 (-0.496 to +0.654) -0.020 (-0.064 to +0.008) N1-ERA5 minus B0, seed 1 7 +0.263 (+0.061 to +0.538) +0.063 (+0.025 to +0.108)
  • Against both control seeds every contrast has the same sign and a similar size: N1 is +0.110 and +0.086, O is +0.218 and +0.194, and the control seeds differ by +0.024. The noise floor is small beside the shifts but the event-lag intervals still include zero, so the event-lag result is "no help" and not "harm".
  • Signed-MW six and MVA-only eight, separately. N1 minus B0 on event-lag rows is +0.277 (-0.508 to +1.002) at the signed-MW six and -0.068 (-0.314 to +0.084) at the MVA-only eight. The pooled 16-Primary result is driven by D10 (+1.85) and D16 (+0.78) among the signed-MW six; leaving D10 out gives +0.049.
  • Own surprise alone (N0) moved the event-lag rows by -0.038, an 18% cut of the 0.207 oracle gap, which meets prediction P1 in size but with an interval that includes zero. The neighbour columns undid it and more (N1 minus N0 +0.314), against prediction P2.
  • The oracle gap on contaminated rows. O minus B0 is +0.218 at all 16 Primaries, +0.207 at the signed-MW six, and +0.332 at the MVA-only eight, so a hand-label flag also did not help at the MVA-only Primaries.
  • Absolute scores (all rows, days 1 to 10, signed-MW six, seed 0): B0 3.123, N1 3.229, O 3.110, BG2 3.016. These use the 150-round screening recipe, so they are not comparable to experiment 381's.
  • ERA5-fed against ENS-driven surprise (C6): N1-ERA5 is -0.020 (-0.064 to +0.008) on ordinary rows, so hindsight weather does not rescue the surprise columns.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost (GBP, all rows, signed-MW six): B0 12.65M, seed 1 12.63M, N0 13.10M, N1 13.15M, N1-ERA5 12.80M, O 12.26M, manual_heuristic 12.66M, BG2 8.35M.

docs.title: The detector and its gate
docs.text:
The pre-registered known-answer gate failed. Injected transfers at shares of capacity of 10% and 25%: recall at 25% and 2 days or more was 0.42 (gate 0.55); the veto kept 0.98 of plain hits (gate 0.95); the veto dropped 0.33 of placebo alarms (gate 0.5). At the tuned threshold (k = 2.3 ENS, 2.35 ERA5-fed) the detector marked 0 of 7 labelled transfers in the ENS version (1 of 7 in the ERA5-fed version), at 1.70 false alarms per Primary-year.

A post hoc gate in megawatts passed, and is labelled as such. The label table holds transfers of 0.71, 1.1, and 2.3 MW at the quartiles, which are small shares of a Primary's capacity. Re-running the gate with those depths gave recall 0.63, veto keeps 0.98, and veto drops 0.91 of placebo alarms. This was chosen after seeing the failure, so it does not replace the pre-registered result. It suggests the detector works at the real transfer depths and failed the gate through the choice of depths.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site (points, days 1 to 10). B0 and N1 differ by less than 0.1 at most Primaries. The one sign change is at D22 (+0.098 for B0, -0.110 for N1). The full table is in work/scores_core/printed_report.txt.
  • Mean error beside the quantile contrasts. The mean absolute error of the median moves with CRPS: N1 minus B0 +0.210 (-0.311 to +0.748) on event-lag rows, seed noise +0.025.
  • Which audit triggers fired. Two: the neighbour columns reversed the sign of prediction P2, and O came out worse than the control. A Sonnet audit of the scoring and the oracle flags found no bug. The seed-1 control shows that seed noise (+0.001 outside events) is far smaller than the +0.072 harm outside events.
  • Design target. The sweep for the three median and tail tolerances was not run (see below).

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• N2, N2 without the veto, N3 were not fitted. The manager held them. Predictions P3 and the C3, C4, C5, and C7 contrasts are therefore untested, and the lag-encroachment sweep, the P5 correlation, and the code-review check for leakage were not run as separate steps.
  • The detector's tuning window is shorter than the distillation's (2024-11 to 2025-06, because stage 1 starts in 2024-10).
  • The recipe is the 150-round screening recipe, not experiment 87's 500 rounds, so scores are not comparable to experiment 381's.
  • Two sets of Primaries. B0, N1, and O ran at all 16; N0 and N1-ERA5 at 7 (the signed-MW six plus D8), so their contrasts use those 7.
  • Event-lag rows are about 2.4% of the rows (64,006 of 2.63M at 16 Primaries) and come from 27 events; every event-lag interval is wide.
  • Scores were printed from saved rows at half precision for the 16-Primary pass (float32 except the CRPS and error columns), after the full-precision pass ran out of memory.
  • Stop rule. By the verdict in each page's front matter, experiments 89 and 90 (refuted) and 383 (not supported) count on the idea "handle load-shift events inside the XGBoost lags", and this experiment is the fourth. Experiment 5 (refuted) tests lag placement, so the manager decides whether it counts. Experiments 8, 18, and 88 (inconclusive) do not count; 390 (partly supported) does not count either, and the manager decides whether it tests the same idea.

docs.title: Data and reproduction
docs.text:
• Surprise tables for experiment 392: data/ml-experiments/00391-xgboost-lag-surprise-second-stage/surprise_tables/.
  • Boosters: .../work/boosters/<arm>/ (12 monthly refits per Primary).
  • Printed reports: .../work/scores_core/printed_report.txt and .../work/scores_subset/printed_report.txt.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00391-xgboost-lag-surprise-second-stage/; run order is stage 1, detector, fit, assemble, score, charts.

docs.title: An NRA forecast from XGBoost trained with load-shift events removed from its targets
docs.text:
Removing the labelled load-shift events from the training targets of the monthly XGBoost demand model does not stop its median forecast from following a load shift in its lagged power inputs. A load shift is a period when National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) moves a substation's load onto its neighbours. A forecast of what the substation would draw without a load shift is a normal-running-arrangement (NRA) forecast. The model is refitted monthly on each substation's half-hourly demand. We left the half-hours of 66 hand-labelled load shifts, and the 48 hours after each, out of its training targets. We compared that XGBoost model with two others: the same model trained on all half-hours, and one trained with the same number of half-hours left out in random blocks.

A synthetic load shift in the lagged power inputs moves the forecast median by about 40% of its size, with or without the mask. We added a constant step of 5% of the substation's capacity to the lagged power inputs (the reading at the forecast origin, one day earlier, and one week earlier) of half-hours that contain no real load shift. With all three inputs shifted, the median moved by about 40% of the step in every arm that has those inputs. Only the XGBoost model trained without the lagged power inputs did not move.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• The scores are interim, from a screen of four monthly folds. A fold is one refit and the month it scores: 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. Each scores 16 Primaries, leads to 336 hours, and headline days 1 to 10. Four folds give wide intervals, so no interval or 99% claim is made. Settings: colsample 1.0, one seed, and experiment 87's whole-history training window and n1h recipe. Widening means scaling the quantile spread about the median; scores are unwidened unless stated.
  • Arms.
    • R0: unmasked. Its lagged form is experiment 381's stored monthly control, reproduced to within 0.0011 of capacity at D2 and D8 (two Primaries). Experiment 402's boosters of it feed the sweep.
    • R1: the labelled events and the 48 hours after them are dropped from the training targets.
    • RC1: as many half-hours dropped at random, in blocks of the same lengths.
    • R5: experiment 391's N1 (surprise columns), not refitted, lagged form only.
    • Every arm except R5 has a lagged and a lagless form.
  • R2 and RC2 were dropped. They need the detector masks of experiment 391, which are on hold, and R1 already gave a null result.
  • Pooled CRPS over the four folds, in percentage points of effective capacity. Outside events and the 48 hours after (879,769 half-hours): lagged R0 4.214, R1 4.233, RC1 4.235, R5 4.278; lagless R0 4.950, R1 4.961, RC1 4.915. Inside events (13,494): lagged R0 25.25, R1 24.98, RC1 25.65, R5 25.50; lagless 26.45, 26.28, 26.64. In the 7 days after (46,176): lagged 5.298, 5.256, 5.376, 5.189 (R5); lagless 7.591, 7.449, 6.065. All rows (906,597): lagged 4.548, 4.563, 4.576, 4.614; lagless 5.310, 5.316, 5.259.
  • The screen rule depends on the widening, and its second half cannot be decided. Rule (a) requires CRPS outside events and the 48 hours after them to be no worse than +0.02 against the control in at least 3 of 4 folds. R1 lagged passes 2 of 4 folds and R1 lagless 1 of 4 without widening, and 3 of 4 and 2 of 4 with 1.15 widening. Rule (b) requires the lagless form to follow less labelled depth than R0 lagless in at least 3 of 4 folds. It cannot be decided, because the matched events fall in 3 of 4 folds and every arm follows about 0 of the depth. R1 is indistinguishable from RC1 on every pooled score, so the full year was not run.
  • All arms under-cover inside events. The 5% to 95% band covers 0.31 to 0.32 of readings for the lagged arms (nominal 0.90) and 0.23 for the lagless arms.
  • The avoidable-curtailment cost differs by under 2% between arms. The cost is that of curtailing generation that a correct forecast would have avoided, using experiment 383's definition, on the six Primaries with signed-MW metering (limit 0.9), and one Primary (D16) dominates it. During events: lagged R0 GBP 8.71 million, R1 GBP 8.76 million, RC1 GBP 8.77 million, R5 GBP 8.88 million; lagless R0 GBP 9.02 million, R1 GBP 9.01 million, RC1 GBP 9.07 million. In the 7 days after: lagged GBP 257 thousand, 256 thousand, 261 thousand, and 260 thousand (R5); lagless GBP 232 thousand, 234 thousand, and 231 thousand.
  • The median moves by about 40% of the step when all three lags are shifted, and the band does not widen. The lag-encroachment sweep (step of 5% of capacity added to the lag columns of clean half-hours; level k adds it to the origin lag, then also the day-earlier lag, then also the week-earlier lag; both signs; leads 0 to 240 hours). The median moves, as a share of the step: k = 1, about 0 to 2%; k = 2, 15% to 20%; k = 3, 38% to 41%, for lagged R0, R1, and RC1 in both metering groups, and within one point of one another. Lagless forms move by exactly 0 at every k, which tests the code. The 5% to 95% band width stays within 1% of its width at k = 0. Coverage of the event-level reading rises from 0.68 to 0.70 at k = 0 to 0.78 to 0.82 at k = 3, while coverage of the clean reading falls from 0.86 to 0.88 to 0.81 to 0.85. Experiment 391's N1 (R5) was not swept, because its surprise columns need recomputing from the shifted lags.
  • The injected-transfer check cannot show recovery either way. It uses 4 Primaries, the 2026-01 fold, 15 to 18 synthetic events of 0.71, 1.1, or 2.3 MW per Primary added to the training targets and lags. The mean absolute difference of the median from the clean-trained forecast is 0.79 points of capacity for the unmasked lagged model and 0.87 for the masked one, and 0.42 and 0.59 for the lagless forms. Depth recovered, the share of the injected depth that the forecast no longer follows, is -0.11 (lagged) and -0.40 (lagless). The lagless difference of 0.42 is a fit-noise floor.
  • Check 2 cannot tell the arms apart. The share of labelled depth followed, over 9 matched events in 3 folds, is 0.00 plus or minus 0.05 for every arm, including the unmasked one, because at leads beyond a day the lags sit far from the event half-hours. One merged event (D5, 2025-12-05 to 2026-01-14) is excluded.
  • Dropping the flagged half-hours changes no result. Scoring on experiment 87's observed.parquet with flagged half-hours dropped from every arm removes 173 half-hours (170 at D18 in the 2025-10 fold, 3 at D8 in the 2026-03 fold); none of the per-fold results changes.
  • Six real events are plotted. figure_events_1.svg to figure_events_6.svg draw six real labelled events across both metering groups (two are report-only Primaries), marking the start and end of each and showing the actuals, the median, and the 5% to 95% band of the unmasked lagged, unmasked lagless, and masked lagged forecasts. figure_examples.svg is a fan chart of one event.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed. The stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile score: printed by the scorer, not tabulated.
  • Audit trigger 5 (a control arm that should change nothing changes a score) fires, and one failed fit explains it. The random-block control moves the 7-day-after slice of the lagless form by 1.5 CRPS points (6.065 against 7.591 for the unmasked model). A second reviewer found that the whole gap comes from D18 in the 2026-01 fold (2,149 half-hours): there the unmasked and R1 lagless medians sit near 0.27 of capacity against an actual of 0.81, and only RC1 lagless is normal. Without D18 the lagless ordering outside events flips to 4.913 (R0), 4.920 (R1), and 4.947 (RC1). So the lagless differences between arms are not a random-block effect, and no conclusion rests on them.
  • A second reviewer re-derived the pooled scores, the sweep shares, and the row alignment from the stored forecasts and found them correct. It did not re-derive Check 2, the injected transfers, the curtailment costs, or R5. It found no training row at or after a refit time.
  • The code review ran after the first fits had started. Its fixes touched only the random-block control and events closer than 48 hours apart, and RC1 was fitted after them; R1 and the lagless R0 were fitted before them.
  • The k = 3 share varies by fold. It ranges from 33% to 50% between folds, and 38% to 41% is the pooled range by metering group.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The headline scoring actuals include half-hours that the cleaning step flagged. The feature cache comes from experiment 103's rows.parquet without the drop_reason filter; it supplies the load-shift event masks and the headline scoring actuals. The fits read experiment 87's own files, where flagged half-hours are nulls.
  • One R0 lagless fit ran on a CPU, and the rest ran on a GPU. The CPU fit (D2, 2025-10) was a speed benchmark, and its forecast matches the GPU fits' noise level.
  • Four folds and one seed limit the evidence. The screen holds only four test months. Of the 66 labelled events, 27 fall in the scored months, and 9 of those have a labelled depth.
  • The forecasts are monthly-refit forecasts, so absolute and tail numbers are monthly-schedule numbers, not weekly-refit numbers.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether an NRA forecast needs a model that is told which lags to distrust, such as one trained on synthetic events injected into its lags and targets together (the sweep shows the lags carry about 40% of a step into the median), or whether dropping the lags on suspect rows and widening the band is enough. The injected-transfer check here was too noisy to answer it; a second seed of the control would give its noise floor.

docs.title: What experiment 383 already settles
docs.text:
• 383's mask rule differs from R1's. Its lagless arm drops training rows whose valid time lies in the padded hand-filtered mask of the feature cache (24 hours of padding on each side of an event, taken from load_or_build_feature_cache). R1 here drops rows inside an event and the 48 hours after it ends, with no padding before the onset. Its refits are weekly; this experiment refits monthly. Its forecasts are therefore not comparable with R0 arm for arm.
  • Consequence for R1. The rules differ, so R1 is refitted monthly under the brief's rule (event plus 48 hours after), as R0's twin; the manager agreed on 2026-10-29. 383's stored lagless arm is not reused because its padding, its weekly cadence, and its single lagless form make it incomparable with R0 arm for arm.
  • Which NRA checks 383 reports. Check 4 (tails and avoidable-curtailment cost) on contaminated-lag rows, during events, in the 7 days after, and on all rows, and a partial check 1 (main score outside events, days 1 to 10, no lead bands). It does not report check 2 (share of labelled depth followed), check 3 (injected transfers), or the lag-encroachment sweep (its boosters were not saved). All three are new here, as are R2, R3, R4, and the random-block control.
  • Evidence read so far. 383's lagless arm lowered CRPS on contaminated rows at the signed-MW six (rests on two events) and raised it at the MVA-only eight; nulling lags (c1) did nothing.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Every arm is experiment 87's n1h XGBoost member, refitted monthly (maintainer rule, 2026-10-29), colsample_bytree and colsample_bynode fixed at 1.0, one seed, the same training rows and parameters as R0. Each arm is fitted in a lagged form (three origin lags) and a lagless form (no power lags). Weekly refits are not used, so every absolute and tail number is labelled monthly; any winner is re-checked weekly before a release claim.

  • R0: no rows dropped; the control.
  • R1: rows whose valid time lies inside a hand-labelled transfer, or within 48 hours after it ends, are dropped, using only events that ended before the fold's train_end. A ceiling, never a candidate.
  • R2: the same rule applied to half-hours the "deep and long" detector marks (not run).
  • RC1, RC2: as many rows as R1 and R2 drop, in random blocks of the same lengths, as a control for the smaller training set (RC2 not run).
  • R5: no mask; experiment 391's arm N1 with surprise columns, stored and not refitted.

  • R3, R4: the train-detect-retrain loop and R2 with neighbour surprise columns (not run).

  • Detector. Taken from experiment 391's e00391_detector.py (plan PR 41, not yet merged); if 391 has not merged when R2 is due, the file is copied into this folder with a note. The mask for a fold uses only half-hours before its train_end, and the detector's tuning months are fixed before any score is read.

  • R5 shares 391's N1 forecasts and surprise tables; the plan does not refit it. The published tables are in data/ml-experiments/00391-xgboost-lag-surprise-second-stage/surprise_tables/ (half_hourly/<site>.parquet: quantiles, u, r_mw, and the refit that predicted each row; origins/<site>.parquet: z, z_noise, r_sigma per 6-hourly origin). Each row comes from a monthly lagless fit that trained on no row at or after its refit. They cover all 16 Primaries from 2024-10-01 (D15 and D18 from 2025-03) to 2026-06-30, which spans the scored months 2025-07 to 2026-06. The same tables serve the R2 detector mask, which therefore starts in 2024-10: R2's training masks for early refits rest on under a year of detector history, and the page says so. N1 keeps the three lags, so R5 exists in the lagged form only. Experiment 391 refits with no widening and scores raw and at 1.15, which this experiment copies. N1's forecasts will be under its work/arm_preds/monthly/n1/ and its boosters under work/boosters/n1/, which the sweep reads.
  • R0 lagged reuses experiment 381's monthly control (work/arm_preds/monthly/control/, 192 files, 16 Primaries by 12 refits, origins 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-01, no 1.15 widening), as the manager allowed. The recipe matches: 381's control uses fd.input_columns(a7=False) and experiment 87's n1h configuration with common.N_ROUNDS, the same modules this experiment's fit script calls, and drops no rows. A reproduction gate confirms it before use: one refit (D2, 2025-07-01) is fitted here and must match the stored file within 0.0043 CRPS points, 383's gate. If it fails, R0 lagged is refitted. R0 lagless is always fitted here.
  • Widening. Each arm's quantiles are stored raw, and every score is reported raw and at the 1.15 widening factor, for R0 and every arm alike. The widening of 391's N1 is read from its page before any comparison with R5.
  • Porting cost: R1 and R2 change only the training targets (R2 needs the detector in the training loop, not in serving); R5 adds a stage 1 model and two column sets to serving.

docs.title: Planned contrasts
docs.text: C1 R1 minus R0. C2 R2 minus R0. C3 R2 minus R1 (does the detector mask match the oracle). C4 R5 minus R0. C5 R5 minus R2 (does surprise match the detector). C6 R1 minus Rc1. C7 R2 minus Rc2. Each is read on four slices: outside events and the 48 hours after (harm), inside events, the 7 days after, and all rows.

docs.title: Few-fold screen (manager's instruction, 2026-10-30; rule fixed before any score is read)
docs.text:
All new fits first run on four monthly refits only: 2025-10 (autumn), 2026-01 (winter), 2026-03 (spring), and 2026-06 (summer), each scoring the month to the next refit. Deviation from the common brief's screen: the training window stays experiment 87's n1h window (whole history), not 24 months, because experiment 381's stored control (R0 lagged) uses that window and reusing it saves its fits; the window is the same for every arm. R0 lagless, R1 and RC1 are fitted on the four refits; R2 and RC2 follow on the same four.

  • Advance rule. An arm advances to the other eight refits when, against its control on the same folds, (a) pooled CRPS outside events and the 48 hours after is no worse than +0.02 points in at least 3 of 4 folds, and (b) on rows inside events or the 7 days after, the lagless form follows less of the labelled depth than R0 lagless in at least 3 of 4 folds. R1 is run on the full year only when it beats RC1 on (b) in 3 of 4 folds; otherwise the control shows that the removal is not the cause and the full year is not run for R1 or RC1.
  • Noise floor. A second seed of R0 lagless on the same four folds, at two Primaries (D2, D8).
  • What the screen says. Four months give wide intervals, so screen numbers are interim and carry no 99% claim. Check 3 (injected transfers) and the sweep need only the saved boosters and run on the four folds regardless of the advance rule.

docs.title: The four NRA checks (pre-registered)
docs.text:
1. No harm outside events: arm minus R0, all 16 Primaries to 14 days, by lead band.
  2. NRA gap inside events: for the half-hours inside a labelled transfer and the 48 hours after, the median's movement from its pre-event level divided by the label table's depth (MW), as a share of capacity. Low-confidence labels are reported separately.
  3. Injected transfers: steps of known depth and duration (quartiles of the label table, 0.71, 1.1, and 2.3 MW; both signs; durations drawn from the labelled events) are added to clean periods of the training history as in the dp_nra experiment, the arm is refitted with the injected events treated as labelled (R1) or run through the detector (R2), and the share of the clean original recovered is reported per arm. Restricted to the signed-MW six and four of the MVA-only eight; the subset is fixed before looking.
  4. Tails and cost: coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99 and avoidable-curtailment cost during events, in the 7 days after, and across all rows.

docs.title: Lag-encroachment sweep
docs.text: Prediction-only, on the saved boosters of every refit (path in the front matter's size line). The three lags are ordered by recency: origin, day-earlier, week-earlier (the exact times come from experiment 87's origin_lags). Levels k = 0 to 3. A step of depth D (2%, 5%, 10% of capacity and the three quartile depths; both signs) is added to every lag inside the synthetic event. For R5 and R4 the surprise and neighbour columns are recomputed from the shifted lags, with the neighbour carrying the opposite step. Cases (a) event under way and (b) event ended are reported separately, by lead band, per group and per Primary. The lagless forms must show share 0 and no widening, which tests the code. A few real labelled events chosen by a rule fixed here (the longest event per Primary with high confidence) are compared with the synthetic ones.

docs.title: Time series plots of real events (maintainer, 2026-10-30)
docs.text: At least 6 plots, spread over both metering groups (the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight), each for one real labelled event from the corrected label table. Each plot marks the event's start and end and shows the actuals, the median, and the 5% to 95% band of R0, R1, and R5, in the lagged and lagless forms where both exist, from the forecast origin one day before the onset. The events are chosen by a rule fixed before looking: for each of the two groups, the three events with the largest labelled depth that fall inside the four screen folds (fewer if fewer exist, said on the page). Plots follow the dataviz skill, label substations by anonymised letters, and name no generator.

docs.title: Also reported
docs.text: Per Primary, worst Primary, per group (signed-MW six, MVA-only eight, D15 and D18 report-only), labelled events per Primary and per slice, D2 and D4 as placebos, the mean of the median minus the mean forecast per site, and which audit triggers fired. Figures follow the dataviz skill and show no metered generator's name or ID.

docs.title: Order and compute
docs.text: R0 and R1 first, then RC1, then the checks, the sweep, and the injected-transfer fits. The fits ran as three single-thread GPU processes (the sweep on CPU), each under a 16 GB memory limit.

docs.title: Caveat: flagged exact-zero half-hours (manager, 2026-10-30)
docs.text:
The fits are clean; the scoring actuals are not yet. The fits read training targets from common.ENS_TRAIN_PATH and lags from common.load_series_arrays (the ERA5 file and experiment 87's own inputs/observed.parquet), where flagged half-hours are nulls. The feature cache from experiment 103's rows.parquet, which has no drop_reason filter, enters only the load-shift event masks and the scoring actuals (experiment 377's actuals_and_context). About 622 flagged exact-zero Primary half-hours (the manager's figure, to be re-counted here) therefore sit in the scored actuals, identically for every arm, so contrasts between arms are like-for-like while absolute scores include them. The scorer takes the actuals source as a parameter and reports both: the headline uses experiment 381's actuals (experiment 377's actuals_and_context), so the numbers stay comparable; the check column uses experiment 87's observed.parquet, with the flagged half-hours dropped from every arm (the same rows for all arms) and the count of dropped half-hours reported per fold and per Primary. Which source becomes the standard is the maintainer's choice, via the XGBoost Discuss session, and the merge waits for it.

Flagged-count check column, measured by the scorer before any arm is read. Of the half-hours in the four screen folds that are finite in the cache, 173 are null in observed.parquet: 170 at D18 in the 2025-10 fold, 3 at D8 in the 2026-03 fold, and none in the 2026-01 and 2026-06 folds. That is far below the manager's figure of about 622, which presumably spans more than these folds. The event masks still come from dp_features (experiment 103's rows); only the masks do, because the fits read training rows, lags, and inference inputs from experiment 87's own files.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: Builds on experiment 383's oracle-mask arms, experiment 75 (a training-target mask in the weekly XGBoost model) and experiment 44 (the share of the best guess's score a perfect detector could gain), experiment 100 (dropped half-hours in XGBoost), experiment 391's detector and surprise columns, and the dp_nra experiment's injected-transfer scoring.

docs.title: Does apparent power's fold of signed power explain the GAM stack's gap at eight Primaries?
docs.text:
Folding the signed series moves the stack's gap to BG2 by only -0.015 points pooled, so the fold does not explain the gap. We asked whether the generalised additive model (GAM) stack of experiment 377 trails BG2 (the best-guess forecast of experiment 87, which production does not run) at the eight Primary substations that report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA-only) because apparent power is the absolute value of a signed flow. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation, labelled D2 to D22 here. Six other Primaries report signed megawatts (MW).

A score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), estimated from 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity (percent of the Primary's effective capacity in MW). A negative stack-minus-BG2 difference favours the stack. Reactive power is assumed zero at the MVA-only Primaries, and nothing was fitted. The stack is "stack without S below 168 h" of experiment 377: it has no two-number solar summary below 168 hours.

We took the stored forecasts of the stack, BG2, and the manual heuristic (NGED's rule of thumb), and replaced both the forecast and the observation by their absolute values at the six signed-MW Primaries. We also measured how often each Primary's demand falls below 10% of its peak (the "near-zero share") and how the stack's gap varies with that share. Folding barely moves the gap, and the gap does not follow the near-zero share with a statistically clear relation. D5 is the exception, where folding lowers the gap by 0.092. D8 is reported on its own throughout.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Verdict: not supported. The hypothesis counted as supported only if both predictions held, and neither did. The stack-minus-BG2 gap over days 1 to 10 reproduces experiment 377's: -0.068 (99% interval -0.280 to +0.138) over the six signed-MW Primaries and +0.344 (+0.093 to +0.595) over the eight MVA-only Primaries.
  • Prediction 1 (the gap grows with the near-zero share): not shown. Across the 14 countable Primaries the Spearman correlation is +0.53 (95% bootstrap over Primaries -0.11 to +0.92). It is +0.41 without D8, +0.79 within the eight MVA-only Primaries, and +0.41 within the six signed-MW Primaries. The interval includes zero. The near-zero share is 0 at D2, D3, D4, D19, D11, and D14, under 0.1% at D9, D16, and D21, and positive at D12 (16.4%), D8 (5.7%), D10 and D5 (4.6% each), and D22 (3.0%). Pooled over the 14, the gap is +1.31 on near-zero half-hours and +0.14 elsewhere (descriptive).
  • Prediction 2 (the gap is more positive on the folded target): refuted. Pooled over the six, stack minus BG2 is -0.068 on the signed target and -0.083 on the folded target (99% intervals -0.280 to +0.138 and -0.284 to +0.107). The folded minus signed difference is -0.015 (-0.034 to -0.002), so folding makes the stack look slightly better, the opposite of the prediction. Only D5 moves (-0.092, 95% interval -0.180 to -0.024). D10 moves by +0.001, and D9, D11, D14, and D16 move by under 0.001. Against manual_heuristic the pooled gap is -0.657 signed and -0.671 folded. The mean absolute error (MAE) of the median is 5.03 for the stack and 5.24 for BG2 on the folded target, and 5.06 and 5.24 on the signed target. D10 flows backwards in 0.7% of half-hours and D5 never does, so D10's folded series is nearly its signed series.
  • D8's gap is not a near-zero effect. D8's gap is +1.61: +1.68 on half-hours above 10% of peak and +0.43 inside the near-zero half-hours, mostly at 30% to 70% of peak. At D12 (gap +0.76) the gap is +1.72 inside and +0.58 elsewhere. At D22 (gap +0.36) it is +2.47 inside and +0.29 elsewhere.
  • Contrast 3 (error shape). At the eight MVA-only Primaries the stack's median forecast is on average 16.0 points too high when the observation is under 10% of the Primary's peak (8.7 at the six signed-MW Primaries), and the gap to BG2 there is +1.54 (+0.69 at the six). The largest 5% of absolute residuals fall on half-hours under 20% of peak 33% of the time at the eight MVA-only Primaries (12% of all their rows) and 18% of the time at the six signed-MW Primaries (7% of all their rows). The sign estimate of experiment 387 joined to none of the stack's rows, so the residual is not split by flow direction.
  • Contrast 4 (other explanations). The stack-minus-BG2 gap on days 1 to 3 and on days 8 to 10 is +0.39 (+0.15 to +0.61) and +0.34 (+0.05 to +0.67) at the eight MVA-only Primaries, and -0.15 (-0.38 to +0.08) and -0.02 (-0.27 to +0.19) at the six signed-MW Primaries (99% intervals). Experiment 384 stores the number of generators at each Primary's bulk supply point, not their share of capacity: D12, D22, D8, D14, D16, and D5 each have 8 generators, so the count does not separate the large gaps from the small. Experiment 386 found the stack trailing BG2 by +1.02 (+0.68 to +1.43) at two bulk supply points and +2.01 (+1.41 to +2.60) at two grid supply points, which are sums of many Primaries' demand; this analysis does not decide between aggregation level and the fold.
  • Floor against the benchmarks (demand-v2, days 1 to 10). The floor requires a Primary's CRPS to be no greater than manual_heuristic's and no more than 1.10 times BG2's. The stack fails it at D12 (1.113 times BG2's CRPS) and at D8 (1.212 times BG2, and 9.23 against the heuristic's 8.31). The other 12 Primaries pass; D22 is the nearest at 1.095.
  • Tail coverage, stack against BG2 (days 1 to 10). At the six signed-MW Primaries, coverage at q05 is 0.050 to 0.087 for the stack and 0.036 to 0.061 for BG2 (target 0.05), and at q99 0.956 to 0.996 and 0.950 to 0.985 (target 0.99). At the eight MVA-only Primaries the stack's q05 coverage is 0.056 to 0.079 and its q99 coverage 0.970 to 0.988. The stack's lower tail is too narrow, as in experiment 377.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Zero at every Primary: the stored mean equals the stage-2 median by construction (experiment 377), so no independent mean-forecast contrast exists.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile score. The MAE contrast points the same way as the folded CRPS contrast (stack better than BG2, slightly more so folded).
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the group gaps, the near-zero shares, the inside and outside gaps at D8, D12, and D22, the folded gaps, and the Spearman correlations from the raw stored files and matched every number.
  • Triggers. None of the seven triggers of the audit rule fired. Removing D8 lowers the MVA-only gap from +0.344 to +0.178 (experiment 377), and the verdict does not depend on it.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Four of the six signed-MW Primaries rarely come near zero, so the folded test has little power. The test cannot run at D12, which reverses flow, because its series is already folded. Experiments 152, 372, and 374 found a fold gain at D12 only, with an interval including zero over a full year.
  • The folded quantiles are the sorted absolute values of the 11 quantiles. This is exact where the whole forecast sits on one side of zero and understates the mass at zero otherwise.
  • No Primary has a stored reactive-power series alongside its active power (the prior-work check searched experiments 79, 110, 152, and 358), so true MVA was not built.
  • One option for a next test is a term for the lowest-demand state at the MVA-only Primaries, where the median forecast is 16.0 points of capacity too high under 10% of peak.

docs.title: Does the ensemble mean or the ensemble spread give the simple XGBoost demand model its gain at all 16 Primaries?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the mean of the 51 ensemble weather members gives the simple XGBoost demand forecast its gain from those members, and the spread of the members adds almost nothing. Here "the simple XGBoost demand forecast" is the monthly-refitted XGBoost model of the half-hourly demand of 16 Primary substations. We gave that model, as extra inputs, only the mean across the 51 members of the temperature and of the shortwave radiation (the mean-only arm), or only their standard deviation (the spread-only arm). The error score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in percentage points of each substation's effective capacity. The mean-only arm lowers it by 0.052 points at the 6 substations whose meters record the direction of flow (the signed-MW six) and by 0.029 points at the 8 whose meters record apparent power only (the MVA-only eight). The spread-only arm lowers it by 0.001 and 0.008 points. Neither input fixes the tails: on cold nights the 95% quantile of the forecast still lies above only 0.77 to 0.78 of outcomes at the signed-MW six, against a nominal 0.95. The verdict is supported: the mean-only arm recovers about 110% of the gain of experiment 389's four-column arm at the signed-MW six and 82% at the MVA-only eight, and the spread-only arm recovers about 1% and 24%.

Experiment 389 found that four extra input columns (the mean and the standard deviation across the 51 members, each for temperature and for shortwave) lowered the CRPS by 0.047 and 0.035 points at the two groups, and that the gain looked like an effect of the mean. This experiment splits the four columns into two arms of two columns each. Both arms use the recipe of the stored monthly forecast of experiment 87 (12 monthly refits at all 16 Primaries). The control is that stored forecast, which receives none of the extra columns. All quantiles are widened about the median by a factor of 1.15, as in experiment 87. Experiment 389's four-column arm is the second comparison. The hypothesis and two predictions (see the front matter) were written after experiment 389's scores and before either arm was scored. The mean-only score was read before the spread-only arm was scored, so the spread-only comparison is not blind.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are in points of effective capacity for forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead on the half-hours of July 2025 to June 2026 that every arm scores (3,844,106 half-hours, a different set from experiment 389's because the arm set differs, so S0M and S1M differ from experiment 389's printed values in the third decimal). Intervals are 99% intervals from resampling whole calendar months, 20,000 resamples. All numbers come from e00394_score.py and e00394_bins.py.

Group Arm CRPS MAE of median q05 q95 q99 Signed-MW six Stored monthly member (S0M) 3.121 5.375 0.034 0.932 0.986 Signed-MW six Four columns (S1) 3.074 5.284 0.037 0.925 0.985 Signed-MW six Mean only 3.069 5.281 0.037 0.926 0.985 Signed-MW six Spread only 3.121 5.373 0.034 0.930 0.985 Signed-MW six BG2 3.016 5.244 0.045 0.932 0.976 MVA-only eight Stored monthly member (S0M) 3.847 6.855 0.043 0.955 0.995 MVA-only eight Four columns (S1) 3.812 6.796 0.049 0.949 0.994 MVA-only eight Mean only 3.818 6.808 0.048 0.950 0.994 MVA-only eight Spread only 3.839 6.847 0.043 0.953 0.995 MVA-only eight BG2 3.788 6.766 0.042 0.955 0.995

The q05, q95, and q99 columns are the share of outcomes below that quantile (nominal 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99).

  • Mean-only arm. Mean only minus S0M: -0.052 (-0.082 to -0.009) at the signed-MW six, -0.029 (-0.044 to -0.013) at the MVA-only eight, and -0.041 (-0.057 to -0.025) at the eight without D8. Leaving out any one Primary leaves each contrast negative with a 99% interval excluding zero (-0.050 to -0.054 at the six; -0.024 to -0.041 at the eight). Mean only lowers the CRPS at 14 of 16 Primaries; it is worse at D8 (+0.058) and D15 (+0.403, report only).
  • Spread-only arm. Spread only minus S0M: -0.001 (-0.011 to +0.013) at the six, -0.008 (-0.014 to -0.002) at the eight, and -0.009 (-0.014 to -0.003) at the eight without D8. The spread-only arm lowers the CRPS at 12 of 16 Primaries (11 if D16, where the change is -0.0005, counts as zero).
  • Mean and spread together. Mean only minus S1: -0.005 (-0.019 to +0.006) at the six and +0.006 (+0.002 to +0.010) at the eight. Spread only minus S1: +0.047 (+0.011 to +0.072) at the six and +0.027 (+0.010 to +0.042) at the eight. The mean-only arm recovers about 110% of the S1 gain at the six (0.052 of 0.047) and 82% at the eight (0.029 of 0.035), so the prediction of at least 70% holds. The spread-only arm recovers 1% at the six and 24% at the eight (0.008 of 0.035), so the prediction of under 30% holds.
  • Tails. A negative change in absolute coverage error means the share of outcomes below the quantile moved towards nominal. Against S0M at the signed-MW six, the change at q95 is +0.006 for the mean-only arm (99% interval -0.006 to +0.012) and +0.002 for the spread-only arm (-0.004 to +0.006). At q05 it is -0.003 for the mean-only arm (-0.005 to -0.001), a small gain from 0.034 to 0.037 towards 0.05. At the MVA-only eight the change at q95 is -0.004 and -0.001. At q99 the intervals include zero except at the MVA-only eight (-0.0004, -0.0009 to -0.0000, and -0.0002, -0.0006 to -0.0000). No arm moves any coverage by more than 0.006.
  • Cold nights. The share of outcomes below q95 at the six is 0.775 (S0M), 0.769 (S1), 0.776 (mean only), 0.769 (spread only), and 0.800 (BG2), over 44,370 half-hours; at the eight it is 0.851, 0.850, 0.855, 0.849, and 0.845. Mean only lowers the CRPS on cold nights by 0.086 (six) and 0.113 (eight) against S0M; spread only by -0.006 and 0.032.
  • Sunny half-hours (April to June). Mean only lowers the CRPS by 0.131 (six) and 0.070 (eight); spread only raises it by 0.011 (six) and 0.017 (eight).

docs.title: Spread terciles
docs.text:
The maintainer expected spread to help when weather uncertainty is high and to calibrate sunny summer half-hours. We cut each Primary's rows, within each of the five lead bands of experiment 389, into terciles of the ensemble's temperature spread at the row's lead, and scored every arm in each tercile. All-hour rows are the stored half-hours of days 1 to 10 with a finite actual (not the scorer's shared set). Intervals resample the calendar months of the valid time (13 months, because leads run past 30 June 2026).

  • High spread does not favour the spread columns. At the signed-MW six, spread only minus S0M at q95 is -0.003, +0.007, and +0.011 points in the low, middle, and high temperature-spread terciles (99% intervals -0.016 to +0.013, -0.004 to +0.023, and +0.002 to +0.022), so it is worse in the high tercile. At the eight it is -0.010, -0.004, and +0.001.
  • The mean's gain is also largest in the low-spread tercile. At q95, mean only minus S0M is -0.023, -0.011, and -0.013 at the six and -0.014, -0.011, and -0.007 at the eight; the interval of every tercile at the six includes zero, as does the high tercile at the eight.
  • q05 and q95 coverage barely moves across terciles. At the six, the share below q05 for S0M is 0.044, 0.035, and 0.036 across the three terciles; the arms move it by at most 0.004. The share below q95 is 0.947, 0.937, and 0.931 for S0M; the arms move it by at most 0.008.
  • June to August sunny half-hours: no arm calibrates them. Sunny means the ensemble-mean shortwave is in the top quarter of all of a Primary's June-to-August rows, night included, so the selection is roughly the brighter half of daytime rows. Terciles cut the shortwave spread within each Primary and lead band. At the six, the stored monthly member's q95 covers 0.98, 0.97, and 0.97 of outcomes in the low, middle, and high shortwave-spread terciles, above the nominal 0.95, and the mean-only arm covers 0.970, 0.966, and 0.965; the q95 pinball loss falls by 0.047, 0.036, and 0.051 points with the mean, and by 0.012, rises by 0.004, and rises by 0.009 with the spread. The scored year holds only 3 June-to-August months (July and August 2025, June 2026), so the intervals resample whole days (99 to 102 days per tercile); they are too narrow to trust as a month-level claim.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not computed: the stored frames hold quantiles and no mean. The mean absolute error of the median falls in step with the CRPS (mean only 5.281 against 5.375 at the six), so the quantile and median contrasts point the same way.
  • Triggers. Audit trigger 2 (a result that contradicts an earlier experiment's finding) fired. Experiment 371 found that an ensemble-mean arm added 0.007 points, and this experiment finds 0.052 and 0.029. A possible explanation is that experiment 371 changed only the prediction inputs while the arms here train on the columns. This experiment did not test that explanation.
  • Audit and review. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the pipeline these arms share with the four-column arm in experiment 389. It re-derived the four-column contrasts from the stored forecasts and found no use of a later forecast run or later weather in the training rows or the prediction rows. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed this experiment's code after scoring had started and found no blocking problem.
  • Leaving one Primary out. Leaving out any one Primary does not flip the sign of the mean-only contrast. For the spread-only arm at the signed-MW six the leave-one-out contrasts range from -0.003 to +0.001, with intervals that include zero, which matches the pooled contrast.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• No fresh S0M refit. The control is the stored monthly member, as in experiment 389; experiment 389's audit found that a fresh refit of it at D5 and D12 (4 of 192 fits) differed from the stored member by -0.002 to +0.004 CRPS, while S1 differed from it by -0.143 to +0.340 at the same refits.
  • Cleaned data and the short-history cut. Experiment 87's pipeline, which these arms inherit, predates the standing practices that clean the power data of substation_zero half-hours and cut D15 and D18 before 2025-03-01, so the result holds for the stored recipe and not for a cleaned one.
  • Four columns, two variables. The mean-only and spread-only arms each hold the columns of temperature and of shortwave together, so the page cannot say which variable carries the gain.
  • Lead range. All scores run to days 1 to 10; days 11 to 14 are in the log.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: The mean of the 51 members carries the gain, which suggests testing the mean of each weather variable the model already uses, and the temperature mean without the shortwave mean, to see which variable carries it. The cold-night under-coverage stays open, because no ensemble input moved it.

docs.title: A level state, a winter re-score, spread bins, a short-history anchor, and lag-event harm, all on stored forecasts
docs.text:
A level filter on the weekly XGBoost model's own residuals closes part of the model's gap to the GAM stack at D14 and widens it at D11, so the filter is not the whole explanation. The weekly bundle is experiment 381's XGBoost model (solar summary, sunny flag, 1-year half-life). The GAM stack is experiment 377's stack without its smoothing stage S below 168 hours. D11 and D14 are two of the 16 Primaries (primary substations) scored here. The filter follows experiment 136's two-state filter, which in turn follows the variational noise filter of de Vilmarest and Wintenberger (2022). Experiment 390 found that a rolling median offset does not copy the filter.

Terms used below. A load-shift event is a labelled period in which load was moved between Primaries. The signed-MW six (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) are the Primaries whose readings are signed megawatts, and the MVA-only eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22) report apparent power only. D15 and D18 have under a year of history and are reported separately. K0 to K4 are the Part A arms. Experiment 383's arm d is the plain weekly member, c1 drops the lags that lie inside an event, and c2 serves a lagless model on rows with a lag inside an event and arm d elsewhere. S0M and S1M are experiment 389's arms (S1M adds the ensemble mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation as columns; S0M does not). Economy 7 is a UK off-peak electricity tariff. An event's depth is its labelled change in load in megawatts, and the padded mask is experiment 390's mask, which extends each labelled event by 24 hours on each side.

Nothing in this experiment is refitted. Every number re-scores forecasts that earlier experiments stored, so the monthly-refit rule does not apply. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity (1 point is 1% of the Primary's effective capacity), for days 1 to 10 unless stated, on fold_a_daily_gap_v1 under demand-v1. Intervals resample whole months, or whole events in Part F. "Raw" means the stored forecast without widening, and _w means widened by the factor 1.15 about the median.

docs.title: Part A: a level state on the weekly bundle
docs.text:
The stack's two-state filter closes 41% of the bundle's D14 gap and widens its D11 gap. K0 is the stored weekly bundle. K1 runs experiment 377's two-state filter (a level plus an AR(1) transient, one filter per hour band, pooled noise settings from e00377_run.noise_hyper) on the bundle's residuals, using readings at least 3.5 hours before the origin. K2 is a one-state random-walk level with a gain and a per-half-hour decay fitted per Primary on an expanding window (prior gain 0.05, decay 0.998 where there is no training data), and K3 pools K2's two numbers across the 16 Primaries.

Primary K0 K1 K2 K3 GAM stack D11 2.577 2.672 2.615 2.679 2.429 D14 2.510 2.387 2.45 2.44 2.209
  • K1 at D11 is worse than K0 by +0.095 points (interval +0.035 to +0.152).
  • K1 closes 41% of the D14 gap, K2 closes 19%, and K3 closes 25%.
  • On the signed-MW six, K0 scores 3.023, K2 3.001, K3 3.000, K1 3.043, and the GAM stack 2.949.
  • On the MVA-only eight, K0 scores 3.721, K2 3.743, and K1 3.804.
  • In the 0 to 24 h band on the signed-MW six, the raw scores are K0 2.564, K1 2.457, K2 2.399, and the GAM stack 2.293 (widened by 1.15: K0 2.584, K2 2.429).
  • Raw cold-night q95 coverage on the signed-MW six rises from 0.736 (K0) to 0.772 (K2) and 0.812 (K1), against 0.880 for the GAM stack (widened by 1.15: 0.773, 0.806 and 0.841).
  • K4 (the GAM stack without its filter, plus K2, on six Primaries) scores 2.898 against 2.954 for the stack on the same rows, so K4 beats the stack by 0.056 points, more than P3's 0.03 band, in the favourable direction. K4 has no interval, and it is worse than the stack at D14 (2.263 against 2.211).

P1 and P2 fail, P3 and P4 hold, so the porting threshold is not met. P1 fails: K1 closes at least half of the gap at neither D11 nor D14. P2 fails: K2 closes under half at D14 and widens the D11 gap. P3 holds: K4 recovers the stack's score within 0.03 points. P4 holds: the 0 to 24 h band improves, so the transient does not hurt it. The porting threshold is not met.

docs.title: Part B: winter re-score
docs.text: Economy 7 columns change nothing, and the ensemble mean and spread columns help cold nights. Against monthly/control, the Economy 7 arm differs by -0.000 on the winter signed-MW six (interval -0.004 to +0.004), and by +0.005 at D14 in winter (+0.001 to +0.012). Experiment 389's S1M (mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation as columns) differs by -0.040 on the signed-MW six (-0.065 to -0.010), -0.031 on the MVA-only eight, -0.058 at D11, -0.032 at D14, and -0.070 (six) and -0.144 (eight) on cold nights. S0M equals the control. S1M closes 36% of the D11 gap and 7% of the D14 gap; the solar arm closes 12% of the D14 gap. Cold-night q95 coverage on the signed-MW six is 0.734 for the control, 0.726 for S1M, and 0.879 for the GAM stack. P5's top-quartile and pooled clauses are not scored here, and S1M's pooled interval excludes zero, so P5 is untested. In winter the S1M difference on the signed-MW six is -0.019 (-0.093 to +0.091), against -0.040 over the year, so winter does not carry the gain.

docs.title: Part C: spread bins
docs.text: S1M's gain over S0M does not rise with temperature spread. Experiment 394's tables were not available, so only the top-decile and regime bins are scored. S1M minus S0M by temperature-spread bin: lower tercile -0.038, middle -0.017, upper -0.020, top decile -0.019 (-0.053 to +0.018). By the share of the 51 ensemble members below 5 °C at the week's coldest day: all warm -0.023, 0 to 25% +0.021, split +0.015, 75 to 100% -0.067, all cold -0.075. The gain therefore sits where the ensemble agrees on cold weather, not where it is split. All-row q95 coverage moves from 0.921 to 0.913, and the ratio of 90% band width to absolute error from 3.74 to 3.62. The intervals are 95%. P6 fails.

docs.title: Part D: short-history level anchor
docs.text: A 7-day level anchor cuts D15's median bias and harms the other 14 Primaries. The anchor is the median of the bundle's own residuals over the previous 7, 14 or 28 days, shrunk by the days of history over the window length. At D15 (4 scored months) the score falls from 15.186 to 13.593 (7 days), 14.071 (14 days), and 14.151 (28 days); the 7-day change is -1.593 (-3.574 to +0.609), and the mean signed error falls from -17.0 to -4.8 points (7 days), -4.7 (14 days), and -5.9 (28 days). D18 (6 scored months) gains nothing. On the other 14 Primaries the 7-day anchor changes the score by +0.101 (+0.049 to +0.153), the 14-day anchor by +0.069 (+0.006 to +0.137), and the 28-day anchor by +0.017 (-0.025 to +0.057). P7's bias clause holds for the 14-day anchor (a 72% cut), and its no-harm clause fails. The 7-day score change at D15 is within its interval. Part A's filters improve D15 more than the anchors do (K0 15.186, K1 13.380, K2 13.445), so the anchor is not the only fix.

docs.title: Part E: lag-encroachment sweep on experiment 391's boosters
docs.text: Shifting lag readings into an event moves the median by up to a third of the step and leaves the band as wide. Experiment 391's stored b0 boosters, 16 Primaries and 86,907 distinct rows per setting (one run on the 15th of each of 12 months), were given lag columns shifted by the event step for k = 1, 2 and 3 of the origin, day and week lags. The median moves by 1.3%, 17.3% and 36.8% of the step. The 90% band is 1.005, 1.009 and 1.008 times as wide as with clean lags. The clean reading lies inside the 90% band on 0.875 of rows at k = 0 and 0.826 at k = 3, and the event-level reading inside it on 0.681 and 0.784. The q95 reaches the event level on 0.701 of rows at k = 0 and 0.812 at k = 3. No lagless booster is stored, no n1 sweep was run, and no real-event comparison was made.

docs.title: Part F: score on unpadded hand-labelled load-shift events
docs.text:
On rows whose target lies outside every event, a power lag inside an event raises the score by about 1 point for the weekly bundle on the signed-MW six, and by 1.7 to 2.0 points for the GAM stack. Events are the 184 merged hand-labelled intervals of briefs/sw_block_detector_label_table.csv, unpadded. No forecast predicts an event, so a median that stays at normal running is the desired behaviour; the harm table therefore scores rows whose target lies outside the event, and coverage inside events is description only. Harm is the CRPS of rows with one to three lags in an event, minus the same Primaries' rows with clean lags; intervals resample whole events (34 events for the signed-MW six, 25 for the MVA-only eight). Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped (filtered, the headline); the unfiltered point estimates differ in the third decimal and the interval bounds by up to 0.1. The baseline is each Primary's overall clean mean. Matching it on Primary, month and lead band gives +1.06 (-0.05 to +2.48) for the bundle and +1.25 (-0.01 to +2.89) for the GAM stack on the six, so the reading that the interval excludes zero is fragile.

Forecast Six: harm (interval) Eight: harm (interval) Six, 3 lags: q95 coverage Weekly bundle +1.03 (+0.05 to +2.32) +0.37 (-0.18 to +1.05) 0.831 Monthly control +0.57 (-0.03 to +1.49) +0.50 (-0.13 to +1.25) 0.818 GAM stack +1.67 (+0.06 to +3.77) +1.97 (+0.46 to +3.80) 0.840 Experiment 383 d +0.97 (+0.08 to +2.10) +0.47 (-0.17 to +1.24) 0.822 Experiment 383 c1 +0.79 (+0.09 to +1.74) +0.44 (-0.14 to +1.19) 0.735 Experiment 383 c2 +0.36 (-0.15 to +1.15) +0.60 (+0.02 to +1.38) 0.779

With clean lags the bundle's q95 coverage is 0.928 on the six.

The median sits about halfway to the event reading when no lag is in the event and nearly at the event reading when lags are (sign-free). The depth missed per event is |median(actual − median forecast)| over |depth|, where 0 means the median reaches the event reading and 1 means it stays at normal running. For the weekly bundle it is 0.50 with no lag in the event (52 events), 0.19 with one or two (27), and 0.16 with three (16). The monthly control scores 0.42, 0.20 and 0.12; the GAM stack 0.63, 0.30 and 0.27; experiment 383's c2 0.39, 0.15 and 0.14. Lag encroachment is therefore consistent with dragging the median into the event. The 90% band stays about as wide (the bundle's median width is 23.1, 26.1 and 24.2 points).

The 24-hour padded mask gives a lower coverage figure. On the bundle's signed-MW six, rows with a lag in the padded mask and a target outside it have q95 coverage 0.786 (interval 0.506 to 0.932, 13 events); the unpadded labels give 0.902 (0.819 to 0.960, 34 events). The two row sets differ (17,111 and 29,631 rows) and the intervals overlap, so the data do not show that padding changes the result. Of 36,718 padded-contaminated rows, 8,485 have no lag in an unpadded event.

Curtailment cost was not re-scored in this experiment. Part H below corrects the label table's sign column; the harm table, coverage and the sign-free depth above do not depend on it. Experiment 390's event-fan figure is redrawn below with the event masks shaded.

docs.title: Part H: the label table's sign convention
docs.text:
In the label table, every "X to Y" row has a positive depth_mw and means that X's power falls. The audit measures, for each labelled event and each Primary it names, the mean cleaned power in the event's first 48 hours (or the whole event if shorter) minus the mean in the 48 hours before the onset. Power is read through studies.power.scan_power, so flagged zeros are dropped. The step is a plain difference of means, with no weather correction. Of the 112 rows with an end time and a depth, 104 are measurable.

  • At X, the measured step is negative in 36 of the 44 measurable "X to Y" rows.
  • In the other 60 measurable rows, the first-named Primary's step has the sign of depth_mw in 53.
  • The rule "X to Y: X falls; any other row: the sign of depth_mw" matches the measured sign in 89 of 104 events. The earlier convention (first-named Primary takes the sign of depth_mw in every row) matched 61 of 104.
  • 51 of 112 signs are corrected: 43 from measurement and 8 from the rule where no step could be measured. The corrected copy is ml-experiments/00395-.../sw_block_detector_label_table_corrected.csv.
  • The measured step has a median of 0.63 times the labelled |depth_mw|. The labelled size is kept, because a 48-hour mean dilutes a drop that deepens later.
  • Among 72 events with a measurable second Primary, the two steps have opposite signs in 44, so load conservation between the pair is only partly visible in 48-hour means.

With the corrected signs, the median follows the event about halfway with no lag in the event and nearly fully with three. The share followed is 1 − (actual − median forecast) / signed depth, where 0 means the median sits at normal running and 1 means it sits at the event reading. Medians over events, for 0, 1 or 2, and 3 lags in the event:

Forecast 0 lags (52 events) 1 or 2 lags (27) 3 lags (16) Weekly bundle 0.52 0.83 0.94 Monthly control 0.60 0.83 0.94 GAM stack 0.40 0.88 0.97 Experiment 383 d 0.63 0.85 0.95 Experiment 383 c1 0.67 0.87 0.92 Experiment 383 c2 0.70 0.85 0.95

The sign-free depth missed in Part F, 0.50, 0.19 and 0.16 for the bundle, becomes 0.48, 0.17 and 0.06 as a share of the depth not followed. With the corrected sign, the median of actual minus forecast has the sign of the event in 90% of events with no lag in the event (it was 69%). Part E does not use labelled depth, so the correction does not change it.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Which actuals the scorer read. Experiment 103's rows.parquet, through the feature cache. It carries no drop_reason filter, so 38 unique scored half-hours of 256,981 (0.015%) are flagged substation_zero, all exactly zero: D21 13, D8 7, D22 5, D9 5, D12 4, D18 3, D16 1. The 622 flagged rows counted elsewhere are the cleaned table's flagged rows over the year, not scored half-hours. Part F drops the flagged rows and also reports the unfiltered numbers. Parts A to E score unfiltered; the 38 rows cannot move a mean by more than their share of the rows.
  • Flagged zeros inside labelled events. 6 inside unpadded events (D22 5, D8 1) and 5 inside the 24 h padded mask (D22 5).
  • Median minus mean. Not computed: the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Error of the mean beside each contrast. Every contrast above carries its interval. Contrasts without an interval are descriptive.
  • Which audit triggers fired. P1 and P2 contradicted the hypothesis, and P7's no-harm clause failed.
  • Verdict. Partly supported: P3 and P4 hold; P1, P2 and P6 fail; P5 and P7 are untested as written.
  • Cadence. Nothing is refitted, so the monthly-refit rule does not apply.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• D15 has 4 scored months and D18 has 6, so Part D rests on very few months.
  • Part C could not be set beside experiment 394's tables, and its spread bins are ranked over all leads before days 1 to 10 are kept (38% lower, 33% middle, 21% upper, 8% top decile of the scored rows). Ranked within days 1 to 10, the bins read lower -0.046, upper -0.012, top decile -0.023. S1M's q95 coverage falls in every bin by 0.005 to 0.013, so P6, which concerns coverage, is judged on CRPS only here.
  • Part F draws no per-forecast chart of coverage by lag count and event length; the tables carry it.
  • The Part F events for D5 overlap in the padded mask, which merges later events.
  • Experiment 391's n1, n0, and o boosters were not swept, and no lagless booster exists.
  • The measured event sizes use 48-hour means, so they dilute drops that deepen later; the corrected table keeps the labelled size.
  • K1's D14 gain (-0.122, interval -0.354 to +0.059) includes zero and sits in winter rows. K2 also worsens D11 slightly (+0.038, +0.000 to +0.074).
  • K3 chose the prior (0.05, 0.998) in all 192 Primary-months, and K2 chose it in 91, so the prior may have been tuned on this same year. The gain grid often hits its lower edge, 0.005.
  • K1's pooled noise settings come from an earlier experiment's fit, whose window was not checked against 2025-07 to 2026-06.

docs.title: Which changes to the weekly XGBoost demand recipe are worth a full year of testing: holiday columns, winter weather columns, hyperparameters, ensemble-summary inputs, or a split by lead?
docs.text:
Take-home: giving the weekly XGBoost demand model the ensemble's view of the weather lowered the forecast error a little in both main test months and at both metering groups, and no other change did so as clearly. Two ways of giving the model that view did best. The first trains the model on the mean of the 51 ensemble members and then applies it to each member (arm E4_em_pool). The second adds the ensemble's mean and spread of temperature and shortwave radiation (arm E1_es2). They lowered the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) by 0.015 to 0.120 points and by 0.026 to 0.072 points of effective capacity, which is 0.4% to 2.7% of the control's CRPS. Two main test months cannot support more than a full-year test. Holiday columns lowered the error on the Easter bank holidays by about 0.5 points, but raised it on all days in January and at the Primaries with signed meters at Easter. The winter weather columns were neutral to worse, 200 boosting rounds was clearly worse than 500, and the window-summary arms of the lag-surprise idea all raised the error. Verdict: partly supported. A screen supports no 99% claim: every number here is a point difference from the control, set against a noise floor from refitting with another seed, in a few test months.

What we asked. We asked which small changes to the weekly XGBoost demand model of experiment 87 lower its CRPS enough to deserve a full year of testing. That model fits one XGBoost model per Primary substation, trained on the control member of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble forecast. We refitted it monthly with each change on up to four test months, and compared each arm with an unchanged control (C0) over days 1 to 10 of the forecast, the horizon that the electricity distribution network operator (NGED) cares about. Primaries split into two metering groups: the signed-MW six (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, whose meters record the sign of power flow) and the MVA-only eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22, whose meters do not). D15 and D18 are scored for the report only. D-codes are anonymised Primary substations. The caveat that matters most for NGED's use: the screen covers days 1 to 10 pooled, and holds no result for any single lead band.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The table lists the change in all-rows CRPS from C0 in the two main test months. Negative is better. The last two rows give C0's own CRPS and the noise floor, the absolute CRPS gap between C0 and a second control fitted with another seed (C1).

Arm 2026-01 signed-MW 2026-01 MVA-only 2026-06 signed-MW 2026-06 MVA-only E4_em_pool -0.120 -0.099 -0.045 -0.015 E1_es2 -0.072 -0.038 -0.047 -0.026 E2_es7 -0.033 -0.058 -0.033 -0.010 E3_em_em -0.044 -0.048 -0.027 +0.003 W7 -0.020 -0.012 -0.028 -0.005 P_hl1 -0.035 +0.003 -0.023 -0.002 H1 +0.011 +0.022 -0.014 -0.020 HT +0.004 +0.001 +0.002 -0.009 HW -0.004 0.000 0.000 -0.002 W1 +0.005 -0.006 +0.026 +0.033 W2 -0.009 0.000 +0.009 +0.020 W3 -0.008 +0.010 +0.011 +0.053 W4 +0.176 +0.388 +0.005 +0.090 P_rounds_r1000 +0.096 +0.021 -0.045 -0.009 P_rounds_r200 +0.237 +0.188 +0.137 +0.117 H0_nocal +0.139 +0.108 +0.077 +0.064 C0's CRPS 4.509 3.823 2.725 3.527 Noise floor 0.015 0.004 0.001 0.002
  • Ensemble-summary arms lowered the error most consistently. E1_es2 (the ensemble's mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation replace the control member's two columns) is the only arm of the first screening tier, other than W7, below C0 in both main months and both groups. E1_es2 gained 0.7% to 1.7% of C0's CRPS. E4_em_pool (train on the ensemble mean of the seven weather variables, then apply to the 51 members and pool them) is the best Tier B arm, and beats E1_es2 clearly only in January (second figure below). E2_es7 (E1_es2's summary for all seven variables) is also below C0 in all four cells, but gains less than E1_es2 in 2026-01 at the signed-MW six, although it holds more inputs.
  • W7 is a small gain. W7 (trailing means of shortwave radiation and the 3-hour change in the clear-sky index) is below C0 in all four cells, by 0.005 to 0.028 points. Each gap exceeds that cell's noise floor, but one gap (0.005 points) is under 0.01.
  • Holiday columns help on bank-holiday days and raise the error on all days in January and at the signed-MW six at Easter. At Easter (2026-04) H1 lowered CRPS on the bank-holiday days by 0.592 points at the signed-MW six and 0.523 at the MVA-only eight. The same arm raised all-rows CRPS by 0.039 at the signed-MW six in 2026-04, and raised the Christmas-slice CRPS by 0.065 and 0.594 points in 2025-12 and 2026-01 at the signed-MW six. H1d (only the signed days to the nearest bank holiday) lowered Easter CRPS by 0.209 at the signed-MW six and 0.344 at the MVA-only eight, and the Christmas slice by about 0.05 at the signed-MW six. Its all-rows changes range from -0.024 to +0.048. In 2026-06, which holds no bank holiday, H1 and H1d lowered all-rows CRPS by 0.014 to 0.020 points; this screen does not explain why. HW did nothing, and HT and HWT raised the Christmas-slice CRPS by up to 0.49 points (third figure below).
  • Winter weather columns are neutral to worse. W1, W3, and W4 raised CRPS in at least three of the four main cells, and W4 (sine and cosine of the day of year) raised it by 0.176 and 0.388 points in January. W2 (the monotone constraint on temperature) helped beyond the noise floor only in 2025-12, by 0.026 and 0.016 points.
  • Boosting rounds. 200 rounds is clearly worse than 500 in every cell (+0.117 to +0.237). 1000 rounds helps in June (-0.045 and -0.009) and hurts in January (+0.096 and +0.021). A half-life of 1 year (P_hl1) lowers CRPS in 3 of 4 cells, by up to 0.035 points.
  • The calendar columns the control holds matter. Removing the hour and weekday columns (H0_nocal) raised CRPS by 0.064 to 0.139 points, so those columns carry real information.
  • Tails. The control's 95% upper quantile covers 78% of readings at the signed-MW six and 90.5% at the MVA-only eight in January (nominal 95%). No arm repairs that. 1000 rounds lowers coverage further, from 0.781 to 0.749 and from 0.922 to 0.881 at the signed-MW six in January and June.

Window-summary arms hurt. The arms WS A1 to A3 (window summaries of the lag surprise of experiment 391) were scored against that experiment's b0 control on 7 Primaries (the signed-MW six and D8), over 1,034,930 scored half-hours at the signed-MW six and 172,780 at D8. All rows, change in CRPS from b0 (b0's CRPS in brackets): at the signed-MW six +0.100, +0.106, and +0.111 for A1, A2, and A3 (3.123); at D8 +0.134, +0.041, and +0.121 (7.684). The second b0 seed differs by at most 0.001 on all rows and 0.010 on the 21,601 event-lag rows outside events, where A1 to A3 raised CRPS by +0.114, +0.250, and +0.275 (b0 4.957). None of the three arms improved on b0 in any group or slice.

docs.title: Folds and dropped half-hours
docs.text:
Each fold trains on all rows from 2024-04-01 up to a 24-month window and scores the following month's daily runs. All 16 Primaries are scored in every fold. 2026-01 and 2026-06 are the main folds, and 2025-12 (Christmas) and 2026-04 (Easter) are event folds. The scorer dropped 11 half-hours flagged substation_zero in 2025-12 and none in the other three folds.
