docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The hypothesis is not supported, by the decision rule as written. All four of T1 to T4 failed, so no arm is carried forward. H1, H2, C6, and C7 do not count towards the decision. The smallest change worth carrying forward was a 3% lower q99 pinball loss at no CRPS loss; no arm met it.

docs.title: Components adopted or not adopted
docs.text:
• Adopted, unchanged. The global 1.15 widening, the 0.5-year half-life, 3 Gaussian components, and the D15 and D18 start cut.
  • Not adopted. 5 components, split-normal components, the per-lead-band widening fitted on held-out weeks, the quantile head, and half-lives of 1 year and 0.25 years. The quantile head is worth testing as a tail model.
  • Attention over input groups (a0) is not adopted. a0 beats the per-Primary neural network (C7) but scores 3.334 at the signed-MW six against 3.302 for ctrl; the logs print no interval for that contrast.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Interim. Five test months give wide intervals, most of all at D15 and D18, and no claim of benefit rests on any number here.
  • The widening fitted on held-out weeks barely changed the coverage. The logs do not print the fitted factors. The held-out weeks are rows the neural network never trains on, and they are older on average than the test months. The experiment did not test whether that age explains the result.
  • The avoidable-curtailment cost is not reported. The scorer logs hold no curtailment-cost figure.
  • Seed averaging. The widening was fitted and applied per seed and the three seeds were then averaged, so the averaged _bw forecast is not exactly calibrated.
  • Unlogged load-shift events. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so the training rows and the scoring rows can hold events no label covers.
  • Cleaned data. Training rows drop every half-hour that the cleaned power table flags as an exact zero. The scorer dropped 1,179 flagged half-hours from the actuals of every arm, including the references from experiments 397 and 406, which were trained without this cleaning.
  • Departure: the widening is fitted on held-out weeks, not on a validation month, as the plan states. The load-shift event plots are not drawn.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Plan as committed before any fit
Question and design
docs.text:
We change one thing at a time in the pooled plain network and compare each change with the same network widened by a global factor. Experiment 397 found that the networks cover too few outcomes with their 95% quantile at the six signed-MW Primaries, and that a widening of 1.15 only lifts the coverage to about 0.89. This experiment tests four ways to fix the tails and two row-weight half-lives.

  • The networks. The pooled plain network of experiment 397 (setting g09, summary scheme, an 8-wide Primary embedding) on its five screen folds (test months 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), with three seeds averaged in quantile space and the same refits and scoring rows.
  • ctrl. 3 Gaussian components, row-weight half-life 0.5 years. Its widened version ctrl_w115 is the reference.
  • k5. 5 Gaussian components.
  • skew. 3 split-normal components. A split-normal component has one standard deviation below its mode and another above it, so a component can be skewed. Each component's density and distribution function have closed forms, so the quantiles come from the same bisection as the Gaussian mixture. A Student-t family is not tested, because the Student-t distribution function has no closed form in the neural-network library used.
  • ctrl_bw: widening fitted per lead band. For each of five lead bands (day 1, days 2 to 3, days 4 to 7, days 8 to 10, days 11 to 14) and each of q01, q05, q95, and q99, the factor that makes the share of held-out rows below the widened quantile equal the nominal level. The held-out rows are the one week in every 12 that the network did not train on (the same rows that stop its training), so the widening is fitted inside each refit on rows the network has not seen. The factor is limited to between 0.5 and 4. Every arm also gets its _bw version, and the 1.15 _w115 version.
  • qhead. 11 quantiles output directly (a median and cumulative positive steps either side, so they cannot cross) and trained with the pinball loss averaged over the 11 levels.
  • hl365 and hl91. ctrl with row weights that halve every 1 year and every 0.25 years (the control halves every 0.5 years, as the XGBoost member does).
  • a0. Experiment 397's group-attention network with uniform weights, fitted with the start cut, to redo experiment 403's contrast.
  • The start cut. D15 and D18 lose every training row before 2025-03-01, and every row whose weekly lag reaches back before that date (maintainer's rule of 2026-10-30, from experiment 399). The scoring rows start in 2025-10, so no scoring actual or inference input is affected.
  • Input ports from XGBoost (the solar summary column and sunny flag with a 1-year half-life, and trailing temperature means) are not in this experiment and follow as a separate experiment.

docs.title: Components adopted from earlier results
docs.text:
• Adopted. One pooled network with a Primary embedding (experiment 403: it scored lower than per-Primary networks); the ensemble mean and spread passed through the network once (experiment 397: within 0.05 points of 51 passes; experiment 394 found the mean carries most of the gain); the half-life of 0.5 years and monthly refits of the XGBoost member; the 1.15 widening of experiments 389 and 397; and the D15 and D18 start cut of experiment 399. Every arm of this experiment is therefore pooled, one-pass, widened where stated, and cut, and the arm names say what changed from that base.
  • Not adopted. Attention over input groups (experiment 397: the gate stayed within 0.01 of uniform), which survives only as the a0 arm that redoes experiment 403's contrast; and dropping the spread columns, which experiment 394 suggests is harmless but which no arm here tests.

docs.title: Standing practices followed, and the deviations
docs.text:
This experiment follows the standing practices of the ml-experiment skill and common.md, and departs from two.

  • Followed. Monthly refits; the D15 and D18 start cut; every fitted network saved in the private data folder; stored forecasts reused as references and never refitted; a few-fold screen with every number labelled interim; tails and the avoidable-curtailment cost reported beside the CRPS; example forecast charts; a fresh Sonnet code review before the first fit.
  • Cleaned data. Training rows drop every half-hour that the cleaned power table flags as an exact zero (substation_zero), and every row whose lag reaches a flagged half-hour. The scorer drops flagged half-hours from the actuals of every arm, including the references from experiments 397 and 406. The number of rows dropped is printed for each fold. A forecast row whose inference input reaches a flagged lag half-hour is kept, because the flagged half-hours are rare (experiment 398 found 38 in the scored Primary half-hours), and the same rows enter every arm. The references from experiments 397 and 406 were trained without this cleaning.
  • Departure: the widening is fitted on held-out weeks, not on a validation month. The rule asks for a validation month inside the refit. A validation month would need a second fit per refit. The held-out weeks (one in every 12 across the 24-month window) are rows the network never trains on, so they play the same part at no extra fit, but they are older on average than the month before the refit.
  • Departure: the load-shift event plots are not drawn, because this experiment does not score performance during or after load-shift events.

docs.title: Fit counts, time, and memory
docs.text:
• Fits. ctrl, k5, skew, qhead, hl365, and hl91: 6 arms by 5 folds by 3 seeds, so 90 pooled fits, and 15 more for a0. The widenings need no refit.
  • Time. Experiment 397 fitted a pooled plain network in about 50 s and A0 in about 130 s on the GPU, so the experiment is expected to take about 2.5 hours.
  • Memory. One GPU process with at most 8 GB of host memory and one feeder core. The per-Primary raw rows that experiment 397 wrote are read once per fold, a fold's tables are built once per half-life and shared by every arm and seed with that half-life, and the held-out rows' widening is computed once per fit.

docs.title: Checks the write-up reports
docs.text:
• Absolute CRPS of every arm beside experiment 397's uncut networks, per group and per Primary.
  • Tails first. Coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99, on all half-hours and on sunny low-demand half-hours, which are the sunny half-hours (experiment 381's flag) whose reference median is in the lowest quarter for the Primary. The rows are chosen from the forecast, never from the outcome.
  • Example forecasts. For D10 (signed-MW) and D4 (MVA-only), the reference's median, 50% band, and 90% band against what happened: one day-ahead forecast and one full 14-day forecast from a single run, in winter (made on 2026-01-12) and summer (made on 2026-06-15).
  • Unlogged load-shift events. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so the training rows and the scoring rows can hold events no label covers.

docs.title: Caveats registered before the scores
docs.text:
• Widening factors are fitted per seed and applied per seed, and the scorer then averages the widened quantiles over the three seeds, so the averaged _bw forecast is not exactly calibrated at the nominal level.
  • The widening is fitted on the unweighted held-out weeks across the whole 24-month window. For hl91, whose network concentrates on recent rows, the factors reflect older rows that the network fits less closely.
  • The sunny low-demand quarter is taken over all leads of the sunny half-hours, and the tail table then uses the days 1 to 10 rows of it.

docs.title: Counting towards the demand-v2 stop rule
docs.text: This experiment does not count. It tests changes to the tails of an existing model, not a new demand model, so no idea's count rises whatever the verdict.

docs.title: Can the monthly XGBoost model infer signed MW from MVA readings, in lab conditions?
docs.text:
Take-home: two satellite solar columns lowered the forecast error at 15 of the 16 Primary substations, but only because the lab gives the model the realised sunshine, and the attempt to recover a signed MW forecast failed its known-answer test. At the eight Primaries whose meters record apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA-only: D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22) the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) fell by 0.359 points of effective capacity (99.67% interval -0.500 to -0.229) when the monthly XGBoost demand model received the CAMS solar columns, and by 0.772 (95% interval -1.037 to -0.521) at D12. In production the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) value arrives about a day late, so this gain is a ceiling, not a forecast of what production would see. The registered rule for labelling reverse flow recovered the sign of injected solar output with pooled balanced accuracy 0.834 against a pass line of 0.85, so the stop rule applied: the signed-label arms were not run and there is still no trusted signed forecast at the MVA-only Primaries. Verdict: partly supported.

At the eight MVA-only Primaries the meter records apparent power in megavolt-amperes, which has no sign, so reverse flow from embedded solar looks like demand. D-codes are anonymised Primary substations of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), the electricity distribution network operator that supplies the data. Experiments 152, 372, 374, and 387 each tried a different fold treatment and none gave a trusted signed forecast. This experiment gave the monthly XGBoost model two CAMS columns and labelled reverse flow by a physics rule before training. It first tested that rule on six Primaries whose meters record sign, after adding the recorded output of a metered solar farm so that the true answer is known.

docs.title: What changed since the brief was written
docs.text:
• Experiment 387 merged (not supported: a folded loss leaves the sign set by the start, and its custom objective scored about 0.11 points worse than the built-in quantile loss). This experiment therefore uses only the built-in reg:quantileerror loss and a label.
  • Standing rules added to common.md on 2026-10-30 are applied: monthly refits only, cleaned data with the substation_zero half-hours dropped, the D15 and D18 rows before 2025-03-01 cut, boosters saved as .ubj, tails and avoidable-curtailment cost reported, and example forecasts plotted.
  • Stored control not reused for A0. Experiment 381's monthly/control was fit on the uncleaned cache without the D15 and D18 cut, so A0 is refit here. Experiment 381's stored forecasts serve only the code check.

docs.title: The known-answer test failed
docs.text:
The registered rule recovered the sign of injected reverse flow for about three half-hours in four, which is short of the pass line. At the six Primaries whose meters record sign, we added a metered solar farm's output (twice the median sunny-midday reading), discarded the sign, and asked the rule-labelled XGBoost model (A2 at tau 0.7) to recover it. The signed median's pooled balanced accuracy (the mean of the share of reverse-flow half-hours it called and the share of other half-hours it left alone) was 0.834 against 0.85. The signed median's mean absolute error was 9.3 points against 19.5 for the plain model read as signed. It did not beat a rule that flips the sign whenever realised ERA5 shortwave irradiance exceeds a threshold fitted on the training years: that rule scored 0.86 to 0.88 per Primary, 0.036 above the model, though it wrongly flipped 14% to 19% of the half-hours with no reverse flow against 2% to 5% for the model.

  • Criteria (pooled over six Primaries, 12 monthly refits, days 1 to 10, daylight half-hours). Pooled balanced accuracy 0.834 (needs 0.85: fail). Lowest Primary 0.788 at D5 (needs 0.70: pass). False-reverse rate 3.6% (needs at most 5%: pass). Margin over the shortwave rule -0.036 (needs +0.03: fail). Signed mean absolute error 9.3 against 19.5 (pass).
  • Per Primary. D5 0.788, D9 0.841, D10 0.825, D11 0.849, D14 0.846, D16 0.843, with recall on reverse flow 0.60 to 0.75.
  • The shortwave comparison favours that rule. That rule reads realised ERA5 (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis) shortwave at the valid time, which a 10-day forecast does not know. The gate fails on pooled balanced accuracy alone, so dropping the margin criterion would not change the verdict.
  • Most of the loss belongs to the rule. Used alone on the injected data (no model fit), the rule's labels reach recall 0.64 to 0.79 with false-reverse 3.8% to 6.1% at level 2.0. A single-fit rule scores 0.74 to 0.85 per Primary, so the 0.85 pass line sits at the ceiling the rule's own labels allow. D9 is the exception: the model (0.841) beat the single-fit rule (0.737).
  • The miss is small but not noise. A bootstrap over (Primary, refit) pairs gives a pooled balanced accuracy of 0.821 to 0.846 (5th to 95th percentile), so the miss is about 0.016.
  • The rule's gate opens at two real Primaries. Read as apparent power, real readings open the gate only at D10 (a signed-MW Primary with 130 real reverse half-hours) and at D12. At those two Primaries the rule labels 97% and 92% of sunny summer-midday training half-hours as reverse flow, because the constant C is fitted from the same rows that it then labels. The 92% at D12 is therefore not evidence that D12 exports on 92% of sunny middays.
  • Stop rule. The gate failed at level 2.0, so level 1.0 and the A2 arms (tau 0.7, tau 0.5, off, shuffled, and forced gate) were not run. This would be the fifth fold treatment after experiments 152, 372, 374, and 387, so the next step is the maintainer's decision.

docs.text:
The CAMS columns (A1) lowered CRPS at 15 of 16 Primaries. Differences are A1 minus A0, days 1 to 10, in points of effective capacity; 95% intervals per Primary from resampling whole months. Negative is better.

Widening every quantile band by 15% (A0_w115, A1_w115) gives -0.363, -0.464, and -0.793, so the gain does not come from the bands.
  • D15 is the only Primary without a gain. Its +0.048 is just under the +0.05 limit of the porting rule and rests on 4 scored months, with an interval of -0.314 to +0.341. D18 rests on 6 scored months and D8 on 11.
  • Sunny half-hours gain most. On the sunny_unit_shape slice C1 is -0.969 (-1.393 to -0.610) pooled over the eight MVA-only Primaries and -2.349 (-3.731 to -0.969) at D12.
  • Cold nights and the Economy 7 step are unchanged. On cold winter nights C1 is -0.019 (-0.040 to +0.018) pooled and -0.007 (-0.229 to +0.110) at D12; on the Economy 7 step it is -0.005 (-0.024 to +0.006) pooled and -0.046 (-0.154 to +0.012) at D12. All four intervals include zero.
  • References on the same rows (CRPS, days 1 to 10). At D12 BG2 scored 6.747, the GAM stack 7.512, manual_heuristic 7.921, and climatology 8.827, so A1 (6.027) is below all four; A0 (6.800) is above BG2. At D2 A1 (1.809) is below BG2 (2.297), the stack (2.474), and manual_heuristic (2.857). The other Primaries' reference scores are in the printed report in the private folder.
  • Code check. A0 reproduces experiment 381's stored control to within 0.002 CRPS (D5 3.887 against 3.888; D12 6.811 against 6.812).

The CAMS columns remove the sunny-half-hour under-forecast at D12 and leave a bias of the opposite sign. The mean error of the median on sunny_unit_shape half-hours at D12 was -4.79 points for A0 at days 1 to 10 (-2.06 at day 1, -6.15 at days 8 to 10) and +2.14 for A1 (+1.65 at day 1, +2.65 at days 8 to 10). Experiment 381 found about -5 at D12. The lab's CAMS value is the realised weather at every lead, so A1's bias does not grow with lead the way A0's does. In production the columns would describe only past half-hours, so the day-1 to day-10 pattern would look more like A0's.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Dropped half-hours. The cleaning rule dropped 622 half-hours over the cache year, at D12 (4), D15 (196), D16 (1), D18 (389), D21 (13), D22 (5), D8 (9), and D9 (5). The 196 for D15 and 389 for D18 fall before those Primaries' first scored refits (2026-03-01 and 2026-01-01); within the scored windows D15 lost none and D18 lost three.
  • Median minus mean forecast. Per Primary, in megawatts, between about -0.19 and +0.01 for both arms, and A1 is closer to zero at most Primaries (D12 -0.167 for A0, -0.148 for A1).
  • Lead band. The headline lead_days_1_10 band is lead above 0 and up to 240 hours.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 (a known-answer test failed) fired. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts a prediction) fired: P3 predicted -0.05 to -0.20 at D12 and the result is -0.772. The explanation is oracle weather: the lab columns carry the realised CAMS value at every lead, so the gain grows with lead where production's would not.
  • Audit of the numbers. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the CRPS, the contrasts, and the code check from the stored forecasts. They match within about 0.2%, except D8 (about 1% in CRPS, traced to a difference in the row set), with no leakage and no Primary worse than +0.05.
  • Audit of the gate. A second fresh Sonnet agent rebuilt the injected truth and the scores from the stored files. Every per-Primary and pooled figure matches, the injection uses only data before 2025-07-01, and "failed at level 2.0" is a sound reading. The gate auditor also noted that the reverse flow share is 17% to 26% of daylight half-hours, that Q is zero by construction (which favours the model, so real meters would do no better), and that the 0.85 line was set without knowing the rule's ceiling.
  • Prediction outcomes. P1 failed (0.834). P2 (placebos) was not run. P3 failed on D12 (-0.772 against -0.05 to -0.20) and at the other seven (each moved by more than the predicted -0.03 to +0.03; D4's -0.053 is the smallest). P4 and P5 were not run. P6 cannot be tested in the lab, because the columns carry realised CAMS values at every lead.
  • Cadence. Monthly refits only, as the brief required.
  • Saved models and data. Fitted boosters are .ubj files, one per Primary per refit, in the experiment's private data folder (work/full/real/boosters and work/full/inj_2.0/boosters), never in git. Injected farm data and per-farm scores stay in the private store, and no farm name or series is published here.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the CAMS gain at production lags. An arm that gives the model the CAMS value only for half-hours at least one day old, or as an anomaly against the forecast weather, would show how much of the 0.359 survives. The porting rule for the columns (the pooled interval below zero and no Primary worse than +0.05) is met formally, but the lab gain is not a production gain.
  • Whether to continue signed-latent work at the MVA-only Primaries is the maintainer's decision. The stop rule has fired on the fifth treatment. One option the gate audit points to is fitting the reverse-flow constant on rows other than those it labels; another is to stop and use a structural term (demand minus non-negative generation).

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Base recipe (all arms). Experiment 381's monthly control: 12 refits with origins 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-01, built-in reg:quantileerror with 11 quantiles, 500 rounds, eta 0.05, depth 6, seed 0, the default constant base_score, hist, 3 threads. Fits at 3 threads, no GPU (many small per-Primary fits, as experiment 381 found), memory capped at 8 GB.
  • CAMS source and delay. cams_demand_points.parquet (CAMS solar radiation time series, hourly global horizontal irradiance at each Primary's coordinates, 2019-09 to 2026-09); each hour-ending value is repeated on the two half-hours that end inside the hour (studies.dp_features). The service publishes with about a 1-day delay, so the columns cannot describe the first day of lead in production. Lab conditions use the half-hour's own CAMS value. u_t is studies.dp_features.unit_pv_shape; k_t is CAMS GHI over the Haurwitz clear-sky GHI (studies.baselines.haurwitz_w_m2) at the half-hour's solar zenith.
  • Signed-label rule (A2), refreshed at each refit from the training window only. The gate is open at a Primary when the Spearman correlation of the reading with u on summer-midday rows with k at least 0.7 exceeds +0.3, or the 1st percentile is below 1.0 point of capacity (experiment 366's rule, not re-tuned). D_ref(h) is the median reading at UTC hour h on April-to-September training rows with k below 0.3. C is the median of (y + D_ref)/u on clear summer-midday training rows. A reading is reverse flow when the gate is open, k is at least tau, C u exceeds D_ref(h), and C u - y is at least 2 points. The label is -y for reverse flow and +y otherwise. The lags stay unsigned readings.
  • Shape check (maintainer's rule), pre-registered. For each Primary, the correlation between the inferred reverse-flow magnitude and C u on reverse half-hours is reported. A correlation of at least 0.8 counts as following the shape; below 0.5 counts as not following it.
  • Fold at serving. Build a piecewise-linear CDF F from the 11 signed quantiles and set H(x) = F(x) - F(-x) for x at least 0. The MVA quantile at level alpha is the inverse of H. This is the identity whenever q01 is at least 0.
  • Arms. A0 (control, refit here). A1 (A0 plus u_t and k_t). A2 (tau = 0.7, registered), A2 (tau = 0.5), A2-off (tau infinite; must equal A1 to the last bit, a code check), and A2-shuffle (k permuted across days within the same month and hour before labelling). A1 is also run at the other 8 Primaries as a no-harm check. The A2 arms are run only after the known-answer gate passes at level 2.0.
  • Known-answer test, run first. Sites: D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16. Three different metered solar farms rotate across the Primaries (the injection frame of experiment 39 that experiment 152 uses), scaled to 2.0 times, then 1.0 times, the median sunny-midday reading of the training window. The farm output never enters the inputs, C, or u. Reading is y' = sqrt(P'^2 + Q^2) with Q = 0. The farm data stay in the private store and no farm name, ID, or series is published. Placebos on the real readings: at most 1% false reverse flow on sunny middays at D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16; D10's 130 real reverse half-hours reported; forcing the gate open at D5 must leave the MVA score about unchanged and make the signed MAE worse.
  • Scoring. demand-v1 at all 16 Primaries on fold_a_daily_gap_v1; days 1 to 10 headline and by lead band; q01, q05, q95, q99 tails; avoidable-curtailment cost; cold winter nights; sunny half-hours shown three ways (realised sunny_clear_sky_index, CAMS k at least 0.7, sunny_unit_shape); D12's sunny bias by lead band for A0 and A1. Half-hours dropped as substation_zero are counted per fold.
  • Reuse. Stored GAM stack, BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology forecasts are read as references; 16 Primaries x 12 refits x 3 fit arms are fitted here.
  • Reviews. (1) Code is written by Sonnet. (2) A fresh Sonnet agent reviews it before the first fit (leakage, the train_end cut, scoring, matching the copied recipe). (3) A second review if the first flags many problems. (4) Run. (5) A fresh Sonnet agent re-derives the headline numbers and the audit triggers are run. (6) Write-up. (7) A fresh Sonnet agent reviews the write-up for numbers and prose.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• D12's reverse flow is inferred, not measured (fitted PV capacity about 148 points, 6.9 MW, unverified), and D12's solar response bottoms out at 100 to 200 W/m2, so a "very sunny" gate probably mislabels moderate-sun reverse flow there.
  • A solar-only gate mislabels reverse flow from other generators; the assumption is unsafe at Primaries with other generation (D15 is negative on 78% of its half-hours, 63% of them at night).
  • Reactive power is unknown, so every result assumes Q = 0, except a power-factor-0.97 check at the July, November, and March refits.
  • The brief's exploration used ERA5 with Haurwitz, not CAMS, so k is recomputed from CAMS here.

docs.title: Can the explicit solar term inside the mixture density network read the sky once the network has a day-of-year home for the daylight profile, and does it then improve the net-demand forecast?
docs.text: Status: done. The anomaly gate could not be tested, so the score arms ran ungated. The sections below up to "Results" are the plan, written before any fit; the amendment was written after the noise check and before any score arm. The plan follows the maintainer's request after experiment 405, whose placebo gate could not be met.

docs.title: What is asked
docs.text: The question is whether the explicit solar term can be shown to read the sky, and if so whether it lowers the net-demand error. Experiment 405's known-answer test failed its placebo gate because a day-shuffled farm series keeps 79% of the real series' variance through its monthly daylight profile, and the network had no day-of-year term to hold that profile. The aim behind the series is a mixture density network that combines the best of the GAM and XGBoost: interpretable, differentiable physics parts (here an explicit solar term) beside flexible learned parts, so that the fitted network gives explainable outputs and the best CRPS. This plan therefore also stores and plots the learned solar contribution, so that the solar term can be read on its own.

docs.title: Review of the plan against the latest evidence
docs.text:
• Experiment 405 and its audit (merged) set every change below: the profile-only benchmark, the day-of-year term, the anomaly injection, and the dropped divisor.
  • Experiment 403 (merged): pooled A0 is the reference network, CRPS 3.351 at the signed-MW six. Its stored forecasts are the A0 control if its rows match this experiment's rows (checked before scoring; otherwise A0 is refitted).
  • Standing rules added to common.md since the brief: cleaned data, the D15 and D18 start cut, monthly refits, saved models, tails, example forecast graphs, the seven-step process. All are followed below. No result merged since the brief answers the question.
  • Departures from experiment 405: the divisor is dropped (finding 4: the three other farms carry the same signal, so the ratio sits near 1); the increment-penalty arm is dropped (no effect); the placebo limit is set from a measured benchmark instead of copied from experiment 129.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Net demand, signed-MW six, MVA-only eight, solar term, capacity: as in experiment 405. The solar term is a capacity per Primary and season-year times a fixed physical unit shape, and the network subtracts it from the demand mixture.
  • Daylight profile. The mean of a farm's output at each half-hour of the day within a calendar month of a year. Day-to-day anomaly. The farm's output minus its daylight profile.
  • Least-squares read-out. The capacity change that best explains an injected series from the ensemble unit shape on the fold's training rows, dC_LS = eff * sum(f * u) / sum(u^2), over daylight rows of the last season-year, where f is the injected series (a fraction of effective capacity eff) and u the unit shape. It is the benchmark a network that read the shape linearly would reach.

docs.title: Data and rows
docs.text: As in experiment 405: experiment 397's raw matrices in the summary scheme (ECMWF ENS mean and spread, one pass), 16 Primaries, pooled network with an 8-wide Primary embedding, 3 Gaussian components, 2 hidden layers of 64. Cleaned data: substation_zero half-hours are dropped from training, lags, inference, and scoring, as experiment 397's matrices do; the dropped count per fold is reported. Start cut: D15 and D18 drop every row, lag input, and scoring actual before 2025-03-01 (applied; D15 and D18 stay report-only). Cadence: monthly refits on a 730-day window, five screen months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 3 seeds, each booster saved to the experiment's private folder. Weather at lag times: the lags are the Primary's own power, so no weather is used at lag times and the ERA5 delay does not apply.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The solar module is experiment 405's. The net-demand mixture keeps the demand mixture's weights; component k has mean mu_k - m and variance sigma_k^2 + s^2, where m = C[p, y] * u * g and s follows the ensemble spread. Capacity is learned per Primary and season-year under a Gaussian prior from the studies page (C2), with the adapter g (C3).

The change is a day-of-year by hour term in the demand module. The demand module of every C arm and of A0-noirr-doy gets 20 extra inputs: the sine and cosine of the day of year at one and two harmonics (4 inputs), and each of the four by the four existing hour-of-day inputs (sin_hour, cos_hour, sin_hour_2, cos_hour_2; 16 inputs). The network can then represent the monthly daylight shape of the Primary's net demand in the demand module. Irradiance and the three solar-geometry columns stay removed, as in experiment 405.

docs.title: Known-answer test (runs first, gates the score arms)
docs.text:
The test injects a held-out farm's output into the six signed-MW Primaries and asks whether the learned capacity rises by the share the ensemble forecast can explain. It runs on the 2026-06 fold only. Injection follows experiment 405 (farm C, increment 50% of the studies page's 2025/26 capacity, subtracted from the target and the three lags, dropouts removed from every condition).

Condition Injected series control none held_profile the real farm series (variant a) placebo_profile the real farm series with its days shuffled within the month (variant a) held_anomaly the farm's day-to-day anomaly, its daylight profile removed (variant b) placebo_anomaly the anomaly with its days shuffled within the month (variant b) pos_anomaly the ensemble's own day-to-day anomaly of the unit shape, scaled to the same increment (positive control: perfectly readable) pos_profile the ensemble's monthly daylight profile of the unit shape (negative control: should read near 0 once the day-of-year term exists)

The daylight profile is the farm's mean at each half-hour within each calendar month of each year, so each month's anomaly has zero mean at every half-hour and the shuffled anomaly keeps no profile. The two controls use the ensemble unit shape u itself, so they say whether the network can read a perfectly forecastable anomaly, and whether it still puts a pure profile into the solar term. Arms: C2 (prior) with 5 seeds on every condition, C4 (no prior, neutral 3 MW start) with 3 seeds on the five farm conditions. That is 7 x 5 + 5 x 3 = 50 fits.

Recovery, in common units. Recovery is the seed-mean learned capacity increment (injected minus control, at the last season-year in the window) divided by dC_LS(held_anomaly) for every anomaly-variant condition, and by dC_LS(held_profile) for every profile-variant condition. Dividing the placebo by its own read-out (near 0) is what produced experiment 405's -1.88. dC_LS is computed on the fit's own rows and weights (all training rows of the as-of season-year with positive unit shape, with the fold's sample weights), in MW, with a standard error from a bootstrap over days. The placebo benchmark is the mean of dC_LS over 5 different shuffles divided by dC_LS(held), so it is not one random draw. The lag route is part of the test: the injected series is subtracted from the three lags too, as in experiment 405. The 20 day-of-year inputs are not lag features.

Noise check before any gate is read. From experiment 405's stored per-seed capacities and the new dC_LS, a script computes the expected seed standard deviation of the recovery ratio. If the expected standard deviation of the held-anomaly ratio exceeds 0.5 at more than 2 of the 6 Primaries, the gate is declared uninformative (not failed) and the page says so.

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
1. The test is informative only if both controls behave. pos_anomaly recovery of C2 lies in 0.8 to 1.2 at 4 of the 6 Primaries, and pos_profile recovery (relative to its own read-out) is at most 0.30 at 4 of the 6. If not, the page reports the known-answer test as uninformative about the real farm, and the score arms do not run.
  2. Gate K1 (recovery, anomaly variant). C2's recovery on held_anomaly lies in 0.5 to 1.5 at 4 of the 6 Primaries, and exceeds placebo_anomaly recovery by more than 2 seed standard errors at 4 of the 6. The band is wider than experiment 129's 0.75 to 1.25 because the anomaly is only about one fifth of the farm's variance.
  3. Gate K2 (placebo, anomaly variant). C2's recovery on placebo_anomaly is at most the placebo benchmark plus 0.20, in median and in maximum over the six.
  4. K3, P1 to P3 and the profile variant are descriptive. The profile variant (a) reports the real-minus-placebo recovery and how much of the profile the day-of-year term absorbs (the learned capacity increment on pos_profile with and without the term would show it; the without-term fit is C2 on experiment 405's inputs, 3 seeds, 6 more fits). C4 is reported beside C2.
  5. If the controls, K1, or K2 fail, the page reports it, with the profile variant and C4 beside it, and the score arms do not run.
  6. If all hold, the score arms run: A0-noirr-doy, C1 (capacity pinned to the experiment 269 estimate), C2, C3, C4, C5a (monthly capacity path, smoothness penalty, built on C3), and C5b (persistence penalty, built on C3), all with the day-of-year term, 3 seeds, 5 folds. A0 (without the term, with irradiance) is read from experiment 403. Contrasts at the signed-MW six, CRPS at days 1 to 10, month-block bootstrap at 95% with 20,000 resamples, Bonferroni across the seven, each changing one factor: C3 minus A0-noirr-doy (solar term with adapter against none), C2 minus A0-noirr-doy, C3 minus C2 (adapter), C2 minus C1 (learned against pinned capacity), C4 minus C3 (prior), C5a minus C3 (time variation), C5b minus C3 (persistence penalty). C3 minus A0 is reported as the practical comparison and differs by the day-of-year term and the irradiance inputs as well, so it is not a contrast. The MVA-only eight are reported.
  7. A gain needs both the Bonferroni interval excluding zero and the point estimate beyond the minimum detectable effect. Both thresholds must hold.

docs.title: Amendment: the anomaly gate cannot be tested, so the score arms run without a gate
docs.text:
Written after the noise check and the profile test, and before any score arm was fitted or read.

  • The noise check failed. The least-squares read-out of the injected anomaly is 0.03 to 0.05 MW at the signed-MW six, against an injected increment of about 1 MW and a seed standard deviation of 0.18 to 0.59 MW in experiment 405's fits. The expected standard deviation of the recovery ratio is 3.8 to 12.4, so the anomaly gate (K0, K1, K2) is uninformative, not failed. Making it testable would take an injection of about 20 times the size. The anomaly fits did not run.
  • The profile test ran (descriptive, 24 fits, 3 seeds). C2 with and without the day-of-year term on the control, real-farm, day-shuffled-farm, and pure-profile injections. The results are in "Results". The day-of-year term stays in every C arm and in A0-noirr-doy.
  • The maintainer wants the explicit solar term tested on CRPS, so the score arms run ungated: A0-noirr-doy, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5a, and C5b, 5 folds, 3 seeds, with A0 read from experiment 403. A pass of the known-answer test therefore no longer licenses a claim about capacity. The page reports learned capacities beside the studies page as description only.
  • Dropped: the cost at the scaled export limit (studies.node_curtailment), which needs a node and its generators and so cannot be scored per Primary here. The tail report stays.

docs.title: Pre-registered no-gate decision rule
docs.text:
The contrasts, all at the signed-MW six, CRPS at days 1 to 10, in points of effective capacity, with the month-block bootstrap of studies.eval_protocol (20,000 resamples) at the Bonferroni-corrected level (family-wise 95% across the seven one-factor contrasts, so 99.29% per contrast): C3 minus A0-noirr-doy, C2 minus A0-noirr-doy, C3 minus C2, C2 minus C1, C4 minus C3, C5a minus C3, and C5b minus C3. C3 minus A0 is reported and not tested. The minimum detectable effect of a contrast is 2 times the standard deviation over the 5 folds of the seed-to-seed difference of the contrast.

  • Slices. The headline band is days 1 to 10 at all signed-MW-six half-hours. The sunny slices are sunny_unit_shape and sunny_april_june, each within days 1 to 10. The minimum detectable effect is computed separately for each slice. Each contrast is tested in 3 slices, so the true family is 21 tests; with 5 test months the month-block interval excludes zero only when about 4 or 5 months agree, and the write-up says so.
  • Main question: C3 minus A0-noirr-doy (the explicit solar term with the adapter, against the same network with no solar term). A slice "passes" when the difference is below zero, its interval excludes zero, and its magnitude exceeds that slice's minimum detectable effect.
    • Supported: the headline band passes and at least one sunny slice passes, and the tail rule holds.
    • Partly supported: the headline band passes and neither sunny slice passes, or a sunny slice passes and the headline band does not, or the headline band has an interval excluding zero with a magnitude below the minimum detectable effect; and the tail rule holds.
    • Not supported: no slice has an interval excluding zero, or any slice has a positive difference with an interval excluding zero (harm), whatever the other slices show.
    • Tail rule not met: a result that is otherwise supported or partly supported is downgraded one level.
  • The prediction that can fail (P1): C3 minus A0-noirr-doy lies between -0.15 and 0.00 points in the headline band. A difference outside that range counts as the prediction failing, whatever the verdict word.
  • Tail rule. In the headline band at the signed-MW six, C3's pinball loss at q95 and at q99 is no more than 5% higher (relative) than A0-noirr-doy's, and C3's coverage at q95 and at q99 differs from A0-noirr-doy's by at most 0.02 (an arm-to-arm difference). The q01, q05, and threshold-weighted CRPS are reported and do not enter the rule.
  • Secondary contrasts are reported with their intervals and called gains only on the same three-part rule (interval, minimum detectable effect, no worse tails). C3 minus A0 is the practical comparison and is described at the same level, not judged, because it differs in the day-of-year term, the irradiance inputs, and possibly the training rows (experiment 397 may not have applied the D15 and D18 start cut, which does not affect the scored rows).
  • Learned capacity is described against the studies page, with seed intervals. No capacity claim rests on a known-answer test.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• Tails and slices. Coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99, raw (the 1.15 widening is not applied to the arms); the sunniest third of daylight half-hours and sunny April to June. The curtailment cost is dropped (see the amendment).
  • The solar contribution, readable on its own. The learned solar output m in MW is stored per scored row. The page plots, for each of the six, the mean learned output by month and hour beside the physical clear-sky shape times the studies-page capacity, the learned capacity path with intervals from seeds, and the same Primary's forecast from the network with the solar term beside the forecast from A0-noirr-doy (the same network with no solar term).
  • Example forecasts. A day-ahead and a full 14-day forecast from one run, for one signed-MW and one MVA-only Primary, in a winter and a summer month.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per site, the mean-forecast error beside each contrast, the audit triggers that fired, the flagged half-hours dropped per fold, and the saved-booster path.

docs.title: Compute and fits
docs.text:
• Known-answer test: 56 fits (50 plus 6 for the without-term profile check) at 50 to 200 seconds each, 1 to 3 hours.
  • Score arms (only if the gate holds): 7 arms x 5 folds x 3 seeds = 105 fits, 1.5 to 6 hours.
  • Stored predictions reused: experiment 403's A0 forecasts, the XGBoost, BG2, and GAM-stack references. Experiment 405's extras and u99 files are reused, which saves the unit-shape pass.
  • Resources: one GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. No fit starts until the manager grants the fit slot (idle CPU at least 30%, available memory at least 15 GB).

docs.title: Earlier advice followed and departed from
docs.text:
• Followed: calibrate the placebo gate to the network; give the demand module a day-of-year by hour term and inject the anomaly (experiment 405 advice); use an as-of capacity; report absolute skill beside contrasts.
  • Departed from: experiment 129's divisor and five-year drift gate; the former is uninformative (experiment 405 audit, finding 4) and the latter does not fit a two-season-year window.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Take-home message: the explicit solar term did not reliably lower the net-demand error, and the known-answer test could not show that the neural network reads the sky. All numbers are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity at the signed-MW six (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16), days 1 to 10, five test months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), monthly refits on a 730-day window, 3 seeds, so every interval is interim. Weather inputs are the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble mean and spread, one pass; cleaned data; D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 (report-only).

  • Verdict by the pre-registered rule: not supported (P3 also missed). C3 minus A0-noirr-doy is -0.064 (interval -0.131 to +0.028; minimum detectable effect 0.397) in days 1 to 10, -0.053 (-0.750 to +0.207) in the sunniest third, and +0.152 (+0.030 to +0.168) in sunny April to June. The rule reads the last slice as harm. The sunny April to June slice holds only 2 test months (2026-03 and 2026-06), so its interval is the range of two monthly values and is not a test. The same caveat covers C3 minus C2 and C2 minus A0-noirr-doy in that slice. The rule's headline band and sunniest-third slice agree on "not supported" without it, because neither interval excludes zero. Every interval in this section is at the 99.29% level (Bonferroni across seven contrasts). P1 held on the point estimate (-0.064 is in -0.15 to 0.00). P2 (C2 minus A0-noirr-doy between -0.30 and -0.05) held on the point estimate (-0.077) with an interval that includes zero. P3 (C3 minus C2 between -0.10 and 0.00) missed (+0.013). A noise floor to keep in mind: the MVA-only eight's A0-noirr-doy scores 3.996 against 4.05 to 4.06 for the C arms, which carry no solar term there, so networks that differ only in their inputs already differ by 0.06 points.
  • Absolute CRPS, signed-MW six / MVA-only eight. Pooled A0 (experiment 403) 3.351 / 3.791; A0-noirr-doy 3.457 / 3.996; C1 3.406 / 4.062; C2 3.380 / 4.059; C3 3.393 / 4.052; C4 3.393 / 4.051; C5a 3.404 / 4.051; C5b 3.395 / 4.053. The MVA-only eight have no solar term and lose 0.2 to 0.3 points against A0 because their irradiance inputs are removed (not contrasted).
  • Other contrasts (days 1 to 10, none beyond its minimum detectable effect). C2 minus A0-noirr-doy -0.077 (-0.151 to +0.039); C3 minus C2 +0.013 (-0.012 to +0.037); C2 minus C1 -0.026 (-0.195 to +0.092); C4 minus C3 +0.001 (-0.019 to +0.026); C5a minus C3 +0.012 (-0.004 to +0.023); C5b minus C3 +0.002 (-0.001 to +0.011). C3 minus A0, described only, is +0.041 (-0.080 to +0.154). The adapter, the prior, and the capacity-path penalties made no measurable difference.
  • Tails (days 1 to 10, signed-MW six, mean over Primaries; A0-noirr-doy / C3). Pinball q95 1.127 / 1.096; pinball q99 0.461 / 0.427; coverage q95 0.835 / 0.840; coverage q99 0.924 / 0.931; coverage q01 0.018 / 0.018; coverage q05 0.051 / 0.057; threshold-weighted CRPS 0.631 / 0.627. The tail rule holds, and every solar arm has a lower q99 pinball than A0-noirr-doy (0.404 for C4, 0.415 for C2, 0.418 for C1, 0.425 for C5b, 0.427 for C3), but no interval was computed for these differences.
  • Learned capacity (2025/26 season-year, mean over folds and seeds, MW) against the studies page. C2 is 0.59, 1.38, 1.69, 1.98, 2.24 at D9, D10, D11, D14, D16 against 3.11, 3.06, 4.21, 4.14, 4.50, and is 2.64 at D5 against 2.19; C3 and C4 are similar, C4 (no prior) higher. The seed ranges are wide (for example D5 1.8 to 3.5 for C2). The capacity is therefore weakly identified, as the profile test below shows.
  • Profile test (descriptive; 24 fits, 3 seeds). Learned capacity increment as a multiple of the least-squares read-out of the real farm series. With the day-of-year term, the real farm recovers 0.16 to 0.87 (median 0.47), the day-shuffled farm 0.11 to 0.48 (median 0.25), and a pure ensemble profile 0.19 to 0.43. Without the term, the real farm recovers 0.45 to 1.09 (median 0.62), the shuffled farm 0.34 to 0.63 (median 0.47), and the pure profile 0.28 to 0.40. The benchmark for the shuffled farm is 0.95 to 0.96, so no arm reads the profile fully. The day-of-year term lowers the pure-profile reading by about 0.1 and the real-farm recovery by about 0.15, with D10 moving the other way, and the seed standard errors (0.03 to 0.42) are as large as these gaps.
  • Anomaly gate: not testable. The least-squares read-out of the injected anomaly is 0.03 to 0.05 MW at the signed-MW six, against an injected increment of about 1 MW and a seed standard deviation of 0.18 to 0.59 MW in capacity, so the expected standard deviation of the recovery ratio is 3.8 to 12.4 (limit 0.5). The gate is uninformative, not failed. The anomaly fits did not run.
  • Compute and data. The experiment ran 24 profile-test fits and 105 score fits, about 10 to 60 seconds each on one GPU process; the flagged zero half-hours were dropped by experiment 397's matrices (count per fold not recomputed here). Fitted networks are saved as .pt files in the experiment's work/seed_preds/<arm>/ folder; the solar outputs per half-hour are in the matching .solar.parquet files.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline from the stored forecasts for all five months. The pooled absolute scores match the printed 3.457 and 3.393, and the mean of the monthly differences (-0.063) matches the printed -0.064. Triggers that fired:

  • A slice with fewer than 3 test months. Sunny April to June holds 2 months, so its bootstrap interval is degenerate (the endpoints equal the two monthly differences).
  • A month that is not April to June inside that slice. The slice includes 2026-03 forecasts. The slice is defined by the protocol's sunny_april_june flag, which this page does not redefine; it is reported as defined, and the slice's membership is flagged for the protocol owner.
  • Every headline contrast is below its minimum detectable effect, so none counts as a gain.
  • Seed disagreement in the learned capacities (above).
  • Not run: median minus mean forecast per site, and a comparison of the capacity seed ranges with the studies page intervals.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the solar term on a target it can read. Inject a signal about 20 times larger, or add the solar term where the weather forecast has more skill (short leads), before asking about CRPS.
  • Keep the free irradiance input in the pooled network until an explicit term beats it.
  • Look at the tails: the lower q95 and q99 pinball loss of the solar arms is worth a calibration experiment with intervals from more test months.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None, apart from needing seven experiment folders on PYTHONPATH to run the scripts.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
• Design review (fresh Sonnet) found nine points. Accepted 1 to 8: the noise check, common-unit recovery, positive and negative controls, the profile-absorption report, the read-out on the fit's rows, the lag route stated, one-factor contrasts, and descriptive rules. Point 9 is noted: the profile comes from the test period, which gives the network no information it could not learn.
  • Code review before the first fit (fresh Sonnet). Found two high, two medium, four low points. Fixed: the noise check read the wrong file names; the control fold kept raw lags while every other condition had gap lags set to missing (the control now goes through the injection path); the read-out included the early-stopping weeks (now excluded); the placebo benchmark now drops gap rows as the real placebo does; the pos_profile rule uses the absolute value; each fold is freed after use. Noted, not changed: the pos_anomaly control averages the ensemble unit shape over origins, so its recovery at long lead may miss for reasons unrelated to the network (the read-out uses the row's own shape, which partly corrects it); the score stage and its day-of-year inference inputs are added only if the gate holds.
  • Code review of the score stage and the decision rule (fresh Sonnet, before any score arm). Found no crash and no leakage; five medium or low points on the rule and script. Fixed: the script asserts every seed file exists; the minimum detectable effect is computed per slice; the sunny slices are within days 1 to 10; the rule now has a fallback for a passing headline band with no sunny pass, defines harm, defines the tail rule (slice, relative tolerance, arm-to-arm coverage difference), names P1's slice, and states the 21-test family. The training-rows caveat for C3 minus A0 is added.
  • Results review and audit (fresh Sonnet). Re-derived the headline from stored forecasts and found the printed numbers consistent; the triggers that fired are listed under "Audit".
  • Write-up review (fresh Sonnet). Found five numbers to correct (the lowest q99 arm, the scope of the q99 claim, the effect of the day-of-year term on the profile reading, the D9 capacity, the contrast cited in the advice), four medium points (interval level, unreported P2 and P3, the seed spread range, the two-month caveat on all three slices), and prose points (a money metaphor, unexpanded acronyms, bare pronouns). All applied.

docs.title: How much does the pooled mixture density network lose when the weather forecast is a day old or the power readings are delayed?
docs.text: Take-home message: a one-run-old weather forecast and readings delayed by 6 or 24 hours change the forecast little, but readings delayed by 12 hours and missing readings change the forecast a lot. The pooled plain mixture density network (a neural network trained once on all substations, from experiment 397) loses 0.03 points of continuous ranked probability score (CRPS; days 1 to 10; points of effective capacity, where one point is 1% of a substation's capacity) at the six primary substations whose meters record signed power (the signed six), when the weather forecast is one run (24 hours) older. It loses 0.02 points when the power readings are delayed by 6 hours and 0.04 when they are delayed by 24 hours. Each such change to the inputs is an "arm" below. The same network loses 0.20 points when the readings are delayed by 12 hours and 9.7 points when the three newest-reading lags are missing. The monthly XGBoost model (S1M, experiment 389: a gradient-boosted tree model given the ensemble mean and spread of temperature and shortwave radiation) loses 0.03, 0.02, 0.04, 0.31, and 4.5 points in the same five arms. The pre-registered rule calls for a second experiment, because the 12-hour delay makes the loss exceed its limit. Tail coverage holds: the share of outcomes below each model's 95% and 99% quantiles (q95 and q99 coverage) falls by under 0.02 in every arm except the missing-lag arm.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text:
A day-old weather forecast changes the forecast little, and the time of day of the newest reading matters more than its age. We re-scored the stored neural networks of experiment 397, and the stored XGBoost boosters of experiment 389, with stale inputs and fitted nothing. The live service ingests one ECMWF run a day and receives power readings every 6 hours. A forecast can therefore pair recent readings with an old weather forecast, or the reverse.

The decision rule says no second experiment is needed only if every limit holds. The limits are 0.05 points of loss for P6 and P12 and 0.10 for the other four arms in the key below, together with a coverage fall under 0.02. The planning session for the mixture density network proposed them without evidence, and the manager and the maintainer may change them. P12 and W24+P12 fail the rule. The plan for the second experiment (training with random staleness and two age inputs) is a separate brief.

Key to the arms (the arm table under "Design, data, and caveats" gives the details):

  • FRESH: the weather forecast of the forecast's own run and the newest power reading 3.5 hours before the forecast origin (the training pairing).
  • W24 and W48: the weather forecast from the run one day or two days earlier.
  • P6, P12, and P24: the power readings delayed by 6, 12, or 24 hours.
  • W24+P12 and W24+P24: both at once.
  • DROP: the three lags that depend on the forecast origin (newest reading, same time yesterday, same time last week) are missing.
  • S1M: the XGBoost model with the ensemble mean and standard deviation of temperature and shortwave radiation as extra columns.
  • Signed six: the six primary substations whose meters record signed power. MVA-only eight: the eight primary substations whose meters record apparent power only.
  • Details: W24 and W48 are matched on valid time, and the lead and calendar inputs stay those of the fresh origin. P6, P12, and P24 recompute the lag values and the lag-age inputs from the delayed origin, and the lead is unchanged. DROP uses the neural network's missing-flag inputs and the XGBoost model's native missing value.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS loss against the fresh case at days 1 to 10 (points of effective capacity; positive is worse), five screen months, with the 95% month-block interval in brackets. W48 has no limit. The pooled network's P6 interval at the MVA-only eight reaches 0.083, above the limit of 0.05, although its estimate passes.

Arm Pooled network, signed six Pooled network, MVA-only eight XGBoost S1M, signed six XGBoost S1M, MVA-only eight Fresh CRPS 3.270 3.873 3.525 3.995 W24 0.029 (-0.004 to 0.067) 0.047 (0.036 to 0.062) 0.029 (0.009 to 0.051) 0.032 (0.022 to 0.045) W48 0.056 (-0.005 to 0.130) 0.093 (0.072 to 0.122) 0.058 (0.015 to 0.106) 0.064 (0.042 to 0.089) P6 0.024 (0.006 to 0.044) 0.022 (-0.027 to 0.083) 0.020 (0.004 to 0.041) 0.010 (-0.016 to 0.040) P12 0.197 (0.096 to 0.315) 0.151 (0.081 to 0.210) 0.306 (0.204 to 0.433) 0.098 (0.073 to 0.129) P24 0.037 (0.017 to 0.058) 0.031 (0.015 to 0.055) 0.042 (0.023 to 0.064) 0.041 (0.024 to 0.061) W24+P12 0.229 (0.135 to 0.334) 0.197 (0.117 to 0.270) 0.338 (0.244 to 0.455) 0.130 (0.095 to 0.163) W24+P24 0.064 (0.044 to 0.089) 0.076 (0.057 to 0.099) 0.071 (0.052 to 0.092) 0.072 (0.058 to 0.087) DROP 9.73 (4.29 to 14.85) 6.50 (2.86 to 9.87) 4.53 (2.94 to 5.70) 3.68 (3.35 to 4.00)

The XGBoost model loses about as much as the neural network in most arms. The XGBoost model loses more at the signed six when the readings are 12 hours late (0.31 against 0.20 at P12) and less when the lags are missing (4.5 against 9.7). At the MVA-only eight it loses less than the neural network at P12 (0.10 against 0.15) and in DROP (3.7 against 6.5).

docs.title: Tails and widening
docs.text:
• Coverage barely moves. At the signed six and the MVA-only eight, q95 coverage falls by at most 0.011 and q99 coverage by at most 0.004 in every arm except DROP, for both models. The limit is 0.02, so the arms other than DROP need no rule that widens the intervals.
  • DROP breaks the neural network's tails. The neural network's q95 coverage falls from 0.891 to 0.560 at the signed six and from 0.942 to 0.674 at the MVA-only eight, and its q99 coverage from 0.959 to 0.845 and from 0.988 to 0.853. Its 90% interval is 1.79 and 1.32 times as wide as with fresh inputs, That widening does not make up for the missing lags. The XGBoost 90% interval is 1.10 and 1.02 times as wide, and its q95 coverage falls by 0.115 and 0.017.
  • Interval width changes by under 3.1% in every other arm.

docs.title: Design, data, and caveats
docs.text:
• What the stored runs allow. Only the 00:00 UTC run is stored, one per day, so no 6-hour or 12-hour stale-weather arm could be built. W24 and W48 are the stale-weather arms the stored runs allow.
  • Models. The pooled plain neural network, summary scheme, three seeds averaged in quantile space, from experiment 397; the S1M boosters of experiment 389 (monthly refits, one booster per Primary and refit). The per-Primary neural network was not re-scored. The 1.15 widening of experiment 397 is applied to every arm. Both models read the five screen months of experiment 397 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06).
  • Reproduction gates. FRESH on unfiltered power reproduces experiment 397's stored forecasts to 6e-7 and experiment 389's stored S1M forecasts exactly.
  • Rows. Older runs do not reach the last day of the horizon, so W24 and W48 score fewer half-hours (1,538,592 and 1,430,473 half-hours against 1,645,943). Each stale arm and FRESH are compared on their shared rows.
  • Cleaned data. The stored power arrays already hold the flagged substation_zero half-hours as missing, so cleaning the lag inputs changes nothing. The scorer drops flagged half-hours from the actuals: 153, 11, 0, 3, and 0 in the five months.
  • Why P12 fails (tested by the audit on one primary substation, D5, in 2026-01). In training the forecast origin was always 09:00 UTC, so the newest reading was always the 05:30 overnight trough. P12 makes it the 17:30 reading of the previous day, the evening peak. The mean absolute change of the newest-reading lag against FRESH is 0.30 to 0.45 of capacity at P12, against 0.02 to 0.07 at P6 and 0.00 to 0.07 at P24. The loss at P12 rises with lead (0.15 at day 1 to 0.25 at days 8 to 10 at the signed six) and is largest at valid times 00 to 03 UTC. On D5 in 2026-01 (seed 0, pooled neural network), the audit replaced only P12's newest lag with the 05:30 reading of the previous day, and that removed 97% of the P12 loss. Putting P12's 17:30 value into FRESH reproduced 94% of it. The age inputs are not the cause, and a newest lag declared missing is worse than any of these variants. The finding is therefore a mismatch between the time of day of the newest reading in training and in use, not a response to 12 hours of delay. P6 (newest reading at 23:30) and P24 (05:30) are tolerated. The arm grid confounds delay with time of day, because the origin is always 09:00.
  • Checks. A fresh Sonnet reviewer re-derived the results on its own. The W24, P12, and P24 losses agree to within 0.005 points at both groups. The reviewer's FRESH CRPS at the signed six is 3.252 against the scorer's 3.270, and its DROP loss is 9.45 against 9.73. The gap is unexplained, and this page reports the scorer's numbers. The audit rules for a result that contradicts its prediction and for a result a later design depends on both applied, and a fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the P12 lags from the raw power array and confirmed them (the audit checked one Primary, one month, and one seed).
  • Prediction outcomes. P1 held for W24, P6, P24, and W24+P24 and failed for P12 and W24+P12. P2 failed: the loss does not grow with delay (P6 0.024, P12 0.197, P24 0.037 at the signed six), and the loss falls with lead in P24 but not in P12 or W24. P3 held, by a wide margin. P4 held for W24 and P6 to P12 (every coverage fall is under 0.012) and failed for P24, whose coverage fall is 0.002; the coverage collapse in DROP was not predicted. P5 failed: the XGBoost model lost more than the neural network at P12 and W24+P12 at the signed six (by 0.11), and by 0.005 to 0.012 at W48, P24, and W24+P24 at the signed six and P24 at the MVA-only eight. The XGBoost model lost less in DROP and, at the MVA-only eight, in the other arms.
  • Caveats. Five test months give wide intervals, so every number is interim. One run per day confounds the arm grid with the time of day. Only two kinds of forecasting model were tested.
  • What to try next. A second experiment, in a separate brief: train with the newest reading at random times of day (vary the training origin hour), a random weather-forecast age, and the origin lags sometimes missing, with the age of each input as an input. Compare delays that land on the same hour of day, such as 24 against 48 hours, to measure how loss grows with delay.

docs.title: By how much would the forecast with power lags improve on harm rows if the lags inside each real load-shift event were replaced by clean values?
docs.text: Status: done. The scored sample is too small to settle batch 0. The sections from "Question" onward are the plan, written before any score existed. This experiment is batch 0 of the experiment 404 plan, run as its own experiment so that the experiment 404 session is not blocked. This experiment needs no neural network, no GPU, and no fit.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Real lags scored better than clean lags at the six signed-MW Primaries, but 9 events carry the result. The gain is the mean CRPS with real lags minus the mean with clean lags, in points of effective capacity, so a positive gain would mean that cleaning the lags helps. Intervals are 95% event-cluster bootstraps (2,000 resamples).

Group Harm rows Events CRPS real lags CRPS clean lags Gain 95% interval Six signed-MW 5,354 9 5.061 5.897 -0.836 -2.578 to +1.226 Eight MVA-only 3,241 6 6.514 6.489 +0.024 -0.574 to +1.529 All 14 8,595 15 5.609 6.120 -0.512 -1.804 to +0.909

  • By lead band at the six: days 1 to 2 -0.773, days 3 to 5 -1.333, days 6 to 10 -0.463. Every interval includes zero.
  • By Primary at the six: D5 -3.800 (1,629 rows, one event), D10 +0.190, D11 -0.031, D14 +1.957, D16 -0.109. D9 has no scored event.
  • Without D5's one event the six give 3,725 rows, 8 events, a gain of +0.460, and an interval of -0.102 to +1.631. The range over every leave-one-event-out gain at the six is -1.278 to +0.460, and only dropping that event flips the sign.
  • Clean lags win on fewer rows: at the six, 2,284 rows score better with clean lags, 3,046 worse, and 24 tie; at the eight, the counts are 1,633 and 1,608.

The decision rule in the experiment 404 plan says to skip batches 1 and 2, and the data does not support relying on it. The point estimate at the six, -0.836, is under the 0.1 threshold. The interval runs from -2.578 to +1.226, so it includes the threshold, and one event decides the sign. The prediction for the six (a gain of 0.02 to 0.15) is not met. The prediction for the eight (under 0.05) is met, with a gain of +0.024 and an interval of -0.574 to +1.529.

docs.title: Why the sample is small
docs.text:
The harness scores 15 of the 184 corrected events. Of the 78 events at the six, 9 are scored, and of the 88 at the eight, 6 are. The other 18 corrected events belong to D15 (6) and D18 (12), which are in neither group, and the script was not run for them. Seven Primaries (D9, D2, D4, D12, D19, D15, and D18) have no scored event.

Only 36 of the 184 events have a lag that any test forecast origin reads, as experiment 414's audit counted them. A forecast origin reads lags up to about 7.1 days older than itself, and the 123 daily origins of the 4 test refit months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) read none of the other 148 events: 129 lie outside the span from the first to the last origin, and 19 fall in the untested months between refits. Of the 99 events with a gap in the stage-1 median, 96 are among the 148. The 36 events that are read divide into 2 with a gap in the observed power, 6 that fail the sign filter, 7 that fail the step-share filter, 3 that fail the bias filter, and 18 that pass every event filter. The 15 scored events are among the 18.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed. The boosters' mean forecast is not stored, and this experiment scores the mixture quantiles only.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside the quantile contrast: not computed, for the same reason.
  • Triggers fired: three of the seven.
    • Trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction): the prediction was a gain of 0.02 to 0.15 and the gain is -0.836. No explanation was tested, so the page offers an explanation as a caveat only: the clean replacement may be a worse input than the observed reading at D5.
    • Trigger 4 (leaving one out flips the sign): dropping D5's one event flips the six-Primary gain from -0.836 to +0.460.
    • Trigger 7 (a later design depends on the headline): the experiment 404 plan skips batches 1 and 2 on this number.
  • Audit: a fresh Sonnet agent re-derived every number in the results table from the per-row scores and agreed. It found no duplicated rows and no missing scores, ran the leave-one-out checks. Its bootstrap, with a different seed, gave intervals within 0.2 of the ones reported, a spread that is unsurprising with 9 and 6 clusters. Its findings are in the sections above. Its event counts were superseded by the lag-reach count in "Why the sample is small".

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The booster, not the bundle. The gain is for experiment 392's R1 lagged boosters. Experiment 402's stored tables use experiment 381's weekly-refit XGBoost bundle, which scores 5.119 with lags on its harm rows at the six. This experiment's 5.061 is on a different, much smaller row set.
  • The replacement is an estimate. Clean lags are the stage-1 median plus a pre-event bias, so they are not the true demand without the event. Two explanations for the negative gain at D5 are untested. The replacement may be a poor estimate, or the boosters, which were fit on real lags, may score worse on inputs they never saw in training.
  • Single seed and four refit months. Every number is interim.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: This experiment sets out to measure the most any lag-trust method can gain on harm rows. A lag-trust method down-weights the lagged power readings that sit inside a load-shift event. If the readings inside the event were replaced by clean values, the forecast could not be misled by them, so the score gain from that replacement is an upper bound on the gain of any method that changes no other input to the forecast. If the upper bound is under 0.1 points, a learned trust weight cannot be worth building.

docs.title: Stored forecasts versus re-prediction
docs.text: The stored forecasts cannot be re-scored with replaced lags, so the script re-predicts with the boosters. Experiment 402 step 1 read experiment 400's stored forecast files (experiment 381's weekly bundle, with and without lags). Those files hold forecasts made from the observed lags only. Replacing the lags means predicting again, which needs the XGBoost boosters. Experiment 402's step 2 already re-predicts with experiment 392's R1 lagged boosters, which are on disk, so this experiment uses those. This experiment reuses that harness and adds a score. The consequence is that the gain is measured on the R1 boosters, not on the weekly bundle that experiment 402's other tables use. The report states this, and also states the R1 boosters' own CRPS with real lags, so that a reader can compare it with the bundle's 5.119.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Events and clean values. Experiment 400's corrected events per Primary. Inside each event, the reading is replaced by experiment 391's stage-1 median plus the mean of (reading minus median) over the 7 days before the event. Events whose measured step is under 25% of the labelled depth, whose sign disagrees with the label, or whose pre-event bias exceeds half the step are skipped, as in experiment 402 step 2.
  • Runs. For each event and each of the four refit months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), up to 6 daily forecast runs, spread evenly over the runs whose lags touch the event. Each run is predicted twice by the refit's booster for that Primary: with the observed series, and with the clean series. The actual power is the observed series in both cases.
  • Harm rows. Rows with at least one of the three lags inside the event, a target time outside every event of that Primary, a finite actual, and a lead of up to 240 hours.
  • Scores and contrast. Row CRPS for both forecasts. The gain is the mean CRPS with observed lags minus the mean with clean lags, over all harm rows. The interval resamples whole events.
  • Groups. The six signed-MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) carry the decision. The eight MVA-only Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22) are reported beside them. Gain by lead band (days 1 to 2, 3 to 5, 6 to 10) and per Primary are reported.

docs.title: Caveats written before the run
docs.text:
• The sample of runs is not the full harm-row set. At most 6 runs per event and refit month are scored, so events with many runs are under-weighted against the full set. Row counts are smaller (8,595 against experiment 402's 43,024).
  • A row can appear under two events. Each event is scored on its own, with only that event's lags replaced, so a row whose lags touch two events is scored twice, once per event.
  • The replacement is itself an estimate. The stage-1 median plus a bias is not the true clean load, so the gain is an estimate of the upper bound, not the bound.
  • Four refit months, one seed. The R1 boosters are single-seed, so every number is interim.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None so far. Experiment 402's modules sit on an unmerged branch, so this experiment copies the files it needs.

docs.title: Can a mixture density network that writes signed power as demand minus a learned capacity times the CAMS solar shape recover the sign of reverse flow from MVA readings, in lab conditions?
docs.text: Status: done. The registered first test and five post hoc capacity variants all failed; the take- home message above summarises why. The plan sections below were written before any fit, and the results sections follow them.

docs.title: Evidence the plan follows
docs.text:
• Experiment 405 merged as inconclusive. Its placebo gate, a day-shuffled farm, could not be passed, because a shuffled series keeps the monthly daylight profile, which carries 79% of its variance. The same limit applies to S1c-shuffle here, so P3 asks for a margin over the shuffle (0.1 balanced accuracy) and over an hour-and-month baseline (0.05) and does not assume the shuffle scores near chance. The write-up also reports the capacity learned under the shuffle and with u forced to zero, as the design's identifiability check asks. Experiment 409 (planned) tests the day-of-year repair; this plan does not wait for it.
  • Experiment 408 is planned (draft PR 64) and has not reported. Its injection is copied here: three farms rotate across the six signed-MW Primaries (D5 and D11 farm A, D9 and D14 farm B, D10 and D16 farm C), scaled to level times the median absolute sunny-midday reading (CAMS clear-sky index at least 0.7, April to September, 10:00 to 14:00 UTC) before 2025-07-01. Its pass thresholds (0.85, 0.70, 0.03, 5%, 1%) are copied and not otherwise justified, as the design says. Per the manager, no scored fit runs until the neural Discuss session has read 408's page.
  • Experiment 387 merged (not supported). It found Q0 of 0, 2, and 4 points within 0.01 of each other, and a sign set by the start. Here Q0 = 2 points is fixed and the sign comes from the CAMS term, not from a start.
  • Standing rules added on 2026-10-30 are applied. Monthly refits only; cleaned data (the rows of experiment 397, which drops flagged exact-zero half-hours) with the dropped count per fold reported; D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; one pass on the ensemble summary; every fitted network saved as a state file; tails, curtailment cost, and example forecast charts in the score run; draft pull request; the seven-step review order.
  • Two small departures from the design, stated so a reviewer can overrule them. (1) The threshold rule uses the CAMS unit shape in place of "M0c's median", because the rule needs no reading forecast and the first test has no M0c arm. (2) In S1c-shuffle only the solar term's input is permuted. The gate (u >= 0.3) keeps the real unit shape, so the shuffle arm is not handed a different set of folded half-hours, which would make the comparison easier to win.

docs.title: Scoring rules from experiment 408's interim gate (design section 8)
docs.text:
• Matched false-reverse rate replaces the 0.03 margin. The XGBoost experiment's threshold rule scored 0.86 to 0.88 per Primary but called reverse flow on 14 to 19% of half-hours with none, and it reads realised ERA5 shortwave. The write-up reports S1c's recall at the rule's false-reverse rate and the rule's recall at S1c's false-reverse rate, on the same half-hours, and states that the rule is a laboratory reference. The pooled 0.85, per-Primary 0.70, and 5% false-reverse bars stay.
  • Capacity is not read from the rows it labels. The shared log-normal prior stays. The learned C_p is reported at each Primary against the prior centre, and D12's share of negative signed medians is reported only beside the shuffle arm and the prior, never as evidence that D12 exports.
  • D10's real reverse flow is a small sample (130 half-hours). Every recall is reported with the count of half-hours behind it, and the D10 recall is descriptive.
  • Lab conditions. S1c reads realised CAMS at every lead, so the sign's day-ahead behaviour is untested until S1e.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Neural network. Experiment 397's pooled plain mixture density network with the Primary embedding is D, fed the ECMWF ENS mean and spread once (the summary scheme). The irradiance columns and solar geometry are removed from its inputs, as in experiment 405's C arms, so D cannot rebuild the solar bell. Signed power is X = D - C_p u in points of effective capacity (percent). The CAMS unit shape u is studies.pv_physics.plant_power_mw of the fleet plant driven by CAMS hourly irradiance (the quantity studies.dp_features.unit_pv_shape computes), divided by one constant, its 99th percentile over daylight half-hours pooled over the 16 Primaries (the shape is clipped at the plant's inverter limit, so the constant is 1.0 and a capacity is in points at plant clipping). C_p >= 0 is learned per Primary under a log-normal prior centred on the median studies-page capacity of the six signed-MW Primaries (33.5 points at the 2026-06 refit), with a log standard deviation of 0.7.
  • Likelihood, in physical units. Signed Primaries use the mixture density f(x). A folded Primary reads r = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2). Where u >= 0.3 the likelihood is f(y') + f(-y') with y' = sqrt(max(r^2 - Q0^2, 0)) and Q0 = 2 points, and the censored probability P(|X| <= Q0) when r <= Q0 (a reading at or below Q0 bounds |P| by Q0). Where u < 0.3 the likelihood is f(r) truncated to x > 0 and renormalised. The Jacobian of the transform is left out, so log-likelihoods are never compared across arms. The reading forecast is sqrt(q^2 + Q0^2) for each quantile q of |X|.
  • Cadence, rows, and data. Monthly refits on a 730-day window, experiment 397's validation weeks, a recency weight, three seeds in the full run and one in the first test. Test months are 2026-03 and 2026-06. Rows are experiment 397's raw matrices (work/raw/summary), CAMS comes from cams_demand_points.parquet and describes the half-hour itself, which is realised weather available about a day late, so this is lab conditions.
  • Known-answer test. A rotation hides the sign at two signed-MW Primaries (r1: D5 and D10; r2: D9 and D14; r3: D11 and D16) by replacing the reading with sqrt(P'^2 + Q^2), where P' is the signed power minus the injected farm. The other four stay signed. Lags at the hidden pair are folded the same way. A half-hour where any of the three rotation farms has a gap leaves training at the hidden pair in every setting, so the settings train on identical rows, and the dropped count is reported. The farm series stay in the private store, and no farm name, ID, or series is published.
  • Scoring. Gate-open half-hours (u >= 0.3) with CAMS clear-sky index at least 0.7 form the headline slice. A predicted reverse flow is P(X < 0) > 0.5. True reverse flow is P' < 0. Balanced accuracy is the mean of recall on reverse half-hours and specificity on the rest. The false-reverse rate has as its denominator the sunny summer-midday half-hours with neither injected nor real reverse flow. Test rows are the runs whose origin falls in the test month, at leads up to 240 hours. Intervals come from a paired month bootstrap (20,000 resamples) once the full run exists; the first test has two months and reports point estimates only, labelled interim.

docs.title: Arms and settings
docs.text:
