Arm What it is S1c The structural neural network with CAMS u S1c-shuffle S1c with u in the solar term permuted across days within year, month, and half-hour S1c-u0 S1c with C_p fixed at 0 (the identifiability check; the loss gap to S1c is reported) S1c-start-low, S1c-start-high S1c with C_p started at 0.1 and at 3 times the prior centre S1e S1c with u from the ENS mean shortwave, as in experiment 405 (the version that could serve; runs only if P1 passes) M0, M0c Score run only: the plain neural network (stored experiment 397 forecasts) and the plain neural network with CAMS u and clear-sky index as inputs

Settings at the hidden pair: level 2.0 with Q = 2 points and with Q = 4 points (main), level 2.0 at power factor 0.97 (reported only), level 1.0 (P2), and no injection (the placebo of P4, with D10's real reverse flow: 130 half-hours in the registered count, 140 in the scored slice).

docs.title: First test and fit counts
docs.text:
The first test is 12 fits and answers the maintainer's aim before anything larger runs. Rotation r1 (D5 and D10), level 2.0, one seed, test months 2026-03 and 2026-06: S1c at (level 2.0, Q = 2), (2.0, Q = 4), and no injection (6 fits); S1c-shuffle at (2.0, 2) and (2.0, 4) (4 fits); S1c-u0 at (2.0, 2) (2 fits).

If P1, P3, and P4 pass, the full run adds S1c over three rotations, four settings, two folds, and three seeds (72 fits, including the first test), S1c-shuffle at level 2.0 (18), the start check (12), S1c-u0 (6), S1e (36), and the score run of four refitted arms over five folds and three seeds (60), about 204 fits. At 50 to 200 seconds per fit on one GPU process under 8 GB with one feeder core, that is 3 to 11 hours. A timed S1c fit on the 2026-06 fold took 29 s for 15 epochs (45 s with the fold build, 1.4 GB of GPU memory), so 204 fits take about 2.5 hours.

docs.title: Decision rules
docs.text:
• After the first test. Continue only if S1c at (2.0, Q = 2) has balanced accuracy at least 0.85 at each of D5 and D10 and pooled, with a false-reverse rate at most 5% (P1); S1c exceeds S1c-shuffle by at least 0.1 and the hour-and-month baseline by at least 0.05 (P3); and the no-injection placebo has at most 1% false reverse flow at D5 and recalls at least half of D10's real reverse half-hours (P4). Otherwise stop and write up.
  • After the full run. P1 to P5 are read pooled over the three rotations with month-bootstrap intervals. If P1 passes and P2 holds, label signed output "inferred, heavy reverse flow only". If P2 fails because the method passes at level 1.0, that is a positive result.
  • XGBoost result. Experiment 408's gate and tau set the interpretation. If 408 passes level 2.0 and S1c fails, the decomposition is at fault; if both fail, the readings lack the information.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• The open-gate likelihood is not normalised. The folded density already covers all |X|, and the censored band for r <= Q0 counts the band |X| <= Q0 again. The extra term fires only on the rare readings at or below Q0, and the design prescribes it. Reading Q = 4 as "floor exactly right" is wrong: every reading is then at least 4 points, so the fit leans towards |X| >= 3.5 on gate-open rows. Only Q = 2 matches Q0.
  • The prior centre uses all six signed-MW Primaries, including the hidden pair, so their known capacity enters slightly (a median of six, log standard deviation 0.7).
  • The shuffle keeps the daylight profile, so S1c-shuffle may score well above chance (experiment 405). P3 is a margin, and the capacity learned under the shuffle is reported.
  • D can absorb the PV shape from hour of day, month, temperature, and the Primary embedding. If S1c-u0 loses little against S1c, the Primary embedding is removed from D and kept in the head and in C_p.
  • Moderate reverse flow may stay invisible, as in experiment 366, and non-solar reverse flow breaks the physics assumption, as at D15.
  • A real farm's shape differs from the CAMS unit shape, which is why the test cannot pass by construction, unlike experiment 387's.
  • Lab conditions. CAMS is realised weather available about a day late, so S1c describes a laboratory result; S1e is the version that could serve.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text: Sonnet writes the code. A fresh Sonnet agent reviews the code before the first scored fit, and a second review follows if the first flags many problems. The timed fit is not scored. Results get a fresh Sonnet re-derivation of the headline numbers and the audit triggers, and the write-up gets a Sonnet review of the numbers and of the prose.

docs.title: Post hoc capacity variants (fixed before any variant score was read)
docs.text:
The maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-30 allows three labelled post hoc variants after the first test failed P1 and P4, then stops the experiment. The registered first test stays reported as a failure. The variants test whether the placebo's invented reverse flow comes from fitting the capacity C_p on the rows it labels. All three use rotation r1, level 2.0 with Q = 2 points, one seed, and the two test months, and the P1 and P4 bars and the matched false-reverse comparison are unchanged.

  • Variant (a), cfix. Every C_p is held at the prior centre (33.5 points at the 2026-06 refit) and is not trained.
  • Variant (b), cknown. Only Primaries whose target is not folded set C_p. A folded Primary (the MVA-only eight and the hidden pair) uses the geometric mean of the learned C_p of D9, D11, D14, D15, D16, and D18, and the folded rows send no gradient to that mean. The prior applies to the six.
  • Variant (c), sd03. As S1c with the prior's log standard deviation cut from 0.7 to 0.3.
  • Fits per variant. The real-sky arm at (level 2.0, Q = 2) and with no injection, and the shuffled-sky arm at (level 2.0, Q = 2), each on both test months: 6 fits, 18 in all.
  • Decision. If a variant passes P1 and P4, the result is labelled post hoc and reported beside the failed registered test. If none passes, the page is written up as the sixth failed treatment of the MVA problem, and S1e and the full run do not run.

docs.title: Second post hoc round: the capacity prior at full weight (fixed before any score was read)
docs.text:
The neural Discuss session asked for one more labelled rerun after sd03 showed the registered prior to be inert. The registered loss adds the prior's negative log density to the mean loss divided by the effective row count (5.6 million rows with weights). That is the posterior over the summed log-likelihood, so the prior weighs as little as one row in 5.6 million. The rows are not independent, because each valid time appears once for every run that forecasts it, which is why the request is reasonable. The two new arms add the prior to the mean loss undivided, so its weight is the effective row count times larger.

  • p07. Undivided prior, log standard deviation 0.7 (the registered width).
  • p03. Undivided prior, log standard deviation 0.3.
  • Fits. As the first post hoc round: the real-sky arm at level 2.0 with Q = 2 and with no injection, and the shuffled-sky arm at level 2.0 with Q = 2, on both test months, 6 fits per arm and 12 in all. Rotation r1 and seed 0.
  • Reported. The capacity reached at D5 against the prior centre of 33.5 points, and the prior's share of the gradient on the log capacities (all Primaries, and D5 alone) at the start of training and at the best state, measured on one fixed batch of 16,384 training rows.
  • Decision. The P1 and P4 bars and the matched false-reverse comparison are unchanged. If neither arm passes, the page is written up as the seventh failed treatment and the maintainer decides what follows.

docs.title: Variant results (post hoc, one seed, two test months, interim)
docs.text:
No variant passed. Holding the capacity down removed the false reverse-flow calls and the skill with them, and narrowing the divided prior changed nothing. Figure 1 shows every arm.

  • cfix (capacity held at 33.5 points). Pooled balanced accuracy 0.542 (March) and 0.612 (June), false-reverse rate 0.1% and 1.7%, no false reverse flow at D5 with no injection. Its shuffled-sky arm scores 0.583 and 0.575, so the real sky beats the shuffle by -0.04 and +0.04. The held capacity is below the injected farm's size, so the neural network cannot explain the dip.
  • cknown (capacity set by the six Primaries whose target is not folded; the hidden pair uses their geometric mean, 27.6 to 29.5 points). Balanced accuracy 0.551 and 0.574, false-reverse rate 0.5% and 1.4%, no false reverse flow at D5 with no injection. The shuffled-sky arm scores 0.553 and 0.508. The pair's true capacity need not equal the six's mean, so part of the miss is a capacity mismatch.
  • sd03 (prior log standard deviation 0.3, divided by the row count). Within 0.001 of S1c in balanced accuracy, with the same learned capacities (71 to 78 points at D5). The prior is added to the loss divided by the effective row count of 5.6 million rows. At the fitted capacities it is worth 13 nats (S1c) or 70 nats (sd03) in the summed loss, which moved the capacities by under 0.2 points. The registered prior therefore did not constrain the capacity.
  • Matched false-reverse rate. At the threshold rule's false-reverse rate, cfix and cknown recall 0.98 to 1.00 of the reverse half-hours. At their own near-zero false-reverse rate the rule recalls 0.0 in March and 0.33 to 0.46 in June.
  • Not produced. The example forecast charts and event plots the standing rules ask for are not drawn. The truth series of the hidden pair is the signed power minus a metered farm's output, and publishing it would reveal that farm's series.
  • Reviews. The code review (fresh Sonnet) found no must-fix; a second fresh Sonnet review of the variant code found no must-fix and one labelling fix (applied: the score output calls the capacities "used"). A fresh Sonnet agent recomputed the first-test numbers, which matched. The variant numbers come from the same scoring code, and the write-up review follows.

docs.title: Second post hoc round: the prior at full weight (interim, same rotation and seed)
docs.text:
Giving the prior full weight held the capacity at the prior centre and reproduced cfix. With the prior added to the mean loss undivided, the capacity at D5 reached 33.5 to 33.7 points (against 71 to 78 without it), and the sign skill fell with it. The two arms scored within 0.003 of each other and of cfix.

  • p07 (log standard deviation 0.7) and p03 (0.3). Pooled balanced accuracy 0.543 and 0.541 (March), 0.611 and 0.613 (June). False-reverse rate 0.1% (March) and 1.7% to 1.8% (June). With no injection, no false reverse flow at D5. The shuffled-sky arms score 0.583 and 0.586 (March) and 0.574 and 0.575 (June), so the real sky beats the shuffle by -0.04 and +0.04. P1 and P3 fail.
  • Prior's share of the gradient on the log capacities. The share is the norm of the prior's gradient over the norm of the total gradient on one fixed batch of 16,384 training rows. It is 0 at the start, by construction, because the capacity starts at the prior centre. After the first epoch it is 1.3 to 2.4 over all Primaries and 1.1 to 17.8 at D5, and at the best state it is 0.8 to 2.5 over all Primaries and 0.4 to 40 at D5. A share above 1 means the likelihood's gradient opposes the prior's: the two nearly cancel at the capacity the fit reaches, so the likelihood pulls upwards about as hard as the prior pulls down. The D5 share varies widely because the total gradient there is close to zero.
  • Reading. The likelihood prefers a capacity of 70 to 80 points and the sign skill needs it. A prior strong enough to keep the capacity near the 33.5-point centre of the six signed Primaries removes the skill, so the capacity that reads the injected farm is also the capacity that reads a real midday dip as reverse flow. Gradient clipping at a global norm of 1 includes the log capacities, so the large prior gradient also rescales the demand module's gradients; Adam absorbs most of that.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet review of the changed loss found no must-fix. It noted that the extra random draw for the gradient-share batch shifts the batch order, so the earlier arms would not bit-reproduce on a rerun (the draw now uses its own generator).

docs.title: First test result (interim: two test months, one seed, no intervals)
docs.text:
The first test failed P1 and P4, so the full run was not started. S1c reaches pooled balanced accuracy 0.854 in 2026-06 but 0.741 in 2026-03, and its false-reverse rate on gate-open sunny half-hours is 16.9% (June) and 6.7% (March), against a 5% bar. The no-injection placebo invents reverse flow at D5 on 18% (March) and 47% (June) of those half-hours. The learned capacity at D5 rises to 74 to 78 points without any injected farm, against a prior centre of 33.5, so the capacity is fitted from the rows it labels.

  • P1 (level 2.0, Q = 2). Fails. Pooled balanced accuracy 0.741 (March, 1,416 reverse half-hours) and 0.854 (June, 3,460); D5 0.736 and 0.834, D10 0.757 and 0.872. False-reverse rate 6.7% and 16.9%. Q = 4 gives the same numbers to within 0.003.
  • Matched false-reverse rate. At S1c's false-reverse rate the threshold rule's recall is 0.47 to 0.49 in March (S1c: 0.53 to 0.59) and 0.86 in June (S1c: 0.87 to 0.89). At the rule's false-reverse rate (57% to 64% in March, 40% to 42% in June) S1c's recall is 0.98 to 1.00. The rule is a laboratory reference that reads realised CAMS here.
  • P3. Passes. S1c exceeds S1c-shuffle by 0.18 (March) and 0.32 (June) balanced accuracy, and the hour-and-month baseline by 0.20 and 0.09. The shuffle scores 0.53 to 0.56, near chance, so the daylight profile alone does not carry the sign here.
  • P4. Fails. With no injection, D5 has no real reverse flow, yet S1c calls it on 18% (March) and 47% (June) of gate-open sunny half-hours. D10's recall of its real reverse flow is 0.06 on 140 half-hours in June (none are in the March slice); that recall is descriptive.
  • Identifiability check. S1c with C_p fixed at zero scores 0.55 (March) and 0.74 (June) pooled, against 0.74 and 0.85 for S1c, so the demand module absorbs part of the sign from hour, month, temperature, and the Primary embedding, and the CAMS term adds about 0.1 to 0.2.
  • Sunny summer middays. On sunny summer-midday half-hours (UTC 10:00 to 14:00, April to September) with no reverse flow, S1c calls reverse flow on 85% of them in June (245 half-hours) and 14% in March (147 half-hours; the March subset is small).
  • Re-derivation. A fresh Sonnet agent recomputed every number above, including the matched false-reverse comparison and the learned capacities, from the forecast files with its own code. All matched within 0.005, and the files have no duplicate rows, no origins outside the month, and a median sign that agrees with P(X < 0) on every row.
  • Lab caveat. S1c reads realised CAMS at every lead, so the day-ahead behaviour of the sign is untested until S1e.

Per the stop rule, the work ends here as the seventh failed treatment of the MVA problem; the maintainer decides what follows. Fits: 12 in the first test, 18 in the first post hoc round, and 12 in the second, each taking 29 to 83 s. A fresh Sonnet agent recomputed the numbers and reviewed the write-up; its findings are applied.

docs.title: Can one neural network that mixes shared libraries of learned daily shapes and learned temperature responses forecast Primary demand about as well as the plain mixture density network?
docs.text:
Take-home message: a neural network built from shared, readable parts forecast substation demand less accurately than the plain neural network. We asked whether a neural network that writes each substation's demand as a mix of shared learned daily shapes and shared learned temperature responses can forecast as accurately as the plain pooled neural network of experiment 397. Both predict a full range of outcomes, and we tested both on five held-out months, with three training runs (seeds) each. The error score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) at 1 to 10 days ahead, in points of the substation's capacity. The library network scored 0.174 points worse at the 6 substations that record the direction of flow (the signed-MW six) and 0.228 points worse at the other 8 (the MVA-only eight). It beat the plain network in 2 of 5 months at the six and in 1 of 5 at the eight.

The first month we scored was misleading. In 2026-01 alone, with one seed, the library network scored 0.379 points better at the six. A fresh audit found no code error. It traced the gain to the library network's own yearly (day-of-year) coefficients, which had learned the level of the one earlier January in the training data. Over the five months the mean difference reversed, and the verdict is not supported. All numbers are interim: five test months, no interval.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS at days 1 to 10, mean over the five test months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), equal weight per Primary substation, in points of capacity (smaller is better). Arms D0 to D2 use 3 seeds averaged in quantile space. D0 is the plain pooled network, D0Y is D0 plus the yearly columns, D1 adds the shape library, and D2 has the shape and response libraries.

Arm Signed-MW six MVA-only eight D0, pooled plain network 3.322 3.908 D0Y, D0 plus the yearly columns 3.336 3.893 D1, shape library, head reads all inputs 3.405 3.956 D2, shape and response libraries, Primary mix 3.496 4.136 Generalised additive model (GAM) stack (experiment 377, stored) 3.247 4.135 Monthly XGBoost (experiment 389, stored) 3.544 4.019 Pooled plain network of experiment 397 (stored, no D15 and D18 cut) 3.270 3.866
  • The library network scored worse than the plain network at both groups (C1, D2 minus D0). The difference is +0.174 at the six and +0.228 at the eight. The monthly values at the six are in the second figure.
  • The libraries did not help one at a time either. D1 minus D0 is +0.082 and +0.048 (C2), and D2 minus D1 is +0.092 and +0.180 (C3).
  • The yearly columns alone do not explain the loss. D2 minus D0Y is +0.160 and +0.243 (C5), and D0Y minus D0 is +0.014 and -0.015 (C6).
  • Under the pre-registered rule D2 does not advance. The five-month mean of D2 minus D0 exceeds +0.03 at both groups. It lies between +0.03 and +0.30, so the stop rule did not fire on the mean, and the choice to continue or stop is the maintainer's. D2 minus D0 reached +0.699 at the six in 2025-12.
  • Arm D3 (one fleet-wide mix) was fitted on 2026-01 only, with one seed. It scored 4.745 at the six and 4.503 at the eight, so D3 minus D2 was +0.883 and +0.565.
  • The median error of D2 was larger at both groups. The mean absolute error of the median forecast, in MW at the six and the eight, is 5.69 and 7.08 for D0, 5.76 and 7.04 for D0Y, 5.82 and 7.13 for D1, and 6.02 and 7.23 for D2.
  • D2 covered the upper tail better than D0 at the six and worse at the eight. The table gives coverage (nominal 0.95 and 0.99) and pinball loss in points, mean over months.
Arm, group q95 coverage q99 coverage pinball q01 pinball q05 pinball q95 pinball q99 D0, six 0.829 0.926 0.216 0.712 1.091 0.436 D2, six 0.880 0.975 0.323 0.954 0.932 0.243 D0, eight 0.899 0.969 0.224 0.851 1.011 0.281 D2, eight 0.889 0.966 0.292 0.998 1.164 0.372
  • At the six, D2's upper quantiles have the lower pinball loss and its lower quantiles the higher. For example, the q99 loss is 0.243 against 0.436. At the eight, both tails are worse. The curtailment-cost measure was not computed for this screen.
  • Per Primary (C1, mean of five months), D2 is better at D5 (-0.276), D16 (-0.094), D14 (-0.068), and D21 (-0.053). It is worse at D11 (+1.161), D8 (+0.657), D12 (+0.401), D3 (+0.262), and D10 (+0.249). D15 and D18 are report-only.

  • Learned curves (D2, 2026-01 fold, seed 0). The three heating curves are nearly identical, so the library did not learn three different responses. The eight learned shapes are smooth and mix freely, and this page does not claim that any one of them is a physical daily profile. The comparison with the GAM's fitted curves and the three-seed stability check were not run, because D2 did not advance.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
The predictions were written for the 2026-01 fold with one seed. We judge them here on the five-month means, and note the one-fold outcome where it differs.

  • P1 (D2 minus D0 between -0.05 and +0.25 at both groups): held on the five-month means (+0.174 and +0.228). It failed on 2026-01 with seed 0 at the six (-0.379).
  • P2 (D1 minus D0 between -0.05 and +0.10): held on the means (+0.082 and +0.048). It failed at the six on 2026-01 (+0.269 with three seeds).
  • P3 (D3 minus D2 between 0 and +0.30): failed on 2026-01, the only fold with D3 (+0.883 at the six, +0.565 at the eight).
  • P4 (q95 coverage at the six between 0.82 and 0.90): held on the means for D0 (0.829), D1 (0.827), and D2 (0.880). It failed for D0 and D1 on 2026-01 with seed 0 (0.757 and 0.698).
  • P5 (mixed temperature response monotone at 14 of 16 Primaries): all 16 were monotone, which holds by construction.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The median forecast and the mean forecast agree. Median minus the weighted mean of the 11 quantiles (MW) is -0.028 for D0, -0.026 for D0Y, -0.033 for D1, and -0.026 for D2, so no arm's spread shifts its forecast.
  • The median error points the same way as the CRPS. The error figures are in Results.
  • Two audit triggers fired. D2 minus D0 on 2026-01 with seed 0 was -0.379, outside the predicted -0.05 to +0.25. D1, which contains D0's inputs, scored worse than D0 on 2026-01.
  • A fresh Sonnet audit found no bug. It re-derived the per-Primary scores, found no leakage, and traced the 2026-01 gap to D2's yearly coefficients: zeroing them at inference, without a refit, moved D2's seed-0 score at the six from 3.861 to 5.298. The audit could not say why seed-0 D0 sat 0.1 to 0.25 above the stored seeds of experiment 397 on 2026-01. On five months the gap is 0.05 at the six and 0.04 at the eight.
  • The five months show the 2026-01 gain was specific to that month, because D2 minus D0 is positive in four of the five months at the eight and in three at the six.
  • Not tested: the screen has no intervals and no leave-one-Primary-out check, so the audit triggers for those were not run.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The advance threshold of 0.03 points is the manager's default, and the maintainer has not confirmed it. The five months have no interval, so every number is interim.
  • The headline range is 1 to 10 days ahead, the range NGED care about.
  • Yearly harmonics sit in D1, D2, and D0Y but not in D0. The data start in April 2024, so the yearly terms were fitted on at most two years.
  • D0 is not a copy of the network of experiment 397. It uses the D15 and D18 cut, its own standardiser, and its own seed stream, and it scores 0.05 worse than the stored 3-seed pooled network at the six.
  • No rows with a missing target were found. The raw matrices from experiment 397 omit the flagged half-hours already, so this experiment did not count them.
  • Shapes and the gate are normalised on 4,096 sampled training rows, not on a grid of ordinary days.
  • Unlogged load-shift events. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from their logs, so the rows may hold events that no label covers.
  • Resources. The fits ran on the GPU. A D2 fit took 51 to 257 s, peak GPU memory was 1.6 GB, and peak host memory was 8.3 GB on the largest fold. Fitted networks are in the experiment's private folder under work/models/, and the scripts are in ml-experiments/00413-differentiable-physics-demand-network-part-1/.

docs.title: Plan as committed before any fit
docs.text: Status: planned. Nothing has been fitted. The plan follows the Design session's note (differentiable_physics_demand_design_answer.md, Opus-reviewed and approved by the maintainer on 2026-10-30) and the manager's programme brief for experiment 7.

docs.title: What is asked
docs.text: The question is whether a neural network built from shared, readable parts can forecast Primary demand as well as a plain neural network. The aim behind the series is a forecaster that keeps the GAM's (generalised additive model's) readable shapes and temperature curves and gains the adaptability of the networks. Experiment 397's page gave its pooled plain network 3.264 points of CRPS (days 1 to 10) at the signed-MW six, close to the GAM stack's 3.239. The first fit checks, on one winter month, whether the library design loses much against that plain network. It is a screen to stop a poor design early, not a ranking.

docs.title: Review of the plan against the latest evidence
docs.text:
• Experiment 397 (merged): the pooled plain network is the control. Its inputs, rows, folds, early-stopping rule and training loop are copied. The attention gate was inert, so the design has none.
  • Experiment 403 (merged): pooling beat one network per Primary by 0.185 at the signed-MW six and 0.161 at the MVA-only eight, so the libraries are shared across all 16 Primaries.
  • Experiment 405 (merged, inconclusive) and the open plan for experiment 409 (PR 66): a network with no day-of-year term had no other home for the monthly daylight profile, so a solar term could not be separated from it. The design note already keeps fixed yearly harmonics with Primary-specific coefficients, and this plan adds them to the physics output of arms D1 to D3 and flags that difference from D0 (see "Caveats").
  • Experiment 394 (merged): the ensemble mean carries the XGBoost gain, the spread adds little. The network reads the mean for the responses and the spread only in the residual head.
  • Experiment 398 (merged) and the standing rule of 2026-10-30: scoring actuals and lags are cleaned (flagged substation_zero half-hours are nulls in experiment 87's observed.parquet), D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01 in training, lags, inference and scoring, and retraining is monthly. All three are applied; the fold counts of dropped half-hours are printed.
  • Experiments 404, 406, 407, 410, 412 are still open. None changes this plan. Their results may change the control (a lagless module, no embedding), and the manager decides whether D0 is then replaced before the five folds.
  • Nothing in the design note changed, except two points the note left open and this plan fixes below: which inputs the residual head reads in D1, and how arms are compared across the two groups.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Every arm predicts the Primary's power as a fraction of its effective capacity, standardised per Primary on the fold's training rows, as a 3-component Gaussian mixture (the head of experiment 397's PlainMdn). The arms differ in what produces the mixture's means.

  • D0, control. The pooled plain network of experiment 397: all summary inputs, an 8-wide Primary embedding, 2 hidden layers of 64 (setting g01).
  • Shape library. 8 learned curves (K_s = 8) from a small network (2 hidden layers of 32) that reads the calendar and holiday columns of experiment 397 (the hour of day as sine and cosine of one and two cycles, the day of the week, the COVID indicator, and the Christmas and bank-holiday columns). Each curve is normalised on a fixed grid of ordinary days (48 half-hours by 7 days of the week): zero mean and unit root-mean-square over the grid.
  • Response library. 6 learned monotone curves (K_r = 6): 3 heating curves that fall with the ensemble-mean temperature below the reference of 15.5 °C and are zero above it, 1 cooling curve that rises above the reference and is zero below it, 1 curve of the ensemble-mean shortwave radiation (zero at no sunshine), and 1 curve of the cosine of the solar zenith angle (zero when the sun is down). Each curve is a piecewise-linear function with 16 knots, whose slopes are non-negative or non-positive by a softplus, so monotonicity holds by construction, and each is normalised to unit root-mean-square over the training range.
  • Primary mix. An 8-wide Primary embedding feeds linear layers with softmax outputs, which give mixing weights over the shapes and over the responses, one non-negative amplitude per library, and a Primary-specific level. A third softmax-free layer gives the gate: the response part is multiplied by gate(t) = exp(c · shape(t)), divided by its mean over the grid, so the gate has a daily mean of 1. This is the interaction between the temperature response and the part of the day. The mean physics output is mu = level + A_s * sum_i a_i shape_i(t) + A_r * sum_j b_j response_j * gate(t) + yearly, where yearly is the sine and cosine of the day of the year at 1 and 2 cycles with Primary-specific coefficients (the GAM's fixed low-order harmonics).
  • Residual mixture. The mixture's component means are mu plus learned offsets, and its weights and widths are learned. In D2 and D3 the mixture reads only the three origin lags and their missing flags and ages, the lead, the ensemble spread columns, and mu. It does not read the weather means or the calendar, because it could then learn the demand itself and leave the library curves unidentified.
  • D1, shape library only. mu = level + A_s * sum_i a_i shape_i(t) + yearly. The design note says "plain MDN residual" and does not say what it reads. Without a response library the residual has no other route to temperature, so in D1 the mixture reads all of D0's inputs, the Primary embedding, and mu. D1 is therefore D0 plus a shape-library mean, not a restricted network.
  • D2, shape and response libraries with the Primary mix (the main arm), as above.
  • D3, D2 with one fleet-wide mix. The Primary embedding is removed everywhere: one set of mixing weights, amplitudes, gate, and level for all 16 Primaries.

Identifiability constraints. Shapes are zero-mean and unit-RMS on the grid, responses are zero at the reference and unit-RMS, mixing weights are softmax, and the gate has a daily mean of 1. The yearly term and the temperature response stay collinear, and so do the solar-zenith response and the daily shapes in daylight. The first fit does not test whether those pairs separate; the stability check in the five-fold stage does.

docs.title: Folds, rows, and compute
docs.text:
• Fold and seed. The 2026-01 fold of experiment 397 (the test month 2026-01, trained on the 24 months before 2026-01-01), seed 0, 4 arms. Selection of rows, early stopping (one week in 12 held out with purging), recency weights, widths and training loop are experiment 397's.
  • Hyperparameters. K_s, K_r, the knot count, and the embedding width are fixed above from the design note, and are not tuned on any scored month.
  • Cleaning and cuts. Rows, lags, and scoring actuals from experiment 87's cleaned observed data; D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01 (training, lags, inference, and scoring); the number of dropped half-hours is printed for the fold.
  • Cadence. One fit per fold, equivalent to a monthly refit.
  • Compute. One GPU process under 8 GB of GPU memory, 1 feeder core, MemoryMax=8G. The timed fit is D2 on the fold, on the GPU, plus one epoch on 1 CPU thread for comparison, as the GPU rule requires. Reused stored forecasts: none for D0 (its stored forecasts predate the D15 and D18 cut, so D0 is refitted); the GAM stack and XGBoost forecasts are references only.
  • Fitted networks are saved as .pt files under the experiment's private work/models/.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
• Contrasts, each on CRPS at days 1 to 10 per group (signed-MW six, MVA-only eight, D15 and D18 report-only): C1 D2 minus D0, C2 D1 minus D0, C3 D2 minus D1, C4 D3 minus D2. One fold and one seed give no interval, and every number is interim.
  • Per-Primary table of C1, so a gap concentrated at one Primary is visible.
  • Tails: coverage at q95 and q99 and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99, per group, with and without the 1.15 widening of experiment 87.
  • Interpretation outputs: the 8 shape curves, the 6 response curves, a table of each Primary's mixing weights and amplitudes, and the monotonicity check of the mixed temperature response at each Primary. The comparison with the GAM's fitted curves and the three-seed stability check wait for the five-fold stage.
  • Example forecasts: a day-ahead forecast and a 14-day forecast from one run at a Primary, for D0 and D2, with median, 50% and 90% bands, and actuals.
  • Checks (the skill's audit triggers): the median minus the mean forecast per group, the mean forecast's error beside the quantile score, and which of the seven triggers fired.

docs.title: Code review
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet reviewer read the code before any fit. It found no leakage and no blocker. Six findings were triaged: D1's mixture now reads the Primary embedding as D0's does (so D1 is D0 plus a shape-library mean); the gate exponent is clamped to plus or minus 3; D0's initial weights are seeded; the scorer's mean check is labelled in MW and uses the stored quantile weights; a guard rejects a reference temperature outside the input clip range. The sixth finding is accepted as a caveat below.

docs.title: Plan caveats
docs.text:
• The monotonicity check cannot fail. Each curve is monotone by construction, so P5 and its stop rule test the code, not the design.

  • Shapes and the gate are normalised on 4,096 sampled training rows, not on a grid of ordinary days.

  • Yearly harmonics are in D1 to D3 and not in D0. A gain or loss of D2 against D0 therefore mixes the effect of the library design with the effect of the yearly harmonics. If D2 advances, the five-fold stage adds D0 with the yearly harmonics as an input.

  • Lead range. The headline band is 1 to 10 days, the horizon NGED cares about.
  • One winter month, one seed. No claim of benefit, and cold winter nights are not scored separately until the five-fold stage.
  • Unlogged load-shift events. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from their logs, so the rows may hold events that no label covers.

docs.title: Post hoc: does filling the gaps in the stage-1 median, so that more load-shift events are scored, change the counterfactual-lag gain on harm rows?
docs.text: Status: done. Filling the gaps added no scored event. The sections from "The fill rule" onward are the plan, written before any score of the filled run was read. The experiment is post hoc: it exists because experiment 411 scored only 15 of 184 corrected events, and the design change (the fill rule) was chosen after that result was read. The fill rule below was fixed from counts of the input gaps, not from any score.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The filled run scored the same 15 events as experiment 411, with the same numbers. The prediction of at least 40 events scored failed, because the gaps were not what limited the sample. The prediction of a gain between -0.5 and +0.3 at the six also failed, because the gain is -0.836. Intervals are 95% event-cluster bootstraps (2,000 resamples). This run's random stream differs from experiment 411's, so its intervals differ from experiment 411's by up to about 0.1 (experiment 411 reports -2.578 to +1.226 at the six for the same rows).

Group Harm rows Events CRPS real lags CRPS clean lags Gain 95% interval Six signed-MW 5,354 9 5.061 5.897 -0.836 -2.468 to +1.301 Eight MVA-only 3,241 6 6.514 6.489 +0.024 -0.568 to +1.550 All 14 8,595 15 5.609 6.120 -0.512 -1.798 to +0.863
  • Added events: none. The report's "added events" section is empty.
  • Leave-one-event-out gain range: -1.278 to +0.460 at the six, and -0.354 to +0.877 at the eight. Dropping D5's one event still flips the six-Primary sign.
  • No figure: the scored events are experiment 411's, so its figure applies unchanged.

docs.title: Why no event was added
docs.text:
Only 36 of the 184 corrected events have a lag that any test forecast origin reads. A forecast origin reads lags up to about 7.1 days older than the origin. The audit listed every grid index read by the 123 daily origins of the 4 test refit months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) and checked each event. This leaves 148 events that no origin reads: 129 lie outside the span from the first to the last origin, and 19 fall in the untested months between refits. The audit's counting script is not part of the experiment's code. Of the 99 events that have a gap in the stage-1 median, 96 are among the 129, so experiment 411's count of "99 events lost to gaps" mostly counted events that no origin could read. The 36 events that are read divide as follows:

  • Gap in the observed power: 2 events. Each also has a gap in the stage-1 median, and the fill cannot repair observed power.
  • Sign, step share, and bias filters: 6, 7, and 3 events.
  • Pass every event filter: 18 events. The 15 scored events are among them. The other 3 either produce no harm rows in the sampled runs or belong to D15 and D18, which this run did not score.

The fill repaired none of the events that are read, so it changed no score. That is why the rows match experiment 411 exactly.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site and the error of the mean forecast: not computed, because the boosters' mean forecast is not stored; the scored forecasts are the mixture quantiles.
  • Reproduction: the 8,595 row scores are bit-identical to experiment 411's (a full join on Primary, event, origin, and valid time leaves no unmatched row, and the largest difference in either CRPS is 0.0), so every point estimate in the table matches.
  • Triggers fired: three of the seven.
    • Trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction): 15 events were scored against at least 40 predicted, and the gain is -0.836 against a predicted -0.5 to +0.3. The reason is explained and checked above (the lag-reach count).
    • Trigger 4 (leaving one out flips the sign): dropping D5's one event flips the six-Primary gain from -0.836 to +0.460.
    • Trigger 7 (a later design depends on the headline): the experiment 404 plan skips batches 1 and 2 on this number.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first run and found that the fill would change the pre-event bias of the original events; the fix computes the bias on the unfilled median, and the reproduction above confirms it. A second fresh Sonnet agent then re-derived the table from the row scores, rebuilt the event accounting with its own script, and reviewed this page's prose. It found that the first draft misdescribed the reach count, claimed the fill worked on 3 events, and quoted two different intervals for the same rows. All findings were applied.

docs.title: The fill rule
docs.text:
The rule is fixed before any score is read. Experiment 411 scored 15 of the 184 events, and 99 events have a gap in the stage-1 median. The plan chose the fill rule because 46% of the event half-hours (14,184 of 30,832) have no stage-1 median. The gaps are median-only in 75 events and in both the median and the observed power in 24 events; the observed power alone is never missing. Of the 75 median-only events, the longest gap is at most 12 half-hours in 8 events, at most 48 in 30 events, at most 96 in 39, and at most 336 in 70. Linear interpolation across gaps that long would invent a median, so the fill is different:

  • Where the stage-1 median is missing, it is replaced by the mean observed reading at the same half-hour of the previous 4 weeks. The mean uses only readings that are finite and outside every labelled event of the Primary. The fill leaves the value missing when fewer than 2 of the 4 weeks qualify.
  • Every reading used is older than the half-hour it fills, so a lag never receives a value from after itself.
  • The pre-event bias is computed on the unfilled median, so the 15 original events keep the bias that experiment 411 used and should reproduce its scores.
  • Nothing else changes. Events with missing observed power stay skipped (24 events). The 25% step filter, the sign filter, the bias filter, the run sample (at most 6 runs per event and refit month), and the scoring are the same as in experiment 411.

docs.title: What the experiment answers
docs.text: The experiment tests whether the fill rule changes the answer, not whether the filled median is the true clean load. A seasonal profile ignores weather and holidays, so the clean lags are an estimate with an error that grows with the gap. The report therefore gives the gain separately for the 15 original events, which have no filled values, and for the added events, which do.

docs.title: Caveats written before the run
docs.text:
• The sample is selected. Events with missing observed power stay out, and the sign, step, and bias filters still apply, so the scored events are not a random sample of the 184.
  • The filled median for a long gap is a seasonal average. It is as good as the previous weeks are for the event's own weeks; an event with a holiday in it is badly filled.
  • Single seed and four refit months. Every number is interim.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Code. The scripts copy experiment 411's, with one added function (fill_median). The scripts re-predict experiment 392's R1 lagged boosters twice per sampled run, with the observed series and with the clean series, and score both forecasts against the observed power on harm rows (target outside every event, at least one lag inside it, lead up to 240 hours).
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first run. A second fresh Sonnet agent audited the results and reviewed the write-up in one pass.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Does the pooled plain mixture density network forecast demand at two bulk supply points and two grid supply points as well as it does at Primaries, and do the Primaries beneath a node help?
docs.text:
Take-home message: one pooled neural network, fitted on the 16 Primaries and the four supply points together, forecasts the bulk supply points better than the weekly XGBoost forecast does. At the grid supply points it ties the XGBoost forecast, and only with prediction bands about 100 points of capacity wide. The Primaries beneath a supply point do not help as inputs.

We asked whether the pooled plain mixture density network of experiment 403 works at two bulk supply points (BSPs: D13, D17) and two grid supply points (GSPs: D1, D6). We call these four the nodes. They are the nodes of experiment 386. A BSP connects the 132 kV electricity network to the 33 kV electricity network, and a GSP connects the transmission network to the 132 kV electricity network. A Primary is one of the 16 primary substations that experiments 397 and 403 forecast. "Pooled" means one neural network fitted jointly to many substations. A mixture density network is a neural network that outputs a probability distribution as a mixture of three bell curves. BG2 is the weekly-refitted XGBoost forecast of experiment 87.

For each of four test months we fitted the network on the 24 months before the month and scored it on that month. We compared it with a copy fitted at the Primaries only and with the forecasts that experiment 386 stored. The verdict is supported. "Interim" applies to every interval, because four test months give wide intervals. The BSP gain over BG2 is the one claim made.

docs.title: Stop rule and decision rule
docs.text:
We registered these rules before reading any score.

  • Stop rule A. Stop if N1 is worse than climatology at 3 or more of the 4 nodes in both stage 1 test months.
  • Stop rule B. Stop if N1 minus P0 at the 14 countable Primaries exceeds +0.10 points in both stage 1 test months.
  • Stop rule C. Skip stage 3 if N2 minus N1 is 0 or higher in both stage 2 test months at both groups of nodes.
  • Decision rule. The hypothesis is supported if N1 beats P0 at the nodes at both groups and is not worse than the monthly XGBoost control by more than 0.30 points at either group.

docs.title: Arms and results
docs.text:
CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score estimated from 11 quantiles, in points of effective capacity (the percentage of the substation's effective capacity), at days 1 to 10. The four test months are 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. Each CRPS is the average of 3 seeds, averaged level by level over the quantiles. P0 and N1 count 14 Primaries as countable, because D15 and D18 share a substation number and lack data before 2025-03-01. The 95% intervals come from resampling the four test months.

  • P0: the pooled network fitted at the 16 Primaries only, applied to a node with the mean of the 16 Primary embeddings and the node's own target statistics.
  • N1: fitted at the 16 Primaries and the 4 nodes, with a node-type input.
  • N2: N1 plus the mean of three lagged readings of the Primaries beneath the node (origin lags: the newest reading before the forecast origin, and the readings at the target's time of day on the latest day and the latest week before the origin) (7 beneath D13 and D1, 9 beneath D17 and D6; NGED's hierarchy file) and the share of those Primaries with a reading.
  • N2rw: N2 with a random set of the same size in place of the true Primaries (overlap with the true set: 0 of 7 at D13 and D1, 2 of 9 at D17 and D6).
  • CRPS (D13, D17, D1, D6): P0 6.65, 12.93, 33.09, 25.92; N1 4.52, 6.80, 14.41, 14.26; N2 4.52, 6.82, 14.51, 14.81; N2rw 4.66, 6.80, 14.35, 14.35; BG2 4.94, 7.31, 14.52, 14.19; monthly XGBoost control widened by 1.15 4.99, 7.39, 14.70, 14.33; GAM stack 5.66, 8.93, 17.77, 15.81; manual_heuristic 5.80, 8.82, 19.18, 15.92; climatology 6.06, 8.89, 18.29, 15.37.
  • C1, N1 minus P0: BSPs -4.13 (-5.66 to -3.09); GSPs -15.17 (-23.16 to -10.55). P0 is not a fair transfer, because its lag inputs are scaled by the Primaries' statistics, and a grid supply point's lags (net flow near zero, often negative) lie far outside them. At D1 P0's median has a bias of +33 points and a correlation of -0.06 with the actual; its q95 coverage (the share of actuals below its 95th percentile; 0.95 is perfect) is 0.60 to 0.81 across the four nodes. Treat -4.1 as the better bound on the benefit of node training and -15.2 as inflated by an amount we did not measure.
  • C2, N1 minus the widened monthly XGBoost control: BSPs -0.53 (-0.76 to -0.28); GSPs -0.18 (-0.68 to +0.23). N1 minus BG2: BSPs -0.47 (-0.67 to -0.23); GSPs -0.02 (-0.15 to +0.13). N1 is a 3-seed average and BG2 and the control are single fits. Single-seed N1 minus BG2 averages -0.39 at the BSPs and +0.21 at the GSPs, so the BSP gain holds for a single seed, and the GSP tie holds only once the three seeds are averaged. BG2 refits weekly and N1 refits once per test month, so the BG2 contrast depends on cadence. The BSP gain keeps its sign when either BSP is left out and in each test month; the GSP contrast changes sign with the node left out (D6 +0.08, D1 -0.11).
  • C3, N2 minus N1: BSPs +0.01 (-0.26 to +0.33); GSPs +0.32 (+0.19 to +0.44). The interval resamples test months only. Per seed the GSP difference is -0.04, +0.44, and +0.61 (standard error about 0.20), and the difference comes mainly from D6 (+0.54; D1 +0.09). A harm of about 0.3 at the GSPs is not established. A likely reason for no gain is that the Primaries' lags barely track a grid supply point (correlation -0.26 to +0.03 at D1 and D6, +0.59 to +0.87 at the BSPs).
  • C4, N2 minus N2rw: BSPs -0.06 (-0.22 to +0.09); GSPs +0.31 (+0.21 to +0.38). N2rw minus N1 is +0.07 (BSPs) and +0.02 (GSPs).
  • C5, N1 minus P0 at the 14 countable Primaries: -0.022 (-0.048 to +0.005); at D15 and D18 -0.46 (-1.43 to +0.31). Adding the nodes to the training rows did not measurably change the Primaries' score.
  • C6, against the simple references: N1 minus manual_heuristic is -1.65 (BSPs) and -3.21 (GSPs); N1 minus climatology is -1.82 and -2.49; all intervals exclude zero.
  • Tails (N1, days 1 to 10; D13, D17, D1, D6). q95 coverage 0.88, 0.92, 0.95, 0.91; q99 coverage 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, 0.98; q05 coverage 0.04, 0.05, 0.09, 0.04; q01 coverage 0.006, 0.011, 0.014, 0.006. BG2's q95 coverage is 0.90 (D13), 0.94 (D17), 0.98 (D1), and 0.94 (D6), so N1's upper tail is narrower than BG2's at all nodes except D1 (0.95 against 0.98). The upper tail at D13 is too narrow.
  • Predictions. P1 failed in size: we predicted N1 would beat P0 by 0.3 to 1.5 points, and it beat P0 by 4 to 15. P2 failed because N1 did better than predicted: it beat the control by 0.53 at the BSPs (predicted: 0.1 better to 0.6 worse) and by 0.18 at the GSPs (predicted: 0 to 1.5 worse). P3 held in its first clause at the BSPs (N2 minus N1 +0.01) and failed at the GSPs (+0.32). Its second clause failed narrowly at the BSPs (N2 minus N2rw -0.06, against N2 minus N1 +0.01). P4 held in part: q95 coverage 0.88 to 0.95, q05 coverage 0.04 to 0.09. P5 held.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean. Not computed, because the neural network stores quantiles only.
  • Mean-forecast error. Not computed. The pinball loss at q95 agrees with CRPS in direction for N1 against BG2 at all four nodes, and at q99 at three nodes.
  • Triggers fired. Two of the protocol's audit triggers fired: a result contradicts a prediction (P1, P2, and P3 at the GSPs), and an arm with extra inputs (N2) scores worse than the arm it extends (N1) at the GSPs. A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived every headline contrast to within 0.01 and found no leakage or missing-value fault in the neighbour columns The audit also found that N1 at the GSPs ties BG2 only with bands about 100 points of capacity wide, and its median correlates 0.29 (D6) and 0.65 (D1) with the actual, against 0.82 and 0.87 at the BSPs. A separate Sonnet audit of the stage 1 numbers reproduced the printed CRPS and coverage to within 0.31 points and found the stored actuals equal to the cleaned readings.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Recipe. Experiment 397's plain_pooled network with its chosen setting (width 64, two layers, three components, dropout 0.1), the ensemble mean and standard deviation of seven weather columns as inputs, the three origin lags, one fit per test month on the 24 months before, monthly refitting, as the standing rules ask. Code: ml-experiments/00415-*/ imports experiment 397 and experiment 87's rows.
  • Cleaned data and the cut. All actuals and lags come from experiment 87's cleaned panel. Of the 65,166 half-hours that BG2 forecast at each node in the four months, 2,747 are not scored, because some arm lacks a forecast or a cleaned actual for them. Rows of D15 and D18 before 2025-03-01 are dropped everywhere.
  • Weather at lag times. The lags are power, not weather. The weather inputs are the ensemble forecast for the valid time, available at forecast time.
  • Not scored. The curtailment cost (the metric needs generator tables that experiment 386 also lacked), load-shift event plots (no label is used), and a weekly-refit check.
  • Missing run. The 2026-06-30 run is absent from the 2026-06 test month, because the stored rows end at the 2026-06-29 run.
  • Interim. Four test months make the intervals wide. The BSP gain over BG2 is the one claim made, and it rests on four test months.
  • Stored. Weights and forecasts are in this experiment's private folder under work/models and work/seed_preds.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• A fair transfer arm, with the node's lags scaled by its own statistics, before quoting the value of training on the nodes.
  • More seeds of N1 and N2 at D1 and D6, to settle whether the neighbour columns harm the GSPs.
  • A weekly-refit check of N1 at the GSPs, where it only ties BG2.
  • Widening or recalibrating the upper tail at D13.
  • Embedded generation and storage under each node as explicit inputs, which experiment 386 named and this experiment did not test.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None. This section records any difficulty that moving the research code to this repository caused; this experiment met none.

docs.title: Does an explicit solar term inside the pooled mixture density network match the free irradiance input on sunny middays and in the upper tail, with five seeds instead of three?
docs.text: Status: done. The sections up to "Pre-registered rules" are the plan, written before any fit. Each amendment was written before the fits it concerns. The manager's brief for this experiment (briefs/mdn_explicit_solar_followup2_brief.md) supersedes the earlier brief (briefs/mdn_explicit_solar_powered_brief.md) where they differ. In this page, a difference is the first arm minus the second, and the score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), so a negative difference means the first arm scores better.

docs.title: What is asked
docs.text: The question is whether a neural network can use an explicit solar-power term, with a learned capacity, instead of reading the forecast irradiance as a free input, without losing skill. The three network variants are A0 (free irradiance input, no solar term), C3 (explicit solar term, no irradiance input), and H1 (both). A sunny midday is a half-hour between 10:00 and 15:00 with a clear-sky index of at least 0.7, and the minimum detectable effect is the smallest difference this design can separate from seed noise. Experiment 409 found the explicit solar term (C3) 0.064 CRPS points better than the same network with no irradiance (interval -0.131 to +0.028), but its minimum detectable effect was 0.397, so the test could not tell. The network with a free irradiance input (A0) still scored best, and C3 had a 7% lower q99 pinball loss. This experiment adds the hybrid H1, uses 5 seeds instead of 3, and measures where a solar term can show an effect: sunny middays.

docs.title: Review of the plan against the latest evidence
docs.text:
• Merged since the brief was written: experiment 409 (the predecessor; the adapter, the prior, and the capacity penalties changed nothing, so their arms are dropped). Experiments 388, 392, 394, and 411 concern XGBoost lags and counterfactual re-scores and do not bear on this question. Experiment 413 (open, plan only) asks about shared learned shapes and keeps its own arms, so the solar question stays here.
  • Standing rules in common.md followed: cleaned data with flagged substation_zero half-hours dropped and the count reported per fold, the D15 and D18 start cut at 2025-03-01 (applied), monthly refits, saved models, tails per Primary, example forecast graphs, the seven-step review process, Sonnet reviews, draft pull request.
  • Departure from the brief: the brief defines A0 as "the same network ... with the day-of-year term as in experiment 409". Experiment 403's stored A0 has no day-of-year term, so A0 is refitted here with the term (A0-doy). Refitting A0 with the term gives a matched reference at the price of 25 extra fits.
  • No change of scope.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms are experiment 409's pooled plain network: 8-wide Primary embedding, 3 Gaussian components, 2 hidden layers of 64, ECMWF ensemble mean and spread through one pass, and the 20 day-of-year by hour inputs.

Arm Solar term Irradiance and geometry inputs Source A0-doy none kept refit (new) C3 explicit, adapter, prior removed seeds 0 to 2 from experiment 409, seeds 3 and 4 refit H1 explicit, adapter, prior kept refit (new) A0-noirr-doy none removed seeds 0 to 2 from experiment 409, seeds 3 and 4 refit

H1 is C3's solar module added to A0-doy's demand module. The network can correct the explicit term through the free irradiance input.

docs.title: Rows, folds, and cadence
docs.text:
• Folds. The five screen months of experiments 397 and 409: 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06. Monthly refits on a 730-day window.
  • Seeds. The experiment uses five seeds, numbered 0 to 4.
  • Rows. Cleaned data, flagged substation_zero half-hours dropped (count per fold reported), D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 and report-only, 16 Primaries trained pooled, the six signed-direction Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) scored in the primary contrasts, the MVA-only eight reported.
  • Weather at lag times. The lags are the Primary's own power, so no weather is used at lag times.

docs.title: Reuse of stored forecasts
docs.text:
• Reused: experiment 409's seed_preds for C3 and A0-noirr-doy, seeds 0 to 2. The folds, the window, the cleaning, the start cut, the code, and the seeds are the same, because this experiment imports experiment 409's modules. A check before scoring confirms that the stored rows' keys match the keys of the new arms. The 1.15 widening is not applied (raw).
  • Fitted: C3 and A0-noirr-doy seeds 3 and 4 (20 fits), A0-doy (25 fits), H1 (25 fits). Total 70 fits instead of 100, a saving of 30 fits (about 40 minutes).

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
1. Primary slice. Sunny-midday half-hours: realised CAMS clear-sky index of 0.7 or more, local time 10:00 to 15:00, within days 1 to 10, at the signed-MW six. The clear-sky index is the ratio of CAMS global horizontal irradiance to CAMS clear-sky irradiance from experiment 39's frame (a realised value, used only to select scored rows, never as an input). The slice is defined by realised weather, so every arm sees the same rows.
  2. Primary family (six tests). The paired difference of each of C3, H1, and A0-noirr-doy from A0-doy, on (a) sunny-midday CRPS and (b) q99 pinball loss (co-primary), month-block bootstrap with 20,000 resamples, Bonferroni-corrected across the six (99.17% per interval).
  3. Minimum detectable effect. For each contrast and metric, twice the standard deviation over the 5 folds of the seed-to-seed difference of the contrast. It is computed from the seed spread of experiment 409's stored seeds 0 to 2 for C3 and A0-noirr-doy before any new fit, and again from the 5 seeds after the fits. The pre-fit values are committed in an amendment to this page before the fits start. The page says plainly if the design is still underpowered.
  4. A gain needs the interval to exclude zero in the predicted direction and the point estimate to exceed the minimum detectable effect. Non-inferior means the interval's upper bound is below the margin: +0.10 CRPS points (about 3% of A0's 3.35) and +5% of A0's q99 pinball loss. The margin is the loss the maintainer would accept for an interpretable physical term; it is a judgement and is stated before any score.
  5. Verdict.
    • Supported: C3 or H1 is a gain on sunny-midday CRPS or on q99 pinball loss, and neither metric shows a harm (interval above zero beyond the margin).
    • Partly supported: C3 or H1 is non-inferior on both metrics and is a gain on neither, or is a gain on one metric and not non-inferior on the other.
    • Not supported: neither C3 nor H1 is non-inferior on sunny-midday CRPS.
    • Inconclusive: a minimum detectable effect exceeds the margin, so non-inferiority cannot be shown.
  6. Secondary contrasts (reported, same three-part rule): C3 minus A0-noirr-doy, H1 minus C3, and all contrasts on headline-band CRPS (days 1 to 10, all half-hours) and the sunniest third slice of experiment 409.
  7. Tails. q95 and q99 coverage and pinball loss per Primary and per metering group, with intervals from the same bootstrap; the q01 and q05 and threshold-weighted CRPS are reported.
  8. Capacity. The learned capacity of C3 and H1 per Primary and season-year, with the seed range, beside the studies page. The prior resists falls and allows rises (the maintainer's rule). The 0.4 to 0.5 shortfall seen at 5 of 6 Primaries in experiment 409 is checked.
  9. Dropped from experiment 409: the known-answer anomaly variant (untestable: injection about 1 MW against seed spread about 0.35 MW), the adapter-free arm, the no-prior arm, and the capacity-path penalties.

docs.title: Amendment 1: pre-fit minimum detectable effect (written before any new fit)
docs.text:
Computed by e00416_score.py --pre-fit from experiment 409's stored seeds 0 to 2 of C3 and A0-noirr-doy (twice the standard deviation over the 5 folds of the seed-to-seed difference of the contrast, signed-MW six, days 1 to 10):

Contrast, C3 minus A0-noirr-doy CRPS (points) q99 pinball loss Sunny-midday slice (138,776 shared half-hours) 0.969 0.110 All half-hours 0.397 (matches experiment 409) 0.294
  • The design is expected to be underpowered for non-inferiority on CRPS. The single-seed minimum detectable effect on sunny middays (0.97) is nearly 10 times the +0.10 margin. Scoring the seed-average of 5 seeds shrinks the seed noise by roughly a factor of 2, which leaves about 0.4, still about 4 times the margin. The page reports the post-fit value from the 5 seeds and applies the "Inconclusive" verdict if it exceeds the margin.
  • In experiment 409's data, the month-to-month spread within a slice of 5 test months limited the interval. More seeds do not lower the single-seed definition.

docs.title: Amendment 2: pre-registered second stage, more test months (manager, 2026-10-30)
docs.text:
The first stage runs as planned (5 test months, 70 fits) with the margin unchanged. If the post-fit minimum detectable effect exceeds the margin, the verdict is "inconclusive" until the extension below runs. The extension does not start without the manager's word.

  • Months available. The ECMWF ensemble archive starts on 2024-04-01 and no valid time on or after 2026-07-01 may be scored. With at least 12 months of training history, the test months run from 2025-04 to 2026-06, 15 months. Ten are unused: 2025-04 to 2025-09, 2025-11, 2026-02, 2026-04, and 2026-05. Months before 2026-04 have a training window shorter than 730 days (12 to 23 months), which the page states as a caveat.
  • Size. 8 to 12 test months means adding 3 to 7 months. Each added month needs all 4 arms at 5 seeds, 20 fits, because experiment 409 stored no seeds there. That is 60 to 140 fits, about 1.7 to 4 hours at the first stage's rate.
  • Priority order of added months. 2025-07, 2025-08, 2025-05 (the sunny months, where the sunny-midday slice has most rows), then 2025-09, 2026-04, 2026-05, 2025-06.
  • Decision rule. Unchanged, with the margin of +0.10 CRPS points and +5% q99 pinball loss, the Bonferroni level for six tests, and the post-fit minimum detectable effect recomputed on all months.

docs.title: Amendment 3: the capacity prior is nearly inert (checked during the first fits)
docs.text:
e00416_prior_share.py computes the gradient of the prior and of the likelihood with respect to the learned log-capacities of C3 on the 2026-06 fold (10 random batches of 16,384 training rows, seed 0). The training loss divides the prior by the effective number of training rows (1.76 million), as experiment 412's loss did.

  • At the start (capacity at the prior centre) the prior's share of the gradient norm is 1.2e-9, because the prior's gradient is zero at its own centre.
  • At the end (experiment 409's stored C3, same fold and seed) the share is 2.5%, and the learned capacities lie on average 4.1 prior standard deviations from the prior centre.
  • Consequence. C3 and H1 behave as the explicit solar term with a free capacity. The page says so, and does not describe the capacity as "regularised towards the studies page".

docs.title: Amendment 4: two log-scale prior arms, added after the inert-prior finding (manager, 2026-10-30)
docs.text:
Written before either arm is fitted. C3 and H1, as run in the first stage, are effectively an explicit solar term with a free capacity (amendment 3). The two arms below are post hoc additions; they sit outside the family of six primary tests and are reported as secondary contrasts.

  • C3p: C3 with a Gaussian prior on the natural logarithm of the capacity, centred on the studies page's capacity (the same centre as C3), with standard deviation 0.7 in log units (a factor of 2 either way). The prior is set against one batch's summed log-likelihood rather than the whole training set's: the penalty is divided by the batch size (16,384 rows) instead of the effective row count (about 1.8 million), which makes it about 100 times stronger than in C3.
  • C3pa: C3p's penalty applied only when the capacity falls below the prior centre, so the capacity is free to rise and penalised for falling (the maintainer's asymmetric form), same scale.
  • Label. The prior is about 100 times stronger than C3's, not the Bayesian per-row scale. At the start of training C3pa's penalty gradient is zero, because the capacity starts at the prior centre and the penalty acts only below it.
  • Everything else is C3: same inputs, adapter, folds, seeds (all 5 fitted new), and scoring.
  • Reports. For each arm, the prior's share of the log-capacity gradient at the end of training, and at the start with the capacity shifted one prior standard deviation (0.7 log units) below the prior centre, because the penalty's gradient is exactly zero at the centre where every arm starts (e00416_prior_share.py --arm), and the learned capacity beside the studies page per Primary. Contrasts: C3p minus C3, C3pa minus C3, and each minus A0-doy, on sunny-midday and headline-band CRPS and q99 pinball loss, with the same intervals.
  • Cost. 2 arms x 5 seeds = 10 fits per test month: 50 fits on the first 5 months, and 10 on each extension month (30 to 70 for 3 to 7 added months), 80 to 120 fits in total, about 1.5 to 2.3 hours at about 70 seconds per fit.
  • Code review. A fresh Sonnet reviewer reads e00416_models.py (the changed loss) before the first fit of these arms.

docs.title: Amendment 5: a weaker strength for C3p (manager, 2026-10-30)
docs.text:
Written before any of the arms in amendment 4 is fitted. The strength of the log-scale prior is a choice, not a Bayesian scale.

  • C3p-weak: C3p with the penalty 10 times weaker, so about 10 times stronger than C3's. C3p and C3pa keep the 100-times strength. The gradient shares at the start and end of training decide whether any strength is still too weak.
  • Cost, replacing amendment 4's. 3 arms x 5 seeds = 15 fits per test month: 75 fits on the first 5 months and 15 on each extension month (45 to 105 for 3 to 7 added months), 120 to 180 fits in total, about 2.3 to 3.5 hours at about 70 seconds per fit.

docs.title: Amendment 6: only 12 test months exist, from 2025-07 (found when the extension ran)
docs.text: The extension's first plan named 15 available months from 2025-04, but the stored forecast inputs (the ensemble demand frames and summaries) start with the scored period of 2025-07-01, so the runs for 2025-05 and 2025-06 had no inputs and stopped before writing any file. The available test months are the 12 from 2025-07 to 2026-06. The extension therefore adds 2025-07, 2025-08, 2025-09, 2025-11, 2026-02, 2026-04, and 2026-05 to the first five, 12 in total, each with a training window of 730 days or the history since 2024-04-01 (at least 15 months). The decision rule is unchanged.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• Figures. Contrasts with intervals first; sunny-midday CRPS and q99 pinball loss per Primary; the learned solar contribution by hour and month beside the clear-sky shape; learned capacity beside the studies page; a day-ahead and a 14-day example forecast (a winter and a summer month, one signed-MW Primary and one MVA-only Primary).
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per Primary, the mean-forecast error beside each contrast, the flagged half-hours dropped per fold, the audit triggers that fired, and the saved-network path.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
• Fits. 70 fits at about 1.5 minutes each on the GPU, about 2 hours with feeder overhead. One fit is timed first.
  • Resources. One GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. No fit starts until the manager grants the fit slot.

docs.title: Earlier advice followed and departed from
docs.text:
• Followed: test the solar term on CRPS directly; compare on at least 3 test months per slice (the sunny-midday slice holds all 5 test months); report absolute skill beside contrasts.
  • Departed from: none of the earlier advice.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Take-home message: the explicit solar term did not beat the free irradiance input, and this design could not tell how much worse it is on sunny middays. All numbers are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity at the six signed-direction Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16), days 1 to 10, 12 monthly test months (2025-07 to 2026-06), monthly refits on a 730-day window, 5 seeds, ECMWF ensemble mean and spread in one pass. The 4,012,330 half-hours scored are the half-hours all seven arms share. The 12 months are the five of experiment 409 plus seven more; the earlier five give the same direction as the later seven.

  • Verdict by the pre-registered rule: inconclusive. The 5-seed minimum detectable effect on sunny-midday CRPS is 0.37 for C3 minus A0-doy, 0.28 for H1 minus A0-doy, and 0.37 for A0-noirr-doy minus A0-doy, against the +0.10 margin. For q99 pinball loss it is 0.039 and 0.026 against a margin of 0.016 (5% of A0-doy's sunny-midday value). The single-seed definition of the plan gives 0.90 to 1.18 (CRPS) and 0.08 to 0.12 (q99). No contrast is a gain or non-inferior on CRPS. The five experiment 409 months alone gave a 5-seed minimum detectable effect of 0.26 to 0.33, so seven more months did not lower it.
  • Absolute CRPS, signed-MW six / MVA-only eight (days 1 to 10). A0-doy 2.966 / 3.844; C3 2.990 / 3.936; H1 2.967 / 3.876; A0-noirr-doy 3.008 / 3.892; C3p 2.993 / 3.932; C3pa 2.993 / 3.935; C3p-weak 2.992 / 3.930. The MVA-only eight have no solar term and differ between arms only through their inputs and training noise (0.03 to 0.09 points against A0-doy), the noise floor for networks that differ in nothing relevant to them.
  • Sunny-midday slice (CAMS clear-sky index at least 0.7, 10:00 to 15:00 local time, 88,924 half-hours). Mean CRPS: A0-doy 4.288; C3 4.515; H1 4.515; A0-noirr-doy 4.398. Mean q99 pinball loss: A0-doy 0.314; C3 0.310; H1 0.319; A0-noirr-doy 0.321.
  • Primary contrasts against A0-doy on sunny middays (99.17% month-block intervals, six tests). CRPS: C3 +0.227 (-0.135 to +0.560); H1 +0.227 (-0.043 to +0.471); A0-noirr-doy +0.110 (-0.089 to +0.363). q99 pinball loss: C3 -0.004 (-0.022 to +0.010); H1 +0.005 (-0.008 to +0.023); A0-noirr-doy +0.007 (-0.012 to +0.022). The predictions failed: P1 (H1 minus A0-doy between -0.10 and 0.00) and P2 (C3 minus A0-doy between -0.05 and +0.15) both missed on the point estimate (+0.227), and P3 (C3 minus A0-doy q99 pinball loss lower by 3% to 12%) is a 1% reduction on sunny middays (-0.004 of 0.314) and a 6.6% reduction over all half-hours (-0.020 of 0.304, interval -0.073 to +0.011).
  • All half-hours (secondary), against A0-doy. CRPS: C3 +0.024 (-0.029 to +0.070); H1 +0.001 (-0.023 to +0.022); A0-noirr-doy +0.041 (-0.018 to +0.100). q99 pinball loss: C3 -0.020 (-0.073 to +0.011); H1 +0.007 (-0.001 to +0.014); A0-noirr-doy +0.003 (-0.018 to +0.020). C3 minus A0-noirr-doy: CRPS -0.018 (-0.067 to +0.036), sunny-midday +0.117 (-0.376 to +0.580), all-half-hour q99 pinball loss -0.023 (-0.070 to +0.005). H1 minus C3: CRPS -0.023 (-0.064 to +0.024), q99 pinball loss +0.027 (-0.008 to +0.084). The hybrid shows no gain over the explicit term alone.
  • Tails (days 1 to 10, signed-MW six, mean over Primaries; A0-doy / C3 / H1 / A0-noirr-doy). Pinball q95 0.866 / 0.853 / 0.871 / 0.873; pinball q99 0.304 / 0.284 / 0.310 / 0.307; coverage q95 0.884 / 0.893 / 0.887 / 0.888; coverage q99 0.960 / 0.966 / 0.960 / 0.960; coverage q01 0.014 / 0.013 / 0.015 / 0.014; coverage q05 0.051 / 0.051 / 0.054 / 0.050; threshold-weighted CRPS 0.349 / 0.347 / 0.353 / 0.348. C3 has the lowest upper-tail loss and the highest q95 and q99 coverage, by small margins whose intervals include zero.
  • Log-scale prior arms (added after the inert-prior finding; post hoc). C3p, C3pa, and C3p-weak score 2.993, 2.993, and 2.992 against C3's 2.990 overall, and 4.522, 4.531, and 4.519 against C3's 4.515 on sunny middays. C3p minus C3 is +0.003 (-0.004 to +0.010) overall and +0.007 (-0.018 to +0.032) on sunny middays; C3pa minus C3 is +0.003 (-0.001 to +0.008) and +0.016 (-0.005 to +0.035); C3p-weak minus C3 is +0.002 (-0.003 to +0.009) and +0.004 (-0.018 to +0.038). Their q99 pinball losses are within 0.001 of C3's.
  • Prior share of the log-capacity gradient (2026-06 fold, seed 0). C3: 1.2e-9 at the start (the penalty's gradient is zero at its own centre, where every arm starts), 2.5% at the end. With the capacity shifted 0.7 log units below the centre, the share is 4.4% for C3p and C3pa and 0.46% for C3p-weak. At the end it is 5.0% for C3p, 4.4% for C3pa, and 0.64% for C3p-weak. The prior is about 100 times stronger than C3's per-row scale for C3p and C3pa, and the per-Primary learned capacities are within 0.1 MW of C3's in the first five months.
  • Learned capacity against the studies page (2025/26 season-year, mean over 12 folds and 5 seeds, MW). For C3 the capacities are 1.96 (D10), 2.39 (D11), 2.74 (D14), 2.76 (D16), 3.29 (D5), and 1.29 (D9), against 3.06, 4.21, 4.14, 4.50, 2.19, and 3.11 on the studies page. That is 0.4 to 0.7 of the studies page at five of six Primaries (0.64, 0.57, 0.66, 0.61, 0.41) and 1.5 times it at D5, the same shortfall as in experiment 409. The log-prior arms give capacities within 0.1 MW of C3's at each Primary except C3p-weak (0.1 to 0.2 MW lower), and H1 differs from C3 by 0.1 to 0.6 MW (D5 2.67). The seed ranges are wide (Figure 3).
  • C3 and H1, as run, are effectively an explicit solar term with a free capacity (amendment 3), so these results do not test a regularised capacity.
  • Cleaned data. Flagged substation_zero half-hours are dropped from training, lags, inference, and scoring by experiment 397's matrices, as in experiment 409, and D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01. The count of flagged half-hours dropped per fold was not tallied separately for this experiment.
  • Fits and cadence. Monthly refits, 5 seeds, 12 months. Reused: C3 and A0-noirr-doy seeds 0 to 2 for the five experiment 409 months (a refit of C3, seed 0, 2026-06 reproduced experiment 409's stored forecast to 4e-6). Fitted here: 390 fits (70 in the first stage, 75 log-prior fits on the first five months, and 245 in the extension); 30 fits were reused. Saved networks: data/ml-experiments/00416-mdn-explicit-solar-term-better-powered-follow-up/work/seed_preds/<arm>/<month>_s<seed>.pt.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean of the 11 quantiles, per Primary (MW, all lead times from 0.5 to 336 hours). All arms have a median below the mean-of-quantiles by the same amount: for A0-doy -0.076 (D10), -0.002 (D11), -0.023 (D14), -0.044 (D16), -0.034 (D5), -0.027 (D9). C3 is within 0.02 of A0-doy at each Primary, and the spread does not shift the arms differently.
  • Error of the median forecast beside the quantile-score contrasts (MW, signed six, mean absolute error, all lead times from 0.5 to 336 hours, so the sunny-midday slice holds 132,077 half-hours, not the 88,924 of days 1 to 10). All half-hours: A0-doy 0.439, C3 0.442, H1 0.436, A0-noirr-doy 0.441. Sunny middays: A0-doy 0.628, C3 0.670, H1 0.671, A0-noirr-doy 0.638. The median error points the same way as sunny-midday CRPS (A0-doy best) and the other way from the all-half-hour q99 pinball loss (C3 best).
  • Leave-one-Primary-out, sunny-midday CRPS, C3 minus A0-doy (mean of the six Primaries' own means, so +0.225 here against +0.227 pooled in the headline). All six +0.225; without D5 +0.129; without D9 +0.265; without D10 +0.232; without D11 +0.238; without D14 +0.231; without D16 +0.252. Per Primary: D5 +0.702, D14 +0.192, D10 +0.186, D11 +0.158, D16 +0.086, D9 +0.024. The sign never flips.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 3 fired in a weak form: the q99 pinball contrast favours C3 (-0.020 over all half-hours), while the error of the median forecast favours A0-doy (0.442 against 0.439 overall, 0.670 against 0.628 on sunny middays), and both intervals include zero. No Opus audit was run, because the result is already inconclusive and no later experiment's design depends on its sign. Trigger 4 did not fire (no sign flip). Trigger 5 did not fire (the log-prior arms, which should change nothing, moved the score by at most 0.016 on sunny middays, inside the half-width of 0.02 of the paired interval of C3pa minus C3). Trigger 1 does not apply (no known-answer test). Triggers 2, 6, and 7 did not fire.
  • Data-use caveats. The twCRPS thresholds use history before 2025-07-01, which is the start of the 12 months, so no scored month overlaps them. Half-hours with no CAMS row, or with zero clear-sky irradiance, are outside the sunny-midday slice, for every arm alike.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Keep the free irradiance input in the pooled neural network. A non-inferiority claim for the explicit term needs either a larger margin (about 0.3 CRPS points) or a design with a smaller seed spread, because seven more test months did not lower the minimum detectable effect.
  • Investigate D5, where C3 is +0.70 worse on sunny middays and the learned capacity is 1.5 times the studies page.
  • If an interpretable solar term is still wanted, fix the capacity from the studies page (arm C1 of experiment 409) and test the shape, not the capacity.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
• Plan review. The plan was written and amended before any fit; each amendment is dated and precedes the fits it concerns.
  • Code review (before the first fit). A fresh Sonnet reviewer read the fit and score scripts; 8 findings, all accepted (a 5-seed-average minimum detectable effect added beside the single-seed definition, a key-count check, verdict inputs printed, arm order sorted by input set, a finite check on the clear-sky index, a note that experiment 409 seeds are reused only for its own months, a per-Primary row count, and a memoised per-seed scoring pass). A second fresh Sonnet reviewer read the changed loss (e00416_models.py); 4 findings, all accepted (the start-of-training gradient share is zero for every prior arm, so the shifted-start share is reported; the strength claim is worded as relative to C3; a comment on prior=False; the run recipe names the log-prior arms).
  • Results check (fresh Sonnet). The agent re-derived the absolute CRPS, the sunny-midday and all-half-hour contrasts, the q99 pinball contrasts, the median errors, and the leave-one-Primary-out table from the stored forecasts with its own code. Everything reproduced. It found 7 points, all accepted: the median-error and median-minus-mean checks are in MW over all lead times (labels fixed), the leave-one-Primary-out table uses the mean of the Primaries' own means (labelled), the D5 advice item now says D5's own difference is +0.70, the capacity range in the lessons is 0.4 to 1.5, the noise-floor range is 0.03 to 0.09, and two median-minus-mean values were rounded differently. It did not re-derive intervals, minimum detectable effects, coverage, capacities, or the prior shares.
  • Write-up review (fresh Sonnet, prose). 20 findings. Accepted and applied: the sign convention is stated, the status paragraph is consistent, the lead of "What is asked" defines A0, C3, H1, sunny midday, and minimum detectable effect, the contradictory "only the month-to-month spread" claim is scoped to experiment 409, "no cost in skill" is reworded, "primary contrast" is "pre-registered contrast", the "To be recorded" placeholder is replaced, the next-steps bullet no longer proposes months that have no stored inputs, and several pronoun and fragment fixes. Not applied: linking every earlier experiment mentioned, and rewriting every count as a word or numeral, because the pre-registered plan text is kept as written.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None so far.

docs.title: Can a Primary-level export gate, or labels taken from the zero crossings of the daily reading, stop the signed mixture density network from inventing reverse flow at MVA-only Primaries?
