The ungated reference scores the same as A on reverse-flow rows, so the gain over P0 measures how much it helps to let the forecast go below zero. A against ref is -0.061 (-0.149 to 0.024): A is worse by 0.06, and the interval includes zero (ref has one seed and A two; at seed 0 alone A is slightly better, 6.98 against 6.99). The gate matters where there is no export: with no farm injected, the ungated reference is worse than P0 at D5 by 1.21 points (+0.23 pooled over the five placebo Primaries, interval 0.07 to 0.42), and A is worse by 0.03.

The sign is still often wrong, and the lower tail is too narrow. The numbers below are descriptive, at level 2.0 and seed 0, for A, on the half-hours with the CAMS unit shape at least 0.3 and clear-sky index at least 0.7 (115,040 rows, 12,526 unique half-hours).

Measure Value Balanced accuracy at P(X < 0) > 0.5 0.852 (AV 0.851, A-shuffle 0.582) Recall of reverse flow 0.859 False-reverse rate, every non-reverse half-hour of the slice (rows) 15.5% False-reverse rate, non-reverse sunny summer-midday half-hours (the registered denominator, rows) 66.8% False-reverse rate with a 2-point dead band 12.9% Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.930 Recall at a matched 5% false-reverse rate 0.623 q01 coverage on reverse-flow rows (nominal 0.01) 0.062 q99 coverage on reverse-flow rows (nominal 0.99) 0.998
  • In every fit with an injected farm, the Primary-level gate opened at the six hidden Primaries and at D8 and D12, and stayed shut at D2, D3, D4, D19, D21, and D22. This is why A and ref score alike at level 2.0.
  • Level 1.0 (moderate export): A's gain over P0 is 5.64 (4.61 to 6.41) and AV's 5.69 (4.60 to 6.52). AV against A is +0.05 (-0.06 to 0.16). A's balanced accuracy at level 1.0 is 0.716, with recall 0.524.
  • The shared variance scale s learned 0.071 on average at level 2.0 (range 0.027 to 0.145), from a start of 0.1. The tails did not improve: AV's q01 coverage was 0.060 against A's 0.062.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reference check against the plain network. The plain neural network (P0) cannot forecast below zero, so B1 is a low bar. The ungated reference scores the same as A on reverse-flow rows, as the results section reports.
  • Median forecast against the mean forecast. Not computed, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles and no mean. The error of the median forecast on reverse-flow rows (seed 0) points the same way as the CRPS: P0 31.98, A 12.19, AV 12.79 points. Audit trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Audit triggers (the numbered conditions in the ml-experiment skill's "Audit before merge" section). Trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm that contains it) fired: AV contains A (its added variance can shrink to zero) and scored 0.225 worse (interval 0.155 to 0.300), beyond the null difference between A's two seeds (-0.341 to 0.040). The cause is not settled; AV is not carried forward, so no audit was requested. Trigger 7 (a later design depends on an unreplicated headline) applies: the planned serving test with ENS inputs depends on A's gain, which this experiment has replicated over three rotations and seven months but only in the laboratory. The controls passed: the shuffled sky is 9.13 worse than A, and no placebo Primary was harmed by more than 0.04. Leaving one Primary out cannot flip B1, because the gain is positive at every Primary. No Opus audit was run, because the Opus design note of 2026-10-30 already audited the gates.
  • Step 0, design I's diagnostic with the corrected threshold (0.0742), reported with no bar. The corrected threshold did not rescue the diagnostic. At level 2.0 the area under the curve is 0.702 (0.73 in experiment 417), the paired area 0.676, and recall 0.20 of 822 positive days (0.22). The false-flag rate is 5.9% at D5 and 7.0% at D10 (5.5% and 8.2%). The broken-cloud class still holds 97% to 99% of the injected days (for example 151 of 153 at D5), because the threshold was fixed on clear days only and the other days are rougher. Only 17 positive days fall in the smooth class, so the smooth-day area is undefined, as in experiment 417. The result is in work/day_flip/day_flip.json, and the placebo pool still includes D10 (audit finding 7).
  • Not done. Avoidable-curtailment cost (see Departures), and a serving test with ENS inputs.
  • Caveats. The inputs are realised CAMS irradiance and ERA5 temperature, so every result is a laboratory result. The scored range is lead 0 to 240 hours (days 1 to 10), as the families' horizon of 1 to 10 days requires. The 2025-07 refit trains on 15 months, not 24.

docs.title: Review log
docs.text:
Plan review (fresh Sonnet agent, before any fit). 10 findings, all triaged.

  • Accepted: the decision rule had no outcome for a failure of B1, B3, or B5 alone (a final clause now says "not shown"; B4 is judged per arm; B3 is measured on A); the stage-1 stop rule needed a definition for D5 and D10 only; the prediction for B2 contradicted the hypothesis; the threshold pool for step 0 is a departure from the note and is now listed; the descriptive list had no separate no-injection D5 line; the stage-1 time estimate was stale; the seed asymmetry is now a departure; prose slips ("plain network", sentences opening with "It", 5.1 against 5.10).
  • Kept as written: the minimum detectable effect still uses A's two-seed null, because the audit note specifies it. The page now says it is a noise floor resting on few blocks.
  • Not changed: the avoidable-curtailment cost stays out (the page states why).

Code review (fresh Sonnet agent, before any fit). No blockers and no leakage. One important finding and seven minor ones, all accepted: B4 always failed because D10 returned a missing value (now only the five placebo Primaries are scored); the B4 interval ends were not swapped with the sign; the two minimum-detectable-effect figures now go to separate files that cannot be overwritten (stage 1 and full); threshold.json cannot be overwritten; P0's stored fit information says the gates were forced shut; the CRPS docstring says it approximates the CRPS; read_arm refuses a partial seed set. The seed-weight-decay note needs no change.

Write-up review (fresh Sonnet agent, against the stored scores). No high or medium findings, and nine low findings, all accepted: four interval ends rounded wrongly, a "within 0.3" that should read 0.31, the sign and tail tables and the median-error line labelled seed 0, "rows" named in the lesson about false-reverse rates, the direction and seed difference of A against ref stated, and "no harm" qualified as "beyond the registered tolerance".

Prose review (fresh Sonnet agent). 35 findings. Accepted: the opening paragraph now defines "signed", "reverse flow", the CRPS, the gate, and the rotations, and gives units and direction; MVA, the anonymised Primary codes, and the 16 trial-area Primaries are defined once; the contradiction between the Departures and the example figure is fixed; the gate-opening claim is scoped to fits with an injected farm; the lead about the lower tail now matches the coverage table; the audit triggers are named; money metaphors, bare pronouns, and the count slip ("Ten") are fixed. Not changed: the pre-registered hypothesis and prediction wording, which keeps the arm names P0, A, and AV that the plan defines, and the title.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text:
• The docstrings of experiments 412 and 417 tell the reader to source an env.sh, which does not exist in this repository. This experiment's scripts need PYTHONPATH to list the folders of experiments 87, 397, 405, 412, 417, and 420, and DATA_PATH_INTERNAL. I assembled both by hand. Command that showed it: ls env.sh in the worktree root.
  • python -I, which the repository's guidance suggests for untrusted data, ignores PYTHONPATH and so cannot import an experiment's modules. Command: uv run --no-sync python -I -c "import e00417_inputs".

docs.title: Can the pooled mixture density network tell which Primary it is forecasting, and forecast a Primary it never saw, from the last 7 days of that Primary's power alone?
docs.text: Take-home message: the last 7 days of power identify the Primary, but a learned label still forecasts better, and the encoder adds nothing the raw readings lack. We asked whether a neural network that is told the last 7 days of a substation's power can work out which substation it is forecasting, so that the learned substation label (the Primary embedding) becomes optional. We trained the pooled network of experiment 406 with and without the label, with and without a convolutional encoder of the 7 days, on the same five test months and 16 substations. A linear classifier finds the substation from the encoder's output 87% of the time (chance is 6%), but it finds the substation 90% of the time from the raw readings with no learning. The network with the label and the three recent readings scores 3.315 points of capacity at the six signed-direction substations. The same network with no label scores 3.739, and adding the encoder narrows that to 3.640 (a gain of 0.099 whose interval spans zero). The verdict is not supported. For a substation left out of training, the network with no label and no encoder scored best (4.318), and a placeholder label scored much worse (5.527). Every number comes from five test months, so all are interim.

docs.title: Example forecasts
docs.text: NH's median, 50% band, and 90% band against what happened, for D10 (a signed-MW Primary) in winter and D4 (an MVA-only Primary) in summer.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held. E3g minus E406 is -0.007 and +0.011.
  • P2 failed. N3g minus E3g is +0.424 (limit +0.39) at the six and +0.584 (limit +0.40) at the eight. Rescaling the target recovered 46% of experiment 406's loss at the six and 28% at the eight.
  • P3 failed. NH minus N3g is -0.099 at the six (needed -0.15 or lower, and the interval spans zero).
  • P4 failed. NH minus EH is +0.162 at the six and +0.107 at the eight (limit +0.10).
  • P5 held on its wording and failed on its intent. The prediction said EH is no more than 0.05 below E3g. EH is 0.162 and 0.173 above E3g (worse), so the wording holds, but the intent was that the 7 days add little, and they made the score worse.
  • P6 failed narrowly. The Primary probe on NH reaches 0.871 (needed 0.90; EH 0.853, NH0 0.899). The three-lag probe stays at 0.280, which meets the limit of 0.50. The month probe reaches 0.719 within one month (needed 0.60), but the untrained encoder already reaches 0.600.
  • P7 held at the six and failed at the eight. NH0 minus NH is +0.021 and +0.075 (limit 0.05).
  • P8 held on the point estimate, with an interval that spans zero. NH minus E3g with the mean label is -0.735 at the six (needed -0.20 or lower; interval -2.695 to +0.562). The prediction named only the six. At the eight the contrast is -2.382 (-3.115 to -1.844).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus the mean of the 11 quantiles, per Primary. Within 0.05 MW at 12 of 16 Primaries for E3g and 13 of 16 for NH and EH. D15 (-0.15 to -0.20 MW), D12 (-0.12 to -0.145), and D8 (-0.065 to -0.131; it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap) are exceptions for all three arms, and D4 (-0.094) for E3g. The mean of the stored quantiles stands in for the mean forecast, which the networks do not store.
  • Error of the median beside CRPS (mean absolute error, points of capacity, six / eight). E3g 5.760 / 6.594, EH 6.175 / 6.762, NH 6.493 / 6.935, N3g 6.609 / 7.364. The order matches the CRPS order, so trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 5 fired: EH, which contains E3g's inputs, scores 0.162 worse. Trigger 2 fired: P2, P3, P4, and P6 missed, P5 missed in intent, and P7 missed at the eight. A fresh Sonnet audit (briefs/e421_audit_main.md, private) re-derived every printed score and contrast point estimate to three decimals and found no leakage. EH minus E3g has the same sign in each of the three seeds (+0.155 to +0.206 at the six), so the effect is not seed noise, but it flips sign in two of five folds. The encoder arms stop after about 15 epochs against 33 for E3g, and EH has the worse validation loss too. The audit did not test whether the encoder opens a channel for memorising each Primary's unique history. Leaving out any one Primary flips no sign among C3, C4, C5, and C9, and C9 at the six drops to -0.003 without D11.
  • Triage of the audit. The audit found that the alignment check failed for D15 and D18 on 957 rows whose history lies before the start cut. I fixed the check to compare flags only after the cut, and the check now passes for all 16 Primaries. The training and scores are unaffected, since those rows are cut from training. N3g hit the 40-epoch limit in 7 of 15 fits and E3g in 4 of 15, so the contrasts against N3g (C2, C3) may flatter the encoder arms.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Interim. Five test months; no claim of benefit rests on the intervals.
  • D8 caveat: it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap.
  • Unlogged load-shift events. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so the history of an origin can sit inside an unlogged event, and the encoder may read such an event as a property of the Primary.
  • Lead range. The headline band is days 1 to 10, the range NGED cares about.
  • Training rows keep flagged exact zeros as in experiment 406; the scorer drops 1,179 flagged half-hours from the actuals.
  • Held-out stage. Two seeds, quarters of four Primaries that mix metering groups, and D15 and D18 are report-only. The placeholder labels are a weak stand-in for a fitted label.

docs.title: Departures from the plan
docs.text:
• Not reported. The lower tail on sunny, low-demand half-hours, the avoidable-curtailment cost, absolute scores beside BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology, a per-Primary score table, left-out Primaries scored against climatology and manual_heuristic, example forecasts from E3g, and the share of origins whose history has a gap. The scoring scripts do not compute them, and the verdict does not depend on them.
  • Added after the plan. The held-out stage also scored the mean embedding within the metering group, and the plan's shuffled-history arm NHs was added after the plan review.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
Whether a label fitted from a few weeks of a new Primary's history beats the label-free network for onboarding. The label-free network with three lags loses 0.58 points at the six when a Primary is left out, against 2.21 points for E3g given the mean-label placeholder (5.527 against 3.315). An experiment that fits only the new Primary's label on its first 4 to 12 weeks, with the rest of the network frozen, would settle that. The maintainer has ranked onboarding low, so this is a proposal only.

The plan as committed before any fit.

docs.title: Question and design
docs.text:
We test whether recent power plays the part of a language model's context. The maintainer's idea is that the 7 days before the forecast origin tell a pooled network which Primary it is looking at, and where in the seasonal cycle that Primary sits, without a learned Primary embedding. The maintainer does not propose dropping the embedding. The experiment asks whether the history could replace it, which matters for the 1,300-substation case, where a new substation has no embedding of its own.

  • The base network. Experiment 397's pooled plain mixture density network (setting g09, 3 Gaussian components, ECMWF ENS mean and spread passed through once), on the five screen folds of experiment 397 (test months 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), monthly refits, with the D15 and D18 start cut of experiment 399, as in experiment 406.
  • The history. For each origin, the 336 half-hours (7 days) of power over effective capacity that end at the newest usable reading (grid index origin - NEWEST_AGE, the same reading as lag_origin). Every run is daily at 00:00 UTC, so every history ends at the same time of day. The history comes from the same cleaned grid as the three origin lags (observed.parquet of experiment 87, with the flagged substation_zero half-hours as nulls), so the lags and the history agree. Values are standardised with the fold's training rows and clipped at 5 standard deviations. A missing half-hour is set to 0 and flagged in a second channel, so the encoder sees a gap and not a zero. A check before any fit asserts that the last history value equals lag_origin on every row, and that no history index is later than the newest usable reading.
  • The encoder. Two 1D convolution layers (kernel 5, 16 channels, stride 2, GELU) over the two channels (value and missing flag), then the flattened output (84 steps by 16 channels) through one linear layer to 32 values with a LayerNorm. The flattened output keeps the time of day, which a global pooling would lose. The 32 values join the network's other inputs.
  • The target scale. Experiment 406's targets were standardised per Primary, so a network with no Primary input could not invert the scale, and its 0.789-point loss mixes "no identity" with "no scale". All new arms therefore use one global target mean and standard deviation, fitted on the fold's training rows, and the arms with a letter g in the name carry that change.
  • Experiment 404 does not make any arm redundant. Experiment 404 (plan on PR #58 (Experiment 404: a lagless module and a calibration module with continuous trust weights for the lagged power inputs), no fit run yet) attends over three lag tokens and a lagless-forecast token (arm B3). Its arm B7 adds a 7-day CNN, but only on top of the trust head and the cross-fitted lagless forecast, and it is the lowest priority. The arms below ask the narrower question of identity, so they run now.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Names say which components each arm carries: g is the global target scale, 3 is the three origin lags (lag_origin, lag_same_time_latest_day, lag_same_time_latest_week, each with its age and missing flag), H is the 7-day encoder, E is the 8-wide Primary embedding, and N is no embedding.

  • E406 (stored). Experiment 406's pooled network with the embedding and per-Primary targets (pooled_emb). Zero fits; read with experiment_store.read_predictions.
  • E3g. Embedding, three origin lags, global target. The control for everything below.
  • N3g. No embedding, three origin lags, global target. Experiment 406's pooled_noemb made scale-fair.
  • NH. No embedding, three origin lags, and the 7-day encoder. The arm the hypothesis names.
  • EH. Embedding, three origin lags, and the 7-day encoder.
  • NHs. As NH, but each origin's history is that of a different Primary on the same run day (a fixed derangement of the Primaries, the same for training and scoring). It has the encoder's capacity without the Primary's own history, so NH minus NHs separates information from capacity.
  • NH0. No embedding, the 7-day encoder, and no origin lags. Tests whether the history makes the lags redundant, as experiment 388's arm E suggests.
  • Held-out stage (advance rule above). Arms N3g, NH, E3g, and EH, each fitted four times per fold and seed with one quarter of the Primaries (every fourth, by index) left out of training entirely, and scored only on that quarter. E3g and EH have no embedding for an unseen Primary and receive the mean embedding of the Primaries they trained on (a placeholder), and a second forecast from the same network uses the mean embedding within the left-out Primary's metering group (a stronger placeholder). Both are named in the tables. The code prints which Primaries fall in each quarter, and the tables say how many signed-MW and MVA-only Primaries each holds. Left-out Primaries are also scored against climatology and manual_heuristic.

The probe. After each fit of NH, EH, and NH0, a linear softmax classifier is trained on the frozen 32-wide encoder output of every training origin to predict the Primary (16 classes) and the month of the year (12 classes), and scored on the held-out early-stopping weeks (purged exactly as in experiment 397, so no probe row sits within 14 days before or 7 days after a held-out week). Reference probes use (a) the three origin lags with their missing flags, (b) the raw 336-value history, and (c) the encoder at random initialisation. A chance level is printed beside each accuracy.

docs.title: What the held-out result would change
docs.text:
• Held-out stage gate (maintainer's rank). The held-out arm is a test of onboarding a new Primary, which the maintainer has ranked low, so it adds no arm beyond N3g, NH, E3g, and EH. Only two seeds are fitted, and a contrast is read as undecided if its interval spans zero.
  • If NH beats both placeholders in C7 (point estimate at least 0.20 below at the signed-MW six). The history encoder becomes the first candidate route for onboarding a substation with no embedding, and a later experiment can compare it with static covariates (experiment 1c).
  • If NH does not beat the placeholders. The embedding-free route is closed for now, and a new Primary would need a fitted embedding from a short history, as experiment 406 suggested.

docs.title: Components adopted from earlier results, and not adopted
docs.text:
• Adopted. Pooled network with an 8-wide embedding and the ensemble mean and spread passed through once (experiment 397 and experiment 403); the three origin lags, with no extra weekly analogues (experiment 388: six weekly analogues raised the CRPS by 0.137 points); the D15 and D18 start cut (experiment 399); the Primary embedding in every arm that can use one (experiment 406: dropping it cost 0.789 points); the 1.15 widening is reported beside the raw scores, and the Gaussian 3-component head is kept (experiment 407: no tail arm beat the widened pooled network).
  • Missing-lag handling. Experiment 410 found that the pooled network loses 4 to 10 points when the three newest-reading lags are missing, so the encoder's missing channel matters. Each write-up table of the encoder arms includes the share of origins whose history has any gap.
  • Not adopted. Attention over input groups (experiment 397: the gate stayed within 0.01 of uniform). The lag-trust architecture, the explicit PV term, ERA5 and CAMS pretraining, and the input ports (experiments 404, 405, 418, and 419, none merged), because adopting an unmerged component would tie this experiment to a result that may not hold. Combining a winner of this experiment with those components belongs to the best-architecture assembly.

docs.title: Standing practices
docs.text:
• Followed. Monthly refits; cleaned data (see "The history"; the training rows are experiment 397's rows, so flagged exact-zero targets stay in training as in experiment 406, and the scorer drops them from the actuals and prints how many); the D15 and D18 start cut in the training rows, lags, history, and scoring actuals; every fitted network saved in the private folder; stored forecasts reused as references and never refitted; a screen of five folds with every number labelled interim; tails (coverage and pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99, raw and widened by 1.15) and the avoidable-curtailment cost beside CRPS; example forecast charts (a day-ahead forecast and a 14-day forecast, for one signed-MW Primary and one MVA-only Primary); a fresh Sonnet plan review and a fresh Sonnet code review before the first fit.
  • Lower-tail check. The tables report the lower tail (q01 and q05) on sunny, low-demand half-hours too, because curtailment depends on it.
  • Departure. The training rows are experiment 397's rows, as in experiment 406, so the fits stay paired with the stored controls. Experiment 398 found that dropping flagged half-hours moved the CRPS by at most 0.008 points in four earlier experiments.
  • D8. Any D8 figure carries the caveat "it is unproven whether the generator explains the steps and the gap".

docs.title: Fit counts, time, and memory
docs.text:
• Main stage. 6 new arms (E3g, N3g, NH, NHs, EH, NH0) by 5 folds by 3 seeds is 90 pooled fits, and E406 adds none.
  • Held-out stage. 4 arms by 4 quarters by 5 folds by 2 seeds is 160 pooled fits (seeds 0 and 1 only, because each fit trains on 12 Primaries). It runs only if the advance rule holds.
  • Probes. 45 probe sets (3 encoder arms by 5 folds by 3 seeds), each a few seconds on the GPU.
  • Time. Experiment 406 fitted one pooled plain network in about 50 s on the GPU. The encoder adds convolutions over 336 steps for every row, so the estimate is 60 to 120 s per fit, and the whole experiment is expected to take 4 to 8 hours. The first task after the fit slot is granted is to time one fit of each arm and replace this estimate.
  • Memory. One GPU process under 8 GB of GPU memory, one feeder core, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, and systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p OOMPolicy=continue. The history table is 16 Primaries by about 820 origin days by 336 half-hours in float16 (about 9 MB) plus a missing mask, gathered per batch by (Primary, origin day). The fit script logs the peak GPU memory.
  • Stop line. The fit script reads MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo before each fit and exits cleanly, leaving finished fits in place, when it falls to 12 GB or below. Every fit writes its own file atomically, so a stopped run resumes where it stopped.

docs.title: Checks the write-up reports
docs.text:
• Absolute CRPS of every arm beside E406, experiment 406's per-Primary network, BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology, per group and per Primary.
  • The median forecast minus the mean forecast per Primary, the error of the mean forecast beside every quantile-score contrast, and which audit triggers fired.
  • The probe accuracies with chance levels (1 in 16 for the Primary, 3 in 12 for a month within one), run for NH, EH, and NH0 only.
  • Example forecasts: one day-ahead forecast and one 14-day forecast for one signed-MW Primary and one MVA-only Primary, from NH and from E3g.
  • Unlogged load-shift events. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs. The history of an origin can sit inside an unlogged event, so the encoder may read an event as a property of the Primary. The write-up states that the training and scoring rows can hold events no label covers.

docs.title: Counting towards the demand-v2 stop rule
docs.text: This experiment does not count. It tests where a pooled network gets its sense of identity, not a new demand model, so no idea's count rises whatever the verdict.

docs.title: Does training the pooled mixture density network at many origin hours, with the age of the weather forecast and of the newest power reading as inputs, remove its loss from stale inputs?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the pooled network's loss from stale readings was a time-of-day mismatch, and training with the forecast origin at many hours of the day removes most of it. We asked whether the pooled mixture density network (a neural network that outputs a probability distribution; one network for all substations, from experiment 397) can be trained to cope with a weather forecast that is a day old and with power readings that arrive late. Each change to the inputs is an "arm" (key below). Experiment 410 found that the newest power readings arriving 12 hours late raised the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lead times of days 1 to 10, points of effective capacity, where one point is 1% of capacity) by 0.20 and 0.15 points; the refit here (T0) gives 0.18 points at the six primary substations with signed meters (the signed six) and by 0.13 at the eight with apparent-power meters (the MVA-only eight). When the network is trained with the origin at eight hours of the day, those losses fall to 0.04 and 0.02 points (arm T1). The pre-registered rule gives "partly supported". Every experiment 410 limit holds at both groups for the main arm T3, but T3's score on fresh inputs is 0.078 points worse at the MVA-only eight, above the +0.03 the pre-registered rule allows for the fresh-case score. The age inputs do not help: T2n, the same training without them, does as well as T2 (and better at one stale-weather arm).

Key to the arms. Training arms (offsets in hours after the 00:00 UTC weather run; each random draw is made once per training row and seed):

Arm Origin offset h Reading delay d Previous weather run Origin lags missing Age inputs T0 9 0 never as in the data no T1 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30 0 never as in the data no T2 as T1 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24 never as in the data yes T2n as T1 as T2 never as in the data no T3 as T1 as T2 probability 0.25 as in the data yes T4 as T1 as T2 probability 0.25 all three, probability 0.10 yes
  • Test arms are experiment 410's: FRESH, W24, and W48 (the weather forecast from the run one or two days earlier), Pn (readings delayed by n hours: P6, P12, P24), both at once (W24_P12, W24_P24), and DROP (the three origin lags missing). Four test arms are new. P30, P36, and P48 put the newest reading at the same hour of day as P6, P12, and P24, a day further back (23:30, 17:30, 05:30). P10 lies off the 3-hour training grid.
  • Reference columns. S397 is experiment 410's stored pooled network (trained at 09:00 on power with no cleaning rules). S1M is experiment 410's XGBoost model, which is not refitted.
  • The age inputs are the hours since the weather run and the hours since the newest reading (3.5 plus d), each divided by 48. The reading age is a linear function of two existing inputs (the lag ages and the lead), so it is redundant by construction; arm T2n tests that.
