R and A of experiment 425: the pooled plain network with the 8-wide Primary embedding, 3 Gaussian components, setting g09, and the ensemble mean and spread inputs, trained on ensemble rows only (R) or pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS rows and fine-tuned at a learning rate of 2e-4 (A). Same rows, the D15 and D18 start cut at 2025-03-01, the flagged exact-zero drop, held-out weeks, row weights, 1.15 widening, and monthly refits. The stored seeds 0 to 2 of both arms on the four screen folds are the controls. A check (e00437_fit.py check) proves that a fold built here without extra columns equals experiment 425's fold, bit for bit.
  • Arms. Each arm appends columns to the 46 inputs and changes nothing else. Bundles:
    • T, thermal lag (8 columns). Trailing means of the ensemble-mean temperature over 3, 6, and 24 hours; the temperature change over 3 and 6 hours; the minimum and maximum over the local day of the valid time; and the days since the trailing 24-hour mean last exceeded 5 degrees C, capped at 10.
    • S, solar gain (6 columns). Trailing means of the ensemble-mean shortwave over 3, 6, and 24 hours; the 3-hour change in the clear-sky index (shortwave over Haurwitz clear-sky shortwave, held at its last daylight value overnight; the helper of experiment 396 arm W7); and the realised CAMS irradiance of the last complete UTC day before the origin (its mean in W/m2 and its ratio to CAMS clear-sky). CAMS publishes the previous day at midnight UTC, so production can read both.
    • F, look-ahead (6 columns). Forward means of ensemble-mean temperature and shortwave over the 6 and 24 hours after the valid time, taken from the same run only, and the share of each window the run covers (windows are truncated at the end of the 14-day horizon).
    • C, calendar, tariff, and national signals (14 columns). The Economy 7 step as a UTC half-hour indicator and that indicator times degrees below 15.5 C; five Lincolnshire school-term columns from experiment 11's calendar (term flag; signed days to the nearest term start and end; signed days from the year's first working day; a window flag); and seven signals of the local day before the origin: the mean, maximum, and 16:00 to 19:00 mean of the Elexon market index price, a Demand Flexibility Service flag, and the day's mean national demand, embedded solar, and embedded wind (NESO historic demand). All 16 Primaries lie at 52.9 to 53.3 degrees N, 0.2 degrees W to 0.3 degrees E, inside the box that experiment 11 found to be Lincolnshire, so one county's calendar applies to every Primary.
  • Pretrained form. T, S, and F are also run as T_pre, S_pre, and F_pre: pretrained on experiment 418's ERA5-and-CAMS pseudo-run rows with the same columns computed from the dense weather, then fine-tuned on ensemble rows at 2e-4. C has no pretraining form, because the pretraining rows carry no school or national columns. A pretrained network is fitted for each bundle, fold, and seed, and cannot be shared across folds: the pretraining rows end 3.5 hours before each fold's refit, so a network pretrained for a later fold has seen the earlier fold's test month.
  • Window construction. A trailing window ends at the valid time. For half-hours at or before the forecast origin (09:00 UTC) the series holds the ensemble mean of the previous run that covers them (leads of about 9 to 33 hours); after the origin it holds this run's own ensemble mean. ERA5 is not used, because it arrives about 5 days late and a column built from it could not be served. e00437_features.py check rebuilds sample runs with every later run deleted and requires identical columns. In the pretrained form the windows come from the dense ERA5-and-CAMS series, which is the same stand-in the pretraining rows use for the valid-time weather.
  • Known mismatch in the pretrained form. check-pretraining printed each column's standardised mean and spread in the pretraining rows and the ensemble rows for the 2026-01 fold. The weather windows agree to within 0.25 standard deviations in the mean and 0.07 in the spread, except csi_change_3h, whose spread is 2.6 in the pretraining rows against 0.9 in the ensemble rows. CAMS irradiance changes more over 3 hours than the mean of 51 ensemble members does, the same smoothing gap that affects the shortwave input itself. The write-up reports it as a caveat for S_pre.
  • Dismantling. A bundle that advances is split into halves and refitted in the same form: T_means/T_rest, S_means/S_rest, F_temperature/F_shortwave, and for C C_tariff/C_school/C_national. A combination of the winning bundles (T+S+F, with or without C) is fitted once at least two bundles advance. These are descriptive.
  • Fits and compute. 4 bundles by 4 folds by 3 seeds is 48 ensemble-only fits (about 75 seconds each including the forecast) and 36 pretrained fits (about 55 seconds of pretraining and 40 of fine-tuning each, plus a pretraining-row build of about 2 minutes per fold and bundle). That is about 1.0 plus 1.8 GPU-hours before dismantling, and up to 2 more GPU-hours for the halves and the combination. One GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, 8 GB of host memory, one BLAS thread.
  • Standing practices followed. Monthly refits; cleaned data (flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped, counts printed per fold); the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01; every fitted network saved under work/models/; stored controls reused; tails, the avoidable-curtailment cost, and the example forecasts reported; four-fold screen with every number labelled interim.

docs.title: Caveats registered before the fits
docs.text:
• Window seam at the origin. The ensemble-mean summaries hold no half-hour at or before the run's own origin, so half-hours between 00:00 and 09:00 on the origin day come from the previous run (leads of about 9 to 33 hours). Trailing windows therefore mix two runs at 09:00.
  • T is partly a look-ahead bundle. The daily minimum and maximum temperature use the later hours of the valid time's local day, which the run already forecasts. F isolates pure look-ahead.
  • Publication latency of the previous-day signals. The CAMS, Elexon price, and NESO demand columns use the whole local or UTC day before the origin date. The brief states that CAMS arrives at midnight UTC; the latency of the Elexon and NESO files at 09:00 UTC was not measured, and the training values are the final revised ones. The write-up states both as open points for serving.
  • Forward windows in the pretrained form come from ERA5 and CAMS, which do not degrade with lead, while the ensemble-mean forward windows do. The write-up reports this as a caveat for F_pre.
  • Economy 7 is on the UTC clock, as the brief and experiments 121, 137, and 281 define it. The protocol's economy_7_step slice is on local half-hours, so during British Summer Time the two differ by one hour. The write-up reports C on that slice and states the offset.
  • Bundle C has no pretrained form. The brief asks for the weather bundles in both forms; the pretraining rows hold no school or national columns, so C runs ensemble-only.
  • No summer fold. The four folds are autumn, Christmas, winter, and spring; 2026-06 is not included, so a solar-gain effect in summer cannot show.
  • Data searched for bundle C. On disk and used: Lincolnshire County Council term dates (experiment 11, 2021-22 to 2025-26), Elexon market index prices (p3-price-download), NESO historic demand and embedded generation (experiment 185), and Demand Flexibility Service requirements (experiment 177). A school calendar for another county is not needed, because all 16 Primaries lie in Lincolnshire. No download is made.
  • Reported beside CRPS: the 12-to-36-hour band, tail calibration per group and per Primary, the cold winter night slice, the avoidable-curtailment cost, and the dropped half-hours per fold. Load-shift plots and load-shift row sets do not apply. Experiment 396 arm W7 has no result yet; the write-up cites it if it lands.
  • Process, in order. Draft pull request; plan review (fresh Sonnet); code review (fresh Sonnet) before the first fit; fits; results review with the audit triggers; write-up; prose review.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
No bundle lowered the CRPS by the registered bar, so no dismantling or confirmation run is planned. The best arms lowered the CRPS at only one group, by less than 0.03 points, in 2 of 4 folds. The next step is to leave these bundles out of the pooled plain network and, if the question returns, to test the thermal-lag bundle T on more folds.

Arm key. R is the ensemble-only pooled plain network, and A is its pretrained form; both are the controls. T adds thermal-lag columns, S solar-gain columns, F look-ahead columns, and C calendar, tariff, and national-signal columns (C_tariff adds only the 2 tariff columns of C). A _pre suffix marks the pretrained form of a bundle, whose control is A. "The six" and "the eight" are the 6 signed-MW Primaries and the 8 MVA-only Primaries.

docs.title: Contrasts
docs.text:
CRPS at days 1 to 10 in points of capacity, four monthly folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03), seeds 0 to 2. A positive difference means the arm is worse than its control. Intervals are the descriptive month-block bootstrap at the 99.69% level, which with four blocks spans the fold range; the decision rests on the fold counts.

Arm (control) Signed-MW six MVA-only eight Verdict T (R) +0.016 (-0.078 to +0.081) -0.022 (-0.071 to +0.007) 2 of 4 folds at the eight S (R) +0.043 (-0.037 to +0.136) +0.002 (-0.069 to +0.099) tail harm at q95 C (R) +0.059 (-0.054 to +0.163) +0.038 (-0.057 to +0.170) worse C_tariff (R) +0.047 (+0.005 to +0.165) +0.021 (-0.041 to +0.045) worse F (R) +0.042 (-0.002 to +0.086) -0.000 (-0.047 to +0.049) no change T_pre (A) +0.025 (-0.036 to +0.089) -0.029 (-0.094 to +0.015) 2 of 4 folds at the eight S_pre (A) -0.016 (-0.086 to +0.078) +0.011 (-0.115 to +0.107) below the bar F_pre (A) +0.026 (-0.041 to +0.084) +0.020 (-0.002 to +0.036) tail harm at q95

Controls: R scores 3.404 and A 3.341 at the six, 3.917 and 3.764 at the eight. The group of Primaries D15 and D18 is report-only; every arm except T_pre (-0.176) is worse than its control there, by 0.14 to 0.66 points.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (solar gain S helps most on cold sunny days) is not supported. S was worse than R on cold sunny days (+0.308 at the six) and better on cold overcast days (-0.236), the opposite order.
  • P2 (thermal lag T helps at both groups, most on cold winter nights) is not supported. T was worse at the six (+0.016). The small gain of T at the eight came from two folds, 2025-12 (-0.071) and 2026-01 (-0.025); 7 of 8 Primaries improved.
  • P3 (look-ahead F helps at the eight) is not supported. F changed the CRPS at the eight by -0.000.
  • P4 (calendar, tariff, and national signals C help on the Economy 7 step) is not supported. C was worse on that slice at the six (2.985 against 2.805 for R).
  • P5 (the pretrained form gains at least as much over its control) is not supported. For each bundle, the gain over the control of the pretrained form beat that of the ensemble-only form at one group and lost at the other. The gain of S_pre over A beat the gain of S over R by 0.059 at the six and lost by 0.009 at the eight. For F_pre against F, the figures are 0.016 better at the six and 0.020 worse at the eight. For T_pre against T, they are 0.009 worse at the six and 0.007 better at the eight.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Fold-by-fold differences, per-Primary CRPS, tails, and the cold-night, sunny, Economy 7, and cold sunny-versus-overcast slices are in the figures below; the slice intervals are not shown because few half-hours (769 and 911 on cold overcast days) make them unreliable.
  • A fresh reviewer re-derived the pooled CRPS of R, A, T, and S_pre from the raw forecast files and matched the scorer to three decimals. The median-error and CRPS contrasts agree in sign in all 16 arm-and-group pairs. Leaving out any one Primary flips no verdict.
  • The new columns are not degenerate: their standardised spread is near 1 and the first layer of the neural network uses them. The ensemble-only fold without extra columns equals experiment 425's fold bit for bit.
  • C_tariff (2 columns) beat C (which contains them) by 0.012 at the six. Both differences from the control are inside the noise.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The screen is too coarse to show "no effect". The minimum detectable effect is 0.064 points against R and 0.045 against A, which is 1.5 to 2 times the 0.03 bar, and fold-to-fold differences swing by more than the bar.
  • The four folds hold no summer month, so the second example is spring and S cannot be judged in summer.
  • The hyperparameters were tuned at 46 inputs and reused at 48 to 60. Extra inputs at fixed capacity may explain the worse scores of C and S, and a bundle might help with another setting.
  • The scorer does not compute P1 and P4 as single numbers, and it pairs by fold, not by fold and seed. The slice contrasts above were read by hand.
  • The pretraining mismatch for csi_change_3h registered above applies to S_pre.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Test bundle T on more folds, since it is the only bundle that lowered the CRPS at the eight with both controls (R and A).

docs.title: Data used and where it lives
docs.text:
• Data. The cleaned NGED Primary-substation power series, ECMWF ensemble forecasts, ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather for the pretrained arms, and the on-disk school, price, and national-demand series for bundle C.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00437-neural-demand-thermal-lag-solar-gain-and-tariff-feature-bundles/.
  • Saved networks and forecasts. $DATA_PATH_INTERNAL/ml-experiments/00437-neural-demand-thermal-lag-solar-gain-and-tariff-feature-bundles/work/.

docs.title: If the day-window neural network is told exactly which of its recent half-hours lie inside a load-shift event, does it forecast better inside real events?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the control failed, so this experiment cannot say whether detecting events is the limit on trusting recent power. We gave the three-day neural network (E3) a sixth input channel that marks exactly which half-hours of its three windows lie inside a load-shift event (E-oracle). On injected harm rows the mark is exact, so E-oracle should have scored clearly better than E3. E-oracle scored 0.035 CRPS points worse (3.033 against 2.998), against a pre-registered range of -0.60 to -0.15. Under the plan's decision rule, a result like this is a failed control and not a finding. The verdict is therefore inconclusive. The audit found no wiring bug. The explanation we have not tested is that the neural network already infers events from the power values, so the flag adds variance and no information.

How to read the numbers. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. Unless a column says otherwise, each number is the CRPS in percentage points of effective capacity at days 1 to 10 (smaller is better) after the 1.15 widening of the bands. Every number comes from four test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), three fit seeds (0 to 2), and monthly refits. A fresh reviewer re-derived the headline numbers from the stored forecasts, and they matched. A contrast is the first arm minus the second, so a positive number means E-oracle scored worse. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is 1.96 x sqrt(2) x s / sqrt(3), where s is R-inj's seed-to-seed standard deviation on the row set. Intervals are 95% intervals from resampling months and days. The signed-MW six are the Primary substations metered in signed megawatts (MW), and the MVA-only eight are metered in unsigned megavolt-amperes (MVA) only. E3, S1, and R-inj are the arms of experiment 428: E3 is the three-day neural network without the flag, S1 is the three lags plus their surprise, and R-inj is the three lags trained on injected events. NGED is National Grid Electricity Distribution, the distribution network operator.

A row is a clean row when its recent power lies outside every logged load-shift event. A real event row is one whose time being forecast lies inside a logged event. A real harm row is one whose time being forecast lies outside every logged event but whose recent power lies inside one. An injected harm row is the same as a real harm row, with simulated events added to clean power. The real events are the corrected label table's events, each padded by 48 half-hours (24 hours) before the onset and after the end, as in experiment 402 and experiment 428. The table holds 170 padded events across the experiment's Primaries, and 33 of them have target rows in the four test months (56,214 target rows, before the split into the two metering groups). The largest event supplies 6,640 of those rows, which is why the real-event contrasts are also given without it.

The pre-registered rule says this is a failed control. At the signed-MW six, E-oracle minus E3 on injected harm rows is +0.035 (0.021 to 0.049). The plan counted the result as a failed control if that contrast was above minus the MDE (the MDE there is 0.071), and +0.035 is above it. Of the five pre-registered predictions, only P2 held (clean rows within plus or minus 0.05: +0.032). P1 failed (+0.035, predicted -0.60 to -0.15). P3 failed (E-oracle minus S1 on real event rows is +0.607, predicted -0.40 to 0.00). P4 failed (E-oracle minus E3 on real harm rows is +0.068, predicted -0.20 to 0.00). P5 failed (the MVA-only eight do not show the same signs, see below).

Table 1 gives the three contrasts at the signed-MW six, with the MDE and the absolute CRPS of E-oracle and E3. O1 is E-oracle minus E3, O2 is E-oracle minus S1, and O3 is E-oracle minus R-inj.

Row set Rows E-oracle / E3 CRPS O1 E-oracle - E3 O2 E-oracle - S1 O3 E-oracle - R-inj MDE Clean 254,725 3.029 / 2.997 +0.032 (+0.016 to +0.048) +0.165 (+0.135 to +0.196) +0.082 (+0.057 to +0.107) 0.077 Injected harm 432,081 3.033 / 2.998 +0.035 (+0.021 to +0.049) +0.137 (+0.108 to +0.166) +0.077 (+0.056 to +0.098) 0.071 Real harm 40,643 3.062 / 2.994 +0.068 (+0.044 to +0.093) +0.135 (+0.087 to +0.182) +0.127 (+0.097 to +0.157) 0.123 Real event 31,898 6.295 / 5.964 +0.331 (+0.086 to +0.578) +0.607 (+0.331 to +0.873) +0.438 (+0.266 to +0.598) 0.153 Real event, without the largest event 25,258 5.553 / 5.311 +0.242 (+0.112 to +0.387) +0.638 (+0.375 to +0.936) +0.388 (+0.245 to +0.537) 0.329

Absolute scores show the same order on every row set at the signed-MW six. Table 2 gives the CRPS of each arm.

Row set E-oracle E3 R-inj S1 Clean 3.029 2.997 2.947 2.865 Injected harm 3.033 2.998 2.956 2.897 Real harm 3.062 2.994 2.935 2.928 Real event 6.295 5.964 5.857 5.687

At the signed-MW six, E-oracle is the worst of the four arms on all four row sets, and S1 is the best. The flag therefore did not turn the three-day neural network into a better forecaster than the arms that see three lagged readings. Because the control failed, the reading rule for O2 is not applied: O2 on real event rows (+0.607) is above the MDE, which the rule would read as "the limit is downstream of detection", but that reading needs a working control.

At the signed-MW six, E-oracle minus E3 is positive in three of the four test months. On clean rows O1 is positive in 3 of 4 test months (-0.083 in 2026-06, +0.019 in 2025-10, +0.119 in 2026-01, +0.059 in 2026-03). On injected harm rows it is positive in 3 of 4 (-0.062, +0.038, +0.094, +0.059, in the same order).

docs.title: The MVA-only eight
docs.text:
At the MVA-only eight, E-oracle beat E3 on real event rows and real harm rows. This is one observation at one group. Table 3 gives the same contrasts.

Row set Rows E-oracle / E3 CRPS O1 E-oracle - E3 O2 E-oracle - S1 O3 E-oracle - R-inj MDE Clean 389,812 3.739 / 3.694 +0.045 (+0.031 to +0.059) +0.177 (+0.149 to +0.204) +0.090 (+0.061 to +0.120) 0.082 Injected harm 663,901 4.175 / 4.181 -0.006 (-0.020 to +0.008) +0.094 (+0.072 to +0.117) +0.022 (-0.008 to +0.052) 0.081 Real harm 35,235 5.465 / 5.575 -0.110 (-0.166 to -0.054) +0.038 (-0.020 to +0.092) -0.016 (-0.059 to +0.028) 0.368 Real event 18,810 7.232 / 7.476 -0.244 (-0.397 to -0.082) +0.026 (-0.066 to +0.122) -0.131 (-0.241 to -0.013) 0.401

The flag lowered the error on real event rows (O1 -0.244, CRPS 7.232 against 7.476) and real harm rows (O1 -0.110, 5.465 against 5.575), and did not change it on injected harm rows (-0.006, 4.175 against 4.181, interval from -0.020 to +0.008). Both gains are smaller than the MDE of their row sets (0.401 and 0.368). Against S1, E-oracle is no better on real event rows (+0.026, interval from -0.066 to +0.122; CRPS 7.232 against 7.207). In the 2026-01 and 2026-03 test months O1 on real event rows is -0.466 and -0.378, and it is +0.102 in 2025-10 (2026-06 has no real event rows for this group). We report this as a single-group observation, from three of four test months, with no tested cause.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Wiring audit. A fresh Sonnet sub-agent re-derived the headline numbers from the stored forecasts, which matched, and read the code. It found no wiring bug. The flag is (code != 0) | real-event mask, gathered at the same window positions as the power values, multiplied by the observed channel, and appended as channel 5. The fit and the prediction both build the neural network with one more channel.
  • Untested explanation. This explanation is untested. The encoder may already infer events from the power values, and the training loss gives no reason to read the flag. An extra input would then add variance.
  • Triggers fired: the control failed (see above). No nested arm beats its container.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Arms and rows. E-oracle is experiment 428's E3 with the sixth channel, fitted with experiment 428's training recipe: injected worlds 1 to 3 mixed with the clean series, cleaned data with the D15 and D18 start cut, and monthly refits on the 24 months before each test month. It is scored on the held-out injected worlds 4 to 6 and the real series. E3, S1, and R-inj are experiment 428's stored forecasts, scored on identical rows (the scoring script asserts this).
  • Fits saved. The 12 neural networks (4 test months x 3 seeds) and their forecasts are in this experiment's private data folder, never in git.
  • Seeds and folds. Three seeds and four test months. The MDE comes from R-inj's seed-to-seed spread on three seeds (mde.parquet), and the real-event row sets are few and dominated by one event, so their intervals are wide.
  • Unlogged events. NGED says some load-shift events are missing from its logs. Clean rows can therefore hold events no label covers, the flag is zero for those events, and the real-event rows may undercount events. The padded real-event mask is also hindsight: it covers each logged event with the padding above, which no live detector could know.
  • Exact flag on injected worlds only. The flag is exact only on injected worlds. On the real series it is the padded label table.
  • Group D15 and D18. The contrasts for D15 and D18 are in contrasts.parquet; they are report-only and are not discussed here.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• The failed control means a flag-as-input neural network is not yet a test of detection. A repeat could first find why E-oracle does not beat E3 on injected harm rows, for example by checking whether the fitted weights on channel 5 are near zero, or by training with the flag as a gate on the lagged power values.
  • The MVA-only eight observation could be re-checked on a different set of seeds before it is trusted.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. The signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight are the two groups of Primary substations by metering.

This control asks whether the limit on trusting recent power is detection. Experiments 404 and 428 never gave the neural network an event label, so a failure to follow fewer event steps might mean the neural network cannot find events or might mean that, even told where the events are, it cannot use the information. E-oracle tells it exactly. The idea is the maintainer's (2026-10-31). The oracle follows the flag-oracle controls of experiment 402, which set XGBoost mixture weights from event flags.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Network. Experiment 428's E3 (three windows of 48 half-hours, a convolution, one attention head, the unchanged mixture head), with a sixth channel on every window position: 1 where the half-hour is inside an event, else 0, and 0 where the half-hour is unobserved.
  • Flag. On the clean series, a half-hour of the padded real-event mask of the corrected label table. On an injected world, a half-hour with a non-zero injected-event code (donor, recipient, or spike), or inside the padded real-event mask. The flag is exact on injected worlds. The padded real-event mask is hindsight: it covers each logged event with the padding of experiment 428, so the real-event result carries the unlogged-event caveat (NGED may have events missing from its logs).
  • Training and rows. Experiment 428's: injected worlds 1 to 3 mixed with the clean series, cleaned data with the D15 and D18 start cut, monthly refits on the 24 months before the test month, scored on the held-out injected worlds 4 to 6 and the real series. The 1.15 widening is applied at scoring, as in 428.
  • Compute. Twelve fits (4 folds, 3 seeds), about 15 GPU-minutes each (a one-epoch timing took 27 s including start-up), so about 3 GPU-hours, one process under 8 GB. E3, S1, and R-inj are not refitted: their stored forecasts are read.
  • Reported. The real event count and definition, the absolute score of each arm beside the contrasts, tails, and the plots of example forecasts and of six labelled real events.

docs.title: Does adding the surprise at the three lags to the lagged network still lower the error on three new seeds?
docs.text:
Take-home message: adding the surprise to the three lagged power readings still lowered the forecast error on three new fit seeds, by about as much as on the first three seeds, so S1 meets the pre-registered rule and is the base for later neural lag experiments, pending the maintainer's decision on the serving-path requirement.

Experiment 428 found that a neural network given three lagged power readings plus the surprise at each reading (S1) beat the same network without the surprise (R-inj) by 0.083 continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) points on clean rows. That margin was only slightly larger than the spread between fit seeds. We refitted both networks with three new seeds (24 fits, where one fit is one network for one arm, test month, and seed) and scored them on the same rows. S1 again scored lower than R-inj in all four test months on clean rows at the six Primary substations metered in signed megawatts, though the gain is uneven (-0.210 in 2026-01, -0.053 in 2026-03).

The lagless forecast is a forecast that sees no lagged power. The surprise at a lag is the difference between the lagged reading and the lagless forecast, divided by half the width of the lagless forecast's 5% to 95% band.

How to read the numbers. Unless a column says otherwise, each number is the CRPS in percentage points of effective capacity at days 1 to 10 (smaller is better) after the 1.15 widening of the bands. Every number is interim, from four test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). A contrast is S1 minus R-inj, so a negative number favours S1. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is 1.96 x sqrt(2) x s / sqrt(n), where s is R-inj's seed-to-seed standard deviation and n is the number of seeds. A row is a clean row when its recent power lies outside every logged load-shift event. A row is a real harm row when the time being forecast lies outside every logged event but its recent power lies inside one, and a real event row when the time being forecast lies inside one. Injected harm rows are the same as real harm rows, with simulated events added to clean power. The signed-MW six are the Primaries metered in signed megawatts, and the MVA-only eight are metered in unsigned megavolt-amperes. A row is one forecast of one Primary, issued at one time, for one valid time.

The pre-registered rule is met on seeds 3 to 5. At the signed-MW six, S1 minus R-inj on clean rows is -0.106 (95% interval -0.121 to -0.091), below minus the MDE of 0.061, and all four test months are negative. At the MVA-only eight, S1 minus R-inj on clean rows is -0.103 (-0.112 to -0.094), with an MDE of 0.087. Pooled over seeds 0 to 5, the signed-MW six give -0.094 (-0.106 to -0.083), with an MDE of 0.066.

S1 lowered the error clearly on injected harm rows, and by less than the MDE on real event rows and real harm rows. Table 1 shows the contrasts at the signed-MW six.

Row set Seeds 3-5 Seeds 0-5 MDE (seeds 3-5) Test months negative (seeds 3-5) Clean -0.106 (-0.121 to -0.091) -0.094 (-0.106 to -0.083) 0.061 4 of 4 Injected harm -0.088 (-0.108 to -0.069) -0.074 (-0.091 to -0.057) 0.071 4 of 4 Real event -0.216 (-0.355 to -0.079) -0.193 (-0.309 to -0.068) 0.246 3 of 4 Real harm -0.031 (-0.056 to -0.005) -0.019 (-0.043 to +0.008) 0.102 2 of 4

There are 31,898 real event rows and 40,643 real harm rows at the signed-MW six. At the MVA-only eight the real harm contrast is -0.039 (-0.077 to +0.002), with an MDE of 0.262.

Absolute scores (seeds 3 to 5, signed-MW six, CRPS points). On clean rows R-inj scores 2.972 and S1 2.866. On injected harm rows they score 2.987 and 2.899, on real event rows 5.921 and 5.705, and on real harm rows 2.944 and 2.912.

docs.text:
S1's tails are better on clean rows and real event rows, and slightly worse on real harm rows. Table 2 gives the pinball loss (points) and coverage at q95 and q99 (the 95th and 99th percentile forecasts) at the signed-MW six, seeds 3 to 5.

At the MVA-only eight, S1's q99 pinball loss on real harm rows is lower (0.349 against 0.368).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary (clean rows, pooled seeds). The stored forecasts hold 11 quantiles and no mean, so the mean is the average of the 11 quantiles (a proxy). The difference ranges from -6.4 points (D15) to +0.06 (D22). The difference is nearly identical for S1 and R-inj at every Primary (for example D15 -6.44 and -6.20), so the median-minus-mean difference does not explain the contrast.
  • Error of the median forecast. The mean absolute error of q50 on clean rows is lower for S1 in every group: 5.092 against 5.270 (signed-MW six), 6.320 against 6.489 (MVA-only eight), and 16.116 against 16.820 (D15 and D18). The sign agrees with the CRPS contrast.
  • Triggers fired: none. No control exists here, the result agrees with its prediction and with experiment 428, no nested arm beats its container, and the interval widths match 428's.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Arms and rows. S1 and R-inj of experiment 428, refitted with experiment 428's code on seeds 3, 4, and 5 (4 months x 3 seeds x 2 arms = 24 fits), monthly refits on the 24 months before each test month, cleaned data, the D15 and D18 start cut at 2025-03-01, and the simulated load-shift events that experiment 428 added to clean power. Seeds 0 to 2 are experiment 428's stored forecasts. Each seed has its own cross-fitted lagless table. The tables for seeds 3 to 5 were built with experiment 404's frozen code (15 tables: 5 months x 3 seeds), and the tables for seeds 0 to 2 are untouched.
  • Fits saved. Networks and forecasts are in this experiment's private data folder, never in git.
  • Experiment 404 harness. The arm needs only the lagless table and the three lags, so it could also run in experiment 404's harness.
  • Row identity. The scoring script asserts that S1 and R-inj are scored on identical rows.
  • Unlogged events. NGED (the distribution network operator) says some load-shift events are missing from its logs. Clean rows can therefore hold events no label covers. The real-event rows may undercount events, and the clean-row and harm-row figures may understate the effect of events.
  • Forecast horizon. The stored forecasts reach 10 days (240 hours), so the long example covers 10 days.
  • Serving-path requirement. S1 needs a lagless forecasting model in the serving path. The maintainer must accept that requirement before a release. R-inj is the fallback that needs no lagless forecast.
  • Schedule. Monthly refits, the research default. A weekly-refit re-check has not been run.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Later neural lag experiments (recent history, window statistics, untrusted inputs) could use S1 as the base network.
  • Those experiments could report the q99 pinball loss on real harm rows.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. The signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight are the two groups of Primary substations by metering.

This experiment checks a result that cleared its minimum detectable effect by 0.006. Experiment 428 found S1 lowered CRPS against R-inj by 0.083 on clean rows (minimum detectable effect 0.077), and one of four folds did not clear the minimum. New fit seeds are the cheapest independent check.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Arms. S1 and R-inj of experiment 428, fitted with its code unchanged on seeds 3, 4, and 5 (4 folds, so 24 fits, about 6 GPU-hours, one process under 8 GB).
  • Lagless tables. S1's surprise reads experiment 404's cross-fitted lagless forecast (K = 6 blocks). Experiment 404 froze tables for seeds 0 to 2 only, so tables for seeds 3 to 5 are built with the same frozen code (15 builds of about 1 minute each) so each fit seed has its own table.
  • Other. Cleaned data, D15 and D18 start cut, injected worlds, and scoring rows as in 428. The frozen tables for seeds 0 to 2 are untouched; experiment 428's stored forecasts supply seeds 0 to 2.
  • Reported. Absolute CRPS beside each contrast, the minimum detectable effect, per-fold and per-seed contrasts, the pooled contrast over seeds 0 to 5, tails, example forecasts, and whether the arm can run in experiment 404's harness.

docs.title: Does reading the surprise in a window around each lag, and against what the neighbouring Primaries did, help the lag network tell a load-shift event from a genuine level shift?
docs.text:
Take-home message: giving the lag network more ways to read the surprise did not lower the forecast error, so the network given the surprise at its three lagged readings alone (S1) stays the base for later lag experiments. The window statistics (S2) and the neighbour columns (S3) scored slightly worse than S1 on ordinary rows, and neighbours chosen at random scored about as well as the real neighbours. The limit on trusting recent power therefore does not lie in how the surprise is summarised.

We tested whether a lag network forecasts better when it is told more about how unusual each reading is. A lag network is a neural network that forecasts a substation's power from three earlier readings of that power. The surprise at a reading is the reading minus a forecast made without any lagged power, divided by half the width of that forecast's 5% to 95% band. Experiment 428 gave the network the surprise at each reading (S1), and experiment 439 confirmed that S1 beats the same network without the surprise (R-inj). Here S2 adds the average, spread, and extremes of the surprise in a 12-hour window around each reading, and S3 adds the same figures for the neighbouring Primary substations, because a load-shift event that moves load between neighbours shows an opposite shift next door and a genuine level shift does not. The window statistics come from experiment 404's module, copied with credit. We fitted 36 neural networks (3 arms, 4 test months, 3 fit seeds), added a control with randomly chosen neighbours (S3-rw), and scored all of them on experiment 428's rows. None of the arms beat S1 by the margin we set before any fit, so the verdict is not supported.

One arm, H-lvl, joined the experiment after the 36 window-arm fits. H-lvl is S1 plus a learned level offset per forecast origin. We added H-lvl after those fits and before we read any H-lvl score. The sweep covers seed 0 only. A fresh reviewer re-derived the window-arm numbers from the stored forecasts; the H-lvl numbers have not been audited separately.

Every number is interim, and its unit is CRPS points of effective capacity. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. Unless a column says otherwise, each number is the CRPS in percentage points of effective capacity at days 1 to 10 (smaller is better) after the 1.15 widening of the bands. All numbers are from four test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) and three fit seeds (0 to 2). H1 is H-lvl minus R-inj and H2 is H-lvl minus S1. A contrast is the first arm minus the second, so a negative number favours the first arm. Intervals are 95% intervals from resampling (test month, origin day) blocks. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is 1.96 × sqrt(2) × s / sqrt(3), where s is R-inj's seed-to-seed standard deviation. The pre-registered margin for a gain is the larger of 0.03 and the MDE of the row set. The signed-MW six are the Primaries metered in signed megawatts, and the MVA-only eight are metered in unsigned megavolt-amperes. A clean row is a forecast whose recent power lies outside every logged load-shift event. A real event row is one whose target time lies inside a logged event, and a real harm row is one whose target time lies outside every logged event but whose recent power lies inside one. An injected harm row is a real harm row with simulated events added to clean power. A row is one forecast of one Primary, issued at one time, for one valid time.

No contrast shows S2 or S3 beating S1 by the pre-registered margin, so neither advances. Table 1 gives the contrasts at the signed-MW six. The margin is 0.077 on clean rows, 0.071 on injected harm rows, 0.123 on real harm rows, and 0.153 on real event rows. Four contrasts on real event rows exceed their margin: W3 (+0.406, which favours the control), W5 (-0.313, which favours S3-rw over S2), H1 (-0.569), and H2 (-0.400). W5 numerically meets the gain rule, because -0.313 is below minus 0.153 and its interval excludes zero. W5 comes almost entirely from one test month, however: W5 on real event rows is -0.504 in 2026-01 against -0.050, -0.017, and +0.032 in the other three months. For the related contrast of S3-rw with S3 (W3), the audit found that 41 of 93 event-days favour S3-rw and that 91% of the gain comes from 2026-01 and from a single Primary (see Checks). None of the four decides whether S2 or S3 advances: W3 and W5 involve the control with random neighbours, and H1 and H2 involve H-lvl. The attention version of S3 did not run, because its condition (W2 a gain on clean or injected harm rows) failed.

S2 and S3 raised the error on clean rows and injected harm rows, and lowered it on real harm rows by less than the margin. On real harm rows S2 beat S1 by 0.037 (interval excludes zero), a difference under a third of the 0.123 margin. The lower error on real harm rows does not offset the higher error on clean rows, which number about six times as many as the real harm rows. The gap between S3 and S2 is small (W2 on clean rows +0.021). The control with random neighbours scored within 0.02 points of S3 on every row set except real event rows, where it scored better (W3 +0.406).

Absolute scores (signed-MW six). Table 2 gives the CRPS of each arm, which shows that S1 is the lowest on clean rows and injected harm rows, and that the differences between the five lag arms are under 0.1 points on every row set except real events.

S3 raised the q99 pinball loss on real event rows by 0.174 points over S1, above the 0.02 maximum increase that the research programme allows. Table 4 gives the pinball loss at the 95th and 99th percentile forecasts (q95 and q99) at the signed-MW six. S2 lowered the q99 loss on real event rows (1.047 against 1.127 for S1) and added no tail harm on any row set.

docs.title: Sweep
docs.text: A step in the lags reaches the forecast median in a share of 0.175 for S2, S3, and S3-rw, against 0.225 for S1 and 0.075 for R-inj. The sweep adds a step of 5% of effective capacity (both signs) to the three lags of clean rows, one more lag at each k (k = 1 steps the newest lag, k = 2 also steps the daily lag, and k = 3 also steps the weekly lag), and reads the forecasts 24 to 72 hours ahead. The median share at k = 3 is the share of the step that appears in the forecast median, where 1 means the forecast follows the step in full. S3 follows as large a share of the step as S2 (0.175 each), so P5 holds. The 90% band width ratio is at most 1.007 for every arm, and the lag-masked control gives exactly 0 gap for every arm, so the sweep ran as designed. The sweep covers seed 0 only.

docs.title: H-lvl
docs.text:
H-lvl failed its first condition: it scored worse than R-inj on clean rows at leads of 12 to 36 hours. H1 on those rows is +0.072 (0.000 to 0.152) CRPS points (26,620 rows), against the required -0.03 or lower, and over the whole range of leads it is +0.111 (0.048 to 0.183). The contrast over all leads is positive in three of four test months (2025-10 +0.013, 2026-01 +0.466, 2026-03 +0.067) and negative in 2026-06 (-0.095). H2 at 12 to 36 hours is +0.183 (0.108 to 0.263). The level-trace diagnostic for the second condition (the learned level moves the right way in at least 7 of 10 real events) was not run, because the first condition had already failed.

H-lvl scored lowest of the six arms on real event rows, and the evidence for that gain is weak. On those rows H-lvl has CRPS 5.288 against 5.857 for R-inj and a q99 pinball loss of 0.737 against 1.323. The interval on that gain is wide (-1.048 to -0.099), and H-lvl scored worse on the other three row sets. We read the real-event gain as a tail-calibration effect and not as evidence for the learned level. H-lvl was added after the 36 window-arm fits and before any H-lvl score was read, and its numbers have not been audited separately.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The three arms give almost the same forecast. Figures 6 and 7 show a day-ahead and a 10-day forecast of one Primary from the signed-MW six, from an origin in 2026-01, for S1, S2, and S3. The medians differ by a few points of capacity at most, and the 5% to 95% bands overlap.

Figure 8 shows six labelled events, with the forecasts of S1, S3, and S3-rw made the day before each event starts. Three events are from the signed-MW six and three from the MVA-only eight.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (clean rows, signed-MW six and MVA-only eight). The stored forecasts hold 11 quantiles and no mean, so the mean is the average of the 11 quantiles (a proxy). The median minus the mean ranges from -0.499 (S3) to -0.579 (R-inj) points at the signed-MW six and from -0.717 (S3) to -0.833 (R-inj) at the MVA-only eight. The difference is similar for every arm, so the median-minus-mean difference does not explain the contrasts.
  • Error of the median forecast. The mean absolute error of q50 on clean rows at the signed-MW six is 5.097 for S1, 5.153 for S2, 5.173 for S3, 5.154 for S3-rw, 5.281 for R-inj, and 5.394 for H-lvl. The order agrees with the CRPS contrasts. At the MVA-only eight S2 has the lowest error (6.309 against 6.352 for S1), which also agrees with the CRPS.
  • S3-rw's gain over S3 on real event rows is not shown to be a real effect. An audit found that 41 of 93 event-days favour S3-rw, that 91% of the gain comes from 2026-01, and that 91% comes from one Primary. The random neighbours are degree-matched (each Primary keeps its number of neighbours), were drawn once with seed 12345 and are the same for every fold and seed, and they overlap the real neighbours for 8 of 16 Primaries. The overlap is a mild weakness of the control.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 5 fired twice. S1 is nested inside S2 and S3 and beats both on clean rows, and the control S3-rw beats S3 on real event rows by more than the half-width of the interval. Trigger 2 fired, because P1 and P2 failed (see below) and no explanation of the failure has been tested. A fresh Sonnet agent computed and audited the score tables, and a fresh reviewer re-derived the headline CRPS of S1, S2, S3, S3-rw, and R-inj from the stored forecasts, and the numbers matched. No reviewer re-derived the H-lvl numbers (Tables 1, 2, and 4, and the H-lvl section), which were not audited separately. The leave-one-Primary-out check of trigger 4 was not run for the other contrasts.
  • Predictions against outcomes. P1 failed (S2 minus S1 is +0.023 on clean rows against a predicted -0.06 to 0.00, and +0.026 on injected harm rows against -0.15 to -0.02). P2 failed on injected harm rows (+0.007 against -0.15 to 0.00) and held on real harm rows (-0.006 against -0.20 to +0.05). P3 held (-0.016 against -0.12 to -0.01). P4 held (+0.021 against +-0.04). P5 held (equal shares). P6 failed on clean rows, where the MVA-only eight show W1 -0.030 and the signed-MW six +0.023.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Arms and rows. S2 (S1 plus 24 window statistics), S3 (S2 plus 30 neighbour columns), and S3-rw (S3 with random neighbours that keep each Primary's degree). All three use experiment 428's rows, injected worlds, training loop, and experiment 404's frozen cross-fitted lagless tables. S1 and R-inj are experiment 428's stored forecasts. H-lvl is experiment 428's arm, refitted into this experiment's folder with 428's code. Experiment 438's oracle control failed, so it supplies no ceiling for these arms; see experiment 438.
  • Statistics. Per lag: the mean, signed sum, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, the counts above the 95% and below the 5% lagless quantile, and a triangular-tent mean of the surprise in a window of 12 hours either side of the lag, cut at the newest usable reading. Neighbour columns are capacity-weighted means of the same statistics, the lag's surprise minus the weighted neighbour surprise, and the weighted sign agreement. The neighbour graph is from experiment 383.
  • Sweep approximation. A step shifts the window's mean, sum, minimum, maximum, and tent by the step. The standard deviation and the two counts do not move under the step, because prefix sums cannot update them, so the sweep leaves three of the eight window inputs unchanged. The protocol is experiment 392's.
  • Seeds and folds. Three seeds and four test months. The MDE comes from R-inj's seed spread over three seeds, so it is itself uncertain.
  • Unlogged events. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), the distribution network operator, says some load-shift events are missing from its logs. Clean rows can therefore hold events no label covers, and the real-event rows may undercount events.
  • Step count of H-lvl. H-lvl keeps experiment 428's convolutional training settings, which take more optimiser steps per epoch than R-inj, so H1 and H2 mix the level offset with the step count.
  • Forecast horizon. The stored forecasts reach 10 days (240 hours), the horizon NGED cares about, and the lead figure covers all 10 days.
  • Sweep scope. The sweep covers seed 0 only, for R-inj, S1, S2, S3, and S3-rw. H-lvl was not swept.
  • H-lvl timing. H-lvl was added after the 36 window-arm fits and before any H-lvl score was read. Its numbers are not separately audited.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Later lag experiments can take S1 as the base, because S2 and S3 add inputs without lowering the error.
  • A question that remains open is whether a neighbour-aware design helps on events that really move load between neighbouring Primaries. The real event rows are too few and too concentrated in one test month and one Primary to answer it with these arms.

docs.title: Plan, as registered before any fit
docs.text: The plan below is kept as written. The section on arm H-lvl at the end was added after the 36 window-arm fits and before any H-lvl score was read.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
The signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight are the two groups of Primary substations, split by metering. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. A Primary's neighbours are the Primaries that share a supply route with it, from the adjacency file of experiment 383.

Experiment 428 gave the lag network the surprise at each lag, and the maintainer asks whether the surprise is better read in a window and against the neighbours. A load-conserving load-shift event shows an opposite shift at the neighbours, so the lag should be ignored. A genuine level shift shows no mirror, so a large surprise should raise the lag's weight. A gate that can only down-weight a surprising lag cannot express this, so these arms feed the features to the network as plain inputs and let the network learn either direction. The window statistics are experiment 404's (copied, with credit).

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Arms. S2 (S1 plus 24 window statistics), S3 (S2 plus 30 neighbour columns), S3-rw (S3 with random neighbours keeping each Primary's degree). All three use experiment 428's rows, injected worlds, training loop, and the frozen cross-fitted lagless tables of experiment 404.
  • Statistics. Per lag: the mean, signed sum, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, counts above the 95% and below the 5% lagless quantile, and a triangular-tent mean of the surprise in a window of 12 hours either side of the lag, cut at the newest usable reading. Experiment 404's median is omitted (prefix sums cannot give it). Neighbour columns are capacity-weighted means of the same statistics, the lag's surprise minus the weighted neighbour surprise, and the weighted sign agreement.
  • Sweep. Prediction only, on the saved networks, stepping the same lags (k = 1, 2, 3) in every arm including R-inj and S1, with the masked-lag control. A step shifts the window's mean, sum, minimum, maximum, and tent by the step and leaves the standard deviation and counts unchanged (an approximation).
  • Compute. 36 fits (3 arms, 4 folds, 3 seeds), about 6 to 10 graphics-processing-unit hours, one process under 8 GB (a one-epoch timing used 2.9 GB). Twelve more only if the attention version runs.
  • Reported. Absolute CRPS beside every contrast, tails, the real event count, and example forecasts and labelled-event plots.

docs.title: Arm H-lvl and its criteria (registered after the 36 fits, before any H-lvl score)
docs.text: H-lvl is experiment 428's S1 lag network plus one learned level offset per forecast origin, and the arm joined this experiment after the 36 window-arm fits. The offset fades with the lead at a learned rate, and a four-way soft regime vector joins the head. Experiment 428's code, rows, worlds, and training loop are used unchanged, and the 12 fits (4 folds, 3 seeds) took 28 to 63 minutes each. The criteria come from the brief recent_history_encoder_brief, aim (a): H-lvl passes only if H-lvl minus R-inj on clean rows at leads of 12 to 36 hours is at most -0.03 CRPS points, and the learned level moves the right way in at least 7 of 10 real events. Two contrasts are added: H1 (H-lvl minus R-inj) and H2 (H-lvl minus S1), on the same row sets as W1 to W5. The level-trace diagnostic for the second condition is run only if the first condition holds.

docs.title: Do the input bundles of experiment 437 lower the neural network's error on cold winter nights, cold sunny days, Christmas, and heat waves, without raising it elsewhere?
docs.text: Take-home message (here a bundle is a set of extra input columns added to the neural network of experiment 437, and "points" are percentage points of a Primary substation's effective capacity): the bundles did not help on the difficult rows either, but four test months cannot show a gain smaller than 0.12 to 0.26 points on these slices, so this is inconclusive, not a finding of no effect. Thermal lag was the only one of the eight arms that looked better on cold winter nights at both groups, and the signed-MW part of that gain came from two Primaries. The clearer lesson is about tails: on cold winter nights the signed-MW Primaries' upper quantiles are badly under-covering.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, a single error number for a probabilistic forecast. The signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight are the two groups of Primary substations by metering.

This re-score asks whether the input bundles that did not help on average help on the rows NGED cares about most. Experiment 437 added eight bundles of extra input columns to the pooled neural network and judged them on the annual mean. The maintainer expects thermal-lag columns and similar bundles to help mostly in winter, so a gain on cold winter nights, Christmas, or heat waves would be averaged away. No network is refitted: the stored forecasts of experiment 437 are scored again on slices of difficult rows.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Forecasts. The eight arms of experiment 437 (T, S, C, C_tariff, F, T_pre, S_pre, F_pre) and controls R and A, four folds, three seeds, loaded by e00437_score.load_frames. Experiment 437 folder is imported; nothing in it is edited.
  • Slices. Each is defined from the ENS-mean 2 m temperature and clear-sky index of the forecast's own run, from solar elevation, and from the calendar, per Primary. Thresholds that are percentiles come from the 730 days of runs before each fold's refit (runs exist from 2024-04-01, so the first fold's window is 18 months).
    • Cold winter nights. Elevation below 0, local month November to March, ENS-mean temperature at or below the Primary's 10th percentile of winter-night ENS temperatures in the window.
    • Cold sunny days and cold overcast days. Daily-mean ENS temperature below 5 °C; sunny if the daily-mean clear-sky index is at least 0.7, overcast if at most 0.3. Daylight half-hours only.
    • Christmas and other bank holidays. 24 December to 2 January; and Good Friday to Easter Monday and the May and August bank holidays of England and Wales.
    • Heat-wave days. Daily-maximum ENS temperature at or above the Primary's 95th percentile of June to August daily maxima, on at least 2 consecutive days of the same run.
  • Counts before scoring (from work/pre_output.txt, days are distinct local valid dates, rows are scored half-hours at days 1 to 10 summed over the folds and Primaries):
Slice Signed-MW six MVA-only eight Folds with rows Cold winter nights 11,793 rows, 21 days 16,958 rows, 28 days 3 Cold sunny days 7,005 rows, 24 days 8,340 rows, 19 days 3 Cold overcast days 971 rows, 6 days 1,011 rows, 5 days 1 (2026-01) Christmas 23,040 rows, 10 days 30,720 rows, 10 days 2 Other bank holidays 5,664 rows, 4 days 7,552 rows, 4 days 1 (2026-03) Heat-wave days 0 0 0
  • Minimum detectable effect, from the seed spread, before any arm is scored (7-day valid-date blocks; control R or A; six or eight):
Slice R, six R, eight A, six A, eight Cold winter nights 0.23 0.16 0.21 0.12 Cold sunny days 0.19 0.18 0.13 0.26

Every cell is above the 0.05 bar, so no slice can detect a gain of 0.05: an arm meets the decision rule only if its gain is several times the bar. A failure to meet it is not evidence of no effect. The same figures over folds are smaller (0.02 to 0.16) but rest on three folds. - Standing practices. Monthly refits (stored); cleaned data (flagged exact zeros dropped, 1,179 half-hours in the scored set); the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01; stored controls reused and no fit; tails reported. The four-fold screen labels every number interim. - Figures. Per slice, a gain-with-interval chart for every arm; example winter-night week of forecast, actual, control, and best arm; the sunny-minus-overcast gap of S and S_pre; a day-ahead and a 14-day example forecast. - Reviews. Draft pull request; fresh Sonnet code review before the arms are scored (it found that the protocol's own christmas column overrode the registered mask, now fixed, which moved the Christmas count from 9 to 10 dates; the six tested cells were unaffected); results review with the audit triggers; write-up; prose review.

docs.title: Caveats registered before scoring
docs.text:
• The folds hold no summer month, so heat waves cannot be scored at all.
  • Christmas, other bank holidays, and cold overcast days have 10 dates or fewer and one or two folds, so they are descriptive.
  • Winter nights come mostly from two folds (2025-12 and 2026-01), with 3 dates in 2026-03.
  • The first fold's percentile window is 18 months, not 24, because ENS runs are stored from 2024-04-01.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS differences are arm minus control in points of capacity at days 1 to 10 (negative is better), pooled over rows. The all-rows contrasts reproduce experiment 437's table exactly (gate in work/score_output.txt). Every number is interim.

No tested cell advanced. Of the 10 tested cells, the gain bar of -0.05 was met only by T at the signed-MW six (-0.059) and at the MVA-only eight (-0.099). Both cells fail the interval condition (the interval includes zero) and the fold condition (2 of 3 folds negative).

  • Cold winter nights (21 dates at the six, 28 at the eight; folds 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03). T: -0.059 (-0.185 to +0.062) at the six and -0.099 (-0.124 to +0.088) at the eight. T_pre: +0.242 and -0.043. F: +0.049 and -0.027. F_pre: +0.044 and +0.007. Intervals are 99.5%, month blocks (3 blocks, so the interval is the range of three fold values).
  • Cold sunny days (24 dates at the six). S: +0.287 (-0.238 to +0.362), S_pre: +0.201 (-0.457 to +0.408). Solar gain did not help on cold sunny days; the S arm was worse in 2 of 3 folds.
  • Sunny minus overcast. S: +0.41 (-0.23 to +0.76) at the six and +0.23 (-0.10 to +0.42) at the eight. Overcast days exist in one fold (6 dates), so the gap is descriptive and its sign (S helped on overcast days, not on sunny days) is the opposite of the solar-gain hypothesis.
  • Christmas (10 dates, two folds, descriptive). T at the eight: -0.28 (-0.31 to -0.22, 7-day blocks); F at the six: +0.34. These intervals cover one run's weeks, not other refits.
  • Other bank holidays (4 dates, one fold) and cold overcast days (6 dates): descriptive; see work/figure_tables/contrasts.parquet.
  • Heat waves. No rows, because no screen fold holds a summer month.
  • Harm elsewhere. Outside the two primary slices every arm stays within +0.061 of its control (point estimates); no arm's q95 or q99 pinball loss rose by more than +0.027 outside the slice.

docs.title: Tails and absolute skill
docs.text:
• Signed-MW tails fail on cold winter nights. R covers 75.6% at q95 and 82.9% at q99 on those half-hours (95% and 99% nominal), against 88.6% and 95.5% over all rows. A covers 76.6% and 84.7%. At the MVA-only eight, R covers 93.2% and 99.2%, and A 93.9% and 99.4%.
  • Absolute skill on cold winter nights (CRPS, A, R, BG2, manual_heuristic, climatology): signed-MW six 5.84, 6.34, 6.46, 9.39, 9.08; MVA-only eight 3.14, 3.39, 3.78, 5.90, 5.90. The neural network beats the weekly XGBoost model (BG2) and both naive baselines on these rows at both groups.

docs.title: Example forecasts
docs.text: The week figures stitch day-ahead forecasts (24 to 48 hours ahead) and compare the control with the arm that scored best on cold winter nights at that group. The signed-MW Primary is not named.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (T lowers cold-night CRPS by 0.05 to 0.30 at the eight, -0.20 to +0.10 at the six) is partly supported. T fits both ranges (-0.099, -0.059); T_pre misses both (-0.043, +0.242).
  • P2 (S lowers cold-sunny-day CRPS by 0.00 to 0.20 at the six) is not supported. S +0.287, S_pre +0.201.
  • P3 (F within +-0.10 on cold nights) is supported in all four cells.
  • P4 (outside every primary slice within +-0.06) is supported except one cell at +0.061 (C outside cold sunny days at the six).
  • P5 (no slice detects 0.05) is supported.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast: not available; the networks store quantiles only.
  • Error of the median beside each CRPS contrast: same sign in all primary cells except S at the eight on cold winter nights (CRPS -0.014, median error +0.025; descriptive).
  • Triggers fired: the leave-one-Primary-out trigger (trigger 4) for T on cold winter nights at the six: dropping Primary D14 or D16 flips the sign (-0.059 to +0.039 or +0.123), and dropping Primary D10 takes it under the bar. The gain rests on Primaries D16 and D14, while D5 pulls the other way. T_pre at the eight meets the bar if Primary D4 or D8 is dropped, and its sign never flips. No verdict changes. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the six headline cells and the masks of two Primaries from the stored forecasts and ENS tables, and all matched to 5 decimals.
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet reviewer found that the protocol's own christmas column overrode the registered mask, so the first Christmas counts were wrong (9 dates, not 10). It was fixed before any arm was scored; the six tested cells were unaffected.
  • Dropped half-hours: 1,179 flagged exact-zero half-hours are excluded from the scored set (as in experiment 437).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Three blocks make the interval degenerate. With 3 month blocks the 99.5% interval is the range of the three fold values, so condition 2 reduces to "all three folds negative" and conditions 2 and 3 are not independent.
  • The slices are thin. Cold winter nights come mostly from 2025-12 and 2026-01; 2026-03 holds 3 dates. The first fold's percentile window is 18 months.
  • Slice masks are ENS-mean based, so a night the ensemble mean calls cold may not be cold; ENS smoothing leaves few overcast days (6 dates).
  • Absolute table weights Primaries equally, while the contrasts pool rows, so differences in the absolute table need not equal the contrasts on thin slices.
  • Interval widths (7-day blocks) on Christmas and bank holidays describe one run's weeks only.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Recalibrate cold-night tails at the signed-MW six (widen or condition the uncertainty on a cold-night flag), since the coverage gap is far larger than any bundle's gain.
  • Retest thermal lag (T) on many more winter months, the only one of the eight arms that looked better on both groups.

docs.title: Data used and where it lives
docs.text:
• Data. Experiment 437's stored forecasts (arms and controls, 4 folds, seeds 0 to 2), experiment 425's controls, and the stored ENS summaries; no new data.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00441-difficult-row-rescore-of-the-neural-demand-input-bundles/; it imports experiments 87, 377, 381, 396, 397, 407, 418, 425, and 437.
  • Tables and logs. $DATA_PATH_INTERNAL/ml-experiments/00441-difficult-row-rescore-of-the-neural-demand-input-bundles/work/ (pre_output.txt, score_output.txt, figure_tables/, masks.parquet).

docs.title: Does the thermal-lag bundle lower the pooled neural network's error on cold winter nights, on six winter-weighted monthly folds?
docs.text: Take-home message: adding thermal-lag columns (bundle T) to the pooled neural network (control R) did not lower its error on cold winter nights by an amount six monthly folds can detect. The gain that experiment 441 saw at the eight MVA-only Primary substations did not appear in the two new winter months. The error measure is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of capacity, and a negative difference is a gain. Pooled over five folds, T minus R on cold winter nights was -0.086 at the six signed-MW Primary substations and -0.014 at the eight MVA-only ones. Both intervals include zero. The minimum detectable effect (0.15 to 0.19) is three to four times the 0.05 bar. All numbers are interim.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
CRPS is a single error number for a probabilistic forecast. The signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight are the two groups of Primary substations by metering.

This experiment asks whether thermal-lag columns help the pooled neural network on cold winter nights. Experiment 441 found a gain of at least 0.05 points there, but its intervals included zero. The scored year holds five winter months (November to March); experiment 437 fitted three of them and October. This experiment fits bundle T on the other two winter months, November 2025 and February 2026, so that the cold-night slice rests on five folds.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The registered rule was not met at either group. Adding two winter folds moved the pooled gain at the MVA-only eight from the 0.05 or more of experiment 441 to 0.014. At the signed-MW six, the gain stayed at 0.086, and one fold (February 2026, +0.205) contradicts it. T is experiment 437's thermal-lag neural network, and R is its control.

  • Primary contrast, T minus R on cold winter nights (CRPS, points of capacity, days 1 to 10, widened by 1.15, seeds 0 to 4, 97.5% month-block interval; 16,185 half-hours on 35 dates at the six, 22,459 on 42 dates at the eight):

    Group Difference Interval Folds negative Tail pinball q95, q99 Reading Signed-MW six -0.086 -0.241 to +0.141 4 of 5 -0.195, -0.160 does not advance MVA-only eight -0.014 -0.102 to +0.138 3 of 5 -0.007, +0.002 does not advance

  • Conditions that failed. At the signed-MW six, two conditions failed: the interval is not wholly below zero, and the upper end outside the slice is +0.033 against the allowed +0.02. At the MVA-only eight, four failed: the gain is below 0.05, the interval is not below zero, only 3 of 5 folds are negative, and the upper end outside the slice is +0.080.

  • Fold by fold at the six: 2025-11 -0.059, 2025-12 -0.017, 2026-01 -0.256, 2026-02 +0.205, 2026-03 -0.165. At the eight: 2025-11 +0.116, 2025-12 -0.125, 2026-01 -0.014, 2026-02 +0.146, 2026-03 -0.019. The two new folds (November and February) are worse at the eight. February is also worse at the six.
  • Rows outside the cold winter nights. T minus R on all rows was -0.004 (-0.034 to +0.021) at the six and +0.013 (-0.034 to +0.081) at the eight. At the eight, November 2025 alone is +0.159 on all rows, so part of the eight's fold spread is not specific to cold nights.
  • Absolute CRPS (equal weight over Primaries): on cold winter nights R scores 5.137 and T 5.034 at the six, R 3.150 and T 3.135 at the eight. On all rows R scores 3.245 and T 3.242 at the six, R 3.841 and T 3.854 at the eight. References on cold winter nights, six and eight: the monthly XGBoost recipe 5.779 and 3.646, BG2 (the best-guess forecast of experiment 87) 5.318 and 3.561, manual_heuristic 7.963 and 5.442, climatology 7.911 and 5.621.
  • Tails on cold winter nights, six: coverage at q95 rises from 0.820 (R) to 0.829 (T) and at q99 from 0.877 to 0.895; pinball loss at q95 falls from 2.067 to 1.850 and at q99 from 1.226 to 1.046. Eight: coverage at q95 0.948 to 0.960, at q99 0.994 to 0.997; pinball loss at q95 0.717 to 0.709, at q99 0.187 to 0.189. Both networks undercover the tails at the six on these nights (q99 coverage 0.88 to 0.90).
  • Descriptive slices (not tested by the rule): cold sunny days +0.003 (six) and +0.023 (eight); cold overcast days -0.073 and -0.104 (3 folds, 12 and 10 dates); Christmas +0.120 and -0.268 (2 folds, 10 dates); other bank holidays +0.032 and +0.048 (1 fold, 4 dates). Christmas at the eight is the largest gain in the table but rests on 10 dates in two folds.
  • D15 and D18 (report only): all rows -0.014 (-0.326 to +0.108); cold winter nights -0.170 (-0.532 to +0.355).
  • Predictions. P1 (a gain of 0.05 to 0.30 at the eight) failed: -0.014. P1 at the six (-0.30 to +0.10) held: -0.086. P2 (within +-0.04 outside the slice) held at both groups. P3 (minimum detectable effect above 0.05) held.
  • Data. 1,179 flagged exact-zero half-hours were dropped from the scoring actuals; D15 and D18 start at 2025-03-01.
  • Gate. The four-fold, seeds 0 to 2 contrast of T minus R on all rows reproduced experiment 437's published +0.016 (six) and -0.022 (eight).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• A fresh Sonnet reviewer re-derived the headline from the raw seed files (their own seed averaging, widening, and CRPS from the 11 quantiles) and reproduced every contrast and fold value to 3 decimals. Pooling is by row; the equal-weight mean over folds is -0.058 at the six and +0.021 at the eight, so the sign at the eight depends on the weighting.
  • Audit triggers fired: three of the seven listed in the ml-experiment skill's "Audit before merge".
    • A registered prediction failed (P1 at the eight).
    • The sign of the CRPS contrast differs from the sign of the mean and median error. At the eight on cold winter nights CRPS is -0.014, but the absolute error of the mean forecast is +0.044 and of the median forecast +0.017. At the six all three agree (CRPS -0.086, mean -0.041, median -0.012). On all rows at the eight, CRPS +0.013, mean +0.036, and median +0.043 agree.
    • Leaving out one Primary flips a sign. At the six on cold winter nights, D16 alone is -0.996; dropping it turns -0.086 into +0.070, and dropping D5 (+0.448) gives -0.186. The six Primaries' own values are D10 -0.113, D11 +0.067, D14 -0.118, D16 -0.996, D5 +0.448, D9 +0.095. At the eight, dropping D19, D8, or D22 moves -0.014 to between 0.000 and +0.008, and D12 (+0.31) and D4 (+0.14) are the worst Primaries.
  • The gain at the signed-MW six depends mainly on one Primary substation (D16), so the result is not evidence of a gain at that group.
  • Median minus mean forecast per Primary on cold winter nights is within +-0.5 points of capacity at almost every Primary for both networks. The exceptions are D12 (-0.91 for R, -0.98 for T), D8 (+0.94, +0.68), and the report-only D15 (-2.04, -3.13).
  • Tails per fold. At the six, the q95 and q99 pinball losses are lower for T in all 5 folds, including February 2026 where CRPS is +0.205. At the eight, q95 and q99 are higher for T in 3 of 5 folds.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Six folds, not eight, and the folds are not independent of experiment 441: three of the five cold-night folds were seen there. The two new folds alone are the November and February values above.
  • The cold-night slice rests on very few days in March (3 dates) and none in October.
  • The minimum detectable effect is above the bar (0.19 and 0.15 over blocks; 0.063 and 0.090 over folds), so a failure to meet the rule is not evidence of no effect.
  • The in-slice interval resamples 5 months and is nearly all-or-nothing.
  • The hyperparameters were tuned at 46 inputs and reused at 54, as in experiment 437.
  • Seeds come from two experiments. T seeds 0 to 2 on four folds come from experiment 437. Seeds 3 and 4 on those folds, and all five seeds on the new folds, were fitted here.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Leave thermal lags out of the pooled plain neural network unless a test with at least 10 winter months and an interval narrow enough to resolve 0.05 becomes possible.

docs.title: Data used and where it lives
docs.text:
• Data. The cleaned NGED Primary-substation power series and the ECMWF ensemble forecasts.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00442-thermal-lag-cold-night-test-on-six-winter-folds/; it imports experiments 11, 48, 87, 377, 381, 396, 397, 407, 418, 425, and 437, and its masks, scorer, and figures are copied from experiment 441.
  • Saved networks and forecasts. $DATA_PATH_INTERNAL/ml-experiments/00442-thermal-lag-cold-night-test-on-six-winter-folds/work/.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Arms. T (experiment 437's thermal-lag bundle, ensemble-only form; T_pre is skipped because it was worse) and the control R.
  • Base network: R, not S1 and not the brief's "R-inj". The S1 confirmation (experiment 439) is still a plan, so S1 has not passed. The brief names "R-inj" as the reference, but experiment 428's R-inj is the lagged network trained on injected load-shift worlds, which bundle T was never tested on. The contrast that experiments 437 and 441 measured is T minus R, so the contrast here is the same.
  • Folds: six, not eight. The brief asked for two further winter months before 2025-07 (January and February 2025). They cannot be scored: the 51-member demand frames, the forecast origins, the stored references (BG2, manual_heuristic, climatology, the XGBoost recipe), and the protocol rows all cover only 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30, so a 2025 fold would need those rebuilt first, and its training window (stored runs start on 2024-04-01) would be 9 to 10 months against the 18 to 24 of the other folds. The six folds are 2025-10, 2025-11, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-02, and 2026-03; October holds no cold winter nights.
  • Reuse and fits. The control R is stored by experiment 425 for every month with seeds 0 to 4, so it is not refitted. T is stored by experiment 437 for four folds with seeds 0 to 2. New fits: T on 2025-11 and 2026-02 with seeds 0 to 4 (10 fits) and T on the four old folds with seeds 3 and 4 (8 fits), 18 fits of about 75 seconds each, under 1 GPU-hour. One GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The fits wait for a free slot from the manager.
  • Slices. The masks of experiment 441 (copied, because its pull request is not merged): cold winter nights (primary), cold sunny days, cold overcast days, Christmas, and other bank holidays; heat waves cannot be scored. Row and day counts per slice and fold are printed before scoring.
  • Standing practices. Monthly refits (stored neural networks); cleaned data (flagged exact zeros dropped, count per fold printed); the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01; tails reported; every number labelled interim.
  • Figures. Gain-with-interval chart for T on each slice; fold-by-fold table; example winter night week (forecast, actual, R, T); a day-ahead and a 14-day example forecast.
  • Reviews. Draft pull request; plan review (fresh Sonnet); code review (fresh Sonnet) before the first fit; results review with the audit triggers; write-up review; prose review.

docs.title: Counts and minimum detectable effect, printed before T was scored
docs.text:
The scorer's pre stage read only the control R (stored seeds 0 to 2 against seeds 3 and 4).

  • The pooled cold-winter-night slice is large enough to decide on but not to detect 0.05. It holds 16,185 scored half-hours on 35 local dates at the signed-MW six, and 22,459 half-hours on 42 dates at the MVA-only eight. Both groups have rows in five folds: 2025-11 (7 dates at each group), 2025-12 (13), 2026-01 (15 at the six, 22 at the eight), 2026-02 (7), and 2026-03 (3). October 2025 has none.
  • The minimum detectable effect of the pooled cold-night slice exceeds 0.05 at both groups. Over 7-day valid-date blocks it is 0.19 at the six (15 blocks) and 0.15 at the eight (16 blocks). Over the five folds it is 0.063 at the six and 0.090 at the eight. A gain of 0.05 can therefore meet the decision rule only if the interval is unusually narrow, and a failure to meet it is not evidence of no effect. The write-up reports the interval whatever the rule's reading.
  • Cold sunny days hold 40 dates at the six and 35 at the eight (minimum detectable effect 0.20 and 0.29 over blocks); cold overcast days 12 and 10 dates; Christmas 10 dates in two folds; other bank holidays 4 dates in one fold. The last three are descriptive.

docs.title: Caveats registered before the fits
docs.text:
• Six folds, not eight, for the reason above; the sign rule is scaled from 6 of 8 to 4 of 5.
  • Two of the five cold-night folds are new, three were seen in experiment 441, so the pooled result is not an independent replication. The new folds alone are reported beside the pooled result.
  • Seeds 3 and 4 of T on the old folds are fitted after experiment 441's result was read. They fix the number of seeds, not the design.
  • The in-slice month-block interval is nearly all-or-nothing. It resamples 5 origin months, so an upper end below zero needs almost every fold to be negative, which is stricter than the "4 of 5" condition.
  • The mask thresholds use runs up to the refit, whose later valid times pass it. Only ECMWF ensemble (ENS) weather enters the thresholds, never a score or an actual, and experiment 441 used the same window.

docs.title: Does changing any one setting of the neural network for the six metered solar farms improve its quantile score by 0.5%?
docs.text:
Changing any one setting of the neural network that forecasts solar output did not improve its forecast by the 0.5% margin we required. One neural network is trained on all six metered solar farms at once (labelled A to F). For each half-hour it outputs a probability distribution of the farm's output, as a fraction of the farm's capacity, from the 51-member ensemble weather forecast of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Experiment 430 found that adding inputs or components to this network improved its score by 0.4% at most (a clear-sky column). We therefore left the design alone and changed 25 settings one at a time, comparing each against the unchanged network (the "reference network") on the quantile score, which measures how well the whole distribution matches the observed output (lower is better). The settings were the network's width, depth, farm embedding (a learned vector per farm), learning rate, weight decay, number of training epochs, number of Gaussian curves in the output distribution, dropout, and a weight that favours recent training rows. No change passed, so the random search that the plan reserved for a positive result was not run.

The best change, a learning rate of 4e-3, shrank from 0.47% to 0.14% on fresh seeds, and both intervals span zero. The learning rate of 4e-3 scored 0.47% better on the three screening seeds (a seed fixes the starting weights and the batch order) (99% interval −1.41% to +0.08%), and 0.14% better on three fresh seeds (−0.74% to +0.55%). The fresh-seed check was run after the results were read (post hoc), on this one arm. The minimum detectable effect from seed noise is 0.40% at three seeds, so a screening gain of 0.47% is barely above the seed noise. One mixture component is the only clear change, and it is worse: 3.15% worse (+1.43% to +5.52%), with a 0.99 pinball loss (the loss at the quantile that 99% of outcomes fall below) 0.077 points higher.

Figure 1. Percentage change in the farm-equal quantile score of each arm against experiment 430's g0_onepass, over all day bands, three seeds, with 99% month-block intervals. Negative is better. The dashed lines mark 0 and the −0.5% margin.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are quantile scores in points of capacity (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 levels; lower is better), farm-equal means over experiment 430's scored year (2025-09 to 2026-08), 410,899 rows, all day bands, seeds 0 to 2 for every arm and for the skeleton. The "skeleton" (the reference network) is experiment 430's g0_onepass, read from its stored predictions. The 0.01 and 0.99 pinball losses are row-pooled differences in points of capacity.
