Removing the Primary embedding raises CRPS by 0.649 (0.597 to 0.702) at the six and 0.741 (0.689 to 0.798) at the eight. Removing the surprise inputs raises it by 0.033 (0.026 to 0.040) and 0.027 (0.017 to 0.037). Removing B-mix lowers CRPS by 0.059 and 0.096, and removing pretraining lowers it by 0.059 and 0.047.

docs.title: Pretraining
docs.text:
• Pretraining S1 with every recent-power input masked raises CRPS. C1 is above zero, so no interval lies below -0.03. Plan predictions P1 (pretraining helps) and P4 (the assembly beats the five-seed pool) failed. At the eight, C1 changes sign between folds (lower CRPS in 2 of 4 folds, higher in 2 of 4), and the within-fold interval hides that. At the six, 3 of 4 folds are higher and the fourth is lower by 0.002.
  • The same pretraining helps the lagless network. F1 and F4 are negative at the six and eight: pretraining lowered the CRPS of L0 by 0.073 and 0.138. Experiment 425 found 0.050 and 0.124 for its network on its own rows. L0 has no lag inputs, so masking removes nothing from its pretraining rows. The leading suspect for the failure in S1 is therefore masking the lag inputs in pretraining and then switching them on in fine-tuning.
  • Experiment 425 pretrained on real lagged power and gained. Its network takes three origin lags, and its pretraining rows carry real lagged power from 2019 onwards. Rescored on this experiment's clean rows, which match its own rows exactly, pretraining lowered CRPS by 0.044 at the six and 0.107 at the eight, against +0.053 and +0.047 here. Experiment 449 (pull request 107) tests real lagged power in the pretraining rows of S1. That test has not been run on this page.

docs.title: Other components
docs.text:
• B-mix raised clean-row CRPS above the +0.03 cap at both groups, so it stays a named option. On real harm rows its q99 pinball loss is lower than S1's at the six (0.255 against 0.278) and higher at the eight (0.367 against 0.347), without intervals. At D15 and D18 it lowers real-event CRPS.
  • The five-seed pool advances, and beats every single seed at both groups. C3 is below zero. At the six the pool scores 2.809 against 2.842 to 2.875 for single seeds, and at the eight 3.506 against 3.539 to 3.591. The pool beats each seed over the four folds pooled and beats the seed mean in every fold. Single seeds win some folds: in 4 of the 8 group-by-fold cells a seed scores lower than the pool, by up to 0.014. This supports the minimum-detectable-effect caveat below.
  • The five-seed pool gains more than the three-seed pool, as expected if the gain comes from averaging away seed variance. Against the same S1 seeds 0 to 2, the three-seed pool gains 0.041 and 0.044 (C3b) and the five-seed pool gains 0.056 and 0.056. The C3 row compares the five-seed pool with all five S1 seeds and gains 0.048 and 0.056. The production cost of the pool is five fitted networks per refit and five forward passes per row. Of the 20 S1 fits of the screen, 12 stopped at the 60-epoch cap, so single S1 fits may be under-trained, and the pool's gain may partly make up for that.
  • Width 256 fails rule (a) at the six and rule (b) at the eight, although it had the lowest clean CRPS of any arm. S1-w256-pool5 scored 2.7929 at the six and 3.4722 at the eight, below the pool's 2.809 and 3.506. Rule (a) asks for the clean gain to hold on the four screen folds at both groups. C5 held in 3 of 4 folds at the six and 4 of 4 at the eight, and the gain at each group is under the minimum detectable effect. Rule (b) caps real-event CRPS at +0.03 and q99 pinball loss at +0.02 against S1. At the eight, real-event CRPS is +0.323 (0.215 to 0.426), so rule (b) fails. At the six, real-event CRPS is -0.200, and the q99 pinball loss is 0.025 lower. At the eight the q99 pinball loss is unchanged (0.449). F5 gives the same picture inside the pool: the gain is -0.016 and -0.034, and D15 and D18 are +0.396 worse. Width 256 also lowers upper-tail coverage at the six (q95 0.901 and q99 0.973, against 0.920 and 0.984 for S1). The variant does not advance.
  • The surprise inputs are worth 0.1 points in single unpretrained fits and 0.03 inside the pretrained pool. F2 and F3 give 0.100 and 0.088 (single fits) and 0.103 and 0.086 (pools of five seeds) at the six and eight, on rows and seeds shared with the leave-one-out arms. F3 equals F2, so pooling does not shrink the worth of the surprise inputs. The leave-one-out values of 0.033 and 0.027 compare a pretrained network with the surprise inputs against a pretrained network without them, and that pretrained network is itself 0.05 worse than S1. That the pretrained network causes the smaller worth is a hypothesis, which this experiment did not test. The comparison in experiments 428 and 439 (0.106 at the six) used seeds 3 to 5 only. Experiment 425's R, which has no surprise inputs, scores level with S1 (below), so the surprise gain may only make up for a weakness in the R-inj base.

docs.title: Against the references
docs.text:
• On the shared rows the five-seed pool is level with BG2 and ahead of the monthly XGBoost recipe at the six and the eight, and behind both at D15 and D18. The table covers days 1 to 10 on the 579,044 half-hours that every arm and reference shares. The monthly XGBoost recipe is unwidened.
Slice S1 Five-seed pool BG2 XGBoost monthly manual_heuristic climatology Signed-MW six 2.850 2.802 2.845 3.017 3.554 3.946 MVA-only eight 3.556 3.501 3.543 3.615 4.171 4.599 D15 and D18 9.160 8.952 7.687 8.879 12.088 22.740 Cold nights, six 2.801 2.722 2.405 2.814 4.820 5.159 Cold nights, eight 2.917 2.821 2.848 3.015 4.450 4.799

The pool leads BG2 by 0.043 at the six and 0.042 at the eight. Both differences are under the minimum detectable effect and have no interval. BG2 is better on cold nights at the six and at D15 and D18. Pooled over all 16 Primaries, BG2 leads on four folds (3.746 against 3.844), because of D15 and D18.

  • Experiment 425's pretrained network A ties the S1 pool at the six and beats it by 0.069 at the eight. The table scores experiment 425's networks on this experiment's clean rows (254,725 half-hours at the six and 389,812 at the eight, four folds, 1.15 widening; the rescoring is stored outside this folder, see Caveats).
Network Signed-MW six MVA-only eight Experiment 425 A (pretrained, mean of single seeds, no pool) 2.809 3.437 Experiment 425 R (not pretrained) 2.852 3.544 S1 five-seed pool 2.809 3.506 S1 (one fit) 2.857 3.562

Experiment 425's A has no pool and no surprise inputs. Its R is level with single S1. Experiment 425's recipe gains 0.044 and 0.107 from pretraining on these rows (the table's rounded entries differ from those by 0.001), where S1's masked-lag pretraining loses. The masked-lag recipe is the leading suspect for the difference (see Pretraining), because the folds and the rows are the same. Experiment 425's networks also lack surprise inputs, so a second difference exists.

  • With the fifth month, BG2 leads at the six and the pool leads at the eight, but the lead at the eight is under the minimum detectable effect. With 2025-12 (S1, its pool, and the references on the same 713,323 rows), CRPS at the six is 3.038 for S1, 2.949 for the five-seed pool, 2.856 for BG2, and 3.046 for XGBoost monthly. At the eight it is 3.602, 3.523, 3.563, and 3.654. The pool leads BG2 at the eight by 0.040 (3.523 against 3.563), which is under the four-fold minimum detectable effect of 0.056, so the two are not separated.

  • BG2's lead on five folds comes from the fifth fold, 2025-12, where the S1 pool is worse than experiment 425's A from 11 December onwards, and most so after 22 December. The figures are for the six, clean rows, 67,598 half-hours, by origin day, and come from a CPU rescoring stored outside this folder (see Caveats).

    • On 1 to 10 December the pool and A are close (2.8 to 3.4 against 2.7 to 3.3). From 11 to 14 December the pool scores 3.1 to 3.3 against 2.4 to 2.8 for A, and from 15 to 21 December 3.3 to 3.8 against 2.1 to 2.6.

    • For origin days 22 to 31 December the pool scores 4.10 and the five-seed average of A's quantiles 2.55. By valid-time day, 22 to 31 December, the scores are 3.86 and 2.10. The whole-December scores are 3.50 for the pool and 2.65 to 2.83 for single seeds of A.

    • The result is seed-dependent. Single S1 seeds score 3.39 to 4.29 over all of 2025-12, and seeds 0 and 4 (4.29 and 4.08) are much worse than the other three (3.39 to 3.49).

  • On five folds BG2 scores lower than the pool on cold nights and at D15 and D18, and XGBoost monthly beats the pool on cold nights at the six. At the six, BG2 scores 2.568 on cold nights, the pool 3.237, and XGBoost monthly 3.045. At D15 and D18 the pool (8.548) ties XGBoost monthly (8.551), and BG2 scores 7.380. At the eight on cold nights the pool scores 3.108 and BG2 3.080.

  • The pool lowers real-event CRPS at the six and the eight, and its q99 coverage on real events stays far below 0.99. Real-event CRPS is 7.049 against 7.142 for S1 at the eight and 5.569 against 5.689 at the six. The pool's q99 coverage at the six is 0.871 against 0.860 for S1, where the target is 0.99. NGED's logs may miss events, so clean rows may hold unlogged events and real-event rows undercount.

docs.title: Tails and widening
docs.text:
• The pool's lower quantiles cover far too little, so the lower band is too wide. On four folds, clean rows, days 1 to 10, the pool has coverage 0.0015, 0.0128, 0.925, and 0.987 at q01, q05, q95, and q99 at the six, and 0.0024, 0.0222, 0.946, and 0.989 at the eight. The nominal levels are 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99. S1 has 0.0018, 0.0140, 0.920, and 0.985 at the six. The 1.15 widening that was fitted for single S1 widens the lower band further.
  • On five folds the upper quantiles come closer to nominal. The pool has q95 coverage 0.932 and q99 coverage 0.989 at the six, and 0.949 and 0.990 at the eight. S1 has 0.925 and 0.987 at the six.
  • The pool's cold-night q99 pinball loss at the six is lower than BG2's and XGBoost monthly's. On the four folds it is 0.155 for the pool, 0.26 for BG2, and 0.39 for XGBoost monthly. On five folds it is 0.161 for the pool and 0.242 for BG2.
  • Figure 4 differs from these coverages in the third decimal. The figures in this section are averages over all clean rows (254,725 at the six, 389,812 at the eight), and for single-seed S1 they average the five seeds' coverages. Figure 4 uses the half-hours shared with the references (204,529 and 311,777) and the seed-mean quantile forecast for single-seed arms.
  • A widening factor of 1.10 at the six and 1.05 at the eight scores best for the pool, within 0.014 of the 1.15 score. The sweep covers clean rows on four folds, and the raw forecast is factor 1.00.
Group and arm Factor CRPS q01 q05 q95 q99 Six, S1 pool 1.00 2.813 0.0042 0.0238 0.890 0.971 Six, S1 pool 1.10 2.806 0.0022 0.0158 0.915 0.983 Six, S1 pool 1.15 2.809 0.0015 0.0128 0.925 0.987 Eight, S1 pool 1.00 3.493 0.0069 0.0411 0.920 0.979 Eight, S1 pool 1.05 3.492 0.0048 0.0339 0.929 0.983 Eight, S1 pool 1.15 3.506 0.0024 0.0222 0.946 0.989 Six, S1 1.00 2.871 0.0049 0.0253 0.885 0.967 Six, S1 1.15 2.857 0.0018 0.0140 0.920 0.985 Eight, S1 1.00 3.560 0.0078 0.0438 0.916 0.976 Eight, S1 1.15 3.562 0.0028 0.0244 0.943 0.988

The 1.15 widening was fitted for single S1, and the pool already widens the mixture. The 1.15 factor lifts the upper tail towards 0.95 and pushes the lower tail further from its nominal level. The pool's lowest CRPS is 2.806 at a factor of 1.10 at the six and 3.492 at 1.05 at the eight. - The mean forecast sits above the median forecast. The stored column is the median minus the mean forecast, which is negative where the mean sits above the median. For S1 it is -0.28 points at the six, -0.41 at the eight, and -1.79 at D15 and D18. Per Primary the S1 gap runs from -3.19 to +0.02 points. These checks use raw quantiles, clean rows with a finite actual, days 1 to 10, seeds 0 to 4, and four folds. - The 11-quantile approximation of the mean forecast is accurate to 0.005 points on average. It was validated once against the exact mixture mean of S1 seed 0 on one month: approximate minus exact mean -0.001 points, mean absolute 0.005, 99th percentile 0.032. - The mean forecast has about the same absolute error as the median forecast. Its bias (forecast minus actual) is -1.74, -0.74, and -8.02 points at the six, the eight, and D15 and D18. Its mean absolute error is 5.06, 6.36, and 15.57, against 5.08, 6.32, and 16.10 for the median. - The pool's mean-forecast bias and mean absolute error are within 0.001 of S1's at the six and eight, and its median-minus-mean gap is slightly larger. The gap is -0.286 against -0.277 at the six and -0.423 against -0.406 at the eight. - Pretrained S1 and B-mix have larger mean-forecast errors than S1 at all three groups, and pretraining lowers the mean-forecast error of the lagless network. This agrees with the CRPS contrasts. For L0PT against L0 the mean absolute error is 5.29 against 5.42 at the six and 6.65 against 6.94 at the eight.

docs.title: Table P recalibration
docs.text:
• Experiment 435's Table P leaves the S1 pool below the 0.93 floor at q95 on clean rows. Applied to the raw pool forecast, Table P gives clean-row q95 coverage of 0.914 at the six and 0.924 at the eight. Experiment 435's own R-inj forecasts give 0.904 and 0.919 against the 0.93 floor (experiment 435). Both are still below the floor.
  • Table P scores worse than the 1.15 widening at the six and at D15 and D18, and better at the eight. On the same rows the widened pool has q95 coverage 0.910 at the six and 0.940 at the eight, and CRPS 2.986 and 3.668 against 3.004 and 3.655 under Table P. At D15 and D18 Table P scores 9.053 against 8.968 widened. Cold nights at the six stay poor: q95 coverage is 0.817 under Table P, against 0.861 widened and 0.811 raw.
  • The Table P comparison is approximate, because the factors were fitted on a different neural network and cover three months. The factors are the ones in experiment 435's table_p_factors_full_428.parquet, fitted on R-inj, not on S1. Demand quantiles are not clipped. Only the months 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06 are scored, because Table P for a month needs the earlier folds. Rows are the world-0 clean rows, and the scope is experiment 435's clean condition class. The pool is the S1 pool, not experiment 425's A, whose forecast schema differs. Experiment 435's cold-night class is not applied.

docs.title: Avoidable-curtailment cost
docs.text: • The pool's avoidable-curtailment cost is lower than BG2's at export limits of 0.5 and 0.75 of the reference value and higher at 0.9, and one series, D14, dominates the totals. The cost is the cost of curtailing more than needed, for the signed-MW six at a lead of 12 to 36 hours, four folds, shared clean half-hours, with the seed-mean forecast for the S1 arms. At 0.5 and 0.75 the pool costs £18.0M and £5.82M against £19.3M and £6.40M for BG2. At 0.9, BG2 is lower (£1.28M against £1.76M). D14 carries £1.58M of the pool's £1.76M at 0.9 and £3.29M of its £5.82M at 0.75.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Arms. S1; the pretrained S1; the pretrained S1 fine-tuned at the full learning rate; S1 with B-mix; the three-seed and five-seed pools; the pretrained five-seed pool, with and without B-mix; the leave-one-out arms without the embedding and without the surprise inputs; S1 with hidden width 256; and, for the follow-up contrasts, L0, L0PT, R-inj, and their five-seed pools. S1 seeds 0 to 2 (experiment 428) and seeds 3 and 4 (experiment 439) were already stored.
  • Fits. 141 new fits, counted from the model folders: 20 pretrained S1, 20 full-learning-rate, 40 leave-one-out, 16 lagless, 20 width-256, 20 pretrained lagless, and 5 S1 fits at the fifth fold. These follow 80 pretraining runs (20 each for S1PT, L0PT, RinjPT, and the arm without the embedding). Each fit took about a minute.
  • Pretraining. ERA5 and CAMS rows (reanalysis estimates of past weather) from experiment 418 pass through the input scaling fitted on the fold's training data. The ensemble-spread inputs are set to the median spread at each lead-time band, since past-weather estimates have no ensemble. Every recent-power input is masked (lag values 0, missing flags 1, surprise 0). Fine-tuning then switches the lags on, so the network meets live lag values for the first time there.
  • Pooling. The pool averages the members' cumulative distribution functions on the capacity scale. Single-seed arms report tails from the seed-mean quantile forecast, as in experiment 428, so their tail coverage is not strictly comparable with the pool's.
  • Reused code. Experiments 428, 439, 425, 418, 404, and 446, imported and not edited.
  • Cadence and cleaning. Monthly refits; cleaned data; D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01.
  • Not run. The planned final test (5 folds by 3 seeds, 72 fits) was not run, because no component advanced except the pool, and the pool was scored on the fifth fold from 5 S1 fits. The export gate is not a ladder arm, because it is scored on signed output (see experiments 420 and 424). Table P is a post hoc stage that ran after the screen, and the main tables hold raw and 1.15-widened scores.
  • Reference rows. The reference forecasts of experiment 87 cover only 25 of 31 forecast origins per month. The reference comparison therefore loses about 20% of the S1 rows. All other tables use every row.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Four screen folds plus a fifth fold for S1 and its pool; every number is interim with no 99% claim. The pool's gain at the six (0.048) is under the minimum detectable effect of 0.057, which comes from seed-to-seed spread in single-seed contrasts, and its gain at the eight (0.056) equals the minimum detectable effect of 0.056. The pool beats each of its five single seeds over the four folds pooled and beats the seed mean in every fold, and the paired interval excludes zero. Single seeds win some folds (see Other components), and the intervals are not Bonferroni-corrected.
  • In 2026-01, D5 has no clean rows and D16 has 10, so the signed-MW six holds effectively four series that month.
  • The 14-day horizon is not available; stored forecasts end at 240 hours.
  • Pretraining with masked lags is one design (see Pretraining). S1 pretraining was not run for the fifth fold.
  • Some numbers come from an audit's CPU rescoring and log reading that this experiment's folder does not store: the December figures, experiment 425's rescored scores, the range of single-seed scores (2.842 to 2.875 at the six and 3.539 to 3.591 at the eight), and the count of fits that stopped at the epoch cap.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Treat the five-seed pool of S1 as a candidate default in the next demand experiments; the roadmap owns the decision. Look at why BG2 is better on cold nights at the signed-MW six and in the fifth fold.
  • Read experiment 449 (pretraining S1 with real lagged power) before any further pretraining decision, and compare a five-seed pool of experiment 425's A with the S1 pool on the same rows.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Audit triggers. Trigger 2 (the result contradicts its predictions and earlier experiments) fired: P1, P2, P4, and the surprise-input range failed, and experiments 425 (pretraining helped) and 428 and 439 (surprise inputs worth 0.106) point the other way. F1 to F4 explain part of the contradiction. Trigger 3 is cleared: the median minus mean forecast per Primary and the mean-forecast error are computed above. Trigger 4 (leave one site out) was not run. Trigger 7 may apply, because the pool is a candidate default and is not replicated.
  • Reviews. The plan review, code review, numbers review, and prose review ran; their findings are in the pull request. An independent audit checked the arithmetic against the stored scores and rescored experiment 425's networks on this experiment's rows.

docs.title: Does pretraining the S1 demand network on ERA5 and CAMS weather help when the pretraining stage itself sees the recent-power lags and the surprise inputs?
docs.text: Take-home message: pretraining helps S1 once the pretraining rows carry real recent-power inputs, but the gain is small, rests on one test month at the six, and experiment 425's simpler recipe is ahead of the pooled network over all 16 Primaries. PT1 scores 0.082 CRPS points below S1 at the signed-MW six and 0.068 below at the MVA-only eight (four screen folds, seeds 0 to 2, injected-world clean rows). Experiment 448's masked-lag pretraining scored 0.048 and 0.042 above S1, so the live lags are the difference (PT1 against PT0: -0.129 and -0.110). All numbers are interim, from four test months.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Which rows each table uses. The first table and the cold-night columns use the 579,044 half-hours that every arm and reference shares (real-world clean rows, four folds). The contrasts below use injected-world clean rows (275,534 at the six, 381,834 at the eight, 9,567 at D15 and D18) unless a row says "real rows" (83,458 at D15 and D18). D15 and D18 are headlined on real rows; the injected-row figure follows, labelled.

The minimum detectable effect is 0.065 points at the six, 0.080 at the eight, and 0.98 (injected rows) to 1.18 (real rows) at D15 and D18. The minimum detectable effect comes from the seed spread of S1, for two single-seed arms. For a pool against a pool or a fixed reference the minimum detectable effect is a loose upper bound. The Bonferroni intervals count 26 tests (13 contrasts at the six and the eight); D15 and D18 are outside that count.

Arm Six Eight D15 and D18 Six, cold nights Eight, cold nights S1 2.857 3.556 9.309 2.784 2.957 PT0 (448's masked-lag pretraining) 2.910 3.598 10.046 2.784 2.928 PT1 2.772 3.467 9.205 2.569 2.799 PT1-full 2.784 3.465 9.326 2.607 2.826 PT1b (live lags, no surprise) 2.817 3.487 9.377 2.674 2.811 PT2 (lag dropout 0.3) 2.796 3.442 9.341 2.697 2.775 S1-pool5 2.802 3.501 8.952 2.722 2.821 PT1-pool5 2.740 3.416 8.865 2.537 2.708 425 arm A, five seeds 2.763 3.373 8.283 2.636 2.656 BG2 2.845 3.543 7.687 2.405 2.848 Monthly XGBoost (1.15 widening) 3.026 3.621 8.852 2.811 3.020 manual_heuristic 3.554 4.171 12.088 4.820 4.450 climatology 3.946 4.599 22.740 5.159 4.799

Days 1 to 10 CRPS in points of effective capacity, 1.15 widening. The 425 arm A row averages the quantiles of five seeds and used experiment 397's fit loop; PT1-pool5 mixes the distributions of five seeds. The two recipes differ in more than the surprise inputs.

Contrasts (injected-world clean rows, month-block bootstrap, 95% interval, Bonferroni interval in brackets):

  • C1 PT1 minus S1. Six -0.082 (-0.108 to -0.057; -0.124 to -0.044). Eight -0.068 (-0.103 to -0.035; -0.124 to -0.018). D15 and D18 on real rows -0.044 (Bonferroni -0.191 to +0.113; by fold +0.917, +0.082, -0.158, -0.264). On 9,567 injected rows D15 and D18 is -0.169 (95% -0.287 to -0.047; Bonferroni -0.357 to +0.029). Both D15 and D18 figures are far smaller in magnitude than the minimum detectable effect of about 1.0.
  • C4 PT1 minus PT0. Six -0.129, eight -0.110, D15 and D18 on real rows -0.742. Every Bonferroni interval lies wholly below zero.
  • C6 PT0 minus S1. Six +0.048 and eight +0.042, which reproduces experiment 448's loss. The plan's refit check (a validation loss equal to the stored one) was run only for 2025-12 and its result is not stored, so this page does not claim it.
  • C8 PT1 minus PT1b. Six -0.042 (-0.063 to -0.022 Bonferroni), eight -0.016 (interval spans zero).
  • C3 PT2 minus S1. Six -0.057, eight -0.086, D15 and D18 on real rows +0.102 (Bonferroni -0.047 to +0.280).
  • C5 PT2 minus PT1. Six +0.025 (Bonferroni +0.009 to +0.041) and eight -0.018 (-0.030 to -0.005), D15 and D18 on real rows +0.146 (-0.035 to +0.321): PT2 is slightly worse at the six and slightly better at the eight.
  • C9 PT1-full minus PT1. Six +0.011 (Bonferroni +0.003 to +0.019), eight +0.001, D15 and D18 on real rows +0.113 (+0.061 to +0.170): the full learning rate is slightly worse.
  • Pool contrast 1, PT1-pool5 minus S1-pool5. Six -0.058, eight -0.058, D15 and D18 -0.052 on real rows (-0.210 on injected rows). Pool contrast 3, PT1-pool5 minus PT1. Six -0.035, eight -0.037.

By fold at the six, the gain of PT1 over S1 is -0.281 in 2026-01 and -0.004, -0.047, and -0.047 in the other three folds. Leaving 2026-01 out, the four-fold gain is -0.036, below the minimum detectable effect of 0.065. The gain is negative in 4 of 4 folds on injected rows, but on real rows 2025-10 is +0.018, so the count is 3 of 4 on real rows. The gain at the eight is carried by 2026-03: without it the eight is -0.026. In 2026-01 S1 is unusually poor (3.188 at the six, against 2.907 for BG2).

The fifth fold, 2025-12, cannot be read as a gain at the six. Over five folds C1 is -0.272 at the six, -0.114 at the eight, and +0.200 at D15 and D18 on real rows (a harm; Bonferroni +0.017 to +0.407). The minimum detectable effect at the six rises to 0.34 on five folds because S1's seeds diverge in 2025-12, where S1 fails across the whole month (2025-12 alone is -1.006). Over 1 to 21 December the six score S1 3.514, PT1 3.021, and BG2 3.181. Over 22 to 31 December (days 1 to 10) they score S1 4.223, PT1 2.441, PT1-pool5 2.312, BG2 2.323, and 425 arm A 2.092. At D15 and D18 that week BG2 scores 2.344 and PT1-pool5 3.268.

Experiment 425's arm A, averaged over five seeds, is ahead of PT1-pool5 overall. PT1-pool5 minus 425 arm A on shared rows over four folds is -0.023 at the six (Bonferroni -0.059 to +0.012; the whole gap comes from 2026-01, -0.132, with +0.001, +0.003, and +0.029 in the other folds), +0.043 at the eight (Bonferroni -0.003 to +0.086), +0.582 at D15 and D18 (Bonferroni +0.330 to +0.830), and +0.078 over all 16 Primaries (Bonferroni +0.030 to +0.138). Over five folds the figures are +0.003, +0.036, +0.574, and +0.076. The surprise inputs plus the pool are therefore not shown to add to 425's recipe.

Against the other comparators, PT1-pool5 minus each, four folds (Bonferroni intervals), at the six, the eight, D15 and D18, and all 16 Primaries:

  • S1-pool5. -0.062 (-0.100 to -0.029), -0.084 (-0.143 to -0.029), -0.087 (-0.246 to +0.085), -0.077 (-0.116 to -0.039).
  • BG2. -0.105 (-0.184 to -0.024), -0.127 (-0.199 to -0.047), +1.178 (+0.459 to +2.046), +0.022 (-0.082 to +0.131). On five folds the six is -0.118 (-0.206 to -0.027) and all 16 Primaries tie. BG2 leads on cold winter nights at the six by 0.10 to 0.13 (interval spans zero).
  • Monthly XGBoost (1.15 widening). -0.286, -0.204, +0.013 (-0.376 to +0.360), -0.210.
  • Experiment 448's S1PT-pool5. -0.121, -0.129, -0.957, -0.216. manual_heuristic and climatology are beaten everywhere by 0.76 to 14 points.

Avoidable-curtailment cost: no candidate wins at every limit, so the maintainer must choose the threshold f. The table gives the cost over the four folds, signed-MW six, lead 12 to 36 hours, in millions of pounds, with a 95% interval from resampling the 24 cells (6 series by 4 test months) with replacement 20,000 times. Each cost is the energy-proxy cost of the forecast minus that of a perfect forecast on the same half-hours. The intervals on totals are wide because a few cells dominate; the paired differences below are narrower.

Arm f = 0.9 f = 0.75 f = 0.5 BG2 1.28 (0.09 to 3.47) 6.40 (2.21 to 12.35) 19.31 (13.46 to 26.19) PT1 1.33 (0.07 to 3.69) 4.82 (1.77 to 9.48) 16.47 (11.33 to 22.93) PT1-pool5 1.35 (0.08 to 3.73) 4.86 (1.79 to 9.55) 16.32 (11.29 to 22.52) 425 arm A, five seeds 1.70 (0.08 to 4.74) 5.81 (1.63 to 12.55) 17.38 (10.97 to 26.26) S1 1.76 (0.07 to 5.02) 6.27 (1.87 to 13.52) 18.98 (11.92 to 29.32) S1-pool5 1.76 (0.07 to 5.01) 5.82 (1.86 to 12.23) 18.01 (11.67 to 26.87) manual_heuristic 1.83 (0.14 to 4.97) 10.28 (3.35 to 20.77) 29.92 (19.12 to 44.80)
  • PT1-pool5 minus BG2. +0.07 at f = 0.9 (-0.11 to +0.33), -1.54 at f = 0.75 (-3.26 to -0.29), and -3.00 at f = 0.5 (-4.52 to -1.75). PT1-pool5 is cheaper than BG2 at the two lower limits and level at f = 0.9.
  • PT1-pool5 minus 425 arm A. -0.35 (-1.02 to +0.00), -0.96 (-3.08 to +0.30), and -1.06 (-4.04 to +0.78): not separable.
  • 425 arm A minus S1. -0.07 (-0.36 to +0.13), -0.46 (-1.19 to +0.17), and -1.60 (-3.37 to -0.09).
  • BG2 against 425 arm A and S1. BG2 is cheaper at f = 0.9 (S1 minus BG2 +0.48, interval -0.15 to +1.64; 425 arm A minus BG2 +0.42, -0.02 to +1.28), and dearer at f = 0.5 (S1 minus BG2 -0.34, 425 arm A minus BG2 -1.94), with every one of those intervals spanning zero.

PT1 has lower q95 and q99 pinball loss than S1 at the six, and the lower tail is over-wide for every S1-family arm. On clean rows q95 and q99 pinball loss of PT1 is at or below S1's at the six (0.676 and 0.184 against 0.718 and 0.191). The lower tail is over-wide for every S1-family arm (q05 coverage 0.010 to 0.013 at the six, against 0.05 nominal). At D15 and D18 PT1b has a poor q95 pinball loss (2.739 against 2.261 for S1) and is the one pretrained arm to avoid there.

Raw forecasts, and widening of 1.05 and 1.10, leave the contrasts unchanged. PT1 minus S1 at the six is -0.089 raw, -0.086 at 1.05, -0.084 at 1.10, and -0.082 at 1.15. The pool contrast 1 is -0.062, -0.061, -0.059, and -0.058. The 1.15 widening is slightly too wide for a pool: PT1-pool5 at the six scores 2.8096 raw, 2.8052 at 1.05 and at 1.10, and 2.8090 at 1.15, and at D15 and D18 7.753 raw against 7.840 at 1.15.

The advance rule is met by PT1 against S1 on injected rows. Point gain at least 0.03 with the interval wholly below zero (six and eight), negative in at least 3 of 4 folds, the other group not above +0.02, and the clean-row tails within +0.02 at the six and the eight (D15 and D18 q99 is +0.030). The rule does not compare with 425's arm A, and the comparison with 425's arm A is where the evidence is weakest. PT1 was chosen as the best arm for the pool by a near tie (mean gain 0.075 against 0.072 for PT2 on injected rows). The encroachment sweep of experiment 392, required of an advancing arm, has not been run.

docs.title: What the evidence supports
docs.text:
• Supported. Live lags in pretraining reverse experiment 448's harm. PT1 beats S1 on 3 of 4 folds at the eight and on 4 of 4 (injected rows) or 3 of 4 (real rows) at the six. PT1-pool5 beats BG2 at the six and the eight on four and five folds.
  • Not supported. PT1-pool5 as the first-release demand candidate, because 425's arm A is ahead over all 16 Primaries. Any claim at D15 and D18, where BG2 leads PT1-pool5 by about 1.2 points. Any claim on cold winter nights at the six, where BG2 leads by 0.10 to 0.13. A tie with BG2 over all 16 Primaries is all that is shown (+0.022 on four folds, -0.020 on five).
  • Production cost. Serving a pool of five needs five networks, five forward passes, and five ensemble-weather lagless modules (experiment 404's further module, one per seed), because each member reads its own seed's table. The ERA5 lagless modules are used in training only. A monthly refit needs about 75 fits against eight for S1: 5 ERA5 tables of 6 modules (30), 5 ensemble tables of 6 cross-fit modules plus 1 further module (35), five pretraining runs of 60 epochs on about 7.4 million rows, and five fine-tunes. Sharing one lagless table across the members is untested. Training also needs an ERA5 and CAMS feed.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Mean-forecast checks. Median minus mean, mean bias, and mean absolute error per group are in figure_tables/mean_forecast_checks.csv. They rank the arms as CRPS does at the six and the eight (PT1 4.923 against S1 5.072 at the six; PT1-pool5 4.931 against S1-pool5 5.056). Every arm under-forecasts the mean: about -1.7 points at the six and -8.0 to -11.2 at D15 and D18. No audit trigger 3 signal. The checks omit 425's arm A and BG2.
  • Pretraining length. All 55 PT1, PT1b, and PT2 pretraining runs stopped at the 60-epoch cap, so pretraining may be too short.
  • Leakage. Each of the 25 ERA5 lagless tables (seeds 0 to 4, five folds) covers 2019-09-01 to the half-hour before the refit, fits each module on 5 of 6 contiguous blocks and forecasts the sixth, and repeats no (primary, grid). No table holds a half-hour at or after its refit.
  • Lag semantics. PT1 pretrains through the same input class as fine-tuning, so the lags come from the same origin-lag function over the same power from 2019-09. The stages differ in the surprise source, in the spread columns (set to the fold's median per lead band in pretraining), and, for PT2, in the dropout.
  • Not done. The encroachment sweep, the figures (headline chart by lead day, contrasts by fold, surprise distribution by source, example forecasts, lag-jump event plots), and the nulled-input interval check for PT2. The tables for them are under figure_tables/.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Experiment 448 pretrained the S1 network on ERA5 and CAMS weather with every recent-power input masked, then fine-tuned it on ensemble rows with the inputs live. The result lost to S1 by 0.05 points at the signed-MW six and at the MVA-only eight. The maintainer expected that pretraining across all history and all Primaries would add signal. This experiment asks whether the loss came from the masking: the lag pathway of the pretrained network never saw a lag, so fine-tuning on the shorter ensemble history could not recover it.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• S1 recipe. Experiment 447's width-256 finding is interim and unaudited, so the S1 reference keeps hidden width 64.
  • Reused stored forecasts. Only seeds 0 to 2 of S1 and PT0 are used (both are stored to seed 4); the minimum detectable effect comes from S1's seeds, so the PT arms' own seed spread is read from the result. S1 seeds 0 to 2 (experiment 428) and PT0, which is experiment 448's S1PT (stored networks and forecasts in experiment 448's private folder). Their rows are the same four folds, worlds, and row set, so no S1 network is refitted and PT0 is refitted for 2025-12 only. The reproduction check (a refit of one PT0 fold and seed with a validation loss equal to the stored value) was run only for 2025-12, and its result is not stored.
  • Experiment 425 pretrained with real lags (Opus audit of experiment 448). Experiment 425's pretraining rows carried real lagged power, so its pretraining gained 0.044 points at the signed-MW six and 0.107 at the MVA-only eight on experiment 448's rows, while experiment 448's masked-lag pretraining lost. 425's single-seed arm A (no surprise inputs, no pool) ties the five-seed S1 pool at the six (2.809) and is 0.069 better at the eight. PT1 is therefore 425's arm A with the S1 surprise inputs added: pretrained with real lags and the cross-fitted lagless surprise. The prediction P1 used 425's gains (-0.050 and -0.124 on its own rows) as the expected size.
  • Fifth fold for the holiday slice. The Christmas and bank-holiday slice (22 to 31 December, where BG2 leads) lies in the 2025-12 fold, which is not one of the four screen folds. Every arm is therefore also fitted for 2025-12 (experiment 448 stored S1 for it; PT0 is refitted there). The advance rule reads the four screen folds only. The fifth fold is read for the Christmas slice and for the five-fold table.
  • Standing practices followed. Monthly refits; cleaned data (flagged and start-cut half-hours dropped); the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01 applied; every network saved in the data folder; draft PR; Sonnet for every review (code before the first fit, results, and write-up) and one Opus audit. Pools used the spawn method.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Arm Pretraining stage Fine-tuning stage New neural networks S1 none ensemble rows, lr 2e-3 0 (stored) PT0 ERA5 and CAMS, lags and surprise masked lr 2e-4 0 (experiment 448's S1PT) PT1 ERA5 and CAMS, lags and surprise live lr 2e-4 12 + 12 PT1-full the PT1 pretrained network lr 2e-3 12 PT1b ERA5 and CAMS, lags live, surprise masked (zero) lr 2e-4 12 + 12 PT-pool5 five seeds of the best of PT1, PT1-full, and PT2 (fixed before reading C-pool) as the arm 5 networks per refit PT2 ERA5 and CAMS, each lag masked with probability 0.3 lr 2e-4 12 + 12

The best PT arm is the one among PT1, PT1-full, and PT2 with the lowest mean of its point differences against S1 at the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight over the four screen folds, fixed before any pool contrast is read. Its seeds 3 and 4 are fitted in a second stage (with the lagless tables for those seeds) and pooled with seeds 0 to 2 by experiment 448's equal-weight mixture pool. C-pool is the PT-pool5 minus S1-pool5 (experiment 448's five-seed pool of S1) and PT-pool5 minus PT0-pool5 (experiment 448's S1PT-pool5), at both groups. PT1b is a diagnostic that needs no lagless table: it separates the effect of the lags from the effect of the surprise. Each lag token (the lag value, its missing flag, and its surprise; the age column stays) is masked as a unit in PT2, so the network keeps a pathway that works without the lags. Fine-tuning shows all lags. PT1 and PT1-full share one pretrained network per fold and seed.

docs.title: How the surprise is built for the pretraining years
docs.text:
The surprise at a lag is the lag minus a lagless forecast of the same half-hour, divided by the lagless forecast's half band width. The lagless forecast must not have seen the half-hour it forecasts, or the surprise shrinks towards zero in pretraining and the network learns a lag pathway that fails on ensemble rows. The plan therefore builds one cross-fitted lagless table per fold and seed on ERA5 and CAMS weather, by the method of experiment 404's table:

  • Span and blocks. 2019-09-01 to the fold's refit, split into 6 contiguous blocks. A lagless module fitted on 5 blocks forecasts the sixth. Nothing at or after the refit enters.
  • Module and inputs. Experiment 404's lagless module (a pooled mixture density network with a Primary embedding, 64 hidden units, 6 epochs, learning rate 2e-3). The inputs are the 7 ERA5 and CAMS weather means, the solar-position, calendar, and holiday columns of experiment 397, and no lag and no lead. Experiment 404's ensemble spread columns are dropped because ERA5 has no spread. Rows have equal weights.
  • Early cut. Targets before experiment 418's first-usable date of D11, D10, D5, D14, and D16 are left out of the fits, as in the pretraining targets.
  • Target. Cleaned power over capacity (world 0), with flagged half-hours and the D15 and D18 start cut as missing and left out of the fits.
  • Table. Per (primary, grid): the q50 and half the q05-to-q95 width, in the layout the S1 code already reads.
  • Rescale. The smoke check on 2026-01 seed 0 found the ERA5 table's surprise standard deviation (1.245) well above the ensemble table's (0.850), over 2025-02 to 2026-01. The ERA5 half band width is therefore multiplied, per Primary, by the ratio of the two surprise standard deviations over the half-hours before the refit where both tables exist (the ensemble years), so the pretraining surprise has the scale the network sees in fine-tuning. The ratio uses no data at or after the refit. The ratios are printed per fold and Primary; a ratio outside 0.25 to 4 stops the run (widened from 0.3 to 3 after the first 2025-12 build gave 0.295 at one Primary; the other builds gave 0.41 to 2.31).
  • Overlap years. Pretraining rows after 2024-04 use the ERA5 table in pretraining and the ensemble table in fine-tuning, for the same half-hours.
  • Non-causal and unpurged. A module forecasting a block is trained on later blocks too, as in experiment 404, and the held-out and purged weeks of pretraining are not excluded from the other blocks' fits. Neither uses anything at or after the refit.
  • What differs from experiment 404's recipe. The span is 2019-09 to the refit rather than 24 months, rows have equal weights, and the inputs are ERA5 and CAMS, so the ERA5 modules are not identical in quality to 404's. The further module of experiment 404 (scoring months) is not needed.
  • What differs from use. In fine-tuning, and in use, the surprise comes from experiment 404's table, built from ensemble weather. The pretraining surprise comes from ERA5 and CAMS weather, which is more accurate, so its half-hours are less surprising on average. A smoke check prints the surprise standard deviation by source and asserts that the pretraining table differs from the fine-tuning table. ERA5 arrives about 5 days late and is not available at forecast time; the live service uses the ensemble-based table, as the fine-tuned networks do.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text: 131 networks were fitted (lagless tables, pretraining, and fine-tuning over five folds and up to five seeds), on up to three GPU processes under 8 GB each.

docs.title: Does a recalibration table meet the wind upper-tail rule, and does changing any one setting of the plain wind network, or pretraining it on ERA5, lower its quantile score by 0.10 points?
docs.text:
Take-home (interim, unaudited): the plain wind network is at a plateau, and Farm A's upper tail is the open problem. After table P, 1.39% to 1.50% of observations fall above q99 for the 10 neural arms of experiment 429 pooled over the three farms (limit 1.5%; Wind farms research default 2: 1.64%), but Farm A stays at 1.7% to 2.1% in every arm and in every setting of the plain network. None of 9 changes to the plain network lowers its quantile score by the 0.10-point margin, so the pre-registered rule to stop when no setting helps ended the experiment after stage 1 (9 arms with 5 seeds each = 45 fits; the ERA5 arm also needed 5 pretraining fits; the base arm re-used stored forecasts).

Terms. Table P (experiment 435) rescales each quantile forecast per farm and lead band, fitted on earlier months only, so that coverage matches the nominal level. Kept rows are the half-hours left after experiment 210's idle-band mask removes periods when a farm is idle. True days 1 to 10 means forecast lead times of 24 to 240 hours. The base network is member_plain from experiment 429, the plain pooled wind neural network, whose stored forecasts the base arm reproduces. The 10 neural-network arms are all experiment 429 arms except the repeat of Wind farms research default 2.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Step 1, table P (kept rows, true days 1 to 10, after clipping to [0, 1]). Pooled share above q99: 1.39% to 1.50% for the 10 neural arms (member_plain 1.41%, 95% month-block interval 0.85% to 1.97%), 1.64% for default 2 (0.98% to 2.29%), against 2.1% to 2.5% before table P. Farm A: member_plain 1.76% (0.85% to 2.78%), default 2 2.07%; Farm B 1.13%; Farm C 1.31%. All rows: 1.32% to 1.48% and 1.63%. q01 and q05 coverage are not harmed. Without the clip, the share above q99 would read 0.7% to 1.1%; observations between 1.0 and 1.09 of capacity count as covered by a q99 above 1. An earlier version of experiment 435's table P code had the same missing clip; the merged version clips, and this experiment's own copy of the table P logic (e00450_step1.py) clips too.
  • Step 2, stage 1 (kept rows, true days 1 to 10; score and difference to member_plain, 99.4% interval). member_plain 10.533. Hidden width 32: -0.001 (-0.046 to +0.062); width 128: +0.034; depth 1: -0.012 (-0.046 to +0.033); depth 3: +0.061 (+0.007 to +0.112); encoder width 8: +0.077; encoder width 32: +0.003; 2 mixture components: -0.011; 5: +0.007; ERA5 pretraining: +0.039 (-0.020 to +0.137). Positive is worse. No setting reaches -0.10.
  • Tails of the settings. The q99 pinball loss rises by 0.067 points (2 components) and 0.063 (ERA5 pretraining), above the 0.02 allowance, and by 0.022 (encoder width 8); the share above q99 after table P is 1.37% to 1.55% pooled (depth 1 is 1.51%, above the limit). Farm A is at 1.69% (encoder width 32) to 1.88% (2 components) in every setting.
  • Farm C is above 1.5% for 2 mixture components (1.60%) and ERA5 pretraining (1.68%).
  • Seed spread. The member_plain seed standard deviation is 0.027 points, a seed-only minimum detectable effect of 1.96 x sqrt(2) x 0.027 / sqrt(5) = 0.034 for 5 seeds; the month-block intervals above are wider.
  • Cost. 50 fits of about 56 to 69 seconds each, about 0.8 GPU-hours, one process of 5.5 GB. Stage 2 and the confirmation did not run, because no setting moved the network.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (kept rows, true days 1 to 10, points of capacity): -3.16 for the base network; -3.33 (Farm A), -3.35 (Farm B), -2.77 (Farm C); -2.95 to -3.23 for the settings (-3.57 for 2 mixture components). The median sits well below the mean everywhere, the signature of a right-skewed mixture, so the median and the mean score differently.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast (positive is worse): depth 1 score -0.012 but mean-forecast error +0.022; 2 components -0.011 but +0.060; width 32 -0.001 but +0.024; 5 components +0.007 but -0.010. Other settings are worse on both (width 128 +0.016, depth 3 +0.070, encoder width 8 +0.132, encoder width 32 +0.047, ERA5 pretraining +0.037). The score gains of depth 1 and 2 components are inside noise, so the verdict stands.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 3 fired (score and mean-forecast error disagree for four settings). Triggers 2 and 5 did not fire; triggers 4 and 6 were not tested.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Step 1 was run before its rule was written; the rule is post hoc. The step 2 rule was fixed before the first stage 1 fit.
  • Step 1 gives 11 scored months to resample and step 2 gives 12; the per-farm intervals include 1.5%.
  • Table P comes from the merged experiment 435 page. This experiment re-implements the fit in e00450_step1.py from the code at commit 552c3f87, with the clip added as in the merged code.
  • Every number is interim until the maintainer has read this page; a fresh reviewer reproduced the headline numbers.

docs.text: None.

docs.title: Why does Farm A's upper tail stay above the 1.5% limit after table P, and does a Farm A-specific table fix it?
docs.text:
Take-home (interim): Farm A's upper-tail failure after table P is partly a clipping effect. Raising the clip on every rescaled quantile from 1.0 to the farm's largest earlier power over capacity cuts Farm A's share of observations above q99 from 1.76% to 1.17%, under the 1.5% limit, and all three farms pass (pooled 0.96%). At Farm A, 1.04 of the 1.76 points are half-hours where the forecast q99 is at the clip of 1.0 and the farm produced 1.00 to 1.035 of its effective capacity; raising the clip removes 0.59 points. Experiment 341's capacity-state table says "full" at Farm A for every scored half-hour, so no flagged capacity reduction explains the exceedances. A finer table makes the share worse, so no tail-weight fits were run.

Terms. q99 is the forecast's 0.99 quantile; 1.5% is the limit on the share of observations above it. Table P (experiment 435) rescales each tail quantile's distance from the median per farm and lead band, with factors fitted on earlier months so that coverage matches the nominal level. Clip means bounding a rescaled quantile to a range, here 0 to 1.0 unless stated. Power over effective capacity is measured power divided by the farm's effective capacity (the divisor that turns its power into a fraction of capacity). Kept rows are the half-hours outside experiment 210's idle-band mask. True days 1 to 10 means forecast lead times of 24 to 240 hours. member_plain is experiment 429's plain pooled neural network for the three wind farms. In figure 1, "none" is the unrecalibrated forecast, P_med adds the forecast-median band to table P, and P_wind adds the wind-speed tercile.

The finer-table half of the hypothesis is refuted and the clip half is supported, so the verdict is partly supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Finer tables do not help (step 1). Farm A's share above q99: unrecalibrated 2.90%; table P (farm x lead band) 1.76%; plus forecast-median band 1.98%; plus ensemble-mean wind-speed tercile 2.08%. Farm B and Farm C move the same way (Farm B 1.13%, 1.33%, 1.32%; Farm C 1.31%, 1.54%, 1.62%).
  • Raising the clip removes about a third of Farm A's exceedances. With the upper bound of every rescaled quantile set to the farm's largest power over capacity in earlier months (at least 1.0): Farm A 1.17%, Farm B 0.71%, Farm C 1.00%, pooled 0.96%, against 1.76%, 1.13%, 1.31%, and 1.41% with the clip at 1.0. The 1.17% that remains equals the share of Farm A half-hours with power over capacity above 1.0, so the remaining exceedances are the highest-output half-hours.
  • The clip at 1.0 matters at Farm A. 1.17% of its kept half-hours at true days 1 to 10 have power over capacity above 1.0 (maximum 1.035; Farm B 0.80%, Farm C 0.74%). Table P's q99 is at the clip (0.999 or more) for 38.6% of Farm A's half-hours; 1.04 points of exceedance are half-hours with q99 at the clip and 0.73 points are half-hours with q99 below it. Half the exceedances have an output above 1.008.
  • Where the exceedances sit (step 2, table P with the clip at 1.0; 332 exceedances in 18,831 half-hours).
    • By wind speed: 19.9% above q99 at 12 to 16 m/s ensemble-mean 100 m wind (418 half-hours) and 19 of 21 above 16 m/s, against 0.9% at 4 to 8 m/s and 1.9% at 8 to 12 m/s. The 106 exceedances at 4 to 8 m/s have a mean excess of 0.084, larger than in the other bins, and the clip does not explain them.
    • By forecast median: 19.4% above q99 where the forecast median is at least 0.7 of capacity (581 half-hours), against 0.5% to 2.4% in the three lower bands.
    • By month: 5.1% in 2026-03, 3.5% in 2025-11, 3.3% in 2025-09, 2.6% in 2026-04, and 0.1% or less in 2025-10 and 2026-01.
    • By hour: 0.25% to 1.0% from 04:00 to 06:00 and 2.1% to 3.3% from 16:00 to 22:00.
    • By lead band: 1.4% to 2.6%, with no pattern.
  • No flagged capacity reduction. Experiment 341's capacity-state table says "full" for every scored half-hour at Farm A. This rules out a flagged outage or derating. It does not test whether the effective capacity figure itself is correct.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• This is a screen on one year of data with 11 scored months. The 95% month-block interval of Farm A's 1.76% in experiment 450 was 0.85% to 2.78%, and the intervals of 1.17% and 1.76% overlap, so this screen does not show that the raised clip is better than the clip at 1.0.
  • The raised clip uses the largest power over capacity in earlier months, a single extreme value. It may be below the scored months' maximum of 1.035, in which case some exceedances persist.
  • That the effective capacity is slightly too low is a reading of the data, not a test: nobody has checked the capacity figure.
  • The wind-speed tercile edges use all scored months, and the lower clip at 0 also applies to q01 at Farm B, which has 298 actuals below 0. Neither changes the upper-tail result.
  • Every number is interim until the maintainer has read this page. A fresh reviewer reproduced the headline numbers (the 38.6% and 1.04 points need the 0.999 threshold stated above), and another reviewed the write-up.

docs.title: Do the surprise inputs and a longer pretraining cap improve experiment 425's pretrained pooled mixture density network for Primary demand?
Take-home
docs.text:
A longer pretraining cap and the surprise inputs together do not beat experiment 425's arm A. The 150-epoch cap lowered the pooled CRPS of the five-seed quantile average by 0.017 points at the MVA-only eight and 0.005 at the signed-MW six, against minimum detectable effects of 0.056 and 0.057. The surprise inputs helped at the six only (-0.042, Bonferroni interval -0.061 to -0.023, still below 0.057) and made no difference at the eight. Neither new arm beats A-ref at the eight (+0.021 and +0.037), so A-ref stays the demand candidate. The A-ref comparisons are confounded with the fit loop. A-ref (experiment 397's loop) and the new arms (experiment 428's loop) differ in more than the cap.

Pretraining stopped on patience in 47 of the 50 runs (median 104 epochs, range 78 to 150), so 150 epochs bound in 3 runs, all A-S1-long. The 60-epoch cap of experiment 449 did bind in every run. The timed fit (2026-06, seed 0) lowered pretraining validation loss from 0.2722 to 0.2533, and the fine-tuned scores still differ by less than the noise.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: Figures 2 and 3 show A-S1-long for the first Primary in the 2026-01 fold at one forecast origin. The horizon of every stored forecast is 10 days (240 hours), so the "full horizon" example is 10 days.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• A-ref (stored). Experiment 425's arm A, seeds 0 to 4, run in experiment 397's fit loop.
  • A-S1 (stored). Experiment 449's PT1, 60-epoch cap, seeds 0 to 4, scored alone and as a five-seed quantile average.
  • A-S1-long (new). PT1's recipe with a 150-epoch pretraining cap (AS1L).
  • A-long (new). The same cap without the surprise inputs (AL). A-long has 8,393 parameters against 8,585, because the surprise channels are absent.
  • Common. Experiment 428's fit loop (0.2 of the rows per epoch, patience 8), pretraining on ERA5-and-CAMS rows from 2019-09, fine-tuning at learning rate 2e-4 with the 60-epoch cap, 1.15 widening, monthly refits (cadence not under test; the contrasts could depend on it only through the fold windows). ERA5 weather appears only in pretraining, so no past-weather caveat applies at forecast time.
  • Compute. 50 neural networks (25 per arm), about 1 GPU-hour on 3 processes. The stored lagless tables of experiment 449 (25) and experiment 404 (seeds 0 to 5) were reused.
  • Cleaning. Rows are the cleaned shared half-hours (579,044 on four folds, 713,323 on five). The D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 is applied, as in experiments 428 and 449.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
• Adopt A-S1-long over A-S1? No. Its eight-Primary gain (0.017) is below the minimum detectable effect (0.056).
  • Adopt A-S1-long or A-long over A-ref? No. A-S1-long is not better than A-ref at the eight (+0.021, interval spans zero) and is worse over all 16 and at D15 and D18. A-long is worse at the eight (+0.037). A-S1-long is better at the six by 0.029, below the minimum detectable effect.
  • Does the cap, rather than the surprise inputs, do the work? Neither exceeds the minimum detectable effect at the eight. At the six, A-S1-long beats A-long by 0.042, but A-long is also worse than A-S1 by 0.038, so the surprise inputs recover a loss from dropping them rather than adding to A-S1. No short-cap arm without the surprise inputs exists in this loop, so their effect cannot be isolated further.
  • Cold-night, Christmas-week, and q99 gates. A-S1-long minus A-ref on cold nights at the eight is +0.023 (-0.081 to +0.102) and A-S1-long minus A-S1 is -0.013, so neither worsens by more than 0.02 against A-S1. Against A-ref the gate is not met on Christmas week at the six (+0.138). The q99 gate is met at the six and the eight.
  • Predictions. P1 fails (the cap gain at the eight is -0.017, below the predicted 0.02 to 0.08). P2 holds at the eight (A-long and A-S1-long differ by 0.016) and fails at the six (0.042). P3 holds.
  • Five folds. The cap-only contrast at the eight is -0.019 (-0.036 to -0.001) over days 1 to 10, and the gains stay below the minimum detectable effect. The five-fold six is not read (minimum detectable effect 0.34).
  • Outcome. A-ref stays the demand candidate on this evidence.

docs.title: Production cost
docs.text:
• A-S1-long: 5 neural networks and 5 lagless modules at serving, and about 75 fits per monthly refit (5 ERA5 tables of 6 lagless modules, 5 of experiment 404's ensemble tables of 7, 5 pretraining runs, 5 fine-tunes). The pretraining run is about 2.5 times longer than 60 epochs when it runs to the cap.
  • A-long: 5 neural networks per refit and no lagless modules at serving.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewer read the run script before the first fit (no leakage; three minor fixes applied). A fresh Sonnet reviewer then re-derived the numbers and checked the prose; the PR body lists the findings.
  • Audit triggers. The mean-forecast check (median minus mean forecast per site) was not re-run for this experiment; the new arms differ from experiment 449's PT1 only in the cap and the surprise inputs.
  • Quantile average. The five-seed average of the stored PT1 forecasts is a quantile-space mean like experiment 425's seed average. The pool of experiment 449 was a mixture and is not used.
  • Past-weather. No weather is used at lag times beyond the pretraining years.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Loop confound. A-ref was fitted in experiment 397's loop, so differences against A-ref mix loop, cap, and surprise inputs.
  • Row sets. D15 and D18 are scored on real rows (83,458) with a minimum detectable effect far above the contrasts, so they carry no gate.
  • Unlogged events. Not applicable (no load-shift analysis).
  • Fits stopped on patience. The 150-epoch cap bound in 3 of 50 runs, so a cap above 150 would affect at most a few runs.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Evidence for the roadmap. The 60-to-150 epoch cap and the surprise inputs both fall inside the fit-to-fit noise at the eight.
  • If the loop confound matters, refit A-ref in experiment 428's loop (25 neural networks) before deciding between A-ref and the new arms for a release.

docs.title: Do the metered wind and solar farms' power series hold implausibly high values, and should effective capacity be the maximum, the 99.99th, the 99.9th, or the 99th percentile?
docs.text:
Take-home (interim, unaudited): the wind farms hold almost no implausible high values, and the 99.9th percentile is a safer effective capacity than the 99th for both wind and solar. At Farm A, Farm B, and Farm C, 98% to 100% of half-hours above p99.9 are plausible, and the three maxima are plausible too. For solar, the maximum is unsafe: Solar E's maximum is a two-half-hour spike on the second day of its record, and Solar A, Solar B, and Solar D produced more in 2021 to 2023 than they do now. Capacity at p99.9 of the power before each test month takes the pooled share of actuals above q99 (after table P) from 1.41% to 0.85% for wind and from 3.42% to 1.48% for solar, against the current rule. Against p99 of the earlier power, the shares are 1.38% and 3.67%, and the score in MW is 0.31% lower for solar on average over the series. The operator check of Farm A's capacity figure no longer decides the rule.

Terms. Operator check is a request to the farm's operator to confirm Farm A's capacity figure. Current rule is the 99th percentile of a series' whole cleaned record, including months after the test month; p99 of earlier power is the same percentile of power before the test month. Effective capacity is the divisor that turns a series' power into a fraction of capacity; the current rule sets it to the 99th percentile of the series' whole cleaned record. p99.9 and p99.99 are the 99.9th and 99.99th percentiles. Power over capacity above 1.0 means the series produced more than the current capacity. Table P is experiment 435's recalibration of each tail quantile, per series and lead band, fitted on earlier months. q99 is the forecast's 0.99 quantile, and 1.5% is the limit on the share of actuals above it. Farm A, Farm B, and Farm C are experiment 429's wind farms; Solar A to Solar F are experiment 430's solar series (the question named Solar A and Solar B). The solar member arm of experiment 430 and the wind member_plain arm of experiment 429 are the stored forecasts.

The verdict is partly supported. The wind half of the hypothesis is supported, and the solar half is supported for p99.9 but not for the maximum.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• The tail is smooth for wind. Maximum over capacity: Farm A 1.035, Farm B 1.096, Farm C 1.191. Above p99.9 there are about 125 half-hours per series (on 23 to 44 distinct days). The half-hours above 1.0 occur at a median ERA5 100 m wind speed of 16.0 m/s (Farm A), 16.2 m/s (Farm B), and 17.8 m/s (Farm C), against 11.0, 11.5, and 12.5 m/s at which each farm's median output reaches half of capacity. At Farm A, 37 of the 1,257 half-hours above 1.0 have no ERA5 wind speed.
  • Solar has larger tails and level changes. Maximum over capacity: Solar A 1.21, Solar B 1.13, Solar C 1.07, Solar D 1.15, Solar E 1.49, Solar F 1.07. Solar E's 1.49 and its 1.27 neighbour are two half-hours on 2024-02-08, the second day of Solar E's record, at clear-sky irradiance of 322 and 337 W/m2, against a 99th percentile of 878 W/m2 over daylight.
  • Classification of the half-hours above 1.0 (plausible / total). Farm A 1,257 / 1,257, Farm B 1,208 / 1,218, Farm C 1,211 / 1,216, Solar A 676 / 1,097, Solar B 1,038 / 1,141, Solar C 1,091 / 1,106, Solar D 820 / 957, Solar E 328 / 339, Solar F 1,069 / 1,101. No series has a stuck run of 4 or more equal readings. The implausible half-hours are single-half-hour spikes (0 to 93 per series), weather mismatches (Farm B 7, Solar D 4, Solar E 3), and, for Solar A (380), Solar B (71), and Solar D (46), half-hours in months whose output level is more than 0.10 above the median month.
  • Solar A, Solar B, and Solar D changed output level between years (the monthly files cover April to August only). At strong clear-sky irradiance, Solar A's monthly 90th percentile was mostly 1.0 to 1.15 of capacity in 2021 to 2023 and 0.86 to 0.98 in 2025 to 2026. A static whole-record capacity does not describe those series.
  • Plausible share above each percentile (level-shift flag ignored). Above p99.9: 100% at Farm A and Farm B, 98% at Farm C, 97% to 100% at Solar A, Solar B, Solar C, and Solar F, and 88% at Solar D and 91% at Solar E. The maximum is one half-hour per series; it is flagged at Solar A, Solar B, Solar D, Solar E, and Solar F (Solar E's by weather) and plausible at the other series.
  • Share of actuals above q99 after table P (11 test months, true days 1 to 10).
Series current rule p99 of earlier power p99.9 p99.99 maximum Farm A 1.76% 1.76% 1.05% 0.98% 0.97% Farm B 1.13% 1.09% 0.65% 0.60% 0.60% Farm C 1.31% 1.28% 0.84% 0.84% 0.84% Solar A 2.26% 2.26% 1.47% 1.47% 1.47% Solar B 4.70% 5.11% 1.53% 1.34% 1.34% Solar C 2.37% 2.55% 0.98% 0.98% 0.98% Solar D 3.57% 3.81% 1.10% 1.03% 1.03% Solar E 4.38% 5.02% 2.45% 2.43% 2.43% Solar F 3.45% 3.55% 1.49% 1.48% 1.48%
  • Pooled. Wind: current rule 1.41%, p99 of earlier power 1.38%, p99.9 0.85%. Solar: 3.42%, 3.67%, and 1.48%.
  • Share of actuals above 1. Farm A 1.15% at p99, 0.14% at p99.9; Solar B 4.60% at p99, 0.79% at p99.9. Every series is at or under 0.8% at p99.9 and 0.3% at p99.99.
  • Score. In MW, the percentage change in the score against p99 of earlier power, averaged over the series of each technology (month-block bootstrap, 1,000 draws): wind +0.01% (+0.01 to +0.02) at p99.9 and +0.02% at the maximum; solar -0.31% (-0.60 to -0.08) at p99.9 and -0.31% at the maximum. No rule changes the score by 1% in either technology. Against the current rule, solar's change at p99.9 is about -0.2%.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
• Wind: p99.9 of the series' earlier power. The highest percentile that passes the plan's rule is the maximum, whose single half-hour is plausible at all three farms. p99.9 is preferred (post hoc) because it does not depend on one reading and loses nothing: every wind series is under 1.5% above q99 at p99.9, and the score in MW is unchanged.
  • Solar: p99.9 of the series' earlier power, and not the maximum. The plan's rule (at least 90% plausible, no more than 1% worse) is not met above p99.9 at Solar A (29%), Solar B (74%), or Solar D (72%) with all flags counted, because of spikes and level-shift months, and not above p99 either, so the choice is a judgement: p99.9 gives the pooled 1.48%, and the Solar E spike lies above its p99.9.
  • Still above 1.5% at p99.9: Solar B (1.53%) and Solar E (2.45%).
  • Farm A's operator check. Farm A's top half-hours are smooth, at wind speeds of 13.8 m/s or more (10th percentile), and reach 1.035 of the p99 capacity. They are consistent with a capacity figure a few per cent too low, not with bad data. The operator check would settle the figure and does not change the rule.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• No weather model, XGBoost model, or neural network was refitted. Stored forecasts were rescaled to each capacity and recalibrated with table P. A neural network trained on a power-over-capacity target at another capacity could behave differently.
  • Spikes and level shifts are labelled by rules, not by hand. A single-half-hour solar spike is also what cloud-edge brightening looks like, so the 0 to 93 spikes per solar series are possible artefacts. The level-shift flag marks months whose output level is above the median month, which may be real output at an earlier, higher capacity. The flag marks only upward level shifts.
  • The stored wind quantiles reach at most 1.0 of the old capacity, so the raw variant (without table P) shows no change for wind. Table P is what lets the upper quantiles use the extra room.
  • The interval resamples months. The 1,000 bootstrap draws assume the 11 test months are independent.
  • Scope. 11 test months; the bootstrap resamples months and assumes they are independent. Every number is interim until the maintainer has read this page.
  • Effective capacity is one static number per rule and month. The experiment does not test a rolling or yearly capacity.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewed the code and classification: no leakage or rescaling bugs. The level-shift flag marks whole months, so the plausible share is reported with and without the flag. The spike flag on solar is a possible artefact, as the caveats say. The stuck-run rule has no hits. A second Sonnet re-derived the numbers and reviewed the prose.
  • Audit triggers. No model was fitted and no stored forecast was changed.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: The wind scripts import torch through experiment 347's data module, so the worktree needed uv sync --all-packages --group gpu for a job that needs no GPU.

docs.title: Which combination of lagged and lagless forecasts scores best, and is any combination better than a fixed 50/50 mixture of one of each?
What this experiment found
docs.text:
Mixing a lagged and a lagless forecast beats averaging several lagged forecasts. S1 also improves the lagged half. We asked which combination of lagged and lagless neural-network forecasts scores best for the demand at 14 Primary substations (6 metered in signed megawatts, 8 in megavolt-amperes), and whether any combination beats B-mix, a fixed 50/50 mixture of one lagged network (A0-inj) and one lagless forecast. A lagged network is given the Primary's measured power from three earlier times. A lagless forecast is made without any recent power readings; in B-mix it is read from a stored table, not run as a network at serving time. We scored 20 constructs (equal-weight mixtures of lagged networks and lagless forecasts, 1 to 10 forecasts each) on 5 test months with experiment 404's rows, and compared each with B-mix on identical rows.

K3-S1 beats B-mix by 0.139 points of capacity on rows with no labelled event, and the smallest construct within 0.03 of it is K2-S1. Averaging two A0-inj networks closes 30% of the gap between one A0-inj network and B-mix, so most of B-mix's gain is the lagged-plus-lagless diversity. Replacing A0-inj by S1 gives a better mixture on rows with no labelled event (S1-mix, 0.067 points of capacity better than B-mix at the signed-MW six), and a mixture of two S1 and two lagless heads (K2-S1) is 0.121 better. Inside real events, scored against normal-running-arrangement (NRA) actuals, only K3-A beats B-mix with an interval that excludes zero at the six; no S1 construct does. Applying the adoption rule selects K2-S1 as the construct to port (below), on a point estimate that its interval does not confirm. K2-S1 runs 4 forecasts per forecast pass against 2 for B-mix.

Units and terms. "Harm rows" are rows with no real event at the target but at least one observed half-hour of a real event inside the three-day window before the forecast, ; "metered actuals" are the stored power, and "NRA actuals" are the stored power corrected to the normal running arrangement of the network. "Raw" means before any widening or correction. "Table P" is the recalibration table of experiment 435, fitted on earlier months' rows with no labelled event. "Mass-weighted" means each Primary's score is weighted by its share of capacity. "BG2" is experiment 87's five-model blend with the solar offset. Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of capacity, 11 quantiles, lower is better, on forecasts up to 10 days ahead. "No labelled event" means rows whose target and recent power readings lie outside every logged load-shift event; NGED's event logs are incomplete, so unlabelled events remain in these rows. The signed-MW six are the six Primaries metered in signed megawatts (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16); the MVA-only eight are metered in megavolt-amperes and are never pooled with the six. A construct named K2-S1 mixes 2 S1 and 2 lagless heads; A-ens2 averages 2 A0-inj heads. Interim, five months, no 99% claim.

Figure 2 shows day-ahead forecasts of Primary D5 from B-mix and K2-S1, issued in 2026-01 and 2026-06.

Figure 3 shows the same two forecasts over 14 days.

Figure 4 shows six real events at the six signed-MW Primaries.

docs.text:
Signed-MW six, mean over 5 months, construct minus B-mix (points of capacity; negative is better), Bonferroni 95% interval over 57 headline contrasts (month-block; with 5 months this is close to the range of the monthly contrasts), months better out of 5, absolute score beside it. B-mix scores 3.508 (clean), 3.546 (harm), 5.872 (inside real events, metered actuals).

  • Minimum detectable effect (single fit against single fit, from the spread of B-mix across fit seeds 0 to 2): 0.24 on clean rows, 0.53 on harm rows, 0.38 inside events at the six; at the eight, 0.12 on clean rows, 0.28 on harm rows, and 0.80 inside events (all in points of capacity). The monthly contrasts above are paired on identical rows and are far tighter than these figures suggest, but a contrast inside events is not established unless its interval excludes zero.

A-ens2 stays 0.238 behind B-mix, far outside the 0.03 bar, so the gain is not ensembling alone and the lagless head is worth its serving cost.
  • Tails, signed-MW six (pinball loss of the q99 quantile, difference against B-mix in points of capacity; the 0.02 limit is the pre-registered one): S1-mix raw clean -0.01, harm +0.01, events -0.01; K2-S1 raw -0.03, -0.04, -0.11; after table P S1-mix -0.00, -0.00, -0.00 and K2-S1 -0.02, -0.02, +0.01 (K3-S1 +0.02 inside events). All are within +0.02. Coverage of the q95 quantile on clean rows is 0.864 (S1-mix), 0.875 (K2-S1), and 0.858 (B-mix) raw against 0.95 nominal; after the 1.15 widening 0.901, 0.911, and 0.895; after table P 0.913, 0.911, and 0.913. Coverage of q99: 0.954, 0.961, 0.951 raw; 0.972, 0.978, 0.970 widened. Raw coverage of q01 on clean rows is 0.003 to 0.012 across the 20 constructs (nominal 0.01; A0-inj and S1 sit above it), and of q05 is 0.018 to 0.042, below the nominal 0.05 for every construct.
  • Widening sweep (1.0, 1.05, 1.10, 1.15). B-mix, S1-mix, K2-S1, and K3-S1 still gain from the widest setting on q99 pinball loss (K2-S1 0.00202 at 1.15; B-mix 0.00258 raw and 0.00220 at 1.15; S1-mix and K3-S1 reach 0.0021 and 0.0020), so a mixture of many heads does not need less widening than 1.15. CRPS is flat from 1.05 to 1.15 (K2-S1 3.386, 3.386, 3.386).
  • Production cost per forecast pass: B-mix 2 networks (1 lagged, 1 lagless); S1-mix 2; K2-S1 4; K3-S1 6; K5-S1 10. Each monthly refit trains one lagged network per Primary for B-mix and S1-mix, and as many as K for K2-S1, K3-S1, and K5-S1. The S1 variants also need the lagless table and a store of past lagless forecasts at each of the three lag times.

docs.title: How the decision rule applied, and which predictions held
docs.text:
• Adopt the smallest construct within 0.03 of the best on clean rows at the six. The best is K3-S1 (3.369). K2-S1 (+0.018 from the best) and K5-S1 (+0.025) are within 0.03; S1-mix (+0.072) is not. The smallest within the margin is K2-S1. Its point estimate is no worse than B-mix on harm rows (-0.067) or on NRA event rows (-0.034), and its q99 loss is within +0.02 in every slice (K3-S1 on table P inside events sits at about +0.02, at the limit). "Not worse" is judged on the point estimate: the NRA interval of K2-S1 (-0.127 to +0.102) includes zero, as does that of S1-mix, so neither is shown better or worse inside NRA events. So K2-S1 is the construct to carry forward.
  • S1-mix replaces B-mix only if at least 0.03 better on clean rows, not worse on harm or NRA event rows, and within the q99 limit. It is 0.067 better on clean rows and within the q99 limit, but its NRA event contrast is +0.019 (interval -0.068 to +0.189, 3 of 5 months), so its point estimate is above zero, so the rule is not met. The minimum detectable effect inside events (0.38) is far larger than 0.019, so the experiment cannot tell.
  • If two-seed A0-inj ensembles match B-mix within 0.03. They do not (+0.238), so the gain is not just ensembling.
  • Predictions. P1 held (30% recovered, A-ens2 does not reach B-mix). P2 held on size (0.067 lies within 0.02 to 0.10) and failed on the second half: 0.067 exceeds the 0.03 adoption bar. P3 held (K = 5 is 0.025 worse than K = 3, not better). P4 failed (the four multi-head constructs checked still gain from the widest setting).

docs.title: Checks on the scores and the audit triggers
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site (points of capacity, clean rows at the six, seed cell 0): -0.39, -0.15, -0.66, -0.77, -0.02, -0.29 for B-mix at D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16; the other constructs are within 0.7 of these, and none is larger than 0.9 in size.
  • Mean forecast error beside the quantile score (mean absolute error of the mean forecast, six, clean rows, cell 0): B-mix 4.931, S1-mix 4.881, K2-S1 4.778, K3-S1 4.793, A-ens2 5.237, A0-inj 5.300. The median forecast puts K3-S1 (4.707) ahead of K2-S1 (4.732), the reverse of the mean forecast, and keeps the rest of the order. The error of the mean and the quantile score agree in direction for every construct.
  • Triggers. One audit trigger fired: the first-release lag design and row 4 are ordered behind this experiment and depend on its result. The manager decided on no separate audit. The other six did not fire: there was no control or placebo, the results match the predictions except P4, no nested construct beats the one that contains it (K5-S1 loses to K3-S1 by 0.025, inside the minimum detectable effect), and no sister experiment on the same rows reports intervals to compare. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline contrasts from the stored forecasts and matched every figure to 4 decimals.

docs.title: Event-weighted pooling and curtailment
docs.text:
Pooling events instead of rows does not change the picture. At the six, against metered actuals, with each event given equal weight (a month-block bootstrap over 25 events, 5,000 draws), K2-S1 minus B-mix inside events is -0.110 points of capacity [-0.195, -0.039], and -0.103 [-0.190, -0.030] with the largest event removed. S1-mix is -0.061 [-0.142, +0.011], and -0.054 [-0.139, +0.019] with the largest event removed. On harm rows K2-S1 is -0.081 [-0.121, -0.040]. These intervals are not Bonferroni-adjusted and use metered, not NRA, actuals.

Avoidable-curtailment cost: the S1 constructs cost less than B-mix, and BG2 costs less than every construct. The cost is experiment 449's avoidable-curtailment cost in millions of pounds, summed over 5 months and the six signed-MW Primaries (30 month-by-Primary cells; 95% interval from resampling cells, 20,000 draws). Forecasts are the mean over stored cells, widened by 1.15, on the half-hours with no labelled event that BG2 and manual_heuristic also hold. The cost is the pounds of energy-proxy cost of the forecast minus that of a perfect forecast on the same half-hours, at a node-only limit equal to f times the Primary's earlier maximum (f = 0.9 is a loose limit, f = 0.5 a tight one).

  • K2-S1 minus B-mix: -0.11 [-0.29, +0.00] at f = 0.9, -0.78 [-1.95, -0.08] at 0.75, and -1.82 [-4.30, -0.25] at 0.5. S1-mix minus B-mix: -0.06, -0.53 [-1.31, -0.03], and -1.34 [-3.18, -0.18]. K3-A minus B-mix includes zero at every f.
  • Against the references: B-mix minus BG2 is +0.59 [-0.08, +1.70] at 0.9 and K2-S1 minus BG2 is +0.48 [-0.08, +1.41], so BG2 is lower at f = 0.9 but the interval includes zero. At f = 0.75 and 0.5 K2-S1 and BG2 are within noise. Both B-mix and K2-S1 are below manual_heuristic at f = 0.75 and 0.5 (K2-S1 minus manual_heuristic -4.66 [-8.08, -1.91] and -11.15 [-15.77, -7.01]).
  • Cells are few. The 30 cells are 5 months of 6 Primaries, so the intervals are wide and the months are not independent of the Primaries.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• 5 months, one real world. The month-block interval has 5 values, so it is close to the range of the monthly contrasts. Inside real events at the six the sample is 18 harm, 25 event, and 37 clean bootstrap clusters (a cluster is one corrected event or one run of rows with no labelled event, resampled whole; experiment 455's reconciled counts, 46 corrected events in the 5 months, 21 at the six). Two months (2026-03, 2026-06) hold few event rows.
  • Rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events (NGED's logs are incomplete). The 0.03 bars are read against possibly contaminated rows. The second row set (rows a label-free step scan finds step-free) is not reported. Experiment 456 showed that the label-free step scan cannot separate genuine level changes from noise, so the step-free row set is dropped.
  • Seeds 3 and 4 share training worlds with seeds 0 and 1. Experiment 404 built training worlds (copies of the training power with injected faults) for seeds 100 to 102 only, so fit seeds 3 and 4 reuse worlds 100 and 101 and differ in initialisation and batch order. The 5-head constructs (K5, A-ens5, S1-ens5) are therefore less independent than five full draws, and K = 5 is shown beside K = 3, which has independent worlds. The seed spread and the minimum detectable effect are computed from seeds 0 to 2 only.
  • Experiment 439's seeds were not reused. For 2026-06 on the real world, experiment 404 holds 259,166 rows and experiment 439 holds 192,056, the keys differ, and 439 trains with early stopping (setting g09) where 404 trains six epochs of Adam on stride-2 rows. All 36 additional networks were fitted in the 404 harness (about 20 s each on the GPU, 0.17 GPU-hours).
  • Not done. The injected-fault training worlds are not rescored, and forecasts are not widened beyond the variants listed. The label-free step-scan row set is dropped (see above).
  • Curtailment rows differ from the headline rows. The curtailment cost uses the half-hours with no labelled event that BG2 and manual_heuristic also hold, so it covers fewer half-hours than the headline table. - Schedule. Monthly refits (404's schedule), not weekly; a candidate that wins here is re-checked weekly before any release claim. Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 cut are inherited from 404's rows.
