docs.text:
• Scripts: ml-experiments/00454-*/e00454_fit.py (extra fit seeds), e00454_build.py (heads, constructs, exact mixture quantiles, recomputed heads checked against stored 404 forecasts to within 5e-4 of capacity), e00454_score.py, e00454_report.py, e00454_checks.py, e00454_figures.py. They import experiment 404's modules (folder ml-experiments/00404-mdn-lagless-and-calibration-module-trust-weights), experiment 435's tail helpers, and experiment 445's figure helpers.
  • Stored: 36 networks in experiment 404's model folder (work/models/{A0-inj,S1}/<month>_s<seed>.pt), cached heads and constructs under this experiment's work/ folder (private, not in git), one forecast table per construct, month, and cell.

  • Generate training worlds for seeds 3 and 4 (cheap, the 404 world generator) to make the 5-head constructs independent draws.

docs.title: Does an exact record of which power readings lie inside a load-shift event help a lagged and lagless mixture when the forecast is scored against the normal running arrangement?
docs.text: Knowing exactly which recent readings lie inside a load-shift event still does not make a mixture beat B-mix, even when forecasts are scored against the normal running arrangement (NRA). B-mix is the fixed 50/50 mixture of the plain lagged neural-network forecast (A0-inj) and the lagless forecast. At the six primary substations (Primaries) metered in signed megawatts (the signed-MW six), O-hard switches to the lagless forecast whenever an exact flag marks a lag. It scores 0.16 to 0.19 points of capacity worse than B-mix at the three depth factors of experiment 435's NRA correction, against 0.38 worse on metered actuals. Event detection is therefore not a blocker for the lag-trust line. The numbers are interim and unaudited.

docs.title: Scope and definitions
docs.text:
This experiment fits nothing. It rescores forecasts stored by experiments 404 and 445 on the rows inside real events. It adds the lagless head and the three flag-oracle mixtures of experiment 445 to the rescore that experiment 404's audit ran for its own arms.

  • Row 1 of the lag-trust review (the audit re-pool of experiment 404) is answered by experiment 404's audit, not here: e00404_audit.py and the files cells.parquet, pooled_event_weighted.csv, and event_counts.csv in 404's work/audit/ folder. Experiment 404's audit found B3 and B6 behind B-mix when months are weighted by events (+0.13 and +0.15). It also found that the 1.15 widening and table P (experiment 435's recalibration of the tail quantiles) move every entry by 0.03 or less, so A0-inj minus B-mix on clean rows stays near +0.29.
  • Arms. A0-inj is the plain lagged neural network trained on injected events, S1 is A0-inj plus the lag surprise, B3 is attention over the lags, and B6 is learned windows over the surprise series. The lagless head scores on its own. O-hard, O-soft, and O-floor mix the lagged and lagless forecasts using the exact flags: O-hard switches to the lagless forecast when any lag is flagged, O-soft puts weight (flagged lags / 3) on it, and O-floor puts 0.5 plus half the flagged share on it. Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of capacity.
  • Groups. The MVA-only eight are the eight Primaries that report apparent power in megavolt amperes (MVA) only, so their sign is unknown. D15 and D18 are the two short-history Primaries.
  • Harm row. The scoring code (experiment 428's window flags) calls a row a harm row when its target lies outside every padded real event and outside the 96 half-hours after one. It also requires that any observed half-hour of the three day-windows of its lags lies inside a padded event. Experiment 404's plan defined a harm row on the three origin lags only. A clean row has no real event near it. A row "inside real events" has its target inside a padded event or in the 96 half-hours after one; experiment 455 scores those rows.
  • Event counts. The five scored months overlap 46 corrected events (21 at the signed-MW six, 16 at the MVA-only eight, 9 at D15 and D18) and 42 padded runs. Experiment 445 counts 49 and experiment 435 counts 41 with different windows. At the six the bootstrap clusters are 18 on harm rows, 25 inside events, and 37 on clean rows. The whole history holds 184 corrected events (170 padded runs).
  • Unlogged-event caveat. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs. The 46 events are a lower bound, so rows called clean may hold unlabelled real events, and the harm and inside-event rows undercount. The NRA-corrected actuals correct only labelled events (a measured deviation for 34 of 184, the labelled depth for the other 150).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Rows and scores. Rows are the real-event rows of forecasts with leads of 0 to 240 hours, as in 404's audit. The score is the mass-weighted pinball loss in points of capacity from 11 quantiles. A contrast is the arm's score minus B-mix's on the same rows, mean of month means (seeds within a month averaged first), so negative is better than B-mix. B-mix scores 13.13 at the signed-MW six and 9.36 at the MVA-only eight at depth 1.0 (5.94 and 7.76 on metered actuals). B6 has fit seed 0 only; the other arms have seeds 0 to 2 in 2026-06.
  • Intervals. Resampling the months gives a 95% interval and a Bonferroni interval for 48 contrasts (8 arms against B-mix, at 3 depth factors, in 2 groups; the metered column and the drop-largest variants repeat contrasts and are not counted again). Five months (four at the MVA-only eight, which has no 2026-06 real-event rows) cannot resolve the Bonferroni tail beyond the smallest and largest resampled mean, so a Bonferroni interval is nearly the range of the monthly values and is conservative. The minimum detectable effect (2.8 times the standard error of the monthly differences) is in the last column. The Bonferroni tails come from 20,000 resamples of 4 or 5 months and can move by a few hundredths between runs.

  • O-hard minus B-mix at the signed-MW six is +0.19 [+0.07, +0.29] at depth 0.75, +0.17 [+0.04, +0.27] at 1.0, and +0.16 [+0.01, +0.25] at 1.25 (95% intervals, positive means B-mix is better). With the largest event of each month dropped it is +0.26, +0.21, and +0.17, with Bonferroni intervals above zero at all three (+0.10 to +0.56, +0.10 to +0.43, +0.08 to +0.35). The rule for "detection matters" needs a negative contrast, so it is not met at any depth.
  • Metered actuals give O-hard +0.38 [+0.21, +0.62] at the six. The NRA correction therefore removes about half of the gap but not the sign.

Only O-floor at depth 1.25 has a 95% interval that excludes zero (-0.31 to -0.00), and no Bonferroni interval does.
  • Against the predictions. P1 holds (the O-hard contrast stays above zero, moving from +0.38 to +0.16 to +0.19). P2 holds at the six (the lagless head is +0.09 to +0.11 behind at every depth, with intervals that include zero). P3 fails: dropping the largest event of each month never changes the sign of an O-hard contrast.
  • Checks. No new forecast is written, so the median-minus-mean and mean-forecast-error checks do not apply. None of the audit triggers fired: the numbers for A0-inj, S1, B3, and B6 reproduce 404's audit tables (+0.35, +0.42, +0.08 at depth 1.0 at the six).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Few months and events. Five months and 25 events at the six cannot detect a difference below about 0.2 points of capacity for the oracle arms and 0.26 to 1.64 for the others (0.38 to 0.40 for A0-inj, S1, and B3), and the MVA-only eight has four months.
  • Depth. The NRA correction uses the labelled depth for 150 of 184 events, so the correction's error is repeated at all three depth factors, which scale the same correction.
  • Tails. Experiment 455 scores CRPS only. The tails and the avoidable-curtailment cost are not rescored; experiment 445 found B-mix's q99 covers 71.8% inside real events at the six.
  • Row set. Rows with leads above 240 hours are excluded to match 404's audit; experiment 445's +0.465 includes them, which is why the metered figure here is +0.38.
  • Unlogged events may sit in clean rows and make every event slice an undercount (see above).

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Stop work on event detection for the mixture rule. Exact flags lose to B-mix under both targets.
  • Row 3 of the lag-trust review (a mixture and ensemble family) and the ambiguous-world test are the live lines; experiment 455 changes neither.

docs.title: How often does a Primary's demand show a sustained level step that no neighbouring Primary mirrors?
docs.text: Take-home: a scan of Primary substations' daily demand for level steps cannot yet separate genuine level changes from noise. The scan runs on each Primary's daily weather-corrected demand residual and looks for steps: new levels that last 7 days or more. It finds 166 steps in 93.6 Primary-years (one Primary substation observed for one year), or 1.77 per Primary-year. Synthetic copies of the same residuals, which keep their slow drift but have no abrupt steps, give 1.74 per Primary-year, so the data do not separate the two. The mirror test (does a neighbouring Primary show an opposite-sign step of similar size within 1 day?) passes about as often at the wrong dates as at the true dates. The 0.75 unmirrored steps per Primary-year are therefore an upper bound, and row 4 of the lag-trust design (a test of genuine level changes in the training data) should keep its placeholder rates of 2% and 5% of training rows. For the forecast, rows inside a scan step that no NGED event label covers keep most of the 50/50 mixture of a lagged and a lagless neural-network forecast (B-mix) over the lagged forecast alone, so the scan does not find rows where B-mix fails.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Data. The 16 Primaries of experiment 87's loader, 2019-09 to 2026-07, flagged exact-zero half-hours already removed. 4,717 half-hours are missing between the first and last reading of the 16 Primaries (flagged zeros and any other gaps). D15 and D18 drop rows before 2025-03-01. 93.6 Primary-years of valid daily levels.
  • Residual. Method (b): a lagless XGBoost median forecast (13 calendar and ERA5 features, absolute-error objective, 300 rounds), cross-fitted in 6-month blocks, boosters saved as .ubj under the experiment's data folder. Method (a), the stored cross-fitted lagless tables of experiment 449, agrees with method (b) on the five stored months (median daily-level correlation 0.90, 80 Primary-months; the lowest is -0.28). ERA5 weather is a lab condition, not available at forecast time. Cadence: not applicable.
  • Scan. Optimal partitioning of the daily level (squared-error cost, penalty 3 times ln(n) times a lag-7 noise variance, segments of 7 days or more). A step counts at 3 times the Primary's spread and 2 points. The scan on one Primary takes 0.05 s; the whole experiment took about 5 minutes after the block fits (about 13 minutes).
  • Compute. CPU only, 2 threads. Reviews: Sonnet plan review, Sonnet code review before the first run (its findings changed the injection sizes and the surrogate scan), Sonnet results review (re-derived the headline numbers; no discrepancy), prose reviews as the PR body records.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Counts (baseline). 36 mirrored, 70 unmirrored, 60 temporary, 0 unassessable. Rates per Primary-year: 0.39, 0.75, and 0.64. 66 of the 70 unmirrored steps match no labelled event, so 0.71 per Primary-year are unlabelled. The median step is 14.6 points of effective capacity (1.1 MW). Dropping 5 unmirrored steps that start within 3 days of a block boundary gives 0.69.
  • Sensitivity of the unmirrored rate. Spread multiple 2: 1.27; 4: 0.43. Floor of 1 or 4 points: 0.75 (the spread sets the threshold at every Primary). Segment of 14 days: 0.52. Penalty 2 times or 5 times: 0.80 and 0.74. Mirror start within 3 days: 0.69. All 15 other Primaries as neighbours: 0.49. The rate moves by a factor of three across the grid.
  • Share of days inside an unmirrored step (first 60 days of each): 5.1% at baseline, 2.7% at 4 times the spread. P2 (under 2%) failed at baseline.
  • False alarms. Phase-randomised surrogates keep each residual's power spectrum and remove abrupt steps. The scan finds 1.74 steps per Primary-year in them, from 0.0 at D3 and D15 to 8.8 at D4 and 16.8 at D9. At D4 and D9 the surrogates produce more steps than the real series (4.8 and 4.1 per Primary-year). Excluding D4 and D9 the pooled rate is 0.63. Neither meets the 0.2 limit. Nine Primaries (D2, D3, D8, D10, D11, D12, D14, D19, D21) have under 0.7 false alarms per Primary-year (D15 also, but over 1.4 years only). At the 14 Primaries other than D4 and D9 the real series gives 1.44 steps per Primary-year against 0.63 in the surrogates, so about 44% of the steps there could be false alarms; D4 and D9 drive the pooled match.
  • Mirror at chance. With the table pairs, 0.217 of the 166 steps are called mirrored at their true start and 0.163 to 0.223 when the start is shifted by 30 to 90 days. With all 15 other Primaries it is 0.554 against 0.518 to 0.614. The tolerance (opposite sign, MW within a factor of 2, start within 1 day, at any neighbour) is too loose, so the mirrored class is not evidence of load shifting.
  • Injection (quiet windows, daily residual). Steps of 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 times the detection threshold are recalled at 0.48, 0.98, and 1.00 (random windows 0.43, 0.91, 0.97), flat in duration at 1.5 times the threshold or more. With a mirror injected at a neighbour, 0.98 of detected steps are classed mirrored at 1.5 times (quiet and random windows alike); for unmirrored injections about 10% are called mirrored by chance. A refit of D2 with a 30-day step of 1.5 times the threshold injected into the half-hourly power (two windows) recovered 11.4 and 11.8 of the injected 11.8 points, so the cross-fit did not absorb it. Recall is high only for large steps; steps of 3 times the spread (1.0 times the threshold at the typical Primary) are recalled at under 0.5, so P3 failed.
  • Quiet windows. The step-free rule leaves a median 41,500 of 120,000 half-hours per Primary as injection windows (D18 keeps 3,900 of 24,400) (quiet_windows.csv).
  • Recall on labelled events (experiment 400's corrected table, 184 event-by-Primary rows in 93 events). 11 rows and 10 events are found (a same-sign step starts within 2 days of the onset); of events lasting 7 days or more, 7 of 13 events and 7 of 23 rows. P1 held for events lasting 7 days or more (7 of 13 is above half). This is a lower bound on recall and says nothing about unlabelled events.
  • What the scan changes for the stored forecasts (experiment 404, A0-inj against B-mix, 5 months, 1,649,447 rows; a row is "in a scan step" if its origin day or target day lies in the first 60 days of any detected step at its Primary, mirrored, unmirrored, or temporary).
Row set Share of rows B-mix lead (lagged minus B-mix, points) Step-free 66% 0.64 [0.55, 0.75] In a scan step, unlabelled 14% 0.55 [0.45, 0.67] Labelled event only 14% 0.37 [0.24, 0.49] Labelled event and scan step 5% 0.23 [0.05, 0.40]
  • Reading the table. Removing the unlabelled scan-step rows would cut 18% of the rows not labelled as events and move B-mix's lead on the rest from 0.63 to 0.64, so the scan would not change a score. The intervals of the first two rows overlap. The row sets differ by Primary (the scan flags 58% of the rows of one Primary and none of the rows of three others), so the four row sets are not a matched comparison.
  • Candidate list. candidate_steps.csv beside this page lists every step (Primary, start day, start date, end day, size in points and MW, class, nearest neighbour and its change, labelled, near a block boundary). 26 mirrored steps match no labelled event (0.28 per Primary-year); given the chance rate, most of them are coincidences. The list is reliable only for the nine Primaries with low false-alarm rates.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• NGED's event labels are incomplete. The 184 label rows are a lower bound on events, so the measured recall is a lower bound on the true recall, and an unlabelled candidate may be a real event. Clean rows may hold unlogged events.
  • The scan cannot tell three kinds of case. It cannot recognise a genuine level change that a neighbour mirrors by coincidence, it cannot see a step shorter than 7 days, and it cannot say what caused a step. It does not see mirrors at bulk supply points, grid supply points, or unmetered Primaries.
  • Injection is into the daily residual with the spread and noise scale fixed at the real series' values (a lab shortcut, checked by one refit).
  • Neighbour sets are the pairs in the corrected label table of experiment 395.
  • Post-run change. The first false-alarm surrogate (14-day block bootstrap) created steps at the block joins (5 per Primary-year, three times the real count), so it was replaced by phase randomisation after the first run. Injection sizes (multiples of the threshold) and the surrogate's spread were fixed after the code review and before the numbers were read.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Repeat at the nine low-false-alarm Primaries with a stricter mirror rule: a mirror must beat its own shifted-date distribution.
  • Use a residual with less drift (a level state or an annual refit) at D4 and D9.
  • Keep row 4's 2% and 5% placeholders until a repeat separates the unmirrored steps from noise.

docs.title: Does the out-of-fold forecast of the convex GAM, given to the pretrained pooled mixture density network as an input or as a base, improve Primary demand forecasts?
Take-home
docs.text:
Giving arm A the GAM's forecast as one extra input lowers CRPS by 0.036 points at the eight MVA-only Primaries. A gain of 0.036 is 1.1% of the score and is within 0.0005 of the minimum detectable effect of 0.0355, so the gain is real but marginal. At the signed-MW six the gain is 0.035 (Bonferroni interval -0.042 to -0.027), below that group's minimum detectable effect of 0.070. The tail pinball losses (q01, q05, q95, q99) and the pooled cold-night scores do not get worse. Using the GAM as an additive base for the neural network made the forecast worse by 0.291 at the eight. The GAM's own forecast is worse than the pretrained neural network's, and fine-tuning for 8 to 16 epochs does not recover the loss. The pre-registered rule is met narrowly for the input arm, and the requirement is a GAM in the serving path with its monthly refit.

All numbers are from experiment 425's arm A recipe on the five folds of experiment 449, rows with no labelled event (NGED's event labels are incomplete, so these rows may hold unlabelled real events).

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: Example forecasts are GAM-as-input, seed 0, D5, one origin each. The horizon of every stored forecast is 10 days (240 hours).

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• A-ref (stored). Experiment 425's arm A (folder ml-experiments/00425-*), run in experiment 397's loop with pretraining on ERA5-and-CAMS rows and fine-tuning at learning rate 2e-4, seeds 0 to 4, scored again and never refitted.
  • A-gam-in (Gin). Two extra input columns, the standardised GAM forecast and a missing flag. The new first-layer weights start at zero.
  • A-gam-base (Gbase). The GAM forecast shifts the mixture means by z_gam minus the frozen pretrained neural network's mixture mean, so training starts at the GAM forecast with the pretrained component offsets, weights, and spreads. Rows without a GAM value are the pretrained neural network.
  • Both arms start from experiment 425's stored pretrained arm A weights (no new pretraining), so the GAM input is learned in fine-tuning only and arm A is the matched reference. ERA5 pretraining years have no out-of-fold GAM.
  • Deviation from the plan. The size line anticipated 50 new pretrained networks. None was pretrained, and the 50 fine-tuned networks start from experiment 425's stored pretrained weights.
  • Stage 0 (the GAM). Stored monthly per-site T-all GAM fits of experiment 136 (six signed-MW Primaries) and experiment 252 arm A1 (eight MVA-only Primaries), no Kalman filter and no lagged-error input, driven by the calibrated ensemble mean to 240 h. The 14 Primaries are fitted per site, not pooled. Stage 0 took 2 min 10 s of CPU time in total and forecast every ensemble run from 2024-04. D15 and D18 have no fit, and D8 has none before 2025-07, so their rows carry the missing flag. Leads above 240 h train as "GAM missing" (experiment 425's rows run to 351 h).
  • Settings shared by all arms. Monthly refits, five-seed quantile averages, 1.15 widening, five folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, flagged zero half-hours dropped. The scores use 713,323 shared half-hours, of which 385,855 are at the eight. Fifty fine-tunes took about 90 s each on one GPU process, about 1.5 GPU-hours in total.

docs.title: Headline numbers (CRPS in points of effective capacity, days 1 to 10; negative is a gain)
docs.text:
• Minimum detectable effect: 0.0355 at the eight, 0.070 at the six, 0.517 at D15 and D18, 0.061 at all 16 (arm A's five single seeds, experiment 428's formula; printed before any contrast).
  • Absolute CRPS at the eight: arm A 3.363, GAM-as-input 3.327, GAM-as-base 3.654, BG2 3.563, manual heuristic 4.163, climatology 4.564. At the six: 2.734, 2.699, 2.898, 2.856, 3.760, 4.091.
  • Gin minus A at the eight: -0.036 (Bonferroni -0.045 to -0.028; 95% -0.042 to -0.030). Cold nights -0.050 (-0.080 to -0.012; the 2026-03 fold alone is +0.061, and at the six it is +0.040). Christmas week -0.003 (-0.021 to +0.019; one year, report-only).
  • Gbase minus A at the eight: +0.291 (+0.219 to +0.366). Cold nights +0.317, Christmas week +0.441.
  • Per fold, Gin minus A at the eight: June -0.001, October -0.044, December -0.052, January -0.029, March -0.052. The gain is absent in the June fold.
  • Per Primary (leave-one-site-out, from the results review): the Gin gain stays between -0.043 and -0.027; it is largest at D19 (-0.092), D4 (-0.079), and D8 (-0.058) and about zero or positive at D12, D22, and D3.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only): Gin minus A +0.021 (95% interval +0.013 to +0.030; Bonferroni +0.011 to +0.034), so the GAM input slightly hurts where the GAM is missing.
  • Tails, Gin minus A at the eight (pinball, upper one-sided 95% bound): q01 -0.004 (-0.003), q05 -0.011 (-0.009), q95 -0.010 (-0.008), q99 -0.004 (-0.003). Coverage at the eight: q95 0.946 and q99 0.990 for Gin against 0.949 and 0.991 for A. Gbase raises q05 pinball by 0.127 and q95 by 0.045.
  • Decision rule for Gin at the eight: CRPS gain 0.036 against the minimum detectable effect 0.0355 (the rule is met only just: 0.0005 above); pooled cold nights and Christmas week do not worsen; no tail pinball loss worsens. The rule is met. Gbase fails it (CRPS +0.291).
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost, signed-MW six, lead 12 to 36 h: the total over the five folds and the six Primaries, in millions of pounds, with a 95% bootstrap over the 30 (fold, Primary) cells. At f = 0.9: arm A 1.89, Gin 1.88, Gbase 1.25, BG2 1.37, manual heuristic 2.02; Gin minus A -0.012 (-0.044 to +0.015). At f = 0.75: arm A 7.05, Gin 6.96, Gbase 6.35, BG2 8.24, manual heuristic 12.9; Gin minus A -0.089 (-0.229 to +0.028). At f = 0.5: arm A 21.6, Gin 21.3, Gbase 21.5, BG2 25.9, manual heuristic 37.8; Gin minus A -0.323 (-0.690 to +0.035). Gbase has the lowest cost at f = 0.9 although its CRPS is worst, but its difference from arm A (-0.641, -1.854 to +0.063) includes zero, and at f = 0.5 it is no better than arm A.
  • Widening sweep 1.0 to 1.15 (eight, q95 coverage): Gin 0.918 to 0.946, arm A 0.922 to 0.949; the Gin-minus-A CRPS gap stays about -0.035 at every factor. These rows exclude BG2, so they differ slightly from the shared-row figures above.
  • The GAM alone: its mean absolute error at the eight is 6.75 points of capacity, against 6.09 for the median forecast of arm A and 6.02 for the median forecast of Gin.
  • Bonferroni count: 6 tests (two arms times three gating row sets: the eight, cold nights at the eight, and Christmas week at the eight). Other rows are reported with the same level but are not counted as tests.
  • Production requirement: the GAM must run in the serving path with its monthly refit, and the neural network needs the GAM forecast for every forecast origin.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewer read the code before the first fit (no leakage; the GAM-as-base mixture collapse, a missing Primary-join assertion, a broad exception handler, and an unclipped input were fixed). A fresh Sonnet reviewer then re-derived the 2026-01 and five-fold differences (identical to the files) and found no bug. A third fresh Sonnet reviewer checked this page's numbers and prose; the PR body lists what it found and what changed.
  • Leakage. Every GAM value comes from the latest fit whose cut is at or before the forecast origin (3.5 hours earlier, checked by choose_fit), and stage 0 additionally requires the cut to be on or before the first day of the origin's month. Cuts are the first day of each month at 00:00 UTC (gam_cuts_*.json). The ensemble calibration comes from the odd months 2024-07 to 2025-05.
  • Audit triggers. Mean-forecast check: the change in the mean forecast's absolute error against arm A is -0.063 points for Gin and +0.440 for Gbase, with the same signs as the CRPS contrast, so that trigger does not fire. Median minus mean forecast on 2026-01 is -0.49 points for A, -0.47 for Gin, and -0.59 points for Gbase (largest at D12 and D8). No leave-one-site-out sign flip. The prediction-contradiction trigger fires for Gbase (predicted a gain of 0.05 to 0.15, found a loss of 0.29). Predictions P2 (Gin gains less than Gbase) and P1 (Gbase gains) failed, and P3 held for Gin. The cause, checked numerically in the results review: at the start of fine-tuning the Gbase mixture mean equals the GAM forecast to 2.4e-7. On validation rows the GAM's mean absolute error is 0.353 standardised units, against 0.304 for the pretrained mean. Gbase therefore starts at a validation negative log-likelihood of about 0.67 against 0.52. Its final value (0.496 for 2026-01 seed 0) stays far above Gin's (0.364). Fine-tuning ran 8 to 16 epochs (see work/logs).
  • Past-weather. The GAM is driven by the calibrated ensemble mean at forecast time, so no past-weather caveat applies. The ERA5 pretraining years carry no GAM value.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The Gin gain is within 0.0005 of the minimum detectable effect, so it could be noise-level; the interval excludes zero, but the gain is absent in the June fold and concentrated at three Primaries.
  • Fits are per site, not pooled, and cover 14 of 16 Primaries; D15 and D18 are report-only.
  • Rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled real events (NGED's event labels are incomplete).
  • Christmas week is one year (22 to 31 December 2025), report-only.
  • The sweep rows exclude BG2 and so cover more half-hours than the shared set.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Port the GAM input only if the serving path already runs the GAM; the gain is too small to justify building a GAM service for it alone.
  • Test the GAM's partial effects (not only its forecast) as inputs, and a GAM input fitted pooled across Primaries, which would also cover D15 and D18.

docs.title: Can a fitted weight, a prequential weight, or a shrunk level offset on the lagless forecast beat the fixed 50/50 mixture of the lagged and lagless forecasts?
docs.text: No combination rule beat the fixed 50/50 mixture of the lagged and lagless forecasts (B-mix). The lagged weight that fits best falls with lead time, but the fitted weight moves by 0.2 or more between months, so weights fitted on earlier months do not generalise. A shrunk recent-level offset on the lagless forecast (arm d) is better on rows with no labelled event and much worse inside real events. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold real events that nobody logged, and every real-event slice undercounts. Every number is interim and unaudited. The scores bear on forecast quality, and the inside-event rows bear on robustness to bad inputs.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are points of effective capacity; a contrast is the arm minus the 50/50 mixture of the same lagged head and the lagless head, so negative is better. Months are the resampling unit (4 scored months; seeds averaged within 2026-06; the warm-up month 2025-10 is excluded for every arm). Intervals are 95% month-block intervals; the Bonferroni interval for 20 contrasts is in the tables of the experiment's private folder and in the figure.

  • Arms. (a) B-mix. (b) one lagged weight per group and lead band, fitted by minimum exact CRPS on earlier months. (c) prequential weight from each head's 7-day loss, floor 0.2, softmax temperature fitted on earlier months. (d) lagless forecast plus k times its median residual over the last 24 hours of delivered actuals. Lagged heads: A0-inj and S1 of experiment 404; lagless head: the frozen table of experiment 445. Arm (d) uses no lagged head.
  • Reference. The stored B-mix mixes Gaussian-mixture heads; the arms mix the stored 11-quantile heads. A recomputed 50/50 mixture ("half") scores within 0.001 to 0.02 points of the stored B-mix, so contrasts use the recomputed 50/50 (same algebra). Contrasts against the stored B-mix are in contrasts.csv.
  • Signed-MW six, inside real events (NRA depth 1.0; 50/50 scores 14.262 with A0-inj, 14.267 with S1; minimum detectable effect 0.51 and 0.63; the seed-to-seed spread of B-mix in 2026-06 is 2.931 to 2.957 at the signed-MW six on rows with no labelled event). (b) A0-inj +0.006 [-0.005, +0.023]; (b) S1 +0.043 [-0.000, +0.119]; (c) A0-inj +0.085 [-0.009, +0.267]; (c) S1 +0.069 [-0.004, +0.142]; (d) +1.210 [+0.145, +2.276]. A0-inj alone is +0.396 and the lagless head alone +0.120.
  • Signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event (50/50 scores 3.680 and 3.638; minimum detectable effect 0.40 and 0.36). (b) A0-inj +0.054 [+0.010, +0.099]; (b) S1 +0.072 [+0.000, +0.144]; (c) A0-inj -0.019 [-0.052, +0.006]; (c) S1 -0.037 [-0.117, +0.013]; (d) -0.234 [-0.584, +0.091], with 2 of 4 months negative. The lagless head alone is +0.306.
  • MVA-only eight. Inside real events (3 months with events): (b) +0.031 and +0.070, (c) +0.069 and +0.066, (d) +0.251 (all intervals include zero except (b) S1, +0.024 to +0.118). Rows with no labelled event: every arm within 0.065 of 50/50 and every interval of (b), (c), and (d) includes zero.
  • Candidate rule. No arm is a candidate: none lowers the inside-event score by more than the larger of 0.03 and the minimum detectable effect (0.51 at the six). (b) is also 0.054 and 0.072 worse than 50/50 on rows with no labelled event, over the 0.03 allowance.
  • Stop rules. The fitted weights of (b) at the six lie between 0.41 and 0.86 (within 0.05 of 0.5 in 1 of 40 cells), so the "50/50 is near-optimal" rule does not fire literally. Held out, however, they score no better than 50/50. The prequential weights stay within 0.05 of 0.5 on 18% to 82% of rows at the six (below 90%). k in (d) is 0.2 to 0.95 at the six (not near 0), so the lagless forecast does not already do the work.
  • Weight stability. Arm (b) at the six: 0-12 h weight 0.68 to 0.81 and days 6-10 weight 0.43 to 0.62 across the four fitted months; some lead bands move by 0.2 or more between 2025-12 and 2026-01, and most move by 0.2 or more across the four months (figure 2). Rows in 2025-12 are fitted on 2025-10 alone, so that fit is thin.
  • Tails at the six, rows with no labelled event. q95 coverage is 0.860 for B-mix and 0.863 and 0.863 for (b) and (c); table P lifts it to about 0.944. q99 coverage 0.952, then 0.985 to 0.986 after table P. Arm (d) covers q01 at 0.017 and q05 at 0.060 raw, above the nominal 0.01 and 0.05. Inside real events (row-weighted) q99 coverage is 0.706 for 50/50, 0.705 for (b), 0.707 for (c), and 0.781 for (d). The q99 pinball loss is 0.0227 for 50/50 and differs by under 0.001 for (b) and (c). Arm (d) has the lower q99 pinball loss inside events, 0.0182, although its CRPS is 1.21 points worse.
  • Production cost. Arm (d) needs only the lagless head and 24 hours of delivered actuals, so it costs less than two neural networks; it does not match 50/50 inside real events.
  • Checks. A recomputed 50/50 reproduces the stored B-mix score to 0.001 (2026-06) and about 0.01 elsewhere. A fresh reviewer re-derived the 2026-01 B-mix score (3.9628, 59,530 rows) and found no leakage in (d): moving its offset window back 0, 2, 4, and 14 days raises the score 3.160, 3.308, 3.484, and 4.100, so the gain is a persistent bias of the lagless table, and it is not uniform (worse than B-mix in 2025-12 and 2026-06). Rows already omit half-hours that the cleaned power table lacks, so flagged zeros are dropped; experiment 399's start cut falls before every scored month. The check of median minus mean forecast does not apply, because every arm is a mixture or a shift of stored quantiles with no mean forecast.
  • Predictions. P1 partly holds: the weight falls from about 0.75 at 0-12 h to about 0.5 at days 6-10, but (b) is 0.054 worse than 50/50 on rows with no labelled event, not better. P2 fails (18% to 82% of rows within 0.05). P3 fails: k is 0.2 to 0.95 (below 0.3 in one cell), and (d) is better, not worse, on rows with no labelled event. P4 holds.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Four months cannot separate a difference of 0.09 from zero. Arms (b) and (c) match 50/50 inside events within 0.09 points, so the hypothesis holds in part: they match, and none beats 50/50. The advice to skip the 50-fit experiment rests on four scored months.
  • Four scored months and 3 to 4 months with events, so the minimum detectable effect is 0.4 to 0.6 points at the six and the Bonferroni intervals are nearly the range of the monthly values.
  • Unlogged events. Rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled real events, so the (d) gain on those rows may be partly a level offset that follows an unlogged event.
  • Not run. Avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5, cold-night rows, the rows that the label-free step scan (experiment 456) finds step-free, months with a single real event shown apart, the XGBoost R0 pair, and the encroachment sweep. The curtailment and cold-night code reads frames of experiments 448 and 449's harness, which these stored forecasts do not share.
  • Seeds. Seeds 0 to 2 only in 2026-06 and seed 0 in the other months; experiment 454's new seeds are not yet scored.
  • Fit objective. Weights minimise the exact CRPS of the piecewise-linear mixture, not a likelihood, because the stored heads are 11 quantiles.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Re-score on experiment 454's seeds 0 to 4 when its heads land, and add the curtailment cost.
  • If a combination is wanted, test arm (d)'s offset on the lagged head's forecast as well; a persistent bias in the lagless table is what it corrects.

docs.title: Experiment 459: does a load shift leave the sum over the donor and its recipients unchanged?
docs.text:
When NGED moves load between Primary substations, the sum over the donor and its labelled recipients still steps by about half of the donor's step, as it does in windows with no logged event. That sum is therefore not conserved by the event, and a forecast of the sum split by a slowly changing share cannot absorb a transfer. The pre-registered stop rule fired on both its tests, and the oracle share-split forecast is no more accurate than experiment 392's R0 lagged XGBoost forecast, so the group-sum forecast does not reach its threshold. With 15 events at the six the evidence is thin. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so every count is a lower bound and every placebo window may hold an unlogged event.

Terms. NGED's label table names a donor Primary and usually a recipient Primary for each event; the step is the median change in a series' power over the event's interior, from its 7-day half-hour-of-day baseline. G1 is the donor plus its labelled recipients among the 16 Primaries, G2 is G1 plus the donor's neighbours in NGED's interconnection table, and G3 is all 16 Primaries. The leak share is the absolute step of the group's sum divided by the absolute step of the donor: 0 means the transfer cancels inside the group, and 1 means no cancellation. The six Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) report signed MW, the eight (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22) report MVA magnitude only, and D15 and D18 are reported apart. A placebo window has the event's duration and group at a random onset outside every labelled event and the 7 days after it (20 per event). The oracle forecast is given the true group sum and splits it by the trailing 30-day median share. A harm row is a forecast row whose target lies outside every labelled event but whose 1, 2, or 7-day lag lies inside one. The R0 lagged forecast is experiment 392's XGBoost forecast with power lags, refitted on plain targets by experiment 402 (the stored forecast read here). Points are percentage points of a Primary's effective capacity.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: If load were conserved, the black sum line in figure 1 would stay flat through the shaded event.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• P1 (fails). P1 predicted a median G1 leak share of at most 0.25 at the six for events with a recipient among the 16, against a placebo above 0.5. Observed: 0.53 (15 events) against a placebo median of 0.54, and 13% of events at 0.25 or less (placebo 30%).
  • Stop rule (fires). The median G2 leak share at the six is 1.73 (28 events with a valid sum out of 31; limit 0.5), and 13% of observed-recipient events have a G1 leak share of 0.25 or less (limit 50%). A leak share above 1 means the sum moves more than the donor alone.
  • P2 (holds). Of the 112 events, 31 (28%) name no recipient, inside the predicted 20 to 40%. By donor group the share is 24 of 46 at the six (52%), 4 of 54 at the eight (7%), and 3 of 12 for D15 and D18. At the six, the median G2 leak share of these events is 1.21 (14 valid of 16), above the predicted 0.5.
  • P3 (fails). The oracle share-split error has a median of 3.91 points at the six, against 3.31 for the R0 lagged forecast on the same rows (ratio 1.2; 30 group-and-Primary pairs, one with a ratio under the predicted 0.5).
  • Harm rows (fail). The oracle's median paired gain over the R0 lagged forecast is −0.10 points at the six (18 pairs, 26,786 rows); the rule needs at least 0.1. Per Primary the gain is +0.21 at D10, −0.47 at D11, and −0.36 at D14; D5, D9, and D16 have no harm rows, because the R0 forecast covers four test months. The oracle uses the true group sum at the target time, so its gain is a ceiling for a trailing-share split.
  • At the eight, leak is worse than placebo. Median G1 leak share 0.89 against 0.40, and 12% at 0.25 or less (placebo 38%). MVA magnitudes are not conserved when flow reverses, and 19 of the 34 events mix MW and MVA readings.
  • At all 16 Primaries (G3), the median leak share is 5.1 at the six, with a valid sum for only 16 of 31 events, because the sum needs all 16 readings in the same half-hour.
Pre-registered contrast (G1, observed recipient) Events Estimate Interval Six: median leak minus placebo median 15 −0.01 −0.27 to 0.91 Six: share at most 0.25 minus placebo share 15 −0.16 −0.38 to 0.14 Eight: median leak minus placebo median 34 0.49 0.23 to 0.65 Eight: share at most 0.25 minus placebo share 34 −0.26 −0.39 to −0.11

Intervals resample events with their placebo windows, at 98.75% so that the four contrasts hold together at 95%. The smallest median-leak contrast the placebo spread can detect is 0.18 at the six and 0.16 at the eight, so the six's interval, much wider than that, cannot separate the events from the placebo. Leaving out one donor moves the six's median-leak contrast between −0.21 and 0.34, and dropping the largest event gives 0.07.

  • Share stability. The trailing share moves slowly (figure 3): the month-to-month range of a six Primary's share has a median of 0.06 and a maximum of 0.38 (D14 with D18). Multiplied by the group sum, the one-day-ahead share error has 80% band edges between −14 and +11 points at the six, against a median absolute error of 2.9 to 4.2 points for the R0 lagged forecast.
  • Dead meters. Placebo windows at the six with more than 5% missing half-hours in the group (a gap proxy for a dead or flagged meter, not a direct test) have a median G1 leak share of 0.85 against 0.59 for the rest, from only 11 windows. That is too few to conclude, and the windows give no sign of a shield.
  • What an operator would see. The forecast for a Primary would read "the group's demand times this Primary's usual share". The group sum is not smooth through logged events: in figure 1 the black sum swings as much as, or more than, the donor.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Incomplete labels. Placebo windows are outside labelled events, not clean windows.
  • Exclusions. Of the 112 events, 37 are excluded (22 with a donor step under 0.3 MW, 8 with no measurable donor step, 7 whose measured sign disagrees with the corrected sign), leaving 75 (31 at the six, 38 at the eight, 6 for D15 and D18).
  • Event baselines. Of the 75 events, 52 (24 of 31 at the six) have a 7-day baseline that overlaps an earlier labelled event or its 7-day tail, because the same donors repeat. Placebo baselines never do. Placebo onsets are uniform over the record, not matched in season.
  • Scope. Experiment 456's candidate steps are not used. The brief's 12 to 36 hour band is not reported, because the oracle does not depend on lead.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Treat a labelled event as a property of one Primary's own series, as experiments 400 and 402 do.
  • A forecast that borrows the neighbours' lag surprise (as experiment 402's gate does) stays open.

docs.title: Code and data
docs.text:
• Code: ml-experiments/00459-load-shift-conservation-check-donor-and-recipient-sum/. It reuses experiment 377's series table, experiment 391's neighbour graph, experiment 395's corrected label table, and the R0 lagged forecast stored by experiment 402.
  • Tables: table_groups.csv, table_contrasts.csv, table_allocation.csv. The per-event and placebo rows, with the monthly shares, are in the private work folder.

docs.title: When forecasts made from each power lag alone disagree, are the lags wrong, and can the disagreement set the width of the bands?
docs.text:
Take-home message. When one neural network hides its power lags, its forecast barely changes, so the disagreement between its five forecasts (all lags, each lag alone, no lags) cannot show which lags are wrong. The disagreement did not widen the bands or choose a mixture weight better than a fixed rule. Training with random lag dropout also made the neural network slightly worse. The next step is a forecast that depends more on its lags, or more diverse members such as a three-seed ensemble, not a disagreement signal from one network.

We asked whether a neural network that has learned to forecast with or without each of its three recent power readings (lags) can tell when those readings are wrong. We trained such a network, scored each forecast five times (all lags, each lag alone, no lags), and measured how far the five medians disagree. We then tested whether that disagreement picks out the half-hours whose lags lie inside a load-shift event while the target does not (harm rows), and whether it can widen the bands or set a mixture weight. It cannot: the area under the curve (AUC) is 0.51 at the signed-MW six Primaries, and no arm that uses the disagreement beats a fixed 50/50 mixture of a lagged and a lagless network (B-mix). NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows are called "rows with no labelled event"; the label-free step scan has not reported, so that second row set is not used. Every number is interim and unaudited by the maintainer.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
• Figure 1 and Figure 2: each arm minus B-mix at the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight.
  • Figure 3: AUC of the spread signals.
  • Figure 4: absolute scores.
  • Figures 5 and 6: example forecasts. Figures 7 to 12: six real events.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are the mass-weighted pinball loss (CRPS-like) in points of capacity, seeds averaged within a row, rows with leads of 0 to 240 hours, a mean over months. Arms c and d have no 2025-10 forecast (nothing earlier to fit on), so their contrasts use four months. Arm letters are those of the design below. Intervals are unadjusted 95% intervals (Bonferroni count 42 for the pre-registered contrasts), and no 99% claim is made.

  • Spread signal (diagnostic, AUC). Harm rows against rows with no labelled event, pooled over months and averaged over the 3 seeds. Signed-MW six: AUC 0.51 (months resampled 0.48 to 0.59; real events resampled 0.48 to 0.54). MVA-only eight: 0.47 (0.40 to 0.52; 0.44 to 0.51), so the spread is slightly lower on harm rows. D15 and D18: 0.40 (report-only). The maximum-over-pairs signal gives 0.52, 0.46, and 0.40. Lead in hours alone, with no neural network, gives 0.52 at the six and 0.54 at the eight, so the spread separates harm rows no better than the lead does. Within lead bands the mean AUC is 0.49 (six) and 0.47 (eight). Month by month the six's mean-spread AUC is 0.48 (2025-10), 0.48 (2025-12), 0.63 (2026-01), 0.58 (2026-03), and 0.52 (2026-06), so the pooled null hides two months with some separation. The 0.65 bar is still missed. This diagnostic is read beside its effect on forecast scores (arms c and d below).
  • Known-answer control missed its prediction. On the injected scoring worlds the AUC for the spread is 0.53 (six) and 0.55 (eight) for rows with an injected event anywhere in the three day windows; prediction P2 was above 0.75. Post hoc, with only rows whose three origin lags lie inside an injected event as positives, the AUC is 0.60 (six) and 0.62 (eight) for the mean spread, and 0.63 and 0.65 for the maximum. The five-pass medians move little even under exact lag corruption: across all rows the median of the mean spread is 0.037 of the band width, and the all-lags and no-lags medians differ by 0.016 of capacity on average (2026-01, seed 0).
  • The lag-dropout network (b) against stored S1 (a). On rows with no labelled event at the six, b minus a is +0.08 [+0.01, +0.14] (3.86 against 3.77 row-pooled; b is worse in 4 of 5 months; leaving out one month gives +0.06 to +0.11) and +0.05 [-0.06, +0.16] at the eight. The stop rule (a loss above 0.03 at the six) fires. The loss is below the minimum detectable effect of 0.16, so the sign is the information, not the size. Month by month the difference is -0.03 (2025-10), +0.18 (2025-12), +0.01 (2026-01), +0.14 (2026-03), and +0.12 (2026-06), so the exceedance of 0.03 is a point estimate that two months do not show. The score_a and score_b columns of contrasts.csv pool rows, while diff is the mean of the month means, so the columns need not subtract to diff. The absolute scores quoted in this section are the row-pooled values; absolute.csv and Figure 4 give the mean over month means, which differ by 0.07 to 0.2 (for example 3.79 against 3.71 for b and a), while the contrasts agree.
  • Arms c and d against B-mix (rows with no labelled event, six). Arm c (b widened by spread) 4.09 against B-mix 3.72, +0.34 [+0.13, +0.65], worse in 4 of 4 months. Arm d (b mixed by spread) 4.10, +0.35 [+0.17, +0.64]. At the eight: +0.23 and +0.26. Both exceed the 0.03 non-inferiority bar, so neither is a candidate under rule 2. On real harm rows the gaps are +0.36 and +0.40 (six), +0.97 and +0.99 (eight); inside real events (NRA-corrected actuals) +0.17 and +0.27 (six), +0.97 and +1.02 (eight).
  • Spread adds nothing over the controls. Arm c minus c0 (table P with no spread) is -0.003 [-0.006, -0.000] (C6); arm c minus b is -0.003 [-0.036, +0.027] and arm d minus b is +0.009 [+0.001, +0.021] (post hoc, C9 and C10); the fitted mixture weights are flat across the four spread bins (for example 0.4 in every bin at the six for 2026-06). Arm c against f (S1 with a constant 1.15 widening) is +0.12 [+0.03, +0.18], and arm d against g (the three-seed S1 ensemble) is +0.28 [+0.19, +0.41].
  • 12 to 36 hours (post hoc contrast C7). The three-seed S1 ensemble (g) beats B-mix by 0.21 [0.07, 0.38] at the six and 0.22 [0.10, 0.34] at the eight, but across all leads it trails B-mix by +0.05 [-0.16, +0.31] and +0.02. One possible reason is that the lags matter most at short lead, where a diverse ensemble does best; no experiment here tests that.
  • Tails. See the table. Recalibration with table P lifts q99 coverage inside real events at the six from 0.970 (b) to 0.996 (c and c0), the same for the spread-conditioned and the plain version.
Six, NRA-corrected actuals inside events q99 coverage inside events q99 coverage, rows with no labelled event q99 pinball loss, rows with no labelled event (fraction of capacity) e: B-mix 0.979 0.951 0.0026 a: stored S1 0.973 0.917 0.0035 b: lag-dropout network 0.970 0.913 0.0036 c: b, spread widening (4 months) 0.996 0.976 0.0036 d: b, spread mixture (4 months) 0.968 0.896 0.0041 f: S1 widened by 1.15 0.982 0.944 0.0028 g: three-seed S1 ensemble 0.980 0.940 0.0027 c0: b, table P only (4 months) 0.996 0.974 0.0038

The q01, q05, and q95 coverages, the MVA-only eight, and the table-P tails of the other arms are in work/score/tails.csv. At the eight, q99 coverage inside events is 0.925 (B-mix), 0.895 (b), 0.940 (c), and 0.904 (d).

  • Avoidable-curtailment cost: not computed. The measure needs forecasts for each grid supply node and its generators; this harness forecasts 16 Primaries only (as in experiment 445).
  • Serving cost. Five passes of one neural network per forecast, against B-mix's two neural networks.
  • Minimum detectable effect (read before any contrast, from the spread between seeds of B-mix on rows with no labelled event): 0.16 at the six, 0.08 at the eight, 1.65 at D15 and D18.
  • Fits. 15 fits (3 seeds times 5 months), 36 seconds each on the GPU (about 0.15 GPU-hours). Networks are saved under the experiment's data folder (work/models/S1d/).
  • Reuse. Experiment 404's rows, S1 and A0-inj networks (fit seeds 0 to 2) and lagless tables; experiment 435's table P and NRA-corrected actuals; experiment 454's mixture code. Recomputed S1 and B-mix forecasts match experiment 404's stored seed 0 tables to within 2.2e-5 (capacity fraction).
  • Rows dropped. The flagged substation_zero half-hours and the D15 and D18 cut are those of experiment 404's rows; their count was not re-derived here.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary (rows with no labelled event, points of capacity): the median lies below the mean at every Primary for b, from -0.02 (D14) to -0.81 (D5) at the six and -0.00 (D22) to -1.30 (D12) at the eight (D15 -1.28, D18 -0.27). B-mix has the same sign (D5 -0.35), so the skew is in the weather-driven demand forecast, not in the spread arms.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile contrasts (mean absolute error, points of capacity, metered actuals, six): rows with no labelled event B-mix 4.99, a 5.21, b 5.33; harm rows 4.70, 4.96, 5.11; inside events 9.68, 9.65, 9.79. The ordering agrees with the quantile score on the first two row sets. Inside events, a is marginally better than B-mix on the mean forecast, and its metered quantile contrast is +0.13 [-0.11, +0.32], so the two do not contradict each other.
  • Triggers that fired. Trigger 1 (a control failed): the injected-world control (P2) fell short, and the post hoc explanation test above (exact lag corruption gives an AUC of 0.60 to 0.65) supports "the network barely uses its lags". Trigger 2 (result contradicts its prediction): P3 predicted a loss of 0.00 to 0.05 against S1 and observed +0.08; P1 expected 0.52 to 0.62 at the six and observed 0.51, and 0.47 at the eight. Triggers 3 to 7 did not fire (leaving one month out does not change the sign of C1, C2, or C3). A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the headline numbers; its findings are triaged in the pull request.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• NGED's event labels are incomplete. Rows with no labelled event may hold events no label covers, so the harm table is optimistic and the real-event rows undercount.
  • The experiment covers five months and 18 harm-row events at the six (19 at the eight), which is few; the MVA-only eight has four months with a row inside an event.
  • Arms c and d are fitted on 1 to 4 earlier months and score four months; the fit for the summer month rests on winter months. About 650 half-hours of January targets also appear as actuals in the December fitting rows, which can only favour arms c and d, and they still lose.
  • Arm g is a single ensemble with no seed spread, so C5 and C7 compare it with a 3-seed average of single networks; comparing a single ensemble with a 3-seed average does not bias the sign of the contrast, but hides the ensemble's seed noise.
  • Arms c, c0, and the table-P rows use a floor of 1.0 on every factor (no narrowing), unlike experiment 435's table P, and fit on all real rows of earlier months, not only rows with no labelled event.
  • The no-lags pass appears in only 2.7% of training rows, so it is the least trained pass.
  • The AUC subsamples the rows with no labelled event to 40,000 per month and seed.
  • The extra contrasts C8 to C12 are post hoc and not among the 42.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• The result gives no reason to continue with disagreement as a trust signal for neural networks that hide lags, because the forecast does not depend on the lags enough.
  • Test the three-seed S1 ensemble against B-mix at 12 to 36 hours in a held-out year, because that post hoc contrast is the only positive contrast among those we ran.
  • If a lag-trust signal is still wanted, use a network whose forecast moves with its lags (for example, one trained without a lagless input) and check the injected-world control first.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Harness. Experiment 404's: its rows, its five months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), six epochs of Adam on stride-2 rows, training on the injected worlds of seeds 100 to 102 (one per fit seed 0 to 2), the frozen cross-fitted lagless tables, and the same fit seeds as experiments 404 and 454. Rows are equal to experiment 454's. A fit was estimated at about 20 seconds on the GPU (36 seconds measured), so 15 fits (3 seeds times 5 months) cost minutes of GPU; the first fit is timed and reported before the rest.
  • Network. S1 (the plain network with three origin lags and the surprise at each lag) trained with random lag dropout: for each training row each of the three lags is masked independently with probability 0.3. A masked lag has its value, age, and surprise set to 0 and its missing flag set to 1; the missing flag is the mask flag, so a lag that is really missing and a lag that is masked look the same to the network. Experiment 404's PlainLagMdn and fit_arm are reused, but its drop_lags cannot handle the 12 columns of S1, so a subclass in this folder has new masking code (mask_lags). Training and the five passes call the same function, so the single-lag and no-lags passes are not off-distribution.
  • Passes. The saved network is scored five times per row: all lags, each single lag alone (the other two masked), and no lags. One network, five passes per serving call.
  • Arms. (a) the stored S1 network; (b) the lag-dropout network with all lags; (c) arm b with its tail quantiles widened by a factor that is a monotone function of the mean spread; (d) arm b mixed with its no-lags pass, with a mixture weight that is a monotone function of the mean spread; (e) B-mix; (f) arm a with a constant 1.15 widening; (g) the three-seed S1 ensemble, an equal-weight density mixture of the S1 networks of fit seeds 0 to 2. Control c0: arm b after a table P (experiment 435's tail recalibration) with no spread, so a gain from recalibration alone is not read as a spread signal.
  • How arms c and d are fitted. On the real rows of earlier months only, per seed, per group, with leads 0 to 240 hours. Arm c: four spread bins whose edges are the quartiles of the fitting rows' spread per group; within each bin and lead band, table P's per-tail factors (the quantile of the standardised miss, as in experiment 435); the factors are then made non-decreasing in the bin with a running maximum. Arm d: the same four bins per group; within each bin, the weight on the no-lags pass from the grid 0, 0.1, ..., 1 that minimises the fitting rows' mean CRPS (a subsample of up to 60,000 rows per group per earlier month), made non-decreasing in the bin with a running maximum. Nothing in the fit uses an event label. The fitting rows of each earlier month are that month's own out-of-sample forecasts (made by the network trained before that month), so the fit is not on rows the scoring network trained on; the earlier months cover other seasons, which limits the fit for the summer month. Arm d is a density mixture (log weights shifted by log of the weight, as in B-mix), and its fitting CRPS is computed on the mixture's quantiles. Control c0 uses the same procedure and rows as arm c with one bin, not experiment 435's table.
  • Confounds of the spread. Lag age grows with lead, and the no-lags pass is seen in only 2.7% of training rows. The AUC is therefore also reported within each lead band (mean of the band AUCs) and beside a lead-only score (the lead in hours as the signal), and the 12 to 36 hour band's CRPS is reported separately.
  • Row classes. Experiment 404's report.load classes with the window flags of experiment 428: a harm row has its target outside every padded real event (and outside the 96 half-hours after one) and an observed half-hour of its three day-windows inside a padded event; rows inside real events have the target inside a padded event or in the 96 half-hours after one; rows with no labelled event have neither. The injected scoring worlds (seeds 200 to 202) are used only for the AUC known-answer control (P2).
  • Actuals. Inside real events the headline actual is experiment 435's NRA-corrected value (normal running arrangement), the metered value secondary, each with and without the largest event of each month; months with a single event are shown apart.
  • Tails and cost. q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage and pinball loss, raw and after table P, per group and lead band, and the 12 to 36 hour band separately. The avoidable-curtailment cost is not computed: it needs forecasts for each grid supply node and its generators, and this harness forecasts the 16 Primaries only (the same reason experiment 445 gives).
  • Absolute scores are printed beside every contrast. Serving cost: five passes of one network per forecast against B-mix's two networks.
  • Standing practices followed. Monthly refits (not a cadence question, so no weekly gate), cleaned data with the flagged substation_zero half-hours dropped by experiment 404's rows, the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01 (report-only), every fitted network saved under this experiment's data folder, stored forecasts reused as references, a fresh Sonnet code review before the first scored number, the five-month screen of experiment 404 rather than four folds (so rows equal experiments 404 and 454), tails reported beside CRPS, draft pull request.
  • Unlogged-event caveat. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs. Rows with no labelled event may therefore hold events no label covers, the harm table is optimistic, and the real-event rows undercount.
  • Earlier advice followed. Experiment 445: score against both metered and NRA-corrected actuals. Experiment 404: report single-event months apart, and weight by event. Departure: the curtailment cost is not computed (above).

docs.title: Does retraining the wind and solar networks with effective capacity at the 99.9th percentile of earlier power keep their quantile score and bring the upper tail inside the 1.5% limit?
docs.text:
Take-home: setting each wind farm's capacity to the 99.9th percentile of its earlier power keeps the wind forecast as accurate and changes the share of actuals above the 99% quantile forecast only slightly, from 0.96% to 0.88% (all three farms were already under the 1.5% limit). For solar the change passes the pre-registered rule by a hair, fails it if any one series is dropped, and makes Solar A's score 2.3% worse.

Capacity is the divisor that turns a series' power into a fraction between 0 and 1 for the neural network. The old capacity is the 99th percentile of the series' whole cleaned record (experiments 429 and 430). The new capacity is the 99.9th percentile of the series' cleaned power before the end of the fit's training (wind: before 2025-04-16; solar: before each refit's cutoff). Retraining the wind neural network member_plain (5 seeds, one fit per seed) and the solar neural network a2_member (3 seeds, 4 quarterly refits) under the new capacity gives the results below. Farm A to C are experiment 429's wind farms, and Solar A to F are experiment 430's solar series. Rows are the half-hours at true days 1 to 10 that experiment 210's mask keeps for wind and all scored half-hours for solar.

Terms. Table P adjusts each tail quantile forecast per series and lead band, using the share of actuals that fell beyond it in earlier months, and clips the upper quantile at the larger of the capacity in use and the largest earlier actual (experiments 435 and 451). The limit is that at most 1.5% of actuals exceed the 99% quantile forecast (a calibrated forecast gives 1%). The margin is the largest worsening of the quantile score that the plan accepts: 0.10 points of capacity for wind (about 0.1% of the score) and 1% of the pooled score for solar. Pooled means summed over the series of a technology, so each series weighs by its capacity.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Wind passes the rule. The upper bound of the 95% interval of the score change is under 0.00005 MW, against a margin of 0.10 points of capacity (about 0.1% of the score). The pooled share above the 99% quantile forecast is 0.88%. The plan predicted an old pooled share of about 1.4%, but experiment 451's clip already brings it to 0.96%, so the wind tail was not failing the limit before this change.
  • Solar a2_member passes the rule by a hair. The upper bound is +0.0064 MW (+0.97% of the old score, against 1%), and the pooled share is 1.496% (against 1.5%). Over six bootstrap seeds the upper bound ranges from 0.96% to 1.01%, and dropping any one of the six series fails the rule (below). The solar score change has the opposite sign to the prediction (predicted 0.3% better, measured 0.4% worse), and the difference is smaller than the minimum detectable effect.
  • Wind score. Pooled 1.1765 MW (old) and 1.1744 MW (new), a change of -0.0020 MW (-0.17%; 95% interval -0.0040 to -0.0000 MW). Farm A -0.23%, Farm B -0.13%, Farm C +0.15%, all inside the margin. The minimum detectable effect is 0.0034 MW (0.29%), the mean score gap between two old single-seed fits. The new fits differ from each other by 0.0077 MW, so the change lies inside fit-to-fit spread.
  • Wind share above q99 after table P (old to new). Pooled 0.96% to 0.88%; Farm A 1.17% to 0.95%; Farm B 0.71% to 0.79%; Farm C 1.00% to 0.90%. Before table P the pooled share is 2.36% (old) and 1.75% (new). Every farm is under 1.5% in both arms.
  • Solar score and share (a2_member). Pooled 0.6601 MW (old) and 0.6627 MW (new), +0.0026 MW (+0.39%; 95% interval -0.0029 to +0.0064 MW). Solar A +2.29% (+0.77% to +3.77%), Solar F +0.76%, the other four within 0.4%. The minimum detectable effect is 0.0017 MW (0.26%). Shares after table P, old to new: Solar A 1.69% to 1.45%, B 1.42% to 1.47%, C 1.18% to 1.18%, D 1.08% to 1.12%, E 2.72% to 2.41%, F 1.48% to 1.48%. Solar E is the only series above the 1.5% limit (95% interval 1.42% to 3.39%).
  • Tails after table P, pooled (share at or below the quantile, nominal 1%, 5%, 95%, 99%). Wind, old to new: q01 1.36% to 1.35%, q05 5.47% to 5.44%, q95 95.13% to 95.13%, q99 99.04% to 99.12%; q99 pinball loss 0.0647 to 0.0641 MW. Solar a2_member: q01 3.33% to 3.29%, q05 7.05% to 6.69%, q95 94.61% to 94.45%, q99 98.43% to 98.50%; q99 pinball loss 0.0248 to 0.0248 MW. Solar D's q01 coverage is 12.3% in both arms, so the capacity rule does not cause it.
  • Other solar arms (exploratory). g0_onepass: pooled share 1.64% to 1.41%, score +0.41% (upper bound +0.78%), so it passes. a5_plain: share 1.60% to 1.50%, score +0.72% (95% interval +0.24% to +1.1%), so it fails the 1% rule. Solar A is 2.2% to 2.8% worse in all three arms.
  • Refit against the re-scoring of experiment 453. Experiment 453's re-scoring gave wind +0.01% and solar -0.31% (against p99 of earlier power). The refit gives wind -0.17% and solar +0.39%. The solar gap of 0.7 points is under the 1% margin, so the re-scoring did not mis-state the effect beyond the margin. The refit's new capacity also uses only earlier data, while the old capacity used the whole record, so the contrast includes that difference.
  • Capacities. New over old capacity: Farm A 1.024, Farm B 1.061, Farm C 1.098. Solar, over the four refits: A 1.135 to 1.142, B 1.095 to 1.103, C 1.059 to 1.060, D 1.076 to 1.079, E 1.051 to 1.057, F 1.054 to 1.056. Solar E's earlier history holds only 21,852 to 31,278 half-hours (the others 83,000 to 110,000), so its p99.9 is the noisiest.
  • Rows and seeds. Rows are equal across arms: wind 54,899 half-hours (Farm A 18,831, B 18,403, C 17,665); solar 345,510 (A 60,210, B 60,039, C 60,885, D 54,864, E 49,770, F 59,742). Seeds: 5 wind, 3 solar. The bootstrap resamples months and is conditional on the fitted seeds, and the old and new seeds are not paired fits.
  • Leave-one-out on solar a2_member. Dropping one series at a time (score change, upper 95% bound, new share): A +0.09%, +0.68%, 1.505%; B +0.45%, +1.11%, 1.503%; C +0.48%, +1.08%, 1.563%; D +0.39%, +0.99%, 1.568%; E +0.67%, +1.18%, 1.343%; F +0.33%, +0.97%, 1.501%. No drop changes the sign of the score change, and every drop fails the rule on the share, the bound, or both.
  • Bonferroni count. 11 intervals are reported for the headline arms (2 pooled, 3 wind, 6 solar series); the adjusted level is 99.55%. At that level only Solar A's score change excludes zero (+0.0011 to +0.0217 MW).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Reproduction gates. Fits with the ratio set to 1 reproduce experiments 429 (wind, seed 0) and 430 (solar a2_member, seed 0, refit 2025-09) bit for bit.
  • Capacity is fixed per fit, not per scored month. The old and new arms therefore differ in the training-target scale and in using later data, not only in the divisor.
  • Wind rows. The cleaned-zero row set of experiment 432 was not scored.
  • Solar A, B, and D produced more in 2021 to 2023 than now. A capacity rule does not remove this level shift in the training history. Solar A's loss may come from the level shift, which is a hypothesis that no experiment here tests.
  • The avoidable-curtailment cost does not apply to wind and solar farms.
  • Porting effort. The rule is one number per series, recomputed at each refit.
  • Scored range. Scored rows stop at true day 10 (lead 240 hours).
  • The neural network's quantile head clips its quantiles to 0 to 1 of the capacity in use, so the new arm's head reaches the new capacity.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewed the plan (decision rule and pooling defined, clip restated, bootstrap described as conditional on seeds: all accepted) and the code before the first fit (no defect; two minor points accepted: serial fits, a dead call removed). A fresh Sonnet re-derived every headline number from the stored predictions with its own code and found no mismatch and no unit error. Two more fresh Sonnet reviews checked this page's numbers and prose.
  • Median bias moves with the score for wind and, in the pooled signed bias, against it for solar. The pooled mean of the median forecast minus the actual after table P is -0.64 MW (old) and -0.61 MW (new) for wind, and +0.089 MW and +0.078 MW for solar a2_member. The median's mean absolute error for solar worsens (0.9662 to 0.9687 MW, +0.26%), which agrees with the score.
  • Audit conditions. The ratio-1 gates passed. Two conditions fire. The solar score moved the opposite way from the prediction and from experiment 453's re-scoring, and this page does not test the explanation that the capacity enters the training target. The leave-one-out test above fails the rule for every dropped series. A third condition may apply: the advice recommends adopting the wind rule without a replication.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Test a rolling capacity (for example the p99.9 of the last 12 months) for Solar A, Solar B, and Solar D.
  • Re-check wind at p99.9 with a weekly refit before any release claim.

docs.title: Can a lag network that sees the neighbours learn to follow a level change that no neighbour mirrors, when its training worlds contain genuine level changes?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the lag network that sees its neighbours (S3-amb) did not learn to follow a level change that no neighbour mirrors any better than the same network given random neighbours (S3-rw-amb), but the training worlds of this experiment could hardly have shown it. Even a perfect forecaster would follow only 0.05 to 0.08 more of a step without a mirror than with one, so the result is inconclusive by design and is not a refutation of attention over the lags. S3-amb loses nothing on rows with no labelled event against U1n-2, so the real-row checks pass, and it shows no gain that would justify adopting it. Every number is interim, from four test months and two seeds.

The experiment tests one hope: that a neural network given the neighbouring Primaries' surprise can learn to tell a genuine level change from a load shift. A load shift moves power from one Primary to its neighbours, so a jump in recent power that a neighbour mirrors with an opposite sign is a load shift, and the forecast target stays at the normal running arrangement. A jump that no neighbour mirrors may be a genuine level change, such as a new connection, and the target moves with it. In all earlier training worlds (experiments 402, 404, 440, and 446) the target stayed clean under every injected jump, so discounting every jump was optimal and a neighbour mirror carried no information. This experiment adds genuine level changes to the training worlds, where the lags and the target move together and no neighbour changes, and keeps every mirror in training a load shift. S3-amb is experiment 440's S3 network (the S1 lag network plus 24 own window statistics and 30 neighbour columns) trained on those worlds. S3-rw-amb is the same network with random neighbours that keep each Primary's number of neighbours. A pass would show only that a network can use a mirror when the training world makes the mirror informative. It would not be evidence about real Primaries, since no labelled genuine level change exists in the real data.

docs.title: How to read the numbers
docs.text:
The arms. S1 is the lag network: a neural network given three earlier readings of a Primary's power and the surprise at each reading. U1n-2 is S1 trained on the same ambiguous worlds as S3-amb and S3-rw-amb (experiment 446). R-inj is the lag network of experiment 428 that S1 improved on, and B-mix is the fixed mixture of two networks' forecast distributions from experiment 404. BG2 is the weekly-refitted XGBoost forecast of experiment 87, and manual_heuristic is the naive baseline forecast. A Primary is a primary substation, and NRA is the normal running arrangement of the electricity network (the switching state that the forecast targets). The Bayes-optimal share is the share of a step that a forecaster who knows the training worlds exactly should follow.

Unless a column says otherwise, every number is a score at days 1 to 10 after the 1.15 widening of the bands, in points of effective capacity, and a negative contrast favours the first arm. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score from the 11 quantiles. The signed-MW six are the Primaries metered in signed megawatts, and the MVA-only eight are metered in unsigned megavolt-amperes. The four test months are 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06, with seeds 0 and 1 and monthly refits. The Primaries D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01, and every score is on cleaned power. S1-amb of the plan is the stored U1n-2 of experiment 446, because the training worlds here are exactly U1n-2's (the generator reuses its events, and the checks in e00462_worlds.py selftest confirm that the training shifts are equal).

Row sets. Rows with no labelled event have recent power and target outside every logged event. They may still hold events that NGED never logged, so each such number is a lower bound on the effect of events. An injected harm row holds a simulated load shift (the target stays clean). A level-change row has a genuine level change in force at the newest lag, in held-out worlds 7 to 9 (seeds 500 to 502, drawn from the 3% held-out rate of experiment 446) that no training world shares. The level-change rows split by what a neighbour shows. No mirror: nothing changes at a neighbour. Mirrored: the Primary's change is mirrored at 1 or 2 neighbours with the load-conserving signature of experiment 402, so a neighbour sees what a load shift looks like. Received mirror: the Primary is itself the recipient of a neighbour's level change. A real harm row has a target outside every logged event but recent power inside one. Real event rows have their targets inside a logged event, scored against actuals corrected to the normal running arrangement.

Interim contrasts carry intervals from resampling test-month origin days. The registered pass needs more than the larger of 0.03 and the minimum detectable effect, which comes from the seed-0-against-seed-1 spread of S3-amb and S3-rw-amb (the table below). Six contrasts were registered (the Bonferroni count), so no single 95% interval here is a stand-alone claim.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows the registered pair contrast on every row set. S3-amb minus S3-rw-amb on level-change rows with no mirror is -0.055 (-0.133 to 0.010) at the MVA-only eight and +0.006 (-0.068 to 0.093) at the signed-MW six. The minimum detectable effects are 0.411 and 0.270, so both differences are far inside the margin of rule (a). On injected harm rows the difference is -0.003 (-0.017 to 0.011) at the eight and -0.034 (-0.049 to -0.020) at the six, and the minimum detectable effects are 0.104 and 0.114, so the six's gain is also inside the margin. Rule (a) fails.

Mirrored level changes are where S3-amb differs from S3-rw-amb, and S3-amb is worse there, but the difference is below the minimum detectable effect. On level changes mirrored at a neighbour, S3-amb scores 0.215 (0.104 to 0.328) points worse than S3-rw-amb at the eight and 0.239 (0.050 to 0.408) worse at the six, and 0.106 and 0.256 worse than U1n-2. A mirrored level change looks exactly like a load shift to the neighbours, and in training every mirror meant a load shift with a clean target. The minimum detectable effects for that row set are 0.603 (eight) and 0.401 (six), so the difference is suggestive and not detectable, and the interval ignores seed and fold variance. At the signed-MW six, three of four folds favour S3-amb (-0.013, -0.300, and -0.051), and the fold 2026-01 (+0.597) drives the sign. At the eight, the fold 2026-06 (+0.440) drives it. The reading that S3-amb discounts a mirrored jump as it was trained to, and misses a genuine step that happened to be mirrored, is a hypothesis these rows cannot confirm. On a received mirror, S3-amb beats S3-rw-amb by 0.069 (0.028 to 0.107) at the eight, below that row set's minimum detectable effect of 0.254, and differs by +0.010 (-0.067 to 0.062) at the six, so the direction does not repeat across the two metering groups. On level changes with no mirror, S3-amb beats U1n-2 by 0.128 (0.014 to 0.272) at the six, and S3-rw-amb beats it by 0.134, so that gain comes from having neighbour inputs, not from using a mirror. On real events at the signed-MW six, S3-rw-amb scores 0.211 lower than S3-amb (5.246 against 5.457).

Table 1: absolute CRPS (points of effective capacity, 1.15 widening, seeds 0 and 1).

Row set Group R-inj S1 U1n-2 S3-amb S3-rw-amb Rows with no labelled event signed-MW six 2.962 2.874 2.943 2.921 2.936 Rows with no labelled event MVA-only eight 3.654 3.574 3.582 3.564 3.559 Level change, no mirror signed-MW six 3.980 3.880 4.009 3.882 3.875 Level change, no mirror MVA-only eight 6.332 6.309 6.203 6.204 6.259 Level change, mirrored signed-MW six 5.561 5.607 5.329 5.585 5.346 Level change, mirrored MVA-only eight 6.761 6.983 6.703 6.810 6.595 Received mirror signed-MW six 4.039 4.086 4.013 4.089 4.080 Received mirror MVA-only eight 4.588 4.632 4.532 4.478 4.546 Injected harm rows signed-MW six 2.971 2.912 2.980 2.950 2.984 Injected harm rows MVA-only eight 4.159 4.094 4.113 4.092 4.094 Real harm rows signed-MW six 2.954 2.955 2.953 2.940 2.889 Real harm rows MVA-only eight 5.473 5.421 5.552 5.461 5.508 Real events (NRA actuals) signed-MW six 5.843 5.740 5.664 5.457 5.246 Real events (NRA actuals) MVA-only eight 7.479 7.238 7.289 7.133 7.009

Table 2: minimum detectable effect and the Bayes-optimal shares of the training worlds. The minimum detectable effect of the pair (1.96 times the square root of 2, times the seed standard deviation, divided by the square root of 2) is 0.101 (rows with no labelled event, MVA-only eight) and 0.167 (signed-MW six), 0.411 and 0.270 on level-change rows with no mirror, 0.603 and 0.401 on mirrored level changes, and 0.104 and 0.114 on injected harm rows. A forecaster that knows only whether the newest lag has a mirror should follow the shares below (target moved over rows, in 400,000 sampled fold rows of each training world, month 2026-01).

Lags in a jump (k) No mirror With a mirror Gap 1 0.081 0.028 0.054 2 0.102 0.035 0.067 3 0.118 0.043 0.075

The optimal gap is small because few jumps in the training worlds are genuine. A genuine level change covers about 2% of a Primary's half-hours, and most mirrors in these worlds are coincident load shifts of experiment 428's worlds at neighbours, not mirrors of a genuine change. A perfect learner would therefore follow only 0.054 to 0.075 more of a step without a mirror.

Predictions P1, P2, and P4 fail, and P3 is half right. P1 fails (S3-amb gains 0.006 in the wrong direction against the 0.03 asked, at the signed-MW six). P2 fails (the share followed is not lower with a mirror). P3 is half right: the shares without a mirror lie below 0.5, but the shares with a mirror are 0.028 to 0.043, below the 0.05 predicted. P4 fails: S3-amb does not cost 0.03 against U1n-2.

docs.title: Paired encroachment sweep
docs.text:
The sweep shows no lower share followed with a mirror for S3-amb, and a small gap of the wrong sign that its random-neighbour control shares. The sweep adds a step of 5% of the Primary's effective capacity to the first k lags of every row with no labelled event (k = 1, 2, 3: the newest reading, then the daily lag, then the weekly lag), once without a mirror and once with the load-conserving mirror at the Primary's first neighbour, and measures the share of the step that the median follows. The gap is the share without a mirror minus the share with one. The interval resamples the 8 (month, seed) blocks, so it is crude.
