  • Learned weight on the lagged forecast (mean over scored months). At the six signed-megawatt substations, G1-trust is 0.41 at 0-12 h, 0.43 at 12-36 h, 0.43 at 36-72 h, 0.40 at days 4-5, and 0.36 at days 6-10. G1-insample falls from 0.93 to 0.82, and B1 rises from 0.73 to 0.80. The range over months within a lead band is 0.18 to 0.24 for G1-trust (0.31 to 0.55 at 0-12 h), above the 0.1 stability rule, so seed 1 was not run. At the eight MVA-only substations, G1-trust falls from 0.52 to 0.45.
  • Training-row diagnostic. The weighted negative log-likelihood of the lagged forecast on the training rows is 0.83 to 0.92 out of fold and 0.19 to 0.24 in sample, against 0.71 to 0.97 for the cross-fitted lagless forecast. An out-of-fold neural network is therefore a much weaker forecast than the full-data one that scores the scored month.
  • Tails at the six signed-megawatt substations, no label. Coverage at q01, q05, q95, and q99 is 0.006, 0.029, 0.845, and 0.943 for G1-trust, and 0.006, 0.028, 0.855, and 0.949 for B-mix. The q99 pinball loss is 0.0027 and 0.0026. Inside real events, q99 coverage is 0.805 for G1-trust and 0.807 for B-mix. Every arm under-covers the upper tail (the nominal values are 0.95 and 0.99), and G1-trust is no different from B-mix. Curtailment cost does not apply in the 404 harness.
  • Predictions. P1 failed on level: the weight is 0.41 falling to 0.36, not 0.75 falling to 0.5; the monthly swing is 0.18 to 0.24 (at least 0.2 in 2 of 5 lead bands). P2 half held: the real-event contrast is inside the minimum detectable effect, but its interval excludes zero, and the no-label contrast (-0.021) is just outside the predicted 0.00 to +0.10. P3 held (-0.158 within -0.05 to -0.30). P4 held.
  • Fit count and time. 40 fits: 30 out-of-fold lagged-forecast fits at about 14 s each and 10 trust fits at about 7 to 12 minutes each, about 1 hour 50 minutes on one GPU process under 8 GB.
  • Where the code and outputs are. The code is in ml-experiments/00463-lag-trust-cross-fitted-trust-fit-seed-zero/. It reuses the modules of experiment 404 and of experiments 87, 48, and 397, and the scoring pattern of experiments 455 and
  • Forecasts and trust networks are in the experiment's private data folder. The 30 out-of-fold networks are not kept; their out-of-fold forecasts are, as oof_<month>_s0.npy. Retraining is monthly. The cleaned data and the D15 and D18 cut are inherited from experiment 404's rows.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site. This check is not available because the 404 harness stores 11 quantiles and no mean forecast. The error of the median forecast is reported instead.
  • Error of the median beside the score contrasts. G1-trust minus B-mix, mean absolute error of the q50 forecast (fraction of capacity): +0.0002 (no label), -0.0011 (harm), and +0.0005 (real event) at the six signed-megawatt substations, and +0.0008, +0.0019, and -0.0008 at the eight MVA-only substations. One point of score is 0.005 of capacity at q50 (the pinball loss at q50 is half the absolute error), so +0.0002 is about +0.02 points. The no-label score contrast is slightly negative (-0.021) while the median error is slightly positive; both lie inside their noise.
  • Trigger that fired. Audit trigger 2 (a result that contradicts its prediction and an earlier experiment) fired: the learned weight of 0.41 falling to 0.36 contradicts the prediction (0.75 falling to 0.5) and experiment 458's fitted weights. Triggers 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 did not fire.
  • What the audit confirmed. A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived every headline contrast from the stored forecasts and matched the printed values to three decimals. It found no leakage, and found the low weight consistent with an out-of-fold lagged forecast weaker than the full-data one.
  • What the audit qualified. The best constant weight on the scored months is 0.6 falling to 0.4 at the six signed-megawatt substations, above the learned weight; that gap lowers the score by 0.03 to 0.08 points. Training on five sixths of the rows is one of three candidate causes: the fold also removes a four-month season, and the full network memorises its training rows.
  • Caveats the audit adds. The lagless forecast has the same mismatch between its cross-fitted and full-data versions; this has not been tested. The trust trains on the injected world (4.6% of half-hours carry an injected event) and is scored on real power. The weight is fitted by negative log-likelihood and scored by pinball loss, so the fitted weight need not be the weight that minimises the score.

docs.title: What it rules out and what to try next
docs.text:
• What it rules out. Experiment 404's in-sample fit is no longer a reason for a learned trust to lose to 50/50 on rows with no labelled event, because fitting out of fold removes that loss. A learned combination weight is not an improvement over 50/50 in this harness.
  • What could be tested next. A finer fold split (12 folds or interleaved weeks) and a lagged forecast evaluated on the scored month would show whether the remaining gap closes. B1's NRA-corrected result inside events (-0.63, interval spanning zero) is the only sign we found of a gain from a learned weight there. Otherwise the fixed 50/50 mixture stays.

docs.title: Does multiplying the stored solar forecasts by each farm's recent efficiency, the ratio of actual power to the power the observed weather should have produced, lower the quantile score?
docs.text:
Scaling the stored solar forecasts by each farm's recent efficiency did not lower the score at any farm, so slow efficiency change is not what limits the forecast. The test used the stored a2_member forecasts of experiment 430 only. The best of 18 scaling methods lowered Solar C's mean quantile score by 0.46% and raised Solar A, B, and D by 0.3% to 2.0%. The efficiency itself does vary: the 56-day trailing ratio at Solar A fell to about 0.8 of its earlier average for several months and then recovered (figure 2). The ratio's swings do not line up with the forecast's monthly bias (correlation +0.04, figure 3). What this narrows: the remaining error is mostly weather error, and a long history of the ratio is unlikely to add to it.

Question and method. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) meters six solar farms, labelled Solar A to Solar F here. Efficiency is the farm's actual power divided by the power the observed weather should have produced. This page reports stage 0 of a four-stage line that would feed the efficiency to the neural network as an input (stages 1 to 4); stage 0 asks the cheapest version of the question. Each day gets one ratio, and a trailing median, an exponentially weighted level, or a Kalman filter turns the days into one multiplier at the forecast origin. The multiplier is normalised: it is divided by the farm's median ratio over all days before the refit, because the stored neural network already learned the farm's average efficiency. A raw multiplier skips that division. The experiment multiplied the quantiles of experiment 430's stored a2_member forecast by the multiplier (no neural network refitted) and compared the quantile score with the unscaled forecast over the 12 scored months. The quantile score is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity; lower is better.

Three sources of expected power were used. Source (a) is an XGBoost model of power on observed weather that saw the scored quarter, so it is not causal. Source (b) is a clear-sky proxy: the farm's clear-sky power times a constant. Source (c) is the same XGBoost model trained on earlier quarters only. Sources (b) and (c) are causal. Arm names read network|source|method|multiplier|lag: for example a2_member|c|med14|norm|lag2 is the 14-day trailing median of source (c), normalised, with the newest day two days before the origin. ew14 is an exponentially weighted level with a 14-day half-life, kalman is the filter, and g0_onepass is experiment 430's other stored forecast, used as a replication.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• The prediction failed and the line stops. A gain means an interval below zero and a point estimate below -1% against the unscaled forecast. The prediction was a gain of more than 1% at Solar A, B, and D and under 1% elsewhere. No primary arm gains significantly at any farm, so the verdict is not supported.
  • Every point estimate is above -1%. Lowest change in the mean quantile score per farm over days 1 to 10 for the 18 primary arms (a2_member, sources (b) and (c), 2-day lag, normalised): Solar A +0.34%, Solar B +0.54%, Solar C -0.46%, Solar D +0.08%, Solar E -0.01%, and Solar F -0.03%. The lowest group means are {Solar A, B, D} +0.85% (c|ew14) and {Solar C, E, F} +0.28% (c|med112). Source (b), the clear-sky proxy, is worse at every farm: +0.4% to +4.6% at the best method per farm, and up to +24% at the worst.
  • The intervals are wide because single months dominate. Two consecutive scored months at Solar A change by -18.5% and +18.8% when scaled. The 12 months are resampled as blocks, so Solar A's interval swings by about 9 points. Solar C has one month of -8.6%. Both are month-level outliers of the multiplier, not a code fault.
  • Only Solar B, D, and F rule out a 1% gain. The Bonferroni intervals are widened so that all 108 contrasts hold together at 95%. On c|med14 their half-widths are 8.4%, 2.7%, 3.0%, 1.9%, 2.3%, and 1.4% for Solar A to F. An interval rules out a 1% gain when its lower bound is above -1%: Solar B (-0.46%), Solar D (-0.94%), and Solar F (-0.40%). At Solar A, C, and E the interval is too wide to rule it out, so the verdict rests on every point estimate being above -1%.
  • Secondary arms give the same picture. The 6-day lag, source (a), the raw multiplier, and the g0_onepass forecast have lowest changes of -0.05%, -0.18%, -0.33%, and -0.73% (Solar C on g0_onepass|c|med14).
  • Day 1 (12 to 36 hours) is the one place a later stage could look. The lowest point estimate is at Solar A (-4.8% for c|med14), with an interval of -25% to +3%. Day 1 is not a primary contrast and is not a finding.
  • The 0.99 quantile gets worse. On a2_member|c|med14 the 0.99 pinball loss rises at every farm (+0.012 to +0.127 points). It exceeds the 0.02 limit at Solar A (+0.127), Solar C (+0.035), Solar D (+0.057), and Solar E (+0.054). The 0.99 coverage falls from 97.5% to 95.7% at Solar A and from 99.4% to 97.6% at Solar C.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Missing multipliers. Source (c) is missing at 0% to 3% of origins at Solar A to D and F and 20.8% at Solar E. Source (b), averaged over the nine methods, is missing at 25% to 27% of origins at Solar A to D and F and 41% at Solar E, and at 48% to 55% (76% at Solar E) for the longest window. Missing multipliers bias source (b) toward no effect but cannot explain a loss of up to 24%.
  • Clipping. 1% to 11% of scaled 0.99 quantiles hit the cap (the largest q99 of that farm and refit).
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile score (a2_member|c|med14, mean absolute error in points of capacity, unscaled to scaled): Solar A 12.61 to 12.84, B 13.22 to 13.23, C 12.17 to 12.25, D 14.78 to 14.71, E 14.44 to 14.47, F 12.64 to 12.69.
  • Seeds. Three seeds, averaged quantile by quantile, in every arm.
  • Cleaning. Stuck runs, daylight zeros, spikes above 1.5 of capacity, and curtailment-flat days are dropped from the ratio; days whose ratio was exactly 0 are treated as missing.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Source (a) saw the scored quarter's power, so it is not causal; sources (b) and (c) are.
  • Source (c)'s XGBoost model for a farm's first four year-quarters is leave-one-quarter-out within that year.
  • Source (b) takes its ratio from near-clear half-hours and applies it to all-sky forecasts.
  • The multiplier assumes observed weather and power reach the service two days after the day ends; ERA5 arrives about 5 days late, and the 6-day lag arms are within 0.05% of the best.
  • The stored forecasts cover only the scored year, so the efficiency-versus-bias check has 70 farm months.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Look for the forecast's remaining error in the weather forecast itself, for example at the irradiance forecast's spread and bias by sky type.
  • If stage 1 is ever run, restrict it to Solar A on the day-ahead band, the only place a point estimate (-4.8%) was visibly below zero.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• Plan review: a fresh Sonnet agent made 13 review comments; all were accepted or folded in (forward-only source (c), per-farm primary contrasts, Bonferroni correction over 108 contrasts, 6-day lag arms, defined Kalman multiplier).
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet agent found two critical bugs (zero daily ratios made the exponential and Kalman methods NaN at four farms; a duplicate band column in the aggregation) and five lower-severity points; all were fixed before the scoring run.
  • Results review: a fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline numbers from the raw forecasts with its own code. It averaged six seeds where this page averages three, so per-farm changes differ by up to 0.5 points (Solar A +0.9% against +0.3%), and the signs agree for Solar C (-0.6%) and Solar E (+0.9%). It found no lookahead and no clipped multiplier.
  • Write-up review: a fresh Sonnet agent corrected eight numbers and one logic error (which farms' intervals rule out a 1% gain), and asked for terms to be defined earlier; all were applied.

docs.title: Do the median of the last 7 same-time-of-day readings and of the last 3 same-time-of-week readings, in place of the day and week power lags, make the XGBoost demand forecast far less sensitive to a load-shift event that lasts under 7 days?
docs.text:
Median day and week lags make the median forecast 20% to 50% less sensitive to a step in the last 1 to 3 days of power, but not more accurate. The shielding shrinks as the event lengthens and is gone at 7 days. A stuck meter is shielded almost completely, but a dropout to zero and a spike are not. The clean-row loss against the original lags is +0.050 points of capacity at the six Primaries metered in signed megawatts. Two fits of the original lags differ by 0.06, so the loss is not separable from fit-to-fit noise. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold unlogged events, and every real-event slice undercounts. Every number is interim and unaudited.

Figures 4 and 5 show a day-ahead and a fourteen-day forecast with no labelled event, and figures 6 to 9 show forecasts issued 12 hours or more before a labelled event (labels D3, D12, D14, and D19 are anonymised Primary labels).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are CRPS-like pinball loss in points of effective capacity; a contrast is the first arm minus the second, so negative favours the first. Arms: (a) the original lags (experiment 402), (b) the lagless forecast (experiment 392), (c) the median lags, (e) the 50/50 mixture of the probability distributions of (c) and (b), (f) the 50/50 mixture of (a) and (b). The signed-MW six are the 6 Primaries metered in signed megawatts (D5, D10, D11, D14, D16, D9); the MVA-only eight are the 8 metered only in megavolt-amperes. Months are the resampling unit (4 scored months, 3 with labelled events). Every interval below is a month-block interval at the Bonferroni level of 99.72% for the 18 pre-registered contrasts (a 95% level would be narrower); all are in contrasts.csv.

  • Speed. The 64 fits of arm (c) took 6,442 s on 6 CPU cores, including the median feature build.
  • Sweep share at 24-72 h leads, step 5% of capacity (figure 2). At the signed-MW six, for an event of 24, 48, and 72 hours, arm (c) moves the median forecast by 0.081, 0.109, and 0.153 of the step, against 0.171, 0.192, and 0.192 for (a). At 5 and 7 days the shares are 0.289 and 0.384 for (c), 0.308 and 0.427 for (a). At the MVA-only eight the shares for 24, 48, and 72 hours are 0.113, 0.144, and 0.184 for (c) against 0.213, 0.236, and 0.236, and at 7 days 0.403 against 0.422. The lagless control moves by exactly 0. A step of 2.5% gives shares within 0.02 of these.
  • Very short events leak more. At an event of 6 hours, (c) leaks 0.058 against 0.036 for (a) at the six, because the origin lag, which the median leaves single, carries more weight in (c). Moving the origin lag alone by 5% moves the median by 0.054 of the step in (c) against 0.006 in (a) at the six, and 0.087 against 0.043 at the MVA-only eight.
  • Band width and coverage. The 5% to 95% band width does not change with the injected step in any arm (ratio 0.996 to 1.003). Clean-row coverage of the 5-95 band is 0.853 for (c) and 0.863 for (a) at the six for an event of 48 hours, and 0.898 and 0.906 at a widening of 1.15. Event-row coverage is 0.722 for (c) and 0.764 for (a) at 48 hours, and 0.785 and 0.825 at 1.15.
  • Bad data, mean shift of the median, signed-MW six, lead 24-72 h (points of capacity). Stuck 24 h: -0.036 for (c), -2.308 for (a). Dropout to zero for 6 h: +1.141 for (c), +0.926 for (a). Spike x20: +4.340 and +3.192. Spike x4: +2.706 and +1.616. The median shields a stuck meter but not a dropout or a spike, because a single bad reading at the origin lag passes straight through.
  • Level change (5% of capacity for 30 days). The median forecast follows the new level slowly at first and further later: 0.310 of the step by day 6, 0.511 by day 24, 0.562 by day 30 for (c) at the six, against 0.373, 0.456, and 0.490 for (a).
  • Clean rows, signed-MW six (rows with no labelled event, lead 0-240 h). (c) minus (a) is +0.050 [-0.004, +0.087], with 3 of 4 months worse. (c) minus (b) is -0.101 [-0.285, +0.159]. (c) minus (f) is +0.082 [-0.002, +0.220]. (e) minus (f) is +0.014 [-0.008, +0.045]. The early stop rule (clean-row loss of 0.10 or more) does not fire.
  • Noise floor. Refitting arm (a) on CPU with this experiment's settings and scoring it against experiment 402's stored forecast on the 2026-01 refit month, over all rows, gives a difference of -0.060 at the six and +0.002 at the MVA-only eight. The CPU refit of (a) scored better than the stored (a), so a contrast of (c) against a CPU-fitted (a) could be about +0.11 at the six, which is at the stop limit of 0.10. This is one month and one refit, so it indicates the size of the noise and does not bound it.
  • Harm rows (during a labelled event), signed-MW six. (c) minus (a) is -0.207 [-0.219, +0.827], 1 of 3 months worse. (c) minus (f) is -0.769 [-1.001, +0.304]. (e) minus (a) is +0.588 [+0.575, +0.971], 3 of 3 months worse. No arm beats (a) with an interval that excludes zero (the prediction P3 required -0.1 with an interval excluding zero).
  • Harm rows, MVA-only eight. (c) minus (a) is +0.690 [+0.050, +0.970], 3 of 3 months worse, and (e) minus (a) is -1.423 [-1.911, -0.248], 0 of 3 months worse. The groups disagree in sign.
  • After a labelled event ends (days 7 on), signed-MW six. (c) minus (a) is +0.194 [-0.188, +0.345]. (c) minus (f) is +0.852 [+0.111, +1.232], 3 of 3 months worse. At the MVA-only eight, (c) minus (a) is -0.123 [-0.358, -0.007].
  • Avoidable curtailment cost (widening 1.15, units of the cost report). On the three Primaries with event rows, (a) 3.394e6, (b) 2.152e6, (c) 3.422e6, (e) 2.374e6, (f) 2.218e6. Over all rows at the six, (a) 4.507e7, (b) 5.615e7, (c) 4.660e7, (e) 4.602e7, (f) 4.526e7. Arm (c) costs slightly more than (a) in both.
  • 12-36 h lead band, (c) minus (a). Signed-MW six: clean rows +0.030 [-0.006, +0.064], harm rows -0.188 [-0.221, +0.814], after the event +0.371 [+0.019, +0.713]. MVA-only eight: clean rows +0.015 [-0.040, +0.063], harm rows +0.789 [-0.039, +1.114]. The signs match the 0-240 h band.
  • Predictions. P1 holds for the leak of events up to 48 hours: 0.081 to 0.109 at 24 to 72 hour leads, under 0.15, rising to 0.384 at 7 days. The plan's baseline for (a) of 0.38 to 0.41 came from experiment 392's column-level sweep (a step in all three lags) and matches only (a)'s share at 7 days (0.427); for events up to 48 hours, (a) leaks 0.17 to 0.19. P2 holds on the rounding edge: +0.0498 against the limit of +0.05, and the noise-floor control suggests the fair figure may be nearer +0.11. P3 fails: harm rows show no gain with an interval excluding zero at the six, and (c) is worse at the MVA-only eight. P4 narrowly fails: the origin lag alone moves arm (c) by 0.054 at 24 to 72 h at the six (predicted 0.01 to 0.05), and by 0.087 at the MVA-only eight.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per site was not computed, because the stored tables hold quantiles and no mean forecast. The robust lags assert the leakage rule of origin_lags. The noise-floor difference (-0.060 at the six) is of the same size as the clean-row loss, so the clean-row loss is reported as not separable from noise. The harm-row contrast changes sign between the two groups, so no pooled claim is made. The leave-one-Primary-out check was not run.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Events longer than 7 days defeat any 7-day median. At 7 days the share is 0.37 to 0.40.
  • The median follows a genuine level change more slowly early. Arm (c) reaches 0.31 of a persistent step by day 6 against 0.37 for (a), then overtakes (a) (figure 3).
  • Unlogged events. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold events, and harm-row counts are lower bounds.
  • CPU against GPU. The fits ran on CPU and experiment 402's on CUDA. The noise-floor control differs by 0.06 at the six, from one month and one refit.
  • Three event months and 18 contrasts. The Bonferroni family is 18 contrasts. The (c) minus (e) contrasts are descriptive.
  • Not run. Arm (d) (robust plus original lags, demoted by the brief), the cold-night rows, the NRA-corrected actuals of experiment 455, and the CRPS at widenings 1.05 and 1.10.
  • Production options for a missing or stale day. If a day of power is missing, the 7-reading median can use the remaining readings, as the fit does, or fall back to the lagless forecast. This page describes the options and leaves the choice to the maintainer.

docs.title: Does weighting recent training rows more raise the quantile score of the wind and solar networks?
docs.text:
Take-home: weighting recent training rows more does not improve the wind or solar forecasts, so the line closes. The wind neural network scores 0.22% to 0.25% worse with half-lives of 9 and 4.5 months. The best solar arm gains 0.14%, which is less than the difference between two fits of the same network and a seventh of the 1% margin.

Farms change efficiency slowly, and each upgrade of the ECMWF ensemble shifts the statistics of the inputs, so recent rows might train a better network. We multiplied each training row's loss by 0.5 ** (age / half_life) and refitted the wind neural network member_plain and the solar neural networks g0_onepass and a2_member at the p99.9 capacity of experiment 461. Farm A to C and Solar A to F are the anonymised series of experiments 429 and 430. The training history is 12.5 months for wind and 17 to 26 months for solar, so only the shorter half-lives differ much from equal weights.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Contrasts are arm minus the equal-weight reference in MW after table P (a per-series tail correction) and experiment 451's clip (an upper bound), pooled over a technology's series, so a positive change is worse. Rows are the half-hours at true days 1 to 10 (lead 24 to 240 hours) that experiment 210's mask keeps for wind, and all scored half-hours for solar. Intervals are 95% month-block bootstrap intervals over 11 scored months.

  • No arm passes. The margin is 1% of the pooled reference score for solar (about 0.0067 MW) and 0.10 points of capacity for wind. The best arm gains 0.0009 MW.
  • Wind member_plain (5 seeds, reference 1.1744 MW). Half-life 9 months: +0.0026 MW (+0.22%; -0.0008 to +0.0060), better in 3 of 11 months. Half-life 4.5 months: +0.0029 MW (+0.25%; -0.0033 to +0.0088), better in 5 of 11 months. Per farm, 9 months: Farm A +0.15%, Farm B +0.44%, Farm C -0.01%.
  • Solar g0_onepass (3 seeds, 4 refits, reference 0.6655 MW). Half-life 0.5 year: +0.11% (-0.0024 to +0.0039 MW). At 1 year: -0.04% (-0.0032 to +0.0020). At 2 years: -0.14% (-0.0024 to +0.0005), better in 7 of 11 months. At 3 years: -0.14% (-0.0020 to +0.0002), better in 7 of 11 months. At 2 years, Solar C is the one series whose 95% interval excludes zero in the favourable direction (2 years: -0.20%, -0.0028 to -0.0001 MW, better in 9 of 11 months), and its adjusted interval does not.
  • Solar a2_member (reference 0.6627 MW). At 2 years: +0.17% (-0.0010 to +0.0032 MW). At 3 years: +0.14% (-0.0005 to +0.0030). Solar B at 2 years is +0.32% worse with an interval that excludes zero (+0.0004 to +0.0043 MW).
  • Minimum detectable effect (mean gap between two single-seed fits of the reference, stated before any arm was scored): wind 0.0077 MW, g0_onepass 0.0050 MW, a2_member 0.0036 MW. Every pooled contrast is smaller than the wind and g0_onepass values.
  • Cycle 49r1 indicator (diagnostic, g0_onepass). Pooled +0.01% (-0.0023 to +0.0025 MW). Solar A improves 0.36% in 9 of 11 months (-0.0036 to +0.0002 MW), and Solar E worsens 0.20%. The indicator has no training signal for Cycle 50r1, and the indicator is not adopted.
  • Tails after table P, pooled. Coverage is the share of actuals at or below the quantile. Wind, equal weights to 9 months: share above q99 0.88% to 0.86%; q95 coverage 95.13% for both; q99 pinball loss 0.0641 to 0.0643 MW. Wind at 4.5 months: share above q99 0.94%, q99 pinball 0.0646 MW. Solar g0_onepass, equal weights to 2 years: share above q99 1.41% to 1.37%; q95 coverage 94.58% to 94.82%; q99 pinball loss 0.0247 for both. a2_member equal weights to 3 years: share above q99 1.50% to 1.48%. No half-life arm changes a pooled tail coverage by more than 0.4 points or a pinball loss by more than 0.0009 (wind q95 at 9 months); the Cycle 49r1 indicator moves g0_onepass q95 coverage by 0.65 points.
  • Bonferroni count. 57 intervals (arms times pooled and per series); at the adjusted level no contrast excludes zero in the favourable direction.
  • Rows and seeds. Equal across arms: wind 54,899 half-hours (Farm A 18,831, B 18,403, C 17,665); solar 345,510 half-hours per arm (A 60,210, B 60,039, C 60,885, D 54,864, E 49,770, F 59,742). Wind 5 seeds; solar 3.
  • The 12 to 36 hour band. The scored rows start at lead 24 hours, so the band holds only leads 24 to 36 hours (wind 3,361 half-hours, solar 18,014). The scores for that band were not separated, because no pooled contrast is near the margin.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Reproduction gates. With all weights 1 the wind fit (seed 0) and the solar g0_onepass fit (seed 0, refit 2025-09) reproduce experiment 461's stored forecasts bit for bit. The four other wind reference seeds are copies of experiment 461's p99.9 fits.
  • Short history. Wind trains on 12.5 months, so a half-life of 3 years or 1.5 years is nearly equal weighting, and those arms were dropped. A training window that starts after Cycle 49r1 was not tested, because it leaves 5 months of wind rows and 10 to 19 months of solar rows. Cycle 50r1 (2026-05-12) falls inside the scored months, and no month's contrast shows a step there (figure 2); the figures do not mark it.
  • Scored years. Wind spans 2025-08 to 2026-06 and solar 2025-10 to 2026-08, so the contrast by month stands in for the contrast by year.
  • Experiment 443's p99 forecasts are not reused. Experiment 443's 0.5-year and 1-year arms were refitted at p99.9 here, and agree with its p99 result: neither gains.
  • Cleaned-zero rescore. Experiment 432's cleaned-zero row set was not scored for wind.
  • Production cost. None for a half-life, which is a training-time weight. An indicator would need a retrain at each ECMWF cycle.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewed the code before the first fit and found no defect; it asked for three low items (a stale docstring, a check on unknown labels, and an assertion), all fixed.
  • Median bias. The pooled mean of the median forecast minus the actual after table P is -0.614 MW for wind with equal weights and with 9 months, and +0.115 MW (equal weights) and +0.109 MW (3 years) for g0_onepass, so the bias does not drive any contrast.
  • Audit triggers. None fired: no contrast is near the margin, so no audit was run.

docs.title: Does a small lag-correction network, penalised towards zero on top of the frozen lagless forecast, match the lagless forecast where the lags are wrong and improve on it where they are fresh?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead the lagless anchor is stronger than a forecast made at the origin can be, so the gain of the lag correction over its anchor is understated there, and the gaps to B-mix and K2-S1 are not valid forecasts. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

A forecast made without recent power readings (the lagless forecast), plus a small correction that reads those readings, beats the lagless forecast alone and B-mix on rows with no labelled event. It does not help inside real events. A lag is a power reading available at the forecast origin: the newest one, and the readings at the same time on an earlier day and in an earlier week. B-mix is the fixed 50/50 mixture of the lagless forecast and a neural network that reads the lags. The correction is a neural network with one hidden layer of 32 units. It reads the three lags, the surprise at each lag (the lag minus the lagless median), and the lead time. It shifts and rescales the lagless mixture, and its last layer starts at zero, so it begins as the lagless forecast. The penalty on its outputs (1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, and 1) never limited them, so all four penalties give nearly the same forecast. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold real events that nobody logged. NRA means normal running arrangement. Every number is interim and unaudited. The scores on rows with no labelled event measure forecast quality, and the scores inside real events measure robustness to wrong lags.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are points of effective capacity (CRPS, lower is better), raw quantiles, metered actuals unless stated, and the mean over 5 scored months and fit seeds 0 and 1. Intervals are 95% month-block intervals. Experiment 454's minimum detectable effect at the signed-MW six is 0.24 on rows with no labelled event and 0.38 inside events.

  • Arms. LL is the lagless forecast alone (the anchor). C1e-3, C1e-2, C1e-1 (penalty on the squared outputs), C1 (penalty 1, post hoc), and Z1e-2 (post hoc control: the same network with the lag and surprise inputs set to zero, leaving the lead features). References: LL, B-mix, S1 (a neural network that reads the lags and the surprise at each lag), S1-mix (S1 mixed 50/50 with LL), and A0-inj (a neural network that reads the lags only).
  • Relation to A0-inj. A0-inj has no lagless input and re-learns the weather response. The correction sits on the frozen anchor, and the correction is the only new part.
  • Signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event.
    • C1e-2 3.212, C1 3.206, C1e-1 3.205, C1e-3 3.212, Z1e-2 3.611, LL 3.708, B-mix 3.498, S1-mix 3.435, S1 3.736, A0-inj 3.851.
    • C1e-2 minus LL -0.496 (-0.865 to -0.254, 5 of 5 months); minus B-mix -0.286 (-0.807 to +0.195, 4 of 5 months). By month against B-mix: -0.01, +0.25, -0.87, -0.55, -0.24 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). Leaving out 2026-01 leaves -0.14; leaving out 2025-12 leaves -0.42.
    • Z1e-2 minus LL -0.097 (-0.200 to -0.019): recalibrating the spread by lead time gains 0.10, and the lags gain a further 0.40.
  • Signed-MW six, inside real events. On metered actuals C1e-2 is 5.440 against 6.158 for LL and 5.932 for B-mix. On NRA-corrected actuals (the headline for events) C1e-2 is 14.864 against 14.822 for LL (+0.042, -0.509 to +0.911), 14.641 for B-mix (+0.223, -0.259 to +1.127), and 14.543 for Z1e-2. The lags carry the level shift of the temporary running arrangement, so they stop helping once the target is the normal running arrangement.
  • MVA-only eight. Rows with no labelled event: C1e-2 4.179, LL 4.523, B-mix 4.349, Z1e-2 4.498. Metered inside events: C1e-2 7.800, B-mix 7.607 (+0.194, -0.547 to +0.793). NRA events: C1e-2 10.101, B-mix 10.603 (-0.502, -0.666 to -0.332).
  • Lead band 12 to 36 hours. Signed-MW six, no labelled event: C1e-2 2.995, LL 3.654, B-mix 3.392 (-0.397, -0.812 to -0.139). NRA events: C1e-2 15.423 against LL 15.189 and B-mix 15.081.
  • Tail calibration (signed-MW six, no labelled event, raw). Coverage at q95 and q99: C1e-2 0.946 and 0.989, LL 0.839 and 0.943, B-mix 0.858 and 0.951, Z1e-2 0.926 and 0.986. Pinball loss at q95 and q99: C1e-2 0.00698 and 0.00204, B-mix 0.00842 and 0.00254. After the table-P recalibration (4 months, because it is fitted on earlier months) the CRPS is 3.327 (C1e-2), 3.674 (B-mix), 3.878 (LL), 3.769 (Z1e-2). Much of the gain over B-mix is the upper tail of the anchor being under-dispersed, and Z1e-2 also fixes part of this under-dispersion.
  • Stop rule. The stop rule did not fire: the share of rows with a shift below 0.01 of capacity is 0.29 at the signed-MW six for penalties 1e-3 to 1e-1 and 0.32 at penalty 1. The mean log-scale change is +0.16 to +0.26, so the correction widens the anchor.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost (experiment 449's cost, millions of pounds, signed-MW six, fit seeds 0 and 1, widened by 1.15; interval from resampling month-by-Primary cells). At f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5: C1e-2 2.23, 8.08, 24.4; B-mix 2.08, 9.20, 28.7; LL 2.34, 10.15, 30.2; manual_heuristic 2.02, 12.9, 37.8; BG2 1.37, 8.24, 25.9. C1e-2 minus manual_heuristic is -13.4 (-26.6 to -3.0) at f = 0.5, and C1e-2 minus Z1e-2 is -3.3 (-5.8 to -1.5) at f = 0.5. The other contrasts at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5 include zero.
  • Decision rule. C1e-2 passes the first part at the signed-MW six: it beats the anchor on rows with no labelled event by more than the larger of 0.03 and the minimum detectable effect (0.24). It fails the second and third parts, the real-event gate on NRA-corrected actuals: +0.042 against LL (limit 0.03) and +0.223 against B-mix (limit 0.03). Verdict: partly supported.
  • Fits. 50 correction fits of 16 to 28 s each (30 pre-registered, 20 post hoc), one GPU process under 8 GB, monthly retraining, about 25 minutes in total. The networks are saved under data/ml-experiments/00467-*/work/models/.
  • Rows and reuse. Experiment 404's rows and injected worlds (training worlds 100 and 101); scoring on the real world only (stored B-mix, LL, S1, S1-mix, and A0-inj of experiment 454 exist for it). Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped; the start cut applies to D15 and D18, which are report-only.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewer found no leakage in the code and corrected the plan's seed notes. The second reviewer reproduced the headline numbers independently and asked for the control with the lag inputs zeroed (Z1e-2) and for a penalty that binds (C1), both added and labelled post hoc.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers. Trigger 2 fired: the result contradicts the prediction that C1e-2 stays behind B-mix on rows with no labelled event. Triggers 3 and 4 did not fire. An audit by a fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline from the stored forecasts, and each finding is triaged below.
  • Median and mean forecast error beside the quantile score (signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event, C1e-2 minus reference, points of capacity; the audit averaged all 3 stored seeds of LL and B-mix, so its CRPS differs from this page's by up to 0.05). Against LL: CRPS -0.55, median error -0.77, mean error -0.74. Against B-mix: CRPS -0.30, median error -0.35, mean error -0.43. The signs agree in every month against LL and in every month except 2025-10 and 2025-12 against B-mix, where C1e-2 trails slightly on all three measures.
  • Median minus mean forecast per Primary. C1e-2 tracks LL within 0.06 points at every one of the six Primaries, so the correction does not shift the median away from the mean. B-mix differs at D11 (-0.75 against +0.14 to +0.17) and D5 (-0.38 against -0.16 to -0.21).
  • Bias. The mean of actual minus median is positive at five of the six Primaries for every arm (the forecasts are low). C1e-2 roughly halves the mean absolute bias (1.30 points against 2.55 for LL and 2.50 for B-mix), and Z1e-2 only reduces it to 2.17. Much of the lag gain is therefore a level correction.
  • Leave one Primary out keeps the sign: C1e-2 minus LL stays between -0.38 and -0.66, and C1e-2 minus B-mix between -0.11 (D14 left out) and -0.46. D14 carries most of the gain over B-mix, and without it the margin falls below the minimum detectable effect of 0.24. D11 is the one Primary where C1e-2 is worse than B-mix (+0.40), and the gap grows with lead time.
  • By lead band and hour. C1e-2 beats B-mix in each lead band pooled (-0.25 to -0.39) and in all 24 hours of the day. It trails B-mix in three month-by-band cells: 2025-12 at 36 to 120 hours (+0.06) and at 120 to 240 hours (+0.36), and 2025-10 at 120 to 240 hours (+0.14).

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• The penalty sweep is uninformative. At 1e-3 to 1 the L2 penalty shrinks the outputs by under 5%, so it does not separate the arms. A penalty of 10 or more, or a per-row penalty that is larger inside events, is the next test.
  • The Bonferroni count is 15 per reference in the contrast tables (5 arms times 3 row classes); the pre-registered count was 9 (3 penalties times 3 row classes). No gain in this page is claimed at the 99% level.
  • Not done: the drop-largest-event interval, leave-one-Primary-out (infeasible with 21 events at the six), and the wind and solar versions (they need the stored member_plain and g0_onepass heads in their own harnesses). The demand version passes the no-labelled-event gate only, so the manager decides whether to run them.
  • Porting. It would need one lagless neural network plus a 32-unit correction, instead of the two neural networks that B-mix needs.

docs.title: How do the best wind, solar, and demand forecasters behave hour by hour and event by event, and where do they fail?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

Take-home. Over a year, the wind and solar forecasts that experiment 461 selected have tails close to the shares expected of a perfectly calibrated forecast. Single months miss, and the demand forecasts that read lagged power are not reliably better than the forecast that does not during real events.

We asked where the selected wind, solar, and demand forecasts fail, by plotting stored forecasts against what happened. Nothing was fitted. Part A covers wind and solar. Part B covers Primary substation demand during real events, where an event is a labelled load shift or a level step found by a scan. The injected-shift half of Part B is not done.

Part A uses experiment 461's stored forecasts. Wind is member_plain, a neural network whose effective capacity is the 99.9th percentile of earlier power, at the three metered wind farms Farm A, B, and C. Solar is a2_member at the two metered solar farms Solar A and B, at the old capacity rule (the 99th percentile of the whole power record). Experiment 461 did not adopt the new capacity rule for Solar A. Table P is a table of factors, one per farm, lead band, and tail level, that moves the tail quantiles towards or away from the median. The factors are fitted on earlier months only. The time-series charts of these generators carry megawatts and stay in the private store (data/ml-experiments/00468-.../part_a/). This page shows only charts without a generator time series.

Part B uses experiment 454's stored demand forecasts. All four are neural networks. The lagless forecast does not read recent power. S1 reads three lagged power readings and their distance from the lagless forecast. B-mix is a fixed 50/50 mixture of a lagged forecast and a lagless forecast. K2-S1 mixes two S1 forecasts with two lagless forecasts. Quantile names such as q99 mean the forecast quantile at that level; the share above q99 is the share of actuals above it, and 1% is the share a calibrated forecast gives.

docs.title: Part A: wind and solar
docs.text:
• Pooled over the year the tails are near nominal. After table P, the share above q99 is 0.95% at Farm A, 0.79% at Farm B, 0.90% at Farm C, 1.69% at Solar A, and 1.42% at Solar B. The share below q01 is 0.31%, 1.41%, 0.86%, 0.65%, and 1.10% in the same order.
  • Single months miss. In the worst month the share below q05 is 14.1%, 10.3%, and 16.3% at the three wind farms (nominal 5%), and the share above q99 is 2.6%, 2.1%, and 3.1% (nominal 1%). Solar A's worst month above q99 is 12.3%.
  • Prediction P1 did not hold. It said the q05 and q95 shares would sit within 3 points of nominal in every month, and that the share above q99 would stay under 1.5% in every month. Only the pooled share above q99 at the wind farms stayed under 1.5%.
  • Error rises with lead time. For wind, the mean absolute error of the median forecast rises from about 9% of capacity at day 1 to 17% to 21% at days 9 to 10 at Farm A and B and to 19% at Farm C. For solar, it rises from 9% to 10% at day 1 to 15% at days 9 to 10.
  • Solar contrasts. Each is a2_member minus a reference, in points of capacity (negative means a2_member has the smaller error). The interval is a month-block bootstrap at 98.75% (a Bonferroni correction for 4 contrasts) over 11 scored months and 120,249 half-hours of Solar A and B together. The minimum detectable effect is in brackets. Blend +0.23 (-0.18 to +0.74; 0.60). XGBoost model alone -0.56 (-1.05 to -0.03; 0.69). Climatology -3.71 (-4.29 to -2.94; 0.92). Manual heuristic -3.32 (-4.23 to -2.34; 1.27). Absolute errors: a2_member 12.7% of capacity, blend 12.5%, XGBoost 13.3%, climatology 16.4%, manual heuristic 16.1%. The gain over the XGBoost model is smaller than its minimum detectable effect.
  • Table P cuts the share above q99 at the wind farms without changing the score. At Farm A the share falls from 2.10% to 0.95%, and the score changes by under 0.1% of its value at every wind farm.
  • Prediction P2 (the worst half-hours sit in a few storm days) is not tested. The 20 worst q99 half-hours at each wind farm fall in 5, 7, and 6 different months at Farm A, B, and C, and 12 of Farm A's fall in two months. The stored table records months, not days, so a day-level check was not run. The tables are private.

docs.title: Part B: demand in real events
docs.text:
Seven events fit inside one stored month. Six are labelled events from experiment 404. One is a step that experiment 456's scan for level steps found and that NGED has not labelled; the scan found six more that did not fit. NGED's labels are incomplete, so the scan-found event may be a load shift, a level step, or neither. The columns of the table give the mean absolute error of the day-ahead median forecast (12 to under 36 hours ahead) during the event, in points of effective capacity. D5, D12, D14, and D16 are Primary substations.

Event Substation Lagless S1 B-mix K2-S1 1 D5 3.9 5.2 3.7 3.7 2 D5 16.0 16.1 15.5 15.2 3 D5 5.3 4.2 4.8 3.9 4 D14 24.8 26.8 26.3 25.8 5 D16 4.0 3.4 3.7 3.5 6 D14 13.6 10.0 12.6 12.0 7 D12 (scan) 21.2 14.7 17.1 15.8
  • S1 was less accurate than the lagless forecast in 3 of 7 events, and K2-S1 was more accurate in 6 of 7. Prediction P3 said the lagged forecasts would be worse in at least half the events. That did not hold. P3 also said the lagged forecasts would follow the shifted power within one day, and that the lagless forecast would stay near the pre-event level. Neither delay nor pre-event level was computed, so those two parts are not tested.
  • Two events are large for every forecast. Events 2 and 4 have errors of 15 to 27 points for all four forecasts, so the lagged power does not explain them.
  • These numbers are interim and unaudited. With 7 events no interval is reported.

docs.title: Not done
docs.text:
• Wind reference contrasts against research defaults 1 and 2, climatology, and the manual heuristic. The stored wind references load through code that needs PyTorch, which this CPU-only session does not install.
  • The 14-day wind chart. Experiment 429 holds one.
  • The solar q01 contrast, and a curtailment week (no label exists for wind or solar).
  • For demand: the normal-running-arrangement (NRA) corrected actual, the surprise inputs, the injected-shift scenarios, and the avoidable-curtailment cost.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: not computed, because this page scores no mean forecast.
  • Triggers fired: none. No control or nested arm exists.
  • Reviews: one fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code, and its findings were applied.
  • Caveats: NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold events. The wind rows cover true days 1 to 10 only. Solar a2_member is at the old capacity rule.

docs.title: Does a finer cross-fit (12 folds instead of 6) let the learned trust weight approach 0.5 and beat the fixed 50/50 mixture?
docs.text:
Doubling the number of cross-fit folds from 6 to 12 does not make the learned trust weight beat the fixed 50/50 mixture, so the weaker-fold-head explanation is not supported. Experiment 463 fitted a trust weight, which sets how far to trust the lagged forecast (the one that reads recent power readings), on lagged forecasts from neural networks that did not see the fitting rows. Experiment 463's learned weight sat near 0.4 and did not beat 50/50. We asked whether those networks were too weak because each trained on only 5/6 of the rows. Here each lagged-head network trains on 11/12. The pre-registered prediction failed: the contrast against 50/50 on rows with no labelled event stayed within the 0.03 stop band (+0.002), and the learned weight at the six signed-megawatt substations fell (0.34 against 0.41). Both conditions of the stop rule hold (the contrast is within +-0.03, and the learned weight is below 0.45). On this evidence the trust line closes. The intervals are wide (minimum detectable effect 0.32 points): the point estimate is far from the predicted -0.06, but the lower bound of the 95% interval is -0.060, so an effect that size is not excluded. This result is interim: five months were scored with one seed. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlogged events.

The score of G1-trust-12 is indistinguishable from the score of the 6-fold G1-trust, and its point estimate is slightly worse. Against 50/50 on rows with no labelled event at the six signed-megawatt substations, G1-trust-12 is +0.002 points of capacity (95% interval -0.060 to +0.074, Bonferroni interval -0.089 to +0.108, minimum detectable effect 0.32; Bonferroni count 24). The paired contrast against the 6-fold G1-trust is +0.023 (-0.013 to +0.069), so the 12-fold fit is no better and is, by its point estimate, slightly worse.

  • Harm rows (a lag inside an event, the target outside). Against 50/50 at the six: +0.067 (-0.044 to +0.240, minimum detectable effect 0.42). At the eight MVA-only substations: +0.120 (-0.019 to +0.327, minimum detectable effect 0.68).
  • Real-event rows (actuals corrected to the normal running arrangement, depth factor 1.0). Against 50/50 at the six: +0.029 (-0.042 to +0.071, minimum detectable effect 0.38; +0.013 without the largest event). At the eight: +0.203 (+0.033 to +0.377, minimum detectable effect 0.27), so G1-trust-12 scores worse than 50/50 there at the 95% level only (the Bonferroni interval is -0.049 to +0.464).
  • Eight MVA-only substations, rows with no labelled event. +0.045 against 50/50 (-0.031 to +0.136).
  • Absolute scores (rows with no labelled event, six; points of capacity). 50/50 3.513, G1-trust 3.492, G1-trust-12 3.515, K2-S1 3.369, A0-inj 3.824.
  • Tails (rows with no labelled event, six). Coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99: G1-trust-12 0.006, 0.030, 0.849, 0.947; 50/50 0.006, 0.028, 0.855, 0.949. The upper tail is under-covered by about 5 percentage points at q95 in both arms.
  • Median forecast. The mean absolute error of the median differs from 50/50's by +0.0004 on rows with no labelled event at the six; the median is not the cause of any score gap.

The learned weight does not approach 0.5 at the six signed-megawatt substations. The mean learned lagged weight is 0.34 at 12 folds and 0.41 at 6 folds there, and 0.53 against 0.50 at the eight MVA-only substations. Across the five scored months the weight at the six ranges from 0.29 to 0.38 (a swing of about 0.08, under the 0.1 that experiment 463's rule treats as a reason to run seed 1). The weight is lowest in the 6 to 10 day band (0.31). The out-of-fold negative log-likelihood of the lagged head is 0.71 to 0.86 per month, against 0.24 in sample, so the head is still far weaker on a held-out block than on rows it saw.

K2-S1 beats G1-trust-12 and needs no cross-fit table. Against K2-S1 on rows with no labelled event at the six, G1-trust-12 is +0.145 points worse (+0.001 to +0.310). On real-event rows at depth 1.0 the two are level (-0.012, -0.162 to +0.138). The adoption rule (beat K2-S1 on rows with no labelled event, real events, and curtailment cost) fails.

Avoidable-curtailment cost (six signed-megawatt substations, widening 1.15, from experiment 454's costing). G1-trust-12 minus 50/50: +0.023 (f = 0.9; -0.235 to +0.268), +0.127 (f = 0.75; -0.552 to +0.949), and +0.253 (f = 0.5; -1.331 to +1.810). G1-trust-12 minus K2-S1 is +0.204, +1.352, and +3.420, and the intervals exclude zero at all three. Costs are in the units of experiment 454's table.

Compute needed per refit with 12 folds. Each refit needs 12 out-of-fold lagged fits, 1 trust fit, and 13 lagless fits, against 6, 1, and 7 at 6 folds, plus a stored past-forecast table. K2-S1 needs 4 networks and no cross-fit.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Lagged head and fit loop. Experiment 404's A0-inj lagged head, with experiment 463's fit loop (e00463_crossfit.py) at 12 folds. The scored month is forecast with 404's stored full-data A0-inj network and the new trust head.
  • Lagless table. Rebuilt at 12 folds in this experiment's folder (65 module fits). The scored month's lagless forecast comes from a module refitted for this table, so the comparison against experiment 463's G1-trust differs in more than the fold count: the module's fitted weights differ, though its recipe is the same.
  • Reused, not refitted. 404's B-mix and A0-inj, 454's K2-S1 (mean of its 3 stored cells in quantile space, no widening), 463's G1-trust and G1-insample. There is no 12-fold G1-insample control; 463's 6-fold one is the reference.
  • Compute. 60 out-of-fold fits (6 to 11 s each) and 5 trust fits (about 7 minutes each) plus the table rebuild (70 s per month): about 1 GPU-hour in all, one process.
  • Scoring. e00469_score.py reuses e00463_score.py; e00469_curtailment.py reuses experiment 454's costing. Months are the resampling unit.
  • Audit triggers. The median-error check above is the only trigger run on this free re-score.

docs.title: Which assembled demand forecaster should be the first release: one pretrained network, a mixture of lagged and lagless networks, or either of those with the GAM forecast as an input?
docs.text: Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

docs.title: Which assembled demand forecaster should be the first release?
docs.text:
Take-home message. The pretrained network scores almost as well as the best mixture and holds up better on cold winter nights and 12 to 36 hours ahead, so the lagged-plus-lagless design adds nothing the 5 months of data can confirm. Recommendation: release A-pool, the five-seed pretrained network, unless the maintainer prefers A-gam-in, the same network with the GAM forecast as an extra input. The lowest scores are K2-425A's (4.608 at the eight MVA-only Primaries and 3.353 at the six signed-MW Primaries, on rows with no labelled event). They are only 0.072 and 0.098 points of capacity below A-pool, against a minimum detectable effect of 0.065 and 0.100 points. The pre-registered rule does not give one robust answer. The plan's tie clause for A-pool and K2-S1 recommends A-pool. The rule's clause-by-clause admissibility test, read literally, leaves only A-gam-in. The choice between those two is the maintainer's. Every score is selection-biased.

We asked which demand forecaster to release first for the 14 Primary substations with a generalised additive model (GAM) forecast: the eight that report in megavolt-amperes (MVA) only, and the six that report in signed megawatts (MW). We took 5 candidates that earlier experiments built, put all of them on the same half-hours (1,145,256 half-hours over 5 test months, 1,003,611 of them at the 14 Primaries), and scored them with the same code. Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of capacity, so lower is better. A lagless forecast uses no recent power readings as inputs, and a mixture averages the density of lagged networks and lagless networks. The candidates are the pretrained network alone (A-pool, five seeds averaged; pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS weather and fine-tuned on ensemble weather), three mixtures of lagged and lagless networks (K2-S1, K2-425A, and K2-425A+S1), and A-gam-in. No neural network was refitted. Experiment 425 stored only quantiles for the pretrained network, so a forward pass of its saved networks recovered the mixture parameters. The recovered parameters reproduced the stored quantiles to within 4e-5.

Figure 1 shows the gaps that matter: the mixtures lose on cold nights and 12 to 36 hours ahead.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. A-pool is experiment 425's arm A, seeds 0 to 4, quantile-averaged. K2-S1 is experiment 454's mixture of 2 S1 networks and 2 lagless networks. K2-425A mixes 2 arm A seeds with 2 lagless networks, and K2-425A+S1 mixes 1 arm A seed, 1 S1 network, and 2 lagless networks, with the lagless seeds (c, (c+1) mod 3) in cell c. A-gam-in is experiment 457's Gin (five seeds). Controls are A-ens2 (2 arm A seeds as a density mixture), B-mix, and the S1 three-seed ensemble. Reuse: experiments 425, 454, and 457 for stored forecasts, experiment 404 for the lagless tables, experiment 449 for the XGBoost forecast, and experiment 472 for the descriptive row. Fits: 0. - Rows. The key is (Primary, forecast origin, target half-hour) on experiment 404's grid. Experiment 454's rows lie inside experiment 425's rows; the 1,520 rows that 425 holds and 454 does not are at D15 and D18 (the two Primaries with no GAM forecast), after the 2025-03-01 start cut. Row sets are gam14 (every candidate holds the row, 1,003,611 half-hours at 14 Primaries), main16 (all 16 Primaries without A-gam-in, 1,145,256), and ref14 (gam14 rows that BG2, manual_heuristic, climatology, and the XGBoost forecast also hold, 802,838, which cuts days 8 to 10 because BG2 stops at 168 hours). Each month's size is printed by e00470_score.py rows. Scoring actuals dropped for flagged exact zeros: 1,179 in the scoring context.
  • Scale. CRPS is mass-weighted pinball loss in points of capacity (experiment 404's definition), so absolute values differ from experiments 454 and 457, which scored other row sets and an equal-weight definition. The four tail quantiles of every neural arm are widened by 1.15 about the median; BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology are not.
  • Minimum detectable effect. Arm A's five single seeds give 0.065 points at the eight and 0.100 points at the six, and 0.652 at D15 and D18. The seed spread of the mixtures uses three cells built from overlapping seed pairs, so the values (eight: 0.049 for K2-425A, 0.059 for K2-S1, 0.084 for K2-425A+S1; six: 0.117, 0.104, 0.134) are lower bounds.

At f = 0.5: 21.629, 26.634, 23.771, 24.543, 21.306, 25.918, and 37.789. At f = 0.5 K2-S1 costs 5.0 more than A-pool (0.85 to 10.5), while K2-425A (2.1, -0.4 to 6.3) is not conclusively different. The saving against manual_heuristic at f = 0.75 is 601 pounds per MW per day for A-pool (288 to 992, six Primaries, 49.82 MW, 195 days) and 480 for K2-S1; at f = 0.5 it is 1,663 and 1,148. Our understanding of manual_heuristic as NGED's baseline is unconfirmed.

  • AvgAnchor (experiment 472; descriptive and unreplicated, outside every count): 4.586 at the eight, 3.131 at the six (0.32 below A-pool, the lowest score of any arm), 23.231 on real-event rows (worse than every candidate), 6.193 on cold winter nights at the six, and q99 pinball 0.293 at the eight, which is worse than A-pool's. It serves four networks. Experiment 472's own page reports that it fails its tail gate and that its real-event result is inconclusive.

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
• Pre-registered tie clause applies. A-pool and K2-S1 tie at the eight and the six (both Bonferroni intervals include zero; at the eight the gap of 0.066 sits 0.002 above the minimum detectable effect of 0.065), so the plan says the lag design adds nothing over pretraining and recommends A-pool. K2-S1 is also conclusively worse than A-pool on cold winter nights and 12 to 36 hours ahead.
  • Admissibility test read literally leaves A-gam-in only (decision.csv). K2-425A has the lowest CRPS and makes A-pool inadmissible at the eight (gap 0.072 against a minimum detectable effect of 0.065, interval -0.139 to -0.003), but K2-425A fails the q99 clause by 0.0008 (excess 0.0208 against 0.02, measured against the arm with the lowest q99 loss, A-gam-in). K2-425A+S1 fails by 0.0017. A-gam-in passes every clause through the inconclusive route, but it needs the GAM at serving time.
  • Three margins decide which candidate the rule selects. The audit found three: A-pool's conclusiveness at the eight (0.0715 against 0.0645, interval edge -0.003), A-gam-in's gaps (0.032 and 0.057, over the 0.03 tolerance, admissible only because they are inconclusive), and the q99 margin of K2-425A. Measuring the q99 excess against A-pool makes K2-425A and K2-425A+S1 pass, and then the rule picks K2-425A.
  • Production requirements. A-pool: 5 neural networks per forecast, 5 pretrained and 5 fine-tuned fits per monthly refit, no lagless table. K2-S1 and K2-425A+S1: 4 networks, the lagless table and, for S1, the store of past lagless forecasts that S1's surprise inputs read. K2-425A: 4 networks and the lagless table but no store. A-gam-in: 5 networks plus the GAM forecast in the serving path with its own monthly refit.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary (points of capacity, mean-forecast from the quantile masses): at the eight, A-pool -1.70 to -0.03, K2-425A -2.23 to +0.23, K2-S1 -1.91 to +0.32; at the six, A-pool -0.67 to -0.07 and K2-S1 -0.75 to -0.01. No candidate's median sits far from its mean.

  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts. Mean absolute error of the mean forecast at the eight: A-pool 6.833, K2-425A 6.779, K2-S1 6.940, A-gam-in 6.774; at the six (no labelled event): A-pool 4.895, K2-425A 4.805, K2-S1 4.855, A-gam-in 4.827. Every sign matches the CRPS contrast. Trigger 3 (the mean-forecast error contradicting the CRPS contrast) did not fire.

  • Triggers that fired. Trigger 2 (the result contradicts prediction P3: K2-425A and K2-425A+S1 are 0.24 to 0.42 points better than K2-S1 on real-event rows, where they were predicted to be no better) and trigger 4 (leaving one Primary out flips K2-425A+S1 minus A-pool at the eight and K2-S1 minus A-pool at the six). A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the absolute scores, the contrasts, and the intervals from the raw stored forecasts (agreement to 4 decimals; intervals within 0.002) and found no artefact in P3's contradiction: one Primary holds 29,436 of the 50,168 real-event rows, and there K2-425A beats K2-S1 by 0.75 points. The audit also found that two Primaries drive each leave-one-out flip. The audit's margins are in "Decision rule".

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Selection bias. The five folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) both choose and score the candidate. The first month in none of the folds of experiments 404, 425, 435, 448, 454, and 457 is July 2026, which is held back for a finalist. Scoring July 2026 needs the monthly refit with 24 months of training, the arm A pipeline of experiment 425 (e00425_fit.py), and the scorer of this experiment on the new rows. The maintainer can run it when July 2026 lands. That scoring is not a gate here. Experiment 470 scored 9 hours of valid times (target half-hours) on 2026-07-01, so some of July 2026 was used; July scoring in later work starts at 2026-07-02 00:00.
  • Interval width. The bootstrap resamples one forecast day per block. Each target half-hour appears under up to 10 consecutive origin days, so neighbouring blocks share weather and actuals. The intervals are therefore probably too narrow.
  • Unlogged events. NGED says its load-shift logs miss events, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events, and the real-event slice undercounts.
  • Scope. The 5 months and 14 Primaries with a GAM scored here; D15 and D18 are report-only (minimum detectable effect 0.65), where A-pool scores 10.648, A-gam-in 10.680, K2-425A 11.163, and K2-S1 11.319. The curtailment intervals are plain 95% intervals, not Bonferroni, and cover six Primaries.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Score the winner on July 2026 when it lands, with the same scorer.
  • Decide whether the 0.001 q99 margin or the tie clause governs, and whether the 0.9% CRPS gain at the eight justifies running the GAM at serving time.
  • Test arm A and K2-425A with a lagless head trained on ERA5 weather, to see whether the cold-night gap closes.

docs.title: Which simple changes to NGED's manual heuristic lower its quantile score and its avoidable-curtailment cost?
docs.text:
National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) forecasts the demand at a substation with its manual heuristic: it reads one number, the 95th percentile of 13 equally weighted historical analogues (the demand at the same half-hour 1 to 6 weeks and 49 to 55 weeks earlier). We asked whether cheap changes to that rule lower its forecast error, without training a neural network. We tested a calibration fitted on the last 28 or 56 days of errors (ensemble model output statistics, EMOS, Gneiting et al. (2005)), a recalibration of the quantile levels, and a shift by the recent error, and scored each beside the unchanged ("faithful") heuristic on 5 months. The error score is CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score, in points of effective capacity; it equals twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 stored quantile levels. The two groups of substations are the eight Primaries whose meter records only apparent power (MVA-only) and the six whose meter records signed real power (signed-MW). None of the 10 variants lowered CRPS at either group by more than its interval.

Take-home: the faithful heuristic is hard to beat with a cheap fit, so it stays the benchmark. Rank histograms of the actual among the 13 analogues are close to flat on the whole record (stage 0, 2025-07 to 2026-06), and the 95th percentile is exceeded in 9.5% of half-hours at the eight and 10.6% at the six, at or below the 11.4% that perfectly calibrated analogues give with 13 members. The analogues are not calibrated everywhere: q01 and q99 are exceeded far more often than 1%, and the q95 coverage on cold winter nights is 0.59 at the eight and 0.66 at the six. The Gaussian fit corrects part of the cold-night shortfall, but over the five scored months it raises CRPS elsewhere. Verdict: not supported. What this narrows: these cheap fits did not close the gap to BG2; whether a regime-specific correction can is untested.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Rows. Experiment 457's row set (fold_a_daily_gap_v1), five months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 709,353 shared half-hours: 385,855 at the eight, 258,993 at the six, and 64,505 at the report-only Primaries D15 and D18, whose tables are in work/scores/ and not discussed here. The row set ends at 168 hours, so leads of 168 to 240 hours are not scored (stage 0 covers them).
  • Faithful heuristic, absolute scores (CRPS, points of capacity). Eight: 4.163; six: 3.760. References on the same rows: BG2 3.563 and 2.856, arm A-avg5 3.363 and 2.734, monthly XGBoost 3.655 and 3.051, climatology 4.564 and 4.091.
  • Primary variant, EMOS (56-day window, weekly refit). CRPS difference from the faithful heuristic +0.063 at the eight (Bonferroni interval -0.081 to +0.232) and +0.235 at the six (+0.050 to +0.442). It does not clear the pre-registered rule.
  • Every gating contrast (10 variants, 2 groups, 20 tests; CRPS, all rows):
    • No variant lowers CRPS at both groups by more than its Bonferroni interval.
    • The recalibrated q95 alone (Tau95_56) is neutral: -0.004 at the eight and -0.0004 at the six, because the recalibrated level is the maximum member in 1,696 of 3,154 fits.
    • The remaining variants raise CRPS by 0.02 to 0.34 points.
  • Cold winter nights (secondary, interval uncorrected for the wider family). EMOS lowers CRPS by 0.90 at the eight (-1.21 to -0.36) and 0.36 at the six (-0.58 to -0.03), and lowers the q99 pinball loss at both. At the eight, the recalibrated levels, the mean shift, and the 99-member EMOS also have cold-night intervals below zero.
  • Where EMOS loses. At the six, CRPS rises by 2.28 points in Christmas week, the q01 pinball loss rises by 0.148, and the median forecast's mean absolute error is 7.04 against 6.69 points. At the eight, EMOS lowers Christmas-week CRPS by 0.19 (-0.33 to -0.05).
  • Tail coverage, eight and six (EMOS against faithful). q95 0.891 and 0.916 against 0.881 and 0.880; q99 0.946 and 0.966 against 0.912 and 0.911.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost, signed-MW six, millions of pounds over the five months (faithful heuristic against EMOS; difference with 95% interval over month-by-series cells). At f = 0.9: 2.02 against 1.71 (-0.31, -1.54 to +0.45). At f = 0.75: 12.88 against 10.92 (-1.97, -7.07 to +1.24). At f = 0.5: 37.79 against 33.68 (-4.11, -13.21 to +1.95). BG2 gives 1.37, 8.24, and 25.92. No interval excludes zero.
  • Emitting a distribution as members. Emitting the Gaussian as 13 equiprobable members raises CRPS by 0.10 to 0.11 over the exact Gaussian; 99 members raise it by 0.013 to 0.015.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary. The analogue median sits 0.0005 to 0.06 MW from the analogue mean (work/scores/checks.csv); no spread-driven shift.
  • Error of the median forecast beside the CRPS contrasts. Median mean absolute error, eight and six: faithful 7.27 and 6.69 points; EMOS 7.40 and 7.04. The median and the CRPS point the same way.
  • Triggers fired. None of the seven audit triggers. The prediction that the q95 exceedance moves from 11% to 14% towards 5% (P2) failed, because stage 0 measured 9.5% and 10.6% before any fit. On the scored months the faithful q95 coverage is 0.881 at the eight and 0.880 at the six, an exceedance of about 12%, so the 11.4% comparison holds on stage 0's twelve months and not on the scored five.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first scored run. The reviewer found no lookahead or alignment bug, and the findings were accepted: the Bonferroni count covers only the gating cells, every variant is floored at zero at the eight MVA-only Primaries, rows with fewer than 6 members take the faithful quantiles, and the check against experiment 87 asserts. The reviewer also noted that the probability-integral-transform recalibration cannot extend the tails beyond the member range, which explains Tau95_56.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Stage 0. Rebuilt from the stored members (data/power_forecasts/experiment_name=manual_heuristic), the 11 quantiles equal experiment 87's stored reference to 4e-15 MW. Rows hold 13 or 12 members at 92% of half-hours; the rest hold 3 to 11 because observed power is missing. The Spearman correlation of analogue spread with the absolute error of the analogue mean is 0.43 to 0.57, so the spread carries information, yet the EMOS spread term did not lower CRPS over the five months.
  • Stage 1 and the level adjustment. Variants E28, E56, E56m13, E56m99, MeanLS56, Q56, Tau95_56, Lvl7, Lvl14, Lvl28. Fits are per Primary and lead band (0 to 24, 24 to 72, 72 to 120, 120 to 168 hours), weekly refits, pairs whose valid time is at least 24 hours before the refit. A 112-day window (E112) was written and not scored, because the member store starts in mid-June 2025 and 2025-10 lacks the history.
  • Not run. The pre-registered stop rule applied. Holiday-aligned analogues, the clock-change arm, 7 and 26 analogues, and the load-growth arm, because no stage 1 variant beat the faithful heuristic. Per-Primary results, Economy 7 and sunny slices, and the largest-event-removed sensitivity were not produced. The D15 and D18 tables exist and are not discussed.
  • Selection bias. Windows were chosen and scored on the same five months, so every variant's result is, if anything, optimistic.
  • Cadence and cleaning. Weekly refits of the calibration, not of a model. Actuals are the cleaned scoring actuals (1,179 flagged exact-zero half-hours removed). The cut of D15 and D18 before 2025-03-01 is moot for the five scored months.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00471-manual-heuristic-calibration-and-analogue-upgrades/, importing the folders of experiments 448, 452, 457, 449, and 425.
  • Predictions. data/ml-experiments/00471-manual-heuristic-calibration-and-analogue-upgrades/work/predictions/<variant>.parquet.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: A correction fitted only on cold winter nights, since that is where EMOS gained, and a scoring row set that reaches 240 hours.

docs.title: Can a penalty of 100, or an anchor averaged over three lagless seeds, keep the gain of the lagless-anchor-plus-lag-correction forecaster on rows with no labelled event and remove its loss inside real events?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead the lagless anchor is stronger than a forecast made at the origin can be, so the gain of the lag correction over its anchor is understated there, and the gaps to B-mix and K2-S1 are not valid forecasts. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

A stronger penalty does not make the lag correction safe, and an anchor averaged over three lagless seeds makes the correction score better than K2-S1. The correction is experiment 467's 32-unit network on a frozen lagless forecast. The neural network reads the three lags, the surprise at each lag, and the lead time. A penalty of 100 on its outputs (P100) shrinks the shift to under 0.01 of capacity on 99.9% of rows and keeps 18% of the gain over the lagless head, so the stop rule for the penalty fires. The averaged-anchor arm (AvgAnchor) replaces the single lagless seed with the equal-weight mixture of seeds 0 to 2, nine components, and scores 3.094 points of capacity at the signed-MW six on rows with no labelled event. Its anchor LL-ens3 scores 3.622, K2-S1 3.387, B-mix 3.508, and experiment 467's C1e-2 3.212 (seeds 0 and 1). NGED's event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold real events that nobody logged. NRA means normal running arrangement. Every number is interim and unaudited by an Opus agent.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are points of effective capacity (CRPS, lower is better), raw quantiles, metered actuals unless stated, leads up to 240 hours, and the mean over 5 scored months and the stored cells (fit seeds 0 to 2; LL-ens3 has one cell; C1e-2, C1, and Z1e-2 have seeds 0 and 1 only). Intervals are 95% month-block intervals, except where the Bonferroni count of 27 is named. Experiment 454's minimum detectable effect at the signed-MW six is 0.237 on rows with no labelled event and 0.382 inside events (0.124 and 0.798 at the MVA-only eight), read before any contrast. A contrast inside it is inconclusive. Nothing here is claimed at the 99.8% level that 27 contrasts need.

  • Arms and predictions. P100 uses a penalty of 100, a single-seed anchor, two serving neural networks, and 7 fits per monthly refit. AvgAnchor uses a penalty of 1e-2, a nine-component anchor, four serving neural networks, 21 lagless fits plus 1 correction per monthly refit). Predictions written before any fit: P1 (P100 keeps at least half of the gain over the lagless head) failed, with 18% kept. P2 (AvgAnchor within 0.05 of K2-S1) failed in the favourable direction: AvgAnchor is 0.29 points better. P3 (the shift share below 0.01 of capacity goes to 1) held: 0.999 at the six.
  • Signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event.
    • AvgAnchor 3.094, C1e-2 3.212, C1 3.206, Z1e-2 3.611, P100 3.664, LL-ens3 3.622, LL 3.761, B-mix 3.508, K2-S1 3.387.
    • P100 minus LL -0.098 (-0.147 to -0.048, 5 of 5 months), inside the minimum detectable effect, so inconclusive in size.
    • AvgAnchor minus LL-ens3 -0.528 (-0.939 to -0.221, 5 of 5 months, above 0.237); minus K2-S1 -0.293 (-0.766 to +0.093, 3 of 5 months); minus B-mix -0.414 (-0.919 to -0.073, 5 of 5 months).

AvgAnchor minus LL-ens3, with absolute scores (AvgAnchor against LL-ens3): -0.303 on target rows (-0.497 to -0.156; 3.104 against 3.406), -0.393 on harm rows (-0.693 to -0.120; 3.619 against 4.012), -0.442 on clean rows (4.083 against 4.525). P100 minus LL (P100 against LL): -0.074 (3.479 against 3.553), -0.078 (4.075 against 4.152), -0.080 (4.593 against 4.673), all intervals excluding zero. Both arms pass the 0.03 limit on injected rows. The neural networks trained on injected worlds of the same kind, so the comparison measures robustness to the injected load shifts and not to every real event.

    • Month-block, NRA-corrected actuals, six: AvgAnchor minus LL-ens3 +0.295 (-0.426 to +1.720; 14.943 against 14.647); P100 minus LL -0.003 (-0.099 to +0.143; 14.793 against 14.796). On metered actuals: AvgAnchor -0.654 (-1.628 to +0.045; 5.285 against 5.939); P100 -0.095 (-0.152 to -0.014; 5.995 against 6.091).

P100 minus LL +0.034 (-0.039 to +0.086) and +0.013 (-0.050 to +0.098). The two poolings give the same sign and different sizes.

  • Definition of the gain. The gain of a correction is its score subtracted from the score of the single-seed lagless head LL on the same rows: 0.549 for C1e-2 (seeds 0 and 1, interval -0.976 to -0.204) and 0.098 for P100, which is 18% (about 9% to 27% from the interval of P100's gain). Prediction P1 quoted 0.50 from experiment 467's seeds.

The forecasts of every arm are low on average, and AvgAnchor corrects most of that level offset.

At f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5: AvgAnchor 1.83, 7.25, 22.9; K2-S1 1.85, 8.22, 26.6; B-mix 1.96, 9.00, 28.5; LL-ens3 2.11, 9.30, 28.5; P100 2.07, 9.04, 27.8; LL 2.19, 9.62, 29.4; BG2 1.37, 8.24, 25.9; manual_heuristic 2.02, 12.9, 37.8.
