    • AvgAnchor minus LL-ens3, K2-S1, and B-mix include zero at all three fractions. The scaled limit is the headline and the real thermal limit is not used.
    • Serving load. P100 serves two neural networks per pass and needs 7 fits per monthly refit. AvgAnchor serves four neural networks (3 lagless seeds and a correction), 21 lagless fits and 1 correction fit per refit. K2-S1 also serves four neural networks.
    • Fits. The experiment ran 30 correction fits (23 s for P100, 39 s for AvgAnchor on one GPU process each), two processes under 8 GB, about 60 minutes in all with the four-world forecasts. The networks are saved under data/ml-experiments/00472-*/work/models/. Monthly retraining.
    • Rows and reuse. Experiment 404's rows and injected worlds (training worlds 100 to 102, scoring worlds 200 to 202); real-world rows equal experiment 454's experiment_404_scoring_rows (346,672 to 259,166 rows per month). Stored references from experiments 454 and 467. Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped, and D15 and D18 are report-only. Code reused: experiment 404's modules, experiment 454's mixture builder and scorer, and copies of experiment 467's e00467_arm.py, e00467_score.py, e00467_curtailment.py, and e00467_figures.py.
    • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet reviewer found no bug in the arm script. A second reviewed the scoring script and found four faults: a mis-weighted mean approximation, event ids built from lags and not from the target, an unguarded cold-night index, and duplicate reference rows. All four were fixed. A third re-derived the headline scores from the stored forecasts with its own code, and agreed with every printed number to 0.001. The write-up reviews follow in the pull request.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast. At the six, the mean of the mean forecast minus the median forecast is +0.2 points for AvgAnchor and LL-ens3, +0.3 for K2-S1, and +0.4 for B-mix. The per-Primary table was not produced.
  • Error of the mean and median beside each contrast. The mean absolute error of the median and of the mean forecast move in the same direction as the quantile score for every contrast (AvgAnchor 4.5 against LL-ens3 5.3, K2-S1 4.9, and B-mix 5.0; P100 5.1 against LL 5.2).
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired for P1 and P2: the explanations are the tested ones above (P100 minus Z1e-2 shows the penalty removes the spread recalibration; the correction on an averaged anchor scores better than the correction on a single seed, 3.094 against 3.212). Trigger 4 did not flip the contrast against the anchor (the gain stays above the minimum detectable effect without D14), but the contrast against B-mix with D14 removed has an interval that includes zero, which is why gate 1 is a diagnostic. Trigger 7 holds, because the demand assembly adds AvgAnchor as a candidate on this unreplicated result. Triggers 1, 3, 5, and 6 did not fire. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline from the stored forecasts.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• AvgAnchor is a candidate for the assembly's held-out test and not an adopted design. AvgAnchor fails the coverage clause of gate 3 as written and the result is unreplicated, so the demand assembly treats it as one unreplicated candidate.
  • Real-event safety of AvgAnchor is unproven. The point estimate on NRA-corrected actuals is 0.30 to 0.66 points worse than its anchor, and the evidence is mixed: the month-block interval includes zero, and the event-cluster pooling over all events excludes zero (+0.66, +0.05 to +1.09).
  • The coverage limit of gate 3 fails as written, so AvgAnchor does not meet the pre-registered rule for a candidate as written, because the anchor under-covers. A coverage limit relative to the nominal level would pass.
  • AvgAnchor and C1e-2 differ in more than the anchor: C1e-2 has seeds 0 and 1 only, and the networks of AvgAnchor train on the other seeds' tables, so the 0.12 gap between them is not a clean test.
  • Unlogged events. Clean rows may hold events no label covers, so the harm contrasts are optimistic and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Next step. AvgAnchor goes into the demand assembly's held-out test as a further candidate. A test of a correction that ignores the lags inside events (a gate on the surprise) would address the real-event reading.

docs.title: What makes Generators X, Y, and Z hard to forecast, and can any of them be forecast from weather and calendar?
docs.text:
Generator X is the one candidate for a first forecast, and its output shows only a weak relationship with price. The question was what makes NGED's three metered generators hard to forecast, and whether any of them is forecastable at all. Generator Y has been inactive since mid-2024, and Generator Z has 400 active half-hours in total. All three series are in MW, none carries a cleaning flag, and none has duplicate keys, nulls, NaNs, or off-grid timestamps. The checks narrow the stage 2 candidates to Generator X, plus Generator Y if its folds end in mid-2024. Stage 2 is the first forecast, fitted only after this look; its gate is 35,040 valid half-hours.

Generator Y runs in winter-heavy spells, then stops. Its active share is 22.0% from October to March and 12.6% from April to September, with 515 active spells (median 11 half-hours, longest 13.6 days). The last active month is 2024-06. After that, Generator Y is idle for 36,367 half-hours with output at or below 3.9% of its maximum, and its idle level moves from a small import (about -1.5% to -2.1% of the maximum, until 2024) to about +0.1% from 2025. A level shift of that size could be a disconnection or a metering change, and the data cannot say which. In 2021, Generator Y has 305 active half-hours and a peak output of 16% of the series' overall maximum, so 2021 is a near-idle year of unknown cause. Generator Y's record also thins in 2026, with 422 to 525 half-hours per month in July to September against about 1,400 expected.

Generator Z is almost absent. It has 4,643 valid half-hours across a span of 49,008, with 52 gaps over an hour, 37 over 7 days, and a longest gap of 111 days. All 400 of its active half-hours fall in 2023-07 and 2023-08. After the last active half-hour, it reads exact zero in 94.0% of 2,584 half-hours. Its longest run of exact zeros is 2,384 consecutive recorded half-hours, which spans 881 calendar days because the run crosses gaps. Before that run, the median of its non-zero idle readings was -0.4% of its maximum (-0.2% counting the exact zeros), so the exact zeros could be a meter fill, genuine idle, or sparse reporting. The data cannot say which, and the count of exact-zero half-hours is a lower bound for missing data.

Generator X is a two-sided series with short spells and a two-peak daily cycle. It has 91,387 valid half-hours, and 5,236 more are missing in gaps: 117 gaps over an hour, with the 4 gaps over 7 days and the longest gap (28 days) all in 2021. Of its half-hours, 58.9% are negative, 4.2% are exact zeros, and 30.0% are active. Active spells are short (median 2 half-hours, 90th percentile 5), and about 2,100 begin per year. The active share is 30.2% from October to March and 29.8% from April to September, so the two half-years do not differ. The daily cycle peaks at +3% of the maximum at 08:00 and +5% at 18:00 local time, with troughs of -4.5% at 04:00 and 15:00 (Figure 3). That swing is small against half-hour changes of up to 100% of the maximum. Single half-hours that differ by more than half the maximum from two otherwise equal neighbours occur 439 times, and the data cannot say whether they are real dispatch or glitches.

Generator X's mean output rises with price, but the evidence is weak. The mean rises from -3.0% of its maximum in the cheapest price decile to +0.1% in the dearest. The share of negative half-hours does not fall (63% in the cheapest decile, 67% in the dearest), the rank correlation with price is only 0.035 (0.046 after removing each hour's mean), and price and hour of day are entangled. Generator Y is active in 35% of half-hours in the dearest decile and 8% in the decile with a median price of 98 GBP per MWh. Its rank correlation with price is -0.066, and price cannot be separated from season here. Generator Z's active share is 3% in the cheapest decile and 9% to 16% from the fifth decile up, on 400 active half-hours.

National demand and embedded wind generation add little. Rank correlations with national demand are 0.175 (X, 0.038 after removing hour means), -0.085 (Y), and -0.280 (Z, -0.002 after removing hour means). Rank correlation with embedded wind generation stays within 0.03 for X and Y, and is -0.286 for Z, which rests on 400 active half-hours.

docs.title: Verdict and next step
docs.text:
• H0 fails for Y and Z on data grounds and is untested for X. The prediction that at least two of three series fail H0 holds, and so does the prediction that Generator Z fails the stage 2 gate. No weather-and-calendar forecast was fitted, so whether one describes Generator X is open.
  • Gate in half-hours. Generator X has 91,387 valid half-hours (passes 35,040). Generator Y has 119,514, of which 83,147 fall up to its last active month; it passes by count and fails by regime (Figure 1). Generator Z has 4,643 (fails).
  • Options for stage 2. (a) Generator X alone, about 36 to 48 fits (1.5 to 2 GPU-hours at 2.5 minutes per fit). (b) Generators X and Y with Generator Y's four folds placed before 2024-07, about 72 to 96 fits and 3 to 4 GPU-hours. The choice belongs to the ML manager.
  • Stop rule. If the best forecast arm does not beat climatology and persistence, the generators are not forecastable from the available inputs.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Cleaning. The substation_zero rule flagged no half-hour at any of the three series, so no flagged exact-zero half-hours were dropped or reported.
  • Idle texture. Generators X and Y idle at small imports, not zero. The median idle reading is -0.13% (X) and -1.5% (Y) of the maximum, like the solar import in experiment 433 and unlike the wind farms' exact zeros and repeats in experiment 210.
  • Unexplained zeros. Generator Y reads exact zero in 6,151 half-hours of 2020 (43% of its idle half-hours that year) and in 4,594 of 2025 (26%); its other years hold under 900 each. Generator X has 1,233 exact zeros in 2021 and under 810 in each later year.
  • Stuck runs. Longest runs of one value, counted in consecutive recorded rows (a run can cross a gap): X 278 half-hours of exact zero, Y 156, Z 2,384. The longest non-zero run is 23 half-hours (X, at a small import) and 4 (Y). X has 47 non-zero runs over 6 half-hours.
  • Timestamps. All timestamps are UTC-labelled and fall on the half-hour. Generator Y's hour-of-day profile is too flat to test the timestamp convention, and Generator X's peaks do not decide it, so the convention rests on the metadata.
  • Sign. Positive means export, as in experiment 223. Both signs are valid readings.
  • Units and capacity. The metadata lists all three in MW. No stated capacity is compared with the readings, so "above stated capacity" was not checked, and capacity fractions use each series' own maximum absolute output.
  • Weather. No site weather was joined. National demand and embedded wind generation are weak weather proxies, and the rank correlations carry no interval because half-hours are autocorrelated.
  • Not applicable. The avoidable-curtailment cost needs an agreed economic story, and none has been agreed. A production forecast would need a live price or dispatch feed, and none is available to us.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's event logs may miss outages, so the idle spells of all three series may include unlogged outages.

docs.title: PV capacity: a placebo-gated ladder and a per-Primary table with intervals
docs.text:
How to read the NGED table. The table is in nged_table.md, beside this page. Each row is one Primary, meaning one primary substation. The capacity columns give the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile, across bootstrap resamples of the fit, of the estimated solar capacity behind that substation's meter, in megawatts. AC capacity is what the inverters can export. DC capacity is the panels' rating, assumed to be 1.1 to 1.5 times the AC capacity. A narrow range does not mean a certain estimate. The Confidence column says how well the method found a metered solar farm that we added to a Primary's reading as a test, and the Status column names Primaries that need extra care. Every row's placebo test failed (the next paragraph explains the test).

Take-home message (generalised additive model side, interim): no candidate solar shape passes the placebo test, and a cloud-load term is what makes the capacity ranges honest. The test of a candidate method, called a rung, injects a metered solar farm's output into a Primary's reading and asks the convex fit of experiment 129 to find it again. Recovery is the share of the injected output the fit finds (1 is all of it). Without the cloud terms, each rung recovers 0.75 to 0.94. The placebo test injects a fake farm that keeps the season and time of day but not the real daily weather: the farm's day-of-year profile plus the anomaly of another day of the same month. A rung passes only if the 95th percentile of the placebo's recovery stays under 0.20. It reaches 0.25 to 0.40 (the maximum over Primaries), because the profile alone recovers 0.13 to 0.26 (0.39 to 0.41 once the cloud terms are added). A cloud-following load (extra demand on cloudy days) lowers the 80% interval's coverage of the injected capacity to 0% to 24% at every rung without the cloud terms. Two smooth cloud terms in the fit (day-mean and half-hour cloud response) restore coverage to 73% to 93%, and raise the placebo to 0.49 to 0.51. The table therefore uses the rung with the best coverage in both cases: the pooled plant table driven by the mean of ERA5 and CAMS irradiance, with the cloud terms (recovery 0.87).

docs.title: Ladder results
docs.text:
Raw recovery over 6 Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) and 5 farms, with injections of 2 and 4 MW. Placebo, profile-only, and cloud-load tests use 2 MW. Placebo figures are the 95th percentile over 20 shuffles, taken as the maximum over Primaries. Coverage figures are the 80% interval widened by the spread of recoveries, except where C0 also gives the bootstrap alone. Numbers are in the private file work/rung_summary.parquet; the main rows follow. CAMS is the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service's satellite irradiance, and ERA5 is the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' reanalysis (an estimate of past weather). A rung is one candidate solar shape: C rungs come from experiments 129 and 269 (C0 is the mean learned plant response of the other farms read at the Primary's irradiance, and C1 and C1b are physics shapes at two panel tilts), and R rungs were added in this experiment.

  • C0, pooled plant table (CAMS sky): recovery 0.874, placebo 95th percentile 0.36 (maximum over Primaries), coverage 27% (bootstrap alone) and 80% (bootstrap plus recovery spread); with a cloud- following load 0% and 7%.
  • C1, physics shape, tilt 20 degrees: 0.823, placebo 0.28, coverage 75%; cloud load 0%.
  • C1b, physics shape, tilt 35 degrees: 0.752, placebo 0.25, coverage 75%; cloud load 0%.
  • R1, nearest farm's recorded output as the shape (instead of CAMS): 0.876, placebo 0.35, coverage 79%; cloud load 24%.
  • R2, nearest farm's learned plant response: 0.881, placebo 0.36, coverage 86%.
  • R3, pooled table plus nearest farm's output (as well as CAMS): 0.938, placebo 0.37, coverage 79%.
  • R4, pooled table driven by the mean of ERA5 and CAMS irradiance: 0.940, placebo 0.40, coverage 85%; cloud load 3%.
  • R5, pooled table driven by ERA5 alone: 0.814, placebo 0.40, coverage 77%.
  • With the cloud terms: C0 0.882 (placebo 0.49, coverage 77%, cloud load 73%); C1 1.030 (0.51, 80%, 80%); R4 0.868 (0.51, 93%, 93%).

docs.title: Table for NGED (nged_table.md)
docs.text: The table is in nged_table.md (latest season-year) and in the private file work/nged_table.parquet (every season-year). The table uses rung R4 with the cloud terms. DC capacity is AC capacity times an assumed ratio between 1.1 and 1.5 (centre 1.25), because experiment 73 found that the ratio cannot be fitted.

docs.title: Where the neural estimate is reported (experiment 477)
docs.text: The neural estimate and the pros-and-cons scores are on the page of experiment 477, which also holds the side-by-side plot of neural and GAM capacities. Experiment 477 reads this experiment's files: the table nged_table.md (latest season-year), and the private files work/nged_table.parquet (every season-year, with the columns ac_p10, ac_p50, ac_p90, dc_p10, dc_p50, dc_p90, pinned_mw, status) and work/rung_summary.parquet, under data/ml-experiments/00474-pv-capacity-placebo-gated-ladder-and-per-primary-intervals/.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• No rung passes the placebo gate, so every capacity carries a "gate failed" note.
  • D12 uses the physical fleet shape and the fit through the meter; D15 is a generator case with no estimate; D18 has data only from 2025-03-01.
  • MVA-only Primaries are fitted to apparent power with reactive power assumed zero, which experiment 370 found fails at a power factor of 0.97.
  • The cloud-load test uses one form of load (experiment 129's), and the cloud terms match that form exactly, so the restored coverage is an optimistic figure.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the readings may hold unlabelled events.
  • Deviations from the plan: 20 placebo shuffles ran at every rung (the plan's metric line said 5 at some rungs); the injection test ran at 6 Primaries and the prediction text counts 5; C3 (a rise allowed, a fall resisted) was dropped because the fit already boxes every capacity increment to be non-negative, so the capacity path cannot fall; C2 was applied after the fit as an assumed ratio.
  • The D12 bootstrap ran about 30 resamples (each fit takes about 40 seconds).

docs.title: Does the first-release candidate recipe forecast the two bulk supply points and two grid supply points better than the pooled plain network of experiment 415?
docs.text: Take-home message: the first-release recipe does not clearly beat the plain pooled network at the bulk supply points, but it gains about 0.5 points of capacity at the grid supply points. The registered rule needs a win at both bulk supply points, so the verdict is not supported. The recipe lowers CRPS below BG2 at all four nodes. Only four nodes have a usable series (two bulk and two grid supply points), so every node result is a case study with n = 4, and four test months make every interval interim.

docs.title: Question and what experiment 415 already answered
docs.text: Experiment 415 fitted one pooled plain network (experiment 397's recipe) on the 16 Primaries and the four nodes (D13 and D17 are bulk supply points; D1 and D6 are grid supply points) with a node-type input. It beat BG2 by 0.47 points of effective capacity at the bulk supply points, tied it at the grid supply points, and found that the Primaries' lags add nothing. This experiment does not repeat 415's N1, N2, N3, or N4(a). It asks only whether the better recipe, which the first-release candidate will use, improves on 415's N1 at the four nodes. Only four nodes have a usable series (2 bulk, 2 grid), so every node result is a case study with n = 4, and a pooled-by-type network would pool two series.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• Reused, not refitted: 415's N1 (3 seeds, 4 folds; 00415.../work/seed_preds/N1), and experiment 386's BG2, monthly XGBoost control, GAM stack, manual_heuristic, and climatology.
  • A-nodes (fitted): experiment 425's arm A recipe (loop e00425_fit.py, which imports experiment 418's ERA5-and-CAMS pretraining rows) extended from 16 to 20 series, with 415's node-type input and 415's ensemble-summary node weather. ERA5 rows exist for all four nodes.
  • S1-nodes (fitted if the timing gate passes): the S1 base with lags and surprise inputs (loop of experiment 428). Experiment 415 used experiment 397's loop, which has no surprise inputs; A-nodes uses 425's loop and S1-nodes uses 428's, and the page says which.
  • Report-only: a per-type pooled network (two series each) and the metered generators as children (N4(b), which experiment 223 left untested because unmetered solar and the battery confound it). Experiment 470 (the demand assembly) has not reported; if it reports before the fits finish, its base replaces A-nodes.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Four folds: 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06; 24 months of training before each; monthly refits; three seeds. A fit sees only data before its forecast time.
  • Cleaned data with flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped; D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 (applied). The dropped counts per fold are reported.
  • Compute: one GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core, MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. One fit is timed first and the total (fits and GPU-hours) goes to the manager before the rest.
  • Lags: the nodes' series support the three origin lags used for the Primaries (newest reading, same time of day on the latest day and the latest week); the plan checks that each node has them in all four folds.
  • Process: code review by a fresh Sonnet agent before the first fit, results review, write-up review; Bonferroni count 8 (4 nodes, 2 contrasts each: against 415's N1 and against BG2).

docs.title: Decision rule
docs.text:
Registered before any score is read.

  • Minimum detectable effect: the seed spread of 415's N1 at the grid supply points (per-seed spread of 415's N1: 0.44 at D1 and 0.79 at D6; about 0.4 is the low end), stated before any contrast.
  • The recipe is a candidate for the nodes if its point estimate beats 415's N1 at both bulk supply points and does not lose at the grid supply points, with q99 pinball loss within 5%.
  • A node-level contrast inside the minimum detectable effect is inconclusive.
  • Otherwise 415's N1 stays the node forecaster and BG2 is the reference at the grid supply points.
  • The curtailment cost does not apply at nodes (no generator tables), and the page says so.
  • Interim: four test months give wide intervals; the bootstrap over four month blocks cannot reach 95%.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• 415's N1 is a 3-seed average and BG2 a single weekly fit; the contrast against BG2 depends on cadence and seed count and is stated that way.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete: rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events.
  • The forecast frames omit the 2026-06-30 run, as in 415.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS at days 1 to 10 in points of effective capacity, four test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), equal-row set of 62,419 half-hours per node across all leads, then restricted to days 1 to 10 (shared with experiment 386; 2,747 of 65,166 not scored). A and N1 are 3-seed averages; BG2 is a single weekly fit.

Node A 415's N1 BG2 (weekly-refit XGBoost best guess) Monthly XGBoost, bands widened by 1.15 manual_heuristic climatology D13 (bulk supply point) 4.61 4.52 4.94 4.99 5.80 6.06 D17 (bulk supply point) 6.66 6.80 7.31 7.39 8.82 8.89 D1 (grid supply point) 13.92 14.41 14.52 14.70 19.18 18.29 D6 (grid supply point) 13.69 14.26 14.19 14.33 15.92 15.37
  • A minus N1: BSPs -0.025 (-0.104 to +0.053); GSPs -0.532 (-0.815 to -0.215). Per node: D13 +0.09, D17 -0.14, D1 -0.50, D6 -0.57.
  • A minus BG2: BSPs -0.491 (-0.661 to -0.299); GSPs -0.550 (-0.943 to -0.116). A minus the widened monthly XGBoost: -0.557 and -0.710. A minus manual_heuristic: -1.68 and -3.75. A minus climatology: -1.84 and -3.03.
  • Decision rule: not met. A loses to N1 at D13 by 0.09, inside the minimum detectable effect (about 0.4). Its gain at the grid supply points (0.5) is only just above the minimum detectable effect, and the intervals resample four test months, so they are interim.
  • Tails (A against N1, days 1 to 10), q99 pinball loss: D13 0.246 against 0.242 (+1.7%), D17 0.355 against 0.362 (-1.8%), D1 0.787 against 0.797 (-1.3%), D6 0.604 against 0.626 (-3.5%); all within 5%. q95 coverage of A: 0.878 (D13), 0.935 (D17), 0.952 (D1), 0.920 (D6); the D13 upper tail is still too narrow, as in N1 (0.876).
  • Predictions: P1 failed (we predicted -0.30 to 0.0 at the BSPs; D13 was +0.09). P2 failed in size (we predicted -0.30 to +0.30 at the GSPs; the gain was -0.5). P3 held. P4 held: A is below BG2 at all four nodes.
  • Bonferroni count: 8 (four nodes by two contrasts); the intervals above are unadjusted 95% intervals.

docs.title: Setup and caveats
docs.text:
• Recipe. Experiment 425's arm A: ERA5-and-CAMS pretraining (about 10.7 million rows), fine-tuning on 7.17 million ensemble-summary rows (2026-06 fold), setting g09, monthly refits, 3 seeds. Pooled with the 16 Primaries and a node-type input. The loop is experiment 425's (e00425_fit.py); experiment 415 used experiment 397's loop. Code: ml-experiments/00475-*/, importing experiments 87, 397, 407, 415, 418, and 425.
  • Cuts. D15 and D18 rows before 2025-03-01 dropped; flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped from training rows (2026-06 fold: 68,680 start-cut and 4,073 flagged-zero fine-tuning rows). Scoring uses experiment 386's equal-row set, which is not re-cleaned for A.
  • Not like for like with 425. The standardiser and the ensemble-spread table are fitted on all 20 series; experiment 425 used the 16 Primaries. No early-history cut was set for the nodes (their data start 2019-09-17, D17 in 2022-07).
  • Not run: S1 (experiment 428's loop; it needs new code), the per-type pooled arm, and the generators-as-children arm. Curtailment cost does not apply at nodes, and no load-shift plots are drawn because no load-shift label is used. Nodes are substations, so no generator is named.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first fit (no bugs; its findings on node early-history cuts and flagged-zero keys were checked and needed no change), and a second reviewed the numbers and prose; the fixes are applied. The figures were not rendered for a visual check in this session (no browser available).
  • Interim. Four test months; NGED's event labels are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Run S1 on the nodes if the demand assembly (experiment 470) adopts it.
  • Repeat the grid supply points with more seeds to settle whether 0.5 exceeds the refit noise.

docs.title: Problems caused by the move
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Can a mixture density network forecast Generator X better than same-hour climatology and last-output persistence, and do weather or price inputs help?
docs.text: Generator X's output is not forecastable from calendar, recent output, weather, or lagged price: the best of four network versions beats the usual output at the same half-hour, weekday type, and season (climatology) by 0.015 points, below the 0.019-point minimum detectable effect. One point is 1% of Generator X's maximum absolute output, measured on the quantile score (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels). The minimum detectable effect is the seed-to-seed spread of the score. We asked whether a mixture density network, a neural network that outputs a probability distribution, can forecast Generator X's output (positive for export, negative for import) better than two plain references: climatology, and persistence (the last output seen before the forecast was made). We fitted four versions of the network that differ in their inputs, for 4 test months and 3 random seeds each (4 versions x 4 test months x 3 seeds = 48 fits). Each version was scored on 55,533 forecast half-hours (pairs of forecast origin and lead time, up to 10 days ahead). Every version beats persistence by about 4 points of quantile score. No version beats climatology by more than the minimum detectable effect, so the stop rule we fixed before fitting fires: stop if no version beats both references by more than that effect. The result narrows the search to inputs of a different kind, such as the operator's dispatch schedule.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are in points, one point being 1% of Generator X's maximum absolute output; smaller is better. The metric is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, averaged over 3 seeds, for leads up to 240 hours. The setup is four test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 24-month training windows, monthly refits, and equal rows for every arm. The intervals are interim.

  • Arms. A0: calendar and the three origin lags. A1: A0 plus ensemble weather mean and spread. A2: A0 plus market index price at the three lag times. A3: calendar and weather, no lags.
  • Absolute scores, days 1 to 10. A0 4.068, A1 4.065, A2 4.004, A3 4.210, climatology 4.018, persistence 8.267. In the 12 to 36 hour band: A0 4.229, A2 4.173, climatology 4.232.
  • Noise floor. The minimum detectable effect is 0.019 points (A0's seed spread). There are 5 planned comparisons (the Bonferroni count), so each interval is widened to the 99% level.
  • C1, A0 minus climatology. +0.050 (interval -0.008 to +0.103); A0 loses in 3 of the 4 test months (2026-01 +0.211, 2026-03 +0.091, 2025-10 +0.038, 2026-06 -0.206).
  • C2, A0 minus persistence. -4.199 (-5.740 to -3.109).
  • C3, A1 minus A0. -0.003 (-0.024 to +0.016). Weather adds nothing.
  • C4, A2 minus A0. -0.065 (-0.085 to -0.046), negative in all four months. A2 minus climatology (post hoc, not a planned contrast) is -0.015, below the noise floor.
  • C5, A3 minus climatology. +0.192 (+0.144 to +0.244). Weather and calendar alone lose.
  • Tails, days 1 to 10 (pinball q01 / q05 / q95 / q99). A0 0.596 / 1.448 / 1.369 / 0.563; A2 0.583 / 1.437 / 1.312 / 0.508; climatology 0.791 / 1.540 / 1.411 / 0.724. Coverage (share of actuals at or below the quantile; nominal 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.95 / 0.99): A0 0.019 / 0.058 / 0.924 / 0.980; A2 0.018 / 0.063 / 0.942 / 0.983; climatology 0.029 / 0.067 / 0.933 / 0.971. The network sharpens both tails and loses in the middle levels.
  • Median error. Mean absolute error of the median: A0 6.015, A2 5.977, climatology 5.881.
  • Idle and active half-hours (idle means output under 5% of the maximum; 35,475 of 55,533 rows). Score on idle rows: A0 1.105, A2 1.125, climatology 1.218. On active rows: A0 9.310, A2 9.096, climatology 8.971.
  • Sign (import versus export). Brier score of the probability of a negative output: A0 0.2404, A2 0.2344, climatology 0.2257. Accuracy: 58.4%, 61.1%, 63.3%. No arm beats the cell frequency.
  • Widening sweep (days 1 to 10). Multiplying every spread by 1.15 gives A0 4.044, A2 3.984; by 1.3 gives A0 4.041, A2 3.986. A2 at 1.15 beats climatology by 0.034, but that is a post hoc choice of factor.

Prediction check. The plan predicted A0 would beat climatology by 3% to 10% at 12 to 36 hours; A0 scored 0.1% better (-0.004 points), so the prediction failed. The prediction that weather adds nothing (C3) held at days 1 to 10 only: in the 12 to 36 hour band A1 scores 0.035 worse than A0 (interval +0.001 to +0.077). The prediction that A0 would beat climatology by under 2% beyond 3 days failed: from 3 to 10 days A0 scores 0.071 worse (interval +0.006 to +0.133). The prediction that A0 beats persistence beyond 6 hours held (C2). The prediction that A3 stays within one minimum detectable effect of climatology failed (A3 is 0.19 worse). The prediction that price adds nothing failed (C4). The sign prediction failed: no arm beat the overall share of negative half-hours in the same calendar group.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers. Two audit triggers fired: the quantile-score and median-error contrasts of A0 against climatology point opposite ways, and the price result (C4) contradicts its prediction. A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the headline scores from the stored forecasts (all reproduced) and found: the tail gain explains the median reversal; the price lags leak nothing (newest price lag is exactly 3.5 hours before the origin, a completed settlement period); and the first climatology fell back to the whole training window for about 29% of rows, which understated it. We replaced that climatology with one pooled over three neighbouring months and report the old one only as a sensitivity (days 1 to 10: 4.129). The audit also found the weekend flag marked Friday; the flag was fixed and all 48 fits were rerun, so no number from the first runs is quoted.
  • Median minus mean forecast. The median-error figures are in Results. The mean forecast was not scored, because the quantile scores carry the contrast.
  • Cleaning. The substation_zero rule flagged no half-hour of Generator X, so none was dropped; exact zeros are kept as readings. The 2026-06 test month loses leads past 2026-07-01 for late-June origins, so lead bands are not balanced in that fold.
  • Epoch cap. A first run capped at 40 epochs stopped 42 of 48 fits early; the cap is 200 and no fit reached it.
  • Persistence. The newest reading was missing for 1,578 rows; they use the climatology median. The 12 to 36 hour band and days 1 to 10 are scored; the predicted loss to persistence under 3 hours was not tested.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• No curtailment cost. No avoidable-curtailment cost is computed, because no economic story is agreed. A forecast that uses price lags needs a live price feed that does not exist today.
  • Weather. The weather is the stored ensemble summary of a Primary within 1 km of the site (a Primary substation), so the inputs are not the weather grid cell that contains the site.
  • Interim. Four test months and one series give wide intervals; the score trend with lead in figure 3 reflects the mix of test months, and climatology falls with lead as well.
  • Anonymisation. The example forecasts (a day-ahead and two 10-day forecasts, one winter and one summer) stay in the private store, because they plot Generator X's own half-hourly output.
  • Next step. An input that carries the operator's dispatch, not a different network.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• Scripts. ml-experiments/00476-generator-x-first-forecast-dispatch-lags-weather-price/ holds e00476_fit.py, e00476_score.py, and e00476_charts.py; it reuses code from experiments 87 and 397, and the lag recipe of experiment 428.
  • Stored forecasts, networks, and tables. Private, under data/ml-experiments/00476-generator-x-first-forecast-dispatch-lags-weather-price/ (work/ holds the networks and one forecast table per arm, month, and seed).
  • Citations. The network is the mixture density network of Bishop (1994).

docs.title: Does the explicit PV module inside the net demand neural network recover a plausible, placebo- gated capacity per Primary, and what does the explicit split improve or worsen the forecast on sunny half-hours?
docs.text:
Take-home: the capacities that the PV module learns are unvalidated, and the explicit split changes the forecast by less than the noise. In a known-answer test, the PV module read a placebo as strongly as a real solar farm, so its capacity cannot yet be trusted as a measurement of unmetered solar capacity. The explicit split moves the forecast by less than the seed-to-seed noise.

Experiment 416 fitted a neural network that forecasts net demand (demand minus solar output) at each Primary substation. The network has a PV module (a learned solar capacity per Primary times a physics curve of irradiance and temperature) beside a demand module that gets no direct irradiance. This experiment asks whether the learned capacity is a measurement. The test adds a known solar farm's output to six Primaries' data and checks whether the capacity rises by the injected megawatts. A Primary passes the gate only if the real farm is read out above a placebo (the same farm's monthly daylight profile with its day-to-day sky shuffled within the month) by more than 2 seed standard deviations.

Name PV module Irradiance input Power lags Day-of-year inputs C3 (PV-split) yes only through the PV module yes yes A0-doy (free irradiance) no free input yes yes A0-noirr-doy no none yes yes H1 yes free input and PV module yes yes C3-nolag yes only through the PV module no yes C3p-weak yes (weak log prior on capacity) only through the PV module yes yes

Power lags are the network's inputs of the Primary's own earlier power readings. The read-out is the megawatts obtained by regressing the change in a network's median forecast (against the same network with no injection) on the ensemble's unit shape of irradiance; a read-out of 1 is the full injection. The capacity increment is the change in the learned capacity parameter of the PV module. "Signed-MW six" means the six Primaries whose telemetry carries the sign of power flow (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16); D15 and D18 are report-only. Sunny middays are half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 with a CAMS clear-sky index of at least 0.7. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, in points of effective capacity.

The placebo gate failed at all six signed-MW Primaries. The PV-split network read the 4 MW real farm out at 0.86 to 0.92 and the placebo at 0.90 to 0.95. The A0-doy network, which has no PV module, read the placebo out at 0.91 to 0.97. The read-out therefore measures the profile that a network learns from the hour and the day of year, not the sky.

The forecast difference matches experiment 416. On sunny middays C3 minus A0-doy is +0.223 CRPS points (interval -0.137 to +0.556), against a minimum detectable effect of 0.365. The 0.02 loss limit of the decision rule cannot be tested at an overall minimum detectable effect of 0.105. The overall point estimate is +0.023 CRPS points (interval -0.031 to +0.070), and q99 pinball loss at days 1 to 10 is -0.021, about 7% lower. Adoption therefore rests on the explanation clause. That clause needs capacities that pass the gate. The capacities do not pass, so the PV module is not recommended for production on this evidence.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. Stored from experiment 416, not refitted: A0-doy (free irradiance, no PV module), A0-noirr-doy, C3 (PV-split), H1 (explicit term plus free irradiance), C3p-weak (weak log prior). New: C3-nolag (C3 with the power lags held constant), fitted on the 5 fold months of experiment 449, 3 seeds. Base recipe: experiment 397's plain loop with day-of-year inputs and no pretraining. Physics as experiment 405 (ensemble-mean and spread of shortwave, tilt 35, DC to AC 1.15, 0.4% per kelvin). Monthly refits.
  • Rows. One shared set of half-hours with the stack, BG2, the manual heuristic, and climatology (row set fold_a_daily_gap_v1); signed-MW six; D15 and D18 report-only and excluded from the six; D5 (export limit) and D12 (reverse flow, no PV module) marked. Flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped; D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01. Neural arms raw (no 1.15 widening); references as stored.
  • Gate limit. The limit per Primary was written before any C3 placebo score: D5 0.973, D9 0.924, D10 0.921, D11 0.914, D14 0.941, D16 0.944.
  • Gate result. The first clause passes everywhere because the limit is so high. The second clause (real farm above the placebo by 2 seed standard deviations) fails at all six Primaries. Real minus placebo in read-out is -0.027 to -0.046.
  • Capacity increment. The learned capacity rises by 0.17 to 0.45 of the injected 4 MW (0.03 to 0.46 across all real-farm injections). Real minus placebo in capacity increment is +0.06 to +0.15, which lies inside 2 standard deviations at 5 of the 6 Primaries (D14 is the exception).
  • Lags. The real-farm capacity increment (in fractions of the injected 4 MW, in the order D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) is 0.24, 0.41, 0.43, 0.25, 0.25, 0.17 for C3-nolag and 0.30, 0.40, 0.43, 0.17, 0.17, 0.17 for C3. It is higher without lags at D9, D10, D11, and D14 on point estimates, all inside seed noise, and the read-out is lower at all six (0.836 to 0.904 against 0.858 to 0.924). Removing the lags worsened CRPS by 0.249 points at days 1 to 10 (interval +0.113 to +0.422) and by 0.139 on sunny middays (interval +0.006 to +0.210).
  • Capacity. Neural medians (season-year 2025) against the GAM: D5 3.19 against 3.15 MW, D9 0.93 against 2.15, D10 2.06 against 2.89, D11 2.33 against 3.19, D14 2.65 against 3.74, D16 2.76 against 3.08, D18 1.82 against 1.82. D15 has no GAM estimate. See the experiment 474 page.

docs.title: Pros and cons of explicit PV for net demand
docs.text:
12 months, signed-MW six, CRPS in points of effective capacity (absolute scores), days 1 to 10 unless stated. Bonferroni count: 6 tests (3 contrasts, 2 metrics), level 99.17%.

Slice A0-doy A0-noirr-doy C3 H1 Stack BG2 Manual heuristic Climatology Overall 2.961 3.002 2.985 2.961 2.949 3.016 3.606 3.832 Sunny middays 4.263 4.366 4.486 4.490 4.888 4.497 5.600 5.693 All daylight 3.730 3.833 3.783 3.745 3.861 3.893 4.550 4.674 Cloudy daylight 4.705 4.916 4.668 4.569 4.194 4.863 5.617 5.769 12 to 36 hours 2.652 2.719 2.687 2.659 2.416 2.594 3.603 3.852 Cold winter nights 4.688 4.616 4.633 4.715 4.183 4.553 6.283 6.573
  • Where explicit PV helps. The PV module narrows the upper tail: q99 pinball loss on sunny middays is 0.310 for C3 against 0.314 for A0-doy and 0.320 for A0-noirr-doy, and over days 1 to 10 it is 0.285 against 0.306 and 0.309; q99 coverage is 0.966 against 0.960. The PV-split network scores better than A0-noirr-doy on cloudy daylight (-0.248, interval -0.479 to -0.029). The PV module gives a PV profile that can be plotted by sky condition (third figure).
  • Where explicit PV worsens the forecast. On sunny middays C3 is +0.223 CRPS points worse than A0-doy (not significant). The capacity is not identified (gate). The module needs a capacity table per Primary (refreshed at each monthly refit) and a physics chain on ensemble irradiance and temperature at forecast time. Removing the lags, one way to force the PV module to carry the sky, worsens the forecast.
  • Minimum detectable effect. Sunny middays 0.365 (12 months), 0.275 (5 fold months); overall 0.105 and 0.126. None of the C3 contrasts against A0-doy or A0-noirr-doy exceeds its minimum detectable effect; the C3-nolag minus C3 overall contrast (+0.249 against 0.114) does.
  • Fold months (5 months, 3 seeds for C3-nolag). C3 minus A0-doy sunny middays +0.193 (-0.295 to +0.645); overall -0.019. C3-nolag minus C3 overall +0.249.
  • Tails and avoidable-curtailment cost. On the 12 months q99 coverage on sunny middays is 0.996 (C3), and cold winter nights q99 pinball loss is 0.96 for C3 against 1.09 for A0-doy (stack 0.83). Christmas week (report-only, 20,736 rows): CRPS 4.32 C3, 4.50 A0-doy, 3.71 BG2. Avoidable-curtailment cost, energy-proxy, sum over the six Primaries and the scored months, GBP million at limit fractions 0.9, 0.75, 0.5: C3 9.55, 28.23, 80.81; A0-doy 9.49, 28.61, 82.06; stack 4.24, 16.62, 59.80; manual heuristic 10.41, 37.43, 104.84. D14 and D16 dominate the totals.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• (1) C3 recovers 0.4 to 0.9 of the injected megawatts at 4 of 6 Primaries: fails; the capacity increment reaches 0.4 at 2 of 6 (D9 and D10).
  • (2) The placebo stays under the limit and the real farm beats it by 2 seed standard deviations at 4 of 6: the first half holds at 6 of 6 (the limit is high); the second half holds at 0 of 6 on the read-out and 1 of 6 on the capacity increment (D14).
  • (3) C3-nolag recovers more than C3 at 4 of 6: holds on point estimates (capacity increment), not beyond seed noise.
  • (4) Sunny-midday C3 minus A0-doy repeats experiment 416: holds (+0.223, interval -0.137 to +0.556).
  • Departure from rule 1. Rule 1 defines recovery on the capacity increment, and the gate limit is defined on the read-out. The gate was applied to the read-out, which applies to A0-doy too. On the capacity increment the gate fails at 5 of 6 Primaries.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the injection and fit code before the first fit and found no bugs; three small fixes were applied (saved lead and validation flag, an assertion on the six lag columns, the read-out restricted to the signed six). Reviews of the results and of this page are recorded in the pull request.
  • Not computed. Median minus mean forecast per site and the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast were not computed; this experiment re-scores stored forecasts.
  • Caveats. The read-out uses rows inside the fold's own training window (in sample), so it measures attribution, not skill. Injected megawatts are in units of the farm's 99th-percentile output. NGED's event labels are incomplete: rows with no labelled event may still hold unlabelled events. The equivalent capacity is a least-squares read-out on the ensemble unit shape. The C3-nolag fits used 3 seeds; the stored arms use 5.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Inject the anomaly only. An injection whose daylight profile is removed (experiment 409's anomaly variant) at 4 MW or more tests the sky read-out without the profile that any network absorbs.
  • Use the GAM capacity as the PV module's capacity (pinned, as C1 of experiment 405) and judge the neural module on the forecast only.

docs.title: What is asked
docs.text: The question is whether the PV module of the net demand neural network reads the sky well enough to give a capacity per Primary worth plotting, and whether the explicit split helps or hurts the net demand forecast. This experiment reuses the four stored score arms of experiment 416 and fits only the new work.

docs.title: Review of the plan against the latest evidence
docs.text:
• Reused, not refitted: A0-doy (A-free), A0-noirr-doy (No-irr), C3 (PV-split), C3p-weak (weak prior), and H1 (explicit term plus free irradiance), from experiment 416's work/seed_preds/, 12 months, 5 seeds, with the *.capacity.json files.
  • Base recipe: experiment 397's plain loop (e00397_prep, e00405_{prep,models,pv,fit}, e00409_*, e00416_*), day-of-year inputs, no pretraining. Experiment 425's arm A (pretrained) is a reference row only.
  • Physics as in experiment 405: irradiance is the ensemble mean and spread of shortwave in training and forecasting alike; CAMS defines the sunny flag at scoring only. Tilt 35 degrees, DC to AC ratio 1.15, 0.4% per kelvin. The brief's 1.25 ratio and its 1.1 and 1.5 sensitivity are dropped, because they break the reuse of every stored C3 fit.
  • Scope: the six signed-MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16), with D15 and D18 report-only. D5 (export limit), D12 (reverse flow, no PV module), D15 and D18 are marked in every table. The MVA-only Primaries are covered by experiment 474's GAM-side table.
  • Standing rules followed: cleaned data, the D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01, monthly refits, saved networks, the tails, the seven-step process, draft pull request.

docs.title: New work (about 50 fits, one GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core)
docs.text:
1. Placebo and injection (runs first, gates the capacity plots). On the 2026-06 fold, 3 seeds, inject a metered solar farm's output (Solar A and Solar C of the six; named only by letter) into all six signed-MW Primaries, with the lags injected as in experiment 405. Conditions: control (no injection); held farm at 2 MW and 4 MW for both farms; placebo (the farm's monthly daylight profile plus its day-to-day anomaly shuffled within the calendar month, 4 MW); profile only (the farm's monthly daylight profile, 4 MW). C3 takes all of them (7 conditions, 21 fits). A0-doy takes control, placebo, and profile only (9 fits) to calibrate the gate.
  2. One new arm: C3-nolag. C3 with the three power-lag values and their missing flags held constant in training and at inference. It is fitted on the five fold months of experiment 449 (3 seeds, 15 fits) and on control and the 4 MW held farm in the 2026-06 fold (6 fits).
  3. Re-scoring on CPU: the stored arms plus C3-nolag on the 12 months and on the five fold months of experiment 449, from stored forecasts.
  4. Plots: capacity per Primary with the prior and the 10th to 90th percentile over seeds, beside experiment 474's GAM estimates; implied PV on a sunny and a cloudy day; PV share of net demand by hour; recovery against injected MW.

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
1. Recovery is the seed-mean learned capacity increment (injected minus control, last season-year cell) divided by the injected MW, per Primary. The least-squares read-out of experiment 409 (dC_LS) is reported beside it.
  2. The gate limit is the equivalent capacity that A0-doy shows on the profile-only injection: the least-squares regression of the change in its median forecast between control and the injection on the ensemble unit shape, over daylight rows of the 2026-06 test month, divided by the injected MW. The limit is the larger of the profile-only equivalent and the placebo equivalent, seed-averaged, per Primary. The number is committed to this page, in a separate commit, before any PV-split placebo score is read.
  3. The gate passes at a Primary when C3's placebo recovery is at most that Primary's limit plus 0.20, and the held-farm recovery exceeds the placebo recovery by more than 2 seed standard deviations. A failed gate marks the Primary's capacity "unvalidated" in the plots. Scores are reported regardless.
  4. Score contrasts (12 months and the five fold months, signed-MW six, CRPS days 1 to 10 and sunny middays): C3 minus A0-doy, C3 minus A0-noirr-doy, C3-nolag minus C3 (fold months only). Month-block bootstrap at 95% with 20,000 resamples, Bonferroni across the 3, one equal-row intersection (row set fold_a_daily_gap_v1), minimum detectable effect first. Sunny middays are CAMS clear-sky index at least 0.7, 10:00 to 15:00.
  5. Other scores: q01, q05, q95, and q99 coverage and pinball loss; the 12 to 36 hour band; cold winter nights; Christmas week (report-only); the 1.15 widening; avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5 for the signed-MW six (metrics.avoidable_curtailment_cost); absolute scores beside every contrast.
  6. Expected result: close to experiment 416, which is not new evidence by itself. The 0.02 loss limit is untestable at the sunny-midday minimum detectable effect of 0.28 to 0.37 (overall 0.057).

docs.title: Gate limit (written after the A0-doy fits and before any C3 placebo score was read)
docs.text: The limit is non-binding: A0-doy recovers 0.91 to 0.97 of the injected megawatts from the placebo, and 0.84 to 0.89 from the profile alone. The free-irradiance network absorbs the farm's monthly daylight profile through its hour and day-of-year inputs, and the profile is most of the injected signal. Limits per Primary (placebo recovery, the larger of the two): D5 0.973, D9 0.924, D10 0.921, D11 0.914, D14 0.941, D16 0.944. Rule 3 stands as written, so the first clause (C3 placebo recovery at most the limit plus 0.20) can only fail above about 1.1, and the discriminating clause is the second one: the held farm must exceed the placebo by more than 2 seed standard deviations. The read-out uses rows inside the fold's own training window, so it measures how much of the injection the fitted network attributes to the sky and the profile, not out-of-sample skill.

docs.title: Production cost of the PV term
docs.text: The PV term needs a capacity table per Primary, refreshed at each monthly refit, and a physics chain (irradiance and temperature from the ensemble to plane-of-array power) at forecast time. The write- up reports this beside the score.

docs.title: Part F2 of experiment 395: what do load-shift events cost in avoidable curtailment, and how long does the harm last after an event ends?
docs.text:
A power lag inside a labelled load-shift event keeps raising the forecast error for a week after the event ends. A power lag is a past power reading that the forecast takes as an input. For the weekly bundle of experiment 381 (weekly-refitted XGBoost forecasts) at the signed-MW six, targets 0 to 24 hours after the end of the lag's event score 1.66 points of continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) worse than targets with no lag in an event (95% interval -0.06 to +3.69). Targets 3 to 7 days after score 1.05 worse (+0.04 to +2.36). The GAM stack of experiment 377 (a generalised additive model with a Kalman filter) is worse by 2.90 and 1.61 at the same two positions. The surprise arm (n1) of experiment 391 does not reduce the harm. Avoidable-curtailment cost, the pounds of generation curtailed that a perfect forecast would have avoided, cannot separate the forecasts during events, because it rests on 2 to 11 events per Primary substation.

Part F2 of experiment 395 re-scores stored forecasts and fits nothing. "Unpadded" means each event runs from its labelled onset to its labelled end, with no extra 24 hours on either side. "Signed-MW six" means the six Primaries D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, whose meters report signed megawatts. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so a comparison row is a row with no labelled event, which is not the same as a clean row. Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped as in Part F, and experiment 398 showed that dropping the flagged half-hours moves no contrast, so nothing needed repeating.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Each chart shows q95 coverage (the share of readings below the forecast's 95% quantile; nominal 0.95) by the number of lags inside an event and the length of that event, at the signed-MW six, for targets outside events.

The charts of the monthly control (coverage_monthly_control.svg), experiment 383's d, c1, and c2 (coverage_w383_*.svg), and experiment 391's o (coverage_b391_o.svg) sit in the same folder.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
All figures use leads of days 1 to 10 for harm and 12 to 36 hours for cost, drop flagged zeros, and resample whole events (95% intervals). Harm is the CRPS in points of effective capacity minus each Primary's mean on rows with no lag in an event and a target outside events.

The harm falls with distance from the event but is still distinguishable from zero 3 to 7 days after for the bundle and the GAM stack. Event counts are 30 (0-24 h), 30 (1-3 days), 34 (3-7 days), and 34 (7-21 days).

Forecast 0-24 h 1-3 days 3-7 days 7-21 days Weekly bundle +1.66 (-0.06 to +3.69) +0.98 (-0.32 to +2.32) +1.05 (+0.04 to +2.36) +0.81 (-0.07 to +2.12) Monthly control +1.41 (-0.12 to +3.63) +0.59 (-0.31 to +1.65) +0.58 (-0.07 to +1.61) +0.27 (-0.13 to +0.95) GAM stack +2.90 (+0.18 to +5.76) +1.90 (-0.35 to +4.85) +1.61 (+0.04 to +3.78) +1.27 (+0.04 to +3.18) Plain weekly member (383 d) +1.77 (-0.02 to +3.96) +0.98 (-0.28 to +2.23) +0.94 (+0.06 to +2.03) +0.78 (-0.04 to +1.97) 391 control (b0) +1.42 (-0.11 to +3.65) +0.57 (-0.30 to +1.65) +0.57 (-0.11 to +1.62) +0.26 (-0.14 to +0.97) 391 surprise (n1) +1.44 (-0.03 to +3.37) +0.75 (-0.25 to +1.60) +0.69 (+0.02 to +1.57) +0.39 (-0.11 to +1.05) 391 oracle (o) +1.25 (-0.12 to +3.01) +0.72 (-0.26 to +1.90) +0.61 (-0.13 to +1.62) +0.28 (-0.14 to +0.99)

Three lags inside an event do far more harm than one or two (+2.71 against +0.34 and +0.35). For the bundle, one lag gives +0.34 (+0.01 to +0.76), two give +0.35 (-0.33 to +1.19), and three give +2.71 (-0.19 to +5.99). printed_report.txt holds the other forecasts.

The length and depth slices are too thin to rank. The signed-MW six has 4 events longer than 7 days and 4 events in the third depth quartile, so the report prints no interval for those slices. The bundle's harm is +0.16 for events of 1 to 7 days (11 events) and +0.46 for events under 1 day (19 events), and neither interval excludes zero. The MVA-only eight are in printed_report.txt.

With Part H's corrected signs, the median follows the labelled depth about as Part H found. Part H of experiment 395 corrected the sign of each labelled depth. The share of the depth that the forecast's median follows, for events with 0 lags, 1 or 2 lags, and 3 lags inside the event:

  • Weekly bundle: 0.52, 0.83, and 0.94, as in Part H.
  • Experiment 391 control (b0): 0.60, 0.85, and 0.90.
  • Experiment 391 surprise arm (n1): 0.53, 0.86, and 0.92.
  • Experiment 391 oracle (o): 0.55, 0.85, and 0.91.

Avoidable-curtailment cost during events does not separate the forecasts. Cost is the energy proxy of metrics.avoidable_curtailment_cost at limit fraction f = 0.9 (the limit is 90% of the Primary's largest earlier reading), in pounds. Costs below are per-event means of the difference from the plain weekly member, with 99.17% pooled intervals (each of six contrasts at a 95% family-wise level) over 33 events during and 34 events after.

  • Bundle during events: -£3,752 (-£17,632 to +£149).
  • Bundle in the 7 days after events: -£558 (-£1,330 to -£26), so the bundle costs less than the weekly member, not more.
  • GAM stack during events: -£117,202 (-£543,668 to +£692).
  • GAM stack in the 7 days after: +£4,425 (+£121 to +£12,476).
  • Experiment 383's arms, including the plain weekly member, carry the 1.15 widening. The bundle and the monthly control do not, and the stack and experiment 391's arms are scored as stored. A difference from the member therefore mixes the widening with the forecast skill.

Across all rows, the GAM stack costs far less than the weekly forecasts at D14 and D16. At D14 the plain weekly member and the bundle cost £1.14 million and £1.15 million more than the stack, and at D16 £3.84 million and £3.69 million more. In the 7 days after events the bundle costs £4,983 per event less than the stack (-£13,695 to -£376). D16 has 4 events with scored rows and carries almost all of the pounds during events, D9 has none, and D11 has 2. Costs at f = 0.75 and 0.5 are in printed_report.txt.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (the bundle costs more than the member in the 7 days after events) failed: -£558 (-£1,330 to -£26).
  • P2 partly held: the point estimate is largest at 0 to 24 hours, but at 3 to 7 days the interval still excludes zero for the bundle and the stack, and at 7 to 21 days for the stack.
  • P3 failed: n1 has the same or higher harm than b0 at every position.
  • P4 cannot be tested: the signed-MW six has 4 events longer than 7 days.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Coverage of the row sets. All nine forecasts cover all 2,824,844 half-hour rows of the Part F slice table.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first run and found two problems: unchecked row coverage, and a target position measured from the wrong event. Both are fixed. Two further fresh Sonnet agents checked the numbers against the printed report and reviewed the prose.
  • Event counts. Labelled events per Primary at the signed-MW six: D5 33, D9 1, D10 12, D11 3, D14 13, D16 16. The cost intervals use only events with scored rows: D5 11, D10 7, D11 2, D14 9, D16 4.
  • Incomplete labels. The baseline rows can still hold unlabelled events, so the harm figures are lower bounds.
  • Median minus mean. We did not compute it, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Audit triggers. P1 and P3 contradicted the hypothesis and the prediction respectively.
  • Options for next steps. Rescore the cost with the widening matched across forecasts, and add events from Primaries with few labels.

docs.title: Unmetered solar capacity at each Primary, anomaly regression (NGED table)
docs.text:
Season-year July 2025 to June 2026, in megawatts. Estimator: anomaly regression with the two cloud terms. No row is validated, because the estimator recovers only 0.73 to 0.83 of an injected farm (see the experiment page). The intervals are the 10th to 90th percentile of a month-block bootstrap and do not include that bias, so the true capacity is likely higher.

docs.title: PV capacity: a new solar-capacity estimator compared with experiment 474's
docs.text:
Take-home message: an estimate of solar capacity built only from day-to-day weather within a month cannot be fooled by season, but it finds only 0.62 to 0.83 of a solar farm we added as a test, so it validates no Primary's capacity. The estimator (the anomaly regression) removes from the reading and from the physics solar shape the mean of the same calendar year-month, hour of day, and weekday class. A placebo is a deliberately wrong input that the estimate should not respond to, and this estimator passes the irradiance-shuffle placebo by construction. At the 6 Primaries whose reading is signed megawatts (signed-MW Primaries), it recovers 0.62 to 0.72 of the injected farm (0.73 to 0.83 with two cloud terms), against a gate of 0.85, and no Primary passes in any gated combination of world and estimator variant. Its capacities land within 5% of experiment 474's at 4 of the 6 signed-MW Primaries. The two methods use the same readings and the same physics solar shape, so this agreement is weak support. The estimator gives a negative capacity at D12 (reverse flow), and it differs from experiment 474 by 1.3 MW at D3 and 5.4 MW at D8.

The question was whether an estimate that the season and time of day cannot fake could validate the capacities that experiment 477's placebo gate rejected. The known-answer test shows that passing the placebo is not enough: the injected farm is recovered at about 0.67 without the cloud terms, so the mean removal erased about a third of the signal. One way to try next is a method that keeps more of the signal than a group-mean anomaly does, or that corrects for the recovery measured here.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. Recovery of an injected farm by Primary, world, and estimator variant.

Figure 2. The 95th percentile of both placebos by Primary.

Figure 3. Capacity found when only a cloud-following load is added.

Figure 4. Capacity at each Primary against experiment 474's.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. Two estimator variants: the anomaly regression without cloud terms and with the two cloud columns of experiment 474. Both fit temperature jointly (ERA5 temperature and its 24-hour mean, piecewise-linear at 5, 10, 15, and 20 degrees Celsius, three local-hour bands). Physics shape: tilt 35 degrees, DC to AC ratio 1.15, with the temperature derate. One capacity per season-year. 2,000-draw month-block bootstrap.
  • Row set. Experiment 474's: default rows with a finite reading and CAMS shape before 2026-07-01; D18 from 2025-03-01 only; D15 not run (generator case). The injection test used Solar A, B, C, D, and F at D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, with the rows each farm has.
  • Recovery (easy world: no load follows the clouds). The median over five farms is 0.62 to 0.72 per Primary without cloud terms (median 0.67) and 0.73 to 0.83 with them (median 0.77). The gate is 0.85, so no Primary passes. The 2 MW and 4 MW injections give identical recovery, because the fit is linear, so the 4 MW injection adds no information. Experiment 474's rungs recovered 0.75 to 0.94 without cloud terms. The cloud terms raise recovery in the easy world and lower it in both cloud-load worlds.
  • Cloud-following load, linear form. Without cloud terms recovery rises to 0.84 to 0.92, because the load adds about 0.2 of spurious capacity (figure 3) on top of the shortfall. With cloud terms 0.73 to 0.83. The widened 80% interval covers the injected capacity in 0% to 60% of the injections (one injection is one farm at one size at one Primary) without cloud terms, and 0% with them. No cell passes the 70% coverage gate.
  • Cloud-following load, squared form (report only). Without cloud terms recovery is 0.94 to 1.01 and the interval covers in 60% to 100% of injections. This coverage comes from the spurious load (0.29 to 0.31 of a 2 MW farm, figure 3) cancelling the shortfall, not from a sound estimate. With cloud terms recovery is 0.69 to 0.80 and coverage 0%.
  • Cloud load alone, no farm. Without cloud terms the linear load invents 0.20 to 0.21 of a 2 MW farm and the squared load 0.29 to 0.31. With cloud terms the linear load invents 0.000006 (the terms match its form exactly, so this figure is optimistic) and the squared load -0.03.
  • Profile-aware placebo (a), 95th percentile over 20 shuffles and 5 farms. 0.09 to 0.12 without cloud terms (passes at 6 of the 6 signed-MW Primaries). With cloud terms 0.187 to 0.206 (passes at 4 of the 6; D5 and D16 exceed 0.20). Experiment 474's rungs reached 0.25 to 0.51.
  • Irradiance-shuffle placebo (b), share of the real capacity. 95th percentile 0.06 to 0.10 without cloud terms and 0.08 to 0.12 with them. This placebo passes by construction.
  • Interval coverage. The bootstrap interval of an injected-minus-base increment is narrow because the reading's noise cancels between the two fits. A coverage failure therefore reflects bias (the recovery shortfall) and not an interval that is too narrow for the noise.
  • Capacity at the 6 signed-MW Primaries, July 2025 to June 2026, with cloud terms (AC, MW, median; experiment 474 in brackets): D5 3.2 (3.1), D9 2.2 (2.2), D10 2.5 (2.9), D11 3.2 (3.2), D14 3.7 (3.7), D16 3.6 (3.1). The recovery of 0.73 to 0.83 suggests the true capacity is higher. No bias correction is applied. The full table, with DC capacity at an assumed DC-to-AC ratio of 1.25 (the AC capacity times 1.25; other ratios rescale it the same way), is in nged_table.md.
  • 8 MVA-only Primaries. The estimates are fitted to apparent power with reactive power assumed zero, which experiment 366 found fails at a power factor of 0.97. D2 7.0 (6.9), D3 2.9 (4.2), D4 1.1 (0.8), D8 3.2 (8.6), D19 1.7 (1.8), D21 1.5 (2.0), D22 1.7 (1.5); D12 is -3.0 (reverse flow; the estimate is not a capacity). D18 (report-only, history from 2025-03-01) is 2.0 (1.8). None is validated.
  • Signal share and detectability (stage 0). About 0.24 of the shape's variance survives the mean removal (0.21 at D18). At the 6 signed-MW Primaries the indicative minimum detectable capacity from the ordinary-least-squares error is 0.08 to 0.19 MW (0.09 to 0.22 MW with cloud terms), and 0.05 to 0.35 MW across all 14 Primaries without them. The bootstrap standard deviation of the capacity at the 6 signed-MW Primaries is 0.05 to 0.10 MW without cloud terms, which is 2 to 5 times the ordinary-least-squares error, so the stage 0 figure understates the noise by that factor. The bias in recovery is larger than either.
  • Capacity-rises prior. Clipping at zero and taking the running maximum over season-years changes the latest season-year's median by at most 0.011 MW at the 6 signed-MW Primaries. At D3 and D4 it changes by 0.03 to 0.06 MW, and at D12 it replaces the negative capacity with zero. At D10 without cloud terms, season-year 2024 moves from 1.95 to 2.01 MW. Both versions are in work/real_<site>.parquet.
  • Not applicable. No forecast is scored, so tail calibration, the avoidable-curtailment cost, the equal-rows check, and the forecast-use step do not apply. The 5th and 95th percentiles of the bootstrap capacity are in work/capacity_table.parquet. The weather inputs are CAMS irradiance and ERA5 temperature, both estimates of past weather. Solar A to F are named by letter only, and no farm is paired with a Primary.

docs.title: Deviations and caveats
docs.text:
• Failed predictions. Prediction 3 failed with cloud terms at D5 and D16 (placebo 0.205 and 0.206). Prediction 4 failed: easy-world recovery was 0.62 to 0.72. Prediction 5 failed: coverage with cloud terms was 0%.
  • Optimistic cloud-load result. The cloud terms match experiment 129's linear load exactly, so the linear cloud-load result with cloud terms is optimistic.
  • Unresolved MVA-only Primaries. D3 and D8 show the largest gaps from experiment 474 (1.3 MW and 5.4 MW). D4, D21, and D22 differ by 15% to 45%, and the two methods leave all five unresolved.
  • Definitions. The group mean is the mean of the same calendar year-month in local time, the same local hour of day, and the same weekday class. A season-year gets its own capacity column with 4,000 half-hours in at least 3 months.
  • Labels. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the readings may hold unlabelled events.
  • Compute. CPU only, 4 processes, about 3 minutes. Running the scripts needs uv sync --all-packages --group gpu, because experiment 474's modules import torch.

docs.title: Pre-registered plan
docs.text:
• Estimator. For each Primary, remove from the reading (megawatts) and from every regressor the mean of the same calendar year-month, local hour of day, and weekday class (Monday to Friday, Saturday, Sunday). Regress the reading's anomaly on the physics PV shape's anomaly: tilt 35 degrees, DC to AC ratio 1.15 as in experiment 405, with the temperature derate, one capacity coefficient per season-year (July to June). The coefficient is the negative of the capacity in MW AC. Temperature enters the same regression, so heating and cooling load is fitted jointly with the PV capacity: ERA5 temperature and its 24-hour trailing mean, each with piecewise-linear hinges at 5, 10, 15, and 20 degrees Celsius, in three local-hour bands (0 to 8, 8 to 16, 16 to 24), all as anomalies. The comparison arm adds the two cloud columns of experiment 474 (the day-mean and half-hour cloud response).
  • Capacity-rises prior. A post-hoc step after each fit: clip each draw's capacity path at zero and take its running maximum over the season-years, so a fall is resisted. Both versions are reported.
  • Uncertainty. A month-block bootstrap of 2,000 draws, resampling months within each season-year and calendar quarter (experiment 269's stratification). The 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles of AC capacity. DC capacity is AC capacity times 1.25, with 1.1 and 1.5 as a post-hoc rescaling (experiment 73 found the ratio not identified, and the AC capacity does not change).
  • Known-answer worlds (experiment 474's harness, same farms and injection sizes). The injected series is subtracted from the reading (so the reading's anomaly falls by the series' anomaly) before the group means are removed. The easy world, with no load that follows the clouds, injects 2 MW and 4 MW of Solar A to F's output (five farms, E left out for its short history). The cloud-load world adds experiment 129's cloud-following load (a load whose mean equals 2 MW of capacity, linear in the day's mean cloud response). A third world adds a load that follows the squared day-mean cloud response, scaled to the same mean, to test a load the cloud terms do not match exactly. Each world runs with and without the cloud terms.
  • Placebos. (a) The profile-aware placebo of experiment 474: the farm's day-of-year profile plus the anomaly of another day of the same month, injected at 2 MW. The group-mean removal deletes the profile, so this placebo can pass trivially. (b) The irradiance-shuffle placebo: the PV shape's days and the two cloud columns' days are permuted together, by one permutation within each calendar year-month, and the real reading is refitted, and the placebo capacity is reported as a share of the real capacity. This placebo is true by construction. Both use 20 shuffles. The page states plainly that a placebo that passes by construction can hide a real signal that was removed together with the means, so the known answer (recovery of the 2 MW and 4 MW injections) is the check that the means did not erase the signal.
  • Coverage. The nominal 80% interval is the 10th to 90th percentile of the bootstrap's increment (injected-world capacity minus base capacity, same draw), reported alone and widened by 1.28 times the standard deviation of the point recoveries over the five farms (experiment 474's definition).
  • Scope. Six signed-MW Primaries run the known answer. The eight MVA-only Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22) are fitted to the apparent-power reading with reactive power assumed zero, by experiment 366's rule and experiment 420's export gate: the rule fails at a power factor of 0.97, so these capacities carry that caveat. D5 (export limit; the clip-free solar term does not represent it), D12 (reverse flow), D15 (generator case, not run), and D18 (history only from 2025-03-01, report-only) are marked. The 6 signed-MW Primaries and the 8 MVA-only Primaries are reported separately, never pooled.
  • Not applicable. No forecast is scored, so the avoidable-curtailment cost, tail calibration (including the rule that q99 coverage must stay within 5%), and the forecast-use step do not apply. The tails reported are the 5th and 95th percentiles of the bootstrap capacity. Experiment 474's forecast-use step repeats experiments 405, 409, 416, and 477 and is dropped.
  • Anonymisation. Solar A to F by letter; no nearest-farm names; distance bands only ("under 15 km", "15 to 30 km", "30 km or more"). Rows with no labelled event: NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the readings may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: Stage 0: numbers fixed before any recovery or placebo is read
docs.text:
Ordinary-least-squares standard errors on the real reading (no injection, no placebo), at the latest season-year (July 2025 to June 2026). The standard error assumes independent rows, so it is a lower bound (rows within a day are strongly correlated); the bootstrap interval will be wider.

  • Post-removal signal share: 0.23 to 0.25 of the PV shape's variance at each of the 14 Primaries, and 0.21 at D18. Experiment 405 found 0.21 on its farm. About one quarter of the shape's variance survives the group-mean removal.
  • Variance inflation factor of the latest season-year's capacity column against all other columns: 1.02 to 1.05 without the cloud terms, 1.35 to 1.65 with them, 2.4 for D18.
  • Minimum detectable capacity (80% power, two-sided level 0.05 divided by the Bonferroni count of 36 tests: 6 signed-MW Primaries, 2 estimators, 3 gates): 0.05 to 0.35 MW AC without the cloud terms and 0.06 to 0.40 MW with them (D8 is widest, D21 narrowest). The count suits the 6 signed-MW Primaries only, and the figure tests a capacity against zero, which none of the gates does, so it is indicative. A capacity under those figures cannot be told from zero by this estimator.
  • Bonferroni count: 36.

The full table is in the private file work/stage0_signal.json.

docs.title: Checks and reviews
docs.text: Plan review, code review before the first fit, results review, and write-up review: Sonnet reviewers, as the ml-experiment skill requires. Their findings and triage are in the PR body.

docs.title: Do two columns from realised satellite irradiance lower the XGBoost demand forecast's error at the eight Primaries whose meters report apparent power only?
docs.text: Take-home. Giving the monthly XGBoost demand model the satellite-measured sunshine of each half-hour lowered its error at all 16 primary substations in the point estimates (the sites that step 33 kV down to 11 kV, called Primaries below). Over the eight Primaries that report apparent power only (MVA), the error fell by 0.36 points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a substation's effective capacity). Over the six that report signed real power (MW), it fell by 0.48 points. The gain is an upper bound on what a live service can have: these are lab conditions, in which the model sees the realised sunshine at every lead, and the satellite data arrives about a day late. The next experiment should build the same two columns from the ECMWF ensemble weather forecast and measure how much of the gain remains.

docs.title: The columns lowered the error at every Primary
docs.text:
We asked whether two extra input columns, computed from the sunshine (irradiance, in watts per square metre) that a satellite measured in each half-hour, lower the error of the monthly XGBoost demand forecast. The two columns are the output of a generic south-facing solar fleet under that irradiance, and the ratio of the measured irradiance to the irradiance under a cloudless sky. We refitted the model monthly for 12 months with the columns (arm A1) and without them (arm A0), on the same rows. We compared the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) of forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead, in points of capacity. A negative difference favours A1.

A1 was better in the point estimates at all 16 Primaries, and the gain was far larger than the 0.03 to 0.10 points predicted. The gain is largest on sunny half-hours and grows with lead time, which is what realised weather in place of a forecast would give. The planned tests of a signed-power label (the known-answer test and arms A2) were not started: A1 shows that the columns lower the error without a sign label, and the brief runs them only if the maintainer asks.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. A0 is experiment 381's monthly control refitted on CPU. Its recipe is experiment 87's n1h configuration (500 rounds, learning rate 0.05, depth 6, training rows weighted with a half-life of 0.5 years, the 51 ensemble members' quantiles mixed at prediction time). A1 is A0 plus cams_unit_pv_shape and cams_clear_sky_index. Cadence: monthly refits, 12 refits from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-01, 384 fits in 8.6 hours wall time. Code: ml-experiments/00480-xgboost-cams-columns-at-mva-only-primaries-lab-conditions/, which imports the folders of experiments 87, 377, and 381.
  • Weather source at lag times. The CAMS radiation service's satellite retrieval at each Primary's coordinates, hourly. CAMS publishes about a day late, so the columns would be unavailable at forecast time for the first day of lead. Here the columns hold the half-hour's own realised value at every lead, so every figure is a lab-condition upper bound, and use at lag times older than a day was not tested.
  • Row sets. The contrasts use the half-hours shared by A0, A1, and experiment 381's stored control: 4,012,330 half-hours at the 16 Primaries under fold_a_daily_gap_v1. The absolute tables use the half-hours shared by all seven arms, 2,824,844, which leaves out part of D15 and D18. No scored half-hour has a missing actual. The noisy start of D15 and D18 (before 2025-03-01) is cut from training rows and lags. D5, D12, D15, and D18 are the marked Primaries.
  • Minimum detectable effect, computed before any score. 0.032 points at the eight and 0.105 points at D12, the half-widths of experiment 381's solar arm minus its control arm. The pooled contrast at the eight (C1) is about 11 times 0.032.
  • Code check. A0 minus experiment 381's stored control, which was fitted on the GPU: +0.001 (-0.003 to +0.005) at D5 and +0.006 (-0.010 to +0.036) at D12, inside the 0.05 limit.
Contrast (A1 minus A0), CRPS days 1 to 10 Estimate Interval C1, the eight MVA-only Primaries -0.355 99.67%: -0.497 to -0.228 MVA-only seven (without D8) -0.386 99.67%: -0.543 to -0.241 Signed-MW six -0.476 99.67%: -0.627 to -0.316 D15 and D18 -0.313 99.67%: -0.429 to -0.201 D12 -0.769 99.67%: -1.180 to -0.406 D8 -0.138 99.67%: -0.220 to -0.058
  • Per Primary (95%). All 16 point estimates are negative, from -0.053 at D4 to -0.843 at D5. Of the 16 intervals, 15 lie wholly below zero. D15 is the exception, -0.149 (-0.305 to +0.018). No Primary is worse than +0.05.
  • Absolute CRPS (days 1 to 10, all-arm row set). Per-Primary values for every arm are in scores/scores.parquet in the data folder. At D12: A0 6.82, A1 6.05, stack 7.52, BG2 6.75, manual_heuristic 7.92, climatology 8.83. At D5: A0 3.89, A1 3.05, stack 4.08, BG2 3.94. A1 is below manual_heuristic and climatology at all 16 Primaries, and below BG2 at D12 and D5. At D15 the all-arm table shows A1 (15.53) above A0 (15.51), because that row set leaves out part of D15; on the 4,012,330 shared half-hours A1 is 0.149 lower.
  • Lead bands. At the eight, the gain grows from -0.24 at day 1 to -0.42 at days 8 to 10 and is level at -0.41 for days 11 to 14. At the signed-MW six it grows from -0.32 to -0.57.
  • Slices. On sunny half-hours (unit PV shape high) the gain is -0.97 (-1.41 to -0.61) at the eight and -1.33 (-1.77 to -0.96) at the six.
