With the CAMS index at least 0.7 it is -0.63 at the eight and -0.88 at the six. Winter nights, cold nights, and Economy 7 step hours move by under 0.02 points. In the 7 days after a labelled event the gain is -0.37 (-0.73 to -0.17) at the eight, and during a labelled event it is -0.28 (-0.65 to +0.05). NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events, and these event counts are lower bounds.
  • D12 bias on sunny half-hours (median forecast minus actual, in points of capacity, over days 1 to 10). A0 -4.89, A1 +2.09. A0 runs from -2.10 at day 1 to -6.34 at days 8 to 10. A1 runs from +1.87 at day 2 to +2.37 at days 8 to 10 and +2.87 at days 11 to 14. The columns remove the under-forecast and overshoot it. At D8 the bias falls from +9.97 to +7.90.
Tails, mean over each group (days 1 to 10) A0 MVA-only A1 MVA-only A0 signed-MW A1 signed-MW Coverage q01 (nominal 0.01) 0.0126 0.0124 0.0074 0.0070 Coverage q05 (0.05) 0.069 0.072 0.052 0.055 Coverage q95 (0.95) 0.933 0.936 0.909 0.913 Coverage q99 (0.99) 0.991 0.991 0.980 0.981 Pinball q01 0.248 0.242 0.249 0.240 Pinball q05 0.883 0.829 0.674 0.600 Pinball q95 0.975 0.903 0.947 0.844 Pinball q99 0.332 0.326 0.385 0.378 twCRPS 0.201 0.191 0.386 0.380
  • Tails. The upper tail improves most: pinball q95 falls by 0.07 at the eight and 0.10 at the six. Coverage moves by under 0.005 and stays on the same side of nominal as A0.
  • Avoidable curtailment cost, signed-MW six, scored year, in pounds (as metrics.avoidable_curtailment_cost defines it). At the 0.9 limit (the headline limit of the curtailment rule), A1 is lower than A0 at D10 (28,733 against 29,036), D11 (201,909 against 213,752), and D5 (426,074 against 427,491). A1 is higher at D14 (2.217 million against 2.177 million), D16 (7.465 million against 7.446 million), and D9 (169,524 against 166,786). The total over the six is slightly higher for A1, about 10.51 million against 10.46 million. The stack is lower than A1 at all six Primaries at both limits, and manual_heuristic is below A1 at D5 (232,138). At the 0.5 limit A1 is lower than A0 at all six (for example D16, 24.3 million against 25.2 million). The costs during a labelled event and in the 7 days after one could not be scored: the function needs a perfect-forecast arm that is empty on those rows. The better CRPS did not give a consistent saving at the 0.9 limit.
  • Pre-registered rules. C1's interval lies wholly below zero and no Primary is worse than +0.05, so the rule for porting the two columns is met on lab-condition numbers. The no-harm contrasts at the signed-MW six and at D15 and D18 have upper bounds of -0.316 and -0.201, below +0.05. The stop rules for the A2 arms were not tested.
  • Predictions. P1 (0.03 to 0.10 points at the eight) failed on size: -0.355. P2 (largest at D12 and D8, and 0.10 to 0.40 points on sunny half-hours) failed on size: -0.97 at the eight and -2.36 at D12 on sunny half-hours, and D8 is among the smaller gains. P3 (gain concentrated in days 1 to 3) failed: the gain grows with lead. P4 (under 0.03 at the other eight) failed: the signed-MW six gain 0.476.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary. The mean of each forecast distribution is estimated from the 11 stored quantiles by the trapezoid rule, with the lowest and highest quantile held flat to levels 0 and 1. In A0 the gap runs from -0.093 MW to +0.0005 MW, and in A1 from -0.089 MW to +0.004 MW, so the spread does not shift the forecast. The gap is closer to zero in A1 at 14 of 16 Primaries.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrasts. The median's mean absolute error is lower in A1 at all 16 Primaries (for example D5 6.76 to 5.11 MW, D12 12.27 to 10.67 MW), so the CRPS and the error of the median point the same way.
  • Result against prediction. The size contradicts the prediction. The tested explanation is that the columns hold realised irradiance in place of a forecast: the gain is 96% within 08:00 to 16:00 UTC (peak -1.43 points at 12:00), under 0.015 points between 19:00 and 05:00, negative in all 12 scored months, and largest in March to May. A fresh Sonnet audit (private briefs/e480_audit_report.md) rebuilt the CRPS from the stored quantiles with its own code, matched all 16 per-Primary contrasts to within 0.0005, and found no leakage in the CAMS join. The audit did not retrain, so a refit with the CAMS columns shuffled across days at one Primary remains the stronger test.
  • Leaving one Primary out. Dropping any one Primary leaves the pooled eight between -0.295 (without D12) and -0.398 (without D4), and the pooled six between -0.404 (without D5) and -0.503 (without D11). Every interval is wholly below zero, so no single Primary carries the result.
  • Control against the stored control. At D5 and D12, A0 moved by under 0.01 against experiment 381's stored control. On the all-arm row set A0 differs from the stored control by 0.089 at D15, which has the 2025-03-01 cut that the stored control lacks, and by 0.037 at D16, which is unexplained and below the 0.05 limit.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Lab conditions. The gain is an upper bound. A live service has the realised satellite value only for data at least a day old, and that use was not tested.
  • Mixed result at the tail cost. The better CRPS at the signed-MW six did not lower the avoidable curtailment cost consistently at the 0.9 limit.
  • D12 overshoot. A1 over-forecasts sunny D12 half-hours by 1.9 to 2.9 points, from day 2 to days 11 to 14, so the correction overshoots.
  • Not tested here. The reverse-flow rule of experiment 366 holds only for reactive power zero and fails at a power factor of 0.97. The known-answer test and the A2 arms repeat work in experiments 366, 372, 374, 387, 393, 420, and 424, so they were not started.
  • Next. Build the same two columns from the ensemble's forecast irradiance and from CAMS only for lag times older than a day, and measure how much of the 0.355-point gain remains. A refit with the CAMS columns shuffled across days at one Primary would test the mechanism directly.

docs.title: How many fit seeds does the first-release neural forecaster need before averaging more seeds stops helping, for Primary demand and for wind farms?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead the value of the lagless head over averaged S1 seeds (3.441 against 3.628) is overstated. The seed-averaging results for the lag-free networks built on experiment 425A are unaffected, because experiment 532 found 425A's weather taken from the run published at the forecast origin. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

The solar half of the original brief is dropped because experiment 430 already stores six seeds for a2_member and g0_onepass.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
• Reuse. Arm A seeds 0 to 4 for the five months (experiment 425 work/seed_preds/A); wind member_plain seeds 0 to 4 (experiment 429 parts/); S1 seeds 0 to 4 (experiment 454).
  • New fits (60). Arm A seeds 5 to 9 on five months: 25 pretrains and 25 fine-tunes (pretraining is per seed and month). Wind member_plain seeds 5 to 9: 5 fits. S1 seed 5 on five months: 5 fits, so the S1 pool reaches K = 6 (experiment 404 stores the lagless tables for seeds 0 to 5 only). Seeds 3 to 5 of S1 share training worlds with seed seed % 3 (experiment 454's caveat), so S1 curves past K = 3 are lower-bound on diversity and the page says so.
  • Cadence. Monthly refits; five of the twelve months. No weekly refits.
  • Standing practices followed. Cleaned data (flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped, counts reported per fold), the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, saved networks in the experiment's data folder, stored predictions reused, tails and curtailment cost reported, example forecasts plotted, draft pull request. Load-shift event plots are not needed because the experiment does not score events. Nearest-farm pairings are named by letter only.
  • Compute. One timed arm A fit (month 2025-10, seed 5): 43 s pretrain plus 61 s fine-tune and forecast. Estimated total about 1.2 GPU-hours, one process under 8 GB, one feeder core.
  • Where new seeds are written. This experiment's own data folder. The timing fit above wrote pretrained/A/2025-10_s5.pt, seed_preds/A/2025-10_s5.parquet and the matching models/A/ files into experiment 425's folder. They were moved here afterwards, and the wrapper refuses to overwrite any existing file.

docs.title: Take-home
docs.text: A second seed gives the largest gain, and later seeds add little. For Primary demand, two seeds score 0.035 points better than one (99.55% interval +0.025 to +0.053, better in 5 of 5 months). The point estimate is above the 0.03 bar for porting, and the interval spans it. Each later step gains at most 0.011 points. Wind follows the same curve with more noise. Averaging seeds of the lagged neural network S1 does not replace the lagless head. Five demand months make these results interim, so they support a choice for the first release and no more.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are points of effective capacity (demand) or capacity (wind). Before any contrast the scorer prints the Bonferroni count, 11 (experiment 425's arm A 4, S1 3, wind 4; interval level 99.55%), and the minimum detectable effect: 0.0427 for arm A at the signed-MW six, 0.0864 for wind (12 monthly blocks), and 0.0612 for S1.

  • A second demand seed gains 0.035 points; later seeds gain at most 0.011. Arm A, signed-MW six, days 1 to 10, widened 1.15, 100 random draws of K seeds from 10: K = 1 scores 3.2572, K = 2 3.2218, K = 3 3.2104, K = 5 3.1998, and K = 10 3.1931. The gains per step are +0.0354 (+0.0252 to +0.0526), +0.0113, +0.0106, and +0.0067. Every interval excludes zero, and every gain is below the minimum detectable effect by point estimate.
  • Other demand slices fall the same way. MVA-only eight: 3.760 (K = 1) to 3.680 (K = 10). Rows with no labelled event, six: 2.772 to 2.710. Cold nights, six: 4.212 to 4.132. 12 to 36 hours, six: 2.932 to 2.866.
  • Demand tails stay under-covered at every K. With the widening at 1.15, q99 coverage runs 0.960 to 0.964, q95 coverage 0.889 to 0.896, and q99 pinball loss 0.344 to 0.325. The best widening is 1.15 at every K, the top of the grid, so the optimum is censored.
  • The pre-registered rule recommends K = 2 for demand. K = 2 is the smallest K within 0.0427 of K = 10 with a q99 pinball loss within 5% of K = 10's (K = 1 fails at a ratio of 1.059). The scorer's "marked K" (the K beyond which every gain is inside the minimum detectable effect) is 1, because all four gains are below 0.0427. The 0.03 porting bar also gives K = 2.
  • For wind, one seed meets the pre-registered rule, and a second seed gains 0.041 points. member_plain, kept rows, true days 1 to 10, equal-weight months: K = 1 scores 10.414, K = 2 10.373, K = 3 10.359, K = 5 10.349, and K = 10 10.340. The gains per step are +0.041, +0.014, +0.010, and +0.009. K = 1 is within the minimum detectable effect of K = 10 (0.0735 against 0.0864), so the rule recommends K = 1. Reading K = 2 as the better choice is post hoc: it rests on the 0.03 porting bar, and the lower bound of the K = 2 gain (+0.030) sits exactly on it. The best widening is 1.10, and q99 coverage at 1.0 is 0.976. Farms are named A, B, and C.
  • For S1, three averaged seeds meet the rules under quantile averaging, and six under the density mixture. The quantile average of seeds 0 to 5 scores 3.737 (K = 1), 3.640 (K = 2), 3.607 (K = 3), and 3.573 (K = 6), raw. The gains per step are +0.097, +0.033, and +0.034, against a minimum detectable effect of 0.0612. The density mixture (experiment 454's construction) fails the 5% q99 rule at K = 3, so its recommended K is 6. Seeds 3 to 5 share training worlds with seeds 0 to 2, so a random pair of seeds can share a world, and the S1 curves understate the diversity that independent worlds would give.
  • Averaging S1 seeds does not match a mixture with the lagless head at the same number of networks. All values are raw scores. At 2 networks, S1-mix scores 3.441 and B-mix 3.508, against 3.640 for two averaged S1 seeds (3.628 as a density mixture). At 4 networks, K2-S1 scores 3.387, against 3.607 for three seeds and 3.573 for six (neither count is four; the S1 pool has no four-seed entry). At 6 networks, K3-S1 scores 3.369, against 3.573 for six averaged seeds. The lagless table counts as a network in these counts. Prediction P4 fails.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost shows no monotone trend in K. Signed-MW six, 12 to 36 hours, f = 0.9, five months, 10 random subsets per K: K = 1 costs 7.19M pounds, K = 2 6.98M, K = 3 7.43M, K = 5 7.02M, and K = 10 7.28M, against 9.31M for the manual heuristic. K = 1 is the highest cost at all three limit fractions, but the differences are smaller than the 5th-to-95th-percentile range across subsets (0.9M to 2.4M). A second seed therefore does not improve the metric NGED cares about by a measurable amount.
  • A second demand seed doubles the refit cost. Arm A takes about 80 GPU seconds per seed per monthly refit (46 s pretrain plus 34 s fine-tune), so K = 2 takes 158 s. Wind takes 56 s per seed, and S1 29 s per seed plus cross-fitted lagless tables (not timed). The timings are medians from a loaded workstation. Serving latency was not measured.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (arm A): partly supported. The K = 1 to K = 2 gain is 0.035, below the predicted 0.05 to 0.12. The K = 3 to K = 5 gain (0.011) and the K = 5 to K = 10 gain (0.007) are inside the predicted bounds.
  • P2 (best widening falls with K): not testable. The best widening is 1.15, the top of the grid, at every K.
  • P3 (wind): supported. The K = 5 to K = 10 gain is 0.009, inside the predicted bound.
  • P4 (averaging S1 seeds beats B-mix at equal networks): not supported.
  • The verdict "partly supported" refers to the predictions. The hypothesis itself holds for arm A (K = 5 to K = 10 gains 0.0067), wind (0.0086), and S1 (K = 3 to K = 6 gains 0.0337, below the minimum detectable effect of 0.0612).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Equal rows. One row set serves every K and seed (1,273,228 scored demand rows). The scorer asserts identical keys for all 10 seeds in every month.
  • Gates. Demand scoring agrees with metrics.scored_rows to 4e-6 points. Wind seeds 0 to 4 pooled over rows give 10.533, the value experiment 429 stored. S1 seed 0 gives 3.7518 and the seed 0 to 2 mixture 3.5604, both equal to experiment 454's stored values.
  • Median against mean. A reviewer's re-derivation (not in the score report) found the median-forecast absolute error falls with K in the same direction as CRPS (5.614 at K = 1 to 5.575 at K = 10), and the K = 1 to K = 10 gain is positive at all six signed-MW sites (+0.044 to +0.082).
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 fires: P1 and P4 are contradicted, and the grid censors P2. Trigger 7 fires if the first release sets its seed count from this result before another replication. A results review found one bug, now fixed: the curtailment subsets were the first 10 in sorted order, so seed 0 sat in every K = 2 subset.
  • The minimum detectable effect is a weak bar. The demand value rests on 5 monthly differences, and 2026-01 (a difference of 0.143) sets it. On the other four months it is 0.0077, and against that value the gains from K = 1 to K = 2 and from K = 2 to K = 3 would lie outside it. Read the bootstrap intervals beside it.

docs.title: Caveats and files
docs.text:
• Interim. Five of the twelve demand months and one wind year are scored, so the choice needs a repeat on the other seven months before the first release fixes it.
  • Loop and files. Arm A uses experiment 425's 12-fold loop, read at 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. Demand seeds 5 to 9 are in this experiment's data folder (work/seed_preds/A, work/models/A, work/pretrained/A) and wind seeds 5 to 9 in wind/parts. The five S1 seed 5 networks are experiment 404's work/models/S1/<month>_s5.pt. Nothing is left in experiment 425's or 429's folders.
  • Equal-weight months. The scores differ slightly from the row-pooled values of experiments 425 and 429.
  • Solar. Dropped, because experiment 430 stores six seeds.
  • Data rules. The D15 and D18 cut and the flagged exact-zero drop follow experiment 425; its fit logs hold the counts per fold. Load-shift event plots are not needed, because this experiment does not score events.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Repeat the K = 2 choice on the other seven demand months.
  • Test a widening grid above 1.15 for demand.

docs.title: How do the lagged and lagless demand forecasts respond to injected load shifts and level changes, and how does the wind forecast compare with its references?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead the comparison of K2-S1 with A-pool is not a valid forecast comparison. The change in one forecast when shifts are injected into its lags, and A-pool's own change, are unaffected. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

A forecast that mixes lagged and lagless heads (K2-S1) was in none of the eight scenarios meaningfully worse than the lagless forecast when we injected load shifts into its lags. The pooled neural network that was never trained on shifted lags (A-pool) is the one that suffers. At the wind farms, member_plain is level with research default 2 (the interval includes zero).

The page shows wind reference contrasts, a 14-day wind chart, real-event charts, and eight injected scenarios on stored demand neural networks. The real-event charts add the actual with the normal running arrangement (NRA) restored, and the surprise inputs. Experiment 468 holds the earlier charts. Nothing was fitted: every neural network forecasts from stored weights.

A scenario shifts one donor Primary's lags by 1, 2, or 3 times its lag spread. The lag spread is the standard deviation of the Primary's 24-hour change in power before 2025-10-01. The shift lasts 1, 3, or 14 days. A load shift leaves the target alone, and a genuine level change moves the target too. Mirrored scenarios subtract the same energy from up to two neighbours. Each scenario runs on 16 donors and 5 test months (80 clusters). The scored rows are the donor's rows whose lags fall inside the event. The clean actual is the actual without the injected shift.

The page compares five forecasts. They are the lagless neural network (LL, which reads no lag), S1 (a lagged neural network trained on injected shifts), B-mix (a 50/50 mixture of a lagged and a lagless head), K2-S1 (a mixture of two S1 and two lagless heads), and A-pool (experiment 425's arm A, a pooled plain neural network trained on real lags only). Experiment 470's assembly winner is not shown. The scenarios are numbered 1 to 8, and "S1" always means the S1 neural network. The signed-MW six are the six Primaries whose power is signed in MW, and the MVA-only eight are the eight Primaries recorded only in MVA. D15 and D18 are two Primaries that are reported separately.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
• Scenario 1 to 8 are defined by shift size, duration, and mirror. Scenario 1: +1x, 1 day, no mirror. Scenario 2: -3x, 1 day, no mirror. Scenario 3: +1x, 14 days, mirror. Scenario 4: -3x, 14 days, no mirror. Scenario 5: +3x, 14 days, mirror. Scenario 6: -1x, 14 days, no mirror. Scenario 7: +3x, 1 day, mirror. Scenario 8: +2x, 3 days, genuine level change.
  • The neural networks barely followed the shift. On rows whose newest lag is inside the event, the median moved by 1% to 6% of the shift for K2-S1, 1% to 4% for B-mix, 3% to 12% for S1, and 8% to 25% for A-pool. The lagless neural network moved by 0.
  • A-pool is harmed by a large negative unmirrored shift. In scenario 4 its CRPS is 8.08 points of capacity against 5.62 for the lagless neural network and 5.67 for K2-S1. Its q95 covers 72% of actuals (nominal 95%), and its q05 covers 1.0% (nominal 5%). K2-S1 minus A-pool is -2.41 points (interval -3.10 to -1.73 at the Bonferroni level for 40 contrasts, 99.875%).
  • In scenario 5 (+3x, mirror), the mirror left A-pool over-confident on the lower side. Its q05 covers 16.6% of actuals and its q95 covers 97%.
  • S1 is worse than the lagless neural network in scenarios 2 and 4. The contrast is +0.58 points in scenario 2 and +0.71 in scenario 4. K2-S1 minus lagless is -0.20 in scenario 1, -0.32 in scenario 3, and -0.28 in scenario 8, and each excludes zero at the Bonferroni level. K2-S1 cannot be told apart from lagless in the other five scenarios.
  • Absolute scores are close for the lagless network and K2-S1. In rows with a lag inside the event, CRPS in points of capacity is 5.4 (1-day scenarios) to 6.2 (scenario 8) for lagless, and 5.2 to 5.9 for K2-S1. The row counts are 146,975 (1-day), 994,340 (14-day), and 332,691 (scenario 8).
  • The ranking differs between the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight. In scenario 4, K2-S1 and the lagless neural network score 3.92 and 3.99 at the signed-MW six and 4.95 and 4.96 at the MVA-only eight. A-pool scores 6.46 and 6.95. B-mix is lowest at the MVA-only eight (4.94 against 4.95 for K2-S1). The lagless neural network leads at D15 and D18 (13.31 against 13.90 for K2-S1).
  • K2-S1's band widens by under 2% inside unmirrored shifts. Its 90% band is 27.9 points wide inside scenario 4 and 27.6 before the event. The widths are 28.1, 28.1, 27.9, and 27.7 points in scenarios 1, 2, 4, and 6. The band covers 85% of actuals inside scenario 4 rows (nominal 90%). The lagless neural network's q95 covers 87% to 88% of actuals in scenarios 1 to 7 and 84% in scenario 8.
  • Widening by 1.15 does not change the ranking, except in scenario 2. Experiment 454's widening is stored beside every raw score (crps_by_scenario_widened.csv). In scenario 2, the lagless neural network and B-mix swap places.

docs.title: Example forecasts
docs.text:
• D5 is one of the signed-MW six and D12 is one of the MVA-only eight. All six charts show day-ahead forecasts (12 to 36 hours ahead).
  • A-pool follows the shift. In scenario 4 its median sits below the others throughout the event, while the other four medians stay near the clean actual.

docs.title: Real events with NRA, lags, and surprise
docs.text:
• Each chart adds the NRA actual, the lags, and the surprise. The NRA actual is drawn for labelled events only. The chart shows the three lags each neural network reads, and each lag minus the lagless median at its own half-hour (the surprise that S1 reads).
  • Surprise is large during real events. The largest absolute surprise on a lag inside an event is 22, 35, 31, 36, 11, and 21 points of capacity at the six labelled events and 88 at the scan-found D12 step.
  • Caveat. NGED's labels are incomplete, so the scan-found D12 step may be a load shift, a level change, or neither. Rows with no labelled event may hold events no label covers, so the injected scenarios sit on a series that is not event-free.

docs.title: Wind reference contrasts
docs.text:
• member_plain beats research default 1 and is level with research default 2. Each contrast is experiment 461's member_plain (p99.9 capacity, after table P, the correction fitted to 24 to 240 hours) minus a reference, in points of the p99.9 capacity, over 54,899 half-hours and 11 months, month-block bootstrap at 98.75% (Bonferroni count 4), minimum detectable effect in brackets. Research default 1: -0.41 (-0.79 to -0.04; 0.52). Research default 2: -0.05 (-0.18 to +0.09; 0.18). Climatology: -4.72 (-6.25 to -3.24; 2.04). Manual heuristic: -5.35 (-7.06 to -3.71; 2.23). In the 24 to 36 hour band (3,270 half-hours) the contrasts are -0.24, -0.05, -12.71, and -12.80.
  • Absolute errors are 14.3 to 19.7 points. The mean absolute error of the median, in points of capacity, is member_plain 14.33, research default 1 14.74, research default 2 14.38, climatology 19.06, manual heuristic 19.68. The gain over research default 1 is smaller than the contrast's minimum detectable effect.
  • Research default 2 has the lowest error at two of three farms. It has the lowest error among the references at Farm A (14.31 against 14.78 for default 1) and Farm B (15.31 against 16.03), and not at Farm C (13.50 against 13.37).
  • The 14-day chart uses member_plain before table P. Table P is fitted to 24 to 240 hours. The 90% band covers 92% (calm fortnight) and 83% (stormy fortnight) of Farm A's half-hours.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 did not hold. The first-day cut was not made, so rows pool the whole event. A-pool moved by 8% to 25% of the shift, not at least 50%. The predictions for K2-S1 (under 50%) and the lagless neural network (under 5%) held.
  • P2 did not hold. On the genuine level change (S8) the medians of K2-S1, S1, and A-pool moved by 3%, 6%, and 14% of the shift, so none followed the new level.
  • P3 held in part. The K2-S1 band was wider inside unmirrored shifts by under 2%, and its coverage stayed above 80% (83% to 87%).
  • P4 held at two of three farms. The figures are in the wind bullet above.

docs.title: Not done, and caveats
docs.text:
• Curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5 is not computed, because the node-plus-generators machinery takes a whole month of computing per series and the injected worlds replace one Primary's forecast only.
  • The 12 to 36 hour band, a minimum detectable effect for the demand scenarios, and a run with and without the largest scenario are not computed. Demand intervals are cluster bootstraps over 80 (month, donor) clusters.
  • Recipients of mirrors are forecast but not scored here. Row classes by newest lag are in crps_by_scenario_and_class.csv; in scenario 8 the rows classed before and after mix shifted and unshifted targets, because the class follows the lags only.
  • A shift on an MVA-only Primary is clipped at zero, so its recorded size can overstate a negative shift.
  • The 14-day chart is wind only, because demand and solar forecasts end at 240 hours.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Self-test passed. The no-shift forecasts match experiment 454's stored cells to 7.6e-05 and experiment 425's stored arm A to 6e-06 (capacity fraction), in every month.
  • The stored neural networks were refitted monthly. Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 split come with the stored forecasts.
  • Median minus mean forecast: not computed, because no mean forecast is scored.
  • Triggers fired: none.
  • Production training load. K2-S1 needs three S1 networks and three lagless tables per refit, A-pool five pooled networks.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first scored run; three findings were fixed (non-finite actuals in the 14-day pick, row-alignment asserts, an origin check). The reference heuristic keeps experiment 303's definition.

docs.title: Does a widening or table P make the tails of the first-release demand candidates honest?
docs.text:
The candidates' bands are too narrow on the upper tail, and widening only that tail fixes the eight. The bands of A-pool and A-gam-in (the first-release demand candidates of experiment 470) are too wide on the lower tail and too narrow on the upper tail. A widening of both tails by 1.15 (every tail quantile's distance from the median times 1.15) therefore repairs the upper tail while it damages the lower one. Widening only the upper tail brings the eight into range as well. Table P, which multiplies each tail quantile's distance from the median by its own factor, brings all four tails into range at the eight MVA-only Primaries, for both candidates. It does not at the signed-MW six, where it misses by a narrow margin, and cold winter nights stay under-covered at the six. Experiment 435 found that table P failed on clean rows, but it recalibrated a different forecaster (experiment 428's arm R-inj, whose raw q95 was 0.851 at the six and 0.904 at the eight), so the two results are not a like-for-like contradiction. Table P passes at the eight here. Its factors are fitted on the other four folds, including folds later in time than the one scored, so its coverage is optimistic. The strict fit, which uses earlier folds only, is the figure to plan on.

Terms.

  • The eight and the six: the eight Primary substations whose telemetry is in MVA, and the six whose telemetry is in signed MW. They are scored separately. D15 and D18 are two further Primaries with a short history, reported but never judged.
  • A-pool, A-gam-in, K2-425A: the demand forecasters of experiment 470. A-pool averages five seeds of experiment 425's arm A. A-gam-in adds a generalised additive model input and exists for the eight only. K2-425A is a variant of A-pool that experiment 470 found worse at q99.
  • Table P: a factor, per metering group, lead band, and tail, on each tail quantile's distance from the median. A lead band is a range of hours ahead, such as 12 to 36 hours.
  • NRA-corrected actuals: actuals with the effect of a load shift removed, giving the power on the normal running arrangement (NRA). BG2 is the best-guess demand forecaster of experiment 425's series, and manual_heuristic is NGED's rule. In the curtailment rows, f is the fraction of the node's past maximum export used as the limit.

Question and answer. The question was whether a widening, rather than table P, makes the tails honest. The prior from experiment 435 was that a widening would. The answer is no at the eight: the widening misses the q05 and q01 floors. The experiment narrows the first release's recalibration choice to table P at the eight and leaves the six open.

Figure 1 shows coverage with 95% intervals against the target ranges (green).

Figure 2 shows how often actuals exceed q99, raw and widened, by fold.

Figure 3 ranks the 20 worst half-hours of A-pool (widened) by q99 pinball loss.

Figure 4 shows the 12 worst of those half-hours, each as the forecast from its origin with the target half-hour marked in orange.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and method
docs.text:
• Arms: A-pool (experiment 425's arm A, five seeds averaged), A-gam-in (the eight only), and K2-425A (the eight and D15/D18; three cells averaged in quantile space). Variants: raw, w1.15 (distance of the four tail quantiles from the median times 1.15), and P (table P, fitted on the clean rows of the other four folds, one factor per group, lead band, and tail). The sweep 1.05 and 1.10 is in free_tails.parquet.
  • Rows: the gam14 set of experiment 470 plus D15 and D18 (report-only). Folds: 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06; July 2026 is nearly unused (experiment 470's scoring included 9 hours of valid times on 2026-07-01, so July scoring in later work starts at 2026-07-02 00:00). Flagged exact-zero half-hours are dropped (inherited from experiment 470's scoring context). The experiment 399 start cut for D15 and D18 is inherited from experiment 470's rows.
  • Actuals: rejoined from experiment 470's scoring context. "Rows with no labelled event" are cls == "clean". NGED's event labels are incomplete, so these rows may hold unlabelled events.
  • Intervals: month-by-origin-day block bootstrap, 20,000 resamples. The Bonferroni count is 10 (8 contrasts of table P minus the widening, on CRPS and q99 pinball loss, each for 4 combinations of group and candidate; plus 2 contrasts of K2-425A minus A-pool at q99 pinball loss, raw and widened).
  • Minimum detectable effect (A-pool five single seeds, 1.15 widening): at the eight, CRPS 0.044 points, q95 coverage 0.010, q99 coverage 0.003, and q99 pinball loss 0.0095 points; at the six, CRPS 0.087 points, q95 coverage 0.014, q99 coverage 0.008, and q99 pinball loss 0.018 points.
  • Limits on the claims: (1) The raw lower tail at the eight (q05 0.036, q01 0.005) is already inside its target range, so only a widening of both tails breaks it. The upper-tail widening above is as good as table P at the eight, so table P is needed only at the six. (2) The K2-425A contrast after table P (+0.002) has no interval, because only the raw and widened contrasts were counted. (3) Table P's pooled coverage hides fold-level misses: for A-pool at the eight, 2025-10 has q05 0.072 and q99 0.979, and 2025-12 has q05 0.027 and q95 0.966. (4) Table P's CRPS gain over the widening (0.004 points) is a tenth of the minimum detectable effect (0.044), and the six's q99 pinball difference (0.011) is below its minimum detectable effect (0.018). At the six, the Bonferroni interval for that difference spans about 4.8% to 7.4%. (5) The 20 worst half-hours are 20 rows in one fold, probably one event; the 2025-12 fold's raw exceedance share is the lowest of the five. (6) Curtailment intervals are wide: no candidate variant is distinguishable from BG2, and table P at f = 0.9 (1.79) is above BG2 (1.37).
  • Selection bias: every score is selection-biased, because the same five folds choose the candidates and score them.
  • Cadence: the stored forecasts come from monthly refits. This experiment fits only table P's factors.
  • Reused code: experiment 435 (e00435_table_p_provisional, e00435_tailcore), experiment 470 (e00470_score, e00470_build, e00470_curtailment), and experiments 449 and 454 through them.

docs.title: Results (clean rows, points of effective capacity; coverage is a fraction)
docs.text:
Group Candidate Variant q01 q05 q95 q99 q99 pinball CRPS eight A-pool raw 0.0053 0.0364 0.9216 0.9812 0.238 4.244 eight A-pool w1.15 0.0019 0.0189 0.9487 0.9906 0.235 4.246 eight A-pool P 0.0103 0.0509 0.9498 0.9894 0.236 4.242 eight A-gam-in raw 0.0057 0.0376 0.9179 0.9802 0.236 4.200 eight A-gam-in w1.15 0.0020 0.0199 0.9459 0.9899 0.231 4.202 eight A-gam-in P 0.0104 0.0512 0.9494 0.9895 0.233 4.198 eight K2-425A raw 0.0034 0.0286 0.9404 0.9881 0.236 4.132 eight K2-425A w1.15 0.0012 0.0138 0.9625 0.9941 0.246 4.140 eight K2-425A P 0.0105 0.0512 0.9493 0.9893 0.238 4.131 six A-pool raw 0.0030 0.0186 0.8851 0.9708 0.195 3.451 six A-pool w1.15 0.0011 0.0098 0.9232 0.9853 0.181 3.451 six A-pool P 0.0103 0.0443 0.9479 0.9863 0.192 3.443

Targets: q01 0.005 to 0.02, q05 0.03 to 0.07, q95 0.93 to 0.97, q99 0.98 to 0.995. The eight has 482,895 rows and the six 323,235 rows per candidate.

  • Decision rule at the eight: A-pool and A-gam-in pass with table P. CRPS is 0.004 and 0.003 points better than with the widening (A-pool: -0.0038, Bonferroni interval -0.0054 to -0.0021), and q99 pinball loss is +0.0009 (-0.0012 to 0.0035) and +0.0014 (-0.0003 to 0.0036), which is under 1% and well under the 5% limit.
  • Decision rule at the six (A-pool): the four coverages pass, but q99 pinball loss is +0.0110 (0.0087 to 0.0135) against the widening, which is +6.1% and above the 5% limit. The six fails the pinball-loss clause.
  • Widening the upper tail only (q95 and q99 distance from the median times 1.15): at the eight, A-pool gives q01 0.005, q05 0.036, q95 0.949, q99 0.991, q99 pinball loss 0.235, and CRPS 4.243, and A-gam-in gives q95 0.946, q99 0.990, and q05 0.038. Both are inside every target range, so this widening passes the decision rule at the eight as table P does. At the six it gives q95 0.923 (below the 0.93 floor) and q05 0.019 (below its 0.03 floor), so the six needs table P's lower-tail narrowing as well, and table P lifts q05 to 0.044.
  • K2-425A's q99 failure: the widening raises K2-425A's q99 pinball loss. Against A-pool, K2-425A is -0.0022 (-0.0145 to 0.0074) raw, +0.0110 (0.0021 to 0.0177) widened, and about +0.002 after table P (0.238 against 0.236). Table P repairs K2-425A's q99 loss. K2-425A's raw q95 coverage (0.940) is already inside the target range, so a 1.15 widening moves it to the top of that range (0.963) and pushes q05 to 0.014 and q01 to 0.001, below their floors.
  • Strict earlier-only fit (each scored fold is fitted on the folds before it, so 2025-10 is never scored): A-pool at the eight gives q05 0.045, q95 0.949, q99 0.992, and q99 pinball loss +0.9% against the widening, which still passes. At the six it gives q95 0.927 and q99 pinball loss +6.2%, which fails, as experiment 435 found. The leave-one-fold-out figures above are therefore optimistic.
  • Cold winter nights (rows with no labelled event): at the eight, A-pool q95 rises from 0.874 raw to 0.929 with table P and 0.940 with the cold-night class (q05 0.049, q01 0.033, so the lower tail overshoots its 0.02 ceiling). At the six, q95 rises from 0.835 to 0.904 and 0.919, and q99 stays at 0.972, below the 0.98 floor. The gap at the six is reported and no fix is added.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only, A-pool): raw q95 is 0.908; the widening gives 0.949 but q05 0.005; table P gives q95 0.918 and q05 0.023.
  • Christmas week: raw q95 coverage (A-pool) is 0.963 at the eight and 0.931 at the six. Table P raises the eight's coverage to 0.986, above the 0.97 ceiling, and the cold-night class changes nothing, so the table over-widens that week.
  • Real-event rows (NRA-corrected actuals): A-pool coverage is poor whatever the recalibration (eight: q95 0.856, q99 0.887; six: q01 0.513), so no recalibration here repairs event rows.
  • Tails by fold: the share of actuals above q99 for A-pool raw at the eight runs 0.011 to 0.029 per fold and at the six 0.015 to 0.079 (2026-01), against a target of 0.01. All of the 20 worst q99 half-hours at the eight (A-pool, widened) fall in 2025-12, so that fold alone drives the worst cases.
  • Curtailment cost at the signed-MW six (£ million over the scored rows; lower is better; 95% interval): at f = 0.9, raw 2.18 (0.19 to 5.79), widened 1.89, table P 1.79, against BG2 1.37 and manual_heuristic 2.02. At f = 0.75: 8.63, 7.05, 6.81, BG2 8.24, manual_heuristic 12.88. At f = 0.5: 24.10, 21.63, 21.75, BG2 25.92, manual_heuristic 37.79. Table P minus raw is -0.39 (-1.04 to -0.01) at f = 0.9 and -2.35 (-6.58 to +0.85) at f = 0.5.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Audit triggers: the result contradicts experiment 435 (table P failed there) and parts of the prediction, and the explanation tested is the fit (leave-one-fold-out against earlier-only, above). The maintainer's choice of first-release candidate also depends on this result. A comparison with the mean forecast was not made, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only. A fresh Sonnet audit (briefed with the PR number alone) confirmed that the fit uses none of the scored fold's actuals, that the row sets are identical, that clean rows hold no real-event rows, and that the six's +6.05% is correct. Three findings: the folds are origin months and targets run up to 10 days ahead, so 5% of 2025-12 half-hours also sit in 2026-01 (dropping them from the fit moves q95 by at most 0.0004); the six's +6% differs by fold (+1.6% to +9.0%) and by Primary (-0.4% to +13.9%); and experiment 435 recalibrated a weaker forecaster, so it is not a contradiction. The audit also asked for the upper-tail widening, which is the new bullet above.
  • Prediction outcome: P1 held. P2 held (table P matches the best widening on q95: 0.950 against 0.949, and an upper-tail widening matches it on every tail at the eight). P3 held for the six and failed for the eight (the cold class lifts cold-night q95 to 0.940). P4 failed (table P repairs K2-425A's q99 loss; the 1.15 widening of both tails does not). P5 held for q95 (D15/D18 stay under 0.93 after table P).

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Caveats: the leave-one-fold-out fit uses later folds; the strict fit is the planning figure. Five non-contiguous folds are few, and the 2025-12 fold dominates the worst half-hours. NGED's event labels are incomplete. K2-425A averages three cells in quantile space, so its numbers differ slightly from experiment 470's mean of per-cell scores.
  • Open options: fitting table P on all five folds for the eight, and scoring July 2026 once the maintainer chooses the candidate. For the six, a smaller upper-tail factor or a per-Primary variant is untested.

docs.title: Does weighting the fine-tuning rows toward cold nights, high-flow half-hours at the signed-MW six, or winter improve the demand network on those rows without losing elsewhere?
Weighting the fine-tuning rows toward hard rows did not help
docs.text:
Take-home message. The weights did not improve the forecast on the rows NGED cares about by more than the noise floor, and winter weighting raised CRPS. The result suggests the hard rows are limited by the inputs, so the next experiment could change an input or the neural-network architecture, not the weights.

We fine-tuned experiment 425's pretrained demand network (five folds, three seeds each) with a weight of 3 on cold nights (W-cold), on half-hours at or above 0.75 times a Primary's maximum flow at the signed-MW six (W-curt), and on December to February (W-season). The reference W0 is experiment 425's own stored fit: a W0 refit of 2026-01, seed 0 reproduced it exactly. Scores are CRPS in points of effective capacity on experiment 470's rows, 1.15 widening, month-block bootstrap with Bonferroni intervals (count 27). All scores are selection-biased, because the five folds that choose also score.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• W0. Experiment 425's stored arm A fits, seeds 0 to 2 (pretrained weights 00425-.../work/pretrained/A/{month}_s{0-2}.pt).
  • W-cold. Weight 3 on night half-hours (sun below -5 degrees) with ERA5 temperature at or below 3 degrees Celsius.
  • W-curt. Weight 3 on half-hours at the signed-MW six (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) whose flow is at least 0.75 times that Primary's maximum flow in the fold's window.
  • W-season. Weight 3 on local December, January, and February.
  • Compute. 45 fine-tunes, about 35 s each (about 0.5 GPU-hours), one GPU process.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Minimum detectable effect (printed before any contrast; three-seed mean). 0.083 at the eight, 0.112 at the six on rows with no labelled event, 0.169 on cold nights at the eight, and 0.236 on cold nights at the six.
  • W-cold does not meet P1. Cold-night CRPS at the eight fell by 0.068 [-0.104, -0.031], inside the 0.169 minimum detectable effect, so the contrast is inconclusive at the eight. At the six it rose by 0.031 [-0.008, +0.060]. All-row CRPS changed by -0.005 at the eight and the six.
  • W-curt does not meet P3. Avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.75 changed by -0.065 million pounds [-0.46, +0.31] against a required -0.1 with an interval below it. At f = 0.9 it rose by 0.079 [-0.03, +0.27] and at f = 0.5 it changed by -0.073 [-0.78, +0.57]. Its CRPS fell by 0.096 [-0.122, -0.072] at the six on rows with no labelled event (inside the 0.112 minimum detectable effect) and by 0.093 on cold nights at the six, but rose by 0.328 [+0.245, +0.402] on real-event rows scored against normal-running-arrangement actuals. The loss bound of 0.02 points is defined on the eight and the six overall; read on the real-event rows, it is not met.
  • W-season raises CRPS. The rises are inside the minimum detectable effect, but the Bonferroni intervals exclude zero. CRPS rose by 0.070 [+0.048, +0.094] at the eight, by 0.081 on cold nights at the eight, and by 0.133 on cold nights at the six.
  • P2 (all-row equivalence) holds for all three arms. Every all-row difference is inside the minimum detectable effect (W-season +0.070 against 0.083 at the eight; W-curt -0.096 against 0.112 at the six).
  • Absolute CRPS (W0, all arms on identical rows). Eight 4.764 (W-cold 4.759, W-curt 4.765, W-season 4.834); six, no labelled event 3.517 (3.512, 3.421, 3.543); cold nights at the eight 4.286 (4.218, 4.278, 4.367); cold nights at the six 5.955 (5.985, 5.862, 6.087).
  • Tails. On the rows with no labelled event, q99 pinball loss rose by at most 0.005 points (W-season at the eight), inside the +0.02 rule. On cold nights at the six it rose by 0.074 (W-cold) and 0.154 (W-season), outside the rule, and W-season raised q95 pinball loss at the eight by 0.024. Cold-night q99 coverage at the six is 0.872 for W0 against a 0.99 target, and no arm moved it by more than 0.01 (W-cold 0.863, W-curt 0.878, W-season 0.863).

docs.title: Rows, cost, and caveats
docs.text:
• Descriptive results outside the count. W-cold raised CRPS in Christmas week at the eight by +0.051 [+0.013, +0.086] and avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.75 by +0.17 million pounds [-0.11, +0.63]. W-season raised Christmas-week CRPS at the eight by +0.220. W-curt lowered CRPS at the six by 0.086 [-0.120, -0.054] in the 12 to 36 hour band and by 0.103 in Christmas week, a gain on the signed-MW six that the cost and the real-event rows do not confirm.
  • Cold-night intervals rest on three folds (2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03), so a month-block bootstrap on them is fragile.
  • Checks. Not run: median minus mean forecast per site, the mean-forecast error beside each quantile contrast, and the audit triggers. Triggers 3 (quantile against mean-error contrast) and 4 (leave-one-site-out) are plausibly live for W-curt, whose clean-row and real-event CRPS move in opposite directions; they are recorded as not run, and the arm is not a candidate.
  • Weighted rows. The share of training rows up-weighted at 2026-01 was 4.1% (W-cold), 2.4% (W-curt), and 20.3% (W-season); the fit logs give the per-fold and per-Primary shares.
  • Early stopping. The held-out-week loss is unweighted for every arm, and every weight multiplies the recency weight that experiment 425 already applies.
  • Production cost. None: a weight adds no serving network and no refit.
  • Not done. The example-forecast plots, the load-shift event plots, and the audit-trigger checks (median minus mean forecast, mean-forecast error) were not produced, because the verdict is a null on the contrasts above; a follow-up that builds on a weighted arm would need them.
  • Cold-night rule. The weight uses the scorer's cold_nights rule (sun below -5 degrees and ERA5 temperature at or below 3 degrees Celsius), not the brief's per-Primary decile, so the weighted and scored rows match.
  • Curtailment weight. The scorer fixes the limit from the whole history before the scored year; the weight uses each fold's window maximum, so the weighted rows are near, not equal to, the scorer's near-limit rows.
  • Label gaps. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold events.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the plan and code before the fits, and another reviewed the scorer before its numbers were read; neither found a bug.
  • Files. Fitted networks and forecasts are in the experiment's private work/ folder.
  • What to try next. Change an input (for example an explicit cold-night or load-shift signal) rather than the weights.

docs.title: Does treating 22 December to 2 January as its own regime improve the pretrained demand network's forecast over Christmas?
docs.text: No arm gained more over Christmas than one holiday can detect, and three cost skill on other days. The experiment tested five treatments of 22 December to 2 January (H1 a day-type input, H2 a Christmas weight with ERA5 replay, H3 a lag substitute, H4 all three, P a Christmas-weighted pretraining) against H0, experiment 425's arm A. The eight are the eight MVA-only Primaries, and the six are the six signed-MW Primaries. The Christmas minimum detectable effect is 0.27 CRPS points at the eight and 0.26 at the six, from the three-seed spread of the stored fits on 22 to 31 December 2025. The largest Christmas differences (H2 -0.222 at the eight, P -0.190 at the six) lie below those values, so the pre-registered stop rule applies and no gain was detected. The minimum detectable effect reflects seed spread only, so it does not prove equivalence.

docs.title: Results (CRPS in points of effective capacity, 1.15 widening, difference from H0)
docs.text:
• Row sets: differences and intervals use rows that H0 and all five arms hold. Levels such as H0's 4.777 use the smaller set that BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology also hold, so a level can differ from a difference by up to 0.005.
  • Gate, days outside the window, eight: H1 -0.004, H3 -0.002, P +0.047, H4 +0.077, H2 +0.081. H0's own score is 4.777. The gate allows +0.02, so H2, H4, and P fail. The minimum detectable effect at the eight is 0.054.
  • Gate, six on rows with no labelled event: H3 -0.018, H1 -0.001, H4 +0.009, P +0.018, H2 +0.037. H0 scores 3.563. H2's point estimate exceeds the 0.02 gate, but its Bonferroni interval (-0.009 to 0.089) spans zero. The minimum detectable effect is 0.122, so every arm is inside it.
  • q99 pinball loss on the gate rows: H2 +0.009 and H4 +0.008 at the eight (Bonferroni intervals exclude zero), everything else within 0.003. The +0.02 absolute rule is met by all arms.
  • Cold winter nights, outside the window: at the six H3 is +0.309 (outside the minimum detectable effect of 0.26), P +0.210 and H4 +0.127 (inside it), and H2 -0.124; at the eight P is +0.213, H4 +0.255, and H2 +0.178, all outside the minimum detectable effect of 0.15.
  • Real-event rows at the six (normal-running-arrangement actuals): H3 +0.301, H4 +0.226, P +0.222. H3's lag substitute therefore hurts when an event is present.
  • Christmas, 22 to 31 December 2025 (suggestive, one holiday, day-block bootstrap, no count): at the eight H2 -0.222 (uncorrected 95% interval -0.312 to -0.131; Bonferroni with 45 tests -0.367 to -0.077), H4 -0.180, P -0.050, H3 -0.037, H1 +0.033; at the six P -0.190, H2 -0.097, H3 -0.017, H4 -0.015, H1 +0.014. H0 scores 4.604 (eight) and 4.199 (six); BG2 scores 5.173 and 3.990; manual_heuristic 5.783 and 6.801; climatology 6.929 and 7.133.
  • Days either side (17 to 21 December, 3 to 6 January): H2, H3, H4, and P are worse than H0 at both groups (+0.07 to +0.31); H1 is slightly better (-0.04, -0.06).
  • 1 and 2 January of fold 2026-01 (report-only, lag leakage): H3, H4, and P are worse (+0.2 to +0.9) at the six.
  • Tails on Christmas: q95 coverage at the eight is 0.968 for H0 and 0.949 to 0.971 for the others; at the six it is 0.873 for H0 and 0.832 to 0.875 for the others (below 0.95 for all).
  • Pre-registered predictions: P1 (H3 gains by more than the minimum detectable effect) failed. P2 (H1 helps least) held. P3 (H4 gains and passes the gate) failed on both counts. P4 (H2 and P stay inside the minimum detectable effect elsewhere) failed for H2 and H4 (+0.081 and +0.077 against 0.054) and for P (+0.047, inside 0.054 only narrowly).
  • Compute: 1 reproduction fit (H0r, 2026-06 seed 0: 15 epochs, val NLL 0.3641, the stored value), 75 fine-tunes of 36 to 70 seconds, and 15 P pretrainings; about 1.3 GPU-hours.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The experiment did not score avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5, the "Checks" bullets (median minus mean forecast, mean-forecast error beside each score), the load-shift event time-series plots, or a second scored Christmas (December 2024 held out). Figures 3 and 4 show one Primary and one run.
  • The Christmas and either-side slices come from one holiday, so every number there is suggestive.
  • H2 and H4 take 1.33 times the optimiser steps per epoch, so their loss differs from H0's in the batch mix and the step count as well as in the weight. Their gate losses cannot be separated from that.
  • The voted day type uses only earlier Christmases, so fold 2025-12 has years 2019 to 2024 for the Primaries with that history and none for D15 and D18; for such dates the day type is the weekday's.
  • Every score is selection-biased: the five folds that choose the arm also score it. July 2026 is unused. NGED's event labels are incomplete: "rows with no labelled event" may hold events.
  • Reference H0 is experiment 425's stored fits; the reproduction fit matched the stored fit.

docs.title: Audit (fresh Sonnet agent, from the raw stored forecasts)
docs.text:
• Trigger: three pre-registered predictions failed (P1, P3, P4) with no tested explanation.
  • Numbers reproduce: the audit re-derived H2 +0.081, H4 +0.077, P +0.047, H1 -0.004, and H3 -0.002 at the eight outside the window, and H3 +0.301 on real-event rows at the six. Every H2 and H4 seed loses to the matching H0 seed, and all arms are scored on the same 1,145,256 rows. It found no leakage in the day-type vote, the replay rows, or the lag substitution.
  • Accepted: the H2, H4, and P loss sits in two winter folds and is not specific to Christmas. The loss at the eight is +0.139 (H2) and +0.172 (P) in fold 2025-12, and +0.195 (H2) and +0.132 (P) in fold 2026-01, against at most +0.05 elsewhere. In fold 2025-12 H2 loses +0.112 on 1 to 16 December, more than five days before the window. P has neither the weight nor the replay and shares the loss, so a factor common to the winter folds may explain part of it. H2 bundles the weight with the replay (each replay row is seen about 70 times in a 10-epoch fit), so the experiment cannot say which component hurts. The advice below therefore rejects the bundles as tested, not the ideas separately.
  • Accepted: the H3 real-event harm rests on one episode. The six's real-event rows are mostly two Primaries and one long episode. In fold 2026-01 the harm is +0.725 on targets from 3 to 16 January that have a substituted lag, and -0.005 elsewhere, which fits the substituted lag removing event state. In fold 2025-12 the harm is +0.405 on rows with no substituted lag, so the +0.30 mixes substitution and a changed fit. Excluding 3 to 13 January the figure is +0.113.
  • Accepted: the gate slice includes targets up to about 16 January, which H3 and H4 affect, because long leads carry a lag back into the window. The gate numbers keep that definition.
  • Not run: a weight-only arm, a replay-only arm, and H0r in folds 2025-12 and 2026-01. The H0r run in 2026-06 matches the stored fit to 1e-8.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Score Christmas 2026 with H0 and H1, the arm that passes the gate.
  • Run a weight-only arm and a replay-only arm, and H0r in folds 2025-12 and 2026-01, before ruling out either idea.
  • Hold out December 2024 as a second scored Christmas before spending more on the question.

docs.title: Question and what the data can say
docs.text:
• Scored Christmases: one. Fold 2025-12 holds 22 to 31 December 2025 (10 days); fold 2026-01 holds 1 and 2 January and trains on Christmas 2025 beside them, so those two days are report-only (lag leakage). The window is 22 December to 2 January by UTC date everywhere.
  • Training Christmases: pretraining (ERA5 and CAMS rows with real lags, from 2019-09) holds Christmas 2019 to 2024; the ENS fine-tuning window (from 2024-04, 730 days) holds Christmas 2024 and, for folds after the new year, Christmas 2025. Fold 2025-12 never trains on its own Christmas.
  • Consequence: the Christmas minimum detectable effect on 10 days is large. It is printed before any contrast, every Christmas contrast is suggestive, and Christmas stays report-only for the usual gates. A second scored Christmas (December 2024 held out) needs a new fold cut and is not run.

docs.title: Design (all fine-tune experiment 425's stored arm A pretraining, three seeds, five folds)
docs.text:
• Folds: 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06 (experiment 449's), one refit per fold, monthly cadence as in 425. The experiment 399 start cut for D15 and D18 and the flagged exact-zero drop are applied exactly as in 425; the per-fold counts are logged.
  • H0 (reference, not refitted): 425's own stored fits; H0r refits seed 0 of 2026-06 to show the widened network reproduces them within noise.
  • H1: adds two input columns, sat_like and sun_like, with zero-initialised first-layer weights. On a window day the Primary's own history gives the day type: weekday-like (both zero), Saturday-like, or Sunday-like. A year votes by taking the nearest of three reference levels (mean daily power of weekdays, Saturdays, and Sundays from 15 November to 14 December and from 10 January to 10 February); the calendar dates are voted by mode over earlier years whose window ended at least 4 days before the refit. Bank holidays outside the window are not remapped (425 has a bank-holiday flag; experiment 396's holiday columns raised January error, the prior for the gate). The network already has christmas_inside, christmas_days, christmas_tent, and the day-of-week inputs, so only the day type is new.
  • H2: Christmas-period rows (valid time in the window) get weight 5 in fine-tuning, multiplying 425's recency weight 0.5 ** (age_days / SHORT_HALF_LIFE_DAYS). ERA5 and CAMS rows whose valid time is in the window (about 0.27 million rows, held-out weeks excluded) are replayed: each batch of 16,384 holds 12,288 fine-tuning rows and 4,096 replay rows drawn with replacement, the fold's mean recency weight (so replay carries about a quarter of the loss), so an epoch (one pass over the fine-tuning rows) takes 1.33 times the steps. Early stopping sees the unweighted held-out-week negative log-likelihood of the fine-tuning rows only.
  • H3: if a row's day or weekly lag half-hour lies in the window, the lag becomes the cleaned power at the same half-hour of the latest earlier day outside the window with the target date's day type (voted type in the window, weekday type outside; the day-type vote for a date uses only earlier years, and a substituted lag's age input grows by the days stepped back); a third input column lag_substituted flags it. The newest-usable-observation rule is kept because the search only moves back. The origin lag is not touched. The rule is the same in training and at forecast time.
  • H4: H1 plus H2 plus H3.
  • P (requested 2026-11-01 by the manager for the maintainer): a new pretraining of arm A's network with the window rows weighted 5 over Christmas 2019 to 2024 (pretraining cap and patience as 425), then the plain 425 fine-tune. It separates "Christmas skill from pretraining on all six Christmases" from "fine-tune emphasis" (H2).

docs.title: Does the share of training rows with a corrupted lag, and how it changes during training, alter how far the lagged network follows a level change in its lags?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead B-mix's lead over the lagged network is partly the look-ahead. Contrasts between variants of the lagged network are unaffected. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532. Training with more artificial load-shift events in the lags makes the forecast follow a step in its recent readings less, and raises its error on ordinary rows; none of the shares or schedules tried removes the following for free. We asked whether the share of training rows that hold an artificial event, and how that share changes during training, alters how far a neural network's median forecast follows a sudden step in its recent power readings (its 3 lags: the newest usable reading, the reading at the same time of day on an earlier day, and the reading at the same time of day and weekday on an earlier week). We trained the same neural network on copies of the training data (called worlds) in which artificial load-shift events had been inserted into the readings, so that 5% (arm R05), 28% (arm A0-inj, the reference), or 50% (arm R50) of the training rows had at least one lag inside an inserted event. Two further arms started at 50% and ended at 5% (Cur-down), or the reverse (Cur-up). We then added a step of 5% of the Primary substation's capacity to all 3 lags and measured the share of the step that appeared in the median forecast. That share was 0.224 for R05, 0.100 for A0-inj, and 0.058 for R50. R50 scored 0.119 points of capacity worse than A0-inj, and R05 0.101 better, on rows outside every event that NGED (the electricity distribution network operator) has labelled. No neural network alone beat the fixed 50/50 average of A0-inj and a forecast built without lags (B-mix).

Verdict: not supported. The hypothesis was that Cur-down would reach the low following of a high share without its loss of score. Cur-down follows 0.177 of the step, more than the 0.100 of A0-inj, and no arm improves on A0-inj on injected harm rows. The hypothesis text described a lower following for a schedule that ends at a low share, which the sweep shows is the wrong way round. All numbers are interim: they come from five months and one to three seeds, and no interval is adjusted for the 16 contrasts. The sweep and the bad-data injections cover leads under 48 hours. NGED's logs may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may hold events.

Terms. A lag is one of those 3 readings of the substation's power from an earlier time. A harm row is a forecast target outside every event whose lags lie inside one, so a forecast that trusts its lags is misled. Injected harm rows are harm rows in the injected scoring worlds (w200 to w202), where events are many. Points of capacity are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, computed from 11 quantiles) as a percentage of the Primary's capacity. The signed-MW six are the 6 Primary substations that report signed power. B-mix is the 50/50 mixture of the stored A0-inj forecast and the lagless forecast, which is built without any lag. The lagless table holds that forecast for every half-hour.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and rates. Every arm is experiment 404's A0-inj neural network, trained for 6 epochs on one injected world per epoch. The share of training rows with at least one of the 3 lags inside an injected event, at 2026-06 seed 0, is 4.9% for R05, 27.8% for A0-inj (experiment 404 called it 20%), and 49.3% for R50. Cur-down uses 49.3%, then 27.8%, then 4.9%, for 2 epochs each; Cur-up uses the reverse. In the other cells the shares are 4.4% to 5.7%, 25.9% to 28.8%, and 45.4% to 49.6%.
  • Reproduction. The re-fitted A0-inj at 2026-06 seed 0 matches the stored forecasts to at most 1.4e-4 of capacity at every quantile.
  • Minimum detectable effect. From the seed spread of the stored A0-inj at 2026-06 (seeds 0 to 2), 2.8 standard deviations: 0.144 on rows with no labelled event and 0.155 on injected harm rows. Experiment 404's month-to-month spread (0.3 to 1.0 points) is larger. The clean-row equivalence limit of experiment 439 is 0.061.
  • Contrasts at the signed-MW six (points of capacity, negative is better; unadjusted 95% intervals from resampling months; the number after the interval is the cells better than the reference, of 7). The pre-registered Bonferroni level for k = 16 is stricter, and only the interval for R05 on rows with no labelled event (-0.144 to -0.048) would plausibly survive it.
Arm Absolute, no labelled event Minus A0-inj Minus B-mix Absolute, injected harm Minus A0-inj Minus B-mix A0-inj (stored) 3.698 +0.350 (0.171 to 0.598) 4.019 +0.365 (0.177 to 0.566) R05 3.590 -0.101 (-0.144 to -0.048), 7 +0.250 (0.068 to 0.530) 4.077 +0.066 (0.019 to 0.113), 1 +0.431 (0.229 to 0.679) R50 3.793 +0.119 (0.006 to 0.220), 2 +0.469 (0.248 to 0.768) 4.065 +0.071 (-0.008 to 0.150), 3 +0.436 (0.220 to 0.717) Cur-down 3.676 -0.009 (-0.087 to 0.081), 5 +0.342 (0.151 to 0.609) 4.065 +0.071 (0.012 to 0.130), 2 +0.436 (0.257 to 0.662) Cur-up 3.768 +0.092 (-0.001 to 0.186), 3 +0.443 (0.233 to 0.745) 4.056 +0.061 (-0.021 to 0.152), 3 +0.427 (0.233 to 0.691)
  • P1 partly holds. At 3 lags and leads under 48 hours, R05 follows 0.124 more of the step than A0-inj (0.224 against 0.100). R50 follows 0.042 less (0.058), which is 0.008 short of the 0.05 that P1 asked for. At leads of 48 to 120 hours, R50 follows 0.037 less (0.054 against 0.091), which is 0.013 short.
  • P2 fails. R50 scores 0.119 worse than A0-inj on rows with no labelled event (0.006 to 0.220), against the 0.05 predicted. The gap is inside the 0.144 seed spread and above the 0.061 clean-row limit of experiment 439.
  • P3 holds as an equivalence check. Cur-down is 0.092 behind R05 on rows with no labelled event, inside the 0.144 seed spread. It is 0.009 better than A0-inj there, and 0.005 behind R05 on injected harm rows.
  • P4 holds. Every neural network alone is 0.25 to 0.47 behind B-mix on rows with no labelled event, and R05 narrows the gap from 0.35 to 0.25.
  • Stop rule. The stop rule does not fire, because R05 differs from A0-inj on the sweep share by 0.124, more than 0.05. R50 differs by 0.042, so the rate is shown to matter below 28% and not shown to matter above it.
  • Mixtures (descriptive, not in k). Mixed with the lagless table, R05 is 0.073 better than B-mix on rows with no labelled event (-0.094 to -0.048, better in 7 of 7 cells) and 0.030 better on injected harm rows (-0.060 to 0.000). The mixed R50, Cur-down, and Cur-up are within 0.06 of B-mix.
  • Sweep. Median shift as a share of a step of 5% of capacity at 3 lags, leads under 48 hours (mean of 5 months; lowest to highest month): A0-inj 0.100 (0.084 to 0.128); R05 0.224 (0.161 to 0.268); R50 0.058 (0.052 to 0.070); Cur-down 0.177 (0.152 to 0.213); Cur-up 0.067 (0.050 to 0.085). The ratio of band width to its width without the step stays within 1.006 for every arm. The control that hides all three lags was not run, because experiment 404's sweep builds it only for arms whose names start with "B". The lagless forecast follows 0 by construction, so the mixture follows about half of the neural network's share.
  • Bad-data injections. Median shift as a share of the corruption, mean of 5 months, in the order A0-inj, R05, R50, Cur-down, Cur-up. A stuck reading for 24 hours: 0.056, 0.102, 0.028, 0.086, 0.030. A dropout to zero for 6 hours: 0.024, 0.032, 0.019, 0.051, 0.017. A spike of 4 times the week-on-week change: 0.024, 0.032, 0.023, 0.036, 0.022. A spike of 20 times: 0.004, 0.014, 0.010, 0.013, 0.011. The corruption definitions are experiment 465's, with the size measured over the corrupted readings only.
  • Tails (signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event, raw quantiles; coverage of q01, q05, q95, and q99, then q99 pinball loss in points of capacity). A0-inj: 0.011, 0.043, 0.813, 0.915; 0.349. B-mix: 0.005, 0.025, 0.856, 0.950; 0.259. R05: 0.011, 0.043, 0.822, 0.928; 0.305. R50: 0.011, 0.041, 0.796, 0.901; 0.415. Every neural network alone is under-covered at q95 and q99. Its q99 pinball loss is 0.046 (R05) to 0.156 (R50) above B-mix's, beyond the +0.02 limit. The four mixtures with the lagless table are within 0.018 of B-mix on rows with no labelled event, and within 0.022 on injected harm rows. The full table, including the 12 to 36 hour band, is in work/scores/tails.csv.
  • Avoidable curtailment (signed-MW six; million pounds summed over the cells of the five months; 95% interval resampling cells). At f = 0.9, R05 minus A0-inj is -0.09 (-0.44 to 0.17) and R50 is -0.06 (-0.35 to 0.14). At f = 0.75, R50 is +1.58 (0.25 to 3.32) and Cur-up +1.21 (0.23 to 2.42). At f = 0.5, R05 is -3.12 (-7.94 to 0.37), R50 +4.78 (1.46 to 8.82), and Cur-up +3.31 (0.49 to 6.57). A0-inj minus B-mix is +0.19, +0.90, and +2.69 at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5, with every interval including zero.
  • Serving cost. Each arm serves one neural network per pass, with no table to refresh and no detector or gate, and the share and schedule of injected rows add nothing at serving. B-mix serves two neural networks (the lagged network and the lagless one), the cross-fitted lagless table, and a mixture step. Removing that complexity leaves a gap to B-mix of +0.25 (R05) to +0.47 (R50) on rows with no labelled event and +0.43 to +0.44 on injected harm rows.
  • What the share would change for an operator. A forecast trained with a higher share of artificial events follows a sudden step in the last few days of power readings less, and is a little less accurate on ordinary days. The share needs no event labels.
  • Row counts (signed-MW six, summed over the 7 cells): 626,771 rows with no labelled event and 1,138,838 injected harm rows. Rows inside real events, rows after events, and cold-night rows were not scored separately.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, and the error of the mean forecast. Neither was computed: the stored forecasts hold 11 quantiles and not the mean of the mixture.
  • Audit triggers. No control failed, no nested arm beat the arm that contains it, and the headline intervals are of the same order as experiment 404's. The prediction for R50 in P1 missed by 0.008 at leads under 48 hours; the miss is small, and no audit was run.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet review of the plan and code before the first fit, one Sonnet review of the scoring scripts before the numbers were quoted, one Sonnet check of the numbers against the stored tables, and one Sonnet prose review. Each finding was triaged in the pull request.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Do not tune the share further. The 3 rates between 5% and 50% show one trade-off between the following and the error on ordinary rows; other rates were not tested, and the best-scoring arm (R05) follows the most.
  • Stage the difficulty of events (the follow-up named for this experiment) only if the leak must fall at constant score; this experiment gives no evidence for it.
  • Stored artefacts. Fitted neural networks are in data/ml-experiments/00486-lagged-network-injection-rate-and-schedule/work/models/, forecasts under work/predictions/, and tables under work/scores/.

docs.title: Plan (written before any score was read)
docs.text: The lagged neural network (A0-inj of experiment 404) learns from training worlds in which power readings have been corrupted by injected load-shift events, and the share of training rows with a corrupted lag has never been varied. Experiment 404 chose it once. This experiment trains the same network, on the same rows and with the same loss, on worlds with a different share, and on two schedules that change the share during training. It then asks whether the network's median still follows a step in its lags, and what that costs on rows with no labelled event.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms are experiment 404's A0-inj network (mixture density network, three origin lags, six epochs, experiment 397's recency weights, monthly refit, lagless table frozen), trained on injected worlds saved to disk, one per rate and seed. Only the world in each epoch changes.

Arm Share of training rows with a lag inside an injected event Schedule A0-inj (reference, stored) 27.8% measured at 2026-06 (experiment 404 called it 20%) constant R05 4.9% constant R50 49.3% constant Cur-down 49.3%, then 27.8%, then 4.9% epochs 1 to 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 6 Cur-up 4.9%, then 27.8%, then 49.3% epochs 1 to 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 6
  • Rate definition. Spikes count as events, and the shares are for 2026-06 seed 0 (the write-up reports the share in every cell). The share counts training rows with at least one of the three origin lags inside an injected event, measured on the 2026-06 training pool at seed 0 (e00486_fit.py share). The brief's 5%, 20%, and 50% are the labels; the stored world measures 27.8% by this definition. The new worlds use experiment 428's injection with the event coverage changed to 0.016 (R05) and 0.18 (R50), set by measuring candidate worlds (0.02, 0.04, 0.20, 0.30 gave 6.4%, 11.4%, 54.1%, and 73.4%).
  • Worlds are per seed and new for each rate. Training seeds 100 to 102; the scoring worlds w200 to w202 and the clean world w-1 are experiment 404's, unchanged, so every arm is comparable with the stored A0-inj and B-mix.
  • Reproduction. A0-repro re-fitted A0-inj for 2026-06 seed 0: on world w200 its quantiles differ from the stored A0-inj by at most 1.4e-4 of capacity. The check passes if every arm-level score matches the stored one within the minimum detectable effect; it is also the noise floor. No other cell is refitted.
  • Mixtures. Each new arm is also scored as the fixed 50/50 mixture with the cross-fitted lagless table (X+lagless), read alone and in the mixture; the mixture contrasts are descriptive.

docs.title: Minimum detectable effect, row sets, and the stop rule
docs.text:
• Minimum detectable effect (MDE). Computed from the stored A0-inj and B-mix before any new arm is read, and printed first. Source 1: the seed spread at 2026-06 (seeds 0 to 2). Source 2: experiment 404's month-to-month spread (0.4 to 1.0 points on harm rows, 0.3 to 0.9 inside events, 0.3 to 0.8 on clean rows). Clean-row equivalence uses experiment 439's bar of 0.061. For the sweep share, equivalence means within 0.05 of A0-inj.
  • Row sets of the 16 contrasts. Signed-MW six only (the MVA-only eight apart, never pooled). Rows with no labelled event: the clean real world w-1. Injected harm rows: pooled over w200 to w202. Contrasts use the five months at seed 0; seeds 1 and 2 at 2026-06 give the MDE and descriptive rows. Intervals are month-block bootstraps with the sign count over the five months beside each; event slices use whole-event intervals.
  • Stop rule. Evaluated after the seed-0 cells of R05 and R50. If it fires, Cur-down and Cur-up still run on those cells, but 2026-06 seeds 1 and 2 are not fitted for any arm.
  • References. The gain is read against A0-inj; q99 pinball loss within +0.02 is against B-mix; no loss on rows with no labelled event is judged against the 0.061 bar.

docs.title: What the write-up will state
docs.text:
• One sentence an operator could read on what the regime changes in the forecast; that the regime needs no event labels.
  • Serving cost per arm and per reference: networks per pass (one for an arm, two for B-mix), tables stored and refreshed (none, against the lagless table), detector or gate (none), and the score gap to B-mix on rows with no labelled event, harm rows, and injected harm rows.
  • q01, q05, q95, and q99 coverage and pinball loss, the 12 to 36 h lead band, raw and after table P with the 1.15 widening; row counts per row class (including rows inside real events, after events, and cold nights); avoidable curtailment at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5.
  • The readings-level sweep and the bad-data injections of experiment 465 (copied from its branch with credit, since it is unmerged), the time series plots, and the dataviz skill's rules.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
• Fits: 4 arms × 7 cells (five scored months at seed 0; 2026-06 at seeds 0 to 2) = 28 fits at about 26 s each on the GPU, about 0.2 GPU-hours, one GPU process under 8 GB and one feeder core.
  • Reused: the stored A0-inj and B-mix forecasts on all 7 cells; one reproduction fit.
  • Scoring: forecasts on w200 to w202 and w-1 for 8 arms (four networks alone and mixed), the sweep, the corruption injections, curtailment, and the bootstrap dominate the wall time.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Monthly refits; cleaned data with flagged substation_zero half-hours dropped (the count per cell is printed with the scoring); the D15 and D18 start cut before 2025-03-01; fitted networks saved under this experiment's data folder; stored forecasts reused; tails and curtailment reported; the unlogged-event caveat stated: NGED's logs may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may hold events, the harm table is optimistic, and real-event slices undercount. Weather inputs are the ECMWF ENS mean and spread of experiment 404 (no past-weather lags enter the network, so the past-weather caveat does not apply).

docs.title: Reading earlier advice
docs.text: The plan follows experiment 404's advice to use the fixed 50/50 mixture B-mix as the reference and to report the absolute score and event counts beside every contrast. It departs from nothing.

docs.title: Does mixing ERA5-and-CAMS rows into the fine-tuning batches improve the demand neural network on cold winter nights and in the tails?
docs.text:
Replaying ERA5-and-CAMS rows does not fix cold winter nights at the eight, and its gain at the six is below the seed-noise minimum detectable effect. Fine-tuning experiment 425's arm A with 25% or 50% of each step's loss on ERA5-and-CAMS pretraining rows left CRPS at the eight MVA-only Primaries unchanged on all rows (R25 +0.006, R50 +0.031), and replaying only cold-night rows (Rcold) made the eight slightly worse (+0.037). On rows with no labelled event, R25 lowers the eight's CRPS by 0.028 (Bonferroni interval excludes zero), so the all-rows result hides a gain on clean rows and a loss on event rows. At the signed-MW six, plain replay lowered CRPS on rows with no labelled event by 0.075 to 0.088 points (about 2 to 2.5%). The block bootstrap excludes zero for that gain, with or without the 2026-01 fold (R25 −0.039 and R50 −0.034 without it), but the gain is below the 0.112-point three-seed minimum detectable effect, which measures the seed noise the bootstrap leaves out. The match with a five-seed pool and the six's cold-night gain both come from 2026-01 alone. The experiment is inconclusive and no arm is a candidate. All scores are selection-biased, because the five folds that choose the candidate also score it. July 2026 is unused.

The neural network shows no sign of forgetting cold nights at the eight. The question was whether the neural network forgets rare cold nights during fine-tuning on the ensemble (ENS) rows, which start in 2024-04. The answer at the eight is no sign of forgetting. The experiment narrows replay to a possible regulariser at the six and rules out cold-night-only replay.

Figure 1 shows each replay arm minus R0 on the seven CRPS row sets, with 27-test Bonferroni intervals. Below zero is better.

Figure 2 shows the same differences by fold for the eight and the six on rows with no labelled event. The six's gain comes mainly from the 2026-01 fold.

Arms and design.

  • Arms: all fine-tune the stored arm A pretrained weights of experiment 425 (learning rate 2e-4, seeds 0 to 2, folds 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). R0 is experiment 425's stored fit. R25 and R50 put 25% and 50% of each step's loss weight on ERA5-and-CAMS rows. Rcold does as R25 but draws replay rows only from cold nights (sun more than 5 degrees below the horizon, 2 m temperature of 3 degrees Celsius or below; about 4.7% of the replay rows). Drawing from cold nights as the scored slice defines them replaces the decile definition of lowest temperature, December to February, sun below -6 degrees. The slice is called "cold nights" because it covers every month.
  • Step and loss: an epoch is one pass over the ENS training rows in batches of 16,384 ENS rows (R0's steps). Each step adds 5,461 (R25, Rcold) or 16,384 (R50) replay rows, drawn with replacement. Step loss is (1 - r) times the recency-weighted ENS loss plus r times the unweighted replay loss. Early stopping reads the unweighted ENS held-out weeks only. The replay share is a loss share, not a row share per batch.
  • Replay rows: the fold's pretraining rows with the held-out weeks and purge excluded and both standing cuts applied; the same 46 inputs, with the std_* columns set to the fold's median ENS spread by lead band. ERA5-and-CAMS weather is not available at forecast time; it enters training only.
  • Fits and cost: 45 fits plus one reproduction fit, about 65 minutes with one GPU process (peak 3.2 GB, one feeder core). Predictions, weights, and logs are in the experiment's private folder work/. Code reused from experiments 397, 418, 425, 454, and 470.
  • Reproduction check: the R0 refit (2026-01, seed 0) matches the stored fit: largest quantile difference 1e-5, 10 epochs each, CRPS 4.5462 at the eight and 4.8854 at the six for both. Passed.
