  • Production cost: serving is unchanged. The monthly refit needs the ERA5-and-CAMS table and 1.33 times (R25) or 2 times (R50) the rows per epoch.

Cold-night CRPS cannot be resolved below 0.169 at the eight and 0.236 at the six. The minimum detectable effect was printed before any contrast (points of capacity). Five single seeds of arm A give a seed standard deviation of 0.052 (eight), 0.070 (six, no labelled event), 0.105 (cold nights, eight), and 0.147 (cold nights, six). For two arms of three seeds each the minimum detectable effect is 0.083, 0.112, 0.169, and 0.236.

No arm lowered cold-night CRPS with an interval that excludes zero. The table gives CRPS in points of effective capacity, 1.15 widening; difference against R0 with the 27-test Bonferroni interval; Bonferroni count 27).

Row set R0 R25 − R0 R50 − R0 Rcold − R0 Eight, all rows 4.764 +0.006 (−0.023, 0.037) +0.031 (−0.012, 0.078) +0.037 (0.013, 0.065) Six, no labelled event 3.517 −0.075 (−0.106, −0.048) −0.088 (−0.133, −0.048) −0.049 (−0.083, −0.017) Six, real events (NRA) n/a +0.053 (−0.030, 0.132) +0.034 (−0.081, 0.139) +0.042 (−0.126, 0.206) Eight, cold nights 4.286 −0.012 (−0.068, 0.046) +0.026 (−0.058, 0.107) +0.047 (−0.024, 0.120) Six, cold nights 5.955 −0.100 (−0.190, 0.002) −0.112 (−0.237, 0.016) −0.025 (−0.128, 0.063) Eight, 12 to 36 h n/a −0.019 (−0.064, 0.028) +0.013 (−0.058, 0.091) +0.012 (−0.025, 0.053) Six, 12 to 36 h n/a −0.083 (−0.127, −0.040) −0.104 (−0.169, −0.042) −0.025 (−0.068, 0.017)
  • Context: A-pool (five-seed average) scores 4.680 (eight), 3.451 (six), 4.161 and 5.931 (cold nights, eight and six). R25 and R50 at the six (3.441, 3.429) match A-pool in the pooled mean, but only through 2026-01: in the other four folds R25 is 0 to 0.05 worse than A-pool. At the eight, R0 is 0.084 worse than A-pool and the replay arms 0.09 to 0.12 worse.
  • Predictions: P1 (Rcold lowers cold-night CRPS by 0.05 at both) is inconclusive at the eight (+0.047, interval −0.024 to 0.120, against a minimum detectable effect of 0.169, so the wrong-sign estimate is within seed noise) and inconclusive at the six. P2 holds at the eight (R25 and R50 intervals lie inside ±0.083) and fails at the six (an improvement, so not equivalence). P3 holds: q99 pinball loss changes by at most +0.003 points (eight) and −0.012 (six).
  • Stop rule: not met, because the cold-night minimum detectable effect (0.169 and 0.236) is above 0.05. The idea is not closed; the cold-night result is inconclusive.
  • Candidates: none. All three arms fail the +0.02 non-inferiority gate at the eight (upper bounds 0.037 for R25, 0.078 for R50, and 0.065 for Rcold), and R25 and R50 do not lower cold-night CRPS with an interval excluding zero at both groups.
  • Eight on rows with no labelled event (not one of the 27 tests): −0.028 (R25, Bonferroni interval −0.052 to −0.005), −0.024 (R50, −0.055 to +0.006), and +0.014 (Rcold, −0.006 to +0.033). Rcold's loss at the eight rests on all rows.
  • Epoch cap: R50 reached the 40-epoch cap in 4 of its 15 fits and R25 reached 37 epochs, so early stopping did not fire in those fits and the replay arms may be under-trained (R0 stops near 10 epochs). A higher cap could change R50 and the eight's null in either direction.
  • Cold nights exist in only 3 of the 5 folds (2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03; none in 2025-10 and 2026-06). Without 2026-01 the six's cold-night difference is +0.024 (R25), +0.067 (R50), and +0.072 (Rcold), so the sign flips; at the eight it stays small and negative to near zero (−0.023, −0.007, −0.006).
  • Validation loss: replay lowers the ENS held-out negative log-likelihood (2026-01: R25 0.355, R0 0.364 to 0.369) but not CRPS at the eight.

Replay changes tail coverage by 0.007 or less at the eight, and cold nights at the six stay far under target. Coverage is of the 1.15-widened bands, with targets q95 0.95, q99 0.99, q05 0.05, and q01 0.01. At the eight, R0 has q95 0.945 and q99 0.989; the replay arms move by at most 0.007. At the six, q95 rises from 0.918 (R0) to 0.925 to 0.928 (R25, R50). On cold nights at the six every arm stays far below target (q95 0.787 to 0.804, q99 0.871 to 0.877; Rcold's cold-night q99 pinball loss rises by 0.061), and Rcold raises cold-night q01 coverage at the eight to 0.009 and at the six to 0.068 (target 0.01), so its lower tail worsens. Full tables are in work/scores/absolute.csv.

Every replay arm lowers avoidable-curtailment cost at the six at f = 0.9, by an amount whose 95% interval only just excludes zero. The cost is in GBP million summed over the five scored folds, rows with no labelled event, scaled limit f. R0: 1.87 (f = 0.9), 7.07 (0.75), 21.70 (0.5); manual heuristic at f = 0.75 is 12.88. Paired difference against R0 with a 95% interval (not corrected for the nine comparisons): at f = 0.9, R25 −0.29, R50 −0.41, Rcold −0.39, each statistically significant at the 5% level; at f = 0.75 and 0.5 the intervals mostly include zero (f = 0.5: R25 −1.38, significant). The totals carry wide intervals (R0 at f = 0.9: 0.18 to 4.90), as in experiment 470.

Checks.

  • Audit: two triggers fired (gain concentrated in one fold, and a prediction answered the other way). A fresh Sonnet auditor re-derived every contrast, the 27 Bonferroni intervals, the fold shares, and the minimum detectable effects, and confirmed the verdict "inconclusive, no candidate". It found that leaving out 2026-01 does not remove the six's no-event gain for R25 and R50 (−0.039 and −0.034, Bonferroni intervals −0.060 to −0.019 and −0.065 to −0.008) and removes only Rcold's (−0.003). The wording above follows its findings. The 2026-01 fold supplies 58% (R25) and 68% (R50) of the pooled gain (−0.237 and −0.325 in that fold).
  • Not run: the median-minus-mean check and the mean-forecast error contrast, the load-shift event plots (no event contrast is claimed), and the example probabilistic forecast plots (the forecasts are fine-tunes of experiment 425's arm A, whose examples are on its page).
  • Caveats: NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events. Three seeds and five folds give wide seed noise. The block bootstrap does not include seed variance. Rcold draws about 4 rows per cold-night row per epoch, so memorisation of the pool is possible and is not visible to the ENS-only early stopping.

What to try next. Repeat plain 25% replay with five seeds on a second set of folds before using it at the six. Do not pursue cold-night-only replay. Leave the cold-night under-coverage at the six to recalibration.

docs.title: Do real labelled events, mixed into training or used to fine-tune, improve the lagged network?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead B-mix's lead over the lagged network is partly the look-ahead. Contrasts between variants of the lagged network are unaffected. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

Real labelled load-shift events (periods when NGED moved a substation's load to a neighbouring substation), added to the training of the lagged-power neural network, change nothing detectable. The question was whether the real events from months before the scored month improve the lagged-power neural network (A0-inj of experiment 404, a mixture density network that reads the three most recent power lags and was trained on synthetic events injected into the data) when mixed into training or used to fine-tune it. The answer at the signed-MW six is no: RealMix (real events mixed into training) is within the minimum detectable effect (MDE) of A0-inj on every row class, and PT-FT (pretrained on injected events, then fine-tuned on real ones) is worse on four of the five row classes. The result narrows the search: the label-free recipes that could replace real labels (injected or scanned events) have nothing to match beyond the target correction.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and method
docs.text:
• Terms. The signed-MW six are the six Primary substations that report signed power (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16). A harm row is one whose target lies outside every event but whose lags lie inside one. The 1.15 widening scales each quantile's distance from the median by 1.15. The lagless table holds forecasts made without power lags.

  • Network and recipe. Experiment 404's A0-inj (PlainLagMdn, injected world of seed 100, 6 epochs, experiment 397's recency weights), monthly refit, seed 0, five scored months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). One fit takes about 78 s on the GPU; the 18 fits took about 0.4 GPU-hours. Code in ml-experiments/00488-*, importing experiments 404, 428, 435, 400, and 397 without edits.

  • Arms. RealMix: rows whose target lies inside an event that ended at least 14 days before the scored month get the corrected target (actual minus experiment 435's NRA share, depth 1.0) and the observed lags; the uncorrected copies are removed. PT-FT: stored A0-inj, 2 epochs at one tenth of the learning rate, on the corrected event rows plus an equal number of rows with no labelled event from the same months. RealMix-shuf: each event's lag pattern and depth injected into a random clean period of the same Primary, with the clean target. repro: the A0-inj recipe through this experiment's loop. RealMix-d075 and RealMix-d125: RealMix with the correction scaled, 2026-06 only. +LL marks the 50/50 mixture with the cross-fitted lagless table, as B-mix does for A0-inj.
  • Training events. At the signed-MW six, 20, 28, 29, 38, and 43 events were available to the five months (64 to 113 at all 16 Primaries); no month was dropped. Rows whose target lies inside an available event are 3.45% of 2026-06 training rows, above the 2% target, so RealMix does not oversample and differs from A0-inj only by the corrected target and the observed lags on those rows.
  • Scored rows (signed-MW six, seed 0, five months pooled): 604,246 injected harm rows, 533,170 injected rows with no event, 323,235 rows with no labelled event, 44,145 real harm rows, 50,168 rows inside a padded real event (24 events), and 12,654 rows in the 96 half-hours after one. The three scoring worlds are 200 to 202; the real world is -1. Flagged zeros are dropped as in experiment 404; they were not tallied again here.
  • MDE. Seed spread of A0-inj at 2026-06 (seeds 0 to 2), for a five-month pool: 0.09 on injected harm rows, 0.13 inside events, 0.08 on rows with no labelled event, and 0.31 on real harm rows. The month-to-month spread of each contrast's own monthly differences gives larger values (0.26 on injected harm rows, 0.74 on corrected event rows, 0.25 on rows with no labelled event). The seed-based values (0.08 to 0.13) overlap P1's predicted 0.05 to 0.2, and the month-to-month values (0.25 to 0.74) exceed it, so P1 could mostly be reported as "within the MDE".

docs.title: Results (signed-MW six, raw forecasts, points of effective capacity)
docs.text:
Five-month mean of the monthly differences; the absolute scores of A0-inj and B-mix are in the second and third columns.

  • Intervals. The Bonferroni (k = 12) month-block intervals: RealMix on injected harm rows [−0.19, +0.23], on rows with no labelled event [−0.23, +0.19]; PT-FT on injected harm rows [+0.69, +1.74], on rows with no labelled event [+0.59, +1.57]; RealMix inside real events, NRA-corrected [−1.02, +0.23]; PT-FT inside real events, NRA-corrected [−4.72, +0.71] (3 of 5 months negative). Largest event dropped: RealMix −0.02, PT-FT −0.20 on corrected event rows.
  • PT-FT trades four row classes for an uncertain gain on corrected event rows. Fine-tuning scores better on corrected event rows in three of the five months but worse on rows with no labelled event in all five, so fine-tuning on event rows costs accuracy on ordinary rows.
  • The mixtures with the lagless table are the same as B-mix. RealMix+LL minus B-mix: −0.03 on injected harm rows, −0.05 on rows with no labelled event, +0.003 on metered event rows (all inside the MDE); PT-FT+LL is worse (+0.40, +0.34, +0.31).
  • Reproduction check. repro was fitted for 2026-06 only. Its difference from A0-inj is 0.000 on every row class there, so this experiment's training loop reproduces the stored recipe exactly.
  • Depth sensitivity (2026-06 only, depth-1.0 corrected event rows, minus A0-inj). RealMix-d075 −0.02 and RealMix-d125 −0.14, against RealMix −0.22 over five months; a single month cannot rank them.
  • The eight MVA-only Primaries (descriptive). RealMix +0.19 [0.04, 0.34] on injected harm rows and +0.10 on rows with no labelled event; PT-FT +0.73 and +0.59. Corrected event rows: RealMix −0.49 [−0.82, −0.16], RealMix-shuf −0.39 [−0.81, +0.03], PT-FT −0.69 [−1.38, +0.07] (26 events). Both RealMix and RealMix-shuf improve the corrected event rows at the eight by a similar amount, so the gain there does not come from the real events' content.
  • Tails, signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event (coverage at q01, q05, q95, q99; pinball loss at q95 and q99): RealMix 0.015, 0.046, 0.814, 0.913; 0.0096, 0.0036. A0-inj 0.012, 0.044, 0.806, 0.912; 0.0098, 0.0035. B-mix: q95 0.855, q99 0.949; 0.0085, 0.0026. PT-FT 0.002, 0.013, 0.837, 0.943; 0.0105, 0.0032. After the 1.15 widening RealMix reaches q95 0.854 and q99 0.940, PT-FT 0.881 and 0.966. The q99 pinball loss is within 0.001 of B-mix for every arm.
  • Encroachment sweep (2026-06, all 16 Primaries, a 5% step in the lags). The median shifts by a share of the step, for the newest 1, 2, and 3 lags: A0-inj 0.041, 0.069, 0.104; RealMix 0.039, 0.077, 0.128; RealMix-shuf 0.040, 0.078, 0.118; PT-FT 0.037, 0.074, 0.110; B-mix 0.022, 0.036, 0.054; RealMix+LL 0.020, 0.039, 0.066. The band width ratio is 1.00 for every arm. No arm differs from A0-inj by more than 0.024.
  • Bad-data injections (2026-06, median shift as a share of the corruption). A 6-hour dropout to zero: A0-inj 0.021, RealMix 0.023, PT-FT 0.016, RealMix-shuf 0.021. A spike of 20 times the weekly spread: 0.011, 0.018, 0.003, 0.009. A stuck reading for 24 hours: 0.028, 0.032, 0.032, 0.028. The injection definitions are copied from experiment 465 (experiment 465); the spread is the median absolute change from the same half-hour a week earlier, as there.

docs.title: Serving requirements and the accuracy lost by simplifying
docs.text:
• RealMix and PT-FT serve one network per pass, with no lagless table, no mixture step, and no detector. Their accuracy loss against B-mix, which serves two networks and a refreshed table, is +0.29 and +1.49 on injected harm rows and +0.25 and +1.33 on rows with no labelled event.
  • RealMix+LL serves the same two networks and table as B-mix and matches it within the MDE.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean forecast: not computed. The stored forecasts hold the 11 quantiles only, so the mean forecast is unavailable.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. The control that should change nothing (repro) moves the score by 0.000, no nested arm beats the arm that contains it, and the intervals are similar in width to those of experiment 404 and 455. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the injected-harm and no-labelled-event contrasts of RealMix and PT-FT from the stored forecasts with its own code, and matched them to three decimals.
  • Prediction outcome: P1 reported as within the MDE for RealMix; PT-FT is worse than A0-inj, not better. P2 held (RealMix-shuf does not improve on A0-inj). P3 held (no arm beats B-mix on rows with no labelled event). P4 held (3.45% natural share).

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• NGED's event labels are incomplete. Rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events, so a real-event slice undercounts and the clean-row figures are optimistic.
  • This is a diagnostic. At about 1,300 substations NGED will supply no event labels, so a gain here could not ship without a label-free way to find events; none was found.
  • Not run: avoidable curtailment cost. The experiment 449 pipeline depends on experiment 448's stored rows and reference forecasts, which this experiment's rows do not match. Every contrast above is within the MDE or worse than A0-inj, so a curtailment difference would be small; the scoring can be added if wanted.
  • Not run: seeds 1 and 2 of the new arms. The MDE uses A0-inj's and B-mix's stored seeds; each new arm has seed 0 only. The sweep ran for 2026-06 only.
  • Depth error. The corrected target uses the labelled depth; the 0.75 and 1.25 arms ran for one month.
  • Next. A label-free recipe has only the target correction to replace; whether a scanned or injected stand-in matches RealMix is not worth testing, because RealMix itself gains nothing.

docs.title: Can one neural network, trained to match the five-network pool, forecast Primary demand as well as the pool?
Take-home message
docs.text: One network trained to copy the five-network pool scores like a single seed, not like the pool. At the eight MVA-only Primaries the single seed is 0.084 CRPS points worse than the pool, and at the eight every student sits within 0.006 points of the single seed. At the six the students are worse than the single seed by 0.012 (Dpool50) to 0.045 (Dpool80) points. The under-40% rule applies: under this recipe the pool's gain is not learnable by one network. The students match the tail coverage of a single teacher network.

docs.title: Question and answer
docs.text: Can one student network, fine-tuned to match the pool's quantile forecast, score within the minimum detectable effect of the pool? No. The pool's advantage over a single seed comes from averaging five independently fitted networks. A student that starts from the same pretrained weights and sees the teacher only on rows the teacher was fitted on scored no better than a single seed. The explanation is a likely cause, not a tested one.

The cold-night minimum detectable effect is not separately estimated; cold-night contrasts below the gate are descriptive.
  • Decision rule (Bonferroni 27): the upper bound of student minus pool must be at most the minimum detectable effect. Dpool50 gives +0.082 (upper 0.102) at the eight, which fails, and +0.077 (upper 0.094) at the six, which passes. Dpool80 (+0.090, upper 0.113 at the eight; +0.110, upper 0.135 at the six) and DpoolERA5 (+0.085, upper 0.109; +0.106, upper 0.128) fail at both. No student passes both.
  • q99 pinball loss (the +0.02 bound): the upper Bonferroni bound of student minus pool is 0.008 to 0.015 points for every student, so the bound holds. Coverage at q95 is 0.945 to 0.948 at the eight against the pool's 0.952.
  • Gap closed (descriptive): Dpool50 about 2% and Dpool80 and DpoolERA5 below 0% at the eight; the under-40% rule applies.
  • Held-out-week coverage (mean over folds and seeds) of the students at q05, q95, q99: 0.045 to 0.046, 0.949 to 0.950, 0.991 to 0.992, against the teacher's single network 0.049, 0.950, 0.991. On training rows the coverage is sharper (q05 0.034 to 0.035, against the teacher's 0.036), as the in-sample teacher is.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost at the six, f = 0.9 (in the cost units of experiment 470's curtailment table, 95% intervals): pool 1.89 (0.18 to 4.98), single seed 1.87, Dpool50 1.91, Dpool80 2.00, DpoolERA5 1.94, manual heuristic 2.02. Student minus pool is +0.019 (-0.032 to 0.093) for Dpool50. At f = 0.75 Dpool80 is +0.38 (0.08 to 0.75) above the pool. At f = 0.5 Dpool80 is +0.79 (0.34 to 1.35), DpoolERA5 +0.49 (0.19 to 0.89), and Dpool50 +0.15 (-0.20 to 0.44) above the pool.
  • Epochs: Dpool50 11.5, Dpool80 13.5, DpoolERA5 17.3 on average.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Recipe: monthly refits of experiment 425's folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06); the D15 and D18 start cut and the flagged exact-zero drop apply; the teacher is the same-month pool, so no scored actuals reach the student; the students start from the stored pretrained weights of the same seed, so student seed s shares its initialisation with teacher s. Code reviewed by one fresh Sonnet agent before the first fit (no bugs, three small fixes).
  • Design change from the brief: pinball loss against the teacher's quantile distribution, not against one value, because the point-target form made the timing fit's tails too wide (q05 coverage 0.027 against 0.049).
  • Early stopping sees the composite loss, so val_loss differs by alpha and is not compared across arms.
  • Not run: the mixture-teacher arm (dropped on the queue-order check), the earlier-months-only variant, EMA/SWA as a reference, example-forecast figures, and event plots. Every score is selection-biased; July 2026 is unused. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold unlabelled events.
  • Christmas week and D15 and D18 are in work/scores/contrasts.csv (report-only). The pool's advantage over a single seed is 0.231 points at the eight and 0.141 at the six in Christmas week. It is 0.454 points at D15 and D18.
  • The cold-night minimum detectable effect is not estimated, so cold-night contrasts are descriptive. On rows with real events scored against normal-running-arrangement actuals (six_nra), the students score slightly better than the pool; the slice is in the contrasts file.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• If the pool's gain is worth keeping, serve the pool; if one network is wanted, spend the effort on better single-network training, not on copying the pool.
  • Distillation could be retried with a teacher that is out of sample on the student's rows (a different month's pool on rows the teacher did not train on), at the cost of a leakage review.

docs.title: Plan (as registered)
docs.text: The plan as committed before any fit; the loss paragraph was updated once after the timing fit.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Teacher. The five same-month fine-tuned arm A networks of experiment 425 (work/models/A/<month>/s0..s4), all trained before the scored month. The teacher target of a row is the mean of the five networks' 11 sorted standardised quantiles, which is the quantile average that A-pool serves. Using another month's teacher would leak the scored actuals, so none is used.
  • Student. Experiment 425's pooled plain network, started from the stored pretrained arm A network of the same seed and fine-tuned on experiment 425's ENS fold rows at 2e-4 with experiment 397's loop (batch 16,384, at most 40 epochs, patience 6, gradient clip 1.0). The cuts of experiments 399 and 425 apply (the D15 and D18 start cut, the flagged exact-zero drop).
  • Loss. For a row, in standardised units: NLL(y) + alpha * P(q_s, teacher) + (1 - alpha) * P(q_s, y), multiplied by the fold's recency weight 0.5 ** (age_days / SHORT_HALF_LIFE_DAYS) and normalised by the batch's weight sum. NLL is the student's own mixture likelihood. P is the pinball loss summed over the 11 levels. Against the teacher it is the expected pinball loss over the teacher's quantiles as atoms (the scorers' level masses), because a pinball loss against one teacher value is asymmetric and widened the student's tail quantiles in the timing fit (q05 coverage 0.027 against the teacher's 0.049). Student quantiles are differentiable through the implicit function theorem on the mixture CDF. Early stopping sees the same composite loss on the held-out weeks, unweighted.
  • Arms (3 seeds, 5 folds of experiment 449: 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06):
    • Dpool50: alpha 0.5;
    • Dpool80: alpha 0.8;
    • DpoolERA5: alpha 0.5, plus one batch per step (16,384 rows) of the ERA5-and-CAMS rows that pretrained the teacher, with the teacher term only and equal row weights. The teacher outputs on those rows come from the same five networks.
    • References: A-pool (the teacher, stored), and S0 (single seeds 0 to 2 of arm A, stored).
  • Not run. D-mix (distilling the mixture of arm A seeds and lagless networks): dropped on the manager's queue-order check. The variant that distils only from rows of months before the student's validation month: not run. EMA/SWA is read from the weight-averaging experiment's page when it merges.
  • Teacher in sample. Every teacher is in sample on the fine-tuning rows, so its quantiles are sharper there than on new months. The 0.5 true-target mix and the student's own likelihood limit the copying. A student cannot exceed an honest teacher. The log under work/logs/ stores coverage at q05, q95, and q99 of the teacher and each student on the held-out weeks and on training rows.
  • Fits. 45 student fits (3 arms x 5 folds x 3 seeds), plus five teacher passes per fold (inference). One fit takes about 128 s on the GPU (experiment 425's fit, for comparison, takes 30 to 37 s with the forecast). Estimated 2.3 GPU-hours in total.
  • Monthly refits. The stored folds are the monthly refits of experiment 425. The students are scored at the same cadence.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: Rows are experiment 470's intersection (experiment_470_intersection_v1). Forecasts are widened by 1.15 as in experiment 470. Slices: the eight, the signed-MW six on rows with no labelled event, cold winter nights, and the 12 to 36 hour band; Christmas week and D15 and D18 are report-only. The month-block bootstrap with Bonferroni 27 intervals, absolute CRPS beside every contrast, July 2026 unused, every score selection-biased.

docs.title: Can one neural network that reads recent power be trained to forecast as well as a mixture of four networks and a lagless table, even when its recent power readings are wrong?
docs.text: Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead the gap between the imitation network and B-mix or K2-S1 is partly the look-ahead, so the conclusion that the lagless forecast carries information the raw readings do not is shown only at 0 to 24 h. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

docs.title: What this experiment found
docs.text:
Imitating the four-network mixture did not teach one neural network what the lagless forecast adds. We asked whether one neural network, whose demand inputs are the Primary substation's measured power at 3 earlier times, can be trained to forecast as well as K2-S1. K2-S1 is the equal-weight mixture of 2 such networks (given extra inputs) and 2 forecasts made without any recent power readings (the lagless forecast, read from a stored table). If so, the live service could run 1 network and store no table. We trained the network on injected worlds (experiment 404's copies of the real power series with artificial level shifts added), with the K2-S1 forecast, or the simpler B-mix forecast (a 50/50 mixture of 1 such network and the lagless forecast), as an extra training target at weight 0.5 on every row. We scored it on the same 5 test months as experiment 454.

On rows with no labelled event, the imitation network (D-K2) scores 3.79 points of capacity at the 6 Primaries metered in signed megawatts, against 3.85 for A0-inj (the same network trained without a teacher), 3.51 for B-mix, and 3.39 for K2-S1. A point of capacity is 1% of a Primary's effective capacity. The gap to B-mix, 0.28, is larger than the minimum detectable effect from this experiment's seed spread (0.24) and from experiment 470 (0.10). The plan's stop rule is: if the student is worse than B-mix on rows with no labelled event by more than the minimum detectable effect, one network cannot absorb the lagless forecast and the idea closes. The point estimates meet that rule by a small margin: the interval for the gap to B-mix at the 8 Primaries metered in megavolt-amperes just reaches zero. The verdict is not supported, because D-K2 is also 0.40 behind K2-S1, so the plan's recommendation rule fails on its first clause.

Glossary. "The six" and "the eight" are the 6 Primaries metered in signed megawatts and the 8 metered in megavolt-amperes. "Better in n of 5 months" counts the test months in which the arm scores lower (better) than the reference. "Bonferroni 95% interval" is a month-block bootstrap interval at the family level the plan fixes (18 contrasts).

docs.text: Figure 1. Every arm's score minus K2-S1's on rows with no labelled event, in points of capacity (negative is better).

References are experiment 454's stored forecasts of A0-inj, S1, B-mix, and K2-S1. Student seeds 0 to 2, each on its own injected world (100 to 102).
  • Signed-MW six, absolute score. K2-S1 3.387, B-mix 3.508, S1 3.708, D-K2 3.791, D-K2-corr 3.822, D-Bmix 3.839, A0-inj 3.846.

  • D-K2 minus K2-S1. +0.404 at the six (Bonferroni 95% interval 0.182 to 0.715, better in 0 of 5 months); +0.289 at the eight (0.166 to 0.419, 0 of 5).
  • D-K2 minus B-mix. +0.283 at the six (0.033 to 0.622, 0 of 5); +0.150 at the eight.

The q99 pinball loss is 0.0024 for D-K2 against 0.0022 for K2-S1 at the six (+0.02 points of capacity if the stored fraction is scaled by 100, so at the +0.02 limit; with the 1.15 widening 0.0022 against 0.0020) and 0.0026 against 0.0025 at the eight. The q95 coverage is 0.880 (D-K2) and 0.875 (K2-S1) at the six, below the nominal 0.95 for both; the 1.15 widening lifts both to about 0.91. The student is no more overconfident than its teacher on the five held-out months.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Not run, because the stop rule had already applied: cold winter nights (so no cold-night minimum detectable effect was printed), the 12 to 36 hour band, avoidable-curtailment cost, the encroachment sweep, the bad-data injections, the example forecast and real-event plots, and the K2-S1 forecast on the injected worlds. None of them can reverse the clean-row gap, but the write-up makes no claim about them.
  • Scored but not discussed: the NRA-actual event rows and the table P variant are in contrasts.csv. On NRA actuals at the six, D-K2 minus B-mix is -0.028 (interval -0.327 to +0.186, better in 2 of 5 months) and D-K2 minus K2-S1 is +0.006 (-0.251 to +0.273). Prediction P2 (no worse than K2-S1 by more than the minimum detectable effect on event rows and injected harm rows) holds on the event rows at the six; it cannot be checked on injected harm rows because K2-S1 has no forecast there.
  • The teacher networks are in sample on the student's training rows; only the lagless table is cross-fitted. The lagless forecast's standard deviation is limited to a fixed range twice (as in experiment 404's B-mix scoring). D-Bmix distils from A0-inj of the same fit seed, so it partly imitates a network with the same initialisation and batch order. The teacher's in-sample sharpness did not show up as overconfidence on the 5 test months (q95 coverage above).
  • 5 scored months, 3 seeds, and NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlogged events. Every score is selection-biased, and July 2026 stays unused.
  • Every interval quoted is a month-block bootstrap interval at the Bonferroni level of the 18 contrasts the plan fixes. The stop rule rests on point estimates, and the interval for D-K2 minus B-mix at the 8 runs from -0.0002 to +0.339.
  • Reviews: one fresh Sonnet language-model code review before the first fit (it found no blocking bug; three crash guards applied). One Sonnet write-up review checked the numbers and prose; its 10 findings were applied.

docs.title: Can one demand network, trained once with an exponential moving average or a stochastic weight average of its weights, recover a useful share of the five-network pool's gain?
Take-home
docs.text: One averaged neural network gains almost nothing over one ordinary neural network, while a pool of seeds closes most of the gap to the five-network pool. The demand networks here forecast power at 16 substations, and CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, in points of effective capacity; lower is better) scores each forecast. At the eight MVA-only Primaries, the fixed-budget single network scores 4.762 points, the five-network pool 4.680, the exponential moving average (EMA) network 4.760, and the stochastic weight average (SWA) network 4.757. The pool of three EMA networks scores 4.697. At the six signed-MW Primaries, on rows with no labelled event, the same five arms score 3.524, 3.451, 3.508, 3.515, and 3.451. The gap to the five-network pool is 0.082 points at the eight and 0.073 at the six. The seed-noise minimum detectable effect is 0.083 at the eight and 0.112 at the six. Each gap is therefore about the size of the noise, so the experiment can show only that weight averaging gains little. It cannot rank the arms closely. These results are interim, because they rest on 5 months of data and one fine-tune trajectory per seed.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. CRPS of each arm.

Figure 2. Share of the gap from S0f to Pool5 that each arm closes.

Figure 3. Counted contrasts with Bonferroni intervals.

Figure 4. Example forecasts of one Primary.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Every score is in CRPS points of effective capacity at the 1.15 tail widening, the mean of three seeds on experiment 470's rows. Experiment 470 (the first-release demand forecaster comparison) supplies the rows, which hold the eight MVA-only Primaries (substations metered in MVA only) and the six signed-MW Primaries (substations metered in signed MW). Each arm is scored over 15 fine-tunes: 5 held-out months times 3 seeds. A negative contrast means the first arm scores lower, which is better. The scorer printed the Bonferroni count (54) and the minimum detectable effect for the mean of three seeds before any contrast: 0.083 at the eight, 0.112 at the six on rows with no labelled event, 0.169 at the eight on cold nights, and 0.236 at the six on cold nights. Every score is selection-biased, because the five folds that choose also score.

Arms:

  • S0f: one network fine-tuned for a fixed 4 epochs, final weights.
  • S0: one network fine-tuned with early stopping (experiment 425's stored fit; the production recipe).
  • EMA, EMA99, SWA: the same fine-tune read out as an exponential moving average of the weights (decay 0.999, or 0.99 for EMA99) or a stochastic weight average over the last epoch.
  • Pool2, Pool3, Pool5: the quantile mean of 2, 3, or 5 seeds of S0 (experiment 425's stored seeds). PoolEMA3, PoolSWA3: the quantile mean of 3 EMA or SWA networks from different seeds.

  • P0f, Pswa, Pswa+EMA, Pswa+SWA: the one-fold pretraining arms (final or SWA pretrained weights, then the fine-tune read out as in the lines above).

  • The gap from one network to five is small. From S0f to Pool5, the gap is 0.082 points at the eight and 0.073 at the six (0.119 and 0.036 on cold nights). The plan required a gap above 0.15 points before a closure share could be tested. Every gap here is below that, so the closure shares are reported without a test.

  • Weight averaging gains 0.002 to 0.016 points at the eight and the six. EMA minus S0f: -0.002 at the eight (Bonferroni interval -0.015 to +0.011) and -0.016 at the six (-0.033 to -0.002). SWA minus S0f: -0.005 (-0.009 to -0.001) and -0.008 (-0.013 to -0.004). The closure shares of the gap to Pool5 are 2% (EMA) and 6% (SWA) at the eight, and 22% and 12% at the six. The 95% intervals of the EMA share run from -8% to 11% at the eight and 10% to 36% at the six.
  • Averaged networks stay far from the pool. EMA minus Pool5 is +0.080 at the eight (+0.063 to +0.099) and +0.057 at the six (+0.036 to +0.078). SWA minus Pool5 is +0.077 and +0.064. The differences from Pool5 are within the minimum detectable effect at the eight (0.083). The plan's condition that the gap exceed 0.15 points fails. The plan's recommendation rule is therefore not met.
  • Two seeds do what weight averaging cannot. Pool2 (three pairs of seeds) closes 59% of the gap at the eight and 71% at the six. A pool of three EMA networks closes 79% and 99%, and a pool of three SWA networks 86% and 91%. A pool of three plain networks (Pool3) scores 4.697 at the eight and 3.457 at the six.
  • Weight averaging helps slightly on cold nights. EMA minus S0f on cold nights at the eight is -0.024 (-0.057 to +0.006), and SWA minus S0f is -0.014 (-0.021 to -0.008). Both are within the cold-night minimum detectable effect (0.169).
  • SWA worsens the six's real-event rows. SWA minus S0f is +0.023 on those rows (+0.012 to +0.036). EMA minus S0f is -0.008 (-0.050 to +0.033). The scorer printed no minimum detectable effect for the real-event rows.
  • The q99 rule holds. EMA, SWA, and S0f differ by at most 0.005 points of q99 pinball loss at the eight and the six (EMA is 0.004 better than S0f at the six). The averaged networks are 0.006 to 0.010 above Pool5 (rule: at most 0.02). Coverage at q99 is 0.991 (EMA) and 0.990 (SWA) at the eight, against 0.992 for Pool5, and 0.985 and 0.983 at the six against 0.985.
  • The best widening is 1.05 at the eight and 1.05 to 1.10 at the six for every arm, including S0 and Pool5, with differences of at most 0.004 points from the 1.15 headline, so averaging seeds or weights does not change the widening.
  • The fixed budget scores about the same as early stopping. S0f minus S0 is -0.002 at the eight, +0.007 at the six (+0.004 to +0.010), and -0.11 on real-event rows at the six (-0.14 to -0.08).
  • SWA in pretraining (2026-01 only, three seeds, descriptive) does not help at the eight and helps at the six. At the eight: S0f 4.552, P0f 4.557, Pswa 4.560, Pswa+EMA 4.586, Pswa+SWA 4.564, Pool5 4.492. At the six: S0f 3.932, P0f 3.891, Pswa 3.866, Pswa+EMA 3.818, Pswa+SWA 3.857, Pool5 3.889. At the six, Pswa scores 0.025 below P0f and Pswa+EMA 0.073 below P0f, and Pswa+EMA scores below Pool5. This is one fold and the differences are below the six's minimum detectable effect.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost is the one metric where EMA looks as good as the pool, within wide intervals. At f = 0.75 at the signed-MW six on rows with no labelled event, over the 5 months, the cost in millions of pounds is 7.36 for S0f, 6.80 for EMA, 7.18 for SWA, 7.16 for Pool2, 7.05 for Pool5, 6.52 for the pool of three EMA networks, and 12.88 for the manual heuristic. EMA minus S0f is -0.56 (95% interval -1.52 to -0.01), EMA minus Pool5 is -0.25 (-1.00 to +0.19), and SWA minus Pool5 is +0.14 (-0.01 to +0.28). At f = 0.9 the EMA minus S0f difference is -0.12 (-0.33 to +0.00), and at f = 0.5 it is -0.95 (-2.47 to -0.05). SWA is not as good as the pool at f = 0.5: SWA minus Pool5 is +0.66 (+0.32 to +1.00).
  • The curtailment ranking of EMA above Pool5 is within noise. The intervals of EMA minus Pool5 include zero, and the cell bootstrap treats each month and Primary as independent. The curtailment-cost contrasts are descriptive and uncounted.
  • A fine-tune takes a median of 104 s on a loaded workstation, and all four networks of a run come from that one fit. A pretraining takes about 40 s. S0f, EMA, and SWA each serve one network per pass and need one fit per monthly refit. Pool5 serves five networks and five fits. Serving latency was not measured.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (EMA or SWA closes at least 40% of the gap at the eight): not supported. The shares are 2% and 6%. The P1 test is inconclusive because the gap is below 0.15 points.
  • P2 (EMA lowers the held-out-week loss in at least 12 of 15 fits): refuted. EMA is lower in 7 of 15. The range of EMA minus raw weights is -0.009 to +0.004.
  • P3 (the closure share is under 20%): supported at the eight (2% and 6%), not supported at the six for EMA, because the point estimate of 22% exceeds 20%, although its interval (10% to 36%) reaches below.
  • P4 (SWA in pretraining closes more of the gap than fine-tune averaging alone): not supported at the eight, and descriptively supported at the six (Pswa+EMA 3.818 against 3.865 for EMA alone).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Both fine-tune loops reproduce experiment 425's stored validation loss. The loop that stops at the best epoch and the loop that averages weights each give 0.36901423 for 2026-01, seed 0 (epoch 4 of 10).
  • The fine-tune budget is 4 epochs, not the 10 planned. The stored fine-tune lengths (median 10 epochs) include 6 patience epochs, so the median best epoch is 4.
  • None of the seven audit triggers fired. No control failed, and the results agree with experiment 481 (a second seed gives the largest gain among the seed counts it scored).
  • The median forecast against the mean forecast was not computed. The contrasts here are quantile-score contrasts only.
  • Five months, shared pretrained networks, and descriptive curtailment arms limit these results. One pretrained network per seed is shared by S0f, EMA, and SWA, so their scores are correlated. Pool2 is the quantile mean of seeds (0,1), (0,2), and (1,2).

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: The plan was followed, with two deviations. The fine-tune budget is 4 epochs, and the EMA99 arm and the P0f pretraining control were added.

docs.title: Can two constants per metering group replace table P for the first-release demand candidates?
docs.text:
Two constants recalibrate the demand forecast as well as table P does at the eight Primaries whose series are in megavolt-amperes (MVA) only, but not at the six whose series are in signed megawatts (MW). A Primary is a primary substation. Table P is the recalibration from experiment 483. It holds 20 widening factors per metering group (the eight, the six, or the two short-history Primaries), one for each of 5 lead bands (ranges of hours ahead) and 4 tail quantiles (q01, q05, q95, and q99, the 1%, 5%, 95%, and 99% points of the forecast distribution). At the eight, the first-release demand forecasts (A-pool, five seeds of one neural network averaged, and A-gam-in, the same network with an additive-model input) have upper quantiles that sit too close to the median and lower quantiles that are already in range. At the six, the lower quantiles sit too far below the median as well. This experiment asked whether one lower constant (scaling q01 and q05) and one upper constant (scaling q95 and q99) per metering group can replace the table. Each constant was fitted on earlier months only and compared with table P on the same held-out forecast rows. At the eight the constants match table P. At the six, q95 coverage (the share of actuals at or below q95) is 0.011 to 0.013 lower than with table P. Wind and solar were not tested, because their stored forecasts sit in other experiments' folders; this experiment covered demand only.

Figure 1 shows the coverage of the two-constant rule minus table P's, with 99.8% Bonferroni intervals (24 tests), against the 0.01 limit (green band). The fit uses earlier folds only.

Figure 2 shows the same difference in pinball loss as a share of table P's, against the 5% limit.

The tables use clean rows and four scored folds (2025-12 to 2026-06), fitted on earlier folds only. A fold is one test month of origin times.

The difference from table P is -0.011 (interval -0.013 to -0.009) for A-pool and -0.013 (-0.015 to -0.011) for A-gam-in, against a limit of 0.01. Pinball loss is within 5% (q99 is 2.1% better than table P), and CRPS is 0.003 points worse (0.002 to 0.004). Two-constant q95 coverage is 0.916 against the 0.93 floor; table P is also below it, at 0.927.
  • Fitted constants: the lower factor is 0.95 to 0.98 at the eight (so the lower tail is left almost untouched), 0.77 to 0.88 at the six. The upper factor is 1.10 to 1.24 at the eight and 1.03 to 1.26 at the six, and the upper factor varies by fold.

The other coverage and pinball limits at the eight hold; the six fails q95 coverage as above (-0.013).
  • Lead times of 12 to 36 hours (not a gating slice): the constants do worse here than over all leads, in both directions. At the eight A-pool's q95 coverage is 0.958 with the constants against 0.946 with table P (+0.012, interval +0.008 to +0.017), and q05 is 0.033 against 0.051 (-0.018, interval -0.023 to -0.014), both outside the 0.01 limit. At the six q95 is 0.922 against 0.938 (-0.017). One pair of constants per metering group does not match table P's lead-band factors within this band.
  • Cold winter nights: at the eight A-pool's q95 coverage is 0.930 (constants) and 0.929 (table P), against 0.874 raw. A-gam-in's is 0.927 and 0.926. At the six it is 0.867 and 0.879, against 0.835 raw. Cold nights stay under-covered under both rules.
  • Serving table. Table P: 20 factors per metering group, a lead-band lookup, and a clip rule. Two constants: two numbers per metering group, refitted on the earlier months at training time. No other part of the serving path changes. The eight can use the constants; the six keeps table P.
  • Not tested: wind and solar. Experiment 481 found a constant widening of 1.10 best for wind at every number of seeds, which suggests the rule may fit wind, but the stored forecasts of experiments 429, 430, 450, and 461 have not been re-scored. This is a named gap.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Arms and rule. A-pool, A-gam-in (the eight only), and K2-425A (report-only) from experiment 483's cache. The lower factor scales the distance of q01 and q05 from the median and the upper factor scales q95 and q99. Each is the 0.50 to 1.80 grid value (step 0.01) that minimises the summed pinball loss of its two quantiles on the fitting rows, per metering group.
  • Fits. Earlier-folds-only (each scored fold is fitted on the folds before it; 2025-10 is never scored) is the planning figure. Leave-one-fold-out is the comparison with experiment 483. Table P is fitted on the same rows as the constants, with its own rule (it skips cells with fewer than 200 rows or a spread under 1e-6, which fall back to a factor of 1).
  • Rows and cleaning. The gam14 row set of experiment 470, clean rows (those with no labelled event), flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped and the experiment 399 start cut for D15 and D18, both inherited from experiment 483's cache. July 2026 is unused. Stored forecasts come from monthly refits; nothing is refitted.
  • Intervals. Paired row-level differences, resampled in blocks of one origin day within a month (20,000 resamples). The Bonferroni count is 24 (four tail quantiles, coverage and pinball loss, for A-pool at the eight, A-pool at the six, and A-gam-in at the eight; the A-gam-in six, K2-425A, cold-night, and 12 to 36 hour intervals use the same level but are not counted). The equivalence limits (0.01 of coverage, 5% of pinball loss) sit at or below experiment 483's minimum detectable effects at the six (q95 coverage 0.014), so a result inside the limits whose interval crosses one is inconclusive, and a claim of equivalence cannot show a smaller difference than the minimum detectable effect.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00492-*/e00492_two_constant.py and e00492_report.py; the scoring reuses e00470_score.row_metrics and experiment 483's e00483_tails and experiment 435's e00435_table_p_provisional. Tables are under data/ml-experiments/00492-*/work/.

docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not available, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Mean or median error beside the contrast: not computed; the contrast is a calibration difference between two recalibrations of the same median, so the median is unchanged.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. The prediction missed in one respect (the six fails on q95 coverage, not on the q05 and q99 pinball clauses the plan named).
  • Reviews: the code review, the numbers review, and the prose review are recorded in the PR body.
  • Prediction outcome: P1 held (earlier-folds-only). P2 held in direction (the six fails) but for q95 coverage. P3 held (upper factor 1.10 to 1.24, lower factor 0.95 to 0.98 at the eight). P4 held at the six and is marginal at the eight (0.926 to 0.930 under both rules, against a floor of 0.93).

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Caveats: five non-contiguous folds are few, and the earlier-folds-only comparison scores four. Every score is selection-biased, because the same folds choose the candidates and score them. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events. No time series plots of forecasts are drawn, because the forecasts are experiment 483's and this experiment changes only the tail widths; those plots are on the experiment 483 page.
  • Next steps: re-score wind and solar with the same rule from the stored forecasts of experiments 429, 430, 450, and 461. For the six, a lead-band-specific upper factor is untested.

docs.title: Can the pooled solar network for the six metered farms be refitted once a year instead of every quarter without losing more than 1% of its quantile score?
docs.text:
Refitting the solar neural network once a year scores within 1% of refitting it every quarter, for both neural networks we tested, so the first production solar forecast needs one refit a year instead of four. The score is the quantile score, a pinball loss averaged over 11 quantile levels (lower is better). One further comparison fails. At Solar E, the neural network that reads only the mean and spread of the ensemble weather forecast ("one pass") with annual refits scores 1.3% worse than the neural network that reads all 51 ensemble members ("the encoder") with quarterly refits. Most of that gap comes from the network design and not from the refit schedule, because the one-pass network with quarterly refits is already 1.0% worse than the encoder at Solar E.

We asked whether the pooled neural network for the six metered solar farms (Solar A to F, metered by National Grid Electricity Distribution) can be refitted once, on data to 31 August 2025, and then forecast all 12 scored months, instead of being refitted every quarter. A 51-member ensemble weather forecast drives each network. Experiment 430 built both networks and refitted them quarterly; we refitted each of them once, with six random initialisations (seeds), and compared the forecasts with experiment 430's stored quarterly forecasts. Experiment 430 also found that the one-pass network scores 6.842 against 6.810 for the encoder over all bands (three seeds; 0.18% at six seeds), so we quote that result and did not rerun it.

Both annual-refit schedules passed the pre-registered 1% limit. Scores are quantile scores in percentage points of installed capacity, farm-equal means over experiment 310's scored year. We resample whole months 10,000 times, and each interval covers 98.33% so that the three contrasts together have a 5% error rate. The minimum detectable effect from the seed spread is 0.58% for the annual one-pass network, 0.28% for the quarterly one-pass network, 0.38% for the annual encoder, and 0.58% for the quarterly encoder, so the 1% limit lies above all four. The margin is small for the encoder: a later check (Audit, below) estimates that adding seed noise to the interval lifts the upper end to about 0.88% for C2 and 0.95% for C3.

Contrast All bands 12 to 36 hour band Worst farm (all bands) Verdict C1: one pass, annual against quarterly −0.07% (−0.48% to +0.23%) +0.40% (−0.04% to +0.98%) Solar E +0.31% (−0.30% to +0.86%) equivalent C2: encoder, annual against quarterly +0.21% (−0.06% to +0.51%) +0.39% (+0.02% to +0.87%) Solar E +0.53% (+0.08% to +1.09%) equivalent C3: one pass annual against encoder quarterly (baseline) +0.11% (−0.43% to +0.57%) +0.37% (−0.14% to +0.94%) Solar E +1.28% (+0.46% to +2.02%) not equivalent: Solar E exceeds +1%

Figure 1. Percentage change in quantile score of the annual-refit network against its reference, with 98.33% month-block intervals, over all bands and in the 12 to 36 hour band. Negative is better. The dashed lines mark 0 and the 1% limit.

Figure 2. The same contrasts for each farm, all bands.

Figure 3. The same contrasts by months since the 2025-09 refit, grouping runs by their init month. The first group is zero by construction, because the annual and quarterly fits are the same fits. Each interval resamples the 3 to 4 valid-time months that the group's forecasts fall in, so it is descriptive.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute scores (all bands, six seeds). Annual one pass 6.825, quarterly one pass 6.830, annual encoder 6.832, quarterly encoder (the baseline) 6.818.
  • The loss does not grow with the age of the network. The annual schedule scores +0.53% and +0.45% against the quarterly schedule in months 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 for the one-pass network, +0.59% and +0.60% for the encoder, and −0.60% and −0.31% in months 9 to 12 (annual better).
  • The predicted growth through the year did not appear. One refit date and one year cannot separate the season from the age of the network.
  • C3 exceeds 1% in months 6 to 9 (+1.12%), which mixes the schedule and the network design. The per-quarter intervals are too narrow (Audit), so we do not read them.
  • The 12 to 36 hour band loses a little more. The loss is +0.4% for both networks, inside the limit, with the C2 interval just above zero (+0.02% to +0.87%).
  • Control passed. On the first three init months the annual and quarterly forecasts agree to below 1e-5% for both networks (largest row difference 1.2e-5 points), as the same fit and seed give.
  • Prediction against result. C1 was predicted at +0.3% and came out −0.07%, inside the interval the prediction stated. C2 was predicted at +0.3% and came out +0.21%. C3 was predicted at +0.5% with the upper end below +1.5%, and came out +0.11% with an upper end of +0.57%. The prediction that the last quarter alone may exceed 1% did not hold.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Averaged over all rows, the median forecast minus the mean forecast is −0.035 points of capacity for the annual one pass, −0.072 for the quarterly one pass, +0.022 for the annual encoder, and −0.116 for the quarterly encoder (Tails table), so no arm's median differs from its mean by more than 0.12 points.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts. The mean absolute error of the mean forecast favours the annual schedule in all three contrasts: −0.41% for C1 (−0.91% to −0.05%), −0.08% for C2 (−0.40% to +0.26%), and −0.22% for C3 (−0.88% to +0.41%). The quantile score favours it for C1 only. The gaps are 0.4 to 1.2 times the seed-resampling standard deviation of the contrast (0.18 to 0.35 percentage points), so we read them as noise.
  • Triggers fired. Of the seven audit triggers in the ml-experiment skill, trigger 3 fired for C1 and C2 (the mean-forecast error and the quantile score point in different directions, by an amount inside seed noise), and trigger 4 fired for C1 (omitting Solar D flips the sign, from −0.07% to +0.03%) and C3 (omitting Solar E flips the sign, from +0.11% to −0.15%). A fresh Sonnet agent audited the result (below). Triggers 1, 2, 5, and 6 did not fire, and trigger 7 does not apply.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the contrasts with its own code and tried to break them.

  • Re-derivation: the three all-band point estimates and the per-farm estimates match the printed values to three decimals, and the intervals agree to 0.01 percentage points. Accepted, no change.
  • Control: for each of the six seeds and both networks, annual and quarterly forecasts agree to 3.3e-6 in every quantile on the first three init months. They first differ in the init month 2025-12, as expected. Accepted.
  • Rows: all four arms hold 410,899 rows per seed, with identical keys and actuals. No leakage, misalignment, or dropped rows. Accepted.
  • Leave-one-farm-out: the sign flips for C1 (omit Solar D) and C3 (omit Solar E), and both contrasts sit within ±0.3% of zero, so the flips are immaterial. The interval part of the verdict never changes (largest upper ends: +0.33%, +0.57%, +0.69%). C3 becomes equivalent without Solar E, so its verdict rests on that one farm. Accepted, stated in the opening.
  • Seed noise in the interval: the month-block interval treats the six-seed averages as fixed. The audit adds seed noise in quadrature and estimates the upper ends at about 0.57% for C1, 0.88% for C2, and 0.95% for C3. Accepted: the equivalence of C2 and C3 has little margin below the 1% limit, and the page says so.
  • Per-quarter intervals: a cut of 3 or 4 valid-time months allows only 10 to 35 distinct resamples, so the intervals are too narrow and uncorrected. Accepted: Figure 3 is descriptive.
  • Staleness prediction: the last group is better for the annual schedule, so the predicted growth of the loss through the year did not appear. Accepted.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One scored year, one refit date. Both schedules share the training end of 2025-08-31, so the result is for one year of staleness starting in September. A refit date in another month could differ.
  • The quarterly references come from experiment 430's run, on a different day. The control shows that the same configuration and seed give the same forecast on the first quarter, so the stored references are consistent with a refit of that configuration.
  • Solar E under the encoder. The farm rule reads point estimates, and the Solar E interval for C2 reaches +1.09%, so one farm is not shown to stay within 1%.
  • Solar E. The comparison of the one-pass network with the encoder at Solar E (C3) is dominated by the network design, as experiment 430's leave-one-farm-out check found.
  • Own history only, no recalibration table. The networks train on each farm's own record and the forecasts carry no post-hoc widening factor (table P in the serving path).
  • Seed noise. The month-block intervals leave out seed noise, and the minimum detectable effects cover seed noise only.

docs.title: Design
docs.text: See the plan in the opening commit of this pull request: two arms (annual_g0_onepass, annual_a2_member) from experiment 430's g0_onepass and a2_member configurations with one refit at 2025-09 that predicts the runs of all 12 months, six seeds, scored against experiment 430's quarterly forecasts. Code reuse: this folder imports the modules of experiments 310 and 430 (ml-experiments/00310-metered-farm-long-lead-scoring/ and ml-experiments/00430-unified-forecaster-solar-and-pretraining-ablations/). Fitted networks are in the private data folder.

docs.title: Can the Primary demand network be refitted less often, or pretrained once and only fine-tuned at each refit, without losing forecast skill?
docs.text:
In five scored months, pretraining the demand neural network once and fine-tuning it each month scored within 0.03 points of pretraining it at every refit (a lower score is better), and would save about 42 of the 80 GPU seconds that refitting one network takes (46 per refit, less the one yearly pretraining). A network refitted 3 months earlier scored about 0.07 points worse than a freshly refitted one at the eight Primary substations that report only apparent power, and five months are too few to say how much worse. Whether to refit less often than monthly is therefore open until a larger test.

We asked whether the neural network that forecasts demand at 16 Primary substations could be simplified. A refit has two stages: pretraining on estimates of past weather (ERA5 and CAMS), then fine-tuning on archived ECMWF ensemble (ENS) forecasts. One change was to refit every 3 or 6 months instead of every month. The other was to pretrain once and fine-tune each month. We scored three arms against the average of two neural networks (trained from different random seeds, each refitted in the scored month; experiment 425's arm A). All four were scored on the same half-hours of the same five months. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in points of effective capacity, a percentage of each Primary's capacity. The 16 Primaries are 8 that report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA), called "the eight"; 6 that report signed megawatts, called "the six"; and D15 and D18, which are reported separately.

Arm What it is K2 The fresh pool: two neural networks, each pretrained and fine-tuned in the scored month. Stale3, Stale6 Two networks refitted 3 or 6 months before the scored month. PretrainOnce Two networks fine-tuned each month from pretraining done once, with data to 2025-07.

Verdict: partly supported. In these five months, PretrainOnce is equivalent to K2 at both groups, meaning its upper Bonferroni bound lies inside the limit of 0.086 points at the eight and 0.170 at the six. Stale3 and Stale6 are equivalent at the six but not shown equivalent at the eight.

docs.text:

Stale11 is the single fold 2026-06 from the 2025-07 networks. Experiment 489's 5-seed values (0.065 and 0.100) do not apply to a 2-seed pool. Limits: 0.086 for Stale3 and PO at the eight, 0.100 for Stale6, 0.170 at the six; q99 pinball loss 0.02. Stale3: 3 refits per year if the 4-month cadence's worst month held, +0.067 and +0.022 points.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary. K2 has a median below the mean at 15 of 16 Primaries (the two largest gaps are -2.4 and -1.7 points of capacity) and PO at all 16 (-2.6 and -2.1); PO's values differ from K2's by under 0.5 points.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrast. Mean absolute error of the median forecast at the eight: K2 6.777, Stale3 6.885, Stale6 6.892, PO 6.724 points; at the six: 5.652, 5.710, 5.678, and 5.662. The directions agree with the CRPS contrasts except for PO at the six (CRPS -0.002, median error +0.009), a gap too small to fire trigger 3.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 (the 3-month network missed the prediction of 0.05 at the eight) was tested: the loss does not follow the length of the ENS fine-tuning window (15 to 23 months), and the stale-network loader reproduces experiment 425's stored forecasts exactly (a maximum difference of 0.0 in all 10 files). Trigger 4: dropping 2025-12 turns PO's -0.030 into -0.008, which leaves the equivalence verdict unchanged, so trigger 4 did not fire. No audit was run. A Sonnet results review re-derived every contrast from the stored row tables and agreed with them.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Five folds, each from one pair of networks, give wide intervals across folds; the origin-day interval treats each fitted network as fixed, so that interval is optimistic. Read the interval across folds for cadence.
  • Stale3 and Stale6 differ from K2 in age and in the length of the ENS history they trained on (12 to 23 months, against 24 for K2), and the two Stale6 refits at 2025-04 and 2025-06 were fitted here with 12 and 14 months. Stale12 could not be run because refits before 2025-04 have under 12 months of ENS history.
  • PO also reuses the 2025-07 pretraining's target statistics and ENS-spread table, which the fine-tuning replaces with each month's.
  • Stale3 measures the worst month of a 4-month cadence, not its average.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete: "rows with no labelled event" may hold unlabelled events. Every score is selection-biased, and July 2026 is unused.
  • Reviews: one Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review before the first fit, one Sonnet results review, and two Sonnet write-up reviews.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
