  • Port pretrain-once into the demand recipe, then re-check weekly before any release claim.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Production refits the demand network every month, pretraining on ERA5-and-CAMS rows and then fine-tuning on ENS rows. Fewer fits per year and no pretraining at each refit would simplify serving and training. This experiment ages the network on purpose, and also fine-tunes from one pretraining run reused at every refit. The baseline is experiment 425's arm A with 2 seeds.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Rows and folds. The 5 folds of experiment 449 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) on the rows of experiment 470 (experiment_470_intersection_v1). The D15 and D18 start cut and the flagged exact-zero drop apply. Cleaned data everywhere; monthly refits.
  • K2 (baseline). Quantile average of seeds 0 and 1 of arm A, stored in experiment 425 (work/seed_preds/A). The 1.15 widening is applied to every arm as in experiments 470 and 489.
  • Stale3, Stale6 (cadence). For scored month M, forecast with the arm A networks (seeds 0 and 1) that were pretrained and fine-tuned at refit R = M minus 3 (or 6) months. The network's own standardiser and target statistics are used. No retraining: the networks are experiment 425's stored work/models/A/<R>/s<seed>. The arm is named by the network's age at the start of the scored month. A network that old is also about one month older by the month's end, so Stale3 is the worst month of a 4-month cadence and Stale6 of a 7-month cadence: a conservative reading, and the page says it that way. The test covers the worst month of a cadence, not its average.
    • Stale3 needs R in 2025-07, 2025-09, 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-03: all stored, so no fits.
    • Stale6 needs R in 2025-04, 2025-06, 2025-07, 2025-09, 2025-12. Experiment 425 stores only the last three, so the first two are fitted here: arm A, seeds 0 and 1, pretrain and fine-tune, with e00425_fit.run_arms unchanged. Their ENS fine-tuning windows hold 12 and 14 months, not 24, because the ENS history starts in 2024-04 (so every stale network also has a shorter ENS window than K2: 15 to 23 months at the stored cuts; the page prints the window per fold and reads age and window length as confounded); the plan reads Stale6 on all 5 folds and on the 3 folds with stored networks.
    • Stale12 cannot be run: refits before 2025-04 would have under 12 months of ENS history. The single fold 2026-06 from the stored 2025-07 networks (Stale11) is reported as descriptive.
  • PretrainOnce. Each of the 5 scored months is fine-tuned from the pretrained arm A network of the first stored cut (2025-07) of the same seed, instead of the network pretrained at that month's cut. Fine-tuning is experiment 425's (learning rate 2e-4, same rows, same loop, seeds 0 and 1). The fold's standardiser is the scored month's own, so the fine-tuning sees an input scale that differs slightly from the pretraining's. The pretraining also used the 2025-07 fold's target mean and standard deviation per Primary and its median ENS spread by lead band, which the fine-tuning replaces with the scored month's. All three mismatches are part of what the arm tests, because a production refit would also fine-tune with its own statistics. Ten fine-tunes; no pretraining.
  • Caveats named in advance. D15 and D18 are uninterpretable for the stale arms (Stale6 at the 2025-04 cut has about 1 month of their rows after the start cut), and are report-only. Each network's recency weight is relative to its own refit, which is part of staleness. The origin-day block bootstrap ignores dependence across days of one fold, so intervals are optimistic for every arm alike.
  • Not run. A cadence on the fine-tune alone with fresh pretraining (a pure fine-tune staleness arm): the question the brief asked, but it needs a pretraining cut at each scored month paired with a fine-tune R months earlier, and production would pretrain once, which PretrainOnce covers.

docs.title: Scoring and stop rules
docs.text:
• Experiment 489's scorer pattern: the experiment 470 scorer, tail script, and curtailment script pointed at this folder. Because Stale6 and Stale11 cover fewer folds, each arm is scored in its own call against K2 on the folds the arm has.
  • The scorer prints the MDE before any contrast (experiment 428's definition from the seed spread of arm A, as in experiment 489). Experiment 481 uses another definition; the page reports both.
  • Report per arm: CRPS at the eight, the signed-MW six, cold winter nights, the 12 to 36 hour band; q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage and pinball loss; avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, 0.5 at the six. Christmas week and D15 and D18 are report-only.
  • Stop. Do not run Stale6's two new fits if Stale3 already fails its limit at either group.
  • Serving table (required). Networks per serving pass, refits per year, pretrainings per year, GPU seconds per refit (experiment 481: about 80 per seed, 46 pretraining and 34 fine-tuning), and the change in CRPS against K2.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text: • Stale3: 0 fits, 10 month-forecast passes. Stale6: 4 networks (2 cuts x 2 seeds), about 5 GPU minutes, plus passes. PretrainOnce: 10 fine-tunes, about 6 GPU minutes. One GPU process under 8 GB; one feeder core.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Monthly refits; cleaned data; D15 and D18 cut; saved networks; stored forecasts reused; tails and cost; example forecasts and the 14-day plot; the process order of the ml-experiment skill. Not applicable: load-shift event plots (no event slice is headline).

docs.title: Series
docs.text: Step 3 of the neural simplification series (brief of 2026-11-01); step 6 shares this pull request. Steps 1 and 4 run in other pull requests.

docs.title: Does training the lagged network a second time on the injected rows where it follows an event in its lags lower how far its median follows a step in its lags?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The lagless forecast on this page, including the lagless half of B-mix and K2-S1, comes from experiment 404's table, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead. Above 24 h of lead B-mix's lead over the lagged network is partly the look-ahead. Contrasts between variants of the lagged network are unaffected. Scores at 0 to 24 h are unchanged. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532. Retraining the lagged neural network on its own worst rows lowered the share of a step in its readings that reaches its median forecast by only 0.021, and made its score on rows with no labelled event worse, which puts it on the trade-off that experiment 486 found between following a step and scoring those rows. We asked whether a neural network that forecasts a Primary substation's power from its recent readings (its 3 lags: the newest usable reading, the reading at the same time on an earlier day, and the reading at the same time and weekday on an earlier week) can be taught to trust a sudden step in those readings less. We trained it on a copy of the training data into which artificial load-shift events had been inserted, for 3 epochs. We then scored every training row, marked as hard the 20% of rows with the highest pinball loss (a quantile-forecast error score) in their class, plus the rows where its median followed the inserted step, and trained 3 more epochs with each hard row shown 3 times (arm HN, for hard-negative mining). We then added a step of 5% of the Primary's capacity to all 3 lags (the scoring step) and measured the share of that step that appeared in the median forecast (the follow share): 0.079 for HN, meaning 7.9% of the step, and 0.100 for the same network trained on the injected events without mining (arm A0-inj). HN scored 0.095 percentage points of the Primary's capacity worse than A0-inj on the mean continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), on rows outside every event that National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), the distribution network operator, has labelled. We call those the rows with no labelled event.

Verdict: not supported. The prediction was a drop of at least 0.05 in the follow share, and the drop is 0.021 (lower in 4 of the 5 months: 0.007, -0.002, 0.033, 0.043, and 0.024 for 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06). The pass bar set in the experiment brief was a follow share of at most 0.10 together with a loss of under 0.05 points on rows with no labelled event; the first part holds and the second does not. The stop rule fires: the point (0.079, +0.095) sits 0.035 above the piecewise-linear curve of experiment 486 through R05, A0-inj, and R50 (the curve gives +0.060 at 0.079), inside the 0.061 clean-row bar (experiment 439's). This stop rule is weak, because its 0.061 tolerance is wider than HN's whole move in follow share, so even a network identical to A0-inj would sit on the curve. The result therefore says that HN cannot be told apart from the curve, and closes only the two regimes tested: the share of injected rows and this one mining rule. HN is 0.445 points of capacity behind B-mix on rows with no labelled event, as the plan expected.

All numbers are interim and have four limits. They come from five months and one to three seeds (seven cells, so 2026-06 counts three times in the absolute scores and the curtailment sums), and the intervals are unadjusted for the four contrasts. The mining pass mostly retrained on ordinary high-loss rows, and no control oversamples a random 20% of rows, so selection and extra exposure are confounded. NGED's logs may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may hold events.

Terms. A hard row is a training row marked by the mining pass. Harm rows, injected harm rows (the three injected scoring datasets, worlds w200 to w202), the signed-MW six (the six Primaries that report signed power), the MVA-only eight (the eight that report apparent power only), B-mix, and the minimum detectable effect are as in experiment 486. Points of capacity are CRPS from 11 quantiles as a percentage of the Primary's capacity, and B-mix is the 50/50 mixture of the stored A0-inj forecast and the forecast built without any lag. A cell is one scored month with one seed; there are 7. The event step used by the mining pass is the mean over the 3 lags of the injected minus the clean reading, and differs from the scoring step.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Mining. Of the 3,860,882 training rows at 2026-06 seed 0, 21.1% are hard (813,673). The loss rule marks 20.0% by construction in each class and the follow rule marks 90,839 rows (2.4%, or about 7% of the rows with a corrupted lag); across the 7 cells the hard share is 20.5% to 21.3% and the follow rule marks 1.5% to 2.5%. Among rows with a lag inside an injected event 23.2% are hard, against 20.0% of the other rows, so about 70% of the hard rows have no corrupted lag and the pass mostly marks ordinary high-loss rows. Each fit took 59 to 82 seconds on the GPU, about 0.14 GPU-hours for the 7 cells.
  • Minimum detectable effect (2.8 standard deviations of the seed spread at 2026-06, seeds 0 to 2, signed-MW six): A0-inj 0.144 on rows with no labelled event and 0.155 on injected harm rows; B-mix 0.050 and 0.070; HN 0.088 and 0.106. Experiment 404's month-to-month spread (0.3 to 1.0 points) is larger, and experiment 439's clean-row bar is 0.061.
  • Contrasts at the signed-MW six (points of capacity, lower is better; unadjusted 95% intervals from resampling months; the number after each interval counts the cells, out of 7, where HN beats the reference). The pre-registered Bonferroni level for k = 4 is 98.75%, which gives intervals wider than the 95% ones shown. The absolute scores are means over the 7 cells; the contrasts are means of month means (seeds within a month averaged first), so a contrast need not equal the difference of two absolutes.
Rows HN absolute Minus A0-inj Minus B-mix No labelled event (A0-inj 3.698, B-mix 3.371) 3.794 +0.095 (-0.012 to 0.224), 1 +0.445 (0.308 to 0.649), 0 Injected harm rows (A0-inj 4.019, B-mix 3.664) 4.119 +0.116 (0.036 to 0.242), 0 +0.481 (0.378 to 0.623), 0
  • P1 fails. At 3 lags and leads under 48 hours HN follows 0.079 of the step against 0.100 (a drop of 0.021, not the 0.05 predicted; lowest to highest month 0.055 to 0.104 against 0.084 to 0.128). At leads of 48 to 120 hours HN follows 0.073 against 0.091.
  • P2 holds as an equivalence check only. HN is 0.116 worse than A0-inj on injected harm rows, inside the 0.155 minimum detectable effect of A0-inj (HN's own is 0.106). The unadjusted interval excludes zero, which is not the registered test, so the cost is reported but not claimed.
  • P3 holds. HN does not beat B-mix on either row class.
  • Mixture (descriptive, not in k). Mixed with the lagless table, HN scores 3.385 on rows with no labelled event (+0.005 against B-mix, -0.034 to 0.045) and 3.684 on injected harm rows (+0.017, -0.030 to 0.065). Mining therefore changes the mixture by less than the minimum detectable effect.
  • MVA-only eight (descriptive). HN minus A0-inj is +0.224 on rows with no labelled event (0.114 to 0.322) and +0.271 on injected harm rows (0.165 to 0.362); HN minus B-mix is +0.649 and +0.790.
  • Sweep. Median shift as a share of a 5% step, leads under 48 hours (mean of the months), A0-inj then HN: 1 lag 0.021 and 0.018; 2 lags 0.062 and 0.050; 3 lags 0.100 and 0.079. The band-width ratio is in work/sweep/.
  • Bad-data injections (median shift as a share of the corruption, mean of 5 months), A0-inj then HN. A stuck reading for 24 hours: 0.056 and 0.045. A dropout to zero for 6 hours: 0.024 and 0.018. A spike of 4 times the week-on-week change: 0.024 and 0.020. A spike of 20 times: 0.004 and 0.001.
  • Tails (signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event, raw quantiles; coverage of q01, q05, q95, and q99, then q99 pinball loss in points of capacity). A0-inj: 0.011, 0.043, 0.813, 0.915; 0.349. B-mix: 0.005, 0.025, 0.856, 0.950; 0.259. HN: 0.006, 0.029, 0.846, 0.932; 0.317. HN+lagless: 0.003, 0.019, 0.877, 0.958; 0.246. HN is 0.058 above B-mix on q99 pinball loss, beyond the +0.02 limit, and 0.032 below A0-inj. HN+lagless is 0.013 below B-mix. On injected harm rows the q99 pinball loss is 0.636 (A0-inj), 0.538 (B-mix), 0.607 (HN), and 0.526 (HN+lagless). The 12 to 36 hour band is in work/scores/tails.csv.
  • Avoidable curtailment (signed-MW six; million pounds summed over the cells of the five months; 95% interval resampling cells). HN minus A0-inj: +0.09 (-0.10 to 0.28) at f = 0.9, -0.11 (-1.66 to 1.25) at f = 0.75, and -0.30 (-2.58 to 1.72) at f = 0.5. HN+lagless minus B-mix: +0.09 (-0.02 to 0.25), +0.15 (-0.68 to 1.04), and +0.21 (-1.07 to 1.56). Every interval includes zero.
  • Serving cost. HN serves one neural network per forecast with no table, mixture, or detector, and mining adds training cost only. B-mix serves two networks, the cross-fitted lagless table, and a mixture step. Removing that complexity leaves HN 0.445 points behind B-mix on rows with no labelled event and 0.481 behind on injected harm rows.
  • What the regime would change for an operator. The network was shown its own worst mistakes about events and trained on them more. The network was retrained mostly on ordinary high-loss rows, followed a step in its last days of readings about a fifth less (0.079 against 0.100), and was a little less accurate on ordinary days. The regime needs no event labels.
  • Row counts (signed-MW six, summed over the 7 cells): 626,771 rows with no labelled event and 1,138,838 injected harm rows, as in experiment 486. Rows inside real events, after events, and cold nights were not scored separately.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, and the error of the mean forecast. Neither was computed: the stored forecasts hold 11 quantiles and not the mean of the mixture.
  • Audit triggers. No control failed, no nested arm beat the arm that contains it, and the headline intervals are of the same order as experiment 486's (0.236 wide for HN minus A0-inj on rows with no labelled event, against 0.214 for R50). No audit was run.
  • Caveats. The follow share uses the mean step over the 3 lags, so a row with only the oldest lag inside an event has a diluted step. HN has no control that oversamples a random 20% of rows, so a part of its effect may be the extra rows seen (about 40% more per mined epoch) and not their selection. Both caveats came out of the code review and are not tested here.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet code review before the first fit (findings: the step definition, the missing random-oversampling control, nanquantile for the class limits, and a stale example command; the last two were applied, the first two are the caveats above). The results, write-up, and prose reviews are listed in the pull request.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Do not mine on loss again. The loss rule picks 20% of rows in every class. A follow-share-only rule marks 1.5% to 2.5% of rows and targets events, but a rule marking so few rows is unlikely to move the trade-off. Any new mining run needs a control that oversamples a random 20% of rows.
  • Stored artefacts (not a next step). Fitted networks and epoch-3 checkpoints are in data/ml-experiments/00495-lagged-network-hard-negative-mining-on-injected-events/work/models/HN/, hard-row tables under work/hard/, forecasts under work/predictions/, and score tables under work/scores/.

docs.title: Plan (written before any score was read)
docs.text: The plan, written before any score was read. Experiment 486 showed that the share of training rows with a corrupted lag trades how far the lagged network's median follows a step in its lags against its score on ordinary rows. Hard-negative mining is the one regime of the injection family that experiment does not duplicate: it keeps the 28% share and changes which rows the last epochs see.

docs.title: Arm and mining rule
docs.text:
• HN. Experiment 404's A0-inj network (mixture density network, three origin lags, experiment 397's recency weights, monthly refit, the lagless table frozen) trained on the stored injected world of experiment 428 for 3 epochs. The epoch-3 checkpoint is saved. A mining pass scores every training row once. The last 3 epochs shuffle the training rows together with two extra copies of each hard row, so each hard row appears 3 times per epoch.
  • Hard row. (a) The row has a lag inside an injected event, its three lags differ from the clean readings by at least 0.5% of capacity on average (the step), and the median on the injected lags minus the median on the clean lags exceeds 0.25 of the step; or (b) its pinball loss against the clean target (mean of the 11 quantiles) exceeds the 80th percentile of its class (a lag inside an injected event, or none). The hard set is computed once.
  • Why 3 plus 3 epochs. The brief says 60% of 6 epochs (3.6) and an epoch-3 checkpoint; the checkpoint falls on a whole epoch, so the split is 3 plain epochs and 3 mined epochs. The first 3 epochs reproduce the stored A0-inj recipe, whose re-fit matched the stored scores to 1.4e-4 of capacity in experiment 486.
  • Dropped from the brief. Arms W3 and W3+HN (weight 3 on event rows), dropped by the load-shift Discuss session after experiment 486 (PR 148) showed that weight 3 on 20% event rows is about the effective share of R50. The earlier brief's conditional dependence on brief 1 is therefore gone.
  • Reproduction. Not refitted: experiment 486's A0-repro already matched the stored A0-inj to 1.4e-4 of capacity; HN's first 3 epochs use that recipe.

docs.title: Cells, row sets, and scoring
docs.text:
• Cells. Seven: five scored months at seed 0 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) and 2026-06 at seeds 1 and 2, as for experiments 404 and 486. Seven full refits. The scoring worlds w200 to w202 and the clean world w-1 are experiment 404's, unchanged.
  • Minimum detectable effect. Both sources, printed first: the seed spread of the stored A0-inj and B-mix at 2026-06 (seeds 0 to 2), and experiment 404's month-to-month spread (0.4 to 1.0 points on harm rows, 0.3 to 0.9 inside events, 0.3 to 0.8 on rows with no labelled event). Experiment 439's clean-row bar of 0.061 judges clean-row equivalence. Harm-row claims are judged on the injected harm rows; real harm rows and rows inside real events are descriptive.
  • Contrasts. The four of the decision rule, as month-block bootstraps with the sign count over the five months. The 50/50 mixture of HN with the lagless table, and the MVA-only eight, are descriptive and outside k.
  • Reported beside CRPS. q01, q05, q95, and q99 coverage and pinball loss (raw and after table P with the 1.15 widening, with the 12 to 36 hour band); the encroachment sweep of experiment 404 and the bad-data injections of experiment 465 (stuck 24 hours, dropout to zero 6 hours, spikes of 4 and 20 times) on HN, A0-inj, and B-mix; avoidable curtailment at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5; row counts per row class; a figure of the hard set by lead band and by event depth; the plots of the standing rules (a day-ahead and a 14-day forecast, and at least 6 real labelled events across both metering groups, with generators anonymised).
  • Serving cost. One network per pass, no table, mixture, or detector, and no change at serving from the mining pass (training only). B-mix serves two networks, a stored lagless table, and a mixture step. The write-up states the score gap to B-mix on rows with no labelled event and on injected harm rows as the price of removing that complexity.
  • Operator sentence. "The network was shown its own worst mistakes about events and trained on them more." The regime needs no event labels.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
• Fits. 7 fits at about 20 to 36 s plus one mining pass each (a forward pass over the training rows, minutes at most), about 0.1 GPU-hours. One GPU process under 8 GB and one feeder core. A fit starts only when free -g shows more than 20 GB available. The first fit is timed and the total reported to the manager before the rest.
  • Reused. The stored A0-inj and B-mix forecasts on all 7 cells, and experiment 486's results.
  • Scoring. Forecasts on w200 to w202 and w-1, the sweep, the corruption injections, curtailment, and the bootstrap dominate the wall time.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Monthly refits; cleaned data with flagged substation_zero half-hours dropped (the count per cell is printed with the scoring); the D15 and D18 start cut before 2025-03-01; fitted networks saved under this experiment's data folder; stored forecasts reused; tails and curtailment reported; the unlogged-event caveat stated: NGED's logs may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may hold events, the harm table is optimistic, and real-event slices undercount. Weather inputs are the ECMWF ENS mean and spread of experiment 404 (no past-weather lags enter the network, so the past-weather caveat does not apply).

docs.title: Reading earlier advice
docs.text: The plan follows experiment 486's advice to keep B-mix as the reference and not to tune the share of injected rows, and experiment 488's finding that real labelled events add nothing detectable beyond injected events. It departs from nothing. Experiment 484 weights hard rows in demand network fine-tuning, a different network and loss; it is cited as related work only.

docs.title: Can the demand neural network drop its ensemble-spread inputs, merge its holiday columns, drop its weekly lag, or use one Gaussian instead of three without losing forecast skill?
docs.text:
The demand neural network can drop its 7 ensemble-spread inputs (46 inputs down to 39) with no loss on the whole scored sample. The change in forecast error (CRPS, continuous ranked probability score, in percentage points of each Primary substation's capacity; a lower score is better) was +0.012 at the 8 Primaries that report only apparent power (MVA) and -0.043 at the 6 that report signed megawatts. Both changes are inside the equivalence limit. On cold winter nights at the 6 signed-MW Primaries the network without spread inputs scored 0.187 points worse, and on the 6 Primaries' rows with a labelled event it scored 0.408 worse. The whole-sample equivalence claim does not show those losses.

Each of four removals is tested alone against PretrainOnce (PO), with the printed minimum detectable effect as the limit. PO is experiment 494's network: pretrained once at the 2025-07 cut and fine-tuned each month, two seeds. Experiment 494 found PO equivalent to a fresh refit. "The eight" are the 8 MVA-only Primaries and "the six" are the 6 signed-MW Primaries, scored on rows with no labelled event. The limits are the smallest differences that two seeds per fold could reliably detect: 0.086 points at the eight and 0.170 at the six. "Bonferroni" bounds are 95% interval bounds adjusted for 20 comparisons.

Arm What is removed Inputs Output values (3 per Gaussian) CRPS change to PO, eight / six PO nothing (PretrainOnce) 46 9 0 a the 7 ensemble-spread (std_*) inputs; the ensemble mean stays 39 9 +0.012 / -0.043 c the 4 Christmas and bank-holiday columns, replaced by one day-type column 43 9 +0.095 / +0.229 d the 3 weekly-lag inputs (value, missing flag, age) 43 9 +0.079 / +0.050 b two of the three Gaussians of the output 46 3 +0.152 / +0.082 dF arm d, with fresh pretraining at every fold (a check, not a candidate) 43 9 +0.080 / +0.064

Only arm a is equivalent to PO at both the eight and the six. An arm is equivalent when the upper Bonferroni bound of its CRPS difference to PO is at most the limit. Arm a's upper bounds are +0.042 at the eight and -0.004 at the six. Arm c is not shown equivalent at either group: its CRPS difference could be as large as +0.143 at the eight and +0.332 at the six. Arm d could be as large as +0.124 at the eight (not shown equivalent) and +0.089 at the six (equivalent). Arm b could be as large as +0.201 at the eight, and its q99 pinball-loss difference could be as large as +0.029 against a limit of 0.02. No combined network was run, because arm a is the only arm equivalent at both groups. Verdict: partly supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Setup. Each arm is experiment 425's arm A (pooled plain network, Primary embedding, g09) behind a fixed input transform, pretrained once at the 2025-07 cut and fine-tuned at each of the 5 folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0 and 1, widening 1.15, rows of experiment 470 (experiment_470_intersection_v1), cleaned data with 1,179 scoring actuals dropped for a flagged exact zero, the D15 and D18 start cut applied. Experiment 425's arm A is the pooled plain network with a Primary embedding (setting g09). The removed inputs are multiplied by zero inside the network, after the standardiser and after the pretraining spread table, so training, forecasting, and reloading share one code path. A gate before any arm: an identity transform started from experiment 425's stored 2025-07 weights reproduced PretrainOnce's stored forecasts to within 5e-6.
  • Minimum detectable effect (two seeds, five folds). 0.086 points at the eight and 0.170 at the six. The caps in the series brief (0.03 for a, 0.02 for c, 0.05 for d and b) lie below those limits, so an equivalence claim at the limit cannot show a loss smaller than the minimum detectable effect, and an interval that reaches past the limit is inconclusive. Bonferroni count 20 (5 arms x 2 groups x CRPS and q99 pinball loss), with 100,000 origin-day block resamples. The scorer's Bonferroni interval is two-sided, and the decision rule reads its upper end.
  • CRPS, difference to PO (points). The first interval is the Bonferroni interval over origin days; the second is the 95% interval over folds.

The upper Bonferroni bounds are all inside the 0.02 limit except arm b at the eight: a -0.003 (bound +0.001) and -0.008 (-0.003); c +0.003 (+0.007) and +0.013 (+0.018); d +0.005 (+0.008) and +0.005 (+0.009); b +0.016 (+0.029) and -0.003 (+0.003), the first number at the eight and the second at the six.
  • Absolute CRPS (points). At the eight: K2 4.720, PO 4.690, a 4.702, c 4.785, d 4.769, b 4.842. At the six: K2 3.486, PO 3.484, a 3.441, c 3.712, d 3.534, b 3.566.
  • Against K2 (descriptive). Arm a is also equivalent to K2: -0.018 [-0.049, +0.011] at the eight and -0.045 [-0.077, -0.014] at the six. Arms c, d, and b are not shown equivalent to K2 at the eight (+0.065, +0.049, +0.122).
  • Fold by fold. Arm a's gain at the six comes mostly from 2026-01 (-0.268; the other four folds range from -0.059 to +0.083), so the improvement at the six is not established. Leaving one fold out moves arm a's point estimate at the eight between 0.000 and +0.023, which stays inside the limit.
  • Fresh-pretraining check on arm d (dF). dF against K2 (both pretrained fresh): +0.051 [+0.007, +0.096] at the eight (not shown equivalent) and +0.062 [+0.031, +0.092] at the six (equivalent). dF against PO gives +0.080 and +0.064. The verdicts equal arm d's, so the pretrain-once shortcut did not change a verdict.
  • Cold winter nights (CRPS difference to PO, Bonferroni interval; descriptive; 3 folds: 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03). At the eight: a +0.051 [-0.041, +0.172], c +0.053 [-0.037, +0.203], d +0.225 [+0.042, +0.445], b +0.273 [+0.155, +0.405]. At the six: a +0.187 [+0.014, +0.312], c +0.745 [+0.353, +1.109], d +0.167 [+0.051, +0.261], b +0.288 [+0.042, +0.475]. Every arm is worse on cold nights at the six. Among the arms called equivalent at the six (a and d), both lose there although neither loses on the whole sample. Arm a's cold-night loss is +0.376 in 2025-12, +0.073 in 2026-01, and -0.003 in 2026-03, so it comes almost entirely from the December fold. Against K2 the loss is +0.128 [-0.007, +0.240], which includes zero.
  • 12 to 36 hours (CRPS difference to PO). At the eight: a -0.027, c +0.024, d +0.025, b +0.116. At the six: a +0.033, c +0.265, d +0.083, b +0.114.
  • Christmas week (descriptive, one Christmas). At the eight a is -0.320 [-0.411, -0.206] better than PO; c -0.017, d +0.010, b -0.162. At the six: a +0.046, c +0.204 [+0.064, +0.476], d +0.228, b +0.200. Arm c does not lose at the eight in Christmas week.
  • Rows with a labelled event at the six (six_nra, descriptive). Arm a is +0.408 [+0.244, +0.577] against PO and +0.420 [+0.279, +0.562] against K2; arm c is +0.223 [-0.059, +0.518]. The loss of arm a is largest in 2026-01 (+0.590) and 2025-12 (+0.424), so removing the spread inputs hurts on rows where a labelled event occurred, which "rows with no labelled event" leaves out.
  • Against the briefs' original caps. The upper Bonferroni bounds against the caps in the series brief (0.03 for a, 0.02 for c, 0.05 for d and b): a +0.042 at the eight (past 0.03) and -0.004 at the six (inside), c +0.143 and +0.332 (past), d +0.124 and +0.089 (past), b +0.201 and +0.129 (past). Only arm a at the six meets the original cap. The q99 pinball-loss minimum detectable effect and the month-by-half-hour climatology row named in the plan were not computed.
  • The pre-registered predictions. P1 held (a equivalent at both groups). P2 failed (c not shown equivalent at either group). P3 held at the six (+0.050, inside 0.00 to 0.08) and failed at the eight (not shown equivalent). P4 failed on the CRPS range (+0.152 at the eight, outside 0.00 to 0.10; +0.082 at the six, inside) and q99 coverage fell by 0.008, inside the predicted 0.02. P5 did not apply, because no combined network ran.
  • Tails (widened 1.15, all folds, rows with no labelled event). q99 coverage at the eight: PO 0.991, a 0.991, c 0.989, d 0.989, b 0.983. At the six: PO 0.986, a 0.989, c 0.980, d 0.983, b 0.980. Arm b's q99 coverage falls by 0.008 at the eight and 0.006 at the six, inside the 0.01 limit. q95 coverage is 0.949 (PO) and 0.937 (b) at the eight, and 0.921 (PO) and 0.909 (c) at the six.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost at the six, difference to PO (experiment 470's cost measure; unadjusted 95% bootstrap intervals). At curtailment fraction f = 0.9: a -0.461 [-1.370, +0.039], c +0.193 [-0.009, +0.541], d -0.119 [-0.265, -0.004], b -0.307 [-0.917, +0.027]. At f = 0.75: c +1.267 [+0.116, +2.899]; a, d, and b include zero. At f = 0.5: a -1.234 [-4.226, +0.888], c +2.539 [+0.773, +4.654], d +0.917 [-0.219, +2.230], b +0.195 [-1.315, +1.698]. Arm c's cost is higher at f = 0.75 and 0.5; arm d's is lower at f = 0.9.
  • D15 and D18 (report only). CRPS: PO 11.588, a 10.566, c 10.868, d 11.523, b 11.068, K2 10.956. Arms a, c, and b score 0.5 to 1.0 points better than PO here, and PO scores 0.63 worse than K2, so on these two series pretraining once did not match a fresh refit.
  • Serving table. Every arm keeps 2 networks per pass, 12 monthly fine-tunes, and 1 pretraining per year (about 38 GPU seconds per seed-refit, experiment 494). Arm a needs 39 inputs instead of 46 and no ensemble-spread values at serving; change in CRPS against PO +0.012 at the eight and -0.043 at the six. Arm c: 43 inputs, +0.095 and +0.229. Arm d: 43 inputs and no read of the load one week earlier, +0.079 and +0.050. Arm b: a 3-value output instead of 9, +0.152 and +0.082.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary. PO has a median below the mean at 16 of 16 Primaries (largest gap -2.6 points of capacity), K2 at 15 of 16 (-2.4), and arm a at 15 of 16 (-1.7). Arm b's gap is zero by construction, because one Gaussian is symmetric.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrast. Mean absolute error of the median forecast at the eight: PO 6.724, a 6.734, c 6.854, d 6.840, b 6.970 points; at the six: PO 5.662, a 5.600, c 5.979, d 5.700, b 5.749. The directions agree with the CRPS contrasts for every arm (a at the six improves in both), so trigger 3 did not fire.
  • Triggers. No audit trigger of the ml-experiment skill fired and no audit was run. A leave-one-fold-out check on arm a at the eight stays inside the limit (0.000 to +0.023).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Five folds, each from one pair of networks, give wide intervals across folds; the origin-day interval treats each fitted network as fixed, so that interval is optimistic. The interval across folds for arm a at the six reaches +0.125 and for arm c reaches +0.588.
  • Each removal is tested alone; the removals might interact, and no combined network was run.
  • Arm c is a design choice: a single ordinal (0 to 3) in place of four columns. A different merge (for example a one-hot day type) might lose less; this experiment does not test that.
  • Zeroing an input gives the same function as removing it, but the unused first-layer weights start at random values, so initialisation differs slightly from a network built without them.
  • Arm b keeps the 1.15 widening used for the three-Gaussian arms; a different widening might change its q99 result.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete: "rows with no labelled event" may hold unlabelled events. Every score is selection-biased, and July 2026 is unused.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Re-test the removal of the spread inputs on more folds, scoring cold winter nights at the six separately before any change to serving.
  • Test other merges of the holiday columns (a one-hot day type, or keeping the Christmas position inside the merged column) before dropping the idea.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: The demand neural network has 46 input columns, a weekly lag, and a three-Gaussian output. Each removable input is a column production must compute and store, and each removable output shrinks the network. This experiment removes them one at a time from experiment 494's PretrainOnce recipe, which is equivalent to the fresh refit (experiment 494) and saves the pretraining stage.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Rows and folds. The 5 folds of experiment 449 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) on the rows of experiment 470. Every arm trains on exactly the rows of experiment 425's arm A: the D15 and D18 start cut and the flagged exact-zero drop apply, and the row set does not depend on the inputs. Cleaned data, monthly refits, seeds 0 and 1, widening 1.15.
  • Removing an input. Each arm trains the experiment 425 network (pooled plain network, Primary embedding, g09, learning rate 2e-4 in fine-tuning) with a fixed input transform in front of the first layer: the removed columns are set to zero, and the merged column is computed from the columns it replaces. For (a) and (d), a zeroed input carries no information and receives no gradient, so the network computes the same function as one built without those columns (the unused first-layer weights start at random values, so initialisation differs slightly). Arm (c) is not of that kind: the merged ordinal is a design choice, and bank_holiday is also recoverable from nearest_days. The serving table counts the inputs actually needed.
    • (a) No ensemble spread. The 7 std_* columns are zeroed. The ensemble mean stays.
    • (c) One day-type column. christmas_inside, christmas_days, christmas_tent, and bank_holiday are replaced by one column bank_holiday + 2 * christmas_inside (0 for an ordinary day, 1 for a bank holiday, 2 inside the Christmas period, 3 for both). This removes the graded position within the Christmas period. nearest_days and nearest_inside stay.
    • (d) Two origin lags. lag_week, lag_week_missing, and lag_week_age are zeroed. The newest-reading lag and the same-time-yesterday lag stay. Training rows do not change.
    • (b) One Gaussian. components = 1, so the output layer is 3 values, not 9.
    • Combined. The arms that pass, together.
  • Where the transform sits. The input mask or merge is a wrapper module created inside fit397.make_model, driven by an arm field recorded in meta.json. Training, pretraining, forecasting, and reloading a saved network all pass through it. It acts after the standardiser's clipping and NaN fill, and after prep425.fold_pretrain overwrites the std_* columns with the lead-band median table, so pretraining rows carry no residual spread values. Pretraining uses the 2025-07 fold's standardiser and spread table, as the stored PretrainOnce does, and fine-tuning uses each month's own. Gate before any arm is read: an identity-transform arm must reproduce the stored PretrainOnce forecasts, up to GPU nondeterminism.
  • Pretrain once, with a fresh check. Each arm pretrains once, at the 2025-07 cut (seeds 0 and 1, ERA5 and CAMS rows, the arm's own transform), and fine-tunes at each of the 5 folds from those weights. This is experiment 494's PretrainOnce recipe, so the baseline is PretrainOnce. To check that the pretrain-once shortcut does not change a verdict, arm (d) is also run with fresh pretraining at every fold (80 GPU seconds per seed-fold) and compared with K2, with the same limits and group split. Arm (d) is chosen because the lags are the inputs most tied to pretraining. The check passes if its equivalence verdict agrees with (d) against PretrainOnce. If the verdicts disagree, the page reports both and (d) stays out of the combined arm.
  • Not run. Experiment 494 measured pretrain-once, so no arm tests it again. Arms that change hidden width, depth, or the training rows are other experiments.

docs.title: Scoring and stop rules
docs.text:
• The experiment 470 scorer as in experiment 494: each arm against PretrainOnce, all on the same rows, with the printed two-seed MDE before any contrast. The scorer reports the eight, the six, cold winter nights, the 12 to 36 hour band, q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage and pinball loss, and avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5 at the six. D15 and D18 and Christmas week are report-only.
  • Stop. An arm that is not equivalent is not combined.
  • Serving table. Inputs, output values, networks per pass, refits per year, and the change in CRPS against PretrainOnce, per arm.

docs.title: Compute
docs.text: • Pretraining: 4 arms x 2 seeds x about 46 s. Fine-tuning: 4 arms x 5 folds x 2 seeds x about 34 s. The fresh-pretraining check: 5 folds x 2 seeds x 80 s. The combined arm: about 7 minutes. Roughly 50 GPU minutes in all (GPU only; per-fold data preparation and forecasting bring the wall clock to about 1.5 hours), one GPU process under 8 GB, one feeder core. The briefs ask for arms a, c, and d first and b only if budget allows; at this cost all four run.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Monthly refits; cleaned data; D15 and D18 cut; saved networks; stored forecasts reused (PretrainOnce and K2); tails and cost; example forecasts and the 14-day plot; the process order of the ml-experiment skill. Not applicable: load-shift event plots.

docs.title: Baseline choice
docs.text: The brief names experiment 425's arm A and K2 as the baseline. This plan uses PretrainOnce as the primary baseline, because every arm shares its pretraining cut and fine-tuning recipe, and experiment 494 found it equivalent to K2. K2 stays in the serving table. Step 1 of the series (the calibration rule) does not change the demand networks, so it leaves this baseline unchanged.

docs.title: Series
docs.text: Step 6 of the neural simplification series (brief of 2026-11-01), after experiments 494 (refit cadence and pretrain once) and steps 1 and 4 in other pull requests.

docs.title: Which part of the Christmas weight with ERA5 replay acts: the weight alone or the replay alone?
docs.text: In this experiment the ERA5 replay carried both the Christmas gain and the loss on other days, and the weight carried neither; the replay's extra optimiser steps are not ruled out as the cause. We asked which half of experiment 485's combined arm (labelled H2 there: a weight of 5 on Christmas rows plus a replay of earlier Christmases drawn from ERA5 weather estimates, 25% of each batch) did the work. We fitted each half alone (WO the weight, RO the replay) from the same stored pretrained neural network, on five folds (test months) and three seeds, and scored both on the same rows as H0 (experiment 425's unmodified fine-tune). Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity. The eight are the eight Primary substations whose meters report MVA only, and the six are the six whose meters report signed MW. RO lowers CRPS over 22 to 31 December 2025 at the eight by 0.230 points and raises it by 0.073 points on days outside 22 December to 2 January. WO moves the days outside that window by 0.009. The Christmas minimum detectable effect (from the three-seed spread of the stored fits) is 0.27 at the eight and 0.26 at the six. Neither arm clears that effect, so the stop rule applies: we report no demonstrated Christmas gain. The next test is the Christmas of 2026.

docs.title: Results (CRPS in points of effective capacity, 1.15 widening, difference from H0)
docs.text:
• Minimum detectable effect, printed first (three-seed spread of the stored fits): 0.054 (eight, outside the window), 0.122 (six, no labelled event), 0.148 and 0.260 (cold nights, eight and six), 0.082 (12 to 36 hour band, eight), 0.27 and 0.26 (22 to 31 December, eight and six). The 0.02 gate is below the first two, so a pass there is inconclusive.
  • Absolute scores outside the window: H0 4.780 (eight) and 3.569 (six, no labelled event). WO 4.788 and 3.592; RO 4.853 and 3.585.
  • Gate, eight: WO +0.009 (Bonferroni -0.018 to 0.031), RO +0.073 (0.037 to 0.112). RO fails.
  • Gate, six, no labelled event: WO +0.023 (-0.007 to 0.058), RO +0.016 (-0.017 to 0.054). Both are inside the minimum detectable effect, so the gate is inconclusive for both.
  • q99 pinball loss on the gate rows: RO +0.0087 at the eight (Bonferroni 0.002 to 0.019), which stays inside the +0.02 limit; WO +0.0023 at the eight and +0.0016 at the six.
  • Christmas, 22 to 31 December 2025 (suggestive, one holiday, day-block bootstrap, uncorrected 95% intervals): at the eight RO -0.230 (-0.315 to -0.145) and WO +0.148 (0.038 to 0.238); at the six RO -0.078 (-0.238 to 0.067) and WO -0.031 (-0.234 to 0.157). H0 scores 4.613 (eight) and 4.171 (six). Experiment 485 reported H2 at -0.222 (eight) and -0.097 (six).
  • 12 to 36 hour band, outside the window: eight WO +0.006, RO +0.054 (Bonferroni 0.010 to 0.099); six WO +0.015, RO -0.036 (-0.077 to 0.004).
  • Cold winter nights, outside the window: eight WO +0.017, RO +0.154 (-0.002 to 0.327); six WO -0.075, RO -0.089. Minimum detectable effects are 0.148 and 0.260.
  • Tails on Christmas, eight: q95 coverage H0 0.968, WO 0.923, RO 0.976; q99 coverage 0.996, 0.987, 0.998. At the six q95 coverage is 0.874 (H0), 0.816 (WO), 0.859 (RO), below 0.95 for all. WO's six q99 pinball loss on Christmas is 0.477 against H0's 0.341 (day-block interval 0.012 to 0.309, uncorrected).
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost at the signed-MW six, rows with no labelled event, all five folds (units of experiment 470's table; difference from H0, 95% cell-bootstrap interval): at f = 0.9 H0 1.852, WO -0.139 (-0.503 to 0.072), RO -0.167 (-0.557 to 0.049); at f = 0.75 H0 7.408, WO -0.178 (-1.046 to 0.411), RO -0.515 (-1.705 to 0.187); at f = 0.5 H0 22.711, WO +0.168 (-1.248 to 1.439), RO -0.970 (-2.908 to 0.315). manual_heuristic costs 2.017, 12.883, and 37.789. On the Christmas half-hours alone the costs are 0.000 to 0.002 at f = 0.9, 0.19 at f = 0.75, and 1.2 to 1.3 at f = 0.5 for all three arms, with no contrast distinguishable from zero.
  • Where RO's loss outside the window sits: mostly the two winter folds, +0.150 (2025-12) and +0.174 (2026-01) at the eight, as in experiment 485's H2.
  • Pre-registered prediction: failed. Neither arm lowered Christmas CRPS by the minimum detectable effect at both groups.
  • Fits and compute: 30 fine-tunes of 30 to 41 seconds each (0.29 GPU-hours), no reproduction fit needed because experiment 485 matched H0 to 1e-8. Rows dropped per fold: 68,680 for the D15 and D18 start cut and 2,155 to 2,925 flagged exact-zero half-hours. Replay sets hold 218,689 (folds 2025-10 and 2025-12), 274,171, 286,075, and 286,075 rows. Fitted networks are in the experiment's data folder under work/models/{WO,RO}.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean of the 11 quantiles, per group (points; gate rows / Christmas rows): H0 -0.847 / -0.189 at the eight and -0.471 / -0.672 at the six; WO and RO differ from H0 by at most 0.12 on gate rows, and by up to 0.12 at the eight and 0.24 at the six on Christmas rows. No arm shifts the forecast in a way the CRPS contrast does not show.
  • Mean absolute error of the median forecast beside each CRPS contrast: outside the window RO is +0.100 at the eight and +0.020 at the six against H0 (WO +0.007, +0.016); on Christmas RO is -0.399 at the eight and -0.125 at the six (WO +0.180, -0.144). Every sign agrees with the matching CRPS contrast.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. The prediction failed, but it was written with a stated prior against it and the cause (the replay) is what the split tests. RO and WO add up to H2's pattern (RO +0.073 plus WO +0.009 against H2's +0.081 outside the window at the eight), so no nested arm beats its container.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One Christmas is scored, so every Christmas number is suggestive. December 2024 is not scored: no pretrained weights exist for that cut, and the ensemble history starts 2024-04-01.
  • RO takes 1.33 times the optimiser steps per epoch, so an RO effect is a replay effect plus a step-count effect. No step-matched control was run.
  • Fold 2026-01 trains on Christmas 2025, so its rows for 1 and 2 January are reported but not counted in any test.
  • Every score is selection-biased: the five folds that choose the arm also score it. July 2026 is unused. NGED's event labels are incomplete: "rows with no labelled event" may hold events.
  • The serving cost is nil for both arms: each changes the training loop only, and the refit count stays at 12 monthly refits a year.
  • Code reuse: the scripts import experiment 485's fit loop, regime helpers, scorer, and figure code, which in turn import experiments 87, 397, 407, 418, 422, 425, and 470.

docs.title: Review of the work
docs.text:
• Code review (fresh Sonnet agent, before the first fit): no blocking problems; two wording fixes (the curtailment table has no BG2 column; H2 is quoted from experiment 485, not rescored), both applied.
  • Results review (fresh Sonnet agent, from the raw stored forecasts): re-derived the seven headline numbers to four decimals, found identical rows and correct seed pairing across arms, and found no leakage in the replay set.
  • Prose review (fresh Sonnet agent): 25 findings. Accepted: the lead's missing definitions and its overclaim about the replay (step count not ruled out), the wording of the weight's Christmas contrast, and the "network", "costs", "meets", and "which" ambiguities. Rejected: the request to explain every statistical term (Bonferroni, day-block bootstrap) inline, because experiment 485's page, which this one follows, defines them once.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Christmas 2026 would give a second scored holiday for H0 and RO.
  • A step-matched control and a smaller replay share would show whether the loss outside the window comes from the extra optimiser steps.

docs.title: Is the loss from refitting the Solar E network once a year instead of every quarter larger than 1% once the network design is held fixed?
docs.text:
Refitting the neural network for Solar E (one of the six anonymised metered solar farms) once a year instead of every quarter raises its quantile score by about 0.3%, inside the 1% limit, so Solar E does not block annual refits. The quantile score is a pinball loss (the penalty for a quantile forecast that sits on the wrong side of the observed output) averaged over 11 quantile levels; lower is better. Experiment 493 reported that, at Solar E, the one-pass neural network (which reads the ensemble weather forecast's mean and spread) with annual refits scored 1.28% worse than the encoder (which reads all 51 ensemble members) with quarterly refits. The 1.28% figure compares two arms that differ in both network design and refit schedule. Holding the design fixed at the encoder, annual refits score +0.26% worse than quarterly refits at 10 random initialisations (seeds), with a 97.5% interval of −0.19% to +0.78% from resampling whole calendar months (a month-block bootstrap).

We first re-read the six seeds that experiment 493 stored, with no new fits. At six seeds the schedule-only contrast was +0.53% (+0.10% to +1.06%). The upper end exceeded 1%, and the seed spread of the contrast was too large to rule out a loss of 1% (a minimum detectable effect of 1.01%). We then fitted seeds 6 to 9 (16 fits, as the brief required in that case). The 10-seed contrast is +0.26% with a minimum detectable effect of 0.71%, so the 1% limit lies above it and the result is conclusive.

Figure 1. Change in quantile score at Solar E, annual against quarterly refits. Each dot is one seed, the diamonds are the mean of the per-seed contrasts, and the bar is the 97.5% month-block interval of the 10-seed average forecast for C2. The dashed lines mark 0 and the 1% limit. C3 has six seeds only.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• C2, the schedule alone (encoder, annual against quarterly), Solar E. 10-seed average forecast: +0.265% over all bands (−0.190% to +0.780%) and +0.409% in the day-ahead band (+0.160% to +0.720%), month-block intervals at 97.5% (Bonferroni count 2, family level 5%, 12 valid-time months, 10,000 draws). Quarter-block intervals (4 blocks, at most 35 distinct resamples) are −0.18% to +0.99% and +0.09% to +0.71%. The all-bands upper end of +0.99% sits at the limit, so the verdict rests on the pre-registered month-block interval.
  • Seed spread. The 10 per-seed contrasts run from −1.23% to +2.17% (mean +0.14%, standard deviation 1.14). The mean of the per-seed contrasts differs from the contrast of the average forecast (+0.26%) because averaging 10 forecasts lowers each arm's score by a different amount.
  • Minimum detectable effect. Printed before any score: 1.96 × standard deviation ÷ √seeds, the half-width of a normal-approximation 95% interval for the mean per-seed contrast. The minimum detectable effect is 1.01% at six seeds and 0.71% at 10. At six seeds the 1% limit was below the minimum detectable effect, so the six-seed read was inconclusive; at 10 seeds the limit is above it. A t quantile instead of 1.96 would give about 1.32% at six seeds and 0.82% at 10.
  • Absolute scores (points of capacity, 10 seeds, all bands, rows pooled). Annual 7.273, quarterly 7.257. The month-block contrasts above weight the 12 valid-time months equally; the per-seed contrasts and these scores pool rows (see the audit below).
  • Six-seed per-seed mean of C2. +0.57% (range −1.23% to +2.17%), the figure that fell to +0.14% at 10 seeds.
  • C3, the one-pass network with annual refits against the encoder with quarterly refits (six seeds). +1.28% (+0.52% to +1.96%), per-seed mean +1.29% with a range of −0.64% to +2.18%. The schedule contributes about 0.3% of it at 10 seeds, so the rest, about 1%, belongs to the network design. C3 has no 10-seed version because the one-pass network was not refitted.
  • The loss is not one quarter. By refit quarter (10 seeds), annual against quarterly is 0.00% in the first quarter (same fit by construction), then +1.28%, +0.35%, and −0.37% in the second to fourth quarters. The per-seed standard deviation in each of those quarters is 1.9, 2.3, and 0.8 points, larger than the contrast in all three, so the brief's prediction that the contrast exceeds the seed spread in at least 2 of 4 quarters failed. Quarters are groups of forecast run dates, and no interval is shown because four blocks give too few resamples.
  • By valid-time month. The contrast is positive in January (+1.2%) and February (+2.2%), near zero in March and May to July, and negative in April (−0.6%) and August (−1.2%). The contrast is zero by construction for September to November. See Figure 2.
  • By hour of day. The loss sits in the daytime hours: 14:00 to 18:00 UTC hold 93% of the score difference, and the 05:00 to 08:00 UTC hours favour annual refits. See Figure 3.
  • Not a clip effect. The 460 rows whose output is at least 98% of the year's 99.9th percentile carry −2.9% of the total score difference (annual is slightly better there). Output as a share of effective capacity rises from 0.43 (December) to 1.07 (April and May), a seasonal pattern; the scored year shows no capacity step. The 2021 to 2023 production level that experiment 453 found at other farms is outside the scored year, so this read could not test it.
  • Control. In the first quarter the annual and quarterly forecasts are the same fit, and agree to below 1e-6 percent for all 10 seeds.

Figure 2. Change in quantile score by valid-time month (10-seed average forecast).

Figure 3. Change in quantile score by hour of day (10-seed average forecast).

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text:
• Code review (fresh Sonnet). Redirects, row assembly, leakage cut-off, and bootstrap level were correct. Accepted: fixed the "six-seed" headings printed in 10-seed mode, grouped the quarter table by run date (the refit quarter) instead of valid time, and corrected the capacity heading. Accepted and stated above: the minimum detectable effect is a normal-approximation half-width, not a power-based figure.
  • Audit (fresh Sonnet). It re-derived every headline number from the raw forecasts with its own code (10 seeds +0.265% and day-ahead +0.409%, six seeds +0.534%, per-seed contrasts, absolute scores), and found complete rows, no duplicate keys, a first quarter identical to the stored quarterly fit (largest quantile difference 2.6e-6), and no leakage in the cut-off. Accepted: the headline contrasts weight the 12 valid-time months equally, while the absolute scores and the per-seed contrasts pool rows (September 2025 holds 890 rows and May 2026 holds 8,310). Pooling rows gives +0.22% (−0.37% to +0.79%) over all bands and +0.54% (+0.27% to +0.78%) in the day-ahead band at 10 seeds, so the verdict stands; the day-ahead upper end stays below 1%. Accepted: the gap between +0.26% and the per-seed mean +0.14% is seed noise (standard error 0.36) plus an ensembling effect, not a fault. Accepted: the annual-minus-quarterly gap shrinks with horizon (row-pooled: day 1 +0.53%, days 6 to 7 +0.19%, days 8 to 10 −0.06%).
  • Prose review (fresh Sonnet). Accepted: glossed Solar E, the one-pass network, the encoder, the quantile score, and the month-block interval in the opening; wrote "neural network"; replaced the money metaphor and the overreach to "all six farms"; corrected "almost entirely" to "mostly"; used numerals for 10 seeds; fixed the tail ranges (0.002 to 0.015 points; 0.8 to 1.8 percentage points); stated the six-seed per-seed mean; noted the +0.99% quarter-block upper end; removed the duplicate audit bullet and the empty problems heading. Rejected: re-deriving the "2 of 4 quarters" prediction into the front matter, because it came from the brief and the page now says so.

• Seeds 6 to 9 were added after the six-seed read, as the brief specified for an ambiguous six-seed result. The six-seed and 10-seed numbers are both shown.

The scored year runs to August 2026, so it includes forecasts for July and August 2026, which the standing rule keeps unused. docs.title: Can two constants per farm replace table P for the wind and solar forecasts?
docs.text:
Two constants per farm tune the wind and solar tails about as well as table P on the stored forecasts, but the stored year is too short to prove it. Table P is the recalibration of experiment 450 and experiment 461: one widening factor for each farm, lead band, and tail quantile (16 per farm), plus a clip. A tail quantile here is q01, q05, q95, or q99, the 1%, 5%, 95%, and 99% points of the forecast distribution. This experiment re-scored experiment 461's stored forecasts (wind member_plain, solar a2_member, the neural-network arms named on that page, both scaled by the 99.9th percentile of the series' output as its capacity) with one number scaling the lower tail (q01 and q05) and one scaling the upper tail (q95 and q99), fitted on earlier months only. Rule d fits one pair for each family, rule e one pair for each farm, and rule f one pair for each farm and lead group (the first stored band, 36 to 72 hours, and 72 to 240 hours). It follows experiment 492, which tested the same rule for demand. No forecasting model was fitted.

On wind, every two-constant rule sat within 0.004 of table P's coverage at every tail, and the rules' mean tail pinball loss differed from table P's by under 0.3%. The pre-registered rule needs the minimum detectable effect (printed before any contrast) to be at or below each limit, and it is not, except for wind q99 coverage. Only that criterion is called equivalent, so no rule matches table P on all six. On solar, per-farm constants match table P's coverage within 0.005, but one pair for all six solar sites misses it at q05 and q95.

Figure 1 shows each rule's coverage minus table P's, pooled over farms, with the limit (green).

Figure 2 shows the mean tail pinball loss of each rule relative to table P's.

Figure 3 shows the share of actuals above q99, minus table P's.

Figure 4 shows each rule's absolute tail coverage, including the raw forecast and the 1.15 widening, against the nominal level.

Figure 5 shows the constants of rule e per farm and scored month.

Figure 6 shows one wind run (Farm A, January 2026) and one solar run (Solar A, June 2026) in fractions of capacity, with the median, the 50% band (q25 to q75), the 90% band (rule d's tails), and the actual. The horizontal axis is hours since the run started; the stored leads start at 24 hours for wind and 29.5 hours for solar. The first panel of each pair is the day-ahead window.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
All rows are true days 1 to 10. The scored months are wind 2025-08 to 2026-06 (54,899 rows, 3 farms) and solar 2025-10 to 2026-06 (264,951 rows, 6 series). Every row is scored by every rule.

The cells are the share of actuals at or below the quantile, except the last two columns.

  • No rule matches table P on all six criteria, for either family. The minimum detectable effect exceeds every limit except wind q99 coverage (below), so a result inside the limits is reported as inconclusive. Only wind q99 coverage, for rules d, e, and f, is called equivalent. Table P stays for both families.
  • On wind, the intervals alone put rule d inside the limits on all six criteria. Differences from table P (interval at the Bonferroni level, a correction for 36 tests): q01 +0.0026 (+0.0006 to +0.0052), q05 -0.0011, q95 +0.0036, q99 +0.0016, share above q99 -0.16 percentage points (-0.49 to +0.20), and tail pinball +0.11% (-1.07% to +1.44%). Rules e and f are inside the limits on five criteria. The share above q99 is inconclusive for both (e: -0.09 points, interval -0.41 to +0.27; f: +0.08 points, -0.19 to +0.37).
  • On solar, one pair for all six sites fails at q05 and q95, but per-farm pairs do not. Rule d differs from table P at q05 by -0.0145 (interval -0.0223 to -0.0084) and at q95 by +0.0081 (+0.0053 to +0.0114), both crossing the limit of 0.01. Rules e and f are inside the limits on coverage (every difference under 0.005) and tail pinball loss (-0.23% and -0.28%, intervals about -2.3% to +2.3%). Their share above q99 is inconclusive (+0.07 and +0.08 points, intervals reaching +0.28).
  • Table P misses the 1.5% limit on actuals above q99 for solar. That limit, at most 1.5%, is experiment 461's operating limit for wind and solar. Table P passes for wind (0.86%) and fails for solar (1.98%). Rule d passes for wind (0.70%) and for solar (1.497%, just inside the limit). The raw forecast fails for both (1.75% and 1.65%), as do rules e and f for solar (2.05% and 2.06%).
  • The minimum detectable effect is a conservative bound, and mostly larger than the limits. It comes from the run-block spread of table P's own rows, at 80% power and the Bonferroni level. Wind, pooled, all rows: coverage 0.010 (q01) to 0.035 (q05), share above q99 0.84 points, tail pinball 20%. Solar: coverage 0.016 to 0.041, share above q99 1.6 points, pinball 16%. Every value except wind q99 coverage exceeds its limit.
  • The bound ignores that both rules are scored on the same rows. The paired intervals above are 1.2 to 12 times narrower than the bound, and only 1.2 to 1.5 times narrower for wind q99 coverage and share above q99. verdict in contrasts.csv is the interval's verdict, and verdict_after_mde applies the rule. Wind rule d's share above q99 sits about 0.002 percentage points inside its limit, so a different resampling seed could flip that cell.
  • Shorter solar blocks would change four verdicts. With one block per day instead of one per week, solar intervals are about 2.2 times narrower (contrasts_init_blocks.csv). Rule d's q05 difference is then not equivalent. Rule d's q95 and the share above q99 of rules e and f are then equivalent. Weekly blocks stay as the pre-registered choice, because consecutive daily runs share their weather.
  • In the first lead band, the intervals are wide. The stored first band is 24 to 36 hours for wind (3,133 rows) and 29.5 to 36 hours for solar (12,565 rows). Wind q95 coverage differs from table P's by +0.0045 (d), +0.0041 (e), and +0.0080 (f, interval +0.0018 to +0.0160). Only about 30 wind actuals are expected above q99 here. Solar d differs at q05 by -0.0153 (-0.0276 to -0.0062).
  • Per farm, most cells are inside the limits, and Solar E is the exception. For rule e on all rows, wind has 12 of 18 criteria inside the limits and 6 inconclusive. Solar has 25 of 36 inside, 10 inconclusive, and 1 not equivalent: Solar E's share above q99 is +1.25 points (interval +0.29 to +2.84). Solar E has the fewest scored rows of the six solar series (41,076, against 41,994 to 45,936), and its fitted constants (lower 1.25, upper 0.83, means over the months) are the most extreme of the six. Four of its constants sit on the edge of the 0.50 to 1.80 grid in 2025-10.
  • Constants vary by farm and month. Rule d: wind lower 0.99 and upper 1.15; solar lower 1.01 and upper 1.02. Rule e, upper constant: wind 1.18 (Farm A), 1.11 (Farm B), and 1.17 (Farm C); solar 0.83 (Solar E) to 1.10 (Solar D). Figure 5 shows the month-by-month values.
  • The gate holds. Table P with experiment 461's plain fitting window reproduces that experiment's pooled wind share above q99 at 0.88% (solar: 1.75%; gate.csv). The main run uses the stricter window described in Method, where wind table P is 0.86%.
  • Fallbacks were rare. A cell is one farm, one lead group, and one scored month (99 wind cells and 162 solar cells). Rule f used its farm's pair from rule e in 5 wind cells and 8 solar cells. Separately, table P left a farm and lead band at factor 1 where fewer than 200 fitting rows existed; constants.csv counts those (fit_rows).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Forecasts. Experiment 461's rows_member_plain_p999.parquet and rows_a2_member_p999.parquet (folder 00461-*/work), in MW; wind is 52 Tuesday runs with 5 seeds averaged; solar is daily runs with 3 seeds averaged. July 2026 and later are dropped. Wind has 47 run blocks in the scored months. Weather at forecast time only.
  • Fit window. A fitting row's valid time (initialisation plus lead) must precede the scored month's first initialisation. Experiment 461's plain "earlier months" window would fit actuals unknown at the first run (up to 10 days for wind, whose month key is the initialisation month).
  • Rules. raw; 1.15 widening; table P (experiment 450's fit_factors, copied); d, e, f fitted as the 0.50 to 1.80 grid value (step 0.01) minimising pinball loss in fractions of capacity. Rule f has three lead groups: the first stored band, 36 to 72 hours, and 72 to 240 hours. All but raw use experiment 451's clip.
  • Intervals. Paired run-block bootstrap, 100,000 resamples, blocks of one run (wind) or one initialisation week (solar), at the Bonferroni level for 36 tests. A sensitivity run with daily solar blocks is in contrasts_init_blocks.csv.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00499-*/e00499_two_constant.py and e00499_report.py; the table P copy follows experiments 450 and 461; the folder of experiment 461 is read only as data.
  • Serving table. Table P: 16 factors per farm plus the clip. Rule d: 2 numbers per family. Rule e: 2 per farm (6 wind, 12 solar). Rule f: 6 per farm. Each is refitted when the forecasts are.
  • Not applicable. Cold winter nights and the avoidable-curtailment cost are demand measures. The cut of the noisy start of two short-history Primaries (D15 and D18) and the flagged exact-zero half-hours concern demand only. No ERA5 reanalysis or other past weather enters. No forecasting model was fitted or saved.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: unchanged by every rule, because each rule scales distances from q50 (the median) and leaves the median alone; stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Audit triggers: none fired.
  • Prediction outcome. P1 held for rule d, and held on five of six criteria for rules e and f (the intervals alone; the minimum detectable effect rule withholds equivalence on all but wind q99 coverage). P2 held for the family pair (d fails q05 and q95), and failed in part for the per-farm rules, which are inside the coverage limits but inconclusive on the share above q99; the stated low-sun mechanism was not tested. P3 held (f is no better than e). P4 held for per-farm cells once the minimum detectable effect rule is applied (18 of 18 wind and 33 of 36 solar cells are then inconclusive; on the intervals alone 12 and 25 are inside the limits). P4 missed for the first-band wind q99 criteria of rules d and f, whose intervals sit inside the limits.
  • Reviews: recorded in the PR body.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Caveats. Wind has 3 farms, 47 scored runs (52 stored), and 11 scored months; solar has 6 series and 9. Every score is selection-biased, because the same year chose the candidates and scores them. The data partner NGED's event labels are incomplete, and these rows are generator output with no event labels at all. The minimum detectable effect used here is an unpaired bound, so "inconclusive" overstates the doubt for most cells. Constants are fixed in each resample, so fitting uncertainty is not in the intervals. The constants are fitted by pinball loss and table P by matching coverage, so the comparison is partly of fitting methods.
  • Next steps. Re-score when 6 or more further months are stored. Try rule e with the family pair as the fallback for a series with under 3 months of history. Test whether solar's q05 and q95 gap of rule d comes from low-sun hours by adding an hour-of-day slice.

docs.title: Does a rolling correction from the last days of delivered errors fix the upper tail of the signed-MW six?
docs.text:
A correction built from each quantile's own recent errors does not fix the upper tail at the signed-MW six, but shifting the whole forecast by the recent median error comes close. We asked whether the forecast's tails could be repaired with no fitted table, by shifting every quantile of the demand forecast by the matching quantile of the errors it made over the last 7, 14, or 28 days (rolling conformal correction). The answer is no: q95 coverage at the six Primary substations whose telemetry is in signed MW stays below its 0.93 floor for every buffer length (0.874 to 0.913, against 0.885 for the raw forecast), so the pre-registered stop rule fires and the hypothesis is not supported. An arm added after the scores were seen, which shifts all 11 quantiles by only the median of the last 28 days' errors, brings all four tails into range (q95 0.935, q99 0.988) and lowers q99 pinball loss by 13%, but most of its CRPS gain comes from one Primary.

The correction follows conformalized quantile regression (Romano et al. (2019)) and its online form (Gibbs and Candès (2021)). The experiment re-scores forecasts stored by earlier experiments and fits no model.

Terms.

  • The six, the eight, A-pool, table P: as in experiment 483. The six are the Primaries with signed-MW telemetry, the eight those with MVA-only telemetry, A-pool is the five-seed average of experiment 425's arm A, and table P multiplies each tail quantile's distance from the median by a factor per metering group, lead band, and tail.
  • RC7, RC14, RC28: rolling conformal with a buffer of 7, 14, or 28 days of delivered errors. RC14+w1.05 adds a final symmetric widening of the four tail quantiles by 1.05.
  • RC28-bias (post hoc): the 28-day buffer's median error added to all 11 quantiles, with no tail shift of its own.
  • Clean rows: rows with no labelled event. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events.

Figure 1 shows each arm's coverage at the six with 95% intervals against the target range (green). Only table P, the two-constant rule, and RC28-bias reach the q95 range, and the four rolling arms fall short of the q95 and q99 floors.

Figure 2 shows q95 and q99 coverage by fold for four arms.

Figure 3 shows the change in CRPS and q99 pinball loss against the raw forecast, with the Bonferroni intervals.

Figure 4 shows the mean 28-day shifts of the median, q95, and q99 for the 12 to 36 hour band.

Figure 5 shows a day-ahead forecast and a full 10-day forecast at one signed-MW Primary, in January and June 2026.

Figure 6 shows six forecasts that cross labelled load shifts, three at the six and three at the eight, with the labelled half-hours marked in orange. NGED's logs may miss events, so unlabelled events may also appear in these panels.

docs.title: Arms, rows, and method
docs.text:
• Forecasts: A-pool, from experiment 425's seed_preds/A (12 months, 2025-07 to 2026-06, each month out of fold) for the buffers, and experiment 483's cache for the scored rows (gam14 plus D15 and D18, five folds: 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). A-gam-in is dropped, because it exists for the eight only and has no history before its folds. K2-425A is not used.
  • Dropped half-hours of July 2026: experiment 483's 2026-06 fold holds 2,736 half-hours with valid times on 2026-07-01 (leads of 39 hours or more), which the rule that keeps July 2026 for a finalist excludes. Every arm drops them, so the numbers here differ slightly from experiment 483's (the six's raw q95 is 0.8848 here).
  • Buffer: at each daily 09:00 UTC origin, for each Primary and lead band, every stored forecast row whose target is at least 6 hours before the origin (12 half-hour steps) and within the last 7, 14, or 28 days of target times. The buffers hold every delivered reading with a flagged exact zero removed, including readings inside labelled events, because a serving system holds no labels. The smallest buffer cell holds 113 residuals (7 days), 274 (14 days), and 547 (28 days), so the rule that leaves a cell with fewer than 100 residuals unchanged never fired. The 28-day buffer of a fold's first origin reaches back to forecasts initiated on 2025-08-24 (fold 2025-10), 2025-10-24 (fold 2025-12), 2025-11-24 (fold 2026-01), 2026-01-22 (fold 2026-03), and 2026-04-24 (fold 2026-06), so the months of out-of-fold forecasts that supply each fold's buffer are 2025-08 and 2025-09, 2025-10 and 2025-11, 2025-11 and 2025-12, 2026-01 and 2026-02, and 2026-04 and 2026-05. Those forecasts come from the XGBoost model fitted for their own month, not the fold's model. No in-sample forecast enters.
  • Shift and sorting: each of the 11 quantiles is shifted by the empirical (linear interpolation) quantile of the buffer's residuals at its own level. The shift leaves 7.2% (RC7), 4.3% (RC14), and 1.8% (RC28) of rows with crossed quantiles, which the scorer sorts as experiment 483 does.
  • Row sets: the five folds hold 322,323 clean rows at the six and 481,527 at the eight. The four folds from 2025-12 hold 267,233 clean rows at the six and add the arms fitted on earlier folds only (P-earlier, two-constant-earlier). Every arm in a set holds identical rows.
  • Cleaned data: the 483 rows inherit the drop of flagged exact-zero half-hours. About 151, 11, 0, 3, and 0 flagged half-hours fall among the five folds' scored valid times (2025-10 to 2026-06, 16 Primaries). The start cut for D15 and D18 is inherited and those two Primaries are reported, never judged. July 2026 stays unused.
  • Cadence: the stored forecasts come from monthly refits; this experiment fits only table P's factors and the two constants of experiment 492, as in those experiments.
  • Intervals: month-by-origin-day block bootstrap, 20,000 resamples. The Bonferroni count is 8 (RC7, RC14, RC28, and RC14+w1.05, each minus raw, on CRPS and q99 pinball loss, clean rows at the six), so the level is 99.375%. The 8 counted tests are the only tests with a stated family level; every other interval is 95% and descriptive. A sensitivity run with blocks of 14 origin days widens the counted intervals of the relative q99 pinball loss, and all four then include zero.
  • Minimum detectable effect (A-pool made from five single seeds, 1.15 widening, clean rows; printed before any arm was scored): at the six, CRPS 0.087 points, q01 coverage 0.0009, q05 0.0032, q95 0.0145, q99 0.0076, and q99 pinball loss 0.018 points; at the eight, CRPS 0.044, q01 0.0008, q05 0.0040, q95 0.0096, q99 0.0028, and q99 pinball loss 0.0095.
  • Selection bias: every score is selection-biased, because the same five folds choose and score the arms, and RC28-bias was chosen after the scores of the pre-registered arms were seen.
  • Reused code: experiments 435, 470, 483, and 492 (their folders are on the script's PYTHONPATH); experiment 425's stored predictions and experiment 483's cache.

Targets: q01 0.005 to 0.02, q05 0.03 to 0.07, q95 0.93 to 0.97, q99 0.98 to 0.995.

  • Pre-registered rule: no arm passes. RC7 fails q01, q05, q95, and q99. RC14 and RC28 keep q01 and q05 in range but miss q95 (0.893, 0.913) and q99 (0.957, 0.970). RC14+w1.05 misses q95 (0.903) and q99 (0.964). The stop rule applies, and the decision rule then says the tails need a different forecaster, not a different correction. The post hoc result suggests a different correction, not a rolling shift of every quantile.
  • Prediction outcome: P1 failed (no arm passes the q95 and q99 floors). P2 held for RC28 only (q99 pinball loss -3.4% against raw, Bonferroni interval -12.4% to +5.5%), and failed for RC7 (+37%), RC14 (+17%), and RC14+w1.05 (+11%). P3 held: the fold range of q95 coverage is 0.039 for RC28 against 0.107 for table P and 0.132 for the raw forecast. P4 held in part: RC7 is noisiest, and RC28 is the best of the three on q95, q99, and q99 pinball loss, so the 28-day buffer, not the 14-day buffer, is the best compromise. P5 held: cold-night q95 stays at 0.811 (RC14) and 0.864 (RC28).
  • Counted contrasts against raw (Bonferroni intervals): CRPS is lower by 0.172 for RC14 (-0.269 to -0.079) and 0.216 for RC28 (-0.293 to -0.146), against a minimum detectable effect of 0.087; RC7 gives -0.019 (-0.128 to +0.093). The q99 pinball loss rises by 0.073 for RC7 (+37%, +18% to +61%) and falls by 0.007 for RC28 (-3%, -12% to +6%). The CRPS gain of RC14 and RC28 comes from a shift of the median, as the post hoc arm shows below, and with blocks of 14 origin days the RC14 and RC28 relative CRPS intervals stay below zero (-11% to -0.2%, and -12% to -1.7%).
  • Why the tails fail (post hoc test of an explanation): RC28 beats table P on CRPS by 0.207 (95% interval -0.260 to -0.157) but misses q95 by 0.017. An arm that adds only the median shift to every quantile (RC28-bias) has the same CRPS gain (-0.205 against raw, 95% interval -0.261 to -0.151) and passes every clause. The difference between the two arms is the tail shifts. The audit found that the 28-day shift of q99 is noisier than the shift of the median: in the 12 to 36 hour band its standard deviation across origins is 1.25 to 6.12 points of capacity across Primaries, against 0.65 to 3.05 for the median. RC28-bias beats RC28 on q99 pinball loss in all five lead bands. The raw forecast under-forecasts persistently (the median residual is positive in most Primary-by-fold cells, up to +6.9 points) and the raw forecast's lower tail is too wide, so a shift of the whole forecast fixes both tails at once.
  • Post hoc arm (RC28-bias): q01 0.0073, q05 0.0393, q95 0.9353, q99 0.9877, and q99 pinball loss -13.2% against raw (95% interval -0.037 to -0.016 points). Its q95 coverage lies in range in 4 of 5 folds and q99 in 5 of 5 (range across folds 0.024 and 0.011), against 3 and 1 for table P. The pass holds on the point estimate: the Bonferroni interval for RC28-bias q95 is 0.928 to 0.943, so its lower bound sits below the 0.93 floor.
  • RC28-bias beside table P and the two constants (point differences, no interval): CRPS is 0.196 points lower than table P's (3.252 against 3.448) and 0.198 lower than the two constants' (3.450). The q99 pinball loss is 0.023 lower than table P's (0.170 against 0.192) and 0.018 lower than the two constants' (0.188). The two constants and table P were fitted on other folds, which includes later folds.
  • Four folds with the earlier-only fits: P-earlier gives q95 0.927 and q99 0.982 with q99 pinball loss 0.199, and two-constant-earlier gives 0.916 and 0.982 with 0.195. RC28-bias gives q95 0.934, q99 0.989, and q99 pinball loss 0.171 on the same 267,233 rows. Among the earlier-only arms of the four-fold set, only the post hoc bias arms clear the q95 floor: RC14-bias (not otherwise reported here) also does, with q95 0.934, q99 0.989, and q99 pinball loss 0.171, so the choice of 28 days over 14 days is not a clear one.
