  • Usable range. Ratio below 1.5, floor 0: midday 0.82 (95% interval 0.78 to 0.86), morning 0.75 (0.72 to 0.78), evening 0.78 (0.74 to 0.81), whole day 0.94 (0.92 to 0.95). Ratio 1.5 to 3: midday 0.51 (0.42 to 0.58), morning 0.85 (0.74 to 0.91), evening 0.88 (0.80 to 0.93), whole day 0.84 (0.73 to 0.90). At power factor 0.97 the 1.5 to 3 values are 0.52, 0.84, 0.87, and 0.84. The midday window stops being usable at a ratio of 1.5 to 3, earlier than the predicted 3 to 6.
  • Named contrasts, shoulder minus midday, ratio 1.5 to 3. Floor 0: +0.33 (morning) and +0.37 (evening); power factor 0.97: +0.32 and +0.36. All four are above zero at the 0.025/64 level (lower bounds +0.03 to +0.07; minimum detectable effect 0.16 to 0.18). In the ratio bin below 1.5 the shoulders are worse than midday by 0.04 to 0.07 at floor 0 (0.01 to 0.04 at power factor 0.97), not significant after correction.
  • Not estimable above ratio 3. In the 3 to 6 and above 6 bins 99.4% and 97.4% of days cross zero (5 and 11 ordinary days), so no area under the curve can be computed. D12's ratio is 5.3 (81.6 over 15.6 in experiment 506's May to July days; 5.27 here), so D12 lies where this calibration cannot say whether a shoulder window works.
  • D12 placebo (post hoc, thresholds of the 1.5 to 3 bin). The morning threshold of 37 points is passed on 98.2% of sunny days and 93.7% of cloudy days, a sunny-to-cloudy ratio of 1.05 (1.01 to 1.10). The evening threshold of 46 points is passed on 96.3% of sunny days and 98.9% of cloudy days (0.98; 0.95 to 1.01). The statistic is saturated, because the thresholds were set at lower export and nearly every D12 day is below them. The cloudy-day condition of the decision rule fails (lower bound 1.01, under 1.5), and so does the first condition (D12's bin is not calibrated). The dark-window condition is met: of the sunny days with no dark-window dip, 53% (15 days) show a morning shoulder dip and 58% (38 days) an evening one, against the 3% bar, so prediction A3's "fewer than 3%" arm is refuted. D12's shoulder dips are not shown to be export.
  • The other seven. With thresholds of 40 to 53 points, the evening dip rate at D8 is about twice the cloudy rate (ratio 1.9, lower bound 1.2), as at D22 in the morning (1.5, lower bound 1.2). D8's dips with no dark-window dip are 10% to 13% of such days, D22's 10% to 19%, and D2, D3, and D4 at most 2%. The thresholds sit far above zero, so these are low-reading days and not proven sign changes.
  • Bonferroni count. 32 area intervals, 16 named contrasts, and 16 placebo ratios were planned:
  • Of these, 16 areas and 8 contrasts were not estimable and D12 has no placebo ratio at its own bin. Decision rule intervals are plain 95% by design.

docs.title: Part B: D8 and D22 midday dips
docs.text:
• Dip days reproduced. 71 at D8, 13 at D22, and 13 at D12 (experiment 506). D8's share of sunny days with a dip is 0.7% in 2023, 3.9% in 2024, 23% in 2025, and 32% in 2026; D22's is 0.7% to 4.2%.
  • Engine running (D8). In 55 of the 71 dip days (77%; Wilson interval 66% to 86%) more than half the dip half-hours are flagged as engine running. The mean flagged share is 0.78 in dip half-hours, 0.60 in the same half-hours on the 14 nearest non-dip days (difference 0.18, 95% interval 0.08 to 0.28), and 0.007 at D5, D10, and D11. The detector reads D8's own residual and is high on about 60% of D8's midday half-hours in 2025 and 2026 whatever the day, so the placebo share is high; an engine-running dip is neither solar nor a load transfer. The engine class cannot be assessed at D22.
  • Season and sky. From March to October, D8 has 62 dips in 717 sunny days (the remaining dip days fall in other months) and 2 in 129 cloudy days (Mantel-Haenszel cloudy-to-sunny ratio 0.18, interval 0.04 to 0.57); D22 has 13 in 710 and 0 in 122 (0.29, 0.16 to 0.71). A solar cause predicts almost no cloudy dips, but the two intervals reach 0.57 and 0.71, from April to September D8's ratio is 0.44 (0.11 to 1.11), and the D22 figure rests on zero cloudy dips, so neither cause is excluded. Prediction B2 (an upper bound under 0.2) is not met at either Primary.
  • Shape test fails its known answer. It labels 63% of injected solar-shaped drops and 85% of injected boxcars correctly (target 80% each; D22 alone labels 74% of boxcars), and 72% of D10's real reverse-flow days solar. The dip days are 32% (D8) and 67% (D22) solar-labelled. The shape test carries no weight.
  • Spark spread and neighbours. Positive spark spread on 57% of dip days against 47% of other sunny days (difference +0.10, interval -0.03 to +0.22). The neighbours' readings over D8's dip half-hours move by -7.1 (D3), +22.6 (D12), and -14.3 (D22) points against placebo changes of -0.6, +2.4, and -0.2, and D22's dips by -6.2, -0.9, and +26.0 against placebo changes of +2.1, +6.1, and -10.1; with unmetered neighbours and opposite signs this is a low-power diagnostic and shows no clear recipient.
  • Growth and labels. The dips began in 2023 at both Primaries. 71 of 71 D8 dip days and 12 of 13 D22 dip days fall outside every labelled event that has times, but only 3 such events exist for D8 (the last ended on 2025-10-02, and 27 D8 dips fall in 2026) and 14 for D22, so the count of dips outside NGED's labelled events is a weak lower bound.
  • Cause classes. D8: 55 engine running, 16 not separable. D22: 12 not separable (one dip day had no usable drop curve). The 55 are consistent with the engine; the rest could be solar or a load transfer.

docs.title: Part C: what the answers change
docs.text:
• D12. Experiment 370's reverse flow at D12 is not shown by the shoulder dip, which is as common on cloudy days and was not calibrated at D12's ratio. A probability of reverse flow at D12 should not use shoulder dips alone.
  • D8. Label D8's dips as a probable engine regime, not "inferred, heavy reverse flow only". The 16 days not flagged and the 13 D22 dips remain candidates for either a signed-power estimate or an unlabelled load shift, and are listed as unlabelled events in the training rows for the history-encoder line later. No count is promised to experiment 507.
  • Question for NGED. What changed at D8 and D22 between 2023 and 2026: did the gas engine behind D8 start or change its running hours, were any connections added, or were loads transferred in the daytime at either Primary? Which of the dip days from 2023 to June 2026 does NGED's own log explain?

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean forecast: not applicable, no forecast was made.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 1 (a known-answer test failed: the shape test) and trigger 2 (results contradict predictions A1 and A2, with the explanation recorded above). A fresh Sonnet audit (briefs/508_audit.md) is recorded in the audit section.
  • Deviations. Windows by sun elevation and April to September, not the clock; a daylight crossing label on all-sky days; ratio bins in place of injection levels; the D12 post hoc read; a different shape-test metric from the 506 audit; the plan review and code review changed the design, as the plan section records. Part B's cloudy half-hours need a clear-sky index of 0.1 to 0.3. Two daylight-saving days a year are dropped from the day matrices.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
A fresh Sonnet auditor re-derived the three headlines with its own code (briefs/508_audit.md). Triage:

  • Part A bin 1.5 to 3 survives. Midday 0.509, morning 0.846, evening 0.875 against the stored 0.508, 0.846, 0.875. Leaving out D10 and moving the shoulder band to 8 to 20 or 12 to 25 degrees leave the ordering unchanged. Accepted as a caveat: the pooled midday interval (0.42 to 0.58) does not separate it from 0.5 exactly.
  • Selection of days (accepted as a caveat). Only about 22% of April to September days qualify, because the recorded farm output is missing in 20% to 63% of shoulder half-hours, so the sample leans toward days on which the farm was already producing at both shoulders. Requiring 2 shoulder half-hours instead of 3 gives 3.4 times as many days and the same ordering (midday 0.50, morning 0.84, evening 0.83).
  • Farm extension (accepted as a caveat). The extension creates no spurious crossings, but without it the evening area rises from 0.875 to 0.91, so shoulder areas are mildly sensitive to it.
  • Engine overlap (accepted; wording weakened). The count of 55 reproduces and the index alignment is right, but the engine flag is also high on D8 days whose lowest reading is 7 to 25 points (0.72 to 0.85), and the flag is fitted to D8's own series. The page therefore says "consistent with" and treats the engine as an unproven explanation.
  • Sky test (accepted; wording weakened). D8's ratio of 0.18 holds from March to October (one-sided Fisher p = 0.0013) but is 0.44 (0.11 to 1.11) from April to September. D22's 0.29 rests on 0 cloudy dips in 122 days (Fisher p = 0.12), so the sky test does not support a solar cause at D22.
  • Crossing share above ratio 3 (corrected). 99.4% in the 3 to 6 bin, 97.4% above 6 (98.7% combined); the page already gives the two figures.
  • Shape test (accepted). The injected solar drop uses the recorded farm shape while the classifier fits the fleet shape, and the no-injection control is labelled solar 25% (D8) and 47% (D22) of the time. The page already gives the test no weight.

docs.title: Pre-registered plan
docs.text:
The first version of this plan took u over the clear-sky index as the clear-sky shape. A Sonnet plan review (16 findings, briefs/508_plan_review.md) showed that u is computed from the actual sky, so the plan below replaces that choice and the choices that depended on it.

  • Rows. Cleaned power (scan_power, flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped), the experiment 399 start cut (D15 and D18, neither in the six nor the eight), July 2026 untouched, the experiment 506 data layer (folder ml-experiments/00506-*). Part A uses April to September only, so that the midday, shoulder, and whole-day windows describe the same days.
  • Sun position. The shoulders are the half-hours in which the sun's elevation (pvlib, at the half-hour midpoint) lies between the two elevations at which the clear-sky fleet shape u of experiment 412 reaches 0.05 and 0.3 on rising-sun half-hours with a clear-sky index of 0.9 or more at D12. Morning is rising sun, evening is setting sun. The midday window is 10:00 to 15:00 UK time, and the fourth window is the whole day.
  • Qualifying days and one label. A day qualifies when every window has enough finite half-hours (6 midday, 3 per shoulder, 40 whole-day), so every window's area under the curve uses the same days and any sky. The label is the same for all windows: the day's signed power is both below and above zero while the sun is above the horizon.
  • Injection. signed = p - level x median|p| x farm shape, levels 1, 2, 4, and 8, farm rotation of experiment 408 (Solar A to C), the median taken over sunny middays as in experiment 506. The recorded farm shape is zero below 15 degrees of elevation, which is where the shoulders sit, so there the farm shape is the site's own u times the median ratio of the farm shape to u where u is 0.3 to 0.5. The share of half-hours extended this way is printed.
  • Ratio bins. The export-to-import ratio is the median clear midday reading over the median dark-hour reading (sun more than 6 degrees below the horizon), May to July, from each arm's own reading in each injected world, never a fitted capacity. Worlds are pooled into the bins 0 to 1.5, 1.5 to 3, 3 to 6, and above 6, per arm, and the area under the curve is computed per bin. D12's observed ratio (about 5.3) is read off the bin that contains it.
  • Arms, counts, and what counts as usable. Two arms (floor 0 and power factor 0.97; floors 0, 2, and 4 give identical areas). Bonferroni families, counted at the end of the run: 32 area-under- the-curve intervals (4 bins x 4 windows x 2 arms), 16 named contrasts (each shoulder minus midday, per bin and arm, named in advance with no choice of the better shoulder), and 16 placebo ratios (8 Primaries x 2 shoulders), 64 in all, plus the Part B tests counted separately. The decision rule uses plain 95% intervals on purpose; the named contrasts are also shown at the 0.025/64 level. A cell with fewer than 30 crossing or 30 ordinary days, or fewer than 10 month blocks holding both, is reported as not estimable. Every area carries its crossing and ordinary counts, the number of month blocks, and every contrast carries 2.8 standard errors as its minimum detectable effect. A window is usable at a ratio if its area is at least 0.8 with a lower end above 0.6 (as in experiment 506); the same criterion is used throughout.
  • Thresholds. Youden-optimal per bin, window, and arm on the six, frozen to disk before the eight are read. Each of the eight uses the threshold of the bin that holds its own observed ratio; because thresholds for every bin are computed from the six alone, reading the eight's ratios only selects a row. For the eight, the power factor 0.97 arm is the matched one and floor 0 a lower bound, because the meters report apparent power.
  • Placebos. Sunny days (mean clear-sky index of the window 0.7 or more) against cloudy days (below 0.3) for each Primary and shoulder, with the ratio of the dip rates (0.5 added to each count) and a month-block interval, and the Primary's own dark-hour reading over a window of the same number of half-hours immediately on the dark side of the shoulder. Cloudy-day maintenance patterns are a confound that the placebo cannot remove, and the page says so.
  • Part B. A dip day is a sunny day (clear-sky index 0.7 or more) whose 10:00 to 15:00 minimum reading is below 6.9 points of capacity (experiment 506). The run stops unless it finds 71 dip days at D8, 13 at D22, and 13 at D12. Cause classes are solar export, load transfer, and gas engine running. Engine running is scored against matched placebo days (the same half-hours on the 14 nearest same-day-type non-dip days after 2023-08-15) with D5, D10, and D11 as controls, using experiment 196's engine states as stored by experiment 291, and cannot be assessed at D22. The shape test fits one amplitude to the drop (baseline of the 14 nearest non-dip days minus the reading), once with the fleet shape u and once with a boxcar over the half-peak run around the deepest half-hour; injected boxcar and solar-shaped drops of 40 to 50 points on D8 and D22 days before 2023 give the known answer, and the shape test enters the cause classes only if at least 80% of each injected class is labelled correctly. The dip rate on cloudy against sunny middays of March to October is a Mantel-Haenszel risk ratio over year-month strata with a stratum bootstrap; with few cloudy dips it is reported as underpowered. Spark spread (experiment 186) compares dip days with other sunny days after 2023-08-15. The neighbour check reads the other Primaries under the same supply point and is a low-power diagnostic. The count of dip days outside every labelled event with times is a stand-alone result.
  • Prediction and rule changes. Prediction A1 and the usable criterion now share one threshold (area 0.8, lower end above 0.6). The decision rule for D12 requires: a usable shoulder area in the bin that holds D12's ratio; a sunny-to-cloudy ratio of dip rates with a lower bound above 1.5 (sensitivity at 1 and 2 reported); and, among sunny days with no dark-window reading below the frozen shoulder threshold, a shoulder dip share of at least 3% (sensitivity at 1% and 2%).
  • Deliverables. Part C of the brief (what each answer changes, using "consistent with") and the exact question for NGED about what changed at D8 and D22 from 2023 to 2026, including the engine, new connections, and load transfers.
  • Reuse. No predictions are reused or fitted. CPU only, 2 cores. Cadence: not applicable. Past-weather caveat: the clear-sky index comes from CAMS and describes the day observed, so the sunny and cloudy day labels are not available at forecast time. Advice followed: experiment 506 says to treat the dip as a screen, not a signed label.

docs.title: Reuse and cost
docs.text: CPU only; each script takes under a minute. Scripts import the experiment 506 data layer (folder ml-experiments/00506-*) and experiment 87's grid_times. Stored tables are under data/ml-experiments/00508-*/work/.

docs.title: Are the forecast bands appropriately confident when a power lag sits inside a load-shift event?
docs.text:
When a load shift is added to one of the earlier power readings that a demand forecast uses, the forecast that mixes lagged and lagless neural networks (K2-S1) keeps almost the same band and almost the same coverage as on the same rows with no shift, so the shift does not make its band narrower relative to the errors. The pooled neural network that never saw an added shift (A-pool) is the exception. At the three Primary substations we could check, every forecast under-covers its upper tail with or without a shift, so the bands need widening everywhere, not only inside load-shift events. The verdict is partly supported, because K2-S1's coverage in scenario 6, K2-S1's band width in scenarios 5, 7, and 8, and A-pool's coverage in scenario 2 missed the pre-registered thresholds (see Predictions).

We asked whether the 90% band of a demand forecast is too narrow, too wide, or about right when one of its three lags falls inside a load-shift event. A lag is the power reading from an earlier time, such as 24 hours before the forecast, that the neural network takes as an input. A load-shift event is a period when NGED moves demand from one feeder to another, which steps the recorded power without changing true demand. Experiment 482 added artificial shifts to the lags of stored forecasts, and found that K2-S1's central 90% band covered 85% of actuals inside the event. That 85% could not be told apart from the networks' ordinary under-coverage, because experiment 482 did not score the same rows with no shift. This experiment scores both forecasts on identical rows: the forecast with shifted lags (stored by experiment 482) and the forecast with unshifted lags (stored by experiments 454 and 470). It reports the difference.

The comparison covers three Primary substations, D5, D12, and D14, in five test months. Those 15 (month, Primary) pairs are the only ones for which experiment 482 stored forecasts row by row. Experiment 482 shifted each of 16 Primaries in turn, and the other 13 keep summary tables only. D5 and D14 are among the six Primaries whose power is recorded in signed MW, and D12 is among the eight recorded only in MVA (apparent power). Five forecasts are compared, as defined in experiment 482:

  • LL is the lagless neural network, which reads no lag.
  • S1 is a neural network that reads lags and was trained on added shifts.
  • B-mix is an equal mixture of a lagged and a lagless network.
  • K2-S1 is a mixture of two S1 and two lagless networks.
  • A-pool is a pooled neural network trained on real lags only.

"q95 coverage" is the share of actual values at or below the forecast's 95th-percentile line, with a nominal value of 0.95. The headline rows have the newest of the three lags inside the event (experiment 482's newest_in class) and a lead of 24 to 240 hours. That is 6,495 rows in the 1-day scenarios, 90,915 in the 14-day scenarios, and 19,485 in scenario 8. Widths are in points of capacity, which are percentages of the Primary's effective capacity.

Scenario Shift Duration Neighbours compensated 1 +1x 1 day no 2 -3x 1 day no 3 +1x 14 days yes 4 -3x 14 days no 5 +3x 14 days yes 6 -1x 14 days no 7 +3x 1 day yes 8 +2x 3 days no, and the actual also moves (a genuine level change)

A shift of 1x is one standard deviation of the Primary's 24-hour change in power. "Neighbours compensated" means the same energy is taken off up to two neighbouring Primaries.

docs.title: Shifted lags against unshifted lags
docs.text:
• K2-S1's q95 coverage moves by -0.024 to +0.025. The differences are +0.011, -0.014, +0.016, -0.015, +0.018, -0.024, +0.019, and +0.025 in scenarios 1 to 8, with bootstrap standard deviations of 0.004 to 0.009. Its q95 coverage with shifted lags is 0.78 to 0.85, and 0.78 to 0.83 with no shift. Intervals at the Bonferroni level for 48 contrasts (the interval widened so that 48 comparisons together keep a 5% error rate) exclude zero in scenarios 1, 3, 5, 6, and 8.
  • K2-S1's 90% band changes by -0.7% to +7.5%. The changes are +1.5%, -0.7%, +3.0%, +1.3%, +7.5%, -0.7%, +4.0%, and +4.1% in scenarios 1 to 8. The band is 30 points of capacity wide.
  • A-pool's q95 coverage falls by 0.09 in scenario 2, 0.24 in scenario 4, and 0.13 in scenario 6. These are the negative shifts with no compensating neighbours. Standard deviations are 0.025, 0.039, and 0.025. A-pool's q95 coverage rises by 0.04 to 0.15 in the other scenarios, because a positive shift lifts its median above the actual. Its q05 coverage in scenario 4 falls to 0.007 from 0.042.
  • S1 loses 0.05 to 0.07 of q95 coverage in the three negative scenarios with no compensating neighbours, and B-mix loses 0.01 to 0.03. The lagless network changes by exactly zero in all 8 scenarios, which confirms that the code leaves an unshifted forecast untouched.
  • The same pattern holds at 12 to 36 hours ahead (735 rows in the 1-day scenarios and 10,289 in the 14-day scenarios). K2-S1's q95 coverage changes by -0.031 to +0.033, and A-pool's by -0.304 in scenario 4.
  • Tail calibration, scenario 4, newest_in rows, 24 to 240 hours ahead. The table shows q05 and q95 coverage (nominal 0.05 and 0.95) with shifted and unshifted lags, and the pinball loss at q95 (the quantile score at the 95th percentile, in points of capacity).
Forecast q05 shifted q05 unshifted q95 shifted q95 unshifted q95 pinball shifted q95 pinball unshifted LL 0.061 0.061 0.771 0.771 1.789 1.789 S1 0.042 0.062 0.693 0.759 2.231 1.790 B-mix 0.044 0.054 0.762 0.790 1.725 1.666 K2-S1 0.038 0.049 0.786 0.802 1.601 1.594 A-pool 0.007 0.042 0.574 0.811 3.293 1.598

docs.title: Probability integral transform and widening factor
docs.text:
• The probability integral transform of every forecast piles up in the top bin. The transform places each actual within the forecast's distribution, and a flat histogram means calibrated. In scenario 4, 27% of actuals fall above the forecast's 90th percentile for K2-S1 and A-pool with no shift (nominal 10%). Shifted lags raise that share to 30% for K2-S1 and to 54% for A-pool.
  • The widening factor is the multiplier on each quantile's distance from the median that makes q95 coverage equal 0.95. For K2-S1 it differs between shifted and unshifted lags by -0.03, +0.01, -0.05, -0.03, -0.11, +0.03, -0.04, and -0.06 in scenarios 1 to 8, so it is within 0.05 in 6 of 8 scenarios. In the two exceptions (scenarios 5 and 8) the factor is lower with shifted lags, so the band was already wider.
  • B-mix is within 0.05 in 6 of 8 scenarios too, but not the same six. Its differences are 0, 0, -0.04, +0.06, -0.14, +0.04, -0.02, and -0.04.
  • Most of the gap is general, not specific to events. K2-S1's factor with no shift is 1.8 to 1.9 in scenarios 1 to 7 and 2.4 in scenario 8, and the widening stored by experiment 454 is 1.15.
  • A-pool's factor falls to 0.89 in scenario 5 and rises to 2.33 in scenario 4. Its band is too wide when a positive shift with compensated neighbours lifts its median, and too narrow when a negative shift pulls the median down.
  • The lower tail needs less widening. K2-S1's q05 factor is 0.91 to 1.27 with shifted lags and 1.00 to 1.27 with none.

docs.title: Real events (sensitivity)
docs.text:
• This is not a paired result. The page compares rows with any of the three lags inside a labelled event (58,638 rows at 12 of 30 (month, Primary) pairs in the signed-MW six, and 40,819 rows at 12 of 40 pairs in the MVA-only eight) with rows that have no label, 24 to 240 hours ahead. The two kinds of rows come from different Primaries and months, so the contrast mixes the event with the Primary.
  • Against the NRA-corrected actual, K2-S1's q95 coverage is 0.92 on event rows and 0.88 on rows with no label in the signed-MW six (difference +0.044, bootstrap standard deviation 0.040, minimum detectable effect 0.113). The NRA-corrected actual is the metered actual with the normal running arrangement restored (the correction of experiment 435). In the MVA-only eight the figures are 0.92 and 0.92 (difference -0.005, standard deviation 0.025).
  • Against the metered actual, the signed-MW six drop to 0.70 (difference -0.176, standard deviation 0.080). The metered power during the event is itself shifted, so the NRA-corrected actual is the headline.
  • K2-S1's band is 1.2 points narrower on event rows in the signed-MW six (standard deviation 1.5). In the MVA-only eight, event rows are 15 points wider than rows with no label for every forecast including the lagless network, so the difference comes from the Primary, not the event.
  • The labels are incomplete. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so rows with no label may hold events no label covers, and the real-event slices undercount.

docs.title: Other 13 Primaries (summary level, not the same rows)
docs.text: • The three stored Primaries are the worst covered. K2-S1's q95 coverage with the stored raw quantiles on newest_in rows is 0.790 at the three stored Primaries and 0.902 at the other 13 in scenario 4, 0.828 and 0.929 in scenario 1, and 0.774 and 0.855 in scenario 8. With the 1.15 widening, scenario 4 gives 0.836 and 0.933. The other 13 have no unshifted scores, so these figures do not form a pair.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held in part. K2-S1's q95 coverage changed by less than 0.02 in scenarios 1 to 5 and 7. In scenario 6 it fell by 0.024, which is below the 0.03 fall that would call the band too confident. The band was under 3% wider in scenarios 1 to 4 and 6 (scenario 3 is 2.98%), and 4.0% wider in scenario 7, which fails.
  • P2 held in two of three scenarios. A-pool's q95 coverage fell by 0.24 and 0.13 in scenarios 4 and 6, and by 0.09 in scenario 2, just short of the 0.10 line (interval -0.17 to -0.01).
  • P3 held in 6 of 8 scenarios for K2-S1 (tolerance 0.05). It failed in scenarios 5 and 8, by -0.11 and -0.06, where the factor was lower with shifted lags.
  • P4 held, but every other scenario also under-covers. In scenario 8 every forecast's q95 coverage is 0.76 to 0.87, below 0.95, so the prediction that the bands are too narrow could not fail, and scenario 8 is not worse than the others.
  • P5 held. The width threshold failed in scenario 5 (+7.5%) and scenario 8 (+4.1%). The early check on the same rows had found +4.0% and +3.1% over all leads; this page uses 24 to 240 hours.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• A difference of 0.02 is 2 to 5 bootstrap standard deviations at 15 pairs. The coverage minimum detectable effect (2.8 times the seed standard deviation of the pooled coverage) is 0.011 at q95 for K2-S1 (0.008 to 0.012 at q05) and 0.022 to 0.028 at q95 for A-pool. The seed standard deviation comes from 3 seed cells (5 for A-pool), so it is noisy, and it measures seed variation, not the clustering of rows.
  • The Bonferroni count is 48 for the confirmatory contrasts (3 forecasts, 8 scenarios, coverage and width). Every other contrast is descriptive.
  • Scenario 8 is a different contrast. Both forecasts are scored against the shifted actual, so the contrast is between a forecast that saw the shifted lags and one that did not. In scenario 8 the before and after classes mix shifted and unshifted targets.
  • The stored forecasts reproduce. The unshifted forecasts of experiments 454 and 470 match experiment 482's no-shift rows to 2.4e-06 on before rows for every forecast. K2-S1's scenario 4 newest_in q95 coverage over all lead hours (0.790) matches experiment 482's summary tables.
  • The absolute coverage figures come from three Primaries that under-cover more than the other 13. They are not representative of all 16. The 80-pair re-run was not done, because it needs a GPU stage that has not been timed and the result is not borderline.
  • No mean forecast is scored, so the median-minus-mean check does not apply.
  • No audit trigger fired. P1 and P2 each failed in part, and neither contradicts an earlier finding.
  • No new example forecast charts. This page re-scores stored quantiles. Experiments 468 and 482 hold six injected-scenario fan charts and four real-event charts for the same forecasts.
  • Not scored here: the avoidable-curtailment cost, the price of widening on rows with no labelled event (experiments 446 and 483 hold it), and table P (experiment 435's recalibration) for LL, S1, and B-mix, because it exists only for K2-S1 and A-pool.

What the next experiment should answer. The three stored Primaries under-cover at q95 by 0.12 to 0.19 without any event. Whether the other 13 Primaries also need a factor above 1.15 on rows with no event is a question for experiment 483's widening results, not for an event rule.

docs.title: Can a demand network that reads no lagged power, fine-tuned every week with a recency weight, get close to K2-S1 on ordinary rows and avoid the load-shift problem?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

A lag-free demand neural network that is refitted every week scored 0.17 to 0.19 points of continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) better than one refitted every month (a lower score is better). A 90-day recency weight added a further 0.07 to 0.08 points. The best lag-free arm, L-Ww, stayed 0.13 to 0.16 points behind K2-S1, the demand network of experiment 470 that reads lagged power. The 90-day weight made the next week's forecast follow an injected load shift (a sudden, lasting change in a substation's demand) more closely. Neither dropping labelled events nor adding a latent outlier component reduced how much of the injected shift leaked into the next week's forecast. In the Christmas week of 2025 (both groups) and the last week of January 2026 (the six only), L-Ww scored better than K2-S1, so the gap to K2-S1 is not uniform.

We asked whether a network that reads no lagged power can come close to K2-S1 by being fine-tuned more often. The lag-free neural network is pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather (reanalysis datasets), then fine-tuned on archived ECMWF ensemble (ENS) forecasts. We compared a monthly refit with a weekly refit, and a 182.6-day with a 90-day recency half-life. We also tried two ways to make the fine-tune ignore load-shift events, and injected a shift into the training targets to measure how much of it the next week's forecast absorbs. All arms are scored on the half-hours of experiment 470's row set, over five months, in points of effective capacity (a percentage of each Primary's capacity). "The eight" are the eight Primaries that report only apparent power; "the six" are the six that report signed megawatts. Headline scores use rows with no labelled event.

Arm What it is L-M Lag-free network, refitted monthly, 182.6-day half-life weight (experiment 425's recipe). L-W Same network, refitted weekly (days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 of the scored month). L-Ww Weekly refit with a 90-day half-life weight. L-Ww-D L-Ww with the half-hours inside labelled events (padded by 96 half-hours) dropped. L-Ww-O L-Ww with a fourth, wide Gaussian component that is dropped at serving. K2-S1, A-pool Stored references that read lagged power (experiments 470 and 425).

Verdict: partly supported. The weekly refit helped by much more than predicted. The 90-day weight helped by 0.07 to 0.08 points, below the minimum detectable effect. No arm got within 0.1 points of K2-S1 at the six, and neither arm meant to reduce the leak of an injected shift worked.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Setup. Seeds 0 and 1 (L-Ww-D and L-Ww-O seed 0 only); widening 1.15; rows of experiment 470 (experiment_470_intersection_v1, 572,041 half-hours at the eight and 322,323 at the six); folds 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06; cleaned data; the D15 and D18 start cut. Forecasts reach 240 hours, so the page scores leads up to 10 days; the row set excludes longer leads.
  • Minimum detectable effect from this experiment's own two seeds. 0.164 points at the eight and 0.123 at the six, not the 0.086 and 0.170 in the plan (those came from experiment 494, with other arms). Bonferroni count 28 CRPS tests (56 with q99 pinball loss).
  • CRPS contrasts (points; Bonferroni 95% interval; negative favours the first arm).
Contrast Eight Six L-W minus L-M -0.173 [-0.219, -0.133] -0.185 [-0.246, -0.132] L-Ww minus L-W -0.083 [-0.168, -0.012] -0.068 [-0.104, -0.031] L-Ww-D minus L-Ww +0.079 [+0.044, +0.117] +0.032 [+0.005, +0.062] L-Ww-O minus L-Ww +0.062 [+0.004, +0.118] +0.034 [-0.019, +0.087] L-M minus K2-S1 +0.412 [+0.319, +0.505] +0.385 [+0.300, +0.474] L-W minus K2-S1 +0.239 [+0.130, +0.338] +0.200 [+0.114, +0.294] L-Ww minus K2-S1 +0.156 [+0.027, +0.275] +0.132 [+0.020, +0.238] L-Ww minus A-pool +0.238 [+0.157, +0.322] +0.098 [+0.031, +0.174]
  • Absolute CRPS (points). Eight: L-M 5.175, L-W 5.003, L-Ww 4.920, L-Ww-D 4.998, L-Ww-O 4.982, K2-S1 4.763, A-pool 4.682. Six: L-M 3.807, L-W 3.623, L-Ww 3.555, L-Ww-D 3.587, L-Ww-O 3.589, K2-S1 3.423, A-pool 3.457.
  • Week of the month (figure 2). The weekly gain is zero in week 1, because the first weekly fit is the monthly fit, and grows afterwards: at the six -0.170, -0.195, -0.366, and -0.268 points in weeks 2 to 5, and at the eight -0.116, -0.170, -0.345, and -0.386.
  • Christmas week and January (report only; figure 3). From 22 to 31 December 2025, L-Ww scored 4.332 at the eight and 2.861 at the six, against 5.406 and 3.210 for K2-S1 (-1.074 and -0.349). From 25 to 31 January 2026 at the six, L-Ww scored 4.027 against 4.271 for K2-S1 (-0.244). From 1 to 14 January it scored 0.090 (eight) and 0.216 (six) points behind. One Christmas week is a single event, and the noise floor of a single Christmas week given in the brief is about 0.26 (six) to 0.27 (eight) points, so the Christmas result is suggestive only.
  • Injected-shift leak (descriptive; one seed, 5 folds, both signs). The shift is 3 times the standard deviation of a Primary's 7-day mean target (on average 31 to 36 points of capacity), added to the 7 days before the refit. The next week's median moves by this many points of capacity (share of the shift in brackets): L-W 3.84 (11%), L-Ww 6.11 (18%), L-Ww-D 6.18 (18%), L-Ww-O 5.94 (17%). The leak is largest in 2026-01 (7.4 for L-W, 14.5 for L-Ww, 15.2 for L-Ww-D, 16.9 for L-Ww-O). L-Ww-D and L-Ww-O do not cut L-Ww's leak by the pre-registered 30%.
  • Learned outlier weight of L-Ww-O. The mean weight is 0.020 for rows with no labelled event, 0.020 inside labelled events, 0.020 on cold winter nights (48,742 rows), and 0.019 in Christmas week. The component does not pick out events or weather; the prior pins it near the same value everywhere.
  • Tails (widened 1.15, metered actuals). On rows with no labelled event at the six, q99 coverage is 0.989 (L-W and L-Ww), 0.985 (L-Ww-D), 0.982 (L-Ww-O), 0.978 (L-M), and 0.979 (K2-S1). On event rows q99 coverage is poor for every arm (0.77 for K2-S1, 0.79 to 0.87 for the lag-free arms). no arm has a q99 pinball loss more than 0.02 points worse than K2-S1 at the six (L-W and L-Ww-D are 0.020 and 0.021 better), but L-Ww is 0.036 worse than A-pool at the eight.
  • Cold winter nights and horizon bands. On cold winter nights at the eight L-Ww scores 4.60 (K2-S1 4.61); at the six 6.80 (K2-S1 6.86). In the 12 to 36 hour band L-Ww scores 4.55 (eight) and 3.81 (six), against 4.48 and 3.86 for K2-S1.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost at the six. At f = 0.9, L-Ww 0.95 [0.15, 2.29] against K2-S1 1.90 [0.24, 4.89]; at f = 0.75, 5.96 against 8.43; at f = 0.5, 22.26 against 26.94. Every difference to K2-S1 has an interval that includes zero, so the lag-free arms are not shown worse.
  • D15 and D18 (report only). L-Ww scores 11.19 against 11.53 for K2-S1.
  • Event rows (figure 6). Metered event rows at the six: L-Ww 7.776, L-W 7.624, L-Ww-D 8.071, L-Ww-O 7.875, K2-S1 7.554. NRA-corrected rows: L-Ww 22.78, K2-S1 22.62.
  • Serving workload per arm. 1 network per serving pass for every lag-free arm. Monthly refit: about 1 fine-tune per month; weekly refit: about 5 per month (3 to 9 seconds each on one GPU). No stored tables are added.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Pre-registered rules.
    • Weekly beats monthly: pass (point estimates -0.173 and -0.185, intervals exclude zero, q99 pinball loss within +0.02).
    • A recency weight helps: fail (gains of 0.083 and 0.068 are below the minimum detectable effects of 0.164 and 0.123, and the leak is 2.3 points larger, not at most 0.05).
    • A lag-free candidate exists: not within the pre-registered 0.03 of K2-S1 (gap 0.132 at the six, 0.156 at the eight); the gap is narrowed, not closed, and the line is not closed because the weekly arms score better than K2-S1 in some weeks.
    • L-Ww-D or L-Ww-O worth adopting: fail for both (the leak did not fall by 30%).
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 (a prediction contradicted) fired: the weekly gain was 2 to 4 times the upper end of the predicted range (0.08 at the six, 0.05 at the eight). A Sonnet audit re-derived the two headline contrasts from the raw forecasts (-0.1846 and -0.1725; -0.0681 and -0.0829), found L-M equal to experiment 448's L0PT forecasts to 9.5e-6, found no refit using later data than its cutoff, and found the first week of L-M and L-W identical to zero. Nothing in the audit explains the gains away.
  • Median minus mean forecast per Primary (checks). The median is below the mean at the eight for every arm (-0.38 to -0.61 points), as in earlier experiments.
  • Conditional half-life sweep. Not run: L-Ww did not beat L-W by the minimum detectable effect.
  • Seed 1 for L-Ww-D and L-Ww-O. Not run: both failed the leak rule.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The cause of the weekly gain is not isolated. L-M minus K2-S1 does not grow through the month (at the six 0.46, 0.37, 0.41, 0.37, and 0.16 points in weeks 1 to 5), so the lag-free network does not age faster than the lagged one; a weekly refit may simply beat any monthly refit. No arm refits K2-S1 weekly.
  • The 90-day weight helps unevenly. At the eight L-Ww minus L-W is about +0.07 in weeks 1 and 2 and -0.32 in week 4, and positive in 2026-06.
  • Intervals are origin-day block bootstraps and ignore dependence across days of one fold; five folds is few. The Christmas and January results are two folds.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete and are hindsight labels. "Rows with no labelled event" may hold unlabelled events, and event counts are lower bounds. L-Ww-D validates on a different early-stopping set than L-Ww.
  • The Beta(3, 97) prior is applied once per row in the fine-tune loss only, so it pins the outlier weight near 0.02 on every class of row; the arm tests that setting and not an outlier component in general.
  • The scorer widens only q01, q05, q95, and q99 about the median; widening all 11 levels changes the contrasts by about 0.01 points.
  • The stress run is one seed and one refit week per fold; its leaks are descriptive.
  • Forecasts reach 240 hours only; the saved networks allow a later 14-day pass.
  • Reviews: one Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review before the first fit, one Sonnet audit of the headline contrasts, a Sonnet numbers review, and Sonnet prose reviews.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Refit K2-S1 weekly as well, to separate "weekly refits help any network" from "weekly refits help only a lag-free network".
  • Test the weekly lag-free network and K2-S1 over a full winter, including a second Christmas.
  • Repair the hindsight labels in the fine-tune targets (untested here) rather than dropping rows.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
Can a demand network that reads no lagged power at forecast time, pretrained once on ERA5 and CAMS rows and then fine-tuned every week or every month on ENS rows, match K2-S1 and A-pool on rows with no labelled event while avoiding the load-shift problem entirely?

The gap to close is 7% to 10% at the signed-MW six. On ordinary rows the lag-free average of experiment 472 scores 3.622 and a single-seed lag-free network about 3.71, against 3.387 for K2-S1: 0.23 to 0.32 points. (The brief's earlier "4% to 5%" is not what experiment 482 shows.)

docs.title: Base network (checked before this plan)
docs.text:
• L0PT is arm A minus the lag columns. Experiment 448's L0PT weights and experiment 425's arm A are the same PlainMdn of experiment 397 (setting g09: hidden 64, 2 layers, 3 components, dropout 0.1, 8-wide Primary embedding), built from the same summary feature scheme. Arm A takes the scheme's 46 columns plus the embedding (first-layer weight 64 x 54). L0PT takes the 37 columns left after dropping the scheme's nine lag columns (lag_origin, lag_day, lag_week, their _missing flags, and their _age columns) plus the embedding (64 x 45). Every other weight has the same shape. Arm A's own pretrained weights have the lag columns and do not load.
  • Pretraining rows. L0PT folds exist for 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06 (5 seeds each). Fold 2025-12 is pretrained here (seeds 0 and 1, about 46 s each) with experiment 448's pretrain_rows and loop.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Folds and rows. The five experiment 449 folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) on the rows of experiment_470_intersection_v1. July 2026 is unused. The D15 and D18 start cut (2025-03-01) and the flagged exact-zero drop apply (cleaned data). Reported per fold.
  • Standing practices followed. Cleaned data; D15 and D18 cut; saved networks; stored forecasts reused as references; tails and curtailment cost; example forecasts and the 14-day plot; load-shift event plots (at least 6, both metering groups); the process order of the ml-experiment skill. Not followed: the monthly-only rule, because the question is the refit cadence.
  • Arms (pooled over the 16 Primaries; two seeds, 0 and 1; widened by 1.15 unless said):
    • L-M: fine-tuned monthly with experiment 425's recency weight, 0.5 ** (age_days / 182.6). The queue-order check found that 425's recipe already weights rows with a half-life of 182.6 days, so the "unweighted" arms of the brief are weighted at 182.6 days.
    • L-W: fine-tuned weekly with the same 182.6-day weight.
    • L-Ww: fine-tuned weekly with a 90-day half-life. L-Ww against L-W is the one recency test. L-Mw (monthly, 90 days) is dropped: experiment 407 tested a 0.25-year half-life with the pooled network (+0.073 at the six, +0.025 at the eight, not better).
    • L-Ww-D: L-Ww on rows minus the half-hours inside labelled events (see "Appended arms").
    • L-Ww-O: L-Ww with a latent outlier component (see "Appended arms").
    • Stress runs of L-W and L-Ww (see "Stress run").
  • Weekly refit rule and leak check. For scored month M the refits are at 00:00 UTC on days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 of M (five refits; the last covers the days left in the month). Each refit fine-tunes the month's L0PT weights on rows with valid time at most the refit minus 3.5 h and origin at most the refit (experiment 425's build_ens_fold rule, with the refit set to the week's first origin), over the 24 months before the refit. The early-stopping held-out weeks (the absolute weeks of experiment 422's purge_masks) must end before the refit as well. The forecast of a scored week uses only its own refit. Age in the recency weight is measured from the refit. A script prints, for every refit, the latest training valid time and origin, the number of rows past the cut (it must be 0), and the number of early-stopping rows left, and does the same for the pretraining rows of each fold (experiment 448's rule: valid time at most the month's refit minus 3.5 h), before any score is computed. Week 1 of each month is the monthly refit, so L-M and the first week of L-W share one fit per seed. The month's standardiser, target mean and standard deviation, and spread table are fitted once at the monthly refit and kept for the month's weekly refits, so the pretrained weights see the input scale they were pretrained on.
  • Fits (counted per arm). Seeds 0 and 1 unless stated; the stress runs use refit week 3 of each fold, both signs.
Arm Fine-tunes L-M and L-W, monthly refit (shared with L-W week 1) 5 folds x 2 seeds = 10 L-W, weeks 2 to 5 5 x 4 x 2 = 40 L-Ww (week 1 differs from the monthly fit: 90-day weight) 5 x 5 x 2 = 50 L-Ww-D, seed 0 5 x 5 = 25 L-Ww-O, seed 0 5 x 5 = 25 Stress: L-W, L-Ww, L-Ww-D, L-Ww-O (seed 0, 5 folds, 2 signs each) 4 x 10 = 40 Total 190

Pretrainings: 2 (fold 2025-12, 3 components, seeds 0 and 1) plus 5 (4 components, seed 0, all five folds) = 7, at about 46 s each. About 190 x 31 s + 7 x 46 s = about 1.7 GPU-hours. Seed 1 of a passing L-Ww-D or L-Ww-O (about 25 more fits each, up to 0.4 GPU-hours) is conditional on the rules below. One GPU process under 8 GB (MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1) and one feeder core. Each month's rows are built once and masked by cutoff. The exact count is reported to the manager before the fits run. - Control of L-Ww-O. The seed-0 control is L-Ww seed 0 fine-tuned from the 3-component L0PT weights (the 2025-12 fold pretrained here with the same recipe). It has no outlier component; the only difference from L-Ww-O is the head. - References (stored, no refit): K2-S1, the lag-free average of experiment 472, A-pool (five seeds, and its two-seed version), BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology.

docs.title: Stress run
docs.text:
• The shift. 3 times the standard deviation of a Primary's 7-day mean target (printed per Primary, computed from cleaned data before the refit only), added to the training target of the 7 days before the refit, excluding the early-stopping weeks, both signs. One refit week per fold (the week after the injection, chosen before any score is read as week 3 of each month), one seed. L-W and L-Ww (and L-Ww-D, L-Ww-O) are refit on the same injected rows, with matched uninjected controls from the main run.
  • What it measures. The leak is the sign-adjusted bias of the following week's median forecast against the matched uninjected fit (injected sign times the change in the median, in points of capacity, averaged over the two signs), with the CRPS change beside it. The stress run has one seed and 5 weeks, so the minimum detectable effect of the scored months does not apply: the stress run is descriptive, with the five fold-paired values shown. The effective weight of 7 days in a window of about 730 is small (about 5% at the 90-day half-life), so the leak may fall below the minimum detectable effect. A lag-free network is not exposed to a bad lag at forecast time; the training targets are exposed, and this arm measures that.

docs.title: Appended arms
docs.text:
• L-Ww-D (drop labelled events). Fine-tune on L-Ww's rows minus the half-hours inside NGED's labelled events, padded by 2 days either side. An event is known at a refit if its start is at or before the refit; only such events count: an event that started before the cutoff and ends after it is dropped from its start to the cutoff, with no use of its future end, and the 2-day pad applies only before the cutoff. The rows leave the training set and the early-stopping week alike. NGED's labels are hindsight labels, unavailable in real time at a weekly refit, and they are incomplete, so unlabelled events stay in. Report the share of rows dropped per fold and, per scored week, whether it contains or follows an event. The injected shift is unlabelled by construction, so L-Ww-D cannot drop it.
  • L-Ww-O (latent outlier component, dropped at serving). A fourth Gaussian component whose mean is the mixture's mean (weights-averaged main mean), whose scale is the widest main scale times (3 + softplus(learned offset)), and whose weight has a Beta(3, 97) prior (mean 3%) that enters the fine-tune loss only. The fourth component changes the output head, so the arm is re-pretrained with 4 components (5 folds, seed 0) and L-Ww gets a seed-0 control pretrained the same way. At serving the outlier component is dropped and the main weights are renormalised. The 1.15 widening no longer applies: the widening sweep 1.0, 1.05, 1.10, and 1.15 runs per arm, with q95 and q99. The learned outlier weight is reported by row class (rows with no labelled event, rows inside labelled events, cold winter nights with their count, Christmas week).
  • Seeds. Seed 0 is a screen for L-Ww-D and L-Ww-O. Any arm that passes runs at seed 1 (about 25 more fits) before an adoption claim. Comparisons are paired with seed-0 L-Ww and with the two-seed L-Ww; the minimum detectable effect comes from the two-seed arms and is indicative only.
  • Widening. All arms are scored at 1.0, 1.05, 1.10, and 1.15, and the headline uses 1.15 for every arm. No factor is chosen from the scored data; L-Ww-O is additionally shown at the factor that gives it the lowest CRPS, labelled post hoc.
  • Held, not run: a two-sided step repair of the training targets (held until experiment 507 reports), a penalty holding the fine-tune near the pretrained weights, and a robust 28-day median level adjustment.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
• Scorer. The experiment 470 scorer, tail script, and curtailment script pointed at this folder, as in experiment 494. Predictions are raw quantiles in experiment 425's seed-prediction layout, widened by 1.15 (L-Ww-O: by the sweep).
  • Minimum detectable effect, stated before any score: 0.086 at the eight and 0.170 at the six (2 seeds, 5 folds, experiment 494), recomputed from this experiment's own seed spread and printed.
  • Headline contrasts: each arm minus K2-S1 and minus A-pool; L-W minus L-M; L-Ww minus L-W; on rows with no labelled event, at the signed-MW six and the MVA-only eight separately (CRPS in points of effective capacity, days 1 to 10 and the 12 to 36 hour band). Bonferroni count 28 CRPS tests (56 with q99 pinball loss): 14 contrasts x 2 groups, namely L-M, L-W, L-Ww, L-Ww-D, and L-Ww-O each minus K2-S1 and minus A-pool (10), plus L-W minus L-M, L-Ww minus L-W, L-Ww-D minus L-Ww, and L-Ww-O minus L-Ww (4). The horizon bands, event rows, cold nights, and stress runs are descriptive and not counted. The row set is the intersection of experiment 470; rows that the lag-free networks have and the references lack are counted and reported separately. The weekly-against-monthly contrast is reported as a 2-seed contrast with a fold interval beside the origin-day interval.
  • Also: real events (NRA-corrected actuals headline, metered secondary; the events of experiments 435 and 482, 184 labelled events in the scored months) with the event count and the minimum detectable effect, including weeks that contain or follow an event; cold winter nights; Christmas week (report-only); q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage and pinball loss; the widening sweep; avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5 at the six; D15 and D18 report-only. NGED's labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events.
  • Serving cost per arm: networks per serving pass (1), fits per month (about 1 for monthly, about 5 for weekly), stored tables (none), and the added work of a weekly refit.

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
• This experiment is underpowered by design: the limits below sit under the minimum detectable effect, so the expected outcome is "not shown", and a pass can only read "interval excludes zero" or "not shown worse".
  • Weekly beats monthly if L-W minus L-M at the eight or at the six has a Bonferroni interval that excludes zero with a point estimate at most -0.03, q99 pinball loss within +0.02, and no worse on labelled-event rows beyond the minimum detectable effect. Otherwise stop; keep monthly.
  • A recency weight helps if L-Ww beats L-W by at least the minimum detectable effect of a group (0.086 at the eight or 0.170 at the six, that group passing) and the L-Ww stress leak is no more than 0.05 points of capacity larger than L-W's (descriptive). Otherwise the 90-day weight is not adopted.
  • A lag-free candidate exists if the better of L-W and L-Ww by six-group CRPS (a choice made after the scores, and counted as one) has a point estimate within 0.03 of K2-S1 on rows with no labelled event at both groups ("not shown worse", not equivalent) and a point estimate not worse than K2-S1 on labelled-event rows. K2-S1 has no stress run here, so its stored injected-lag scenarios from experiment 482 are the reference. A gap between 0.03 and 0.1 reads "narrowed, not closed". If so, say it has 1 network per serving pass and no load-shift exposure at forecast time, and leave the first-release choice to the maintainer. If no arm gets within 0.1 of K2-S1, say the lags carry information a refit cannot replace at these leads, and close the line.
  • L-Ww-D or L-Ww-O is worth adopting over L-Ww only if the injected-shift leak falls by at least 30% of L-Ww's leak (descriptive, five fold-paired values shown), rows with no labelled event stay within 0.03 of L-Ww, cold winter nights are no worse than +0.05 against L-Ww, and q99 pinball loss stays within +0.02. If L-Ww-O's learned outlier weight on cold winter nights is more than twice its weight on other rows with no labelled event (leave-one-fold-out, with a count), the component is absorbing weather and the arm fails. If both arms fail to cut the leak by 30%, close them and name the hindsight target repair as untested.

docs.title: Caveats named in advance
docs.text:
• Interim numbers are labelled "interim, unaudited" until the audit triggers have run. If L-Ww or L-Ww-D beats its twin by the minimum detectable effect, a 30 and 180 day half-life sweep runs as an addition. Intervals are month-block bootstraps with Bonferroni correction; seeds and rows are equal across arms. Titles say "load-shift", never "switching". The merge follows the skill's rule.
  • The Beta(3, 97) prior is applied once per row, so it acts as a per-row regulariser that pins the outlier weight near 3%; early stopping scores the three served components alone. NGED's labels are hindsight labels, sharper than a live detector, and L-Ww-D validates on a different set than L-Ww.
  • Weights and standardisers of the pretraining are the month's, not refreshed per week.
  • The 2025-12 fold has no stored L0PT weights; the 2-seed pretraining here is new.
  • Lag-free rows need no lag-age cut, so more rows survive than in experiment 425's arm A; scoring uses the intersection and the page prints both row counts.
  • Intervals ignore dependence across days of one fold.

docs.title: Series
docs.text: Neural simplification series; runs alongside experiment 507 (writes only to its own folder).

docs.title: How often should the lag-free demand network be refitted, which recency half-life suits it, and does pretraining on ERA5, CAMS, and ENS rows together help?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

Refitting the lag-free demand network every day scored 0.065 points of CRPS better than refitting it every week at the eight and 0.061 better at the six (lower is better; Bonferroni intervals exclude zero), and refitting twice a week scored 0.036 and 0.041 better. The daily refit leaves the network 0.091 points (eight) and 0.071 points (six) behind K2-S1, the network that reads lagged power, so it closes 42% (eight) and 46% (six) of the weekly network's gap of 0.156 and 0.132. Neither a 30-day nor a 60-day recency half-life reached the -0.05 bar against the 90-day half-life, and the mixed pretraining on ERA5, CAMS, and ENS rows scored worse than the ERA5 and CAMS pretraining of experiment 510.

We asked whether refitting more often than weekly, or changing the recency weight, or pretraining on ENS rows as well, closes more of the gap to K2-S1. All arms are lag-free, restart each fine-tune from the fold's pretrained weights, average two seeds, and are scored on experiment 470's row set, in points of effective capacity. "The eight" are the MVA-only Primaries and "the six" are the signed-MW Primaries. Headline scores use rows with no labelled event. Each model scores only the origins from its own cutoff to the next cutoff of the same cadence.

Verdict: partly supported. Prediction P1 held: L-1d beat L-3d, which beat L-Ww, and L-1d ended 0.07 to 0.09 behind K2-S1, inside the predicted 0.05 to 0.12 (the L-3d gains of 0.036 and 0.041 are inside the predicted 0.03 to 0.08). P2 held: L-Ww-30 did not beat L-Ww and its leak was larger. P3 failed: L-mix scored worse than L-Ww by 0.06 and 0.05, a result outside the predicted "less than 0.05 better".

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute CRPS (eight / six), five folds, two seeds. L-Ww 4.920 / 3.555; L-3d 4.883 / 3.513; L-1d 4.854 / 3.493; L-Ww-30 4.954 / 3.538; L-Ww-60 4.917 / 3.535; L-mix 4.981 / 3.599; K2-S1 4.763 / 3.423; A-pool 4.682 / 3.457.
  • Paired contrasts against L-Ww (Bonferroni interval, corrected for 56 tests). L-3d -0.036 [-0.058, -0.017] eight, -0.041 [-0.071, -0.019] six. L-1d -0.065 [-0.096, -0.038] eight, -0.061 [-0.104, -0.028] six. L-Ww-30 +0.035 [-0.010, +0.079] eight, -0.016 [-0.055, +0.022] six. L-Ww-60 -0.003 [-0.032, +0.025] eight, -0.020 [-0.039, -0.001] six. L-mix +0.062 [-0.015, +0.148] eight, +0.045 [+0.009, +0.081] six. L-1d minus L-3d -0.029 [-0.050, -0.009] eight, -0.020 [-0.041, -0.002] six. The minimum detectable effect with two seeds is 0.164 (eight) and 0.123 (six), experiment 510's values, so every gain here is below it: the intervals exclude zero because the contrasts are paired on the same rows, but a gain "of at least 0.05" is not established.
  • Gap to K2-S1 (unadjusted 95% block interval). L-1d +0.091 [+0.012, +0.168] eight, +0.071 [+0.005, +0.135] six; L-Ww +0.156 and +0.132. The unadjusted intervals exclude zero, but the Bonferroni intervals of L-1d and L-3d against K2-S1 include zero at both groups ([-0.039, +0.216] eight for L-1d), so the data do not rule out that the daily refit reaches K2-S1.
  • Decision rule for the daily refit. The point estimate and the Bonferroni interval pass at both groups. q99 pinball loss is 0.286 against 0.287 (eight) and 0.183 against 0.184 (six), inside +0.02. Cold winter nights: L-1d minus L-Ww -0.124 [-0.182, -0.069] eight, -0.060 [-0.103, -0.017] six, so no worse. The injected-shift leak is a reported trade-off (below). Twice weekly does not reach the -0.05 point estimate. L-Ww-30 and L-Ww-60 fail the rule, and L-mix is worse.
  • Horizon bands, L-1d minus L-Ww (eight / six). Day 1 -0.101 / -0.099; days 2 to 3 -0.087 / -0.068; days 4 to 10 -0.053 / -0.054; the 12 to 36 hour band -0.090 / -0.077. The gain is largest on the first day but reaches days 4 to 10, so the daily refit's new rows help beyond the short leads they reach directly.
  • Staleness curve (figure 2). CRPS rises about 0.02 points per day of model age in every arm (L-1d at the eight: 4.917 at age 0 to 5.062 at age 7). The curve is on the origins whose age-7 model exists in every fold, so its levels are higher than the headline. Experiment 510's L-M minus K2-S1 does not grow with the week of the month (0.46, 0.37, 0.41, 0.37, 0.16), so the curve alone does not isolate staleness from the weeks' differing weather.
  • Injected-shift leak (one seed, five folds, both signs; descriptive). L-1d: 7.2 points of capacity on the day after the block, 5.4, 5.1, 4.1, 3.2, 3.0, and 3.4 on the following days. L-Ww-30: 9.5, against 6.1 for experiment 510's L-Ww (range across folds 3.4 to 14.5). The weekly L-Ww-30 leaks 3.4 points more than L-Ww, so a shorter half-life makes the forecast follow an injected shift more closely. The daily refit's leak is larger the day after a bad block and fades within about 5 days.
  • Real events and holidays. Christmas week 2025, L-1d minus L-Ww: -0.162 [-0.261, -0.070] eight, -0.144 [-0.244, -0.045] six. The plan's noise floor for one Christmas is 0.27 at the eight and 0.26 at the six; both differences are smaller than it. The slice holds the 22 to 31 December target half-hours with no labelled event (22,580 rows at the six); the unsliced xmas_six set in contrasts.csv (28,800 rows) gives -0.234. For 1 to 14 January 2026 the differences are -0.069 [-0.119, -0.023] (eight) and -0.104 [-0.171, -0.029] (six).
  • Tails. q01 and q99 pinball loss and coverage are within 0.003 of L-Ww at both groups for L-1d and L-3d (largest gap: six-group q99 coverage, 0.9913 against 0.9891); see absolute.csv in the private data folder. Coverage of the 99% quantile is 0.995 (eight) and 0.991 (six).
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost at the six, f = 0.9 / 0.75 / 0.5. L-Ww 0.95 / 5.96 / 22.26; L-1d 0.73 / 5.47 / 21.43; K2-S1 1.90 / 8.43 / 26.94; manual_heuristic 2.02 / 12.88 / 37.79. L-1d minus manual_heuristic is -1.28 [-3.54, -0.07], -7.41 [-15.51, -2.17], and -16.36 [-28.27, -8.12]. L-1d minus K2-S1 is -1.17 [-3.30, -0.02] at f = 0.9 and includes zero at the other two.
  • D15 and D18 (report only). CRPS L-Ww 11.19, L-3d 11.00, L-1d 10.88, L-Ww-30 10.70, K2-S1 11.53, A-pool 10.65. L-Ww-30 and A-pool beat L-1d there, and L-1d is 0.17 behind A-pool at the eight on the main rows.
  • Warm start (L-1d-warm, seed 0, report-only). One epoch from the previous day's weights scored 0.018 [-0.013, +0.050] (eight) and 0.032 [+0.008, +0.057] (six) worse than a daily restart on seed 0, and +0.27 / +0.20 worse in Christmas week, which suggests errors accumulate in a warm start. Restart each day.
  • L-mix. The source flag is a 38th input; arm A already has lead and lead_sqrt inputs and the ERA5 and CAMS pseudo-runs carry real leads, so no lead input was added. Pretraining took 31 to 32 seconds per network. The mixed pretraining scored worse at the six (the eight interval includes zero), so the daily repeat (L-mix-1d) was not run.
  • Not run. L-1d-oldPT, because it is optional and experiment 494's PretrainOnce arm already tests stale pretraining.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Per group the absolute error of the median and of the mean forecast differ by at most 0.1, and median minus mean is -0.61 (eight) and -0.15 (six) for L-1d, the same as L-Ww (-0.61, -0.15). The mean-forecast error contrast L-1d minus L-Ww (6.380 against 6.447 at the eight, 4.998 against 5.074 at the six) has the sign and size of the median contrast.
  • Leak check. Printed before any fit: 0 rows past the valid-time or origin cut for every cutoff and half-life, and the scored windows tile each month and start at their own cutoff. The reused day-0 weights reproduce experiment 510's forecast exactly (maximum difference 0.0).
  • Reviews. One fresh Sonnet code review before the first fit, and one fresh Sonnet review of the results, the numbers, and the prose, whose findings are applied in this page. L-1d seed 1 is not scored alone: the headline pools both seeds, and the plan's separate replication was not computed.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Scale of the gain. The daily refit's gain (about 1.3% of CRPS) is below the two-seed minimum detectable effect; the paired intervals are narrow because the rows are shared, but the gain could depend on the five folds. Seed 1 of L-1d is the replication: both seeds are pooled in the headline.
  • Folds. Five test months of one year; only two of them are winter months.
  • Labelled events. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold events, and the event slices undercount.
  • Staleness. The staleness curve is on a subset of origins and mixes the effect of age with the weather of the later weeks.
  • Stress run. One seed and a fixed block; the leak differs threefold across folds, so the 1-point limit of the plan cannot be tested.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Refit daily over a full winter before any release claim, because the weeks that favour a fresher model come from few folds.
  • Test whether the daily gain survives when ENS rows arrive with the real publication delay in production.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Experiment 510 found that refitting the lag-free network weekly rather than monthly scored 0.17 to 0.19 points of CRPS better, and that the gain grew through the month (zero in week 1, about 0.35 by week 4). That pattern is a staleness effect. We ask whether refitting twice a week or every day closes more of the remaining gap to K2-S1, whether a 30-day or 60-day half-life does, and whether a pretraining that sees ENS rows as well as ERA5 and CAMS rows helps the weekly fine-tune. A fourth question, how stale the ERA5 and CAMS pretraining may be, is optional (L-1d-oldPT, below).

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms are lag-free (37 non-lag inputs, 3 mixture components, widened 1.15 at scoring), restart every fine-tune from the fold's pretrained weights (seeds 0 and 1), and train on ENS rows with valid time at most the cutoff minus 3.5 hours.

Arm Refit cadence Half-life Seeds Note L-3d twice weekly: days 0 and 3 of each 7-day block, 00:00 UTC (45 cutoffs over 5 folds) 90 days 0, 1 L-1d daily, 00:00 UTC (154 cutoffs) 90 days 0, 1 seed 1 is run unconditionally and reported alone as the replication L-Ww-30, L-Ww-60 weekly (25 cutoffs) 30, 60 days 0, 1 take the slot experiment 510 reserved for a 30/180-day sweep L-mix weekly 90 days 0, 1 mixed ERA5, CAMS, and ENS pretraining (below) L-1d-warm daily 90 days 0 gated and report-only (below) L-1d-oldPT daily 90 days 0 optional: only if L-1d beats L-Ww; not in the fit count References, not refitted L-M, L-W, L-Ww (experiment 510); K2-S1, A-pool (experiments 470, 454, 425)

Scoring window. Every model scores only the forecast origins from its own cutoff to the next cutoff of the same cadence (one day for daily, 3 or 4 days for twice weekly, one week for weekly, the whole month for monthly L-M). The windows tile the month, so each origin has one scoring model. The leak command prints the check, before any fit, that the windows tile each month and that no scored origin lies before its own cutoff.

Reuse. A fit whose cutoff day (0, 7, 14, 21, or 28) coincides with one of experiment 510's weekly L-Ww fits uses 510's saved weights, because the rows, the half-life, the seed, and the pretrained weights are identical. The window forecast is produced afresh. That saves 50 of L-3d's 90 fits and 50 of L-1d's 308.

L-mix. Pretrain on ERA5 and CAMS rows (source flag 0) and the fold's ENS rows (flag 1, rows from 2024-04) together, with each batch half from each source (4,096 + 4,096), so the fewer ENS rows are not swamped. Arm A already has a lead input: the lead and lead_sqrt columns, and the ERA5 and CAMS pseudo-runs of experiment 418 carry real leads of 0.5 to 351 hours. So the plan adds only the source-flag column (a 38th input) and keeps the existing lead inputs for both sources. Early stopping uses the mean of the held-out negative log-likelihood of the two sources. The fine-tune then uses ENS rows only (flag 1), weekly, with the 90-day half-life. The flag-1 pretraining rows must satisfy the same cut as the fine-tune rows (valid time at most the pretraining cut minus 3.5 hours, origin at most the cut); the pretrain-mix command prints and asserts the check before fitting. If L-mix passes its rule, it is repeated daily (L-mix-1d).

L-1d-warm (defined before running). Continue from the previous day's weights for one epoch (20% of the training rows, as in experiment 510's harness) at the fine-tune learning rate, with a fresh optimiser each day and no early stopping. The first cutoff of a fold starts from the pretrained weights and is the full L-1d fine-tune; nothing chains across folds. Run it only if L-1d beats L-Ww (seed 0, report-only).

L-1d-oldPT. Optional; run only if L-1d beats L-Ww. Experiment 494's PretrainOnce arm already tests stale pretraining. If run, it ships the old fold's standardiser and per-Primary target statistics with the old weights.

docs.title: Fit counts and cost
docs.text:
• New fine-tunes: L-3d 40, L-1d 258, L-Ww-30 and L-Ww-60 100, injected-shift stress 80, L-mix 50: 528 fine-tunes, plus 10 mixed pretrainings.
  • Timed cost: a daily fine-tune takes 2.5 to 3 seconds of training (the first one 7.8 seconds) and 0.15 seconds of row selection, because each month's rows are built once and held on the GPU. About 1 GPU-hour in all, with the staleness inference. One GPU process under 8 GB.
  • Gated, not counted: L-1d-warm up to 154 fits and L-mix-1d 154 per seed.

docs.title: Scoring and contrasts
docs.text:
• Staleness curve. Score each origin with the model refit k days earlier (k = 0 to 7), for every arm. This is inference only, and works for daily refits. Beside it, report experiment 510's L-M minus K2-S1 by week of the month (0.46, 0.37, 0.41, 0.37, 0.16), which does not grow with the week, so staleness is not isolated, and 510's L-Ww minus L-W of +0.07 in weeks 1 and 2 at the eight. Say which horizon bands a daily refit can affect: the newest daily rows reach only short leads.
  • Contrasts (paired, same seeds and pretrained weights). L-3d, L-1d, L-Ww-30, and L-Ww-60 against L-Ww (4); L-1d against L-3d (1); each of the four against K2-S1 and A-pool (8); L-mix against L-Ww (1). That is 14 contrasts, at the eight and the six, so 28 CRPS tests (56 with q99 pinball loss). Bonferroni count: 28 for CRPS. Absolute scores are reported beside every contrast.
  • Minimum detectable effect. Experiment 510's two-seed values: 0.164 at the eight and 0.123 at the six (from its mde_k2.csv).
  • Rows. Rows with no labelled event (NGED's event labels are incomplete), days 1 to 10, the 12 to 36 hour band, and the horizon bands day 1, days 2 to 3, and days 4 to 10.
  • Injected-shift leak. Experiment 510's stress run (a 7-day shift of 3 times the standard deviation of a Primary's 7-day mean target, both signs) for L-1d and L-Ww-30 only, one seed, five folds (about 80 fits). For L-Ww-30 the block ends at the day-14 cutoff as in 510. For L-1d the block is fixed (days 7 to 14 of the month) and the daily refits at days 14 to 20 are compared with their uninjected fits, so the leak is reported by the age of the block (0 to 6 days). Descriptive: 510's L-Ww leak ranges from 3.4 to 14.5 points across folds, so the 1-point limit cannot be tested and is reported as a trade-off beside the score gain of every arm.
  • Other slices. Rows inside labelled events against NRA-corrected actuals (sensitivity), Christmas week 22 to 31 December 2025 and 1 to 14 January 2026 per arm (noise floor 0.26 at the six and 0.27 at the eight for one Christmas), cold winter nights, q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage and pinball loss, the widening sweep 1.0 to 1.15, avoidable-curtailment cost at f = 0.9, 0.75, 0.5 at the signed-MW six. D15 and D18 are report-only.
  • Production cost per arm. Fits per day, seconds per fit, stored ensemble rows, pretraining cadence, and networks per serving pass (1 for every arm).

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
• More frequent refit worth porting: contrast against L-Ww with a Bonferroni interval excluding zero and a point estimate of at most -0.05 at the six or the eight, q99 pinball loss within +0.02, cold winter nights no worse than +0.05. The leak is reported as a trade-off (its 1-point limit cannot be tested).
  • Shorter half-life worth porting: the same terms, against L-Ww.
  • L-mix adopted: L-mix minus L-Ww with an interval excluding zero and a point estimate of at most -0.05 at either group, and q99 pinball within +0.02.
  • Stale pretraining acceptable (if L-1d-oldPT is run): not shown worse than L-1d by 0.03.
  • No arm within 0.1 of K2-S1: say so and state the distance; the choice between a simpler first release and the 4-network lagged mixture is the maintainer's.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 (through experiment 428's rows); stored references reused (L-M, L-W, L-Ww, K2-S1, A-pool, BG2, climatology, manual_heuristic) on the same rows; seed 0 and 1 averaged by quantile as in 510; July 2026 unused; no XGBoost work; widening 1.15. Schedule: the refit cadences are the experiment's subject. Titles say "load-shift", never "switching".

docs.title: Implementation details (deleted when this ships)
docs.text: Code in ml-experiments/00511-.../: e00511_common.py (cadences, the month's rows on the GPU), e00511_fit.py (leak, time, pretrain-mix, fit, assemble, stale). Experiment 510's harness is imported; its weekly offsets are hard-coded, so this folder adds cadence-aware cutoffs, windows, and a build_month that extends rows to the last daily cutoff.

docs.title: Does a second December (2024, with only 7 months of ensemble history) show the same weekly-refit and recency-weight gains for the lag-free demand network?
docs.text:
A second December (2024) shows the same direction as experiment 510 for the weekly refit at the six signed-MW Primaries, but not at the eight MVA-only Primaries. In Christmas week 2024 the weekly refit scored 0.704 points of continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) better than the monthly refit at the six (0.28 better in 2025) and 0.018 better at the eight (0.31 better in 2025). The 90-day recency weight scored 0.121 points better than the 182.6-day weight at the six and 0.005 worse at the eight (interval includes zero).

Experiment 510 refitted the lag-free demand neural network (it reads no lagged power) every month (L-M) or every week (L-W), with a recency weight whose half-life is 182.6 days, or every week with a 90-day half-life (L-Ww). Its months had at least 12 months of archived ECMWF ensemble (ENS) forecasts to fine-tune on. This page runs the same harness, unchanged, on December 2024, where only 7 months of ENS forecasts exist before the first refit (the stored data begins on 2024-05-01). Pretraining on ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather was repeated for this fold with two seeds. There is no K2-S1 or A-pool for this month, so the page compares each arm only with the other arms. Scores are in points of effective capacity (the rated capacity of a Primary; one point is 1%) of each Primary's capacity), over all rows that have an actual reading, with no filter for labelled events. "The eight" are the eight Primaries that report only apparent power in megavolt-amperes; "the six" are the six that report signed megawatts.

Verdict: partly supported. The weekly refit beat the monthly refit over the month at both groups, with the six gain larger than the minimum detectable effect of 0.123 that experiment 510 found for five folds; the 90-day weight helped only at the six.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Setup. Fold 2024-12, five weekly refits (days 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29), seeds 0 and 1, widening 1.15, 3-component lag-free network with experiment 448's pretraining recipe. Leak check: 0 rows past any cut. About 20 fine-tunes. The rows are 119,040 half-hours at the eight and 89,280 at the six.
  • CRPS over the whole month (points). Eight: L-M 5.772, L-W 5.662, L-Ww 5.659. Six: L-M 4.695, L-W 4.358, L-Ww 4.277.
  • Contrasts (points; 95% origin-day block bootstrap, no multiplicity correction).
Contrast Eight Six L-W minus L-M, whole month -0.110 [-0.215, -0.026] -0.336 [-0.465, -0.209] L-Ww minus L-W, whole month -0.002 [-0.036, +0.033] -0.081 [-0.126, -0.040] L-W minus L-M, Christmas week -0.018 [-0.085, +0.055] -0.704 [-0.810, -0.587] L-Ww minus L-W, Christmas week +0.005 [-0.007, +0.016] -0.121 [-0.165, -0.092]
  • Two Christmas weeks. Christmas week is valid time 22 to 31 December. Experiment 510's December 2025 values, on all rows, were: L-W minus L-M -0.31 at the eight and -0.28 at the six; L-Ww minus L-W -0.47 and -0.24. Experiment 510's brief put the noise floor of a single Christmas week at about 0.26 (six) to 0.27 (eight) points. The six-group gains of both Christmases lie above that floor, and the eight-group gain of 2024 lies below it.
  • Week of the month (origin days). L-W minus L-M is exactly 0 in days 1 to 7, because the first weekly fit is the monthly fit. At the six it is +0.004, -0.860, -0.391, and -0.565 in days 8 to 14, 15 to 21, 22 to 28, and 29 to 31; at the eight -0.043, -0.119, +0.049 (interval includes zero), and -0.879. L-Ww minus L-W is +0.143 (eight) and +0.078 (six) in days 1 to 7: with 7 months of history, the 90-day weight scored worse in the first week, and better in days 8 to 28 at the six (not in days 29 to 31).
  • Not scored here. Tail coverage, avoidable-curtailment cost, and event rows. No labelled-event filter was applied, so the numbers include any event in the month.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Leak check. The harness printed 0 rows past any cut for every refit and variant before any fit.
  • Week-1 identity. L-M and L-W agree exactly for origins in days 1 to 7, as in experiment 510.
  • Review. One Sonnet review of the page against the score table.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One fold is one December. The intervals are origin-day block bootstraps, ignore dependence across days, and are not corrected for multiplicity.
  • The ENS history is 7 months, against at least 12 for experiment 510's folds. The gains may be larger or smaller for that reason, and this page cannot separate that from the month.
  • The rows include labelled events and use no event filter, unlike experiment 510's headline rows. The December 2025 comparison values are from experiment 510's Christmas slices (rowset main16, all classes of row).
  • This adds a second Christmas for the weekly-versus-monthly and recency contrasts. It adds nothing for the comparison of the lag-free candidate with K2-S1, because K2-S1 does not exist for this month.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows treated as clean may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Refit K2-S1 weekly as well, to test whether the weekly gain is specific to lag-free networks.
  • Give December 2024 a longer fine-tuning history from the ENS backfill (2021-03 to 2024-03), to separate the effect of 7 months of history from the effect of the month.

docs.title: Can the lag-free demand network use the whole-day electricity price shape at training time to forecast better, when no price exists at serving time?
docs.text: We asked whether a demand neural network forecasts better if it is shown the electricity price of the whole day during training, because batteries and gas engines behind a substation follow the price. We gave the network the exact price shape of each day, as 10 numbers such as the day's cheapest and dearest half-hours and the evening-minus-overnight spread, at both training and scoring. The oracle test is an upper bound, because no price exists when we forecast days 2 to 10. The network did not forecast better by an amount we can resolve: its error changed by +0.037 points of capacity at the eight Primaries that report only apparent power and by -0.048 at the six that report signed megawatts (intervals include zero), where the minimum detectable effect is about 0.17 points.
