A shuffled day's shape and the shape of national demand minus wind did no better. All numbers are interim and unaudited until the reviews are recorded in the pull request.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Setup. Five folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0, 1, and 2, rows of experiment 470 with no labelled event, widening 1.15. The scoring mask excludes the half-hours of price-missing days. None of the 1,145,256 half-hours of the five months' base rows (before the scorer's own filters) falls on one, so the mask removed no row.
  • Minimum detectable effect of a 3-seed mean (four arms pooled). 0.176 at the eight and 0.168 at the six.
  • CRPS contrasts (points; Bonferroni count 12; negative favours the first arm).
Contrast Eight Six PO minus P0 (oracle) +0.037 [-0.037, +0.118] -0.048 [-0.100, +0.004] PP minus P0 (placebo) +0.057 [+0.017, +0.101] +0.018 [-0.005, +0.040] PN minus P0 (national) +0.054 [-0.008, +0.118] -0.003 [-0.060, +0.055] PO minus PP -0.020 [-0.068, +0.031] -0.065 [-0.112, -0.017] PO minus PN -0.017 [-0.086, +0.048] -0.045 [-0.098, +0.013]
  • Absolute CRPS (points). Eight: P0 5.150, PO 5.187, PP 5.207, PN 5.204. Six: P0 3.741, PO 3.693, PP 3.758, PN 3.738.
  • Per fold (PO minus P0). Eight: +0.001, +0.244, +0.015, +0.081, -0.201 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). Six: +0.089, -0.191, -0.085, +0.103, -0.181. Five month blocks give near min-to-max intervals, and the signs are mixed.
  • Stop rule. Neither group's point estimate reaches minus the minimum detectable effect, and the six's interval includes zero, so P-drop, P-aux, and P-teach did not run.
  • Known-asset Primaries (D2, D5, D8, D9, D11, D14) against the others, oracle minus control. Eight: +0.059 against -0.003. Six: -0.027 against -0.089.
  • Horizon bands, oracle minus control. Eight: +0.059 (day 1), +0.053 (days 2 to 3), -0.011 (days 4 to 10). Six: +0.014, -0.020, -0.065.
  • Evening peak and overnight. The six's overnight half-hours gain -0.134 against -0.025 for the rest, one slice of many and not corrected for the number of slices.
  • Predictions. P1 held at the six (-0.048, inside 0.00 to 0.06) and did not hold at the eight, where the oracle was worse by an unresolved +0.037. P2 and P3 did not apply, because the oracle did not pass the stop rule. P4 is reported as a descriptive slice, uncorrected for the number of slices.
  • Christmas week 2025 and the report-only rows (descriptive; not gating). In the 2025-12 fold's Christmas week the oracle scored -0.459 [-0.502, -0.414] at the eight and -0.417 [-0.491, -0.311] at the six against the control, while the placebo scored -0.182 and -0.039 and the national control +0.309 and -0.284. One Christmas week is a single event, and the 2025-12 fold's full-month eight score was +0.244 worse. The report-only rows (D15 and D18 included) scored +0.190 [-0.336, +0.702] for the oracle, with +3.02 in the 2026-03 fold, so the interval is wide.
  • Interim timing run. A single-fold, single-seed run (2025-10, seed 0, pinball loss) scored all three shape arms better than the control; five folds and three seeds did not reproduce that.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: The plan below was written before any fit that produced a quoted number. The plan covers Part 1 of the brief (the price shape) only; whether the 0/1 lockdown flag is still needed is a separate experiment.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
Batteries charge when the electricity price is low and discharge when it is high, and a gas engine runs when the price is high. We know the price of the whole delivery day exactly when we train, and we know none of it when we forecast days 2 to 10. We ask whether a lag-free demand neural network that is shown the day's price shape during training forecasts better than one that is not. The first test is an upper bound, the oracle, which sees the true shape at training and at scoring. It is never deployable. If the oracle shows no gain that the placebo and national controls do not already explain, no training-time-only variant can recover a gain, and the experiment stops there.

The idea comes from the maintainer. The lag-free network is that of experiments 448 and 510, pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS rows and fine-tuned monthly on ensemble forecast rows. Among experiments 10, 15, 25, 437, 476, and 510, none tested a forward whole-day price shape for demand: experiment 25's shape columns look back 24 hours only.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms use experiment 510's L-M recipe (monthly refit, 182.6-day half-life weight, 3 mixture components, hidden width 64, 2 layers, dropout 0.1) with the same rows, loop, folds, and seeds. Every arm, the control included, is pretrained by this experiment's own script, so the arms differ in their input columns and nothing else. The shape columns widen the input from 37 to 48, so the pretrained weights of experiment 448 do not load, and no new column is zero-initialised.

Arm Extra input columns (11) What it tests P0 none The control. PO The 10 shape features and a missing flag, from the true Market Index price of the target half-hour's local day, at training and scoring. Upper bound: does the true day shape help at all? PP The same columns of a seeded other day of the same calendar month, day type, and length (the shuffled-day placebo). What a typical shape for that kind of day gives. PN The same 10 features of national demand minus national wind, of the target local day. What realised national state gives: the realised price encodes realised national demand, wind, and weather error. P-drop, P-aux, P-teach Conditional on the stop rule; defined below. Whether the oracle's gain survives with no price at serving time.

The oracle is an upper bound on the information in the realised national state, not a battery result. A passing oracle that PN matches means the realised national state helps, not that batteries do.

docs.title: The 10 shape features
docs.text:
A delivery day is a local settlement day (Europe/London midnight to midnight, so it starts at 23:00 UTC in summer) and has 46, 48, or 50 half-hours. Every feature uses only the target day's own values: there is no trailing, centred, or multi-day mean. Six features vary per half-hour and four are constant within the day.

  • Per half-hour: rank (position within the day, scaled 0 to 1), minus_mean (value minus the day's mean), hours_from_min (signed hours since the day's minimum, divided by 12), hours_to_max (signed hours until the day's maximum, divided by 12), cheapest_4h and dearest_4h (1 on the 8 lowest and the 8 highest half-hours of the day).
  • Per day: day_min, day_max, day_spread (maximum minus minimum), and evening_minus_overnight (mean of the 16:00 to 19:00 local half-hours minus the mean of the 00:00 to 05:00 local half-hours).
  • Dropped from the brief's list: the slope-sign-change count (noise on half-hourly data) and the day's mean relative to a 7-day mean (it needs a multi-day mean).
  • Scaling: the level features (minus_mean, day_min, day_max, day_spread, evening_minus_overnight) are z-scored with the mean and standard deviation of the non-missing half-hours before the fold's refit, so a test month never sets its own scale.

Price source. market_index.parquet is the Elexon Market Index (provider APXMIDP), not verifiably the day-ahead price; N2EX day-ahead exists only from 2025-09. Rows are deduplicated on (time, dataProvider), and rows with zero volume count as missing.

Missing-price days. A day with any missing half-hour is a missing day: its ten shape columns are 0 and its missing flag is 1, in training and at scoring. The grid holds 2,527 local days; the checks print how many are missing (101 for price, 50 for the national series). The scored rows exclude the half-hours of missing days, for every arm, so the contrasts stay paired on one row set; the number of excluded half-hours is reported.

Shuffled-day placebo. Each non-missing day takes the shape of another non-missing day with the same calendar month (any year), the same day type (Monday to Friday, Saturday, Sunday), and the same length in half-hours. Days of one group are shuffled once with a seeded generator (seed = 513) and each takes the next day in that order, so a donor is never the day itself and is used once. The same draw serves training and scoring. A group of one day, and every missing day, takes the missing flag. The checks print the number of unmatched days (3, 2, 2, 2, and 1 in the five folds).

National control. The same 10 features of national demand outturn (INDO) minus FUELHH wind generation, per half-hour, so they describe the day's residual demand shape.

docs.title: Folds, seeds, and cost
docs.text:
• Folds and seeds. The five folds of experiments 448, 449, and 510 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0, 1, and 2. July 2026 is unused.
  • Fit count. Four arms, five folds, and three seeds give 60 pretrainings and 60 fine-tunings, above the brief's cap of 30 to 45 pretrainings, because the control is re-pretrained too. All three shape arms run before the stop rule is read, as the brief's core cap requires; running P0 and PO first would halve the cost and give the same stop-rule verdict. The conditional arms add about 55 pretrainings and 55 fine-tunings (one at a time, if the stop rule passes).
  • Timed cost. One fold, seed 0, all four arms: feeder 13 s (rows and shape tables), pretraining 17 to 24 s per arm, fine-tune 3 to 6 s, so about 2 minutes per fold and seed and 0.4 GPU-hours for the 60 pretrainings and 60 fine-tunings. One GPU process under 8 GB, with MemoryMax=8G and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.

docs.title: Scoring and contrasts
docs.text:
• Rows and scorer. Experiment 510's pipeline on experiment 470's row set (experiment_470_intersection_v1), rows with no labelled event, leads up to 10 days, forecast quantiles raw (no widening). "The eight" are the eight Primaries that report only apparent power (D15 and D18 report-only); "the six" are the six that report signed megawatts.
  • Contrasts (negative favours the first arm). Gating, against P0: PO, PP, PN, and, if run, P-drop, P-aux, P-teach (6 contrasts at 2 groups, so 12 CRPS tests: Bonferroni count 12; the family of the whole price-and-lockdown brief is 18 with Part 2's 6). Descriptive, at the same interval width: PO minus PP and PO minus PN.
  • Minimum detectable effect. From the seed spread of the four arms pooled (three seeds, five folds), printed by e00513_score.py baseline before any contrast. A seed spread cannot exist before any fit, so this replaces the brief's "before any fit". The minimum detectable effect is scaled to a 3-seed mean. Experiments 448 to 510 report 0.057 to 0.164 points, so a pooled pass of 0.05 or less is unlikely to be resolved: the price terms are 3 to 5% of the error at the one Primary where they were measured.
  • Intervals. Month-block bootstrap with five blocks gives near min-to-max intervals; the page says so and gives the sign per fold beside every interval.
  • Slices. Per Primary and by half-hour of day, with the Primaries that have a known battery or gas engine (D2, D5, D8, D9, D11, D14) against the other Primaries; evening-peak and overnight half-hours against the rest; horizon bands day 1, days 2 to 3, and days 4 to 10 beside days 1 to 10; the half-hours of missing price days are excluded and counted. A pooled gain at Primaries with no known asset is a leak check, not a finding. The chart of the oracle gain by Primary and by half-hour of day uses the OCF palette and no mark in the background colour.

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
• Stop rule. Continue to P-drop and P-aux only if, at either group, the Bonferroni interval of PO minus P0 excludes zero and its point estimate is at most minus the 3-seed minimum detectable effect. Otherwise stop and report.
  • Printed test count. The scorer prints 10 counted tests (it counts the two descriptive contrasts); the Bonferroni family stays 12.
  • Missing flags. PO and PP carry the missing flag on the 101 days without a price; PN carries it on the 50 days without a national series. The scoring mask uses the price-missing days only, for every arm.
  • Reading a passing oracle. If PN or PP reproduces at least 0.75 of the oracle's gain at a group, call that gain a national-state or day-type effect. A battery reading needs the oracle to beat both, at the Primaries with a known asset.
  • P-drop (conditional). The shape columns plus a missing flag as inputs. Training hides the shape (flag on, columns zero) on a random 50% to 100% of the days, the fraction drawn per batch. Scoring always sends the flag as missing, so the serving input is constant.
  • P-aux (conditional). No price input. An extra 10-output head predicts the day's standardised shape features from the network's own inputs, with a loss weight tuned on folds 2025-10 and 2026-01 only and scored on the other three folds, or a fixed grid of weights reported in full and counted in the Bonferroni family.
  • P-teach (demoted). Runs only if the oracle passes and P-drop and P-aux both fail to recover its gain, and only after asking the manager, because it needs the Discuss session's approval. A teacher per fold and seed, equal hidden widths (64) for teacher and student.
  • Excluded (maintainer ruling). No price and no predicted price shape at serving time.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 start cut (through experiment 428's rows); rows with no labelled event; July 2026 unused; no XGBoost work; metered generators are not shown (this experiment scores substations); titles say "load-shift", never "switching"; every interim number is unaudited.

docs.title: Can a small calibrated classifier give each Primary half-hour a probability of sitting inside a load-shift event, using only data before a refit?
docs.text:
A calibrated probability of "this half-hour is inside a load-shift event" can be built from four signals, but it is weak: pulses as large as the series' own spread are found a quarter of the time, and real rows keep nearly full weight. The expected calibration error is 0.008 to 0.022 on the four held-out axes at 7% of rows inside a pulse, so a probability of 0.3 means about 30%. The recall of injected pulses of at least 1 times the spread that last at least 6 hours is 0.27, against a pre-registered 0.8. A Sonnet results review re-derived the headline numbers and agreed with all of them.

We asked whether a small calibrated classifier, trained on injected pulses and hard negatives and fed four signals (a step at each end, a return to the earlier level, edges at the same times in other series, and the symmetry of the sizes), gives each Primary half-hour a probability of sitting inside a load-shift event, using only data before a refit. The classifier is a depth-3 decision tree chosen over a logistic regression on validation Brier score (0.0300 against 0.0314). It is recalibrated per row and prior-shifted to 7% of rows inside a pulse. "The six" are the signed-MW Primaries D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16; "the eight" are the MVA-only Primaries D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22; D15 and D18 are in neither group. The fifth fold of experiment 511 (2025-12) has no experiment 507 table and is dropped, so the tables cover 4 folds and 123 daily cutoffs, not 154. Experiment 510's binary mask of labelled events cost CRPS (+0.079 at the eight, +0.032 at the six) and could not speak on the leak, so a soft weight is untested; this page does not test it.

Verdict: partly supported. P1 held, P3 held, P4 held for g = 1 and narrowly failed for g = 2, P5 held, and P6 held (trivially, because p is low almost everywhere). P2 failed (recall 0.27 against 0.8) and P7 failed. The pre-registered hand-off rule stops the tables here, because the recall is under 0.5 and the Brier skill is under 0.20 on two of four held-out axes at 7%; the manager decides.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Checks run before any number. The perturbation check replaced every residual at or after the cut with noise and rebuilt the whole chain: the largest difference in p was 0.0 at cutoff days 3, 10, and 20 of 2026-01 (about 1.78 million rows checked each). A full recompute at the same cutoffs changed 863, 1,371, and 2,157 rows older than the 45-day recompute window (under 0.12% of rows).
  • Calibration (row level, 7% prevalence; bootstrap over Primary-months, 300 resamples). Expected calibration error and Brier skill: held-out seeds 0.008 (0.003 to 0.017) and 0.198; months 0.013 (0.005 to 0.022) and 0.240; shapes 0.014 (0.008 to 0.021) and 0.217; Primaries 0.022 (0.012 to 0.034) and 0.162. Training worlds 0.012 and validation worlds 0.008 are fit statistics. At 2% (the intercept shifted by the change in log-odds) the errors are 0.003 to 0.009 and the skill 0.13, 0.16, 0.16, and 0.045 (the last with an interval from -0.05 to 0.11).
  • Recall at p of 0.5 or more, injected grid (2,880 pulses of at least 1 times the spread and 6 hours). 0.27 (0.23 to 0.29); the six 0.22, the eight 0.34. By size: 0.5 times, 0.000; 1 times, 0.001; 2 times, 0.16 (0.11 to 0.20); 3 times, 0.48 (0.42 to 0.54). By duration: 1 hour and 6 hours, 0.000; 1 day, 0.17; 3 days, 0.30; 14 days, 0.33. Shape makes no difference (0.16, 0.16, and 0.16 for box, circuit, and own-shaped). 1,200 pulses per size and 960 per duration.
  • False flags. On 164 Primary-years of worlds with no injection: 0.14 runs of p of 0.5 or more per Primary-year (0.08 to 0.20), 2.3 at p of 0.3 or more. The brief's limit of 2 per Primary-year is reached at p of 0.3, where recall is lower than the 0.27 above. Experiment 456's 1.74 false steps per Primary-year used a daily 7-day scan and does not transfer.
  • Genuine level changes. Of rows from day 15 after an injected step with no return (196 worlds, held-out months), 0.0% reach p of 0.5.
  • Real rows with no labelled event (4 folds, daily cutoffs). 0.4% to 0.7% of rows have p of 0.5 or more. The mean weight (1 - p)^g is 0.94 for g = 1 and 0.89 to 0.90 for g = 2 (P4 asked for at least 0.90: it held at g = 1 and fell short at g = 2 by 0.002 to 0.006). The Kish effective sample size is 99% of the row count at both g, with recency weights 99% to 100% of the recency-only value. The weight is below 0.5 on 0.4% to 0.6% (g = 1) and 2.3% to 2.8% (g = 2) of rows. The floor p of an uncovered row (about 0.04 after the 7% prior shift) alone holds the mean weight below 0.96.
  • Labelled events (report only). The area under the curve of mean p on the labelled events against matched rows with no labelled event is 0.67 (0.61 to 0.73) for fold 2026-06 (100 events, 500 matched windows, 60 day blocks) and 0.65 (0.59 to 0.71) for fold 2026-03 (99 events); a lower bound. Mean p is 0.16 on events and 0.06 on matched windows.
  • D8 and D22 dips (report only). p stays under 0.5 on all scored rows (10:00 to 15:00 only) of D8's 16 unexplained dip days (fold 2026-06) and of D22's dip days (9 fall in the window). The dip rows were set to missing in every training world, so this check cannot fail; training D8's 22 engine-explained dips before 2025-07 as hard negatives makes this expected for D8.
  • Experiment 511's national same-sign shift (extrapolation test; P7 predicted under 30%). The share of shifted rows with p of 0.5 or more is 0.00 to 0.01 on the day the block ends and 0.48 to 0.58, 0.58 to 0.70, and 0.65 to 0.82 on the following three days (4 folds). The shift is picked up only once the return is missing, as an unreturned step.
  • Mask table and thresholds. Written at p of 0.5 or more, with tier, size, shape correlation, open flag, and the cutoff it is valid for; thresholds that flag 5% and 7% of unlabelled rows are 0.17 and 0.07 to 0.11. Flagging 1% or 2% is not possible (p has a tie plateau at 0.31). SHA-256 sums of the tables are in work/sha256.txt.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reviews. Sonnet plan review (27 findings; accepted except one, the number of reviews); Sonnet code review 1 (12 findings, fixed before any number was read); Sonnet code review 2 (11 findings; 9 fixed or answered, and the worlds, classifier, and every table were rebuilt before the numbers above; not taken: the held-out Primaries still act as partners in every world, which the plan now says); results review (re-derived calibration, recall, false flags, weights, and the area under the curve with independent code; no disagreement beyond bootstrap noise; no leakage between train, validation, and held-out months).
  • Selection history. A first fit ran before the second review. Its held-out numbers were seen (skill 0.14 to 0.18, recall 0.05). The second review's fixes (time-disjoint windows, detectable recipients, held-out dip days made missing in every world) changed the worlds, and the classifier was refit once with no feature or setting changed. No tuning followed any held-out number.
  • Triggers. The classifier is a depth-3 tree, so no median-minus-mean forecast check applies; no forecast is scored.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Only the held-out months set is time-disjoint from training; the held-out seeds, shapes, and Primaries share real background rows with training worlds. The minimum detectable effect belongs to the fine-tune experiment (no contrasts here, Bonferroni count 0).
  • Calibration is against injected truth. Real residuals hold unlabelled events, so a high-score candidate that counts as a false flag may be a real load shift: candidates scoring 6 to 10 noise units were injected pulses only 24% of the time.
  • NGED's labels are incomplete; the area under the curve is a lower bound and real-event slices undercount.
  • The classifier runs at each refit and needs the lag-free residual series at that time; weights are training-time only.
  • Held-out months are 2025-01 to 2025-06 only; July 2026 is unused.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Raise recall at 2 false flags per Primary-year before using p as a weight: a return-to-level score that uses the shape of the step, or a partner signal restricted to neighbours, are the two signals not yet exploited.
  • If the manager still wants the soft-weight fine-tune, run it with the injected-shift leak as the only gate; the real rows would change by about 6% in weight at g = 1.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Experiment 510 masked the NGED-labelled load-shift events from the training rows of the lag-free demand network and scored 0.079 points of CRPS worse at the eight MVA-only Primaries and 0.032 worse at the six signed-MW Primaries (dropping 6.0% to 7.6% of rows; Bonferroni intervals exclude zero). Its leak of an injected shift was 6.18 points of capacity against 6.11 without the mask, but that null holds by construction: the injected shift carries no label, so a label mask cannot touch it. A binary mask therefore showed a cost for dropping rows and said nothing about the leak. A soft weight might do better, because a false flag at weight 0.1 costs less than a dropped row. The soft weight needs a probability that each half-hour sits inside a load-shift event. This experiment builds that probability from data before the refit, calibrates it on injected pulses, and freezes it. A second experiment will then use the frozen tables as weights in a lag-free fine-tune.

docs.title: Data and residual series
docs.text:
• Source. Experiment 507's lagless mixture tables (work/lagless_era5_mixture/month=2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06, seed 0; each holds 16 Primaries from 2019-09 to the month's refit as crossfit rows, then 62 days of further rows). The residual of a Primary is the cleaned power over effective capacity (experiment 510's clean_stack, flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01) minus q50. The scaled residual z divides by the Primary's median band half-width (q95 - q05) / 2 over its crossfit rows. The spread s of a Primary is 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of z over those rows. At the eight, the series is apparent power, so the sign of a shift cannot be recovered across zero (reported by group).
  • Folds and cutoffs. The four folds are 2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. The fifth fold of experiment 511 (2025-12) has no 507 table. This experiment drops it and says so. Rebuilding it costs 7 fits (GPU) and is left to the fine-tune experiment. The cutoffs are every day at 00:00 UTC of each fold month (123 cutoffs: 31 + 31 + 31 + 30); the 25 weekly cutoffs (days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 over 5 folds) are a subset, of which 20 exist.
  • Causality. At the cutoff c the detector sees z only for half-hours at least 3.5 hours before c (experiment 510's cut). A script perturbs every z at or after the cutoff and checks that the stored p is unchanged, and prints the check before any other number. Every fold's scale statistics (spread, noise scales of the scan) come from the residual history before that fold's refit.
  • Built-in steps. Each fold table has a junction between crossfit and further rows and five internal edges between the six cross-fit blocks (experiment 507's leaks.csv found 1 to 9 Primaries with a junction jump above the usual q90). Each cross-fit block is centred on its own median (history only). The junction is detrended causally at each cutoff by matching the median of the first up to 7 observed days after it to the 7 days before, and when fewer than 2 days of further rows exist the rows after the junction are left out of the detector. The report counts the flags that touch a junction or edge (within 1 day).
  • Partner series. The other 15 Primaries (scaled residuals) and the 4 bulk and grid supply points (the power minus its median over the same half-hour of the 4 earlier weeks, a causal profile difference, because no lagless forecast exists for them).

docs.title: The detector
docs.text:
• Candidate pulses. For each Primary and each duration d in {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 672} half-hours (1 hour to 14 days) and each start a, compare the mean z inside [a, a+d) with the mean in the flank before and the flank after (f = clip(d, 12, 336) half-hours each). Signal 1 (step) is the size of each edge, scaled by the robust noise of that statistic over the fold's history; a ramp of up to 4 half-hours is allowed because the edge is a difference of means. Signal 2 (return) is the closed-pulse score min(|edge_in|, |edge_out|) with the same sign at both edges, and the return ratio |after - before| / min(|edge_in|, |edge_out|). Candidates above a low admission score are thinned by greedy suppression of overlapping spans.
  • Open pulses. A pulse whose end is not yet observed at the cutoff (no flank after, or fewer than 4 half-hours of it) is scored as an open step from its start to the cutoff, for starts within the last 672 half-hours. It enters the classifier with an open flag, so a step in the last 14 days is scored high by training, not by hand. A step with no return for 30 days or more has a closed score near zero and is reported as "unreturned". It is not masked.
  • Signal 3 (synchrony). For each candidate, count the partner series with an edge of the opposite sign within 2 half-hours (1 hour) of its start, of its end, and of both, with the partner edge scaled by its own history. Count the same-sign edges too, because a same-sign edge in many series at one time is a weather or data artefact. A shifted-date placebo (partner series shifted by 7 to 60 days) gives the chance rate of the counts.
  • Signal 4 (symmetry). For a candidate with a synchronised partner, compare the size of the donor's change in MW with the sum of the partners' changes in MW (log of the ratio of magnitudes). Experiment 459 found a median leak share of 0.53 against a placebo of 0.54, so this is a low-power signal, reported against the placebo and never used alone.
  • Shape correlation. For candidates of 24 half-hours or more, the correlation of the pulse's residual with the Primary's own median daily profile over the 28 days before. It is a feature and a column of the mask table.
  • Tiers. Tier A: a candidate with a synchronised partner (both edges) and a symmetry ratio inside a stated tolerance. Tier B: a single-series pulse. Tier A symmetry is a diagnostic and does not gate tier A (the tolerance and the tier shares are reported, not tuned).
  • Classifier. A logistic regression on the standardised feature set (log score, log duration, open flag, return ratio, edge asymmetry, amplitude, counts of opposite-sign and same-sign partner edges at start, end, and both, symmetry ratio and its flag, shape correlation) and a depth-3 tree on the same features. The choice between them is made on the validation worlds' Brier score. The chosen model is recalibrated with a one-variable Platt fit on those validation worlds. No neural network. The row probability is the largest candidate probability that covers the row (0 if no candidate does). A candidate is a positive if at least half of its rows lie inside an injected pulse.

docs.title: Series-level injector
docs.text:
Not experiment 507's window-level generator (its pull request has not cleared review). A world is a 60-day window of all 20 series built from real residual history, with a random cutoff inside the window.

  • Pulses. Sizes from 0.4 to 3.5 times the donor's spread (log-uniform), durations from 2 to 672 half-hours (log-uniform), both signs, 1 to 4 per world, with a ramp of up to 4 half-hours at each edge. Shapes: constant-MW box, own-demand-shaped, and (held out from training) circuit-profile (a random daily profile with morning and evening bumps or an Economy 7 night step).
  • Mirrored pairs. Half the pulses add the opposite change at 1 or 2 neighbours of the donor (from experiment 395's corrected neighbour table), scaled by the capacity ratio and by a leak share drawn from 0.3 to 1.2 (experiment 459 measured 0.53). The rest have no mirror (tier B).
  • Real events stay out. Window starts avoid the labelled events (padded 2 days) of the donor and of the neighbours; labelled rows are never injected over and never used as training negatives.
  • Hard negatives. (a) Genuine level changes: a step with no return, injected at a random time, size 0.4 to 3.5 times the spread; (b) D8's 55 engine-explained dip days from experiment 508 that fall before 2025-07 (real rows, label 0); (c) step-free surrogates: windows with no injection, from months before 2025-07. D22's 13 dip days and D8's 16 unexplained dip days are held out from every negative set and from training.
  • Training, validation, and held-out sets. Residual history ending before 2025-07 for training. Training worlds: months 2021-01 to 2024-06, two shapes, seeds 0 to 1999. Validation worlds (classifier choice and the Platt fit): months 2024-07 to 2024-12, seeds 2000 to 2499. Held-out worlds for calibration, never used to fit or choose anything: (i) held-out shape (circuit-profile), (ii) held-out seeds (2500 to 2999), (iii) held-out months (2025-01 to 2025-06). Evaluation grids for recall use sizes 0.5, 1, 2, and 3 times the spread and durations 1 hour, 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, and 14 days. Training prevalence about 7% of rows inside a pulse (the labelled share with the pad); calibration is also reported at about 2%.
  • The national same-sign shift of experiment 511. The fine-tune experiment applies it to all 16 Primaries at once with one sign, so signals 3 and 4 are silent and the size lies outside the classifier's training range. This experiment evaluates p on that world and reads it as an extrapolation test (what share of the shifted rows receives p of at least 0.5).

docs.title: Outputs, frozen before any fine-tune score is read
docs.text:
• Per fold and cutoff, a float32 array of p over (Primary, target index) for the 730 days before the cutoff, keyed by (Primary, target_idx). Only the last 30 days before each cutoff are recomputed; older rows are taken from the previous cutoff's table, which saw at least 29 days after them. The first cutoff of a fold computes the whole history.
  • The mask table (Primary, start, end, tier, size, shape correlation, open flag, and the cutoff it is valid for) at p of at least 0.5.
  • The classifier, the feature scalers, the thresholds, and the freeze commit, written to the private folder; a file of SHA-256 sums of the p tables.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• Calibration. Reliability curve, Brier score, and expected calibration error per row and per candidate, on training worlds (a fit statistic), validation worlds, and each held-out axis, at prevalences of about 7% and 2%.
  • Injected recall and false flags. By size, duration, shape, and tier, with bootstrap intervals over Primary-months and the replicate counts as numbers. Genuine level changes called pulses.
  • Real rows. Share of rows with p of at least 0.5 on rows with no labelled event, per Primary-year, by tier; the Kish effective sample size (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 of w = (1 - p)^g (g = 1 and 2, floor 0.1) with and without p over experiment 511's training windows; the share of the unlabelled rows whose weight falls under 0.5.
  • Report only, after the freeze. Area under the curve of p on the 184 labelled rows against matched rows with no labelled event (day-block bootstrap), and p on the 34 events with a measured deviation. NGED's labels are incomplete, so the matched rows hold unlabelled events and the area is a lower bound. D8 and D22 dip weights.
  • Group split. At the eight the sign of a shift is not recoverable across zero; every figure is reported for the six and for the eight.

docs.title: Compute and cost
docs.text: CPU only, at most 2 cores, one process per core, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. The scan is vectorised by cumulative sums. The whole run is expected to take about 1 to 3 hours; the first fold's time is reported to the manager. Memory under 8 GB.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; no model fitted other than the logistic regression and the tree; July 2026 unused; titles say "load-shift", never "switching"; NGED's labels are called incomplete ("rows with no labelled event"); no generator time series is shown. The earlier results the plan follows: experiments 510 (a label mask costs CRPS and cannot speak on an unlabelled leak) and 511 (the baseline cadence, daily, and its leak by block age), and the earlier detector results of experiments 217, 302, 295, 332, and 392. Serving dependency: the weights are training-time only and the classifier runs at each refit, not at serving, but production would still need the lag-free residual series available at each refit.

docs.title: Implementation details (deleted when this ships)
docs.text: Code in ml-experiments/00514-load-shift-probability-detector-and-calibration/: e00514_data.py (residual and partner series, junction detrending, labels), e00514_detect.py (scan, candidates, features), e00514_inject.py (series-level injector), e00514_train.py (worlds, classifier, calibration), e00514_tables.py (the p tables, the causality check, real-row reports), e00514_report.py (figures, numbers).

docs.title: Amendments after the plan review (Sonnet, 27 findings; accepted unless noted)
docs.text:
• Causality. All detrending, scale statistics, and noise scales use only half-hours at least 3.5 hours before the cutoff. The perturbation check recomputes the whole chain (detrend, candidates, cached rows) with every later z replaced and compares p, for the cached rows too. Cached rows are valid because the previous cutoff computed them with strictly less data. The recompute window is 45 days (a 14-day pulse, a 14-day flank, and margin), and a measured check reports how many p values older than the window would change with a full recompute.
  • Scale statistics. For injected worlds the spread and noise scales come from the world's own history before its cutoff. Months 2025-10 to 2026-06 are only scored, never trained or validated on. Months 2025-01 to 2025-06 are used only as the held-out-month axis.
  • Held-out axes. Four axes: held-out shape (circuit-profile), held-out seeds (a weak axis, said so), held-out months, and held-out Primaries (Primary indices 3, 8, and 13, excluded from every training and validation world). The resampling unit is the Primary-month on each axis.
  • World mixture. Of the training worlds, 45% hold only pulses, 25% add a genuine level change, 10% are windows around D8 engine dips before 2025-07, and 20% hold no injection. Prevalence near 7% comes from the pulse count; the 2% reading subsamples pulses, and the intercept is shifted by the log-odds change in prevalence (a prior-shift correction, not a separate Platt fit); P1 uses both readings.
  • Labels and matching. An injected pulse matches its highest-overlap candidate; other candidates overlapping it by under half their rows are negatives, and greedy suppression (a candidate that overlaps an already-kept one by more than half is dropped) prevents duplicates. An open genuine level change is labelled 0 in training, an open injected pulse 1, so the prior for an open step is the share of each in the mixture (reported).
  • Numbers fixed from the training worlds before any held-out number is read. Admission score 2.5 noise units; flank clip 12 to 336 half-hours; symmetry tolerance a donor-to-partner magnitude ratio between 1/2.5 and 2.5; partner edge thresholds 3 and 5 noise units. Pulses per grid cell of the recall tables: at least 100 (sizes 4 x durations 5 x shapes 3 x signs 2, sixteen Primaries).
  • Group of eight. Signal 3 uses the sign of the apparent-power change as recorded; the feature set also carries sign-free counts, and every figure is reported for the six signed-MW Primaries and the eight MVA-only Primaries separately.
  • Fold consequence. The fine-tune experiment either rebuilds the 2025-12 table (7 GPU fits) or runs four folds (123 daily cutoffs, not 154).
  • Mask tables. Written at p of at least 0.5 and at the thresholds giving 1%, 2%, 5%, and 7% of rows flagged. No contrasts are run here; the minimum detectable effect belongs to the fine-tune experiment. Interim numbers are labelled interim and unaudited.
  • D8 and D22 dips. The dip days after 2025-07 are not in any training set by date; those before 2025-07 are held out explicitly (D22's 13 and D8's 16 unexplained), and the report says how many of each fall on each side.
  • Reports to the manager at plan PR open (done), code review done, results, and merge, with the timed first fold.
  • Not taken. Reducing the number of reviews (finding 26): the plan keeps them.
  • Code review (Sonnet, 12 findings). Fixed before any number was read: dip worlds now evaluate D8 (Primary index 4) and respect each set's months; held-out dip days are excluded from every world; worlds containing a labelled event (padded) in the donor, a recipient, or the extra series are rejected; recipients without data are skipped; D15 and D18 are never partners (in training and in the tables alike); "own" pulses use a profile one week older than the feature's shape profile; fold statistics use rows below the refit minus the 3.5-hour cut; recall-grid pulses always have an observed after-flank; the held-out-Primary axis scores donors only; uncovered rows are marked -1, not 0; the mask table uses the calibrated probability and carries tier, size, shape correlation, open flag, and cutoff; the training and validation reports are labelled fit statistics and P3 is read on held-out months only. Counts: D22 has 12 dip days with a date in the stored table (the plan said 13), and 22 of D8's 55 explained dip days fall before 2025-07.

docs.title: Do trailing weather windows lower the error of a lag-free demand network that cannot see recent power, on ten winter folds?
docs.text:
Take-home: trailing temperature windows may help the lag-free demand network a little on cold nights at the eight MVA-only Primaries, but this experiment cannot tell the real windows from a shuffled-day placebo, so the verdict is "not resolved".

  • Arms. W0 is the base lag-free neural network with 37 input columns. W-T adds trailing temperature means over 6, 24, and 72 hours. W-S adds trailing shortwave-radiation means. W-X adds the product of the 24-hour temperature (minus 15.5 °C) and the 24-hour shortwave. W-ALL combines all of these with W-DH (heating and cooling degree-hours), and "W-ALL minus W-DH" drops W-DH. W-null is the placebo: it gives every row the windows of a randomly drawn other day of the same month and day type. W-seam builds W-T differently before the forecast origin. W-CNN is a later pull request with learned windows.
  • Seed spread alone limits what this experiment can detect. The minimum detectable effect (the smallest difference in the continuous ranked probability score, CRPS, that seed spread alone would resolve) is 0.34 points of effective capacity on all rows and 0.48 on cold nights for one fold with 3 seeds. Pooled over 10 folds the seed-only figure is about 0.11 and 0.15, and fold-to-fold variation widens the intervals further. W0 scores 5.40 (all rows) and 4.67 (cold nights) at the eight MVA-only Primaries, and 4.16 and 3.44 at the six signed-MW Primaries (those whose metered power carries a sign). A lower score is better.
  • At the eight MVA-only Primaries, only W-T and W-S beat W0 on cold nights, and the placebo gains almost as much. Cold nights are half-hours below 5 °C between 18:00 and 08:00 local time. The contrast is arm minus W0 (negative favours the arm), with a Bonferroni interval corrected for 20 comparisons, and the count is of negative folds out of 10:
    • W-T: -0.150 [-0.314, -0.075], 10 of 10. W-S: -0.122 [-0.358, -0.017], 9 of 10.
    • W-X -0.081, W-ALL -0.086, and W-ALL minus W-DH -0.105 include zero.
    • W-null: -0.071. W-T minus W-null is -0.079 [-0.290, +0.089], so the real windows do not resolve from the placebo.
  • At the six signed-MW Primaries, no window resolves on cold nights. W-T is -0.147 [-0.596, +0.055], W-S -0.160 [-0.574, +0.009], W-ALL minus W-DH -0.167 [-0.614, +0.004], and W-null -0.108.
  • On all rows nothing resolves. W-T is -0.004 at the eight and -0.099 at the six.
  • One fold, 2024-11, supplies part of every gain, because W0 scores badly there. Every arm, the placebo included, gains 0.46 to 1.29 points in that fold (Figure 2). A post hoc check, chosen after seeing the per-fold table, leaves 2024-11 out (Figure 3). At the eight, W-T then keeps about 80% of its gain: -0.119 [-0.205, -0.071] in 9 of 9 folds, while W-null falls to -0.023. At the six, W-T falls to -0.044 and W-S to -0.062 [-0.122, +0.021].
  • In the tails the placebo gains as much as W-T. On cold nights at the eight, W-T lowers q95 pinball loss by 0.043 and q99 by 0.023, and the placebo lowers them by 0.038 and 0.024. The share of observations below the q95 and q99 forecasts (coverage) was not saved in the report, so it is not quoted.
  • Combining windows did not help. W-ALL (-0.086) did no better than W-T alone (-0.150), which suggests that each extra column adds noise as well as signal.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (W-T, cold nights, eight: gain of at least 0.05): passes on the point estimate (gain 0.150), but not against the placebo.
  • P2 (W-S, six: gain on cold sunny days exceeds gain on cold overcast days by at least 0.05): passes on the point estimate (cold-sunny contrast -0.065, cold-overcast contrast +0.178), with both intervals spanning zero.
  • P3 (W-X: negative on sunny slices, within +0.02 on all rows): winter folds contain no warm-sunny or warm-overcast rows, so P3 cannot be tested. The cold-sunny clause is unresolved.
  • P4 (W-null inside plus or minus the minimum detectable effect): passes only because the test cannot fail. The cold-night minimum detectable effect (0.48) is far wider than the placebo gain (-0.071).
  • P5 (W-seam within plus or minus 0.02 of W-T, all rows): fails, at +0.025 (eight) and +0.023 (six). The cold-night values (+0.019, +0.016) are inside.
  • Stop rule: W-T and W-S met the condition for continuing at the eight, so W-ALL and W-ALL minus W-DH ran. Neither W-ALL nor W-ALL minus W-DH beat W-T.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Three audit triggers fired: the placebo gained, W-ALL did worse than its nested arm W-T, and the minimum detectable effect was wider than the plan expected. The median-minus-mean forecast check and the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast were not run.
  • The placebo takes 88 to 100% of W-T's tail gains, and W-T minus W-null is negative in only 5 of 10 folds at the eight.
  • W0 for 2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03 is reused from experiment 513's P0. W0 is fitted here for the other 7 folds.
  • Warm slices are empty, so no claim covers warm days.
  • Example probabilistic forecast graphs were not drawn in this experiment.
  • A 6-hour window holds only two distinct ensemble samples on day 1 and one beyond day 6.
  • Event labels are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events and counts are lower bounds.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Repeat W-T against W-null with more seeds, and with a stronger W0 in 2024-11, before building the convolutional-network version of the windows (W-CNN) on W-T.
  • The temperature windows would be a candidate for the six signed-MW Primaries only after a run that resolves the placebo.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit that produced a quoted number)
Question
docs.text:
The lag-free demand network (37 input columns plus an 8-wide embedding of the Primary) sees the weather only at the valid time. We ask whether it forecasts better when it also sees the weather of the previous hours. The maintainer's argument is that every earlier neural test of trailing, forward, or daily-mean weather fed the network three origin lags of power, so those nulls may not transfer. Among the merged result pages searched for the brief, the only lag-free test of trailing temperature is experiment 6 (XGBoost, with a 0.1-point floor), and none tested a trailing shortwave window or a temperature-by-shortwave product in a lag-free neural network.

This pull request holds the core arms (W-T, W-S, W-X, W-null, and the seam control W-seam). The learned-window arms (W-CNN) are a separate later pull request. W-ALL, and W-DH as a drop-one inside W-ALL, run here only if the stop rule passes.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Every arm adds columns to the 37 and is re-pretrained from scratch with them, using one loop for all arms (experiment 513's P0 loop). The pretrained weights of experiment 448 do not load, and no new column is zero-initialised.

Arm Added columns What it tests W0 none The control (experiment 513's P0, reused for three folds). W-T Means of temperature over the 6, 24, and 72 hours ending at the valid time (3 columns). Thermal lag. W-S Means of shortwave over the 6 and 24 hours ending at the valid time, and over the 24 hours ending 24 hours before the valid time (3 columns). Stored solar gain. W-X One column: (24-hour mean temperature minus 15.5 °C) times the 24-hour mean shortwave. Cold-sunny and warm-sunny against cold-dull and warm-overcast. W-null The 9 columns of W-ALL (W-T, W-S, W-X, and the two degree-hour columns) taken from a shuffled other day. A gain from nine extra columns alone. W-seam W-T built with persistence fill before the forecast origin instead of the previous run's ensemble mean. Whether the seam, not the physics, drives W-T. W-ALL, W-ALL minus W-DH Conditional on the stop rule. W-DH is heating degree-hours below 15.5 °C and cooling degree-hours above 20 °C accumulated over 24 hours (2 columns). Whether the arms add up, and whether W-DH is needed.

The valid-time product of temperature and shortwave is dropped: the network can learn it from two existing columns.

docs.title: How a window is built
docs.text:
• One rule at every lead (maintainer, 2026-11-02). Every window is built on the half-hourly weather series that the stored ensemble summaries already are, with no lead-dependent definitions. The ensemble mean is a linear interpolation of 3-hourly steps to 144 hours and of 6-hourly steps from 144 to 360 hours, so a 6-hour window holds only two distinct samples on day 1 and one beyond day 6. The write-up says so beside every result.
  • Ensemble rows (fine-tuning and scoring). A row belongs to a run with origin O (09:00 UTC). For half-hours after O the series is that run's ensemble mean. For half-hours at or before O it is the "analysis proxy" of experiment 437: the first day of the freshest earlier run that covers that half-hour (leads of about 9.5 to 33.5 hours). No later run is used. The proxy is available at serving, because every earlier run was published by O. The 72-hour window reaches back three days, so it uses up to three earlier runs. The module is copied from experiment 437's e00437_features.py with the new columns added, and its check, which rebuilds sampled runs with every later run deleted and requires the same result, is re-run on the new columns, because the original covers only the 22 columns of experiment 437.
  • Training rows (pretraining on ERA5 and CAMS). ERA5 temperature is the :00 rows of the half-hourly era5_features.parquet (the :30 rows are interpolation and contain the next hour), and shortwave is the hourly CAMS file with its hour-end stamps. Both are subsampled to the ensemble's step grid, at 3-hourly UTC stamps for half-hours up to 144 hours after the run's 00 UTC start and at 6-hourly stamps after that, and then linearly interpolated to half-hours. A pretraining row's pseudo-run is experiment 418's: its origin is 09:00 UTC and its start is 9 hours earlier, and that start decides where the step grid changes. Before the first fit, the code check compares the stored ensemble shortwave step with the CAMS hour-end value; if the ensemble step is a mean over the preceding step, CAMS is averaged over the preceding 3 or 6 hours before interpolation. The pretraining windows are therefore as smooth as the serving windows, and the grid change follows the lead of the window's half-hour, not the lead of the valid time.
  • Missing earlier runs. A window silently shortens when an earlier run is missing. Each row carries a degradation count, diag_missed_runs: the number of the three days before the origin whose run is absent. It is a scoring diagnostic, never a network input. The scorer reports the share of rows with a non-zero count by horizon band. Windows at the start of the ensemble history (April 2024) are truncated to what exists and flagged.
  • Calibration of the ensemble level. The 2 K level offsets between the ensemble mean and ERA5 are not corrected in the core arms. Arms that pass the stop rule get the noise arm of the brief (below).
  • Scoring uses ensemble windows built exactly as at serving, never ERA5 windows. A gain that exists with ERA5 windows but not with ensemble windows does not count.
  • Standardisation. Each new column is standardised with the mean and standard deviation of the fold's ensemble fine-tuning rows that are not held out for early stopping, in the pretraining, fine-tuning, and scoring stages alike, so a test month never sets its own scale. W-null takes the donor's raw values and applies the same scale as W-ALL, so it has the real columns' distribution. The ERA5 windows are smoother and offset from the ensemble windows by up to 2 K; this offset is the mismatch that the conditional noise arm addresses.

docs.title: Placebo and seam control
docs.text:
• W-null. For each local valid day (Europe/London midnight to midnight), a seeded draw (seed = 515) picks another valid day of the same calendar month, the same day type (Monday to Friday, Saturday, Sunday), and the same length in half-hours (46, 48, or 50, so a clock-change day matches only another clock-change day), at least 3 days away so that persistent weather cannot make the donor informative, without replacement, and from the same side of the fold's refit (training rows take donors that start before the refit, scored rows take donors from days after the refit (the later side), within the ensemble period). The row takes the nine window columns of the donor day at the same half-hour of day and the same lead: its origin and valid time both move by the whole-day shift between the two days, so an ensemble row takes the donor shift's run, and an ERA5 row builds the columns at the shifted origin and valid time. If the donor's run is missing the row takes the next donor in the seeded order. The number of rows with no donor is printed, and those rows take the column means. The same draw serves training and scoring.
  • W-seam. Persistence fill holds the run's first value (the value at its first half-hour after O) for every half-hour at or before O. W-seam shares W-T's pretrained weights, because ERA5 windows have no seam, so it adds 30 fine-tunes and no pretrains. P5 uses a contrast of the two builds' 3-seed mean quantiles on common rows, with per-seed contrasts alongside, because the 0.02 limit sits below the minimum detectable effect.

docs.title: Folds, seeds, and the minimum detectable effect
docs.text:
• Folds. Ten winter months (the "10 winter folds"): 2024-11, 2024-12, 2025-01, 2025-02, 2025-03, 2025-11, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-02, and 2026-03. Ensemble summaries exist for every daily run from 2024-04-01 to 2026-06-30. The five early months have 7 to 11 months of ensemble fine-tuning, no L0PT pretrained weights, and no D15 or D18 (their cut is 2025-03-01; report-only). 2025-11 and 2026-02 need new pretrains. Experiment 437 scored 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03, and experiment 442 added 2025-11 and 2026-02, so four of the ten months were read before this question; the five early months and the exact weather windows are new. Seeds 0, 1, and 2. July 2026 is unused. Christmas week is inside 2024-12 and 2025-12.
  • Control reuse. Experiment 513's P0 weights and forecasts give W0 for 2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03, because P0 is the same network, loop, rows, and seeds. W0 is fitted here for the other seven folds.
  • Minimum detectable effect. Stated first, from the seed spread of the base and the null arm over the ten folds, before any contrast is read (e00515_score.py baseline). References from earlier experiments: 0.13 at the eight and 0.10 at the six on all rows, and 0.034 at the eight and 0.085 at the six on cold nights in 2026-01 alone (a lower bound), all at 3 seeds. The limits of 0.05 and 0.03 are at or below the minimum detectable effect on all rows, so a pass at those limits reads "not shown worse", and only the pooled ten-month cold-night slice can resolve them.
  • Intervals. Month-block bootstrap over ten folds, with the fold count printed beside every interval and the sign per fold beside it. Few blocks give near min-to-max intervals.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
• Rows and groups. Rows with no labelled event, leads up to 240 hours, cleaned data, the D15 and D18 start cut, and the eight MVA-only Primaries and six signed-MW Primaries as the gating groups. D15 and D18 are report-only. Experiment 470's row set covers only five months, so this experiment builds its own, experiment_515_winter_v1: every forecast row of the ten months whose actual is cleaned power with no labelled event, that every scored arm holds. The row counts per fold and group are printed.
  • Widening. Forecast quantiles are scored raw and widened by 1.15, as experiment 510 does. The widening is a fixed table for every arm.
  • Slices (pre-registered). All rows; cold nights (temperature below 5 °C, 18:00 to 08:00); cold sunny, cold overcast, warm sunny, and warm overcast days, with experiment 441's definitions extended to warm days (a local day's mean temperature of at least 15.5 °C); slice membership comes from the stored ensemble mean at the valid time, which no arm edits, never from an arm's own columns; Christmas week; horizon bands day 1, days 2 to 3, and days 4 to 10. Tail results are q95 and q99 pinball loss and coverage on cold nights beside CRPS (experiment 441 found signed-six cold-night coverage of 76% and 83%).
  • Bonferroni count. The primary family is 20 tests: 5 hand-built arms (W-T, W-S, W-X, W-ALL, W-ALL minus W-DH) times 2 groups times 2 slices (all rows, cold nights). The core arms contribute 12 of them (3 arms times 2 groups times 2 slices); intervals use 20 throughout so arms that run later do not change an interval. The reported family is 84 tests: 7 arms times 2 groups times 4 slices (all rows, cold nights, cold sunny, cold overcast) is 56 CRPS tests, plus 28 q95 and q99 cold-night tests. Both numbers are printed by the scorer.
  • Quoted earlier effects. Experiment 437's -0.022 at the eight is all rows. The -0.099 is experiment 441's cold-night figure (inconclusive, 2 of 3 folds). Experiment 442 gave -0.014 at the eight and -0.086 at the six (D16 drives it).

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
• Stop rule. Continue to W-ALL and W-ALL minus W-DH if a Bonferroni interval of a core arm against W0 excludes zero at either group and its point estimate is at least 0.03 points better. Otherwise stop and report "not resolved". W-CNN does not wait for this rule.
  • Noise arm (conditional). Only for an arm that passes. The noise has one level per window column and lead band: the root mean square of (ensemble window minus ERA5 window) over the training window before the refit, temporally coherent (independent noise averages out in a 24-hour mean). The level offset between ensemble and ERA5 is one offset per column and lead band, fitted on data before the refit and never on the scored month.
  • What counts. A gain counts through CRPS at both groups and through the cold-night tail slices, not through a feature's importance. A simple hand-built window that passes is preferred to W-CNN for the first release.

docs.title: Folds, fit count, and cost
docs.text:
• Fit count. Pretrainings: 4 core arms (W-T, W-S, W-X, W-null) times 10 folds times 3 seeds is 120, plus W0 on 7 folds times 3 seeds is 21, so 141 pretrainings. Fine-tunes: the same 141, plus 30 for W-seam, so 171 fine-tunes. W-ALL and W-ALL minus W-DH, if they run, add 60 pretrainings and 60 fine-tunes. The noise arm adds pretrains only for passing arms.
  • Cost. To be timed on the first arm and reported to the manager before the remaining fits. The estimate from experiment 513's logs (pretrain 18 to 24 s, fine-tune 3 to 6 s, rows 13 s per fold) is 0.9 to 1.4 GPU-hours for the core fits, plus building the window columns (not yet timed). One GPU process under 8 GB, with MemoryMax=8G and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; launches are staggered against the other workers' GPU jobs.

docs.title: Departures from the brief
docs.text:
• The brief's five anchor folds of experiment 513's P0 reduce to 3 here (2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03), because 2025-10 and 2026-06 are not winter months. W0 is fitted for the other 7 folds.
  • Experiment 513's P0 comes from its branch price-shape-privileged-input, whose commit is recorded in the pull request before the reuse. Fits start after experiments 511 and 513 Part 1 are scored, which has happened.
  • W-DH has no prediction of its own, because it runs only as a drop-one inside W-ALL.
  • The cost estimate is lower than the brief's 1.2 to 2.6 GPU-hours because it uses experiment 513's measured pretrain time (18 to 24 s) at 141 pretrainings; the brief assumed longer fits.
  • The minimum detectable effect comes from seed spread; the fold-to-fold term enters through the month-block bootstrap, and the page states both.
  • The month-block bootstrap resamples the 10 folds with each fold's 3-seed mean (seed-paired), at the Bonferroni level 0.05 / (2 x 20) per tail. With 10 blocks the interval approaches min-to-max.
  • Charts show per-fold gains, cold-night and sunny slices, in the OCF palette with no mark in the background colour; metered generators are not scored (substations only).
  • The reported family of 84 tests counts 7 arms: W-T, W-S, W-X, W-ALL, W-ALL minus W-DH, and the two W-CNN variants of the later pull request. The scorer prints 84; this pull request runs at most 5 of those arms. P4 and P5 are descriptive tests outside both families.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 start cut; rows with no labelled event; July 2026 unused; no XGBoost work; metered generators are not shown (substations only); titles say "load-shift", never "switching"; the Plan, a fresh Sonnet code review before the first fit that produces quoted numbers, and Sonnet reviews of the results and the write-up follow the ml-experiment skill.

docs.title: Does a small convolutional encoder over a 24-hour weather window improve a lag-free demand network that cannot see recent power?
docs.text:
Take-home: a learned 24-hour weather window did not help the lag-free demand network, and the hand-built trailing windows of experiment 515 remain the only window input with any sign of a gain (on cold nights at the eight MVA-only Primaries, itself unresolved against a shuffled-day placebo). Both encoders scored worse than the 37-column base on all rows. The encoder that read real windows scored numerically worse than the same encoder reading shuffled-day windows, but the interval includes zero. The next step is to stop spending fits on learned windows and to resolve experiment 515's placebo question first.

We asked whether a one-dimensional convolutional encoder over the seven ensemble-mean weather variables (shortwave, longwave, temperature, dew point, surface pressure, precipitation, and 10 m wind speed) at 48 half-hourly positions improves the lag-free demand network. The folds, seeds, rows, slices, bootstrap, and base forecasts are experiment 515's. Contrasts are arm minus W0 in points of CRPS (negative favours the arm), with a Bonferroni-8 interval over fold blocks (10 blocks). "The eight" are the eight Primaries that report only apparent power (MVA); "the six" are the six that report signed megawatts. W0 is experiment 515's 37-column base, and W-T, W-S, and W-X are experiment 515's hand-built trailing temperature, shortwave, and temperature-by-shortwave windows.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. C-CNN reads the window centred on the valid time (12 h before to 11.5 h after). T-CNN reads the 24 h ending at the valid time. C-CNN-null is C-CNN reading the window of a shuffled other day (experiment 515's placebo rule). Each encoder is two strided convolutions (16 and 32 channels, kernel 5), flattened into an 8-number vector that joins the 37 columns. Every arm is pretrained afresh on ERA5 and CAMS rows and fine-tuned on ensemble rows, with 3 seeds on 10 winter folds (90 pretrains, 90 fine-tunes).
  • Scoring windows are built as at serving. Windows read the half-hourly series, which is a linear interpolation of the ensemble's 3-hourly steps to 144 h and 6-hourly steps after, so nothing is finer than 3 h on day 1 and nothing finer than 6 h beyond day 6. ERA5 windows used in pretraining are subsampled to the same step grid and then interpolated.
  • Minimum detectable effect from seed spread alone, 3-seed mean: 0.26 (eight) and 0.34 (six) on all rows and 0.37 and 0.49 on cold nights for one fold. Pooled over the 10 folds the seed-only figures are 0.08 and 0.11 on all rows and 0.12 and 0.15 on cold nights. The fold-block intervals are about 0.5 points wide, which is the larger limit: this experiment cannot resolve a gain of 0.03 to 0.10.
  • All rows. C-CNN: +0.072 [-0.165, +0.338] at the eight (3 of 10 folds negative) and +0.125 [-0.068, +0.410] at the six (4 of 10). T-CNN: +0.086 [-0.172, +0.376] (6 of 10) and +0.079 [-0.132, +0.337] (5 of 10).
  • Cold nights. C-CNN: -0.044 [-0.248, +0.146] at the eight (6 of 10) and +0.131 [-0.141, +0.538] at the six (4 of 10). T-CNN: -0.087 [-0.391, +0.193] and +0.046 [-0.237, +0.351].
  • Cold sunny days at the six are worse with the centred encoder. C-CNN is +0.430 [+0.025, +1.066] (3 of 10 folds negative) and T-CNN +0.250 [+0.091, +0.557] (1 of 10). These intervals are at the Bonferroni-8 level and exclude zero, but the slice is exploratory, not in the 8 primary tests, and not corrected for the full reported family.
  • Against experiment 515's hand-built windows, the encoders are no better. C-CNN minus W-T is +0.077 [-0.180, +0.357] at the eight and +0.225 [-0.069, +0.638] at the six on all rows. T-CNN minus W-T is +0.090 and +0.178. The 0.03 margin for "learned beats hand-built" is not met.
  • The shuffled-day control scored numerically better than the real windows, unresolved. C-CNN-null minus W0 is +0.004 [-0.102, +0.084] at the eight and -0.096 [-0.344, +0.052] at the six on all rows, and -0.167 [-0.512, -0.004] and -0.167 [-0.539, +0.010] on cold nights. C-CNN minus C-CNN-null is +0.069 [-0.149, +0.308] and +0.221 [-0.050, +0.651] on all rows. A control that reads no information about the day scored 0.17 points better than the base on cold nights, with an interval that excludes zero at the eight. That shows the control's own variation is large; the cause (seed spread, or the extra inputs changing the pretrained weights) is not identified.
  • Tails. On cold nights, C-CNN changes q95 pinball loss by -0.018 (eight) and +0.059 (six), and q99 by -0.012 and +0.045; coverage moves by at most 0.008, all intervals include zero. T-CNN changes q95 by -0.037 and -0.034.
  • Horizon bands. No band resolves: at days 4 to 10, C-CNN is +0.060 (eight) and +0.128 (six).
  • Absolute CRPS (points of capacity), all rows and cold nights. W0: 5.40 and 4.67 at the eight, 4.16 and 3.44 at the six. C-CNN: 5.47 and 4.63, 4.29 and 3.57. T-CNN: 5.49 and 4.58, 4.24 and 3.49.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (C-CNN vs W0, -0.08 to +0.02 at both groups on all rows): fails at the six (+0.125); at the eight (+0.072) the loss is above +0.02 too, so P1 fails at both groups.
  • P2 (C-CNN beats T-CNN by under 0.03): C-CNN minus T-CNN is -0.014 at the eight and +0.046 at the six, so P2 holds there. At the six the gap has the opposite sign (C-CNN worse), which P2 did not anticipate, so P2 is not supported at the six.
  • P3 (best CNN beats best hand-built arm by under 0.03): passes, because the CNN arms are worse.
  • P4 (C-CNN-null within the minimum detectable effect of the base): passes on all rows and cold nights, against the one-fold figure (0.26 to 0.49), as in experiment 515, but only because that figure is wide. Against the pooled figure (0.12 and 0.15 on cold nights) the control's -0.167 would fail P4.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Weather inputs come from runs issued at or before the origin. e00516_leak_check.py rebuilt 144,000 window positions (3,000 test rows of 2025-12 x 48 positions) from the stored summaries. Every position after the origin came from the row's own run and every position at or before it from an earlier run's first day; the largest source-run origin minus row origin was 0 half-hours, and values agreed to 1.1e-5 (float32). Example row: Primary index 4, origin grid index 109746, valid grid index 109977.
  • Windows with a missing source are filled with the training mean (0 after standardising). The check zero-filled any position whose source row was absent and asserted that fill; it does not print how many positions that was. Placebo rows with no donor day keep their own window: 10,752 to 19,068 rows per fold across pretraining, fine-tuning, and test tables.
  • ERA5 windows differ from ensemble windows. On fine-tuning rows, ERA5 minus ensemble windows differ by 0.35 (temperature) to 0.81 (precipitation) standardised standard deviations. The encoder is pretrained on ERA5 windows and scored on ensemble windows, which may explain why real windows score worse than shuffled ones; this is unproven.
  • Not done: the noise arm (experiment 515's coherent ensemble-minus-ERA5 noise) because no variant passed the stop rule.
  • Event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold unlabelled events.
  • Review: one fresh Sonnet review of the whole diff ran after the fits, not before them. It found no leak and no mismatched number; its findings on interpretation and wording are applied. It also found a window position past the run's 360 h horizon that would have read a later run's history; no row reaches it (the longest lead is 240 h), and the gather now returns no value there. The leak check was re-run after the change. The fit script had no review before the first fit.
  • Cost. Per fold: feeder 16 to 22 s; pretrain 14 to 40 s, median 26 s (about the same as a 37-column pretrain, not the 3 to 5 times assumed); fine-tune 2 to 14 s, median 6 s; peak 6.1 GB of RAM. The log holds 89 of the 90 pretrains and fine-tunes, because the timing run came first.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Resolve experiment 515's placebo question before any learned window. A shuffled-day control beat the real windows here and gained at the eight in experiment 515, so a control with the same columns is the first thing a window experiment has to beat.
  • Pretrain on ensemble-like windows, by adding the coherent noise of experiment 515 to the ERA5 windows, only if a hand-built window passes first.

docs.title: Is the 0/1 lockdown flag still needed by the lag-free demand network now that pretraining reaches back to 2019?
Take-home message
docs.text: No arm is a clear replacement for the flag, and the experiment cannot rank the arms. The flag is 0 in every fine-tune and scored row, so the flag acts only through pretraining. Arm C2 (flag removed, 2020-03-23 to 2021-07-19 rows dropped from pretraining) scored 5.117 at the eight and 3.751 at the six, against 5.150 and 3.741 with the flag (C0). C2 is better than C0 at the eight in 3 of 5 folds, and that gain rests on two Primaries (see Checks). Removing the flag with the lockdown rows kept (C1) scored 0.029 worse at the six, and that difference disappears when one Primary is left out. On 22 to 31 December (at the six) and on D15 and D18, C2 scored worse than C0. Every difference is below the minimum detectable effect (0.125 at the eight, 0.133 at the six, 3-seed means). The result does not show that the lockdown rows hurt, and it keeps the flag as the default.

docs.title: Figure
docs.text: Pooled difference per horizon band and group; bars span the lowest to the highest of the five per-fold differences, so they are ranges, not confidence intervals. Negative favours the first arm.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Counted contrasts (CRPS over days 1 to 10, difference with Bonferroni-18 interval, folds negative of 5):
    • C1 minus C0: eight +0.011 (-0.020 to +0.042, 2 of 5), six +0.029 (+0.007 to +0.052, 2 of 5).
    • C2 minus C0: eight -0.033 (-0.060 to -0.007, 3 of 5), six +0.010 (-0.017 to +0.038, 3 of 5).
    • C2 minus C1: eight -0.044 (-0.069 to -0.021, 5 of 5), six -0.019 (-0.049 to +0.009, 3 of 5).
  • Pre-registered rules. "Flag not shown to be needed" fails: the six's upper bound for C1 minus C0 is 0.052, above the 0.05 margin. "Flag needed" passes at the six only (lower bound +0.007, a twentieth of the minimum detectable effect; the point estimate +0.029 is a fifth). "Lockdown rows hurt" passes at the eight (upper bound -0.021). Post hoc, using the same margin: C2 is not shown worse than C0 at either group (upper bounds -0.007 and +0.038, both below 0.05). Prediction P1 failed at the six; P2 held.
  • Absolute scores (eight / six): C0 5.150 / 3.741, C1 5.161 / 3.770, C2 5.117 / 3.751.
  • Horizon bands (C2 minus C1, eight): day 1 -0.040, days 2 to 3 -0.034, days 4 to 10 -0.048; (C1 minus C0, six): +0.012, +0.020, +0.034. No band reverses the sign of its group.
  • Tails (q99 pinball loss, eight / six): C0 0.280 / 0.186, C1 0.286 / 0.192, C2 0.292 / 0.189. Coverage of the q99 is 0.9915, 0.9900, and 0.9898 at the eight, and the q01 coverage is 0.0032, 0.0024, and 0.0032. C2's q99 loss is higher than C0's at the eight, so the CRPS gain does not come from the upper tail.

docs.title: Example forecasts
docs.text: Day-ahead and 10-day forecasts from 09:00 UTC on 2026-01-12 and 2026-06-15 for D10 (signed MW) and D4 (MVA only), seeds averaged and widened by 1.15 as in experiment 510 (the scored numbers above use raw quantiles). C0 and C2 look nearly the same in both seasons, and the bands widen only mildly with horizon.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Audit by a fresh Sonnet agent; interim and unaudited beyond the Sonnet reviews and this audit.

  • Median error beside the quantile score. The absolute error of the median forecast has the same sign as the CRPS contrast in all nine contrast-by-group cells. The mean forecast is not stored, so the median stands in for it, and no median-minus-mean check per site was possible.
  • Re-derived contrasts. The audit's own CRPS from the raw seed forecasts matches the stored scores to four decimals.
  • Leaving one Primary out (trigger 4 fired). At the six, dropping Primary 6 turns C1 minus C0 to -0.010 (-0.036 to +0.014), so "flag needed" fails and "not shown to be needed" would pass at both groups. At the eight, C2 minus C0 loses significance when Primary 4 or 15 is left out, and the gain rests on Primaries 15 (-0.209) and 8 (-0.082). C2 minus C1 at the eight survives every deletion.
  • Nested arms (trigger 5 fired). C2 uses a subset of C1's pretraining rows and beats C1 at the eight in all 5 folds. No size-matched placebo was run, and C2 also drops the flagged rows from the early-stopping set, so its stopping point differs. A single seed's CRPS varies by 0.06 to 0.11 within a fold, so only the eight's C2 minus C1 clearly exceeds seed and fold noise.
  • Interval width (trigger 6 fired). The intervals here are 0.4 times as wide as those of experiment 513 on the same rows; the arms differ, so this is a prompt, not a fault.
  • Seeds are not paired across arms, because the first layer has a different width.
  • Earlier finding. Experiment 6 found that the flag helps XGBoost; this result agrees only weakly (+0.029 at the six, not stable).
  • Triggers 1, 2, and 7 did not fire. The audit report is in the private data/ml-experiments/briefs/ folder.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The minimum detectable effect is larger than every difference. The minimum detectable effect comes from the seed spread (0.078 and 0.083 points per seed; 3 seeds, 5 folds). The intervals come from a bootstrap that resamples blocks of month and origin day (about 150 blocks), so the intervals ignore variation between folds and between training runs. A paired t test across the 5 folds, uncorrected, gives p values of 0.06 to 0.82; the lowest is the eight's C2 minus C1 (0.058). The minimum detectable effect, not the bootstrap interval, sets how far to trust a difference.
  • Christmas week (22 to 31 December, fold 2025-12 only). C1 minus C0 is -0.15 at the eight and +0.09 at the six. C2 is worse than C0 at the six (+0.31) and no different at the eight (-0.008), and worse than C1 at both (+0.15 and +0.22). Treat these as single-fold results.
  • Report-only Primaries (D15 and D18, pooled over all rows). C1 minus C0 is +0.38 (Bonferroni +0.17 to +0.58) and C2 minus C0 is +0.62 (+0.47 to +0.76), worse in all 5 folds for both arms; C2 minus C1 is +0.24. These Primaries have short history, so the 2020 rows may matter there. This was not a pre-registered contrast.
  • Folds. C2's gain over C0 at the eight comes from 3 folds (2025-10, 2026-03, 2026-01); folds 2025-12 (+0.050) and 2026-06 (+0.020) go the other way.
  • Load-shift events. Rows with no labelled event are scored; NGED says some events are unlabelled, so these rows may hold events that no label covers.
  • Not run. The load-shift event plots: the scored rows are those with no labelled event.
  • Schedule. Monthly refit; the contrast could differ under weekly refits.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Keep the flag in later lag-free experiments until the 2020 rows are tested at the report-only Primaries and at Christmas on more than one fold.
  • Test C2 against a size-matched placebo (an equal number of ordinary 2019 to 2021 rows dropped), on weekly refits, and on more December folds before any release claim.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: The plan was written before any score was read. One fold and one seed (2025-10, seed 0) were timed first; their forecasts are kept as part of the final fits and were not scored until the code review had run. The plan covers Part 2 of the brief (the lockdown flag); the whole-day price shape is experiment 513.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: The lag-free demand network takes a 0/1 input that is 1 from 2020-03-23 to 2021-07-19. The network is pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS rows from 2019-09, which include that period, and fine-tuned on ensemble forecast rows from 2024-04, which do not. The flag is 0 in every scored month. Is the column still needed, and do the lockdown rows hurt a network that cannot see the flag?

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms use experiment 510's L-M recipe (monthly refit, 182.6-day weight, 3 mixture components, hidden width 64, 2 layers, dropout 0.1), pretrained here by experiment 513's loop. They differ only in the flag column and the pretraining rows.

Arm Flag column Pretraining rows Network inputs C0 kept all 37 non-lag columns C1 removed all 36 C2 removed the flagged rows (2020-03-23 to 2021-07-19) dropped, from training and early stopping 36

C2 is a pretraining-only change. The fine-tune rows hold no flagged row, and the scripts assert this for every fold. C1 changes the fine-tune too, because the network has one input fewer, so the pretrained weights of experiment 448 do not load and every arm, C0 included, is pretrained here. In the first fold 1,395,832 of 7,005,809 pretraining rows are flagged (19.9%).

docs.title: Folds, seeds, and cost
docs.text:
• Folds and seeds. The five folds of experiments 448, 449, and 510 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0, 1, and 2. July 2026 is unused.
  • Fit count. 3 arms x 5 folds x 3 seeds: 45 pretrainings and 45 fine-tunings.
  • Timed cost. Fold 2025-10, seed 0: feeder 13 s per fold; pretraining 20 s (C0), 16 s (C1), and 18 s (C2); fine-tuning 7 s, 4 s, and 5 s. About 0.3 GPU-hours for everything (13 s x 5 + 45 x (18 + 5.3) s = about 19 minutes). One GPU process under 8 GB, with MemoryMax=8G and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.

docs.title: Scoring and contrasts
docs.text:
• Rows and scorer. Experiment 510's pipeline on experiment 470's row set, rows with no labelled event, leads up to 10 days, raw quantiles (no widening). "The eight" are the eight Primaries that report only apparent power (D15 and D18 report-only); "the six" are the six that report signed megawatts.
  • Contrasts (negative favours the first arm). C1 minus C0, C2 minus C0, C2 minus C1, at CRPS over days 1 to 10, at the eight and the six: 6 tests. The Bonferroni count is the family of the whole price-and-lockdown brief, 18.
  • Slices. Horizon bands day 1, days 2 to 3, and days 4 to 10 beside days 1 to 10, and Christmas week (22 to 31 December, fold 2025-12).
  • Minimum detectable effect. From the seed spread of the three arms pooled (three seeds, five folds), scaled to a 3-seed mean, printed by e00517_score.py baseline before any contrast. Earlier experiments report 0.057 to 0.164 points for single-seed or two-seed comparisons.
  • Intervals. The scorer's bootstrap over month and origin-day blocks; the page gives the sign per fold beside every interval.

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
• Not shown to be needed. At both groups the upper Bonferroni bound of C1 minus C0 is below the non-inferiority margin of 0.05 points. "Within the minimum detectable effect" is not used: below the minimum detectable effect, no difference can be proved.
  • Needed. The lower Bonferroni bound of C1 minus C0 is above zero at a group.
  • Lockdown rows hurt. The upper Bonferroni bound of C2 minus C1 is below zero at a group.
  • Otherwise the experiment cannot tell, and says so.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
