docs.text: Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 start cut (through experiment 428's rows); rows with no labelled event; July 2026 unused; no XGBoost work; titles say "load-shift", never "switching"; every interim number is unaudited.

docs.title: Implementation details (deleted when this ships)
docs.text: Code in ml-experiments/00517-.../: e00517_fit.py (pretrain, fine-tune, forecast) and e00517_score.py (experiment 510's scorer pointed here), and e00517_slices.py (horizon bands and the figure). Run with PYTHONPATH set to the ml-experiments/* folders and DATA_PATH_INTERNAL=/home/jack/dev/nged-substation-forecast/data.

docs.title: Can a small neural network learn to find and size a shifted block in 14 days of power readings, and how long does one fit take?
docs.text: This page is interim and unaudited, and its result is a weak null. A small neural network (the history encoder, 86,747 parameters) was trained once, for 69 seconds, on injected shifts in 14 days of power readings at the fold 2026-01 Primaries. The encoder did not pass the pre-registered proxy for the plan's kill rule (c). The fit used one seed and a noisy validation block of 401 windows, so the result does not rule out a learned repair.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Question. Experiment 507 showed that a perfect repair of the three lag readings improves the lag correction. This experiment asks whether a small neural network can learn to find and size injected shifts in the 672 half-hours (14 days) of readings, and how long one fit takes.
  • Data. Experiment 507's generator, with temporary shifts (family A), genuine level changes (family B), and hard negatives drawn three times as often (family D). One window is a Primary and a day. The two input channels are the surprise (reading minus the ERA5 and CAMS lagless median, over the Primary's residual spread) and the median standardised within the window. Windows touching a labelled event are dropped. Test windows have origins in January 2026; training windows end 68 days before the refit, the validation block (30 days) sits before a 24-day embargo.
  • Encoder. A dilated convolution stem, 168 two-hour tokens, two transformer layers with a learned relative-position bias, and heads for the step probability, the step size, and whether the step in force at the newest reading is genuine. The losses were a positive-unlabelled step loss with a size loss (weight 0.5), a genuine-head cross-entropy (0.2), and a total-variation penalty (1e-3). Adam at 2e-3, batches of 128, a fresh generator world each epoch.
  • Checks. The four checks P1 to P4 and their thresholds were written into the plan before the fit. A candidate step is a half-hour where the mean estimated step over the next 4 half-hours differs from the mean over the previous 4 by at least 0.5 spreads.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Terms. A spread is a Primary's residual standard deviation (the reading minus the lagless median, which is the forecast of a network that sees no power input). A candidate step is defined in the Method. The ceiling is the score of a predictor that outputs the injected step. A temporary shift (family A) ends; a genuine change (family B) persists. The signed-MW six are the Primaries that report signed megawatts and the MVA-only eight report apparent power only.

Scores are on the 372 test windows (origins in January 2026) in injected worlds 200 to 202. Intervals resample whole Primaries (13 in the test month). "Ceiling" is the same score for a perfect predictor that outputs the injected step, read through the same candidate rule.

Check Threshold (fixed before the fit) Result Outcome P1: best epoch of the validation step loss (L_u, the pre-registered measure) 8 or later 14 (L_u 0.244) Passed on that measure only: the loss moved between 0.24 and 0.57 from epoch to epoch, and the plain cross-entropy beside it was lowest at epoch 4 P2: error at the three lags on rows a step touches under half of the unrepaired error 0.446 against 0.988 spreads (45%) Passed P2: error added on rows no step touches under 0.1 of the mean injected step 0.144 Failed (no interval computed) P3: steps found within 6 hours at least 70% of the ceiling (0.896) 0.396 (0.365 to 0.434), 44% of the ceiling Failed P4: planted-step precision at a 2% rate at least 0.3 0.165 (0.07 at the six, 0.40 at the eight) Failed on the pooled value (no interval computed; the groups straddle the threshold, so the pooled failure is not firm)

  • The encoder found a third of the steps within 2 hours. The shares found within 2, 6, and 24 hours were 0.313, 0.396, and 0.464, against ceilings of 0.870, 0.896, and 0.910. The ceiling is below 1 because a step under 0.5 spreads is never a candidate. At the signed-MW six the share within 2 hours was 0.297 (4 Primaries), and at the MVA-only eight 0.326 (7 Primaries).
  • Size was roughly right when a step was found. The median relative size error among found steps was 0.25, and 50% were within 25%.
  • The false-flag rate depends on which median is used. On test windows with no injection it was 0.032 (0.003 to 0.085). On the validation block's real windows it was 0.297. A possible cause (not tested) is that 78% of test half-hours take their median from the table's post-refit module, while training and validation use cross-fitted medians, so the test surprise is quieter.
  • Raising the candidate threshold trades recall for precision. At 1.5 spreads the planted-step precision was 0.334, but only 7% of steps were found within 2 hours. The thresholds of 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, and 1.5 spreads gave precisions of 0.165, 0.188, 0.246, and 0.334. P4 was fixed at 0.5.
  • The genuine-change head was weak. Its area under the ROC curve was 0.64 on 373 labelled window-world pairs (windows with a step in force at the newest reading, pooled over the three worlds). The generator makes 75% of steps in force at the newest reading genuine.
  • Cost. One fit took 69 seconds (22 epochs of 16,384 windows, about 3 seconds each), against a cap of 2 hours.

docs.title: Outcome against the plan
docs.text: Item Outcome Kill rule (c), clause 2: validation step loss stops falling before epoch 10 Not fired (best epoch 14), but the curve is noisy Kill rule (c), clause 1, read through the proxy P2 to P4 The proxy failed (P2 on the clean-row guard, P3, P4) Consequence in the plan The neural encoder stops unless the neural Discuss session overrules

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• A weak null. One seed, a 69-second fit, and a validation block of 401 windows (the step loss swung by more than a factor of two between epochs) cannot separate "the encoder cannot learn this" from "this fit was too small". The thresholds were fixed before the fit.
  • The total-variation test of experiment 507 is also weak. Its tuning hit the edge of the grid (weight 16 and tau 5, the weakest repair), so this experiment cannot say how a learned encoder compares with a well-tuned non-learned repair.
  • The noise curve was not run, by the maintainer's standing instruction, so the first clause of rule (c) is read only through the proxy.
  • The lab setting flatters detection, and the test month holds 4 Primaries at the six (D5 and D16 are excluded by labelled events) and 7 at the eight.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the real windows used for the false-flag rate hold events that no label covers.
  • Training prevalence. 19% of the valid training half-hours are positives, against at most a few per cent in real data, so the step probability is calibrated to a busier world than the real one.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Attempt 2 (below) asked whether a longer, three-seed fit with a larger validation block, a lower learning rate, and a flag threshold chosen on validation reaches the thresholds. It did not, so the line closes unless the neural Discuss session overrules.

docs.title: Attempt 2 (design fixed before it ran)
docs.text:
A second, bounded attempt changes the fit in six ways and reads the same four checks. The maintainer approved it, and the lag-free results of experiment 511 (the lag-free network beats the lagged network below about 2 days, and the gap sits at days 5 to 10) weaken the case for a lag encoder. The changes: 3 seeds (each with its own network initialisation and training worlds); a validation block of 130 days (1,558 windows) in place of 30; early-stopping worlds 150 to 152 and separate threshold worlds 160 to 162; a learning rate of 5e-4; epochs of 32,768 windows; and early stopping after 10 epochs. The flag threshold is chosen per seed on the validation block alone, as the grid value (0.5, 0.75, 1.0, or 1.5 spreads) that maximises planted precision times recall within 2 hours, and is written to a file before any test window is scored. P1 to P4 are read unchanged at the frozen threshold, per seed, with the spread over seeds. The cap is 0.5 GPU-hours for the fits together (the scoring passes are not counted).

  • Tuned design. The test windows and worlds 200 to 202 were read in attempt 1, and the changes above were chosen afterwards, so a pass is a pass of a design tuned after that read-out.
  • Best epoch. A loss counts as better only if it is 0.5% below the best, so "best epoch" means the last such improvement. A best epoch of 8 to 12 is reported as inconclusive for P1.
  • Seeds. The three seeds share one training pool, one validation block, and one set of test windows, so the spread over seeds understates the uncertainty. If the seeds disagree on P2 to P4, the page says so and does not pick a seed.
  • A second null closes the line. The neural Discuss session decides what follows.

docs.title: Attempt 2 results
docs.text:
All three seeds fail P2, P3, and P4, and the seeds agree. The result is a second null, so the line of work on a learned history encoder closes. The scores below are at each seed's frozen threshold on the same 372 test windows and worlds 200 to 202. The three fits took 332, 164, and 287 seconds (783 seconds, 0.22 GPU-hours, inside the 0.5 GPU-hour cap, and no fit aborted).

Seed Frozen threshold (spreads) Best epoch (P1) Repaired / unrepaired lag error (P2, below 0.5) Error on untouched rows / injected step (P2, below 0.1) Found within 6 h / ceiling (P3, at least 0.7) Planted precision at 2% (P4, at least 0.3) 0 0.5 59 (pass) 0.478 (pass) 0.312 (fail) 0.463 / 0.896 = 0.52 (fail) 0.025 (fail) 1 0.5 19 (pass) 0.440 (pass) 0.243 (fail) 0.404 / 0.896 = 0.45 (fail) 0.067 (fail) 2 1.5 41 (pass) 0.477 (pass) 0.314 (fail) 0.078 / 0.466 = 0.17 (fail) 0.197 (fail)
  • P1 passes in every seed. Seed 0 reached the 60-epoch cap with its best epoch at 59, so its validation loss was still falling when the fit stopped.
  • The repair shrinks the lag error but adds error elsewhere. The ratio of repaired to unrepaired lag error is 0.44 to 0.48, but the encoder also puts an error of 0.24 to 0.31 of the mean injected step on rows where no step touches a lag, three times the allowed 0.1.
  • The seeds differ in how they fail. Seeds 0 and 1 chose the lowest threshold and found 46% and 40% of injected steps within 6 hours, with false-flag rates of 0.277 and 0.089 on real test windows. Seed 2 chose 1.5 spreads, found 8%, and flagged 0.5% of real windows. At the threshold the validation block chose, no seed gets near the 0.3 planted precision.
  • The genuine-change head is weak. Its ranking area under the ROC curve is 0.63, 0.66, and 0.64 across the seeds (373 labelled window-world pairs).
  • Limits. The seeds share one training pool, one validation block, and one set of test windows, so the spread over seeds understates the uncertainty. The design was tuned after attempt 1 read the same test windows. The noise curve was withheld by the maintainer's standing instruction, so the proxy is not the noise-curve region itself. The tuning of the total-variation repair in experiment 507 hit the edge of its grid (weight 16, tau 5, the weakest repair), so that test was weak as well.

docs.title: How large a share of ECMWF ENS rows should the lag-free demand neural network's pretraining contain?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

Putting ENS rows into the pretraining batches of the lag-free demand neural network made its mean forecast worse at the eight MVA-only Primaries, and the loss grew steeply from a 50% share upwards. Against the 0% control F0, CRPS rose by 0.076 points at a 10% share, 0.059 at 25%, 0.105 at 50% (experiment 511's L-mix), 0.183 at 75%, and 0.220 for ENS only (lower is better; the Bonferroni intervals for 32 tests exclude zero for all five). At the six signed-MW Primaries only 75% (+0.097) and ENS only (+0.135) have intervals that exclude zero. The ENS rows lowered the q99 pinball loss (75%: -0.032 at the eight), so the share trades a worse mean score for a better top tail. Removing the flag, or fine-tuning and scoring at flag 0, moved the CRPS by at most 0.041 points, so the flag does not explain experiment 511's deficit; it does explain part of the q99 gain.

Verdict: not supported. The pre-registered rule needed a share that beats the control, and none did; the prediction that 10% and 25% are non-inferior (upper bound below +0.03) also failed at the eight. The numbers were re-derived from the score tables by a fresh reviewer (see "Checks").

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Setup. Weekly refits, 90-day half-life, restart from the month's pretrained weights, five folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0 and 1, scored on experiment 470's rows ("rows with no labelled event" at the six), in points of effective capacity. The 50% arm is experiment 511's L-mix; its fits were reused. Weekly refits, so the contrasts are for the weekly cadence only. Scoring actuals dropped for a flagged exact zero: 1,179 half-hours across the five folds and all groups.
  • Absolute CRPS (eight / six). L-Ww 4.920 / 3.555; F0 (0%) 4.876 / 3.558; E10 4.952 / 3.551; E25 4.936 / 3.577; L-mix (50%) 4.981 / 3.599; E75 5.060 / 3.654; E100 5.096 / 3.693; K2-S1 4.763 / 3.423; A-pool 4.682 / 3.457. F0 is within the 0.164 (eight) and 0.123 (six) two-seed minimum detectable effect of L-Ww at both groups.
  • Contrasts against F0 (Bonferroni interval, 32 CRPS tests; negative is better). Eight: E10 +0.076 [+0.034, +0.119]; E25 +0.059 [+0.023, +0.099]; L-mix +0.105 [+0.052, +0.173]; E75 +0.183 [+0.109, +0.260]; E100 +0.220 [+0.116, +0.333]. Six: E10 -0.007 [-0.050, +0.038]; E25 +0.019 [-0.011, +0.050]; L-mix +0.042 [-0.001, +0.086]; E75 +0.097 [+0.043, +0.155]; E100 +0.135 [+0.059, +0.223]. The sign by fold is positive in 3 to 4 of 5 folds for each share at the eight; the 2026-06 fold favours 25% to ENS only (-0.03 to -0.09), and 2026-01 favours 10% and 25%.
  • Shape. E75 minus E25: +0.124 [+0.076, +0.174] (eight), +0.077 [+0.029, +0.126] (six); E100 minus E25: +0.160 and +0.116; E25 minus E10: -0.017 and +0.027 (both include zero). The curve is flat from 0% to 25% within 0.06 and rises steeply beyond 50%.
  • Experiment 511's contrast recomputed. L-mix minus L-Ww +0.062 [-0.012, +0.148] (eight) and +0.045 [+0.008, +0.083] (six), against +0.062 [-0.015, +0.148] and +0.045 [+0.009, +0.081] in experiment 511 (which used 56 tests). F0 minus L-Ww is -0.043 [-0.079, -0.009] at the eight and +0.003 [-0.031, +0.038] at the six. The eight-group difference is below the 0.164 two-seed detectable effect, and F0 has a different input width and draws 8,192 ERA5 and CAMS rows per step, so the difference is not evidence that the flag column helps. The 2026-06 fold alone contributes -0.151 of it.
  • Flag ablation (fixed at 25% and 50%). No flag column: NF25 minus E25 -0.005 [-0.053, +0.038] (eight) and -0.041 [-0.070, -0.015] (six); NF50 minus L-mix +0.019 [-0.038, +0.068] and -0.008 [-0.043, +0.021]. Flag 0 at fine-tuning and scoring: Z25 minus E25 +0.007 [-0.028, +0.036] and -0.006 [-0.019, +0.006]; Z50 minus L-mix -0.036 [-0.076, +0.000] and +0.004 [-0.012, +0.020]. F0z (F0's weights fine-tuned and scored at flag 0, report only) scored 4.875 / 3.556 against F0's 4.876 / 3.558, so the untrained flag input in F0 did no harm.
  • Horizon bands (CRPS minus F0, eight / six, pooled over five folds, no interval). Day 1: E10 +0.115 / +0.022; E25 +0.062 / +0.050; L-mix +0.078 / +0.056; E75 +0.168 / +0.109; E100 +0.262 / +0.178. Days 2 to 3: E25 +0.048 / +0.053; L-mix +0.062 / +0.065; E75 +0.154 / +0.130; E100 +0.212 / +0.184. Days 4 to 10: E25 +0.062 / +0.005; L-mix +0.122 / +0.033; E75 +0.194 / +0.085; E100 +0.216 / +0.114. The ENS-only deficit is largest at day 1 at the eight and at days 2 to 3 at the six. E10 and E25 are level with F0 at days 4 to 10 at the six (-0.022 and +0.005), and E10 at days 2 to 3 is +0.095 (eight) and +0.027 (six).
  • Tails. q99 pinball loss minus F0 (Bonferroni interval, eight / six): E10 -0.003 [-0.007, +0.002] / -0.006 [-0.012, -0.002]; E25 -0.014 / -0.009; L-mix -0.021 / -0.013; E75 -0.032 / -0.011; E100 -0.026 [-0.035, -0.016] / -0.007 [-0.016, +0.002]. F0 minus L-Ww is +0.009 / +0.008. Removing the flag raises q99 pinball loss: NF25 minus E25 +0.012 [+0.007, +0.016] and NF50 minus L-mix +0.012 at the eight, and flag 0 at fine-tuning does the same (Z25 minus E25 +0.011, Z50 minus L-mix +0.012), so the q99 gain depends on the flag. Against L-Ww the q99 gain of E25 is inside zero (-0.005 [-0.010, +0.001] eight, -0.002 [-0.006, +0.002] six). q99 coverage at the eight: F0 0.9936, E25 0.9937, L-mix 0.9937, E75 0.9913, E100 0.9887 (nominal 0.99), so ENS-only pretraining under-covers slightly. q01, q05, and q95 are in absolute.csv of the private data folder and were not analysed.
  • Two-stage control TS (own family, 4 CRPS tests, 8 with q99). TS scored 4.923 / 3.559. TS minus L-Ww +0.004 [-0.002, +0.010] / +0.005 [-0.001, +0.010]; TS minus F0 +0.047 [+0.017, +0.078] / +0.002 [-0.028, +0.030]. One epoch of ENS-only training at 0.1 times the rate lowered the held-out ENS loss in every fold (for example 0.5904 to 0.5179 in 2025-10) but left the forecast unchanged from L-Ww. TS is within 0.013 of the best mixed share (E25 at the eight, E10 at the six).
  • Fit counts and cost. 70 pretrains (12 to 49 s each), 10 stage-2 epochs, 550 fine-tunes (2 to 5 s each), about 1.1 hours of wall time on one GPU process; peak host memory 5.3 GB and GPU memory 2.1 GB at the timed fold. The 60-epoch cap bound only for E25 in the timed fold.
  • Serving cost. A production pretraining with ENS rows would store about 4.2 to 5.0 million ENS rows and keep a pool of 7.4 to 7.9 million ERA5 and CAMS rows per fold, about 12 million rows of 37 float32 inputs (about 1.8 GB). F0 needs only the ERA5 and CAMS pool.

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (no share beats the 0% control by 0.03 or more): held. No share improved on F0 at the eight; at the six the best was E10 at -0.007.
  • P2 (10% and 25% non-inferior to 0%; 75% and ENS only worse than 25%): half failed. The upper Bonferroni bounds of E10 and E25 exceed +0.03 at both groups, so non-inferiority is not shown, and at the eight the lower bounds are above zero. 75% and ENS only were worse than 25% (+0.124 and +0.160 at the eight).
  • P3 (removing the flag changes the score by less than 0.03): held in 6 of 8 cells on point estimates. NF25 at the six (-0.041, interval [-0.070, -0.015], no flag better) and Z50 at the eight (-0.036, interval [-0.076, +0.000]) are outside it. Several "held" cells have intervals that reach past 0.03 (NF25 at the eight, [-0.053, +0.038]), so the point estimates support the prediction less strongly than the count suggests.
  • P4 (two-stage control no better than the best mixed share): not tested. TS was within 0.013 of the best mixed share at both groups (TS beat E25 by 0.013 at the eight, E10 beat TS by 0.008 at the six). No TS-versus-mixed contrast was computed; TS minus L-Ww and TS minus F0 form their own family.
  • P1's parenthetical ("every difference is inside the minimum detectable effect") failed at the eight for E75 (+0.183) and E100 (+0.220), which exceed 0.164. P1 itself held. P1 to P4 are the front-matter prediction, and the plan section below lists the arms and rules, not the predictions.
  • Minimum detectable effect. 0.164 (eight) and 0.123 (six), experiment 511's two-seed values, not refitted; the paired intervals are narrower because the rows are shared.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Leak check. pretrain asserts that no ENS or ERA5 and CAMS row lies past the refit cutoff minus 3.5 hours and that no origin lies past the cutoff, for every fold; it printed 0 for all five folds. Weekly fine-tunes use experiment 511's row selection and windows.
  • Reviews. One fresh Sonnet review of the plan and code ran before the first fit. It found: the claim that F0 differs from L-mix only in ENS rows was not strictly true (F0 draws 8,192 ERA5 and CAMS rows per step); the flag column of F0 is untrained at pretraining; the hypothesis could not separate the share from the double use of rows; the contrast list was not enumerated. All four were accepted and the plan was edited; F0z was added for the second. One fresh Sonnet review of the results and the write-up re-derived the numbers and found them correct, and found: the P3 count was 6 of 8 (not 7); P4 was untested; the flag carries part of the q99 gain; the take-home overstated a monotone trend; one claim of "best" held at the eight only; and several bare "network" and pronoun uses. All were accepted and edited.
  • Not run. The median-minus-mean check and the other audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill were not run, and no second write-up review ran.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Weekly cadence only. The contrasts may differ at a daily refit, which experiment 511 found better.
  • Fewer ERA5 and CAMS rows. Every arm takes the same number of steps per epoch, so a larger ENS share also means fewer ERA5 and CAMS rows seen per epoch; the sweep varies both together.
  • Overlap of rows. Every ENS pretraining row also lies in the 730-day fine-tune window, so the sweep cannot separate the share from the double use of those rows.
  • Seed noise. Two seeds and five folds; the seed standard deviation is 0.083 (eight) and 0.063 (six), larger than most contrasts here, so small differences (under 0.06) are not established.
  • Rows with no labelled event. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so these rows may hold events.
  • Not done in this experiment. Cold winter nights, Christmas week, the injected-shift leak, the ENS date range (recent 90 and 180 days only), and the daily refit repeat belong to the diagnostics experiment that follows.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Do not spend more experiments on the ENS share of pretraining for the mean score: the share is not supported. The planned diagnostics experiment (ENS date range, cold nights, leak) is dropped.
  • A tail-focused variant (25% to 75% ENS rows, flag set at fine-tuning) would need its own test on q99 pinball loss and the avoidable curtailment cost, because the q99 gain against the 37-input network is inside zero at 25%.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Experiment 511's L-mix pretrained the lag-free neural network on ERA5, CAMS, and ENS rows together and scored worse than L-Ww, which pretrains on ERA5 and CAMS rows only: +0.062 [-0.015, +0.148] at the eight (not significant) and +0.045 [+0.009, +0.081] at the six, in points of CRPS. We ask what ENS share in the pretraining batches is best, and whether the deficit comes from the share, the source flag, or the double use of rows.

docs.title: What experiment 511 built (Step 0)
docs.text:
• Share. Each pretraining batch held 4,096 ERA5-or-CAMS rows and 4,096 ENS rows, drawn uniformly: 50% ENS by batch share, but about 36 to 40% by row count (4.2 to 5.0 million ENS rows against 7.5 to 7.9 million ERA5-and-CAMS rows per fold). There were no row weights in pretraining.
  • Overlap. Every pretraining ENS row also lies in the 730-day fine-tune window, so L-mix saw those rows twice. This is a design choice, not a test leak: pretrain_mix asserts that no ENS or ERA5/CAMS row lies past the cutoff minus 3.5 h or has an origin past the cutoff.
  • Flag and spread. The source flag is a 38th input: 0 for ERA5-and-CAMS rows, 1 for ENS rows, and 1 at fine-tuning and scoring. ERA5 and CAMS rows carry the fold's median standardised ENS spread by lead band, as in experiment 418.
  • ENS history. 18, 20, 21, 23, and 26 months before the five fold cutoffs (the 730-day window caps it at 24).

docs.title: Arms (all weekly cadence, 90-day half-life, restart from the month's pretrained weights)
docs.text:
Shares are shares of each 8,192-row pretraining batch. Every arm takes the same number of steps per epoch (20% of the ERA5-and-CAMS training rows at 4,096 rows per step) with the same batch size, so the number of ERA5-and-CAMS rows drawn per epoch falls as the ENS share rises. Contrasts are written "arm minus control", so a negative difference is a gain.

  • F0, the 0% control. The 38-input network, the flag column fixed at 0 in every pretraining row (all rows are ERA5 and CAMS), flag 1 at fine-tuning and scoring, as in L-mix. F0 differs from L-mix in having no ENS rows in pretraining (and so drawing 8,192 ERA5-and-CAMS rows per step), and it keeps the seed pairing. Caveat: the flag column is 0 in every F0 pretraining row, so its first- layer weights stay at their random start and the switch to flag 1 at fine-tuning adds an untrained input. F0z (report-only, outside the counted family) fine-tunes and scores the same weights at flag 0. L-Ww (37 inputs) anchors the cadence only.
  • E10, E25, E75, E100. Same, with 10%, 25%, 75%, and 100% of every batch drawn from the ENS rows.
  • E50 is L-mix. Experiment 511's 2 seeds x 5 folds of fits are reused.
  • Early stopping at any share uses the held-out NLL averaged with the batch shares as weights, so 50% reproduces L-mix's mean of the two sources, and E100 uses the ENS term alone.
  • Flag ablation, fixed in advance at 25% and 50%. NF25 and NF50: no flag column (37 inputs), same pretraining mix. Z25 and Z50: the pretrained weights of E25 and L-mix, with the flag set to 0 (not 1) at fine-tuning and scoring. "Flag 1 at fine-tuning" is what L-mix did.
  • TS, the two-stage control. Experiment 510's ERA5-and-CAMS pretrained weights (37 inputs), then one epoch (20% of the ENS training rows) on ENS rows only at 0.1 times the pretraining learning rate, keeping the stage-2 weights only if the held-out ENS NLL fell; then the usual fine-tune with no flag.

docs.title: Pre-registered rules
docs.text:
• Tests. 16 contrasts x 2 groups = 32 CRPS tests (64 with q99). Against F0: E10, E25, L-mix (the 50% share), E75, E100. Against L-Ww: F0, E25, L-mix (repeats experiment 511's contrast). Flag ablation: NF25 against E25, NF50 against L-mix, Z25 against E25, Z50 against L-mix. Shape: E25 against E10, E75 against E25, E100 against E25, L-mix against E25. The optional two-stage control TS is its own family (TS against L-Ww and against F0: 4 CRPS tests, 8 with q99) and is reported separately. Minimum detectable effect: 0.164 (eight) and 0.123 (six), experiment 511's mde.csv from two seeds, not refitted.
  • Seeds. Seeds 0 and 1 for every arm. No outcome-selected third seed.
  • Scored set. Experiment 470's rows, five folds, "rows with no labelled event"; D15 and D18 report only; horizon bands day 1, days 2 to 3, days 4 to 10.
  • Month-block bootstrap with the fold count stated beside every interval, and per-fold signs.
  • Diagnostics left to the next experiment. The ENS date range, the cold-night and Christmas slices, and the injected-shift leak.

docs.title: What the plan costs
docs.text: • 7 new pretraining variants (F0, E10, E25, E75, E100, NF25, NF50) x 5 folds x 2 seeds = 70 pretrains (about 32 s each) + 10 stage-2 epochs, and 11 new arms (F0, F0z, E10, E25, E75, E100, NF25, NF50, Z25, Z50, TS) x 25 weekly fine-tunes x 2 seeds = 550 fine-tunes (about 3.8 s each). About 1.2 GPU-hours in all.

docs.title: At which lead times does the lagged-and-lag-free network K2-S1 beat the daily-refit lag-free network, and is the gap a lag effect, a refit-age effect, or a mixture-width effect?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

K2-S1's advantage over the daily-refit lag-free neural network L-1d is largest at 120 to 240 h, and the point estimates favour L-1d below 48 h, so the advantage is not a lag advantage. K2-S1 reads lagged power; L-1d does not. The gap is 0.174 points of CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, lower is better) at the eight MVA-only (megavolt-ampere-metered) Primaries and 0.196 at the six signed-MW (megawatt-metered) Primaries. A short-horizon correction on a lag-free anchor is therefore not what the gap calls for. At the eight, a monthly five-head lag-free ensemble (LL-ens5) is 0.017 behind K2-S1 at 120 to 240 h, which is consistent with head count driving the gap. At the six, LL-ens5 matches L-1d and is 0.20 behind K2-S1, so K2-S1's lagged heads may contribute there. Every number on this page is interim and unaudited until a human has read it.

Experiment 511 left L-1d 0.091 (eight) and 0.071 (six) points behind K2-S1. We re-cut experiment 511's stored per-row scores by lead time, and fitted no neural network. "Gap" means L-1d minus K2-S1 CRPS in points of capacity, so a positive gap means K2-S1 is better. The gap mixes three differences: lagged against lag-free heads, daily against monthly refit, and four heads against two.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held for the sign pattern and the share. The gap is negative below 48 h at both groups except the eight's 48 to 72 h band (+0.01), and positive from 72 h at both groups. The 120 to 240 h band holds 94% of the eight's summed gap (more than the predicted 70%).
  • P2 fits neither branch cleanly. At 120 to 240 h at the eight, LL (monthly, one head) is 0.066 worse than L-1d and L-Ww (weekly) 0.042 worse, as refit age would predict. But LL-ens3 and LL-ens5 are better than L-1d, as head count would predict. The Bonferroni interval of L-1d minus LL-ens5 includes zero.
  • P3 held at the eight and failed at the six. At 120 to 240 h at the eight, K2-S1's q95 coverage is closer to nominal than L-1d's (0.948 against 0.960), and so is q99 (0.989 against 0.995). At the six, L-1d is closer (q95 0.934 against 0.909).
  • P4 failed. No Primary carries more than 40% of the eight's gap (largest: D2, 32%; D4 is -16%).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• L-1d is better below 48 h in point estimate only, and K2-S1 is better at 120 to 240 h. At the eight, the gap is -0.15 [-0.39, +0.10] at 0 to 6 h, -0.12 at 6 to 12 h, -0.03, -0.02, +0.01, +0.07, and +0.17 [+0.02, +0.32] at 120 to 240 h (Bonferroni intervals over origin-day blocks, 28 tests). Only the 120 to 240 h interval excludes zero.
  • At the six, two bands exclude zero. The gap is -0.08, -0.15, -0.25 [-0.39, -0.10] at 12 to 24 h, -0.11, -0.04, +0.05, and +0.20 [+0.07, +0.33] at 120 to 240 h.
  • The whole-month block check is much wider. With 5 blocks, the interval is near the minimum-to-maximum range of the five folds. At the eight every band includes zero (120 to 240 h: [-0.11, +0.51]), and at the six only 12 to 24 h excludes zero. This check cannot support a claim.
  • The minimum detectable effect is as large as most gaps. From L-1d's two seeds it is 0.10 to 0.27 per band at the eight and 0.11 to 0.17 at the six. The 120 to 240 h gap (0.17 and 0.20) is at or just above it, and every gap below 72 h at the eight is smaller.
  • The sign of the 120 to 240 h gap is positive in 4 of 5 folds at both groups. Below 48 h the number of positive folds ranges from 0 to 3 of 5.
  • The pooled gaps reproduce experiment 511. They are 0.091 at the eight and 0.071 at the six. On rows with no labelled event the eight's gap is 0.131.
  • Reference arms at 120 to 240 h (CRPS, eight / six). K2-S1 4.967 / 3.523; L-1d 5.140 / 3.719; L-Ww 5.182 / 3.769; LL 5.206 / 3.829; LL-ens3 5.029 / 3.690; LL-ens5 4.984 / 3.724. K2-S1 minus LL-ens5 is -0.017 [-0.056, +0.023, uncorrected] at the eight and -0.201 at the six. L-1d minus LL-ens5 is +0.157 [+0.059, +0.253, uncorrected; Bonferroni -0.001, +0.310] at the eight and -0.005 at the six.
  • Below 72 h the monthly ensembles score worse than L-1d. LL-ens5 is 0.18 to 0.45 worse at the eight and 0.35 to 0.72 worse at the six. In this comparison the daily refit matters most at short lead, but it is confounded with ensemble size.
  • Tail calibration over all leads. q95 coverage (nominal 0.95) is 0.952 for K2-S1 and 0.968 for L-1d at the eight, and 0.912 and 0.943 at the six. q99 coverage (nominal 0.99) is 0.990 and 0.996 at the eight, and 0.979 and 0.991 at the six. K2-S1 is closer to nominal at the eight, and L-1d is closer at the six, where K2-S1's bands are too narrow. The q99 pinball loss gap (L-1d minus K2-S1) is +0.010 [-0.002, +0.021] at the eight and -0.019 [-0.031, -0.007] at the six (56 tests).
  • L-1d's bands are wider than K2-S1's in every band. The mean q05 to q95 width (points of capacity, L-1d against K2-S1 cell c0) at the eight is 41.1 against 38.9 at 0 to 6 h, 32.5 against 30.1 at 24 to 48 h, and 34.0 against 31.6 at 120 to 240 h. At the six it is 30.2 against 27.6, 22.8 against 20.9, and 24.0 against 22.5. Both widen by about the same from 12 to 24 h to 120 to 240 h (7.3 points for L-1d and 6.9 for K2-S1 at the eight). The wider mixture of K2-S1's four heads therefore does not give it the wider bands, and the narrower bands come with the lower CRPS. The tables are scores/widths.csv, scores/absolute.csv (coverage and pinball loss by band), and scores/contrasts.csv, in this experiment's private data folder.
  • No Primary dominates the eight, and the six is a sum of offsetting terms. At the eight the pooled gap is D2 +0.235 (32%), D12 +0.223 (31%), D3 +0.166 (23%), D8 +0.124 (17%), D21 +0.124 (17%), D19 +0.025, D22 -0.052, and D4 -0.115 (-16%). At the six, D14 is -0.496 against D9 +0.317, D16 +0.295, D10 +0.276, D5 +0.193, and D11 -0.141.
  • L-1d is far better inside labelled events and in Christmas week. At the eight the gap (uncorrected 95% interval) is +0.131 [+0.055, +0.206] on rows with no labelled event, -0.611 [-0.794, -0.412] inside a labelled event, -1.235 [-1.290, -1.183] in Christmas week, and -0.135 [-0.303, +0.036] on cold winter nights. K2-S1 is worse there, which is the opposite of what a lag advantage would produce, because K2-S1's lagged heads follow the shifted readings. The six's slices use all 429,176 of its rows (pooled gap 0.070): cold winter nights -0.250 and Christmas week -0.637. D15 and D18 have a pooled gap of -0.651.
  • The gap by half-hour of day (figure 6) is noisy and shows no single ramp or peak that carries it.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Experiment 511's K2-S1 score is cell c0 alone. The stored column reproduces exactly from cell c0 (maximum difference 0.0). The all-lead CRPS of the three cells at the eight is 4.763 (c0), 4.741 (c1), and 4.742 (c2). The mean of the three cells gives a pooled gap of 0.106 at the eight and 0.064 at the six, and 0.190 and 0.187 at 120 to 240 h. The headline uses c0 so that it reproduces experiment 511.
  • L-1d recomputed from its two stored seeds (quantile average, 1.15 widening) reproduces experiment 511's column to 0.0.
  • The audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill do not apply. No forecast was made and no score changed; stored scores were re-cut. The median-minus-mean check was therefore not run.
  • Row counts per band match the earlier first look (eight 13,456 / 14,678 / 29,365 / 58,578 / 58,194 / 115,237 / 282,533).
  • 2,736 rows of fold 2026-06 have NaN coverage and pinball columns in experiment 511's table. All 2,736 are outside main16, so none enters any table here.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet code review before the first number was used (one finding, the choice of cell c0 against the 3-cell mean, accepted; band shares and q99 contrasts added), a Sonnet results review that re-derived the headline numbers (all matched; it found a unit error in the example figures and the band widths, both fixed), and a Sonnet write-up review (accepted in full).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The gap mixes refit age, ensemble size, and averaging method. K2-S1 is refitted monthly with four heads per cell mixed as distributions; L-1d is refitted daily with two seeds averaged by quantile. No daily four-head lag-free ensemble was built, because none can be built from stored seeds.
  • Experiment 454 does not say that K2-S1's gain is mostly ensembling. It says that mixing a lagged and a lag-free forecast beats averaging lagged networks, and it has no result by lead.
  • There are only 153 origins (one a day) in 5 folds. Rows are strongly correlated within a day, and most bands cannot be told apart from zero.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so rows with no labelled event can hold unlogged events, and the labelled-event slices undercount.
  • The profile does not say whether a better use of lags exists. It shows only that K2-S1's current use of lags does not lower CRPS below 48 h compared with the daily lag-free network.
  • No load-shift event time series were drawn. This experiment re-cuts stored scores and asks no question about how forecasts respond inside an event.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the head-count reading at the eight directly. Refit the daily lag-free network with five heads and compare it with K2-S1 at 120 to 240 h. This needs fits, so it needs the manager session's approval.
  • Find what makes K2-S1 better at the six at long lead. LL-ens5 does not match it there, so the S1 heads or the mixture are the candidates.

docs.title: Does the lag-free demand network's 8-wide Primary embedding carry more than a random identity tag?
docs.text:
The lag-free demand network's Primary embedding is not just a random label, but it is also not a map of physical behaviour. The embedding is the table of 8 numbers that tells the network which primary substation (Primary) a row belongs to. Each vector starts as a random draw. Pretraining moves each vector about half its own length, and the network needs that movement: scoring a Primary with its own random start vector, instead of its trained vector, raised the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lower is better) by 0.80 percentage points of effective capacity (a percentage of the Primary's capacity) for the pretrained network and by 1.32 for the fine-tuned network. What the movement encodes is only weakly physical.

We asked whether the embedding carries more than a random identity tag. We read the stored weights of experiments 448 (the lag-free network, 4 folds x 5 seeds), 425 (the lagged network, arm A), and 511 without fitting anything. We regenerated each random start, measured how far the vectors moved, tested the movement against 10 per-Primary descriptors of demand shape and weather response and against the metering type, and replaced the vectors in the network and rescored the 2026-01 test month. Verdict: partly supported. "The six" are the 6 Primaries that report signed megawatts and "the eight" are the 8 that report apparent power (MVA) only; D15 and D18 (the two short-history Primaries) are left out of every mean.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Part 1, displacement. The regenerated start correlates 0.85 to 0.93 with the stored vectors of the same seed (20 files). The stored vectors sit 0.52 of the start's norm from the start (95% bootstrap interval 0.50 to 0.54 over 20 fold-and-seed cells; arm A 0.68). Daily fine-tuning moves them a further 3.6% (3.0% to 4.2%); the one fine-tuned L-1d network of experiment 511 moved 1.8%. The per-dimension standard deviation is 0.56 to 1.51, and 6 or 7 of 8 dimensions carry 90% of the variance (5 or 6 for the random start alone).
  • Part 1, alignment. Same-seed stored vectors agree across folds (Spearman 0.92 mean over 30 matrix pairs of 120 distances), as the shared start makes certain. After the start is removed, same-seed movements still agree (0.88 over 30 pairs). Different seeds agree on the movement (0.38 mean, 0.09 to 0.59, 40 pairs) far more than on the stored vectors (0.16, -0.06 to 0.34), against a permutation null with standard deviation 0.14: part of the movement is the same whichever start it begins from. Arm A and the lag-free network agree 0.73 on the movement (20 pairs).
  • Part 2, Mantel tests. Eleven counted tests (10 descriptors and the metering type) plus the probe, level 0.05 / 12 = 0.0042, on fold 2026-01 with the 5-seed average distance matrix. One test passes: winter weekday profile shape (Spearman 0.51, p 0.0014, 14 Primaries, since D15 and D18 have no winter data in that window). It also has p 0.002 at fold 2025-10 and 0.0096 at 2026-03 and 0.012 at 2026-06. With cosine distance, which ignores how far a vector moved, the same test gives 0.09 (p 0.28). The movement's length correlates 0.67 with the winter profile's deviation from the mean, so the pass reflects the size of the movement and not its direction. Temperature slope in winter (0.33, p 0.026), load factor (0.36, p 0.047), and midday shortwave slope (0.36, p 0.045) do not pass the count. The 120 pairs come from 16 Primaries, so they overstate the independent evidence.
  • Part 2, metering type. The Mantel correlation is -0.00 to 0.03 at every fold (p 0.50 to 0.97). The leave-one-Primary-out probe classifies 31% to 38% of the 16 Primaries correctly from the movement and 50% to 69% from the stored vectors, against 50% for chance (exact binomial interval at the Bonferroni level, 0.06 to 0.74 for the movement; the lower bound never exceeds 0.5). D15 and D18 sit in the group of their own metering unit, so there are two groups of 8. The metering type is not separated.
  • Part 2, power of the test. A planted-signal control (a movement built from one descriptor at 25% or 50% of its variance, 100 draws) detects the weekend ratios, the temperature slopes, and (at 50%) the profiles at rates of 0.54 to 1.00 and 0.65, but demand level and load factor only at 0.06 to 0.43. A null result for demand level is therefore weak evidence.
  • Part 3. One fold (2026-01), one seed (0), 14 scored Primaries, each Primary's day equally weighted. The identity arm reproduces experiment 448's stored quantiles to 2.2e-5 of capacity at every level. The table gives the CRPS change in percentage points at the six and at the eight, with the 95% interval from resampling the 31 origin days. The minimum detectable effect is 0.246 (six) and 0.328 (eight).
Network Arm Six Eight Lag-free, pretrained vectors swapped (mean of 20) 3.63 (3.52 to 3.73) 6.31 (6.06 to 6.55) Lag-free, pretrained mean vector 0.80 (0.73 to 0.86) 4.76 (4.50 to 5.02) Lag-free, pretrained own random start 0.44 (0.32 to 0.56) 1.07 (0.94 to 1.20) Lag-free, pretrained fresh N(0, 1) (mean of 20) 2.59 (2.54 to 2.65) 5.37 (5.15 to 5.59) Lag-free, fine-tuned vectors swapped 4.30 (4.17 to 4.43) 6.82 (6.50 to 7.16) Lag-free, fine-tuned own random start 0.86 (0.74 to 0.98) 1.67 (1.34 to 1.98) Lagged (arm A) vectors swapped 2.64 (2.51 to 2.78) 4.67 (4.45 to 4.91) Lagged (arm A) own random start 0.81 (0.75 to 0.88) 1.98 (1.70 to 2.27)

The identity scores are 5.55 (six) and 5.67 (eight) for the pretrained network, 5.53 and 4.74 for the fine-tuned network, and 4.91 and 4.54 for arm A. Swapping vectors raises CRPS by 5.16 points on average for the pretrained network, 5.74 for the fine-tuned network, and 3.80 for arm A. Arm A loses 34% less than the fine-tuned lag-free network and 26% less than the pretrained one. The swap shows that the vectors are used, not that they are informative.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (displacement 0.40 to 0.60, fine-tune movement under 0.05): met.
  • P2 (no Mantel test passes): not met. One of 11 passes, and the cosine distance and the movement-size correlation explain it.
  • P3 (swap raises CRPS by more than 0.5): met at every network.
  • P4 (own start costs under the minimum detectable effect): not met. It raised CRPS by 0.44 to 1.98, above 0.246 (six) and 0.328 (eight) in every row of the table.
  • P5 (arm A loses at least a third less): met against the fine-tuned network (34%), not against the pretrained network (26%).
  • Decision rule: one Mantel test passes and the own-start arm is worse by more than the minimum detectable effect, so the rule returns "healthy". We read this as "used, only weakly arranged", because the one passing test depends on movement size.

docs.title: Part 4: options for telling the network which Primary it is
docs.text:
None was run. "Window" says whether the option uses only the training window, so it adds no live-data dependency at serving. The evidence cited is experiment 406 (removing the embedding raises CRPS by 0.79 and 0.81 points at the six and the eight), 421 (raw last-7-days power identifies the Primary 90% of the time, yet a learned label beats it by 0.28 to 0.33), 425, and 448.

  • Initialise the embedding from descriptors (for example a PCA of each Primary's training-history profile). Prediction that could fail: the cross-seed agreement of the movement rises from 0.38 to above 0.7, and CRPS falls by more than the minimum detectable effect. Cost: low, one code change and a pretrain. Window: yes.
  • A higher learning rate, or no weight decay, on the embedding. Prediction: the displacement from the start rises above 0.8 and CRPS falls. Cost: low. Window: yes.
  • Static descriptor inputs recomputed at each refit. Prediction: the network matches the embedding's CRPS without a learned label, and the fresh-vector arm of this experiment stops being worse than the descriptors. Cost: medium (a descriptor table per fold and the feature columns). Window: yes.
  • A wider embedding (16 or 32). Prediction: no CRPS gain, because 6 of 8 dimensions already carry the variance of the start. Cost: low. Window: yes.
  • A per-Primary output scale and bias head. Prediction: a gain at the eight, where the start-vector arm cost the most. Cost: low. Window: yes.
  • Feature-wise modulation of the hidden layers from the embedding. Prediction: a gain only if Primaries differ in weather response, which the temperature-slope Mantel tests did not show. Cost: medium. Window: yes.

docs.title: Consistency with experiment 511
docs.text: Experiment 511 found the daily-refit lag-free network ahead of K2-S1 below about 2 days and behind at days 5 to 10. A weak embedding would hurt at every lead, so the result is not evidence that the embedding is thin. The weather columns come from each Primary's own H3 cell, which carries per-Primary information besides the embedding.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, tail calibration, curtailment cost, and load-shift plots do not apply: no forecast was fitted and the page scores only swapped weights.
  • Triggers: trigger 2 fired for P4 (the movement is used) and for P2. The cosine and movement-size tests and the fresh-vector arm are the tested explanations. No audit ran, because of quota, and the PR says so.
  • Row set: the 2026-01 test rows with a cleaned actual, which is not experiment 454's row set; the raw quantiles are not widened.
  • Skipped: the reverse-flow share and the midday-dip share (experiments 506 and 508) were not computed, and the 2025-12 weights of experiment 510 are not used.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Part 3 is one fold and one seed, and the minimum detectable effect is an assumption carried over from experiment 511's two-seed, five-fold value.
  • Part 1 and 2 intervals come from 20 cells and 5 seeds.
  • Rows with no labelled event are not separated: NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so these numbers include unlogged events.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Test per-Primary descriptors as static inputs, against the embedding at the same seeds, with the metering type as a direct input.

docs.title: Does the lag-free neural network know what lead time means, and do per-lead widening or ERA5 pretraining explain its long-lead gap to K2-S1?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

The lag-free neural network does not widen its prediction bands with lead, but neither does K2-S1, and widening the bands separately for each lead recovers almost none of K2-S1's advantage at days 5 to 10. Lead is how far ahead the forecast looks. The lag-free neural network L-1d reads no recent power readings and is refitted every day. It starts from weights pretrained on ERA5 weather, in which the forecast is the truth at every lead. We asked whether L-1d has learned that a longer lead means a larger weather error. K2-S1 is the neural network that also reads lagged power. We re-read the forecasts that experiments 511, 454, and 448 had stored, scored them by lead band (a range of leads, such as 120 to 240 h), and fed experiment 511's stored L-1d weights altered lead inputs. Replacing the lead input changed the mean width of the 90% prediction band by at most 4%. The band grows only 5% from 12-24 h to 120-240 h once the half-hour of the day is held fixed (every forecast origin is at 09:00 UTC, so lead fixes the half-hour), against 27% in the pooled figures. K2-S1's band grows by 4%. Widening the bands separately for each lead, with factors fitted on earlier held-out forecasts, changes the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lower is better) by at most 0.024 points of effective capacity. ERA5 pretraining lowers CRPS in every lead band as a point estimate. Its Bonferroni interval over origin-day blocks excludes zero in 5 of 7 bands at the eight and 6 of 7 at the six, but the whole-month Bonferroni interval only in 0 of 7 and 2 of 7. Every number on this page is interim and unaudited until a human has read it.

Here "the eight" are the 8 MVA-only (megavolt-ampere-metered) Primary substations and "the six" are the 6 signed-MW (megawatt-metered) Primary substations, as in experiment 521. CRPS (the continuous ranked probability score, lower is better) is in points of effective capacity. This experiment fitted no neural network and used no GPU. A Bonferroni interval widens each interval so that the stated number of tests share one 5% error rate. A PIT (probability integral transform) histogram shows where actuals fall within the forecast distribution. Origin-day blocks resample whole forecast days.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 held for the width and failed for the median. Setting every row to day 10 changes L-1d's mean 90% width by -4% to +3% across lead bands (under the predicted 10%). It moves the median by a mean absolute 0.7 to 4.1 points of capacity (day 10), against the predicted 1% of capacity or less. The network ignores lead for the band and uses it for the centre of the forecast.
  • P2 held. Within one half-hour of the day the 90% width grows by 4.9% (L-1d) and 3.7% (K2-S1) at the eight and by 5.0% and 4.6% at the six, differences of 0.012 and 0.003 as ratios.
  • P3 half held. Per-band widening lowers CRPS at 120-240 h by 0.008 points at the six (Bonferroni interval -0.012 to -0.003, excludes zero) and by 0.002 at the eight (includes zero). The eight part held (under 0.03). The predicted 0.03 at the six was not reached. Against the gaps of 0.196 (six) and 0.174 (eight) from experiment 521's rows, per-band widening closes 4% and 1%. Those gaps use different rows from the folds 2025-12 onward in the contrast, so the percentages are approximate. On the contrast's own rows the gaps are not stored.
  • P4 mixed, and confounded by recipe. L0PT minus LL is negative in 2 of the 4 bands below 48 h as predicted (0-6 h: -0.043 eight, -0.022 six; 12-24 h: -0.100, -0.146), positive in the other 2 (6-12 h and 24-48 h), and positive at 120-240 h by 0.37 (eight) and 0.53 (six) as predicted. LL differs from L0PT in training recipe, so this contrast does not isolate pretraining. Against L0, the same network without pretraining, the pretrained L0PT has the lower CRPS in every band as a point estimate (see Results).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Pretraining helps at every lead as a point estimate (like-for-like). L0PT minus L0, in points of CRPS (negative means pretraining is better; Bonferroni intervals over origin-day blocks, 28 counted tests). At the eight, L0PT minus L0 is -0.39 [-0.58, -0.22] at 0-6 h, -0.14 [-0.23, -0.05] at 120-240 h, -0.13 [-0.21, -0.06] pooled (the pooled rows are not among the 28 counted tests). At the six it is -0.18 [-0.33, -0.04] at 0-6 h, -0.05 [-0.09, -0.01] at 120-240 h, -0.08 [-0.11, -0.05] pooled. Origin-day intervals exclude zero in 5 of 7 bands at the eight and 6 of 7 at the six. The Bonferroni whole-month intervals (4 blocks, near the range of the folds) exclude zero in 0 of 7 bands at the eight and 2 of 7 at the six (72-120 h and 120-240 h; at 120-240 h the six's is -0.083 to -0.021). The unadjusted whole-month intervals exclude zero in 1 and 6.
  • The contrast with LL is confounded. L0PT minus LL is +0.37 [+0.22, +0.53] at 120-240 h at the eight and +0.53 [+0.34, +0.73] at the six, but LL is a cell of experiment 454's lag-free heads, which come from experiment 404's cross-fitted lag-free table and another training recipe. LL scores 5.084 and L0 5.596 at the eight, so the difference lies in the recipe and not in pretraining.
  • Per-band widening gains under 0.03 everywhere. Per-band minus flat 1.15, CRPS: -0.002 (eight) and -0.008 (six) at 120-240 h; -0.018 and -0.007 at 0-6 h; -0.005 and -0.009 pooled (folds 2025-12 onward). The flat 1.15 was chosen on the scored rows, so it is not held-out. The per-band factors, fitted on earlier forecasts, leave q95 coverage at 0.920 (eight) and 0.938 (six) pooled, below the 0.95 target, because the earlier folds were better covered than the later ones.
  • Hour of day and lead are tied together. Every origin is at 09:00 UTC, so lead fixes the half-hour of the target. The pooled 90% width grows 27% (eight) and 30% (six) from 12-24 h to 120-240 h, and 5% once the half-hour is held fixed.
  • The Part 3 gate does not hold. L-1d minus K2-S1 q95 coverage at 120-240 h is 0.015 (eight) and 0.027 (six) lower than at 12-24 h, short of the 0.03 gate, and L-1d covers more than K2-S1 in both bands. Part 3 is not run.
  • PIT histograms. At 120-240 h the top PIT bin holds 0.124 (eight) and 0.172 (six) of L-1d's rows against 0.1 if calibrated, and the bottom bin holds 0.084 and 0.051. The actuals fall above the bands more often than below.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. The widening in this experiment changes only the distance of each quantile from the median, so the median is unchanged. The median minus the atom-weighted mean of the 11 stored quantiles is -0.6 (L0PT) and -0.5 (L0) points at the eight, and -0.2 (L0PT) and -0.3 (L0) at the six, pooled over bands.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrast. The mean absolute error of the median, L0PT minus L0, is -0.22 at the eight and -0.08 at the six at 120-240 h, the same sign as the CRPS contrast.
  • Leave one Primary out. The L0PT minus L0 CRPS at 120-240 h is between -0.17 and -0.10 at the eight and between -0.06 and -0.03 at the six, whichever Primary is left out.
  • Triggers. The protocol's second audit trigger (a result contradicts its prediction) fired for P1's median part, P3, and P4; the explanation is the 09:00 UTC origin (P1), non-stationary coverage (P3), and the recipe difference between L0PT and LL (P4), tested by adding L0. The other triggers except the seventh did not fire. The seventh (a later design depends on an unreplicated result) may fire: the manager's next lead experiments could depend on the pretraining sign, which rests on one pair of experiments (448's L0 and L0PT, 3 seeds, 4 folds); no audit has run.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet plan review, a Sonnet code review (no blocking findings; the hour stratification, the width comparison rows, the Bonferroni tail resamples, and unused code were fixed), and a Sonnet results review that re-derived the L0PT minus LL contrast, the width ratios, one widening factor, and the L-1d reproduction without a mismatch. The L0 contrast has had the same code review as the other contrasts. The results review did not cover it.
  • Reproduction. The panel reproduces experiment 511's stored L-1d CRPS to 5e-7 in every month. The lead-swap "true" condition reproduces experiment 511's stored seed-0 quantiles to 5.4e-5 of capacity. Experiment 511's 2,736 rows of 2026-06 with NaN cov_* and pin_* are in no row set and are excluded.

docs.title: Method and data
docs.text:
• Arms and rows. Rows are experiment 511's scored rows (row set experiment_470_intersection_v1; folds 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06; D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01; cleaned data). L-1d is the quantile average of experiment 511's two seeds. K2-S1 and LL are experiment 454's three cells each. L0PT and L0 are experiment 448's seeds 0 to 2 (world 0; no 2025-12 fold, so four folds). All scores use the 1.15 widening, and the cells are scored one by one and averaged.
  • Cadence. Monthly for experiments 448 and 454, daily for L-1d. No refit here.
  • Part 2 factors. Estimated per daily cutoff from the unwidened L-1d quantiles whose target is at least 3.5 h before the cutoff; floor 0.5, cap 3, fallback 1.15 when a band holds under 2,000 rows (100 of 6,832 day, set, band, and tail cells; part2_fallbacks.csv).
  • Past-weather caveat. No weather enters this experiment; it re-reads stored forecasts, whose inputs are the stored ensemble mean and spread.
  • Minimum detectable effect. From the seed spread, for L0PT and L0 at 120-240 h: 0.13 and 0.20 (eight), 0.21 and 0.09 (six). At 120-240 h the L0PT minus L0 contrast of -0.14 (eight) sits below the L0 arm's own 0.20, so it is a point estimate with 3 of 4 folds negative at the eight (4 of 4 at the six), and its Bonferroni interval excludes zero over origin-day blocks only at the eight; at the six the whole-month interval also excludes zero.
  • Lead swap. L-1d, fold 2026-01, seed 0, 31 daily lag-free neural networks, CPU. K2-S1's lag-free heads cannot be swapped: experiment 454 stored their forecasts, not their weights.
  • No load-shift event plots. This experiment scores no event slice.
  • Not done. Part 3 (L-Pshare waits for experiment 519; L-lead-head is not supported by the lead swap and Part 2). Comparison with experiment 435's table P factors, which were fitted on other arms.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The long-lead gap may lie in the centre of the forecast rather than the band width. The lead swap moves L-1d's median by up to 4 points of capacity while its band stays put, and a per-band width correction recovers under 5% of the gap. The next experiment can test whether the advantage of K2-S1 and of experiment 454's five-head lag-free ensemble at days 5 to 10 comes from averaging several heads, by scoring the mean absolute error of each arm's median by lead.

docs.title: Can a weather-to-power network that never sees lead time, plus a small ensemble calibrator, match the single-stage lag-free demand network?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04, metering group). Every stage-2 arm on this page ran with the metering-group input set to 0 for all 16 Primaries, so none of them tested a group input. The code (e00524_stage2.group_flag) compared each Primary's group to "signed_six", but the label in the data is "signed-MW six", so the flag never matched. The stored stage-2 input tables confirm it: the group column is 0 in every training and test row of all 10 cache files (5 months, 2 seeds), checked by e00524_group_flag_check.py. Three kinds of arm are affected: the form-B arms (S2-F-B-nll and S2-F-B-crps) and the joint arms (S2-J-0.4x and S2-J-0.1x) had a constant group input in their multilayer perceptron, and the form-A arms (S2-F-A-nll and S2-F-A-crps) fitted one shift per lead bin shared by both groups, not one per group and lead bin. S2-0, S2-0F, L-Ww, and the other stored references have no stage 2 and are unaffected. The numbers on this page are correct as measurements of a calibrator without a group input, and every statement that the calibrator "sees the metering group" or has a per-group form should be read that way. This affects the form-A, form-B, and S2-J results, so the S2-J equivalence to L-Ww, the S2-F contrasts, P4, and the best arm all describe the group-free calibrator. The code is left as run, and a rerun with the corrected label is not queued.

Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532.

A weather-to-power network that never sees lead time or ensemble spread, fine-tuned together with a small calibrator, forecasts as well as the current single-stage lag-free network L-Ww; the same two parts with the first network frozen forecast worse. We split the lag-free demand network in two. The first network maps ERA5 and CAMS weather, the calendar, and the Primary substation to a probability distribution of power. It was trained on past-weather rows only and has no lead-time or spread input. A small second network takes that distribution plus the lead, the ensemble spread, the hour, and the metering group, and returns a corrected distribution. We scored five test months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) with weekly refits, two seeds, and CRPS in points of capacity (lower is better). The method builds on the lag-free network of experiments 448 and 510, and on experiment 449's cross-fit for the second network's training rows. Interim, unaudited numbers.

Verdict: partly supported. S2-J, with the first network fine-tuned together with the calibrator, is inside the minimum detectable effect (MDE) of L-Ww in all six group-and-band cells (equivalence holds). The pre-registered gain for the frozen arm S2-F (P1) did not appear: S2-F is worse than L-Ww. Several arms in the plan did not run (below).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms. S2-0: the stored L0PT network with no fine-tune (the CPU gate; keeps lead and spread). S2-0F: the new lead-free, spread-free first network alone. S2-F: S2-0F plus a second network trained on cross-fitted outputs, form A (a shift of the means and log standard deviations per group and 30-hour lead bin) or form B (2 x 32 multilayer perceptron), with the negative log-likelihood (nll) or the closed-form CRPS as loss. S2-J-0.4x and S2-J-0.1x: first network and form-B head fine-tuned together at 0.4x or 0.1x of the 5e-4 pretraining rate (0.4x is experiment 511's L-1d rate).
  • Absolute CRPS (eight / six), all lead bands. K2-S1 4.763 / 3.423; S2-J-0.1x 4.828 / 3.529; S2-J-0.4x 4.849 / 3.537; L-Ww 4.920 / 3.555; S2-F-B-nll 5.040 / 3.634; S2-F-B-crps 5.137 / 3.653; S2-0F 6.118 / 4.022; S2-0 6.287 / 4.041; S2-F-A-nll 6.168 / 3.924; S2-F-A-crps 6.071 / 4.041. The MDE of a two-seed pool is 0.164 (eight) and 0.123 (six).
  • Counted contrasts against L-Ww (18 tests; first minus second; negative is better). S2-J-0.1x: eight -0.075, -0.094, -0.098 and six -0.031, -0.021, -0.028 in the bands under 48 h, 48 to 120 h, and 120 to 240 h. S2-J-0.4x: eight -0.042, -0.057, -0.091 and six -0.011, -0.011, -0.024. S2-F-B-nll: eight +0.149, +0.137, +0.098 and six +0.107, +0.085, +0.063. The Bonferroni intervals exclude zero for S2-J-0.1x at the eight in all three bands (upper bounds -0.015, -0.038, -0.039) and for S2-J-0.4x at the eight only at 120 to 240 h (-0.029). No S2-J gain reaches the MDE, so none counts as a gain; the equivalence is the finding. S2-J-0.1x is better than L-Ww in 4 or 5 of 5 folds at the eight and 3 or 4 of 5 at the six.
  • Predictions. P1 (S2-F beats L-Ww at 120 to 240 h by 0.087 / 0.098): not supported, S2-F-B-nll is +0.098 / +0.063 worse. P2 (S2-J within the MDE): holds in every band. S2-J-0.4x closes 42% of the eight's 120 to 240 h gap to K2-S1 (0.091 of 0.215) and 10% of the six's; S2-J-0.1x closes 46% and 11%. P4 (form A recovers 70% of form B's gain over S2-0F): not supported; form A is +0.03 to +0.08 worse than S2-0F at the eight and recovers 8% to 32% of form B's gain at the six. P3, P5, P6, P7: not run (below).
  • What the calibrator adds. Form B minus S2-0F: -1.21, -1.09, -1.02 (eight) and -0.46, -0.39, -0.36 (six), in all 5 folds. S2-J-0.4x minus S2-F-B-nll: -0.19, -0.19, -0.19 (eight) and -0.12, -0.10, -0.09 (six). The nll loss beats the CRPS loss for form B by 0.05 to 0.13 at the eight (descriptive).
  • Tails (all leads; 95th and 99th percentile pinball loss / coverage, eight). L-Ww 1.015 / 0.964 and 0.287 / 0.995; S2-J-0.1x 1.014 / 0.958 and 0.285 / 0.993; S2-J-0.4x 1.027 / 0.959 and 0.293 / 0.993; S2-F-B-nll 1.092 / 0.954 and 0.309 / 0.991. Six: L-Ww 0.699 / 0.935 and 0.184 / 0.989; S2-J-0.1x 0.694 / 0.933 and 0.184 / 0.989. The two-stage tails match L-Ww's. The 1st and 5th percentiles, the tails by lead band, and the avoidable-curtailment cost were not computed.
  • Gate (S2-0). The stored L0PT weights with no fine-tune score +1.37 (eight) and +0.49 (six) CRPS above L-Ww, so fine-tuning on ensemble rows carries most of the skill.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Setup. Weekly refits, 90-day half-life, rows by experiment 510's rule (valid time at most 3.5 h before the cutoff, within 730 days), widening 1.15 applied by the scorer to every arm, cleaned data (1,179 scoring half-hours dropped as flagged exact zeros across the folds), the D15 and D18 cut from the rows of experiment 454. The contrasts are for weekly refits only. L-Ww, L-W, L-M, K2-S1 are stored predictions from experiments 510 and 454. Stage 1 and the cross-fit networks are saved under work/stage1 and work/stage1_crossfit (60 + 10 files) in the private data folder; the stage-2 and S2-J weights were not saved.
  • Cross-fit. Each second-network training row uses a first network that left out a 3-day-padded block of the history around its valid time (6 blocks per fold and seed). That network is slightly staler than the full one used at test, which may over-widen S2-F. The CRPS loss is in units of each Primary's standard deviation, so it weights low-variance Primaries more than nll does.
  • Not run (quota pause until Wednesday 2026-11-04 01:00 UTC). The stage-0 arms, S2-M, S2-R, the daily harness, the injected-shift leak, the eleven-quantile control, the 1st and 5th percentile tails, tails by lead, widths and the probability integral transform by lead, the avoidable curtailment cost, and the load-shift plots. They remain proposals.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 fired for P1; the page tests an explanation (S2-J minus S2-F above: the frozen first network cannot track recent demand). Trigger 3 was not checked: the mean-forecast error and the median-minus-mean forecast per site were not computed. The results review, the prose review, and the audit were skipped for quota, and every number is interim and unaudited. The author checked the quoted numbers once against the stored score tables. Trigger 7 applies to any later design that builds on S2-J's equivalence.
  • Seeds and statistics. Two seeds, five folds; the intervals resample 153 origin days, with the five whole-month blocks as a check (per-fold signs above). The Bonferroni count is 18.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so clean rows may hold events no label covers; this page scores no event slice.
  • What to try next. Run S2-M (51 members through the first network), the stage-0 weather adaptor, and the injected-shift leak once the quota returns. Test whether the S2-J head still helps against a lead-free network without a head, to see whether the head adds anything.

docs.title: Does telling the lag-free demand network whether a Primary reports signed MW or apparent power in MVA, with one 0/1 input column, improve its forecast?
docs.text:
Correction (2026-11-04). The gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead on this page is voided. K2-S1 mixes in experiment 404's lag-free head, which took its weather from the freshest run at each target's valid time (leads of 9 to 33 h at every horizon), a look-ahead that a forecast made at the origin does not have. The gap at 0 to 24 h is unchanged, and comparisons that do not involve K2-S1 are unaffected. The rebuilt K2-S1 will restate the gaps. Evidence: experiments 531 and 532. Telling the lag-free demand network whether a Primary reports signed MW or apparent power in MVA did not improve its forecast. M is the network with one 0/1 metering column (1 for MVA), C the same network with that column fixed at 0, P a copy with the column assigned to a random 8 of the 16 Primaries, and L-Ww the 37-input network. At the eight MVA-only Primaries, M scored worse than C by 0.038 points of CRPS (Bonferroni interval +0.019 to +0.058; lower is better), and P scored worse by 0.041, so the loss comes from adding a per-Primary column of that shape, not from metering type. At the six signed-MW Primaries M scored better than C by 0.030 (-0.060 to -0.001), and P did not (-0.009, -0.040 to +0.023). The flag did not cut the mixture's probability mass below zero at the eight. Every number on this page is interim and unaudited until a human has read it.

Verdict: not supported. P1 (no CRPS move at either group) and P2 (mass below zero halved) failed, and the falsifier P5 (M worse than C, with an interval excluding zero) held at the eight. The embedding is therefore not shown to be too thin.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute scores (CRPS, points of capacity; eight / six). L-Ww 4.920 / 3.555; C 4.875 / 3.556; M 4.913 / 3.526; P 4.915 / 3.547; K2-S1 4.763 / 3.423 for scale. Five folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0 and 1, weekly refits, experiment 470's intersection rows. C is experiment 519's stored F0z, reused unrefitted (a forced-zero check reproduced its forecast to 6e-6 on 53,760 rows). July 2026 unused. Scoring actuals dropped for a flagged exact zero: 1,179 half-hours across the five folds, as in experiment 519.
  • Counted family (Bonferroni, 8 tests), difference and interval. M - C CRPS: eight +0.038 (+0.019 to +0.058), six -0.030 (-0.060 to -0.001). M - C q99 pinball loss: eight +0.001 (-0.003 to +0.005), six -0.007 (-0.011 to -0.003). M - L-Ww CRPS: eight -0.006 (-0.028 to +0.014), six -0.029 (-0.054 to -0.005). M - L-Ww q99: eight +0.009 (+0.004 to +0.013), six +0.000 (-0.002 to +0.003).
  • Report-only family (Bonferroni, 12 tests). P - C CRPS: eight +0.041 (+0.016 to +0.066), six -0.009 (-0.040 to +0.023). M - P CRPS: eight -0.002 (-0.031 to +0.025), six -0.021 (-0.047 to +0.005). P - C q99: eight -0.008 (-0.012 to -0.005). C - L-Ww CRPS: eight -0.045, six +0.001 (this repeats experiment 519's F0 against L-Ww; M - L-Ww is confounded with that width and batch difference).
  • Minimum detectable effect. Experiment 511's two-seed values (0.164 at the eight, 0.123 at the six) are shown for scale only. The paired intervals above are tighter than those values, so an effect smaller than about 0.02 to 0.03 points could not have been detected.
  • Tail table (coverage at q01 / q05 / q95 / q99; eight, then six). C 0.002 / 0.017 / 0.961 / 0.994 and 0.001 / 0.011 / 0.935 / 0.988. M 0.002 / 0.018 / 0.961 / 0.994 and 0.001 / 0.011 / 0.941 / 0.991. q95 pinball loss rose at the eight (M - C +0.023, +0.012 to +0.035) and fell at the six (-0.020).
  • Mass below zero (mean of the mixture's mass below 0 MW over the scored half-hours; M / C / L-Ww). D8 0.0065 / 0.0046 / 0.0033; D12 0.0025 / 0.0026 / 0.0023; D22 0.00054 / 0.00031 / 0.00040. The M over C ratio was at most 0.5 in 1 of 10 fold-and-seed cells at D8, 2 of 10 at D12 (both seed 0), and 2 of 10 at D22, so P2 fails. D22's baseline mass is below 0.1%, so a halving is untestable there. At D8 the share of half-hours with q05 below zero rose from 0.2% (C) and 0.02% (L-Ww) to 2.1% (M).
  • D10 reverse-flow case study (single Primary). Only 3 of the 15 days since 2025-10 with a negative reading at D10 fall in the scored months (2,420 half-hours). The share of those half-hours whose q05 is below zero is 18.1% for M, 17.9% for C, 14.2% for L-Ww, and 15.9% for P; no median is below zero in any arm. D10's flag is 0 in both M and C, so the M - C difference is interference.
  • Choices. The flag is the 38th input (experiment 519 keeps the 37-input recipe). The group comes from the units column of the Primary table (D15 and D18 are MW and report-only). P is one random draw of the 8/6 split.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The plan review and one code review ran (Sonnet) and were triaged on the pull request; the code review found no blocking defect. A results review that re-derives the headline numbers, the audit triggers, and the write-up reviews were not run, on the manager's instruction to spend at most one review because the quota is tight. The median-minus-mean forecast check was not run.
  • No lookahead: the flag is a fixed fact about each Primary, and the pretraining and refit row assertions of the copied harness (rows past the cut equal 0) ran.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Two seeds and five folds leave seed-to-seed noise of 0.06 to 0.08 points (experiment 519), larger than the six's gain, so the six's -0.030 is a point estimate near the 0.03 margin set in the plan.
  • At the six, M and C have identical inputs (flag 0 in both), so the six's contrast measures interference through shared weights and noise, not information.
  • The mass is measured on every scored half-hour of the test rows, not only experiment 470's row set.
  • NGED load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Truncate or clip the mixture at 0 MW at the eight if forecasts must be non-negative.
  • Leave the Part 4 embedding options in their current order.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit)
docs.text:
• The metering flag is the 38th input, not the 39th. Experiment 519 (merged) keeps the 37-input L-Ww recipe as the base: its best arm F0 carried a source flag only as a constant column (0 in every ERA5-and-CAMS pretraining row, so its first-layer weights never trained), and its advice is to pretrain on ERA5 and CAMS rows alone. The recipe therefore has no source flag, and the metering flag is the only added column.
  • Arms. M: 38 inputs, the 37 lag-free columns plus a metering column read from the Primary index (1 for apparent power in MVA, 0 for signed MW), pretrained with it, fine-tuned weekly from those weights. M is pretrained with experiment 519's train_share at share 0 (8,192 ERA5 and CAMS rows per step), with the column derived from the Primary index, so M and C share the recipe, the width, and (with the same torch.manual_seed) the initial weights. C: experiment 519's stored F0 pretrains and F0z fits, reused unrefitted; its column is a source flag held at 0, which is a constant column here. A sanity check runs M's code path with the lookup forced to 0 and must reproduce F0z to float tolerance, and the row counts must match 519's. L-Ww: experiment 510's stored forecasts. The M minus L-Ww contrast is confounded with the width and batch difference that 519 documented (F0 minus L-Ww is -0.043 at the eight). P (report-only): the same network with a fixed random 8/6 assignment of the 16 Primaries to the flag, one draw, to separate "metering type" from "any extra per-Primary column". At the six, M and C have identical inputs (flag 0 in both), so the six's contrast tests interference and noise, not information.
  • Recipe. The L-Ww harness: ERA5-and-CAMS pretraining (experiment 448's rows and loop), weekly refit, 90-day half-life, restart from the month's pretrained weights, five folds (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0 and 1, weekly cadence because L-Ww is the weekly anchor. July 2026 stays unused. Cleaned data throughout, with the flagged exact-zero half-hours dropped (the count is printed per fold), and the D15 and D18 rows before 2025-03-01 cut.
  • Group of each Primary. The flag takes the metering unit of each of the 16 Primaries. The eight are D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, and D22; the six are D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16; D15 and D18 take the flag of their own metering unit (checked against the metering table before any fit) and are report-only. The code review checks the Primary-index-to-label mapping against sites() before any per-Primary number is quoted, because the earlier proxy inferred it.
  • Mass below zero. For each row, the sum over the three components of the softmax weight times the normal CDF of (z0 - mean_k) / std_k, with z0 = -target_mean / target_std of the Primary; no outlier component. It is not zero for a correct network, because demand sits near zero at the eight.
  • Inference-only baseline first (CPU, no GPU go needed). Load experiment 510's stored L-Ww fine-tuned state dicts (models/hl90), run them on the scored rows, and compute for each Primary the mixture's probability mass below zero (the mixture CDF at 0 MW after undoing the Primary's target standardiser), before any clipping. Report it per Primary at D8, D12, and D22. A Primary whose baseline mass is below 0.1% of rows cannot show a halving.
  • Reverse-flow case study at D10. Take the stored reverse-flow days of experiment 506 (part1_days_six, level 0: 15 of 117 days since 2025-10 at D10; D5 has 5 days in all, not enough) and report, for M, C, and L-Ww, the share of those days' half-hours whose forecast median or q05 is below zero beside the share of half-hours whose actual is below zero. It is a single-Primary case study.
  • Statistics. Paired contrasts over origin-day blocks as in experiment 519's scorer, Bonferroni family of 8 (above), the two-seed minimum detectable effect printed beside every contrast, per-fold signs reported, intervals worded as "not shown to move CRPS (interval a to b)". The Part 2 probe of experiment 522 (the leave-one-Primary-out linear probe of metering type from the embedding) is reported beside the result, not as a gate, once experiment 522 merges. Tail table: coverage and pinball loss at 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99. The load-shift reporting rule is not triggered, because no labelled event is scored.
