  • Figures. CRPS and q99 contrast of M minus C and M minus L-Ww with intervals (headline), the per-Primary mass below zero at D8, D12, and D22 for L-Ww, C, and M, the D10 reverse-flow days with the three forecasts, two example forecasts (day-ahead and 14-day, one Primary), and the per-fold signs.
  • Compute. About 0.4 GPU-hours: 20 pretrains (arms M and P x 5 folds x 2 seeds, 31 to 46 s each) and 100 weekly fine-tunes (2 arms x 5 folds x 2 seeds x 5 weeks, about 5 s each) plus the month builds; C costs nothing because 519 stored it. One GPU process under 8 GB (MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1). No fit starts before the manager's "GPU go". Experiment 510's L-Ww forecasts and weights and 519's F0 and F0z are reused, which saves 10 pretrains and 50 fine-tunes. Code changes: a 16-long flag lookup in sites() order (asserted), a with_flag variant that appends lookup[p] in pretraining, validation, GpuMonth, and the test rows, and a mixture-mass function.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review before the first fit, a results review that re-derives the headline numbers, and two write-up reviews.

docs.title: Do trailing temperature windows beat a shuffled-day placebo on cold nights in the lag-free demand neural network, with five seeds, four summer folds, and the checks experiment 515 did not run?
docs.text:
Take-home: on cold winter nights at the eight MVA-only Primaries, trailing temperature windows lowered the error of the lag-free demand neural network by a small amount more than a shuffled-day placebo of the same three columns did, but the margin is only just above what the seeds can resolve, so the next step is a check on more winters at the eight.

A Primary is a primary substation of NGED's electricity distribution network. The eight MVA-only Primaries report power in MVA with no sign, and the six signed-MW Primaries report power in MW with a sign. We asked whether the cold-night gain of experiment 515's trailing temperature windows came from the windows' content or merely from giving the neural network three extra columns. "W-T" gives the lag-free demand neural network (one that reads no recent power) the means of temperature over the previous 6, 24, and 72 hours. "W-Tnull" gives it the same three columns filled with the temperatures of a randomly drawn other day. "W-noise3" gives it three columns of random numbers, and "W0" is the plain network. We compared the four on the 10 winter test months of experiment 515, with 5 seeds and then 11 seeds, and on 4 summer months. Cold nights are half-hours below 5 °C between 18:00 and 08:00 local time. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score in points of effective capacity, and a negative difference favours the first arm. The "seam check" compares W-T with a build that fills the hours before the forecast origin with the run's first value ("W-seam").

Maintainer decision. The pre-registered adoption rule was not met, because the seam check failed narrowly (below). The maintainer's decision, relayed by the manager, is to adopt W-T for the first-release recipe despite that failure. This experiment changed no recipe, serving code, or dependency pin and records results only, so adopted_in stays none until a model release is cut.

  • Primary (registered): W-T minus W-Tnull, cold nights, eight. 5 seeds: -0.104, bootstrap 95% interval [-0.168, -0.040], 8 of 10 folds negative. 11 seeds: -0.093 [-0.133, -0.053], 9 of 10 negative. Without 2024-11: -0.086 [-0.123, -0.045]. The 5-seed point estimate is above the registered -0.12 line, so the 5-seed result reads as a tighter interval and not as a verdict. The intervals are month-block bootstraps over 10 folds, so they are near min-to-max.
  • Minimum detectable effect (seed spread only), eight, cold nights, pooled over 10 folds: 0.140 at 5 seeds and 0.083 at 11 seeds (all rows: 0.104 and 0.062).
  • Predictions. P1 (point estimate -0.05 or lower): passes. P2 (W-noise3 minus W0 inside plus or minus 0.118): passes, +0.014 [-0.075, +0.105]. P3 (seam, all rows, within plus or minus 0.02): fails, W-seam minus W-T is +0.030 [+0.002, +0.071] at the eight and +0.026 [-0.002, +0.060] at the six (experiment 515 also failed it at 3 seeds).
  • Against the other comparators (eight, cold nights, 5 seeds). W-T minus W0 -0.152 [-0.300, -0.062] (experiment 515 found -0.150). W-Tnull minus W0 -0.048 [-0.189, +0.047], so about a third of the gain over W0 also appears with shuffled days at 5 seeds, and almost all of that comes from fold 2024-11 (W-Tnull minus W0 -0.683 there). W-T minus W-noise3 -0.166 [-0.384, -0.055] (Bonferroni-21), 10 of 10 negative. W-null minus W0 -0.047; W-T minus W-null -0.105 [-0.358, +0.176].
  • Absolute CRPS (11 seeds, cold nights / all rows). Eight: W0 4.557 / 5.351, W-T 4.441 / 5.290, W-Tnull 4.534 / 5.312. Six: W0 3.373 / 4.108, W-T 3.305 / 4.062, W-Tnull 3.329 / 4.060.
  • The placebo contrast resolves nowhere else (5 seeds unless stated). All rows at the eight: W-T minus W-Tnull -0.020 [-0.106, +0.095]. All rows at the eight, W-T minus W0 does resolve: -0.062 [-0.092, -0.027] at 11 seeds, so W-T is no worse than +0.03 (adoption condition ii, also met at the six: -0.047 [-0.169, +0.060] at 11 seeds). Six cold nights: W-T minus W-Tnull -0.064 [-0.243, +0.127]. Summer (4 folds): warm sunny W-T minus W-Tnull -0.047 at the eight and -0.010 at the six, intervals spanning zero. W-S and W-X minus W0 on cold nights at the eight (-0.079, -0.055) do not resolve.
  • Tails (eight, cold nights, W-T minus W0). q95 pinball loss -0.030 [-0.039, -0.015], q99 -0.010 [-0.017, -0.001]; the share of actuals below the q95 forecast rises by 0.008 [0.001, 0.016] and below the q99 forecast by 0.001 [-0.0001, 0.002]. Horizon bands (all rows, eight): days 4 to 10 -0.060 [-0.155, +0.016], earlier bands about -0.02.
  • Fold 2024-11 gives W-T minus W0 -0.83, but W-T minus W-Tnull is -0.147 there and -0.101 without it, so the placebo contrast does not depend on that fold. Folds 2025-11 and 2026-01 favour W-Tnull.
  • Weather inputs and timing. Every window column comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin, as in experiment 515's causality check (later runs removed, same result). This experiment did not repeat that check row by row.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (eight, cold nights, points of capacity): W0 +0.139, W-T +0.093, W-Tnull +0.102, W-null +0.108, W-noise3 +0.142; all rows +0.21 to +0.29. The mixture mean sits slightly above the median for every arm, so the spread does not shift the forecast by more than 0.3 points.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside CRPS: W-T minus W0 mean error -0.238 [-0.454, -0.095] and median error -0.203 [-0.457, -0.058], the same sign as the CRPS contrast. W-Tnull minus W0 mean error -0.072 includes zero. The refit that supplies the mean for seeds 0 to 2 reproduced experiment 515's quantiles to within 0.00003. The mean is not available for W-S, W-X, and W-seam.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 fired: the placebo W-Tnull gained 0.048 on cold nights, mostly in fold 2024-11. No audit was run, to save quota. The result is worded as a small gain only just above the minimum detectable effect, and a reader should weigh the missing audit.
  • Bonferroni. 1 primary test at 0.05; a secondary family of 21 tests (the W-T minus W-null, W-noise3, and W-Tnull contrasts at the registered slices). Everything else is descriptive and uncorrected.
  • Caveats. W-noise3 columns are frozen across seeds, so its intervals are narrower than a re-drawn noise arm's. Event labels are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events. Warm sunny rests on 4 summer month blocks. W0 for 2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03 seeds 0 to 2 comes from experiment 513's P0. No example forecast shows a metered generator. W-noise9 was not run.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Check W-T at the eight on a longer history (more winters) before relying on a 0.09-point gain.
  • Repeat with a nine-column noise arm only if the W-null contrast needs a column-count control.
  • The six signed-MW Primaries need a different test: no window arm resolved there at 11 seeds.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit that produced a quoted number)
Question
docs.text:
Experiment 515 (result page) gave a lag-free neural network the trailing means of temperature over 6, 24, and 72 hours (W-T) and found a cold-night CRPS gain of 0.150 points at the eight MVA-only Primaries. A placebo that gave every row the nine window columns of a randomly drawn other day (W-null) gained 0.071, so the real windows did not resolve from the placebo. That comparison confounded the content of the columns with their number (three real columns against nine shuffled ones), used three seeds, and had no summer fold. It also did not run the median-minus-mean forecast check, the mean-forecast error beside each contrast, or the example forecast graphs.

This experiment repeats the comparison with a placebo matched to W-T's three columns, five seeds, a column-count control, four summer folds, and the missing checks. It adds files only: no e00515_* file is edited, and every output goes to this experiment's own folder, because the 515 scorer lists arms by scanning its own work/seed_preds/*.

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• The primary comparator is W-Tnull: the shuffled-day version of exactly W-T's three columns, drawn with the same donor days as W-null. W-null (nine columns) is a secondary comparator.
  • W-noise3 is three frozen independent standard-normal columns, the same for every training seed. It controls the number of columns, not their content, so the W-T minus W-noise3 leg of the adoption rule is easier to pass than the W-Tnull leg. Noise columns are appended unscaled, because they already have mean 0 and standard deviation 1. A nine-column noise arm is the follow-up if the W-null contrast needs a column-count control.
  • The seam check of the adoption rule needs W-seam at 5 seeds, so W-seam seeds 3 and 4 run on the 10 winter folds. They start from W-T's pretrained weights and need no pretraining.
  • The mean-forecast refit needs only fine-tunes, because experiment 515 stored the pretrained weights of W0, W-T, and W-null for seeds 0 to 2 (and experiment 513 stored P0's for the three reused folds).
  • The new scorer e00526_score.py replaces 515's hard-coded 20 tests with 1 primary and 21 secondary tests and reads 515's forecast files by path, without scanning 515's folders. The new fit script subclasses 515's Fold, because W-Tnull needs the temperature columns of the placebo array and W-noise3 needs unscaled columns.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Every arm starts from the 37 non-lag columns and is pretrained from scratch with its added columns, in experiment 513's P0 loop, as in 515.

Arm Added columns Role W0 none Control W-T 3 trailing temperature means (6, 24, 72 hours) The candidate W-Tnull The same 3 columns, taken from a shuffled other day (515's donor rules) Primary comparator W-null 515's 9 shuffled columns Secondary comparator W-noise3 3 frozen independent N(0,1) columns Column-count control W-S, W-X 515's trailing shortwave means; the temperature-by-shortwave product Carried over from 515 W-seam W-T with persistence fill before the origin Seam check

W-noise3 columns are drawn once per fold and stage from a fixed seed, so they carry no information about demand.

docs.title: Folds and seeds
docs.text:
• Winter folds (10): 2024-11, 2024-12, 2025-01, 2025-02, 2025-03, 2025-11, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-02, 2026-03, as in 515. Each reports with and without 2024-11.
  • Summer folds (4): 2025-05, 2025-07, 2025-09, 2026-04. The refit cutoff is the start of the test month. Every fold scores only valid times before 2026-07-01, and July 2026 is unused. Summer folds add no cold nights, so they serve the warm-sunny slice only.
  • Seeds: 5 (0 to 4) for W0, W-T, W-Tnull, W-null, and W-noise3 on the winter folds, then 11 (0 to 10) for W0, W-T, and W-Tnull (approved extension). Seeds 0 to 2 of W0, W-T, W-null, W-S, W-X, and W-seam are read from 515 (W0 for 2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03 from experiment 513's P0) and are not refitted. Summer folds fit every arm at all 5 seeds. The harness skips any forecast that exists, so more seeds can be added later without refitting.

docs.title: Statistics (pre-registered)
docs.text:
• Primary: 1 test, W-T minus W-Tnull, cold nights, the eight, level 0.05. The month-block bootstrap resamples the 10 winter folds, each carrying its 5-seed mean.
  • Secondary family: 21 tests, Bonferroni-corrected. W-T minus W-null at five slice-and-group pairs: eight and six on all rows, eight and six on cold nights, and six on cold-sunny. W-T minus W-noise3 and W-T minus W-Tnull at eight and six on all rows, cold nights, cold sunny, and warm sunny (8 + 8 tests). The primary cell appears in both the primary and the family, which is conservative. Fold sets: all rows, cold nights, and cold sunny use the 10 winter folds; warm sunny uses the 4 summer folds, so those 8 tests rest on 4 month blocks and read as weak. W-S, W-X, W-null minus W-Tnull, and W-noise3 minus W0 are descriptive. D15 and D18 are report-only.
  • Minimum detectable effect at 5 seeds, from the single-seed spread of 515 (0.215 all rows, 0.300 cold nights per fold): one fold 0.267 and 0.371; pooled over 10 folds 0.084 and 0.118. The scorer recomputes them from the five seeds and prints them beside every contrast.
  • State plainly: the primary is not resolvable at 5 seeds. Its standard error is about 0.06, so the 95% half-width is about 0.12 and the 80%-power minimum detectable effect about 0.17, against an observed 515 contrast of -0.079. The 11-seed extension for W0, W-T, and W-Tnull costs about 1.7 to 1.9 GPU-hours and is part of this plan.
  • Lead bands: day 1, days 2 to 3, days 4 to 10, as 515 scored.
  • Rows: experiment_526_v1 repeats 515's row rules (cleaned data, the D15 and D18 start cut, leads up to 240 hours, no labelled event) and keeps the rows every core arm holds.
  • Widening: 1.15 about the median for CRPS, as in 515.

docs.title: Checks that 515 did not run
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per arm. The mixture mean is sum(exp(log_w) x mean) as in e00510_common.py, converted to a fraction of capacity. Every new fit saves the mean column beside the quantiles, and the seeds 0 to 2 forecasts of W0, W-T, and W-null are refitted from the stored pretrained weights (90 fine-tunes). The refit's quantiles are compared with 515's stored quantiles, so the check also reports whether the fine-tune reproduces.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each CRPS contrast (absolute error of the mean, in points), through the same interval code.
  • Example forecast graphs: a cold night, a cold sunny day, and a warm sunny day at a Primary (substations only; no metered generator).
  • Peak resident memory of the first fold, measured with /usr/bin/time -v.

docs.title: Run order and cost
docs.text:
The GPU runs in stages, each started only on the manager's "GPU go". One GPU process under 8 GB (MemoryMax=8G, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1). A fit pair (pretrain plus fine-tune) takes about 22 seconds, plus 13 to 35 seconds of row building per fold and stage. This experiment runs before experiment 516's GPU fits.

Stage Contents Pairs Estimate (GPU-hours) 1 Winter seeds 3 and 4 of W0, W-T, W-null 60 0.4 2 Winter W-Tnull and W-noise3 at 5 seeds 100 0.7 3 11-seed extension: seeds 5 to 10 of W0, W-T, W-Tnull, winter 180 1.3 4 W-S and W-X, winter seeds 3 and 4 40 0.3 5 Four summer folds, 7 arms at 5 seeds 140 1.0 6 W-seam seeds 3 and 4, winter 20 fine-tunes 0.05 7 Mean refit of seeds 0 to 2 of W0, W-T, W-null, winter 90 fine-tunes 0.15

The total is about 3.9 GPU-hours, of which the core 5-seed comparison (stages 1 and 2) is 1.1.

docs.title: Reuse and standing practices
docs.text: Stored forecasts reused: 515's seeds 0 to 2 of W0, W-T, W-null, W-S, W-X, and W-seam, and 513's P0. Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 start cut apply. Refits are monthly. Fitted networks are saved in the experiment's private data folder. July 2026 is unused. Generators are not scored. The reviews follow the ml-experiment skill: a Sonnet plan review, a Sonnet code review before the first fit, a Sonnet results review, an audit if a trigger fires, and two Sonnet write-up reviews.

docs.title: What closes the gap between the lag-free demand network and the demand models that use recent power?
docs.text:
The lag-free neural network L-1d scores 0.2 to 0.3 points of capacity worse (CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score) than the lag-enabled network A-pool at 24 to 120 h lead for the eight Primary substations metered in MVA only, and adding the day-ago and week-ago lags closes 76% to 83% of that gap (point estimates). Experiments 527 to 539 tested whether head count, recency, restart, refit cadence, network family, or the weather's age explain the gap. The next step is to decide whether the lags are worth a larger injected load-shift leak (5.68 against 4.49 points of capacity for the day-ago and week-ago lags, in one seed). Verdict: supported. Every number on this page is interim and unaudited: no experiment in the series has had a code or write-up review.

Names used below. L-1d is the daily-refit lag-free neural network of experiment 511. A-pool is the same family of network with 9 lag inputs (the newest value, the same half-hour a day ago, and the same half-hour and weekday a week ago, each with a missing flag and an age), refitted monthly, of experiment 425 arm A. K2-S1 is the mixture of lagged and lag-free heads of experiment 521. The eight are the MVA-only Primaries and the six the signed-MW Primaries. R1, R-DW, and R9 are L-1d with the newest-value lag, the day-ago and week-ago lags, and all 9 lag inputs added at fine-tuning. A-nolag is A-pool with its 9 lag inputs removed. A lead is the time between the forecast origin and the target. CRPS is in points of capacity, and a positive "arm minus reference" means the arm is worse.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• (a) K2-S1's edge at 120 to 240 h was a look-ahead (experiments 531 and 532). Experiment 404's lag-free heads, which K2-S1 contains, took the weather for a target's valid time from the freshest run, so a target 5 to 10 days ahead got weather issued about a day before the target, which is 4 to 9 days after the forecast origin. Scoring L-1d with that weather lowered its 120 to 240 h CRPS at the eight from 5.140 to 4.940 (-0.201, interval -0.369 to -0.059) and, in the point estimate, removed its whole gap to K2-S1 (0.174 to -0.027; the Bonferroni-widened interval of the CRPS change, -0.452 to +0.008, includes zero). At the six it closed 58% of the gap (0.196 to 0.081; the CRPS change, -0.114, has an interval that includes zero). Scoring the 404 head with the weather of the run available at the origin raised its 120 to 240 h CRPS by 1.124 (interval 1.027 to 1.210) at the eight. Five such heads averaged are 1.0 worse than K2-S1 at the eight and 1.1 at the six. Every gap to K2-S1 above 24 h of lead is therefore not a valid forecast comparison. K2-S1 with an origin-time lag-free half was not scored.
  • (b) Head count, recency, restart, cadence, and a richer stage 2 do not explain the gap (experiments 527 to 530, 534, 536). Experiments 527 to 530 measured their factors against K2-S1, so finding (a) means they speak to K2-S1's look-ahead and not to A-pool. Within that frame, four daily seeds closed 11% (eight) and 21% (six) of the 120 to 240 h gap to K2-S1 (527). Recency half-lives of 365 days or none, a from-scratch restart, and weekly or monthly refits all widened the gap, and daily beat weekly beat monthly (529). A stage 2 that sees every stage-1 input sat 0.576 above K2-S1 at the eight (528). The network ladder pointed to the weather's age, which 531 confirmed (530). Against A-pool directly, a shorter half-life raised the eight's 120 to 240 h CRPS monotonically (90 days 5.140, 30 days 5.169, 14 days 5.228, 7 days 5.277, 3 days 5.386; A-pool 5.058), and 180 days was no better than 90 (534 for 3 to 90 days, 536 for 180 days).
  • (c) A-pool beats L-1d by 0.2 to 0.3 points at 24 to 120 h at the eight, and the lags carry it (experiments 533 and 537). L-1d minus A-pool is +0.288 (interval +0.189 to +0.374), +0.254 (+0.171 to +0.332), and +0.200 (+0.102 to +0.300) at 24 to 48 h, 48 to 72 h, and 72 to 120 h, with 5 of 5 folds positive in each band. At 120 to 240 h the gap is +0.082 (-0.034 to +0.213), which is not shown. At the six L-1d is not shown to differ from A-pool, except at 12 to 24 h (+0.196). On cold nights at the eight the point estimate is larger, +0.535 at 24 to 48 h. Only three folds have cold nights, and the interval overlaps the all-rows interval. Removing A-pool's 9 lags raises its CRPS by +0.567, +0.512, and +0.454 points in the same three bands (every interval excludes zero, 5 of 5 folds). That network, A-nolag, is then worse than L-1d by 0.255 to 0.279. A-nolag differs from L-1d in cadence and half-life as well as in lags, and experiment 537 does not split those factors.
  • (d) The day-ago and week-ago lags close most of the gap, and the newest value does not (experiments 538 and 539). At the eight, with lags added at fine-tuning only, the share of the gap closed at 24 to 48 h, 48 to 72 h, and 72 to 120 h is 24%, 26%, and 28% for the newest value, its flag, and its age (R1); 76%, 79%, and 83% for the day-ago and week-ago lags with their flags and ages (R-DW); and 82%, 85%, and 87% for all 9 lag inputs (R9). R1 minus A-pool excludes zero in all three bands (5 of 5 folds). R-DW minus A-pool excludes zero only at 24 to 48 h (+0.069, interval +0.016 to +0.122). R9 minus A-pool includes zero in all three bands. At the six, R1 and R9 are level with A-pool at 24 to 240 h. Outside that range, R9 is better at 6 to 12 h (-0.179) and R1 is worse at 12 to 24 h (+0.113).
  • (e) The lags raise the injected load-shift leak (experiments 538 and 539). In the stress world a shift of plus or minus 3 standard deviations of the Primary's 7-day mean is added to the targets and to every lag whose observation time falls in a 7-day block. Averaged over all leads, the median forecast moves by 4.49 points of capacity for L-1d, 4.52 for R1, 5.38 for R9, and 5.68 for R-DW. At block age 0 the figures are 7.20 (L-1d), 10.7 (R9), and 11.5 (R-DW). The day-ago and week-ago lags are the route, because R1 adds none measurable. These figures are descriptive. They come from one seed and five folds, and the fold ranges overlap (all leads: L-1d 2.6 to 10.5, R1 2.3 to 10.3, R9 2.2 to 11.3; no range was stored for R-DW).

docs.title: What was tried
docs.text:
The Bonferroni count is the number of counted contrasts in the experiment's own correction.

Experiment Question Finding Bonferroni count 527 Do more daily lag-free heads close K2-S1's 120 to 240 h edge? 11% (eight) and 21% (six) of the gap closed 56 528 Does a stage 2 that sees every stage-1 input close it? No: 0.576 above K2-S1 at the eight 126 529 Do recency, restart, or cadence close it? No: every change widened the gap 168 530 Does the network family or the weather's age explain the edge? Weather age: the ladder's first step raises CRPS by 0.88 at 120 to 240 h at the eight 30 531 Is the edge a look-ahead? Yes in the point estimates: all of the eight's gap, 58% of the six's 28 532 Does an origin-time lag-free network match K2-S1? No: 1.0 (eight) and 1.1 (six) worse at 120 to 240 h 280 533 How big is L-1d's gap to A-pool on the same rows? +0.200 to +0.288 at 24 to 120 h at the eight 28 534 Does heavier recency weighting close the gap to A-pool? No at the eight; not shown at the six, apart from 12 to 24 h 70 535 What differs between A-pool and L-1d? Code reading only: lags are the largest difference none 536 Does a 180-day half-life help? No: no better than 90 days 14 537 What does A-pool lose without its lags? +0.454 to +0.567 at 24 to 120 h 28 538 Do the newest value, or all 9 lags, close the gap when added to L-1d? 24% to 28% and 82% to 87% 56 539 Do the day-ago and week-ago lags alone close it? 76% to 83% 28

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Weather from the run issued at or before the origin, row by row. This page fits nothing and scores nothing. Experiments 538 and 539 passed it row by row on every test and training row. Experiment 537 passed it on the scored rows only. Experiments 532, 534, and 536 passed it on a 48,000-row sample of the shared feature source. Experiment 539, for example, asserted it on all 153 test origins and 25.0 million training rows. Example row from experiment 539: target 2025-10-03 07:00 UTC, origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC. The 404 head's freshest-run weather is the violation found, and finding (a) is about it.
  • Lags observed at or before the origin minus 3.5 h. Experiments 538 and 539 passed this row by row. Example from 539: origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, target 2025-10-01 12:30 UTC, day lag observed 2025-09-30 12:30 UTC.
  • Figures. Figure 1 rescales the stored arm-minus-A-pool intervals by the stored point estimate of L-1d minus A-pool (0.288, 0.254, 0.200), so its intervals ignore the uncertainty in that denominator. Figure 2 plots the stored means. e00540_figures.py holds every plotted number with the experiment it came from.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Every experiment in the series is interim and unaudited. Intervals are 95% month-block bootstraps with 5 blocks, which is near the minimum to the maximum of the five folds.
  • Experiments 538 and 539 add the lags at fine-tuning only, from zero first-layer weights. Pretraining with the lags was not tried. They use two seeds, and they do not replicate A-pool's row cuts (about 2,900 of 4.9 million rows in 2026-01 and the D15 and D18 weekly-lag start cut). The remaining 0.03 to 0.05 points between R9 and A-pool are not attributed.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events. The minimum detectable effect from L-1d's two-seed spread (0.10 to 0.27) is a proxy for each arm's own.
  • D15 and D18 are report-only, and the standing numbers for them are in each experiment's tables.
  • The look-ahead finding rests on experiment 531's refit of the 404 head, which reproduced the stored table to 5.2e-06.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: The injected-shift leak is the drawback of the lags. One open question is whether a lag network that gives less weight to lags inside a shifted block keeps the 76% to 83% gain at a lower leak. The maintainer decides whether to run it.

docs.title: How much of K2-S1's score survives when its lag-free heads use only weather from the run issued at or before the forecast origin?
docs.text: Take-home message: K2-S1's advantage over the daily lag-free network L-1d at 5 to 10 days is not there once its weather is limited to what was known at the forecast origin. With the lag-free heads still trained on the old weather, K2-S1 is 0.48 (eight) and 0.51 (six) points of capacity worse at 120 to 240 h, which isolates the look-ahead. With the heads retrained on origin-time weather the loss is 0.43 and 0.41, and also includes the missing lead input. By point estimate K2-S1 is then worse than L-1d in every lead band, but the Bonferroni intervals include zero except at the eight for 12 to 24 h, so L-1d is not shown to be better elsewhere. The next step is a lag-free head that also sees the lead time. Verdict: partly supported (see "Predictions"). Terms: the eight are the 8 Primaries with MVA-only (megavolt-ampere) telemetry and the six the 6 with signed-MW telemetry; K2-S1 is experiment 454's mixture of two lagged S1 and two lag-free heads; L-1d is experiment 511's daily-refit lag-free network; A-pool, A-pool minus lags, and R-DW are the networks of experiments 533, 537, and 539.

docs.title: What was rebuilt
docs.text:
• Unchanged S1 heads. The S1 heads of experiment 454 already read weather from the run issued at the forecast origin, and their lag inputs sit at or before the origin. The S1 heads also read experiment 404's frozen lag-free table at past lag times only, which is not a look-ahead.
  • Heads trained on look-ahead weather. The lag-free heads (experiment 404's "further" module, seeds 0 to 2) are refitted with experiment 531's code, which reproduced the stored table to 5e-6. They are trained as experiment 404 trained them, on the freshest run published before each valid time, and fed origin-time weather when scored. Call this the first rebuild.
  • Heads trained on origin-time weather. The same module, loss, seeds, epochs, recency weights, and short-history cut, trained on experiment 397's rows instead: one row per Primary, forecast origin, and valid time, with origin and valid time before the refit date, leads up to 240 h, and no lead input (about 5 million rows per refit). Call this the second rebuild. The second rebuild was added after the first rebuild's scores were read, at the manager's request, so its predictions were not registered beforehand.
  • Cells. Experiment 454's three seed pairs, each an equal-weight mixture of two S1 heads and two lag-free heads. Code reused from experiments 404, 454, 521, and 531 (copied into this folder).
  • Weather check. All 1,142,520 rows on which the lag-free heads were scored (before the row filters of experiment 511's scoring) were matched to the summary of the run initialised at origin minus 9 h, with all 14 weather columns equal. Example: Primary D2, origin 2026-06-01 09:00 UTC, target 2026-06-07 15:30 UTC, run initialised 2026-06-01 00:00 UTC and published 09:00 UTC, lead 150.5 h, mean shortwave radiation 444.776 in both the table and the run. The check ties each row to its summary row, whose stored origin is the run time plus 9 h. The training rows of the second rebuild select origin and valid time before the refit date by assertion.
  • Rows. Rows with no labelled event, experiment 511's row set, five folds of 511, July 2026 unused. Eight means the 8 Primaries with MVA-only (megavolt-ampere) telemetry, six the 6 Primaries with signed-MW telemetry.

docs.title: Scores
docs.text: Differences are rebuilt minus old K2-S1, in points of CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, lower is better). Each cell shows the difference, the Bonferroni-widened month-block interval, the folds with a positive difference, and the minimum detectable effect (MDE): 1.96 sqrt(2) sd / sqrt(3), where sd is the standard deviation of the three cells' per-fold means. The pre-registered Bonferroni count was 28; it is 56 (4 counted contrasts, 7 bands, 2 row sets). Intervals are month-block bootstraps with 5 blocks (near the minimum to maximum of the folds). The cells share seeds, so the MDE is optimistic.

docs.title: Heads trained on look-ahead weather, minus old K2-S1
Heads trained on origin-time weather, minus old K2-S1
Heads trained on origin-time weather, minus L-1d
Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (same score as the old K2-S1 below 24 h, inside the MDE). Held for the first rebuild: the largest difference is 0.042 against an MDE of 0.12. Failed for the second rebuild at the eight (12 to 24 h: +0.085 against an MDE of 0.07, interval +0.03 to +0.15; 0 to 6 h: +0.193 against 0.16, interval -0.04 to +0.50, which includes zero). Retraining on all leads without a lead input may cost short-lead skill that the day-ahead feed gave the old heads; this is not tested.
  • P2 (a fall of about 0.17 at the eight and 0.20 at the six at 120 to 240 h, within 0.05). Failed for both rebuilds: +0.477 and +0.508 for the first, +0.433 and +0.413 for the second. The falls are 2.1 to 2.8 times the prediction. The pre-registered P2 failed under both rebuilds; the direction was right.
  • The 24 h boundary is not sharp. The 24 to 48 h difference for the first rebuild at the eight is +0.081 (interval +0.006 to +0.137), which exceeds its MDE of 0.07 and barely clears zero.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• No rebuild has a lag-free head that sees the lead time, and L-1d does. The gap to L-1d therefore mixes the loss of the look-ahead with the missing lead input.
  • The second rebuild trains on about 10 origins per valid time, so about 10 times as many rows and gradient steps as experiment 404's head, and each valid time is weighted by its origin count. That confounds any comparison of the two training feeds.
  • The "report" row set (D15 and D18) in the stored tables is not part of the Bonferroni count.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events.
  • The comparison with A-pool minus lags in the absolute table is a comparison of different networks. Only A-pool against A-pool minus lags isolates lags (5.058 against 5.430 at the eight, 3.717 against 3.995 at the six, 120 to 240 h).

docs.title: Correction table: gaps to K2-S1 that change
docs.text: Gap = reference CRPS minus K2-S1 CRPS in points of capacity (positive: K2-S1 is better). Each cell reads: old K2-S1 → rebuilt with heads trained on look-ahead weather → rebuilt with heads trained on origin-time weather. Point estimates only.

docs.title: Experiments whose gap to K2-S1 used the old weather
docs.text:
The sibling task that writes correction notes on those pages uses this list. Classified from each page's headline only, so each entry is a pointer and not a conclusion.

  • The conclusion that a model stays behind K2-S1 may not survive: 510 (L-Ww behind K2-S1 by 0.156 and 0.132 over all leads), 511 (L-1d behind by 0.091 and 0.071), 521 (K2-S1 advantage at 120 to 240 h). The retrained K2-S1 is worse than both L-1d and L-Ww at 24 h and beyond by point estimate, but only where intervals exclude zero should a flip be stated. A negative gap means K2-S1 is the worse forecast. Below 12 h K2-S1 was already behind L-Ww and L-1d at the eight in the old scores, and the retrained heads widen those gaps.
  • Probably stands, being lag-free against lag-free or about short-lead events: 519, 523, 524, 525 (lag-free contrasts); 468 (events, lead not stated in the headline).
  • Not assessed: 470, 527, 529, 530.

docs.title: Which earlier pages used experiment 404's look-ahead weather, and which headlines depend on it?
docs.text: Almost every earlier lagged-power page rests on experiment 404's lagless forecast, whose weather came from the freshest run at each target's valid time (a look-ahead). Above 24 h of lead the lagless forecast, B-mix, and K2-S1 on those pages look better than a forecast made at the origin can be. Experiments 531 and 532 confirmed the look-ahead and found experiment 425A's weather clean. This experiment lists which pages are affected, adds a dated correction note to the 17 whose headline depends on the table, and leaves the other 6 unchanged. It fitted and scored nothing.

docs.title: Pages whose gap to K2-S1 used the look-ahead weather
docs.text:
Each of these has a correction note at the top of its result.md.

Experiment Note 468, 470, 510, 511, 521, 523, 524, 525, 519 Gap to K2-S1 above 24 h voided; 0 to 24 h unchanged; comparisons without K2-S1 unaffected. 527, 529, 530 Not on main: the pages are not merged, so there is no page to correct. The same note belongs on each when its page merges.

docs.title: Dependants of experiment 404's table and of experiment 425A
docs.text:
"404 table" means the cross-fitted lagless table built by e00404_lagless.py (or a copy in e00445_lagless.py), which takes each target's weather from the freshest run published before the target's valid time. "425A" means the rows of experiment 397's summary tables, which experiment 532 checked row by row against the run published at the forecast origin.

Experiment Weather source Headline depends on it? docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The classification reads each page's scripts and take-home message, not the stored forecasts, so a page marked "No" is a judgement about its contrast, not a rescore.
  • No weather input was recomputed in this experiment. Experiment 532's row-by-row assertion covers 397's summary tables (the feature source of 425A, A-pool, and 428) and not 425's ERA5 and CAMS pretraining rows, which are not forecasts.
  • Triggers in "Audit before merge": none fired, because nothing was scored.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The rebuilt K2-S1 on origin-time weather should restate the gaps above 24 h of lead and the lagged-versus-lagless gain on the pages marked "Yes".

docs.title: Can an auxiliary head that predicts the recent power level, or the reverse flow, close the gap between the lag-free demand network and the lagged forecast without lag inputs at forecast time?
docs.text:
Training a demand neural network without lagged-power inputs to predict the recent power level as a side task did not help it forecast. Its continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, the quality measure of a probabilistic forecast, here in percentage points of substation capacity; lower is better) was 0.049 points worse than the same network without the side task, averaged over the eight substations whose power is metered only as apparent power (MVA) and over forecasts 24 to 72 hours ahead. None of the 0.271-point gap to the neural network that reads lagged power closed. The reverse-flow side task scored 0.017 worse and the two side tasks together 0.059 worse. The next step is to give the network the day-ago and week-ago lags as inputs, as experiment 539 did, because the recent level was not learnable as a side task in this test.

We asked whether a lag-free demand network can recover what lag inputs tell a lagged network without receiving them at forecast time. We added extra outputs to the last layer of experiment 511's best lag-free network (L-1d) and trained them on power values from before each row's forecast origin, which the network never sees as inputs. F1 predicts the newest observed power at the origin, the day-ago power, and the week-ago power (three standardised values; this follows Caruana (1997) in sharing hidden layers between a main and a side task). F2 predicts whether power at the target time is below -0.005 of capacity (a reverse flow), where the sign is metered. F3 has both heads. Each side loss has weight 0.5. Scores are on experiment 511's five folds of one month each, 2 seeds, rows with no labelled event.

Verdict: refuted. The pre-registered prediction was that F1 would close at least half of the gap between L-1d and A-pool (the lagged network of experiment 425) at lead 24 to 72 h at the eight, meaning F1 minus A-pool of at most +0.144 and +0.127. F1 minus A-pool was +0.345 and +0.295. F2 was predicted to change the eight by less than the minimum detectable effect (0.135), and it did (+0.017). F3 was predicted to be no better than F1 and F3 was 0.010 worse.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Lead 24 to 72 h, CRPS (points of capacity) Eight Six F1 (recent-level head) 4.574 3.234 F2 (reverse-flow head) 4.541 3.226 F3 (both heads) 4.584 3.236 F1-w01 (post hoc: F1 with weight 0.1) 4.530 3.220 L-1d (no head; experiment 511) 4.525 3.219 R-DW (day-ago and week-ago lags as inputs; experiment 539) 4.314 3.129 A-pool (lagged network; experiment 425) 4.254 3.142
  • F1 minus L-1d is +0.049 at the eight (month-block interval +0.035 to +0.061, 5 of 5 folds worse, minimum detectable effect 0.135) and +0.016 at the six (+0.008 to +0.024, 5 of 5 folds).
  • F3 minus L-1d is +0.059 at the eight (+0.040 to +0.074, 5 of 5 folds) and +0.018 at the six (+0.002 to +0.033, 4 of 5 folds). F2 minus L-1d is +0.017 at the eight (+0.004 to +0.028, 4 of 5 folds).
  • The gap that had to close is L-1d minus A-pool: +0.271 at the eight (+0.182 to +0.352, 5 of 5 folds) and +0.077 at the six (-0.015 to +0.160, 3 of 5 folds).
  • Interval method. The intervals are 95% month-block bootstraps with 5 blocks, which is close to the range from the best fold to the worst fold. The Bonferroni count is 56 (4 counted contrasts, F1 minus A-pool, F1 minus L-1d, F2 minus L-1d, and F3 minus L-1d, times 7 bands times 2 sets). The minimum detectable effect (0.135 at the eight) is two to three times every contrast above, so one contrast alone could not detect a gain or loss of that size; the fold signs (5 of 5 worse for F1 and F3 at the eight) are the stronger evidence. At lead 24 to 120 h, F1 minus L-1d is positive in every band at the eight.
  • Injected-shift leak (511's stress world, 7-day block of 3 times the weekly-mean standard deviation, seed 0, mean of five folds): F1 3.88, F2 3.96, F3 3.81, L-1d 4.49 points of capacity. The pre-registered limit was 4.99. The point estimates are lower for every head (the fold ranges overlap L-1d's, so a reduction is not shown), on day 1 (4.3 against 5.4) and on days 2 to 3 (3.7 to 3.8 against 4.6) alike. We did not test why.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only) scored 10.42 for F1, 10.28 for F2, and 10.36 for F3 at lead 24 to 72 h, against 10.37 for L-1d. F2 is 0.09 better there, where reverse flow is common; this was not tested. July 2026 was not scored and not tuned on.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Weather inputs. Every row's weather comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin, asserted for all 153 test origins. Example: target 2026-06-07 15:30 UTC, origin 2026-06-01 09:00 UTC, weather run 2026-06-01 00:00 UTC. The 9 lag columns are removed from the network inputs before training and scoring; they remain only as training targets, each observed at least 3.5 hours before its origin (asserted row by row).
  • Targets match the cleaned power. After rounding the lag time to the half-hour grid, 100% of kept side targets equal the cleaned power at that time; targets whose cleaned power is missing were dropped (about 0.1% of rows), and so were values clipped at 5 standard deviations.
  • Reverse-flow labels. The label exists at the six and at D15 and D18 and is masked at the eight. Reverse flow is rare at the six (at most 0.26% of half-hours at any one Primary, from a one-off look at the cleaned power that is not stored), so most positive labels come from D15, which is report-only. F2 therefore had little to learn from, which is a reason its effect is small, not a finding about reverse flow.
  • Explanation tested (trigger 2). F1 with weight 0.1 (post hoc, not in the plan, not counted in the Bonferroni count) scored +0.005 against L-1d at the eight (+0.002 to +0.008) and +0.001 at the six. The harm is smaller at the lower weight but does not vanish (the interval still excludes zero), and neither weight tested gives a gain. The weight 0.5 was fixed before any score; no other weight was run. The gradient clipping includes the side gradients, a small difference from L-1d besides the extra outputs, which the design cannot avoid.
  • Error of the mean or median. Not computed: no contrast here points in a direction that a quantile-score disagreement could reverse, because every arm shares the same mixture output.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired (the result contradicts the prediction) and the weight test above is the explanation; the other triggers did not. No audit was run, because the explanation was tested and no later experiment's design depends on this result's sign.
  • Not done. The rebuilt K2-S1 (experiment 541) was not stored when this ran, so it is not a comparator. The research default's absolute scores against BG2 and manual_heuristic are in experiments 511 and 539. Lead range: 6 to 240 h; the headline concerns 24 to 72 h.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Which of the day-ago and week-ago lag inputs, in what reduced form, keeps most of experiment 539's 76% to 80% gap closure while leaking an injected load shift least.

docs.title: Can a median of the same half-hour over past days, or training with the power readings randomly removed, make the lag-light demand network less sensitive to load-shift events and to missing readings without losing its gain?
docs.text:
Averaging the same half-hour over several past days did not make the lag-light demand network safer, and randomly removing the readings in training cost most of its gain. The question was whether two changes to experiment 539's network (the lag-free network plus the day-ago and week-ago power readings) keep its gain and cut its sensitivity to load-shift events. R-MED replaces the two readings by medians of the same half-hour over the last 7 and 28 days. R-DROP removes all six reading inputs in 30% of rows during training. All numbers are interim and unaudited, in points of capacity; lower CRPS is better.

Verdict: not supported. P1 failed on both parts, P2 failed, and P3 held.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Pre-registered predictions. Judged in the 24-48 h, 48-72 h, and 72-120 h bands at the eight. P1 (R-MED within 0.03 of R-DW, leak at most 5.2): failed. R-MED minus R-DW is +0.060, +0.056, and +0.040, and the leak is 7.02. P2 (R-DROP with readings present keeps 90% of R-DW's closed gap): failed. R-DROP closes 31%, 37%, and 40% of L-1d's gap to A-pool, which is 40%, 47%, and 48% of R-DW's closed gap. P3 (R-DROP with readings absent costs at most 0.15 more than L-1d): held. It is 0.028, 0.028, and 0.015 below L-1d.
  • Absolute CRPS at the eight, 24-48 h / 48-72 h / 72-120 h. A-pool 4.197 / 4.311 / 4.538; R9 4.249 / 4.349 / 4.565; R-DW 4.266 / 4.363 / 4.572; R-MED 4.326 / 4.419 / 4.612; R-DROP 4.397 / 4.471 / 4.659; R-DROP absent 4.457 / 4.537 / 4.723; L-1d 4.485 / 4.565 / 4.738; manual_heuristic 5.543 / 5.406 / 5.568. The full table, every band, and the six are in the stored scores/absolute.csv.
  • Counted contrasts at the eight (95% month-block bootstrap, 5 blocks, near min-to-max; Bonferroni count 42 = 3 contrasts x 7 bands x 2 sets; minimum detectable effect 0.13, 0.14, 0.10). R-MED minus R-DW: +0.060 (+0.041 to +0.093; 5 of 5 folds worse), +0.056 (+0.016 to +0.104), +0.040 (+0.009 to +0.074). R-DROP minus R-DW: +0.131 (+0.046 to +0.277; 5 of 5 folds worse), +0.109 (+0.043 to +0.240), +0.086 (+0.024 to +0.244). R-DROP absent minus L-1d: -0.028 (-0.087 to +0.024), -0.028 (-0.079 to +0.031), -0.015 (-0.066 to +0.019). The R-MED contrasts are smaller than the minimum detectable effect, so their sign is consistent across folds but their size is not firmly established.
  • At the six the contrasts are inside the minimum detectable effect: R-MED minus R-DW +0.008, +0.015, +0.005; R-DROP minus R-DW +0.011, 0.000, -0.017 (all intervals include zero). R-DROP absent minus L-1d is +0.028 (+0.006 to +0.054), +0.027, +0.031 (+0.004 to +0.061).
  • Injected-shift leak (experiment 511's stress world, seed 0, five folds, all leads). L-1d 4.49, R1 4.52, R-DROP 4.97, R9 5.38, R-DW 5.68, R-MED 7.02. At block age 0 the leak is 7.20 (L-1d), 9.23 (R-DROP), 11.49 (R-DW), and 11.90 (R-MED). The leak of R-MED is above R-DW's at every block age from 0 to 6. A likely reason, not tested here, is that the 7-day median has most of its members inside the 7-day shifted block, so the whole shift enters the input for several days.
  • Checks. Every power value and every median member is at least 3.5 h older than the origin, asserted for all rows (24,979,347 training rows and 1,142,520 test rows); 2,000 random rows per month recomputed with an explicit loop matched the medians. Every weather input comes from the run issued at or before the origin (nwp_init_time <= power_fcst_init_time asserted for all 153 test origins and every training origin). Example test row: origin 2026-01-01 09:00 UTC, target 2026-01-01 15:00 UTC, weather run 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC, day-ago reading observed 2025-12-31 15:00 UTC. Cost under 1 GPU-h, one process under 8 GB.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet code review before the first fit found a crash in the checks writer, a cache key that could be reused across months, and a missing empty-window marker for the absent scoring; all three were fixed. No results review and no write-up review were run, because the quota is tight, so the numbers are unaudited.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Two seeds and five folds; the leak is one seed. R-DROP and R-MED differ from R-DW only in the six inputs, so the fit-to-fit noise of 539 applies.
  • R-DROP's dropout is drawn once per refit, not once per epoch, and covers the early-stopping rows. "Flag 0" in the brief was read as "present flag 0", which is the missing flag set to 1.
  • The 4-week median is the 28 most recent days at the same half-hour, and the 7-day median the 7 most recent, with at least 10 and 3 members observed; other choices were not tried.
  • Experiments 538 and 539 are unmerged, so R-DW and R9 numbers come from their private tables.
  • NGED load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events, and the leak is measured on injected shifts only.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Guard the day-ago and week-ago readings with a shift detector's probability (nullify the lag when the probability is high), then measure the leak and CRPS together.
  • Accept experiment 539's leak of 5.68 if it stays under the 6-point limit, since neither variant improved both numbers.

docs.title: Does splitting the lag-free demand network into a weather encoder, a datetime encoder, and a mixer, with or without auxiliary forecast heads, improve the day-ahead to five-day-ahead forecast?
docs.text:
Splitting the demand neural network into a weather encoder, a datetime encoder, and a mixer improved the forecast one to five days ahead at the eight primary substations whose readings are in MVA (apparent power) by 0.14 to 0.21 points of capacity (CRPS, lower is better), against the single multilayer neural network L-1d. The network used no past power as input. Most of that gain stayed when the new mixer learned at the same rate as L-1d. The network also has a higher point estimate of the injected-shift leak (7.6 against 4.49 points of capacity, with overlapping fold ranges), and more than half of the gain at the eight comes from one substation, D8. The auxiliary heads did not help at the eight.

We asked whether a neural network built from three parts forecasts better than L-1d, the single-network daily-refit forecaster of experiment 511. The weather encoder sees only the forecast weather and the substation's embedding. The datetime encoder sees only the calendar, the holidays, and the sun's position. A mixer joins the two. The network is first trained on estimates of past weather (ERA5 and CAMS), with a mixer that sees nothing else. That mixer is then discarded. A new mixer, which also sees the spread of the ECMWF ENS ensemble weather forecast and the lead time, is trained on ENS forecasts. A second network (M1) adds a small forecasting head after each encoder. Every arm refits daily with a recency weight that halves every 90 days, and averages 2 seeds, as L-1d does. Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity, on rows with no labelled event. "The eight" are the MVA-only primary substations and "the six" are the signed-MW primary substations.

Verdict: partly supported. The modular network without auxiliary heads (M0) forecast better than L-1d, where prediction P1 expected it within 0.05 points. M1 did not beat M0, so prediction P2 failed. The decision rule bounds the injected-shift leak at L-1d's 4.49 plus 0.5, and every modular arm's point estimate exceeds that.

docs.title: Arms and prediction results
docs.text:
• M0: weather encoder, datetime encoder, and mixer, with no auxiliary heads.
  • M1: M0 plus an auxiliary mixture head after each encoder, each with weight 0.25.
  • M0lr (post hoc control, added after M0 scored): M0 with the fresh mixer's learning rate set to L-1d's fine-tuning rate, 2e-4, instead of 5e-4.
  • M2 (not run): one pooled network over the Primaries and the bulk and grid supply points. The input matrices and cleaned-power stack hold the 16 Primaries only, and building them for the four supply points is a data-preparation task.

Prediction P1 (M0 within 0.05 of L-1d at 24-120 h at the eight) failed in the better direction. M0 was 0.208, 0.182, and 0.137 better than L-1d.

Prediction P2 (M1 beats L-1d by at least 0.05 in each of the three bands) failed. M1 beat L-1d by 0.170, 0.133, and 0.089, but its interval at 72-120 h includes zero and its leak is 7.30. The stop rule (M0 more than 0.05 worse than L-1d) did not fire.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The table shows CRPS at the eight, the mean of 5 folds and 2 seeds. Each arm row adds, in brackets, the contrast against L-1d (negative is better), its Bonferroni month-block interval, and the number of folds in which the arm is worse. The bootstrap has 5 month blocks, which is near min-to-max, and 28 tests are counted (2 counted contrasts, M0 and M1 against L-1d, times 7 lead bands times 2 sets). The leak column is the injected-shift leak of experiment 511's stress world (seed 0, all leads, points of capacity), whose fold ranges are 2.59 to 10.47 for L-1d, 2.44 to 17.48 for M0, 2.74 to 16.75 for M0lr, and 1.72 to 16.13 for M1. The minimum detectable effect is 0.134 at 24-48 h, 0.139 at 48-72 h, and 0.101 at 72-120 h.

Arm 24-48 h 48-72 h 72-120 h Leak, all leads L-1d 4.485 4.565 4.738 4.49 M0 4.277 (-0.208; -0.374 to -0.098; 0/5) 4.383 (-0.182; -0.327 to -0.116; 0/5) 4.601 (-0.137; -0.296 to -0.055; 0/5) 7.60 M0lr 4.312 (-0.173; -0.371 to -0.052; 0/5) 4.421 (-0.144; -0.335 to -0.012; 0/5) 4.638 (-0.100; -0.298 to +0.060; 1/5) 7.71 M1 4.316 (-0.170; -0.365 to -0.053; 0/5) 4.431 (-0.133; -0.327 to -0.001; 1/5) 4.649 (-0.089; -0.316 to +0.100; 1/5) 7.30 R-DW (experiment 539, L-1d plus day-ago and week-ago power) 4.266 4.363 4.572 5.68 A-pool (experiment 425, lagged power) 4.197 4.311 4.538 not run

Most of the gain is not the learning rate. M0lr keeps 0.173, 0.144, and 0.100 of M0's 0.208, 0.182, and 0.137, and M0 minus M0lr is -0.035, -0.038, and -0.037 (the interval excludes zero only at 24-48 h, by 0.002). M0 reads no power, yet lands near R-DW, which reads day-ago and week-ago power.

The learning rate does not explain the higher leak. M0lr leaks 7.71, almost M0's 7.60. The leak could come from the fresh mixer or from the separate encoders, and this experiment cannot tell which.

At the six signed-MW Primaries, the gain is smaller and less certain. At the six, M0 minus L-1d is -0.117, -0.095, and -0.043 and the intervals include zero except at 24-48 h; M1 is -0.183, -0.148, and -0.102 there.

One Primary carries about half of the gain at the eight. Leaving D8 out, M0's mean contrast over 24-120 h falls from -0.166 to -0.071, M0lr's from -0.129 to -0.043, and M1's from -0.121 to -0.021. Leaving any other Primary out leaves M0 between -0.163 and -0.209. The sign holds at 7 of 8 Primaries for M0 and M0lr and at 5 of 8 for M1. D15 and D18 (report-only) show M0 scoring 9.891 over all leads against 10.876 for L-1d.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Inputs, with no power or target-time quantity. The weather encoder reads the 7 ensemble-mean columns mean_shortwave, mean_longwave, mean_temperature_2m, mean_dew_point_temperature_2m, mean_pressure_surface, mean_precipitation, and mean_wind_speed_10m, plus the 8-wide substation embedding. The datetime encoder reads cos_zenith, sin_azimuth, cos_azimuth, sin_hour, cos_hour, sin_hour_2, cos_hour_2, dow_1 to dow_7, covid, christmas_inside, christmas_days, christmas_tent, bank_holiday, nearest_days, and nearest_inside, plus the embedding. The fine-tuning mixer reads both encoder outputs, the embedding, the 7 ensemble-spread columns std_*, and lead and lead_sqrt. None is derived from power; the 9 lag columns are removed (non_lag_layout), and the only target-time inputs are the calendar and sun position of the target half-hour, which a forecast made at the origin knows.
  • Origin-time weather, asserted row by row. For every test origin (153) the script asserts nwp_init_time <= power_fcst_init_time, power_fcst_init_time == origin, and that the weather-run summary file exists; for every training origin it asserts the file exists 9 hours before the origin and that the target is after the origin (check totals in checks_M0.json). Example, 2025-10 test row: target 2025-10-03 07:00 UTC, origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC.
  • Audit triggers (the skill's seven conditions that call for an independent audit before merge). None fired: P1's contradiction was tested by M0lr and recorded; D8 shrinks the gain without flipping its sign; M1 does not beat M0 in the 24-120 h bands, and its gap to M0 there is inside the interval. No audit ran. The skill also asks for the median minus mean forecast per site and for the contrast on the error of the mean forecast; neither was computed, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Not done. No forecast-example figure was drawn. The rebuilt K2-S1 (experiment 541) had no stored predictions when scored. The fresh mixer's initialisation is the same for every seed (seed 12345), so seed spread excludes mixer-initialisation variance. Only one learning-rate control was run.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
Which part of the modular network makes it follow recent data harder (the fresh mixer, or encoders that see weather and calendar apart), and does the gain at the eight hold without D8. Compute used: about 1.2 GPU-hours in all (pretraining, fits, and stress runs of M0, M1, and M0lr).

The code is in ml-experiments/00545-modular-lag-free-demand-network-weather-and-datetime-encoders/ and reuses experiments 397, 428, 448, 510, 511, and 539 (the scorer and the stress script).

docs.title: Can a demand network that sees no recent power learn what a network with day-ago and week-ago power knows, by being trained on that network's forecasts?
docs.text:
A demand network that sees no recent power did not learn what a network with day-ago and week-ago power knows, even when trained on that network's forecasts, so the lags must stay an input at forecast time. We asked whether a lag-free "student" network could be taught by a "teacher" network that reads the power from the same half-hour a day ago and a week ago. The student was fine-tuned on a loss that gave half its weight to the real target and half to draws from the teacher's forecast distribution. The teacher is R-DW of experiment 539, which closed 76% to 83% of the gap between the lag-free network L-1d and A-pool. The student follows experiment 511's L-1d recipe, with the same rows and the same pretrained weights. The idea is knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015).

Verdict: refuted. At the eight MVA-only Primaries the student scored 0.028, 0.013, and 0.026 points of capacity (CRPS) worse than L-1d at 24-48 h, 48-72 h, and 72-120 h, so it closed a negative share (-8%, -5%, and -10%) of L-1d's gap to A-pool. The pre-registered stop rule (under 15% on the first 2 folds) ended the experiment after folds 2025-10 and 2025-12. The other 3 folds, the injected-shift leak, and the rebuilt K2-S1 comparison were not run. Every number is interim and unaudited.

docs.title: Results (first 2 folds, the eight)
docs.text:
• Student minus L-1d: +0.028 (24-48 h), +0.013 (48-72 h), +0.026 (72-120 h), +0.012 (120-240 h). Intervals are month-block bootstrap with 2 blocks (the range of the 2 folds): 0.017 to 0.039, 0.003 to 0.023, 0.011 to 0.041, and -0.001 to 0.026. Both folds are positive, except at 120-240 h (1 of 2). The minimum detectable effect is 0.21, 0.21, 0.15, and 0.18, so the differences are far below what the experiment could resolve; they show no gain, not a loss.
  • Absolute CRPS at 24-48 h: student 4.552, L-1d 4.524, teacher 4.257, A-pool 4.177. At 72-120 h: 4.753, 4.727, 4.581, 4.464.
  • At the six (signed MW) the student is also 0.027 to 0.052 worse than L-1d at 24 to 240 h.
  • The Bonferroni count is 28 for the counted contrasts of this scoring script. No interval here was widened to it, and the claim does not rest on one.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Weather input for every row comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin, asserted row by row for 62 test origins and all training origins. Example: target 2025-10-03 07:00 UTC, origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC. The teacher's lags were observed at or before origin minus 3.5 h, also asserted per row. The student has no lag column.
  • The teacher fitted on the same rows it labels, so its forecast on them is sharper than on new rows. The 0.5 weight on the real target limits the effect. A student cannot beat an honest teacher and did not match it.
  • Median-minus-mean forecast, tail scores, and the leak were not computed because the experiment stopped. No audit trigger was tested beyond the prediction itself: a refuted prediction has one untested explanation, that the lag information is not recoverable from the weather and calendar inputs. One seed pair, one teacher weight (0.5), and one loss form were tried.
  • Cost: about 0.15 GPU-h for the 2 folds. Code review: one Sonnet review, all five findings triaged (four applied, one a design note).

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a robust same-slot summary (the median of the same half-hour over the last 4 weeks) keeps the lags' gain with a smaller injected load-shift leak than the 5.68 points of the day-ago and week-ago lags.

docs.title: Does a blend of the lag-free neural network L-1d and the lag-light neural network R-DW, with one weight per lead band fitted on earlier folds, forecast better than either network alone?
docs.text:
Averaging the lag-free network L-1d with the lag-light network R-DW, with a fixed weight per lead band, forecasts no better than R-DW alone. We asked whether the two networks make different enough errors that their blend beats both. The blend averages the 11 stored quantiles of each network (mixture parameters are not stored), with the weight on R-DW fitted on the earlier folds and applied to the next. Nothing was fitted except the weights, and no new forecasts were made.

Verdict: not supported. At the eight MVA-only Primaries and 24-120 h, the blend scored 4.404 points of capacity (CRPS) against R-DW's 4.403 and L-1d's 4.597. The pre-registered gain was at least 0.05 below both parents in each of 24-48 h, 48-72 h, and 72-120 h, and the blend minus R-DW was +0.003, +0.002, and -0.002 in those bands (positive means the blend is worse). The blend does clear 0.05 against L-1d (-0.21, -0.21, and -0.17), so only the R-DW half of the rule fails. The first fold (2025-10) supplies weights only, so everything below is the four folds 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. July 2026 is unused. Every number is interim and unaudited.

docs.title: Results (four scored folds)
docs.text:
• Eight, blend minus R-DW: +0.003 (24-48 h), +0.002 (48-72 h), -0.002 (72-120 h), +0.000 (24-120 h). The 24-120 h interval is -0.018 to +0.013 (month-block bootstrap, 4 blocks, near min-to-max), with 3 of 4 folds positive (the blend worse) and an MDE of 0.04. The difference is far below both the 0.05 goal. The per-band MDE (0.054 and 0.057 at 24-48 h and 48-72 h) is above 0.05, so a per-band test could not resolve a gain of 0.05.
  • Eight, blend minus L-1d: -0.19 at 24-120 h (interval -0.28 to -0.11, 0 of 4 folds positive); that difference is R-DW's own gain over L-1d, not a gain from blending.
  • Six (signed MW, rows with no labelled event): blend minus R-DW is -0.001 to -0.004 in each of the three bands (-0.002 at 24-120 h, interval -0.016 to 0.006, MDE 0.08); blend minus L-1d is -0.06 at 24-120 h.
  • Weights: at the eight the fitted weight on R-DW is 1.0 at 6-24 h, 0.8 to 1.0 at 24-72 h, 0.7 to 0.8 at 72-120 h, and 0.5 to 0.6 at 120-240 h (figure 2). At 120-240 h the blend is -0.010 from R-DW (interval -0.064 to 0.052).
  • A fixed half-half blend is worse than R-DW at the eight (+0.041 at 24-120 h, interval 0.006 to 0.086): equal weights move the forecast towards the worse network.
  • Versus A-pool at the eight, 24-120 h: blend +0.021 (interval -0.027 to 0.061).
  • Cold winter nights (eight, 24-120 h, 13,092 rows): blend 3.976, R-DW 3.945, L-1d 4.318. 22-31 December (fold 2025-12 only, 15,360 rows, so one fold): blend 3.987, R-DW 4.062, L-1d 3.975.
  • Tails (eight, 24-120 h, blend): the share of actuals below q01 is 0.25% (nominal 1%) and below q05 is 1.5% (nominal 5%), and the share below q95 is 96.2% (nominal 95%) and below q99 is 99.4% (nominal 99%). The lower tail is therefore about 3 to 4 times too wide in coverage terms, and the upper tail is close to nominal.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only), 24-120 h: blend minus R-DW +0.084 (folds -0.16, +0.14, +0.33, 0.00); blend minus L-1d -0.92.
  • Counted tests: 28 (2 contrasts x 7 bands x 2 sets). No interval above is widened to that count, and no claim rests on one.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Weather inputs: none are read here. Both networks used the weather run issued at or before the forecast origin, asserted row by row in experiment 539's checks. This script asserts that every weight was fitted on earlier folds only and prints one example row: fold 2025-12, Primary 0, origin index 109602, target index 109705 (lead 51.5 h), weight 0.9, L-1d median 0.786, R-DW median 0.791, blend median 0.790, actual 0.892 (fractions of capacity).
  • The parents' CRPS recomputed from the stored quantiles matches experiment 539's stored per-row CRPS to under 0.01 on every row (asserted).
  • The weights come from quantile averaging with walk-forward weights. The four scored months are not contiguous, so earlier folds are not always the same season. Four month blocks are near the min-to-max of the folds.
  • The first fold is not scored. The MDE comes from the two seeds of each parent, blended with the same weights.
  • The avoidable-curtailment cost was not computed. The related experiment 458 (a weight per lead band on the lag-free forecast in a lagged and lag-free mixture) also found no gain.
  • Code review: one Sonnet review of the pull request, findings triaged in the pull request.
  • Cost: no GPU, under 1 minute on 2 cores.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a blend of R-DW with a network of a different kind, such as K2-S1 rebuilt on origin-time weather (experiment 541), has errors different enough to give the 0.05 gain.

docs.title: Does the daily-refit lag-free demand network with trailing temperature windows get within reach of the lag-enabled network, once weather is limited to the run issued at the forecast origin?
docs.text:
Take-home message: adding recent temperature to the daily-refit neural network that sees no recent power lowered its error a little in every lead band, although no interval excluded zero. At 120 to 240 hours ahead its error was inside the minimum detectable effect of the same neural network given recent power. At 0 to 120 hours ahead, for the eight Primaries metered in MVA only, its CRPS stayed 0.13 to 0.34 points of capacity worse. The verdict is partly supported by the predictions below: the pattern predicted (a gap at 24 to 48 hours, none at 120 to 240 hours) held, and the size predicted for the temperature columns' gain narrowly missed.

We asked how good a demand forecast can be when its neural network sees no recent power (it is "lag-free"), only weather that was known at the forecast origin. We assembled the parts that earlier experiments had found useful: pretraining on past weather estimates, a refit every day with a 90-day half-life, three columns holding the mean temperature over the last 6, 24, and 72 hours (experiment 526), and bands widened by 15% at scoring. We scored the result on the five test months of experiment 511 against the same neural network without the temperature columns (L-1d), the neural network that also sees recent power (A-pool), the neural network with only the day-ago and week-ago power lags (R-DW, experiment 539), and the rebuilt K2-S1 (a mixture of lagged and lag-free neural networks) of experiment 541.

Terms. E is the assembled neural network. The eight are the eight Primary substations with MVA-only (megavolt-ampere, unsigned) telemetry, and the six are the six with signed-MW telemetry. D15 and D18 are two further Primaries with short histories, reported separately. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score in points of capacity (percentage points of a substation's capacity; smaller is better). A-pool is experiment 425's arm A as scored in experiments 533 and 537. Each row is one forecast of one Primary's power for one valid time from one forecast origin. The scored set holds 1,142,520 rows with no labelled event, from the five test months of experiment 511. July 2026 was not used.

How intervals are built. Each interval resamples whole months in five blocks, so it spans nearly the minimum to the maximum of the folds (a fold is one test month). It is widened for 42 counted comparisons (3 contrasts, 7 lead bands, 2 row sets), which is the Bonferroni correction. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is the smallest difference between two networks that the spread between the two seeds, over the folds, could reliably resolve; a difference inside the MDE is not shown.

docs.title: Predictions (written before any score was read)
docs.text:
• P1, met; the gap at 24 to 48 h was smaller than predicted. E minus A-pool at the eight is +0.031 at 120 to 240 h (interval -0.125 to +0.200, MDE 0.16), inside the MDE. At 24 to 48 h it is +0.205 (+0.138 to +0.283, MDE 0.13), above the MDE but below the predicted +0.23 to +0.27.
  • P2, narrow miss. E minus L-1d at the eight is -0.083 and -0.084 at 24 to 48 h and 48 to 72 h, just outside the predicted -0.08 to 0.00; the other bands from 24 h are inside it. No interval at the eight excludes zero, as predicted.
  • P3, met. E minus the rebuilt K2-S1 at 120 to 240 h at the eight is -0.310 (-0.584 to +0.058), not shown different from zero (1 of 5 folds positive).
  • P4, met. The injected-shift leak of E is 4.55 points of capacity over all leads, against 4.49 for L-1d (threshold 4.99) and 5.68 for R-DW.

docs.text:

The full tables are in this experiment's private scores/ folder.

  • Cold winter nights, the eight (report-only, no correction). Only three test months hold cold winter nights (2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03), so each interval is the minimum to maximum of three folds. E minus L-1d is -0.169 over all leads (-0.221 to +0.103; 1 of 3 folds positive), which is about 2.6 times the -0.065 over all rows and is not shown different from zero. E minus A-pool is +0.148 (+0.076 to +0.207), a larger gap than over all rows.
  • Tails, the eight. The q95 and q99 pinball loss of E minus L-1d is within 0.013 of zero in every band (q99 within 0.007). The share of rows below the q95 forecast is 0.967 for E, 0.968 for L-1d, and 0.952 for A-pool. The widened bands of E and L-1d are therefore somewhat wide at the top.
