docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Arm E. Experiment 511's L-1d (daily refit at 00:00 UTC, 90-day half-life, two seeds, five folds) with three columns appended after the 37 lag-free columns: the mean ensemble temperature over the 6, 24, and 72 hours ending at the valid time (experiment 515's previous-seam tables). Code reused from the folders of experiments 397, 428, 510, 511, 515, 521, and 539. Weights stored under this experiment's private data folder.
  • Pretraining. E starts from W-T pretrained weights: experiments 515 and 526's for 2025-12, 2026-01, and 2026-03, and this experiment's for 2025-10 and 2026-06 (same code). L-1d starts from experiment 510's pretrained weights, so the E minus L-1d contrast measures the temperature columns and the new pretrained weights together. W-T is experiment 515's name for the three columns.
  • Origin-time weather, row by row. Every training and test row's weather run was issued 9 h before its origin and the target follows the origin (asserted for all 24,979,347 training rows and 1,142,520 test rows; nwp_init_time <= power_fcst_init_time for all rows of all 153 test origins). The window columns use only that run and earlier runs. Example (2025-12 test row): origin 2025-12-31 09:00 UTC, target 2026-01-08 08:30 UTC, weather run 2025-12-31 00:00 UTC.
  • Dropped, with reasons. The four-head mixture, because experiment 527 found head count does not explain the gap. Per-lead widening, because experiment 523 found at most 0.024 points from it. A two-stage ensemble calibrator, because no stored follow-up of experiment 524 supports it.
  • Not scored. Experiment 526's ten winter folds hold no L-1d, A-pool, or R-DW scores.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean forecast beside CRPS: not computed. The fitted forecasts store 11 quantiles and no mean column, so audit trigger 3 of the ml-experiment skill (the quantile and mean contrasts pointing in different directions) cannot be assessed.
  • Triggers fired: the miss on P2 (audit trigger 2, a result contradicting its prediction) is 0.003 to 0.004 points. Its likely explanation is that E also starts from different pretrained weights than L-1d; this was not tested. No audit was run. Leave-one-fold-out checks were not run; the fold signs above show E minus L-1d negative in 4 of 5 folds.
  • Caveats. Two seeds, five folds, one stress seed. The comparison with L-1d mixes the windows with new pretrained weights. Labelled events are incomplete: the logs of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may still hold one. No example-forecast figure is included because arm E stores forecasts without the actual power; experiments 511 and 523 show the day-ahead and 14-day forecasts of the same network without the windows.
  • Lead range. The forecasts cover 0 to 240 h, which spans the NGED 1 to 10 day horizon.

docs.title: Open question after this experiment
docs.text: The data does not say whether a neural network with both the temperature columns and the day-ago and week-ago power lags would close the 0 to 120 hour gap with less injected-shift leak than R-DW has. Down-weighting lags near a flagged event is one way to test it.

docs.title: Does a blend of the lag-light network R-DW with the retrained K2-S1 beat both, and did any stored blend with climatology help at 120 to 240 hours?
docs.text: Averaging R-DW with the retrained K2-S1 gains 0.022 points of capacity at 1 to 5 days, under the 0.05 we asked for, and no stored blend of climatology into a demand network helped at 5 to 10 days. Part 1 asks whether two demand networks of different kinds make errors that cancel. Part 2 asks whether earlier experiments found that climatology helps at long lead. The result is partly supported for Part 1; Part 2 stops, as pre-registered. Every number is interim and unaudited.

docs.title: Part 1: blend of R-DW and the retrained K2-S1
docs.text:
The blend averages the 11 stored quantiles of R-DW (experiment 539) and of each of the three cells of the retrained K2-S1 (experiment 541, heads trained on origin-time weather), with the weight on K2-S1 fitted per group and lead band on earlier folds only. The code is a copy of experiment 547's (ml-experiments/00549-k2-s1-blend-and-climatology-stored-check/). CRPS is in points of capacity, on rows with no labelled event, for the four folds 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06; the first fold (2025-10) only supplies weights. July 2026 is unused.

  • Eight, 24-120 h: blend 4.381, R-DW 4.403, K2-S1 4.776, A-pool 4.382. Blend minus R-DW -0.022 (month-block interval -0.037 to -0.006, 4 blocks, near min-to-max), per-fold signs -0.035, -0.038, +0.003, -0.019. The cell-to-cell minimum detectable effect is 0.011. Blend minus K2-S1 is -0.395 (-0.599 to -0.243), a difference that reflects K2-S1's own deficit, not a blending gain.
  • Pre-registered rule: the gain must be at least 0.05 below both parents. The blend is 0.022 below R-DW, so the verdict is partly supported (below -0.02, so not not supported).
  • By band at the eight, blend minus R-DW: -0.009 (0-6 h), -0.002 (6-12 h), -0.001 (12-24 h), -0.017 (24-48 h), -0.023 (48-72 h), -0.025 (72-120 h), -0.025 (120-240 h; interval -0.046 to +0.008). The gain is largest at 2 to 10 days, and it never reaches 0.05.
  • Weights: the fitted weight on K2-S1 is 0.0 to 0.2 at 0-24 h and 0.1 to 0.2 beyond. K2-S1 alone is 0.37 worse than R-DW at 24-120 h (0.21 to 0.56).
  • Six (signed MW): blend minus R-DW -0.030 at 24-120 h (-0.082 to +0.006, MDE 0.020; folds -0.110, +0.016, -0.001, -0.026). Blend minus A-pool is -0.049 (-0.085 to -0.020).
  • A half-and-half blend is worse than R-DW at the eight (+0.037, -0.008 to +0.079).
  • Tails (eight, 24-120 h, 184,393 rows): the share of actuals below q01 is 0.24% (nominal 1%) and below q05 is 1.6% (nominal 5%); below q95 is 95.9% and below q99 is 99.4%. Only 0.24% of actuals fall below q01 and 1.6% below q05, so the lower quantiles sit too low and the lower tail is too wide.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only): the blend is 0.42 worse than R-DW (0.015 to 0.99), on short history.
  • Counted tests: 28 (2 contrasts x 7 bands x 2 sets). No interval above is widened to that count. The MDE reflects the three cells of K2-S1 only, with R-DW held at its seed average, so the minimum detectable effect understates the noise.

docs.title: Part 2: stored blends with climatology or a calendar-only forecast
docs.text:
Experiment What was blended Where Result at long lead Weather issued at or before the forecast origin? 262 Climatology by lead day into the ECMWF wind members 3 metered wind farms (not Primaries), days 7 and later Helped by 0.45 without the offset table, 0.08 (-0.48 to +0.23) with it Yes, assuming the run is available at 09:00 UTC 528 (interim files only, no page) Gate between the lag-free network and a calendar-only mixture (S2-G) Eight and six, five folds, all seven lead bands Worse than L-Ww at every band, +0.46 (eight) and +0.52 (six) at 120-240 h; gate collapsed to calendar-only Yes (the L-Ww contrasts do not use K2-S1, so the K2-S1 correction does not touch them) 319 and 322 Manual heuristic (same half-hour in earlier weeks and years), not climatology Six Primaries on the convex GAM chain, 168-240 h 319: all-hours blend helped by 0.145 and harmed cold winter nights by 0.076. 322: daylight-only blend helped by 0.075 with no harm on cold winter nights Yes (origin 09:00 UTC)

Two further pages do not blend: experiment 329 planned a climatology of the solar response but did not run, because the gap it targeted was already closed, and experiment 317 uses climatology only as a comparator (the research default beats it by 11% to 13% at 168-240 h).

No stored blend of a calendar-only or climatology forecast into a demand network helped by 0.05 at 120-240 h, so Part 2 stops and the two proposed arms (an auxiliary climatology head and weather-input dropout) have no stored evidence. The only blend in the table that helped by 0.05 at these leads, the manual-heuristic blend of experiments 319 and 322, mixes in a forecast built from recent power history, not a calendar-only table, and was scored on the GAM chain. Its all-hours form harmed cold winter nights. The wind gain in experiment 262 (0.45, or 0.08 with an interval including zero once the offset table was applied) is at three wind farms, not Primaries. The stored evidence covers 168-240 h (319, 322, 329, 317) and day 7 onwards (262), not 120-168 h. The blend in experiment 528 did not carry a pre-registered comparison to climatology itself, and its numbers have no reviewed page.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Weather inputs: none are read here. Both networks used the weather run issued at or before the forecast origin (R-DW in experiment 539, K2-S1 in experiment 541). The script asserts that target > origin on every row and that each weight was fitted on earlier folds only. Example row: fold 2025-12, Primary 0, origin index 109602, target index 109705 (lead 51.5 h), weight on K2-S1 0.2, R-DW median 0.791, K2-S1 cell 0 median 0.813, blend median 0.795, actual 0.892 (fractions of capacity).
  • Reproduction: blending at weight 0 and 1 reproduces the stored R-DW and K2-S1 per-row CRPS to under 0.01 on every row (asserted). The scored rows are those of experiment 541 (about 227,000 per fold), fewer than experiment 547's, so numbers are not comparable across the two pages.
  • Review: one Sonnet code review before the run. Accepted: print the row counts (all rows survive), assert non-empty training selections, and set the MDE to NaN for contrasts it does not cover. Rejected: writing NaN to unscored rows (the main16 filter protects every table here).
  • Cost: no GPU, 38 seconds on 2 cores. July 2026 unused. Labels are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Nothing follows from Part 1 beyond closing the question of blending these two networks. If a gain at 120-240 h is still wanted, the open question is why the monthly lag-free heads beat the daily refit there (the post-reset queue's items on the monthly lag-free heads).

docs.title: Do trailing temperature windows still help the lag-light demand network once the day-ago and week-ago power lags are in?
docs.text:
Three average-temperature inputs still lower the forecast error on cold winter nights, by about 0.10 points of capacity, when the neural network also reads the power from one day and one week earlier. Over all rows we cannot show any gain. We asked whether the three trailing temperature windows of experiment 526 (the average forecast temperature over the 6, 24, and 72 hours before each half-hour) still lower the error of a demand neural network that already sees the substation's own power at the same time one day and one week earlier (experiment 539's network, called R-DW, which is not yet on this site). We trained R-DW twice: once with the real windows (R-DW + W-T) and once with the same three inputs copied from a different, shuffled day (R-DW + W-Tnull, the placebo), so that only the real weather information differs. Error is CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score, in points of capacity: percentage points of each Primary substation's capacity, where lower is better. Cold winter nights are below 5 degrees C, 18:00 to 08:00, and "the eight" are the Primary substations that report apparent power (MVA) only. On those nights at the eight, the real windows score 4.162 and the placebo 4.266. The verdict is supported by the rule written before scoring (a difference of at most -0.05 with an interval excluding zero), with the caveats below. Every number is interim and unaudited.

  • Pre-registered contrast (cold nights, below 5 degrees C, 18:00 to 08:00, eight MVA-only Primaries, rows with no labelled event): R-DW + W-T minus R-DW + W-Tnull is -0.104 (month- block interval -0.113 to -0.009, 3 blocks, one per winter fold; per-fold signs -0.112, -0.113, -0.009, all negative; 32,716 rows). The rule asked for at most -0.05 with an interval excluding zero, and both hold. Experiment 526 found -0.093 without the lags.
  • Minimum detectable effect: 0.212, twice the effect. The interval is narrow only because it rests on 3 blocks. Treat the size as uncertain. The size is similar to the -0.093 that experiment 526 found without the lags, but 526 used more winter folds, so the two are not like for like.
  • By lead band on cold nights, eight: -0.119 (24-48 h), -0.157 (48-72 h), -0.096 (72-120 h), -0.101 (120-240 h; interval -0.114 to -0.023). Intervals at 24-72 h and at 72-120 h (-0.169 to +0.005) include zero; the 12-24 h band is -0.110 to -0.027 and the 6-12 h band is positive (+0.045, 2 blocks).
  • All rows, eight: -0.018 (-0.054 to +0.037), per-fold signs -0.030, -0.044, -0.049, +0.088, -0.065. The interval includes zero.
  • Six signed-MW Primaries: all rows +0.000 (-0.041 to +0.046); cold nights -0.124 (-0.242 to -0.028; MDE 0.115).
  • Absolute CRPS (points of capacity), eight, all rows / cold nights: R-DW + W-T 4.677 / 4.162, R-DW + W-Tnull 4.695 / 4.266, R-DW 4.713 / 4.270, L-1d + W-T (experiment 548, arm E) 4.790 / 4.309, A-pool 4.682 / 4.161, L-1d 4.855 / 4.479, manual_heuristic 5.616 / 6.379. Six, all rows: 3.386, 3.385, 3.449, 3.446, 3.457, 3.493, 4.717.
  • Against R-DW: R-DW + W-T minus R-DW is -0.037 (-0.075 to -0.002) at the eight over all rows and -0.108 (-0.150 to +0.097) on cold nights. R-DW + W-T minus L-1d + W-T is -0.114 at the eight (-0.173 to -0.063): the lags still add to the windows.
  • Seam check of experiment 526 (persistence fill before the origin, 3 winter folds): RDW-seam minus R-DW + W-T is +0.003 over all rows (-0.001 to +0.009) and +0.016 on cold nights (+0.003 to +0.034). The gain does not come from how the window is filled across the forecast origin.
  • Injected-shift leak (a 7-day block of shifted power; change in the median forecast per 100 points of shift, seed 0, five folds): R-DW + W-T 5.7, R-DW + W-Tnull 7.8, R-DW 5.7, L-1d 4.5, L-1d + W-T 4.5. The windows do not raise the leak above R-DW's, but the seed-0 ranges across folds are wide (about 2.4 to 13), and the placebo's 7.8 is higher by 2 points, so these figures cannot rank the arms.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only): R-DW + W-T minus R-DW + W-Tnull is +0.061 (-0.325 to +0.428) over all rows and -0.016 on cold nights; short history, not scored.
  • Counted tests: 28 (2 contrasts x 7 bands x 2 site sets, the eight and the six, all-rows slice only). The cold-night contrast was pre-registered and is not counted. No interval is widened to that count. Intervals are month-block bootstraps, near the minimum to maximum of the folds (5 blocks all rows, 3 cold nights).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Both arms are experiment 539's R-DW on experiment 511's harness (daily refit at 00:00 UTC, 90-day weight half-life, ERA5 and CAMS pretraining, 2 seeds, five folds 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06; July 2026 unused). The window inputs are experiment 515's three W-T columns, appended after the six lag inputs; the pretraining weights are the lag-free W-T and W-Tnull networks of experiments 515, 526, and 548, with W-Tnull pretrained here for 2025-10 and 2026-06. The code copies experiment 539's lag code (not on main) and uses the window code of experiment 548. It lives in ml-experiments/00550-lag-light-network-trailing-temperature-windows-with-placebo/. The "winter folds of 526" are the three winter folds of these five (2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03).

  • Origin-time weather and lags, asserted row by row: every day-ago and week-ago lag was observed at or before the origin minus the data delay, and the 9-hour-earlier weather-run file exists for all 153 test origins. Example: origin 2025-12-01 09:00 UTC, target 2025-12-01 20:00 UTC, lag observed 2025-11-30 20:00 UTC; weather run 2025-11-23 00:00 UTC for a training row at origin 2025-11-23 09:00 UTC.
  • Placebo caveat: the donor day is a different day of the same calendar month group and day type (experiment 515's draw) and can lie after the row's own day, so some placebo window values come from a run issued after the origin. The donor day is a different day, so it carries no information about the target. If a later donor day helped the placebo at all, the contrast would be understated, not inflated. We did not measure that.
  • Unlabelled events: NGED's event labels are incomplete, so "rows with no labelled event" may hold unlabelled load shifts; counts are lower bounds.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast: not computed; these arms store quantiles only.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside the quantile score: not computed, for the same reason.
  • Triggers for an audit (listed in the ml-experiment skill): none fired (the placebo moves the score by 0.018 at the eight, inside its interval half-width of about 0.04; the cold-night interval is of the same order as experiment 526's). Leave-one-site-out was not run. No audit was run.
  • Not done: forecast examples, tail coverage, and the curtailment cost are not shown on this page.

docs.title: Lessons and what the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The windows keep their cold-night gain beside the lags. The all-rows gain is not shown. The next experiment should add the other winter folds of experiment 526 (2024-11 to 2025-03 and 2025-11, 2026-02) to the lag-light harness, to lift the cold-night contrast above its minimum detectable effect.

docs.title: Is the lag-light demand network safe to release: do its lag timestamps look ahead, does it hold up in Christmas week and on bank holidays, and does it survive removed or late power readings?
docs.text:
No lag input looks ahead of the forecast origin. R-DW fails the Christmas-week limit, and R-DROP passes every pre-registered test but keeps less of the gain. The question was whether the lag-light demand networks R-DW (experiment 539) and R-DROP (experiment 544) are safe to put in a release. All numbers are interim and unaudited, in points of capacity; lower CRPS is better. Nothing was refitted.

Verdict: partly supported. P1 held, P2 failed, and P3 held for R-DROP and failed (in the safe direction) for R-DW.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• P1, lag-timestamp audit: zero violations. The audit recomputed each lag's source half-hour from its definition, for the day-ago, week-ago, and newest reading, in 34.8 million rows (104,481,990 lag checks): the raw summary matrices of all 16 Primaries, and each of the five folds' training and test tables. It found 0 sources later than the origin minus 3.5 h, 0 age columns that differ from the target minus the source time, 0 missing flags that disagree with the cleaned power, and 0 values that differ from the cleaned power (tolerance 1e-5 on raw values, 1e-4 on standardised tables inverted with the fold's own standardiser; 981,447 rows clipped at 5 standard deviations are skipped in the built tables and are covered by the raw pass). One row of every lag and lead band is printed in audit_lag_timestamps.json; for example, a 2026-01-01 09:00Z origin with target 2026-01-03 05:00Z has its day-ago lag from 2026-01-01 05:00Z (origin minus 4.0 h) and its week-ago lag from 2025-12-27 05:00Z. The same standing weather rule holds: the 2026-01 test example uses weather run 2026-01-01 00:00Z for origin 2026-01-01 09:00Z, and the check that nwp_init_time is at or before the origin passed for every test origin.
  • One data-cleaning gap, not look-ahead. The raw lag matrices still hold D15 and D18 readings from before 2025-03-01, which the cleaned power drops (261,287 lag checks). Those two Primaries are report-only, so no headline number changes.
  • P2, Christmas week: failed at the eight. R-DW minus L-1d is +0.171 over 9 target days (24 December 2025 to 1 January 2026; 5 of 9 days worse; +0.170 and +0.284 in the two folds that hold them), above the 0.10 limit and below the 0.2 stop rule. A-pool is +0.160, R-DROP -0.097, and the lag-free recipe of experiment 548 -0.065. At the six R-DW is +0.299. With one winter and a few days no interval is shown, and the minimum detectable effect (0.12) is the seed spread of all rows, so it understates the noise of a slice.
  • Bank holidays. Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year's Day windows (3 days each) are worse for R-DW by +0.36, +0.37, and +0.19 at the eight. Good Friday and Easter Monday windows reach only long leads (3 to 10 days), where R-DW is better (-0.37 and -0.85), so they say little about the short leads.
  • Cold nights and rows with no labelled event. R-DW is better than L-1d at the eight (-0.209 and -0.117), and worse at the six on cold nights (+0.178). R-DROP is better or equal in both.
  • P3, lag removal (eight, 24-120 h, minimum detectable effect 0.116, Bonferroni count 28). R-DROP with every reading removed minus L-1d is -0.021 (interval -0.057 to +0.009, 5 month blocks, near min to max; 1 of 5 folds worse), inside the 0.15 limit in every band (largest upper end +0.035). It reproduces experiment 544's stored R-DROP-absent forecasts exactly. R-DW with every reading removed is +0.201 (-0.047 to +0.379; 4 of 5 folds worse), +0.390 against its own readings-present forecast, so the predicted loss over 0.5 did not occur (largest band 6-12 h, +0.342). At the six R-DW is +0.355 and R-DROP +0.029.
  • Partial removal and late reading. Removing only the day-ago or only the week-ago reading leaves R-DW at -0.052 and -0.058 against L-1d. Readings 1, 2, and 3 days late leave R-DW at -0.173, -0.163, and -0.152 and R-DROP at -0.081, -0.079, and -0.075, so ageing costs R-DW at most 0.04 and R-DROP at most 0.01 against their readings-present forecasts. Removing 25% of rows at random leaves R-DW at -0.090 and R-DROP at -0.069.
  • Release checklist. Passed: lag-timestamp and weather audits; removal with R-DROP within 0.15; late reading within 0.1. Failed: R-DW in Christmas week (0.10 limit).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events and the slices undercount them.
  • Christmas week is one winter (9 target days), so a per-year sign cannot be read. D15 and D18 are report-only and July 2026 is unused. The six-Primary holiday windows are signed-MW rows with no labelled event.
  • Part 3 scores the stored networks with their readings altered at inference only. A network trained to expect late readings may do better.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does R-DW with the week-ago reading replaced by a holiday-aware reading, or with its readings switched off on public holidays, remove the Christmas-week loss and keep the gain?

docs.title: Code
docs.text: ml-experiments/00551-*/: e00551_audit.py (Part 1), e00551_calendar.py (Part 2), e00551_removal.py, e00551_rows.py, and e00551_score.py (Part 3), e00551_figures.py. They import the folders of experiments 087, 397, 428, 454, 470, 510, 511, 521, and 544, and read experiments 539, 544, and 548's stored weights and scores. The Sonnet code review found no look-ahead; its tolerance, reproduction, and gating findings were applied, and its caveats on the Easter windows and the slice minimum detectable effect are in the text.

docs.title: Does an ICON-EU run issued four times a day improve the lag-free demand forecast at the 00, 06, 12, and 18 UTC issue times?
docs.text: An ICON-EU run issued four times a day did not improve the lag-free demand forecast: the adaptor was worse than the ECMWF ensemble mean while it had under 3 months of history, and level with it afterwards. The verdict is not supported. This covers March to June 2026 only, so it says nothing about winter. Every number is interim and unaudited.

docs.title: What was compared
docs.text:
• N0: the ECMWF ensemble mean (the latest 00 UTC run usable at the issue time) through experiment 524's frozen stage-1 network, which takes no lead time and no spread.
  • N1: the same network, with its seven mean-weather inputs replaced by the output of a 2 x 32 multilayer perceptron fed the latest usable ICON-EU run (shortwave as direct plus diffuse, 2 m temperature, dew point, surface pressure, precipitation, 10 m wind speed).
  • N2: N1 with the ECMWF means and spreads as extra adaptor inputs.
  • Timing: an ICON-EU run is usable 4 h after its init time (an assumption), and an ECMWF run at 09:00 UTC on its day (the project's convention). The code asserts this row by row. One example: issue 2026-03-16 06:00, ICON-EU run 2026-03-16 00:00, ECMWF origin 2026-03-15 09:00, valid 2026-03-17 15:30.
  • Fitting: each monthly fold fits the adaptor on ICON-EU rows from 2026-02-10 to the month start minus 3.5 h (19, 50, 80, and 111 days). Phase A regresses the seven standardised ECMWF means; phase B trains through the frozen stage 1 on the power likelihood. Two seeds.
  • Not run: N3 (a Previous Runs table back to 2024), because the run times of that table are not fixed. ICON-D2 has no true-run archive.
  • Data: 564 Dynamical.org runs (CC BY 4.0) at the 16 Primary points, 12 GB, read in 85 minutes. The store has no longwave radiation and no 100 m wind, so the adaptor learns longwave from the other inputs. Reused code: experiments 87, 397, 422, 428, 448, 510, and 524.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• P1 fails. N1 minus N0 at 0-24 h at the eight is +0.58 (06 UTC), +0.61 (12 UTC), and +0.61 (18 UTC), against the required -0.10. Per-fold values at 06 UTC: +1.57, +0.73, -0.03, +0.04 (March to June). The minimum detectable effect is 0.30 to 0.38, the month-block interval excludes zero only at 18 UTC and runs up to +1.4, and 4 blocks make that interval near min-to-max.
  • P2 holds: N1 minus N0 at 00 UTC is +0.60 (folds +1.65, +0.75, -0.02, +0.03).
  • P3 holds: N2 minus N1 at 24-74 h is -0.43 (interval -0.84 to -0.05, folds -0.93, -0.54, +0.01, -0.25; MDE 0.04). N2 is still no better than N0 overall: 4.93 against 4.79 at the eight.
  • N2 against N0 by fold (eight, all leads): +0.71, +0.10, -0.10, -0.18 (March to June). Only June is below -0.10, and that is a single fold.
  • Six (signed MW): pooled N0 3.24, N1 3.65, N2 3.12; N1 minus N0 by fold +1.33, +0.38, +0.02, -0.14.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only): N0 16.8, N1 14.6, N2 14.3, so the adaptor helps there by 2 points in every fold. These two series have short history, and the adaptor trains on power, so the gain may come from correcting the stage-1 network's bias there and not from the ICON-EU weather.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Spring only, four folds. The fold-to-fold spread is larger than any difference in May and June, so those two folds do not separate N1 from N0 in either direction.
  • The adaptor is trained through a stage-1 network that has seen the same power, without the cross-fit that experiment 524 uses. This can flatter or hurt N1 and N2 against N0.
  • Early stopping is close to in-sample: every fifth issue day is held out, but neighbouring issue days share valid times, and March has 19 days of history.
  • Absolute scores are not comparable with experiments 524 and 448: the quantiles here are not widened about the median, and CRPS is twice the unweighted mean pinball loss over 11 levels.
  • N0 is scored only on rows where an ICON-EU run exists, which removes the first hours of 2026-02-10 only.
  • The minimum detectable effect is 2.8 times the spread of two seeds, a crude estimate.
  • NGED's event logs are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled load-shift events.

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text: The ICON-EU archive that exists is too short to answer the question. The adaptor needs a year or more of runs. With 111 days it only reaches the ECMWF mean. The ECMWF ensemble mean through a network trained on estimates of past weather is a strong baseline to beat.

docs.title: Does one demand neural network that reads the day-ago and week-ago power readings, trailing temperature windows, and is trained with those readings randomly removed keep most of the gain of the readings and still work without them?
docs.text:
One demand neural network can use the day-ago and week-ago power readings, the trailing temperature windows, and lag dropout together, and 15% dropout keeps as much of the gain of the readings as no dropout does. We asked whether three earlier ideas combine into a network that is accurate when yesterday's and last week's power readings are present and still works when they are missing. The three ideas are the two readings (experiment 539's R-DW, whose page is not yet merged), the trailing temperature windows of experiments 515 and 548, and randomly removing the readings in training (experiment 544's R-DROP). The network with 15% dropout scored the same as R-DW when the readings were present, and scored no differently from the lag-free network when they were removed. The network with 15% dropout missed one target: it closed 82% of the gap between L-1d and A-pool, against a target of 85%. Verdict: partly supported. All numbers are CRPS in points of capacity (lower is better), over five test months, interim and unaudited.

Terms. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, here as a percentage of each substation's effective capacity. L-1d is the demand neural network without power readings (experiment 511). R-DW adds the day-ago and week-ago readings. R-DROP is R-DW trained with the readings removed in 30% of rows. E is the lag-free network with the trailing windows (experiment 548). A-pool is the network that reads all recent power readings (experiment 425). The eight are the MVA-only Primary substations, and the six are the signed-MW Primaries. Bands are lead times, such as 24-48 h. The RDWT-D15 and RDWT-D30 arms are R-DW plus the windows, trained with 15% and 30% dropout.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Pre-registered predictions (the eight MVA-only Primaries, 24-120 h, rate chosen before scoring as the one with more gap closed among rates with leak at most 6.0, which is 15%).
    • P1, gap closed with readings present of at least 85%: failed. 15% closes 82% (24-48 h 75%, 48-72 h 80%, 72-120 h 88%); 30% closes 64%. R-DW closes 80% over the same band. The gap is above the 70% stop line.
    • P2, readings removed within 0.15 of the lag-free recipe (E): held. 15%: 4.524 against 4.555, difference -0.031 (-0.103 to +0.031).
    • P3, Christmas week no worse than L-1d by more than 0.10: held. 15%: 4.164 against 4.243 (-0.079). R-DW was 4.414 (+0.171) in the same week. It is one week of one winter, so it has no interval.
    • P4, injected-shift leak at most 6.0 points of capacity: held. 15%: 5.33 (5.89 for positive shifts and 4.78 for negative ones, so the positive-shift figure sits just under the limit). 30%: 5.10. R-DW: 5.68. L-1d: 4.49. These are means over block ages 0 to 6 and both signs, and the range across folds is wide (about 2.6 to 10.7). At block age 0 the leak is 10.1 (15%) and 9.0 (30%), against 11.5 for R-DW and 7.2 for L-1d.
  • Absolute CRPS at the eight, 24-120 h. A-pool 4.395; RDWT-D15 4.438; R-DW 4.442; RDWT-D30 4.481; RDWT-D15 readings removed 4.524; RDWT-D30 readings removed 4.535; R-DROP 4.546; E (lag-free with windows) 4.555; R-DROP readings removed 4.609; L-1d 4.631; manual_heuristic 5.521. At the six: RDWT-D15 3.209, RDWT-D30 3.230, R-DW 3.269, A-pool 3.280, L-1d 3.342.
  • Counted contrasts at the eight, 24-120 h (95% month-block bootstrap, 5 blocks, near min-to-max; Bonferroni count 84 = 2 rates x 3 contrasts x 7 lead bands x 2 row sets; minimum detectable effect 0.116). RDWT-D15 minus L-1d: -0.193 (-0.285 to -0.119; 0 of 5 folds worse). RDWT-D15 minus R-DW: -0.004 (-0.055 to +0.046; 2 of 5 folds worse). RDWT-D15 readings removed minus E: -0.031 (-0.103 to +0.031; 3 of 5 folds better). The 30% arm gives -0.150, +0.038, and -0.020. Every lead band from 0-6 h to 120-240 h shows the same sign for the 15% arm against L-1d.
  • Dropout rates. The 15% arm against the 30% arm: -0.043 (-0.080 to -0.020; 5 of 5 folds in favour of 15%). With readings removed the two rates differ by -0.011 (inside the minimum detectable effect).
  • At the six the 15% arm is 0.133 better than L-1d (-0.133, interval ending at -0.053) and 0.071 better than A-pool; both are inside or near the minimum detectable effect of 0.155, and the gap ratio is not meaningful there because L-1d is just 0.061 behind A-pool.
  • Tails. At the eight, 24-120 h, pinball loss at q95 is 0.050 better than L-1d (-0.092 to -0.011) and 0.042 worse than A-pool (-0.003 to +0.088); at q99, 0.020 better than L-1d and 0.019 worse than A-pool (+0.010 to +0.025).
  • Cold winter nights, 24-120 h, eight: RDWT-D15 3.952, RDWT-D30 3.985, L-1d 4.318, A-pool 3.790. A-pool is 0.16 better than the 15% arm on those nights. Bank-holiday windows, all leads: RDWT-D15 4.875 against L-1d 4.982.
  • Retrained K2-S1 (experiment 541). Its per-band table is on the same rows; see 00541-k2-s1-rebuilt-on-origin-time-weather. The page does not pair that table with these arms.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers fired: none that need an audit. The nested-arm trigger does not fire, because the 15% arm is not worse than R-DW. The headline rests on pools of seeds 0 and 1; see the caveats.
  • Origin-time weather and lag timestamps, asserted row by row for 24,979,347 training rows and 1,142,520 test rows over 153 test origins. Example: origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, target 2025-10-01 12:30 UTC, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC, day-ago reading observed 2025-09-30 12:30 UTC (at least 3.5 h before the origin).
  • Median minus mean forecast per site and the error of the mean or median forecast were not computed (these checks expose a spread that shifts the forecast); the pinball contrasts above agree in sign with the CRPS contrasts.
  • Cost about 1.5 GPU-hours, one process under 8 GB.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet code review before the first fit (no problems found, one unused path removed). Write-up review: see the pull request.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Seed 2 is not comparable. The RDWT-D15 and RDWT-D30 arms are pools of seeds 0 and 1, and the -s2 arms are single fits of seed 2. A pool of two seeds averages their quantiles, which scores lower CRPS than one seed, and every stored comparator is a pool of seeds 0 and 1. Seed 2 alone gives 4.523 (15%) and 4.570 (30%), higher than the pooled arms, and the gap closed would read 46% and 26%. The headline therefore rests on two seeds; a fit of seeds 0 and 1 alone is not available.
  • The 85% target was set above what R-DW itself reached (80% over this band), so it was unlikely to hold for any dropout.
  • Christmas week is one week in one winter. NGED's load-shift logs may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events and the leak is measured on injected shifts only.
  • The lead range is 0 to 240 h, which covers the 1 to 10 day horizon NGED care about; the conclusion is drawn on 24-120 h.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Run the final bake-off of the release plan with 5 seeds, comparing this 15% network with the lag-free recipe and A-pool, since the 15% network and the lag-free recipe are within the minimum detectable effect of each other when the readings are removed.
  • Try a dropout rate between 0% and 15% only if the bake-off shows the readings-present gap matters.

docs.title: Does the modular lag-free demand network (M0) keep its gain over L-1d with 5 seeds, which of its two changes raises its injected-shift leak, and does the gain survive without D8?
docs.text:
The modular demand network M0 still beats the single network L-1d at leads of 1 to 5 days when both are averaged over 5 seeds, by 0.176 points of capacity at the eight MVA-only Primaries (CRPS, lower is better), and the gain mostly survives a slower learning rate. About half of it comes from one Primary, D8: without D8 the gain is 0.091, with an interval that includes zero. The leak mitigations and the diagnostic arms were not run, so what raises M0's injected-shift leak is still unknown.

We asked whether the gain of experiment 545 holds with more seeds. M0 has a weather encoder, a datetime encoder, and a fresh mixer at fine-tuning; M0lr is the same with the mixer at L-1d's learning rate. The control is L-1d refitted here for seeds 2 to 4, so that both sides average 5 seeds (seeds 0 and 1 are the stored fits of experiments 511 and 545). Scores are CRPS in points of effective capacity on rows with no labelled event. "The eight" are the MVA-only Primaries and "the six" the signed-MW Primaries. The maintainer cut stage 2 (M0-hl180, M0-c3, M0-sep, M0-mix) after this stage scored, so prediction P2 was not tested.

Verdict: partly supported. P1 held (M0 0.176 and M0lr 0.136, both at least 0.10, with intervals excluding zero). P3 held on its point estimate (0.091 without D8, at least 0.05) but its interval includes zero. P2 was not tested. No failure condition fired, and the stop rule did not fire (M0lr's gain is 0.136, above 0.03).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS minus L-1d (5 seeds each), negative favours the modular arm, over leads of 24 to 120 h pooled. Brackets give the Bonferroni month-block interval (5 blocks, near the minimum to maximum of the five folds; 28 counted tests) and the number of folds in which the arm is worse. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is 0.111 at the eight, 0.088 at the eight without D8, and 0.091 at the six.

Set M0 M0lr M0 minus M0lr Eight -0.176 (-0.304 to -0.095; 0/5) -0.136 (-0.301 to -0.043; 0/5) -0.040 (-0.105 to +0.007; 2/5) Eight without D8 -0.091 (-0.211 to +0.008; 2/5) -0.067 (-0.212 to +0.081; 1/5) -0.025 (-0.090 to +0.026; 2/5) D8 alone -0.767 (-1.421 to +0.016; 1/5) -0.626 (-1.248 to +0.201; 1/5) -0.142 (-0.212 to -0.012; 1/5) Six -0.061 (-0.177 to +0.103; 1/5) -0.021 (-0.154 to +0.213; 1/5) -0.040 (-0.119 to -0.001; 0/5)

The gain is not a 2-seed accident. In the bands the pre-registration names, M0 minus L-1d is -0.216, -0.182, and -0.153 at 24-48 h, 48-72 h, and 72-120 h (experiment 545, 2 seeds: -0.208, -0.182, -0.137), and no fold is worse. M0lr keeps -0.172, -0.140, and -0.116.

One Primary carries about half of the gain. M0 gains at 7 of the 8 Primaries (D4 is worse, by 0.108), and D8 gains 0.767 against at most 0.34 for any other of the eight. Without D8 the bands are -0.134, -0.097, and -0.067, and only 24-48 h has an interval that excludes zero. The gain is not carried by D8 alone, but it is not shown at the other seven.

M0 reaches R-DW and sits close to A-pool without reading power. At the eight over 24-120 h, M0 scores 4.433, R-DW 4.442, A-pool 4.395, the 5-seed L-1d 4.609, the 2-seed L-1d 4.631, and the manual heuristic 5.521 (M0 minus A-pool +0.038, interval -0.101 to +0.162). At the six the gain is smaller and its interval includes zero (M0 3.245, the 5-seed L-1d 3.306, A-pool 3.280).

Averaging 5 seeds helps L-1d a little. The 5-seed L-1d is 0.022 better than the 2-seed L-1d at the eight (-0.040 to +0.001).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Origin-time weather, asserted row by row. For every one of the 153 test origins the script asserts nwp_init_time <= power_fcst_init_time, power_fcst_init_time == origin, and that the weather-run summary file exists; every training target is after its origin and its weather run exists 9 hours before. Example, 2025-10 test row: target 2025-10-03 07:00 UTC, origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC (checks_*_s2-3-4.json: 24,979,347 training rows and 1,142,520 test rows per arm).
  • Inputs are experiment 545's: no power-derived column, the 9 lag columns removed.
  • Reuse. Seeds 0 and 1 of M0, M0lr, and L-1d are the stored fits of experiments 545 and 511 (unchanged code); seeds 2 to 4 were fitted here, with new pretrained weights for M0 (all five folds) and for L-1d in fold 2025-12.
  • Not done. Stage 2 (M0-hl180, M0-c3, M0-sep, M0-mix) and the injected-shift leak were not run, so P2 is untested; the leak figures of experiment 545 (L-1d 4.49, M0 7.60, M0lr 7.71, seed 0) are unchanged. The climatology was not scored here, and no forecast-example figure was drawn. One Sonnet reviewer read the code before the first fit and found no bug; the write-up was checked against the printed report by its author only. The 5-seed gain over 2 seeds is not paired with a 5-seed A-pool or R-DW, which keep their own seeds.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
Whether a 180-day half-life or a 3-day refit cadence brings M0's injected-shift leak under 6.0, and which part of the network raises it. Compute used: about 3.5 GPU-hours (pretraining and 1,377 fits).

The code is in ml-experiments/00554-m0-replication-five-seeds-leak-mitigations-and-leave-d8-out/ and reuses experiments 397, 428, 448, 510, 511, 521, 539, and 545.

docs.title: Do the power readings available at the 06, 12, and 18 UTC issue times improve the demand forecast over the 00 UTC weather run aged to that issue time?
docs.text:
Question and answer. NGED, the operator of the distribution network, wants the forecast of demand at its primary substations (Primaries) updated every 6 hours. The ECMWF ensemble weather forecast arrives once a day: the 00 UTC run, usable from 09:00 UTC. We asked whether the power readings available at later issue times (the times of day a forecast is issued: 12 and 18 UTC the same day, 00 and 06 UTC the next day) make the demand forecast better than a forecast that reads no power readings, when both use the same 00 UTC weather run. The test used neural networks that were already trained for the 09:00 UTC forecast. The first reads the power from the same half-hour one day ago and one week ago (R-DW). The second reads no power readings (L-1d). We rebuilt each network's inputs as they would be at each issue time. The network that reads the power readings stayed better: its probabilistic error (CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score; lower is better) was about 0.28 points of capacity lower at 0 to 12 h ahead, at the 8 Primaries whose power is metered in MVA (the eight). This is the same gain as at 09:00 UTC.

Verdict: supported. P1 held (-0.290 at 12 UTC against the required -0.2). P2 held at 06 and 18 UTC. All numbers are interim and have not been audited; CRPS is in points of effective capacity and lower is better.

docs.title: What was compared
docs.text:
• Arms. L-1d, the lag-free network of experiment 511 (read from its stored forecasts, which do not depend on the issue time). R-DW (experiment 539) and R-DROP (experiment 544) read the day-ago and week-ago readings. R9 (experiment 538) also reads the newest reading. R-DROP was trained with 30% of its rows having the readings removed. Stored daily refits and both seeds are used unchanged; nothing was refitted.
  • Issue times. 12 and 18 UTC on the run's day; 00 and 06 UTC on the next day; 09:00 UTC (the origin the networks were trained on) is shown for reference. Rows are those with a valid time after the issue time, and lead bands are counted from the issue time.
  • What changes at an issue time. The lead input, and the day-ago and week-ago readings (value, flag, age; for R9 the newest reading as well), are retaken from the latest same-clock half-hour at or before the issue time minus the 3.5 h data delay. The weather inputs are those of the 00 UTC run.
  • Checks, row by row at each issue time and fold (75 tables, 1.1 million rows kept at 12 UTC). The weather run is usable at or before the issue time; each lag source is on the right clock slot, is the latest such slot, and is at or before the issue time minus 3.5 h; the ages equal an independent recomputation (asserted in e00555_infer.py). The rebuild at 09:00 UTC reproduces the stored table, and the 09:00 UTC forecasts reproduce the stored forecasts of experiments 538, 539, and 544 exactly (maximum difference 0). One example: issue 2026-03-01 12:00 UTC, weather run 2026-03-01 00:00 UTC (usable 09:00), target 2026-03-02 12:30, day-ago reading from 2026-02-28 12:30, week-ago reading from 2026-02-23 12:30.
  • Statistics. Intervals are 95% month-block bootstraps with 5 blocks, one per fold, so each interval spans nearly the range of the fold values. The counted tests are R-DW minus L-1d at 4 issue times, 4 lead bands, and 2 row sets, so the Bonferroni count is 32. The minimum detectable effect (MDE, 2.8 times the spread of L-1d's two seeds) is 0.11 to 0.18 at 0-12 h. Other contrasts are report-only.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• P1 holds. At 12 UTC, 0-12 h, at the eight, R-DW minus L-1d is -0.290 (-0.42 to -0.16; MDE 0.14), with every fold negative: -0.330, -0.443, -0.111, -0.127, -0.449 (October to June). R-DW scores 4.219 and L-1d 4.509.
  • Per-fold signs. Of the 32 counted contrasts, 6 have a positive fold: at the eight, 12 UTC at 0-6 h and 06 UTC at 6-12 h; at the six, 06 UTC at 0-6 h, 12 UTC at 12-24 h, and 00 and 06 UTC at 6-12 h. Every other fold of every counted contrast is negative.
  • P2 holds. At 0-12 h at the eight, the difference is -0.266 at 06 UTC (-0.45 to -0.08), -0.279 at 18 UTC (-0.34 to -0.22), and -0.280 at 00 UTC (-0.41 to -0.18), against -0.287 at 09:00 UTC. The gain does not grow at later issue times.
  • Lead bands at the eight (R-DW minus L-1d). 0-6 h: -0.239 (12 UTC), -0.333 (18), -0.234 (00), -0.327 (06). 6-12 h: -0.336, -0.229, -0.321, -0.210. 12-24 h and 24-48 h stay between -0.22 and -0.27 at every issue time. All 32 counted contrasts are negative with a 95% month-block interval that excludes zero: the 16 at the eight lie between -0.21 and -0.34, and all 16 also exclude zero at the Bonferroni level. The 16 at the six lie between -0.07 and -0.23, and 14 exclude zero at that level.
  • The six (signed MW), 0-12 h. -0.160 at 12 UTC (-0.22 to -0.09), -0.223 at 18, -0.165 at 00, and -0.096 at 06 (-0.14 to -0.05).
  • R-DROP keeps about 40% of the gain: -0.114 at 12 UTC at 0-12 h at the eight (-0.16 to -0.07).
  • R9 adds nothing at the eight. R9 minus R-DW at 0-12 h at the eight is -0.001 to -0.018 at 00, 06, and 18 UTC and +0.018 at 12 UTC. Every interval includes zero or has an upper end under +0.001 (figure 2). A fresher newest reading does not help at these lead times beyond the day-ago and week-ago readings. At the six, R9 minus R-DW is -0.012 to -0.037 at 0-12 h, and only the 00 UTC interval (-0.081 to -0.003) excludes zero.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only). R-DW minus L-1d at 0-12 h is -0.93 to -1.27 across issue times.
  • Tails. At 0-12 h at the eight, the share of actuals below the q95 forecast is 0.965 to 0.972 for R-DW and 0.976 to 0.983 for L-1d (nominal 0.95); below q05 it is 0.014 to 0.018 against 0.012 to 0.015 (nominal 0.05). The 5% to 95% forecast intervals are therefore too wide, because actuals fall outside them less often than the nominal level, and R-DW is slightly nearer to the nominal level. Full table: tails_0_12h_eight.csv.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean forecast beside the quantile score. Not run: the networks output quantiles and nothing here re-fits them.
  • Audit triggers. None fired: the 09:00 UTC rows reproduce experiments 539's R-DW numbers (for example -0.351 at 6-12 h at the eight), no control failed, and R9 (which contains R-DW's inputs) is not significantly worse than R-DW (+0.018 at 12 UTC, interval -0.013 to +0.049). Triggers 3 and 4 were not tested (no leave-one-out run).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Weather input is old. At 06 UTC on the next day the 00 UTC run is 30 h old, and the network saw only runs 9 h old in training. The lead input is counted from the issue time, so the network cannot see the staleness. The result holds up to that staleness anyway.
  • Absolute scores differ between issue times because the rows differ (valid times after the issue) and the time of day of the target changes. L-1d's CRPS at 0-12 h is 5.38 at 06 UTC and 3.56 at 18 UTC. Compare arms within an issue time, not across issue times.
  • Refits are those of the 09:00 UTC origin day, up to one day older than a live service would use at 00 and 06 UTC on the next day.
  • No fine-tune on issue-time rows, and one network trained on 09:00 UTC origins only. A network trained on issue-time rows may do better.
  • Five folds and 5 month blocks, so each interval spans nearly the range of the fold values. Two of the 16 counted contrasts at the six have Bonferroni-level intervals that include zero. July 2026 is unused.
  • NGED's event logs are incomplete, so clean rows may hold unlabelled load-shift events.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: A later experiment could test whether a short fine-tune on rows with issue-time origins, or a fresher weather run (ICON-EU, which did not help in experiment 552 with 4 months of history), improves on the lag-light network's 0.28 points.

docs.title: Code
docs.text: ml-experiments/00555-*/: e00555_infer.py (inference at each issue time), e00555_rows.py and e00555_score.py (scores), e00555_figures.py, and run.sh. They import the folders of experiments 087, 397, 428, 454, 470, 510, 511, 521, and 551, and read the stored weights and forecasts of experiments 538, 539, and 544 (private data folder). The scripts of experiments 538 and 539 are not in this repository.

docs.title: How much of a load-shift event does the lag-free demand neural network absorb through its fine-tune, and how fast does it unlearn the event?
docs.text:
A step added to the fine-tuning targets of the lag-free demand neural network reaches the next week's median forecast by a share that grows with the step's length, about one in ten for a 3-day step of 10% of capacity, and the effect fades over about 2 weeks. A real labelled event leaks 1.5% of its depth. We asked how much of a load-shift event in the rows a neural network is refitted on ends up in its next forecasts. We added a step of 10% of a Primary's capacity to the fine-tuning targets of the 16 Primaries, for the 1, 3, 7, or 14 days before a refit, and compared the median forecast with the matched refit without the step. We also fitted once on metered and once on corrected targets around 74 real labelled events, injected a lasting step, and scored two rules that might cut the leak: leaving the newest 3 days of targets out (F3d-E3), and shrinking the weight of rows far from the previous fine-tune's median (F3d-R).

Verdict: partly supported. Of the six pre-registered predictions, P1 (the leak rises with step length) and P6 (the real-event share is under 0.10) held; P2 (the daily leak is under 10% of its first value within 7 days), P3 (90% adaptation within 14 days), and P5 (F3d-R cuts the leak by 30%) failed; P4 passed on the leak (98% cut) and missed its CRPS bound (+0.057 and +0.051 against +0.05). The leak is real but small at realistic lengths, F3d-E3 removes it for short steps at a score cost just above the bar, and F3d-R does not reach the bar. F1d, F3d, and F7d refit daily, every 3 days, and weekly (F7d is L-Ww of experiments 510 and 511), and F1d-182 refits daily with a recency half-life of 182.6 days instead of 90. "The eight" are the MVA-only Primaries and "the six" the signed-MW Primaries. A "leak" is the sign-adjusted shift of the median, in points of capacity (percentage of each Primary's capacity). Scores use rows with no labelled event, two seeds, and five folds of 511 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The leak grows with the step's length and does not depend on the refit cadence. The first refit after a step is the same fit for the daily, 3-day, and weekly arms, so the three arms share every first-refit number below; cadence matters only for the refits that follow. One seed, mean of five folds, two origins, and both signs.

Step before the refit Leak at the eight (points) Share of the step Leak at the six (points) Share of the step 1 day 0.43 4% 0.49 5% 3 days 1.14 11% 1.21 12% 7 days 2.64 26% 2.84 28% 14 days 4.08 41% 4.36 44% 3 days, alternating signs across Primaries 0.62 6% 0.62 6%
  • Reproduction of experiment 510: a step of 3 standard deviations of the 7-day mean over 7 days, at the week-3 origin and all 16 Primaries, moved L-Ww's median by 6.12 points (experiment 510: 6.11), and by 14.5 points in the 2026-01 fold.
  • The stop rule did not fire: F1d's leak at L = 3 days is above 1.0 point in each of the first four lead bands (0 to 48 h) at both groups: 1.24 to 1.54 at the eight and 1.30 to 1.63 at the six.
  • Bad data leak little: a 24 h stuck reading leaks 0.30 (eight) and 0.18 (six) points, a 6 h dropout 0.07 and 0.04, and a 6 h spike of 10 residual median absolute deviations 0.26 and 0.10.
  • Noise: the standard deviation between the two signs' leaks for one fold and origin, over the square root of 2, is 0.1 to 1.0 points for the arms that leak. The leak is one seed per cell, so no leak difference smaller than about 1 point is read as an effect.

The leak fades over about 2 weeks at every cadence. After a 3-day step, the daily arm's leak at the eight falls from 1.23 points to 0.10 by day 14 (8%), and the weekly arm's from 1.14 to 0.16 (14%). Figure 2 shows all six arms. The leak halves by about day 6 for every arm except F3d-E3, whose leak starts near zero and rises to 1.21 at day 3. The first-refit values differ slightly by arm (1.23, 1.18, 1.14) because this series uses each refit's own window.

The neural network adapts slowly to a genuine lasting step. None of the six arms reached 90% of a lasting step of 10% of capacity in 29 days, the eight stayed under 50% (F1d 49% at day 28), and at the six F1d reached 50% on day 20, F3d on day 21, F7d on day 21, and F3d-R on day 24. F1d-182 and F3d-E3 never reached it. Early stopping on clean held-out weeks and the 90-day recency weight may explain the plateau; this experiment did not test either.

Real labelled events leak 1.5% of their depth. Over 74 events with a labelled depth, fitted once on metered and once on corrected targets (only the measured event corrected), the F1d fits absorbed a mean of 1.5% of the depth (median 0.3%; fold means 1.1%, 0.6%, 3.8%, 0.4%, and 1.1%; five-block interval 0.6% to 2.6%, narrower than the range of the fold means, 0.4% to 3.8%). Without the largest event the mean is 1.1% (interval 0.6% to 1.7%). One event absorbed 27.6% of its depth (a 22.9-point step aged 3.5 days, at one Primary in the 2026-01 fold). Among the other events of 10 points or more the largest share was 7.4%.

F3d-E3 passes the leak bar and misses the score bar by 0.007 points of CRPS at the eight; F3d-R misses the leak bar. Leak of a 3-day step at the eight (six): F3d 1.14 (1.21), F3d-E3 0.02 (0.02), F3d-R 0.98 (1.05), F1d-182 0.92 (0.92). F3d-E3 cuts the leak by 100% at 1 day and 98% at 3 days, by 34% at 7 days (1.74 against 2.64), and by 15% at 14 days. F3d-E3 delays adaptation by about 3 days (share of a lasting step after 3 days 0.1% against 19%, after 14 days 27% against 39%, after 28 days 44% against 46%). F3d-R cuts the leak of a 3-day step by 14% at the eight and 13% at the six.

  • Tails: q99 pinball loss of every arm is within +0.0024 of L-Ww (limit +0.02); coverage of the nominal 99% quantile is 98.5% to 99.6% for every arm at both groups. - Cold winter nights (eight, six): L-Ww 4.348 and 3.494, F1d 4.224 and 3.434, F3d 4.283 and 3.481, F1d-182 4.308 and 3.555, F3d-E3 4.349 and 3.472, F3d-R 4.306 and 3.530. - Lead bands: F1d's CRPS is the lowest of the six arms in all seven lead bands at the eight and in six of seven at the six, where F1d-182 is lower at 0 to 6 h (4.029 against 4.041; table in the data folder, crps_by_band.csv). - Curtailment at the six (avoidable-curtailment cost in experiment 449's units, f = 0.9, 0.75, 0.5): L-Ww 0.95, 5.96, 22.26; F1d 0.73, 5.47, 21.43; F3d 0.75, 5.64, 21.77; F1d-182 0.88, 5.60, 21.58; F3d-E3 0.96, 6.04, 22.46; F3d-R 0.96, 5.98, 22.04. - Minimum detectable effect: CRPS 0.164 (eight) and 0.123 (six), carried from experiment 510's two seeds, not refitted. The CRPS contrasts of F3d-E3 and F3d-R against F3d are below it, so they read as "interval excludes zero", not as "at least this large".

docs.title: Serving complexity
docs.text: Every arm serves one neural network per forecast pass. F1d and F3d refit daily or every 3 days (a fine-tune of about 3 s). F3d-E3 is the F3d schedule with the newest 3 days of targets left out, which an operator can read as "never learn from the last 3 days". F3d-R is the F3d schedule with each row's weight multiplied by min(1, 3 / |z|), where z is the row's residual against the previous 3-day fine-tune's median in units of the Primary's residual median absolute deviation over 90 days. The CRPS difference against L-Ww is in the table above. Comparisons with K2-S1 are not reported: K2-S1's forecasts beyond 24 h of lead are voided (the correction at the top of experiment 511's page).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: • Median minus mean forecast: not computed; the arms output quantiles of one mixture and no mean forecast, so the check does not apply. - Quantile score against error of the median: CRPS and q99 pinball loss against L-Ww point the same way for F3d-E3 at the eight (zero) and F3d-R at the eight (both lower), and differ in sign for F3d-R at the six (CRPS -0.004, q99 +0.0024), where both intervals include zero. - Triggers fired: none. The reproduction of 510's 6.11 passed (6.12). A code review before the first run is triaged below. - Look-ahead: for each arm, the rows selected at 2026-01-11 had 0 rows past the valid-time cut (cutoff minus 3.5 h) and 0 past the origin cut; the example row has valid time 2024-04-11 05:00, origin 2024-04-10 09:00, cutoff 2026-01-11. The fine-tune of F1d at 2026-01-10 reproduced the stored weights of experiment 511 to 8e-5 points in the median (maximum).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text: • Deviations from the pre-registered plan: one seed for every stress cell, no stored two-seed leak interval, and the leak contrasts use the sign-pair noise above; F1d-182 skipped the bad-data cells and the 1-day, 14-day, 3-standard-deviation, and alternating-sign cells, and F3d-E3 and F3d-R skipped the bad-data cells, to stay within the compute cap; the unmirrored injection hits all 16 Primaries together (the plan's "donor and recipient" wording was implemented as all Primaries, and the mirrored sensitivity as alternating signs). - Not computed: curtailment differences against L-Ww, F1d, and BG2 with block intervals (only the absolute costs above and the script's differences against K2-S1 and the manual heuristic); the "harm rows" of the pre-registered plan; the fold-by-fold signs of the CRPS contrasts beyond what the stored table holds. - The unlearn time of F3d-E3 is not comparable: its first refit contains no leak by construction at L of 3 days or less, so "days to 10% of the first value" has no meaning for it. - F3d-R's reference is the plain F3d fit 3 days earlier under the same injection, with the residual median absolute deviation computed in-sample, which makes the clipping stricter than an out-of-sample rule would. - A "1-day" step covers 20.5 h because the newest training targets are 3.5 h old at the refit. - The lasting step's first refit contains no injected row, so day 0 reads zero by construction. - The labels are incomplete: unlogged load-shift events may sit in the fine-tuning windows, so every leak here is a lower bound for the real leak and the real-event counts are lower bounds. - Horizon: the scores cover leads of 0 to 240 h; the leak is reported by the seven lead bands in the data folder (leak_by_band.csv).

docs.title: Triage of the code review
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed e00556_fit.py before the first run. Accepted: the stuck-reading sign (the leak is read along each Primary's realised injection direction), the stuck-reading start index and its silent-zero case (now the last finite reading, with an assertion), the wrong return annotation, float64 sums, and runtime assertions for the look-ahead cut and for injected rows being non-empty. Rejected: stricter gating of the run on the reproduction check (the check passed and is in "Checks"); the in-sample residual deviation of F3d-R, kept and caveated; the 20.5 h step and the zero day-0 adaptation, kept and caveated.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: An experiment that explains the plateau of adaptation, by fine-tuning without early stopping on the clean held-out weeks and with a shorter recency half-life, is the next test; the shorter half-life was already shown in experiment 511 to raise the leak, so the pair of results would fix the trade-off.

docs.title: Does one demand network for all 14 Primaries lose accuracy against using the lag-light network at the eight and the lag-free network at the six?
docs.text:
One lag-light network for all 14 Primaries beats the per-group choice, because the lag-free recipe is 0.081 points of CRPS worse than the lag-light network at the six. We asked whether the lag-free recipe is good enough at the six signed-MW Primaries to use there, with the lag-light network (which reads yesterday's and last week's power) only at the eight MVA-only Primaries. We re-scored the stored forecasts of two earlier experiments and ran no fit. The pre-registered test failed at the six: the mean difference between the two networks exceeds 0.03 in every lead band (by 0.001 at 120-240 h). Nothing is adopted. Verdict: not supported. All numbers are CRPS in points of capacity (lower is better), over five test months, interim and unaudited.

Terms. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. The eight are the Primary substations metered in MVA only, and the six are the Primaries metered in signed MW; D15 and D18 are two further Primaries scored report-only. L-1d is the daily-refit demand network without power readings (experiment 511). "Folds" are the five test months. A Bonferroni interval is widened for the number of counted tests. Lag-light is arm RDWT-D15 of experiment 553: day-ago and week-ago power readings, trailing temperature windows, and 15% lag dropout, with the readings present. Lag-free is arm E of experiment 548. A-pool is the network that reads all recent power (experiment 425). The three options are (a) lag-light at all 14, (b) lag-free at all 14, and (c) lag-light at the eight and lag-free at the six. Option (c) is a row selection of the two stored arms, so it equals (a) at the eight and (b) at the six.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Pre-registered test. (a) within 0.03 of (c) at the six: failed. The difference is -0.081 over 24-120 h and -0.059 over all leads, and larger than 0.03 in every band (smallest -0.031 at 120-240 h). At the eight the test holds by construction, since (a) and (c) are the same network. The failure runs the other way from the cost the test guards against: (a) is better than (c), so the per-group choice gives up accuracy, and one network for all 14 does not.
  • Predictions. P1 (six, 24-120 h, lag-light minus lag-free between -0.10 and 0.00): held, -0.081. P2 (lag-free at the eight trails by 0.10 to 0.14): held, 0.117. P3 (Christmas week at the eight, lag-light no worse than lag-free by more than 0.10): held, -0.064 (3.902 against 3.965 over 24-120 h; one week, no interval). P4 (leak above lag-free, under 6.0): held as stored, 5.33 against 4.55.

Table 1. Lag-light minus lag-free, 24-120 h (report-only; the 14 counted contrasts are the 7 bands at each of the eight and the six) (95% month-block bootstrap, 5 blocks, near min-to-max; Bonferroni count 14; MDE = minimum detectable effect, from the two seeds of L-1d).

Primaries CRPS lag-light CRPS lag-free Difference Interval MDE Folds worse Eight 4.438 4.555 -0.117 -0.174 to -0.078 0.116 0 of 5 Six 3.209 3.290 -0.081 -0.119 to -0.044 0.155 0 of 5 All 14 (a) against (c) 3.993 4.022 -0.029 -0.043 to -0.017 0.126 0 of 5

Both 24-120 h intervals exclude zero after the Bonferroni widening for 14 tests (upper ends -0.065 and -0.032). Of the 14 counted per-band contrasts, the two at 0-6 h include zero after widening; the other 12 exclude it. The difference at the six is under its MDE, and the eight's difference (-0.117) equals its MDE (0.116), so neither is confirmed by the seed noise alone, but the sign agrees in all five folds.

  • Per band. Lag-light minus lag-free at the eight, from 0-6 h to 120-240 h: -0.090, -0.194, -0.159, -0.133, -0.120, -0.108, -0.053. At the six: -0.046, -0.135, -0.120, -0.091, -0.082, -0.075, -0.031. The gain is largest at 6-12 h and shrinks with lead time.

At the six, lag-light is -0.071 (-0.109 to -0.015) and lag-free is +0.010 (-0.046 to +0.079). The lag-free recipe is not shown to differ from A-pool at the six; the lag-light network is better than A-pool there.

The six has no rows outside the clean class, so its "no labelled event" row equals its all-rows row. Intervals for the one-week and bank-holiday slices rest on 1 to 5 blocks and are not reliable. The cold-night slice at the six over all leads is the one cell where the mean difference favours lag-free better (2 of 3 folds; this slice has 3 test months), and its interval includes zero.

  • D15 and D18 (report only). Lag-light is 0.441 better over 24-120 h (interval -0.702 to -0.128) but 0.604 worse in Christmas week; the minimum detectable effect at these two series is 1.4, so neither figure is resolved.
  • Tails, 24-120 h. Pinball loss at q95: -0.051 (-0.071 to -0.032) at the eight and -0.022 (-0.034 to -0.007) at the six, in favour of lag-light. At q99: -0.017 and -0.003.
  • Injected-shift leak (stored, experiment 553, all 14 Primaries pooled): lag-light 5.33 points of capacity, lag-free 4.55, L-1d 4.49. The leak is not split by group, so it does not separate the eight from the six.
  • Operational cost of each option. (a) One recipe to maintain, and the day-ago and week-ago power readings are required at all 14 Primaries (with 15% dropout, the network still runs when they are absent, at the lag-free score). (b) One recipe, no readings required, 0.104 CRPS worse over 24-120 h at the 14. (c) Two recipes to maintain, readings required only at the eight, 0.029 CRPS worse than (a) over 24-120 h at the 14.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Origin-time weather is the standing rule; this experiment reads only stored per-row scores of experiments 548 and 553, which assert it row by row (experiment 553: 1,142,520 test rows over 153 test origins, for example origin 2025-10-01 09:00 UTC, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC). No forecast is made here, so there is no new row to assert.
  • Rows. 1,145,256 stored rows; 1,142,520 have a finite CRPS for every arm used and form the row sets (the same count as experiment 553). July 2026 is not scored.
  • Counted contrasts: 14, matching the Bonferroni count.
  • Reviews. One Sonnet code review before scoring. It found that the first draft omitted experiment 553's finiteness mask, which would have let the absolute means of different arms average over different rows. That mask is now applied. It also found that the first assertions were tautological; they are now null checks on the per-group column. Its other findings are recorded below in the caveats. Write-up review: see the pull request.
  • Cost: CPU only, 2 cores, a few minutes. No GPU.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Seeds. Both arms are pools of seeds 0 and 1, as every stored comparator is. The difference at the six (0.081) is under its MDE (0.155), so it needs the multi-seed bake-off to confirm.
  • The six is the clean class. The six's row set is rows with no labelled event, as in experiments 521 and 553, so the 14 here are the eight plus the clean rows of the six. NGED's load-shift logs may miss events, so these rows may hold unlabelled events.
  • No forecast plots. The experiment makes no new forecast, so it has no day-ahead or 10-day example of its own. The forecasts of arm RDWT-D15 are plotted in experiment 553; the stored predictions of arm E are not drawn here.
  • Lead range. The lead range is 0 to 240 h, which covers the 1 to 10 day horizon NGED care about.
  • Bootstrap draws differ in order from experiment 553's, so intervals for the same contrast may differ from experiment 553's in the third decimal place.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Take the lag-light network forward as the single candidate for all 14 Primaries in the planned multi-seed bake-off, and keep the lag-free recipe as the fallback for missing readings.
  • Look at the six on cold winter nights, the one slice whose mean difference favoured lag-free, in that bake-off.

docs.title: What does a 24-hour cap on the newest lag cost the lag-light demand network, and do lags in ERA5/CAMS pretraining recover it?
docs.text:
Take-home message. Dropping every reading newer than 24 hours raises the lag-light network's CRPS by 0.09 to 0.23 points of capacity at the eight MVA-only Primaries from 6 h to 120 h. Putting the same capped lags into the ERA5/CAMS pretraining lowers CRPS again by 0.13 to 0.19 points from 12 h to 72 h, which brings the capped network to within the minimum detectable effect of the uncapped one. The next step is to weigh that against a higher injected-shift leak: 7.7 points of capacity for the pretrained, capped network, against 5.4 without lags in pretraining and a 6.0 limit. Every number here is interim and unaudited.

Arm key. R-DW is experiment 539's lag-light network with uncapped day and week lags. R-DW-24 caps both lags at 24 h and adds block dropout, with lags added at fine-tuning only. R-DW-24-PT is R-DW-24 with the same capped lags also in the ERA5/CAMS pretraining. A-pool-24 is the capped recipe with A-pool's monthly refit and 182.6-day half-life, built in this experiment's fitting code, not in experiment 425's. L-1d is the lag-free network and A-pool the lag-enabled network. "The eight" are the MVA-only Primaries, "the six" the signed-MW Primaries. CRPS is in points of capacity.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
P1 fails: the cap raises CRPS at 48-120 h by more than the 0.05 limit. At the eight, R-DW-24 minus R-DW is 0.12, 0.23, and 0.16 at 0-6, 6-12, and 12-24 h, 0.13 and 0.11 at 24-48 and 48-72 h, and 0.09 at 72-120 h. The month-block interval excludes zero from 6 h to 120 h (0.03 to 0.36). The difference is positive in 5 of 5 folds in each of those bands. At 0-6 h the interval includes zero (-0.02 to 0.29), so the 0-6 h rise is not shown. The rises at 48-72 h and 72-120 h are below those bands' minimum detectable effect (0.14 and 0.10).

P2 is supported at 12-72 h, with the gain near the detectable limit. R-DW-24-PT minus R-DW-24 is -0.19, -0.16, -0.13, and -0.09 at 12-24, 24-48, 48-72, and 72-120 h at the eight. The interval excludes zero from 12 h to 72 h, with a negative sign in 5 of 5 folds. At 72-120 h the interval includes zero (-0.24 to 0.01), so that gain is not shown. The gains at 48-72 h and 72-120 h are below the minimum detectable effect. R-DW-24-PT against R-DW is not shown to differ in any band.

P3 fails on the point estimates. A-pool-24 minus R-DW-24-PT is 0.17, 0.16, and 0.14 at 24-48, 48-72, and 72-120 h, above the 0.04 limit. After the Bonferroni correction (4 tests) the intervals at 24-72 h include zero, so the gap is established only at 72-120 h. The gap also includes the difference between this experiment's fitting code and experiment 425's.

P4 fails on the point estimates. The injected-shift leak is 7.75 points of capacity for R-DW-24-PT, 5.43 for R-DW-24, 5.68 for R-DW, and 4.49 for L-1d. The intervals overlap (R-DW-24-PT 5.8 to 12.1, R-DW-24 2.6 to 11.5, L-1d 2.6 to 10.5), and no paired test was run. The R-DW-24-PT leak is highest on the first day after the shift (9.95).

docs.title: Other results
docs.text:
The capped, pretrained network matches the uncapped one overall. Over all leads at the eight, CRPS is 4.72 for R-DW-24-PT, 4.71 for R-DW, 4.79 for R-DW-24, 4.85 for A-pool-24 and L-1d, 4.68 for A-pool, and 5.62 for the manual heuristic.

Removing the lags at inference worsens the pretrained networks most. CRPS rises by 0.05 for R-DW-24, 0.26 for R-DW-24-PT, and 0.38 for A-pool-24. The pretrained arms therefore rely more on their lags, which fits their higher injected-shift leak.

At the six, the cap changes CRPS by little. Over all leads CRPS is 3.43 for R-DW-24, 3.45 for R-DW, and 3.39 for R-DW-24-PT.

Leaving out training rows with a missing capped lag does not explain the A-pool-24 gap. CRPS is 4.852 with the rows left out and 4.850 without, a difference of 0.003, against a 0.13 gap between A-pool-24 and R-DW-24-PT.

docs.title: Method notes and limits
docs.text:
The statistics use 5 month blocks, which is close to the minimum-to-maximum range of the folds. Intervals are bootstraps over 5 month blocks. The minimum detectable effect, from the two L-1d seeds, is 0.10 to 0.27 by lead band. The pre-registered Bonferroni count is 4. All contrasts, with their per-fold signs, are in contrasts.csv in the private data folder.

Block dropout masks whole origin days. Each day is drawn from (seed, day number). The expected shares are 25.5% of days with all lags masked and 4.5% with only the day lag, the literal reading of "30% of days, 15% of those day-only". In one fine-tuning fit (R-DW-24-PT, fold 2025-10, seed 0) the realised shares were 23.1% and 7.1% of rows. Block dropout also masks the validation rows used for early stopping. The lag value statistics come from the uncapped lags and apply unchanged to the capped lags. In the pretraining rows of fold 2025-12, 0.65% lack the capped day lag and 0.79% the capped week lag (printed at run time).

Weather and lag timing are asserted. Every test row's weather run is at or before its origin (153 origins). Every capped lag is at least 24 h before its origin, checked against an independent loop on 2,000 rows per fold.

NGED's load-shift event labels are incomplete. Rows with no labelled event may hold unlabelled events, and these results are not corrected for that.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Test the capped recipe with delayed telemetry. The test that ages the lags by 1, 2, and 3 extra days was not run, and it is the direct check of the requirement that production survives telemetry delayed by days.
  • Stress A-pool-24. Its monthly refit has no day-14 refit, so its injected-shift leak was not measured.
  • Build A-pool-24 in experiment 425's own pipeline. The 0.14 to 0.17 gap to R-DW-24-PT mixes the capped recipe with a different fitting loop.
  • Reduce the injected-shift leak of lag-aware pretraining. For example, draw the dropout again at each pretraining epoch, or raise the share of days with all lags masked.

docs.title: Can the modular lag-free demand network (M0) keep its gain while an injected shift in the recent data leaks less into its forecasts, using a three-step training schedule, frozen encoders, an L2 penalty, gentler fine-tuning, weight averaging, or a metering-type output head?
docs.text:
M0's leak and its skill move together in the step-2 arms: each arm that cut the leak lost skill at the eight. The injected-shift leak (a 7-day shift in the recent data, in points of capacity) falls from 7.60 for M0 to between 2.1 and 5.0 for arms A1 to A6 and A8, which is at or below the release limit of 6.0. Each of those arms is also worse than M0 at 24 to 120 h at the eight MVA-only Primaries, by 0.09 to 0.42 points of CRPS, and the stronger the leak cut the larger the loss (figure 1). The trailing-temperature arm (A9) and the drift embedding (A10) left the leak at 6.67 and 7.28. The wind arm (A11) cut it to 5.12 with a CRPS change of +0.032 at the eight, but its placebo (A11-null) cut it to 7.15 from 7.60, and A9's placebo differs from A9 by 2.55 points, so leak differences of about 2.5 points are within placebo noise.

Take-home message and next step. Training the mixer once on the whole ensemble history (step 2) and then fine-tuning daily (A1) is the cheapest way to cut the leak, but it gives back about half of M0's gain over L-1d at the eight (0.086 of 0.166 points). A fine-tune that cannot move far (A2 frozen encoders, A3 penalty, A4 gentle rate) cuts the leak further and loses all of M0's gain at the eight. Whether the release limit or the gain matters more at the eight is the maintainer's call; the experiment does not settle it.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Arms: A1 to A8 are the plan's arms (step 2 shared by A1 to A5, A6 and A7 as in experiment 554, A8 the folded-normal head). A9 adds experiment 515's and 526's three trailing-temperature columns to the weather encoder, with a matched shuffled-day placebo (A9-null). A10 adds a per-Primary drift embedding with monthly knots, smoothness penalty 10 times the mean squared second difference, flat extrapolation, learned over the 2019-09 ERA5 and CAMS history; both encoders are frozen in fine-tuning. A11 adds 10 m and 100 m wind u and v (mean and standard deviation), with a column-count-matched placebo (A11-null). A11c adds total cloud cover with a placebo (A11c-null), on four folds only.
  • Scoring: five folds of 511 (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 2 seeds, rows with no labelled event, month-block bootstrap with 5 blocks (near the minimum to maximum of the five folds), 28 counted tests (11 arms against M0 and the 2 placebo pairs, each at the eight and at the six over 24 to 120 h, plus the 2 placebo pairs on cold nights at the eight). The minimum detectable effect (MDE) comes from the 5 stored seeds of L-1d in experiment 554. Every real weather input of a target comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin; the scripts assert it row by row for the base frames and print one example row per fold. The placebo columns take their values from a donor day, which can be a later run, and carry no weather information.
  • Not tuned: the L2 strength was chosen on fold 2025-10 alone, as the plan said. All four strengths were within 0.012 of the best early-stopping loss, and the largest (1.0) was chosen, so A3 stays very close to the step-2 weights.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS against M0, 24 to 120 h (points of capacity; positive means worse than M0). Interval: month-block, 5 blocks. Leave-D8-out: the eight without Primary D8.

Arm Leak Eight Eight, leave-D8-out Six M0 7.60 (against L-1d: −0.166) (−0.071) (−0.075) A1 4.84 +0.086 (−0.037 to +0.202) +0.052 (−0.108 to +0.195) −0.009 (−0.093 to +0.068) A2 frozen encoders 3.31 +0.167 (+0.019 to +0.315) +0.115 (−0.063 to +0.301) +0.039 (−0.050 to +0.128) A3 penalty 2.11 +0.416 (+0.285 to +0.557) +0.308 (+0.127 to +0.504) +0.148 (+0.046 to +0.262) A4 gentle rate 2.79 +0.241 (+0.114 to +0.367) +0.164 (−0.027 to +0.343) +0.061 (−0.028 to +0.158) A5 weight average 4.73 +0.133 (+0.021 to +0.252) +0.098 (−0.053 to +0.259) +0.023 (−0.052 to +0.103) A6 half-life 180 4.64 +0.117 (+0.024 to +0.277) +0.108 (−0.038 to +0.311) +0.043 (+0.001 to +0.088) A7 3-day cadence 7.95 +0.035 (+0.018 to +0.055) +0.039 (+0.024 to +0.057) +0.048 (+0.017 to +0.092) A8 folded head 4.99 +0.090 (−0.009 to +0.190) +0.046 (−0.094 to +0.171) −0.010 (−0.093 to +0.066) A9 6.67 −0.020 (−0.054 to +0.022) −0.019 (−0.049 to +0.012) −0.004 (−0.095 to +0.087) A10 7.28 −0.024 (−0.184 to +0.162) −0.057 (−0.256 to +0.170) −0.157 (−0.362 to +0.038) A11 5.12 +0.032 (−0.050 to +0.100) +0.039 (−0.036 to +0.092) +0.066 (+0.034 to +0.091)

The MDE is 0.18 at the eight, 0.14 at the six, and 0.38 and 0.36 on cold nights at the eight and six. Most intervals include zero; the intervals above that exclude zero at the 5-block month level are A2 (eight), A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, and A11 at the six. Five blocks limit the interval to the range of the five folds, and the cold-night tests rest on 3 blocks, so the Bonferroni-corrected intervals are weak evidence: A3 (eight and six), A4 (eight), A6 (eight), A7 (eight and six), and A11 (six) still exclude zero after the correction for 28 tests, and each has the same sign in at least 4 of 5 folds.
