  • Coarse cadence: one fit per fold leaves the fit up to 30 days old, so the absolute scores are month-old-fit scores. Daily refits lower T0 by 0.280 at the eight MVA Primaries (interval -0.445 to -0.086) and are the fairer comparison with experiment 559's M0.
  • Un-standardised spread: three of the seven block columns are recovered from columns clipped at five standard deviations, so they cap at five; the cap was not counted per fold.
  • Not computed: the median minus the mean per site, the tail coverage and pinball tables, the day-ahead and 14-day example forecasts, load-shift time series plots, T6, and daily refits for T1 and T5 (agreed with the manager because the placebo matched T1). NGED's event labels are incomplete, so real-event counts are lower bounds.
  • Audit triggers: two fired: a nested arm beat the arm containing its inputs (T4 beats T1), and the result contradicts its prediction (P1, P4, P5). The prediction failures are explained above by the placebo and the MLP control. The headline contrasts are re-derived by e00568_score.py from the stored per-row scores. No separate audit agent was run.
  • Weights: fine-tuned weights of every arm are in work/models/<arm>/ (coarse fits, and daily fits for T0 and T4), step-2 and pretrained weights in work/step2/ and work/pretrained/ATT/, in the experiment's private data folder. About 3 GPU-hours were used (estimated from logged run times).

docs.title: Does each input group help the modular network when it also enters pre-training, through the encoder that matches it?
docs.text:
Status: finished. Every number is interim and unaudited.

Take-home message. We gave a neural network that forecasts demand at 16 primary substations ("Primaries") six groups of extra inputs: thermal-lag and solar-gain windows (B1), look-ahead weather windows (B2), school terms (B3a), national signals of the previous day (B3b), a whole-day price shape (B4), and school terms gated by the number of schools nearby (B3c). Experiment 562 added the first five only during fine-tuning on ensemble weather forecasts; here they also enter pre-training on ERA5 (the ECMWF reanalysis) and CAMS (Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service) rows. Each group entered through the part of the network that matches its content. We compared each group with a shuffled-day placebo: columns of the same width taken from a different day. Errors are CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) in points of effective capacity (percentage points of a substation's rated capacity); smaller is better. No group beat its placebo by the minimum detectable effect (the smallest gain this test could tell from noise) on any of the four slices that can justify keeping an input (all rows, cold winter nights, Christmas week, and high-spread days), three contrasts were worse, and every arm scored worse than the baseline network (plain M0), so the verdict is not supported. The next step is a second seed (a second random initialisation) for every arm and a plain M0 re-pre-trained the same way. A name ending in p (B1p) is the placebo of the arm without it.

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Network and folds. The modular lag-free network of experiment 554 (arm M0), refitted once per fold (coarse refit, scored for the whole month) on experiment 511's five folds, July 2026 unused, seed 0. Plain M0 (stored pre-trained weights, seeds 0 and 1) is the control. The code reuses experiments 437, 448, 511, 515, 554, and 562.
  • Routes. B1 (thermal lag, solar gain, 14 columns) and B2 (look-ahead windows, 6) enter the weather encoder. B3a (school terms, 5 columns plus a presence flag) and B3c (B3a plus 5 columns gated by the count of schools within 2 km) enter the datetime encoder. B3b (national signals of the previous day, 7 plus a flag) and B4 (whole-day price shape, 12) enter a small parallel encoder that feeds both mixers.
  • Pre-training history. School terms exist from 2021-09, national signals from 2023-01, and the price shape from 2023, while pre-training starts in 2019-09. Earlier pre-training rows get zeros and a presence flag of 0.
  • School proximity. The count of open schools within 2 km comes from the Department for Education's "Get Information about Schools" register (source, Open Government Licence v3.0, downloaded 2026-11-05 into the private data folder).
  • Weather timing. Fine-tuning and scoring rows assert, row by row, that the weather run is issued at or before the forecast origin. One example row per fold is in the logs: origin 2025-10-01 09:00, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00. Pre-training rows use the same ERA5 and CAMS stand-ins as the 37 base inputs.
  • Statistics. Month-block bootstrap with one block per fold (5 blocks on all rows, 3 on cold nights, 1 on Christmas week), so each interval is close to the range of the fold means, per-fold signs, the minimum detectable effect (MDE) from the fold-by-seed spread of plain M0 seeds 0 and 1, 48 counted contrasts (6 contrasts x 2 groups x 4 keep-rule slices) for the Bonferroni interval, and 120 uncorrected "hurt" checks (6 x 2 x 10 slices). Heatwave and high-PV-ramp days were not scored.

docs.title: Step 1: school terms in experiment 562
docs.text:
• The spread of the school-term effect across Primaries is smaller than seed noise. Real minus placebo ranges from -0.230 to +0.314 points (standard deviation 0.137 over 16 Primaries); plain M0 seed 0 minus seed 1 on the same rows has standard deviation 0.224. Only D8 has a 5-block interval that excludes zero, on the harmful side.
  • School proximity does not explain the spread. Spearman correlation of the effect with open schools within 2 km is +0.28 (bootstrap over Primaries -0.30 to +0.72), within 5 km -0.09. The pre-registered expectation (at most -0.3, interval excluding zero) fails. D15 and D18 share one location.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• No group improves any keep-rule slice by its MDE. Real minus placebo on all rows, 24-120 h, eight MVA Primaries and six MW Primaries: B1 -0.036 and -0.135; B2 +0.052 and -0.059; B3a -0.028 and -0.013; B3b -0.040 and +0.010; B4 +0.106 and -0.049. The MDE on all rows is 0.103 and 0.299. On cold nights the largest gain is B4 at the six MW Primaries, -0.225 (interval -0.58 to -0.05), against an MDE of 0.72.
  • Three contrasts are worse. B4 at the eight MVA Primaries on all rows (+0.106, worse in 4 of 5 folds, MDE 0.103), B3c minus B3a at the eight on all rows (+0.112, 4 of 5 folds) and on rows with no labelled event (+0.100). B3c minus B3a at the six is +0.131 (Bonferroni interval +0.01 to +0.33).
  • Every extra-input arm is worse than the two-seed mean of plain M0. On all rows, 24-120 h, that mean scores 4.841 at the eight MVA Primaries and 3.639 at the six MW Primaries; M0 seed 0 alone scores 4.902 and 3.668, and seed 1 alone 4.917 and 3.724. The arms score 4.87 to 5.10 at the eight and 3.68 to 3.93 at the six, so against a single M0 seed a few arms are level or slightly better (B3b at the eight, 4.871). The gap between each arm and M0 includes a different random initialisation, because widening a layer changes the random draws.
  • Injected-shift leak (interim). The leak is the change in the median forecast, as a percentage of capacity, when a 7-day shift is injected into the fine-tuning history (all lead times, mean of 5 folds; fold range in brackets): M0 9.8 [1.9, 25.6], B1 5.3 [1.0, 13.6], B1 placebo 10.9 [2.2, 28.4], B3a 2.2 [1.1, 3.8], B3a placebo 8.4 [1.5, 21.6]. The real columns carry less of the injected shift than their placebos in this single seed; the fold ranges overlap, and the leak does not enter the keep rule.

Predictions. P1 failed (B1 cold nights at the six: -0.107 against an MDE of 0.72). P2 failed (B3a -0.028 at the eight, interval includes zero). P3 failed for all three by its point-estimate wording: B2 (+0.052 at the eight, -0.059 at the six), B3b (-0.040 at the eight), and B4 (+0.106 at the eight, harmful); the intervals of B2 and B3b include zero and their size is below the MDE. P4 failed (B3c worse than B3a by 0.112), as the step-1 correlation suggested.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Single seed. The MDE comes from two M0 seeds, and the arms have one. A gain smaller than 0.10 points (eight) or 0.30 (six) on all rows could not have been seen.
  • Placebo limits. Pre-training placebos take a donor day from the pre-refit side; a placebo row keeps the real row's presence flag, so a donor from before 2021-09 or 2023 can give zeros where the real row has values. Cut-day-14 placebo fits use donor days drawn for the month's start, not day 14.
  • High-spread slice. The stored scores hold no ensemble-spread column, so the slice is the top tercile of M0's own q95 minus q05 within Primary, fold, and lead band.
  • Not scored. Heatwave and high-PV-ramp days, per-Primary tables, example forecast plots, and the leak for arms other than M0, B1, B1p, B3a, and B3ap. NGED's event logs may be incomplete, so rows with no labelled event can hold unlabelled events.
  • Availability at serving. B1 and B2 need ECMWF runs and, for two B1 columns, the CAMS feed. B3a is a fixed calendar. B3b needs daily Elexon and NESO feeds that production does not read today.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does a plain M0 re-pre-trained with the same code, and a second seed for every arm, shrink the gap to the arms, and does B1 still lower cold-night error at the six MW Primaries once the control is matched?

docs.title: Does training a price encoder on the true electricity price give the weather and datetime encoders of the modular lag-free demand network cleaner supervision, even though price is absent at forecast time?
docs.text:
Status: finished. One combined review and audit checked every number; the findings are in the pull request.

Take-home message. We asked whether teaching a neural network that forecasts substation demand about electricity prices, while it learns from weather and calendar inputs, would make its weather and calendar parts learn cleaner patterns. The price part is thrown away before the forecast is made, so no price feed is needed in production. The price part did not improve the forecast. After fine-tuning, the forecast was worse than a forecast built without any price part: by 0.29 points of capacity at the six MW Primaries and by 0.09 at the eight MVA Primaries. Errors are CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) in points of effective capacity; smaller is better. A control that fed the same extra part noise gave 61% of the harm at the six MW Primaries, and a constant gave 43%, so most of the harm comes from the extra part. A controlled test, in which we added a synthetic price-driven generator to the six MW Primaries, showed the price part could not find the simple threshold or rank rules, and found a battery rule only partly. The next step is a repeat of that controlled test with a generator large enough to see, before any more real-data price work. The verdict is not supported.

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Network and folds. The modular lag-free network of experiment 554 (arm M0), on experiment 511's five folds, July 2026 unused, refitted once a month, 2 seeds (0 and 1). Pre-training used the same ERA5 and CAMS rows as experiment 554, written again here for every arm so that arms differ only in the price part. Fine-tuning followed experiment 554's M0 recipe exactly, with a fresh mixer.
  • The price encoder. A new neural network part that reads three windows of the true price (97 half-hours either side of the target, 7 days of hourly means, and 28 days of daily summaries), a short vector of hand-made shape features, a bank of eight learned price-day shapes, and attention over the fine window. The price encoder outputs 16 numbers, or a learned null vector when price is absent. Price comes from Elexon's market index price, the system price minus the market index price, and the net imbalance volume, 2019-09 to 2026-09, fetched for this experiment (see below).
  • Arms. A6: price encoder in pre-training only; the weather encoder, datetime encoder, and embedding go to a fresh price-free mixer. A1: price encoder kept in fine-tuning, present in a seeded 50% of rows, null vector at forecast. A3: as A1 but the encoder is new at fine-tuning. Each comes with price inputs of kind res (calendar-residualised), raw, p1 (a shuffled day), p2 (the typical shape for month, half-hour, and day type), noise, or const. M0 is the control with no price part. A "-oracle" arm scores the same fitted networks with the true price present. M0-R of the brief is identical to M0 here, because M0's fine-tuning mixer is already fresh.
  • Standing rules. Every weather input comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin, asserted row by row, with one example row printed per fold. Price windows may look 14 days forward in the oracle (true price) but are cut at the refit time for every training row, so no price from the test month reaches training. Scoring reads the uncut series only for the "-oracle" arms.
  • Price data and licence. See the last section.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute CRPS, 24 to 120 h leads. Plain M0: 4.834 (eight MVA Primaries) and 3.633 (six MW Primaries). A6-res: 4.926 and 3.926. A6 fed noise: 4.896 and 3.811. A6 fed a constant: 4.945 and 3.758. A3-res: 4.784 and 3.748. A1-res: 4.875 and 4.118.
  • None of the six counted tests passes. The tests are T1 and T2, A6-res minus A6-noise; T3 and T4, A1-res minus A1-noise; at the eight and the six, 24 to 120 h, Bonferroni count 6. A6-res minus A6-noise is +0.03 at the eight (minimum detectable effect, MDE, 0.113) and +0.115 at the six (MDE 0.128): worse, not better, and below the MDE. A1-res minus A1-noise is -0.073 at the eight (3 of 5 folds better) and +0.035 at the six. T5 and T6 (arm A7) were not run.
  • Pre-training with price made the fine-tuned stack worse. A6-res minus M0 is +0.092 at the eight (interval -0.022 to +0.181, 4 of 5 folds worse) and +0.293 at the six (interval +0.053 to +0.555, 5 of 5 folds worse). Noise and constant inputs account for much of it (+0.06 and +0.11 at the eight, +0.18 and +0.12 at the six). At the six, A6-res was also worse than the constant-fed control by 0.168 (5 of 5 folds, driven by the 2026-01 fold at +0.58) and than the noise-fed control by 0.115; at the eight it was 0.019 better than the constant-fed control. One Primary carries much of the six's harm: its A6-res minus M0 gap, in unnormalised CRPS, is about 0.86 against at most 0.24 at every other Primary of the 16, so the six-Primary result rests mainly on one series. Prediction A6-1 (a gain of at least 1% at the Primaries) fails.
  • Which kind of price did least harm. Raw price beat residualised price (res) at the eight by 0.05 (A6-raw minus A6-res -0.051, within the MDE, raw better in 4 of 5 folds). Prediction A6-4, that raw would be worse by at least 0.03 points, fails in the opposite direction. A6-res was 0.05 worse than its shuffled-day control at the eight and 0.235 worse at the six (5 of 5 folds each). The typical-shape control (p2) was better than the real price by 0.063 and 0.165.
  • Scoring with the true price was not better. A1-res scored with the true price minus scored with the null vector: +0.19 at the eight (5 of 5 folds worse, interval +0.096 to +0.289) and +0.063 at the six. The kept encoder, shown the true price, did worse than with the null vector.
  • Pre-training validation loss. Mean validation negative log-likelihood over 5 folds and 2 seeds (oracle price present, lower is better; the early stopping also reads this loss, and A6 arms stopped after 22 to 26 epochs on average against 40.5 for M0): M0 0.4891, A6-p2 0.4765, A6-const 0.4917, A6-raw 0.4996, A6-res 0.5034, A6-p1 0.5345, A6-noise 0.5489. A6-res is above M0 in 5 of 5 folds (+0.005 to +0.024). The typical-shape price is below M0 in 5 of 5 folds (-0.001 to -0.024).
  • Leave-D8-out. A6-res minus M0 is +0.087 at the eight without D8 (interval -0.024 to +0.192, 3 of 5 folds worse) and +0.127 at D8 alone (interval -0.183 to +0.423); the sign matches the eight's. D15 and D18 are report-only; every set is in work/scores/contrasts.csv.

docs.title: Known-answer test
docs.text:
The price part recovered a battery rule only partly and the other two rules not at all. We subtracted a synthetic price-driven generator from the six MW Primaries' pre-training rows, at 2% of each Primary's effective capacity (0.1 to 0.2 MW), and asked how much of the injected output the price part's forecast change recovered. M0 without price was trained on the same rows to give the baseline. "Recovered" is one minus the mean squared gap between the injected output and the forecast change, relative to the mean squared injected output; 0.6 is the pass mark of the brief. The share can be negative, and a separately trained network gives values near -0.1 to 0 from seed noise alone, so a share in that band means "indistinguishable from nothing". The held-out rows are the weeks that also drive early stopping, which makes the shares mildly optimistic, and the "real" price features are the raw kind, not the residualised kind of the headline arm.

  • K2 fails for the threshold and rank rules. R1 (full output above 90 GBP per MWh) recovered -0.09 to +0.01 across 5 folds, and R2 (six dearest half-hours) -0.15 and -0.12 (2 folds). The learned threshold (K1) was never found: the fitted response did not reach half of full output at any price, and the gain at prices above 150 GBP per MWh was 11% to 18% of capacity, against 100% injected.
  • R3, the battery rule, was found partly. Recovered 0.46 and 0.44 (2 folds), below the 0.6 pass mark. The typical-shape control recovered -0.06 and -0.08, so the recovery is price-specific (K3 passes for R3 only; for R1 and R2 the control also recovers negative values, so K3 says nothing).
  • K4 was not run in the intended form. The brief's test fine-tunes after discarding the price part. We ran only a pre-training form: contaminating the training rows only, and scoring clean rows. The price network scored worse (validation NLL 0.853 and 0.809 against 0.698 and 0.675 for M0), consistent with the price network applying the rule to clean rows that do not obey it. The loss also drives early stopping, so model selection contributes. This says nothing about damage to the discarded-encoder stack. K4 is not tested.
  • The injected generator may be too small. At 0.1 to 0.2 MW it is small beside the forecast error (not computed here). A failure to recover it shows the encoder at this size cannot see a 2%-of-capacity rule, and does not show the encoder cannot learn such rules.

docs.title: Step 0 (report-only)
docs.text:
• Step 0(a). Stored experiment 554 M0 forecast residuals of the 16 Primaries, on the months of price then on disk, regressed on same-time price features after removing the half-hour-by-weekend mean: in-sample R-squared 0.2% to 4.1%, and leave-one-month-out R-squared negative at all 16 (-0.3% to -16%). This regression does not transfer across months. It does not rule out a nonlinear rule. Script: e00570_step0a.py.
  • Step 0(b) and 0(c) were not run: the metered-battery check and the measured BSP-and-GSP minimum detectable effects. The MDEs quoted are the brief's two-seed values.

docs.title: What was not done
docs.text:
The brief listed more arms than the 6 GPU-hour budget allowed. Not run: the national-weather part of the residualisation (the residual is calendar-only), arm A7 and its shuffled control, arm A6-F (frozen encoders), the feature ladder and arm G1, the four BSP and GSP pooled structures, the probes of the encoder outputs (A6-2) and partial dependence, and the oracle arms A4 and A5. The known-answer test covers only the six MW Primaries, rule R1 on 5 folds and rules R2 and R3 on 2 folds; the K1 minimum run time is not measured; the shuffled-day control was dropped from it. No cold-night, Christmas, tail coverage, or curtailment-cost slice was scored, and the page draws no example forecast.

GPU time was about 5.3 hours by the worker's own estimate; no GPU accounting was kept, and the logs span about 7.3 hours of wall clock including failed runs and the known-answer test.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Triggers that fired. (1) Controls failed: the known-answer test failed for R1 and R2. (5) A control that should change nothing moved the score by more than its own paired interval's half-width: the noise-fed and constant-fed encoders moved CRPS by +0.18 and +0.12 at the six. The audit that these triggers call for is in the pull request.
  • Scored rows. Each fold's forecasts cover targets inside the fold month only (237,026 to 194,792 rows per fold of the experiment 511 row set; 1,145,256 over the five folds, 1,142,520 with every arm finite).

docs.title: Lessons for later experiments
docs.text:
• Do not add a price encoder to pre-training of the modular lag-free network. A noise-fed encoder of the same size gives 61% of the harm at the six MW Primaries, so the extra encoder is what lowers accuracy.
  • A known-answer test must inject a visible generator. At 2% of capacity, the test cannot tell "the encoder cannot learn the rule" from "the rule is below the noise".
  • The typical-shape price lowered pre-training validation loss in 5 of 5 folds. Calendar information fed through the encoder may help pre-training; this page did not test it.

Attribution line, required on every chart of price data: "Contains BMRS data © Elexon Limited copyright and database right 2026."
  • Fetch: market index price (APXMIDP provider) and system price with net imbalance volume, for 2019-09-01 to 2025-08-31, through the public keyless API with 2 threads, at no cost. Saved under this experiment's private data folder (market_early/), never committed. The longer series, joined to the cached later days, is *_2019-09_to_2026-09.parquet there.
  • Gaps: 71 whole days of market index price and 9 whole days of system price are not published (listed by the fetch script); the price encoder treats them as missing.
  • Definition is unchanged across the span: the system sell and buy prices are identical in every row from 2019 to 2026 (single imbalance price), and every zero market index price coincides with zero traded volume, so zero-volume rows are masked. The market index mean is 37 GBP per MWh in 2019, 198 in 2022 (the gas shock), and 72 to 103 in 2024 to 2026, which is why the transform normalises by trailing 28-day statistics.

docs.title: Maintainer decisions
docs.text: • Step 0 was report-only and the known-answer test a check, not a gate (2026-11-05). The real-data arms ran regardless, with the budget capped at 6 GPU-hours.

docs.title: Does a slow output offset take level shifts while a drift embedding takes changes in behaviour? Known-answer synthetic worlds first, then the real data
docs.text: We asked whether a slow output offset takes level shifts while a drift embedding takes changes in behaviour, using worlds where the answer is known. We injected a known component into the demand series of six Primary substations (three MVA, three MW), fitted the offset (D5), the embedding (A10), the joint hybrid, and a staged hybrid, and measured how much of the CRPS gain of an oracle (a network given the true component) each recovered. In the readable world the embedding recovered nearly all of it and the offset alone under a third, so the hypothesis is not supported. The results are interim and unaudited, from one fold (2025-12) and two seeds.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• First worlds were unreadable. With steps of 3% to 6% of capacity and sensitivity up to 0.4% per degree, the oracle gained 0.27 CRPS points over the drift-free base (2 folds, 2 seeds), and the oracle was worse than frozen D5 (recovery above 100% for several arms; figures from the Wc world's two-fold summary, regenerated in summary_recovery.csv and summary_absolute.csv). Recoveries above 100% and a negative oracle gap at the three MW Primaries of the sensitivity-only world show that the oracle is not a ceiling here. The seed spread of the base was 0.1 to 0.18. This world was dropped, as the pre-registered pass condition requires.
  • Worlds with tripled amplitudes (-big), fold 2025-12, injected Primaries, 24-120 h. Oracle gain over the base: 2.76 points in the combined world (seed spread of the base about 0.7), 2.71 in the steps-only world (1 seed), 0.35 in the sensitivity-only world (0.75 at the three MVA Primaries and -0.06 at the three MW Primaries), so the sensitivity-only world is unreadable and its contrasts are dropped (the 0.35 gain is also too small for the combined world's gain to say anything about sensitivity: the steps alone gain 2.71).
  • Combined world (2 seeds), recovery of the oracle gain. A10 96.5%, joint hybrid 99.9%, staged hybrid 85.0%, D5 28.6%. At the three MVA Primaries D5 recovered -10.6% and at the three MW Primaries 53.6%. CRPS minus D5: A10 -1.87, joint hybrid -1.96, staged hybrid -1.55.
  • Steps-only world (1 fold, 1 seed). D5 recovered 78.6% and A10 113.9%. The offset does take steps, but the embedding does too, so the prediction that the embedding recovers at most 40% fails in this one run.
  • Untouched Primaries (combined world). CRPS of the ten untouched Primaries (including D15 and D18): base 5.61; A10 5.70, D5 5.59, joint hybrid 5.61, staged hybrid 5.46. Differences are within the seed spread; the neighbour-leak prediction was not tested against a minimum detectable effect, which was not computed.
  • Predictions. S0 failed (step 0). W-level fails (A10 recovered more than 60% of the steps in one run). W-behaviour could not be tested (unreadable world). W-both: the joint hybrid recovered over 60%, but the selected construction does not beat the joint hybrid. W-compete fails: the joint hybrid did not recover less than the better single component. W0 and the real-data check were not run.
  • Stop rule. No hybrid construction beat the joint hybrid's recovery in the combined world, so the real-data check was skipped. The film and orthogonal hybrids were fitted in the first combined world only (unreadable), where no ranking is possible.

docs.title: What was not done
docs.text:
• The 2026-06 fold, the clean control W0, the evening-bump world, and the oracle-based seed-spread minimum detectable effect were not run: the first worlds consumed most of the budget (about 2.5 GPU-hours of the 4 GPU-hours ceiling) before larger amplitudes were requested.
  • Component-level recoveries (offset path against the injected path, implied sensitivity against the injected sensitivity) were planned as read-outs and not computed, so the selection rule was not applied; the CRPS recovery is the only recovery reported.
  • Caveats: one fold and two seeds (one seed for the single-component worlds) give no intervals; the free-encoder base and oracle are compared with frozen-encoder arms, which can lower the frozen arms' recovery; the oracle sees the realised temperature, which forecast-driven arms do not. NGED generator series are not plotted.

docs.title: Lessons and next step
docs.text: No amplitude between the unreadable and the tripled worlds was tried. Options for a next experiment are a sensitivity-only world with amplitudes that make it readable on several folds, and the film and orthogonal hybrids in a readable world.

docs.title: Plan as written before any fit
docs.text: Experiment 565 found that adding the drift embedding to the output offset removed the offset's gain. This experiment asks whether that failure came from the two components competing for the same slow variance, by (1) building worlds with a known injected answer, (2) building the hybrid four ways, and (3) checking the best construction on the real data.

docs.title: Step 0 result (CPU and one GPU pass over experiment 565's stored hybrid fits)
docs.text: The prediction S0 failed: the embedding and the offset do not compete through correlated level paths. Over the five fold months and seeds 0 and 1 (fits of day 14), the mean per-Primary correlation between the embedding's level path and the offset's level path is 0.09 at the eight MVA Primaries, 0.04 at the six MW Primaries, and 0.04 at D15 and D18 over all months, and 0.21, 0.15, and 0.67 over the last 12 months. The embedding carries 93% to 99% of the slow variance (embedding path variance 0.15 to 0.56 in standardised units squared, offset 0.006 to 0.007). So the joint hybrid is dominated by the embedding. Low correlation with a dominant embedding is a winner-take-all form of competition, so step 0 neither supports nor refutes the hypothesis. As the brief states, the correlation criterion failed, so the staged and orthogonal constructions are less certain to help.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Worlds (real ERA5 weather and real Primary series; injection into the cleaned power over capacity, so training, pre-training, and scoring actuals all carry it). Injected Primaries: 6 (3 MW, 3 MVA) with the fewest labelled events, not D8 or D14. Wa: 3 abrupt steps per Primary (3% to 6% of effective capacity, random sign, at least 60 days apart, one in the 15 months before a fold's start and one 20 to 40 days before it, none in a scored month); Wa-in has one step inside the scored month (report-only). Wb1: extra load of s(t) times the heating degrees below 15 degrees Celsius, s rising linearly from 0 (2023-01) to 0.4% of capacity per degree (2025-06), then constant. Wb2 (reference arms only): an evening bump, 17:00 to 21:00 local, amplitude rising from 0 to 3% of capacity. Wc: Wa and Wb1 together. W0: no injection. Folds: 2025-12 and 2026-06 for the synthetic worlds, all five for the real data.
  • Arms on the lag-free base: D5, A10, H-joint (565's hybrid), H-staged (offset fitted first and frozen, then the embedding and mixer fitted), H-film (the embedding is a per-channel scale of 1 plus delta on the weather encoder's output, dimension 3, strong L2 shrinkage, no additive path, offset fitted jointly), H-orth (H-film plus a penalty that makes the embedding's mean effect on the mixture location zero within every Primary and month, and a penalty on the squared covariance of the two level paths; covariance rather than correlation because the first penalty drives the embedding's level path towards zero, where a correlation is unstable). H-staged-S (the abrupt-step offsets of addendum 24) is not run: its known-answer test has not yet been run.
  • Oracle: the base network given the true injected component, standardised by the Primary's target standard deviation, as one extra input to the mixer in pre-training and fine-tuning.
  • Recovery = (CRPS of the base without drift minus the arm's) / (the base's minus the oracle's) on the injected Primaries at 24-120 h, per fold. Seeds: 2 for Wc and the real data, 1 for Wa, Wb1, W0.
  • Timing asserts (row by row, one printed example per arm): the weather comes from the ensemble run at or before the origin minus 9 h (the harness assertions of experiments 510 and 565); the base has no lag column; the injected truth enters only the target and, in the oracle only, the oracle input.
  • Standing practices followed: cleaned data everywhere, D15/D18 cut, saved fitted models, stored predictions reused (565's D5, A10, and H on the real data), coarse refits (days 0 and 14). Departed from: none. Earlier advice followed: carry slow change as an offset (565); the A10 embedding added to D5 lost the gain (565), which this experiment tests rather than repeats.

docs.title: Choices fixed after the plan review, before any fit
docs.text:
• Component recoveries in Wc (needed by the selection rule; planned and never computed) are read-outs, not CRPS: step recovery is the R-squared of the arm's total monthly level path (offset plus the embedding's level path) against the injected step path over the 24 months before the fold; sensitivity recovery is the R-squared of the implied sensitivity (slope of the mixture- location change against heating degrees, newest embedding knot against the 2023-01 knot) against s(t). The oracle-based CRPS recovery is the pooled measure, reported beside them.
  • Oracle ceiling: in Wb1 and Wc the oracle is given the realised-temperature component, which no forecast-driven arm sees, so 100% recovery is not reachable and the W-both threshold is read with that in mind.
  • Frozen versus free encoders: the base (M0w) and oracle fine-tune free encoders; D5, A10 and the hybrids freeze them, as in experiment 565. Recovery is measured against the free base, so a frozen arm can show lower recovery partly because of the freezing.
  • H-film is not strictly level-free: the scale change of a GELU output can move the mixture location. Its level path is reported as a read-out; only H-orth penalises it. H-orth's penalty is measured on 64 fixed probe rows per Primary pooled over months, not per month, and in fine-tuning acts on the one trainable knot, so it is weak there.
  • Staged hybrid: the encoders copied from D5 stay trainable in staged pre-training while the offset knots are frozen.
  • Seeds and intervals: Wa-in and Wb2 use 1 seed; synthetic results use 2 folds, so they are reported as per-fold values with the minimum detectable effect from the W0 seed spread, not as intervals. W0 is reported as CRPS differences only. The offset has monthly knots, so step dates are resolved to a month, not 3 days.
  • Timing asserts are the harness asserts of experiment 565 (summary file of the run exists at or before the origin minus the publication delay; nwp_init_time <= power_fcst_init_time on every test row). No slow summary input exists, so the end-time assert has nothing to check.

docs.title: Cost and stop rules
docs.text: Ceiling 4 GPU-hours (unmeasured guess in the brief: oracles 0.4, synthetic cells 2.2, real-data check 1.2). The first cell's cost is measured and the total projected; the manager is told before 4 GPU-h is exceeded. If no hybrid beats H-joint's minimum recovery in Wc, the real-data check is skipped.

docs.title: Do power lags still help the modular demand network once a slow per-Primary output offset (D5) exists, and does the offset make lags unnecessary at 24 to 240 hours?
docs.text:
We asked whether a slow offset added to the demand forecast makes power lags unnecessary. The forecast comes from a neural network for demand at 16 primary substations (Primaries). Lags are the half-hourly power readings from the previous day and week. The offset is one number per Primary and month, added to the forecast's mean. We fitted the network with the offset and no lags (arm E2), with lags and no offset (arm v3), and with both (arm v3+D5) on five test months, one per fold. Error is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of capacity, where lower is better, for forecasts 24 to 120 hours ahead unless a band is named. At the eight Primaries that report only apparent power (the eight MVA Primaries), E2 was behind v3+D5 by 0.224 points (interval excludes zero) and behind v3 by 0.131 points (interval includes zero). At the six Primaries that report signed power (the six MW Primaries), E2 and v3 were not distinguishable (+0.005). All numbers are interim and unaudited, because no audit has run.

Verdict: partly supported. The data support lags and the offset together at the eight MVA Primaries. They do not show that either replaces the other at the six MW Primaries. The brief's stop rule needs a gain of at least 0.10 at both groups, and v3+D5 beat E2 by 0.224 at the eight and 0.049 at the six, so the rule is not met. Whether Part 2 also runs on v3+D5 is the maintainer's decision.

Arm labels: M0 has no offset and no lags; E2 has the offset learnt in pre-training and no lags; E2-ft has the offset learnt in fine-tuning only; v3 has lags at least 24 hours old and no offset; v3+D5 has both; v3-3.5 has lags at least 3.5 hours old. D5 is the name of the offset in experiment 565.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Reused from experiment 565: M0 (no offset, no lags) is its C-M0 and E2 is its D5, both coarse refits on days 0 and 14 of each fold (five folds, seeds 0 and 1). Step 0: D5 learnt its monthly knots in pre-training (from 2019-09, slope penalty of weight 10, added to the three mixture means) and fine-tuning trained only the newest knot, so E2 is exactly D5.
  • New fits (code ml-experiments/00572-*/, copying experiments 560 and 565): E2-ft (every knot learnt in fine-tuning only), v3 (experiment 560's v3 weights, refitted coarse), v3+D5 (v3 plus the offset, pre-trained here with lags and block dropout), and v3-3.5 (lags at least 3.5 h old, report only). E2-ft and v3+D5 freeze the weather and datetime encoders as D5 does; v3 and v3-3.5 do not, as in experiment 560.
  • Timing asserts (printed in the fit logs): weather from the run issued at the origin minus 9 h (every test origin), every lag at least the cap before the origin (lag_indices asserts all rows; the printed example check samples 200,000 rows), and the 24 h cap matches experiment 560's columns exactly. Example: origin 2025-10-01 09:00, target 2025-10-03 07:00, weather run 2025-10-01 00:00, day lag at 2025-09-30 07:00.
  • Code review: one fresh Sonnet review before the first fit. Review findings applied: the stress-run guard, and the unaged missing-lag code in the aged variants. Not changed: the example check samples rows, and a crash between writing a forecast and its twins fails loudly in assemble.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS (mean single-seed), points of capacity:

Group, band M0 E2 E2-ft v3 v3+D5 v3-3.5 Eight, 0-24 h 4.484 4.377 4.378 4.190 4.105 4.120 Eight, 24-120 h 4.762 4.651 4.646 4.520 4.427 4.489 Eight, 120-240 h 5.300 5.164 5.145 5.134 5.007 5.102 Six, 0-24 h 3.294 3.121 3.183 3.017 3.007 2.962 Six, 24-120 h 3.604 3.376 3.448 3.371 3.327 3.337 Six, 120-240 h 3.953 3.705 3.760 3.823 3.741 3.806

Counted contrasts at 24-120 h (first arm minus second, Bonferroni 24 tests, 5-block month bootstrap near the minimum to maximum of the folds; positive means the first arm is worse; minimum detectable effect, MDE, beside each; folds in which the first arm is worse):

  • E2 minus M0: eight -0.111 (-0.195 to +0.017, MDE 0.125, 1 of 5), six -0.228 (-0.549 to +0.058, MDE 0.189, 1 of 5).
  • E2 minus v3: eight +0.131 (-0.127 to +0.336, MDE 0.123, 3 of 5), six +0.005 (-0.091 to +0.243, MDE 0.202, 1 of 5).
  • E2 minus v3+D5: eight +0.224 (+0.006 to +0.394, MDE 0.077, 4 of 5), six +0.049 (-0.139 to +0.128, MDE 0.182, 4 of 5).
  • v3+D5 minus v3: eight -0.093 (-0.153 to -0.041, MDE 0.127, 0 of 5), six -0.044 (-0.191 to +0.166, MDE 0.088, 2 of 5).
  • Other bands: at 0-24 h, E2 minus v3 is +0.187 at the eight (-0.094 to +0.400) and +0.104 at the six; at 120-240 h it is +0.030 and -0.117, and E2 minus v3+D5 is +0.157 (-0.044 to +0.438) and -0.036. Leave-D8-out leaves every 24-120 h sign unchanged (E2 minus v3+D5 +0.289 at the eight).
  • Descriptive, uncorrected: v3-3.5 minus E2 at 0-24 h is -0.257 at the eight and -0.159 at the six; v3-3.5 minus v3 is -0.070 and -0.055 (0 of 5 folds worse). E2 minus E2-ft at 24-120 h is +0.006 at the eight and -0.072 at the six (negative means E2 is better).

Predictions.

  • P1 fails at the eight, holds at the six: E2 is behind v3 by 0.131 at the eight (fails at 0.10), and level at the six (+0.005).
  • P2 holds: v3-3.5 beats E2 by 0.257 and 0.159 at 0-24 h, but v3-3.5 beats v3 by only 0.070 and 0.055, so most of the gain over E2 comes from lags at least 24 h old.
  • P3 fails at the eight (the criterion names v3 and is read here as covering v3+D5 too): E2 is behind v3+D5 by 0.157 at 120-240 h (fails at 0.05), and behind v3 by 0.030; at the six, E2 is ahead of both.
  • P4 is not supported as worded: v3+D5 beats v3 by 0.093 at the eight (interval excludes zero) and 0.044 at the six (interval includes zero). Both gains are below the MDE of 0.127 and 0.088, so the "at least the MDE" clause is not met, and both are above 0.03, so the "fails if within 0.03" clause is not met either. The interval comes from the month blocks and the MDE from the seed spread, so a gain can be below the MDE with an interval that excludes zero.
  • P5 holds at the six only: E2 beats E2-ft by 0.072 at the six and is 0.006 worse at the eight; E2-ft's knots start at zero and see only the ensemble history.
  • P6 not measured: the real-event absorbed-share harness was not run for the new arms.

Slices at 24-120 h, E2 minus v3+D5, positive means E2 is worse. Cold winter nights: +0.260 at the eight (MDE 0.106) and -0.129 at the six; Christmas week (a single block, so no interval): +0.436 (MDE 0.432) and -0.488; D8 alone -0.230; D14 alone +0.209 at the six; rows with no labelled event +0.259 and +0.049. D15 and D18 are in the report-only tables in the private scores folder.

docs.title: Leak and lag removal
docs.text:
• Injected 7-day shift (seed 0, coarse window of the day-14 fit, points of capacity, mean of five folds with range): M0 9.76 (1.89 to 25.56), E2 9.03 (4.05 to 22.23), E2-ft 10.48, v3 7.28 (4.65 to 12.41), v3+D5 7.29 (3.96 to 10.27), v3-3.5 6.33 (4.12 to 10.82). Lower is better. The ranges overlap, so the data do not show that one arm leaks less than another. The real-event absorbed share (the primary leak measure) was not run for E2-ft, v3+D5, or v3-3.5.
  • Lags removed or aged (24-120 h, eight): v3 4.520 normal, 4.767 removed (back to M0's 4.762), 4.552 aged one day, 4.631 aged three days. v3+D5 4.427, 4.647 removed, and 4.526 aged three days. v3-3.5 4.489, 4.788 removed, and 4.606 aged three days. Aged by one day, v3 scores 4.552, v3+D5 4.457, and v3-3.5 4.527, so one day of ageing loses little of the gain; removing the lags loses all of it.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site was not computed.
  • Audit triggers: trigger 2 (P1 and P3 fail) was answered by the leave-D8-out and per-fold checks above, which leave signs unchanged; the quantile-score and mean-error contrast comparison was not run, so trigger 3 is unchecked; no nested arm lost to its parent at 24-120 h at the eight. No audit was run.
  • Coarse v3 here scores 4.520 at the eight, against 4.315 for experiment 560's daily refits; the two harnesses differ, and only coarse arms are compared on this page.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Part 2 could build its two offsets on v3+D5 as well as on E2, because the offset and the lags carry different information at the eight MVA Primaries. Whether to do so is the maintainer's decision.

docs.title: Can a piecewise-constant output offset (daily knots with a total-variation penalty, or sparse jumps) recover abrupt steps in a Primary's level, where D5's monthly knots smear them?
docs.text:
Terms: CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score; GPU is graphics processing unit; MVA and MW Primaries are the eight substations that report apparent power only and the six that report signed power; D5 is experiment 565's output-offset design; M0 is the plain modular neural network; S0 to S3 and K-S1 to K-S3 are defined below.

We ask whether a model of a substation's slow level can see an abrupt step. Experiment 565's D5 adds one number per Primary and month to the forecast's mean. A sudden change of a few percent of capacity therefore appears as a slope over several months, and a short event does not appear. This experiment tests two offsets that can change abruptly, on worlds where the answer is known: we add steps of known date and size to real Primary series, refit the offset alone on top of a frozen network, and check whether each offset finds the steps. Only if that check passes do we fit the network and the offset together on the real series.

Verdict: not supported. Take-home: at the penalties tested, a free jumpy offset did not find steps of 2% to 6% of capacity; the weights that stop apparent false steps also stop real ones. Step 1 failed, so the stop rule applied and no real-data arm was run. The sections below are the plan, followed by the results.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms use experiment 565's D5 base neural network, which is experiment 559's frontier arm and is lag-free. D5 adds a knot value per Primary to the three mixture component means, in standardised units (the Primary's target standard deviation).

  • S0 (reference): D5 as built in experiment 565, monthly knots, linear interpolation, squared first-difference penalty.
  • S1 (daily knots, total variation): one knot per Primary and day, held constant between knots (zero-order hold, so a step is not spread over a day), with an L1 penalty on the first differences of the knots. The penalty weight is swept over 3 values on the training days of the first fold of the worlds, and all three are reported.
  • S2 (sparse jumps): the offset is the sum over every day k of a gate g_k, an amplitude a_k, and a step at that day, with hard-concrete gates (Louizos et al. (2018)) and a penalty on the expected number of open gates, swept over 3 values. If gradient fitting is unstable, S2 starts from S1's thresholded jumps, and the page says so.
  • S3 (no-labelled-event fit): the better of S1 and S2 in Step 1, with the rows inside labelled events removed from the loss. S3 is an offset for the normal-running forecast and is not a detection source, because it never sees the events.

docs.title: Step 1: known-answer worlds
docs.text:
Worlds. Real weather, real Primary series, six injected Primaries (three MW, three MVA) with the fewest labelled events, and the other ten untouched. The step is added to the cleaned power over capacity at the one place every reader of the target calls (experiment 422's cleaned_arrays), the MVA series are clipped at zero afterwards, and the truth is saved per Primary and half-hour.

  • Ks (steps): 1 to 3 abrupt steps per injected Primary and year between 2022 and 2026, of 2% to 6% of capacity with a random sign, at least 30 days apart, about half reverting after 5 to 60 days and half persistent.
  • Kr (ramp): a ramp of 3% of capacity over 12 months, with no step.
  • K0 (clean): no injection.
  • Kt (transfer pairs, from experiment 402's inject()): deferred to Step D, which the brief runs only after S1 or S2 passes Step 1.

Cheap path. The network is frozen at experiment 554's pretrained M0 weights. For each fold the network's nine mixture outputs on the fold's ERA5 and CAMS pre-training rows are computed once, and each arm fits only its offset on top of those outputs by minimising the mixture negative log-likelihood of the injected targets. Step 2's arms fit the network and offset together, so Step 1 tests the offset's recovery and not the joint fit.

Scoring a recovered step. A recovered offset path is turned into steps by thresholding its first differences at 1% of capacity (merging adjacent days). A truth step is recovered when a recovered step of the same sign lies within 3 days of it and its size is within 25% of the truth. A recovered step with no truth step is a false step. Recall is the share of truth steps recovered and precision the share of recovered steps that are true; both are reported with n and the binomial half-width. An offset in the standardised unit is converted to capacity fractions through the Primary's target standard deviation.

Seeds and folds. One seed; the five folds of 511, each fold's training span being its pre-training rows. The injected series are the same for all five folds, so the folds differ only in the training span and the fold's frozen weights.

docs.title: Step 2: real data (only if Step 1 passes)
docs.text: Described in the brief and run only if K-S1 and K-S2 pass: CRPS at 24-120 h of S0, S1, S2, and S3 against M0, the part C slices, the absorbed share on the 74 real events, the error in the 30 days after the last jump, the jump count per Primary-year, the share of the 9 long labelled events that appear as a step on and a step off, and offset plots per Primary. Step D (the offset as a load-shift detector) runs only if S1 or S2 passes Step 1. Seeds: 2; coarse refits (one fit per fold). Cost is measured on the first pre-training and projected before the rest runs.

docs.title: Scoring protocol for Step 1 (fixed before any score is quoted)
docs.text:
• Offset fits. Each offset is fitted with Adam on a fixed random 25% of a fold's pre-training rows (about 1.8 million of 7 million; the weights below are per this subsample), 1,000 steps, rate 0.02 decaying to 0.002. S0 uses experiment 565's weight of 10 on the mean squared first difference of the monthly knots. S1's total-variation weight is swept over 300, 1000, and 3000 nats per standardised unit, and S2's gate weight over 30, 100, and 300 nats per expected open gate, on the first fold (2025-10) of worlds Ks and K0. One weight per arm is then fixed: the one with the highest F1 (the harmonic mean of recall and precision) in world Ks among those with at most 1 false step of 1% or more per Primary-year in world K0.
  • Extracting steps. A day's change of the offset counts toward a step when it is at least 0.1% of capacity; same-direction days up to 2 days apart merge; a merged run of total size 1% of capacity or more is a step, dated at the day where half of its change has happened.
  • Recall and precision. Truth steps in the last 10 days of a fold's span are not scored. K-S1 uses the truth steps of size 3% or more, pooled over the six injected Primaries, per fold; S1 or S2 passes when at least 4 of the 5 folds have recall 0.80 or more. Precision is the share of extracted steps that match a truth step.
  • K-S2. Extracted steps of 1% or more in world K0, counted on the six Primaries that world Ks injects, divided by the six Primaries times the years of the fold's span; passing means 1 or fewer per Primary-year on at least 4 of 5 folds. These steps include real, unlabelled level changes of the real series, so the count is an upper bound on false steps. The count on the ten untouched Primaries is reported beside it.
  • K-S3. For each injected Primary whose ramp ends at least 30 days before the span ends, the recovered rise from 30 days before the ramp starts to 30 days after it ends is within 25% of the truth, and the ramp window holds at least 5 steps of 0.3% of capacity or more (days of change of 0.05% or more). S1 or S2 passes when at least two thirds of the (Primary, fold) pairs pass.
  • Which arm. S1 and S2 are each scored on K-S1 to K-S3; "S1 or S2" means at least one of them passes all three. S0 is scored the same way for reference.

docs.title: Predictions that could fail (written before any score)
docs.text:
• K-S1 to K-S3 pass for S1 or S2, and S0 recovers under 40% of the steps. Fails if S0 recovers 60% or more, or if neither S1 nor S2 reaches 60%.
  • S2 has at least 0.1 higher precision than S1 at a recall within 0.1. Fails if within 0.05.
  • On real data, S1 or S2 beats S0 by at least 0.03 on all rows at one group, or the 30-day post-jump error is at least 0.05 lower. Fails if both are within 0.02.
  • At least half of the 9 long labelled events appear as an on-and-off step pair at the labelled Primary under S1. Fails if under 30%.
  • S3's absorbed share on the 74 real events is at most half of S1's. Fails if inside-event gain is within 0.05.
  • S1 or S2 finds between 1 and 12 jumps of 2% or more per Primary-year. Fails if over 30 or under 0.5.

docs.title: Timing and cost
docs.text: The weather of every row comes from the ensemble run issued at or before the origin minus 9 h, as in experiment 565 (its row-by-row assertions are inherited); no lag column exists; the end time of every offset used at an origin is the refit cut. Ceiling about 2 GPU-hours, one GPU process under 8 GB. Step 1 is offset-only and costs minutes.

docs.title: Plan review and standing practices
docs.text: Standing practices followed: cleaned data everywhere; the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 where real series are scored; July 2026 unused; monthly or coarser refits; models saved in the private data folder. Departures: none in Step 1. Earlier advice items followed: carry slow Primary-level change as a per-Primary output offset (experiment 565), and state the minimum detectable effect beside every contrast.

docs.title: Departures found in the code review (recorded before the scored run)
docs.text:
• S2 starts from S1. Gates started closed never opened, so S2 starts with a gate open at every day where S1's offset changes by 0.1% of capacity or more, and the gate penalty then closes the gates it does not need. A precision gain of S2 over S1 tests thresholding of S1, not independent sparse recovery.
  • Truth steps need data. A truth step is scored only when the Primary has at least 100 cached rows in each of the 5 days either side (a quarter of a typical 400), because some Primaries have no rows before 2023 or 2024.
  • Per-Primary years. K-S2's years run from each Primary's first cached day.
  • Unlabelled real drift. The real series moves on its own, so the offset path holds real level changes as well as the injection. K-S3 therefore also reports the rise in world K0 beside the rise in world Kr, and a paired path (world Ks minus world K0) is reported as a descriptive diagnostic.

docs.title: Results (Step 1, five folds, one seed)
docs.text:
Recall is the share of injected steps of 3% of capacity or more that an arm recovers (date within 3 days, size within 25%), pooled over the six injected Primaries; n is 39 to 43 steps per fold, so one step is about 2.5 points of recall. False steps are extracted steps of 1% of capacity or more per Primary-year in the clean world K0, on the six Primaries that world Ks injects (real unlabelled level changes count as false, so this is an upper bound).

Arm Recall per fold Precision per fold False steps per Primary-year (clean world) Ramp pass share per fold S0, monthly knots 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 0 0.00 to 0.06 0 S1, weight 3000 3%, 3%, 0%, 3%, 2% 3% to 8% 0.31 to 0.41 0 S1, weight 1000 21%, 18%, 15%, 17%, 14% 5% to 8% 2.47 to 2.76 0.17 to 0.33 S2, from S1 at 3000, gate 300 8%, 15%, 5%, 5%, 2% 1% to 6% 2.31 to 2.97 0 to 0.17 S2, from S1 at 1000, gate 30 23%, 13%, 2%, 7%, 16% 1% to 4% 6.83 to 8.55 0 to 0.17
  • K-S1 fails for every arm: no arm reaches 80% recall on any fold. The best fold is 23% (S2 from S1 at 1000, gate 30), with 7.8 apparent false steps per Primary-year; S1 at 1000 reaches 21%.
  • K-S2 holds only for S0 and S1 at weight 3000 (at most 1 false step per Primary-year), and those two recover at most 3% of the steps. No arm passes K-S1 and K-S2 together.
  • K-S3 fails for every arm: the best ramp pass share is 0.33 (S1 at 1000, first two folds), against the required two thirds.
  • The prediction that S0 recovers under 40% holds (it recovers none), but the prediction that S1 or S2 reaches 60% fails, so the experiment stops by its own rule. The prediction that S2 has higher precision than S1 fails: no S2 row is more than 0.02 above the S1 row of the same start weight.
  • Penalty sweep (first fold, worlds Ks and K0): S1 weights 300, 1000, and 3000 give recall 46%, 21%, and 3% with 11.8, 2.5, and 0.41 false steps per Primary-year. The weight that satisfies the false-step limit of the selection rule is 3000, so 3000 is the selected weight; 1000 is shown as the sensitivity.
  • Untouched Primaries. The ten Primaries with no injection show 0.26 to 0.43 (S1, 3000) and 2.88 to 3.23 (S1, 1000) apparent false steps per Primary-year, close to the six injected ones, so the false steps are a property of the real series and not of the injection.
  • Why (a hypothesis, untested): the clean world's steps may be the real series' own unlabelled level changes, or the weather model's error. In an unscored first look at three Primaries, the recovered path correlated 0.3 to 0.7 with the injected path and varied more than it did. The paired path (world Ks minus world K0) that would separate the causes was not computed.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One seed, one frozen neural network (experiment 554's M0, seed 0), and a 25% row subsample, so the numbers carry no interval; they are known-answer checks of recovery, not significance tests.
  • The fits ran on the neural network's outputs with the network frozen; a joint fit might behave differently, which Step 2 would have tested.
  • S2 starts from S1's jumps, so a precision gain of S2 over S1 tests thresholding of S1.
  • Steps called false are apparent: the clean world's real, unlabelled level changes count against precision, so precision is a lower bound and false-step rates are upper bounds.
  • The first-fold sweep numbers are in the sweep output files in the private data folder, not in the printed report.
  • Step 2, Step D, and world Kt were not run. Weather in these rows is the ERA5 and CAMS analysis of the target time, as in experiment 565's pre-training; no ensemble forecast is involved.
  • Every number is interim and unaudited. GPU time used: about 0.3 GPU-hours.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The median-minus-mean forecast and the quantile-score contrasts do not apply: no forecast was scored.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. A control (S0 on the clean world) behaved as expected; no result contradicted its prediction except the predicted success of S1 or S2, which is the recorded result.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a second signal (a neighbour Primary's offset, or the labelled events) lets a jumpy offset separate a step from drift, for example by testing the paired path of world Ks minus world K0 first.

docs.title: Which add-ons (multi-variable ensemble spread, thermal-lag and solar-gain columns, an expected signal from the ERA5/CAMS encoders, a three-step schedule) improve the modular lag-encoder neural network with the D5 output offset, and what does the combined final candidate score?
docs.text:
We asked which add-ons improve the modular demand neural network that combines power lags and a slow output offset. The neural network forecasts demand at 16 primary substations (Primaries). Its base recipe, P0, is experiment 572's v3+D5: a lag encoder for the previous day's and week's power, plus one offset per Primary and month, fine-tuned daily. We tested four add-ons against P0 on five test months: the multi-variable ensemble spread in the mixer (P1), thermal-lag and solar-gain columns through the weather encoder (P2), unfrozen encoders in fine-tuning (P3-E0), and a three-step schedule (P4, and P4-E with a 3-day embargo). We then combined the survivors (P5). Error is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of capacity, where lower is better. The three-step schedule with the embargo, combined with the thermal-lag columns, is the only recipe we tested that helped: P5 is 0.090 below P0 at 24 to 120 hours at the eight Primaries that report apparent power (the eight MVA Primaries, interval includes zero) and 0.215 below at the six Primaries that report signed power (the six MW Primaries, interval excludes zero). P5 beats E2 (offset, no lags) and the daily-refit A-pool-24 by about 0.3 at both groups, and follows an injected 7-day shift of the history 2.9 points against P0's 7.3. All numbers are interim and unaudited, because no audit has run.

Verdict: partly supported. Of the four add-ons, one improves the forecast (P4-E), one leaves error unchanged at the eight MVA Primaries and lowers the leak (P2), and two make the forecast worse (P1 and P3-E0). P5 meets every pre-registered P5 prediction except the leave-one-out removals, which were not run; its absorbed-share fall against P0 is a point estimate (interval includes zero). The numbers do not show that P5 beats P0 at the eight MVA Primaries by the minimum detectable effect.

Arm labels: P0 is experiment 572's v3+D5. E2 is experiment 565's D5 (offset, no lags). P1 adds the 7 spread columns of experiment 568's T4 to the fine-tuning mixer. P2 passes the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns (B1) of experiment 569 through the weather encoder; P2-plac is the same with the days shuffled. P3-E0 unfreezes the weather and datetime encoders in fine-tuning. P4 fits a fresh mixer on the whole ensemble history before the daily fine-tune; P4-E adds the 3-day embargo of experiment 556. P5 is P4-E plus B1. P6 is P5 plus three trailing-temperature columns (6, 24, and 72 h) from experiment 515. P7 is P0 with lags at least 3.5 h old. A-pool-24 is experiment 558's network with a 24-hour lag cap, and L-1d is experiment 511's network refitted daily; both references are refitted daily.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• P3 as planned was identical to P0. The plan gave the lag encoder's expected embeddings from a frozen copy of the encoders trained on ERA5 and CAMS alone (E1). P0 already uses exactly those encoders, frozen, so P3 and P0 have identical weights. The contrast that tests a different question is P3-E0 (encoders unfrozen), which replaces P3 in the counted family. The Bonferroni count stays 42.
  • Reused from earlier experiments: P0 and its pre-training are experiment 572's V3D5 and pretrained_V3D5; E2 is experiment 565's D5; the fine-tune is experiment 559's one-step schedule (frozen encoders, fresh mixer seed 12345, 90-day half-life, early stopping). The folds are 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06, refitted at days 0 and 14 of each fold, with seeds 0 and 1. The stress run injects a 7-day shift at day 14 (seed 0).
  • B1 at lag times. The thermal-lag and solar-gain columns enter the weather encoder at the target time. At a lag's own time the lag encoder's expected embeddings read 0 in the B1 slots, because the lagged power has no matching columns.
  • Three-step schedule. Step 1 pre-trains on ERA5 and CAMS rows. Step 2 fits a fresh mixer on the whole ensemble history up to the cutoff minus 3.5 h, without recency weighting. Step 3 is the daily fine-tune from the step-2 weights, with the mixer at its ordinary learning rate. P4-E removes the 3 days before the cutoff from steps 2 and 3.
  • Timing asserts are printed in the fit logs, one example per arm and lead band. Example for the 0-24 h band: origin 2025-12-01 09:00, weather run 2025-12-01 00:00 (origin minus 9 h), target 2025-12-02 07:30, day lag at 2025-11-30 07:30 (at least 24 h before the origin).
  • Statistics. 42 counted tests (four add-one contrasts, plus P5 against P0, E2, and A-pool-24, each at 2 groups and 3 lead bands) plus a separate family of 2 (P2 against P2-plac on cold winter nights, once per group). Intervals resample the five months as five blocks. Minimum detectable effect (MDE) is printed beside every contrast.
  • Leak. The primary leak measure is the share of the labelled load-shift events' depth that the fitted forecast absorbs (experiment 556's harness). The harness scored 37 of the 74 labelled events: the others end too late for a fit at least 3 days later within 30 days. The flag at 6.0 points on the injected shift is a flag, not a gate.
  • Budget. The fits stayed below the 6 GPU-h ceiling. The leave-one-out removals, the stretch E3 arm, seeds 2 to 4, and the daily-refit harness were not run.

• The reference arms A-pool-24 and L-1d are refitted daily, while P0, P5, and P6 are refitted at days 0 and 14 of each fold. The comparison favours the references, so P5's lead over them is conservative on cadence and open on everything else.

  • The inside-event slice, scored against actuals corrected by the labels, is descriptive (see inside_events_nra.csv in the private data folder).

docs.title: Can a piecewise-constant output offset recover large, label-sized level steps and mirrored pairs of steps, where experiment 573 found it recovered steps of 2% to 6% of capacity in none of its tests?
docs.text:
Terms: S0, S1, and S2 are the monthly-knot, daily-knot, and gated-jump offsets of experiment 573. Kl, Kp, and K0 are the worlds defined below. MVA and MW Primaries are the eight substations that report apparent power only and the six that report signed power.

We ask whether the offsets that failed on small steps can find large ones. Experiment 573 added steps of 2% to 6% of capacity to real Primary series and found that no tested offset recovered more than 23% of the steps of 3% or more. A labelled load-shift is much larger, so the failure may mean only that small steps drown in weather-error noise. Here we add steps drawn from the sizes and durations of the labelled events to the same series, with the network frozen and only the offset refitted, as in experiment 573.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Sizes and durations come from the labelled events. The 184 events in experiment 400's events_corrected.parquet have depth quartiles of 11%, 19%, and 31% of the Primary's capacity, and length quartiles of 0.4, 2.1, and 3.6 days (the full printout is in the results). Only 65% last a day or more. The injected events use depth 10% to 50% of capacity (log-uniform) and duration 1 to 180 days (log-uniform), the ranges the manager's note proposed, so the test covers the long events that a daily-knot offset might reach. The labelled events themselves are mostly shorter, which the results discuss.

  • Kl (large single steps): per injected Primary, events starting between 2022-01-01 and 2026-05-31 with 30 days or more between the end of one and the start of the next (about 2 events a year), a random sign, and a reversal at the end. At the three injected MVA Primaries an event is always a gain, because a loss could clip at zero. Three random draws of the world.
  • Kp (mirrored pairs): a donor Primary changes by x and a neighbour on an edge of Primary Substation Interconnections.csv changes by -rho times x in MW (rho uniform from 0.6 to 1.0), with the same onset and end; about 30% of events have no recipient. Donors and recipients are among the same six injected Primaries, so the ten untouched Primaries stay clean. No MVA Primary loses load. Three draws.
  • K0: experiment 573's clean world. Its fitted paths are reused to count false steps of 5% or more; the ten untouched Primaries in Kl and Kp give a second count.
  • Arms: S0, S1 at total-variation weights 3000 and 1000, and S2 at gate weights 300 and 30 on each, exactly as experiment 573's full run. No new tuning.

Weather timing (standing rule). The network is experiment 554's pre-trained M0 with its outputs cached by experiment 573's e00573_cache.py, which asserts row by row that each row's origin is not after the fold's refit, the target is not after the refit minus the cutoff age, and the origin precedes the target, and prints one example row. This experiment reads that cache and changes no weather input.

Scoring. A step is the change at an event's onset. It counts as recovered when the offset has a step of the same sign within 3 days of the onset (within 1 day for steps of 20% or more) and within 25% of its size. The return step is scored separately. Only events that finish at least 10 days before the fold's span ends and have at least 100 cached rows on each side of both changes are scored. Recall is reported by size bin (10% to 20%, 20% to 35%, 35% to 50%) and duration bin (1 to 3 days, 3 to 14 days, 14 to 30 days, 30 to 180 days; the note's 3 to 14 days is split at 7 days for the first prediction). For a pair, both halves must be recovered. The detectability curve uses, per injected Primary, the standard deviation of the offset-free daily residual of the frozen network (in the clean world), and the smallest step that exceeds three standard errors after n days is three times that standard deviation over the square root of n.

Statistics. Per-fold results are shown beside the pooled results. No contrasts are counted. Intervals on recall are binomial, not month-block bootstraps, because the quantity is a count of injected steps.

Advice followed. The plan follows experiment 573's advice to use known-answer worlds before real data, and keeps its monthly knots as the slow-drift reference.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Verdict: not supported. Take-home: a free per-day offset cannot find label-sized steps, so Step D is cancelled. The first prediction fails clearly: its best arm recovers 32%, under the 50% at which it was called failed. Draws are the random worlds of Kl and Kp. The headline pool is the latest fold (refit 2026-06) with five draws of each world. The two earlier folds (2025-10 and 2026-01) have three draws and are shown as per-fold signs only, because the folds' training spans are nested and so not independent. The other two folds of experiment 573 were not run, to stay inside the compute budget. The Bonferroni count is 0.

Labelled events are shorter than the events we injected. The 184 labelled events have depth quartiles of 11%, 19%, and 31% of capacity, and length quartiles of 0.4, 2.1, and 3.6 days. Of the events, 65% last a day or more, and 1.6% last over 30 days. The injected events (1 to 180 days) therefore test mostly longer events than the labels hold.

docs.title: Recovery of steps of 20% or more that last 7 days or more (prediction 1)
docs.text:
False steps are those of 5% of capacity or more per Primary-year, on all 16 Primaries in experiment 573's clean world (K0) and on the ten untouched Primaries in Kl.

Arm Recall (latest fold, n = 53) Per fold (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-06; draws 0 to 2) False steps per Primary-year, K0 / Kl S0 0.00 (±0.00) 0, 0, 0 0.00 / 0.00 S1, weight 3000 0.00 (±0.00) 0, 0, 0 0.01 / 0.02 S1, weight 1000 0.32 (±0.13) 0.38, 0.31, 0.37 0.29 / 0.28 S2, 3000 / gate 300 0.00 (±0.00) 0, 0, 0 0.24 / 0.17 S2, 3000 / gate 30 0.00 (±0.00) 0, 0, 0 0.25 / 0.19 S2, 1000 / gate 300 0.08 (±0.07) 0.07, 0.03, 0.10 0.78 / 0.60 S2, 1000 / gate 30 0.08 (±0.07) 0.03, 0.07, 0.10 0.90 / 0.81

The intervals are binomial half-widths, which are also the minimum detectable effect beside each recall. Recall of the return step is about the same (S1 at weight 1000: 0.26 ±0.12).

Recall rises with event length but stays low. For steps of 20% or more, S1 at weight 1000 recovers 0% of events of 1 to 3 days (n = 22), 4% of 3 to 7 days (n = 25), 17% and 18% of the two bins from 7 to 30 days (n = 12 and 11, unresolved), and 43% of 30 to 180 days (n = 30, ±18). Recall does not rise with size: S1 at weight 1000 recovers 20%, 19%, and 14% of the three size bins (10% to 20%, 20% to 35%, and 35% to 50%).

docs.title: Level-following check (not planned)
docs.text:
The offset itself under-reaches. For events of 20% or more lasting 30 days or more (n = 30, latest fold), the table gives the offset's change over the event as a share of the injected step.

Arm Median share of the injected step Share within 25% of the step S0 0.02 0.00 S1, weight 3000 0.09 0.00 S1, weight 1000 0.49 0.27 S2, 3000 / gate 300 0.14 0.03 S2, 1000 / gate 30 0.43 0.17

The step extractor therefore did not miss a step that the offset held. In most of these events the offset never moved to the injected level.

docs.title: Other predictions
docs.text:
• Recall for 1-day steps is at most 30% at every size below 50% (holds, unresolved). Every arm recovered none of the 15, 10, and 2 steps in the three size bins, but each bin holds fewer than 20 steps.
  • Recall falls with duration, matching the detectability curve (fails). The curve gives the smallest step above three standard errors as 22% of capacity at 1 day, 8% at 7 days, and 4% at 30 days (from the median daily residual spread of 7.2% of capacity). A step of 20% or more lasting 7 days exceeds the curve by a wide margin, yet the best arm recovers 17% of such steps. The curve assumes independent daily residuals, which weather errors are not, so it is optimistic.
  • Both halves of a pair recovered in at least 70% of pairs (fails, unresolved). The best arm (S1 at weight 1000) recovers both halves of 17% of 12 pairs with a donor step of 20% or more lasting 7 days or more; the pair counts are too small to resolve.
  • S0 recovers under 20% of steps lasting under 30 days (holds). It recovers 0 of 125.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Step D is cancelled by the decision rule. If load-shifts are to be found from the forecast, the step needs to enter the model as an explicit input or state (a labelled-event flag, or a level state estimated with a filter), and the test is whether that improves the forecast on the rows near events. Penalty weights below 1000 were not tested here because the experiment kept experiment 573's grid unchanged; experiment 573 saw many false steps at weight 300.

docs.title: Why do lags beat the lag-free output offset at the eight MVA Primaries but not at the six MW Primaries: sunny half-hours or one Primary?
docs.text:
Lags beat the lag-free network at the eight MVA Primaries in sunny half-hours and at night, not mainly in sunny ones, and not because of D8. The maintainer's two hypotheses were that the gap sits in sunny half-hours (hypothesis a) and that D8, a Primary with a gas generator (Gas A), supplies much of it (hypothesis b). Neither hypothesis holds. The gap is as large at night and in low sun as in sunny half-hours, and D8 pulls the gap down, so leaving D8 out raises it. Three Primaries (D4, D12, and D19) hold 85% of the v3+D5 gap. Next step: find what D4, D12, and D19 have in common. All numbers are interim and unaudited. The page re-scores the stored forecasts of experiment 572 (E2, v3, v3+D5; two seeds; five folds). E2 is experiment 572's lag-free network with the output offset (experiment 565's D5), v3 is its network with lags and no offset, and v3+D5 has both. The gap is E2's CRPS minus the lag arm's, in points of capacity at 24-120 h unless a band is named, and positive means the lag arm is better.

Verdict: not supported (both hypotheses). Pa is not met. The sunny to cloudy ratio in daytime half-hours is 1.7 for v3+D5 (0.230 and 0.134, intervals overlap), under the 2 predicted and above the 1.5 that would fail the prediction. The three largest half-hour types hold more than half of the gap, as predicted, but all three are night or low-sun types, and the night gap (0.244) equals the sunny gap, which a correction of reverse flow cannot produce. Pb fails: leaving D8 out removes none of the gap and raises it.
