docs.title: Setup and checks
docs.text:
• Code: ml-experiments/00576-*/e00576_gap.py and e00576_figures.py, importing experiment 572's scoring module and experiments 448, 470, and 521's helpers. No fit ran.
  • Weather timing: every half-hour's weather comes from the run issued at origin minus 9 h; the script asserts that the run precedes the origin and that the target follows the origin, for every row, and prints one example row. The label is used only to slice the scores.
  • Limits: solar elevation uses one point for every Primary, not each Primary's own latitude. The ensemble-mean shortwave is smoother than the weather a Primary saw, so some half-hours labelled cloudy had sun.

docs.title: Do offsets that stay constant between sparse steps, and offsets whose uncertainty widens the forecast, improve the output-side slow offset (D5) of the modular lag-free demand neural network?
docs.text:
We asked two questions about the slow offset (D5) that the modular lag-free demand neural network adds to the forecast's mean: does an offset that stays constant between sparse steps forecast better, and does carrying the offset's uncertainty into the forecast improve it? We tested three total-variation or gated-jump penalties (O1 to O3) and six ways to carry the uncertainty (Q1 to Q5 and a placebo), on the same 16 Primary substations (14 scored) and five test months as experiment 565, with 5 seeds for the arms that showed a point gain and 2 for the rest. Neither idea improved the forecast. A steadier offset loses no accuracy, and widening the forecast by the offset's uncertainty changes CRPS by under 0.03 points of capacity.

Verdict: refuted. Take-home: D5 is already as good as these refinements make it, so the next step is to keep D5 unchanged. Every interval below is a Bonferroni month-block interval over 28 contrasts (22 pre-registered plus 6 for Q5) with 5 blocks, which is near the minimum to maximum of the five folds. The rest of this page says "interval excludes zero" only where it does.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Absolute CRPS of D5 at 24-120 h (seeds 0 and 1). 4.651 points of capacity at the eight MVA Primaries and 3.376 at the six MW Primaries. On seeds 5 to 9, D5 is 4.646 and 3.475.
  • Steadier offsets (O1 to O3), seeds 0 and 1, CRPS minus D5 (minimum detectable effect, MDE). O1 +0.017 at the eight (MDE 0.119) and +0.021 at the six (0.120); O2 -0.042 (0.128) and +0.018 (0.229); O3 +0.118 (0.179) and -0.026 (0.149). No interval excludes zero. Penalties picked on fold 1's pretraining NLL: O1 lambda 3000, O2 3000, O3 1000.
  • O2 on fresh seeds 5 to 9. CRPS minus D5 is -0.008 at the eight (interval -0.068 to +0.082, MDE 0.102, 2 of 5 folds positive) and +0.054 at the six (-0.085 to +0.357, MDE 0.123, 2 of 5 positive). O2 narrows the 90% interval by 0.9 points of capacity (eight) and 1.6 (six), and the 80% interval covers 2.5 and 3.9 points less than D5's (interval excludes zero). Q4-O2 on the same seeds: -0.010 and +0.067.
  • Offset-uncertainty widening, seeds 0 and 1. Q1 (spread across seeds) is -0.001 and -0.002; Q-const (placebo) is -0.001 and -0.001; Q2 (variational newest knot) is +0.028 and +0.000; Q4-O2 is -0.046 and +0.015. None meets the 0.03 threshold, and no interval excludes zero.
  • Q3 (jump-risk widening) as pre-registered is worse. CRPS is +0.183 at the eight (0.128 to 0.217) and +0.152 at the six (0.085 to 0.199), the summed 1% and 99% pinball loss rises by 0.158 and 0.201, and the 90% interval is 11 points of capacity wider; all 5 folds are positive. Q3b, the same widening with statistics taken from O2's own jumps, is a post hoc variant and is neutral.
  • Q5 (slow per-Primary scale offset). CRPS minus D5 is +0.007 (MDE 0.159) and +0.014 (0.131); the shuffled-across-Primaries placebo is +0.000 and +0.033, so the learnt scale knots are not better than shuffled ones. The knots do differ across Primaries and drift over time, and agree across seeds (correlation above 0.93), see the Q5 scale-knots figure.
  • Slices (24-120 h, CRPS minus D5, O2 / Q4-O2). Leave-D8-out at the eight: -0.053 / -0.057. D8 alone: +0.032 / +0.033. D14 alone at the six: +0.002 / +0.055. Rows with no labelled event: -0.053 / -0.060 (eight), +0.018 / +0.015 (six). Cold nights (3 folds): -0.093 / -0.091 (eight) and -1.091 / -1.118 (six, interval -2.073 to +0.424, 1 of 3 folds positive). Christmas week (1 fold only): -0.430 / -0.286 (eight) and +0.349 / +0.262 (six). No slice is shown to improve.
  • The offsets are not much steadier. The share of month pairs without a labelled event whose offset moves by under 0.2% of capacity is 37% for D5, 60% for O1, 40% for O2, and 36% for O3. O1 gains 23 points, short of the 70% target.

docs.title: Known-answer check
docs.text:
The penalties were tested where the true offset is known. They were fitted on experiment 573's cached neural-network outputs with nothing added (K0) and with two persistent steps of 10% to 20% of capacity per Primary (Kl). Static-period RMSE is in percent of capacity, averaged over five folds.

Arm K0 RMSE Kl RMSE Steps recovered Mean step-size bias D5 2.89 1.33 8 of 45 -52% O1, lambda 3000 2.77 0.85 19 of 45 -19% O1, lambda 30000 0.87 7.59 10 of 45 -33% O2, lambda 3000 1.81 8.24 40 of 45 -70% O2, lambda 30000 0.47 10.58 0 of 45 n/a

The pre-registered 40% cut is not met at the picked penalty. The prediction (O1 or O2 cuts the static-period RMSE by at least 40% in K0) fails at the picked penalty (4% for O1, 37% for O2) and holds only at lambda 10000 or more, for both O1 and O2. A larger penalty cuts K0's error but recovers fewer steps and shrinks the ones it recovers.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Audit triggers fired. The trigger for a result that contradicts its pre-registered prediction fired twice: for Q3, and for the 40% known-answer prediction for O1. Both failures are explained by the known-answer table: a penalty that calms the path also shrinks steps, so no separate audit was run.
  • Preliminary penalty grid. The first grid of penalties was too weak (validation NLL 0.36 and 0.40 against D5's 0.325) and was replaced; its fits are kept in the private data folder and are not used here.
  • Not run. The absorbed-share and stress-run fits, and the raw (unwidened, factor 1.0) sensitivity: every score includes the 1.15 widening about the median that all stored arms use.
  • Event labels are incomplete, so the "no labelled event" slice may hold unlabelled events, and the static-ness shares are lower bounds on how often the offset moved for a real reason.
  • Compute. About 2.6 of the 3 GPU-hours; the extra seeds were run for O2 and Q4-O2 only.
  • Weights. Pretrained and fine-tuned weights for every arm are in models/ and pretrained_* under this experiment's private data folder; the final candidate is D5 of experiment 565.

docs.title: Does the lag network follow long, deep load-shift events, and would an inference-time gate on its lags stop it?
docs.text:
Erratum (experiment 580, 2026-11-05). Of the 23 labelled events of at least 7 days only event 55 (D16, mirrored by D5 from 2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13) is confirmed by the telemetry. The follow ratios, level shares, and coverage of the normal running arrangement for every other labelled event, including events 115, 143, 146, 28, 112, and 113, used a corrected power that the telemetry does not confirm (for events 146 and 143 it contradicts the telemetry; event 146 has the wrong sign and dates). Do not quote them. The event 55 numbers stand. See experiment 580 for the audit of the labels against the telemetry.

The forecast follows long, deep load-shift events, and the lags account for a modest share of that: 0.087 of the event's depth on average over the whole event (median 0.029), 0.163 after day 4, and 0.175 in the 7 days after the event ends, when day-old and week-old lags still contain the event and the forecast stays shifted after the snap-back. We asked whether the neural network that reads power lags follows long, deep events in NGED's log of load transfers between Primaries, and whether a gate that drops the lags during such an event would stop it. We re-forecast the v3+D5 network (lags plus a slow output offset) of experiment 572 with the lags taken from the NRA-corrected power, which has the logged load transfer added back, and compared the two forecasts at 24-120 h ahead. NRA is NGED's normal running arrangement. The after-day-4 and after-end intervals are 0.11 to 0.23 and 0.13 to 0.23 (7 long-and-deep events). Over all 12 long events in the folds, the mean after day 4 is 0.185 (0.14 to 0.23), and all 12 are positive. A descriptive gate with untuned thresholds triggered on 2 of 12 events. All numbers are interim and unaudited. Next step: decide with the maintainer whether the gate is worth tuning on injected worlds, or whether to test a control on the offset and the fine-tune instead.

Verdict: not supported. The prediction that the lag effect is at least 0.30 on obvious events fails. Obvious events among the long-and-deep ones (E-obv, defined in the plan) number 0: no long- and-deep event shows 3 consecutive days with a daily gap above 3 event-free standard deviations from the lag-free D5 expectation. One shorter event passes the rule (event 55, D16, 16% deep, not long and deep). The whole-event mean is under the 0.15 stop line and the mean after day 4 is just above it, so the stop rule is borderline. At the manager's request the gates G1 and G2 with action A2 were run as a descriptive check on stored forecasts (below); G3, A1, A3, A4, and the injected-world tuning were not. Bonferroni count: 0 of the 8 planned tests were run. All numbers are descriptive, with n = 7 long-and-deep events (12 long events in the folds), so only a large difference could be resolved.

docs.title: The forecast being examined
docs.text:
The network is the v3+D5 arm of experiment 572, in ml-experiments/00572-*/e00572_fit.py (Spec("V3D5", "24h", "lagoff", True), line 104). Line references below are to the files in ml- experiments/, in the folders of experiments 572, 560, 559, 545, 510, 428, 397, and 558.

  • Encoders. A weather encoder (7 weather columns plus an 8-dimensional Primary embedding, 64 hidden units, 32 outputs, dropout 0.1) and a datetime encoder (21 columns, the same sizes) (e00560_model.py:57-71). A lag encoder (mode v3) reads the day lag and the week lag, each as a value, a missing flag, and an age, plus 4 "expected" embeddings that pass the weather and datetime rows of the lag times through the same frozen encoders (e00560_model.py:77-124).
  • Mixer and head. A mixer of 2 hidden layers of 64 units reads the encoder outputs and the Primary embedding (fine-tuning adds 7 weather spread columns and 2 lead columns) (e00560_model.py:93-157). The head is a 3-component Gaussian mixture, trained on its negative log-likelihood, and read out at 11 quantile levels from 0.01 to 0.99 (e00397_models.py:19-91).
  • D5 offset. One monthly knot per Primary from 2019-09 to the fold month, interpolated linearly by the target's valid time, added to the 3 component means (e00572_model.py:52-66, e00559_extra.py:363-388). All knots are learnt in pre-training. In fine-tuning only the newest knot is trained and the older knots are fixed (e00572_model.py:35-39,69-81). A smoothness penalty on the knots has weight 10 (e00565_model_variants.py:27).
  • Pre-training. ERA5 and CAMS weather estimates standing in for forecasts, with every row cleaned of flagged half-hours, no recency weights, learning rate 5e-4, and early stopping on held- out weeks, one fit per fold and seed (e00572_fit.py:567-647, e00448_run.py:123-179). Block dropout masks all lags on 25.5% of origin days and only the day lag on 4.5% (e00558_lags.py:18-64).
  • Fine-tuning. Ensemble-mean weather of daily runs from 2024-04-01, over the 730 days before the fit, with a recency weight of 0.5 to the power (age in days / 90), a fresh mixer (learning rate 5e-4, seed 12345), the lag encoder and the Primary embedding at 2e-4, and the weather and datetime encoders frozen (e00572_fit.py:211-259, e00510_common.py:50-61,261-279). There is no embargo and no three-step schedule.
  • Refit cadence and seeds. One coarse fit on day 0 and one on day 14 of each fold month, each scoring the origins until the next cutoff, with seeds 0 and 1; the forecasts here are the seed mean (e00572_fit.py:63,131-138). Origins are daily at 09:00 UTC, the ensemble run at 00:00 UTC plus a 9 h publication delay, with leads up to 240 h (e00087_common.py:93,231).
  • Lags. The day lag and the week lag are the latest values at least 24 h before the origin (cap_steps 48), asserted row by row (e00572_lags.py:132-143,193-222). The 3.5 h in the brief belongs to arm V35 and to the training cut-off age, not to this network. The gate of the brief reads observations up to the origin minus 3.5 h; no gate was run here.
  • Cleaning. Half-hours flagged substation_zero are dropped, and for D15 and D18 everything before 2025-03-01. Labelled load-shift events are not dropped (e00510_common.py:97-100).
  • The two twins. The lags-masked twin sets both lag inputs to the missing state with the same fitted weights (e00572_lags.py:182-190). The corrected-lag twin rebuilds the lag values from the cleaned power plus the NRA correction of experiment 435, leaving the lag times unchanged (e00578_fit.py:48-64).

docs.title: The metrics
docs.text:
Every metric below is computed per event on the valid times inside the event, for forecasts issued 24 to 120 h earlier, from the seed-mean median forecast. Depth is the labelled size of the event as a signed share of the Primary's effective capacity (positive when the transfer raised the Primary's load). The code is ml-experiments/00578-*/e00578_nra.py, which reads the tables from e00578_follow2.py and writes nra_metrics.csv.

  • Follow ratio = mean over valid times of (median forecast with the observed lags minus median forecast with the NRA-corrected lags) divided by the depth. 0 means the lags do not move the forecast; 1 means the lags move it by the whole event. Worked example with illustrative numbers: depth 0.23, forecast 0.80 with observed lags and 0.75 with corrected lags, so (0.80 - 0.75) / 0.23 = 0.22.
  • Lag effect = the same, with the lags-masked twin in place of the corrected-lag forecast. It measures what reading the lags adds, whether or not the lags are right. Example: 0.80 with lags and 0.72 masked gives 0.35.
  • Error during the event = mean of the absolute difference between the median forecast and the observed power, divided by the absolute depth. Example: an absolute error of 0.04 at depth 0.23 is 0.17.
  • Recovery error = the same error over the 7 days after the event ends, when power has snapped back. It is high when the forecast stays shifted.
  • Level share = sum of (forecast minus corrected power) over sum of (observed minus corrected power). 0 means the forecast sits at the counterfactual level; 1 means it reproduces the event's level.
  • Absorbed share and the 74 pairs. The share of an event's depth that a fine-tune absorbs into the next week's median, taken from experiment 566: 0.026 for the lag network and 0.040 for the lag-free network over 74 (month, event) pairs (59 distinct events). Not recomputed here.
  • Lag-following on the 43 events. Correcting the lags inside an event moves the lag network's forecast by 0.122 of the depth (43 events, intervals about 0.11 to 0.15), from the same page of experiment 566. This page's follow ratio is the same quantity for 12 long events (mean 0.110), at 24-120 h.
  • Injected 7-day shift leak. A step of 10% of capacity in the fine-tuning targets reaches the next week's median by 26% of the step after 7 days, from experiment 556. Not recomputed here.

Glossary. NRA is NGED's normal running arrangement; the corrected power is the metered power with a logged departure from it removed. Depth and follow ratio are defined above. Fold is one scored month of experiment 572, fitted on data before it. D3 to D22 are anonymised Primary labels; the eight MVA Primaries have no signed power, the six MW Primaries do.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Which events can be tested. Of 184 labelled events (experiment 400), 23 last at least 7 days. Their median depth is 22.1% of effective capacity, and 12 are at least that deep (long and deep). Five of the 12 (ids 122, 85, 183, 157, and 136) cannot be tested, because the ensemble weather summaries start on 2024-04-01. The other 7 lie in the five folds of experiment 572 (ids 115, 146, 178) or in the two folds added here, 2025-07 and 2025-08 (ids 143, 172, 173, 175). Five more events of at least 7 days (ids 28, 55, 112, 113, 174) lie in the folds and are shown beside them. Duration quartiles (days): 0.15, 0.4, 2.1, 3.6, 39.7; depth quartiles (% of capacity): 1.6, 10.9, 19.2, 31.3, 99.6.

Counts behind each number. Follow ratio, lag effect, error, and level share: 12 events at 7 Primaries (D3, D5, D8, D14, D16) in 7 folds, of which 7 are long and deep (D3, D5, D8). The lag-free D5 network exists only in the five old folds, so it has 4 events (55, 115, 146, 178).

Follow ratio by day. Over the 7 long-and-deep events, the mean follow ratio after day 4 is 0.163 (95% interval from resampling events 0.11 to 0.23; median 0.13; 2 of 7 above 0.15), and over the 7 days after the event ends it is 0.175 (0.13 to 0.23). Over all 12 long events the values are 0.185 (0.14 to 0.23) and 0.19 (0.15 to 0.24), all 12 positive. The per-day curve (figure above) rises from 0.00 on day 0 to 0.16 on day 4, and stays between 0.15 and 0.22 for the week after the end.

Day-ahead plots for the other testable events: 115, 143, 172, 175, 178.

The forecast already holds the event's level. With observed lags the median level share over the 12 long events in the folds is 0.95, with corrected lags 0.84, with masked lags 0.96, and for the lag-free D5 network 0.73 (4 events). So the forecast reproduces most of a long event's level even when it reads no event lags. That comparison does not isolate the offset: the corrected-lag forecast uses weights fine-tuned on the uncorrected targets, so the offset and the fine-tune are both candidates. The exception is the example pair at D16 (event 55) with level share 0.24 with observed lags and 0.12 with corrected or masked lags.

Cross-check. Experiment 566 measured 0.122 of the depth on 43 events for correcting the lags. The 12 long events here give a mean of 0.110, so the two agree.

Not run. G3, A1, A3, A4, the injected-world tuning, and CRPS on rows with no labelled event. The lag-free D5 network was not re-fitted for 2025-07 and 2025-08, so those events have no figures for it.

docs.title: A descriptive gate on the lags (G1, G2, action A2)
docs.text:
The thresholds are untuned and the numbers are descriptive. The gate reads the daily mean gap between the observed power and the lags-masked v3+D5 day-ahead forecast (the lag-free expectation, issued at least 24 h earlier) over the last 3 complete UTC days before the origin. It triggers when the gap keeps one sign on all 3 days and exceeds both 3 event-free standard deviations of that Primary's daily gap (0.05 to 0.62 of capacity as the threshold, D15 the largest) and 5% of capacity. G2 also needs a neighbouring Primary, from the interconnection list, with a sustained gap of the opposite sign. The gate releases after 2 days below half the threshold. Action A2 replaces the forecast of a gated origin by the lags-masked twin's. The code is e00578_gate.py.

The gate triggers on 2 of the 12 long events. G1 triggers on event 55 (D16) 3 days after onset and gates 60% of its origin days, and on event 146 (D5) 4 days after onset, gating 82% of origin days. G2 triggers on the same two events, event 146 only 28 days after onset. Neither gate triggers on the other 10 events, including the D3 and D8 events, because the gap stays under the threshold. That is 17% of the events, against the 70% predicted.

Effect of A2. On event 55, the follow ratio falls from 0.169 to 0.019 during the event and from 0.359 to 0.073 in the 7 days after it, and the error in those 7 days (divided by depth) falls from 0.52 to 0.33. During the event the error rises from 1.06 to 1.21 times the depth. On event 146 the follow ratio during the event moves from 0.132 to 0.122 (G1) and rises from 0.135 to 0.174 after the event, while the error after the event falls from 0.21 to 0.17. The mean over all 12 events moves little because 10 events are not gated: the follow ratio goes from 0.110 to 0.097 during the event and from 0.190 to 0.169 after it.

Cost on event-free days. On 2,557 Primary-origin days at least 3 days away from any labelled event, G1 gates 24 days, which is 3.4 false triggers per Primary-year (above the 3 that the brief allows), and G2 gates none. The mean absolute error of the median forecast with A2 is 0.0614 against 0.0612 ungated for G1, as fractions of capacity (a median absolute error, not CRPS). Unlogged events sit among these days, so the false-trigger rate is an upper bound.

docs.title: Method notes
docs.text:
• The re-forecast of the five old folds equals experiment 572's stored v3+D5 forecasts exactly (maximum absolute difference 0.0 over 1,142,520 rows).
  • Weather: every forecast row uses the ensemble run issued at or before the origin minus 9 h (example row: origin 2026-06-08 09:00, run 2026-06-08 00:00). Every lag, observed or corrected, is at least 24 h before the origin; the corrected variant leaves the lag times unchanged.
  • Event-free gap standard deviations and the lag-free expectation use experiment 565's D5 forecasts, the shortest stored lead per half-hour.
  • GPU time: about 0.5 GPU-h (unmeasured), against a ceiling of 4. Reused code: experiments 400, 435, 556, 565, 572, and 575. How to recompute: e00578_step0.py, then e00578_fit.py through run.sh, then e00578_follow2.py, e00578_level.py, e00578_nra.py, and e00578_figures.py.
  • The clean-lag rows may hold events no label covers, because NGED's logs may miss events, so these counts are lower bounds.

docs.title: Is the modular demand network limited by the size of its encoders, by what they are given, or by its architecture?
docs.text:
Making the encoders of our demand forecasting neural network bigger, or giving them richer datetime inputs, did not lower the forecast error beyond what a different random seed changes. The network forecasts a Primary substation's demand from four parts: a weather encoder, a datetime encoder, a lag encoder (which reads demand from earlier days), and a mixer that combines them into a forecast distribution. We changed one part at a time (15 arms), refitted each arm on the same five test months as experiment 572's best network (the base B), and compared the error, measured as CRPS in points of effective capacity (percentage points of the Primary's capacity; lower is better). The Primaries split into the eight MVA Primaries and the six MW Primaries, which differ in how their power is metered, so they are scored apart. The one large-looking gain is the larger datetime encoder (DL) at the six MW Primaries, 0.135 lower than B. A copy of DL with the same depth and no extra width (DT) achieved 0.077 of it, and the intervals of both include zero.

Every number is interim and unaudited. The Primaries appear as D-numbers. The real-event absorbed share and the encoder probes of the brief were not run (see "Not run").

docs.title: What the base holds, and what was changed
docs.text:
The base datetime encoder already holds hour harmonics 1 and 2 and a day-of-week one-hot. Its 21 input columns are cos_zenith, sin_azimuth, cos_azimuth; sin_hour, cos_hour, sin_hour_2, cos_hour_2 (local hour); dow_1 to dow_7; covid; christmas_inside, christmas_days, christmas_tent; and bank_holiday, nearest_days, nearest_inside. F1 therefore adds only 14 columns (hour harmonics 3 and 4 of the fractional local hour, 2 day-of-week harmonics, 3 day-of-year harmonics), and F2 adds a fifteenth column, an Economy 7 proxy (1 between 00:30 and 07:30 local time with a 10-minute logistic ramp at each edge; the real tariff window varies by supplier). The base has 3,104 weights in the weather encoder and 4,000 in the datetime encoder.

Arms run (code in ml-experiments/00579-*/, one change each to B; the encoder-changing arms were pre-trained afresh on the ERA5 and CAMS rows):

  • Encoder size: WL, DL, WDL (2 hidden layers of 256 units and 64 outputs in the weather encoder, the datetime encoder, or both; DL has 89,920 datetime-encoder weights), and DT (C-tied: DL's shape with each layer's units a weight-tied copy of 64-unit layers, 8,160 weights, so it keeps DL's depth but not its width).
  • Embedding and inputs: EW (Primary embedding 16 wide instead of 8), P1 (separate 16-wide embedding for the datetime encoder), P2 (learnt half-hour-of-day embedding per Primary), F1, F2.
  • Mixer and mixture: ML (3 layers of 256), K5 and K8 (5 and 8 mixture components), A2 (rank-4 per-Primary adapter on the mixer's last layer). These four re-use experiment 572's stored encoders and fine-tune only.
  • Blocks and conditioning: RB (pre-layer-norm residual blocks in both encoders and the mixer; with one hidden layer this is about 4 times the encoder weights, so RB tests depth and size as well as block type), A1 (FiLM conditioning of both encoders by the Primary embedding).

B is experiment 572's v3+D5 (stored forecasts and weights). The new code reproduces its fit exactly on one fold and seed (20 epochs, validation negative log-likelihood 0.396829 in both). In P1 and P2 the extra embeddings train in fine-tuning at the normal rate while the encoder layers stay frozen, as the shared Primary embedding does in B.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Stage 1 (seed 0, all arms) and Stage 2 (seed 1 for DL, ML, P1, and DT). CRPS at 24-120 h, in points of effective capacity (B is 4.427 at the eight MVA Primaries and 3.327 at the six MW Primaries; M0 is 4.803 and 3.641):

Arm Eight MVA Primaries Six MW Primaries Tail pinball relative to B, eight / six WL -0.003 +0.095 -0.7% / +0.8% DL (2 seeds) +0.046 -0.135 +1.2% / -4.1% DT (2 seeds) +0.020 -0.077 -2.9% / -2.3% WDL -0.027 -0.022 -1.8% / -2.0% EW +0.037 +0.003 -2.3% / -2.9% ML (2 seeds) -0.057 -0.021 -2.4% / +0.5% K5 -0.012 +0.023 -0.6% / -0.3% K8 -0.007 +0.021 -0.7% / +1.3% RB +0.260 -0.047 +0.5% / -4.2% F1 +0.032 +0.084 +0.5% / +0.8% F2 +0.047 +0.014 -2.1% / -2.8% P1 (2 seeds) -0.014 -0.036 -0.7% / -2.4% P2 -0.003 +0.011 -4.8% / -2.0% A1 +0.041 -0.001 +0.6% / -0.5% A2 -0.012 -0.018 -3.0% / -1.8%

Each cell is the arm's CRPS minus B's (negative is an improvement); arms with one seed are compared with B's seed 0, and the arms marked 2 seeds with B's mean of seeds 0 and 1. No arm met the CRPS rule (a gain of at least the minimum detectable effect with 4 of 5 folds agreeing). The two-seed minimum detectable effect is 0.123 at both groups (the brief's stored-seed values were 0.113 and 0.128), and the noise of a difference between two single-seed fits is about 0.25. The tail rule (2% gain) was met by 9 of the 15 arms, which shows that it is too loose for single-seed contrasts. I therefore chose the Stage 2 arms by hand: DL (the maintainer's hypothesis, and the largest gain at the six MW Primaries), ML (the clearest sign at the eight MVA Primaries), and P1.

Stage 2 counted tests (16, Bonferroni, month-block interval of 5 blocks, which is near the minimum to maximum of the folds): only ML at the eight MVA Primaries excludes zero (CRPS -0.057, interval -0.079 to -0.012; tail pinball -2.4%, which is -0.047 in loss units, interval -0.096 to -0.014), and the gain is under half of the minimum detectable effect. DL at the six MW Primaries is -0.135 with interval -0.437 to 0.044. DL against DT is -0.058 at the six MW Primaries (interval -0.205 to 0.031) and +0.026 at the eight (interval -0.085 to 0.131). Leave-D8-out: ML gains -0.046 without D8 (4 of 5 folds), so the ML sign does not rest on D8.

Slices at the six MW Primaries (descriptive; slice minimum detectable effects are 0.38 for cold winter nights and 0.97 for Christmas week). DL changes cold winter nights by -0.434 (3 of 5 folds better) and Christmas week by -1.156 (Christmas week falls in one fold only, so its interval is degenerate). The gain is largest in the slices the maintainer's hypothesis names, but both changes are inside their slice minimum detectable effect, so the pattern is not established. F1 and F2 change cold winter nights by -0.164 and -0.046 at the six MW Primaries and Christmas week by +0.443 and +0.619; they do not show a gain. Sunny days: no arm moves them by more than 0.2.

Leak. The injected 7-day shift (stress, in points of capacity) is 7.29 for B, 6.59 for DL, 6.45 for ML, and 6.72 for P1, so the three Stage 2 arms are within 1.0 of B, and all four are above the flagged 6.0 limit, B included. Lags aged by one extra day worsen the CRPS of every arm by 0.006 to 0.036 at 24-120 h, as they do for B.

K5 and K8 did not collapse. Averaged over the 10 fits, the smallest component weight is 0.106 (K5) and 0.060 (K8), and the smallest weight in any single fit is 0.058 (K5) and 0.040 (K8), all above the 0.02 flag.

The 16-Primary table (primaries.csv, seed 0) shows each of DL, ML, and P1 at or better than M0 at 14 of 16 Primaries, with different exceptions: DL loses to M0 at D8 (10.23 against 9.46) and D5 (5.97 against 5.78); ML at D8 (9.69) and D5 (5.83); P1 at D8 (9.74) and D11. B itself loses to M0 at D5, D8, D10, and D11. DL is 0.27 worse than B at D8 and 0.77 better at D15. A2 does not improve the four Primaries with the largest error (D15, D8, D12, D5): it worsens D15, D12, and D5 and improves D8.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• DL gains at least 0.05 at one group, largest on cold winter nights and Christmas week: met in size at the six MW Primaries (-0.135), not at the eight MVA Primaries (+0.046); the interval includes zero, and the slice pattern is not established (see above).
  • WL within 0.03 of B: not met at the six MW Primaries (+0.095, worse); met at the eight MVA Primaries. XL was not run.
  • F1 gains at least 0.03 on cold winter nights or Christmas week: met in size on cold winter nights (-0.052 and -0.164) inside the slice minimum detectable effect; Christmas week is worse. F2 gains at least 0.03 on cold winter nights: met in size at the six MW Primaries only (-0.046).
  • P1 and P2 gain at least 0.03 at one group: P1 yes in size (-0.036 at the six MW Primaries, inside the minimum detectable effect); P2 no.
  • K5 and K8 lower tail pinball by at least 2% with no collapse: not met (-0.6% and -0.7% at the eight MVA Primaries).
  • RB, GB, ML, A1, A2, EW within the minimum detectable effect of B: RB is 0.26 worse at the eight MVA Primaries (interval excludes zero); ML, A1, A2, and EW are within it. A2 does not improve the weakest 4 Primaries. GB was not run.
  • C-tied within the minimum detectable effect of B: held as written (DT -0.077, minimum detectable effect 0.123). The brief also said the prediction fails if DT gains at least half of DL's gain; DT gains 0.077 of DL's 0.135 at the six MW Primaries, so the brief's clause fails.
  • Leak: the injected shift of each Stage 2 arm is within 1.0 of B's; the real-event absorbed share was not run.

docs.title: Not run
docs.text:
• F3, U, and GB were cut to stay under the 5 GPU-h ceiling, and XL was not run because no encoder-size arm cleared the screen. EW was run at 16 only.
  • The real-event absorbed-share harness and the probes of addenda 8 and 9 were not run, because the harness code of experiments 556 and 566 is not ported to the new arms and experiment 572 also left it out. The leak result above is the injected shift alone.
  • Seeds 2 to 4 were not run, so every contrast has 1 or 2 seeds.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site: not computed.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside the quantile-score contrasts: not computed; the tail pinball loss at the 5%, 95%, and 99% quantiles is reported beside CRPS.
  • Audit triggers: the brief's C-tied clause failed (DT gained more than half of DL's gain), which is an explanation to test next (more seeds, and a tied control that also matches B's depth), not a method fault; no other trigger fired. No audit was run.
  • Timing asserts (row by row, with examples printed in the checks JSON files): weather from the run at or before the origin minus 9 h; every lag at or before the origin minus 24 h; every extra datetime column a function of the valid time's grid index only (asserted against the valid time for training and test rows).
  • Cost: about 3.4 GPU-h of wall time on a shared GPU (Stage 1 about 2.3 h, Stage 2 and C-tied about 1.1 h).

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does DL's gain at the six MW Primaries survive 5 seeds, and does DT's gain survive them too? If DT's gain survives, depth, training noise, or regularisation explains it better than capacity, and a one-layer tied control would separate depth from the rest.

docs.title: Which of NGED's 184 labelled load-shift events can be found in the telemetry?
docs.text:
We asked how many of NGED's labelled load-shift events (transfers of load between two Primaries, the primary substations of the electricity distribution network) show up as steps in the Primaries' own power readings. We treated each label as a candidate window only. We measured the step at the start and at the end of each event in the cleaned half-hourly power at the labelled Primary, required the step to exceed that Primary's own noise, and required a mirrored step at a second Primary. 1 of the 23 events of at least 7 days, and 1 of all 184 events, passed the pair rule below, and none passed the stricter 99th-percentile rule. The verdict word "supported" means the prediction held: the plan review predicted at most 6 of 23.

Take-home message: the labels cannot be relied on to build a corrected target. The correction removes a labelled event of the labelled sign, so for events 146, 143, and 85 the mismatch is in what the labels say. For most other long events the audit cannot tell a wrong label from a step too small to see. Event 146 shows the problem: the label says D5 carried 2.9 MW more from 2025-12-05 to 2026-01-14, the correction removed that amount, and the corrected power fell to about 0.3 of capacity (0.2 to 0.4), which D5 never reads. D5 shows no step on 2025-12-05. It drops by about 1.5 MW on 2025-12-29, mirroring D16, and recovers on about 2026-01-14. Experiments 578, 566, and 565 carry an erratum (last section).

Terms. D5, D16, and the other D-numbers are anonymised labels of Primaries. A "twin" is the same fitted neural network run with its lag inputs replaced (masked, or corrected with a label). The "follow ratio" is the median forecast with the observed lags minus the twin's median forecast, divided by the event's depth, so 0 means the lags did not move the forecast and 1 means they moved it by the whole depth. The "level share" is the share of the event's level that the forecast reproduces. The "absorbed share" is the share of the labelled depth that a refit absorbs from the event's rows. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score.

docs.title: What a rejection means
docs.text: A rejected event is not proven absent, and a label that passes the check is not proven right in its depth. A 3-day step must exceed the 95th or 99th percentile of |step| at event-free dates, which is 0.07 to 0.45 (95th) and 0.10 to 0.56 (99th) of capacity depending on the Primary. A transfer of 1 to 2 MW at a 10 MW Primary is 10% to 20% of capacity, which weather and holidays also produce. So the check finds large steps only. NGED's logs are incomplete, so rows the check treats as event-free may still hold events.

docs.title: How the check works
docs.text:
• Candidate window. The labelled onset and end, searched within 3 days each side.
  • Step. For each of the 48 half-hours of the day, the median over the 3 days after the candidate time minus the median over the 3 days before it, averaged over the 48 half-hours (1 day or 6 hours for shorter events).
  • Noise threshold (per Primary). A percentile of |step| on dates more than 4 days from every labelled onset and end at that Primary, and at least 5% of capacity. The strict rule asks each Primary alone to clear the 99th percentile. The pair rule asks both Primaries of a mirrored pair to clear the 95th percentile, because the same mirrored step at two Primaries on the same dates is much rarer by chance.
  • A verified step pair has onset and end steps of opposite sign, within a factor of 2 in size.
  • A verified transfer needs the same at the partner Primary, onsets and ends within 1 day, opposite signs, and load conserved to within 30% (the sum of signed MW under 30% of the larger).
  • Sign convention. Depth is signed MW; positive means the Primary carries more power after the onset. The counterfactual is observed - depth over the inclusive span from onset to end. The stored correction of experiment 435 is the array f1.0, and experiments 566 and 578 apply corrected = observed + shift with shift = -f1.0. Inside an event f1.0 is the label depth over capacity, or a step measured from the telemetry where that step has the label's sign, is at least a set share of the label, and exceeds twice its pre-event bias (experiment 435's filters). For events 146, 143, 85, 154, and 161 the stored f1.0 equals the label depth. For event 55 it is 0.229 of capacity (2.1 MW), measured, against a label of 1.5 MW. A unit check (e00580_check_sign.py) builds a synthetic event of +0.3 of capacity and confirms that the correction recovers the baseline exactly, that this experiment's correct() agrees, and that a label of the opposite sign doubles the event.

docs.title: Is the mismatch in the code or in the labels?
docs.text: For events 146, 143, and 85 the stored correction is the label depth, and it contradicts the telemetry. The code removes the labelled depth with the labelled sign (unit check above), so these corrected series are wrong because of the label's span, sign, or size. A label-corrected power below zero at a demand Primary (event 143) is a symptom of a label for a step that is not in the data. For the other long events the audit cannot say whether the label is wrong or the step is too small to see, and the measured-step branch of experiment 435 was not inspected event by event.

At D16 the follow ratio against the corrected-lag twin is 0.17, 0.24, and 0.36 in the same three phases, so the twin choice matters little there. At D5 the follow is small. The level share is noisy on one event: 0.27 at D5 and -0.14 at D16 against the telemetry counterfactual, against 1.04 for event 146 against the label counterfactual, which is the figure the label error produced. Each ratio is one event, so no interval is shown.

Only 2 of the 41 (fold month, labelled event) overlaps in the five fold months of experiment 578 belong to the confirmed event 55, so the shares of experiments 565 and 566 are mostly shares of a labelled depth that the telemetry does not confirm.

docs.title: The injected event bank
docs.text: The bank (injected_event_bank.parquet, 358 designs; e00580_bank.py) follows the plan review: mirrored transfers between connected Primaries from experiment 400's list (excluding D15 and D18), 15%, 30%, and 50% of the smaller capacity, lengths of 3, 7, 15, and 30 days, an onset at 00:00 or at 12:00 UTC, 3 start dates in each of the five fold months, one event per design. The donor changes by a depth and the recipient gains the same MW. inject() of experiment 402 draws depths, lengths, and dates at random, so the bank fixes the design in its own module and keeps the load-conserving convention of inject(). A known-answer check confirms that correct() returns the original power and that the two depths sum to zero MW. Use the bank twice: in the lags only (forecast-time following) and in the lags and the fine-tune targets (absorption).

docs.title: ERRATUM for experiments 578, 566, and 565
docs.text:
• Experiment 578: the follow ratios, level shares, and normal-running-arrangement (NRA) coverage for the labelled events other than event 55, including events 115, 143, 146, 28, 112, and 113, used a corrected power that the telemetry does not confirm. Do not quote them. For events 146 and 143 the corrected power contradicts the telemetry. The headline "whole event 0.087, after day 4 0.163" and "the corrected-lag forecast still reproduces a median 0.84 of the event's level" are not supported. The event 55 numbers stand, with its stored correction measured at 2.1 MW against a telemetry fit of 1.4 to 1.8 MW. The verdict "not supported" rested on a prediction (P1) tested over a set that the audit reduces to one event.
  • Experiment 566: the real-event absorbed shares (0.026, 0.040, 0.014 of the labelled depth) divide by labelled depths that the telemetry mostly does not confirm. Treat them as unproven. The CRPS, coverage, and lag-encoder results do not depend on the labels and stand.
  • Experiment 565: the real-event absorbed share (74 pairs) has the same problem; the other results stand.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site: not applicable (no forecast is fitted).
  • Error of the mean or median beside every quantile contrast: not applicable.
  • Triggers: none fired (no control, contrast, or nested arm).
  • Standing rule on weather inputs: not applicable; no weather input enters.
  • Interval statistics: none; the tables are counts. No bootstrap or Bonferroni count applies.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss events, so rows with no labelled event may still hold events.
  • Lead range: not applicable (no forecast is scored). NGED care about 1 to 10 days.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does a lag neural network that reads a robust multi-week summary of its lags keep its gain and stop following injected long events? Run it on the injected event bank, and ask NGED to check the labels for events 146, 143, and 85 and the D3, D5, and D8 events.

docs.title: Does reading five weeks of power lags through a median and a spread, instead of one day lag and one week lag, stop the forecast following a load-shift event, without losing the lag gain?
docs.text:
A median over five weeks of power lags does not stop the forecast following a load-shift event, but training on synthetic lag-only events does roughly halve it. We asked whether the neural network that reads a day-old and a week-old reading of a Primary's power can be made to ignore an event that sits in a few of its lags. We built a variant that reads the median of five same-weekday readings and their spread (X3-med). We then added a shift of 15%, 30%, or 50% of capacity to the lag inputs of every Primary for 3 to 30 days, in 24 passes that give every Primary every depth and length with both signs, and measured how far the day-ahead forecast moved. The real power, the target, was never shifted, so the unshifted power is the reference (the normal running arrangement, NRA). We also scored the one verified real transfer of the telemetry set of experiment 580 that lies inside the five fold months, and the May 2026 transfers. All numbers are interim and unaudited.

Verdict: partly supported. X3-med passes its accuracy condition and misses its following target; the synthetic-event arms meet the after-the-end target (0.038 for X3-syn, 0.040 for v3+D5-syn at the eight MVA Primaries) but still follow 0.085 to 0.104 of the depth from day 4 to the end. In CRPS (points of capacity, 24-120 h) at the eight MVA Primaries, lag-free D5 scores 4.651, v3+D5 4.427, and X3-med 4.423, so X3-med keeps 102% of the lag gain. At the six MW Primaries v3+D5 scores 3.327 and X3-med 3.328. The median follow ratio (the share of the injected depth that the median forecast moves towards) is 0.065 after the end against a predicted 0.05 or less, and 0.172 from day 4 to the end against 0.196 for v3+D5. The prediction that v3+D5 follows at least 0.15 after the end also fails: it follows 0.075.

docs.title: What changed from the plan
docs.text:
• X3-set was not run. The condition (X3-med keeps 80% of the lag gain) held, but X3-med did not move the following, so a learned set encoder on the same inputs had no stated reason to.
  • X3-syn was built on X3-med, not on X3-set, and v3+D5 with the same synthetic events (v3+D5-syn) was added as a control. It shifts the lag inputs on 5% of each Primary's time, with random depths, lengths, and signs, seeded by the fold month, and leaves the targets clean. This is post hoc.
  • Fold months. Only the five folds of experiment 572 were used. The extra months planned for the verified transfers of 2024 cannot be built, because the demand frames start in July 2025. The 2026-05 fold reuses the v3+D5 weights of experiment 582.
  • The lag-free D5 reference and the recalibrated control of experiment X2 were not built for the tail tables.
  • Statistics. Intervals for CRPS are the 5-block month bootstrap at the Bonferroni level of 12 tests; the injected-bank and real-event numbers carry no intervals. The unlogged-event caveat applies: NGED's logs may miss events, so the "no labelled or verified event" rows may hold events.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site and the error of the median beside each quantile contrast were not computed; the contrasts above are quantile scores only.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 fired: v3+D5's following after the end (0.075) is below the 0.15 the prediction assumed, taken from experiment 578's labelled events. The explanation tested here is that the following is nearly independent of event length, so it is carried by the day lag, and that the labelled events of experiment 578 were in part mislabelled (experiment 580). No other trigger fired; leaving one Primary out was not run.
  • Leakage checks. Each lag is at least 24 h (X3-3.5h: 3.5 h) before the forecast origin, each lag's weather run is at or before the lag time, and each forecast's weather run is at or before the origin (asserted row by row; the example rows print in the fit logs). One Sonnet code review before the first fit found no problems.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
Whether the synthetic-event fine-tune keeps its gain when events are also present in the training targets, and whether a gate or a union band (experiments X2 and X4 of the plan review) lifts the coverage after an event ends from about 0.5 to the 0.90 target, since the lag network alone does not.

Scripts: ml-experiments/00581-robust-multiweek-lag-encoder-x3/ (e00581_arm.py wraps experiment 572's fit; e00581_report.py prints every table above). Code reused from experiments 560, 565, 572, 578, and 580.

docs.title: The tail metrics of experiment 582, explained with one worked example
docs.text: This page explains every number in experiment 582 for a reader who has not met them. All figures use one made-up half-hour, so the arithmetic can be followed by hand. Power is in percent of the Primary's effective capacity.

docs.title: The words
docs.text:
A load-shift is a logged transfer of load from one Primary to a neighbouring Primary for days or weeks. The Primary that gives load away sees its readings fall, and the neighbour sees them rise by the same amount. Experiment 580 found the load-shifts that show in the telemetry alone, so only those are used here.

The normal running arrangement (NRA) is the power the Primary would have drawn without the load- shift. Inside a load-shift, the NRA is the observed power minus the load-shift's signed fitted depth (negative when the load fell). Outside it, the NRA is the observed power. The NRA is what NGED want the forecast to cover, because the network operator must plan for the moment the load-shift ends.

A quantile forecast gives several levels, and a band is the range between two of them. The q05-q95 band is the range between the 5th and 95th percentile of the forecast, so a well-calibrated forecast holds 90% of readings inside it. The q01-q99 band should hold 98%.

A phase is a stretch of valid times measured from the event. The five phases are the 7 days before onset, days 0 to 3, day 4 to the end, 0 to 7 days after the end, and 7 to 14 days after the end. The forecasts are scored at two lead bands: forecasts issued 0 to 24 hours before the valid time, and 24 to 120 hours before it.

docs.title: The worked example
docs.text:
One half-hour, one Primary. A load-shift has lowered the Primary's load by a depth of 15 points. The NRA at this half-hour is 80, and the observed power is 65. The corrected-lag forecast, whose lags have been corrected for the load-shift, says q05 = 74, q50 = 79, q95 = 85, q99 = 88. The forecast being tested (the arm) has followed the load-shift and says q05 = 64, q50 = 69, q95 = 75, q99 = 78.

Metric Formula Worked value NRA coverage 1 if q05 ≤ NRA ≤ q95, otherwise 0; averaged over rows 80 is not between 64 and 75, so 0 One-sided NRA coverage The load-shift lowered load, so the NRA lies above the forecast: 1 if NRA ≤ q95, otherwise 0 80 ≤ 75 is false, so 0 Tail follow ratio at q95 (q95 of the arm − q95 of the corrected-lag forecast) × s ÷ depth, where s = −1 when the load-shift lowered load and +1 when it raised load (75 − 85) × (−1) ÷ 15 = 0.67 Coverage of the corrected-lag median 1 if the arm's q05 ≤ the corrected-lag q50 ≤ the arm's q95 79 is not between 64 and 75, so 0 Pinball loss at level τ (τ × (NRA − q)) if NRA ≥ q, otherwise ((1 − τ) × (q − NRA)) At q95: 0.95 × (80 − 75) = 4.75. At q05: 0.05 × (80 − 64) = 0.80 Band width q95 − q05 75 − 64 = 11 Width inflation Band width of the arm ÷ band width of the recalibrated control R If R's width is 10, the inflation is 1.1

How to read each one.

  • NRA coverage answers "did the band hold the power NGED must plan for?" A value of 0.90 is the target. A value far below 0.90 means the forecast has followed the load-shift away from the NRA.
  • The tail follow ratio answers "how far did the edge of the band move towards the load-shift?" A value of 0 means the edge did not move. A value of 1 means it moved by the whole depth. The worked value of 0.67 means the q95 edge dropped by two-thirds of the load-shift. The sign s makes a positive value always mean "moved towards the load-shift", whichever way the load went.
  • The safe-side quantile is q95 or q99 when the load-shift lowered load, and q05 or q01 when it raised load. This is the edge of the band that must stay put to keep the NRA covered.
  • Pinball loss is the standard score of one quantile. Smaller is better. A quantile that is too high or too low is charged in proportion to the miss, and the charge is heavier on the side that the level protects: at q95, a reading above the quantile costs 0.95 per point, and a reading below costs 0.05 per point.
  • CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. This page approximates it as twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantile levels.

docs.title: Comparing arms without fooling ourselves
docs.text:
R is the recalibrated control, and every other arm is compared with it. R is the v3+D5 forecast with each level's distance from the median multiplied by a factor, so that on earlier months' rows with no labelled event the share of readings below each quantile equals its level. A widening that only fixes calibration therefore shows no gain over R.

The false-alarm cost is the pinball loss minus R's, on rows with no labelled event within 7 days. A positive value means the arm is worse than R when nothing is happening. The interval comes from resampling whole months (5 months here, so close to the minimum and maximum of the monthly values).

The calibration share is the share of observed readings at or below each quantile on those rows. The target at q95 is 0.95. A share of 0.91 means the q95 edge is too low.

An event-block bootstrap resamples whole events with replacement. There are only 6 Primary- events, so each interval is descriptive. A leave-one-Primary-out range, which drops each Primary in turn, shows whether one Primary decides the result.

docs.title: Do the forecast's tails hold the normal running arrangement during and after long load-shift events that the telemetry confirms?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the forecast with lags stops covering the normal running arrangement (NRA) once a long load-shift ends, and in the test pair hiding the lags for the week after the end raised coverage from 0.40 to 0.64. We asked how often the 5% to 95% band of an electricity-demand forecast issued 1 to 5 days ahead holds the power a substation would have drawn without a logged transfer of load (the NRA), during and after long transfers that the telemetry itself confirms (experiment 580). We took the stored forecasts of experiments 565 (lag-free network), 572 (lag network), and 578 (gate), added one new test month (May 2026), and rebuilt the NRA as the observed power minus each transfer's fitted depth. A plain-language explanation of every metric, with a worked example, is here.

Result: partly supported. The clean test is one pair, the 15-day mirrored transfer between D5 and D16 in December 2025 and January 2026. The other four events (D10, D11, D12 and D16 in May 2026) fail a plausibility check (below), so they are shown but not used for the verdict. Every number is at 24-120 hours lead, from the mean of 2 seeds, and descriptive: 2 Primary-events cannot support an interval.

Arm (D5 and D16, 24-120 h) Inside q05-q95, days 4 to end Inside q05-q95, 0-7 days after NRA-side share at q95 or q05, 0-7 days after v3+D5 (lags) 0.80 0.40 0.54 Lags masked 0.72 0.64 0.79 Week lag only masked 0.74 0.63 0.78 Lag-free D5 0.76 0.58 0.73 R (v3+D5 recalibrated on earlier months) 0.85 0.45 0.59 50/50 mixture, recalibrated 0.89 0.58 0.72 Mixture with per-lead weights, recalibrated 0.90 0.55 0.69 Union band (lags and masked) 0.86 0.67 0.81 Gated (G2), masked while on, week lag masked 7 days after 0.74 0.64 0.80
  • P1 holds: after the end, v3+D5 covers the NRA on 0.40 of rows (prediction: at most 0.60). D5 gives 0.31 and D16 gives 0.48.
  • P2 partly holds: the gated arm lifts after-end coverage by 0.25, but reaches 0.64, not the predicted 0.75. The week-lag-only rule adds 0.07 at D16 and 0.00 at D5 on top of masking while the gate is on, so the gate is nearly the same as masking.
  • P3 fails: on rows with no labelled event the unrecalibrated 50/50 mixture beats R by 0.019 points of capacity at q95 at the eight MVA Primaries (interval -0.037 to -0.005) and by 0.026 at the six MW Primaries (-0.052 to 0.006). The prediction allowed 0.01. The recalibrated mixtures lose 0.006 and 0.036 points of pinball loss at q05 against R.
  • Stop rule not met: R alone lifts after-end coverage from 0.40 to only 0.45.
  • v3+D5 is miscalibrated at the top: on rows with no labelled event 0.922 (eight MVA Primaries) and 0.902 (six MW Primaries) of readings fall below q95, against 0.95.

The May 2026 load-shifts fail a plausibility check. Inside these load-shifts the lags-masked and lag-free forecasts cannot know about the transfer, so their median should sit about one depth away from the observed power. For D16 (depth 0.14 of capacity), D10 (0.15) and D11 (0.11) the lag-free forecast's median sits 0.03, 0.01 and 0.01 from the observed power (the masked forecast: 0.05, 0.01 and 0.02; D12, depth 0.43, is not checked), and every arm covers the NRA on only 0.15 to 0.32 of rows from day 4 to the end. For the December load-shift the gap is 0.22 (D5 depth 0.26) and 0.22 (D16 depth 0.15). It is unproven whether the fitted depths or the NRA reference is wrong, so these four events carry no verdict here.

Day-ahead forecasts with the q05-q95 and q01-q99 bands for each event and each arm (3 days before onset to 7 days after the end; the last panel also marks the days the gate is on and the 7 days it is held): D5 2025-12, D16 2025-12, D16 2026-05, D12 2026-05, D10 2026-05, D11 2026-05.

docs.title: What is not done
docs.text:
• The injected event bank of experiment 580 is not used. It would turn 2 clean real events into hundreds of tests of the after-end claims; it needs about 1,400 forward passes and was left for a follow-up.
  • Three transfers of 2024 (verified in the telemetry) cannot be forecast: the stored demand frames start on 2025-07-02, so no earlier test month can be built with the 572 recipe. 2025-07 is the first possible month.
  • The avoidable-curtailment difference is not computed. The gate triggered on 28 of 2,934 origin-days with no labelled event for G1 (3.5 per Primary-year) and on none for G2.
  • Phases are by valid time. The sign rule in the experiment plan for the follow ratio ("s is -1 when the transfer raised load") contradicts its own meaning ("positive means moved towards the event"). We used the meaning.

docs.title: Injected load-shifts from experiment 581
docs.text:
On 1,248 injected Primary-events, the lag network's after-end coverage falls to 0.77, and masking the lags or the union band restores it to 0.86 or 0.92. Experiment 581 forecast the lag network with a constant shift added to the lag inputs only, for every Primary in four test months (2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) and 24 passes. The shift has a depth of 0.15, 0.30, or 0.50 of capacity, a length of 3, 7, 15, or 30 days, and a sign that either raises or lowers the lags. The observed power is unchanged, so it is the NRA, and the gates are not scored (they see no gap). We reuse 581's stored forecasts, so no forward pass was repeated and no GPU time was spent. Arms that never read the lags are the stored forecasts of this experiment. R, the union band, and the mixtures are rebuilt from the injected forecast with the factors and weights fitted on earlier months. The 14 Primaries of the eight MVA and six MW groups are scored (D15 and D18 are left out), at 24-120 h, with every second half-hour.

Share of the NRA inside the q05-q95 band (target 0.90), mean over events, by phase:

Arm Before Days 0-3 Day 4 to end 0-7 days after 7-14 days after v3+D5 0.87 0.85 0.78 0.77 0.88 Lags masked 0.88 0.84 0.86 0.86 0.88 Week lag masked 0.87 0.84 0.86 0.86 0.88 Lag-free D5 0.90 0.86 0.87 0.84 0.86 R 0.89 0.87 0.80 0.79 0.90 Union 0.90 0.87 0.91 0.92 0.90 Mix50-R 0.91 0.90 0.90 0.87 0.89 MixPL-R 0.91 0.89 0.88 0.86 0.89
  • The injected result agrees with the December pair: v3+D5 loses coverage from the lag shift, and the loss is larger at greater depth (0-7 days after: 0.82, 0.76, and 0.74 at depths 0.15, 0.30, and 0.50).
  • R alone does not repair it: 0.79 after the end, against 0.77 for v3+D5.
  • The union band comes closest to target (0.92) because its lower and upper edges take the wider of the lag network and the masked twin. It does so by widening.
  • Interval and spread: the event-block interval of v3+D5 after the end is 0.72 to 0.82 (leave-one-Primary-out range 0.70 to 0.85), against 0.89 to 0.94 for the union band.
  • Length does not matter beyond 3 days: coverage after the end is the same for lengths of 7, 15, and 30 days (0.76 for v3+D5), because only the week lag at the end of the shift enters the forecast, and the 3-day shift is only partly in it (0.81).
  • Scope: the lag shift is a stylised stand-in for a real transfer, because the real transfer also changes the targets and the neighbour's lags. The tables are bank_event_phase.csv and bank_summary.csv in the private data folder.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: not applicable; the arms are quantile forecasts with no separate mean. The q50 follow ratio sits beside the q05-q99 ratios in event_phase.csv.
  • Reproduction: the v3+D5 and lags-masked forecasts of 2025-12 and 2026-01 match experiment 578's stored forecasts to a maximum absolute difference of 0.
  • Statistics: event intervals are 95% event-block bootstraps over 6 Primary-events with a leave-one-Primary-out range, descriptive only. False-alarm intervals come from 5 month blocks, which are close to the minimum to maximum of the months; the Bonferroni count is 4 per arm, and the 95% interval is not adjusted for it, so only the Mix50 intervals that exclude zero are worth reading and they are small (the minimum detectable effect is about 0.04 points: 1.4 times the interval half-width for the six MW Primaries and about 2.5 times for the eight MVA Primaries).
  • Months and rows: every arm exists on 574,755 rows in 5 months (2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-05, 2026-06). The first fold month with each arm has no recalibration fit and is dropped.
  • Standing weather rule: the forecasts come from experiment 572's code, which asserts for every test origin that the weather run was issued at or before the origin (nwp_init_time <= power_fcst_init_time); an example row: origin 2026-01-01 09:00, weather run 2026-01-01 00:00, valid time 2026-01-05 09:00.
  • Audit triggers: the check that a lag-blind forecast sits about one depth from the observed power failed for the May transfers, so the write-up reviewer was asked to recompute the December headline numbers from the stored forecasts.
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet review of the code found no leak and no sign error. Findings applied: the gate state no longer carries over a gap between fold months; the 5-day overlap of recalibration training rows with the first origins of the fold month is purged; the gate noise floor is guarded. Not applied: the d0 and d14 files never overlap on a key.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Recheck the fitted depths of the May 2026 transfers against a forecast that never saw them, then run the after-snap-back rule and the union band on the injected event bank of experiment 580, where the answer is known.

docs.title: Does keeping a wider forecast band for 7 days after a load-shift ends make the forecast bands hold the normal running arrangement again, with only a small rise in pinball loss on days with no load-shift?
docs.text:
Widening the band for 7 days after the gap collapses puts the normal running arrangement (NRA) inside the band on no more rows than widening the band for 7 random days. The rule detects the end of the load-shift too late. By then the readings the lag neural network takes as input no longer contain the load-shift, so the wider band is applied to forecasts that no longer need it. Of the arms tested, only A2, which keeps the wider band on whenever the gate has been on, lifts coverage after the end to about 0.92 on injected events, and A2 is almost the same as a union band that is always on. Verdict: not supported.

Experiment 582 found that after a load-shift ends, the forecast's q05-q95 band contains the NRA (the power the substation would have drawn without the load-shift) on too few rows. We asked whether a rule that watches the gap between the recent power readings and a forecast made without them, and widens the band for 7 days after that gap collapses, closes the shortfall. We re-scored the stored X3-syn forecasts of experiment 581 on 1,248 injected events and on the verified December load-shift, and compared the rule with the same rule fired on random days. A load-shift is a period in which part of one Primary's demand is supplied through another Primary, so the observed power no longer shows the normal running arrangement. An injected event adds such a shift to the lag inputs only. A1 and A2 are two ways of applying the wider band; the arms are defined under Results. The rule is a version of experiment 578's gate on the lags and experiment 582's union band; nothing is refitted.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms: V is X3-syn with lags; M is the same weights with lags masked; Union is the widest of both bands on every row (experiment 582's control); A1 is the union band for 7 days from the origin day a snap-back is seen; A2 is the union band while the gate is on plus those 7 days; A3 is A1 with the lags-masked median; A4 is A1 at random days (20 draws, same count per Primary).
  • Gate: own gap only (experiment 578's G1), 3 sustained days above max(3 standard deviations, 5% of capacity), reading only days at least 24 h old (newest day read: origin day minus 2). Snap-back: the newest gap day falls below half the threshold. Row set: the five fold months with stored X3-syn forecasts; 24-120 h unless stated; July 2026 unused. Retraining: none; the weights are experiment 581's.
  • Injected bank, 24-120 h, 0-7 days after the end, 15 and 30 day events (672 Primary-events, both groups), q05-q95 coverage with 95% event-bootstrap interval:
Arm Coverage after end Day 4 of the event to its end V (X3-syn) 0.826 (0.816 to 0.837) 0.844 M (lags masked) 0.876 0.882 Union (always on) 0.921 (0.915 to 0.927) 0.921 A1 0.848 (0.839 to 0.857) 0.844 A2 0.915 (0.909 to 0.922) 0.880 A3 0.848 0.844 A4 (placebo) 0.847 (0.837 to 0.856) 0.856
  • A1 against the placebo: A1 minus A4 is +0.0014 (interval -0.0002 to +0.0031, audit). The 7-day widening applies to 25% of after-end rows when it starts at the snap-back, and to 21% when it starts on random days.
  • Per group and length: the same pattern holds at the eight MVA Primaries and the six MW Primaries and at 7, 15, and 30 days (A1 within 0.004 of A4 except the six MW Primaries at 15 days, 0.871 against 0.867).
  • Tails (24-120 h, injected 15 and 30 days, after the end): NRA-side share at q05 or q95 is 0.848 (V), 0.869 (A1), 0.936 (A2), 0.941 (Union), against 0.95 nominal. Pinball at q01 and q99 and the coverage at q01-q99 are in bank_summary.csv (private data folder).
  • Verified D5 and D16 pair, after the end (descriptive; one transfer pair, not two independent events):
Event V A1 A2 Union D16 0.677 0.703 0.822 0.822 D5 0.447 0.447 0.552 0.552
  • D5 is not a detection result: its gate turned on 19 days before the event, on a gap of the opposite sign, and did not release until 14 days after the end. A2 equals Union there because the gate was on, and A1 equals V because no snap-back fell inside the window.
  • Timing on the bank: the gate triggered on 83% to 88% of events, a median 4 to 6 days after the onset. The snap-back was detected on 87% of events, a median 2 days after the end. The gate does not fire at Primaries with a high threshold (largest: 0.61 of capacity at one MVA Primary).
  • Pinball loss on days with no load-shift (24-120 h, mean pinball in points of capacity, A1 and A2 against V): at the eight MVA Primaries, q05-q95 band -0.0003 and +0.0002, q01-q99 band 0.0000 and -0.0001; at the six MW Primaries exactly 0. The half-width of the Bonferroni interval (the minimum detectable effect here) is under 0.001 for A1 and A2. For comparison, the always-on union changes the same loss by -0.007 to +0.005 and widens the 90% band by 9% at the eight MVA Primaries and 8% at the six MW Primaries.

  • Predictions: P1 holds numerically (A1 0.848, and V's band already contains the NRA on 0.844 of rows from day 4 to the end) but not because of the rule. P2 holds (extra loss under 0.001 points, under 1 false trigger per Primary-year). P3 fails: the placebo's lift (+0.021) is 94% of A1's (+0.022), not under a quarter. Bonferroni count: 16 (4 arms, 2 groups, 2 coverage bands, event-free rows).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per Primary: only 11 quantiles are stored, so the mean forecast is not stored. As a proxy, X3-syn's median minus the mean of its 11 quantiles is -0.008 of capacity on average (standard deviation 0.026), pooled over Primaries.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile contrasts: not available, for the same reason; the median's absolute error is in event_free.csv (ae50) and does not change for A1, A2, and A3 except through A3's median swap on held days.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 1 (a placebo control matched the rule). A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived every headline number from the stored forecasts with its own code, and all reproduced. It showed that the placebo performs as well as the rule, because the injected contamination is gone before the snap-back is detected. We accepted that result, and it is the main finding of this page.
  • Code review (before the first run): a fresh Sonnet review found no leakage and six issues; four were fixed (event-free rows and activity shares polluted by holds after real events, false-trigger rate understated by month-start days that cannot trigger, misleading trigger-time rows, and a point estimate that did not match its interval). Two were kept as caveats: the design limit that a rule keyed on origin day covers about half of after-end rows (valid-time phases), and the gate threshold being computed on all five months.

docs.title: Caveats and untested alternatives
docs.text:
• Width is untested: Union and A2 may gain coverage only because they are wider. A control that scales X3-syn's band to the same mean width would test this. It has not been run.
  • Only two verified events, both from one transfer pair (a load moved from one Primary to the other and back).
  • Injected events add a shift of constant depth to the lag inputs only, leaving the observed power unchanged, so the gate reads the injected lags and not a change in the power.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss events, so the event-free rows may contain events no label covers. The false-alarm loss measured on them is then too low, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Horizon: X3-syn stores 0 to 120 h. NGED cares about 1 to 10 days, so these results cover the short end only.
  • Untested alternative: a rule fired by the lags themselves (a robust z-score of the newest day lag) would act at the snap-back itself rather than 2 days later; the gate cannot see the end earlier than the 24 h age rule allows.
  • Reuse: code in ml-experiments/00583-after-snap-back-event-band-on-x3-syn/, importing experiments 578, 581, and 582; no fitted models, no new forecasts; tables in data/ml-experiments/00583-after-snap-back-event-band-on-x3-syn/.

docs.title: Does the best normal-running-arrangement forecast we can assemble (the embargoed three-step recipe trained with lag-only synthetic load-shifts, plus a wider band while a load-shift is suspected) put the normal running arrangement inside its band on 0.90 of rows after a load-shift ends, and is that more than extra width?
docs.text:
The best of the five arms keeps its 90% band (the q05 to q95 quantile range) around the normal running arrangement (NRA) on 0.93 of rows in the week after an injected load-shift ends, up from 0.76 for the earlier v3+D5 forecast. On the verified December 2025 pair of real load-shifts, the same band covers 0.84 and 0.58 of rows at the two substations (D16 and D5), below the 0.90 target.

A load-shift moves part of one primary substation's demand onto another, so the recent power readings no longer show the NRA, the power the substation would have drawn without the load-shift. A row is one forecast half-hour for one primary substation (a Primary), 24 to 120 hours ahead. We asked whether a neural-network forecast, trained on lag inputs (power readings one day and one week old) that carry synthetic load-shifts, plus a band that widens while a gate is on (a rule that fires when the lags disagree with a forecast made without them), can put the NRA inside its 90% band on 0.90 of rows in the week after the load-shift ends. We scored it on 1,248 injected load-shifts (a constant shift added to the lag inputs only; the headline rows use the 672 that last 15 or 30 days) and on the verified December pair. We compared the gated band with a band widened by one constant factor to the same mean width on those rows. The gated band reaches 0.927 and the matched-width band 0.890, so about 0.04 comes from placing the width where the gate is on, not from width alone. The arms C0 to C4w are defined under "Arms and what each one is".

Verdict: partly supported. Nothing here is adopted for production. All numbers come from the five fold months, with refits on days 0 and 14.

Day-ahead forecasts around four injected events (fixed rule: month 2025-10, the lowest-numbered Primary of each metering group, 15 days at 50% of capacity, up and down). Each of the five arms is one panel.

Other cuts (all lengths, one-sided shares, each group alone) sit beside this page as coverage90_* and nra_side95_*. Stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 hours only, so no 14-day horizon plot exists; NGED care about 1 to 10 days, so every number here is a short-lead result.

docs.title: Arms and what each one is
docs.text:
• C0: the v3+D5 forecast of experiment 572 (stored): a neural network that reads day-old and week-old power lags, with a slow output offset, refitted on days 0 and 14 of each fold month.
  • C1: the P5 recipe of experiment 574 (embargoed three-step schedule with the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns), with one new fine-tune per fold month, refit day, and seed (20 fits) in which the lag inputs carry lag-only synthetic load-shifts on 5% of each Primary's time, the recipe of experiment 581 (depths 15%, 30%, 50% of capacity, lengths 3, 7, 15, 30 days, random sign). The targets stay clean. Step 2 and the B1 statistics are experiment 574's stored files.
  • C2: C1 with the gated band of experiment 583 (A2): the widest of C1's band and the band of C1's lags-masked twin while the gate on the lags is on and for 7 days after it releases, C1 elsewhere. The gate, its 3-day sustain rule and its 24 h lag age rule are experiment 583's.
  • C3: C1 with the union band on every row (experiment 582's control).
  • C4: C1 scaled about its median by 1.0001 so that its mean q05-q95 width on event-free rows at 24 to 120 h equals C2's. C4u: the same, scaled by 1.0635 to equal C3's. C4w (post hoc): scaled by 1.081, the ratio of C2's to C1's mean width on the after-end rows of the injected bank.
