  • Event-free rows, 24 to 120 h (rows with no labelled or verified event within 7 days; 578,209 rows at 16 Primaries: the eight MVA, the six MW, and D15 and D18): C1 minus C0, month-block bootstrap at the Bonferroni level of 16 counted tests, in points of capacity. CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, estimated as 2 × the mean pinball loss over the 11 stored quantile levels): eight MVA Primaries -0.064 (-0.250 to +0.101), six MW Primaries -0.142 (-0.453 to +0.012), minimum detectable effects 0.175 and 0.233. Pinball at q05 and q95: -0.030 (minimum detectable effect 0.085) and -0.041 (-0.113 to -0.013, excludes zero). Absolute CRPS (eight MVA, six MW): C0 3.146 and 2.611, C1 3.081 and 2.465. Each contrast is the mean of five monthly differences, so it differs slightly from the difference of the pooled scores.
  • False-alarm loss of the bands (pinball loss at q05 and q95 minus C1's, minimum detectable effect in brackets): C2 +0.0001 (0.0001) at the eight MVA Primaries and 0.0000 at the six MW Primaries; C3 +0.0076 (0.0132) and +0.0050 (0.0055); C4u -0.0015 (0.0060) and -0.0016 (0.0086). The gate was on for 0.4% of event-free origin days at the eight MVA Primaries (1 false trigger, 0.44 per Primary-year) and for none at the six MW Primaries.
  • Verified December pair, 0 to 7 days after the end, 24 to 120 h (descriptive; one transfer, two Primaries):
Event C0 C1 C2 C3 C4u D16 0.479 0.824 0.840 0.840 0.833 D5 0.313 0.369 0.583 0.583 0.405
  • Real-event caveat for C1: before the event, D5's coverage is 0.428 for C1 and 0.832 for C0, and D16's coverage from day 4 to the end is 0.677 for C1 and 0.858 for C0. Experiment 574's P5 without synthetic lags, scored on the same rows as a diagnostic, gives 0.505 (D5 before the event) and 0.710 (D16 from day 4 to the end). The difference therefore comes from the P5 recipe and not from the synthetic lags. The synthetic lags raise D16's coverage after the end from 0.775 to 0.824. The gate at D5 was on for 19 days before the event, on a gap of the opposite sign.
  • Architecture and training regime: every arm is the modular lag-encoder mixture-density neural network of experiments 560 to 574 with a monotone-quantile output (11 stored quantiles). C0 is one-step fine-tuning from experiment 572's pre-training. C1 to C4w use experiment 574's three-step schedule (pre-train on ERA5 and CAMS, a fresh mixer on the whole ensemble history with a 3-day embargo, then a daily fine-tune with the embargo), where the daily fine-tune alone is re-run here.
  • Predictions:
    • P1 holds: C2 covers 0.927 against at least 0.90.
    • P2 fails as worded: C4 covers 0.860, not at most 0.85. The pre-registered control had a factor of 1.0001, so it tested nothing about width. C2 exceeds C4 by 0.067, but exceeds the stricter post hoc C4w by 0.037, which is neither within 0.03 nor at least 0.05.
    • P3 holds for C1 and C2, fails for C3: C1's CRPS is not worse than C0's. C2 adds +0.0001 of pinball loss at q05 and q95 on event-free rows, under the 0.001 threshold; C3 adds +0.0076 and +0.0050, over the threshold but under their minimum detectable effects.
    • P4 holds: D5 0.583 and D16 0.840 for C2, against 0.313 and 0.479 for C0.
  • Decision rule: coverage 0.90 or more on the injected bank holds for C2 and C3; extra event-free loss within the minimum detectable effect holds for both; a margin of 0.05 over the width-matched control holds against C4 and fails against C4w. Bonferroni count: 16.
  • Not computed: the avoidable-curtailment cost, which needs node-level forecasts with generators; BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology rows ; weekly refits.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean of the 11 stored quantiles, event-free rows, % of capacity: C0 -0.58 (eight MVA Primaries) and -0.25 (six MW Primaries); C1 -0.52 and -0.38. Only quantiles are stored, so the mean forecast is not stored.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile contrasts: mean absolute error of the median, event-free, % of capacity: C0 5.61 and 4.74, C1 5.52 and 4.47 (eight MVA, six MW). The error of the median points the same way as the quantile contrasts.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 2 (the D5 and D16 coverage of C1 contradicts experiment 581's finding that all arms covered D5 before the event on 0.75 to 0.83); the explanation was tested above with P5 without synthetic lags. P2's control failure is explained above (a degenerate factor, not a defect in the method). No other trigger fired; leaving one Primary out was not run.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet review of the fit wrapper before the first fit found no leakage or write-location problems and four lint and guard items, all fixed. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the width factor, the coverage after the end, the CRPS contrast, and the verified-pair coverage from the raw stored forecasts with its own code, and all matched. It found no leak of the injected rows into the width factors and no error in the NRA reference; its three notes (in-sample factors, two row selections, empty phases) are in the caveats. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the prose, and its findings were applied, apart from the suggestions to rename the shared figure file false_alarm_cost.svg and to expand every inherited acronym (P5, X3-syn, B1) beyond the links to the experiments that define them.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Only one verified transfer pair is in the fold months (a load moved from D5 to D16 and back, December 2025), so every real-event number is descriptive.
  • Injected events add a constant shift to the lag inputs only, so the gate reads the injected lags and not a change in the power; the injected bank therefore flatters any rule keyed on the lags.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss events, so the event-free rows may hold events no label covers. The false-alarm loss is then too low, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Horizon: stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 h; NGED care about 1 to 10 days.
  • D15 and D18 (report-only): C1's pinball loss at q95 is 2.78 against 2.50 for C0 on event-free rows.
  • Width factors were fitted on event-free rows, apart from the post hoc C4w factor, which was read from the bank's after-end widths .

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether the P5 recipe's weaker December D5 and D16 coverage is a property of the recipe or of that one pair, tested on the May 2026 transfers once enough unlogged events are ruled out, and whether a gate that reads the lags themselves, and so fires at the snap-back, lifts the day-4-to-end coverage of C2 from 0.889 to 0.90.

docs.title: Plain-language definitions
docs.text:
• Coverage: the share of half-hours at which the true NRA lies inside the stated band; a 90% band should contain it on 0.90 of rows.
  • One-sided share on the safe side: the share of readings at or above q05 (or at or below q95); nominal 0.95.
  • Pinball loss at q05 (or q95, q01, q99): the penalty for a quantile forecast, small when the quantile sits where the reading falls. Pinball loss is the score for the tails.
  • Gate: a rule that turns on when the recent power lags disagree with a forecast made without them for 3 days in a row.
  • Width: the distance between q05 and q95, in per cent of capacity.

Further definitions, with worked examples, are in experiment 582's metrics page.

Scripts: ml-experiments/00584-nra-candidate-pack-x6/ (e00584_arm.py wraps experiment 574's fit; e00584_score.py wraps experiment 583's scoring and adds the width controls; e00584_report.py prints every table above). Code reused from experiments 572, 574, 580, 581, 582, and 583. Fitted weights (.pt) and tables are in data/ml-experiments/00584-nra-candidate-pack-x6/ (private); the C1 weights are under c1/work/models/P5.

docs.title: Does the modular demand network forecast better with a different number of power lags, or with a power reading from one year earlier, when both go through the lag encoder?
docs.text:
Reading a power value from one year earlier did not lower the forecast error on all rows, and it helped only at Christmas and New Year at the six MW Primaries; it followed a load-shift event only 0.025 to 0.028 less and covered the normal running arrangement (NRA) worse. We gave the neural network that forecasts a Primary's demand (the modular demand network, with the slow output offset D5; experiment 572's v3+D5 is the control N2) more power lags and asked two questions the maintainer set as the main hope. First, does a year-ago lag, or a different number of lags, lower the forecast's leak during a load-shift event? Second, does it improve the forecast at Christmas and New Year, at Easter, and on bank holidays? CRPS on all rows (the continuous ranked probability score, in points of capacity, lower is better) is reported beside both. All numbers are two-seed means over five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) and are interim and unaudited.

Verdict: partly supported. Of the two questions, only the Christmas one has an answer in favour, and it rests on one December fold at the six MW Primaries (at 120-240 h; at shorter leads the slice also holds a January fold that goes the other way).

  • Load-shift leak: no arm helps except the arm with no day lag, and that arm is worse on CRPS. On the injected bank (a lag-only shift added to the recent lags, the real power untouched), from day 4 to the end of the event, the control follows 0.196 of the depth at the eight MVA Primaries. Y1 follows 0.168, Y1c 0.170, and Y3 0.171, but the share of NRA readings on the safe side of q95 or q05 falls from 0.770 to 0.706, 0.710, and 0.675, because the year-ago lags narrow the 90% interval by 11 to 14% and the interval then covers the NRA less. N5 follows 0.172 and keeps the safe side at 0.785. N1 (no day lag) follows least (0.116) and keeps the safe side at 0.855, and it costs 0.137 CRPS at 24-120 h.
  • Christmas and New Year: Y1, Y1c, and Y3 improve the six MW Primaries beyond the minimum detectable effect (MDE) at 120-240 h, and nothing improves the eight MVA Primaries. At the six MW Primaries, 120-240 h, the CRPS contrast against the control is −0.53 for Y1 (MDE 0.44), −0.32 for Y1c (MDE 0.07), and −0.65 for Y3 (MDE 0.05). At the eight MVA Primaries the contrasts are +0.03 (Y1) and +0.08 (Y1c), inside the MDE. Easter has no scored rows, because no fold month contains it.
  • All rows: no arm improves by its MDE. Y1 and Y1c are within 0.09 of the control at both groups and all lead bands, N3 and N5 are within 0.02 at the eight MVA Primaries, and Y3 is worse by 0.28 at the eight MVA Primaries, 24-120 h (MDE 0.18).

Under the maintainer's keep rule, a slice gain stays unless it actively hurts (worse than the control by more than the larger of 0.03 and the contrast's MDE, with the interval excluding zero, or worse in 4 of 5 folds). Y1 meets the slice route at one cell (six MW Primaries, Christmas and New Year, 120-240 h; the bank-holiday cell at the same group and band, −0.37 against 0.36, is the same December fold). It is positive in 4 of 5 folds on all rows at three cells (eight MVA 24-120 h, six MW 0-24 h, and six MW 120-240 h), which is the rule's other harm test, so no arm is kept. Y1c actively hurts at the eight MVA Primaries, 0-24 h (positive in 5 of 5 folds, +0.069, interval +0.028 to +0.116) and at the six MW Primaries, 0-24 h (+0.088, interval +0.003 to +0.214, MDE 0.048). Y3 actively hurts at the eight MVA Primaries. We also do not recommend porting Y1: its gain is one December fold, the slice route is not corrected for 4 slices times 2 groups times 6 arms, and the injected bank says the extra lag makes the tails less safe.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
• Lag. The Primary's cleaned power at an earlier time, at least 24 h before the forecast origin. The control reads a one-day lag and a one-week lag.
  • Year-ago lag. Y1 reads the power 364 days earlier (the same weekday and half-hour). Y1c reads the power 365 days earlier (the same calendar date, a different weekday). Y3 reads 357, 364, and 371 days earlier, each in its own input slot.
  • N1, N3, N5. N1 drops the day lag. N3 adds a second weekly lag, 14 days earlier. N5 is experiment 581's X3-med, stored: a median and spread of five weekly lags in place of the one-week lag (a different layout from the brief's shared encoder).
  • Follow ratio. The share of an injected shift's depth by which the median forecast moves. Safe side. The share of NRA readings on the side of q95 (event raised load) or q05 (event cut load) where a shifted forecast is wrong; nominal 0.95.
  • MDE. The smallest contrast two seeds can detect; it is printed beside every contrast. Bonferroni count 36 (6 arms against the control, times 2 groups, times 3 lead bands). Bands are 0-24 h, 24-120 h, and 120-240 h ahead.

docs.title: Load-shift events
docs.text:
On the injected bank no extra lag makes the forecast safer; the year-ago lags make it less safe. Each row below is a mean over 480 events at the eight MVA Primaries and 360 at the six MW Primaries (lengths of 3, 7, and 15 days), 24-120 h ahead, from day 4 to the end of the event. The control and N5 reuse experiment 581's stored event tables. The bank shifts only the recent lags, so it measures whether the extra lags dilute following, not contamination of the year-ago lag itself.

Arm Eight MVA: follow Eight MVA: safe side Eight MVA: 90% width Six MW: follow Six MW: safe side Six MW: 90% width Control (N2) 0.196 0.770 0.268 0.176 0.735 0.211 N1 0.116 0.855 0.262 0.110 0.816 0.203 N3 0.192 0.722 0.255 0.170 0.690 0.193 N5 0.172 0.785 0.263 0.155 0.750 0.200 Y1 0.168 0.706 0.235 0.156 0.657 0.173 Y1c 0.170 0.710 0.238 0.158 0.656 0.173 Y3 0.171 0.675 0.230 0.161 0.635 0.166
  • The day lag carries the following. N1 follows 0.116 against 0.196, which supports experiment 581's reading that the day-old lag, not the weekly lags, is the channel. N1 pays for it with +0.137 CRPS at the eight MVA Primaries, 24-120 h (interval +0.034 to +0.233, MDE 0.155).
  • Year-ago lags shave following by 0.025 to 0.028 and narrow the intervals. They narrow the 90% interval by 11 to 14% at the eight MVA Primaries and about 18 to 21% at the six MW Primaries, which lowers the safe-side share by 0.06 to 0.10. Following 0.168 against 0.196 is a gain in the median and a loss in the tails.
  • After the event ends (0 to 7 days), the arms differ little: follow 0.065 to 0.092, safe side 0.809 (Y3) to 0.874 (N1) at the eight MVA Primaries, against 0.860 for the control.
  • Real events. Experiment 581 found only one verified transfer (number 23, at D5 and D16, 29 December 2025 to 13 January 2026) inside the five folds, so these numbers are descriptive, not a test, and the unlogged-event caveat applies. Weighted over D5 and D16, 24-120 h, day 4 to the end: the control follows 0.200 with a safe side of 0.834; N1 0.130 and 0.861; N5 0.168 and 0.860; Y1 0.192 and 0.781; Y1c 0.152 and 0.769; Y3 0.191 and 0.754. In the week after the transfer ends, q05-q95 covers the NRA on only 0.488 of readings for the control and 0.424 for Y1 and Y1c (0.364 for Y3), against the nominal 0.90. No arm improves the tails there (N1 0.427 and N3 0.366 also cover less than the control). Experiment 581's table also holds transfers 24 to 26 (May 2026, D10 to D12); we report transfer 23 only because it is the one 581 used for tails. The two Primaries sit in a short December fold, and the D5 and D16 Christmas plots below show its first 3 days. Six real-event plots across both metering groups cannot be made from one transfer.
  • Y1-mask. The forecast from Y1's saved weights, with the year-ago lag set to missing wherever it lies in a verified load-shift event, differs from Y1 on 23,140 of 2,285,040 rows (1.0%). On those rows the median moves by 0.012 points of capacity on average (0.006 signed); on every other row it does not move. Contamination of the year-ago lag is therefore too rare in these folds to matter for CRPS, and Y1-mask is descriptive.

docs.title: Christmas and New Year, Easter, and bank holidays
docs.text:
At the six MW Primaries every year-ago arm improves Christmas and New Year at 120-240 h, with Y3 largest; at the eight MVA Primaries none does. Christmas and New Year is 24 December to 2 January, which in these folds is the December fold at 120-240 h and the December and January folds at shorter leads (one Christmas, split across two fold months). Entries are CRPS minus the control (points of capacity; negative is better), with the MDE in brackets. The slice route is not corrected across slices. The six MW gains at 0-24 h and 24-120 h do not hold in January: Y1 is −0.32 in December and +0.46 in January at 0-24 h, and Y3 is −0.48 and +1.50, so their Bonferroni intervals include zero.

  • Y3's gains at 0-24 h and 24-120 h at the six MW Primaries (−0.20 and −0.37) clear their MDEs (0.19 and 0.12) but not a fold check: Y3 is −0.39 in December and +1.40 in January at 24-120 h. The MDEs are small because the slice holds one or two folds.
  • Y1 (weekday-aligned) beat Y1c (calendar-aligned) at 120-240 h at the six MW Primaries, the reverse of the prediction. At shorter leads Y1c is the steadier arm (December −0.17 and −0.15, January −0.13 and −0.43) while Y1 flips sign in January. We did not test why.

docs.title: Predictions against results
docs.text:
The predictions are in the front matter; this is how each fared. A "within 0.03" claim is withdrawn wherever the printed MDE exceeds 0.03, which was every cell.

  • Y1 lowers CRPS at 120-240 h by 0.05 at one group: failed. +0.001 (eight MVA) and +0.031 (six MW).
  • Y1 does not help Christmas and New Year: failed at the six MW Primaries (−0.53, MDE 0.44, at 120-240 h), held at the eight MVA Primaries.
  • Y1c lowers Christmas CRPS by 0.10 beyond the MDE at one group: met at one cell (six MW, 120-240 h, −0.32 against 0.07), not at the other cells.
  • Y1 does not improve cold winter nights: held (no cell beyond the MDE).
  • Y3 beats Y1 by under 0.03: failed. Y3 is 0.259 worse than Y1 at the eight MVA Primaries, 24-120 h.
  • N1 is worse by 0.10 at 0-24 h: held at the eight MVA Primaries (+0.209, interval excludes zero, MDE 0.141), inside the MDE at the six MW Primaries.
  • N3 and N5 within 0.03 of the control: withdrawn (MDE above 0.03 everywhere). N5 matches experiment 581's finding at the eight MVA Primaries.
  • Y1-mask changes CRPS by under 0.03: consistent, though CRPS was not scored; the median moves by 0.012 on 1.0% of rows.

docs.title: What changed from the plan
docs.text:
• Year-ago lags use ERA5 and CAMS weather in fine-tuning, not zero embeddings. Our plan zeroed the expected-weather embeddings where the weather run is missing; 66% of fine-tuning rows had no ENS weather for the lag time, so the ERA5/CAMS pre-training table supplies it for lags of 300 days or more.
  • Easter has no rows, and N5Y1 was not run, because neither N5 nor Y1 cleared the all-rows keep route.
  • The avoidable-curtailment cost was not computed. Pinball loss and coverage at q01, q05, q95, and q99 stand in for it.
  • Forced-missing forecasts of Y1 and Y3 are post hoc.
  • Base recipe is v3+D5 (experiment 572), not the P5 recipe of experiment 574. A kept arm's survival on P5 is the next experiment.
  • Bonferroni count 36 held; the slice route is uncorrected.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Row keys. The code asserts that the stored control, the stored N5, and every new arm share identical row keys on the five months and refit days 0 and 14, and that the stored checks files show seeds 0 and 1 and the same recipe.
  • Leakage. Each lag is at least 24 h before the forecast origin, each lag's weather run is at or before the lag time, and each year-ago lag is exactly 364 or 365 days earlier; nothing after 2026-06-30 (asserted).
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the headline contrasts from stored forecasts and found the same numbers; Y3's cause is unproven.
  • A scorer bug found and fixed during writing. The first run of the holiday slices wrapped month times 100 in 8-bit integers and scored most rows as holidays; the numbers on this page come from the corrected run.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Unlogged events. NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so the "no labelled event" rows may hold events, and counts of events are lower bounds.
  • One Christmas. The Christmas and bank-holiday slices come from the December fold alone. The year-ago lag also needs 364 days of history: D15 and D18 lose it before 2026-03, and 15% of training rows lie before the start of the power history.
  • Weather for year-ago lags is ERA5 and CAMS in fine-tuning and ENS summaries in scoring for lags inside the ENS period, so the two differ.
  • Clock changes. The UTC grid shifts the local hour by one near clock changes, for 1 to 2 weeks a year, for year-ago lags.
  • Horizon and cadence. Scores are over the 10-day horizon with monthly refits on days 0 and 14.
  • Base. The base is v3+D5, not the P5 recipe.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
Whether the Christmas gain of Y1 at the six MW Primaries repeats on a second and third Christmas, which needs the long-history demand frames, and whether a gate that holds the year-ago lag back when the recent lags look contaminated keeps the gain without narrowing the tails.

Scripts: ml-experiments/00585-lag-count-and-year-ago-lags-through-the-lag-encoder/ (e00585_arm.py wraps experiment 572's fit; e00585_score.py, e00585_report.py, e00585_tails.py, e00585_mask.py, and e00585_figures.py produce every table and figure above). Code reused from experiments 397, 422, 428, 510, 511, 558, 559, 560, 565, 572, and 581.

docs.title: Does one lag encoder shared by every lag, told which lag it is reading, forecast better than one encoder that reads all lags at once or a separate encoder for each lag?
docs.text:
Take-home. No way of wiring the lag encoder is shown to beat S0 (one encoder reading all the lags at once). That holds with two lags (day and week) and with four (day, week, 2-week, and year-ago). The differences are at most 0.11 points of capacity in any lead band, and this design cannot detect a difference below 0.10 to 0.30 points. The maintainer's hunch (a shared encoder plus a lag ID is best) is therefore neither supported nor refuted. Wiring showed no detectable difference in the leak of an injected load shift either (one seed).

Terms. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score of the forecast, in points of capacity. The lag encoder is the part of the demand neural network that reads the power from earlier days. One encoder for all lags reads the lags as one input. Shared means one encoder with one set of weights reads each lag in turn. A lag ID tells the shared encoder which lag it is reading, either as a learnt 8-number embedding or as a fixed code of the lag's period. Separate means one encoder with its own weights per lag. Leak is how far the median forecast moves, in points of capacity, when the lag inputs carry an injected 7-day load shift. MDE is the smallest difference the two-seed design could detect. The eight and the six are the eight MVA Primaries and the six MW Primaries.

We asked how the encoder that reads the power from one day ago and one week ago should be wired into the demand network. Stage 1 built four rewirings of experiment 572's v3+D5 network, refitted each on the same five test months with two seeds, and compared them with experiment 572's stored forecasts. Stage 2 repeated the comparison on experiment 585's layout with four lags. The network and recipe are experiment 560's lag encoder and experiment 572's output offset, and the injected load shifts are experiment 581's bank. The verdict is inconclusive for both stages.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (S1 beats S2 by at least 0.03): failed. S1 minus S2 is +0.015 at the eight and -0.006 at the six at 24-120 h.
  • P2 (S2 is worse than S0 by at least 0.03): failed. S2 minus S0 is +0.000 at the eight, where experiment 560 found +0.070 without the offset.
  • P3 (S1 within 0.03 of S0, or better): withdrawn, because the MDE exceeds 0.03. The point estimates are +0.015 and -0.022.
  • P4 (S3 within 0.03 of S1): withdrawn for the same reason. S3 is 0.050 below S1 at the eight and 0.063 below at the six, inside the MDE.
  • P5 (S4 within 0.03 of S1): withdrawn for the same reason. S4 minus S1 is -0.039 and -0.022.
  • P6 (S1's leak at most S0's): held in seed 0 (6.59 against 7.29), but the fold ranges overlap and only one seed was run, so no difference is shown.

docs.title: Two lags (stage 1)
docs.text:
• Arms: S0 (experiment 572's stored v3+D5, seeds 0 and 1), S1 (shared encoder plus a learnt 8-number lag ID), S2 (shared, no ID), S3 (a separate encoder per lag), S4 (shared plus a fixed 9-number code of the lag's period in days). S2 and S3 are experiment 560's b_shared and b_unshared refitted on the D5 recipe. S4's code has only 2 distinct rows (day and week), so S4 against S1 compares a learnt with a fixed 2-valued identity, not richer information.
  • Weights per fine-tuned model file (including the unused pre-training mixer; excludes the knot buffer): S0 41,986; S1 42,322; S2 41,794; S3 48,738; S4 42,370.
  • Setting: coarse refits (days 0 and 14 of each of 5 fold months: 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), cleaned data, D15 and D18 cut at 2025-03-01, weather from the run at or before origin minus 9 h, day and week lags at least 24 h old, July 2026 unused. Fitted weights are in the experiment's private data folder (arms/<arm>/work/models). S1 to S4 were pre-trained afresh and S0 uses experiment 572's pre-training, so S1 minus S0 also contains pre-training noise.
  • Absolute CRPS (points of capacity, 2-seed mean, all rows), 24-120 h: at the eight S0 4.427, S1 4.442, S2 4.427, S3 4.393, S4 4.403; at the six S0 3.327, S1 3.306, S2 3.311, S3 3.243, S4 3.283. References at the eight: E2 (lag-free D5) 4.651 and M0 4.762. Every two-lag arm beats E2 by 0.21 to 0.26 at the eight.
  • Counted contrasts (24 tests; Bonferroni-widened 5-month-block bootstrap), 24-120 h, eight / six: S1 minus S2 +0.015 (-0.027 to +0.057) / -0.006 (-0.079 to +0.096); S1 minus S3 +0.050 (-0.048 to +0.214) / +0.063 (-0.036 to +0.276); S1 minus S0 +0.015 (-0.045 to +0.080) / -0.022 (-0.067 to +0.048); S4 minus S1 -0.039 (-0.088 to +0.018) / -0.022 (-0.147 to +0.065). Every counted interval in every band includes zero. The MDE beside these is 0.13 to 0.30 per contrast; the full list is in the private scores folder.
  • Descriptive: S3 minus S0 -0.035 (eight) and -0.084 (six) at 24-120 h; S2 minus S0 +0.000 and -0.016; S4 minus S0 -0.024 (interval -0.050 to -0.002, one uncorrected test) and -0.044.
  • Cold winter nights (descriptive, not Bonferroni-corrected across slices): S4 minus S1 is -0.112 (-0.207 to -0.013) at the eight and -0.089 (-0.134 to -0.002) at the six, but the slice MDEs are 0.37 and 0.39, so the keep rule does not keep S4.
  • Christmas week: only one fold (2025-12) covers it, so the slice has no interval; S3 minus S0 is -0.125 at the eight and -0.763 at the six with MDEs of 0.48 and 1.79.
  • Leak (injected 7-day shift, seed 0 only, mean over 5 folds, range): S0 7.29 (3.96 to 10.27), S1 6.59 (3.83 to 9.06), S2 6.23 (2.35 to 8.12), S3 6.08 (2.83 to 7.96), S4 6.45 (3.73 to 9.94). The ranges overlap, so no arm is shown to leak less or more than S0.
  • Injected-bank following, days 4 to the end of the event, lead 24-120 h (share of the shift the median follows; share of true readings on the safe side of q95 or q05), eight / six: S0 0.196 and 0.77 / 0.176 and 0.74; S1 0.185 and 0.81 / 0.168 and 0.77; S2 0.192 and 0.80 / 0.166 and 0.76; S3 0.215 and 0.76 / 0.193 and 0.71; S4 0.180 and 0.82 / 0.161 and 0.78. S3 follows the shift most and S4 least; no intervals were computed.
  • Tails, 24-120 h: coverage below q95 is 0.910 to 0.919 for all five arms at the eight and 0.866 to 0.877 at the six. Pinball loss at q95 at the six is 0.953 for S0 and 0.882 to 0.901 for the other four arms. Other tail numbers differ between arms by under 0.04 in pinball and 0.01 in coverage.

docs.title: Four lags (stage 2)
docs.text:
• Arms: S0w (one encoder reads the day, week, 2-week, and year-ago lags, as in experiment 585), S1w (shared encoder plus a learnt lag ID), S3w (a separate encoder per lag). Settings, seeds, folds, and data are those of stage 1.
  • Absolute CRPS, 24-120 h, eight / six: S0 (two lags) 4.427 / 3.327; S0w 4.497 / 3.345; S1w 4.494 / 3.313; S3w 4.491 / 3.264.
  • Counted contrasts (12 tests, Bonferroni intervals), eight / six: at 24-120 h S1w minus S0w is -0.003 (-0.028 to +0.018; MDE 0.099) / -0.031 (-0.121 to +0.059; MDE 0.164), and S3w minus S0w is -0.005 (-0.135 to +0.111; MDE 0.127) / -0.081 (-0.305 to +0.056; MDE 0.116). Across all 12, one interval excludes zero: S1w minus S0w at the six at 120-240 h, -0.064 (-0.135 to -0.015), against an MDE of 0.258, so the keep rule does not keep S1w.
  • Adding the extra lags to one encoder (S0w minus S0, descriptive): +0.112 at 0-24 h (+0.086 to +0.143), +0.070 at 24-120 h (+0.022 to +0.115), and +0.065 at 120-240 h (-0.034 to +0.165) at the eight; +0.017 at 24-120 h (-0.045 to +0.109) at the six. The extra lags did not improve CRPS.
  • Slices at 24-120 h (S1w minus S0w / S3w minus S0w; descriptive, one to three folds):
    • Cold winter nights (3 folds): eight -0.045 (MDE 0.312) / -0.052 (MDE 0.370); six -0.242 (MDE 0.751) / -0.093 (MDE 0.240).
    • Christmas and New Year (2 folds): eight +0.146 (MDE 0.388) / +0.132 (MDE 0.332); six -0.048 (MDE 0.709) / -0.426 (MDE 0.490).
    • Bank-holiday days (1 fold): eight -0.011 (MDE 0.526) / +0.349 (MDE 0.770); six +0.158 (MDE 0.841) / -0.322 (MDE 0.393).
    • No effect reaches its MDE. Easter has no scored days.
  • Four lags against two, S0w minus S0 (and the other arms minus S0), at Christmas, New Year, and bank holidays: S0w minus S0 is +0.123 (MDE 0.188) at the eight at Christmas and New Year and +0.321 (MDE 0.227) on bank-holiday days; at the six it is -0.085 (MDE 0.556) and -0.203 (MDE 0.516). At the eight, four lags are worse on bank-holiday days (+0.321 is above its MDE of 0.227, one fold); the +0.123 at Christmas and New Year is below its MDE of 0.188. S1w and S3w minus S0 at the eight are +0.269 and +0.255 at Christmas and New Year (MDEs 0.544 and 0.427) and +0.310 and +0.670 on bank-holiday days (MDEs 0.299 and 0.543). S3w minus S0 at the six is -0.511 (MDE 0.477) and -0.525 (MDE 0.123), and S1w minus S0 at the six is -0.133 and -0.046 (MDEs 0.213 and 0.326).
  • Injected-bank following, days 4 to the end of the event, lead 24-120 h (share of the shift the median follows; safe-side share at q95 or q05; width of the 90% band), eight / six: two-lag S0 0.196, 0.77, 0.268 / 0.176, 0.74, 0.211; S0w 0.179, 0.69, 0.238 / 0.165, 0.65, 0.177; S1w 0.158, 0.805, 0.259 / 0.140, 0.77, 0.200; S3w 0.182, 0.76, 0.263 / 0.169, 0.72, 0.200. S1w is the safest on the side of the shift, and its bands are wider than S0w's, so part of that gain may come from width.
  • After the shift ends (days 0 to 7), safe-side share at q95 or q05, eight / six: S0 0.86 / 0.84; S0w 0.80 / 0.78; S1w 0.85 / 0.83; S3w 0.85 / 0.83. S1w also keeps following the shift for longer than S0w: in days 7 to 14 it still follows 0.037 of the shift, against 0.025 for S0w.
  • Leak under the injected 7-day lag shift was not run in stage 2. The stage 2 numbers above come from experiment 581's injected bank only, and no interval was computed for them.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus the mean of the nine central quantiles, per group (a proxy, because the stored frames hold quantiles, not a mean): the median sits 0.5 to 0.6 points of capacity below that mean at the eight and 0.13 to 0.21 below at the six, and the gap is the same in every two-lag arm. The wirings therefore do not move the centre of the forecast distribution differently.
  • Error of the median forecast beside the CRPS contrasts (mean absolute error, 24-120 h, points): at the eight S0 6.289, S1 6.309, S2 6.298, S3 6.249, S4 6.270; at the six S0 5.521, S1 5.442, S2 5.421, S3 5.389, S4 5.432. S3 is lowest under both measures at both groups. The order of the other arms differs between the two measures.
  • Triggers: trigger 2 fired (S2 minus S0 is +0.000 at the eight, against experiment 560's +0.070 for b_shared minus v3). Experiment 560 had no offset and one seed, and this design's MDE at the eight is 0.145, so +0.070 lies below what this design detects. No audit was run. The leave-one-site-out check (trigger 4) and a comparison of interval widths with experiment 572's (trigger 6) were not run.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Two seeds give an MDE of 0.10 to 0.30 per contrast (0.10 to 0.22 at the eight and 0.12 to 0.26 at the six for the counted four-lag contrasts), so only a gain above about 0.1 to 0.3 could have been seen.
  • Slice contrasts have one to three folds. The Christmas and bank-holiday slices carry the largest MDEs, and Easter is empty.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so clean-lag rows may hold events no label covers. The injected bank is synthetic, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Leak is from seed 0 only, and for the four-lag arms it was not run.
  • Lead range: the scored leads are 0 to 240 h, the horizon NGED cares about.
  • Compute: process-hours were not metered, so the 3 GPU-h ceiling may have been crossed.

docs.title: How much of a load-shift does the fine-tuned demand network absorb into its forecast, with and without the slow output offset, when the load-shift is a telemetry-verified one or an injected one with a known depth?
docs.text:
We asked how much of a load-shift a demand forecast learns when its neural network is refitted on power readings that contain the load-shift. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) moves load between neighbouring primary substations (Primaries) for days or weeks, so the readings at one Primary rise and at its neighbour fall by the same amount in megawatts (MW). The size of that change as a share of the Primary's capacity is the load-shift's depth. We took one load-shift confirmed in the telemetry (Primaries D5 and D16, 2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13, experiment 580) and 12 load-shifts of known depth that we added to the readings of two connected Primaries. For each, we refitted three demand neural networks on the first day and on the fifteenth day of a month, once on readings with the load-shift and once on readings without it. We then measured how far the first fit's median forecast sits from the second's toward the load-shift, as a share of the depth: 0 means the forecast did not move and 1 means it moved by the whole depth. Experiment 565 and experiment 566 reported such shares (0.014 to 0.040 of the labelled depth) from NGED's labelled events, which experiment 580 could not confirm.

Take-home message: a refit moves the median forecast toward a running load-shift by more than predicted, and by a very different amount from one load-shift to the next. On the injected load-shifts, at the refit on day 14, the neural network without an offset (M0) moves the median forecast by 0.19 of the depth in the 7 days after the load-shift ends (95% interval 0.06 to 0.33), and the one with a slow output offset (the D5 arm) by 0.23 (0.10 to 0.38). The embargoed recipe (P5, which leaves out the newest 3 days of training targets) moves it by 0.08 (0.04 to 0.12), plus about 0.14 from its power-lag inputs, for a total of 0.22 (0.17 to 0.26). The prediction was at most 0.05. Three 15-day designs that start on day 3 carry the means: the medians over the 12 designs are 0.08 (M0), 0.11 (the D5 arm), and 0.07 (P5). The verdict "refuted" applies to the claim that the share is small; whether the offset raises the share above M0's is not settled (the difference is +0.046, with a corrected interval from -0.001 to +0.093).

Terms. M0 is the neural network with no offset and no power lags (experiment 565, arm C-M0). The D5 arm adds a slow per-Primary output offset (experiment 565's arm D5); the Primaries D5 and D16 are separate from it. P5 adds a power-lag encoder, the offset, and a three-step fitting schedule with a 3-day embargo (experiment 574). A refit trains a neural network on the 90-day, recency-weighted history up to the refit day. A design is one injected load-shift with its two Primaries. The refit share is the event's sign times the median forecast of the fit on readings with the load-shift, run on inputs without it, minus the median forecast of the fit on readings without it, over the depth. The total share runs the first fit on inputs that contain the load-shift, so it adds the effect of P5's power lags. Phases follow the forecast's valid time: before the load-shift, its first 4 days, day 4 to its end, and the 7 days after its end.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and recipe. M0, the D5 arm, and P5 as above, refitted on days 0 and 14, seeds 0 and 1, on cleaned power, with Primaries D15 and D18 excluded. Step 2 and the pre-training are the stored weights of experiments 565 and 574, which never see an injected load-shift. Weather comes from the run at or before the origin minus 9 hours (asserted by the harness), and lag inputs are at least 24 hours old. A refit on the observed power reproduces the stored forecast to at most 5e-6 of capacity, so every fit here is a refit through the stored fit's code.
  • Designs. 12 designs drawn with fixed seed 20261106 from experiment 580's bank of 358: the nine cells of depth 15%, 30%, and 50% of the smaller capacity by length 7, 15, and 30 days, each starting on day 3 of its fold month, and three 15-day designs that start on day 12. Each design has two Primary-events, 24 per arm. The bank has no 10% or 25% depths.
  • The cause of the spread between design cells is not tested. Refit shares by cell (days 4 to the end and 7 days after pooled; 3 designs per cell; mean and range). The D5 arm: 7 days from day 3 +0.095 (0.057 to 0.140); 15 days from day 3 +0.642 (0.579 to 0.704); 30 days from day 3 +0.224 (0.196 to 0.255); 15 days from day 12 +0.050 (0.012 to 0.071). M0: +0.064, +0.595, +0.142, +0.060. P5: +0.108, +0.156, +0.077, 0.000. Each cell differs in month and Primary pair as well as in length.
  • Refit share at the day-14 refit, injected designs: mean (95% interval from resampling designs). Days 4 to the end (9 designs): M0 +0.305 (0.148 to 0.483), the D5 arm +0.332 (0.178 to 0.497), P5 +0.082 (0.030 to 0.141). The 7 days after the end (12 designs): M0 +0.186 (0.064 to 0.327), the D5 arm +0.232 (0.100 to 0.378), P5 +0.082 (0.042 to 0.122). The first 4 days rest on 2 designs and carry no interval: M0 +0.114, the D5 arm +0.090, P5 0.000.
  • Medians over designs at the day-14 refit. Days 4 to the end: M0 +0.263, the D5 arm +0.318, P5 +0.047. The 7 days after the end: M0 +0.083, the D5 arm +0.107, P5 +0.069.
  • Total share at the day-14 refit. P5: +0.262 (0.189 to 0.341) in days 4 to the end and +0.219 (0.173 to 0.264) in the 7 days after the end, so its lag inputs add about 0.18 and 0.14. M0 and the D5 arm read no power lags, so their total and refit shares are equal.
  • Day-0 refit, where the load-shift is not yet in the training rows. Refit shares are 0 to 1e-8 for all three arms. P5's total share is +0.014, +0.074, and +0.136 in the first 4 days, day 4 to the end, and the 7 days after the end, which is lag following alone.
  • Contrasts of the refit share at the day-14 refit, paired by design, Bonferroni over 6 tests. The minimum detectable effect is each interval's half-width. The D5 arm minus M0: days 4 to the end +0.028 (-0.027 to +0.104; 0.066), the 7 days after the end +0.046 (-0.001 to +0.093; 0.047). P5 minus the D5 arm: days 4 to the end -0.250 (-0.407 to -0.109; 0.149), the 7 days after the end -0.151 (-0.321 to -0.021; 0.150). The first-4-days contrasts rest on 2 designs and are not interpreted. P5 minus the D5 arm contains the embargo, the three-step schedule, and the lag encoder, so it does not isolate any one of them.
  • Newest offset knot at the day-14 refit, injected, toward the load-shift (share of capacity). The D5 arm: mean +0.012, largest +0.079, with 2 of 24 Primary-events above 0.03. P5: mean +0.001, largest +0.006. The D5 arm's refit share corresponds to +0.059 of capacity absorbed on average (mean depth 0.243 of capacity), so the newest knot carries about a fifth of the movement. Which other parameters carry the rest was not tested.
  • Tail shares (refit, day-14 refit, days 4 to the end). M0: q01 +0.40, q05 +0.37, q50 +0.31, q95 +0.36, q99 +0.38. The D5 arm: +0.41, +0.38, +0.33, +0.35, +0.35. P5: +0.07, +0.07, +0.08, +0.12, +0.13. The whole forecast distribution moves with the median, and P5's upper tail moves slightly more.
  • Verified D5 and D16 pair (one pair; descriptive). At the 2026-01 day-14 refit, 7 days after the end, the refit shares at Primaries D5 and D16 are: M0 +0.177 and +0.085, the D5 arm +0.357 and +0.165, P5 +0.038 and +0.113. P5's total shares are +0.172 and +0.293. At the 2025-12 refits and the 2026-01 day-0 refit (which holds about 3 days of the load-shift) the refit shares run from 0 to 0.13, and P5's total share at the 2026-01 day-0 refit is +0.133 to +0.198. The no-event readings subtract the fitted constant depth, which carries a load mismatch of 0.017 of capacity between the two Primaries.
  • The erratum numbers of experiments 565 and 566. Their real-event shares (0.014 to 0.040 of the labelled depth) refer to events that had ended before the refit. The injected 7-day designs match that case, because the load-shift ends 5 days before the day-14 refit: M0 +0.064, the D5 arm +0.095, and P5 +0.108 (3 designs each, ranges 0.03 to 0.19). The real-event shares on those pages remain unproven, and these figures are the replacement for comparing recipes.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (at most 0.05 of depth at the D5 arm and at P5, and the newest knot at most 0.03 of capacity, for 15 and 30 day events at 30% and 50% depth in the 7 days after the end): failed for the D5 arm only. On those 6 designs the D5 arm has a mean of +0.279 (median +0.139), above the failure line of 0.10. P5 has +0.060, which is above 0.05 and below 0.10. The knot averages +0.012, below 0.03.
  • P2 (the D5 arm within 0.03 of M0 in every phase): failed on the point estimate in one phase. The difference is +0.046 in the 7 days after the end, and its corrected interval (-0.001 to +0.093) includes 0.03.
  • P3 (day-0 refit shares of 0 for M0 and the D5 arm, and P5's total share equal to its lag following): held.
  • P4 (the verified pair within 0.05 of the injected mean of the same arm in the 7 days after the end): held for 3 of 6 Primary-arm pairs. The injected means are M0 0.186, the D5 arm 0.232, and P5 0.082. The verified refit shares are within 0.05 for M0 at Primary D5 (0.177), and for P5 at both Primaries (0.038 and 0.113). They are not for M0 at Primary D16 (0.085) or for the D5 arm at either Primary (0.357 and 0.165).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not applicable, because only quantiles are stored.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile contrast: not applicable, because the measure is a difference of forecast quantiles, and all five quantile shares have the same sign.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 2 (the result contradicts its prediction) fired. A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived the shares from the raw forecast files and reproduced every printed number to 3 decimals. Trigger 5 (a nested arm beats the arm that contains it) fired in form: P5 has a lower refit share than the D5 arm that P5 contains, and the contrast contains the embargo, the three-step schedule, and the lag encoder. Triggers 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 did not fire: leaving one design out flips no sign, and dropping design 234 shrinks the D5 arm minus M0 difference in days 4 to the end to +0.009. The refit placebos (the day-0 refit, and the 14 uninvolved Primaries at day 14, which move by about 0.001 of capacity) show the shares are not fit noise.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet code review before the first run found 5 problems, all fixed. A Sonnet audit and a Sonnet write-up review (numbers and prose) followed, and their findings are applied.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One verified pair. The real-event numbers rest on one verified pair, so the injected designs are the main evidence.
  • Few designs. Each cell holds 3 designs that differ in month and Primary pair, and the bootstrap resamples 9 or 12 designs.
  • Lead range. The shares pool all leads of the forecast, up to 10 days.
  • Early stopping. The number of training epochs differs between the two fits of a design by 2 to 4 on average, and by up to 17.
  • Unlogged load-shifts. NGED's logs may miss load-shifts, so the fits on the other months can contain load-shifts that no label covers.

docs.title: How does the candidate normal-running-arrangement forecast behave, plot by plot, on verified, labelled, and injected load-shifts and on windows with no load-shift?
docs.text:
The plots show the candidate forecast (C2) covering the normal running arrangement (NRA) on more rows than the earlier v3+D5 forecast (C0) in the 7 days after a load-shift ends, and changing nothing on days with no load-shift. The NRA is the power a substation would have drawn without the load-shift. C2 does worse than C0 while the load-shift is under way and, at one real substation, before it starts.

Verdict: partly supported. The pre-registered rule said the prediction fails if P1 or P2 fails, and P2 failed at one metering group, so the prediction as a whole failed. Outcomes:

  • P1 held. C2 equals C1 on all 4 event-free windows.
  • P2 held at the six MW substations (11 of 12 designs) and failed at the eight MVA-only substations (6 of 12). The run drew one substation per design from each group, not the same two substations for every design.
  • P3 did not hold. On the December pair, C2's band is narrower than C0's on the gate-on days before and during the event, and wider only after the end (verified table).

Nothing here is adopted for production.

How to read the plots. A load-shift moves part of one primary substation's demand onto another, so recent power readings no longer show the NRA. A primary substation (a Primary) is named D2, D3, and so on. MW (megawatts) is real power. MVA (megavolt-amperes) is apparent power, and the eight "MVA-only" Primaries report only apparent power; the six "signed-MW" Primaries report signed real power. Each figure shows day-ahead forecasts (issued the day before the valid day) for one Primary, with C0 in the top panel and C2 in the bottom panel, and a key under both. Both panels draw the forecast the same way: the orange band is the q05 to q95 range (the 90% band) and the dark orange line is the median. The black line is the observed power. The pale lilac shade is the load-shift. The sky-blue bar under the C2 panel marks origin days (days on which the forecast was issued) when the gate was on, or held for 7 days after it released. The gate is a rule that fires when the lagged power disagrees with a forecast made without it. No figure draws the NRA, because it is only an estimate (observed power minus the fitted load-shift); every coverage number on this page is scored against that estimate. Where a fold month is mentioned, it is one of the five test months.

The arms. C0 is the forecast of experiment 572. C1 is the P5 recipe of experiment 584: the same network and training as C2, trained with synthetic load-shifts in its lag inputs, with no extra band. C2 is C1 with a wider band (the union of C1's band and the band of its lags-masked twin) while the gate is on and for 7 days after. The union band is that wider band.

docs.title: What the plots show
docs.text:
• Event-free days are unchanged. C2's quantiles equal C1's on all 4 windows (event-free figure).
  • After the end, C2 beats C0 on both verified Primaries. D16 0.85 against 0.33 and D5 0.57 against 0.34 (verified table; descriptive, one transfer).
  • Before and during the event, C2 covers the NRA less often than C0. At D5 before the event 0.46 against 0.80, with the gate on for the whole window. At D16 from day 4 to the end 0.68 against 0.90 (verified table). experiment 584 reports the same.
  • On injected events C2 covers more than C0 after the end in 17 of 24 examples (12 of 15 distinct cases). The exceptions are negative-sign events at D8 and D12, and one near-tie at D11 (0.991 against 0.988; injected table).
  • For labelled events that the power readings did not confirm, the band does not follow the label's dates and sign. The gate was on for 18 origin days of event 147, 6 of event 149, and 42 of event 146, and for none of the others except event 55 (labelled figures).

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Row set: experiment_470_intersection_v1, five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), July 2026 unused, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, cleaned data, seeds 0 and 1 averaged, coarse refits (days 0 and 14). Weather comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin minus 9 h, and lags are at least 24 h old. Stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 h, so NGED's 1 to 10 day horizon is not shown.
  • Descriptive only: one verified pair, 11 labelled events, and 12 injected designs, each at one MVA-only and one MW Primary. No contrast is tested. Where experiment 584 quotes a contrast, its minimum detectable effect is on that page.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss events, so the event-free windows may hold unlabelled events, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Injected events make any rule keyed on the lags look better than it would on real events, because the gate reads the injected lags and not a change in the power (experiment 583).
  • Not computed: the avoidable-curtailment cost (the cost of curtailing a generator more than a perfect forecast would require; it needs node forecasts with generators), tail tables beyond those of experiment 584, and weekly refits.
  • Injected rows are cut by the March origin mask: rows before the start and late after the end are missing, so injected coverage here is not comparable with the 24 to 120 h bank tables of experiment 584.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the script before the numbers were quoted and found no leak and no generator data. A second reviewed the write-up against the tables.

Scripts: ml-experiments/00588-nra-event-gallery-for-the-candidate-forecast/e00588_gallery.py, which wraps the code of experiments 582, 583, and 584 without editing it. Tables are in data/ml-experiments/00588-nra-event-gallery-for-the-candidate-forecast/ (private).

docs.title: Why does the observed power at Primary D5 fall inside the P5 forecast's 90% band on under half of the rows before the December 2025 load-shift, and is that specific to D5 or a property of the P5 recipe?
docs.text:
The P5 forecast does not under-cover in general. Its poor coverage at Primary D5 before the December 2025 load-shift is a level miss that all three forecasts share.

NGED (National Grid Electricity Distribution) is the distribution network operator whose primary substations (Primaries) we forecast. A load-shift moves demand from one Primary to another, here verified from the power readings with onset on 2025-12-29. A row is one forecast half-hour for one Primary, issued 24 to 120 hours ahead. The 90% band is the range from the 5th to the 95th percentile (q05 to q95) of a forecast, and coverage is the share of rows on which the observed power lies inside that band (target 0.90). We compare three forecast variants, called arms. C0 is the earlier v3+D5 forecast of experiment 572. P5 is the embargoed three-step recipe of experiment 574. C1 is P5 further trained on synthetic load-shifts, from experiment 584, which reported that P5 and C1 covered D5's power before the event on 0.51 and 0.43 of rows, against 0.83 for C0.

We asked whether that low coverage is an effect of one Primary, a property of the P5 recipe, or noise. We tabulated the stored forecasts of the three arms by Primary and month, then looked at D5 in the December fold. No fit was run. On rows with no load-shift nearby (no labelled or verified event within 7 days), P5 covers 0.884 of rows against 0.869 for C0. At D5 in the week before the load-shift, the median of every arm lies 8 to 9 percentage points of D5's capacity below the observed power. C0 covers more rows (0.83 against 0.51 for P5) only because its band is wider.

Verdict: partly supported. P5 is not under-covered in general, and D5's December miss is shared by all arms. The hypothesis said the bias sits mainly at one Primary, but other Primaries show the same sign (see Results). All numbers come from the five fold months, with refits on days 0 and 14. Nothing here is adopted for production.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Observed power at D5 (black) rose above both forecasts from early December. The shaded bands are each arm's daily mean q05 to q95.

Each dot is one arm at one Primary. D5 (event-free rows only) is in the middle of the range.

In the December fold before 2025-12-29, D5 has one of the two largest negative biases in all three arms, beside D15.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Row set: experiment_470_intersection_v1, five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 24-120 h, July 2026 unused, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, cleaned data, seeds 0 and 1 averaged, coarse refits (days 0 and 14). Event-free rows: 367,725 at 24-120 h across 16 Primaries (no labelled or verified event within 7 days of the valid time).
  • Stage 1, event-free coverage (pooled; paired difference from C0 with a 95% month-block interval over 5 months; descriptive, no test):
Group C0 P5 C1 P5 minus C0 All 16 Primaries 0.869 0.884 0.882 +0.014 (+0.007 to +0.021) Eight MVA Primaries 0.875 0.886 0.883 +0.011 (-0.001 to +0.022) Six MW Primaries 0.859 0.882 0.880 +0.024 (+0.009 to +0.039) D15 and D18 0.879 0.880 0.879 +0.001 (-0.029 to +0.022)

  • Stage 2, D5 in the 2025-12 fold (24-120 h, observed power, valid-time phases around the verified onset of 2025-12-29; share inside q05-q95 / share above q95 / median minus observed, in points of capacity):
Phase n rows C0 P5 C1 Earlier in December 3,488 0.35 / 0.65 / -9.8 0.32 / 0.68 / -9.3 0.31 / 0.69 / -9.8 7 days before onset 1,344 0.83 / 0.17 / -7.8 0.51 / 0.49 / -7.9 0.43 / 0.57 / -8.8 During the event 1,120 0.27 / 0.00 / +14.0 0.19 / 0.02 / +17.2 0.17 / 0.04 / +16.5

  • The median is below the observed power on 0.93 to 0.95 of the rows in the week before onset, for every arm. The mean q05-q95 width in that week is 23.7 points for C0 and 18.5 for P5.

  • Other Primaries show the same sign as D5: in the December fold before the onset, D5's median minus observed power is -8.9 (P5), D15's is -10.6, D12's is -6.7, and D10's is -6.4. D5 is the only Primary with P5 coverage below 0.70 in that window (0.37 for P5, 0.48 for C0, 0.34 for C1; the next lowest is D12 at 0.75 for P5).

  • D5's level rose before the event. The data alone cannot say whether the rise was weather-driven demand or an earlier unflagged shift. D5's daily mean observed power rose from about 60% of capacity in early November to about 80% from the first week of December, and all three forecasts stayed between about 65% and 76%. The gate of experiment 584, a rule that fires when recent power lags disagree with a forecast made without them, was on for the 19 days before the onset.
  • Predictions:
    • P1's first clause holds; its second does not. P5 and C1 are not below C0 on event-free rows at any group (paired differences +0.001 to +0.024). D5 is not 0.15 below C0 on event-free rows (0.912 for P5 against 0.897), so D5 is not an outlier there, and no other Primary-month is either.
    • P2 holds: the median of P5 is below the observed power on 0.93 of the rows in the week before onset (at least 0.70 predicted), and 0.49 of the observed power lies above q95 (at least 0.40 predicted).
    • P3 not run: stage 3 (a 1-day embargo) was to run only if the cause pointed at the embargo or the schedule. The cause does not point there. C0 does not use the embargoed schedule, and its median bias at D5 (-7.8) equals P5's (-7.9).
  • Bonferroni count: 0 hypothesis tests were run, so no correction applies (the planned count of 2 belonged to stage 3). Every number above is descriptive.
  • Not computed: the avoidable-curtailment cost, tail pinball loss beyond the q05-q95 band, and a 14-day horizon plot (stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 hours only, so every number is a short-lead result; NGED care about 1 to 10 days).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus observed power, event-free rows, 24-120 h, % of capacity (pooled by group, C0 / P5 / C1): eight MVA Primaries -1.42 / -0.98 / -1.03; six MW Primaries -0.86 / -0.82 / -0.92; D15 and D18 -5.72 / -8.47 / -8.25. Only quantiles are stored, so the mean forecast is not stored.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts: not stored, so the contrasts are coverage shares only, and no quantile-score contrast was run.
  • Audit triggers fired: none. We checked whether the result contradicts an earlier experiment (audit trigger 2); it does not, because it explains experiment 584's D5 finding.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet review of the table script before the numbers were quoted found no error in the join, the quantile map, the masks, or the phase definitions. Its findings on the bootstrap (unpaired intervals, a shared random generator, no check on the five months) were accepted and fixed; its note that the event-free mask differs from experiment 583's (valid-time padding only, no origin-day hold) is stated here.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One verified event at one Primary: the D5 analysis is a single case study, and the verdict on "one Primary or P5" rests on one fold month for the phase table.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so the event-free rows may hold events no label covers, and the "before" window at D5 may too.
  • Cause of the level rise unknown: the weather columns and the thermal-lag inputs were not inspected row by row.
  • D15 and D18: on event-free rows P5's median sits 8.5 points of capacity below the observed power, against 5.7 for C0, although coverage is unchanged (0.880 and 0.879). The cause was not traced.
  • P5 against C0 widths: the narrower P5 band at D5 (18.5 against 23.7 points) was not traced to its source (the embargo, the offset, or the fine-tune).

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether D5's December level rise came from the weather or from an earlier unflagged load-shift, using the weather inputs and the neighbouring Primaries' power over the same weeks.

docs.title: Does the gain from fine-tuning on synthetic load-shifts survive when the synthetic load-shift also moves the training targets, as a real load-shift does, and does it teach the network to follow shifts in its lag inputs?
docs.text:
Putting the synthetic load-shift in the training targets as well raises coverage after a load-shift ends from 0.86 to 0.90, but the neural network gets there by widening its band and by following shifts in its lag inputs about twice as much while the event lasts (1.6 times as much after it ends). A placebo that adds random noise to the lags, with no shift, covers as many rows (0.006 more than T0 in the paired contrast). On the injected bank, all of the gain of fine-tuning on perturbed lags over a neural network fine-tuned on clean lags (0.78) therefore comes from the perturbation and not from the shifts. The effect on the verified December pair is too small to read.

A row is one forecast half-hour for one primary substation (a Primary), 24 to 120 hours ahead. The eight MVA Primaries are metered in MVA only, and the six MW Primaries in signed MW. A load-shift moves part of one Primary's demand onto another, so the recent power readings (the lag inputs) no longer show the normal running arrangement (NRA), the power the Primary would have drawn without the load-shift. The follow ratio is the change in the median forecast caused by a shift in the lags, divided by the size of the shift; 0 means the median ignores the shift. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score. Experiment 584 fine-tunes a neural-network forecast on lag inputs that carry synthetic load-shifts while the targets stay clean (arm T0 here). A real load-shift also moves the target. We repeated the fine-tune with the same synthetic load-shifts also applied to the targets (T1), to half of the shifted time (T2), and replaced by random noise (T3), and scored each on the 1,248 injected lag-only load-shifts (960 of 15 and 30 days, which are 672 Primary-events in the table below) of experiment 581. Verdict: partly supported. Nothing here is adopted for production.

docs.text:
• P5 (reference, not an arm of the question): experiment 574's P5 recipe fine-tuned on clean lags, forecasting the same injected bank.
  • T0 (control): experiment 584's C1: the P5 recipe fine-tuned with lag-only synthetic load-shifts on 5% of each Primary's time (depths 15%, 30%, 50% of capacity; lengths 3, 7, 15, 30 days; random sign). Stored forecasts and weights, not refitted.
  • T1: the same schedule applied to the lags and to the targets of every row whose valid time lies inside an event.
  • T2: lag-only shifts on 2.5% of the time and lag-and-target shifts on a further 2.5%. The lag-only set is a prefix of T0's event sequence.
  • T3 (placebo): independent Gaussian noise on the lags, one draw per Primary and half-hour, with the standard deviation of the T0 shift schedule at that Primary. The targets stay clean. The noise has the variance of the shifts and not their persistence.
  • All arms: 20 fine-tunes each (five fold months, refits on days 0 and 14, seeds 0 and 1); step-2 weights (the second of the three fine-tuning steps) and the B1 standardisation statistics are experiment 574's. The target moments stay those of the clean power.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Row set: experiment_470_intersection_v1, five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 24 to 120 h, July 2026 unused, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, cleaned data. Coarse refits (days 0 and 14); the contrast could depend on the cadence. Counted contrasts: 12.
  • Two row selections. The 672-event table sets the phase by valid time, uses the 14 Primaries of the two scored groups, and keeps rows with no real event nearby. The follow table and the paired contrasts set the phase by forecast origin and include D15 and D18 (16 Primaries, 960 events), so their "both groups" rows include those two Primaries. Follow ratios are comparable only within one definition: on the valid-time rows they are 0.105 (T0), 0.183 (T1), 0.131 (T2), 0.087 (T3), and 0.160 (P5).
  • Coverage after the end (injected 15 and 30 day events, 672 Primary-events, 0 to 7 days after, q05-q95, 95% event interval):
Arm Both groups Eight MVA Primaries Six MW Primaries Mean width, % of capacity P5 0.781 (0.768 to 0.795) 0.785 0.775 22.96 T0 0.860 (0.850 to 0.870) 0.859 0.861 22.69 T1 0.896 (0.887 to 0.905) 0.897 0.894 31.52 T2 0.899 (0.890 to 0.908) 0.898 0.900 29.18 T3 0.876 (0.867 to 0.884) 0.877 0.873 22.38
  • Paired contrasts against T0, all 960 events of 15 and 30 days (a different weighting from the table above), 0 to 7 days after the end, Bonferroni level of 12 (difference, with the half-width of its interval as the minimum detectable effect): coverage T1 +0.029 (0.007), T2 +0.022 (0.006), T3 +0.006 (0.003); median follow ratio T1 +0.031 (0.004), T2 +0.011 (0.002), T3 -0.009 (0.001), where lower is better. T1 and T2 therefore beat T0 on coverage and lose on following. Plain P5 covers 0.033 fewer rows than T0 and follows 0.024 more (descriptive).
  • Following by phase, both groups (median follow ratio; 0 means the median ignores the lag shift): days 0-3 T0 0.055, T1 0.098, T2 0.073, T3 0.046; day 4 to the end T0 0.108, T1 0.202, T2 0.146, T3 0.095; 0-7 days after T0 0.049, T1 0.080, T2 0.060, T3 0.041; 7-14 days after, 0.000 for every arm. The 7 days before the event and the first days of the month have no scored origins.
  • Coverage by phase, both groups (follow table, 960 events): day 4 to the end T0 0.821, T1 0.874, T2 0.879, T3 0.836; 7-14 days after T0 0.869, T1 0.903, T2 0.902, T3 0.866.
  • Tails, 0 to 7 days after the end, both groups (mean pinball loss, % of capacity; lower is better):
Arm q01 q05 q95 q99 P5 0.209 0.869 0.969 0.268 T0 0.175 0.695 0.858 0.241 T1 0.272 0.880 1.039 0.311 T2 0.258 0.789 0.997 0.313 T3 0.172 0.675 0.817 0.228
  • Safe side of q05 or q95 (share of the NRA at or above q05 for an upward shift, or at or below q95 for a downward shift; nominal 0.95): P5 0.793, T0 0.876, T1 0.902, T2 0.907, T3 0.895.

CRPS (2 × the mean pinball loss over the 11 stored quantile levels): eight MVA Primaries T1 +0.094 (0.105), T2 +0.034 (0.080), T3 +0.023 (0.022); six MW Primaries T1 +0.118 (0.195), T2 +0.129 (0.209), T3 +0.047 (0.037). Absolute CRPS (eight MVA, six MW): T0 3.081 and 2.465, T1 3.178 and 2.572. Coverage of q05-q95: eight MVA T0 0.883, T1 0.919, T2 0.912, T3 0.882; six MW T0 0.880, T1 0.921, T2 0.921, T3 0.876. Mean q05-q95 width: eight MVA T0 21.6, T1 25.0, T2 24.1; six MW T0 17.5, T1 20.6, T2 21.2.
  • Verified December pair, 0 to 7 days after the end, 24 to 120 h (descriptive; one transfer, two Primaries): D16 P5 0.775, T0 0.824, T1 0.799, T2 0.816, T3 0.830; D5 P5 0.292, T0 0.369, T1 0.441, T2 0.284, T3 0.382. D5 before the event: P5 0.505, T0 0.428, T1 0.798, T2 0.608, T3 0.322. The arms differ by less than the spread between the two Primaries (0.284 to 0.441 at D5 against 0.799 to 0.830 at D16 for the four arms).
  • Predictions: P1 fails on both halves: T1 follows 0.031 more than T0 (predicted at least 0.05) and covers 0.029 more rows (predicted at least 0.03 fewer). P2 holds on following (T2 follows 0.060, between T0's 0.049 and T1's 0.080) and on the 0.82 floor, but not on coverage: T2 covers 0.899, above T1's 0.896, in the 672-event table, and 0.894 against T1's 0.901 in the paired contrast, so the order of T1 and T2 depends on the weighting and the two are indistinguishable. P3 fails (T3 covers 0.016 more than T0 in the 672-event table and 0.006 more in the paired contrast, not 0.03 fewer). P4 holds for T1 and T2 (within the minimum detectable effects) and fails for T3: +0.023 against 0.022 at the eight MVA Primaries and +0.047 against 0.037 at the six MW Primaries, with intervals excluding zero. P5 is not tested. The verdict "partly supported" rests on P2 (following) and P4 holding for T1 and T2, and P1 and P3 failing.
  • Not computed: experiment 587's absorption measure for T0 and T1 (it needs experiment 587's refit on shifted training power run on top of the synthetic fine-tune, which was judged more work than the main question needs); the avoidable-curtailment cost (needs node-level forecasts with generators); a width-matched control for T1 and T2; BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology rows; weekly refits.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Event-free CRPS, all rows at 24 h or more (x100): P5 3.419, T0 3.440, T3 3.470, T2 3.493, T1 3.511, so the clean-lag reference scores best.
  • Median minus mean of the 11 stored quantiles, and the error of the median (event-free rows at 24 h or more, % of capacity; eight MVA Primaries, six MW Primaries): median minus mean T0 -0.52 and -0.38, T1 -0.25 and -0.06, T2 -0.53 and -0.45, T3 -0.53 and -0.38, P5 -0.54 and -0.38. Mean absolute error of the median: T0 5.55 and 4.46, T1 5.69 and 4.59, T2 5.59 and 4.61, T3 5.59 and 4.53, P5 5.52 and 4.40. The error of the median points the same way as the CRPS contrasts: every arm is worse than T0, and P5 is better.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 1 (the placebo T3 matches the treatment T0, so the control did not behave as a null) fired. Trigger 3 did not: the error of the median points the same way as the CRPS contrasts. The explanation tested here is the plain-P5 reference (0.781): perturbing the lags in fine-tuning accounts for the gain, and a constant shift adds nothing measurable beyond it. Leaving one Primary out was not run.
  • Audit (fresh Sonnet agent, as the manager chose): no method fault found. The noise reaches the same lag columns (37 to 44) as the shifts, through the same function; T0 and T3 have identical training-row, test-row, and weather-check counts; every arm scores the same 578,209 rows. The placebo is variance-matched and sign-symmetric but not share-matched or magnitude-matched: it perturbs 0.97 of rows by a standard deviation of about 0.08 of capacity (0.03 to 0.14 by Primary), while T0 shifts about 0.07 of rows by 0.15, 0.30, or 0.50. The T3 minus T0 coverage gap is +0.006 in the paired contrast (interval 0.004 to 0.009, minimum detectable effect 0.0025), so T3 is slightly better, not indistinguishable; the unpaired 0.016 gap in the table should not be quoted as an advantage. T3 loses a little on event-free CRPS (+0.023 and +0.047). The audit could not rule out that fine-tuning on perturbed lags teaches the network to distrust its lags, which gives coverage for free on a bank whose target never moves; follow ratios are lowest for T3 (0.041), then T0 (0.049), then P5 (0.073). It did not diff the experiment 574 sources between the T0 fit (5 November) and the T1 to T3 fits (6 November), and T0 was not refitted.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the fit wrapper before the first fit: no leakage, and it traced that patching the target after the rows are built reaches every fine-tune row, including the early-stopping rows. It suggested running the schedule check for every arm and storing each arm's schedule description; both were applied. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the coverage, width, and follow ratios from the stored forecasts with its own code, and all matched to three decimals; it found no leakage and no reference or twin mismatch, and its note on the event-free row count is applied. A prose review of this page follows.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Only one verified transfer pair is in the fold months, so every real-event number is descriptive.
  • Injected events add a constant shift to the lag inputs only, so the injected bank rewards a network that ignores the lags. It penalises T1 and T2 for following lag shifts that, for a real load-shift, would be correct. The real December pair does not settle which view is right.
  • Width is not controlled: T1 and T2 cover more partly because their bands are wider, on event rows and on event-free rows. No width-matched control was run.
  • T3 is not a share-matched or magnitude-matched placebo. Its noise is independent per half-hour, perturbs about 0.97 of rows by about 0.08 of capacity (T0 shifts about 0.07 of rows by 0.15 to 0.50), and has no persistence. A persistent placebo and a placebo on about 7% of rows at shift depth are not tested.
  • T1 uses the same event schedule as T0, so the two arms differ in the targets; the T0 fits were not rerun.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so clean rows may hold events no label covers, the event-free results are optimistic, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Horizon: stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 h; NGED care about 1 to 10 days.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
Whether noise on about 7% of rows at shift depth, and a persistent zero-mean shift, perform as well as T0, and whether the network's weights on its lag columns explain the gain over plain P5 by distrust of the lags.

Scripts: ml-experiments/00590-synthetic-load-shifts-in-the-training-targets/ (e00590_arm.py wraps experiment 574's fit as experiment 584 did; e00590_score.py wraps experiment 584's scoring; e00590_follow.py computes follow ratios with experiment 581's code; e00590_report.py prints every table above; e00590_figures.py draws the figures). Code reused from experiments 572, 574, 578, 580, 581, 582, 583, and 584. Fitted weights (.pt) and tables are in data/ml-experiments/00590-synthetic-load-shifts-in-the-training-targets/ (private); the T1, T2, and T3 weights are under t1, t2, and t3 in work/models/P5.

docs.title: Does a lag encoder shared across lags, trained with an auxiliary loss that asks it to predict the depth of the load-shift injected into each lag, follow injected load-shifts less and cover the normal running arrangement better after they end than the forecast of experiment 584's C1?
docs.text:
Asking a shared lag encoder to predict the depth of each injected load-shift did not help: the forecast follows the shift as much as before and covers the normal running arrangement (NRA) on no more rows after the shift ends. In these results only the sharing helped. One encoder shared by the day-old and week-old lags raised the share of rows whose NRA lies inside the q05-q95 band from 0.860 to 0.885 in the week after an injected 15 or 30 day load-shift, at the same event-free forecast error.

A load-shift moves part of one primary substation's demand onto another, so recent power readings no longer show the NRA, the power the substation would have drawn without the load-shift. A row is one forecast half-hour for one primary substation (a Primary), 24 to 120 hours ahead. The forecast is the neural network of experiment 584 (the P5 recipe, with the lag inputs carrying synthetic load-shifts during training). We gave its lag encoder shared weights, so that one encoder reads one lag at a time, and added a head that predicts, from the encoder's output, the signed depth of the synthetic load-shift in that lag as a share of capacity. We scored five arms on the injected bank of 1,248 Primary-events (a constant shift added to the lag inputs only) and on the verified December pair of real load-shifts.

Terms used below. Following is how far the median forecast moves with an injected shift, as a share of the shift's depth. CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) is the score of the whole forecast distribution, in points of capacity. Eight MVA Primaries and six MW Primaries are the two groups of primary substations whose power is metered in MVA and signed MW. The gated band is a wider band that a rule on the lags switches on while it suspects a load-shift, from experiment 583. The injected bank is the set of synthetic load-shifts added to the lag inputs of stored forecasts, and a Primary-event is one injected or real load-shift at one Primary. Phase is the position of a row relative to an event (before, days 0 to 3, day 4 to the end, 0 to 7 days after, 7 to 14 days after). The forecasts are for NGED, the electricity distribution network operator.

Verdict: not supported. Nothing here is adopted for production. All numbers come from the five fold months, with refits on days 0 and 14, seeds 0 and 1 averaged.

Other cuts (all lengths, one-sided shares, each group alone) sit beside this page as coverage90_* and nra_side95_*. Stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 hours only, so no 14-day horizon plot exists; NGED care about 1 to 10 days, so every number here is a short-lead result.

docs.title: Arms and what each one is
docs.text:
All arms use the P5 recipe of experiment 574 (pre-train on ERA5 and CAMS weather, fit a fresh mixer on the ensemble history with a 3-day embargo, then a daily fine-tune with the embargo) and a daily fine-tune on lag-only synthetic load-shifts (depths 15%, 30%, and 50% of capacity, lengths 3, 7, 15, and 30 days, random sign, on 5% of each Primary's time) as in experiment 581.

  • A0: experiment 584's stored C1 forecasts. Separate encoders for the day-old and week-old lag, no auxiliary loss. 44,050 weights.
  • A1: one shared lag encoder with a learnt lag-ID embedding, the wiring of experiment 586's S1. No auxiliary loss. 45,475 weights, of which 1,089 sit in a head that is never trained and never used.
  • A2: A1 plus the auxiliary loss, the mean squared error between the head's output and the injected depth, times lambda = 9.085. Lambda is the ratio of the mean gradient norm of the training loss to that of the auxiliary loss on the lag-encoder weights over 20 batches (2025-10, seed 0), so the two gradients are about the same size. The heads were untrained at that point, so the auxiliary gradient is larger once they have learnt, and lambda is therefore probably on the low side of equal. The auxiliary loss is off in validation and in early stopping.
  • A3: A2 with 3 times lambda (27.26).
  • A4: separate encoders plus the auxiliary loss at lambda = 9.085. 52,980 weights, 2,178 in the two heads.
  • A5 (A2 with the head's output fed to the mixer): not run, because A2 and A3 did not help.
  • At forecast time the head is dropped. The depth labels sit in two extra columns that exist only in the daily fine-tune's training tensor, and the neural network reads them in training mode only, so validation, test, and forecast rows carry no label.
