docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean of the 11 stored quantiles, event-free rows, 24 to 120 h, % of capacity, per group (eight MVA Primaries and six MW Primaries): A0 -0.51 and -0.22, A1 -0.45 and -0.19, A2 -0.46 and -0.18, A3 -0.46 and -0.17, A4 -0.51 and -0.18. Only quantiles are stored, so the mean forecast is not stored. The gap is small beside the 6.2 and 5.3 mean absolute error.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile contrasts (mean absolute error of the median, event-free, % of capacity, eight MVA and six MW Primaries): A0 6.22 and 5.32, A1 6.14 and 5.24, A2 6.16 and 5.27, A3 6.18 and 5.27, A4 6.21 and 5.25. The error of the median points the same way as the CRPS contrasts: A1 is lowest, and the auxiliary loss adds none of that gain.
  • Triggers fired: trigger 2 (P1 fails). The explanation was tested above: the median follows the shifted lags only by about a tenth of the depth in A0 already, so the auxiliary loss had little to remove, and sharing alone moved the coverage. No other trigger fired; leaving one Primary out was not run.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the fit wrapper before any fit. The review found that the first pre-training run was overwriting experiment 574's stored B1 statistics files. The stored files were bit-identical to the backup, so no harm was done; the run now writes to its own folder and a check asserts the stored files are unchanged. The review also reported lint and guard items, all fixed.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• We found one verified transfer pair in the fold months (a load moved from D5 to D16 and back, December 2025), so every real-event number is descriptive.
  • Injected events add a constant shift to the lag inputs only, so the head reads the injected lags and not a change in the power; the injected bank flatters any detector keyed on the lags.
  • Lambda was set with untrained heads. Once the heads learn, the auxiliary gradient shrinks, so A2's effective weight may be below the intended equal-gradient setting; A3 (three times as large) bounds that and also found nothing.
  • The first-pair bootstrap has two blocks and cannot be read as an interval.
  • Unlogged events: NGED's logs may miss events, so the event-free rows may hold events no label covers. The false-trigger rates are then too high or too low in ways we cannot tell, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Horizon: stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 h; NGED care about 1 to 10 days.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a detector that reads the lags directly, instead of a head inside the forecast network, can recognise the real December load-shifts and the longer-lead rows (days 5 to 10), where following may matter more than at 24 to 120 h.

docs.title: Plain-language definitions
docs.text:
• Coverage: the share of half-hours at which the true NRA lies inside the stated band; a 90% band should contain it on 0.90 of rows.
  • One-sided share on the safe side: the share of readings at or above q05 (or at or below q95); nominal 0.95.
  • Pinball loss at q05 (or q95, q01, q99): the penalty for a quantile forecast, small when the quantile sits where the reading falls.
  • Auxiliary loss: an extra training target that is not part of the forecast; its head is dropped when the forecast is made.
  • Following: how much the median forecast moves with an injected shift, as a share of the depth of the shift.

Further definitions, with worked examples, are in experiment 582's metrics page.

docs.title: Can a faster gate, or a gate that fires at the snap-back, lift the share of rows with the normal running arrangement inside the band from day 4 of a load-shift to its end to 0.90, with at most 1 false trigger per Primary-year?
docs.text:
A gate that reads the freshest power turns the wider forecast band on about 5 days sooner. A rule that a neighbouring Primary substation must show an opposite-sign gap keeps that gate's false triggers low. On injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, the share of rows from day 4 of the load-shift to its end that hold the normal running arrangement (NRA) inside the forecast's q05-q95 band rises from 0.889 to 0.913 with the best gate, G4. The same gate without the neighbour rule reaches 0.915 but turns on falsely 2.6 times per Primary-year. The two verified December events do not change under any gate. Verdict: partly supported. Predictions P1 to P3 and P5 held and P4 held for G1 only (G2 lifted coverage by 0.014, more than the 0.01 predicted).

A load-shift is a period in which part of one Primary substation's demand is supplied through another Primary, so recent power readings no longer show the NRA, the way the electricity network is normally arranged to supply that Primary. The forecast widens its q05-q95 band (the range from the 5% to the 95% quantile) while a gate reports that a load-shift is in progress. A gate is a daily rule that reads recent power. The gate in experiment 584, copied from experiment 583, reads day-old power and needs 3 days of a gap, so it turns on a median 4 to 6 days after the load-shift begins. We asked whether a faster gate, or a gate that reacts to the end of the load-shift, closes the gap to the 0.90 target. We re-scored the stored experiment 584 forecasts under six gates, G0 to G5, defined below. We scored them on injected load-shifts from experiment 581 (synthetic load-shifts added to real power readings, 1,680 Primary-events in the stored bank) and on the verified December pair of experiment 580 (events that experiment 580 confirmed from the operator's logs and the power data). Nothing is refitted and nothing is adopted for production.

A false trigger is a forecast origin day on which a gate turns on although no load-shift is in progress. A Primary-event is one load-shift at one Primary. A Primary-year is one Primary observed for one year. A phase of a load-shift (before, days 0-3, day 4 to the end, 0-7 days after) is assigned by the valid time of each forecast row. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) is the network operator that supplied the data.

docs.title: Gates
docs.text:
A lag is a past power value used as a forecast input. C1 is the forecast of experiment 584 that reads lags at least a day old, and its lags-masked twin is the same forecast with every lag removed. E2 is the forecast of experiment 565 that never uses lags. All six gates share one threshold per Primary: the larger of 3 standard deviations of the gap and 5% of capacity, taken on days with no load-shift.

  • G0 (control): experiment 583's gate. The gap is observed power minus the lags-masked forecast, averaged over a day, from data at least 24 h old. The gate turns on after 3 days above the threshold, and turns off when the gap falls below half the threshold.
  • G1, G2: the same gate with a sustain of 2 days and of 1 day.
  • G3: one reading per forecast origin: the mean of observed power minus the median of E2, over the 40 half-hours from the previous origin up to 4.0 h before this origin (forecasts are issued at 09:00 coordinated universal time, with a first lead of 0.5 h). The gate turns on after one reading above the threshold, and turns off when a reading falls below half the threshold.
  • G4: G3, turning on only if a metered electrical neighbour (from NGED's interconnection list) has a reading of the opposite sign above its own threshold on the same day.
  • G5: G3, also turning off (a snap-back) when the reading changes sign or falls by more than 60% in one day.
  • The band under every gate is experiment 584's C2: the wider of C1's band and its lags-masked twin's band while the gate is on and for 7 days after it turns off, and C1's own band elsewhere.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Each dot is one gate. Higher is better (more rows with the NRA inside the band) and further left is better (fewer false triggers). G4 is the only gate above the 0.90 line and left of the 1 false trigger line. G3 sits exactly under G5, which has identical coverage and false triggers, so only G5's green dot shows.

Each line is the share of injected events (7, 15, and 30 days) whose gate had turned on by that day after the load-shift began. The fresh-power gates G3 to G5 turn on within 1 to 2 days, the day-old gates G0 to G2 within 4 to 6 days.

Each dot is the share of rows with the NRA inside the q05-q95 band in that phase. The dashed line is the 0.90 target. The gates differ from day 4 to the end and are equal elsewhere.

Orange marks the forecast origin days on which the gate is on, for eight injected events drawn at random with a fixed seed. The black line is the day the load-shift begins. G3 and G5 sometimes turn off before the event ends.

Each bar is the share of events whose gate turned off that many days after the load-shift ended.

Extra pinball loss at q05 and q95 on days with no load-shift, each gate minus G0, with the month-block interval. All intervals sit close to zero.

Share of rows inside the q05-q95 band for the two verified December 2025 events. The six gates give the same bars, with one small exception for G4 on D5 in other phases (see the Results).

The next six charts show day-ahead forecasts (the forecast issued at 09:00 the day before, 24 to 48 h ahead) under C1 alone and under G0, G3, and G4. They stop at 120 h because the stored forecasts go no further, so no 14-day horizon chart exists. NGED needs forecasts 1 to 10 days ahead.

The verified load-shift at D16 in December 2025. The wider band under G3 and G4 starts earlier than under G0.

The verified load-shift at D5 in December 2025.

An injected load-shift. The orange line is the true power, and the title gives its Primary, length, sign, and depth.

An injected load-shift; the title gives its length, sign, and depth.

An injected load-shift; the title gives its Primary, length, sign, and depth.

An injected load-shift; the title gives its Primary, length, sign, and depth.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Row set and recipe. The rows are experiment_470_intersection_v1: five fold months (test months 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), forecasts 24 to 120 h ahead unless stated, July 2026 unused, cleaned data, and D15 and D18 (two Primaries with a short history) cut before 2025-03-01. Seeds 0 and 1 are averaged. The forecast weights were refitted on days 0 and 14 of each month, so the contrast could change with a different refit cadence. No fit ran, so no model was saved. Reused forecasts: experiment 584's C1 (c1/work), its lags-masked twin, its injected bank, and E2 (every scored row has an E2 median).
  • Gates G2 to G5 reach a day-4-to-end coverage of 0.90 or more, and G0 and G1 do not. Injected 15 and 30 day events, 756 Primary-events with a day 4, q05-q95, 95% event-bootstrap interval: G0 0.889 (0.882 to 0.897), G1 0.896 (0.888 to 0.903), G2 0.904 (0.896 to 0.910), G3 0.915 (0.908 to 0.922), G4 0.913 (0.906 to 0.920), G5 0.915 (0.908 to 0.922). With the 3 and 7 day events added (1,092 Primary-events with a day 4): G0 0.884, G2 0.899, G3 0.910, G4 0.908 (0.902 to 0.915).
  • The gates are equal after the load-shift ends. Coverage 0 to 7 days after the end (672 Primary-events): G0 0.927, G3 0.925, G4 0.923, within the intervals of each other. The band was already near 0.92 after the end in experiments 583 and 584.
  • G3 to G5 turn on 3 to 5 days sooner. Median days from onset to the first day the gate is on, and the share of events detected (injected events of 7, 15, and 30 days, 1,260 Primary-events): G0 6 (0.892), G1 5 (0.915), G2 4 (0.956), G3 1 (0.931), G4 1 (0.905), G5 1 (0.931). The median days from the end of the load-shift to the gate turning off is 2 for G0, G1, and G2, and 1 for G3, G4, and G5.
  • G3 and G5 give too many false triggers, and G4 does not. False triggers per Primary-year on event-free origin days at 16 Primaries (4.97 Primary-years for G3 to G5; the one-sided 95% upper bound is in brackets): G0 0.23 (1.1), G1 0.68 (1.7), G2 3.28 (5.0), G3 2.61 (4.2), G4 0.20 (0.95), G5 2.61 (4.2). The rates rest on 1 to 15 triggers each and are rough. Every Primary has at least one neighbour in the interconnection list.
  • The extra loss from false triggers is smaller than the minimum detectable effect, or close to it. Pinball loss on event-free rows at 24 to 120 h, the eight MVA (megavolt-ampere) Primaries and the six MW (megawatt) Primaries together, minus G0's, in points of capacity, with the Bonferroni-level interval over 10 contrasts and the minimum detectable effect in brackets. At q05: G3 plus 0.0014 (0.0001 to 0.0038; 0.0019), G4 plus 0.0002 (-0.0004 to 0.0012; 0.0008). At q95: G3 -0.0026 (-0.0078 to 0.0000; 0.0039), G4 -0.0003 (-0.0011 to 0.0000; 0.0005). The event-free width of the q05-q95 band is 19.97 (G0), 20.07 (G3), and 20.02 (G4) points of capacity, and its coverage is 0.883 to 0.884 for every gate. With five monthly blocks, each interval is close to the range of the five monthly differences.
  • The tails improve a little from day 4 to the end. Injected 15 and 30 day events: q01-q99 coverage is 0.978 (G0), 0.985 (G3), and 0.985 (G4). Pinball loss at q05, q95, q01, and q99 is 0.707, 0.849, 0.178, and 0.226 points of capacity for G0, and 0.695, 0.808, 0.177, and 0.212 for G3. The curtailment-cost metric needs forecasts for a node and its generators, so it is not computed here.
  • The verified December pair does not change. Two Primary-events, descriptive. From day 4 to the end, D16's coverage is 0.685 under every gate, although the share of origin days with the gate on or held rises from 0.64 (G0) to 0.89 (G3, G4, G5). D5's coverage is 0.868 under every gate and 0.583 after the end. D5's gate was already on, or held, before the event under G0 to G3 and G5 (share of origin days 1.0 for G0 to G2 and 0.86 for G3 and G5) and never on under G4 (0.0). G4 differs a little from the other gates on D5 elsewhere (days 0-3 coverage 0.493 against 0.498).
  • G3 and G5 sometimes turn off inside an event. The share of injected events (7, 15, and 30 days) whose gate turned off at least once before the event's end is 0.007 (G0), 0.013 (G1), 0.042 (G2), 0.131 (G3), 0.122 (G4), and 0.207 (G5).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast per site: not applicable, because every gate selects one of two stored bands and keeps C1's median. The median and its error are identical across gates, so the contrasts are in band coverage and quantile loss only.
  • Reproduction: G0 under this experiment's scorer reproduces experiment 584's C2 coverage exactly (largest difference 0.0 over 10,440 injected rows and 28 verified-event rows).
  • The seven triggers of the audit rule in the ml-experiment skill: none fired. No control failed, no nested arm beat the arm that contains it, and G3 and G5 are equal. A leave-one-Primary-out check of the false-trigger counts was not run.
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet reviewer read the code before the first run that fed this page. The findings were triaged. The month-edge treatment of the fresh reading was made uniform, the false-trigger table gained a "with a neighbour" row, the G0 reproduction check was added, the uncounted intervals are labelled, and two docstrings were corrected.
  • Bias of the fresh reading: on days when no gate is on, the mean fresh reading is at most 0.17 of the threshold (median 0.06), so the raw reading and the threshold agree.
  • Write-up reviews: a numbers review and a prose review ran on this page; the findings were applied (the D5 statement, the count of Primary-events, and the order of the sections).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The mirrored neighbour is idealised. In the injected events, one metered neighbour (chosen by the pass number plus the Primary number, modulo the number of neighbours) receives exactly the opposite load, scaled by capacity. The capacity ratio mixes megawatt and megavolt-ampere ratings. Real load-shifts may be split over several Primaries, or go to a neighbour without a meter.
  • The false-trigger sample is 4.97 Primary-years. One false trigger is 0.20 per Primary-year, so "at most 1" holds for G4 with a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.95.
  • The two verified events are 2 Primary-events. Their coverage did not move, so the injected-bank gain is not confirmed on real events. NGED may have load-shifts missing from its logs, so clean rows may hold unlogged events, the false-trigger counts may include real events, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • The injected load-shifts act on the day-old gate as whole days and on the fresh gate to the half-hour, as in experiment 583 for the day-old gate. A partial first day slightly favours G0 to G2.
  • The bank count differs from the brief. The brief quoted 1,248 injected Primary-events; the stored bank holds 1,680 (420 each of 3, 7, 15, and 30 days), and each phase scores fewer events because a phase needs at least 60 forecast rows.
  • The lead range is 0 to 120 h, shorter than the 1 to 10 days NGED uses, so every number here is a short-lead result.
  • The threshold is set from the same data that scores the gates, as in experiment 583, so the false-trigger rates are optimistic.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Options include testing G4 on real load-shifts beyond the December pair, and on a neighbour whose real data mirror the shift.
  • A rule that needs two quiet readings before the gate turns off would stop G3 and G5 turning off inside an event (13% and 21% of events).
  • Counting false triggers over a longer event-free history would tighten the rates.

docs.title: Does the coverage gain from fine-tuning on synthetic load-shifts come from the shape of the shifts or from distrust of the lags in general? Two placebos that match the shifts' rows, size, and persistence.
docs.text:
On the lag-only injected bank, noise on the same rows as the synthetic load-shifts, and shifts whose sign flips every day, give the same coverage after an injected load-shift ends as the synthetic load-shifts themselves (the NRA lies inside the q05-q95 band on 0.86 of rows for all three, against 0.78 for a neural network fine-tuned on clean lags). The coverage gain therefore probably comes from teaching the neural network to distrust its lags on about 7% of rows, and not from the shape of a load-shift. The gain is not specific to persistent shifts, so fine-tuning on synthetic shifts is one recipe among several that give the same result on this injected bank.

Terms. A row is one forecast half-hour for one primary substation (a Primary), 24 to 120 hours ahead. The eight MVA Primaries are metered in MVA only, and the six MW Primaries in signed MW. A load-shift moves part of one Primary's demand onto another, so the recent power readings (the lag inputs) no longer show the normal running arrangement (NRA), the power the Primary would have drawn without the load-shift. Coverage is the share of rows with the NRA inside the q05-q95 band, the band between the 5% and 95% quantiles of the forecast (target 0.90). The injected bank is a set of artificial lag-only load-shifts, 3 to 30 days long, added to the lags of past data. The follow ratio is the change in the forecast median caused by a shift in the lags, divided by the size of the shift (0 means the median ignores the shift).

The arms.

  • P5: experiment 574's neural network fine-tuned on clean lags.
  • C1 (called T0 in the tables): experiment 584's fine-tune on lags that carry synthetic load-shifts on 5% of each Primary's time, with clean targets.
  • T3: experiment 590's fine-tune on lags with non-persistent noise on 97% of rows. T3 matched C1's coverage but differs from C1 in the share of rows, the size of the perturbation, and persistence.
  • PS (P-share): C1's event rows, with independent Gaussian noise on every half-hour whose standard deviation equals the event's depth (0.15, 0.30, or 0.50 of capacity).
  • PP (P-persist): C1's event rows, with a shift of the event's depth whose sign is drawn independently for every day of the event.

Both placebos were scored on the injected load-shifts of experiment 581.

Verdict: partly supported, and nothing here is adopted for production. The pre-registered predictions were P1: PS covers at least 0.03 fewer rows than C1 after the end (failed; the difference is 0.002); P2: PP covers within 0.02 of C1 (held); P3: event-free CRPS of both placebos is within the minimum detectable effect of C1 (held).

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Coverage of the NRA 0 to 7 days after the end; T0, PS, and PP differ by under 0.003 and sit above P5.

Coverage by phase; the placebos track T0 in every phase.

Follow ratio of the median by phase (0 means the median ignores the shift in the lags).

Coverage against band width after the end; PS and PP are 0.3 points of capacity wider than T0.

Tail pinball loss after the end.

Event-free CRPS, coverage, and tail loss against T0; the placebos are within the intervals of zero.

The next six figures are example forecasts: day-ahead forecasts around four injected events (month 2025-10, the lowest-numbered Primary of each metering group, 15 days at 50% of capacity, up and down) and around the verified December pair.

Stored forecasts cover 0 to 120 hours only, so no 14-day horizon plot exists. NGED care about 1 to 10 days, so every number here is a short-lead result.

docs.title: Headline numbers
docs.text:
Two definitions of "after the end" appear below, and both are in the printed report. The paired contrasts and the follow table set the phase by the forecast origin and cover 960 events, which include the report-only Primaries D15 and D18 (T0 0.872). The per-arm coverage table sets the phase by the valid time and covers 672 events without them (T0 0.860). The two give the same ordering of arms.

All numbers come from report.txt (script e00594_report.py). Counted contrasts: eight, intervals at the Bonferroni level for eight tests; the minimum detectable effect (MDE) is the interval half- width.

  • Coverage 0 to 7 days after the end (unpaired, 672 Primary-events, 15 and 30 days): P5 0.781, T0 0.860, PS 0.858, PP 0.864, T3 0.876. Band width 22.7 (T0), 23.0 (PS), 23.0 (PP), 22.4 (T3), 23.0 (P5) % of capacity.
  • Paired contrast against T0 (960 events, both groups): PS -0.0021 (-0.0036 to -0.0005, MDE 0.0015); PP +0.0001 (-0.0018 to 0.0019, MDE 0.0018). Pre-registered threshold: 0.01. T3 +0.0061 and P5 -0.0328 (not counted).
  • Follow ratio of the median 0 to 7 days after the end: T0 0.049, PS 0.053 (+0.0041, MDE 0.0005), PP 0.052 (+0.0026, MDE 0.0007), T3 0.041, P5 0.073. Both placebos follow the lags slightly more than C1, by under 0.005 of the depth (17% of the gap between C1 and P5 for PS, 11% for PP), so shape has a small measurable effect on following, though not on coverage.
  • Safe-side share (NRA below q95 for an upward shift, above q05 for a downward one): T0 0.911, PS 0.908, PP 0.911, T3 0.920, P5 0.875 (paired table, both groups; target 0.95).
  • Tails after the end (pinball x100, both groups, unpaired): q01 / q05 / q95 / q99 for T0 0.175 / 0.695 / 0.858 / 0.241, PS 0.176 / 0.699 / 0.877 / 0.245, PP 0.175 / 0.692 / 0.870 / 0.243.
  • By metering group (coverage after the end, paired diff against T0): eight MVA Primaries PS -0.0033, PP -0.0014; six MW Primaries PS -0.0014, PP +0.0012. The sign of PS is negative in both groups; the sign of PP changes between groups, and PP's intervals include zero everywhere.
  • Event-free rows (24-120 h, 578,209 rows, five fold months): CRPS (points of capacity x100) at the eight MVA Primaries T0 3.081, PS 3.078 (-0.003, MDE 0.009), PP 3.082 (+0.000, MDE 0.012); at the six MW Primaries T0 2.465, PS 2.460 (-0.004, MDE 0.012), PP 2.463 (-0.001, MDE 0.015). Coverage of q05-q95 on event-free rows: T0 0.883 (MVA), 0.880 (MW); PS and PP within 0.002. T3 raises CRPS by 0.023 (MVA) and 0.047 (MW), with the interval excluding zero.
  • Verified December pair (two Primary-events, too few to separate arms): after-end coverage D16 0.824 (T0), 0.825 (PS), 0.827 (PP); D5 0.369, 0.332, 0.345.
  • Events: the schedule of each placebo equals C1's: 45 to 58 events per fold month, about 7% of rows with a changed day lag (0.064 to 0.072). The mean absolute net shift over an event, as a share of its depth, is 0.03 to 0.04 for PS and 0.25 to 0.28 for PP (short events have few daily blocks, so PP's net shift is small but not zero).
  • Choice of block length: the experiment's brief asks for the sign to be "drawn per half-hour block". We used blocks of one day (48 half-hours), because a sign drawn for every single half-hour would make the shift average out to noise, as PS already does.
  • Refit schedule and settings: coarse refits on day 0 and day 14 of each of five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), seeds 0 and 1, experiment 574's P5 recipe, stored weights and rows reused. Fitted weights are in the private data folder (00594-.../ps/work/ and pp/work/). The training rows, power cleaning, and row cuts are experiment 574's, unchanged.
  • Reuse: C1 from experiment 584, T3 and P5 from experiment 590; code copied from experiment 590's folder.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: not computed for this experiment.
  • Error of the median beside the quantile contrasts: the follow ratio of the median is the median contrast; the median forecast's follow ratio moves under 0.005 of the depth while coverage moves under 0.003, so both contrasts are small.
  • Triggers: trigger 2 fired (a result contradicts its own prediction: P1 predicted PS 0.03 below C1, observed 0.002 below). The audit is triaged under Caveats.
  • Curtailment cost: not computed; this experiment scores coverage after injected events, not curtailment.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Audit. Trigger 2 fired, and a fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the coverage and CRPS numbers exactly (report e594_audit.md in the private briefs folder). It found no wiring bug: the 20 weight files per arm differ, the placebo schedule equals C1's, and the noise has the stated spread. Triage: accepted the two-definitions note, the scoped headline, and the caveats below.
  • The bank rewards any lag distrust. Coverage orders the arms the same way as the follow ratio (T3 has the lowest following and the highest coverage), so the likeliest reason the placebos match C1 is that any training that makes the lags look unreliable helps on this bank. The experiment cannot separate that from learning the shape of a shift.
  • PP is not a pure persistence test. Its shift persists for one day at a time, not for 15 to 30 days.
  • Small fine-tune. Every arm moves 2% to 3% (relative L2 distance) from P5's weights and the placebos sit 0.9% from C1's, so a small lag encoder may have room for one global "trust the lags less" setting. A longer fine-tune or a larger encoder was not tested.

  • Intervals are too narrow. The event bootstrap treats 960 events as independent, but they share 20 fine-tuned models, so the PS interval that excludes zero (-0.0036 to -0.0005) should not be read as an effect. It is 15 times smaller than the predicted 0.03.

  • The injected bank adds a constant lag-only shift, which rewards any lag distrust. It cannot tell a network that recognises a persistent shift from one that distrusts lags on some days. A real load-shift also moves the target and is mirrored at neighbouring Primaries; the verified December pair has two Primary-events only.

  • NGED's logs may miss load-shifts, so clean-lag rows may hold events no label covers; the event- free rows are therefore optimistic and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Seeds 0 and 1 only, five fold months, coarse refits. The 14-day horizon is not stored.

docs.title: Options for later experiments
docs.text:
• Scoring the placebos on an event they cannot imitate, such as a persistent shift mirrored at neighbouring Primaries, or more verified real load-shifts, would test the shape of the shift.
  • Varying the share of perturbed lag rows (for example 2%, 7%, and 15%) with noise alone would test whether that share is the active ingredient. The share is held fixed here, as are the event lengths and depths.

docs.title: When a load-shift sits in the training power itself, how much of its depth does the fine-tuned demand neural network absorb into its median forecast if it reads power lags through the P5 recipe fine-tuned on synthetic lag-only shifts (C1), or through a shared lag encoder (A1)?
docs.text:
The two release-candidate demand neural networks, C1 and A1, still learn a load-shift from the power readings they are refitted on, but less than plain P5 does. A load-shift moves load between neighbouring primary substations (Primaries) for days or weeks. Its depth is its size as a share of the Primary's capacity. As in experiment 587, we added 12 load-shifts of known depth to the readings of two connected Primaries, refitted each network on the first day and the fifteenth day of a month, and measured how far the median forecast moves toward the load-shift compared with a refit on readings without it. A value of 0 means the forecast did not move and 1 means it moved by the whole depth. C1 is P5 fine-tuned on synthetic shifts in its lag inputs (experiment 584). A1 shares one lag encoder across the lags and adds a lag-identity embedding, with the same synthetic-shift fine-tuning (experiment 591). P5 is the same network without the synthetic shifts. M0 has no offset and no lags, and D5 adds the slow output offset (both from experiment 587). Every share below is at the median forecast (q50) unless a tail quantile is named.

Take-home message: C1 and A1 lower the leak a little but do not reach 0.10. Seven days after an injected load-shift ends, at the day-14 refit, the median forecast still sits 0.168 (95% interval 0.121 to 0.213) of the depth toward the shift for C1 and 0.160 (0.099 to 0.221) for A1. Plain P5 gives 0.219 (0.174 to 0.262). Both pre-registered predictions (at least 0.15) held. The hypothesis, that the two arms absorb no less than P5, failed for the total share and held for the refit share. The drop from P5 is 0.051 for C1 (Bonferroni interval -0.070 to -0.032; minimum detectable effect 0.019) and 0.059 for A1 (-0.114 to -0.010; minimum detectable effect 0.052). The refit alone moves the median by 0.089 (C1), 0.084 (A1), and 0.082 (P5) of the depth, a difference from P5 of at most 0.007 that we did not test. Total minus refit leaves a lag part of 0.137 (P5), 0.079 (C1), and 0.076 (A1), which matches the day-0 lag following. The proposed bar L4 (at most 0.10) is therefore a concern for both candidates. The next experiment should test a training change, such as dropping or down-weighting the newest training rows during a suspected load-shift.

Figure 1. Share of the depth that the median forecast moves toward an injected load-shift, day-14 refit, 12 designs (2 designs in the first 4 days). Dot: mean over designs; line: 95% interval from resampling designs. Top panel: the refit alone; bottom panel: the refit and the lag inputs.

Figure 2. Four injected load-shifts. Each arm's day-ahead median (daily mean) against the observed power and the power without the shift (the normal running arrangement). Shaded: the shift.

Figure 3. The one verified real transfer (D5 and D16, December 2025). Descriptive only.

  • Arms. C1 and A1 fitted with the code of experiments 584 and 591 on the injected power; M0, D5, and P5 read from experiment 587's stored forecasts (same designs, folds, seeds, refit days). No arm other than C1 and A1 was refitted. Code folders reused: 574, 581, 584, 587, 591.
  • Total share at q50, day-14 refit, mean over designs (95% interval). First 4 days (2 designs): M0 0.114, D5 0.090, P5 0.094, C1 0.060, A1 0.069. Day 4 to the end (9 designs): M0 0.305, D5 0.332, P5 0.262, C1 0.195 (0.121 to 0.272), A1 0.189 (0.105 to 0.288). 7 days after the end (12 designs): M0 0.186, D5 0.232, P5 0.219, C1 0.168, A1 0.160. Medians over designs after the end: P5 0.224, C1 0.173, A1 0.141.
  • Refit share, 7 days after the end. C1 0.089 (0.047 to 0.133), A1 0.084 (0.041 to 0.131), P5 0.082 (0.042 to 0.122).
  • Day-0 refit (the shift is not in the training rows). The total share is the lag following alone: 7 days after the end, P5 0.136, C1 0.075, A1 0.077 (6 designs). The synthetic shifts lower the lag following by about 45% (descriptive, outside the 6 counted tests).
  • Contrasts. Counted tests: 6 (C1 minus P5 and A1 minus P5, in three phases, total share, day-14 refit). C1 minus P5: -0.034 (2 designs), -0.067 (9 designs; minimum detectable effect 0.027), -0.051 (12; 0.019). A1 minus P5: -0.025, -0.073 (0.070), -0.059 (0.052). A1 minus C1 (descriptive): -0.008 after the end (-0.040 to +0.020; 0.030), so the two candidates cannot be told apart.
  • Tails, total share 7 days after the end. q01 / q05 / q95 / q99: P5 0.163 / 0.176 / 0.285 / 0.291; C1 0.122 / 0.133 / 0.251 / 0.265; A1 0.120 / 0.134 / 0.223 / 0.243. The upper tails move further than the median for every arm.
  • Design cells (total share pooled over day 4 to the end and the 7 days after). The 15-day designs that start on day 3 have the highest share (P5 0.357, C1 0.286, A1 0.296); the 15-day designs that start on day 12 give 0.122, 0.064, and 0.065.
  • Verified D5/D16 pair (descriptive, 2026-01 day-14 refit, 7 days after the end, total / refit). Primary D5: P5 0.172 / 0.038, C1 0.138 / 0.041, A1 0.141 / 0.051. Primary D16: P5 0.293 / 0.113, C1 0.240 / 0.104, A1 0.189 / 0.111.
  • Checks. The q50 forecast of each new arm's refit on the observed power matches the stored fit of experiments 584 and 591 to 2e-6 (mean 1e-8). Cells with fewer than 48 half-hours are dropped (6). The score is a share of q50 differences, not a quantile score, so there is no median-minus-mean or CRPS contrast to audit; the audit triggers for score contrasts do not apply.
  • Caveats. Injected shifts are not real ones; the real evidence is one pair. Two seeds. Only 2 designs fall in the first 4 days, so that phase has wide uncertainty. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so the clean rows may hold unlabelled events and the shares here describe injected shifts only. Weather at lag times: none is used by the share measure; the forecasts use the ENS run issued at least 9 h before the forecast origin, as in 587. Nothing is adopted.
  • What to try next. (1) Test a training-side change that targets the refit share (0.08 to 0.09): an embargo of the newest rows once a gate fires, or down-weighting rows near a detected shift. (2) Repeat the measurement for the gated candidate C1 plus G4 once it is assembled.
  • Reviews. One fresh Sonnet code review before the first fit found no blocking issue and four minor ones (all fixed). A fresh Sonnet write-up review is recorded in the pull request.
  • Data and compute. Forecasts and fitted weights are in the private folder data/ml-experiments/00595-nra-target-side-absorption-for-p5-lag-encoder-with-synthetic-shifts/ (work/<arm>/<world>/work/{fits,models}; scores in scores/). Fits took about 0.4 GPU-h in total, one process at a time.

docs.title: Do the May 2026 load-shift transfers show up in the readings, and can they serve as a second real test of the candidate forecast?
docs.text:
Take-home message: the four May 2026 load-shifts do not show up as a gap between the observed power and a forecast that reads no lags, so they cannot serve as a second real test. We asked whether the transfers that NGED logged for May 2026 (at the primary substations, called Primaries, D10, D11, D12, and D16) leave the signature a real transfer should leave. A forecast that reads no recent power cannot know about a transfer, so inside the event the observed power should sit about one fitted depth away from that forecast. We measured the gap at 24 to 120 hours ahead, after taking away the gap in the following week. We compared the result with the gaps that the same Primary shows on days with no transfer. No event passes. The prediction written first, that D10, D11, and D16 would not pass, held. The experiment's verdict is "not supported" because the hypothesis expected at least one pass. Because none passed, no fine-tune ran, no GPU was used, and the candidate forecast (the C1 forecast of experiment 584 with the G4 band of experiment 592, which widens the band when a load-shift looks likely) was not scored on May 2026. Here the normal running arrangement (NRA) is the power a Primary would draw with no load-shift.

Primary Fitted depth (share of capacity) Measured gap S S as a share of depth (rule: 0.5 to 1.5) Placebo 95th percentile of |S| (rule: S must exceed it) Passes D10 +0.153 +0.010 0.07 0.156 No D11 +0.106 +0.039 0.37 0.106 No D12 (three transfers merged) -0.426 -0.014 0.03 0.253 No D16 +0.143 +0.028 0.20 0.045 No

Each event fails both the size test and the placebo test. The placebo distributions hold 108, 107, 79, and 34 windows for the four Primaries. The transfer test (a passing Primary on each side) was never reached. No contrast was tested, so there is no Bonferroni count (the correction for running several tests) and no minimum detectable effect to report.

The dashed line is the gap the fitted depth predicts. The measured gap stays near zero. At D16 it comes within about a quarter of the depth on only 4 days (11 to 14 May).

D12's power steps down on about 3 May and back up on about 22 May. D16's power rises on 11 May, not on 4 May, so the pair does not mirror on the labelled dates. D10 and D11 show no clear step.

An event passes only if the orange bar reaches half the grey bar and exceeds the blue bar.

docs.title: What to ask NGED
docs.text:
• Which Primaries exchanged load in May 2026, and on which days? The labelled dates (D12 from 3 to 21 May, D16 from 4 to 22 May, D10 from 11 to 21 May, D11 from 12 to 22 May) do not match a mirrored pair in the readings.
  • How large was each transfer in megawatts? The fitted depths come from steps in the telemetry, and the depth of D12 combines three overlapping transfers.
  • Did D12 change its running arrangement on about 3 May and about 22 May? The observed power at D12 steps down by about 0.22 of capacity on the first date and up by 0.13 to 0.22 on the second (see the second figure), but it returns near its old level on 7 to 10 May, and no Primary mirrors the steps. This is an observation, not a finding. D12's gap to the lag-free forecast is positive on most days, so the negative S comes only from the week after the span.

docs.title: Caveats and what was not done
docs.text:
• The lag-free forecast carries a level bias (experiment 589 found 5 to 9 points of capacity at D5 in December 2025), which is why the rule subtracts the following week's gap. A different reference window could change a ratio, so the rule's verdict is for this window only.
  • NGED's logs may miss events, so the readings may hold transfers no label covers.
  • Not done: the fine-tunes of C1 and A1 for 2026-05, the scoring of C1 plus G4, and any measurement of when G4 fires on a May event. Without a confirmed event, scores on May 2026 would measure a forecast against a target that the readings do not show.
  • Sources. Pass rule, placebo, and check table: this folder and ml-experiments/00596-nra-may-2026-transfers-recheck-and-second-real-event/e00596_check.py. Forecasts and transfers: experiment 582 and experiment 580, which reuse the code of experiments 400, 565, 572, and 578. The level bias comes from experiment 589.

docs.title: Pass rule (fixed before any gap was computed, 2026-11-06)
docs.text:
Rule. For each Primary-event (D10, D11, D12, and D16, from the events_verified table of experiment 580, with D12's three overlapping transfers merged as in experiment 582), using the lag-free D5 median at 24 to 120 h lead:

  1. Signal. S is the mean of (observed power minus lag-free median) over the rows whose valid time lies from 1 day after the onset to 1 day before the end, minus the same mean over the 7 days that start 1 day after the end. All values are shares of effective capacity.
  2. Sign and size. The event passes only if S has the sign of the fitted depth and S lies between 0.5 and 1.5 times the depth.
  3. Placebo. |S| must also exceed the 95th percentile of |S| for the same Primary and the same span length, computed over placebo windows slid by one day across the fold months that have lag-free forecasts and lie more than 7 days from every verified transfer.
  4. Transfer. A transfer passes when the Primary on each side passes, the two signals have opposite signs, and the signed MW differ in sum by less than 30% of the larger. D12 enters with its merged depth, and the three May transfers are judged through D10, D11, and D16 against D12.
  5. Neighbours. For each passing transfer, the daily mean of the partner Primary is plotted beside it, to look for the mirror by eye.

The lag-free forecast carries a level bias of 5 to 9 points of capacity in December 2025 (experiment 589), which is why the signal subtracts the same gap after the span.

Reported whatever the outcome: the table of S, depth, ratio, placebo p95, and verdict per Primary-event; time series plots of observed power, lag-free median, and the fitted NRA at all four Primaries, with the span marked; the daily means of the neighbouring Primaries. The caveat that NGED's logs may miss events applies throughout. July 2026 is not used.

docs.title: Do C1 and A1 with the G4 gated band, assembled as single forecasts, hold the normal running arrangement inside the q05-q95 band on 0.90 of rows from day 4 of a load-shift to its end?
docs.text:
We assembled two single forecasts from stored parts and tested them without any new fit. On the injected load-shifts, both hold the normal running arrangement (NRA) inside the q05-q95 band on at least 0.91 of rows from day 4 of a load-shift to its end, with pinball loss at q05 and q95 on event-free rows within the minimum detectable effect. The median still follows about 0.11 of the shift, and the two real December 2025 events show gaps that the injected shifts do not. Verdict: supported. All four pre-registered predictions held: P1 reproduced (difference 0.000000), P2 held (A1 + G4 0.928), P3 held, and P4 held for C1.

A load-shift moves part of one Primary substation's demand onto a neighbour for days or weeks, so recent power readings stop showing the NRA, the way the electricity network is normally arranged to supply that Primary. Earlier experiments built the parts of a forecast that copes with this: the C1 neural network (experiment 584), the A1 neural network with a shared lag encoder (experiment 591), and the G4 rule that widens the band (experiment 592). None of the three experiments joined the parts and scored the result as one forecast. We did, and we exported both forecasts for others to score. Nothing is adopted for production.

How the forecast is assembled. The median is the neural network's own median. While the G4 gate is on, and for 7 days after the G4 gate turns off, every quantile is the widest of the network's value and the value of its lags-masked twin (the same weights with every lag removed). On other days the quantiles are the network's own. G4 reads three inputs: observed power up to 4.0 hours old, the lag-free neural network E2, and a mirrored opposite-sign gap at a neighbouring Primary. The state is therefore the same for C1 and A1. The rebuilt state equals experiment 592's stored state exactly.

docs.text:
Share of rows with the NRA inside q05-q95, on injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, by phase. Dot: mean over Primary-events. Line: 95% interval from resampling events. Dashed line: the 0.90 target. Grey and sky blue are the plain neural networks; orange and blue are the assembled forecasts. The gated band lifts coverage in the two phases where the gate is on, and changes nothing 7 to 14 days after the end.

Share of rows with the NRA on the safe side of q05 or q95: below q95 when the shift lowered the load, above q05 when it raised it. Dashed line: the 0.95 target.

This figure repeats the first figure for all injected events (3, 7, 15, and 30 days). Only the 3 and 7 day events have rows before the shift and in days 0 to 3, because the 15 and 30 day events start before the scored month begins.

How far the median moved towards the injected shift, event by event, from day 4 to the end. 0 means the median ignored the shift. The shift is 15, 30, or 50 points of capacity. Most events move the median by under 5 points, and a few move it by 10 to 20 points in 50% events.

D5 through the verified December 2025 load-shift: C1 + G4 above, A1 + G4 below, day-ahead, from 14 days before the start to 14 days after the end. The lilac shade is the verified window of experiment 580 (2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13). The dashed vertical lines are the maintainer's switch times (2025-12-30 01:00 and 2026-01-14 11:30). Observed power falls below both forecasts for most of the load-shift, and the NRA (not drawn, because it is only an estimate) stays close to the bands. The two bands lie close together. The sky-blue strip is the G4 gate: the gate_on column of the export files is true for origin days 2025-12-31 to 2026-01-21 at both Primaries, plus the 7-day hold. Coverage in this page is scored against the NRA estimate.

The same for D16, whose power rises during the load-shift. At D5 the 24-hour average power falls by 2.3 MW around 2025-12-30 00:00 and rises by 2.1 MW around 2026-01-14 11:30, matching the maintainer's times. At D16 the two steps (a rise of 1.7 MW and a fall of 1.8 MW) come about 7 hours later, around 08:30 on 30 December and 19:30 on 14 January. A 24-hour average cannot place a step to the hour, so the times are approximate.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Row set and recipe. The rows are experiment_470_intersection_v1: five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 16 Primaries, forecasts 24 to 120 h ahead unless stated, July 2026 unused, cleaned data, and D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01. Refits ran on days 0 and 14 of each month, so a contrast could differ at another cadence. Seeds 0 and 1 are averaged quantile by quantile, then sorted across the 11 levels. No fit ran and no weights were saved. Reused: the stored forecasts of C1 (experiment 584) and A1 (experiment 591) with their lags-masked twins and injected-bank forecasts, E2, and the injected bank of experiment 581.
  • Reproduction. C1 + G4, day 4 to end, 15 and 30 day events: 0.9132 (0.9062 to 0.9201), experiment 592 0.9132, 756 Primary-events.
  • Headline, injected 15 and 30 day events, both metering groups, q05-q95 coverage (95% event-bootstrap interval), safe-side share, median follow ratio.
Forecast Day 4 to end 0-7 days after Safe side, 0-7 days after Follow, day 4 to end C1 0.854 (0.844 to 0.863) 0.860 (0.850 to 0.869) 0.876 0.106 C1 + G4 0.913 (0.906 to 0.920) 0.923 (0.917 to 0.930) 0.939 0.106 A1 0.878 (0.869 to 0.886) 0.885 (0.876 to 0.894) 0.901 0.110 A1 + G4 0.925 (0.918 to 0.931) 0.928 (0.922 to 0.934) 0.944 0.110

  • Other phases, all event lengths (3, 7, 15, and 30 days). Before the shift: C1 + G4 0.882, A1 + G4 0.885. Days 0 to 3: 0.872 and 0.883. These coverages are below 0.90, and the gate does not change them, because it is off until it fires about 1 day after onset. In the 7 to 14 days after the end, coverage is 0.890 and 0.885, unchanged by the gate.
  • Tail pinball, day 4 to end, points of capacity. q05 and q95 for C1: 0.73 and 0.90; for C1 + G4: 0.69 and 0.81. For A1: 0.72 and 0.88; for A1 + G4: 0.71 and 0.82. The median is the network's own, so the gate cannot lower following: 0.106 (C1) and 0.110 (A1) of the depth, which is a mean move of 2.1 to 2.3, 2.9 to 3.5, and 3.9 to 4.6 points of capacity at depths of 15%, 30%, and 50%. docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not available: the stored forecasts hold quantiles only. The median of each assembled forecast equals its network's median on every row (0 rows changed), so the median error is the same with and without the gate.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile contrasts. The gated and plain forecasts share the median, so the median's absolute error is identical; the contrasts above are in the band only.
  • Triggers. None of the seven audit triggers fired: no control failed, the reproduction matched, the quantile and median contrasts agree in direction, and no nested arm beat its container.
  • Code review. A fresh Sonnet agent found no bug that changes a headline number. It noted that the gate thresholds use the whole backtest's event-free days (the readings are causal, the thresholds are in-sample), that the G4 safe-side follow ratio mixes the network's movement and the band widening, and that the intervals resample events inside the same 5 months, so they are narrower than a month-block interval would be.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The injected bank gives the lag neural networks an easier test than a real load-shift would. It changes the lag inputs only, not the power, so it says nothing about a load-shift that enters the training power. That test (target-side absorption) has not been run on C1 or A1.
  • One real pair. Real-event numbers rest on two Primary-events. The network operator's (National Grid Electricity Distribution, NGED) labels are imperfect, and NGED says load-shifts may be missing from its logs, so clean rows and training periods can hold events no label covers.
  • Horizon. The forecasts stop at 120 hours; NGED cares about 1 to 10 days.
  • The G4 false-trigger rate rests on 1 trigger in 5 Primary-years.
  • Real events at D5. C1 + G4 and A1 + G4 both miss the level before the shift and the band does not cover the NRA after it.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Target-side absorption for A1 + G4 and C1 + G4 (a shift in the training power and the inputs, 12 or more designs).
  • A second real event: score both assembled forecasts on May 2026.
  • A gate-free network that receives the gate's signals as inputs, judged at equal band width.

docs.title: Does a neural network that reads the gate's signals as inputs cover the normal running arrangement as well as the hand-built gate does, at the same band width?
docs.text:
We asked whether a neural network can learn to widen its own forecast band during a load-shift if it is given the signals that a hand-built rule, the G4 gate, uses. A load-shift moves part of one Primary substation's demand onto a neighbour for days or weeks. The G4 gate widens the q05-q95 band of the forecast while recent power readings disagree with a forecast made without them, and for 7 days afterwards. The q05-q95 band holds the 5% to 95% range of the forecast.

We took the A1 neural network (experiment 591) and fine-tuned it on synthetic load-shifts with the gate's signals as extra inputs. Call that neural network S. We scored S on injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts in the months 2025-10 and 2025-12, against the A1 neural network with the G4 gate (R, experiment 597). Coverage is the share of rows where the normal running arrangement (NRA), the way the electricity network is normally arranged to supply a Primary, lies inside the q05-q95 band. From day 4 of a load-shift to its end, S covered 0.888 of rows and R covered 0.928.

The pre-agreed stop rule then called for one more arm, S-g (S plus the gate's on-or-off state), which also fell short, so the gate stays. We also ran S-p, S with noise in place of the signals, although the stop rule would have dropped it. S-p is the only arm that separates "the signals carry little" from "the signals are in sample". The result comes from two fold months and two seeds; the five-month comparison was not run.

Verdict: not supported. P1 failed (gap 0.040), P2 failed, P3 failed, P5 was marginal at the eight MVA Primaries (0.031 against a 0.03 margin), and P4 failed: S is only 0.004 above S-p (-0.008 to 0.014).

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Share of rows with the NRA inside q05-q95, injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, 24-120 h. Coverage is scored against the estimated NRA. Look at the phases from day 4 to the end and 0 to 7 days after: R leads, and S and S-g sit close to plain A1.

Share of rows with the NRA on the safe side of q05 or q95: look for dots below the dashed 0.95 line.

Mean q95 - q05 in points of capacity, by arm. S is 0.936 of R's width from day 4 to the end; the width-matched arms are 1.02 of R's.

How far the median moved towards the injected shift, event by event (0: ignored the shift). S follows 0.101 of the depth, against R's 0.119.

The next five figures show the December 2025 example event, D5 and D16, from 14 days before to 14 days after, with dashed lines at the maintainer's switch times 2025-12-30 01:00 and 2026-01-14 11:30. The maintainer's times match the observed steps (summed absolute step 0.90 of capacity, against 0.22, printed by e00598_figures.py example, for the window of experiment 580, about a day earlier). One arm per figure; coverage is scored against an estimated NRA, which is not drawn. Look at where the observed power (black) leaves the shaded band after the onset, and at whether the strip under the panel is on while it does. The strip is plotted at valid time (the origin day plus one), and "on" includes the roughly 7 days the band is held after the gate turns off. R's strip also turns on again for 27 to 30 January, and S-g's does not. The gate strips of R and S-g were checked against the stored gate state (the 597 mode_g4.npy and the saved S-g bits): both Primaries are on from 2025-12-31 to 2026-01-21. The W band is A1's band widened by one constant factor, so it looks close to A1's.

Coverage of S against S-p, one dot per phase and group. Dots on the dashed line mean the signals changed nothing; dots above it mean S covers more than S-p.

docs.title: Results (first fold pair, 2025-10 and 2025-12; 24-120 h; injected 15 and 30 day events)
docs.text:
• Headline for "is placement worth anything beyond width". Rescaled to R's width, S covers 0.915 from day 4 to the end against R's 0.928: a gap of 0.013 (-0.003 to 0.032, MDE 0.017), inconclusive at this sample size. Without rescaling the gap is 0.040.
  • Arms. R: A1 + G4 from experiment 597. W: A1 widened by one constant factor to R's width (1.069 and 1.077 by month). S: signals as inputs. S-g: S plus the G4 state bit. -rs: each S arm rescaled to R's width. G4T: G4 computed on the table T. S-p: the placebo, with noise in place of the signals.
  • Day 4 to the end, coverage. A1 0.884, W 0.909, S 0.888, S-g 0.888, S-rs 0.915, S-g-rs 0.916, G4T 0.928, R 0.928. R minus S: 0.040 (0.022 to 0.060, MDE 0.019). R minus S-rs: 0.013 (-0.003 to 0.032).
  • 0 to 7 days after the end. A1 0.917, W 0.936, S 0.921, S-rs 0.941, R 0.956. P2: S minus W is -0.015 (-0.023 to -0.009); S-rs minus W is +0.005 (0.0001 to 0.010), below the 0.03 margin.
  • Follow ratio (P3). S 0.101 (0.079 to 0.129), R and A1 0.119 (0.092 to 0.163), S-g 0.100. The 0.08 target was not met; the interval of S includes it.
  • Placebo S-p (P4). Day 4 to the end 0.884, 0 to 7 days after 0.917, band 0.252 (A1 0.252), follow 0.118, event-free CRPS minus A1 -0.0003 (eight MVA) and +0.0017 (six MW). S minus S-p: +0.004 (-0.008 to 0.014, MDE 0.011), below the 0.02 margin.
  • Event-free CRPS (P5, S minus A1, points of capacity). Eight MVA Primaries +0.031 (0.020 to 0.042, MDE 0.011); six MW Primaries +0.029 (0.001 to 0.056, MDE 0.028). The fixed margin is 0.03. R itself is +0.012 (0.001 to 0.022) above A1 at the eight MVA Primaries. S and S-g are +0.40 to +0.49 above A1 at the report-only D15 and D18 (interval 0.12 to 0.87). Two fold months are two blocks, so these intervals are rough.
  • Tails. On the injected bank, pinball loss at q05 and q95 for S is within 0.001 of A1. On event-free rows S's q95 pinball is worse than A1's by 0.013 (eight MVA Primaries) and 0.021 (six MW Primaries); the event-free tail table is in the printed report.
  • Real December pair (descriptive). Before the event, S covers 0.28 to 0.33 at D5 against 0.59 to 0.62 for A1 and R, and about the same as A1 at D16 (0.92 against 0.91). From day 4 to the end, all arms stay below 0.80 at D5 and D16. R matches A1 on this one real event (D5 0.74 against 0.74), so the gate shows no gain there, and S halves the coverage before the event at D5.
  • Counted tests: 7, Bonferroni level 0.0071; minimum detectable effects are in the contrasts above. P1 is flagged untestable at its 0.01 margin because its MDE is 0.019.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Gate and rebuilt state. The rebuilt G4 state equals experiment 592's stored state, and R reproduces experiment 597 on its own row sets to within 1e-6.
  • Median minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean forecast beside the quantile contrasts: not computed. The network outputs quantiles, and the median error ae50 is in the printed report.
  • Triggers fired. None of the seven triggers changes the keep-the-gate decision: no control failed in a way that reverses it, no nested arm beats its parent, and no later experiment depends on this result yet. P4 was run after the stop rule fired and did not trigger one.
  • Reviews. Sonnet plan review (12 findings, all applied), Sonnet code review (15 findings, 12 applied or answered, 3 declined), Sonnet figure review (see the pull request).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Training signals are in-sample. The lag-free table T comes from the fold's own A1 step-2 network, which saw the training rows. In the pre-fit check on 2025-12 with seed 0, two Primaries fell below the 0.8 standard-deviation ratio and received added noise; the other folds' counts are in the fit logs. S-p (noise with the same per-column marginals) is indistinguishable from plain A1, so the network ignores noise inputs. S differs from S-p in follow ratio (0.101 against 0.118) and in event-free CRPS (+0.031 against 0 at the eight MVA Primaries) without gaining coverage. That fits signals that are used but mismatched between training and test, and it does not rule out signals that carry little.
  • Two months only. The stop rule ended the experiment after the first fold pair, so the five-month bake-off was not run. Running S-p after the stop rule fired is a deviation from the stop rule, made at the manager's request.
  • Not done: target-side absorption for R and S (experiment 595's method), the avoidable-curtailment cost, and the Bonferroni count above covers only the coverage and event-free CRPS tests.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's logs may miss load-shifts, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Thresholds. The S-g gate threshold and the training-noise standard deviation use all of the fold month's real rows, as R's threshold does.
  • Weather source. Weather at lag times comes from the run issued at or before the forecast origin minus 9 h, so it exists at forecast time.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Rebuild T from a cross-fitted lag-free network (trained without the block it is applied to) and rerun S on the first fold pair, to separate the in-sample explanation.

docs.title: Plan (fixed before any score)
docs.text:
• Arms (all P5 recipe with A1 wiring, fine-tuned on lag-only synthetic shifts mirrored at one neighbour). R: A1 + G4 band (stored from experiment 597). W: A1 with the band widened by a constant factor to R's mean width on event rows. S: signals as inputs, no gate. S-g: S plus the G4 state bit. S-p: S with noise of the same variance in place of the signals.
  • Reuse. The A1 pre-training and step-2 weights of experiment 591 start every S arm, with the new input columns zero-initialised, so each S arm begins as A1. Only the fine-tune is new, which is why the GPU estimate is below the brief's 3 GPU-h ceiling.
  • Cadence. Coarse refits (day 0 and day 14), as in experiments 584 and 591; seeds 0 and 1; five development months 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06, first fold pair first. D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01 and reported only.
  • Where the signals come from (a departure from the brief's wording). The brief takes the disagreement from the lags-masked twin's median. Stored lag-free forecasts exist only for the five test months, so training rows would have none. Instead, a frozen copy of the fold's A1 step-2 network, run with its lags masked, gives a lag-free median and band for every grid time and Primary, in training and test months alike (the table T). Every signal is then a lookup on T plus the observed power, as the G4 gate does with E2: the disagreement of each lag with T at the lag's own time, its sustain count, the fresh residual (observed power minus T up to the origin minus 4.0 h, never as a lag), the lag ages, the neighbour's disagreement, and T's q05 and q95. T is in-sample on training rows and out-of-sample on test rows; this is a caveat that S-p tests.
  • No lookahead. The disagreements and the sustain count use lags at least 24 h old. The fresh residual uses power up to the origin minus 4.0 h. A training row's signals use only its own synthetic lags and earlier rows.
  • Counted tests. Seven: P1 (two phases), P2, P3, P4, P5 (two groups). The Bonferroni level and the minimum detectable effect are printed beside each contrast.
  • Stop rule. As in the decision rule. One GPU process at a time under 8 GB; ask the manager before crossing 3 GPU-h.
  • Maintainer's example event (2026-11-06). Plots of forecast behaviour during and after load-shifts use the December 2025 pair (D5 and D16), which the maintainer dates "2025-12-30 01:00 to 2026-01-14 11:30". One figure per Primary shows 14 days before to 14 days after, with dashed vertical lines at those two times, for R, W, S, S-g, and S-p. The verified window in experiment 580 is 2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13, about a day earlier. The scoring script checks the readings to see which window matches the step, and the caption says which, and does not choose silently. The predictions are unchanged.
  • Time-series plot style (maintainer, 2026-11-06). Every time-series figure has panels at least 280 px high and at most two panels per figure. Each panel shows one arm's median and q05-q95 band with the observed power and the NRA, and a thin strip under the panel marks when the gate is on. A legend outside the data area names each line, band, shade, and bar. The five arms (R, W, S, S-g, S-p) therefore go in separate figures or small multiples of one arm each, never on one panel.
  • Further figure rules (maintainer, 2026-11-06). The NRA line is not drawn on time-series plots, because it is an estimate, and each caption says coverage is scored against that estimate. Observed power is black, no other mark is black or grey, and the load-shift shade is a pale colour that no arm uses. A gate strip is checked against the stored gate state before it is published. Before the pull request is marked ready, a fresh Sonnet reviewer opens each figure rendered to PNG and answers the six-question figure checklist in writing; the pull request body records "figure review: passed" with the date.
  • Changes after the Sonnet plan review (all 12 findings accepted; the review is in the private briefs folder as 598_plan_review.md).
    • Equal width. Each S arm also gets a width-matched control: its band rescaled about the median so its mean q95 - q05 on R's G4-on-or-held origin days equals R's, one factor per fold and seed, printed with its row count. The factor is fitted on the injected bank's 24-120 h rows, which are the rows P1 and P2 read. P1 and P2 are read on the rescaled S as well as on S, and count as passed only if S's own event-row width is within 5% of R's or the rescaled S also passes. W uses the same factor rule applied to R.
    • Training signals are in-sample. Cross-fitting the frozen network is too expensive, so a pre-fit check prints, per Primary, the standard deviation of the fresh residual and of the lag disagreement on training rows against test rows. Where the training-to-test ratio is below 0.8, Gaussian noise is added to the training-row signals to match the test standard deviation, and the write-up says so.
    • The table. T holds the lag-free median by Primary and grid time, taken from the freshest origin that covers it. The lags-masked q05 and q95 are per row (Primary, origin, valid time), computed by one masked inference pass over the rows used. The build asserts that no entry used for an origin comes from an NWP run issued after that origin.
    • Signals in training. The synthetic shift is added to the signal inputs (lag disagreement, fresh residual, neighbour disagreement) and not to the target, as FreshGap.gap(shifts=...) does in experiment 592. The sustain count and the neighbour disagreement are precomputed per row from earlier origins only and are zero where history is missing, with an assertion. A known-answer row checks the shift reaches each signal.
    • Reference parity. A fifth reference, G4 computed on T instead of E2, separates the gate from the change of expectation. Arm S-p (noise signals, same fine-tune and columns) is the second fine-tune of the A1 wiring with no usable signal, so it serves as the parity arm.
    • Outcome bands. Gap of S to R in day-4-to-end coverage: under 0.01 passes, 0.01 to 0.03 is inconclusive (S-g is not run), 0.03 or more fails (run S-g as the stop rule says).
    • Detectability. The minimum detectable effect of every prediction is printed before the fits are scored; a prediction whose margin is below its minimum detectable effect is reported as untestable. P5's margin is fixed at 0.03 points of capacity of event-free CRPS (S minus A1, both metering groups), set before any score; its interval resamples the fold months as blocks. R's and S-p's follow ratios are printed beside P3. Contrasts counted: seven, as above. S-g, the target-side absorption score (experiment 595's method, for R and S), and the real pair are descriptive and uncounted.
  • Standing practices followed. Monthly-equivalent coarse refits, cleaned data, the D15 and D18 cut, saved weights, reuse of stored forecasts, tails and avoidable-curtailment cost, load-shift event plots (at least 6, both metering groups), example forecasts, and the unlogged-event caveat.

Reviews: one Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review before the first fit, one Sonnet write-up review (details in the pull request).

docs.title: Can a longer embargo, or down-weighting the newest rows, lower the share of an injected load-shift that the daily fine-tune of the A1 demand neural network absorbs into its median forecast?
docs.text:
A longer embargo and down-weighting of the newest rows do lower how much of a load-shift the refit absorbs, but not enough on their own to reach the proposed bar. A load-shift moves load between neighbouring primary substations (Primaries) for days or weeks. Its depth is its size as a share of the Primary's capacity. As in experiment 595, we added 12 load-shifts of known depth to the readings of two connected Primaries, refitted the A1 demand neural network on the first and the fifteenth day of a month, and measured how far the median forecast moves toward the load-shift compared with a refit on readings without it. A value of 0 means the forecast did not move and 1 means it moved by the whole depth. E0 is A1 as stored by experiment 595. E1 lengthens the embargo of the daily fine-tune from 3 to 7 days. E2w keeps the 3-day embargo and halves the weight of the rows aged 3 to 10 days. E3 does both: a 7-day embargo, and the rows aged 7 to 14 days halved. The embargo is the number of newest days of power readings held out of each daily fine-tune. The proposed bar of 0.10 is the release bar L4 of experiment 595: at most 0.10 of the depth carried by the median forecast. The verdict is partly supported: P1 holds for E3 only, P2 holds for the MVA and MW Primaries and fails for D15 and D18, and P3 holds weakly.

Results at the day-14 refit: E3 lowers the share from 0.160 to 0.114 of the depth, and the mean 0.114 is above the proposed bar of 0.10. Seven days after an injected load-shift ends, at the day-14 refit, the median forecast sits 0.114 (95% interval 0.073 to 0.154) of the depth toward the shift for E3, 0.128 (0.083 to 0.172) for E1, 0.142 (0.084 to 0.197) for E2w, and 0.160 (0.099 to 0.221) for E0. The E3 interval includes 0.10, and the median over designs is 0.097. The pre-registered prediction P1 (at least one arm lowers the share by 0.04) holds for E3 only: the drop is 0.045 (Bonferroni interval -0.080 to -0.020; minimum detectable effect 0.030). E1 drops by 0.032 (-0.063 to -0.010), below the 0.04 target, and E2w by 0.018 (-0.037 to +0.000). Prediction P2 (no event-free CRPS rise beyond the minimum detectable effect) holds for the eight MVA Primaries and the six MW Primaries and fails for D15 and D18, which are report-only. Prediction P3 (the 7-day embargo costs more at 0 to 24 h than later) holds weakly.

Figure 1. All four arms share each panel. Share of the depth that the median forecast moves toward an injected load-shift, day-14 refit, 12 designs (2 designs in the first 4 days). Dot: mean over designs; line: 95% interval from resampling designs. Top panel: the refit alone; bottom panel: the refit and the lag inputs.

Figure 2. An injected load-shift (design 234, Primary D4, 15 days, 0.5 of the smaller capacity). One arm per panel: the half-hourly median and q05 to q95 band at 24 to 48 h lead of E0 (top) and E1 (bottom), against the observed power (which carries the shift) and the normal running arrangement (NRA), the observed power minus the shift. Shaded: the shift.

Figure 3. The same load-shift for E2w (top) and E3 (bottom).

Figure 4. A second injected load-shift (design 77), E0 (top) and E1 (bottom), as in Figure 2.

Figure 5. The same load-shift for E2w (top) and E3 (bottom).

Figure 6. The one verified real transfer (December 2025), arm E0 at both Primaries, 14 days before to 14 days after. Dashed lines and shade: the switched window the maintainer gave, 2025-12-30 01:00 to 2026-01-14 11:30. The readings match that window better than experiment 580's window (2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13) at the end: the mean level changes by 1.6 to 1.7 MW across 2026-01-14 11:30 against 0.26 to 0.34 MW across 2026-01-13. At the start the evidence is weaker: the largest 2-hour change at D16 is at 2025-12-30 00:30, and at D5 the start change is no clearer (0.35 and 0.37 MW; check in scores/verified_window_check.txt). The fits and shares still use 580's window. Descriptive only.

Figure 7. The same transfer for E3.

  • Arms. E0 is experiment 595's A1, read from its stored forecasts. E1, E2w, and E3 are the same A1 code, with one training-side setting changed in the daily fine-tune: the embargo (E1, E3), and a step weight of 0.5 on the rows aged 3 to 10 days (E2w) or 7 to 14 days (E3), on top of the existing 90-day recency weight and applied to training and early-stopping rows alike. Step-2 weights and pre-training are experiment 591's stored A1 chain, which never sees the injected shift, so the step-2 embargo stays at 3 days. Code folders reused: 574, 587, 591, 595. Schedule: coarse refits on days 0 and 14 of each fold month, seeds 0 and 1, five development months, July 2026 unused. A no-change smoke run of the wrapper reproduced experiment 595's A1 to 4e-7 at most.
  • Total share at q50, day-14 refit, mean over designs (95% interval). First 4 days (2 designs): E0 0.069, E1 0.065, E2w 0.067, E3 0.063. Day 4 to the end (9 designs): E0 0.189 (0.105 to 0.288), E1 0.145 (0.083 to 0.208), E2w 0.168 (0.090 to 0.251), E3 0.127 (0.076 to 0.181). 7 days after the end (12 designs): E0 0.160, E1 0.128, E2w 0.142, E3 0.114. Medians over designs after the end: E0 0.141, E1 0.106, E2w 0.123, E3 0.097.
  • Refit share, 7 days after the end. E0 0.084 (0.041 to 0.131), E1 0.058 (0.029 to 0.088), E2w 0.070 (0.033 to 0.113), E3 0.047 (0.021 to 0.074). Total minus refit leaves a lag part of 0.076 (E0), 0.070 (E1), 0.072 (E2w), and 0.067 (E3). At the day-0 refit, where the shift is not in the training rows, every arm gives 0.077 or 0.078, so the arms differ only through the refit.
  • Contrasts. Counted tests: 3 (E1, E2w, and E3 minus E0, total share, 7 days after the end, paired by design). E1 minus E0: -0.032 (Bonferroni interval -0.063 to -0.010; minimum detectable effect 0.026). E2w minus E0: -0.018 (-0.037 to +0.000; 0.019). E3 minus E0: -0.045 (-0.080 to -0.020; 0.030). Descriptive, day 4 to the end: E1 -0.045, E2w -0.021, E3 -0.062.
  • Tails, total share 7 days after the end. q01 / q05 / q95 / q99: E0 0.120 / 0.134 / 0.223 / 0.243; E1 0.089 / 0.104 / 0.181 / 0.203; E2w 0.101 / 0.115 / 0.205 / 0.229; E3 0.084 / 0.098 / 0.157 / 0.179. From E0 to E3 the q01 and q05 shares fall by 0.036, the median by 0.046, and the q95 and q99 shares by 0.066 and 0.064. The upper tails stay further from zero than the median for every arm.
  • Event-free CRPS (arm fitted on the observed power, all five months, mean pinball-based CRPS in MW over the 0.01 to 0.99 levels, mean over Primary-by-month cells; minus E0, 95% interval). The eight MVA Primaries (E0 0.3675 MW): E1 +0.0000 (-0.0023 to +0.0022), E2w +0.0005 (-0.0008 to +0.0019), E3 +0.0005 (-0.0021 to +0.0030; minimum detectable effect 0.0026). The six MW Primaries (E0 0.3102 MW): E1 +0.0024 (-0.0013 to +0.0061), E2w +0.0007 (-0.0010 to +0.0025), E3 +0.0031 (-0.0013 to +0.0072; 0.0043). D15 and D18 (report-only, E0 0.3543 MW): E1 +0.0144 (+0.0033 to +0.0312), E2w +0.0065 (+0.0019 to +0.0120), E3 +0.0179 (+0.0053 to +0.0358).
  • Effect on the freshness of the forecast (CRPS at 0 to 24 h lead against 24 h and later). E3 minus E0: eight MVA Primaries +0.0025 at 0 to 24 h and +0.0002 later; six MW Primaries +0.0044 and +0.0029. E1 minus E0: +0.0020 and -0.0002 (MVA), +0.0041 and +0.0022 (MW). CRPS rises most at short leads, as predicted, by 1 to 2% and inside the minimum detectable effect.
  • Tail calibration on event-free rows (coverage of q05 to q95; share below q01; share above q99). Eight MVA Primaries: E0 0.865 / 0.0121 / 0.0240, E3 0.867 / 0.0117 / 0.0224. Six MW Primaries: E0 0.830 / 0.0214 / 0.0426, E3 0.817 / 0.0216 / 0.0477. D15 and D18: E0 0.845 / 0.0111 / 0.0387, E3 0.831 / 0.0108 / 0.0444. The six MW Primaries lose 1.3 points of coverage with E3, and the upper tail (above q99) gets worse for them.
  • Verified D5/D16 pair (descriptive, 2026-01 day-14 refit, 7 days after the end, total / refit). D5: E0 0.141 / 0.051, E1 0.126 / 0.029, E2w 0.129 / 0.037, E3 0.114 / 0.012. D16: E0 0.189 / 0.111, E1 0.150 / 0.069, E2w 0.155 / 0.082, E3 0.119 / 0.041. The real pair moves the same way as the injected ones.
  • How a longer embargo slows a real tracking forecast. A 7-day embargo means a genuine, permanent level change enters the fine-tune 4 days later than with a 3-day embargo. This experiment scored no such change, so the size of that delay's effect is unmeasured. The event-free CRPS, which includes ordinary drift, did not rise measurably at 14 of 16 Primaries and rose by 4 to 5% at D15 and D18.
  • Checks. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the four shares independently (0.1599, 0.1283, 0.1421, and 0.1144) and found no audit trigger: the rows match across arms, no quantiles cross, and E3 minus E0 is negative or about zero in all 12 designs (more than 0.02 below in 8; design 83 is the largest at -0.178, and without it the mean is still -0.034). The agent's CRPS level for the eight MVA Primaries was about 0.001 MW lower than the table's (cell weighting), with the same E3 minus E0 sign and size (+0.0002 against +0.0004). Share cells with fewer than 48 half-hours are dropped (12 of 580); the CRPS table drops flagged actuals, and none fell in the scored rows. The CRPS here omits the two outer strips of the distribution for every arm alike. The intervals for CRPS resample Primary-by-month cells as independent, so they are approximate. There is no median-minus-mean check because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only.
  • Caveats. Injected shifts are not real ones; the real evidence is one pair. Two seeds. Two designs fall in the first 4 days. The step-2 weights keep their 3-day embargo. NGED says load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so the clean rows may hold unlabelled events, and the event-free CRPS may include some of them. Weather: the ENS run issued at least 9 h before the forecast origin, as in 595. Nothing is adopted.
  • What to try next. (1) Test an embargo and down-weighting that start only when a gate fires, so that ordinary periods keep the 3-day embargo. (2) Measure the delay's effect on genuine permanent level changes (the real pair after the transfer ends is one). (3) Repeat with C1 plus G4 once assembled. (4) Check D15 and D18 separately for a shorter embargo.
  • Reviews. One fresh Sonnet code review before the fits found no blocking issue and six minor ones (four fixed, two noted in the checks above). One fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline numbers. A fresh Sonnet write-up review is recorded in the pull request.
  • Data and compute. Forecasts and fitted weights are in the private folder data/ml-experiments/00599-nra-refit-embargo-and-down-weighting-of-the-newest-rows-against-load-shift-absorption/ (work/<arm>/<world>/work/{fits,models}; scores in scores/). Fits took about 0.55 GPU-h in total, one process at a time.

docs.title: Do C1, A1, and their G4 assembled forecasts still hold the normal running arrangement inside the q05-q95 band at 120-240 h ahead, where NGED's horizon reaches 10 days?
docs.text:
At 5 to 10 days ahead, the G4 band still lifts the share of rows with the normal running arrangement (NRA) inside the 5th-to-95th-percentile (q05-q95) band to 0.905 for the A1 neural network and 0.891 for the C1 neural network, from day 4 of an injected load-shift to its end. The G4 band adds less coverage than at 1 to 5 days ahead, and the 0.90 target is not shown for A1. We re-scored the four stored forecasts C1, A1, and their versions with the G4 band, where experiment 597 had stopped at 5 days. Verdict: partly supported. The pre-registered predictions were: P1 (coverage at least 0.90 from day 4 to the end at 120-240 h) held on the point estimate for A1 and failed for C1; P2 (the gate's gain is not smaller at long lead) was refuted; P3 (G4 costs no event-free pinball loss) held on the point estimates; P4 (the 24-120 h numbers reproduce experiment 597) held.

A load-shift moves part of one Primary substation's demand onto a neighbour for days or weeks, so recent power readings stop showing the NRA. NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days, and earlier results covered only the first 5 days. All stored forecasts already reached 10 days (240 h), so we changed one constant in experiment 597's scoring code and scored again with no fit. Coverage means the share of rows with the NRA inside the q05-q95 band (target 0.90). The NRA is the way the electricity network is normally arranged to supply a Primary. C1 and A1 are neural networks that read lagged power; the G4 band widens the q05-q95 band while a load-shift is detected; E2 is a neural network that reads no lagged power. The injected events are the shifts of experiment 581's bank, added to the lag inputs only. Nothing is adopted for production.

Terms used below. A Primary-event is one injected load-shift at one Primary substation; 732 of them have a day 4. The phases are by the time being forecast: before the load-shift, days 0 to 3, day 4 to the end, 0 to 7 days after the end, and 7 to 14 days after. The safe-side share is the share of rows with the NRA on the safe side of the band: below q95 when the shift lowered the load, above q05 when it raised it. The median follow ratio is the fraction of the injected shift that the median forecast moves. Metering groups: the eight MVA Primaries and the six MW Primaries. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is the half-width of an interval widened for the eight counted tests (Bonferroni). CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score.
