"Points of capacity" are percentage points of a Primary's capacity.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Share of rows with the NRA inside q05-q95 on injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, by phase of the event and by lead band, both metering groups. Dot: mean over Primary-events; line: 95% interval from resampling events; dashed line: the 0.90 target. The orange and blue dots with G4 lie above their plain versions in the two phases where the gate is on. The 120-240 h panel sits lower than the other two for the day-4-to-end phase. Phases before the shift and days 0 to 3 are not drawn, because only 3 and 7 day events have rows there. Panels for each metering group are in coverage_by_phase_and_lead_mva.svg and coverage_by_phase_and_lead_mw.svg.

Coverage that the G4 band adds to each network (G4 minus plain), by lead band. Dot: mean over Primary-events; line: 95% interval. The gain at 120-240 h is smaller than at 24-120 h in both phases and for both networks; the A1 drop after the end is small (0.004).

Share of rows with the NRA on the safe side of q05 or q95 (below q95 when the shift lowered the load, above q05 when it raised it). Dashed line: the 0.95 target. Look for the G4 dots above the plain dots, and for the 120-240 h panel sitting lower than the other two.

Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lower is better) on event-free rows, by lead and metering group, for the plain networks C0, C1, A1 and the lag-free network E2. Look for C0 and E2 above C1 and A1 at every lead, and for every bar rising with lead. C0 is the earlier candidate of experiment 572; E2 reads no lagged power. The G4 band changes the CRPS by less than 0.01 and is not drawn separately.

The forecast of A1 + G4 issued 9 to 10 days before each half-hour, for the two Primaries of the maintainer's example load-shift (D5 and D16), from 14 days before the first switch time to 14 days after the last. Dashed green lines (legend: "Load-shift times"): the start and end times "2025-12-30 01:00" and "2026-01-14 11:30" from the maintainer's log. The observed power steps down at D5 and up at D16 on 2025-12-30 and steps back on 2026-01-14, so the logged times match the step. Experiment 580's verified span starts about one day earlier, and the phase scores below use that span. Purple bar: the half-hours whose forecast was issued while the G4 wide band was on; it runs to the axis end because the band stays wide for 7 days after the gate releases. The bar is placed by the half-hour being forecast, so it starts about 9 days after the gate fired. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the NRA, which is not drawn.

The same figure for C1 + G4. Look for the same purple bar: the G4 wide band starts at the same days for both neural networks.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Row set and recipe. experiment_470_intersection_v1: five fold months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), 16 Primaries, July 2026 unused, cleaned data, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 (report-only; the injected bank has no events at D15 and D18). Coarse refits on days 0 and 14 of each month, so a contrast could differ at another cadence. Seeds 0 and 1 averaged. Weather from the run issued at or before the forecast origin minus 9 hours. No fit and no GPU. Code reused from experiments 582, 583, 584, 592, and 597 (the e00600_common.py file raises MAX_LEAD_H from 120 to 240). Stored forecasts: C1 (584), A1 (591), C0 (572), E2 (565).
  • Reproduction (P4). The rebuilt G4 state equals experiment 592's for C0, C1, and A1. At 24-120 h, day 4 to end, C1 + G4 is 0.9132 and A1 + G4 is 0.9251, the same as experiment 597, and the event-free CRPS values of experiment 597 reproduce.
  • P1: coverage from day 4 to the end at 120-240 h (732 Primary-events). C1 + G4 0.891 (95% 0.884 to 0.898; Bonferroni 0.881 to 0.901; minimum detectable effect, MDE, 0.010): does not hold. A1 + G4 0.905 (95% 0.898 to 0.911; Bonferroni 0.896 to 0.914; MDE 0.009): holds on the point estimate only, and the lower bound is below 0.90, so under the pre-registered wording the target is "not shown". Plain neural networks: C1 0.856 and A1 0.878. By metering group, A1 + G4 is 0.910 at the eight MVA Primaries and 0.897 at the six MW Primaries; C1 + G4 is 0.893 and 0.889.
  • P2: the gate's value at 120-240 h against 24-120 h (coverage of G4 minus plain). A1, 0-7 days after the end: +0.043 then +0.039, difference -0.004 (Bonferroni -0.008 to -0.001; MDE 0.003), so P2 is refuted by the rule, by a small amount. A1, day 4 to end: +0.048 then +0.027, difference -0.021 (-0.025 to -0.018). C1, 0-7 days after: +0.063 then +0.051, difference -0.012 (-0.017 to -0.008; MDE 0.004). C1, day 4 to end: +0.061 then +0.035, difference -0.025 (-0.030 to -0.021).
  • Why the gain falls (post hoc, descriptive). The G4 band is decided at the forecast origin. The share of day-4-to-end rows issued while the wide band was on is 0.829 at 0-24 h, 0.762 at 24-120 h, and 0.685 at 120-240 h, for both networks. That accounts for about a quarter of the fall from day 4 to the end (a gain proportional to the share would fall from 0.048 to 0.043 for A1, not to 0.027), so most of the fall is unexplained. After the end the share is the same (0.885 and 0.878), yet C1 still loses 0.012, so the share is not the whole reason.
  • Safe-side share and median follow, day 4 to the end, 120-240 h, then at 24-120 h. A1 + G4 0.934 (0.941), C1 + G4 0.925 (0.932). Median follow ratio: C1 0.079 (0.106) and A1 0.080 (0.110); the median is the network's own, so G4 cannot change it.
  • Tail pinball, day 4 to end, injected events, points of capacity, 120-240 h (24-120 h in brackets). q01, q05, q95, q99 for C1 + G4: 0.18, 0.72, 0.91, 0.24 (0.18, 0.69, 0.81, 0.21); for A1 + G4: 0.19, 0.73, 0.90, 0.24 (0.18, 0.71, 0.82, 0.22). The plain neural networks are 0.02 to 0.06 higher at q05 and q95 at 120-240 h.
  • Event-free rows (CRPS, points of capacity; coverage). The eight MVA Primaries, 24-120 h then 120-240 h: C1 3.081 then 3.595; A1 3.057 then 3.568; C0 3.146 then 3.700; E2 3.352 then 3.791 (C1 rows). The six MW Primaries: C1 2.465 then 2.777; A1 2.445 then 2.803; C0 2.611 then 2.943; E2 2.640 then 2.899. Coverage at 120-240 h is 0.855 to 0.857 at the eight MVA Primaries and 0.874 to 0.877 at the six MW Primaries for C1 and A1, below 0.90 for the plain neural network and for G4. At 24-120 h it is already 0.88 at both metering groups.
  • P3: event-free pinball loss, assembled minus plain, both groups, 120-240 h (Bonferroni intervals, points of capacity). C1: q05 -0.0003 (-0.0012 to +0.0002; MDE 0.0007), q95 +0.0001 (-0.0004 to +0.0008; MDE 0.0006). A1: q05 -0.0004 (-0.0018 to +0.0003; MDE 0.0011), q95 +0.0004 (0.0000 to +0.0014; MDE 0.0007). Every point estimate is within its MDE, so P3 holds on the point estimates. The pre-registered rule asked for the whole interval to lie within the MDE, which cannot happen when the MDE is the interval half-width, so this is a deviation from the rule. The A1 q95 lower bound is 0.0000, so G4 may cost a little there.
  • Counted tests: 8 (P1 for two forecasts, P2 for two networks, four event-free pinball contrasts), each at the two-sided 5% level divided by 8, with the half-width printed as the MDE.
  • Real December pair (D5 and D16, 2 Primary-events, descriptive only), 120-240 h, coverage on experiment 592's verified span. A1 + G4 at D5: before 0.57, days 0-3 0.54, day 4 to end 0.83, 0-7 days after 0.77. D16: 0.94, 0.78, 0.55, 0.84. C1 + G4 at D5: 0.40, 0.45, 0.79, 0.77. D16: 0.97, 0.72, 0.55, 0.83. The D16 miss from day 4 to the end sits on the safe side (0.99 of rows have the NRA on the safe side); at 24-120 h experiment 597 found 0.69 and 0.70.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. The stored forecasts hold quantiles only, so the mean forecast does not exist. G4 leaves the median unchanged, so the error of the median forecast is the same with and without the G4 band; no contrast can differ in sign from the quantile-score contrast.
  • Leave one Primary out. P1 and P2 keep their sign and verdict when any one of the 14 injected-bank Primaries is removed: C1 + G4 coverage 0.889 to 0.897, A1 + G4 0.902 to 0.910; the A1 and C1 gate-value difference after the end stays between -0.003 and -0.014.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 fired in form: P1 for C1 and P2 contradicted the prediction. A post hoc description of one possible cause is recorded above (the gate is decided at issue time); it was not tested as a counterfactual and explains only part of the fall. No other trigger fired, so no audit ran.
  • Unlogged-event caveat. NGED may have missed load-shifts in its logs, so event-free rows may hold unlabelled events and the real-pair slices undercount. The real pair is two Primary-events and cannot rank forecasts.
  • Lab shortcut. The injected bank changes only the lag inputs, not the training power, so it flatters networks that read lags (experiment 595).
  • What to try next. A band that widens at issue time for rows valid inside a suspected load-shift when the gate has not fired, and a separate long-lead calibration step for event-free rows (0.855 to 0.877 coverage).

docs.title: Does the G4 gated band lower or raise the curtailment cost of C1 and A1, and how well are the upper tails of the assembled load-shift forecasts calibrated?
docs.text:
On injected load-shifts the G4 band brings the q95 exceedance close to the nominal 0.05 after the load-shift ends and lowers the curtailment cost at tighter limits, but at the headline limit the reduction is small and rests on one Primary. The G4 band (the gated band named G4 in experiment 592) widens a forecast's quantiles on the days after a load-shift is detected. We scored C1 and A1 (the two lag networks assembled in experiment 597; A1 shares one lag encoder) with and without that band, beside C0 (an earlier lag network) and E2 (a network that reads no lags), using the avoidable curtailment cost of experiments 277 and 478, unchanged. Nothing was refitted. In the one real event where a Primary's load rose (D16), the lags-masked twin (the lag network with every lag input masked, which the G4 band uses as its wide quantiles) forecast as low as the lag network, so the band did not help there. Terms: q95 and q99 are the 95th and 99th percentile forecasts; exceedance is the share of rows where the observed power lies above one of them; the bank is experiment 581's set of injected load-shifts; the minimum detectable effect is the half-width of a Bonferroni interval (an interval widened for four counted tests). Intervals in the Results are 98.75% intervals, and intervals in the figures are 95%.

Cost units. The cost is pounds per Primary-day: the mean over day-ahead forecast rows (12 to 36 hours ahead) of the cost of the energy the forecast curtailed, priced at £2,000 per megawatt-hour, plus 20 times that price for any energy still above the limit after curtailment, minus the same cost for a perfect forecast. The limit is a fraction (0.9, 0.75, or 0.5) of the Primary's largest metered power before 2025-10-01. The cost is defined only for the six MW Primaries, whose meters show the sign of the flow.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Avoidable cost on event-free rows, limit 0.9 of the past maximum, six MW Primaries, 5 test months. Dot: estimate; line: 95% interval from resampling Primary-months. The gated and plain forecasts coincide here: the wide band changes q95 on only 127 (C1) and 159 (A1) event-free rows, all at D14 in October 2025, and those rows have no planned curtailment at limits 0.9 and 0.75.

Share of event-free rows with the observed power above q95 (dashed line: the nominal 0.05), 24 to 120 hours ahead. At the six MW Primaries every interval lies above 0.05, so the upper tail is too thin there.

The same for q99 (dashed line: 0.01). The C1 interval at the six MW Primaries includes 0.01.

C1 on the injected load-shifts of 15 and 30 days (six MW Primaries, limit 0.9). Blue: the network alone on contaminated lags; orange: with the G4 band; green: the lags-masked twin, which reads no lags. Intervals resample events; smaller is better.

The same for A1.

C1: share of rows with the observed power above q95, by phase of an injected load-shift of 15 or 30 days, for the six MW Primaries (top) and the eight MVA Primaries (bottom). Dashed line: the nominal 0.05.

The same for A1.

C1, q99 (dashed line: 0.01).

A1, q99.

Primary D5 in the maintainer's example event, with day-ahead forecasts. The readings fall within 30 minutes of the labelled start (2025-12-30 01:00 UTC) and recover over the morning of 2026-01-14, so the labelled load-shift times (dashed purple lines) match the readings; experiment 580's window starts about a day earlier. Observed power averages about 1.2 to 1.4 MW lower inside the window, while both median forecasts stay at or above the normal running level and reach about 7 MW at peaks. The orange strip marks origin days on which the G4 band is wide. Coverage is scored against the estimated normal running arrangement, which is not drawn.

Primary D16 in the same event: its power rises by about 2 MW on average (3 to 4 MW at peaks), and neither forecast follows it. The G4 band is flagged on from 31 December, but its q95 is at most 0.08 MW above C1's. Coverage is scored against the estimated normal running arrangement, as above.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• The q95 and q99 exceedance targets failed (P3). The q95 exceedance on event-free rows is 0.081 (C1) and 0.084 (A1) at the six MW Primaries, not within 0.01 of 0.05; the q99 rate is 0.017 and 0.019, not within 0.005 of 0.01.
  • Pre-registered tests (four counted; Bonferroni level 0.0125 each; the results at limits 0.75 and 0.5 are descriptive). Event-free cost, G4 minus plain, six MW Primaries: £0.00 at limits 0.9 and 0.75, +£0.56 (Bonferroni interval 0 to +1.96; minimum detectable effect £0.98) at 0.5 for C1, and -£2.37 (-8.3 to 0) for A1. P1 holds. After an injected end, limit 0.9, 15 and 30 day events: C1 -£41 (-124 to +7; minimum detectable effect £66), A1 -£124 (-268 to -19; £124). P2 holds for A1 and not for C1 at 0.9. At 0.75 and 0.5 both gated forecasts lower the cost (C1 -£1,173 and -£6,535; A1 -£901 and -£3,367, intervals exclude zero).
  • Leave-one-out. Leaving D16 out turns the limit-0.9 contrast to +£5.7 (C1) and +£2.5 (A1). The saving comes from D16 in 2025-12, where 13 scored rows per event exceed the limit, so it rests on one real near-limit period and not on six independent events. At 0.75 and 0.5, leaving any one Primary out keeps the sign. The leave-one-out result is audit trigger 4 (see Checks).
  • Cost of each arm (event-free, limit 0.9, pounds per Primary-day, 95% interval). C0 406 (67 to 847); E2 463 (50 to 1,082); C1 311 (63 to 639); C1 + G4 311; A1 282 (45 to 602); A1 + G4 282. The ordering at limits 0.75 and 0.5 is the same (A1 and C1 lowest, E2 highest).
  • Event rows (within 7 days of a labelled event), limit 0.9. The cost is 28,000 to 36,000 pounds per Primary-day, 70 to 125 times the event-free cost, almost all at D16 during the real December event. At limit 0.9 G4 changes that cost by under £50 per Primary-day. At 0.5 it lowers the cost by £1,415 (C1) and £995 (A1) per Primary-day, with an interval that reaches zero.
  • Tail calibration, event-free rows, 24 to 120 h. Share above q95 (nominal 0.05): C1 0.081 and A1 0.084 at the six MW Primaries, C1 0.072 and A1 0.072 at the eight MVA Primaries; C0 0.104 and E2 0.102 at the six. Share above q99 (nominal 0.01): C1 0.017, A1 0.019, C0 0.027, E2 0.022 at the six; C1 0.020 and A1 0.023 at the eight. Over-forecast share of the median: 0.44 to 0.46 for C1 and A1 (0.50 would be balanced).
  • Tail calibration after an injected load-shift (15 and 30 days, 24 to 120 h). G4 lowers the q95 exceedance at the six MW Primaries from 0.105 to 0.070 in day 4 to end and from 0.081 to 0.048 in the 7 days after (C1; A1 0.100 to 0.064 and 0.074 to 0.049), and at the eight MVA Primaries from 0.061 to 0.036 (C1; A1 0.052 to 0.033). q99 falls from 0.025 to 0.014 at the six (C1).
  • Real December pair (D5 and D16). At D5 in the 7 days after the end, G4 lowers q95 exceedance from 0.49 to 0.31 (A1) and 0.49 to 0.28 (C1). At D16 it leaves the q95 exceedance unchanged in every phase (0.31 for C1 and 0.30 for A1 from day 4 to the end), and leaves the cost unchanged except in days 7 to 14 after the end, where the gated forecasts cost £129 (C1) and £194 (A1) more per Primary-day. At D16, limit 0.9, the C1 cost is £583,000 per Primary-day from day 4 to the end and £115,000 in the 7 days after; the A1 cost is £570,000 and £111,000 (day-ahead rows, 12 to 36 h). Only this one real event (D5 and D16, December 2025) was scored, so the cost reductions at 0.75 and 0.5 come from injected load-shifts.
  • Not scored. The manual heuristic and climatology are not stored for these 5 months, and fitting them was outside the brief. C0 and E2 have no injected-bank forecasts, so the bank rows use the lags-masked twin as the reference that reads no lags. The eight MVA Primaries have tail scores only, because their meters hide the sign of the flow.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not computed: the stored forecasts hold quantiles, and G4 leaves the median unchanged on every row (checks.txt of the export), so the contrasts cannot be moved by a median shift.
  • Error of the median beside the tail contrasts. The median is identical in the gated and plain forecasts, so the contrast on the median error is exactly zero.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 4 fired (leave-one-out above). A Sonnet audit re-derived the event-free cost to the penny and confirmed the D16 mechanism (a wider q95 after a sign -1 injection avoids a breach priced at 20 times). The audit found that the claim "event-free differences are zero because the gate is off" was wrong: the gate is on for 190 event-free cost-window rows at D14 in October 2025, and those rows cost nothing extra only because they sit below the limit. At limit 0.5 the event-free effect (+£0.56 for C1, -£2.37 for A1 on a base of about £31,500) comes from 10 and 14 non-zero rows, so its minimum detectable effect is weak evidence. The other triggers did not fire. The claim that G4 does not raise the event-free cost holds only for the firing rate seen, because G4 fired on 190 event-free cost-window rows at one Primary. The known-answer check agreed to within £3 in millions on every system and limit.
  • Reviews. The code review ran after the first scoring pass, not before. The code review found one high-severity fault (the report-only group label did not match the export, so D15 and D18 had no rows; fixed and re-run), a real-pair cost window that was 24 to 36 h instead of 12 to 36 h (fixed), and mislabelled interval levels (relabelled 98.75%). Cost, leakage, and units were confirmed. Not changed: no quantile rearrangement (q95 never crosses, per the audit), and bank events are resampled as independent. The figure review failed on the first pass (black used twice, gate strip missing from the legend, two metering groups averaged in the bank exceedance figures, caption numbers); all were fixed.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Row set and cadence. The row set is 5 development test months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06; the injected bank covers the same months), 16 Primaries, and forecasts 0 to 120 hours ahead, refitted on days 0 and 14 of each month and averaged over seeds 0 and 1. The forecasts are the stored forecasts of experiments 584, 591, and experiment 593 (the stored export), with the G4 band of experiment 597. July 2026 is unused.
  • Cost is against the metered flow, tail calibration against the estimated normal running arrangement. The two coincide outside the verified events.
  • Injected events overlap. Event intervals resample events as independent, although several share a Primary and month.
  • Unlogged events. NGED says some load-shift events are missing from its logs, so event-free rows may hold events no label covers.
  • Nothing here is adopted for production.

docs.title: What does each encoder of the modular demand network (datetime, weather, power lag) contribute to its forecast, on the December 2025 load-shift, on injected load-shifts, and in an event-free month?
docs.text:
Each encoder adds a recognisable part of the forecast, and the lag encoder follows a load-shift in its inputs by only a small share of the shift's depth. The datetime encoder alone gives a daily and weekly shape. The weather encoder moves the level with temperature. The lag encoder adds a daily-shaped correction to the forecast level that is there with and without a load-shift. When we inject a load-shift into the lag inputs, the lag encoder follows it by 0.14 of the depth for P5 and by 0.09 for C1 (P5 plus lag-only synthetic load-shifts) and for A1 (shared lag encoder).

Verdict: partly supported, with one of the three predictions holding. P1 held. P2 failed as registered: the responses of C1 (0.09) and A1 (0.09) fall just under the registered floor of 0.1, with intervals that reach 0.11 and 0.105, and their sign was right. P3 failed: C1's response is smaller than P5's, the opposite of the prediction. Nothing is adopted for production.

docs.title: How to read the figures
docs.text:
Each figure shows what one encoder adds to the median forecast. A load-shift moves part of one primary substation's demand onto another, so the recent power readings no longer show the normal running arrangement (NRA). MW (megawatts) is real power. The network has three encoders: small neural networks that turn the datetime, the weather, and the lagged power into numbers that the mixer (the part that combines the encoders' outputs) reads. We switch them on one at a time:

  • Stage 1: datetime encoder only. The weather and lag embeddings are replaced by their mean over a sample of the day's fine-tuning rows (after the 3-day embargo).
  • Stage 2: datetime and weather encoders. The lag embedding is the mean.
  • Stage 3: all three encoders, which is the full network. The probe's stage 3 matches the network's own forecast to under 0.0001 of capacity.

Stages 1 and 2 are probes that are off-distribution: the mixer never saw a mean embedding in training, so they show what the network reads from each encoder and are not forecasts anyone would issue. All forecasts are day-ahead (24 to 48 hours ahead, issued at 09:00 UTC from a weather run at least 9 hours old), one seed (0), the refit in force on each date, and clean lags. The orange band is q05 to q95 and the dark orange line is the median. The black line is observed power. No figure draws the NRA, because it is only an estimate.

docs.title: December 2025 example event
docs.text:
The readings step at the maintainer's switch times, so the plots shade that window. D5 falls 1.6 MW at 2025-12-30 01:00 and rises 1.5 MW at 2026-01-14 11:30. D16 moves the other way (+1.4 MW and -1.8 MW). Each step is the difference of 24-hour mean power either side (switch_time_steps.csv, written by e00602_figures.py). Experiment 580's verified window starts about a day earlier and ends about a day and a half earlier. The readings show no step at its edges.

Caption: P5 at D5. The top panel shows the datetime encoder only: a daily shape sitting about 15 to 40 points below the readings. The bottom panel adds the weather encoder, which lifts the median above the readings inside the shaded window. Dashed lines are the switch times.

Caption: P5 at D5. The top panel is the full network. The bottom panel is the lag encoder's contribution (stage-3 median minus stage-2 median). Look for a step at the dashed lines: the contribution drifts from about 8 to about 5 points after the first 4 days (window means in the table). D5's power fell by about 28 points of capacity (1.6 MW of 5.7 MW). The drift is in the right direction and is within the range the contribution takes in the event-free month.

Figures of the same two kinds exist for C1 and A1, and for D16, where power rises: real_<network>_<D5 or D16>_stages_1_2.svg and real_<network>_<D5 or D16>_stage_3_and_lag_contribution.svg.

Mean lag contribution, points of capacity Before (14 d) First 4 days Day 4 to end After (14 d) D5 P5 7.8 8.0 4.7 5.2 D5 C1 6.9 7.4 5.5 4.9 D5 A1 6.6 7.2 2.7 2.3 D16 P5 5.7 5.9 9.7 8.8 D16 C1 4.9 5.2 8.1 7.6 D16 A1 4.5 5.3 7.9 6.0

docs.title: What the weather encoder adds on its own
docs.text:
Caption: C1 at D5. The top panel keeps only the datetime encoder live. The bottom panel keeps only the weather encoder live, with the datetime and lag embeddings at their mean. The weather-only median has no daily shape, and it lifts above the readings inside the shaded window, as in stage 2. These are off-distribution probes.

Figures of the same kind exist for P5 and A1, and for D16: real_<network>_<D5 or D16>_single_encoders.svg.

docs.title: How much weight the mixer gives each encoder
docs.text:
The lag encoder carries about 0.1 to 0.4 of the three encoders' summed effect on the median, and that share fell at D5 but not at D16 during the load-shift. The mixer is a plain multi-layer perceptron, so it has no attention weights to plot. Two sensitivity measures stand in for them, and neither is attention:

  • Leave-one-encoder-out: per half-hour, the absolute change in the median when one encoder's embedding is replaced by its training-set mean.
  • Gradient times input: per half-hour, the gradient of the mixture mean with respect to an encoder's embedding times that embedding, summed over the embedding's dimensions (the signed contribution of that embedding to the mean).

The lag encoder's share is its absolute value over the sum of the three encoders' absolute values.

Caption: the lag encoder's share at D5 by leave-one-encoder-out, every half-hour (top) and as a daily average (bottom), for P5, C1, and A1. Look at the daily average: the share falls from about 0.3 to about 0.2 around 3 days after the start of the load-shift and to 0.1 to 0.15 by about 7 days. P5 and C1 climb back to 0.2 or more within about 10 days after the end, and A1 stays near 0.07 for about a week after the end. It is a sensitivity measure, not attention.

Caption: the same at D16. The daily share rises from about 0.2 to a peak of 0.35 to 0.42 around the end of the load-shift, and then falls back, so the network does not ignore the lag encoder here. It is a sensitivity measure, not attention.

The gradient-times-input versions are weights_grad_D5.svg and weights_grad_D16.svg.

Lag encoder's share Measure Before (14 d) First 4 days Day 4 to end After (14 d) D5 P5 leave-one-out 0.28 0.29 0.14 0.19 D5 C1 leave-one-out 0.25 0.27 0.16 0.18 D5 A1 leave-one-out 0.25 0.26 0.10 0.10 D5 P5 gradient times input 0.24 0.22 0.09 0.09 D5 C1 gradient times input 0.21 0.20 0.07 0.07 D5 A1 gradient times input 0.15 0.18 0.14 0.16 D16 P5 leave-one-out 0.23 0.24 0.33 0.30 D16 C1 leave-one-out 0.20 0.22 0.28 0.26 D16 A1 leave-one-out 0.22 0.28 0.28 0.24 D16 P5 gradient times input 0.23 0.24 0.27 0.23 D16 C1 gradient times input 0.19 0.21 0.22 0.19 D16 A1 gradient times input 0.20 0.29 0.24 0.15

Experiment 568's stored attention weights cannot answer this question. They are monthly means per lead band over four tokens (weather, datetime, Primary, and spread) for the attention mixer, which has no lag token, and they are not per half-hour. Plotting them here would not show the lag encoder.

The shares are one Primary, one event, and one seed each, and the fall at D5 starts about 3 days into the event and lasts to about 10 days after its end for P5 and C1 (longer for A1). Weather also changed over those weeks, so the fall may not be a reaction to the load-shift. The leave-one-out and gradient measures disagree about A1 at D5 (0.10 against 0.14 in the day 4 to end column).

docs.title: Injected load-shifts
docs.text:
Caption: C1 at D5 in March 2026 with a +0.50 shift (50 points of capacity) added to the lag inputs for 30 days. The event began on 14 February, before the plotted window, and ends on 15 March. The contribution stays between about -6 and +16 points and does not rise to 50, so the median stays near the observed power. The injected depth is in the figure title and is off the scale of the panel.

The injected-event figures exist for D5 for four designs and three networks: injected_<network>_D5_<length>d_<up or down>_<depth>pct_*.svg.

Caption: for each injected design, the lag encoder's response as a share of the injected depth (stage-3 median with a positive shift minus with a negative shift, over twice the depth, averaged over days 2 to the end of the event). One dot per Primary, coloured by the injected depth. Look at how the dots rise with length and stay below 0.35, far from 1.0, which would be a response equal to the depth. The 3-day designs sit at 0 because only about one day of the event remains after day 2.

docs.title: Event-free month
docs.text:
Caption: C1 at D5 in 2025-10, a month with no verified load-shift: stages 1 and 2 of the same network. The lag encoder's contribution in the same month is in free_C1_D5_stage_3_and_lag_contribution.svg. Its mean absolute size over all 16 Primaries is about 4 points of capacity (5th to 95th percentile -13 to +7), so it is a baseline and not only a reaction to an event.

In the event-free month, stage 1's median is within 0.25 of capacity of the full network's median on 96.1% (P5), 96.2% (C1), and 98.0% (A1) of the 23,704 event-free rows, so the mean-embedding probe gave plausible output and no linear heads were needed. The mean band widths (q95 minus q05, share of capacity) grow from 0.217 (stage 1) through 0.229 (stage 2) to 0.245 (P5 stage 3).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Response of the lag encoder to the injected depth (designs of 7 days or longer, 16 Primaries, bootstrap interval over Primaries): P5 0.143 (0.122 to 0.162), C1 0.089 (0.070 to 0.110), A1 0.086 (0.069 to 0.105).
  • What the synthetic-shift fine-tune changed (paired, same Primary and design): C1 minus P5 -0.054 (-0.061 to -0.046); A1 minus P5 -0.057 (-0.073 to -0.040). The response is lower, not higher, for both.
  • Predictions: P1 held (96% to 98%, threshold 90%). P2 failed as registered (C1 0.09, A1 0.09, floor 0.1); P5 (0.14) was not part of the registered claim. P3 failed: P5's response is larger than C1's.
  • Choice made after seeing the data: the headline responses use designs of 7 days or longer, because the 3-day designs sit at 0 (only about one day of the event remains after day 2). Over all 12 designs the means are P5 0.108, C1 0.067, and A1 0.065, so the conclusions are the same.
  • Count of tests: 0 (descriptive). Minimum detectable effect: the interval half-widths above, 0.01 to 0.02.
  • Arms and data: P5 is experiment 574, C1 is experiment 584, A1 is experiment 591. The injected designs come from the bank of experiment 581 and the real pair from experiment 580. Inference only, seed 0, stored weights, about 15 minutes on the GPU.
  • Extra measures (maintainer, 2026-11-06): the weather-only stage and the two sensitivity measures use the same stored weights and one extra pass of the probe, about 0.3 GPU-h in all.
  • Not scored: no CRPS, tail coverage, or curtailment cost, because no forecast here is a candidate.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• The sensitivity measures are not attention. Leave-one-out and gradient times input describe how the trained mixer reacts to its inputs, not how it weighs them.
  • The probe is off-distribution. Stages 1 and 2 show what the mixer reads from the encoders it is given, not a trained forecaster. Frozen linear heads were not needed (P1 held) and were not run.
  • One seed and one injected Primary in the plots. The response-share numbers use all 16 Primaries; the time series figures show D5 (injected, event-free) and D5 and D16 (December).
  • Labels are imperfect. The real pair is one event, so its numbers are descriptive.
  • Next step. Experiment 591 tried an auxiliary depth loss, and its response is the A1 value above (0.09).

docs.title: Does perturbing the lagged power in pre-training and step 2, and keeping the first half of the mixer through every training stage, make the demand network follow a load-shift less than the network of experiment 584 (C1)?
docs.text:
Take-home message. Showing the demand network synthetic load-shifts earlier in training, and freezing the first half of its mixer, did not make the forecast band hold the normal running arrangement on more rows after a load-shift. The band held it on fewer rows, because the bands were narrower. At the eight MVA Primaries the median's error fell by about 10% (J3), and at the six MW Primaries it did not fall. This is a one-month screen, so it stops the idea and does not measure it finely. Verdict: not supported.

We asked whether the demand network of experiment 584 (arm C1, here called J0) would behave better after a load-shift if it saw synthetic load-shifts from the first training step. The network trains in three steps: pre-training on ERA5 and CAMS weather, then step 2 (a fresh output stage on the whole ensemble history), then a daily fine-tune (step 3). J0 sees synthetic load-shifts in step 3 only. We also asked whether splitting the mixer (the layers that combine the encoder outputs) into a kept first stage and a refitted second stage, and letting the second stage read the raw encoder outputs, would help.

We added synthetic load-shifts to the lagged power of every Primary in December 2025. (A Primary is a substation that feeds the lower-voltage network. The eight MVA Primaries and the six MW Primaries are the two metering groups.) Then we measured how often the normal running arrangement, the power without the shift, stayed inside the forecast's q05-q95 band. The synthetic shifts follow experiment 581, and the three-step recipe follows experiment 574.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms start from experiment 584's recipe (C1) and share its rows, refit days 0 and 14, seeds 0 and 1, and the five development test months (this pilot ran 2025-12 only). The core is the concatenation [hw, hd, hl, emb] of the weather, datetime, and lag encoder outputs and the Primary embedding (width wide). The synthetic shifts are experiment 581's: 5% of the time, lag- only, depths of 15%, 30%, and 50% of capacity, lengths of 3, 7, 15, and 30 days, random sign, clean targets. "Perturb" means "add these synthetic load-shifts to the lagged power".

  • J0: stored C1 (perturbation in step 3 only; unsplit mixer).
  • J1: unsplit mixer; perturbation in pre-training and step 3.
  • J2: unsplit mixer; perturbation in pre-training, step 2, and step 3.
  • J3: split mixer, perturbation in all three stages. Stage 1 is Linear(wide, 64), GELU, dropout, learnt in pre-training and frozen (and held in evaluation mode) in steps 2 and 3. Stage 2 is a fresh mlp(hidden 64, 1 hidden layer, 9 outputs) on [h1, spread, lead] in steps 2 and 3 (on h1 alone in pre-training). The total depth equals the unsplit mixer's.
  • J3c: as J3, perturbation in step 3 only.
  • J4: as J3, but stage 2 reads [h1, hw, hd, hl, spread, lead], the raw outputs of the three encoders beside stage 1's output.
  • J4b: as J4, without the lag encoder: stage 2 reads [h1, hw, hd, spread, lead].
  • J5: as J3, with a residual stage 1: h1 = core + g(core), where g is Linear(wide, 64), GELU, dropout, Linear(64, wide), so the dimensions match and the raw embeddings reach stage 2 through the residual path. Stage 2 reads [h1, spread, lead] (width wide + 9).

J3, J3c, J4, J4b, and J5 freeze stage 1 after pre-training. J3, J4, J4b, and J5 perturb in all three stages; J3c perturbs in step 3 only.

docs.title: Coverage by arm
docs.text: Share of rows with the normal running arrangement inside the q05-q95 band, on injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, 24-120 h ahead, December 2025. Each arm has three dots, one per phase. Compare each arm's day 4 to end and 0-7 days after the end dots with J0's: in both metering groups, no arm is above J0 in either phase. The 7-14 days after the end dots are above J0 for most arms at the eight MVA Primaries. Nominal coverage is 0.90. Pilot month only, so no intervals.

docs.title: Results (pilot month 2025-12, descriptive)
docs.text:
The predictions are P1 to P6 in the front matter. Below, "cover90" is the share of rows inside the q05-q95 band, and "median error" is the median forecast's absolute error against the normal running arrangement. The stored scorer has no follow ratio, so the median error stands in for it.

  • P1 fails: no arm raises coverage by 0.02 or more over J0. Day 4 to end, eight MVA Primaries: J0 0.893, J1 0.877, J2 0.852, J3 0.883, J3c 0.876, J4 0.873, J4b 0.857, J5 0.872. Six MW Primaries: J0 0.830, J1 0.791, J2 0.755, J3 0.729, J3c 0.792, J4 0.744, J4b 0.693, J5 0.742. 0-7 days after the end: eight MVA J0 0.912 against 0.886 to 0.910 for the others; six MW J0 0.905 against 0.787 to 0.890.
  • The bands are narrower. Width of the q05-q95 band (capacity fraction) on day 4 to end, eight MVA Primaries: J0 0.267, J3 0.232. Six MW Primaries: J0 0.209, J3 0.160. J3c is about as wide as J0.
  • The median error falls only at the eight MVA Primaries. 0-7 days after the end, eight MVA: J0 0.0643, J1 0.0604, J2 0.0587, J3 0.0578, J4 0.0583, J4b 0.0592, J5 0.0592, and J3c higher at 0.0658. Six MW: J0 0.0467, J3 0.0476, J3c 0.0498, so no arm is clearly lower. The follow clause of P1 was not tested.
  • P3 (event-free rows) partly holds. Event-free cover90 at the six MW Primaries falls from 0.890 (J0) to 0.867 (J3) and 0.854 (J4). At the eight MVA Primaries it ranges from 0.893 (J5) to 0.911 (J4). The pinball loss of the q05-q95 band at the eight MVA Primaries is lower than J0's in every arm except J3c. At the six MW Primaries it is lower than J0's 0.654 for J3 (0.633), J4b (0.622), and J5 (0.625), and equal or higher for J1 (0.678), J2 (0.654), J3c (0.660), and J4 (0.656). No minimum detectable effect was computed in this pilot.
  • P4 (J3 minus J3c) is not positive everywhere. Day 4 to end: 0.883 against 0.876 at the eight MVA Primaries, and 0.729 against 0.792 at the six MW Primaries.
  • P2, P5, and P6 (refit absorption) were not tested. The manager's cut stopped the run after the pilot. The cut kept an arm only if it beat J0 by 0.01 on coverage on day 4 to the end or 0-7 days after the end, and no arm did.
  • Later phase. 7-14 days after the end, every arm except J4b exceeds J0 at the eight MVA Primaries (0.925 to 0.961 against 0.914). At the six MW Primaries only J1 exceeds J0 (0.970 against 0.961). That phase is outside the decision rule.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed.
  • The median error beside the coverage contrast: the third bullet above.
  • Triggers: trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction) fired for P1. A fresh Sonnet audit (report briefs/e603_audit.md, private folder) re-derived all 32 coverage cells from the stored injected-bank forecasts and matched the tables to 1e-6. Its findings, all accepted:
    • Narrower bands. Rescaling each band about its median to J0's width closes the gap at day 4 to the end in both groups for J1, J2, J3, J4, J4b, and J5 (J3: eight MVA -0.010 becomes +0.029, six MW -0.101 becomes +0.027). It does not close it for J3c, whose band is 1% to 3% wider than J0's yet covers 0.018 to 0.038 less. The rescaling is a blunt control, because the shift pushes the median to one side.
    • No re-run control for J0. J0 is experiment 584's stored fit. Every other arm re-ran pre-training and step 2 with this experiment's code, and no unsplit, clean pre-training arm exists. J1's and J3c's gaps of 0.016 to 0.039 are the size that re-training could produce. The six MW deficits of J3 (-0.10 and -0.08) are far larger.
    • Leave-one-Primary-out. No single Primary flips the sign of J3 minus J0 in any group and phase. With Primaries as the resampling unit, the eight MVA gap for J3 is indistinguishable from zero (interval -0.030 to +0.007), and the six MW gap is not (-0.171 to -0.054).
    • Event counting. The 15 and 30 day events give identical 0-7 days after the end rows, so an event bootstrap over them would be too narrow in that phase.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One fold month (December 2025), two seeds, J0 not re-run (see Checks), injected shifts only, no intervals, and no Bonferroni count. The fold pair 2025-10 and 2025-12 was not run.
  • The real December 2025 pair, the tail quantiles, and the avoidable-curtailment cost were not scored.
  • Pre-training sees ERA5 and CAMS analysis weather, so a distrust of lags learnt there may not transfer to the ensemble stages. The pilot cannot separate that from other explanations.
  • The pilot's pre-training changed the day lag of 3.6% of finite pre-training rows (printed by e00603_arm.py).
  • Code reused from experiments 574, 581, 583, and 584.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • A band that is wider where the lags look unusual (the gated band of experiment 584) addresses coverage directly. Whether to run it is a decision for the plan, not this page.

docs.title: What would a pilot that backtests the best demand forecast at the 2 bulk supply points and 2 grid supply points need, and what would it cost?
docs.text:
A pilot that backtests a forecast of the 2 bulk supply points (BSPs) and 2 grid supply points (GSPs) is affordable and its data are clean; the projected cost is about 1.9 GPU-h, against a ceiling of 6 GPU-h. The projection is an estimate scaled from the fit times of other experiments, and a timed pilot fit must confirm it before the full run. No network was fitted for this page and no forecast was scored.

The design below answers six questions. The ranked recommendation is at the end.

docs.title: 1. The four series
docs.text:
All four are signed "Raw Flow" series in MW, not MVA, from NGED's metadata. History comes from the raw power table, and flagged shares from the cleaned table. All readings are read on 2026-11-06.

Table 1. The 4 series. Capacity is the effective capacity (MW) in data/effective_capacity, dated 2026-09-22, which the data-check script prints.

Series id Name Kind Naming First reading Clean half-hours Flagged share Negative share Median of clean readings (MW) Capacity (MW) 1 Boston 33kV BSP D17 2021-11-29 75,288 0.05% 9.2% 22.6 47.6 2 Skegness 33kV BSP D13 2019-09-17 125,099 0.004% 1.2% 31.7 55.3 27 Walpole 132kV GSP D6 2019-09-14 125,105 0.12% 32% 88.2 384.3 28 Bicker Fen 132kV GSP D1 2019-09-11 122,692 0.89% 69% -39.8 170.9
  • Every flagged half-hour is an exact-zero reading (the substation_zero rule). No other cleaning rule fired.
  • D1 mostly exports. Its median is -40 MW, and 69% of its clean half-hours are negative, so it behaves like a net generator for most of the year. Embedded wind and solar sit inside this reading.
  • Coverage by month. In all five development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), all 4 series have 99.9% to 100% of their half-hours present and clean. The 0.07% gap in 2026-03 is one missing half-hour in each of the 4 series.
  • Gaps outside the development months. D17 has data only from 2021-11-29 and about two thirds of 2022-07 is missing. D1 has 2 gaps that matter: 2025-08 (57% clean) and 2025-09 (42% clean), and smaller gaps in 2025-01 and 2025-04. D1's September 2025 gap lies just before the 2025-10 fold, so the weekly lag may be missing at D1 for the first days of that fold.
  • History before each fold. In the 24 months before each of the five fold starts, D17, D13, and D6 have all but at most 2 half-hours of 35,040. D1 has 33,351 (95.2%), because of the 2025 gap.

Figure 1. Weekly mean power of the 4 series. Look at the grid supply point D1 (purple): its level rises from about -60 MW in 2021 to near zero in 2026, which is a drift of 60 MW inside a series of 170 MW capacity. D17 starts near 0 MW in November 2021, when almost all of its first month is flagged zero readings.

docs.title: 2. The grid supply points are not copies of the bulk supply points
docs.text:
Experiment 563 read the hierarchy file and wrote that a grid supply point "should include one bulk supply point", so the two series are probably close. I compared the cleaned series on the half-hours when both are clean.

Table 2. Grid supply point minus the bulk supply point beneath it, by hierarchy file.

Pair Correlation, all years Correlation, 2026 Mean of GSP, 2026 (MW) Mean of BSP, 2026 (MW) Standard deviation of GSP minus BSP, 2026 (MW) Walpole (D6) over Boston (D17) 0.30 0.41 164 19 126 Bicker Fen (D1) over Skegness (D13) -0.51 -0.67 4.5 29.6 89
  • A bulk supply point is a small share of its grid supply point. Boston's mean is 12% of Walpole's in 2026.
  • The residual is as large as the grid supply point itself. The standard deviation of GSP minus BSP is 126 MW, against 131 MW for Walpole alone.
  • At Bicker Fen the correlation is negative. The residual of GSP minus BSP carries generation that the bulk supply point does not.

Figure 2. Two pairs, 14 days from 2026-06-08. Look at the top panel: Walpole (D6, orange) moves with a daily shape that Boston (D17, blue) does not share. Look at the bottom panel: Bicker Fen (D1, purple) swings between about -85 and +220 MW, and is below zero in 43% of these 14 days (69% of clean half-hours over all years), while Skegness (D13, light blue) stays positive.

The consequence is that the leak risk named in the brief for experiment 564 (a GSP's target as an input for its child BSP) is real but small. A lag-free network reads no power, so it cannot leak. A lag network that pools a GSP with its BSP reads each series' own past power only, and the two series are not close enough for one to stand in for the other.

docs.title: 3. What each network class needs
docs.text:
A class is a fixed combination of three parts: power lags, the gate, and the output offset. "D5 offset" is the name that experiment 565 and experiment 572 give to the slow per-series output offset (it is unrelated to the Primary D5). Each class is pooled across the 2 BSPs and, separately, across the 2 GSPs; the second row of each need applies to both groups.

Table 3. The three classes, in the order of their cost.

(c) Lag-free (b) Lag without gate (a) Lag and gate Built from E2 of experiment 572 C1 of experiment 584 C2 of experiment 584, or the G4 gate of experiment 597 Reads power No Yes: lags of 1 day and 1 week, at least 24 h old Same as (b) D5 offset Yes, learnt in pretraining Yes Yes Extra training None One extra fine-tune with synthetic lag-only load-shifts per fold month, refit day, and seed Same as (b) Extra at forecast time None None The gate state and a "lags-masked twin" of the same weights Capacity Effective capacity from the table above (constant per series) Same Same

The needs shared by all three classes:

  • Weather. The run issued at or before the forecast origin minus 9 h, mapped to the series by its resolution 5 H3 cell. All 4 cells are in data/h3_grid_weights.parquet (experiment 563).
  • Lead range. 0 to 240 h. The stored backtests in backtest_export_2026-11-06/ reach only 120 h, so the pilot must score 120 to 240 h as experiment 600 does (the ensemble weather runs must carry 10 days).
  • Series type input. The one-hot Primary, BSP, or GSP input of experiment 564, because the 4 series are pooled with at most 2 others.
  • Pooling. Pooling "across the 2 BSPs and the 2 GSPs separately" gives two networks of 2 series each. Experiment 564 found that a network pooled with the Primaries forecasts these 4 series better than a climatology (CRPS 5.0 to 18.4 against 6.8 to 23.1 at 24 to 120 h), so I treat the Primaries as free extra training rows in the first design (below) and as a variant, not a requirement.
  • Gate (class a only). The gate fires on a load-shift. The verified set of experiment 580 covers Primaries, and I found no verified load-shift at these 4 series. The gate would therefore be untested and probably idle here.

docs.title: 4. What the earlier experiments found
docs.text:
Table 4. Earlier BSP and GSP experiments, in date order. "Points" are points of effective capacity of CRPS (lower is better) unless stated.

Experiment Question Finding Verdict 21 Does a 14-day additive error correction help? +0.36 (-0.19 to +0.98) at the 4 series; bias fell at the GSPs without lowering the score inconclusive 27 Do PV_Live lags help at the 2 GSPs? -0.03 (-0.13 to +0.09) refuted 28 Does a solar forecast help at the 2 GSPs? -0.14 (-0.34 to +0.04) inconclusive 36 Do children's forecasts help? +0.04 and +0.19 at the BSPs inconclusive 124 Does a BSP closure hint help? Worse on clean data by at least 0.385 not supported 161 Top-down or bottom-up at a BSP? Bottom-up 0.026 and 0.035 worse inconclusive 204 All children in the sum? +0.005 and -0.011 inconclusive 223 Do generators sit inside the BSP reading? All 7 coefficients non-zero, none cleanly -1 or 0 inconclusive 386 GAM stack against the weekly XGBoost model (BG2) GAM worse by 1.02 (BSPs) and 2.01 (GSPs), days 1 to 10 refuted 415 A pooled neural network with lags (N1) N1 minus BG2: -0.47 (BSPs, -0.67 to -0.23); -0.02 (GSPs, -0.15 to +0.13) supported 564 A lag-free modular network pooled with the Primaries Better than climatology at all 4; no gain for the Primaries not supported

The best recipe left by these results is experiment 415's N1, with BG2 as the reference to beat. N1 is a pooled neural network with lags, a node-type input, and training on the 4 series plus the Primaries. It beat BG2 at the BSPs in all four test months, and tied it at the GSPs. N1 is a 3-seed average and BG2 a single fit, so part of the gap may come from seed averaging. The other evidence is negative: children's forecasts, error correction, PV_Live, and a closure hint did not help, so I do not carry them into the pilot.

Two limits of this table matter for the pilot. First, no experiment has tested the modular recipe of experiments 572 to 597 at these 4 series, so N1 is the best evidence and not the best-known recipe at the Primaries. Second, the experiments used different months and different row sets (415 used four months; 564 used five), so their scores cannot be compared with each other.

docs.title: 5. Folds
docs.text:
• The five development months are 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06, as in the stored backtests. All four series are present and clean in each (Section 1).
  • Refits are coarse, on day 0 and day 14 of each month, with seeds 0 and 1.
  • July 2026 is not touched. The pilot scripts must exclude 2026-07 from every fit and score.
  • Leak rule. A fit sees only rows before the fold's cutoff minus 3.5 h, the leak rule in the brief for experiment 564. A parent series contains its children's power, so a GSP's target is never an input for its BSP.
  • Training history. D17 has at least 24 clean months before every fold. D1 has 95.2% of 24 months before every fold, and the pilot should print the share per fold.

docs.title: 6. GPU-hour projection
docs.text:
I did not time a fit for this page. The projection scales from the fit times that other experiments report, and it is a guess until a timed pilot confirms it.

  • Basis. A fine-tune takes about 10 seconds (experiment 584). A three-arm, two-seed, coarse-refit run of experiment 599 took about 0.55 GPU-h, which is about 0.09 GPU-h per arm and seed. Experiment 554 used about 3.5 GPU-h for pretraining and 1,377 daily fits.
  • A pooled network is fitted once per group, not once per series. The count of fits does not grow with the number of series.

Table 5. Projected GPU-h (every cell is a guess scaled from the basis above: 0.09 GPU-h per arm and seed, 0.55 GPU-h divided by 3 arms and 2 seeds, scaled by the fine-tune count). A group is the 2 BSPs or the 2 GSPs. Each class is fitted for 2 groups and 2 seeds. Pretraining is one run per group, and is not shared with the Primaries.

Class Fine-tunes Per group and seed Total (2 groups, 2 seeds) (c) Lag-free 10 per seed 0.09 0.36 (b) Lag without gate 20 per seed (adds the synthetic-shift fine-tune) 0.15 0.60 (a) Lag and gate As (b), plus gate inference 0.17 0.68 Pretraining, 2 groups 0.3 (guess) Whole pilot about 1.9

The sum is about 1.9 GPU-h, below the ceiling of 6 GPU-h, so I do not need to stop and ask. The pretraining line is the least certain: 4 series are far fewer than the 16 Primaries, so the run should be quick, but I have no timing. Pretraining on all 20 series (the variant that pools with the Primaries) would raise the total, and the timed pilot fit must price it.

docs.title: 7. Risks
docs.text:
• Electrical hierarchy. The Primaries sum into the BSPs. In experiments 161 and 204, the Primaries with a long history covered 42% and 56% of capacity at the two BSPs, and the sum added no skill. The pilot should not use a bottom-up sum.
  • Generators netted into the series. The GSP readings contain embedded generation: D1 is negative for 69% of its clean half-hours. Experiment 223 found that the BSPs' readings move with the metered generators beneath them, with coefficients that were not -1. A forecast of D1 is therefore partly a forecast of wind and solar, which a demand network that reads weather may handle only partly. No generator's series or name appears on this page.
  • Short history. D17 has 5 years of data, and its first month of 2021-11 is almost empty. The other three have 7 years. All four are far shorter than the 16 Primaries' best-case history, and a pooled network of 2 series has little to share. Experiment 564 found that 4 extra series do not change what the shared encoders learn.
  • No verified load-shift. The gate (class a) is untestable here. Any gate result would rest on injected shifts only.
  • A drift of 60 MW at D1. Figure 1 shows a slow level change, which the D5 offset is designed to absorb. Class (c) with the offset is the class most likely to follow it.
  • Labels are incomplete. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so a clean half-hour may hold an unlabelled event.

docs.title: Ranked recommendation
docs.text:
1. Design 1: lag-free network with the D5 offset (class c), pooled per group. A variant adds the 16 Primaries to the training rows, as experiment 564 did. It reads no power, so it cannot leak across the hierarchy. It is the cheapest class (about 0.4 GPU-h without the variant), it was already shown to beat a climatology at all 4 series in experiment 564, and the D5 offset handles the D1 drift. Its weak point is that it has not been compared with BG2 at these series on the five development months. Add BG2, manual_heuristic, and climatology as stored references.
  2. Design 2: lag network without the gate (class b), pooled per group. It is the closest to experiment 415's N1, the one recipe that beat BG2 at the BSPs. It costs about 0.6 GPU-h. Pooling per group gives 2 series per network, so treat each result as a case study with n = 2.
  3. Design 3: lag and gate (class a), pooled per group, as a report-only extra. It has no verified load-shift to test it on, so its only evidence would be injected shifts. Run it only if Design 2 is cheap and the reviewers want the gate's behaviour at a node. It costs about 0.7 GPU-h.

Total of the three designs: about 1.9 GPU-h. The pilot's output is the layout of backtest_export_2026-11-06/: one Parquet file per design and month, with the columns time_series_id, power_fcst_init_time, valid_time, lead_hours, q01 to q99, observed_power, and unit (always MW here), and a README. The columns nra_power, in_verified_event, event_id, and gate_on would be empty or false at these 4 series, except gate_on in class (a).

docs.title: Is the data for the final bake-off test complete and clean?
docs.text:
The recorded power and the stored weather forecasts for the final test are nearly complete, but every cached input file we listed stops before the end of the test window. A cached input is a file built from the stored tables, which a candidate trains and scores on. The final test is the one held-out test (forecasts issued from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31) on which each release candidate, meaning a model proposed for production, is scored once. We asked whether the stored power readings and the stored weather forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble (ENS) cover those four months cleanly. We counted the missing and flagged half-hours of each series in each month, counted missing daily ensemble runs, and listed the newest date in each of the 11 cached input files. No forecast and no forecast error was read. A Primary is a 33 kV to 11 kV substation. Separately, the solar and wind farms report no half-hours of exactly zero power after 2026-03-26.

Two of three predictions held, so the verdict is partly supported. Prediction P2 held: no ensemble run is missing. Prediction P1 failed: every series would miss under 2% of half-hours in each test month, but the three wind farms and four Primaries (Stickney, both Wrangle transformers, and Kirton) miss more in at least one month. Prediction P3 held: the derived inputs stop early. Nothing here is adopted for production.

Colour is the share of a month's half-hours with no stored reading. Solar farms are left out and shown in the next figure. Months marked (dev) are the five development months. Months not drawn: 2025-11, 2026-02, and 2026-04.

Each point is the share of a month's stored half-hours that read exactly 0, over six solar farms (top) and three wind farms (bottom). Both drop to 0 in April 2026. March ends on the 26th, so the March point is lower than a full month.

A green dot reaches the end of the test window. An orange dot stops before it.

docs.title: Power
docs.text:
• Demand series are complete. The 8 Primaries metered in MVA, the 8 metered in MW, and the 4 bulk and grid supply points each miss 0.0% to 0.5% of half-hours across July to October, except Stickney (2.0%) and the two Wrangle transformers (1.7% and 2.3%). The development months miss 0.0% to 0.9%, pooled over the five months. Stickney lost 48.5 hours ending 2026-07-08, and 10 series lost the same 6.5 hours on 2026-08-28 (20:30 UTC).
  • No half-hour is flagged from 2026-05 onward. The cleaning rule substation_zero is the only drop_reason in the table. It flags 183 half-hours in the five development months (169 of them at one Wrangle transformer in October 2025) and none from May to October 2026.
  • The raw and cleaned tables hold the same rows, 561,278 for these 29 series since 2025-09-01.
  • Wind farms miss more. W1, W2, and W3 miss 7.6%, 1.7%, and 6.1% of half-hours in July to October, against 0.9%, 0.4%, and 1.2% in the development months. They have 31, 3, and 12 gaps longer than 3 hours.
  • Solar farms need a different count. Night half-hours are absent, so the solar group's missing share is 33% to 62% a month from May. In the four middle daylight hours (10:00 to 14:00 UTC), farm E misses 73% in July and 70% in October, farm D misses 2% to 18% a month, and farms A, B, C, and F miss under 2% apart from three months (A 6% in October, B 8% in August, F 16% in May).

docs.title: Generators have no exact-zero readings from late March 2026
docs.text: The nine solar and wind series have no half-hour reading exactly 0 after 2026-03-26. The last zero is between 2026-03-23 and 2026-03-26 at all nine, so the change falls within four days at all nine and probably sits in how the source reports, not in any one farm. In the six full months before March, solar farms read 0 in 47% to 68% of half-hours a month and wind farms in 0.3% to 4.8%. The cause is not determined: the list of files the ingest has downloaded only starts on 2026-04-27, and the ingest code holds no zero filter. A missing generator half-hour therefore can mean night, calm, or a fault. Scoring on the rows present would drop the zero-output half-hours that the development months include, so the development and test scores would not be comparable.

docs.title: Ensemble weather
docs.text:
• Every daily ENS run exists. All 432 runs from 2025-09-01 to 2026-11-06 are present, so none of the 214 runs from 2026-04-01 to 2026-10-31 is missing. Every run holds 51 members, 1,671 grid cells, 85 valid times, and a 360-hour horizon, and no run has more than 5% nulls in five checked columns.
  • The derived inputs stop early. The ensemble summaries, the version with wind components, and the cloud-cover table all end with the run of 2026-06-30. The cloud-cover table also starts on 2025-11-21, so it misses the October 2025 development month.
  • The other cached inputs stop between 2024-03 and 2026-10-14 (third figure): the observed-power cache on 2026-10-14, the ERA5 stage-1 and wind-component tables on 2026-07-31, the ERA5 and CAMS site tables on 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-11, and the ERA5 farm-cell table on 2024-03-31.

docs.title: Assertions
docs.text:
• Run timing holds. For all 123 origins (daily, 09:00 UTC), the newest ENS run issued at or before the origin minus 9 hours is that day's 00:00 UTC run, and the run exists with all 51 members and a 360-hour horizon.
  • Lag ages hold. Across the 123 origins and a 10-day horizon, no capped day or week lag (experiment 558's recipe, used by the v3 and 24-hour-cap designs) is stamped less than 24 hours before the origin. The day lag holds a reading for 99.35%, 98.55%, 100.0%, and 99.99% of targets in July, August, September, and October; the worst origin is 88.9% (August).
  • This is not yet a row-by-row check. No feature frame exists for these origins, so the assertion covers the timing rules. The origin-timing assertion only detects a missing run, because the origin and the cut-off share the same 9 hours. The experiment that builds the frames repeats the check on the frames themselves.
  • Actuals limit the last origins. Power ends on 2026-11-06 at 08:00, so a 10-day horizon is fully scorable for origins up to 2026-10-26 and a 14-day horizon up to 2026-10-22. Every origin reaches its 10-day horizon on 2026-11-11 once the daily ingest has run.
