docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether the source stopped reporting zero readings from the generators, so that the generators' final-test scores can be compared with their development scores.

docs.title: Which inputs should the lag encoder of the demand network read so that it follows a load-shift less: the lag's identity or age, the expected-input embeddings, the gap between a lag and the lag-free forecast, weighted averages of that gap, or the gaps at the electrical neighbours?
docs.text:
We asked whether the demand neural network can learn to follow a load-shift less if its lag encoder is given more than the lag itself. A load-shift moves part of one Primary substation's demand onto a neighbour for days or weeks. "Follow" is the share of the injected depth that the forecast's median moves with the shifted lags (lower is better). The lag encoder is the part of the A1 network (experiment 591) that reads the two lagged power readings. The lag-free forecast is the same network's forecast with its lags removed (experiment 598). The gap is a lag minus the lag-free forecast at the lag's own time. The coverage of a forecast is the share of rows where the normal running arrangement (NRA) lies inside the q05-q95 band.

We fine-tuned A1 on synthetic lag-only load-shifts (experiment 584), with different extra inputs on the lag encoder, and scored it on injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts in the months 2025-10 and 2025-12. Weighted gap averages (P5) cut follow from 0.119 to 0.065, and neighbour summaries (P7) cut it to 0.035. The same networks fed noise follow 0.117 to 0.118, so the inputs carry the gain. At R's band width (experiment 597, A1 plus the hand-built G4 gate) P7 covers 0.932 of rows from day 4 to the end and R covers 0.928.

Verdict: partly supported. The predictions that held: P5 beats P4 by more than 0.01, and P5 beats its noise placebo by more than 0.02. The predictions that failed: the per-lag gap does not lower follow by 0.015 (P3), and the own-plus-sum column does not matter (P7 against P7b). Three predictions are untestable on two fold months because the minimum detectable effect exceeds the margin: neighbours lower follow by a further 0.01, P7 beats its noise placebo by 0.02, and R covers at least 0.01 more than P7 at R's width (the point estimate is 0.005 in P7's favour). The cost: event-free continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) is higher than A1's at both metering groups in point estimate. Experiment 606 ran on two fold months and two seeds, and no arm was run on the remaining three development months.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Follow, injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, day 4 to the end, 24-120 h ahead. Look at the drop from A1 (0.119) to P5 (0.065) and P7 (0.035), and at the two placebos (P5-p, P7-p), which sit on A1.

Share of rows with the NRA inside q05-q95, by phase of an injected load-shift, 24-120 h ahead. Look at P5 and P7 at their native width (close to A1) and at their width-matched versions (-rs, close to R). Coverage is scored against the estimated NRA.

Event-free CRPS minus A1's, by arm and metering group. Look at the six MW Primaries, where P5, P6, P7, P7b, and P7c cost more than at the eight MVA Primaries.

The December 2025 pair (D5 and D16, the maintainer's example event), day-ahead forecasts from 14 days before the onset to 14 days after the end. The observed readings match the maintainer's dates (see the printed window match). Look at whether the median moves with the shifted readings (in the figure it does not for A1, R, P5, or P7) and at the band width inside the shaded span. The real pair is descriptive: one pair, with imperfect labels.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Numbers are from score/arm_summary.csv and score/contrasts.csv in the private data folder. Intervals are at the Bonferroni level (12 counted contrasts, alpha 0.05/12 = 0.0042), resampling (month, Primary) clusters, 24 clusters from 288 Primary-events. "MDE" is the minimum detectable effect, half the interval's width.

Arm Follow, day 4 to end Coverage, day 4 to end Coverage, 0-7 days after Width-matched coverage, day 4 to end A1 0.119 0.884 0.917 not applicable R 0.119 0.928 0.956 not applicable P3 0.114 0.891 0.921 0.908 P4 0.110 0.893 0.925 0.912 P5 0.065 0.894 0.927 0.929 P6 0.064 0.895 0.929 0.930 P7 0.035 0.886 0.920 0.932 P7b 0.039 0.889 0.922 0.933 P7c 0.052 0.887 0.923 0.931 P5-q 0.023 0.857 0.890 0.945 P7-q 0.029 0.840 0.858 0.932 P5-p (noise) 0.118 0.884 0.917 0.908 P7-p (noise) 0.117 0.883 0.917 0.909

Contrasts (follow differences are over Primary-events paired on month, pass, and Primary):

Contrast Difference Interval MDE Pre-registered margin P3 minus A1, follow -0.005 -0.015 to 0.005 0.010 0.015 (failed) P4 minus P3, follow -0.004 -0.004 to -0.003 0.001 not applicable P5 minus P4, follow -0.045 -0.052 to -0.038 0.007 0.010 (held) P7 minus P5, follow -0.030 -0.069 to -0.007 0.031 0.010 (point estimate held; MDE above the margin, so untestable) P7 minus P7b, follow -0.004 -0.008 to 0.002 0.005 0.005 (failed) R minus P7-rs, coverage, day 4 to end -0.005 -0.022 to 0.013 0.018 0.010 (untestable: MDE above the margin; point estimate favours P7-rs) R minus P7-rs, coverage, 0-7 days after 0.002 -0.009 to 0.014 0.012 0.010 (untestable: MDE above the margin) P5 minus P5-p, follow -0.053 -0.070 to -0.037 0.017 0.020 (held) P7 minus P7-p, follow -0.082 -0.136 to -0.047 0.044 0.020 (point estimate held; MDE above the margin, so untestable) P7-q minus P7, follow -0.006 -0.032 to 0.020 0.026 not applicable P5-q minus P5, follow -0.043 -0.057 to -0.029 0.014 not applicable P7 minus A1, event-free CRPS, eight MVA Primaries 0.021 0.019 to 0.024 0.002 0.030 (within) P7 minus A1, event-free CRPS, six MW Primaries 0.068 0.010 to 0.126 0.058 0.030 (exceeds; flag)

The gap at the lag's own time does little; its weighted history does most of the work. P3 gives the encoder the per-lag gap and lowers follow by 0.005. The sustain count (P4) adds 0.004. The weighted averages at half-lives of 1, 3, and 7 days (P5) add 0.045, which is the largest single step. Adding the sustain count to P5 (P6) changes nothing (0.064).

Neighbour summaries lower follow further, and the injected bank flatters them. P7 follows 0.035, P7b (no own-plus-neighbours sum) 0.039, and P7c (the single best opposite-sign neighbour) 0.052. The own-plus-sum column therefore adds at most 0.004 and the summaries over all neighbours beat the single best neighbour by 0.017 in point estimate. Each injected event mirrors the shift at one neighbour by construction, so the injected bank favours every neighbour input. A real transfer may split across several neighbours or leave the 16 Primaries, and only one real pair is verified. The target-side bank of experiment 595 (events in the targets as well as the lags) was not run.

The paired perturbation lowered follow, native-width coverage, and band width together. In P5-q and P7-q, step 2 and step 3 both see a shift at one Primary and a smaller opposite shift (half the megawatts) in the lags of one neighbour. Follow fell for P5 (0.065 to 0.023). Coverage at native width fell (0.894 to 0.857 for P5) and the band is narrower (0.201 against 0.235); the tables do not separate the two effects. Rescaled to R's width, P5-q covers 0.945 and P7-q 0.932. P7-q does not follow less than P7 by more than the minimum detectable effect. Event-free CRPS is also worse for the paired arms (P5-q 0.058 and P7-q 0.037 at the eight MVA Primaries; 0.051 and 0.102 at the six MW Primaries).

Event-free CRPS is higher than A1's for every input arm in point estimate. P7 is 0.021 points of capacity worse than A1 at the eight MVA Primaries (interval 0.019 to 0.024) and 0.068 worse at the six MW Primaries (0.010 to 0.126). The first is within the 0.03 margin. The second exceeds it, and its minimum detectable effect (0.058) is large because two fold months are two blocks. By the keep rule of the shared standing rules, this slice cost is a flag and not yet harmful.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Two fold months, two seeds. The five-month comparison was not run. Every interval is wide.
  • Injected events mirror each shift at one neighbour. The neighbour inputs (P7, P7b, P7c) are flattered by construction.
  • The signals come from lag-free forecasts that are in sample in training. The training rows read the lag-free forecast of a network trained on those rows. The safeguard of experiment 598 adds noise where the training-to-test spread ratio is below 0.8, and it reads the test month's observed spread of the gap, a small formal use of test-month information (no target values; one noise standard deviation per column and Primary). The noise is added to each continuous column independently, so the identities between a column and its sum or mean hold exactly at test time and not in training. This weakens the P7 against P7b contrast.
  • The expected-missing flag is 1 where the stored weather table has no row for the lag's valid time (the table holds the smallest-lead row for each valid time); about 0.3% to 0.8% of rows. Its effect on all-rows CRPS was not checked separately.
  • Not run. Per-Primary shares of the expected-missing flag (only the pooled range is quoted), the O2 offset arm, the pre-training variant, the target-side bank with a mirrored neighbour, the removal arms (P0, P1, P2), the best subset scored on the remaining months, and the all-rows CRPS check of the expected-missing flag. The paired-perturbation arms (P5-q, P7-q) ran in step 2 and step 3 and not in pre-training.
  • Labels are imperfect. NGED's logs may miss events, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events, the event-free costs are optimistic, and the real-event slices undercount.
  • Lead range. NGED care about 1 to 10 days ahead; the scored band is 24 to 120 h.

docs.title: Standing practices followed
docs.text: Cleaned data, the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, refits at day 0 and day 14, every fitted network saved in the private data folder, A1 and R reused from experiments 591 and 597, July 2026 unused, weather from the run issued at or before the forecast origin minus 9 h, and lag inputs at least 24 h old (asserted in e00606_signals.py). The code of this experiment is in ml-experiments/00606-nra-lag-encoder-signal-permutations-gap-averages-and-neighbours/; the arm code (e00606_signals.py, e00606_model.py, e00606_arm.py) is meant to be copied by later experiments on the same inputs. This experiment reuses the code of experiments 574, 584, 591, 592, 597, and 598.

docs.title: Plan (as pre-registered; the Not run bullet above lists what was dropped)
docs.text: Standing practices followed. Refit at day 0 and day 14 of each fold month (the coarse cadence of experiments 584, 591, and 598), cleaned data everywhere, the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, every fitted network saved in the data folder, stored predictions of A1 and R reused as controls, the first fold pair screened before the other months, and July 2026 unopened. The advice lists of earlier experiments were read; the plan follows 598's "build signals from out-of-sample lag-free forecasts" advice by keeping its in-sample safeguard and a noise placebo, and departs from its "keep the gate" conclusion only in testing a wider set of inputs.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
All arms start from experiment 591's A1 step-2 weights and its shared lag encoder, and differ only in step 3, the fine-tune on synthetic lag-only load-shifts of experiment 584's C1 (5% of each Primary's time, depths 15, 30, and 50% of capacity, lengths 3, 7, 15, and 30 days, random sign, clean targets). The shifts are applied only in step 3; pre-training and step 2 stay unperturbed (experiment 603 tests perturbing them, and the best arm is rerun with that change if 603 shows it helps). Every extra column is computed from the shifted lags in training and from the real lags at test time, by one code path (e00606_signals.signal_columns): a shifted lag changes the gap, and the lag-free median at the lag's time is unchanged. Gap inputs use only lags and lag-free forecasts at least 24 hours old; the fresh residual is not used. Training rows keep experiment 598's in-sample safeguard: where the training-to-test standard deviation ratio of a continuous column is below 0.8, noise brings the training variance up to the test variance.

The lag encoder of A1 reads, per lag, the lag's value, missing flag, and age, the weather and datetime embeddings of the lag's own time with the freshest weather run issued at or before it (the "expected" inputs), the Primary embedding, and an 8-number lag ID.

Arm Lag encoder reads A1 the control, stored P3 A1 + per-lag gap (4 columns) + expected-missing flag (2) P4 P3 + sustain count (2) P5 P3 + weighted gap averages at half-lives of 1, 3, and 7 days (12 columns), the default design P6 P5 + sustain count P7 P5 + summaries over all electrical neighbours (see below) P7b P7 without the own-plus-neighbours sum P7c P5 + the single best opposite-sign neighbour (not run) the best subset of P3 to P7c, scored on the remaining months O2 the best arm with experiment 577's O2 total-variation penalty on the D5 offsets Q-pair the best neighbour arm and the best non-neighbour arm with the paired perturbation in step 2 and step 3 Q-pre one pre-training variant of the best arm (only if GPU time is left)

Stages. Stage 1: P3 to P7c with the step-3 perturbation only. Stage 2: the best neighbour arm and the best non-neighbour arm again, with the paired perturbation in step 2 and step 3 as well. The paired perturbation lowers demand at one Primary and raises it by a smaller amount at its electrically connected neighbours (a transfer of megawatts split across them), and the neighbour summaries are computed from those perturbed lags. Stage 3, only if GPU time is left: one pre-training variant of the best arm, whose lag-free table T comes from a clean-lag A1 step-2 network of the same fold and seed, held fixed and trained only on rows before the fold's test month. That dependency is circular (pre-training now needs a step-2 network) and is a caveat of the page. The neighbour arms (P7, P7b, P7c) are also scored on a target-side bank with a mirrored neighbour (experiment 595's method), because the lag-only bank rewards any perturbation. At most 2 GPU processes; ceiling 4 GPU-h.

The expected-missing flag is 1 where no stored weather run exists at or before the lag's time (about 0.3% to 0.8% of rows); the page reports its share per Primary and checks that adding it does not change all-rows CRPS by more than the minimum detectable effect.

Neighbours. An electrical neighbour is first one listed in Primary Substation Interconnections.csv, then a sibling under the same bulk supply point among the 16 Primaries; the rule is experiment 592's G4 neighbour table (b400.nged_neighbours(), reused through experiment 598). P7 gives the encoder, for the gap and for each of the three weighted averages at each lag's time, the neighbours' sum, mean, minimum, and maximum (signed, scaled to the Primary's capacity), the sum of the Primary's own value and the neighbours' sum (near zero for a pure transfer), the neighbour count, and a flag that is 1 where the Primary has no neighbour with a gap (all values then zero). The injected events mirror the shift at one neighbour by construction, so the injected bank flatters every neighbour input; a real transfer may split across several neighbours or leave the 16 Primaries, and only one real pair is verified.

Scoring. First fold pair 2025-10 and 2025-12, seeds 0 and 1, the injected bank of 15 and 30 day load-shifts, as in 598. The best arm is then scored on 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. Every arm also has a version rescaled about its median to R's band width, so coverage compares at equal width. The placebo arm replaces the best arm's extra columns with a column-wise resample of the training block. The real December 2025 pair (D5 and D16) is shown descriptively with the maintainer's example event.

docs.title: Can the cached inputs be extended to 2026-10-31 so the final bake-off test can run?
docs.text:
All 11 cached inputs that experiment 605 found stopping early now reach the end of the final test window. A cached input is a file built from stored tables that a model trains and scores on. We rebuilt each one from the production power and ensemble tables, or fetched the missing months from the same free weather services. Then we checked every row of the rebuilt tables against the timing rules. We also asked why solar and wind farms stopped reporting zero readings in late March 2026. The final test is the held-out test, with forecast origins from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31, on which each release candidate (a model proposed for production) is scored once. No forecast and no forecast error was read. This page extends experiment 605.

Two of three predictions held in full and one in part, so the verdict is partly supported. Prediction P1 held for every input. Prediction P2 held: no row breaks the origin or lag rules. Prediction P3 held in part: the site tables reach 2026-10-31 with no duplicate keys, no null cells, and no gap at the join. The wind table is the only site table whose new request overlaps stored hours, and it agrees there exactly. The other site tables start after the stored table ends, so agreement was not tested for them. The extended copies sit beside the stored tables, and no stored table was edited. Nothing here is adopted for production.

Look at the dashed line. Top: before 2026-03-26 solar farms read exactly 0 in 47% to 70% of their half-hours, and wind farms in 0% to 12% of half-hours (weekly pooled); after the line, no reading is exactly 0. Bottom: at the same line, readings per solar farm per day fall from about 44 to about 23 to 32 in April to August (48 is complete), and to about 16 by October as the nights lengthen, because the night half-hours are absent. Wind farms lose a few of 48 (43 to 48 a week).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Ensemble tables. The ensemble summary and the summary with wind components hold 944 runs each (2024-04-01 to 2026-10-31). The cloud-cover summary holds 345 runs (2025-11-21 to 2026-10-31), fetched at about 6 MB a run from Dynamical.org. Each folder holds the 821 and 222 earlier files, hard-linked, so each folder is complete.
  • Observed power. The cache holds 2,376,271 rows for 22 series, to 2026-11-06 14:00 UTC. Its power column equals the stored cache on all 2,352,228 shared rows.
  • ERA5 and CAMS site tables. The Open-Meteo ERA5 irradiance table (20 cells) and wind table (3 wind farms) end on 2026-10-31 23:00. The CAMS tables for 6 solar farms and 22 demand series end on 2026-11-01 00:00 (period-ending stamps). The wind request reproduced the stored table's 1,584 overlapping rows with a largest difference of 0.
  • ERA5 stage-1 box. The 11 x 11 cell block holds 13 variables fetched from the Climate Data Store (2,208 hours, 267,168 rows each) and precipitation type fetched from the Google ARCO-ERA5 store (2.7 GB). On the four overlapping days the largest difference from the stored values is 4e-7 of each variable's maximum (0 for most). Rows are partly ERA5T, the preliminary release: the expver column says which. era5_features and era5_wind_components were rebuilt from it with the existing builders, to 2026-10-31 23:00 (97,152 new rows each), and equal the stored tables on every shared row.
  • Why not ARCO for all of it. One global hourly chunk is about 4 MB, so 14 variables for 2,208 hours would have read about 120 GB, over the limit set for the workstation. The Climate Data Store cuts the box on the server and sent about 6 MB a month. Precipitation type was missing from the Climate Data Store's files, so its 2,208 chunks came from ARCO.

docs.title: Assertions
docs.text:
• Weather timing holds on every row. Across 10.6 million, 10.6 million, and 3.9 million rows of the three ensemble tables, power_fcst_init_time is the run time plus 9 hours, every valid_time is after it, there are no duplicate keys, no null cells, and every run holds all 16 Primaries. The violation count is 0 for each rule, so no row-level list exists.
  • Lag ages hold. All four lag columns of the observed cache equal the observed power 24, 48, 168, and 336 hours earlier on every row. Across the 123 origins, no capped day or week lag (experiment 558's recipe) is stamped less than 24 hours before the origin. The day lag holds a reading for 96.4% of targets on average, and 88.4% at the worst origin.

docs.title: Why the generators have no zero readings after 2026-03-26
docs.text:
The zeros vanish because the source files change on that day, not because of the farms. The stored files before the change come from one bulk history export (2016-01-01 to 2026-03-26 08:30); every file after it covers a 6-hour window. The ingest code holds no zero filter, and the raw power table, not only the cleaned table, holds no zero after the change. Four findings fit the explanation that the 6-hour files omit zero-valued readings:

  • Solar farms lose about half of their half-hours in the weeks just after the change (the night half-hours, which were zeros).
  • The wind farms' single missing half-hours sit next to readings near zero: the neighbouring reading has a median of 2% of the farm's 95th percentile, against 17% for all readings.
  • Before the change, the wind farms have no single missing half-hour, and the solar farms have one.
  • The last exact zero at all 6 solar farms falls between 2026-03-25 05:30 and 2026-03-26 06:30, a few hours before the bulk export ends. The wind farms have too few zeros to pin the date: their last zeros are on 2026-03-23.

We did not read the raw files from the source, so the cause is the best fit to the stored data, not a confirmed statement by the source.

Look at July and October. In the two months where Solar E has about half the midday readings, its median daily peak is near 0 MW (July 0.2 MW; October -0.007 MW, too small to see as a bar); in the other months it is 13 to 17 MW. Midday is 10:00 to 14:00 UTC.

Solar E lacks midday readings in July and October because it was producing almost nothing, so the absent half-hours are zero-output half-hours. The median daily midday peak is 0.2 MW in July and about 0 MW in October, against 13 to 17 MW from April to June, August, and September. The other solar farms have 98% to 100% of their midday readings on the 31 days when Solar E has none, which rules out a data feed failure shared by all farms. The cause of Solar E's near-zero output, such as an outage or an export limit, is not in the data. We did not change the series.

docs.title: ERA5 farm-cell wind table
docs.text:
• The table now reaches 2026-10-31 23:00. It is experiment 288's farm-cell table, which stopped on 2024-03-31, for the four wind variables at the same 43 cells. We added 974,208 rows (43 cells and 22,656 hours, 2024-04-01 to 2026-10-31) from the Climate Data Store, in 12 three-month requests (the service refused a six-month request as too large), in the new file era5_farm_cells_2024-04_2026-10.parquet in this experiment's data folder.
  • The overlap agrees. On the three days before the join (3,096 rows), the largest difference from the stored values is 0.0005 m/s for every variable. The size was about 150 MB, the data are free, and the licence is the ERA5 licence.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, and the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast: not applicable, because this experiment reads no forecast.
  • Triggers fired: none of the seven audit triggers applies to a data build with no control, no contrast, and no earlier result to contradict.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00607-bakeoff-extend-cached-inputs-to-2026-10-31/. e00607_build.py (ensemble, cloud cover, observed power; reuses experiment 397, experiment 561, and the stage 1 pilot's builders), e00607_fetch_wind_sites.py, e00607_fetch_cams_demand.py, e00607_fetch_era5_box_cds.py, e00607_fetch_ptype_arco.py, e00607_derive_era5.py, e00607_fetch_era5_farm_cells_cds.py, e00607_assertions.py, e00607_zeros.py, and e00607_report.py. The Open-Meteo irradiance and CAMS site fetches use the published scripts with ERA5_FIRST_DATE=2026-09-11, ERA5_LAST_DATE=2026-10-31, and ERA5_OUTPUT_SUFFIX=_2026-09-11_2026-10-31.
  • Licences and sources: Dynamical.org ECMWF ensemble (CC-BY-4.0), ERA5 from the Climate Data Store and ARCO-ERA5 (Copernicus licence; contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information), CAMS (Copernicus Atmosphere Data Store). Nothing was paid for.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether the source stopped sending zero readings from the generators on purpose, so that the generators' final-test scores can be compared with their development scores.

docs.title: Which parts of the combined lag-and-gate, lag-without-gate, and lag-free demand neural networks are needed, when each part is removed alone?
docs.text: On injected load-shifts, the lag-and-gate network (K1) keeps the normal running arrangement (NRA) inside its q05-q95 band on 0.927 of rows from day 4 of a shift to its end, and the G4 gated band is the largest single part of that. K1 is experiment 591's shared lag-encoder network (A1) with the refit rule E3 and the G4 band. Without G4 (K2) the same fits cover 0.886. In the tested arm, the steadier offset O2 narrows the band and lowers coverage relative to D5. This page covers the planned removals only in part: see "Not run".

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Each dot is the arm minus K1, with its multiplicity-adjusted (Bonferroni) interval over 28 counted tests. The dashed line marks no difference from K1. Left and middle: share of rows with the NRA inside q05-q95, injected 15 and 30 day events, 24-120 h, first fold pair. Right: the share of an injected shift's depth that the median forecast follows. Left of the dashed line means lower coverage in the left and middle panels, and lower follow in the right panel. The G4 (K2) row appears only in the table below, because K2 ran on five months.

Share of event-free rows with the observed power inside q05-q95, by metering group, at 24-120 h, four months (2025-10 is used only to fit the constants). The dashed line is the 0.90 target. Look at the eight MVA Primaries, where the tail constants lift K1 to the target, and at the six MW Primaries, where they barely move it.

Day-ahead forecasts through the December 2025 load-shift for the two Primaries, one neural network per panel. Look at the gate strip, which turns on from about day 4 and widens the band in K1 only. The dashed lines are the switch times the maintainer gave. The mean power steps by 0.27 of capacity at D5 (0.80 to 0.53) across 2025-12-30 01:00, against 0.13 across 2025-12-29 00:00 (the start of experiment 580's verified window), so the data match the maintainer's time better. The shaded span is still the verified window. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the normal running arrangement, which these panels do not draw.

The lag-free neural network K3 through the same load-shift. Look at whether the median drops when the load-shift starts: the dashed lines are the switch times the maintainer gave.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Reference check. K1-ref (A1 with D5, 3-day embargo, no tail constants, G4) re-scored from experiment 591's stored forecasts with the gate state rebuilt gives day-4-to-end coverage 0.9251 against experiment 597's 0.925 (both five-month figures; on the first fold pair the stored A1 + G4 gives 0.929 and K1 0.926). The rebuilt state equals experiment 592's stored state. - Headline (five months, 756 events with a day 4). K1 0.927 (0.921 to 0.934) day 4 to end and 0.921 (0.914 to 0.928) in the 7 days after the end; K2 0.886 and 0.882. Median follow 0.111. G4 had 0 false triggers in 1,817 event-free origin days (five months). - Leave-one-out table. First fold pair, where K1 covers 0.926 (day 4 to end) and 0.946 (after). Differences to K1 carry multiplicity-adjusted (Bonferroni) intervals over 28 tests, and verdicts follow the plan's tolerances.

Further results.

  • Event-free CRPS. No arm's point difference from K1 exceeds 0.0011 (CRPS as a fraction of capacity, as in experiment 597's event-free table), and every interval lies within -0.0017 to +0.0029. - O2. K1 with O2 has event-free coverage 0.868 against 0.895 for D5 on the same two months. The steadier offset narrows the band, as experiment 577 saw on the lag-free network. - Tail constants (fitted per metering group and lead band on earlier months, applied before G4). Event-free q05-q95 coverage at the eight MVA Primaries, 24-120 h: 0.887 to 0.903. At the six MW Primaries: 0.860 to 0.862, with the share below q05 rising from 0.045 to 0.074 and the share above q95 falling from 0.095 to 0.064. docs.text:

  • No Bonferroni count above the stated 28 was needed; the counted tests are four contrasts for each of seven arms.

docs.title: Reproduction notes
docs.text: • Rows and data. Cleaned power; 2025-07-01 onwards unused; injected bank of experiment 581 as in experiments 584, 591, 597; seeds 0 and 1; refits on days 0 and 14. - Code reused. 00591-* (A1 chain, read only), 00599-* (E3), 00584-* (C1), 00577-* (O2), 00565-* (lag-free D5), 00592-* (G4), 00597-* (scoring), 00492-* (tail constants). - Fits and compute. Roughly 5 GPU-hours on up to 3 processes (not timed); fits in the private folder data/ml-experiments/00608-*/arms. - Caveats. NGED's logs may omit load-shift events, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events and the event counts are lower bounds. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the normal running arrangement. The injected bank changes only the lags, which flatters lag networks (experiment 595). Labels are imperfect (experiment 580). Nothing is adopted for production. - Checks. Median-minus-mean forecast and the mean-forecast error beside each contrast were not computed, so the audit triggers were not run. - Next. Run the remaining removals on all five months, refit the tail constants on O2's own forecasts, and add the absorption and 120-240 h scores.

docs.title: How should the final bake-off score the best forecasts of the 3 metered wind farms and the 6 metered solar farms, and what would it cost?
docs.text:
The wind and solar part of the bake-off is cheap to fit and costly to prepare: about 0.4 GPU-h for the cheapest design and about 3 GPU-h for the most thorough, against a ceiling of 8 GPU-h. The fit times come from the logs of earlier experiments and are estimates, so the first worker must time one fit of each kind before relying on them. No weather model was fitted and no forecast was scored for this page. The page is a design that a later worker can follow once the list of release candidates is frozen.

The bake-off scores each frozen candidate once, on forecasts issued from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31 (the final test, opened once). The five development months are 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. July 2026 is the first month of the final test. Nothing here is adopted for production, and the generators appear only as W1 to W3 (wind) and Solar A to F (solar).

docs.title: 1. Candidates, stored artefacts, and cost
docs.text:
Every candidate must be re-run for the final test, because no stored forecast reaches past 2026-08. The first table lists the candidates. "Stored" means a file under data/ml-experiments/ that holds the forecasts or fitted weights for the development period.

Technology Candidate What it is Stored Needs for the final test Wind Wind default 2 Experiment 347, arm y2: the frozen physics plant, run on each of the 51 ensemble members, then a three-component mixture-density head; capacity at p99.9 of earlier power (experiment 461) Plant files (plant_stage3.json), ensemble summaries, and predictions_y2.parquet for 53 Tuesday runs Plant summaries for the new runs (CPU), a head refit (GPU), and a daily-origin run for the development months Wind Wind default 1 ERA5-trained XGBoost on the 51 members plus the offset table of experiment 259 Predictions for 53 Tuesday runs (experiments 303 and 347) A refit on CPU Wind climatology Per-farm climatology Not stored as forecasts Build on CPU Wind Persistence, hours 0 to 6 Last reading held Not stored Build on CPU Solar a2_member The 51-member encoder network of experiment 430, refitted once a year (experiment 493 and experiment 498) Weights annual_a2_member_s0.pt to s5.pt and predictions, six seeds One annual refit per seed Solar a2_member quarterly The same network refitted every quarter Predictions of experiment 430 (seeds 0 to 5, four refits) Two refits per seed in the test window Solar GAM reference The additive-curve arm a3_gam_full of experiment 272 Predictions, three seeds, per farm A refit on CPU Solar XGBoost reference The XGBoost reference of experiment 243 with the floors of experiment 224 Predictions under 00243-*/predictions/ A refit on CPU Solar manual_heuristic and climatology The two baselines of the solar protocol Not stored as forecasts Build on CPU

Two stored sets do not match the bake-off's rows. The wind default was scored on 53 Tuesday runs, not on daily origins, so the development months need a daily-origin run of the plant summaries. The solar forecasts were scored over 2025-09 to 2026-08 on refits dated 2025-09, 2025-12, 2026-03, and 2026-06, so the stored solar forecasts cover the five development months only where those refits apply. The stored annual forecasts come from a single refit dated 2025-09, so they match that rule even less well. The worker must check the refit dates against the coarse-refit rule of the common brief (day 0 and day 14 of each test month) and refit where the dates differ.

Fit costs are small. The numbers below are read from logs, and the totals are estimates.

Fit Cost per fit Source Solar a2_member, one refit, one seed 29 to 61 s wall time (24 s of GPU time) Logs of experiment 430 and the cost table of experiment 493 Solar one-pass network, one refit, one seed 8 s of GPU time Experiment 493 Wind head, one seed, one refit about 25 s Log of experiment 347 stage 4 (the 45 timed head fits took 1,102 s in all) Wind plant summaries, one farm, hindcast and scored sets about 96 s of CPU inputs_W1.log of experiment 347 XGBoost, GAM, climatology, manual_heuristic CPU only, minutes Earlier pages

The projection has three designs, ranked.

Rank Design GPU-h Notes 1 Final test only. Solar: one annual refit and two quarterly refits, six seeds. Wind: one head refit at 2026-07-01, five seeds. Stored forecasts stand in for the development months where their rows match. about 0.4 The cheapest design: 18 solar fits at 61 s and 5 wind fits at 25 s, plus 30% for data loading. 2 Design 1, plus re-running the five development months with the same code (day 0 and day 14 refits, two seeds for wind and six for solar), so that the development and final-test numbers come from one script. about 1.9 Adds 60 solar fits and 20 wind head fits (10 refits). Catches a mismatch between the stored forecasts and the new code before the test is opened. 3 Design 2, plus a wind head refit every quarter inside the test window, and ten seeds for Solar E (experiment 498 needed ten seeds to resolve a 1% contrast). about 3.1 Adds 1 wind refit and 4 more solar seeds for 13 refits. The extra seeds matter only if a contrast at one farm decides a ranking.

All three designs are below the 8 GPU-h ceiling, so no stop is needed. The estimate counts the longest fit time seen (61 s) for every solar fit and 25 s for every wind head fit, and adds 30% for data loading. The first worker confirms it with one timed fit of each kind.

docs.title: 2. Scoring rules
docs.text:
Every candidate is scored by the quantile score over 11 levels in points of capacity, on the same rows, with the same capacity. The levels are q01, q05, q10, q25, q40, q50, q60, q75, q90, q95, and q99. The continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) is twice the mean pinball loss over those levels. Capacity is the p99.9 rule of experiment 461 for the wind farms. For the solar farms the capacity follows experiment 505: the old capacity at Solar A and Solar E, where the rolling and all-history p99.9 rules failed (Solar A on score, Solar E on the tail test), and the worker chooses the rule for the other four farms from experiments 461 and 505 and records the rule. The scoring code reads each capacity from one file, so no candidate can use another.

Metric Definition Why Quantile score Mean pinball loss over 11 levels, in points of capacity The headline of both protocols CRPS Twice the mean pinball loss Comparable with the demand pages Interval coverage Share of rows with the observed power inside q05 to q95; target 0.90 Calibration Tail calibration Share of rows above q99 (target 0.01) and below q01 (target 0.01); the 0.99 and 0.01 pinball losses Experiment 347 found 2.3% above q99, so the worker reports both shares for every candidate Threshold-weighted CRPS Weight on observed power above 80% of capacity (this page's own choice; no earlier page sets a threshold) The part of the distribution that matters for curtailment

No curtailment-cost metric exists for generators yet. The avoidable curtailment cost of experiment 601 is defined for demand nodes with an import limit, and experiment 347 lists a generator version as "not computed". The design therefore reports the 0.99 pinball loss and the threshold-weighted CRPS instead. The maintainer must choose whether to define a generator curtailment cost before the test is opened; this page does not choose.

Every metric is reported in every slice below, and every slice row shows its half-hour count. Intervals resample whole calendar months of origin, as in the earlier pages. The final test has only 4 months, so intervals will be wide. The page states the minimum detectable effect beside every contrast and counts the contrasts, so that the Bonferroni level is a number. Bonferroni count: the number of contrasts is the number of candidates compared with each technology's default, times the 3 lead bands, and the worker computes it from the frozen list.

Slice Definition Lead band 0 to 24 h, 24 to 120 h, 120 to 240 h; the headline is the whole range 0 to 240 h Month Each of 2026-07, 2026-08, 2026-09, 2026-10; the development months beside them Season Summer and autumn from the final test; winter and spring from the development months. The final test holds no winter and no spring, so no season is compared across the two periods Hour of day Each hour 0 to 23 UTC; daylight half-hours only for the solar farms Very sunny days Days on which the observed solar output reaches 90% of the clear-sky output on at least half the daylight half-hours (the clear-sky definition of solar-v1 is not spelled out on its page, so the worker states the rule used) High-wind days Days on which the observed wind output of at least 2 of the 3 wind farms exceeds 80% of capacity on any half-hour Near a data gap Half-hours within 24 hours of a gap of at least 3 hours in the same series Series Every farm on its own row; the pooled number is a mean over farms, not over rows

Slices use the observed power only to label days, never as a forecast input.

docs.title: 3. Missing readings and the experiment 605 gaps
docs.text:
The nine generators have had no exact-zero reading since 2026-03-26, so the final test cannot be compared with the development months unless both are filtered the same way. Experiment 605 found that the last exact zero at all nine series falls between 2026-03-23 and 2026-03-26. Solar farms read zero in 47% to 68% of half-hours in the six months before March, and wind farms in 0.3% to 4.8%. The cause is unknown, and Solar E also misses about 70% of its four middle daylight hours in July and October 2026.

Three versions of each score are reported, and a fourth is reported for the development months.

Version Rows kept Comparable with the development months? A, rows present Every half-hour that has a reading Only after the development months are filtered the same way (version A-dev) B, night filled Version A plus the solar night half-hours (sun elevation at or below 0 degrees) added with an observed power of 0 Yes for solar, with the development months scored as they were before C, calm filled (wind only) Version A plus wind half-hours that have no reading and whose ensemble-mean 100 m wind speed is below the plant's cut-in speed, added with an observed power of 0 Yes for wind, as a sensitivity run only, because the fill rule uses a weather forecast A-dev The development months with every exact-zero reading dropped The match for version A

Version A is the headline, and A-dev is its development-period match. Dropping zeros removes the easy half-hours, so version A scores are higher than the scores in the earlier pages and must never be set beside them. Version B is a bound: night half-hours are scored with zero forecasts and zero actuals, so the night fill lowers the score and is reported separately, never pooled with daylight half-hours. The solar protocol already scores daylight half-hours only, so version A and version B differ only through the dawn and dusk half-hours that read exactly zero.

Solar E is reported on its own row, and every pooled solar number is shown with and without it. Its missing midday readings are the largest gap in the final test, and the missing readings remove the half-hours that carry most of its score. A pooled solar mean that includes Solar E is not comparable with the development months.

What is comparable with the development months.

  • Comparable: version B for solar, and A against A-dev for both technologies.
  • Not comparable: version A against the development scores of earlier pages; any pooled solar number that includes Solar E; and any season comparison.
  • Open question: whether the source stopped reporting zeros or the farms stopped reading zero. The manager's question to NGED is listed in the risks.

docs.title: 4. Plots
docs.text:
Every plot follows the standing plot rules of the common brief and the dataviz skill. The plots are anonymised: the axis shows the day of the week (1 to 7, repeated for the second week) and never a calendar date. Plots are drawn from the saved forecasts, not from refits.

Group Panels Stretch Wind farms W1 to W3, one figure per farm Two panels, each 280 px or taller: the default 2 median with its q05 to q95 band in one panel, and the same for wind default 1 in the other. Observed power in black; no other mark is black or grey A 14-day high-wind stretch, a 14-day calm stretch, and a 14-day stretch around a gap Solar farms A to F, one figure per farm Two panels: a2_member annual with its band, and a2_member quarterly with its band A 14-day very sunny stretch, a 14-day cloudy stretch, and a 14-day stretch around a gap; Solar E gets two gap stretches (July and October) Score by lead band, month, and hour Bars with 95% intervals, one panel per technology The whole final test Coverage and tail calibration Points against the 0.90 and 0.01 targets, one row per candidate The whole final test

Each figure has a legend outside the data area, a plain caption saying what to look at, and a gate or gap strip checked against the data. The gap strip is a thin bar under the panel and is drawn from the rows with no reading. A strip that is on across the whole axis is a bug until checked against the stored rows. A fresh Sonnet reviewer opens every figure rendered to PNG and answers the figure-review checklist before the pull request is marked ready.

docs.title: 5. Outputs
docs.text:
Forecasts are saved as Parquet in the layout of backtest_export_2026-11-06/, one file per candidate and month, with a README. The README states the candidates, the seeds, the refit dates, the version of the missing-reading rule, and the caveats of section 3. The files hold:

  • series (W1 to W3 or Solar A to F), power_fcst_init_time, valid_time, and lead_hours;
  • q01 to q99, in points of capacity and in the generator's unit (MW);
  • observed_power (null where there is no reading) and observed_filled (the version B or C value);
  • sun_elevation_degrees, reading_present, and near_gap (true within 24 hours of a gap of at least 3 hours).

No file holds a generator's name, its identifier, or its location. The generator files are private: they stay under data/ and are not published.

docs.title: 6. Dependencies and risks
docs.text:
Dependencies.

  • Experiment 607 (extend the cached inputs to 2026-10-31) must finish first. Experiment 605 found the ensemble summary, wind-component, and cloud-cover tables ending with the run of 2026-06-30.
  • The inputs of the two networks are not on experiment 605's list of 11 cached inputs. Wind default 2 reads the 51-member farm-point tables that experiment 303's builders write, and a2_member reads the member arrays of experiment 430 (member_arrays, 402 MB). The first worker checks the newest date of both and adds them to experiment 607's list if they stop early.
  • The experiment 605 gaps (section 3) fix the scoring rules. The filter must be agreed before the first candidate is scored.

Risks.

  • Capacity can leak. Wind recomputes the p99.9 capacity at each refit, and the solar capacity is fixed or rolling according to the rule the worker records. A capacity computed from power that includes the test months would leak, so the worker asserts that every capacity uses only readings from before the refit.
  • Only 4 test months and 3 wind farms. The intervals are wide. Experiment 347 found a gain of 0.23 points with a 99.75% interval that included zero. The bake-off may not separate close candidates, and the page reports ties as ties.
  • Upper tail of wind default 2. 2.3% of observations exceeded q99 in experiment 347. The worker reports this share for every candidate, and it is not a pass or fail rule here.
  • Solar E. Solar E has the fewest scored rows, and ten seeds were needed to resolve one contrast. Design 3 adds those seeds; designs 1 and 2 do not.
  • One question for NGED. Whether the source stopped reporting exact-zero readings on about 2026-03-26. The answer decides whether version A or version B is the headline.
  • Frozen list. The candidates must be frozen before the first score is read. Any change after that is a new bake-off.

  • Sources read: the pages of experiments 347, 461, 464, 466, 493, 498, 499, 505, 506, 508, 605, and 607, the solar evaluation protocol, and the file listings under data/ml-experiments/ of experiments 272, 347, 430, 461, and 493. The fit times are read from the logs of experiments 347 and 430 and the cost table of experiment 493.

docs.title: Can the demand network's lag encoder keep following a load-shift this little (follow at most 0.05) while its event-free forecast stays as good as the A1 network's, by changing the span of the neighbour summaries, building the gap signals out of fold, dropping the signals during training, or adding a label head?
docs.text:
The neighbour-summary inputs make the forecast follow a load-shift much less, but no variant keeps both the benefit and the ordinary-day accuracy. A load-shift is a spell when a Primary substation's demand moves because the electricity network has been reconfigured, not because of weather. The demand forecast reads lagged power (the power readings from the previous day and week), so a load-shift leaks into the forecast. "Follow" is the share of a load-shift that the median forecast copies. A1 is the demand neural network of experiment 591, with follow 0.119. P7 is the best variant of experiment 606. P7 gives A1's lag encoder (the part of the network that reads the lagged power) summaries of the neighbouring Primaries' recent lags, and it cut follow to 0.035. P7 also made the forecast worse on ordinary days. That extra error is measured as CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, the quantile-forecast error) minus A1's, in percentage points of capacity: +0.021 at the eight Primaries rated in MVA and +0.068 at the six Primaries rated in MW.

Experiment 610 tried 27 variants of P7 and a placebo on the first two test months (2025-10 and 2025-12, two seeds). No variant met the keep rule: follow at most 0.05; ordinary-day CRPS within the minimum detectable effect (MDE, the smallest difference that the two test months can tell from noise) of A1's at both groups of Primaries; and coverage at the gate's band width within 0.01 of the gate's. The gate is R, A1 plus the load-shift gate of experiment 597. The closest variant, P7+D50 (P7 with all signals hidden on 50% of the training rows), follows 0.040 and passes at the eight MVA Primaries (+0.005, MDE 0.024). At the six MW Primaries its extra error is +0.059 against an MDE of 0.044, so 0.015 percentage points of capacity remain. The audit below shows that the eight-MVA pass rests on two test months that disagree.

The question was whether P7's extra error on ordinary days comes from a mismatch between training and test signals, or from a network that has learnt to depend on signals that are sometimes uninformative. Building the signals out of fold (CF) to remove the mismatch raised both follow (0.035 to 0.067) and the eight-MVA extra error (+0.021 to +0.033), so the mismatch is not shown to be the cause. Hiding the signals on half of the training rows (D50) lowered the eight-MVA extra error from +0.021 to +0.005, but that difference is smaller than D50's minimum detectable effect (0.024), and D30 did not lower it. At the six MW Primaries the extra error stayed at +0.04 to +0.08 in every arm that followed at most 0.05, so dependence on the signals is not shown to explain the six-MW extra error either.

Each dot is one arm, scored on 2025-10 and 2025-12 with two seeds. The horizontal axis is follow on injected 15 and 30 day load-shifts, from day 4 to the end (lower is better; A1 is 0.119). The vertical axis is event-free CRPS at 24-120 h ahead minus A1's (lower is better), and each vertical bar is the minimum detectable effect. The keep rule needs a dot left of the vertical dashed line (follow at most 0.05) whose bar reaches the horizontal dashed line (extra error within the minimum detectable effect of A1's). No dot meets both: the two bottleneck arms (P7+BN and P7+D50+BN, bottom right) sit on or below the horizontal line but follow 0.10.

The same arms at the eight MVA Primaries. Look at P7+D50 (follow 0.040): its bar reaches the horizontal dashed line, so it passes the keep rule at this group.

The injected events are not mirrored at a neighbour in this bank, so it does not test the neighbour inputs' benefit; it tests whether the benefit survives when the shift is also in the targets. R was not re-run on this bank.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site. Not computed. Every contrast here is on follow or on the CRPS of the median and quantiles, and the stored forecasts hold no mean forecast, so the check needs a rerun of the predictions.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside the quantile-score contrasts. Not computed, for the same reason.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 fired: the shuffled-neighbour placebo followed 0.056, 0.016 more than P7+D50 against 0.02 predicted. Trigger 2 fired: most predictions were refuted. Trigger 5 fired: P7+O3 gives less input than P7 and its six-MW extra error (+0.039) is below P7's (+0.068). Triggers 3, 4, 6, and 7 were not checked: the mean-forecast error was not computed, no leave-one-Primary-out run was made, no other experiment than experiment 606 reports the same contrasts, and no later experiment's design depends on this result yet.
  • Audit findings (a fresh Sonnet agent re-derived follow and the event-free extra CRPS from the stored forecasts, and every printed number reproduced). The findings change how to read the numbers, not the numbers themselves:
    • The minimum detectable effect is half the gap between the two fold months. With two fold months, the interval reduces to the two monthly differences. P7+D50's eight-MVA extra error is +0.029 in 2025-10 and -0.019 in 2025-12, giving the minimum detectable effect of 0.024, so its eight-MVA pass of the keep rule comes from the two months disagreeing. The placebo's two months agree (+0.033 each), and it fails. The "0.015 percentage points short" at the six MW Primaries also rests on two months that may disagree.
    • Seed noise is large. At the eight MVA Primaries the extra error of P7 is +0.011 for seed 0 and +0.153 for seed 1 (P7+D50: +0.006 and +0.124). The printed values average two seeds, so the differences of 0.01 to 0.02 between arms, including the refuted "lowers by 0.02" predictions, are not distinguishable from seed noise.
    • The placebo is leaky and the own-signal columns stay on. The shuffle is a fixed shift of 5 Primaries with the Primary itself removed, applied at training and test time, and 7 of 16 Primaries keep at least one true neighbour. No arm tests the own-signal columns alone, which may explain the follow reduction.
    • O3's lower six-MW extra error is consistent across both seeds and both months (-0.028 against P7 in both seeds) and is concentrated at Primaries 6, 11, and 9. Its cause is untested, and O3 also changes the initialisation, so it is not a strict subset of P7.
    • No leave-one-Primary-out run was made. The six-MW results are dominated by Primary 6 and by December. The full audit is in the private data folder, in briefs/e610_audit.md.
  • Caveats. Two fold months, two seeds, an injected bank that mirrors the shift at one neighbour by construction, and one verified real pair. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the ordinary-day rows may hold unlabelled events and the extra-error figures are lower bounds on harm.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
Standing practices followed. Refit at day 0 and day 14 of each fold month (the coarse cadence of experiments 584, 591, 598, and 606), cleaned data everywhere, the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, every fitted network saved in the data folder, stored forecasts of A1, R, and P7 reused as controls, the first fold pair (2025-10 and 2025-12) screened before the other months, seeds 0 and 1, and July 2026 unopened. The code is a copy of experiment 606's arm, model, signal, and scoring modules (not imported across worktrees), with the changes listed below.

Arms (every arm starts from experiment 591's A1 step-2 weights and its shared lag encoder, and differs only in step 3, as in 606). Inputs, per lag: P7 is A1's lag encoder inputs plus the per-lag gap (lag minus the lag-free forecast's median at the lag's own time), three exponentially weighted averages of the gap (half-lives 1, 3, and 7 days), the expected-missing flag, and summaries over all electrical neighbours (sum, mean, minimum, and maximum of the gap and of each average, the sum of the Primary's own value and the neighbours' sum, the neighbour count, and a "no neighbour" flag).

Stage Arm Definition 0 A1, P7, R stored forecasts, not refitted 1 B1, B3, B7, B14 P7 with the three weighted averages replaced by one trailing mean of the gap over the last 1, 3, 7, or 14 days up to the lag's time 1 B1-14 the four trailing means together (1, 3, 7, 14 days) 1 B1-28 the four trailing means plus a 28-day mean 1 E1, E7 P7 with only the weighted average of half-life 1 day, or only 7 days 2 CF the best stage 1 inputs, with the lag-free forecast table built out of fold (below) 2 D30, D50 the best stage 1 inputs; on 30% or 50% of training rows, all signal columns take the "no information" value (zero, the missing flags set to 1, the neighbour "none" flag set to 1) 2 BN the best stage 1 inputs reach the lag encoder only through one learnt scalar (a 1-hidden-layer network with 16 units, read by both lags) 2 X1, X3 the best stage 1 inputs plus a head on each lag-encoder output that predicts whether the lag is inside a synthetic shift (cross-entropy) and the shift depth as a share of capacity (squared error on shifted lags), added to the loss at weight 0.1 or 0.3 2 O1 compact summaries: only the neighbours' mean and the own-plus-neighbours sum 2 O2 adds the share of neighbours whose gap has the opposite sign and exceeds 5% of capacity, for the gap and each average 2 O3 signals for the week lag only (the day lag reads no signals) 2 O4 dropout of 50% on the neighbour columns only (own columns always kept) 3 COMBO the stage 2 changes that individually met the prediction, together 3 placebo the best arm with each Primary reading another Primary's neighbours (a fixed derangement) 3 widened the best arm rescaled about its median to the gate's band width (scoring only) 3 winner on 3 more months the best arm on 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06

Cross-fitting. In experiment 606 the lag-free table T is the lags-masked median of the step-2 network, which has seen the training rows, so the training gaps are smaller than the gaps at test time. CF builds T for the training rows from networks trained without them. The training window of step 2 is split into three contiguous blocks by valid time; for each block, a copy of the step-2 recipe (the same pre-trained weights, fresh mixer, 20 epochs at most) is trained on the other two blocks and predicts the lags-masked median on the block. Test rows use the full step-2 network. Cost: three extra step-2 trainings per fold month and seed (each on two thirds of the rows). If a training takes more than 15 minutes, CF runs on one seed only and the page says so.

Screening rule (to save GPU). Every arm is fitted and its event-free CRPS scored. An arm is injected (the 15 and 30 day bank) only if its event-free CRPS minus A1's is below P7's at both groups. Arms that fail are reported with their event-free CRPS only.

Dropout details. Dropout rows are drawn once per refit over the training rows only (the early-stopping rows keep their signals), so the mask does not change between epochs. O4 is a 50% dropout of the neighbour columns only. The screening rule is applied by hand: an arm is injected only after its event-free CRPS is read.

Target-side bank. The winner is also scored on the target-side bank with a mirrored neighbour (experiment 595's method), because the lag-only bank flatters neighbour inputs. If the GPU ceiling does not leave time for it, the page says that the check was not run.

Label head check. For X1 and X3, the head's "active" output is also read on the observed lags around the real December 2025 pair (D5 and D16), descriptively; the head is never trained on real events.

Plots. Every time-series plot follows the standing plot rules (at least 280 px per panel, one forecast arm per panel, a legend, the maintainer's example event of 2025-12-30 01:00 to 2026-01-14 11:30, the NRA left off the lines). A fresh Sonnet reviewer opens every rendered figure.

docs.title: How well does the lag-free demand network forecast the 2 bulk supply points and 2 grid supply points when each group is pooled on its own?
docs.text:
A neural network that reads weather and the calendar but no recent power forecasts the two bulk supply points (BSPs) better than the weekly XGBoost model (BG2), and the two grid supply points (GSPs) about as well. The measure is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in points of effective capacity (percent of the series' capacity; smaller is better). At 24 to 120 h ahead, the network scores 6.23 at the BSPs against 7.05 for BG2, and 17.89 at the GSPs against 18.00. A second network that also reads the previous day's and the previous week's power (Design 2) gave no clear further gain. The 90% band (q05 to q95) is too narrow for both networks: it holds the observed power on 0.84 of rows at the BSPs and 0.86 at the GSPs, against a target of 0.90.

We backtested two designs over the five development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), at leads of 0 to 240 h, with seeds 0 and 1. The backtests prepare the final model comparison (the bake-off). The design comes from experiment 604. The two BSPs are D13 and D17 and the two GSPs are D6 and D1. Design 1 is the neural network with no power inputs (lag-free) and the O2 offset of experiment 577, a slowly changing per-series correction to the forecast mean. Design 2 is the neural network with power lags of experiment 415. Each group is one neural network of two series. BG2, a climatology, and the manual heuristic are the stored forecasts of experiment 87. Forecasts are in the private Parquet export.

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• Held as point estimates: Design 1 has a CRPS at least 1 point below the climatology at all four series at 24 to 120 h (D13 5.19 against 7.12, D17 7.26 against 11.32, D1 15.66 against 24.65, D6 20.12 against 21.50, a gap of 1.4 points). The interval excludes zero at the BSPs only (Table 3). Design 1 differs from BG2 at the BSPs by less than the minimum detectable effect (-0.84 against 1.11), although its Bonferroni interval excludes zero.
  • Failed: Design 1 was not worse than BG2 by more than 1 point at the GSPs (difference -0.05). The q05 to q95 band did not cover between 0.85 and 0.95 at every lead band (Design 1's group coverage is 0.83 to 0.85 at the BSPs; Design 2's is 0.80 to 0.84). The exporting GSP D1 did not have the lowest coverage (0.88, against 0.80 at D13).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Leakage: a fresh Sonnet reviewer found none: fits stop at the refit cut, training rows end 3.5 h before it, and the weather run is issued at or before the origin minus 9 h.
  • Mean forecast against median forecast, and the triggers: not computed, because the stored forecasts are quantiles only. No audit trigger could fire on a contrast of the mean forecast. Design 2 is not a nested arm of Design 1, because the two use different fitting schedules.
  • July 2026: never read.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Five months and two series per group. Each interval resamples 5 months, so the intervals are wide, and the GSP contrasts cannot rank any forecast. The result is a pilot, not a ranking.
  • Design 2 is not the A1 network. The shared lag encoder A1 sits in the three-step stack of experiment 574 for the Primaries, so Design 2 uses experiment 415's plain lag network, one fit per month, without A1.
  • BG2 and the other references are single stored fits of experiment 87, scored on the rows they share with each design. The lead range is 0 to 240 h. NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days.
  • Pretraining reached the 60-epoch cap in the Design 1 fits, so early stopping did not trigger, as in experiment 577.
  • Not scored: q01 and q99 pinball loss and curtailment cost. The export holds q01 and q99, so either can be scored later.
  • Labels are incomplete. NGED's event labels miss some events, so a clean half-hour may hold an unlabelled load-shift.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text: run_d1.sh fits Design 1, run_d2.sh fits Design 2, e00611_score.py D1 D2 writes the scores and the export, and e00611_figures.py draws the figures. Cost: about 15 minutes of GPU process time, against a ceiling of 3 GPU-h. Code reused: the folders of experiments 87, 397, 415, 428, 448, 510, 511, 559, 564, 565, and 577.

docs.title: Which network should each of the three load-shift classes use, once the tail constants, the steadier offset, a neighbour-summary class 2 candidate, and the missing measures are added to experiment 608's table?
docs.text:
With tail constants fitted on each neural network's own earlier forecasts, the steadier offset O2 does not measurably change coverage in K1, K2, or K3. The test is too coarse to prove O2 equal to the current offset D5, because the printed minimum detectable effects are larger than the 0.01 coverage tolerance. The class 2 candidate covers like K1 on injected load-shifts without the gate, at a band 12 to 18% wider than its unscaled band. The page completes experiment 608's table for the three load-shift classes, using the five development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06) and seeds 0 and 1.

Terms. Each class is a neural-network design for one kind of series. Class 1 uses K1, class 2 starts from K2, and class 3 uses K3. K1 is the lag neural network with synthetic shifts (lagged power with injected load-shifts during training), the 7-day-embargo refit rule E3, and the G4 gated band (a band that widens when a load-shift is detected). K2 is the same fits without G4. K3 is the lag-free neural network. D5 is the slow monthly output offset, and O2 is the steadier daily-knot offset of experiment 577. The class 2 candidate adds neighbour summaries and 50% signal dropout from experiment 610's arm P7 with D50. Primaries are primary substations: the eight MVA Primaries are metered in megavolt-amperes (MVA) and the six MW Primaries in megawatts (MW). Follow is the share of an injected shift's depth that the median forecast tracks. Absorption is the share of the shift that the median forecast takes up when the neural network is refitted on rows that contain the shift. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, as a share of capacity. The normal running arrangement is the load pattern without the load-shift.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Share of event-free rows with the observed power inside the 90% band (the 5th to 95th percentile), by metering group, at 24-120 h, on the four months after the first (the first month only supplies the first fit). Tail constants are the fitted factors that widen the band's lower and upper edges. D5 and O2 are the two output offsets. K2 is omitted because it has the same numbers as K1 in this chart. The dashed line is the 0.90 target. Look at the eight MVA Primaries, where the tail constants lift every network by 0.02, and at the six MW Primaries, where they lift only the O2 and lag-free networks.

Each dot is the coverage of the O2 offset minus the coverage of the D5 offset with its Bonferroni interval (30 counted tests), with the tail constants applied to both. The dashed line marks no difference. Look at the injected 0-7 days after the end, where O2 covers more, and at how wide the event-free intervals are.

Each dot is the class 2 candidate at K1's band width minus K1 (or K2), with its Bonferroni interval (22 counted tests), 24-120 h, five months. Look at the injected panel, where the interval against K1 touches zero from the left.

The same contrasts for the event-free continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), as a share of capacity. Every dot is above zero, which means a higher (worse) CRPS. The intervals include zero except at the six MW Primaries.

Day-ahead forecasts through the December 2025 load-shift at the Primaries D5 and D16, one network per panel. The shaded span is the verified window. The dashed lines are the load-shift start and end the maintainer gave. The blue strip under K1 is the gate, which is on from about day 4. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the normal running arrangement, which these panels do not draw.

Three further situations at the same scale: a week with no load-shift, a cold winter night, and a very sunny day at a Primary with embedded solar generation. Look at whether the bands stay at a similar width in K1 and K2 when the gate is off, and at how the class 2 candidate's band compares with K3's.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Tail constants (a lower and an upper factor per metering group and lead band, fitted on earlier origins of earlier months only, applied before G4). At 24-120 h on the same four months, event-free coverage of the 5th-to-95th-percentile band at the eight MVA Primaries rises from 0.887 to 0.904 in K1 and K2, and from 0.868 to 0.891 in K3. At the six MW Primaries the coverage stays at 0.860 to 0.862 in K1 and K2 (the share below the band rises from 0.045 to 0.075 and the share above falls from 0.095 to 0.063) and rises from 0.836 to 0.863 in K3. On the injected bank, day 4 to the end, K1 moves from 0.924 to 0.928 and K2 from 0.885 to 0.888. At 120-240 h, K1 covers 0.902 to 0.907 from day 4 to the end.
  • O2 against D5 with tail constants on both (30 counted tests, Bonferroni level 0.05/30; tolerance 0.01 in coverage and 0.0006 in CRPS, the printed minimum detectable effect of experiment 591). No event-free interval lies inside the tolerance: the minimum detectable effects are 0.02 to 0.06 in coverage and 0.001 to 0.002 in CRPS, so the contrast cannot show equivalence. K1 with O2: injected day 4 to the end 0.926 against 0.928 (difference -0.002, interval -0.012 to +0.006); 0-7 days after the end 0.934 against 0.916 (+0.018, +0.011 to +0.026, better); follow 0.099 against 0.112 (-0.013, -0.016 to -0.010, lower and so better). Event-free coverage at the eight MVA Primaries is 0.905 against 0.904, and at the six MW Primaries 0.882 against 0.862 (+0.021, -0.019 to +0.058). Three differences go against O2. K1's event-free CRPS at the eight MVA Primaries is higher by 0.0004 at 24-120 h and by 0.0007 at 120-240 h (the second point estimate exceeds 0.0006; both intervals include zero). K3's coverage at the eight MVA Primaries at 120-240 h is lower by 0.017 (-0.034 to +0.0003). K3 with O2 otherwise covers 0.012 less at the eight MVA Primaries and 0.005 less at the six MW Primaries at 24-120 h, with all intervals including zero. K2 behaves as K1.
  • Without tail constants O2 lowers event-free coverage by 0.02 to 0.04 in all three networks (K1, same four months: 0.864 against 0.887 at the eight MVA Primaries, 0.839 against 0.860 at the six MW Primaries), which is the loss of coverage experiment 608 saw. Refitting the constants on O2's own forecasts removes it.
  • Class 2 candidate at the gate's band width (22 counted tests; every figure in this bullet is on rows matched with K1). Its own band covers 0.895 from day 4 to the end, so its band is scaled by factors of 1.12 to 1.18 per month (the ratio of K1's mean band width to the candidate's own, on the injected bank at 24-120 h). At that width it covers 0.933 against K1's 0.927 from day 4 to the end (+0.006, -0.0005 to +0.012) and 0.925 against 0.921 after the end (+0.004, -0.003 to +0.011). It follows 0.047 of an injected shift against K1's 0.111 (better). Event-free coverage is higher than K1's (0.920 against 0.886 at the eight MVA Primaries, and 0.901 against 0.868 at the six MW Primaries) because the band is wider everywhere. Event-free CRPS is 0.0002 higher at the eight MVA Primaries and 0.0005 higher at the six MW Primaries than K2's. Those point estimates are inside 0.0006, but the interval at the six MW Primaries (+0.0001 to +0.0012) is not. By the plan's rule (coverage within 0.01 of K1 and CRPS within 0.0006 of K2) every interval touches the tolerance, so the replacement is not shown.
  • Absorption (experiment 595's method, day-14 refit, mean over injected designs with 95% interval). From day 4 to the end, K1 and K2 (experiment 599's E3 arm) absorb 0.127 (0.076 to 0.181), K3 absorbs 0.063 (0.018 to 0.114), and the class 2 candidate, whose neighbour of an injected transfer carries the mirrored opposite shift, absorbs 0.071 (0.037 to 0.107). In the 7 days after the end the shares are 0.114, 0.073, and 0.064. Compared with K1 and K2, K3 is lower by 0.064 (-0.089 to -0.038) and the candidate by 0.056 (-0.084 to -0.032) from day 4 to the end; both intervals lie beyond the 0.03 tolerance, but these two contrasts are not among the 2 counted tests, so their intervals are not Bonferroni-adjusted. In the 7 days after the end (the counted contrasts) the differences are -0.041 and -0.050, and the verdict is inconclusive.
  • Ablations on 2025-10 and 2025-12, injected day 4 to the end (12 counted tests). Without E3, coverage changes by +0.002 (inconclusive) and follow by -0.002 (equivalent); coverage 0-7 days after the end changes by +0.010 (+0.004 to +0.018), and event-free coverage at the six MW Primaries by +0.014 (+0.001 to +0.027). Without the offset, coverage changes by -0.002 and follow rises by 0.036 (worse), and event-free coverage at the six MW Primaries is 0.011 higher (inconclusive).
  • Scores at 120-240 h. Event-free CRPS without tail constants, five months: K1 and K2 0.0355 (eight MVA Primaries) and 0.0284 (six MW Primaries), K3 0.0383 and 0.0311, the class 2 candidate 0.0355 and 0.0288. With tail constants, four months: K1 0.0361 and 0.0297, K3 0.0390 and 0.0323. Event-free coverage with tail constants: K1 0.881 and 0.853, K3 0.878 and 0.852.
  • Curtailment cost (pounds per Primary-day, mean over the six MW Primaries' months, event-free, 24-120 h; reported only). At limits 0.9, 0.75, and 0.5: K1 and K2 305, 5,615, and 32,440, and with tail constants 233, 5,262, and 32,022; K3 405, 6,831, and 39,444, and with tail constants 367, 6,396, and 38,987; K1 with O2 398, 6,082, and 34,004, and with tail constants 415, 5,016, and 32,649; the class 2 candidate at gate width 290, 5,171, and 32,769. The figures without tail constants cover five months and those with tail constants four.
  • G4 false triggers. 0 in 1,817 event-free origin days for K1 with D5 and with O2. The ungated rule G0 had 2 false triggers in 1,568 event-free origin days.
  • D15 and D18 (report only, 24-120 h, event-free, without tail constants). K1 covers 0.861 with CRPS 0.0869, K3 covers 0.840 with CRPS 0.0824, K1 with O2 covers 0.843 with CRPS 0.0937, and the class 2 candidate at gate width covers 0.887 with CRPS 0.0908.
  • Predictions. P1 (O2 within 0.01 of D5 on event-free coverage) is not shown: the intervals are too wide. P2 (O2 at least 0.01 below D5 on day-4-to-end coverage in K1) failed (-0.002). P3 (the class 2 candidate within 0.015 of K1 and within the CRPS minimum detectable effect) held for the point estimates. P4 (dropping E3 raises absorption by 0.03) was not tested. P5 (dropping the offset lowers six MW coverage by 0.02) failed (+0.011).

docs.title: Not run
docs.text:
• Absorption of K1 and K3 with O2, and a refit of K1 and K2 absorption in this experiment (the K1 and K2 figures are experiment 599's E3 arm; K3 and the class 2 candidate were refitted here).
  • The ablations ran on the first fold pair (2025-10 and 2025-12). Tail constants need an earlier month, so the ablation contrasts are on plain K1.
