docs.title: Reproduction notes
docs.text:
• Rows and data. Cleaned power; the final test months, 2026-07-01 onwards, are unused; injected bank of experiment 581; seeds 0 and 1; refits on days 0 and 14. The tail constants of a month are fitted on earlier months' event-free rows whose origins precede the month's first origin; experiment 608's constants used rows without that purge, so its tail figures were slightly optimistic.
  • Code reused (copied into this folder). Experiments 608 (K1, K2, K3 arms), 610 (P7 with 50% signal dropout, the arm of a draft experiment nearest to this design), 577 (O2), 565 (lag-free D5), 599 (E3), 592 (G4), 597 (scoring), 595 and 587 (absorption), 601 (curtailment cost), and 492 (tail constants).
  • Fits and compute. Fits are in the private data folder; the fit time on the GPU was well under the ceiling of 10 GPU-hours.
  • Caveats. NGED's logs may omit load-shift events, so clean rows may hold unlabelled events and the event counts are lower bounds. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the normal running arrangement. The injected bank changes only the lag columns, which flatters lag networks (experiment 595). Nothing is adopted for production.

docs.title: Do five seeds give intervals tight enough to show that the class 2 candidate can replace the gate, that O2 is equivalent to D5, and that dropping E3 changes absorption?
docs.text:
Experiment 612 left three claims unproven, because each rested on a single estimate that fell inside the tolerance (the largest difference we accept as no real change). This experiment refitted the neural networks behind them on three more seeds and replaced the estimates with intervals. We asked whether three changes can be made without changing the forecast by more than the tolerance. The three changes are the class 2 candidate for the gate, the steadier offset O2 for the slow offset D5, and the 3-day refit embargo for the E3 rule. We refitted each neural network on seeds 2 to 4, joined them to experiment 612's seeds 0 and 1, and scored the mean of the five seeds' quantiles on the five development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06). The class 2 candidate matches K1's injected-load-shift coverage and safe-side share, but its event-free CRPS is not shown equivalent in 3 of 4 cells. The two other changes stay unproven, because five seeds left the intervals as wide as before.

Terms. Class 1, 2, and 3 are the three families of forecast network in experiment 612: class 1 is the lag network, class 2 adds neighbour summaries to it, and class 3 has no lags. D5 is the slow monthly offset that corrects the forecast level, and O2 is the steadier offset fitted from daily knots. Tail constants are two factors per group of Primaries and lead band that widen the outer quantiles, fitted on earlier months only. The injected bank is the set of synthetic load-shifts added to the readings. A cell is one pairing of Primary group (eight MVA or six MW) with a horizon band (24-120 h or 120-240 h). A Bonferroni interval is widened so that all counted contrasts in a family hold together. The minimum detectable effect (MDE) is half the interval width. A Primary is a primary substation: the eight MVA Primaries are metered in megavolt-amperes and the six MW Primaries in megawatts. K1 is the lag neural network with the G4 gated band (a band that widens when a load-shift is detected). K2 uses the same fitted networks as K1 without the gated band. K3 is the lag-free neural network. The class 2 candidate is K2 plus neighbour summaries and 50% signal dropout from experiment 610, scaled about its median so its band is as wide as K1's. E3 is a 7-day embargo on the newest rows of the daily refit, with half weight on the 7 days before that. Follow is the share of an injected load-shift's depth that the median forecast tracks, and a lower follow is better because the forecast should not track a shift it cannot know about. Absorption is the share the median forecast takes up when the network is refitted on rows that contain the shift. Safe-side share is the share of rows where the normal running arrangement (NRA, the load pattern without the load-shift) lies on the safe side of the band's edge. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the NRA. A contrast is equivalent only if its whole Bonferroni interval lies inside the tolerance: 0.01 for coverage, follow, and safe-side share, 0.03 for absorption, and 0.0006 for event-free continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), the minimum detectable effect of experiment 591.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Each dot is an estimate and each line its Bonferroni interval. Coverage and absorption are scored against an estimate of the NRA. The dot is the class 2 candidate at K1's band width minus K1 (CRPS: minus K2), with its Bonferroni interval (12 counted contrasts, plus 2 for absorption). The pale cyan band is the tolerance. Look at the top panel, where both injected intervals lie inside the band and every event-free coverage interval lies above it, and at the bottom panel, where absorption is lower but the intervals touch the band.

Each dot is the O2 offset minus the D5 offset, tail constants on both (30 counted contrasts). Look at how wide every event-free interval is compared with the band.

Each dot is the 3-day embargo minus E3 (12 counted contrasts, plus 2 for absorption). Look at the injected panels, where every interval lies inside the band, and at absorption, where E3 absorbs less.

The December 2025 load-shift at Primaries D5 and D16, one network per panel, day-ahead forecasts from 14 days before the start to 14 days after the end. The dashed lines are the start and end dates the maintainer gave. The pale shade is the window verified in experiment 580, about one day earlier. In both figures the observed power drops at the maintainer's start date and rises at the end date, so the maintainer's dates fit the readings better than the verified window. The blue strip under K1 is the gate: the stored gate state has it on from 1 January to 22 January inclusive, about 8 days after the end date, not over the whole axis. The candidate has no gate. Each figure is one Primary. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the NRA, which these panels do not draw.

A quiet week at Primary D2 in March 2026, chosen as the week with the smallest median-forecast error, so it shows a best case. K1's gate stays off, so no strip is drawn. The two bands are close to identical, because the candidate's band is scaled to K1's width; look at where the median sits relative to the observed power.

Three days at Primary D2 around the highest overnight demand in January 2026, a proxy for a cold winter night. K1's gate stays off, so no strip is drawn. Look at whether the observed power stays inside the band on the evening peaks.

Three days at a six MW Primary in June 2026 around the deepest midday dip, a proxy for a very sunny day. K1's gate stays off, so no strip is drawn. Look at whether the band covers the midday dips.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Seeds 0 and 1 reproduce; seeds 2 to 4 are new fits. Seeds 0 and 1 are experiment 612's stored fits. Seeds 2 to 4 are new fits, with pre-training and step-2 weights fitted afresh. Refitting K1 on seed 0 with the new code reproduced the stored fit to within 6e-7 in the median forecast, whereas seed 1 differs from seed 0 by 0.02. K3 with O2 had pre-training for seeds 0, 1, and 5 to 9 only, so every K3 contrast between O2 and D5 uses seeds 0, 1, 5, 6, and 7 for both offsets. Splitting the seeds into {0, 1} and {2, 3, 4} (K3: {5, 6, 7}) gives 15 contrasts whose sign differs between the two subsets, for example the class 2 safe-side share (+0.0027 against -0.0017), so the sign of those contrasts is not stable. The five-seed intervals are inside the tolerance for the injected class 2 coverage contrasts, while the two subsets alone are inconclusive on them.
  • Class 2 candidate against K1: injected coverage matches within 0.01, event-free coverage is 0.02 to 0.03 higher. (12 counted contrasts; 2 more for absorption; band width set from the candidate's own month, as in experiment 612). Day 4 to the end: coverage -0.0043 (-0.0097 to +0.0011; mde 0.0054), safe-side share +0.0014 (-0.0040 to +0.0068), follow -0.0595 (-0.0657 to -0.0537, better). 0-7 days after the end: coverage -0.0033 (-0.0090 to +0.0027). Levels: K1 covers 0.926 and 0.918, the candidate 0.921 and 0.915. Event-free coverage is higher by 0.019 to 0.030 (all four cells above the tolerance) because the band is wider everywhere. Event-free CRPS minus K2: +0.0003 and +0.0005 at 24-120 h (intervals -0.0002 to +0.0006 and +0.0002 to +0.0010), 0.0000 and +0.0003 at 120-240 h (-0.0006 to +0.0006, and +0.0001 to +0.0006); one cell (six MW Primaries, 120-240 h) is equivalent. With each month's width set from the other four months, the injected contrasts move by at most 0.001.
  • Absorption: the candidate absorbs less, but the result is inconclusive. (candidate against K1 and K2; experiment 599's E3 arm, 9 designs from day 4 to the end and 12 after, seeds 0 and 1, 2 counted contrasts). Day 4 to the end: -0.056 (-0.089 to -0.029; MDE 0.030). 7 days after the end: -0.050 (-0.074 to -0.029; MDE 0.022). Both upper ends lie just above -0.03, so neither interval lies wholly below the tolerance.
  • O2 against D5: no event-free contrast is equivalent. (30 counted contrasts: 24 event-free and 6 injected; four months, because tail constants need an earlier month to fit on). One injected contrast is equivalent: K2 day 4 to the end, +0.0010 (-0.0082 to +0.0094). Half-widths are 0.021 to 0.057 in coverage and 0.001 to 0.002 in CRPS, Experiment 612's matching cells had half-widths of 0.038 and 0.0017, so seeds 2 to 4 did not narrow the intervals. Differences are O2 minus D5. K1 injected 0-7 days after the end: O2 covers 0.012 more (0.007 to 0.017); K2: +0.020 (0.013 to 0.026, better). K1 follow: -0.009 (-0.011 to -0.007; lower is better). K3 at the eight MVA Primaries: coverage -0.011 (24-120 h) and -0.016 (120-240 h), intervals reaching +0.010 and +0.005.
  • E3 against the 3-day embargo: injected contrasts are equivalent, absorption is inconclusive. (12 counted contrasts; five months). Equivalent on all four injected contrasts: coverage -0.0040 (-0.0061 to -0.0018) and +0.0052 (+0.0034 to +0.0071), follow +0.0021, safe-side share -0.0029. Event-free, equivalent at the eight MVA Primaries at 24-120 h (coverage -0.0032, CRPS +0.0001) and inconclusive in the other six cells, with the six MW Primaries 0.009 more covered without E3 (0.0004 to 0.019 at 24-120 h). Absorption (experiment 599's E0 and E3 arms, 9 and 12 designs, 2 counted contrasts): the 3-day embargo absorbs 0.062 more from day 4 to the end (0.020 to 0.115) and 0.045 more in the 7 days after (0.020 to 0.078). The direction is clear and the size is inconclusive against 0.03.
  • Predictions. P1 held (injected coverage intervals inside 0.01). P2 failed (O2 is not equivalent in K1 or K2 event-free). P3 held for the point estimates (+0.062 and +0.045 for the embargo minus E3), but each interval's lower end is 0.020, short of 0.03. P4 held: the half-width barely changed (K1, six MW Primaries, 24-120 h: 0.038 against 0.0385).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not computed: these forecasts are stored as 11 quantiles, with no mean.

  • Why prediction P2 failed. The explanation tested was that the interval width comes from resampling over 16 Primaries and 5 months, not over seeds. The half-width did not change with five seeds, which supports it.

docs.title: Not run
docs.text:

  • K1 and K3 absorption with O2.

docs.title: Reproduction notes
docs.text:
• Code reused (copied into this folder). Experiment 612's folder (K1, K2, K3, candidate, tail constants, scoring, tables), which copies experiments 565, 574, 577, 584, 591, 592, 595, 597, 599, 601, and 610. New in this folder: e00613_link.py (joins seeds 0 and 1 to the new seeds), e00613_widths.py (the band-width factors), e00613_roster.py (the contrasts), and the CHAIN613 and --seeds options.
  • Fits and compute. About 4 GPU process-hours, under the ceiling of 10. Fits are in the private data folder.
  • Caveats. NGED's logs may omit load-shift events, so the event counts are lower bounds. Coverage is scored against an estimate of the normal running arrangement. The injected bank changes only the lag columns, which flatters lag networks. Nothing is adopted for production.

docs.title: Can the three candidate neural networks be exported as stored backtests that reproduce experiments 612 and 613, and can a final-test runner be built that scores each frozen candidate once?
docs.text:
Three candidate neural networks, five development months, one folder. The folder holds the stored forecasts of K1 (class 1, the lag network with the gated band), the class 2 candidate (a neural network that also reads neighbouring Primaries' power and has random signal dropout in training, with its band scaled to K1's width), and K3 (class 3, the lag-free network). Each forecast is the average of five training runs (seeds 0 to 4), taken quantile by quantile, as experiment 613 scored it. Experiment 614 also wrote a script for the one-shot final test, which has not been run on the held-out months.

Terms. A Primary is a primary substation, and the export covers 16 Primaries: eight metered in megavolt-amperes (the eight MVA Primaries) and six in megawatts (the six MW Primaries), plus two report-only Primaries with a short history. The five development months are 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. A load-shift is a transfer of demand between neighbouring Primaries. The final test is the one held-out scoring on forecast origins from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31. Event-free rows are rows with no labelled or verified load-shift within 7 days at that Primary. Coverage is the share of rows with the observed power inside the q05-q95 band (target 0.90).

Look at the median (dark orange) staying near the pre-load-shift level while the observed power (black) moves at the first dashed line, and at the band widening once the blue gate strip comes on. The panels show K1's day-ahead forecasts (issued at 09:00 UTC the day before) at D5 and D16, from 14 days before the load-shift to 14 days after. The dashed lines are the start (2025-12-30 01:00) and end (2026-01-14 11:30) the maintainer gave. The pale lilac shade is the window verified in experiment 580, which starts about one day earlier. The readings agree with the maintainer's dates: D5's mean power falls from 4.65 MW in the day before 2025-12-30 01:00 to 3.04 MW in the day after, and does not move at the verified window's start. The gate strip (stored gate_on) is on from 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-22 (1,056 of 2,085 half-hours), not over the whole axis. Coverage in the experiments is scored against an estimate of the normal running arrangement, which is not drawn here.

The same two Primaries and dates for K3, which reads no power lags. Look at the median holding the level it would have had without the load-shift, and at the band staying narrow, though it widens a little after 20 January at D16. K3 has no gate, so the strip is empty. The legend and the dashed lines are as above.

docs.title: The export
docs.text:
• Files. One Parquet file per network and month: 15 files, 132 MB, in data/ml-experiments/backtest_export_roster_2026-11-07/ (private, never committed), with substations.csv, a README.md for a junior colleague, and checks.txt. The layout is experiment 593's. The three files of a month hold identical keys: 236,533 (2025-10), 236,960 (2025-12), 237,584 (2026-01), 237,407 (2026-03), and 191,737 (2026-06) rows each.
  • Lead range. Every network's forecasts are stored to 240 h (the largest lead is 239.5 h), so no network falls back to 0 to 120 h.
  • Seeds. Seeds 0 to 4, averaged quantile by quantile and sorted across the 11 levels. K3 uses D5, as experiment 613's K3 scores do. No tail constants are applied.
  • K1. The network's quantiles, except that the band is the union band of the network and its lags-masked twin where the G4 gate is on or held for 7 days (the gate state is experiment 613's stored mode_g4.npy).
  • Candidate. The network of experiment 610's arm P7 with 50% signal dropout, scaled about its median by experiment 613's per-month width factor (1.076 to 1.120). The factors are in-sample, as in experiment 613.
  • BSP/GSP pilot. The export of experiment 611 stays in its own folder, and the README points to it.
  • Anonymisation. All 16 series are Primaries. No file holds a metered generator's time series or ID.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Experiment 613's cells reproduce exactly. From the exported files only, event-free q05-q95 coverage for every Primary, month, and lead band matches experiment 613's event_free_cells.csv for K1, the candidate (system K2w), and K3: 228 cells each, largest difference 0.00000 against the 0.003 tolerance, with identical row counts. One cell (D10, 2025-10, 0-24 h, 36 rows) is below experiment 613's 100-row minimum and is not in its table. Pooled over the five months, K1 covers 0.890 at the eight MVA Primaries and 0.864 at the six MW Primaries at 24-120 h.
  • Experiment 612's printed coverage reproduces from seeds 0 and 1. Experiment 612 printed event-free coverage at 24-120 h on four months (2025-12 to 2026-06) from seeds 0 and 1: K1 0.887 and 0.860, K3 0.868 and 0.836. Rebuilding the export from seeds 0 and 1 gave exactly those four figures. The five-seed files give 0.892, 0.859, 0.875, and 0.837, so the figures differ because of the extra seeds, not because of an error in the export. The five-seed figures differ from the printed ones by more than 0.003 only for the eight MVA Primaries (0.005 for K1 and 0.007 for K3). The seeds 0 and 1 rebuild is recorded in seeds01_check_summary.txt beside the export.
  • Not checked. The injected-load-shift headline numbers of experiments 612 and 613, because the injected bank is not exported.
  • Compute. No fit and no GPU. The ceiling of 3 GPU hours was not used.

docs.title: The final-test runner
docs.text:
e00614_final_runner.py runs the one final test on origins 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31. It was not run on those origins, and no forecast error beyond 2026-06-07 was read.

  • Order of a run. The runner reads the configuration, refuses if the lock file exists, checks every listed artefact against its SHA-256 hash, creates the lock with an exclusive create (so two runs cannot both start), and then loops over the daily origins.
  • Row-by-row assertions. For every row of every origin, the runner asserts that the weather run is the newest run at or before the origin minus 9 hours, that the run's table row carries that origin, that the valid time is after the origin, that no (series, valid time) pair is duplicated, and that both the day and the week power lag are stamped at least 24 hours before the origin (experiment 558's capped lags), on the extended inputs of experiment 607. A violation stops the run.
  • What a candidate sees. A predictor class gets the input rows: the keys, the weather run time, the weather summary columns, the lag times, and the two lag readings. It never gets the observed power at the valid time. A predictor that reads power or weather by itself is not covered by the assertions, so each frozen network's predictor has to use the supplied columns.
  • Scoring and output. Each candidate is scored once: its forecasts are written as Parquet, and scores.csv holds the continuous ranked probability score (as points of capacity) and q05-q95 coverage by lead band. The lock then records the hash of every output.
  • Refusing a second run. In final mode the lock must be final_test.lock beside the runner, so a second configuration cannot name a fresh lock. The runner loads the predictors and builds and checks the rows of every origin before it creates the lock, so a bad configuration cannot use up the test. Each predictor's module file is hashed into its candidate's combined hash. The lock file holds the configuration hash, the runner hash, the git commit, and each candidate's artefact list and combined hash. A lock left by a failed run also blocks a rerun, because the runner treats a started test as a used test. Only the maintainer may delete the lock.
  • Modes. In development mode the runner refuses any origin from 2026-07-01 onwards. In final mode it needs the origins to be exactly 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31, the command-line flag --run-final-test, and a date in approved_by_maintainer. --check verifies the configuration, the hashes, and the timing rules on every origin without predicting or writing a lock, and --hash-artefacts prints the hashes to put in the configuration.

Development-month test. e00614_dev_run.py runs the runner on origins 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07 with two dummy frozen candidates (a persistence rule that stands in for a lag network, and a per-Primary mean that stands in for a lag-free network) and passed 15 of 15 checks:

  • the check mode passed and wrote no lock;
  • the first run completed, wrote both candidates' forecasts (53,648 rows each: 7 origins, 16 Primaries, leads 0.5 to 239.5 h) and scores.csv, and recorded both candidates' hashes in the lock;
  • a second run was refused;
  • a changed artefact was refused and wrote no lock;
  • one row with a wrong origin stopped both the check and the run;
  • a missing ensemble run stopped the check;
  • a power lag younger than 24 hours (the lag cap lowered to 12 hours) stopped the run;
  • development mode refused an origin in July;
  • final mode refused to start without the flag, without the maintainer's approval, and with a lock file other than the pinned final_test.lock.

The dummy candidates' scores (continuous ranked probability score 6.9 and 8.2 points of capacity, coverage 0.60 and 0.92) show only that scoring works. They say nothing about forecast skill.

docs.title: What the maintainer must do before the final test
docs.text:
• Freeze the three candidate neural networks. Their weights and statistics files must be chosen and listed with their hashes, one configuration per frozen set of weights.
  • Wire the networks. The runner has no predictor for K1, the candidate, or K3 yet. Each needs a class that loads its frozen weights and builds its features from the supplied columns plus experiment 607's other extended tables (wind components, cloud cover, ERA5 columns). Experiments 574, 591, and 613's fit code builds those features inside month-by-month fits, so that wiring is a separate piece of work.
  • Approve and run. Fill in approved_by_maintainer, run --check, then run once with --run-final-test.

docs.title: Not run
docs.text:
• No refit of any network, and no new seeds.
  • The final test itself, and anything from 2026-07-01 onwards.
  • Predictors for the three real networks.
  • The injected-load-shift bank export.

docs.title: Reproduction notes
docs.text:
• Code. e00614_export.py (reuses experiment 593's Context and experiment 613's score folders), e00614_check.py, e00614_figures.py (reuses experiment 588's panel code), e00614_final_runner.py, e00614_dummy_predictors.py, and e00614_dev_run.py. Experiments 593, 597, 605, 607, 612, and 613 are the code and data reused.
  • Counted tests. 0 (no hypothesis about forecast skill), so no Bonferroni correction and no minimum detectable effect apply.
  • Caveats. NGED's logs may omit load-shift events, so event-free rows can hold unlogged load-shifts. The candidate's band-width factors were set on the months they are applied to. Nothing is adopted for production.

docs.title: How do the candidate forecasts for the 3 metered wind farms and the 6 metered solar farms score on the 5 development months, and which should be the default for each technology?
docs.text:
Wind default 2 scores clearly better than climatology and a little better than wind default 1, and solar a2_member scores better than every solar reference, though not decisively against the GAM. Its upper band on very sunny days is too low. This experiment scored every candidate forecast for the 3 metered wind farms and the 6 metered solar farms on the 5 development months (forecast origins in 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), with the scoring rules that experiment 609 fixed for the final test. The final test (origins from 2026-07-01) was not run, and no valid time in July 2026 or later is scored. Nothing here is adopted for production. Forecasts are stored in the private folder backtest_export_wind_solar_dev_2026-11-07/, and the generators appear only as W1 to W3 and Solar A to Solar F.

Terms. The quantile score is the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantile levels (q01 to q99), in points of capacity (smaller is better). Lead bands are 0 to 24, 24 to 120, and 120 to 240 hours. Coverage is the share of observations inside the q05 to q95 band (target 0.90). "Above q99" is the share of observations above the q99 forecast (target 0.01). "Exact zeros dropped" removes rows whose observed power is exactly zero, which experiment 609 calls version A-dev. Intervals resample whole forecast-origin months (5 months), so they are wide. Every contrast is "other candidate minus the default", so a positive number means the default scored better.

docs.title: What was scored
docs.text:
• Wind default 2 is the physics plant of experiment 347, run on each of the 51 ensemble members, followed by a mixture-density neural network head. This experiment rebuilt the member inputs for every daily run from 2025-06-17 to 2026-06-30 and refitted the head at day 0 and day 15 of each development month (10 refits, seeds 0 and 1 averaged), with capacity at the 99.9th percentile of earlier power (the rule of experiment 461, recomputed at each refit).
  • Wind references. climatology is a per-farm, month, and hour table of power before 2025-10-01. Wind default 1 and the stored wind default 2 exist only for Tuesday origins, so they are scored on those rows only.
  • Solar candidates are stored forecasts: a2_member refitted every quarter, from experiment 430, and the yearly refit from experiment 493 (6 seeds each), and the GAM, XGBoost, climatology, and manual_heuristic references of experiment 310 (seed 0).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Wind default 2 scores 4.28 points over 0 to 240 h and beats every wind reference. The table shows the pooled mean over the 3 farms with exact zeros dropped. Against climatology the gap is 1.04 points (99.4% interval 0.56 to 1.53, minimum detectable effect 0.68, 9 contrasts). Against wind default 1, on the 40,847 Tuesday rows that both forecasts cover, the gap is 0.13 points (0.04 to 0.24, minimum detectable effect 0.15), and the interval excludes zero only at 120 to 240 h (0.15, interval 0.08 to 0.25). The stored single-fit wind default 2 scores 0.03 points worse than the refitted one (0.020 to 0.035) on the same rows.

Candidate Rows Score (points) q05-q95 coverage Above q99 Wind default 2 275,863 4.28 0.898 0.0130 climatology 275,863 5.34 0.935 0.0164 Wind default 2, stored single fit, Tuesday rows 40,901 4.30 0.899 0.0207 Wind default 1, Tuesday rows 40,901 4.39 0.932 0.0137

The row counts are each candidate's own count. The gap to wind default 1 is paired on the 40,847 shared rows, so it does not equal the difference of the two table scores.

Look at the wind default 2 bars (orange) sitting below the climatology bars (purple) in every lead band. The lines are 95% intervals from resampling the 5 months. Wind default 2 gains most at short leads (2.35 against 5.33 points at 0 to 24 h) and least at 120 to 240 h (4.99 against 5.36).

Look at wind default 2's coverage of 0.898, close to the dashed 0.90 target, and climatology's wider band at 0.935.

Look at wind default 2's share above q99 (circle) of 0.013, above the dashed 0.01 target, and its share below q01 (diamond) of 0.002, below the target.

Wind default 2's band is too narrow in January and March and on high-wind days. Coverage is 0.861 in 2026-01 and 0.869 in 2026-03, and 0.807 on the 50 high-wind days (days on which at least 2 of the 3 farms exceed 80% of capacity), where 4.1% of observations are above q99.

Months 1 to 5 are 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06. Look at month 5 (a calm month, 2.5 points) against the other four months (4.3 to 4.8 points).

Look at the orange wind default 2 line staying below the purple climatology line at every hour of the day.

Solar a2_member scores 3.30 points and beats the GAM and XGBoost references, but not by a decisive margin. Quarterly and yearly refits score the same: the gap is 0.005 points (interval -0.018 to 0.028, minimum detectable effect 0.033, 15 contrasts). The GAM is 0.073 points worse over all leads (-0.017 to 0.157), which includes zero, and its gap excludes zero only at 0 to 24 h (0.137, 0.003 to 0.315) and 24 to 120 h (0.081, 0.017 to 0.134). XGBoost is 0.255 points worse (0.019 to 0.557). climatology and manual_heuristic are 0.87 and 0.83 points worse, with intervals that exclude zero in every lead band. Solar rows are daylight half-hours at 12 to 251.5 h, so the 0 to 24 h band holds only the 12 to 24 h part.

Candidate Score (points) q05-q95 coverage Above q99 a2_member, quarterly refit 3.30 0.915 0.0168 a2_member, yearly refit 3.30 0.908 0.0177 GAM 3.36 0.905 0.0140 XGBoost 3.57 0.853 0.0058 climatology 4.20 0.955 0.0015 manual_heuristic 4.17 0.821 0.0543

Look at the two a2_member bars (orange and light orange) being equal in every lead band, and the purple and green reference bars being far above them.

Look at manual_heuristic missing the dashed 0.90 target (0.82) and XGBoost at 0.85.

Look at the a2_member and GAM circles (share above q99) sitting above the dashed 0.01 target.

Solar a2_member's upper band is far too low on very sunny days. On the 12 days that reach 90% of the farm's own monthly 95th percentile on at least half their daylight half-hours (2,345 rows), 17% of observations are above q99 and coverage is 0.62. The rule for these days is a proxy built from the observed power, because no clear-sky series is stored with the forecasts. The count is small, so the figure is a warning, not an estimate.

Months 1 to 5 are as above. The a2_member scores are lowest in months 2 and 3 (winter, 2.3 to 2.7 points) and highest in month 4 (4.3 points).

Daylight hours only. Every candidate scores worst around 11 to 12 UTC. The quarterly refit of a2_member has the lowest score at every hour from 9 to 18 UTC. The GAM is lower at 5 UTC, and the yearly refit is lower at 6 to 8 and 19 UTC.

docs.title: Forecast examples
docs.text:
Each figure shows 14 days of day-ahead forecasts (wind: lead 24 to 48 h; solar: lead 12 to 36 h) in percent of capacity, with the axis in day numbers. The blue strip under each panel marks half-hours with no reading, or, for wind, dropped by the idle mask. The strip counts are listed in strip_checks.txt, beside the figures.

W1 over 14 days in December 2025. Look at the orange median following the black observation in the top panel (wind default 2), while the bottom panel's climatology band stays wide and flat.

W2 over 14 days in March 2026, the stretch with the most missing half-hours (135 of 672).

Solar A over 14 days in June 2026. Look at the observed power touching the top of the band at midday; the yearly refit is on top and the quarterly refit below. Lines break at night.

Solar E over 14 days in June 2026, with 54 of 406 usual half-hours missing. The other 23 stretches are in the folder beside this page (wind_* and solar_* SVG files). In the Solar A stretch of March 2026, the observed power reads exactly zero for about 3 days while the forecast stays high. The cause is not known.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Keep wind default 2 as the wind default, and a2_member as the solar default. For wind, the refitted physics-plus-head forecast beats climatology clearly and wind default 1 modestly, and refitting twice a month improves on the single fit. The upper tail and the January and March coverage are the weak points to watch. For solar, the quarterly refit of a2_member has the lowest score in 3 of the 5 months (the GAM is lower in 2026-03 and XGBoost in 2025-12) and beats every reference over all leads, but the a2_member interval against the GAM includes zero. No difference between yearly and quarterly refits was detectable above 0.033 points. The maintainer decides; neither is adopted here.

docs.title: What this experiment did not do
docs.text:
• No final test was run, and July 2026 is unused.
  • Solar was not refitted. The stored solar forecasts come from refits at day 0 of each quarter (2025-09, 2025-12, 2026-03, 2026-06), not the day 0 and day 14 rule of the common brief. The stored forecasts cover 12 to 251.5 h only. The GAM and XGBoost references have one seed.
  • Wind default 1 and XGBoost were not rebuilt for daily origins. Wind default 1 is scored on the Tuesday origins where it is stored. Persistence was not built.
  • The solar scoring capacity is the stored forecasts' older capacity for every candidate, so the choice of rule for four of the farms in experiment 505 was not applied. The wind scoring capacity is the 99.9th percentile of power before 2025-10-01.
  • The wind head's early stopping uses the 62 days before each refit date, and those rows contain short leads only for the last days, so the stopping loss favours short leads (as in experiment 347).
  • Exact-zero rows are few in these months, so the two score versions barely differ. The solar score is 3.34 on all rows and 3.30 with exact zeros dropped. Dropping zeros therefore lowered the solar score slightly (better) and left the wind score unchanged, so the prediction that the score would be larger did not hold.
  • The wind threshold-weighted score uses 80% of capacity as its threshold, and the solar very-sunny day rule is a proxy. Both are this experiment's choices.
  • The refitted wind heads' weights were not stored, because the reused training function returns only forecasts.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Gates. The rebuilt plant summaries equal experiment 347's stored summaries exactly (largest difference 0.0) on the 35,691, 35,600, and 35,755 shared Tuesday cases of W1, W2, and W3. Refitting experiment 347's head with its own inputs reproduces its stored seed 0 forecasts exactly (largest difference 0.00000 over 107,121 rows).
  • Bonferroni count. Solar: 5 candidates times 3 lead bands, 15 contrasts (interval level 99.67%). Wind: 3 candidates times 3 lead bands, 9 contrasts (99.44%). The minimum detectable effect uses the bootstrap standard error with the Bonferroni level and 80% power.
  • Code review. One Sonnet review of the wind scripts before the first fit found no leakage or scaling bug. The review's four accepted findings (finite-summary assert, mask and series coverage checks, old-capacity check, a stray folder) were fixed, and its fifth was a note on the stopping window (listed above).
  • Compute. 20 head fits at about 30 s each on the GPU, one process under 8 GB: about 0.2 GPU-h.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00615-bakeoff-wind-and-solar-development-month-backtests/. It imports the folders of experiments 230, 259, 303, 310, 326, 336, 347, 429, 461, and 588.
  • Figure review: passed on 2026-11-07 after two rounds. The first round found faults that are fixed in this page (identical coverage panels, calendar labels, lines bridged across gaps, empty-strip legend entries). The second found no mismatch with the data. Orange marks a candidate in the summary figures and the forecast in the time-series figures, as the maintainer's panel rule requires.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The open questions are whether a wider upper band for solar a2_member on very sunny days removes the 17% above q99 without worsening the score elsewhere, and whether the same ranking holds on the final test.

docs.title: Probing a lag-free neural network for unmetered PV capacity, on stored weights
docs.text: Take-home message: the stored neural networks respond to the sky as solar output would, and the response is steady, but this probe cannot show that the response is solar capacity. Each stored neural network was given a fixed calendar and the weather of other days. The probe read how much the network's net-demand forecast falls as the donor sky clears. At the six MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16, the Primary substations whose power is metered in megawatts) the response equals 1.87 to 3.19 MW of alternating-current (AC) photovoltaic (PV) capacity. The probed capacity is 0.65 to 0.99 of the estimate of experiment 474 and 0.70 to 0.98 of the estimate of experiment 479. The verdict is partly supported. Four of the 6 predictions hold, one holds at 5 of the 6 Primaries, and the placebo prediction fails for one of its two placebos.

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Weights. The probe reads the stored weights of 50 design-5 neural networks from experiment 565 (5 folds, 10 seeds) and 50 M0 neural networks from experiment 554. Both were pretrained on ERA5 (the ECMWF Reanalysis v5) and CAMS (the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service) estimates of past weather, and neither takes recent power as input. A fold is named by its test month, and the fold's weights were trained on data that ends before that month. The probe fits nothing and runs on a CPU.
  • Probe. The probe dates are 12 Tuesdays from 2025-04-15 to 2025-09-16 and 3 Tuesdays in April and May 2026. For each date and each daylight half-hour, the datetime inputs and the drift position are fixed. The weather inputs come from donors. A donor is the same half-hour of a day within 21 days of the probe date's day of the year, in the fold's pretraining years, at the Primary's own location. The donor's shortwave radiation is rescaled to the probe date's sun.
  • Regression. The probed net demand (MW) is regressed on the donor's temperature and on the pooled unit PV curve of experiment 269, with one intercept per half-hour slot. The unit curve is the PV output per MW of AC capacity as a function of irradiance and sun elevation, read at the donor sky. The capacity is minus the slope on the unit curve.
  • Intervals. The spread over the 10 seeds, and a day-block bootstrap of 200 resamples of whole donor days.
  • Placebos. A placebo repeats the regression with a sky that carries no day-to-day signal. The shuffled-sky placebo permutes the donor skies within a slot. The climatological-sky placebo replaces each donor's sky by the mean sky of its 7-day bin of offsets from the probe date.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. The probe matches the earlier estimates at D5 and D9, and is 15 to 35% below them at the other four Primaries. The probe's own interval is narrow because it counts seeds and donor days only. The interval does not count the shortfall of recovery that experiment 479 measured on injected farms.

Figure 2. The probed net demand falls almost in a straight line as the donor sky gets sunnier. Binning by equal counts shows no reversal at any of the six Primaries (see the monotonicity bullet below).

Figure 3. The probed response follows the unit curve from 9 h to 16 h, and lags it before 9 h. The median correlation over probe dates is 0.89 to 0.92.

Figure 4. A shuffled sky reads zero, and the seasonal trend of the sky alone does not. Fitting the climatological sky beside the real sky leaves the climatological sky's slope at -0.02 to 0.06 of the real capacity. The real response therefore carries the trend, and the climatological placebo is not a null here.

Figure 5. Temperature-matched donors change the capacity by 1% or less, and the two cloud terms change it by up to 35%. The cloud terms are close to collinear with the unit curve (within-slot correlation about -0.9), so the regression with cloud terms is not identified.

Figure 6. The capacity depends on the probe date. It is about 13% above the Primary's mean in April and about 12% below it in June and July. A fixed unit curve does not capture the network's seasonal response. The date-to-date spread (0.2 to 0.4 MW) is therefore larger than the seed spread.

Figure 7. The capacity differs by up to 0.18 MW between folds, and by up to 6% between the design-5 and M0 neural networks. Fold 2026-06 averages 15 probe dates and the other folds 12, and the 3 extra spring dates read high (figure 6). On the 12 common 2025 dates the fold range is at most 0.15 MW.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• Seed standard deviation under 0.3 MW at 4 of the 6 Primaries: holds at 6 of 6 (0.04 to 0.09 MW on the headline dates, and at most 0.12 MW in any fold or arm). The bootstrap standard deviation is 0.01 to 0.02 MW on the headline dates.
  • Monotone fall in the unit curve at all 6 Primaries: holds (Spearman correlation -1.0 and no rise between bins at 6 of 6, for both designs).
  • Hour-profile correlation of 0.9 or more: holds at 5 of 6 Primaries. Primary D5 is 0.89 and the other five Primaries are 0.90 to 0.92. D5 has 14 probe dates.
  • Within 0.6 to 1.4 of experiment 479 at 4 of 6 Primaries: holds at 6 of 6 (0.70 to 0.98). Against experiment 474 the ratio is 0.65 to 0.99.
  • Placebos under 0.20 of the real capacity: the shuffled-sky placebo holds (-0.01 to 0.01). The climatological-sky placebo fails (0.80 to 0.96) for the reason given under figure 4.
  • Temperature-matched donors move the capacity by less than its interval: holds (0.99 to 1.00 of the headline capacity).
  • Stop rules: neither fires. The seed standard deviation never exceeds 0.5 MW, and the response is monotone at all 6 Primaries.

docs.title: Reproduction, coverage, and review notes
docs.text:
• All 50 design-5 neural networks reproduce their logged validation loss to within 0.00005. The check uses the same validation rows and seeds as the training did. The 50 M0 neural networks load strictly and give finite losses (0.46 to 0.52). Experiment 554 logged none to compare. The script is e00616_reproduce.py. The stored forecasts of the two experiments come from fine-tuned networks, which the probe does not use.
  • Headline set. The headline uses the design-5 networks of fold 2026-06 and the 9 probe dates from July 2025 to June 2026 (8 at D5). Figures 1, 4, and 5 use the same set. The values are AC MW, as the mean with the 10th to 90th percentile over seeds and bootstrap: D5 3.11 (3.02 to 3.19), D9 2.01 (1.87 to 2.10), D10 1.87 (1.83 to 1.92), D11 2.62 (2.51 to 2.70), D14 3.19 (3.08 to 3.28), and D16 2.49 (2.43 to 2.55). The median of experiment 474's rung R4 is 3.15, 2.15, 2.89, 3.19, 3.74, and 3.08. Experiment 479's median is 3.17, 2.18, 2.55, 3.25, 3.71, and 3.57.
  • Spread over probe dates. The standard deviation over the 15 probe dates is 0.22 to 0.42 MW. The interval above leaves this spread out, and it is the larger uncertainty.
  • Designs and folds. The M0 neural networks give 0.94 to 1.00 of the design-5 capacity. The other folds give 0.92 to 1.01 of the 2026-06 fold's capacity.
  • Coverage. Primary D5 has no probe row on 2026-05-12, so it has 14 probe dates. Primary D9 has about 2 years of donors against about 6 at the other Primaries, because its power history is shorter.
  • This experiment does not test recovery of an injected farm or of a load that follows the clouds. A probed capacity below experiment 474's at D10 and D16 could mean the probe falls short, or that experiment 474 overestimates. An injection test would show which.
  • No forecast was scored, so the forecast-score checks do not apply. The median-minus-mean, mean-forecast-error, and tail-calibration checks were skipped, and none of the audit triggers fired. The experiment found no new data-processing problem.
  • No metered generator series is shown. The unit curve is a pooled shape of six metered farms, and it stays in the private data folder.
  • The inputs respect the July 2026 holdout. The weather inputs are ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather, so the probe describes the weather-to-demand mapping and is not a forecast.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00616-lag-free-network-pv-capacity-probe-on-stored-weights/. The code imports from experiments 269, 397, 418, 428, 448, 510, 554, and 565. The results are in the private data folder of the same name.
  • A Sonnet code review before the final numbers gave seven findings. The review showed that the climatological placebo is not a null, so the joint fit was added. It also found a dead function, which was removed, and a wrong docstring, which was fixed. The unidentified cloud regression and the narrow bootstrap are reported as caveats. A Sonnet figure review found 10 problems, all fixed and re-checked. A Sonnet write-up review corrected the figure 1, 6, and 7 captions and the date-set statements, and a Sonnet prose review shaped the wording.
  • Pre-registration. The pipeline was debugged on the 2026-06 fold with one run that averaged the seeds and fitted the temperature regression only. That run found a missing-row bug, and the thresholds above were not changed afterwards.

docs.title: Recommendation on step 2
docs.text: The decision rule of the plan is not met, because the climatological placebo failed, and the recommendation is still to run step 2, the injected known-answer test (2 to 4 GPU-hours). The rule asked for both placebos to pass. The climatological placebo fails for a reason that the joint fit explains after the fact (figure 4), so this departure rests on a post hoc analysis. The probe is stable, because the seed standard deviation of 0.04 to 0.09 MW makes a 2 MW injection more than 20 seed standard deviations. The probe also passes the shuffled-sky placebo and the temperature-matched check. The probe cannot show recovery. It sits 15 to 35% below experiments 474 and 479 at four Primaries (D10, D11, D14, and D16), and an injected farm and an injected cloud-following load would test whether the probe or the two earlier estimates are wrong. The design review recommends testing the 4 MW injection first. Leave the cloud terms out of the regression, and quote the probe interval together with the spread over probe dates.

docs.title: Options for follow-up
docs.text:
• Step 2 of the design review, with the climatological placebo replaced by the joint fit of figure 4.
  • Probe the fine-tuned networks of the same Primaries, to see whether fine-tuning on the ECMWF ensemble (ENS) forecasts moves the capacity.

docs.title: Can a hidden Markov model find whole-turbine capacity steps at the 3 metered wind farms, in a known-answer test and in the real histories?
docs.text:
A hidden Markov model that looks for whole-turbine outages in the daily top of wind-farm power finds 14-day outages of 2 or more turbines only about a third of the time at W1 and W2, and it raises 2 to 4 false steps a year on data that hold no outage. The cause is the data. Only about 20% of days at W1 and W2 have 6 or more half-hours with wind strong enough for the farm to reach full output, so a 14-day outage is often seen on one or two days. A signal that is observed on most days is therefore needed to track turbine-step capacity. The test injected artificial outages into the real daily series and checked whether the model found them (a known-answer test). The fit to the real histories (part B of the plan) was not run, because the stop rules fixed in advance both fired. Nothing is adopted, and no data from July 2026 onwards is used.

Terms. The model's hidden state is the number of turbines out of service. Its daily input is the 90th percentile of power over the half-hours that count as informative. A half-hour is informative when the wind speed from ERA5 (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' reanalysis) at 100 m is above the rated speed plus the blur, and at most 22 m/s (below the cut-out speed minus 3 m/s). The rated speed, the blur, and the cut-out speed come from the plant summary of experiment 347. The blur is the width of the smoothing that experiment 347 fitted to the wind speed. The power series comes from experiment 453. "Recall" is the share of injected outages whose recovered step is at least half the injected step. A "false step" is a rise of one or more turbines out that lasts 3 days or more.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. Share of injected outages detected, by outage length. The dashed line is the 80% bar. No farm reaches it in either panel; W1 reaches 64% (2 turbines) and 74% (3 turbines) at 60 days.

Figure 3. Recovered step size, in turbines, of detected outages with 2 or 3 turbines injected. Boxes span the 25th to 75th percentile, the white line is the median, and the whiskers are the minimum and maximum. The dashed line is the injected size. Boxes are missing where no outage of that length was detected.

Figure 4. False steps a year on permuted history, by daily failure probability. The dashed lines mark the pass bar (1 a year) and the stop rule (3 a year). W1 and W2 are above the stop rule at every probability; W3 is below it at 0.001.

Figure 5. One run at W1: six injected 60-day outages of 3 turbines (black), the recovered deficit (blue line), and its 90% interval (light band). Under the detection rule (a step of at least half the injected size), 1 of the 6 outages is recovered; several outages are invented.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Design. 405 known-answer cells (3 farms, 3 failure probabilities, 3 turbine counts of 6, 10, and 14, 3 outage sizes, 5 lengths), 3 runs each, up to 15 outages a run. The events table holds 17,496 outages, because long outages leave room for fewer than 15 in the record. The failure probability a was to be chosen as the one with false steps under 1 a year and the best recall; none qualified, so the smallest (0.001) was used.
  • Recall, 2 or more turbines, 14 days or more (bar 80%). W1 31%, W2 32%, W3 14%. Counting only outages with an informative day inside them, W1 44%, W2 50%, W3 23%; 71%, 65%, and 60% of outages have such a day. At 60 days, recall at W2 is 52% and 51% (2 and 3 turbines) and at W3 31% and 20%.
  • False steps (bar 1 a year, stop rule 3 a year). At a=0.001 on days permuted at random: 3.5 (W1), 3.5 (W2), and 2.4 (W3) a year. At a=0.01: 5.8, 6.0, and 4.3. The drift placebo raises 3.7 to 4.1 steps a year at a=0.001, and the estimated final capacity is 10% to 11% above the true value (bar 3%).
  • Step size. Of detected outages, 66% (W1), 67% (W2), and 75% (W3) are within half a turbine of the injected size. The recovered step is 0.24 to 0.36 turbines too small on average.
  • Turbine count. The count is recovered within 15% in 10% (W1), 32% (W2), and 10% (W3) of runs (bar 70%); only W2 with 14 true turbines passes, at 71%. The median estimate is 16 at W1 for every true count, 13 to 14.5 at W2, and 11.6 at W3, so the data do not identify the count.
  • Interval coverage. The 90% interval covers the true deficit on 27% to 29% of outage days and on 59% to 84% of all days (bar 85% to 95%).
  • Register and fixed count. The public Renewable Energy Planning Database matches W1 and W3 by position and capacity, and W2 ambiguously. The counts stay in the private data folder. At W1, recall for 2 and 3 turbines at lengths 14 to 60 days was 34% with the count fixed and 33% with the count inferred, so knowing the count did not help.
  • Stop rules. W1 recall is under 50% and W1 false steps exceed 3 a year, so the wind line stops here. The real fit, and the check against the ensemble analysis proxy (the ECMWF ensemble analysis that the forecaster reads), were not run.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The known-answer test is easier than the real problem in four ways. All outages in one run have one size; real outages of about 10% or more were removed from the base series; the ceiling (the full-farm output) is estimated from the series with the injected outages; and the detection rule accepts a recovered step of half the injected size. The permutation placebo uses the unfiltered series, which is the harsher null.
  • The tuning is on the real series. The failure probability was chosen on the same days that part B would fit.
  • Turbine counts of 6, 10, and 14 replace the plan's turbine sizes of 1.5 to 3.5 MW, which do not fit the two smaller farms.
  • Missing real events. NGED's logs may omit real outages, so the base series may hold unlabelled outages.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• A fresh Sonnet reviewer read the code before the run. The ceiling, the placebo base, step counting, block permutation, the window off-by-one, and coverage on observed days were fixed; same-size outages and the detection rule are recorded above as caveats.
  • A fresh Sonnet reviewer then checked the numbers, figures, and prose; its findings were applied.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00617-wind-turbine-step-capacity-known-answer-and-fit/. Private outputs: data/ml-experiments/00617-wind-turbine-step-capacity-known-answer-and-fit/.

docs.title: Can the capacity of a metered solar farm be tracked from its very sunny half-hours alone, and did Solar A, Solar B, and Solar D really produce more in 2021 to 2023?
docs.text:
Very sunny half-hours alone are enough to find a capacity step of 8% or more at four of the five testable solar farms, and the real histories show a fall at Solar A, a dip at Solar B, and no step at Solar C or Solar F. The method is blind to anything smaller than about 8% (Solar D: 12%) and lags a slow decline. It says nothing yet about whether a forecast would improve: experiment 464 found no forecast gain from slow scaling, so none was tested.

We asked whether a solar farm's capacity can be tracked from the half-hours that tell us most about it: those with a clear-sky index of at least 0.9 (observed over clear-sky irradiance, from CAMS, the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service), clear-sky irradiance of at least 700 W/m2, and at least six such half-hours in a row. Step 1 counted those half-hours per month and passed the stop rule. Step 2 reduced each sunny day to one number (the median of output over a modelled expectation), fitted a level that changes rarely (an exact change-point fit with a penalty per step), and tested it on capacity steps we injected into the real daily numbers and on placebos with no change. It then fitted the real histories to 2026-06-30. This is experiment 618, written for a junior colleague; terms are explained where they first appear.

Figure 1 (headline). Each line is one farm. A step of 8% is found at least 92% of the time at Solar A, B, C, and F and 11% of the time at Solar D, which needs 12%. The dashed line is the 80% pass bar. 40 random start days per size, up and down, at each farm.

Figure 2. Daily index (blue dots), fitted level (orange line), and 90% interval of the level (light blue band) for Solar A and Solar B. Sunny days exist only in April to August, so each cluster of dots is one summer. A step is dated to the first sunny day of its new level. The 5-day segment at the left of Solar A is too short to trust.

Figure 3. The same for Solar C (no step) and Solar D (no step; only 65 sunny days, so a step under 12% could not be seen).

Figure 4. The same for Solar E (7 months of sunny days, not tested) and Solar F (no step).

Figure 5. A known-answer example: a 12% fall (purple dashed line) injected half-way through the step-free series. The fit (orange line) finds it at both farms.

Figure 6. Placebo series with no true change, 20 shuffles per farm, worst farm. These are the tuning shuffles that chose penalty 40, so the curve at 40 is by construction under the bar; the fresh shuffles are in the results. Where the orange line is hidden, it lies under the sky-blue line.

Figure 7. Median count of very sunny half-hours by calendar month. The dashed line is the stop-rule level of 20.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Step 1 passes. The median over April to August months is 32, 32, 35, 13, and 33 very sunny half-hours for Solar A, B, C, D, and F; only Solar D is under 20 (1 of 5, the rule stops at 3 of 5). Solar E has 37 in its 7 months. Share of months with at least 20: 58%, 64%, 64%, 35%, 70% (Solar E 100%). April and August often fall under 20, June is best. Totals: 1,158, 1,303, 1,141, 492, 1,275, and 303 half-hours.
  • Daily index and estimator. Days with at least 6 sunny half-hours: 144, 162, 145, 65, 162 (Solar A, B, C, D, F) and 38 for Solar E. The daily noise sigma is 0.033 to 0.068 of the expected output (Solar D largest). Penalty grid 3 to 60 sigma^2; the smallest penalty keeping false steps within 1 a year on all four placebo kinds is 40.
  • Recall (40 start days per size and sign, fresh seeds). Step of 4%: 60%, 4%, 26%, 0%, 29% (Solar A, B, C, D, F). 8%: 96%, 93%, 98%, 11%, 93%. 12%: 100%, 100%, 100%, 88%, 100%. 20%: 100% everywhere. Pass bar (80% at 8% or more): met at four farms; Solar D meets it at 12%.
  • False steps. At penalty 40, 40 fresh shuffles per farm: 0 false steps a year when days are shuffled singly, on both the real and the step-free series; 0.67, 0.37, 0.01, 0, and 0 a year at Solar A, B, D, C, F when the real days are shuffled in 7-day blocks. Pass bar (at most 1 a year): met. In injected runs, extra steps beyond the injected one occur in 2% to 3% of runs.
  • Size error. Among steps found at 8% or more, 100%, 100%, 100%, 96%, and 94% (Solar A, B, C, D, F) are within 25% of the injected size; the recovered size is on average 0.3%, 1.1%, 0.1%, 4.9%, and 2.4% too large. Pass bar (80%): met. The bias is upward, not the downward bias the larger penalty gave in experiment 577.
  • Interval coverage. The naive interval (1.645 sigma over the root of the days in the segment) covers the true level on 74% of all days in the injected runs, because day-to-day errors are correlated. Widened by 2.25 (chosen on separate tuning runs, 89.8% there), coverage is 89.7% pooled; per farm 97.5%, 86.8%, 91.2%, 80.8%, 92.0% for Solar A, B, C, D, F. The pooled bar (85% to 95%) is met; Solar A is above and Solar D below it.
  • Smooth drift (10% fall over three years, shuffled step-free days). 0.12 to 0.29 false steps a year (bar: 3). The final level is too high by 2.2%, 3.3%, 3.0%, 5.5%, and 3.4% (Solar A, B, C, D, F); the bar (3%) is met at Solar A and Solar C only (Solar C by 0.04 points).
  • Real fits to 2026-06-30 (penalty 40). Solar A: a fall of 12.6% at 4.67 years since the first reading, and an earlier rise of 14.2% at 0.87 years that follows a 5-day segment. Solar B: a fall of 12.0% at 1.88 years and a rise of 17.9% at 3.90 years. Solar C, D, E, and F: no step.
  • Comparison with experiment 453. Mean output in 2021 to 2023 over 2025 to 2026, with a 90% interval from resampling 7-day blocks: Solar A 1.14 (1.09 to 1.20), Solar B 0.89 (0.85 to 0.92), Solar C 1.01 (0.99 to 1.02), Solar D 1.04 (0.97 to 1.13), Solar F 0.99 (0.97 to 1.00). Solar A agrees with experiment 453; Solar B disagrees in sign; Solar D cannot say.

docs.title: Prediction against result
docs.text:
• Held. Steps of 8% or more recovered at least 80% of the time at Solar A, B, C, and F, and Solar D weaker. Solar A shows a fall.
  • Did not hold. Solar B shows a dip in 2021 to 2023, not a higher level. Solar D shows no fall; it has too few sunny days to tell.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Rows and units. Hourly CAMS irradiance interpolated to half-hours (experiment 218); the expected output comes from one robust regression per farm over the whole record, so a level of 1 is the farm's long-run level, not its rated capacity. Errors in CAMS aerosol and cloud estimates cannot be told apart from capacity changes.
  • Dating. About 150 sunny days exist per farm in 7 years; a step is dated to the first sunny day of its new level and could have happened in the winter before.
  • Outages are not capacity. No log of curtailment or outages exists, so a step of weeks could be an outage; the fit sees only levels.
  • Injection base. The injected series are the real daily values divided by their own fitted levels (penalty 12), so real noise is kept and real steps removed. Recall is conditional on that choice.
  • Edges and noise. Injected steps start at least 15 days from each end of the series, so steps in the first or last weeks were not tested. The injection base is slightly smoother than the real series, so recall is somewhat optimistic. The fitted level is the plain mean of the days in a segment while step positions use values clipped to 4 sigma, so a few low outlier days pull a level below the bulk of the dots (visible at Solar E).
  • Not tested. Solar E (7 months), any forecast gain, July 2026 onwards. No contrast is tested, so no Bonferroni count applies.
  • Audit triggers. None apply: no forecast is scored, no skill is quoted, and no model is trained.
  • Lead range. Not applicable (no forecast).

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Treat Solar B's dip as a question for NGED (an outage, a re-rating, or a data fault); it is the largest finding.
  • Add a second irradiance product (ERA5 surface radiation) to see whether Solar D's sunny rows improve.
  • A change-point forecast test is not worth running first: experiment 464 found none.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• Code: ml-experiments/00618-solar-effective-capacity-sunny-rows-and-known-answer-test/ (e00618_common.py, e00618_step1.py, e00618_known_answer.py, e00618_real.py, e00618_report.py). Reuses rows from experiment 218.
  • Private tables: data/ml-experiments/00618-solar-effective-capacity-sunny-rows-and-known-answer-test/ (counts, placebo steps, injected runs, drift runs, real levels and steps).
  • Reviews: see the pull request.

docs.title: Does a lag-enabled demand network forecast the 2 bulk supply points and the 2 grid supply points better than the lag-free network at days 1 to 3?
docs.text:
Giving the demand network the previous day's and the previous week's power lowered its error a little at the 2 bulk supply points (BSPs) and the 2 grid supply points (GSPs), by less than the 5 development months can resolve. The measure is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity (percent of the series' capacity; smaller is better). At days 1 to 3 the lag-enabled network scores 5.50 at the BSPs against 5.62 for the lag-free network, and 15.48 at the GSPs against 16.80. Both gains are smaller than the minimum detectable effect (0.49 and 3.64 points), so the pre-registered prediction of a gain at least that large failed. The 90% band (q05 to q95) still holds the observed power on only 0.84 to 0.88 of rows.

We fitted the network of experiment 574 (arm P4E: lags at least 24 h old, the D5 offset, a three-step schedule with a 3-day embargo) with the shared lag encoder and lag age of experiment 591, one network per group, on the five development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) with seeds 0 and 1. Rows, months, scoring, and the stored references are those of experiment 611. The lag-free network is that experiment's Design 1. Load-shifts are ignored: no gate, no synthetic load-shifts, no neighbour inputs.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. CRPS of the lag-enabled network minus the lag-free network, by day of lead time. Look at the dots: they sit below zero at the BSPs on all 10 days and at the GSPs on days 1 to 9, and every interval includes zero except those of BSP days 9 and 10. Those intervals are not adjusted for the 20 cells; Table 2 gives the adjusted intervals.

Figure 2. CRPS by day of lead time. Look at the dark blue line: the lag-enabled network is the lowest of the four forecasts on all 10 days at the BSPs and on days 1 to 9 at the GSPs, and both networks beat BG2 and the climatology at every day at the BSPs.

Figure 3. Mean absolute error of the median forecast. Look at the BSPs: the order of the forecasts matches Figure 2.

Figure 4. Share of rows inside the q05 to q95 band. The dashed black line is the target of 0.90. Look at the lines: every forecast sits below it on every day.

Figure 5. D13 (bulk supply point): forecast issued at 09:00 UTC the day before, for the 14 days around the night of highest observed power in December 2025 and January 2026 (the windows of experiment 611). Look at the winter peaks: both networks follow them.

Figure 6. The same window for D17 (bulk supply point).

Figure 7. The same window for D6 (grid supply point). Look at the band width: it spans several hundred MW.

Figure 8. The same window for D1 (grid supply point that mostly exports power).

Figure 9. D17: one forecast run issued on 13 January 2026 at 09:00 UTC, over its full 10 days. Look at the band: it follows the daily shape of the observed power.

Figure 10. D6: one forecast run issued on 25 January 2026 at 09:00 UTC.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Table 1. Pooled scores on the 228,968 rows per forecast that the lag-enabled network, the lag-free network, BG2, and the climatology all have. "Days 1 to 3" is a lead of 0 to 72 h and "days 4 to 10" is 72 to 240 h. Coverage is the share of rows inside q05 to q95 (target 0.90). MAE is the mean absolute error of the median.

Group Lead Forecast CRPS MAE Coverage BSPs Days 1 to 3 Lag-enabled 5.50 7.83 0.865 BSPs Days 1 to 3 Lag-free 5.62 8.00 0.847 BSPs Days 1 to 3 BG2 6.59 9.26 0.878 BSPs Days 1 to 3 Climatology 9.20 13.13 0.845 BSPs Days 4 to 10 Lag-enabled 7.14 10.20 0.843 BSPs Days 4 to 10 Lag-free 7.32 10.47 0.830 BSPs Days 4 to 10 BG2 7.96 11.41 0.876 BSPs Days 4 to 10 Climatology 9.05 12.93 0.849 GSPs Days 1 to 3 Lag-enabled 15.48 22.29 0.878 GSPs Days 1 to 3 Lag-free 16.80 24.31 0.872 GSPs Days 1 to 3 BG2 16.70 23.81 0.873 GSPs Days 1 to 3 Climatology 22.95 34.53 0.810 GSPs Days 4 to 10 Lag-enabled 19.33 28.58 0.856 GSPs Days 4 to 10 Lag-free 20.19 29.36 0.847 GSPs Days 4 to 10 BG2 20.46 29.75 0.871 GSPs Days 4 to 10 Climatology 22.96 34.59 0.816

Table 2. Contrasts in CRPS (points; negative favours the lag-enabled network). The Bonferroni count is 16: 4 reference forecasts (the lag-free network, Design 2 of experiment 611, BG2, the climatology) times 2 lead sets times 2 groups. Each interval resamples the 5 months at the Bonferroni level. The minimum detectable effect is beside each contrast. Every contrast uses the 228,968 common rows.

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• Failed: the lag-enabled network beats the lag-free network at days 1 to 3 by at least the minimum detectable effect, in both groups (differences -0.12 against 0.49 and -1.28 against 3.64).
  • Held: ties at days 4 to 10, meaning the interval includes zero (-0.40 to +0.17 and -3.64 to +1.00).
  • Held: the band covers fewer than 0.90 of rows (0.84 to 0.88).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Code review: a fresh Sonnet reviewer read the fit script before the first fit and found no leakage and no Primaries-only stored data on the paths it runs. Its two hardening suggestions (refuse months outside the development months; check each month's forecast origins span the month) were applied.
  • Mean forecast against median forecast: not computed, because the stored forecasts are quantiles only. The lag-enabled network is not a nested arm of Design 1: it differs in the lag inputs, the D5 against the O2 offset, and the schedule.
  • July 2026: never read.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Five months and two series per group. Each interval resamples 5 months, so intervals are wide and the GSP contrasts cannot rank any forecast.
  • The lag-free comparator uses the O2 offset, the lag-enabled network the D5 offset. The lag-free network of experiment 611 is Design 1, which uses O2. A lag-free network with D5 was not fitted, so part of the contrast may come from the offset.
  • No thermal-lag and solar-gain columns. The recipe of the Primaries (K1) feeds the weather encoder those columns, and their stored values exist only for the Primaries, so this network omits them.
  • Pretraining and weather at lag time. Lag-time weather is the expected-weather embedding from the ensemble run issued at or before each lag time, as in experiment 586, so it is available at forecast time. Lags are at least 24 h old.
  • Load-shifts at the BSPs and GSPs are ignored, so lag rows hold unlabelled events. NGED's event labels are also incomplete.
  • Lead range is 0 to 240 h, against NGED's horizon of 1 to 10 days. A lead of exactly 240 h is dropped.
  • Not scored: curtailment cost.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text: run_all.sh runs pretraining, step 2, the fits, and the assembly for both groups (about 20 minutes on one GPU process under 8 GB). e00619_score.py, e00619_tails.py, and e00619_figures.py write the scores, the tails, and the figures. Forecasts are in the private Parquet export export/lag_enabled_<month>.parquet, in the layout of experiment 611's export (columns time_series_id, power_fcst_init_time, valid_time, lead_hours, q01 to q99, observed_power, unit), with substations.csv. Fitted weights are under work/<group>/models/P4E in the experiment's data folder. Code reused: the folders of experiments 87, 397, 415, 428, 448, 510, 511, 559, 560, 572, 574, 577, 591, and 611.

docs.title: How do the three frozen candidate demand networks score on the held-out months July to October 2026 at the 16 Primaries?
docs.text:
Three frozen demand networks were trained once on data before 2026-07-01 and scored once on the 123 forecast origins from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31. K1 and the class 2 candidate did not beat the manual heuristic on continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) or on the mean absolute error (MAE) of the median. K3 was worse than the heuristic on CRPS. All three beat climatology clearly, and the ranking K1, candidate, K3 is the one the development months gave. This is a descriptive result: the window is scored once, nothing was tuned on the window, and nothing is adopted for production.

Terms. K1 is the lag neural network with the G4 gate (a band that widens while a load-shift is detected and for 7 days after). The class 2 candidate is the ungated lag network with neighbour summaries and 50% signal dropout from experiment 610, with its band scaled about the median by a factor of 1.0934. K3 is the lag-free neural network. All three use the slow offset D5 and the refit rule E3 (7-day embargo, then half weight for 7 days). The manual heuristic forecasts a time as the observed powers at the same weekday and time of day 1 to 6 weeks back and 49 to 55 weeks back, using only lags longer than the lead. Climatology is the quantiles of the power before 2026-07-01 in the same calendar cell (local month, half-hour of day, weekday or weekend). Scores are percentages of each Primary's capacity. CRPS is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels. Coverage is the share of readings inside the q05-q95 band. A Primary is a primary substation: the eight MVA Primaries are metered in megavolt-amperes and the six MW Primaries in megawatts. D15 and D18 are the two report-only Primaries with short histories.

docs.title: The pooled result rests on one unlabelled load transfer between D14 and D18
docs.text:
The daily power at D14 and D18 stepped in opposite directions on 2026-07-06/07 and stepped again on 2026-10-26/27. D14 fell from about 48 to about 42 percent of capacity and stayed near 39 to 44 until mid-October, then rose to 63 to 69. D18 rose from 44 to 48 to between 60 and 93, then fell to 62 to 65. The pattern looks like a load transfer between the two Primaries lasting about 16 weeks (D14 lost about 1 MW and D18 gained 1 to 2 MW), although neither Primary returned to its old level. NGED's labels hold no event in the window, and the label file is a one-off dump that will not be updated, so an audit of the stored results found the transfer from the power itself, not from labels. K1's gate was on for 116 of the 123 origin days at both Primaries, so K1 widened its band, but its median stayed at the old level, as the lag neural networks are built to do. The heuristic's weekly lags followed the step within a few weeks.

Two second readings of the window show how much of the pooled result this transfer carries. Both are descriptive readings made after the window was opened. Neither was used to rank the systems, choose a network, or tune anything, and both were recomputed from the stored forecast tables with no network re-run (e00620_second_reading.py).

  • Event-free rows (rule R1). The rule was fixed before any score on the rows it removes was computed, although the per-Primary headline scores had already been seen, so the rule is not blind to which Primaries it flags. It reads only observed power, the heuristic, and climatology, never a network. For each Primary and UTC day it takes the daily mean of observed power minus the median of the heuristic (all 13 members) and of climatology, subtracts that day's median across the 16 Primaries, averages the two residuals, and standardises by the Primary's median and 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation over 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30. It flags days with an absolute z of more than 3, bridges single-day gaps, keeps runs of 3 or more days, and removes every row of that Primary on those days for all five systems alike. It removes 142,949 of the 929,870 rows (15.4%): D18 accounts for 120 Primary-days, D14 for 73, D10 for 50, and nine other Primaries for 82 together.
  • Without D15 and D18. This drops the two report-only Primaries with short histories, which carry 114,434 rows. The pooled mean gives each Primary about equal weight, so these two count as much as any other.
Reading Rows K1 Candidate K3 Heuristic Climatology All rows: CRPS 929,870 4.94 5.00 5.32 4.85 8.12 Event-free rows (R1): CRPS 786,921 4.06 4.07 4.33 4.31 7.86 Without D15 and D18: CRPS 815,436 3.61 3.66 4.01 3.85 7.37 Rows removed by R1: CRPS 142,949 9.83 10.13 10.75 7.78 9.54 All rows: MAE 929,870 8.30 8.42 8.85 8.49 14.75 Event-free rows (R1): MAE 786,921 7.34 7.37 7.80 7.62 14.20 Without D15 and D18: MAE 815,436 6.32 6.46 6.95 6.83 13.49

Caption: percent of capacity, lower is better. The first row of each measure is the pooled headline. The fourth row shows the rows R1 removed.

The ranking against the heuristic reverses on both second readings. The differences in CRPS, network minus heuristic, with day-block 95% intervals, are below.

Reading K1 Candidate K3 All rows +0.10 (-0.03 to +0.22) +0.15 (+0.03 to +0.28) +0.47 (+0.34 to +0.61) Event-free rows (R1) -0.26 (-0.36 to -0.15) -0.25 (-0.35 to -0.14) +0.02 (-0.10 to +0.14) Without D15 and D18 -0.24 (-0.33 to -0.16) -0.20 (-0.28 to -0.12) +0.16 (+0.07 to +0.24)

Caption: percentage points of capacity; negative favours the network. These intervals are not Bonferroni-corrected and are not used to rank.

Per-Primary wins on the kept rows are the same under each reading, so the change comes from how far the networks lose, not from which Primaries they lose at. K1 and the candidate have a lower CRPS than the heuristic at 12 of 16 Primaries on all rows and on the event-free rows, and at 12 of 14 without D15 and D18. K3 does so at 9 of 16, 9 of 16, and 9 of 14. Climatology wins at none.

  • R1 under-removes. The heuristic adapts to a long step after some weeks, so the rule stops flagging D14 after mid-September. Some of the D14 loss therefore stays in the event-free rows.
  • Both second readings are made after the window was opened. The two readings remove different Primaries: R1 mainly D18, D14, and D10, and the other reading D15 and D18. They support the description that the pooled loss comes largely from a few Primaries, and D15 and D16 are not explained by the transfer. Neither reading supports any ranking among K1, the candidate, and K3.
  • The transfer is unconfirmed. It is inferred from the power at two Primaries. NGED has not said that load moved between them.
