docs.text: Caption: D5, 14 days from 2026-08-03. Each panel shows the median and the q05-q95 band of the forecasts issued 24 to 48 hours ahead, with the observed power. Both panels use the same colours. The window holds no verified load-shift event, so there is no event example. The date range was fixed before the window was scored.

docs.title: Predictions, decision rule, and what was not measured
docs.text:
• P1 fails. No network has a lower CRPS than the manual heuristic over the window.
  • P2 fails. Q05-q95 coverage is 0.73 to 0.77. It was predicted to lie between 0.85 and 0.95. The window has no labelled events, so coverage is over all rows.
  • P3 holds. The CRPS ranking K1, candidate, K3 equals the ranking in experiment 613, and the Bonferroni intervals exclude zero for all three pairwise contrasts.
  • Not compared: BG2 and the weak production-style XGBoost model have no forecasts for the window, and none were generated for this run. A later, separately frozen run could add them.
  • Not measured: follow ratio and absorption, because no verified load-shift event is labelled in the window. The NGED event labels are incomplete in general, so a clean row may hold an unlabelled event.

docs.title: Limits and deviations
docs.text:
• One fit and no refits. Each network was fitted once, at the cutoff 2026-07-01, and not refitted during the four months. The development months refit on day 0 and day 14. The window is therefore probably a harder test than weekly production retraining. This page has not tested that, nor whether the effect is the same for all three networks.
  • Candidate band. The band-width factor 1.0934 is the mean of experiment 613's five development-month factors. The candidate was scored with E3 only: E3 is a fixed refit rule and no embargo trigger exists, so there is no comparison with and without it.
  • G4 gate. The gate's per-Primary threshold comes from the development months of experiment 592, not from the window.
  • Comparators. The manual heuristic and climatology were regenerated in numpy from the definitions of the baseline_forecasters package, using cleaned power. The heuristic reads the observed power of the window at the lags it is allowed.
  • Generator readings. Zero readings of NGED's metered generators are missing since 2026-03-26. This run scores Primaries only, so no generator series is shown.
  • National signals. The price data stop on 2026-10-12, demand on 2026-10-01, and the Demand Flexibility Service table on 2026-03-27. The three networks read none of these columns.
  • Standardisers. The predict-time standardisers were rebuilt on the extended inputs and differ from the train-time ones by about 23 rows of 85,000 at D5. No window power is involved.
  • BSP and GSP demand networks were not scored here.

docs.title: How the run was frozen and run
docs.text:
The networks were trained with the held-out power hidden, and the freeze config (freeze_config.json, SHA-256 75d09345…4dfc17) lists the SHA-256 of 319 artefacts and 12 code files. The timing assertions of experiment 614's runner (weather run equals origin minus 9 hours, every lag at least 24 hours old) passed on all 123 origins. A fresh Sonnet reviewer checked the first freeze, the patch below, and the final config.

The first attempt aborted before any forecast existed. The feature build stopped with ValueError: 931752 rows have no row in experiment 437's table, because experiment 437's stored weather-column tables stop before the window. No forecast, score, or test power had been produced or read. The patch rebuilt those tables with experiment 437's own code from the extended weather summaries and CAMS irradiance (weather only, no power). On every key the old tables held, every column is bit-equal (maximum difference 0.0), and the three networks still reproduce experiment 613's development forecasts exactly. The aborted run left a lock file with only its "started" line. The maintainer approved moving it aside, and it was renamed to final_test_620.lock.aborted-20261107T1123Z, not deleted.

Two assembly fixes after the forecasts existed. e00620_assemble.py first failed on a missing output folder, and then on experiment 48's loader copy, which still used the old grid. The fixes were out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and pointing that loader copy at the extended grid and inputs. Neither touched a forecast, the gate threshold, the neighbour list, or the width factor. The hash of e00620_assemble.py was bf86c135…21551b at the freeze and is daf00981…74c94 after the fixes.

Lint-only edits after the run. Before the pull request, ruff and ty edits changed the text of every e00620_*.py file: removed unused imports and noqa directives, added ruff and ty suppressions, and re-formatted. They changed no computation, so freeze_config.json no longer matches the code hashes, and the forecasts' hashes in output_hashes.txt are the evidence that the forecasts are the ones the frozen run produced.

The exported forecasts are in data/ml-experiments/backtest_export_final_test_demand_2026-11-07/, in the layout of experiment 614's export.

docs.title: Injected known-answer and placebo test of the donor-day PV probe
docs.text:
Take-home: the donor-day probe reads an injected real solar farm at about 0.68 of its megawatts, so it fails the 0.85 to 1.15 bar, and the line stops here with no rescue tuning. The reading is stable (0.66 to 0.70 at each of the six MW Primaries, and 0.65 to 0.72 when split by cutoff and size), so a divided estimate is possible. The probe separates a real farm from a profile-only and a shuffled-sky placebo, which the neural attempts of experiments 405 and 477 could not. It cannot separate PV from a load that follows the clouds: without a cloud template a strong linear load reads as 0.39 to 0.45 of a 2 MW farm, and with the template the real PV is mostly removed too.

The question: if a lag-free neural network (experiment 554's modular network M0, pretrained on ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather) is trained on data with a known PV farm added at the six MW Primaries, does a probe with its datetime inputs held fixed read the injected capacity back? Each injected network is compared with an uninjected twin of the same cutoff and seed. The cutoffs are 2026-03 and 2026-06, with 3 seeds each; 15 conditions give 90 pretrainings of about 22 s each on the GPU (about 0.7 GPU-hours in all).

Pass or fail, as pre-registered (a bar passes at 5 of 6 Primaries; 4 of 6 for the 2 MW farm):

Bar Result Pass Real farm 4 MW inside 0.85 to 1.15 0 of 6 (medians 0.65 to 0.71) fail Real farm 4 MW median 0.75 to 0.90 (prediction 1) 0.68 pooled not met Real farm 2 MW inside 0.85 to 1.15 0 of 6 (medians 0.67 to 0.70) fail Physics-curve world recovers more than the real farm (prediction 2) 0.98 against 0.68 met Profile-only placebo, 95th percentile under 0.20 6 of 6 (0.08 to 0.12) pass Shuffled-sky placebo, 95th percentile under 0.20 6 of 6 (0.09 to 0.16) pass Cloud load under 0.15 of 2 MW with the template 6 of 6, all four loads, but negative, down to -0.68 pass, uninformative 80% interval covers truth, physics-curve world 0.68 (bootstrap only 0.10) fail 80% interval covers truth, linear cloud load (weak, strong) 0.72, 0.69 pass, fail
  • Arms. Real farm (farms A, B, C, F, two rotations, 2 MW and 4 MW), physics curve driven by the Primary's own CAMS shortwave (2 MW and 4 MW), profile-only and shuffled-sky placebos (4 MW, two rotations), cloud-following load (linear and squared, averaging 0.10 and 0.30 of 2 MW over daylight half-hours), and the uninjected twin.
  • Absolute readings (uninjected twins). Probed effective AC capacity 1.7 to 2.6 MW per Primary (D5 2.0, D9 1.7, D10 1.7, D11 2.4, D14 2.7, D16 2.1), 2.07 MW at the 2026-03 cutoff and 2.10 MW at 2026-06 on average, with a seed standard deviation of 0.04 to 0.13 MW. Whether these are right is untested.
  • Physics-curve world. Recovery 0.95 to 1.03 at each Primary and size (0.81 to 1.17 for single networks); this world uses the probe's own regressor as the injected shape, so it shows what the probe loses when the shape is known exactly (about 2%) and is not evidence for the real-farm worlds.
  • Cloud load without the template. A weak linear load reads as 0.11 to 0.16 of 2 MW, a strong linear load as 0.39 to 0.45, and a strong squared load as 0.56 to 0.66. The template removes these but also cuts the real-farm recovery to a median of 0.08 (0.04 to 0.16 by cutoff and size), and the strong squared load reads as -0.38 to -0.68, so the template is not a usable fix.
  • Interval. The interval is the day-block bootstrap widened by the across-seed spread, as pre-registered. It is too narrow because the error is bias, not noise: it covers the injected capacity at 0 of 144 real-farm injections.
  • Deviations (fixed before the grid was read). The network has no time input, so the step world is not run. Farms D and E are left out for their daylight gaps, so the six Primaries take farms A, B, C, F, A, B. Half-hours with a gap in any of those four farms (15.5% of the six Primaries' rows at the 2026-06 cutoff) are dropped from every arm. The cloud load runs at two sizes.
  • Not run. The contrastive variant (a synthetic +1 MW of PV added to net demand and compared with the uninjected rows) was not run here; another session runs contrastive injections on this pipeline.
  • Caveats. The cloud load is a UTC-day mean of the cloud response, which the probe's single donor half-hour only partly sees; one injected farm shape per Primary and rotation; the probe is tested on one network family (stage pre of M0, no lags, no drift input).
  • Reuse. Code: ml-experiments/00621-pv-probe-injected-known-answer-and-placebo-test/; it imports experiments 405, 409, 510, 554, and 448 and edits none of them.
  • What to try next. (1) Decide whether to publish the probe's capacity divided by 0.68, with an interval widened for bias. (2) Test whether the 0.68 shortfall comes from the unit curve (orientation, tilt, clipping) by injecting the physics curve with a different tilt. (3) Keep experiment 474's R4 estimate as the main capacity table, with the probe as a second, independent reading.

docs.title: Does a lag-enabled demand network beat a lag-free network at days 1 to 3 at the 2 bulk supply points and the 2 grid supply points, when both use the D5 offset and the thermal-lag columns?
docs.text:
In these 2 bulk supply points (BSPs), 2 grid supply points (GSPs), and 5 development months, giving the demand network the previous day's and the previous week's power lowered its error at days 1 to 3 by 0.11 points of capacity at the BSPs, and by 0.73 points at the GSPs, when the two networks differ in nothing else. Error is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in points of effective capacity (percent of the series' capacity; smaller is better). At the BSPs the gain passes the pre-registered bar: its interval excludes zero and it exceeds the minimum detectable effect (0.08). At the GSPs the interval only just excludes zero (-1.52 to -0.005) and the gain is below its minimum detectable effect (1.16), so the gain is not shown. From day 4 the BSP gain fades to zero, and the GSP gain is neither shown nor ruled out. The 90% band (q05 to q95) still holds the observed power on only 0.85 to 0.89 of rows at days 1 to 3.

Experiment 619 compared a lag-enabled network with experiment 611's lag-free network, which used a different offset and no thermal-lag columns. This experiment refits both arms with the D5 offset of experiment 565, the three-step schedule with a 3-day embargo of experiment 574 (arm P5), and the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns of experiment 569, on the same 5 development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), the same 2 seeds, and the rows and scoring of experiment 611. Labels: D5 is the output offset of experiment 565; B1 is the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns; BG2 is the weekly-refitted XGBoost reference model; D13 and D17 are the 2 BSPs, D1 and D6 the 2 GSPs. The lag-free arm is the lag-enabled network with the day-lag and week-lag power values, missing flags, and ages replaced by their "absent" encoding in every row of pre-training, fine-tuning, and scoring. Load-shifts are ignored: no gate, no synthetic load-shifts, no neighbour inputs.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. CRPS of the lag-enabled network minus the lag-free network, by day of lead time. Look at the dots: at the BSPs they rise from about -0.11 on day 1 to zero by day 6 to 7, and at the GSPs they stay below zero on all 10 days, with intervals that include zero from day 4. The intervals are not adjusted for the 10 days, so they are narrower than those of Table 2.

Figure 2. CRPS by day of lead time. Look at the purple and amber lines: the lag-enabled network is lowest on the first days. The two networks meet from day 6 at the BSPs, and stay 0.3 apart at day 10 at the GSPs.

Figure 3. Mean absolute error of the median forecast. Look at the GSPs: the lag-enabled network (purple) is lower on every day.

Figure 4. Share of rows inside the q05 to q95 band. The dashed black line is the target of 0.90. Look at the lines: every forecast sits below it on every day.

Figure 5. D13 (bulk supply point): forecast issued at 09:00 UTC the day before, for the 14 days from 28 December 2025 to 11 January 2026 (the fortnight around the night of highest observed power). Look at the winter peaks: both networks follow them, and compare the band width between the panels.

Figure 6. D17 (bulk supply point), 8 to 21 January 2026, chosen by the same rule. Look at the peaks and the band width in both panels.

Figure 7. D6 (grid supply point), 19 January to 2 February 2026, chosen by the same rule. Look at the band width: it spans several hundred MW.

Figure 8. D1 (grid supply point that mostly exports power), 19 to 31 December 2025, chosen by the same rule. Look at whether the median follows the observed power.

Figure 9. D17: one forecast run issued on 13 January 2026 at 09:00 UTC, over its full 10 days. Look at the band: it widens and narrows with the daily shape of the power, and the median misses some dips.

Figure 10. D6: one forecast run issued on 25 January 2026 at 09:00 UTC. Look at how the band widens with lead time.

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• Held at the BSPs, failed at the GSPs: the lag-enabled network beats the lag-free network at days 1 to 3 by at least the minimum detectable effect (-0.109 against 0.083 at the BSPs; -0.734 against 1.159 at the GSPs).
  • Held: the two networks tie at days 4 to 10, meaning the interval includes zero (-0.069 to +0.022 and -1.074 to +0.411).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Code review: a fresh Sonnet reviewer read the fit code before the first fit and found no leakage. Finding on the lag grid indices: see Caveats.
  • Lag-free arm check: the fit logs show every row's day-lag and week-lag as missing (share_day_lag_missing 1.0) in the lag-free arms and about 0.3 in the lag-enabled arms (the block dropout of experiment 558).
  • Thermal-lag tables: built for the 4 series from the ensemble-mean summaries of experiment 415; experiment 437's causality check (a column never depends on a later run) gave a largest difference of 0 on D13.
  • Mean forecast against median forecast: not computed, because the stored forecasts are quantiles only.
  • July 2026: never read.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Five months and two series per group. Each interval resamples 5 months. The GSP contrasts cannot rank any forecast.
  • The lag-free arm still receives weather at lag times. Masking replaces the power values, the missing flags, and the ages, but the lag encoder still reads the expected weather and calendar row at the lag times. Both arms receive that input, so the contrast isolates the power lags. The lag-free arm is therefore "power-lag-free", not input-free.
  • Labels: D5 is the output offset of experiment 565; B1 is the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns; BG2 is the weekly-refitted XGBoost reference model; D13 and D17 are the 2 BSPs, D1 and D6 the 2 GSPs. The lag-free arm is the lag-enabled network with masked lags, not experiment 611's Design 1. The lag-free arm's parameters include an unused lag encoder. Design 1 is in Table 1 as a reference.
  • Thermal-lag columns for the 4 series are built from ensemble-mean summaries at each series' location and from CAMS irradiance, as for the Primaries. The Primaries' stored tables were not used.
  • Lag-time weather is the expected-weather embedding from the run issued at or before each lag time, so it is available at forecast time. Lags are at least 24 h old.
  • Load-shifts at the BSPs and GSPs are ignored, so lag rows hold unlabelled events. NGED's event labels are also incomplete.
  • Lead range is 0 to 240 h, against NGED's horizon of 1 to 10 days. A lead of exactly 240 h is dropped.
  • Schedule: coarse refits on day 0 and day 14 of each test month, as in experiment 619.
  • Not scored: curtailment cost.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text: run_all.sh builds the thermal-lag tables, then runs pre-training, step 2, the fits, and the assembly for the three new arms and both groups (about 40 minutes on one GPU process under 8 GB). e00622_score.py, e00622_tails.py, and e00622_figures.py write the scores, the tails, and the figures. Forecasts are in the private Parquet export export/{lagged_b1,lagfree_b1}_<month>.parquet, in the layout of experiment 611's export (columns time_series_id, power_fcst_init_time, valid_time, lead_hours, q01 to q99, observed_power, unit), with substations.csv. Fitted weights are under work/<group>/models/{J_LG_B1,J_LF_B1,J_LF_NB} in the experiment's data folder. The lag-enabled arm without B1 is experiment 619's stored forecast.

docs.title: Monotone arm of the injected known-answer test of the donor-day PV probe
docs.text: A network forced to lower net demand as shortwave irradiance rises still recovers only about 70% of an injected real farm, against 68% for the plain network. Both networks recover a physics-curve injection almost exactly, so the probe works when the injected shape is the unit PV curve and loses about 30% when the injected shape is a real farm's. The real-farm bar (median recovery 0.80 to 1.20 at 4 of 6 Primaries) fails in both arms, at 0 of 6 Primaries each time. The stop rule (median recovery under 0.70 in both arms, or a placebo over 0.30) did not fire, because the monotone arm's median is 0.71 and the largest placebo read is 0.17.

docs.title: Bars
docs.text:
Bar (fixed before any read-out) Plain arm Monotone arm Median 4 MW real-farm recovery in 0.80 to 1.20 at 4 of 6 Primaries Fail, 0 of 6 (median 0.68) Fail, 0 of 6 (median 0.71) 95th percentile of each placebo under 0.25 at 4 of 6 Pass (largest 0.16) Pass (largest 0.17) Spurious capacity from a cloud load under 0.20 of a 2 MW farm with the cloud-template regression (a one-sided bar; negative values are over-correction), at 4 of 6 Pass Pass 80% interval covers the injected capacity in at least 60% of injections Fail: 23% of the real-farm and physics-curve injections together (real farm 0%, physics curve 68%) Fail: 26% (real farm 0%, physics curve 76%) Seed standard deviation lower in the monotone arm at 4 of 6 Primaries Fail: lower at 3 of 6 Validation negative log-likelihood rises by under 0.01 nats Fail: +0.0104 (2026-03 cutoff) and +0.0113 (2026-06 cutoff)
  • Real-farm recovery is the same at both cutoffs (monotone 0.711 and 0.712; plain 0.682 and 0.683) and at both farm rotations, so the shortfall is not an accident of one cutoff or one farm-to-Primary assignment.
  • The interval fails because recovery is biased, not because it is narrow. The real-farm injections are covered 0% of the time in both arms, since the interval is centred on about 0.7 of the truth. The interval passes in the physics-curve world for the monotone arm (76%) and the plain arm (68%), and in the linear strong cloud-load world (75% and 69%).
  • The monotone arm does not lower the seed spread of the probed capacity. It is lower at D10, D14, and D9 and higher at D11, D16, and D5 (spread of the uninjected networks' probed capacity, the measure in the seed-spread figure; the spread of the injected differences is also lower at 3 of 6).
  • Validation loss. The mean validation negative log-likelihood of the uninjected networks is 0.467 (plain) and 0.477 (monotone) at 2026-03, and 0.472 and 0.484 at 2026-06. The CRPS on the same validation rows rises from 0.365 to 0.368 MW (2026-03) and 0.365 to 0.369 MW (2026-06) over all 16 Primaries (0.8% and 1.0%), and from 0.276 to 0.278 MW (2026-03) and 0.275 to 0.277 MW (2026-06) at the six MW Primaries. Each network's early stopping reads these rows, so the figures compare the arms and do not measure out-of-sample skill.

docs.title: The probed response against the unit PV curve
docs.text: The probed difference between an injected network and its twin falls linearly in the unit PV curve of the donor weather in both worlds and both arms. In the physics-curve world the lines follow the dashed 4 MW slope. In the real-farm world the slope is about 0.7 of it. The monotone constraint changes neither slope visibly. The cause of the flatter real-farm response is untested. A real farm's orientation, shading, and inverter clipping, which the unit curve lacks, are candidates.

docs.title: Placebos and the cloud-following load
docs.text:
Both placebos read under 0.18 of the injected megawatts at every Primary in both arms. The monotone arm's shuffled-sky placebo reads slightly higher (0.13 to 0.17) than the plain arm's (0.09 to 0.16).

Without the cloud template, both arms read a cloud-following load as PV (weak loads 0.11 to 0.23, strong loads 0.35 to 0.66 of a 2 MW farm). With the template, both pass. The plain network over-corrects (negative spurious capacity as large as -0.7 for the strong squared load), and the monotone network stays closer to zero (-0.2). Over-correction is not faking, but it shows that the template regression absorbs more than the cloud load alone in the plain network.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Monotone network (e00623_model.py). The weather encoder sees the other six weather columns with shortwave zeroed. A context network reads the datetime encoder's output and the Primary embedding and returns an amplitude, a slope, and an offset for each of 16 units. The shortwave effect h is the sum of softplus(amplitude) * softplus(softplus(slope) * sw + offset), which is non-decreasing in sw, and h is subtracted from every mixture component's mean. A sweep over 50 shortwave values on 2,000 random rows found no increase of the mixture means. Monotonicity holds with every other input fixed, so the other weather inputs (longwave, temperature, dew point) can still carry cloud information.
  • Everything else is experiment 621's (experiment 621): worlds, farms A, B, C, and F, rotations, cutoffs, seeds, probe, bootstrap, and the plain-arm results. The code in this folder is a copy of experiment 621's, with the model, the recovery bars, the arm comparison, and the validation CRPS script added. The pretraining takes about 26 s per network (about 25 to 29 s over the grid), so the 90 networks took about 0.7 GPU-hours.
  • Not run. The step world, as in experiment 621. The seed standard deviation of the probed capacity is 0.05 to 0.15 MW, so a 2 MW injection exceeds 4 seed standard deviations at every Primary, and the 2 MW injections were kept.
  • Earlier work. Experiment 129, 235, 269, 405, 474, 477, and 479 set the worlds, the placebos, and the recovery of 0.62 to 0.83 that this result matches.

docs.title: Contrastive injection arms for the donor-day PV probe
docs.text: The contrastive loss failed: it takes real-farm recovery from 0.68 to 0.00, at every Primary, and raises the validation CRPS by 37% (all 16 Primaries) to 59% (the six MW Primaries). The pre-registered stop rule (real-farm median recovery of arm (a) under 0.70) fired, so no rescue tuning was run. The loss was built as a paired-difference term and tested in three arms. A separate diagnosis, requested after experiments 621 and 623, explains most of why a real farm reads 0.68 where the physics curve reads 0.97: a real farm scaled to a given 99th-percentile output has 0.72 to 0.84 of the energy of the physics curve scaled the same way.

docs.title: The contrastive arms
docs.text:
Every real training row of the six MW Primaries has a physics twin (+1 MW of the unit curve) and a profile twin (+1 MW with no sky link), each with its own embedding vector. Arm (a) trains with the twin rows and a paired-difference term. Arm (b) refits only the twin vectors of experiment 621's plain networks. Arm (c) applies the refit to arm (a)'s networks. Each network is also trained in one held-out world, as in experiment 621.

Bar Plain network (experiment 621) Arm (a), contrastive loss Median 4 MW real-farm recovery in 0.80 to 1.20 at 4 of 6 Primaries Fail, 0 of 6 (median 0.68) Fail, 0 of 6 (median 0.00) Physics-curve world recovery (context) 0.98 -0.01 95th percentile of each placebo under 0.25 at 4 of 6 Pass (largest 0.16) Pass (largest 0.01; recovery is 0 everywhere) Spurious capacity from a strong linear cloud load under 0.20 of a 2 MW farm (regression without the cloud template) 0.39 to 0.45 (above 0.20) 0.00 Same, with the cloud-template regression (sensitivity) Pass Pass (0.00 to 0.03) 80% interval covers the injected capacity in at least 60% of real-farm and physics-curve injections Fail, 23% (real farm 0%, physics curve 69%) Fail, 0% Validation CRPS within 1% of the plain network's Fail: 0.50 MW against 0.36 MW at all 16 Primaries (2026-03), 0.44 against 0.28 MW at the six MW Primaries
  • Scoring of the pre-registered predictions. Prediction (1) is refuted (median 0.00). Prediction (2) holds, trivially, because arm (a) reads zero in every world. Prediction (3) holds with the cloud template. Prediction (4) is refuted (0% coverage). Prediction (5) is refuted (CRPS up 37% to 59%). Prediction (6) is refuted: arm (b) reads the physics twin at about 0.20 MW, not near 1 MW. - The cloud bar has two versions. The original bar, with the cloud template in the regression, passes. The amended headline bar, without the template, fails for the plain network (0.39 to 0.45). - Arm (a) passes the placebo bars only because it reads zero in every world. The probe response of the network through the real Primary's vector is flat, including in the physics-curve world. - In sample, the twin vectors read the synthetic +1 MW. The physics twin reads 0.98 to 1.03 MW and the profile twin 0.05 to 0.07 MW, so the loss was satisfied on the twin rows while the network fitted the real rows badly. The validation negative log-likelihood of arm (a) is 0.61 to 0.74 against 0.42 for the matched control (nopair: twin rows in the likelihood, no paired-difference term). - The matched control shows that the twin rows alone do not change recovery. The nopair networks recover a real farm at a median of 0.70 (0.68 to 0.74 across Primaries), against 0.68 for the plain network. - The post-hoc check (b) cannot absorb the synthetic +1 MW. Fitting only the twin vector of a plain network recovers a median of 0.20 MW of the physics twin's 1 MW (range -0.26 to 0.25 over Primaries, for the uninjected networks), and 0.11 MW of the profile twin. Arm (c) recovers a median of 0.00 MW over worlds (0.02 to 0.52 MW over Primaries in the uninjected world). A frozen network may not let one 8-wide embedding vector reproduce a sky response. - A calibration from the physics twin would not have found the real-farm shortfall. In the arms where the loss ran, the physics twin was read at about 1, whereas a real farm reads 0.68.

docs.title: Calibration and interval coverage (changes agreed after experiments 621 and 623)
docs.text: For the plain network, the leave-one-farm-out factor (median 4 MW real-farm recovery of the networks whose farm differs) is 0.683, 0.684, 0.678, and 0.684 when holding out farms A, B, C, and F, so the factor is stable and lies in 0.55 to 0.85 for all 4 farms. Farms D and E are not injected, so the stability bar is judged over 4 farms, not 6. The calibrated recovery is 1.00 by construction, because the factor is the median recovery. The raw interval, widened by the spread of per-farm recoveries, covers the injected capacity in 0% of real-farm injections, because it is centred on 0.68. The calibrated interval, widened by the spread of the factors, covers 68% (experiment 624's plain networks), 72% (experiment 621's plain networks), and 69% (experiment 623's monotone networks). Arm (a)'s recovery is zero, so a factor fitted to it is meaningless and is not reported. With the cloud template in the regression, the per-farm recovery falls to 0.04 to 0.10, which is why the template is a sensitivity row and not the headline.

docs.title: Why a real farm reads 0.68 and the physics curve 0.97
docs.text:
Three cheap tests, each with one set of plain networks, address three hypotheses.

Test 1, scaling audit: the injected real farm has 0.72 to 0.84 of the physics curve's energy over all daylight half-hours. Each farm's series is its output divided by its own 99th percentile and then multiplied by the injected MW, so the injected series reaches the injected MW at its 99th percentile by construction (observed 99th percentile 1.000 to 1.003 for farms A, B, C, and F). The physics curve is scaled the same way. At the same half-hours, on each Primary's own CAMS shortwave, the sum of a farm's series is 0.72 to 0.84 of the sum of the physics curve:

Farm Mean ratio to the physics curve, six MW Primaries (range) A 0.72 to 0.78 B 0.74 to 0.79 C 0.79 to 0.81 F 0.81 to 0.84

A probe that recovers energy exactly would read 0.97 times 0.79, about 0.77, for a real farm. The measured 0.68 is 0.88 of that. Farm F has the highest energy ratio, but the median recovery by farm is 0.67 to 0.70, so the probe does not track the ratio farm by farm.

Test 2, clipped physics-curve world: clipping lowers recovery, but not to 0.68. Median recovery of the injected 4 MW is 0.95 at a DC-to-AC ratio of 1.0, 0.90 at 1.2, and 0.81 at 1.4. Clipping at a ratio of 1.4 removes about half of the 0.29 gap between the physics curve and the real farm; the farms' own ratios are unknown.

Test 3, displaced-sky world: displacing the sky by up to 17 km lowers recovery by about 0.05. The CAMS downloads are point series per site, so an offset of one or two CAMS grid cells is not available locally. The injection is the physics curve driven by the shortwave of the nearest and second-nearest other Primary, which lies 0.8 to 17 km away. Median recovery is 0.93 for the nearest Primary and 0.95 for the second nearest, against 0.98 with the Primary's own sky (0.949 for the matched plain networks). At D14, whose nearest Primary lies 0.8 km away, recovery stays at 0.98 to 1.01; at 9 to 17 km it is 0.90 to 0.96, so recovery is lower at larger distances, from few Primaries. A displacement of this size does not explain the gap. A displacement larger than the Primaries' spacing, or an offset of one or two CAMS grid cells, is untested.

Hypothesis summary. The scaling convention (the real farm's lower energy at the same 99th percentile) is arithmetically consistent with about two-thirds of the gap (0.97 to 0.77), clipping at a ratio of 1.4 for up to half, and a sky displaced by 5 to 17 km for under 0.05. These shares overlap and do not sum, because the three tests were each run alone. Smoothing of the real farm's shape by the neural network (the third hypothesis in the brief) is a candidate for the remainder, and it is untested directly.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Contrastive arms. e00624_common.py builds the twin rows and the paired-difference term 1.0 * mean(((mean_twin - mean_real - delta) / 0.05)^2), with dropout on in both forwards. e00624_fit.py trains arm (a) and the nopair control, and e00624_post.py fits the twin vectors for arms (b) and (c). The network, rows, loop, seeds, and probe are copied or imported from experiments 621 and 623.
  • Worlds. Control, real farm at 4 MW (two rotations), physics curve at 4 MW, profile-only and shuffled-sky placebos at 4 MW, and a strong linear cloud load, at 2 cutoffs (2026-03 and 2026-06) and 3 seeds. The three diagnostic tests use experiment 621's plain network and 3 seeds at both cutoffs.
  • Size. Arm (a) trains in about 100 s per network (against 26 s without twin rows). The whole experiment, including the diagnostic worlds, took about 2 GPU-hours.
  • Earlier work. The worlds and placebos descend from experiment 129, 405, 474, 477, and 479.

docs.title: How few member paths can NGED's power-flow studies use, and does a Schaake shuffle of residual paths give the 16 Primaries any coherence gain?
docs.text:
A Schaake shuffle of past observed paths makes the farms' paths coherent (34% below independent draws) and 20 paths lose 2% to 3% of the 51-path score across the farms (1% across the Primaries), but no coupling helped the 16 Primaries. NGED want member paths that are coherent across sites and time for power-flow studies. This experiment reuses the 51-path scenario tables of experiments 434 and 436 and adds a K sweep (5, 10, 20, and 51 paths), a shuffle of anomaly paths for the Primaries, the CRPS of K paths, member-spread coverage, a neighbouring-farm check, and a step-change autocorrelation check. The registered verdict is partly supported: farms passed (C1), Primaries did not (C2). While scoring we found that experiment 436's joint block mixed nodes and members; the corrected joint block is below.

Terms: IND independent draws; ECC ensemble copula coupling (ranks from the weather members); SS Schaake shuffle of 51 past observed paths; SS-R the same shuffle ranking anomaly paths (observed power minus the mean of the four preceding same-weekday dates at that clock time); J5 ECC ranks mixed with a Gaussian error copula; MW member-wise quantiles. Scores are variogram scores (order 0.5) in points of capacity, days 1 to 10, over 44 Tuesday runs in 10 calendar months; intervals are 98.33% month-block bootstrap intervals.

Example paths (reused from experiment 436, generators anonymised): winter day-ahead, winter 14 days, summer day-ahead, summer 14 days.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• C1, farms (supported). SS against IND on the nine farms: -34.4% (-42.5% to -26.1%), absolute 2.26 against 3.45. Wind farms -28.3% (-35.6% to -20.0%); solar farms -40.2% (-50.4% to -31.3%). ECC with ensemble ranks: -16.1% (-29.4% to -3.1%); J5 -36.2% (-42.5% to -29.4%).
  • C2, Primaries (not supported). SS-R against IND on the 16 Primaries: -0.3% (-1.6% to +1.2%), absolute 1.600 against 1.605. SS +0.4% (-1.1% to +2.1%), J5 -0.7% (-1.5% to +0.2%), ECC +6.8% (+4.5% to +9.2%). Prediction P2 failed as expected.
  • Why the Primaries gain nothing. From experiment 436's dependence table, the realised correlation of normal scores between Primaries is 0.29. IND gives 0.00, SS 0.47, ECC 0.93, and J5 0.26. J5 matches the realised value best and still gains only 0.7%, so the variogram score on 16 weakly correlated nodes cannot resolve the coupling; ECC overshoots and loses 6.8%. SS-R ranks anomaly paths from at most 43 earlier dates in each run's pool, so its ordering is noisy as well. This account is descriptive, not a test. The share of the Primaries' variance explained by two common components was not computed.
  • C3, K sweep (K = 10 is enough not met; prediction P1 failed). Variogram score of K paths against 51 of the same coupling: farms SS K = 5 +20.9%, K = 10 +7.9% (+6.8% to +9.2%), K = 20 +2.5% (+1.6% to +3.5%); Primaries SS-R K = 5 +5.9%, K = 10 +3.0% (+2.0% to +3.9%), K = 20 +1.0% (+0.6% to +1.4%). By the registered tests, farms need K = 51 (K = 20 misses the 2% point test by 0.5 points) and the Primaries need K = 20. Wind farms alone pass at K = 20 (+2.0%, +0.9% to +3.0%); solar farms do not (+3.1%).
  • Corrected joint block (all 25 nodes, 6-hourly leads). Against IND (absolute 2.19): ECC +0.2%, SS +0.5%, SS-R +0.0%, J5 -0.1%, MW +0.8%. No coupling differs by more than 1%. K = 20 costs +0.8% and K = 10 +2.6%.
  • MW against SS on the farms: +0.9% (-3.7% to +7.6%); MW is not beaten, and not better.
  • CRPS of K paths against the direct 51-value CRPS (days 1 to 10). K = 20: +0.28% demand, +0.50% wind, +0.32% solar. K = 10: +1.28%, +1.66%, +1.20%, so K = 10 fails the 1% marginal bar. K = 5: +4.0%, +4.4%, +3.8%. Prediction P3 held. MW at 51 paths: +1.07% wind, +4.13% solar (fails the bar). Demand at K = 51 is identical by construction (the stored marginal), so the stop rule did not fire.
  • Coverage of the member spread, days 1 to 10 (nominal 50%, 80%, 90%; K = 5 and 10 are given for the Primaries only). K = 51: demand 46%, 75%, 89%; wind 46%, 74%, 85%; solar 46%, 75%, 84%. K = 10: 40%, 66%, 74% (demand). K = 5: 33%, 55%, 61% (demand). The coverage is a property of the marginal and of K and does not depend on the coupling. The tail bands of wind and solar are under-covered, as experiment 436 found.
  • Opposite sky states (top-quarter-spread days, 111 run-days, five most-correlated farm pairs chosen on 2025-03 to 2025-08). Observed 0.82% (0.31% to 1.54%); IND 7.7%; ECC 0.00%; SS 0.21% (0.14% to 0.30%); SS-R 0.45%; J5 0.02%; MW 0.30%. IND puts neighbouring farms in opposite states about ten times as often as the observations; every coupling is at or below the observed rate. Hypothesis claim (3) was half met: SS is far below IND, but also below the observed share. Prediction P4 failed for SS, which fell below the observed share rather than between it and IND.
  • Step-change autocorrelation (days 1 to 3, lag 1). Observed: Primaries 0.34, wind farms 0.04 (the solar observed value is unavailable: solar actuals hold missing night half-hours, so no full window qualifies). In the order Primaries, wind farms, solar farms: IND -0.40, -0.49, -0.35; SS 0.40, 0.02, 0.14; SS-R 0.34, 0.00, 0.10; ECC 0.47, 0.47, 0.32; MW 0.47, 0.10, 0.05. IND's negative autocorrelation is the artefact of drawing each half-hour independently; SS-R matches the Primaries exactly. Prediction P5 holds: MW is further from the observed value than SS for the Primaries and the wind farms.
  • Tails. Marginals are unchanged from experiments 425, 429, and 430, so no new tail scores. K = 51 coverage at 90% is given above. No curtailment cost, load-shift events, or fits are involved.
  • Reused and new. Reused, not recomputed: the 51 values per node and half-hour and the J0, J2, J3, J5, and J6 scenario tables of experiment 436. New: SS-R, every K cut, all scores in this page (including the 51-path scores, recomputed with the corrected joint block), CRPS, coverage, sky-state, and autocorrelation tables. Experiment 434 flattens its joint vector correctly (reshape(N_MEMBERS, -1) without the transpose) and is unaffected.
  • Checks. No forecast was fitted, so the median-minus-mean and audit triggers do not apply. The K = 51 CRPS check was exact. A toy test (e00625_check_joint_reshape.py) fails on experiment 436's reshape and passes on the one used here. A check on a normal distribution (e00625_check_k_values.py) shows the plain CRPS of K values at levels j/(K+1) is within 3.5% of the true value at K = 5 and 0.5% from K = 10.
  • Caveats. Ten calendar months give wide intervals. The opposite-sky check rests on 111 run-days and the observed share has an interval from 0.3% to 1.5%. The spread proxy for member disagreement is the q90 minus q10 of the stored quantile forecast (XGBoost and neural network models), not the ensemble's own spread. The solar observed autocorrelation is missing. The pool of past paths starts on 2025-03-01 and is thin for the earliest runs.
  • Options for later. A Schaake shuffle that ranks forecast-error paths (actual minus median forecast) once more than 43 runs exist; the same sweep on BSP and GSP nodes once the topology lands; and testing whether NGED's power-flow studies change their answer between K = 10 and K = 20 paths.
  • Reviews. Sonnet plan review (12 findings; accepted the margin, per-contrast wording, K stride, weekday baseline, and pair-selection window; the fair energy score was replaced after the numeric check); Sonnet code review before the first run (found no holdout mask, the stride, a sky-total mismatch, and a NaN sort; all fixed). The results review and the two write-up reviews are recorded in the pull request.

docs.title: Reused and new
docs.text:
• Reused, not recomputed. The 51 values per node and half-hour (work/runs), and the 51-path scenario tables of IND (J0), ECC (J2), SS (J3), the copula-corrected ranks (J5), and MW (J6; wind and solar only, demand follows J2) from experiment 436's work/paths. The marginals are those of experiments 425 (demand, widened 1.15), 429 (wind), and 430 (solar).
  • New. Scores at K = 5, 10, 20, 51; SS-R (anomaly-path shuffle); CRPS from K values; member-spread coverage; opposite-sky-state shares; step-change autocorrelation. Experiment 436's 51-path scores are recomputed in the same script.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• K paths. For K below 51 the K values are the 51 values interpolated at levels j/(K+1). The ordering of a coupling is cut to K by taking every (51/K)-th path of its 51 (members are in the order of nearest day of year for SS and SS-R, so the K paths spread over the pool) and ranking those K paths. The 51 values are themselves interpolated from the 11 stored quantiles, so the K values interpolate twice; this is a stated limit. MW has no cut and is scored at 51 only. Before the first run, a check on a known normal distribution shows the plain CRPS of K values at levels j/(K+1) is within 3.5% of the true value at K = 5 and within 0.5% from K = 10 (the fair form, with the pair term divided by K(K-1), is 13% low at K = 5, so it is not used).
  • SS-R. The anomaly of a past date is its observed path minus the mean of the same clock time on the four same-weekday dates 7, 14, 21, and 28 days before the path's start, per node (the runs are Tuesdays). The pool and the 16-day buffer are 436's. SS-R is applied to all nodes; the report uses it for the Primaries, and for the farms beside J3. The weather source is none (observed power only), so every input is available at forecast time.
  • Why nothing helped across the Primaries. Reported from the stored diag_dependence table: the realised and the constructed correlations of the normal scores between Primaries, and the share of the Primaries' PIT variance that two common components explain, from the other months (eigenvalues of the correlation matrix). No new fit.
  • Opposite sky state. Pairs are the five solar-farm pairs with the highest correlation of daylight observed output over 2025-03 to 2026-06 (a descriptive grouping that stands in for distance). For a pair and a daylight half-hour (10:00 to 14:00 UTC, lead days 1 to 10), a path is opposite if one farm is above its own q80 of the 51 values and the other below its own q20. The share is taken over days whose farm-mean spread (q90 minus q10 of the 51 values) is in the top quarter of all run-days, and the observed share uses the actuals on the same half-hours.
  • Autocorrelation. Lag-1 autocorrelation of the half-hourly change along each path (and along the observed path), over days 1 to 3, averaged over paths and runs per family.
  • Standing practices. Cleaned data as in 436 (flagged half-hours dropped); the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; dev months only, no half-hour on or after 2026-07-01; generators anonymised in every chart and table; example fans reuse 436's figure 4 style (a winter and a summer day-ahead and 14-day example). Not applicable: no fit, so no refit cadence, model saving, GPU, load-shift events, or curtailment cost. The 3% stop rule above is the brief's.

docs.title: Compute and reviews
docs.text:
• CPU only, no GPU, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p OOMPolicy=continue, spawn-based workers. About 2 to 4 hours (estimate from 436's scoring times).
  • Reviews: Sonnet plan review; Sonnet code review before the first run; Sonnet results review; two Sonnet write-up reviews.

docs.title: Can the tails of the 51 scenario values be widened until the q05 and q95 exceedance rates are within 1 point of 5%, without changing the Schaake-shuffled scenario paths' variogram and energy scores by more than 2%?
docs.text:
Rescaling the 51 scenario values (the 51 values per series and half-hour that the forecast hands to a power-flow study) with a separate upper and lower factor (arm D) brought demand's q05 and q95 exceedance to the registered 4% to 6% bar in every lead band, but not wind's or solar's. Demand's q90 was still exceeded by 14.2% of actuals at 12 to 36 hours for the unchanged forecast and 15.6% for arm D (target 10%; 36 test-month runs). Experiment 436's finding that the tails were too narrow came largely from its choice of quantile definition. The question was whether a factor per family and lead band, fitted on earlier months, could bring the q05 and q95 exceedance rates to within 1 point of 5% without disturbing the Schaake-shuffled scenario paths (51 values re-ordered at each half-hour to follow the ranks of historical observed paths; experiment 436's arm J3). The four arms are: A, the stored values unchanged; B, one factor applied above and below the median; C, the values re-drawn at levels stretched about the median; and D, separate upper and lower factors. A cell is one family (demand, wind, or solar) in one lead band; the exceedance of a quantile is the share of actuals beyond the weibull quantile of the 51 values, meaning the k-th smallest value is taken as the level k/52. Demand is the 16 Primaries (the substations that feed the distribution network from the transmission network), and "points of capacity" are percentage points of a series' effective capacity. The registered rule gives partly supported, because the bar held for demand alone; the premise that the tails were too narrow did not hold. Arm D met the q05 half of the bar by narrowing demand's lower side (its lower factor was 0.80 to 0.86, on the 0.8 floor of the fitting grid in most folds) and the q95 half with an upper factor of 0.81 to 1.06. Arm D is therefore a recalibration of two tails, not evidence that the tails were too narrow. The scenario paths and the CRPS changed by under 1.2%. The tail problem of experiments 434 and 436 looks like a demand median bias plus modest wind and solar tail misses, not a uniform shortage of spread.

Figure 1 colours: black is arm A, blue arm B, green arm C, orange arm D. Wind and solar intervals mostly span the whole 4% to 6% band, so those cells cannot be told apart from 5%. In figure 2, the orange band is arm D's q05 to q95, the blue lines are arm A's q05 and q95, and both arms share the median (grey).

Figure 3: demand's q90 is exceeded for 7% to 22% of actuals by month and 11% to 16% by lead band (target 10%), while actuals fell below q10 for 5% to 10% by month.

docs.title: Where demand's bias comes from
docs.text:
The excess above q90 is already in the quantile forecast of experiment 425 (arm A), not added by the member construction. The 51 values are the stored quantiles interpolated linearly in the level, and q10 and q90 are not widened by the 1.15 factor that experiment 436 applies to q01, q05, q95, and q99. Reading q10 and q90 back from the 51 values reproduces the stored q10 and q90 of the quantile table to 0.00001 points of capacity (runs 2026-01-06 and 2026-01-13, all 16 Primaries). The direct quantile forecast therefore shows the same exceedance on the same rows. Script: e00626_bias.py; it uses all 44 runs (not only the 36 test-month runs), because no factor is fitted here, 16 Primaries, leads to 240 hours.

  • By month, all 44 runs (above q90 / below q10 / mean of actual minus median, points of capacity). 2025-09 10.6% / 10.0% / +2.0; 2025-10 14.6% / 7.7% / +2.6; 2025-11 6.6% / 9.8% / -0.2; 2025-12 21.7% / 5.2% / +2.8; 2026-01 16.9% / 9.9% / +1.2; 2026-02 10.7% / 8.5% / +1.2; 2026-03 20.5% / 5.4% / +4.6; 2026-04 11.8% / 8.9% / +1.1; 2026-05 16.3% / 8.0% / +2.3; 2026-06 16.0% / 6.7% / +1.0. The upper tail fails by 1.5 points or more in seven of ten months, worst in December and March; November is the one month where the upper tail is too wide.
  • By lead band (all 44 runs). Above q90: 11.0% at 0 to 12 hours, 13.4% at 12 to 36, 14.7% at 36 to 120, 15.5% at 120 to 240. Below q10: 8.2%, 7.2%, 7.1%, 8.7%. The upper-tail miss grows with the lead; the lower tail stays under 10% at every lead.
  • By Primary. Above q90 runs from 6.1% (D11) to 24.2% (D6); D3, D6, D10, and D13 exceed 19%. D4 has a mean error of +15.2 points of capacity.
  • Reading. The median forecast sits below the outcome on average (mean error +1.0 to +4.6 points in nine of ten months), and the q10 to q90 width is about 20 points, so the upper tail is too narrow and the lower tail too wide: a shift of the median should reduce both misses. The cause (for example the monthly refit, the training window, or demand growth) was not investigated here.

docs.title: Design and numbers
docs.text:
• Arms. A unchanged (experiment 436's stored 51 values and J3 Schaake ranks); B one factor per family and lead band applied above and below the median; C values re-drawn at levels stretched about the median, with one stretch per family and band (end values extrapolated by the end slopes); D separate upper and lower factors. Wind and solar values are clipped to 0 to 100 points of capacity. Every arm keeps J3's ranks.
  • Rows. 44 Tuesday runs of experiment 436; 7 test months (2025-12 to 2026-06), 36 runs; each month's factors fitted on all earlier runs (13 to 39 runs). Scored rows: leads to 240 hours with an actual and a non-degenerate forecast. Data: experiment 436's cleaned actuals. No machine-learning model was fitted.
  • Exceedance, arm A (q95 / q05, share of actuals beyond the weibull quantile of the 51 values). Demand 3.9% to 6.2% / 1.8% to 2.5%; wind 4.6% to 8.0% / 5.2% to 6.0%; solar 5.2% to 6.5% / 4.4% to 7.3%. Demand above q90: 11.7% to 16.8% (target 10%); below q10: 6.2% to 7.8%.
  • Arm D, pooled over families, by band (0 to 12, 12 to 36, 36 to 120, 120 to 240 hours). q05 5.1%, 4.5%, 4.4%, 4.8%; q95 6.1%, 5.6%, 5.8%, 5.7%. Arm A pooled: q05 3.3%, 3.0%, 2.7%, 3.4%; q95 4.3%, 4.8%, 5.6%, 6.3%.
  • Cells within 1 point of 5% (of 12). q95 / q05: A 7 / 4; B 3 / 5; C 5 / 4; D 6 / 7. Arm B raised demand's q95 exceedance in every band (for example 4.7% to 7.1% at 12 to 36 hours) because its single factor, below 1 for demand, narrowed the upper tail.
  • Cold winter nights (demand). Arm A: above q90 16.9% to 18.3%, above q95 6.2% to 7.4%. Arms B and C raised above-q95 to 8.9% to 11.2%; arm D 7.4% to 10.1%. Very sunny half-hours (solar). Arm A above q95 5.4% to 7.3%; arms B to D 8.1% to 13.5%, so widening hurts the sunny slice.
  • CRPS of the 51 values, relative to A (bands pooled, 95% month-block interval). Demand B +0.4% (0.0% to +0.6%), C +0.1% (-0.0% to +0.3%), D -0.2% (-0.6% to +0.1%); wind B -0.2%, C -0.2% (-0.4% to -0.0%), D -0.4% (-1.1% to +0.8%); solar B +0.3% (-0.0% to +0.9%), C +0.4%, D +0.4%. All within the 1% limit. Absolute CRPS of A: demand 5.08, wind 10.47, solar 8.61 points of capacity.
  • Path scores, days 1 to 10, relative to A. Joint variogram B +1.1% (+0.7% to +1.5%), C +0.6% (+0.2% to +1.0%), D +0.7% (+0.5% to +1.0%); joint energy within 0.2%. Spatial variogram +0.6% to +1.0%; temporal variogram within 0.2%. All point estimates are within the 2% limit; the spatial variogram interval for arm B reaches +2.5%. Joint variogram of A: 7.39.
  • Tail calibration at q01 and q99 and pinball loss. Not reported: the stored run files hold 51 values, not the q01 and q99 quantile forecasts, and the scenario values stop at levels 1/52 and 51/52.
  • Registered predictions. P1 failed (arm A does not reproduce 7% to 9%; the 7.6% to 8.8% quoted by experiment 436 used numpy's default quantile of the 51 values, as the re-score under 'Checks' shows). P2 partly held. It predicted that arms B and D would reach the pooled bar and fail in at least one cell: arm D pooled came within 0.1 point of the bar (6.1% at 0 to 12 hours), arm B pooled missed in all bands (q95 6.2% to 7.4%, q05 3.1% to 4.5%), and arms B to D failed in at least one cell. P3 failed (pooled CRPS rises were at most 0.4%, and the largest per-band rise, solar arm D at 0 to 12 hours, was about 0.9%, so none exceeded the 1% limit). P4 cannot be judged: the path scores are pooled over families, and none moved by more than 1.1%. P5 failed (wind factors changed by at most 14% between folds; the largest change was 28%, for solar).
  • Stop rule. Largest-to-smallest ratio of a fitted factor across folds: 1.28 (solar, arm D upper factor, 0 to 12 hours), under the 30% limit, so all arms were scored.
  • Caveats. Demand's lower factor reached the grid floor of 0.8 in six of seven folds for each lead band up to 120 hours and in none for 120 to 240 hours, so the grid, not the data, set that factor; the registered grid was kept. Solar's lower quantile is often 0 after clipping, so a solar q05 cell can sit well under 5% for that reason. Training runs from late in a month have leads of up to 10 days whose actuals fall in the next month, the test month (a small leak in the letter of "earlier months"). Seven test months and 36 runs; intervals are month-block. The fit clips wind and solar quantiles after interpolating, and the scoring clips the values before interpolating (a negligible difference). Experiments 577 and 608 were not reused because their widening applies to a different forecast.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first scoring run and found no blocking bugs (its low-severity points are kept as caveats). A fresh Sonnet agent checked every number against the printed report; a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the rendered figures (applied: outline for arm A, left-aligned titles, a subtitle on figure 1, and figure 3); and a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the diff and prose (applied: the verdict now follows the registered rule, arms and terms are defined in the opening, and the 36-run and 44-run sets are labelled). Figure 1's colour legend does not render in the review renderer; the SVG contains it.
  • What to try next. Remove the demand median bias (for example a per-Primary, per-lead offset fitted on earlier months), then refit arm D on the debiased values and re-check the tails; then compare with the planned experiment 483 (table P).
  • Checks. The experiment reports no mean forecast, so the median minus mean per site cannot be computed; the mean of actual minus median is in the bias section (+1.0 to +4.6 points of capacity in nine of ten months). No quantile-score contrast is paired with a mean-forecast contrast. Audit triggers: trigger 2 fired (arm A contradicted experiment 436's tail figures), and the explanation was tested here, which is the trigger's own condition: re-scoring arm A on all 44 runs and days 1 to 10 with numpy's default quantile gives a q95 exceedance of 7.9% (demand), 8.4% (wind), and 7.4% (solar), against 7.9%, 8.8%, and 7.6% in experiment 436, and 5.2%, 6.5%, and 5.7% under the weibull quantile. Experiment 436's "too narrow" finding therefore came largely from its quantile definition. Triggers 1 and 3 to 7 did not fire (no control, no nested arm, no sister-experiment interval, and no later design that depends on this result). No audit ran.

docs.title: Which 3, 5, or 10 of the 51 coherent member paths should NGED's power-flow studies use, with no label attached to any path?
docs.text:
We asked which 3, 5, or 10 of 51 forecast scenarios NGED should run by hand, and found that choosing 5 by rank on one measure beats choosing 5 at random but still misses the extremes. At 10 scenarios the mismatch fell below 10% of the range for every rule we tried; we did not test 6 to 9. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), the distribution network operator, will run a handful of power-flow studies by hand (calculations of how electricity flows through its network under one forecast scenario). We took the 51 equally likely forecast scenarios, called paths, that experiments 436 and 625 stored for each of 44 weekly runs. Each path is one joint forecast of demand, wind, and solar for 25 sites (16 Primary substations, 3 wind farms, 6 solar farms) over the next 10 days. We chose K = 3, 5, or 10 of the 51 paths in several ways. For each way, we measured how far the chosen paths' 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles sit from those of all 51, as a share of the range between the 5th and 95th percentile of all 51 (the gap). Part 2 repeats the choice for the summed demand of the three Primaries under each of two bulk supply points (BSPs). Part 1 and Part 2 reuse experiment 161's choice of covered Primaries.

Terms: K is the number of paths chosen. R random sample of K paths (1,000 draws per run); S-wind, S-solar, S-net, S-demand rank the 51 paths by one summary, cut them into K equal groups, and draw one path from each; C k-medoids clustering (each cluster is represented by its most central path), each medoid weighted by its cluster size; Oracle the best of 5,000 random K-subsets chosen on the gap itself, a floor that no rule can reach; gap the difference between a percentile of the chosen paths and the same percentile of the 51, divided by the spread (95th minus 5th percentile) of the 51; tail coverage the share of draws that include a path in the lowest or highest 10% (ranks 1 to 6, or 46 to 51) of the 51 on a summary. The summaries are the mean wind-farm output, the mean solar-farm output, the peak net demand (an unweighted proxy, in points of capacity), and the peak Primary demand, over days 1 to 10. Intervals are month-block bootstrap intervals over 10 months. Generators are anonymised.

Figure 1 shows the share of draws that include a path in the lowest or highest 10% of the 51, with 95% month-block intervals; higher is better.

Figure 2 shows the mean gap at the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles as a share of the range of the 51; the dashed line is 10%.

Figure 3 shows how much worse than all 51 paths each rule scores against the observed vector of all 25 sites; lower is better.

Figure 4 shows the share of observed days on which the daily peak export beat the largest chosen path; the dashed line is the gate (all 51 plus 5 points).

Figure 5 shows the rank correlation of the 51 paths between days 1 to 3 and days 4 to 10 within a run, for two ways of coupling the paths.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Verdict (K = 5, days 1 to 10, Schaake-shuffled paths, J3: each path takes the day-to-day pattern of a different past date for each lead). partly supported: all four stratified rules pass the tail condition and none passes the 10% coverage condition. The decision rule's 99% intervals for tail coverage minus R were +4.2 points (+3.7 to +4.8) for S-wind, +4.5 (+3.9 to +5.2) for S-solar, +4.2 (+3.7 to +4.7) for S-net, and +4.9 (+4.3 to +5.6) for S-demand, positive in 10 of 10 months each. C: +3.9 points (-3.2 to +11.9), positive in 5 of 10 months.
  • Absolute scores at K = 5 (mean of the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentile gaps; tail coverage). R 0.158 and 48.0%; S-wind 0.121 and 52.2%; S-solar 0.119 and 52.5%; S-net 0.123 and 52.2%; S-demand 0.116 and 52.9%; C 0.122 and 51.9%; Oracle 0.039 and 86.7%. The 5th, 50th, and 95th percentile gaps are in the table below. R's gap at the 95th percentile varies by 0.156 (mean per-run standard deviation across draws), so one random draw can be much better or worse.
  • K = 3 and K = 10. Mean gap at K = 3: R 0.226, S 0.174 to 0.185, C 0.182. At K = 10: R 0.098, S 0.072 to 0.077, C 0.085, so the mean gap of every rule is under 0.10 at K = 10. Per percentile, R is 0.101 at the 95th and C 0.123, so only the stratified rules (at most 0.083 at each percentile) pass the 10% coverage condition at K = 10. The plan predicted that K = 10 would narrow the gap without closing it; that prediction failed. Tail coverage at K = 10: R 75%, S 83% to 85%, C 78%; at K = 3: R 32%, S 34%, C 24%.
  • Each stratified rule matches best the summary it ranks. S-wind has a wind gap of 0.058 at the 50th percentile and 0.085 at the 95th; on the other summaries its gaps are 0.11 to 0.19, close to R. A stratified pick on one summary therefore helps little on the others.
  • Joint score (variogram, 25 nodes, relative to all 51; absolute 2.161). K = 5: R +16.4% (+14.7% to +18.4%), S +14.4% to +14.9%, C +14.9% (+11.4% to +18.9%), Oracle +15.1%. K = 10: R +7.2%, S +6.2% to +6.5%, C +7.5%. K = 3: R +28.6%, S +25.6% to +26.5%, C +22.4%. At K = 5 and K = 10 no rule differs from the others by more than about 2 points; at K = 3 the rules span 6 points (C +22.4%, R +28.6%). The loss comes mostly from using fewer paths.
  • Labels do not carry over. Within a run, the Spearman correlation between the 51 paths' ranks on days 1 to 3 and on days 4 to 10 is 0.19 for wind, 0.41 for net demand, 0.62 for solar, and 0.74 for Primary demand under the Schaake shuffle (J3), and 0.18, 0.01, 0.10, and 0.11 under ensemble copula coupling (J2). Prediction P4 (a path's wind rank correlates below 0.5 between lead bands) held for wind and failed for solar and demand under J3, because the Schaake shuffle gives each path one past date for every lead.
  • Coupling. J2 (ensemble copula coupling: each path follows one weather-forecast member) at K = 5 keeps S ahead of R (mean gap 0.146 to 0.149 against 0.167; tail coverage 50.5% to 50.9% against 48.0%), but C is worse than R (gap 0.195, tail coverage 51.1%), unlike under J3.
  • Selection inside each band (secondary): selecting inside the 12-to-36-hour or days 1 to 3 band instead of on days 1 to 10 improves that band's gap by about 0.01 to 0.016 for the stratified rules (the days 4 to 10 band has no gap for the run of 2026-06-30, so it is not compared). Within days 1 to 10 the two selections are the same.
Arm (K = 5) Gap at 5th percentile Gap at 50th Gap at 95th Tail coverage R 0.145 0.152 0.177 48.0% S-wind 0.119 0.105 0.139 52.2% S-solar 0.113 0.105 0.139 52.5% S-net 0.119 0.108 0.141 52.2% S-demand 0.114 0.099 0.133 52.9% C 0.086 0.104 0.173 51.9% Oracle 0.041 0.041 0.034 86.7%
  • Part 2: BSP group peak export (D13 and D17, K = 5 unless stated). The gate is the share of observed days on which the daily peak export exceeded the largest daily peak export among the chosen paths, over up to 9 full days per run (381 days in 43 runs). All 51 paths: 1.6%. K = 5: R 14.3%, S-bsp 12.1%, C 12.6%; all fail the gate (at most 1.6% + 5 points). K = 4: Q (paths at the 50th, 90th, 95th, and 99th percentile) 8.0% (the difference to All is +6.3 points, +2.1 to +11.8), against S-bsp 14.7% and R 17.4%. K = 10: S-bsp 6.3% (+4.7 points, +2.4 to +7.1) passes the gate; R 7.3% and C 7.0% fail by 0.7 and 0.4 points. The stratified pick on the BSP's own peak export has the lowest 50th percentile gap (0.045 at K = 5) and a 95th percentile gap of 0.114. Q hits the export tail on every run but its 5th percentile gap is 0.49 of the spread, by construction.
  • Tails. The summaries are forecasts of the stored marginals of experiments 425, 429, and 430; no new quantile scores are computed. The tail results above are the experiment's tail results.
  • Checks. No forecast was fitted, so the median-minus-mean check and audit triggers 3 to 6 do not apply. Audit trigger 1 (a control fails) did not fire. Audit trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction) fired: prediction P3, that C would have lower tail coverage than R, and the prediction that K = 10 would not close the gap both failed (P1 and P2 held, and the verdict partly supported was predicted). For P3, (C was not below R on tail coverage; C's interval is wide, +3.9 points, -3.2 to +11.9); the explanation, that medoids carry the cluster's weight but sit near the centre, was not tested. Audit trigger 7 (a later design depends on this result): none does. Part 1 scored all 44 runs; the last run, 2026-06-30, has an identical wind summary on all 51 paths in days 4 to 10 (spread zero), so its gaps for that band and summary are missing and the means use the other runs. Means in the table weight each month equally.
  • Caveats. Demand is the stored XGBoost demand of experiment 436, not the neural networks of the bake-off. The net-demand summary is an unweighted proxy in points of capacity. The BSP groups are 3 Primaries each (experiment 161's covered children) and omit unmetered load and Primaries that report apparent power; the groups are in MW from each Primary's capacity. Ten months give wide intervals; the gate for K = 10 passes by 0.3 points and should not be read as a safe margin. Forecast paths for valid times after 2026-07-01 are used in the selection of the last runs; only the observed values are held out. The gate takes an observed daily peak over at least 44 of 48 half-hours, which can miss a peak, and so understates the exceedance for all arms, All included. The 51 member values are those of experiments 425, 429, and 430; experiment 626 widens their tails and was not used. The day-to-day stability score was dropped, so prediction P5 (stratum persistence across weekly runs) was not tested.
  • Reused and new. Reused: experiment 436's work/runs and work/paths/J3 and J2, and the folder of experiment 625 (read only; nothing written to either). New: every selection rule, the summaries, the gap, tail, joint-score, and gate tables, and the figures. The folders of experiments 434, 436, and 377 are on PYTHONPATH for the series table and capacities.
  • Options for later. Test whether NGED's power-flow answer changes between K = 5 and K = 10 paths; repeat Part 2 with the neural-network demand exports and the topology of every BSP; and choose the paths on the gate itself with a rule that trades the median gap against the tail.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet plan review (12 findings: accepted a fourth demand summary, a bound for the coverage condition from an oracle floor, a within-run label check, absolute scores and R's spread beside each contrast, the corrected tail rank, 5 arms in the Bonferroni correction, one scale per node in the clustering; rejected a toy test of the reshape, since the vector is built member first, and a fractional-day variant). A Sonnet code review before the first run (the last run crashed the oracle on a zero spread, fixed; the k-medoids seed was made independent of the other arms; per-draw 5th and 95th percentiles were added). A Sonnet code review of the BSP script found the gate covered 14 days instead of days 1 to 10, fixed before the reported run. The write-up reviews are recorded in the pull request.

docs.title: Can NGED rebuild coherent scenarios from stored quantiles alone, and which tail rule should the client use?
docs.text:
Eleven stored quantiles are enough to rebuild the marginal forecasts and a Schaake-shuffle coupling. The tail rule hardly changes scores, but it changes how far the extreme draws reach.

Terms.

  • Client: NGED's own Python code, which reads stored forecasts from S3 and builds scenarios.
  • Scenario: one possible future path of power for every site and half-hour in a forecast run. A scenario set is coherent if the sites and half-hours within each path move together as they do in reality.
  • Stored forecast: 11 quantiles (0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99) per site and half-hour.
  • Dependence table: the information a client needs to couple the sites and half-hours. This is the fitted copula's 25 by 25 factor and 25 first-order autoregressive terms (the fitted copula), or 51 past observed paths (for the Schaake shuffle, which reorders independent draws into the rank order of past paths).
  • Tail rule: how the client extends the quantile function past q01 and q99. Clamp repeats the q01 and q99 values. Linear extrapolates the line through the outer two levels. Gaussian extends a normal distribution fitted to the outer two levels.
  • Primaries: 16 NGED primary substations. Their power is in MW or MVA. A BSP (bulk supply point) is the substation that feeds a group of Primaries.
  • CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) scores one site's marginal forecast. The variogram score scores how well a scenario set's coupling matches reality. Exceedance is the share of actuals above a quantile (or below it, for levels under 0.5).
  • Ensemble-rank component: the part of the pipeline's coupling that reuses the ranks of the weather ensemble's members.
  • J0, J3, J5: experiment 436's 51-path scenario sets with independent, Schaake-shuffled, and fitted-copula-plus-member-rank coupling. N is the in-pipeline reference for the marginals: J0 for CRPS, and the stored quantiles for exceedance. M is the mixture arm.
  • K1, K3: two neural networks of the bake-off, scored on the 16 Primaries. D3 is one Primary.
  • NGED is National Grid Electricity Distribution.

We asked whether NGED can draw scenarios as good as the ones our pipeline builds, if they hold only the stored forecast and a dependence table. We wrote a 70-line client helper that inverts the quantile function by linear interpolation, extends it past q01 and q99 by one of the three tail rules, and draws 1,000 scenarios per forecast run. We scored those against the 51 scenarios of experiment 436, as corrected by experiment 625, on 44 forecast runs for 16 Primaries, 3 wind farms, and 6 solar farms. We also scored a second set of forecasts from the bake-off's neural networks K1 and K3 for the 16 Primaries. The answer is yes for the marginal forecasts and for the Schaake shuffle, and no for one coupling: the fitted copula for solar farms.

Mixture parameters (arm M) are not available for demand and not stored for wind and solar. The Primaries in the 44-run set come from an XGBoost fit, whose output is a set of quantiles rather than a mixture. The wind and solar neural networks are mixture-density networks, but only their 11 quantiles were stored. The neural networks for demand have 3 mixture components, and the export stores only the mean of 5 seeds' quantiles. That mean is not any single mixture, and pooling the seeds would give 15 components. Recovering the parameters needs a rebuild of the inference of experiments 612 and 613, about a day of work, and was not done.

Look at how far each bar sits from 0.2%, the share a calibrated forecast would give. The Gaussian tail is nearest on the lower side. All three rules overshoot on the upper side, because the stored upper quantiles are too narrow. 44 runs; the three families are scored separately. The two panels have different horizontal scales, and the bars are point estimates with no intervals: the share from month to month varies by more than the sampling error.

Look at the purple fitted-copula dot for the solar farms: about 6.6% above the in-pipeline score. Every other dot is within 2% of zero. Zero means the client's 51 stratified paths score the same as experiment 436's 51 paths, over days 1 to 10. Lines are 98.33% month-block intervals; for the Schaake shuffle they are narrower than the dot. The panels have different horizontal scales.

Top panel: the Schaake shuffle's pick changes least between draw sets, but its 1,000 draws repeat 51 distinct paths, so the two sets are not independent information. The fitted copula changes by 0.1 MW. Bottom panel: the Schaake shuffle's pick sits furthest (0.6 MW) from the 51-path pick, and the fitted copula 0.36 MW. The tail rule barely changes either panel. The pick is the 95th percentile over scenarios of the Boston BSP's summed Primaries on day 3 (leads 48.5 to 72 hours), from neural network K1 at 82 origins; MVA Primaries are added as if MW. The Skegness BSP is computed and not drawn. No intervals are shown.

One Primary (D3), forecast from neural network K1. We drew the forecast run, out of the five development months' runs, with the most scored half-hours. Black is the reading, the blue line the median, and the blue bands the 50% and 90% ranges. The purple lines are four of the client's 1,000 copula scenarios with a Gaussian tail (one random draw, not an average). Look at how the scenarios scatter around the median.

The same forecast and scenarios over 10 days. Look at how the bands and the spread of the scenarios widen with lead time.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Marginal skill (CRPS, days 1 to 10, 44 runs, 98.33% month-block intervals). 1,000 client draws with a Gaussian tail against the 51 in-pipeline values: demand +0.09% (-0.07% to +0.28%), wind -0.06% (-0.28% to +0.16%), solar +0.02% (-0.12% to +0.19%). At 12 to 36 hours: demand +0.16%, wind +0.32% (-0.09% to +0.73%), solar +0.11% (-0.33% to +0.57%). Absolute scores in points of capacity: demand 5.02, wind 10.43, solar 8.57. At 51 stratified paths the client equals the pipeline exactly, because all 51 levels lie inside the stored q01 to q99.
  • Marginal skill by lead band (CRPS, 1,000 draws with a Gaussian tail against the 51 values). 0 to 12 h: demand +0.12%, wind -0.15%, solar +0.07%. 12 to 36 h: +0.16%, +0.32%, +0.11%. 36 to 120 h: +0.19%, +0.01%, +0.03%. 120 to 240 h: +0.01%, -0.12%, +0.00%. Every interval spans zero except demand at 36 to 120 h (+0.00% to +0.41%). The largest upper bound is +0.74% (wind, 12 to 36 h), so all 12 cells are within 1%.
  • Tail rule on CRPS. Gaussian against clamp, days 1 to 10: -0.01% in every family. The tail rule changes the extreme 0.2% of a distribution, which contributes almost nothing to CRPS.
  • Exceedance at q01, q05, q95, q99. The client's quantile function equals the stored knots at these levels, so the difference is 0.00 percentage points in every lead band and family. The in-pipeline 51 paths cannot resolve q01 and q99 and differ from the stored quantiles by up to 3.5 percentage points (J5, solar). Stored quantiles are off nominal too, and the J5 paths are often closer to nominal than the stored knots at q01, q05, and q95; only at q99 are the knots closer. The stored q99 holds 1.0% to 1.6% of actuals for the Primaries, 1.4% to 2.7% for wind farms, and 1.6% to 2.6% for solar farms. The stored q95 holds 3.7% to 6.1% for Primaries, 4.8% to 8.3% for wind, and 5.6% to 6.8% for solar. The knots are up to 3.3 points off nominal (wind q95).
  • Past the knots (share of actuals beyond the quantile; nominal 0.2% at the 0.2% and 99.8% levels). Below the 0.2% quantile: Primaries 0.53% (clamp), 0.44% (linear), 0.26% (Gaussian); wind 1.04%, 0.69%, 0.45%; solar 1.05%, 0.55%, 0.20%. Above the 99.8% quantile: Primaries 1.49%, 1.19%, 0.66%; wind 2.35%, 1.89%, 1.19%; solar 1.99%, 1.59%, 0.94%.
  • Sampling error at q99. The binomial standard error of the q99 exceedance is 0.02 to 0.07 percentage points, but the 10-month spread of the monthly rate has a standard deviation of 1.1 to 1.4 points (the half-hours of a month are strongly correlated), so a q99 exceedance should be read to the nearest point, not to the nearest tenth.
  • Coherence (variogram score at 51 stratified client paths against experiment 436's 51 paths, days 1 to 10). Independent draws against J0: demand -0.0%, wind -0.1%, solar +0.1%. Schaake shuffle against J3: +0.0% in demand and wind, and -0.0% in solar. Fitted copula (no ensemble-rank component) against J5: demand -0.0%, wind +1.9% (-0.7% to +4.5%), solar +6.6% (+2% to +14%). The J5 paths use the stored member ranks, and the copula does not, which is the likely cause of the solar gap; we did not run an ablation. Against independent client draws, the copula scores -0.7% for Primaries, -27.9% (-32.8% to -22.1%) for wind farms, and -39.1% (-43.5% to -34.4%) for solar farms. The Schaake shuffle scores +0.4% (-1.2% to +2.2%) for Primaries, -28.2% for wind farms, and -40.2% for solar farms.
  • Query picks, 44 runs, day 3 (points of capacity). The client's Schaake shuffle matches J3 on the variogram score but not on these picks (lowest wind 10.7 against 11.9; solar 318 against 358), so it does not reproduce the pipeline's shuffle path for path. Lowest-wind scenario: independent 27.8, fitted copula 11.4, Schaake shuffle 10.7, in-pipeline J5 15.1 and J3 11.9; the picks of two independent sets of 1,000 differ by 0.46 (independent), 1.9 (copula), and 0.07 (Schaake, which repeats 51 paths). Fifth percentile of summed solar output: independent 586, copula 442, Schaake 318, against J5 404 and J3 358, with set-to-set differences of 1.8, 7.7, and 4.2. A Gaussian tail makes the lowest-wind pick lower and less steady than clamping (copula: 11.4 against 12.0 points; set-to-set difference 1.9 against 1.4).
  • Query pick, neural networks (82 complete origins each), 95th percentile of each BSP's summed Primaries on day 3 (MW; MVA Primaries are added as if MW). Boston, K1: fitted copula 40.5 MW, Schaake shuffle 42.3 MW; two draw sets differ by 0.11 MW (copula) and 0.01 MW (Schaake); the pick sits 0.36 MW (copula) and 0.62 MW (Schaake) from the 51-path pick. K3 gives the same pattern (40.5 MW, 42.5 MW, 0.12 and 0.01, 0.38 and 0.68). The map from Primary to BSP is NGED's hierarchy file; all 16 Primaries sit under Boston or Skegness.
  • Neural networks, marginal skill (CRPS, % of capacity, 82 origins, 5 months). K1: 4.684 for 1,000 copula draws with a Gaussian tail against 4.692 for the 51 values (-0.16%, -0.45% to +0.26%). K3: 4.916 against 4.923 (-0.15%, -0.41% to +0.12%). The Schaake shuffle gives -0.20% and -0.21%. Stored q95 holds 7.6% to 8.1% of event-free actuals (K1) and 8.5% to 10.2% (K3); q99 holds 1.9% to 2.3% (K1) and 2.4% to 3.1% (K3). Past the knots, Gaussian: 0.21% (K1) and 0.16% (K3) below the 0.2% quantile; 0.59% and 0.82% above the 99.8% quantile.
  • Storage per forecast run. 11 quantiles for 25 sites and 702 half-hours: 772 kB as float32 (337 kB for the 16 Primaries over 479 half-hours). Fitted copula: 2.6 kB (a 25 by 25 factor and 25 autoregressive terms), refitted rarely. Schaake history: 3.6 MB for 51 paths per run, or one 3.1 MB compressed history of all sites shared by every run. Client code: 70 non-blank lines.
  • What 13 delivery levels would add. The 13 NGED delivery quantiles (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.98, 0.99) share only 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.50, 0.90, 0.95, and 0.99 with the 11 stored levels. They add 0.02 and 0.98 in the tails and 0.20, 0.35, 0.65, 0.80 in the body. This experiment cannot measure the effect: the networks would need to output the 13 levels, so the stored forecasts would be re-predicted. The tail rule would still apply past q01 and q99, and the extra 0.02 and 0.98 levels would make a linear tail rule (extrapolating from 0.01 and 0.02) shorter and steeper than now (from 0.01 and 0.05).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site: not computed. No forecast was fitted; the scenarios are rebuilt from stored quantiles, and the client draws equal the stored marginals by construction.
  • Error of the mean forecast beside each score contrast: not applicable, for the same reason.
  • Triggers. Trigger 2 fired once: the prediction that a Gaussian tail gives the steadiest picks (P3) failed. The Gaussian tail extends the tail further than clamping does, so the extreme picks move more between draw sets, and the Schaake shuffle looks steadiest only because its draws repeat 51 paths. That explanation is a hypothesis; the Schaake shuffle's steadiness follows from the repeated paths. No other trigger fired, so no audit ran.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Predictions. P1 (CRPS moves up to 2% between tail rules for wind and solar): refuted, the difference is under 0.02%. P2 (outer exceedance within 1 percentage point of nominal): refuted. The client equals the stored knots exactly, and the knots are off nominal by up to 3.3 points (wind q95; the neural K3 q95 reaches 10.2%).
