The second half of P2, that the 51 pipeline paths sit further from nominal, is mixed: J5 is often closer than the knots at q01, q05, and q95. P3: refuted (above). P4 (fitted copula within 3% of J5 for demand and wind, up to 10% worse for solar): supported (-0.0%, +1.9%, +6.6%).
  • Decision rule. Q11 sufficient: the best tail rule is within 1% of the in-pipeline arm on CRPS in every family and lead band, and equal to it on exceedance at the four outer levels. The stop rule (a client arm more than 2% worse than the in-pipeline arm) fired for the fitted copula on solar farms, +6.6%. The likely cause is that J5 also uses the stored member ranks, not the quantile form, so the quantile form was probably not at fault. We did not test that by ablation. No neural network was rebuilt.
  • Rows. The 44 runs are experiment 436's Tuesday runs of 2025-09 to 2026-06 (XGBoost demand from experiment 425, wind from experiment 429, solar from experiment 430). The neural-network set has 82 of the 153 origins of each network, because the 71 origins that lack some Primary's rows were skipped. Half-hours on or after 2026-07-01 were never scored. The July to October 2026 window was not opened. The solar clipping shares in data-processing.md come from e00628_clip_check.py.
  • Calibration of the stored quantiles. The Primaries' stored upper quantiles are too narrow (q99 exceedance 1.0% to 1.6% for XGBoost and 1.9% to 3.1% for the neural networks), consistent with experiment 626's finding for demand tails. Experiment 626 was still open when this was written. These results hold the scenarios to the stored marginals, so a client inherits that bias.
  • The copula has no tail dependence. The fitted Gaussian copula cannot put several Primaries or farms in the extreme tail together more often than its correlations imply. This experiment did not test joint extremes.
  • Day 3 means leads 48.5 to 72 hours. The BSP pick adds MW and MVA Primaries as if both were MW. Unlogged load shifts may lie in event-free rows (NGED's logs are incomplete), so the neural-network coverage figures are lower bounds on the harm.
  • Reuse. The scripts import experiments 87, 310, 347, 377, 429, 434, 436, and 625. Experiment 436's joint-block scoring is not used; experiment 625's corrected joint rows are.
  • Next. Ask NGED which of the three query types they will run. If they want the pipeline's J5 coupling for solar farms, store the member ranks. If they want tails beyond the 0.2% level, widen the stored upper quantiles before storage (experiment 626).

docs.title: Do coherent Primary scenarios, summed to a bulk supply point, give a trustworthy tail for the flow through that point, compared with a direct forecast of its own meter?
docs.text:
Summing coherent scenarios of the 16 Primaries did not give a usable tail for either bulk supply point (BSP), and the nodes the sum leaves out are the largest cause we found; the coupling cannot be judged until they are in the sum. At Boston BSP (D17), 70.9% of actual flows fell below the q05 of the Schaake-shuffled sum (J3), against 4.6% for the direct forecast of the BSP's own meter (the export side, where 5% is nominal; J0 is independent draws, J2 ensemble copula coupling, J5 a fitted Gaussian copula). At Skegness BSP (D13) the figures are 43.9% and 6.9%. The Primaries under a BSP do not include the metered wind farms, solar farms, battery, and other customers connected at BSP level. The meter minus the Primaries' observed sum averages -12.1 MW at Boston and -5.2 MW at Skegness, and -26.3 and -23.9 MW at summer midday. A constant correction for that gap, fitted on the other months, brought J3 only to 24.3% and 23.4%. The question could not be answered as registered, because neither BSP's meter reached the scaled export limit in any development month, so the threshold-weighted CRPS (twCRPS) at that limit is zero for every source.

In figure 3 the blue band is the sum of the Primaries, the green band the same sum plus the gap correction, and the orange band the direct forecast. In the summer run the meter dips to 30 MW of export at midday, The Primaries' sum, and its corrected form, do not follow this dip. The direct forecast does.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Row set. 153 daily runs at 09:00 UTC of 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06 (1 day of the 154 has no stored run), leads 0 to 240 hours, valid times before 2026-07-01 only. 182 valid days at Boston and 184 at Skegness. Demand is the stored K1 neural-network forecast, one of the three bake-off demand networks (K1, Candidate, K3; Candidate and K3 give the same picture, see Other networks); the 16 Primaries have 11 stored quantiles each.
  • Topology. The hierarchy file puts 9 of the 16 Primaries under Boston and 7 under Skegness. Two BSPs have a stored direct forecast (experiments 611, 619, and 622). The two grid supply points (GSPs) have direct forecasts too, but the Primaries are a small part of their flow (meter minus Primaries: +135.8 MW at Walpole, -39.6 MW at Bicker Fen), so GSP sums are not scored.
  • Missing nodes. Each BSP has other metered series beneath it (Boston: 1 wind farm, 4 PV, 1 battery, 1 biofuel, 1 other generator; Skegness: 2 wind farms, 3 PV) and unmetered load, losses, and MVA Primaries that carry no flow direction (8 of the 16 Primaries). None of these is in the sum. A post hoc regression of the Skegness gap on its wind and PV series (6,523 half-hours) gave R squared 0.94; Boston has only 317 half-hours with every series present, so its R squared (0.995) is not reliable.
  • Export q95 exceedance, days 1 to 10 (share of actual flows below the q05 of each source; 95% month-block interval in brackets). Boston: J0 79.0% [74.3, 83.6], J2 55.3% [50.8, 59.8], J3 70.9% [66.0, 75.7], J5 75.7% [71.2, 80.3], J3 plus gap correction 24.3% [20.0, 28.8], direct 4.6% [4.0, 5.1]. Skegness: J0 52.6% [41.7, 66.9], J2 33.9% [21.4, 48.6], J3 43.9% [30.7, 58.7], J5 43.8% [31.1, 58.0], J3 plus gap correction 23.4% [9.2, 39.2], direct 6.9% [2.2, 12.7]. The binomial standard error at 5% with 182 days is 1.6 points (two standard errors: 3.2 points). Every lead band gives the same ranking (see the report file).
  • Import q95 exceedance. Boston: J3 0.3%, J0 0.9%, direct 7.3% [5.4, 8.8]. Skegness: J3 4.3%, J5 5.8%, J0 11.9%, direct 11.8% [2.2, 26.8]. The sums' import tail is too low at Boston because the sum sits about 12 MW above the meter.
  • Bias (actual minus the median of the sum, MW). Boston J3: -11.6 over all rows, -26.3 at summer midday, -11.5 at winter evening; with gap correction +0.5, -8.3, +0.6; direct -0.1, +0.5, +0.4. Skegness J3: -4.7, -23.3, -0.5; with gap correction +0.6, -12.2, +3.4; direct +0.7, -0.2, +0.1.
  • CRPS (MW, all rows). Boston: J0 10.8, J2 9.6, J3 10.4, J5 10.6, direct 3.8. Skegness: J0 5.4, J2 5.0, J3 5.1, J5 5.2, direct 3.1.
  • Scaled limit. Zero half-hours of either meter exceeded 0.9 times the pre-2025-10 maximum export (35.2 MW Boston, 18.0 MW Skegness) in the development months; 20 Skegness half-hours exceeded the import limit (63.3 MW). The twCRPS at the scaled export limit is therefore zero for every source, and the registered twCRPS test cannot rank anything.
  • Post hoc limit (labelled). Using the 2nd percentile of the meter in the scored rows as the export limit (12.3 MW at Boston, 0.2 MW at Skegness), twCRPS is identical for J0, J2, J3, and J5 (0.115 MW at Boston, 0.129 MW at Skegness), because no scenario sum reaches the limit. The direct forecast scores 17.7% lower at Boston (interval -18.8% to -7.8%) and 16.9% lower at Skegness (interval -24.1% to +66.4%).
  • Decision rule. sum usable: no, at either BSP, as is or gap-corrected (no coupled set was within two binomial errors of 5%, and the twCRPS condition is not evaluable at the scaled limit). direct needed: not evaluable at the scaled limit; at the post hoc limit it holds at Boston (upper end -7.8%, below -5%) and not at Skegness. Verdict not supported.
  • Other networks. Candidate and K3 give the same picture: export q95 exceedance of J3 is 68.5% and 68.9% at Boston, 41.7% and 41.5% at Skegness, and the direct forecast is 4.6% and 7.1%.
  • Registered predictions. P1 held (every as-is sum failed by a wide margin and the direct forecast won on bias). P2 failed: after the gap correction J3 and J5 were 18 to 21 points above 5% (22.9% to 26.3%) at both BSPs, and ECC (J2) was below J0, not above. P3 cannot be judged (identical twCRPS). P4 cannot be judged at the scaled limit; at the post hoc limit the direct forecast's gain is clear at Boston (-17.7%) and not at Skegness (interval -24.1% to +66.4%).
  • Coupling. The sums' ranking follows the sums' spread, not their calibration: ECC (J2) has the widest sums and the lowest exceedance (55.3% at Boston), J0 the narrowest and the highest. The ranking of couplings says nothing about which coupling is correct, because every as-is sum is biased by 4.7 to 11.6 MW over all rows (up to 26 MW at summer midday).

docs.title: Reviews and caveats
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first scored run and found that the copula had been fitted on July 2026 observations (valid times of the June runs) and on observations from the test month. Both defects were fixed (the fit now masks valid times from 2026-07-01 and in the test month), and the sums were rebuilt. Further findings accepted: score every source on one common row set, and take the gap correction only from other valid months. Not applied: the nominal binomial error treats valid days as independent, which understates the interval; the intervals from five origin months are coarse. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline numbers; the reviewer's findings are in the pull-request body.
  • Caveats. Five origin months only, one summer month (2026-06). The gap correction (constant by half-hour of the day, fitted on the other four months) is post hoc and is not in the registered rule. Demand is K1 (a neural network that uses lagged power) with no tail widening; experiment 626 found that the stored forecasts' q90 was exceeded too often, a bias that could add to the sums' shortfall. Experiment 436's stored scenario sets (XGBoost demand models, 44 Tuesday runs, metered wind and solar included) were not re-scored here, so whether a sum that includes the generators is usable remains untested. J5 uses no ensemble mixing (weight 0). J3 for 2025-10 draws its dates from 2025-03 to 2025-09 only. The Primaries are cleaned half-hours, flagged rows dropped.
  • What to try next. Re-score experiment 436's stored sets as BSP sums with the metered generators included, on every daily run, and compare with the direct forecast; or sum the Primaries plus a direct forecast of the generators' total beneath each BSP.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per site: not applicable (no mean forecast stored). Audit triggers: none fired (no control with a sister-experiment interval, no nested arm, and the result contradicts no earlier experiment's number).

docs.title: Is the upper demand tail of the three stored neural-network forecasts too low on ordinary days, and would a bias correction fitted on earlier months remove the excess out of sample?
docs.text:
The stored demand forecasts put too little weight on high demand on ordinary days, not only around load-shifts, and a correction fitted on the first three months removed only part of the excess on the last two. A load-shift is NGED moving a block of demand from one primary substation to a neighbour for a while. We asked whether readings above the forecast 90th percentile (q90, which should be exceeded by 10% of readings) and the 95th percentile (q95, 5%) come mainly from days near a load-shift, or from a bias present on every day. We re-scored the stored forecasts of three neural networks (K1, the class-2 Candidate, and K3) for 16 primary substations over five test months (October, December 2025, January, March, and June 2026), with no refit. We split the half-hours by whether a load-shift was labelled or verified at that substation within 7 days, and by month, forecast lead time, hour, substation, and temperature. We then fitted two corrections on the first three months and scored them on the last two. Experiment 626 found a similar pattern in the stored demand forecasts of experiments 434 and 436: widening the tails did not fix the q90, which pointed to a median that sits too low. The registered decision rule gives bias on ordinary days, and the correction fails its correction usable test. The decision rule defines no verdict word, so partly supported is our judgement: the bias exists, and the first correction tried does not remove it.

  • Arms and rows. Three stored neural networks, no refit: K1, the Candidate (class 2, band widened by the per-month factor of experiment 613, set on the months it is scored on), and K3, from backtest_export_roster_2026-11-07/. Rows: every half-hour with a cleaned observed power (observed_power non-null) at lead under 240 hours, 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06 only; 1,140,221 rows per neural network, 153 origin days. The July to October 2026 window was not opened. Pooled results include D15 and D18, the two Primaries the export reports only (their history is short); excluding them, the Candidate's event-free q90 exceedance is 11.3% (eight MVA Primaries) and 14.6% (six MW Primaries), against 17.0% for those two. The eight MVA Primaries report apparent power (MVA); the six MW Primaries report real power (MW), which can be negative.
  • Event-free and event rows. Event-free rows are the export's event_free rows (905,502 per network); event rows are the other 234,719. NGED's logs may miss events, so event-free rows can hold unlogged load-shifts, and every event count is a lower bound.
  • Pooled exceedance, all five months, 95% interval from resampling origin days (nominal: q90 10%, q95 5%, below q10 10%, below q05 5%):
Network and rows Above q90 Above q95 Below q10 Below q05 K1, event-free 14.7% (14.1, 15.3) 8.4% (8.0, 8.9) 9.3% (8.7, 9.8) 4.6% (4.2, 4.9) K1, event 18.8% (17.9, 19.8) 12.8% (11.9, 13.7) 13.3% (12.3, 14.4) 8.3% (7.3, 9.3) Candidate, event-free 13.2% (12.6, 13.8) 7.2% (6.8, 7.7) 7.7% (7.2, 8.2) 3.4% (3.2, 3.7) Candidate, event 17.2% (16.3, 18.1) 11.4% (10.5, 12.4) 11.6% (10.7, 12.7) 7.0% (6.1, 8.0) K3, event-free 17.0% (16.0, 18.0) 10.0% (9.3, 10.7) 9.0% (8.4, 9.6) 4.4% (4.1, 4.8) K3, event 17.7% (16.7, 18.7) 12.5% (11.6, 13.4) 13.6% (12.6, 14.7) 8.2% (7.2, 9.2)
  • Decision rule. The Candidate's pooled event-free q90 exceedance is 13.2%, outside 8% to 12%, and the event rows are 4.0 points higher (rule: at least 5), so event-driven fails. The event-free exceedance by month is 12.4%, 13.1%, 12.4%, 17.6%, and 9.3% (2025-10 to 2026-06): above 12% in 4 of 5 months, so bias on ordinary days holds. The December 2025 event rows reach 27.9% (the verified D5 and D16 transfer), so event days add to the excess, but ordinary days carry most of it.
  • Where the excess sits. Candidate, event-free rows. By lead band: 11.9% (0 to 24 hours), 12.5% (24 to 72), 13.0% (72 to 120), 13.8% (120 to 240). By hour of valid time in 4-hour UTC blocks: 16.9% for 00:00 to 04:00 and 11.3% to 11.4% for 08:00 to 16:00. By ensemble-temperature third: 15.5% (cold), 14.2% (middle), 9.9% (warm). Cold nights (18:00 to 06:00 UTC, cold third): 16.4% against 12.4% for all other hours, and K3's are 21.6% against 16.0%. By Primary: 7.3% (D8) to 21.1% (D15); 9 of 16 Primaries have an interval entirely above 10%, 3 entirely below (D3, D8, and D12), and 4 straddle it. K1's lower tail (below q05 4.6%, below q10 9.3%) is close to nominal, and the Candidate's is below nominal (3.4% and 7.7%), so its band is wider than needed below the median.
  • Size of the bias. The mean of observed power minus the median forecast on event-free rows is +0.098 MW for K1, +0.102 MW for the Candidate, and +0.109 MW for K3. As a share of capacity it is −0.3% to 2.0% across Primaries, apart from D15 at 16%. A share of median demand is not reported because D15's median demand is −0.45 MW (signed power).
  • Correction test, Candidate, event-free rows of 2026-03 and 2026-06 (fitted per Primary and lead band on event-free rows of the first three months; S adds the median of observed power minus the median forecast to every quantile above the median; R rescales the distance above the median so that the training q90 exceedance is 10%; 95% interval from resampling origin days):
Arm Above q90 Above q95 CRPS (MW or MVA) CRPS vs uncorrected Uncorrected 13.9% (13.1, 14.7) 8.0% (7.4, 8.6) 0.2785 1.000 S, shift 12.6% (11.9, 13.4) 7.2% (6.7, 7.9) 0.2812 1.0095 (1.0083, 1.0106) R, rescale 11.7% (11.0, 12.4) 6.5% (6.0, 7.1) 0.2809 1.0087 (1.0057, 1.0114)

CRPS here is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantiles, in MW or MVA. Neither arm brings q90 or q95 inside an interval around nominal, so correction usable fails. K1 and K3 behave the same way: R lowers K1's event-free q90 from 15.5% to 12.2% and K3's from 17.0% to 12.7%, with CRPS up 0.9% and 0.4%. The fitted shift is a median of 0.02 to 0.07 MW and the fitted factor a median of 1.05 to 1.15 (Candidate); both vary widely by Primary (factor 1.0 to 1.55). The training q90 exceedance before correction averaged 12.2% to 13.4% across the Candidate's four lead bands, which is what R pulls down to 10% on the training rows.

  • Why the correction falls short. The uncorrected Candidate's q90 exceedance is 17.6% in March and 9.3% in June on event-free rows, against 12.4% to 13.1% in the fitting months, so the bias is seasonal. By group (post hoc slice): the eight MVA Primaries went from 13.1% to 11.0% above q90 and from 7.0% to 5.5% above q95 under R, both intervals containing nominal (the q90 interval at its lower edge), with CRPS +0.49% (−0.01%, +0.95%); the six MW Primaries went from 9.9% to 7.1% above q90, already near nominal before correction in these two months, and CRPS rose 2.2% to 3.6%. June CRPS rose 1.8% to 2.3% under either correction.
  • Tails and cost. Only the q05, q10, q90, and q95 levels are scored here (the stored export holds q01 and q99 too, but this question concerns the upper tail). Curtailment cost is not scored: the experiment re-scores 16 Primaries' demand forecasts, which have no generators to curtail.
  • Caveats. The 95% intervals resample origin days independently, but adjacent days share weather and valid times, so the intervals are somewhat too narrow. Five months are too few to separate a seasonal bias from a trend. The Candidate's band-width factors were set on the months scored. The temperature third (taken per Primary over its own rows) comes from the ensemble-mean 2 m temperature of the latest run that started at or before each valid time, at the Primary's H3 cell (a near-analysis proxy, not a quantity known when the forecast is made); it only labels rows. The unlogged-event caveat applies to every event-free number.
  • Example forecast. Figure 5 shows the first Candidate run issued on 13 January 2026 at Primary D2, chosen as an arbitrary winter example and not for a large miss. The observed power stays inside the q05 to q95 band for most of the run.
  • Pre-registered predictions. P1 held (4 of 5 months above 12%; event rows 4.0 points higher). P2 held for cold nights and failed for lead: exceedance rises with lead, 11.9% to 13.8%. P3 failed: S left q90 above nominal (12.6%, interval excludes 10%). P4 failed: R left q95 above nominal (6.5%, interval excludes 5%) as well as q90. P5 held at the point estimate (+0.95% and +0.87%) and both intervals straddle 1%.
  • Reviews. One fresh Sonnet code review ran after the first scored run, not before it (done late). It found no leakage; it found that the temperature description in the plan was wrong (fixed), that the joined row order needed an assertion (added, numbers unchanged), and that a share of median demand is meaningless at D15 (replaced by a share of capacity). A second Sonnet review of the results and write-up found overstatements in the size of the correction, the Primary count, and a shift-versus-rescale mix-up in the advice (all fixed), and prose and figure faults (fixed).
  • Checks. The export holds no mean forecast, so the median-minus-mean check does not apply; the corrections leave q50 unchanged, so the error of the median forecast is the same in every arm, and trigger 3 cannot fire. Trigger 2 did not fire: although P3 and P4 failed, the explanation (the bias differs by month and metering group) was tested in the by-month and by-group slices above. Trigger 4 is covered by the by-group correction slice, which shows the verdict is not driven by D15 and D18. Triggers 1, 5, 6, and 7 do not apply (no control, no nested arm, no sister experiment on these rows, nothing yet depends on the result). No audit ran.
  • What to try next. Fit the upper-tail correction by metering group and season, or let the forecast's median depend on temperature at cold nights; test on July to October 2026 only in the final test.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00630-roster-upper-demand-tail-calibration-event-days-and-bias-correction/ (e00630_prep.py, e00630_score.py, e00630_correct.py, e00630_report.py, e00630_figures.py); tables in the experiment's private data folder; reuses no earlier experiment's code.

docs.title: Once the metered wind and solar farms beneath a bulk supply point are added to the sum of its Primaries, does a coherent scenario sum give a usable tail for the flow through that point?
docs.text:
Adding the nine metered wind and solar farms to the sum of Primaries fixes most of the export-side miss that experiment 629 found, but no sum put both tails near 5% at both bulk supply points (BSPs), and the direct forecast of each BSP's own meter came closest. For the Schaake-shuffled sum (J3) at Skegness, the share of actual flows below the sum's q05 fell from 41.7% (Primaries only) to 4.3% (with the farms) and 3.0% (with a time-of-day remainder). At Boston it fell from 72.8% to 26.2% and 10.6%. The import side moved the other way: the share above the q95 rose from 4.4% to 32.6% at Skegness and from 0.1% to 14.3% at Boston. The direct forecast gave 4.9% and 7.2% below the q05 and 6.7% and 9.9% above the q95. With the farms in, coupling helps: J3 and the fitted copula (J5) beat independent draws (J0) on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) by 2.6% to 7.7%, with intervals wholly below zero. The registered rule gives direct needed. Two BSPs are thin evidence.

The missing nodes explain most of the export-side miss of experiment 629 and none of the import-side miss. Experiment 629 asked whether the Primaries alone were enough; with the farms in, the export tail is close to nominal at Skegness and still twice nominal at Boston, and the import tail is too narrow at both BSPs. The scaled export limit was never reached, so the threshold-weighted CRPS (twCRPS) cannot rank the sums on the export side.

In the example figures the purple band is the 90% band of J3 with farms and the time-of-day remainder, the orange band is the direct forecast, and the black line is the meter. The summer run shows midday export dips that both forecasts follow. The runs are issued on 2 December 2025 and 10 June 2026.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
• Arms. Primaries (the primary substations) from the stored K1 neural network (the lag network of the bake-off roster) (51 values per node and half-hour from the 11 quantiles); metered farms from experiment 615's stored backtests (wind: physics plant with the mixture-density head; solar: quarterly-refitted neural network), converted to MW by each farm's scoring capacity. BSP flow = Primaries minus farm output plus a remainder. Couplings: J0, J3, J5 with and without the farms; J2 (ensemble copula coupling) without the farms only. Remainders: none, constant, and by half-hour of the day, each the mean of the observed meter minus the observed Primaries (and farms) over all history from 2025-03-01 to 16 days before the test month.
  • Topology (anonymised). Boston: 9 Primaries and 4 farms with a stored forecast (1 wind, 3 solar). Skegness: 7 Primaries and 5 farms (2 wind, 3 solar). Of the 10 wind and photovoltaic series beneath the two BSPs, one photovoltaic farm at Boston has no stored forecast (too little history). Boston also has other metered generation that is neither wind nor solar, and both BSPs have unmetered load; none of these is in the sums, and all sit in the remainder (the constant or time-of-day mean gap added to the sum).
  • Row set. 153 daily runs of the five development months; valid times before 2026-07-01; leads 0 to 240 hours. The farms' stored forecasts omit half-hours with a missing reading or in the idle band, so the common row set holds 62,526 half-hours at Boston (of 69,606) and 58,235 at Skegness (of 71,277), on 181 and 180 valid days. Experiment 629's Primaries-only result reproduces on the full row set (Boston J3 export 70.8% against 70.9% there).
  • Observed gap (meter minus Primaries, MW). Boston -12.2 and Skegness -5.0; with the farms subtracted, -4.6 and +1.6. Mean farm output was 7.6 and 6.6 MW.
  • Share of actuals below the q05 (export) and above the q95 (import), 0 to 240 hours; nominal 5%; 95% month-block interval for the sums in the figures. Boston, export / import: J0 with farms and time-of-day remainder 11.6% / 18.6%; J3 10.6% [8.2, 13.3] / 14.3% [12.2, 15.5]; J5 10.0% / 15.6%; J3 with farms and no remainder 26.2% / 1.5%; J3 with a constant remainder 10.2% / 19.6%; direct 4.9% [4.2, 5.6] / 6.7% [5.0, 8.1]. Skegness: J0 6.1% / 48.7%; J3 3.0% [0.9, 6.5] / 32.6% [18.8, 44.0]; J5 3.1% / 34.4%; J3 with farms and no remainder 4.3% / 23.9%; direct 7.2% [2.5, 13.5] / 9.9% [2.2, 23.9]. Two binomial standard errors are 3.2 points.
  • Lead bands. The shares change little with lead (bands 0 to 12, 12 to 36, 36 to 120, and 120 to 240 hours); J3 with farms and remainder at Boston is 11.5%, 10.1%, 10.0%, and 11.0% below the q05.
  • CRPS (MW, mean of the five monthly means; common rows). Boston: J0 4.22, J3 4.11, J5 4.11, direct 3.77 (with farms and time-of-day remainder). Skegness: J0 3.83, J3 3.53, J5 3.56, direct 2.87. Without a remainder the sums with farms score better at Skegness (J3 3.16) and worse at Boston (J3 4.93). Primaries only: Boston J3 10.78 (none) and 6.03 (time of day); Skegness 5.03 and 5.47.
  • CRPS contrasts against J0 (same variant and remainder). With farms and time-of-day remainder: Boston J3 -2.6% [-4.1, -1.0], J5 -2.7% [-3.6, -1.6]; Skegness J3 -7.7% [-8.6, -6.9], J5 -6.9% [-7.9, -6.2]. Without farms, with the time-of-day remainder: J2 -12.8% (Boston) and -10.5% (Skegness), J3 -5.0% and -6.3%, J5 -2.4% and -5.1%. Direct against J3 with farms and remainder: Boston -8.3% [-11.0, -5.5]; Skegness -18.6% [-39.6, +1.8].
  • Scaled limit and twCRPS. Zero half-hours of either meter exceeded the scaled export limit (0.9 times the largest export before 2025-10-01: 35.2 MW Boston, 18.0 MW Skegness). With the 90th percentile of positive exports as the limit (19.4 and 11.4 MW, post hoc), the export twCRPS is 0.028 MW at Boston and 0.003 MW at Skegness for every sum, because no scenario sum reaches the limit; the direct forecast scores 0.026 at Boston. Import twCRPS at the 90th percentile of positive imports: Boston J3 0.235, direct 0.217; Skegness J3 0.232, direct 0.192 (-17.1% [-27.1, +1.1]).
  • Bias (actual minus median, MW; all rows / summer midday / winter evening). Boston J3 with farms and time-of-day remainder +0.5 / -2.5 / +0.4; without farms and without a remainder -11.9 / -27.1 / -11.7; direct -0.4 / +0.1 / +0.4. Skegness J3 with farms and remainder +3.3 / +0.9 / +4.5; without farms -4.1 / -25.3 / -0.5; direct +0.1 / -2.9 / +0.1. The farms remove most of the summer-midday bias. The Skegness sum with the remainder sits too low in winter evenings by 4.5 MW, which fits the sum's import-side miss; the cause was not separated.
  • Decision rule. sum usable: no, with either fitted remainder. J3 and J5 beat J0 on CRPS with an interval wholly below zero at both BSPs, and the Skegness export side is within two binomial errors of 5%; the Boston export side (9.6% to 10.6%) and the import side at both BSPs are not. direct needed: yes. Verdict not supported.
  • Registered predictions. P1 half held: with the farms and no remainder the export exceedance fell under 30% at both BSPs, but it fell to 4.3% at Skegness, below the predicted 10%. P2 half held: it held on the export side only (Skegness 3.0% to 3.1%, Boston 10.0% to 10.6%) and failed on the import side. P3 failed: coupling beat independent draws by 2.6% to 7.7%, not under 2%. P4 held on three of the four tails and failed on the Skegness export tail, where several sums (J0 5.8% to 6.1%, J3 3.0% to 4.3%) are as close to 5% as the direct forecast (7.2%, interval 2.5% to 13.5%). The Skegness intervals of the direct forecast are wide enough to include 5%, so the claim that direct is safer rests mainly on Boston.

docs.title: Reviews and caveats
docs.text:
• Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first scored run. Accepted: the cleaned solar power is missing at 27% to 43% of night half-hours, which dropped them from the with-farms remainder and from the Schaake pool; the observed grid takes zero for a missing night reading, as the forecast side does. Not applied: the meter used for the remainder (scan_power) and the meter scored (the stored 622 observed_power) were not compared. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the headline shares and row counts and matched them to 0.002; its CRPS figures matched on the row-weighted mean and differ from this page's figures, which average five monthly means (Skegness J3 3.59 row-weighted against 3.53). The write-up review is in the pull-request body.
  • Departures from the plan. Row set B (the Tuesday runs of experiment 436's stored 25-node scenario sets, with J2 and the farms) was not run, so J2 with farms is missing; the plan's wording that the daily runs hold no member weather at the farms is why. The remainder is fitted on all history from 2025-03-01, not only the earlier development months, and the J5 copula is fitted leaving out the test month and the 15 days before it, as in experiment 629 (the copula can use later months). Both twCRPS limits (the 90th percentile of positive exports and of positive imports) are post hoc, and the constant remainder was added to the registered two.
  • Caveats. Five origin months, two BSPs, one summer month. The farms' stored forecasts omit idle-wind and missing-reading half-hours (10% to 18% of the Primaries' half-hours), so scores with farms hold for the windier half-hours. Demand is K1 with no tail widening; experiment 626 found its q90 exceeded too often. NGED's event labels are incomplete, and no load-shift analysis was run. Candidate and K3 demand neural networks were not re-run.
  • Checks. Median minus mean forecast per site: not applicable (no mean forecast stored). Audit triggers: none fired (no control with a sister-experiment interval, no nested arm, and the Primaries-only arm reproduces experiment 629).
  • What to try next. Find why the import side is too narrow with the remainder (the Skegness winter-evening bias of +4.5 MW points to the Primary forecasts or the remainder), by fitting the remainder on the forecast error and not on the observed gap; build J2 with the farms from member weather at the farms; add a direct forecast of the farms' total as a node.

docs.title: Does a network with two gated recurrent units and three self-attention layers, pre-trained on ERA5 and CAMS weather, forecast Primary demand better than the existing pre-trained networks?
docs.text:
Seq did not beat the existing lag network on ERA5 and CAMS weather, so stage 3 does not run. Nothing here is adopted for production. Every number is a ceiling for a live forecast, because ERA5 arrives about 5 days late.

Terms. Seq is the sequence neural network of this experiment. ERA5 is ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather, and CAMS is the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service irradiance product; both are estimates of past weather. P2-pre is the pre-training of arm P2 of the lag neural network of experiment 574, from which K1, K2, and the Candidate start. K3-pre is the lag-free pre-training of experiment 565. The monthly offset is the slow monthly output offset of experiment 565, and B1 is the set of 14 trailing-temperature and solar-gain columns of experiment 569 that the weather encoder of P2 reads. A sequence is one Primary and one forecast origin (09:00 UTC); a pass is one sweep over a random 20% or all of the training sequences. The eight MVA Primaries are rated in megavolt-amperes and the six MW Primaries in megawatts; the short-history Primaries D15 and D18 are report-only. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, MAE the mean absolute error, and GRU a gated recurrent unit. K1, K2, and the Candidate are the lag neural network arrangements of experiment 612.

docs.title: Question and stages
docs.text: The question is whether a neural network that reads the last 6 days of power uses that history better than the two power lags the existing neural networks read. Stage 1 pre-trains Seq for all 16 Primaries on ERA5 and CAMS weather with an 8-number Primary embedding. Stage 2 scores Seq beside P2-pre, P2-hist6, and K3-pre on ERA5 and CAMS weather only, and is this experiment's headline. Stage 3 (fine-tuning on ensemble weather, comparison with K1, the Candidate, and K3) is a separate later experiment.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Tokens. 336 history tokens (7 days to the origin) and 336 future tokens (leads 0.5 to 168 h), half-hourly, width 64. The peak GPU memory of a fit was 2.3 GB at batch 256 with fused attention, and a fit took 5 to 12 minutes.
  • Inputs per token. The weather encoder reads the 7 weather columns and the 14 B1 columns at the token's own time (the 2 CAMS previous-day columns take the origin's value). The datetime encoder reads the 21 datetime columns. Every token adds a position embedding (steps from the origin) and a segment embedding (history or future). A history token also has a lag encoder reading power as a share of capacity, a missing flag, the age in days, the token's weather and datetime embeddings, and the Primary embedding. Future tokens take a learnt "no lag" vector in that slot.
  • No lookahead. A token carries power only if its half-hour is at least 24 h before the origin, the same cap the lag neural networks use (lags observed at least 24 h before the origin). The 48 newest history tokens carry power 0 and missing flag 1, as do flagged tokens. The loss sits on future tokens only.
  • Recurrence and attention. The encoder GRU reads the history embeddings. The decoder GRU reads the future embeddings and starts from a linear map (tanh) of two encoder states at fixed positions: the last one and the one at origin minus 24 h. Three joint self-attention layers (4 heads, feed-forward width 256, no causal mask, because every input is known at the origin) follow. Seq has about 250,000 parameters against about 30,000 for P2.
  • Output. A three-component Gaussian mixture per future token, trained with the negative log-likelihood of experiment 397 and read out as 11 quantiles. The monthly offset is added to the component means with the module of P2 (monthly knots from 2019-09, a penalty on first differences, flat extrapolation after the newest knot). Knots start at zero and are fitted on training targets only; a test-month origin reads the newest knot.

docs.title: Training
docs.text:
• Sequences and cut-offs. Daily 09:00 UTC origins from 2019-09 to the fold's refit, with ERA5 and CAMS pseudo-weather, cleaned power only. Every target at or after the refit minus 3.5 h is set to missing, so a late origin contributes only its early targets. Validation is the held-out weeks of experiment 422's rotation (7 days in every 42, with a purge around each), so training reaches the refit and the newest offset knot sees targets, as it did for P2-pre and K3-pre.
  • Standardisation. Seq uses the fold's stored statistics that P2-pre used (the standardiser and target mean and standard deviation of e00428_data.build_fold, and B1's stats/B1/<month>.npz), asserted equal to a recomputation within 1e-6.
  • Fit. AdamW, learning rate 5e-4, 300 warm-up steps, cosine decay, weight decay 1e-2, dropout 0.1, gradient clip 1.0, batch 256, patience 8 passes, at most 60 passes; block dropout as in the lag neural networks (all power masked on about 25% of sequences, the newest 24 h of power on about 5%). Seq starts fresh, as P2-pre and P2-hist6 did, so no arm has extra epochs.
  • Seeds and folds. Seeds 0, 1, and 2 on 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06, monthly refits. P2-pre, K3-pre, and P2-hist6 are scored at seeds 0, 1, and 2. The ablations, the synthetic-shift arm, and the 3-week arm have seed 0 only, so they are compared with Seq's seed 0 as well.
  • July 2026. The dense grid ends at 2026-07-01. Origins in 2026-06 are kept only if their 168 h window ends before 2026-07-01 (origins through 23 June), for every arm, so all arms are scored on identical keys.
  • Saved models. Each fitted state dict goes to data/ml-experiments/00632-*/models/, outside git.

docs.title: Comparison (stage 2)
docs.text:
• Arms. Seq; P2-pre and K3-pre from stored weights through the pre-training head (inference only), on ERA5 test rows built like experiment 574's pre-training rows at the test-month origins; P2-hist6, a per-row control trained here with the P2 recipe whose lag encoder reads up to 6 daily lags 24 h or older, mean-pooled; and a month-by-half-hour climatology row (e00632_climatology.py: the quantiles of cleaned power at the same calendar month and half-hour over all history before the refit).
  • Row set. 09:00 UTC origins, leads 0.5 to 168 h, valid times before 2026-07-01, event-free rows of the backtest export, cleaned observed power as the target; a join assertion checks that every arm's (Primary, origin, valid time) keys are identical before any score is read.
  • Interval. Each resample draws one seed and five month blocks with replacement (the bootstrap_month_totals routine of the studies package), and the interval is taken at the Bonferroni level. With five month blocks it is wide, and it also holds seed-to-seed variation, so it can extend beyond the range of the month-block means of the seed-mean contrast.
  • Scores. CRPS by forecast day and pooled over days 2 to 7 (24 to 168 h); mean absolute error (MAE) of the median; q05-q95 coverage; share above q90; the share of readings beyond q01, q05, q95, and q99; winter nights; the injected bank. Half-hours flagged by cleaning and so missing from the training targets are 300,537 to 301,110 per fold (the 16 Primaries together, from 2019-09).
  • Anonymisation. Demand Primaries only, so not applicable. No leaderboard post.

docs.title: Run order and compute
docs.text:
1. Score P2-pre and K3-pre from stored weights.
  2. Fit Seq seed 0 on 2025-12 and 2026-06 and apply the stop rule (passed: Seq is better than K3-pre at days 1 and 2 in both groups, and not worse than P2-pre by 0.10 in both groups).
  3. Fit Seq on all five folds at seeds 0, 1, and 2; one seed on all five folds for each of the three ablations: no attention (GRUs only), no recurrence (attention only), and neighbour inputs (mean power of the electrical neighbours and the share with a reading, same 24 h cap, 50% dropout).

  4. Further arms: P2-hist6 (3 seeds), Seq trained on synthetic load-shifts (seed 0), the injected-bank read-out of experiment 581 for Seq, P2-pre, and K3-pre, and a Seq with 3 weeks of history (seed 0).

  5. Compute. The fits took 5.8 process-hours for the planned work (Seq 2.5, ablations 2.4, synthetic-shift arm 0.4, P2-hist6 about 0.5) against the ceiling of 6, and 1.0 for the 3-week arm against its own 3-hour allowance. Fits ran two or three at a time on one GPU, so the wall clock was shorter than the process hours.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Seq is not shown better than P2-pre, and P2-hist6 is the lowest arm at the eight MVA Primaries. The table gives CRPS pooled over 24 to 168 h in points of capacity (smaller is better), with the MAE of the median in brackets. Seq, P2-pre, P2-hist6, and K3-pre are scored on the mean of their seeds 0, 1, and 2 forecasts; the ablations have seed 0, so the last two columns give seed 0 for every arm they compare with.

docs.title: Load-shift ride-through
docs.text:
Seq follows an injected load-shift more than P2-pre does, and training on synthetic shifts brings its follow below P2-pre's. The bank is experiment 581's: 24 passes in which every Primary meets every combination of a shift of 15%, 30%, or 50% of capacity lasting 3, 7, or 15 days, added to the cleaned power that the forecast reads and never to the target. "Follow" is the mean over forecasts of the movement of the median forecast divided by the shift, against the same weights' forecast from unshifted history, for forecasts 24 to 120 h ahead. "Safe side" is the share of unshifted readings on the safe side of the band (the nominal value is 0.95). The shifts hit every Primary at once, so the neighbour summaries Seq reads are shifted as well. A shift that hits one Primary alone may be followed less, because the neighbour summaries would then stay clean.

Arm Eight MVA: follow, day 4 to end safe side Six MW: follow safe side Eight MVA: follow, 0-7 d after Six MW: follow K3-pre (no lags) 0 0.932 0 0.887 0 0 P2-pre 0.270 0.752 0.214 0.738 0.108 0.087 Seq (3 seeds) 0.397 0.577 0.282 0.685 0.217 0.163 Seq, seed 0 0.412 0.576 0.294 0.667 0.241 0.170 Seq trained on synthetic shifts, seed 0 0.152 0.818 0.055 0.841 0.090 0.029
  • K3-pre reads no power, so its follow is zero by construction. Its safe side is the event-free value.
  • Seeds do not change the finding. The three-seed mean of Seq follows 0.40 and its seed 0 follows 0.41, so the synthetic-shift arm (one seed) is compared with Seq's seed 0.
  • The synthetic-shift arm adds lag-only shifts to 5% of each Primary's history in training, on random days, with depths and lengths of the bank and a random sign (experiment 581's recipe, the history power and the neighbour summaries shifted, the targets unshifted). It cuts the follow at the eight MVA Primaries from 0.41 to 0.15 and lifts the safe side from 0.58 to 0.82, better than P2-pre on both.
  • The synthetic-shift arm raises CRPS. Its CRPS is 3.13 and 2.29 at seed 0, against 3.00 and 2.17 for Seq at seed 0 (+0.13 and +0.12), and its q05-q95 coverage falls to 0.857 and 0.839. One seed was run, so the size of the increase is uncertain.

docs.title: Longer history
docs.text: Three weeks of history made Seq no better. A Seq with 1,008 history tokens (half-hourly, no token reduction; 4.5 GB of GPU memory, 12 minutes per fit) scored 3.010 and 2.248 at seed 0, against 3.001 and 2.171 for the one-week Seq. It follows an injected shift about as much (0.30 at the eight MVA Primaries from day 4 of the event). The extra arm requested for the week one year earlier was not run, because the rule agreed in advance was to skip it unless three weeks helped.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Leakage. Every batch passed the row-by-row check that no own-power or neighbour value is newer than origin minus 24 h and that the newest 48 history tokens carry zero power and a missing flag. The first training batch and every test window passed a per-sample comparison against a poisoned copy of the arrays, and the negative control (a lag cap of 0 or 24 steps) raised as intended.
  • Join. Every arm covers the same (Primary, origin, valid time) keys; the scorer raises if a join is not one to one or drops a row.
  • Median against mean. The mean signed error of the median at days 2 to 7 is -0.63 (Seq), -0.53 (P2-pre), and -0.72 (P2-hist6) points of capacity at the eight MVA Primaries. All three arms under-forecast on average.
  • Error of the median beside CRPS. The MAE of the median ranks the arms as CRPS does at both groups.
  • Audit triggers. None fired: no arm used a test-period value in training, and the scorer's row set is the same for every arm.

docs.title: Not run
docs.text:
• Stage 3, fine-tuning on ensemble weather, because the prediction failed.
  • The year-earlier week as extra history tokens, because three weeks of history did not help.
  • Three seeds of the ablations, the synthetic-shift arm, and the 3-week arm.
  • The injected-bank read-out for P2-hist6.

The comparator and bank code import the folders of experiments 397, 418, 422, 560, 565, 574, 581, 591, and 610.

docs.title: How does BG2 score on the held-out months July to October 2026 beside the three demand networks at the 16 Primaries, and how does the lag-enabled network score at the bulk and grid supply points?
Result
docs.text:
BG2 is an XGBoost forecast of the kind production runs; K1, the candidate, and K3 are the three neural-network demand forecasts of experiment 620, and K3 reads no power lags.

BG2 scores the lowest CRPS of six systems on all rows, but the event-free and follow-penalised readings narrow its lead, and BG2 reads fresher power lags than the networks.

  • All rows: BG2-single-fit has CRPS 4.23 points of capacity against K1's 4.94, a lead of 0.71 points (Bonferroni interval -0.82 to -0.59).
  • Event-free rows: after experiment 637's flagged days are removed, BG2 has 3.91 against K1's 4.29, a lead of 0.38 points (-0.49 to -0.26).
  • Follow penalty: at Primary D18, BG2's median follows 0.56 of the load-shift against 0.33 for the lag-free K3. Following a load-shift is the wrong behaviour for a normal-running-arrangement forecast.
  • Lag asymmetry: BG2's power lags come from 3.5 hours before the forecast origin and K1's and the candidate's from at least 24 hours before (K3 uses none), so a BG2 win over the networks is not like-for-like.
  • Lead time: BG2's lead over K1 is largest on day 1 (0.78 points) and stays at 0.68 to 0.73 points from day 2 to day 10.
  • Bulk and grid supply points: the lag-enabled network ties BG2 at days 1 to 3 and beats the manual heuristic.

docs.title: Part 1: BG2 beside the three demand networks at the 16 Primaries
docs.text:
BG2-single-fit scored lower CRPS than all three networks on the held-out months, but it saw fresher power lags, so the margin is not a like-for-like win. BG2-single-fit is experiment 87's weekly XGBoost member, fitted once on data before 2026-07-01, forecasting each of the 51 ensemble members and pooling them into 11 quantiles with the 1.15 spread factor. It is scored on the same 929,870 half-hourly rows, 16 Primaries, and 123 forecast origins (2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31) as the three networks of experiment 620. Every figure is in percent of capacity, scored once, with no row dropped.

Two caveats limit the comparison.

  • BG2's power lags come from the newest reading at least 3.5 hours before the forecast origin. The networks use lags at least 24 hours old. BG2 therefore holds an information advantage, and a BG2 win over the networks is not like-for-like on lags.
  • The weekly-refit arm, "BG2-weekly", was pre-agreed as optional and was skipped. Refitting 20 boosters (one per Primary and per supply-point series) on each of 17 weeks was estimated at 3.7 hours or more of fitting on a shared GPU, over the 3-hour cap. BG2-single-fit is the like-for-like comparator (one fit at the training cutoff, as for the networks); the production cadence is not shown.

BG2-single-fit omits the monthly, analogue, pooled, and stacked members and the solar offset of the full five-member BG2. It also takes all power from the cleaned grid and drops D15 and D18 before 2025-03-01.

BG2 has the lowest MAE on every forecast day. K1, the candidate, and the manual heuristic lie close together, and their lines overlap from about day 4.

BG2 has the lowest CRPS on every forecast day. K1, the candidate, and the manual heuristic lie within 0.3 points of each other, and the climatology is far above all of them.

docs.title: Part 1b: BG2 on event-free rows and the follow penalty
docs.text: BG2 keeps the lowest CRPS after the days that experiment 637's detector flags are removed, but on the flagged days at Primary D18 BG2's median follows the load-shift more than any other system's median. NGED want a forecast of the normal running arrangement (NRA, the load pattern without the load-shift), so a forecast that follows a load-shift (a transfer of load between Primaries) is the wrong behaviour. BG2 is scored here on the rows that the detector as experiment 637 fixed it, in experiment 637 does not flag, and then measured on the rows it does flag. Nothing was refitted: all forecasts are the stored ones scored in Part 1.

docs.title: Event-free scoring
docs.text:
The detector is experiment 637's, unchanged. The rule file ara_rule.json has SHA-256 e5fb5cc08a67327d74dbc93ee51ba4e31dfc25bb25d8d4fab426bb32762b0566, the hash that page states (the committed copy matches it apart from a trailing newline). At the operating point (threshold k = 3.5, runs of at least 2 days) the detector flags 56,699 of 929,870 rows (6.1%) and 119 Primary-days, the counts that page reports, so the detector was reproduced. Of the 119 Primary-days, 102 are at D18, 8 at D21, 5 at D14, and 2 each at D8 and D10.

BG2's CRPS falls from 4.23 to 3.91 points of capacity on event-free rows, and BG2 stays the lowest of the six systems. The other systems fall by more, so BG2's margin over the networks narrows. Intervals are day-block bootstrap 95% intervals over forecast origin days, as in Part 1.

On all rows BG2 minus K1 is -0.71 (-0.82 to -0.59 here; the Part 1 table's interval is wider because its Bonferroni count is 42 rather than 8), so removing the flagged days nearly halves BG2's CRPS lead over K1. docs.title: Follow penalty on the flagged rows
docs.text:
Only D18 gives a usable measurement. At D18 the observed power on the flagged days is on average 27.9 points of capacity (7.6 robust standard deviations of the detector's daily residual) above the estimated normal level. The other flagged Primaries do not give a usable measurement: D14's observed power is only 2.5 points of capacity (0.8 robust standard deviations) away from its estimated normal level, and D8, D10, and D21 are flagged on 12 days between them. The follow ratios there are in follow_penalty.csv but are not interpretable, because the transfer is smaller than the drift of the estimate.

The normal level is an estimate, and every table and figure here says so. The estimated normal level of a Primary is its median power in the 28 days before its first flagged day, taken separately for each half-hour of the day and for weekdays and weekends. For D18 the first flagged day is 2026-07-06, and the estimate is 43.6% of capacity on average. The estimate is the same for every system, so a system's follow ratio is the mean over flagged rows of (its median minus the estimated normal level) divided by the mean observed shift. The definitions follow experiments 586 and 613, with the estimated normal level in place of the true normal level and the observed shift in place of the injected depth. Safe-side share is the share of flagged rows on which the estimated normal level lies at or above the system's q05 when the shift raises the load (at or below q95 when it lowers it). NRA-side coverage is the share of flagged rows on which the estimated normal level lies inside the system's q05-q95 interval.

System Follow ratio Follow ratio minus K3's NRA-side coverage Safe-side share BG2 0.56 (0.51 to 0.60) +0.22 (+0.21 to +0.23) 0.27 (0.23 to 0.31) 0.27 (0.23 to 0.31) K1 0.35 (0.30 to 0.40) +0.02 (+0.01 to +0.02) 0.62 (0.55 to 0.68) 0.62 (0.55 to 0.68) Candidate 0.31 (0.26 to 0.36) -0.02 (-0.03 to -0.02) 0.61 (0.54 to 0.68) 0.61 (0.54 to 0.68) K3 (lag-free control) 0.33 (0.29 to 0.38) 0 0.54 (0.48 to 0.61) 0.55 (0.48 to 0.62) Manual heuristic 0.40 (0.33 to 0.47) +0.07 (+0.04 to +0.09) 0.70 (0.64 to 0.76) 0.70 (0.64 to 0.76) Climatology (control) 0.34 (0.33 to 0.35) +0.01 (-0.04 to +0.06) 0.87 (0.85 to 0.89) 0.87 (0.85 to 0.89)

Rows at D18 on flagged days from day 7 after the first flagged day (45,853 rows, 121 forecast origin days). Intervals are day-block bootstrap 95% intervals; the minus-K3 column is paired by row. Follow ratio: 0 means the median ignores the transfer, 1 means the median follows all of it.

BG2 follows about 22 percentage points more of the transfer than the lag-free K3 does, which is about 6 points of capacity. K3 reads no lagged power and the climatology reads none either, yet both show a follow ratio of 0.33 to 0.34. That 0.33 to 0.34 is most likely the gap between the estimate and these systems' own level forecasts, which comes from the season and the weather between the 28 baseline days and the window, not from lags. Subtracting K3's ratio isolates how much of the transfer each system follows through its lags: BG2 +0.22, the manual heuristic +0.07, K1 +0.02, and the candidate -0.02. Following is the wrong behaviour for an NRA forecast, so BG2's follow ratio is higher and its estimated-normal-level coverage lower: BG2's q05-q95 interval contains the estimated normal level on 0.27 of the flagged rows, against 0.54 to 0.70 for K1, the candidate, K3, and the manual heuristic, and 0.87 for the climatology.

The follow starts about a week into the transfer, which is when the 7-day power lag first contains it. In days 0 to 6 after D18's first flagged day, every system except the climatology has a follow ratio within 0.07 of zero (BG2 +0.03) and a safe-side share of at least 0.89. From day 7 BG2's ratio jumps to 0.56 and its safe-side share falls to 0.27. BG2 also holds an information advantage on lags: its power lags come from the newest reading at least 3.5 hours before the forecast origin, whereas the networks use lags at least 24 hours old (Part 1). Part of BG2's follow is therefore a consequence of its fresher lags, and the comparison with the networks is not like-for-like.

The result holds at two other settings. At lead times of 24 to 120 hours only, BG2's ratio is 0.58 and exceeds K3's by 0.25 (0.23 to 0.26). With the estimate corrected for drift (adding the daily median change of the other Primaries' power since the 28-day baseline, excluding Primaries flagged that day), D18's mean shift falls to 25.1 points of capacity, BG2's ratio is 0.50, K3's is 0.26, and BG2 exceeds K3 by 0.25 (0.23 to 0.26). The drift correction is a second, rougher estimate and is labelled as such in follow_penalty.csv; it does not bring K3's and the climatology's ratios to zero.

docs.title: Injected-shift follow ratio on development months
docs.text: None of experiments 87, 586, and 613 stored a BG2 forecast on an injected shift, so the development-month follow ratio and safe-side share of BG2 were not computed. Experiment 87 stored BG2 forecasts for 2025-07-02 to 2026-06-30 on the row set fold_a_daily_gap_v1, but those forecasts used the real power lags. Experiments 586 and 613 ran their injected-shift banks through the networks only, and no experiment folder holds BG2 forecasts made with shifted lag inputs. Computing the injected follow ratio for BG2 would need BG2 to forecast again on the shifted lags, which is a new run rather than a re-score, so it was not done.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The labels are incomplete. NGED's event labels are incomplete, and the detector misses transfers of about 1 MW or less and transfers shorter than 2 days, so unflagged rows may still contain a transfer.
  • One Primary carries the follow measurement. D18 is the only flagged Primary with a transfer large enough to measure.
  • The normal level is an estimate. A gap of about a third of the transfer, most likely from the season and the weather, sits in every system's follow ratio, so the comparison between systems (the minus-K3 column) is firmer than any single ratio.
  • Descriptive only. Nothing here is adopted or tuned, and the window was read once already in Part 1 and in experiment 637.

Code: ml-experiments/00633-bakeoff-final-test-bg2-and-lag-enabled-bsp-gsp- network/e00633_events.py. CSV outputs: data/ml-experiments/00633-*/events/ (event_free_scores.csv, event_free_contrasts.csv, event_free_wins.csv, event_free_by_primary.csv, follow_penalty.csv, nra_estimates.csv, d18_daily.csv, census.csv).

docs.title: Part 2: the lag-enabled network at the bulk and grid supply points
docs.text:
At the 2 bulk and 2 grid supply points the lag-enabled network ties BG2 and beats the manual heuristic and the climatology. The network is experiment 622's arm lagged_b1 (the D5 offset, power lags at least 24 hours old, and the thermal-lag columns), fitted once on data before 2026-07-01 with seeds 0 and 1 as in that experiment, pooled per group of 2 series. All 4 series (D13, D17, D1, and D6) have readings in the window (5,893 to 5,904 half-hours each), so all 4 are scored, on 233,844 rows common to the four systems. BG2 here is BG2-single-fit's stored forecasts for the same four series. The bulk supply points are D13 and D17, and the grid supply points are D1 and D6.

Slice Days Lag-enabled network BG2 Manual heuristic Climatology All 4 series 1 to 3 7.45 7.51 9.83 15.12 All 4 series 4 to 10 8.88 8.82 10.23 14.98 2 bulk supply points 1 to 3 5.03 5.00 6.63 11.68 2 bulk supply points 4 to 10 6.01 5.83 6.68 11.47 2 grid supply points 1 to 3 9.88 10.02 13.03 18.55 2 grid supply points 4 to 10 11.75 11.80 13.77 18.49

Mean CRPS in points of capacity. Bonferroni count 60.

The network and BG2 are indistinguishable at days 1 to 3 in both groups. The network minus BG2 is +0.03 points (Bonferroni interval -0.16 to +0.21) at the bulk supply points and -0.14 (-0.78 to +0.54) at the grid supply points. At days 4 to 10 the bulk-supply-point difference is +0.18 (-0.002 to +0.35) and the grid-supply-point difference is -0.04 (-0.49 to +0.46). The Bonferroni count is 60. Both groups beat the manual heuristic with intervals that exclude zero, for example by 1.60 points (-1.98 to -1.18) at the bulk supply points and 3.16 (-4.52 to -1.74) at the grid supply points at days 1 to 3.

The series split in two. At D13 (days 1 to 3: 3.98 against 4.27) and D6 (7.76 against 8.84) the network scores lower CRPS than BG2, and at D17 (6.08 against 5.74) and D1 (12.00 against 11.19) BG2 scores lower.

Predictions (Part 2). P3 predicted that the network beats BG2 by about 0.1 CRPS points at the bulk supply points at days 1 to 3 and ties it at the grid supply points. The bulk-supply-point result is +0.03, so the predicted gain did not appear, and the grid-supply-point tie holds. BG2's 3.5-hour power lags are fresher than the network's 24-hour lags, so a tie means the network matches a forecast that holds an information advantage. This experiment refitted neither forecaster in the window, so both rows are single-fit.

The predict-phase standardiser statistics differ slightly from the training-phase ones. The predict phase builds its standardiser and target statistics from a raw matrix that holds about 22 more rows per series (valid 2026-06-30 09:30 to 20:30, all before the cutoff), so the statistics differ from the ones the weights were trained with by about 1e-5 relative. This is not leakage. The check on the development months reproduced experiment 622's stored 2026-06 forecast exactly on the extended inputs (maximum difference 0.0 in all 8 files), which does not cover this case.

docs.title: Common limits
docs.text:
• One window, scored once per candidate set. Nothing was tuned on it.
  • The development-month ranking was not rechecked. The hypothesis that the ranking of BG2 against the networks equals its development-month ranking was not tested.
  • The freeze hashes of the code files predate a comment-only edit. After both windows were scored, the docstrings of the code files were re-wrapped and lint headers adjusted to pass the documentation lint. No executable line changed, so freeze_part1.json and freeze_part2.json record the code as it ran, and their code hashes no longer match the committed files.

docs.title: A step in solar capacity, and recovery in energy, for the donor-day PV probe
docs.text: We asked whether a probe of a neural network can follow a step in solar capacity, and whether the probe's 0.68 recovery of an injected real solar farm is mostly an effect of the units. The probe takes a neural network that is given no past power readings as input (a lag-free network, from experiments 554 and 621) and measures how much its demand forecast falls when the sky clears. We added the half-hourly output of a real solar farm, scaled to 2 MW or 4 MW, to the demand that the network was trained to predict at six MW Primary substations. We then checked how much of that added capacity the probe found again, which we call the recovery (probed capacity divided by injected capacity, in megawatts or in megawatt-hours). In energy the probe recovers 0.78 to 0.88 of a real farm, against 0.68 in megawatts, so part of the shortfall comes from measuring in megawatts. A step is an addition that starts on 1 April 2025 or on 1 July 2025 and continues to the end of the training data. The probe found a step starting in April at 0.32 to 0.51 of its size, found a placebo step with a shuffled shape at about half of that, and found a step starting in July at 0.0 to 0.1. The probe's estimate tracks the weather of the step's months as well as the step. Verdict: not supported.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
• Recovery: the probed capacity of a network trained with the injection, minus that of the network trained without it (same cutoff, seed, and Primary), divided by the injected capacity.
  • Donor rows: for each probe date and half-hour, the training rows within 21 days of the same day of the year at the same half-hour. The probe regresses the network's forecast on the PV output that the clear-sky irradiance of the donor rows implies.
  • Cutoff: the last date of the training data of one set of networks. The four cutoffs are 2025-07, 2025-10, 2026-03, and 2026-06.
  • Calibrated: the recovery divided by the leave-one-farm-out factor, which is the median recovery of the constant-injection networks of the same cutoff whose injected farm differs from the farm injected at that Primary.
  • Plain network and monotone network: experiment 554's unconstrained network, and experiment 623's variant constrained so that net demand cannot rise with shortwave irradiance. Part 2 uses the plain network only.
  • Placebo step: a step of the same size and calendar whose shape is the farm's monthly mean output with the within-month anomaly shuffled. The page's results show it keeps some sky link.
  • Energy ratio: the sum of the farm's output over the sum of the physics unit PV curve, on one set of rows. Part 1 uses three sets: the probe cells, the donor rows, and all daylight rows.
  • Spread across Primaries (or farms): the standard deviation of the per-Primary (or per-farm) median recoveries divided by their mean.
  • Step bar: for each of the four steps (spring or summer, 2 MW or 4 MW), the median calibrated recovery over seeds is at least 0.7 at 4 of the 6 Primaries at 2025-10.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
All four step bars fail, the placebo bar fails, and the noise-floor bar and the coverage bar of the constant injection pass.

Bar (fixed before any step-world recovery was read) Result Calibrated step at 2025-10 at least 0.70 at 4 of 6 Primaries, each of the four steps Fail for all four: spring 0.32 (2 MW) and 0.38 (4 MW); summer 0.01 and 0.02 Shuffled-shape step under 0.3 MW at every cutoff Fail for the spring placebo (95th percentile over seeds up to 2.06 MW at one Primary; the median Primary's 95th percentile 0.55 to 1.33 MW) and for the summer placebo at 2025-10 (median 0.23, maximum 0.39 MW) and 2026-03 (median 0.33, maximum 0.64 MW) Seed noise floor, 95th percentile under 0.3 MW Pass: 0.244 MW over 72 differences (median 0.094 MW) Widened interval covers the constant-injection truth in at least 60% Pass: 0.66 (0.64 to 0.69 by cutoff) Same interval covers the full step / the calendar-blind share 0.01 / 0.25 Lag to 0.7 within 9 months Stop rule fired: no cutoff reaches 0.7, so only season-year values are reportable Energy-based recovery of a 4 MW real farm in 0.80 to 1.00 (median over Primaries) Mixed: 0.78 on donor rows (fail), 0.80 on probe cells and 0.88 on all rows (pass) Energy-based spread across Primaries narrower than the megawatt spread Fail: see "Energy-based recovery"
  • The spring step is read at far more than its share of training rows. Only 19% of the donor rows (23% at 2026-06) are dated after 1 April 2025, but the calibrated recovery is 0.32 to 0.51. The summer step is read below its share at 2025-10 and 2026-03 (0.09 of donor rows against 0.01 to 0.02 and -0.02 to -0.01 read) and near it at 2026-06 (0.14 against 0.08 to 0.12).
  • The recovery of the spring step does not grow steadily with time. The 4 MW step is recovered at 0.45, 0.38, 0.33, and 0.51 at the four cutoffs. The fall from 2025-07 to 2025-10 holds at all six Primaries (mean 0.08). The audit traced it to the donor mix: the ordinary July to September 2025 donors dilute the sunny April to June 2025 ones.
  • The constant injection calibrates to 1. The leave-one-farm-out factor is 0.671, 0.689, 0.680, and 0.685 at the four cutoffs, and the calibrated constant injection is recovered at 0.95 to 1.04 at every Primary and cutoff.
  • The summer-step networks at 2025-07 read zero to within 6.5e-7 MW, because they train on rows identical to the control's. This is a determinism check and the only pre-step check of a real-farm step that this experiment runs, because the spring step starts before the earliest cutoff.
  • Primary D9 is the highest. The 4 MW spring step reaches 0.82 at 2025-07 at D9 and 0.60 to 0.67 at the other cutoffs; the other five Primaries stay below 0.55.

docs.title: Why a placebo step is read as capacity
docs.text:
A step whose donor rows fall mostly in a sunny period is learned as a response to sunshine. The clearness (the ratio of measured to clear-sky shortwave irradiance) over the six MW Primaries was 0.76 in April to June 2025. It was 0.61 in April to June 2024 and 0.65 to 0.69 in 2020 to 2023, and 0.61 in July to September of both 2024 and 2025. A demand step that exists only in the sunny months is correlated with sky clearness in the training rows, and the probe reads that correlation. In the audit's regressions of the injected megawatts on the unit PV curve over the probe's own cells, sky clearness explains the summer step completely, the spring step by 55% to 65%, and the placebo by 10% to 30%. The calendar-blind share (0.19 to 0.23 of the donor rows) and the weather coincidence overlap and do not add.

  • The shuffled-shape placebo probably keeps a month-level sky link. The placebo keeps the monthly mean of the farm's actual output and shuffles only the anomaly within the month, so a sunny April carries a large injection. The placebo's recoveries are therefore an upper bound on spurious capacity.
  • Moving the probe dates one year earlier changes the spring step's recovery by at most 0.02 at three cutoffs. With probe dates 364 days earlier (before either step) the 4 MW spring step is recovered at 0.37, 0.31, and 0.48 at 2025-10, 2026-03, and 2026-06, against 0.38, 0.32, and 0.49 with the 2025 dates. At 2025-07, where only 6 dates exist, it is 0.33 against 0.43. The network shows no sign of using a calendar or holiday signature to switch the step on. This probe was run after the audit asked for it and is post hoc.

docs.title: Energy-based recovery of a real farm
docs.text:
In energy, the probe recovers a real farm at 0.78 (plain network) to 0.81 (monotone network) over the probe's donor rows. The same recovery is 0.81 and 0.85 over the probe cells and 0.88 and 0.92 over all daylight rows, against 0.68 and 0.72 in megawatts. The figures pool the cutoffs 2026-03 and 2026-06 and the 2 MW and 4 MW injections of experiments 621, 623, and 624. The energy ratio of the farms to the physics curve is 0.72 to 0.84 over all rows, the figure that experiment 624's audit found, and 0.76 to 0.95 over the probe cells.

  • Energy-based recovery is not more stable. The spread across Primaries is 0.023 in megawatts and 0.029 (donor rows), 0.039 (probe cells), and 0.032 (all rows) in energy. Across farms it is 0.017 in megawatts and 0.027 (donor rows), 0.061 (probe cells), and 0.035 (all rows) in energy.
  • The energy figure depends on the rows summed over. The donor-row figure is the closest to the regression's own rows and is the lowest of the three, so the range 0.78 to 0.88 is the honest statement.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text:
• The plan assumed the pretraining rows start in April 2024. They go back to 2019 or 2020, so only about 19% of donor rows follow a step on 1 April 2025, not about 50%. The predicted share (0.5 for the spring step, 0.2 for the summer step) was wrong, and the full-step bar was out of reach from the start.
  • The widened interval is too narrow. The leave-one-farm-out factor's own spread (0.001 to 0.009) is smaller than the spread of recoveries across farms (0.017 in megawatts and up to 0.061 in energy), so constant-injection coverage is 0.66, not the nominal 0.80. The bar passes.
  • The scope is narrow. Two step months, one rotation of the real-farm shape (farms A, B, C, F, A, B at the six Primaries), the plain network, and six MW Primaries. The calibration is in-sample at each cutoff, with the injected farm left out.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, per site: not applicable, because the experiment scores no forecast.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside every quantile-score contrast: not applicable, for the same reason.
  • Triggers that fired: a placebo failed its bar, and the result contradicted its own prediction (the spring step was recovered at 0.32 to 0.51 against a predicted share of 0.5 at most). The audit was a fresh agent that re-derived the headline numbers from the stored probe outputs. Triage:
    • The step bar, the placebo, and the non-monotone ordering reproduced (accepted).
    • The sunny-spring explanation holds in direction and not fully in size (stated above with the 55% to 65% figure).
    • The placebo's monthly profile and the wrong 2024 start of the rows (accepted, stated above).
    • The understated spread of the factor (accepted, stated above).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Part 1 (e00634_energy.py) re-scores the stored recoveries of experiments 621, 623, and 624 as recovery_energy = recovery_MW x sum(u) / sum(farm).
  • Part 2 (e00634_fit.py, e00634_probe.py, e00634_analyse.py, e00634_report.py) copies experiment 621's scripts and adds the step conditions. The scripts import experiments 397, 405, 409, 428, 448, 510, 554, 621, and 623 and edit none of them. The 108 fits took about 0.7 GPU-hours of fitting. Farm gaps dropped 15.4% to 15.9% of the six Primaries' rows from every arm.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The probe measures a capacity that holds across the training window, so the open question is whether the capacity can be read per season-year by training one network per window. A cleaner test of the step reading would inject steps in an ordinary spring and a sunny summer, with a placebo built from a multi-year climatological profile, to separate the weather coincidence from the probe's date-blindness.

docs.title: Plan, as written before the results
docs.text:
Standing practices followed. Cleaned data, development months only, the six MW Primaries, and anonymised farms (Solar A to F, by letter). Not followed: no forecast is scored, so there is no tail-calibration, curtailment, or example-forecast reporting. Earlier advice followed: report a calibrated figure beside the raw one, widen intervals by the leave-one-farm-out spread of the factor, and drop the cloud template from the headline (experiments 623 and 624).

Part 1: energy-based recovery (CPU, no fitting; reported before any fit). For each stored recovery in experiments 621, 623, and 624, recovery_energy = recovery_MW x sum(u) / sum(farm). Here u is the physics unit curve of the Primary's own CAMS and ERA5 weather and farm is the farm's normalised series, each summed over the probe cells (12 dates, half-hour ends from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC, cells where the farm has no gap). The injected energy is the injected megawatts times sum(farm). The energy the probe implies is the probed capacity times sum(u). Report per Primary, per farm, and per cutoff, beside the megawatt figure, for the plain network (621, 623, and 624) and the monotone network (623). The same ratio over all of the six Primaries' pretraining rows is reported as a cross-check of experiment 624's audit (0.72 to 0.84). The physics-curve world is the control: its energy ratio is 1 by construction.

Part 2: capacity-step world. Four injected conditions, each added to the target of the six MW Primaries from the first day of a step month, using the real-farm shape of experiment 621's rotation 0 (farm A, B, C, F, A, B): step_spring_mw2 and step_spring_mw4 from 2025-04-01, and step_summer_mw2 and step_summer_mw4 from 2025-07-01. Two placebo conditions use the same calendar and energy with the sky link removed (the shuffled shape of experiment 621): shufstep_spring_mw4 and shufstep_summer_mw4. A control condition has no injection. Every condition shares one row mask, as in experiment 621. The network, rows, loss, early stopping, and seeds (0, 1, 2) are experiment 554's pretrain through experiment 621's fit; the probe is experiment 621's probe. Cutoffs: 2025-07, 2025-10 (the first summer cutoff after both steps), 2026-03, and 2026-06. Two constant-injection controls, farm_mw4_r0 and farm_mw4_r1 (4 MW of the real-farm shape on every row, as in experiment 621), also run at every cutoff. They give a calibration factor on the same rows and cells as the step networks, with every farm injected at two Primaries so that the leave-one-farm-out factor can be built, and they show whether the network reads a full size or a share. That is 9 conditions x 3 seeds x 4 cutoffs = 108 fits, about 1.3 GPU-hours.

Probe cells and the pre-step check. The probe needs the base row of each probe date. At 2025-07 only the 6 dates from 2025-04-09 to 2025-06-18 have rows; at the other three cutoffs all 12 do. The summer-step networks at 2025-07 train on rows identical to the control's, so their step reads zero by construction: a determinism check, and the only pre-step check of a real-farm step, because the spring step starts before the earliest cutoff. The seed noise floor and the shuffled steps stand in for the brief's pre-step placebo.

What a network that cannot tell the year can know (written before the results). The pretraining inputs carry the sun's position, the time of day, the day of the week, and holiday columns, and no year or day of the year. Weekday and moving holidays carry some information about the year, so the network may not be fully calendar-blind; the constant-injection controls and the step networks test this. A calibrated probe would then read the average of the injected capacity over the rows the probe reaches. The probe's donor days are within 21 days of the probe date's day of the year and at the same half-hour, so the truth a calendar-blind network can know is mw x post-step share of the donor rows. We compute that share per cutoff and Primary from the probe's donor rows and report the recovery against both the full step and this share.

Bars (fixed before any step-world recovery was read).

  • Step bar. The calibrated step at 2025-10 is at least 70% of the injected step, at 4 of the 6 Primaries, for both step months and both sizes.
  • Before-the-step bars. (a) The shuffled-shape step reads under 0.3 MW at every cutoff. (b) The seed noise floor (the probed capacity of one uninjected network minus another, per Primary and cutoff) has a 95th percentile under 0.3 MW. (c) At 2025-07 the summer-step networks train on rows identical to the control's, so their step reads zero by construction; the check confirms the probe returns the same number.
  • Coverage bar. The nominal 80% interval, widened by the leave-one-farm-out spread of the factor, covers the constant-injection truth of the 2 MW and 4 MW real-farm networks of experiment 621 in at least 60% of injections (calibrated). For the step worlds it is reported against both the full step and the calendar-blind share.
  • Lag. Months from the step to the first cutoff at which the calibrated recovery of the full step reaches 0.7 at the median Primary; stop rule above.

docs.title: Metered neighbour PV as a sky input to the donor-day probe
docs.text:
Take-home: giving the neural network the measured output of a solar farm 5 to 25 km from the Primary substation did not help the probe find an injected farm. The probe recovered 0.691 of each injected megawatt of AC capacity, against 0.683 without the measured farm. The neural network does use the added input, because its probabilistic score on the six MW Primaries is 2.1% better. A satellite sky-pixel error therefore does not explain the shortfall, and a possible next test is the shape of a real farm (clipping, tilt, and energy per unit of peak). Verdict: not supported, because the gain was -0.004 against a threshold of +0.04.

We asked whether a satellite pixel from CAMS (the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service), which can sit kilometres from a solar farm, hides part of the farm's output from a neural network, so that a measured local sky would let the probe find more of it. The probe adds the recorded output of a real solar farm to the net demand (demand minus embedded generation) of a Primary substation, trains the network on the result, and then estimates how many megawatts of AC capacity the network attributes to sunshine. Recovery is that estimate for the injected network, minus the estimate for an uninjected twin, divided by the injected megawatts. Experiment 621 is the baseline (arm a, CAMS shortwave radiation only). In arm b the neural network also takes the nearest metered farm's output, normalised by its own 99th percentile, as an input column (never the farm injected at that Primary). In arm c the neural network takes that column instead of the CAMS shortwave radiation. Recovery stayed at about 0.69 in arm b and fell to 0.65 in arm c.

Figure 1: each dot is the median over 3 seeds and 2 farm rotations of the recovery of a 4 MW real farm at one MW Primary.

Figure 2: boxes span the quartiles and whiskers the minimum and maximum over 3 seeds. The profile-only and shuffled-sky boxes cover six Primaries and two farm rotations (36 networks per arm); the physics-curve world and the metered-column-shuffled placebo use one rotation (18 per arm).

Quantity (median, 2026-06 cutoff, 3 seeds) a: CAMS b: CAMS + metered c: metered only Real farm 4 MW, recovery per injected AC MW 0.683 0.691 0.651 Real farm 4 MW, recovery per injected energy 0.809 0.825 0.784 Real farm 2 MW, per MW (per energy) 0.677 (0.810) 0.692 (0.819) 0.636 (0.762) Difference to arm a, per MW (90% interval over 12 Primary-rotation pairs) -0.004 (-0.010 to +0.026) -0.039 (-0.066 to -0.016) Physics-curve world 4 MW (2 MW) 0.99 (0.99) 0.98 (0.96) 0.77 (0.80) Profile-only placebo, 95th percentile 0.116 0.093 0.097 Shuffled-sky placebo, 95th percentile 0.127 0.142 0.150 Profile placebo with the metered column shuffled, 95th percentile not run 0.089 0.058 Cloud-following load (no template), per MW of a 2 MW farm 0.333 0.297 0.274 Validation CRPS (continuous ranked probability score), all Primaries (six MW Primaries) 0.2605 (0.2047) 0.2591 (0.2003) 0.2671 (0.2059)
