The test worlds are those of experiment 621: the physics-curve world injects a modelled solar output driven by the CAMS shortwave radiation; the profile-only placebo injects only a real farm's average daily shape; the shuffled-sky placebo injects that shape plus the farm's day-to-day variation moved to other days of the month; the cloud-following load raises demand with cloudiness.

  • Pre-registered result. Prediction 1 failed (arm b needed 0.72 or more and gave 0.691). Predictions 2, 3, and 4 held: arm c is below arm b, the largest placebo is 0.142 of 0.691 (0.21, under 0.25), and arm b's CRPS is lower than arm a's. The decision rule fails on its gain of at least 0.04, and the interval of the difference includes zero.
  • Per energy. Dividing by the farm's share of the unit curve's energy gives 0.81 for arm a, 0.83 for arm b, and 0.78 for arm c, so the energy view shows the same ordering.
  • The input farms. Primaries D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 take farms F (7.7 km), A (18.7 km), C (7.8 km; A at 9.3 km when C is the injected farm), C (24.4 km), B (9.5 km; F at 10.9 km when B is the injected farm), and F (4.8 km). The injected farm is excluded at every Primary. Every Primary has at least 3 of the 6 NGED farms within 30 km.
  • Public units. Sutton Bridge Solar Farm is the one public Balancing Mechanism Unit we found within 30 km of a MW Primary, searching the 12 single-site units of the solar BMU census (D5 20.6 km, D14 22.1 km, D16 29.5 km). The census gives it 12 months of settled output, too short for pretraining, so the farm entered the distance count and no neural network.
  • Possible reason the recovery does not move. Arm b's CRPS is 2.1% lower on the six MW Primaries (0.2003 against 0.2047), so the neural network takes up the column, yet the injected farm is still recovered at 0.69. The Discuss session's diagnostics from experiment 624 (pull request 291, unmerged when this page was written) put the real farm's energy at 0.72 to 0.84 of the physics curve's at the same peak, and found that moving the sky pixel 5 to 17 km costs only a few points. We did not test this explanation here.
  • Checks. A result that contradicts its prediction normally calls for an audit. No audit was run; the CRPS gain and the energy view are offered as the explanation, and neither was tested. The probe reads only the neural network's mixture mean, so the median-minus-mean check does not apply. Every placebo passed, and no arm that adds an input scored worse than the arm that lacks it except arm c.
  • Caveats. This test used one cutoff (2026-06), 3 seeds, and farms in one region. The donor rescaling uses the horizontal clear-sky shape, which is approximate for a tilted farm. Arm c keeps the six other CAMS weather columns, including longwave radiation, so arm c is not metered-only for cloud. The shuffled column takes zeros from real gaps in farms A, B, C, and F (up to 12% of half-hours in 2019, 8% in 2020, and 1% or less from 2021). This is a known-answer test, so no forecast lead is involved.
  • Reuse. Code: ml-experiments/00635-pv-probe-metered-neighbour-pv-as-sky-input/; it imports experiments 397, 405, 409, 428, 448, 510, 554, and 621 and edits none of them. Arm a is experiment 621's stored networks and probe results.
  • A possible next test. Whether the injected farm's own clipping and tilt explain the shortfall: a physics-curve world with a farm-like shape (clipped at its DC-to-AC ratio, with the farm's orientation) would show how much of the gap the shape alone produces.

docs.title: Can a monthly regression of power on irradiance find known capacity steps at the six metered solar farms, including a loss of direct-current capacity hidden under inverter clipping?
docs.text:
A monthly regression of power on irradiance finds a 10% loss of capacity within 3 months at Solar C and Solar F, and does not find it at Solar A, B, or D at any horizon up to 12 months. The pre-registered stop rule fires, because three of the five farms miss. The slope is therefore reported as not usable at Solar A, B, and D, and the line stops with no tuning. A direct-current loss hidden under the inverter limit is found as often as a proportional loss of alternating-current output, but only because clipping is rare at these farms.

We injected capacity losses into each farm's real series, refitted both estimators, and counted how often the loss was found. A loss counts as found when the mean level of the months after the start falls below the mean of the 12 months before by more than the 95th percentile of the same statistic on the farm's real series. Experiment 618's sunny-row envelope is the comparison estimator.

Figure 1 (headline). The slope finds a 10% loss at Solar C (95%) and Solar F (90% and 85%). The envelope finds 5% to 45%. 20 start months a farm.

Figure 2. Solar C passes the 80% bar from a loss of about 6%, Solar F from about 9%. Solar A, B, and D do not reach it by 15%.

Figure 3. Recall of a 10% loss at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months.

Figure 4. Top: zeroing 5% of one month's daylight half-hours, with no capacity change. Bottom: false steps on the real, uninjected series.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Rows: experiment 218's stored farm rows: every daylight half-hour of Solar A to F to 2026-06-30, with output as a fraction of stored capacity, CAMS irradiance, and ERA5 temperature.
  • Slope: per farm, a robust regression of output on irradiance terms over half-hours with clear-sky irradiance of at least 100 W/m2; each month's value is the least-squares slope of output on that expectation, weighted by the clear-sky index squared, divided by the same calendar month's median in earlier years.
  • Envelope: experiment 618's sunny-row filter, one median ratio per sunny day, averaged by month.
  • Worlds: 1 multiplies output by one minus the loss; 2 removes the loss from direct-current power and clips at the inverter limit (99.5th percentile of output); 3 injects at each farm's 3 cloudiest months; 4 zeroes 5% of one month's daylight half-hours, three repeats at each start. Losses 3%, 5%, 7.5%, 10%, and 15% at 20 start months (January, April, July, and October of 2021 to 2025).
  • Found: the mean of the k months from the start over the mean of the 12 months before, minus 1, is below minus the farm's 95th-percentile threshold from the uninjected series. Windows with no data count as missed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Stop rule (10% at 3 months, slope, recall under 80% is a miss). World 1: A 15%, B 25%, C 95%, D 0%, F 90%. World 2: A 15%, B 25%, C 95%, D 0%, F 85%. Three farms miss in each world, so the stop rule fires. The envelope misses at all 5 farms in both worlds (5% to 45%).
  • Why Solar A, B, and D fail. The 3-month thresholds from their real series are 24%, 16%, and 49% (Solar C 4%, Solar F 7%), because the real histories hold level changes and noisy winters. Recovered size over injected size, over all windows, is 0.99 to 1.02, so the estimator shows no bias. In the windows where a step is found it is 0.81 at Solar A and 0.88 at Solar B, because only the larger random falls cross their high thresholds, and 0.97 to 1.00 at Solar C and Solar F. The threshold is the problem. A base with real steps removed, as in experiment 618, is not tested here.
  • Minimum detectable loss (80% recall), slope, world 1 / world 2. 3 months: Solar C 6.3% / 6.3%, Solar F 9.3% / 9.7%. 12 months: Solar C 3.0% / 3.0%, Solar F 4.8% / 5.8%. At 1 month only Solar F reaches it (14.3%). Envelope, 12 months only: Solar C 7.5% / 10%, Solar F 8% / 11%.
  • Smaller losses (slope, 3 months, world 1). A 5% loss: Solar C 70%, Solar F 25%. A 3% loss: Solar C 45%, Solar F 15%.
  • The envelope and the slope do not separate the two worlds here. In world 2 the envelope, which responds only to the alternating-current limit, recovers 83% to 87% of a 10% direct-current loss when it finds one at Solar C, D, and F (75% to 85% over all windows). It finds the loss in only 30% to 35% of cases at Solar C and F, against 95% and 85% for the slope. A clipped half-hour is only 0.4% (Solar A) to 1.1% (Solar F) of daylight half-hours, so a direct-current loss barely differs from an alternating-current loss.
  • Cloudy months (world 3). False-step rate on the real series, pooled over the five farms: 7% (interval 1% to 30%, 15 windows) in the three cloudiest months against 1% to 2% in other months, and 6% (2% to 16%, 50 windows) in the ten cloudiest. Injected 10% losses at the three cloudiest start months of each farm are found 40% of the time at 3 months, pooled over the five farms (15 windows, 20% to 64%). The same pooled figure in ordinary months is 45%, so cloudy months do not reduce recall detectably.
  • Curtailment placebo (world 4). Zeroing 5% of a month's daylight half-hours is flagged as a fall at 1 month in 10% of 300 cases (7% to 14%) for the slope, twice the 5% bar. By farm: A 5%, B 17%, C 7%, D 15%, F 5%. Post hoc, dropping zero-output rows leaves it at 8% (6% to 12%) and raises recall of a 10% loss at 1 month at C and F to 95% (world 1; Solar F is 90% in world 2). The envelope flags 1%.

docs.title: Prediction scorecard
docs.text:
• World 1: met (C 95%, F 90%; A 15%, B 25%, D 0%).
  • World 2: the slope is within 10 points of world 1 at every farm, met. The prediction that the envelope sees under half of a 10% direct-current loss at Solar C, D, and F is not met: it recovers 83% to 87% of the loss when it finds one. The premise that 1% to 2.5% of daylight half-hours are clipped was too high (0.4% to 1.1%).
  • World 3: not tested per farm, because each cloudy group has 3 windows a farm. Pooled over the five farms the false-step rate is 7% in the three cloudiest months against 1% to 2% in other months, but the interval is 1% to 30%, so the prediction is undecided.
  • World 4: not met. The slope flagged the 5% zeroing at C and F in 7% and 5% of cases, not over 50%, because the 1-month thresholds there are 13% and 9%. The false-alarm rate (10%) did exceed 5%.
  • Stop rule: fired, as predicted.

docs.title: Caveats and checks
docs.text:
• Setup: five farms are testable (Solar E has only 20 months of data). Each has 20 start months, so recall resolves in steps of 5 points. Irradiance is from CAMS (Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service) to 2026-06-30, development data only, and no forecast is scored. No cleaning beyond the stored farm rows.
  • Deseasonalising uses only months before the start month (code review change), so an injected loss cannot move the reference.
  • Direct-current world is a stress case: clipped half-hours are assumed to hold 15% more direct-current power than their output. The data cannot show the true excess. Because only 0.4% to 1.1% of half-hours are clipped, world 2 is close to world 1 by construction.
  • Windows past the end of the data (starts in 2025 at 6 and 12 months) average the months that exist, in thresholds and injections alike.
  • Audit triggers: the audit rule's seven triggers all concern forecast scores. This experiment scores no forecast, so none applies. Anonymised: no coordinates, no calendar dates.
  • Code: ml-experiments/00636-metered-solar-monthly-slope-capacity-known-answer-test/; it copies experiment 218's rows and experiment 618's envelope filter. One Sonnet code review before the run found a world 2 injection that left clipped half-hours unclipped; the stress case replaced it.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Do not tune this estimator for Solar A, B, and D. A step-removed base, or a second irradiance product to lower the monthly error, is the open route, and neither is a pre-registered part of this experiment.
  • Use the slope at Solar C and Solar F only, to date steps of about 6% to 9% or more.

docs.title: How do the five bake-off systems score on July to October 2026 once days flagged as an abnormal running arrangement are removed?
docs.text: Removing the days that a frozen detector flags as an abnormal running arrangement (ARA, a temporary load transfer between Primaries) turns the networks' small loss to the manual heuristic into a lead. K1's continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) minus the heuristic's falls from +0.10 to -0.15 points of capacity. Nearly all the removed days are at one Primary, D18. The page is a second reading of a window that was already scored once, so it is descriptive and ranks nothing.

docs.title: Frozen detector (written before the window was touched)
docs.text:
• Input: cleaned observed power only. No network forecast is read.
  • Daily statistic: for each Primary and UTC day, the day's mean of observed power minus the heuristic (all 13 members), and minus the climatology fitted to data before 2025-07-01. Each residual has the cross-Primary daily median subtracted. The two are averaged.
  • Scale: each Primary's median and 1.4826 x median absolute deviation over 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30.
  • Rule: flag days with |z| above k, bridge one-day gaps, keep runs of at least n days. Operating point k = 3.5, n = 2. Stricter k = 4.0, looser k = 3.0 (same n).
  • Chosen on development days only (2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30), by the mean of the F1 on injected known-answer steps (4 worlds of 30 steps, 0.5 to 8 MW, 2 to 28 days) and the F1 on the verified real transfers over 1 day. At the operating point: injected precision 0.46 and recall 0.58; real recall 0.31, with 55 flagged days outside any labelled event (an upper bound on false alarms, since NGED's labels are incomplete). Injected recall by size: 0.5 MW 0.14, 1 MW 0.43, 2 MW 0.84, 4 MW and above 1.00.
  • Rule file ara_rule.json SHA-256: e5fb5cc08a67327d74dbc93ee51ba4e31dfc25bb25d8d4fab426bb32762b0566 (committed in the plan, and printed again by the window run). The committed file later gained a trailing newline for the pre-commit hook; its hash is now e1c8df968b2da090b7c959077e38894d621a437796058e7cac4f0b33272280e5. No other byte changed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A Primary-day is one Primary on one UTC day. Dashed lines in the first figure mark a contrast of zero; in the second they mark the threshold of +3.5 and -3.5.

  • Rows removed: 56,699 of 929,870 (6.1%) at the operating point; 5.3% stricter; 8.0% looser. 119 of 1,968 Primary-days (6.0%).
  • Flag rate by month: 6.3% (July), 5.6% (August), 6.3% (September), 6.0% (October).
  • By Primary: D18 102 of 123 days; D21 8; D14 5; D8 2; D10 2; the other 11 Primaries none.
  • Episode: of the 112 days from 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-26, D18 is flagged on 101 and D14 on 5. D18's daily residual has a median of about +5 robust standard deviations. Gap bridging joins its days above 3.5 into long runs. D14's residual runs from -4.3 to -0.1 and exceeds 3.5 in size on 9 days, and the 2-day minimum run keeps only 5 of them.
  • CRPS, points of capacity (day-block 95% interval):
Rows Rows scored K1 Candidate K3 Manual heuristic Climatology All rows 929,870 4.94 (4.88 to 5.01) 5.00 5.32 4.85 (4.74 to 4.96) 8.12 Kept, stricter (k=4.0) 880,815 4.34 4.37 4.70 4.48 7.84 Kept, operating (k=3.5) 873,171 4.29 (4.23 to 4.34) 4.31 4.64 4.44 (4.34 to 4.54) 7.83 Kept, looser (k=3.0) 855,275 4.21 4.24 4.55 4.38 7.84
  • Contrast with the heuristic (CRPS minus the heuristic's, interval): operating K1 -0.15 (-0.26 to -0.05), candidate -0.13 (-0.23 to -0.02), K3 +0.20 (+0.08 to +0.32). Stricter and looser give the same signs. MAE at the operating point: K1 7.58, candidate 7.65, K3 8.12, heuristic 7.82, climatology 14.19.
  • Wins against the heuristic by Primary: K1 and the candidate 12 of 16, K3 9 of 16, on all rows and at every threshold. At D18, K1's CRPS falls from 14.98 to 7.72 on the kept days and the heuristic's from 11.12 to 7.45, so K1 still trails the heuristic there. D14 is unchanged (K1 5.94, heuristic 3.03).
  • Against rule R1 (experiment 620): R1 removed 290 Primary-days; the detector's 119 include 113 of them. The detector removes fewer Primary-days than R1.

docs.title: Predictions and what was not measured
docs.text:
• Prediction: K1 minus heuristic falls below +0.05: supported (-0.15). The detector flags most days of the D14 and D18 episode at D18 and not at D14. Verdict: partly supported.
  • Blind spots: the detector cannot see transfers of about 1 MW or less (development recall 0.43 at 1 MW and 0.14 at 0.5 MW). It misses transfers shorter than 2 days. It reads only the daily mean, so a transfer within one day is invisible.
  • Incomplete labels: NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the development false-alarm count is an upper bound and the real-transfer recall is measured on the labelled subset only.
  • Audit triggers: this is a re-score of stored forecasts. No model was refitted, no median or mean forecast comparison applies, and the window was read once before; no trigger fired.
  • Code: reuses ml-experiments/00620-bakeoff-final-test-demand-networks-at-primaries/ (e00620_score.py, e00620_second_reading.py) and the labelled set of experiment 41.

docs.title: Why the PV probe missed a capacity step: mostly the sunny spring, not a limit of the probe
docs.text: We tested a method that estimates how much solar capacity a demand-forecasting neural network has learned, by feeding the network different weather and measuring how its forecast changes (the probe). The question was whether the probe can follow a rise in solar capacity that starts partway through the training years. We make the rise synthetic: we add the recorded output of a real solar farm, scaled to 4 MW, to the demand that the network trains on at six Primary substations metered in megawatts, from a chosen start date. In an earlier experiment, 634, a rise starting in April 2025 was found at 0.32 to 0.49 of its added size, and a placebo (an addition with a shuffled shape) was found at about half of that. This experiment asked whether the failure came from the unusually sunny spring of 2025, or from a limit that holds in any year. A rise starting in April 2023 was found at 0.82 to 0.88 of its size. A placebo with no link to the sky of any date was found at 0.20 to 0.36 of the real rise's read at the three later training cutoffs. The sunny spring and the small fraction (0.19 to 0.23) of the training rows after the April 2025 start therefore explain most of experiment 634's failure. The probe reads a real rise higher than a linear regression on the physics curve and the temperature would, and we did not find why. The hypothesis is partly supported.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
• Step: a real solar farm's output (4 MW of its capacity) added to the demand target of the six MW Primaries from a start date to the end of the training data, as in experiment 634. Names: spring23 (from 2023-04-01), summer24 (2024-07-01), spring25 (2025-04-01), and summer25 (2025-07-01).
  • Climatological placebo: the same injection with the farm's mean output per day of the year and half-hour over all years before July 2026, smoothed over 7 days either side. It has the farm's seasonal and daily shape and almost no information about any one date's weather (one date moves its own profile value by under 2%). Its energy after each start is 0.93 to 1.10 of the real farm's.
  • Calibrated read, cutoff, and donor rows: as in experiment 634. The calibrated read is the probed capacity of the injected network minus its control's, divided by 4 MW and by the leave-one-farm-out factor of 0.67 to 0.69. The control, constant-injection, spring25, summer25, and shuffled-placebo networks are experiment 634's, unretrained.
  • Clearness: measured over clear-sky shortwave irradiance, 10:00 to 15:00 UTC.
  • Share: the fraction of the probe's donor rows dated after the step's start.
  • Previous-year base: every probe date moved 364 days earlier.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The ordinary-spring step is tracked, and the placebo of the sunny spring-2025 step reads about a third of the real step. Experiment 634 set a step bar: a calibrated read of at least 0.70 of the step's size.

Step Share Clearness after minus before Real step, calibrated read (four cutoffs) Climatological placebo spring23 (ordinary spring) 0.57 to 0.59 0.004 to 0.021 0.86, 0.82, 0.88, 0.86 0.09, 0.09, 0.07, 0.12 summer24 0.20 to 0.32 0.023 to 0.090 0.47, 0.47, 0.45, 0.55 0.21, 0.09, 0.07, 0.07 spring25 (sunny spring) 0.19 to 0.23 0.049 to 0.100 0.43, 0.38, 0.32, 0.49 0.28, 0.14, 0.08, 0.10 summer25 0.00 to 0.14 -0.052 to 0.012 0.00, 0.02, 0.00, 0.11 none, -0.08, -0.11, -0.05
  • The stop rule did not fire. The spring-2025 placebo reads 0.36, 0.25, and 0.20 of the real step at 2025-10, 2026-03, and 2026-06 (a ratio of medians over six Primaries and three seeds), below the 0.5 that stops the experiment. At 2025-07, with six probe dates, the ratio is 0.64.
  • The placebo bar holds for spring23 and for spring25 at the three later cutoffs. Reads are at most 0.14, below 0.15. At 2025-07 the spring25 placebo reads 0.28 and the summer24 placebo 0.21, so the bar fails there. The 95th percentile of the placebo's absolute raw read over all networks is 0.48 to 0.62 MW at the later spring25 cutoffs, against 0.74 to 0.93 MW for the shuffled placebo and a noise floor of 0.244 MW.
  • The spring23 step reads above its donor share, so prediction (2) fails on the high side. The read is 0.82 to 0.88 and the share 0.57 to 0.59, a difference of 0.23 to 0.31, against a predicted at most 0.2. The step bar of 0.70 is passed, at all four cutoffs.
  • The summer24 step is read at 0.45 to 0.55, above its share of 0.20 to 0.32. The summer25 step is read at 0.00 to 0.11, as experiment 634 found, with a clearness difference of about -0.05. A step's read rises with its share, and the sunny-spring clearness difference adds only the amount that the placebo already reads.
  • The widened 80% interval is too narrow for these reads. It contains the share for 0% to 22% of the 18 real spring23 and spring25 networks at each cutoff. It covers zero for 0% to 44% of the climatological placebo networks. Experiment 634's page states that its intervals understate the spread between farms, so the intervals are not used for any claim here.

Moving the probe dates a year earlier changes the median read by at most 0.05, except at 2025-07. The change is at most 0.01 at the other cutoffs for the real steps of spring23, spring25, and summer24. At 2025-07 (six probe dates) the real spring25 read falls from 0.43 to 0.33 and its climatological placebo from 0.28 to 0.22. The networks do not use the date of the base row.

docs.title: The read compared with a date-blind regression
docs.text:
A linear regression of the injected megawatts on the physics unit curve and the temperature, over the probe's own cells, gives the raw read of a learner that cannot tell the date. The networks read more than that.

Step and shape Regression (raw, per injected MW) Networks (raw), four cutoffs spring23, real 0.39 to 0.42 0.57 to 0.59 spring23, placebo -0.04 to -0.01 0.04 to 0.09 spring25, real 0.12 to 0.18 0.22 to 0.35 spring25, placebo 0.00 to 0.06 0.05 to 0.17 summer24, real 0.19 to 0.25 0.30 to 0.38
  • The donor share was the wrong yardstick. The regression gives 0.39 to 0.42 raw for spring23, which is 0.57 to 0.62 after the factor of 0.68, about the share. The network's 0.86 is about 1.45 times that.
  • The remaining excess is 0.1 to 0.2 raw for a real step and 0.05 to 0.1 for a placebo, and we did not find its cause. One untested candidate is that the network reads weekday, holiday, or pandemic columns of the input that differ between the step's years. The previous-year base shows the networks do not read the base row's date. The unexplained excess is the reason the verdict is not "supported".

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text:
• The sunny-summer step that the follow-up brief asked for could not be built from a sunny summer. No July to September in the data has clearness above 0.63, so summer24 stands in: its post-step period is sunnier than its pre-step period by 0.02 to 0.09.
  • The plan's coverage bar and the full-step reference were replaced before any fit (reviewer finding): coverage is judged against the share and zero, and the summer25 base dates partly precede the step.
  • Prediction (2) failed (above), and the decision rule read strictly gives "inconclusive" because the sunny-year support rule needs prediction (2). The verdict "partly supported" rests on prediction (1), the stop rule, and the ordinary-spring read.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, per site: not applicable, because no forecast is scored.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside every quantile-score contrast: not applicable.
  • Triggers that fired: prediction (2) contradicted its result. The session tested one explanation (the yardstick, above) and recorded the unexplained remainder. No audit was run; the page therefore makes no claim that depends on the remainder.
  • Review: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the plan and code before any fit. Its findings on the coverage bar, prediction (4), the decision rule, the stop-rule floor, the figures in prediction (2), and the unused noise-floor bar were accepted and applied before the fits. Its note that the profile contains a little of each date's own weather was accepted and stated in the definitions.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• The scripts e00638_fit.py, e00638_probe.py, e00638_analyse.py, e00638_oracle.py, and e00638_report.py import the modules of experiment 634 and, through them, experiments 397, 405, 409, 428, 448, 510, 554, 621, and 623, and edit none of them. Farm gaps drop the same rows from every arm. The 69 fits took about 0.6 GPU-hours.
  • The shuffled-placebo reads in the figure are experiment 634's.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The excess of the networks over a date-blind regression is the open question: a step that starts in an ordinary spring and ends after one year, and a network whose weekday, holiday, and pandemic columns are held at fixed values, would show whether the weekday, holiday, and pandemic columns carry the excess.

docs.title: A physics solar term with a probed capacity forecasts sunny middays better, but mostly by fixing a bias
docs.text:
A demand neural network given a physics solar curve and a probed solar capacity forecasts sunny middays better than a neural network that learns the solar response from irradiance, but much of the gain is a bias in the free network, and the test does not show that each Primary's own capacity matters. The error measure is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in percentage points of each Primary's effective capacity (smaller is better). Sunny middays are the half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC with a clear-sky index of at least 0.7.

We asked whether a demand neural network that is told how much solar capacity sits behind a Primary substation forecasts sunny middays better than one that learns the solar response from its irradiance inputs. The capacity comes from the probe of experiments 621, 623, and 638, which reads the capacity a trained network has learned by feeding it weather from other days. It is combined with the capacity table of experiment 474. We trained the networks on recorded weather (ERA5, from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, and CAMS, from the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service) up to three cutoffs (July 2025, March 2026, and June 2026), and scored the 60 days after each, at the six Primaries metered in megawatts. We scored two worlds. In the real world the demand is the recorded demand. In the step world, 4 MW of a real solar farm's output has been added to the demand since April 2023.

On sunny middays the explicit network's CRPS was 3.30 against 4.05 for the free network in the real world, and 6.09 against 8.99 in the step world. A placebo that swapped the capacities between Primaries scored only 0.14 points worse than the explicit network in the step world. That is below the 0.18 points that the test can resolve. Two of the three pre-registered predictions hold: the gain in the step world, and no loss on the real months. The third holds for one of its two placebos: the shuffled-sky placebo loses clearly, and the capacity-swap placebo does not. The hypothesis is partly supported.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
• Free network: experiment 554's pretraining network (a mixture density neural network) on the net demand, which is demand with the solar generation netted off. It is the recipe of experiment 565, and it learns the solar response from its irradiance input. Seeds 0 to 2 are experiment 634's (real world) and 638's (step world); seeds 3 and 4 are trained here.
  • Explicit network: the same neural network trained on gross demand, which is net demand plus a physics solar curve (the curve for 1 MW) times a capacity timeline in megawatts. The forecast subtracts the same term. The timeline is k (a scale factor on experiment 474's table) times the table, plus D (the capacity step in megawatts, zero in the real world) from the step date, plus a trainable offset. Arms: cal (k and D read by the probe and divided by the leave-one-farm-out recovery factor of 0.67 to 0.69, the share of an injected farm's capacity the probe recovers), raw (as probed), r4 (the table unchanged), oracle (the table plus exactly 4 MW from the step), and the placebos perm (the capacity timelines shifted by two Primaries) and shuf (the curve built from the weather of another date).
  • CRPS is pooled over test rows, with each row in percentage points of its Primary's effective capacity.
  • Minimum detectable effect (MDE): the half-width of the interval of a null contrast, which is the free network's seeds {0, 2, 4} against {1, 3} (averaged over all ten 3-and-2 splits), at the same 98.75% level as the contrasts (95%, Bonferroni-corrected over four contrasts). It is 0.067 in the real world and 0.181 in the step world.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The explicit network beats the free network by far more than the MDE. Each entry is the arm's CRPS minus the cal arm's, so a positive value favours cal. Intervals are day-block bootstraps at the 98.75% level.

Arm minus cal Real, sunny Step, sunny free +0.75 [0.51, 1.01] +2.90 [2.15, 3.65] raw -0.05 [-0.15, 0.05] +0.20 [-0.10, 0.50] r4 (fixed table) -0.10 [-0.14, -0.05] +1.78 [1.15, 2.40] oracle not run +0.21 [0.04, 0.38] perm placebo +0.31 [0.22, 0.39] +0.14 [0.06, 0.22] shuf placebo +3.30 [3.02, 3.58] +8.81 [8.09, 9.61]

  • C1 holds. In the step world free minus cal is +2.90, above the MDE of 0.181, and 16 times the MDE. The MDE exceeds the 0.10 limit set in the plan, so the plan's predicted gain of 0.05 to 0.15 could not have been resolved. The prediction was also too low: the observed gain is 19 to 58 times the predicted one.
  • C2 holds. On all half-hours of the real months cal is 0.13 points better than free [0.08, 0.19], so it loses nothing. The windows cover March to August (the June 2026 window is 30 days).
  • C3 fails. The shuffled-sky placebo loses by 8.81. The capacity-swap placebo loses by 0.14 in the step world, below the MDE of 0.18, so the test does not show that each Primary's own capacity matters there. The injected 4 MW is the same at every Primary, so swapping the timelines changes only the table part. In the real world, which is outside the pre-registered C3, the swap loses 0.31, above the real-world MDE of 0.067, so the Primary's own capacity does help there.
  • The best real-world arm is the fixed table. r4 beats cal by 0.10 in the real world. The best arm in best_arm is chosen in the step world, where the table has no step. raw and cal differ by 0.2 points or less, and raw does not beat cal by the MDE.
  • The probe's step. The raw probed step is 2.1 to 2.6 MW of the 4 MW injected (0.53 to 0.65 per injected megawatt), and the calibrated step is 3.2 to 3.8 MW (0.80 to 0.95). Per injected megawatt-hour, divide by the farm's energy share of 0.78 of the physics curve's (experiment 634's rows basis): the calibrated step is about 1.0 to 1.2 and the raw step about 0.7 to 0.8.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The gain is mostly a bias in the real world. The free network's median forecast is too high on sunny middays by 5.0, 4.2, and 2.7 points of capacity at the three cutoffs in the real world (calibrated explicit network: 2.3, -0.4, 0.8), and by 7.7, 10.3, and 4.0 in the step world (calibrated explicit network: 1.6, -2.6, 0.2). Shifting the free forecast by the free network's own bias at each cutoff leaves cal ahead by about 0.07 in the real world (the audit's figure). Shifting it by that bias at each cutoff and Primary, a correction available only in hindsight, makes the free network 0.52 better than cal in the real world and leaves cal 0.90 ahead in the step world. The free network is also overconfident (its 50% interval covers 38% to 49% of sunny rows), and in the step world its 5% to 95% width is about twice that of cal.
  • The gain is uneven. By cutoff, free minus cal is +0.85, +0.89, and +0.27 (real), and +3.12, +3.73, and +0.48 (step). One of the six Primaries carries +3.05 (real) and +7.15 (step); two Primaries score slightly better with free in the real world (-0.39 and -0.29). Without that Primary the real-world gain is still +0.27 on average.
  • Error of the median forecast beside CRPS. The mean absolute error of the median on sunny middays is 5.81 (free) against 4.44 (cal) in the real world, and 11.74 against 8.37 in the step world, in the same direction as the CRPS. The median minus the approximate mean (from the 11 quantiles) is -0.17 for free and 0.02 for cal in the real world, and -4.30 against -0.38 in the step world.
  • Triggers. An audit ran, with a private brief and report. The trigger "a gain after five earlier nulls on the mean score" was explained as a bias, partly. The trigger "a nested arm beats the arm that contains it" (oracle loses to cal) has the energy-ratio explanation above, but regularisation by the random draws of k and D each epoch could also explain it, and these files cannot separate the two. The trigger "a later experiment depends on the sign" holds, and the result is unreplicated. The audit reproduced every headline CRPS with its own code, and found no lookahead and no unequal training between arms (free networks stopped after 30 to 54 epochs, explicit networks after 39 to 52).
  • Finding not applied. The audit asked for experiment 474's table for the one dominant Primary without later data. That was not run, because the table's own fit used the whole history, and Limits states this.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Recorded weather, not forecasts. The weather is ERA5 and CAMS at the valid time, so this is a hindcast. A gain here does not show a gain for a forecast that uses ensemble weather forecasts.
  • Short lead range. The rows have no forecast lead, so the 1 to 10 day range that the network operator (NGED) cares about is untested.
  • Capacity table. Experiment 474's table was fitted on data that includes the test windows. The networks use only its season-years that ended before the cutoff, and hold the last value.
  • What C1 tests. The free network has trained on two to three years of post-step rows, and k and D come from probing that same network, so the test shows the value of the explicit structure, not tracking of a capacity that appeared shortly before the cutoff.
  • The test windows. Three cutoffs cover 150 days from March to August, with 4,397 sunny rows pooled over six Primaries (the bootstrap resamples whole days). The shuffled-sky donor falls in the same 21-day block of the year, and a test row's input-spread columns use one lead band.
  • Not reported. The plan listed one sunny and one cloudy example week, and a plot of all cutoffs. Only one example week is shown.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does the gain survive ensemble weather forecasts and a free network shifted by its bias? Repeat the contrast with ensemble weather forecasts, include a free network shifted to the latest level after one refit month, and test a step that starts within 60 days of the cutoff.

docs.title: Standing practices followed and departed from
docs.text:
• Followed: cleaned data, the D15 and D18 cut, saved weights, reuse of stored networks, one paired contrast per question, and day-ahead and 14-day forecast plots (here one sunny week and one cloudy week instead, because the rows are hindcasts without leads).
  • Departed from: monthly refits (one pretraining per cutoff, as in experiment 634); the load-shift slices (no event is injected); the screen on four test months (three cutoffs only, chosen below).
  • Earlier advice followed: experiment 638 advises a step that starts in an ordinary spring with more than half the donor rows after it, so the step world is its spring23 step. The placebo is the shuffled-day sky and the permutation of capacities, as the design review asks.

docs.title: Worlds, networks, and arms
docs.text:
• Real world: experiment 634's control rows (no injection). Step world: the spring23 step of experiment 638 (a real farm's output scaled to 4 MW added to the six MW Primaries' demand from 2023-04-01; farms A, B, C, F, A, B in order, anonymised by letter).
  • Network: experiment 554's ModularMdn at stage pre, trained with experiment 634's train. The free arm is that network on the net target. Every explicit arm trains the same network on the gross target y + C(t) * inc * u(t) (u is experiment 634's physics unit curve of the row's own CAMS-and-ERA5 weather, inc the inverse effective capacity of the Primary), and subtracts C(t) * inc * u(t) from each quantile at prediction. The shortwave input stays.
  • Capacity timeline. C(t) = (k + e_k) * R4(season-year of t) + (D + e_D) * 1[t >= step] + delta. R4 is experiment 474's table (ac_p50, per Primary and season-year). k rescales the table to the probe's level: the probed capacity of the free real-world network (median over seeds) divided by R4 at season-year 2025, clipped to 0.5 to 1.5. D is the probed capacity of the free step-world network minus that of the free real-world network, floored at zero, and zero in the real world. e_k and e_D are drawn once per epoch from a normal distribution whose relative spread is the quadrature sum of the seed spread, the bootstrap spread, the factor spread, and 0.04 for the spread of the factor between farms. delta is a trainable offset per Primary with a normal prior of 0.25 MW.
  • Arms.
    • free: the free arm.
    • cal: k and D divided by the leave-one-farm-out factor of experiment 638 (0.67 to 0.69).
    • raw: k and D as probed.
    • r4: the fixed table, k = 1, D = 0.
    • oracle: the table with D = 4 MW exactly (step world only; a ceiling, not a contrast).
    • perm: the cal timelines of the six Primaries cyclically shifted by two.
    • shuf: the cal timeline with u built from the weather of another date. The date is drawn within the same Primary, the same half-hour of the day, and the same 21-day block of the year.

docs.title: Scoring and contrasts
docs.text:
• Test rows: the 60 days after each cutoff (the pretraining rows end 3.5 hours before it), so every test row postdates training. Targets include the step from 2023-04-01. Sunny half-hours: 10:00 to 15:00 UTC with a CAMS clear-sky index of at least 0.7.
  • C1: free minus cal, step world, sunny middays. C2: free minus cal, real world, all half-hours; support needs cal to lose at most 0.02. C3a, C3b: perm minus cal and shuf minus cal, step world, sunny middays. Also reported without a bar: raw and r4 against cal, oracle against cal, the contrasts in the real world, and the same contrasts on all half-hours.
  • Seeds and intervals: seeds 0 to 4, day-block bootstrap over test days with 2000 resamples. The MDE is defined in the decision rule.
  • Probe reads in two units: the probed step per injected megawatt and per injected megawatt-hour over the probe dates, using experiment 634's farm-to-curve energy ratios.
  • Stop: if C1 fails, the write-up reports that and no version with ensemble weather forecasts is planned.

docs.title: Changes after the plan review
docs.text:
• Table lookahead. Experiment 474's R4 table was fitted on the whole history. Each explicit network uses only season-years that ended before its cutoff (2024 and earlier at all three cutoffs, because a season-year ends in June) and holds the last value for later dates. The table's own fit still saw later months, so the write-up states this as a caveat.
  • What C1 tests. The free network has trained on two to three years of post-step rows, and k and D come from probing that same network. C1 therefore tests whether an explicit term built from the probed level forecasts at least as well as the network's own implicit level. It does not test tracking of a capacity that appeared shortly before the cutoff, and the write-up says so. A late-step world is not part of this plan.
  • Calibrated or raw. Dividing by the factor may overstate the PV energy, because the real farm carries 0.72 to 0.84 of the unit curve's energy. All of raw, cal, and oracle are reported on sunny middays, with each arm's implied PV energy against the injected energy. If raw beats cal, the write-up names raw as the better explicit arm, and C1 and C3 are repeated for it.
  • Minimum detectable effect. The null contrast and its split are computed and printed before any explicit network is fitted, at the same confidence level as the contrasts. If it exceeds 0.10 points, C1 is reported as unable to resolve the predicted gain.
  • Training detail. Explicit networks standardise the gross target with the net target's mean and standard deviation. The offset delta enters the gross target and trains by gradient. Validation for early stopping uses the mean capacity (no draw) with the current delta. The loop is experiment 634's train with that change only. Seeds 3 and 4 of the free networks use experiment 634's train unchanged.
  • Test rows. A new builder takes experiment 448's pretraining rows with the valid-time filter moved to the test window. It keeps one row per Primary and valid time (the first origin), excludes no purged week (the rows postdate training), and applies experiment 634's farm-gap mask. The free and explicit arms score the same rows.
  • Definitions. A sunny half-hour has x[:, 0] (the shortwave column) divided by the Haurwitz clear-sky value at least 0.7. Pooling weights every test row equally, in points of that Primary's effective capacity. C2 covers March to August only, so it says nothing about winter. The perm placebo shifts the table and the step increment together, and the shuf placebo is a sanity check.

docs.title: Review order
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet agent reviews the code before the first fit. A fresh Sonnet agent reviews the write-up against the printed report, and a second runs the prose review. An audit follows if a trigger in the ml-experiment skill fires (for example, a nested arm beating the arm that contains it, or a placebo that does not lose).

docs.title: How much worse does the demand network score the longer ago it was fitted: 0, 4, 8, 16, or 26 weeks before the forecast month?
docs.text:
A demand forecast made from an older fit scores worse, and the loss is largest at the two substations with the least training data. We refitted two neural-network demand forecasters for each of five development months (October 2025, December 2025, January 2026, March 2026, and June 2026). The training data of each fit ended 0, 4, 8, 16, or 26 weeks before the month started. We scored each fit on the whole month and compared the five fit ages. K1 is the forecaster that reads recent power readings, and K3 reads none. The K1 scored here does not include the gate that widens its band during load transfers. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, lower is better) over 16 Primary substations. At the 14 Primaries other than D15 and D18, K1's CRPS was 3.0% worse after 4 weeks and 6.3% worse after 8 weeks than for the fit made at the month's start, and the loss then rose to 10.0% at 16 weeks and fell back to 6.1% at 26 weeks (a wide interval). At D15 and D18, whose power history starts in March 2025, K1's CRPS was 17% worse after 4 weeks (pooled over the months) and about twice as bad after 26 weeks.

The limit set before the fits, a loss under 1% of CRPS for every 4 weeks of fit age, fails for both forecasters at all 16 Primaries and is not safely met at the other 14. The slope is the CRPS change per 4 weeks of fit age, as a percentage of the age-0 CRPS. At the 14 Primaries K1's slope is 1.0% (97.5% interval -0.2 to +1.8) and K3's is 1.0% (-0.3 to +2.3). It rises to 1.6% for K1 when the fits whose training history is short are left out, and K1's loss in the first 4 weeks is about 3% (K3's is 1.1%, with an interval that includes zero). The loss is not a straight line: it rises for 16 weeks and then falls.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Caption: at the 14 Primaries without D15 and D18, K1 scores 3.0% worse at 4 weeks and 10.0% worse at 16 weeks than at age 0, and the curve is flat or falling after that. At all 16 Primaries the loss reaches 35% for K1 at 26 weeks. Error bars are 97.5% month-block bootstrap intervals, and they are wide because they rest on 5 months.

Caption: at the 14 other Primaries the CRPS moves from 3.0 to 3.2 (K1) and from 3.4 to 3.5 (K3) percent of capacity between age 0 and 26 weeks, with peaks of 3.3 and 3.7 at 16 weeks. At D15 and D18 it doubles between the same ages, from 9.3 to 19.0 (K1) and from 8.8 to 20.2 (K3).

Caption: the slope is similar at every lead band, and K1 and K3 do not differ. At the 14 Primaries the intervals contain 1% at every band.

Caption: the 90% band holds 0.86 of the readings at age 0 and 0.79 (K1) or 0.77 (K3) at 26 weeks. Both forecasters are over-confident at every age.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Scored system. Each forecaster is scored on its own quantiles, without the gate that experiment 620 added to K1, because the gate's code is tied to month names. The scored rows are the rows that experiment 613 scored: 16 Primaries, event-free rows unless stated (rows outside any verified load transfer), leads 0 to 240 hours, seeds 0 to 2.
  • The reproduction check (P4) holds for K1. The age-0 K1 fit scores 0.03643 on the first 14 days of the five months, against 0.03677 for experiment 613's K1 without the gate, a ratio of 0.991 that lies inside the 1% tolerance. Experiment 613 refits on day 14 and uses five seeds, so only days 0 to 13 compare.
  • The limit of 1% per 4 weeks (P1) fails at 16 Primaries and is not safely met at 14. The table gives the slope in percent of the age-0 CRPS per 4 weeks, at leads of 0 to 240 hours, with 97.5% intervals.
Primaries K1 K3 All 16 5.4 (2.9 to 7.6) 6.2 (4.3 to 7.4) 14, without D15 and D18 1.0 (-0.2 to 1.8) 1.0 (-0.3 to 2.3)
  • CRPS above the age-0 fit at the 14 Primaries. The table gives percent with 97.5% intervals. The lower end of K1's 4-week interval is under 1%.
Fit age (weeks) K1 K3 4 +2.95 (0.92 to 5.25) +1.14 (-0.15 to 2.68) 8 +6.25 (1.78 to 11.96) +5.77 (2.61 to 9.90) 16 +9.97 (3.43 to 16.98) +11.32 (4.43 to 20.42) 26 +6.08 (-0.77 to 11.69) +4.62 (-1.65 to 12.76)
  • K1 does not lose more than K3 per 4 weeks (P2 fails). At 24 to 120 hours the slopes are 1.1 and 1.1 at the 14 Primaries, and 5.9 and 6.3 at all 16. In the first 4 weeks K1 loses more (+2.95% against +1.14%), but the intervals overlap.
  • P3 cannot be settled. Primary-months with a labelled load transfer lose 7.7% (K1; 2.2 to 16.0) per 4 weeks on event-free rows, against 4.8% (2.0 to 6.9) in Primary-months without one. The intervals overlap, and D15 and D18 contribute to both groups.
  • Absolute scores (percent of capacity, 16 Primaries, event-free rows). MAE is the mean absolute error of the median forecast. Coverage is the share of readings inside the q05-q95 band.
Fit age (weeks) K1 CRPS K1 MAE K1 coverage K3 CRPS K3 MAE K3 coverage 0 3.76 6.74 0.864 3.99 7.15 0.855 4 4.03 7.17 0.850 4.20 7.48 0.853 8 4.18 7.41 0.836 4.45 7.86 0.821 16 4.67 8.54 0.803 5.24 9.19 0.770 26 5.08 8.94 0.788 5.50 9.44 0.768
  • Tails. The pinball losses at q95 and q99 grow most with fit age (K1 q99: 0.0029 at age 0 and 0.0064 at 26 weeks), and the loss at q01 barely moves. An older fit therefore mainly misses upward excursions.
  • Not shown. Climatology and the manual heuristic are not scored at each fit age, because neither depends on the fit age of the neural network. Their scores are on experiment 613's page.

docs.title: What would change production
docs.text:
• Monthly refits are worth running for K1, and not shown to be for K3. At the 14 Primaries, K1's CRPS at 4 weeks of fit age exceeds the age-0 CRPS by 2.95%, with an interval above zero (0.92 to 5.25), and K3's exceeds it by 1.14% (-0.15 to 2.68). The lower end of K1's interval is under 1%.
  • Weekly refits are not shown to be worth more than monthly refits. The loss is about 3% in the first 4 weeks and flattens later, and this experiment ran no weekly refit, so it does not measure the extra gain of a weekly schedule.
  • D15 and D18 may need frequent refits. Their CRPS rises 17% (K1, pooled over the months) within 4 weeks. This experiment cannot say whether fit age, their short history, or level shifts in their power cause the rise.

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed, because the stored forecasts hold quantiles only. The mean absolute error of the median rises with fit age at the same rate as CRPS (K1 +33% and K3 +32% from age 0 to 26 weeks, against +35% and +38% for CRPS), so the two scores point the same way.
  • Audit triggers fired: trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) and trigger 4 (leaving D15 and D18 out changes the verdict of P1, and leaving out any one of three other Primaries moves the 14-Primary slope to 1.1 to 1.2). A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the numbers from the stored forecasts and reproduced them to within bootstrap noise, apart from the group-figure levels, and raised these findings, all accepted:
    • The verdict that P1 holds at the margin at 14 Primaries is fragile, so this page says P1 is not safely met there.
    • The leave-out of short-history fits raises K1's slope from 1.0% to 1.6% (0.7 to 3.2) at the 14 Primaries, so short history does not explain the loss there.
    • The D15 and D18 loss cannot be pinned on fit age or history length (next bullet).
    • No leakage was found. Two loaders (e00428_data.load_stack and prep422.cleaned_arrays) bypass the training-phase patch, and the audit found by grep that the chain never calls them, without tracing a run.
    • Averaging quantiles over seeds inflates the 16-Primary slope by about 0.2 points and changes no verdict.
    • P4 reproduces for K1 only: by month the ratio spans 0.972 to 1.019, and experiment 613 stores no K3 reference.
  • Fit age, history length, and level shifts are confounded at D15 and D18. Both Primaries start on 2025-03-01, so they have 1.0 month of cleaned power at the oldest cutoff of October 2025 and 3.0 months at that of December 2025, and never under 5.8 months for March and June 2026.
  • Their CRPS depends more on the test month than on fit age or history length. K1's age-0 CRPS at the two is 16.4% of capacity in March 2026 and 4.8% in January 2026. The audit found that the CRPS steps line up with level shifts in their raw power, so this page does not attribute their loss to any one cause.
  • The shorter history does not add to the loss at the 14 Primaries. The oldest cutoffs of the earliest months have fewer months of training rows, and leaving the October 2025 fits older than 16 weeks out raises K1's slope there from 1.0% to 1.6% (0.7 to 3.2).
  • Lab conditions. Each fit has no refit inside the month, so the oldest forecast origins are about 30 weeks after the fit. The gate is not in the scored K1. The synthetic load-shift events used in K1's fine-tuning are seeded from the development month, so every fit age of one month shares them.
  • Lead range. Scores cover leads of 0 to 240 hours, the range NGED care about.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Refit D15 and D18 monthly or more often in an experiment of their own, with a control that holds the number of training months fixed while the fit age varies, and a check of the level shifts in their power.
  • Add climatology and the manual heuristic to the headline chart after a run that scores K1 with the gate at each fit age.

docs.title: Registered plan (written before any fit)
docs.text:
• Question. The production service will refit on some schedule. Experiments 494 and 511 measured the price of an old fit on the lag-free network only, and the July to October window of experiment 620 used one fit with no refit, so its fit age rose from 0 to 17 weeks. This experiment measures the loss per 4 weeks of fit age on the development months, where an answer cannot touch the closed window.
  • Design. For each development test month (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06), fit K1 and K3 once with the cutoff A weeks before the month starts, for A = 0, 4, 8, 16, and 26. Each fit has no refit during the month, so the fit age of a forecast origin is A plus its days into the month, and the score by weeks since fit covers 0 to about 30 weeks. The recipe, seeds, 16 Primaries, and pretraining rules are experiment 613's. Pretraining reruns at each cutoff, with its newest row older than the cutoff by the usual refit age, as experiment 620's final fold does. Each fit's cleaned power is hidden after its cutoff, as in experiment 620's training phase, so no code path can read a later reading.
  • Cheapest recipe. One cutoff per fit and no day-14 refit, with seeds 0 to 2 in place of experiment 613's five (the recipe is otherwise experiment 613's, and the K1 seeds 0 and 1 are not bit-identical to 613's, which came from experiment 591's stored chain). From experiment 620's logs, K1 takes about 7.5 minutes per cutoff at 3 seeds and K3 about 4 to 5 minutes, so the 25 cutoffs cost about 5.5 to 6.5 GPU-hours with the prediction processes. That reaches the 6 GPU-hour ceiling, so the first cutoff of each network is timed before the chain starts, and the manager is asked before crossing the ceiling. Prediction P4 checks that the recipe reproduces the reference within 1%; if it fails, the page quotes only the contrast between ages.
  • History confound. The oldest cutoffs of the earliest months have less fine-tune history (about 12 months at 2025-10 with age 26, against about 18 at age 0), and D15 and D18 have under 3 months of cleaned power there. The slope is therefore also reported without D15 and D18, and with the 2025-10 fits older than 16 weeks left out. The synthetic load-shift events are seeded from the development month, so every age of one month shares them.
  • Scoring. Reuse experiment 613's scorer (e00613_score.py) for the cells by Primary, month, and lead band, with K1 assembled with the gate from the K3 fit of the same cutoff, and group the rows by weeks since the fit. Report separately the Primaries with a labelled event in the test month (NGED event labels, a lower bound because labels are incomplete) and the others. Quote the age-0 reference rows, climatology, and the manual heuristic beside the networks, and the tail table (q01, q05, q95, q99 coverage) beside the CRPS.
  • Standing practices followed. Cleaned data everywhere; the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01; models saved as .ubj or state files in the data folder; stored 613 predictions reused as the reference; the closed window (valid time from 2026-07-01) is never opened; the run is a screen on the development months, not a protocol change, so kind: other.
  • Compute. Ceiling 6 GPU-hours (process hours). One GPU process at a time, 8 GB host cap and one OMP thread, as experiment 620's gpu.sh does, and systemd-run with -p MemoryMax=8G -p OOMPolicy=continue.
  • Reporting. The headline chart is CRPS against weeks since the fit for K1, K3, climatology, and the manual heuristic, with month-block intervals. Further figures: slope per lead band, the event and non-event split, and per-month curves.

docs.title: What the plan said would change production
docs.text:
• If the slope interval's upper end is under 1% per 4 weeks, a refit every 4 to 8 weeks is enough, and the production service should not spend effort on weekly refits.
  • If the lower end exceeds 1% per 4 weeks, weekly or monthly refits are worth running, and the experiment names which by the age at which the loss passes 1%.

docs.title: What drives the forecast error at the Primary substations D15 and D12, and does a correction that needs no refit lower it without harming the other 14 Primaries?
docs.text: D15's forecast error is a one-sided bias that lasts for days but not weeks, and correcting for the previous 14 days of errors did not detectably fix it. The experiment asked why the forecasts of K1 (the lag-using neural network of the bake-off) are so wrong at two Primary substations, D15 and D12, and whether shifting K1's stored forecast by its own recent errors lowers the error without a refit. A shift that removed each day's bias exactly (an oracle, not usable in practice) would cut D15's continuous ranked probability score (CRPS; here the mean pinball loss over the 11 stored quantiles, times 2) by 48%. The shift that uses only past errors recovered 27% of that gap at D15, with an interval that includes zero, and raised the CRPS of the other 14 Primaries. At D12 the error is largest at midday, and the same shift did not lower it. The verdict is not supported.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
Rows. Leads of 24 to 240 hours, the cleaned observed_power of the stored export of experiments 612 and 613 (5 development months), all rows, and D15 rows from 2025-03-01 only. Errors are in percentage points of capacity, and bias is observed minus forecast. The export holds only cleaned readings, so no count of dropped half-hours is available per month.

  • D15 has the largest error. K1's mean absolute error of the median is 24.8 points at leads of 24 to 240 hours, against 2.6 to 14.1 at the other 15 Primaries. The bias is +15.4 points on average and +50.7 in March 2026, when 55% of readings lay above q95.
  • D15's error is flat across the hours and concentrated in a few days. The hourly mean absolute error runs from 23.4 to 26.9 points. The worst 5%, 10%, and 20% of days carry 19.3%, 31.2%, and 49.5% of D15's CRPS.
  • D15's bias lasts for days. The daily mean error has an autocorrelation of 0.81 at 1 day, 0.39 at 7 days, and 0.27 at 14 days. In March 2026 the median forecast was -1.34 MW and the median reading +0.32 MW (capacity 3.01 MW); the readings step up by about 1.5 MW on 8 to 9 March, so part of the March error is a step that K1's lags had not yet followed. Of the 10 days flagged as level shifts (more than 3 robust standard deviations from the previous 28 days), 70% carry no event label in the export.
  • K3 beats K1 at D15. The CRPS is 14.53 for K1, 15.05 for the Candidate (+3.6%, worse than K1), and 13.58 for K3, the neural network that reads no recent power (-6.5%, better than K1). K3 is worse than K1 at D12 (+7.0%) and at other Primaries, so D15 may be a special case.
  • D12's error peaks at midday. The mean absolute error is 18.9 points at 10:00 to 14:00 local time against 9.3 at 00:00 to 04:00. The bias is +4 at 05:00 and -5 at 17:00 and +8 in December 2025, and the worst 20% of days carry 32.2% of the CRPS. Its daily bias autocorrelation falls to 0.19 at 7 days. Its apparent-power meter folds reverse flow (experiment 152).
  • Nearby metered series. The nearest series in the TimeSeriesMetadata table to each Primary are photovoltaic, 4 to 7 km away. No generator output is drawn here.

docs.title: Fixes scored (K1's stored forecasts, leads 24 to 240 hours)
docs.text:
Both fixes shift all 11 quantiles by an amount known 24 hours before the origin. F1 is the mean error of K1's 24 to 48 hour forecasts over the 14 days up to that time, per Primary. F2 is the same mean per half-hour of the local day. F1 was applied to 92% of rows; the other rows had no known error in the previous 3 days and keep K1 unchanged. A unit test adds 1000 MW to every reading after 2026-03-15 09:00 and checks that the shift of every origin up to 24 hours later is unchanged, and that later origins do change.

Quantity (change in CRPS against K1; negative is better) D15 D12 Other 14 Primaries K1 CRPS (% of capacity) 14.53 6.90 1.4 to 7.7 F1, 14-day level term -12.9% (-34.0 to +4.8) +5.5% (-2.0 to +17.0) +4.7% (+0.6 to +10.1) F2, per half-hour level term -13.1% (-33.8 to +3.5) +5.9% (-1.5 to +16.9) +4.5% (+0.6 to +9.8) Oracle, each day's bias removed (a bound, not causal) -47.9% -16.4% -8% to -47% Candidate +3.6% (+1.3 to +6.6) -0.0% (-2.4 to +2.0) not computed K3 -6.5% (-11.5 to -1.7) +7.0% (+3.3 to +11.5) not computed

Intervals are 95% over week-long blocks.

  • Not supported. The rule needs an interval that excludes zero and a gain of at least 5%, with the other 14 Primaries not worse by more than 1%. F1 and F2 meet none of these at D12 or at the other 14, and D15's interval includes zero.
  • The oracle shows the headroom is real but fast-moving. Perfect knowledge of each day's bias leaves D15's CRPS at 52% of K1's, and F1 recovers 27% of that gap.
  • Predictions. P1 (half of D15's error on at most 20% of days) failed narrowly: 49.5%. P2 (midday error at least twice the night error at D12) held: 2.04. P3 (a gain of at least 5% with the interval excluding zero) failed. P4 (no harm of more than 1% to the other 14) failed: +4.7%.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site. Not computed, because the export holds 11 quantiles and no mean forecast.
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrast. The mean absolute error of the median moves in the same direction as the CRPS: -12.9% at D15, +4.5% at D12, and +3.5% at the other 14 Primaries.
  • Audit triggers. None fired. No control or placebo was run (trigger 1). The failed predictions P3 and P4 contradict no earlier finding of a stored-forecast level term (trigger 2; experiments 149 and 500 found recent-level gains only post hoc). The CRPS and median-error contrasts agree (trigger 3). There are no nested arms and no sister-experiment interval to compare (triggers 4 to 6), and no later experiment depends on the headline (trigger 7).
  • Reviews. One Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review (it found a causal unit test that tested nothing, which was rewritten and passes, and the pooled-row interval, now saved to a table), and one Sonnet prose review. The accepted findings were applied. Comparisons the plan listed and the experiment did not run are under "Not done".

docs.title: Not done
docs.text:
• Weather regime, step sizes, the neighbour comparison, and midday error against sunshine were not computed. The persist-the-last-error and best-of-network comparisons were not run, because the oracle and the two stored alternatives already showed that D15's gap is not recoverable from recent errors at 14 days. The transfer-aware and generator-aware fixes were not tested, because the diagnosis did not isolate a transfer flag or a generator behind either Primary.
  • MAE, coverage, and pinball loss beyond CRPS were not scored for the fixes. K1's q95 is exceeded by 14.6% of D15's readings and 4.5% of D12's (nominal 5%).
  • The example figure shows one 10-day forecast per Primary; the horizon is 240 hours.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Selection. D15 and D12 were chosen as the largest errors in the same 5 months the fixes are scored on, so every number is interim.
  • Cleaning. observed_power is cleaned with the whole table, so the correction sees slightly cleaner recent readings than production would.
  • Scope. The result covers 5 development months, one trailing window, and 2 Primaries. D15 has 4 usable months after its cut.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so rows without a label can hold events and counts of events are lower bounds.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• D15. Find out why K1's median is about 1.7 MW below the readings in March 2026, and compare K3 with K1 using an interval. A generator behind the Primary and the power lags are untested guesses.
  • D12. Test the midday error against sunshine and against the fold of the apparent-power reading.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: • ml-experiments/00641-d15-d12-error-diagnosis-and-cheapest-fixes/: e00641_diagnose.py, e00641_fixes.py, and e00641_figures.py. Tables are in data/ml-experiments/00641-d15-d12-error-diagnosis-and-cheapest-fixes/tables/. No model was fitted or saved.

docs.title: Can a correction fitted on other months bring the upper demand tail of K1 and the Candidate within 1.5 percentage points of nominal without raising CRPS by more than 1%?
docs.text:
Shifting each stored demand forecast to the level of recent weeks, and then widening its upper range, comes closest to fixing the too-low upper end of the forecasts, but no correction fitted without the held-out month passes the bar registered in the plan. We asked whether five corrections, each fitted on other months, can bring two shares close to their nominal values. The first share is the half-hour readings above a forecast's 90th percentile (q90, nominal 10%), and the second is the readings above its 95th percentile (q95, nominal 5%). The forecasts are the stored output of three neural networks for 16 primary substations (Primaries): K1 (reads power from 24 hours or more before the forecast), the Candidate (the same, plus summaries of the neighbouring Primaries' power), and K3 (reads no recent power). Experiment 630 found that K1 and the Candidate exceed those percentiles too often, on ordinary days as well as around load-shifts (NGED moving demand from one Primary to a neighbour). We tested the corrections on five test months (October 2025, December 2025, January 2026, March 2026, and June 2026). Each correction was fitted on the other four months, with the held-out month and the 10 days around it removed from the fitting rows, and scored on the held-out month. The corrections change the stored forecasts only, and no neural network was refitted. "Event-free" half-hours are those with no labelled or verified load-shift within 7 days at that Primary. D15 and D18 are the two Primaries with a short history. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, the quantile score of the whole forecast, and a CRPS ratio above 1 means the corrected forecast scores worse than the stored one.

  • Verdict partly supported. The registered bar needs, per network, an arm whose pooled event-free q90 exceedance lies in 8.5% to 11.5%, whose q95 lies in 3.5% to 6.5%, whose CRPS is at most 1.01 times the uncorrected network's, and whose q90 exceedance lies in 7% to 13% in every held-out month. On 16 Primaries arm M passes the first three conditions for K1 (11.4%, 6.4%, 1.000) and misses the first two for the Candidate (11.7%, 6.6%, 0.992). Every arm fails the month condition, so no arm passes in full. The rule gives partly supported when an arm passes the first two conditions and fails another, and arm M (the arm with the smallest distance from both nominal levels) is the best arm. The month failure and the neutral CRPS both come from D15 and D18. On the 14 Primaries without them, arm M keeps every month between 9.2% and 12.5% above q90 and passes the q90, q95, and month conditions, but its CRPS ratio is 1.021 (K1) and 1.016 (Candidate), above 1.01. The pre-registered bar gates on all 16 Primaries, so the verdict stands.
  • Arms (all fitted on event-free rows of the other four months; held-out lead 0 to 240 hours, the whole 1 day to 10 day range that NGED uses). S: a scale per Primary on the distance above the median of every upper quantile (fitted scales per Primary, averaged over folds, 0.87 to 1.63, median 1.09 for the Candidate). B: S, then a scale pooled over Primaries per lead band and 4-hour block of valid time. C: a rolling conformal adjustment of each upper quantile from the previous 56 days. Q: quantile mapping of the whole distribution per Primary and lead band. M: a shift of every quantile by the median error of the previous 28 days, then S refitted on the shifted forecasts. Corrections S, B, and Q are fitted on later as well as earlier months (a lab design); C and M use only residuals from before the forecast was issued.
  • Row set. The five development months, roster_export_2026-11-07_dev_months: 905,502 event-free rows per network of 1,140,221 (asserted against experiment 630). The July to October 2026 window was not opened. Every development month is later than 2025-03-01, so the D15 and D18 cut removes no row. Event-free rows are the export's event_free rows, and NGED's logs may miss events, so event-free rows can hold unlogged load-shifts.
  • Pooled event-free exceedance, with 95% intervals from resampling origin days (nominal: 10% and 5%; CRPS in MW or MVA; K1 uncorrected CRPS 0.2447, Candidate 0.2477):
Forecast and arm Above q90 Above q95 CRPS ratio to uncorrected K1, uncorrected 14.7% (14.1, 15.3) 8.4% (7.9, 8.9) 1 K1, S 11.9% (11.3, 12.5) 7.1% (6.6, 7.6) 1.027 (1.024, 1.030) K1, B 12.1% (11.5, 12.7) 7.2% (6.8, 7.7) 1.027 (1.024, 1.030) K1, C 14.8% (14.2, 15.5) 9.2% (8.7, 9.7) 1.012 (1.003, 1.021) K1, Q 12.1% (11.5, 12.7) 7.3% (6.8, 7.8) 1.055 (1.051, 1.059) K1, M 11.4% (10.8, 12.0) 6.4% (6.0, 6.8) 1.000 (0.985, 1.016) Candidate, uncorrected 13.2% (12.6, 13.8) 7.2% (6.8, 7.7) 1 Candidate, S 12.1% (11.5, 12.7) 7.3% (6.8, 7.8) 1.033 (1.031, 1.036) Candidate, B 12.2% (11.6, 12.8) 7.3% (6.8, 7.7) 1.033 (1.031, 1.036) Candidate, C 14.8% (14.1, 15.5) 9.2% (8.7, 9.8) 1.012 (1.002, 1.022) Candidate, Q 12.2% (11.7, 12.9) 7.5% (7.0, 8.0) 1.064 (1.059, 1.068) Candidate, M 11.7% (11.1, 12.3) 6.6% (6.2, 7.0) 0.992 (0.976, 1.008)
  • Month-block intervals. Resampling the five held-out months with replacement gives much wider intervals, because five months are few: the Candidate's arm M q90 is 11.7% (10.0, 13.6), its q95 6.6% (5.5, 8.0), and its CRPS ratio 0.992 (0.939, 1.051). The bar uses the point estimates, so these intervals are descriptive.
  • By month. On the 14 Primaries without D15 and D18, the Candidate's q90 exceedance, uncorrected and for arm M, is: October 12.0% and 9.2%; December 13.7% and 10.8%; January 14.2% and 11.3%; March 13.2% and 12.4%; June 10.1% and 11.9% (K1: 9.6% to 12.5% for arm M). S, B, and Q reach 9.4% to 9.5% in June, an overcorrection. At D15 and D18, March is 45.5% (Candidate) and 45.9% (K1) above q90 uncorrected and 30.2% to 32.2% for arm M, while the other months are 2% to 22%. On all 16 Primaries March therefore stays at 17.1% to 17.8% for every arm except M (15.1%).
  • Cold nights. The Candidate's q90 exceedance on cold nights (18:00 to 06:00 UTC, coldest third of ensemble temperatures) is 16.4% uncorrected against 12.4% elsewhere. Arm M brings it to 12.3% against 11.5%, and S leaves it at 15.1%. K1: 17.6% against 14.1% uncorrected, and 11.9% against 11.3% for arm M.
  • Metering groups (Candidate, event-free). The eight MVA Primaries: 11.3% and 5.9% uncorrected, 10.0% and 5.4% for arm M (CRPS ratio 1.025). The six MW Primaries: 14.6% and 8.1% uncorrected, 12.9% and 7.2% for arm M (CRPS ratio 1.001). The two report-only Primaries (D15 and D18): 17.0% and 10.6% uncorrected, 15.2% and 10.5% for arm M (CRPS ratio 0.845). On the 14 Primaries without D15 and D18, uncorrected, S, and M give q90 and q95 exceedance of 12.7% and 6.8%, 11.5% and 6.5%, and 11.2% and 6.1% for the Candidate, and 14.2% and 8.0%, 11.3% and 6.4%, and 11.0% and 5.9% for K1. Their CRPS ratios are 1.014 (S) and 1.016 (M) for the Candidate and 1.010 (S) and 1.021 (M) for K1, so arm M raises CRPS by 0.2 to 1.1 points more than S for a q95 closer to nominal. At D15 and D18 alone, arm M improves CRPS by 13% to 15% (ratio 0.845 to 0.866) and S worsens it by 13% to 15%.
  • Arm C. The rolling conformal adjustment raised q90 exceedance from 13.6% to 15.6% on the rows it corrected (86% of event-free rows; in October 55% of rows are corrected, because the previous 56 days hold too few residuals). The adjustment at q90 averages −0.016 MW with a standard deviation of 0.34 MW across rows and is positive on 44.5% of rows, so it behaves as noise. The code recovers the nominal level on stationary synthetic data (15.2% before, 11.2% after), so the failure comes from the forecasts, as in experiment 500, and not from a coding fault.
  • Tail and lower-tail effect. The shift in arm M moves the whole distribution, so its lower tail moves too: the share below q05 rises from 3.4% to 5.2% (Candidate) and from 4.6% to 6.5% (K1), and the share below q10 from 7.7% to 9.9% and 9.3% to 11.6%. Quantile mapping (Q) raises the Candidate's share below q05 to 6.6%. Only the q05, q10, q90, and q95 levels were scored. The threshold-weighted CRPS (threshold: the 95th percentile of the fitting rows' power at each Primary) rises by 9.5% (S) and 1.0% (M) for the Candidate and by 7.6% (S) and 0.2% (M) for K1.
  • Curtailment cost (the protocol's avoidable curtailment cost, node-only, 12 to 36 hour leads, six signed-MW Primaries, limit as a fraction of each Primary's earlier maximum, summed over the five months; no interval was computed). At limit fraction 0.9, arm M changes the cost by −10.4% (Candidate) and −12.2% (K1), and S by −7.4% and −10.5%. At 0.5, arm M changes it by −6.0% and −8.8% and S by +10.8% and +6.0%. The cost falls for arm M at every fraction tried for K1 and the Candidate, and for arm C too (−5.2% to −14.0%).
  • Pre-registered predictions. P1 failed (no arm passes). P2 failed in its first half: C and M corrected 86% and 77% of event-free rows, above the predicted 70% limit, and held in part of its second half (C misses by more than S; M does not). P3 failed: Q raised the Candidate's share below q05 from 3.4% to 6.6%, past nominal, and gave the largest CRPS rise (+6.4%). P4 held on 16 Primaries for March (above 12% for every arm, a result that D15 and D18 produce) and for June for S, B, and Q, not for C or M. P5 held for the metering groups and for K3 (median fitted scale per Primary 1.25, against 1.15 for K1 and 1.10 for the Candidate); the curtailment part was not tested (no interval).
  • Reviews. One Sonnet plan review found a leak through valid times overlapping the held-out month, an in-sample Candidate band width, a pooled bar that lets months cancel, undefined minimum sizes, and weak predictions; the plan was revised before any run. One Sonnet code review before the first scored run found a leak in arm M (training shifts computed from a window that included the held-out month), fixed before the run; its other findings (ties, crossings) cannot occur in the stored quantiles. A Sonnet review of the results and the write-up reproduced the numbers and found that arm M's neutral CRPS and the March failure both come from D15 and D18, that the Candidate with arm M also misses the q95 limit, and a wrong statement about quantile mapping and the median; the write-up, the headline, the advice, and figure 2 were rewritten to show the 14 Primaries separately.
  • Checks. The median error: arm M lowers the mean of observed power minus q50 from 0.0975 to 0.0464 MW (K1) and cuts the median's absolute error by 0.8% (K1, 0.4414 to 0.4380 MW) and by 1.9% (Candidate, 0.4477 to 0.4390 MW), in the same direction as its CRPS ratio, and arms S and B leave the median unchanged while Q worsens its absolute error by about 4%, so trigger 3 does not fire. The export holds no mean forecast, so the median-minus-mean check does not apply. Trigger 2 did not fire: P1 failed, but the by-month, by-group, cold-night, and arm C diagnostics above test the explanation. No other trigger applies, so no audit ran.
  • Caveats. The Candidate's band width factor was set on the months it is scored on (experiment 613), so its uncorrected row is optimistic and K1 is the cleaner reference. Intervals resample origin days that share weather, so they are somewhat too narrow. Five months cannot separate a seasonal bias from a trend. Corrections S, B, and Q are not causal, because they use later months. The temperature third labels rows only, and comes from the ensemble mean of the latest run (a near-analysis proxy). The unlogged-event caveat applies to every event-free number. The page re-scores stored forecasts with no refit, so retraining cadence does not apply; the absolute scores are those of experiment 613's stored networks, and no comparison to BG2, the manual heuristic, or climatology is made here.
  • What the next experiment should answer. How D15 and D18 should be corrected, since their level changed in March 2026, and whether a shift applied to the upper quantiles only keeps arm M's q95 gain without its 2% CRPS rise; test it before opening the July to October 2026 window.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00642-roster-upper-tail-correction-out-of-sample-leave-one-month-out/ (e00642_arms.py, e00642_score.py, e00642_report.py, e00642_cost.py, e00642_checks.py, e00642_figures.py); imports e00630_common from experiment 630's folder; tables in the experiment's private data folder.

docs.title: The explicit solar term beats two fixed bias corrections, but a correction from recent errors beats it
docs.text:
The explicit solar network beat both bias corrections that the plan fixed in advance, so the rule set in the plan says to build an ensemble-weather version. That result is not safe to act on alone. Neither pre-registered correction could see a bias that appears after training. A correction from the previous 14 days' errors, added after the results, forecast real sunny middays better than the explicit network.

We asked whether the gain of experiment 639 came from telling a demand neural network the solar capacity behind each Primary substation, or only from the plain network's sunny-midday forecast running too high. The plain network, called the free network, learns the solar response from weather alone. The explicit network is told each Primary substation's solar capacity and subtracts a physics solar curve of that capacity. Both forecast demand with the solar output netted off. Sunny middays are the half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC when the ratio of observed to clear-sky irradiance is at least 0.7. The error measure is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in percentage points of each Primary substation's solar capacity, and a smaller value is better.

We scored the 60 days after each of three training cutoffs in two worlds. The real months use the recorded demand. The step world adds 4 MW of a real solar farm's output to the demand of each Primary substation from April 2023. In the real months the CRPS on sunny middays was 3.30 for the explicit network and 4.05 for the plain free network. A free network shifted by a constant fitted on training months scored 3.99, and a free network with a trainable offset scored 4.02. The explicit network beat both corrections by about 0.7 points. The smallest gain that counts (the bar, from experiment 639) is 0.067 points. A free network corrected by its own mean error over the previous 14 days (the 14-day tracker), a control added after the results, scored 2.81 and beat the explicit network by 0.48 points. The capacity-swap placebo, where each Primary substation gets another one's capacity, lost by less than its bar of 0.181 points. The hypothesis is partly supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Both pre-registered corrections leave most of the gap. Each entry is the arm's CRPS minus the explicit network's, in points on sunny middays, so a positive value favours the explicit network. Intervals are day-block bootstraps at the 99% level (95%, Bonferroni-corrected over five contrasts).
