The bars are experiment 639's minimum detectable effects: 0.067 in the real months and 0.181 in the step world.

Arm minus explicit Real, sunny Step, sunny Free network (plain) +0.75 [0.50, 1.03] +2.90 [2.14, 3.67] Free, shifted by a training-month constant (C1, C3) +0.70 [0.45, 0.96] +3.64 [2.79, 4.47] Free, trainable sunny-midday offset (C2, C4) +0.72 [0.48, 0.98] +3.11 [2.33, 3.89] Free, shifted in hindsight by the test window's own error (bound) -0.52 [-0.66, -0.38] +0.90 [0.51, 1.29] Free, 14-day tracker (post hoc) -0.48 [-0.66, -0.30] +0.72 [0.39, 1.03]

Absolute CRPS on sunny middays, real months then step world: explicit 3.30 and 6.09; plain free 4.05 and 8.99; training-month constant 3.99 and 9.73; trainable offset 4.02 and 9.20; hindsight shift 2.78 and 6.99; 14-day tracker 2.81 and 6.81. On all half-hours in the real months the two pre-registered corrections lose to the explicit network by +0.13 [0.07, 0.18] and +0.14 [0.09, 0.20].

  • C1 and C2 hold, and the plan's rule is met. The explicit network beats both corrections in the real months by about 10 times the bar. The rule fixed in the plan recommends building the ensemble-weather version and naming its cost. The cost is a new row builder with forecast leads, a probe and capacity table per cutoff, and a refit per lead band, which is more than the experiment 639 pipeline's roughly 1.8 GPU-hours. The Checks section gives reasons not to act on that recommendation yet, and the maintainer decides.
  • The gain was larger than predicted. The plan predicted 0.3 to 0.6 points and expected the hindsight shift to close most of the gap. The observed gains are 0.70 and 0.72, and the hindsight shift beats the explicit network by 0.52.
  • C3 and C4 (no bar). In the step world the training-month constant makes the free network worse than the plain one: its gap to the explicit network is 3.64 against 2.90 for the plain network, a difference of 0.74.
  • C5, the placebo, is decided: below the bar. The mean over five permutations of the capacity timelines loses to the explicit network by +0.05 [-0.00, +0.10], and the upper end is under 0.181. The five shifts give +0.09, +0.14, +0.05, +0.05, and -0.08. The placebo does not support the claim that each Primary substation's own capacity matters.

Red line: the 0.181 bar. Dashed line: zero.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Neither pre-registered correction can see the bias. The free network's sunny-midday median forecast runs too high by +4.1 points of capacity in the real months and +8.3 in the step world. The constants fitted on the held-out training weeks are -0.6 to +1.4 points (real) and -5.6 to +0.5 (step), because the network was chosen on those weeks. The training-month constant moves the real-months bias only from +4.11 to +3.84, and the step-world bias from +8.30 to +10.16. The learned offsets of the trainable-offset network are 0.016 to 0.085 MW, close to zero. The explicit network's bias is +0.61 points (real) and -0.87 points (step).
  • The bias appears after training. The hindsight shift (fitted on the test window) and the 14-day tracker (fitted only on earlier days of the window) both beat the explicit network in the real months, by 0.52 and 0.48. The tracker scores 2.81, beside 2.78 for the hindsight shift. The tracker is a post hoc control: it was added after the audit found that the pre-registered controls could not see the bias. It is unaudited, it has no pre-registered bar, and it uses power observed on the previous days of the window, which a forecast made 1 to 10 days ahead may lack.
  • The step-world comparison favours the explicit network by construction. A tracker with a 14-day window adjusts slowly to the injected 4 MW step, so the explicit network's +0.72 lead over the tracker there does not show that the capacity table or the probe adds value.
  • One Primary substation carries the real-world gain. By Primary substation, the training-month constant minus the explicit network is -0.43, -0.31, +3.31, +0.78, +0.36, and +0.34. Without the Primary substation at +3.31, C1 is +0.14 [-0.03, +0.33], which is not a gain, and C2 is +0.25 [0.07, 0.45]. Two Primary substations score better with the free network. By cutoff, C1 is +0.75, +0.85, and +0.24.
  • Why the placebo is weak. The injected 4 MW is the same at every Primary substation, and the probed step is 3.1 to 3.8 MW, so swapping timelines changes at most about 0.7 MW of about 3.4. Falling below the 0.181 bar does not show that each Primary substation's own capacity is irrelevant. A placebo with capacities scaled by 0.5 and 1.5 would decide that.
  • Error of the median forecast beside CRPS. The mean absolute error of the median forecast on sunny middays, real months then step world, is 4.44 and 8.37 for the explicit network, 5.81 and 11.74 for the plain free network, 5.73 and 12.97 for the training-month constant, and 5.76 and 12.13 for the trainable offset. The direction matches the CRPS. The median minus the approximate mean (from the 11 quantiles) is -0.17, -0.17, -0.15, and +0.02 points in the real months for the plain free network, the constant, the offset, and the explicit network, and -4.30, -4.30, -4.22, and -0.38 in the step world.
  • Triggers and audit. An audit ran (private report e643_audit_report.md), because the capacity-swap placebo did not lose and because a later experiment's design depends on the sign. The audit re-derived the CRPS of the explicit network, the plain free network, and both pre-registered controls, the contrasts C1 to C5, and a leave-one-Primary-out table, with its own code. It found no lookahead in the rows, and did not examine the hindsight shift or the 14-day tracker. Triage:
    • Accepted: the pre-registered controls cannot see a bias that appears after training, so the page states it and adds the 14-day tracker, labelled post hoc.
    • Accepted: the placebo is weak by construction, and one Primary substation carries the real-world gain. Both are stated above.
    • Not applied: a placebo with scaled capacities. It belongs to the next experiment.
    • Not checked here: whether the probes behind the capacity parameters read only data before the cutoff. Experiment 639's audit covered that.
  • Fits. Only stage 1 ran, because the placebo was decided: 30 trainable-offset fits and 60 permutation fits. A code review before the first fit found that the offset could never leave zero under experiment 639's floor at zero, and the fix is in place.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Recorded weather, not forecasts, and no lead. The weather is ERA5 and CAMS at the valid time, so the 1 to 10 day range that the network operator (NGED) cares about is untested, as in experiment 639.
  • The 14-day tracker is a hindcast. In the first days of each window it has fewer than 14 days of errors, and its use in production needs the previous days' metered power at forecast time.
  • Three cutoffs. The windows are 60, 60, and 30 days starting at the cutoffs, with 4,397 sunny rows pooled over six Primary substations.
  • The recommendation. The rule fixed in the plan recommends the ensemble-weather version. The post hoc tracker and the one-Primary dependence argue for testing the tracker first. That departs from the rule, so the maintainer decides.
  • Not reported. Stage 2, because the placebo was decided.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does the explicit solar term beat a 14-day tracker once the weather is an ensemble forecast, and does a placebo with wrong capacities of a size that matters lose? Add the tracker, with and without an explicit curve, to the step world and the real months, and give each Primary substation a capacity scaled by 0.5 and 1.5 as the placebo.

docs.title: Plan (pre-registered)
docs.text:
Written before any result existed. The trailing 14-day tracker was added afterwards and is not part of it.

We ask whether a demand neural network that is told a Primary substation's solar capacity forecasts sunny middays better than a network that learns the solar response from irradiance, or whether the gain of experiment 639 is only that the free network's sunny-midday forecast runs too high. We give the free network two bias corrections that use no capacity information, and compare the explicit network with each.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All networks, rows, cutoffs, worlds, and seeds are experiment 639's. The free and explicit networks are read from its stored weights and quantiles. Only the arms below are new.

  • fbias: a constant fitted on training months. For each free network (cutoff, world, seed) and each of the six Primaries, take the mean of the median forecast's error (forecast minus actual) on the sunny-midday rows of the held-out weeks of the training data, and subtract that from every quantile of the network's sunny-midday test forecasts. The held-out weeks are the early-stopping rows, which the network did not fit directly.
  • foff: a trainable sunny-midday offset. Train a new free network (experiment 639's loop, train_explicit) on the target y + delta_p * inc * s, where s is 1 on sunny middays and 0 elsewhere, and delta_p is a trainable offset in megawatts for each of the six Primaries (six parameters, the same number as the explicit term's offset, with the same prior of 0.25 MW). At forecast time subtract delta_p * inc * s. This is the explicit network with no physics curve, no capacity table, and no probed capacity.
  • fhind: the hindsight bound (not eligible for the decision). Shift each free network's sunny-midday forecast by its own mean median error on the test window, per cutoff and Primary. Experiment 639 computed this once on the pooled rows; here it is a per-arm score with an interval.
  • perm shifts 1 to 5. The explicit network with the capacity timelines of the six Primaries cyclically shifted by one to five places (experiment 639 used two). Shift 3 swaps three pairs. Capacity parameters are experiment 639's cal parameters, rearranged as in its perm arm.

docs.title: Contrasts
docs.text:
• C1: fbias minus cal, real world, sunny middays. C2: foff minus cal, same rows.
  • C3, C4: the same two contrasts in the step world (4 MW added from 2023-04-01).
  • C5: the mean over shifts of perm minus cal, step world.
  • Also reported, without a bar: free minus cal (to reproduce experiment 639), fhind minus cal, each contrast on all half-hours, and the median forecast minus the mean forecast.

docs.title: Standing practices followed and departed from
docs.text:
• Followed: cleaned data, the D15 and D18 cut, saved weights, reuse of stored networks and predictions, a paired contrast on identical rows, five seeds, development months only, anonymised generators (farms A to F by letter), CAMS and ERA5 weather only, six MW Primaries only.
  • Departed from: monthly refits (one fit per cutoff, as in experiments 634 and 639); the load-shift slices (no event is injected); the screen on four test months (three cutoffs); the forecast-example plots (recorded weather has no lead, so one example week is shown).
  • Earlier advice followed: the shifted-free-network control and a placebo with an MDE below the expected loss (both from experiment 639's advice).

docs.title: Review order
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet agent reviews the code before the first fit. A fresh Sonnet agent checks the write-up against the printed report, and a second runs the prose review. An audit follows if a trigger in the ml-experiment skill fires.

docs.title: The solar capacity does not help the forecast, but a 14-day error correction does
docs.text:
Telling the neural network that forecasts a Primary substation's demand the solar capacity behind that substation makes its forecast for 10:00 to 15:00 UTC on clear days worse than the same network without the capacity, once the weather inputs are ensemble forecasts. A correction that adds the network's own mean error over the previous 14 days makes the same forecast better, by 0.3 to 0.6 continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) points of capacity. We therefore stop testing whether to give the network the solar capacity, and the 14-day correction is the method to test next.

Experiment 639 gave a neural network the solar capacity behind each Primary substation and had it subtract a physics solar curve. That experiment used estimates of past weather (CAMS and ERA5). We asked whether its gain holds with forecast weather: the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) ensemble, at leads 0 to 240 hours. The free network learns the solar response from weather alone. The explicit network is told the capacity (arm b uses a capacity calibrated against injected solar farms, arm c the raw probed capacity, and arm f the table of experiment 474). The 14-day tracker (arm d) is the free network plus its own mean error over the previous 14 days, as in experiment 643. Arm e shifts the free network by a constant fitted on held-out fine-tuning rows. The step world adds 4 MW of a real solar farm's output to every Primary substation's demand from April 2023. We scored the six MW Primaries on sunny middays (10:00 to 15:00 UTC, observed clear-sky index at least 0.7, the ratio of observed to clear-sky irradiance) in the 60 days after each of three cutoff dates (the last day the network is pretrained on), with five seeds. CRPS is in percent of each Primary's effective capacity ("points"), and smaller is better.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Real months, sunny middays Day 1-2 Day 3-5 Day 6-10 Free network (a) 3.75 4.28 5.05 Explicit, calibrated capacity (b) 4.11 4.53 5.33 Explicit, raw capacity (c) 3.92 4.41 5.24 Explicit, table capacity (f) 3.99 4.44 5.23 14-day tracker (d) 3.41 3.82 4.48 Free + training-month constant (e) 4.30 4.94 5.81 Capacity-permuted placebo 4.19 4.63 5.39 Shuffled-day placebo 5.40 5.60 6.09
  • The explicit network does not beat the free network at any lead band. Free network minus explicit network is -0.37 [-0.54, -0.20], -0.25 [-0.45, -0.08], and -0.27 [-0.40, -0.14] at the three bands (negative favours the free network; intervals are 99.7% day-block bootstraps, Bonferroni over 19 contrasts). The best of d and e (d at every band) beats the explicit network by 0.71, 0.71, and 0.84.
  • Over all half-hours the two networks tie. The explicit network is 0.007 points worse [-0.04, +0.03]. The point estimate is inside the planned 0.02 limit and the interval's upper end is not.
  • In the step world the explicit network does not beat the free network or the tracker. It ties the free network (-0.45 [-0.99, +0.05], -0.20 [-0.63, +0.19], +0.04 [-0.35, +0.38]) and loses to the tracker by 1.2 to 1.3 points. In this test the 4 MW step lies wholly before the ensemble rows begin. The contrast therefore tests carrying capacity from pretraining to fine-tuning, not tracking a step.
  • The explicit network barely beats a wrong capacity. The explicit network beats the capacity-permuted placebo by 0.08, 0.10, and 0.07 points. That is below the bar at day 1-2 (0.084) and day 6-10 (0.123) and marginally above it at day 3-5 (0.097 against 0.093), so the explicit network's small edge over a wrong capacity is not established. It beats the shuffled-day placebo by 0.8 to 1.3. The bars are recomputed per band as the larger of experiment 639's value (0.067 real, 0.181 step) and the seed-split null on these rows: 0.084, 0.093, and 0.123 in the real months; 0.205, 0.246, and 0.266 in the step world.
  • The 14-day tracker's intervals are the best calibrated. Coverage of the 5% to 95% quantile interval on sunny middays (nominal 90%) is 88.0% (a), 89.2% (b), 91.9% (d), and 82.3% (e). The mean absolute error of the median over all sunny-midday leads, in points of capacity, is 6.33 (a), 6.67 (b), 5.58 (d), and 7.37 (e).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Two review conditions fired: a placebo that should lose to the explicit network does not, and the result contradicts experiment 639. A fresh Sonnet sub-agent re-derived the CRPS contrasts from the stored quantiles and could not break them. The explicit network is worse at all 10 lead days and in all five seeds at lead days 1-2. Every contrast keeps its sign when one Primary is left out in turn. The per-cutoff signs are not uniform: the 2026-06 cutoff at day 3-5 favours b by 0.06.
  • Tested explanation: the sub-agent tested whether the smooth ensemble-mean curve hurts on days the ensemble calls cloudy. The loss appears at every forecast-sunniness level, so that explanation is not supported. The ensemble spread was not available to the sub-agent, so a spread explanation is untested.
  • Median minus mean forecast per site: not computed, because only the 11 quantiles are stored, so a skew in the forecasts is unchecked.
  • Not audited: the 14-day tracker (d) and the constant shift (e), which are post-processing in e00644_analyse.py. Both are applied on realised-sunny half-hours, a selection a production tracker would not have.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: **** Does the 14-day tracker still beat the free network when it is applied by forecast sunniness instead of observed sunniness, and does a shuffled-error placebo fail to match it? The explicit capacity term is not worth further work in this form.

docs.title: Departures and caveats
docs.text:
• The cached ensemble tables hold the mean and standard deviation per run, not the 51 members, so the physics curve uses the ensemble-mean shortwave. A member-level version is untested.
  • The 0.5 and 1.5 capacity-scaling placebos and the curtailment-cost proxy were not run (see the plan in the first commit of this pull request).
  • The second month of each test window scales its inputs with the mean and standard deviation of its own fold, not of the cutoff month, so its inputs are slightly rescaled relative to the pretraining, equally for all arms.
  • Code: this experiment imports experiments 510, 554, 634, 638, 639, and 643 and edits none of them.

docs.title: Did K1 beat BG2 on the five development months, when both were scored on the same rows?
docs.text: On the five development months K1 had a lower CRPS than BG2 at 13 Primaries, so BG2's lead in July to October 2026 is not a lead BG2 already held on those months. We compared K1 with BG2 on the five development months, using forecasts issued in October 2025, December 2025, and January, March, and June 2026. K1 is a neural network, fitted once, that reads power readings at least 24 hours older than the forecast's issue time. BG2 is the blend of models from experiment 87, refitted weekly, and reads readings 3.5 hours older than the issue time. We took stored forecasts of both, matched them row by row, and scored them with the same code. The score is the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in percentage points of each Primary substation's capacity; lower is better. We left out D14 and D18, which had a load transfer in the later window, and D15, which has a short history. At the remaining 13 Primaries K1's CRPS was 0.32 below BG2's. Experiment 633 scored all 16 Primaries on July to October 2026 (the window) and found BG2 ahead by 0.71. This result re-scores months that experiments 87, 425, 449, 470, and 613 already used, so it ranks nothing.

docs.title: What was compared
docs.text:
• Six systems. K1, the Candidate (experiment 610's network with 50% signal dropout and neighbouring Primaries' power summaries, its band widths set on these months), K3 (a neural network that reads no power lags), BG2, the manual heuristic (the median of the power at the valid time one to six and 49 to 55 weeks earlier), and the climatology (the quantiles of the power in the same month, half-hour, and weekend flag, fitted before each month's first day).
  • K1, Candidate, K3: the stored forecasts of the backtest export (experiments 612 and 613, five seeds averaged), read from backtest_export_roster_2026-11-07/. Nothing was refitted.
  • BG2: arm p_s6_bg2 of experiment 87: a blend of five models (weekly- and monthly-refitted XGBoost, an analogue model, a model pooled by Primary type, and a frozen stack) with an added solar-output term at the Primaries that have a solar capacity estimate, refitted weekly, with the quantiles widened about the median by a factor of 1.15 already applied. It reads the three power lags of origin_lags, whose newest reading is 3.5 hours before the issue time (NEWEST_AGE in e00087_common.py). K1 reads lags at least 24 hours old.
  • Rows: a row is one forecast for one Primary, issue time, and valid time. We scored the 915,135 of the 1,140,221 exported rows on which all six systems have a forecast. BG2 has no forecast on the other 225,086 rows, because experiment 87 stored 292 of the 365 daily runs (row_audit.csv lists each month). No cleaned reading was missing. No valid time is on or after 2026-07-01.
  • Event-free: the days that the detector of experiment 637 flags as an abnormal running arrangement (a temporary load transfer between Primaries) are removed: 23,339 of the 915,135 rows (2.6%). The detector's rule file is unchanged (we checked its hash). The export's own event_free flag is a second reading and gives the same sign in every contrast of the Results section.
  • Scorer and intervals: the formulas of the scorer of experiment 620. The intervals resample the five origin months, so they are coarse; day-block intervals are in contrasts.csv and agree.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The table gives CRPS in percentage points of capacity for days 1 to 10, on the 722,649 event-free rows at the 13 Primaries other than D14, D15, and D18. The month-block 95% intervals are on the contrasts in the bullets below the table.

System CRPS MAE of the median Coverage of q05 to q95 (nominal 0.90) q99 pinball loss K1 3.31 5.95 0.865 0.241 Candidate 3.35 6.01 0.891 0.241 K3 3.57 6.41 0.858 0.271 BG2 3.63 6.42 0.891 0.322 Manual heuristic 4.18 7.31 0.822 0.495 Climatology 7.42 13.75 0.899 0.408
  • K1 minus BG2: CRPS -0.32 (-0.42 to -0.22); MAE of the median -0.47 (-0.62 to -0.33); q95 pinball loss -0.10 (-0.18 to -0.04); q99 pinball loss -0.08 (-0.11 to -0.06). The Candidate is -0.28 (-0.38 to -0.19). K3, which reads no power lags, is -0.06 (-0.14 to +0.00). The manual heuristic is +0.55 (+0.43 to +0.70).
  • Pre-registered reading: the upper end of K1's interval (-0.22) is below +0.10, so "K1 held its own" is met, and K1's contrast is below the predicted +0.05. K1 was ahead, not level.
  • Cuts: on all rows at 16 Primaries, K1 minus BG2 is -0.23 (-0.50 to +0.08). D15, whose own contrast is +1.41, pulls this value up. Without D15 and D18 the contrast is -0.31. On event-free rows at 16 Primaries it is -0.24 (-0.52 to +0.08).
  • By month (13 Primaries, event-free): K1 minus BG2 is -0.22 (October 2025), -0.51 (December 2025), -0.29 (January 2026), -0.36 (March 2026), and -0.18 (June 2026). The sign holds in every month.
  • By lead band (13 Primaries, event-free): -0.23, -0.33, -0.34, and -0.32 at day 1, day 2, days 3 to 5, and days 6 to 10. BG2's fresher lags did not put BG2 ahead at day 1.
  • By Primary (event-free rows): K1 is ahead at 14 of 16 Primaries. BG2 leads at D15 (+1.41) and, by under 0.1, at D5. K1 leads most at D18 (-0.77) and D8 (-0.58).
  • Tails: K1's coverage of q05 to q95 is 0.865 against BG2's 0.891, so K1's band covers slightly less than the nominal 0.90. K1's q99 pinball loss is lower (0.241 against 0.322). The threshold-weighted CRPS (the CRPS of values clipped below at each Primary's 90th percentile of power before 2025-10-01) contrast, K1 minus BG2, is -0.05 (-0.09 to -0.01).

K1 minus BG2 CRPS, in percentage points of capacity. Window values are copied from experiment 633's leakage audit with the sign flipped, not recomputed.

Rows Reading Day 1 Day 2 Days 3-5 Days 6-10 16 Primaries, all rows Development months -0.04 -0.17 -0.22 -0.29 16 Primaries, all rows Window +0.78 +0.71 +0.69 +0.71 13 Primaries, event-free Development months -0.23 -0.33 -0.34 -0.32 13 Primaries, event-free Window +0.03 +0.01 +0.01 +0.04
  • K1 against the manual heuristic changed between the periods. On the development months (13 Primaries, event-free), K1 is 0.87 below the manual heuristic and BG2 is 0.55 below it. In the window (16 Primaries, all rows), BG2 is 0.61 below the heuristic and K1 is 0.10 above it. The change between the periods is in K1's score.
  • Lag age does not explain K1's development-month lead: BG2 has the fresher lags in both periods, yet K1 scores lower here.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Mean against median forecast: the stored forecasts are quantiles, with no mean forecast. The median is the point forecast. The MAE of the median moves the same way as the CRPS in every contrast above, so the check for a mismatch between the two did not fire.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. No control run was needed, for three reasons. The result agrees with experiments 425, 449, and 470, in which the neural networks scored better than BG2. Dropping D15 and D18 does not flip the sign. No nested arm or sister-experiment interval is involved.
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet agent read the code before the run and found four defects: a sign and a threshold wording in the plan, a missing filter on BG2's valid times, no guard for fewer than three bootstrap blocks, and no assertion that the two capacity tables agree. All four are fixed.
  • Not done: no avoidable-curtailment cost, and no load-shift event plots (the export holds one verified transfer, D5 and D16 in December 2025).
  • Thresholds of the threshold-weighted CRPS: one value per Primary, from the cleaned power before 2025-10-01, for every month.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• BG2 has forecasts on 80% of K1's rows (292 of 365 daily runs), so the months have unequal row counts, and June 2026 ends on 30 June; the rows are common to all six systems, so the comparison stays paired.
  • Development months favour the neural networks. The Candidate's band widths were set on these months (experiment 613, in-sample), and K1 was selected on them too. BG2 was tuned on experiment 87's validation year (July 2025 to June 2026), which overlaps these months, so neither side is out of sample.
  • Next: find what K1 lost after one unrefitted fit in July to October 2026. A refit of K1 on the window's early months is the direct test.

docs.title: Does running the demand networks once per ensemble member and pooling the 51 outputs beat giving them the ensemble mean and spread?
docs.text:
Running the demand neural networks K1 and K3 once per ensemble member and pooling the 51 answers did not beat giving them the ensemble mean and spread. We asked whether a demand neural network that reads one weather member at a time, run 51 times and pooled, forecasts demand better than the same neural network reading the mean and the spread of the 51 members once. We tested two ways. In the first, the stored (already fitted) networks ran on each member without any refit. In the second, the networks were refitted on rows holding one randomly drawn member each, and then pooled. The first way matched the stored forecasts once the bands had equal width, and the second way made them worse. The result narrows the search: the mean and spread already carry what the members add, so for these two neural networks the weather inputs are not where the next gain lies. The experiment follows experiment 397, which ran a plain neural network once per member and found the per-member scheme within 0.05 points of capacity of the mean-and-spread scheme.

Terms. K1 is the lag network, scored here without its gated band (the stored forecasts call this arm K2), and K3 is the lag-free network, both from experiment 613 and experiment 612. Arm A is the stored forecast, seed 0. Arm B runs A's stored weights on each member. Arm C refits step 2 (K1 only) and the daily fine-tune on single-member rows. "Run spread" keeps the run's own ensemble standard deviation in the spread inputs, and "zero spread" sets the standard deviation to 0 in training and testing. Pooling takes the 51 members' 3-component mixtures with equal weights into one 153-component mixture. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, in points of capacity (lower is better). The scored rows are event-free (experiment 637's detector) at the 14 Primaries other than D15 and D18, on the five development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06), days 1 to 10. Equal width scaling gives every arm, A included, one width factor per metering group and lead band, chosen to bring the 5% to 95% forecast-band coverage closest to 90%, using only months before the scored month, except that 2025-10 uses the factor chosen on 2025-12.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Each dot is an arm's event-free CRPS minus the stored forecast's, with its 95% interval from resampling the five origin months. Look at the B dots with run spread, which sit just below 0 as fitted (blue) and on 0 once the widths match (orange), and at the C dots, which sit above 0 in both readings.

The same difference by lead band for the two run-spread arms, bands as fitted. Look at the days 6 to 10 row, where pooling lowers the score most (K3 -0.024), and at C, which is worse at every lead.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Verdict, stop rule. Neither arm B nor the seed 0 arm C met the bar fixed in the plan (CRPS lower by at least 0.06 points in at least two of three fold groups). The experiment stopped, so seeds 1 and 2, the injected-shift follow ratio, the avoidable-curtailment cost, and the cold-night split were not run.
  • Arm B, run spread. CRPS (as fitted) 3.289 against 3.296 (K1 without the gate, -0.007, interval -0.012 to -0.003) and 3.565 against 3.581 (K3, -0.016, -0.025 to -0.007). After equal width scaling the differences are +0.002 (-0.004 to +0.008) and +0.001 (-0.004 to +0.005). The prediction that B would be at least 0.05 worse (P1) failed.
  • Arm B, zero spread. CRPS +0.020 (-0.019 to +0.051) and +0.015 (-0.026 to +0.058), worse by 0.056 and 0.024 at day 1 (K1, K3). Zero spread is out of the training distribution of the mixer.
  • Arm C. Run spread: +0.023 (-0.016 to +0.058) for K1 without the gate and +0.071 (+0.034 to +0.109) for K3. Zero spread: +0.040 (+0.019 to +0.062) and +0.112 (+0.051 to +0.174). Every contrast is above 0 in every fold group. The prediction that C would lower the score at days 6 to 10 (P2) failed.
  • Fold groups (B, run spread, as fitted, K1 without the gate and K3). 2025-10 and 2025-12: -0.006 and -0.007; 2026-01 and 2026-03: -0.010 and -0.028; 2026-06: -0.002 and -0.011. No group reaches -0.06.
  • Absolute scores. Stored K1 without the gate 3.296 and K3 3.581 as fitted, from score_B/summary.csv. The comparison with BG2, the manual heuristic, and climatology is in experiment 645 and is not repeated here.
  • Tails, days 1 to 10, as fitted (event-free, 14 Primaries). The share of readings at or below q95 should be 0.95: A 0.913 (K1 without the gate) and 0.896 (K3); B 0.921 and 0.913; C 0.917 and 0.905. q99 pinball loss: A 0.253 and 0.295; B 0.248 and 0.285; C 0.243 and 0.282. Pooling widens the band, so q95 coverage rises by 0.008 and 0.017 (days 6 to 10: 0.011 and 0.024). Arm B therefore shows the rise P3 predicts for arm C. For arm C, q95 coverage at days 6 to 10 rises by +0.011 (K3) and +0.002 (K1 without the gate), so P3 is met for K3 only, and the q99 half is not checked here. q99 and q95 pinball loss fall slightly for B and for C, except that q95 pinball loss for C K3 rises from 0.983 to 0.985. The lower tail changes little.
  • Row set and data. experiment_470_intersection_v1 rows of the roster export (experiment 614), 971,813 scored rows. The networks use seed 0 and are refitted on days 0 and 14 of each month, as in experiments 612 and 613. The member weather is the 51-member frame of each run, read for test rows and for training rows from 2025-07-02. Runs before that date store only the control member, so arm C trained on the control member for those rows (2,750,046 of 5,571,065 rows of the 2026-06 fold hold all 51 members, from the arm's run log). This is a limit on arm C, and the 2025-10 and 2025-12 fold group is the most control-heavy.
  • Compute. Arm B made 4 runs (K1 and K3, each with run spread and zero spread) over 5 months, and each run took minutes. Arm C: 20 fine-tunes and 10 step-2 fits for K1, 20 fine-tunes for K3 (7 to 21 seconds each, from the run logs). The GPU time is under 1 hour, against the 6-hour ceiling. The fitted weights are in data/ml-experiments/00646-per-ens-member-neural-demand-networks-pooled-quantiles/arms/*/work/models.
  • Lead range. The scored leads are 1 to 10 days.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Pooling code. With the members replaced by the stored mean (--identity), the pooled forecast equals the stored K1 and K3 forecasts to 2e-7 (2025-10, seed 0). The members' mean matches the stored mean to 0.0003 standard deviations in the five smooth weather columns.
  • Median and mean forecasts. The quantile frames hold no mean forecast, so the median minus the mean per site is not computed. The error of the median forecast (MAE) moves with the CRPS: B run spread -0.002 (K1 without the gate) and -0.007 (K3) points, C +0.081 and +0.168.
  • Triggers. None of the seven fired: no control failed, no result contradicts its prediction in a way left unexplained (P1 and P2 failed and are explained above; C K3 is also 0.051 and 0.073 worse at days 1 and 2, where P2 asked for within 0.03), the CRPS and the MAE agree in direction, leaving one site out was not run because no contrast is near the bar, no nested arm beats its container by more than its interval, no interval is more than twice as wide as a sister experiment's, and no later experiment depends on this result. This experiment has no audit.
  • Not run. The unlogged-event caveat does not apply (no load-shift slices were scored). The example-forecast graphs were not drawn because the stop rule ended the experiment before any arm was worth showing.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Member inputs do not help these networks, so the question moves to what the networks do with the ensemble spread: whether a spread-aware network with a calibrated band improves the tails, or whether the spread input contributes anything at all (arm C with zero spread was worse, but the zero-spread arms also removed the input).

docs.title: Can a small departure head on the frozen K1 neural network forecast the arrangement now in force better than K1 shifted by its own recent error?
docs.text:
Experiment 647 asked whether a small second neural network can forecast a Primary's demand better while a load shift is in force than a simple correction of the first network's forecast can. A Primary is a primary substation. A load shift is a period when the network operator moves part of a Primary's demand onto or off a neighbouring Primary. K1 is the neural network of experiments 612 and 613 that forecasts the normal running arrangement (NRA), the demand with no load shift. We froze K1 and fitted the departure head, a small second neural network whose output departs from K1's NRA forecast. The head reads K1's 11 quantiles, the age of the current departure, and the gap signals: the differences between recent power readings and the lag-free forecast (the forecast made without power lags, from experiment 598), averaged over 1, 3, and 7 days, and the same differences at neighbouring Primaries.

R0 is the no-fit baseline: K1's mean error over days 2 to 8 before the forecast, times exp(-lead/tau), added to each K1 quantile, with tau of 72 h or 168 h. We scored the head leave-one-month-out on the 5 development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06) on three row sets: the bank (synthetic shifts of chosen depth and length added to real power, from experiment 581), the days flagged by the experiment 637 detector, and the verified D5 and D16 pair (the load shifts verified at the Primaries D5 and D16 in December 2025 and January 2026). CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, approximated from the 11 stored quantiles and expressed in points of capacity: 100 times the score as a share of the Primary's capacity. MAE is the mean absolute error of the median forecast.

Take-home message. On injected shifts the head scores 10.0 points of capacity below K1, but R0 at tau of 168 h, with no fit, already closes most of the gap, so the head is 0.9 points better and the no-fit shift matches the head after a shift ends. Widening K1's band with no signal gets 60% to 68% of the head's gain over K1, and about 3.3 points come from reading the gap signals. The gain depends on the bank's length mix (-0.8 for 3-day events, about -14 for 15- and 30-day events). On real flagged days the gain rests on the verified pair, and the head fails in the first 3 days of an event. After a synthetic end the head scores 3.7 points worse than K1. The encoder arms gave no gain over H1. The next step is an experiment that separates the signal from the widening and from the no-fit shift, using shifts that end on varied days, before any head is considered for production. Verdict: partly supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
CRPS values are in points of capacity, intervals resample the 5 months and 5 seeds, and a negative contrast favours the first arm. The 5 months cover 16 Primaries, and leads run from 24 to 240 h. H1 and H2 are this page's arm labels and are unrelated to the engineering hypotheses H1 and T1.2. In H1, p is the survival probability: the probability that a shift is still running h hours later, given its age.

Arm Inputs What it controls for K1 stored forecast of experiments 612 and 613 reference R0, R0_168 K1 plus its decayed mean error, tau 72 h or 168 h no-fit shift R0* variant of R0 matching the design answer's verified-pair figure design answer's baseline Widened K1 K1's band widened by a fixed factor, no signal recalibration alone H1 K1 quantiles, gap signals, age, gate; mixture of K1 and K1 shifted the proposed head H2 same inputs; 11 free offsets to K1's quantiles whether the mixture helps H1-p H1 with noise in place of the signals and age whether signals matter AG, AS age and gate only; H1 with shuffled age gain without gap signals; age leak E1, E2, E3 head on K1's frozen encoder; own encoder copy; joint neural network whether the encoder helps
  • The head beats K1 inside an injected shift, but R0 at tau of 168 h is only 0.9 behind (P2). K1 24.37 [23.97, 24.73], R0 19.09, R0* 18.94, R0_168 15.24 [15.03, 15.42], H1 14.35 [13.97, 14.68], H2 15.18, H1-p 23.78. H1 minus K1 is -10.02 [-10.65, -9.55], minus R0 -4.73 [-5.30, -4.31], and minus R0_168 -0.885 [-1.375, -0.501] (stage4_contrasts.csv).
  • After a synthetic end, H1 scores worse than K1 and no better than R0 at tau of 168 h (P3). K1 3.19, R0 4.16, R0_168 6.83 [6.65, 7.04], H1 6.88, H1-p 3.30. H1 minus K1 is +3.69 [3.29, 4.09], and H1 minus R0_168 is +0.050 [-0.258, 0.486].
  • On event-free rows the head ties K1 and trails both R0 arms (P1). K1 3.713, R0 3.593, R0_168 3.536, H1 3.685 [3.212, 4.421]. H1 minus K1 is -0.029 [-0.215, 0.132], minus R0 +0.092 [0.045, 0.148], and minus R0_168 +0.149 [0.058, 0.277]. The q05-q95 band covers 0.889 of rows for H1 and 0.869 for K1.
  • On real flagged days the head's gain over K1 is small and its band is too narrow (P4). K1 10.52 [8.19, 16.98], R0 9.79, R0_168 9.48, H1 8.40 [7.31, 13.01], H1-p 10.11, E2 8.22. H1 minus K1 is -2.12 [-6.93, -0.15], minus R0 -1.39 [-4.52, -0.10], minus R0_168 -1.081 [-3.238, 0.092], and minus H1-p -1.71 [-6.45, 0.23]. The q05-q95 band covers 0.62 of rows for H1, 0.47 for R0, and 0.44 for K1. On the verified pair alone (13,068 rows) K1 scores 14.93, R0 13.77, R0* 13.42, H1-p 14.24, H1 10.90, E2 10.22, and E1 10.97.
  • One episode carries the P4 gain. H1 minus K1 per month is -2.11 (2025-10), -0.14 (2025-12), -7.20 (2026-01), and -0.21 (2026-03). Without 2026-01 it is -0.24, and H1 minus H1-p is +0.15. The 2026-01 rows are the verified pair in progress. The month-block interval treats that one episode as several independent months.
  • Part of the gain is recalibration, which H1-p cannot show. H1-p cannot widen its band, so it is a weak control. Gains over K1 on pooled P4 are -2.12 for H1, -1.28 for K1 widened to H1's coverage (60%), -1.89 for K1 with the best widening (89%, in-sample), and -1.45 for AG (68%). On P2, widened K1 scores 18.36 and best-widened K1 17.61 (audit); AG scores 20.98 and AS 19.26. H1's median moves the right way on 90% to 98% of the rows it moves, but in the first 3 days of an event it agrees in direction on only 42% of them, and CRPS rises from 13.40 to 13.79.
  • The loss after a shift ends is a prior-versus-bank mismatch. The mean survival probability is 0.67, against an empirical 0.28. With the empirical p the audit's rebuild moves P3 from 6.74 to 4.08 and P2 from 14.5 to 16.9. These rebuilt figures are on a different basis from the figures above. The bank ends every shift on day 14, so P3 does not measure behaviour after real shifts end. Probability-weighted CRPS (audit, subset) changes no sign: K1 to H1 is 26.6 to 16.9 on P2 and 4.02 to 8.63 on P3.
  • E1 and E2 gave no gain over H1 and were slightly worse on event-free rows. E1 minus H1 is +0.977 [0.156, 2.485] on P2 and +0.195 [0.082, 0.289] on P1; E2 minus H1 is +0.328 [-0.551, 1.306] and +0.208 [0.091, 0.310]. Both P4 intervals include zero. E3 (forward-chained, 2025-12 only; score/enc_nra_2025-12_fcb.csv) scored 3.164 on event-free rows against K1's 3.283, but E3's placebo scored 3.236. E3 scored worse than K1 on flagged days (8.484 against 8.302) and on the verified pair (13.976 against 13.774).
  • The head narrows K1's tails inside a shift and widens them after it. On P2 the q01 pinball loss is 3.282 for H1 against 8.613 for K1, and the q99 loss is 3.107 against 7.519. The share of rows above q99 is 0.149 against 0.393 (nominal 0.01). After a shift ends H1's q01 and q99 losses are 0.335 and 0.342 against K1's 0.170 and 0.220. On P4 they are 0.863 and 1.771 against 1.964 and 2.922.

The avoidable-curtailment cost proxy comes from the experiment 601 function, in its own units with no pounds conversion and no interval, for the six MW Primaries at leads 24 to 36 h with the limit at 0.9 of the earlier peak.

Set K1 R0 H1 P2 259,512 130,891 72,547 P3 807 11,551 25,275 P4 183,820 77,983 43,413
  • The depth signal detects most shifts the 637 detector misses. On the bank the depth signal alarms on 95% of 0.3-depth 3-day shifts and 99% of 0.3-depth 7-day shifts, and the experiment 637 detector alarms on 0% to 4% and 18% to 36%. The experiment 637 rows come from score5/detector.csv (signal "experiment 637"), which e00647_score.py computes by running experiment 637's rule on the bank's contaminated power. False alarms per Primary-month on event-free origins average 6.0 for the survival signal and 1.7 for the depth signal, over 25 runs (5 months by 5 seeds).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per Primary (event-free rows, points of capacity). A large gap would mean a skewed quantile forecast, so that the median and mean forecasts differ. For K1, 14 of 16 Primaries lie within 0.65; Primary 10 is -5.181 (H1 -4.579) and Primary 8 is -1.388.
  • Mean-forecast contrast. The mean forecast's error was not scored. The median's MAE agrees with CRPS for H1 against K1 (P2 21.28 against 30.06; P3 13.39 against 5.96). It disagrees for H1 against R0_168 on P2: H1 beats R0_168 on CRPS (14.35 against 15.24) but not on MAE (21.28 against 19.98). No MAE was computed on P4.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 1 fired: H1-p moved P2 by -0.59, and H1 minus H1-p on P4 is -1.71 [-6.45, 0.23] (+0.139 on the first month pair, the feasibility gate). Trigger 2 fired: P4 coverage and P3 miss their bars. Trigger 3 fired for H1 against R0_168 on P2 (above). Trigger 5 fired: AG and AS close 3.4 and 5.1 of H1's 10.0 points without gap signals. Triggers 4, 6, and 7 were not run or assessed (Limits).
  • Audit (briefs/647_audit.md, private): the audit reproduced every headline contrast, found no code error that changes a sign, and all its points are accepted. The audit did not examine the R0 contrasts, E1 to E3, per-Primary scores, the curtailment cost, or the detector read-out.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Every injected shift ends on day 14.
  • The permuted control was not run.
  • The 28 to 112 day part of the duration prior is untested.
  • The bank covers 13 to 14 Primaries, 15- and 30-day events are 62% of P2 rows, and K1(Dec) is in-sample on the October rows.
  • The verified pair is two load shifts on two Primaries in one episode.
  • R0's verified figures do not reproduce the design answer's (13.77 and 13.35 against 13.42 and 12.79), so R0* is the matching baseline.
  • Row counts for P1 and P4 are slightly smaller than K1's own counts, and leads run from 24 to 240 h only.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so false alarms are an upper bound.
  • The detector read-out is a lab test on the bank the head was fitted on, and the 30-day days-to-alarm (about 16.7) are inflated.
  • Rows without R0 residual history are dropped from every arm (r0_dropped_rows.csv): 35.0% of P2 (691,356 of 1,973,286), 8.4% of P1, 4.8% of P3, and 4.1% of P4. Contrasts against R0 hold on the remaining rows, and H1 minus K1 changes by about 0.2 on all usable rows.
  • Leaving one Primary out (trigger 4) was not run, and triggers 6 and 7 were not assessed: no sister experiment scored the same rows, and no later experiment depends on the headline yet.

docs.title: Next experiments
docs.text: Two questions follow, and neither is committed. Can a head trained on shifts that end on varied days, and on shifts of 4 to 16 weeks, keep the gain inside a shift without the loss after it, and beat R0 at tau of 168 h by more than 0.9 points? Would a head trained as a detector on the gap serve the need to mask rows when scoring NRA forecasts on new data?

docs.title: Does a larger or differently shaped part of the K1 or class 2 candidate demand network lower its quantile score by the agreed margin, now that the lag encoder also reads neighbour summaries?
docs.text:
Making two demand neural networks wider, deeper, or otherwise bigger did not lower their forecast error by the amount we required, so their sizes and training settings stay as they are. The required gain was 0.11 percentage points of a Primary's capacity in the CRPS (a score of the full forecast distribution; lower is better). That is the larger of two figures: experiment 447's margin, and the smallest difference that the seed-to-seed spread of experiment 613 lets one seed detect. Of the settings that pass the safety guards, the best gain is 0.04 points. That gain comes from one Primary substation, D15, which has a short history: without D15 and D18, the two short-history Primaries, the same change is slightly negative. Adding a small neighbour-summary layer (a bottleneck) gains more (0.05 points, interval above zero), but it makes the forecast follow an injected load-shift (a synthetic step added to the history) more closely, which one of the safety guards forbids. The verdict is not supported: no change helped enough to adopt. These scores cover forecasts 24 to 120 hours ahead, not the whole 1 to 10 day range that NGED uses. The lag-time weather is read from stored estimates of past weather. At forecast time that weather does not exist for the later days, so the scores are a ceiling for those days.

We asked whether larger or differently shaped parts of two demand neural networks lower their forecast error. K1 is the neural network that reads the power 1 day and 1 week earlier; the class 2 candidate also reads summaries of its electrical neighbours' power. We changed one setting at a time (15 settings in all), refitted the network, and scored the 24 to 120 hour forecasts for 3 test months (2025-10, 2026-01, 2026-06) on one seed, against the unchanged network refitted the same way. The unchanged K1 reproduces experiment 613's seed 0 to four decimals. The margin (0.113 points for K1, 0.109 for the candidate) is the larger of experiment 447's margin scaled to these networks and 1.96 x sqrt(2) x the seed standard deviation, fixed before any arm was scored. Because no change passed, the plan's five-fold, three-seed step and the random search did not run.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. Gain in 24-120 h CRPS over the unchanged network (points of capacity; positive is better), 3 test months, one seed. The orange dashed line is the margin (0.113 for K1, 0.109 for the candidate). Two candidate intervals reach past the margin line, but every point estimate sits far below that line. An arm passes only when its point estimate reaches the margin.

Figure 2. The two guards on the injected load-shift bank (days 4 to 10): the change in the share of a shift that the median forecast follows (top; the dashed line is the limit, +0.03) and in the safe-side share at q95 (bottom; limit -0.03). The three neighbour-bottleneck arms fail the top guard, and dropout 0.0 fails the bottom guard in both networks.

Figure 3. Three consecutive days of forecasts for one Primary (one of the eight MVA Primaries): the unchanged candidate and the candidate with lag-encoder width 128. The two are close; they differ most in the afternoon of day 3, where the wider network tracks the observed rise better.

Figure 4. One forecast of one Primary (one of the six MW Primaries) from its origin to 10 days ahead, for the same two networks. The bands widen with horizon, in both networks.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Gain is the unchanged network's CRPS minus the arm's (points of capacity, 24-120 h, all 16 Primaries, 3 months, seed 0). The unchanged networks score 3.088 (K1) and 3.145 (candidate).

  • Architecture and arms. K1 and the class 2 candidate of experiment 613 (arm P7+D50, the network's own quantiles with no G4 gate or band scaling), one setting changed per arm through e00648_run.py, which patches the module constants of experiments 545, 559, 560, 510, and 613 before they run. Each arm repeats pre-training, step 2, and the daily fine-tune; the learning-rate scale does not reach the step-2 mixer's fixed 5e-4.
  • Departure from the plan. The plan named the width-16 bottleneck arm as the reference for the other bottleneck widths. The page instead scores all three widths against the unchanged candidate, which has no bottleneck, so these arms add a component and change more than one factor. Widths 8 and 32 differ from width 16 by about +0.002 and -0.003 points.
  • Row set and data. experiment_470_intersection_v1, 24-120 h, 3 test months, seed 0, cleaned data, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 (the cut is applied by the stored recipe). Rows scored per arm: 211,126 (24-120 h), 52,482 (0-24 h), and 252,441 (120-240 h). Weather at lag times is the source that experiments 612 and 613 use, unchanged, so the scores are a ceiling for the days whose lag-time weather does not exist at forecast time.
  • Reproduction. The unchanged K1 matches experiment 613's seed 0 to four decimals (3.0882 points). The unchanged candidate scores 3.145 here; experiment 613's candidate seed 0 was scored through the same script and arm folder (c2_613) as a reference.
  • Margin. The seed standard deviation is 0.041 (K1) and 0.039 (candidate) points, estimated from experiment 613's seed sets 0 to 1 and 2 to 4, and rests on one noisy month (2025-10).
  • Where the gain comes from. Lag-encoder width 128 in the candidate gains 0.74 points at D15 and 0.14 at D18 but loses 0.31 at D10, 0.18 at D8, and 0.12 at D12 (24-120 h). By group, it gains 0.32 to 0.60 points at D15 and D18, about -0.005 at the eight MVA Primaries, and -0.015 to -0.049 at the six MW Primaries (three lead bands). Hidden width 128 shows the same pattern. The D15 and D18 group has the highest mean CRPS (6.3 points against 2.4 for the six MW and 3.0 for the eight MVA Primaries), but D15 alone causes that (9.8 points; D18 scores 2.0). D8 (7.6) and D12 (6.0) also score high yet lose with a wider lag encoder, so error level alone does not predict who gains.
  • Lead bands. The 0-24 h and 120-240 h gains of the best arms have the same sign and similar size as the 24-120 h gains; the D15 and D18 group gains at every lead band for lag-encoder width 128 (0.32 at 0-24 h, 0.60 at 120-240 h).
  • Tails. The unchanged candidate's event-free coverage is 0.860 of rows inside q05 to q95 at 24-120 h (a calibrated forecast has 0.05 below q05 and 0.05 above q95; measured 0.053 below and 0.087 above), and K1's is 0.871 (0.048 below, 0.080 above). No arm raises q05 or q95 pinball loss on event-free rows by more than 0.02 points except the learning-rate x2 and dropout 0.0 arms (both raise the loss by more than 0.02) and hidden width 384 (q95 +0.024). In the three bottleneck arms the bank q95 pinball loss rises by 0.08 points, four times the 0.02 limit, and the bank q99 loss rises by 0.02, level with the limit. The bank q99 loss falls by 0.01 to 0.04 in most other arms.
  • Curtailment cost. The scorer's cost at limit 0.9 (six MW Primaries, 12-36 h, 3 months) is 4,009 for the unchanged candidate and 4,411 to 4,447 for the two best arms; only 5 of 15 cells are non-zero, so three months cannot rank the arms. At limit 0.75 lag-encoder width 128 lowers the cost from 103,813 to 89,178 and hidden width 128 raises it to 118,111. No significance test was run on these costs.
  • Load-shift events. The guards in Figure 2 use the injected bank. This page does not score the real December 2025 load-shift events, so it carries no event plots. NGED's logs may miss events, so the clean-lag rows can hold events that no label covers.
  • Retraining. Monthly refit with daily fine-tunes, as in experiment 613. No weekly check was run because no change passed the screen.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median error beside the quantile score. The stored forecasts hold quantiles and no mean, so the median-minus-mean check cannot be run. The median's absolute error on the injected bank before each event (24-120 h) is 0.0444 for the unchanged K1 and 0.0448 for the unchanged candidate, in fractions of capacity.
  • Triggers. Trigger 4 fired: leaving out D15 and D18 turns the positive pooled gain of lag-encoder width 128 and hidden width 128 (+0.04) negative (-0.01). The verdict does not depend on it, because no arm passes the margin with or without D15 and D18. Prediction P3 (a wider lag encoder raises the follow ratio by 0.01 to 0.05) failed: the change in follow was 0.000. That contradiction fires trigger 2. We did not investigate why the follow ratio did not move. The other triggers did not fire. The unchanged K1 reproduces experiment 613, so no control failed.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the launcher before the first fit and all findings were accepted. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the results; it found the D18 explanation, the bottleneck contrast, and the tails wording wrong, and the page was corrected. A fresh Sonnet agent read the page as a newcomer, and a third reviewed its prose; the accepted findings are fixed.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• The neighbour-summary bottleneck is the only change with an interval above zero. Test it with a loss that keeps the follow ratio down before judging it.
  • Treat D15 and D18 as a separate question: the networks appear to improve there with width, and nowhere else.
  • Look for gains in the inputs rather than in the sizes, as experiment 447 advised.

docs.title: Plan (written before any fit)
docs.text:
Question. Experiment 447 changed one setting of the S1 demand network at a time and found no gain above 0.064 points. K1 and the class 2 candidate are different networks (a shared lag encoder with a lag ID, and neighbour summaries in the candidate), so this experiment repeats the screen on them. It follows the advice of experiment 447 to look at inputs and the lag-trust design before more tuning, and departs from it only because the maintainer asked for a new look after the lag encoder gained neighbour summaries.

Networks. K1 is the lag network with the G4 gated band; the class 2 candidate is K2 plus neighbour summaries and 50% signal dropout from experiment 610, scaled to K1's band width (experiment 613). Both are refitted from pre-training through step 2 and the daily fine-tune, with the changed setting applied at every stage.

One-factor arms (default in bold). Each arm changes one module constant before the network is built, through a wrapper around experiment 612's and 613's arm scripts.

Factor Levels Applies to Lag-encoder width (LAG_HIDDEN) 32, 64, 128 K1, candidate Lag-encoder depth (layers) 1, 2 K1, candidate Neighbour-summary bottleneck width (BOTTLENECK_HIDDEN; the candidate has none, so the reference is the width-16 bottleneck arm) 8, 16, 32 candidate Mixture components (COMPONENTS) 3, 5 K1, candidate Hidden width of the encoders and the mixer (ENCODER_HIDDEN, MIXER_HIDDEN) 64, 128, 256, 384 K1, candidate Dropout (DROPOUT) 0.0, 0.1, 0.2 K1, candidate Learning rate (pre-training, step 2 encoders and offsets, daily fine-tune; not the step-2 mixer's fixed 5e-4) x0.5, x1, x2 K1, candidate Maximum epochs and patience current, both x2 K1, candidate

That is 15 arms on the candidate and 13 on K1, each with 3 folds at seed 0. If one fold-seed fit chain takes long enough that all 30 arms exceed the 8 GPU-hour ceiling, the arms are dropped in this order until the projection fits: K1 arms for the neighbour-summary-free factors that the candidate arm already covers least (dropout, maximum epochs), then the hidden width 384, then the learning- rate x2 arm. The projection is made from the measured time of the first arm and recorded before the second arm starts.

Standing practices followed. Monthly refits with daily fine-tunes as in experiment 613, cleaned data, the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, fitted weights saved in the private data folder, stored experiment 612 and 613 forecasts reused only as a reproduction check, tail and cost reporting, a draft pull request, and the example-forecast and event plots in the write-up. The weather source at lag times is the one experiments 612 and 613 use, unchanged; the code review names it in the PR body, and the write-up says whether it exists at forecast time.

Process. Plan commit and draft pull request; a fresh Sonnet code review before the first fit; a free step-0 script that computes the margin from K1's stored seeds and commits it; the screen; a fresh Sonnet agent that re-derives the headline numbers; the write-up; one Sonnet prose review. Chat updates go to the manager only: plan pull request open, fits started, fits finished, pull request merged.

docs.title: Margin (fixed before any arm is scored)
docs.text:
e00648_margin.py reads experiment 613's stored event-free cells for seed sets 0 to 1 and 2 to 4 on the three screen months, 24-120 h, all Primaries. The seed standard deviation comes from the disagreement of the two seed-set means.

  • K1: CRPS 3.009 points of capacity, seed standard deviation 0.0407, minimum detectable effect for one seed against one seed 0.1129, experiment 447's margin scaled 0.0640. Margin 0.113 points.
  • Class 2 candidate: CRPS 3.056 points, standard deviation 0.0393, minimum detectable effect 0.1089, scaled 0.0650. Margin 0.109 points.
  • Caveat: the two seed sets differ by 0.064 in 2025-10 and by under 0.016 in the other two months, so the standard deviation rests on one noisy month. The margin is a lower bound on what a single seed can detect and is not tuned afterwards.

docs.title: Code review triage
docs.text: A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the launcher before the screen. Accepted: the bottleneck arms contrast with the width-16 bottleneck arm, not the reference (above); the learning-rate scale does not reach the step-2 mixer (above); the candidate's signal tables are experiment 598's and 610's tables built from the stock width-64 K1, so every candidate arm reads the same signals (a caveat for the write-up); the launcher now restricts commands, checks the tables exist, and records each chain's settings; the driver takes a lock so one GPU process runs at a time. The patches reach every place the constants are read, including the five-component output, which the agent checked by building the networks.

docs.title: Two separately fitted methods agree on the unmetered solar behind the six MW Primaries
docs.text:
Take-home. A neural-network probe estimates how much unmetered solar (small solar that NGED does not measure, so it shows only as lower demand) sits behind each of the six primary substations whose power is recorded in MW (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16). The probe is a trained demand-forecasting neural network, asked how much a Primary's net demand falls for a given amount of sunshine. Dividing its answer by the share of an added real solar farm that it finds again (0.68 of the added megawatts) gives 2.4 to 3.9 MW of alternating-current (AC) capacity for April to September 2025. The 80% intervals (10th to 90th percentile) overlap those of the regression table of experiment 474, fitted separately, at all six Primaries, and the probe's medians lie 6% below to 14% above its medians. The estimates describe the summer as a whole and cannot show how capacity changed between one year and the next. Experiment 644 found that adding an explicit solar term did not improve the forecast, so this table is for explaining and cross-checking solar capacity.

The probe's capacity is divided by the share of an injected farm that it finds again. Experiments 621, 634, and 638 trained neural networks that have no year input, and probed how much each Primary's net demand falls for a given amount of sunshine. This experiment reads the stored probe results and refits nothing. It divides the probe's capacity by the share of an injected real farm that the probe finds again (0.68 of the injected megawatts), and widens the interval by the spread of that share across four farms.

Figure 1. At every Primary the calibrated probe (orange) overlaps experiment 474's R4 interval (blue), and the register floor (dashed) lies below the probe's 10th percentile. The probe's 10th percentile is above the floor at all 5 Primaries that have one.

docs.title: Table: AC capacity of unmetered solar, April to September 2025
docs.text:
The raw value is the probe's capacity before calibration. The calibrated value is the raw value divided by 0.679. That is the mean, over four injected farms, of the share of a farm's added output that the probe finds when that farm is left out of the calibration. The 2026-06 cutoff is the date up to which the neural network was pretrained. Each row gives the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles (p10, p50, p90) in MW. The probe is the version without a cloud-cover correction (a cloud template).

April to September 2024 (recovery factor 0.684), calibrated p10, p50, and p90: D5 2.84, 2.96, 3.08; D9 2.16, 2.39, 2.63; D10 2.44, 2.51, 2.59; D11 3.09, 3.40, 3.72; D14 3.69, 3.86, 4.03; D16 2.92, 3.12, 3.32. The raw and calibrated values of every cutoff are in the private work/capacity_table.parquet.

Measured in energy, the capacity agrees with the megawatt basis to 1.0%. Measured in energy, the probe finds 0.88 (all daylight rows) or 0.78 (donor rows) of an injected farm's energy, against 0.68 in megawatts, because a real farm carries less energy per unit of peak than a physics curve does. Dividing the raw value by the energy recovery gives the capacity of a physics-shaped plant carrying the same energy: at D5 2.29 MW (all daylight rows) or 2.59 MW (donor rows), and at D14 3.01 or 3.40 MW. Dividing again by the farms' energy ratio gives the AC capacity of a fleet shaped like the injected farms, which is 1.0% below the megawatt basis at every Primary, so the energy basis and the megawatt basis agree.

The comparison interval for experiment 474 is the range spanning its two season-years that overlap the probe's half-year (July 2024 to June 2025 and July 2025 to June 2026, for April to September 2025). Experiment 479's anomaly regression has one interval per Primary. "Share" is the overlap as a share of the narrower interval, and a negative overlap is the size of the gap between the two intervals.

  • Experiment 479: overlap at 4 of 6 for both half-years. D5 and D16 are separated by a gap, and the probe is 10% below experiment 479's median at both.
