docs.title: The estimates describe a whole summer, not changes within it
docs.text: The values describe a summer half-year and cannot date a change inside it. Experiment 638 showed that a capacity step is followed at 0.82 to 0.88 only in an ordinary spring, and experiment 634 showed that a sunny spring is read as solar capacity. At the 2026-06 cutoff the two probe summers differ by at most 0.07 MW at every Primary (0.05 MW at 2025-10 and 2026-03, and 0.23 MW at 2025-07), and the four pretraining cutoffs differ by 2% to 9% (largest to smallest median). Experiment 474's R4 table, in contrast, moves by up to 0.37 MW between season-years (D10, 2024 to 2025). The probe therefore agrees with experiment 474 on the level and says nothing about the trend.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and mean-forecast error: not applicable, because no forecast is scored.
  • Audit triggers (checks that call for a fresh audit): none fired. No control or placebo is run here, no nested arm exists, and no later experiment depends on this result. Prediction (4) missed its range (see below).
  • Coverage: the widened interval covers the truth in 0.81 of 96 leave-one-farm-out constant injections (0.75 to 0.92 per cutoff and half-year). Experiment 634 read 0.66 with a different widening (the standard deviation of the four leave-one-farm-out factors, against the standard deviation of the four farms' median recoveries here, and the factor is the mean over held-out farms of the median of the other three farms' medians), so the two coverage values are not comparable. A reviewer's variants of the construction give 0.78 to 0.91 overall, so the value is not pinned down to better than about 0.1. With 96 injections, 0.81 is consistent with the nominal 0.80 and says nothing finer, so the extra widening that the plan allowed was not needed.
  • Predictions: (1) held: overlap 6 of 6, and medians within 0.94 to 1.14 times R4's. (2) held: the calibrated median is 1.46 to 1.47 times the raw median. (3) held: 5 of 5. (4) missed on the high side, 0.81 against 0.60 to 0.80. (5) held: -1.0%.
  • Stop rules: the seed standard deviation of the raw capacity is at most 0.17 MW (stop at more than 0.5 MW at 3 Primaries); the cutoffs' medians differ by at most 9% (stop at 30% at 3 Primaries).
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first run, another re-derived the numbers, and another reviewed the prose; each review's findings were triaged and the valid ones applied.

docs.title: Caveats and next steps
docs.text:
• Caveats: the injected farms are four real metered farms that resemble each other, so the recovery factor, and therefore the table, may not transfer to an unmetered fleet of rooftop panels with other tilts. The farm spread is estimated from four farms. Experiment 474 flags its own table at D5, D9, and D16. The probe covers April to September, so winter capacity is unprobed. Nothing dated 2026-07-01 or later is used. The raw rows, the table, and the figure source are in this experiment's private folder.
  • Next: compare the table with NGED's connection records where NGED will share them, starting with D5, D9, and D16.

Code: ml-experiments/00649-pv-capacity-table-season-year-from-stored-probes/e00649_table.py reads experiment 634's stored probes, experiment 634's energy_recoveries.csv (which holds experiment 621's recoveries), and the stored tables of experiments 129, 474, and 479. It edits none of them.

docs.title: Does a departure head trained on shifts with random ends, varied shapes, and varied depths beat K1 shifted by its own decayed recent error, once band widening is removed?
docs.text:
Experiment 650 asked whether the departure head of experiment 647 improves when it trains on a richer set of injected load shifts. A load shift is a period when the network operator moves part of a Primary's demand onto or off a neighbouring Primary. A Primary is a primary substation. K1 is the neural network of experiments 612 and 613 that forecasts the normal running arrangement, the demand with no load shift. The departure head is a small second neural network that reads K1's quantiles and the gap signals (differences between recent power and a lag-free forecast), and shifts K1's forecast towards the arrangement now in force. R0 (168 h) is the no-fit baseline: K1's quantiles plus K1's own mean error over valid days 2 to 8 before the forecast, decayed by exp(-lead / 168 h).

Take-home message. All shifts here are synthetic: they are injected into real history, and only one real episode (the verified pair, below) checks the result. Trained on shifts with random ends, varied shapes, and depths from 3 to 50 points of capacity, the head beats R0 (168 h) by 2.29 points of capacity inside shifts that lie outside the training range (R-new is the head trained on the extended generator, R-old the head trained on the old bank), after every arm's band is scaled to the same coverage. R0 (168 h) beats R-new on event-free rows and after a shift ends. After a shift ends, however, the head scores 3.59 points worse than K1, and 1.83 points worse than the head trained on the old bank. The head is therefore not ready for production. Verdict: partly supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are CRPS (twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 stored quantiles) in points of capacity, where 1 point is 1% of a Primary's effective capacity. A negative difference favours the first arm. Intervals are percentile bootstraps over the 5 development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) of the mean of 2 seeds. Equal width scaling multiplies every arm's quantile spread about its median by one factor per month and phase, chosen so that the q05-q95 band covers 0.90 of the rows. The factor is fitted on the scored rows and knows which phase each row is in (before, inside, or after the shift), so the scaling is an oracle that production cannot use. It applies to K1 and R0 as well. Pinball loss is the asymmetric quantile loss; CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score; MW and MVA Primaries are those metered in megawatts and in megavolt-amperes; NGED is National Grid Electricity Distribution.

  • Inside a shift outside the training range, R-new beats every other arm (decision contrast). Scaled CRPS: K1 21.01, R0 (168 h) 16.69, R-old 15.85, R-new 14.40, placebo 19.18. R-new minus R0 is -2.29 [-2.63, -1.95]; minus R-old, -1.45 [-1.69, -1.22]; minus K1, -6.61 [-7.41, -5.79]; minus placebo, -4.78 [-5.72, -3.68]. Unscaled CRPS: K1 26.64, R0 18.10, R-old 15.81, R-new 13.13. Scaling cuts R-new's gain over R0 from 4.96 unscaled points to 2.29.
  • The gain holds on in-support events and at every depth. Inside events within the training range, R-new scores 9.48 against R0's 10.90 (-1.42 [-1.90, -0.95]). By depth (0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.65), R-new scores 7.12, 10.43, 14.57, and 21.75 against R0's 8.31, 12.34, 17.07, and 24.64. On the training family in the scored month (events the head never saw), R-new scores 6.65 against R0's 7.94.
  • Both vetoes fail or are not cleared. After a held-out shift ends, scaled CRPS is K1 3.80, R0 6.52, R-old 5.57, R-new 7.40, and the placebo 4.08. R-new minus K1 is +3.59 [+2.70, +4.41] against the 0.5 limit, and R-new minus R-old is +1.83 [+1.24, +2.53]. On event-free real rows, R-new minus K1 is +0.05 [-0.24, +0.31] scaled and +0.03 [-0.28, +0.31] unscaled against the 0.03 limit, so the experiment cannot tell whether the head scores worse there; at the point estimate the unscaled loss is 0.034 above K1, which misses the 0.03 limit. R-new is also worse than R0 after the end (+0.88 [+0.22, +1.55] scaled) and on event-free rows (+0.18 [+0.10, +0.27] scaled). R-new carries a shift for about 3 days past its end in the examples.
  • The placebo prediction failed. The plan predicted the placebo within 0.05 of K1 after scaling. On the decision rows the placebo scores 19.18 against K1's 21.01 scaled (24.42 against 26.64 unscaled). No table here explains the gap. R-new minus placebo is -4.78 [-5.72, -3.68].
  • On the verified D5 and D16 pair (descriptive, 13,000 rows, one episode), unscaled CRPS is K1 15.02, R0 13.25, R-old 9.76, R-new 9.57, and the placebo 14.12. R-new and R-old are equal there.
  • Tail calibration (unscaled). Inside a shift, q05-q95 coverage is K1 0.23, R0 0.37, R-old 0.55, and R-new 0.59, against a nominal 0.90. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99 is K1 6.91, 9.09, 11.35, and 8.84; R0 4.25, 5.95, 7.31, and 5.28; R-old 2.56, 4.21, 5.33, and 3.25; R-new 2.59, 4.08, 4.68, and 3.02. After a shift ends, coverage is K1 0.90, R0 0.62, R-old 0.88, and R-new 0.81, and the q99 pinball loss is 0.26, 0.98, 0.33, and 0.84. On event-free rows coverage is 0.87 for K1, 0.88 for R0, 0.89 for R-old, and 0.89 for R-new, and the q99 pinball loss is 0.275, 0.250, 0.256, and 0.258.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost (experiment 601's function, in the units of its code, which labels them pounds per Primary-day without a check against a tariff, six MW Primaries, leads 12 to 36 h, limit 0.9 of the earlier peak, mean over the held-out rows; the range is the lowest and highest of the 5 months). Inside a shift: K1 549,533, R0 213,749, R-old 167,632, R-new 147,900 (range 70,859 to 247,869), placebo 482,589. In the 7 days after the end: K1 541, R0 13,980, R-old 8,087, R-new 10,512, placebo 1,967. Over all rows: K1 316,942, R0 126,244, R-old 97,594, R-new 87,208, placebo 278,503. Every head cuts the cost inside a shift, and every head raises it after the end.
  • The head's median is a better forecast too. Over all held-out rows inside a shift, the mean absolute error of the median is K1 30.59, R0 21.92, R-old 22.18, and R-new 17.42 points of capacity. R-new leads on both CRPS and median error, but R0 beats R-old on median error and loses to it on CRPS.

docs.title: Arms, data, and method
docs.text:
• Arms. R0 (168 h), K1 (stored), R-old (experiment 647's head recipe refitted on experiment 647's constant-shift bank, because its stored weights were deleted to free disk), R-new (the same head on the extended generator), placebo (R-new with the shifts shuffled across the bank rows of the training fold). All heads read K1's 11 quantiles and experiment 647's inputs, one head per scored month (trained on the other 4 months), 2 seeds, with early stopping on origin days 21 onward of the training months. Arm G (a head trained on generated bases instead of real ones) was not run, and neither was the realness classifier planned beside it.
  • Extended generator. One shift per Primary per pass, 12 training passes per month. Constant or proportional shape (MVA Primaries constant only), step or 6 to 48 h ramp onset, depth log-uniform from 3 to 50 points, duration 3 to 14 or 28 to 112 days with onset from 10 days before the month to day 20, so ends fall before, inside, and after the 10-day horizon. The donor's loss reaches one or two real electrical neighbours at 0.5 to 1 times the loss (15% of shifts have none), kept out of MW-and-MVA sums by a power factor of 0.97.
  • Held-out family. 4 passes per month, constant shape, depths 0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.65, durations 5, 10, 21, 45 days, half the events with a 72 to 120 h ramp. Events with a long ramp, depth 0.65, or a duration of 15 to 27 days are outside the training range; the decision contrast pools them. A 5-day event with a 120 h ramp never reaches its labelled depth.
  • K1 on the bank. K1's five saved seeds ran on CPU on each shifted bank, then experiment 613's tail constants and G4 gate were rebuilt with this experiment's shifts. The rebuild reproduces experiment 647's stored K1 rows on its constant bank (0.4% of rows in one pass differ where the daily-mean gate differs from experiment 613's constant per-day step).
  • Rows and cleaning. The development months only; no row on or after 2026-07-01 is read (asserted). Power comes from the stored clean stack, with flagged rows excluded from real-row training and scoring; the count of flagged half-hours per fold was not tabulated separately. Rows without R0 history are dropped from every arm: 14% to 26% of held-out rows per month, and 37% of the real rows in 2025-10 (score5/dropped.csv).
  • Cadence. K1 is stored and not refitted. The heads are small and are fitted once per scored month, so no refit cadence applies.
  • Reused code. Experiment 647 (data build, head, fit helpers, K1 rebuild pattern), experiment 581's bank interface, experiment 591 and 613's K1 inference, experiment 613's scorer, and experiment 601's cost.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (points of capacity, all held-out rows inside a shift): K1 -0.75, R0 -0.75, R-old -0.38, R-new -0.32. Event-free real rows: -0.61, -0.61, -0.53, -0.53.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the contrasts (all held-out rows inside a shift, mean absolute error of the mean forecast): K1 30.59, R0 22.02, R-old 22.37, R-new 18.40. R-new leads on both measures; R0 beats R-old on this one only.
  • Triggers fired. The placebo moved the decision rows by 2.2 unscaled points against K1 (placebo trigger), and the two vetoes missed their bars (bar trigger). The leave-one-Primary-out, sister experiment, and later-dependency triggers were not assessed.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet agent reviewed the plan and another the code before the first scored run. The code review found a held-out family with no in-support cells, unbalanced signs, a reversed power-factor conversion, MVA Primaries given proportional shapes, and an events file overwritten per batch; all were fixed and the inference was rerun. The results review and the write-up review are listed in the pull request.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The intervals use 5 month blocks, so every interval is coarse.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so event-free rows may hold unlogged shifts. The event-free cost is therefore optimistic and the number of real flagged events is a lower bound.
  • The held-out shifts differ from the training family in a few attributes only, they are constant shapes, and an MVA Primary's target is clipped at zero.
  • Equal width scaling is an oracle fitted on the scored rows. The scaling widens every under-covered arm: inside held-out shifts the factors are 6.5 for K1, 5.5 for R0, and 3.6 for R-new, and R-new's unscaled q05-q95 coverage is only 0.59. The scaled gain therefore depends on widening R-new's band by about 3.6 times.
  • One episode (the verified pair) carries the real-row evidence; no real flagged day beyond it was scored.
  • R-old is a refit on the same one-bank training months as R-new, not the stored head of experiment 647.
  • Arm G and the realness classifier were not run.
  • The first-month-pair gate (2025-10 and 2025-12) passed: R-new minus R0 was -2.33 and -2.83. Fold-by-fold values for every contrast are in the per_month column of score5/contrasts.csv.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Let the head end a shift from the gap signals: replace the fixed duration prior with a prior learned from the extended bank, and test it on shifts that end during the 10-day horizon.
  • Re-test the decision contrast with a fixed width-scaling rule that targets pinball loss, not coverage.
  • Run arm G once the head's after-shift loss is fixed.

docs.title: Does a graph layer over the electrical neighbours let the class 2 candidate keep its low follow of a load shift while removing its extra error on ordinary days at the six MW Primaries?
docs.text:
A graph layer over the electrical neighbours did not help. The class 2 candidate (C) is the stored neural network of experiments 612 and 613. It follows an injected false load shift (a synthetic step in its own recent power readings) less than the pretrained network without neighbours (A1) does, but on ordinary days it has an extra forecast error at the six Primary substations that report power in megawatts (MW). We asked whether a layer that lets each Primary read the hidden states of its neighbouring Primaries, wired like the real electricity network, would keep the low follow (the share of the injected shift that the forecast copies) and remove the extra error. We added that layer in five forms to the candidate without its neighbour summaries (the control G0), fitted each form on two development months (October and December 2025) with two seeds, and scored each form against C. No form passed the gate fixed in advance. The graph layers made little use of the neighbours, and a placebo wired at random scored the same as the real wiring. The six MW Primaries' extra error is therefore not caused by missing neighbour information. Following the plan, this page is the final answer: the confirmation experiment (G2) and the extension to substation parents (G3) do not run.

The experiment follows the maintainer-approved design (Opus, 2026-11-08). It builds on the class 2 network of experiment 612 and experiment 613, the neighbour summaries of experiment 610, the injected load shifts of experiment 581, the pretrained shared lag encoder (A1) of experiment 591, and the E3 rows of experiment 599. The graph layers are the graph convolution of Kipf and Welling (2017) and the graph attention of Veličković et al. (2018). Edges come from the 29 interconnections of experiment 383.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
• Verdict: not supported. No arm passes the gate (next section).
  • Take-home. The extra error at the six MW Primaries (about 0.13 to 0.14 points of capacity over A1) is the same for G0, which has no neighbour inputs, and for C. The graph layers did not remove it.
  • The graph layers make little use of their neighbours. Moving from bank M to bank X changes the median forecast by 0.19 points of capacity for GAT-E and 0.92 for C, against a mean injected shift of 31.7 points (FLOW-E: 0.25; GAT-R: 0.11).

Panel (a): the share of a false shift that each forecast follows (lower is better; 0 ignores the shift). Look at FLOW-E, the only arm below C on banks M and S, and at the three graph arms (GCN-E, GAT-E, GAT-R) that sit above G0. Panel (b): six MW event-free CRPS minus A1's; every interval sits above zero, and the intervals of C, G0, and the graph arms overlap almost entirely. The scorer stores no paired contrast against C, so panel (b) shows A1 as the reference.

docs.title: Arms and the gate
docs.text:
All arms use experiment 613's recipe: E3 rows (7-day embargo, half weight on the next 7 days), the D5 monthly offset, 50% signal dropout (D50), refits on days 0 and 14, seeds 0 and 1, the synthetic lag-only load shifts of experiment 581, and monthly folds on 2025-10 and 2025-12. G0 drops the neighbour summaries. A graph arm adds one layer, h_i + U * aggregate_j(message_ij), with U initialised to zero so every arm starts as G0, and with each neighbour's message hidden on half of the training rows. GCN-E averages neighbour states with a degree-normalised sum. GAT-E attends over neighbour states with two heads. GAT-R is GAT-E on a graph rewired at random with every node's degree preserved (the placebo). GAT-F lets every Primary attend to every other Primary, with no topology. FLOW-E sends an antisymmetric flow in megawatts along each edge and trains it with an auxiliary loss on the known synthetic shift.

The injected banks are M (each shift mirrored on one neighbour, experiment 581), S (shift split 60/40 over two neighbours; the degree-1 Primary D9 loses 40% of its mirror, so it understates the benefit for D9), and X (no mirror).

Arm Follow, bank M Follow, bank S Follow, bank X Six MW CRPS, 24-120 h Gate (i) Gate (ii) Gate (iii) Passes A1 0.119 0.119 0.119 2.320 n/a n/a n/a n/a C 0.044 0.046 0.074 2.458 n/a n/a n/a n/a G0 0.059 0.059 0.059 2.458 n/a n/a n/a n/a GCN-E 0.065 0.065 0.072 2.452 fail fail fail no GAT-E 0.064 0.065 0.072 2.452 fail fail fail no GAT-R 0.068 0.068 0.068 2.452 n/a n/a n/a placebo GAT-F 0.057 0.058 0.068 2.475 n/a n/a n/a n/a FLOW-E 0.038 0.038 0.059 2.479 pass fail moot no

The gate, checked by e00651_gate.py on the width-rescaled forecasts (the raw forecasts give the same pass or fail result; the CRPS cells in the table above and the margins below are raw), requires of GCN-E, GAT-E, or FLOW-E: (i) follow on bank M at most C's + 0.01 and on bank S at most C's; (ii) six MW event-free CRPS below C's by at least 0.044, or follow on bank S below C's by at least 0.03; and (iii) beating GAT-R by half the gate threshold on the measure that passed (ii), which is moot when (ii) fails. The 0.044 threshold is a constant fixed in e00651_gate.py from experiment 610's minimum detectable effect, not the per-arm interval half-width that the scorer prints. GCN-E and GAT-E fail (i): they follow 0.020 to 0.021 more than C on bank M and 0.019 more on bank S. FLOW-E passes (i), but its CRPS is 0.021 worse than C's and its follow is only 0.008 lower on bank S, so (ii) fails.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Predictions. Six predictions were written before any score.
    • P1 (GAT-E's follow within 0.01 of C's) failed although the author expected it to hold: 0.064 against 0.044.
    • P2 (GAT-E's CRPS within 0.044 of G0's) holds in its letter (−0.005), but its purpose, removing the extra error, fails: G0 itself is 0.133 above A1 and every arm stays 0.129 to 0.154 above A1 (month-averaged). The pre-registered "+0.059" was a wording error: C and G0 have equal CRPS here.
    • P3 (GAT-R follows at least 0.01 more than GAT-E) failed, as expected: +0.004 on bank M and +0.003 on bank S.
    • P4 (GCN-E and GAT-E differ by less than the threshold) held.
    • P5 (GAT-F within 0.044 of G0) held: +0.017.
    • P6 (FLOW-E on bank X no worse than C by more than 0.01) held: 0.059 against 0.074, which is 0.015 better.
  • G0 stands in for C on ordinary days. On the six MW rows the median forecast of G0 correlates 0.9998 with C's (mean absolute difference 0.18 points). On injected rows the median forecasts of G0 and C differ by 1.05 points, because C reads neighbour summaries. We did not refit one C cutoff to check the stored forecasts; the G0-versus-C comparison stands in for that check on ordinary rows only.
  • Tails. At the six MW Primaries the graph arms match C: q99 pinball loss 0.182 for G0, GCN-E, GAT-E, and GAT-R against 0.188 for C and 0.158 for A1, and q05 to q95 coverage 0.859 to 0.873 against 0.901 for A1. FLOW-E is worse in the upper tail (q99 0.196, q95 0.696 against C's 0.682), and GAT-F has the lowest coverage (0.859). At the eight MVA Primaries C has the lowest q95 and q99 loss of the trained arms (0.786 and 0.258 against 0.794 to 0.818 and 0.260 to 0.282), and A1 is worse than C there (CRPS 2.883 against 2.876), so the extra-error finding applies to the six MW Primaries only.
  • Curtailment cost. Not computed: no arm passed the gate, so none goes forward to a decision that needs it.

Tail table, six MW Primaries (24-120 h, pinball loss; coverage of the 90% band):

Arm q01 q05 q95 q99 Coverage A1 0.140 0.519 0.613 0.158 0.901 C 0.142 0.535 0.682 0.188 0.873 G0 0.142 0.536 0.678 0.182 0.872 GCN-E 0.141 0.536 0.681 0.182 0.869 GAT-E 0.142 0.535 0.678 0.182 0.871 GAT-R 0.141 0.535 0.677 0.182 0.871 GAT-F 0.141 0.536 0.688 0.185 0.859 FLOW-E 0.141 0.536 0.696 0.196 0.869

docs.title: Examples of forecasts
docs.text:
The two real load shifts in the two development months that experiment 580 verified, at D5 and D16 (both six MW Primaries). The stored forecasts end on 1 January 2026, before the events end on 13 January. The figures show the forecasts only; no score is attached to them.

G0 and FLOW-E at D5, for comparison of the one arm that holds follow.

The six figures below show injected load shifts of 15% and 30% of capacity, up and down, at three six MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10) and three MVA-only Primaries (D2, D3, D4), C above and GAT-E below. The injected span is shaded and the shifted lag input is dashed. The six figures show the forecasts of two arms through injected shifts; the follow scores are in the first table.

The stored forecasts reach 119.5 hours (5 days), so the full 14-day horizon is not drawn. For the winter evening the median error is 1.91% of capacity (C) and 1.95% (GAT-E), with 0.933 and 0.946 of the readings inside the 90% band. For the quiet week the errors are 2.26% and 2.29%, and both hold 0.979 of readings inside the band.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Scorer reproduced. A fresh audit recomputed six MW CRPS from the stored quantile forecasts and matched the scorer to 2e-7 on all 14 system levels and 26 contrasts.
  • Median and mean forecasts agree with CRPS. The mean absolute error of the median forecast and of the mean forecast point the same way as every raw CRPS contrast against C; only the width-rescaled G0 minus C contrast flips (CRPS −0.003, median error +0.008). Median minus mean forecast is small at every six MW Primary (at most 0.062 points from C's gap). At D8 and D15, neither a six MW Primary, G0 and the graph arms differ from C's gap by up to 0.4 to 0.8 points, most for FLOW-E.
  • Triggers fired, none changing the verdict: (a) seed noise exceeds every contrast except FLOW-E's: arm minus C changes sign between seed 0 and seed 1 for G0, GCN-E, GAT-E, GAT-R, and GAT-F, and between the two months; (b) leaving one Primary out flips the sign of 16 of 84 six MW CRPS contrasts, mostly by dropping D10, while no flip occurs for follow on bank M, and GAT-F and FLOW-E minus C never flip; (c) GAT-R sits inside GAT-E's interval (GAT-E minus GAT-R +0.0001, interval −0.006 to +0.007); (d) the graph layers make little use of the neighbours (above).
  • Not fired: a failed control, a nested arm that beats the arm containing it (G0 does not beat C; GAT-F is worse than GAT-E), and a disagreement between the quantile score and the mean-forecast error on the raw contrasts.
  • Leak guard. Replacing every neighbour reading after the origin minus 24 hours with noise leaves the inputs and forecasts bit-identical (e00651_test_leak.py; the positive control with a shortened guard window fails as it should).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Few months, few seeds. Two development months and two seeds. The scorer's 99.75% interval over the two months spans both months' values, so panel (b) is wide; it excludes none of the contrasts that matter. No contrast among C, G0, GCN-E, GAT-E, and GAT-R is resolved. FLOW-E is worse than C and G0 (day-block 95% interval of FLOW-E minus C: +0.010 to +0.032).
  • Seen once. G2 did not run, so no arm was confirmed on 2026-01, 2026-03, or 2026-06.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's logs may miss load-shift events, so clean rows can hold unlabelled events; the injected-bank numbers are optimistic and the real-event slices undercount.
  • MVA nodes. Eight of the 14 Primaries in the group tables (D15 and D18 are tabled separately) report MVA, which has no direction, so FLOW-E's conservation holds only approximately there.
  • Bank S. The 60/40 split hides 40% of the mirror at the degree-1 Primary D9.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The class 2 candidate and G0 both score 0.13 points worse than A1 at the six MW Primaries, with or without neighbours. The next experiment should find which part of the recipe causes that excess (E3 rows, the D5 offset, or 50% signal dropout), for example by dropping each in turn on G0.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text: Code is in ml-experiments/00651-graph-layer-over-electrical-neighbours-in-the-demand-network-part-1/: e00651_arm.py (fits, three banks), e00651_score.py (wraps experiment 613's scorer), e00651_gate.py, e00651_audit.py, e00651_figures.py, and the two tests. The GPU cost was about 3.0 process-hours of fits and injections of the 5-hour ceiling.

docs.title: Does a departure head with an explicit survival output beat the best forecast that does not know when a shift ends, once each forecast is scored under its own rules?
docs.text:
A Primary is a primary substation. A load shift is a period when the electricity network operator moves part of one Primary's demand onto, or off, a neighbouring Primary. K1 is the neural network of experiments 612 and 613 that forecasts the normal running arrangement (NRA), the demand with no load shift. Experiment 652 defines two forecasts, scores each under its own rules, and asks whether a departure head with a learned survival output beats a no-fit survival curve. R-haz is the departure head with a survival output. B-haz is K1 shifted by its recent error and decayed by a survival curve fitted to shift durations, with no neural network. R0 (168 h) is the same shift decayed by a fixed exponential. R-new and R-old are the departure heads of experiment 650 with a fixed duration prior. Scaled CRPS means the score after equal width scaling (see Results), and points of capacity are percentages of a Primary's effective capacity. Every shift here is injected into real history; the real rows check only the event-free veto and one verified episode.

Take-home message. Where a shift is in force at the forecast origin, R-haz scores 5.8 points of capacity against K1's 9.9 (unscaled), and B-haz scores 5.85 (unscaled), so on shifts that follow the training mixture the learned survival output adds nothing measurable (R-haz minus B-haz -0.02 [-0.35, +0.24] scaled). On held-out durations R-haz is better by 0.74 points. In the last 24 hours before a shift ends, R-haz scores 3.5 and B-haz 4.6 points worse than K1 (7.44, 8.56, and 3.98 unscaled); that cost cannot be avoided without knowing the end. Verdict: not supported.

docs.title: Two forecasts and their scoring rules
docs.text:
The two forecasts answer different questions, so each is scored on its own truth and its own rows.

  • The normal-running-arrangement (NRA) forecast ignores shifts. Its target is the demand the Primary would draw with no shift. In the injected bank that truth is known exactly (the unshifted real power). On real rows it is scored only outside detected or labelled shifts. NGED's labels are a one-off, incomplete dump, so the counts of real shifts are lower bounds and clean real rows may hold unlabelled shifts. Scoring the NRA forecast on rows that contain a shift would blame it for riding through the shift, which is its job. The NRA output in this experiment is K1, unchanged.
  • The prevailing forecast continues the arrangement now in force. Its target is the observed power, and it is scored on all rows. A prevailing forecast issued during a shift will carry the shift past its end, because shift ends are random and cannot be known at the origin. One hedge is a survival probability that decays the shift over the forecast horizon. A bad score after a shift ends is therefore an expected cost, and the question is whether the forecast is worse than the best forecast with no knowledge of the end time.

docs.title: Scoring by the state at the forecast origin
docs.text:
The row is assigned to a stratum by the state of the shift at the origin, not at the valid time. The strata, on the injected bank, are:

  • Event-free origin: no shift in force at the origin, none ended in the previous 7 days, and none starting before the row's valid time.
  • Onset ahead: the shift starts after the origin and before the valid time. No forecast can see an onset, so these rows are reported in their own stratum and kept out of the veto only because the veto is also reported with them in.
  • Far from the end: a shift is in force and remains for more than 10 days.
  • Middle: a shift is in force and remains for 1 to 10 days.
  • Near the end: a shift is in force and remains for at most 24 hours.
  • Just ended (context): the origin is within 7 days after the end.

An origin inside an onset ramp counts as in force. A shift whose end was clipped at the 2026-07-01 window edge has a false end, so its rows are excluded from the survival target and from the far, middle, and near strata. The strata use the future end, so they are for scoring only: the equal width scaling uses one factor per arm and month, fitted on all that month's scored rows pooled across strata, so that scaling cannot absorb stratum-specific widening. Unscaled CRPS is reported beside every scaled figure. The dropped rows (no R0 residual history) are tabulated per stratum, and every arm is scored on the rows that all arms share.

Every table and figure reports the loss by lead day, 1 to 9 (leads of 24 to 239 h). Real rows give the event-free veto and a descriptive row for the verified D5 and D16 pair.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
All arms use the same rows, the same equal width scaling, and 2 seeds (the fitted ones). Age is the age of the departure estimated from the lags (experiment 647's departure_age, from the gap signals); R-haz reads it as an input, and B-haz uses the same estimate in S(age + 1 + lead / 24) / S(age + 1). Neither arm sees the true onset.

  • K1: the NRA output; context only for the prevailing scoring.
  • R0-168: K1's quantiles shifted by K1's recent residual times exp(-lead/168 h). No fit.
  • B-haz: the same residual decayed by S(age + 1 + lead / 24) / S(age + 1), where S(d) is the fitted probability that a shift lasts at least d days, the age is in days and the lead in hours, and S is the best single parametric survival curve (exponential, Weibull, log-normal, or log-logistic, chosen by likelihood) fitted to the training shift durations. No neural network. Refitted under each duration mixture.
  • R-old and R-new: experiment 650's heads (fixed duration prior) from its five-month fits, reused. R-old is a refit of experiment 647's head, because that experiment's weights are not available.
  • R-haz: R-new plus an explicit survival output (a non-negative hazard per lead day, so that survival falls monotonically with lead) trained with a binary cross-entropy against the observed share of shifts still on, added to the pinball loss. Training rows are weighted so that the durations follow the stated mixture. The prevailing quantiles are the NRA quantiles plus the depth times the survival probability, in the mixture form of experiment 647, so the band widens with the uncertainty about whether the shift survives.
  • Placebo for R-haz: the same head refitted with each bank training row's target, survival label, in-force label, and weight permuted among the bank rows of the same Primary, so that the target is real but unlinked to the inputs (the in-force flag is a label only, never an input). It keeps the Primary's marginal shift distribution, so it can still move the score; no threshold is set on it. The report gives R-haz minus placebo beside every contrast. A zero-input head is not run.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 stored quantiles) in points of capacity. A negative difference favours the first arm. Cells are the mean over lead days 1 to 9 (leads of 24 to 239 h; no row has a lead of 240 h) of the event-weighted mean, seeds averaged, then the mean of the 5 development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). Intervals are percentile bootstraps over the 5 months. All numbers are on unseen training-family shifts of the scored month (the heads trained on the other 4 months) unless stated. Equal width scaling multiplies each arm's quantile spread about its median by one factor per arm, month, and seed, chosen so that the q05-q95 band covers 0.90 of the month's scored rows pooled across strata.

  • Primary contrast: not met. Where a shift is in force (far, middle, and near pooled), scaled CRPS is K1 9.18, R0 (168 h) 6.72, B-haz 5.98, R-new 5.84, R-haz 5.96, and the placebo 8.31. R-haz minus B-haz is -0.02 [-0.35, +0.24], against the pre-registered -0.05. R-haz minus R0 is -0.76 [-1.01, -0.34], minus R-new +0.13 [-0.11, +0.43], minus the placebo -2.35 [-2.90, -1.49], and minus K1 -3.22 [-4.03, -1.97]. Unscaled: K1 9.93, R0 6.77, B-haz 5.85, R-new 5.65, R-haz 5.80, placebo 8.53.
  • Carrying a shift forward wins far from the end and loses near it. Scaled CRPS far from the end (more than 10 days remain): K1 10.50, R0 7.24, B-haz 5.86, R-new 5.71, R-haz 5.94. Within 24 hours of the end (unscaled, because the scaling factors pool across strata): K1 3.98, R0 6.03, B-haz 8.56, R-new 7.38, R-haz 7.44, placebo 4.50. R-haz minus K1 near the end is +1.41 [+0.42, +2.40] scaled; R-haz minus B-haz there is -0.06 [-0.71, +0.72], so R-haz is no worse than the no-fit hazard baseline, as the plan required. R0 (168 h) hedges better near the end and loses far from it: R-haz minus R0 is +1.45 [+0.76, +2.25] near and -1.30 [-1.38, -1.22] far. The strata use the future end, so far-end rows are shifts that did last and near-end rows are shifts that ended. The pooled in-force row is the fair summary.
  • Middle of a shift and just after the end. Scaled R-haz minus B-haz is -0.19 [-0.50, +0.12] in the middle. Within 7 days after the end (unscaled), K1 3.70, R0 4.92, B-haz 5.25, R-new 4.56, R-haz 4.58.
  • The duration mixture matters for the contrast. Under the short-heavy mixture (0.8 short), R-haz minus B-haz is +0.43 [+0.04, +0.80], so R-haz is worse than B-haz there. Under the long-heavy mixture (0.8 long) it is -0.06 [-0.35, +0.16]. R-haz minus R0 is +0.10 [-0.08, +0.40] and -1.13 [-1.49, -0.58]. The sign of the primary contrast does not hold across the mixtures.
  • The survival probabilities are not within 0.10 in every cell. Averaged over in-force rows on training-family shifts, R-haz predicts survival 0.88, 0.76, and 0.68 at lead days 1 to 3, 4 to 7, and 8 to 10, against observed shares of 0.92, 0.83, and 0.78. B-haz predicts 0.92, 0.81, and 0.73. On the held-out durations (5, 10, 21, and 45 days) R-haz predicts 0.87, 0.75, and 0.67 against 0.86, 0.71, and 0.61. Individual bins with at least 500 rows differ by up to 0.42 for R-haz (see the reliability figures). R-haz sits further from the observed share than B-haz and the fixed prior of experiment 647 (0.89, 0.80, and 0.74).
  • Held-out durations. The same contrasts, scaled and in-force: R-haz minus B-haz -0.74 [-0.96, -0.51], minus R0 -1.46 [-1.89, -0.89], and minus R-new -0.13 [-0.27, -0.01]. The head and the fitted curve are no longer tied there.
  • Veto: not cleared. On injected-bank event-free origins, R-haz minus K1 is -0.13 [-0.69, +0.36] unscaled, so the upper bound is above the 0.03 limit and the experiment cannot tell. On real event-free rows it is +0.00 [-0.33, +0.27] (descriptive). Unscaled CRPS on real event-free rows: K1 3.64, R0 3.49, B-haz 3.58, R-new 3.68, R-haz 3.65, placebo 3.72.
  • NRA forecast. K1_nra is K1's own forecast scored against the unshifted base power, which is the NRA truth. Scored against the unshifted base, K1 scores 3.68 where a shift is in force; against the shifted truth it scores 9.93. The 6.3-point gap is the scoring's fault and not the forecast's. On event-free origins K1 scores 3.70 against the unshifted base and R-haz 3.65 against the observed power.
  • Placebo. Near the end of a shift the placebo scores 4.50 unscaled and K1 3.98, both below R-haz's 7.44, and R-haz minus the placebo there is +1.91 [+1.32, +2.58] scaled; the placebo's lower loss near the end was not explained. The plan's prediction that R-haz beats R0 at every in-force state therefore fails near the end (+1.45). Where a shift is in force, the placebo scores 8.53 unscaled where a shift is in force, 1.4 below K1, so a head unlinked to its inputs still gains by shifting and widening on average. R-haz minus placebo is -2.35 [-2.90, -1.49] scaled, which is the part of the gain attributable to the inputs. No threshold was set on the placebo.
  • Tail calibration (unscaled, where a shift is in force). q05-q95 coverage is K1 0.49, R0 0.63, B-haz 0.73, R-new 0.82, R-haz 0.83, placebo 0.73, against 0.90. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99: K1 2.19, 3.66, 3.59, and 2.04; R0 1.04, 2.12, 2.10, and 0.99; B-haz 0.81, 1.66, 1.73, and 0.80; R-new 0.53, 1.43, 1.47, and 0.51; R-haz 0.53, 1.45, 1.51, and 0.52. On event-free origins R-haz's coverage is 0.89 and its q99 loss 0.24 (K1 0.87 and 0.29).
  • Rows dropped for no R0 history. On training-family shifts, the share of rows kept is 35% for event-free rows, 83% for middle rows, 86% for near rows, 88% for far rows, and 91% for just-ended rows (score/dropped.csv). All arms are scored on the same kept rows.

docs.title: Arms, data, and method
docs.text:
• Arms. K1 (stored, the NRA output); R0 (168 h); B-haz (K1 plus the same residual times S(age + 1 + lead / 24) / S(age + 1) for the best of an exponential, Weibull, log-normal, or log-logistic curve fitted to the training durations of the other 4 months; the best curve was log-normal, log-logistic, or Weibull, depending on month and mixture); R-old and R-new (experiment 650's five-month fits, reused; ml-experiments/00650-*); R-haz (the survival head below); and the placebo for R-haz. Reused code: experiment 647's head, inputs, and fit constants, experiment 650's banks, K1 rebuild, and scaling.
  • R-haz. Experiment 647's mixture head with the survival probability read from 10 non-negative daily hazards (the survival probability falls with lead), a binary cross-entropy against the observed still-on label with weight 0.05, and the departure's age as an input. Rows are weighted so that each shift counts equally and the short-to-long mix is 0.5 (0.8 and 0.2 in the sensitivity runs). The placebo permutes each bank training row's target, label, and weight among the bank rows of the same Primary.
  • Rows and cleaning. Development months only; no valid time on or after 2026-07-01 is read (asserted). Shifts whose end was clipped at that date are excluded from the survival label and from the far, middle, and near strata. Power comes from experiment 650's stored clean stack.
  • Cadence and compute. One small head per scored month, trained on the other 4 months, 2 seeds, so no refit cadence applies. The 40 fits took about 6 minutes on the CPU (8 processes); no graphics processor was used. Fits are in data/ml-experiments/00652-*/fits.
  • Reuse. R-old and R-new predictions come from experiment 650's fits5; K1 rows and banks from experiments 650 and 647.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast (in-force training-family rows, mean of the 11 quantiles as the mean, points of capacity): K1 -0.95, R-new -0.64, R-haz -0.51. Mean absolute error of the median: K1 14.53, R-new 9.81, R-haz 10.18.
  • Triggers fired. The placebo gained 1.4 points against K1 (placebo trigger), the primary contrast missed its bar, and the reliability prediction failed. The leave-one-Primary-out, sister experiment, and later-dependency triggers were not assessed.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet agent reviewed the plan (10 findings; all accepted, 9 changed the plan and 1 was wording) and another reviewed the code before the first fit (12 findings; 1 to 6 and 9 fixed, the rest documented): the class of an event clipped at the window edge, a survival curve fitted to clipped durations, the survival loss on rows with no detected departure, the conditioning of B-haz on the origin, the loss normalisation, and per-event weights. A third agent re-derived the headline numbers (see the pull request).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Every shift is injected. The strata that use the shift's future end (far, middle, near) select on the outcome, so equal width scaling fitted across strata cannot absorb stratum-specific widening, but it inflates K1's factor and makes scaled event-free numbers for K1 misleading; unscaled numbers are given where that matters.
  • The duration mixture is an assumption (0.5 short, 3 to 14 days; 0.5 long, 28 to 112 days). The only measured durations we have are one verified 15-day pair and one unconfirmed step of about 16 weeks. Both heads learn that prior, and the survival curve of B-haz is fitted to it.
  • The intervals use 5 month blocks, so every interval is coarse. The held-out family differs from the training family in a few attributes only.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so real event-free rows may hold unlogged shifts, and the real-row veto is optimistic.
  • No real-row 14-day example forecast is shown; the example figure uses injected shifts.
  • The first-month-pair gate was not run as a separate step.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Train the survival output on shifts whose end depends on observable signals (the gap signals falling back towards zero), because a duration prior alone gives no more than the fitted curve.
  • Train the head with a pinball loss weighted towards rows in the last 24 hours before a shift ends, and test a fixed widening rule that is wider in the last day.
  • Re-test with a measured duration mixture once NGED supplies one.

docs.title: Can a penalised segmentation of the Primaries' residuals build a table of load-shift events with partners, start times, and end times?
docs.text:
At 15 Primary substations, penalised segmentation finds most injected load shifts but did not pair a shift with the neighbour that received the power. A Primary substation is the substation that steps electricity down to the local distribution network, and the project forecasts the demand at each one. Operators sometimes switch a circuit from one Primary to a neighbour, which moves demand between the two. We asked whether the unexplained demand at 15 Primaries, read together, can produce a table of these load shifts: when each starts and ends, which Primary received the power, and how many megawatts moved. The unexplained demand (the residual) is the observed cleaned power minus a demand forecast that uses no lagged power.

We added synthetic load shifts to the residual and decoded the real record from 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30. The table found 0.64 of the injected megawatts (95% interval 0.58 to 0.70), against a predicted 0.70. It paired the two ends of only 0.18 of injected transfers correctly (0.09 to 0.31). On the real record it matched 8 of the 77 logged shifts that last more than a day under the strict timing rule, where the alarms of the earlier detector LR_b20 matched 19 (the table has 246 events, LR_b20 has 78 alarms). The verdict is not supported.

The pre-registered stop rule fires, but only at its boundary. A shuffled neighbour graph gave 2 edge events (5th to 95th percentile 0 to 4) where the real graph gave 4, which is exactly half. Four real edge events are too few to give that placebo much power. The injected pairing recall of 0.18 is the stronger evidence.

docs.title: Terms used below
docs.text:
• Primary-year: one Primary observed for one year. Edge-year: one neighbour link between two Primaries observed for one year.
  • Noise unit: a Primary's typical difference between successive 6-hour block means, in megawatts (0.16 to 1.02 MW across the 15 Primaries, median 0.22 MW). "4 noise units" is 4 times that.
  • World: one copy of the residual panel with synthetic events added. There are 6 worlds in the scored years.
  • Edge event: a pair of opposite-sign shifts at two neighbouring Primaries that start and end together. A shift without a partner has no such pair.
  • LR_b20, RO-NC: the label-trained and label-free detectors of experiment 254 and experiment 130. K1: the day-ahead median forecast of the leaderboard. D3, D5, D16, D22 and the like: anonymised Primary names. P1 to P6: the predictions in the front matter.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: The second figure shows only the bands that the sparse long-event worlds contain, so it has no bars below 7 days.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Recall of injected events (default arm; 6 worlds; 227 events of 4 noise units or more that last 1 day or more). MW-weighted found 0.64 (0.58 to 0.70); unweighted 0.56. Edge transfers (109 donor or recipient ends, from 76 transfers): paired correctly 0.18 MW-weighted (0.09 to 0.31); 0.17 unweighted. This is a share of ends, and only 38% of the 76 transfers have every end found. P1 asked for 0.70 on edge transfers; 0.18 fails. The all-event figure of 0.64 is below 0.70, but the 95% interval reaches 0.70. The intervals resample whole worlds, 2000 draws, so with 6 worlds they are probably too narrow.
  • By duration band (found, MW-weighted, events of 4 noise units or more). 3 hours to 1 day 0.24; 1 to 7 days 0.63; 7 to 21 days 0.70; 21 to 60 days 0.78; over 60 days 0.60; permanent 0.40. Pulses shorter than the 6-hour block were never found.
  • Timing (P2, over the same 227 events, a miss counts as a failure). The start is within 2 hours for 0.53 of events, against 0.70 predicted. The end is within 6 hours for 0.48, against 0.50 predicted.
  • Slow-level arms (sparse worlds; median share of an event taken by the slow level; events per cell 4 to 14, so indicative). Masked and frozen: 7 to 21 days 0.00 (n=4), 21 to 60 days 0.04 (7), over 60 days 0.24 (14), permanent 0.04 (11). Huber with no mask: 0.07, 0.05, 0.33, 0.28. A 30-day random walk: 0.77, 0.90, 0.88, 0.84. The absorption targets of P5 hold (0.10 or less for the masked arm, 0.30 or more for the random walk, in the 21-to-60-day band), as does recall in that band (0.78 against 0.6 or more).
  • Temporary against permanent (P5). Of the 147 found events that start 180 days or more before the record end, 145 were temporary and classed temporary. The other 2 were permanent and were also classed temporary, so no permanent event was ever classed permanent. The 98.6% accuracy therefore says nothing about the permanent class.
  • False events from solar growth and seasonal bias, per injected Primary-year. Solar growth 0.93 (masked), 0.87 (Huber), 0.27 (random walk); seasonal bias 2.2, 2.3, and 0.04. P5 asked for 0.5 or fewer, and the masked arm fails both. This is the only part of P5 that fails.
  • Hard negatives. None of the injected routine steps (389), ramps (221), pulses (221), solo shifts (277), or placebo pairs (98) was classed as an edge transfer. Of the routine steps, 2 were classed as routine and 73 were called shifts without a partner.
  • Where injected edge transfers went (231 events). 148 decoded as no event at all, 51 as a shift without a partner, 31 as an edge event. Because the injected shares (0.5 to 1.1) lie inside the pairing window (0.3 to 1.5), the window does not explain the failure. A re-decode of the 6 worlds with a share window of 0.1 to 3 and conservation limit 10 pairs 0.22, and with wider start and end windows 0.25, so relaxing the rule recovers at most 7 points. Half of the ends are not found at all. All 31 ends called an edge transfer had the right partner, so the pairing has high precision and low recall.
  • Shape of the injected events. Constant-megawatt events: found 0.66, paired 0.14. Events proportional to the donor's own power: found 0.56, paired 0.24. Short-heavy and long-heavy mixtures found 0.62 and 0.43. The stress arm (shares 0.2 to 1.8, starts up to 12 hours apart) found 0.65 and paired 0.07.
  • Real record (2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30, default arm). 246 events, 6.6 per Primary-year: 211 shifts without a partner, 27 ramps, 4 edge transfers, and 4 routine steps. D8 has 9.6 events per Primary-year against a median of 6.8, inside the factor of 2 the plan allows. There are 25 edges between the 15 Primaries. A 100-draw degree-preserving rewiring of the graph gave a median of 2 edge events (5th to 95th percentile 0 to 4), against 4 for the real graph. P3 (a third or fewer) fails, and the stop rule (half or more) fires at its boundary: 2 of 4 is exactly half, and 4 lies inside the placebo's 0-to-4 range. The 4 real edge events are 2 pairs (D10 with D21, D12 with D14), neither of them the verified D3/D22 or D5/D16 pair. The rewired counts are all even, and 21 of 100 draws reach 4 or more (about 0.2 on a one-sided test), so the placebo is weak evidence.
  • Logged shifts (P4). Of 77 logged shifts of more than 1 day that start on or after 2024-01-01, LR_b20's 78 alarms in those years (2.1 per Primary-year) match 19 at the strict rule and 24 at the loose rule. All 246 events of this table (6.6 per Primary-year) match 8 and 17. No confidence threshold gives exactly LR_b20's alarm count: the table at confidence 0.99 or more has 45 events (1.2 per Primary-year, fewer alarms than LR_b20) and matches 5 and 8. P4 asked for 24 of 35 at LR_b20's rate and fails. The 77 and the 35 are different sets of logged shifts: the 35 span the whole record and the 77 are the scored years.
  • Event-free rows. 27.6 of the 37.5 Primary-years lie more than 14 days from every labelled or verified event. The masked arm decodes 5.4 events per Primary-year there, the Huber arm 6.2, and the random-walk arm 2.0. These are upper bounds on false events, because NGED's logs miss events.
  • Verified pair (P6). The verified onsets and ends come from experiment 580: D5 from 2025-12-29 01:00 to 2026-01-13 11:30, and D16 from 2025-12-29 16:00 to 2026-01-13 11:30. The masked arm decodes D5 from 2025-12-30 01:00 to 2026-01-14 11:30 at -1.08 MW, which is 24 hours late at both ends and below P6's floor of 1.2 MW. It decodes D16 from 2025-12-27 02:00 (2.6 days early) to 2026-01-14 12:00 (24.5 hours late) at +2.05 MW. The two events were not paired, because the recipient-to-donor ratio is 1.9 and the pairing window ends at 1.5. The slow level moved by 0.4 points of capacity or less across both, which meets that part of P6. P6 fails on timing, amplitude, and pairing.
  • The October 2024 transfer between D3 and D22 (a seen case, because it set the generator). The masked and Huber arms find events at both Primaries, whose ends differ by about 19 days, and only the Huber arm pairs them. The random-walk arm finds only a 2-day fragment of D3 (18 to 20 November 2024). The December 2025 episode at D10 and the unpaired step at D12 are not shown.

  • Four scenarios (normalised MAE of the median forecast, in per cent of effective capacity; 15 Primaries; scored years). The forecast is the lag-free demand model of experiment 130, not K1. "After the table" subtracts the slow level and the decoded events from the residual, in hindsight. Each half-hour belongs to a scenario according to the decoded events.

    Scenario Half-hours Before the table After the table All rows 631,470 6.31 5.29 Quiet rows (not inside an event, and not in the 7 days after one) 374,405 5.28 5.01 Inside events 185,873 8.62 5.87 The 7 days after an event ends 71,192 5.69 5.30

    The inside-event row falls by construction, because the events are decoded from the same residual. The figure above draws the D5 and D16 case, 14 days before the start to 7 days after the end, with the K1 day-ahead median as the baseline. The other three scenarios are scored but not drawn, because the brief's required example (a verified event) is the only case with labelled ends.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, tail calibration, and the curtailment-cost score: not applicable, because the table produces no forecast.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast: the normalised MAE in the four scenarios above is the only forecast-error measure.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 (a control or known-answer test failed) fired: D5 and D16 were not paired, and the rewired-graph placebo separates from the real graph by 2 events. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its own prediction) fired: P1 to P4 and P6 fail, and P5 fails in its false-event part. A fresh Sonnet auditor re-derived the headline numbers from the stored outputs; see the end of "Reviews and triage" for what it found.
  • Not run: the unconfirmed edge events per edge-year (the second half of P1), the discriminator between injected and real windows, the recall-by-size table, the cross-generator check, the RO-NC count in the second part of the stop rule, the baselines other than LR_b20 (RO-NC, the 24-hour residual detector, the label-free pipeline of experiment 327, the edge-flow fit of experiment 131, and the pair alarm), the wobble check, the rate check at 13 or more Primaries, an ERA5-driven residual for D5, the grouping of two solo shifts into an unseen donor, MW-against-MVA handling of injected amplitudes, the pooled seasonal shape for D18 (it has a one-harmonic seasonal fit), and a staged-return arm apart from the 10% of injected events that carry one.

docs.title: Reviews and triage
docs.text:
• Plan review (Sonnet). 12 findings, 5 of them high severity; all accepted and written into the plan before any code ran.
  • Code review (Sonnet). 15 findings, 2 of them high severity: censored events could never match in the tuning worlds, and permanent events tapered to zero at the record end. Both were fixed. The placebo, the found definition, and the false-event bookkeeping were also fixed or restated. Not fixed: the missing decoder states (see Method) and the weak binding of the conservation cost, which the share window decides in practice.
  • Write-up numbers review (Sonnet). All figures in Results matched the printed reports except the items below. Accepted: the D3 and D22 statement, the permanent-event count, the alarm-rate wording, the D16 offset, the interval method, the Method statements that described unrun components, the unsourced numbers, the missing items in "Not run", the stop-rule and P1 wording, and the per-part pass or fail for P5 and P6.
  • Write-up prose review (Sonnet). Accepted: the cold-read opening and terms, the pronoun and number fixes, the bolded leads, the table indentation, the three required Checks bullets, the trigger-by-trigger audit statement, the present-tense Method, the Files list, and the citations. Rejected: drawing the three other scenario examples (the page says why they are not drawn), and turning every Method bullet into a paragraph (the bullets are short enough to skim).
  • Tuning. Penalties were chosen on 2022 and 2023 injected worlds only (on cost 6, stay cost 0.05), as the highest injected recall with at most 6 decoded events per Primary-year on the real residual of those years. The chosen setting has 5.90 decoded events per Primary-year there, against 6.57 in the scored years. Three settings tie at recall 0.6314 (on cost 6 with stay cost 0.05 or 0.1, and on cost 8 with stay cost 0.1); the choice of stay cost 0.05 is a tie-break. The plan's event-free stratum was not used, because defining it needs labels.
  • Audit (Sonnet, fresh). It re-derived the found share (0.639, interval 0.575 to 0.703), the pairing figure (0.179), and the logged-shift counts (8 and 17 against 19 and 24) from the stored outputs, and found no leakage of 2024-onward years or labels into tuning, and no double matching of a truth event. Accepted: the per-end wording of the pairing figure, the weak-placebo reading, and the relaxed-rule result above. D8 and D5 account for 42 of the 77 logged shifts. The scripts e00653_inject.py and e00653_run.py were edited about a minute after the injected score file was written; the audit's re-run reproduced the stored default-spec results exactly but did not re-run the other generator specs.
  • Lab shortcuts. Injected events are added to the stored residual and not to the power before the demand model is refitted, so recall is a ceiling for events as large as real events. The residual's demand model trained on all rows, so earlier real events leak into its baseline. The grid starts on 2022-01-01, not 2019, and has 15 Primaries.
  • Step 0. The step widths measured on half-hourly power were 0 to 42 half-hours and are not trustworthy at this noise level. A proportional shape beat a constant shape by 4% to 10% of residual variance at D3 and D22 and by 1% to 6% at D5 and D16, which is inconclusive, so both shapes were injected. The generator kept its default edge width of 0 to 4 half-hours.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should test an event table per Primary that leaves out partners. The segmentation found most injected events of 7 days or more; the weak parts are events under a day and the pairing. A longer record with more Primaries, or a residual that already removes more of the daily shape, would be the changes to try before any neural network.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture and algorithm.

  • Input. The residual is the observed cleaned power minus the forecast of the lag-free convex demand model of experiment 130, as stored by experiment 327 (arm C, trained on every half-hour that has a reading). Weather is ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather, so the table is a hindsight product and cannot be made live. Half-hours that the substation_zero rule flags are missing. D15 and D18 lose every row before 2025-03-01. The median residual across all Primaries (the common mode) is removed before segmentation.
  • Noise unit. For each Primary, one noise unit is the robust spread of the difference between successive 6-hour block means, computed once on the uninjected residual and frozen.
  • Slow level (default arm). A seasonal level per Primary, following the slow-level addendum of 9 November 2026 to the design answer: 3 day-of-year harmonics shared by all years plus a linear spline with knots every 365 days, fitted with a Huber (1964) loss. The fit gives zero weight to any window whose 3-day mean residual exceeds 1.5 noise units, widened by 2 days on each side. It refits three times and then freezes, so the segmentation cannot change it. D18 uses a one-harmonic fit. A trend in unmetered solar panels is left out of the default arm, and the page counts the false events that solar growth causes instead.
  • Slow level (comparison arms). Arm S0 is a 30-day random walk with a penalty on its curvature. Arm S1 is the same seasonal fit with a Huber loss and no mask.
  • Segmentation. Each Primary's residual, with the slow level removed, is cut into 6-hour block means. An exact dynamic programme decodes 25 states per block: no shift, and 12 amplitudes log-spaced from 1 to 20 noise units in each sign. The emission is a Student-t density with 4 degrees of freedom. The decoder is a Viterbi (1967) pass, and a forward-backward pass (Rabiner, 1989) gives the posterior that a block is shifted. Staying shifted costs a fixed amount per block and switching on costs an onset price. A final pass refines each start and end to the half-hour by maximising the step statistic within 12 hours of the block boundary.
  • Classing an event. Ramp, routine, and permanent classes are assigned after decoding, not as decoder states. An event is a ramp when at least 0.25 of its change happens gradually over 4 hours or more. An unpaired event of 3 days or less is a routine step when 4 or more such events lie within 30 days of its start at the same Primary. A shift with no return within 180 days is permanent, and one whose end lies beyond the record is open.
  • Pairing. Opposite-sign events at neighbouring Primaries (the graph of experiment 383) are paired when their starts are within 6 hours and their ends within the larger of 12 hours and 25% of the duration. The recipient's share of the donor's step must be 0.3 to 1.5, there are at most 3 recipients, and a loose conservation cost (limit 2.5, after experiment 459) rejects poor sums. A paired event is an edge transfer and an unpaired one is a shift without a partner.
  • Output. One row per event: start and end with intervals, Primaries, direction, megawatts per Primary, class, duration band, and posterior confidence.

Training regime.

  • Fitting. There is nothing to train. Penalties and thresholds are tuned on the 2022 and 2023 injected worlds (see Tuning above), and the 2024 to 2026 years are scored once. NGED's labels enter no penalty, threshold, or mask.
  • Compute. CPU only, 2 cores, no GPU, no fitted neural network. The residual panel already exists.

Measurement.

  • Generator. Injected events follow the design answer's section 4 and the generator ideas file: a donor with 1, 2, or 3 recipients, or an unseen partner; a recipient share of 0.5 to 1.1; amounts from 1 to 20 noise units; durations from 3 hours to 180 days (log-uniform) with short-heavy and long-heavy mixtures; start hours and weekdays drawn from the logged start times; mostly an exact return, some partial and staged returns; a slow drift inside an event; overlap at about 5% of each Primary's time. It also injects permanent shifts and transfers, solar-panel growth of 0.2 to 1 MW a year, and a seasonal bias that repeats every year. Hard negatives are routine steps, ramps of 2 to 12 hours, pulses under 3 hours, solo shifts, opposite-sign steps at two unconnected Primaries (the placebo pairs), and a smooth common mode. MVA Primaries receive |MVA ± transfer|.
  • Step 0. On each verified transfer, the width of each step in half-hours and whether the extra power is a constant number of megawatts or a share of the donor's own daily shape were measured before the generator was fixed. The generator is fixed from D3 and D22 alone; D5 and D16 are measured too, but only to compare, so they stay a hold-out for the pair check. The ranges in P6 were read off this residual in the design answer beforehand, so P6 is not blind.
  • Lab shortcut. Events are added to the stored residual, not to the power before the demand model is refitted, as experiment 297 did with a frozen model. Injected events therefore escape the demand model's absorption. The slow level is refitted in every injected world (mask, three refits, freeze).
  • Injected events, scored years. MW-weighted and unweighted recall by duration band and class, start and end error (a miss counts as infinite error), absorption by band, a confusion matrix of temporary against permanent, false events from solar growth and seasonal bias, and constant against proportional shape. A found event has the right Primary and sign, a start within 12 hours, and (for an edge transfer) the right donor with at least half the recipient megawatts matched.
  • The real record. Events per Primary-year by class, the D8 rate against the median Primary, the 100-draw rewired-graph placebo (the same decoded events, with the neighbour graph rewired so each Primary keeps its number of neighbours), the event-free stratum, and logged shifts matched under the strict rule (start within 4 half-hours) and the loose rule (within 48), as in experiment 254. Alarms of LR_b20 are counted per Primary-year and so are events of this table.
  • Event time series. One figure shows the decoded events beside the observed power and the K1 baseline from 14 days before to 7 days after the verified D5 and D16 pair. Labelled real events are few, so it is descriptive.
  • Intervals. Whole worlds are resampled with 2000 draws. A claim about the real record from the D5 and D16 episode alone rests on one episode.

docs.title: Does one network that outputs both the normal-running forecast and the prevailing forecast, with a learned end detector, beat a frozen K1 plus a separate survival head?
docs.text:
Status: planned. The sections below are the plan; the finished page replaces them.

A Primary is a primary substation. A load shift is a period when the electricity network operator moves part of one Primary's demand onto, or off, a neighbouring Primary. K1 is the neural network of experiments 612 and 613 that forecasts the normal running arrangement (NRA), the demand with no load shift. Experiment 652 built a prevailing forecast (the arrangement now in force) as a small head on the frozen K1 and found that a learned survival output ties a survival curve fitted to shift durations. This experiment asks whether training one network end to end, with an NRA output and a prevailing output, and then adding a learned detector for the end of a shift, does better than that frozen K1 plus head.

docs.title: Results so far
docs.text:
Status: the development-month fits, the first final-test scoring, and a rough Step 0 are done. This experiment did not run the end detector (E1d, E2d, and the placebo), the final-fold fits and window scoring of E0, or the staged-return arm. A follow-up experiment owns them.

Numbers are CRPS in points of capacity. K1 is the neural network of experiments 612 and 613 that forecasts the normal running arrangement (NRA). E0 is the frozen K1 plus the survival-hazard head R-haz of experiment 652. B-haz is K1 plus its residual decayed by the best single survival curve, and R0 is the observed power one week earlier. "Scaled" CRPS multiplies each arm by one factor that equalises the width of its quantile band across strata, months, and seeds.

"J1" is the end-to-end neural network whose prevailing loss does not reach the lag encoder (stop-gradient). "J2" lets the prevailing loss reach the lag encoder. Both read only the lag-encoder outputs: neither reads the hand-built G4 gate state or neighbour summaries, so J2 is the plan's E1 and E2 without those inputs. "C0" is the matched-compute control with no prevailing head.

On the development months, the end-to-end networks lose to the frozen K1 plus R-haz (E0) while a shift is in force. J2 minus E0 is +1.74 scaled points over the in-force strata (month-block 95% interval +1.00 to +2.47), so the predicted gain did not appear. J2 beats J1 by 0.32 points (interval -0.54 to -0.05), and J1 and J2 both beat the matched-compute control C0 in the far stratum.

The NRA veto fails on the development months for all three jointly fine-tuned arms. The veto asks for the upper bound of the 95% interval of each arm's NRA CRPS minus K1's NRA CRPS to stay below 0.03. Unscaled, on injected rows scored against the unshifted base in the far stratum, the NRA output scores 3.90 for J2, 3.91 for J1, and 3.91 for C0, against 3.76 for K1 (+0.14 to +0.15). On event-free rows it scores 3.81, 3.82, and 3.81 against 3.70 (+0.11 to +0.12). Every point estimate already exceeds 0.03. C0 has no prevailing head and fails by the same margin, so the most likely cause is the joint fine-tune recipe (cuts at day 0 and day 14, synthetic shifts), which is weaker than the daily fine-tune of the stored K1.

J2 does better than E0 near and after the end of a shift. In the "ended in the last 24 hours" stratum J2 scores 6.52 and E0 scores 7.44 on the scaled measure, and J2 is lower on all 9 lead days (by 1.81 on day 1 down to 0.33 on day 9). In the "near" stratum J2 scores 6.44 against 7.34.

Table: scaled CRPS on the injected bank, training family, 5 development months, seeds averaged. These are injected shifts on real bases, not real events. The J2 NRA column is scored against the unshifted base, so it is not comparable with the other columns. The unscaled values and the normalised mean absolute error of the median sit in score/tables.json.

docs.text:
Far from the end of a shift, the prevailing outputs of J1 and J2 are 2.2 to 3.1 points worse than E0 on every lead day. After the end of a shift, J2 beats E0 on every lead day, by 0.3 to 1.8 points. K1, C0, and R0 are lower than J2 on most lead days, because K1 and C0 carry no shift. Scaled CRPS, the same rows as the table above:
