Half the injected events are long, so lagged power can help on them. The injected-event generator is experiment 650's, not the log-uniform draw the plan below describes. The training family draws half its durations uniformly from 3 to 14 days and half uniformly from 28 to 112 days, so about a quarter of events last at most 8 days and half last at least 28 days; the held-out family uses 5, 10, 21, and 45 days. All injected tables on this page use that earlier generator. The generator agreed later with the graph-approach discussion (durations log-uniform from 1 to 112 days with random ends, plus a short band down to 3 hours, and experiment 653's injector) was not used, so these tables are not comparable with injected tables built on it. The follow-up experiment uses the later generator. The file score/by_lead_day.csv holds the 95% month-block interval of every cell. The manual heuristic and climatology are not scored on the injected bank: both need the shifted observed power rebuilt at each lag time, which is a separate piece of scoring code, so they appear on the final-test window only.

docs.title: Step 0: edges of the verified transfers
docs.text:
A rough measurement, from the cleaned power at each Primary, of the largest jump within 2 days of the stated start or end. Width is the number of half-hours between 10% and 90% of the step. Where a daily-profile jump is larger than the transfer's own edge, the method picks the wrong jump, so the D3 start (2024-10-28 instead of the 26th) is not usable. At the D16 start one half-hour holds 149% of the step, so the width of 3 there is unreliable too.

Transfer and Primary Start width (half-hours) End width (half-hours) D5/D16, D5 (step about 0.4 of capacity) 6 7 D5/D16, D16 3 0 (one jump) D3/D22, D3 unusable 0 (one jump) D3/D22, D22 2 3

The donor's edge at D5 spreads over about 3 hours, so not every edge is within one half-hour. The generator's training family already draws a ramp for half of its events and a single half-hour step for the other half, so the plan's step-only rule was not applied and the staged-return arm was not run. The numbers sit in score/edges.json.

docs.title: Final-test window, scored once for J2, J1, C0, K1, and the manual heuristic
docs.text:
The frozen candidates are in final/freeze.json (hashes included). The window has no labelled events in the export, so "inside" means rows where the hand-built G4 gate is on: five spells, of 20 to 121 days (median 37 days), so these are long detected states, not injected events. The lead range is 24 to 240 hours. The scoring script holds intervals blocked by origin month (4 months), which are coarse, in final/score/window.json. A row counts as gate-on when the gate is on at the forecast's target half-hour.

Rows Count K1 Manual heuristic J2 NRA J2 prevailing J1 prevailing C0 All 837,868 4.98 4.86 4.82 5.05 5.15 4.84 Gate off, 7 or more days from a spell 694,709 4.11 4.43 3.94 4.45 4.54 3.98 Gate on 137,676 9.40 6.97 9.30 8.11 8.29 9.20 Gate off, under 7 days after a spell 5,483 4.36 5.28 4.42 4.46 4.48 4.40

The "after a spell" row holds 5,483 rows from one month and one spell end, so it carries almost no weight.

Prevailing is not best on all rows, and for J2 the most likely reason is extra error from false alarms on rows with no gate. The next figures come from a second split, which counts a row as gate-on when the gate flag stored on the row is on (119,050 rows, 14%) and gate-off otherwise (718,818 rows, 86%), so they differ slightly from the table above. On the gate-off rows, J2's prevailing output scores 4.54 against 4.05 for its NRA output. Its median differs from its NRA median by 2.75 points on average there, with a mean survival probability of 0.15, so the head carries a shift that is not in force. On gate-on rows that really depart from K1's median by 3 points or more, the prevailing output beats the NRA output (8.97 against 10.56). On the 12% of gate-on rows that do not depart (1.68 against 1.41) it is worse.

The manual heuristic wins on gate-on rows because the shift outlasts its lags. The heuristic is the median-style quantile mix of the observed power 1 to 6 weeks and 49 to 55 weeks earlier. For gate-on rows, 94% of the 1-week members and 76% of the 6-week members lie inside the same gate-on spell, so the old lags already hold the shifted level. The spells last 20 to 121 days, which is close to the long half of the injected durations (28 to 112 days). The other half of the injected durations is 3 to 14 days, which a lag of 1 week or more cannot follow. On the window the old lags help because the real spells are long, whereas many injected events are too short for them to help.

docs.title: Updates to the brief after reading the merged pages
docs.text:
• The maintainer approved opening the final-test window once for this candidate set on 2026-11-09 (the brief records it). The freeze-first rule and the message to the manager still apply.
  • Experiments 647, 650, and 652 are merged; the reference E0 is experiment 652's R-haz and its stored fits. The newest merged experiment, 651, does not change the design.
  • The brief asks that the final-test window (2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31) be opened once. The ml-experiment skill still says no experiment scores a valid time on or after 2026-07-01, so the worker messages the manager, and waits for the maintainer's confirmation, before the window is touched.

docs.title: Feasibility finding that sets the design
docs.text: K1 is not one network. It is a pre-trained network per held-out month and seed (five seeds), followed by a daily fine-tune (d0 and d14 cut-offs), stored as .pt files under data/ml-experiments/00612-*/arms/k1_d5/work/models (seeds 0 and 1) and data/ml-experiments/00613-*/chains/d5/work/ (seeds 2 to 4). Experiment 650 injects shifts by replacing the lag block of the stored input matrix and running the saved networks. Retraining the whole chain on injected shifts would repeat experiments 559, 574, 591, 612, and 613, which is not affordable. The plan therefore starts each end-to-end arm from the saved K1 weights of the fold and seed, and fine-tunes jointly on input matrices with injected lags, as one extra stage. Nothing stores those matrices: experiment 591's run_inject rebuilds them per month (_build_month_p5, build_test) and overwrites the lag block with the injected power, so this experiment adds a cache of them on disk, built with the fold month's standardiser. Everything before that stage is K1 as stored. The cost is that the end-to-end arm differs from a network trained from scratch with the prevailing loss; the page says so.

docs.title: Arms (matched rows, epochs, seeds, folds: leave one development month out, 2 seeds)
docs.text:
• E0: frozen K1 plus R-haz (experiment 652's stored fits; reference).
  • E1: K1's body initialised from the frozen weights and fine-tuned jointly with a prevailing head that reads the lag-encoder outputs and the G4 gate state. First variant: stop-gradient from the prevailing loss into the NRA output. Second variant: the prevailing loss reaches the lag encoder.
  • E2: as E1, with no gate and with neighbour summaries (experiment 610's class 2 recipe, 50% signal dropout). The gate is not an input and G4 is not applied.
  • E1d, E2d: E1 and E2 plus the end detector.
  • Placebo for E2d: E2d refitted with each training row's shift targets, labels, and weights permuted among the rows of the same Primary.
  • No-fit references: R0 (168 h), B-haz, and K1 as context.

docs.title: The end detector
docs.text: The detector takes the freshest half-hours up to the origin of the observed power minus the NRA forecast, in noise units, with the slow seasonal level removed, the all-Primaries median residual removed, and the same quantity at connected neighbours (29 edges of neighbours_nged.json). Two extra inputs: the opposite-sign step at a connected neighbour (a score boost, never a requirement), and a per-Primary routine-step rate from a 60-day context. Its output is the probability that the shift has ended, multiplying the survival output. Placebo for the neighbour input: a degree-preserving rewired copy of the edges. Prediction that could fail: below about 5 points of capacity of depth, the detector does no better than the fitted survival curve. Cost to watch: false alarms on event-free origins and on origins more than 14 days from any event, per Primary-month.

docs.title: Generator
docs.text: Real unshifted bases; onsets and ends are instantaneous steps; duration log-uniform from 1 to 112 days; depth log-uniform from 3 to 50 points of capacity with constant-MW and proportional shapes; donor and receiver, hard negatives, held-out family, and start times from logged starts, as in the brief. Step 0 measures the real edge width at D5/D16 and D3/D22 before any fit; if every edge is within one half-hour, the staged-return arm is dropped. Un-injected time is unlabelled, not negative.

docs.title: Strata, scoring, and final test
docs.text: Strata, lead days 1 to 9, scaling across strata, and the single veto are those of experiment 652, plus the strata "event-free and more than 14 days from any event" and "ended in the last 24 hours". The final test freezes candidates in a file before the window is read, then scores E0, the best end-to-end arm, and the manual heuristic once, in the four scenarios of the brief, with counts of real events per scenario stated as lower bounds.

docs.title: Fold structure and leakage
docs.text:
• K1's weights are keyed by (held-out month, daily cut, seed). The joint fine-tune uses the other four development months for training and early stopping (origin days 0 to 17 train, 21 and later validate, as in experiment 650); the scored month's bank passes and rows never enter either. Fine-tuning from fold-month weights on later months is accepted, as in experiment 652's heads, and the page states it.
  • K1's own daily fit uses month-m rows before its cut. The joint fine-tune trains on no month-m row, so no row has a valid time at or after an origin it was trained under.
  • Equal-width scaling is pooled across strata, one factor per arm, month, and seed, as in 652.
  • The end detector's "observed minus NRA forecast" for past half-hours comes from the NRA forecast issued at an earlier origin for that half-hour (a frozen K1 output), never from the network scoring its own training rows. Whether the freshest half-hours exist at the origin in production is stated on the page; the detector's gain is a ceiling if they do not.
  • Detector training rows contain the hard negatives (D8-style routine steps, pulses under 3 hours, ramps, placebo pairs, common-mode perturbations) at 30% of injected rows, and detection is reported separately on them.
  • Mirrored receiver shifts are not in K1's inputs, as in experiments 647 and 650.

docs.title: Staging and the fit count
docs.text: The full design is about 5 months x 2 cuts x 2 seeds x 7 arms, roughly 140 joint fits. Stage 1 fits E2 and E2d only, at the d0 cut, one seed, on 2025-10 and 2025-12, and times them; the head-only end detector is first fitted on the frozen body, as in experiment 652. Stage 2 adds E1 (both variants), the second seed, and the other months if E2 minus E0 passes the feasibility gate: E2 is no worse than E0 by more than 0.1 points and the veto bound holds on both months. The placebo runs only if E2d shows an effect. The d14 cut is added only if d0 results are not cut-dependent in the stage 1 timing check. The manager is told the staging; the GPU-hour estimate is restated from the timed fold against the fit count before 8 hours are crossed.

docs.title: Added controls and selection rules
docs.text:
• Matched-compute control C0: K1 fine-tuned the same way and for the same epochs with only the NRA loss and no prevailing head, so that E2 minus E0 is not read as a gain from extra epochs. E2 minus E1 is the clean read on dropping the gate; the neighbour-summary inputs are new to the pretrained body, and the page says so.
  • Second contrast bar: E2d minus E2 counts as a gain in a stratum when its month-block 95% interval excludes zero and the point estimate is below -0.3 points there; elsewhere it is descriptive.
  • Best end-to-end arm for the final test: the arm with the lowest pooled in-force scaled CRPS on development months among those that clear the veto, fixed before the window is read.
  • The NRA prediction (within 0.03 of K1) is tested as the veto's interval bound, not as a point estimate.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Figures (at most two panels each): headline loss by lead day and stratum; the time series of observed power, K1, the NRA output, and the prevailing output from 14 days before to 7 days after the verified D5/D16 pair and a few injected events; survival reliability on training-family and held-out durations; the end-detector figure (delay by depth, false alarms); the Step 0 edge-width figure; the four final-test scenario plots; day-ahead and 14-day example forecasts.
  • Sensitivity: short-heavy and long-heavy duration mixtures, with the sign of the primary contrast under each; results by shape; the in-event level drift on a share of events; the staged-return arm unless Step 0 finds pure steps.
  • Release candidate: one parquet per arm under data/ml-experiments/00654-*/release_candidate/ with the brief's columns, and a plain-words README in that folder.
  • The Method section lists K1's body widths, read from experiments 545, 560, 591, and 612. The manual-heuristic forecasts for the final-test origins are looked up first and computed if absent.
  • One line to the manager at: plan PR open, fits started, fits finished, final-test scored, PR merged.

docs.title: Priority and reporting (manager, 2026-11-09)
docs.text:
• The maintainer needs backtest forecasts on disk by the end of 2026-11-09, so the release-candidate parquet files and README come first. The first file is built from E0's stored outputs (experiment 652's R-haz fits and K1's rebuilt quantiles on the real rows); each end-to-end arm adds its own file when its fits finish.
  • Every metric table also reports the normalised MAE of the median forecast (MAE divided by the Primary's effective capacity, as the other tables do).

docs.title: Four scenarios on the development months too (skill, PR 314)
docs.text: The ml-experiment skill (merged 2026-11-09) requires four scenarios for any experiment related to load-shift events, whatever the testing period: all rows; rows outside events and at least 7 days after one; rows inside events; and the 7 days after an event ends. The development-month tables therefore report all four scenarios for each arm, on the injected bank (events known exactly) and, descriptively, on the real labelled and detected events; the final test reports the same four. Each scenario gets its metrics (CRPS, normalised MAE of the median, coverage, tails) and an example time series from 14 days before to at least 7 days after an event.

docs.title: Compute and process
docs.text:
• One GPU process at a time. One fold is timed first. The estimate is 4 to 8 GPU-hours, unmeasured; the worker asks the manager before crossing 8.
  • Standing practices followed: monthly refit, cleaned data, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, save every fitted network, reuse stored predictions (E0, K1, R0, B-haz), tails and avoidable-curtailment cost reported, example forecasts and event time series plotted, draft pull request.
  • Reviews: one Sonnet plan review, one Sonnet code review before the first fit, one results review, one write-up review, one prose review.

docs.title: A per-member solar curve with cell temperature does not help, and the tracker needed observed sunniness
docs.text:
Giving the demand network a solar-output curve for each of the 51 ensemble members, with a panel temperature, still makes its sunny-midday forecast worse than the free network (the same network with no solar curve) (Part 1). The error is 0.2 to 0.35 points, where a point is one percent of a Primary substation's effective capacity, in continuous ranked probability score (CRPS; smaller is better). An ensemble member is one of the 51 alternative weather forecasts that the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts issues for each run.

The 14-day error correction gains almost nothing once it uses only the ensemble forecast's sunniness (Part 2). Experiment 644 found that the free network, plus its own mean error over the previous 14 days, scored 0.3 to 0.6 points better than the free network alone. That experiment applied the correction on half-hours observed to be sunny, and the explicit-solar curve there used the ensemble-mean sunshine. This result gives no support for continuing the explicit-solar line or for the 14-day correction in its experiment 644 form.

Part 1 computes the solar curve per ensemble member (plane-of-array irradiance, a Faiman-model cell temperature, a 0.4% per kelvin derate, clipping at inverter capacity) and subtracts the member average. Part 2 applies the 14-day correction on half-hours the ensemble-mean forecast calls sunny. Both parts reuse experiment 644's rows, cutoffs, five seeds, and bars. "Sunny middays" are 10:00 to 15:00 UTC half-hours with an observed clear-sky index (observed over clear-sky irradiance) of at least 0.7, in the 60 days after each of three cutoff dates (2025-07, 2026-03, and 2026-06).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Arm key. (a) free network; (b) experiment 644's explicit term on the ensemble-mean sky; (c0) the same with this experiment's physics; (c) the curve averaged over members, air-temperature derate; (d) as (c) with a cell temperature; (e) as (d) plus the spread of the curve over members as one network input; (p) and (s) placebos on (d): capacities swapped across Primaries, and the curve of another date.

Each arm's CRPS gain over the free network, with 99.9% intervals; a negative gain means the arm loses to the free network.

Sunny middays, CRPS (points) Day 1-2 Day 3-5 Day 6-10 Free network (a) 3.75 4.28 5.05 Mean-sky term of experiment 644 (b) 4.11 4.53 5.33 Mean-sky, new physics (c0) 4.12 4.53 5.29 Member-level, air temperature (c) 4.10 4.50 5.25 Member-level, cell temperature (d) 4.10 4.51 5.26 Member-level, cell temperature, plus spread input (e) 4.07 4.55 5.32 Capacity-permuted placebo on d 4.22 4.67 5.45 Shuffled-day placebo on d 5.26 5.51 6.09 14-day tracker, observed sunniness (644's arm d) 3.41 3.82 4.48 14-day tracker, forecast sunniness (binary) 3.72 4.35 5.17 14-day tracker, forecast sunniness (continuous) 3.71 4.31 5.15 Shuffled-error placebo of the binary tracker 3.83 4.30 5.08
  • Part 1 fails the decision rule. The free network minus arm (d) is -0.35 [-0.62, -0.16], -0.23 [-0.47, -0.03], and -0.21 [-0.34, -0.06] (negative favours the free network; intervals are 99.9% day-block bootstraps, Bonferroni over 40 contrasts). Over all half-hours the difference is -0.010 [-0.046, +0.025], inside the 0.02 limit, but arm (d) does not beat the free network.
  • Members and cell temperature each add almost nothing. Mean-sky (c0) minus member-level (c) is +0.02 [-0.01, +0.05], +0.03 [0.00, +0.07], and +0.04 [-0.01, +0.09]. Air (c) minus cell temperature (d) is -0.002 [-0.024, +0.014], -0.006, and -0.005. The spread input (e) is 0.03 better than (d) at day 1-2 [-0.06, +0.14] and worse at the other bands.
  • The placebos lose as they should. The capacity-permuted placebo is 0.12 [+0.01, +0.23], 0.16, and 0.19 worse than (d), above experiment 644's bars (0.084, 0.093, 0.123) but with lower interval ends under them at day 1-2. The shuffled-day placebo is 0.8 to 1.2 worse.
  • Part 2 fails the decision rule. The free network minus the forecast-sunniness tracker is +0.03 [-0.12, +0.17] at day 1-2, and -0.06 and -0.12 at days 3-5 and 6-10, against the required +0.17, +0.23, and +0.285. The binary tracker beats its shuffled-error placebo by 0.11 [-0.05, +0.27] at day 1-2 and loses to it at the later bands. The observed-sunniness tracker beats the forecast-sunniness tracker by 0.32 [0.08, 0.57], 0.52, and 0.69.
  • The observed-sunniness gain is consistent with a selection on the outcome. On the 3,657 middays (day 1-2) where observed and forecast sunniness disagree, the free network minus the observed tracker is +0.33 [+0.11, +0.64] (0.41 at day 3-5 and day 6-10), and minus the forecast tracker -0.01 [-0.17, +0.17].

CRPS on sunny middays by lead day for four arms; bands are 95% day-block intervals.

Net demand of one MW Primary, forecast of the free network and arm (d) against the metered value (dashed), for one run in each of two seasons.

The same two runs over the full 240-hour horizon.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does any bias correction of the free network, built only from forecast-time information, beat the plain network on sunny middays? The 14-day tracker does not, and the explicit solar term does not. The remaining sunny-midday error then needs a different input (for example a satellite cloud product) rather than a correction.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median and mean forecast. The median forecast minus the mean of the 11 quantiles averages -0.2 to -1.2 points per Primary for arm (a) and -0.2 to -0.9 for arm (d), so both forecasts are skewed in the same direction.
  • Mean-forecast error beside the quantile score. The mean absolute error of the median forecast on sunny middays (points of capacity, mean over seeds) is 6.42 (a), 6.85 (b), 6.79 (d), 6.52 (forecast-sunniness tracker), and 5.67 (observed-sunniness tracker), so it ranks the arms as CRPS does.
  • Tails on sunny middays. Coverage of the 0.05 quantile is 11.1% (a) and 9.3% (d), and of the 0.95 quantile 99.2% (a) and 98.9% (d), so the lower band is too narrow and the upper band is too wide for all arms. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99: 0.174, 0.700, 1.071, 0.291 (a) and 0.193, 0.752, 1.075, 0.287 (d).
  • Leave one Primary out. The free-minus-(d) contrast stays negative at every band when any one of the six Primaries is left out (day 1-2 range -0.12 to -0.46).
  • Audit triggers. The shuffled-error placebo does not lose to the tracker by the bar (trigger 1), and the tracker result contradicts experiment 644 (trigger 2). The disagreement slice above tests the explanation for the contradiction. A results review found no error in the three headline contrasts.
  • Confound in the disagreement slice. The observed-sunniness tracker corrects only observed-sunny rows and the forecast tracker only forecast-sunny rows, so the two are scored on different corrected rows within one slice, and the observed tracker's gate uses the scored row's own realised sunniness. A test that applies one tracker's history to the other's gate is not run. A results review re-derived the three headline contrasts (-0.354, +0.025, and +0.34) with its own code and matched them.
  • Fitted cell-temperature scale. The farms' posterior mean is 0.65 (standard deviation 0.047) at the 2025-07 cutoff and 0.63 (0.024) at the other two, against a prior range of 0.61 to 1.65; the data pull the scale to the range's weak-heating end.

docs.title: Departures and caveats
docs.text:
• Real world only; experiment 644's step world is not repeated.
  • The cell-temperature scale is one value per cutoff for all six farms, not per Primary, because the farms are not at the Primaries. Its air temperature is the ensemble-mean day-1 forecast (the farm frame has no temperature), and its wind is a fixed 3 m/s.
  • Arms (c0) to (s) were fine-tuned from experiment 639's pretrained weights, which used the old curve; only arm (b) matches its pretraining. Contrasts (c) against (c0), (d) against (c0), and (d) against (c) are free of this mismatch, and they also show no gain.
  • The continuous tracker multiplies the correction by its weight as well as using the weight to average the history.
  • The scoring rows keep experiment 644's selection on observed sunniness, which favours any arm that knows the observed sunniness; this is why the tracker by observed sunniness is shown, not proposed.
  • Per-seed mean absolute errors differ slightly from experiment 644's printed 6.33 for arm (a) because this page averages the error per seed instead of the seeds' mean median.
  • Fewer than 3 dates of history give no correction to a tracker row.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Architecture, arm (d): experiment 554's modular mixture-density network (a weather encoder, a date-time encoder, and a fresh fine-tuning mixer), with an embedding for each of the 16 Primaries, outputs three mixture components, then 11 quantiles. The weather inputs are the cached ensemble mean and standard deviation of 7 variables (shortwave, longwave, 2 m temperature, dew point, surface pressure, precipitation, 10 m wind speed); there are no power lags.
  • The explicit term: the network's target is the demand plus C * u, with C the Primary's calibrated capacity in MW (experiment 639's cal arm, offset learned within a 0.25 MW prior) and u the solar curve per MW divided by one constant per cutoff (the 99th percentile over daylight half-hours of the 24 months before the cutoff, pooled over the six Primaries). The same term is subtracted from every forecast quantile.
  • The curve, per ensemble member: Erbs split of the member's shortwave irradiance, plane of array at tilt 20 degrees and azimuth 180 degrees, direct-current to alternating-current ratio 1.15 clipped at 1, then a derate of 0.4% per kelvin above 25 degrees C on the cell temperature T_air + s * G_poa / (25 + 6.84 * wind). The curve is averaged over the 51 members (a member with a missing value is left out of the mean).
  • Differences of the other arms: (c0) uses the ensemble-mean sunshine, temperature, and wind and an air-temperature derate; (c) averages the per-member curve with an air-temperature derate; (e) adds one mixer input, the standard deviation over members of the curve, standardised; (p) swaps the capacities across Primaries (experiment 639's permutation) and (s) takes the curve of another date (same Primary, half-hour, and 21-day block of the year).

docs.title: Training regime
docs.text:
• Training regime: each network starts from experiment 639's pretrained weights (ERA5 and CAMS estimates of past weather), is fine-tuned on the 24 months of ensemble rows before the test month with a 90-day recency half-life (experiment 554's arm M0), monthly refits, five seeds (0 to 4), 150 fine-tunes in total, 0.49 GPU-hours on one GPU shared with another experiment. Cleaned power only; the six MW Primaries. Experiment 644's farm-gap rows are dropped.
  • Cell-temperature scale: for each cutoff, the posterior mean over a grid of 81 values on a log-normal prior (standard deviation 0.25 in the logarithm, range 0.61 to 1.65), with the likelihood of the six farms' sunny-midday output (clear-sky index at least 0.7, 10:00 to 15:00 UTC, before the cutoff) counted once per farm-day and a free amplitude per farm.

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text:
• Measurement: the 60 days after 2025-07, 2026-03, and 2026-06 (July 2025, August 2025, March 2026, April 2026, and June 2026; nothing from 2026-07-01), every ensemble run at lead 0 to 240 hours, 336,520 half-hours over all hours and six Primaries. CRPS from the 11 quantiles (levels 0.01 to 0.99), averaged over seeds; day-block bootstrap intervals (2,000 resamples) at 1 - 0.05/40; bars are experiment 644's. Row keys are asserted equal to experiment 644's.
  • Tracker: the free network (a) plus the weighted mean error of its day-1 forecasts (lead below 24 hours) over the 14 dates before the forecast's origin date, on midday half-hours whose ensemble-mean clear-sky index is at least 0.7 (binary) or ramps from 0.5 to 0.8 (continuous), and applied on the same half-hours. Shuffled placebos permute the correction across origin dates of the same Primary and cutoff.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• e00655_extract.py (CPU): writes extract/run=<date>.npz, the 51-member shortwave, temperature, and wind speed of each Primary for each daily run from the archive; checks three runs' member means against the cached summaries.
  • e00655_curves.py (CPU): fits the cell-temperature scale, builds the curve tables (curves/<cutoff>/p<index>.npz: c0, c, d, and the spread) for each cutoff.
  • e00655_fit.py (GPU): fine-tunes arms k (c0), c, d, e, p, and s and writes fits/<cutoff>/<month>_real_<arm>_s<seed>.pt, .npz (quantiles), and .json.
  • e00655_analyse.py: scores every arm and tracker, the 40 contrasts, tails, and slices (analysis/contrasts.json).
  • e00655_report.py: draws the figures and prints the quoted numbers.
  • Data, all under data/ml-experiments/00655-pv-member-level-cell-temperature-term-and-forecast-sunniness- tracker/work/ and never committed: extract/ (1.4 GB, read from data/NWP), curves/, fits/, analysis/, logs/.
  • Reused from earlier experiments: experiment 644 (rows, fits of arms a and b, tracker, scoring), experiment 639 (pretrained weights, capacities, placebo rules), and the modules of experiments 48, 87, 397, 405, 428, 510, 554, 634, and 638.

docs.title: Can a solar-capacity probe still work when the substation meter reports apparent power?
docs.text:
The run is inconclusive: the pre-registered gate failed after one cutoff, but the failure came from a flaw in bar A1 and from the starting capacities of the fold fit. The linear probe from experiment 621 loses most of its signal once an added solar farm can push a substation's flow through zero. A probe that models the fold recovered 0.76 to 0.82 of an added fleet's megawatts at 0.5 to 2 times the midday reading, and 0.88 at 6 times only after the starting capacities were widened following the failure (post hoc).

We asked whether the unmetered solar capacity behind a substation can be read when the meter reports apparent power (megavolt-amperes, which never goes negative) rather than signed megawatts. Six Primary substations report signed megawatts. We converted their flow to synthetic apparent power, added a solar fleet of known size to the data, and trained a neural network on the result. The probe then holds the calendar inputs of that neural network fixed, feeds it the weather of other days, and regresses its output on a solar-output curve. The slope is the capacity it reads, in megawatts of alternating current (AC). We compare the capacity read from a neural network trained with the fleet against its twin trained without the fleet. Only the 2026-06 cutoff ran: 24 conditions with 3 seeds each is 72 neural networks, at 23 seconds per fit on the graphics processing unit (GPU).

Terms used below.

  • MW Primaries and MVA Primaries. The six MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) are metered in signed megawatts. The eight MVA Primaries are metered in apparent power: D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21 never come near zero flow on a sunny midday, and D8, D12, and D22 do (they "fold").
  • The fold. Apparent power is the length of a real-power part and a reactive-power part. When solar output exceeds demand, the reading falls to the reactive floor and then rises again, so a linear fit reads the wrong sign.
  • Midday reading. A Primary's median flow over sunny half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC in April to August, in MW.
  • Injection level. The AC capacity of the added fleet as a multiple of the midday reading (0.5×, 1×, 2×, 6×). A fleet is half a real metered farm's output shape and half a physics mixture.
  • Recovery. The capacity read from the neural network trained with the fleet, minus the capacity read from its twin, divided by the fleet's AC capacity. The values below are medians over seeds and Primaries.
  • Probes. L0 is the linear probe of experiment 621. L1 is L0 on rows well above the reactive floor. F4 is the fold model with four solar-output curves, F1 with one, and FA is F4 with a prior on each probe cell's demand from the night reading.
  • Worlds. In the power-factor (PF) world the reactive power is 0.25 times the median real power of that half-hour of the week (power factor 0.97). In the floor world the reactive power is a constant. In the native world the five non-folding MVA Primaries take the same transformation.
  • Tier A and Tier B. Tier A gates a capacity table for the five MVA Primaries that do not fold. Tier B asks whether capacity can be read through the fold, where D8, D12, and D22 stay report-only.

Figure: look at the right half. Orange and green (the linear probes) fall below zero at 2× and 6×. Blue (the fold model, pre-registered starting capacities) holds near 0.7 to 0.8 up to 2×, then also falls at 6×, which the post hoc section explains. Dots are single Primaries, so D5 and D10 sit lowest at 0.5× and 1×.

The pre-registered gate failed: 4 of 11 bars passed (2026-06 cutoff only). The bars are as fixed in the plan commit.

Bar Result Pass A1 Fold-free loss: ratio of PF 0.5× recovery to the signed-world recovery at 1×, for L0 and F4, in 0.90 to 1.10 at 5 of 6 L0 ratios 0.56, 0.90, 0.44, 0.87, 0.88, 0.91 for D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16; F4 0.47 to 1.28 fail A2 Native worlds: recovery within ±0.12 of the six's median (0.68) at 4 of 5 4 of 5 (D3 0.83 is outside; D2, D4, D19, D21 are 0.73 to 0.78) pass A3 Placebos: 95th percentile of capacity read under 0.25 of the real 0.5× capacity read climatological 6 of 6 MW Primaries and 5 of 5 MVA Primaries; boxcar 5 of 6 and 5 of 5 pass A4 Leave-one-Primary-out factor in 0.55 to 0.95, spread under 0.15 0.677 to 0.683 at all six pass A5 Interval coverage at least 60% 0.18 fail B1 Four worlds (PF 1×, PF 2×, floor 1×, floor 2×) each have FA calibrated recovery in 0.75 to 1.25 at 4 of 6 4, 5, 1, and 5 of 6 respectively fail B2 PF 6×: FA calibrated recovery in 0.75 to 1.25 at 4 of 6 2 of 6 (values 0.55 to 6.78) fail B3 At PF 2×, FA's median absolute error from 1 is at least 0.10 below L1's 0.152 against 0.234, gap 0.08 fail B4 Sun-rising-load placebo: FA under 0.25 of the 6× recovery at 5 of 6, and crossing flags on under 10% of cells 6 of 6; flags on 0.0% of cells pass B5 Interval coverage at least 60% at PF 1× and 2× 0.17 and 0.14 fail B6 Crossing map: balanced accuracy at least 0.80 at 1× and 2×, false crossings at most 10% at 0.5× 0.73 and 0.94; 7.6% fail
  • A1's denominator is a design flaw. No signed world was trained at 0.5×, so the code divides by the signed world at 1×. The linear probe's recovery falls from 0.68 to 0.53 between those levels in the PF world and stays at 0.76 to 0.79 in the signed world. At the same level (1×), the ratio of PF to signed recovery is 0.69 for L0, 0.89 for L1, and 1.09 for FA.
  • A3 is a one-sided bar. The linear probe reads the climatological placebo at -0.21, which is far from zero and still passes, because a negative reading is under 0.25.
  • D5 and D10 cause several bars to fail. Their midday readings are 0.88 and 1.2 MW, so a 0.5× injection is 0.44 and 0.60 MW, close to the seed spread.
  • Intervals are narrow. A5 and B5 fail because the bootstrap (40 draws over days) carries no variation between neural networks, and the leave-one-Primary-out factor spread (0.01) does not widen the interval to include it.

docs.title: Post hoc: widening the fold fit's starting capacities fixes the failure at 6×
docs.text:
The audit found that the fold fit sits on its zero-capacity bound at almost every MW Primary in the 6× worlds. The fit started at 0.25, 1, and 3 times the midday reading, and a true capacity of 6 times lies beyond every start. Starting also at 6 and 8 times, post hoc and with no retraining, gives:

Condition (median over seeds and the six MW Primaries) FA F4 F1 Fleet 0.5× 0.74 0.67 0.70 Fleet 1× 0.70 0.64 0.72 Fleet 2× 0.80 0.78 0.71 Fleet 6× 0.88 0.83 0.72 Physics mixture 6× 0.94 0.87 0.78 Sun-rising load (placebo; no solar added) -0.11 -0.13 -0.09

FA at 6× reads 0.99 at D11 and 0.63 at D5, and the five native MVA Primaries read 0.91. No bar is re-scored with these rows.

Figure: the cloud-following load is the placebo that fails. The fold model reads it at 0.62 of its size and the linear probe at 0.44, so neither probe separates solar output from demand that follows the clouds. Dots at the same level as the reference row would count as a read-out of real solar.

docs.title: Real-data capacity (uninjected 2026-06 neural networks, raw)
docs.text:
For the five MVA Primaries that do not fold, the linear probe's raw capacity divided by the 0.68 factor of bar A4 gives a calibrated column, which assumes power factor 0.97. The fold-model column is raw, with the pre-registered starting capacities.

Primary Linear raw (MW) Linear divided by 0.68 (MW) Fold model FA raw (MW) D2 5.2 7.6 8.0 D3 2.1 3.0 3.0 (up to 4.8) D4 1.0 1.4 3.2 (1.1 to 3.6) D19 1.1 1.7 2.1 D21 1.2 1.8 1.4 D8 (report only) 1.8 2.6 2.1 D12 (report only) -3.0 not defined 5.3 D22 (report only) 1.3 2.0 1.7

Figure: compare orange with blue at D12. The linear probe reads -3.0 MW there, as experiment 479 did on the raw reading, and the fold model reads +5.3 MW. D12 is the only Primary whose probed reading rises with sun; the other 13 fall. Sites labelled report only fold. The estimates are raw and uncalibrated.

Figure: D12 is flagged at midday in most months and D22 is not flagged. The map is unvalidated because bar B6 failed. Grey cells have no flagged crossing, and blank cells have no probe cell.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text:
• Fold fit. Three starting capacities (0.25, 1, and 3 times the midday reading) in place of a profile over 121 capacities; 40 bootstrap draws in place of 200; 40 donor rows per probe cell. The post hoc starts at 6 and 8 times are labelled above.
  • A1. Compared with the signed world at 1×, as above. Stop rule 3 (stop if A1 fails) fired as pre-registered.
  • Fleet. The physics half of the fleet is driven by the Primary's own sky, with no offset to a neighbouring pixel. The boxcar placebo is capped at the Primary's midday reading per event, because an event sized to the daily energy of the 2× fleet exceeded the load.
  • L1 probe. The floor estimate in the one-sided probe's threshold is capped at half the midday reading.
  • Native worlds apply only in the PF world.
  • Not run. The 2026-03 cutoff, the signed-world energy conversion, and the example S(u) curves beyond their class (falling at 13 Primaries, rising at D12).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The reactive power of the real meters is unknown, and power factor 0.97 is an assumption.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the clean rows may hold unlabelled events.
  • D8's flow regime changed in 2025, and the neural network has no year input, so it averages over the change.
  • Nothing here is replicated: one cutoff and one set of farms.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Forecast checks: the experiment scores no forecast, so the median-minus-mean and quantile-score checks do not apply.
  • Audit triggers that fired: a control failed (A1), the result contradicted its prediction for Tier B at 6× (explained by the audit), and a follow-up would depend on the unreplicated 0.79 at 2×. A leave-one-site-out flip and a nested-arm win did not fire. The audit report is e656_audit.md in the private briefs folder.
  • Audit triage: accepted finding 1 (the post hoc table), accepted finding 3 (the A1 caveat), and accepted the trigger list (finding 5). Finding 2 reproduced the headline numbers, and finding 4 found no bug in the world construction.
  • Code review (Sonnet): accepted the boxcar cap, the sun-rising-load scaling, the arm-specific night reading, the basis-curve normalisation, and native worlds in the PF world only. Rejected the profile-likelihood deviation as a defect, and listed it above.
  • Write-up review: accepted the A2 and rounding corrections, the missing captions, and the figure fixes.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does the fold model with a night prior keep its 0.7 to 0.9 recovery at a second cutoff and a second set of farms, with a signed twin at every level, starting capacities out to 8 times, and an injection that is not sized by D5's small midday reading? Does it still pass the sun-rising-load placebo, and can anything separate solar output from the cloud-following load that it misreads?

docs.title: Does subtracting an explicit solar term from the Primaries' residuals reduce false events at sunny midday without losing injected events?
docs.text:
An explicit solar term changed nothing, because the demand forecast already allows for the sunshine at these substations. A Primary substation steps electricity down to the local distribution network. Some solar panels sit behind the substations without being metered, so they appear only as lower demand. The previous experiment, experiment 653, searched the demand forecast's errors (the residual) for load shifts and decoded 5.4 events per Primary-year in rows far from any logged event, which are probably false. We asked whether unmetered solar behind the six Primaries whose power is reported in megawatts (the MW Primaries: D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16) explains some of them. We built a solar curve from ERA5 (the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' reanalysis of past weather), scaled it by the capacity of experiment 649, and subtracted it from each MW Primary's residual.

The fitted scale (the gain) is 0.003, against a gate of 0.05 below which the solar term is too small to be worth using. The solar arm therefore decodes the same 246 events as the plain arm, finds the same injected megawatts, and changes the error on sunny middays by 0.01% in the scored years. The verdict is not supported, and the contrasts below are reported as null, not as passes.

docs.title: Terms used below
docs.text:
• Residual: actual power minus the forecast of the lag-free demand model of experiment 130, in MW. Sunshine that the forecast ignores makes the residual negative, so the gain is fitted on the negated residual.
  • Gain (g) and gate: g is the fitted scale of the solar term. The gate is a stop rule fixed in the plan: when g is under 0.05, the solar term is too small to matter and the arms are not expected to differ.
  • Plain, solar, and placebo arms: the residual of experiment 653; that residual with the solar term subtracted; and the same with each Primary given another Primary's capacity. The placebo is neutral by construction, because it leaves the decoder and the nine other Primaries unchanged.
  • Event-free stratum: rows more than 14 days from any labelled or verified event. A Primary-year is one Primary observed for one year. A sunny-midday day has 70% or more of its half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC with a clearness index of at least 0.7. The clearness index is ERA5 irradiance divided by the clear-sky irradiance of Haurwitz (1945).
  • World, noise unit, common mode, slow level: a world is one copy of the residual panel with synthetic load shifts added; a noise unit is a Primary's typical difference between successive 6-hour block means; the common mode is the median residual of all Primaries, removed before decoding; the slow level is a seasonal baseline fitted to each residual. All are as in experiment
  • The strict and loose rules for matching a logged shift are those of experiment 254.
  • P1 to P5 (front matter): P1, sunny-midday false events fall by 20% or more; P2, injected recall falls by at most 0.03; P3, other-day events change by under 10%; P4, the placebo lowers the sunny-midday rate by at most half as much as the real capacity; P5, the sunny-midday error falls by 3% or more.
  • K1: the leaderboard's day-ahead median forecast. D5, D16, and the like: anonymised Primary names.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: In the third figure the shading marks decoded events: the lower half is the plain arm and the upper half is the solar arm. The two residual lines coincide, and so do the two sets of events.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Gain and P5 (the gate). The pooled Huber slope of the negated residual on C·u(t) is g = 0.0031 over 50,115 half-hours (ordinary least squares 0.0013), under the gate of 0.05. The normalised mean absolute error of the residual on sunny-midday half-hours at the six Primaries moves by +0.11% in the tuning years and +0.01% in the scored years, against a planned fall of 3%. The placebo moves it by +0.07% and -0.02%. P5 fails.
  • P1, sunny-midday false events (event-free stratum, six MW Primaries, scored years). The stratum holds 24 events over 4.43 Primary-years, 5.42 per Primary-year, in all three arms. The change is +0.0% (month bootstrap interval +0.0 to +0.0). P1 asked for a fall of 20% or more and fails. The sunny-day definition uses the same irradiance as the solar term, so P1 would have been partly mechanical.
  • P3, other days. The stratum holds 43 events over 6.95 Primary-years, 6.18 per Primary-year, in all three arms. The change is +0.0%, which meets P3's limit of under 10%.
  • P2, injected recall at the six Primaries (events of 4 noise units or more that last 1 day or more; 87 events in 6 worlds). MW-weighted recall is 0.579 in every arm, and the paired difference is +0.0000. P2 holds, but trivially.
  • P4, placebo. The solar arm's fall in the sunny-midday rate is zero, so the ratio of the placebo's fall to the solar arm's is undefined. P4 cannot be scored.
  • Equal width. The arms have 104 events each at the six Primaries, so no thinning is needed.
  • Logged shifts. Of the 77 logged shifts that last more than 1 day, every arm matches 8 under the strict rule and 17 under the loose rule (2 and 5 of 30 at the six Primaries).
  • Event-free stratum per arm (15 Primaries). 148 events over 27.5 Primary-years, 5.39 per Primary-year, in every arm (6.57 over all scored rows).
  • Plain arm against experiment 653. The plain arm reproduces experiment 653's 246 real events.

  • Four scenarios (normalised MAE of the median forecast, in per cent of effective capacity; scored years; the forecast is the lag-free demand model of experiment 130, not K1). "After the table" subtracts the slow level and the decoded events, in hindsight.

    Scenario Half-hours Plain before Plain after Solar before Solar after All rows, 15 Primaries 631,470 6.31 5.29 6.31 5.29 Quiet rows, 15 Primaries 374,405 5.28 5.01 5.28 5.00 Inside events, 15 Primaries 185,873 8.62 5.87 8.62 5.87 The 7 days after an event, 15 Primaries 71,192 5.69 5.30 5.69 5.30 All rows, six MW Primaries 262,438 5.05 3.95 5.05 3.95

    The solar arm differs from the plain arm in the second decimal at most. The solar arm's quiet-row and inside-event half-hour counts differ slightly from the plain arm's (374,426 and 185,852), because some event edges move by a few half-hours. The figure above draws the D5 and D16 case, 14 days before the start to 7 days after the end. The other scenarios are scored but not drawn, because the lines would coincide.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, tail calibration, and the curtailment-cost score: not applicable, because the table produces no forecast.
  • Mean-forecast error beside each contrast: the normalised MAE of the forecast's median in the four scenarios above is the only forecast-error measure.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 (a control or known-answer test failed) did not fire: the plain arm reproduces experiment 653 exactly. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fired, because P1 and P5 fail and P4 cannot be scored. The other triggers did not fire: no later experiment relies on this result, and no arm was nested in another. A fresh Sonnet reviewer tested whether the null is a bug (see the next section) and found that it is not, which serves as the audit.
  • Not run: the other three scenarios at the six Primaries, recall by size, a decoder run on the residual before the common mode is removed, a forecast-weather version of the solar term (experiment 644 found that ensemble weather removed the gain of an explicit term), a month-class gain, and an injection before the solar term.

docs.title: Reviews and triage
docs.text:
• Plan review (Sonnet). 12 findings. Accepted: the pooled gain with the placebo reusing it (a per-Primary gain would cancel the capacity), the sign convention, the stop gate, frozen noise units, a single capacity vintage, the paired interval for recall, counting an event by its start day, and the feature-table facts. Rejected: a month-class gain and an injection-before-the-term sensitivity run (both listed under not run), and the simpler per-Primary regression (the design already is one).
  • Code review (Sonnet). 10 findings. The reviewer re-derived the null and found it real: the series mapping is right; shifting the curve by up to 4 half-hours leaves g between 0.0023 and 0.0034; the sign is right; and the mean midday residual at the six Primaries differs between sunny and cloudy days by at most 0.37 MW (D5), where about 1 MW would show a missing solar term. Before the common mode of all Primaries is removed, g is 0.075 in the tuning years and 0.024 in the scored years; the 0.075 is above the gate but was not tested in the decoder. The reviewer did not re-run the decoder; the plain arm matching experiment 653's 246 events covers that.
  • Lab shortcuts. The capacity table comes from probes pretrained to 2026-06, so it carries information from the scored years. The solar term is hindsight irradiance and cannot be made live.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should inspect the false events of the event-free stratum one by one. The solar term does not explain them, and sunny middays are not their main home, so the experiment can list what each one is: a step in one Primary's residual, a step in the common mode of the Primaries, or a missing-data edge.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture and algorithm.

  • Solar curve. For each of the six megawatt Primaries, u(t) is the ERA5 surface shortwave irradiance (the shortwave column of the feature table of experiment 6, half-hourly), divided by its 99th percentile over daylight half-hours of 2022 and 2023 at that Primary. The code checks that the column carries no forecast-origin, lead, or ensemble column, no duplicate rows, zero irradiance at night, and a clearness index of at most 1.10.
  • Capacity. C is the calibrated 50th-percentile AC capacity of experiment 649 (probe cutoff 2026-06, April to September 2025): 2.98, 2.44, 2.54, 3.42, 3.92, and 3.16 MW at D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16.
  • Gain. One pooled gain g is the slope of a Huber regression of the negated residual on C·u(t), over daylight half-hours from April to September of 2022 and 2023 at the six Primaries, with half-hours inside logged or verified events left out, clipped to 0 to 1.5. The solar arm's residual is the plain residual (after the common mode of all Primaries is removed) plus g·C·u(t). The placebo gives each Primary another Primary's C in a fixed cycle, with the same g.
  • Decoder. The decoder, penalties, and slow level of experiment 653, with that experiment's frozen noise units; the slow level is refitted on each arm's residual.

Training regime.

  • Fitting. Only the gain is fitted, on 2022 and 2023. Nothing else is tuned, and the 2024 to 2026 years are scored once. NGED's labels enter only the exclusion of event rows from the gain fit.
  • Compute. CPU only, one core, under 2 minutes for all stages. No fitted neural network.

Measurement.

  • Injected worlds. The six worlds of experiment 653 with the same seeds. Events are added to each arm's residual, and truth is identical across arms.
  • Real record. Events per Primary-year in the event-free stratum, split by whether the day of the event's start is a sunny-midday day, with month-bootstrap intervals; recall of injected events by duration band, with a paired world bootstrap; logged shifts matched at the strict and loose rules; the four-scenario normalised MAE; and the D5 and D16 time series.

docs.title: Does a neural network that reads all 15 Primaries' demand residuals at once find and pair load-shift events better than the penalised segmentation of experiment 653?
docs.text:
A neural network that reads all 15 Primaries' demand residuals together did not find or pair injected load-shift events better than the penalised segmentation of experiment 653. A Primary substation is the substation that steps electricity down to a local distribution network, and the project forecasts the demand at each Primary. Operators sometimes switch part of a circuit from one Primary to a neighbour, which moves demand between the two (a load shift). The unexplained demand (the residual) is the observed cleaned power minus a demand forecast that uses no lagged power. Experiment 653 decoded the residual of each Primary with a penalised segmentation. We asked whether a recurrent neural network, trained on many synthetic load shifts added to the real residual, finds more of those load shifts and pairs the two ends of a transfer more often. We scored the network on experiment 653's own residual panel, synthetic events, and scorer.

The network found 0.48 of the injected megawatts (mean of 3 seeds, seed range 0.44 to 0.54) in the first look and 0.52 (0.50 to 0.54) in the second look, against 0.64 for experiment 653. The network paired 0.16 and 0.17 of injected transfers, against 0.18. The verdict is not supported. The pre-registered stop rule closes the neural-network line of work on this panel. This panel is not the full 2019-onward history of ERA5 and CAMS weather estimates, because the cross-fitted 2019-onward residual does not exist (the experiment reads experiment 653's panel: 15 Primaries, 2022-01-01 to 2026-06-30). The result therefore does not show that a much larger training history would fail; a rerun on the full history is the step to take only if the maintainer wants that question answered.

The first look is the plan as pre-registered. The second look is a re-run made after the first look showed overfitting (validation loss flat while training loss fell). The plan allowed one re-run after a fixable bug, and we used it for overfitting, which stretches that rule. The second look used a smaller network (32 hidden units), dropout 0.3, weight decay 0.01, Gaussian noise on the inputs, and 300 injected worlds instead of 120. It was chosen after the first look's scored numbers were read, so its numbers are not blind to them. A seed is one random start of network training; each look has three.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: The first figure shows that the second-look network found fewer injected megawatts than experiment 653 in nearly every duration band. The second figure shows the verified D5 and D16 transfer, which the network decoded late and did not pair.

docs.title: Terms used below
docs.text:
• Noise unit: a Primary's typical difference between successive 6-hour block means (experiment 653). World: one copy of the residual panel with synthetic events added; there are 16 scored worlds. Edge: a neighbour link between two Primaries in the electricity network. Edge transfer: a pair of opposite-sign shifts at two linked Primaries that start and end together.
  • Found: an injected event counts as found when it has a decoded event at the same Primary and sign, a start within 12 hours, and a span overlap of at least half. Paired: an injected transfer is found and decoded as an edge transfer with the right partner.
  • Strict and loose match: a logged shift counts as matched when a decoded start lies within 2 hours or 24 hours of the logged onset (experiment 254, which defines LR_b20 and RO-NC). K1: the day-ahead median forecast of the project's leaderboard. RO-NC and LR_b20: two alarm rules from experiment 254 that flag likely logged shifts; LR_b20 is the one compared here. D5, D16, and D18: anonymised Primary names.
  • Validation worlds: injected worlds built on 2023-07-01 to 2023-12-31, used to choose decoder settings and the stopping point, never the scored years (2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Injected events found (spec default, 227 events of 4 noise units or more lasting 1 day or more, MW-weighted). Experiment 653 0.64; first look 0.47, 0.54, 0.44 by seed (mean 0.48; 95% interval for seed 0, resampling the scored worlds, 0.40 to 0.54); second look 0.54, 0.52, 0.50 (mean 0.52; seed 0 interval 0.46 to 0.66). The experiment 653 figure reproduces its stored table exactly. P1 (0.72 or more) fails in both looks.
  • Equal-rate comparison. The network calls 0.4 to 0.8 real-record events per Primary-year, so the comparison at experiment 653's 6.6 events per Primary-year is not available. Across the whole decoder grid (events per Primary-year from 0.4 to 2.1, seed mean) the first look found 0.29 at the highest rate and 0.48 at its chosen setting. Within the grid, recall did not rise with the rate, so raising the rate in that range would not have closed the gap. Rates near 6.6 were not tested.
  • Paired. MW-weighted share of injected transfer ends paired correctly: experiment 653 0.18; first look 0.17, 0.19, 0.11 (mean 0.16); second look 0.20, 0.19, 0.13 (mean 0.17). Applying experiment 653's pairing rule to the network's events instead of the network's edge posterior gives 0.15 (first look) and 0.17 (second look). P2 (0.50 or more) fails.
  • By duration band (second look, found). 1 to 7 days 0.53, 7 to 21 days 0.58, 21 to 60 days 0.60, over 60 days 0.53, permanent 0.30. Experiment 653: 0.63, 0.70, 0.78, 0.60, 0.40. Events shorter than a day are not in this subset.
  • By injector spec (found / paired; second look; experiment 653 in brackets). Constant megawatts 0.48 / 0.20 (0.66 / 0.14); proportional to the donor's power 0.37 / 0.02 (0.56 / 0.24); short-heavy 0.40 / 0.09 (0.62 / 0.20); long-heavy 0.43 / 0.03 (0.43 / 0.11); stress 0.42 / 0.03 (0.65 / 0.07).
  • Timing (spec default, a miss counts as a failure). The start is within 2 hours for 0.39 to 0.44 (first look) and 0.37 to 0.40 (second look) of injected events (experiment 653 0.53); the end is within 6 hours for 0.35 to 0.40 (0.48). Among found events with an end, the end is within 6 hours for 0.73 to 0.83 (experiment 653 0.82). P6 (0.65 of all injected events) fails.
  • Cross-injector check (first look only; found by a network trained on the test injector, by a network trained on the other injector, and the drop). Test injector g1 (constant megawatts, square edges): seed 0 0.32 / 0.48 / -0.15, seed 1 0.42 / 0.47 / -0.06, seed 2 0.61 / 0.34 / +0.27. Test injector g2 (shares of the donor's power, wide edges, loose shares, staggered starts): 0.39 / 0.39 / +0.01, 0.39 / 0.36 / +0.03, 0.29 / 0.52 / -0.24. The drop ranges over 0.42 (g1) and 0.27 (g2) across seeds, 5 to 8 times the 0.05 threshold, so P3 is not shown either way. The verdict does not depend on P3, because P1 already fails. The second look did not rerun this check.
  • Real versus injected events. A logistic classifier on four window features (step size, step width, noise after, noise before) separates 81 injected edge events from 56 real events (all verified events of experiment 580 plus experiment 653's 4 real edge events) with an area under the curve of 0.91 (95% interval 0.84 to 0.94, out-of-bag injected events). P4 (below 0.65) fails. The real set mixes Primaries and years, so part of the separation may be a Primary or season effect.
  • Real record, scored years. First look: 15, 17, and 26 events (0.40, 0.45, 0.69 per Primary-year); strict and loose matches of the 77 logged shifts of more than a day 2 / 4, 3 / 4, and 7 / 11. Second look: 18, 20, and 29 events; matches 4 / 6, 4 / 8, and 5 / 8. Experiment 653: 246 events, 8 / 17. LR_b20: 78 alarms (2.1 per Primary-year), 19 / 24. P5 (at least 11 strict matches) fails in every seed. Edge events on the real record: 0, 2, and 0 per seed in the first look and 0, 2, and 0 in the second look; the rewired graphs give a median of 0, so P7 is not informative.
  • Event-free rows. In rows more than 14 days from every logged or verified event, the second look (seed 0) decodes 3 events (0.11 per event-free Primary-year) and experiment 653 decodes 148 (5.4). The low rate follows from the boost selected by tuning on validation worlds (see Method), not from higher precision, since the network also finds fewer injected events.
  • Verified pair (D5, D16). The verified onsets are 2025-12-29 01:00 (D5) and 2025-12-29 16:00 (D16), with a shared end on 2026-01-13 11:30. All six networks decode D5's start 24 hours late (2025-12-30 01:00). Five decode D16's start 9.5 hours late (2025-12-30 01:30) and one (second look, seed 1) 36 hours late. Both ends are about 24 hours late (2026-01-14 11:30 and 12:00), D5 at about -1.1 MW and D16 at +2.1 MW, and none pairs them. Experiment 653 is also 24 hours late at D5.
  • Four scenarios (normalised MAE of the median forecast, per cent of effective capacity; the forecast is the lag-free demand forecasting model, seed 0; "after" subtracts the slow level and the decoded events in hindsight). Second look: all rows 6.31 to 5.88; rows outside events and 7 or more days after an event 6.01 to 5.83 (614,336 rows); inside events 19.62 to 8.14 (13,438 rows); the 7 days after an event 7.36 to 6.99 (3,696 rows). First look: 6.31 to 5.94; 6.07 to 5.86; 16.78 to 8.99; 7.41 to 8.45. Experiment 653: 6.31 to 5.29; 5.28 to 5.01; 8.62 to 5.87; 5.69 to 5.30. The inside-event row falls by construction, and each arm's row sets differ because the decoded events differ.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site, tail calibration, and the curtailment-cost score: not applicable, because the table produces no forecast. The normalised MAE in the four scenarios is the only forecast-error measure.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 (a known-answer or discriminator control failed) fired: P4 and the D5 and D16 pairing fail. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fired: P1, P2, P4, P5, and P6 fail. The audit and its triage are in "Reviews and triage".
  • Unlogged events. National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED)'s logs miss events, so the fractions of decoded events that match a logged shift undercount true matches, and counts of true events are lower bounds.
  • Not run: the cross-injector check on the second look, the recall-by-size comparison on real events, the causal variant, the 2019 to 2021 history, and the injected-world rewired-graph placebo (pairing recall on rewired graphs).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture.

  • Input. Per Primary and 6-hour block: the residual with experiment 653's masked frozen slow level removed, in noise units (clipped at 30); a present flag; the 1-day and 3-day step statistics (mean of the next blocks minus mean of the previous blocks) in noise units; the share of blocks in a centred 60-day window whose 1-day step exceeds 4 noise units; and the sine and cosine of the block's position in the day.
  • Encoder. A two-layer bidirectional gated recurrent unit shared by all Primaries (48 hidden units per direction in the first look; 32 with dropout 0.3 in the second look), a layer that joins each Primary's state with the mean state of its neighbours, and a second bidirectional recurrent layer.
  • Heads. Per Primary and block: four class logits (none, shift, ramp, routine), a sign logit, and an amplitude. Per link between two Primaries: three logits (off, first donates, second donates), antisymmetric in direction by construction.
  • Decoder. A four-state Viterbi path per Primary (none, up, down, other) with onset penalty 0.5, sign-flip penalty 1.0, and a factor of 10 on the 'none' probability (chosen on validation worlds); segments under 1 noise unit are dropped; starts and ends are refined to the half-hour within 36 half-hours of the block boundary. Pairing joins opposite-sign events at linked Primaries whose starts are within 6 hours, whose spans overlap by at least half, whose recipient-to-donor megawatt ratio lies in 0.3 to 1.5, and whose mean edge posterior reaches the cut-off (0.3 or 0.5, chosen on validation worlds).

Training regime.

  • Data. Experiment 653's injector, unchanged, adds synthetic events to the real residual of 2022-01-01 to 2023-06-30 (120 worlds in the first look, 300 in the second, half constant-megawatt and half proportional shapes). Each step draws 8 random 180-day crops; 20% of crops carry no injection. D18 has no data in these years. The injector is the one merged in experiment 653; the later shared generator of experiment 660 was not used.
  • Targets and loss. Class, sign, amplitude, and edge state per block from the injected truth; time with no injected event has target 'none' at weight 0.1. Weighted cross-entropy, binary cross-entropy for sign, Huber loss for amplitude (weight 0.1), and a small penalty on state changes. AdamW, learning rate 0.003 with a one-cycle schedule, 2,400 steps, checkpoint with the lowest validation loss, 3 seeds. About 3 minutes per network on the shared GPU; 0.7 GPU-hours in all, including the cross-injector networks and tuning.
  • Cross-injector networks. One network trained on constant-megawatt square-edge events and one on proportional events with wide edges and loose shares, three seeds each, tuned on validation worlds from their own training injector.

Measurement.

  • Scored worlds. Experiment 653's injected worlds (same seeds, noise units, and scorer), 16 worlds across 6 specs; experiment 653's default arm is re-run beside them. The residual's demand model trained on all rows, and the slow level, noise units, and common mode are fitted on the whole record without labels, as in experiment 653. Injected events are added to the residual, not to the power, so recall on injected events may not carry over to real events (the direction of any bias is unknown).
  • Real record. Events per Primary-year, logged shifts matched strictly and loosely, the rewired-graph placebo (100 degree-preserving rewirings applied at inference), the verified pair, the event-free stratum, and the four scenarios.
  • Intervals. Whole worlds are resampled (2,000 draws) for seed 0; the three seeds are reported side by side. A claim about the real record rests on a small number of events.

docs.title: Reviews and triage
docs.text:
• Plan review (Sonnet). 15 findings, 5 of them high: window leakage at the split dates, the verdict rule, the equal-rate comparison, the discriminator's power, and the cross-injector design. All were accepted except the removal of P4 from the verdict (kept, with its low power stated).
  • Code review (Sonnet, before the first run). 13 findings. Accepted and fixed: tuning on the wrong injector for the cross networks, a pairing rule looser than experiment 653's, a pairing arm that changed the event set, a NaN tail the network never trained on, pulses overwriting shift labels, the rate denominator, the square-edge injector setting, and the cross-test seed collision. Accepted and disclosed: checkpoint selection by validation loss rather than recall, and merging same-sign fragments only for shifts.

  • Tuning detour. The first tuning showed the network calling a shift in most blocks (the 0.1 weight on unlabelled time distorts the class prior). The decoder gained a boost on the 'no event' probability and a 1-noise-unit amplitude floor, both tuned on validation worlds only.

  • Prose review (Sonnet). 22 page-level findings and many sentence-level ones. Accepted: moving the figures and this section, defining first look, second look, seed, edge, RO-NC, and LR_b20, correcting the D16 lateness, the cross-injector range, the real-record wording, and the overclaims about the injector, the 0.64 baseline, and the ceiling. Not done: turning the Results bullets into tables.

  • Numbers audit (Sonnet). Re-derived the Results from the stored files; everything matched except the start-timing range (it covered only the second look), D16's start (9.5 hours late in five networks, 36 hours in one), and two roundings. All three were corrected. Not re-derived: the classifier area under the curve and the experiment 653 pairing arm.
  • Audit triggers 1 and 2 (see Checks) are covered by this audit and the reviews above.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00658-edge-state-event-table-neural-network/e00658_data.py: builds features and targets for injected worlds, using experiment 653's injector and slow level.
  • e00658_net.py: the network and its loss.
  • e00658_decode.py: the Viterbi decode, event extraction, and pairing.
  • e00658_train.py: builds the banks of injected worlds and trains the networks (steps bank and train).
  • e00658_run.py: tunes the decoder on validation worlds, scores the injected worlds, decodes the real record, and runs the rewired-graph placebo.
