docs.title: Does one simple pooled network, with or without a fixed physics-lite power input, forecast the 3 metered wind farms and the 6 metered solar farms as well as the current defaults?
docs.text:
A small network that sees only the average and spread of the weather forecasts scores no worse than the two current defaults for the 3 wind farms and the 6 solar farms, and a hand-written power curve as an extra input adds little. The two current defaults are wind default 2 and solar a2_member (experiment 615's stored forecasts), each with a physics-based plant model and an elaborate neural network. We asked whether those parts are needed. We trained one small neural network per technology, shared by all farms of that technology. The network reads summaries across the 51 members of the ECMWF ensemble weather forecast, and we scored it on 5 development months (forecast origins in October, December, January, March, and June). The final test (valid times from 2026-07-01) was never read. "No worse" means the 99% interval of the score difference lies below 0.15 points of capacity for wind and 0.10 points for solar. Nothing here is adopted for production. The forecasts are stored in the private data folder, and the generators appear only as W1 to W3 and Solar A to Solar F.

Terms. The quantile score is the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity (smaller is better). The tables also give the normalised mean absolute error of the median forecast (MAE). Arms: S reads the mean and standard deviation across members of the raw weather. PLP (physics-lite power plus raw weather) reads S plus the mean and standard deviation of a fixed physics-lite power: a power curve for wind, and an irradiance-and-cell-temperature formula for solar, computed from each of the 51 members separately. PL reads the physics-lite power only. The GAM is the generalised additive model of experiment 615, and climatology is a forecast from the farm's own past power. The q05-q95 coverage is the share of observations between the 5% and 95% quantiles (0.90 is ideal). Intervals resample the 5 forecast-origin months, so they are wide and fragile. Wind leads run from 0.5 to 240 h and solar leads from 12 to 240 h. Wind scores treat idle readings (the idle mask of experiment 210) as zero ("idle-zeroed rows"); "kept rows" drops them and "all rows" leaves them as observed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Look at the S and PLP bars sitting at or just below the wind default 2 bar in every lead band, and climatology far above all of them. The differences are small compared with the intervals.

Wind arm (idle readings as zero) Quantile score Median MAE (% of capacity) q05-q95 coverage Above q99 Below q01 S 3.684 13.64 0.911 0.0175 0.0050 PLP 3.685 13.66 0.903 0.0162 0.0056 PL 3.764 13.97 0.923 0.0147 0.0051 S plus calendar 3.778 14.00 0.894 0.0239 0.0055 PLP plus calendar 3.777 13.95 0.889 0.0215 0.0061 Wind default 2 3.766 13.90 0.835 0.0106 0.0226 Wind default 2, 730-day capacity 3.766 13.90 0.835 0.0111 0.0225 climatology (193,699 kept rows only) 5.322 20.15 0.929 0.0167 0.0021

Wind S is no worse than wind default 2 and scores 0.082 points better on idle-zeroed rows (99% interval -0.151 to -0.008, minimum detectable effect 0.103), but most of that gap comes from the default. PLP gives -0.081 (-0.160 to -0.002) and PL gives -0.003 (-0.117 to 0.143). The default's score is 3.713 on all rows and 3.766 on idle-zeroed rows, so zeroing the idle readings worsens the default by 0.053 points; S moves by under 0.01. The default's band is too narrow once idle readings count as zero (q05-q95 coverage 0.835, and 0.0226 of observations below its q01). On all rows the S minus default difference is -0.036 (-0.087 to 0.020), and on kept rows it is +0.019 (-0.018 to 0.066), with S scoring 3.865 and the default 3.846. The idle-zeroed intervals that exclude zero are sensitive to the resampling seed: the upper bound of S minus default is -0.008 or +0.005 depending on the seed (-0.003 by enumerating all 3,125 resamples), and the upper bound of PLP minus default is -0.002 or +0.009 (+0.002 by enumeration). Only 4 of the 5 months favour S; December 2025 favours the default. The idle mask missed 51% to 69% of idle periods out of sample (experiment 210), so some idle noise stays in the "zero" rows.

Look at the S, PLP, and a2_member bars being close in every lead band, with the GAM slightly higher and climatology far higher. PL is clearly worse than PLP at 120 to 240 h (3.750 against 3.631).

Solar arm Quantile score Median MAE (% of capacity) q05-q95 coverage Above q99 Below q01 S 3.301 12.51 0.881 0.0140 0.0092 PLP 3.279 12.42 0.888 0.0136 0.0101 PL 3.346 12.70 0.892 0.0120 0.0063 a2_member, quarterly refit 3.308 12.55 0.886 0.0154 0.0111 a2_member, 730-day capacity 3.305 12.51 0.887 0.0153 0.0087 GAM 3.345 12.49 0.895 0.0132 0.0106 climatology 4.208 16.24 0.950 0.0013 0.0148

Solar PLP is no worse than a2_member (-0.028 points, 99% interval -0.089 to 0.012), and is 0.021 points better than S (-0.044 to -0.004, minimum detectable effect 0.026). The PLP minus a2_member interval includes zero, so only the PLP minus S contrast excludes it. S is level with a2_member (-0.007, -0.070 to 0.039). PL is 0.038 worse than a2_member (-0.117 to 0.160).

Look at every interval including zero: no arm is detectably better or worse than its default over the 5 months, apart from the narrow wind S and PLP intervals discussed above.

Calendar columns hurt wind. S plus calendar scores 0.094 points worse than S (0.012 to 0.180), and its upper tail is worse (0.024 of observations above q99, against a target of 0.01).

Refit schedule (wind S, lower priority). Fitting the wind S arm once at the first development month, quarterly, or twice monthly gives 3.697, 3.697, and 3.684 points on idle-zeroed rows. Each less frequent schedule is 0.013 points worse than twice monthly (single: -0.004 to 0.027; quarterly: -0.011 to 0.055), so the intervals include zero. Both scores are within the 0.15 threshold of wind default 2 (single: -0.069, -0.124 to 0.004).

Capacity. Recomputing capacity as the 99.9th percentile of the previous 730 days changes wind default 2 by -0.001 points and a2_member by -0.002 (interval -0.045 to 0.028). In the one stored set of wind refits, the 730-day capacity was 2.4%, 6.1%, and 9.5% above the old capacity for W1, W2, and W3. Solar farm E had 571 calendar days of history at the first refit, with readings on 488 dates.

Tails. Very sunny days are still the weak point: on 27 farm-days reaching 90% of the farm's own monthly 95th percentile on at least half their half-hours (2,086 rows, a proxy built from observed power), 10.6% to 12.7% of observations exceed q99 for every simple arm and 11.7% for a2_member with quarterly refit (coverage 0.66; the 730-day a2_member row gives 12.2%). On the 44 high-wind days (at least 2 of 3 farms above 80% of capacity, kept rows), coverage is 0.82 for S and 0.83 for wind default 2, and 4.4% to 5.2% of observations exceed q99. On kept rows, coverage in January and March is 0.88 to 0.89 for S, against 0.855 and 0.867 for the default. Two-constant tail widening (experiment 499's rule, fitted on earlier months) did not improve any arm: scores moved by at most 0.013 points except solar climatology (improved by 0.014), and it left more observations below q01 because exact zeros fall below a lifted q01. For solar, widening roughly doubled the share of observations above q99 (see Checks).

Look at the PLP median following the black observation about as closely as wind default 2's.

Look at the observed peaks of days 9 and 10 poking above the 90% band for both arms.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Predictions P1 to P5 (written before any new forecast was scored):
    • P1 passed: wind S is within 0.15 points of wind default 2.
    • P2 failed: PLP is not 0.05 points better than S for wind (+0.001), and for solar it is 0.021 better.
    • P3 passed: PL is within 0.1 points of PLP for wind (+0.079) and solar (+0.067).
    • P4 failed, with the wrong sign: replacing idle readings by zero raised the default's score (worse) by 0.053 points and left the new arms within 0.01, instead of lowering every score by 0.1 points.
    • P5 passed: the 730-day capacity moved both defaults by under 0.01 points.
  • Median minus mean forecast, per site: not computed, because the mixture mean is not stored with the quantiles. Treat this as a gap.
  • Error of the median forecast beside each contrast: it points the same way as the quantile score for wind S against the default (-0.257 points of MAE, interval -0.541 to 0.066; score -0.082), and for solar PLP against a2_member (-0.130, -0.420 to 0.051; score -0.028). The MAE intervals include zero, so the median alone does not separate the arms from the defaults.
  • Audit triggers (the ml-experiment skill's list of reasons to run an independent audit): trigger 2 (a prediction failed with no tested explanation) fired, because P2 and P4 contradicted the predictions. No audit has been run, so the P4 explanation (the default's band is too narrow on zeroed rows) is untested. The other triggers did not fire.
  • Gate: experiment 347's own head reproduced to 0.00000, and a2_member seed 0 for the 2026-06 refit reproduced experiment 430's stored forecast to a maximum absolute difference of 0.0 on q01, q50, and q99.
  • Experiment C is the re-score of both defaults with the 730-day capacity (see Capacity above).
  • Widening artefact: the widened rule shrinks q01 towards the median on rows where the median is near zero, so exact-zero observations fall below q01. The widened scores (scores/*_tails.csv) are therefore not a fair tail comparison.
  • Reviews: fresh Sonnet agents reviewed the wind and the solar scripts before the first quoted score (four wind findings were fixed), then the numbers and the prose and figures of this page. Their findings are applied above. There was no Opus review.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Each arm is a pooled network of two hidden layers of 64 units with a three-component Gaussian mixture over power as a fraction of capacity. It is the MixtureHead of experiment 310, with 11 quantiles read from the mixture and capped at capacity.
  • Wind inputs: mean and standard deviation across the 51 members of 10 m and 100 m wind speed, the sine and cosine of the 100 m direction, and air temperature, plus the lead (sine and cosine of its hour of day, and hundreds of hours) and a one-hot wind-farm column.
  • Solar inputs: mean and standard deviation of shortwave, air temperature, and 10 m wind speed, the ensemble means of relative humidity, longwave radiation, precipitation, and surface pressure, the sun's elevation, the sine and cosine of its azimuth, and the lead. There is no farm column, as in a2_member, and no calendar column.
  • The mixture's centre is the mean physics-lite power for PL and PLP and the training mean of the target for S, so S has no physics-lite input anywhere.
  • Physics-lite wind: a cubic rise of 100 m wind speed from cut-in 3 m/s to rated 12 m/s, flat to cut-out 25 m/s, zero above, with unit capacity. Physics-lite solar: irradiance over 1000 W/m2 times (1 - 0.004 per kelvin times (cell temperature - 25 C)), clipped to 0 to 1, with the Faiman cell temperature T_air + G / (25 + 6.84 times wind speed). Both are applied to each member before the mean and spread. The solar arms also read the mean and spread of the cell temperature.

docs.title: Training regime
docs.text:
• Weather is the ECMWF 51-member ensemble forecast (an issued forecast, available at forecast time). Wind trains on the daily 00 UTC runs from 2024-04 and solar on the stored runs of experiment 430.
  • Wind refits on day 0 and day 14 of each development month (10 refits), training on runs before 62 days earlier and stopping early on the last 62 days, 40 epochs. Solar refits at 2025-09, 2025-12, 2026-03, and 2026-06 (as in experiment 430), 20 epochs, stopping on the last 61 days.
  • Capacity is the 99.9th percentile of the farm's power over the 730 days before each refit. Wind idle readings are set to zero in training and scoring. Three seeds per arm, averaged quantile by quantile.
  • AdamW, learning rate 0.002, batch 2048, weight decay 0.0001. A wind fit took about 43 s on the GPU and a solar fit about 14 s. All arms and re-scores took about 2.2 GPU-hours (wind 150 fits, solar 36, wind re-score 20, solar re-score 12, and the 12 schedule fits). A final-test refit of one arm per technology would take about 20 minutes for wind (10 refits, 3 seeds) and under a minute per solar refit.

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text:
• Scores are on the rows of experiment 615 (daylight half-hours for solar), wind leads of 0.5 to 240 h and solar leads of 12 to 240 h, in points of the same scoring capacity as experiment 615. Wind default 2 is the stored refits of experiment 615 (old capacity rule) and a2_member is experiment 430's stored quarterly forecast, seeds averaged.
  • Intervals are 99% intervals from 10,000 resamples of the 5 forecast-origin months; the minimum detectable effect is 3.418 times the bootstrap standard error. No Bonferroni correction is applied to the 99% level beyond that choice, and the contrasts are descriptive.
  • Experiment C refits wind default 2 (seeds 0 and 1) and a2_member (seeds 0 to 2) with the 730-day capacity, keeping scoring capacity fixed.
  • Not done: the estimate of cost in money, and the Opus review the brief allows.

docs.title: Can one shared generator of injected load-transfer events look real enough to train and test detectors on?
docs.text:
A shared generator of fake load transfers looks real enough to train and test detectors on, as far as 49 real windows and 2 verified transfers can tell. A load transfer happens when an operator switches a circuit from one Primary substation (the substation that steps electricity down to the local distribution network) to a neighbour, so one Primary loses demand and the other gains it. We built one tested module that adds such transfers, and the other kinds of step and ramp that detectors must not mistake for them, to real half-hourly power history. We then asked four questions of the module: how fast and in what shape the real steps change, whether a classifier can tell injected windows from real ones, whether a detector tuned on one configuration still works on another, and whether the detector finds injected events as often as real ones.

The classifier could not tell injected windows from real ones (area under the curve 0.55, where 0.5 is chance). A detector tuned on constant-MW square steps lost 0.01 of its recall on shaped transfers, and the reverse lost none (−0.02). Both pre-registered tests pass, so the verdict is supported. The real evidence is thin, and every number below says how thin. The module sits in this experiment's folder.

The code is the module e00660_generator.py, its tests, and the evidence scripts, all in ml-experiments/00660-shared-generator-of-injected-load-transfer-events/. This page documents the module: the assumption table, the traps and their guards, a usage example, and the four evidence checks.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows an injected transfer beside a real one. Both panels show the residual (power minus the forecast of the lag-free demand forecast of experiment 327's arm C), averaged over 6-hour blocks. The real transfer is a verified one; the injected transfer uses the module's default shape and ramp.

Figure 2 shows that the classifier does little better than shuffled labels. The bar is the mean over 20 repeats of 5-fold cross-validation, and the grey band runs from the mean to the 95th percentile of the same procedure on shuffled labels. The lower panel gives each feature used alone. The two end-of-event features score highest (0.62 and 0.64), still under the 0.65 target.

Figure 3 shows that the detector's recall depends on the test configuration, not on the configuration it was tuned on. The detector found 0.42 to 0.49 of the megawatts moved by events of at least 4 noise units that last a day or more.

Figure 4 compares the detector's recall by event size on injected events and on real events. The real events are those visible in the telemetry (22 of at least a day in the scored years), and the detector found 3 of them. Bins with 3 or fewer real events cannot support a comparison.

Figure 5 shows the fitted ramp width at each end of the two verified transfers. Every best fit is 4 half-hours or fewer. Only 2 of 8 intervals lie inside the default range, because a small step beside the residual's noise fixes a ramp width poorly.

Figure 6 shows how much of each step follows the donor's daily profile. The four estimates run from 0.31 to 0.96, so every step follows the profile in part.

docs.text:

A noise unit is the robust spread of one Primary's 6-hour block means of the residual, from experiment 653.

docs.title: Traps from earlier experiments and the guard for each
docs.text: Trap Guard the module provides Real events in training months taught as negatives (experiment 302) The table lists injected events only, so there is no negative row; event_windows gives the mask of injected time, and everything else stays unlabelled A placebo that is not neutral: a head trained on shuffled shifts still gained (experiment 650) shuffled_placebo keeps sizes, durations, donors, and recipients and moves each group to a random start Band widening mistaken for signal (60% to 68% of the head's gain in experiment 647) None: scoring after equal width scaling belongs to the experiment that uses the module A duration prior meeting a different bank duration_bands, short_heavy(), and long_heavy() change the law, and check 3 tests one such change One verified episode counted as several independent months group_id ties each donor to its recipients, so a consumer can cluster its intervals by event; the module generates no real events Strata defined by the future end select on the outcome None: the table's end column is for scoring only, and the page of an experiment that stratifies by it should say so Neighbour inputs flattering the model (unconfirmed) None

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
Put the folder on the import path, load a panel, and inject. The module takes a real power panel (PowerPanel: one series per Primary, MW and MVA kept apart by is_mva, one noise unit per series, the edge list, and the time of index 0), a configuration, and a seed. It returns the injected panel and a table with one row per participant of each event.

import sys
from dataclasses import replace

sys.path.insert(0, "ml-experiments/00660-shared-generator-of-injected-load-transfer-events")
import e00660_data as data  # loads the 15-Primary panel of experiment 653
import e00660_generator as gen

panel = data.load_panel()
config = replace(gen.default_config(), events_per_primary_year=2.0)  # or gen.short_heavy()
world = gen.inject(panel=panel, config=config, seed=1, start_times=data.logged_start_times())
world.power  # injected series (NaN stays NaN)
world.events  # one row per participant: start, end, role, delta in MW or MVA, ...
placebo = gen.shuffled_placebo(panel=panel, events=world.events, seed=2)

The injected series can be rebuilt from the table alone with gen.apply_events.

The table has these columns. event_id and group_id (a donor and its recipients share a group), site, role, event_class (the three edge classes, the two shift classes, and the hard-negative classes), label (edge_transfer, shift, or hard_negative), start and end (half-hour indices), residual_frac (level left after the end), delta (signed peak change), units (size in noise units), shape, prop_share, shape_source, ramp_in_hh, ramp_out_hh, drift, mid_factor, staged_hh, share (receiver share), period_hh and phase (common mode only), partners, and chain_parent.

The configuration is GeneratorConfig. Every range in the assumption table is a field. The sensitivity constructors are short_heavy(), long_heavy(), constant_mw_square() (no ramp, no drift, no second step, no staged or partial return), and shaped_transfers() (follows the donor's profile, ramps, stages the return, short-heavy). The generator refuses a panel with a reading on or after 2026-07-01, and clamps the configuration's cutoff to that date.

docs.title: Results of the four evidence checks
docs.text:
Check 1: the real ramp is 4 half-hours or shorter at best fit, and the recipient starts about 15 hours after the donor. For each of the four Primaries and each end of its event, we fitted the residual in a window of 4 days either side with a level, a trend, and one step ramping over w half-hours (the generator's own ramp), and read the best w off a grid. Intervals come from resampling whole days. The best w is 0 to 4 at all 8 edges (figure 5), but only 2 intervals lie inside 0 to 4 (D5's end, 2 to 4; D22's end, 0 to 1), so a step of this size beside the residual's noise cannot fix a width. The recipient started 14.5 and 15 hours after the donor. Prediction P4 holds for the best fits and is not established by the intervals.

Check 1 also finds that every step follows the donor's daily profile in part. The share is 0.36 (90% interval 0.16 to 0.57) at D5, 0.96 (0.74 to 1.17) at D16, 0.76 (0.44 to 0.99) at D22, and 0.31 (−0.31 to 0.91) at D3 (figure 6). The module's default draws that share from 0.3 to 1.0. The sample is two events.

Check 2: the classifier's area under the curve is 0.55, under the 0.65 target. The real windows are 49 events visible in the telemetry (verified transfers and unpaired steps of at least a day, from experiment 580). The injected windows are 358 events from default worlds, sampled so that the injected windows' size histogram matches the real one. The mean over 20 repeats is 0.548 (spread over repeats 0.025), against 0.503 for shuffled labels (95th percentile 0.581). With 49 real windows the shuffled-label spread is wide, so the check excludes only a large gap. Used alone, the share of the end step that arrives in the first 6 hours scores 0.64, the size of the end step over the onset step 0.62, and the size of the onset step 0.59.

Check 2 failed on its first run, for a reason unrelated to the generator. At the logged onset time the area under the curve was 0.69 (spread 0.03), because the features read the timing noise of NGED's logged onsets and ends. The final run snaps both real and injected onset and end times to the largest local step within a day. The snapping is a post hoc change, applied to both classes, and the first-run numbers are stored beside the final ones.

Check 3: the cross-injector recall drop is 0.01 and −0.02, under the 0.05 target. The detector is experiment 653's penalised segmentation, and "tuning" means choosing its two penalties on injected worlds under experiment 653's cap of 6 real alarms per Primary-year. Configuration A is constant-MW square steps; configuration B is shaped transfers with ramps, staged returns, and a short-heavy duration law. Tested on A, a detector tuned on B lost 0.010 of MW-weighted recall (95% interval −0.002 to 0.027). Tested on B, a detector tuned on A lost −0.016 (−0.033 to 0.002). The tuning surface is nearly flat for B (recall differs by 0.02 or less across the nine penalty pairs) and spans about 0.10 for A, mostly at on-cost 4, which breaks the alarm cap. The check shows that the generator's configurations do not break this detector, and says little about a detector with more freedom.

Tuned on Tested on Recall of events of at least 4 noise units and a day (95% interval) A, constant-MW square A 0.43 (0.33 to 0.51) B, shaped, short-heavy A 0.42 (0.33 to 0.49) A, constant-MW square B 0.49 (0.44 to 0.54) B, shaped, short-heavy B 0.47 (0.43 to 0.51)

Check 4: injected recall by size rises with size, and the real sample is too small for more. Injected recall is 0.06 (0.01 to 0.10) at 1 to 2 noise units, 0.23 (0.18 to 0.27) at 2 to 4, 0.42 (0.29 to 0.54) at 4 to 6, 0.37 (0.27 to 0.48) at 6 to 10, and 0.58 (0.41 to 0.75) at 10 to 20. Real events visible in the telemetry were found 0 of 5 times at 1 to 2 units (95% Wilson interval 0 to 0.43), 0 of 3 at 2 to 4, 3 of 11 at 4 to 6 (0.10 to 0.57), and 0 of 3 at 6 to 10. In the two bins with at least 5 real events, the injected value falls inside the real interval. The real set was chosen by a step detector, which flatters any step detector's recall.

docs.title: What remains unmeasured
docs.text:
• The real rate, class mix, number of recipients, overlap, chaining, return behaviour, and hard negative rates. Rows marked "unmeasured guess" in the assumption table have no test.
  • Whether real steps differ from injected ones in ways the nine features miss. With 49 real windows the classifier cannot exclude a small gap in area under the curve.
  • The ramp width of a small step, and the end-time offsets of the recipient. Two events fix neither.
  • The conversion between MW and MVA Primaries, which carries no power-factor conversion.
  • Detectors other than one penalised segmentation with two penalties. A neural detector may separate the configurations more easily.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, per site: not applicable, because this experiment scores no forecast.
  • Error of the mean or median forecast beside each quantile-score contrast: not applicable, for the same reason.
  • Audit triggers: the first realness run exceeded its target; the explanation (real onset times are off by hours) was tested by snapping both classes and is recorded above. The generator's defaults for the recipient lag and the share of proportional steps were changed after check 1, and checks 2 to 4 were run again with the final defaults.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the final runs, and its findings were fixed (the cutoff could be overridden, hard negatives could land where a Primary has no data, and some tests were weak). A fresh Sonnet agent then reviewed the numbers and the prose.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture (the generator).

  • Inputs: a PowerPanel of one half-hourly series per Primary (15 Primaries, 2022-01-01 to 2026-06-30, cleaned power from experiment 327, with D18's rows before 2025-03-01 removed), is_mva per series (eight MVA-only Primaries), one noise unit per series, and the edge list.
  • Event draw: a Poisson number of events per Primary-year, a class from the mix above, a start at a logged hour and weekday where the Primary has data, a duration from the bands, and a size from the two log-uniform ranges.
  • Profile: each change is delta times a profile with a linear ramp at each end, a linear drift, an optional second step, an optional staged return, a level left after the end, and a blend of constant MW with the donor's normalised daily profile.
  • Panel: the injected series is the base plus the changes at a signed-MW Primary, and the magnitude of the base plus the changes at an MVA Primary, wherever the change is non-zero and the base has a reading.
  • Hard negatives have their own event_class and the label hard_negative.

Training regime.

  • Detector tuning (checks 3 and 4): the nine combinations of on-cost and stay-cost of experiment 653's detector, on 4 injected worlds per configuration in 2022 and 2023, picking the best recall under the real-alarm cap.
  • Classifier (check 2): a gradient-boosted classifier with shallow trees, balanced by weights, 20 repeats of stratified 5-fold cross-validation grouped by event.
  • Compute: CPU only, at most 2 cores. The runs use no GPU.

Measurement.

  • Rows scored: injected events that start in 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30 for checks 3 and 4, in 8 worlds per configuration. Real events for check 2 from the whole panel and for check 4 from 2024.
  • Recall: the matching of experiment 653. Check 3 is MW-weighted on events of at least 4 noise units that last a day or longer. Check 4 counts events of at least a day.
  • Intervals: resampling whole worlds for injected recall, Wilson intervals for real recall, resampling days for the step shape and the ramp width.
  • Residual: observed power minus the lag-free forecast of experiment 327's arm C, as in experiment 653. The weather behind that forecast is estimates of past weather, so the checks describe the lab setting and not live service.
  • Final-test window: never read. The module and the loaders stop before 2026-07-01.

  • .../e00660_data.py: loads the panel, the forecasts, the edge list, and the logged onsets.
  • .../test_e00660_generator.py: 20 tests (determinism, the table rebuilding the panel, no change outside event windows, conservation at the stated share, MVA magnitude, the cutoff guard, class topology, start times, profile shapes, and the placebo).
  • .../e00660_ev1_real_edges.py: check 1, the ramp width and the step shape of the two verified transfers.
  • .../e00660_ev2_realness.py: check 2, the realness classifier.
  • .../e00660_ev34_detector.py: checks 3 and 4, importing experiment 653's folder by path insertion.

docs.title: The ensemble's time step is not why the explicit solar term loses
docs.text:
The explicit solar term (telling the demand neural network each Primary substation's solar capacity, so that it subtracts a computed solar output) helps by about 0.8 points of capacity when weather is real, and hurts by about 0.3 points when weather is an ensemble forecast. We tested whether the ensemble's coarse time step is the reason, and the time step is not the reason. We averaged real weather (CAMS and ERA5 estimates of past weather) into 3-hour and 6-hour windows, rebuilt half-hourly values with production's window-mean resampler, and retrained the neural networks. The explicit gain did not fall. The audit found nothing wrong with how ensemble shortwave becomes half-hourly values, and a small neural adapter in front of the solar curve did not rescue the term. The most likely cause that remains is the ensemble's forecast cloud error, which this experiment did not test directly.

This page follows experiment 639 (real weather, gain 0.75), experiment 644 and experiment 655 (ensemble weather, loss 0.25 to 0.37). Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in percent of each Primary's effective capacity ("points"), on sunny middays (10:00 to 15:00 UTC, clear-sky index at least 0.7), at the six MW Primaries. Smaller is better. The free network learns each Primary's solar response from the data alone; the explicit network is told the capacity. A positive contrast (free minus explicit) favours the explicit network.

  • Averaging real weather into 3-hour or 6-hour windows did not reduce the explicit gain. Free minus explicit CRPS is 0.753 [0.478, 1.050] at hourly resolution, 0.839 [0.581, 1.127] with 3-hour windows, and 0.773 [0.512, 1.058] with 6-hour windows (three cutoffs, five seeds, 99.6% day-block intervals). The 3-hour gain exceeds the hourly gain by 0.086 [0.016, 0.162]; the 6-hour gain by 0.020 [-0.084, 0.120]. The decision rule (a fall of at least half) is not met. The gain is concentrated: Primary 6 carries about 3 points, and the other five Primaries together gain 0.27 [0.07, 0.49] at hourly resolution, with 3-hour minus hourly still positive at 0.113 [0.053, 0.176].
  • The ensemble loss is the same at both step widths. Free minus explicit is -0.281 [-0.426, -0.147] at 3-hourly ensemble leads (up to 144 hours) and -0.297 [-0.413, -0.182] at 6-hourly leads. The two groups also differ in lead, so the comparison is a weak test on its own.

docs.title: Interpolation audit (Part 1)
docs.text:
• The pipeline is production's resampler. Stored summary tables, the half-hourly rows of experiment 48, and a fresh call of ml_core agree to 0.0 W/m2 on 15 runs between 2024-06 and 2026-06. Production's code is the same file as the version the experiments imported.
  • No time-stamp shift. The ensemble's window-mean shortwave correlates best with CAMS (hourly values stamped at the end of the hour) at a shift of zero at all six Primaries (r 0.966 to 0.986). The other CAMS convention gives a shift of two half-hours and r of 0.878 to 0.914 at zero shift.
  • Production's method is the best of the three methods tested (window mean, linear flux, step-holding). Rebuilding known weather from 3-hour windows leaves a root-mean-square error of 5.3% of the CAMS midday peak (peak bias -2.5%); linear flux gives 15.5% and step-holding 10.4%. With 6-hour windows the errors are 6.6%, 30.8%, and 19.5%.

docs.title: Bias adapter (Part 3)
docs.text:
Sunny middays, ensemble rows of experiment 644 Day 1-2 Day 3-5 Day 6-10 Free network (644 arm a) 3.75 4.28 5.05 Explicit network (644 arm b) 4.11 4.53 5.33 Adapter arm (A) 4.04 4.42 5.18
  • The adapter arm is not kept. Free minus A is -0.291 [-0.479, -0.124], -0.135 [-0.316, 0.036], and -0.129 [-0.275, 0.013]; the bar was a gain of 0.084 at day 1-2. A beats the explicit network by 0.075 [-0.006, 0.150], 0.115 [0.030, 0.190], and 0.146 [0.079, 0.217], and the 14-day tracker beats A by 0.63, 0.60, and 0.70.
  • The mixture without the adapter scored about the same as the adapter arm at day 1-2. The mixture-only arm (A0) is 0.024 [-0.070, 0.121] behind the adapter arm (A) there, and 0.081 and 0.089 behind at day 3-5 and day 6-10.
  • The learned fleet shape stayed uniform. The mixture weights ended near equal across the three tilts and five DC-to-AC ratios at every Primary, so the Dirichlet prior dominated and no ratio was learned. The fleet shape is reported and not gated.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Audit trigger that fired: the Part 2 result contradicts the prediction of a 20% to 45% fall. The explanation, forecast cloud error, rests on experiments 644 and 655 and was not tested here. A fresh Sonnet agent re-derived the step 5 contrasts from the stored quantiles.
  • The checks of median against mean, per-site contrasts, and the error beside each contrast were not run for step 5, because its arms share the pretraining and scoring code of experiment 639. For Part 3, the mean absolute error of the median on sunny middays is 6.49 (A), 6.63 (A0), 6.33 (free), and 6.67 (explicit), in the same order as the CRPS contrasts.
  • Tails (Part 3, sunny middays): coverage of the 5% to 95% interval is 88.4% (A), 89.4% (A0), 88.0% (free), and 89.2% (explicit). The 0.01 and 0.99 quantiles cover 2.7% and 99.8% of outcomes for A.
  • Caveats: each day is its own trajectory in the degradation, so interpolation never crosses midnight (the 6-hour window that holds sunrise is affected in summer); only shortwave is degraded; capacities are experiment 639's, calibrated on undegraded weather; no example-forecast figure is shown; the Part 2 gain is measured on real-weather rows (the figure's blue rows) and the ensemble loss on ensemble rows, so the two are not paired.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Architecture. The networks are experiment 639's modular mixture-density network (free, and calibrated explicit with the term C * inc * u subtracted from every quantile). Arm A replaces u with a differentiable curve: a 6-input adapter (ensemble-mean clear-sky index, ensemble standard deviation over clear-sky irradiance, lead, hour of day as sine and cosine, temperature; 16 and 16 tanh units; zero-initialised output) gives kt' = kt + 0.25 tanh(output), clipped to 0 to 1.4; plane-of-array irradiance is tabulated at 16 clear-sky indices for tilts of 20, 35, and 50 degrees and interpolated; a per-Primary softmax mixture over 15 components (three tilts times DC-to-AC ratios 1.0, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7) applies the cell-temperature derating and a smooth clip z / (1 + z^8)^(1/8), under a Dirichlet prior of concentration 2.
  • Training regime. Step 5 pretrains the free and calibrated-explicit networks on CAMS and ERA5 rows of experiment 418 with shortwave replaced by 3-hour or 6-hour window means rebuilt by ml_core's resampler (three cutoffs, five seeds, real world). Part 3 fine-tunes from experiment 639's calibrated pretraining on 24 months of ensemble rows with experiment 644's recipe (90-day recency half-life, fresh mixer, monthly refits, five seeds). The adapter learning rate is 0.002. About 0.6 GPU-hours for step 5 and 0.5 for Part 3.
  • Measurement. Part 1 compares with CAMS on sunny days (daily CAMS energy at least 80% of clear sky) in 2025-07, 2026-03, and 2026-06. Steps 5 and 6 and Part 3 score the rows, cutoffs, and sunny-midday mask of experiments 639 and 644, with 99.6% day-block bootstraps (Bonferroni over 12 contrasts) and 644's bars (0.080, 0.090, and 0.118). Nothing from 2026-07-01 is scored.

docs.title: Can a probe read the capacity of unmetered solar at substations that report apparent power?
docs.text:
The hypothesis is partly supported: a fold model reads 0.7 to 0.9 of an added solar fleet at every level tested, and the linear probes fail from 2 times upward. The pre-registered gate failed, and two Primaries, D5 and D10, decide several bars. Six of the 12 pre-registered bars passed at the 2026-06 cutoff. The matched-level bar A1 failed, so only the 12 uninjected neural networks (four conditions) ran at the 2026-03 cutoff. The fold fit now ends on a bound in 0% of fits, which removes the fault that sank experiment 656's 6-times worlds.

We asked whether the unmetered solar capacity behind a substation can be read when the meter reports apparent power (megavolt-amperes, which never goes negative) rather than signed megawatts. Six Primary substations report signed megawatts. We converted their flow to synthetic apparent power, added a solar fleet of known size, and trained a neural network on the result. The probe holds the calendar inputs of the neural network fixed, feeds the neural network the weather of other days, and regresses the neural network's output on a solar-output curve. The slope is the capacity the probe reads, in megawatts of alternating current (AC). We compare the capacity read from a network trained with the fleet against its twin trained without it. This page covers 130 neural networks at the 2026-06 cutoff (26 conditions of 5 seeds each, a condition being one world: a reactive-power arm, a kind of injection, and a level) and 12 uninjected neural networks at the 2026-03 cutoff.

Terms used below.

  • MW Primaries and MVA Primaries. The six MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) are metered in signed megawatts. The eight MVA Primaries are metered in apparent power: D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21 never come near zero flow on a sunny midday, and D8, D12, and D22 do (they "fold").
  • The fold. Apparent power is the length of a real-power part and a reactive-power part. When solar output exceeds demand, the reading falls to the reactive floor and then rises again, so a linear fit reads the wrong sign.
  • Midday reading. A Primary's median flow over sunny half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC in April to August, in MW. D5's is 0.88 MW and D10's is 1.2 MW.
  • Injection level. The AC capacity of the added fleet is the larger of the level times the midday reading and 2.0 MW. The floor makes the 0.5-, 1-, and 2-times worlds at D5 all 2.0 MW, and D10's 0.5- and 1-times worlds 2.0 MW.
  • Recovery. The capacity read from the network trained with the fleet, minus the capacity read from its twin, divided by the fleet's AC capacity.
  • Probes. L0 is the linear probe of experiment 621. L1 is L0 on rows well above the reactive floor. FA is the fold model with four solar-output curves and a prior on each probe cell's demand from the night reading. F4 is FA without the prior, and F1 is F4 with one curve.
  • Worlds. The PF world has reactive power 0.25 times the median real power of that half-hour of the week (power factor 0.97). The signed world keeps the signed target. The floor and zero- reactive worlds change the reactive power only.

Figure: in the upper panel the linear probes fall below zero at 2 times, and the fold model does not. The signed panel shows the same farms with no fold. Linear recovery stays at 0.74 to 0.88 there. The fold model falls from 0.81 to -0.04 as the level rises, because a model that can only add a fold fits badly to a target that never folds (see the audit section).

At 2026-06, 6 of 12 pre-registered bars passed. The bars are as fixed in the plan commit.

Bar Result Pass A1 Matched-level fold-free loss: PF over signed recovery of the same farm in 0.90 to 1.10 at 5 of 6, for L0, L1, and FA at 0.5, 1, and 2 times no cell of the nine reaches 5 of 6; the best is 3 of 6 (FA at 1 times) fail A2 Native worlds within ±0.12 of the six's median (0.68) at 4 of 5 4 of 5 (D3 at 0.82 is outside) pass A3 Two-sided placebos under 0.25 of the real 0.5-times read climatological 0 of 6 and 0 of 5; boxcar 4 of 6 and 5 of 5 fail A4 Leave-one-Primary-out factor in 0.55 to 0.95, spread under 0.15 0.661 to 0.692 at all six pass A5 Interval coverage at least 60% (L0 at 0.5 times) 0.36 fail B1 FA calibrated recovery in 0.75 to 1.25 at 4 of 6 in four worlds (PF and floor, 1 and 2 times) 3, 5, 3, and 4 of 6 fail B2 PF 6 times: FA calibrated recovery in 0.75 to 1.25 at 4 of 6 5 of 6 (D5 is 0.72) pass B3 At PF 2 times, FA's median absolute error from 1 at least 0.10 below L1's 0.15 against 0.37 pass B4 Sun-rising-load placebo: FA under 0.25 of the 6-times read at 5 of 6, and no crossing flags 4 of 6; flags on 0.0% of cells fail B5 Interval coverage at least 60% at PF 1 and 2 times (FA) 0.50 and 0.42 fail B6 Crossing map: balanced accuracy at least 0.80 at 1 and 2 times, false crossings at most 10% 0.84 and 0.94; 3.1% pass C1 Under 10% of FA fits end on a bound 0.0% pass

Two changes from experiment 656 worked. The fold fit's five starting capacities (0.25 to 8 times the midday reading) remove the 6-times failure: FA reads 0.89 and 0.90 there, against -0.11 in experiment 656. Intervals that add the between-seed spread raise coverage in bar A5 to 0.36 (experiment 656: 0.18) and in bar B5 to 0.50 and 0.42 (experiment 656: 0.17 and 0.14), still below the 0.60 bar.

Median recovery over the six MW Primaries 0.5 times 1 times 2 times 6 times PF world, L0 0.66 0.53 -0.12 -0.81 PF world, L1 0.66 0.68 -0.13 -0.81 PF world, FA 0.73 0.73 0.80 0.89 Signed world, L0 0.76 0.77 0.78 0.79 Signed world, FA 0.81 0.62 0.32 -0.04

docs.title: Audit of the failures
docs.text:
An independent Sonnet audit reproduced every bar and explained each failure below; no bar is re-scored. The audit brief is briefs/e662_audit_brief.md in the private folder.

  • A1 also fails at D9, D11, D14, and D16, where the floor does not apply. At D9, D11, D14, and D16 the linear probes read -0.01 to -0.15 at 2 times, so the fold itself, not only D5 and D10, breaks them. At D5 and D10 the floor injects 2.26 and 1.66 times the midday reading even at the 0.5-times level. Both Primaries therefore sit past the fold at every level, and L0 reads them at -0.34 to -0.02.
  • The fold model is not a fair A1 denominator. On the signed target, which never folds, FA sets at least one reactive term to zero in 59 to 74% of fits (both in 39 to 56%) and flags crossings on 41 to 72% of cells at the six MW Primaries at 2 and 6 times. A square-root output cannot match a target that goes negative. A1's FA ratios (2.1 to 3.8 at 2 times) come from this collapsed denominator.
  • A3 fails because it is two-sided. The linear probe reads the climatological placebo at -0.2 to -0.5, and experiment 656's one-sided bar would have passed it at 11 of 11 sites. FA reads it at -0.05 to 0.08 except at D5 (-0.50), but several of those reads exceed 0.25 of the real FA 0.5-times read (D11 0.42, D16 0.33, D4 0.53), so FA would fail a one-sided bar too. The placebo is sized at 2 times and compared with the 0.5-times read, a level mismatch in the bar. At D5 and D10 the real 0.5-times L0 read is itself near zero or negative (-0.34 and -0.03), so the bar cannot pass there for L0.
  • B4 and B5 depend on D5 and D10. The sun-rising load reads 1.13 and 0.34 of the real read at D5 and D10, and 0.07 to 0.16 elsewhere. Without D5 and D10, B5 reads 0.875 at both levels. The same exclusion fails A4 (only four Primaries) and B6 (balanced accuracy 0.71 at 1 times), so the verdicts rest on the two small-reading Primaries in both directions. B1 fails with or without them, because D11 and D16 overshoot to 1.3 and 1.4 at 1 times.
  • Coverage is set by the seed spread alone. The bootstrap half-width is 0.01 to 0.07 MW and the seed term 0.04 to 1.4 MW. The leave-one-Primary-out factors barely differ (0.66 to 0.69), so the intervals carry no uncertainty about the factor. Native Primaries are scored with the six Primaries' factor and miss at all five.
  • The FA prior is stronger in the injected fit than in the twin fit. The prior's weight scales with the median within-cell spread of the probed reading. The audit found that spread 0.9 to 2.4 times the twin's at 0.5 and 2 times and up to 12 times at 6 times (not re-checked here). Some of FA's capacity difference is therefore a change of regularisation, which we did not refit to measure.
  • C1 measures capacity collapse only. At least one reactive term sits at zero in 37 to 60% of PF FA fits and 59 to 74% of signed FA fits, and a flag on fits with reactive terms at zero would not have passed.

Figure: the cloud-following load is read as solar by both probes. The fold model reads 0.64 of the load's size and the linear probe 0.44, so neither separates solar output from demand that follows the clouds, as in experiment 656. Against the real 2-times fleet's read, the ratios are 0.83 for the fold model and -3.7 for the linear probe, which has the wrong sign there.

Figure: in the real-farm fleets and twins, the only fits on a bound are one-curve fits at 6 times (about 7%). The night-prior and four-curve fits never end on a bound there. In the sun-rising-load placebo, which has no solar to find, FA ends on a bound in 77% of fits, as it should.

docs.title: Real-data capacity (uninjected neural networks, both cutoffs)
docs.text:
The calibrated columns divide the linear probe's capacity by 0.68 (bar A4's factor) and the fold model's capacity by 0.70 (its recovery in the power-factor (PF) world at 1 times on the six MW Primaries). Both calibrations therefore assume power factor 0.97 and the response of the six MW Primaries. The ranges are 80% intervals from the bootstrap and the seed spread.

Primary Linear raw, 2026-06 / 2026-03 (MW) Linear calibrated, 2026-06 (MW) Fold model raw, 2026-06 / 2026-03 (MW) Fold model calibrated, 2026-06 (MW) D2 5.2 / 5.0 7.7 8.0 / 7.4 11.3 (10.4 to 12.1) D3 2.1 / 2.0 3.0 4.4 / 4.6 6.3 (4.0 to 8.6) D4 1.0 / 1.0 1.5 3.1 / 4.0 4.4 (1.1 to 7.7) D19 1.1 / 1.1 1.7 2.1 / 2.3 3.0 (2.0 to 4.1) D21 1.1 / 1.1 1.7 1.4 / 1.3 1.9 (1.3 to 2.5) D8 (report only) 1.8 / 1.3 2.6 2.1 / 1.6 2.9 (2.0 to 3.9) D12 (report only) -3.0 / -2.9 not defined 5.3 / 5.2 7.5 (7.2 to 7.8) D22 (report only) 1.3 / 1.3 1.9 1.7 / 1.6 2.4 (2.3 to 2.5)

Figure: the two cutoffs' intervals overlap at all 14 Primaries, for both probes. The fold model's medians differ most at D4 (3.1 and 4.0 MW), D14 (3.9 and 3.3 MW), D2 (8.0 and 7.4 MW), and D8 (2.1 and 1.6 MW). D12 is the Primary whose linear read is negative at both cutoffs while the fold model reads +5 MW. The capacities are raw and uncalibrated.

Figure: D12 is flagged at midday in all six months, April to September, and D22 is not flagged. The map passed bar B6 on injected worlds, but that pass relied on D5 and D10 (see the audit section). On the uninjected twins, D8 and D22 are flagged on 0% of cells, so D8 does not behave as a folding Primary here, while D5 is flagged on 46% of cells and D4 on 19%.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text:
• Fold fit. 40 bootstrap draws in place of 200, 40 donor rows per probe cell, and the bootstrap only on the PF twin and the PF real-farm fleets.
  • 2026-03. Stop rule 2 fired when A1 failed, so only the four twins ran at that cutoff. The calibration at 2026-03 reuses the 2026-06 factors.
  • B4. Coded two-sided (the absolute read) after the code review; the plan table now states this.
  • Boxcar placebo. The boxcar's height stays capped at the midday reading, so at D5 and D10 the placebo carries less energy than the 2.0 MW fleet.
  • Not run. The signed-world energy conversion and the 2026-03 injected worlds.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The reactive power of the real meters is unknown, and power factor 0.97 is an assumption.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the clean rows may hold unlabelled events.
  • D5 and D10 have midday readings of about 1 MW, so a 2.0 MW floor puts them past the fold in every injected world.
  • One set of farms and one network architecture.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Forecast checks: the experiment scores no forecast, so the median-minus-mean and quantile-score checks do not apply.
  • Audit triggers that fired: a control failed (A1, A3), a leave-two-out flip (A4, B5, B6 with D5 and D10 removed), and a nested-arm result (FA on signed worlds). The audit report is in the private briefs folder.
  • Code review (Sonnet): the review accepted the per-cutoff grouping in the coverage bar, the two-sided B4, the 0.05 guard on A1's denominator, and the relative bound threshold. It also suggested raising the boxcar cap, which stays because a load transfer cannot remove more than the load.
  • Audit triage: all findings are recorded above; none changes a pre-registered bar.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does a fold model with a night prior hold 0.7 to 0.9 recovery when the injection is sized past the fold at every Primary by construction, the signed denominator is a plain linear probe, and the intervals include the site-to-site variation of the calibration factor? And what separates solar output from the cloud-following load that both probes misread?

docs.title: Does a learned end detector, reading the freshest half-hours at a Primary and its neighbours, make the prevailing forecast drop a load shift sooner after it ends, without more false alarms?
docs.text:
This experiment tests whether a learned end detector improves the prevailing forecast of experiment 654. A Primary is a primary substation. A load shift is a period when the electricity network operator moves part of one Primary's demand onto, or off, a neighbouring Primary. K1 is the neural network of experiments 612 and 613 that forecasts the normal running arrangement (NRA), the demand with no load shift. The prevailing forecast is the demand under the arrangement now in force. Experiment 654 built two bases for it: E0 (frozen K1 plus the survival-hazard head R-haz of experiment 652) and J2 (one network fine-tuned end to end). This experiment adds an end detector to each: a two-layer neural neural network that reads the freshest 48 hours of observed power minus K1's day-ahead forecast, at the Primary and at its electrical neighbours, and outputs the probability that the shift has ended (q_end). The detector multiplies each base arm's probability that the shift is still in force by one minus the detector output. The probability becomes p_base * (1 - q_end). E0d is E0 with the detector and J2d is J2 with the detector. Scaled continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) is the CRPS in points of capacity after multiplying each arm's quantile widths about the median by one factor per arm, month, and seed, chosen so that the q05-q95 band covers 90% of the month's scored rows.

Take-home message. On injected shifts, the detector lowers the error in the 24 hours after a shift ends, by 1.08 scaled points for E0d and 0.89 for J2d, and the detector raises the error while a shift is in force, by 0.30 for E0d. The neighbours add no gain that this experiment could measure: the same detector on a randomly rewired graph scores the same as on the real graph. On the real final-test window, the detector made E0 worse (4.81 points against 4.26) and J2 better (4.85 against 5.02), and plain E0 scored lowest of the arms on the window. Verdict: not supported.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
On the final-test window, E0 scores 4.26 over all rows and 5.40 where the G4 gate (experiment 620's hand-built rule for marking half-hours inside a load shift) marks a shift in force. E0d scores 4.81 and 8.52. J2d improves J2 (4.85 against 5.02) and stays above E0.

On the five development months, orange dots are the detector's change against its own base. Blue dots are the real graph minus the rewired graph; the interval includes zero in every stratum for rewiring 0 (rewiring 1 is +0.14 [+0.06, +0.23] in the "ended in the last 24 hours" stratum for E0d), so the gain does not come from the neighbours that this experiment could measure. The "middle" stratum is omitted from the figure.

The detector output (q_end) is 0.19 on average in the week before an injected shift ends and 0.39 in the days after. The detector output never reaches 0.5 on average, and the real graph, the rewired graph, and the no-neighbour variant rise alike.

The false-alarm share is the share of rows with no shift in force on which the median of the prevailing forecast departs from the median of the NRA forecast by 3 points of capacity or more.

D5 and D16 are the verified pair of labelled shifts (29 December 2025 to 13 January 2026). Both prevailing forecasts follow the drop only partly (on D5 the forecast stays near 4 to 5 MW for several days while the observed power falls to 2 to 3 MW), and the E0 and E0d forecasts look alike: the detector changes them little. The figures are not drawn for J2d, and they do not show q_end. Each line is the day-ahead median (lead 24 to 48 hours) at hourly means.

The window starts on 1 July, so the figure shows 7 days before the run starts, not 14. D14 holds the longest run of days with the gate on in the window (from 8 July to the window's end, a run that continues past it). E0 stays within about 1 MW of the observed power in August and September; E0d forecasts several megawatts above the observed power from late August. The cause is not diagnosed.

docs.title: What the detector reads
docs.text: For each Primary and origin the detector reads 16 three-hour block means of the residual over the freshest 48 hours, 8 daily means before that, the same summaries averaged over the Primary's electrical neighbours, 4 flags for missing blocks, the opposite-sign neighbour step (a boost, never a requirement), and the routine-step rate over the previous 60 days (the count of daily-mean changes larger than 3 noise units, per day). The residual is observed power minus K1's day-ahead median, with the median across the 16 Primaries at each half-hour removed, and every input ends at the origin.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
All numbers below are scaled CRPS in points of capacity over lead days 1 to 9, averaged over seeds and then over the 5 development months. They are measured over lead days 1 to 9 on experiment 650's injected bank (training family), averaged over seeds, then over the 5 development months. Intervals are percentile bootstraps over the 5 months. "Pooled" means the "ended in the last 24 hours" and "near" strata together.

  • Both detectors gain after an ending (decision-rule contrast 1 is met). Pooled, E0d minus E0 is -0.46 [-0.92, -0.03] and J2d minus J2 is -0.57 [-0.78, -0.37], against the bar of -0.3 with an interval excluding zero. In the "ended in the last 24 hours" stratum alone, E0d minus E0 and J2d minus J2 are -1.08 [-1.68, -0.50] and -0.89 [-1.18, -0.63]. For E0d the gain is confined to events of 3 to 14 days (-0.48 [-0.90, -0.06]). For events of 28 to 112 days the pooled contrast is +1.14 [-1.12, +4.35]. For J2d both duration bands gain (-0.60 for 3 to 14 days and -0.15 for 28 to 112 days).
  • E0d loses while a shift is in force, and J2d loses only in the "far" stratum. E0d minus E0 is +0.27 [+0.07, +0.47] in the "far" stratum and +0.30 [+0.11, +0.45] over all in-force strata. J2d minus J2 is +0.16 [+0.05, +0.26] in "far" and -0.23 [-0.34, -0.07] in "near". The prediction P1 fails: the "near" stratum does not reach -0.3 for E0d (+0.22 [-0.11, +0.54]) or for J2d (-0.23), and the detector moves the "far" stratum by more than 0.1 points for both arms (E0d +0.27, J2d +0.16) and the "middle" stratum for E0d (+0.13).
  • Placebo (contrast 2): the gain is not specific to the real graph. Pooled, real graph minus rewired graph is -0.05 [-0.17, +0.04], +0.08 [+0.02, +0.14], and +0.05 [-0.03, +0.17] for E0d (rewirings 0, 1, and 2) and -0.01 [-0.04, +0.03], +0.01 [-0.02, +0.04], and 0.00 [-0.03, +0.04] for J2d. The real graph minus the no-neighbour arm is -0.11 [-0.40, +0.14] for E0d and -0.01 [-0.04, +0.03] for J2d. Against a pooled gain of -0.46 (E0d) and -0.57 (J2d), rewiring 0 recovers about 89% and 98% of the gain, and the other two rewirings recover all of it or more, so the prediction that the rewired graph recovers at most half of the gain (P3) fails. For E0d the no-neighbour interval is wide enough to hide a gain beyond the bar, so "adds no consistent gain" is as much as 5 months support. The three rewirings keep 3, 2, and 3 of the 29 pairs of electrical neighbours.
  • False alarms. On real development-month rows with no labelled shift, the share of rows on which the prevailing median departs from the NRA median by 3 points or more is 10.4% for E0, 11.5% for E0d, 16.8% for J2, and 12.1% for J2d. J2d cuts J2's share by 28% (an estimate; J2's interval is 10.7% to 23.1%), which meets the prediction (P4); E0d raises the share relative to E0 (10.4% to 11.5%), which does not meet the prediction. On the final-test window rows outside the gate's events the shares are 13.2% (E0), 15.1% (E0d), 11.7% (J2), and 9.8% (J2d). On injected rows with no shift the departure share of E0d minus E0 is -1.1 [-1.8, -0.4] percentage points, so E0d departs less there.

  • CRPS added by the departures. The CRPS of the prevailing forecast minus the CRPS of the NRA forecast on the departure rows, averaged over all real event-free rows, is +0.009 for E0, +0.046 for E0d, +0.265 for J2, and +0.012 for J2d (points of capacity, development months; figure 4, lower panel). J2's departures cost far more than the others'.

  • Veto on event-free rows: not met for E0d; J2d passes by its interval but not in every month. On injected bank rows with no shift, the unscaled CRPS of E0d minus E0 is +0.01 [-0.19, +0.21], and the upper bound of that interval exceeds 0.03. J2d minus J2 is -0.11 [-0.25, -0.01], so the interval passes the bar of 0.03, but the 2026-03 month is +0.06, above 0.03, and the plan's strict reading of the veto asks that every month stay below it. On real event-free rows E0d minus E0 is +0.04 [+0.01, +0.09].

  • No arm is best in every stratum. E0 is best far from the end and with no shift, K1 is best near the end, and J2d is best in the 24 hours after an ending. Scaled CRPS, normalised mean absolute error of the median (as a fraction of capacity), and unscaled CRPS, all lead days 1 to 9:
Stratum K1 E0 E0d J2 J2d Far from the end, scaled CRPS 10.49 5.93 6.20 8.41 8.56 Near the end, scaled CRPS 5.93 7.35 7.57 6.45 6.22 Ended in the last 24 h, scaled CRPS 5.95 7.45 6.37 6.53 5.64 No shift, scaled CRPS 5.24 3.75 3.81 4.53 4.43 All rows, scaled CRPS 9.15 6.15 6.35 7.66 7.71 All rows, normalised MAE 0.14 0.10 0.10 0.12 0.12 All rows, unscaled CRPS 9.75 6.03 6.23 7.54 7.53

Table: five development months, experiment 650's injected bank; the arms are scored on the same rows as in experiment 654. B-haz and R0 (168 h) score, in the order far, near, ended in the last 24 h, no shift, all rows (scaled CRPS): 5.86, 7.42, 7.84, 3.97, 6.13 and 7.22, 5.92, 6.11, 4.16, 6.89. The matched-compute control C0 of experiment 654 is not rescored here.

docs.title: Final-test window (2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31)
docs.text:
The window was opened once, for the frozen candidates. final/freeze2.json holds the hashes of 26 files and was written before any window score. K1, the manual heuristic, and J2 are experiment 654's forecasts, not rescored. E0 is refitted on all five development months; E0d and J2d train on the same months. Scenarios come from the G4 gate of experiment 620, because NGED's labels end before the window and the window export holds no labelled or verified event. The gate marks 16.6% of scored rows as inside a shift, and the count is a lower bound. The table gives unscaled CRPS point estimates; the intervals, bootstrapped over the 4 origin months, are in final/score/window.json.

Scenario Rows K1 Manual heuristic J2 E0 E0d J2d All rows 820,893 4.96 4.82 5.02 4.26 4.81 4.85 No shift in force, 7 days or more after 678,832 4.07 4.39 4.41 4.03 4.06 4.19 Shift in force 136,578 9.37 6.94 8.07 5.40 8.52 8.14 No shift in force, under 7 days after 5,483 4.36 5.28 4.46 4.34 4.39 4.44

Table: unscaled CRPS in points of capacity. The 5,483 rows of the last scenario come from too few origin months for an interval.

  • E0 has the lowest CRPS over all rows and inside shifts, and the lowest mean absolute error of the median. On the avoidable-curtailment cost E0 (186) is above K1 (178) and the manual heuristic (165). The mean absolute error of the median over all rows, in points of capacity, is 7.66 for E0, 8.55 for E0d, 8.61 for J2d, 8.90 for J2, 8.34 for K1, and 8.46 for the manual heuristic.
  • The detector made E0 worse. E0d minus E0 is +0.54 over all rows and +3.13 inside shifts. The avoidable-curtailment cost, with the curtailment threshold at 90% of each Primary's peak demand and in pounds per day averaged over the six MW Primaries, is 186 for E0, 309 for E0d, 187 for J2, 187 for J2d, 178 for K1, and 165 for the manual heuristic.
  • The detector made J2 slightly better. J2d minus J2 is -0.17 over all rows, and J2d still scores worse (a higher CRPS) than E0 and the manual heuristic over all rows.

docs.title: What was not done
docs.text:
• A second duration law, and a statement of the length distribution. The brief asked for the 653 injector's length distribution (log-uniform 1 to 112 days plus a short band); this experiment instead used experiment 650's bank, so its events last 3 to 14 days or 28 to 112 days, with none of 1 to 3 or 14 to 28 days, which is a deviation from the brief. The detector alone on a second duration law: The plan also scored the detector on injected shifts that follow experiment 653's duration law (log-uniform 1 to 112 days plus a short band). It was not run. The figures above use experiment 650's bank only, whose events last 3 to 14 days or 28 to 112 days. Experiment 660's shared injector draws its durations from a different law, so scoring on that injector would change the delay and false-alarm figures. The detector-delay figure shows the mean detector output by day, not a delay in days.
  • Real events on the development months as a scenario table. The window scenarios use the G4 gate. The four load-shift scenarios on the development months' labelled events are not tabulated.
  • A "no shift within 14 days" stratum. It holds no rows in the injected bank (the cause was not checked), so the false-alarm share is measured on real event-free rows.
  • Shallow shifts (P2), day-ahead and 14-day example forecasts, and detection delay per Primary-month were not run.
  • The window segmenter (experiment 653's) was not run, so the window events are the gate's.
  • Event time-series figures for J2d are not drawn.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• E0 refit reproduces experiment 652. The maximum absolute difference between the refitted E0 head's quantiles and the stored E0 quantiles is 0.0.
  • The J2 forward pass matches experiment 654 for 2025-10 and for the window forecasts. The stored J2 quantiles are matched for 2025-10, and the window forward pass of the frozen J2 networks has a maximum difference of 0.0 from experiment 654's window forecasts.
  • No look-ahead. A test perturbs observed power after the origin; no detector input changes (maximum difference 0.0). The noise unit and constants use the four training months only.
  • Detector training. The detectors add a cross-entropy against "the shift has ended" (weight 0.5). Without that loss q_end barely moves, and the apparent gain is a constant shrink of the survival.
  • Reviews. The plan and the code were each reviewed by one Sonnet agent before the first fit. The pull request holds the results, write-up, and prose reviews.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Every development-month shift is injected, and the strata use the shift's future end. Scaled numbers are pooled across strata, so unscaled CRPS sits beside them in score/tables.json.
  • The intervals use 5 development months (4 window months), so every interval is coarse.
  • NGED's event labels are an incomplete one-off dump. Rows counted as event-free can hold unlabelled shifts, so false-alarm shares are upper bounds on false alarms. Window scenario counts are lower bounds.
  • The G4 gate, not a human label, defines the window's "inside" scenario, so a gate error shifts rows between scenarios for every arm alike.
  • Telemetry up to the origin is assumed available at forecast time. If it is not, the detector's gain after an ending is a ceiling.
  • The window failure of E0d (Primary D14) is not diagnosed.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Check why E0d departs upward on D14 from late August to the end of the window (a change in the detector inputs, or a refit artefact), before any further detector work.
  • Train the detector only on the "ended" label with the survival untouched, and score it as a classifier (delay and false alarms per Primary-month) before using it to scale the survival.
  • If a detector is wanted, leave out the neighbour feed: the placebo shows it is not what helps.

docs.title: Neither a spread recalibration nor a sum of distributions beats the free network
docs.text:
We asked whether the explicit solar curve helps mainly by getting the width of the net-demand forecast right, rather than by moving its centre. Net demand is the power a substation draws after rooftop solar output has been subtracted, and gross demand is the power before that subtraction. The free neural network is experiment 644's forecasting model, which has weather inputs but no solar curve. We tested two ways to fix the width. The first widens or narrows the free neural network's forecast bands with a map fitted on earlier rows (the recalibration). The second builds the forecast as the gross-demand forecast of experiment 655's neural network minus the solar output of one randomly chosen ensemble member (the sum of distributions). An ensemble member is one of the 51 alternative weather forecasts that the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) issues for each run. Neither approach beat the free neural network.

The free neural network is miscalibrated on sunny middays, but as a one-sided bias, not a wrong width. Sunny middays are the half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC whose observed clear-sky index is at least 0.7. At lead days 1 to 2, the realised power falls below the network's 5% quantile in 9.3% of those half-hours, and above its 95% quantile in 1.9%. Experiment 655 found that four explicit-solar forms lost to the free neural network. Experiment 664 finds that the loss is not explained by a missing spread.

Scores are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS; smaller is better) in points, where a point is one percent of a Primary substation's effective capacity. The test half-hours are those in the 60 days after each of three test-window start dates (2025-07, 2026-03, and 2026-06), pooled over the six Primary substations that are metered in MW and over five seeds.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Each arm's CRPS gain over the free network on sunny middays, with 99.9% day-block intervals (a negative gain means the arm is worse). Arm (b) is the recalibrated free network. Arm (c) is the sum of distributions with independent draws, and (d) is arm (c) recalibrated. The last two are the sum with coupled draws and its recalibration. Arm (c0) subtracts the member-average curve, and (p) and (s) are the placebos with another Primary's capacity and another date's curves.

Probability integral transform (PIT) of the realised power in each forecast's distribution: flat at 0.1 would be perfectly calibrated. The free network (a) piles up near 0, meaning the realised power is often below the forecast; recalibrating it (b) does not flatten it on the test months, and the sum of distributions (c) flattens the lowest bin and leaves the same slope.

One forecast run at D5 in the 2026-06 test month, from the free network (top) and the sum of distributions (bottom). The sum of distributions has the wider upper band around the day-time peak and the lower band that dips below zero at night.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Decision rule: neither (b) nor (c) beats (a) by the bar, so the rule says to stop. The contrasts below are the control's CRPS minus the arm's, in points, with the Bonferroni interval over 36 contrasts (12 per band, three bands); a negative number favours the control.
  • Planned contrasts, sunny middays (bar 0.084, 0.093, 0.123 at day 1-2, 3-5, 6-10):
    • free minus recalibrated free (a minus b): -0.07 [-0.15, +0.03], +0.06 [-0.05, +0.15], -0.26 [-0.45, -0.10];
    • free minus sum of distributions (a minus c): -0.38 [-0.64, -0.18], -0.29 [-0.53, -0.09], -0.33 [-0.49, -0.17];
    • recalibrated free minus sum (b minus c): -0.31 [-0.62, -0.07], -0.35 [-0.62, -0.12], -0.06 [-0.32, +0.19];
    • recalibrated free minus recalibrated sum (b minus d): -0.28 [-0.50, -0.09], -0.20 [-0.42, 0.00], -0.28 [-0.44, -0.11].
  • Coupled draws (same quantile level for both) are worse still: a minus the coupled sum is -0.68, -0.89, and -1.54, with 5%-95% coverage of 63%, 43%, and 19%. On the fine-tuning rows the correlation between the member-average solar curve and the position of the realised gross demand in its forecast distribution is 0.09 (range -0.04 to 0.17 over the 25 month-and-seed runs), so the independence assumption is close and the coupling is unsupported.
  • Placebos pass pooled: The sum of distributions beats the version with another Primary's capacity by 1.84, 1.48, and 0.97 points, and the version with another date's curves by 2.54, 2.02, and 1.05 points (intervals exclude zero). The member solar curve therefore carries information about the centre. At D10 the other-Primary placebo (5.47 points) beats the sum (5.83), so the placebo result does not hold at every Primary.
  • What the member draw adds: Against subtracting the member-average curve from the same gross draws (arm c0), the random member costs 0.02 [-0.01, +0.04], 0.06 [+0.02, +0.12], and 0.12 [+0.02, +0.21] points at the three lead bands. The interval widens (coverage 93.1% against 90.0% at lead days 1 to 2) without a better score. The measured correlation between the spread of the member curves and the size of the gross-demand error on the fine-tuning rows is 0.06, so the spread carries little information about the error.
  • Coverage on sunny middays (5% to 95%, nominal 90%): free network 88.8%, 88.2%, 87.6% at the three bands; recalibrated 86.6%, 85.1%, 90.3%; sum 93.1%, 94.9%, 96.5%; recalibrated sum 89.6%, 88.0%, 93.5%. Mean 5%-95% width, free network: 23.8, 26.8, and 31.2 points; sum: 27.9, 33.5, and 41.1.
  • Tail calibration, sunny middays, all leads (free network / sum): coverage below the 0.01 quantile 2.5% / 0.6%, below 0.05 11.1% / 3.9%, below 0.95 99.2% / 99.2%, below 0.99 99.8% / 99.8%; pinball loss at 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99 is 0.174 / 0.190, 0.700 / 0.716, 1.071 / 1.222, and 0.291 / 0.330 points. At the upper tail both arms cover 99.2% below the 95% quantile, so the upper band is too wide.
  • PIT distance from uniform (total variation, sunny middays day 1-2): free network 0.176, recalibrated 0.198, sum 0.125, recalibrated sum 0.144. The sum is closer to uniform and still scores worse, because CRPS also rewards a sharp centre.
  • Error of the median beside the score: the mean absolute error of the median on sunny middays is 6.42 points for the free network, 6.58 for (b), and 6.84 for (c), so the median and CRPS point the same way (trigger 3 does not fire). The median minus the mean of the 11 quantiles over all half-hours is -0.67 points (free network) and -0.55 (sum).
  • Per Primary (CRPS, sunny middays, free network / sum): D5 4.32 / 5.65, D9 4.27 / 4.34, D10 5.61 / 5.83, D11 3.79 / 4.06, D14 3.79 / 4.00, D16 5.33 / 5.19. The sum wins only at D16 (by 0.14); D5 accounts for most of the pooled loss, but leaving D5 out still leaves the sum behind the free network at the other five Primaries on average.
  • All half-hours: free minus sum is -0.02 [-0.06, +0.03] and free minus recalibrated free is -0.09 [-0.13, -0.06], so the recalibration also hurts overall.
  • Audit triggers: The prediction (a gain of 0.05 to 0.15 points at lead days 1 to 2) was contradicted, which is trigger 2. This page tests three explanations: the explicit curves already lost in experiment 655, the member draw adds width without information, and the bias is one-sided. The tests are the arm that subtracts the member-average curve from the same gross draws (arm c0), the placebos, and the PIT histograms. The two placebos lose pooled, and the median and CRPS agree. Leaving D5 out does not flip the sign. No audit was run. The free network's CRPS of 3.75, 4.28, and 5.05 points reproduces experiment 655's values exactly.
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first full run. It found no bug that biases the comparison; two findings were applied (clip the recalibrated levels to [0.001, 0.999], assert the fine-tuning leads lie in 0 to 360 hours), and one finding was accepted as a caveat (below).
  • Caveats: arms using draws (c, d, and the coupled and placebo arms) rest on 2,000 draws per row, so their 0.01 and 0.99 quantiles use about 20 draws each and carry sampling noise that arms (a) and (b), computed from the exact mixture, do not; the median check against experiment 655's stored arm d differs by 0.13 points on average, consistent with that noise. The recalibration cells use the ensemble forecast's clear-sky index, pool the six Primaries, and use at least 2,733 held-out fine-tuning rows each; none fell back to a pooled cell.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Architecture:
    • Arm (a) is experiment 644's free network, a modular mixture-density neural network (three Gaussian components) whose fresh fine-tuning mixer reads the ensemble-mean weather, date-time, and ensemble-spread columns and the lead time; it is read from its stored weights.
    • Arms (c) onward use experiment 655's arm d network, trained on gross demand (the target plus capacity times the member-average cell-temperature solar curve, with the calibrated season-year probe capacity of experiment 644's arm b), from its stored weights.
    • The sum of distributions (c) draws 2,000 gross-demand values from arm d's mixture per row and subtracts the solar curve of an independently drawn ensemble member (curve per member, cell temperature, 655's physics); (c, coupled) sorts both sets of draws and pairs them.
  • Training regime: nothing is trained. Both neural networks come from experiments 644 and 655 (monthly fine-tuning on the 24 months before each test month, five seeds); the per-member curves are recomputed from the 51-member extract of experiment 655 and match its member-average table. GPU time for this experiment is under 0.2 hours.
  • Measurement:
    • Rows, cutoffs, and the five seeds are experiment 644's (the code asserts the row keys), with cleaned power and the six MW Primaries; weather is the ensemble forecast, available at forecast time.
    • The recalibration maps level tau to the tau-quantile of the held-out fine-tuning rows' PITs in each of six cells (lead band by forecast sunny call), applied to the arm's own distribution. It uses fine-tuning rows only.
    • CRPS comes from the 11 quantiles; intervals are day-block bootstraps at the Bonferroni level for 36 contrasts; the bars are experiment 644's.
    • Placebos are applied at forecast time only (the network is not refitted).
