docs.title: How much of an injected load-shift event does each event-table method find, split by how long the event lasts and how deep the step is?
docs.text:
Where an injected (synthetic) load shift lasts more than 7 days and steps 8 noise units or more, the event table of experiment 653 finds events carrying 0.67 of the injected megawatts and the neural network of experiment 658 finds 0.65. Shallower and shorter shifts are found much less often. A Primary substation steps electricity down to a local distribution network, and the project forecasts the demand at each Primary. A load shift is the switching of part of a circuit from one Primary to a neighbour, which moves demand between the two. The residual is the observed cleaned power minus a demand forecast that uses no lagged power, so a load shift shows as a step in the residual. A noise unit is a Primary's typical difference between successive 6-hour block means, which is between 0.16 and 1.02 MW depending on the Primary.

Experiment 653 built an event table of load shifts by splitting each Primary's residual into segments with a penalised segmentation method. Experiment 658 did the same with a recurrent neural network. Each page reported one recall: 0.64 for the event table and 0.52 for the neural network, where recall is the share of the injected megawatts that belong to an event the method found. This page re-scores their stored outputs on six types of injected event (three lengths times two depths). No XGBoost model was fitted and no neural network was trained.

The event table found 0.67 (95% interval 0.60 to 0.76) of the megawatts in the long and deep type, and the neural network found 0.65 (0.56 to 0.74). Neither method linked the two ends of an injected transfer well in any type: 0.42 was the best, from only 14 transfer ends. On the real record the long and deep type is almost empty. The verdict is partly supported: 3 of the 6 predictions held (P1b, P2, and P5), and P1a, P3, and P4 failed. The hypothesis was only half right: shallow shifts of more than a day are found at 0.50 to 0.52 (event table) and 0.31 to 0.32 (neural network), well above the quarter the hypothesis allowed.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Type, or cell. One of six groups of injected events. Long is more than 7 days (including events with no end), medium is more than 1 day up to 7 days, and short is 1 day or less. Deep is 8 noise units or more and shallow is 2 to under 8.
  • Injected event, world. A synthetic load shift added to the real residual by experiment 653's injector. A world is one copy of the residual panel with injected events; there are 6.
  • Found. An injected event is found when the method has an event at the right Primary and sign with a start within 12 hours (and, for a transfer, the right donor).
  • Edge transfer, end, paired. An injected edge transfer moves demand from a donor Primary to a recipient Primary, so it makes a step down at one and a step up at the other. Each step is an end of the transfer. An end is paired when the method links it to the other end of its transfer.
  • MW-weighted share. The share of the injected megawatts (absolute value) in events that are found, or in transfer ends that are paired.
  • Primary-year. One Primary observed for one year. There are 36.0 Primary-years with a reading in the scored years (2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30, 15 Primaries).
  • Stored units and panel depth. The event table and the neural network store each real event's size in noise units (stored units). For logged shifts and detector alarms, this experiment measures the size in the residual instead (panel depth, defined in Method).
  • Real record. NGED's measured half-hourly power at the 15 Primaries and its log of load shifts (NGED is National Grid Electricity Distribution, the network operator). The logs miss events.
  • LR_b20, RO-NC. The label-trained and label-free detectors of experiment 254: a logistic-regression detector trained on NGED's labels, and the refit-offset neighbour-count detector. Their output is a list of alarms.
  • D5, D16, and similar. Anonymised Primary names. A seed is one random start of neural-network training; there are 3.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
The first figure shows that both methods find more in the deep cells than in the shallow ones, and that the neural network falls away fastest for short shifts.

The second figure shows the verified D5 and D16 transfer: both methods decode D5 as a step of -1.1 MW and D16 as +2.0 to +2.1 MW, but their starts differ from the verified starts and neither method pairs the two Primaries.

The third figure shows the events each method calls in time that is more than 14 days from any logged or verified event, which is mostly small steps of under 2 noise units.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Not applicable: median minus mean forecast, tail calibration, curtailment cost, the normalised MAE of the median forecast, and the four scenarios, because no forecast is scored.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 1 (a control fails): the reproduction gates passed. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fired for P1a, P3, and P4. P1a missed by 0.03 with an interval that reaches 0.76, P3 missed by 0.01, and P4's miss rests on 14 edge-transfer ends with an interval of 0.13 to 0.66. These misses are consistent with small cells and do not show a method error. Triggers 3 to 7 do not apply, because the experiment has no forecast contrast, no nested arm, no sister experiment on the same rows, and no later design that rests on it. The numbers review (a fresh Sonnet agent) re-derived the injected-cell, real-record, event-free, and D5 and D16 figures from the raw stored files.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's event logs are an incomplete one-off dump, so clean rows may hold events that no label covers. Matched-shift counts are lower bounds.
  • Lab shortcuts. The injected events are added to the stored residual and not to the power before the demand model is refitted, so injected recall probably overstates recall on real events. The demand model trained on every row, so earlier real events leak into the residual's baseline.

docs.title: Reviews and triage
docs.text:
• Plan review (Sonnet). It made 15 findings, 4 of them high: the sign and weight of the injected shares, the coding of permanent events, the reproduction gate's row filter, and the exclusion of pulses. All 15 were accepted and written into the plan before the scoring.
  • Code review (Sonnet). It made 8 findings, and none changed an injected-world number. The code review ran after the first scoring run, not before it, as the plan said it would. Accepted and fixed: the per-Primary-year denominator, the split of rows in no type into under 2 noise units and unmeasured depth, the extra measurement of the event table's depth in the residual panel, and a check that event-free spans end after they start. Accepted as page text: the missing end errors and the first-seed counts. Not changed: the cosmetic type: ignore comments.
  • Numbers review (Sonnet). It made 8 findings, 1 high. Accepted and fixed: the per-cell rates used the nominal 37.45 Primary-years instead of 36.0 (a bug in the script, fixed and re-run); the claim that short events pull the headline recalls down (the headline rows hold no short event); the count of events missing an end error; the pairing advice item; the deep-minus-shallow range; the short-event wording; the event-free range; and the 184 and 181 counts. All figures in Results match the stored files after the fixes.
  • Prose review (Sonnet). It made 59 findings. Accepted: the opening and the Terms section (moved ahead of the figures), the take-home message, the bare "network" and "table", the placeholder in this section, the tables for pairing and matched shifts, the topic-label leads, and the full sentences in Method. Rejected: a rewrite of the next-experiment section into a bare description (it states a proposal, which the plan page owns); the hypothesis text, which stays as pre-registered.
  • Figure review (Sonnet). It made 22 findings. Accepted: the event counts and pair counts on the axis, larger text, the band-height note, the experiment 580 label on the verified lines, the "under 2 noise units" group and sample-size note in the third figure, and plain method names in its legend.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should test whether the shallow events of more than a day can be found more often. Both methods find about two thirds of the long and deep megawatts, but the real record holds few such events. Most real events the event table calls are shallow, and in those types the event table finds about half of the injected megawatts and the neural network about a third. LR_b20 and RO-NC also match more of the logged medium shifts than either method.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture and algorithm.

  • The event table of experiment 653 (arm masked, spec default). The input is the observed cleaned power minus the forecast of the lag-free convex demand model of experiment 130, as stored by experiment 327. It covers 15 Primaries on a half-hourly grid from 2022-01-01 to 2026-06-30, with the median across Primaries removed. A seasonal slow level per Primary is fitted with candidate events masked and then frozen. A dynamic programme (Viterbi, 1967) decodes 6-hour blocks into 25 states (no shift, and 12 log-spaced amplitudes of 1 to 20 noise units in each sign) with a Student-t emission. Events at neighbouring Primaries are paired by sign, start, end, and share. The page of experiment 653 has the full description.
  • The neural network of experiment 658 (second look, arm net). A bidirectional recurrent neural network reads all 15 Primaries' residuals and their neighbour links. It has 32 hidden units, dropout 0.3, weight decay 0.01, and Gaussian noise on the inputs. It is trained on experiment 653's injector over 300 worlds of 2022-01-01 to 2023-06-30. Its decoder is tuned on validation worlds of 2023 (boost 10, cut-off 0.5, onset cost 0.5). The page of experiment 658 has the full description.
  • This experiment. It fits nothing. It assigns each stored injected event, logged shift, event, and alarm to a type by its length and depth, and recomputes the scores per type.

Training regime.

  • No training happens here. Experiment 653 trains nothing, and experiment 658 trained a neural network from 3 random starts. This experiment reads their stored outputs and ran on 1 CPU core in a few minutes, with no GPU.

Measurement.

  • The injected events are the 6 worlds of experiment 653's injector in its default spec, scored over 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30. The rows are events of kind edge (a transfer between two Primaries), solo (a shift with no partner), permanent_transfer, or permanent_shift, of 2 noise units or more, in both signs, weighted by absolute megawatts. The hard negatives (ramps, routine steps, and placebo pairs) are excluded, and pulses are reported apart.
  • A type is set by the injected length and depth. The length comes from the injected days, where -1 means no end and counts as long. The depth comes from the injected units. The cut points are 1 day, 7 days, and 8 noise units.
  • Found, paired, and timing are scored as the decision rule states. The intervals are 2000 resamples of whole worlds, with the 3 seeds averaged in each draw.
  • The real-record events are the stored events of the scored years, with the type taken from stored units. The LR_b20 and RO-NC alarms of experiment 254 (duplicates removed) and the logged shifts of experiment 580 get a panel depth. The panel depth is the absolute difference between the median residual over the 3 days after the onset (or to the end if that comes sooner) and the median over the 3 days before, in noise units, and it needs 48 readings in each window. A logged shift is matched when a method's start at the same Primary lies within 4 half-hours (strict) or 48 half-hours (loose) of the logged onset.
  • Event-free time is the set of half-hours with a reading that lie more than 14 days from every labelled or verified event of experiment 580 at the same Primary. A decoded event counts as event-free when none of its half-hours lies in the excluded time.
  • The standing practices hold. The data are cleaned, D15 and D18 lose every row before 2025-03-01, and no row from 2026-07-01 onward is read (the script asserts it).

docs.title: What does a one-year backtest of the simple shared wind network S and the simple shared solar network PLP forecast for the 3 metered wind farms and the 6 metered solar farms?
docs.text:
The year-long backtest is complete. wind.parquet and solar.parquet hold forecasts for 365 daily origins. Both neural networks score sensibly at every lead out to 14 days, and solar at days 10 to 14 is only slightly better than climatology. The files are private (they hold the time series of NGED's metered generators, labelled by their original time_series_id). The backtest is descriptive, not a ranking: the year overlaps the development months of experiment 659, and origins from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31 lie in the window earlier experiments kept as a final test, so those months are no longer a held-out test for choosing between the networks and the defaults. No figures are included on this page; the scores below come from scores/*.csv.

Scores fall with lead for both neural networks, and solar PLP stays below climatology in every band. CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) is the mean pinball loss over 11 quantile levels, in points of capacity (smaller is better). Capacity is the production effective capacity, the same table as the shared folder's series_capacity.parquet. Bands are half-open ranges of days from the 12:00 UTC origin to the valid time; the "7-14 d" and "10-14 d" rows overlap the other rows, so the table is not a partition. Wind scores count idle readings (experiment 210's idle mask) as zero until 2026-09-13; solar is scored on daylight half-hours only.

Lead band Wind S CRPS Wind coverage q05-q95 Solar PLP CRPS Solar coverage q05-q95 Solar climatology CRPS 0-1 d 2.29 0.901 2.19 0.894 3.38 1-3 d 2.73 0.904 2.41 0.889 3.38 3-7 d 3.84 0.909 2.87 0.882 3.38 7-14 d 4.82 0.919 3.18 0.884 3.38 10-14 d 4.93 0.922 3.24 0.886 3.39 All 4.06 0.913 2.91 0.885 3.38

Wind S (raw ensemble weather only) and solar PLP (physics-lite power plus raw weather) are the networks of experiment 659. Wind S median mean absolute error (MAE, % of capacity) runs from 8.2 at 0-1 d to 18.3 at 10-14 d, and solar PLP from 7.9 to 12.8 (climatology: 13.3). Share of observations above q99 (ideal 0.01): wind 0.016 at 0-1 d and 0.023 at 10-14 d; solar 0.012 and 0.011. Share below q01: wind 0.011 and 0.007; solar 0.028 and 0.032 (most solar rows below q01 have an observed power of zero or less). By origin month, wind S scores best in July and August (2.67 and 2.77) and worst in November (5.52); solar PLP scores best in December (1.27) and worst in March (3.95) and September (3.74).

docs.title: Checks and caveats
docs.text:
• Wind S matches experiment 659 on matched rows. On the rows both cover (December, January, March, and June origins, 231,000 rows), this experiment scores 4.174 and experiment 659 scores 4.179 when both use experiment 659's scoring capacity. The absolute numbers on this page are about 5% higher than experiment 659's because the production effective capacity is 2.3% to 8.7% below experiment 659's wind capacity. Solar is 0.13 points worse than experiment 659 on 120,000 matched rows (3.350 against 3.224), possibly because each refit here is one month older for the scored months and the solar neural network here trains on leads up to 348 h.
  • Prediction (1) (within 0.15 points of 3.684 on overlapping months) cannot be judged on that basis: the overlap-month score here is 4.011 because of the capacity difference and because the 3.684 includes October 2025. On matched rows and matched capacity the two agree. Prediction (2) holds overall (3.24 against 3.39) but not from November to March, when solar PLP at 10-14 d scores worse than climatology by 0.03 to 0.42 points; it is better by 0.17 to 0.48 points from April to September. Prediction (3) holds for wind and solar coverage in every band (0.88 to 0.92; solar is just under 0.90). The share of very sunny-day observations above q99 is 2.8% on this experiment's own definition (each farm's top tenth of days by energy in its month), which is not comparable with experiment 659's 10.6% to 12.7%; the weak upper tail on very sunny days is not resolved.
  • Seasonal bias. The solar median is high in spring (+6.5 points of capacity in March) and low in autumn (-6.9 in September, -8.5 in October, all 6 farms), and the solar neural network has no calendar input; one year with quarterly refits cannot separate a seasonal effect from refit age. The wind median at 10-14 d is low in November and December (only 28% and 32% of observations fall below q50). Wide bands at long leads may explain why coverage stays near 0.90.
  • Wind idle mask ends on 2026-09-13. From that date idle readings count as observed in scoring and in the 2026-10-01 refit's training target, so September and October are scored on a different target (one farm's share below q01 rises from 1.1% to 5.4%).
  • Capacity scale. The networks scale by the 99.9th percentile of cleaned power over the 730 days before each refit, which is 1.02 to 1.12 times the stored effective capacity, so some quantiles exceed the stored capacity (the largest q99 is 1.12 times, at solar series 22). Observed solar power exceeds the stored capacity on 5% to 9% of April daylight rows.
  • Solar night. Night half-hours are zero. The daylight flag is the mean cosine of the zenith over the 3-hour or 6-hour ensemble period, so about 3,000 half-hours around dusk and dawn at leads of 6 days or more carry small non-zero quantiles (q99 at most 0.7% of capacity), and some dawn and dusk half-hours in a mostly dark period are forecast as zero. The solar all-half-hours tables in scores/ are diluted by night rows and by 3.8% negative night readings; use the solar_daylight_*.csv tables.
  • Scoring rows. Rows without observed power are dropped, so origins after about 2026-10-26 are scored on part of their 14 days. Observed power is not in the files.
  • No break at any refit boundary in the median, band width, or q99: consecutive-origin forecasts for the same valid times differ by no more than the ordinary day-to-day change at all 11 wind boundaries and all 3 solar boundaries. Median minus mean forecast per site was not computed (the mixture mean is not stored).
  • Reviews (all fresh agents; every finding was triaged against the code):
    • Before the first fit, 2 Sonnet reviews (leakage and contract) found 8 minor points. The accepted fixes were assertions that no training valid time reaches the refit, coverage and archive checks that raise, and Int8 and origin-count checks.
    • Before the first fit, 1 Opus review of leakage and fold logic found 3 low or informational points and no leakage.
    • After the files were written, 1 Sonnet file audit found 4 low points. Both files were clean, one wind fold and one solar fold re-ran from scratch to 0.0 MW difference, and the scores reproduced.
    • 1 Opus review of the files and scores found 12 points, which are the caveats above.
    • 1 Sonnet prose and number review found no wrong number; its prose findings are applied.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Neural networks and weather inputs. Wind S and solar PLP of experiment 659: a pooled network of two hidden layers of 64 units with a three-component Gaussian mixture over power as a fraction of capacity, 11 quantiles read from the mixture and capped at capacity, 3 seeds averaged quantile by quantile and then sorted. Wind S reads the mean and standard deviation across the 51 ensemble members of 10 m and 100 m wind speed, the sine and cosine of the 100 m direction, and air temperature, plus the lead (sine and cosine of its hour of day, and hundreds of hours) and a one-hot wind-farm column. Solar PLP reads 18 inputs: mean and standard deviation of shortwave, air temperature, and 10 m wind speed, the ensemble means of relative humidity, longwave radiation, precipitation, and surface pressure, the mean and standard deviation of the fixed physics-lite power and of the Faiman cell temperature, the sun's elevation, the sine and cosine of its azimuth, and the lead; there is no farm column and no calendar column. No ERA5 or CAMS pre-training.
  • Origins and weather. One origin per day at 12:00 UTC from 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31, using the 00 UTC ECMWF ENS run of that day (51 members, treated as available at 09:00 UTC); valid times run half-hourly for 672 half-hours from 12:00 (lead from the 00 UTC run 12 h to 347.5 h). Where the ensemble steps are 3-hourly or 6-hourly, the value is interpolated as in experiments 310 and 430; the share of daylight half-hours lacking their own stamp is 0% at every lead.
  • Power lags. Neither network reads a power lag, so the 6-hour power delay changes no feature. The power delay sets only the training cut-off of each refit. The first forecast half-hour (valid 12:00) has already ended at the origin; no power is an input, so this leaks nothing.
  • Refits. Wind S refits on day 0 of each month (12 refits), training on runs and valid times before 62 days earlier and stopping early on the last 62 days, 40 epochs. Solar PLP refits on 2025-11-01, 2026-02-01, 2026-05-01, and 2026-08-01 (each scores the next three months), training on valid times before one day earlier, with the last 61 days for early stopping, 20 epochs, and daylight rows with leads below 348 h from the 00 UTC run (experiments 430 and 659 stopped at 251.5 h); solar trains on all daylight half-hours, including more low-sun half-hours than experiment 659 kept. Wind training leads run to 351 h from the 09:00 stamp, as in experiment 659. Capacity is the 99.9th percentile of cleaned power over the 730 days before each refit. Wind idle readings are zero in training and scoring until 2026-09-13.
  • Compute time. About 20 minutes of GPU time in 3 parallel processes (36 wind fits, 12 solar fits).
  • Scoring. The 11-level pinball loss times 100 and the normalised median MAE, by origin-to-valid lead band and origin month, against cleaned observed power (outside the files). Solar climatology is the farm's own power at the same month and half-hour before each refit.

docs.title: What does a one-year backtest of the class 2 Candidate demand network with a survival-hazard prevailing output score at the 16 Primaries, with every input at least 6 hours old?
docs.text:
A one-year backtest of the Candidate demand neural network at the 16 Primaries scored a CRPS of 4.14 points of capacity for the prevailing output and 4.32 for the NRA output. The year runs from 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31, with one forecast origin per day at 12:00 UTC and 672 half-hours (14 days) per origin. The backtest is descriptive, not a ranking: the year overlaps the development months and the final-test window, nothing was tuned on it, and nothing is adopted for production. A Primary is a primary substation, metered in MW or MVA (megavolt-amperes, apparent power). The Candidate is the neural network that experiment 612 chose from three classes of demand network design: it reads lagged power, power summaries from neighbouring Primaries, and the ECMWF ensemble weather forecast (ENS, 51 members). It outputs 11 quantiles per half-hour.

The two outputs differ in how they treat a load shift. A load shift is a transfer of load between Primaries, usually for days to weeks and not labelled in NGED's data. The NRA output (normal running arrangement) is the Candidate's 11 quantiles, which forecast power as if no load shift were in force. The prevailing output mixes those 11 quantiles with a copy of them shifted by a learned depth, weighted by the probability that a load shift is still in force (the survival probability, read from a small neural-network output called the survival head, which predicts a hazard for each of 14 days). In November and December 2025 the survival probability comes from a fixed log-normal curve (the fallback), because no earlier month had yet produced training data for the survival head.

The score rises with lead time by 28% (prevailing) and 18% (NRA). The prevailing output's CRPS rises from 3.46 points of capacity at days 0 to 1 to 4.43 at days 7 to 14.

Lead band NRA CRPS NRA median error Prevailing CRPS Prevailing median error 0 to 1 days 3.84 6.70 3.46 6.12 1 to 3 days 3.96 6.92 3.66 6.48 3 to 7 days 4.23 7.43 4.04 7.19 7 to 14 days 4.53 8.00 4.43 7.94 All 4.32 7.59 4.14 7.39

CRPS is twice the mean pinball loss, and median error is the normalised mean absolute error of the median. All values are points of capacity. "Median error" is the normalised mean absolute error of the median (q50): 100 times the absolute error divided by the Primary's capacity, averaged over scored half-hours. CRPS is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantile levels, divided by capacity, times 100. The pooled value weights each half-hour equally, so a Primary with a large spread counts once per half-hour, not once per Primary.

By month of the origin, the prevailing output has the lower CRPS in 9 of 12 months, but the two outputs are not scored like for like. The NRA output is lower in 2025-12 (the second fold that uses the fallback survival curve), 2026-01, and 2026-06.

Month of origin NRA CRPS NRA median error Prevailing CRPS Prevailing median error 2025-11 3.63 6.45 3.59 6.39 2025-12 4.32 7.42 4.42 7.56 2026-01 4.11 7.06 4.14 7.46 2026-02 3.80 6.98 3.73 6.83 2026-03 5.45 9.73 4.88 8.95 2026-04 4.26 7.78 4.15 7.39 2026-05 3.98 7.27 3.88 7.03 2026-06 3.64 6.45 3.79 6.76 2026-07 5.12 8.50 4.62 8.09 2026-08 4.89 8.18 4.38 7.86 2026-09 4.32 7.76 3.98 7.18 2026-10 4.18 7.33 4.05 7.06

The month is the month of the forecast origin. An origin on 31 October scores valid times until 14 November under 2026-10. The NRA output deliberately excludes load shifts that the metered power contains, so a lower prevailing CRPS partly reflects that the prevailing output may move with them.

Both outputs are too narrow, and the pre-registered coverage prediction P3 failed. P3 said that the q05 to q95 coverage of the NRA output would lie within 0.05 of 0.90 in every month. The NRA coverage lies within 0.05 of 0.90 in 3 of 12 months (2025-11, 2026-02, 2026-06). The NRA coverage runs from 0.72 (August) to 0.89 (November), the prevailing coverage from 0.80 (July) to 0.89 (November).

Lead band NRA q05 to q95 NRA q25 to q75 Prevailing q05 to q95 Prevailing q25 to q75 0 to 1 days 0.826 0.425 0.872 0.465 1 to 3 days 0.821 0.418 0.864 0.456 3 to 7 days 0.815 0.408 0.851 0.440 7 to 14 days 0.810 0.403 0.839 0.426

Part of the NRA output's coverage shortfall is built in. The NRA output is a counterfactual target, scored here against metered power, so event windows fall outside its band by construction. Part of the coverage gap between the two outputs comes from that effect and not from a fault in the NRA band. The band was not rescaled in this experiment.

The example shows a Primary where the two outputs differ visibly. It is series 26 (metered in MVA) from the origin of 2026-02-01 12:00 UTC, one of the three origins at that Primary where the prevailing median differs most from the NRA median. The prevailing output moves often at this Primary and does not beat the NRA output there, and its q05 falls below zero MVA (see Caveats).

Predictions P1 and P2 were not tested. P1 compared the Candidate's score at days 0 to 10 after the extension to 14 days with experiment 620's stored Candidate on the same months. No matched run was made, so P1 is unevaluated. P2 asked whether the survival output stays calibrated at days 10 to 14, and the page has no measurement of it. The survival probability at days 10 to 14 is read from the generator, not checked against observed events (see Caveats).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Base neural network: the Candidate (arm P7+D50: neighbour power summaries, 50% signal dropout, no explicit gate) of experiment 612 and experiment 613, as set up by experiment 610, experiment 620, and the encoder pre-training of experiments 559, 565, and 574. The Candidate's seed-mean 11 quantiles are the NRA output. The horizon limit is raised from 240 to 339 hours; ENS summaries reach about 351 hours.
  • Origins and weather: the weather is the ECMWF ENS 00Z run of the origin day (51 members), which the Candidate treats as available at 09:00 UTC. The forecast is made at that native 09:00 UTC origin and relabelled to the contract's 12:00 UTC origin by adding 3 hours. Valid times before 12:00 UTC are dropped, leaving 672 half-hours per origin. nwp_init_time is 00:00 UTC of the origin day.
  • Lags and the 6-hour cut: the Candidate's lags and neighbour summaries read power observed at least 24 hours before its native origin, so the newest power read is from 09:00 UTC on the day before, 27 hours before the contract's 12:00 UTC origin. The contract's rule (nothing newer than origin minus 6 hours) therefore needed no change to the recipe. A check asserts that every lag time is at least 24 hours before the native origin.
  • Folds and training: 12 monthly refits, with test months 2025-11 to 2026-10. Each fold trains on cleaned power and weather available before its month, with the embargoes of experiment 613 (3 days at the mixer step, 7 days at the daily fine-tune), 2 seeds with seed-mean-then-sort quantiles, and the 90-day recency half-life. Lag, weather, and date-time encoders are pre-trained on ERA5 and CAMS, a fresh mixer is trained on the whole ENS history (starting 2024-04-01, so the early folds have less ENS data), then the daily fine-tune runs. The cleaned power drops the substation_zero rows, and the D15 and D18 histories are cut before 2025-03-01.
  • Prevailing output: the 11 quantiles of the mixture (1 - p) NRA + p (NRA shifted by a learned depth d, with spread sigma), with the shifted part as 3 Gauss-Hermite components at d + g sigma and the quantiles read from the mixture's cumulative distribution (experiment 647's mixture_quantiles). p = exp(-cumulative hazard), where the head outputs 14 daily hazards, so p keeps falling to day 14. The head of experiment 652 (R-haz) sits on the Candidate and not on K1, with its gate-state input removed.
  • Training the head: the head trains on banks of injected shifts (the generator of experiment 650), one bank per earlier month, built from the real history of that month with synthetic shifts and forecast by that month's Candidate chain (inference only). Fold M's head trains only on banks of months before M and on rows whose valid time is before the start of M. Two seeds are averaged.
  • Fallback in the first two folds: with fewer than 2 earlier banks (folds 2025-11 and 2025-12), the prevailing rows use B-haz instead: the Candidate plus its own recent residual times a log-normal survival curve fitted on synthetic durations (no fit on observed power). The prevailing rows equal the NRA rows exactly on 74% of November origins and 65% of December origins (where the residual is missing), and on no origin from 2026-01 onward.
  • Full-row test matrices: inputs are built for every valid time from 12:00 UTC to 14 days later for every origin, including half-hours with no observed power, so that no input gap follows the stored matrices' gaps after 2026-10-17. Scoring is restricted to half-hours with observed, unflagged power.
  • Units: quantiles are scaled by each Primary's capacity and stored in MW for series 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 16, 17, and 18, and in MVA for series 3, 9, 11, 14, 15, 24, 25, and 26.
  • Scoring: against ground_truth_primaries.parquet (cleaned power, outside the file), divided by series_capacity.parquet, as defined under the first table.
  • Compute: about 0.5 GPU-hours per fold for the Candidate chains, inside the 10 GPU-hour ceiling.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Row count: 7,848,960 = 16 series x 365 origins x 672 half-hours x 2 outputs; 672 rows per series-origin-output.
  • No duplicate keys; no null or non-finite quantile; no crossing in any of the 10 adjacent quantile pairs; all times are UTC.
  • Timing: the file's NRA rows for a 12:00 UTC origin equal the native 09:00 UTC fit's seed-mean quantiles times capacity exactly (maximum difference 0.0), so the 3-hour offset is applied once.
  • Leakage, fold logic: reviews by a Sonnet reviewer for leakage, a Sonnet reviewer for the contract, and an Opus reviewer of the fold logic found no leak into any fold's training data.
  • Leakage, prevailing head: no automatic flag mask computed from the scored month is applied to the head's training rows, and fold M's head trains only on banks of months before M. A Sonnet review of the head's code checked both.
  • File and scores: a Sonnet audit of the file, with a from-scratch re-run of one fold, passed. An Opus review of the file and the scores reproduced every score to 3 decimals and found no unit, timing, or scaling error.
  • No observed power is stored in the file.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The survival probability beyond day 10 reflects the bank generator's duration prior. The generator draws short events of 3 to 14 days and long events of 28 to 112 days, none of 15 to 27 days, so hazards for days 11 to 14 are not estimated from observed events.
  • The prevailing output has no floor at zero for MVA-only series. Series 26, 14, and 15 produce more negative q01 rows than the NRA output (the lowest prevailing q01 is -2.26 MVA at series 26, against -1.21 for NRA). Neither output is clamped.
  • Series 12 exports power (observed power runs from -0.92 MW to 1.28 MW, against a capacity of 3.0 MW), so its CRPS (13.0 to 13.6 points) is about three times the pooled value and adds about 0.6 points to it.
  • The prevailing output loses to the NRA output at series 14 and 26 (CRPS 7.16 against 6.90 at series 14, 7.41 against 7.37 at series 26), and its median at series 26 differs from the NRA median by more than 5 points of capacity, at some lead, on 52% of origins.
  • The first row of each origin covers the half-hour ending at the origin (11:30 to 12:00 UTC): valid_time is the end of the half-hour, and lead 0 is that row.
  • The bank's injected lags use the month's later power for proportional shifts, which stays within the months before the fold being scored.

docs.title: What do the one-year backtest files hold, how were the five models behind them built and trained, and how well do they forecast?
docs.text:
This page documents the five Parquet files of the one-year backtest in data/ml-experiments/backtest_year_2025-11_to_2026-10/. It has two readers: the colleague at NGED who receives the files, and an engineer who must re-implement one of the five models behind them. A Primary is a primary substation, a BSP is a bulk supply point, and a GSP is a grid supply point. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, and MAE is the mean absolute error. Both are in points of capacity, and smaller is better.

Take-home message. The five backtest files hold forecasts that are better than climatology at every lead band for the demand types and for solar, and better for wind out to day 10. The CRPS gain over climatology falls with lead time: for Primaries it falls from 35.3% at days 0 to 1 to 26.9% at days 10 to 14 (normal running), and for BSPs from 41.0% to 12.5%. The wind network has a CRPS 1.8% worse than climatology at days 10 to 14 (interval -3.3 to -0.4). On the common rows of the six MW Primaries the backtest outputs and research default 3 are close, and the backtest outputs are better at the seven MVA-only Primaries. The prevailing output scores better than the normal-running output overall, and worse in the 7 days after the one verified load shift. The files describe one year that overlaps the development months, so the scores are not a ranking.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: The five figures below show the normalised MAE of the median by forecast horizon, one per forecast type, beside the baselines. The y-axis does not start at zero.

docs.title: The files
docs.text:
The files are private. They hold forecasts and no observed power. The year overlaps the development months and the final-test months of earlier experiments, so the scores are a description of one year and not a ranking.

  • Period. One forecast origin per day at 12:00 UTC, from 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31 (365 origins, no gaps).
  • Horizon. Valid times run half-hourly from 12:00 UTC on the origin day to 11:30 UTC 14 days later: 672 half-hours per origin. The valid times of the last origin reach 2026-11-14.
  • Weather. The 00Z run of the ECMWF ensemble (51 members) of the origin day, treated as available at 09:00 UTC. The ensemble's lead from 00Z is 12 to 348 hours, inside the 360 hours that the run provides. Where the ensemble steps are 3 hours or 6 hours, the half-hourly values come from the production resampler (experiment 661).
  • Power delay. At 12:00 UTC the observed power is available only up to 06:00 UTC of the same day. No input of any model reads newer power. Wind and solar read no power lag, so the delay moves only the training cut-off of each refit.
  • Files and series.
File Series Units Rows (series x 365 origins x 672 half-hours) primaries.parquet 16 Primaries MW; MVA for the eight MVA-only Primaries 7,848,960 (two rows per key) bsps.parquet 2 BSPs (D13 Skegness, D17 Boston) MW 490,560 gsps.parquet 2 GSPs (D6 Walpole, D1 Bicker Fen) MW 490,560 wind.parquet 3 wind farms MW for one farm; MVA for the other two 735,840 solar.parquet 6 solar farms MW 1,471,680
  • Columns, in this order.
    • time_series_id: the series' original identifier from the metadata table, as an 8-bit integer.
    • valid_time: the half-hour the forecast is for, a UTC timestamp.
    • nwp_init_time: the 00Z ensemble run used, a UTC timestamp.
    • power_fcst_init_time: the forecast origin, 12:00 UTC.
    • q01, q05, q10, q25, q40, q50, q60, q75, q90, q95, q99: the forecast quantiles, sorted within the row, in the series' own units. q50 is the median forecast. Each quantile is the value that the observed power falls below with that probability, so q05 to q95 is a 90% band.
    • NRA_or_prevailing (primaries.parquet only): "NRA" or "prevailing".
  • What NRA_or_prevailing means. The normal running arrangement (NRA) rows forecast the demand the Primary would draw if the electricity network operator had made no load shift. The prevailing rows forecast the demand under the arrangement in force at the forecast origin, carrying a shift that is already running forward and widening the band with the probability that the shift ends. Each key (series, valid time, origin) has one row of each kind.
  • Checks. Each file is checked for the row count above, no duplicate key, no null or non-finite quantile, no crossing quantiles, and UTC time-zone. Each experiment's page states the results and a spot check that no input is newer than the limits above.
  • Clamps applied after the models ran. Two files are post-processed, and only the quantile values change. In solar.parquet, every quantile is zero on the half-hours where the sun is not above the horizon at the middle of the half-hour (the rule that the scores use for daylight). The clamp changes 271,808 of 1,471,680 rows (18.5%), and the largest change is 6.1% of capacity. The daylight rows are bit-identical to the unclamped file. In primaries.parquet, every quantile of the eight MVA-only Primaries is at least zero, because apparent power cannot be negative. That clamp changes 206,487 of 7,848,960 rows (2.6%), in D12, D22, and D8 only, and the largest change is 2.80 MVA. Both clamps are monotone, so no quantile crosses. The wind file is not clamped. The Primaries measured in MW keep their negative lower quantiles; the observed power of D10 and D15 is also negative at times.
  • Effect of the clamps on the scores. The solar scores are unchanged, because the scores use daylight half-hours only. The Primaries tables and figures on this page score the clamped primaries.parquet. The other tables and figures use the unclamped files.

docs.title: The ground-truth files
docs.text:
Five more private files hold the observed power, so a reader can score the forecast files without the NGED data store: ground_truth_primaries.parquet, ground_truth_bsps.parquet, ground_truth_gsps.parquet, ground_truth_wind.parquet, and ground_truth_solar.parquet. The forecast files never hold observed power. The script is ml-experiments/00668-documentation-of-the-one-year-backtest-files-models-training-and-performance/e00668_ground_truth.py.

  • Rows. One row per series per half-hour, from 2025-11-01 00:00 UTC to 2026-11-09 08:00 UTC, the last half-hour in the data store when the files were written. Every series has the full time grid, and a missing reading is an explicit null row. No row exists after 2026-11-09 08:00 UTC, so the last origins of the forecast files have no observed power for their later valid times, and a join from a forecast file gives no match there.
  • Columns, in this order.
    • time_series_id: the series' original identifier, an 8-bit integer. The data store and the metadata table hold it as a 32-bit integer, so a join to them needs a cast.
    • valid_time: the half-hour, a UTC timestamp, with the same name and meaning as in the forecast files so that the two join on (time_series_id, valid_time). The stamp is the source time column, which the power contract defines as the end of the observation period.
    • power: the cleaned reading as a 32-bit float, null where the production cleaning flagged the half-hour. The value is power_raw wherever drop_reason is null.
    • power_raw: the reading as delivered, a 32-bit float, read from the raw power table, and null where no reading exists.
    • drop_reason: a nullable string, the production cleaning rule that flagged the half-hour. The only rule in the cleaning code when the files were written is substation_zero, an exact zero from a Primary, BSP, or GSP.
    • research_flag: a nullable string, null in every file but the wind file. In the wind file it holds the rule name of the idle mask of experiment 210 (low_wind_idle or outage_suspected). The mask is a research tool and not part of the production cleaning. It does not null power, and it ends at 2026-09-13 17:30 UTC, so a wind row after that carries no flag whether or not the farm was idle.
    • power_unit: "MW" or "MVA" for each series, never implicit. Some Primaries and two wind farms are MVA series.
  • How to read the nulls. A null power means no usable reading and is not zero. Solar nulls are frequent at night, because the feed omits many night readings, so solar scores use daylight half-hours. Earlier experiments scored the half-hours that the wind idle mask flags as zero, by setting the target to 0; a scorer that reproduces those numbers does the same, and a scorer that drops them gets different numbers.
  • Capacity. A private series_capacity.parquet in the same folder holds the capacity that the scores divide by, one row per series. The rule is the production effective-capacity table, which has one value per series. It is not the capacity that the wind and solar networks train with (the 99.9th percentile of the 730 days before each refit). This page lists no generator capacity or identifier.
  • Baselines. The manual heuristic and climatology need power from before 2025-11-01, which these files do not hold. They read the cleaned power table of the data store.
  • Checks. The row count equals the series count times the half-hours in the grid for every file, no key repeats, the time-zone is UTC, and the series are 16 Primaries, 2 BSPs, 2 GSPs, 3 wind farms, and 6 solar farms. A fresh audit re-read all five files against the raw and cleaned tables for every series and found no mismatch.

docs.title: Primaries
docs.text: Primaries are forecast by the Candidate demand network (experiment 620), which gives the NRA rows, with the survival-hazard prevailing head R-haz (experiment 652), which gives the prevailing rows. The backtest itself is experiment 667. Its page fixes the choices that the earlier experiments left open, and this section restates both.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Inputs of the Candidate. One row per (Primary, ensemble run, valid half-hour); the network runs once per ensemble run, on summaries of the 51 members.
    • Weather: the mean over the 51 members of 7 variables (shortwave and longwave radiation, 2 m temperature, 2 m dew point, surface pressure, precipitation after log1p of the value clipped at zero, and 10 m wind speed), and the standard deviation (ddof=0) of the same 7. The 7 means (with log1p precipitation) and the 7 standard deviations are z-scored with the training rows' mean and standard deviation and clipped at plus or minus 5. Each series reads the weather of the H3 resolution-5 cell that holds it.
    • Calendar and sun: 21 columns: solar zenith cosine, azimuth sine and cosine, the sine and cosine of the local hour at periods of 24 h and 12 h (Europe/London), a one-hot day of week, a COVID flag, three Christmas columns, and three bank-holiday columns.
    • Lead: the lead in hours divided by 336, and its square root.
    • Power lags: for each of a day lag and a week lag, the latest same-half-hour reading at least a minimum age before the network's origin, as a z-scored value, a missing flag, and an age code. The network's own origin is 09:00 UTC (the 00Z run plus 9 hours), and the lag cap counts back from that origin. The Candidate in the backtest keeps the stored cap of 24 hours, so the newest lag is the 09:00 reading of the day before the origin day.
    • Thermal-lag and solar-gain columns (14): trailing temperature means (3, 6, and 24 hours), temperature changes (3 and 6 hours), the day's minimum and maximum, the count of cold-snap days, trailing shortwave means (3, 6, and 24 hours), the 3-hour change in the clear-sky index, and two columns from the previous day's CAMS irradiance.
    • Neighbour and gap signals (60 columns, read only by the lag encoder): for each lag, the gap between the observed power and a lag-free forecast table (the median of the lags-masked network of the same seed at its freshest earlier origin with a lead of at most 24 hours), exponentially weighted means of that gap with half-lives of 1, 3, and 7 days, and, over the electrical neighbours of the Primary, the sum, mean, minimum, and maximum of those quantities scaled by capacity ratio, the own-plus-neighbour sum, a neighbour count, and a flag for no neighbour. The neighbours are the Primaries that NGED's "Primary Substation Interconnections" list links to the Primary. During fine-tuning, all signal columns of a random 50% of rows are set to no information (the "D50" dropout).
    • Series identity: an 8-dimensional embedding of the Primary.
    • Target: cleaned power divided by effective capacity, then z-scored per Primary.
  • Architecture of the Candidate. The weather encoder (7 means, an 8-wide embedding, and 14 thermal-lag and solar-gain columns, so 29 inputs) and the datetime encoder (21 columns and the embedding, 29 inputs) each map to 64 hidden GELU units and then 32 outputs. One shared lag encoder runs twice, on the day lag and then the week lag. Its 143 inputs are the lag's 3 columns, the 32-wide embeddings that the weather and datetime encoders give for the weather expected at the lag's own time, the 8-wide embedding of the Primary, an 8-wide embedding of the lag's identity, and the 60 signal columns; it maps to 64 and then 32, and the two outputs are concatenated. The mixer takes 145 inputs (the weather and datetime outputs of 32 each, the 64 lag outputs, the embedding, the 7 spread columns, and the 2 lead columns), has two hidden layers of 64 units, and outputs 9 numbers: the logits, means, and log standard deviations of a 3-component Gaussian mixture. Each hidden layer has 10% dropout.
  • Offset. A per-Primary piecewise-linear function of time with one knot for each month start from 2019-09 (a slow drift term) is added to the three component means. Fine-tuning trains only the newest knot, and a penalty of 10 times the mean squared difference between neighbouring knots keeps the function smooth.
  • Quantiles. The 11 quantiles come from the mixture's cumulative distribution by 40 bisection steps on a range of plus or minus 40 standard deviations. The mixture weights are a log-softmax and each standard deviation is exp of the raw output clamped to plus or minus 3. The values are then rescaled to power and sorted within the row. The final test of experiment 620 averaged 5 seeds quantile by quantile, sorted again, and widened the band about the median by a factor of 1.0934, which experiment 613 fixed before that test. The backtest averages 2 seeds and applies no widening.
  • Loss. The negative log-likelihood of the mixture on the standardised target, weighted, plus the knot penalty.
  • Training, in three steps.
    • Pre-training uses ERA5 and CAMS (shortwave) as stand-in weather, in pseudo-runs every 2 days from 2019-09-01 at 09:00 UTC with leads of 0.5 to 351 hours (about 8.1 million rows for the 2026-07 fold). Five Primaries start later (D11 2019-09-17, D10 2019-12-01, D5 2020-02-01, D14 2020-07-01, D16 2021-02-01). ERA5 has no ensemble, so the 7 spread columns hold the fold's median ensemble spread for each 24-hour lead band. All weights train: AdamW, learning rate 5e-4, weight decay 1e-3, batch 8,192, 20% of the rows per epoch, up to 60 epochs, patience 8, gradient-norm clip 1.0.
    • Step 2 loads the pre-trained weights except the mixer, draws a fresh mixer with seed 12345, freezes the weather and datetime encoders, and trains on the whole 730-day history with uniform weights and a 3-day embargo. Learning rate 2e-4, and 5e-4 for the fresh mixer.
    • The fine-tune starts from the step-2 weights with the same frozen encoders, learning rate 2e-4 throughout, and weights of 0.5 to the power of age in days over 90 (a 90-day half-life). The refit rule drops rows with valid times in the newest 7 days before the cut-off and halves the weight of rows 7 to 14 days old.
    • Early stopping holds out one week in every 12 weeks of origin days, with 15 days purged before and 9 days after each held week, and uses at most 200,000 held rows.
  • Missing and delayed inputs. A flagged or absent lag reads as value 0, a missing flag, and the maximum age code. In training, 30% of origin days mask both lags and, of those, 15% mask only the day lag. Absent signal columns read as 0 with a missing flag. Neighbour-signal columns whose training spread is under 80% of their spread in the last development month receive matching Gaussian noise during training. All weather columns must be finite.
  • Injected load shifts in training. Each Primary receives random synthetic shifts, added to the lag inputs only, until they cover 5% of its row span: depth 15%, 30%, or 50% of capacity, length 3, 7, 15, or 30 days, random sign. Each shift on a Primary is subtracted, scaled by the capacity ratio, from one electrical neighbour, so the neighbour summaries see the transfer.
  • R-haz, the prevailing head. Experiment 652 fitted it on top of the frozen K1 network of experiments 612 and 613, and the backtest puts it on the Candidate. It is a small network that reads 58 origin features (the gap and neighbour signals above, built from lags), 4 age columns (the log of the departure's age in days, the age over 30, the gate flag, and the age of the freshest lag), and 3 row inputs (the lead over 240 hours and the lower and upper half-widths of the Candidate's band). The gate flag is kept as a column and set to zero, so there are 65 such columns. The backtest head appends 28 more columns, the extra lagged power inputs described next, so it has 93 inputs. R-haz has two hidden layers of 64 ReLU units and 12 outputs: a signed depth (0.5 times the hyperbolic tangent of the first output, so up to half of capacity), a spread, and daily hazards. Each hazard is softplus(output - 3), and the survival probability p is the exponential of minus the hazards accumulated over the days before the lead. The probability is 0 when the departure is younger than half a day.
  • How the prevailing quantiles are formed. The Candidate's 11 quantiles define a piecewise-linear cumulative distribution with two tail knots 1.5 times the outer spacing beyond the 1% and 99% quantiles. The prevailing distribution is the mixture (1 - p) times the Candidate's distribution plus p times the Candidate's distribution shifted by the depth, with the depth uncertain at three Gauss-Hermite points. The 11 prevailing quantiles are read off that mixture and are monotone by construction. When p is 0, the prevailing rows equal the NRA rows.
  • Extra lagged power inputs of R-haz. The head reads 14 lagged inputs of the Primary's own cleaned power, each as a residual plus a missing flag (28 columns), appended after the 65 columns above. The inputs come from experiment 681. Every time below is measured back from the origin of the neural network (09:00 UTC), and every residual is the cleaned power minus the Candidate's lag-free median forecast for that time, as a fraction of capacity. The 14 inputs are the residuals at 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, and 72 hours; the means of the residuals over the last 6, 12, and 24 hours, each window ending 6 hours before the origin; and three differences between the means of four adjacent 24-hour windows, the newest window ending 6 hours before the origin: newest minus second newest, second minus third, and third minus fourth. A mean is missing when under half of its window holds a reading. The newest reading any input uses is 6 hours old, and a test perturbs every later half-hour and checks that no input moves. Each of the 12 monthly refits trains on the banks of earlier months only, and the lag inputs of an injected shift are built from the same shifted power as its target. 2025-11 and 2025-12 use the fallback head, which has no inputs to widen, so those two months carry no extra lagged inputs.
  • Loss and training of R-haz. The loss is the pinball loss over the 11 levels plus 0.05 times the binary cross-entropy of p against the observed state of an injected shift. The training rows mix real rows with injected shifts, with durations drawn half from 3 to 14 days and half from 28 to 112 days (an assumed mixture) and each injected shift counted equally. Adam, learning rate 0.003, weight decay 1e-4, batch 4096, up to 30 epochs, patience 4, 2 seeds averaged by mean quantile. The head of experiment 652 has 9,164 parameters (12 outputs) and no dropout. The backtest head has 14 daily hazards (16 outputs) and 93 inputs, which gives 11,216 parameters.
  • B-haz, the fallback prevailing head (2025-11 and 2025-12). B-haz fits a survival curve to the durations of the injected shifts. It multiplies that curve by the residual of the Candidate's day-ahead median over the days 2 to 8 before the origin, and adds the product to the normal-running quantiles. R-haz replaces it from 2026-01.
  • Training set of R-haz in the backtest. A "bank" is the set of injected-shift training rows built from one earlier test month. Each monthly fit of R-haz trains on the banks of all earlier months. Each fit samples 60,000 real rows and 6,000 bank rows. Origin days 0 to 17 of an injected shift train the head and origin days from 21 onward validate it.
  • Refits and embargo in the backtest. Twelve monthly refits (test months 2025-11 to 2026-10), each trained on data before the first of the month with the 7-day embargo of the refit rule. The ensemble history starts 2024-04-01, so the early folds fine-tune on less ensemble history than the later folds. The D15 and D18 rows before 2025-03-01 are cut, as in every recent experiment. The Candidate and R-haz each average 2 seeds.
  • Where each piece came from. The modular network and its widths: experiment 545. Frozen encoders and the three-step schedule: 559. ERA5 and CAMS pre-training: 418. The offset: 565 and
  • The thermal-lag columns: 437 and 569. The embargoed schedule: 574. The shared lag encoder: 586 and 591. The signal columns: 598 and 606. The signal dropout: 610. The refit rule: 599. The list of series and the width factor: 612 and 613. The prevailing head: 647, 650, and 652.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Both outputs beat the manual heuristic and climatology at every lead band, and the prevailing output scores better than the normal-running output overall but worse in the 7 days after the one verified load shift ends. Every number is a normalised error in points of capacity (percent of capacity; smaller is better) over all 16 Primaries, pooled. For the MVA-only Primaries the denominator is the capacity in MVA, so the numbers mix real and apparent power. Of the 3,924,480 rows of each output, 3,895,784 are scored: the rest have no observed power, the cleaning flagged the half-hour, or a baseline is missing. The manual heuristic and climatology are described under Comparison baselines. Gains are those of the output over the baseline, with a 95% day-block bootstrap interval from 2,000 resamples of origin days.

Over all rows, the CRPS is 4.31 for normal running and 4.09 for prevailing, and the normalised MAE of the median is 7.58 and 7.30. The experiment 667 page scores the prevailing head without the extra lagged inputs, so its prevailing numbers are higher (4.14 for CRPS and 7.39 for the normalised MAE); its normal-running numbers (4.32 and 7.59) agree with this page to within 0.01. This page scores the 3,895,784 half-hour rows that have cleaned observed power, and the 667 page scores the full ground truth.

From 2026-01 the prevailing output has a lower (better) CRPS than the normal-running output, by 0.17 points of capacity in 2026-01 to 2026-06 and by 0.42 in 2026-07 to 2026-10. The prevailing head has trained weights and the extra lagged inputs from 2026-01. The table splits the pooled scores by the months of the forecast origin. The months from 2026-07 form the final-test window, so no choice rests on them.

docs.title: The load shift at D5 and D16
docs.text:
The December 2025 transfer of load between D5 and D16 is the one verified load shift in the backtest year, and the prevailing output first moved at the first origin of January 2026, 61 hours (D5) and 52 hours (D16) after the step starts. The transfer is experiment 580's transfer 23: a fitted -1.47 MW at D5 and +1.37 MW at D16, 15 days from 2025-12-29. The step found in the observed power is at 2025-12-29 23:00 UTC and ends at 2026-01-14 11:30 UTC at D5, and starts at 2025-12-30 08:30 UTC and ends at 2026-01-14 19:30 UTC at D16. These times are the largest change of the 12-hour mean of the observed power within 3 days of the dates of experiment 580.

From the file, the first daily origin at which the mean of the prevailing median over the next 24 hours differs from the normal-running median by at least half of the fitted transfer is 61.0 hours after the start at D5 and 51.5 hours at D16. After the end, the first origin at which the two outputs agree to within half of the transfer again is 24.5 hours after the end at D5 and 40.5 hours at D16. Origins are daily, so each of these hours has a resolution of one day. This is one descriptive event at two Primaries, so it supports no general statement about the delay.

The prevailing output of December 2025 comes from the B-haz fallback head, and the end of the shift in January 2026 from R-haz, so the two ends of the event are forecast by different heads. Both step starts fall in December 2025, a fallback month, and the first origin with a trained head is 2026-01-01 12:00 UTC. The two start delays equal the gaps from the step starts to that origin (61 hours at D5 and 51.5 hours at D16), so they show no reaction speed. The fallback head has no inputs that could react to a step.

docs.title: BSPs and GSPs
docs.text: The two BSPs and two GSPs are forecast by the lag-enabled network of experiment 633, which is experiment 622's arm lagged_b1. The backtest is experiment 669. The network has no neighbour inputs and no model of load-shift events. Its readings are net of embedded generation, which no input models.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Inputs. The same 37 lag-free columns, 8 lag columns, knot position, expected-weather table for the lag encoder (the weather and calendar columns of the freshest run issued at or before the lag's own time, passed through the same encoders), and 14 thermal-lag and solar-gain columns as the Candidate network above, at the 4 series, with one embedding of the series (2 entries per group), and no signal columns and no neighbour inputs. The 51-member means and standard deviations are taken at the series' H3 resolution-5 cell.
  • Lags. The stored network read lags at least 24 hours old. The backtest retrains it with the 3.5-hour cap of experiment 572 (7 half-hours before the 09:00 origin), so the newest power is the 05:30 reading, 6.5 hours before the 12:00 origin.
  • Architecture. The same encoders and mixer as the Candidate with a lag encoder of 83 inputs (3 lag columns, the two 32-wide expected-weather and expected-datetime embeddings, and the embeddings of the series and the lag), and a mixer with 145 inputs. One network is fitted per group (the two BSPs together, the two GSPs together), so the weights are shared across the 2 series of a group except for the series embedding and the offset.
  • Offset, loss, and quantiles. The offset, loss, quantile bisection, and sorting are those of the Candidate, with no width factor.
  • Targets. Power divided by effective capacity (D13 55.3 MW, D17 47.6 MW, D6 384.3 MW, D1 170.9 MW), z-scored per series. The series are signed MW series.
  • Training. The same three steps as the Candidate (ERA5 and CAMS pre-training, a step 2 with a fresh mixer of seed 12345 and frozen encoders, and a fine-tune with a 90-day half-life), the same optimiser settings, and a 3-day embargo. Fine-tuning rows span 730 days before the cut-off, with targets ending 3.5 hours before it. Lag block dropout is 30% of days (both lags), of which 15% mask the day lag only. Two seeds are averaged quantile by quantile and sorted.
  • Origin. The network runs at its own origin of 09:00 UTC, the 00Z run plus 9 hours, and its output is relabelled with 12:00 UTC. Every input that the network reads at 09:00 was available at 12:00.
  • Refits. Twelve monthly refits, one per test month 2025-11 to 2026-10, with the 3-day embargo of the schedule. The final-test network of experiment 633 was one fit at 2026-07-01.
  • Where each piece came from. As for the Candidate; the node harness and pooling: 564 and 611; the lag network at the nodes: 619; the matched rematch: 622; the final test: 633.

Wind
docs.text: Wind farms are forecast by the simple network S of experiment 659. The backtest is experiment 666.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Inputs. The mean and standard deviation over the 51 members of 10 m and 100 m wind speed, the sine and cosine of the 100 m wind direction, and 2 m air temperature, plus the lead (the sine and cosine of the lead in hours modulo 24, and the lead in hundreds of hours) and a one-hot wind-farm column. There is no power lag, no calendar column, and no physics-lite input in network S.
  • Architecture. Two hidden layers of 64 units feeding a three-component Gaussian mixture over power as a fraction of capacity, centred on the training mean of the target. The 11 quantiles are read from the mixture and clamped to the range 0 to 1 of capacity. Inputs are standardised with the fit rows' mean and standard deviation.
  • Training. AdamW, learning rate 0.002, batch 2048, weight decay 0.0001, 40 epochs, and the epoch with the lowest negative log-likelihood on the last 62 days is kept. Idle readings (experiment 210's idle mask) are set to zero in training and scoring. Three seeds are averaged quantile by quantile.
  • Capacity. The 99.9th percentile of the farm's power over the 730 days before each refit.
  • Refits. Wind refits on day 0 of each month (12 refits), training on runs before 62 days earlier. No ERA5 or CAMS pre-training. Experiment 659 refitted twice a month.
  • Missing inputs. The network reads only the ensemble weather. The end date of the idle mask is read at run time, and the performance section states it.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: The network beats climatology at short leads and the margin shrinks with the lead time. All numbers are normalised error in points of capacity (percent of capacity; smaller is better), averaged over 709,776 half-hours with observed power (of 735,840 rows). The only baseline is climatology: the quantiles of the farm's own cleaned power in the same month, half-hour, and neighbouring cells, trained before the first day of the origin's month. No manual heuristic exists for wind farms, so none is shown. Gains are those of the network over climatology, with a 95% day-block bootstrap interval from 2,000 resamples of origin days. The observed power of half-hours inside experiment 210's idle mask, which ends in September of the backtest year, is set to zero, as it was when the network was fitted. Excluding those half-hours instead scores 655,288 half-hours (709,776 with the idle half-hours as zero), and the network's CRPS gain over climatology changes from 16.2% to 15.0%. The 26,064 rows with no observed power are not scored.

docs.title: Solar
docs.text: Solar farms are forecast by the simple network PLP of experiment 659. The backtest is experiment 666.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Inputs. The mean and standard deviation over the 51 members of shortwave radiation, air temperature, and 10 m wind speed; the ensemble means of relative humidity, longwave radiation, precipitation, and surface pressure; the sun's elevation and the sine and cosine of its azimuth; the lead; and the mean and standard deviation of a physics-lite power and of the cell temperature. There is no farm column and no calendar column.
  • Physics-lite power. Irradiance over 1000 W per square metre, times one minus 0.004 per kelvin times the cell temperature minus 25 degrees Celsius, clipped to the range 0 to 1, with the Faiman cell temperature T_air + G / (25 + 6.84 x wind speed). The formula runs on each of the 51 members separately, and the network reads the mean and standard deviation. The mixture is centred on the mean physics-lite power.
  • Architecture, loss, and optimiser. As for wind, with 20 epochs, the epoch with the lowest negative log-likelihood on the last 61 days kept, and a lead range extended to 336 hours (experiments 430 and 659 stopped at 251.5 hours). Solar has no idle mask, and the target is the raw output.
  • Night rows. The network forecasts only the half-hours where the mean cosine of the solar zenith angle over the ensemble step is above zero, and the network sets the quantiles of the other half-hours to 0. That gate is not the daylight rule that the scores use, which takes the zenith at the middle of the half-hour, so a coarse ensemble step that contains a sunrise or a sunset leaves small non-zero quantiles on the neighbouring night half-hours. The file is clamped afterwards (see "The files"): every quantile is 0 wherever the zenith at the middle of the half-hour is 90 degrees or more.
  • Refits. Quarterly: 2025-11-01, 2026-02-01, 2026-05-01, and 2026-08-01, each scoring the next three months, 3 seeds each, with no pre-training.
  • Capacity. As for wind.
  • Missing inputs. The network reads only the ensemble weather.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: The network beats climatology at short leads and the margin shrinks with the lead time. All numbers are normalised error in points of capacity (percent of capacity; smaller is better), averaged over 685,472 daylight half-hours with observed power (of 1,471,680 rows, which include night half-hours). The only baseline is climatology: the quantiles of the farm's own cleaned power in the same month, half-hour, and neighbouring cells, trained before the first day of the origin's month. No manual heuristic exists for solar farms, so none is shown. Gains are those of the network over climatology, with a 95% day-block bootstrap interval from 2,000 resamples of origin days. Only daylight half-hours are scored: those where the sun is above the horizon at the middle of the half-hour. 64,772 daylight half-hours have no observed power and are not scored, mostly in the warmer months (up to 14,010 in one month).

docs.title: Comparison baselines, slices, and summary figures
docs.text: The backtest outputs have lower error than the manual heuristic and climatology on the all-days row of every table in this section, and the comparison with research default 3 and BG2 is limited to stored rows. The section gives the baselines, the load-shift slices, the horizon and dot plots, and the comparison with two earlier forecasts.

docs.title: Baselines beside every model
docs.text:
• Manual heuristic. The median of the observed power at the valid time minus 1 to 6 weeks (168 to 1,008 hours) and minus 49 to 55 weeks, as in the production baseline code. A lag of h hours is used only if h is at least the lead plus 6 hours, because observed power reaches the forecaster only up to 6 hours before the origin. The 1-week lag therefore drops out beyond a lead of 162 hours, and the longer lags remain. The heuristic has the 11 quantiles of the same lags.
  • Climatology. The quantiles of the series' cleaned power in the same cell of the Europe/London month, half-hour, and weekend flag, pooled over the 9 neighbouring cells (months and half-hours), and trained on the power before the first day of the origin's month. For wind and solar the weekend flag is left out.
  • Not in the files. Both baselines are computed for the same origins and valid times and are not written into the Parquet files. Wind and solar have no manual heuristic.

docs.title: Load-shift slices of the Primaries
docs.text:
The set of load shifts that are longer than 7 days and 8 noise units or more is empty in the backtest year. The rule is the one of experiment 665: long means more than 7 days and deep means 8 noise units or more, a noise unit being a Primary's typical difference between successive 6-hour block means. The event source is the stored real event table of experiment 653, which covers 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30. It holds one such event, at D9 in January 2024, outside the backtest year. Because that set is empty, the page reports three further sets, each shown on its own and never mixed with another.

  • Event table, over 7 days, 2 noise units or more. The events of the same table that last more than 7 days at 2 noise units or more. This is a descriptive proxy for the empty set.
  • Verified transfer. The verified D5 and D16 transfer of experiment 580, 2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13.
  • Gate-on origin days. The origin days on which the G4 gate of experiment 592 is on, stored only for the fold months of that experiment that fall in the backtest year (December 2025, January 2026, March 2026, and June 2026), beside the gate-off origin days of the same months.

Each slice is scored on the subset of the 3,895,784 scored rows that fits it. A row is "inside" if its valid time falls within an event of its own Primary, "7 days after" if it falls in the 7 days after the end, and "outside" otherwise, for the same Primaries. docs.title: Error by horizon and by condition
docs.text:
The tables and dot plots use the code of studies.eval_protocol unchanged. The error measures are the normalised MAE of the median, the CRPS (twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 levels), and the twCRPS, which clips the observation and every quantile at a threshold, the 95th percentile of the series' power in the earlier months, before taking the quantile score. The conditions are those of slices.py: winter (December to February), winter nights (winter and the sun more than 5 degrees below the horizon), cold nights (the sun more than 5 degrees below the horizon and the ERA5 temperature at 3 degrees Celsius or below), Economy 7 step hours (local half-hours 1 to 6 of the day, starting 00:30 to 03:00, whatever the lead), Christmas (24 December to 1 January), bank holidays, and sunny half-hours (the unit solar shape at or above the series' own two-thirds quantile of daylight rows). Each lead band includes its lower edge and excludes its upper edge, so a day holds 48 half-hours. Units are points of capacity (percent of the Primary's effective capacity in MW, or in MVA for the MVA-only Primaries).

The manual heuristic and climatology in the comparison tables are the stored arms of experiment 87, not the baselines described above. Their means differ from the baselines of this page by at most 0.003 points (heuristic) and 0.13 points (climatology) on the common rows, but their per-row errors differ.

The comparison covers the common rows of the six forecasts: the backtest outputs, research default 3, BG2, the manual heuristic, and climatology. The stored forecasts of default 3 (experiment 378) and BG2 (experiment 87) have 09:00 UTC origins and end on 2026-06-30. Each is relabelled with the 12:00 UTC origin of the same day and a lead 3 hours shorter, and joined to the backtest on series and valid time. The common rows are the valid times from 2025-11-01 12:00 UTC to 2026-06-30 inside the protocol's rows, which exclude half-hours inside the hand-filtered load-shift events. The stored default 3 omits every fifth origin day, so the common rows hold about four fifths of the origin days. The protocol's holdout begins on 2026-07-01. Default 3 and BG2 are stored to 10 days and reach no further. Default 3 below 168 hours equals research default 1. The comparison has no BSPs or GSPs because neither forecast exists for them.

For the six Primaries that report signed real power (MW) the common rows hold 537,136 half-hours for the all-days row, and for the seven MVA-only Primaries 628,272. Of the 8 MW Primaries, 6 are in the comparison (D15 and D18 are not). Of the 8 MVA-only Primaries, 7 are in the comparison (D8 is not). The comparison does not score those three Primaries.
