docs.title: Why research default 3 can look better on another chart
docs.text:
Four differences between row sets can make research default 3 look better than the backtest outputs on an earlier chart: the season the rows cover, whether rows inside load-shift events are included, whether the chart covers 6 or 16 Primaries, and which lead gaps the stored forecast leaves. The tables above restrict every forecast to the same rows, so none of the four differences affects them. The gaps in the stored default 3 and BG2 are stated plainly here:

  • Every fifth origin day is missing.
  • The rows inside hand-filtered load-shift events are missing.
  • Nothing is stored after 2026-06-30.
  • The stored origins are at 09:00 UTC, so the comparison joins on valid time and subtracts 3 hours from the lead.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• A descriptive year, not a ranking. The year overlaps the development months and the final-test window. The origin months 2026-07 to 2026-10 lie inside the final-test window.
  • Less ensemble history early. The ensemble history starts 2024-04-01, so early folds train on less ensemble data.
  • Days 10 to 14 are reported separately. The files hold 14 days, and the scores for days 10 to 14 are in their own lead band, so a reader can discount them.
  • Solar's upper band fails on very sunny days. About 11% of observations exceed q99 on the sunniest days in experiment 659.
  • The shift labels are an incomplete dump. NGED has said that load-shift events may be missing from its logs, so clean rows can hold unlabelled shifts.
  • Default 3 and BG2 comparisons use stored rows only. Every fifth origin day is missing, the hand-filtered load-shift rows are missing, nothing is stored after 2026-06-30, and the 09:00 origins are joined on valid time with 3 hours subtracted from the lead. BSPs and GSPs have no such comparison.
  • The Primaries heads change in January 2026. 2025-11 and 2025-12 use the B-haz fallback head, and 2026-01 to 2026-10 use R-haz trained on all earlier months' banks. Only R-haz reads the extra lagged power inputs.
  • The prevailing output over-persists after a load shift ends. One verified load shift, at D5 and D16, is the only example, so the size of the effect is not estimated.
  • Quantiles exceed table capacity in the files. The highest quantile reaches 2.1 times the capacity table's value for D15 and 2.2 times for GSP D1 (observed maxima 1.28 and 1.34 times), 1.4 times for GSP D6, and 1.35 to 1.7 times for five more Primaries (D5, D12, D16, D18, and D22; observed maxima 1.2 to 1.55 times). Capacity is therefore not a ceiling for the demand series. The wind and solar files exceed it by up to 12%. The files keep the quantiles above capacity on purpose. Capping them at the larger of the table capacity and the highest cleaned power before the origin's month would change 2,604 rows of GSP D1, 4 rows of GSP D6, and no rows of D15.
  • The q05 to q95 band covers less than 90% of observations. Coverage is 81.4% for the Primaries in normal running and 85.1% for the prevailing output, 86.7% for the BSPs, 87.7% for the GSPs, 91.3% for wind, and 89.3% for solar on daylight half-hours.
  • The calibrated copies are post-processing, not part of the neural networks. The folder holds four calibrated copies beside the originals: the prevailing Primaries rows, the BSPs, the GSPs, and the solar file. Each scales the distance of every quantile from q50 by one factor per series, origin month, and lead band, fitted walk-forward on earlier power, so q50 is unchanged. The originals are the files as first written, with the clamps described above, and the scores on this page use the originals. D18 and D14 keep their 2026-06 factor from 2026-07, a rule chosen after seeing the final-test months, so the rule is post hoc. D18 stays at 63% to 77% coverage in 2026-07, 2026-08, and 2026-10 even in the calibrated copy, because a load transfer moves its power outside any band fitted on earlier months. The normal-running Primaries rows are not recalibrated, and wind has no calibrated copy.
  • The positive-output fix and the physical solar night gate are not applied to the files. Experiment 684 tested both as fixes inside the neural network, at four Primaries and two solar farms, and found them to be candidates to replace the clamps (experiment 684). The files carry the post hoc clamps instead: the quantiles of D12, D22, and D8 are clamped at zero, and the solar quantiles are zero at night. D5 and D18 are measured in MW and never go negative in the observed power, yet their lower quantiles go below zero in 703 and 6 rows, and the files keep those rows.
  • Band widths step at some refits. D4 narrows by about a third at the refit that starts May 2026; D18 widens by about half at the refit that starts September 2026; six Primaries widen by 1.2 to 1.5 times at the refit that starts February 2026.
  • Two Primaries miss for two months. The normal-running band of D18 and D14 covers about 22% to 28% of observations in July and August 2026, probably because of a load shift that normal running deliberately ignores; the cause has not been checked against the event table.
  • Numbers are provisional until the pages of experiments 667, 669, and 666 merge. Those pages own the models behind the files.
  • The last origins cannot be fully scored. Observed power ends on 2026-11-09 and the wind idle mask ends on 2026-09-13.

docs.title: Anonymisation
docs.text: Wind farms appear as Wind A to Wind C and solar farms as Solar A to Solar F, with no coordinates, no calendar dates on any generator's series, and no generator identifiers. Substations carry their names and dates.

docs.title: What does a one-year backtest of the lag-enabled demand network score at the 2 bulk supply points and the 2 grid supply points, with every power input at least 6 hours old and forecasts out to 14 days?
docs.text:
The lag-enabled network forecasts the 2 bulk supply points (BSPs) and 2 grid supply points (GSPs) at a CRPS of 7.4 points of capacity on day 0, and its error rises to about 10.5 by day 7 and stays near that to day 14. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, here in percent of effective capacity, so smaller is better. The BSPs score 4.3 (day 0) to 6.3 (days 7 to 14) and the GSPs 10.5 to 14.6. This is a descriptive backtest of 365 daily origins from 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31. It overlaps the development months and the held-out months of experiment 633, so no number here is a held-out score and nothing is ranked.

A bulk supply point is a substation that takes power from the transmission network. A grid supply point is a substation where the distribution network meets the transmission network. The 4 series are D13 Skegness and D17 Boston (BSPs) and D1 Bicker Fen and D6 Walpole (GSPs). Substations may be named, so the names stay.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1. CRPS rises over the first 7 forecast days and then flattens, in both groups. Forecast day n covers leads of (n - 1) x 24 to n x 24 hours.

Figure 2. CRPS by month: highest in November to March and in October, lowest in June to August.

In Figures 3 to 5, the blue line is the median, the dark band is the 50% interval, the light band is the 90% interval, and the red line is the observed power.

Figure 3. Day-ahead forecasts (first 24 hours of one forecast), one winter and one summer origin.

Figure 4. The full 14-day horizon of one forecast. The bands widen with lead time.

Figure 5. The largest observed demand of the year at each of the 4 series, with the forecast issued two days before the day (3 days shown). At Walpole (bottom panel), the observation sits about 100 MW below the median in the daytime of 2026-10-18. From about 01:00 to 21:00 on 2026-10-19 it holds between 300 and 497 MW, while the median falls to about 140 MW at midday and the 90% band lies below the observation for most of the daytime. This is a level step consistent with a load transfer, which is not confirmed in NGED's logs, and the network has no model of load shifts. At Bicker Fen, a plateau of 220 to 229 MW lasting about 6 hours sits above the 50% band. At Skegness (top), the median and the 90% band track the observed peak.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Network: experiment 633's lag-enabled network, which is experiment 622's arm lagged_b1: the pooled group-of-2 mixture density network of experiment 619, one network per group (BSPs, GSPs), with the D5 output offset of experiment 565, the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns of experiment 569, the shared lag encoder of experiment 591, frozen encoders in fine-tuning, and the three-step schedule of experiment 574 (arm P5). No neighbour inputs, no gate, and no model of load shifts. Two seeds, with the quantiles averaged and sorted within the row.
  • Pre-training and weather: the encoders pre-train on ERA5 and CAMS rows (experiment 564's matrices, which end on 2026-07-31, so the folds from 2026-08 share the same pre-training rows); the mixer and fine-tune use the 00Z ECMWF ENS run of each day (ensemble mean and spread) from 2024-04-01. The fine-tuning rows of each fold are given below.
  • Why 3.5-hour lags, not experiment 633's 24-hour lags: the stored network reads power at least 24 hours before its origin and needs no retraining to meet the contract, but the maintainer wants the fresher lags that a 6-hour power delay allows. This network uses experiment 572's 3.5h cap: the newest power is the 05:30 reading on the origin day, which is 6.5 hours before the 12:00 label.
  • Origin: the network runs at its own origin, 09:00 UTC (the 00Z run plus 9 hours). The file relabels it as 12:00 UTC and keeps valid times from 12:00 to 11:30 on day 14, so lead 0 is a forecast made 3 hours before the label, and lead bands count from the 12:00 label. Every input the network read at 09:00 was available at 12:00.
  • Training regime: 12 monthly refits (test months 2025-11 to 2026-10). Each trains on data before the first of the month with the recipe's 3-day embargo (the contract's 7 days does not apply to this recipe), forecasts every origin of the month, and may read in-month power only from 3.5 hours before the 09:00 origin. The early-stopping weeks of experiment 422 are purged by 9 days, shorter than the 14-day leads, so a held-out week's targets can sit in training rows of later origins (inside the training period).
  • Fine-tuning rows per fold (BSP group; GSP group 2% to 3% fewer): 570,000 (2025-11), rising to 735,000 (2026-10). The ENS history starts on 2024-04-01, so the 2025-11 fold has 19 months of it.
  • Leads and test rows: the training matrices hold leads of 0.5 to 351 hours, so the network needs no retraining for 14 days. The stored test matrices drop half-hours without an observed reading, so this experiment rebuilds them with experiment 633's code and no filter (e00669_testrows.py).
  • Weather at lag times: the thermal-lag and solar-gain columns of experiment 437 use, before the origin, the analysis proxy built from the first day of the previous 00Z run, which exists at forecast time. They never read ERA5 or power. ERA5 arrives about 5 days late, so the last roughly 5 days of the ERA5 and CAMS pre-training rows could not be read at a real cutoff; they are estimates of past weather from before the cutoff, so nothing from after the cutoff enters.
  • Set-ups reused (each restated above): the network and its schedule follow experiments 619, 565, 569, 591, 574, and 572; the pre-training matrices follow experiment 564 and the flagged-zero-actuals cleaning experiment 398.
  • Cleaning: flagged half-hours come from the cleaned power of experiment 398's flag file, which holds no flags for these series after 2025-09, so no half-hour is dropped in the test year; the scores skip the 7,680 of 981,120 half-hours with no observed reading.
  • Scoring: against observed power outside the file (the cleaned power), in points of capacity (effective capacity from series_table). CRPS is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 levels, so it is an approximation from 11 quantiles. Intervals are day-block bootstrap intervals (1,000 resamples) over origin days. No spread factor is applied.
  • Load shifts: the network assumes no load shifts, so a transfer between substations reads as a level change in its lags. NGED's event labels are incomplete and none were applied here.
  • Reviews: a Sonnet plan review (7 findings: 6 applied, 1 left), two Sonnet code reviews (2 and 4 findings: all applied), an Opus leakage review (5 findings; the 2026-07 BSP fold was refitted with the final code; a perturbation test found no leak), a Sonnet file audit (no contract violation; the scores reproduced within 0.03 points; a GPU re-run of the 2026-03 GSP fold matched the stored forecasts to 5e-6 of capacity), and an Opus review of the file and scores (8 findings, all applied to this page).
  • Compute: about 2 GPU-hours on one process, 1 core.
  • Standing practices: cleaned data, monthly refits, saved weights (.pt, in the data folder), and tail plots. The D15 and D18 cut does not apply.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• data/ml-experiments/backtest_year_2025-11_to_2026-10/bsps.parquet (D13 id 2, D17 id 1) and gsps.parquet (D1 id 28, D6 id 27), private. Each holds 490,560 rows (2 series x 365 origins x 672 half-hours): time_series_id (Int8), valid_time, nwp_init_time (the 00Z run), power_fcst_init_time (12:00 UTC), and the 11 quantiles q01 to q99 in MW (Float64). All 4 series are MW series.
  • The code is in ml-experiments/00669-one-year-backtest-of-the-lag-network-at-bulk-and-grid-supply-points/ (e00669_fit.py, e00669_fold.py, e00669_testrows.py, e00669_export.py, e00669_score.py, e00669_compare633.py, e00669_figures.py). The scores are in data/ml-experiments/00669-*/score/ and the fitted networks in data/ml-experiments/00669-*/work/{bsp,gsp}/models/.
  • Checks passed by the export: the row count equals 4 series x 365 x 672 in total, there is no duplicate key, no null or non-finite quantile, no crossing, the time zone is UTC, time_series_id fits Int8, and no lag index is newer than 05:30 on the origin day.
  • Reading the values: a negative quantile is net export. The q01 is below zero in 94% of the D6 rows and 99.6% of the D1 rows. Effective capacity is a normalising constant, not a limit: observed power reaches 1.34 times it at D1, and q99 sits above it in 33% of the D6 rows. The lead counted from the 12:00 label is 3 hours shorter than the true lead from the 09:00 forecast origin.
  • Unscored half-hours: 7,260 of the 7,680 half-hours with no observed reading are October origins past the last reading (2026-11-06). The remaining 420 are gaps inside the year.
  • Weather spot check: the weather columns at lag times were read from the analysis proxy of the previous 00Z run, never from data newer than the origin day's 00Z run.
  • Not reported: the curtailment cost against the manual heuristic, because neither BSPs nor GSPs have a manual heuristic baseline here. The 24-hour-lag network was not used for the file, since it would read power the production service already has at 3.5 hours.
  • Leakage caveats from the Opus review: the embargo of 9 days is shorter than the 14-day leads, and the Extras table is built with the grid end from before the redirect. Neither changed a result.
  • Scoring end and the hardest series: scoring stops where the cleaned observed power ends, about midday on 2026-11-08. D1 (id 28) is the hardest series: its median is 18 MW below the observed median overall, and its monthly mean error swings from -39.8 MW in 2025-11 to +25 MW in 2026-10.

docs.title: Does a search for the recipient of each donor step let the event table pair injected load transfers, split by how long the transfer lasts and how deep its step is?
docs.text:
A search at the neighbouring Primaries for the recipient of each large downward step lets the event table pair 0.29 of the injected transfer megawatts in the longest and deepest transfers, against 0.09 without the search, but not the 0.60 that adopting it required. A Primary substation steps electricity down to a local distribution network. A load shift moves part of the demand from one Primary (the donor) to a neighbour (the recipient), so the donor's power steps down and the recipient's steps up. The residual is the observed cleaned power minus a demand forecast that uses no lagged power. A noise unit is a Primary's typical difference between successive 6-hour block means, between 0.16 and 1.02 MW.

Experiment 653 built an event table (E1) of load shifts by splitting each Primary's residual into segments, and E1 paired few transfers. This experiment adds a search (E1-J). For each downward step of 4 noise units or more that E1 left unpaired, E1-J looks at each connected Primary for an upward step of 2 noise units or more that starts within a few hours of the donor, and accepts it when the steps conserve the donor's step. We scored both on 40 synthetic worlds from experiment 660's generator, in the six cells of event length and depth of experiment 665, and decoded the real record. The verdict is not supported: 1 of the 15 predictions held (the rewired graph), and the stop rule gives branch (b) by a narrow margin that leaving out one world or one Primary can reverse, so the result does not show that pairing is unidentifiable.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Cell. One of six groups of injected events: long is over 7 days (or no end), medium is over 1 day up to 7 days, short is 1 day or less; deep is 8 noise units or more, shallow is 2 to under 8.
  • Found, paired. An injected event is found when the method has an event at the right Primary and sign with a start within 12 hours. An end of an injected transfer is paired when the method links it to the right other end. Shares are weighted by absolute megawatts.
  • World. One copy of the real power panel with injected events; there are 40 default worlds. Intervals resample whole worlds.
  • E1-J rewired. The same method on a connection graph with the links rearranged at random (each Primary keeps its number of links). The rewired graph is the placebo.
  • Donor found. The share of injected edge-transfer megawatts at the donor end that E1 finds.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
The first figure shows that E1-J pairs about three times as much as E1 in every deep cell, that the rewired graph removes the gain, and that the search leaves the share found almost unchanged.

The second figure shows the verified D5 to D16 transfer: E1-J pairs the two Primaries in the right direction, but its starts are late, and E1 leaves both unpaired. The E1-J band at D16 shows two overlapping events: an unpaired +2.0 MW step that starts 5 days early and the paired +1.3 MW event.

The third figure shows that the real graph gives 8 transfers where 100 rewired graphs give 0 to 4.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Paired shares in the default worlds: E1-J adds 0.03 to 0.19 in every cell, and falls short of every prediction. MW-weighted, with 95% intervals; n is injected events and edge-transfer ends.

    Cell Events (ends) E1 paired E1-J paired Predicted E1-J minus E1 E1-J rewired Long, deep 220 (146) 0.09 (0.04 to 0.17) 0.29 (0.20 to 0.40) 0.60 +0.19 (0.12 to 0.29) 0.04 Medium, deep 127 (103) 0.07 (0.01 to 0.17) 0.25 (0.14 to 0.38) 0.50 +0.17 (0.09 to 0.28) 0.06 Long, shallow 840 (524) 0.08 (0.05 to 0.11) 0.19 (0.14 to 0.24) 0.30 +0.11 0.03 Medium, shallow 458 (347) 0.05 (0.01 to 0.09) 0.13 (0.09 to 0.18) 0.20 +0.09 0.01 Short, deep 163 (129) 0.01 (0.00 to 0.04) 0.08 (0.02 to 0.16) 0.20 +0.07 0.00 Short, shallow 561 (435) 0.00 0.03 (0.01 to 0.05) none +0.03 0.00

    No cell is too small to read. Differences are computed before rounding. - Found shares barely change, and all miss their predictions. E1-J finds 0.50 (0.44 to 0.57) in the long and deep cell (predicted 0.85) and 0.47 in the medium and deep cell (predicted 0.80); E1 finds 0.49 and 0.46. In the other cells E1-J finds 0.37, 0.35, 0.12, and 0.04, against predictions of 0.55, 0.45, 0.40, and 0.15. - Both ends pair less than they find, the donor end because of missed donors and the recipient end for untested reasons. In the long and deep cell E1 finds 0.44 of the donor megawatts, and E1-J pairs 0.36 of them (about four fifths of the donors found). At the recipient end E1-J finds 0.73 of the megawatts but pairs only 0.22, so the search loses about 70% of the recipient megawatts it finds. The medium and deep cell shows the same split (donors found 0.40 and paired 0.30, recipients found 0.58 and paired 0.19). Candidate causes are splits over more than 3 recipients, the start window, and the share bounds; none is tested here. Averaging the two ends gives the paired share of 0.29. - E1-J's decoded transfers are less often correct. In the default worlds E1 decodes 198 transfers, of which 113 (57%) match no injected end; E1-J decodes 788, of which 544 (69%) match none; E1-J on a rewired graph decodes 442. Correct pair ends per decoded transfer fall from 0.41 (81 of 198) to 0.28 (220 of 788). The 12 injected solo shifts that E1-J decodes as transfers (E1: 2) fall outside the paired share. Event-free time on the real record shows no false transfer, so these false transfers occur near injected events or in the injected worlds' extra structure. - Pairing is scored per end, not per mutual pair. In the long and deep cell, 10 of the 20 injected transfers with a correct recipient end have a donor end that is not correct, and E1 has 5 of 10. The donor test accepts a decoded partner list that covers at least half of the true recipients' megawatts, whatever else it holds. - The share varies a lot between Primaries. E1-J's long and deep paired share runs from 0 (D9, 7 ends) to about 0.8 (D4 and D16). Leaving out one world gives 0.26 to 0.31, and leaving out one Primary gives 0.26 to 0.31. - The sensitivity worlds agree. E1-J's long and deep paired share is 0.28 (0.19 to 0.39) in the 10 long-heavy worlds, 0.22 (0.06 to 0.55) in the 10 short-heavy worlds, and 0.28 (0.08 to 0.52) in the 10 constant-megawatt square worlds, all under 0.30. The medium and deep cell is too small in those worlds (13 to 30 ends). The donor-found share in the long and deep cell is 0.47, 0.24, and 0.46. - Timing is that of E1. In the long and deep cell E1-J starts within 2 hours for 0.49 of events (E1: 0.48) and ends within 6 hours for 0.44 (E1: 0.43), with median errors of 0.5 and 1.0 hours. - Real record: E1-J calls 8 transfers in 36.0 Primary-years, E1 calls 4, and the rewired graph gives a median of 2 (range 0 to 4). The rewired graphs keep 16% of the real links on average, so the placebo is not fully clean. None of the 8 transfers is in the long and deep or medium and deep cell: 5 are long and shallow, 1 is medium and shallow, and 2 are under 2 noise units. E1 and E1-J both call 246 and 247 events, 6.8 per Primary-year. - Real record: logged shifts matched are unchanged. Of the 77 logged shifts of more than 1 day, E1 matches 8 within 2 hours and 17 within 24 hours, and E1-J matches 8 and 18. For long and shallow shifts (7 logged) E1-J matches 1 and 5, E1 1 and 4. LR_b20 (the label-trained detector of experiment 254) matches 3 of those 7 within 2 hours, 6 of 7 medium and deep shifts, and 7 of 19 medium and shallow ones, from experiment 665. - Real record: event-free time gives no transfer. In the 27.6 Primary-years more than 14 days from any logged or verified event, all three methods call 148 events and none is a transfer. - Real record: E1-J pairs D5 and D16 in the right direction, but the prediction fails. E1-J decodes D5 as -1.08 MW and D16 as +1.28 MW. The starts are 24 and 12.5 hours after the verified starts and both ends are 24 hours late, against the 12 hours predicted. E1 leaves D5 unpaired and decodes D16 as an unpaired +2.05 MW step that starts 5 days early. - One of 15 predictions held. None of the 6 found predictions and none of the 5 paired predictions held, nor the two differences over E1 (+0.19 and +0.17 against +0.25) or the D5 and D16 prediction. The rewired-graph prediction held (a median of 2 against 8 edge events). - The stop rule gives branch (b) by point estimate, and the data cannot tell 0.286 from 0.30. E1-J's long and deep paired share is 0.286 (interval 0.20 to 0.40; about 39% of world resamples reach 0.30 or more), and the medium and deep share is 0.25 (0.14 to 0.38). Because both ends lose megawatts for reasons a better method could fix, the finding is not "pairing is unidentifiable at 15 Primaries". The decision for the next step, and whether to run the graph model (X2), is left to the maintainer. X2 was not started.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Not applicable: median minus mean forecast, tail calibration, curtailment cost, the normalised MAE of the median forecast, and the four scenarios, because no forecast is scored.
  • Reproduction gates passed. Gate 1: E1 on seeds 900 to 907 reproduces experiment 660's recall by size to three decimals in every bin. Gate 2: E1 calls 246 events in the scored years on the real record, as experiment 653 stored.
  • Audit triggers. Trigger 2 (a result contradicts its prediction) fired for 14 of 15 predictions. The donor-found share (0.44) caps the donor end; the recipient end's loss is untested. Trigger 7 (a later design, X2, rests on this result) fired, and the sensitivity worlds replicate the long and deep share (0.22 to 0.28). A fresh Sonnet agent audited the headline numbers (see Reviews and triage). Triggers 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 did not fire: E1-J contains E1 and never pairs less.
  • Unlogged events. NGED's event logs are an incomplete one-off dump, so clean rows may hold events no label covers, and matched counts are lower bounds.
  • Lab shortcuts. The injected events are added to the power and the residual uses a lag-free forecast that trained on every row, so earlier real events leak into the residual's baseline. The real record's noise units use the whole record (as in experiment 653); the injected worlds use the tuning years (as in experiment 660). A classifier that tells injected events from verified real ones scored 0.55 on experiment 660's generator (0.5 is chance); this experiment did not rerun it.

docs.title: Reviews and triage
docs.text:
• Plan and code review (Sonnet). The reviewer made 27 findings, 1 high: E1-J cannot find a donor that E1 missed. Accepted: reporting the donor-found share beside every cell, a false-pairing measure, the verdict and stop rule coded in the report, the gate against experiment 660 printed, the event-free stratum, the retained-links share of the rewired graph, and the clarifications in the plan. Not changed: the search window of -6 to +42 half-hours, which the plan states.
  • Second code review (Sonnet). The reviewer found no high bug. Accepted: skip a recipient already paired, take the nearest event to reuse, and draw 30 rewirings and keep the one with the fewest real links . Not changed: the 15-prediction count is tallied by hand, because two predictions are on the real record.
  • Results audit (Sonnet). The auditor re-derived every headline number from the stored files with its own code, and they agreed exactly, as did gate 1. It made 5 findings. Accepted and written into Results: the branch (b) result is not robust (leave-one-out 0.26 to 0.31); the donor cap explains only the donor end, and the recipient end loses half again; E1-J adds many false transfers (69% match no injected end); pairing is scored per end; Primaries differ widely. The take-home, headline, lessons, advice, and next-experiment sections were rewritten to match. Not changed: the donor test that accepts extra partners, which is experiment 653's rule and is kept for comparability.
  • Write-up and prose review (Sonnet). The reviewer made about 60 findings. Accepted: the inverted D5 and D16 delays, the recipient-loss figure (0.22 of 0.73 is a loss of about 70%), the scope of the rewiring, placebo, and event-free statements, the pronouns, the check wording, and the rounding note. Not changed: the hypothesis text, which stays as pre-registered, including its 0.18 (experiment 653's headline for events of 4 noise units or more lasting a day) and its window of 36 half-hours (the plan and Method give the window searched, -6 to +42 half-hours).

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The next experiment should find out why the search pairs only 0.22 of the 0.73 recipient megawatts it finds, and what raises the 0.44 donor share. In the long and deep cell the donor end pairs 0.36 of 0.44 found, and the recipient end 0.22 of 0.73 found. A graph model that decodes donors and recipients together (X2) could raise both, and its margin over E1-J has to be measured against these two ends and against the false transfers.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture and algorithm.

  • E1 is the default arm of experiment 653: the residual of the lag-free convex demand model of experiment 130, with the median across Primaries removed, a seasonal slow level per Primary fitted with candidate events masked, a Viterbi decoder (Viterbi, 1967) over 6-hour blocks with 25 states and a Student-t emission, and a pairing of events across neighbours by sign, start, end, and share. Its penalties are experiment 653's tuned values (onset and offset 6, stay 0.05).
  • E1-J keeps E1's events and, for each downward event of 4 noise units or more that E1 left unpaired, searches each connected Primary for the upward step of largest size that starts from 6 half-hours before to 42 half-hours after the donor's start. The step size is the median of the residual (slow level removed) after the start, for up to 3 days or the donor's end, minus the median over the 3 days before. A candidate needs 2 noise units, and at most 3 recipients are taken together when the share of the donor's step is 0.3 to 2.0 and the conservation cost is at most 2.5, with a loose conservation allowance of 0.5 of the donor's step. A recipient that E1 already decoded near the found start is reused; otherwise a new event is added with the donor's end.
  • E1-J rewired re-runs E1's own pairing and the search on a degree-preserving rewired graph (the draw with the fewest real links of 30).

Training regime.

  • Nothing is trained. The penalties are experiment 653's. The injected worlds come from experiment 660's generator in its default configuration (seeds 900 to 939) and in its long_heavy, short_heavy, and constant_mw_square configurations (seeds 1000 to 1009 each), injected into the power with the real start-time distribution of NGED's logged shifts. The residual panel is experiment 653's (from 2022), not the 2019-onward panel, which would help only a trained model. It ran on 2 CPU cores in about 6 seconds per world, with no GPU.

Measurement.

  • Rows and cells are experiment 665's: injected events of 2 noise units or more of kind edge, solo, permanent_transfer, or permanent_shift, in the scored years 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30, found and paired as defined above, weighted by absolute megawatts. Intervals are 2000 resamples of whole worlds; the difference E1-J minus E1 is resampled on the same draws.
  • Real record. Events are the table's events in the scored years, with cells from stored size. Logged shifts are the 77 of more than 1 day in experiment 580's labels, matched within 2 hours or 24 hours, with panel depth as in experiment 665. The event-free time lies more than 14 days from any logged or verified event. The standing practices hold: clean data, D18 cut before 2025-03-01, and no row from 2026-07-01 onward.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00670-event-table-recipient-search-on-six-cell-grid/e00670_search.py: E1-J's recipient search (search_recipients).

docs.title: Does the fold model lose recovery with a fair denominator, and which probe should be trusted at D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21?
docs.text:
Converting a flow to apparent power costs the linear probe recovery even where the flow never nears zero, and the fold model's extra capacity at D3 and D4 comes from its free reactive terms, not from a folded curve. The fair-denominator test A1' fails for all three probes (decision-rule branch 3: quantify the loss). Fixing the two reactive terms of the fold model at zero returns the linear probe's capacity at D2, D3, D4, and D19 to within 0.5 MW. For D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21 we recommend the linear probe, scaled by the recovery measured on injected farms, with the fold model's free-reactive reading as an upper bound. Both parts re-use experiment 662's stored networks (2026-06 cutoff, 5 seeds) and its probe outputs; no network was trained.

Figure: L0 sits near 0.9 only at 0.5 times, L1 also at 1 times, and the fold model scatters around 1. Each dot is one Primary at one level. D5 and D10 sit past the fold in every injected world (2.0 MW floor), so their ratios are shown apart.

Figure: every curve is monotone falling or flat, not V-shaped. D3 and D4 are nearly flat (under 2 MVA across the range of u), and the three fits lie on top of each other in this cell. The disagreement between the probes therefore comes from the fits across cells, not from the curve class in one cell.

docs.title: Part 1: A1' at the six MW Primaries (median over seeds, first farm rotation)
docs.text:
Terms: L0 is the linear probe, L1 the linear probe on rows above the reactive floor, and FA the fold model with a night prior (all as in experiment 662). "PF" is the apparent-power world with power factor 0.97. A ratio is valid where the signed-world denominator is at least 0.05.

  • Bar. 0.90 to 1.10 at 5 of 6. It passes for no probe at any level. Valid ratios in the bar: L0 2, 0, 0; L1 2, 2, 0; FA 3, 2, 2 of 6 at 0.5, 1, 2 times.
  • Loss in points of recovery (PF minus signed L0), D9, D11, D14, D16.
Probe 0.5 times 1 times 2 times L0 -5 to -12 -22 to -25 -75 to -94 L1 -6 to -12 -2 to -9 -78 to -95 FA -6 to +10 -4 to +18 +1 to +13
  • Pre-registered predictions. The plan predicted that A1' passes for L0 and L1 at 0.5 times and for FA at 0.5 and 1 times. All three failed (L0 2 of 6, L1 2 of 6, FA 3 and 2 of 6), so the first hypothesis (no loss where the floor does not apply) is refuted for L0 and L1 and not supported for FA. The prediction for Part 2 (curves not V-shaped; most of the extra capacity gone with the reactive terms fixed) held.
  • Deviation. The plan said median over seeds and both farm rotations; only the first rotation is used, because the signed arm has no second rotation.
  • Signed-world L0 denominators are 0.73 to 0.82 at all six Primaries and levels.
  • D5 and D10 (2.0 MW at every level, past the fold): L0 and L1 lose 79 to 115 points; FA loses 53 to 57 points at D5 and 6 to 12 points at D10.
  • Bias reading (FA over signed L0). FA's ratio is 0.85 to 1.22 at D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 and 0.30 to 0.33 at D5. FA therefore recovers about as much of the signed-world capacity as the linear probe does in the signed world, except at D5, and overshoots by up to 22% at D11 and D16.
  • Reading against the decision rule. Neither FA nor L0 passes, so the apparent-power conversion costs recovery even where the floor does not apply. The cost is 5 to 12 points for the linear probe at 0.5 times and 22 to 25 points at 1 times.

docs.title: Part 2: D2, D3, D4, D19, D21 (and D5, D10)
docs.text:
Terms: a "twin" is the network trained on the real data with no injected farm. "q = 0" fixes both reactive terms of FA at zero; "q1 = 0.25" fixes the reactive share at the power-factor 0.97 value. The midday reading is the median flow on sunny half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 UTC, April to August. The "A2 rows" are experiment 662's recoveries in native apparent-power worlds.

Primary Midday reading (MW) L0 (MW) FA free (MW) FA, q = 0 FA, q1 = 0.25 Share of FA's extra gone with q = 0 D2 8.84 5.20 7.95 (7.4 to 8.2) 5.70 6.05 82% D3 6.62 2.06 4.44 (2.7 to 4.7) 2.26 2.37 91% D4 7.09 0.98 3.09 (1.1 to 4.0) 1.10 1.15 94% D19 2.56 1.13 2.13 (1.3 to 2.4) 1.28 1.36 85% D21 2.94 1.13 1.35 (1.2 to 1.8) 1.26 1.32 42%
  • Real twins, raw capacity, median over 5 seeds (min to max for the free fold fit).
  • Reactive floor of the free fit. The free fit's q0 is 3.3 to 5.7 MW at D2, 2.1 to 5.1 MW at D3, and 0 or 3.5 to 3.8 MW at D4, where two of five seeds find no floor and read 1.1 MW.
  • Known-answer recoveries in native PF worlds (experiment 662, A2 rows). The linear probe recovers 0.63 to 0.82 at 0.5 times and 0.51 to 0.64 at 1 times, and is negative at 2 times (-0.10 to -0.19). The fold model recovers 0.49 to 0.97 at 0.5 times, 0.54 to 0.91 at 1 times, and 0.73 to 0.92 at 2 times. The calibrated linear capacities are 0.2 to 0.5 times the midday reading at D3 and D4, where the linear probe recovers 0.74 to 0.82 at 0.5 times, and about 0.5 to 0.9 times it at D2, D19, and D21, where the linear recovery falls to 0.51 to 0.63 at 1 times.
  • Known answer at D5 and D10 (injected 2.0 MW, past the fold). Recovery per probe: L0 -0.34 and -0.03; FA free 0.24 and 0.65; FA with q = 0 1.16 and 0.00; FA with q1 = 0.25 0.01 and 1.07. No probe reads both correctly, so past the fold the reactive-term setting decides the answer.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Capacity ranges divide the raw linear capacity by the native-world 0.5-times recoveries (0.63 to 0.82) of experiment 662; the "upper bound" divides the free fold fit by 0.71, the median recovery of the fold model at 1 times at the six MW Primaries (a different level from the linear divisor, because the fold model's 0.5-times recovery at D3, D4, and D19 is lower). Both assume power factor 0.97.

Primary Probe to use Capacity range (MW) Upper bound, free fold (MW) Confidence D2 L0 6.3 to 8.3 11.2 provisional D3 L0 2.5 to 3.3 6.2 provisional D4 L0 1.2 to 1.6 4.3 provisional D19 L0 1.4 to 1.8 3.0 provisional D21 L0 (the fold model's median is 0.2 MW higher) 1.4 to 1.8 1.9 provisional D5, D10 none not defined not defined report-only
  • Why L0 for D3, D4, and D19. Fixing the reactive terms at zero or at the power-factor value returns the linear capacity, so the extra 1.0 to 2.4 MW of the free fold fit at D3, D4, and D19 is a reactive-term effect that the injected farms give no sign of supporting. The fold model recovers less than the linear probe at 0.5 times at D3, D4, and D19 (0.68, 0.55, 0.49 against 0.82, 0.74, 0.63).
  • What stays open. The injection tests difference a twin against a fleet, so they cannot show whether the twin's own absolute read of 3 to 4 MW is true. A real reactive floor of 3 to 5 MW at D3 and D4 would also produce the free fit's answer.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• One cutoff (2026-06) and one network architecture; the 2026-03 networks are not re-probed.
  • The reactive power of the real meters is unknown, and power factor 0.97 is an assumption.
  • D5 and D10 have midday readings near 1 MW, so a 2.0 MW floor puts them past the fold at every level.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the clean rows may hold unlabelled events.
  • The S(u) lines use one cell and seed 0; the linear line omits the temperature term.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Forecast checks: the experiment scores no forecast, so the median-minus-mean and quantile-score checks do not apply.
  • Code review (Sonnet): no wrong-number bugs. It asked for the plan to say that the first farm rotation only is used (done) and noted that the temperature term is omitted from the plotted linear line (stated).
  • Compute: CPU only, 2 processes; Part 2 took about 15 minutes.
  • Reproduce: e00671_a1.py, then e00671_part2.py (twice, for the twin and the injected networks), then e00671_report.py, in this experiment's folder.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Does a reactive floor of 3 to 5 MW exist at D3 and D4? A test needs the real meters' active and reactive power, which the meters may record.

docs.title: Does a graph neural network find the donor of an injected load transfer, and pair it with its recipients, better than experiment 670's search at connected Primaries?
docs.text: A graph neural network trained on injected transfers pairs far less than the search of experiment 670, and it does not find donors better, so the graph line is closed at 15 Primaries. The graph neural network (G) pairs 0.08 of the injected transfer megawatts in the long and deep cell, against 0.29 for E1-J (difference -0.20, 95% interval -0.33 to -0.09), and 0.04 in the medium and deep cell, against 0.25. G finds 0.47 of the long and deep donor megawatts, against 0.44 for E1-J, a gain of +0.03 (interval -0.16 to +0.23) where +0.10 was predicted. The verdict is not supported: the pairing margin of +0.10 failed in both deep cells, so stop rule (a) fires. Stop rules (b) and (c) did not fire: the cross-injector drop was 0.03 on the same-test-world reading, and G-R decoded no real edge events.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• G, G-R, G-0, GS. The graph network on the real connection graph; the same network trained and run on a rewired graph; the same network with no links; and G with the explicit solar term added to the residual at the six Primaries metered in megawatts.
  • Cell. One of six groups of injected events by length (long: over 7 days or no end; medium: over 1 up to 7 days; short: up to 1 day) and depth (deep: 8 noise units or more; shallow: 2 up to 8).
  • Donor, recipient, found, paired. As in the plan below and in experiment 670. Donor found is the share of the megawatts of injected donor steps (edge transfers with a metered recipient) that the decoded table finds.
  • E1-J. The event table of experiment 653 plus the recipient search of experiment 670, read from that experiment's stored rows for the same 40 worlds.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
The first figure shows that G pairs less than E1-J in every cell, and that G finds donors about as often as E1-J in the long and deep cell only.

The second figure shows that G finds fewer injected events than E1-J in every cell, and that the links add 0.03 to 0.08 of found share over the no-link arm in the four cells of 1 day or longer.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Pairing. MW-weighted, default worlds (40 worlds), mean of three networks for G, with the world-resampled 95% interval of the difference from E1-J.

    Cell Injected events (edge-transfer ends) E1-J paired G paired G minus E1-J Long, deep 220 (146) 0.29 0.08 -0.20 (-0.33 to -0.09) Medium, deep 127 (103) 0.25 0.04 -0.21 (-0.34 to -0.09) Long, shallow 840 (524) 0.19 0.04 -0.15 (-0.20 to -0.10) Medium, shallow 458 (347) 0.13 0.01 -0.12 (-0.17 to -0.07) Short, deep 163 (129) 0.08 0.00 -0.08 (-0.15 to -0.02) Short, shallow 561 (435) 0.03 0.00 -0.03 (-0.05 to -0.01)

  • Donor end and recipient end, long and deep cell. E1-J finds 0.44 and pairs 0.36 of the donor megawatts, and finds 0.73 and pairs 0.22 of the recipient megawatts. G finds 0.47 and pairs 0.09 of the donor megawatts, and finds 0.55 and pairs 0.08 of the recipient megawatts. The graph neural network finds donors and then fails to link them.

  • Found share. G minus E1-J is -0.05 (-0.14 to +0.03) in the long and deep cell, -0.10 (-0.25 to +0.03) in the medium and deep cell, and -0.10, -0.17, -0.11, and -0.04 in the other four cells, each below its predicted margin. G minus the no-link arm G-0 is +0.06 (-0.03 to +0.15) and +0.08 (-0.03 to +0.19) in the long and deep and the medium and deep cells.
  • Timing. Of the found events in the long and deep cell, 88% start within 2 hours and 75% end within 6 hours of the truth (medium and deep: 94% and 88%), so P5 holds.
  • False transfers. G decodes 86 transfers in 40 worlds, of which 46 match no injected end (E1-J: 788 and 568). G pairs conservatively and still pairs little.
  • Placebo and no-link arms. G-R and G-0 pair 0.00 of the megawatts in every cell, by construction for G-0 and because the injected transfers use the real graph for G-R. G-R found shares are 0.41 (long and deep) and 0.29 (medium and deep).
  • Cross-injector test (one network per injector, 10 worlds each). Found share in the long and deep and medium and deep cells together: a network trained on constant-megawatt square steps finds 0.42 on those worlds and 0.35 on shaped transfers; a network trained on shaped transfers finds 0.32 on shaped transfers and 0.38 on constant-megawatt worlds. The drop is read on the same test worlds, as the network trained on that injector minus the network trained on the other: 0.416 minus 0.384 = +0.03 on constant-megawatt worlds, and 0.320 minus 0.352 = -0.03 on shaped worlds. Read per network instead (each network's own injector minus the other injector's worlds), the drops are +0.06 and -0.06, and stop rule (b) would also fire. Each reading rests on 10 worlds and a handful of deep events, so P9 is not a firm result.
  • Real record, 15 Primaries, scored years (36.0 Primary-years). G calls 0.75 to 0.97 events per Primary-year (E1: 6.83) and 2 to 4 edge events, none in the long and deep or the medium and deep cell (E1-J: 8, none in those cells). G-R calls 0 edge events, and G-0 calls none. G locates a D5 step of -1.08 MW 24 hours after the verified start and a D16 step of +2.1 MW 9.5 hours after it (62 hours before it in one network), in all three networks, and links neither. The D5 step is below the 1.2 MW bar of P6, and both starts miss P6's 6-hour bar. G matches 5 to 6 of 77 logged shifts of more than 1 day with the start within 2 hours (E1: 8).
  • Explicit solar term. GS minus G is -0.02 and -0.01 in found share, +0.04 and 0.00 in donor-found share, and 0.00 in paired share in the long and deep and the medium and deep cells, with found and donor-found intervals of +-0.1 or more. Experiment 657 found the same inside E1.
  • Post hoc wider decoder grid (arm Gw). The tuned none-boost of G sat at the edge of its grid (10), the decoder weight that raises the cost of calling no event, so the three G networks were re-tuned with boosts from 3 to 1000. The long and deep cell then gave found 0.48, donor found 0.52, and paired 0.10 (G: 0.45, 0.47, 0.08), and the real record gave 0.14 to 0.64 events per Primary-year. The verdict does not change.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (pairing margin +0.10): failed in the long and deep, medium and deep, and long and shallow cells, and the margins of +0.05 failed in the medium and shallow and the short and deep cells.
  • P2 (donor-found margin +0.10 over E1-J): failed. +0.03 in the long and deep cell and -0.06 in the medium and deep cell.
  • P3 (found margins and absolute paired shares): failed in all six cells.
  • P4 (G minus G-0): failed. +0.03 and +0.04 in the long and shallow and medium and shallow cells (needed +0.05), and +0.06 in the long and deep cell (needed within 0.03).
  • P5 (timing): held in both deep cells.
  • P6 (verified D5 and D16 pair): failed on pairing, on start timing, and on the size of the D5 step.
  • P7 (G-R at most a third of G's real edge events in the two deep cells): unreadable. G has no real edge events in those cells.
  • P8 (events per Primary-year within a factor of 2 of E1's): failed. 0.75 to 0.97 against 6.83.
  • P9 (cross-injector drop at most 0.05): held on the same-test-world reading (0.03), failed on the per-network reading (0.06); one network per injector.
  • P10 (GS within 0.03 of G): failed in donor-found share in the long and deep cell (GS is 0.04 higher, interval about +-0.2), and held in the other measures and cell.
  • Reproduction gate: held by reading, not re-scoring. The E1-J rows are experiment 670's stored rows on the same worlds, and they match that page's headline cells (0.29 and 0.25 paired).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site and the mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast. Not applicable: no forecast is scored.
  • Audit triggers. None fired: the result is a clear failure of every pairing prediction against a stored benchmark, and the post hoc arm left the verdict unchanged.
  • Caveats. NGED's logs are an incomplete one-off dump, so matched logged shifts are lower bounds. One network trained per injector, three per arm, 120 training worlds, and 2,400 steps; a larger network, more worlds, or 1-hour blocks might pair more, and this experiment does not test them. The explicit solar term carries a capacity table fitted partly inside the scored window.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• The pre-registered stop rule closes the graph line at 15 Primaries, and X3 (history length) is not started because the stop rule fired. Whether to reopen the graph line, and which event table to use, is for the roadmap.
  • Reduce the false transfers of E1-J (72% of its decoded transfers match no injected end in this experiment's tally; experiment 670's page gave 69%) before any further pairing method is built.

docs.title: The plan as committed
docs.text: The plan below was committed before any network was trained.

docs.title: The question
docs.text: Experiment 670 gave the event table of experiment 653 a search at connected Primaries for the recipient of each donor step. That event table (E1-J) paired 0.29 of the injected megawatts in the long and deep cell, against 0.09 without the search. Two losses limit it: E1 finds only 0.44 of the donor megawatts (E1-J pairs 0.36), and the search pairs only 0.22 of the recipient megawatts although it finds 0.73. E1-J also decodes false transfers (69% of its decoded transfers match no injected end, against 57% for E1). This experiment asks whether a graph neural network, trained to find the donor and reading the recipient evidence at the linked Primaries, improves both ends, by at least 0.10 of paired megawatts over E1-J.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• G. The donor-finding network on the real connection graph (below).
  • G-R. The same network trained and run on a degree-preserving rewired graph, the placebo (one rewiring per seed, the draw, out of 300, that keeps the fewest real links, because experiment 670's best of 30 kept 16% of the real links; the share kept is reported).
  • G-0. The same network with no links and no neighbour layer: each Primary sees only itself.
  • GS. G with the explicit solar term added to the residual at the six Primaries metered in megawatts: known weather from CAMS and ERA5, and the capacity table of experiment 649, built by experiment 657. Experiment 657 tested this term inside E1 and found that it left the residual and the recall unchanged; GS repeats the test inside the network. The capacity table's 2026-06 cut-off and the gain fitted on 2022 and 2023 sit partly inside the scored years, as in experiment 657, so a gain would be an upper bound.
  • Reference rows. E1-J and E1 from experiment 670's stored scored rows on the same worlds.

Each arm trains 3 seeds, on the default generator configuration. Two further networks, each one seed, give the cross-injector test: G trained on the constant_mw_square configuration of experiment 660 and G trained on its shaped_transfers configuration. Each is scored on 10 worlds (seeds 1000 to 1009) of both configurations, so the test reads in-injector minus cross-injector found share in both directions. P9 is a one-seed reading.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Network. Experiment 658's recurrent encoder, shared by the 15 Primaries, a neighbour-mean layer, and a link head, on the 6-hour block grid of experiment 653. A donor head is added: per Primary, the chance that the Primary is the donor of a transfer with a metered recipient. The link head also reads the two Primaries' donor logits, so the recipient state is conditioned on the donor. The loss is experiment 658's plus a weighted cross-entropy on the donor flag (donor blocks weigh 5, about 2% of blocks). The graph specification's loss table is not used: 658's loss is the one already shown to train on these worlds.
  • Decoder. Experiment 658's Viterbi decode and link pairing, with one addition: the decoder moves lambda times the donor probability of each block's 'none' mass to 'shift, down' (lambda 0 is the ablation of the donor head's role in decoding; 1 is the donor-aware decode, chosen on validation worlds from {0, 1}).
  • Resolution. Blocks are 6 hours, as in experiment 658, not the 1-hour blocks the specification estimated would take about 10 times as long to train; boundaries are refined to the half-hour by experiment 653's refinement. If the timing prediction (P5) fails for this reason, the write-up says so.
  • Ends reported separately. As experiment 670's advice asks, every cell reports the donor end and the recipient end separately (found and paired), and the false transfers (decoded transfers that match no injected end) beside recall.
  • Donor recall. The share of the megawatts of injected donor events (negative step, an edge transfer with a metered recipient, 4 noise units or more) that the decoded table finds, by the matching rule of experiment 653, reported beside pairing for every cell.
  • Panel. Experiment 653's panel from 2022 (no 2019-onward panel exists on disk, and a fetch is outside this experiment's scope); the history-length question belongs to X3.
  • Real record. As in experiment 670: events per Primary-year, logged shifts matched, edge events per cell, the verified D5 and D16 transfer, and the event-free stratum, for G, G-R, G-0, and GS.
  • Compute. 14 networks of about 2,400 steps each. One network is timed first. One network took 70 seconds, so all 14 networks ran 2,400 steps. Decoder tuning and scoring run on CPU while the GPU trains the next network, and the ceiling of 8 GPU-hours counts training time only. One GPU process at a time, at most 4 CPU cores, MemoryMax=16G per script. The one-year backtests hold priority: a fit pauses when a backtest worker needs the GPU.
  • Definitions. A cell is one of six groups of injected events by length (long over 7 days or no end, medium over 1 up to 7 days, short up to 1 day) and depth (deep 8 noise units or more, shallow 2 up to 8). An event is found when the decoded table has an event at the right Primary and sign starting within 12 hours; an end is paired when the decoded table links it to the right other end; an edge event is a decoded transfer. Shares are weighted by absolute megawatts.
  • Inherited leaks, stated. The noise units (experiment 653's, fitted before 2024-01-01) saw the validation months, and the injected start hours and weekdays come from NGED's logged onsets up to 2026-07, so the scored window has shaped both. Both are shared with experiment 670, so the contrast with E1-J is unaffected. The GS arm also carries the capacity table (cut-off 2026-06) and a gain fitted before 2024-01-01, so a GS gain would be an upper bound.
  • Caveat. NGED's logs are an incomplete one-off dump, so matched logged shifts are lower bounds.

docs.title: Reviews
docs.text: A Sonnet plan review and a Sonnet code review ran before the first fit and are triaged in the pull request. A Sonnet write-up review and a Sonnet prose review ran on the finished page and are triaged in the pull request.

docs.title: Unmetered solar capacity per Primary, beside what three registers list
docs.text:
At 8 of the 12 Primaries that have a probe interval, the probe's capacity lies above the solar capacity that three registers list. A Primary is a primary substation of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), which steps 33 kV down to 11 kV, and the project labels each one D followed by a number. The probe is a trained demand-forecasting neural network, asked how much a Primary's net demand falls for a given amount of sunshine. Its capacity is in MW of alternating current (AC) for unmetered solar only, so it excludes every generator that NGED meters. The three registers are the Feed-in Tariff, the Embedded Capacity Register, and the Renewable Energy Planning Database. The register floor is the capacity they list inside the Primary's service area, with the sites that NGED meters removed. D2, D3, D5, and D21 lie below theirs.

The probe reads 2.4 to 3.9 MW at each of the six Primaries metered in megawatts (MW), and 1.25 to 6.62 MW at the five main Primaries metered in megavolt-amperes (MVA). The five main MVA Primaries (D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21) are those whose flow never comes near zero on a sunny midday. A reading "folds" where solar output exceeds demand, because an apparent-power meter cannot tell exporting from importing. A twelfth Primary, D12, has a fold-model reading only. D8 and D22 are reported but not compared with the floor. The MVA figures assume that NGED's meters read power factor 1 with a small reactive floor. Under that assumption experiment 679 measures a conversion loss of 0.5 points (80% interval -1.0 to 7.7), and the upper end does not rule out a loss of 7.7 points. Every figure is a whole-summer value, so none shows how capacity grew from month to month.

The hypothesis, that the probe's 90th percentile is at or above the floor at every Primary, fails at D2, D3, D5, and D21. The verdict "supported" follows the decision rule fixed before any total was computed, which reads only the six MW Primaries (5 of 6). The count falls to 5 of 12 if the Feed-in Tariff band of 50 kW to 1 MW is added to the floor.

Every probe number on this page is a stored row of experiments 649, 662, and 671, and this page trains no new neural network.

Figure 1. At 8 of the 12 Primaries with a probe interval, the bar (probe, 10th to 90th percentile) lies right of the black tick (register floor). The eight are D4, D9, D10, D11, D12, D14, D16, and D19. The bars of D2, D3, D5, and D21 lie left of their ticks. D8 and D22 are report-only (grey) and are not among the 12. The floor is the lower bound defined in the register section, with metered sites removed.

docs.title: The six Primaries metered in MW: D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16
docs.text:
The six MW Primaries need no apparent-power conversion, so the probe's calibration was measured directly on their own flow. The table is experiment 649's calibrated capacity for April to September 2025 at the 2026-06 pretraining cutoff (10th, 50th, and 90th percentile, MW). The raw value is the probe's reading, and the calibrated value divides it by 0.679, the share of an added real solar farm that the probe finds again.

docs.title: The five MVA Primaries that do not fold: D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21
docs.text:
At D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21, the main figure is the linear probe calibrated by the signed-world recovery of 0.79. The fold model's figure is an upper bound. The linear probe is experiment 662's L0 and the fold model is its FA, both at the 2026-06 cutoff. The signed-world recovery is experiment 662's recovery of an added farm at 0.5 times the midday reading, measured on the six MW Primaries with no apparent-power conversion (median 0.79). Dividing by the signed-world recovery assumes that NGED's meters read power factor 1 with a small always-present reactive floor. Experiment 679 measured the conversion loss of the linear probe at 0.5 times under that assumption: 0.5 points (80% interval -1.0 to 7.7), against 10.7 points when the six MW Primaries are converted with a reactive part of 0.25 times the median real power (power factor 0.97, the "PF arm"). The upper end of the interval does not rule out a loss of 7.7 points, and the loss may lie in the 5-to-12-point range that experiment 671 reported for the PF arm. Experiment 671 recommends the same probe and marks all five figures provisional.

Primary Raw linear p50 Linear, calibrated 0.79: p10 / p50 / p90 Sensitivity, calibrated 0.68 (PF-arm loss): p10 / p50 / p90 Fold model, upper bound: p10 / p50 / p90 D2 5.20 6.35 / 6.62 / 6.89 7.38 / 7.69 / 8.01 10.44 / 11.28 / 12.13 D3 2.06 2.44 / 2.62 / 2.80 2.84 / 3.04 / 3.26 4.03 / 6.30 / 8.58 D4 0.98 1.05 / 1.25 / 1.45 1.22 / 1.45 / 1.69 1.12 / 4.38 / 7.68 D19 1.13 1.35 / 1.44 / 1.54 1.56 / 1.68 / 1.79 1.96 / 3.03 / 4.11 D21 1.13 1.29 / 1.43 / 1.58 1.50 / 1.66 / 1.83 1.32 / 1.92 / 2.52

Figure 2. S(u) is the probed reading S plotted against the solar-output curve u (a clear-sky solar share). At D19 the probed reading (MVA) falls steadily as the solar-output curve rises, so a straight line fits it; at D12 the reading rises with the solar-output curve, and the linear fit misses at low values (it reads about 1.5 MVA where the readings are about 1.2). The panels share a vertical axis. Experiment 671's own figure shows the curves of D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21, which are all falling or flat, not V-shaped (see its S(u) figure). D19's cell is 671's stored cell. D12's cell was re-probed for this page with the same probe code on experiment 662's stored uninjected neural network (2026-06 cutoff, seed 0), because no stored output holds D12's curve. The re-probe reproduces 671's D19 capacities exactly (linear 1.12 MW, fold 1.34 MW, seed 0), and reads D12 at -3.13 MW (linear) and 5.35 MW (fold, reactive terms free), against -3.0 and 5.3 MW in experiment 662's five-seed medians. The rising curve at D12 matches 662's crossing-map call that D12 folds.

Conversion loss and the reactive-power setting. The calibrated 0.79 column divides the raw linear reading by the linear probe's recovery in the signed (no apparent-power) world. The sensitivity column divides by 0.68, the recovery when the conversion is the PF arm. The sensitivity column is the capacity if the conversion loss were the PF arm's 10.7 points, and its figures are about 16% higher than the main figures. NGED's statement, relayed by the maintainer, is to assume power factor 1 for the substation meters, with some reactive power always present. Experiment 662 simulated that with a reactive-floor arm (a constant reactive power of 0.10 times the median sunny-midday power) and a zero-reactive arm (a reactive power of zero, so the reading is the absolute value of the real power). The table gives the median recovery of the injected farm over the six MW Primaries for the first farm rotation. The cells marked (679) are experiment 679's, which use all farm rotations (signed recovery 0.746 at 0.5 times, not 0.79), so compare them with 0.746 and not with the 0.79 beside them. The zero-reactive linear cell is derived as 0.746 plus the loss of -0.5 points.

Probe and reactive model 0.5 times 1 times 2 times 6 times Linear, PF arm 0.68 0.53 -0.12 -0.80 Linear, reactive-floor arm 0.73 (679) 0.63 -0.11 -0.83 Linear, zero-reactive arm about 0.75 (679, derived) not run -0.10 not run Linear, signed (no conversion) 0.79 0.78 0.77 0.78 Fold model, PF arm 0.73 0.71 0.78 0.88 Fold model, reactive-floor arm 0.88 (679) 0.67 0.78 0.88 Fold model, zero-reactive arm 0.77 (679) not run 0.77 not run Fold model, signed 0.85 0.63 0.28 -0.03

At 0.5 times, the level of the five MVA Primaries, the reactive-floor arm loses 0.5 points of linear-probe recovery, against 10.7 points in the PF arm. Experiment 679 states the loss as the median over the six MW Primaries of each Primary's own difference between the signed and converted recoveries, so it differs from the difference of the medians in this table. Experiment 679's recoveries use all farm rotations (signed 0.746), not the first. The interval of the loss is -1.0 to 7.7 points (80%), and the zero-reactive arm's is -0.5 (-3.3 to 6.8). The fold model's 0.5-times cells are not read as a loss, because experiment 679 finds it reads above the signed world in the floor world (0.88 against 0.80). At 1 times the floor arm recovers 0.63 and the PF arm 0.53, against 0.78 without the conversion, and at 2 times the arms match (-0.11, -0.10, and -0.12).

The conversion loss is therefore probably small at the MVA Primaries, but the data do not rule out a loss of up to 7.7 points. If the meters read power factor 1 with a small floor, the main figures need no further correction. If the loss were 7.7 points, the divisor would be approximately 0.71 (0.79 minus 0.077) and the figures would be about 11% higher. The loss measured at 0.5 times in the PF arm was 5 to 12 points at D9, D11, D14, and D16 (experiment 671). Using experiment 671's per-Primary signed-world values of 0.73 to 0.82 instead of 0.79, the main figures would change by about +8% to -4%.

The reactive power of the real meters is unknown, and no native-world read at the five MVA Primaries exists under the floor arm. Experiment 662's code builds no native floor-arm worlds, so the loss is measured on the six MW Primaries and carried over to the five MVA Primaries.

The main MVA figures use the signed-world recovery 0.79; the PF-arm calibration (reactive power 0.25 times the median real power) appears only in the sensitivity column and in the known-answer tests of experiments 662 and 671.

docs.title: Three Primaries without a main figure to compare: D12, D8, and D22
docs.text:
D12 has a fold-model figure only, because its linear probe reads negative. The fold model reads 7.19 / 7.48 / 7.77 MW (10th / 50th / 90th percentile, calibrated by 0.704, experiment 662's fold-model recovery factor) and the linear probe reads -3.0 MW raw. Figure 2 shows the rising curve behind the negative linear reading.

D8 and D22 are report-only for the MVA conversion, as are D5 and D10.

  • D8: the linear probe reads 1.72 / 2.63 / 3.59 MW (calibrated). Experiment 508 tested whether a gas engine behind D8 explains a large share of its midday dips, so a solar reading there is not separable from the engine.
  • D22: the linear probe reads 1.83 / 1.94 / 2.06 MW. Experiment 508 treated D22's midday dips as a mix of causes, so the reading is not a clean solar capacity.
  • D5 and D10 for the MVA conversion: in experiment 662's injected worlds both sit past the fold at every level, because their midday readings are about 1 MW and the injected farm is at least 2.0 MW. The reactive-term setting then decides the recovery (experiment 671 reads 0.0 to 1.16 across the fold variants). Their main figures are the MW-probe values above, which need no conversion.

docs.title: Register cross-check: probe against the register floor at 12 Primaries, and 2 reported only
docs.text:
The floor is the capacity that three registers list inside the Primary's service area, with the sites that NGED already meters removed. The probe estimates unmetered solar, so the floor must exclude metered sites. The definitions below were fixed before any total was computed.

  • Where the registers are. The Feed-in Tariff installation report (Ofgem, covering 2010-04-01 to 2025-03-31) is data/ml-experiments/00045-.../outside/fit_solar_pv_installations.parquet. NGED's Embedded Capacity Register (August 2026 release) is literature/NGED/NGED ECR AUG 2026.xlsx. The Renewable Energy Planning Database (Q2 2026) is cached in repd_register.json under the solar BMU census's inputs/raw/ folder. Experiment 129's registers.parquet holds the older Feed-in Tariff totals that experiment 267 used.
  • Coverage and size cuts. The Feed-in Tariff lists photovoltaic installations of every size that it records, by postcode district only. The Embedded Capacity Register lists generation of 50 kW and above that is connected (the table counts only "Connected" solar rows, and some rows carry no coordinate, so they cannot be placed in a polygon). The Renewable Energy Planning Database lists operational solar, mostly 150 kW and above.
  • Polygons. The Embedded Capacity Register and the Renewable Energy Planning Database carry British National Grid coordinates, so each row is placed by point-in-polygon against the Primary's area_wkt. The Feed-in Tariff has no coordinates, so a postcode district's capacity is shared to a Primary by the share of the district's delivery points inside the polygon (experiment 45's fit_district_polygon_shares). The Feed-in Tariff column is therefore a share, not a point-in-polygon total.
  • De-duplication. Feed-in Tariff sites above 50 kW can also appear in the Embedded Capacity Register, and a Feed-in Tariff row cannot be matched to a register row (no coordinates), so the floor counts the Feed-in Tariff only up to 50 kW. A Renewable Energy Planning Database row within 1 km of an Embedded Capacity Register row inside the same polygon counts as the same site and is dropped. The match is by distance only, so it can miss a site that the two registers place more than 1 km apart, and can merge two neighbouring sites.
  • Metered sites. A register row within 1 km of a solar generator that NGED meters is removed from the floor. The page does not name those generators.
  • Floor (main). Feed-in Tariff up to 50 kW (declared net capacity, the AC figure) plus Embedded Capacity Register rows below 1 MW, plus Embedded Capacity Register rows of 1 MW and above connected at 11 kV or below, plus Renewable Energy Planning Database rows below 1 MW that match no Embedded Capacity Register row, all with metered sites removed. A row with a corrupted coordinate (203 Embedded Capacity Register rows have a coordinate inflated by a power of 10) is divided by 10 until it lies in Great Britain; rows with no coordinate (655 connected rows) are not placed, so the floor is a lower bound. Sites of 1 MW and above that connect at 33 kV or above are left out of the main floor, because they connect above the Primary and are not behind its meter. They are in the all-sites sensitivity column, together with Renewable Energy Planning Database rows of 1 MW and above that match no Embedded Capacity Register row (adding the Renewable Energy Planning Database rows of 1 MW and above changes no flag).

All values are MW inside the Primary's polygon. FiT is the Feed-in Tariff, ECR the Embedded Capacity Register, and REPD the Renewable Energy Planning Database. The Embedded Capacity Register's capacity is its "already connected registered capacity" and the Renewable Energy Planning Database's is its "installed capacity (MWelec)". Neither register states a direct-current or alternating-current basis in these columns, so they are read as AC.

At 8 of 12 Primaries the probe's interval lies above the floor; D2, D3, D5, and D21 lie below it. "Probe above floor" means the probe's 10th percentile is at or above the floor, "overlaps" means the floor lies inside the 10th to 90th percentile, and "below floor" means the 90th percentile is below the floor.
