  • D5 is below the floor mainly because of one site. Embedded Capacity Register sites of 1 MW and above at 11 kV or below contribute 2.70 MW of D5's 4.55 MW floor. Without it the floor is 1.85 MW and the probe's interval is above it. The data cannot say whether that site lies behind the Primary's meter or is metered, so this is a flag, not a cause.
  • D3 is below the floor by 0.47 MW. Its floor is 3.27 MW (2.07 MW from the Feed-in Tariff up to 50 kW and 1.20 MW from an Embedded Capacity Register site at 11 kV) against a probe 90th percentile of 2.80 MW. With the sensitivity calibration (0.68) the margin is 0.01 MW. Experiment 671 reads D3's linear capacity as provisional, and the fold model's upper bound is 4.03 to 8.58 MW.
  • D2's floor (8.01 MW) lies 1.12 MW above the probe's 90th percentile (6.89 MW), and includes 5.00 MW from sites of 1 MW and above. With the sensitivity calibration the 90th percentile is 8.01 MW, the same as the floor, and D2 overlaps it. D2 is the only flag that depends on the calibration. At D2 the fold model's upper bound is 10.44 to 12.13 MW.
  • D21 is below the floor. Its floor is 2.21 MW, mostly 0.96 MW from the Embedded Capacity Register below 1 MW and 1.25 MW from the Feed-in Tariff up to 50 kW. The linear probe reads 1.29 to 1.58 MW (1.50 to 1.83 MW with the sensitivity calibration) and its calibration is provisional. The data cannot say which side is wrong.
  • D16's all-sites floor of 59.37 MW is not a comparison. It includes 56.70 MW of sites of 1 MW and above that connect at 33 kV or above.
  • Feed-in Tariff band of 50 kW to 1 MW. Adding it to the floor lowers the count above the floor from 8 to 5 of 12 (D11 and D16 move to "overlaps", and D10 moves to "below floor", because its floor of 2.27 MW plus 0.54 MW is 2.81 MW against a probe 90th percentile of 2.62 MW), but it is probably counted twice with the Embedded Capacity Register's sheet below 1 MW, so the main floor leaves it out.
  • Double counting that remains. The Feed-in Tariff between 50 kW and 1 MW overlaps the Embedded Capacity Register's smaller sheet. The band is left out of the floor and listed in the table. The Feed-in Tariff is a share of postcode districts, so it can over- or under-count a Primary whose boundary cuts a district.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The MW-Primary factor 0.68 may not transfer to rooftop panels with other tilts. The probe finds 0.68 of an injected real farm's AC MW (0.676 to 0.708 across the four injected farms). The factor comes from four injected farms that resemble each other, and may not transfer to a fleet of rooftop panels with other tilts.
  • Energy-basis spread. Measured in energy, the recovery is 0.78 (donor rows) to 0.88 (all daylight rows), so the capacity of a physics-shaped plant carrying the same energy is 0.77 to 0.87 times the megawatt-basis capacity.
  • The fleet is many systems with no single clip. An unmetered fleet has many panel tilts and inverter limits, so the AC capacity here is an effective figure for a fleet shaped like the injected farms.
  • Intervals. The 80% interval is widened by the farm-to-farm spread of the recovery factor. In the checks of experiment 649 it covered the injected truth in 0.81 of 96 constant injections, a value consistent with 0.80 and not more precise than about 0.1.
  • No month-by-month change. Nothing here shows how capacity changed from one month or year to the next. The probe's 2024 and 2025 summers differ by at most 0.07 MW at every MW Primary.
  • MVA Primaries. The main MVA figures assume power factor 1 with a small reactive floor, where experiment 679 measures a conversion loss of 0.5 points (80% interval -1.0 to 7.7). The interval's upper end does not rule out a loss of 7.7 points, which would raise the figures by about 11%. The reactive power of the real meters is unknown, and no native-world read at the five MVA Primaries exists under the floor arm.
  • The two newest registers may list sites built after the probes' 2026-06 cutoff. The Embedded Capacity Register is the August 2026 release and the Renewable Energy Planning Database the Q2 2026 release, so both can list sites connected after the probes' 2026-06 cutoff, and neither carries a date that could remove them. The Feed-in Tariff ends at 2025-03-31.
  • Feed-in Tariff shares. The district shares of overlapping Primary polygons can sum above 1 over Primaries, so the Feed-in Tariff column can count one district's capacity twice.
  • Registers. The registers lag installations, list some sites twice, and list sites connected above the Primary. The probe and the registers also measure different things (a probe reading of a whole summer against capacity as registered).
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the rows behind the probes may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: What would change this
docs.text:
• NGED's list of connected solar behind a Primary, if it lies outside the probe interval by more than the interval's width. Where the list (a count and total capacity at 11 kV and below) does, the probe's calibration or the floor's match to metered sites is wrong at that Primary. D2, D3, D5, and D21 are the four where the flags already point that way, so those four records would settle most. D2's probe 90th percentile is 1.12 MW below its floor.
  • A reactive-floor arm in the native worlds of the five MVA Primaries. That would replace the MW-Primary measurement of the conversion loss with a measurement at the five MVA Primaries themselves. It needs a code change in experiment 662's native-world builder.
  • Knowing which of D5's and D2's large sites lie behind the Primary's meter would settle both flags.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Forecast checks: the experiment scores no forecast, so the median-minus-mean and quantile-score checks do not apply.
  • Prediction (1) held: the probe's 80% interval lies above the combined floor at 5 of the 6 MW Primaries (D5 is below it). Prediction (2) held: the probe is above the Feed-in Tariff floor (up to 1 MW, the floor of experiment 267, reproduced from experiment 649's table) at 6 of 6 MW Primaries and above the combined floor at 5 of 6. Prediction (3) held: 3 of the 5 main MVA Primaries lie below the floor (D2, D3, and D21). Prediction (4) was not tested: experiment 267's totals are Feed-in Tariff only, and the Feed-in Tariff here uses the same district-share method.
  • D12 re-probe: one CPU process, one stored network, about 1.5 minutes. No neural network was trained.

Code: ml-experiments/00673-pv-capacity-for-nged-per-primary-with-register-cross-check/: e00673_deliverable.py (tables and figure 1), e00673_d12_probe.py (the D12 re-probe, which imports experiment 662's and 671's modules), and e00673_s_of_u.py (figure 2).

docs.title: Can a per-Primary day labeller tell whether an apparent-power Primary was exporting, and does a soft or a hard PV prior help?
Summary
docs.text:
Take-home. A day labeller that reads two features of each day finds injected solar export well at moderate export, but real reverse flow at the six substations that report signed power is shallow and short, and the labeller finds 5 of 59 such days. On the eight substations that report apparent power it flags 39% of sunny April to August days at D8 and 13% at D4, so it is not yet a usable sign label for them. A simple midday rule, chosen after seeing the real days, does better on those 59 days. Verdict: inconclusive under the rule registered in the plan, because P1 was met by the point estimates but not firmly, and P2, P3, and P5 failed. P4 held only in the pooled bin. All numbers come from injected days or 59 real days, never from truth at the eight. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so counts are lower bounds.

What we asked. Eight of the National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) primary substations report apparent power (megavolt-amperes, which includes reactive power and is never negative), so a day on which one exported power to the grid looks like a day of low demand. We built a per-day labeller from two features: the lowest reading at the edges of the sun's path (experiment 508), and how much better a V-shaped curve fits the day's reading than a falling curve does (experiment 417's W-shape score). We tested it on six substations that report signed power in megawatts, after adding the recorded output of real solar farms to their readings and hiding the sign ("injected" days), and on the 59 real reverse-flow days of those six. Then we applied it to the eight. No weather or forecasting model is fitted.

Terms. A primary substation ("Primary", D2 to D22 are anonymised identifiers; substations may be named) steps 33 kV down to 11 kV. A reverse-flow day has at least 2 daylight half-hours of negative signed power and at least 1 of positive. Readings are in points of the substation's capacity. The night import is the median reading with the sun more than 6 degrees below the horizon, April to September. The day ratio is the day's median reading from 10:00 to 15:00 divided by the night import; a day with ratio 3 or more is labelled sign-unknown. Days are sunny, mixed, or cloudy by the mean clear-sky index from the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) from 10:00 to 15:00 (0.7 or more, between, below 0.3). The three arms differ in how they use the expectation that export happens on sunny days: C uses no prior, B flags only sunny days with enough solar capacity, and A raises the evidence needed on less sunny days. P1 to P5 are the pre-registered predictions in the plan below. NGED's "Reverse Power Flow?" column (file "Monitor Direction") is a hint, not truth: it has no confidence column, and this page reports agreement and conflicts with it as findings, never as labels or training truth.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1: recall and false-reverse rate by arm on the six, leave-one-Primary-out, 95% month-block intervals.

Figure 2: share of April to September days in each label, on the eight.

Figure 3: example days with the reading and each arm's label (the real D10 days first).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• At export 1.5 to 3 times the night import the labeller finds about 64% of injected days. The 1,004 reverse-flow days in this bin are all injected. Recall and false-reverse rate: C 0.644 (0.598 to 0.690) and 0.030 (0.014 to 0.055); B 0.553 (0.503 to 0.602) and 0.010 (0.002 to 0.021); A 0.578 (0.525 to 0.630) and 0.038 (0.018 to 0.067). Not scorable: 0.216. No day is sign-unknown on the six.
  • Below 3 times the night import, recall is much lower. Pooled, C 0.314 (0.290 to 0.337), B 0.191 (0.174 to 0.208), A 0.277 (0.254 to 0.300); false-reverse 0.036, 0.018, 0.029. By injection level (1, 2, 3 times) C's recall is 0.121, 0.257, 0.420. Not scorable: 0.237, because farm dropouts remove half-hours.
  • P1 to P4. P1 holds for C by the point estimates but not firmly, and fails for A (recall 0.578). P2 fails: B cuts false-reverse by 68% (bar 40%) but recall by only 14% (bar 25%) at 1.5 to 3 times, because 956 of the 1,004 days are sunny, where injected output lies; pooled below 3 times B loses 39% of recall, and experiment 417's drop was larger (0.77 to 0.37). P3 fails: A's recall is within 0.10 of C's, but on mixed and cloudy days A's false-reverse rate is 0.034 against C's 0.030, not half. P4 held only pooled below 3 times (no subset reaches recall 0.6 there), and not at 1.5 to 3 times (C: 0.658 on low-demand days). C's false-reverse rate is 0.104 on low-demand days against 0.026 on other days, pooled below 3 times.
  • Real reverse flow is mostly invisible to the labeller. Of 59 real days (D10 54, D5 3, D9 2), C flags 5, A and B 2. The real days are shallow midday exports (median day ratio 0.15) whose shoulders stay near the night import (median shoulder ratio 0.83), and the W-shape score is 0 or null on 56 of 59.
  • On the eight, P5 fails at D4 and D8. In arm A, the reverse-flow label covers this share of sunny April to August days: D2 0.2%, D3 1.1%, D19 0.8%, D21 0%, D22 0.9% (all at most 5%), D4 13.3%, D8 38.9%, and D12 5.7% (63.4% of its days that are not sign-unknown; 91.0% are sign-unknown). Arm C labels more days than A at D8 (448 against 431) and D22 (14 against 6), mostly on mixed and cloudy days, as predicted. Without the capacity gate D4 rises to 44.3% for A and B. Against NGED's hint: D8 "Yes" agrees, D2, D3, D19, and D21 "No" agree, D4 "No" disagrees, D12 and D22 "Maybe" make no claim.
  • Why the eight flag more. D4's day ratio lies in the 1.5 to 3 bin on 71% of days (7% for the six without injection), where the shoulder threshold of 0.85 times the night import is loose. D8's flags come from the below-1.5 bin, where its shoulder minimum is bimodal. A real gas engine is behind D8: 42 of the 44 dip days of experiment 508 in April to September are labelled reverse by C and A, and 32 of those carry the engine flag, so the labeller does not separate engine from sun.
  • Other counter-examples. D22's 11 dip days (of experiment 508's 13) are labelled no reverse flow by every arm. 27 of D12's 28 winter days with a midday reading below 6.9 points are labelled reverse by C and A (B: no reverse flow); experiment 506 counted 13 such days with a stricter sun rule, and the thresholds are calibrated on April to September, so this is an extrapolation with non-dip winter days flagged at about 18%. A signed-power series negative on 19,054 of 24,058 rows was not scored, because the CAMS arrays hold only the 16 demand Primaries.
  • Soft-prior sweep (post hoc). A_flat (5%, 5%, 5%) and A_steep (5%, 1.25%, 0.25%) move recall by under 0.04 but change D4's sunny-day flag rate (A_steep 1.4%, A 13.3%, A_flat 21.9%).
  • Calibration check. The held-out false-reverse rate of C stays below 10% in both day-ratio bins (0.037 below 1.5, 0.030 at 1.5 to 3), so the thresholds count as calibrated on injected days. 8 threshold cells used a fallback pool.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast per site. Not applicable: no forecast is made.
  • Mean-forecast error beside quantile contrasts. Not applicable.
  • Triggers fired. Trigger 1 (real days missed), trigger 2 (P2, P3, and the conflict with experiment 417), and trigger 4 (see below). A fresh Sonnet agent audited the numbers (briefs/674_audit.md) and reproduced every headline figure and the leave-one-Primary-out thresholds.
  • Trigger 4. Leaving out D10, which holds 453 of the 626 known non-reverse days at 1.5 to 3 times, makes P3 true on a small base and reverses B's false-reverse contrast against C.
  • Audit findings accepted. The headline bin holds only injected days (9% of reverse-flow days); the W-shape threshold is degenerate (zero in every 1.5 to 3 cell, so the training flag rate is about 2.5% to 2.6%, not 5%); D4's flag rate follows from its day ratio. No finding was rejected.
  • Post hoc (audit finding, reproduced in the printed report). The rule "day ratio below 0.3" was chosen after seeing the 59 real days. It flags 52 of them (47 at D10) and 198 of 6,231 other days (3.2%; D5 160, D10 32, D9 6). Treat it as a lead, not a result.
  • Extrapolation. The six report megawatts and the eight megavolt-amperes, so the known-answer scores need not carry over; the audit puts D12's false-reverse rate outside the calibration season at about 15% to 20%.
  • Lab shortcuts. ERA5 temperature is dropped from the W-shape profile; the capacity gate uses the injected farm's true size in the injected worlds; the profile is built on the scored days.
  • Resampling unit. Month blocks (Primary and calendar month, four levels pooled), which is stricter than resampling days; threshold uncertainty is not in the intervals.
  • Data. Cleaned data, nothing dated 2026-07-01 or later. Thresholds frozen from the six before the eight were built (file digest starts 7cf8570b). No fitted models. Code and printed report: ml-experiments/00674-mva-sign-labels-soft-and-hard-pv-prior-day-labeller/.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Start from the midday dip (day ratio below 0.3), and test it at the eight with the shoulder minimum as a separate second signal.
  • Calibrate on real days where they exist (D10), and use injected days as a stress test.
  • Ask NGED for a few weeks of signed power at D12 and D8, which would settle both without a fit.

docs.title: Plan (as registered)
docs.text:
Reading the plan. r is a ratio of observed magnitudes, not a measured export: on an injected day it can look like an ordinary high-demand day, so the 1.5 to 3 bin mixes both. A Primary (NGED's 33 kV to 11 kV substation) reports signed real power in megawatts (six of them, D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16, used for the known-answer tests) or apparent power in megavolt-amperes (eight, D2, D3, D4, D8, D12, D19, D21, D22). Readings are in points of the Primary's capacity. The night import I of a Primary is its median reading when the sun is more than 6 degrees below the horizon, from April to September, before 2026-07-01. The day export ratio r is the day's median reading from 10:00 to 15:00 UK clock time divided by I. A day is reverse flow when its signed power is negative somewhere in daylight and positive elsewhere.

Day features (both computed from readings only).

  • Shoulder minimum s. The lowest reading in the morning and the evening shoulder windows of experiment 508 (sun 5.6 to 19.0 degrees above the horizon), divided by I, taking the smaller of the two windows. A day needs at least 3 finite half-hours in each window.
  • W-shape score w. Experiment 417's limb score (e00417_day_flip.score_days), built on a Table made from the Primary's readings and CAMS arrays. The score is copied into this experiment's folder, so no earlier script is edited. Lab shortcut: the ERA5 temperature term is dropped (the copy has none), so the demand profile is an overcast-day median by block, day type, and hour with no temperature slope, and bank holidays are not used. The profile is built from the readings of the world being scored, with no labels, so it uses the scored days too (hindsight, a lab shortcut).
  • Sign-unknown class. A day with r of 3 or more is labelled sign-unknown, because experiment 508 found that nothing calibrates there (over 98% of injected days cross zero). A day with neither s nor w computable is not scorable; a day with one feature is scored on that feature alone. w needs a daily maximum of the clear-sky shape of at least 0.6 (experiment 417's rule, and the shape includes cloud), so on most cloudy days the labeller rests on s alone. Solar-farm dropouts also remove half-hours from the injected worlds (experiment 508 found about 22% of days qualify), which raises the not-scorable share there. Sign-unknown and not-scorable days count as "not flagged" in recall (the conservative reading) and are reported on their own.

Arms (all use leave-one-Primary-out thresholds frozen before the held-out Primary is read). A day is flagged when s is below tau_s or w is above tau_w. Each threshold is the value at which the rule alone flags alpha / 2 of the non-reverse training days of the same r bin (below 1.5, and 1.5 to 3) and the same stratum. A cell with fewer than 30 training days pools the two r bins, then all strata; the number of fallbacks is reported.

  • C, no PV prior. One stratum for all days, alpha = 5%.
  • B, hard PV-high mask. Only days in the PV-high stratum can be flagged, with alpha = 5% calibrated on those days; all other days are labelled no reverse flow. Reproduces the idea of experiment 417's A+H arm.
  • A, soft PV prior. Three strata with alpha of 5% (PV-high), 2.5% (mixed), and 0.5% (cloudy): the evidence needed to flag a day rises where solar output is less likely, and never becomes infinite. The 1 : 0.5 : 0.1 ratio is a pre-registered choice and a sweep (post hoc, labelled) over 1 : 1 : 1 and 1 : 0.25 : 0.05 is reported.
  • Strata. PV-high: mean clear-sky index k (CAMS) from 10:00 to 15:00 of at least 0.7 and the capacity gate holds. Cloudy: k below 0.3. Mixed: the rest. Capacity gate: the Primary's AC p90 PV capacity in the latest season-year of experiment 474's R4 table (plus, in the injected worlds, the injected farm's true size, an oracle lab shortcut) is at least 0.5 times the night import in MW. The gate is circular at the eight (experiment 474 fitted that table on the same readings at reactive power zero and its placebo failed), so a post hoc sensitivity run drops the gate and strata use k alone.

Known-answer test. The six Primaries rotate as held-out Primary; the other five at levels 0 (no injection), 1, 2, and 3 calibrate the thresholds. Farms Solar A to C rotate over the six as in experiment 408, and no generator's name or series appears on the page. April to September days only for the headline; all months for the counter-example in D12's winter dips. Report, per arm, per r bin: recall (flagged reverse-flow days over all reverse-flow days, and over those not sign-unknown), false-reverse rate (flagged over all non-reverse days), the share sign-unknown, the share not scorable. Low-demand days are the 20% of each Primary's April to September days with the lowest median 10:00 to 15:00 reading before injection, reported separately. D5 and D10's real crossing days (level 0) give a no-injection recall (59 days, so the interval will be wide).

Application to the eight. Thresholds are frozen from all six Primaries and written to disk before any of the eight is read. Report label counts per class (reverse flow, no reverse flow, sign-unknown, not scorable) per Primary, arm, and stratum, for April to September and for sunny April to August days. Agreement with NGED's hint is reported as agreement with a hint (D8 "Yes", D12 and D22 "Maybe", the other five "No"): a Primary agrees when the reverse-flow share of sunny April to August days is above 5% for "Yes" and at most 5% for "No", and "Maybe" makes no claim.

Counter-examples and how each arm treats them.

  • A signed-MW series negative on 19,054 of 24,058 rows at all hours (Wrangle T1). Not scored, because experiment 412's CAMS arrays hold only the 16 demand Primaries (checked in the folder). By construction arm B never flags a day outside the PV-high stratum, and arm A needs strong evidence there; arm C has no such protection.
  • D8's gas engine pulling apparent power to zero without sun. Flagged days at D8 split by stratum, per arm; if experiment 508's stored day table holds an engine flag, the overlap is reported too.
  • D22's unexplained dips. The 13 dip days of experiment 508 against each arm's label.
  • D12's 13 midday dips between October and February. The labeller is calibrated on April to September, so winter days are outside its calibrated domain (low sun, few shoulder half-hours). Report each arm's label on those 13 days, most of which may be not scorable or sign-unknown, and count them as an extrapolation, not a test.

Standing practices. Cleaned data throughout (flagged half-hours dropped by scan_power), nothing dated 2026-07-01 or later is read (the CAMS arrays are cut at that date), the D15 and D18 cut does not apply (neither is used). Monthly refits, saved models, stored predictions, tails and curtailment cost, forecast examples, and load-shift event plots do not apply, because no forecast is made. Caveat to repeat: NGED's event logs are incomplete, so clean days may hold unlogged load shifts and counts are lower bounds.

What the earlier advice implies, and where the plan departs from it. Follows experiment 508's advice to use sun-elevation shoulders and not the 10:00 to 15:00 minimum, not to calibrate above three times the night import (hence the sign-unknown class), and to check a shoulder dip against cloudy days (the strata). Follows experiment 417's advice that a hard mask costs recall. Departs from nothing.

Reproducing experiment 417. The write-up says which of 417's two figures arm B reproduces: its drop in false-reverse rate (12.0% to 3.6%) and its drop in recall (0.77 to 0.37), side by side with this experiment's day-level figures, which use different rows.

Plan review (Sonnet, 2026-11-09). Twenty-two findings. Accepted and applied above: the complete verdict mapping, the point-versus-firm bar wording, the P5 bars, the farm-leakage fix, the minimum cell size, the 2-half-hour crossing rule, the W-score cloud limit, the winter domain, the hindsight and oracle notes. Also applied after the code review: days with no ratio count as not scorable, the false-reverse rate is reported over both known-label days and all non-reverse days, and low-demand membership no longer depends on the injection level. Not applied: threshold uncertainty in the intervals (stated as a limit).

Reviews. One Sonnet plan review, one fresh Sonnet code review before any score is read, one Sonnet results check (re-derives the headline numbers), one Sonnet prose review. The audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill run on the finished numbers.

docs.title: Why does the search of experiment 670 leave most recipient megawatts unpaired, and does a pretrained encoder find the donor of an injected load transfer better than the event table's own features?
docs.text: Masked pretraining did not help find the donor of a load transfer, and the donor end, not the recipient search, is where E1-J loses megawatts. Experiment 675 reopens the graph line that experiment 672 closed under its stop rule, at the maintainer's request, with experiment 660's generator unchanged. Step 0 found that the donor was not found for 0.87 of the found-but-unpaired recipient megawatts in the long and deep cell. The frozen probe then found 0.28 of the long and deep donor megawatts with the pretrained encoder (P-M), against 0.59 with a random-init encoder (R), 0.63 with a logistic regression on the node inputs (F), and 0.44 for E1-J, all at E1-J's false-donor rate of 0.63 per Primary-year. The verdict is not supported.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• P-M, P-C, R, F. The probe's four arms. P-M: a temporal convolutional encoder pretrained to reconstruct masked windows of real residual history, then frozen. P-C: the same encoder pretrained to predict the next 3 to 6 hours causally. R: the same encoder, randomly initialised, frozen. F: a logistic regression on the node inputs, with no encoder.
  • Cell, donor, recipient, found, paired, E1-J. As in experiment 672. In short: cells group injected events by length (long: over 7 days or no end; medium: over 1 up to 7 days; short: up to 1 day) and depth (deep: 8 noise units or more; shallow: 2 up to 8). A noise unit is the block-difference noise of a Primary substation's residual, in megawatts. E1-J is experiment 653's event table plus experiment 670's recipient search. Stop rule 0 adopts E1-J on the new residual panel if it pairs 0.60 or more in both deep cells. Arm C is experiment 327's residual.
  • Donor megawatts found at E1-J's false-donor rate. The share of the megawatts of injected donor steps (edge transfers with a metered recipient) that lie within -12 to +24 hours of an alarm, where each arm's alarm threshold is set so that its false alarms per Primary substation and year equal E1-J's (0.63). Every arm's achieved rate matched that target. E1-J's own figures differ from the 0.22 and 0.29 of experiment 670's page only by cell and measure: 0.22 is the paired share of recipient megawatts, and 0.29 the paired share of all transfer megawatts.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: The figure shows that masked pretraining finds fewer donor megawatts than the random-init encoder and than the no-encoder regression in both deep cells, fewer than causal pretraining in the medium and deep cell, and more than the no-encoder regression in both shallow cells. The intervals resample worlds only: they leave out fit variance, the random-init encoder's seeds range from 0.46 to 0.70, and the no-encoder regression is one fit.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Step 0 has four CPU-only parts. 0a diagnoses where E1-J loses recipient megawatts, 0b chooses the residual panel, 0c re-runs E1-J on that panel, and 0d classifies the verified D5 and D16 transfer into a cell.
  • Step 0a, where E1-J loses recipient megawatts. E1-J re-run on worlds 900 to 939 reproduces experiment 670's long and deep count exactly (37 found-but-unpaired recipient ends, 139.8 MW). Each end is sorted into the first reason in this list that applies. Share of those megawatts, long and deep (37 ends) and medium and deep (24 ends): donor not found 0.87 and 0.84; recipient start outside the search window 0.02 and 0.00; megawatt ratio outside the share window 0.01 and 0.00; linked to the wrong donor 0.00 and 0.00; split across 2 or 3 recipients 0.04 and 0.02; other 0.05 and 0.14.
  • Step 0b, the residual panel. Experiment 327's arm C (the convex model of experiment 130, a rolling 24-month monthly refit, no lagged power, a fitted solar capacity) stays as the residual. Leave-one-year-out copies of the same model (fitted capacity, capacity pinned at experiment 649's calibrated median, and capacity pinned at experiment 45's latest vintage) had a lower noise unit than arm C at 2, 1, and 3 of 15 Primaries respectively (arm C: 9), because a year-out fit cannot follow the structural change at D8 (1.61 against 1.45 MW) and D18 (0.23 against 0.14 MW). Arm C does not absorb the verified D5 and D16 transfer: its event-window mean residual minus the 28 days before is -1.35 MW at D5 and +1.98 MW at D16. A neural lag-free cross-fit was not built.
  • Step 0c. E1-J pairs 0.29 and 0.25 in the long and deep and medium and deep cells, below 0.60, so stop rule 0 does not fire.
  • Step 0d. The verified D5 transfer lasts 15.4 days at 9.04 noise units (long and deep); D16 lasts 14.8 days at 4.52 noise units (long and shallow).

  • Donor megawatts found, mean of three seeds (donors per cell in brackets; E1-J and F have no seeds, F being one fit).

    Cell E1-J P-M P-C R F Long, deep (59) 0.44 0.28 0.33 0.59 0.63 Medium, deep (47) 0.40 0.16 0.28 0.47 0.41 Long, shallow (303) 0.25 0.24 0.14 0.21 0.10 Medium, shallow (214) 0.17 0.26 0.17 0.14 0.05 Short, deep (55) 0.17 0.09 0.31 0.28 0.12 Short, shallow (229) 0.05 0.06 0.11 0.04 0.02

  • P-M minus R and P-M minus F, with world-resampled 95% intervals. Long and deep: -0.31 (-0.43 to -0.19) and -0.35 (-0.49 to -0.20). Medium and deep: -0.31 (-0.51 to -0.16) and -0.25 (-0.47 to -0.07). Long and shallow: +0.02 (-0.03 to +0.07) and +0.13 (+0.07 to +0.19). Medium and shallow: +0.13 (+0.06 to +0.20) and +0.21 (+0.14 to +0.28).

  • Seed spread. R's long and deep result is 0.70, 0.62, and 0.46 over its three seeds, and 0.55, 0.56, and 0.31 in the medium and deep cell. P-M's seeds give 0.26 to 0.29 and 0.12 to 0.21. Every P-M seed is below every R seed in both deep cells.
  • Short cells. The short and deep and the short and shallow cells are in the table but not in the figure or the verdict, which the plan restricts to the deep cells. In the short and deep cell the causal arm P-C finds 0.31, more than P-M (0.09) and F (0.12) and about as much as R (0.28).
  • Recipient AUROC. Between 0.91 and 0.94 for every arm in the two deep cells (P-M minus R: +0.01 long and deep, 0.00 medium and deep). The pair block of neighbour step ratios, shared by all arms, sets most of it.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P-M minus R in donor megawatts found: failed in the long and deep (-0.31), medium and deep (-0.31), and long and shallow (+0.02, needed +0.05) cells, and held in the medium and shallow cell (+0.13, needed +0.03).
  • P-M minus F: failed in both deep cells (-0.35 and -0.25, needed +0.03), and held in the long and shallow cell (+0.13).
  • P-M minus R in recipient AUROC: failed (about 0 in the deep cells, needed +0.05; -0.01 in the long and shallow cell, needed +0.03).
  • P-M minus P-C: failed in both deep cells (-0.05 and -0.11, needed 0 or more).
  • Step 0 prediction: held. The largest reason is the donor not being found, and E1-J pairs under 0.60.
  • Probe stop rule fires. P-M fails both its R bar and its F bar in both deep cells, so pretraining is dropped. P-C beats P-M by 0.05 (interval -0.16 to +0.07, within noise) and 0.11 in the deep cells, which meets the rule's 0.03 bar, but P-C is itself 0.26 and 0.20 below R. The two clauses of the rule therefore point to different starting weights for experiment 676.
  • Per-seed condition. For the held predictions, every seed is above its bar (medium and shallow, P-M minus R; long and shallow, P-M minus F).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Leak tests. The masked-window and scored-target leak tests, and a causal test, passed in the code review before any fit, with a positive control for each.
  • Matched false-donor rate. All arms reached 0.625 per Primary-year, E1-J's rate.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet reviewer re-derived the long and deep donor megawatts found for P-M seed 0 (0.262), R seeds 0 and 2 (0.701, 0.461), and F (0.625) from the raw score files with its own code. It found no train and test mismatch, normalisation error, window error, threshold-matching error, or world mismatch that explains the deficit. The audit triggers fired (R beats P-M, R varies by seed, and a nested control beats the pretrained arm). The reading stands because P-M is below R in all three seeds in both deep cells. The intervals resample worlds only, so they do not include fit variance, and F is one fit.
  • Sample sizes. The probe trains on 200 injected worlds and tests on 40, with three seeds, and R's seed spread is as large as some contrasts. The long and deep cell has 59 donor steps and the medium and deep cell 47.
  • Inherited caveats. NGED's logs may miss load shifts, so matched logged shifts are lower bounds. The noise units saw the validation months, and the injected start hours come from NGED's logged onsets up to 2026-07, as in experiments 670 and 672.
  • Pretraining length. Pretraining ran 10,000 steps per arm and seed (the plan said about 20,000, timed against the GPU budget) and used about 1.8 GPU-hours over six runs. The masked loss was still falling slowly, so a longer run might change P-M, though not by the 0.3 that separates it from R.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Experiment 676 should use the hybrid arm (the graph neural network's donor posterior as the candidate source inside E1-J's recipient search), because step 0a puts the loss at the donor end. Whether it starts from a randomly initialised encoder or from the causal arm's weights is for the graph Discuss session, because the two clauses of the stop rule disagree.
  • In the long and deep cell, a logistic regression on the node inputs finds more donor megawatts than E1-J (0.63 against 0.44). Whether that holds with the false-donor rate measured on the real record is untested.

docs.title: The plan as committed
docs.text:
The plan below was committed before any score was read.

This is the plan, committed before any score is read. It reopens the graph line that experiment 672 closed at 15 Primaries under its pre-registered stop rule. The maintainer asked for the second test, and the page says so because the stop rule is not overturned by new evidence. It is a deliberate test of components that experiment 672 did not build, not a repeat of it. Experiment 675 is part 1; the edge-state network is part 2 (experiment 676), run only if part 1 does not adopt the event table.

docs.title: The question
docs.text: Experiment 670 found that the event table with a recipient search (E1-J) pairs 0.29 of the injected megawatts in the long and deep cell and 0.25 in the medium and deep cell. It finds 0.73 of the recipient megawatts in the long and deep cell and pairs 0.22, and no experiment has said where the other 0.51 is lost. Experiment 672's graph network found donors as well as E1-J and then failed to link them (0.47 of donor megawatts found, 0.09 paired). This part answers two questions in order. First, why does E1-J leave found recipients unpaired, and does a residual panel built by the lag-free modular network (instead of experiment 327's convex residual) change what E1-J finds? Second, does an encoder pretrained on masked windows of real history carry information about donors and recipients that a random encoder and the event table's own features do not?

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Step 0a, E1-J's unpaired recipients (CPU). From experiment 670's stored rows for the long and deep and the medium and deep cells, each found but unpaired recipient end is sorted into the first reason that applies: the donor was not found; the recipient start lies outside the search window; the megawatt ratio lies outside the share window; the recipient was linked to the wrong donor; the transfer was split across two or three recipients; other. The page reports the megawatt share of each reason and says which end the next step should aim at.
  • Step 0b, the residual panel. In order, the first that succeeds is used: (1) the lag-free modular network (weather encoder, date-time encoder, mixer, no lags) on ERA5 and CAMS from 2019-09, cross-fitted by year so each year is scored by the copy trained on the other years, for the 15 Primaries with experiment 591's early-calibration cuts; (2) the same network from 2022 if the 2019 to 2021 cleaned power or weather is not on disk; (3) experiment 327's convex residual. The all-Primaries median is removed in all three. At the maintainer's instruction (relayed by the manager), the lag-free model is made as good as the tricks that worked allow. Before the panel is built, the plan's first task is an inventory from the merged pages of the lag-free demand recipes and tricks that helped: the best-guess and K1/K3 lag-free bodies, the explicit solar term of experiments 639 and 643, temperature-trend inputs such as experiment 622, the D5 offset question, holiday and calendar features, and whatever else the pages show. The expected-power model then takes (1) an explicit solar term from CAMS and ERA5 known weather (experiment 649's capacity table as the centre with its interval, a physics curve from the pooled plant table with a learned fleet blur, calibrated rather than raw capacity, never scored on forecast weather; traps: a sunny spring can look like a capacity step, and a cloud-following load looks like solar), (2) temperature-trend inputs, and (3) the other proven tricks. It uses no lagged power and no free slow offset that could absorb a long event (E1's masked frozen seasonal slow level instead), is cross-fitted by year so a year's events are not in the copy that scores it, and cuts ERA5 and CAMS at 2026-07-01. The page reports its out-of-fold residual noise per Primary against experiment 327's arm C residual (the one E1 and E1-J used), uses the better residual for E1, E1-J, and the network alike, and re-runs E1 and E1-J on it so that a better residual cannot pass for a better detector. If this needs more than 1 GPU-hour in step 0, the plan pull request says so. The page names the panel used and whether its weather exists at forecast time (it does not: ERA5 arrives about 5 days late, so the panel is a laboratory residual, as in experiments 670 and 672).
  • Step 0c, equal treatment. E1 and E1-J are re-run on the new panel with experiment 660's default generator, unchanged, and E1-J's penalties are retuned on validation worlds with experiment 670's grid. These re-runs are the baselines for the probe and for experiment 676.
  • Step 0d. The verified D5 and D16 transfer is classified into its cell with experiment 653's noise units.
  • Probe encoder. A shared bidirectional temporal convolutional network per Primary on two streams: a 1-hour stream of 6 dilated layers with 64 channels, and a daily stream of 4 layers with 32 channels, fused by adding the upsampled daily features. Node inputs are the residual in noise units (clipped at 30), a present flag, the expected-power q05 to q95 width in noise units, the mean-residual gaps over the past and the future 1, 3, and 7 days, step statistics at 6-hour and daily scales in both directions of time, the noise unit as log megawatts, the routine-step rate, a megawatt-or-megavolt-ampere flag, and hour and weekday as sine and cosine. Each past statistic has a future twin stored as a separate channel, and every window carries a coverage channel.
  • Pretraining. The masked arm (P-M) reconstructs the residual in masked windows with a Student-t distribution per hour (1-hour stream, windows of 3 to 24 hours, 1 to 3 per Primary) and a daily mean (daily stream, windows of 1 to 7 days). In 30% of samples the same window is also masked at one or two neighbours, and 40% of Primaries carry a mask. The loss counts masked hours only. The causal arm (P-C) predicts the mean and spread of the next 3 to 6 hours with causal convolutions. Rows before 2024-01-01 only; AdamW at learning rate 1e-3 with cosine decay, about 20,000 steps, timed over the first 500 steps against the GPU budget.
  • Leak tests (both run in the code review, before the first fit). (1) Masked-window leak: for 200 seeded samples, replace the masked residual (at the masked Primary and every co-masked neighbour) with Gaussian noise of 10 noise units, recompute every input, and assert the inputs are bit-identical (torch.equal, float64, CPU) and the reconstruction predictions agree to 1e-12; repeat with a step of +20 noise units. Every statistic whose window overlaps the mask is recomputed from the readings outside the mask, per sample, after the mask is drawn. (2) Scored target leak: replacing the injected-truth table by a shuffled copy must leave every input unchanged.
  • Probe arms and training data. P-M, P-C, R (random initialisation), F (logistic regression on the node inputs, no encoder), and P-M-noemb (P-M without the optional weather and date-time embeddings), each with 3 seeds. The probes train on 200 injected worlds and are tested on the 40 scored worlds. The donor probe asks whether an hour lies inside the first 24 hours of a donor step; the recipient probe asks, for each true donor onset and each linked neighbour, whether the neighbour is the recipient.
  • Measurement. The share of donor megawatts found at a false-donor rate equal to E1-J's on the scored worlds, and the recipient AUROC, per cell, with intervals that resample whole worlds. Cells are experiment 665's six cells; shares are MW-weighted; found and paired follow experiment 670.
  • Standing practices. Cleaned data and the D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01 as in the injected panel of experiment 660 (no refit cadence applies; no forecast is scored). One GPU process at a time, behind the maintainer's one-year backtests, checkpoint every 1,000 steps. CPU work runs under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue. The ceiling is 9 GPU-hours for experiments 675 and 676 together: step 0 under 1, the probe at most 3.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet plan review before the code; a fresh Sonnet code review (including both leak tests) before the first fit; a Sonnet results review; a Sonnet write-up review; and a Sonnet prose review. The review findings are triaged in the pull request.
  • Unlogged-event caveat. NGED's logs may miss load shifts, so matched logged shifts on the real record are lower bounds. The long and deep cell is nearly empty on the real record (experiment 665 found none of the 77 logged shifts longer than 1 day in it), so success there can be shown only on injected worlds.
  • Inherited leaks. The noise units (experiment 653) saw the validation months, and the injected start hours come from NGED's logged onsets up to 2026-07, as in experiments 670 and 672.

docs.title: Does a neural network with an explicit state for every link between two Primaries, and a recipient lag, pair more injected load-transfer megawatts than the donor-probe hybrids of experiment 678?
docs.text: A neural network that learns, hour by hour, whether power is moving between two neighbouring substations, and how long the receiving substation lags the giving one, names the right pair of substations for no more of the transferred power than simpler methods do, so we stop building graph models at 15 substations. We added fake load transfers (power moved from one Primary substation to its neighbours for hours or days) to real power history, and measured the share of the moved megawatts for which each method names the correct giving and receiving substations (the paired share). For transfers longer than 7 days and 8 or more noise units deep (a noise unit is a substation's usual difference between successive 6-hour averages), the new network pairs 0.32 of the megawatts, against 0.29 for the search of experiment 670, 0.35 and 0.36 for the two hybrids of experiment 678, and 0.60 set as the share needed to adopt a method. For transfers of 1 to 7 days and 8 or more noise units, it pairs 0.23, against 0.25, 0.30, and 0.32. Earlier stop rules had closed the graph line (experiment 672 and experiment 678), and the maintainer asked to continue it here. NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so counts of real events are lower bounds. A plain-words summary of the whole line is on the event-table summary page.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Primary, E1-J, cell, paired, found. As in experiment 678.
  • G, G-R, G-0. The edge-state neural network trained and scored on the real graph (G), on a rewired graph that keeps 0.16 of the real links (G-R), and with the link features removed (G-0). G-0 still decodes recipients from the real neighbours.
  • F-hyb, R-hyb. The hybrids of experiment 678 with a logistic-regression probe and with a randomly initialised encoder probe.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: The figure shows G inside the intervals of E1-J, F-hyb, R-hyb, and G-0 in both deep cells, and the rewired graph near zero. The bars to pass were 0.395 and 0.347.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• First-look gate: failed. G pairs 0.315 (95% interval 0.22 to 0.41) in the long and deep cell and 0.226 (0.10 to 0.38) in the medium and deep cell. The bars were R-hyb plus 0.05: 0.395 and 0.347. No further seeds were trained.
  • Differences, with 95% intervals from resampling 40 worlds. G minus R-hyb: -0.03 (-0.16 to +0.10) and -0.07 (-0.27 to +0.13). G minus E1-J: +0.03 (-0.10 to +0.16) and -0.02 (-0.22 to +0.18). G minus G-0: -0.02 (-0.09 to +0.05) and -0.06 (-0.15 to +0.03). G minus G-R: +0.28 (+0.17 to +0.40) and +0.16 (+0.00 to +0.34).
  • Other cells. G pairs 0.18 (long, shallow), 0.22 (medium, shallow; E1-J 0.13, interval of the difference +0.02 to +0.17), 0.08 (short, deep), and 0.02 (short, shallow). G-0 pairs 0.25, 0.18, 0.03, and 0.02.
  • Donor megawatts found. Long and deep: G 0.30, G-0 0.39, E1-J 0.44, R-hyb 0.48. Medium and deep: 0.24, 0.31, 0.40, and 0.43.
  • Decoder. The decoder grid (4 onset costs by 4 cut-offs, widened to 6 by 6) never reached the band of 3 to 9 decoded donor events per Primary-year on the real record in 2023-07 to 2023-12. G reaches 0.40, and the network's probabilities are near 0 or 1, so the grid barely changes the result. The fallback picked the pair nearest the band: onset cost 2 and cut-off 0.15 in all three arms.
  • Real record. G calls 0.31 (2022-01 to 2023-06, the training years), 0.39 (2023-07 to 2023-12), and 0.80 (2024-01 to 2026-06) donor events per Primary-year, against 6.8 events of all kinds for E1.
  • False transfers. Decoded transfer events (donor and recipient ends) that are not a correct pair: G 5.9 and G-0 7.4 per Primary-year, against 0.38 for E1-J. G decodes 2.85 donor events per Primary-year on the injected worlds, of which 0.085 are correct pairs and 2.3 have no injected event within 24 days (the generator's hard negatives are not in the truth table, and were not checked as a cause).
  • Timing. The median start error of correctly paired recipients is 8 half-hours for G, against 3 for E1-J and 2 for R-hyb.
  • Part A (post hoc): ending the added donors after 6 hours instead of 2 days does not help the short cells. Paired share in the short and deep and short and shallow cells stays at 0.08 and 0.027, medium and shallow rises to 0.153 (F-hyb) and 0.155 (R-hyb) against 0.131 for E1-J, and long and deep falls to 0.31 and 0.32 (experiment 678: 0.36 and 0.35). False transfers rise to 0.51 (F-hyb) and 0.52 (R-hyb, mean of 3 seeds) per Primary-year, against 0.38.
  • Compute. Each of the three networks took about 25 minutes on the GPU, so the first look used about 1.3 GPU-hours of the 2-hour ceiling.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• G1 (G at least R-hyb plus 0.05 in both deep cells): failed (0.315 against 0.395; 0.226 against 0.347).
  • G2 (G at least E1-J plus 0.10): failed (0.315 against 0.386; 0.226 against 0.345).
  • G3 (G-R at most a third of G in the deep cells): held (0.039 against 0.105; 0.063 against 0.075), but G-R keeps only 0.16 of the real links and has almost no labelled transfers to learn from, so the placebo is near zero by construction.
  • G4 (false transfers at most 1.5 times E1-J's, 0.57): failed (5.9).
  • G5 (median recipient start error at most 4 half-hours): failed (8).
  • H1 (post hoc variant): failed. Medium and shallow gains +0.02 for each hybrid against +0.03 predicted, the short cells gain 0.00, although false transfers stay under 1.5 times E1-J's (0.57) on average over the three R-hyb seeds, and two seeds give 0.58.
  • Verdict: not supported. The first look fails G1, so the stop branch applies.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and the mean-forecast error beside each contrast. Not applicable: the experiment scores event tables on injected worlds, not forecasts.
  • Triggers fired, and the audit. Three fired: the nested no-link arm G-0 pairs as much as G; the decoder scored 0.706 paired on the 20 validation worlds and 0.315 on the scored worlds; and G's false-transfer rate exceeds its real-record rate. A fresh Sonnet audit re-derived every headline share from the stored rows and found them correct. It traced the validation gap to a small sample (the 0.706 rests on 23 events, interval 0.43 to 0.89) and a slightly easier world construction, and the page does not quote 0.706 as a skill. It found that the decoder grid selection fell through to the nearest-to-band fallback in all arms, so the decoder is not tuned to the validation worlds. It showed that the false-transfer comparison with the real record counted both ends in one number and donors only in the other, now corrected above. It showed that G-0 is not blind to the graph, because the decoder draws recipients from the real neighbours, so G minus G-0 tests only the link features and the message passing.
  • Leak tests. Four tests passed in two Sonnet code reviews before the first fit. The masked-window test (1) is vacuous for this network, which masks nothing during fine-tuning, and is kept as a regression check on the inputs of experiment 675. The meaningful tests are the receptive-field test (4), which shows that hours beyond a window's quarter margin do not change the posterior, and the check that labels are read only by the loss (2).
  • Unlogged-event caveat. The real-record rates above are lower bounds, because NGED's logs and the E1 mask of real events miss some events.

docs.title: The question
docs.text: Experiment 678 added the donor alarms of a probe to E1-J's recipient search and gained +0.08 in the two deep cells (the stop rule asked for +0.10). The hybrids only improve where E1-J looks for a donor. The remaining untested part of the design is a network that carries an explicit state for every link between two connected Primaries, with a lag of 0 to 36 half-hours before the recipient follows, so that the donor and the recipient are found together instead of one after the other. This experiment builds that network once, trains it on injected worlds from a random initialisation, and reads whether it pairs more transfer megawatts than the hybrids do.

docs.title: Part A: a post hoc variant of experiment 678 (CPU, at most 2 cores)
docs.text:
• Question. Experiment 678's added donors could not end sooner than 2 days after their start, so the short cells equalled E1-J exactly. Do donors that may end after 6 hours or more help the short cells?
  • Construction. Everything of experiment 678's donor construction is kept except the earliest end (6 hours after the start instead of 2 days) and the running-median window of the end search (6 hours instead of 1 day). The probe scores, thresholds, duplicate rule, and recipient search are experiment 678's, so the arms are F-hyb and R-hyb (three seeds), each with the changed end rule.
  • Reporting. Post hoc; every cell, with the false-transfer rate beside each result, and the deep-cell numbers beside experiment 678's to show what the changed end rule does there.

docs.title: Part B: the edge-state network (GPU)
docs.text:
A network that reads the node inputs of experiment 675 and outputs, per link and hour, the state of the link and the recipient lag. The construction below is fixed before any run, and it departs from the Opus specification of the line in the ways listed under "Departures from the specification".

  • Architecture, node side. The bidirectional encoder of experiment 675 (an hourly stream of 6 dilated convolutions with 64 channels, a daily stream of 4 dilated convolutions with 32 channels, one round of neighbour averaging), from a random initialisation, on the 35 node-input channels of experiment 675.
  • Architecture, link side. For each of the 25 links of the real graph and each hour, the features are the two Primaries' encoder outputs, the cross-correlation of the Primaries' 6-hour forward steps at 19 recipient lags (0 to 18 hours at 1-hour spacing), the log ratio of the two steps' amplitudes, and the two Primaries' megawatt-or-megavolt-ampere flags. The link head is antisymmetric by construction: it scores "first donates" on the features in one orientation and "second donates" on the same features swapped, and scores "off" on the symmetrised features. A second head scores the 19 recipient lags given the donating orientation.
  • Node side head. Each Primary-hour also gets a three-class state (no step, a downward step, an upward step). Its evidence is added to the link decode, so the two are decoded together.
  • Decoder. A three-state chain per link with a fixed stay probability, run forward and backward over the hours of a world. The onset cost and the link cut-off are chosen on the validation worlds from a grid frozen in code (at least 4 log-spaced values each), by the highest paired share in the two deep cells together, subject to 3 to 9 decoded edge events per Primary-year on the real record in 2023-07 to 2023-12. A greedy pass accepts the link segment with the highest posterior, removes its hours from the donor Primary, and repeats. Each accepted segment becomes a donor event, with the size measured on the residual by step_size, and recipient events at the decoded lag, as the recipient search of experiment 670 emits them. There is no post hoc pairing window.
  • Training worlds and labels. 200 injected worlds (seeds from 100000, experiment 660's default generator, unchanged). Link labels come from the generator's truth table: the link is "donates" in the donor's hours, the lag is the recipient's start minus the donor's, and all other time is "off" at full weight, except in the hours before 2023-07-01 where E1 decodes an event on the un-injected real record (weight 0). That mask uses no label and no hour from the scored years. Training worlds start their events before 2023-07-01 (the generator's cutoff), so no training onset lies in the validation or scored years. The weight of the transfer states is 5.
  • Loss and optimiser. Cross-entropy on the link state (weight 1.0), on the lag (0.3), and on the node state (0.5). AdamW with a learning rate of 1e-3 and cosine decay, windows of 2,880 hours, a batch of 4, half the windows centred on an injected edge transfer. The number of steps follows from timing the first 500 steps against the 2 GPU-hour ceiling; a checkpoint is saved every 1,000 steps and a rerun resumes.
  • Arms. G (the network on the real graph), G-R (the same network trained and scored on the degree-preserving rewired graph that keeps the fewest real links, from 300 draws, with the share kept reported), and G-0 (no links: the neighbour averaging in the encoder and the link features are both zeroed, so the link head has no information about neighbours; G minus G-0 is read without a bar). References, read from experiment 678's stored rows: E1-J, F-hyb, and R-hyb.
  • Departures from the specification. The following are not built, to keep the first look inside 2 GPU-hours (the brief's logistic baseline is F-hyb, read from experiment 678's stored rows): masked pretraining (experiment 675 found it did not help), the daily-scale pretraining masks, 1,000 or more training worlds (200 are used), the lag-free modular network as the residual panel (experiment 327's arm C is used, as in experiments 670 to 678), the amplitude and recipient-share head, the conservation and wobble terms, the donor head (the node state replaces it), the 16-wide weather embedding, the cross-injector arms, the fine-tuning curriculum, three rounds of message passing (one is built), the boundary loss and half-hour refinement, G-hyb (Part A is a related post hoc test), the timing and real-record rate predictions and the D5 and D16 check, step 0a's diagnosis (done in experiment 675), and the semi-Markov duration prior (a fixed stay probability replaces it). Each departure may make the neural network weaker than the specification, so a failure here is a failure of this smaller neural network.
  • Leak tests. Both run in a fresh Sonnet code review, before any GPU fit, on CPU with a fixed seed. First, replacing the residual inside a hidden window (Gaussian noise of 10 noise units, then a step of +20 noise units), with the mask drawn before any statistic is computed and the statistics recomputed from the readings outside it, leaves every node input and every link feature bit-identical in float64, including the cross-correlations, at the masked Primary and its neighbours; a positive control that reads the unmasked panel must fail the same test. Second, replacing a scored world's truth table with a shuffled copy leaves the network's outputs bit-identical, because labels enter only the loss.

docs.title: Reviews and running
docs.text:
• Panel caveat. The residual panel, experiment 327's arm C, is the one that experiments 670 to 678 used, and training, validation, and scored worlds share it. The neural network could therefore memorise real residual patterns of the training years. Scored events lie in 2024 to 2026, which the training worlds never show.

  • Order. Sonnet writes the plan and the code. A fresh Sonnet agent has reviewed the plan (findings triaged in the pull request), then two more review the code, one after the other (including both leak tests passing) before the first fit. A fresh Sonnet agent reviews the results and the write-up, and a second reviews the prose. At most one Opus review is added, and only if a verdict could change.

  • Running. CPU work runs under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue, with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, at most 2 cores. One GPU process runs at a time, after nvidia-smi and uptime show that the maintainer's backtests have the GPU free; a fit pauses between networks if they need it.
  • Inherited caveats. NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so matched logged shifts on the real record are lower bounds. The injected start hours come from NGED's logged onsets up to 2026-07, as in experiments 670, 672, 675, and 678.
  • Summary page. Whatever the outcome, the PR also adds a plain-words summary page of the whole event-table line (experiments 653, 665, 670, 672, 674, 675, 678, and this one), written after the results.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00676-*/e00676_worlds.py: builds the 20 validation worlds and the real-record E1 mask (reads experiment 660's generator, writes worlds/).
  • e00676_data.py, e00676_net.py: link, lag, and node labels from the truth table; the edge-state network (reuses experiment 675's encoder and node inputs).
  • e00676_train.py, e00676_run.py, e00676_decode.py: training (weights/<arm>_seed0.pt), decoder selection and scoring on the 40 scored worlds (scored/<arm>_seed0_rows.parquet).
  • e00676_report.py, e00676_chart.py: aggregate rows into summary.json and the figure.
  • e00676_diag.py: real-record event rate by period (scored/G_seed0_real_rate.json).
  • e00676_leaktests.py: the four leak tests.
  • e00676_posthoc.py, e00676_posthoc_report.py: Part A, which patches experiment 678's run and report code and writes posthoc/rows_*.parquet.
  • Data under data/ml-experiments/00676-*/, read from earlier experiments: the 200 training worlds and 40 scored worlds of experiment 675 (worlds/), the probe scores of experiment 675 (probe/), and the rows of experiment 678.

docs.title: How much does each component of the Candidate demand network contribute to its one-year backtest score, when the network is built up from the date-time encoder alone, one component per step?
docs.text:
This page builds the Candidate demand neural network up one component at a time. The Candidate is the neural network that forecasts demand at 16 Primary substations (substations that step 33 kV or 66 kV down to 11 kV). Step 1 has the date-time encoder alone, each later step adds one component, and step 8 is the Candidate. The sequence of steps is the ladder. Steps 9a and 9b refit step 5 and step 8 monthly instead of quarterly. Scores are the normalised mean absolute error (MAE) of the median forecast, in points of capacity, over 12 months of daily forecasts up to 14 days ahead.

The earliest step in this ladder to score below the manual heuristic is step 3b, the date-time and weather encoders pre-trained on ERA5 and CAMS. (ERA5 and CAMS are two reanalyses, which are estimates of past weather.) Step 3b scores 8.30 against 8.73 for the manual heuristic. Step 5, the first step with both lags, scores 7.88.

Steps 6 to 8 add no skill over step 5 on the annual mean. Step 8 is the Candidate. It scores 7.99, which is 0.105 worse than step 5 (95% interval 0.078 to 0.132). Monthly refits improve both step 5 and step 8 by about 0.47 points, which is a larger gain than any component added after step 3b.

Colours are assigned within each figure, not across the page. In the second figure the lines of steps 7 and 8 nearly coincide.

Steps 6 to 8 make the median forecast copy less of an injected shift, and they raise error on rows away from logged events. An injected shift is a simulated step added to the lag inputs. The copied share is the fraction of the shift's depth that the median forecast reproduces, so 0 means the forecast ignores the shift. On a held-out bank of such shifts, the median of step 5 copies 5.9% of the shift and the Candidate copies 2.8%. Steps 6 and 7 copy 4.7% and 3.3%. Away from the logged events, the same steps raise MAE by 0.05 (step 6) and 0.12 (steps 7 and 8) against step 5. Gap columns, which step 6 adds, hold the difference between the observed power at the lag time and the forecast made with both lags masked. Step 7 adds exponentially weighted averages of that gap, and step 8 adds the same columns from neighbouring substations.

docs.title: Take-home
docs.text:
• Order of importance. Pre-training the encoders (step 3b, −0.59 against step 3a) and the 24-hour lag (step 4, −0.28) account for most of the gain over the manual heuristic. The 1-week lag adds −0.13. Steps 6 to 8 add +0.04, +0.06, and +0.005.
  • Steps 1 and 2 are worse than the manual heuristic (9.73 and 9.61 against 8.73), and step 3a is too (8.89). Climatology scores 11.79.
  • Training with injected events raises MAE by 0.07 to 0.10 points on every row and cuts the copied share by about half to two-thirds. Step 5 trained without injected events copies 11.0% of a shift, and the Candidate trained without them copies 8.1%.
  • Monthly refits (step 9) improve skill more than any component added after step 3b. Monthly refits lower MAE by 0.47 (interval 0.31 to 0.64) for step 5 and 0.47 (0.32 to 0.64) for step 8 on matched seeds. The Candidate at monthly refits (step 9b) scores 7.48, against 7.53 for the monthly file of experiment 667.
  • On the six MW Primaries the GAM is level with the best monthly arm and ahead of every quarterly step; the networks win on the seven MVA-only Primaries. See Standard methods beside the ladder.
  • The ladder describes one order of adding components, on 12 months that overlap the Candidate's development months. It ranks nothing for production.

docs.title: Skill by step
docs.text:
Skill rises steeply to step 3b, then flattens. The figure below shows steps 1 to 5. Each is a separate network trained with the Candidate's settings and the components named in its label.

The table lists the annual scores in points of capacity. CRPS is the continuous ranked probability score, which scores the whole forecast distribution. The 95% intervals come from resampling 7-day blocks of origin days, and every step is scored on the same 3,879,313 rows, which are the rows that all the steps share.

Step MAE of the median 95% interval CRPS 1: date-time only 9.73 5.50 2: weather only 9.61 5.47 3a: date-time + weather (ENS only) 8.89 5.12 3b: date-time + weather (pre-trained) 8.30 7.99 to 8.61 4.74 4: + 24 h lag 8.01 4.56 5: + 24 h and 1-week lags 7.88 7.56 to 8.21 4.49 6: + gap columns 7.93 4.52 7: + weighted averages of the gap 7.98 4.56 8: + neighbour columns (Candidate) 7.99 7.66 to 8.33 4.57 9a: step 5, monthly refits 7.39 7.14 to 7.67 4.19 9b: step 8, monthly refits 7.48 7.21 to 7.77 4.26 Manual heuristic 8.73 8.41 to 9.07 4.98 Climatology 11.79 6.60 Experiment 667, monthly refits (a) 7.53 4.29

(a) Experiment 667's file scored on the same rows with the scoring code of experiment 668; the private table is scores_668/primaries_NRA/scores.csv.

The contrast between adjacent steps carries intervals that are tighter than the intervals of the scores themselves, because the two steps are scored on the same rows.

docs.title: Whether the later steps ride through load shifts better
docs.text:
The logged events cannot show which step handles a load shift better, because every step's error jumps at the event start. The figure pools 12 logged events (10 at days −7 to 3 after the start, because two began before the backtest) (10 shifts that lasted more than 7 days and involved two units or more, plus the verified transfer at D5 and D16). NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so these counts are lower bounds. The normal-running output is meant to carry on as if the shift had not happened, so a jump in error is expected at every step.

The cell of long events with a deep shift (more than 7 days, 8 or more noise units) holds no rows. No logged shift fell in it.

An injected shift measures the same question without the label problem. The bank holds simulated shifts of known depth, injected into the lag inputs only, on rows the networks never trained on. The share of the shift that the median copies is the headline measure here: 0 means the forecast ignores the shift, and smaller is better for the normal-running output.

Step Copied share, trained with injected events Copied share, trained without Copied share, monthly refits 5 0.059 0.110 0.071 6 0.047 0.103 0.059 7 0.033 0.082 0.042 8 0.028 0.081 0.030

Each cell is the mean over seeds 0 to 2 of the pooled share over days 0 to 14, and the standard deviation over seeds is 0.002 to 0.008. The monthly column is the "trained with" version. Steps 7 and 8 copy similar shares (0.033 and 0.028), so their lines overlap in the figure and the neighbour columns add little here.

Away from the logged events, the later steps have a higher MAE. On rows more than 14 days from any logged event of the same series, MAE rises against step 5 by 0.049 (interval 0.037 to 0.061) at step 6, 0.120 (0.084 to 0.156) at step 7, and 0.119 (0.082 to 0.155) at step 8.

In the 7 days after an event the monthly refits score worse on these 10 logged shifts. The slice holds 34,706 half-hours from 102 origin days, and no interval was computed, so the result is descriptive. With seeds 0 to 2 on both sides, step 9a scores 5.77 against 5.23 for step 5 at quarterly refits, and step 9b scores 5.69 against 5.15 for step 8. Inside the events and on all other rows, the monthly arms score better.

docs.title: The Candidate's prevailing output
docs.text: Only experiment 667's Candidate has a prevailing output. The normal-running output (NRA) is the forecast made as if no shift had happened. The prevailing output is the forecast that follows a detected shift. It comes from a survival head (R-haz), and it needs the lag-free table's signals, so the ladder's steps have none. The rows of experiment 667 used here are the extra-lag head of experiment 681 (the folds 2025-11 and 2025-12 keep the older head). Over the 8 logged events where the shift could be timed, the prevailing output recovered half of the shift after a median of 4 days (range 2 to 6 days). The two figures below show the NRA and prevailing outputs of experiment 667 over the verified transfer.

docs.title: Time series of the forecasts
docs.text:
At D16 both step 5 and step 8 follow the daily shape but stay well below the observed peaks during the confirmed shift, and at D5 they stay above the observed power. D5 and D16 are the two Primaries between which load was transferred. Each figure has one arm per panel, where an arm is one step. The line is the median, the dark band is q25 to q75, the light band is q05 to q95, and each is the mean over seeds. The orange line is the observed power. The grey rectangle marks the confirmed load shift from 2025-12-30 to 2026-01-15, with 14 days either side. The scored "verified transfer" window starts and ends one day earlier, on 2025-12-29 and 2026-01-14. At D16 the observed peaks reach about 13 MW, and the medians of both steps stay near 9 to 10 MW through the shift. At D5, which gave up load, the observed power falls and the medians stay above it. The normal-running output is meant to carry on as if the shift had not happened.

A warm week at D16 shows the same arms away from the event.

docs.title: Tails, CRPS, and curtailment cost
docs.text:
The forecasts are under-dispersed at both ends. For steps 5 to 8, 3.4% to 3.8% of observations fall at or below the q01 forecast and 3.6% to 3.9% fall above q99, against a nominal 1%. Step 3b has 4.4% below q01 and 4.0% above q99. Monthly refits move the observed shares about half a point closer to the nominal 1%.

Curtailment cost mostly follows the CRPS ranking of the arms, with the GAM lowest. XGBoost is the exception: its CRPS equals step 8's, but its cost is lower than every network's. The curtailment-cost scale is set by a stress limit of 50% (and 90%) of each series' earlier maximum, so the amounts in pounds are an index of ranking and not a forecast of spend. Each cell is relative to the manual heuristic (1.00) on the six MW Primaries, summed:

docs.title: Standard methods beside the ladder
docs.text:
Both stored arms cover a different row set than the ladder, so this section is scored on the rows that the stored arms and the ladder both cover. The GAM (Primary demand research default 3) and XGBoost (arm p_s6_bg2 of experiment 87) are stored with 09:00 UTC origins, and the rows the arms share run from origin 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-29 at lead times of 0 to 10 days (1,365,447 half-hours over the 16 Primaries). The six MW Primaries are scored separately from the seven MVA-only Primaries, because the MVA meters hide reverse flow.

The seven MVA-only Primaries are those whose meters record apparent power in megavolt-amperes, which hides the direction of flow; the six MW Primaries record real power in megawatts. twCRPS is the threshold-weighted CRPS, which weights errors at high demand more heavily. Each cell is in points of capacity, and the MAE rows are for the median. The three Primaries in neither group are left out. On the six MW Primaries the GAM is level with the best monthly arm (5.36 against 5.35) and ahead of every quarterly arm; on the cold nights the GAM leads steps 5 and above by 0.5 to 1.0 points. On the seven MVA-only Primaries the networks at step 5 and above beat the GAM and XGBoost on all rows, and the GAM leads on cold nights. The Christmas rows hold 20,448 and 23,856 half-hours, so those columns are descriptive.
