docs.title: Predictions that could fail
docs.text:
• P1 (step 8 matches experiment 667 within 0.10 CRPS on the pilot fold): met. At the annual scale, step 9b scores 4.26 CRPS against 4.29 for the monthly file of experiment 667.
  • P2 (the drop from step 3b to 5 exceeds every other adjacent drop over days 0 to 3): not met. The drops from step 2 to 3a and from 3a to 3b are larger over the same days.
  • P3 (step 8 lowers the copied share by at least 0.03 against step 5): met by a small margin. The drop is 0.031, from 0.059 to 0.028, and the standard deviation over seeds is 0.007.
  • P4 (no step before step 4 beats the manual heuristic over days 0 to 14): refuted. Step 3b scores below the heuristic in all four lead bands, 8.30 against 8.73 over all rows. The intervals of the two scores overlap, and the paired contrast was not computed.

The decision rule counts a contrast separable only when its interval excludes zero and it exceeds the standard deviation of the CRPS across seeds 0 to 2 of the same step. Every contrast in the contrast figure has an interval that excludes zero except step 1 to step 2 and, on MAE, step 7 to step 8 (+0.005, interval −0.003 to 0.012). The per-seed standard deviation of the CRPS was not tabulated, so the second half of the rule and the minimum detectable effect beside each contrast are not reported; the only seed spread reported is that of the injected-shift measure.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The step-8 network does not reproduce the monthly file of experiment 667 at the quarterly cadence (7.99 against 7.53). The monthly step 9b (7.48) is level with it. The two ladders differ from experiment 667 by seed count (5 or 3 against 2) and by the per-fold reference month of the signal noise.
  • The Candidate's settings were tuned on 5 of the 12 months, which favours the later steps. The year overlaps the development months and the final-test window of experiment 620 (2026-07 to 2026-10), and no model-selection choice was made from it.
  • Steps 1, 2, and 3a differ from step 3b in three ways: no pre-training, no frozen encoders, and only the newest D5 knot.
  • The ladder is one order of adding components. It says what each component adds given those already present, not what removing it from the Candidate would cost.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so every event count is a lower bound and the "none and at least 7 days after" slice can hold unlabelled events. The long-and-deep cell is empty.
  • The stored GAM and XGBoost forecasts end on 2026-06-30, so the comparison with them covers 8 months at lead times of 0 to 10 days. The stored Candidate of experiment 620 is one fit for 2026-07 only and is not scored, because experiment 667's file covers the whole year.
  • The curtailment-cost amounts depend on a stress limit and are read as a ranking.
  • Seeds: steps 1 to 4 use seeds 0 to 2, steps 5 to 8 use seeds 0 to 4 at quarterly refits and seeds 0 to 2 at monthly refits. Contrasts that cross cadences use seeds 0 to 2 on both sides.
  • One fit was killed for lack of memory. The 8 GB cap on the GPU wrapper script stopped three Candidate-type fits when three streams ran at once; the cap was raised to 14 GB and the three fits were re-run unchanged.

docs.title: Method
docs.text: Each step adds one component to the previous step, and every step keeps the Candidate's other settings. The Candidate is the class 2 neural network of experiment 620 (arm P7 with D50 of experiment 610). Each step adds one component to the previous step. The order matters: a reverse ablation gives each component's gain given the components already present, and says nothing about what removing the component from the full Candidate would cost.

docs.title: Components of the Candidate and where each sits on the ladder
docs.text:
These settings are the same in every step that contains the part the setting belongs to:

  • Loss and output: a three-component Gaussian mixture, negative log-likelihood, 11 quantiles from the mixture CDF, sorted (so no step has crossing quantiles).
  • Widths (8-wide Primary embedding, encoders 64 to 32, mixer 64), dropout 0.1, AdamW with weight decay 1e-3, batch 8192, 20% of rows per epoch, patience 8, gradient-norm clip 1.0.
  • The 730-day window, the 90-day recency half-life, the E3 refit rule (7-day embargo), and the slow per-Primary output offset D5. ENS-only fits (steps 1, 2, and 3a) have no pre-trained D5 knots: the offset keeps only the newest knot, which departs from the Candidate and is named as a caveat.
  • The 7 weather means, the 7 spread columns, the 2 lead columns, the 21 date-time columns, and the 14 B1 columns (thermal lag and solar gain) read by the weather encoder.
  • The cut of D15 and D18 before 2025-03-01.
  • No band-width factor at any step. The Candidate's factor 1.0934 is post-processing; step 8 is reported without it, and with it as one extra row if 667 applies it.

Added where:

Step Components added 1 Date-time encoder, Primary embedding, and mixer. The weather, spread, and lead inputs are removed, so the mixer sees only the date-time embedding. 2 Weather encoder alone (B1 columns included); the date-time and lead inputs are removed. The mixer sees the weather embedding and the Primary embedding. 3 Both encoders into the mixer; the lead columns enter here (the spread columns enter with the weather encoder at step 2). Version a: trained on ENS only, no pre-training, nothing frozen. Version b: ERA5 and CAMS pre-training, then fine-tuning on ENS with both encoders frozen (the chain of experiment 620). 4 One lag encoder at 24 hours, with its expected-weather and expected-date-time embeddings at the lag's own time, the lag-ID embedding, and block dropout of lags (30% of days). 5 A second lag at one week through the shared lag encoder. Two versions: with and without injected events. 6 The gap columns: power at the lag time minus the lag-free table, plus the exp_missing flags (arm P3 of experiment 606). Signal dropout D50 applies from here on, because the Candidate applies it whenever signal columns exist. 7 The exponentially weighted averages of the gap, half-lives 1, 3, and 7 days (arm P5 of experiment 606). 8 The 42 neighbour columns (arm P7 of experiment 606). Step 8 with injected events is the Candidate.

docs.title: Schedule and frozen parts of each step
docs.text:
All steps use the Candidate's three-stage schedule where it applies: stage 1 pre-training, stage 2 (encoders frozen, fresh mixer), stage 3 fine-tuning (recency weights, E3). "Stage" below never means a ladder step.

Step Stage 1 (pre-training) Stage 2 Stage 3 Frozen after stage 1 1, 2, 3a None; random initialisation Same as other steps, learning rate 5e-4 throughout Same as other steps Nothing 3b ERA5 and CAMS, lag-free Yes Yes Both encoders 4 ERA5 and CAMS, one lag Yes Yes Both encoders 5 (with, without) ERA5 and CAMS, two lags (shared) Yes, shared by the two versions Yes; "with" adds the 581 shifts to the lag inputs Both encoders 6, 7, 8 The step-5 chain The step-5 stage-2 checkpoint Starts from it with the signal columns zero-initialised Both encoders

Steps 3b, 4, and 5 each have their own pre-training, because the lag encoder is trained in stage 1, so the contrast between adjacent steps includes a re-pre-trained encoder. Steps 4 and onward do not start from the step-3b checkpoint. Only stage 3 of the Candidate sees the 581 shifts.

The lag-free table T is the median of the step-5 stage-2 checkpoint of the same version and seed with both lags masked, taken at the freshest origin with lead at most 24 hours. This is the Candidate's own construction (its stage-2 network), not a fine-tuned network. Steps 6 to 8 build T once per fold, version, and seed and share it (in-fold, as the Candidate does). The lag-free table uses the stage-2 lag network because the Candidate does, and step 8 reproduces the Candidate. The 606 reference month for the signal noise is the latest month before each fold's cutoff, not the Candidate's fixed 2026-06, which is future data for earlier folds.

docs.title: What "without injected events" removes
docs.text:
The Candidate trains on the lag-only synthetic shifts of experiment 581 (5% of each Primary's row span, depths 0.15, 0.30, 0.50 of capacity, lengths 3, 7, 15, 30 days). From step 8, each shift is also mirrored into one neighbour's summaries; at steps 4 to 7 the shifts reach only the own lag inputs. Steps 4 and below have no injected-event version (step 4 trains with the 581 shifts, as in the Candidate, in both ladders). Decisions:

  • The with version is the Candidate recipe as it stands (581 shifts), so step 8 with injection can reproduce 667.
  • The without version removes the 581 shifts from the lag inputs of stage 3 and the neighbour mirror at step 8; nothing else changes. The contrast therefore means different things at different steps (own lags only before step 8, own lags plus neighbours at step 8).
  • The held-out scoring bank is built by experiment 581's own generator with seeds disjoint from every training seed, so the bank matches the "with" arm's training distribution, which favours the "with" version by design. A second bank from experiment 660's generator (e00660_generator.py, the shared generator its page tells readers to import) is scored as a check on that bias. Both inject into lag inputs only. Each bank also mirrors the shift into one neighbour's summaries, so step 8's neighbour columns can show their effect. The injection reaches lag inputs only, never the targets.
  • Follow is the share of an injected shift's depth that the median forecast copies (0 means the forecast ignores the shift, 1 means it copies all of it); lower is better for an NRA forecast. Absorption is the share of the shift that the network's fitted values take up in its training power (experiment 595's definition). Absorption was not scored on this page.

The real long-and-deep cell is nearly empty (experiment 665 found none of NGED's 77 logged shifts lasting more than a day in the long-and-deep type), so the real-record slices are descriptive and every slice reports its rows and events first.

docs.title: Refit cadence, window, and seeds
docs.text:
• Window: the 12 months of experiment 667 (daily 12:00 UTC origins, 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31, 14-day horizon). Origins after about 2026-10-26 have valid times beyond the stored data, so each lead band reports its row count. The native origin of the networks is 09:00 UTC; the 12:00 contract origin follows 667's convention (power_fcst_init_time carries the 12:00 origin). The window overlaps the development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06) and the final-test window of experiment 620 (2026-07 to 2026-10); the Candidate's settings were tuned on 5 of the 12 months, which favours the later steps. The year is descriptive, and no model-selection choice is made from it.
  • The ladder refits quarterly, at the starts of 2025-11, 2026-02, 2026-05, and 2026-08, each fold scoring three months. Step 9 refits steps 5 to 8 monthly (12 folds). Experiment 667's own file is the monthly reference; the quarterly step 8 differs from it by cadence, seed count (5 against 2), and the per-fold reference month.
  • Pilot fold. Before the other folds ran, the 2026-05 fold ran step 8 with injection at the monthly cadence and 2 seeds, and was compared with the file of experiment 667 on the same rows. P1 was read there.
  • Seeds: steps 1 to 4 use seeds 0 to 2. Steps 5 to 8 use seeds 0 to 4 at quarterly refits and seeds 0 to 2 at monthly refits. A contrast across cadences, and every contrast on the contrast figure that involves the monthly arms, uses seeds 0 to 2 on both sides, which the ! (quarterly, seeds 0 to 2) and @1 (monthly) names mark in the private tables.
  • Intervals: block bootstrap over 7-day blocks of origin days, 2,000 draws.
  • Lags follow the Candidate's rule, which keeps every lag at least 24 hours before the 09:00 UTC native origin. The plan's second per-row check, that every lag was observed before 06:00 UTC on the origin day, was not added as a separate assertion.

docs.title: Reference arms
docs.text:
• The manual heuristic and climatology, from baseline_forecasters, as in 620 and 668.
  • The monthly file of experiment 667. The stored Candidate of experiment 620 (one fit, 2026-07 fold only) is not scored.
  • GAM: the Primary demand research default 3 (experiments 251 below 168 h and 322 above), refit weekly on the whole history, as stored. XGBoost: BG2, arm p_s6_bg2 of experiment 87, refit weekly, as stored.
  • Both stored arms have 09:00 UTC origins and end on 2026-06-29. The ladder is scored on the rows it shares with them, joined on series and valid time (each arm with its own lead). The shared rows cover 16 Primaries, 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-29, and leads of 0 to 10 days. A CPU re-run to cover the full year was not run.

docs.title: Prevailing output
docs.text: The survival head (R-haz) is trained on the frozen Candidate's quantiles with a bank of injected shifts and needs the signal columns, so no step before step 8 can have one. Every ladder file holds NRA_or_prevailing equal to "NRA". The prevailing rows shown on this page are those of experiment 667's own file.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
All files are private and live under data/ml-experiments/00677-building-up-the-candidate-demand-network-one-component-at-a-time/backtests/. Each holds 16 Primaries with the columns time_series_id, valid_time, nwp_init_time, power_fcst_init_time (the 12:00 UTC contract origin), the 11 quantile columns q01 to q99, seed, step, version, and NRA_or_prevailing. Files named _sp3 refit quarterly and _sp1 refit monthly. The rows are 365 origins × 16 Primaries × 672 half-hours × the number of seeds.

File Seeds Rows step1_ens_only_sp3, step2_ens_only_sp3, step3a_ens_only_sp3, step3b_pretrained_sp3, step4_pretrained_sp3 3 11,773,440 each step{5,6,7,8}w_with_injected_sp3, step{5,6,7,8}wo_without_injected_sp3 5 19,622,400 each step{5,6,7,8}w_with_injected_sp1, step{5,6,7,8}wo_without_injected_sp1 3 11,773,440 each

The checks run on every one of the 21 files were: no duplicate key over seed, time_series_id, power_fcst_init_time, and valid_time; no null quantile; no crossing quantile (each q column is at most the next); and UTC timestamps. All 21 files passed with 0 duplicates, 0 nulls, and 0 crossings. The weights that the fold scripts wrote are in each fold folder's work/models/ (682 .pt files, 131 MB in total). The settings and seeds are in the experiment folder, and its e00677_*.py files re-run every fit.

The score tables behind every number on this page are in scores/ of the same private folder, and the banks of injected shifts are in each fold folder's work/bank/. The figures are in this page's folder.

docs.title: Does feeding a probe's donor alarms into the recipient search of experiment 670 pair more injected load-transfer megawatts than the event table alone?
docs.text: Feeding the donor alarms of a probe into E1-J's recipient search pairs a little more of the transfer megawatts, but less than the predicted +0.10, so the graph line is closed at 15 Primaries. Experiment 678 tests whether the donor alarms of the probes of experiment 675 raise the pairing of the event table, on experiment 660's generator unchanged. It continues the graph line that experiment 672 closed under its stop rule and that the maintainer asked to reopen. The hybrid with the logistic regression's alarms (F-hyb) pairs 0.36 of the long and deep megawatts against 0.29 for E1-J (difference +0.08, 95% interval -0.00 to +0.17), and 0.32 against 0.25 in the medium and deep cell (+0.08, +0.03 to +0.13). The verdict is not supported: no hybrid reaches +0.10 in either deep cell.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• F-hyb, R-hyb, P-M-hyb, P-C-hyb. E1's event table plus one added downward donor event per alarm of the probe named, searched for recipients by experiment 670's search. The probes are experiment 675's: a logistic regression on the node inputs (F), a randomly initialised encoder (R), and encoders pretrained by masked reconstruction (P-M) and by causal prediction (P-C).
  • Primary, E1, arm C, noise unit. A Primary is a primary substation. E1 is the event table of experiment 653, which segments each Primary's residual into steps. Arm C is the demand forecast of experiment 327 whose residual E1 reads, and a noise unit is the block-difference noise of a Primary's residual in megawatts. The 15 Primaries and 40 scored worlds are those of experiment
  • The probes read a per-Primary, per-hour vector of 35 inputs (the residual, step statistics, and calendar terms).
  • Rewired placebo. The same hybrid on a degree-preserving rewired graph, with the draw out of 30 that keeps the fewest real links.
  • Cell, paired, found, E1-J. As in experiment 672. Paired is the MW-weighted share of injected edge-transfer ends whose decoded event has the right partner.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: The figure shows point estimates 0.03 to 0.08 above E1-J in the long and deep and the medium and deep cells, with the intervals of four of the eight deep-cell hybrids reaching zero, and all below the +0.10 bar. The logistic regression's lead over the random-init encoder is within the seed spread of the encoder.

docs.text:
• Paired share per cell, MW-weighted, with 95% intervals from resampling the 40 worlds (hybrids are means over 3 seeds, except F-hyb, which has one fit):

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text:
• P1 (F-hyb or R-hyb at least +0.10 in both deep cells): failed. F-hyb +0.08 and +0.08, R-hyb +0.06 and +0.05.
  • P2 (R-hyb at least +0.10): failed, as above.
  • P3 (F-hyb at least +0.05 in the long and shallow cell and +0.03 in the medium and shallow cell): failed (+0.01 and +0.03; the second is +0.027, short of +0.03).
  • P4 (false transfers at most 1.5 times E1-J's, 0.57): held for F-hyb (0.51), R-hyb (0.54), and P-C-hyb (0.46), and failed for P-M-hyb (0.58). Seeds range from 0.41 to 0.62 for R-hyb and 0.55 to 0.61 for P-M-hyb, so "held" rests on the mean.
  • P5 (the rewired placebo pairs at most a third of its hybrid in the deep cells): held (0.04 against 0.36, and 0.06 against 0.32).
  • Adoption bar (0.60 in both deep cells): not reached. The best hybrid pairs 0.36 and 0.32.
  • Reading of the verdict. The pre-registered +0.10 bar is missed on the point estimates, and F-hyb's upper interval limits (+0.17 and +0.13) do not rule it out.
  • Stop rule fires. No hybrid reaches +0.10 in either deep cell, so the graph line is closed at 15 Primaries and the edge-state network is not built.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Code review. A fresh Sonnet reviewer found no use of injected truth in the donor construction. Before any score was read, the plan and code were changed on its findings: the start-search window now matches the window in which experiment 675 credits an alarm (24 hours before to 12 hours after), an alarm near any E1 downward event of 4 noise units or more is skipped whether or not E1 paired it, a donor counts as permanent at 180 or more days of record left (experiment 653's rule), and donors added by earlier alarms count for the near-duplicate rule.
  • Known biases. The alarm thresholds are calibrated on the scored worlds with truth (above). The added donor's end is late by up to about 12 hours and is searched from 2 days after the start. Donor-found and false-transfer counts include added donors under 4 noise units, which the search ignores but the scoring can match. The real-graph hybrid and its rewired placebo have different added-donor lists, because E1's pairing differs on the two graphs. The donor start and end of each alarm were not scored separately. A post hoc rule for short events was not tried.
  • Audit. A fresh Sonnet reviewer re-derived the paired shares of E1-J, F-hyb, and R-hyb in the two deep cells and the false-transfer rates from the scored rows with its own code, found the bootstrap consistent across arms, and found no injected truth in the donor construction, apart from the alarm thresholds, which experiment 675 set on these 40 worlds so that each probe's false-donor rate equals E1-J's. The comparison is therefore at a matched alarm rate, not at a threshold that could be deployed.
  • Caveats. F-hyb is one fit, and the intervals resample worlds only, not fit variance. NGED's logs may miss load shifts, so matched logged shifts on the real record are lower bounds, and the injected start hours come from NGED's logged onsets up to 2026-07, as in experiments 670, 672, and 675. The probes are experiment 675's, trained on 200 worlds.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • The pre-registered stop rule closes the graph line at 15 Primaries. A donor probe is worth testing again only with a donor end that can be shorter than 2 days, and on the fleet-scale adjacency of about 1,161 Primaries; both are for the roadmap to decide.

docs.title: The plan as committed
docs.text:
The plan below was committed before any score was read. The code review changed it once, before any score was read, as the Checks section lists.

This is the plan, committed before any score is read. It continues the graph line that experiment 675 reopened, and which experiment 672 had closed under its stop rule. Experiment 675 found that masked pretraining did not help, and that neither did causal pretraining as designed (the causal arm finds 0.26 and 0.20 fewer donor megawatts than the random-init encoder in the two deep cells). The graph Discuss session therefore asked for the cheapest test of the finding that matters: a donor probe finds more long and deep donor megawatts than E1-J, so does that gain turn into more pairs?

docs.title: The question
docs.text: Experiment 675's step 0a showed that the donor, not the link to the recipient, is where E1-J loses the megawatts it finds at the recipient. The no-encoder logistic regression (F) found 0.63 of long and deep donor megawatts against E1-J's 0.44 (one fit, no interval for E1-J), and the random-init encoder (R) found 0.59 (seeds 0.46 to 0.70). The question here is whether adding those donors to E1-J's search lifts the paired share. F is the non-neural baseline that any neural donor head has to beat, so it is run beside R.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Probe scores. Experiment 675's stored probe scores for the 40 scored worlds: F (1 fit) and R, P-M, and P-C (3 seeds each). No probe is retrained, and no GPU time is used.
  • From an alarm to a donor event. Each alarm becomes a downward donor event whose start and end are measured on the arm-C residual by the rule in the decision rule above, with the size from experiment 670's step_size. An alarm near any E1 downward event of 4 noise units or more, or near an earlier added donor, adds nothing.
  • Recipient search. Experiment 670's search_recipients, unchanged, on E1's events plus the added donors, on the real graph. Placebos: the degree-preserving rewired graph of experiment 670 (rewire_low_overlap, the draw keeping the fewest real links, with the share kept reported) and an empty graph.
  • Scoring. Experiment 653's match and experiment 665's cell statistics, as in experiment 670, with world-resampled intervals. Decoded transfers matching no injected end are counted per Primary-year.
  • Reviews and running. A fresh Sonnet code review before the first run (checking that no injected truth enters the donor construction and that the probe scores are the stored ones), a results audit, a write-up review, and a prose review. CPU work runs under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue.
  • Inherited caveats. NGED's logs may miss load shifts, so matched logged shifts on the real record are lower bounds, and the injected start hours come from NGED's logged onsets up to 2026-07, as in experiments 670, 672, and 675.

docs.title: Does the linear probe lose recovery when the substation meter has power factor 1 and a small reactive floor?
docs.text:
Almost none: at half the midday reading, the linear probe recovers 0.73 of an added farm in the reactive-floor world, against 0.75 with no conversion at all. The median conversion loss is 0.5 percentage points (80% interval -1.0 to 7.7), where the power-factor 0.97 world that experiments 656, 662, and 671 used loses 10.7 points (7.8 to 17.1). The floor world matches NGED's statement of power factor 1 with some reactive power always present, so the 10-point loss was probably an overestimate for the five MVA Primaries whose midday reading never nears zero (D2, D3, D4, D19, D21). The pre-registered rule (under 5 points) is met on the point estimate; the verdict is supported.

We repeated experiment 662's test at 0.5 times the midday reading, the level that matches D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21. The six MW Primaries are converted to synthetic apparent power, a known farm is added, a neural network is trained, and the probe reads the farm's capacity. The conversion loss is the signed-world recovery minus the apparent-power-world recovery of the same farm, in percentage points. The headline loss is the median over the six Primaries of each Primary's own difference, so it can differ from the difference of the medians (0.746 minus 0.733 is 1.3). L0 is the linear probe of experiment 621, L1 is L0 on rows well above the reactive floor, and FA is a fold model that fits the reading as apparent power. This page covers 9 new neural networks (3 conditions of 3 seeds) beside 24 neural networks that experiment 662 trained (the twin and farm networks of 8 conditions, seeds 0 to 2), at the 2026-06 cutoff.

Figure: the loss is near zero in the floor and zero-reactive worlds and about 11 points in the power-factor world, for both linear probes. The fold model (FA) is not a fair comparison, because it reads above the signed world in the floor world (0.88 against 0.80) and below it in the zero-reactive world (0.77), so its losses are negative and carry no meaning.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Median over the six MW Primaries, 2026-06 cutoff, 3 seeds. Loss is in percentage points of recovery in megawatts; the interval is 80%.

Probe Level Signed recovery Power factor 0.97 loss Reactive-floor loss Zero-reactive loss L0 0.5 0.746 10.7 (7.8 to 17.1) 0.5 (-1.0 to 7.7) -0.5 (-3.3 to 6.8) L1 0.5 0.758 10.6 (8.4 to 17.5) 0.4 (-1.2 to 7.8) -0.4 (-3.3 to 6.7) FA 0.5 0.798 3.3 (-13.4 to 8.8) -14.1 (-28.0 to -6.7) -6.1 (-18.2 to -3.8) L0 1 0.777 24.3 (23.3 to 27.8) not run 8.7 (7.4 to 13.2) L1 1 0.787 9.4 (7.8 to 13.8) not run 3.1 (0.6 to 6.4) FA 1 0.596 -11.9 (-22.9 to -8.9) not run -1.1 (-9.9 to 1.2)
  • Which arm matches NGED's statement. The reactive-floor arm (constant reactive power 0.10 times the median sunny-midday reading) is the closest to power factor 1 with a small always-present floor. The zero-reactive arm is a bound.
  • Decision. The floor-arm L0 loss at 0.5 times is 0.5 points, under 5. We recommend that the NGED capacity page's calibration for the five MVA Primaries use the signed-world factor 0.68 alone, with the conversion loss stated as not distinguishable from zero on the point estimate at that level. Experiment 673's table is unchanged here; the edit is proposed in the pull request description.
  • Recovery in energy. The factor from MW to energy is 1.00 to 1.10 per Primary (median about 1.07), so energy recovery at 0.5 times is 0.79 (floor, L0) against 0.80 signed and 0.67 (power factor 0.97). The loss in energy points is 0.6 (floor), -0.6 (zero), and 11.5 (power factor 0.97). The factor compares the standard unit curve averaged over donor weather with the fleet shape on the probe dates, so the factor is approximate.
  • Per Primary (L0, 0.5 times, floor arm). D9 1.0, D11 0.1, D14 -0.5, D16 -3.6, D5 104.7, and D10 73.3 points. D5 and D10 have midday readings near 1 MW, so the 2.0 MW injection floor puts every world past the fold there, as experiment 662 found; the median of six is the mean of the middle two values (D11 0.1 and D9 1.0).
  • Interval caveat. The interval is an 80% interval from independent draws of the day-block bootstrap and the between-seed spread of each recovery, so the interval is probably wider than the true interval of the difference. The interval's upper end (7.7) is above the 5-point line, so a loss up to about 8 points is not excluded.
  • Fold model. FA reads above the signed world in the floor world at 0.5 times (0.88 against 0.80). Experiment 662 found the fold model an unfair signed-world denominator, so the FA rows are for completeness and carry no verdict.
  • Not run. Native worlds at the five MVA Primaries in the floor arm: experiment 662's code builds no floor-arm worlds at those five Primaries, so the read needs a code change that this experiment does not make. The floor arm at 1 times was not rerun (experiment 673 has it).
  • Code. ml-experiments/00679-pv-mva-conversion-loss-reactive-floor-at-half-level/ calls experiment 662's fit and probe code (folder ml-experiments/00662-pv-probe-through-the-mva-fold-matched-level-redesign/), and edits none of it. The new networks are in the private folder work/pretrained/2026-06/; the twins and the signed and power-factor networks are links to experiment 662's.
  • Compute. The 9 fits took 21 to 31 s each on the GPU (cuda, one process), about 4 minutes in all; the probes ran on the CPU. Fits are not forecasts, so no refit cadence applies.
  • Weather. ERA5 and CAMS, as in experiment 662; the probe is a diagnostic, so forecast-time availability does not apply. Development months only (nothing from 2026-07-01).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The reactive power of the real meters is unknown. The floor level (0.10 times the midday reading) and the power-factor 0.97 level are both assumptions.
  • Three seeds and six Primaries, two of which (D5, D10) behave differently from the other four.
  • One set of farms and one neural network architecture.
  • NGED's event labels are incomplete, so the clean rows may hold unlabelled events.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Forecast checks: the experiment scores no forecast, so the median-minus-mean and quantile-score checks do not apply.
  • Code review (Sonnet, before the first fit and again before the report): the script that points experiment 662's code at this experiment's folder reaches every file path; linked weights are never overwritten (a link-existence check was added); targets and rows match experiment 662's (the world files are byte-identical). The report review found no error in the loss pairing or the interval; its asks to assert that all conditions were probed with bootstrap draws and to restrict the seeds were applied. Its note on the energy factor (different weather in numerator and denominator) was accepted as a caveat.
  • Audit triggers that fired: none of the seven apply to a probe experiment that scores no forecast; the pre-registered rule was not changed.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: Does the same near-zero loss hold at the five MVA Primaries' own native worlds, which needs a floor arm in the native-world builder? And does the fold model, with a night prior, stay unbiased at 0.5 times in the floor world?

docs.title: Does a search that also starts from each unpaired rise, and looks for the matching fall at a neighbouring Primary, pair more injected load-transfer megawatts than the one-way search of experiment 670?
docs.text:
Searching from each unpaired rise for the matching fall at a neighbouring Primary pairs 0.38 of the injected transfer megawatts in the long and deep cell, against 0.29 for the one-way search of experiment 670. The gain of 0.09 is just under the 0.10 needed to adopt the search, and the search adds 442 decoded transfers, most of which match no injected end. A Primary substation steps electricity down to a local distribution network. A load transfer moves part of one Primary's demand (the donor) onto a neighbour (the recipient). Experiments 672 and 676 closed the neural-network graph-learning approach at 15 Primaries; the search in this experiment uses no neural network. A noise unit is a Primary's usual difference between successive 6-hour means. The long, medium, and short cells are over 7 days, 1 to 7 days, and 1 day or less, and deep means 8 noise units or more, as in experiment 670. Found means an injected event has a decoded event at the right Primary, sign, and start; paired means the decoded donor and recipient are the right two Primaries.

E1-J-sym adds the mirror search: start at each unpaired rise, and look for the matching fall at a neighbour. Experiment 670's search (E1-J) starts at a large fall and looks for the rise at a neighbour. Experiment 675 found that the donor is the bottleneck. This experiment adds the mirror search (E1-J-sym): it starts at each rise of 4 noise units or more that is still unpaired, and looks for a fall of 2 noise units or more that starts up to 36 half-hours before that rise (the window is widened by 6 half-hours on each side to allow for start error). The verdict is partly supported: both deep-cell differences exceed +0.05, neither reaches +0.10. The pre-registered stage 1 rule (adopt at +0.10 in both deep cells, otherwise continue) therefore sends the line on to part 2, a model that reconstructs both Primaries' residuals jointly from flows on the edges between Primaries.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Gate passed. E1-J, re-run here on the same 40 default worlds (seeds 900 to 939), reproduces experiment 670's paired share in every cell to four decimals.
  • Paired share, E1-J-sym minus E1-J (95% interval from resampling worlds): long and deep +0.094 (0.043 to 0.151); medium and deep +0.071 (0.025 to 0.139); long and shallow +0.076 (0.038 to 0.117); medium and shallow +0.028 (0.004 to 0.061); short and deep +0.003 (0.0 to 0.011); short and shallow +0.003 (0.0 to 0.011).
  • Absolute paired share, E1-J-sym: long and deep 0.379 (0.281 to 0.500); medium and deep 0.316 (0.186 to 0.478); long and shallow 0.263; medium and shallow 0.159; short and deep 0.083; short and shallow 0.030.
  • Found share barely moves (long and deep 0.503 to 0.515). Donor megawatts found in the long and deep cell rise from 0.441 to 0.481, and in the medium and deep cell from 0.399 to 0.434. Most of the gain is therefore pairing of donors that the event table already held.
  • Decoded transfers. E1-J-sym decodes 1230 transfers with 283 correct ends, against 788 and 220 for E1-J. The 63 additional correct ends come with 442 additional decoded transfers.
  • Placebo. On a rewired graph E1-J-sym pairs 0.057 (long and deep) and 0.064 (medium and deep), with 730 decoded transfers and 39 correct ends. The gain depends on the real graph.
  • Robustness. On 20 long-heavy worlds the long and deep difference is +0.043 (0.019 to 0.072); in short-heavy worlds it is +0.018 (0.0 to 0.054), whose interval includes zero, and in constant-MW square worlds +0.083 (0.010 to 0.193). The rest is in injected_by_cell.json.

docs.title: Real record
docs.text:
• Decoded transfers (2024-01 to 2026-06, 36.0 Primary-years): 8 for E1-J, 12 for E1-J-sym, 0 for E1-J-sym on the stored rewired graph (median 2 over 100 rewired graphs, which keep 15.7% of the real links), or 0.22 and 0.33 per Primary-year for E1-J and E1-J-sym.
  • Verified D5 to D16 transfer (December 2025): kept in the right direction, with the same late starts and ends as E1-J (D5 start 24 hours late, D16 start 12.5 hours late, both ends 24 hours late), so the symmetric search adds nothing there.
  • Logged shifts longer than 1 day (77 in the scored years): 9 of 77 have an event start within 2 hours (E1-J: 8) and 19 within 24 hours (E1-J: 18). NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so every count of real events here is a lower bound.
  • Event-free time: neither method calls a transfer in the 27.6 Primary-years more than 14 days from any logged or verified event.

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• Held: long and shallow +0.03 (got +0.076); medium and shallow +0.02 (+0.028); short cells no worse than -0.03; rewired graph at a third or fewer of the real record's transfers; D5 to D16 kept.
  • Did not hold: long and deep +0.10 (+0.094); medium and deep +0.10 (+0.071); donor megawatts found 0.54 or more (0.481).

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Code: ml-experiments/00680-event-table-reconstruction-from-edge-flows-part-1-symmetric-search/, importing the folders of experiments 653, 660, 665, and 670. Unchanged from experiment 670: the panel, the residual, the worlds, the cells, and the found and paired definitions.
  • Thresholds, fixed in the plan: rise at least 4 noise units; donor fall at least 2 noise units; donor start from 42 half-hours before to 6 half-hours after the rise; share 0.3 to 2.0; loose conservation cost at most 2.5. No tuning was done.
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet code review ran before the first scored run. It found that the gate only printed, that the stage 1 branch letters were swapped against the plan, that the verdict rule was not encoded, and that the conservation cost used the found donor's step where experiment 670 uses the anchor event's step. All four were fixed before the scored run.
  • Compute: CPU only, about 7 seconds per world on one core, under 10 minutes in all.
  • Not used: the final-test window from 2026-07-01 is never read, and no NGED generator is named.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: Whether a joint reconstruction of both Primaries' residuals by an edge flow, with a fixed cost per change, pairs more megawatts than E1-J-sym without adding as many transfers that match no injected end (part 2).

docs.title: Do extra lagged power inputs make the prevailing output of the two-output demand network react faster to a load shift, without worsening the NRA output?
docs.text:
Giving the prevailing head 8 to 14 extra lagged power inputs makes the prevailing output react about 20 hours sooner to the start of an injected load shift and about 8 hours sooner to its end, and does not raise the event-free CRPS. The head was trained on injected shifts from the same generator. Over 1152 injected load shifts in the six development folds, the first origin at which the prevailing median has moved half-way to the new level comes 20.4 hours earlier with the 14-input set L3 (95% interval 16.3 to 24.8 hours) and 19.1 hours earlier with the 8-input set L1. Neither placebo gains anything: lags taken from another Primary change the reaction by -1.6 hours, and the same lags read 7 days earlier by +2.3 hours. The gain is under the 24 hours this experiment set in advance as worth porting, so the verdict is a small gain.

A load shift is a transfer of load between Primaries that the metered power contains and the normal-running (NRA) output deliberately ignores. The prevailing output is a separate small neural network, the head of experiment 667, that reads the Candidate's frozen NRA quantiles and a set of origin features and decides how much of a recent shift to carry forward. Its lagged inputs stop at the 24-hour and 7-day lags. This experiment adds more recent lags (6 to 72 hours before the origin, all at least 6 hours old) to that head only, so the NRA output is unchanged by construction.

docs.title: Headline numbers
docs.text:
• Scope. Six development folds (2026-01 to 2026-06), 16 Primaries, daily origins at 09:00, 14-day forecasts. The final-test window (from 2026-07-01) is not read. Every arm is the mean of two seeds, as in experiment 667. Retraining is monthly. No GPU was used.
  • Reaction time on injected events (experiment 660's generator as built into experiment 667's bank; 1152 events, 192 per fold, paired with L0; mean paired difference with a 95% interval from a bootstrap over events; origins are daily, so each time resolves to 24 hours):
Arm Extra inputs Start: paired events Start: difference (hours) End: difference (hours) L1 8 879 -19.1 (-23.1 to -15.3) -7.9 (-9.8 to -6.1) L2 11 873 -18.7 (-22.9 to -14.7) -8.8 (-10.8 to -6.9) L3 14 881 -20.4 (-24.8 to -16.3) -8.1 (-10.0 to -6.2) P (other Primary) 14 862 -1.6 (-5.5 to +2.4) -0.6 (-2.1 to +0.8) P7 (7 days earlier) 14 871 +2.3 (-0.7 to +5.3) -0.2 (-1.7 to +1.2)
  • Share of injected events that react at all. L0 reacts to 78.3% of events after the start and 45.6% after the end; L3 reacts to 82.7% and 45.8%. Events that never react before they end or before the data stop are excluded from the paired differences (the paired counts are in the table).
  • Verified D5 and D16 transfer (2 events, origins from 2026-01-01 only). At D5 the first reacting origin comes 201 hours after the start with L0 and 81 hours with L2 and L3 (129 hours with L1); the placebos give 225 hours. The end moves from 57 hours (L0) to 33 hours (L1 to L3). At D16 the start stays at 81 hours for L0 to L3 and P (129 hours for P7), and the end stays at 57 hours for every arm. Two events support no interval and no general statement.
  • Score, event-free rows more than 14 days from any event (CRPS in points of capacity, 1.78 million half-hours): NRA 3.45 to 4.52 by lead band, L0 4.092, L3 4.042 pooled. The paired difference L3 minus L0 is -0.050 (95% interval -0.119 to +0.000, blocks of Primary and month); the placebo P is -0.021 (-0.059 to +0.007). Normalised MAE of the median: L3 minus L0 is -0.098 points (-0.226 to -0.002).
  • Score, all rows (1.92 million half-hours; CRPS): NRA 4.161, L0 4.079, L1 4.055, L2 4.057, L3 4.028, P 4.058, P7 4.049. By lead band L3 scores 3.08, 3.43, 3.89, and 4.39 (days 0 to 1, 1 to 3, 3 to 7, 7 to 14) against 3.18, 3.50, 3.93, and 4.43 for L0. The q05 to q95 band covers 0.89, 0.88, 0.86, and 0.85 of observed power (L3), against a nominal 0.90.
  • Inside the real events (the 2 verified transfers and the event-table events of experiment 653 that last over 7 days; 1,836 to 13,086 half-hours per band): L3 scores 3.55, 4.56, 6.32, and 6.73 against 3.64, 4.49, 6.30, and 6.61 for L0, so L3 gains 0.09 at days 0 to 1 and loses 0.07, 0.02, and 0.12 at days 1 to 3, 3 to 7, and 7 to 14. L1 scores 3.69, 4.76, 6.71, and 6.91, worse than L0 in every band, and L2 scores 3.53, 4.59, 6.50, and 6.81. The NRA output scores 6.29, 6.56, 7.03, and 6.44, and covers only 0.38 to 0.48 of observed power.
  • Cost of false alarms. The share of event-free rows on which the prevailing median departs from the NRA median by 3 points of capacity or more is 0.1165 for L0 and 0.1144 for L3 (0.1031 for L1, 0.1200 for P, 0.1226 for P7).
  • Tails (prevailing output, all rows; share of observed power below the quantile, then pinball loss in points of capacity): q01 0.021 and 0.226 (L3; L0 0.021 and 0.229); q05 0.081 and 0.866; q95 0.940 and 1.035; q99 0.985 and 0.295. The lags do not change the tail calibration.
  • Injected events by stage (CRPS of the prevailing output against the shifted power, L3 minus L0): before the onset or no event -0.16; in force -0.65; ended in the last 24 hours -1.02; in the last 3 days before the end +0.33 (3.2 million, 5.4 million, 0.17 million, and 0.53 million half-hours). The lags help at the start and in the middle of a shift and cost a little near its end.

docs.title: Arms, method, and checks
docs.text:
• Arms. L0 is experiment 667's head as stored; a refit reproduces its real-row quantiles with a maximum difference of 0 (the gate for every other arm). L1 adds the residual power at 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, and 72 hours before the origin; L2 adds the means of the last 6, 12, and 24 hours; L3 adds the differences of consecutive trailing 24-hour means. A lag is the cleaned power minus the Candidate's lag-free median at that time, as a fraction of capacity, with a missing flag per input. P reads another Primary of the same metering group that is no electrical neighbour (a fixed map); P7 reads L3's own lags 7 days earlier. The placebo reads the other Primary's cleaned power with no injected shift, so it controls for extra capacity and not for a shift in the placebo Primary.
  • Data delay. No input reads power newer than 6 hours before the origin; a test perturbs every later half-hour and checks that no input moves (and that moving the 6-hour half-hour does).
  • Bank rows. The injected shift enters the new lags exactly as it enters the target, and L0's existing lag features are built from the same shifted series. The regenerated injected events match experiment 667's stored table for every fold month.
  • Code reused. Experiment 667's p667_fit.py, p667_data.py, and p667_head.py run unchanged (folder ml-experiments/00667-*/prevailing), with experiments 647, 650, and 668.
  • Fallback months. November and December 2025 use the fallback hazard head with no trained weights, so no arm changes them and no arm is scored there. The D5 start in the transfer, 29 December, falls in a fallback month, so only the first origins of January carry the start reaction.
  • Pre-registered conditions. P2 (NRA unchanged) holds. P3 holds: the false-alarm share is lower with L3, not higher. P4 holds: P gains 1.6 hours (under a tenth of L3's 20.4) and P7 loses 2.3 hours, well under the third pre-registered. P1 fails by its size: the gain on injected events is 20 hours, not the 24 hours pre-registered, and the 95% interval reaches 24.8 hours at its upper end. The D5 gain of 120 hours is real but one event. The veto (an event-free CRPS cost above 0.03) is not triggered.
  • Audit triggers. None fires: no control fails (the placebos gain nothing); P1's size miss is plausibly due to the 24-hour resolution and to censoring, not to a method fault (untested); the CRPS and median-error contrasts agree in sign; leaving any one Primary out of the injected start contrast moves it between -21.5 and -17.5 hours for L1 to L3 and +1.8 to +3.1 hours for P7; the placebo moves the event-free CRPS by -0.021, inside its own half-width of 0.033.
  • Not computed. The median minus mean forecast per site and the curtailment cost are not computed.

docs.title: Reusing the L3 head
docs.text:
• The L3 lag set (14 inputs, each as a residual plus a missing flag, so 28 columns). For a Primary and a forecast origin, with every time in hours before the origin and every value the cleaned power minus the Candidate's lag-free median at that time, as a fraction of capacity: columns 0 to 7 are the residuals at 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, and 72 hours; columns 8 to 10 are the means over the last 6, 12, and 24 hours ending 6 hours before the origin; columns 11 to 13 are the differences between consecutive trailing 24-hour means (the 24 hours ending 6 hours before the origin minus the 24 hours before that, then the next two pairs). A mean is missing when under half of its window is finite. The code is e00681_lags.py (lag_block).
  • The head recipe. Experiment 667's survival-hazard head (p667_head.HazardHead: two hidden layers of 64 units, outputs a depth, a spread, and 14 daily hazards) with its inputs widened by the 28 lag columns, appended after experiment 667's columns. Everything else is experiment 667's recipe, unchanged: its training months, its pre-training chain, the loss and optimiser of experiments 647 and 652, and two seeds averaged. e00681_fit.py wraps experiment 667's p667_fit.fit_rhaz and changes only its input loader. The fitted heads are in fits/L3/ of the experiment's private data folder.
  • Folds fitted: 6 of the 12 monthly folds of experiment 667. The folds are 2026-01 to 2026-06. The missing folds are 2025-11 and 2025-12, which use the fallback hazard head with no trained weights (so there is no head to widen), and 2026-07 to 2026-10, the final-test window, which this experiment does not read. The lag blocks and the head fits for those four months need only e00681_lags.py MONTH and run_arm.sh L3 14 MONTH; experiment 667's banks and Candidate quantiles for them already exist.
  • Fit time per head. 34 to 95 seconds per head and seed (including the prediction pass) on one CPU thread with four fits running at once; the longer times are the later folds, which train on more months. All 12 L3 head fits (6 folds, 2 seeds) take about 12 minutes of one thread. The lag blocks take about 1 minute per month.
  • Leakage check. Every lag is at least 6 hours older than the origin. lag_block asserts that the newest half-hour any input reads is the origin minus 12 half-hours, and selftest adds 123 to every half-hour newer than that for 200 real origins and checks that no input moves (and moves the half-hour at that limit to confirm that the test can detect a change). A head for fold M trains only on the real and injected rows of earlier months, with valid times before the first day of M.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• The conclusions rest on injected events. The generator that builds the injected events also built the bank on which the head trains, so the head meets familiar shapes: exact steps with no measurement noise. Only 2 real events can be read, and one (D16) does not change.
  • The event labels are an incomplete dump. NGED says load shifts may be missing from its logs, so the event-free rows hold unlabelled events and every real count is a lower bound.
  • The event-table events have no reaction time. The events of experiment 653 carry no fitted transfer, so they appear only in the inside-event scores, and only the 2 verified transfers have a real reaction time.
  • Proportional injected events. For an event whose shift scales with the Primary's power, the half-of-the-depth threshold is approximate. It is the same for every arm.
  • Reaction time resolves to 24 hours. The daily origins make the 20-hour mean difference a mixture of 0-day and 1-day steps.
  • Mean reaction times on the figure use only events that react, so they exclude the 17% of events that never react after the start and the 54% that never agree again after the end.
  • The weather inputs are unchanged. Lags use cleaned power only; nothing here needs ERA5, so no past-weather ceiling applies.
  • Next, for the maintainer to choose. Settle the choice between L1 and L3 on more real events, and test whether the loss near the end of a shift (+0.33) goes away when the head also reads the age of the departure. A port needs one check on the final-test months.

docs.title: Does choosing edge flows by a fixed cost per change pair more injected load-transfer megawatts than the searches of experiments 670 and 680, without adding more false transfers?
docs.text:
Choosing edge flows by a fixed cost per change does not pair injected load transfers better than the simple searches of experiments 670 and 680: it pairs 0.33 of the long and deep transfer megawatts, against 0.29 and 0.38, and it decodes 2990 transfers of which only 329 ends are correct. A Primary substation steps electricity down to a local distribution network. A load transfer moves part of one Primary's demand (the donor) onto a neighbour (the recipient). An edge joins two neighbouring Primaries, and an edge flow is the megawatts that move along it. Experiments 672 and 676 closed the neural-network graph-learning approach at 15 Primaries; E1-F uses no neural network.

The terms of the line are these. E1 is the event table of experiment 653, a list of steps at each Primary. E1-J adds a search for a recipient from each large fall (experiment 670), and E1-J-sym adds a search for a donor from each rise (experiment 680). A noise unit is a Primary's usual difference between successive 6-hour means. The long, medium, and short cells are over 7 days, 1 to 7 days, and 1 day or less. Deep means 8 noise units or more, and shallow means 2 to 8. Found means an injected event has a decoded event at the right Primary, sign, and start. Paired means the decoded donor and recipient are the right two Primaries. F-hyb and R-hyb are the donor-probe hybrids of experiment 678.

E1-F decides every pair of opposite steps at two connected Primaries by cost. E1-F compares the saving in change cost with the misfit of one common flow (the donor's step and the recipient's step must roughly match, with a prior on their ratio), and takes the largest savings first. Either end can propose the other. The verdict is not supported: stop rule (a) of the decision rule closes the edge-flow line at 15 Primaries, because E1-F misses E1-J + 0.10 in both deep cells. Stop rule (b) also trips, because the all-pairs graph's false-transfer share is only 0.068 below E1-F's, inside the 0.10 tolerance.

docs.title: Results (40 default worlds)
docs.text:
• Gate passed. E1-F with no edges has the same found share as experiment 670's E1 in every cell, to four decimals (long and deep 0.488).
  • Paired share: long and deep: E1-F 0.327 (0.228 to 0.455), E1-J 0.286, E1-J-sym 0.379. Medium and deep: E1-F 0.272 (0.163 to 0.403), E1-J 0.245, E1-J-sym 0.316.
  • E1-F minus E1-J (95% interval): long and deep +0.041 (-0.041 to 0.124); medium and deep +0.027 (-0.048 to 0.113); long and shallow +0.097 (0.037 to 0.150); medium and shallow +0.090 (0.032 to 0.154). E1-F minus E1-J-sym: long and deep -0.053 (-0.113 to 0.000); medium and deep -0.045 (-0.120 to 0.029).
  • Donor megawatts found, long and deep: E1-F 0.491, E1-J 0.441, E1-J-sym 0.481.
  • Decoded transfers and correct ends. The false-transfer share is one minus the correct ends over the decoded transfers. E1-F decodes 2990 transfers with 329 correct ends (share 0.89); E1-J 788 and 220 (0.72); E1-J-sym 1230 and 283 (0.77).
  • Placebos. E1-F on a rewired graph pairs 0.022 and 0.053 in the two deep cells (2310 transfers, 44 correct ends). E1-F on all pairs pairs 0.316 and 0.257 (7099 transfers, 301 correct ends, share 0.96). E1-F on the real edges is therefore only 0.011 and 0.015 above the all-pairs graph, and its false-transfer share is 0.068 lower, under the 0.10 predicted.
  • Costs. The tuning rule chose c_edge 2 and delta 8. None of the 25 pairs met the constraint of a false-transfer share no higher than E1-J's (0.75 on the validation worlds), so the highest paired share was used. All 25 pairs gave a share of 0.876 to 0.884.
  • Cross-injector check. Tuning on constant-MW square worlds chose the same costs, so the drop is zero by construction. On 20 constant-MW square worlds E1-F minus E1-J is +0.036 (-0.171 to 0.303) long and deep and +0.302 (0.161 to 0.473) medium and deep, the one interval that excludes zero. On long-heavy worlds the differences are +0.003 and +0.040, and on short-heavy worlds +0.020 and +0.101; those intervals include zero.

docs.title: Post hoc grids (not pre-registered)
docs.text:
Because the planned grid gave nearly the same false-transfer share at every pair, two more grids were run on the same validation worlds, and the best pair of each was scored on the 40 default worlds.

  • Wide grid: c_edge 8, 16, or 32 and delta 8, 16, 32, or 64. No pair met the constraint (best share 0.875). The chosen pair (c_edge 8, delta 64) pairs 0.349 and 0.293 in the two deep cells (+0.063 and +0.048 over E1-J, intervals -0.016 to 0.148 and -0.019 to 0.135), with 3008 decoded transfers and 348 correct ends. In E1-F a larger cost for a step that stands alone raises the saving from merging, so this grid ran in the direction that cannot restrict merges.
  • Low grid: c_edge 0, 0.5, or 1 and delta 0, 0.1, or 0.25. No pair met the constraint (shares 0.884 to 0.897). The chosen pair (c_edge 0, delta 0.25) pairs 0.314 and 0.257, with 2858 decoded transfers and 307 correct ends, and the all-pairs graph pairs 0.302 and 0.174.

Costs from 0 to 64 therefore left the false-transfer share between 0.88 and 0.90. The costs of E1-F do not separate a true pair from a coincident pair. The misfit term, the compatibility rule, and the candidate steps were not varied.

docs.title: Real record
docs.text:
• Decoded transfers (2024-01 to 2026-06, 36.0 Primary-years): E1-F 17; E1-J 8; E1-F on the stored rewired graph 4, with a median of 6 over 100 rewired graphs; E1-F on all pairs 30. NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so every count of real events is a lower bound.
  • Verified D5 to D16 transfer (December 2025): one flow with D5 as the donor (-1.08 MW) and D16 as the recipient (+1.28 MW, a share of 1.19), the same pair as E1-J found. Both starts are late (D5 by 24 hours, D16 by 12.5 hours), and both ends are 24 hours late, so the pre-registered bars of 6 hours at the start and 12 hours at the end do not hold. The donor amplitude is under the 1.2 to 2.2 MW range.
  • Logged shifts longer than 1 day (77 in the scored years): 10 have an event start within 2 hours (E1-J: 8, from experiment 670) and 21 within 24 hours (E1-J: 18).
  • Event-free time (27.6 Primary-years more than 14 days from a logged or verified event): E1-F calls three transfers; E1-F on all pairs calls 11.

docs.title: Pre-registered predictions
docs.text:
• Held:
    • Long and shallow E1-J + 0.05: +0.097.
    • Medium and shallow E1-J + 0.03: +0.090.
    • Short cells no worse than E1-J - 0.03.
    • Paired share on all pairs no more than 0.03 below E1-F: 0.011 and 0.015 below.
    • E1-F on the stored rewired graph calls a third or fewer of E1-F's real-record transfers: 4 of 17. The median over 100 rewired graphs is 6, just over a third.
    • D5 to D16: one flow with D5 as the donor, a share of 1.19, and D16 at 1.28 MW.
  • Did not hold:
    • Long and deep paired 0.39 or more: 0.327. Medium and deep 0.35 or more: 0.272.
    • Three points above the better hybrid in both deep cells (about 0.36 and 0.33).
    • Donor megawatts found 0.54 or more: 0.491.
    • E1-F minus E1-J-sym +0.05: -0.053 and -0.045.
    • False-transfer share 0.10 below all pairs: 0.068 below.
    • Rewired pairs 0.05 or less: 0.022 and 0.053.
    • No-edges found share within 0.03 of E1-F: 0.039 and 0.044 below.
    • D5 to D16 start and end timing, and the donor amplitude of 1.2 MW or more.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Code: ml-experiments/00682-event-table-reconstruction-from-edge-flows-part-2-change-cost-model/, importing the folders of experiments 653, 660, 665, 670, and 680. The panel, residual, worlds, cells, and the found and paired definitions are unchanged. E1-J and E1-J-sym are read from the stored rows of experiments 670 and 680.
  • Steps and costs. E1-F uses E1's steps of 2 noise units or more, plus the opposite step that each proposes at each connected Primary. A step that stands alone costs c_edge + delta. An edge flow costs c_edge plus 1 for each recipient beyond the first. The misfit is half the squared distance, in noise units, from the best common amplitude and share (a share between 0.3 and 2.0 on a 24-point grid, with a normal prior on its logarithm of mean log 0.8 and standard deviation 0.5). E1-F does not build the segment-boundary search with end moves, ramps, or a routine-step cost, and uses E1's own segment boundaries.
  • Tuning. The costs were tuned on 60 validation worlds (seeds 20000 to 20059, events from 2023-07-01 to 2023-12-31, readings after 2023-12-31 hidden).
  • Reviews. A fresh Sonnet code review ran before the first scored run. The review found that a flow made only of proposed steps crashed reconstruct, that tuning counted correct ends differently for E1-J and E1-F, that validation truth ran past the hidden readings, that the fitted share was not stored, and that the fallback was not recorded; all were fixed. A bug in the real-record run (noise units from the wrong residual) was found afterwards and fixed before the real-record numbers above. A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the results and the write-up; it found two wrong cost-grid figures, a wrongly marked prediction, a misleading description of the all-pairs comparison, and an unsupported conclusion from the wide grid, and all were corrected.
  • Compute: CPU only, 2 cores, under 1 hour. The final-test window from 2026-07-01 is never read. No NGED generator is named.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The remaining gap is information that the power of the 15 Primaries may not carry: which neighbour received the load. One option is a source of that information, such as NGED's records of which circuits were switched. This experiment does not test whether another model fitted to the same residuals would do better.

docs.text:

docs.title: Can a scale on the width of the stored quantile bands, fitted only on earlier months, bring the q05-to-q95 coverage of the one-year backtest files to 90%?
docs.text:
Widening the stored quantile bands by a factor fitted on earlier months brings four of five outputs close to the 90% coverage their q05 and q95 quantiles promise, and leaves the normal-running Primaries output at 87%. The stored files hold the one-year backtest forecasts of experiments 666, 667, and 669: 16 Primaries (primary substations, each with a normal-running output, which assumes the usual network configuration, and a prevailing output, which assumes the configuration in force at the forecast origin), 2 bulk supply points, 2 grid supply points, 3 wind farms, and 6 solar farms. We multiplied the distance of every quantile from the median forecast by a scale, fitted separately for each series, output, and lead band on the 90 days of actual power that were known when each month started. We then counted how often the actual power fell between the q05 and q95 quantiles. Of those five outputs (the two Primaries outputs, the two kinds of supply point, and solar), four were too narrow and now come within 2 points of 90% on origin months 2025-12 to 2026-06: the prevailing Primaries output (88.0% to 88.4% across the four lead bands, stored 84.0% to 87.9%), the bulk supply points (89.8% to 90.9%, stored 87.5% to 89.3%), the grid supply points (89.1% to 89.8%, stored 86.4% to 90.3%), and solar (89.4% to 91.0%, stored 87.8% to 89.5%). Wind was already above 90% and the scale does not improve it. The normal-running Primaries output rose from 82.4% to 84.5% to 87.1%, and its continuous ranked probability score (CRPS, a measure of the whole forecast distribution, here in percent of each series' capacity) rose by 0.081 points, from 4.23. The normal-running Primaries also fell to 80.1% in December and 80.3% in January, which triggers the stop rule that we set in advance: if pooled normal-running Primaries coverage stays below 86% in any month, the width of the bands is not the whole problem. The method applies the calibration idea of experiment 630, which fitted a shift and a rescale of the upper tail on earlier months.

Verdict: partly supported. The 5 stored files and 4 lead bands give 20 combinations (the Primaries count once, as normal running). In 16 of them, arm 2 brings coverage within 3 points of 90% and raises CRPS by no more than 0.05 points of capacity. The other four are the normal-running Primaries in each lead band, which fail on the CRPS limit. Numbers are from the origin months 2025-12 to 2026-06 ("before July") unless a line says otherwise. The origin months from 2026-07 are the final-test window, described and never used to choose.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Arm 0: the stored file.
  • Arm 1: the distance of every quantile from q50 (the median) multiplied by 1.0934, the factor that experiment 613 fixed.
  • Arm 2: the distance of every quantile from q50 multiplied by a scale fitted per series, output, and lead band (days 0 to 1, 1 to 3, 3 to 7, 7 to 14 after the forecast origin). At the start of each origin month, the scale is the 90th percentile of the ratio of the actual power's distance from q50 to the stored half-width of the band on that side (q95 - q50 above, q50 - q05 below). That choice makes the scaled band cover 90% of the fitting rows. The fitting rows are the half-hours whose valid time lies in the 90 days ending 6 hours before the month starts, because power is available only up to 6 hours before an origin.
  • Arm 3: arm 2 plus a per-series level shift on every quantile, the median of the actual power minus q50 over the same fitting rows.
  • Clipping. After each arm, the quantiles of MVA series (series measured in megavolt-amperes), wind, and solar are clipped at zero.
  • Rows. Cleaned observed power as in experiments 666 to 669 (wind idle half-hours set to zero; solar daylight only). The scored set is the origin months 2025-12 to 2026-10, because 2025-11 has no earlier forecast to fit on: 3,574,946 half-hours per Primaries output, 448,098 at bulk supply points, 448,406 at grid supply points, 651,550 for wind, and 644,760 for solar. Experiment 668 scored 3,893,864 half-hours per Primaries output over all 12 origin months, against 3,897,273 here, because it also required finite manual-heuristic and climatology forecasts.
  • Every "X% to Y%" range in this page is a range over the four lead bands, and every "interval" is a 95% day-block bootstrap interval over forecast-origin days.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Pooled q05-to-q95 coverage by lead band, for each arm and file, on the months before July. The dashed line is the nominal 90%. Wind and solar are pooled over farms.

Pooled normal-running coverage of the 16 Primaries per origin month, all lead bands. In this figure the dashed line is the 86% stop line and the solid line is 90%.

Days 10 to 14 band width at each month start, over its value in the last seven origins of the month before, for the eight Primaries of the refit question. The grey band is the 5th to 95th percentile of the ratio between the two seeds of one fold in experiment 667 (0.89 to 1.10).

One 14-day forecast (origin 2026-01-14 12:00 UTC) of Primaries 13 and 17: stored on the left, arm 2 on the right. Blue is the median, with the 50% and 90% bands; orange is the observed power.

The first day of the same forecasts.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Normal-running Primaries. Coverage is 82.4% to 84.5% stored, 86.0% to 87.6% under arm 1, 87.1% under arm 2, and 82.8% to 83.6% under arm 3. CRPS changes against the stored file are -0.027 under arm 1 (interval -0.031 to -0.023), +0.081 under arm 2 (0.064 to 0.099), and +0.306 under arm 3 (0.253 to 0.362) points of capacity.
  • Prevailing Primaries. Arm 2 coverage is 88.0% to 88.4% (stored 84.0% to 87.9%), and CRPS rises by 0.047 (0.039 to 0.055).
  • Bulk supply points. Arm 2 coverage is 89.8% to 90.9%, and CRPS rises by 0.005 (-0.001 to 0.011). Grid supply points: 89.1% to 89.8%, +0.003 (-0.012 to 0.017). Solar: 89.4% to 91.0%, -0.002 (-0.006 to 0.002). Wind: 90.4% to 92.0%, +0.007 (0.000 to 0.015).
  • Closer to 90% than the stored file. Arm 2 is closer in 20 of the 24 combinations of file and lead band (the two Primaries outputs count as two files). Arm 1 is closer in fewer, because it overshoots wind, solar, and the supply points. Arm 3 is not preferred over arm 2, because its CRPS is worse by 0.23 to 0.84 points.
  • Stop rule fired. Pooled normal-running Primaries coverage under arm 2 is 80.1% in 2025-12 (the scale is fitted on about 30 days) and 80.3% in 2026-01, below the 86% line. Arm 3 gives 78.7% and 66.2%, and the stored file 81.7% and 77.7%. We therefore did not run the sensitivity checks at 45 and 180 days or the refit-ratio diagnostic.
  • P3 and P4 of the plan. P3 (arm 3 gains less than 0.05 points over arm 2) holds, because arm 3 loses. Its premise, that stored medians are unbiased on average, does not hold at the grid supply points (mean fitted shift 5.9 points of capacity). P4 (arm 1 leaves normal-running Primaries coverage below 87%) holds: the mean of its four lead-band values is 86.8%.

docs.title: Primaries 13 and 16 in the July and August transfers
docs.text:
• Stored coverage is 28.3% (July) and 22.9% (August) at Primary 13, and 24.5% and 22.1% at Primary 16, which we think reflects load moved between substations that normal running ignores.
  • Arm 2 coverage is 25.5% and 49.4% at Primary 13 and 26.1% and 66.7% at Primary 16, so P5 (all below 80%) holds.
  • Pooled coverage of the other Primaries in those two months is 80.6% and 79.5% stored and 88.9% and 86.0% under arm 2. For all 16 series it is 73.9% and 72.4% stored and 81.1% and 82.6% under arm 2.
  • After the transfer ends, the scale overshoots: Primary 13 has 97.5% in 2026-09 and 97.8% in 2026-10 under arm 2.

docs.title: Final-test window (2026-07 to 2026-10, descriptive)
docs.text: Arm 2 coverage: normal-running Primaries 85.9% to 86.7% (stored 76.9% to 77.5%), prevailing 88.7% to 89.0%, bulk supply points 86.8% to 88.5% (stored 83.7% to 84.9%), grid supply points 87.5% to 88.1% (stored 86.9% to 89.0%), wind 89.4% to 93.3%, and solar 87.3% to 88.2% (stored 89.5% to 91.3%). The scale lowers coverage at solar and at the grid supply points' long leads below the stored values, so the gain from calibration is not uniform across the year.

docs.title: Tails of the normal-running Primaries (before July, all lead bands)
docs.text:
• Share of actual power below q05: 8.06% stored, 5.43% under arm 2 (nominal 5%).
  • Share above q95: 8.99% stored, 7.47% under arm 2. Below q01: 2.47% and 1.60%. Above q99: 2.94% and 2.56%.
  • Pinball loss at q05 and q95 rises under arm 2, from 0.920 to 0.939 and from 1.164 to 1.286.
  • Curtailment cost is not reported, because it needs the node-plus-generators frame and a thermal limit.
  • One scale applies to all 11 levels, so the tails are only approximately calibrated.

docs.title: Refit boundaries
docs.text:
• February. The days 10 to 14 band width of Primaries 8, 15, 17, 18, 24, and 25 widens at the February month start by 1.26, 1.31, 1.39, 1.48, 1.21, and 1.24 times. September: Primary 13 widens by 1.48 times. April: Primary 11 narrows by 0.76 times.
  • Seed spread. The ratio between the two seeds' widths in one fold ranges from 0.89 to 1.10 (5th to 95th percentile; extremes 0.68 and 1.29), so the February and September steps lie outside the seed spread.
  • Coverage after the step. Under arm 2, coverage at the six February Primaries goes from 76.3% in January to 93.1% in February, 94.1% in March, and 91.0% in April. The overshoot lasts more than the first month, so P6's second clause (the error is confined to the first month after a refit) is not supported.
  • Refitting the scale at every refit is not decided here, because the diagnostic that would decide it was not run.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. Not applicable, because the stored files hold no mean forecast. Arms 1 and 2 leave q50 unchanged, so the error of the median equals the stored file's. Arm 3 moves the median. The mean fitted shift (stored median bias, in points of capacity, unweighted over the fitted series-by-month combinations from 2025-12 to 2026-10) is 0.9 for the normal-running Primaries, -0.2 for the prevailing, -0.4 for the bulk supply points, 5.9 for the grid supply points, 1.7 for wind, and 0.2 for solar.
  • Why arm 3 hurts. A shift-only counterfactual (stored quantiles plus the fitted shift, no rescale) reproduces nearly all of arm 3's damage: grid supply points CRPS 13.88 stored, 14.75 shift-only, 14.72 arm 3; normal-running Primaries 4.23, 4.47, 4.54. The fitted shift does not persist: its correlation with the next month's median error is -0.41 at the grid supply points and +0.26 for the normal-running Primaries.
  • Audit trigger fired: a nested arm beats the arm that contains it (arm 2 beats arm 3, which adds a shift to arm 2). An independent re-derivation from the raw files reproduced the bulk-supply-point and normal-running Primaries coverage and CRPS, rebuilt the Primary 17 scale for 2026-01 (matching the stored arm 2 to 6 significant figures, with no fitting row after the cut-off), and confirmed the stop-rule months and the Primary 13 and 16 figures. It found no bug. The other triggers did not apply, and the contradiction of the P2 prediction is explained by the monthly and Primary 13 and 16 slices above.
  • Scale limits. The scale hit its bounds (0.5 and 3) in 24 of the 704 combinations of series, month, and lead band for the normal-running Primaries, and in none for the other files. No combination fell back to a scale of 1.
  • Caveats. The first calibrated month, 2025-12, fits on about 30 days. The cleaned power comes from a flagging rule run over the whole table, so a fit uses cleaning decisions made with later data. The event logs of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) may miss load transfers, so the fitting rows may hold events that no label covers. Wind's q01 share is about 9% in every arm because the scoring sets idle half-hours to zero, which equals the quantile.

docs.title: What the next experiment could answer
docs.text: A scale on the band half-width cannot be shown to repair a median that is wrong in winter at the Primaries. A learned width head on the normal-running Primaries, conditioned on temperature and the recent error, is one candidate, to be scored on 2025-12 to 2026-01 against arm 2; the Discuss session decides whether to run it.

docs.title: Can output distributions that cannot go below zero, and a solar night gate set at the half-hour's own sun position, replace the post hoc clamps in the one-year backtest files?
docs.text: A Gaussian mixture conditioned on power at or above zero gives the four demand series positive quantiles with CRPS (continuous ranked probability score) improved at two series and worsened by 0.03 points of capacity at one, and a gamma mixture does not. The one-year backtest files held negative lower quantiles at Primaries that meter apparent power (MVA), and small non-zero solar quantiles at night. A post hoc clamp had removed both. We refitted the demand network with two output families that cannot go below zero, on two test months (2026-02 and 2026-05), and gated the solar quantiles at night at each half-hour's own sun position. The truncated Gaussian mixture changed CRPS by -0.070, -0.015, -0.010, and +0.030 points of capacity at four Primaries, and the gamma mixture raised it by 0.68 to 1.48 points at two of them, so it failed its stop rule. Both new families remove every negative q01. The gate removes every non-zero night quantile, lowers night CRPS, and changes no daylight or dawn score. Its zero quantiles lie below night observations that are slightly positive, so the share above q99 at night rises. Two test months and one pair of seeds can rank these ideas but cannot support a claim of benefit.

docs.text:
Demand: the truncated Gaussian mixture passed, the gamma mixture failed. Rows are the normal-running output at test months 2026-02 and 2026-05 (59 origin days; about 38,000 scored half-hours per series). CRPS is in points of capacity (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 levels, times 100). "Stored" is experiment 667's output; "clamp" sets its negative quantiles to zero. The Gaussian refit reproduced the stored forecasts to the printed digits (the training is deterministic), so the refit adds no noise floor, and its rows are not repeated below.

Gamma: 14 -0.048 (-0.093 to -0.007); 15 +1.482 (1.295 to 1.701); 17 +0.683 (0.566 to 0.802); 26 +0.046 (0.015 to 0.078).

P2 failed for the truncated Gaussian, because the changes are not all within 0.01 (two are larger improvements, one is a larger loss). The stop rule did not fire for it (no series worsened by 0.05). P2 and the stop rule failed for the gamma mixture at Primaries 15 and 17, so the gamma family is dropped. P3 held for the truncated Gaussian (coverage change from -0.001 to +0.016) and failed for the gamma mixture at Primaries 15 and 17.
  • The sign differs by month at one series. The truncated Gaussian's CRPS change at Primary 17 is -0.085 in 2026-02 and +0.066 in 2026-05. At Primary 14 it is +0.028 and +0.032 (worse in both months), and at Primaries 15 and 26 it is negative in both.
  • The other 12 Primaries (same shared network, Gaussian output): CRPS 3.468 stored, 3.465 truncated-Gaussian run, 3.496 gamma run. The gamma head therefore also hurt Primaries that kept a Gaussian output.
  • Tails, pooled over both months, stored / truncated Gaussian / gamma. q01 pinball loss: Primary 14 0.295 / 0.292 / 0.272; 15 0.206 / 0.201 / 0.363; 17 0.198 / 0.193 / 0.218; 26 0.348 / 0.342 / 0.348. q99 pinball loss: 14 0.485 / 0.480 / 0.488; 15 0.221 / 0.221 / 0.302; 17 0.216 / 0.221 / 0.284; 26 0.379 / 0.382 / 0.374. Share of observations above q99: 14 0.013 / 0.010 / 0.016; 15 0.008 / 0.009 / 0.028; 17 0.012 / 0.019 / 0.031; 26 0.012 / 0.011 / 0.007.

The fitted shape differs only near zero. At two half-hours of Primary 26 the three arms' 11 quantiles agree in the middle and differ at the lower levels, where the stored output reaches below zero.

Solar: the gate leaves no night quantile and changes nothing else. The gate (arm a) keeps the stored networks of experiment 666 and sets every quantile to zero where the sun's elevation at the middle of the half-hour is at or below zero. The stored output has a non-zero quantile at 21,968 of 57,890 night half-hours of the two farms (32,200 of them have observed power and are scored in the table) (origins from 2026-02-01 to 2026-04-30); the gated output has none.
