docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Reproduction: the Gaussian-loss run of the new chain reproduced experiment 667's stored forecasts at both folds (CRPS equal to 6 digits at the four Primaries).
  • Known-answer test (e00684_check.py): both families' densities integrate to 1 over their support, the quantiles invert the cumulative distribution to 1e-5, Gaussian rows equal the original functions, and the target statistics are recorded when a fold's rows are built.
  • Scored rows: the four demand series have 39,648, 39,648, 37,165, and 39,605 scored half-hours, the stored rows' own.
  • Reviews run: a Sonnet plan review and a Sonnet code review (it found that the target statistics were hooked on the wrong class, which would have stopped the first fit, and that the gamma floor depended on each Primary's standard deviation; both were fixed before any fit). A Sonnet numbers review recomputed every table from the stored forecasts and agreed, apart from the 2026-02 split at Primary 14 (corrected here) and bootstrap bounds that differ by 0.003 to 0.02 between random seeds. A Sonnet prose review led to the rewording of this page.
  • Audit triggers: trigger 2 fired for the gamma mixture, whose result contradicts its prediction with no tested explanation (the shared head reading Gaussian parameters at some Primaries and gamma parameters at others is the likely cause, untested). The gamma result does not support any conclusion beyond dropping the family. The median-error contrast was not run.
  • Not checked: seed-to-seed variation. The two seeds are averaged, so no spread between seeds is available, and the truncated Gaussian's differences of 0.01 to 0.07 may include training variation.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Architecture. The Candidate demand network of experiment 667 (arm P7+D50): encoders for lagged power, neighbours' power summaries, ECMWF ENS weather, and date and time, then a three-component mixture head, one shared network for the 16 Primaries. The output family is replaced only at Primaries 14, 15, 26, and 17. Truncated Gaussian: the mixture is conditioned on power at or above zero, so the negative log likelihood adds the log of the mixture's mass above zero and the quantiles are read from the conditional cumulative distribution. Gamma: three gamma components on power over the Primary's standard deviation, with each component's mean and coefficient of variation read from the head's raw outputs. The Primary index and the fold's target statistics reach the loss and the read-out through a patch of experiment 397's mixture functions.
  • Training regime. The encoders keep experiment 667's weights pre-trained on ERA5 and CAMS (under the Gaussian loss). The step 2 mixer, the cross-fit tables, and the daily fine-tune are refitted under the new loss, with experiment 667's recipe: monthly refit, 2 seeds averaged quantile by quantile, cleaned power, D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, and ENS weather at lags of at least 24 hours. About 0.8 GPU-hours in all (7 to 12 minutes per chain). Solar: no refit.
  • Measurement. Test months 2026-02 and 2026-05 (test month 2026-08 lies inside the final-test window and was not read). Normal-running output only; the prevailing output was not refitted. CRPS, median error, coverage, and pinball loss are experiment 667's (e00667_score.score_frame), against cleaned observed power. Intervals are a paired bootstrap over origin days. Solar uses the scoring rule of experiment 666 (night half-hours: sun elevation at the middle of the half-hour at or below zero).
  • Limits. The lead range is 14 days, which covers NGED's 1 to 10 days. The weather is the ENS forecast, available at forecast time, and the lags are at least 24 hours old.

  • e00684_demand_score.py scores the arms and the clamp; e00684_figures.py draws the demand figures and the bootstrap; e00684_solar_gate.py and e00684_solar_figure.py are the solar arm.

docs.title: Which load-shift candidates does the fixed event table find at the 15 Primaries from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31?
docs.text:
From 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31 the event table of experiment 680, run unchanged on 15 Primary substations, finds 14 rows (13 events, because an edge transfer takes two rows). None of them explains the one-year backtest's flags at four Primaries. A Primary substation steps electricity down to a local distribution network. A load shift is a lasting change in a Primary's demand with no change in the weather, and an edge transfer is a load shift that moves between two neighbouring Primaries. The one-year backtest flagged time_series_id 13 (D18) as above its 95th-percentile forecast on 69% and 73% of half-hours, and 16 (D14) as below its 5th percentile on 75% and 78%. Flags at id 11 (D4) in September and id 18 (D16) in October were also reported.

We ran the event table on the residual, which is the observed power minus the forecast of a convex demand model that uses no lagged power ("lag-free"), extended to the end of 2026-10-31. The table finds no edge transfer between ids 13 and 16 in July or August, and no event at id 11 in September.

Every row is a candidate, never a label. NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so a clean half-hour may hold an event that no label covers, and an absence here is not proof that nothing happened. The final-test window 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31 was read for this event table only, on the maintainer's authorisation. No detector was tuned on it, no method was chosen with it, and no forecasting model was scored on it. Noise unit has the meaning given in Method.

docs.title: Headline rows
docs.text:
Question Result Transfer between id 13 (D18) and id 16 (D14), July and August 2026 None found. Any event at id 11 (D4), September 2026 None found. Any event at id 18 (D16), October 2026 One solo fall of 0.75 MW (2.7 noise units) from 2026-10-04 15:30 UTC, open at 2026-10-31. Open edge transfer from id 13 to id 16 From 2026-10-26 17:30 UTC D18 falls 1.31 MW (8.2 noise units) and D14 rises 0.71 MW (2.2 noise units); both are open at 2026-10-31.

The 14 rows starting in the window are 12 solo shifts (5 in July, 3 in September, 4 in October) and the two rows of the one edge transfer (the per-Primary and per-month counts are in the private SUMMARY.md).

docs.title: Reproduction gate
docs.text:
• Refit cut. The 2026-06-01 cut of the lag-free forecast refitted here matches experiment 327's stored forecast with a maximum difference of 0 MW at all 15 series.
  • Window blanked. With the residual after 2026-06-30 set to missing, the pipeline reproduces experiment 680's 249 stored real-record events exactly (key, end, depth, and class).
  • Window included: 62 of 249 earlier events change. Of the 249 earlier events, 187 keep their Primary, start, class, and partners. The other 62 are replaced by 51 new ones, mostly small solo shifts spread over every Primary. The monthly refits and the median removal are ruled out as the cause. The slow level is refitted on the whole panel, so 4 more months of data move the baseline and the end-of-record handling; no run separated those two, so that cause is an inference by elimination. Among the 56 earlier events of 2 noise units or more that are neither ramps nor routine steps, 47 keep their key and move by a median of 0.05 noise units (largest 1.1), and none of the 47 has a changed end (22 of the 187 keyed matches in the full set do). The other 9 are dropped and 21 are added, mostly near the 2-unit threshold. Six of the added events are 4 noise units or more. Treat events from before July as possibly changed by the extension.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Weather at forecast time. The lag-free forecast uses ERA5 2 m temperature and CAMS irradiance, both estimates of past weather. The table is a hindsight product and cannot be made live.
  • Last half-hour. The forecast for 2026-10-31 23:30 is missing because ERA5 ends at 23:00 on that day. Hours after 2026-06-30 are ERA5T in ARCO-ERA5, whose values are preliminary and may be revised.
  • Window power. Each Primary has 5,784 to 5,904 of 5,904 half-hours with a cleaned reading in the window. Half-hours flagged by the substation_zero cleaning rule are missing.
  • Code review. One fresh Sonnet code review ran before the run. It found a blocking indexing error, a dependence of the noise units on the series length, and a wrong dark flag on half-hour rows (a flag marking half-hours without daylight); all three were fixed. Every refit cut fitted.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Unchanged from experiment 680. E1-J-sym is experiment 653's event table plus two searches, with no parameter changed.
  • Input. The residual is the cleaned power minus the forecast of the lag-free convex demand model of experiment 130, as stored by experiment 327 (arm C, trained on every half-hour that has a reading, refitted on the 1st of each month on a 24-month window). Here the forecast is refitted for the cuts 2026-07-01, 08-01, 09-01, and 10-01, using experiment 327's own code path on a feature cache extended to 2026-10-31. The median residual across the 15 Primaries is removed before segmentation, with each Primary's scale fixed on the data before 2026-07-01. D18 loses every row before 2025-03-01.
  • Noise unit and slow level. One noise unit is the robust spread of the difference between successive 6-hour block means of the residual before 2026-07-01, frozen. The slow level is a seasonal level per Primary fitted with a Huber (1964) loss, as in experiment 653, and refitted on the whole extended panel.
  • Segmentation. Each Primary's residual, less the slow level, is cut into 6-hour block means. An exact dynamic programme decodes 25 states per block (no shift, and 12 amplitudes log-spaced from 1 to 20 noise units in each sign) with a Student-t emission, using the Viterbi (1967) algorithm, then refines each start and end to the half-hour. Events are classed as ramps, routine steps, permanent or open shifts, and paired across neighbouring Primaries (the graph of experiment 383) as in experiment 653.
  • Recipient search (E1-J, experiment 670). From each unpaired fall of 4 noise units or more, look at every connected Primary for a rise of 2 noise units or more starting near the fall, and accept up to three recipients whose combined rise conserves the fall under experiment 653's loose conservation cost.
  • Donor search (E1-J-sym, experiment 680). From each rise of 4 noise units or more still unpaired, look at every connected Primary for a fall of 2 noise units or more that starts up to 36 half-hours before the rise (widened by 6 half-hours on each side for start error), with a recipient share of 0.3 to 2.0 and a conservation cost of at most 2.5.
  • Output table. One row per event of 2 noise units or more that is not a ramp or routine step: the Primaries involved, class (edge transfer or solo shift), onset and end (end-of-half-hour stamps in UTC, or open), depth in megawatts and noise units, confidence, and whether the event starts before the window or ends after it. An edge transfer appears as two rows.
  • Compute. CPU only, 2 cores. The ERA5 extension is 2 m temperature only for August to October 2026 (1.6 MB), read from the ARCO-ERA5 store (Google's public copy of ERA5) with the stage-1 box script.

docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00685-.../e00685_fetch_era5.py: runs the stage-1 ERA5 box fetch with its span set to 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31.
  • e00685_inputs.py: extends experiment 103's row table, the ERA5 temperature, and the CAMS irradiance to 2026-10-31.
  • e00685_refit.py: refits experiment 327's arm C at the cuts 2026-06-01 to 2026-10-01 (the first is the gate) and overrides, in that process only, the three constants in the feature-cache and fitting code that exclude the window.

Inputs and forecasts: inputs/, e327_extended/, era5_box_extension/ in the same folder.

docs.title: Do the donor and the recipient of a load transfer start together, and what kind of false event does solar growth cause in the event table?
docs.text:
At D3/D22 the donor and the recipient step together, and at D5/D16 the two ends start within 2.5 hours of each other, although the D5/D16 onset is too noisy to exclude a lag of 15 hours. The recipient lag of 14.5 and 15 hours that experiment 660 reported is the gap between the two Primaries' labelled times. The fitted gaps are 2.0 hours at the D5/D16 onset, 2.5 hours at its end, −0.5 hours at the D3/D22 onset, and −2.0 hours at its end. Of the 333 false events that injected solar growth causes, few are abrupt steps inside a sunny run, but half last 3 days or less. A composite capacity curve for slow drift would therefore remove fewer false events than the ramp share suggests.

Check 1 asks whether the two ends of a verified transfer start together. A transfer happens when an operator switches a circuit from one Primary substation (the donor) to a neighbour (the recipient). The answer decides how tightly a detector may require the two steps to coincide. Check 2 asks what kind of false event solar growth causes in the event table of experiment 653. A "world" is a copy of the real power record with solar growth injected at 3 Primaries. The "slow level" is the smooth seasonal level the detector subtracts before it looks for events. An "onset" is the start of a transfer and an "end" is its finish. "ERA5" is a weather reanalysis, and "NGED" is the distribution network operator.

The verdict is partly supported, and the decision rule does not produce it by itself. Prediction P1 (a recipient lag of 12 hours or more) is not supported: the fitted gaps are 2.0 and −0.5 hours at the onsets. Prediction P2 (the fit recovers a true gap of 0) fails at D5/D16, where 83% of the injected windows at the onset and 75% at the end fall within 4 half-hours, against the 90% bar. Prediction P3 (most false events are slow ramps or misfits, under a third are sunny-run steps) is supported on the pre-registered definition. The plan gives no rule for combining the three, so the verdict is a judgement. Because P2 fails at D5/D16, the D5/D16 gaps are reported as measurements with their intervals and not as findings. Each section says how far its definition matters.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows that the fitted gap is within 2.5 hours of zero at all four edges, while the labelled gap is 14.5 to 18.5 hours at three of them and 0 at the fourth. The dot is the fitted gap (recipient minus donor) and the line is a 90% interval from resampling whole days. The interval at the D5/D16 onset is wide (−13.0 to 16.5 hours), so that edge alone cannot exclude a lag of 15 hours. The other three intervals can. The D5/D16 end interval (1.5 to 3.5 hours) excludes 0, so that end shows a small lag.

Figure 2 shows the D5/D16 onset in the data. Both Primaries step within a few hours of one another, and the step fitted separately for each Primary falls beside the step fitted jointly.

Figure 3 shows what the fit reports when the true gap is known. A gap of 0 is read as within 2 hours in most windows, but a few windows scatter by 6 hours or more, most at D5/D16. A gap of 14.5 hours is read back with a median of 14.5 to 15 hours. Each dot is one of 120 windows (two step shapes pooled).

Figure 4 shows the class of the false events. The ramp class is the largest, and it mixes slow ramps with short bumps (see the post hoc bullets below).

Figures 5 and 6 show one example of each class, each the event whose size is nearest its class's median size. The grey band marks the false event, the orange line is the injected growth (negative, because it lowers the residual), and the green line is the change in the slow level. The slow level follows only a fraction of the midday-only growth in every example.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Check 1, fitted gap (hours) and test of one shared onset. Window: 5 days either side of the midpoint of the two labelled edges. "Statistic" is twice the log likelihood ratio of separate against shared onsets, computed per Primary; a ratio of 4 is 2.77. The p-value is from a day-block bootstrap under the shared model (300 draws).

Edge Labelled gap Fitted gap (90% interval) Statistic Bootstrap p D5/D16 onset 15.0 2.0 (−13.0 to 16.5) 0.32 0.35 D5/D16 end 0.0 2.5 (1.5 to 3.5) 43.8 0.06 D3/D22 onset 14.5 −0.5 (−6.0 to 0.0) 2.79 0.22 D3/D22 end 18.5 −2.0 (−3.0 to 2.5) 1.66 0.36
  • Method check P2 fails at D5/D16 and passes at D3/D22. With a true gap of 0, the fitted gap lies within 4 half-hours in 83% (onset) and 75% (end) of 120 windows at D5/D16, against the 90% bar, and in 97% and 95% at D3/D22. At D5/D16 the fit reports a gap of 6 hours or more in 7.5% (onset) and 18% (end) of windows. Both a constant step and a step that follows the donor's profile give the same shares.
  • A gap of 14.5 hours is detected. With a true gap of 14.5 hours, the statistic exceeds 2.77 in all 120 windows of every pair and edge, and the fitted gap is within 2 hours of the truth in 67% to 95% of them.
  • The likelihood-ratio cut-off of 4 is too eager. The statistic exceeds 2.77 in 25% to 32% of windows with a true gap of 0, so a rule of "ratio under 4 means simultaneous" would reject a truly simultaneous transfer about 3 times in 10. The bootstrap null is the calibrated test. The D5/D16 end has a statistic of 43.8, which sits at the 95th percentile of its own bootstrap null (44.9).
  • The labelled gap is not a fitted lag. Experiment 660 fitted each Primary in its own window and searched 24 hours either side of its labelled time. Adding each Primary's fitted shift to its labelled time gives recipient lags of 0.5 hours (D5/D16 onset), 2.0 (D5/D16 end), −0.5 (D3/D22 onset), and 18.5 (D3/D22 end). The last equals the labelled gap because both of its shifts sat at the limit of the search, and four of its eight shifts did.
  • Post hoc, constant-MW steps only (constant_only.json): the fitted gaps are 0.5, 2.0, −0.5, and −0.5 hours at the four edges, so allowing a profile-shaped step does not explain the finding.

Check 2, classes of the false events. The 24 worlds (worlds 0 and 1 reproduce experiment 653's 5 and 9 false events) hold 333 false events, or 1.85 per injected Primary-year (95% interval 1.06 to 2.86 from resampling worlds), against experiment 653's 0.93 on its two worlds.

Class (first match) Events Share (95% interval) Per Primary-year (95% interval) Sunny-run step 17 0.05 (0.03 to 0.08) 0.09 (0.05 to 0.14) Slow ramp (rise over more than 1 day, or not complete in 14) 264 0.79 (0.75 to 0.83) 1.47 (0.79 to 2.36) Slow-level misfit 34 0.10 (0.07 to 0.14) 0.19 (0.08 to 0.32) Other step 18 0.05 (0.03 to 0.08) 0.10 (0.06 to 0.14)
  • P3 is supported on the pre-registered definition. Slow ramps and misfits are 0.89 of the events (0.83 to 0.93 from resampling worlds), and sunny-run steps are 0.05 (0.03 to 0.09).
  • Post hoc, the ramp class is mostly not a slow ramp. Of the 333 events, 167 have no completed edge on the midday series, and 173 (52%, interval 47% to 57%) last 3 days or less. Only 97 (29%) are ramps that complete over more than 1 day.
  • Post hoc, a loose reading of "sunny run" gives a different answer. Of the 333 events, 122 (37%, 32% to 42%) start in a run whose first 3 days have a midday clearness of 0.7 or more. Under the pre-registered definition only the 17 with a step-like edge count. The page does not decide which reading the detector needs.
  • Daily shape. The median share of an event's megawatts that falls between 10:00 and 15:00 UTC is 0.26 to 0.29 for the sunny-run, ramp, and misfit classes. A constant step would give 10 of 48 half-hours, 0.21, so the events are only weakly midday-shaped.
  • Season boundaries. Of the 333 events, 20 start within 14 days of 1 April or 1 October.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Two verified transfers are the only real evidence for check 1. The D5/D16 onset interval is wide, so a lag of about 15 hours is not excluded there. The result is consistent with simultaneity at four edges and cannot prove it.
  • The injection check scores the method on residual windows that NGED's logs call event-free. The logs are incomplete, so some windows may hold an event, which would widen the scatter.
  • The edge width in check 2 has a resolution of 1 day (daily mean of the midday half-hours), so a step of 1 hour is not separated from a step of 1 day. The sunny-run clearness uses ERA5 shortwave, a recorded product, not CAMS.
  • Solar growth is injected, not real. The injected growth is a midday-only term of 0.2 to 1.0 MW per year at 3 Primaries per world, so the false-event rate describes experiment 653's masked arm under that injection only.
  • Unlogged events. NGED says its logs may miss load-shift events, so the real-record windows here may hold unlabelled events, and the injected-window scatter is a lower bound.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text:
• Does a detector that requires both ends to coincide within about 4 half-hours cut the false-transfer share? The tolerance should be tested on injected worlds, because the fit misplaces some true simultaneous steps by 6 hours or more at D5/D16.
  • How many of the short bumps in check 2 are a sunny day or two rather than solar growth? A placebo with solar growth removed would count the short bumps the slow level cannot explain.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and error of the mean beside each quantile-score contrast: not applicable, because this experiment trains and scores no forecast.
  • Audit triggers: none of the seven apply (no forecast, no leakage path, no tuned threshold read from the scored rows).
  • Reviews: a fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the scored run, and another reviewed the numbers and the prose.
  • Final-test window: never read. All windows and worlds end before 2026-07-01.
  • Standing practices: no forecast is trained, so monthly refits, saved models, tail scores, and curtailment cost do not apply. D18's rows before 2025-03-01 are dropped as in experiment 653.
