docs.title: Do causal step statistics, the neighbour mirror, and a return-to-level statistic let the small prevailing heads react sooner to a load shift than extra lagged power inputs do?
docs.text:
Throughout, K1 is the frozen two-output demand neural network. Its normal-running-arrangement (NRA) output forecasts demand as if no shift were under way, and its prevailing output forecasts demand including any shift in force. The small head is the neural network that corrects the prevailing output. B0 is experiment 652's head, L1 is B0 plus extra lagged power, F1 is B0 plus the detector features D1 to D6, and P is the placebo.

A load shift is a period when the electricity network operator moves part of one primary substation's (Primary's) demand onto or off a neighbouring Primary. The two-output demand neural network (K1 plus a small head) should follow such a shift in its prevailing output. We asked whether giving the small head the statistics of a simple step detector makes it follow a shift sooner, and compared it with giving the same head extra recent lagged power instead. Every shift is injected into real history, with its start and end known, so reaction time can be measured exactly.

Take-home message. Detector features make the prevailing output cover half of a new shift 1.59 days [-2.26, -1.00] sooner than experiment 652's head (B0), and release half of it 0.63 days [-0.91, -0.36] sooner after the shift ends. Extra lagged power inputs (L1, experiment 681's block) get 1.25 days [-1.87, -0.74] at the start and 0.45 days at the end, and F1 minus L1 is -0.33 [-0.72, +0.07] at the start, so the features are not shown to beat plain lags. The scaled CRPS where a shift is in force improves by 0.12 points of capacity [-0.33, +0.06], below the 0.30 bar. Verdict: partly supported. F1 reacts sooner than B0 (supported); F1 is not shown to react sooner than L1 (not supported); the veto is not cleared, because F1's CRPS on real event-free rows is above the P4 limit.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Scores are CRPS in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a Primary's effective capacity), scaled to a q05 to q95 coverage of 0.90 as in experiment 652, mean of 2 seeds, then of the 5 development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). Intervals are percentile bootstraps over the months (5 blocks, so coarse) or over events. B0 refitted here equals experiment 652's stored R-haz exactly (the gate passes).

  • Step 1, separability (no refit). A logistic regression on experiment 606's summaries and their absolute values reaches an AUROC of 0.83 to 0.85 (training-family shifts) and 0.87 to 0.89 (held-out shifts) for "this lag lies inside an injected shift". Adding D1 to D5 raises it by +0.061 (day lag) and +0.059 (week lag) on training-family shifts, and by +0.063 and +0.048 on held-out shifts, on the stored bank; the mirror-at-60% and no-mirror banks differ by under 0.002. Predicted +0.05 on every bank: met except the week lag on held-out shifts (+0.047). Stop rule (gain under 0.03): not triggered. The placebo scorer (D1 to D5 of another Primary) adds under 0.005.
  • Reaction time, start of a shift (281 held-out events). Mean origin days to cover half the shift, minus B0: F1 -1.59 [-2.26, -1.00] (median -1.0), F1d46 -1.39, F2 -1.79, F1h4 (4 h cutoff) -1.62, L1 -1.25 [-1.87, -0.74], B0g (new age rule, no extra inputs) -0.33 [-0.67, -0.05], P +0.04 [-0.59, +0.59]. P2 (at least 1 day, interval excluding zero) is met for the mean and the median. By event length F1 minus B0 is -0.66, -1.17, -1.48, and -3.34 days (5, 10, 21, and 45 days), so the gain of F1 over B0 is below 1 day for 5-day shifts (audit's own code).
  • Reaction time, end of a shift. F1 minus B0 -0.63 [-0.91, -0.36] mean, median 0.0, so P2's 1-day bar is not met at the end. F1 minus L1: -0.33 [-0.72, +0.07] at the start and -0.18 [-0.42, +0.07] at the end. A 4-hour cutoff reacts no sooner than a 6-hour cutoff (F1h4 minus F1: -0.03 and -0.08).
  • Scaled CRPS minus B0. In force: F1 -0.12 [-0.33, +0.06], F1d46 -0.23, L1 -0.25 [-0.40, -0.13], P +0.06. Near the end: F1 +0.02, L1 -0.02, B0g -0.31. Just ended: F1 -0.37 [-0.66, -0.10], L1 -0.34, F1d46 -0.43. Event-free: F1 +0.01 [-0.16, +0.20], L1 -0.03. P3 (-0.30 in force, near the end, and just ended) is met only for just ended. Within 7 days after the end, the gain of -0.37 meets the 0.30 bar.
  • False alarms. Share of event-free rows where the head's median departs from K1's median (the NRA output) by 3 points or more: B0 0.18, F1 0.19, F1d46 0.18, L1 0.23, K1 0.00. P4 (at most +1 percentage point and +0.02 CRPS) holds for F1 on the bank (+0.7 points; +0.01 CRPS) and not for L1 (+4.5 points). On real event-free rows F1's CRPS is +0.05 [-0.02, +0.13] against B0, an interval that includes zero, so the contrast is unresolved, with a point estimate above the 0.02 limit.
  • Scaled in-force CRPS on held-out-family shifts only (the verdict reads the all-rows figure above). B0 10.96, L1 10.28 (-0.67), F1 10.42 (-0.54), F1d46 10.22 (-0.74), K1 16.05, R0 (168 h) 12.43.
  • Tails, in force (unscaled). q05 to q95 coverage: K1 0.49, B0 0.83, F1 0.85, L1 0.84. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99: B0 0.53, 1.45, 1.51, and 0.52; F1 0.43, 1.31, 1.49, and 0.49; L1 0.43, 1.33, 1.41, and 0.45.
  • Verified transfer between Primaries D5 and D16 (real rows, one episode, 13,068 rows). CRPS: K1 14.9, B0 9.73, B0g 9.35, F1 8.58, L1 8.63, P 9.92. Descriptive only.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost (experiment 601 units, six MW Primaries, leads 12 to 36 h). Inside a shift: K1 549,533, B0 162,976, F1 136,173, F1d46 124,801, L1 136,284. In the 7 days after the end: K1 541, B0 10,786, F1 9,105, L1 9,148. All rows: K1 316,942, B0 95,937, F1 80,090, L1 80,185.
  • Placebo (P). P reacts like B0 at the start (+0.04) and slower at the end (+0.54, an artefact of the release rule, see Caveats), and has a false-alarm rate of 0.36. It cannot serve as the plan's placebo, because the placebo Primary is itself in a shift on 44% to 55% of the target's events (every Primary is shifted in every pass). P5 is not tested.

docs.title: Arms, data, and method
docs.text:
• Arms. B0 (experiment 652's R-haz, refitted), B0x (B0 with L1's age rule), B0g (B0 with F1's age rule, no extra inputs), L1 (B0 plus experiment 681's lag block at 6 to 72 hours before the origin, built here), F1 (B0 plus D1 to D6 at the day lag, week lag, and 6-hour cutoff), F1d46 (D4 to D6 at the 6-hour cutoff only), F2 (F1 plus the explicit flag), F1h4 (4 hour cutoff), F1nd (F1 without dropout), P (features of another Primary). 10 arms x 5 months x 2 seeds = 100 fits.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00687-*/: features e00687_features.py, tables e00687_tables.py, separability e00687_separability.py, fits e00687_fit.py, scores e00687_score.py. Reuses the code of experiments 598, 606, 647, 650, and 652 (imported). Fitted weights and tables are in data/ml-experiments/00687-*/.
  • Cadence and compute. One small head per scored month (no refit cadence), 4 CPU processes, about 25 minutes for the fits, no GPU. Data before 2026-07-01 only (asserted). Cleaned power, as in experiment 650.
  • Features. D1 to D6 of the plan, in noise units; the noise unit uses all five months, including the scored month (scale only; no sensitivity check was run). The age that gates the survival probability is the larger of the day-lag age and the detector's age (F arms), or 1 day when the mean residual at 6 to 24 hours before the origin exceeds 5 points (L1, B0x).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, in force, points of capacity: B0 -0.34, L1 -0.40, F1 -0.51. Mean absolute error of the mean forecast: B0 10.22, L1 9.96, F1 10.15; of the median: 10.20, 9.87, 10.18. The mean-forecast contrast agrees in direction with the CRPS contrast.
  • Plan conditions that fired. (1) The placebo P gained on rows near the end of a shift. (2) The in-force CRPS gain missed its own prediction (P3). (3) F1 scored worse than its subset F1d46 on some strata (nested arm). A Sonnet audit re-derived the contrasts from the stored predictions with its own code and matched them (briefs/e687_audit.md, private). Its findings: the placebo is not independent (accepted: P5 untested, P not read as a control); P's near-end gain is shrinkage, because K1 itself scores 5.93 there against B0's 7.35, so that stratum rewards departing less (accepted); the F1 against F1d46 gap is seed variance of 0.1 to 0.6 points (accepted); the reaction-time definition is partly unsound (accepted, see Caveats). B0 equals experiment 652's stored head exactly because the refit is deterministic, not because a file was read twice.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet plan review (14 findings, 13 accepted, noise-unit leakage kept with a stated reason), a Sonnet code review before the fits (13 findings: pass-family leak in the AUROC, a gate-only arm, assertions fixed; 5 low items noted), the audit above, and a Sonnet prose review (see the pull request).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• The injected world flatters the features. Shifts are exact constants added to clean power, every Primary is shifted in every pass, and the neighbour sees the opposite step at a gain of 0.5 to 1. The fits and scores use only the stored-mirror tables. NGED's event labels are incomplete, so real event-free rows may hold unlogged shifts, and the real-row numbers are optimistic.
  • The reaction-time start rule counts noise. A hit needs only a departure of half the shift at one origin, so false departures count; a two-origin rule gives P minus B0 +0.73 [+0.02, +1.40] and leaves F1 minus B0 unchanged (audit). A start with no hit is censored at the event length, so the mean is dominated by 45-day events (use the median, -1 day).
  • The end rule is relative to each head's own earlier level. With a sign-aware, truth-relative release, F1 minus B0 at the end is -0.46 [-0.65, -0.29] and P minus B0 is +0.01 (audit). Only 55% of events are released within 14 days.
  • Seed noise. The per-event start reaction differs by a standard deviation of 5.7 days (B0) and 3.9 days (F1) between the two seeds.
  • Stored banks. The no-mirror and 60% banks enter only the separability step. The 60% bank is an approximation of a split, not experiment 651's bank.
  • Lead range. The stored rows stop at 10 days, which is NGED's horizon.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text:
• Open the survival gate from the newest readings in every prevailing head, and re-test the detector features against extra lags in a world with few concurrent shifts and a placebo Primary that is never shifted.
  • L1 and B0g, which add no detector statistics, give 1.25 and 0.33 of the 1.59 days, so test whether a feature block helps beyond the lag block on real shifts, where the two cannot be separated yet.

docs.title: Do the 90% bands of the normal-running Primaries miss in winter because of median error and load transfers, or because the bands are too narrow?
docs.text:
The 90% bands of the normal-running Primaries miss in winter mostly because the median forecast is off by a different amount each month, and partly because of load transfers; the bands themselves are close to the right width. We asked why the 16 Primary substations' normal-running forecasts cover only 80% of the observed power inside their 5%-to-95% bands (the q05 and q95 quantiles) in December 2025 and January 2026, where 90% is promised. The normal-running output assumes the usual electricity network configuration. We took the bands as stored (after experiment 683 widened them by a factor fitted on earlier months). Step 1 dropped the half-hours inside labelled and verified load transfers, where demand moves from one substation to another. Step 2 moved each band by that month's observed median error, which no forecast could know in advance. Coverage rose to 90.1% and 88.6%, and the factor by which the bands would still need widening fell to about 1. The prediction written before the run held (coverage above 86% in both months), so the stop rule, which would have justified modelling the band width, did not fire.

  • Arms and steps. Arm 2 of experiment 683 (the walk-forward scale) is the object; the stored quantiles (arm 0) are the reference. Step 1 drops the half-hours whose valid time lies inside a span (the 34 labelled events of experiment 580's label table in the period, plus its verified transfers) at the Primary the span names. Step 2 adds, to all 11 quantiles, the median of observed minus the median forecast per series and origin month. Steps 1 and 2 are both diagnostics: step 2 uses the rows it scores.
  • Rows. The normal-running output of 16 Primaries, origin months 2025-12 to 2026-06, scored rows of experiment 683 with valid times before 2026-07 (74,406 rows from late June origins are left out, so 2026-06 differs from experiment 683's figure; earlier months match it exactly). Step 1 masked 39,163 of 332,611 half-hours in 2025-12 and 23,586 of 333,312 in 2026-01 (11.8% and 7.1%). We reused the stored forecasts, fitted nothing, scored cleaned observed power, and left the final-test window untouched.
  • Coverage, pooled, 95% day-block bootstrap intervals (arm 2): as it is 80.1% (79.3 to 80.9) and 80.3% (79.3 to 81.1); step 1 alone 86.0% (85.2 to 86.8) and 81.9% (81.0 to 82.8); step 2 alone 86.3% (84.7 to 87.8) and 86.5% (85.1 to 87.8); both 90.1% (89.4 to 90.8) and 88.6% (87.7 to 89.5), for 2025-12 and 2026-01. February to June as it is: 90.8%, 87.4%, 88.8%, 90.8%, and 93.5%; after both: 92.3%, 92.0%, 90.3%, 92.9%, and 94.2%.
  • Share of the shortfall from 90% explained (2025-12, 2026-01): step 1 alone 59% and 17%; step 2 alone 63% and 64%; both 101% and 86%. The order changes the split (step 2 after step 1: 42% and 69%; step 1 after step 2: 38% and 22%), because the transfers are also a large error in the median. Intervals are in tables/explained.csv.
  • Tails, arm 2, both steps (2025-12, 2026-01): below q05 5.4% and 6.5%; above q95 4.6% and 4.9% (nominal 5% each). As it is: below 4.7% and 11.6%; above 15.2% and 8.1%. The mix of one-sided misses changes month to month, which is the sign of a median level that moves.
  • Series below 0.86 after both steps: 2025-12: Primaries 12 (80.2%) and 14 (75.4%); 2026-01: Primaries 3 (83.3%), 9 (74.9%), 11 (84.4%), and 12 (81.9%). Primaries 17 and 18 (the verified transfer) go from 50% and 66% as it is to 99.5% and 92.0% over the two months.
  • Width against residuals, pooled Primaries, both winter months. The scale that would make 90% of observations fall inside the band is 1.33 to 1.38 as it is and 0.99 to 1.04 after both steps, in each of the four lead bands (days 0 to 1, 1 to 3, 3 to 7, 7 to 14). The ratio of the median band half-width to the empirical half-width of the residuals is 0.50 as it is and 0.66 after both steps, outside the 0.75 to 1.25 range of P4. The ratio compares a median over rows with a spread that mixes wide and narrow bands, so the needed scale is the fairer verdict on width.
  • Sensitivities (reported, not deciding). One shift per series, origin month, and lead band gives 90.1% and 89.4%. Widening the mask to the fitted spans of experiment 580 and to experiment 685's candidate events gives 91.4% and 88.4% after both steps, and 88.6% and 81.5% for step 1 alone.
  • Predictions. P1 held (90.1% and 88.6% exceed 86%). P2 held in point estimate in both months (63% against 59% in December, where the intervals overlap, and 64% against 17% in January). P3 held (at least two series below 86% in 2025-12 or 2026-01 after both steps, listed above). P4 failed as written (ratio 0.66), because the ratio compares a median over rows with a spread that mixes wide and narrow bands.
  • Checks. The stored files hold quantiles only, so there is no mean forecast. The median's mean absolute error in the two winter months falls from 7.24 to 6.39 percentage points of capacity under step 2 and to 5.71 under both steps. Its mean signed error is 0.67 as stored and 0.15 after both steps. The coverage contrasts and the median-error contrasts therefore point the same way. We made no leave-one-out run: the step 1 gain in 2025-12 is concentrated at Primaries 17 and 18, the verified transfer, and in 2026-01 step 2 carries the gain. No control failed, the result agrees with the lesson of experiment 683, the stages nest in the expected order, and no later experiment's design depends on this result yet, so no audit was run.
  • Open tension. After both steps the January misses are still one-sided (6.5% below q05 against 4.9% above q95). The page drops the width model on the coverage and the needed width factor, not on symmetric tails.
  • Caveats. The mask uses labelled events that experiment 580 could not confirm in the telemetry (only the 2025-12-29 to 2026-01-13 transfer was confirmed), and the event labels of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) are incomplete, so the share explained by transfers is not a count of real events and clean rows may hold unlabelled events. The shift is computed on the month it scores, so it measures how much median error there is, not a gain a forecast could realise. The horizon is 1 to 14 days; the final-test window 2026-07 to 2026-10 is untouched. The July and August 2026 miss at Primaries 13 and 16 is not examined here: it is an unexplained level miss, and the candidate events of experiment 685 are candidates, not labels.
  • Reuse and code. Imports e00668_score_lib (experiment 668) and e00683_calibrate (experiment 683); code in ml-experiments/00688-*/ (e00688_diagnose.py, e00688_tables.py, e00688_checks.py, e00688_figures.py).
  • What to try next. A correction to the median level that a forecast could compute during the month, scored with the same stages; a mask of verified transfers only, to separate confirmed events from unconfirmed labels.

docs.title: Does a width scale fitted on a fixed lookback remove the steps in band width at the model refits, or does the seed average of the quantiles matter?
docs.text:
A width scale fitted on a fixed lookback does not remove the steps in band width at the model refits, and seed averaging does not drive them. Under the 90-day scale of experiment 683 (arm A), 23 of the 151 affected cells (15.2%) end with a ratio of 0.90 to 1.10 across the refit, against the predicted 90%. The scale moves the ratio farther from 1 in 67% of the affected cells. Fitting the scale on each seed's quantiles and then averaging (arm B) changes the ratios by at most 0.05 in 89.4% of the cells, just under the pre-registered 90%, so we read the seed average as having no material effect on the steps.

The question was whether the steps that experiment 683 measured (Primaries 11 and 13, and six widenings in February) are removed by one scale per series and lead band, or come from the seed average of the quantiles changing at a refit. The September step of Primary 13 lies after the last scored origin month, so this experiment tests Primary 11 and the February widenings only. A lookback of 45, 90, or 180 days leaves 7.3% to 15.2% of cells inside 0.90 to 1.10, far below 90%. We expect the new model's raw band width to differ from the old model's, and the scale for a month is fitted on the old model's forecasts, but this experiment did not test that mechanism and did not fit a scale on any new-model forecasts.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Share of the 151 affected cells whose after-to-before ratio of band width lies between 0.90 and 1.10, by arm. The dashed line is the predicted 90%. Whiskers are 95% percentile intervals over resampled origin days, with one set of draws per refit boundary.

Calibrated ratio against stored ratio for each affected cell, by lead band, arms A and B. The grey band is 0.90 to 1.10 and the diagonal is no change. Points above the diagonal on the right are steps that the scale has enlarged.

docs.title: Arms and rows
docs.text:
• Rows: the 16 Primaries, normal-running output, origin months 2025-12 to 2026-06 (refit boundaries 2026-01 to 2026-06; 2025-11 has no earlier forecast to fit on, and origin months from 2026-07 lie in the final-test window and are not loaded). 384 cells (16 series, 6 boundaries, 4 lead bands); 151 are affected (stored ratio above 1.10 or below 1/1.10). Affected cells by boundary: 36, 20, 15, 25, 31, 24 (January to June).
  • Cell ratio: median band width (q95 minus q05, after the zero clamp for the MVA Primaries) of the first 7 origin days after the boundary over the median of the last 7 days before it. Ratios of the width and of the half-width agree away from the clamp.
  • Arm 0: stored seed-mean file. Arm A: experiment 683's rule, 90 days, fitted on the seed mean. Arm B: the same rule fitted on each seed's quantiles of experiment 667's fits (moved 3 hours to the 12:00 UTC origin, times capacity), applied to the same seed, averaged, then clamped. The seed fits are clamped at zero for the fit only. B-cross: each seed scaled by the other seed's fit. Arm C: arm A at 45 and 180 days.
  • Seed check: the mean of the two seed files reproduces the stored file to a maximum absolute difference of 4e-6 in the stored units (3,924,480 rows). Only the normal-running output has per-seed files, so the prevailing output is not tested.
  • Code reuse: the fitting rule is copied from ml-experiments/00683-*/e00683_calibrate.py, which also supplies z_scores, band_index, and load_truth; scoring helpers come from experiment 668. The experiment fits no forecasting model and ran on CPU only.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• P1 (at least 90% of affected cells within 0.90 to 1.10 under arm A): not supported. 15.2% (23 of 151; interval 14.6% to 24.5%). By lead band: 7 of 44, 8 of 46, 4 of 27, 4 of 34 for days 0 to 1, 1 to 3, 3 to 7, and 7 to 14. Stored: 1 of 151.
  • Stored: 1 of 151 is near zero by construction, because affected cells are those whose stored ratio lies outside 0.909 to 1.10. Resampling regresses extreme cells towards 1, which favours the calibrated arms, so the not-supported verdict is not weakened by it.
  • P2 (expected to fail): held. The median absolute step of an affected cell is 15% stored and 24% under arm A; arm A moves the ratio farther from 1 than stored in 67% of cells (in either direction).
  • P3 (arm B within 0.05 of arm A in at least 90% of cells): narrowly not met, at 89.4% (135 of 151); B-cross is 86.8%. No interval was computed for this share. Arm B passes 24 of 151 cells (15.9%), against 23 for arm A.
  • Lookback (arm C): 15 of 151 cells (9.9%) at 45 days and 11 (7.3%) at 180 days, against 23 at 90 days. The steps do not follow the lookback.
  • Named steps: at the February refit, days 7 to 14 ratios (stored, arm A, arm B) are 1.21, 1.25, 1.26 for Primary 8; 1.22, 1.64, 1.59 for 15; 1.30, 1.51, 1.50 for 17; 1.39, 3.62, 3.45 for 18; 1.17, 1.24, 1.24 for 24; 1.16, 1.27, 1.27 for 25. Primary 11 at the April refit goes from 1.30 to 1.37 at days 0 to 1 and from 0.76 to 0.79 at days 7 to 14 (arm A). The September refit of Primary 13 lies after July and is not scored.
  • Coverage, q05 to q95, pooled by lead band, origin months 2025-12 to 2026-06 (weekly-block 95% intervals about 1.7 points wide each side): stored 82.4% to 84.5%, arm A 87.1%, arm B 88.0% to 88.1%, B-cross 88.0% to 88.2%, 45 days 86.8% to 86.9%, 180 days 86.9% to 87.0%. Arm B's coverage is about 1 point above arm A's, which is inside the width of the intervals.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Audit checks (median minus mean forecast, mean-forecast error, audit triggers): not applicable, because the experiment writes no forecast and scores no CRPS. No audit trigger fired.
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet reviewer found five problems: arm B clamped before averaging, arm B fitted on unclamped seed quantiles, independent day draws per cell, the final-test months loaded, and missing duplicate-key and month-pairing guards. All were fixed before the numbers above were produced.
  • Bias in the intervals: cells are chosen for an extreme stored ratio, so resampled days regress towards 1 and every percentile interval sits above its point share (the stored arm: 11.9% to 29.2% against 0.7%). Read the intervals as spread, not as bounds.

docs.title: Caveats and what to try next
docs.text:
• Caveat: each ratio rests on two windows of 7 origin days and may be noisy. The pass share rests on 151 cells that share 6 boundaries.
  • Caveat: the per-seed files exist for the normal-running output only, and for two seeds.
  • Options for a later experiment, not a plan: fit the scale on the first weeks of forecasts after each refit, or on the new model's own back-test forecasts.

docs.title: Does the slow-level state track the July to August level change at Primaries 13 and 16?
docs.text:
The slow-level state of the edge-state addendum tracks the July to August level change at Primaries 13 and 16, so the miss is a slow drift. The stored normal-running forecasts miss the observed power by +0.84 MW at Primary 13 (D18, mean power 2.1 MW before the change) and by -1.09 MW at Primary 16 (D14, 5.9 MW). The masked frozen level crossed half of that change 3 days before (id 13) and 2 days before (id 16) the residual's own crossing, and adding it to q50 halves the median absolute error at both Primaries. The level moved the median absolute error of two control Primaries by 5.5% (a fall, with an interval that includes zero) and 7.5% (a rise), which is above the 5% limit, so the verdict is partly supported. The stop rule did not fire, because neither id missed.

What it narrows. The level miss is a gradual drift that a smooth level absorbs, not an unexplained step. This is a hindsight diagnostic on a lab setting: the level was fitted on the whole record, including the window, from a different forecast's residual. July to September 2026 lies in the final-test window and is read descriptively only; no choice is made from it.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Arms and data. Arm 1: observed power minus stored q50 on normal-running rows (one row per half-hour, the smallest lead). Arm 2: fit_slow of experiment 653 (masked, frozen) on experiment 685's lag-free residual panel (ERA5 and CAMS weather at the target time, so a lab setting), noise units frozen on the residual before 2026-07-01. S1 (Huber, no mask) and S0 (30-day random walk) are the addendum's other arms, reported beside it. No forecast model was fitted, so no retraining schedule applies.
  • Controls, by the rule fixed in the plan: ids 26 and 17 (stored q05 to q95 coverage 0.89 and 0.91 in July, 0.91 and 0.86 in August). Only the 15 panel ids were candidates, because the state needs the panel.
  • Timing (main arm). Half of the change is passed at day 0 (id 13) and day 3 (id 16), counted from 2026-07-01, against day 3 and day 5 for the residual. At id 13 the level estimate rises from May, so the crossing is early. Level change is +0.41 MW at id 13 (residual +0.84) and -0.64 MW at id 16 (residual -1.09).
  • Agreement. Weekly correlation of level with residual: 0.66 at id 13 and 0.87 at id 16 (S0: 0.89 and 0.90). Best daily lag: 28 days at id 13 (the edge of the search) and 6 days at id 16.
  • Median absolute error, July to September, level added (main arm). Id 13: 0.78 to 0.39 MW, -50.3% (95% day-block interval -59.9 to -34.8). Id 16: 0.83 to 0.40 MW, -51.3% (-55.8 to -35.3). Controls: id 26 -5.5% (-9.9 to +1.3); id 17 +7.5% (+1.6 to +14.0).
  • q05 to q95 coverage, same rows. Id 13: 36% to 51%. Id 16: 49% to 66%. Control 26: 85% to 86%. Control 17: 90% to 87%. The level does not restore 90% coverage.
  • Variants. The level change is half the residual change at id 13 (+0.41 against +0.84 MW), and the mean level added there is +0.70 MW, so an offset between the two forecasts enters. The post hoc variant that adds only the change from the 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-14 mean gives -44.0% and -55.1% at ids 13 and 16 and +8.5% and -1.2% at the controls, with coverage 50% and 70% at ids 13 and 16. The random-walk arm S0 gives -52.9% and -59.9%, and +0.7% and +14.4% at the controls.
  • Caveats. The level is a smooth spline, so it ramps over months and misses the step on 2026-07-01 and the fall from late August. The residual panel belongs to a different forecast from the stored one, so a constant offset between them enters the "level" variant. Control crossing days are not meaningful because their changes are under 0.4 MW. NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so "no transfer" in experiment 685 is a lower bound. The 5% limit on the controls was met by neither control, so the main arm fails the pre-registered test on that count.
  • Checks. No new forecast was scored, so the median-minus-mean and mean-forecast audit checks do not apply, and no audit trigger fired.
  • What to try next. Fit the level causally (data before each origin only) to see whether it could be used live; this is a proposal for the maintainer.

docs.title: Method
docs.text: The code is in ml-experiments/00690-slow-level-state-on-primaries-13-and-16-july-august/ (e00690_run.py, e00690_figures.py); it imports the folders of experiments 653 and 685. Intermediate tables are in the experiment's data folder (private, not committed): weekly_miss.csv, daily_level_and_residual.parquet, results.json, and control_choice.csv. Bootstrap: 7-day blocks, 2,000 draws, paired. Review: one fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the run.

docs.title: Does a prevailing head that reads both the causal detector features and the extra lagged power inputs react to a load shift sooner than a head that reads only one of them?
docs.text:
Terms. Throughout, K1 is the frozen two-output demand neural network, and the small head is the neural network that corrects its prevailing output (experiment 652's R-haz head). B0 is that head with no extra inputs, L1 adds the extra lagged power block (experiment 681), F1 adds the causal detector features D1 to D6 (experiment 687), and FL1 adds both.

Take-home message. A head that reads both the detector features and the extra lagged power covers half of a new shift 1.75 days [-2.34, -1.24] sooner than experiment 652's head (B0), but only 0.16 days [-0.45, +0.14] sooner than the features alone (F1) and 0.49 days [-0.84, -0.13] sooner than the lags alone (L1). The pre-registered stop rule fires: the gain over the better single arm is under 0.5 days and its interval includes zero, so the lags add under 0.5 days to what the features give, and no new feature is proposed. The in-force scaled CRPS improves by 0.20 points of capacity [-0.33, -0.04], below the 0.30 bar, and false alarms on event-free rows rise by 5.1 points against B0, so the veto fails as well. Verdict: not supported.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
All scores follow experiment 687's method. CRPS is CRPS in points of capacity (1 point is 1% of a Primary's effective capacity), scaled to a q05 to q95 coverage of 0.90, mean of 2 seeds, then of the 5 development months (2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-06). Intervals are percentile bootstraps over the months (5 blocks, so coarse) or over 281 held-out events. B0, L1, and F1 are experiment 687's stored fits, and the report reproduces experiment 687's point values (bootstrap intervals differ in the second decimal).

  • Real rows first. On real event-free rows the scaled CRPS minus B0 is +0.01 [-0.04, +0.07] for FL1, +0.01 for L1, and +0.05 for F1: no arm moves. The false-alarm rate on those rows is B0 0.104, F1 0.127, L1 0.138, FL1 0.142. The verified D5 and D16 transfer of December 2025 is one episode (13,068 rows) with no known shift size, so reaction time is not scored on it. Its CRPS (descriptive): B0 9.73, F1 8.58, L1 8.63, FL1 8.67, K1 14.93.
  • Reaction time, start of an injected shift (281 held-out events), minus B0. FL1 -1.75 [-2.34, -1.24] (median -1.0), F1 -1.59 [-2.23, -0.98], L1 -1.25 [-1.86, -0.71].
  • Paired contrasts at the start. FL1 minus F1 -0.16 [-0.45, +0.14] (the better single arm, P1 fails), FL1 minus L1 -0.49 [-0.84, -0.13], F1 minus L1 -0.33 [-0.72, +0.07]. By event length (5, 10, 21, and 45 days; each event is scored under 2 seeds) FL1 minus F1 is -0.29, -0.11, -0.54, and +0.34 days.
  • Reaction time, end. FL1 minus B0 -0.61 [-0.93, -0.30] (median 0); FL1 minus F1 +0.02 [-0.21, +0.25]; FL1 minus L1 -0.16 [-0.40, +0.10].
  • Scaled CRPS minus B0, in force (P2). FL1 -0.20 [-0.33, -0.04], F1 -0.12 [-0.33, +0.07], L1 -0.25 [-0.40, -0.13]. The 0.30 bar is not met by any arm. Just ended: FL1 -0.41 [-0.61, -0.21]. Near the end, FL1 minus B0: -0.11 [-0.65, +0.42]. Event-free: -0.04 [-0.15, +0.06]. P2 is scored on in-force rows of all shift families, as in experiment 687; on held-out-family shifts only, the bar is met by every arm (FL1 -0.74, L1 -0.67, F1 -0.54), with raw scores FL1 10.22 against B0 10.96, L1 10.28, F1 10.42.
  • False alarms on event-free injected rows (P3). B0 0.182, F1 0.189, L1 0.226, FL1 0.232: FL1 is +5.1 points against B0, above the 1-point limit, like L1 (+4.4).
  • Tails, in force (unscaled). q05 to q95 coverage: B0 0.825, F1 0.850, L1 0.843, FL1 0.856. Pinball loss at q01, q05, q95, and q99: B0 0.53, 1.45, 1.51, 0.52; F1 0.43, 1.31, 1.49, 0.49; L1 0.43, 1.33, 1.41, 0.45; FL1 0.39, 1.26, 1.48, 0.49.
  • Avoidable-curtailment cost (experiment 601 units, six MW Primaries, leads 12 to 36 h). Inside a shift: B0 162,976, F1 136,173, L1 136,284, FL1 155,122. In the 7 days after the end: B0 10,786, F1 9,105, L1 9,148, FL1 7,970. All rows: B0 95,937, F1 80,090, L1 80,185, FL1 91,417. FL1 is the best in the 7 days after the end. FL1 is the worst of the three input arms inside a shift and over all rows.

docs.title: Arms, data, and method
docs.text:
• Arms. B0, L1, and F1 are loaded from experiment 687's fits (10 arms x 5 months x 2 seeds there); FL1 is B0 plus F1's columns plus L1's 16 lag columns, with the larger of the two ages opening the survival gate and dropout on the extra columns. 10 new fits.
  • Code. ml-experiments/00691-*/ imports experiment 687's folder (e00687_fit.py, e00687_score.py, e00687_report.py) and, through it, experiments 598, 606, 647, 650, and 652. Fits, scores, and weights are in data/ml-experiments/00691-*/.
  • Cadence and compute. One small head per scored month, 4 CPU processes, about 2 minutes for the fits and the scoring. No GPU. Data before 2026-07-01 only (asserted). Cleaned power, as in experiment 687.
  • Lab shortcuts. The injected world of experiment 687 (exact constant shifts, every Primary shifted in every pass, a mirrored neighbour) flatters both blocks.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, in force, points of capacity: B0 -0.34, L1 -0.40, F1 -0.51, FL1 -0.56. Mean absolute error of the mean forecast: B0 10.22, L1 9.96, F1 10.15, FL1 10.04; of the median: 10.20, 9.87, 10.18, 10.09. The mean-forecast contrasts agree in direction with the CRPS contrasts.
  • Audit triggers. The result missed its own prediction (P1, P2, P3), which the stop rule above already treats as an outcome to report plainly. The other audit triggers of the ml-experiment skill did not apply: no placebo arm was run and no arm is a subset of another arm.
  • Reviews. A Sonnet code review before the fits (no blocking findings; two optional notes accepted as cosmetic), a Sonnet check of this page against the printed report, and a Sonnet prose review (see the pull request).

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Three caveats of experiment 687 apply unchanged: the injected world flatters both blocks, the start rule counts a single noisy origin as a hit, and 2 seeds leave a per-event standard deviation of 4 to 6 days; the mean is dominated by 45-day events.
  • The interval on FL1 minus F1 (-0.45 to +0.14) does not exclude a gain of up to 0.45 days, which stays below the 0.5-day bar.
  • NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so real event-free rows may hold unlogged shifts.

docs.title: What to try next
docs.text: • Do not combine the two blocks. A head that reads the features alone gets the reaction gain with fewer false alarms; the open step is experiment 687's: open the survival gate from the newest readings, and re-test in a world with few concurrent shifts.

docs.title: Can a Claude reviewer looking at a figure of each candidate load transfer cut the event table's false transfers?
docs.text:
A Claude Sonnet model shown one picture of each candidate load transfer did not pass the precision mark we set beforehand. A Primary substation steps electricity down to a local distribution network. A load shift is a lasting change in a Primary's demand with no change in the weather, and a load transfer is a load shift that moves between two neighbouring Primaries. The event table is an algorithm that reads the power records of the Primaries and lists the transfers it finds. About three in four of the transfer ends it decodes match no injected transfer, so we asked whether a reviewer looking at a picture could remove them.

We took 613 candidate transfers that the event table (E1-J-sym, from experiment 680) decodes in 40 worlds. Each world is the real power record with synthetic ("injected") transfers added. We drew one picture per candidate and asked the reviewer nine questions and for a verdict. Precision is the share of the reviewer's "transfer" calls that were true: it was 0.45 against the pre-registered gate of 0.80. The reviewer called 24 of the 32 true transfers a transfer, and also called 29 of the 70 candidates that the injected truth labels false a transfer.

Most of the reviewer's false calls were on real-record events that the injected truth omits. Five candidates recur in 13 to 28 of the 40 worlds, which means they come from the real record under every world. The reviewer called 21 of the 22 calibration figures of these candidates a transfer, and the injected truth labels them false. NGED (the electricity distribution network operator) has told us that its event labels are an incomplete dump, so a clean half-hour may hold an event that no label covers. Every row is a candidate, never a label. No data on or after 2026-07-01 was read.

docs.title: Headline rows
docs.text:
Measure Result Precision for "transfer" on the calibration set (102 figures) 0.45 (24 of 53 calls; 95% interval 0.33 to 0.59); gate 0.80, fails Recall of the 32 true transfers (30 injected, 2 verified real) 0.75 (24 of 32; 0.58 to 0.87); gate 0.60, passes Direction of the called true transfers 23 of 24 as drawn; gate 90%, passes The two verified real transfers (D5 to D16, D3 to D22) Both called a transfer, passes Realness: "injected or real?" on 38 figures (30 injected, 8 real) 39% right (balanced accuracy, averaged over the two classes, 43%); gate 60% or less, passes (near 50% means the figures give no sign of which are real), but with 8 real figures the interval is wide Candidates that recur in 10 or more worlds, among the 460 false candidates 111, from 5 distinct real-record transfers Post hoc: precision without the 22 recurring candidates in the calibration set 0.75 (24 of 32; 0.58 to 0.87), still under 0.80, though the interval contains 0.80 False-transfer share of candidates, natural mix (before, after the gate) 0.75, then 0.56 (95% interval 0.44 to 0.66); not at the 0.45 target

The 0.56 after the gate overstates the false share. The gate keeps 21 of the 22 recurring candidates, and the 0.56 counts them as false. We did not recompute the share without them, because the 28 non-recurring false figures would give an interval too wide to compare with the 0.45 target.

Kind of candidate Called a transfer Injected transfers that the detector found 22 of 30 Verified real transfers 2 of 2 Recurring real-record transfers (labelled false) 21 of 22 Other false candidates 6 of 28 Injected look-alikes (placebos, solo shifts) 2 of 20

docs.title: What the reviewer got wrong
docs.text:
• The 8 true transfers it missed. Six were called "unclear" (a gradual donor step, a recipient dominated by solar output, a recipient that ramps over weeks, or an end beyond the record) and two "solo shift" (one Primary shows no clear step).
  • The 8 calls on candidates that do not recur. Six were on the 28 other false candidates and two on injected look-alikes. Of the 27 calls on false candidates that are not look-alikes, 4 overlap an injected transfer between the same two Primaries whose start lies 3 to 129 half-hours from the decoded start. The label "false" there comes from the rule that a true candidate starts within 24 half-hours of the injected start.
  • Example of a call on a high-confidence false candidate. In the figure below both Primaries step together at the onset and return together, as a transfer does, which is why the reviewer called it a transfer.
  • Example of a missed true transfer. The figure below is an injected transfer that the reviewer called "unclear" because the recipient's step is smaller than its day-to-day swings.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast, and mean-forecast error beside each quantile-score contrast: not applicable, because no forecast is scored.
  • Audit triggers: none fired. The result does contradict the prediction of a false-transfer share of about 0.6 before the gate (it is 0.75). Experiment 680 reports 0.77 of the ends, and the per-candidate share here is 0.75, so the prediction was only a wrong guess. The contaminated labels were found and explained by the recurrence check, which is recorded as post hoc.
  • Confidence field. Some reviewer sessions wrote a probability (such as 0.9999) in the field that asked for an integer from 1 to 5, so the confidence is not used.
  • Code review. One fresh Sonnet code reviewer ran before the first reviewer call. It found that the figure identifiers revealed the source (injected, real, or verified), that injected solo shifts were labelled false and not hard, and that the true label has no one-to-one assignment. The identifiers were randomised and the hard set widened. The one-to-one rule and the unmatched real-case step scaling were not changed, and both are small against the recurrence effect.
  • Load-shift scenarios and event plots: not applicable, because no forecast is scored. The two figures above are the example candidates.
  • Unlogged events: the recurrence check shows the real record holds at least five events that no injected label covers, so the false-transfer shares here are overstated by at least those candidates.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Candidates. A candidate is a donor end (a decoded fall) of E1-J-sym with its largest decoded partner, in each of the 40 default worlds of experiment 680 (seeds 900 to 939) with a start in 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-30. There are 613 (153 true, 460 false). A candidate is true when its donor end matches an injected donor end (same Primary, start within 24 half-hours, overlap of 0.5 or more) and a decoded partner is a partner of that injected transfer. A candidate is hard when an injected placebo, common-mode, solo-shift, or hard-negative event at either Primary starts within 2 days of its start. The spec's scorer over candidate pairs does not exist, so the "highest-scoring" false pairs are the ones with the highest detector confidence for the donor end.
  • Calibration set (102 figures). 30 true candidates drawn at random, excluding hard ones; 20 false candidates of the highest confidence, excluding hard ones; 30 false candidates drawn at random, excluding hard ones; 20 hard false candidates drawn at random; and the 2 verified real transfers. The spec asks for 400 figures including routine steps and sunny runs.
  • Figure. One image per candidate, identical for injected and real cases: neutral Primary labels, no dates, no truth marks. Panels: the donor's power and expected power, the donor's residual in noise units with the decoded step, the same for the recipient, the residual of up to 4 other neighbours, and the median residual of all Primaries. Columns: an overview from 7 days before the onset to 7 days after the end (6-hour means, capped at 60 days), and half-hourly zooms of 48 hours either side of the onset and of the end. The ERA5 and CAMS panels of the spec are left out. Figure identifiers are random three-digit numbers.
  • Figure reviewer. Claude Sonnet, never Opus, with one fixed brief (the nine questions R1 to R9 of the spec scored 0 to 2, a verdict, a direction, and a confidence, as JSON), run in fresh sessions of about 10 figures each. Each session reads only the brief and its figures and starts no sub-agent. The answer key was kept in a different folder. Cost: 14 sessions at about 93,000 tokens each, about 1.3 million tokens in all, about 9,000 tokens per figure.
  • Realness reviewer. A second brief, 4 sessions, 38 figures: 30 injected candidates and 8 real ones (the 6 real transfer pairs of experiment 680's real-record table, and the 2 verified transfers). The real record holds too few pairs for the 30 real figures the spec asks for.
  • Scoring. A call is a verdict of "transfer". Precision and recall use the calibration set with Wilson (1927) intervals. The false share after the gate is reweighted to the natural mix of the 40 worlds (153 true, 276 plain false, 184 hard false candidates), using each stratum's call rate, with a bootstrap over the figures of each stratum.
  • Post hoc recurrence check. A false candidate that has the same donor, recipient, and day in 10 or more of the 40 worlds is a real-record event, because the worlds differ only in what is injected. Five such groups cover 111 of the 460 false candidates. The check was run after the answers were read.
  • Standing practices. No refit, no forecast, no tails or curtailment cost. Cleaned power and the D18 cut before 2025-03-01 come from experiment 653's residual. CPU only, 2 cores.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00692-.../e00692_run.py: decodes the 40 worlds, lists the candidates, picks the sets, and draws the figures and the key.
  • e00692_common.py: draws one candidate figure.
  • e00692_ids.py: renames the figures to random identifiers.
  • e00692_score.py: scores the answers against the key and writes scores.json.
  • e00692_diagnose.py: post hoc check of which injected transfers overlap the reviewer's false calls.
  • e00692_figures.py: draws the call-rate figure and copies the two example candidates.
  • Private data, not in git, in data/ml-experiments/00692-event-table-reviewer-calibration-gate/: figures/ (the 140 figures), answers/ (the reviewer's JSON lines), reviewer_brief.md and realness_brief.md, answer_key_private/ (candidates.parquet, key.parquet, and diagnose.parquet), and scores.json. Inputs are experiment 680's stored real-record table and the generator of experiment 660.

docs.title: Would a perfect, causal flag for load transfers improve the Candidate demand forecast at the 16 Primaries?
docs.text:
We asked whether the demand forecast at 16 primary substations gets better when it is told exactly when a load transfer (a switch that moves load between two substations) is happening. The Candidate is the neural network that forecasts demand from weather, calendar, and recent power inputs. The prevailing head is a second neural network that adapts the Candidate's forecast to a transfer already under way. We added simulated transfers from the experiment 660 generator to the recorded power. One copy of each forecast received the logged start of every transfer (the oracle flag), and another copy received start times shifted to other dates (the placebo flag). Errors are the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), in percentage points of capacity, so a lower value is better. The perfect flag did not help. A transfer costs the Candidate 0.1 points of capacity. The prevailing head scored 0.395 points worse with the oracle flag than with the placebo flag while the target lay inside a transfer, a difference that refit noise could explain. Three refits (seeds) of the same head already differ by about 0.4 points, so the comparison cannot separate a gain or loss under about 0.5 points from noise.

Verdict: inconclusive, because the pre-registered checks failed. The rule makes the verdict inconclusive when the placebo check fails or the harm on real event-free rows exceeds 0.05 points. The placebo check gave +0.086 against a bound of 0.05, and the harm was +0.093 against the same bound (the harm comes almost entirely from one Primary). No contrast reached the 0.3-point gain that would justify the work. The Candidate was not retrained with the flag, because the no-retraining ceiling was 0.107 points. Only the prevailing head was retrained, so the oracle flag was tested on the prevailing head alone.

Contrast (points of capacity; negative is better for the first-named arm) Estimate 95% interval Bonferroni interval (three tests) C2: oracle minus placebo, target inside a transfer, injected transfers +0.395 +0.235 to +0.560 +0.202 to +0.595 C3: oracle minus placebo, target after the end, injected transfers +0.188 -0.155 to +0.492 -0.216 to +0.546 C4: oracle minus no flag, event-free real rows (5 month blocks) +0.093 -0.037 to +0.221 -0.063 to +0.242 C5: placebo minus no flag, inside a transfer, injected transfers +0.086 -0.067 to +0.230 (90%: -0.041 to +0.212) not in the family

Two ceilings fall short of the predicted gain of 0.3 to 1.0 points. The no-retraining ceiling is 0.107 points (stage 0, below). Two baselines with no fitted weights bound the prevailing head's gain: one estimates when a transfer began from residuals, and the other is told. The second minus the first is -0.068 points inside a transfer and +0.165 after the transfer ends. The oracle age does lift the age floor (the lowest transfer age the head sees): the share of rows inside a transfer with a non-zero survival probability is 0.774 for the arm with no flag, 0.998 for the oracle arm, and 0.898 for the placebo arm, on the deciding bank.

The intervals ignore refit noise. The audit found that the seed-to-seed standard deviation of one fit is 0.395 points inside a transfer, so a contrast over three seeds and two folds has a standard error of about 0.23 points. One fit (oracle arm, fold 2026-05, seed 1) scored 4.2 points worse than the other two oracle fits of that fold, in every (fold, pass, Primary) group. All three oracle fits of that fold stopped after 5 epochs with the best validation loss at the first epoch. Without the seed-1 fit, C2 is about +0.05.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Six real transfers, day-ahead medians of each arm. The shaded band is the logged transfer. The oracle, placebo, and no-flag heads exist only from the 2026-02 fold, so the December 2025 panels show the Candidate alone and the two hazard baselines. Observed power is the cleaned reading.

The 14-day fans show medians only. Each figure shows the medians of one 09:00 origin out to 14 days. The figures draw only medians, because quantile bands would need the full per-row quantile files, so they cannot show whether the bands widen with lead.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast: not computed, because the stored scores hold quantiles and no mean.
  • The oracle arm is worst on both CRPS and the error of the median. On the deciding bank, inside a transfer, the normalised mean absolute error of the median is 12.65 for the no-flag arm, 13.64 for the oracle arm, and 12.46 for the placebo arm. The CRPS values are 7.75, 8.23, and 7.84. The placebo arm beats the no-flag arm on the error of the median and loses on CRPS, so the two measures differ in direction for that contrast, which fires audit trigger 3 (an error-direction mismatch).
  • Four audit triggers fired: the placebo control failed its equivalence bound (trigger 1), the result contradicts the pre-registered gain of 0.3 to 1.0 points (trigger 2), the median and the quantile scores differ in direction (trigger 3), and a control moved the score by more than its own interval's half-width (trigger 5). The audit report, data/ml-experiments/briefs/e693_audit_report.md, lists six findings; the page accepted five and did not act on one:
    • Accepted: the printed contrasts reproduce to three decimals. Nothing to change.
    • Accepted: the intervals ignore refit noise, and the placebo check could not pass at plus or minus 0.05. The page states both, and the verdict stays inconclusive.
    • Accepted: one oracle fit (fold 2026-05, seed 1) stopped at its first epoch. The page reports it and the contrast without it. The fit was not rerun, because the pre-registered rule fixes three seeds.
    • Accepted: the placebo is not neutral (it lifts the age floor on rows without a transfer, and the flag is almost always 0 on real training rows). Listed in the lessons and the advice.
    • Accepted: leave-one-out. The harm on real event-free rows (C4) comes almost entirely from one Primary that has no bank rows; without it C4 is about 0.000, and its sign flips by fold.
    • Not done: ten or more seeds per arm, a placebo from an independent world, and matched training and deciding generators. Each would change the pre-registered design.
  • Two Sonnet code reviews ran before any quoted fit or score. Review 1 (the flag module and stage 0) found five must-fix problems, all fixed. Review 2 (the head banks, head data, and head fit) found one must-fix problem, a reversed window in dilate that dropped half the "after the end" rows. Review 2's other findings were recorded as caveats: the injected-bank residuals lose the first 8 days of each month (affects only the hazard baselines), and phase P3 also holds transfers that began and ended after the origin's freshest reading.

docs.title: Departures from the plan
docs.text:
• The bank panel runs 15 days past the fold's scored months, so the longest horizons of the last origins lie inside it.
  • Phase flags count neighbour-only rows as "lag inside" on bank L. On bank F the phase uses the oracle's in-progress state at the origin's freshest reading (the origin minus 6 hours). Phase P1 needs the oracle's in-progress state and a target inside a transfer. Phase P2 needs the oracle's in-progress state and a target within 14 days after the end. Phase P3 needs no in-progress state and a target within 14 days after an end.
  • Bank L injects 3 simulated transfers per Primary per year. At 6, 99.7% of rows inside a transfer also had a flagged neighbouring Primary, so the flags could not tell the two apart. Settings: 48 passes, class mix edge_transfer 0.55, edge_transfer_unseen_donor 0.10, edge_transfer_unseen_recipient 0.15, and permanent_shift 0.20, hard_negatives=False, and seed 693000 + 100 × (year × 12 + month) + pass. Bank F reuses the same worlds. Bank F's deciding bank holds 150 to 197 events per scored month over 48 passes (printed by e00693_event_counts.py), under the brief's target of about 200, so each month's interval is wider than planned.
  • The Bonferroni family has three tests (C2, C3, C4-prevailing), because the stage 0 gate dropped C1 and C4-NRA.
  • The one-fold screen checked only whether the oracle flag lifts the age floor. On the 2026-02 fold the share of rows inside a transfer with a non-zero survival probability rose from 0.776 to 0.998, so the 2026-05 fold was also run.
  • Not done: positive controls beyond the two ceilings, the flag-permutation wiring check, the benchmark rows (climatology, the manual heuristic, experiments 677 and 667), the four load-shift scenarios on every arm (real rows only), the q01 and q99 coverage and pinball loss, the cold-winter-night and avoidable-curtailment tables, the reaction-time measurement, and quantile-band figures.
  • The sensitivity with label-plus-verified spans is in the printed head report only.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
• Arms. A0 (default: experiment 677's step-8 Candidate network and the adopted lag-input prevailing head of experiment 681), A1 (default plus oracle flags), A2 (placebo flags with matched span lengths, overlaps, and per-Primary counts). Stage 0 adds the inference-only ceilings A0-mask, A0-clean, and oracle B-haz (the no-fit hazard baseline of experiment 667).
  • Folds. Quarterly refits at the maintainer's request (cut-offs 2025-11-01, 2026-02-01, 2026-05-01), scored on valid times 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-30 only. Seeds 0 to 2.
  • Information sets. The Candidate lag flags use 09:00 UTC origins, and every lag lies at least 24 hours before the origin. The prevailing head uses the 12:00 UTC contract origin, and its freshest reading is 6 hours before the network origin. in_progress is the transfer state at that freshest reading, never at the origin: it is 1 only if the onset is at or before it and no end is at or before it. The oracle age is the origin minus the earliest onset in progress, and is 0 when in_progress is 0. The flags cover the row's own Primary for the prevailing head, and the own Primary and its electrical neighbours for the Candidate. The placebo flags obey the same rules. Both rules are asserted per row in code.
  • Banks (pre-registered). Deciding banks L and F use the experiment 660 generator with hard_negatives=False, class probabilities edge_transfer 0.55, edge_transfer_unseen_donor 0.10, edge_transfer_unseen_recipient 0.15, and permanent_shift 0.20, events_per_primary_year=3, and 48 passes, injected into the cleaned panel of 15 Primaries (the 16th has no noise unit) from 60 days before the fold's first scored month to the end of its scored months. A pass's seed is 693000 plus 100 times (calendar year times 12 plus fold month) plus the pass number, so all arms and network seeds see the same injected worlds. A smoke pass at 6 events per Primary-year left 99.7% of phase P1 rows with a neighbour flag, so the rate was lowered before any quoted run. If a scored month still holds under about 200 events, the pass count is raised in a commit before the first fit. Check banks: experiment 581's generator with seeds disjoint from training (bank L), and experiment 650's held-out passes (bank F).
  • Contrasts (A1 minus A2 unless stated; negative is better). C1: no-retrain-arm (NRA) output, bank L, phases P1 plus P2, November 2025 to June 2026. C2: prevailing output, bank F, phase P1, February to June 2026. C3: prevailing output, bank F, phase P2, February to June 2026. C4-NRA and C4-prevailing: A1 minus A0 on real rows with an event-free origin and target (phase P4), verified transfers deciding. C5 (outside the family): A2 minus A0 on banks L and F and on real P4 rows. Phases: P1 = a lag (for the prevailing head, the origin) is inside a transfer and the target is inside it; P2 = same, but the target is after the end; P3 = lags clean, target after the end; P4 = event-free origin and target. Each contrast has its own row set: oracle693_c1_bankL_nov25_jun26, oracle693_c2_c3_bankF_feb_jun26, and oracle693_c4_real_p4. Experiment 677's file has another row_set_id, so A0 is re-scored on these rows (valid times to 2026-06-30) and checked against 677's stored scores, rather than read as 677's file.
  • Bars apply to the unweighted deciding-bank contrast. The reweighting to the verified transfers' depth and duration and the implied all-rows annual effect are reported beside it. Each contrast is also reported per seed.
  • Stage 0 gate. Seed-mean CRPS(A0) minus CRPS(A0-clean) on bank L, phases P1 plus P2, all three folds pooled. If under 0.3 points, the NRA retraining is not run, C1 and C4-NRA are not computed, the Bonferroni family is C2, C3, and C4-prevailing (three tests), and "supported" needs C2 or C3 at 0.3, C4-prevailing within 0.05, and C5.
  • Screen advance rule. Run stage 0, then fold 2 for A0, A1, and A2 (all numbers interim). Continue to the other folds only if A1's copied share on bank L is at most half of A0's, the share of P1 rows with p above 0 is higher in A1 than in A0, and scoring A1 with its flags permuted changes its predictions. Otherwise stop and debug the wiring.
  • Reading a null. A not supported or small gain verdict supports "switching labels belong in evaluation, not in the forecast" only if A0-clean (bank L) and oracle B-haz (bank F) have been computed and the share of P1 rows with p above 0 is higher in A1 than in A0. Otherwise the verdict stays as scored and the consequence is withheld. A supported verdict on C2 or C3 alone means a detector is worth testing as an input to the prevailing head, with a degradation sweep next.
  • R-haz fit boundary. Every R-haz training row has its target valid time before the fold's cut-off, and its labels (end, verification) known before the cut-off. Spans of verified real transfers are truncated at the cut-off. Both are asserted per fold.
  • Standing practices followed: cleaned data (count of substation_zero half-hours printed per fold), D15 and D18 cut before 2025-03-01, every network saved, stored predictions reused, origin-time weather only (asserted per row), no new calendar inputs (the Candidate's own date-time encoder is unchanged), and normalised MAE of the median in every table. The four load-shift scenarios (all rows; outside events and at least 7 days after; inside events; the 7 days after) are reported, with a day-ahead forecast, a 14-day forecast, and at least 6 load-shift time series across both metering groups. Departures: quarterly instead of monthly refits (the maintainer's request; experiment 677's advice favours monthly, and any gain here applies to quarterly refits), and a one-fold screen instead of four seasonal months.
  • Earlier advice and background. docs/ml-experiments/background/index.md, data-processing.md, and the advice lists of experiments 667, 677, 681, 687, and the switching-detector experiments were read. The plan follows experiment 677's advice to judge on copied share and event-free error together, and treats a seed contrast under 0.03 points as unresolved without five seeds (experiment 651); it departs from the advice to refit monthly.
  • Caveats. NGED's logs miss transfers, so event-free real rows may hold transfers no label covers and the C4 harm figure is optimistic. C4 compares A1 with A0 on rows the oracle never flags, so it measures the extra input columns and refit noise. C4's real rows are four or five month blocks, so its interval is coarse.

docs.title: Stage 0 result
docs.text:
The no-retrain ceiling is 0.107 points of capacity, under the 0.3 gate, so the no-retrain-arm retraining is not run. Stage 0 scored experiment 677's stored step-8 P7+D50 networks on bank L (the experiment 660 generator, 48 passes per fold, seeds 0 to 2, folds 2025-11, 2026-02, and 2026-05; 47.9 million scored rows). The gate statistic is CRPS(A0) minus CRPS(A0-clean) on phases P1 and P2 pooled over the three folds: +0.107 points, 95% interval [+0.087, +0.129] from 2,000 resamples of (fold, pass, Primary) clusters. By fold it is +0.125, +0.073, and +0.128.

  • Copied share. A0 copies 0.031 of the day-lag shift into its median, and A0-mask copies 0.003.
  • Masking. A0 minus A0-mask is +0.027 [+0.004, +0.050] on P1 and negative on P2.
  • Phase P3. The gap is 0.000, as it must be when every lag is clean.
  • Consequence. C1 and C4-NRA are dropped, the Bonferroni family becomes C2, C3, and C4-prevailing, and stage 1 retrains only the prevailing head.

Source: scores/stage0_report.md, printed by e00693_stage0_report.py.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Architecture, Candidate. The Candidate is experiment 677's step-8 P7+D50 neural network. Experiment 677 fine-tuned one copy per quarterly cut-off (2025-11-01, 2026-02-01, 2026-05-01) and seed (0 to 2). This experiment reads those copies without retraining them. The head's origin is the 09:00 origin of the Candidate, so its freshest reading is at 03:00 UTC, 6 hours earlier.
  • Architecture, prevailing head. The head is experiment 667's survival-hazard head with 14 daily hazards on the Candidate's quantiles, with experiment 681's 14 residual lags (28 columns), 93 inputs. Two hidden layers of 64 units output a signed depth, a spread, and 14 hazards.
  • Arms. A0 has no flag. A1 adds three columns (whether a transfer is known to be in progress, the logarithm of its age in days, and the age divided by 30) and takes the larger of the heuristic age and the oracle age as the structural age. A2 is A1 with every Primary's spans rolled circularly inside one window by one offset per month and pass, which keeps nearly every span's length and each Primary's span count (a span that straddles the window edge splits in two). The hazard baselines have no fit: B uses the heuristic age and OB the oracle age with a survival probability of 0 outside a transfer.
  • The oracle knows whether the freshest reading (the 09:00 origin minus 6 hours) lay inside a transfer and when that transfer began; it never knows the end or the depth.
  • Training regime. Each head trains on the real rows and the injected rows of experiment 650's 12 training passes of the months before its cut-off, only on valid times before the cut-off, with the loss, optimiser, and early stopping of experiments 647 and 652 (30 to 75 seconds per fit on a CPU core). The 2025-11 fold has fewer than two earlier banks, so that fold uses only the two baselines B and OB. A quarterly head is applied to all three months of its fold.
  • Stage 0 scores the stored Candidate on bank L (no retraining) with the observed lags (A0-clean), the injected lags (A0), and the injected lags with every flagged lag masked (A0-mask).
  • Measurement. Valid times 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-30 for stage 0, and 2026-02-01 to 2026-06-30 for every head contrast (the heads exist from the 2026-02 fold). CRPS is twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles, in points of capacity, of the seed-mean forecast. The truth is the unshifted observed power on bank L and the shifted power on bank F. Bank L and the deciding half of bank F both come from the experiment 660 generator (48 passes per fold); bank F's check bank is experiment 650's held-out passes 200 to 203. Real rows use experiment 580's verified transfers (the label-plus-verified set is a sensitivity). Intervals resample clusters of (fold, pass, Primary) for banks and calendar months for real rows, 2,000 resamples; the Bonferroni level is for three tests.
  • Compute. Each head fit took 30 to 75 CPU-seconds, and the bank forecasts took about 30 minutes of GPU time per fold. No money was spent.

docs.title: Can the on/off state of the gas engine at D8 be tracked from the substation's raw half-hourly reading alone, with the number of units and the unit size inferred?
docs.text:
The tracker scores F1 0.68 on the one real engine record we hold, and higher on easier synthetic schedules. We asked whether the number of gas-engine units running at a substation (0 to 3), and the size of each unit, can be inferred from the substation's own reading, with no price, no weather, and no forecast of ordinary demand to subtract. The test case is D8, a primary substation (a "Primary") whose reading is half-hourly apparent power in megavolt-amperes (MVA) and which has a gas engine of three units connected nearby. A metered gas-engine generator, labelled "Gas A", has its own output recorded for about 44 days (2,054 half-hours). We subtracted that recorded output from the readings of other Primaries, which makes a known answer ("injection"), and scored each tracker half-hour by half-hour with the F1 score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall of the flag "a unit is running"). On Gas A's record alone the best tracker scores F1 0.68 (precision 0.61, recall about 0.76); pooled with four synthetic schedules built from the record, it scores 0.82. The tracker flagged none of the half-hours of the same Primaries without injection. The trackers extend the load-disaggregation idea of Hart (1992) and Kolter and Jaakkola (2012), in which a hidden state for each appliance is read from the total.

The pre-registered table reads supported, and the recorded verdict is partly supported, because an audit found the gate was not robust. The pre-registered table passes every probe, with thin margins: the best tracker (M2, a filter over demand level and units running; M0 pairs steps and M1 is a count model, both defined in Method; K is the number of units and u the unit size) scores F1 0.819 under the folded rule and 0.805 under the signed rule, against a bar of 0.80. The audit (by a fresh Sonnet agent, using its own scoring code) reproduced every stored count and then found three problems. First, the real record alone scores 0.68, because the 4 synthetic schedules are easier than the record (an idealised record, with output exactly a whole number of units, scores only 0.735 too). Second, the fold (the assumption that the apparent-power reading folds when demand is near the engine's output) has no demonstrated benefit: removing it changes the record's F1 by +0.017 under one injection rule and -0.014 under the other, and both intervals include zero. Third, the fitted unit size is a coarse-grid result: on a 0.05 MW grid the fit for D8 is 1.65 MW, below the pre-registered range of 1.7 to 2.3 MW, and the engine record's own unit size is 1.97 MW. This reading is post hoc, and with it P1 fails, which gives partly supported.

On D8 itself, without any engine record, the tracker finds three units and flags 27% of half-hours from 2023-09 to 2025-02. The fit gives K = 3 units of 1.75 MW (on a 0.25 MW grid). Using a wider range of unit sizes, three units beat one 5 MVA block by about 2,500 on the Bayesian information criterion, so the cap of three units does not create this answer. The fold explains the step directions at low demand: from a level below 3 MVA, 626 of 627 large steps are rises. Fitting without the fold changes the flagged share only from 0.268 to 0.267. From 2025-03-24, when 11 kV solar was connected, the fitted size moves to 2.25 MW (a move of 0.50 MW on the coarse grid, exactly the pre-registered limit, and about 0.7 MW on the fine grid, which would trigger the inconclusive rule if applied post hoc). The cause of the move is untested. After 2026-03 the fit changes to 2 units of 3.5 MW. That change is consistent with experiment 194's finding that the engine fades from D8's reading in 2026, but the count model does not show it.

On the one 1 MW schedule we tried, the tracker almost never finds the units. M2's F1 on injected 1 MW units is 0.12, and it chose "no engine" in 31 of 44 segments, On that one 1 MW schedule, M2 chose at least one unit in only 13 of 44 segments.

All five pre-registered probes (P1 to P5) hold at their pre-registered reading.

Probe Prediction Result Holds P1 K = 3 and a unit size of 1.7 to 2.3 MW on D8, 2023-09 to 2025-02 K = 3, 1.75 MW (1.65 MW on a 0.05 MW grid, post hoc) yes at the pre-registered grid; no on the fine grid P2, folded rule F1 ≥ 0.80, precision ≥ 0.80, recall ≥ 0.80 at 2 and 3 units and ≥ 0.50 at 1 unit, switch error ≤ 1 half-hour 0.819, 0.828, 0.87 and 0.87, 0.72, median 0 (0.71 of true switches matched) yes P2, signed rule same 0.805, 0.824, 0.85 and 0.86, 0.68, median 0 (0.72 matched) yes P3 At most 3% of half-hours flagged and at most 1 active day a month on history without injection, at each of 8 Primaries 0.00% and 0.00 days at all 8 yes P4 M2 beats M0 by at least 0.10 F1, with an interval above zero +0.238 (folded), +0.170 (signed) yes P5 The fold predicts held-out months of D8 better better in 9 of 9 months, +51.6 log-likelihood units yes

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Phase A: D8's engine appears as steps of about 5 MVA, and the direction depends on the level. The engine record reproduces experiment 194's counts exactly (1,704, 137, 133, and 80 half-hours at 0, 1, 2, and 3 units, of 2,054), and one unit puts out 1.97 MW. The record holds 55 running spells (experiment 194 counted 56), with a median of 4 half-hours. D8's reading has steps of about 5 MVA only after the engine connected (Figure 2). The fall that follows an engine start grows with the reading before it, as a folded reading predicts (Figure 3). From a level below 3 MVA, 626 of 627 merged steps of at least 1.5 MVA in 2023-09 to 2025-02 are rises. From 8 to 10 MVA, 259 of 260 are falls (Figure 4). No local maximum of the step histogram sits at 1.75 MW or 3.5 MW, so three units of 1.75 MW is a model fit and not a visible pattern.

Phase B: known answers. Figure 6 shows one injected segment. Figure 7 gives the scores pooled over the engine record and four synthetic schedules, which are built by resampling the record's runs. The intervals are 95%, from resampling schedule-weeks and then segments.

Tracker F1, folded rule F1, signed rule Precision (folded) Recall (folded) M0, difference pairing 0.581 [0.500, 0.646] 0.635 [0.550, 0.701] 0.467 0.769 M1, count model on differences 0.792 [0.746, 0.832] 0.838 [0.788, 0.880] 0.775 0.810 M2, grid filter 0.819 [0.777, 0.857] 0.805 [0.765, 0.842] 0.828 0.810 M2-dwell, grid filter with a minimum dwell 0.778 [0.746, 0.808] 0.765 [0.731, 0.795] 0.769 0.788

"Folded rule" and "signed rule" are the two ways of subtracting the engine's output from a Primary's reading. The folded rule subtracts it from the real power behind the reading and reads the result back as apparent power. The signed rule subtracts it from the reading directly.

The three planned contrasts, at 98.3% (Bonferroni for three), are in the table.

Contrast (difference in F1) Folded rule Signed rule C1, M2 minus M0 (threshold +0.10) +0.238 [+0.153, +0.352] +0.170 [+0.083, +0.288] C2, M2 minus M1 (threshold 0) +0.027 [+0.009, +0.047] -0.032 [-0.049, -0.013] C3, M2-dwell minus M2 (threshold 0) -0.041 [-0.069, -0.018] -0.040 [-0.067, -0.018]

M0 is a weak baseline, because after a large fall it stays flagged until a matching rise, so it flags 12.6% to 37.6% of half-hours without injection at six of the eight Primaries. The fair comparison is M1, and M1 and M2 nearly tie: C2 changes sign with the injection rule. The minimum dwell of 2 half-hours lowers the pooled F1 under both rules, but on the record alone M2-dwell scores slightly higher than M2 (0.686 against 0.678 folded, 0.679 against 0.675 signed), so the pooled loss comes from the synthetic schedules.

Schedule by schedule (M2, folded rule), the tracker finds engines of 2 MW and 3 MW units, and it misses 1 MW units.
