Where the tracker finds the engine, the fitted unit size is near the true size on the 0.25 MW grid: 2.00 MW for 2 MW units, 3.00 MW for 3 MW units, and 1.00 MW for 1 MW units. For the record, 36 of 44 segments choose 1.75 MW, against a true 1.97 MW. The audit found that the log-likelihood profile over unit size has a dip at 2.0 MW and further modes beyond it.

On real D8, the fitted size and the share flagged shift when the 11 kV solar was connected.

Era of D8 M2 units and size M2 share flagged M1 units and size M2 without fold units and size 2023-09 to 2025-02 3, 1.75 MW 0.268 3, 1.75 MW 3, 1.75 MW 2025-03-24 to 2026-02 3, 2.25 MW 0.384 3, 1.50 MW 3, 1.50 MW 2026-03 to 2026-06 2, 3.50 MW 0.262 3, 1.50 MW 3, 1.75 MW

K1 is D8's own 44-day reading with Gas A's record subtracted; it does not decide, because D8's reading already holds whatever D8's own engine did, and Gas A is a separate metered engine, so some of the false positives may be real running. M2 scores F1 0.769 (284 true positives, 105 false positives, 66 false negatives), M1 0.731, M2-dwell 0.709, and M0 0.534.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median forecast minus mean forecast, and the error of the mean or median forecast beside each quantile-score contrast: not applicable, because the experiment forecasts nothing.
  • Leave one Primary out (trigger 4): C1 stays between +0.227 and +0.245 (folded) and between +0.156 and +0.213 (signed). C2 stays positive (+0.006 to +0.034) under the folded rule and negative (-0.007 to -0.039) under the signed rule. No sign changes.
  • Triggers that fired, and the audit. Trigger 1 (a known-answer test fails): the real record alone misses the F1 bar (0.678 folded, 0.675 signed), the 1 MW schedule scores 0.12, and K1 scores 0.77. Trigger 5 (a simpler arm beats the arm that contains it, or a control moves the score): M1 beats M2 under the signed rule, and the fold barely changes D8's fit. Trigger 7 (a later design depends on the result): the inventory project would. A fresh Sonnet agent audited the experiment with its own scoring code, and its report is in the private data/ml-experiments/briefs/e694_audit/ folder.
  • Audit findings and how each was triaged.
    • Accepted: the stored counts replicate exactly. The audit's own injection, window offsets, truth, and week clusters matched all 264 stored comparisons (44 segments, both rules, M0, M1, M2).
    • Accepted: the pooled F1 overstates the tracker. The write-up now leads with the real record's F1 of 0.68. An alternative truth (output above 0.3 MW counts as running) raises the record's precision only from 0.615 to 0.655 and leaves F1 unchanged, and an idealised record scores 0.735, so the cause is the record's switching structure and not ramps.
    • Accepted: the fold has no demonstrated benefit. Without the fold, the record's F1 changes by +0.017 (folded rule, 95% interval -0.006 to +0.041, fold wins 19 of 44 segments) and -0.014 (signed rule, -0.041 to +0.011, 11 of 44). The take-home no longer claims a benefit.
    • Accepted: the unit size is a coarse-grid result. On a 0.05 MW grid, D8's fit is 1.65 MW, and the move between eras is about 0.7 MW. The write-up reports this as a post hoc reading and the verdict becomes partly supported. The experiment did not rerun P1 on the fine grid.
    • Accepted, and the control run by the audit: zero false alarms are not only "no engine" selection. Forcing 3 units at 1.75 MW or 2.0 MW on the 44 segments without injection flags a mean of 0.1% of half-hours (maximum 1.9%).
    • Accepted: three units beat one 5 MVA block. With a unit-size grid to 6.5 MW, the information criterion prefers 3 units by about 2,500 on D8 and by 60 to 350 on injected segments.
    • Deferred to the next experiment: a harder, record-like synthetic schedule, and a grid of 0.05 MW in the fits.
  • Fold versus no fold on real D8: the fold predicts held-out months better in 9 of 9, by 51.6 log-likelihood units in total, but the fitted units, size, and flagged share are almost the same with and without it (0.268 and 0.267).
  • Code review: a fresh Sonnet reviewer found one blocking bug (the backward pass used the transpose of the level kernel, so smoothed marginals were wrong near zero demand) and eight advisory points. The bug is fixed before every number on this page. Seven of the eight advisory points were applied. The eighth is left as designed: matching a true switch to the nearest flagged switch of either direction. The share of true switches matched (0.62 to 0.82) is reported beside the median error.
  • Write-up and prose reviews: two fresh Sonnet reviewers found no number that disagrees with the printed reports. Their findings on overclaims, undefined terms, and pronouns are applied, except where a finding would have repeated a statement made above.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text:
• A penalty on running time was added after one smoke test. The first test on one Primary showed that differences alone cannot tell "0 units" from "1 unit held all the time", and the count model learned "one unit on" as its resting state (5,238 of 5,760 half-hours). Every fit now multiplies each half-hour's likelihood by exp(-0.02 k) for k units running. The penalty leans the Bayesian information criterion towards K = 0 (about 17 log-likelihood units for 5% running over 5,760 half-hours). The audit's forced-3-unit control shows the zero false alarms hold without that selection.
  • The prior transition matrix has a stay probability of 0.995, not 0.9. With 0.9, a first smoke test chose K = 0 on an injected segment, because each half-hour in the same state costs log 0.9 once the model allows switches.
  • K and u are selected in two steps, not by a full grid. The unit size is profiled at K = 3, then K = 0 to 3 are each refitted by 3 rounds of expectation-maximisation at that unit size.
  • The reactive floor q is fixed at 0.14 MVA and is not fitted.
  • The verdict table has a default branch. Any combination the plan did not list is not supported. No result fell into it. The verdict partly supported follows the audit's post hoc fine-grid reading, as set out above.
  • K1 uses the same injection code as the other segments (both rules), and it is placed by timestamp. The record has one gap of 12 half-hours, which is not scored in K1. The host segments use the record as stored, so their schedule is shorter by the gap.
  • P5 holds if the total difference is above zero and the fold wins at least two thirds of the held-out months, a definition fixed in the scoring code before the result was read. The held-out months are the even-numbered months counted from 2023-09. P5's likelihood leaves out the penalty on running time.
  • One D16 segment was dropped because under 90% of its half-hours were present, leaving 44 segments.

docs.title: What the next experiment should answer
docs.text: The tracker is not yet good enough to trust on its own, and four questions remain open. Does a fit on a 0.05 MW grid change the unit size? How does the tracker score on a harder synthetic schedule built with the real record's ramps and part load? Are the engines registered in the Embedded Capacity Register found, and no others, at Primaries the tracker has not seen? What happens to a unit of 1 MW? The maintainer proposed a further use: if the engine is tracked well, subtract it from the series, train the demand forecaster on the cleaned series, and add back a climatology of the engine at forecast time. That use needs the tracker's recall to be high, and it fails if the engine responds to something predictable other than price that the climatology cannot reproduce.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture: the design of each tracker.

  • All four trackers read only the segment's reading in MVA, with a causal spread of the lag-1 difference: 1.4826 times the median absolute difference at the same half-hour of the day over the previous 28 days (at least 7 earlier days, floor 0.03 MVA), rounded to one of 8 log-spaced levels.
  • M0 merges consecutive same-sign differences that each exceed 4 spreads, opens a spell at a merged fall of at least 1.5 MVA, and closes it at the next merged rise of at least half the fall.
  • M1 is a hidden Markov model on the number of units k (0 to 3). The lag-1 difference is -(change in k) times u plus Student-t noise (4 degrees of freedom) at the spread. Any jump in k is allowed.
  • M2 is a grid filter on the demand level L and k. L lies on a 0.1 MVA grid from 0 to 22 MVA and does a random walk with Student-t steps (4 degrees of freedom) at the spread. The reading is sqrt((L - k u)^2 + q^2) with q = 0.14 MVA, plus Student-t noise with scale 0.08 MVA. The forward pass costs O(T K G) for G = 221 grid points.
  • M2-dwell expands the state to k and an age (1 or at least 2 half-hours), so that k cannot change twice in successive half-hours. This is an explicit-duration model in the sense of Yu (2010), with the shortest possible minimum duration. It reuses the units and size that M2 selected for the same segment.
  • A half-hour is flagged when the smoothed probability that k is at least 1 exceeds 0.5. The filtered (online) flag is stored too.
  • No tracker uses a demand forecast, the price, the weather, or Gas A's record when it fits.

Training regime: how each tracker is fitted, and on what.

  • Each segment is fitted on its own reading. The unit size u is profiled over 0.5 to 3.5 MW in steps of 0.25 MW at K = 3. Then K = 0 to 3 are refitted by 3 rounds of expectation-maximisation at that size and compared by the Bayesian information criterion. Then 5 rounds of expectation-maximisation fit the transition matrix, with a prior of 5 pseudo-counts.
  • The synthetic schedules resample the record's runs (a unit level and a duration) with replacement. Seeds 0 to 3 give 3 units of 2 MW and decide the pooled score. Seeds 4 to 7 give 3 units of 1 MW, 3 units of 3 MW, 1 unit of 2 MW, and 2 units of 2 MW, and are reported only.
  • Segments: 28 days of history for the spread, then 120 tracked days, with the schedule injected from day 38. The first period ("pre-solar") has 3 consecutive segments per Primary from 2022-01-01, before the 11 kV solar connected near D8. The second period ("solar") has 3 from 2025-04-01. The Primaries are D3, D4, D11, D14, D16, D2, and D10. D8 has 3 segments before the engine connected on 2023-06-13.
  • No GPU was used. The false-alarm pass took about 7 CPU-minutes and the injections about 4 CPU-hours, on 24 cores.

Measurement: how the trackers are scored.

  • Two injection rules (folded and signed, defined above) are run on every segment.
  • Scored: half-hour F1, precision, and recall for "any unit running" in the injected window, recall by the number of units truly running, and the distance in half-hours from each true switch to the nearest flagged switch (within 6).
  • Intervals: 10,000 cluster-bootstrap draws. A cluster is one schedule-week (7 per schedule), resampled with replacement, and segments are resampled within each drawn cluster. Contrasts are read at 98.3%.
  • False alarms are scored on the same segments without injection: the share of half-hours flagged, and the days with at least 4 flagged half-hours.
  • The engine record's own counts are checked before any tracker runs, and the check passed.
  • P5: fit on the odd months and score on the even months of D8's 2023-09 to 2025-02 era, with the fitted parameters frozen.

docs.title: Does a demand forecast trained on D8's reading with the gas engine removed, plus a climatology of the engine added back at forecast time, forecast D8's metered apparent power better than a forecast trained on the raw reading?
docs.text:
This experiment asks whether a gas engine's output can be taken out of one substation's recorded demand before a neural network learns from it, and added back as an average when forecasting. The substation, D8, is one of the 16 Primary substations (the substations that supply the local distribution network) that this research forecasts. A gas engine, a set of generating units that run on and off, is connected behind D8's meter, so its output is included in D8's recorded power. An on and off tracker, from experiment 694, infers from D8's half-hourly reading alone how many of the engine's units are running.

We compared a neural network trained on the raw reading with one trained on the cleaned reading plus an add-back. Arm A0 is the neural network trained on the raw reading. Arm A1 removes the tracked engine output from the training data and from the recent-power inputs, and adds the engine back to each forecast as an average: for each half-hour of the day, separately for weekdays and weekends, the share of past half-hours in which each number of units ran, over the previous 12 weeks with recent weeks weighted more. Each arm is refitted at the start of each of 8 months from 2025-11 to 2026-06, with 3 random seeds (starting points for the training's random numbers) per refit. The score is the CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, in which smaller is better) of the forecast of D8's metered apparent power. Apparent power is in MVA (megavolt-amperes), and scores are in points of capacity, which are percentage points of D8's effective capacity of 10.379 MVA.

No gain was found, and cleaning plus a calendar add-back is not worth porting. The verdict is not supported, branch 8 of the pre-registered verdict table. Branch 8 is the default that applies when no earlier branch does: no leakage test failed, the reproduction gate G0 (a refit of A0 must match experiment 677's stored result) and the tracker gate G1 (the tracker must find an injected engine) passed, the three seeds agree on the sign of C1, and C1 shows no gain. The planned contrast C1, A1 minus A0, is +0.117 points, with a 98.3% interval from -0.070 to +0.412 and a t interval from -0.037 to +0.268. A gain needs both intervals below zero and an estimate of at least 0.398 points (5.5% of A0's own score). The lower bound of -0.070 rules out any gain above about 0.07 points, so the predicted gain of 0.3 to 1.0 points is ruled out.

A post hoc reading, not pre-registered, suggests that A1 is probably about 0.1 points worse over all rows. It averages the 3 seeds and then resamples whole origin months, which gives +0.036 to +0.245 for C1 at 98.3%. A bootstrap over only 8 months under-covers, so the reading is suggestive. The library interval is 2.3 times wider (0.48 against 0.21) mainly because it draws one seed per resample, and the t interval stays the decision interval.

One open question is whether the engine's state can be forecast from information available at the forecast origin. An upper limit that reads the engine's state at the valid time (the time being forecast) lowers the error by 1.4 to 2.4 points against the raw arm A0, but no forecast has that state. In a private analysis of one 43-day record of an engine's output and of the tracker's labels for D8, the state's persistence improved the Brier score of "running" within about a day, and no forecastable input beat a calendar climatology beyond a day, except possibly a wind forecast out to a few days. Two options follow, and neither is committed: part 3 of this series, which gives the neural network origin-time engine-state features (the tracker's state at the lag times and the engine's trailing running share for the forecast half-hour), and a pre-registered test of a wind forecast as a predictor of the engine's state at days 2 to 5.

docs.title: Predictions against outcomes
docs.text:
Three of the six pre-registered predictions fail, and two hold only in part. "Bound" is defined under "Terms used in the tables below".

Prediction Outcome P1: A1 lowers CRPS by 0.3 to 1.0 points and the normalised MAE of the median by 0.5 to 1.5 Fails: CRPS +0.117, MAE +0.120 P2: the gain is at least as large in the fade months (2026-03 to 2026-06) as in the engine months (2025-11 to 2026-02) Fails: neither is a gain; C2 is +0.164 and C3 is +0.069 P3: AH (cleaning with hindsight) beats A1 by under 0.2 points Fails by 0.003: AH minus A1 is -0.203 (interval -0.363 to -0.050), a bound P4: at the host, WT beats W0, and W1 recovers at least half of that gain Holds in the estimates (WT minus W0 -0.100, W1 minus W0 -0.093, so W1 recovers 93%), but both intervals cross zero, so the ratio of the two estimates is not resolved P5: the state at the valid time lowers CRPS by 2 points or more Holds for AH+state (AH+state minus A0 -2.354), fails for A1+state (A1+state minus A0 -1.413); both are bounds P6: no other Primary moves Holds: all 15 intervals include zero

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Terms used in the tables below.

  • Row: one half-hour of valid time in one forecast. All counts of rows are per seed.
  • Bound: a system that reads the scored reading, a hindsight fit, or the true injected output, so that no forecast can match it.
  • AH: arm A1 with the tracker fitted and smoothed with hindsight, to 2026-06-30. The two eras of the tracker are D8's reading before 2025-03-24 and from then on.
  • A1n: arm A1 with the no-fold cleaning (the engine's output is added to the reading without allowing for the reading's fold, because apparent power is never negative) and a signed add-back clamped at zero. The export branch is the part of the fold where the demand level is below the engine's output, so the engine exports power.
  • Host D4 and injected: D4 is a Primary into which we added (injected) a real engine's recorded output. W0 is the neural network trained on D4's raw injected reading, W1 is the A1 method on it, and WT is the W0 network plus the add-back of the true injected engine's calendar average.
  • +state arms: A1 or AH with the tracked engine state at the valid time added back, and WT+truth adds the true injected output at the valid time.
  • Origins: the contract origin is 12:00 UTC on the forecast day, and the native origin of the neural network is 09:00 UTC, three hours earlier.
  • Engine months and fade months: 2025-11 to 2026-02 and 2026-03 to 2026-06, when the engine's effect on D8's reading fades. Contrasts C2 and C3 split by the month of the forecast origin, and the slices in the text split by the month of the valid time.
  • Step 9a: experiment 677's raw-reading neural network at monthly refits.

The cleaned arms do not beat the raw arm, and only the bounds score much lower. Every row is scored against the metered apparent power at D8, or the injected reading at the host, for leads of 24 to 240 hours from the 12:00 UTC forecast origin, origins 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-30, mean of 3 seeds. "MAE" is the normalised mean absolute error of the median forecast. The reference rows come from experiment 677 on its 80,688 shared rows at D8, a different row set from the 102,310 rows scored here.

System What it is CRPS MAE A0 Raw reading, the control 7.232 13.252 A1 Causal cleaning plus the calendar add-back 7.349 13.372 A1n A1 with the no-fold cleaning and a signed add-back 7.683 13.891 AH (bound) Hindsight cleaning to 2026-06-30 7.146 12.942 A1+state (bound) A1 plus the tracked state at the valid time 5.819 10.386 AH+state (bound) AH plus the tracked state at the valid time 4.878 8.830 W0 Host, raw injected reading 4.489 7.447 W1 Host, causally cleaned plus add-back 4.396 7.390 WT Host, raw neural network plus the true engine's calendar add-back 4.389 7.401 WT+truth (bound) WT plus the true injected output at the valid time 2.232 3.953 Step 9a (reference) Stored control on experiment 677's rows 7.100 13.002 Manual heuristic (reference) Stored 7.934 14.135 Climatology on the raw reading (reference) Stored 8.581 16.189

No planned contrast shows a gain, and the host's gain of about 0.1 is within noise. C1, C4, and C5 are read at 98.3% (a Bonferroni split of 5% over three), and C2 and C3 are descriptive at 95%. Each row gives the estimate, the interval from resampling whole origin months with one seed per draw, and the t interval over the monthly differences. A negative value is a gain.

Contrast Estimate Bootstrap interval t interval Seeds C1: A1 minus A0, D8 +0.117 -0.070 to +0.412 -0.037 to +0.268 +0.182, +0.062, +0.108 C2: C1 in the engine months +0.164 -0.133 to +0.613 -0.146 to +0.472 +0.306, +0.115, +0.070 C3: C1 in the fade months +0.069 -0.071 to +0.184 +0.033 to +0.103 +0.055, +0.007, +0.146 C4: W1 minus W0, host -0.093 -0.203 to +0.021 -0.231 to +0.043 -0.087, -0.085, -0.108 C5: WT minus W0, host -0.100 -0.203 to +0.062 -0.224 to +0.027 -0.119, -0.064, -0.116 MAE of the median, A1 minus A0 (95%) +0.120 -0.487 to +0.788 -0.526 to +0.720 +0.287, -0.019, +0.094

The bounds, and every contrast that contains a bound, show where a forecast could gain, and none is a forecast. AH minus A1 is -0.203 (95% interval -0.363 to -0.050). A1+state minus A0 is -1.413 (-2.245 to -0.550), AH+state minus A0 is -2.354 (-3.488 to -1.344), and WT+truth minus W0 is -2.257 (-2.583 to -1.915). W1 minus WT is +0.007 (-0.052 to +0.069), so the causally cleaned host arm and the perfectly cleaned host arm are indistinguishable. A1n minus A1 is +0.334 (+0.197 to +0.457); A1n is a mis-specified variant, so its result says only that the fold is needed.

A1 is worse than A0 on rows where the engine is tracked as running, on cold winter nights, and over the valid times of 2026-03 to 2026-06 as a whole. On the 35,302 rows per seed that the hindsight tracker flags as running, CRPS is 8.453 for A0 and 9.002 for A1. On the 67,008 rows flagged as not running, it is 6.588 and 6.478. On cold winter nights it is 7.137 and 7.593, and for valid times in 2026-03 to 2026-06 6.439 and 6.492. The origin-month contrast C3, +0.069, splits by origin month and not by valid-time month, which explains the different size. A1 scores better on sunny middays of 2026-03 to 2026-06 (6.856 against 7.061). The median of A1 sits 12.9 points above the reading on running rows, against 10.0 for A0, and the 90% band of A1 is 62.4 points wide against 51.3 for A0, so A1 over-covers the low tail: the share of readings below the q05 forecast is 0.013 for A1 and 0.059 for A0.

A calendar average cannot say which days the engine runs, which is consistent with the add-back widening the forecast. No arm separates the add-back from the cleaning, so the cause is not isolated. In each engine month the add-back's running share was 0.37 to 0.38, against hindsight shares of 0.36 to 0.48, and it lagged the fade: in 2026-03 it was 0.386 against a hindsight share of 0.267 (printed/e00695_audit_out.txt). The add-back mixes two levels, with and without the engine, in every forecast. At the host, perfect cleaning with a perfect calendar average gained no more than the causal tracker did, so the host does not show the tracker as the limit. At D8, the hindsight tracker (AH) scores 0.203 points better than the causal one (A1), and AH scores 7.146 against A0's 7.232, so the tracker may be some of the limit at D8 as well.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Median minus mean forecast. The check looks for a spread that shifts the forecast: a positive gap means the quantiles' mean sits above the median. The neural networks output 11 quantiles and no mean, so the mean is the mean of the 11 quantile values. At D8 the mean of the quantiles minus the median is +1.627 points for A0, -2.774 for A1, and -1.766 for AH; across the other 15 Primaries on A0's output it is +0.155 to +0.996 except +2.648 at D12 and +8.562 at D15, which were not investigated. A1's gap is 4.4 points below A0's, the widening described above (printed/e00695_median_mean.txt).
  • Error of the median beside the CRPS contrasts. The MAE contrast is +0.120 (interval -0.487 to +0.788), the same sign as C1. The mean error of the median at D8 is +0.24 for A0, +2.00 for A1, and +1.15 for AH.
  • Gate G0 (reproduction). Refitted A0 scores 7.231588 at D8 against 7.231586 for the stored step 9a, on 102,310 shared rows (a gap of 1.6e-6 before rounding). The audit found a paired difference of 0.000 at every seed.
  • Gate G1 (tracker in the scored era). At the host, the causal tracker's F1 is 0.785, precision 0.998, and recall 0.647, and it flags 0.03% of un-injected half-hours. The pre-registered bars were F1 0.60, precision 0.50, and at most 3% false flags. G1 passed before any neural network was fitted.
  • Sign check. Of the half-hours with a unit running, 42.1% differ by more than 1 MVA between the folded and the no-fold cleaning (0.35 to 0.51 by fold), above the 10% trigger, so arm A1n ran (printed/sign_check.txt).
  • Identity control. Arm A1id sends D8's raw row through A1's cleaned-row route with cleaning disabled, for fold 2025-11 and seeds 0 to 2. Its quantiles match A0's to a maximum of 8.8e-5 of capacity (printed/e00695_identity_compare.txt).
  • Leakage and weather. Every leakage test gives a change of exactly 0. The scorer reads all 8 per-fold prediction logs of each of the 6 fitted arms (A0, A1, A1n, AH, W0, and W1; the other systems reuse these fits), and finds 242 origins (30, 31, 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, and 30), each asserted to use a weather run at or before the origin.
  • Audit triggers are the conditions under which the ml-experiment skill requires an independent audit: a failed control, a result that contradicts its prediction, a quantile contrast and an error contrast that disagree, a flip when one site is left out, a nested arm that beats its container, an interval much wider or narrower than a sister experiment's, and a later design that depends on the result.
    • Trigger 2 (the result contradicts the prediction) fired: A1 lost 0.117 points where the prediction was a gain of 0.3 to 1.0.
    • Trigger 6 (interval width) fired: the C1 interval is 0.48 wide, against 0.10 for experiment 677's two sister arms, which differ only in injected shifts and barely differ at D8. A contrast of one A0 seed against another is 0.36 to 0.61 wide, so seed noise explains the width.
    • Trigger 7 applies to part 3, if that is run, because its design would depend on the sign of C1.
    • Triggers 1, 3, 4, and 5 did not fire.
  • Audit findings (an Opus audit, printed/e00695_audit_out.txt; none rejected):
    • Every headline number reproduced, so branch 8 stands.
    • The post hoc seed-averaged interval suggests that A1 is a little worse; the page labels it post hoc.
    • The scorer's D8 row in the per-Primary table scored A1 without the add-back; the row is dropped.
    • The scorer read only the last fold's weather count; it now reads all 8 logs.
    • The bounds were unlabelled in the printed table; they are now labelled.
    • Weather alignment, the paired design, and the leakage tests were confirmed.
  • Not done. The sun check, the false-alarm check at the 7 other MVA-only Primaries, the correlation of engine state with forecast error, the climatology row on the cleaned series, and the per-fold count of dropped half-hours were not run; none can change the branch.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• The neural network is experiment 677's step-5 chain at monthly refits (step 9a of experiment 677), pooled over 16 Primaries, with a three-component Gaussian mixture output from which 11 quantiles (0.01 to 0.99) are read and sorted.
  • The inputs are weather, date-time, and two lagged-power encoders. The weather encoder reads 7 weather means, 7 spread columns, 2 lead columns, and 14 thermal-lag and solar-gain columns; the date-time encoder reads 21 columns; the lag encoder reads power at 24 hours and 1 week before the origin, with block dropout of lags. Every power input is at least 24 hours older than its origin.
  • The widths are an 8-wide Primary embedding, encoders from 64 to 32, a mixer of 64, and dropout 0.1. The encoders are trained on ERA5 and CAMS rows and then frozen, a fresh mixer is trained, and the whole is fine-tuned on ensemble weather with experiment 581's injected lag-only shifts.
  • Arm A1 replaces D8's row of the power stack with a series with the engine removed. Where the smoothed most probable unit count is 0, the cleaned value is the reading. Where it is 1 or more, the cleaned value is the posterior mean of the demand level under y = sqrt((L - k u)^2 + q^2), with L the demand level, k the units running, u the unit size, and q = 0.14 MVA the reactive floor. All three training stages read the replaced row, for training targets and lagged inputs alike.
  • The add-back mixes the forecast over the unit count. For each origin, the weights p_j (j = 0 to 3) are the weighted mean of the smoothed marginal P(k = j), by half-hour and weekend flag, over the 84 days of states at least 24 hours before the native origin, with weight 0.5 raised to the age in units of 28 days. The 11 quantiles are extrapolated linearly to 0.001 and 0.999, each level c maps to c for j = 0 and to sqrt((c - j u)^2 + q^2) for j of 1 or more, and the output quantiles are the weighted quantiles of that set. The mixture parameters are not exported, so this is an approximation.
  • The tracker is experiment 694's grid filter (experiment 694), fitted per fold on readings up to 3.5 hours before the refit. Era 1 (to 2025-03-23) is fitted once, and era 2 is refitted per fold and never split at the fade. A training state never reads a reading from 3.5 hours before the refit onward, and at inference the state at time t reads readings up to t + 20 hours.
  • The other arms differ as follows. AH uses one tracker fit and one smoothed series to 2026-06-30 for every fold. A1n uses the no-fold cleaning (y + k u) and a signed add-back clamped at zero. W0 trains on the host's reading with the injected engine, W1 cleans it as A1 does, and WT adds the true injected engine's calendar average to the neural network trained on the raw host reading, reusing W0's fits. The bounds add the tracked or true state at the valid time. Arm A1id is the identity control.

docs.title: Training regime
docs.text:
• Training data are ERA5 and CAMS (pre-training rows to 3.5 hours before the refit) and the ECMWF ensemble 00Z run of the origin day (fine-tuning and inference, treated as available at 09:00 UTC). Power comes from the cleaned power table with substation_zero half-hours dropped, and D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01.
  • The host is D4, chosen before any fit from the MVA-only Primaries D2, D3, and D4 because its median reading over 2025-03-24 to 2025-10-31 is closest to D8's tracked-off median. One real engine's 44-day record is resampled by whole days within weekday and weekend classes (seed 0) and injected by experiment 694's folded rule. The record is never shown with dates.
  • Refits are monthly for the test months 2025-11 to 2026-06, with seeds 0, 1, and 2. The fold equals the origin month. Each fold pre-trains (60 epochs in the logs), fits a fresh mixer, and fine-tunes with a 7-day embargo. Every fitted state file is saved.
  • The run took about 1.5 GPU-hours of wall-clock time against a cap of 12. Arm A0 ran as 8 single-fold jobs started together (929 to 1,030 s each), and the other arms ran 10 jobs at a time for about 75 minutes (printed/e00695_gpu_time.txt).

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text:
• Rows: all 16 Primaries are fitted, and D8 is the decision series. Scored rows have leads of 24 to 240 hours from the 12:00 UTC contract origin, origins 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-30, valid times before 2026-07-01, and a finite metered reading (102,310 rows per seed at D8, 102,391 at the host). The row set is backtest_year_2025_11_to_2026_06_daily_12utc.
  • Metrics: CRPS (twice the mean pinball loss over 11 quantiles) and the normalised MAE of the median, in points of effective capacity, with D8's capacity fixed at 10.379 MVA for every arm. Truth is the metered apparent power, and at the host the injected reading.
  • Intervals: each planned contrast is read through studies.bootstrap.bootstrap_difference_at_level from 20,000 resamples of whole origin months with one seed per draw (167 draws per tail at 98.3%), with a paired t interval on the 8 monthly differences. C2, C3, and the MAE contrast are read at 95% with 2,000 resamples. A Primary "moves" when its 95% interval excludes zero and the estimate exceeds the stored sister-arm difference, the CRPS gap between experiment 677's two arms that differ only in injected shifts.
  • Decision rule: the smallest gain worth porting is 5.5% of A0's CRPS at D8 (0.398 points). The verdict is the first branch of the pre-registered table that applies.

docs.title: Does giving the pre-training mixer of the demand neural network the inferred state of D8's gas engine, and then fine-tuning with a fresh mixer that has no engine input, lower the error of the forecast of D8's metered apparent power?
docs.text: Letting the neural network see the gas engine's state while it learns from weather and the calendar, and then dropping that knowledge before the forecast, did not improve the forecast of D8. The change in error is +0.009 points of capacity, which we cannot distinguish from zero, and the lower ends of the intervals rule out a net gain above about 0.07 points. At a second substation, where we added a recorded engine's output and so know the true state, a post hoc split shows a gain of 0.059 points on half-hours when the engine is off and a loss of 0.225 on half-hours when it runs. Weighted by the 19% of half-hours when it runs, the two cancel. The verdict is not supported.

docs.title: The question and how we tested it
docs.text:
The experiment asks whether a neural network learns better weather and calendar patterns if it is told, in its first training stage only, whether a gas engine is running. D8 is a Primary substation (a substation that supplies the local distribution network), one of the 16 that this research forecasts. A gas engine, a set of generating units that switch on and off, sits behind D8's meter, so D8's recorded power includes the engine's output. The forecast is the 11 quantiles of the power for each half-hour 24 to 240 hours ahead. A "point of capacity" is one percentage point of D8's effective capacity of 10.379 MVA (megavolt-amperes). CRPS (the continuous ranked probability score) is twice the mean pinball loss over the 11 quantiles. For every change in CRPS on this page, a positive value means the forecast got worse. Every contrast, interval, and verdict rule below was written down before any fit (pre-registered), except where a paragraph says post hoc.

The neural network trains in three stages, and the engine state enters only the first. In stage 1, the pre-training stage, a weather encoder and a date-time encoder (the parts that turn weather and the calendar into numbers) learn together with the pre-training mixer, which combines their outputs. In stages 2 and 3 the encoders are frozen, and a fresh fine-tune mixer with no engine input learns from ensemble weather forecasts. The method is learning with privileged information (Vapnik and Vashist (2009); Lopez-Paz et al. (2016)): the state helps training and is never available at forecast time. The state is three columns from the tracker of experiment 694, as stored by experiment 695: the expected engine output as a share of capacity, the probability that one or more units run, and a flag for hidden rows. The tracker infers this "tracked state" from the reading alone. An earlier test of the same kind, experiment 570, used electricity price in place of the engine state and made the forecast worse.

The arms differ only in the state that the pre-training mixer reads. The "host" is D4, another Primary, to whose reading we added the recorded output of a real engine ("injection", from experiment 695), so its "true state" is known. Each arm is refitted at the start of each of 8 months (2025-11 to 2026-06, the refit months) with 10 seeds (starting points for the training's random numbers).

Arm Series What the pre-training mixer reads A0 D8 No state (the control, from experiment 695) S1 D8 The tracked state SP D8 The tracked state with whole days shuffled within the tracker's era, calendar month, and weekday class (placebo) S1d D8 The tracked state, hidden on half of the origin days (3 seeds, descriptive) W0 Host No state (the control, from experiment 695) WST Host The true injected state WS1 Host The tracked state of the injected reading

Four contrasts were planned, each read at 98.75% (a Bonferroni split of 5% over four), and a nine-branch table fixed the verdict. C1 is S1 minus A0 at D8, C2 is S1 minus SP at D8, C3 is WST minus W0 at the host, and C4 is WS1 minus W0 at the host. A contrast passes when all three of its decision intervals lie below zero: a t interval over the 8 monthly differences of the seed means, a bootstrap over whole origin months of the seed-averaged losses, and a t interval over the 10 per-seed means. The branches are applied in order: (1) invalid if a leakage test fails; (2) failed if a reproduction or identity gate fails; (3) not supported, with an audit trigger, if C1 passes and C2 does not; (4) inconclusive if C1 and C2 pass and the encoder probe M1 fails; (5) supported if C1 passes with a gain of at least 0.16 points, C2 and M1 pass, and no veto applies; (6) partly supported if C1 passes at 0.16 or more, C2 and M1 pass, and a veto applies; (7) small gain if C1 passes below 0.16 and C2 and M1 pass; (8) refuted if all three C1 intervals lie above zero; (9) not supported otherwise. The vetoes are a host contrast whose intervals all lie above zero, a rise in the mean absolute error of the median (MAE), and another Primary that moves for the worse. The threshold of 0.16 points is 8 times the project's minimum of 0.02 for a change aimed at one Primary.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The verdict is not supported, branch 9, because C1 does not pass. No leakage test failed, the reproduction and identity gates passed, and all three C1 intervals contain zero. No other planned contrast passes. The estimate is the change in CRPS in points of capacity.

Contrast Estimate t over months Month bootstrap t over seeds C1: S1 minus A0, D8 +0.009 -0.074 to +0.091 -0.055 to +0.064 -0.074 to +0.092 C2: S1 minus SP, D8 -0.002 -0.092 to +0.086 -0.062 to +0.064 -0.059 to +0.055 C3: WST minus W0, host -0.004 -0.047 to +0.038 -0.032 to +0.029 -0.023 to +0.015 C4: WS1 minus W0, host +0.004 -0.021 to +0.029 -0.012 to +0.022 -0.030 to +0.038

The intervals rule out a net gain above about 0.07 points at D8 and about 0.05 at the host, so the 0.16 points needed to justify porting is out of reach. The lower ends of the three C1 intervals are -0.055 to -0.074, and of the three C3 intervals -0.023 to -0.047. The standard deviation of one seed's monthly difference at D8 is 0.233 points, and the smallest effect that 10 seeds could resolve is about 0.10 points at D8 and 0.05 at the host. Mean CRPS is 7.290 for A0, 7.299 for S1, and 7.301 for SP at D8, and 4.487 for W0, 4.483 for WST, and 4.492 for WS1 at the host.

Post hoc, the host's change splits by whether the engine runs, and the two parts cancel. The split was not planned, so its intervals are 95% over the 10 seeds and are not Bonferroni-adjusted. WST minus W0 is -0.059 (-0.079 to -0.039) on the 81% of half-hours when the injected engine is off, and +0.225 (+0.095 to +0.356) on the 19% when it runs. The MAE of the median splits the same way, -0.119 and +0.312. WS1 shows the same pattern at about half the size. Weighting the two parts by their shares gives -0.004, which is C3.

One explanation that fits, not measured directly, is that the weather and calendar parts of the neural network lose the engine's daily pattern, and the fresh fine-tune mixer cannot recover it. The frozen date-time encoder no longer needs to carry when the engine tends to run, yet the forecast target still contains the engine. The encoder probe M1 points the same way but missed its pre-registered gate. M1 freezes each arm's pre-trained encoders and fits a fresh mixer with no state to the host's reading without the engine. Its held-out error is 6.456 points for WST against 6.504 for W0, a change of -0.049 (95% t interval over the 8 folds, -0.099 to +0.002). A t interval over the 10 seed means, -0.090 to -0.007, would pass, but that reading is post hoc.

Next steps are options, and none is committed. The pre-training state could be tried together with a way of putting the engine back after pre-training, either experiment 695's calendar add-back or an origin-time engine state in the fine-tune mixer, and tested first at the host, where the true state is known.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The six pre-registered predictions hold, and M1's estimate is in its range but missed its gate.

    • P1: C1 between -0.08 and +0.05; observed +0.009.
    • P2: S1 better by 0 to 0.10 when the engine is tracked off, and worse by 0 to 0.15 when it runs; observed -0.016 and +0.058.
    • P3: SP within 0.05 of A0; observed +0.011.
    • P4: WST minus W0 between -0.10 and +0.03, and WS1 within 0.05 of WST; observed -0.004 and +0.008.
    • P5: M1 lower by 0.02 to 0.3; observed -0.049, but the 95% interval missed the gate.
    • P6: no other Primary moves; none moves by the rule below.

  • The state does reach pre-training, so the null result is not a failed patch. After pre-training, the pre-training mixer's weights on the two state columns average 1.10 and 0.71 in size for S1, against 0.10 on its original inputs, and 0.44 for SP. In one fold and seed, S1's weather and date-time encoders differ from A0's by 40% to 48% in relative norm, but a different seed of A0 differs from A0 by 140% and SP differs by 22% to 28%, so the size does not show that the state changes what the encoders learn. The stored final networks have encoders identical to the pre-trained file, and the fine-tune mixer has the same shape in S1 as in A0, so no state reaches a forecast.

  • Pre-training loss and length. On seeds 3 to 9 of the controls and all 10 seeds of the state arms, the pre-training validation loss is 0.193 for S1 against 0.207 for A0, and 0.188 for WST against 0.203 for W0 (experiment 695's seeds 0 to 2 gave 0.212 and 0.206). The mean number of pre-training epochs is 56.8 for both A0 and S1, so an earlier stop does not explain a difference.
  • Post hoc, the control's first three seeds score better than its other seven. A0 seeds 0 to 2, fitted in experiment 695, average 7.232 points, and A0 seeds 3 to 9, fitted here, average 7.315. Between the same seed groups S1 moves by -0.001, SP by -0.001, and the host's W0 by +0.002. On seeds 3 to 9 only, C1 is -0.016 (95% t interval over months, -0.092 to +0.065), against +0.067 on seeds 0 to 2. The gap is probably chance among three seeds. Arms G0 and SZ reproduce experiment 695's A0 to 2e-5, the pre-training rows and epochs match, and at the other 15 Primaries the A0 gap between seed groups averages -0.023 against -0.042 for S1. The decision interval stays the pre-registered 10-seed interval.

  • S1d reads better against S1 and SP than against A0. On seeds 0 to 2, S1d scores 7.318 against 7.298 for S1 and 7.300 for SP, so S1d minus S1 is +0.020 (95% t over seeds, -0.173 to +0.214) and S1d minus SP is +0.018 (-0.016 to +0.051), against +0.087 for S1d minus A0. The state is hidden by origin day but indexed by valid time, so one target half-hour is shown with the state on some rows and without it on others.
  • No other Primary moves by the pre-registered rule, which uses the library interval (95%, one seed per resample). The rule needs the interval of the paired difference to exclude zero and the estimate to exceed its sister-arm difference from experiment 677. With a seed-averaged month bootstrap at 95%, two of 15 Primaries exclude zero: D10 at +0.053 (+0.007 to +0.109), which would count as worse, and D11 at -0.031 (-0.068 to -0.001). About one would be expected by chance and two were seen, so the page reports both and does not use either against the verdict.
  • Mean of the 11 quantiles minus the median, per series. At D8 it is +1.716 for A0, +1.629 for S1, +1.744 for SP, and +1.435 for S1d. At the host it is -4.727 for W0, -5.009 for WST, and -4.952 for WS1 (printed/score_report.txt). The check was not run at the other 15 Primaries.
  • Error of the median beside each CRPS contrast. C1's MAE contrast is +0.019 (95%, t over months -0.165 to +0.197), the sign of C1. At the host the MAE contrast of WST minus W0 is -0.036 (95%: t over months -0.080 to +0.009, month bootstrap -0.071 to -0.001, t over seeds -0.061 to -0.011), the sign of C3 (printed/audit_analyse.txt).
  • Gates. The identity control SZ (a state of all zeros, which must reproduce A0), the reproduction gate G0 (a refit of A0), and G0W (a refit of W0) match experiment 695's fits to 1.4e-5 to 1.9e-5, 1.9e-5, and 5.6e-6 of capacity (tolerance 1e-4). Liveness holds for every arm (the state weights are non-zero, and exactly 0 for SZ), and the alignment gaps are 0.0 in all 8 folds. Every real-series leakage test gives a change of exactly 0, and every arm has 242 origins with origin-time weather (printed/checks_fits.txt, printed/checks_real_all.txt, printed/score_report.txt).
  • Audit triggers. The ml-experiment skill requires an independent audit when a trigger fires; an Opus audit ran, and printed/audit_*.txt holds the numbers it reproduced.
    • Trigger 1, a failed control, fired: M1 missed its gate and C3 shows no net gain, which the host split explains.
    • Trigger 2, a result that contradicts its prediction, did not fire: all six predictions hold.
    • Trigger 3, a CRPS contrast and an error contrast that disagree in sign, did not fire: the MAE contrasts above match the signs of C1 and C3.
    • Trigger 4, a flip when one site is left out, was not run, because each contrast sits at one series.
    • Trigger 5, a nested arm that beats its container, did not fire: SP minus A0 is +0.011, inside its 95% half-width of about 0.03.
    • Trigger 6, an interval more than twice as wide or half as wide as a sister experiment's, fired in the letter only: the C1 month-bootstrap and t intervals are 0.12 to 0.17 wide, against 0.48 for experiment 695's C1, which compared different arms with 3 seeds.
    • Trigger 7, a later design that depends on this headline, applies only to a design that reuses the host split.
  • Audit findings (an Opus audit; none rejected). Every headline number reproduced, so branch 9 stands. The seed-group, S1d, host-split, and other-Primaries readings are on this page and labelled post hoc. The patch, the frozen encoders, and the absence of leakage were confirmed.
  • Not done. The climatology row, the example-forecast plots, the load-shift scenarios, the count of dropped half-hours per fold, and the check of the median minus the mean at the other Primaries.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• The neural network is experiment 677's step-5 chain at monthly refits (step 9a of experiment 677, class AuxLagMdn of experiment 591), pooled over 16 Primaries, with a three-component Gaussian mixture output from which 11 quantiles are read and sorted.
  • The inputs are weather, date-time, and lagged power. The weather encoder reads 7 weather means, 7 spread columns, 2 lead columns, and 14 thermal-lag and solar-gain columns; the date-time encoder reads 21 columns; the lag encoder reads power at 24 hours and 1 week before the origin; every power input is at least 24 hours older than its origin.
  • The widths are an 8-wide Primary embedding, encoders from 64 to 32, a mixer of 64, and dropout 0.1. Stage 2 and stage 3 freeze the weather and date-time encoders and train a fresh fine-tune mixer, as in experiment 574.
  • The state arms widen the first layer of the pre-training mixer by 3 inputs. The layer is built at the original width under the original random-number stream and then padded with 3 zero columns, so a zero state reproduces A0. The state columns come from the stored per-fold tracker states of experiment 695 at the valid time of each pre-training row, and other Primaries read zeros. The widened layer is loaded at all three stages and is never called after pre-training.
  • The placebo SP shuffles whole days of S1's columns within the tracker's era (the tracker fits the engine's unit size separately for two stretches of D8's history), calendar month, and weekday class (Monday to Friday, or Saturday and Sunday). It uses only days at or before the fold's cut, with seed 0.
  • S1d hides the state on a random half of origin days, with the hidden flag set. WST reads the true injected output as a share of capacity and whether any unit runs, and WS1 reads the tracked state of the injected reading. The injected engine is experiment 695's resampled 44-day record.

docs.title: Training regime
docs.text:
• Training data are ERA5 and CAMS rows (two sets of weather reanalyses) to 3.5 hours before the refit in stage 1, and the ECMWF ensemble 00Z run of the origin day in stages 2 and 3 and at inference. Power comes from the cleaned table with substation_zero half-hours dropped, and D15 and D18 are cut before 2025-03-01.
  • Everything outside the pre-training mixer's input is step 9a unchanged: the loss, the optimiser, early stopping on held-out weeks, the 7-day embargo, the injected lag-only shifts, and monthly refits for 2025-11 to 2026-06.
  • There are 10 seeds per arm and fold, with seeds 0 to 2 of A0 and W0 reused from experiment 695's stored fits and seeds 3 to 9 fitted here by the same chain. The fits used about 28 job-hours, and the resource log spans 4.5 hours of wall-clock time with 6 to 7 jobs at once and a peak of 33 GB of GPU memory (printed/job_times.txt).
  • The state never reaches a forecast. The state at a pre-training row reads readings only before the refit minus 3.5 hours, and a perturbation of every later reading changes no state value.

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text:
• The metric of record is CRPS at D8 in points of effective capacity (fixed at 10.379 MVA), with leads 24 to 240 hours from the 12:00 UTC contract origin, origins 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-30, valid times before 2026-07-01, and all 16 Primaries scored. The normalised mean absolute error of the median, pinball loss, and coverage at q01, q05, q95, and q99 are printed beside it.
  • The host's truth is the injected reading. The 102,310 D8 rows per seed and the host's rows come from the scorer of experiment 695, and the audit re-derives each number from the raw fits.
  • Intervals are the three decision intervals above, a library interval for the other-Primaries rule, and 40,000 resamples (250 draws per tail at 98.75%). The threshold of 0.16 points follows the project's demand evaluation protocol, demand-v2, which sets a minimum of 0.02 points for a change aimed at one Primary.
  • The verdict follows the pre-registered table of nine branches, evaluated in order.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00696-*/e00696_common.py, e00696_state.py, e00696_model.py, e00696_probe.py, e00696_hooks.py, and e00696_k1.py: the arm table, the state builders, the widened network, the encoder probe, the hooks that attach the state to the pre-training rows, and the wrapper that runs experiment 677's step-5 chain.
  • e00696_chain.sh, e00696_gpu.sh, e00696_queue.sh, and e00696_wait.sh: one fold of one arm, one process under a memory cap, the job queue, and the wait loop.
  • e00696_checks.py: the synthetic and real-series checks and the identity and reproduction gates.
  • e00696_score.py and e00696_verdict.py: the scorer (contrasts, the probe, slices, the weather assertion) and the verdict function, with e00696_selftest_*.py covering every branch.
  • e00696_audit_*.py: the audit's loss, contrast, slice, weight, epoch, and host code. e00696_figures.py draws the three figures from the audit's losses, so its bootstrap bounds differ from the scorer's by up to 0.001. e00696_job_times.py prints the job-hours.
  • printed/: the printed reports of the checks, the scorer, the audit, the job times, and the job lists.
  • Data under data/ml-experiments/00696-*/ (read and written): runs/<arm>/ (fits, models, logs), states/<arm>/<month>.npz (the state columns), checks.json, and audit/ (per-row losses). Experiment 695's states/, stacks/, and the stored fits of A0 and W0 seeds 0 to 2 are read.

docs.title: Experiment 697: exploratory figures
docs.text:
These figures are exploratory, and none of them changes the verdict of experiment 697. Each shows the running share of D8's gas engine as the tracker labels it, in the net era (2023-09-01 to 2025-02-28) and the solar era (2025-03-24 to 2026-02-28), and the null control where a caption names one. The terms (tracker, running share, null control, cell, spell) are defined on the result page. The figures were drawn after the tables were seen, so any reading of them is post hoc. The night share by month (G7), which is the share of half-hours from 00:00 to 05:00 that the tracker flags, and D8's dated rasters stay in the private data folder. Bins that hold fewer than 20 days are not drawn as shares, and G6 shows their counts.

G1: in the net era D8's labels show 4 or more running half-hours on almost every weekday, and on fewer weekend days. The left panel is the share of days with 4 or more running half-hours (a running day), by weekday. The right panel is the share of running days after a running day and after an idle day, for Tuesday to Friday. The null control's truth has no day-to-day link, so its flat line is what a patternless engine gives. The null control is the one built on D8's reading before its engine.

G2: starts cluster around 06:00 to 08:00 and 15:00 to 17:00 local time, and stops around 19:00 to 22:00. Each point is the number of on-spells that start, or end, at one local half-hour, for the summer half and the winter half of each era.

G3: the running share rises with the half-hour's price rank within its day, and is highest in the red band. The left panel ranks the half-hours of each local day by system price. The right panel compares the red band (Monday to Friday, 16:00 to 19:00 local) with the 6 dearest half-hours of the day that fall outside the band, and with other weekday half-hours. Bank-holiday evenings are not drawn, because they hold fewer than 20 days.

G4: the running share rises with the spark spread and not with the gas price. The spark spread is the system price minus the gas price divided by an assumed efficiency of 0.40, in pounds per MWh. The left panel uses the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) held N2EX hourly day-ahead price, which starts in 2025-09, so it holds only the part of the solar era from 2025-09. The Elexon APX within-day price index, which starts in 2023-06, is in G9.

G5: D8's share minus the null control's share falls as the wind speed and the temperature rise. The bars are thirds of each driver within a cell, for the net era only, and the control is the null control on the host series. D8's heating load changes its reading, so D8's raw weather link is not read.

G6: bank-holiday weekdays, Christmas week, and clock-change days each hold fewer than 20 days, so no running share is drawn for them. The bars are the numbers of weekday evenings in each group and era, and the dashed line is the floor of 20 days. This departs from the earlier version of the figure, which drew shares from groups of 2 to 18 days.

G8: the running share and the tracker's fitted block size by month and local half-hour. Left panels: the running share on weekdays. Right panels: the mean fitted block size in MW when flagged, where a block is the tracker's fitted size of one unit of output. White cells hold fewer than 15 days.

G9: the running share is higher in the top third of the within-day price and of national demand, and lower in the top third of embedded wind and of the forecast imbalance. Each row is the running share in the top third of a signal minus the bottom third, within a cell, with a 95% interval, for D8's net and solar eras and for the null control on the host series. The Elexon within-day price index is not the day-ahead auction.

G10: the running share inside and outside a Short Term Operating Reserve (STOR) window. The share is on weekday evenings. Whether the engine holds a reserve agreement is unknown, so we read a match with a window as a coincidence of timing and not as a cause. System warning days (5 in the net era and 0 in the solar era) and gov.uk bank holidays (11 and 8) each hold fewer than 20 days and are not drawn.

docs.title: Does D8's gas engine run to a schedule that follows the working week, and what else regular can be read from the tracker's labels?
docs.text:
This experiment asks whether the gas engine behind D8, one of the 16 Primary substations that this research forecasts, runs to a schedule that follows the working week. The engine is a gas engine with a long-term capacity contract. We read the engine from D8's half-hourly reading with the tracker of experiment 694, a filter that infers from the reading alone how many of the engine's units are running in each half-hour. A unit is one block of output, of about 2 MW, that the engine adds or drops as a whole. The running share is the share of half-hours in a group that the tracker flags as running. No meter on the engine behind D8 is used.

The question is measured as Q1, the weekday-minus-weekend running share from 16:00 to 19:00 local time. That window is the red band: the hours in which NGED's Distribution Use of System charges for half-hourly metered customers in the East Midlands, where D8 sits, are highest on Monday to Friday. All shares in this page come from the tracker's smoothed labels, which use the whole record to place each flag, and not from its filtered labels, which use only readings up to the half-hour.

The tracker could produce a weekday pattern by itself, so we measured the pattern against controls. A host reading is a real reading that an engine is injected into. A null control is a host reading with the one metered engine record that we hold (called Gas A here, 44 days long) injected by experiment 694's method of adding a recorded engine to a reading. The injected days are drawn at random with no regard to the weekday, so any weekday pattern in the tracker's labels of a null control is tracker error. There are six null controls. One uses D8's reading before its engine. Two use that reading with a constant subtracted so that its weekday daytime level matches D8's level in the net era and in the solar era (the level-matched controls, one constant for each era). Three use the readings of three other Primaries (D2, D3, and D4) over the same two periods. Each control ran with 2 or 3 random seeds for the drawn days.

D8's reading changes between the net era and the solar era, so each era is tested alone. The net era is 2023-09-01 to 2025-02-28, and the solar era is 2025-03-24 to 2026-02-28, after 11 kV solar generation began. The fade era is 2026-03-01 to 2026-06-30, when the engine's effect on D8's reading fades while the tracker's flags persist. The fade era carries no part of the verdict.

The verdict is supported. D8's Q1 is +0.392 (95% interval +0.323 to +0.464) in the net era and +0.256 (+0.156 to +0.365) in the solar era. D is D8's Q1 minus a null control's Q1, with independent resampling of whole calendar weeks for the two terms. Against all six null controls in both eras the interval of D lies above zero, and every point estimate is 0.10 or more, which is the condition for supported in the decision rule. In both eras the smallest D is against the level-matched control that uses the solar-era constant: +0.337 (+0.260 to +0.416) in the net era and +0.202 (+0.097 to +0.311) in the solar era.

P1b, a check named in the prediction and not in the decision rule, also passes and does not change the verdict word. P1b requires that, on D8's readings from before the engine with a patternless engine injected, the labels show a weekday-minus-weekend difference below 0.10. The three controls built on D8's history show +0.015, +0.017, and +0.054. The largest, +0.054, is the level-matched control with the solar-era constant, and its interval (+0.023 to +0.084) excludes zero, so the tracker shows a small weekday excess on a patternless engine in that control.

Two limits keep the finding from being a result about the engine itself. First, the shares come from the tracker. D8's own demand is highest on weekday evenings, and the null controls cannot show that the tracker never reads part of that demand as the engine. The labels also understate a weekday pattern: in controls whose injected days do follow the weekday, the ratio of the labels' Q1 to the truth's Q1 is 0.745 at D8's history before the engine. The +0.392 measures the labels and not the size of the engine's pattern. Second, the one metered engine record (Gas A) agrees in direction only. At 2 or more units its weekday-minus-weekend share is +0.233 (+0.057 to +0.442), but the record spans 7 calendar weeks with 12 weekend days, 3 of them with the engine running, so its interval is rough.

docs.title: Questions beyond the verdict
docs.text:
The verdict rests on Q1 alone. Every other question was listed in the experiment's plan before the run and does not change the verdict word. Q4 was dropped in the plan. About 30 intervals were computed, at 95% and without a correction for multiple comparisons, and the table shows the net-era and solar-era estimates of the others. A cell is one local half-hour in one weekday class in one calendar month. A spell is a run of consecutive half-hours with the same flag, an on-spell if the engine is flagged as running and an off-spell if not. The hazard at length n is the share of spells that last n or more half-hours and end at n. A reading of 1 means that D8's interval excludes zero with the same sign in both eras and excludes zero against every null control, a reading of 2 means that a null control reproduces the pattern, and a reading of 3 means that D8's interval includes zero.

Question D8, net era D8, solar era Reading Q1: weekday minus weekend, 16:00 to 19:00 +0.392 (+0.323 to +0.464) +0.256 (+0.156 to +0.365) Supported (the verdict) Q2: dearest system-price third minus cheapest third, within cell +0.284 (+0.251 to +0.316) +0.237 (+0.190 to +0.285) 1, not explained by the controls Q2q: the same with calendar quarters in place of months +0.303 (+0.273 to +0.334) +0.250 (+0.190 to +0.302) 1, not explained by the controls Q3: hazard at 1 to 2 half-hours minus at 3 to 8 +0.007 (-0.014 to +0.027) +0.006 (-0.016 to +0.028) 3, no pattern found Q3a: hazard at 1 half-hour +0.125 (+0.098 to +0.151) +0.095 (+0.072 to +0.120) 2, tracker error not excluded: the null controls show a higher value Q6: winter-half minus summer-half weekday evening +0.011 (-0.064 to +0.083) not asked 3, no pattern found Q7: running day after a running day minus after an idle day +0.133 (-0.032 to +0.294) not estimable 3 in the net era (the interval includes zero and is wide); the solar era has too few days Q8: most common start half-hour, winter half and summer half 32 and 32 (16:00), the same 14 and 13 (07:00 and 06:30), different Not an interval; not read

Q3a is the one question where the tracker's labels at D8 show less than the null controls do. The difference D (D8 minus the null control) is negative in all 12 comparisons, from -0.008 to -0.101, so the null controls' labels show a higher hazard at 1 half-hour than D8's. A patternless injected engine therefore gives at least as many one-half-hour spells in its labels as D8 does.

The running share rises with the half-hourly system price within a cell, and the controls do not explain it. Gas A shows the same direction at 1 or more units (+0.123, +0.038 to +0.256) and at 2 or more units (+0.094, +0.019 to +0.212). Q2 and Q2q are compared with the host controls only, because D8's history before the engine overlaps the half-hourly system price by about 12 days, so the controls built on it have a price for 4% of their half-hours. The price peak, the red band, and D8's own demand peak all fall on weekday evenings, and this experiment cannot separate them.

Q5 is +0.074 (+0.031 to +0.123) and is descriptive. Q5 is the share of half-hours between 00:00 and 05:00 that the tracker flags, in the 6 months after 2025-03-24 minus the same months a year earlier. The host controls show -0.006 to -0.003 for the same contrast, so the rise is not a property of the tracker on other Primaries. D8's night readings changed when its solar generation began, and this experiment does not say whether the engine ran more at night.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows the weekday evening block in D8's labels and not in the null control's. Each D8 panel is a weekday by local half-hour heat map of the running share, for the summer half (the months of British Summer Time) and the winter half of each era. The null-control panels use the control built on D8's reading before its engine (C1), in which the injected engine has no weekday pattern. The bottom panel shows Gas A's running share by local half-hour at 1 or more units (blue) and 2 or more units (orange), for weekdays (solid) and weekends (dashed). A tracker artefact could produce the evening block if the tracker reads D8's weekday evening demand peak as the engine.

Figure 2 shows spell lengths that look alike in D8's labels, in Gas A, and in a control's labels, so they say little about the engine. The panels show the survival curve (the share of spells that last at least n half-hours) and the hazard of on-spells and off-spells of 1 to 48 half-hours. A tracker artefact could produce any shape, because the tracker's built-in assumption about how long the engine stays in one state sets the hazard.

Figure 3 shows the running share rising with the system price in D8's labels and in Gas A, and staying flat in the null control on the host series. The left panel uses system-price fifths over the whole period, and the right panel uses system-price thirds within a cell. A tracker artefact could produce an overall rise, because the price and D8's demand both peak on weekday evenings. The flatness of the control answers that only for the demand shapes that the control contains.

Figure 4 shows that Gas A runs at about 1, 2, or 3 times 1.97 MW and reaches its first full level within 2 half-hours in 94% of its 54 complete on-spells. Left: output in running half-hours, with rules at multiples of 1.97 MW. Right: output as a share of the level reached. Bottom: starts and stops by local clock time. No panel for D8 is drawn, because the tracker places its edges where D8's reading steps. At D8 the tracker fits the size of one block of output (1.75, 2.25, or 3.5 MW, by era), and D8's reading cannot show how many separate units the engine has.

Eight more exploratory figures (G1 to G6 and G8 to G10, less G7) are on the gallery page. G7, the night share by month, and the dated rasters stay in the private data folder.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The null controls on D2 and on the level-matched control with the solar-era constant recover the injected engine worst, and the verdict holds against them too. The attenuation (the ratio of the labels' Q1 to the truth's Q1, which is 1 if the tracker recovers an injected weekday pattern exactly) is 0.745 at D8's history before the engine, 0.687 to 0.821 at D3 and D4, and 0.149 (net era) and 0.221 (solar era) at D2. The F1 score of the tracker against the injected truth is 0.54 to 0.73 at D2 and 0.62 to 0.65 for the level-matched control with the solar-era constant, against 0.80 to 0.90 elsewhere. The six D values above include the one against D2's control, which is the weakest of the six.
  • The audit passed with 0 failed checks. It asserts the row counts, the era lengths, the shares of half-hours flagged in the net, solar, and fade eras (0.268, 0.384, and 0.262), the 1.75, 2.25, and 3.5 MW block sizes, and 0 flags among 253,440 half-hours in 44 segments (separate stretches of readings, at 8 Primaries) of experiment 694's stored false-alarm pass. The stored host reproduction (experiment 695, host D4) gives an F1 score of 0.785 and a precision of 0.998.
  • The smoothed labels match experiment 695's stored probabilities except in the fade era. They agree on 0.999 of half-hours in the net era, 0.989 in the solar era, and 0.867 in the fade era. The smoothed and filtered labels agree on 0.958 (net era), 0.825 (solar era), and 0.798 (fade era).
  • The fade era is never read as a pattern. The smoothed labels flag 0.262 of its half-hours and the filtered labels flag 0.150. Q1 is +0.383 on the smoothed labels and +0.030 (-0.051 to +0.105) on the filtered labels.
  • The timestamp shift is checked. A power stamp marks the end of a half-hour and a price stamp marks the start, so every power-derived stamp is moved 30 minutes earlier before any join. The audit reproduces the five system-price-fifth shares of experiment 194 at the end-stamp join (0.089 to 0.259) and gives the shares at the start-stamp join (0.057 to 0.281). Every hour-of-day axis sits 30 minutes earlier than in experiment 194.
  • Bank holidays are weekdays in Q1. The weekday class follows the local date. NGED's Statement of Use of System Charges for 2025-26 says that its red band includes bank holidays, and the statements for 2023-24 and 2024-25 do not mention them. D8's net era holds 5 bank-holiday weekday evenings (18 in Christmas week and 3 clock-change days), and the solar era holds 5 (9 and 2), all under the 20-day floor, so no share is read or printed for them.
  • No audit trigger from the experiment skill fired. No control failed, and no result contradicted its prediction.
  • A half-hour without a system price is dropped and the price series is never filled. The Elexon APX Market Index Data is the within-day half-hourly price, not the day-ahead auction. Its table has 20 half-hours with a missing price, set to missing where the price and the volume were both 0 (printed/signals_download.txt).
  • We looked for combined heat and power and found no sign of it. The sources were the public Capacity Market register entry for the engine, NESO's reserve results by technology, and public web searches for the operator and the site. None mentions a heat supply, and no permit or planning text was found. That is not evidence either way, and this experiment did not measure whether D8 has a heat load.

docs.title: What the options are for a next experiment
docs.text: A next experiment could build equations for a gas engine's running and test them on Gas A and on D8's labels. The equations could include a minimum on-time and a ramp time, and the experiment could test whether a simple rule reproduces the weekday-evening share and the rise with the system price. The experiment could also add a Primary in the East Midlands that has the same red band and no gas engine, to separate the band from the evening demand peak. No such experiment is agreed.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture and inputs:

  • The tracker is experiment 694's M2 grid filter (a filter over a grid of demand levels and numbers of units running) on D8's apparent-power reading. The eras fit different block sizes: 1.75 MW (net), 2.25 MW (solar), and 3.5 MW (fade).
  • The label sets are Ts (the smoothed flag, which carries the verdict), Tf (the filtered flag), Ta (experiment 695's stored probabilities, used as a mean probability), and Tc (experiment 695's fixed-lag states, in the table of labels only).
  • A half-hour start becomes Europe/London time, the weekday is that of the local date, and the six clock-change days are left out of hour-of-day plots.
  • The drivers are the half-hourly system price, the daily gas price, the spark spread (the system price minus the gas price divided by an assumed efficiency of 0.40, in pounds per MWh), the day-ahead price from 2025-09, national wind, and local temperature, wind speed at 100 m, and irradiance (carried by grid index and never re-joined by time). The price and gas loaders copy a private file, predictability_work/data.py, of the engine-state follow-on. The multi-day demand drops are those of experiment 159, and the spark spread follows experiment 186.

Controls and injected truth:

  • A control injects Gas A's recorded days by experiment 694's method, at a grid offset of 40,944 half-hours between the pipeline's grid and the panel's. Null truth draws days with no regard to the weekday, and weekday-class truth draws days within the weekday class. The engine draw is copied from experiment 695's drive_series, and the era recipe from experiment 694's run script. Neither is imported.
  • C1 is D8's reading before its engine (3 seeds, null and weekday-class truth, 6 runs). C1s, the level-matched control, is C1 with a constant of 0.093 MVA (net) or 3.019 MVA (solar) subtracted (3 seeds, null truth, 6 runs). C2 is the three other Primaries (2 seeds, null and weekday-class truth in the net and solar spans, 24 runs). A job is one series, one span, one kind of truth, and one seed, so the 36 jobs ran at 8 workers on CPU in 205 s of wall-clock time, 31 to 52 s each (printed/controls.txt, which also prints the constants).
  • C3 reads experiment 694's stored false-alarm pass, and C4 reads experiment 695's stored host states. Every control seed differs: the seed is the draw seed plus the job seed plus a per-series and a per-control offset.

Measurement:

  • Q1 is the weekday-minus-weekend running share from 16:00 to 19:00 local, read on Ts, with Tf and Ta shown beside it.
  • Every interval resamples whole ISO weeks of local dates within an era (2,000 draws, percentile method). D uses independent resamples for D8 and the control.
  • Bins with fewer than 20 distinct days are dropped from every plot and test, and the heat-map floor is 15. G6 and G10 show the groups that fall under the floor as counts or leave them out.
  • The verdict rule is the one in the front matter, written before the run, and inconclusive is the default. P1b is a check in the prediction. No gain threshold applies, because no forecast is scored and the experiment changes no production code.
  • Gas A is shown only as aggregates over the whole record: by local half-hour, weekday class, system price third or fifth, spell length, and output level. D8's dated rasters, example weeks, and the night share by month stay in the private data folder.

Signals added after the design (post hoc):

  • Ten open data tables from nine groups of signals were added after the design and show in G9 and G10: Elexon's within-day price index, the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) Short Term Operating Reserve (STOR) windows and auction results (without unit or company names), Elexon's system warnings, the indicated imbalance forecast, NESO's day-ahead demand forecast, NESO's historic demand, Elexon's transmission wind (2023-06 to 2024-06, filling the gap before the held wind table, which starts in 2024-07), the national Carbon Intensity API, and the gov.uk bank holidays. Whether the engine holds a STOR agreement is unknown. Their coverage is in printed/signals_download.txt.
  • Q3a and Q2q are variants that the plan names, split from Q3 and added as a sensitivity.
  • A lookup of NESO's Enduring Auction Capability results asks only for the technology "Gas Reciprocating Engines" and filters by distance on this machine. The lookup found one post code within 5 km of D8's supply area. That match does not confirm the engine's identity, and the match stays in the private data folder.

docs.text:
