  • e00697_selftest.py: 16 known-answer tests that read no stored data apart from one check of the level-matched constants.
  • e00697_audit.py: the data audit, which writes printed/audit.txt and a private file of two checks of the record.
  • e00697_engine.py, e00697_controls.py: the injected-day draw (copied from experiment 695's drive_series) and the 36 control runs, each written to its own file in the data folder, with the log in printed/controls.txt.
  • e00697_frame.py, e00697_drivers.py: build one half-hour table per label set, and load the drivers (copied in part from the private file named in the Method).
  • e00697_analysis.py, e00697_stats.py: Q1 to Q3a and Q5 to Q8, the differences D, the tables T1 to T6, and stats.json.
  • e00697_verdict.py: applies the decision rule and writes printed/verdict.txt, with the P1b values of each control.
  • e00697_figures.py, e00697_private_figures.py: the published figures and the private dated ones.
  • e00697_signals_download.py, e00697_signals.py, e00697_lookups.py: the extra signals (with printed/signals_download.txt and printed/signals_checks.txt), their panels, and the register lookup.
  • printed/: the audit, the tables, the verdict, the controls log, and the signal checks, as printed by the scripts.
  • data/ml-experiments/00697-gas-engine-state-tracker-part-4-running-patterns/: private. It holds the 36 control files (controls/), the half-hour frames (frames/), stats.json, the downloaded signals (signals/), the lookup rows (lookups/), and the private figures.
  • Read, from earlier work: experiment 694's tracker and stored false-alarm pass, and experiment 695's stored probabilities and host states.

docs.title: Does solar generation behind D8's meter make the tracker's labels of the gas engine worse, beyond the harm from the lower level of the reading?
docs.text: The test could not decide, and the numbers it produced point to harm. We asked whether solar panels behind the meter of the substation D8 (which also has a gas engine behind its meter) make a statistical tracker label the engine worse. The tracker is a filter that reads a substation's half-hourly power and estimates how many blocks of the engine are running. We injected the recorded output of a real solar farm, and a recorded gas-engine pattern, into real readings from two substations, D8 and D3, and compared the tracker's labels with the injected truth. Under the decision rule fixed before any score was seen, two audit clauses fired, so the verdict is inconclusive. The pooled numbers point to real solar-farm output lowering the tracker's F1 score (the balance of precision and recall) by 0.140 and raising its false-flag share (the share of half-hours with no injected engine output that the tracker flags as running) by 0.139, against a smooth solar curve of the same size, at D8 with 8.9 MW of solar between 10:00 and 15:00.

docs.title: Terms used on this page
docs.text:
• D8, D3, and host: D8 and D3 are substations. A host is a substation whose real reading carries the injected solar and engine output. The hosts are D8 and D3. Experiment 694's panel gives each host's reading and its CAMS shape (the stored panel of experiment 196, built by studies.dp_features).
  • D8 before the engine: the span of D8's history before its own gas engine was connected, so the reading holds no engine output. The span is experiment 697's control C1. It is earlier than the net era below.
  • Tracker: the grid filter of experiment 694 (its M2 filter). For each half-hour it estimates how many equal blocks of the engine run. A block is 1.75 MW in the fits of the host runs that carry an engine.
  • Flag and false-flag share: the tracker flags a half-hour when its smoothed probability (the probability after a backward pass that also uses later readings) that one or more blocks run exceeds 0.5. The false-flag share is the share of half-hours with zero injected engine output that the tracker flags. The filtered labels use earlier readings only, and the page quotes the smoothed labels unless it says otherwise.
  • PV and the solar term: PV is photovoltaic (solar panel) generation. The solar term is the contribution of solar generation to the reading.
  • CAMS: the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, whose satellite-derived irradiance (the sunlight reaching the ground, in W/m2) we turn into a solar-output shape per megawatt at each host.
  • Net era and solar era: experiment 697 divides D8's history into two periods. The net era is the period before solar generation began on the 11 kV distribution network around D8, and the solar era is the period after it (experiment 697 gives the dates).
  • Fold and reverse flow: the fold is the reflection of the reading at zero. The meter reports the size of the net power and not its sign, so once solar and engine output exceed the demand behind the meter, the reading rises again. Reverse flow is a real power behind the reading below zero. The experiment applies the fold once, to the sum of solar and engine output.
  • Smooth twin: a solar curve of the same capacity that carries the average daily and seasonal shape and no weather. The farm's smooth twin is the farm's own average output for each month and half-hour. The CAMS smooth twin is the average of the CAMS shape for each month and half-hour.
  • Level contrast and weather contrast: the level contrast is the CAMS smooth twin minus a run with no solar, so it holds the harm from the lower level of the reading and its fold. The weather contrast is a run with real weather minus its own smooth twin (the farm run minus the farm's smooth twin, or the CAMS run minus the CAMS smooth twin). Harm is positive when the labels get worse.
  • Bright-minus-dull: the flagged share in the brightest third of CAMS irradiance minus the flagged share in the dullest third, from 10:00 to 15:00. A tracker that reads cloud swings as engine steps shows a larger value.
  • Curve gate: a host and capacity run only if the median reading by fifth of solar output lies within 1 MVA (megavolt-ampere) of D8's solar-era curve in each of the first four fifths.
  • Null control: a series that carries an injected engine with no weekday, price, or schedule pattern, from experiment 697. The solar-free twin of D8 before the engine is that experiment's control C1.
  • Drops and off-spells: the drops are the multi-day periods in which D8's power falls by 3 to 5 MW for days at a time, listed in experiment 159. An off-spell is a run of 48 half-hours or more that the smoothed labels call off. Step 4 (see Method) uses the off-spells.
  • Scorable half-hour and seed: a scorable half-hour has a reading, is not on a clock-change day, and has a finite farm value. A seed fixes which days of Gas A the injected engine draws.
  • Gas A: the one metered gas-engine record we hold. The page shows it only inside scores pooled over a whole run.

docs.title: Verdict: inconclusive
docs.text:
By the rule fixed before any score was seen, the verdict is inconclusive, because the audit blocks the test. Two clauses of the first outcome of the decision rule fired:

  • The paired half-width of the F1 of the farm weather contrast at D8 before the engine is 0.051, above the limit of 0.05.
  • The farm series covers 0.859 of the daylight half-hours at both hosts, under the limit of 0.90. Daylight half-hours are those with a positive CAMS shape at the host.

The other clauses of the test held: the farm shape passes the curve gate at D8 with 8.9 MW, and the solar-free twin reproduces a midday F1 of 0.767.

The clause on coverage concerns half-hours outside the scored window. The farm series has a reading in 0.984 of the daylight half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 in May to September at D8 and 0.992 at D3, so the missing half-hours lie mostly outside the 10:00 to 15:00 window that the criteria read. The farm's gaps are filled with its own average and left out of every score.

A reading chosen after seeing the scores is post hoc and does not change the verdict. Without the two clauses, the rule would have returned supported for the farm contrast, because the farm weather contrast meets a criterion at D8 and at D3 at 8.9 MW, the one capacity that ran at both hosts. A further test on D8's own off-spells (step 4, defined under Method) can lower supported to partly supported only when its half-width is 0.10 or less, and its half-width is 0.69. We report this reading as post hoc only.

Two changes to the rule's clauses were made before any score was seen, and the page lists both. The planning commit (f74324de9) fixed the coverage clause at 95% of all half-hours of D8's span and the half-width clause over every contrast at D8. After the audit printed a coverage of 0.914, commit 4c6b78134 lowered the limit to 0.90 and applied it to each host's span. After a code review estimated that about a fifth of daylight half-hours had no farm value, commit 7665d4dbb counted the coverage over daylight half-hours and narrowed the half-width clause to the farm weather contrast. The first version of the rule, with its 95% limit, would also have returned inconclusive at 0.914. The scores, the jobs, and the contrasts did not exist at either change.

docs.title: What the contrasts show
docs.text:
The farm weather contrast shows harm at every host and capacity that ran, and the CAMS weather contrast is weak. Each cell holds the point estimate and the 95% interval from 2,000 resamples of whole ISO weeks, with 3 seeds pooled and the smoothed labels. D8 before the engine has 73 weeks and 4,911 scored midday half-hours, and D3 has 49 weeks and 3,376. A positive number is worse. The thresholds are 0.05 for F1 and for bright-minus-dull, and 0.02 for the false-flag share. The 7.0 MW run at D8 did not pass the curve gate, and the CAMS shape did not pass it at D3.

Host and capacity Contrast F1 falls False-flag share rises Bright-minus-dull rises D8, 8.9 MW level +0.358 (+0.298 to +0.415) +0.052 (+0.041 to +0.063) +0.005 (-0.016 to +0.028) D8, 8.9 MW weather, farm +0.140 (+0.089 to +0.192) +0.139 (+0.094 to +0.190) +0.183 (+0.100 to +0.268) D8, 8.9 MW weather, CAMS +0.043 (+0.002 to +0.082) +0.006 (-0.004 to +0.016) +0.034 (+0.015 to +0.054) D3, 7.0 MW level +0.297 (+0.224 to +0.377) +0.034 (+0.023 to +0.045) +0.013 (-0.012 to +0.038) D3, 7.0 MW weather, farm +0.189 (+0.132 to +0.250) +0.070 (+0.045 to +0.096) +0.148 (+0.094 to +0.206) D3, 8.9 MW level +0.377 (+0.295 to +0.463) +0.046 (+0.033 to +0.060) +0.023 (-0.004 to +0.049) D3, 8.9 MW weather, farm +0.138 (+0.087 to +0.195) +0.070 (+0.043 to +0.100) +0.103 (+0.033 to +0.183)

The level contrast holds most of the F1 harm, and the weather contrast holds most of the harm to the false-flag share and to bright-minus-dull. At D8 with 8.9 MW, the total harm of the farm run against no solar is F1 +0.495, false-flag share +0.180, and bright-minus-dull +0.181. The level contrast is +0.358, +0.052, and +0.005 of those, and the farm weather contrast is +0.140, +0.139, and +0.183. The same split holds at D3. The level contrast comes from the lower level of the reading and its fold at zero. The smooth twin's real power behind the reading is in reverse flow in 7.5% of the scorable midday half-hours (seed 0, all months), and within 1 MW of zero in another 18.4%, against 0.1% and 0.6% for the solar-free twin. From May to September the share in reverse flow is 8% for the smooth twin, 20% for the farm run, and 23% for the CAMS run (the curve-gate table in printed/audit.txt). The experiment cannot turn the fold off, so it cannot split the level contrast any further. Experiment 697 had already shown the same kind of harm: its level-matched control moved the midday F1 from 0.767 to 0.559.

With no engine injected, the injected farm's half-hourly variation alone makes the tracker flag the engine. The farm run's flagged share exceeds its smooth twin's by +0.146 (+0.098 to +0.198) at D8, and the CAMS run's exceeds its twin's by +0.000. The tracker fits 3 blocks to the farm run with no engine and none to the smooth twin. The farm's half-hourly changes at midday have a robust spread (1.4826 times the median absolute change) of 0.758 MVA at D8, against 0.461 for the farm's smooth twin and 0.276 with no solar. The farm sits at another site, so its cloud pattern is not the weather at D8. The farm weather contrast therefore measures the effect of a rough solar curve and not of D8's own weather.

The CAMS weather contrast is weak, and a smoother curve is a simpler reason than any property of the weather. The CAMS run's F1 falls by 0.043 (+0.002 to +0.082), under the threshold of 0.05. The CAMS shape is hourly and smoother than the farm's half-hourly series: the spread of half-hourly changes is 0.520 MVA for the CAMS run, against 0.758 for the farm run. The thirds of the bright-minus-dull criterion are thirds of the host's CAMS shape, so the criterion can show whether the harm follows the host's own brightness, and it cannot show harm that follows the injected source's brightness at another site. The audit's correlation of the farm with the host's CAMS shape within each cell of month and half-hour is 0.765 at D8 and 0.724 at D3. The statement "weather explains D8's swing between the eras" holds when the bright-minus-dull harm is at least 0.125 (about half of the +0.256 swing in the label-only checks below) with the interval above zero. It holds for the farm contrast (+0.183, 8.9 MW) and fails for the CAMS contrast (+0.034).

Between the no-solar run and the farm run at D8, precision falls from 0.987 to 0.210. The table holds the pooled midday scores of 3 seeds, with the smoothed labels, on the scored rows. The no-solar F1 is 0.766 on those rows and 0.767 on every observed half-hour.

docs.title: What the labels of D8 show before any injection
docs.text:
Three label-only checks show that D8's labels in the solar era behave differently from the labels in the net era, and none of the three shows that solar generation is the cause. The checks read the stored smoothed labels of experiment 694's tracker, with the drops kept. Intervals resample 1,000 times over whole weeks. The checks were seen before the thresholds were set.

Check Net era Solar era Swing (solar minus net) Flagged share on weekends and bank holidays, 09:00 to 15:00, negative spark spread +0.020 (+0.011 to +0.030) +0.188 (+0.118 to +0.262) +0.168 (+0.097 to +0.243) Flagged share at night, 00:00 to 05:00 +0.036 (+0.024 to +0.048) +0.121 (+0.083 to +0.159) +0.086 (+0.043 to +0.127) Bright-minus-dull flagged share, 10:00 to 15:00 -0.170 (-0.225 to -0.113) +0.086 (-0.017 to +0.191) +0.256 (+0.149 to +0.383)

Without the drops the swings are +0.174, +0.036, and +0.298. The solar-era bright-minus-dull value alone includes zero with the drops kept (+0.086, -0.017 to +0.191) and excludes it without them (+0.139, +0.016 to +0.267). The night share also rises, and solar generation makes no power at night, so the labels changed between the eras for at least one reason that solar output cannot supply.

The label-only checks are consistent with restricting experiment 697's price, weekday, and schedule claims to the net era. The weekend cheap-spark flag share rises from 0.020 to 0.188, the night share from 0.036 to 0.121, and the bright-minus-dull share changes sign. These changes are observations about the labels and not a verdict. The changes do not show that the solar-era pattern in experiment 697 is false. Experiment 697's claims concern 16:00 to 19:00, and this experiment computes no criterion there.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figure 1 shows which solar curves reproduce D8's solar-era reading. Each panel is one host and capacity. Lines show the median reading by fifth of CAMS solar output, May to September, 10:00 to 15:00, for D8's solar era, no solar, the CAMS run, the farm run, and the CAMS smooth twin. The farm and CAMS runs at D8 with 8.9 MW and the farm run at D3 pass the gate.

Figure 2 shows the harm from the level and from weather at each host. Dots are estimates and lines are 95% intervals for each criterion. The farm weather contrast is orange, the CAMS weather contrast is sky blue, and the level contrast is blue.

Figure 3 shows the tracker's scores by local hour at D8 before the engine with 8.9 MW. The farm run (orange) and its smooth twin (purple) lie below the no-solar run (green) in the middle of the day and close to it at night. Hourly values are not printed, so the figure carries no further claim.

Figure 4 shows the three label-only checks by era. Blue is the net era and orange is the solar era, with and without the drops.

docs.title: What the experiment cannot show
docs.text:
• The amount of solar generation behind D8's meter is unknown. The capacities of 7.0 MW and 8.9 MW come from the private review and from experiment 673's register row, and the curve gate only checks that the injected curve resembles D8's solar-era reading.
  • The injected farm is at another site. Its cloud pattern is not D8's weather. The CAMS contrast uses the weather at the host's own location, the nearest of the checks we ran, and that contrast is weak.
  • One engine record supplies the engine. Gas A is one engine with its own running pattern, drawn as whole days with no weekday pattern, so other engines may behave differently.
  • Step 4's recall contrast is too imprecise to lower a verdict. The contrast (bright minus dull, solar era minus net era) is +0.275 (-0.617 to +0.754), with a half-width of 0.69 against the 0.10 that the rule requires. Whole local days inside off-spells give 57 days in the net era and 16 days (768 half-hours) in the solar era.
  • The criteria are read at 10:00 to 15:00 only. The experiment says nothing about the evening window of experiment 697.

docs.title: Options for handling solar generation in the reading
docs.text: One option is to subtract an estimate of the solar term before the tracker reads the reading, and another is to restrict the tracker's claims. An estimate of the solar term from CAMS, from a fitted solar model, or from a neighbouring solar farm could shrink the level and weather harm at midday, but adds an estimate whose own error enters the labels. Alternatively, claims could be restricted to hours and seasons with little sunlight, or to the net era, with the solar era left to a method that models the solar term. The experiment gives no basis to choose among the options.

docs.title: Open questions for a later experiment
docs.text: Two designs might settle the weather question. A design whose paired half-width for the farm weather contrast falls under 0.05, together with a coverage measure over daylight half-hours chosen before the audit, might decide it. A test with weather taken from the host's own CAMS irradiance would separate the farm's roughness from real weather as the cause.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• The audit passed with 0 failed checks. The audit asserts the midday F1 of experiment 697's control C1 (0.767) and of its level-matched control (0.559), the false-flag share of the level-matched control (0.020 with zero injected output, 0.027 with under 1 block), the lag-0 alignment of the reading and of the farm with the CAMS shape (strongest correlation at lag 0 in four tests), and step 4's counts in the net and solar eras of 52 and 29 off-spells (4,913 and 2,083 half-hours) and of 57 and 16 whole days.
  • The weekend cheap-spark share is 0.188 under this experiment's row definition (observed half-hours not on a clock-change day, drops kept).
  • None of the conditions that call for an audit of this experiment held, by the author's reading: no control failed, the result agrees in direction with the prediction, a leave-one-out check is not possible with two hosts, and no sister experiment gives an interval to compare with. The maintainer decides whether to run an audit.
  • A fresh Sonnet agent reviewed the code before the first run. The code guards against the three faults the review found: a farm contrast whose twin shared no level with the farm, --ignore-gate writing jobs, and a failed audit writing the gate.
  • Anonymisation holds. No SVG text node holds a four-digit year, no printed file holds a date, and the private data folder holds every dated series.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Architecture.

  • Tracker: experiment 694's M2 grid filter, run through experiment 697's track_span, with the smoothed labels as the headline and the filtered labels beside them. The fitted block is 1.75 MW for the three engine seeds of every scored cell, and 2.25 MW or 3.50 MW in step 4's solar-era fits.
  • Injected engine: Gas A's whole local days, drawn at random with no weekday pattern by experiment 697's drive_series (kind null), with the seed recipe of experiment 697.
  • Injected solar: at 7.0 MW and 8.9 MW of AC capacity, one of four curves: the farm's normalised half-hourly output (the farm is one of the four of experiment 662, chosen as the one with the highest finite share over both spans), the CAMS shape of the host, and the two smooth twins. Farm gaps are filled with the farm's cell mean and are left out of every score. The CAMS shape comes from the stored panel of experiment 196, built by studies.dp_features.
  • Fold: the real power behind a reading is sqrt(max(y^2 - q^2, 0)), where y is the reading and q = 0.14 MVA is the reactive-power floor of experiment 196. Solar and engine output are subtracted together once, and the reading is sqrt((real - total)^2 + q^2). The signed real power is stored for the fold census.
  • Hosts: D8 before the engine (the span of experiment 697's control C1) and D3 in its solar era (control C2).

Training regime.

  • No machine-learning model is trained. The tracker's fits are the fits the filter computes on each injected reading, at 22 to 51 seconds per run on CPU.
  • Jobs: 58 runs (48 on host readings and 10 on D8's own readings), with 3 seeds for each host, capacity, and shape plus a run with no engine, on 8 workers in 283 seconds. The curve gate left 48 of the 72 host runs that the design allows.
  • Seeds: the engine's day draw uses seed 0 to 2 plus the series offset and the control offset of experiment 697, so the D8 twin draws the days of control C1.

Measurement.

  • Rows: scorable half-hours from 10:00 to 15:00 local time. Every run of a host is scored on the same rows.
  • Metrics: F1 against the injected truth (one or more blocks running, at least 0.985 MW), the false-flag share, and the bright-minus-dull flagged share, with thirds of the host's CAMS shape within each cell of local half-hour, weekday class, and month, above 50 W/m2.
  • Intervals: one draw of whole ISO weeks (2,000 resamples) serves every run of a host, so each contrast is paired. The label-only checks use 1,000 resamples.
  • Decision rule: as in the front matter, with the curve gate, the twin's F1, the paired half-width of the farm weather contrast, and the coverage clause tested first.
  • Step 4: Gas A is injected into whole local days inside off-spells in D8's stored labels, 5 seeds in each era, and the recall by CAMS third is compared between the eras.
  • Thresholds: 0.05 (F1 and bright-minus-dull) and 0.02 (false-flag share) were set after seeing the stored controls of experiment 697, so they are not an independent test. The coverage limit is 90% of daylight half-hours, and the changes to it are listed under Verdict.
  • Grey in the figures: the zero line and the threshold line use the theme's grey (ENSEMBLE_LINE), which is not one of the five main Open Climate Fix (OCF) colours. The maintainer may replace that grey.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• ml-experiments/00698-gas-engine-state-tracker-part-5-does-pv-harm-the-disaggregation/e00698_common.py: constants, the job list, the farm loader (copied from experiment 405's farm_norm_series, because importing it needs torch), the solar curves, the fold, the paired week-block intervals, and the audit marker check.
  • e00698_audit.py: the data audit and curve gate (steps 1 and 2). Writes printed/audit.txt and the private audit.json and gate.json.
  • e00698_jobs.py: the tracker runs (steps 3 and 4), one jobs/<name>.npz each. Writes printed/jobs.txt.
  • e00698_labels.py: the three label-only checks of D8 by era.
  • e00698_score.py: the five contrasts, the pooled scores, the fold census, the spread of changes, and step 4's recall. Writes printed/score_report.txt and the private scores.json.
  • e00698_verdict.py: applies the decision rule. Writes printed/verdict.txt and verdict.json.
  • e00698_figures.py: the four published figures, with a guard against a year in any SVG text.
  • e00698_selftest.py: 27 known-answer tests on synthetic inputs.
  • docs/ml-experiments/00698-gas-engine-state-tracker-part-5-does-pv-harm-the-disaggregation/f1_curve_gate.svg to f4_label_only_checks.svg: the four figures.
  • data/ml-experiments/00698-gas-engine-state-tracker-part-5-does-pv-harm-the-disaggregation/: private. It holds jobs/ (dated runs, read by e00698_score.py), audit.json, gate.json, scores.json, and verdict.json.
  • Inputs from earlier experiments: experiment 694's panel and D8 era records, experiment 697's stored frames, controls, and engine draw, experiment 695's grid helpers, and experiment 39's farm frame.

docs.title: Background for experiment workers
docs.text: Read this page, and the pages it links, before you plan an experiment. The pages state what earlier experiments established about the data sets and about the scoring rules, in short bullets, and link the page that owns each fact. The pages exist because several mistakes that cost an experiment a re-run were facts that an earlier experiment had already found and filed on a page the planner did not open.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. This page: the reading order and the update rule.
  2. NGED power telemetry: series, units, tables, timestamps.
  3. Weather inputs by product: which weather exists when.
  4. Row sets and scoring: row sets, metric, intervals, gating.
  5. Substation information fields: metadata, hierarchy, capacity.
  6. Metered generators and anonymisation: farms, caps, labels.
  7. Market and other data: prices, PV_Live, DFS, null results.
  8. Problems and the best forecast: baselines, best guess, scores.
  9. Adopted and open questions: what is settled, who owns the rest.
  10. Data processing: steps every experiment applies to the data.
  11. Glossary: terms the experiment pages use without defining.

The reference page What is on disk says where each data set sits under data/ and how to read it.

docs.title: Three facts that have cost experiments time
docs.text:
• The TimeSeriesMetadata table has 33 rows, and 32 series carry data. Count 32 series; do not change 32 to 33 (NGED power telemetry).
  • ERA5 reaches the forecast about 5 days late. Any ERA5 value used at a lag time is a ceiling. Name the weather source at lag times in every write-up (weather inputs).
  • Read power through studies.power.scan_power. The raw table holds rows that cleaning flags (NGED power telemetry).

docs.title: Update rule
docs.text:
• The experiment that learns or overturns a fact about the data fixes the page. Edit the bullet in place so that the page describes the present, and change its "last checked" line.
  • Add or correct at most five bullets per experiment. Write the bullet where a planner would look first, and link the experiment or page that owns the evidence. If nothing changed, write "background: no change" in the pull request body. The merger checks the pull request body for the list of changed bullets or for that sentence.
  • End every factual bullet with an evidence tag in the form (exp 179; 6 farms, one year; provisional): the experiment ids, the scope of the evidence, and a status of established, provisional, or overturned by N. A bullet about code or disk layout says (code) or (disk). A bullet that digests a linked docs page says (docs), and that page owns the evidence. A bullet whose evidence nobody has traced says (unchecked).
  • Mark a bullet established only when it states a count or a definition, or when a second experiment or row set reproduced the finding. Every other bullet is provisional.
  • Check a tag before you rely on it. Open the result.md of each cited experiment and confirm that the experiment supports the claim, that the scope matches, and that the status fits. Replace (unchecked) with a traced tag whenever you find the owning source.
  • A later experiment may overturn a bullet. The overturning experiment changes the status in the tag to overturned by N, where N is its id, and rewrites the bullet to state the present fact.
  • Do not copy a rule from a page that owns it. Link the owner page instead.

Last checked against experiment 321.

docs.title: Adopted and open questions
docs.text: No experiment result is adopted in production, a set of results are candidates for the next model release, and each open question belongs to one theme. This page gives one line per item and links the theme that owns it. A planner checks here before proposing an experiment that a theme already holds as settled or planned. Evidence tags follow the update rule.

docs.title: Adopted
docs.text: • Nothing is adopted. The release log lists no numbered model release, and no result.md carries production_status: adopted (model releases) (docs).

docs.title: Candidates for the next release
docs.text:
• Primaries and supply points: weekly refits, and a five-member blend at Primaries (experiment 87). Owner: production reference and best guess (docs).
  • Retraining: weekly refitting without the 14-day correction (experiments 34, 48, 81). It holds at 16 Primaries on two sets of runs, but 3 series carry much of the gain. Owner: retraining and training history (exp 34, 48, 81; 16 Primaries; provisional).
  • Solar and wind farms: the pooled mixture over ensemble members, the solar spread factor, and the wind power-curve base margin (experiments 2, 16, 20). Owner: calibration and uncertainty (docs).
  • Solar offset: a forecast of the unmetered solar output as an XGBoost base margin at Primaries with a clean capacity estimate (experiments 64, 78). Owner: solar disaggregation (docs).
  • Physics-based demand model: the convex model with a Kalman filter (experiment 111), a recent-error correction recipe (experiment 155), and a correction neural network with a two-number solar summary (experiment 220). Owner: differentiable physics: forecast engine (docs).

docs.title: Open questions by theme
docs.text:
• Do the spread factor, the blend, and the solar offset hold on a second validation year? The first year chose their settings. Owner: production reference and best guess (docs).
  • Which training source suits solar and wind farms, the ERA5-trained mixture or the ensemble's own history? Needs more than 6 solar and 3 wind farms. Owner: production reference and best guess (docs).
  • Does weekly refitting beat the stack on an unscored year and with the full ensemble, and why do older training years score worse? Owner: retraining and training history (docs).
  • Do old years of history help the physics-based demand model? The answer changed sign between two scored years. Owner: differentiable physics: long history and drift (docs).
  • Does one model pooled across Primaries match a model per substation, and does pooling hold at hundreds of series? Owners: hierarchy and pooling and differentiable physics: pooling across substations (docs).
  • Does a calibrator that sees recent power help solar and wind farms, and does a missing-lag flag widen the band where a lag is missing? Owner: calibration and uncertainty (docs).
  • Does lagged power help once the 14-day correction is in place? No experiment has combined them. Owner: lagged power and error correction (docs).
  • Does the live Met Office UKV feed give wind farms the gain the research archive did? Owners: generator forecasting and weather products and blending (docs).
  • Does a better sunshine forecast close the gap to the true-sunshine oracle? Owner: solar disaggregation (docs).
  • Which extra inputs help Primary demand beyond the calendar and solar set? A heating term gave 0.14 points in cold hours on one winter, under its 0.3 target. Owner: demand inputs (docs).
  • Does any forecast curtail less than another once about 2,500 series are scored, and are the forecast tails too narrow in general? Owner: curtailment cost (docs).
  • What physical plant reproduces each metered solar farm's output, and how much rooftop solar sits behind each substation? Owners: metered solar farms and differentiable physics: embedded generation (docs).
  • Does the physics-based demand model, driven by ensemble weather, forecast Primary demand up to 7 days ahead as well as BG2? Experiment 111 could not tell them apart. Owner: differentiable physics: forecast engine (exp 111; 5 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • How should the physics-based demand model combine its daily profile with holiday, heating, and solar terms? Owner: differentiable physics: demand, calendar and weather (docs).

Last checked against experiment 225.

docs.title: Market and other data
docs.text: Experiments hold public price, demand, solar, and carbon data, and no experiment has yet found a source that improved a forecast of NGED's series by more than the experiment's decision threshold. This page lists each source, what it is for, when its values become known, and where it sits on disk. The price series are described in full on the GB price data page and in the data sources page.

docs.title: What each source is for
docs.text:
Source Folder under data/studies/downloads/market/ What it is Known when Imbalance system price elexon_system_prices Price paid for energy short or long in a half-hour About 19 minutes after the period ends Market index price elexon_mid_apx Short-term exchange price, half-hourly During the half-hour Day-ahead price neso_n2ex_day_ahead Hourly auction price The morning before delivery Demand outturn, generation by fuel elexon_demand_outturn, elexon_fuelhh National demand and generation Demand: about 30 minutes after the half-hour; generation: at publish_time Demand and wind forecasts elexon_ndf, elexon_tsdf, elexon_windfor National forecasts, every publication kept At publish_time Frequency elexon_frequency 15-second values and a half-hourly summary Not checked Bid, offer, and notification data elexon_bod, elexon_boalf, elexon_pn, elexon_mels Per Balancing Mechanism Unit Within minutes, for gate-closed periods Carbon intensity carbon_intensity National forecast and actual, grams per kWh Forecast up to 2 days ahead PV_Live pv_live, pv_live_gsp Sheffield Solar's estimate of solar generation Revised after first publication; updated_at gives the last revision Octopus Agile octopus_agile_east_midlands Half-hourly import tariff, East Midlands The afternoon before the delivery day

The "known when" column digests the publication table and the folders' READMEs (docs, disk). Nothing we hold says when the frequency series is published.

docs.title: Timestamps and coverage
docs.text:
• The market tables mark the start of each period, in UTC, whereas the NGED power feed marks the end of each half-hour. Shift one side by 30 minutes before joining (data sources; docs).
  • PV_Live labels each half-hour by its end. The stored time column is PV_Live's datetime_gmt minus 30 minutes (disk).
  • Most market folders cover one year, 2025-09-01 to 2026-09-30. The two exceptions are pv_live_gsp, which runs from 2019-01-01 to 2026-10-14 for the Walpole and Bicker Fen grid supply points, and octopus_agile_east_midlands, which runs from 2025-08-31 to 2026-09-01 (disk).
  • Experiments 177 and 185 keep the system prices for longer spans in their own public/ folders, under data/ml-experiments/00185-*/public/system_prices (disk).
  • The demand flexibility service (DFS) has no page of its own. The NESO service-requirement archive ends on 2026-03-27 and is stored as dfs_service_requirement.csv under data/ml-experiments/00177-*/public/ (exp 185; 1,231 days with a record; disk).
  • Each licence's attribution wording applies wherever the data is shown (docs).
  • Elexon's indicated demand and generation reach at most 42 hours ahead, and the study found no table that maps their regions to NGED's licence areas, so neither is a ready input (study; docs).

docs.title: Price features tried
docs.text:
• A price at the target half-hour lowered the pooled error by 0.52 points of capacity in the selection year and 0.18 in the confirmation year (interval included zero), and a price from another week matched about 0.45 of the 0.52 (exp 15; pooled series, two years; provisional).
  • Lagged prices gave no gain that survived the confirmation year. A shuffled price from another week reproduced most of the selection-year gain at the one battery-affected substation (exp 10; 2 listed substations, two years; provisional).
  • Adding price changes to the price level lowered the error by 0.037 and 0.050 points of capacity, and by 0.039 and 0.047 against changes taken from another week. The verdict was small gain, under the 0.1-point threshold, and the demand-inputs theme does not adopt it (exp 25; Primaries, two years; provisional). See the demand inputs theme.
  • National system price, DFS events, national demand, wind, solar, and interconnector flow each explain under 1% of the day-to-day variation in the best-guess forecast's loss. Giving the Kalman filter the signal in hindsight made the score slightly worse (exp 185; 5 substations, 1,683 substation-days of one scored year; provisional).
  • Modelling a price-following asset in the history did not improve the forecast at D8 or D14. The ceiling with the true price gained 0.6% at D8 (exp 191; 2 Primaries; provisional).
  • PV_Live lags at the two grid supply points gave no resolved gain (-0.03 points of capacity; exp 27; 2 GSPs; provisional). A PV_Live-based solar forecast gave -0.14 with an interval that included zero, and the true PV_Live value gave -0.50, almost all at leads of 7 to 15 days (exp 28; 2 GSPs; provisional).

  • Add a placebo twin to every price input, a copy with the right level and the wrong timing (exp 10, 15; Primaries; provisional).

  • The Elexon APX Market Index Data is the within-day half-hourly price, not the day-ahead auction. The N2EX provider returns 0.00 in 2023, so use the APX provider only. Of the APX index's half-hours, 20 carry price 0 with volume 0 and are treated as missing (exp 697; 2023-06 to 2026-06; provisional; the rule is in data processing, timestamps and availability).

  • Weekday evenings, high half-hourly prices, and D8's own demand peak coincide, so the engine's running cannot be tied to the price alone (exp 697; D8 and 3 host Primaries; provisional).

Last checked against experiment 697.

docs.title: Metered generators and anonymisation
docs.text: NGED meters 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, and 3 other generator or storage series in the trial area, and the output of every one of them may leave the private data store only under an anonymous label. This page lists the series, the export-cap record for the one generator under active network management, and what a plot or pull request may show. Public data about generators is treated differently, and the last section says how.

docs.title: The series
docs.text:
• The 32 series that carry data include 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, and 3 other generators or storage units. The three are one battery energy storage system, one biofuel generator, and one series of type "Other (Generation)" (disk).
  • Of the 3 wind series, 1 is metered in MW and 2 in MVA (disk).
  • A type of "Other (Generation)" need not be solar. Do not assume a daylight profile (exp 182; one farm behind D8; provisional).
  • Read a farm's cleaned series from cleaned_solar_farms.parquet in data/ml-experiments/00179-*/ and keep rows with a null drop_reason. The file has no site column, so join studies.pv_dataset.pv_sites() on time_series_id for the label, the coordinates, and the capacity (exp 183; 6 farms; provisional).
  • Farms miss 7.6% to 27.6% of their half-hours. Check coverage before comparing farms (exp 179; 6 farms; provisional).
  • About 3.0% of the daylight half-hours of the six solar farms read exactly zero. Count a zero actual as inside a quantile forecast only by a rule stated in advance: the share at or below the 0.01 quantile (3.3% to 3.5% for research default 1) counts them, and the share strictly below it (1.2% to 1.4%) does not (exp 321; 6 farms; provisional).
  • A flat top in a farm's output is not proof of clipping. The cause is not settled (exp 179, 183, 218; 6 farms; provisional). See the metered solar farms theme.
  • A near-zero reading at a wind farm is not always low wind. Of the half-hours above 1.5 times cut-in wind speed, 1.6%, 13%, and 30% sit in the idle band at W1, W2, and W3, and ERA5 wind speed finds only part of them (exp 210; 3 wind farms; provisional).
  • UKV wind lowered the error of the three wind farms by about 0.2 points of capacity at 24 to 54 hours ahead, using a research archive and not the live feed, so the gain is an upper limit (exp 54; 3 wind farms; small gain; provisional). See the generator forecasting theme.

docs.title: Active network management and the curtailment feed
docs.text:
• One generator in the trial area is connected under active network management (ANM), and NGED has confirmed there are no others. A generator with no cap record therefore ran free (network page; docs).
  • Two records exist and they are different quantities. The setpoint history is one row per change of the export cap, in MW. The curtailment/ feed on NGED's S3 bucket is a derived volume of MW lost (data sources; docs).
  • The setpoint history is the one to use. The cap's sign, its start date, and the month the scheme goes live are on the network page (docs).
  • The export sits in data/studies/downloads/observations/NGED-ANM/, and studies.export_cap joins it onto an experiment's grid. It drops capped hours from training and keeps them at scoring (disk).
  • The clamp uses the cap in force, which a day-ahead forecast does not have, so it is an upper bound on what the cap could buy (code).
  • Curtailment at substations is scored by cost, not by this feed. The scoring code is a worked example on 2 bulk supply points and could not rank forecasts at the headline limit (exp 84; 2 BSPs, one scored year; provisional). See the curtailment cost theme.

docs.title: What may be published
docs.text:
• Never publish an NGED metered generator's time series with its name or identifier. The rule covers charts, tables, leaderboards, dashboards, reports, and issue and pull request bodies. The full rule is in CLAUDE.md (docs).
  • Use the labels from studies.anonymise: "A" to "F" for the solar farms and W1 to W3 for the wind farms. site_labels_for assigns them under a fixed seed, and it raises on a different count of generators (code).
  • Put no calendar dates on the axis of a generator's time series, and publish no output in MW. Normalise by the generator's own capacity. The dataviz skill's anonymisation section and the study skill's anonymisation section own the rest (docs).
  • Keep any plot of one farm's time series, and the cleaned series, under data/ml-experiments/. The private tables stay there (docs).
  • D1 to D22 label demand-side series, not generators in general. The glossary defines them, and substations may be named (docs).

docs.title: Public generator data
docs.text:
• Time series from public sources may be named. The settled output of Balancing Mechanism Units in Elexon's published data may be shown with names, in MW, on calendar dates. A study that mixes public and NGED generators anonymises the NGED ones (docs).
  • The public-data studies are the solar BMU census and the solar BMU disaggregation. (docs)

Last checked against experiment 218.

docs.title: NGED power telemetry
docs.text: The power readings are half-hourly telemetry from 32 time series in NGED's trial area, and several of their properties change how an experiment must read them. This page lists the properties that have cost experiments time. The processing steps themselves are on the data-processing page, and the context of the network is on the network page.

docs.title: The series
docs.text:
• There are 32 series that carry data. They are 16 Primary substations, 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, 2 grid supply points (GSPs), 2 bulk supply points (BSPs), and 3 other generators or storage units (home page) (disk).
  • The TimeSeriesMetadata table has 33 rows. One row has no data. Count 32 series, and do not change 32 to 33 (disk).
  • "32" also counts something else on the network page. The 41 connected hydro sites sit across "32 distinct primary substations" (network page). That is a count of Primaries across all four licence areas and has no link to the 32 trial series (docs).
  • The time_series_type column does not say what a generator is. A type of "Other (Generation)" need not be solar, so do not assume a daylight profile (exp 182; one farm behind D8; provisional).
  • Label the generators "Solar farm A" to "Solar farm F" and similar outside the private data store. studies.anonymise holds the labels. Substations may be named. The D codes (D1 to D22) that the write-ups use are anonymised labels of the demand-side series, defined in the glossary (code).

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
• A series is metered in MW (signed active power) or in MVA (apparent power, never negative). Read the unit from the units column. Eight of the 16 Primaries are metered only in MVA, so solar output behind one of them appears as demand in daylight (disk).
  • Use an MVA Primary for demand only on dark rows. The rule, its evidence, and the row counts are in the data-processing page (exp 103; 8 MVA Primaries; established).
  • A negative value at an MVA series is a fault between the meter and us, not an export (PowerTimeSeries field description) (code).
  • GSPs and BSPs are not clean demand. The GSPs are dominated by generation, and the BSPs sum the trial Primaries (data-processing page; exp 103; 2 GSPs, 2 BSPs; established).

docs.title: Raw and cleaned tables
docs.text:
• Two Delta tables hold the power: data/NGED/power_time_series.delta (raw) and data/NGED/cleaned_power_time_series.delta (cleaned). The cleaned table holds every raw row plus a nullable drop_reason column that names the cleaning rule that flagged the row (code).
  • Read power through studies.power.scan_power. scan_power keeps only the rows with a null drop_reason. A study must not name the raw table; a test enforces this (code).
  • Read the raw table only when the question is about availability. The raw table is what NGED delivered, and it holds the rows that cleaning flags (exp 182; series 32 and 33; provisional).
  • One cleaning rule exists today: substation_zero. It flags a reading of exactly 0 from a Primary, BSP, or GSP (nged_data.cleaning) (code).
  • substation_zero drops real zeros for a switched-out transformer. Switching experiments that need those rows must treat the flagged rows as kept (zero-reading entry; exp 132; switching log, few events; provisional).
  • For time_series_id 32 and 33, the cleaned and raw tables hold identical rows (exp 182, e00182_check.py; 2 series; provisional).

docs.title: Timestamps
docs.text:
• The time column marks the end of the half-hour that the reading covers. Do not shift it. Power timestamps show no 30-minute error on either side of NGED's fix of 2026-03-26 08:30 UTC (data-processing page; exp 103; 6 metered solar farms, with the Primaries only weakly tested; provisional).
  • Before that instant, the ingest moves NGED's stamp 30 minutes earlier (PowerTimeSeries.correct_late_timestamps). A study must not shift the stamp a second time (code).
  • Move a power stamp 30 minutes earlier before joining a half-hourly price, because the price stamp marks the start of the half-hour (exp 697; one engine record of 44 days; provisional, data processing).
  • Join hourly power to a weather product that stamps the end of its hour on (time - 1 µs).truncate("1h") + 1h. The evidence is on the data-processing page (exp 103; CAMS and 6 metered solar farms; provisional).
  • Assume a power reading reaches the forecast 3.5 hours after the half-hour it covers. No experiment has measured the delay on live telemetry (exp 87, 104, 106; assumption; provisional).

docs.title: Gaps, ramp-up, and regime changes
docs.text:
• Count a series' history from its first unflagged row. Only five Primaries hold long histories: D5, D10, and D11 from 2019-09, D14 from 2019-10, and D16 from 2020-12. The late starters begin between 2023 and 2025 (exp 103; 16 Primaries; established).
  • The start cuts and the fixed lockdown window are on the data-processing page. See trim the start of each series and fixed windows (exp 6, 102, 103, 173; established).
  • Some series changed regime. D8's weekday daytime demand fell from about 9 MW to about 3 MW between 2023-10 and 2025 (exp 103; D8; provisional).
  • A residual-only segmentation dates D8's break exactly but finds only about half of 10% steps. At a penalty low enough to date the 2023-08-15 break it also finds 2 to 3 false regime changes per Primary-year, and a penalty that keeps false changes under 1 labels 42% of 14 to 60 day load shifts as states (experiment 295; 14 Primaries, injected steps; provisional).
  • D8's multi-day drops coincide with a gas-engine detector's running states. The detector flags 27 of the 28 drops that began after the engine left D8's reading, against about 1 in 5 comparable stretches. The link between the drops and the engine is not proved, because the drops and the detector both read D8's residual (experiment 291; D8; provisional).
  • D8's engine shows as a rise in the reading when demand is below about 3 MVA. D8's reading is apparent power and never negative, so it folds: from a level under 3 MVA, 626 of 627 merged steps of at least 1.5 MVA in 2023-09 to 2025-02 are rises, and from 8 to 10 MVA, 259 of 260 are falls (experiment 694; D8; provisional).
  • A tracker that fits the engine's unit count and size from the reading alone finds three units of about 1.75 MW at D8 and flags none at the other seven Primaries. The tracker finds a 1 MW unit injected into other Primaries in only 13 of 44 segments (experiment 694; 8 Primaries, 44 injected segments; provisional).
  • Solar-farm outages are too rare to test an availability state. Five of the six farms have at most 34 outage half-hours in the scored year, and the sixth has 165. An outage half-hour is a daylight half-hour with output under 5% of the physical power model's forecast (exp 301; 6 farms, one year; provisional).
  • About 3.0% of the six farms' scored daylight half-hours read exactly zero. Count the zeros before reading coverage at the 0.01 quantile: in own history, 1.2% to 1.4% of actual values fall strictly below it (exp 321; 6 farms, scored year; provisional).
  • A metered solar farm can climb to its rated output in stages over months. One farm took eight months (network page). The metered farms miss 7.6% to 27.6% of their half-hours, so check coverage before comparing farms (exp 179; 6 farms, one year; provisional).
  • A flat top in a farm's output is not proof of clipping. A pre-registered rule found AC clipping at 2 of 6 farms and a post hoc rule at 4 of 6, and an export cap or panel geometry makes the same shape (exp 179; 6 farms; provisional).
  • The farm series behind a disaggregated Primary can be almost absent. For D8, one farm has one raw reading ever, so "missing" is the baseline (exp 182; D8; provisional).
  • A metered farm's effective_capacity_mw may itself be estimated from output. Power over capacity near 1.0 is therefore not an independent level (exp 179, 183; 6 farms; provisional).
  • The causal engine tracker (which reads only data available at the time) finds about 65% of an injected engine's running half-hours. At Primary D4, with a real gas engine's recorded output added to its reading, the half-hour F1 score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) for "any unit running" is 0.785. Precision (the share of flagged half-hours that are running) is 0.998 and recall (the share of running half-hours found) is 0.647. The tracker flags 0.03% of D4's un-injected half-hours (experiment 695) (exp 695; one host Primary; provisional).

docs.title: Capacity
docs.text:
• Scores are in points of capacity, where capacity is the 99th percentile of the absolute power over the series' whole observed history. One point is 1% of that value. See the glossary (code).

Last checked against experiment 697.

docs.title: Problems and the current best forecast
docs.text: The experiments serve three problems: demand at Primary substations, the output of metered generators, and curtailment with its tails. Each bullet ends with an evidence tag (update rule), and the linked page owns the evidence.

docs.title: What NGED asks for
docs.text:
• The project must give NGED new information about forecasting for its assets, and a negative result counts (requirements) (docs).
  • The requirements page sets the forecast's shape, horizon, update cycle, and day-ahead deadline. Users mostly act on 1 to 10 days ahead, so skill in that band matters most (requirements) (docs).
  • The forecast is used for two decisions: buying flexibility ahead of a high-demand risk, and curtailing generators ahead of a high-export risk. The question users ask is how likely net demand is to cross a limit, so the tails of each forecast matter most (requirements) (docs).

docs.title: Problem 1: demand at Primary substations
docs.text:
• Version 1 covers 32 time series, of which 16 are Primary substations (NGED power telemetry counts the rest by type) (docs).
  • manual_heuristic is the baseline NGED recognises, and beating it is the core deliverable. It forecasts each half-hour from 13 analogues of past weeks (manual heuristic; glossary) (docs).
  • climatology is the second baseline. It forecasts from past power in the same calendar cell and uses no weather (glossary) (docs).
  • On 292 daily runs at the 16 Primaries, the quantile score was 6.182 for manual_heuristic and 7.368 for climatology, in points of capacity. The production-style xgboost_baseline scored 10.536, and the stack scored 5.543 (experiment 87) (exp 87; 16 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • At the 4 bulk and grid supply points the same three baselines scored 14.506, 14.883, and 20.859. The stack scored 13.559 (experiment 87) (exp 87; 4 supply points, one year; provisional).
  • No gain was found from removing D8's gas engine from the training target and adding a calendar average of the engine back. The CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, smaller is better) of the cleaned arm minus the raw arm A0's was +0.117 points of capacity (percentage points of D8's capacity), with a 98.3% interval from -0.070 to +0.412 that includes zero (experiment 695) (exp 695; D8, 8 monthly refits, 3 seeds; provisional).
  • An upper limit that reads D8's engine state at the valid time lowers CRPS by 1.4 to 2.4 points against the raw arm A0. No forecast has that state, so the limit shows where a gain could lie (experiment 695) (exp 695; D8, 8 monthly refits, a bound and not a forecast; provisional).
  • Giving the pre-training mixer D8's engine state, and then fine-tuning without it, did not improve the forecast: the change in CRPS was +0.009 points of capacity, and +0.009 means no change. The lower ends of the 98.75% intervals are -0.055 to -0.074, so no net gain above about 0.07 points is likely. A post hoc split (not planned, 95% intervals) at a host substation with a recorded engine's output added showed that the true state lowered CRPS by 0.059 when the engine was off and raised it by 0.225 when the engine ran, on about 19% of half-hours (experiment 696 (engine state in the pre-training mixer)) (exp 696; D8 and one host, 8 monthly refits, 10 seeds; provisional).

docs.title: Problem 2: generator output
docs.text:
• The generator experiments score 6 solar farms and 3 wind farms (row sets and scoring) (exp 1; fold A; established).
  • On the 292 runs, the two baselines scored 5.718 and 5.708 at solar farms, and 13.906 and 13.461 at wind farms. The production-style xgboost_baseline scored 8.784 and 17.171 (experiment 87) (exp 87; 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, one year; provisional).
  • climatology is level with manual_heuristic at solar farms, so a solar forecast shows skill only by beating both (experiment 87) (exp 87; 6 solar farms, one year; provisional).

docs.title: Problem 3: curtailment and tails
docs.text:
• Curtailment is the capping of generators beneath a substation when its export would pass a limit. The scoring code plans caps from a forecast of the substation's export, and charges the energy lost to the caps plus a penalty for export that stays over the limit (curtailment cost theme) (docs).
  • The two bulk supply points of the pilot hold too few events to rank forecasts at the headline limit, so no forecast has yet been shown to curtail less (experiment 84) (exp 84; 2 bulk supply points; provisional).
  • Tail calibration is reported beside the headline score in every forecasting experiment (row sets and scoring) (docs).
  • The production-style 0.95 quantile was exceeded in 49% of Primary cases, against 7% for the best guess of experiment 33 (experiment 33) (exp 33; 16 Primaries, 73 runs; provisional).

docs.title: The staged design
docs.text:
• The design under test splits the forecast into stages 0, 1a, and 2 (staged probabilistic forecast; glossary) (docs).
  • N1 is a single-stage model that the best guesses below build on (glossary) (docs).

docs.title: The best-guess recipes
docs.text:
• The best guess of experiment 33 beat the production-style forecast by 4.89 points at Primaries, 3.81 at solar farms, and 6.27 at wind farms. The recipe is N1 with the 14-day correction and a spread factor of 1.15 for Primaries, and an ERA5-trained mixture over the 51 members for farms (experiment 33; glossary) (exp 33; 16 Primaries, 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, one year; provisional).
  • BG2 scored 5.260 at the 16 Primaries and 12.925 at the 4 supply points, against 5.543 and 13.559 for the stack. The Primary gain is 0.283 points (98.75% interval -0.425 to -0.146) (experiment 87) (exp 87; 16 Primaries, 4 supply points, one year; provisional).
  • BG2 for Primaries is a blend of five models with a solar offset at 5 of 16 Primaries (glossary lists the models) (exp 87; 16 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • Refitting weekly instead of monthly lowers the Primary score by 0.123 points, and the blend by another 0.086. Removing the blend from BG2 raises the score by 0.091 (exp 87; 16 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • The solar offset lowers the Primary score by 0.114 points on the rows it can touch, which are the daylight rows from April to September at 5 of 16 Primaries. Over all rows the gain is 0.010 (exp 87; 5 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • Adding the 14-day correction to the supply-point model raises the score by 0.305 points. BG2 serves supply points without it (exp 87; 4 supply points, one year; provisional).
  • For farms, the ensemble-trained model scored 0.050 (solar) and 0.228 (wind) points worse than the ERA5-trained mixture, and neither interval rules out a loss beyond the accepted margin. No farm recipe is ranked (exp 87; 6 solar farms, 3 wind farms, one year; provisional).
  • Removing the three recent-power inputs from the best-guess XGBoost model worsens the Primary score by 0.36 points once one substation's commissioning months are cut, and the supply-point score by 0.28. Farm scores barely change (experiment 102) (exp 102; 16 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • The physics-based demand model could not be told apart from BG2 at 5 Primaries. The convex model with a Kalman filter on recent errors (GAM-K; see the animated explainer) scored 2.800 against 2.780 for BG2 (difference +0.020, interval -0.109 to +0.157, not like for like) (experiment 111) (exp 111; 5 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • Adding a correction neural network and a two-number solar summary to the physics-based best guess lowered its score from 2.752 to 2.616 (C1 -0.136, 99% interval -0.253 to -0.047). The two gains add (ratio 0.99) (experiment 220) (exp 220; 5 Primaries, one year; provisional).

docs.title: Superseded positions
docs.text:
• A 14-day error correction on a frozen model is no longer the default for Primary demand. The position of experiments 17, 19, and 21 is superseded by weekly refitting without the correction (experiments 34 and 48) (retraining theme) (exp 34, 48; Primary demand; provisional).
  • "Keep ERA5 for stage 1a until a CAMS arm has a bias-corrected ensemble" is superseded. Experiment 14 paired a CAMS-trained stage 1a with a stage 0 correction, and scored 0.067 points better than raw ensemble input (97.5% interval -0.094 to -0.039); its verdict is inconclusive because the daylight bias check failed in single months (experiment 14) (exp 14; 16 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • "Train demand stage 1a from 2023-09" is superseded. Each Primary now starts at its first usable date (NGED power telemetry), and whether old years help is unsettled (long history and drift theme) (exp 103, 104, 106, 107; 16 Primaries for start dates, 5 for history; provisional).
  • "ERA5-trained" in experiments 1, 3, 9, and 22 assumes ERA5 is the only estimate of past weather. Name the weather source at lag times in every write-up (weather inputs) (docs).

docs.title: What production does today
docs.text:
• No numbered model release exists, so the live service has no adopted experiment winner (model releases) (docs).
  • The production-style forecast loses to manual_heuristic at Primaries. In experiment 13 its mean absolute error of the median was 1.69 points of capacity higher (99% interval +0.98 to +2.59) (experiment 13) (exp 13; 16 Primaries, 73 runs; provisional).
  • The origin of the stored production-style table is unconfirmed, so its scores may not match the deployed forecast (glossary) (exp 87; stored table; provisional).

docs.title: Which results are provisional
docs.text:
• Every score above rests on one validation year (July 2025 to June 2026), and several settings were chosen on that year. The gains are probably optimistic (production reference and best guess) (docs).
  • Scores on different row sets, quantile levels, or series counts are not comparable. The 16 Primary scores near 5 and the 5-Primary scores near 2.7 come from different rows (row sets and scoring) (docs).

Last checked against experiment 225.

docs.title: Row sets and scoring
docs.text: Two scores are comparable only when they cover the same rows, the same series, and the same quantile levels. This page lists the named row sets, the score and its intervals, the tail and curtailment reporting that every forecasting experiment carries, and the retraining defaults. The procedure is in the ml-experiment skill, and terms are in the glossary.

docs.title: Series sets
docs.text:
• The fold-A demand set has 22 demand-side series (D1 to D22): 16 Primaries, 4 BSPs or GSPs, and a battery and a biofuel generator (glossary) (exp 3; fold A; established).
  • The generator experiments score 9 series (6 solar farms and 3 wind farms) (exp 1; fold A; established).
  • The differentiable-physics (DP) series uses five long-history MW Primaries as its decision set (NGED power telemetry) (exp 103; 5 Primaries; established).

docs.title: Row sets
docs.text:
• A row set is a named set of forecast origins, series, and valid times, and experiment_store.read_predictions raises when a prediction set covers a different row set. State the row_set_id in the plan, and read the benchmark from the same row set (code).
  • No experiment scores a valid time on or after 2026-07-01. The ml-experiment skill owns the rule and the reason (code).
row_set_id Rows Defined in fold_a_tuesdays_v1 53 Tuesday ENS runs and the 9 generator series; every case of the first day sits on a Tuesday or Wednesday, so the set does not suit demand Experiments 1 and 2 fold_a_every5d_v1 Every fifth day at 00:00 UTC from 2025-07-01 (73 runs); each lead band has 14% of its cases on each weekday Experiment 3 fold_a_daily_gap_v1 The 292 daily 00:00 UTC runs from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 that fold_a_every5d_v1 does not hold Experiment 48 control_fold_b_daily_v1 274 runs, 2023-07-01 to 2024-03-31, 9 km grid Experiment 81 era5_val_* ERA5-based validation years (for example era5_val_3folds_2023_07_to_2026_06_v1) Experiments 6 and 11 dp_mw_v1 508,341 half-hours at the MW decision series, after the start cuts, the fixed lockdown window, and the switching mask Experiment 103 dp_mva_dark_v1 352,841 dark half-hours at the MVA-only Primaries Experiment 103 dp_christmas_daily_v1, age1_daily_2025_07_to_2026_06_v1 Christmas-period origins; the old-year training check Experiments 173 and 93
  • Read the defining experiment before reusing a row set (code).
  • The DP series uses season-years from July to June. Tuning is 2023-24, the replicate year is 2024-25, and the scored year is 2025-26 (FIRST_SEASON_MONTH in studies.dp_calendar; exp 109; DP series; established).
  • Count eligible long-history sites at each tuning year's first day. Five Primaries qualify at 2024-07-01 (exp 103; 5 Primaries; established).
  • Choose a row set that covers every weekday, and give each experiment a climatology row (exp 3; fold A; provisional).

docs.title: The score and its intervals
docs.text:
• The score, skill, baselines, capacity, and interval level are defined in the glossary. See quantile score, skill, capacity, interval-level convention, and rolling refit. The procedure is in the ml-experiment skill (code).
  • Experiments 33, 34, and 48 use 9 quantile levels (0.05 to 0.95). Experiment 87 and later use 11 levels (those plus 0.01 and 0.99). Scores with different levels cannot be compared (exp 33, 48, 87; all experiments; established).
  • The sample resolves gains of roughly 0.3 points of capacity or more, on 16 Primaries, 9 generator series, and one validation year (experiments README) (exp 3; 16 Primaries, 9 generators, one year; provisional).
  • Half-hours within a day, and members within a run, are strongly correlated, so a row bootstrap understates the interval (code: studies.bootstrap resamples whole months).

docs.title: Tails and curtailment
docs.text:
• Every forecasting experiment reports tail calibration beside the headline score. The tail table gives coverage and pinball loss at 0.01, 0.05, 0.95, and 0.99, through studies.tail_calibration (code).
  • Write q01 to q99, actual, lead_hours, and time_series_id in the predictions, so the tail and curtailment metrics can score them (code).
  • The curtailment metric is studies.node_curtailment (node plus its generators). The headline limit is a fraction f of the node's maximum observed export before the scored year, with f = 0.9 by default and 0.75 and 0.5 as sweeps. The real published thermal limit appears only as a reference mark and in the event census, because NGED curtails so that one more fault still leaves headroom. Metric details: cost-savings metrics (code).
  • Report the manual-heuristic baseline arm (capacity_forecast) as the maintainer's unconfirmed understanding of NGED's practice. Experiment 84 is the pattern to copy (exp 84; 2 bulk supply points; provisional).
  • Headline f = 0.5, instead of the default 0.9, when f = 0.9 gives fewer than 20 event half-hours. At the Boston and Skegness bulk supply points, experiment 255 found 2 event half-hours at f = 0.9 and 5 at f = 0.75, so it headlined f = 0.5, which gives 72. Experiment 277 also headlines the 0.5 limit (exp 255, 277; 2 bulk supply points, 6 Primaries; provisional).
  • Read the curtailment cost as a ranking, not as money saved. BG2 costs GBP 7.35 million more than the GAM stack on the six Primaries at the 0.5 limit, and the windows around the seven logged load transfers hold too few half-hours to separate the two (exp 277; 6 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • Pair a 00 UTC farm forecast with a 09 UTC node forecast only for valid times before 12 UTC the next day. Later valid times need a run made after the node forecast (exp 255; 2 bulk supply points; provisional).
  • The scored lead band for curtailment is 12 to 36 hours, because scoring needs a stored forecast in that window (curtailment theme; exp 84; curtailment; provisional).
  • NGED's horizon is 1 to 10 days, so a result scored only at short leads carries that caveat. The assembled solar-farm forecast beats climatology at every lead up to 10 days, by 39% at day 1 and 10% at days 8 to 10 (exp 310; 6 farms; provisional).

docs.title: Retraining defaults in R&D
docs.text:
• Do not use quarterly refits, three refits a year, or warm-start boosting as a proxy for monthly retraining (exp 34, 85; XGBoost refit cadence, Primary demand; established).
  • Screen a demand-feature contrast with monthly refits on a rolling 12-month window, and judge cadence, absolute scores, and tail scores with weekly refits. The rolling refit glossary entry gives the settings (exp 34, 48, 81; Primary demand; established).
  • Keep the convex demand model's monthly refits (0.4 s per substation), and give the small neural network that corrects the median no retraining schedule. Quarterly refits of the convex model scored 0.010 points worse than monthly refits (not shown to be acceptable), weekly refits gained nothing, and retraining the neural network quarterly or monthly scored no better than training it once before the scored year (exp 278; 6 Primaries, one year; provisional).
  • Say in each write-up which schedule was used and whether the contrast could depend on it (exp 34, 85; refit schedules; established).

docs.title: How to score and gate an experiment
docs.text:
• Run a known-answer gate before reading any contrast. Inject a known step or shift into real residuals, or use a fake-ensemble gate, so that a null cannot be a wiring fault. Experiments 128, 142, and 172 narrowly missed or failed their gates, so their contrasts are inconclusive, not refuted (exp 111, 128, 142, 172, 175; DP series; established).
  • State the row definition and the lead range before any score. A "sunny" gap was 0.05 MW over six substations, but 63% of it came from D5, and it shrank to 0.015 MW under a different definition of sunny (exp 178; 6 substations; provisional).
  • Use month-block intervals, and report D5 separately where one substation dominates (exp 111, 178, 180; DP Primaries; provisional).
  • Judge calibration where the loss sits: cold nights and daylight bands, not the all-row average. Cold-night q95 coverage was 0.846 under experiment 160's smooth spread table and 0.896 with widening of the upper quantiles only, while ensemble spread added nothing over all rows (exp 160, 164, 169; DP Primaries; provisional).
  • Score a new model component on top of the family's research default, not on a partial stack. The drift term improved the score by 0.40 on the bare GAM-K and worsened arm D by 0.03 once the filter, the winter night offset, and recipe R were in (exp 167, 170; DP Primaries; provisional). The research default rule names the default and says when a win is adopted.
  • Gains do not always remove the same error: the correction network and the two-number solar summary added on arm A. Together they scored 0.136 below arm A, 99% of the sum of their single gains of 0.099 and 0.038 (exp 220; 5 Primaries, one year; provisional).

  • Quote a neural network's score per seed, or say the seeds were averaged. Averaging the quantiles of the three seeds of the correction network scored 0.123 below arm D at six substations, against 0.104 for the mean of the single-seed scores (exp 201, 220; 6 substations, one year; provisional).

  • Score a joint scenario set per family as well as jointly. The joint variogram score over 16 Primaries, 3 wind farms, and 6 solar farms moved by 2% or less between constructions, while the same score across the farms moved by 28% to 43%. The cross-family block holds the same gain whether or not the families are coupled, so it cannot test cross-family dependence (exp 436; 44 Tuesday runs, 10 months; provisional).

Last checked against experiment 321.

docs.title: Substation information fields
docs.text: Four sources describe a substation: the metadata table, NGED's hierarchy files, the effective-capacity table, and the estimates of solar capacity that experiments have built. This page lists what each source holds, where it sits, and which fields have misled an experiment. The power readings themselves are on the NGED power telemetry page, and the paths are on the disk page.

docs.title: The metadata table
docs.text:
• data/NGED/metadata.parquet holds one row per time series, under the TimeSeriesMetadata contract. The field descriptions in packages/contracts/src/contracts/power_schemas.py own the meaning of each column (code).
  • The trial area has 33 rows: 16 Primaries, 2 BSPs, 2 GSPs, and 13 customer connections. Of the 13 connections, 7 are typed PV, 3 Wind, and 1 each BESS, Biofuel, and Other (Generation) (disk).
  • Only the 16 Primaries carry an area polygon (area_wkt), and every customer row has a null polygon (disk).
  • information is a free-text note, filled for 5 of the 33 rows. The notes are a snapshot from July 2026, because the earlier raw files carry no value, so a note cannot say when a fault began (exp 182; 33 rows; provisional).

docs.title: The hierarchy files
docs.text:
• Four NGED files and a README sit in data/NGED/substation_hierarchy_2026-10-15/. They are Substations.csv, Primary Substation Interconnections.csv, Monitor Direction.csv, and Peak Loads.xlsx. They are private (disk).
  • Substations.csv gives each substation's BSP and GSP. The trial area has two GSPs, each with one BSP (disk).
  • Primary Substation Interconnections.csv lists pairs of Primaries that can be connected. Every trial-area Primary has at least one pair, so the topology looks complete (data sources; docs).
  • Monitor Direction.csv gives each series' meter type and flow direction. One solar farm's substation number differs from its metadata row, and the other sources agree with the metadata (docs).
  • Peak Loads.xlsx disagrees with the telemetry at several Primaries, so experiments take the 99th percentile of observed power as the capacity of a series instead (docs).
  • The Primaries beneath a BSP do not sum to the BSP's reading. Primaries that report only apparent power, and the generators and unmetered load beneath the BSP, stop the sum from closing. Adding every child Primary to a bottom-up sum did not improve the BSP forecast (exp 161, 204; 2 BSPs, one scored year; provisional).

docs.title: The effective-capacity table
docs.text:
• data/effective_capacity/ holds one value per series: the 99th percentile of the absolute power over the series' whole observed history, in MW. It is not a nameplate, firm, or connection rating (code).
  • Scores in points of capacity divide by this value. See the glossary (code).
  • The value is built from the series' own output, so a farm's power divided by it near 1.0 is not an independent level (exp 179, 183; 6 farms; provisional).

docs.title: Estimates of solar capacity behind a Primary
docs.text:
• No source tells us the solar capacity behind a Primary, so experiments estimate it from the Primary's power. The estimates are AC capacity in MW, taken as the 99th percentile of the solar output over daylight half-hours (exp 129; 5 Primaries; provisional).
  • Experiment 45 built weekly capacity "vintages", one block per origin Monday, and the frozen variant uses data before the origin only. A cut earlier than a Primary's first vintage receives a later vintage's level, which is hindsight. The rule is in the studies.dp_pinned_capacity docstring (code).
  • The latest week of a real-time vintage has 3.6 times the path error of the same week in the final fit. The pinned-capacity code therefore holds the median of the last 13 weeks (exp 45; 8 Primaries with injected paths; provisional).
  • Experiment 129 gives one capacity per season-year at D5, D10, D11, D14, and D16, with a range. For 2025/26 the estimate is 3.3 to 4.5 MW per Primary at the five tested, and the range is a spread over test scenarios, not a calibrated interval (exp 129; 5 Primaries; provisional).
  • Reading the capacity from the Primary's own power did not improve the forecast. An as-of capacity scored 0.110 points of capacity worse than the pinned vintage on the sunniest third of daylight half-hours (exp 139; 5 Primaries, one scored year; provisional).
  • A curve of irradiance with no capacity estimate matched the pinned capacity at five of six Primaries and beat it at D5. B minus A on sunny daylight half-hours was +0.025 [-0.252, +0.346] over the five and -0.969 [-1.708, -0.176] at D5, so the D5 pin is a suspect (exp 350; 6 Primaries, one scored year; provisional).
  • A monthly capacity path recovered less of an injected farm than a yearly one, 0.67 to 0.78 against 0.75 to 0.87 (exp 157; 6 Primaries, 5 injected farms; provisional).
  • Refreshing the capacity table once per season-year lowered the error by 0.018 points of capacity, and a weekly refresh made no distinguishable difference (exp 78; the fold A row set; small gain; provisional).
  • The one dated list of installations we hold, the Feed-in Tariff register, ends on 2021-03-24. No capacity step after that date can be matched to an installation (exp 215; 6 Primaries; provisional).
  • The published estimates are on the embedded solar capacity study (docs).

Last checked against experiment 218.

docs.title: Weather inputs by product
docs.text: Each weather product reaches the forecast at a different time, and an experiment must name which product feeds each column at forecast time and which feeds it at training time. The two are usually different products. This page is a digest: it holds the table of what exists when, and the traps that cost experiments a re-run. The long accounts are the weather products survey, the data-sources page, the NWP variable conventions, and the ECMWF ENS known issues.

docs.title: Availability at forecast time
docs.text:
Product What it is Delay before use Exists at forecast time? Training rule ECMWF ENS (51 members) Ensemble forecast, stored by delta_store.nwp A run is usable 9 hours after its init_time (NWP_PUBLICATION_DELAY_HOURS) Yes: the production input Train on ENS history, which starts 2024-04-01 on disk ERA5 ECMWF reanalysis, an estimate of past weather About 5 days through the Climate Data Store No: a ceiling at lag times Version-1 plan: the training product for every variable except irradiance CAMS solar radiation Satellite-derived irradiance, point time-series API 1 day: a request that names today is rejected No: nothing about the day being forecast The planned training product for irradiance UKV (Met Office) 2 km deterministic UK weather model Three variants exist; see below Only the live feed Train on the product that will serve; never train on the Centre for Environmental Data Analysis (CEDA) archive and serve the live feed GEFS, ICON-EU, IFS, AIFS-ENS, WeatherNext 3 Further forecast products Differs by product Studies only Not in production; see the weather theme
  • A weather product that is "as accurate as ERA5" is a ceiling for demand, not a forecast. ERA5 weather in place of ENS weather lowered the Primary demand quantile score by 0.10 points (exp 22; Primary demand, one validation year; provisional).
  • Name the weather source used at lag times in every write-up, and say whether it exists at forecast time (data-processing page; exp 33, 37; ERA5 as the lag-time source; established).

docs.title: Training product: the rule
docs.text:
