Done Nothing Finished (not supported): A neural network that learns the state of every link between two Primaries, and the delay before the recipient follows, pairs no more transfer megawatts than the donor-probe hybrids or the search of experiment 670 (paired share of long, deep transfer megawatts: 0.32 for the new network, 0.29 for the search, 0.35 and 0.36 for the hybrids). 680 Does a search that also starts from each unpaired rise, and looks for the matching fall at a neighbouring Primary, pair more injected load-transfer megawatts than the one-way search of experiment 670? Done Nothing Finished (partly supported): Searching from each unpaired rise for the matching fall at a neighbouring Primary pairs 0.38 of the injected transfer megawatts in the long and deep cell, against 0.29 for the one-way search, a gain of 0.09. 682 Does choosing edge flows by a fixed cost per change pair more injected load-transfer megawatts than the searches of experiments 670 and 680, without adding more false transfers? Done Nothing Finished (not supported): Explaining pairs of steps by one flow on an edge, chosen by a fixed cost per change, does not find the donor and recipient of an injected load transfer better than the simple searches: it pairs 0.33 of the long and deep megawatts against 0.29 for the one-way search and 0.38 for the two-way search. 685 Which load-shift candidates does the fixed event table find at the 15 Primaries from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31? Done Nothing Finished (inconclusive): From 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31 the event table finds 13 candidate events (14 rows) at the 15 Primaries and no transfer between time_series_id 13 and 16 in July or August, nothing at id 11 in September, and one open fall at id 18 from 2026-10-04. 686 Do the donor and the recipient of a load transfer start together, and what kind of false event does solar growth cause in the event table? Done Nothing Finished (partly supported): The two verified transfers give no sign of a lag between the substation that lost demand and the one that gained it: the D3/D22 steps coincide within noise, and the D5/D16 steps are 2.5 hours apart at the end and too noisy at the onset to say. 692 Can a Claude reviewer looking at a figure of each candidate load transfer cut the event table's false transfers? Done Nothing Finished (not supported): the reviewer failed the precision gate (0.45 against 0.80), but 21 of its 29 false calls were five real-record transfers that the injected truth does not list; without them precision is 0.75.

Experiment 00116 (differentiable physics, NRA) also bears on this theme. It fits flows on the interconnection edges between Primary substations and scores them on injected transfers; see the Network research plan.

docs.title: Planned experiments
docs.text: Experiment Hypothesis Relevance 00654 two-output-network-end-to-end-with-end-detector One network, trained end to end (K1's body plus a prevailing head that reads the lag-encoder outputs, with no hand-built gate), gives a prevailing forecast at least as good as the frozen K1 plus the survival-hazard head R-haz of experiment 652, with no loss to the normal-running- arrangement (NRA) output; and a learned end detector that reads the freshest half-hours lets the prevailing forecast drop a shift faster after it ends. also relevant

docs.title: SW2: switching-event detection
docs.text:
The SW2 line improves the switching-event detector first, scored by event-level F1 against a labelled set of visible events, and leaves the use of the detector until the detector works. The detector serves two purposes later. The first is a lower forecast error, if switching periods act as unexplained noise for the XGBoost model and corrupt its lagged power inputs. The second, and the more important to NGED, is a forecast under the normal running arrangement (NRA), into which NGED can add its own switching. The switching events roadmap page proposes building that forecast by excluding switching periods from the training target. An event table for NGED is a third purpose, at lower priority. The production detector has to run on power alone, because the switching logs exist only for the trial area, so the logs are used here for evaluation only.

The line reopens a question that experiment 00038 closed, because experiment 00038 tested a different use of the detector. Experiment 00038 masked detected switching from the history of the error correction that runs after the XGBoost model, and the mask made the forecast worse. No experiment has yet masked switching from an XGBoost training target or from a lagged input. Experiment 00037 confirmed 37 of 612 logged closures of 2 hours to 60 days as visible in its own residual, and scored its detectors on the 18 of them in the validation months. That reference set is small, about 6 of the 37 are expected by chance, and the label was built from the residual the detectors use, so a detector that shares the residual's blind spots is flattered by the label. The line therefore starts by building a reference set independent of the detectors.

The full labeller design is in the private file data/ml-experiments/briefs/sw2_labeller_design.md.

docs.title: SW2-4 to SW2-9: detector iterations
docs.text:
Each iteration tests one change to the detector against the experiment 43 scoreboard, tuned on injections and odd months, scored on even months, with recall weighted by the MW moved as the headline from SW2-7 onwards. The order below is a proposal, by expected gain per hour of work, for the plan of each iteration to confirm:

  • SW2-5 (done, experiment 68): three rounds of refitting the lagless XGBoost model without the detected intervals changed the share of the moved MW found by +0.011 and the forecast error by -0.175%, and a random mask did as well.
  • SW2-6 (done, experiment 61): pairing the onset and return steps into one alarm score finds less than D0M at the same alarm rate, but taking the end of D0M's interval from the strongest opposite step in the next 14 days finds 0.19 more of the moved MW.
  • SW2-7 (done, experiment 60): a step statistic that weights each half-hour by the expected power found the same transfers as the constant step on five injection shapes, so the step's shape does not limit the 24-hour detector. About a third of the transfers with a donor step of 6 noise units or more have the right onset and the wrong end, which SW2-6 (paired-step intervals) addresses.
  • SW2-8 (done, experiment 55): a single-series detector first, with neighbour balance as a sense check, not a gate. Every single-series alarm stands. A metered neighbour's opposite step raises the alarm's confidence and names the receiver, a same-sign step on the neighbours vetoes the alarm as a common-mode weather or calendar miss, and an alarm with no metered neighbour keeps its single-series confidence. Experiment 00043 found the neighbour-balance detector D1, which uses the neighbour test as a gate, finding almost none of the injected transfers without a metered receiver. The sum of the neighbourhood's residuals and a subset-sum over neighbours for a split feed the confidence score.
  • SW2-9 (done, experiment 62): whitening, experiment 00037's proposed F4, an autoregressive model of order 1 per series and hour of day fitted to the residual. The filtered detector found less of the moved MW (-0.097 at 24 hours), because the filter shrinks a day-long step faster than the noise of the 24-hour step.

docs.title: Load-shift event detection: state at the January pause
docs.text:
The event table E1 finds about two thirds of the megawatts of long, deep injected load transfers, but the best detector, E1-J-sym, names both Primaries of a transfer for under 0.40 of those megawatts, and 77% of the transfers it decodes are false. The maintainer paused this work after 2026-11-10 and plans to restart it in January. This page records where the work stands, which findings the merged pages do not carry yet, and the options for the restart. Each option is a proposal, not a commitment. The event-table summary explains the line of work in plain words, and the research plan holds the queue. Specs for the restart are copied into january-restart-specs/ (see where the specs went), so a reader does not need the private briefs folder.

Terms. A load transfer is a switching operation that moves part of one Primary substation's demand (the donor) onto neighbouring Primaries (the recipients) for hours or days. E1 is the event table of experiment 653. E1-J adds the recipient search of experiment 670. E1-J-sym adds the search from each unpaired rise of experiment 680. Found means an injected event has a decoded event at the right Primary, with the right sign and start. Paired means the decoded donor and recipient are the right two Primaries. Both shares are weighted by megawatts. A long and deep transfer lasts over 7 days and steps 8 noise units or more. A medium and deep transfer lasts 1 to 7 days and steps 8 noise units or more. Unless a paragraph says otherwise, results come from 15 Primaries and from injected transfers, because the real record holds almost no verified long transfers. A noise unit is a Primary's usual difference between successive 6-hour means. A cell is one combination of transfer length and depth. NGED is the distribution network operator, PV is photovoltaic solar generation, and D3, D5, D8, D10, D12, D16, and D22 are anonymised Primary identifiers. A decoded transfer is false when it matches no injected end, and an end is one Primary's side of an injected transfer. A rewired graph keeps each Primary's number of neighbours but connects it to random Primaries. NGED's event labels are an incomplete dump, so a Primary's clean rows may hold unlabelled events and every count of real events is a lower bound.

docs.title: State at the pause
docs.text:
Of the detectors tested, E1-J-sym pairs the most megawatts, but it pairs under 0.40 even for long, deep transfers. In the long and deep cell, E1 finds 0.67 of the injected megawatts (experiment 665). E1-J pairs 0.29 of them, and E1-J-sym pairs 0.38 (experiment 680). In the medium and deep cell, E1-J pairs 0.25 and E1-J-sym pairs 0.32. A rewired graph removes the gain of both searches, so the gain comes from the real neighbours. The shared simulator that creates the injected transfers (experiment 660) cannot be told apart from 49 real windows (area under the curve 0.55), which rules out gross differences and nothing finer.

Five findings limit the detector.

  • Pairing stays below 0.40. The graph neural network of experiment 672 pairs 0.08. The donor-probe hybrids of experiment 678 pair 0.36 at best. The edge-state neural network of experiment 676 pairs 0.32, and a copy of that neural network with no links between Primaries also pairs 0.32.
  • The donor is the bottleneck. In experiment 675, 0.87 of the recipient megawatts that E1-J located but left unpaired belonged to transfers whose donor E1-J had not found. Masked pretraining made the donor probe worse.
  • Short events are not paired. Transfers of a day or less pair 0.08 (deep) and 0.03 (shallow) of their megawatts (experiment 676, post hoc arms of its part A).
  • False transfers are common. Of E1-J's decoded transfers, 69% match no injected end (experiment 670). E1-J-sym decodes 442 more transfers than E1-J, for 63 more correct ends. The detector spec gives the false-transfer share as 0.69 for E1-J and 0.77 for E1-J-sym.
  • A fixed cost per change does not separate true pairs from coincident ones. The edge-flow reconstruction method of experiment 682 accepts 2,990 transfers for 329 correct ends, and a graph that links any two Primaries pairs 0.32 against 0.33 for the real graph.

Two closures are final. Two further stop rules were met by small margins, and the maintainer chose to continue. Experiments 676 and 682 are final closures: the learnt-graph line of work and the edge-flow line of work are closed at 15 Primaries. The first small margin is experiment 670's pairing of 0.29 in the long and deep cell against a stop line of 0.30 (its leave-one-out range was 0.26 to 0.31). The second is experiment 680's gain of +0.094 against the +0.10 needed to adopt the symmetric search. The 0.29 against 0.30 comparison belongs to experiment 670, not to experiment 672.

On the real record the evidence is thin. The one verified transfer between D5 and D16 (December 2025) is paired in the right direction, but the decoded starts are late. None of the 77 logged shifts longer than 1 day falls in the long and deep type (experiment 665).

docs.title: Timing of the two ends of a transfer
docs.text:
The fitted gaps between the two ends of a verified transfer are small, and at D5 and D16 the interval is too wide to exclude the 14.5 to 15 hour gap between labelled times that experiment 660 reported. Experiment 686 fitted both Primaries in one window at each verified transfer. At D3 and D22 (October 2024) the fitted gaps are -0.5 hours at the onset and -2.0 hours at the end. At D5 and D16 (December 2025) the end gap is 2.5 hours and the onset gap is 2.0 hours with a 90% interval of -13.0 to 16.5 hours, so the interval cannot exclude a lag of 15 hours. The fit misplaces a truly simultaneous step by 2 hours or more in 3% to 25% of windows, worst at D5 and D16. Experiment 660's lag of 14.5 and 15 hours is the gap between the two Primaries' labelled times, not a fitted lag. A scorer that requires both ends to coincide needs a tolerance of at least 2 hours (4 half-hours), tested on injected worlds.

Solar growth causes 333 false events in the injected worlds, and a better solar-capacity curve would remove only part of them. Of the 333, 5% are steps inside a sunny run (95% interval 3% to 8%), 79% fail the step test, and 52% last 3 days or less.

docs.title: Forecast heads that follow a new load shift sooner
docs.text:
Extra lagged power inputs make the prevailing output follow a new shift about 20 hours sooner, and the detector's statistics are not shown to do better. The prevailing output of the two-output demand neural network forecasts demand including any shift in force, and the small head is the neural network that corrects it. NRA is the normal running arrangement. Experiment 681 gave the prevailing head 14 extra lagged inputs. The start-of-shift reaction time fell by 20.4 hours (95% interval 16.3 to 24.8), and the NRA output was unchanged. The page marks the extra inputs as a candidate that no model adopts yet. Experiment 687 found that detector features react 1.59 days sooner than experiment 652's head (interval -2.26 to -1.00), the extra lags react 1.25 days sooner, and the features-minus-lags difference is -0.33 days (-0.72 to +0.07). The features are not shown to beat the lags. The placebo arm is invalid, because every Primary is shifted at once in the banks, so prediction P5 (the placebo gains less than a third of the features arm's gain) is untested.

Experiment 691 gave the head both the features and the extra lags (arm FL1). FL1 reacts 1.75 days sooner than experiment 652's head, but only 0.16 days sooner than the features alone (interval -0.45 to +0.14), below the pre-registered 0.5-day gain, so the lags add under 0.5 days to the features. The in-force score gain is 0.20 points of capacity, below the 0.30 bar, and false alarms on event-free injected rows rise by 5.1 points.

docs.title: Findings the merged pages do not carry yet
docs.text:
Four items below appear on no merged page. The first, a re-analysis of experiment 651's outputs, has not been audited. They come from Discuss sessions (the maintainer's planning conversations) and from the maintainer.

  • The FLOW-E audit (unaudited). The D10 episode of 8 to 12 December 2025 carries about 62% of FLOW-E's extra CRPS at the six MW Primaries (the continuous ranked probability score; experiment 651's graph arm). FLOW-E minus G0 is +0.022 points of capacity at the six MW Primaries and +0.003 without D10's rows for 1 to 16 December 2025. G0's excess over the A1 arm is +0.141 on all rows and +0.078 without that episode. FLOW-E's follow gain needs a metered mirror: on the bank with no mirror, FLOW-E follows 0.059, exactly G0's figure. NGED's labels mark the D10 rows event-free, so the episode may be an unlabelled event, which nobody has verified. Source: flow-e-next-experiments.md.
  • No register gives a solar capacity curve. Step 1 of part B1 of the detector spec cannot be built as written, because the three registers it names (the Feed-in Tariff, the Embedded Capacity Register, and the Renewable Energy Planning Database) do not record recent domestic PV, and NGED removed metered generation from the Primary data. We found no other register-based capacity trajectory.
  • NGED's "Reverse Power Flow?" column is a hint. The column is in Monitor Direction.csv (a private file). The column says "Yes" for D8, "Maybe" for D12 and D22, and "No" for five other MVA Primaries. The column conflicts with the telemetry at D8, D12, and D22 (mva-reverse-flow-hard-mask.md).
  • The maintainer's decisions. The maintainer favours testing a hard PV mask for MVA reverse flow beside a soft prior. D8's gas generator is the large-generator case. The reviewer of detector check 4 (part C of the detector spec) is one Sonnet agent. A learnt scorer combines the logistic regression with E1-J-sym.
  • A Sonnet reviewer failed the pre-registered gate on injected truth, which holds real-record events, so the result is inconclusive. Experiment 692 gave the reviewer 102 figures, and its precision was 0.45 against the gate of 0.80 (at recall 0.75). Post hoc, found after the answers were read, 21 of its 29 false calls were on five candidates that recur in the real record under many injected worlds, and without them precision is 0.75 (interval 0.58 to 0.87), still under 0.80. The new data-processing rule (medium confidence) says to drop such candidates before scoring on injected truth.
  • Experiment 685's event table stays private. Its rows are in the private data folder only (experiment 685 found 13 candidate events from 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31 and none that explains the one-year-backtest flags at four Primaries).

docs.title: Not started, parked
docs.text: Six of the seven options below have not started, and the learnt scorer is the one with the most preparation. Option 2, the reviewer's gate (part C of the detector spec), has run in a reduced form as experiment 692 (102 blinded figures, not 400). FLOW-C, FLOW-P, and FLOW-H are the three FLOW-E proposals of the Opus sub-agent, and only FLOW-C is in the ranked table, as option 6. The causal-features test on the production forecast heads goes beyond experiment 687.

docs.title: January restart, ranked
docs.text:
Seven options are ranked below, and the maintainer has not yet chosen among them. The ranking is the Discuss session's view.

Rank Option Question Cost Depends on 1 Learnt candidate scorer over E1-J-sym's candidates Does a logistic regression, then small trees, on timing, shape, and context features cut the false-transfer share to 0.45 or less without losing paired share? About 5 to 9 CPU-hours (spec estimate) Experiments 660, 675, and 680; part A of the detector spec 2 The one-Sonnet reviewer against the candidates Does a reviewer reach 0.80 precision at 0.60 recall on a blinded calibration set? Experiment 692 (102 figures): the pre-registered gate failed (precision 0.45 at recall 0.75); post hoc (found after the answers were read), without five real-record candidates that the injected truth omits, precision is 0.75, still under the 0.80 gate. About 5 million tokens (spec estimate, made for two Sonnet reviewers plus Opus) A scorer's candidates and the calibration set; part C 3 The neural lag-free year-fold residual with explicit PV Does a residual built from a neural cross-fit lower the noise unit or the event-free decoded rate against arm C? About 1.5 GPU-hours (ceiling 2 GPU-hours) Part B; the maintainer's backtests keep GPU priority 4 Causal detector features for the lag encoder and the prevailing head Do the features help the production heads beyond the extra lags of experiment 681? (Experiment 691: features and lags together add under 0.5 days over the features alone.) About 2 GPU-hours for the fine-tune, after a CPU test Experiment 687; part D 5 The MVA sign label with the hard-mask arm and the D8 gas-generator state Does a per-Primary masked day labeller recover reverse flow at the eight apparent-power Primaries? CPU only, zero fits The MVA spec; no known answer at D12's export level 6 FLOW-C Does FLOW-E keep a lower follow than G0 across five months, against a rewired placebo? About 6 GPU-hours Only if the forecast side still wants FLOW-E 7 Graph-learnt models Do learnt graph models pair better with more data? Not estimated Fleet adjacency from NGED, or more verified events

Option 1 comes first because experiment 682 showed that the detector's problem is precision. A cost per change cannot tell a true pair from a coincident one, and timing and shape features might. The donor limits how many pairs are found, and the false-transfer share is a separate precision problem that option 1 targets. Option 2 follows because the reviewer's precision has to be measured before it cuts false positives, and experiment 692's measurement needs a calibration set free of real-record events. Option 5 runs on CPU alone. Options 6 and 7 are the least likely to improve the result at 15 Primaries.

docs.title: Where the specs went
docs.text:
The restart specs are copied under january-restart-specs/.

  • event-detector-spec.md: parts A to D of the spec, with the maintainer's amendment to part D.
  • flow-e-next-experiments.md: the FLOW-C, FLOW-P, and FLOW-H proposals.
  • mva-reverse-flow-hard-mask.md: the MVA sign-label research and its recommended first experiment.

These briefs are left out, and stay private. The edge-state and edge-flow specs (edge_state_inference_brief.md, edge_state_e2b_graph_spec.md, edge_state_x4_spec.md, edge_flow_reconstruction_spec.md, and their addenda) describe work that experiments 676, 680, and 682 have run (676 and 682 closed their lines of work). The worker briefs, the simulator briefs, and the PV-session replies are conversation, and their findings are in the merged pages.

docs.title: Spec: next steps for the hindsight load-shift detector
docs.text:
This is a copy of the specification that the Discuss session of 2026-11-10 wrote for the January restart, trimmed of conversation. The page state at the January pause says which parts ran since. A0 ran as experiment 686, whose result replaces the conflict that the take-home below describes: the two ends of the verified transfers step together within the noise. Part D's cheap test ran as experiment 687. Parts A1 to A4, B, and C have not run. Two statements below are out of date. Step 1 of part B1 (a register-based solar capacity trajectory) cannot be built, because the registers do not record recent domestic PV. Part C now uses one Sonnet reviewer, not two. The maintainer's amendment to part D was not re-reviewed by the spec's author. Probabilities and costs are the spec author's estimates, not commitments.

Terms.

  • Cells and the found and paired definitions follow experiment 665.
  • "False-transfer share" is the share of decoded transfers that match no injected end.

Baselines.

Method Long and deep paired Medium and deep paired Long and deep donor found Decoded transfers in the 40 scored worlds E1-J-sym (experiment 680) 0.38 0.32 0.48 1,230, with 283 correct ends E1-J 0.29 0.25 0.44 788 F-hyb 0.36 about 0.33 0.52 not given R-hyb 0.35 not given not given not given Logistic donor probe of experiment 675 (alone) not given not given 0.63 not given

The flow model of experiment 682 accepted 2,990 transfers for 329 correct ends. 88% to 90% of its transfers had no correct end at every change cost tried.

docs.title: Take-home
docs.text:
• The detector's main problem is precision, not recall. Experiment 682 showed that a cost per change cannot tell a true pair from a coincident one.
  • Two pieces of information could: the timing of the two ends, and the shape of what moved. Part A turns them into features of a small supervised scorer over candidate pairs.
  • The timing evidence conflicts with the maintainer's statement. The maintainer says real switches are simultaneous. Experiment 660 measured the recipient's step 14.5 and 15 hours after the donor's at both verified transfers. A0 settles this by measurement before the window is shrunk. If switches are simultaneous, matching both ends in time should cut coincident pairs by about 5 to 10 times.
  • The convex residual was a convenience. Arm C was the stored whole-history residual on CPU, not a choice on merit. Part B builds the neural cross-fit, buildable from 2019, and compares the two fairly.
  • A Claude reviewer can cut false positives only once its own precision is measured on blinded injected and verified cases (part C).
  • Part D's features can be tested cheaply on the stored banks of experiments 650 and 652 before any refit.

Candid probabilities.

Part Outcome Probability A False-transfer share cut by at least a third 45% A Paired share E1-J-sym + 0.10 30% B The residual improves recall or false events by the bars 40% C Reviewer precision of 0.80 or more on the blinded set 50% D A gain on the prevailing strata 30%

docs.title: A. A learnt scorer over candidate pairs
docs.text:
A0. Measure end timing first (CPU, about 2 hours).

  • Data. The verified transfers D5 and D16 (2025-12) and D3 and D22 (2024-10).
  • Two models, fitted at half-hour resolution to the residual within ±4 days of each end:
    • a shared onset (and a shared end) for both Primaries;
    • separate onsets.
  • Each model allows two step shapes: constant MW, and a share of the donor's profile. A profile-shaped transfer at 01:00 moves little MW at night, so its onset can look late.
  • Report the likelihood ratio, each onset's profile-likelihood interval, and the residual of each fit.
  • Rules.
    • If the shared onset sits within the noise (likelihood ratio under 4) at both transfers, adopt simultaneity with a tolerance of the joint onset interval, about ±2 to 4 half-hours.
    • Otherwise keep a window of 0 to 36 half-hours. Record that the data do not support simultaneity, and ask the maintainer whether the switching could have run in stages.
  • Inject both kinds. The generator then injects simultaneous transfers by default and keeps lagged ones as a 20% sensitivity arm.

A1. Candidate generation. Generation is tuned for recall; the scorer supplies the precision.

  • Every opposite-sign pair of steps of 2 noise units or more, at either end, on the 25 edges.
  • Ends refined to the half-hour, onset gap within 48 half-hours.
  • Every candidate already proposed by E1-J-sym.
  • An all-pairs copy, over any two Primaries, as a placebo.

A2. Features per candidate pair. These replace the fixed thresholds of 4 and 2 noise units, the 36-half-hour window, the share range of 0.3 to 2.0, the change costs, the 1.5-noise-unit mask, and the 6-hour blocks.

  • Size: the step size at each end in noise units, at 6-hour, 1-day, and 3-day scales; log ρ (the recipient-to-donor MW ratio).
  • Timing:
    • the onset gap and the end gap, each divided by its joint interval;
    • the likelihood ratio of a shared onset, and of a shared end (from A0);
    • whether both ends are seen;
    • the duration;
    • the return to the earlier level at each end, as a fraction.
  • Shape match: the correlation between the daily profile the donor lost and the daily profile the recipient gained, over the event's days. "Behaviour moves", so a coincident pair has no reason to share a profile.
  • Context:
    • the all-Primaries median step at the onset;
    • the number of other Primaries stepping within ±3 hours, in each sign;
    • ERA5 temperature change over ±6 hours;
    • CAMS clear-sky index and the PV-high flag;
    • hour of day and day of week of the onset.
  • Competition: the number of other candidate partners for each end, the best competing pair's score, and this pair's rank among them.
  • Per-Primary statistics: noise unit, routine-step rate (60 days), MW or MVA flag at each end, E1's confidence for each end, and the logistic donor probe's score (experiment 675).
  • Excluded: Primary identifiers, so the scorer can carry over to the fleet.

A3. Labels and training.

  • Labels. A candidate is positive when both ends match one injected transfer, with its donor and recipient. Every other candidate is negative: coincident pairs, placebo pairs, routine steps, ramps, and PV runs.
  • Worlds. Experiment 660's generator, injected into the power, with:
    • default worlds, plus 200 each of short_heavy(), long_heavy(), and constant_mw_square();
    • events from 2022-01 to 2023-06 for training and 2023-07 to 2023-12 for validation;
    • the 40 scored worlds of experiment 680 (seeds 900 to 939), with events from 2024.
  • Models.
    • Logistic regression first, because experiment 675 found it matched every neural encoder.
    • Then gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost, depth 4, 300 rounds), with monotone constraints on the timing likelihood ratios and the step sizes.
  • Decoding. A greedy assignment by score: each end is used at most once.
  • Threshold. Chosen on validation worlds: the highest paired share with a false-transfer share of 0.45 or less. The full precision-recall curve is also reported.

A4. Checks.

  • Realness. Experiment 660's classifier, on the pair features, comparing injected true pairs with real high-score pairs. The area under the curve must be under 0.65. If it is higher, list the features that give the generator away and fix the generator.
  • Cross-injector. Train on constant_mw_square() and score on shaped transfers, and the reverse. The drop must be 0.05 or less.
  • Placebos.
    • The rewired graph: the draw out of 300 that keeps the fewest real links. It must pair 0.05 or less on injected worlds, and call a third or fewer of the real record's transfers.
    • The all-pairs candidates: the real-edge scorer must have a false-transfer share 0.10 or more below the all-pairs scorer's.
  • Feature ablations: without the timing features, without the shape match, and without the context features.

Predictions that could fail.

Measure Long and deep Medium and deep Other cells False-transfer share 0.45 or less (E1-J-sym about 0.69 to 0.77) 0.45 or less not stated Paired share 0.38 or more, so no loss 0.32 or more, so no loss no worse than E1-J-sym − 0.03 Paired share at E1-J-sym's false-transfer share 0.48 or more (+0.10) 0.42 or more (+0.10) not stated
  • If A0 supports simultaneity, removing the timing features raises the false-transfer share by 0.10 or more.
  • On the real record, D5 and D16 are paired with D5 as the donor.

Stop rule. If the false-transfer share falls by less than 0.10 at no loss of paired share, the residual cannot separate true from coincident pairs. Stop part A, and keep E1-J-sym in that case.

Cost. CPU only: about 4 to 8 hours for the worlds and the candidates, under 1 hour for the scorers.

Dependencies. Experiment 660's generator, experiment 680's code and scored worlds, and experiment 675's probe.

docs.title: B. The residual
docs.text:
Why arm C was used.

  • Experiment 653 read the stored whole-history residual of experiments 258 and 327, which is the lag-free convex model of experiment 130, refitted monthly on a 24-month window. That residual was the only one on disk and runs on CPU.
  • Its 24-month window contains earlier events, so the residual absorbs some of them.
  • The X4 worker never built the neural cross-fit, and the panel starts in 2022.

B1. The neural lag-free cross-fit.

  • Model. Use the K3 recipe of the roster: the lag-free class 3 network, with its weather encoder, date-time encoder, Primary embedding, and a mixer with a 3-component mixture.
    • Weather: ERA5 means and CAMS shortwave at the valid time, not ECMWF ENS, because the labeller works in hindsight.
    • Date-time features include holidays.
  • Folds. For each calendar year Y from 2019 to 2026 (2026 ending on 2026-06-30), train on all other years and predict year Y. That gives 8 folds, at 15 Primaries.
    • The early-calibration cuts of experiment 591 apply.
    • D15 and D18 start on 2025-03-01.
    • The final-test window from 2026-07-01 is never read.
  • Buildable from 2019. Experiment 591's step 1 trained on ERA5 and CAMS from 2019-09 on this power. Check that the cleaned power is on disk at the 15 Primaries before starting.
  • Seasonal bias is learned by the date-time and weather encoders from the other years. A change specific to year Y, such as a new connection, stays in that year's residual, which is the change the detector should see.
  • Unmetered PV, at the six MW Primaries.
    • Add an explicit term to the expected power: capacity × the PV curve from CAMS.
    • The capacity is experiment 649's calibrated table: p50 as the centre, p10 to p90 as the width. The table already applies the 0.68 read-back calibration, so use the calibrated values, never the raw ones.
    • Its resolution is a season-year, so a step inside a season is not believed from the table alone.
    • Traps (a) to (e) of the PV session reply apply:
      • (a) never subtract the PV term as a single shift without also removing the all-Primaries median step;
      • (b) a sunny spring or any run of very sunny days can be read as a capacity step;
      • (c) a load that follows cloud looks like PV;
      • (d) never score the term on forecast weather and call that skill;
      • (e) use calibrated values, because of the 0.68 read-back.
  • Unmetered PV, at the MVA Primaries. No usable table exists, so use a soft PV-high prior from the CAMS clear-sky index. Reverse flow at D8 and D22 can have causes other than sun (a generator at D8; unexplained at D22).
  • A solar capacity trajectory is a composite, not a measured series (briefs/pv_session_reply_solar_drift.md).
    • No yearly capacity trajectory exists before 2024, beyond season-year capacities from experiments 129, 474, and 479 at five MW Primaries from 2021. Experiment 649's table covers the summers of 2024 and 2025 only and carries no trajectory.
    • B1 therefore builds the trajectory on CPU, in under 2 hours, in four steps:
      1. a cumulative curve per Primary from the Feed-in Tariff, Embedded Capacity Register, and REPD registers, using the service-area polygons (area_wkt in data/NGED/metadata.parquet);
      2. anchored to experiment 649's calibrated levels in summer 2024 and summer 2025;
      3. plus an unregistered-share term, because the probe sits above the register floor at 8 of 12 Primaries (experiment 673);
      4. with an interval for each year that includes the spread of the 0.68 read-back factor and the farm-to-farm spread.
    • Capacity changes only at season-year boundaries, never inside a sunny run (experiment 634).
    • The trajectory removes only the slow drift, about 0.1 to 0.7 MW a year, which is already below the detector's step size. It does not remove a sunny-spring residual or a load that follows cloud. B relies on the context features of part A (clear-sky index, PV-high flag) and on part C's rubric item R8 for those two.
  • Cheap check before any of this: where do the false events under solar growth come from? CPU only, about 1 hour.
    • Data. Experiment 653's stored injected worlds with solar growth, where the masked arm decoded 0.93 false events per injected Primary-year.
    • Classify each false event by:
      • the decoded edge width: a step of 1 hour or less, against a ramp of more than 1 day;
      • whether it lies within 14 days of a season-year boundary;
      • the mean CAMS clear-sky index over its first 3 days, as a high-clear-sky run (index 0.7 or more) against ordinary days;
      • its daily shape, as the share of its MW in 10:00 to 15:00 UTC;
      • the slow level's misfit to the injected growth at its onset.
    • Prediction that could fail. Half or more of the 0.93 are slow ramps or slow-level misfits, which the composite trajectory would remove, and under a third fall in high-clear-sky runs.
    • If the prediction fails (most are sunny-run steps), the trajectory is not worth building for false events. Keep it only for B1's level, and rely on the part A features.
  • Slow level. Keep experiment 653's masked, frozen slow level, but cut it to a yearly linear trend with no seasonal harmonics, because the encoders now hold the seasonal shape. It stays as an arm, not as the default.

B2. Noise from the model.

  • The model outputs a half-hourly mixture.
  • Each Primary's block-scale noise unit is κ_i × the model's standard deviation of a 6-hour block mean. Compute that standard deviation from the mixture variances, with an order-1 autocorrelation fitted per Primary and fold on E1-masked, event-free, out-of-fold residuals.
  • The noise unit therefore varies in time: it is higher on cold evenings and sunny middays.
  • Check: 90% coverage of the 6-hour block means on event-free rows, in 0.87 to 0.93 at 13 or more Primaries.

B3. A fair comparison with arm C.

  • Rows: the same 15 Primaries and 2022-01 to 2026-06. The 2019-to-2021 years are used only for training the neural model.
  • Decoding: the same E1-J-sym, and the A scorer if it passes, retuned per residual on that residual's own validation worlds with the same grid size.
  • Worlds: the same seeds, injected into the power, with the residual recomputed per arm.
  • Measures:
    • the noise unit per Primary (robust 6-hour block difference);
    • found and paired shares per cell;
    • the false-transfer share;
    • real-record events per Primary-year;
    • the decoded rate in the event-free stratum;
    • D5 and D16, including whether the +11-point bias before the event is gone.
  • Predictions that could fail.
    • The neural noise unit is 15% or more below arm C's at 10 or more of the 15 Primaries.
    • The long and deep found share rises by 0.05 or more.
    • The decoded rate in the event-free stratum falls by 20% or more.
    • The PV term lowers sunny-midday false events at the six MW Primaries by 30% or more.
  • Stop rule. If neither the noise-unit bar nor the event-free bar holds, keep arm C.

Cost. About 5 GPU-minutes per fold, from experiment 640's 2.5 GPU-minutes per cutoff with margin for 7 million rows. 8 folds × 2 seeds come to about 1.5 GPU-hours, ceiling 2. One GPU process at a time; the maintainer's backtests keep priority. A CPU-only fallback is feasible at about 1 to 2 hours per fold on 2 cores, about 16 CPU-hours in all. The decoding re-runs take about 6 CPU-hours.

docs.title: C. Cutting false positives, with a Claude reviewer
docs.text:
Automatic steps first, cheapest first.

  1. The A scorer, with synchrony at both ends if A0 supports it.
  2. The shape match.
  3. A common-mode and weather veto, through the context features rather than a hard rule.
  4. Competition: one partner per end, with the best competitor's score as a feature.
  5. A tiered output:
    • "confirmed": both ends seen, synchronous, and a score of 0.8 or more;
    • "probable";
    • "candidate".

The manual review.

  • One figure per candidate, panels stacked on a shared time axis:
    1. The donor: observed power, the expected-power median, and its 90% band.
    2. The donor's residual in noise units, with the decoded steps.
    3. The recipient's two panels, the same as the donor's.
    4. Small multiples of the other neighbours' residuals, at both ends.
    5. The all-Primaries median residual.
    6. ERA5 temperature and the CAMS clear-sky index, with PV-high hours shaded.
  • Time ranges.
    • An overview of daily means from 7 days before the onset to 7 days after the end, capped at 60 days.
    • Two zooms at half-hour resolution: the onset ±48 hours and the end ±48 hours.
  • What is hidden. No NGED labels, no injected-truth marks, and no generator names. Every case is rendered identically.
  • Fixed rubric. Score each item 0 to 2:
Item Question R1 Is the step instant (1 hour or less) at both ends? R2 Do the donor and recipient start together, and end together? R3 Are the signs opposite, with a ratio of 0.3 to 2? R4 Does each Primary return to its earlier level? R5 Does the recipient's gained profile look like the donor's lost profile? R6 Does the all-Primaries median or the weather explain the step instead? R7 Does another neighbour show a better match? R8 Is there a PV or sunny-run confound? R9 Are the steps quantised like a generator's?

The verdict is one of: transfer (with direction), solo shift, generator or routine, weather or common mode, PV, or unclear. The reviewer adds a confidence from 1 to 5 and writes the output as JSON.

  • Scoring the reviewer first, on a blinded calibration set of 400 figures:
    • 150 injected true transfers;
    • 150 of the scorer's highest-scoring false pairs on injected worlds;
    • 100 hard negatives: placebo pairs, routine steps, and sunny runs;
    • plus D5 and D16, and D3 and D22.
  • Gate. Precision of 0.80 or more at recall of 0.60 or more, direction correct for 90% of transfers, and D5 and D16 called a transfer.
  • Visual realness check. A separate reviewer is shown 100 mixed figures and asked "injected or real?". Its accuracy must be 60% or less.
  • Model tier.
    • Run Sonnet and Opus on the calibration set. Use Sonnet if its precision is within 0.05 of Opus's.
    • On real candidates, use two independent Sonnet reviewers, with Opus only on their disagreements.
  • Real-record sample.
    • Every candidate scoring above the validation threshold in the long and the medium cells, expected at about 50 to 300 for 2022 to 2026.
    • 50 drawn at random from the lower tiers.
    • 50 random event-free windows, to estimate misses.
  • Cost. About 4,000 tokens per review. The calibration set at two tiers plus about 400 real reviews with two Sonnet reviewers come to about 5 million tokens. Rendering is a few CPU-minutes.
  • Feedback.
    • Reviewed real labels are first a validation set for the scorer, split by year.
    • They join training only after the gate holds, at a weight of 0.2, with label noise set from the reviewer's measured precision, and never in the year they score.
    • Calls of "transfer" with confidence 4 or more go to NGED as a list of candidates.
  • Limits.
    • The reviewer sees the same residual as the scorer, so an unmetered partner is invisible to both.
    • Its injected-set precision carries over to real events only if injected figures look real.
    • NGED's labels are incomplete, so the reviewer's real-record calls cannot be checked against them. They are opinions with a measured injected-set precision.
  • Stop rule. If the reviewer fails the gate at both tiers, drop the manual review and keep the automatic tiers.

docs.title: D. Causal features for the production forecast
docs.text:
Per lag (the day lag and the week lag), at the lag's own time, from readings at least 24 hours before the origin.

Feature What it is Needs at inference time D1 The common-mode-removed own gap: the gap minus the all-Primaries median gap, in noise units All Primaries' power and lag-free twins, already in the K chain D2 The mirror at a neighbour: max over neighbours of −sign(own gap) × the neighbour's gap, in noise units, with the onset-time difference of the best mirror The neighbours' power D3 The routine-step rate per Primary over the last 60 days The Primary's own history D4 Causal step statistics at 6, 24, and 72 hours: mean gap over the last w minus over the w before that, at the lag's time and at the newest reading The newest readings D5 "Lag inside a suspected event": a causal cumulative-sum detector on D1, with time since the suspected onset and the suspected depth The newest readings D6 For the prevailing head: the return towards the earlier level, (current gap − gap at the suspected onset) / suspected depth, and a mirror reversal at the neighbour The newest readings

How the features are learnt.

  • D1 to D5 enter the lag encoder per lag, beside experiment 606's gap signals, with 50% signal dropout, as in experiment 610.
  • The synthetic shifts come from experiment 660's generator, applied to the lags only. The target is never shifted (experiment 590).
  • D4 to D6 enter experiment 650's departure head and experiment 652's R-haz head.
  • The prevailing head gains most from fresher readings. Also report, in lab conditions, the same features with readings up to 6 hours before the origin, to measure what lower latency would be worth.

Cheap test, on CPU, with no refit.

  1. On the stored banks of experiments 650 and 652, with K1 inference already on file, compute D1 to D6 causally per origin.
  2. Separability. The AUROC of "this lag lies inside an injected shift", for logistic regressions on:
    • experiment 606's summaries;
    • those summaries plus D1 to D5.
  3. The prevailing head. Refit experiment 652's B-haz and R-haz heads, which are small and fit on CPU, with and without D4 to D6. Score them in the origin strata of experiment 652.

Predictions that could fail.

  • The AUROC rises by 0.05 or more on bank S and bank X, as well as on bank M.
  • In-force scaled CRPS improves by 0.30 or more against R-haz.
  • Near-end and just-ended scaled CRPS improve by 0.30 or more.
  • Event-free cost rises by no more than 0.02 against K1.

Stop rule. If the AUROC gain is under 0.03 and no prevailing stratum gains 0.15, do not refit the lag encoder. Otherwise fine-tune K1 with D1 to D5 on 4 screen folds. That costs about 2 GPU-hours, one process at a time, and the backtests keep priority.

Cost. CPU only, about 3 to 5 hours.

Dependencies. The banks of experiments 650 and 652, the gap-signal code of experiments 606 and 610, and experiment 660's generator.

docs.title: Order and running rules
docs.text:
1. Run A0, then A1 to A4, then C's calibration set. These are CPU only and can run in parallel with B1 when the GPU is free.
  2. Run D's cheap test independently.
  3. Re-decode B3 only after A has its verdict, so the comparison of residuals uses the final decoder.

All parts:

  • Use systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=16G -p OOMPolicy=continue.
  • Never read the final-test window from 2026-07-01.
  • Name no NGED generator.
  • Follow the ml-experiment skill's review order.
  • Use one experiment id per part.
  • Do not change the event-table run of 2022-01-01 to 2026-10-31 that is already in progress with E1-J-sym. Its outputs become the real-record input to A and C.

docs.title: Maintainer amendment to part D (2026-11-10)
docs.text: The "this lag is inside a suspected event" flag need not be an explicit flag. Give the lag encoder the features that the simple detector uses (per-lag causal step statistics in noise units at several scales, the gap with the all-Primaries median removed, the opposite-sign neighbour gap, the routine-step rate, the return-to-level statistic), and let the network learn how to use them. Test the explicit flag only as a comparison arm: features only against features plus flag.

docs.title: Spec: FLOW-E next experiments
docs.text: This is a copy of the answer that an Opus sub-agent gave the Discuss session on 2026-11-09, trimmed of conversation. Every number in it is the sub-agent's own analysis of the stored outputs of experiment 651 and is unaudited. Scores are CRPS in points of capacity, on event-free rows at 24 to 120 hours, in the development months 2025-10 and 2025-12 only. No row on or after 2026-07-01 was read. None of the three proposals has run.

docs.title: Take-home
docs.text:
• FLOW-E's only measured cost comes almost entirely from one probable unlabelled event. I recomputed FLOW-E minus G0 at the six MW Primaries as +0.022 (the page gives +0.021). Five Primary-days at D10, 8 to 12 December 2025, carry 62% of that excess. Dropping D10's rows for 1 to 16 December 2025 (5% of the six MW rows) leaves +0.003, and the two seeds then disagree in sign, as they do for every other arm.
  • In those days D10 runs 15 to 21 points of capacity above G0's median for about ten days, and the forecasts of its electrical neighbours are off too. D12 runs 25 to 34 points above from 8 December, D15 13 to 60 points above, and D11 about 5 points below from 3 to 7 December. NGED's labels mark every one of those D10 rows event-free. FLOW-E lowers D10's median by about 0.7 points there, which is what a normal-running-arrangement (NRA) forecast should do if this was a transfer. I cannot verify that it was a transfer.
  • The same episode also inflates the class 2 recipe's "excess over A1". G0 minus A1 at the six MW Primaries is +0.141 on all rows and +0.078 without D10's rows for 1 to 16 December. D10 itself goes from +0.45 to −0.16. A1 follows load shifts most (0.119 on bank M), so A1 scores best on an unlabelled shift. The remaining excess sits mostly at D16 (+0.29 in October, +0.32 in December).
  • FLOW-E's follow gain needs a metered mirror. On bank X (no mirror) FLOW-E follows 0.059, exactly G0's figure. Its whole gain on banks M and S (0.038 against G0's 0.059 and C's 0.044 and 0.046) comes from reading the neighbour that received the load.
  • So FLOW-E has not yet been shown to cost anything on ordinary days, and it holds follow. The cheapest informative step is the confirmation run that experiment 651's gate cancelled. That run needs a rewired-graph placebo and the probable unlabelled event handled the same way for every arm.

docs.title: Brief facts checked
docs.text:
Claim in the brief Check Antisymmetric MW flow on each of 29 electrical edges; per-node correction = minus net outflow over capacity, times a learnt scale starting at zero Correct (e00651_nbmodel.flow_correction). The flow neural network reads only each end's two current gap values (day lag and week lag), plus the log capacity ratio, and no gap history as the design proposed. The correction is hidden on 50% of training rows. Auxiliary loss on the known synthetic flow, weight 0.1 Not quite. The loss is on the per-node lag correction, not the edge flow. It is (correction + injected lag shift)² / 0.2², and it applies on every training row with a present lag: target zero on unshifted rows, on all rows whether or not messages are hidden. Two months, two seeds, fine-tuning only; pretraining from experiment 591's chain Correct. The graph layer exists only in step 3. Follow on bank M 0.038 against 0.044; six MW CRPS 2.479 against 2.458 (+0.021, interval +0.010 to +0.032); q99 pinball 0.196 against 0.188 Correct (day-block 95% interval). The FLOW-E minus C leave-one-Primary-out contrast never flips: +0.017 to +0.028. The six MW excess over A1 (0.13) is the same for G0 Correct as stated, but about 45% of the excess is the D10 episode above. Seed noise exceeds every contrast except FLOW-E's Correct on all rows. Without the D10 episode it exceeds FLOW-E's as well.

Training data of experiment 651 (from e00418_prep, e00448_run.pretrain_rows, e00574_fit, e00397_prep, and the logs of experiment 591):

  • Step 1, pretraining: estimates of past weather (ERA5 means and CAMS shortwave) in pseudo-runs every 2 days from 2019-09-01, at leads of 0.5 to 351 h. Five Primaries start later after early-calibration cuts (D11 2019-09-17, D10 2019-12-01, D5 2020-02-01, D14 2020-07-01, D16 2021-02-01). Each fold has 7.0 to 7.9 million rows, ending at the start of the fold's month minus the cutoff age.
  • Step 2: a fresh mixer fitted on the ECMWF ENS history from 2024-04-01 to the cutoff, with a 3-day embargo.
  • Step 3, the step in which FLOW-E was trained: a daily fine-tune refitted on days 0 and 14 of each fold, on ENS rows with E3 rows and experiment 581's lag-only synthetic shifts.
  • Not used: the 2021-03 to 2024-03 ENS backfill from Source Cooperative.

docs.title: 1. FLOW-C: confirm FLOW-E on all five development months with a rewired placebo (run first)
docs.text:
• Question. Does FLOW-E keep a lower follow than G0 and the Candidate (C) across five months, and does the real electricity-network wiring beat a rewired graph?
  • Architecture changes. None to FLOW-E. Add FLOW-R, which is FLOW-E on a degree-preserving rewired graph, using experiment 651's GAT-R rewiring. Store the per-node correction (flow_scale × share) per row, so that it can be scored as a detector.
  • Training data. The same as experiment 651, so that G0 and C stay matched. The full 2019-onward ERA5 and CAMS history is already in step 1. This experiment adds none of it to the flow layer, because that would confound the confirmation: proposal 2 tests the full history.
  • Arms. G0, FLOW-E, and FLOW-R, fitted on 2025-10, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-03, and 2026-06 with seeds 0 to 2. The stored G0 and FLOW-E fits for 2025-10 and 2025-12 at seeds 0 and 1 are reused. C comes from the stored seed 0 to 2 forecasts of experiments 612 and 613. Banks M, S, and X.
  • Unlabelled-event screen, fixed before any score. One Primary-day mask for every arm, built from observed power and existing detectors only and never from any arm's residual. An example is K1's G4 gate or the refit-offset neighbour-count detector (RO-NC) firing on 3 or more consecutive days. The unscreened score is primary and the screened score is reported beside it. Report D10 for 1 to 16 December 2025 as its own descriptive row.
  • Predictions that could fail.
    • Pooled over five months, FLOW-E minus G0 follow on bank M is at most −0.015, with the month-block 95% interval excluding zero.
    • FLOW-E minus C on bank M is at most −0.005, in at least 4 of the 5 months.
    • On bank X, FLOW-E is within 0.005 of G0. This is a known-answer check: with no mirror there is nothing to read.
    • FLOW-R follows at least 0.010 more than FLOW-E on bank M.
    • Six MW event-free CRPS: the upper 95% bound of FLOW-E minus G0 is below +0.044 on the screened rows, and the point estimate is at most +0.01.
    • The correction scores an area under the curve (AUC) of at least 0.75 on injected lag-days of bank M against K1's G4.

  • Stop rule. Stop the FLOW line if either of these holds:

    • the FLOW-E minus G0 follow interval on bank M includes zero;
    • FLOW-R is within 0.005 of FLOW-E. In that case write "the mirror helps, the wiring does not", and proposals 2 and 3 do not run.

    Report a CRPS failure on the screened rows as "not non-inferior". Proposal 3 may still run on the correction alone in that case. - GPU-hours. Experiment 651 cost about 0.125 GPU-h per arm-month-seed including three banks. That gives 37 new arm-month-seeds, about 4.6 GPU-h, plus about 0.5 GPU-h for C on banks S and X. Ceiling 6 GPU-h, one GPU process at a time. Time one FLOW-R cutoff first. Outputs about 8 GB, so delete the S and X bank parquet once they are scored. - Dependencies. Experiment 651's code (arm, grouped bank, scorer, gate) and the experiment 612 and 613 stored forecasts. The GPU is idle as of this writing. - Improves: the NRA forecast (follow) directly. The prevailing forecast gains only through the stored correction, which proposal 3 uses.

docs.title: 2. FLOW-P: train the flow layer on the full 2019-onward history, with gap histories as inputs (only if proposal 1 passes)
docs.text:
• Question. Does a flow layer trained from step 1 onward, on the full 2019-onward ERA5 and CAMS history with mirrored synthetic shifts, and reading several days of gap history, follow less than FLOW-E on banks M and S without costing anything on ordinary days?
  • Architecture changes.
    • The flow layer and its auxiliary loss start in step 1 and continue through steps 2 and 3.
    • The flow neural network reads each end's gap at the day lag and the week lag for the last 7 days (14 values per end, instead of 2), a MW-or-MVA flag per end, and the log capacity ratio.
    • Inject experiment 581's mirrored synthetic shifts into the pretraining rows at 5% of each Primary's time, as step 3 already does.
  • Training data. The full 2019-onward ERA5 and CAMS history in step 1, about 7 million rows per fold, against the fine-tuning window alone in experiment 651. Step 2 stays on ENS from 2024-04 so that the arms stay matched. The ENS backfill from 2021 is a separate question. Two caveats:
    • In pretraining the gap signal comes from a twin forecast driven by ERA5, which is less noisy than the ENS-driven twin used at forecast time. Scoring stays on ENS rows.
    • Unlabelled real shifts in the 2019 to 2024 targets teach every arm to follow. G0-P below controls for that.
  • Arms. FLOW-E (from proposal 1); FLOW-P (pretrained, two current gaps as inputs); FLOW-PH (pretrained, 7-day gap histories); and G0-P (the same pretraining bank of mirrored shifts, no flow layer). G0-P tests whether the synthetic bank in pretraining does the work by itself. Five months, seeds 0 and 1, the same screen as proposal 1.
  • Predictions that could fail.
    • FLOW-PH follows at most 0.030 on bank M and at most 0.032 on bank S (FLOW-E: 0.038 and 0.038).
    • FLOW-PH minus FLOW-E on bank M is at most −0.005, with the month-block interval excluding zero.
    • G0-P stays within 0.005 of G0 on bank M.
    • Six MW event-free CRPS of FLOW-PH minus G0 has an upper 95% bound below +0.044 on the screened rows.
  • Stop rule.
    • If FLOW-PH does not beat FLOW-E on bank M by 0.005, keep FLOW-E as it is and stop changing its inputs.
    • If G0-P matches FLOW-PH, the gain comes from the synthetic bank, not from the flow layer, and the flow layer is dropped.
  • GPU-hours. Steps 1 and 2 for 3 arms × 5 months × 2 seeds come to about 30 units at about 0.22 GPU-h with the grouped bank, which is about 6.5 GPU-h. Ceiling 8 GPU-h. Time one step-1 fit first and stop if it runs over 15 GPU-minutes.
  • Dependencies. Proposal 1 passes. A new grouped loader for the pretraining rows is the main code to write, and the leak test of experiment 651 is extended to it.
  • Improves: the NRA forecast.

docs.title: 3. FLOW-H: the FLOW-E correction as evidence for the prevailing forecast (CPU first; only if proposal 1 keeps a working correction)
docs.text:
• Question. Does the neighbour-mirror evidence that FLOW-E's correction carries improve the prevailing-conditions forecast of experiment 652, scored by the state of the shift at the origin?
  • Architecture changes.
    • Add the stored per-node correction for the last 7 days, and a "mirror present" summary (the correction's absolute value over the own gap), as inputs to 652's R-haz head.
    • Add the same two inputs to a B-haz variant whose survival curve is fitted separately for shifts with a mirror and shifts without one (no neural network).
    • Experiment 652's head is a few thousand weights and is fitted on the CPU.
  • Training data. Experiment 652's banks (experiment 650's extended generator, whose donor and receivers are conserved across real electrical neighbours, with no neighbour in 15% of shifts) and K1 on all 5 development months. FLOW-E inference runs on those banks, on the CPU as K1's did in experiment 650. The full history is not needed, because the head reads K1 and FLOW-E outputs only.
  • Arms. R-haz, R-haz+FLOW, B-haz, B-haz-mirror, R0-168, a placebo (R-haz+FLOW with the correction shuffled among the same Primary's origins), and K1 as context. 2 seeds.
  • Scoring. As experiment 652: event-free, far-from-end, middle, near-end, and just-ended origin strata, by lead day 1 to 9, scaled and unscaled, with the one veto (event-free cost against K1 at most 0.03).

  • Predictions that could fail.

    • With a shift in force (strata pooled), R-haz+FLOW minus R-haz scaled CRPS is at most −0.10, with the month-block interval excluding zero, on shifts that have a mirror.
    • On shifts with no neighbour, the same contrast is within ±0.05. The prediction holds only if that placebo-by-construction holds too.
    • On event-free origins, R-haz+FLOW is no worse than R-haz by more than 0.02.

    My prior that the first prediction holds is low, at about 25%. A shift's end reaches both ends' lags at the same delay of at least 24 h, so the mirror cannot reduce the near-end cost. Its only route to a gain is a better estimate of the depth, and fewer false departures. - Stop rule. If the in-force gain is above −0.05 or the placebo moves the score by as much, record that the electricity-network mirror does not help the prevailing forecast and close the FLOW line for the prevailing forecast. - GPU-hours. 0 planned. If FLOW-E inference on CPU is too slow, at most 1 GPU-h. - Dependencies. Proposal 1, with its stored correction for all five months. Experiment 652's code and banks. - Improves: the prevailing forecast only.

docs.title: 0. The option of doing nothing more on FLOW-E
docs.text:
The reasons for stopping here:

  • The follow gain is small. On bank M it is −0.006 against C and −0.021 against G0, and on bank S it is −0.008 against C. FLOW-E does nothing without a metered mirror (bank X equals G0).
  • Eight of the 14 scored Primaries report MVA, which cannot show the direction of a flow.
  • Real transfers can split across neighbours or go to Primaries off the roster.
  • Two verified real episodes is too few to judge on.
  • At 16 Primaries and 29 edges the electricity-network graph has little room, and fleet-scale adjacency (about 1,161 Primaries) has not been supplied.

The reasons against stopping:

  • FLOW-E is the only arm of experiment 651 that held follow.
  • Its measured ordinary-day cost now looks like a scoring artefact of one probable unlabelled event.
  • FLOW-E is the "conservation along electrical edges" framing the roadmap already favours over learned message passing.
  • Proposal 1 costs at most 6 GPU-h and settles the question.

My recommendation: run proposal 1 only. Run proposals 2 and 3 only if proposal 1 passes.

docs.title: Not a FLOW-E proposal, but changed by these analyses
docs.text: The "0.13-point excess over A1" that experiment 651 pointed at the class 2 recipe (E3 rows, D5 offset, 50% signal dropout) is about 45% the D10 episode, and the rest is mostly D16. Re-score that excess with proposal 1's screen on all five months before planning any recipe ablation. A recipe ablation that is planned against the unscreened number could chase a scoring artefact.

docs.title: Spec: MVA reverse flow, sign label and the hard-mask arm
docs.text: This is a copy of the sections of a Sonnet research answer of 2026-11-09 that the January restart needs, trimmed of conversation. "Evidence" means a merged page of this repository, and "inference" means the answering agent's own tabulation of the cleaned power table before 2026-07-01. The answer's survey of earlier experiments and its table of cases against the working assumption are left out; the experiment numbers cited below lead to them. The zero-fit experiment in the last section has not run. NGED's labels in the table below are the Reverse Power Flow? column of a private file. They are a hint, not truth.

docs.title: Short answer
docs.text:
• The working assumption is mostly right but not always. The one real PV-driven case with a signed meter, D10, reverses only in April to August, 09:00 to 15:00 UTC (evidence for the direction, inference: 231 of 231 negative half-hours). At the eight MVA Primaries the best evidence is the same shape at D12. Counter-cases exist: one signed-MW series is negative at every hour of the day, and D8 has a gas engine (Gas A) behind it.
  • A hard high-PV mask is an established precision gate that costs recall. Experiment 417's A+H arm cut false reverse flow from 12.0% to 3.6% and cut recall from 0.77 to 0.37.
  • The eight cannot be calibrated where it matters. Experiment 508: nothing calibrates above an export of about 3 times the night import, and D12 is about 5.3 times.
  • Recommended first experiment: a zero-fit, CPU-only test of a per-Primary masked day labeller (last section).

docs.title: What NGED says, and where it conflicts with our data
docs.text:
Source. The only record is data/NGED/substation_hierarchy_2026-10-15/Monitor Direction.csv (private; README says received 2026-10-15 from NGED), column Reverse Power Flow?. There is no confidence column and the Comments column is empty. I found no written record of NGED saying the label is only a hint; that statement is in the brief.

Series Label Marsh Lane (D8) Yes Stickney (D12) Maybe Langrick (D22) Maybe Warth Lane (D2), Sleaford Road Boston (D3), Ingoldmells (D4), Chapel St Leonards (D19), Alford (D21) No MW series and the 2 MVA wind farms blank (MW series: directional monitoring "Yes") or "No" (wind farms)

Also, docs/background/network.md (this repository) says 10 sites are metered in apparent power (the eight plus two wind farms), and "one site, and possibly two more, have shown reverse flow on sunny days"; it gives no source. Experiment 79 records that NGED cannot supply real and reactive power at the eight.

Conflicts with our data.

  • D8 "Yes". Experiment 370: L0 finds no reverse flow (share at most 0.006). Experiment 506: dips to 0.26 points on at least one sunny day. Experiment 508: 55 of 71 dip days flagged engine, not separable from solar or load transfer. NGED's "Yes" may refer to the engine, not to PV.
  • D12 "Maybe". Our data are far stronger than "Maybe" (3 independent fits, ratio 5.3, 656 fold map flags D12 midday in all six months). The one method that fails to see it is the 10:00 to 15:00 dip statistic (506), because the crossing is in the shoulders.
  • D22 "Maybe". 13 dip days, and the cloudy-day test does not support solar (508: 0 cloudy dips of 122 days, Fisher p 0.12). Fits find about 0% to 3.7% reverse. Unresolved.
  • The five "No". Consistent. D2, D3, D4 have lowest readings of 4.9 to 5.4 MVA (152); D19 0.92 and D21 1.6 MVA, both far above zero given their PV estimates.

docs.title: Known-answer routes and calibration limits
docs.text:
Routes that exist.

  • Hide the sign at six MW Primaries (D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, D16) by taking the magnitude (reactive floor 0, 2, 4 points, or power factor 0.97), injecting a metered farm (Solar A to C) at levels 0.5 to 8 times the median sunny-midday reading, leaving the farm out in rotation (79, 358, 408, 412, 417, 420, 506, 508).
  • Real reverse flow with a signed meter: D10 (58 crossing days), D5 (5 days); 130 real half-hours in 417's count.
  • D12 itself has no truth. Closure against the bulk supply point cannot resolve the sign (152: coefficient 1.02, variance cut 0.7%; 506: only 58% to 71% of the children are metered).
  • Metered solar farm nearby (inference, not run as a test). docs/background/network.md shows D12's MVA peaks absent on 3 and 4 May when a nearby metered solar farm generated less. No experiment scored this as a label.
  • D8's engine: 44 days of the engine's own recorded output (experiment 194).

Calibration limits.

Limit Number 508 dip statistic: usable (area at least 0.8, lower end above 0.6) export-to-import ratio below 1.5, midday 0.82; 1.5 to 3, shoulders 0.85 and 0.88 against midday 0.51; above 3, not estimable (99.4% and 97.4% of days cross zero) 508 D12 ratio 5.3, shoulder dips as common on cloudy days (sunny-to-cloudy 1.05, 1.01 to 1.10); not calibrated 506 power factor 0.97 area 0.838; threshold flags 34% of no-sign-change days; reactive power fills the dip 508 selection only 22% of April to September days qualify, because recorded farm output is missing in 20% to 63% of shoulder half-hours 417 gate false reverse 12.0%; zero-crossing labeller area 0.96 at level 2.0 but 0.58 at level 1.0 427 labeller trained on high-demand Primaries fails at low-demand D5 (61.7% false reverse) D12's export-to-import ratio 5.27 in 508 (81.6 over 15.6 points in 506's May to July clear days); beyond the calibratable range of about 3

docs.title: Data a hard-masked label would need, and what is on disk
docs.text: Need On disk Caveat Power readings, unflagged data/NGED/cleaned_power_time_series.delta (33 series) cut at 2026-07-01 CAMS shape u and clear-sky index k per Primary data/ml-experiments/00412-*/work/cams/D*.npz (16 Primaries, 121,248 half-hours each) span unchecked; by my arithmetic it runs to about the end of July 2026, so cut at 2026-07-01 Extended CAMS and ERA5 00620-*/inputs/cams_demand_points_extended.parquet, 00607-*/work/era5_features.parquet extended to 2026-10-31 for the final test; read only before 2026-07-01 Sun elevation per Primary 00508-*/work/elevation_D*.npy Capacity table for the eight (p10, p50, p90, AC and DC) 00474-*/work/table_R4_pooled_table_era5_cams_mean_cloudterm.parquet; nged_table.md reactive power zero, placebo failed at every row (0.25 to 0.51), so circular at the eight Capacity from other methods 649 (six MW only), 656 and 662 (eight, provisional, one cutoff) D2 differs: 6.9 vs 11.3 MW Capacity from outside the telemetry 00129-*/work/registers.parquet (five MW Primaries only) none for the eight; experiment 506 advises obtaining one Effective capacity data/effective_capacity dated 2026-09-05 Day-level dip tables and frozen thresholds 00506-*/work/part1_*.parquet, 00508-*/work/partA_*.parquet, partA_thresholds.json thresholds frozen on the six Monitor Direction labels data/NGED/substation_hierarchy_2026-10-15/Monitor Direction.csv private; labels only Clear-sky mask k in the 412 arrays; 152 used the Haurwitz clear-sky value no stored per-Primary mask table Explicit PV estimate per Primary and half-hour not on disk as a table build as C_p50 x u; the neural PV module was not adopted (644 per 649)

docs.title: Recommended first experiment
docs.text:
First experiment (CPU only, zero fits): the per-Primary masked day labeller on known answers.

  • Mask. Per Primary, a half-hour is in the mask only if CAMS shape u is at least 0.1 (the sun-edge shoulders 508 found best; 0.3 would lose them) and the capacity gate holds: the Primary's 90th-percentile PV (474 R4) times u exceeds the dark-hour reading. The gate is per Primary because that series shows a global PV mask is wrong where non-PV export exists.
  • Label. Inside the mask, flag a day by 508's shoulder minimum (thresholds frozen on the six in ratio bins) and by experiment 417's W-shape score, and label as reverse flow the half-hours between the two minima on flagged days. Both rules exist already, so no new method is built.
  • Known-answer test. Injection of Solar A to C into D5, D9, D10, D11, D14, and D16 at levels 1, 2, and 3 with leave-one-farm-out, plus the no-injection placebo at the five clean Primaries, plus real D10. Score day-level area under the curve, half-hour recall at a false-reverse rate of at most 5%, and the placebo rate, by export-to-import bin as in 508.
  • Then apply to the eight and report a table of flagged days by Primary, sunny against cloudy, with no claim about truth. Check each Primary's mask coverage: share of its low (below 5 points) readings that the mask excludes.

Prediction that could fail. At export-to-import 1.5 to 3, the masked labeller reaches half-hour recall of at least 0.6 at false-reverse of at most 5%, and its no-injection placebo rate is at most 1% at each of D5, D9, D11, D14, and D16, with thresholds frozen on the other Primaries. On the eight, flagged days exceed 10% of sunny April to August days at D12 only, are at most 5% at D8 and D22, and are 0 at D2, D3, D4, D19, and D21. A prediction written with these numbers can be wrong at either end, and would fail 417's bars if copied.

Strongest reason it may fail. At low-demand Primaries (D5 and D10 mean sunny-midday reading 12 to 16 points against 38 to 53 elsewhere) the dip is a normal low-demand day: 427's labeller called 61.7% of D5's sunny middays reverse with nothing injected. At power factor 0.97 reactive power fills the dip (506: 34% false-flag). Above export of 3 times night import the method cannot be calibrated, and D12 is at 5.3 times. In short: the mask removes night and cloud false calls but not the low-demand sunny-day false calls, and no known answer exists at D12's export level.

Not CPU, but higher value. Signed MW for a few weeks at Stickney from NGED (79's advice, repeated in 79's lessons) would settle D12 without a fit. I found no record that it was asked.

docs.title: Metered solar farms
docs.text:
The current understanding and the options for next work are on the state and next steps page.

The summary of this theme is in progress. This theme covers the six solar farms whose output NGED meters in the trial area (labelled A to F). The experiments ask what shape each farm's output has, what physical plant (panel tilt, azimuth, ratio of direct-current to alternating-current capacity, heat loss, and inverter clip) reproduces it, and what that implies for the unmetered solar behind Primary substations. The Experiments page lists every experiment tried, and the Research plan lists what is planned next.

docs.title: Metered solar farms: experiments
docs.text:
This page lists every experiment tried in the theme, newest first. An experiment that belongs mainly to another theme but bears on this one is marked "also relevant".

Experiment Hypothesis Verdict Production status Take-home message Relevance 00636 metered-solar-monthly-slope-capacity-known-answer-test A least-squares regression of a farm's output on a fitted irradiance expectation over all daylight half-hours of a month, weighted by the clear-sky index squared, finds a known capacity step of 10% within 3 months at 4 of the 5 testable farms (Solar A, B, C, D, and F). It finds the step whether the loss is in alternating-current output or in direct-current capacity under inverter clipping, and it raises few false steps in cloudy months and under random curtailment. refuted not-for-production A monthly fit of a solar farm's output against irradiance can spot a 10% loss of capacity within 3 months at Solar C and Solar F, and a loss of 6.3% or more at Solar C, but not at Solar A, B, or D, whose own history is too noisy. A loss of direct-current capacity hidden under the inverter limit is found as often as a plain loss of output, because very few half-hours are clipped. The line stops here under its stop rule. primary 00618 solar-effective-capacity-sunny-rows-and-known-answer-test A farm's capacity moves rarely, so a piecewise-constant level fitted to one daily number taken from its very sunny half-hours (clear-sky index at least 0.9, clear-sky irradiance at least 700 W/m2, six half-hours in a row) recovers injected capacity steps, raises few false steps, and shows whether Solar A, Solar B, and Solar D produced more in 2021 to 2023 than now. partly supported not-for-production Very sunny half-hours are enough to find a sudden change of 8% or more in a solar farm's capacity at Solar A, B, C, and F, with at most 0.7 false changes a year; Solar D has too few of them and needs a change of 12%. Applied to the real histories, the method finds a fall of 12.6% at Solar A (its output in 2021 to 2023 was 14% higher than in 2025 to 2026, as experiment 453 saw), but at Solar B the output in 2021 to 2023 was 11% lower, not higher, and Solar C and Solar F show no change. The estimate lags a slow fall, so a smooth drift of 10% in three years leaves the final level 2% to 5% too high. primary 00498 solar-e-annual-refit-schedule-only-read At Solar E the 1.28% loss that experiment 493 reported (its contrast C3) comes mostly from the network design (one pass against the 51-member encoder), and the schedule-only loss (annual against quarterly refits of the encoder, contrast C2) is smaller than 1%. supported not-for-production Refitting the Solar E neural network once a year instead of every quarter raises its quantile score by about 0.3% (lower is better), which is less than the 1% limit, so Solar E does not block annual refits. An XGBoost model on the same weather scores 2.8% better overall, and the solar-farm model beats it only at the 0.99 quantile, the upper tail of the forecast, which matters for curtailment (switching a generator off when the electricity network is overloaded). primary 00218 metered-solar-farm-plant-fit The six metered solar farms differ in panel tilt, panel azimuth, ratio of direct-current to alternating-current capacity, heat loss, and inverter clipping, so a plant model with those parameters fitted per farm reproduces each farm's output better than the one fleet shape (tilt 35 degrees, facing south, DC:AC ratio 1.15, 0.4% loss per kelvin, cell temperature equal to air temperature plus 25 K times the shape), and explains why the flat top of farms C, D, E, and F falls 6% to 9% from spring to summer (experiment 183). not supported not-for-production Giving each metered solar farm its own panel tilt, azimuth, heat loss, and inverter limit fits its output only 0.003 better than one fleet shape (a fraction of output fitted of 0.953 against 0.950), so the plant is probably not what limits the fit. About 5% of the squared metered output stays unexplained, and the sunshine data is the likelier source. Per-farm plant parameters look unpromising for forecasting; a better sunshine forecast looks more promising, because the same plants fit only 0.91 with the ensemble forecast. primary
